baseline.description:
## Context
The Engine B metric backend parses per-file entries from scc JSON, but `_metric_invoke` invokes `scc --format json <repo>` without `--by-file`. With maintained scc 3.7.0, the language summary includes `Files: []` unless `--by-file` is requested. Therefore a present scc process can run successfully while `rebar.builtin.smell.metric-oversize` sees no files and can never emit its documented over-800-LOC matches.

The analogous code-health adapter defect was fixed by closed bug rapid-cuboid-velvetcrab. The grounding backend `_scc_files` is a separate, previously unaudited consumer of the same scc JSON shape. Current coverage-reconstruction tests use a 50-LOC fixture or force tool absence, so they do not exercise the positive metric threshold path.

## Reproduction
- Run `scc --format json tests/unit/grounding` and inspect each language `Files` array: it is empty.
- Compare with `scc --by-file --format json tests/unit/grounding`: per-file entries are present.
- Inspect `src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py::_metric_invoke`: its command omits `--by-file` while `_scc_files` depends on `Files`.

## Plan
- Use rebar-debug to reproduce with a real scc binary and an over-800-code-line fixture, then prove the exact argv cause before editing.
- Add a physically withheld RED oracle that observes a real or argv-faithful scc boundary and only produces per-file entries when `--by-file` is present.
- Correct the grounding metric invocation without changing the existing `Code` field, thresholds, or fail-open semantics.
- Add positive match, below-threshold no-match, invalid-output, nonzero-exit, and tool-absent coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A present scc run over a file above the configured LOC threshold emits a normalized metric match for that file.
- [x] A present scc run below the threshold emits no fabricated match.
- [x] The scc command requests per-file JSON explicitly; checked by an argv-sensitive test.
- [x] Tool absence, timeout/nonzero failure, and invalid JSON remain fail-open evidence outcomes.
- [x] The focused grounding backend tests pass with the held-out exact-defect oracle.

## Verification
- Run the focused grounding metric tests with the worktree virtualenv.
- Run the repository lint and typecheck gates.
- Run the default test suite before landing through Gerrit.
baseline.summary: Grounding metric detector omits scc --by-file and can never emit file matches

## Context
Split out of 06e0-fb68-657a-4ea1 (effete-barbaric-xiaosaurus), which promoted every package that was already clean or within a handful of trivial annotations. Tier 1 (`disallow_untyped_defs`) now covers 13 packages and tier 2 (`disallow_any_explicit`) covers `rebar._cli.*` and `rebar._snapshot.*`.

## The residue (measured on main @ ea6ee67e6a)
| package | untyped defs | explicit Any |
|---|---|---|
| llm | 293 | ~165 |
| _commands | 146 | large |
| _engine | 134 | ~224 |

This is epic-sized and NOT trivially small, which is why it was excluded rather than attempted. It also collides with near-cap modules (`llm/plan_review/pass1.py` is at the 800 LOC cap) and with the reconciler port-boundary work already scoped by cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8.

## Approach
Needs decomposition. Prioritise by DRIVER (contract boundaries first), not by count, and promote a package into tier 1 then tier 2 only when `mypy src/rebar/<pkg>` is clean under the respective flags. Do NOT reach for `cast()` — it hides the same blindness the tiers exist to remove.
baseline.summary: Promote llm, _commands and _engine into the mypy strictness ratchet (573 untyped defs, ~390 explicit Any)

## Why
The grep-against-source inventory surfaced ANTI-PATTERN existence tests beyond the report's list, each able to pass while the behavior is broken: `test_applier_exceptions.py` (three `hasattr`-only importability tests that never raise the error); `test_applier_reschedule.py::test_exit_reschedule_constant_is_distinct` (`==75`); `test_fs_tools_extraction.py::test_fs_tools_exposes_the_shared_cluster` (7-symbol `hasattr` sweep); `test_overlap_retrieve.py::test_field_weights_constant` (exact private `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` values); `test_code_review_artifact.py::test_code_review_excluded_from_ jira_sync` (asserts `code_review` present/absent in reconciler source). VALIDATED.

## What
Replace each with a test that provokes the real behavior: trigger each exception path; assert EXIT_RESCHEDULE via the reschedule path that returns it; prove the fs_tools cluster via the existing identity/reuse seam; exercise ranking that `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` drives; run `reconcile` and assert `code_review` tickets are excluded from Jira sync.

## Scope
- The five test files above.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Reported by, not investigated by, an adjacent session

Surfaced while confirming the fix for bug 8070 (external-integration canary). Per operator instruction this was NOT investigated — epic e369 is actively held by another session and owns this subject matter. Filing it here so the owning session sees it. **The root cause below is a candidate, not a finding.**

## Observed (live CI, reproducible)

Run 30651750699 — `workflow_dispatch` of `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` on `main` at commit `b7e6ac963`, 2026-07-31. Job **"jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)"**:

```
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:319
AssertionError: no local ticket was created from DC issue RBJNAZV-1;
  stdout='invariants: scanned=1 filed=0 (cap=5)\nOK: applied 1 of 1 mutations\n'
assert []
FAILED test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance
```

The failing test is `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance`.

## Why this is newly visible

This failure was previously MASKED. Until `b7e6ac963` the whole external tier died at `SnapshotRefError` on an unborn `HEAD` before reaching any behaviour under test (bug 8070). With snapshot resolution fixed, the tier now reaches its subject and this assertion fails on its merits. So this is very likely a pre-existing defect that the canary could not previously report, not a new regression from `b7e6ac963` — which touched only `tests/external/conftest.py` (adds an empty root commit) and added a unit test.

## Candidate cause — UNCONFIRMED, do not treat as diagnosed

`scanned=1 filed=0` says the inbound record was seen and then not filed. That shape is consistent with OPEN bug **5f48-244c-7063-42d0** — "DC inbound identity mint fails silently: 'jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel" — where a silent mint failure would drop the record between scan and file. Linked `relates_to`. If that is the cause, this ticket is a duplicate and should be closed as such rather than worked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism behind `scanned=1 filed=0` is identified and cited (`path:line`), and it is
      determined whether this is the same defect as 5f48 (close as duplicate) or distinct.
- [ ] `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes against the live DC
      harness, or the failure is guarded by a credential-free test in the default suite.
baseline.summary: DC inbound filing is a no-op in live CI: reconcile reports scanned=1 filed=0, no local ticket created from DC issue

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` measures **796 lines** against the repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist escape hatch. Four lines of headroom is not enough for the sibling story that makes the outbound create path target a per-ticket project, so that story cannot land until this file has room.

## Approach

Extract the entire `update_one` sub-tree — lines **432-796** — into a new `dispatch_update.py`. This is a pre-existing call-graph seam, not a mechanical cut: `update_one` (`:447`) calls `_update_one_apply_parent` (`:497`), `_update_one_scalar_update` (`:500`), `_update_one_dispatch_labels` (`:506`) and `_update_one_dispatch_links` (`:510`), and `_update_one_scalar_update` is the sole caller of `_is_illegal_transition_400`. Nothing above line 432 calls into the block; the only dependency runs downward, through `_call_with_retry` (`:71-143`), which stays put.

The repository has already made this exact split twice: `dispatch_apply_phases.py` (226 lines) holds three other `update_one` phases, and `batch_dispatch.py` (148 lines) is the stable re-export facade. This extraction follows the pattern rather than inventing one.

**The import edge the new module must carry.** `update_one` does not only call the four helpers that move with it — it also calls `_update_one_apply_reporter` (`:498`), `_update_one_filter_fields` (`:499`) and `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:507`), which already live in `dispatch_apply_phases` and are imported at `dispatch_one.py:53-55`. Those three imports move to `dispatch_update.py` with their caller; `dispatch_one` drops them, since nothing left in it uses them. This is what makes the extraction land in the module that already owns the other `update_one` phases.

**The one hazard, and how it is avoided.** `dispatch_one.py` must **not** re-export `update_one` back for convenience — that would create `dispatch_one → dispatch_update → dispatch_one`, because `dispatch_update` imports `_call_with_retry` from `dispatch_one`. Instead `batch_dispatch.py`'s import block (`:31-40`) is re-pointed at `dispatch_update` for `update_one` and `_is_illegal_transition_400`. That is the only production re-point needed: `applier.py:122-130` already imports both symbols **from `batch_dispatch`**, not from `dispatch_one`, so its `__all__` at `:329` keeps resolving with no edit.

`batch_dispatch` is the established public surface. Its import block at `:31-38` currently takes six names from `dispatch_one` — `_call_with_retry`, `_find_link_id`, `_index_existing_links`, `_is_illegal_transition_400`, `create_one` and `update_one`. (`delete_one` is **not** among them; it is defined in `batch_dispatch` itself at `:54`.) After the move that block splits three ways: `_call_with_retry` and `create_one` still come from `dispatch_one`; `_is_illegal_transition_400` and `update_one` come from `dispatch_update`; and `_find_link_id` / `_index_existing_links` are taken directly from `dispatch_apply_phases`, where they are actually defined (`:206` and `:180`) and from which `dispatch_one` only re-exports them. Every edge then points from `batch_dispatch` downward and from `dispatch_update` to `dispatch_one`, never back, so the direction stays acyclic.

**The new module's complete import inventory**, derived by scanning the moved range rather than by inspection:

- stdlib: `json`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `urllib` — and only these four. `logging`, `time`, `os`,
  `random` and `pathlib` are imported by `dispatch_one` but unused inside `432-796`, so they stay.
- `typing`: `Any`, `cast`.
- from `rebar_reconciler._errors`: `JiraAPIError`, `http_status`.
- from `rebar_reconciler.dispatch_apply_phases`: `_update_one_apply_reporter`,
  `_update_one_filter_fields`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`, `_find_link_id`,
  `_index_existing_links`.
- from `rebar_reconciler.pass_io`: `record_parent_divergence` only. That module is imported at
  `dispatch_one.py:57` alongside `_write_mapping_atomic`, which the moved range does **not** use, so
  `dispatch_one` keeps its own `pass_io` import for that name.
- from `rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one`: `_call_with_retry`.

**One CI gate keys on the symbol's file.** `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records per-symbol ceilings keyed as `<file>::<symbol>`, and two of its keys name this module — `dispatch_one.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` and `dispatch_one.py::create_one`. The first symbol moves, so its key must be re-pointed to `dispatch_update.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` or the complexity gate fails on a file that no longer defines it; `create_one` stays and its key is untouched. This consumer lives outside the source tree and is invisible to any symbol- or import-level search, which is why it is called out explicitly.

**One consumer does need an edit.** `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py:36` imports `update_one` **directly** from `dispatch_one`, so it breaks the moment the symbol moves and the no-re-export rule forbids papering over it. That import is re-pointed at `batch_dispatch`, which is where every other consumer already gets it. This is the single test edit this story makes, and it is enumerated rather than discovered during implementation — an earlier draft of this plan wrongly claimed no test changes were needed.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_update.py` (new) — the moved sub-tree, ~405 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — drops to ~431 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/batch_dispatch.py` — the `:31-38` import block split across
  `dispatch_one`, `dispatch_update` and `dispatch_apply_phases`; the only production re-point
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — the `_update_one_dispatch_links` ceiling re-keyed to the new
  file
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py` — its direct
  `from ... dispatch_one import update_one` at `:36` re-pointed at `batch_dispatch`

`applier.py` is deliberately **not** in scope: it already imports the moved symbols from `batch_dispatch` (`:122-130`), so it needs no change.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so no new behavioural tests: the oracle is the existing suite passing **unchanged**, which is what proves the move preserved behaviour. Two specific hazards are verified rather than assumed:

- Monkeypatch survival: there are **five** module-attribute patch sites on `dispatch_one`, across
  three test modules — `apply/test_applier_identity_write.py:156,195`,
  `test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py:258,279` and `test_error_taxonomy.py:61` — and every one of
  them patches the same attribute, `dispatch_one.time`. All five stay safe: `time` is consumed by
  `_call_with_retry` and `create_one`, both of which remain resident, and `dispatch_update` reaches
  the retry helper by importing `_call_with_retry` from `dispatch_one`, so the sleep call still
  resolves against `dispatch_one`'s globals where the patch is applied. Confirm all five pass
  unedited — this is the assertion that proves the split did not silently defeat a patch.
- Import-cycle check: importing `dispatch_one` and `dispatch_update` in either order must succeed,
  asserted directly so a future re-export cannot silently reintroduce the cycle.
- Direct-importer coverage: the one re-pointed test
  (`test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py`) passes after its import is changed, and a repository-wide
  grep for `from rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one import update_one` returns no remaining hit. The grep
  is part of the oracle because this consumer was missed by symbol-level analysis and only a string
  search surfaced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatch_one.py` and `dispatch_update.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by running
      the module-size gate and recording both counts.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes, with exactly one existing test file edited —
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py`, whose direct import
      is re-pointed — and one file added,
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dispatch_update_split.py`, which holds this story's
      structural assertions; checked by the gating test command plus confirming the diff under
      `tests/` touches only those two paths.
- [ ] All five `dispatch_one.time` patch sites pass unedited; checked by running the three named
      test modules.
- [ ] `dispatch_update.py` carries the full import inventory named in the Approach and `dispatch_one`
      no longer imports what it stopped using; checked by asserting both modules' import lists.
- [ ] The complexity gate passes with `_update_one_dispatch_links` re-keyed to
      `dispatch_update.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` and `create_one`'s key unchanged; checked by
      running the complexity-baseline gate and inspecting both keys.
- [ ] `batch_dispatch` resolves all six previously-imported names after its block is split; checked
      by importing each from `batch_dispatch` and asserting no `ImportError`.
- [ ] No `from rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one import update_one` remains anywhere in the tree; checked
      by a repository-wide string grep returning zero hits.
- [ ] `dispatch_one.py` does not import from `dispatch_update.py`; checked by a test that imports the
      two modules in both orders and asserts no `ImportError`.
- [ ] `update_one` and `_is_illegal_transition_400` remain reachable through `batch_dispatch` **and**
      through `applier`'s existing re-export; checked by asserting both resolve from each module
      after the move, which confirms `applier.py` needed no edit.
- [ ] No behaviour change: checked by confirming the moved functions' bodies are identical to their
      pre-move text apart from import lines.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the update_one sub-tree from dispatch_one.py into dispatch_update.py

baseline.description:
# J4 — Pin a `UserIdentityModel` contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

User identity is the second real Cloud/DC difference. Jira Cloud identifies users by opaque `accountId` (username and userkey were removed for GDPR); Data Center identifies them by `name`. This leaks into two places in the Cloud adapter: `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee`, which returns `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` and encodes the 3-state account-resolution fast-path the core diff consults (ADR 0035 §(d) canonical-comparison corollary), and the transport's create/update assignee payload shape.

PR #120 handled this by copying `resolve_assignee` and hardcoding `is_account_id=False`, and its copy consulted `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` — an attribute nothing ever sets, so its entire authoritative branch was unreachable and DC would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. That is not a cosmetic bug: a permanently non-authoritative assignee resolution makes the outbound diff re-emit assignee changes it can never converge, which is the churn class epic `ace2` was created to fix.

## Approach

Define a `UserIdentityModel` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `resolve(local_value, remote_identity)` returning the existing `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` tuple, and `to_payload(value)` returning the deployment's assignee field shape. Two implementations: `AccountIdIdentity` (Cloud — the current behavior verbatim, `{"accountId": …}`) and `NameIdentity` (DC — resolves through the DC user-search endpoint, `{"name": …}`).

`NameIdentity` performs a **real** lookup against DC's user-search endpoint rather than echoing the local value, so it can return `authoritative=True` and the diff converges. Its resolver is injected at construction from the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], not discovered via `getattr`, so there is no unreachable branch.

**Alternative rejected:** DC returns the local value with `authoritative=False` always (PR #120's effective behavior). It compiles and passes shallow tests while guaranteeing assignee-diff churn on every pass.

**Alternative rejected:** normalizing both to a single "user reference" string. The core diff's 3-state fast-path genuinely needs to know whether the value is an accountId, so flattening it would push the branch back into core.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — Cloud constructed with `AccountIdIdentity`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_model.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier with a stateful fake resolver for the lookup (the irreducible external boundary), plus a shared contract test over both implementations, since the 3-state contract must hold identically for each.

- shared contract, parameterized over both models: an empty local value yields
  `("", False, <model default>)`; a value that resolves to the SAME identity the remote already has yields
  `(None, True, …)` (converged, nothing to emit); a value resolving to a different identity yields that
  identity with `authoritative=True`.
- Cloud-specific: the resolved value is an accountId and `is_account_id is True`; payload is `{"accountId": …}`.
- DC-specific: the resolved value is a username and `is_account_id is False`; payload is `{"name": …}`.
- failure path: an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (the neutral base at
  `_backend.py:48`) rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value.
- regression oracle for PR #120's defect: a test asserts that for a resolvable assignee, DC returns
  `authoritative=True` — this test fails against the `getattr`-based implementation.
- contrast case: an unassigned local value yields the documented desired-unassigned state, not a lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test covers all three resolution states for both identity models
- [ ] a test asserts DC returns `authoritative=True` for a resolvable assignee (the anti-churn oracle)
- [ ] a test asserts an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for both models
- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` returns nothing — no `getattr`-discovered collaborator anywhere
- [ ] J1's pinned Cloud assignee behavior is unchanged (`make test` green with those assertions unmodified)
baseline.summary: J4 — pin a UserIdentityModel contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py::test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer` intermittently kills its pytest-xdist worker on the macOS py3.13 `Verified` cell, reddening the whole matrix job and costing changes a `Verified -1` they did not earn (observed on change 1731 ps2; the identical commit passed in change 1734).

## Root cause — CONFIRMED, reproduced deterministically
Two measurements, both in this worktree, name the mechanism:

1. **The crash is a per-test-timeout kill, not OOM and not a pandoc fault.** CI runs the unit suite with `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`). pytest-timeout's *thread* method calls `os._exit(1)` from its timer thread, so the xdist worker process dies outright — no traceback, no assertion text. Reproduced by lowering only the budget: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py -n 2 --dist worksteal --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` emits `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated` followed by `worker 'gw0' crashed while running '...::test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer'` — byte-identical in shape to the CI report.
2. **The test's cost is unbounded and load-dependent.** It walks the whole committed corpus in ONE test function: 884 renderable units, each rendered twice (`_convert` plus the `_legacy_convert` oracle) = ~1768 serial pandoc spawns. Measured **91.6s** idle; under saturating CPU pressure (2x `hw.ncpu` spinners, the `fade-ea90` precedent) the same test measured **504.8s** — 1.7x past the 300s guard. macOS is the scarcest cell in the runner pool, so that contention is routine, which is why only that cell reds.

The osprey cross-worker sharing commit `48a3ba0b8a` does **not** cover this file — it touched `test_wiki_render_corpus.py` only, and its `corpus_pass1` artifact holds pass-1 renders of whole bodies, not the per-unit `_convert`/oracle pairs this test compares. Siblings measured healthy post-48a3ba0b8a (worst call 12.5s), so this test is the last one of the shape.

## Approach
Make the per-test cost **bounded and independent of both load and corpus size**, without touching what is compared. Replace the single monolithic loop in `test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer` with a **chunk-parametrized** test: `_renderable_units()` is computed once at module import, sliced into fixed-size batches by a new module constant `_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK = 40`, and the test takes the chunk as a `pytest.mark.parametrize` argument keyed by chunk index.

Why this shape and not the alternatives:
- **Fixed chunk size is the class fix.** Growing the corpus adds *cases*, never lengthens a case, so the per-test budget can never be re-crossed by fixture growth — the failure mode is closed structurally, not tuned away.
- Every one of the 884 units is still compared against the oracle with real pandoc; `_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE` stays 1. The byte-identity property the test exists to protect is untouched.
- 23 cases at ~4.2s idle each leaves ~13x headroom even at the 5.5x inflation measured above, and xdist can now spread the work across workers instead of pinning it to one.
- Explicitly NOT doing: raising `--timeout`, adding a rerun/flaky marker, or asserting on elapsed time (the wall-clock-assert gate forbids the last).

A failing comparison currently reports only `assert <str> == <str>` from an anonymous loop iteration. The chunked assertion carries the unit's **global corpus index** in its message, so a future failure names which unit moved.

To keep chunking from silently dropping units, add `test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit`: a pandoc-free test asserting the concatenation of all chunks equals `_renderable_units()` and that the total is >= 100 (the evidence floor the old inline `assert len(sampled) >= 100` provided, which moves out of the per-chunk body since no single chunk meets it).

The module docstring gains a short cost-discipline note mirroring the one `test_wiki_render_corpus.py` already carries, so the next author sees why the parametrization exists.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py` — chunk-parametrize the equivalence test, add the coverage guard, document the cost discipline. This is the only file changed; the renderer itself (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py`) is deliberately untouched, since the fault is in the test's cost profile, not in `_convert`.

## Testing
Test-only change, so the tests ARE the deliverable; verification is by measurement:
- Happy path: the full file passes with real pandoc and every unit still compared — `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py -q --durations=0`, with no call above ~10s idle.
- Load path (the reproduction, re-run after the fix): the same file under 2x `hw.ncpu` CPU spinners must complete with every individual call well inside 300s, where the pre-fix test measured 504.8s.
- Failure path: the new coverage guard fails if a chunk is dropped — verified by temporarily truncating the chunk list in a scratch run and observing the guard red before reverting.
- Regression path: the whole suite under CI's exact invocation, `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`, must show no worker crash.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The mechanism is recorded on this ticket with its deterministic reproduction — verified by the presence of the lowered-timeout command and the 91.6s/504.8s pair above, both re-runnable in this worktree.
- [x] No single test in `test_wiki_render_hardening.py` exceeds ~10s idle — verified by `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py --durations=0` showing every `call` under that bound.
- [x] Per-test cost is bounded by construction, not by tuning — verified by reading `_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK`: chunk size is a fixed constant, so corpus growth adds cases rather than extending any case.
- [x] The byte-identity property is not weakened — verified by `test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit` asserting the chunks reassemble to exactly `_renderable_units()` (884 units, >= 100), with `_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE` still 1 and real pandoc on both sides.

baseline.description:
# The DC store-copy fixture hard-fails on `git fetch origin tickets` and swallows git's reason

## Context / Problem

Live External Integration run **31587452003** (2026-08-12, head `b13173bb7d`) ended the DC harness at `1 failed, 59 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 error in 2471.11s`. The **error** is a fixture failure, not a cell defect:

    ERROR tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_unassign_round_trips
      - subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git','fetch','origin','tickets']'
        returned non-zero exit status 128.

It aborts at setup of `dc_store_copy_repo` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py`, lines 139-141 at origin/main `cc69cc1179`), which fetches the live `tickets` branch in the outer CI checkout and then `git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x` to seed a scrubbed store copy.

**Two problems, and the second is why the first is still unexplained:**

1. **The failure is undiagnosable, by construction.** The call is
   `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, check=True)`: `capture_output=True` routes git's
   stderr into a captured buffer, and `check=True` then raises `CalledProcessError` whose
   string form carries only the exit status. Git's own message — the one line that would say
   whether this was auth, a missing ref, a refspec miss under the CI partial clone, or a
   network error — is discarded. From the run log, exit 128 is all there is. The `git archive`
   (142-144) and `git ls-tree` (151-156) calls beside it have the identical shape.
2. **The fetch is a single un-retried network call** on the critical path of a 41-minute live
   job, so any transient blip takes the cell out as an ERROR.

## Approach

Fix the diagnostic FIRST — it is what makes the retry policy decidable.

* Add a module-level `_run_git(argv, cwd, ...)` helper in `_dc_fixtures.py` that runs the
  command with captured output and, on a non-zero exit, raises `RuntimeError` carrying the
  joined argv (which names the remote and branch), the exit status, and git's captured
  **stderr** verbatim. Route the fetch, archive and ls-tree calls through it.
* Then add bounded retry to the fetch only: `_fetch_tickets(...)` retries a failing fetch a
  fixed small number of times with a backoff sleep (injectable for test), and on final failure
  re-raises the diagnostic error. Policy is **retry-then-fail**, not retry-then-skip, so a
  genuine misconfiguration still reds the lane rather than silently dropping coverage.

The helpers are plain module-level functions, so the unit tier can load `_dc_fixtures.py` by path (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, the pattern already used by `tests/unit/test_live_dc_isolation_controls_59b2.py`) and drive them with a stubbed `subprocess.run` — no harness image, no live lane, verified on every commit.

## Scope

* `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py` — new `_run_git` / `_fetch_tickets` helpers;
  the `dc_store_copy_repo` fetch/archive/ls-tree calls routed through them.
* `tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` — new unit cell (repo tier).

## Testing

All acceptance evidence is repo-tier and runs under plain `pytest tests/unit/...`; the live lane is operator-spend and is NOT a gate for this ticket (see "Follow-up", below).

* stubbed `subprocess.run` returning exit 128 with a distinctive stderr line proves the raised
  message carries that stderr, the remote, the branch and the status — and the negative
  control proves it goes RED against the old `check=True` shape (a `CalledProcessError` whose
  text does not contain the stderr).
* stubbed `subprocess.run` failing once then succeeding proves the fetch retries and returns.
* stubbed `subprocess.run` always failing proves the attempt count is bounded and the final
  raise still carries git's stderr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_dc_fixtures.py`'s git fetch failure path raises an error whose message contains git's
      captured stderr verbatim plus the remote, the branch and the exit status — proven by a
      unit cell with a stubbed failing `subprocess.run`
- [x] the same holds for the `git archive` and `git ls-tree` calls in `dc_store_copy_repo`
      (no `capture_output=True` + `check=True` pair is left in that fixture)
- [x] the fetch retries a transient failure a bounded number of times before failing — proven
      by one stub that fails once then succeeds and one that always fails, the latter
      asserting the attempt count is capped and the final error still names git's stderr
- [x] no cell is deleted, skipped or `xfail`ed; `make lint`, `make typecheck` and
      `pytest tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` pass

## Follow-up (deliberately NOT an AC here)

Confirming on a live run that `test_outbound_unassign_round_trips` either passes or now fails with git's actual reason requires a Live External Integration run, which is operator-spend and cannot be triggered from this ticket. The next scheduled live run reads the improved message; if it still errors, the log will finally name the cause and that becomes its own ticket.

## Not in scope

The other residual in the same run — `test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers` failing with `rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s` — is the tracker write-lock contention family and is already tracked by `royal-weariless-zebrafish` (`10c3-5a33-2e25-4584`). Do not fold it in here.
baseline.summary: DC store-copy fixture hard-fails on git fetch origin tickets and swallows git's stderr

baseline.description:
# `rebar comment <id> --body-file <path>` stores the literal string \`--body-file\` and exits 0

## Observed twice, by two different sessions

`rebar comment` takes its body POSITIONALLY (`Usage: rebar comment <ticket_id> <body>`). It has no `--body`/`--body-file` option. When invoked with one anyway, the flag token is accepted AS the body: the stored comment is the 11-byte string \`--body-file\` (or the 6-byte \`--body\`), the intended content is silently discarded, and **the command exits 0** so nothing signals the loss.

Evidence in the live store right now:
- ticket b690 comments 5-9: five stubs of length 11, 11, 11, 11, 6 — an entire session's root-cause
  analysis, fix rationale, blast-radius audit and live evidence, all lost.
- session log 55a9 comment 5: also \`--body-file\`, written by an EARLIER session. So this is not a
  one-off slip; the same footgun has now cost two independent sessions their durable record.

## Why this is worse than a normal CLI usage error

rebar's own guidance (AGENTS.md) is emphatic that the ticket store — not scratch notes — is the durable, shared trail, and that agents should write progress and findings back as comments. This failure mode silently defeats exactly that instruction, and it does so in the least detectable way:
- exit code 0
- no stderr
- a comment DOES appear, so a \`len(comments)\` check (which is the natural way to confirm "did my
  write land?") passes while the content is gone
- the loss is only discovered later by something that READS the content — in this case the completion
  verifier, which correctly failed a ticket for having "no concrete attestation recorded" because the
  attestation genuinely was not there.

The cost is not the retyping. It is that work believed to be recorded is not, and downstream gates make correct-but-confusing decisions on the missing evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a body argument that begins with \`-\` is REJECTED with a non-zero exit and a message naming the
      correct form, rather than stored — unless the user clearly meant it (see below)
- [x] the escape hatch exists and is documented: a body that legitimately starts with \`-\` can still be
      written (conventionally via \`--\`, e.g. \`rebar comment <id> -- "-starts with a dash"\`)
- [x] the same guard covers every positional-body command with this shape, not just \`comment\`
      (audit at least \`create\`/\`edit\`/\`session-log\` for the same footgun and fix or document each)
- [x] a test asserts the REJECTION for \`--body-file <path>\` and \`--body <text>\` specifically, since
      those are the two forms that have actually occurred
- [x] consider (and decide explicitly, either way) whether to ADD a real \`--body-file\` option: the
      fact that two independent sessions reached for it suggests it is the expected interface for
      long bodies, and shell quoting of multi-KB markdown through a positional arg is awkward
- [x] no silent truncation or coercion anywhere in the fix: a body that cannot be stored as given must
      fail loudly

## Notes

Filed OUTSIDE epic 061c — unrelated to the LLM provider seam; this is a CLI/store-durability concern. Found when the completion verifier failed story b690 for missing attestations that had in fact been written five times over.
baseline.summary: rebar comment silently stores a flag-looking argument as the comment body, destroying the record (has now hit two sessions)

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase` (`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and `process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds, at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and `_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22` is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus `_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker: `_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [ ] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [ ] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the STATUS cluster from reducer/_processors.py into _processors_status.py

The DET floor is the ONLY blocking tier (every LLM criterion is advisory in v1). It must be a frozen, deterministic, polyglot floor that fails open on any unsupported stack.

## What

  (deps.dev registry + optional syft SBOM); P4 oversize (scc/lizard metrics); P5 task-DAG validity + interference;
  P6 AC/DD quality; P7 destructive/irreversible sniff (escalates T4). The polyglot resolution/dependency/size tooling (P2/P3/P4) is CONSUMED — via the SHIPPED `refute_absence`/`applies`/`scan` facade — from the now-CLOSED prerequisite epic 8f6c-6008-33f3-4f82 (code-grounding oracle, `src/rebar/grounding/`) — this child does NOT re-build it; it owns the rebar-specific checks (P1/P5/P6/P7) + wiring P2/P3/P4 into the DET floor.

## Scope
- Call the 8f6c grounding-oracle facade (refute_absence/applies/scan); its three-valued abstain-by-default contract IS the fail-open guarantee — unsupported lang / no tool / parse-error / timeout -> abstain (recorded reason) -> skipped = PASS (ironclad).
- The shared oracle SHIPPED as prerequisite epic 8f6c (CLOSED; also consumed by code-review `9da1`); this child depends_on it and consumes it as a library, not as new integrations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] P1-P7 implemented in Python, polyglot, fail-open (skipped=pass) tested per tool.
- [ ] Coverage recorded on the attestation.
- [ ] DET floor is the only tier that blocks BY DEFAULT in v1 (every LLM criterion is advisory; per-criterion LLM-tier blocking is OPT-IN via its `block_threshold` — 'DET-only' is the v1 default posture, not an architectural limit).

## (Added) P8 — reviewability / context-budget (DET)
A meta-finding, not tied to any one criterion, so it lives in the deterministic floor as P8: a DET check that PASSES unless the ticket content (or a parent+child pairing for container criteria) EXCEEDS — or is anticipated (token-estimate) to exceed — the largest configured context window even at one-criterion-per-call. In that case it FAILS with 'ticket too big to review in full; reduce/decompose it' (the extreme of P4 oversize / G5 decomposition). Deterministic (a size/estimate check, no LLM); the orchestrator emits it during the size-handling ladder.
## Acceptance Criteria (added)

- [ ] P1–P8 run as the deterministic `exec=DET` tier the orchestrator dispatches via its code executor (no LLM) — an explicit, first-class execution path, not merely a named tier.

baseline.description:
The AWS review-bot holds a persistent tickets clone that a redeploy does not refresh, and it writes on every Gerrit vote. Give it diverged-detection, and fix the deploy path so the change actually reaches the box. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Its clone lives on an EBS-backed external volume (`docker-compose.yml:127`, `external: true`) cloned once behind `if [ ! -d .git ]` (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:117`, itself nested inside `if [ -n "${REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT:-}" ]` at `:112`), so a redeploy does **not** converge it. It writes a `code_review` ticket and auto-pushes on **every** vote (`voter.py:260-343`, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`) — event-driven, not scheduled, so pausing AWS *schedules* does not stop it.

This is **new code, not a predicate fix**: `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` currently does only `git config user.email/user.name` (`:52-53`) then `run_ensures` (`:59`) — no fetch, no reset, no ancestry test. Note its invocation at `Dockerfile.reviewbot:125` sits OUTSIDE the PAT block, so new logic there runs even with the PAT unset.

**Chicken-and-egg:** `autodeploy.sh:186`'s rsync — which is what refreshes the box's copy of these scripts — runs only when `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS` changed (`:55` = `src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot pyproject.toml infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`). A commit touching only these two scripts would never reach the box. So this must land in the **same change** as an `src/rebar/` edit (A6-0a qualifies).

## Approach
1. Add diverged-detection to `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`: if `HEAD` is not an ancestor of
   `origin/tickets` and not strictly ahead, `fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets`. Safe because the
   bot never holds unpushed work (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`).
2. Add `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` to `autodeploy.sh:55`'s `BOT_PATHS`, so future
   edits to it deploy at all.

Vote safety is already guaranteed and must not regress: `voter.py:698` records the vote **before** `emit_code_review_artifact` (`:735`), and that call is wrapped in `except Exception` -> `_artifact_emit_error` + `logger.warning` + `return None` (`:368-371`) — documented as "the vote is already cast, so this never fails the review". A store failure cannot wedge the `LLM-Review` gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a clone diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared tip), the script re-converges it to
      `origin/tickets` and leaves no local commits. Tier: **shell integration** against two real
      temporary repos.
- [ ] Given an up-to-date or merely-behind clone, the script makes **no** destructive change
      (negative control). Tier: **shell integration**.
- [ ] With `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` unset, the new logic still executes (it sits outside the PAT
      block). Tier: **shell integration** with the env var unset.
- [ ] `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` appears in `autodeploy.sh`'s `BOT_PATHS`. Verify:
      grep assertion in a test.
- [ ] A rebar store write failure inside the bot still leaves the vote cast (regression guard). Tier:
      **unit** on `emit_code_review_artifact` with an injected store failure.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0a (and must ship in the same change as an `src/rebar/` edit).

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`review_plan_start(ticket)` returns a `job_id`; callers poll `gate_status(job_id)` and then read retained `REVIEW_RESULT` findings. The bug is that a terminal plan-review poll (`status:"passed"`, `verdict:"BLOCK"`) did not prove that the readable `REVIEW_RESULT` belonged to that same run. A caller reading "latest findings" could silently consume a prior run's findings.

Observed 2026-09-01 on ticket `549b-9cc5-940e-46c3`: job `1788326596882647223-94573cf0d90d404e87c74855306c16f2` reported terminal BLOCK while the newest readable sidecar was prior-run file `1788325963941841589-...-REVIEW_RESULT.json`; the current sidecar `1788327281362056852-...-REVIEW_RESULT.json` appeared later.

## Root cause / actual layer

`review_plan()` already calls `sidecar.emit()` before `_spawn_gate_daemon()` records the terminal `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>` entry. The defect is not a simple in-process order inversion; it is missing per-run sidecar identity:

- `sidecar.emit()` was best-effort and returned only a bool.
- `_spawn_gate_daemon()` discarded sidecar outcome/identity when writing the terminal run index.
- `gate_run_status()` reported terminal status plus attestation currency only. For BLOCK, the attestation is unsigned by definition, so `durable` cannot prove findings readiness.
- `sidecar.latest_review_result(ticket)` is newest-by-ticket, not job-scoped.

Thus a terminal run without an exact sidecar receipt cannot distinguish current findings from stale latest findings, an unreadable tracker view, a legacy index, or permanent sidecar failure.

## Fix plan

Add an exact receipt while preserving existing contracts.

1. `_commands._seam.append_event()` returns the event-envelope timestamp as an additive receipt; existing callers may ignore it.
2. `plan_review.sidecar.emit()` still returns bool, and also stamps `verdict["sidecar_reviewed_at"]` with the timestamp returned by `append_event()`.
3. `plan_review.__init__` keeps `verdict["sidecar_emitted"]` boolean semantics unchanged while carrying that stamped receipt on the verdict.
4. Reuse short-circuits that return current stored findings (`reuse.idempotent_reuse` and `reuse.verdict_reuse`) set `sidecar_reviewed_at` from the reused sidecar's filename timestamp while keeping `sidecar_emitted=false` because they did not write a new sidecar. Drift refresh/cancellation remain no-new-findings paths.
5. `_mcp_llm._spawn_gate_daemon()` copies `sidecar_emitted` and any exact `sidecar_reviewed_at` from the completed review result into the terminal run index.
6. `gate_status(job_id)` adds `findings` for plan-review jobs: `sidecar_type`, `readable`, `reason`, `reviewed_at`, `latest_reviewed_at`, and legacy diagnostic `job_started_at`.
7. `findings.readable=true` only when a file with the exact `sidecar_reviewed_at` prefix exists and parses as a supported `plan_review_result_v1/v2` payload. It never infers freshness from newest timestamp or job start time.

Disposition: no `findings` block is attached when the job is `unknown` because there is no indexed ticket/gate type. For indexed plan-review jobs, `findings.sidecar_type` is always `REVIEW_RESULT`. `current-review-result-sidecar` is readable. `sidecar-not-emitted` is a new record with `sidecar_emitted=false` and no receipt; `review-result-generation-unknown` is a legacy terminal record with no receipt fields; `run-failed` is a terminal gate failure with no review result; `run-stale-running` is a crashed-leader unavailable state. `review-result-sidecar-missing` covers absent, unreadable, corrupt, or unsupported exact-prefix files; callers may keep polling only under their normal bounded wait policy and must not read latest findings while false. `run-running` and `run-attaching` mean keep polling.

## Scope / file impact

- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`: additive timestamp return from `append_event()`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`: stamp `sidecar_reviewed_at` while preserving bool return; reuse reads exact payload timestamps from existing `all_review_results()`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`: verified call site; bool `sidecar_emitted` remains unchanged.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py`: carry reused current sidecar receipts on no-new-sidecar paths.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`: store the exact completed-review receipt in the terminal async run index.
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py`: compute the plan-review `findings` readability block.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`, `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json`: document/model additive fields.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py` and `tests/interfaces/store/test_sidecar_reader.py`: regression and receipt tests.
- `AGENTS.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/mcp-reference.md`: document waiting for `findings.readable` before reading findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Seed an old `REVIEW_RESULT`, record a terminal newer run with expected `sidecar_reviewed_at`, omit that sidecar, and assert `gate_status` is terminal with `findings.readable=false`, `reason="review-result-sidecar-missing"`.
- [x] Write the expected current sidecar and assert the same job reports `findings.readable=true` with `reason="current-review-result-sidecar"`.
- [x] Drive two successive runs and assert poll-then-read returns no findings for the newer job until that job's exact sidecar is readable.
- [x] Assert terminal `sidecar_emitted=false` without a receipt reports `findings.readable=false` and `reason="sidecar-not-emitted"`.
- [x] Assert terminal `sidecar_emitted=false` with a reused `sidecar_reviewed_at` reports `findings.readable=true` for that exact sidecar.
- [x] Assert exact-prefix corrupt or unsupported sidecar files report `findings.readable=false` with `reason="review-result-sidecar-missing"`.
- [x] Assert `findings.latest_reviewed_at` reflects the newest-by-ticket sidecar timestamp for diagnostics only and is not used to infer readability.
- [x] Assert an unknown job has no `findings` block.
- [x] Assert `findings.sidecar_type` is `REVIEW_RESULT`.
- [x] Assert the daemon records the exact receipt returned by `review_plan()` even when a newer same-ticket sidecar is already readable.
- [x] Assert legacy terminal records without a receipt report `findings.readable=false`, `reason="review-result-generation-unknown"`, with `job_started_at` diagnostic only.
- [x] Assert non-terminal plan-review runs report `findings.readable=false`, `reason="run-<status>"`, and `reviewed_at=null`.
- [x] Assert terminal failed plan-review runs without a review result report `findings.readable=false` and `reason="run-failed"`.
- [x] [non-codebase] Validate with targeted pytest, MCP schema coverage, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test`.
  provenance: environment=debug-gate-status-sidecar worktree at merged Gerrit SHA 8a38aa7656d5405813a72ff3d61d4fb6f1759cfd plus GitHub Actions run 33683396633; principal=RebarBotNava/Copilot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Local pytest/lint/typecheck/schema/full-suite commands and Gerrit CI ran against the production code review path.

## Non-goals

- Changing verdict computation or whether a BLOCK is a completed (`passed`) gate run.
- Making `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars required for the verdict; they remain best-effort observability.
- Changing `plan_review_status` or signed-attestation currency.
baseline.summary: gate_status reports a terminal verdict before its REVIEW_RESULT sidecar is readable

## Context / Problem
RP-04 S7.3.a (`insincere-illogical-antlion`, 6633-219e-988a-42f6) records `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` in its file impact because two legacy ambient config reads live there. RP-02 S2 (`brainy-cooked-hog`) MOVES both of them into the new `binding_lifecycle.py` owner, because they are lifecycle-policy config:

- `_env_int` — the defensive `os.environ.get` int parser (registry rationale cites `binding_store.py` L110; the line has already shifted once, to L109, from the RP-02 S1 T2 delegation)
- the `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` read that feeds the absence/retirement grace (registry rationale cites L538)

After the S2 move, S7.3.a's recorded target file no longer contains the reads it is meant to cut to the operation-snapshot seam.

## Why this needs its own ticket
The RP-02 <-> RP-04 coupling is deliberately recorded as a soft `relates_to` rather than a `depends_on`, so nothing enforces the retarget: RP-04 will silently miss the moved reads. This ticket is the durable artifact that prevents that.

`scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py` keys `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` on PATH + SYMBOL (rows are `(relpath, symbol, rationale)`; line numbers appear only inside the human-readable rationale text). There are TWO entries for `binding_store.py` — one for `os.environ.get` and one for `RECONCILE R_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` — so a path change makes both unregistered. RP-02 S2 re-registers them under `binding_lifecycle.py` in the same change so `make lint` stays green, but re-registering a moved legacy read is NOT resolving it: the read stays ambient, with byte-identical sourcing, defensive parse, default 3 and clamp minimum 1. Cutting it to the configuration seam remains RP-04 S7.3.a's slice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RP-04 S7.3.a's file impact names `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_lifecycle.py` instead of (or in addition to) `binding_store.py` for these reads, and names the `_env_int` and `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` symbols explicitly so the target cannot be missed.
- [ ] Both `config_ownership_exceptions.py` legacy entries are confirmed to sit on the post-RP-02 path, with no stale `binding_store.py` row left implying a read that is no longer there.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` passes before and after the retarget.
- [ ] The retarget does not itself change sourcing behavior — it is bookkeeping, so the seam cut stays RP-04's work.
baseline.summary: Retarget RP-04 S7.3.a config reads to binding_lifecycle.py after RP-02 S2

baseline.description:
## Summary

`rebar init` (auto-init / `rebar init --silent`) created a **fresh, empty** local tracker on a new `tickets` branch even though an authoritative `tickets` branch with real ticket history already existed on the configured sync remote (`origin`). The local tracker (`.tickets-tracker`) diverged from `origin/tickets`, so every read command (`rebar list`, `rebar show`, `search`, …) returns an EMPTY store, hiding all existing tickets. Any writes made now land on the divergent local branch and cannot be fast-forward-pushed back to `origin/tickets`.

Root contributing factor: fetching the remote `tickets` branch times out (>100s) through the agent git proxy, so init silently fell back to bootstrapping a fresh store instead of failing loudly or retrying.

## Impact

- `rebar list --status=open --type=bug` (and all other reads) return `[]` — existing
  work is invisible.
- New ticket events are written to a divergent local `tickets` history that will not
  fast-forward onto `origin/tickets`, risking lost or conflicting events.
- Silent data-hiding: no error is surfaced to the operator; the store simply looks empty.

## Environment

- Remote execution environment (Claude Code on the web), ephemeral container.
- Primary working directory: `/home/user/rebar`
- Platform: Linux 6.18.5
- Checked-out code branch: `claude/open-bugs-list-m4iu76`
- rebar version: `nava-rebar 0.10.1`
- `origin` remote: `http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41729/git/navapbc/rebar`
- Outbound git/HTTPS goes through the pre-configured agent proxy.
- No `.venv` was present at session start; `rebar` was not on `PATH`. Bootstrapped with
  `python3 -m venv .venv && make install`.
- Config (relevant): `sync.remote = origin`, `sync.pull = on`, `sync.push = always`.

## Reproduction — exact commands and observed output

1. rebar not installed / not on PATH:

   ```
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   /bin/bash: line 1: rebar: command not found
   $ python3 -m rebar list ...
   /usr/local/bin/python3: No module named rebar
   $ ls .venv
   ls: cannot access '.venv': No such file or directory
   ```

2. Bootstrap env:

   ```
   $ python3 -m venv .venv && make install
   Successfully installed ... nava-rebar-0.10.1 ...
   ```

3. Store reports not initialized, then init produced an EMPTY store:

   ```
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   Error: ticket system not initialized. Run 'rebar init' first (auto-init requires an interactive terminal).
   $ rebar init --silent
   (no output)
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   []
   $ rebar list                       # all statuses
   []
   ```

4. But a real `tickets` branch exists on `origin`, and it is actively moving (other
   agents writing to it) — two `ls-remote` reads minutes apart returned different tips:

   ```
   $ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/tickets'
   aa498170daa39767eab3282f505700e30bbed1ea  refs/heads/tickets   # first check
   ...
   $ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/tickets'
   4b51478a14c150a1032a8b2988d1524bfda1da54  refs/heads/tickets   # minutes later
   ```

5. The local tracker worktree is a FRESH divergent branch (bootstrap commits only, none
   of the remote history):

   ```
   $ git worktree list
   /home/user/rebar               ... claude/open-bugs-list-m4iu76
   /home/user/rebar/.tickets-tracker ... tickets

   $ git -C .tickets-tracker log --oneline -n 6
   37e8b02 chore: add .store-compat.json store-compatibility record (story 21dd)
   ed99e08 chore: add .gitignore for env-id, state-cache, scratch, and reducer cache
   936ec76 chore: add .gitattributes merge=ours for shared mutable root files (epic 97e7)
   a7ad28d chore: add no-op .pre-commit-config.yaml (bug 27d8-b230)
   94e48da chore: initialize ticket tracker
   $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse tickets
   37e8b026cf61e04b651f29b849294f6d549c8210
   ```

   Local tip `37e8b02` shares no history with remote tip `4b51478a` → divergent.

6. Fetching the remote `tickets` branch to reconverge TIMES OUT (reproduced multiple
   times, both from the main checkout and from inside `.tickets-tracker`):

   ```
   $ git -C .tickets-tracker fetch origin tickets      # 100s timeout
   Terminated   (exit 143)
   $ git fetch origin tickets                          # 120s tool timeout
   Command timed out after 2m 0s
   ```

   `rebar fsck` reports the (empty) local store as healthy, so nothing flags the problem:

   ```
   $ rebar fsck
   ensures: 6/6 applied
   authorship: 0 signed, 0 unsigned event(s)
   fsck complete: no issues found
   ```

## Confirmed divergence and fetch-latency (observed this session)

A full (unbounded-timeout) background fetch of `origin/tickets` eventually SUCCEEDED, which let me quantify both the divergence and the latency that caused the fallback:

- The remote `tickets` branch is large and event-sourced — **49,301 commits**:

  ```
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-list --count origin/tickets
  49301
  ```

- The local auto-initialized tracker and `origin/tickets` share **NO common ancestor**
  (definitively a fresh, divergent store — not a fast-forwardable lag):

  ```
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker merge-base tickets origin/tickets
  (no output; exit 1) -> NO COMMON ANCESTOR (divergent)
  $ git rev-parse origin/tickets      # authoritative
  80ec6ba00f4ce4daef8dada62c8056e003e8ef92
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse tickets   # local fresh-init
  dcb0b1ac7ff39999016a7aa73eeef9644b1e0247
  ```

- The branch is **actively written by other agents** — its tip moved four times across
  this single session: `aa498170…` → `4b51478a…` → `80ec6ba…`, etc.

- **Fetch latency is the trigger:** `git fetch origin tickets` was killed at 100s and at
  the 120s tool limit, but the same fetch run WITHOUT a kill-timeout (in the background)
  completed successfully in several minutes. So the branch is reachable; init simply gave
  up (or its bounded fetch timed out) and fell back to a fresh empty store rather than
  waiting/retrying. A bounded init fetch against a 49k-commit branch over the proxy is not
  enough headroom.

## Expected behavior

`rebar init` MUST NOT silently bootstrap a fresh empty store when the configured sync remote already has a `tickets` branch. It should either:

- fetch/adopt `origin/tickets` as the local tracker's base (the store is non-empty), or
- fail loudly (non-zero exit, clear message) when it cannot reach/fetch the existing
  remote `tickets` branch, instead of falling back to a divergent empty store.

Additionally, the remote-`tickets` fetch through the agent proxy should be made resilient (retry/backoff, longer timeout) rather than silently abandoned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar init` / auto-init detects an existing `tickets` branch on `sync.remote`
      before creating a new one, and bases the local tracker on it (reads return the
      existing tickets, not `[]`).
- [ ] When the existing remote `tickets` branch cannot be fetched, init fails loudly
      (clear error + non-zero exit) instead of silently bootstrapping a divergent empty
      store.
- [ ] A health check (`fsck`/`validate`) detects and reports a local `tickets` tracker
      that has diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared history / cannot fast-forward),
      rather than reporting "no issues found".
- [ ] Regression coverage: a test simulates a reachable, non-empty remote `tickets`
      branch and asserts init does not produce an empty divergent store.

## Notes

- Filed per operator request while investigating "show me a list of open bugs" returning
  an empty list.
- Because the local store is currently divergent and the remote fetch times out, this
  ticket may itself be written to the divergent local `tickets` history and may not sync
  to `origin/tickets` until the underlying fetch/reconverge issue is resolved.
baseline.summary: rebar init bootstrapped a fresh empty tracker while origin/tickets already existed (divergent store, reads return [])

baseline.description:
## Context
Operator-approved (2026-08-12): make ticket-directory creation atomic so interrupted-write debris cannot occur. Evidence: fsck found 8 empty stray ticket dirs (MISSING_CREATE + FOREIGN_STORE_PATH), all the `makedirs`-then-die signature — the dir existed before its CREATE event file did, and an interruption (host sleep, kill, timeout) in that window strands a plausible-looking empty ticket dir in the tracker worktree. Swept manually under illsuited-erect-ibis (7c6e-4b8a-59c5-46db); bug 043f ("tolerate, never tidy") rejects automatic cleanup of STORE DATA, so prevention at the writer is the self-healing fix.

## Mechanism (confirmed against origin/main abf3817187)
`_store/event_append.py::_prepare_event` — shared by the single-event `stage_and_commit` and by `batch_stage_and_commit`, so BOTH inherit this window — runs `os.makedirs(ticket_dir, exist_ok=True)` at line 171, OUTSIDE the write lock; the first event file only lands at the `os.replace` in `stage_and_commit` (line 425), after the temp write, `write_lock` acquisition and the rebase guard. Death in that window leaves an empty ticket dir, which fsck flags TWICE: `fsck.py::_scan` Check 2 emits MISSING_CREATE (reduce yields None) and `fsck.py::foreign_store_path_list` emits FOREIGN_STORE_PATH (no event file). Both scanners already skip dot-prefixed top-level entries — the convention this fix relies on.

## Design
New leaf module `src/rebar/_store/staging.py` owning the convention and the atomic publish:
- Convention: staging dirs are `<tracker>/.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>`. The leading dot is the EXISTING exclusion rule already honoured by `fsck._ticket_dirs`, `fsck.foreign_store_path_list`, fsck Check 1 and `relation_snapshot`, so temp paths are invisible to both checks with no scanner change. Documented in the module docstring and docs/concurrency.md.
- `stage_event(...)` -> `StagedEvent`: when the ticket dir does NOT exist, mkdir the staging dir and write the canonical event bytes INSIDE it; when it already exists, keep today's `.tmp-event-*` file staging unchanged.
- BOTH consumers of `_prepare_event` are converted, not just the single-event one. `_prepare_event` is called at `event_append.py:415` (`stage_and_commit`) AND at `:519` (`batch_stage_and_commit`, driven by `_io/import_ndjson.py` and the reconciler flush in `_commands/_seam.py`), so the fix is made in the shared function and both call sites promote through `StagedEvent` — the batch loop replaces its per-event `os.replace` with `promote()` inside the SINGLE existing batch lock, and `_rollback_batch` discards staged trees and rmdirs any ticket dir that batch itself created. The batch path carries the identical makedirs-then-die signature today (its docstring already concedes 'a crash mid-batch ... leaves at most orphaned worktree files'), and fixing the shared function is what closes it for both.
- `StagedEvent.promote()` runs UNDER the existing write lock (lock discipline unchanged): re-checks the final path and either `os.rename(staging_dir, ticket_dir)` — one atomic step publishing dir+CREATE together — or, if a concurrent create won the race, `os.replace(staging_file, final_path)` + rmdir. Staying under the lock keeps an event file invisible until `under_lock_check` (optimistic concurrency) has passed.
- Failure/rollback paths remove the staging tree; a transaction that created the ticket dir then rolled back also rmdirs the now-empty dir it just created, under the lock, in the same transaction.
- `sweep_stale_staging(tracker)`: bounded, best-effort, at ticket-create writer start. Removes ONLY `.tmp-newticket-*` dirs whose owner is provably gone, reusing `lock_owner`'s v2 stamp (host + pid-namespace + start time), which already defeats pid recycling; an absent or unprobeable stamp falls back to a conservative age guard. Bounded scan/removal caps.

043f boundary: the sweep touches ONLY the writer's own staging area (`.tmp-newticket-*`), never a ticket directory and never store data. It does not reintroduce writer-side cleanup of event-less ticket dirs, which stays rejected; the code comment says so.

## AC4 audit — other dir-then-first-file sites in the store write path
Convert (same signature, same tracker, fsck-visible): `_store/event_append.py::batch_stage_and_commit` (shares `_prepare_event`, so it is covered by the same change rather than separately — called from `_io/import_ndjson.py` and the `_commands/_seam.py` reconciler flush); `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py::_write_event_file` (mkdir precedes `_seam.finalize_event`, which can raise CommandError on the secret screen, and lock acquisition, which can time out) and `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` BRIDGE_ALERT emission (mkdir then first alert file). Exempt with reasons: `_store/lock.py::_acquire_mkdir` (dot-prefixed `.ticket-write.lock.d`, invisible to fsck; its mkdir->stamp gap already has a staleness adjudicator); `_store/hlc.py` and `_commands/fsck_repair.py` marker dirs (under `.rebar/` or the resolved git dir, outside the committed worktree); `session_log.py`, `identity.py`, `trusted_env_cmd.py` pointer/config writers (not in the tracker).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1 — Ticket creation stages dir+CREATE atomically: killing the writer at any point between staging start and rename leaves NO path that fsck reports as MISSING_CREATE/FOREIGN_STORE_PATH (temp paths are excluded from both checks by naming convention, documented).
- [x] AC2 — A RED test simulates the interruption (kill/exception injected between mkdir and event write in the OLD code shape) proving the debris signature, and the fix turns it green; a rename-crash test proves the temp path is invisible to fsck and cleaned on the next writer's start (bounded, best-effort temp sweep of stale temp paths owned by dead pids — this does not violate 043f since temp paths are the writer's own staging area, not store data).
- [x] AC3 — Concurrency: two concurrent creates of different tickets don't collide on temp paths (pid/uuid-suffixed staging names); the existing write-lock discipline is unchanged.
- [x] AC4 [operator-attested] — Any other same-signature dir-then-file sites in the store write path are converted or explicitly recorded as exempt with reasons.
- [x] AC5 [operator-attested] — make lint/typecheck pass; store suite green; no change to event formats or committed layout.

## Testing
New `tests/interfaces/store/` test module:
1. RED-shape reproduction: inject an exception where the OLD shape wrote the first event (staging fails after the dir would have been made) and assert `fsck.foreign_store_path_list` plus the MISSING_CREATE scan report the ticket id — the debris signature; the converted writer leaves zero findings under the same injection.
2. Crash-before-rename: fail `os.replace`/the lock; assert a `.tmp-newticket-*` path exists and that both `foreign_store_path_list` and the MISSING_CREATE scan return nothing for it (invisibility by convention).
3. Sweep: plant one staging dir stamped with a dead owner and one stamped live; run a create; assert the dead one is gone, the live one untouched, and no ticket directory touched.
4. Concurrency (AC3): two creates of different tickets in flight produce distinct staging names and both land.
5. AC4 converted sites have their own coverage: a test drives `inbound_translate._write_event_file` with `_seam.finalize_event` patched to raise (the secret-screen refusal path) and asserts no fsck-visible directory is left behind; a test drives the `dispatch_one` BRIDGE_ALERT emission with the alert write failing and asserts the same. A batch test drives `batch_stage_and_commit` with a mid-batch failure across two NEW ticket ids and asserts zero MISSING_CREATE/FOREIGN_STORE_PATH findings afterwards.
6. Byte parity unchanged: existing `test_canonical_event_bytes.py` / `test_store.py` residue assertions stay green.
Commands: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `pytest tests/interfaces/store`.
baseline.summary: Atomic ticket-dir creation: eliminate interrupted-write debris
