baseline.description:
# Continuous auto-deploy: the running Gerrit environment reflects `main` without manual deploy or restart

## Why
Landing a change on `main` does NOT update the running environment. The **review-bot container's code**, the site `replication.config`, and the g2p config all require a MANUAL deploy (SSM / setup-*.sh) and sometimes a restart, causing drift + toil: epic 88ab S2's merge-review code landed on `main` but the running `compose-review-bot-1` still runs the pre-S2 image; the S3 `replication.config` fix had to be hand-applied via SSM. The deployed environment must AUTO-REFLECT `main` shortly after a change lands — WITHOUT ever destabilising the LIVE gate that contributors depend on to review + submit.

## What
### Trigger — RESOLVED: a systemd timer on the Gerrit host (option a; NOT GitHub Actions→SSM)
`rebar-autodeploy.timer` (every 2 min) runs `rebar-autodeploy.service` (oneshot). RATIONALE for the on-box timer over a GitHub-Actions `deploy.yml`→SSM: (1) NO new trust surface — the box already has an instance role and reads the PUBLIC mirror READ-ONLY (no GitHub→AWS OIDC/`ssm:SendCommand` grant, which would make the GH runner a lateral-movement path into the box); (2) self-contained + simplest to back out; (3) ~2-min poll latency is fine for a deploy loop.

### Deploy script (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, idempotent, flock-guarded)
- **flock** `/var/lib/rebar/deploy.lock` (`-n`) — overlapping fires skip; a long deploy is never re-entered.
- **deployed-sha** `/var/lib/rebar/deployed-sha`: on FIRST run (absent) INITIALIZE to the box's
  current HEAD WITHOUT deploying (adopt current state); write atomically (`mv` tmp) ONLY after success.
- **What to deploy (safety):** fetch `origin/main` from the mirror. The mirror's `main` only advances
  via Gerrit SUBMIT (post two-vote gate) → its tip is Verified BY CONSTRUCTION; deploy ONLY that tip,
  never an arbitrary ref. No-op when `origin/main == deployed-sha`.
- **Change detection (path-set per component):** `git diff --name-only deployed-sha..origin/main` ∩ a
  component manifest: review-bot (`src/rebar/**`, `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, `pyproject.toml`,
  `docker-compose.yml`), replication (`replication.config`), g2p (`gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`,
  `materialize-g2p-config.sh`).
- **Per-component apply (only if changed):** review-bot → `docker tag` current image `:prev`, then
  `docker compose up -d --build review-bot`; replication → re-materialise + autoReload (no restart);
  g2p → `materialize-g2p-config.sh`.
- **SCOPE BOUNDARY (v1):** covers review-bot container + replication.config + g2p config. `refs/meta/config`
  (project.config) is OUT of v1 (rare, security-sensitive, needs an operator-only Gerrit admin key):
  a change is DETECTED + signalled (metric + log), never auto-applied. Retry transient git/docker
  failures 3× w/ backoff; persistent failure → fail-safe (leave prior state + marker).

### Stability — live-pipeline safety (the load-bearing section)
The gate is FAIL-CLOSED: no LLM-Review vote ⇒ no submit. So a bad or careless deploy can FREEZE the whole pipeline. Hardening:
1. **Blast radius is bounded by construction.** Auto-deploy NEVER touches the `gerrit` container and
   NEVER modifies `refs/meta/config` (the labels/submit-rules/ACLs). `docker compose` is invoked with
   the EXPLICIT `review-bot` service only (never a bare `up` that could recreate `gerrit`); a guard
   asserts the `gerrit` container id is unchanged across the deploy. Gate INTEGRITY is thus not
   alterable by this mechanism — only the bot's code + replication/g2p config move.
2. **No Gerrit restart, ever.** Config changes use `autoReload` (replication) / materialise (g2p); only
   the review-bot CONTAINER restarts, and only when its code changed. Gerrit availability is untouched.
3. **In-flight reviews are delayed, not lost.** A bot restart drops in-flight webhook processing, but
   the EXISTING reconciler-backfill (events-log cursor) re-reviews any change missed during the
   restart window — so a contributor's vote is at most DELAYED by one restart, never dropped. The
   post-deploy health check confirms the reconciler loop is live.
4. **A broken bot deploy self-heals (never freezes the gate).** After `up -d --build`, an END-TO-END
   health check (30s timeout) verifies the bot is actually able to review (receiver `/health` + a
   probe that the review path is functional), NOT merely that the process is up. On failure →
   IMMEDIATE rollback to the `:prev` image + `up -d` + error marker; deployed-sha is NOT advanced. Max
   gate-frozen window = the health-check timeout, then service is restored to the known-good image.
5. **Circuit-breaker (no thrash on the live pipeline).** A per-target-SHA consecutive-failure counter:
   after 2 failed deploy attempts of the SAME `origin/main` tip, auto-deploy DISABLES itself
   (stop-file) + pages — it does NOT re-attempt the bad SHA every 2 min. An operator clears the
   stop-file after fixing forward. (Because the gate is fail-closed, thrashing restarts would be worse
   than pausing on a known-good image.)
6. **Config validated BEFORE it touches the running Gerrit.** replication.config / g2p config are
   parse-checked (`git config -f … --list`; g2p ini schema) BEFORE apply; a malformed config is
   SKIPPED (prior config retained) + alarmed — a bad config never breaks live replication/CI dispatch.
7. **Post-deploy pipeline-health gate.** deployed-sha advances only after a post-deploy check confirms
   the end-to-end gate still works (bot health OK; a canary confirms review + CI dispatch paths).

### Observability + back-out
Structured deploy log (from→to SHA + components) + `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (host-probe grep of an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, mirroring voter_errors) + a CloudWatch alarm w/ SNS action; the circuit-breaker stop-file is itself alarmed. Back-out: `systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer`; the manual path (compose-up.sh / setup-*.sh) is unchanged.

## Scope
The deploy orchestrator + systemd timer/service + stability guards + observability/back-out on the existing compose stack. Reuses the idempotent setup/materialise appliers. refs/meta/config auto-apply deferred (detect + signal). No change to gate semantics (S1/S2) or the feature-branch flow (88ab).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A change landing on `main` (post-gate + replicated) makes the running env reflect it with NO
      manual action, ≤ 5 min; live-measured latency recorded
- [ ] Idempotent + change-detected: a no-change run is a no-op; a relevant change re-applies ONLY the
      changed component(s) — verified for review-bot code, replication.config, and g2p separately
- [ ] review-bot rebuilt/restarted ONLY when its source-set changed (a docs-only `main` change does
      NOT rebuild it); after a code change the running bot reflects it end-to-end (a merge change gets
      the S2 merge-change tag from the auto-deployed bot)
- [ ] STABILITY — blast radius: the `gerrit` container is provably untouched across a deploy;
      `refs/meta/config` is never auto-modified; no Gerrit restart occurs (verified)
- [ ] STABILITY — self-heal: a deliberately-broken review-bot image triggers the health check to FAIL
      and rolls back to `:prev` (gate restored); deployed-sha not advanced (proven live)
- [ ] STABILITY — circuit-breaker: 2 consecutive failed deploys of a SHA DISABLE auto-deploy + alarm
      (no thrash); malformed replication/g2p config is rejected pre-apply (prior config retained)
- [ ] STABILITY — in-flight: a review dropped by the restart window is recovered by the reconciler
      backfill (delayed, not lost) — demonstrated
- [ ] Concurrency: overlapping fires serialized by flock; deployed-sha written atomically only on success
- [ ] project.config changes DETECTED + signalled (metric + log), not attempted (documented boundary)
- [ ] Deploy log + `deploy_errors` metric + alarm applied; back-out (disable the timer) tested; manual
      path still works
- [ ] Live-verified end-to-end on the running box (a real `main` change auto-deploys within the window)
baseline.summary: Continuous auto-deploy: running Gerrit environment reflects main without manual deploy or restart

baseline.description:
`bridge_fsck` reads `prev_snapshot.json` off disk as its offline Jira oracle and uses the **field values**, so narrowing prev to a key-set (A4-2) would silently degrade its drift classification. Fence it first. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why first
`bridge_fsck.py:306-308` loads the file as `jira_snapshot` and passes `fields=jira_snapshot[key]` into `ObservedJira.PRESENT` at `:344` and `:380`. With `{}` entries, membership still works but every field-based classification degrades. This is an **out-of-band consumer of the file itself**, not of `ctx.prev_snapshot`, so no test that exercises `reconcile_once` would catch it. It reads the **working tree**, so it is unaffected by clone filters.

## Approach
Make the field-dependence explicit: classify on membership where that is sufficient, and where a field value is genuinely required, report the classification as **indeterminate** rather than inferring from an empty dict. Do not silently treat absent fields as absent values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Against a **key-set** prev fixture (`{jira_key: {}}`), `bridge_fsck` drift classification is
      identical to its classification against the equivalent full-payload fixture for every case that
      does not require a field value, and reports **indeterminate** (never a false drift) for cases
      that do. Tier: **unit** with paired fixtures.
- [ ] Against a full-payload prev, behaviour is byte-identical to today (no regression for the
      pre-A4-2 world). Tier: **unit** golden comparison.
- [ ] `rebar bridge-fsck` exit code and JSON shape are unchanged for both fixtures. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py`, tests

Scope: S. No dependencies (independent of A1/A2/A3).
baseline.summary: A4-1: fence bridge_fsck's offline drift oracle before prev_snapshot is narrowed

baseline.description:
## What
Make union recovery (epic minor-haste-ogle WU-2/WU-3) unconditionally
conflict-free by removing the only mutable, non-disjoint shared paths from the
`tickets` branch. Today `.bridge_state/bindings.json` and the reconciler
lock/gate files are committed at the branch root and are rewritten each reconcile
pass, so two clones produce divergent edits to the same path -> merge conflict
(WU-3 mitigates with `merge=ours`; this ticket removes the conflict class
entirely). uuid-named ticket dirs are already disjoint and always merge cleanly;
once these root files are gitignored off the shared history, EVERY path on the
branch is append-only-disjoint and union merge can never wedge.

## Files
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (the committed `.gitignore` / scaffold on the tickets branch)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py` (writes lock/gate + bindings to the shared branch)
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (the existing `.bridge_state` stash/merge dance can be simplified once they leave the branch)

## Scope / risk
The reconciler currently coordinates cross-clone partly VIA these shared-branch
files; moving them off-branch changes that coordination and needs its own design
pass. This is why it is a follow-up, not part of the gc epic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.bridge_state/` and reconciler lock/gate files are no longer committed to the `tickets` branch (gitignored), with reconciler coordination preserved or redesigned
- [ ] union merge of two unrelated/diverged histories is conflict-free on all paths (regression test)
- [ ] WU-3's `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` becomes unnecessary (removed) or documented as defense-in-depth
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green
baseline.summary: Move .bridge_state/ + reconciler lock files off the shared tickets branch (conflict-free union)

# Prompt caching at the runner seam (system-prompt + tool caching, provider-safe)

## Why
Across the container fan-out the re-sent stable bytes (the WHOLE parent plan) live in the SYSTEM PROMPT
(`passes.py:173` renders `parent_plan` into `_resolve_system`); `instructions` already holds only the volatile
per-pairing content. So the correct, minimal lever is caching the SYSTEM PROMPT (+ tool definitions on agentic
calls) — NOT a user-message `CachePoint`. Fidelity-neutral; biggest single token win. (Opus-review BLOCKER 1/2.)

## What
- SPIKE FIRST: confirm what pydantic-ai 1.107.0 `anthropic_cache_instructions` caches for rebar's call shape
  `Agent(system_prompt=...)` + `run_sync(instructions=...)` — does it apply `cache_control` to the `system_prompt=`
  kwarg, or only to `instructions=`? This decides the implementation. If it caches `system_prompt` → use it
  directly; if only `instructions=` → route the stable plan through `instructions=` (or fall back to a
  user-message `CachePoint`, deferred unless the spike requires it).
- Enable `anthropic_cache_instructions=True` + `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True` via `AnthropicModelSettings`,
  GATED to anthropic providers (`resolved.startswith("anthropic")`) — these keys error on openai/gemini. NO
  RunRequest prefix/suffix split and NO user-message content-list change (so the structured-output retry path
  `runner.py:347-363` is untouched — this dissolves BLOCKER 2).
- Capture `result.usage()` (currently discarded at `runner.py:226/343/356`) and surface cache_read/write input
  tokens per run (pin the pydantic-ai 1.107.0 RunUsage field names); thread into observability/coverage.
- Note: `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions` is a no-op on single_turn calls (tools=[]); only agentic calls benefit.

## Scope
- In: the spike; AnthropicModelSettings cache flags + anthropic gating in runner.py; `result.usage()` capture +
  cache-token observability; byte-stability of the container system prompt across pairings.
- Out: engine RunnerAgentStep caching (S2); parallelization/warm-up (S3); merge (S4); bin-pack (S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SPIKE resolved + recorded; the implementation follows it (system-prompt caching if supported, else the
      documented fallback).
- [ ] `anthropic_cache_instructions` + `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions` are enabled and GATED to anthropic
      providers; on openai/gemini the call succeeds unchanged (no cache_* sent) — verified via the per-provider
      message mapper (offline) or an explicit live/integration test.
- [ ] On a repeat anthropic container call (same parent plan), `usage.cache_read_input_tokens > 0`.
- [ ] The container system prompt is byte-stable across pairings — a stability test asserts `_resolve_system`
      output is identical for different children of the same parent.
- [ ] `result.usage()` cache_read/write input tokens are captured and surfaced per run (observability).
- [ ] No behavior/finding change (fidelity-neutral); ≤3 cache breakpoints; `make lint` + tests pass.
baseline.summary: Prompt caching at the shared runner seam (CachePoint + anthropic_cache_*, provider-safe)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Teams running several tracker projects against one codebase (or several repos against one ticket store) cannot use the bridge: it is hard-wired to exactly one project at three points — `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`_config_schema.py`), the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one (`fetcher.jqls_for`), and the applier aborts a pass when any outbound mutation targets a key outside that project (`applier.CrossProjectTargetError`). The only escape is the destructive one-way `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`. Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff` and taken as a dependency, not duplicated here.

(Full original description with line-anchored citations preserved verbatim as a ticket comment, 2026-08-13.)

## Approach

Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects. Each ticket records the project it syncs into and the repos it belongs to.

The STORE owns the project set — `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the tickets branch beside `bindings.json`/`prev_snapshot.json`. Reason (mechanical): `prev_snapshot.json` is last-known-remote state; if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would diff the other's projects as remote deletions. A store-owned project set removes that failure mode by construction and leaves no per-repo list to disagree.

Built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`) and the backend-neutral port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)`, `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`. `Backend.project` ("the backend's effective write/create project scope") is the per-repo default for rebar-created tickets; no new config key; generalizes beyond Jira.

Migration writes NO events. The ticket project field is tri-state — absent=legacy, explicit-empty= never sync, explicit key=sync there — mirroring `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths (`docs/ticket-model.md`). Absent resolves against the legacy default recorded in the mapping, seeded by an idempotent check-then-act ensure unit (`docs/migrations.md`, the sanctioned seam; the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built). A per-ticket EDIT migration was rejected: four-figure event writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot entry runs the ensure sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended — an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + the ensure seed. Delivers migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`. Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces; promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out + snapshot union; per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project. Delivers two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create; guard relaxed from single project to set membership. Delivers explicit-project + guard criteria.
- **Store-compat capability stamp** — conditional `required_capabilities` entry + fail-closed read. Delivers final criterion.
- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: rehearse against two live Jira Cloud projects on an
  isolated tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`,
  hence the depends_on); dry-run-gated, all created issues removed. Fixtures cannot reach the
  cross-project contamination failure mode this validates.
- **Module-size relief** — several files this feature edits sit within ~30 lines of the 800 hard cap.
  Behaviour-preserving extractions along existing seams, each ordered ahead of the story needing room;
  they deliver no epic criterion (preconditions; their own criteria are unchanged suite + measured LOC).

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive at every layer. Absent project = legacy; a pre-feature store behaves as today, no operator action. A single-project store never receives the capability stamp, so older binaries keep working; only a genuinely multi-project store fails closed on them — the intended protection (an older binary would fetch its one project, see other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicates in the wrong project). Rollback is per-change on Gerrit; the mapping and capability entry are inert to older binaries apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to implicit-legacy with the idempotent ensure re-stamping on the next covered write.
baseline.summary: Many-to-many tracker projects: per-ticket bridge project + repo association over one shared store

## Problem
Discovered during an early draft of the sibling "rank aggregation by priority" ticket (beaming-snively-urial): `src/rebar/llm/spec_scan.py:13,137` imports `_severity_rank` from `aggregate.py` directly and sorts its own findings list by it (`findings.sort(key=_severity_rank, reverse=True)`). `spec_scan.py`'s findings come straight from the "spec-alignment" LLM reviewer's structured output via `finalize_findings` (`findings.py`) -- they never pass through `pass3_decide` and never get `priority`.

## OBSOLETED
This ticket's premise no longer holds, for two independent reasons, both confirmed against the ACTUAL, FINAL, landed state of the tickets named below (not an early draft):

1. Ticket `beaming-snively-urial` was itself corrected mid-implementation after research
   showed `aggregate.py::aggregate_findings`/`_severity_rank` is dead code (no caller in
   `src/rebar/` since ADR 0075). Its FINAL, closed scope explicitly excludes `aggregate.py`
   -- its acceptance criteria required (and its landed change satisfies)
   `git diff --stat src/rebar/llm/aggregate.py` being EMPTY. `_severity_rank`/`_SEVERITY_RANK`
   in `aggregate.py` are therefore completely untouched by this epic, in perpetuity as far as
   this epic's scope goes -- there is no migration for `spec_scan.py`'s import of them to be
   broken BY.
2. Separately, `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES`/`normalize_finding`/`Finding.severity`
   vocabulary (which `spec_scan.py`'s findings are normalized through, independent of
   `_severity_rank`) is ALSO staying intact per the epic's corrected architecture: it serves a
   completion-verification module cluster (`completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`,
   `epic_bug_screen.py`, `workflow/gate_ops.py`, `workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py`) that
   hardcodes `severity` as its ONLY signal with no priority/decision/impact alternative --
   deleting it would break that cluster with no fallback. Only the review-kernel
   (`pass3_decide`) stops stamping `severity` onto ITS OWN emitted findings; nothing else in
   `findings.py` changes.

The epic's own AC-3 ("every finding ... carries priority/decision") is being corrected separately (on the still-open epic ticket) to scope that claim to review-kernel/DET-tier findings specifically, not universally to every finding any reviewer anywhere produces -- `spec_scan.py`'s findings were never in that scope.

## Approach (superseded, retained for context only -- not implemented)
Would have mapped spec_scan's severity string to a numeric priority via a fixed ordinal mapping (any unrecognized/missing severity defaulting to 0.0) before sorting by priority instead of `_severity_rank`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Confirmed against the FINAL, closed state of `beaming-snively-urial` (zero diff to
  `aggregate.py`) and the epic's corrected architecture (findings.py's severity vocabulary
  stays intact) that `spec_scan.py` requires no change.

## Testing
Not applicable -- no code change made.
baseline.summary: Give spec_scan.py findings a priority before severity is removed

baseline.description:
## Problem

`rebar transition` **silently accepts and ignores unknown flags**. Demonstrated on a real ticket, no mutation:

```
$ rebar transition major-specified-bream open open --definitely-not-a-real-flag
no change: 50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92 already open
```

No error, no warning, exit 0. A misspelled or unsupported flag does nothing and says nothing.

## Why this is more than a nit: `--caused-by` is documented but not implemented on the CLI

`rebar transition --help` lists only `[--class=<value>] [--reason=<text>] [--force] [--force=<reason>] [--output json]`. There is no `--caused-by`. But it is instructed in at least three places:

- **`docs/user-guide.md:191-194`** — "explicitly with `--caused-by <id>` (which overrides the
  git-blame auto-derivation)", with a worked example:
  `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class=regression --caused-by=<culprit-id>`
- **`docs/clone-guidance.md:15,18`** — "Supply `--caused-by` when an explicit link is preferable."
- **The `/rebar-debug` skill** (lines ~498-512) makes it mandatory: *"`--caused-by` on the close is
  not optional once you have an origin, even if you already linked one"*, and *"Pass the flag on
  the close every time."*

The library side exists — `_lib_writes.py:339` threads `caused_by=`, and `transition_close.py:175` defines `_apply_caused_by` — so this is a **CLI surface gap**, not a missing capability.

**Combined with the silent-ignore behaviour, the effect is that every agent following the documented protocol believes it supplied a proven attribution while the system actually fell back to blame.** The instruction and the outcome diverge, silently, on the exact code path whose purpose is to make attribution trustworthy.

## Observed consequences, this session

Four bug closes today passed `--caused-by=<proven-origin>` per the skill. In each case:

- the flag was ignored;
- the `caused_by` edge that existed came from an earlier explicit `rebar link`;
- blame auto-derivation ran on close and attached a SECOND edge.

That mis-diagnosis was filed as `ruling-magnific-bats` (`10d0-c26c-bdbb-4b1f`) with the wrong premise — "`--caused-by` adds a duplicate edge" — when the actual mechanism is "blame auto-derivation adds an edge without checking whether one is already recorded". A correction is recorded on that ticket.

Worth noting in fairness: in the observed cases **blame landed on the same origin the agent had proven by hand**, so the duplicate was redundant rather than wrong. That is evidence about blame's accuracy, not an argument that the gap is harmless — an agent that believes it overrode the fallback has no way to discover that it did not.

## Two defects, and they should probably be fixed together

1. **Unknown flags are silently ignored.** A typo (`--forse`, `--clas=regression`) does nothing and
   reports success. Rejecting unknown flags is the standard contract and would have surfaced this
   in seconds.
2. **`--caused-by` is documented and instructed but absent from the CLI.** Either implement it
   (the library already supports it) or remove it from `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/clone-guidance.md`
   and the `/rebar-debug` skill. Implementing looks strictly better: the whole point of the
   attribution step is that a proven origin beats a guess.

Fixing (1) without (2) converts a silent failure into a loud one — an improvement, but it would break every documented invocation and every agent following the protocol. Fixing (2) without (1) leaves the next typo silent. Consider ordering deliberately.

## Reproduction

1. `rebar transition <any-open-ticket> open open --definitely-not-a-real-flag` → `no change`, exit 0.
2. `rebar transition --help` → no `--caused-by` in the usage line.
3. `grep -n 'caused-by' docs/user-guide.md` → documented, with an example command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unknown flag passed to `rebar transition` is REJECTED with a message naming the flag, not
      silently ignored — verified by a test asserting a non-zero exit and the flag name in the error.
- [ ] The unknown-flag rejection covers the other mutating verbs too, or a reasoned decision is
      recorded for why `transition` is special — verified per verb touched.
- [ ] `--caused-by=<id>` on a bug close either works end-to-end (the recorded edge is the supplied
      origin, and blame auto-derivation does NOT also run) or is removed from
      `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/clone-guidance.md` and the `/rebar-debug` skill. Decide and test
      whichever is chosen.
- [ ] If implemented: supplying `--caused-by` suppresses the blame fallback entirely, so exactly
      one edge results — verified by a test, and coordinated with `ruling-magnific-bats` (1973),
      which makes the `_apply_caused_by` write idempotent.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.

## Provenance

Found while verifying a subagent's report that `rebar transition` has no `--caused-by` flag. The agent was right and I had been asserting otherwise all session, including in instructions to other agents.
baseline.summary: rebar transition --help omits --caused-by: two help sources for one verb have drifted

baseline.description:
## Context

The `COMMITS` event and `attach_commits` reducer already exist (`rebar.attach_commits`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697`, re-exported from `src/rebar/__init__.py`), used by the code-review workflow. Missing: an author-facing repair surface for a botched `rebar-ticket:` trailer, plus a consumer. Approved design (b902-18af-14ed-4da1): expose retroactive commit linking on CLI + library + MCP, document it, then add a deterministic close-gate check that linked commits' diffs match the recorded `file_impact`. OUT of scope: linked commits as a completion-verifier diff basis (they may be incomplete; CV already prefetches from `file_impact`).

## Plan

1. **Shared DET module** `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py` (new, ~120 LOC): (a) `invalid_commit_shas(shas, repo_root)` via `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`; (b) the step-4 path matchers, including `glob_match` — the `**/`-aware semantics (`fnmatch(p,g) or (g.startswith("**/") and fnmatch(p,g[3:]))`) from `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:746`. Its ONLY true mirror is `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:242`; `src/rebar/grounding/oracle.py:316` uses PLAIN `fnmatch`, is NOT a copy, and is left untouched. The DET close path must not import `rebar.llm` (optional `[agents]` extra), so the helper is hoisted here and BOTH real copies (`prompts._glob_match`, `registry._glob_match`) become thin delegating wrappers — one implementation, no third copy.

2. **CLI verb** `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the existing seam. Registration follows the established seam: add to `_WRITES_FULL` in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`; add a variadic handler (N SHAs) to `_ARGV_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`; ship pinned help `src/rebar/_cli/help/attach-commits.txt` + the `overview.txt` line (golden-pinned; `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` requires it). Thin body in `src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py`.

3. **Validation in the SEAM, not the CLI**, so all three surfaces inherit it identically: `rebar.attach_commits` calls `commit_impact.invalid_commit_shas` before appending. **ALL-OR-NOTHING** — the batch is validated first; if any SHA fails, NO `COMMITS` event is recorded and the call raises naming every offender. Union-add unchanged. Library: `rebar.attach_commits` is already re-exported — confirm and document. MCP: register `attach_commits` in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` with an `AttachCommitsResultOut` outputSchema in `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`, per the existing write-tool pattern (`mcp_server.py` only assembles registrars).

4. **DET close check** in the existing completion precheck `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — the module that today raises "cannot confirm the work landed" (there is no `src/rebar/workflow/close_gate.py`). Discovery unions the two existing sources: (i) `state.commits` from COMMITS events; (ii) the precheck's referencing-commit scan (`_referencing_commit_exists`, `close_precheck.py:94` — commits reachable from HEAD carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject for the ticket or any transitive descendant). It returns only a bool, so it is refactored into a SHA-returning `_referencing_commits(...)` with `_referencing_commit_exists` kept as a thin wrapper — the documented monkeypatch target and its call sites keep working unchanged. For each commit, `git show --name-only` gives changed paths; a path neither covered by `file_impact` nor matched by this check's OWN exemption globs (`tests/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — owned here, not inherited) is a deterministic BLOCK naming the commit and paths. Matching (via step 1, not re-derived): normalized repo-relative POSIX paths; a `file_impact` entry matches on exact equality, or as a directory prefix when it ends with `/` or names an existing directory; exemptions use `**/`-aware `glob_match`. No substring matching. No LLM.

   **Git errors, asymmetric by source:** a source-(ii) commit is local by construction, so a `git show` failure on it FAILS CLOSED (block, naming the SHA). A source-(i) SHA may legitimately be absent locally (attached from another clone, or unfetched), so it is SKIPPED — blocking a foreign SHA would be a false positive on a repair surface built to record commits.

   **Scope symmetry.** Source-(ii) discovery credits commits for the ticket OR any transitive descendant (`accepted_ids`, `close_precheck.py:361-367`), but `field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker)` (`field_reads.py:36`) reads only THIS ticket's — reusing it as-is would false-BLOCK a parent declaring `file_impact` when children's commits touch child-owned paths. So the check compares against the UNION of `file_impact` over the SAME id set discovery uses, making both scopes match by construction.

   A ticket with no discovered commits keeps today's behavior (the existing error). The check is skipped when that union is empty (no ticket in the set declares `file_impact`).

5. **Remedy for a legitimate block:** the message names the offending paths and says to declare them via `rebar set-file-impact <ticket> …`, after which close proceeds; `--force="<reason>"` stays the break-glass.

6. **Docs.** `docs/cli-reference.md` is GENERATED (`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, CI drift gate, subcommand count in header) so it is regenerated, not hand-edited. Hand-edited: `docs/mcp-reference.md` and `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md`. Each names the verb, its use, and the step-5 remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>` records a COMMITS event that `rebar show` reflects. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -x`.
- [ ] An invalid SHA is rejected with an error naming it. Verify: same file, test asserting the offending SHA appears in the error text.
- [ ] A batch containing any invalid SHA records nothing (all-or-nothing). Verify: test asserting `state.commits` is byte-identical before/after a mixed valid/invalid batch.
- [ ] The MCP server exposes `attach_commits` with an outputSchema, routed through the same seam. Verify: the MCP tool-inventory test asserts `"attach_commits"` is in the registered tool names.
- [ ] A commit touching a path outside the declared `file_impact` blocks close, naming the offending path. Verify: unit test asserting the exact path string in the raised message.
- [ ] A commit whose paths are all declared does not block close. Verify: unit test asserting close proceeds.
- [ ] An exempt path does not block, including at the repo root (`README.md` under `**/*.md`). Verify: unit test over each exemption glob.
- [ ] The DET check imports no `rebar.llm` module. Verify: test asserting `[m for m in sys.modules if m.startswith("rebar.llm")] == []` after running it in a fresh interpreter.
- [ ] The `**/`-aware glob semantics have one implementation. Verify: test asserting `prompts._glob_match` and `registry._glob_match` both delegate to `commit_impact.glob_match`.
- [ ] An unreadable source-(ii) commit fails closed naming the SHA; an unresolvable source-(i) SHA is skipped without blocking. Verify: one unit test per direction.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` names the `attach_commits` tool. Verify: `grep -qE '\battach_commits\b' docs/mcp-reference.md` exits 0.
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the verb. Verify: `grep -qF 'rebar attach-commits' src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` exits 0.
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the `set-file-impact` remedy. Verify: `grep -qF 'rebar set-file-impact' src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` exits 0.
- [ ] A parent close does not block on a path declared only in a child's `file_impact`. Verify: unit test closing a parent whose child commit touches a child-declared path, asserting no block.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` is regenerated and its drift gate passes. Verify: `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` exits 0.
baseline.summary: attach-commits repair verb on all three surfaces + DET file-impact-vs-diff close check

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The one S3-specific failure that causes real data loss is **multiple bundles for one ref**. A live experiment this session reproduced it: when two `<sha>.bundle` objects exist for the `tickets` ref, `git ls-remote` returns the ref at two SHAs and a fresh clone **hard-fails** with `multiple updates for ref not allowed` — the store becomes unclonable. The push path also stalls: git-remote-s3's `cmd_push` **rejects while `len(bundles) > 1` before writing anything** (verified in the installed source, `remote.py` — it returns `multiple bundles exists on server` prior to any bundle create/put), and rebar's `src/rebar/_store/push.py:58` `_is_non_fast_forward` classifies that as retriable, but the subsequent fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, so retries never converge.

Upstream ships `git-s3 doctor` (`git_remote_s3.Doctor`), but it is unusable for an autonomous fleet, verified against the installed library (v0.3.2): `Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles` is **interactive-only** (blocking `input()` prompts at `manage.py:137,141`, which crash on EOF) and by default **side-branches the non-chosen head to a new orphan ref** (deletion is opt-in via `--delete-bundle`) — either way that head's events leave the ref's history and are **never merged**, so events unique to it are lost from the store. rebar's store is an append-only event log where each divergent head may carry distinct ticket events, so losing a head is unacceptable.

Prior art for healing a forked append-only log is unanimous (restic `check`/`repair`, git-annex union branch, jj op-log, Fossil/Dolt): **merge, never discard**, and put the storage-specific surface behind a thin seam so the merge logic is written once. rebar already embodies this for ordinary git remotes: `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` `_do_reconverge`/`_union_merge` reconciles a divergent `tickets`-branch head by, per target ref, a **lossless 2-parent `git merge`** (both parents kept; a genuine content conflict → abort → keep local → hint `rebar fsck-recover`). An unrelated-history head (no common ancestor) is still unioned via `--allow-unrelated-histories` — divergent tips of the same configured ref are always losslessly unionable — so the only thing that aborts a fold is git reporting a real content conflict. The only shared mutable file `.bridge_state/*` resolves via the tickets-branch `.gitattributes` `merge=ours` documented at `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:55` `_GITATTRIBUTES`; UUID-named event dirs never collide, which is exactly why the forbidden `merge=union` driver is unnecessary.

**This story reduces the S3 case to the already-solved git case.** The multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence *hidden at git-remote-s3's bundle-storage layer*. The only genuinely S3-specific action is unavoidable: because the helper refuses every ref op while `bundles > 1`, rebar must issue S3 object writes/deletes directly to collapse the bundle count. Those writes — plus bundle enumeration and the repair lock — are performed **through git-remote-s3's own importable library** (its `S3Remote`, its `.s3` boto3 client, its `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`, its bundle key layout), so rebar owns no credential chain, key-layout, or lock code, and adds **no** direct S3 SDK dependency to core rebar (boto3 ships transitively with the helper, under the optional `[s3]` extra only).

## Approach

Add a thin **optional** module `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py` exposing `heal_multi_bundle(base_path, remote, ref)`, invoked from `src/rebar/_store/push.py` when the multi-bundle signature is detected, then retry the push. The module imports `git_remote_s3` **lazily inside its functions**, guarded by the existing `require_s3_helper()` availability/ version check (mirroring `_optional.py`), so importing rebar never requires the helper or boto3.

**Detection (push.py).** Add a narrow `_is_multi_bundle(stderr)` predicate matching the two observed signatures — `multiple bundles exists on server` (helper reject) and `multiple updates for ref` (ambiguous fetch/clone). In `push_tickets_branch`'s retry loop, at the existing `if not _is_non_fast_forward(stderr):` seam, branch to the doctor **once** (a single `healed_once` guard caps this push call at one heal attempt, preventing a heal→retry thrash loop) *before* the normal non-FF recovery, then `continue` the loop to re-push. The one-attempt cap is safe under contention precisely because the remote is **shared**: whichever process wins the S3 lock collapses the bundles to one for everyone, so a process that itself declines to heal (lock held) still converges when its subsequent push retry accepts the winner's single bundle — it never needs to heal twice.

**Heal algorithm — write-merged-tip-first, delete-originals-second, never discard.** All S3 access is via the helper's own `S3Remote` (constructed from the configured `s3://` URL with `parse_git_url`), so credentials/SSE-KMS come from the boto3 chain the helper already owns. The ordering is dictated by two verified helper facts: (i) `cmd_push` cannot write while `bundles > 1`, so the merged bundle is written by a **direct `put_object`**, not the helper's push; (ii) a git-remote-s3 bundle is a plain `git bundle create` object stored at `f"{prefix}/{ref}/{sha}.bundle"`, which rebar reproduces exactly.

1. **Serialize with the helper's own per-ref lock** — `S3Remote.acquire_lock(ref)` (its
   `IfNoneMatch="*"` conditional-put, 60s TTL, stale-lock steal, `remote.py`); on `None`/`412`
   another repair is in flight → this process does **not** heal (returns without merging); it
   does not consume a second heal attempt because the winner's heal collapses the shared remote
   to a single bundle, which this process's subsequent push retry then accepts (within the same
   push call if the winner finishes first, else on the next push/sync cycle that re-detects the —
   by then already single — state). `release_lock` in a `finally`. **No reinvented rebar
   `DOCTOR` marker.**
2. **Re-enumerate under the lock (TOCTOU guard, jj pattern)** — `get_bundles_for_ref(ref)`; if
   now ≤1 bundle, another doctor already converged → release and return.
3. **Fetch every head locally** — for each remaining bundle, fetch its tip into a scratch ref
   (`refs/rebar-doctor/<sha>`) so all divergent commits are present locally.
4. **Fold the N heads by ITERATED 2-parent merges, following sync's per-target reconcile
   semantics, under rebar's `write_lock`** — there is **no octopus merge**. The doctor folds the
   divergent bundle heads into HEAD one at a time: for each fetched head it does the merge-base
   check and then a single 2-parent `git merge` (plain, or `--allow-unrelated-histories` when the
   target shares no common ancestor), with the same conflict → abort → keep-local →
   `fsck-recover` net and the same `.gitattributes merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` that
   `_do_reconverge`/`_union_merge` apply. Per the certified plan's permitted fallback this
   per-target merge is **self-contained in `s3_doctor.py`** rather than lifted into a shared
   `reconcile_one` primitive; it follows sync's semantics exactly (identical 2-parent behaviour
   per call, no new strategy/config parameters) and leaves sync's `reconverge`/`_union_merge`
   untouched (their oracle stays green). The behaviour-preserving code unification — extracting a
   shared `reconcile_one(tracker, target_ref)` that both sync and the doctor call — is deferred to
   **cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc** (discovered_from this ticket). The refuse-vs-union decision is a
   single unambiguous predicate: **every fetched head is a tip of the *same configured ref's*
   bundles** (all already-published ticket history of the store the operator pointed
   `sync.remote` at), so the doctor **always unions** — including an unrelated-history head, via
   `--allow-unrelated-histories` when it shares no merge-base — and the abort/refuse path fires
   **only when `git merge` reports a genuine content conflict** (the same non-derived file edited
   divergently). There is no `_carries_ticket_events` gate: after the first merge HEAD always
   carries events, so keying off that would wrongly refuse same-ref heads; the doctor instead
   distinguishes union from refuse purely by whether git can auto-resolve the merge. On a real
   conflict it aborts (`git merge --abort`), releases both locks, leaves the remote untouched
   (deletes nothing), and surfaces `rebar fsck-recover` rather than silently discarding a parent. The whole fold runs **inside rebar's `_lock.write_lock`** (the same local per-tracker
   lock `reconverge`/`push_tickets_branch` take) because it mutates HEAD/index/worktree exactly as
   `_union_merge` does, so it never races a concurrent local committer. Lock ordering is fixed and
   cycle-free: the helper's per-ref **S3 lock is the outer lock** (step 1, serializes cross-clone
   repairs) and rebar's **`write_lock` is the inner lock** taken only around this fold; local
   committers never take the S3 lock and every doctor takes the S3 lock first, so at most one
   doctor ever reaches the `write_lock`. The resulting HEAD `T` reaches every event from every
   head. **No `merge=union` driver; no octopus merge.**
5. **Write `T` as a NEW bundle object (durability barrier)** — `git bundle create` for `T`, then
   `S3Remote.s3.put_object(Bucket=remote.bucket, Key=f"{prefix}/{ref}/{T_sha}.bundle", Body=…)`.
   Remote now holds N+1 bundles, one of which (`T`) is fully lossless. **Nothing has been
   deleted yet**, so no event can be lost. (If `T_sha` equals an existing head — already-merged
   — the put is idempotent.)
6. **Delete the N original bundles** via `S3Remote.s3.delete_object`, leaving exactly `T`.
   **`T` is never deleted.**
7. **Point HEAD at `T`** via the helper's `init_remote_head(ref)`, then **release the lock** and
   delete the local scratch refs (on both the success and abort paths).

The caller's existing non-FF recovery reconciles the local HEAD against the now-single bundle `T` (the ordinary git path — no new code): the retried `git push` fetches the unambiguous `T`, merges, and pushes, so the final bundle carries local writes plus every divergent head.

Idempotency/recovery, aligned to the ordering above: `T` is content-addressed, so re-running yields the same tip. Crash invariant at **every** point: because `T` is written before any delete and never deleted, at least one bundle carrying the full merged history is always present remotely — a crash before step 5 leaves the N originals (all events present); a crash mid step 6 leaves `T` plus a subset of originals (`T` alone is lossless, and `bundles > 1` simply re-triggers the heal); a crash after step 6 leaves exactly `T`. No fencing token is needed — S3 strong read-after-write plus the conditional-put lock make the worst case "multi-bundle again," itself healable (Kleppmann: this lock guards *efficiency*, not correctness). Running the heal lazily on the next push that hits the anomaly (jj defer-repair / WAL replay-on-startup) means **no daemon**. Each heal emits one structured log record (`ref`, the merged head SHAs, the resulting `T`, and the deleted bundle keys).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py` — NEW optional module: `heal_multi_bundle`, lazy
  `git_remote_s3` import behind `require_s3_helper()`, the lock→enumerate→fetch→merge→write→
  delete flow, scratch-ref cleanup, structured logging, and the self-contained iterated 2-parent fold.
  **All git_remote_s3 access is routed through a single thin adapter function** in this module
  (the one place that imports `S3Remote`/`parse_git_url` and touches `.s3`/`acquire_lock`/
  `release_lock`/`get_bundles_for_ref`/`init_remote_head`), so the private-API dependency has one
  swappable seam. No rebar-owned boto3/credential/key-layout/lock code beyond the one bundle key
  string the helper defines. Target 200–500 LOC; hard cap 800 (split along call-graph seams only).
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — add `_is_multi_bundle`, a `healed_once`-guarded branch to
  `heal_multi_bundle` at the non-FF seam, and the post-heal push retry.
- `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` — **unchanged in this ticket.** The doctor follows sync's existing
  per-target decision-and-merge semantics (the merge-base/unrelated-history choice from
  `_do_reconverge` plus the 2-parent `git merge` in `_union_merge`) via a self-contained fold in
  `s3_doctor.py`, per the certified plan's permitted fallback; sync's `reconverge`/`_union_merge`
  oracle stays green. Extracting the shared `reconcile_one(tracker, target_ref)` primitive that
  both sync and the doctor would call is a behaviour-preserving follow-up deferred to
  **cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc** (discovered_from this ticket).
- `tests/` — new test module (see Testing).

## Testing

- Tier **real temporary git repositories** (git refs / merge / reachability / data loss).
  Oracle: construct a ref with two divergent bundles, each carrying a **unique** commit; run
  `heal_multi_bundle` against an **in-process fake `S3Remote`** (models `acquire_lock`/
  `release_lock`/`get_bundles_for_ref`/`init_remote_head` and a `.s3` with `put_object`/
  `delete_object`/`list_objects_v2` over a local object dir — no real AWS, no new hard test dep);
  assert (a) exactly one bundle remains for the ref, (b) a fresh clone succeeds, and (c) **every**
  unique commit from **both** heads is reachable from the healed tip (collateral invariant: no
  unique commit dropped) — the exact loss upstream's discard would cause.
- Tier **conflict path** (non-derived-file conflict). Oracle: two heads that conflict in a
  non-derived, non-`.bridge_state` file; assert the heal aborts, deletes **nothing** remotely
  (all original bundles intact), releases the lock, and surfaces the `fsck-recover` hint — never
  dropping a parent.
- Tier **multi-process locking race** (repair storm). Oracle: N real processes hit the
  multi-bundle state behind a shared barrier against the shared fake; assert exactly one performs
  the merge (the rest get `None` from `acquire_lock` and back off) and the final state is a
  single healed bundle with full reachability.
- Tier **crash-recovery** (kill after failpoint). Oracle: inject a failure **after** the merged
  bundle is put but **before/among** the original deletes; assert `T` is present, the store is
  still lossless, and the next detection re-heals to a single bundle (idempotency) — the
  failpoint matches the write-then-delete ordering.
- Tier **push-path integration**. Oracle: seed the `multiple bundles` stderr signature and assert
  `push_tickets_branch` auto-invokes the heal exactly once (the `healed_once` guard) and then
  converges (no infinite non-FF retry loop).
- Tier **local-lock serialization** (doctor vs. local committer). Oracle: while a
  `heal_multi_bundle` merge is in progress, a concurrent local ticket write attempts to commit;
  assert the two do not interleave on HEAD/index (the write blocks until the doctor's
  `write_lock`-scoped merge completes) and both the healed bundle and the concurrent write are
  present afterward — proving the merge runs under rebar's `write_lock`.
- Tier **credential-less API-surface guard**. A contract test (no AWS creds) that imports the
  installed `git_remote_s3` and asserts the exact v0.3.2 surface the heal binds —
  `parse_git_url`, `S3Remote(uri_scheme, profile, bucket, prefix)`, `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`,
  `get_bundles_for_ref`, `init_remote_head`, and a `.s3` client — so a helper upgrade that moves
  or renames any of them fails loudly here rather than at runtime.
- **Opt-in live canary** (`tests/e2e/test_s3_doctor_live.py`, AWS-credential-gated, skipped in
  credential-less CI) exercises the happy path against a real ephemeral bucket to validate the
  real conditional-write/multi-bundle semantics the fake models, and pins the git_remote_s3
  v0.3.2 API surface the heal depends on (`parse_git_url`, `S3Remote` construction,
  `acquire_lock`/`release_lock`, `get_bundles_for_ref`, `.s3`, `init_remote_head`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] After `heal_multi_bundle` on a ref with two divergent bundles, exactly one bundle remains,
      a fresh clone succeeds, and every unique commit from both heads is reachable from the
      healed tip. Verified by the real-git-repo oracle.
- [x] The heal never discards a head/event: a commit unique to the non-chosen head is present in
      the healed history (the specific regression upstream's interactive doctor causes). Verified
      by the reachability assertion.
- [x] The heal writes the merged tip before deleting any original bundle and never deletes the
      merged tip, so at every crash point ≥1 bundle carrying the full merged history remains
      remotely; a mid-delete crash re-heals to a single lossless bundle on the next run. Verified
      by the crash-recovery oracle.
- [x] On an unexpected non-derived-file conflict the heal aborts without deleting any remote
      bundle, releases the lock, and surfaces `rebar fsck-recover` — no parent dropped. Verified
      by the conflict-path oracle.
- [x] Concurrent doctors do not corrupt or duplicate-repair: with N processes behind a barrier,
      exactly one merges (the rest observe the helper's held per-ref lock and back off without
      healing), and the final shared remote is a single healed bundle with full reachability — so
      the backing-off processes converge on the winner's collapsed remote, not on a self-heal.
      Verified by the multi-process race oracle.
- [x] `push_tickets_branch` auto-invokes the heal on the multi-bundle signature exactly once and
      the push converges afterward (no infinite non-FF retry loop). Verified by the push-path
      test.
- [x] The doctor's local merge runs under rebar's `write_lock` and cannot race a concurrent
      local committer (HEAD/index are never mutated outside the lock); the helper's S3 ref-lock
      is the outer lock and `write_lock` the inner, a fixed cycle-free order. Verified by the
      local-lock serialization oracle.
- [x] The doctor folds N heads via **iterated 2-parent merges** (not an octopus merge),
      following `sync`'s existing lossless-merge semantics, and `sync`'s
      `reconverge`/`_union_merge` keep identical observable behavior (their oracle stays green,
      no new strategy/config parameters). Verified by the existing sync suite plus the N≥3-head
      fold oracle asserting all heads reachable. Per the certified plan's permitted fallback the
      merge is self-contained in `s3_doctor.py` rather than a shared `reconcile_one` lift; the
      behaviour-preserving code unification is tracked in cb91-1535-fe3a-47fc (discovered_from
      this ticket).
- [x] A fetched bundle head that shares no common ancestor with HEAD is handled explicitly:
      the fold still unions it via `--allow-unrelated-histories` (all heads are tips of the
      same configured ref, losslessly unionable). The abort/refuse path fires only when `git
      merge` reports a genuine content conflict (same non-derived file edited divergently): it
      aborts, deletes nothing remotely, and surfaces `fsck-recover`. Verified by two oracles — an
      unrelated-history union oracle (orphan root reachable after heal) and a content-conflict
      abort oracle (no bundle deleted, `S3DoctorConflict` with `fsck-recover` hint).
- [x] The heal keeps append-only semantics and adds **no** direct S3 SDK dependency to core
      rebar: all S3 access (lock, enumerate, put, delete, HEAD) is via git-remote-s3's own
      `S3Remote`/`.s3` imported lazily behind `require_s3_helper()`; no `merge=union` driver is
      used; the helper lock TTL is unchanged (default 60s). Verified by inspection and by rebar
      importing with the `[s3]` extra absent.
baseline.summary: Non-interactive auto-doctor: heal S3 multiple-bundles by lossless merge (reuse helper lib + rebar reconcile; never discard)

## Problem
Once the review-kernel's downstream consumers no longer read `severity` (sibling tickets 1-5), the review-kernel (`pass3_decide`) itself should stop STAMPING `severity` onto its own emitted findings. `pass3_decide` has FIVE return sites that stamp `severity` (`review_kernel/decide.py`): four via a `sev = severity_label(imp)` variable (lines 690, 706, 724, 740) and one hardcoded literal `"none"` on the no-verification/indeterminate return (line 673, which occurs before `imp`/`sev` are ever computed).

CRITICAL MECHANISM (found by plan-review): omitting `severity` at the source is NOT enough by itself. `code_review/shim.py::_to_common_finding` currently ALWAYS stamps a valid `severity` via `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY.get(raw_sev, _SEVERITY_DEFAULT)` -- for a kernel finding with no `severity` at all, `raw_sev` is `""`, which the map doesn't recognize, so it falls back to `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT = "medium"`. And even if `_to_common_finding` is fixed to omit the key entirely, the finding still flows through `finalize_findings` -> `build_result` -> `findings.py::normalize_finding`, which TODAY unconditionally re-stamps a missing `severity` to `"info"` (`f["severity"] = sev if sev in SEVERITIES else "info"`, where an absent key defaults to `""`, which isn't in `SEVERITIES`). So a naive "just omit it in shim.py" plan would ship review-kernel findings that always carry `severity: "medium"` or `severity: "info"` regardless -- silently reintroducing a meaningless label, exactly the problem this epic retires. `normalize_finding` must be changed too: only clamp to `"info"` when a `severity` key IS PRESENT but holds an unrecognized value; leave it ABSENT when the input genuinely has no `severity` key. Research confirmed this is safe: no production caller or existing test relies on `normalize_finding` backfilling `"info"` onto a finding dict that never had a `severity` key at all (every other real producer -- `completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`, `workflow/gate_ops.py`, `spec_scan.py` -- always supplies a real severity value already).

CORRECTED SCOPE (post-decomposition research): `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES` vocabulary and the `Finding` Pydantic field are NOT removed -- they serve the completion-verification module cluster and `spec_scan.py`, neither of which has a priority/decision alternative. `completion_verdict.schema.json` and `review_result.schema.json` both `$ref` the SAME shared `common.schema.json#/$defs/finding` (confirmed, byte-identical `$ref`), so relaxing that def's `required` list technically loosens both schemas' formal requirement -- but every completion-verification producer always populates `severity` in practice regardless of the schema requirement, so this is a de jure relaxation only, with no de facto behavior change for `completion_verdict`.

## Approach
1. In `review_kernel/decide.py`, remove `severity`/`sev` from ALL FIVE `pass3_decide` return
   sites: the four `sev`-fed sites (lines 690, 706, 724, 740) AND the hardcoded `"none"`
   literal on the no-verification return (line 673). Keep `severity_label()` itself as an
   internal impact-bucketing helper (still used by calibration/eval code and
   `test_divergence_grade_split.py`), just stop writing its output into the finding.
2. In `code_review/shim.py::_to_common_finding`, stop defaulting an absent/unrecognized
   `severity` to `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT = "medium"` -- when the source kernel finding has no
   `severity` key (now the normal case for review-kernel findings), omit the `severity` key
   from the output entirely. Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` and `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT` from
   `shim.py` (their only use site).
3. In `findings.py::normalize_finding`, change the severity-clamp so it only fires when a
   `severity` key IS PRESENT on the input but holds a value outside `SEVERITIES` (still clamps

4. In `common.schema.json`'s `$defs/finding`, remove `severity` from the `required` list

5. Remove the vestigial `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`/`blocking_severities` field and its

6. Add ONE compatibility-note entry to `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`: `severity`

7. Amend `docs/adr/0108-retire-severity-label.md` with an "Amendment" section recording this

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `grep -n '"severity"' src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` finds no finding-shape
  stamping at ANY of the five return sites (the `severity_label` function definition and any

- [x] `review_bot/config.py` has no `blocking_severities`/`DEFAULT_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` symbol;
  `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` and `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py` are updated to

- [x] `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY\|_SEVERITY_DEFAULT" src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py`

- [x] `docs/release-notes.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/adr/0108-retire-severity-label.md`

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit tests. Oracle (three layers, since a single-layer test previously missed the re-stamp defect): (1) `pass3_decide`'s real output has no `severity` key at any of its five return paths; (2) `normalize_finding` in isolation -- absent-key input stays absent, present-invalid-value input still clamps to `"info"`; (3) the FULL production chain (`shim.py` -> `finalize_findings` -> `normalize_finding`) fed a severity-less kernel finding produces a `review_result` finding with no `severity` key -- proving the omission actually survives to the schema-validated output, not just an intermediate function's return value. ## Summary
An agent-executed epic cannot be represented in the store as certified/**signed**-closed when one of its child stories carries an `[operator-attested]` acceptance criterion whose evidence lives outside the codebase and outside the executing agent's access — even when every engineering acceptance criterion across the whole epic is demonstrably complete and landed on `main`. This is a process/tooling gap surfaced while executing epic `bf50-2131-271b-4fdc` (graceless-hominine-jerboa); it is NOT a defect in any of that epic's code changes.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Decompose an epic into stories and execute it with an agent (claim → implement → land each
   child through the Gerrit gate).
2. Include among the children a story whose acceptance criteria contain an `[operator-attested]`
   item whose admissible evidence is inherently out-of-band — e.g. 5f39-cb52-9355-492f AC3:
   configured GitHub repo VARIABLES (`JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_PROJECT`,
   `ACLI_VERSION`/`ACLI_SHA256`), a configured SECRET (`JIRA_API_TOKEN`), a provisioned
   dedicated Jira test project, and the URL of a green `workflow_dispatch` run in which the live
   Jira test EXECUTED (not all-skip).
3. Have the agent complete and LAND every code change (all children `Verified +1` AND
   `LLM-Review +1`, merged to `main`).
4. Attempt to close that child, then the epic.

## Expected
With all engineering acceptance criteria met and landed, the epic — and every child — can be closed with a completion-verifier **signature** (certified), such that the store durably records the epic as fully certified when the work is in fact complete.

## Actual
- The child's completion verifier passes every CODE criterion but FAILS the single
  `[operator-attested]` criterion, because the agent has neither the access nor the
  authorization to produce the required out-of-band evidence (repo secrets/variables, a live
  Jira project, an observed green canary run), and no concrete attestation (run URL/id/timestamp)
  therefore exists to record.
- The child can only be **force-closed UNSIGNED**.
- The epic's own acceptance criterion requires "all child stories closed (**signed**)", so the
  epic's completion verifier fails on that criterion and the epic can only be **force-closed
  UNSIGNED** as well.
- Net: an epic whose entire engineering scope is complete and landed cannot be represented as
  certified/signed, purely because one child's evidence is out-of-band from the agent's reach.

## Evidence / Impact
- Concretely observed on epic `bf50-2131-271b-4fdc`: 19/19 stories implemented and merged to
  `main` (Gerrit changes 537–555 + 559); 18/19 children closed SIGNED (plan-review +
  completion-verifier); child `5f39-cb52-9355-492f` and the epic closed UNSIGNED via force-close.
- Full trail (per-story claims, RED/teeth evidence, landing, the force-close reasoning, and a
  dedicated PROBLEM RECORD entry) is in session log `25f1-5000-760d-4c2b`
  (plump-kitschy-meadowlark), linked to this bug.
- Impact: the "signed = fully certified" invariant cannot be earned for any epic that contains
  an operator-attested criterion the agent cannot attest; such epics are indistinguishable in
  the store (both unsigned) from epics whose OWN engineering work genuinely failed verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The problem is reproducible and characterized: an agent-executed epic with all
      engineering ACs complete + landed, plus one child bearing an out-of-band
      `[operator-attested]` criterion the agent cannot attest, results in unsigned closure of
      both the child and the epic.
- [ ] The gap is documented with the concrete instance (epic bf50, child 5f39) and its evidence
      (the specific out-of-band items required, and why the agent could not produce them).
- [ ] This bug links to the full session log capturing the run and the problem record.
baseline.summary: Agent-executed epic cannot close SIGNED when a child has an operator-attested criterion the agent cannot attest

With a key-set prev, keys present in both prev and curr route to `_compute_mutations_emit_both` with an empty `local_fields`, producing ~516 mutations per pass that are provably inert but not free. Skip them. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Each inert mutation still traverses `_apply_one`, which calls `_recheck_drift` -> `concurrency.snapshot_head(repo_root)` — **a `git rev-parse` subprocess per mutation**. So ~516 extra git invocations per pass, ~516 `RECON: batch_outcome` stderr lines, ~516 outcome records in the manifest, and an inflated `mutation_count` so a converged pass reports 516 instead of 0. It also enlarges the HEAD-drift window. Under `BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` (cap 10) or `BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE` (cap 100) these compete for cap slots with genuine work (`apply_planning.py:90-101`) and can starve it — production defaults to `LIVE` (cap `None`), so that risk is latent, not live.

## Approach
Short-circuit `_compute_mutations_emit_both` when `local_fields` is falsy, or equivalently skip the `_emit` at `differ.py:590` when the resolved `changed` dict contains no field that survives `_mutation_to_batch_dict`. ~5 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With a key-set prev over a real corpus, `(outbound, update)` mutations with an empty effective
      payload are **0** (down from ~516). Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations` + the corpus script.
- [ ] Mutations with a genuine non-empty effective payload are still emitted unchanged — the
      negative control. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `mutation_count` on a converged pass is 0. Tier: **integration** asserting the pass record.
- [ ] `git rev-parse` invocation count per pass drops correspondingly. Tier: **integration** with a
      counting shim.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/differ.py`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A4-2.

## Context / Problem

Making OperationSnapshot authoritative for LLM operations (gaudy-working-mantaray) migrates `LLMConfig.from_env` call sites and threads a snapshot-derived projection through the gate/workflow entry points. `src/rebar/llm/config.py` (799 LOC) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (796 LOC) are within a few lines of the hard 800-LOC module-size cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so that threading would breach the CI module-size gate on first edit.

Create headroom FIRST via behavior-preserving extraction along existing call-graph seams. This story adds no snapshot-threading logic; it only relocates existing clusters.

## Approach

- `llm/config.py`: move `_env_truthy`, `_read_llm_file_table`, `_llm_str_source`, `_llm_str`, `_llm_int`, `_llm_float`, `_llm_drain_mode` into a new sibling `llm/config_readers.py`. `config.py` re-imports all of them (`from .config_readers import (...)  # noqa: F401`) at module top, mirroring the existing `gate_context` re-export pattern (config.py L41-47). `LLMConfig.from_env` (the sole caller) is NOT moved, so its bare-name lookups resolve through `config.py`'s own namespace — this is what keeps the ~15 existing `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar.llm.config, "_read_llm_file_table", ...)` seams live. `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py`'s direct `_read_llm_file_table` import keeps working via the re-export.
- `llm/plan_review/__init__.py`: move ONLY the five pure leaves — `_apply_floor_to_verdict`, `_score_floor_novelty`, `_apply_completion_floor_to_verdict`, `_classify_completion`, `_group_blocking_fix_units` — into a new sibling `llm/plan_review/floors.py`, re-imported (`from .floors import (...)  # noqa: F401`). `_maybe_apply_rising_floor` and `_maybe_apply_completion_floor` STAY in `__init__.py`: they are the entry points `_run_plan_review` calls, and their internal bare-name calls into the five moved leaves must keep resolving through `__init__.py`'s namespace so `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_score_floor_novelty"/"_classify_completion", ...)` (test_plan_review_rising_floor.py, test_completion_floor.py) keeps intercepting. `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "_maybe_apply_rising_floor"/"_maybe_apply_completion_floor"/"_group_blocking_fix_units", ...)` (test_plan_review_sidecar_heldout.py) is unaffected either way since its caller `_run_plan_review` also stays put.
- **`_verifier_cfg`** stays in `__init__.py` (used elsewhere there too). The two moved leaves that call it (`_score_floor_novelty`, `_classify_completion`) reach it via a **lazy in-function import** (`from rebar.llm.plan_review import _verifier_cfg`), not a module-top-level import — `__init__.py` already does `from .floors import (...)` at its own top, so a reverse top-level import in `floors.py` would cycle. By call time the package is fully initialized, so the lazy import is safe; this mirrors the lazy-import style these two functions already use for `rebar.llm.runner`/`review_kernel.verify`/`passes`.

`LLMConfig`, `review_plan`, and public plan_review imports keep working unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/` — new sibling modules (`config_readers.py`, `plan_review/floors.py`); import updates only. Does NOT touch `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (owned by hurt-antigorite-genet).
- `tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/` — import-path updates only, EXCEPT two consumers that pin a physical path/text and must be repointed:
  - `tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py` AST-parses `config.py`'s source TEXT by path (`_CONFIG_PY`) to enumerate `_llm_*` helpers; repoint `_CONFIG_PY` to `config_readers.py` (or also parse it) so the moved names keep being found.
  - `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`'s `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` hard-codes `'llm/plan_review/__init__.py::_score_floor_novelty'`; update to `'llm/plan_review/floors.py::_score_floor_novelty'`.

## Testing

Existing llm/plan-review suites (`tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/`) pass unchanged — every `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar.llm.config, "_read_llm_file_table", ...)` site and every `monkeypatch.setattr(plan_review, "<floor-helper>", ...)` site (rising-floor, completion-floor, completion-floor-e2e, blocking-fix-unit-grouping, sidecar-heldout tests) keeps intercepting the same call. The two path-pinning consumers above are updated and continue to pass. Module-size gate, complexity ratchet, lint, typecheck pass. No new CI-provider/network/Docker dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `config.py` and `plan_review/__init__.py` are each <= 700 LOC via extraction into `config_readers.py` / `plan_review/floors.py` only.
- [x] No new module < 100 LOC; no mechanical split.
- [x] Every existing monkeypatch seam on a moved helper via its ORIGINAL module keeps intercepting the same call site.
- [x] `test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py`'s `_CONFIG_PY` control and `test_subcall_class_selection.py`'s `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` entry are updated to the new locations and pass.
- [x] `floors.py` reaches `_verifier_cfg` via a lazy in-function import; no top-level circular import with `__init__.py`.
- [x] Behavior unchanged across `tests/unit/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/external/`.
- [x] `model_classes.py`'s `_read_llm_file_table` import keeps working unchanged.
- [x] `llm/runner.py` untouched.
- [x] Module-size gate, complexity ratchet, lint, typecheck all pass.
baseline.summary: Create llm config-threading module-size headroom before the authoritative-snapshot cutover

## Context / Problem
`tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py:311` patches `binding_store_mod._now_iso` to advance the wall clock, then asserts that an unchanged second reconcile pass rewrites no bytes. The patch is how the test proves the no-churn contract is real rather than a coincidence of a fast test run.

RP-02 S2 T2 moved the absence/tombstone/comment cluster into `binding_lifecycle.py`, so `clear_absent` (and its siblings) now resolve `_now_iso` from `binding_lifecycle`, not `binding_store`. The existing patch therefore no longer reaches them.

## Impact
The test still PASSES, and correctly so — the no-churn contract means the clock is never consulted on a healthy pass. But its blast radius narrowed: it would no longer catch a regression that made `clear_absent` (or another moved operation) stamp `updated_at` unconditionally. That is a silent weakening of an integration-tier oracle.

Coverage did not disappear, it moved tiers: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_lifecycle.py::test_clear_absent_does_not_dirty_an_entry_with_no_absence` pins the contract directly on the policy owner, and was one of the held-out tests for S2 T2. So the risk here is contained, which is why this is a follow-up rather than a blocker.

## Outcome
Restore the integration oracle's original reach by patching the clock on BOTH modules, so it again fails if any binding operation stamps a timestamp on an unchanged pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The idempotency test patches `_now_iso` on `binding_lifecycle` as well as `binding_store` (or on a single shared source, if one is introduced).
- [x] With the patch in place, making `clear_absent` stamp `updated_at` unconditionally drives the integration test RED — verified by seeding that mutation, not assumed.
- [x] The test still passes unmutated, and still asserts byte-level no-churn across an unchanged second pass.
- [x] Audit the same file for other `binding_store_mod`-targeted patches whose subject moved to `binding_lifecycle.py` during RP-02 S2.

## Notes
Discovered by the implementation subagent during RP-02 S2 T2 and deliberately left alone there: that ticket's instructions forbade touching test files outside its scope, and widening an integration oracle is a test-hygiene change that deserves its own review rather than riding along in an extraction slice.
baseline.summary: Idempotency oracle no longer reaches moved binding clock reads
