# APPROVED BY THE OPERATOR — implement Option 3 (scheduled main-health CI, every 6 hours)

The research below is complete and the recommendation has been **approved**. Do not re-litigate the approach; the operator's instruction and the constraints are recorded in "Operator's decision" immediately below, and the acceptance criteria at the end are binding.

## Operator's decision (the thing to implement)

1. **GitHub CI for `main` runs on a SCHEDULE, not on push to `main`.** Cadence: **every 6 hours**
   — that is the signal density the operator wants. Use an **off-the-hour minute** (not `0`) so
   this repo's runs do not pile onto the hour boundary with every other project on the platform.
2. **Evaluate EVERY GitHub Actions workflow so the policy is CONSISTENT** — no workflow keeps a
   push-on-`main` trigger merely because nobody looked at it. Each workflow gets an explicit,
   recorded disposition.
3. **External-integration jobs stay at MOST once a day.** Their frequency must not increase.
   `external-integration.yml` is weekly today and stays weekly.
4. **Gerrit-verify and the reconciler workflows MUST NOT be changed** — they are separate
   mechanisms with their own semantics (`gerrit-verify.yaml`'s concurrency keys on
   `GERRIT_CHANGE_ID` as a deliberate stale-patchset guard; the reconcilers deliberately run
   with `cancel-in-progress: false`).
5. **`workflow_dispatch` must remain (or be added)** on every main-health workflow, so anyone can
   ask "is `main` healthy?" on demand without waiting for the tick.
6. **Pay for the loss of per-commit attribution, explicitly.** Two items from the approved
   recommendation are NOT optional:
   - Write the **`git bisect run` command into the workflow's FAILURE OUTPUT**, so remediation is
     one copy-paste. A scheduled run covers many commits; the first responder must not have to
     reconstruct the technique under pressure.
   - **Publish the last-known-green `main` SHA** so a bisect has a lower bound (Zuul's periodic
     pipelines and vLLM's "greenest commit on main" practice are the precedent).

## The confirmed mechanism (verify, do not re-derive)

`test.yml` declares:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

On `main`, `github.ref` is the constant `refs/heads/main`, so every push to `main` lands in ONE concurrency group and cancels the previous run. Cancelled runs render as a red X on the commit list, and GitHub offers no native way to suppress that (see mechanics below).

Note that the affected workflows filter pushes with `branches-ignore: ["feature/**"]`, which **includes `main`** — so `main` must be added to that ignore list explicitly. Branch-push CI for NON-`main` branches is preserved.

## Prior art and options analysis

The full research — what four of five major Gerrit-primary mirrors (golang/go, openstack/nova, LibreOffice/core, aosp-mirror, qt/qtbase) surface on GitHub, where their real post-merge signal lives (Go on LUCI; Zuul's supercedent `post` pipeline plus `periodic` pipelines; Chromium's 7-10-hourly post-submit backed by automated bisection and a sheriff rotation), the verified GitHub Actions mechanics (cancelled == red X is unfixable natively; `cancel-in-progress: false` does not help; a workflow cannot decline to report; merge queue is structurally inapplicable), the four options considered, and the rejected alternatives (`delete-cancelled-runs`, `queue: max`) — is recorded verbatim as a comment on this ticket. It is settled input to the approved decision above, not open scope.

## Scope — the trigger inventory this change reasons over

Candidates (run on push to `main` today):

| Workflow | Trigger today | Cancels? |
|---|---|---|
| `test.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch | yes (`test-${{ github.ref }}`) |
| `optionality.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch | no |
| `verify-identity.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch | no |
| `prompt-eval.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch + weekly | yes |
| `codeql.yml` | push `branches: [main]` + weekly | yes |
| `terraform-drift.yml` | push `branches: [main]` path-filtered `infra/terraform/**` + daily + dispatch | no |

Out of scope, MUST NOT be modified: `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `reconcile-bridge.yml`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`, `external-integration.yml`, `mirror-guard.yml`, `lockdown.yml`, `release.yml`, `jira-dc-*.yml`, `structured-output-baseline.yml`, and the four `workflow_call` reusables (`_artifact-probe.yml`, `_build-and-test.yml`, `_eval-discipline.yml`, `_optionality.yml`) — the reusables have no triggers of their own, so only their CALLERS change.

## The safety property that makes this acceptable

Pre-merge gating is **unchanged**. The Gerrit `Verified` lane runs the reusable `_build-and-test.yml` (and `_artifact-probe.yml`) through `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `workflow_dispatch`, which is triggered by Gerrit per patchset. Editing `test.yml`'s **triggers** cannot alter that lane, because the lane never reads `test.yml`. Every change still needs `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` to land. The mirror's `main` CI is, and remains, a safety net — the change only alters WHEN the safety net runs, never what gates a merge.

## Files this touches

`.github/workflows/test.yml`, `.github/workflows/optionality.yml`, `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`, `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml`, `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml`, a new `scripts/main_health_report.py` (the report renderer, kept out of the workflow YAML so the suite can drive it), and two new test modules under `tests/unit/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1 — No workflow triggers on a push to `refs/heads/main`.** For each of `test.yml`,
      `optionality.yml`, `verify-identity.yml`, `prompt-eval.yml`, `codeql.yml`, and
      `terraform-drift.yml`, a push event whose ref is `refs/heads/main` matches no trigger.
- [x] **AC2 — The four `branches-ignore` workflows exclude `main` explicitly.** `test.yml`,
      `optionality.yml`, `verify-identity.yml`, and `prompt-eval.yml` list `main` alongside
      `feature/**` in `push.branches-ignore`.
- [x] **AC3 — The two `branches: [main]` workflows drop their `push` key outright.**
      `codeql.yml` and `terraform-drift.yml` have no `push` trigger at all (each had only
      `branches: [main]`, so there is no other branch to preserve).
- [x] **AC4 — Push CI for NON-`main` branches is preserved.** The four `branches-ignore`
      workflows still trigger on a push to a topic branch such as `wip-some-topic`.
- [x] **AC5 — `feature/**` stays excluded.** The existing S3-replicated feature-branch
      exclusion is unchanged in all four `branches-ignore` workflows.
- [x] **AC6 — The three cheap branch-health lanes gain a 6-hourly schedule.** `test.yml` gets
      `41 */6 * * *`, `optionality.yml` gets `47 */6 * * *`, `verify-identity.yml` gets
      `53 */6 * * *` — four "is main healthy" runs a day each, at deliberately staggered
      off-the-hour minutes so this repo's runs neither pile onto the hour boundary that every
      other project schedules onto nor onto each other.
- [x] **AC7 — `prompt-eval.yml` keeps its weekly cron `0 7 * * 1` and gains no 6-hourly cron.**
      Its live tier is billable; 6-hourly would be a 28x cost increase nobody asked for.
- [x] **AC8 — `codeql.yml` keeps its weekly cron `23 4 * * 1` and gains no 6-hourly cron.** A
      security scanner's cadence is a deliberate cost/coverage choice.
- [x] **AC9 — `terraform-drift.yml` keeps its daily cron `17 6 * * *` and gains no 6-hourly
      cron.** The daily sweep is already this workflow's branch-health signal.
- [x] **AC10 — Every one of the six workflows has `workflow_dispatch`**, so on-demand "is main
      healthy?" works without waiting for the tick (`codeql.yml` gains one; it had none).
- [x] **AC11 — The last-known-green `main` SHA is resolved from the workflow's own successful
      run history** — `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/test.yml/runs` filtered by
      `status=success` and the current `branch`, newest first. No new state is persisted: the
      GitHub side is a read-only mirror, so nothing is pushed.
- [x] **AC11a — That lookup's auth precondition is declared, not assumed.** The run-history
      endpoint needs BOTH the `actions: read` scope and a token on the step. The
      `main-health-report` job therefore declares `permissions: {contents: read, actions: read}`
      and the step passes `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. Missing either would 403, and the
      report would silently degrade to its AC14 placeholder on EVERY run instead of visibly
      once — a permanently useless lower bound is worse than an obviously absent one.
- [x] **AC12 — A GREEN scheduled/dispatched run publishes its own SHA as the new last-known-green
      value** to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so the lower bound is discoverable before an incident,
      not only during one.
- [x] **AC13 — A RED scheduled/dispatched run publishes a copy-pasteable remediation recipe** to
      `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`: a `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` line with both SHAs filled
      in, followed by a `git bisect run` command using this repo's own CI reproduction
      (`uv sync --locked --extra dev`, then `make check`, then `make test`).
- [x] **AC14 — Unresolvable last-known-green degrades gracefully.** Whenever the lower bound
      cannot be established — the Actions API returns no earlier successful run, OR the call
      itself fails (timeout, 4xx/5xx, rate limit, malformed body) — the report emits a recipe
      with a VISIBLE placeholder lower bound plus an explanation, and the step still exits 0. A
      missing lower bound must never turn a green `main` red, and a plausible-but-wrong SHA
      would send the bisect through commits that were never green.
- [x] **AC15 — The report is emitted from a NEW caller-level job in `test.yml`, never from a
      reusable.** `test.yml`'s gates run inside `_build-and-test.yml` / `_artifact-probe.yml`,
      which are in the untouchable set and accept no caller steps; the report therefore lives in
      a caller-level `main-health-report` job with `if: always()` that `needs` every gating job.
      It is carried by `test.yml` only — that is the lane whose failure implies a code
      regression worth bisecting; `optionality.yml` and `verify-identity.yml` are single-purpose
      checks whose failure names its own cause.
- [x] **AC16 — BOTH the lookup and the rendering live in a repo script, not inline YAML**, so
      they are unit-testable off a CI runner (workflow YAML is not reachable by the test
      suite). The `gh` call is injected as a `Runner` — the pattern `scripts/canary_bridge.py`
      already uses for its Actions-API reads — so every failure mode is exercised without a
      network, and the workflow keeps a single step rather than hand-rolled `jq` plumbing.
- [x] **AC17 — The live external tier does not fire more often.** Dispatching `test.yml` is now
      the routine "is main healthy?" button, so its `external` job requires an explicit
      `run_external` dispatch input defaulting to false, and the schedule can never reach it.
- [x] **AC18 — `external-integration.yml` is unmodified** and stays on its weekly
      `0 6 * * 1` cron, within the once-a-day cap.
- [x] **AC19 — The separate mechanisms are byte-identical.** `git diff` shows no change to
      `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `reconcile-bridge.yml`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`,
      `mirror-guard.yml`, or any `_*.yml` reusable.
- [x] **AC20 — Automated regression coverage pins the trigger policy** — a test asserts, per
      workflow, that a push to `refs/heads/main` does not match, that non-`main` push CI
      survives, that each cadence is as specified, that dispatch is present, and that the
      untouchable set is unchanged.
- [x] **AC21 — Automated coverage pins the report rendering** — tests assert the green path
      names the head SHA as the new lower bound, that an unproven (cancelled/skipped) gate is
      never reported as green, and that the red path emits a `git bisect start` line carrying
      both the bad and the resolved good SHA plus a balanced, single-quoted `git bisect run`
      command that reproduces CI.
- [x] **AC21a — Automated coverage pins EVERY lookup failure mode**, not just empty history: a
      non-zero `gh` exit (403 from a missing scope, 5xx, rate limit, timeout), an empty run
      list, a malformed body, and an unexpected response shape each yield no bound rather than
      raising or inventing one — and the CLI still exits 0 in each case.
- [x] **AC22 — Every touched workflow parses and lints.** `make lint` (which runs actionlint

baseline.description:
Set `merge.ours.driver=true` in the reconciler workflow so the tickets branch's `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` attribute actually resolves on GHA. Latent bug today; hard prerequisite for B1. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`init.py:508-511` sets `merge.ours.driver` **per clone**, and it is never committed; `reconcile-bridge.yml` never sets it. So on the runner the `merge=ours` attribute names an **undefined driver** and git silently falls back to a 3-way text merge of an **18,231,660-byte** JSON file — the opposite of the local-wins behaviour the design assumes.

**Scope correction (plan-review G6 remediation): the canary is NOT in scope.** `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` does a bare `git worktree add` at `:88` but then calls **`rebar init` at `:146`**, and its own comment at `:138-140` explains why ("a bare `git worktree add` of the tickets branch does NOT create ... and the write seam refuses every rebar write without it"). So the canary already gets `merge.ours.driver` via `_merge_ours_unit`. `reconcile-bridge.yml` does the bare worktree add at `:117` and **never** calls `rebar init`, which is why only it is affected. An earlier draft listed both workflows; that was wrong.

This must land before B1: `blob:none` keeps commits but removes merge-base **blobs**, which the reconverge path materializes, so filtering while the driver is undefined makes an already-fragile path lazily fault large blobs mid-merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `reconcile-bridge.yml` sets `merge.ours.driver=true` for the tickets worktree before any merge
      step. Tier: **unit** workflow-lint assertion.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py -v`.
- [ ] The canary is asserted to obtain the driver via its existing `rebar init` call, so it needs no
      edit — a regression guard against re-adding the change there. Tier: **unit** workflow-lint.
- [ ] A reconverge against a **diverged** remote in a fresh runner-shaped checkout resolves
      `.bridge_state/*` **local-wins** (not a text merge) and produces no conflict markers. Tier:
      **integration** in a real temporary git repo mimicking the runner setup.
- [ ] The same scenario **without** the config produces the text-merge behaviour — the negative
      control proving the test detects the defect. Tier: **integration**.

## Files
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`, tests (the canary is deliberately untouched)

Scope: XS-S. No dependencies.
baseline.summary: B3: define merge.ours.driver on the reconciler runner (prerequisite for the CI clone filter)

baseline.description:
## Context

rebar's test suite drives the tool largely by SUBPROCESS — the CLI adapter shells out to `python -m rebar.cli`, and many exit-code/CLI tests do the same (≈245 test files use subprocess / spec_from_file_location). coverage.py's in-process tracer never sees that child-process execution, so the measured in-process coverage (**77%** on 2026-06-27, see docs/coverage.md) UNDERSTATES the true exercised fraction. Because of this, `fail_under` is held at a deliberately conservative 70 — it cannot honestly track real coverage while subprocess work is invisible.

Research (peers + coverage.py docs) summary:
- **Modern recipe is ~3 lines**: `[tool.coverage.run] patch = ["subprocess"]` (coverage.py >= 7.10; auto-enables `parallel = true`) plus a `coverage combine` step before the report. pytest-cov >= 7.0 removed its own subprocess support and defers to coverage.py.
- **rebar is the easy case**: its subprocesses run in the SAME environment as the tests (no throwaway venvs), so NO `[tool.coverage.paths]` remapping is needed (unlike pip/tox/virtualenv).
- **Not universal practice**: process-spawning tools (pip, tox, nox, virtualenv, coverage.py itself) measure subprocess coverage; many mature CLIs (pdm, hatch, pipx, pre-commit) accept the in-process undercount with a conservative floor — the current documented stance here.
- **Real gotchas for us**: the `coverage combine` step becomes mandatory (erase -> test -> combine -> report); per-process tracing overhead (mitigate with `core = "sysmon"` on 3.12+); and crucially, rebar has many CLI EXIT-CODE tests — a child that calls `os._exit()` or is SIGTERM-killed never flushes coverage data, so we likely need `patch = ["subprocess", "_exit"]` and/or `sigterm = true`, and should expect to chase some flakiness.

Priority P4: optional, forward-looking. docs/coverage.md already documents this under "Future: subprocess coverage". Pick up when raising the real coverage number becomes worth the combine-step + exit-code-flush complexity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[tool.coverage.run] patch = ["subprocess"]` (or the classic COVERAGE_PROCESS_START + parallel recipe if needed) is enabled and instruments `python -m rebar.cli` children.
- [ ] The exit-code-test flush problem is handled (`patch` includes `_exit` and/or `sigterm = true`); the CLI exit-code suite stays green with no flakiness.
- [ ] The Makefile + CI coverage step run erase -> test -> `coverage combine` -> report in order (the combine step is wired so the report reads the merged parallel data).
- [ ] The reported coverage number measurably rises above the 77% in-process figure (subprocess work now counted); the delta is recorded in docs/coverage.md.
- [ ] `fail_under` is raised to a real guard under the new measured number; docs/coverage.md baseline + 'Future' section updated to reflect that subprocess coverage is now ON.
- [ ] Perf overhead is acceptable (consider `core = "sysmon"` on 3.12+); CI wall-clock regression is noted.
- [ ] CI measures the TRUE exercised coverage (subprocess child processes counted), and `fail_under` is raised to track that real number instead of the in-process undercount — with no new test flakiness.
baseline.summary: Subprocess coverage: measure CLI child-process execution so the floor tracks true coverage

baseline.description:
## Context

A deterministic two-process harness confirms that `sync.reconverge` inspects tracker recovery markers before acquiring the store write lock. Process A performs the non-fast-forward push recovery merge introduced under `cindery-lithe-acaciarat`. It owns the write lock while Git creates `MERGE_HEAD`. Process B calls `sync.reconverge`, sees that marker at the pre-lock early exit, emits an `fsck-recover` warning, and returns without waiting for the lock.

Process A then completes successfully. Its merge marker and lock clear, and the local and remote tips match. The warning therefore diagnoses an abandoned recovery state when the marker belongs to the process that owns the lock. The skipped reconvergence round also delays freshness. The enrichment drain is not involved.

The harness is `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-harness-20260824/h1_stage3.py`. Its SHA-256 is `e65c356bdc288c8729d5170524b89daca01e667600c2b385e4211c50e6083764`.

`cindery-lithe-acaciarat` correctly moved the push recovery merge under the write lock and added an in-lock recovery check. Its plan review explicitly preserved the existing pre-lock check as an early exit. That check predates the lock-owned push recovery interaction and cannot distinguish a stranded merge from work performed by the lock holder.

## Plan

- Make recovery-state classification in `sync.reconverge` authoritative only after the store write lock is acquired.
- Preserve fetch outside the store write lock.
- Preserve the in-lock `check_no_rebase_in_progress` guard in `_do_reconverge`.
- Add a deterministic concurrency test with state-based barriers. Pause a push recovery merge after `MERGE_HEAD` appears, start a peer reconverge, confirm that it remains pending, then release the merge.
- Preserve refusal and recovery guidance when a merge marker remains after lock acquisition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A peer reconverge does not return or emit an `fsck-recover` warning solely because a lock-owning push recovery merge has created `MERGE_HEAD`.
- [x] After the push recovery merge releases the lock, both operations exit successfully, `MERGE_HEAD` is absent, the lock is clear, local and remote tips match, and all seeded events remain reachable.
- [x] A stranded merge marker found after lock acquisition still blocks reset or merge mutation and directs the operator to `rebar fsck-recover`.
- [x] Fetch remains outside the store write lock, and existing fetch coordination and best-effort lock timeout behavior remain unchanged.
- [x] The regression test uses synchronization barriers instead of a wall-clock race.
- [x] [non-codebase] Focused tests, lint, type checking, and the full suite pass.
  provenance: environment=GitHub Actions CI (run 33198160020) + worktree venv (/Users/joeoakhart/debug/consensual-drake/.venv); principal=RebarBotNava <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit change 2324 patchset 2 earned Verified +1 from CI run 33198160020 (success), which executed the full build/test/lint/typecheck suite on macOS and Linux; local focused suites (42 passed), ruff check+format-check, and mypy all ran green in the worktree venv.
baseline.summary: sync.reconverge misclassifies a lock-owned push recovery merge as abandoned

baseline.description:
## What

Add a CI job that **drift-proofs the README quickstart's command TEXT** by extracting the CLI fenced command block from `README.md` and executing those exact lines end-to-end (init → create → ready → claim → close) in a throwaway git repo against a clean install. This is the core maintenance-burden reducer for the P0 defects: a wrong command *printed* in the README (e.g. `session-log` missing its `append` verb, or a hard-coded id) then exits non-zero and FAILS the build.

**Why extract-and-execute (not `probe-rebar.sh` alone, and not a static `--help` check).** `scripts/probe-rebar.sh` already exercises the golden path, but it uses its own internally-correct syntax — it can NOT catch wrong text printed in the README. A static "parse the block and check each command name against `rebar --help`" would catch a bad command *name* but NOT a wrong *subcommand/argument* (the actual P0 defect: `session-log` is a real command, but `session-log "<entry>"` is a wrong invocation) nor a stale hard-coded id, nor ordering/state errors. Only running the literal README lines against the live engine catches all of these. So this ticket adds a small **extractor** that pulls the fenced block(s) from the README and runs them; `probe-rebar.sh` is retained as the COMPLEMENTARY broader end-to-end smoke (kept wired, or invoked alongside) so it does not become stranded/stale.

- Add `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.sh` (or a small Python extractor) that parses the
  ```bash fenced quickstart block from `README.md` and executes those exact lines in an
  isolated temp `REBAR_ROOT` / throwaway git repo. No network, no shared state.
- Wire it as a gating job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, running against an INSTALLED
  rebar (clean `pipx`/`pip install`), so it also catches packaging/entry-point regressions.
- Keep `scripts/probe-rebar.sh` as the broader golden-path smoke (either invoked by the
  same job or left as-is) so its coverage is not lost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A CI job extracts the README quickstart's CLI fenced block and runs those exact
      lines end-to-end; it FAILS the build if any of init/create/ready/claim/close changes
      exit code or the extracted commands error.
- [ ] The job runs against a CLEAN, non-editable install — the new `golden-path`
      job in `test.yml` AND `gerrit-verify.yaml` does `pip install .` (a built wheel,
      not editable) and runs `check_readme_quickstart.py` against it, so
      packaging/entry-point regressions (MANIFEST, package data, console-script
      registration) — which an editable install cannot catch — fail the build.
      Verify (prints nothing): `for f in .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml; do grep -qF 'golden-path' "$f" && grep -qF 'pip install .' "$f" || echo "NO CLEAN-INSTALL JOB: $f"; done`
- [ ] The README *text* itself is what executes: a wrong command *printed* in the README
      — e.g. `session-log` missing its `append` verb, or a disconnected hard-coded id —
      is demonstrably caught (note the manual verification in a comment). Executability of
      an independent probe is NOT sufficient (closes epic finding G6/F4).
- [ ] The CI golden-path is the trimmed init->create->ready->claim->close subset the
      ticket explicitly permits — `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` (which runs
      `rebar init` explicitly and passes non-interactively) — NOT the full
      `probe-rebar.sh`. The broader probe was found to have PRE-EXISTING rot (relies
      on TTY-only auto-init + 10 stale assertions) that is out of this docs epic's
      scope; its fix-and-wire is tracked as discovered follow-up bug
      `slushy-commonlaw-drongo` (linked `discovered_from` this ticket). So T7 is
      addressed by tracking the rot honestly rather than wiring a red probe.

Depends on `a41f` (session-log fix) and `b55f` (quickstart repaired to a runnable
single-ticket block) — this gate extracts and runs the README quickstart, so it must land
AFTER those fix the text, or it would extract currently-broken commands and fail for the
wrong reason. (Dependency edges declared.)

Files: `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.sh` (new extractor), `scripts/probe-rebar.sh`
(retained/complementary), `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
baseline.summary: P0: Wire the existing golden-path probe into CI

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A ticket directory containing NO events — created by a write that never emitted its CREATE event — makes the plan-relation reducer error out, and that error surfaces as an INDETERMINATE verdict on plan reviews of OTHER, UNRELATED tickets. The blast radius is every ticket whose relation graph the snapshot walks, which in practice means an entire epic.

## Reproduced, then fixed, by removing the directory and nothing else

Running `rebar review-plan 5267-f026-0f2b-4c02`:

    verdict INDETERMINATE, exit 2, llm_ran: FALSE
    indeterminate[0] = {id: plan-relation-snapshot-error, reason: reducer-error,
                        canonical_id: None, reference: 0de5-6db1-8058-4e80}
    ERROR rebar.llm.plan_review: plan relation snapshot failed

`0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` was an EMPTY DIRECTORY in `.tickets-tracker` — `ls -A` returned 0 entries, `rebar show` reported `has no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event`. A second one, `4ab3-411d-9736-4a41`, was in the same state.

CRITICALLY, 5267 DOES NOT REFERENCE 0de5. Its only dep is `relates_to 208f-6e90-1326-403a`; the broken directory was reached by walking the epic's relation graph. A grep across the whole store for `0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` returned ZERO references from any ticket — nothing points at it at all.

After removing the two empty directories and changing nothing else, the SAME command on the SAME tree returned `verdict: PASS`, exit 0, attestation certified at ff295b9cf87. That is the causal proof: one variable changed.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than sweeping

* It is NOT transient. An earlier agent on this epic hit the same signature and recorded it as
  "transient store churn from a half-written ticket, retried clean". It is not churn — it persists
  until someone removes the directory, and a retry only appears to work if the racing writer happens
  to complete in the interim.
* The error names the BROKEN ticket, not the one being reviewed, so the failure looks like a problem
  with an unrelated ticket. That is a strong wrong-direction signal for anyone debugging it.
* It is invisible to git. Git cannot track empty directories, so the artifact never appears in
  `git status`, never reaches the tickets branch, and cannot be spotted by inspecting the shared
  history — it exists only in a local clone.
* The LLM never runs (`llm_ran: false`), so the gate fails closed with no spend. That is correct
  behaviour, but it means the whole epic's claims and closes stall on a filesystem artifact.

## Approach (not yet decided)

The reducer should tolerate a ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event rather than failing the whole snapshot — most plausibly by skipping it with a warning naming the path, since a directory with no events carries no information that a relation snapshot needs. Consider also whether the writer can avoid creating the directory before it has an event to put in it, which would remove the artifact at source.

Both directions should be weighed; tolerating the artifact is the smaller, safer change and fixes existing broken clones, while fixing the writer prevents new ones and does nothing for clones already carrying one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event does not fail the plan-relation snapshot; the
      review proceeds and the artifact is reported as a warning naming the offending path.
- [x] A test constructs an event-less ticket directory and asserts `review-plan` on an UNRELATED
      ticket still reaches a verdict; it fails before the fix.
- [x] It is decided and recorded whether the writer should also stop creating the directory before it
      has an event to write, with the reasoning either way.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: An event-less ticket directory fails the plan-relation reducer, turning unrelated plan reviews INDETERMINATE

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`_CASCADING_EDGES` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`) maps each cascading child edge to exactly one eligible parent status and moves the parent along the SAME edge. `docs/concurrency.md` §I4a's headline sentence ("A child never runs ahead of its parent in the lifecycle") overstates what that table guarantees: two reachable residuals — reactivating a `closed` child under a merely-`open` parent, and the `blocked -> in_progress` resume (absent from the table while the start-work gate fires on it) — do not cascade. The operator ruled (2026-08-21, recorded on this ticket) that both residuals are documented-intended behaviour and reclassified this bug -> task: what remains is reconciliation — narrow the §I4a headline to what the table actually guarantees, and resolve the blocked-resume gate/cascade disagreement one way or the other in the table/docs. A second recorded ruling (verbatim on bb73-97de-eeea-4899) binds the work: "no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket" is a required invariant.

## Approach
Keep the ENUMERATED EDGE TABLE; reject the ordering-predicate redesign (AC1's decision, recorded in §I4a and in the scope-restatement comment). The invariant the store actually enforces is the operator-ruled one — no non-terminal child under a closed ancestor — maintained jointly by the table's two closed-source rows and the unconditional open-children close guard in `transition_close.py` (which refuses, --force included, to close a parent over ANY non-closed child), not by a total status ordering. Then:

1. Rewrite §I4a's headline to state the per-edge, same-edge guarantee the table gives, plus the ruled store invariant it and the close guard maintain together.
2. Document residual 1 as accepted: `closed -> in_progress` under an `open` parent does not cascade — only a `closed` parent is eligible on that edge; an `in_progress` child under an `open` parent does not violate the ruled invariant; pinned by `test_reactivate_does_not_disturb_open_parent` (minnow AC2).
3. Resolve the blocked resume as DOCUMENTED NON-CASCADING, alongside the note that the start-work gate DOES fire on it: (a) a blocked child can never sit under a closed ancestor — the unconditional close guard prevents that state arising — so the resume cannot leave a closed ancestor behind; (b) the table's same-edge shape means only a `blocked` parent could be eligible on that edge, and auto-resuming a parent blocked for its own independent reason would be wrong; (c) the gate keys on TARGET `in_progress` by design (task 65e3) — the gate asks "is work starting?", the cascade asks "would this same-edge write leave an eligible ancestor behind?", so gate-fires + no-cascade is consistent once documented side by side.
4. Update the `_CASCADING_EDGES` comment block and the "never runs ahead" docstring phrasing in `transition.py` to match; the table's rows are byte-for-byte unchanged.
5. Add two pinning tests for the facts the doc now leans on.

No behaviour changes: no transition refused today becomes permitted, and the claim-status guard (`txn.claim_core`) is untouched.

## Scope
- `docs/concurrency.md` — §I4a narrowed headline, documented residuals, recorded AC1 decision.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — the `_CASCADING_EDGES` comment block and docstring phrasing only; no code-path change, table rows unchanged.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py` — two pinning tests.

## Testing
The behaviour already exists (ruled intended), so these are pinning tests making the documented residuals executable, run via the file's suite plus lint/typecheck/complexity ratchet:
- `test_blocked_resume_does_not_cascade_open_parent` — a child moved `open -> blocked -> in_progress` under an `open` parent succeeds and leaves the parent `open` (the documented residual, and the documented non-cascading resolution of AC3).
- `test_close_refused_over_blocked_child` — closing a parent over a `blocked` child raises with the unresolved-children message (the guard fact §I4a's blocked-resume reasoning leans on).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A decision is recorded on whether I4a's invariant is enforced by an ordering predicate or by an enumerated edge table. Checked: §I4a and the ticket's scope-restatement comment both record the decision (enumerated table retained) and its grounds.
- [x] Reactivating a closed child under an `open` parent either cascades, or `docs/concurrency.md` §I4a explicitly documents the residual as accepted, with the reason. Checked: §I4a documents it as accepted, citing `test_reactivate_does_not_disturb_open_parent`.
- [x] `blocked -> in_progress` either cascades, or is explicitly documented as non-cascading alongside the note that the start-work gate DOES fire on it. Checked: §I4a documents non-cascading with the three grounds, next to the gate note; `test_blocked_resume_does_not_cascade_open_parent` pins it.
- [x] No transition that is refused today becomes permitted; the claim-status guard is untouched. Checked: the diff touches no permission logic (`txn.claim_core` unmodified, `_CASCADING_EDGES` rows unchanged) and the full cascade suite passes without assertion edits.
baseline.summary: Cascade table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape leaves I4a states reachable

baseline.description:
Make the commit-trailer format + all CLI-served guides resolve for repo-less clients

## Context / Problem

Clients using the `rebar` CLI **without a rebar checkout** hit dead ends in CLI-served prose. Today's commit `c2bfbe217` packaged the two author guides into `src/rebar/_guides/` so `rebar explain plan|review` serves them from any install — but it left the guides' **internal cross-references** as consumer-relative paths (`review-policy.md`, `review-kernel.md`, `../CONTRIBUTING.md`, `plan-review-gate.md`, `plan-review-criteria-guide.md`, `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md`, `AGENTS.md`), which dangle for a consumer with no such tree — the same class of dead-consumer-link bug that `62933ff62` fixed for plan-review deep-links ("client report §5"). Separately, the required `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit-trailer format (`EXPECTED_FORMAT` in `verify_commit.py`) has **no** CLI-discoverable home at all: only `rebar verify-commit-ticket --help` prints it, and nothing points there. The remediation was not comprehensive.

## Approach

Two moves, both grounded in conventions already in this repo:

1. **Give the trailer a first-class CLI home.** Add a third packaged author guide,
   `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md`, registered as the `commit-trailer` topic in
   `AUTHOR_GUIDES` (`registry.py`) — served offline by `rebar explain commit-trailer` and the
   MCP `explain_guide` tool, exactly like `plan`/`review`. It quotes `EXPECTED_FORMAT` verbatim
   (drift-pinned by test) plus how-to-self-check prose (`rebar verify-commit-ticket`).

2. **Repoint every dangling reference in the packaged guides** so it resolves for a repo-less
   consumer, using the established two-way convention: sibling packaged guides →
   `rebar explain <topic>`; repo-only docs → the canonical hosted base
   `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/blob/main/…` (the same base `62933ff62`'s
   `_DEFAULT_DOCS_URL` and pyproject `[project.urls] Documentation` already use).

Then lock it with a guard test asserting no packaged `_guides/*.md` link target is a consumer-relative path (only `https://`, intra-doc `#anchor`, or `rebar explain` are allowed) — so the remediation stays comprehensive. Rejected: a bespoke `rebar trailer-format` subcommand (`explain` is already the on-ramp for `plan`/`review`; a third topic needs no new wiring); rejected shipping the whole `docs/` tree in the wheel (heavy; hosted URLs already resolve).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` — NEW packaged guide; quotes `EXPECTED_FORMAT`
  verbatim + `rebar verify-commit-ticket` self-check prose; links only via `https://`/`rebar explain`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `"commit-trailer"` → the new file in `AUTHOR_GUIDES`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — the MCP `explain_criterion` tool docstring hardcodes the guide
  list (`plan`/`review`); add `commit-trailer` so MCP clients discover it (the tool dispatch at
  L63 already reads `AUTHOR_GUIDES` dynamically — only the human-facing docstring lags).
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — repoint L5 review-policy/review-kernel + L6/L39
  CONTRIBUTING to hosted URLs; L8 sibling → `rebar explain plan`; L35 trailer →
  `rebar explain commit-trailer` + `rebar verify-commit-ticket --help`.
- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` — repoint L6 criteria-guide + L7
  plan-review-gate to hosted URLs; L8 sibling → `rebar explain review`.
- `tests/unit/test_verify_commit_ticket.py` — drift assertion (packaged guide quotes
  `EXPECTED_FORMAT`).
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py` — `rebar explain commit-trailer` returns the format;
  unknown-guide error lists it; LINK-RESOLUTION guard test (below); a guard asserting every
  `AUTHOR_GUIDES` key is named in the MCP `explain_criterion` docstring (so the MCP guide list
  can't silently drift from the registry again).
- `tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py` — make the existing `test_wheel_ships_author_guides` iterate
  `AUTHOR_GUIDES` (not a hardcoded pair) so the new guide — and any future one — is packaging-
  guarded automatically.
- `AGENTS.md` — one-line pointer to `rebar explain commit-trailer` in the trailer bullet.
- `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` — note the CLI discovery paths.

## Testing

- Happy: `registry.explain_guide("commit-trailer")` and CLI `rebar explain commit-trailer` both
  return text containing `EXPECTED_FORMAT` (exit 0).
- Edge: unknown guide name raises `ExplainError("unknown-id", …)` whose message now lists
  `commit-trailer`.
- Drift: the packaged guide contains `EXPECTED_FORMAT` verbatim.
- Link-resolution guard (the core regression-proofing): a single test enumerates ALL
  in-command help prose a repo-less client can see — every registered `AUTHOR_GUIDES` guide
  body AND every `explain_criterion(<id>)` rendering — extracts every markdown link `](target)`,
  and asserts each target RESOLVES for a non-rebar client. The one canonical allow-list, used
  everywhere: a target is OK iff it starts with `https://`, `http://`, `#` (intra-doc anchor),
  or `mailto:`. Any consumer-relative path (`](*.md)`, `](docs/…)`, `](../…)`) FAILS. A second
  axis scans the packaged guide bodies (only) for bare parenthetical/inline repo paths
  (`docs/…`, `../…`) not part of a hosted `…/blob/main/…` URL — catching non-hyperlink dead
  references the `](…)` regex misses. It also validates every `rebar explain <topic>` mentioned
  in that prose names a real registered guide/criterion, so the reachable-pointer claim can't
  rot. Driven by the registries (not a hardcoded file list) so new guides/criteria are covered
  automatically.
- Full `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar explain commit-trailer` exits 0 and prints the canonical trailer format (run it;
      CLI unit test asserts `EXPECTED_FORMAT` in stdout).
- [ ] `commit-trailer` is listed among known guides in `rebar explain` help and the
      `unknown-id` error (unit test).
- [ ] The packaged `commit-ticket-trailer.md` quotes `EXPECTED_FORMAT` verbatim (drift test).
- [ ] The link-resolution guard passes: across every `AUTHOR_GUIDES` guide body and every
      `explain_criterion(<id>)` rendering, no markdown link target is consumer-relative (allowed
      set is exactly `https://`/`http://`/`#anchor`/`mailto:`), no packaged guide has a bare
      `docs/…`/`../…` path, and every `rebar explain <topic>` cited names a real registered
      guide/criterion (test passes; verified by grep too).
- [ ] `rebar explain review` and `rebar explain plan` no longer reference repo-relative files;
      sibling guides read as `rebar explain <topic>`, repo docs as `https://github.com/navapbc/…`
      — confirmed by the link-resolution guard passing (a manual read may spot-check readability).
- [ ] `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` names `rebar explain commit-trailer` and
      `rebar verify-commit-ticket` as CLI discovery paths (grep the file).
- [ ] The MCP `explain_criterion` tool docstring names `commit-trailer`, and a guard test
      asserts every `AUTHOR_GUIDES` key appears in that docstring (test passes).
- [ ] AGENTS.md's trailer bullet names `rebar explain commit-trailer` (grep).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` all pass (run them).
baseline.summary: Make commit-trailer format + CLI-served guides resolve for repo-less clients

## Problem

`rebar claim` (and its library/MCP equivalents) can only claim a ticket whose current status is `open`. `claim_core` (src/rebar/_commands/txn.py, ~L449-455) reads the reduced state and hard-rejects anything else:

```python
actual_status = state.get("status", "")
if actual_status != "open":
    raise ConcurrencyMismatch(
        f'Error: cannot claim {ticket_id}: status is "{actual_status}", not "open" ...'
    )
```

## Observed impact

While closing landed work we found tickets left in `blocked` status with an assignee already set (e.g. b783, c7d5, f643, 7a03 — assignee joeoakhart@navapbc.com, status blocked). Because `claim` fast-fails on any non-`open` status, there was no supported way to (re)claim these to resume/finish work; the only remaining lever was a raw `transition`. A ticket that legitimately moved to `blocked` (including via Jira reconcile now that `blocked` is a valid live-Jira status) becomes unclaimable even by the agent that should own it.

## Expected behavior

`claim` should be able to move a ticket into `in_progress` from ANY non-terminal status (at least `open` and `blocked`; consider `idea` per ticket-model rules), setting/refreshing the assignee to `ticket.default_assignee`, rather than being hard-wired to `open` only.

Special consideration — avoid claim duplication:
- A ticket ALREADY `in_progress` and assigned to SOMEONE ELSE must still raise ConcurrencyMismatch/exit 10 (do not steal an active claim).
- A ticket already `in_progress` and assigned to the SAME caller should be an idempotent no-op (not a spurious concurrency error).
- Preserve the parent-first cascade and the atomic single-commit STATUS+EDIT invariant (I2/I8, docs/concurrency.md).

## Root cause

The status guard in `claim_core` encodes `open` as the sole claimable source status. The allowable-source set should be widened (open + blocked, and any other non-terminal claimable statuses) with in-progress ownership disambiguation, single-sourced with whatever `transition` treats as claimable.

## Notes

Out of scope for the session that discovered this. Filed for later triage.
baseline.summary: claim only accepts open-status tickets; cannot re-claim blocked (or other non-terminal) tickets

## Broken base: `/health` lifespan test asserts a stale exact dict (missing `queue_depth`)

`origin/main` HEAD is **red on CI** (ubuntu py3.12, wherever `fastapi` is installed) due to a semantic conflict between two independently-landed Gerrit changes:

- `2bda965db6` (**9f63**) added `queue_depth` to the `/health` response body — intentional and
  documented (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:274`):
  `return {"status": "ok", "in_flight": _voter.in_flight_reviews(), "queue_depth": queue_depth}`
- `4c89592d88` ("test: make review-bot lifespan safe") added
  `test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs`
  (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1449`) asserting **exact** equality:
  `assert response.json() == {"status": "ok", "in_flight": 0}` — missing `queue_depth`.

Each change passed `Verified +1` in isolation; Rebase-If-Necessary submitted them without re-running the combined suite, so the merged tip fails. It skips locally when `fastapi` is absent (why neither author caught it).

**This deterministically fails EVERY change's CI**, so it must be fixed on `main` before any in-flight change (fc0c change 1528, etc.) can earn `Verified +1`.

### Fix
The endpoint's `queue_depth` key is intentional (bug 9f63); the test's exact-match assertion is stale. Update the assertion to include the intentional key: `assert response.json() == {"status": "ok", "in_flight": 0, "queue_depth": 0}`.

### Acceptance criteria
- AC1: `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs`
  passes with `fastapi` installed.
- AC2: The assertion accounts for all three intentional `/health` keys (`status`, `in_flight`,
  `queue_depth`) — no key dropped, no behavior changed in `app.py`.
- AC3: No other review-bot test regresses.
baseline.summary: Fix stale /health lifespan test blocking all CI

# DC's comment ceiling is admin-configurable and rebar hardcodes the default

## The defect

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` `sanitize_comment` truncates comment bodies at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767), a compile-time constant. On Jira Data Center that ceiling is the default of the admin-settable property `jira.text.field.character.limit`, whose documented range is `0` (unlimited) to `2147483647`.

So on an instance where an administrator has RAISED the limit or set it to `0`, rebar truncates comments that Jira would have accepted in full. **That is data loss, and it is silent to the author of the comment** — the operator sees a truncation warning (`jira_family/sanitizers.py:143-148`), which is why this is low-severity rather than invisible, but the text is still gone from the remote and the local/remote bodies then differ permanently.

This is NOT the "32767 is the wrong number" defect that was originally suspected and is now refuted (see below). It is narrower: the number is right for a STOCK instance and wrong for a CONFIGURED one.

## Established provenance (so nobody re-litigates the number)

`jira.text.field.character.limit`, from Jira's own `jpm.xml`:

    description: "The maximum number of characters to be entered for a single field.
                  Affects Description, Environment, Comments and Text custom fields.
                  0 means unlimited."
    default-value: 32767

Corroborated by JRASERVER-28519 (Resolved/Fixed, fix versions 6.4.1 / 7.0.0): "starting with JIRA 7.0 and Cloud, `jira.text.field.character.limit` will be set to 32767 by default." The DC admin page "Configuring advanced settings" confirms the property, its field scope, `0` = unlimited and the 2147483647 maximum, but does NOT state the default.

Comments and text custom fields share ONE property and therefore one number, by design — so binding DC's comment limit to the same constant as its description limit is structurally faithful to DC, and must not be "fixed" by inventing a separate comment number.

Evidence the ceiling bites people in practice: JRASERVER-64351 has 86 votes from users hitting it, which is also the population most likely to have raised the limit.

## Why the fix is not simply "read the limit"

`/rest/api/2/application-properties` plausibly exposes the key, but **whether it is readable by a non-admin PAT is NOT established and must be tested, not assumed.** rebar authenticates as an ordinary user on DC. If the property is admin-only, discovery is unavailable and the remedy is configuration only.

## Proposed remediation, cheapest first

1. Make the DC comment ceiling CONFIGURABLE, defaulting to 32767. This alone closes the data-loss
   window for any operator who knows their instance's setting.
2. OPTIONALLY probe `application-properties` at connect time and log a warning when the instance's
   value disagrees with the configured one. Gate this on actually confirming the endpoint is readable
   by rebar's credential.
3. Do NOT change the default. It is correct for stock Jira >= 7.0 and matches every independent
   implementation surveyed (carrier-io/dusty annotates its own 32767 as "the
   jira.text.field.character.limit default value").

No surveyed OSS integration queries the live limit — all hardcode — so (1) brings rebar to parity with the field and (2) would make it more correct than the field.

## Two latent traps worth fixing in the same area (not themselves data loss today)

* The constant is named `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` and the comment at `jira_family/rich_text.py:56-60`
  attributes the number to Cloud comment limits, which REVERSES the actual causality. Renaming it
  and citing the property would stop the code asserting a false provenance.
* `sanitize_comment` reuses `fit_outbound`, the DESCRIPTION fitter. Harmless today (plain character
  truncation) but Cloud shows why the coupling is dangerous: Cloud's description fitter is
  ADF-SIZE-based (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` = 32000 ADF chars, fitted empirically because
  `text_to_adf` inflates — a 32767-char description was observed serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars)
  and would be catastrophically wrong applied to comments. Any future change to the DC description
  fitter silently retargets comments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the DC comment ceiling is settable by configuration, defaulting to 32767, with the default's
      provenance (`jira.text.field.character.limit` + JRASERVER-28519) cited at the binding
- [x] a comment longer than the configured ceiling but shorter than a raised one is NOT truncated
      when the ceiling is configured upward, proven by a RED-first unit test
- [x] the readability of `/rest/api/2/application-properties` by rebar's non-admin PAT is RECORDED
      WITH ITS EVIDENTIARY STATUS LABELLED, discovery is dropped, and that is stated at the binding.
      **AMENDED — the original wording required an EMPIRICAL determination and the answer obtained is
      DOCUMENTARY** (Atlassian's permission documentation for the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource,
      where `jira.text.field.character.limit` is exposed). No 403 was captured, because the
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc` harness image is linux/amd64 only and never became usable on the
      arm64 host in three measured attempts. The amendment is justified on two grounds recorded in
      full in this ticket's AC-verification comment: (1) the remedy is INDEPENDENT of the answer — a
      readable endpoint would enable an OPTIONAL auto-discovery layer ON TOP of the config key, never
      a replacement, so the outstanding measurement cannot invalidate what landed; (2) the
      measurement is DEFERRED, not dropped — it is runnable on the amd64 `jira-dc-harness` CI job and
      is filed as [rebar:275e-81a4-f11a-4b5b] (linked `discovered_from` here), which writes its
      outcome back onto this ticket
- [x] `sanitize_comment` no longer depends on the description fitter, so a change to description
      fitting cannot retarget comments
- [x] mutation-checked: reverting the configurability turns the new test red for the right reason
baseline.summary: DC comment ceiling is admin-configurable; rebar hardcodes the default

## Context / Problem

Teams running several tracker projects against one codebase (or several repos against one ticket store) cannot use the bridge: it is hard-wired to exactly one project at three points — `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`_config_schema.py`), the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one (`fetcher.jqls_for`), and the applier aborts a pass when any outbound mutation targets a key outside that project (`applier.CrossProjectTargetError`). The only escape is the destructive one-way `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`. Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff` and taken as a dependency, not duplicated here.

(Full original description with line-anchored citations preserved verbatim as a ticket comment, 2026-08-13.)

## Approach

Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects. Each ticket records the project it syncs into and the repos it belongs to.

The STORE owns the project set — `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the tickets branch beside `bindings.json`/`prev_snapshot.json`. Reason (mechanical): `prev_snapshot.json` is last-known-remote state; if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would diff the other's projects as remote deletions. A store-owned project set removes that failure mode by construction and leaves no per-repo list to disagree.

Built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`) and the backend-neutral port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)`, `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`. `Backend.project` ("the backend's effective write/create project scope") is the per-repo default for rebar-created tickets; no new config key; generalizes beyond Jira.

Migration writes NO events. The ticket project field is tri-state — absent=legacy, explicit-empty= never sync, explicit key=sync there — mirroring `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths (`docs/ticket-model.md`). Absent resolves against the legacy default recorded in the mapping, seeded by an idempotent check-then-act ensure unit (`docs/migrations.md`, the sanctioned seam; the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built). A per-ticket EDIT migration was rejected: four-figure event writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot entry runs the ensure sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended — an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + the ensure seed. Delivers migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`. Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces; promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out + snapshot union; per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project. Delivers two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create; guard relaxed from single project to set membership. Delivers explicit-project + guard criteria.
- **Store-compat capability stamp** — conditional `required_capabilities` entry + fail-closed read. Delivers final criterion.
- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: rehearse against two live Jira Cloud projects on an
  isolated tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`,
  hence the depends_on); dry-run-gated, all created issues removed. Fixtures cannot reach the
  cross-project contamination failure mode this validates.
- **Module-size relief** — several files this feature edits sit within ~30 lines of the 800 hard cap.
  Behaviour-preserving extractions along existing seams, each ordered ahead of the story needing room;
  they deliver no epic criterion (preconditions; their own criteria are unchanged suite + measured LOC).

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive at every layer. Absent project = legacy; a pre-feature store behaves as today, no operator action. A single-project store never receives the capability stamp, so older binaries keep working; only a genuinely multi-project store fails closed on them — the intended protection (an older binary would fetch its one project, see other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicates in the wrong project). Rollback is per-change on Gerrit; the mapping and capability entry are inert to older binaries apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to implicit-legacy with the idempotent ensure re-stamping on the next covered write.
baseline.summary: Many-to-many tracker projects: per-ticket bridge project + repo association over one shared store

## Why

## What
Build eval specs for the four-pass code-review prompts (base, overlays, verify) in the existing rebar eval harness. Seed two families from dso's documented corpus:

## Acceptance Criteria

## Summary

rebar documents a relocatable ticket store as a supported feature, then bypasses its own resolver in 13 shipped code paths, each assuming the store sits at `repo_root/.tickets-tracker`. Any deployment that relocates the store — which the deployed MCP server does — breaks in those paths, with errors naming a path the operator never configured.

## The contract being ignored

`src/rebar/config.py:138-156` (`tracker_dir()`): the env override `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` "wins verbatim"; otherwise the configured `tracker.dir` applies, where "an absolute value relocates the store (EV-3b)". Relocation is a FEATURE, not an edge case.

## Observed failure (live Copilot session)

    bridge_status -> "cannot read local environment id from
     /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code/.tickets-tracker/.env-id: [Errno 2] No such file or directory"

The server sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`; the store is there and healthy — 2763 tickets are readable through the same server.

## Root cause (CONFIRMED at runtime)

`_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:89` composes `repo_root / ".tickets-tracker" / ".env-id"`; the caller `_lib_ops.py:288` passes the repo root, never the resolved tracker. The constant at `:35` has the same defect for the detail file. Reproduced against a CONTROL arm: same env, same store, `rebar list` succeeds (rc=0) while `rebar bridge status` fails.

Attributed to `b69c-5787-81b8-4052` via commit `fe5a447061cde`. `config.tracker_dir()` already carried the relocation contract at that commit's PARENT, so this is a `plan_defect`, not a regression or unmet obligation.

**Triage of all 77 `.tickets-tracker` occurrences (13 defects / 64 legitimate), the caller-dependency sweep, and the RED evidence are in the ticket COMMENTS.**

## Acceptance Criteria

Each confirmed sibling is its own criterion, ordered by MCP reachability.

**Tier 1 — MCP-reachable and mutating**

- [x] AC1: `binding_store.py:601` (`load_binding_store`) resolves the binding read/write root.
- [x] AC2: `reconcile.py:318` resolves the `prev_snapshot.json` root (and `ctx.tracker_dir`,
      consumed by `run_differs.py:434`).
- [x] AC3: `reconcile.py:456` `check_store_compat` validates the CONFIGURED store, so the
      fail-closed precheck cannot be defeated by relocation.
- [x] AC4: `dispatch_one.py:321` writes `BRIDGE_ALERT` events into the configured store rather
      than materializing a shadow store at the repo root.
- [x] AC5: `git_adapter.py:75` + consumer `reconcile_helpers.py:234` stage the commit-back from
      the configured store. `TRACKER_DIR` is PRESERVED (exported in `__all__`, pinned by
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_git_adapter_characterization.py:35`); only the consumer
      changes.
- [x] AC6: `_bridge_runner.py:180` passes the RESOLVED tracker to the delivery subprocess.
- [x] AC7: `projects_store.py:47` reads and writes the sync mapping in the configured store.

**Tier 2 — MCP-reachable, read/diagnostic**

- [x] AC8: `last_pass.py:35` resolves the last-pass detail file.
- [x] AC9: `last_pass.py:89` reads `.env-id` from the configured store.
- [x] AC10: `inbound_translate.py:165` honours the `tracker.dir` key, not only the env override.
- [x] AC11: `__main__.py:239` (reconcile-check) loads local tickets from the configured store.

**Tier 3 — CLI-only**

- [x] AC12: `bridge_fsck.py:663` CLI fallback honours the `tracker.dir` key.
- [x] AC13: `__main__.py:508` dry-run enumeration errors rather than silently reporting an
      empty store when relocated.

**Cross-cutting**

- [x] AC14: This criterion CREATES `scripts/check_tickets_boundary.py` and wires it into the
      `lint` target of the `Makefile`. It rejects new store-path composition in `src/`,
      enforcing the existing `# tickets-boundary-ok` convention with a MANDATORY reason. The 64

## Context
The first live close after direct gated-close instrumentation produced authoritative timings at merged SHA 585888b7a0d4: `pre_verifier_total_ms=21971`, `verifier_call_ms=423502`, `llm_ms=175487.6`, `det_ms=10220.7`, and verifier `total_ms=185758.6`. Therefore 237743.4 ms inside the existing `verify_with_auto_resume` call is not explained by the verifier runtime metrics. That remainder must stay explicitly unattributed until direct boundaries identify it.

## Performance constraint
Instrumentation must only time already-existing synchronous sections with `time.monotonic_ns()`, integer arithmetic, and cheap dictionary assignments/counter increments. It must add no file or tracker read/write, Git subprocess, network/model call, retry, sleep, tracing backend, worker, lock, extra traversal, or new sidecar/event. Metrics must piggyback on the existing `COMPLETION_VERDICT.metrics` payload and existing write.

## Investigation and implementation plan
- Map the exact call graph and timing ownership from the close wrapper through `verify_with_auto_resume`, gate dispatch, workflow execution, auto-resume, enrichment/drain, verdict normalization, signing inputs, and sidecar emission.
- Identify every existing synchronous segment included by `verifier_call_ms` but excluded from the inner verifier `total_ms`; do not name a cause from subtraction alone.
- Add direct monotonic phase timers at the smallest stable call-graph seams that form a closed partition of the wrapper interval. Thread one optional metrics collector through existing calls so callers without it remain unchanged.
- Preserve current consumption/runtime metrics. Add workload counts needed to interpret repeated passes, resume rounds, drain attempts, or equivalent existing work without adding traversal.
- Update the reusable duration probe to prefer the direct fields and report any arithmetic remainder only as explicitly unattributed.
- Add RED-first synthetic tests for propagation, partition arithmetic, existing-metric preservation, optional compatibility, no-extra-work behavior, and direct/legacy probe output.
- Re-run the standard-library bookkeeping microbenchmark and repository gates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A model-backed PASS sidecar directly attributes the synchronous phases inside `verifier_call_ms`.
- [x] A model-backed FAIL sidecar directly attributes the same phases.
- [x] Named direct child phases plus explicitly measured wrapper overhead reconcile to `verifier_call_ms` with a maximum discrepancy of one millisecond per summed phase, capped at 10 ms; any larger difference is emitted as `unattributed_verifier_ms`.
- [x] Any remainder is labeled `unattributed` and is not assigned a causal operation name.
- [x] Existing `llm_ms`, `det_ms`, and `total_ms` remain unchanged.
- [x] Existing request, tool-call, and consumption metrics remain unchanged.
- [x] Existing repeated-pass/resume/drain workload is counted during the same traversal or calls that already perform it.
- [x] Instrumentation adds no I/O, subprocess, network/model call, tracker event/write, retry, sleep, tracing, worker, or lock.
- [x] Existing callers behave unchanged when no optional collector is supplied.
- [x] The duration probe reports direct wrapper phases and preserves legacy rows without causal inference.
- [x] Synthetic tests fail on current main and pass after implementation.
- [x] Complete added bookkeeping remains below 50 microseconds per close in a standard-library microbenchmark.
- [x] Focused tests pass.
- [x] The script import walk passes.
- [x] Lint and typecheck pass.
- [x] The default non-integration, non-external test suite passes.
- [x] This change edits neither `AGENTS.md` nor agent-duration guidance; any expectation update remains a separate follow-up after an adequate cohort and explicit user confirmation.

## Context / Problem

The project routing overlay (`.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, `code_review` section) can today only define standalone `project.*` criteria; it cannot extend a BUILT-IN overlay's triggers. `registry.glob_triggered_overlays` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:256) reads only the committed routing via `applies_to_globs` (registry.py:236), and `registry.content_triggered_overlays` (registry.py:321) is hardcoded to the deletion-impact removed-declaration regex. The parent epic's two-layer trigger design (committed high-precision tier / project noisy tier) requires a project to be able to add trigger vocabulary to a built-in overlay — starting with `concurrency`, but the mechanism is overlay-id-agnostic (a project could equally add tokens to `performance`).

## Approach

Extend the `code_review` side of the project overlay so an entry keyed by a BUILT-IN overlay id (a member of `OVERLAY_IDS`, registry.py:38) may carry two additive keys: `trigger_tokens` — a list of literal substrings matched case-sensitively against the added and removed lines of the unified diff (file headers `+++`/`---` excluded) — and `applies_to` globs, unioned with the committed globs. Consumption path (decided): these additive keys are deliberately NOT read through `effective_routing` — its built-in merge is per-key overlay-wins (`{**merged[cid], **entry}`, src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:362), so a project `applies_to` read from the merged view would REPLACE the committed globs, the opposite of the additive semantics this mechanism needs. Instead, add a small helper in registry.py (e.g. `project_trigger_extensions(repo_root) -> dict[str, dict]`) that reads the project overlay's raw `code_review` entries directly (via the existing loader in `rebar.llm.criteria.overlay`; `_validate_routing_entry` already tolerates unknown keys, so no loader change) and returns, per built-in overlay id, the `trigger_tokens` and `applies_to` lists. `glob_triggered_overlays` and `content_triggered_overlays` union the helper's values with the committed ones, threading `repo_root` from the single call site `workflow_ops.overlay_union` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:98-99). `effective_routing` and its replace semantics stay untouched — it continues to govern thresholds/postures only. Positive rationale: this mirrors the plan-review side's proven project trigger mechanism (`trigger.text_all` on `project.engine-layer-enforcement` in this repo's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`), and literal substrings — not regex — keep the gate a simple filter that is cheap to author and impossible to catastrophically misparse, matching the trigger's filter-not-finder role. ADR 0074 semantics are preserved: for `project.*` ids, empty `applies_to` still means ungated (`project_criterion_applies`, registry.py:282); for built-in ids the project keys are an additive union, so with no project entry present both functions behave exactly as today (committed `applies_to` empty still means escalation-only).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — token-matching helper; `effective_routing` consumption in both trigger functions.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — thread `repo_root` into the trigger calls in `overlay_union`.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py` — NEW module for the code-review trigger-extension cases (the existing `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py` covers only the plan_review side of the overlay loader, and `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` covers the committed content trigger; neither is the right home for project-extension cases, and this module will also host the sibling stories' trigger tests).

Documentation of the mechanism is delivered by the sibling dogfood story (it documents mechanism and worked example together).

## Testing

Unit tier (pure in-process functions plus a `tmp_path` repo fixture writing a project `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`; no live boundary, so one tier lower does not exist). Oracle: the returned overlay-id lists.

- Happy path: a project entry on a built-in overlay id with `trigger_tokens: ["FROBNICATE("]` causes `content_triggered_overlays` to return that id for a diff whose added line contains the token.
- Removed-line path: the same token on a removed (`-`) line also fires.
- Glob union: project `applies_to` globs on a built-in id fire `glob_triggered_overlays` for a matching changed file that the committed globs do not match.
- Negative control: with no project overlay present, both functions return their current results — anchored on the PRE-EXISTING corpus in `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` (which exercises `content_triggered_overlays` with no project overlay) passing unmodified, plus an explicit no-overlay case in the new module.
- Malformed input: a non-list `trigger_tokens`, a non-string token, or an entry under an unknown id is ignored without raising.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A tmp project overlay declaring `trigger_tokens` on a built-in overlay id causes `content_triggered_overlays` to return that id for a diff containing the token on an added OR removed line; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py`.
- [x] Project `applies_to` globs on a built-in id union with the committed globs in `glob_triggered_overlays` (both the committed-glob match and the project-glob match fire); checked by the same module.
- [x] Negative control: with no project overlay, both trigger functions produce byte-identical results to current behavior — the pre-existing tests in `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` pass unmodified, and the new module asserts the no-overlay case directly.
- [x] Malformed project entries (non-list `trigger_tokens`, non-string token, unknown id) are ignored at consumption, not raised; checked by unit test.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` all pass.
baseline.summary: Project-extensible triggers for built-in code-review overlays (trigger_tokens + applies_to union)

Found while validating mechanical-coherent-wolverine's premise (23b2-1a94-6a01-466b).

## Report

`rebar._commands.txn.transition_core` declares `force_close_reason: str = ""` at `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:198` and **never reads it**. The identifier occurs exactly once in the whole file — the parameter declaration itself.

The caller does supply a real value: `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:474` passes `force_close_reason=force_close`, the string an operator typed into `--force=<reason>`. It is accepted, threaded one call deep into the locked write, and silently dropped before it reaches the STATUS event.

## Premise verified in current `origin/main`

* `txn.py:198` — the parameter, declared with a default and never referenced again.
* `transition_close.py:474` — the caller passing it.
* `txn.py:277-296` — the close STATUS event `data`: `status`, `current_status`,
  `parent_status_uuid`, and present-only `close_class`. No reason field of any kind.
* `transition_close.py:511-521` — the ONLY durable trace of a force-close reason today is a
  best-effort `FORCE_CLOSE` audit comment written AFTER the close, via a SECOND lock
  acquisition, and swallowed on failure with only a `logger.warning`.

That last point is what makes this more than tidiness. Force-closing is most attractive precisely when gates or the store are contended — and that is exactly when the second lock acquisition is most likely to time out and take the bypass reason with it, while the parameter designed to record it durably, in the write that already holds the lock, sits unused.

## Direction

Write the reason into the close STATUS event, mirroring `close_class` — which is the exact same shape of datum (a present-only, close-only string) and already has a complete, proven path through the system:

| step | `close_class` (precedent) | `force_close_reason` (this change) |
|---|---|---|
| event write | `txn.py:287-288`, present-only so an absent value omits the key and stays byte-identical to a pre-feature event | same guard, same place |
| reducer fold | `_fold_close_class`, called at BOTH `*->closed` edges (`reducer/_processors.py:203`, `:274` fork-winner, `:301` plain) | a sibling fold at the same two sites |
| reduced state | declared in `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json:187` | declared alongside it |

Present-only matters for the same reason it did for `close_class`: a close with no `--force` omits the key entirely, so ordinary close events are unchanged byte-for-byte and an older reader that does not know the field is unaffected.

**Alternative considered and rejected: delete the parameter as dead.** That is smaller and would also satisfy "no caller silently passes a discarded value". It is rejected because the caller has a genuinely useful value to record, the operator supplied it expressly to explain a gate bypass, and the existing audit-comment path is unreliable under exactly the conditions that produce force-closes. Deleting would lock in the weaker of the two records.

Scope note: this does NOT add wolverine's `completion_expectation` enum, its derivation table, or any computation of gate state. This is one present-only string moved from a discarded parameter into the event that already carries `close_class`. The two tickets touch the same event and should be sequenced, not merged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A `--force=<reason>` close records that reason on the close STATUS event, written in the
      SAME locked write as the close with no additional lock acquisition — verified by a test
      reading the event
- [x] The reason is readable from reduced state by a later reader holding no lock — verified by
      a test
- [x] A close WITHOUT `--force` omits the key entirely, leaving the event byte-identical to the
      pre-change shape — verified by a test asserting absence
- [x] No caller passes a value that `transition_core` discards — verified by a test that would
      fail if the parameter were reintroduced as unused
baseline.summary: force_close_reason is accepted by transition_core and discarded
