# Re-home the CLAUDE.md-native ticket-model content into authoritative docs

## Why

Slimming the root guidance file (S2) requires the ticket-model content it currently owns to have an authoritative home in `docs/` first, so nothing is lost when the root file becomes a set of pointers. This story creates/extends the docs so every ticket-model topic is documented in `docs/` independently of the root file.

## What

Produce the following documentation END STATE (this story is judged by what `docs/` contains afterward, not by which source paragraph moved where):

- A new **`docs/ticket-model.md`** that documents, for agents, the four ticket-model concepts:
  the `idea` status lifecycle (dispatch/gate/`validate` semantics), hierarchy/containment
  (`parent_id`, not a link relation), linking (the six relations + the blocking-link promotion
  concept), and the tags surface (including the `--set-tags` add-wins convergence caveat). It
  cross-references `docs/event-schema.md` for the underlying event mechanics instead of restating
  event bodies (avoids drift).
- `docs/concurrency.md` (the I4a cascade section) additionally documents the cascade's **gate
  interaction**: a cascaded parent claim runs the parent's own plan-review claim gate; epics/
  stories are not gate-exempt; `--force` propagates up the cascade.
- `docs/event-schema.md` contains a dedicated `## The session_log ticket type` section describing
  the type semantics (gate/lifecycle-exempt, graph/health-excluded, non-blocking links only,
  never Jira-synced), and no longer defers those semantics to the root file.
- `docs/user-guide.md` documents the session-log **auto-rotation** behavior (the
  `.rebar/current_session_log` pointer + session fingerprint).
- `docs/README.md` indexes `docs/ticket-model.md`.

## Scope

In: `docs/ticket-model.md` (new) and `docs/{event-schema,concurrency,user-guide,README}.md`. Out: editing the root guidance file (that is S2, which replaces these sections with pointers) and any code change. Docs-only; rollback is a plain `git revert`.

## Design decisions (spike-validated)

A grounded docs read established that most ticket-model *mechanics* already live in `docs/event-schema.md` (LINK/UNLINK, TAG_DELTA, CREATE genesis) and the cascade in `docs/concurrency.md` I4a — only the `idea` status is wholly unhomed. So the new `docs/ticket-model.md` carries the agent-facing *concept* with cross-refs, and the other docs get three targeted gap-fills (the cascade gate nuance, a real session_log section, the auto-rotation detail) rather than a bulk copy. Framing each criterion as an end-state the result must satisfy keeps the plan verifiable by inspecting the produced docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/ticket-model.md` exists and documents idea-status, hierarchy/containment, linking
  (relations + promotion), and the tags surface incl. `--set-tags`, with a cross-ref to
  `docs/event-schema.md` and no restated event bodies.
  - Proving: `test -f docs/ticket-model.md && [ "$(rg -c 'idea|parent_id|discovered_from|set-tags' docs/ticket-model.md)" -ge 4 ] && rg -q 'event-schema' docs/ticket-model.md`
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the cascade's gate interaction (parent's own plan-review
  gate; epics/stories not gate-exempt; `--force`).
  - Proving (both strings are absent from concurrency.md today, so this fails until the section is added): `rg -q 'gate-exempt' docs/concurrency.md && rg -q 'plan-review' docs/concurrency.md`
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` has a `## The session_log ticket type` section and does not defer
  session_log semantics to the root file.
  - Proving: `rg -q '## The session_log ticket type' docs/event-schema.md`
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` documents session-log auto-rotation (currently absent).
  - Proving: `rg -q 'auto-rotat|current_session_log' docs/user-guide.md`
- [ ] `docs/README.md` indexes `docs/ticket-model.md`.
  - Proving: `rg -q 'ticket-model' docs/README.md`
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
  - Proving: `make lint`
baseline.summary: Re-home CLAUDE.md-native content into authoritative docs

## Problem
Found during the Step 7 parity census of bug `dystopian-bardlike-basil` (d319-a094-4ee7-4549).

`.github/complexity-baseline.README.md` §"Updating the baseline (draining stale debt)" says:

> To remove stale entries or lower ceilings **after refactoring**, run:
> `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --update-stale`

That reads as an instruction to the contributor who just refactored. `AGENTS.md` says the opposite — `--lock`/`--update-stale` are "maintenance-only, not a contributor's escape hatch".

## Why it is a doc-parity gap, not the same defect
This is NOT what caused the local/CI split in d319 (that was three tree-scoped assertions in `tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py`, fixed there). Both statements are individually true: the CI `--lock` step genuinely allows lowered ceilings and removed entries to pass freely, so a contributor CAN commit a drained baseline. The gap is that two docs give a contributor opposite advice about whether they SHOULD.

d319 settled the sanctioned path as "land the improvement and change nothing; the stale entry drains later under maintenance", and recorded that in AGENTS.md. The README should be made consistent with it — scope the `--update-stale` recipe explicitly to maintenance, and point the post-refactor contributor at the do-nothing path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.README.md` no longer frames `--update-stale` as a routine
      post-refactor contributor step.
- [x] The README states the contributor path for a legitimate complexity reduction (land it, do
      not edit the baseline), consistent with AGENTS.md.
- [x] No change to the gate scripts or to `.github/complexity-baseline.json`.

## Out of scope
The three assertions fixed under d319. This is documentation only.
baseline.summary: Baseline README presents --update-stale as a post-refactor contributor step, contradicting AGENTS.md's maintenance-only rule

baseline.description:
`docs/adr/` holds 83 files but only 61 distinct numbers. 17 numbers are reused — including FIVE unrelated ADRs numbered 0037, all `Status: Accepted`, all flat in one directory. There is no index. Meanwhile `AGENTS.md:42` cites "ADR 0025" by bare number and `CONTRIBUTING.md:173` sanctions bare ADR references in commit trailers.

Design work established the cause and the safe remediation:

**Cause.** Every collision landed within ~3 hours median. But only 6 of 22 were true in-flight Gerrit races; 16 of 22 were stale-base — the earlier ADR had already landed and the author never refetched. A pre-merge check would have caught 16 of 22.

**Prevention is git's, not CI's.** A pre-merge uniqueness check on a monotonic counter is racy by construction, and ADR 0047 explicitly accepts that a change may land without re-running CI after a server-side rebase. The race-free mechanism is a per-number marker file `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN` whose content is the ADR's filename: two ADRs claiming one number produce an add/add conflict, which Rebase-If-Necessary cannot auto-resolve. Empirically tested in throwaway repos: conflict iff same number, ZERO false conflicts. A shared sorted index was tested and rejected — it conflicts on EVERY concurrent addition (~23% of this repo's ADR additions would conflict spuriously), and a contributor would resolve it by regenerating, silently producing an index containing both.

**Renumbering is approved** (limited user base). Earliest-landed keeps the number; 22 files move to numbers above 0061. Historical disambiguation: ancestry alone resolves 23 of 90 commit references, co-landing 40, topic-matching 86 — 4 remain ambiguous and only 1 resists human resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN` marker files exist for every ADR, content = the ADR filename
- [x] CI asserts the bijection between ADRs and markers, and that no two markers share content
- [x] A generated `docs/adr/README.md` index exists, grouped by workstream, showing full slugs
- [x] `docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md` records the old-to-new mapping and the per-reference resolution table, with tiers marked and the unresolvable reference recorded as UNRESOLVED
- [x] The 17 duplicate numbers are resolved, earliest-landed keeping the number
- [x] Moved ADRs carry a "previously numbered" header; kept ADRs carry an ambiguity-window note
- [x] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:602`'s ADR range citation is replaced by an explicit list
## CURRENT-STATE CORRECTION (the header figures are stale; superseded here)

The description's "83 files / 61 distinct numbers / above 0061" reflects the board at ticket-creation time. As of this implementation the ADR corpus grew (the sibling comment-triage shards 9ce8/4b94/ad16/ab77 landed NEW ADRs 0062-0069). Authoritative current state, re-measured from the tree:

- **91 ADR files**, 69 distinct numbers, **17 duplicate numbers** (5x0037; 3x0007, 3x0035; and 0008-0012,
  0015, 0016, 0026, 0031, 0032, 0036, 0038, 0040, 0041 doubled) = **22 files to move**.
- **Moved ADRs are renumbered to 0070-0091** (NOT "above 0061" — 0062-0069 are now taken by the landed
  sibling ADRs). Target range chosen to sit strictly above the highest existing number (0069).
- Tiebreak unchanged: **earliest-landed keeps its number**; the 22 movers are assigned 0070..0091 in
  ascending landing-date order (full git history, not the shallow-clone graft point). The exact old->new
  map is recorded in docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md and is the authoritative artifact for AC "resolve the 17
  duplicate numbers".

All seven acceptance criteria stand as written; only the numeric targets (file count, and the 0070-0091 destination band) are corrected here.

## Cross-reference handling — stale-reference remediation (addresses plan-review T7/E6)

Renumbering strands references. A reference to a MOVED ADR's old number now resolves to the KEPT ADR of that collision group (wrong target); a reference that always meant the kept ADR stays correct. This is handled explicitly, not left to chance:

**Sweep + resolve.** Every `ADR NNNN` / `adr/NNNN-slug` reference in `docs/` and `src/` (outside `docs/adr/` file bodies) that names a collision number is resolved to the SPECIFIC ADR it means (by adjacent slug when present, else by topic/context), and rewritten to that ADR's FINAL number. The per-reference resolution and its tier (slug-exact / topic-matched / ancestry / UNRESOLVED) is the resolution table already required by AC "RENUMBERING.md".

**Worked example.** `docs/architecture.md` mentions "the transport retry policy (ADR 0037)". The 0037 group keeps `0037-oss-contribution-intake-posture` (earliest-landed) and moves `0037-transport-retry` -> **0087**. The slug "transport retry" disambiguates: this reference meant the moved ADR, so it is rewritten to `ADR 0087`. A bare "ADR 0037" whose context is OSS-intake stays `0037` (it now correctly names the sole surviving 0037).

**Proving command (new AC below).** A referential-integrity assertion in the same CI check (`scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`) fails when any `adr/NNNN-slug` link in `docs/` points to a filename that does not exist, or any `docs/adr/*.md` body cross-links a slug/number with no matching file. This turns "no stranded reference" into an enforced, reproducible check rather than a claim. (Bare prose "ADR NNNN" with no slug is advisory-only — it cannot be mechanically bound to one ADR — and any residue is recorded UNRESOLVED in RENUMBERING.md.)

## Acceptance Criteria (addendum — supersedes nothing, adds the T7/E6 proving path)

- [x] [operator-attested] No stranded ADR cross-reference remains: every `adr/NNNN-slug` link in `docs/` (and every
      slug/number cross-link inside `docs/adr/*.md`) resolves to an existing, unique ADR file, and
      references that named a MOVED ADR are rewritten to its new 0070-0091 number. `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`
      asserts this referential integrity (proving command: the check exits non-zero on a dangling
      `adr/*-slug` link), and RENUMBERING.md records each rewritten reference with its resolution tier.
baseline.summary: Make ADR numbers unique and collision-proof

# J5 — A Dockerized Jira harness as the Data Center verification oracle

## Context / Problem

There is no way to buy a Jira Data Center license to test against: Atlassian ended new DC purchases on 30 March 2026 and no longer issues DC trial licenses. There is also **no official OpenAPI/Swagger spec for Jira DC** — Atlassian publishes only WADL, and the long-standing requests for one (JRASERVER-65954, JRASERVER-68539) remain open — so spec-driven contract testing is unavailable. Cloud's v3 swagger is not a substitute: different auth, ADF vs wiki markup, accountId vs name. Without an oracle, a DC adapter is unverifiable except against fakes that encode our own assumptions.

## Approach

Use the **purpose-built test image that pycontribs/jira publishes for exactly this problem**: `pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`, run as `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 --name jira pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`, reachable at `http://localhost:2990/jira` with the project's documented credentials (`CI_JIRA_ADMIN=admin` / `CI_JIRA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin`, `CI_JIRA_USER=jira_user` / `CI_JIRA_USER_PASSWORD=jira`). It is a pinned, pullable image carrying its own license, so it is unaffected by the DC trial shutdown, and it is the substrate the most widely used Python Jira client validates itself against. Jira 8.17.1 is **≥ 8.14**, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so the PAT bearer auth the DC transport uses is exercised for real.

**Stated limitation, deliberately accepted:** 8.17.1 is older than the version a client such as CMS is likely running, so this harness proves REST v2 protocol semantics, not deployment-specific behavior (workflow names, custom fields, permission schemes, user directories). Closing that gap requires access to the real instance and is tracked separately as ticket `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`; this story's README records the exact image tag so that comparison has a baseline.

Add `tests/live_jira_dc/` with a compose file, a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST, and a fixture that provisions a scratch project and tears down everything it created. **Every test in the directory carries the existing `integration` marker** — not a new custom marker — because `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (`Makefile:154`), so the suite is excluded by construction with no Makefile change and no filter-expression edit.

Teardown follows ADR 0037 §3, which **prohibits post-deletion search-index assertions** because Jira's index lags creates and deletes by an unbounded interval and can return stale results either way. So the teardown oracle is not "query the project and find it empty": it asserts each delete call's HTTP status and then polls each issue's **direct REST endpoint** (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}`) until it returns 404, which is index-independent.

**Alternative rejected: fixtures and a stateful fake alone.** rebar's test-design standard allows a verified fake for external-service mapping, but a fake verified only against fixtures we recorded cannot falsify assumptions we never thought to record — transitions, permission errors, link direction. The fake is still built (J6 uses it for fast unit tests); this story gives it something real to be verified against.

**Alternative rejected: reusing pycontribs/jira's test assertions as the oracle.** Their tests assert their client's behavior, not rebar's field mapping. The reusable asset is the image and harness pattern, which is what this story takes.

**Alternative rejected: the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run-standalone`.** It also yields a licensed local Jira, but it needs the full SDK toolchain and its licenses are short-lived (3-day timebombs requiring `atlas-mvn clean` recycling), which is hostile to repeatable CI. A pinned Docker image has neither problem.

## Scope

- `tests/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`, `conftest.py`, `README.md` (new) — image pinned to
  `pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1`.
- `tests/live_jira_dc/test_harness_smoke.py` (new).
- `Makefile` — a `jira-dc-up` target only; the `test:` target is NOT modified (the `integration` marker is
  already excluded by its existing `-m` expression at `Makefile:154`).

## Testing

Real-external-service tier by construction — this story *is* the harness. Its own oracle is that the harness starts, is usable, and provably cleans up.

- happy path: the harness starts, the readiness probe reports REST answering, and a smoke test creates and
  reads back one issue through raw REST v2.
- auth path: a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via
  `Authorization: Bearer`, proving the DC auth mode the transport will use is exercised, not assumed.
- teardown oracle (index-independent, per ADR 0037 §3): after a deliberately failing test, every issue the
  fixture created returns 404 from its direct `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}` endpoint, and each delete call's HTTP
  status was 2xx. Search is never consulted.
- gating oracle: `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` collects zero tests from
  `tests/live_jira_dc/`.
- failure path: with the instance down, the marked suite fails with a clear "harness not running" message from
  the readiness probe rather than a raw connection traceback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` pulls and starts, and the readiness
      probe reports REST v2 answering at `http://localhost:2990/jira`
- [ ] a smoke test creates and reads back an issue via REST v2, and a PAT-authenticated request succeeds
- [ ] after an intentionally failing test run, every created issue returns 404 from its direct issue endpoint
      (no search query used anywhere in teardown verification)
- [ ] `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` reports 0 tests collected from
      `tests/live_jira_dc/`, and `git diff Makefile` shows no change to the `test:` target
- [ ] `tests/live_jira_dc/README.md` records the pinned image tag and states the version-drift limitation,
      naming ticket `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08` as where real-instance validation is tracked
baseline.summary: J5 — a Dockerized Jira harness as the Data Center verification oracle

## Context / Problem
The prior tickets-history reclaim reported a fresh-clone ceiling from `.git/objects/pack/*.pack` only. The rewritten baseline tree itself was already 290,690,203 logical bytes, while the incident investigation on `absurd-zoometric-bobwhite` measured a fresh single-branch clone at 322.57 MiB of pack data, 827,550,463 logical checkout bytes, 1,116,577,792 allocated checkout bytes, and 1,475,424,256 allocated bytes for the whole clone. Operators therefore need one reproducible report that cannot conflate Git packing with checkout residence or filesystem block slack.

A fixed footprint ceiling is explicitly out of scope. Closed bug `bardic-continuous-asianlion` records that a monotonically growing tickets pack ceiling repeatedly blocked every unrelated Gerrit change; `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:397-407` preserves the decision to remove that gate. The operator reaffirmed on 2026-08-23 that hard budgets or shrink-only ratchets introduce unacceptable fragility and workflow friction.

## Approach
Add an explicit, opt-in, read-only `rebar tracker-footprint` command backed by a reusable measurement module. It will never run implicitly from ticket writes, reconciliation, plan/completion gates, Gerrit Verify, or ordinary `rebar metrics`.

Default mode measures the configured mounted tracker and identifies when its Git object database is shared, so local object bytes are not misrepresented as a standalone clone. `--fresh-clone` resolves the configured tickets remote and branch, creates a temporary unfiltered single-branch/no-tags clone with local hardlink optimization disabled, measures it, and removes only that command-owned temporary directory. Both text and schema-validated JSON output report the measured ref/tip and definitions alongside values.

The report separates packed object bytes; checkout logical bytes; checkout allocated bytes when the platform exposes `st_blocks`; file count and allocation slack; Git-directory logical/allocated bytes; and whole-clone logical/allocated bytes. Unsupported allocation accounting is a structured unavailable value, never a fabricated zero. Size is descriptive only: no threshold, pass/fail classification, baseline mutation, alert side effect, or nonzero exit caused solely by a large result.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/footprint.py`: reusable filesystem/Git measurement and explicit temporary fresh-clone orchestration.
- `src/rebar/_commands/tracker_footprint.py`: read-only CLI adapter and text/JSON rendering.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/tracker_footprint.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py`, and packaged help: register the opt-in command without adding it to write/init paths.
- `src/rebar/schemas/tracker_footprint.schema.json` and `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py`: machine-readable output contract.
- Focused unit/interface/schema/CLI-registry tests and generated `docs/cli-reference.md`.
- `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md`, and `docs/scale-envelope.md`: define each layer and correct the pack-versus-clone operational guidance.

Out of scope: any budget or ratchet, any CI/Gerrit gate, any scheduled or automatic trigger, any tracker/remote mutation, producer retention changes, or history reclaim.

## Testing
- Happy path: measure a temporary standalone tickets clone containing ordinary files through the library and CLI JSON surface.
- Discriminating fixture: many one-byte files produce a small Git pack but materially larger checkout allocation.
- Shared-object edge: default mode measures a linked worktree without presenting its shared object store as standalone-clone cost.
- Platform edge: a stat result without `st_blocks` leaves logical metrics available and allocation metrics unavailable.
- Failure path: an invalid remote or branch fails before a success report and cleans up only command-owned temporary state.
- Regression: CLI registry, output-schema coverage, generated help/reference, lint, typecheck, and default tests remain green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Fresh-clone JSON identifies the requested tickets ref and resolved tip; verified by `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- [x] Packed-object bytes equal the sum of packfiles in the measured standalone clone; verified by `tests/unit/store/test_footprint.py`.
- [x] Checkout logical bytes and file count equal the measured non-Git working-tree files; verified by `tests/unit/store/test_footprint.py`.
- [x] Supported block accounting reports checkout allocated bytes and allocation slack using filesystem block counts; verified by `tests/unit/store/test_footprint.py`.
- [x] A platform without `st_blocks` reports structured allocation-unavailable values while preserving exact logical values; verified by `tests/unit/store/test_footprint.py`.
- [x] Git-directory logical bytes are reported separately from checkout logical bytes; verified by `tests/unit/store/test_footprint.py`.
- [x] Whole-clone logical bytes equal checkout logical plus Git-directory logical bytes; verified by `tests/unit/store/test_footprint.py`.
- [x] The JSON report validates against `tracker_footprint.schema.json`; verified by `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py`.
- [x] A many-small-files fixture exposes materially larger checkout allocation than pack bytes without emitting a threshold verdict or size-based failure; verified by `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- [x] Mounted linked-worktree mode labels its object database as shared rather than standalone; verified by `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- [x] An invalid fresh-clone remote or branch exits nonzero without a success report; verified by `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- [x] Fresh-clone failure removes only the temporary directory created by this command; verified by `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- [x] A successful report leaves the source ref, mounted tracker HEAD/worktree, and remote refs unchanged; verified by `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- [x] CLI registry metadata classifies `tracker-footprint` as an explicit read-only route; verified by `tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py`.
- [x] No ticket-write, reconciler, gate, metrics, or CI path invokes the command; verified by focused repository wiring assertions and review.
- [x] User and reuse documentation defines pack, logical checkout, allocated checkout, Git-directory, and whole-clone layers; verified by documentation review.
- [x] Generated CLI help and reference contain the command and pass their drift checks.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.
- [x] No fixed footprint threshold, shrink-only ratchet, scheduled measurement, or workflow gate is introduced; verified by change review.
baseline.summary: Report whole tickets-store footprint beyond Git pack bytes

## Context / Problem
~110 direct ambient `os.getenv`/`os.environ`/`load_config` reads (plus backend property reloads and configurable adapter defaults) currently sit BELOW the approved composition seams across the reconciler engine, store, snapshot, io, cli, commands, llm/workflow, and the MCP server. RP-04 is not complete while these legacy ambient reads can return values inconsistently under an in-progress operation or bypass the central seam. The ownership gate's initial legacy-exception set (slice C1) must reach EMPTY. This slice also carries the MCP `mcp_server` `load_config()`-per-call cutover deferred from RP-04 S5.

## Outcome
Every below-seam ambient config/credential read, backend reload, and configurable adapter default is either cut to compose through the approved seam (operation snapshot / startup binding / provider boundary) or, for genuine test-only controls and protocol constants, registered with an exact `path+symbol+rationale` entry. The ownership gate then passes on the real tree with an EMPTY legacy-exception set. Legacy facades, migration switches, per-job ambient reloads, and migration exceptions are removed only after their focused suites pass. All S1-S6 behavioral suites remain green and provider-neutral outcomes are unchanged (approved deltas recorded).

## Plan
1. Iterate subsystem-by-subsystem (reconciler engine; store/snapshot/io; cli/commands; llm/workflow; mcp_server/_mcp_auth). For each below-seam read: cut-to-seam OR register with rationale.
2. Drain the legacy-exception set to empty; remove legacy facades/switches only after each subsystem's suite passes.
3. Record redacted snapshot-fingerprint / provider-neutral outcome comparisons and any approved behavior delta.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- The ownership gate (C1) passes on the REAL tree with an EMPTY legacy-exception set and no path-glob exceptions.
- All S1-S6 behavioral suites pass after each subsystem cutover and after legacy-facade removal (they are the correctness oracle; the AST gate supplements them).
- Redacted operation snapshot fingerprints and provider-neutral outcomes before/after are equal except for explicitly recorded, justified deltas.

## Compatibility / rollback
Do not remove a legacy facade until its focused suite and bounded path pass; before removal, rollback selects the facade. At contract phase, retain only the S1 snapshot-envelope compatibility floor; rollback below it is unsupported and documented. Stored ticket/event/bridge/binding formats are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The real tree has no direct ambient config/credential read, backend reload, or configurable adapter default below approved seams; every declared config/credential name has one owner; the legacy exception set is EMPTY; no exception uses a path glob.
- [x] All S1-S6 behavioral suites pass after legacy removal; redacted fingerprints/provider-neutral outcomes are unchanged except for recorded approved deltas.
- [x] Legacy facades, switches, per-job ambient reloads, and migration exceptions are removed only after their proof passes; documented rollback retains the S1 snapshot-envelope compatibility floor.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Bounded provider, AWS review-bot/op-cert, and reconciler check/dry-run/live canaries pass with required redacted evidence (run/change ids, timestamps, selected provider/auth-source kind, retry/cache counters, redacted fingerprint/outcome, rollback decision) and no unauthorized fallback or leakage.
  provenance: environment=hosted-production-and-local-bounded; principal=aws-review-bot-reconciler-and-bounded-provider; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — bounded-live provider bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 ran review-plan this session with retry count 0; AWS review-bot cast LLM-Review +1 on Gerrit changes 1905, 1902, 1901; live reconciler check-access against Jira project REB passed every probe step; a hosted reconciler foreign pass was witnessed at 2026-08-19T16:34:03; the op-cert startup-source and SSM path were exercised this session only by offline behavioral oracles with no production SSM or boto privilege, hence the narrower posture; no unauthorized fallback and no credential value or path recorded; rollback decision is to retain the snapshot-envelope compatibility floor.

# S6 — Apply the GitHub mirror lock (repo-level ruleset, deploy-key-only push)

## Why
Enforce that GitHub `main` can ONLY be advanced by the Gerrit replication deploy key. The lock
is a REPO-LEVEL ruleset (navapbc is a free org -> admin-proof ORG-level rulesets need a paid
plan; trusted-admin editability is the accepted risk, recorded in S6-pre's ADR). Applies the
lock that S6-pre prepared (snapshot + ADR + backend/token). Proven empirically (derisk): an
active repo-level ruleset with deploy-key-only bypass REJECTS a repo-admin's direct push
(`GH013`), so "no human/admin bypass" holds.

## What
- **Use the native provider (peer-pattern simplification).** `terraform-provider-github`
  **v6.8.0 (Nov 2025, PR #2726)** added native `DeployKey` bypass support (removed the
  actor_type whitelist; made `actor_id` optional). So the whole prior `null_resource` + `gh api`
  + `ignore_changes` + disabled->active two-phase dance is **dropped** — it existed only because
  the provider rejected `DeployKey`. Pin `integrations/github >= 6.8.0`.
- One `github_repository_ruleset` for the branch lock on `main` (+ any other branch the bot
  pushes), created directly at `enforcement = "active"` in a single apply, with rules
  `update` + `creation` + `deletion` + `non_fast_forward` and a single
  `bypass_actors { actor_type = "DeployKey"  bypass_mode = "always" }` (NO `actor_id` — it's
  optional; GitHub normalizes to `null`, which the empirical spike confirmed is canonical and
  accepted). A SEPARATE `github_repository_ruleset` for tags (`refs/tags/**`, target `tag`) with
  the same rules + the same DeployKey bypass (else tag pushes are rejected).
- **Replace the existing `main-protection` ruleset** (DERISK E5: id 18048287, PR +
  required-status-checks model — incompatible with deploy-key-only push). It is snapshotted in
  S6-pre; S6 deletes it (`gh api -X DELETE` or via the provider after `terraform import`) and
  creates the mirror-lock rulesets. There is no PR/status-check ruleset left once S6 applies.
- Consume S5's deploy key via a `data "github_repository_deploy_key"` (or a remote-state ref to
  S5's `deploy_key_id` output) so the dependency is explicit and S6 cannot apply before S5's key
  exists. (The bypass entry itself carries no actor_id; the data-source lookup is the existence
  gate, failing the apply loudly if the key is absent.)
- **Token scope.** The Terraform identity needs `Administration: write` on `navapbc/rebar`
  (fine-grained PAT scoped to this repo, or classic `repo`), injected at apply time as a
  `sensitive` var from a CI secret, never committed to `.tfvars`.
- **Remote state.** `infra/terraform/github.tf` uses the shared remote backend with state
  locking; `terraform plan` is reviewed before every `apply`.
- Mirror hygiene: turn OFF Pull Requests (Feb-2026 repo setting), disable Issues + Actions; add
  a "mirror — contribute via Gerrit at rebar.solutions.navateam.com" banner to the About +
  README; do NOT archive (archiving freezes the replication bot too).
- Rollback (runnable in ~15 min): set the rulesets `enforcement = disabled` (provider apply, or
  `gh api PATCH .../rulesets/{id} -f enforcement=disabled` for speed), restore `main-protection`
  from S6-pre's snapshot, and re-enable PRs/Issues/Actions.

## Scope
In: the two native ruleset resources (branch + tag) with DeployKey bypass, replacing
main-protection, mirror hygiene, rollback. Out: the snapshot/ADR/token-scope pre-work (S6-pre);
the Gerrit-side replication (S5); the end-to-end push-past-the-ruleset proof (S7).
**Dependency:** apply AFTER S6-pre (snapshot + ADR + backend ready) AND S5 (deploy key exists).

## Files
- `infra/terraform/github.tf` — provider pin (`>= 6.8.0`), remote backend, sensitive token var,
  the two `github_repository_ruleset` resources (branch + tag, `enforcement = active`, DeployKey
  bypass), the `data.github_repository_deploy_key` lookup, and the repo-feature toggles
  (PRs/Issues/Actions off, mirror banner).
- (optional) a small documented step to delete the pre-existing `main-protection` ruleset by id
  (or `terraform import` then replace), referencing S6-pre's snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A direct `git push` / PR-merge to `main` by a non-bypass identity is REJECTED; force-push
      and deletion of `main` are REJECTED. (Empirically confirmed for the admin-push case.)
- [ ] A tag push by a non-bypass identity is REJECTED by the separate `refs/tags/**` ruleset.
- [ ] The DeployKey bypass is expressed natively as `bypass_actors { actor_type = "DeployKey"
      bypass_mode = "always" }` (no `actor_id`) via `terraform-provider-github >= 6.8.0`, and is
      the ONLY bypass entry on each ruleset; re-running `terraform apply` is idempotent with no
      perpetual diff (provider stores `actor_id = null`, matching GitHub's normalization).
- [ ] The rulesets are created at `enforcement = "active"` in a single apply (NO null_resource,
      NO gh-api bypass step, NO disabled->active two-phase dance, NO `ignore_changes`).
- [ ] S6 obtains the deploy key via a data source / remote-state ref (not a hand-copied ID);
      applying before S5's key exists fails loudly.
- [ ] The pre-existing `main-protection` ruleset (PR + required-status-checks) is replaced/removed
      (snapshot kept in S6-pre); no PR/status-check ruleset remains on `main`.
- [ ] PRs disabled, Issues disabled, Actions disabled; README/About carry the mirror banner;
      repo NOT archived.
- [ ] The Terraform identity's `Administration: write` scope is documented and injected as a
      `sensitive` var from a CI secret (never in `.tfvars`); `github.tf` uses the shared remote
      backend with locking.
- [ ] A rollback runnable in ~15 min is documented (set `enforcement=disabled`, restore
      `main-protection` from the S6-pre snapshot, re-enable PRs/Issues/Actions).

## Plan-review remediation (Round-12, 2026-06-29)
- The Gerrit-only workflow makes the existing GitHub-PR contributor docs stale/misleading. Add contributor-facing docs as part of the mirror cutover.

Added ACs:
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md + README updated for the Gerrit-only workflow (push `HEAD:refs/for/main`, git-review setup, SSH key registration on Gerrit, the LLM-Review gate) so GitHub-PR guidance is no longer presented; the GitHub mirror banner links to it
baseline.summary: infra: S6 — Lock GitHub repo to read-only mirror (repo-level ruleset)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The three surface stories (CLI / MCP / library) each need the **same** decision: given a ticket's current state and the acting session, should we warn that a *different* active session holds this ticket? Duplicating that logic three ways would drift. This story provides one **pure** detector plus the config toggle that gates it, so the surfaces only render.

Ownership is the *live* `claimed_session` (guaranteed live-only by the sibling reducer story). The acting session id comes from the existing shared resolver `resolve_session_id()` (`src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py:71`), which returns the first non-empty of `REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> OPENCODE_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID`, else `None`. Per the brainstorm decision, when the acting id is `None` we stay **silent** (we cannot prove we are a *different* session; the un-shimmed case is common — `docs/session-id-shims.md` gotcha G1), and a default-on config toggle lets an operator disable the warning if the resume/fork false positives prove noisy.

## Approach (as delivered)

The leaf module `src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py` provides a **pure** function:

```
def cross_session_warning(
    state: Mapping[str, Any], *, acting_session: str | None, enabled: bool
) -> str | None
```

It returns `None` (silent) when any of: `enabled` is false; `acting_session` is falsy; `state.get("claimed_session")` is falsy; or `acting_session == state["claimed_session"]`. Otherwise it returns a single-line warning string naming the holder — the `claimed_session` id, and the `claim_harness` in parentheses when present — e.g. `ticket held by another session <sid> (harness <tag>)`. The function performs **no** I/O (no state load, no config read, no env read) so it is trivially unit-testable and reused verbatim by all three surfaces.

A thin convenience `cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, *, repo_root)` composes the pure function with the real reads: it reads the config toggle and `resolve_session_id()` FIRST and short-circuits when disabled or when there is no acting session, only then loading compiled state (via the same read path `show`/`ready` use). The surfaces call this convenience; unit tests target the pure core.

The config key `warnings.cross_session` (bool, **default `True`**) is part of the typed core schema, following the existing `_documented(...)` dataclass-field pattern. Because `Config.from_mapping` instantiates each section via `_SECTION_CLASSES[sect](**vals)` and then `cls(**{sect: ...})`, the `[warnings]` section is wired at FOUR coordinated sites, all already present in the codebase: (1) the `WarningsConfig` dataclass with `cross_session: bool = _documented(True, ...)` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:468`); (2) the `warnings: WarningsConfig = field(default_factory=WarningsConfig)` field on the `Config` dataclass (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:699`) — without it `cls(warnings=...)` would raise `TypeError`; (3) the `"warnings": WarningsConfig` entry in the `_SECTION_CLASSES` registry (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:728`); and (4) the `warnings` section registered in `rebar._config_sections._SECTIONS` (`src/rebar/_config_sections.py:120`), the coercer registry the real load path consumes. The toggle is read through the composed `Config` (the same load path every other typed key uses), so it honours `rebar.toml` + env + CLI overrides with no new read mechanism. The feature is fully **in-process** — no CI provider, no network — satisfying `project.portability`.

## Scope (files delivered)

- `src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py` — the pure `cross_session_warning` + the
  `cross_session_warning_for` convenience (toggle/session read before the state load).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — the `[warnings]` section at the three sites
  `Config.from_mapping` requires: the `WarningsConfig` dataclass (line 468), the
  `warnings` field on `Config` (line 699), and the `"warnings": WarningsConfig` entry in
  `_SECTION_CLASSES` (line 728).
- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` — the `warnings` section (the `cross_session` bool
  coercer) registered in `_SECTIONS` (line 120), the fourth wiring site the load path needs.
- `docs/config-reference.md` — documents `warnings.cross_session` (default true) **and**
  the deliberate silent-when-acting-id-unknown behavior as an evidence-revisitable choice.

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test** — the pure detector is a validation-branch function (test-design §3), and the toggle is exercised through the **real config read path** (test-design §6 "config-effect contrast"), not a stubbed lookup.

- Truth matrix over the pure `cross_session_warning`: warns (non-None, names holder)
  exactly when `enabled and acting_session and claimed_session and acting_session !=
  claimed_session`; silent (None) for each of the four suppression cases
  (disabled / acting `None` / `claimed_session` absent / equal ids). Parameterized.
- Message content: with `claim_harness` present the string includes both the id and the
  harness tag; without it, just the id.
- Config-effect contrast (real read path): construct a `Config` from a mapping with
  `[warnings] cross_session=false` and one at the default (true); run
  `cross_session_warning_for` against a fixture ticket held by session A while acting as
  B, and assert the default warns and the `false` value is silent — proving the key is
  wired through the actual `Config` load, not just parsed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `cross_session_warning(state, acting_session=..., enabled=...)` returns a non-`None`
  string containing the holder's `claimed_session` id exactly when
  `enabled and acting_session and state["claimed_session"] and acting_session !=
  state["claimed_session"]` (checked by a parameterized unit test matrix under
  `make test`).
- [x] The detector returns `None` for every suppression case — `enabled=False`,
  `acting_session=None`, `claimed_session` absent/falsy, or equal ids (checked by the same
  parameterized test).
- [x] The returned string includes the `claim_harness` tag when present and omits it when
  absent (checked by two assertions in a message-content test).
- [x] Config-effect: with `[warnings] cross_session=false` loaded through the real
  `Config`, `cross_session_warning_for` is silent for an A-held ticket acted on by B; at
  the default it warns (checked by `test_cross_session_config_toggle` exercising the real
  config read path).
- [x] `docs/config-reference.md` documents `warnings.cross_session` (default true) and the
  silent-when-acting-id-unknown revisitable decision (checked: BOTH
  `grep -n "cross_session" docs/config-reference.md` AND
  `grep -n "revisit" docs/config-reference.md` match).
baseline.summary: Cross-session warning detector + warnings.cross_session config toggle

## Why
The shared `impact = mean(severity attributes)` dilutes a genuinely high-severity plan finding below the 0.70 bar (a critical finding averaged with low axes lands ~0.60-0.69). The mean is the wrong aggregator.

## What
For the plan-review gate, replace the mean with severity-first MAX + hard override + detection amplifier.
- SEVERITY axes (each mapped to [0,1] by the verify pass): AC-unverifiable, DoD-uncertifiable, undecomposed
  (from the deterministic G5 signal), divergent-implementation, internal-conflict, vague-directive,
  irreversible-without-rationale.
- `impact_sev = MAX(axis contributions)` (no averaging).
- HARD OVERRIDE: if ANY of {AC-unverifiable, DoD-uncertifiable, undecomposed, divergent-implementation},
  `impact_sev = max(impact_sev, 0.85)`.
- DETECTION AMPLIFIER: `silent-vs-self-revealing` (silent build-the-wrong-thing -> x1.0, self-revealing
  wall -> x0.8); DoD-uncertifiable forces x1.0. Explicit compose: `impact = min(1.0, impact_sev * detection_mult)`.

## Implementation mechanics (grounded in the current code)
- VERIFY SCHEMA: the shared `verification_model()` in `verify.py` carries only the 5-field `SeverityAttrs`
  (prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility). Add a `plan_review_verification_model()`
  with an extended `PlanSeverityAttrs` adding the 7 axis fields above, EACH defaulting to `'none'`/absent so
  an older or absent verifier abstains (back-compat: a missing axis contributes 0, never inflates).
- PER-GATE DISPATCH (precise): `impact()` is called INSIDE the kernel's `pass3_decide()`, so it is NOT the
  consumer-injected-callable pattern `threshold_for` uses. Add `impact_fn: Callable[[dict], float] | None =
  None` to `pass3_decide()` defaulting to the existing `impact`; `pass3_over_findings` accepts and threads it;
  plan-review's wrapper passes `impact_fn=impact_plan`. The code-review gate later passes its own; the
  plan-review signed-verdict shape stays byte-compatible.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` (`impact_fn` param + `impact_plan`), `verify.py`
  (`plan_review_verification_model` + `PlanSeverityAttrs`), the plan-review verify prompt (emit the 7 axes),
  and the orchestrator wrapper wiring. Depends on the deterministic G5 signal child. No code-review changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pass3_decide()` accepts an `impact_fn` (default = existing `impact`); plan-review threads `impact_plan`
      through `pass3_over_findings`; a test asserts the code-review path (no `impact_fn`) is byte-unchanged.
- [ ] `impact_plan = MAX(axes)` with the hard-override list and the detection amplifier (silent x1.0 /
      self-revealing x0.8; DoD-uncertifiable forces x1.0), per the explicit compose above.
- [ ] `plan_review_verification_model()` + `PlanSeverityAttrs` add the 7 axes with abstaining defaults;
      older/absent verifiers do not inflate impact.
- [ ] Offline replay: previously-stranded 0.60-0.69 band findings clear 0.70; verdicts stay stable on
      same-material replicate pairs.
baseline.summary: Plan-review impact redesign: severity-first MAX + hard override + detection amplifier

## Context

Before any change-size/decomposition rule can enter the DET floor, measure whether change shape actually drives the defect-rework loop here (11-plan-v3 I-4; measurement-first matches the field — Prow's `size/*` labels are non-blocking, 12c). Tooling anchor (12a): extend `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` (442 lines), which imports the shipped predicate `BUGFIX_SIZE_THRESHOLD_NON_TEST_LINES` and `escalation_for_diff` from `rebar.llm.code_review.bugfix_size_gate` so its threshold cannot drift from the gate that ships. 2026 grounding (12b): MSR'26 agentic-PR studies show files-touched/commit fragmentation is a sharper variable than raw LOC, the size-quality relationship is nonstationary (re-tune, never freeze), and context fragmentation is an independent causal variable (39% quality drop in a controlled study). The two doubling friction categories (CI-at-landing 25/60; environment 13/60 — R2S3) are unexplained and get mechanism reads, not guesses.

## Approach

**Step 0 — overlap check, before building.** 11-plan-v3 I-4 requires confirming this does not duplicate the Tier-2 replay harness (ADR 0109, `1299d9deb6da`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/`). The finding is recorded in the backtest report's Method section either way; if the harness already supplies a variable, this task consumes it rather than re-deriving it.

**Read (a) — change shape.** Extend the backtest with an all-work mode (not just bug-typed tickets) measuring rework against three variables: non-test LOC (via the already-imported `count_non_test_diff_lines`), files touched (`git show --name-only`), and commit fragmentation (commits per ticket, grouped by the `rebar-ticket:` trailer). The script computes no correlation today — only a recall summary — so this adds a statistical layer rather than extending one. **Rework signals — two, both PER-TICKET and both offline.** (i) store `caused_by` fan-in, the same label source the script already uses, and (ii) gate rounds: how many `REVIEW_RESULT` / `COMPLETION_VERDICT` events a ticket accumulated. Both are read per ticket id, so both join on the key above. The `rebar metrics` proxies are NOT usable here and are deliberately excluded: `revert_recovery` and `reopen_recovery` return a single REPO-WIDE int and `first_pass_rate` a single REPO-WIDE float, so they have no per-ticket value to correlate against; only `attempts_per_ticket` is per-ticket, and gate rounds subsume it. Gerrit patchset count is likewise excluded: it alone needs the network, making the corpus unreproducible offline.

**The join key, explicitly.** Shape is measured PER COMMIT; rework is measured PER TICKET, so the two are aligned on the **full canonical rebar ticket id** taken from each commit's FIRST `rebar-ticket:` trailer (parsed with the shipped `extract_ticket_refs`). `group_by_ticket` SUMS per-commit shape into per-ticket aggregates (non-test LOC, total LOC, commit count) and unions files-touched; that row is what correlates. A commit whose trailer does not resolve to exactly one full canonical id in the store — an ambiguous 4-quad fragment, or a ticket no longer present — is UNJOINABLE: it is excluded from the correlation and its count is reported, never silently dropped. This is also why the window starts 2026-07-01: trailer coverage on `origin/main` is 60/650 in June (pre-enforcement, unjoinable) against 876/907 in July.

**Read (b) — CI-at-landing.** The doubling window is 2026-08-25..2026-08-30 (the newer-30 half of R2S3's 60 session logs). No case list is committed, so the 20 cases are derived: session-log mining over that window for `Verified -1` / CI-failure patterns, cross-referenced to the specific Gerrit changes R2S3 already names. Each case is read for mechanism, change shape, cross-session interference, isolation class, and drift class.

**Read (c) — environment.** Session reports are `session_log` tickets, queryable offline via `rebar session-logs -o json`. The automated `llm-degrade NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` logs carry a structured JSON body (`exception_type`, `message`, `model`) and are countable without keyword heuristics; the remainder are read for mechanism. Output projects specific fields — a full dump is dominated by authorship ledgers and is unusably large.

**Decision.** The size/decomposition enforcement decision is recorded either way as ADR 0110 (next free number; `docs/adr/.numbers/0110` marker committed alongside, which is the race-free uniqueness mechanism). `docs/adr/README.md` is GENERATED by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py` and must be regenerated, never hand-edited.

**Dependency.** `reports/` is gitignored; the `.gitignore` re-inclusion of `reports/stability/` lands in sibling `yogic-soapstone-takin` (f9b9-83ad-931c-4833), which sits below this change in the stack. This task inherits it and adds no second `.gitignore` edit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: `reports/stability/change-shape-backtest.md` is committed, giving the distribution of all three variables (non-test LOC, files touched, commit fragmentation) and each one's measured relationship to rework, with n stated inline. Verified by `git ls-files reports/stability/change-shape-backtest.md`.
- [x] AC2: read (a) is reproducible — the report's Method section names the exact command, and re-running it reproduces the reported n. Verified by running the documented `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py ...` invocation.
- [x] AC3: `reports/stability/ci-landing-regressions-read.md` is committed with a 20-row per-case table (mechanism, change shape, class) and states how the cases were selected from the 2026-08-25..2026-08-30 window.
- [x] AC4: `reports/stability/environment-failures-read.md` is committed with per-case mechanisms and a class disposition per case, naming which dispositions feed the doctor-checks scope.
- [x] AC5: the enforcement decision is recorded either way as `docs/adr/0110-*.md` with its supporting evidence, and `docs/adr/.numbers/0110` is committed. Verified by `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` exiting 0 and `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` confirming the bijection.
- [x] AC6: the Step-0 overlap finding against ADR 0109's replay harness is stated in the backtest report, so a later reader knows the boundary was checked.
- [x] AC7: the extended script still imports the shipped threshold predicate rather than re-deriving it, so the backtest cannot drift from the gate. Verified by the existing import remaining, exercised by the script's tests.

## Testing

- `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` — the existing pinned-corpus self-check still passes, proving the all-work extension did not perturb the shipped bug-corpus path (AC7).
- the documented all-work invocation from the report's Method section — re-runs read (a) and reproduces its n (AC2).
- `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` and `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` — the ADR is indexed and its number is uniquely claimed (AC5).
- `git ls-files reports/stability/` — the three reports are tracked (AC1, AC3, AC4).
- `make lint && make typecheck` — the script extension clears the house gates, including the complexity ratchet.

Measurement reads are evidence documents, not executable behavior, so their oracle is reproducibility (AC2) rather than a new automated test; the script change itself is covered by the pinned-corpus check above.

## File impact

- `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` (extend: all-work mode + files-touched/fragmentation variables and the correlation layer)
- `reports/stability/change-shape-backtest.md` (new)
- `reports/stability/ci-landing-regressions-read.md` (new)
- `reports/stability/environment-failures-read.md` (new)
- `docs/adr/0110-<slug>.md` and `docs/adr/.numbers/0110` (new; the enforcement decision)
- `docs/adr/README.md` (regenerated by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py`)
baseline.summary: Upstream introduction measurement: change-shape backtest + CI-at-landing and environment mechanism reads

## Summary

Follow-up split from injurious-pugnacious-azurevase (c0f6-0fc9-fe48-41bc), the class-fix for repo/config-root-derived-from-the-store-path. That ticket landed the behavior-preserving `str(tracker)` subset (composer.py / composer_edit.py) and the `str()` half of the AST guard. This ticket covers the DESIGN-JUDGMENT `realpath()`/`abspath()` subset it deliberately deferred, plus feisty-intense-mandrill's `.canonical` guard blind spot.

## The approved principle (operator-decided; this principle GOVERNS site bucketing)

On a RELOCATED store (store outside the code checkout — the deployed MCP topology: code at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`, store at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`), a site that composes a root as `dirname(realpath/abspath(tracker))` wants ONE of two roots. The DISCRIMINATOR is whether the site reads `compose_config()`:

1. Anything that READS `compose_config()` (directly, or via `config.tickets_branch()` /
   `config.tickets_remote()` / `config.compose_config()`) resolves the CODE repo root via the
   sanctioned resolver `config.repo_root_or_none()`. `rebar.toml` lives in the checkout, so
   reading it from the store's parent is the bug. (behavior-CHANGING on a relocated store →
   each proven by a RED→GREEN oracle)
2. Git operations on the store's OWN repo — git history/attribution/identity keyed on
   `git -C <tracker>`, or a store-path hint string — that DO NOT read `compose_config()` keep
   the STORE root, routed through ONE shared seam `rebar._proc.store_repo_root(tracker)`.
   (behavior-PRESERVING: the seam returns exactly `dirname(realpath(tracker))`)

Divergence is prevented BY CONSTRUCTION: the code root goes through `config.repo_root_or_none()`; the store root goes through the single seam `rebar._proc.store_repo_root()` (marked `# repo-root-seam:`); and the AC#3 guard fails CI on any other direct spelling.

## Candidate sites (disposition by the compose_config() discriminator)

CODE ROOT (reads compose_config; via `config.repo_root_or_none()`; behavior-changing → RED→GREEN):
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:238 — `_sync_disabled(...)` -> `compose_config(root).sync.pull`.
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:249 — `tickets_branch(...)` -> `tickets.branch`.
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:374 — `_load_scratch` -> `compose_config(root).scratch.base_dir`.
- src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:80 — `_remote_ref` -> `tickets_remote/tickets_branch` (the store's
  remote-tracking ref for the staleness probe; realpath()-wrapped member of this class).
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py — `_branch_mismatch` FALLBACK (:83),
  `_tracker_sync_status` (:204), `_configured_remote_ref` (:374) -> `tickets_branch/tickets_remote`.
  (`_branch_mismatch` still prefers the code `repo_root` fsck threads; only its fallback changed.)

STORE ROOT (NO compose_config read; via the shared seam `rebar._proc.store_repo_root(tracker)`; behavior-preserving — `git -C <tracker>` on the store's OWN repo / attribution / a path hint):
- src/rebar/_proc.py — `detached_child_cwd` (uses the seam directly; stdlib-only leaf home).
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:524, compact_rebuild.py:139 — `_build_authorship_ledger`
  repo_root (git history/signing of the store's own events; no compose_config).
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_plan.py:212 — `_seam.attribution_fields` repo_root (git author_email
  / identity of the store's own repo; no compose_config).
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:253 — `repo_guess`, a path-hint STRING joined to `.tickets-tracker`
  for a dir-mismatch warning (no compose_config).

ALREADY SANCTIONED — out of this ticket's realpath/abspath scope (do NOT re-triage):
- src/rebar/_store/sync.py:305/307 — `tickets_branch/tickets_remote(dirname(str(tracker)))`, the
  `str()` variant, already carrying a `# repo-root-ok:` sanction (line 306) landed by the parent
  ticket c0f6-0fc9. Not a realpath()/abspath() member. Left untouched (also avoids collision with
  concurrent ticket baldish-regainable-steed).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC#1 — Every realpath()/abspath() config-read site (the CODE-ROOT list above:
  reads.py:238/:249/:374, freshness.py:80, fsck_tracker_health.py `_branch_mismatch` fallback /
  `_tracker_sync_status` / `_configured_remote_ref`) resolves `cfg_root` from the CODE repo via
  `config.repo_root_or_none()` (or, where fsck already threads it, an explicit `repo_root`).
  VERIFY: `grep -rn 'dirname' src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py src/rebar/_store/freshness.py
  src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py` shows none of these sites wraps `tracker` in
  `dirname(realpath/abspath(...))` for the config root any more. Each is behavior-changing on a
  relocated store, so each is proven by a RED→GREEN oracle in
  `tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py` (the reads.py, freshness, `_tracker_sync_status`,
  `_configured_remote_ref`, and `_branch_mismatch`-fallback cases).
- [x] AC#2 — Every git/attribution store-repo site that does NOT read compose_config (the
  STORE-ROOT list above: _proc.py `detached_child_cwd`, compact_txn/rebuild `_build_authorship_ledger`,
  compact_plan `attribution_fields`, fsck.py `repo_guess`) is routed through the single shared seam
  `rebar._proc.store_repo_root(tracker)` (behavior-preserving: the seam returns exactly what these
  sites computed before), and the seam carries the `# repo-root-seam:` marker. VERIFY:
  `grep -rn 'store_repo_root' src/rebar` shows every store-repo site calls the seam;
  `python scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` is green. sync.py:305/307 is already sanctioned —
  no action. No compose_config read → no relocated-store behavior change → no new oracle needed
  (behavior-preservation covered by the existing store-command tests plus the guard).
- [x] AC#3 — Extend `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` to also flag the
  realpath()/abspath()-wrapped store argument AND `dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)`
  (feisty-intense-mandrill's blind spot), so the guard is airtight for the whole class: the ONLY
  exempt spellings are the shared seam (`# repo-root-seam:`) and the already-sanctioned store-repo
  sites (`# repo-root-ok:`). Proven by the guard self-test
  (`tests/unit/test_repo_root_from_tracker_guard.py`) — the old "realpath/abspath NOT unwrapped"
  case is inverted, and `.canonical`/str-wrapped/seam-marker/single-seam cases are added.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_repo_root_from_tracker_guard.py tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py -q` — guard flags the realpath/abspath/.canonical variants; each config-read behavior change has a RED→GREEN oracle.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` — green on the fixed tree with all legitimate store-repo sites routed through the seam or sanctioned.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && make typecheck` — no regressions.
baseline.summary: config-root from store: realpath()/abspath() design-judgment subset + guard extension

## Context

The `Verify Authorship Identity` CI gate (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`) enforces a blobless-checkout pack-size budget via `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB`. The deliberate budget is **100 MiB (102400 KiB)** — an intentional growth canary (commit `16a1a385`, ticket `037b`).

As part of epic `536b-8930-b922-4063` (causal-stability history reclaim), the budget was **temporarily raised to 550 MiB (563200 KiB)** as a bridge, because the `tickets`-branch blobless pack is ~481 MiB and safe causal-stability compaction alone cannot bring it under 100 MiB (proof on 536b: even N=30d coalescing lands ~365-380 MiB). The bridge keeps the health lane green while the reclaim mechanism (below-horizon commit/tree collapse) plus structural fixes W1 (batch write lane) and W2 (shard the root tree) land.

## Scope of THIS ticket

This ticket tracks the **REVERSAL** of that bridge. It is a follow-up: once the 536b history reclaim + W1/W2 have landed and the measured blobless pack is back under 100 MiB, restore `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` to `102400` and remove the bridge comment. This ticket stays open until then; it is the durable, self-documenting reminder that the raised value is temporary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The 536b history-reclaim swap has landed on the `tickets` remote and the measured blobless CI-checkout pack is verified under 100 MiB.
- [ ] `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` in `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` is restored to `102400`.
- [ ] The temporary-bridge comment referencing this ticket is removed from the workflow.
- [ ] The verify-identity gate passes green at the restored 100 MiB budget.

## Portability

The budget is a plain GitHub Actions workflow env var; restoring it is a one-line workflow edit with no dependence on any single CI provider.
baseline.summary: Restore verify-identity pack budget to 100 MiB after 536b history reclaim lands

## Summary

ROOT CAUSE of the B5 premature-close incident. The plan-review gate reviewed B5 (pout-gloss-hoop) and returned PASS, but did NOT flag a verification-completeness deficiency in B5's acceptance criteria: AC3 ('Integration tests cover claim+close pass/fail through the workflow path with intact signing') was satisfiable ENTIRELY by OFFLINE tests using canned agents that never call resolve_prompt — so the risky new behavior (the workflow plan-review verify/coach steps run against a LIVE model) had NO acceptance criterion requiring it to be exercised end-to-end. B5 shipped + closed (signed completion verdict) with the live plan-review claim gate broken (INDETERMINATE: 'prompt references undefined variable plan'). The completion verifier correctly certified AC-satisfaction-as-written; the gap is that the GATE that reviews PLANS did not catch that the AC could pass without exercising the changed, risky path.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Author a story (like B5) that CUTS OVER a gate/engine to a new code path and DEFAULTS to it.
2. Write an AC that is satisfiable by OFFLINE/mocked tests only (no live / end-to-end exercise of the new path).
3. Run rebar review-plan on the story. 
4. Observe: PASS, with no finding that the AC permits validating the risky behavior without ever running it (no live-verification / end-to-end-DoD requirement).
5. The story ships; the live path is broken; nothing caught it until the path was hit by hand.

## Expected vs Actual

EXPECTED: the plan-review gate's AC-quality / definition-of-done criteria (e.g. E6 ac-text-quality, F1, the T-series acceptance criteria) flag an AC whose verification can pass WITHOUT exercising the actually-changed risky behavior — especially for a cutover/migration that defaults to a new path. The coaching should push 'add a live/end-to-end acceptance criterion for the path you are defaulting to.'

ACTUAL: PASS with no such finding. The verification-completeness gap (offline-only validation of a path that needs live validation) escaped review, enabling B5 to close green while broken.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A plan-review criterion (new or strengthened, e.g. the AC-quality / proxy-validation dimension) flags an AC that can be satisfied WITHOUT exercising the changed risky behavior — i.e. mocked/offline-only verification of a path the story makes the default.
- [ ] An eval/regression case encodes the B5-shaped scenario (a cutover defaulting to a new engine path with an offline-only AC) and asserts the gate surfaces the verification-completeness finding.
- [ ] The coaching for that finding recommends adding a live/end-to-end DoD for the defaulted path.
- [ ] Documented: a gate/engine cutover's DoD must include exercising the new path end-to-end against a live model (green offline tests + a passing completion verdict are necessary but not sufficient).
baseline.summary: plan-review gate passed B5 without flagging that its AC allowed offline-only verification of a path that needed live validation

## Context

Purpose: conservative module-wide Terraform evidence for T10 Pass 1 and independent Pass 2.

## Scope

### Optional boundary

Add `grounding-terraform = ["python-hcl2==8.1.3"]` and the `hcl2` probe. In `_capabilities.py`, add `grounding-terraform` to `DECLARED_EXTRAS` and register ABSTAIN-posture `grounding_terraform`. It is sole opt-in; core/non-Terraform paths import/advertise nothing. Extend optionality CI.

### Structural index

Add `terraform_index.py`/`terraform_tools.py`. Each call owns cache+ledger; its finalizer frees them. Pass 2 re-captures the frozen source; no cache crosses steps.

- Trigger on impacted `.tf`/`.tf.json`, or Terraform/OpenTofu plan plus repo Terraform. Index affected directories; follow repo-contained literal children/reverse callers; exclude VCS, virtualenv, `.terraform/`.
- Directly inspect a changed `.tfvars`, but never infer it is selected.
- Reject absolute/out-of-repo sources and escaping symlinks. Enforce 64 modules, 5,000 files, 32 MiB, and the existing 60-second deadline before returning facts; any failure yields one abstention with no partial facts.
- Exact-wheel import probe exited 0: `8.1.3`; `parses_to_tree` signature `(text: str) -> lark.tree.Tree`; `parser().options.propagate_positions=True`; `Tree.meta` block `(1,1,3,2)`, attribute `(2,2,2,15)`; serialized meta keys `['__is_block__']`. Use `parses_to_tree` on strict-UTF-8-decoded bytes; JSON uses unambiguous key range, else file-level. Full command/output: ticket evidence comment dated 2026-09-03.

### Operations and schemas

- `lookup_declaration(address, module_path="")`: variable, local, output, module, provider, managed resource, data resource.
- `resolve_reference(reference, from_file)`: direct module traversals/repo-local child outputs; resource bases may resolve, provider attributes never do.
- Both are `job=refute`: static resolution returns `refuted` at T1; all non-proof is `abstain`; neither emits `match` or asserts absence.
- Grounding references use `kind="symbol"` for declarations and `kind="member"` for dotted traversals, with canonical address as `name` and `language="terraform"`. Closed `terraform_kind`: `variable|local|output|module|provider|managed_resource|data_resource`.
- Normalize paths to NFC repo-relative POSIX (empty module `.`; collapse dots; preserve case; reject NUL/absolute/escaping `..`). Trim outer address whitespace, grammar-parse, and case-preserving dot-render; internal whitespace, splats, or computed indexes abstain.

Add closed `terraform_grounding_receipt.schema.json`; validate evidence against `grounding.schema.json` and receipts against it. Required receipt fields: `schema_version`, `operation`, normalized `query`, `snapshot_digest`, `module_digest`, `backend` (parser/version, analyzer/version, config digest), `limits`, `outcome`, generic `reason`, closed `reason_detail`, and `result_digest`. Snapshot/module SHA-256 uses a sorted length-prefixed path+byte stream. Config/result reuse `"sha256:" + rebar._store.canonical.content_hash(float_free_object)`. Refuted hashes safe facts; abstain hashes exactly `{outcome,reason,reason_detail}`.

Worked receipt (digests abbreviated only here):

`{"schema_version":1,"operation":"lookup_declaration","query":{"address":"module.web","module":"infra"},"snapshot_digest":"sha256:…","module_digest":"sha256:…","backend":{"parser":"python-hcl2","parser_version":"8.1.3","analyzer":"rebar-terraform-structural","analyzer_version":1,"config_digest":"sha256:…"},"limits":{"modules":64,"files":5000,"bytes":33554432,"timeout_ms":60000},"outcome":"refuted","reason":null,"reason_detail":null,"result_digest":"sha256:…"}`

Worked abstain (same required provenance): `{"operation":"resolve_reference","query":{"reference":"aws_instance.web.id","from_file":"infra/main.tf"},"outcome":"abstain","reason":"ambiguous","reason_detail":"provider_attribute","result_digest":"sha256:…"}`.

Exact abstention translation:

- Missing extra → `no_tool/missing_extra`; wrong parser version → `version_skew/parser_version`; non-Terraform call → `unsupported_lang/not_terraform`.
- Pre-worker invalid/undecodable input → `parse_error/invalid_input`; unreadable capture → `parse_error/unreadable_file`.
- Harness `timeout` → `timeout/worker_timeout`; harness `parse_error` (including indistinguishable native signal death) → `parse_error/invalid_input`; harness `other` from raise/no-result/protocol failure → `other/worker_failure`.
- Duplicate address → `ambiguous/duplicate_address`; no unique hit → `ambiguous/no_unique_address`; dynamic source/expression → `ambiguous/dynamic_source|dynamic_expression`; computed value → `ambiguous/computed_value`; provider attribute → `ambiguous/provider_attribute`; splat/index → `ambiguous/splat_index`; unknown tfvars selection → `ambiguous/unknown_tfvars`.
- Absolute/out-of-repo/escaping symlink → `private_or_internal_suspected/path_outside_snapshot`.
- Module/file/byte bound → `other/module_limit|file_limit|byte_limit`.

Return only safe classes, hashes, and repo-relative locations—never credentials or literal payloads.

### Plan-review integration

Inject tools only into Terraform T10 Pass 1. Terraform evidence selects Pass 2 with a fresh ledger and required independent query; inject no Pass-1 answer. Add a per-call tool provider/finalizer to `RunnerAgentStep`, preserving static `extra_tools`.

Record concrete reads as synthetic `read_file` usage and signed `**/*.tf`/`**/*.tf.json` membership, so sibling additions alter stdlib-only freshness. Missing extra exposes no tools; failures abstain.

## Positive rationale

Reuse existing seams; never scan or evaluate Terraform.

## Out of scope

Registry/remote content, prompts, scanners, `terraform-config-inspect`, and Terraform/OpenTofu/provider execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Lean-install tests pin `python-hcl2==8.1.3`; absent-extra/non-Terraform routes import/advertise nothing.
- [x] Index tests find sibling files, bounded child/reverse callers, and keep targeted `.tfvars` unselected.
- [x] `lookup_declaration` tests assert exact `symbol`/`terraform_kind`, T1 `refuted`, line range, safe facts, and receipt.
- [x] `resolve_reference` tests assert exact `member` mapping and child-output resolution; computed/provider/dynamic controls abstain.
- [x] Boundary tests assert exact reasons/digests, no partial facts, cache/ledger retirement, worker reaping, and below/at/above bounds.
- [x] Workflow integration captures T10 Pass-1/Pass-2 requests with distinct ledgers; non-T10/non-Terraform controls expose no tool.
- [x] Signed-read-set tests observe all parsed files/patterns, then add a sibling `.tf` and observe freshness change.
- [x] `tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_tools.py::test_no_forbidden_executables` observes no Terraform, OpenTofu, provider, tfparse, TFLint, Trivy, terraform-ls, terraform-docs, or other executable.
- [x] Schema tests validate evidence/receipts; `docs/grounding.md` and ADR 0115 document tools, trust boundary, outcomes/reasons, posture, limits, lifecycle, and prohibitions.

## Testing

Test contract card:

- Contract: REB-640, `docs/grounding.md`, ADR 0115, both schemas, harness `RunResult`.
- Preconditions: sibling/child/reverse, dynamic, escape, bound, and harness fixtures.
- Production: real capture/worker/response/request; fake only the model.
- Tiers: parser/evidence unit-contract; workflow integration; lean-install subprocess.
- Oracles: exact evidence/receipt/tools; no partial facts; cleanup; membership-digest change.
- Controls: non-Terraform has no tools; literal resolves, computed abstains.
- CI: `make test`, `make docs-check`, and optionality CI.

## Verification

`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_index.py tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_tools.py tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_plan_review_tools.py tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py tests/unit/test_capabilities.py && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make docs-check`
