baseline.description:
## Why

Per-criterion **blocking is already done** (`code_review/registry.threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3 +
detector fail-closed). What is missing is **attestation integration**: a project criterion's
verdict/coverage must fold into the signed (kind-keyed) attestation, and activating/editing/
disabling a criterion must invalidate a prior attestation — but `claim_gate_check` never
re-compares the routing version, and `registry_version()` hashes only the PACKAGED routing
(`attest.py:44`), so an overlay change produces an identical version and does NOT invalidate.

## What

- `registry_version(repo_root=None)` additionally hashes the `.rebar/` overlay when `repo_root` is
  given; thread `repo_root` through **every** caller: `claim_gate_check` → `compute_validity`, and
  also `drift_refresh_candidate` and `remediation_mode_candidate` (which call `registry_version()`
  without it today). So activating/editing/disabling a criterion invalidates a prior attestation at
  claim time.
- A disabled built-in is recorded in a `disabled_builtins: [ids]` field in the verdict `coverage`
  dict (folded into the signed manifest) so the cert reflects reduced coverage; additive/
  expand-contract (absent on old certs → treated as stale → re-review, never a crash).
- Cross-gate: this applies to **any** gate attestation backed by the shared registry — plan-review
  now; code-review once it signs (code-review signs nothing today; the `attest.py` port to
  code-review rides with story `#6`).

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (registry_version(repo_root), coverage field,
  threading), the claim-gate path.
- Depends on story `#1` (the overlay must exist to hash) and story `#2` (DET blocking).
- Blocking itself is NOT in scope (already shipped via `threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `registry_version(repo_root)` hashes the `.rebar/` overlay; threaded through
      `claim_gate_check`/`compute_validity`/`drift_refresh_candidate`/`remediation_mode_candidate`.
- [ ] Activating/editing/disabling a project criterion invalidates a prior plan-review attestation
      at claim time; an unchanged overlay does not churn (regver == today when overlay absent).
- [ ] A disabled built-in appears in `coverage.disabled_builtins` in the signed manifest.
- [ ] Expand-contract: an old attestation lacking the new basis is treated as stale (re-review),
      never a crash.
- [ ] A project criterion's verdict + coverage fold into the signed attestation; it can never
      rebind a built-in.


## compute_validity regver check + disabled_builtins manifest line (remediation, run 1)

### `compute_validity` gains a regver staleness check (clears G6 blocker 1)
Threading `repo_root` into `compute_validity` is necessary but NOT sufficient — its plan-review
branch must ALSO compare the attestation's recorded regver against the current one:
`manifest_regver(manifest) != registry_version(repo_root)` → the record reads as **not valid**
with reason `"stale-regver"` (a new invalidation reason alongside the existing
material/head-sha/reopen checks). So activating/editing/disabling a project criterion (which
changes `registry_version(repo_root)` because it now hashes the `.rebar/` overlay) makes a prior
attestation read stale at claim time. `manifest_regver(manifest)` is a small helper that extracts
the `regver:` line from the signed manifest (mirroring the existing `manifest_material`). An
attestation with NO regver line (pre-this-change) → treated as stale → re-review (expand-contract,
never a crash).

### `disabled_builtins` is a dedicated signed manifest line (clears G6 blocker 2)
`build_manifest()` emits a NEW `disabled_builtins: [id,id,...]` line (sorted, deterministic) WHEN
the verdict `coverage` carries disabled built-ins (from the overlay disabling a built-in via ef7e's
merge) — so the cert reflects reduced coverage rather than silent omission. A `manifest_disabled_builtins(manifest)`
parser reads it back (like `manifest_material`). The line is ADDITIVE/expand-contract: absent on old
certs (parsed as `[]`), present only when non-empty, so a clean run's manifest is byte-identical to
today (attestation-safe). `verify_signature` re-derives the same manifest and checks the HMAC as usual.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] `compute_validity` (plan-review branch) adds a `manifest_regver != registry_version(repo_root)`
      staleness check returning reason `stale-regver`; a missing regver line → stale (re-review).
      A test proves activating/editing a project criterion invalidates a prior attestation.
- [ ] `build_manifest` emits a deterministic `disabled_builtins: [ids]` line when the verdict
      coverage has disabled built-ins; a `manifest_disabled_builtins` parser reads it; absent/empty
      on a clean run (byte-identical manifest). A test asserts the round-trip + HMAC re-verify.


## No mass re-review + the built-in-disable mechanism (remediation, run 2)

### The regver line ALREADY exists — no mass invalidation (clears T4)
Current signed manifests ALREADY carry a `regver:` line (verified: e.g. `regver: 83e5f63ad06d893a`).
This story adds the CHECK in `compute_validity`, NOT the line. The `registry_version` basis change is
ADDITIVE: for an OVERLAY-ABSENT repo, `registry_version(repo_root)` hashes the same packaged routing
it does today ⇒ the SAME regver value ⇒ existing certs stay valid (zero churn). A repo that has an
overlay is BY DEFINITION new (the overlay feature shipped in ef7e), so it has NO pre-existing certs to
invalidate. The truly-ancient "no regver line at all" case → stale → one re-review, which is the
correct expand-contract behaviour (never a crash). So there is no deployment-wide mandatory re-review.

### The built-in-disable mechanism is part of THIS story (clears G6)
ef7e's MVP implemented overlay RE-TUNE of a built-in (per-key routing merge) but NOT disable. This
story adds disable: an overlay `plan_review` entry for a BUILT-IN id carrying `"disabled": true`
REMOVES that built-in from `effective_criteria(repo_root)` (so its finder never runs) — implemented
in `registry.effective_criteria` (a disabled built-in is excluded from the returned set) +
`effective_routing` (the entry is retained but flagged). The set of disabled built-in ids is exposed
via a small `disabled_builtins(repo_root) -> list[str]` helper. The gate records them in the verdict
`coverage["disabled_builtins"]`, which `build_manifest` folds into the `disabled_builtins:` manifest
line. `_validate_routing_entry` accepts `disabled: bool` only on an un-prefixed (built-in) id (a
`project.` id cannot be "disabled" — it is simply not activated). This keeps the epic's "the overlay
may re-tune OR disable a built-in; a disable is recorded in coverage" AC coherent within this story.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions, run 2)

- [ ] Overlay-absent repos see NO regver change (existing attestations stay valid); the regver line
      already exists, so this adds only the staleness CHECK. A test asserts overlay-absent parity.
- [ ] An overlay `disabled: true` on a built-in id removes it from `effective_criteria`; a
      `disabled_builtins(repo_root)` helper lists them; they flow into `coverage` + the manifest line.
baseline.summary: Blocking policy + attestation integration (registry_version(repo_root), disabled_builtins, invalidation)

baseline.description:
## Symptom
`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` fails from the globally installed build with:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'commit_impact' from 'rebar._engine_support'
  File ".../src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py", line 283, in _check_file_impact_vs_diff
```

Observed against the pipx release snapshot `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases/d83fb4f6fdafeafa696238e76eff6933e5674607.98469`. The same close succeeds from the repo checkout's editable venv, so the module is present in the source tree (`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`, 6086 bytes, present at origin/main and in a worktree at 0b851c8103) but missing from — or unimportable in — the packaged release.

## Why it matters beyond one host
`close_precheck._check_file_impact_vs_diff` is on the completion-gate path, so this breaks closing ANY ticket that records `file_impact` when running a packaged build rather than a checkout. That is the normal path for an operator or agent using an installed rebar.

## The compounding defect: it exits 0
The traceback is printed and the process still reports `[exited with code 0]`. A caller checking the exit status concludes the close succeeded when the ticket is untouched. That silent-success behaviour is arguably the more serious half of this bug: an automated agent will record a close that never happened. A crashing precheck must exit non-zero.

## Repro
1. Install rebar as a package (pipx from a commit at or after the one that introduced `_engine_support/commit_impact.py`).
2. Take any ticket with a non-empty `file_impact` and the completion gate enabled.
3. `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` -> ImportError, exit 0, ticket unchanged.

## Expected
Either the module ships in the release (packaging/`MANIFEST`/package-data fix), or the import is resolved in a way that survives packaging; and a precheck that raises exits non-zero so the failure is not mistaken for success.

## Discovery context
Hit while closing RP-02 story convergent-pinelike-lunamoth. Worked around by closing from a git worktree using the checkout's venv build. Note this host auto-updates its global rebar hourly from origin/main, so the broken snapshot is a build of main, not a stale tagged release.
baseline.summary: Packaged rebar release omits _engine_support/commit_impact.py, breaking every close with file_impact

baseline.description:
## Context

Bug b636 (landed as 5e7d6e71ba) added deleted-source recovery to fsck. After the module-size split, `restore_deleted_sources` and `rebuild_with_restore` live in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py` (:127 and :182) and are re-exported from `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` (bottom-of-module import at :614).

Only ONE call site actually uses the composed helper — `repair_or_plan` (`fsck_repair.py:580`). The per-ticket repair path `_repair_ticket` (`fsck_repair.py:209`) still calls `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` DIRECTLY at :270-274, so it rebuilds from whatever sources survive and never attempts the restore. That path fails closed rather than corrupting anything, but a ticket whose SNAPSHOT source was dropped by legacy compaction is not recovered when repair runs through `_repair_ticket`.

`rebuild_with_restore`'s own docstring already calls itself "the repair path's single entrypoint", and no ADR or ticket records an intentional divergence between the two paths — this is a residual gap, not a deliberate split.

Discovered while closing story 9f7f (superseded into b636): every other acceptance criterion of 9f7f is implemented, this call site is the residual gap.

## Plan

Route `_repair_ticket`'s rebuild through `rebuild_with_restore` so the two repair entry points behave identically, and surface any restored sources in the `disp` dict the caller already consumes.

### The `no_commit` contract (must be preserved)

`_repair_ticket` takes `no_commit: bool = False` and currently forwards it: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)`. `no_commit` gates the git commit in `compact_rebuild.py:234`, and the batch repair loop at `fsck_repair.py:401-408` calls `_repair_ticket(..., no_commit=True)` so commits are deferred until after the whole batch.

`rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]` has NO `no_commit` parameter and calls the rebuild with the default `no_commit=False`. Routing naively would make the batch path commit once per ticket — a behavior change.

Worked example of the required contract:

- `rebuild_with_restore` gains a keyword-only `no_commit: bool = False` and forwards it verbatim: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)`.
- `_repair_ticket` calls `rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, no_commit=no_commit)` and unpacks `(rebuilt, restored)`.
- The existing `repair_or_plan` call at `fsck_repair.py:580` stays `rebuild_with_restore(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir)` — the new parameter defaults to `False`, which is that path's current behavior, so it is unchanged.
- Concretely: `_repair_ticket(tracker, tid, dir, dry_run=False, no_commit=True)` on a ticket with an auto-recoverable orphan restores the deleted source, rebuilds the snapshot, and leaves the tickets worktree DIRTY (no new commit on the `tickets` branch); with `no_commit=False` it commits exactly as it does today.

### Reporting

`_repair_ticket`'s `disp` dict gains a `"restored"` key holding the restored filenames list (empty list when nothing was restored), mirroring what `repair_or_plan` surfaces as "after restoring N deleted event(s)".

### Import cycle

`fsck_repair` imports `fsck_restore` at the BOTTOM of the module (:614) to let the leaf lazily import `snapshot_missing_sources`. `_repair_ticket` therefore uses a function-local `from rebar._commands.fsck_restore import rebuild_with_restore` (the same lazy-import shape the current code uses for `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` at :270) rather than a new module-level import.

### No double-restore

`restore_deleted_sources` skips any name already present on disk as `<name>` or `<name>.retired`, and `rebuild_with_restore` only attempts a restore when `snapshot_missing_sources(ticket_dir)` is non-empty. A second pass over the same ticket therefore restores nothing and reports an empty list — that idempotency is the invariant AC4 asserts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_repair_ticket` obtains its rebuild through `rebuild_with_restore`, not a direct `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` call.
      Verify: `grep -n "rebuild_with_restore" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shows a call inside `_repair_ticket`, and `grep -n "rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` shows no call in `_repair_ticket`.
- [x] `rebuild_with_restore` accepts a keyword-only `no_commit: bool = False` and forwards it to `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`; `_repair_ticket` passes its own `no_commit` through.
      Verify: `grep -n "no_commit" src/rebar/_commands/fsck_restore.py`.
- [x] `_repair_ticket`'s returned `disp` dict carries a `"restored"` list of restored source filenames.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] A held-out test proves a ticket whose SNAPSHOT source was deleted by legacy compaction is recovered when repair runs via `_repair_ticket` (RED before the change).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] A test proves `_repair_ticket(..., no_commit=True)` creates no new commit on the tickets branch while still restoring and rebuilding.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] A test proves a second `_repair_ticket` pass over the same ticket restores nothing (no double-restore, empty `"restored"`).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_repair_restore_08c8.py -q`.
- [x] The `repair_or_plan` call site at `fsck_repair.py:580` is unchanged in behavior and existing fsck repair/restore tests pass unchanged.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py tests/interfaces/store -q -k "fsck or restore or repair"`.
baseline.summary: fsck _repair_ticket bypasses rebuild_with_restore, so repair never restores deleted SNAPSHOT sources

baseline.description:
## The defect is the INVISIBILITY, not the loss

`.tickets-tracker` lives **inside** the worktree (`<worktree>/.tickets-tracker`). Ticket events are committed there immediately and auto-pushed to `sync.remote`. When that push is backed up, retiring the worktree — `git worktree remove`, the retirement step the `/rebar-debug` and `/rebar-implement` skills both prescribe — **deletes unpushed ticket events permanently**.

That alone would be a bug. What makes it a defect worth its own ticket is that **the loss is undetectable by the checks an agent would actually run**:

- `rebar show <id>` reads **local** state, so it reports `status: closed` whether or not the
  close ever left the machine. An agent that closes a ticket, confirms with `rebar show`, and
  retires its worktree has done everything the guidance asks and still loses the close.
- A later reader sees a **closed ticket**. The store does not have it. There is no error, no
  warning at retirement time, and no artifact pointing at what went missing.

This is the `sphinxian-agrarian-snake` (`3fce-cccf-d38b-4072`) shape exactly: *a check whose pass result is indistinguishable from the check never having run*. Here the overloaded signal is `rebar show` reporting `closed` — identical output for "closed and shared" and "closed into a directory that is about to be deleted".

## Measured, on bug 84c7-486f (`surprised-convincing-gopher`), 2026-08-21

The close of that bug came within one command of being destroyed. Numbers as observed:

| Observation | Value |
|---|---|
| unpushed ticket commits in the worktree tracker at close time | **138** |
| backlog across successive auto-push attempts | **103 -> 190 -> 194** (growing, not draining) |
| `rebar doctor` | **structurally clean throughout** — 15 findings, all pre-existing link-shape issues on unrelated tickets; locks free |
| `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` | **0 stranded index entries, 0 foreign top-level paths** |
| `rebar show surprised-convincing-gopher` | `status: closed` |

**That last pair is the crux.** Both existing diagnostics reported a healthy store, and the read command reported a closed ticket, while the close existed **nowhere but a directory about to be deleted**. Whatever remedy is chosen has to close that gap: today, health checks pass and reads look right in exactly the state where retirement destroys data.

The loss was caught only by an **ad-hoc** comparison of local vs remote event sets, which is not a check anything prescribes:

```
        event                 remote   local
        STATUS                  0        1     <- the close
        COMPLETION_VERDICT      0        1     <- the signed verdict
        SIGNATURE               1        2
        LINK                    4        5     <- the caused_by
```

The push was not broken and the store was not corrupt: after a fetch the branch was `remote-only: 0, local-only: 141` — a clean fast-forward was available and rebar's own auto-reconcile merge commits were present. The auto-push was simply losing a race against a busy shared remote. Driving it with further rebar writes eventually reached `unpushed ticket commits : 0`, after which `STATUS 1/1`, `COMPLETION_VERDICT 1/1`, `SIGNATURE 2/2`, `LINK 5/5` and divergence 0 both ways were confirmed against a fresh fetch. **Retirement one minute earlier would have lost all of it.**

Note the exposure is not hypothetical or confined to one session: this is a machine with ~90 live worktrees, and the shared checkout's own tracker showed **14 unpushed** while this ticket was being filed.

## This is the third instance of one class: tracker-derived state living per-worktree

- `intangible-ladyish-vicuna` (`93a9-66cf-e681-4f49`, **closed**) — compaction trigger sidecars
  were worktree-local rather than store-scoped, so two worktree views of one store each held
  the "one compactor at a time" lock simultaneously.
- `nuclear-calm-heron` (`da68-fc7c-068c-4c53`, **in_progress** — the fix for the enrichment
  drain is described in vicuna as landed, but the ticket is not closed, so treat this as an
  open sibling rather than a second completed repair) — "worktree-local drain lock does not
  serialise a shared store".
- **This ticket** — the tracker's *unpushed event backlog* is worktree-local, and worktree
  retirement is a destructive operation with no awareness of it.

The first two are about **correctness under concurrency**; this one is about **durability under teardown**. Same root shape — state that belongs to the store is scoped to a worktree — which is why it is filed as a sibling rather than folded into either.

## Explicitly NOT proposing a design

Several remedies are plausible and they are **not** equivalent in scope, so the choice must be justified rather than assumed. Recording the options only so the next agent does not have to rediscover them:

- a **pre-retirement guard** that refuses or warns when the tracker has unpushed commits;
- a **push-drain** on worktree removal;
- a **`rebar doctor` leg** that reports unpushed commits as a finding (today it does not);
- making `rebar show` (or the close path) **surface unshared state** so the read stops being
  ambiguous;
- **relocating the tracker** out of the worktree entirely.

Some of these are restoration; at least one (relocating the tracker) is a substantial architectural change, and a guard on `git worktree remove` reaches a command rebar does not own — a portability question, since not every environment retires worktrees the same way, and a capability whose only trigger is one workflow is not portable. **Do not treat the option list as a decision.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure is reproduced deliberately: a ticket event committed to a worktree tracker
      with a non-empty unpushed backlog, the worktree retired, and the event shown absent from
      `sync.remote` while `rebar show` still reported the local status.
- [ ] The chosen remedy is **justified against the alternatives listed above**, with the
      reasoning recorded on this ticket, including an explicit statement of whether it restores
      intended behaviour or adds new capability, and whether it is portable across environments
      that do not use git worktrees.
- [ ] After the change, the state in which retirement destroys data is **detectable by a check
      an agent would actually run** — the specific check named, and shown failing before the fix
      and passing after. `rebar doctor` reporting clean and `tracker-maintenance --status`
      reporting 0 stranded entries while a close is unshared must no longer both be true.
- [ ] A test exercises the unshared-close state, seen RED before the fix.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full suite stay green.

## Provenance

Found while closing bug `surprised-convincing-gopher` (`84c7-486f-9a13-4c3f`) under `/rebar-debug`. Not fixed there: that bug is scoped to the `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` table->tree invariant, and the remedy here is undecided and may be architectural.

Two evidence divergences from that bug's close are recorded here as well, since they bear on how much its green result should be trusted:

1. Its AC *"the full unit sweep stays green"* was met by **CI, not by a local run** — the host
   sat at load 22-54 from concurrent sessions for the entire session and no local full sweep
   ever completed. Evidence is CI run 32488951833 (green on ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos
   py3.13); the more informative datum is the patchset-1 run, `1 failed, 15169 passed`, whose
   single failure was that change's own comment-hygiene defect.
2. Its AC *"`tests/scripts/test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` must stay green"* is met in
   final state but **not literally**: removing the ghost rows correctly turned that test RED
   (its fixture selected a helper via `next(iter(KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS))`, which resolved to a
   ghost row), and it required a fixture repair. The divergence was recorded rather than the AC
   reworded, since rewording AC prose would have staled the plan-review attestation.
baseline.summary: Retiring a worktree silently destroys unpushed ticket events, and every existing check reports healthy

## Context / Problem

Adding the `[code_review]` section re-export in ticket `unaroused-undead-ibisbill` took `src/rebar/config.py` from 799 to exactly 800 lines. The CI module-size gate fails on `loc > cap` with cap 800 (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so the file passes today but the NEXT line added to it — a new section class re-export, a new owned accessor — fails CI, and the limit is locked so it cannot be raised by a contributor.

## Approach

Split `src/rebar/config.py` along an existing call-graph seam, the same way `_config_schema.py` and `_config_sources.py` were already carved out of it, so the facade regains headroom without changing any public import path (`from rebar.config import X` must keep working — the module already re-exports every moved name).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/config.py` — extract one cohesive cluster into a sibling private module.
- the new sibling module.
- tests covering the moved surface, if any assert on the old location.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/config.py` is at most 700 lines (`wc -l`), leaving headroom under the 800 cap.
- [ ] Every name importable from `rebar.config` before the split is still importable after —
      verified by the existing config test suite passing unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling selector writes a labeled candidate manifest — per criterion, the candidates with their direction, tier, supporting signals and rank. Nothing yet turns that into files the eval runner can consume, and the format is not free-form: `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` rejects a spec lacking an explicit `epochs`, a satisfiable `at_least(k)` gate, a `coverage_threshold` in [0, 1], a non-empty `scorers` list with a registered deterministic scorer, a balanced dataset, or a non-empty `gold_set` whose entries each carry `input` and `label` (`eval.py:252-272`, `eval.py:288-300`). Each dataset case must also carry a payload field beyond the metadata keys (`eval.py:249-250`).

Two constraints cannot be met by transcription. A criterion may yield candidates on only one side of the fire/no-fire axis, failing the balance rule (`eval.py:252-255`); and a stale file from an earlier run would survive for a now-skipped criterion, keeping a retired assertion in the suite.

## Approach

An emitter that reads the manifest and writes one `.eval.yaml` per criterion into a working directory for the sibling admission runner. It issues no model call and reads NOTHING beyond the manifest — a pure, deterministic function of the manifest rows.

**Case payloads are DERIVED, not transcribed.** The selector's candidate row (`fixture_selection.py:33-38`) carries only `criterion`, `direction`, `norm_id`, `tier`, `rank`, `signals`, `escaped_defect`, `abs_margin`, `review_event_uuid` — no plan prose, no `expect`, no `corpus`, no case `id`, no gold material. The emitter derives every emitted field from those row fields by a fixed rule, with no model call:

- `expect` (dataset) and `label` (gold) come from the row's `direction`: `fire` → `finding`,
  `no_fire` → `pass`. This is the only fire/no-fire → validator-axis mapping.
- `id` is `<prompt_id>-<direction>-<rank>`, `prompt_id` =
  `criteria.ids.criterion_prompt_id(criterion)`; unique because fire/no_fire ranks are
  namespaced by direction.
- `corpus` is the constant `rebar`; `criterion` is the row's `criterion`.
- `input` is a deterministic, model-free provenance descriptor rendered from the row's stable
  fields (its `criterion`, `direction`, `tier`, sorted `signals`, and `norm_id` (fire) or
  `review_event_uuid` (no_fire) and `rank`). It is NOT authored prose and NOT resolved from any
  store; it satisfies the validator's payload-field requirement and gives the gold entry a
  stable, unique reference.
- `gold_set` is one `{input, label}` entry per emitted case (same `input`, `label` = the case's
  `expect`), so gold material exists precisely when a criterion contributes dataset cases.

**Emitted spec fields.** Each file carries the field set of the committed `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`: `prompt`, `model`, `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0`, a `scorers` list holding the registered deterministic scorer `emits_valid_findings`, a `dataset` of `{id, corpus, criterion, expect, input}` cases, and a `gold_set` of `{input, label}` entries. `epochs: 3` with `at_least(2)` matches every shipped spec.

**Case selection.** At most 8 cases per criterion, at most 4 per side, taken in the manifest's recorded rank order, so the output is a deterministic function of the manifest.

**Balance guarantee.** A criterion that cannot supply at least one candidate row on EACH side emits NO file and is counted `skipped-unbalanced`. Because dataset cases and their gold entries both derive from candidate rows, a one-sided criterion — and equally a criterion present only as a `zero_candidate` row — yields no balanced dataset and no gold material, so it never reaches the validator. The sibling self-healing loop counts `skipped-unbalanced` as a failed attempt, so a persistently unbalanced criterion is recorded by that child's `unreliable-criterion:` breaker rather than vanishing silently.

**Output lifecycle.** Each run writes a fresh temporary tree and atomically replaces the working directory, so no file survives for a criterion that has become skipped or already has a spec.

## Scope

The emitter module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/`, its YAML serialization, the deterministic per-field derivation above, the per-side case selection, the balance refusal and the emitter report. It reads the manifest and writes only into its own working directory.

## Non-goals

- Deciding which candidates qualify, their tier, or their rank; the selector owns that.
- Writing into `.rebar/evals/` or admitting a spec; the admission runner owns both.
- Any model call, or any read of the ticket store, git, or the review corpus.
- Emitting for a criterion that already has a spec (`eval.py:69-78` resolves a project spec as
  a replacement, so a mined file would delete the packaged cases).

## Testing

Unit tests over the serializer and the balance refusal using synthetic manifests, invoking the real `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` on every emitted file rather than asserting on YAML text. Every assertion is deterministic because no model is involved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every emitted spec returns zero errors from `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)`;
      verified by `pytest` invoking the real validator over each emitted file.
- [x] An emitted spec carries `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0`;
      verified by `pytest` asserting those three values on a spec from a synthetic manifest.
- [x] An emitted spec's `scorers` list holds an entry naming `emits_valid_findings`; verified
      by `pytest` asserting that scorer name is present.
- [x] Each dataset case's `expect` is `finding` for a `fire` candidate, `pass` for a `no_fire`
      candidate; verified by `pytest` asserting the mapping on a mixed-direction manifest.
- [x] Each gold_set entry's `label` equals its case's `expect`; verified by `pytest` asserting
      label equality on the same spec.
- [x] A criterion whose manifest holds candidates on only one side emits no file and is counted
      `skipped-unbalanced`; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent and the report
      names the criterion.
- [x] A criterion present with no candidate row on either side (e.g. only a `zero_candidate`
      row) emits no file and is counted `skipped-unbalanced`; verified by `pytest` asserting the
      path is absent and the report names the criterion.
- [x] Given a manifest with 6 ranked candidates on one side (the other side non-empty), the
      emitted dataset holds the first 4 in rank order; verified by `pytest` asserting the case
      ids and order.
- [x] A file from a previous run for a criterion absent from the current manifest does not
      survive the next run; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent after the second
      run.
- [x] Two consecutive runs over the same manifest emit byte-identical output; verified by
      `diff -r` of the two output trees exiting 0.
- [x] The emitter completes with the repository's network guard active; verified by `pytest`
      running it under that guard.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` pass; a run over the real manifest emits specs that all pass the strict validator; the diff touches nothing under `.rebar/evals/` or `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`.

## Budget

**$0.** Emission is a pure, model-free function of the manifest.
baseline.summary: Emit validated per-criterion eval specs from the labeled candidate manifest

baseline.description:
## Problem

`llm/workflow/snapshot.py:181-187` streams `git archive` through a pipe with **no timeout, an undrained stderr pipe, and inherited stdin**:

```python
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["git", "-C", root, "archive", "--format=tar", sha],
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.PIPE,          # never drained until AFTER the tar stream
)
with tarfile.open(fileobj=proc.stdout, mode="r|") as tar:   # :187 — blocks here
    tar.extractall(path=str(tmp), filter=_hardened_filter(max_bytes))
_, stderr = proc.communicate()        # unreachable while :187 blocks; also unbounded
```

Three defects in one call:

1. **No `timeout=`** on the `Popen` or on `communicate()`.
2. **`stderr=PIPE` is never drained** while stdout is being consumed. If the child writes more
   than the pipe buffer (~64 KiB) to stderr, it blocks writing stderr, therefore stops writing
   stdout, and the parent blocks forever in `tarfile.__read` waiting for stdout. Classic
   undrained-pipe deadlock; needs no network and no partial clone.
3. **stdin is inherited** (no `stdin=DEVNULL`), unlike `_store/push.py:221` and
   `enrich_drain.py:329` which do set it — so a credential or host-key prompt can block here too.

## Reproduced deterministically (twice)

Found while investigating `unquieting-godsent-mammal` (`b405-d5ec-30b3-4538`). Both reproductions drove the REAL `snapshot_at_ref` and blocked at the same line, with byte-identical stacks:

```
File ".../tarfile.py", line 566 in __read
...
File ".../src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py", line 187 in snapshot_at_ref
```

**Repro A — promisor lazy-fetch stall.** A partial clone (`--filter=blob:none`) with 4 genuinely missing blobs, its promisor remote repointed at a TCP black hole (accepts, never replies). The process sat at `STAT=SN, %CPU 0.0` for 4m26s with zero bytes on stdout and stderr, and was still blocked when killed. `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT=5` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` were both set and neither rescued it. A **control on a full (non-partial) clone against the same black hole completed in 0.02 s**, proving the stall is reached only through the lazy-fetch path.

**Repro B — stderr deadlock, no network at all.** A fake `git` on `PATH` writing a valid tar to stdout and ~200 KB to stderr midway, against a healthy local clone. Parent and child both wedged at `SN / 0.0%` indefinitely.

## Honest scope: this is NOT the cause of b405

`snapshot_at_ref` is referenced only at `llm/workflow/__init__.py:66` (an export) and is **not reachable from `llm/plan_review/` or `_commands/close_precheck.py`** — verified by grep over `src/rebar`. So it is not on the `review-plan` / `transition -> closed` paths that hang in the field. Filing it separately rather than folding it into b405, because attaching a real-but- off-path finding to that investigation would corrupt its evidence.

Note also that repro B's trigger has not been shown to occur naturally: a real `git archive` emitted **0 bytes** of stderr in measurement, because git suppresses progress when stderr is not a TTY — and `Popen` gives it a pipe. So defect 2 is a **proven latent deadlock**, not an observed field failure. Defect 1 (the promisor stall) is the one with a demonstrated multi-minute block.

## Constraints on the fix (from prior tickets)

- `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` is neither `OSError` nor `CalledProcessError`, so it escapes existing
  `except` tuples, and `TimeoutExpired.cmd` carries any `user:token@host` URL — found the hard way
  in `dominant-northbound-blackrhino` (`77e1-7f82-98e6-4fed`). Route it through this module's
  error conversion or a hang becomes a credential disclosure.
- Elapsed time is the wrong axis for a stalled transfer (`_snapshot/git_fetch.py:169`);
  `suave-constant-cow` (`12e4-8c74-a738-4014`) built the reusable `stall_abort_args()` seam
  (`http.lowSpeedLimit` / `lowSpeedTime`). Prefer splicing that for any network-reaching git call
  over only shortening a wall clock.
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` requires a `# raw-git-ok:` marker on new/edited raw git
  subprocess sites.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A `git archive` child that writes more than the pipe buffer to stderr does not deadlock the
      parent — verified by a test using a fake `git` that does exactly that, observed FAILING
      before the fix.
- [x] The subprocess is bounded, and a stalled child is terminated rather than left running —
      verified by a test that stalls the child and asserts both that the call returns and that no
      orphan child survives.
- [x] `stdin` is not inherited, so no prompt can block this call.
- [x] A `TimeoutExpired` raised here cannot leak a credential-bearing command line into an error
      message or log — verified by a test asserting the redaction.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.
baseline.summary: git archive stream in workflow snapshot has no timeout, an undrained stderr pipe, and inherited stdin

baseline.description:
# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: E1 — Force measurement provenance into attested evidence

## Operator remediation — apply the value_wo migration, scrub existing cleartext from remote state, and rotate the exposed crown-jewel secrets

This is the PROD-mutation follow-through for the code change landed under `finedrawn-closed-stud` (eb67-b96c-dcf0-4f86), which migrated every SSM SecureString **secret** parameter to terraform write-only arguments (`value_wo` / `value_wo_version`) so secret values are never persisted to terraform state (ADR 0105). The code change alone does NOT mutate prod; this ticket is the operator cutover.

**Run this only AFTER the value_wo code change has landed on main.** Follow the procedure in `infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` §"REMEDIATE the existing exposure".

### Steps
1. `terraform apply` the value_wo migration. NOTE the one-time cutover reset: on this apply
   `value_wo_version` goes absent -> 1 for each migrated slot, so the provider re-sends
   `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` once and RESETS each live seeded secret to the placeholder. This is
   intended (we rotate these secrets in the same window). `user_data.sh`'s CHANGEME fail-fast is
   the safety net.
2. In the SAME maintenance window, re-seed/ROTATE every affected secret out-of-band
   (`aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite`). Rotate the crown-jewels explicitly — they were exposed
   in cleartext in state and must be treated as compromised: Gerrit admin password, opcert
   Ed25519 signing key, rebar-bot signing key, Anthropic API key, jira-api-token, SSH host keys.
   Update every external system that trusts an old value (Gerrit account, Jira token, bot public
   key, Anthropic console).
3. VERIFY no SecureString value appears in state: `terraform state pull` must show `value: null`
   (and no `value_wo`) for every migrated secret. Only the generated `opcert_origin_guard`
   legitimately still resolves (via its random_password).
4. SCRUB the historical cleartext from the state backend: the prior values persist in the retained
   versions of `s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate` (bucket versioning,
   ~149 versions). Permanently delete the affected object versions (or roll the bucket / lifecycle-
   expire old versions per data-handling policy). Rotated values are retired but still purge them.

### Coordination
- Coordinate with the SEPARATE "rubied" apply that is seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params so the
  state scrub covers those params too (they are also SecureString secrets under /rebar/prod/).
- Cross-reference: ADR 0105 (docs/adr/0105-ssm-secrets-never-in-terraform-state.md) and the runbook
  infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] value_wo migration applied to prod.
- [ ] Every migrated secret re-seeded/rotated; crown-jewels rotated and external trust updated.
- [ ] `terraform state pull` shows no SecureString secret value (all `value: null`, no `value_wo`).
- [ ] Historical cleartext purged from the state bucket's retained versions.
- [ ] rubied MCP-PAT params covered by the same scrub.
baseline.summary: Operator: apply value_wo SSM migration, scrub cleartext from remote tfstate, rotate exposed crown-jewel secrets

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar's CLI facade on current main is 714 lines and reconstructs command identity and policy through 19 overlapping frozensets, an intercept ladder, package-help filenames, a regex-based reference generator, and repeated test censuses. The existing CLI reference is generated, but its syntax authority is not: it embeds 54 hand-maintained help resources plus a curated intercept table, so parser/help drift can pass while the census remains complete.

Twenty-one intercept-only commands lack safe canonical help. `rebar help <command>` reports them unknown, while handler-owned `--help` is inconsistent and can execute work. The maintainer approved normalizing every visible command and approved deriving syntax/options from the same parser definitions used by execution.

## Approved Architecture
Create one stdlib-only immutable lazy route registry. A route records canonical identity, spellings/visibility, lazy handler and parser-factory references, a bounded invocation-adapter kind, generated package-help key, mount/init policy, confirmation/output policy, and possible semantic capabilities. The registry is a routing table, not a plugin system, DI container, or middleware framework.

Every command grammar is built by a side-effect-free stdlib `argparse` factory. Runtime handlers and build-time generation call that same factory. Existing argparse builders are extracted; imperative parsers migrate with accepted/rejected argv, `--` handling, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes pinned by behavioral tests. A narrow shared ArgumentParser subclass/formatter may preserve Rebar diagnostics; no docs-only parser, source-regex grammar, Click dependency, or second parser is introduced.

Generation resolves all parser factories at build/check time using fixed `prog`, width, and formatter policy, then commits package-help and overview bytes. Runtime overview/help, aliases, malformed global syntax, and unknown-command output read only those bytes before RP-04 operation snapshot, config materialization, mount, handler resolution, or optional imports. The lexical top-level selector identifies only the spelling and first-token help/unknown forms; nested argv remains selected-handler-owned.

A separate semantic capability registry maps capabilities to packaging extras and missing postures: `error`, `unavailable`, `abstain`, or intentional `fallback`. Routes advertise possibilities only; checks occur after the selected mode/backend is known, and domain components retain degraded result shapes.

## Compatibility Contracts
Exact aliases reuse canonical grammar/help. `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, and `jira-onboard` compose canonical argument-definition helpers with alias-specific `prog`/replacement prose; `jira-onboard` keeps its historical spelling. Hidden `bridge-status` is explicitly helpable but undiscoverable. `purge-bridge` remains unknown.

Help/unknown paths never compose an operation or mount. Execution retains central best-effort mount, strict init, confirmation/global-output behavior, legacy JSON shapes, tokens after `--`, and established streams/exit codes. Accepted grammar changes are limited to the separately approved safe-help normalization unless a ticket names another intentional delta. `rebar-mcp` remains a separate entry point.

## Migration and Rollback
Use expand/contract by command family. Add the registry/parser contract and derived compatibility exports; migrate each handler and its runtime parser together; generate authoritative artifacts only after the complete parser/route census passes; then move execution, capabilities, docs/distribution consumers, and finally remove compatibility authorities. No shipped phase may contain a docs-only grammar runtime ignores.

During expansion, rollback selects derived compatibility exports and reverts a parser family with its generated artifacts. After contraction, code revert restores the old router. Ticket, event, bridge, and binding formats do not change.

## Delivery Order
1. Record the architecture decision and prior-art constraints.
2. Establish the parser/registry foundation; migrate core and advanced parser families in parallel; generate canonical package help only after both complete.
3. Migrate lazy execution and semantic capability boundaries.
4. Derive reference/distribution checks from registries and generated parser artifacts.
5. Retire duplicate authorities and complete cutover.

## Testing
Use unit tests for pure registry/parser validation; command-family production-path parity tests for accepted/rejected argv and errors; real subprocess tests for exact committed bytes, streams, exit codes, aliases, and absence of operation/config/mount/handler effects; a clean no-extras wheel for every help form; and a full-extra lane for lazy-reference resolution. Generator `--check` must prove parser-rendered artifacts and `docs/cli-reference.md` are byte-current.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every command's runtime parsing and generated syntax/options come from one side-effect-free argparse factory; no docs-only/manual syntax authority remains.
- [x] Every visible canonical command appears once in the grouped overview and both top-level help forms return byte-current generated package data before operation/config/store/handler boundaries.
- [x] Exact, compatibility, hidden, and retired spellings exhibit the approved behavior, including historical `jira-onboard` and unknown `purge-bridge`.
- [x] Lazy execution preserves mount/init, argv, confirmation, stream, exit-code, and legacy-output contracts except the explicit help normalization.
- [x] Selected optional modes/backends preserve approved capability postures without eager optional imports.
- [x] CLI-reference generation, coverage, lean-wheel checks, and full-extra resolution enumerate registries/parser artifacts rather than source regexes or manual command censuses.
- [x] Duplicate authorities are removed after shadow parity; quality gates pass and no stored-data migration occurs.
- [x] ADR 0100 and living architecture record the parser, route, capability, migration, compatibility, and rollback boundaries.
baseline.summary: RP-05 — Lazy CLI command and capability registry with canonical help

## Target
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — **799 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (1 lines of headroom).

One line of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

baseline.description:
# S6 — Bounded concurrent gate executions, with fast-fail admission

Implements the decision headed **"Bounded concurrency with FAST-FAIL admission (S6)"** in the LANDED `docs/adr/0112-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture.md` on `origin/main`. Decisions are cited by HEADING, never number: prerequisite 7dfa records an earlier, shorter Decision list whose numbers do not match the merged file.

## Why

S2–S5 cap each accumulator with a high-water-mark GC, and **a watermark GC assumes evictable data exists**. The janitor takes no per-reader lease and relies on POSIX delete-on-last-close, so it may `unlink` an in-flight snapshot but the blocks return only when the last reader closes. Under the operator's **~10 parallel plan reviews** the held bytes are LIVE, not garbage: the GC finds nothing evictable and the volume fills anyway. Both gates copy the repo at a ref and share **ONE counter** (two caps of N each admit 2N); at capacity the call **fast-fails**, since a queued gate still holds its thread, ~739 MB resident, and the client's request.

## Design

**Seam.** `peak_rss.gate_peak_rss` already wraps this scope and says why: wrapping `review_plan()` / `verify_completion()` "covers both call paths at one seam, since both reach the gate through these functions". Admission takes that seam but sits strictly OUTSIDE it, since `gate_peak_rss` wraps only the run while the bytes are spent earlier. It becomes the **outermost `with`** in each entry point, enclosing every byte-spending step: in `review_plan`, `resolve_gate_handle(...)` plus the run; in `verify_completion` it must open before `resolve_gate_handle` AND enclose `_resolve_completion_ticket_view` (which materializes the pinned ticket store and may rebind `handle`) plus the `try/finally` closing that view — the whole remainder of the function.

**Counter.** N slot files in the store's existing `locks/` dir, each held for the run under a non-blocking `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, released in a `finally`. Cross-process (AC4) and crash-safe (AC5: the kernel drops a flock when the holder dies — no heartbeat, which the janitor rejected as unsound). It also serialises across threads of one process, since a flock is held by the open file description and each acquisition opens its own; and it inherits `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, following gate scratch onto the ADR's dedicated volume.

**Degradation is SPLIT**, per the ADR's consequence that admission must treat an unreachable scratch volume as a refusal, not "an empty cache to repopulate onto the root filesystem":

- **No `fcntl`, or one slot file unusable inside a healthy `locks/` dir** — ADMIT, and emit one
  `GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED {json}` marker naming the reason. Refusing would turn a platform gap
  into a total gate outage, and the free-space floor still applies; but a silently disarmed cap
  is how bug 3276 recurs, so it is never silent.
- **The store root unreachable** (scratch volume unmounted or read-only, so `store_root()` /
  `locks/` cannot be created) — **REFUSE**, with `GateScratchUnavailableError` (same `LLMError`
  base and retryable outcome, its own `gate_scratch_unavailable` code). Admitting would silently
  relocate gate scratch back onto the root filesystem — the failure this epic prevents. No
  marker: a raised refusal already reaches the caller and its log.

**Refusal — the hierarchy decides the mapping.** `GateCongestedError` lives in `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` as a **direct subclass of `LLMError`** (not `LLMRunnerError`: no runner ran) and attaches `.outcome = LLMOutcome(WAIT_AND_RETRY, retryable=True)` in `__init__`. Those two facts fire the mapping through arms that ALREADY exist, so **no new `except` clause is added**:

- MCP: `_review_plan_body` / `_verify_completion_body` catch `rebar.llm.LLMError` →
  `_structured_llm_failure`, which reads `outcome_of(exc)` (`getattr(exc, "outcome", None)`), so
  the attached outcome gives `retryable: true` (without it, `false`), and no `verdict` key is
  emitted — congestion is unreadable as INDETERMINATE, BLOCK or FAIL.
- CLI: both handlers catch `llm.LLMError` → `_llm_error_exit_code`, returning **11** ("transient
  — retry") exactly when `outcome.retryable`, else 1, after an `Error:` line.
- `_errors._llm_error_code` gains branches for both new types returning `"gate_congested"` /
  `"gate_scratch_unavailable"`, in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`, placed **before every existing arm** (the
  bare `isinstance(exc, LLMError)` would otherwise report them as `command_failed`). The
  error-taxonomy contract test asserts the family is EXHAUSTIVELY mapped, so both are registered
  there too — it verifies this in-session.

**Metric (AC7).** One line-start `GATE_CONGESTED {json}` stderr marker per refusal, following the `GATE_PEAK_RSS` journald convention (the containers hold no AWS credentials) — also portable: identical under the CLI with no CloudWatch and no CI provider.

**Config (AC6).** `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, resolved by `resolve_gate_max_concurrent` beside `resolve_gate_min_free_bytes`. `0` disables the bound (the `max_bytes` idiom); a malformed or negative value falls back to the default rather than disarming the cap. No `REBAR_GATE_*` env tier, deviating from the ADR's measured-defaults decision: a new `REBAR_*` literal is a new `env_var` mechanism, unlandable today per bug `a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a`, while `[snapshot]` keys are exempt (`_RESERVED_SECTIONS`, absent from `_SECTIONS`).

**Default = 4, from measurement.** `GATE_PEAK_RSS`: plan_review ~748 MB, verify_completion ~462 MB (the ADR cites ~739 MB and a degraded run at 501 MB, so it varies). The host is a `t4g.large` (8 GiB) shared with Gerrit and the ADR's host-sizing decision forbids growing it; ~2.17 GB steady state plus Gerrit's ~3 GiB reservation leave roughly 3 GiB for gate work. 4 × 748 MB ≈ 2.99 GB fits; a fifth run (~3.74 GB) does not — and 4 is well below the observed ~10 concurrent, so the cap actually sheds load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: one counter bounds both gates — hold `limit` slots as `plan_review`, assert a
  `verify_completion` admission is refused.
- [x] AC2: the refused call returns in under one second while a holder still runs (it
  fast-fails rather than blocking or queueing).
- [x] AC3a: the message names host congestion and says to retry; on the review-bot path this is
  ADR 0069's retryable deferral, never an `LLM-Review −1`.
- [x] AC3b: not readable as a verdict — the MCP body returns `retryable: true`,
  `error == "gate_congested"`, and NO `verdict` key.
- [x] AC3c: the CLI returns exit 11 on a congestion refusal.
- [x] AC4: a real child process holds every slot; this process is refused.
- [x] AC5a: SIGKILL a holder, assert a later admission wins (no lost slot).
- [x] AC5b: raise inside the wrapper, assert the next admission succeeds.
- [x] AC6a: the cap reads `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, defaults to 4, treats 0 as off, and
  falls back to the default on a malformed or negative value — one test each.
- [x] AC6b: `docs/config.md` and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` both name the key, default and
  rationale; the latter says a congestion refusal is an expected outcome, not a failure.
- [x] AC7: a refusal emits exactly one `GATE_CONGESTED` marker naming gate, ticket and limit; an
  admitted gate emits none.
- [x] AC8a: with `fcntl` unavailable the gate is admitted AND one `GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED`
  marker naming the reason is emitted.
- [x] AC8b: with `store_root()` raising, the gate is REFUSED, not admitted.

## Testing & file impact

`pytest tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py -q`, the taxonomy contract test, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q`.

New: `llm/gate_admission.py`, `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py`. Edited: `llm/errors.py`, `llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, `llm/completion.py`, `_config_resolvers.py`, `_errors.py`, the taxonomy contract test, `docs/config.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. Unchanged: `_mcp_llm.py`, `_cli/_llm_commands.py`.
