baseline.description:
## Why
THE security-critical divergence. e165 (change 563, commit 2efdae38f) implemented key validity as an **HLC-epoch** window (ordinal position in the reducer's canonical replay). The APPROVED epic design requires **git-commit-ancestry** validity (tickets-branch commit SHAs). HLC ordering is partly author-assigned, so a malicious clone holding a later-revoked key can write an event with a backdated HLC that sorts BEFORE the revocation and verifies as valid — defeating the feature's "not attacker-controllable" promise. The immutable commit DAG closes that hole. (User rejected the delivered design; see d7c0.)

## Why the DAG is stronger
Commit SHAs chain content+parents, so an event's position in history is a tamper-proof fact — you cannot make a new event an ancestor of an existing revocation commit without forging SHAs. HLC ordering trusts the author-assigned timestamp component; commit ancestry trusts only the DAG.

## Architecture decision — pure reducer + git-aware resolver (READ FIRST)
The reducer (`_processors.py`) is **pure-filesystem** today (no git/subprocess) and MUST stay so (its output is cache-keyed; it runs on plain event-file directories). Commit SHAs are git metadata not in event JSON, so we do NOT store SHAs in reduced state. Instead:

- **Reducer keyring fold (pure):** records each key's lifecycle by **event position** (the
  `{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` filename prefix the reducer already parses) — record shape
  `{public_key, added_at: <position>, revoked_at: <position|None>}`. Drop `added_epoch` /
  `revoked_epoch` / `keyring_epoch`. `state["keys"]` = keys with `revoked_at is None`.
- **Git-aware resolver (new, in `authorship.py`, the attest layer — NOT the reducer):**
  - `resolve_event_commit(position, ticket_dir, *, repo_root) -> str | None`: maps a
    position prefix to the tickets-branch commit SHA that introduced that event file.
    **TYPE is NOT an input** to the resolver, so it globs the position prefix:
    `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "<ticket_dir>/<position>-*.json"` run in the
    tracker dir, taking the (single) introducing commit. Returns `None` on any git failure
    or no match (fail-closed).
  - `verify_authorship_at_commit(envelope, identity_id, event_commit, event_position, *,
    repo_root) -> Verdict`: builds the trust root from exactly the keys valid at
    `event_commit`. A key K is valid iff **`merge-base --is-ancestor(K.added_commit,
    event_commit)` AND NOT `merge-base --is-ancestor(K.revoked_commit, event_commit)`**,
    where `K.added_commit`/`K.revoked_commit` come from resolving K's `added_at`/`revoked_at`
    positions. This is where the AC's commit-anchored record
    `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit}` materializes (resolver output). ANY git
    subprocess failure (`git log` / `merge-base` non-zero, timeout, missing repo) resolves
    to a **non-verified** Verdict — the resolver/verifier NEVER raises (fail-closed, mirrors
    `resolve_trust_root`).
- **Intra-commit refinement (N-events-per-commit):** `batch_stage_and_commit` puts N event
  files in ONE commit, and `merge-base --is-ancestor(C, C)` is true, so when a key's
  add/revoke shares the event's commit the DAG cannot order them — refine with the
  **intra-commit position** (`{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` prefix ordering, which is a total order
  within that commit): a KEY_ADD in the same commit counts as added iff its position ≤ the
  event position; a KEY_REVOKE in the same commit counts as revoked iff its position ≤ the
  event position. NOTE this HLC tiebreak is NOT the rejected inter-commit weakness: events
  in one commit were written by ONE author in ONE atomic batch, so an attacker cannot
  insert an event into someone else's already-sealed commit — intra-commit ordering is not
  attacker-exploitable the way cross-commit backdating was.

## What
- Reducer `process_key_event` folds position-based records (no epoch); `make_initial_state`
  seeds `keyring: []` (no `keyring_epoch`); `_rederive_keyring_keys` → keys with
  `revoked_at is None`; remove `keys_valid_at_epoch`.
- **Genesis / bootstrap:** keys carried on a CREATE (`_bootstrap_genesis_keyring`) get
  `added_at` = **the CREATE event's position** (`{ts}-{uuid}` of the CREATE), so their
  added-commit resolves to the CREATE commit (an ancestor of every later event). There is
  NO separate ambiguous sentinel. TOFU genesis (first `KEY_ADD` on a keyless identity)
  records `added_at` = that KEY_ADD's position.
- **Snapshot restore + v4 migration:** `process_snapshot` restores the position-based
  keyring verbatim. A pre-position (e165 v4) SNAPSHOT whose keyring records carry
  `added_epoch`/`revoked_epoch` (no `added_at`) is MIGRATED by re-seeding from the
  identity's static `keys` via `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` (treated as genesis at the
  CREATE position) rather than trusting the stale epoch fields. Because the stack is
  UNLANDED and lands atomically, no real store holds a v4 epoch snapshot; this migration is
  a defensive floor, not a live path.
- `authorship.py`: add `resolve_event_commit` + `verify_authorship_at_commit` +
  commit-ancestry trust root; **REMOVE `verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`,
  `keys_valid_at_epoch`, `_position_prefix`'s epoch use** (the HLC-epoch API).
- `identity.py` key add/revoke seam is unchanged in shape (TOFU genesis self-signed;
  unsigned non-genesis refused; signed add/rotate/revoke); only epoch wording in docstrings
  becomes commit wording.
- Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` v4→v5 and `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` v5→v6 (both preserve-and-ignore).
- Consumes TS1's in-toto authorship (verify the event's Statement against keys valid at the
  event's commit).

## Stack scoping (why TS2 and TS3 land together)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 563 = commit 2efdae38f (e165), which touches ONLY `authorship.py`, `reducer/{_processors,_state,_version,_cache}.py`, and `identity.py`. The **consumers** of the era model — `verify_authorship.py` (`_verify_signed` → `epoch_for_position` / `verify_authorship_at_epoch`) and `compact.py` (`_build_authorship_ledger` → `epoch`) — live in commit 721702e91 (3183), so they are rewired to `resolve_event_commit` / `verify_authorship_at_commit` in **TS3 (117b, change 580)**. Because TS2 removes the epoch API from `authorship.py` while TS3 updates its commit-7 consumers, the two are pushed together and land atomically with the whole stack; each is internally green at its own patchset (at commit 563 the verify-gate/compact code does not yet exist). TS2 REPLACES e165's OWN tests (`test_identity_e165*`, which assert the epoch model) with commit-ancestry tests.

## Scope
In: position-based key records, `resolve_event_commit`, DAG-ancestry validity (`verify_authorship_at_commit`) with intra-commit refinement + fail-closed git handling, TOFU/write-gate, reducer fold + snapshot + v4 migration + version bumps, removal of the epoch API, transitioning e165's tests. Out: authorship payload format (TS1); the SNAPSHOT ledger schema + `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict + the verify-gate/compact rewiring (TS3 / 3183, commit 7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The resolved key record binds `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit?}`
  (tickets-branch commit SHAs); a test using TWO real fixture commits asserts the resolved
  shape (add key in commit A, revoke in a later commit B; resolver yields A and B).
- [ ] Genesis key-add is accepted ONLY when self-signed (TOFU base case); an unsigned
  NON-genesis key-add is refused (test).
- [ ] Commit-ancestry validity across the revocation boundary: with key K added in commit
  C1 and revoked in a later commit C3, an event signed by K whose commit descends C1 but
  NOT C3 PASSES, and one whose commit descends C3 FAILS (test, both sides of boundary).
- [ ] Validity derives from commit ancestry, NOT event timestamps: an event written AFTER
  the revocation but carrying a BACKDATED `data`/filename timestamp still FAILS, because its
  introducing commit descends the revocation commit regardless of the timestamp (the
  killer test that commit-ancestry beats HLC backdating).
- [ ] Intra-commit refinement: with a KEY_ADD and an event in the SAME commit, a KEY_ADD at
  an earlier intra-commit position → event PASSES; a KEY_ADD at a later position → event
  FAILS; symmetrically a KEY_REVOKE at an earlier position in the same commit → event FAILS
  (test using a batched multi-event commit).
- [ ] Fail-closed git handling: when the position→commit resolution cannot run (git
  failure / no matching commit), verification returns a non-verified Verdict and never
  raises (test, e.g. an unresolvable position).
- [ ] Replay never rejects: a not-yet-valid-key / bad-signature event still folds into
  state (test); the delivered HLC-epoch surface is gone — a grep-assert confirms
  `verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`, `keys_valid_at_epoch`,
  `keyring_epoch`, `added_epoch`, `revoked_epoch` are ABSENT from `src/rebar`.
- [ ] The reducer stays pure: a grep-assert confirms `src/rebar/reducer/` imports no
  `subprocess` and runs no git (the resolver lives in `authorship.py`).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (resolve_event_commit + verify_authorship_at_commit + commit-ancestry trust root + intra-commit refinement + fail-closed git; remove epoch API)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (position-based keyring fold; genesis added_at = CREATE position; remove keys_valid_at_epoch/epoch cursor)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py` (seed keyring, no keyring_epoch)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` (SCHEMA_VERSION v4->v5)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py` (reducer cache v5->v6)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (docstring epoch->commit wording; seam shape unchanged)
baseline.summary: transition: key validity -> git-commit-ancestry (tickets-branch SHAs, replaces HLC-epoch)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at **800 lines against the hard 800-line cap** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which the CI module-size gate enforces with no allowlist. It is one line from red: the next change to any public library write verb fails the build. The sibling story adding two optional `create_ticket` arguments must widen two `@overload` signatures, the implementation, and their docstrings — it cannot land until this is relieved. This ticket buys that headroom by concern, not by line count.

## Approach

`_lib_writes` is the **aggregation point for every public library write**, so it grows on two axes: a new verb appends a wrapper, and an existing verb gaining an argument widens one in place. The facade split (S3/4532) cut the library **by direction** — writes vs reads vs gates vs ops — and that axis is exhausted: the write half alone carries seven concerns. The durable fix is to cut it **by concern**, per the `fsck` split (`defaceable-icy-antelope`), which took two cuts out of one 800-line file.

The seven concerns present today:

1. **Genesis** — `init_repo`, `create_ticket` (two `@overload`s + impl), `idea`.
2. **Identity & key material** — `create_identity`, `ensure_identity_for`, `create_placeholder`,
   `add_identity_key`, `revoke_identity_key`, `use_identity`, `resolve_current_identity`; all
   delegate to `rebar._commands.identity`, none touches ticket state.
3. **Status lifecycle** — `transition`, `claim`, `reopen`. The only place in the module that
   raises `ConcurrencyError`.
4. **Leaf mutations** — `_python_leaf` and its seven in-module callers `comment`, `edit_ticket`,
   `link`, `unlink`, `tag`, `untag`, `archive`.
5. **Session logs** — `append_session_log`, `start_session_log`; own `CommandError` mapping,
   NOT routed through `_python_leaf`.
6. **Store maintenance** — `compact`, `attach_commits`.
7. **Signing** — `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, delegating to `rebar.signing`.

**Two cuts**, mirroring `fsck`:

- **`_lib_mutations.py`** takes 4+5+6. Anchored on the `_python_leaf` call graph: one adapter,
  seven callers, all inside the block, nothing else in this module calling it. Stated honestly,
  5 and 6 **ride along** as the contiguous remainder of the post-genesis mutation surface, not
  because they call `_python_leaf`; the strict call-graph subset is ~130 lines and
  non-contiguous, forcing a scattered cut near the 100-line floor.
- **`_lib_identity.py`** takes 2+7 — the non-ticket, key-material surface. Identities own
  OpenSSH key lines, `use_identity`/`resolve_current_identity` select the current one, and
  signing binds a manifest to the environment key. Stated honestly, signing is ~52 lines and
  **cannot stand alone** under the 100-line floor; identity is the nearest concern by shape,
  and the module already banners signing apart from the write path.
- **`_lib_writes.py` keeps 1+3** — genesis and the status state machine.

The plan of record extracted only 4+5+6 and left `_lib_writes` at ~544 — sound at 778, but at 800 that lands **above** the 200-500 target band on a file that grew 22 lines in weeks. Hence two cuts.

Moved names are **re-exported** from `_lib_writes` with `# noqa: F401`, exactly as `fsck.py` re-exports from `fsck_scan`/`fsck_tracker_health`. That leaves `__init__.py` and `_lib_gates.py` **untouched**, so every `rebar.<name>` and `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` path survives — a smaller diff than re-pointing consumers.

**The pre-move surface, reconciled.** `_lib_writes` has 29 `def` statements = **27 distinct names** plus the two extra `@overload` stubs of `create_ticket`. `__init__.py` re-exports **all 27**, so the facade surface and the definition set coincide — no name defined here is omitted from the facade. `_python_leaf` is one of the 27: it resolves as **`rebar._python_leaf`** (its own `_python_leaf as _python_leaf` alias in `__init__.py`) *and* as `rebar._lib_writes._python_leaf`, the form `_lib_gates.py` imports. The 27 partition across the concerns above as 3 + 7 + 3 + 8 (leaf mutations, counting `_python_leaf`) + 2 + 2 + 2. Dependency direction is one-way — `_lib_writes` imports both new modules, neither imports back — so there is no cycle.

This is **behaviour-preserving**: bodies relocate byte-identically; no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` (new) — concerns 4+5+6
- `src/rebar/_lib_identity.py` (new) — concerns 2+7
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — keeps 1+3, gains the two re-export blocks

`__init__.py`, `_lib_gates.py`, and everything under `tests/` are deliberately **not** touched. The reference audit supports that: the only real-code importers of `_lib_writes` are `_lib_gates.py` (`_python_leaf`) and `__init__.py` (the 27-name re-export), and the string pass (`monkeypatch.setattr` / `getattr` / `importlib`) finds **zero** `_lib_writes` attribute references — every test patch targets the `rebar` facade or `rebar.signing`, both preserved.

`.github/complexity-baseline.json` holds **zero** entries for `_lib_writes.py`, so no moved symbol carries accepted debt and the `--lock` re-key hazard that cast `Verified -1` on the `fsck` change cannot arise. The baseline is therefore not in scope.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing with **no test file edited**. The specific risk is the **public API surface**, since all 27 names are re-exported as `rebar.<name>` and `_lib_gates` depends on `_python_leaf` at three call sites — a silently dropped re-export would still leave the suite green wherever the facade is imported lazily. Checked by name:

- every name previously importable as `rebar.<name>` still resolves after the move, asserted
  name by name against the pre-move list;
- `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` still resolves for all moved names, which is what makes
  `_lib_gates` and any `monkeypatch` target survive;
- the three modules import cleanly in **either** order, catching a cycle introduced by the
  re-export direction.

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the size oracle and needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_lib_writes.py` is at or below 450 lines; checked by
      `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_writes.py)" -le 450 ]` exiting 0.
- [ ] `_lib_mutations.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`.
- [ ] `_lib_identity.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_identity.py`.
- [ ] The repo's size oracle still passes; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve on the facade as `rebar.<name>` — 26 public wrappers plus
      `rebar._python_leaf`; checked by a script asserting `hasattr(rebar, n)` for every name in
      the pre-move list, exiting non-zero on the first miss.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve as `rebar._lib_writes.<name>`, which is the form
      `_lib_gates.py` imports; checked by the same assert-and-exit script against
      `rebar._lib_writes`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/__init__.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` are unchanged; checked by
      `git diff --exit-code HEAD~1 -- src/rebar/__init__.py src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] No file under `tests/` is changed; checked by `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 -- tests/`

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

baseline.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230, store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88 commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py` 14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.** `_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3; `signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP 204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in `llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" — the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [ ] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [ ] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and "Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [ ] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [ ] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [ ] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.
baseline.summary: Comment triage: relocate history, rationale and contracts out of src

baseline.description:
## Problem

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` maintains hand-curated `*_PATHS` manifests (BOT_PATHS, SECRETS_PATHS, MCP_PATHS, CONFIG_PATHS, EDGE_PATHS, MATERIALIZER_PATHS, OBS_PATHS, CERTBOT_PATHS) that decide which merged file changes trigger a redeploy / detect-signal. When a deploy-relevant infra file is ADDED but never listed, a subsequent change to it drifts to the running environment silently. This exact class has recurred four times: 1d1b (nginx edge), 5524 (host-nginx materializers), 5d4c (mcp-entrypoint.sh, MCP_PATHS), 408c (materialize-deploy-key.sh, CONFIG_PATHS). Each was a manual list falling out of sync with reality — a fail-OPEN omission that no test caught.

## Approach — derive-and-diff, NOT a second hand-list

Do not introduce a parallel curated "deploy-relevant files" list; that just relocates the drift. Instead DERIVE the expected path set from sources already maintained for their own reasons, and fail on drift. The enforced list becomes a *derived view* of a source of truth, so it cannot silently drift.

In-repo precedent: `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` already does exactly this for `server.json` — it derives the expected env-var records from the `rebar.mcp_server.MCP_ENV_VARS` code inventory and "rejects missing names, extra names, changed fields". This guard is a fourth sibling of that accepted pattern (cf. also `check_config_ownership.py`, `check_verify_gate_parity.py`). OSS precedent for derive-from-reality vs a curated list: `go mod tidy` + `git diff --exit-code`, Bazel Gazelle, Tinder `bazel-diff` (whose maintainers warn a hand "approximate the affected set" yields "a system you can't trust"), Nx `affected`, Pants `--changed-since`.

Derivation sources (independent of the manifest):
1. Dockerfile/compose directives — parse `infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` + `docker-compose.yml`
   for `COPY` / `install -m` / `ENTRYPOINT` script references (what is baked into the running
   images). Catches 5d4c (mcp-entrypoint.sh named in Dockerfile.mcp).
2. Filename conventions — glob `infra/**/materialize-*.sh`, `infra/**/*-entrypoint.sh`,
   `compose-up.sh`. Catches 408c + 5524 (materialize-*.sh).

### Parser resolution rule (Dockerfile/compose source A)

The Dockerfile/compose parser only accepts `COPY` / `install -m` / `ENTRYPOINT` (and compose `entrypoint:`/`command:`) script references that RESOLVE TO AN EXISTING REPO FILE, and it normalizes container paths to repo-relative POSIX paths first:
- a build-context path like `/app/infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` has its `/app/` prefix
  stripped to the repo-relative `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh`;
- an installed/container-absolute path like the ENTRYPOINT `/usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh`
  is resolved by basename against the checkout's `infra/**`;
- a reference that resolves to NO repo file — a script GENERATED inside the image at build
  time (e.g. the heredoc-written `reviewbot-entrypoint.sh`) or an external binary — is
  discarded, not treated as a deploy-relevant repo path.
This keeps the derived set to real, in-repo, deploy-relevant source files.

### Coverage matching rule (mirror autodeploy's own semantics)

The check cross-references each derived path against the UNION of autodeploy.sh's `*_PATHS`. Coverage is NOT exact string membership: it mirrors the git-pathspec matching autodeploy itself uses. autodeploy decides "did a matching path change" with `git -C "$MIRROR_DIR" diff --name-only <a> <b> -- $PATHS` (its `changed_range` at autodeploy.sh:736), and several manifest entries are DIRECTORY prefixes (e.g. `src/rebar/` with a trailing slash). So a derived path P counts as COVERED when ANY manifest entry T (trailing slash ignored) satisfies `P == T` OR `P` is under directory `T` (`P` startswith `T + "/"`) — the same prefix semantics git pathspec applies. Both sides are compared as repo-relative POSIX paths. A derived path covered by NO manifest entry under this rule -> fail (non-zero), printing the path and which derivation matched it.

## Fail-safe exclusion list

A small, commented exclusion list (in the check script) represents genuinely-intentional exceptions. This is not optional polish: autodeploy.sh ALREADY documents a deliberate exclusion (no AUTODEPLOY_PATHS block — self-update re-exec race, with a multi-line WHY), so the guard MUST be able to encode "derived but intentionally not deploy-triggering". Each excluded path carries an inline reason, and the guard verifies each exclusion still names a real repo file (a stale exclusion is itself flagged). The guard thus OVER-flags (add the path or annotate the exclusion) and never silently misses — the opposite failure mode from a bare hand-list.

## Portability (project.portability)

Runs in-process via `make lint` as `python scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py`, mirroring the ~24 existing `scripts/check_*.py` guards. Stdlib only, no CI-provider trigger: any CI that runs `make lint` enforces it, and the pre-commit hook runs it locally on `git commit`. Portable to diverse-CI / no-CI environments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py` derives the expected path set from (a) Dockerfile/
      compose `COPY`/`install`/`ENTRYPOINT` script refs and (b) `materialize-*.sh` /
      `*-entrypoint.sh` / `compose-up.sh` globs under `infra/`.
- [x] The Dockerfile/compose parser only keeps script references that RESOLVE to an existing
      repo file, normalizing container prefixes (`/app/` stripped; installed-absolute paths
      resolved by basename) and DISCARDING build-artifact / image-generated paths.
- [x] It parses autodeploy.sh's `*_PATHS` (all `^[A-Z_]+_PATHS=` assignments) and exits
      non-zero when a derived path is in NONE of them, printing the path + matched source.
- [x] Coverage mirrors autodeploy's git-pathspec matching (its `changed_range`
      `git diff --name-only -- $PATHS`): a derived path counts as covered when ANY manifest
      entry is that path OR a directory prefix of it (trailing slash ignored), NOT exact
      string membership. A test pins this prefix semantics (e.g. `src/rebar/` covers
      `src/rebar/x.py`).
- [x] A commented exclusion list supports intentional exceptions; each excluded path has an
      inline reason and names a real repo file (encodes at least the documented
      install-autodeploy.sh-class exclusion).
- [x] A test asserts the derivation captures every historically-drifted recurrence class
      (mcp-entrypoint.sh, materialize-deploy-key.sh, materialize-*.sh, compose-up.sh,
      reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh), each with its matched derivation source.
- [x] Wired into the `make lint` target (not a standalone CI workflow), so it runs under the
      pre-commit hook and any CI that runs `make lint`.
- [x] RED->GREEN test: with a derived path removed from all manifests the check fails for the
      right reason; with manifests complete it passes. Mutation-checked (re-omit each covered
      path -> RED; restore).
- [x] Running the check against current `origin/main` PASSES (manifests are complete after
      f87719be9999).

## Out of scope

- No change to autodeploy runtime behaviour or apply/detect scope.
- Fully-dynamic deploy paths named by no convention and no Dockerfile/compose directive
  remain underivable — documented residual, handled by the exclusion list's fail-safe
  direction (a false negative there is no worse than today).

## File impact

- `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py` (new)
- `Makefile` (add to the `lint` target)
- `tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py` (new)
- audited but NOT modified: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp`,
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`
baseline.summary: Guard: derive-and-diff completeness check for autodeploy.sh path manifests

baseline.description:
## Why

108 tickets in the store carry `## Success Criteria`. Their criteria are conventionally plain
`- ` bullets, and `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under `## Acceptance Criteria`
(resetting at the next `##`). So those criteria are invisible to the P1 blocking floor, cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag the completion verifier matches on checkbox text, and are
not individually checkable. Migrating them is the substantive half of this epic — the heading
rename is cosmetic by comparison.

## What

Migrate the store tickets carrying `## Success Criteria` so their criteria live under
`## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items.

## Scope

The ticket descriptions in the `tickets` branch that match `## Success Criteria` (108 distinct
tickets at time of writing; the migration recomputes the set rather than hard-coding it).

A migration script under `scripts/` performing the rewrite via the rebar library
(`rebar.edit_ticket`) so every change is a normal, auditable ticket event — NOT a direct
rewrite of the git-backed store.

OUT OF SCOPE: closed tickets' historical accuracy is not preserved by rewriting; see Approach
for why closed tickets are migrated too and what that costs.

## Approach

For each matching ticket: locate the `## Success Criteria` block (bounded by the next `## `
heading), convert its `- ` bullets to `- [ ]` items, and merge them into the ticket's existing
`## Acceptance Criteria` block, appending if one exists and creating it if not. Tickets already
carrying both headings merge; the SC heading is then removed.

Editing a ticket's description changes its MATERIAL FINGERPRINT, which invalidates any
plan-review attestation as `stale-material`. That is correct and unavoidable — the plan text
genuinely changed — but it means the migration must not be run blindly across claimed work.
The script therefore processes CLOSED tickets by default and requires an explicit flag to touch
open/in_progress ones, so no in-flight claim is silently invalidated. The count of skipped
in-flight tickets is reported so the remainder can be migrated deliberately.

Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the block-rewriting function over fixtures: SC-only, both-headings, SC with
  mixed `- ` and `- [ ]` items, SC as the LAST section (no following `##`), and a ticket with
  no SC block (must be a no-op).
- Dry-run over the real store, with the resulting diff attached as a ticket comment.
- Post-migration assertion that `_count_ac_items` returns >=1 for every migrated ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A script under `scripts/` performs the migration through `rebar.edit_ticket`, with
      `--dry-run` as the default mode and a required explicit flag to modify non-closed tickets.
- [ ] Unit tests cover all five block-shape cases listed under Testing, including the no-op case.
- [ ] After the live run, `git grep -l "## Success Criteria" tickets` matches no ticket
      description outside the skipped in-flight set.
- [ ] Every migrated ticket returns `_count_ac_items >= 1`, verified by a script pass over the
      migrated set.
- [ ] The dry-run diff and the list of skipped in-flight tickets are recorded as comments on
      this ticket.
baseline.summary: Migrate store tickets from Success Criteria bullets to Acceptance Criteria checkboxes

baseline.description:
# J4 — Pin a `UserIdentityModel` contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

User identity is the second real Cloud/DC difference. Jira Cloud identifies users by opaque `accountId` (username and userkey were removed for GDPR); Data Center identifies them by `name`. This leaks into two places in the Cloud adapter: `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee`, which returns `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` and encodes the 3-state account-resolution fast-path the core diff consults (ADR 0035 §(d) canonical-comparison corollary), and the transport's create/update assignee payload shape.

PR #120 handled this by copying `resolve_assignee` and hardcoding `is_account_id=False`, and its copy consulted `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` — an attribute nothing ever sets, so its entire authoritative branch was unreachable and DC would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. That is not a cosmetic bug: a permanently non-authoritative assignee resolution makes the outbound diff re-emit assignee changes it can never converge, which is the churn class epic `ace2` was created to fix.

## Approach

Define a `UserIdentityModel` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `resolve(local_value, remote_identity)` returning the existing `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` tuple, and `to_payload(value)` returning the deployment's assignee field shape. Two implementations: `AccountIdIdentity` (Cloud — the current behavior verbatim, `{"accountId": …}`) and `NameIdentity` (DC — resolves through the DC user-search endpoint, `{"name": …}`).

`NameIdentity` performs a **real** lookup against DC's user-search endpoint rather than echoing the local value, so it can return `authoritative=True` and the diff converges. Its resolver is injected at construction from the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], not discovered via `getattr`, so there is no unreachable branch.

**Alternative rejected:** DC returns the local value with `authoritative=False` always (PR #120's effective behavior). It compiles and passes shallow tests while guaranteeing assignee-diff churn on every pass.

**Alternative rejected:** normalizing both to a single "user reference" string. The core diff's 3-state fast-path genuinely needs to know whether the value is an accountId, so flattening it would push the branch back into core.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — Cloud constructed with `AccountIdIdentity`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_model.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier with a stateful fake resolver for the lookup (the irreducible external boundary), plus a shared contract test over both implementations, since the 3-state contract must hold identically for each.

- shared contract, parameterized over both models: an empty local value yields
  `("", False, <model default>)`; a value that resolves to the SAME identity the remote already has yields
  `(None, True, …)` (converged, nothing to emit); a value resolving to a different identity yields that
  identity with `authoritative=True`.
- Cloud-specific: the resolved value is an accountId and `is_account_id is True`; payload is `{"accountId": …}`.
- DC-specific: the resolved value is a username and `is_account_id is False`; payload is `{"name": …}`.
- failure path: an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (the neutral base at
  `_backend.py:48`) rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value.
- regression oracle for PR #120's defect: a test asserts that for a resolvable assignee, DC returns
  `authoritative=True` — this test fails against the `getattr`-based implementation.
- contrast case: an unassigned local value yields the documented desired-unassigned state, not a lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test covers all three resolution states for both identity models
- [ ] a test asserts DC returns `authoritative=True` for a resolvable assignee (the anti-churn oracle)
- [ ] a test asserts an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for both models
- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` returns nothing — no `getattr`-discovered collaborator anywhere
- [ ] J1's pinned Cloud assignee behavior is unchanged (`make test` green with those assertions unmodified)
baseline.summary: J4 — pin a UserIdentityModel contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context / Problem
The shrink-only complexity gate prints only aggregate counts on failure. Gerrit CI run 32914110990 reported `active=41 new=2 increased=1 stale=7` but did not name the offending symbols or their scores. Diagnosis required a separate local no-cache Ruff census plus manual baseline comparison, which is especially poor in resource-constrained CI-only workflows.

## Plan
- Preserve the existing compact counter summary.
- Emit one deterministic detail line for every `new` symbol with its current score and the configured threshold.
- Emit one deterministic detail line for every `increased` symbol with its current score and recorded ceiling.
- Keep passing/stale-only output compact and keep the scanner/gate runtime unchanged apart from formatting already-computed data.
- Add focused unit coverage for ordering, values, and no-detail passing output.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A failing `--check` names every new symbol and reports its current score plus allowed threshold.
- [ ] A failing `--check` names every increased symbol and reports its current score plus baseline ceiling.
- [ ] Detail lines are stable-sorted and appear with the existing summary.
- [ ] A passing or stale-only check retains compact output without violation lines.
- [ ] Focused tests and project CI gates pass.

## Context
Planning currently mixes snapshot reads, binding decisions, mode limits, and later handler assumptions. Retry recovery cannot be stable until all decisions derive from one frozen observation.

## Outcome
Define immutable `Observation` and `TicketPlan` values and a pure planner that preserves the existing `Mutation` vocabulary/serialization. This task covers deterministic value construction only, not lifecycle dependency logic or preview output.

## Plan
1. Add frozen provider-neutral observation/version and per-ticket plan types with open payloads.
2. Build pure planner inputs from local snapshot, remote snapshot, binding read view, mode, selection/filter, and limits.
3. Refactor existing differ decisions into plan mutation values without filesystem, provider, subprocess, or clock I/O.
4. Preserve existing mutation serialization and canonical hashes exactly.

## Testing

## Finding (audit of epic 3405-c0b7)
**Site:** `src/rebar/_reads.py:99` sets `err.error_code = "pinned_ticket_read_failed"`, returned verbatim by `error_code_for` branch 5 (the `exc.error_code` passthrough). But `pinned_ticket_read_failed` is NOT a member of `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (`src/rebar/_errors.py:48-66`).

**Problem:** the code itself is descriptive (NOT misleading). The defect is a vocabulary-completeness gap: `error_code_for`'s own docstring says it "Returns a stable vocabulary code (one of KNOWN_ERROR_CODES)", but this passthrough emits a code outside that set. Any consumer that validates the returned code against `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (the documented contract) would reject a legitimately-emitted code, or fall back to treating it as unknown.

**Observable vs latent:** OBSERVABLE — emitted on the pinned-ticket read failure path; reaches the MCP envelope guard and the CLI reader envelope.

**Proposed fix — READY-TO-FIX (reuse existing, no design decision):** add `"pinned_ticket_read_failed"` to the `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` frozenset so the emitted vocabulary and the declared vocabulary agree. (Alternatively, add a contract test that asserts every `err.error_code` string assigned in the tree is a member of `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` — see the epic's prevention recommendation.) Low priority; not misleading, but it violates the stated vocabulary contract.

**caused_by / class:** vocabulary drift, not the `llm_unavailable` pattern.

## Problem

The 17 confirmable mutation verbs appear in three places:

- `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:680` `_CONFIRM_SCOPE` — derived, canonical
- `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py:43-46` `EDITORIAL_PREAMBLE`, emitted into `docs/cli-reference.md:8`
- `docs/user-guide.md:27` — hand-authored, the same 17 backticked names

All three agree at 17/17 today, so this is preventive. The existing gate misses BOTH prose copies:

- `_check_mutation_verbs()` (`gen_cli_reference.py:193`) compares the `MUTATION_VERBS` dict KEYS to
  `_CONFIRM_SCOPE` — not the preamble.
- `lint_editorial`'s route rule fires only on `rebar <verb>` forms, and the preamble uses bare
  backticks.
- `docs/user-guide.md` has no gate at all.

So adding a `confirmable=True` route updates the canonical set and the dict, and both prose copies go stale silently — in exactly the documents that tell an agent which commands ask for confirmation.

## Approach — add-parity-check

Extend `_check_mutation_verbs` to parse the backticked verb list out of `EDITORIAL_PREAMBLE` and out of `docs/user-guide.md:27`, and compare both to `_CONFIRM_SCOPE`.

Parsing prose is the right move here rather than generating it: both passages are written as sentences with rationale, not as a bare list, and generating them would flatten guidance a reader depends on. The check therefore asserts the SET matches while leaving the wording to a human.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `_check_mutation_verbs` compares the preamble's backticked verbs to `_CONFIRM_SCOPE` and
      fails on any difference. Verified by a mutation adding a verb to the preamble and seeing RED.
- [x] AC2: it does the same for the `docs/user-guide.md` list. Verified by the equivalent mutation.
- [x] AC3: the failure names which document and which verbs, in which direction. Verified by
      asserting the message content in both mutation checks.
- [x] AC4: both prose copies pass on the committed tree, i.e. the check is green at rest and the
      17/17 agreement is confirmed rather than assumed. Verified by running the generator's checks.
- [x] AC5: the existing dict-keys comparison is retained, not replaced. Verified by the original
      assertion still being present and exercised.

## Testing

- `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` — AC1-AC5 on the committed tree.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "cli_reference or mutation_verbs or editorial" -q`.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING

## Why
This is the dependency root of the oracle. The three-valued evidence contract, the fail-open execution harness, and the optional-extra scaffolding are shared by every engine — they must exist and be stable before Engine A, T0, or Engine B are built. Getting the contract right here is what makes "one implementation, not two" real.

## What
- The normalized **evidence model**: `resolved | abstained(reason)` with a CLOSED structured reason enum
  (`unsupported_lang | no_tool | parse_error | timeout | ambiguous | private_or_internal_suspected |
  network_error | rate_limited | version_skew | invalid_detector | other`), provenance/tier, and a coverage
  record. `version_skew` (the #1 real failure) and `invalid_detector` (a project detector failing validation)
  are first-class; `other` is the explicit catch-all (no open `…`). Resolution-lane resolved value is `refuted`
  (never an asserted absence). One internal finding shape; SARIF 2.1.0 map at the edges (superset).
- The **fail-open recover/timeout harness** every backend runs inside. OUT-OF-PROCESS tools (ctags, ast-grep,
  OpenGrep, scc/lizard, registry HTTP) use the subprocess reaper (mirror `acli_subprocess`: process-group,
  SIGTERM→SIGKILL, structured timeout). IN-PROCESS bindings (tree-sitter) CANNOT be bounded by a thread/signal
  timeout (it can't interrupt a hung C-extension call, and a segfault would kill the host) — so prefer the CLI
  form of every matcher, and run any unavoidable in-process binding inside a WORKER SUBPROCESS so the same reaper
  applies. A crash/timeout/missing-tool/version-skew becomes a recorded `abstain`, never raises; the visible skip
  IS the coverage record — never a silent no-op. Each backend's version is pinned/recorded.
- **Optional-extra scaffolding**: a new extra in `pyproject.toml`, `_optional.py` guard + `guard_import`, core
  stays import-clean (the existing optionality CI gate), non-adopting clients import nothing.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/` (new package) — contract + harness + extra wiring only; no backend logic.
- Polyglot/optional by construction; no Python-specific assumptions in the contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Evidence model + CLOSED structured reason enum (incl. version_skew, invalid_detector, other) + coverage implemented; `refute`/`abstain` representable; SARIF map both directions.
- [ ] Fail-open harness covers OUT-OF-PROCESS (subprocess reaper) AND IN-PROCESS (worker-subprocess) backends: crash / hang / timeout / missing tool / version-skew → recorded `abstain`, never raises — incl. a segfaulting C-extension parse.
- [ ] Optional extra added; core import-clean (optionality CI gate passes); non-adopting client imports nothing.
- [ ] Unit-tested: harness converts each failure mode to the correct `abstain(reason)` + coverage entry.
baseline.summary: Evidence contract + fail-open execution harness + optional-extra scaffolding (dependency root)

## Surface
GitHub Actions, repo navapbc/rebar, workflow **Test Suite (mirror)** (scheduled/dispatch, non-blocking mirror tier), matrix `sweep (…)` jobs. Blocking core tiers pass on main; only the experimental `sweep` matrix is red.

## Signatures (two distinct sub-failures)
1. **sweep (windows)** — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` at collection; Windows tier cannot collect.
2. **sweep (py3.14)** — `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held` fails `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests`.

(The `sweep (macos, full suite)` / `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` legs are the recurrence of closed `e3e0-2e7c-b280-4b4a`, tracked there — not this ticket.)

## Severity: P3
Mirror/experimental tier — non-blocking. CI-hygiene / cross-platform-portability signal.

---

## Fix plan (Phase 2) — two independent root causes, confirmed in Phase 1 RCA comment

**RC#1 (Windows collection blackout):** 4 modules do an *unconditional* module-top `import fcntl` — `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, `src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/marker.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py`. Because `import rebar` transitively hits `doctor_locks.py`, ALL collection dies on non-POSIX. The codebase already establishes that a module-top fcntl import must be made *conditional*, and does so with **three distinct legitimate shapes** (none is a single uniform pattern):
  - **module-top `try/except ImportError → fcntl = None`** — `_snapshot/janitor.py`, `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`, `_snapshot/git_fetch.py`, `rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py`'s sibling guarded modules;
  - **`if sys.platform != "win32": import fcntl` / `else: fcntl = None`** — `_engine/rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py:12-15`;
  - **function-local (lazy) `import fcntl`** — `_commands/recent_creates.py:64` (inside `_journal_lock`), `_store/hlc.py:106` (inside `_hlc_lock`); a deferred import never runs at collection time, so it never breaks collection.

Fix = guard the 4 unconditional imports with the module-top `try/except ImportError → None` shape (collectability only; Windows fcntl *locking* is out of scope — non-support-target). On non-POSIX, `fcntl` binds to `None`, so a subsequent `fcntl.flock(...)` call site inside those 4 modules would raise `AttributeError` at call time — that is acceptable and in-scope-excluded: Windows is not a declared support target and these are POSIX-only lock paths; the deliverable is import/collection success, not Windows locking. Zero behavior change on POSIX (fcntl stays the real module).

**RC#2 (py3.14 red):** the autouse `_network_guard` (`tests/conftest.py`) patches **two** seams: `patch.object(socket.socket, "connect", _guard_socket_connect)` AND `patch("socket.create_connection", side_effect=RuntimeError(...))`. The `connect` seam rejected **all** address families; py3.14's Linux default start-method change `fork`→`forkserver` makes `multiprocessing` reach its server over an **AF_UNIX** (local IPC) connect, which the all-families guard wrongly rejects. Fix = narrow the **`connect`** seam only: block just `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` (real network) and delegate every other family (AF_UNIX etc.) to the captured original `socket.socket.connect`. The **`create_connection`** seam is left AS-IS — it is a real-TCP-only helper (always builds an AF_INET/AF_INET6 socket), so it needs no family check and blocking it wholesale stays correct.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — `import fcntl` guarded (module-top `try/except ImportError → None`); POSIX behavior unchanged.
- [x] `src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py` — `import fcntl` guarded.
- [x] `src/rebar/reducer/marker.py` — `import fcntl` guarded.
- [x] `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` — `import fcntl` guarded (the leaf that breaks `import rebar`).
- [x] RED→GREEN: the 4 modules import under simulated non-POSIX (`sys.modules['fcntl']=None`) and `import rebar` succeeds — proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_fcntl_import_guard.py`.
- [x] Structural guard `scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` (AST; stdlib-only, wired into `make lint`) fails only on a genuinely **unconditional** module-top `import fcntl` in `src/rebar`. It treats an import as guarded when it is (a) inside a `try`, (b) inside an `if`/`else` (the `sys.platform` conditional), OR (c) function-local (never module-top). A `# fcntl-guard-ok: <reason>` marker is the sanctioned escape hatch. Ships true-positive + true-negative (one case for EACH of the three live shapes — try/except like `git_fetch.py`, `sys.platform` like `alert_store.py`, function-local like `hlc.py`) + refactor-survival tests — proven by `python scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` and its test.
- [x] Step7 test siblings `tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py` and `tests/unit/test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py` use `pytest.importorskip("fcntl")` so they skip (not error) on non-POSIX.
- [x] `tests/conftest.py` — the `connect` seam blocks only AF_INET/AF_INET6 and delegates other families to the real connect; the `create_connection` seam is unchanged — proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py`.
- [x] RED→GREEN: a `forkserver` `multiprocessing.Process` starts under the guard; an AF_UNIX connect is allowed; a real AF_INET connect is still blocked (teeth).

## Testing
- `python scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` — the new structural guard (also via `make lint`).
- `pytest tests/unit/test_fcntl_import_guard.py tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py` — the two RED→GREEN regressions.
- `pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py` — original-report replication (under forkserver).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — clean.

### Portability (project.portability)
The structural guard is a stdlib-only AST script wired into `make lint` — no CI provider required, runnable locally and under any CI. The network-guard narrowing is interpreter/OS-agnostic (a socket-family check).

## Provenance
Periodic ops-error sweep. `caused_by` → `13ad-4c6f-4074-4f43` (added both red tiers). See Phase 1 RCA comment for full mechanism proofs + attribution.

# P1.0 — Unify canonical event-byte serialization + zero-dep structural guard

**Prerequisite for P2.1, P2.2, P2.3.** Every later item that adds, reorders, or
signs event content depends on there being exactly ONE canonical byte format.

## Context (problem + research)

Event serialization is scattered across many writers and only **one** is
canonical — `_store/event_append.py:56-61` emits
`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)`. Seven
other LIVE writers emit plain `json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False)` (unsorted):
reconciler `_engine/event_append.py:123`, `ticket_txn.py:219/351/372`,
`graph/_links.py:145`, `ticket-delete-unlink-scan.py:149`,
`batch_dispatch.py:222`; plus bash heredocs in `ticket-comment.sh:90-91`
(live via `ticket-transition.sh:439` force-close), `ticket-revert.sh:170-174`
(live via `ticket-transition.sh:179` un-archive), `ticket-lib-api.sh:994/1017`
(delete), `ticket-compact.sh:274` (SNAPSHOT). There is **no** byte-parity test —
the one cited in `_store/event_append.py:15`'s docstring does not exist.

**Research / proven art.** The "`json.dumps == jq -S -c`" assumption is unsafe:
`jq` parses numbers as IEEE-754 float64, and rebar's ns `timestamp` is a 19-digit
integer **> 2^53** — jq <=1.6 (default macOS) rounds it on parse, and even jq-1.7
rounds it under arithmetic. The TUF/sigstore ecosystem's hard-won lesson is
"canonicalization across implementations is a footgun; standardize on one / sign
the literal bytes" (RFC 8785 JCS; python-tuf#457; sigstore DSSE). So: collapse to
ONE Python serializer, keep jq out of the event path entirely.

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP2: `json.dumps(...ensure_ascii=False)` == `jq -S -c` ONLY with
  `ensure_ascii=False` (`世界` diverges otherwise).
- EXP-jq: jq rounds the >2^53 timestamp (`.t+0` -> `...655000`); confirmed.
- EXP-R3 (real code): real `_canonical_bytes` != plain dumps, but parsed dicts are
  identical -> **re-serialization is replay-safe** (reducer reads keys, not bytes).
- EXP-R7 (real code): `python3 -m rebar._store.<submodule>` works and emits
  canonical sorted output -> bash heredocs can call the helper.
- EXP-R9/R9b (real code): the committed stdlib guard
  `docs/experiments/event_write_guard.py` flags **exactly 7 Python + 7 bash** event writers
  with **0 false positives** across 73 read/output `json.dumps` sites.

## What / Implementation detail

1. Factor a **lock-free** `canonical_bytes(event) -> bytes` helper (out of
   `_store/event_append.py:56-61`) importable without the write lock (the txn/LINK
   paths rename+commit inline, e.g. `ticket_txn.py:236-243`).
2. Route every live writer through it: the 5 Python sites import it; the 4 bash
   heredocs call `python3 -m rebar._store.canonical` (pass the event(s) on stdin;
   **batch** multi-event paths — delete writes STATUS+ARCHIVED+N*UNLINK — in ONE
   invocation to avoid per-event subprocess cost).
3. Delete the dead leaf writers (`ticket-create.sh`, `ticket-edit.sh`) and leave
   `ticket-link.sh` (still serves `link --dry-run`, writes no event) /
   `ticket-migrate-*.sh` (one-shot) exempt. Fix the false docstring at
   `_store/event_append.py:15`.
4. Ship the **stdlib** structural guard as a CI test (semgrep/ast-grep/pre-commit
   are ABSENT here — EXP-R9). Python prong = AST (json.dump(s) on a dict carrying
   `event_type`); bash prong = regex scoped to `json.dump` co-occurring with an
   `'event_type'` dict (a bare grep false-positives on ~10 read/output `.sh`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `canonical_bytes()` extracted as a lock-free helper and imported by the 5 Python writers
- [ ] 4 bash heredoc writers call `python3 -m rebar._store.canonical` (multi-event paths batched)
- [ ] dead leaf writers deleted; `_store/event_append.py:15` docstring corrected
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test-ticket-write-commit-event.sh` added (parity + >2^53/non-ASCII fuzz)
- [ ] stdlib structural guard wired into CI (Python AST + scoped bash regex), expected writer set empty
- [ ] reconciler + compaction suites still green (no replay change)

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.0) for the full write-up and `docs/experiments/` for the prototypes.
- [ ] All event files (every type) are byte-identical regardless of writer, pinned by
- [ ] The structural guard fails CI on any new raw event serializer; after this epic
- [ ] No reducer/replay behavior change (existing committed data unaffected;
baseline.summary: P1.0 — Unify canonical event-byte serialization + zero-dep structural guard

## Why
Operator direction (2026-08-15): approach chauvinist-subsolar-arctichare (19ea-29af-ebb3-410b) as an EXPERIMENT. The auto-resume design (adolescent-evilminded-locust) re-runs the whole verifier and relies on the verdict cache to skip credited criteria; it passes NO information about WHERE the failed attempt already searched. Question to answer empirically: does handing a resumption the prior attempt's search frontier as an EXCLUSION list ("already searched, found nothing: ...") measurably reduce re-search overlap and steps-to-verdict? Blocker noted at design time: verifier telemetry does not carry argument-level tool-call transcripts — the PoC must capture them harness-side.

## Protocol (rapid PoC — throwaway harness, no production code)
1. Corpus: >=2 real CLOSED tickets with large surfaces (description near the 8000-char cap, many prose ACs/comments). Run read-only (--source local, never signs). Cache lifecycle (one policy, all steps): each (ticket, arm) pair gets an ISOLATED cache namespace — the harness monkeypatches `cache_dir` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py:59, the single derivation of `.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/...` from `_resolve_root`) to return a per-arm temp dir, the standard unit-suite technique; nothing under the real store is touched. Attempt 1 (forced exhaustion) runs with cache ACTIVE but EMPTY — banking must fill it, and prior real-store verdicts cannot leak in. Its populated cache is then COPIED once and each resume arm reads its own identical copy.
2. Transcript capture: wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam) to log every tool call with full arguments (file paths read, grep patterns, dirs listed) per criterion.
3. Force exhaustion: a config-level budget cannot go low — the computed floor is AUTHORITATIVE over smaller configured values (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:237 raises max_iterations up to verify_step_floor). The harness therefore monkeypatches `verify_step_floor` to return the reduced budget (e.g. 12-20 steps) for every arm and attempt uniformly — patched at BOTH bindings, since completion_banking.py:38 binds the name at import time: `rebar.llm.completion.verify_step_floor` AND `rebar.llm.workflow.completion_banking.verify_step_floor` (patch-where-used); attempt 1 then FAILs insufficiency-only with a partial bank; keep the transcript.
4. Extract frontier: from the transcript, derive per-criterion searched-set (paths read, patterns tried) and a compact data-shaped frontier block (<=1500 chars, list form, zero imperative sentences).
5. Resume LOOP per arm, same reduced budget every attempt, each arm on its own copy of the attempt-1 cache (per the step-1 policy): repeat the re-run until overall PASS or 3 resume attempts, whichever first; the cache accrues within the arm across attempts (that accrual IS the resume mechanism). (A) CONTROL — plain re-runs, cache-seeded only (locust behavior). (B) TREATMENT — identical, plus a frontier EVIDENCE block spliced into the fenced ticket context, regenerated after each attempt from that arm's cumulative transcript. Seam (mirrors the framework's own evidence precedent): the harness wraps the registered `completion_precheck` step (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:48) and inserts the block into its returned `context` inside the `<untrusted_ticket_context>` fence (:229) — exactly how framework-computed child-closure proof (gate_ops.py:226-228 via build_child_closure_evidence) and the epic bug screen land today. The block is DATA-shaped, never directive ("frontier: searched-and-empty: <path/pattern list>" — no instructions), because the fence renders directive text inert by design; the packaged reviewer prompt is NOT edited. This also makes the treatment production-faithful: if it wins, the productized form IS a framework-attached evidence block at this seam.
6. Metrics table (the deliverable): re-search overlap rate per attempt (tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm) A vs B, newly-banked PASSes per step A vs B, attempts-to-clean-close (or 'not clean in 3') A vs B, token cost delta.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no src/rebar changes).
- [x] Argument-level transcripts captured for >=2 large tickets across forced-exhaustion + both resume arms.
- [x] Metrics table posted as a comment on THIS ticket and on chauvinist-subsolar-arctichare: overlap rate, PASS-per-step, attempts, cost.
- [x] Verdict comment applies the PREDECLARED decision rule: GO if, on EVERY corpus ticket, the treatment arm (B) shows (i) re-search overlap rate reduced by >=30% relative to control AND (ii) attempts-to-clean-close <= control; NO-GO if either fails on any ticket; INDETERMINATE if any arm errors environmentally (report raw numbers regardless). Include what telemetry production would need to carry. N is small (2+ tickets) — the rule is a PoC screen for whether a real investment is warranted, not a significance claim, and the comment must say so.
- [x] No store writes beyond ticket comments; no signatures minted (--source local only).
baseline.summary: Experiment: search-frontier exclusion-list resumption (arctichare PoC)

## Why

Pass-2 (validate each finding) is the strongest reuse candidate: the binary sub-questions
(`is_verifiable`, `evidence_entails_finding`, `path_reachable`, `impact_follows_necessarily`,
`no_viable_alternative_explanation`, `no_existing_mitigation`, `severity_claim_justified` + the
cited-reference veto) and the severity-attribute enums are properties of *a finding*, not of
plans-vs-diffs — so a code-review finding and a plan finding answer the SAME questions. Extracting
it gives one binary vocabulary + one `verification` contract that every gate shares, eliminating
the silent-drift class. The verify orchestration already built for plan-review (token-budget
chunking, merge-by-global-index, the non-frontier verifier-model default) is likewise general and
moves with it.

## What

- Move the Pass-2 verifier into the kernel as `verify_findings(findings, *, context, model,
  headroom) -> verifications`, carrying the chunking + merge-by-index + verifier-model resolution.
- Make the `verification` pydantic/JSON contract the SINGLE registered source of the binary
  vocabulary + severity-attribute enums (one schema, small/flat).
- Reliability: validate with the existing tolerant stack (json-repair + bounded retry +
  pydantic-ai native outputs) and DEGRADE to INDETERMINATE on an unparseable turn — never
  hard-crash a gate. (Reuse `gate_dispatch`'s degrade path; do not add stricter validation.)
- Rewire the plan-review verify step to consume the kernel (the per-gate verify-prompt preamble +
  the plan context are passed in). No behavior change.

## Scope

In scope: the Pass-2 verify function + the `verification` contract + the tolerant-validation
reliability behavior, moved to the kernel; plan-review consumes it. Out of scope: Pass-3 (WS1, on
which this depends), the coach (WS3), the seam doc + behavioral evals (WS4). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (verify builders), `sizing.py` (chunker), `workflow_ops.py`
(verify-inputs op), the verify prompt(s), and the kernel module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The kernel exposes a `verify_findings` Pass-2 entry that takes a findings list + a domain
      context and returns the per-finding `{severity_attributes, binary}` verifications, with the
      token-budget chunking + merge-by-global-index + verifier-model default carried over.
- [ ] The `verification` contract is the single registered source of the binary-question
      vocabulary + severity-attribute enums (one schema; no second copy).
- [ ] Validation uses json-repair + bounded retry and degrades to INDETERMINATE (never crashes a
      gate) on an unparseable structured turn; a test exercises the degrade path.
- [ ] The plan-review verify step consumes the kernel; an offline (FakeRunner) test asserts the
      verifications + downstream verdict are unchanged vs before.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: WS2: Extract Pass-2 finding-verifier + the verification contract into the kernel

## Reproduction Steps

1. Configure local signing (`[identity] signing_key` set; git email resolves to an identity — e.g. 594c).
2. `rebar create task "t"` -> the CREATE event is SIGNED (`author_sig` present).
3. `rebar transition <t> open idea` (or any claim/transition/close) -> the STATUS event is written with `author_id` stamped but **NO `author_sig`** (UNSIGNED).
4. `rebar verify-identity --all --format json` lists that STATUS event as `unsigned` (in-scope, enforceable).

**Expected:** transition/claim/close STATUS (and claim EDIT) events sign like CREATE/COMMENT do. **Actual:** they are attributed but unsigned.

## Root cause

CREATE/COMMENT are written via `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.append_event`, which calls `_apply_authorship` (the signing seam + write-gate). But transitions/claims/closes are written via `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` (`transition_core` ~L249-268, `claim_core` ~L341-372): these build the STATUS/EDIT event dicts, merge `attribution` (author_email/author_id) but write them directly via `fsutil.atomic_write` + git commit, **never calling `_apply_authorship`**. So the transactional path signs nothing AND bypasses the require_authenticated write-gate.

## Why this blocks the flip (dc09 / pristine-horrible-whapuku)

The CI merge-gate `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` runs `rebar verify-identity` over the whole tickets store with posture/boundary from `rebar.toml`. After `require_authenticated=true` lands, every NEW status transition (post-enforce_since) writes an unsigned in-scope STATUS event that the gate flags -> the gate FAILS -> blocks landing. So enforcement is unsafe across the txn writer until this is fixed. This is a foundational signing gap the epic's 5 stories did not anticipate (they assumed signing worked for all writers).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `transition_core` and `claim_core` in `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` sign their STATUS (and
      claim EDIT) events via the same signing seam CREATE/COMMENT use (`_apply_authorship` or an
      equivalent), so a transition/claim/close under a configured signing key produces
      `author_sig`.
- [ ] Under `identity.require_authenticated`, an unsignable transition of a non-exempt ticket is
      refused by the write-gate (parity with `append_event`), while gate-exempt types
      (session_log/code_review/identity) are unaffected.
- [ ] A held-out regression test asserts: with a signing key configured, a transition/claim
      STATUS event has `author_sig` and `rebar verify-identity` reports it `verified`; without a
      key + enforcement on, the transition is refused. Proving command: `make test`.
- [ ] No regression to txn atomicity/locking (claim writes STATUS+EDIT in one commit).
baseline.summary: txn.py transitions/claims/closes write UNSIGNED in-scope STATUS/EDIT events (bypass the signing seam) — blocks safe require_authenticated flip
