## Summary

The `mcp` compose service has **no mechanism anywhere in the repo** to populate the ticket store its tools read. The step is ABSENT, not failing. The deployed server at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` therefore serves a store that does not exist.

## Evidence

- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:42` — `COPY . /app` is the only thing placing files at `/app`;
  `:60` is a bare `CMD ["rebar-mcp"]`. No clone, no init, no entrypoint.
- `.dockerignore:7` excludes `.tickets-tracker` (`:5` excludes `.git`), and the build context is
  the repo root — so `/app/.tickets-tracker` **cannot** be baked into the image by construction.
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:372-373` — the `mcp` service declares only two secret
  volumes. No tracker mount.
- `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` is set for exactly one service, the review-bot
  (`docker-compose.yml:129`). `REBAR_ROOT` appears nowhere in `infra/`.
- Blue-green reproduces the same shape: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:346-368` mounts only
  secrets and sets no tracker env.
- `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:30` provisions a `reviewbot-tickets` site dir; nothing for mcp.
  `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:91-94` provisions a tickets PAT only for the review-bot.
- `docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` has zero occurrences of tracker/tickets/store/clone.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` has a single commit, `8297083532a3` ("Add rebar-mcp HTTP
  service to the AWS box"); the test added in that same commit,
  `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, asserts nothing about a store.

Why the path is `/app/.tickets-tracker`: `rebar.toml` has no `[tracker]` section so the default `.tickets-tracker` applies (`src/rebar/config.py:138-155`); with `.git` dockerignored, `/app` is not a work tree, `git rev-parse` fails and is swallowed at `src/rebar/_config_sources.py:102-103`, falling back to `Path.cwd()` = `/app` (`WORKDIR`, `Dockerfile.mcp:33`).

The review-bot has the mechanism that was never applied to mcp: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:153-155` (entrypoint clone) converged by `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`.

## Observed impact

    list_tickets / search / ready_tickets  -> []                    (silent)
    show_ticket <real alias>               -> "ticket_not_found"
    fsck                                   -> "ticket system not initialized (/app/.tickets-tracker not found)"

Host: EC2 `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (`rebar-gerrit`, us-east-1, 52.3.128.230), up since 2026-07-13. Any agent session that trusted an empty `list_tickets` from this endpoint may have filed duplicate tickets.

## Open design questions (need an operator decision before implementing)

1. Should this server serve the shared `tickets` branch at all, or only certified LLM ops
   (`review_plan`/`verify_completion`)? Those materialize a pinned store via
   `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:672`, which still needs a live tracker or an origin on
   disk — so they likely fail too. Worth confirming whether they have EVER succeeded on the box.
2. Dedicated volume (e.g. `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`) or share the existing
   `reviewbot-tickets` store? Sharing puts two writers on one store; the write lock handles it,
   but it was not designed for that.
3. Read-only or writer? `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` is currently unset. A writer needs a tickets PAT
   that `fetch-secrets.sh` does not provision for mcp.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `mcp` service starts with a usable ticket store, or is explicitly configured and
      documented as not serving tracker reads.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` (or a sibling) asserts the store provisioning, so
      this gap cannot ship silently again.
- [x] `docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` records the decision taken for the three questions above.

## Completion evidence (2026-08-27)

- The `mcp` service starts with a usable ticket store: `provision_store` clones the `tickets`
  branch in `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` (extracted from the Dockerfile under
  `fathomable-yester-thrip`). Verified LIVE: 2763 tickets readable through
  `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`.
- Provisioning is asserted by `test_dockerfile_mcp_entrypoint_provisions_the_ticket_store`
  (`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, on main), alongside an executable suite that drives
  `provision_store` against a temp dir with a stubbed git.
- `docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` is on main and records the decisions.

Follow-ups discovered from this work are tracked separately rather than held here: `fathomable-yester-thrip` (poisoned-store re-clone, merged), `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` (non-blocking boot, merged), `mobile-groovy-badger` (storeless deploy passes readiness, merged), and `rapt-dreadable-dromedary` (a broken store still reads `[]`, open).
baseline.summary: mcp compose service never provisions a ticket store, so every MCP tracker read on the deployed server is empty

baseline.description:
## Context

Operator-declared serious bug: the review-bot's LLM-Review vote publishes only a COUNT of advisory findings ("PASS. N advisory finding(s) (non-blocking)"), and the finding TEXT is retrievable nowhere on the Gerrit change. Operator impact, verbatim: "if they're invisible it makes it difficult for us to determine which advisory findings should be promoted to blocking." This feeds the pending blocking-lane re-enable work.

## Root cause (AC1 — CONFIRMED, see ticket comment #1 for full evidence)

Premise correction: the behaviour is NOT inconsistent. Advisory text is published on NO change. Change 1636 is not a counter-example — live Gerrit shows `revisions/current/comments` = `{}` and `robotcomments` = "robot comments unsupported" for 1636, 1666 AND 1685 alike, and all three carry the same count-only bot message.

Mechanism, single and deterministic:
1. `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:132` `_summarize()`, PASS branch (lines 134-138) renders only
   `len(verdict["advisory"])`. It never itemises the findings.
2. The `"finding"` branch (lines 139-152) itemises BLOCKING findings only — advisory text is
   dropped there too, so a BLOCK vote hides advisories as well.
3. `_translate_findings` (`adapter.py:114`) copies `{severity, dimension, detail}` and DISCARDS
   each finding's `location`, so no file/line anchor ever reaches the Gerrit layer.
4. `voter.py:700` calls `gc.post_vote(change_id, revision, value, message)` — four positional
   args — so `post_vote`'s `robot_comments` parameter (`gerrit_client.py:277-294`) is never
   supplied in production and always falls back to one `/PATCHSET_LEVEL` robot comment carrying
   the same message string. No code path builds a per-file comment map.

Rejected hypotheses: posting failure / auth (the vote POST succeeds — LLM-Review+1 landed on all three) and a size or count threshold (the count is unbounded).

Environmental constraint the fix must respect: robot comments are DISABLED on this Gerrit server, so the review message body is the only surface proven to render. Body enumeration is therefore the guaranteed surface; inline comments are additive.

## Plan

New module `src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` (keeps `voter.py`, currently 778 LOC, under the 800 cap). It OWNS the enumeration logic that `adapter.py:141-152` currently inlines for blocking findings — that block is EXTRACTED here and both adapter branches call it, so the rendering is defined once, not re-implemented:
- `MAX_DETAIL_CHARS = 240` and `MAX_ITEMS = 10` — the exact limits `adapter.py:145-152` uses
  today, promoted to named constants and imported by `adapter.py`.
- `render_findings_block(findings, kind)` — a header line, then up to `MAX_ITEMS` lines of
  `- (criterion) detail [location]` with `detail` truncated to `MAX_DETAIL_CHARS` (ellipsis
  suffix), then an `"N additional <kind> finding(s) omitted from this summary."` note when
  `len(findings) > MAX_ITEMS`. Byte-identical output to today's blocking block for `kind`
  `"blocking"`.
- `parse_anchor(location)` — split a free-text `location` into `(path, line|None)`, tolerating a
  missing or non-numeric line tail; `None` when there is no usable path.
- `partition_findings(findings, revision_paths)` — anchorable only when the parsed path is a key
  of the revision file map; everything else is anchor-less.
- `build_inline_comments(anchorable)` — `{path: [{line, message, unresolved: false}]}`.
  `unresolved: false` keeps the "no unresolved comments" submit requirement untouched.

`gerrit_client.py`: add `GerritClient.get_revision_files(change_id, revision)` — the plain `GET /a/changes/<id>/revisions/<rev>/files`, valid for ANY revision. The existing `get_merge_files` (`gerrit_client.py:184`) delegates to it so the endpoint call exists once and its merge-specific docstring stays accurate. `post_vote` (`gerrit_client.py:277`) gains an optional `comments` mapping, included in the review body only when non-empty; the `robot_comments` default is unchanged (AC5).

`adapter.py`: `_translate_findings` (line 114) also carries `location` through (additive key; existing consumers of `{severity, dimension, detail}` are unaffected). `_summarize` PASS branch (lines 134-138) keeps its count sentence and appends `render_findings_block(advisory, "advisory")`; the `"finding"` branch (lines 139-152) calls `render_findings_block` for blocking and then appends the advisory block.

`voter.py` (minimal delta at the `post_vote` call site, line 700): call `gc.get_revision_files(...)` inside a `try/except` — ANY failure degrades to an empty path set, i.e. zero anchorable findings and body-only publication, never a failed vote. Partition, then post with `comments=`. On `GerritError` from the comment-bearing POST, retry message-only with an appended notice (AC3) and only then treat a second failure as today's fail-closed error.

Design tradeoff, stated deliberately: EVERY advisory is enumerated in the message body, and anchorable ones are ALSO posted inline. Duplication is cheap; invisibility is the bug, and the body is the only surface this server is proven to render.

## Testing

Run from the worktree venv: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py -q`, then `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`. Each AC4 sub-case is a named test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py`, RED-verified by running it against unpatched `main` first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Root cause identified and recorded as a ticket comment (checked: comment #1 cites the live `GET /a/changes/<n>/revisions/current/comments` and `/robotcomments` responses), with the operator's
  "1636 is a counter-example" premise corrected against live Gerrit API state.
- [x] AC2 — Every advisory finding is retrievable from the Gerrit change: enumerated in the
  review message body on both the PASS and the BLOCK path, and additionally posted as an inline
  comment when its location anchors to a real path in the revision.
- [x] AC3 — A comment-posting failure is never silent: the vote still lands, and its message
  carries an explicit notice naming inline publication as failed and pointing at the durable
  `code_review` artifact (`emit_code_review_artifact` -> `rebar.llm.code_review.sidecar.emit`) as
  the full record. Checked by the AC4(e) test asserting the notice substring in the posted message.
- [x] AC4 — Regression tests pin: (a) advisory findings appear as text in the PASS message
  (the reproduced 1666/1685 condition — RED against current main, which emits a count only);
  (b) advisory text also appears on the BLOCK path; (c) an anchorable finding produces an inline
  comment keyed by path with `unresolved: false`; (d) an anchor-less or off-revision finding is
  still enumerated in the body and produces no inline comment; (e) a `GerritError` on the
  comment-bearing POST falls back to a message-only vote carrying the failure notice.
- [x] AC5 — `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck` pass; no change to vote semantics — label name,
  vote values, PASS/BLOCK mapping, fail-closed coverage-gap behaviour and the dedup/retry
  bookkeeping are all untouched.
baseline.summary: Advisory review findings sometimes invisible on the Gerrit change

## What
The release workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `nava-rebar` to PyPI on a `vX.Y.Z` tag but never creates a **GitHub Release**. The v0.2.0/v0.3.0 GitHub Releases were created by hand and that manual step lapsed, so github.com/navapbc/rebar shows **v0.3.0 as Latest** while tags and all three channels (PyPI, Homebrew, MCP Registry) advanced to **v0.6.0**. `docs/releasing.md` does not mention the GitHub Release channel at all.

## Why
GitHub's Releases page is the human-facing "what's the latest version" surface. It being 3 versions stale is misleading to users and contributors.

## Fix (two parts)
- **Backfill (ops):** create GitHub Releases for the missing tags `v0.4.0`, `v0.5.0`, `v0.5.1`, `v0.5.2`, `v0.6.0` with auto-generated notes so `Latest` points at v0.6.0 now.
- **Process (code, via Gerrit):** add a job/step to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that creates a GitHub Release on every `v*` tag push (auto-generated notes, marked latest), and document the channel in `docs/releasing.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GitHub Releases exist for v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.6.0 and `gh release list` shows v0.6.0 as `Latest`.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` creates a GitHub Release automatically on a `v*` tag push (with `contents: write` on that job and auto-generated notes).
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` documents the GitHub Release channel/step.
- [ ] Change lands on main through Gerrit (both LLM-Review and Verified votes green).
baseline.summary: Automate GitHub Release creation in release.yml + backfill v0.4.0–v0.6.0

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` lines 235-242 describe the close's completion precheck inaccurately, and agents reason from the stated mechanism. The current text:

> **After the change MERGES, fast-forward YOUR worktree before you close.** The close's
> completion precheck reads your worktree's git history and requires the merged
> `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit reachable from HEAD (else it fails with "cannot confirm the work
> landed").

Verified against the implementation on this tree (HEAD `1052bc856f`):

1. **"the MERGED commit" is wrong.** `_referencing_commit_exists`
   (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:149`) runs
   `["git", "-C", str(repo_root), "log", "--format=%B%x00"]` (`:159-163`) with **no ref
   argument**, so it scans the whole history reachable from the current HEAD and returns True for
   ANY commit whose message carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or a leading `<id>:` subject that
   `resolve_ticket_id` maps into `accepted_ids` (`:170-176`). Merge status is never consulted. An
   unlanded local commit on your own branch satisfies it.
2. **The precheck is conditional; the doc presents it as unconditional.** It is guarded by
   `if field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker) and not _referencing_commit_exists(...)`
   (`transition_close.py:283-284`), so a ticket with no recorded `file_impact` never reaches it.
   It is also inside `_completion_precheck` (`:195`), which returns early when the
   `require_completion_verification_for_close` gate is off (`:228-236`), on `--force-close`
   (`:237`), and on a live duplicate/supersedes replacement link (`:256`).
3. **`accepted_ids` is a subtree, not one id.** `:277-286` adds every transitive descendant
   returned by `list_descendants` across the `epics`/`stories`/`tasks`/`bugs` buckets, so a
   parent is satisfied by a commit referencing any child.
4. **`--ref` is absent from AGENTS.md.** `rebar transition --ref=<ref>` is documented at
   `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt:7` ("verify (and sign) against the committed tree at <ref>
   instead of HEAD. Use it to close a stacked story against its own commit while your worktree
   stays at the epic tip; default HEAD") and at `docs/plan-review-gate.md:899-916`, whose
   "Stacked-epic recipe" is exactly the workflow this repo runs. AGENTS.md never mentions it —
   `grep -n -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` returns nothing.

The fast-forward advice is a safe superset, so nobody following it is broken. The harm is the false mechanism: believing the precheck ENFORCES land-then-close leads agents to skip `--ref` when closing a stacked story, and to tell operators that a pre-land close is impossible. This happened live — a session told the operator that seven in-progress epic bugs could not be closed before landing; the operator corrected it. The rule that actually orders land-before-close is the POLICY line one bullet above, at `AGENTS.md:233-234`: "Do **not** close a ticket until its change is `Verified +1` — a passing completion-verifier is **not** a substitute for green CI."

## Approach

Rewrite the bullet to state the real mechanism and cite the real ordering rule, keeping the fast-forward guidance for the case it genuinely addresses.

The corrected bullet will:

- lead with the POLICY (`Verified +1`, already stated at `AGENTS.md:233-234`) as the reason to
  wait, instead of implying the precheck enforces it;
- state the precheck accurately: when the ticket records `file_impact` and the
  completion-verification close gate is on, the close requires a commit **reachable from your
  current HEAD** carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer for the ticket **or any transitive
  descendant** — merge status is not checked, so a local unlanded commit satisfies it;
- keep the fast-forward recipe (`git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main`) as the
  remedy for the case it actually fixes: a worktree whose history does NOT contain the commit —
  a fresh worktree, or closing from a checkout that never had it;
- name `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <sha>` as the sanctioned way to close a
  stacked story against its own commit while the worktree stays at the epic tip, and link
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Which commit the completion gate verifies — `--ref`" for the
  detail, per this file's stated "keep this file lean … one-line pointers into `docs/`" rule
  (`AGENTS.md:9-11`);
- state precisely what `--ref` does and does not do: it retargets the completion **verification
  and signature** to that ref's tree; it does **not** narrow the referencing-commit scan, which
  runs `git log` with no ref regardless (`transition_close.py:159-163`);
- preserve the existing NEVER-fast-forward-the-shared-main-checkout warning **verbatim**, as the
  final sentences of the bullet (`AGENTS.md:239-242`).

**Why a rewrite in place rather than a pointer to `docs/`.** AGENTS.md is loaded at launch by every harness, so a wrong mechanism there is the default belief for every agent in the repo; a pointer alone would leave the false statement resident in context. The corrected text stays short and defers the `--ref` detail to `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, which already documents it correctly at lines 899-916 — no new doc is created and no existing doc is duplicated.

**The whole population, not one sample.** The same misstatement exists in a second place: `CONTRIBUTING.md:219-230` (§2f "After merge — fast-forward your worktree, THEN close the ticket") says the precheck "requires the merged `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit to be reachable from HEAD; without the fast-forward it fails with 'cannot confirm the work landed.'" `AGENTS.md:203` sends readers to CONTRIBUTING.md for "the full recipe", so fixing only AGENTS.md would leave the authoritative long-form copy wrong. `grep -rn "cannot confirm the work landed" . --exclude-dir=.git` returns exactly one Markdown hit, `CONTRIBUTING.md:226`, alongside the source string it quotes at `transition_close.py:291` — so those two Markdown passages ARE the population, and both are in scope. `templates/rebar-usage.md` and `templates/AGENTS.md` do not carry the claim (the `test_client_template_sync.py` drift gate covers only the marked rebar-usage region and forbids Gerrit content in it), so they are untouched.

## Scope

- `AGENTS.md` — the single bullet at lines 235-242, rewritten as described above. No other line of
  the file changes.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — §2f, lines 219-230: the same three corrections (not-merged, conditional,
  `--ref`), with the blockquote warning at lines 228-230 preserved verbatim.

No file under `src/` and no test file is edited. This is a documentation-accuracy change with no behaviour change, so there is no new testable behaviour to cover with a new test; the verification is that the existing doc-consistency tests still pass and that the corrected text matches the implementation, checked by the greps in the acceptance criteria below.

Assumption checked, not assumed: no test pins the wording being replaced. `tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py:11-13` slices AGENTS.md between `"**Codex Gerrit workflow rule:"` and `"\n\n## Record your work"`, which ends well before line 235; `tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py` and `tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py:166-167` assert only on the "Navigating the codebase" table; `tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` asserts only the DCO placeholder pattern. None reads the Git-workflow bullet or CONTRIBUTING.md §2f.

## Testing

No new test: nothing executable changes, and the module-size / doc-drift gates that do read these files are already in the suite. Verification is by targeted grep assertions (each exits non-zero on failure) plus the existing suite:

- `! grep -n "requires the merged" AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md` — the false claim is gone from both.
- `grep -q -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` — the stacked-close tool is now named.
- `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" AGENTS.md && grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" CONTRIBUTING.md`
  — the shared-main-checkout warning survives in both (the phrase is on `AGENTS.md:241` and
  `CONTRIBUTING.md:229` today).
- `pytest tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py
  tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py
  tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` — the doc-reading tests still pass.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — unaffected, run to confirm exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The AGENTS.md bullet no longer claims the precheck requires a MERGED commit; verified by
      `! grep -n "requires the merged" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 (no match).
- [x] CONTRIBUTING.md §2f no longer makes the same claim; verified by
      `! grep -n "requires the merged" CONTRIBUTING.md` exiting 0 (no match).
- [x] The AGENTS.md bullet states that the precheck runs only when the ticket records
      `file_impact`; verified by `grep -q "file_impact" AGENTS.md` exiting 0.
- [x] The AGENTS.md bullet states that a referencing commit for the ticket OR any transitive
      descendant satisfies the check; verified by `grep -q "descendant" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 and
      by reading the bullet against `transition_close.py:277-286`.
- [x] The AGENTS.md bullet documents `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <sha>` as the
      way to close a stacked story against its own commit without moving the worktree; verified by
      `grep -q -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 (it matches nothing today).
- [x] The land-before-close ordering is attributed to the `Verified +1` policy rule rather than to
      the precheck; verified by the rewritten bullet naming `Verified +1` — `grep -c "Verified +1"
      AGENTS.md` is one greater than its current value of 3.
- [x] The NEVER-fast-forward-the-shared-main-checkout warning is preserved verbatim in both files;
      verified by `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" AGENTS.md` and
      `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" CONTRIBUTING.md` both exiting 0, and by
      `git diff AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md` showing those warning sentences unchanged.
- [x] No source or test file is modified; verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main` listing
      exactly `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] The doc-reading tests still pass; verified by `pytest
      tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py
      tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py
      tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` exiting 0.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0 and `make typecheck` exits 0.
baseline.summary: AGENTS.md misstates the close precheck: it requires a referencing commit in HEAD's history, not a MERGED one, and omits --ref

baseline.description:
# rebar-debug must trace and record the defect's originating ticket before it closes a bug

## Problem

The `rebar-debug` skill drives a bug to a proven, cited root cause, then throws away the provenance. Phase 1 ends with the mechanism, Phase 2 fixes it, and the ticket closes without naming the ticket whose work introduced the defect. Defect escape rate cannot be measured when escaped defects are not mapped to an origin.

rebar already has the machinery, so this is a skill gap, not a code gap: `caused_by` is a first-class relation (`graph/_links.py:CANONICAL_RELATIONS`); `rebar transition <bug> ... closed` accepts `--caused-by=<id>` (`_commands/transition.py:65,163`); the links feed the `bug_caused_by_fan_in` metric (`metrics/bug_trends.py:255`) and the deterministic epic-close `caused_by` floor (`docs/plan-review-gate.md:1091`).

Absent an explicit `--caused-by`, a bug close silently falls back to blame auto-derivation (`metrics/blame.py:184-227`): it blames `<fixing-commit>~1` across every path in the ticket's `file_impact` and takes a strict majority of **all lines in those files**. Two systematic failure modes follow. It attributes to whoever wrote most of the file rather than whoever wrote the defect. And because it only ever looks at the paths the *fix* touched, it cannot see the common case where the fix site is not the cause site — a producer change introduces an obligation (new field, changed invariant, renamed API) and a consumer is never updated, so the fix lands in consumer code whose lines may be years old and correct-at-the-time. There, blame reliably charges the defect to the consumer's old ticket instead of to the change that shipped the obligation without updating its consumers, which is exactly the escape worth counting.

The skill has strictly better evidence than that fallback and must supply it.

## Plan

Amend two skill files. No code, no behavior change.

**A. `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` — defect attribution:**

1. Add a required attribution step to Phase 1's exit gate (Stage 3), immediately
   before the RCA writeback: find the introducing change by blaming the exact
   lines the confirmed experiment implicated, walk through carrier commits
   (reformat/rename/move), recover the ticket from that commit's
   `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject, and record it.
2. Add an explicit "the fix site is not the cause site" sub-step covering unmet
   obligations and missed consumer updates, with the date test as a cheap
   detector (implicated lines predating the good-to-bad transition cannot have
   caused it) and producer-side search (`git log -S<symbol>`) as the recovery.
3. Route recording through the native surface: `--caused-by=<id>` paired with
   the required `--class` on the bug close, or `rebar link <bug> <origin>
   caused_by` when the link is wanted at the Phase 1 exit instead.
4. Require attribution to meet the root cause's evidentiary standard and
   inherit the fallback's fail-closed discipline, and enumerate four
   resolutions: regression, unmet obligation, omission (attributed by
   scope-of-work), and unattributable (record the searches, leave the link
   unset).
5. Scope attribution to the `defect` and `incomplete-implementation` paths; the
   not-a-bug classifications have no defect to attribute.
6. Gate the bug close on it in "Reporting back" and add a **Defect origin** line
   to the report-back list.
7. Wire the supporting hooks: add the link to the approval-gate own-tracker
   carve-out so recording it needs no user approval; note attribution retention
   on the fast path; point Stage 1's git-history bullet at the exit-gate step.
8. State that `--caused-by` on the close is required whenever an origin is
   known, even if the link was already recorded earlier via `rebar link`:
   `_apply_caused_by` (`transition_close.py:198-201`) calls
   `blame.derive_caused_by` unconditionally when `--caused-by` is empty and
   never checks for an existing `caused_by` edge, so a bare close adds a second,
   guessed edge beside the proven one.

**B. Worktree bootstrap correctness in `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` and `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`:**

9. Replace the bare `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> origin/main` bootstrap
   with `make worktree name=<branch>`, noting that it provisions the worktree's
   virtualenv where the bare form does not.
10. Add one pointer in each skill: run every command with the worktree venv
    first on `PATH` (`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" <cmd>`), because a fresh
    worktree's venv is not on the ambient `PATH` and the pre-commit hook then
    fails on a missing `ruff`/`mypy` even when the code is clean — see
    `docs/local-dev-env.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `SKILL.md` contains an attribution step in Phase 1 Stage 3 that requires
      identifying the originating ticket before the RCA writeback. Verified by
      `grep -n 'Attribute the defect to its originating ticket' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [x] The step gives the literal close syntax including `--caused-by`. Verified
      by `grep -c -- '--caused-by=<origin-id>' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning at least 1.
- [x] The fix-site-is-not-cause-site case is covered as its own numbered
      sub-step. Verified by
      `grep -n 'The fix site is not the cause site' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [x] The unattributable path is present and fails open to a recorded negative
      result rather than a guess. Verified by
      `grep -n 'Unattributable' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning at least one hit in the attribution section.
- [x] The bug close is gated on attribution in "Reporting back". Verified by
      `grep -n 'Do not close the bug ticket until its origin is recorded' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [x] The own-tracker approval carve-out lists the `caused_by` link, so
      recording it is pre-approved. Verified by reading the carve-out paragraph
      and confirming the link appears in its enumerated writebacks.
- [x] The skill frontmatter gate still passes. Verified by
      `python3 scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` exiting 0.
- [x] The close-time flag is stated as required even when a link already
      exists. Verified by
      `grep -n 'is not optional once you have an origin' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`
      returning exactly one hit.
- [x] Both skills bootstrap via `make worktree name=<branch>`. Verified by
      `grep -c 'make worktree' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`
      returning at least 1 for each file.
- [x] Both skills carry the venv-on-PATH pointer. Verified by
      `grep -c 'docs/local-dev-env.md' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`
      returning at least 1 for each file.
- [x] No source file changed. Verified by
      `git show --stat --name-only --format='' HEAD` on the merged commit
      (874a82e73d) listing only the two skill files above.

## Testing

This change is documentation-only (one Markdown skill file); it ships no Python and therefore adds no unit test. It is proven by the repository's own gates plus the per-criterion greps above:

```sh
python3 scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py
git diff --name-only origin/main
awk 'length>100 {print FILENAME":"FNR}' examples/agent-skills/rebar-*/SKILL.md
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py -q
make lint
```

Expected: frontmatter gate PASSes; the diff lists only the two skill files; the line-length scan reports no lines over 100 characters that are not already present on `origin/main`; `test_skill_shared_sync.py` passes (the shared `test-design.md` copies are untouched); `make lint` clean.
baseline.summary: rebar-debug: trace and record the defect's originating ticket (caused_by) before close

## Summary

`ready_tickets` is bounded at 90,000 bytes by bug `daughterly-agitative-ocelot` (`494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0`), but even after that fix's lean projection it sits at **58 rows / 87,893 wire bytes — roughly ONE row of headroom**. The bound is correct and its refusal is actionable (it points at `next_batch`), but the tool will begin refusing its default call about as soon as one more ticket becomes ready. That is a cliff, not a fixed problem.

## The question this ticket answers

Does a DISCOVERY surface need near-full ticket rows at all? `ready_tickets` answers "what can I work on next". Measured on the real store (58 ready rows, 90,000-byte budget):

| shape | bytes/row | rows that fit | headroom vs today |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| as shipped (lean, `TicketStateOut`) | 1,515 | 59 | +1 |
| lean minus `file_impact`/`deps`/author/env fields | 801 | 112 | +54 |
| summary fields, still via `TicketStateOut` | 572 | 157 | +99 |
| summary fields via a NEW closed output model | 234 | 384 | +326 |

Two findings drive this:

1. **The lean ready row still carries fields a discovery caller cannot use.** `file_impact` is
   252 B/row (18.1% of the row) and `deps` 160 B/row (11.5%) — 30% of the payload between them,
   for a question that only needs id/alias/title/type/status/priority and blocking state.
2. **`TicketStateOut`'s declared defaults set a floor.** Projecting to summary fields but
   returning `TicketStateOut` still costs 572 B/row, because `model_validate` re-adds
   `description: null`, `comments: []`, `deps: []`, `inbound_deps: []`, `file_impact: []`,
   `file_impact_scope`, `no_file_impact_reason`, `plan_review_health: null` and
   `cross_session_warning: null`. **338 of those 572 bytes are re-added defaults** — the same
   mechanism that made the parent bug's budget under-estimate by 178%. Reaching 234 B/row
   requires a different, closed output model, which changes the tool's `outputSchema`.

## Scope decision this ticket must make

The cheap half (row 2 of the table) is a further narrowing along the axis `494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0` ALREADY declared breaking, so it folds into that existing release note and needs no schema change. The large half (row 4) changes the declared `outputSchema` and interacts with `full=True`, which must still return the whole shape — so the tool would carry two result types. `docs/api-stability.md` treats declared output schemas as a strong contract, so that half deserves its own decision rather than riding along.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether `ready_tickets` returns a discovery-shaped result via a
      new closed output model, or is merely narrowed further within `TicketStateOut`, with the
      `full=True` behaviour stated for whichever is chosen.
- [ ] Default `ready_tickets` has headroom for at least 3x the current ready count on this
      store, measured on the wire payload (post-`model_validate`, post-`js_safe_result`), not on
      raw reducer rows.
- [ ] Any further narrowing of a default output is recorded in `docs/release-notes.md` and
      `CHANGELOG.md` — folded into the existing `494b` entry if it is the same axis, or as its
      own entry if the declared `outputSchema` changes.
- [ ] `list_tickets` is explicitly considered and the asymmetry justified in the change: it has
      six filter arguments, so an over-budget refusal there is actionable and the budget is a
      guardrail rather than a cliff; `ready_tickets` has none.
- [ ] Regression coverage asserts the per-row size ceiling, so the row cannot silently re-grow.
baseline.summary: Give ready_tickets a discovery-shaped result so its budget stops being a cliff

## Context / Problem

The inbound fetcher can only see one tracker project. `jqls_for(project)` builds exactly one pair of queries — active and recent-done — from a single key (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:78-90`), and `_validate_project_key` refuses an empty or malformed key outright rather than searching unscoped (`fetcher.py:63-75`, bug `626d`). A store that lists several projects in its mapping still ingests only one of them.

## Approach

Fan out: call the existing `jqls_for` once per project in the store mapping and union the results into the snapshot, rather than building a single `project IN (A,B)` query. Two concrete reasons. First, the per-query truncation ceiling (`_ACLI_CEILING = 1200` at `fetcher.py:91`, raising `SilentTruncationError`) stays scoped per project instead of becoming a shared budget that a single busy project could exhaust on behalf of the others. Second, it reuses `jqls_for` and `_validate_project_key` unchanged, so the JQL-injection guard that bug `626d` added keeps applying to every key with no new interpolation site.

Inbound-created tickets record their source project in `bridge_project` and get their `repos` defaulted from that project's mapping entry. The existing local-id derivation already encodes the project (`_jira_key_to_local_id`, `inbound_translate.py:120-124`, `DIG-123` → `jira-dig-123`), so ids stay unique across projects with no change; this story makes the association explicit on the ticket rather than only implicit in the id.

The CREATE event for an inbound ticket is written directly rather than through `create_core` (`apply_inbound_records.py:150-222`, which stamps `creation_channel` at `:221`), so the two new fields are stamped at that same site.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful verified fake fed production-shaped Jira fixtures. The fake must record the queries issued, because "one JQL pair per project" is itself the contract under test and is invisible to a result-only assertion.

- Happy path: a mapping with two projects issues exactly two query pairs — one per key — and the
  resulting snapshot contains issues from both.
- Postcondition: each ticket created from the fetch records the project its issue came from, and its
  `repos` equal that project's mapping entry.
- Edge: a project listed in the mapping that returns zero issues contributes nothing and does not
  fail the pass.
- Failure path: one project exceeding the per-query ceiling raises `SilentTruncationError` naming
  that project, and the ceiling is evaluated per project — a second project under the limit is not
  penalised by the first. This is the contrast case that proves the budget is not shared.
- Collateral invariant: a store whose mapping holds exactly one project issues the same query pair as
  before this change, so single-project behaviour is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mapping with two projects issues one JQL pair per project in a single pass; checked by a fake
      transport recording the issued queries and asserting the exact pair count and contents.
- [ ] Each inbound-created ticket records its source project and the repos from that project's
      mapping entry; checked by asserting both fields on tickets created from a two-project fixture.
- [ ] The truncation ceiling applies per project, not as a shared budget; checked by a test where one
      project exceeds it and a second under-limit project still ingests successfully.
- [ ] A single-project mapping issues an identical query pair to the pre-change behaviour; checked by
      a regression test comparing the recorded queries.
- [ ] A configured project returning zero issues does not fail the pass; checked by an empty-result
      fixture.
baseline.summary: Multi-project inbound fetch: per-project JQL fan-out and source-project recording

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Outbound sync can only write to one tracker project, and it fails closed on anything else. The create client takes its project from a single value set once at construction (`AcliClient.create_issue` uses `self.jira_project`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:271-327`), and the applier scans every outbound mutation pre-flight and raises `CrossProjectTargetError` — aborting the whole pass — if any update or delete targets a key outside the one configured project (`applier.py:217-258`, `_cross_project_targets`, added by bug `626d`). With a mapping that lists several projects, correct mutations to the other projects would be treated as the misconfiguration that guard exists to catch.

## Approach

Two changes, both narrow.

**Create targets the ticket's project.** The outbound create path resolves the destination through `resolve_project` from the mapping module rather than from the client's single construction-time value. A ticket that resolves to "not synced" produces no create mutation at all.

**The guard relaxes from equality to set membership.** `_cross_project_targets` currently compares each target key's prefix against one `configured_project` string; it instead checks membership in the mapping's project set. This is deliberately the smallest possible weakening: the guard stays fail-closed and still aborts pre-flight before any tracker write, so a stale binding pointing at a project the store does not sync is caught exactly as it is today. Only keys the store legitimately owns now pass. Creates remain exempt for the existing reason — their `key` is a local-id placeholder, not a real key, so `_JIRA_KEY_RE` does not match them.

This is the only existing safety property the epic loosens, which is why it is its own story with a paired test rather than folded into another change.

**Module size.** Two files here are close to the repository's hard 800-line gate, and they are treated differently on purpose. `dispatch_one.py` is at 796 lines, so the sibling size-relief story that extracts its `update_one` sub-tree is a prerequisite of this one — four lines of headroom cannot absorb the create-path change. `applier.py` is at 772 and is deliberately **not** split. A structural seam exists there (`_apply_batch` and its helpers), but taking it would relocate `_load_acli` and `_load_concurrency` out of the module against which roughly 62 `patch.object(applier, ...)` test sites are written — and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move, so those tests would keep passing while silently exercising the real Jira and git paths instead of their fakes. Against that, the change needed here is roughly five lines inside `_cross_project_targets` (`:232-257`), which fits comfortably in the 28 lines available. Splitting `applier.py` for this change would be the mechanical split the module-size policy forbids; if it ever must be split, the honest first move is the 67-line `__all__` and the ~126 lines of banner prose in `:1-198`, which disturb no call graph at all.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful fake transport fed production-shaped mutations, recording the create calls it receives, because the destination project carried on the call is the contract under test.

- Happy path: a ticket resolving to project `B` in a store whose mapping lists `A` and `B` produces a
  create call carrying `B`, not the repo default `A`.
- Contrast case (the guard, both directions in one paired test): an update targeting `B-1` where the
  mapping lists `A` and `B` proceeds; an update targeting `C-1` still raises
  `CrossProjectTargetError`. The negative half is what proves the relaxation did not disable the
  guard.
- Precondition assertion: the guard is shown to run **pre-flight** — the fake transport records zero
  writes when the out-of-set mutation raises, proving no partial leak.
- Edge: a ticket resolving to "not synced" produces no outbound mutation of any kind.
- Collateral invariant: with a single-project mapping the guard behaves exactly as before — an
  out-of-project key raises, an in-project key passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An outbound create targets the ticket's own resolved project rather than the client default;
      checked by a fake transport asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [ ] An update inside the configured set proceeds and one outside it raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] When the guard raises, no tracker write has occurred; checked by asserting the fake recorded
      zero writes.
- [ ] A ticket resolving to not-synced emits no outbound mutation; checked by asserting an empty
      mutation list for it while a synced sibling produces one.
- [ ] Single-project behaviour is unchanged; checked by a regression test running the guard against a
      one-project mapping in both directions.
baseline.summary: Multi-project outbound dispatch and cross-project guard relaxation to set membership

It is not a simple rename. In particular, historical `"reconcile-check"` state appears in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:658,717`.

This container separates canonical bridge capability migration from deletion of legacy command/mode/state surfaces. Child 1 maps and implements all useful reconcile-check observables under `bridge preview`, `bridge fsck`, `bridge status`, or one coherent new bridge diagnostic subverb. Child 2 removes CLI/direct-engine modes and persisted-state compatibility only after migration. Child 3 removes library/MCP compatibility methods and schemas after the new bridge contracts are live.

- [ ] No live route, mode, state path, docs, schema, or compatibility profile retains `reconcile` or `reconcile-check` vocabulary.

# `main` is RED on the comment-hygiene gate: three rot-prone run-id references

## Symptom

`python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` fails on current `gerrit/main`:

    comment-hygiene: 3 rot-prone reference(s) found
      tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py:56  [run-id]  30836378745
      tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:1         [run-id]  30836378745
      tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:152       [run-id]  30836378745

The gate runs in the `lint + type-check` job, which is one of the six gating jobs behind the `Verified` vote. **So every change pushed for review right now inherits a `Verified -1` it did not cause.** Observed on Gerrit change 1311, whose own (unrelated) hygiene violations were fixed and which still failed on these three.

## Cause

The references landed with story f124 (`9af278b01f` "live external suite covers many providers" and `1d75850974` "close the ambient-default provider leak"), which cite CI run `30836378745` in docstrings as the evidence for why each test exists.

They were presumably clean when written; the gate itself is recent (`f2b2d0b410` added it, and `d4095763e3` "Fix comment-hygiene acceptor path false-accept" TIGHTENED it). A gate that gets stricter after content lands will surface exactly this shape — pre-existing prose that was acceptable under the looser rule.

## Why the content is worth keeping, and what to do instead

These are not padding. Each docstring explains that the test exists **because a real leak shipped**, and the run id is the evidence. The gate's own message names the accepted alternatives: cite a resolvable ticket id, drop the token for durable prose, or mark it `context: external`.

Story f124 is the durable home for the run id. The fix is to keep the reasoning and cite f124 rather than the run number — the same edit ticket 39c1's cells took.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` exits 0 on `main`
- [x] the three docstrings KEEP their explanation of why each test exists — this is a citation
      change, not a deletion; a fix that removes the reasoning is a regression in a different
      direction
- [x] the run id is replaced by a reference a reader can still resolve (the f124 ticket)
- [x] no test behaviour changes: the suites that cover these files pass unchanged

## Note on ordering

Worth landing AHEAD of other in-flight changes, since it unblocks the `Verified` vote for everything currently in review.
baseline.summary: main is red on the comment-hygiene gate: three rot-prone run-id refs from f124

## Context / Problem
The store-wide compaction sweep stalls every writer in the fleet for minutes at a time. Live operator profiling: "the compaction spawns a fresh git log --full-history child every few seconds (7268 → 7496 …), each at ~100% CPU, holding the global write lock throughout."

Cause, confirmed in code: `_compact_locked` builds the ledger via `_build_authorship_ledger` (`compact_txn.py:72`), which calls `authorship.build_ticket_position_commit_map` (`attest/authorship.py:294`) — one `git log --full-history` walk PER TICKET, INSIDE the lock.

This is bug 7084 one scale up. 7084 found the same walk per SIGNED EVENT (6.78s/event on a 71,041-commit branch; 47.5s of a 48.1s close whose real mutation is ~0.4s) and batched it to per-TICKET — right for compact-on-close, which folds ONE ticket. `gaudy-gangrenous-basilisk` made `compact-all` the standing sweep, so per-ticket became the new per-event.

Two secondary defects in the same path:
- `_commit_backfill` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:275`) stages with an unscoped
  `git add -A`, so a concurrent writer's in-flight event files can be committed under the
  compactor's "chore: backfill SNAPSHOT files" message.
- The sweep never re-yields mid-run: `compact_trigger.run_sweep` probes `write_lock_is_busy`
  once before starting, and the per-ticket loop that follows — in `compact_all_cli`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:386`) — never probes again, so writers arriving after the
  sweep starts wait for the whole run.

## Approach
Batch the read-only prep with no lock held, then take short lock windows for mutations only.

**1. Hoist the history walk out of the lock.** `git log` is read-only and never needed the write lock. Resolve the ledger's introducing-commit data before acquiring; then lock, re-check the ticket's event set is unchanged, write the SNAPSHOT, retire sources, commit, release. Same verify-outside-lock discipline as the original P0 fix, one layer down. A changed event set means the prepared fold is stale — abort that ticket cleanly and let the next pass take it.

**2. Amortize the walk with the primitive that already exists.** Do not write a new batcher: `authorship.build_position_commit_map` (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:466`) already maps every event POSITION to the oldest commit that added its file in a SINGLE pass, walking history once and falling back to the per-entry resolver (fail-closed) for anything it misses. Build it ONCE per sweep and query it per ticket, replacing N directory-scoped walks with one.

The POSITION-keyed builder is the load-bearing detail. Its path-keyed sibling `build_introducing_commit_map` (`:388`) looks equally applicable and is the wrong one: `_build_authorship_ledger` looks up `position_commits.get(position_str)` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:127`), so a path-keyed map would miss every lookup, and every event would fall through to the per-event `resolve_event_commit` — silently re-introducing the exact per-event walks this ticket exists to remove, with correct output and no error to notice. The ledger-parity acceptance criterion below is not enough to catch that on its own, which is why one criterion asserts the WALK COUNT directly.

With the walk gone from the critical section, the per-ticket lock window is the SNAPSHOT write, the renames and the commit — the ~0.4s that 7084's own measurement attributed to real mutation. That subsumes chunking: the hold is already bounded by one ticket's mutation.

**3. Scope the staging and re-yield.** Commit only the paths the sweep folded rather than `git add -A`, and re-probe `write_lock_is_busy` between tickets so a sweep that began on a quiet store stands aside when writers arrive.

The new map parameter on `_build_authorship_ledger` is OPTIONAL (keyword, default `None`), and that is a compatibility requirement rather than a style choice. The function has a second consumer, `compact_rebuild.py:160` (the fsck SNAPSHOT-rebuild path), plus six existing test call sites that pass `(paths, None)` or `(paths, repo_root=...)` positionally. The rebuild path folds ONE ticket, so a per-ticket walk is already the right cost there and it stays UNCHANGED — it simply omits the new argument and keeps building its own map. Only the sweep supplies one.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py` — accept an OPTIONAL prebuilt commit map (default
  `None`, preserving `compact_rebuild.py:160` and the existing test call sites unchanged);
  hoist ledger prep out of the locked section; re-check the event set under the lock.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — build the map once per sweep and thread it through; scope
  `_commit_backfill`'s staging to the folded paths; re-probe `write_lock_is_busy` between
  tickets in `compact_all_cli`'s loop, which is where the per-ticket iteration actually lives.
- `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py` — new tests.

## Testing
- A sweep over N tickets performs ONE history walk, not N — asserted by counting calls to the
  map builder, not by timing.
- No `git log` child is spawned while the store write lock is held — asserted structurally, by
  instrumenting the lock and the walk, never by a duration.
- An event appended to a ticket between prep and the locked re-check aborts that ticket's fold
  cleanly, writes no SNAPSHOT, and leaves its events live for the next pass.
- The ledger produced with a prebuilt map is byte-identical to the one produced by the
  per-ticket walk, over a store containing signed, unsigned and forged-signature events.
- The rebuild path is untouched: `compact_rebuild`'s ledger is unchanged when it omits the new
  argument, so the fsck rebuild keeps its current behaviour.
- `_commit_backfill` commits only the folded paths: a concurrent writer's uncommitted event file
  present during the sweep is NOT included in the compaction commit.
- A sweep re-yields: with the store lock taken after the sweep starts, `compact_all_cli` stops
  folding further tickets and leaves the rest live.
- The prebuilt map is actually CONSULTED: a sweep with the map supplied performs no per-ticket
  walk, proving the key shapes match rather than silently falling back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A store-wide sweep performs exactly one history walk regardless of ticket count — a test
      counts BOTH the per-sweep builder and the per-ticket/per-event resolvers, so a key-shape
      mismatch that silently falls back to per-event walks fails the test rather than passing
      on identical output.
- [x] No history walk runs inside the store write lock — a test instruments both and asserts
      no walk observes the lock held.
- [x] SUPERSEDED, recorded not deleted: no prep/commit TOCTOU window exists to guard. The plan
      proposed hoisting the whole fold out of the lock and re-checking the event set under it.
      What shipped is narrower — only the HISTORY WALK moved out (`_sweep_position_map`, built
      once per sweep before any lock); the fold still runs entirely inside `_compact_locked`.
      That removes the git-log cost from the critical section without splitting it, so there is
      no window and nothing to re-check.
- [x] The authorship ledger is unchanged by the optimisation — a test compares ledgers built
      with and without the prebuilt map on signed, unsigned and forged-signature events.
- [x] The map argument is optional and the fsck rebuild path is unaffected — a test calls
      `_build_authorship_ledger` without it (as `compact_rebuild.py:160` does) and asserts the
      same ledger as before.
- [x] The compaction commit contains only folded paths — a test asserts a concurrent writer's
      uncommitted event file is not swept into it.
- [x] A sweep stands aside mid-run when a writer takes the lock, leaving remaining tickets
      unfolded — and the full local gate set plus CI's pytest tiers pass.
baseline.summary: Sweep walks full git history per ticket under the store lock

## Summary

The mutation sandbox's Linux write-deny (`bwrap`) has **no gating CI lane**. The enforcement tests are gated on `skipif(mutation_sandbox.probe() is None)`. Bubblewrap is installed on the Linux lanes (commit `b63cf799`), but the runners deny unprivileged `CLONE_NEWUSER`, so the functional probe correctly returns `None`, every enforcement test SKIPS, and the leg goes green having proven nothing about Linux enforcement.

This is the silent-skip failure mode: the signal that would report a broken Linux sandbox is indistinguishable from the signal for a healthy one.

## The environment precondition, measured

Two independent mechanisms deny the namespace, and BOTH must be cleared:

1. **Ubuntu 23.10+ AppArmor** sets `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`,
   denying unprivileged `CLONE_NEWUSER`.
2. **Container runtimes' default seccomp** blocks the `clone`/`unshare` outright — so a
   plain `container:` job does NOT work, and neither does relaxing seccomp alone.

Measured on `ubuntu:24.04` (bubblewrap 0.9.0), running a real write through `bwrap`:

| Container mode | Result |
|---|---|
| default | UNUSABLE — `bwrap` never starts |
| `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` | UNUSABLE — `bwrap` never starts |
| `--privileged` | **ENFORCING** — child ran, write outside the allow-list denied |

The probe that produced this table carries a LIVENESS check, and that is load-bearing: a first version without one reported "enforced" for every mode, because a `bwrap` that fails to start never writes the file whose absence was being read as denial — the same false pass fixed under `c100-c4f1`. Any probe used here must assert the child ran.

## Approach

A **privileged container lane**. `--privileged` is a plain OCI runtime capability, not a CI-provider feature: the identical container runs on a developer laptop, which is what `project.portability` requires. The host alternative — `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` on a runner with root — is recorded as a fallback for environments that cannot run privileged containers, but is NOT the primary mechanism, because it was not measured here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A gating lane runs the `bwrap` enforcement tests with `probe()` returning a
      mechanism, so they EXECUTE rather than skip. Verified by the lane's own report
      showing those tests passed, not skipped.
- [x] The lane asserts its own precondition BEFORE running tests: a liveness-checked
      probe confirms `bwrap` both starts and denies a write outside its allow-list. If
      it cannot, the lane FAILS with that message rather than proceeding to a green
      run of skipped tests.
- [x] A skipped enforcement test is a FAILURE on this lane, not a pass. Implemented by
      an env flag that turns the `@live` skip into a hard requirement, so the silent-skip
      mode cannot return. Verified by a test asserting that with the flag set and no
      mechanism available, the suite fails rather than skips.
- [x] The requirement flag is proven load-bearing: with it set and `probe()` forced to
      return None, the enforcement tests FAIL. Demonstrated by real substitution.
- [x] The mechanism is portable: it depends on an OCI runtime capability available
      outside any single CI provider, and the same container is runnable locally
      (`project.portability`). No GitHub-Actions-only construct carries the enforcement.

## Definition of Done

- Linux `bwrap` write-denial is proven by an automated, gating control.
- Skipping is impossible on that lane; a missing mechanism fails it loudly.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Discovered from `e668-b496`: its plan review BLOCKED on a criterion claiming a green `ubuntu-latest` leg proves Linux enforcement when the tests there skip. The same gap was raised as an advisory by the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on change 2256 (patch sets 1, 3, 4).
baseline.summary: Linux bwrap enforcement has no gating CI lane (tests skip silently)

baseline.description: LLM-Review advisory on S10 (52b0-6a6a-c66b-4c59, Gerrit change 2104 patchset 3, doctor_mapping.py:~220). The live-drift diff treats a configured link target absent from the probe's observed set as a drift ERROR. But the probe port's issue_link_types() is fail-soft — it returns [] on any exception (mapping_probe). So a PARTIAL probe failure (link-types API errors while statuses/types succeed) yields an empty observed link set, and EVERY configured link target then appears as drift → false-positive blocking errors, without degrading to 'unavailable'. Non-manifesting on the happy path (a full transport failure degrades to unavailable before this). Fix options: (a) skip the link axis when observed link-types is empty (can't distinguish 'no link types' from 'API failed'); (b) make the probe port distinguish empty-vs-failed for link-types and fold a link-types failure into the unavailable finding. Advisory/defensive; the drift check is best-effort and never the sole gate.
baseline.summary: doctor live-drift: link-axis false-positive when issue_link_types() fails soft to []

## Target
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — **786 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (14 lines of headroom).

Fourteen lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split _commands/init.py (786 LOC) along its concern boundary

## Problem

`_validate_gate_step_ids` already exists (`llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:78`) and has exactly ONE call site: `gate_dispatch.py:154`, `gate_name="plan-review"`. Its docstring records why it was written — a step-id rename in the gate YAML "would otherwise make the recovery lookups silently return `None` and degrade a recoverable run to INDETERMINATE."

The other two gates load a doc at `gate_dispatch.py:437` (`code-review`) and `:697` (`completion-verification`) and validate nothing, while each has python that looks its step ids up BY NAME:

- **code-review** → `llm/code_review/finalize.py` declares `_STEP_VERIFY = "verify"`,
  `_STEP_DECIDE = "decide"` (`:28-29`, used at `:205,211,217,300`) and
  `STEP_ASSEMBLE_DIFF = "assemble_diff"` (`:33`). That file's own comment (`:25-27`) states the
  coupling: these "MUST track gate_dispatch.STEP_VERIFY / STEP_DECIDE ... a rename of those there
  must be mirrored here."
- **completion-verification** → `llm/workflow/completion_metrics.py:34` keys
  `_WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS` on `precheck` / `verify` / `reconcile` / `passthrough`. A rename here
  degrades even more quietly than plan-review's: the row falls through
  `_WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS.get(...)` into `_UNCLASSIFIED_FIELD`, so the timing silently lands in
  "unclassified" and NOTHING errors.

## Approach — add-parity-check at each remaining dispatch site

NOT "one line each". The validator's signature is `_validate_gate_step_ids(doc, required, *, gate_name)`, and the only required-set that exists is `_PLAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED_STEP_IDS`. Each remaining gate needs its own set plus a call.

**The required set must be DERIVED from the constants the dispatcher already references — not re-typed as string literals.** Re-listing the ids would add a THIRD copy of the same fact, which is precisely the defect class this epic exists to remove. Concretely: build code-review's set from `finalize`'s `_STEP_VERIFY` / `_STEP_DECIDE` / `STEP_ASSEMBLE_DIFF`, and completion-verification's from `frozenset(completion_metrics._WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS)`.

Note `completion-verification.yaml` also defines `decide` (`:34`), which no python references — it is correctly NOT required. The set is "ids the code looks up", not "ids the YAML defines"; requiring the latter would fail the gate on any harmless new step.

Import direction is safe: `finalize.py` is a strict leaf that must not back-import `gate_dispatch`, so `gate_dispatch` imports FROM it, which is the direction already in use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `gate_dispatch` validates the code-review doc immediately after `_gate_doc("code-review", ...)`,
      with a required set derived from `finalize`'s step-id constants. Verified by a test that
      renames a step id in an in-memory code-review doc and asserts `GateContractError`.
- [x] AC2: the same for completion-verification after `_gate_doc("completion-verification", ...)`,
      with its set derived from `completion_metrics._WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS`. Verified by the
      equivalent rename test.
- [x] AC3: neither required set re-types a step id as a new string literal. Verified by a test
      asserting each set is equal to the set built from the imported constants, so a literal copy
      would have to drift to pass.
- [x] AC4: the committed gate YAMLs satisfy their own required sets, so the gates still dispatch.
      Verified by a test loading each packaged YAML and calling the validator with no error.
- [x] AC5: `decide` is NOT required for completion-verification, proving the set tracks code
      references rather than YAML contents. Verified by asserting its absence from that set.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "gate_step_ids or gate_dispatch or gate_contract" -q` — the
  rename-detection tests (AC1, AC2), the derivation tests (AC3, AC5), and the
  committed-YAML-passes test (AC4).
- `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` — proves no existing gate-dispatch test regresses, since the
  new calls run on every dispatch.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Validate code-review and completion-verification gate step ids (mirror F13)

## Summary
Reported by a session using the new auto-lander (epic f1fa). When the serial auto-lander rebases a change to the current `main` tip (because `main` advanced under it — the common concurrent case), the rebase mints a NEW patchset. S1 deliberately made the `Autosubmit` label **non-sticky** (empty `copyCondition`) so `addPatchSet` cannot forge a stale land intent (security). But that same non-stickiness means the **bot's own rebase DROPS `Autosubmit`** — so the change no longer matches the selection query `status:open label:Autosubmit+1 is:submittable` and falls out of the lander's pool mid-flight. Under concurrent traffic this stalls the automatic land and forces a manual rebase — defeating the 'set it and walk away' goal.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Set `Autosubmit+1` on a submittable change while other sessions are landing (so `main` advances).
2. The bot selects it, then `main` advances → the bot rebases to the new tip (new patchset).
3. The new patchset has NO `Autosubmit` (empty copyCondition drops it).
4. On the next poll / a re-drive / a bot restart, the change is not `label:Autosubmit+1` → NOT re-selected → the land stalls; the agent must rebase + re-apply Autosubmit manually.

Expected: the bot's own rebase preserves the land intent, so the change keeps being driven to terminal (merged / handed back) without human intervention. Actual: the bot's rebase drops Autosubmit; the in-flight land is orphaned across re-drive/restart under concurrent traffic.

## Root cause (design tension)
S1's non-sticky `Autosubmit` (anti-forgery: addPatchSet must not carry a land intent) collides with S2's rebase drive (which mints a new patchset). Within a single in-memory drive the wipChain still holds the change so my dogfood (#618) landed; the gap bites across a re-drive / hand-back / bot restart, where selection re-queries and the dropped label orphans the change.

## Fix options (to design)
- **Bot re-applies `Autosubmit` after its own rebase** (it holds the change in wipChain and the requester's intent is known/authorized): re-set `Autosubmit+1` (under the bot's or the original requester's identity) immediately after a successful rebase, so the change stays selectable. Must preserve the anti-forgery property (only the LANDER re-applies, keyed to an in-flight wipChain — a random addPatchSet still cannot forge it).
- OR the lander tracks in-flight intent durably in its own state (wipChain persisted) so selection does not rely on the live label surviving the rebase — re-drive/restart reads the durable intent, not `label:Autosubmit+1`.
- Either way: preserve the S1 security invariant (a forged addPatchSet cannot self-request a land).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The bot's own rebase does NOT orphan an in-flight land: after a lander rebase, the change remains driven to a terminal outcome without a human re-applying Autosubmit — verified by a test simulating main-advances-then-rebase across a re-drive, and a live check under concurrent traffic.
- [ ] The S1 anti-forgery invariant is preserved (a third-party `addPatchSet` still cannot carry/forge `Autosubmit`); documented + a config-check or test asserting it.
- [ ] ADR-0042 / land-contract updated with the chosen intent-persistence design.

## Notes
Discovered while dogfooding f1fa (a separate session hit the manual-rebase stall). Related: S1 (843b) non-sticky label; S2b (a9e3) rebase drive; the FFO rebase-treadmill (ADR-0040).
baseline.summary: Auto-lander: non-sticky Autosubmit dropped by the bot's OWN rebase stalls automatic landing under concurrent traffic

baseline.description:
Revise the T10 (overlay-infra) rubric to partition routine durable-infrastructure checks away from transient de-risk experiments while retaining every existing MAJOR safety class. There is no runtime cross-criterion suppression by design, so the boundary must live in the T10 rubric text.

## Work
- Edit `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md`: add this scope clause near the top: "This overlay evaluates the DURABLE infrastructure — the IaC/config that persists. Transient, throwaway experiments used to de-risk a mechanism before committing it — their creation, isolation, and teardown — are out of scope here."
- Immediately after that scope clause, add this exact co-located safety qualifier: "This exclusion does NOT waive the four MAJOR safety classes: a transient apply that is destructive with no safeguard, grants wildcard-admin access, or commits a plaintext secret remains in scope, as does an internet- or untrusted-network-reachable transient service with unspecified human/admin authentication — flag each case." This preserves the current destructive-apply, wildcard-admin, plaintext-secret, and endpoint-auth protections for transient infrastructure.
- Keep the rubric independent: T10 must not name T15 or assign scope to another overlay.
- Add `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-T10.eval.yaml` with ten live dataset cases. Five `pass` controls cover: a throwaway loopback probe with scoped teardown; fully specified durable infrastructure; a private-network transient probe with scoped IAM; a transient probe retrieving its secret from a secret manager; and a disposable sandbox whose teardown cannot touch shared/stateful data. Five `finding` controls cover: under-specified durable lifecycle safety; a destructive transient apply risking shared/stateful data; transient wildcard-admin access; a transient plaintext secret; and an untrusted-network transient service with unspecified human/admin authentication.
- Add a ten-item `gold_set` with one condensed `input` plus `label` entry matching each dataset scenario: five `pass` labels and five `finding` labels, following sibling packaged plan-review specs.
- Add offline text-contract tests in `tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py` that lock the exact scope clause, exact co-located safety qualifier, and rubric independence. Agentic finding behavior is proved separately by the live criterion eval.
- Extend `NEW_SPECS` in `tests/unit/test_new_eval_specs.py` with `plan-review-T10`, so the existing tests exercise strict schema validity, registered scorer discipline, dataset balance, and non-empty gold data for this spec.
- Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` from the registry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The T10 rubric contains the exact durable-infrastructure scope clause.
- [x] The exact four-MAJOR-class safety qualifier appears immediately after the scope clause.
- [x] The T10 rubric does not name T15.

- [x] `tests/unit/test_new_eval_specs.py` registers `plan-review-T10` in `NEW_SPECS`.
- [x] The strict packaged-spec tests pass for `plan-review-T10`.
- [x] The offline T10 text-contract tests pass and assert the exact scope clause.
- [x] The offline T10 text-contract tests pass and assert the exact safety qualifier.
- [x] The offline T10 text-contract tests pass and assert the absence of any T15 reference.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports pass for the scoped throwaway loopback-probe case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports pass for the fully specified durable-infrastructure case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports pass for the private-network scoped-IAM transient case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports pass for the secret-manager transient case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports pass for the sandboxed-teardown transient case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports finding for the under-specified durable-lifecycle case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports finding for the destructive transient-apply case.
- [x] `rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3` reports finding for the transient wildcard-admin case.

- [x] `rebar explain T10` renders the durable-infrastructure scope clause.

- [x] The regenerated T10 guide section renders the durable-infrastructure scope clause.
- [x] The regenerated T10 guide section renders the four-MAJOR-class safety qualifier.

## Testing

- Run `.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval T10 --runs 3`.
