## Why
The single `state["signature"]` slot is last-writer-wins, so one kind clobbers another.
This is the root-cause fix and the riskiest slice (back-compat + compaction), done first.
It is ADDITIVE and behavior-preserving: it introduces the `attestations` map without
changing any existing signature/mirror semantics, so it is safe to ship before the gate
migration (929e).
## What
Add `state["attestations"]`, a kind-keyed map (per-key LWW, like `process_workflow_run`).
`process_signature`:
- MIRROR (unchanged semantics): `state["signature"] = record` for EVERY SIGNATURE event,
  EXACTLY as today — including a blank/retired event (manifest=[], retired=True), which
  still clears the mirror. This preserves 100% of current behavior for the four existing
  `state.get("signature")` consumers and for `retire_attested_pin` (which stays in this
  slice; it is removed only in 929e, together with the reopen-aware validity that replaces
  it — so there is NO window where reopen-invalidation is missing).
- MAP (new, additive): if the event is kindable (non-empty manifest with a derivable kind),
  also set `attestations[kind] = record`. Kind = SIGNED `manifest[0]` substring before the
  first ":" (authoritative); `data["kind"]` is used only as a hint iff it matches, else
  ignored. A blank/retired/unkindable event is SKIPPED for the map (it stays out of the
  map; it does not and cannot clear a kind). Nothing in this slice READS the map yet, so the
  map's presence is inert until cc1b/929e wire consumers to it.
Also add `state["last_reopened_at"]` (in `process_status`): the timestamp of the most recent
`closed -> open` transition (pre-update status == "closed" and target == "open"); null if
never. (Consumed by compute_validity in 929e; recorded here so the data exists.)
Read fold-in: an OLD SNAPSHOT whose compiled_state carries only `signature` (no
`attestations`) is folded into the map on restore, under the kind derived from that
record's own `manifest[0]` (dropped if blank/unkindable). New SNAPSHOTs carry BOTH
`attestations` and the `signature` mirror automatically (the reducer maintains both).
`_present.py` `public_state()`: add a DEDICATED `attestations` branch stripping the
`signature` (HMAC hex) subkey from each per-kind record (the flat `_INTERNAL_SUBKEYS`
cannot express a wildcard kind level); retain the legacy single-`signature` strip.
114f owns the canonical per-record shape.
## Scope
`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (`process_signature`, `process_status`,
`process_snapshot`), `src/rebar/reducer/_present.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`,
`ticket_state.schema.json`. No change to the signed payload; no change to retirement /
mirror semantics; `retire_attested_pin` untouched here.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `attestations` map added; `process_signature` sets the mirror for EVERY event (old semantics preserved, incl. blank/retired clearing the mirror) AND additively sets `attestations[kind]` only for kindable events.
- [ ] Kind from authoritative `manifest[0]`; `data["kind"]` only a validated hint; blank/unkindable events skipped for the map (never clobber a kind).
- [ ] `state["last_reopened_at"]` records the most recent closed->open timestamp (null if never).
- [ ] Old-snapshot fold-in files the legacy record under its manifest-derived kind (dropped if blank/unkindable); new SNAPSHOTs carry both map and mirror.
- [ ] `public_state()` dedicated `attestations` branch strips HMAC hex from every per-kind record; legacy strip retained; no hex in show/MCP.
- [ ] Compaction/SNAPSHOT round-trips all kinds; empty `attestations` omitted; `retire_attested_pin`/mirror semantics unchanged in this slice.
baseline.summary: Reducer + state model: attestations{} kind-keyed map

baseline.description:
## Problem

`MODEL_LADDER` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py`) is the context-limit escalation ladder. Two of its three rungs declare the SAME window:

    ("claude-haiku-4-5",   200_000),
    ("claude-sonnet-4-6", 1_000_000),
    ("claude-opus-4-8",   1_000_000),

Escalation exists to retry on a LARGER context window after a context-limit failure. A sonnet -> opus escalation gains **zero** additional context. The retry that follows is therefore guaranteed to hit the same limit and fail again — but at opus pricing, and after a second full round-trip.

Reproduced by running the code (not by reading the table):

    models_at_or_above('claude-sonnet-4-6') = ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-8']
    window at sonnet rung = 1,000,000; window at opus rung = 1,000,000; gain = 0

## Why it is not merely wasteful

The failure is silent and self-confirming. The escalation reports that it moved to a larger model, the second attempt fails with the same context-limit error, and nothing in the trace says the two rungs were the same size. An operator reads it as "even opus could not fit it", which is a different and more alarming conclusion than the true one: "we never actually escalated".

The wasted spend is the smaller harm. The misleading diagnosis is the larger one.

## The numbers are CORRECT — the design is wrong

The ticket's option 3 ("correct the numbers if either figure is simply wrong") is **ruled out by measurement**, not by assumption. Both figures were verified against the provider's own live Models API (`client.models.retrieve(...)`, field `max_input_tokens`), which is the authoritative per-model capability source:

| rung                | declared | `max_input_tokens` (live API) | verdict  |
|---------------------|----------|-------------------------------|----------|
| `claude-haiku-4-5`  | 200_000  | 200,000                       | correct  |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6` | 1_000_000| 1,000,000                     | correct  |
| `claude-opus-4-8`   | 1_000_000| 1,000,000                     | correct  |

Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 genuinely share a 1M window. The table is honest; the ladder's *use* of it is not. So the fix is option 2 — escalation must SKIP a rung that is not a real capacity increase — and **not** option 1 (dropping the opus rung), because the rung is a truthful ladder entry that `largest_window_tokens` and the model-class vocabulary (task 7761) both legitimately read.

This also means the originally-drafted AC2 ("`MODEL_LADDER` windows are strictly increasing") would assert a falsehood about the real world and would force option 1. It is replaced below by the two guards that are actually true and actually prevent the defect.

## Scope — distinct from its neighbours

* **48b3** (merged) owns rung LOCATION (which rung the walk starts from for a non-Anthropic
  primary).
* **7de4** owns rung TARGET (resolving a rung through the model-class vocabulary).
* THIS ticket owns the ladder's CONSUMPTION — whether consecutive proposed rungs represent a real
  capacity increase at all. Independent of both; can land in any order.
* **e3cd** owns `capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`. Different constant, not touched here.

## Approach

Two functions, because there are genuinely two questions and today one function answers both:

* `models_at_or_above(model)` — "which ladder rungs sit at or above this one?" Contract and
  return value **unchanged**. Task 7761's regression suite observes escalation-target resolution
  through exactly this function (provider stickiness on Bedrock, byte-for-byte bare ids with no
  classes configured, cheapest-first / frontier-last ordering). Narrowing it in place would delete
  the frontier rung from all three of those observables and gut coverage that is not this ticket's
  to weaken.
* `escalation_rungs(model)` — **new**: `models_at_or_above(model)` with rungs that buy no
  additional context removed. This is what a context-limit retry loop should consume, and the name
  says so at the call site.

The filter rule: the START rung is always kept (it is the operator's own model, not an escalation); every rung above it is kept only if its declared window is **strictly greater than the last KEPT rung's**. Comparing against the last kept rung rather than the immediate predecessor keeps the filter correct for a future ladder with several equal-window rungs in a row.

Both context-limit escalation loops switch to the new function, so the defect is fixed in both places rather than one:

* `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` — the Pass-1 size ladder.
* `prerequisites.run_focused_finder` — a one-line change; its existing `ladder.index(model) + 1`
  and `IndexError` handler already yield the correct input-too-large indeterminate when the
  filtered ladder runs out.

Resulting escalation rungs (declared-window filter; targets still resolved through the model-class vocabulary exactly as today, so provider stickiness is unaffected):

| primary               | `models_at_or_above` (unchanged) | `escalation_rungs` (new) |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `claude-haiku-4-5`    | haiku, sonnet, opus              | haiku, sonnet            |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6`   | sonnet, opus                     | sonnet                   |
| `claude-opus-4-8`     | opus                             | opus                     |
| `None` (absent)       | haiku, sonnet, opus              | haiku, sonnet            |
| unlocatable primary   | [that model] (48b3)              | [that model]             |

Dropping the opus rung from *escalation* is safe and correct: the rung is only ever reached after `is_context_limit_error`, and a retry at an identical input window (1M) and identical max-output (128K) cannot succeed where the previous attempt failed. It is a guaranteed-failing paid call. `largest_window_tokens` still reads the FULL ladder and is deliberately left unchanged — its job is "the largest window reachable", which is still 1M, so P8's size budget does not move.

Because `models_at_or_above` is untouched, **no existing test changes its expected values.** The change is additive.

## Implementation

1. `sizing.escalation_rungs(model)` — new; wraps `models_at_or_above` and drops any rung whose
   MODEL_LADDER-declared window is not strictly greater than the last kept rung's. Rung windows are
   looked up by the same bare-name substring match `largest_window_tokens` already uses, so a
   class-retargeted (e.g. Bedrock-qualified) target resolves to its rung's window. A target whose
   rung window cannot be determined is KEPT, never silently dropped — escalation is a recovery path
   and must not become a new failure mode (the same principle `_rung_target` already applies).
2. `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` — iterate `escalation_rungs(cfg.model)` instead of
   `models_at_or_above(cfg.model)`.
3. `prerequisites.run_focused_finder` — one line: `ladder = sizing.escalation_rungs(model)`.
4. Export `escalation_rungs` in `sizing.__all__` alongside `models_at_or_above`.
5. No change to `MODEL_LADDER`'s contents, to `largest_window_tokens`, or to
   `models_at_or_above`'s behaviour.

## Test plan (RED first)

New tests in `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py`:

* **The discriminating escalation test.** Asserting `window == 1_000_000` does NOT distinguish
  sonnet from opus and would pass for the wrong reason. The tests therefore assert on rung
  IDENTITY and on the observed per-attempt model sequence, never on a bare window number:
  - `escalation_rungs("claude-sonnet-4-6") == ["claude-sonnet-4-6"]` — opus, by name, absent,
    while `models_at_or_above("claude-sonnet-4-6")` still returns both rungs.
  - Driven through `pass1_with_ladder` with a runner that records `req.config.model` per attempt
    and always raises a context-limit error: the recorded sequence for a sonnet primary is
    exactly `[sonnet, sonnet]` (batch + one single-criterion retry) and contains no opus id —
    i.e. the paid no-op call is not made.
* **Structural guards** (replacing the drafted AC2):
  - MODEL_LADDER declared windows are **non-decreasing** across consecutive entries — a future
    edit cannot introduce a rung that offers *less* context than the rung below it.
  - For every rung, the windows of `escalation_rungs`'s returned sequence are **strictly
    increasing** — a future edit cannot reintroduce a no-op escalation, whatever the table says.
    This is the guard that actually enforces the fix, and it holds even though the table itself
    has two equal-window rungs.
* **Haiku control (AC4).** The real increase is preserved: `escalation_rungs("claude-haiku-4-5")`
  == `["claude-haiku-4-5", "claude-sonnet-4-6"]`, and a haiku-primary run still escalates onto
  sonnet (observed via the recorded per-attempt model sequence, not just the returned list).
* **Non-regression control.** `models_at_or_above` is unchanged, pinned by re-running
  `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` (task 7761's suite) untouched and green.

MUTATION CHECK both directions: with the filter reverted the new escalation/guard tests must FAIL; with the filter in place the full pre-existing selection must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A context-limit escalation never proposes a rung whose declared window is equal to or
  smaller than the current rung's. Enforced by `sizing.escalation_rungs`, which BOTH context-limit
  escalation loops (`pass1_with_ladder`, `prerequisites.run_focused_finder`) consume.
- AC2: Two structural guards are asserted by test: (a) `MODEL_LADDER` declared windows are
  non-decreasing across consecutive entries, and (b) the windows of the rung sequence returned by
  `escalation_rungs` are strictly increasing from every start rung. Adding a no-op rung fails (b).
- AC3: Both window figures are verified against the provider's published limits, the plan states
  which figure was confirmed and how (live Models API `max_input_tokens`), and the resulting
  decision — numbers correct, filter the consumption — is recorded above.
- AC4: Escalation for a haiku primary (a rung that IS a real increase) still climbs onto sonnet,
  pinned by test; `models_at_or_above`'s own contract is unchanged, pinned by task 7761's existing
  suite passing untouched.
- AC5: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default selection is green, each
  judged by exit code on a clean working tree.
baseline.summary: MODEL_LADDER's sonnet and opus rungs share a 1,000,000 window, so context-limit escalation buys nothing at opus pricing

baseline.description:
## Context

Band-A (A3) auto-remediation drove SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT to zero on the shared store but, by design, LEFT the order-sensitive, human-triage faults for manual reconciliation. As of 2026-07-11 `rebar fsck` reports **17** such faults: **13 ORPHAN_EVENT** (pre-snapshot EDIT events absent from the snapshot's `source_event_uuids`) + **4 MISSING_CREATE** (110e, 957d, 9fa4, cf5d). Auto-repair is unsafe here: `rebar fsck --repair-snapshots` rebuilds from the full log and previously CORRUPTED 11/13 statuses, and `--repair` routes EDIT orphans to human triage (won't fix them). The store has been backed up (188MB git bundle + 967-ticket NDJSON export at HEAD 8c3c26f72) before any mutation.

## Forensic classification (recorded in detail as a comment on this ticket)

- **13 ORPHAN_EVENT** — benign snapshot-staleness from a distributed compaction-vs-reconciler
  write race; live status/assignee verified correct for all 13 (each orphan's effect is a
  redundant duplicate of an identical post-snapshot reconciler EDIT).
- **4 MISSING_CREATE** — local-only phantom dirs (0 tracked files, not in HEAD, no structural
  references). 957d/9fa4/cf5d are empty; 110e's `.cache.json` holds an epic that is a duplicate
  of the already-tracked open epic 6d0d (content not lost).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] Per-orphan disposition applied: retire each of the 13 orphan EDIT files (`.json` ->
  `.json.retired`, which fsck's `is_active_event()` skips) — lossless, touches no status.
- [ ] [operator-attested] MISSING_CREATE disposition applied: delete the 4 local phantom dirs (110e resolved as a
  duplicate of tracked epic 6d0d; 957d/9fa4/cf5d are empty residue).
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar fsck` reports zero ORPHAN_EVENT + zero MISSING_CREATE, and no ticket's displayed
  status/assignee changed (verified via a before/after diff of all 13 orphan tickets — all
  `closed`; assignees `""` except cc5b and f112 = "Joe Oakhart").
- [ ] [operator-attested] Decisions recorded on the ticket (done — see the forensic comment) and the store change
  committed to the `tickets` branch and pushed.

## Notes

- Root cause (compaction snapshotting before observing a remote reconciler write) is a recurring
  race; a durable fix is separate follow-up work, out of scope for this remediate-to-zero ticket.
baseline.summary: Human-triage the 14 residual fsck orphans (13 EDIT ORPHAN_EVENT + 1 MISSING_CREATE)

baseline.description:
## Why
3183 (change 580, commit da27c5f30) delivered the merge-gate + snapshot ledger with a divergent schema and verdict set vs. the APPROVED epic design (AC8/AC9 — the two ACs the epic completion-verifier correctly FAILED on). This story reworks commit 7 to the approved design AND performs the consumer cutover deferred from TS1 (in-toto payload) and TS2 (commit-ancestry era) — the write-seam signing, the merge-gate, and the ledger all live in THIS commit. Depends on TS1 and TS2. (User rejected the delivered design; see d7c0.)

## Stack scoping (why the cutover is here + why TS2+TS3 land together)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 580 = commit da27c5f30 (3183): `_seam.py`'s write-time signing, `verify_authorship.py` (merge-gate), `compact.py`'s ledger, and `_state.py`'s authorship summary. At this commit those consumers currently still call the epoch API that TS2 REMOVED (`epoch_for_position`, `verify_authorship_at_epoch`), so the commit-7 patchset is RED until this story rewires them — TS2+TS3 land together. `ensure_identity_for` (aliased by `create_placeholder`) lives in commit 6, so `create_placeholder` lands here too.

## What

### 1. Write-seam in-toto cutover (`_seam.py::_apply_authorship`)
Stamp `author_sig` by calling `authorship.sign_event_authorship(event, signing_key, principal=author_id)` (the in-toto Statement envelope) instead of `sign_authorship(canonical_bytes, ...)`.

### 2. Merge-gate rewire (`verify_authorship.py`)
- Refactor `_ScopedEvent`: REPLACE the `epoch: int | None` field with `commit_sha: str |
  None` and `position: str | None` (the `{timestamp}-{uuid}` string). Live events populate
  `position` from the filename and resolve `commit_sha` lazily; ledger entries populate both
  from the ledger record (below).
- LIVE-event content binding: parse the DSSE payload as an in-toto Statement and check
  `subject[0].name == ev['uuid']` AND `subject[0].digest.sha256 ==
  authorship.authorship_content_hash(ev)` (replacing the raw-bytes `envelope.payload !=
  ev.payload` compare). Resolve the event's commit via
  `authorship.resolve_event_commit(position, ticket_dir, repo_root)`.
- Verify via `authorship.verify_authorship_at_commit(envelope, author_id, commit_sha,
  position, repo_root=...)` (replacing `epoch_for_position` + `verify_authorship_at_epoch`).
- **Four-way classification (the AC9 distinction):**
  - `unsigned` — no `author_sig`.
  - `unknown-author` — no `author_id` / not an identity ticket.
  - `verified` — content binds AND `verify_authorship_at_commit` verified (key valid at the
    event's commit).
  - `key_not_valid_at_era` — content binds AND the signature is cryptographically valid
    against SOME key in the identity's keyring (any era) BUT not one valid at the event's
    commit. Decided by a NEW helper `authorship.verify_authorship_any_key(envelope,
    identity_id, *, repo_root) -> registry.Verdict` that builds the trust root from ALL
    keyring public keys (regardless of validity window) and runs ONE `registry.verify`
    (boolean). valid-any-key AND NOT valid-at-commit ⇒ `key_not_valid_at_era`.
  - `bad-signature` — content mismatch, malformed envelope, or verifies against NO key the
    identity ever held (forged).
- Add the verdict constant `KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA = "key_not_valid_at_era"` and extend the
  CLI `counts` dict (currently hardcoded `{VERIFIED, UNSIGNED, UNKNOWN_AUTHOR,
  BAD_SIGNATURE}`) with the new key so it is tallied and printed. Document the display
  grouping in the module docstring: `verified` / `unverified` (= `bad-signature` |
  `key_not_valid_at_era` | `unknown-author`) / `unsigned`. When `resolve_event_commit` fails
  for a LIVE event (unresolvable commit), the fail-closed verify yields non-`verified` and
  the event is reported like any other non-verified event.

## Migration note (unlanded + atomic)
The `authorship_ledger` wire format changes from `{event_uuid, author_id, author_sig, epoch}` to `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position}`. The stack is UNLANDED and lands atomically, so no real store holds an old-format ledger; there is no in-place snapshot migration to write (a pre-feature snapshot with no ledger is unaffected; the reducer cache version bump from TS2 already invalidates stale reductions).

### 3. Ledger (`compact.py::_build_authorship_ledger`)
Record `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position}` per signed folded event, where:
- `content_hash` = `authorship.authorship_content_hash(ev)` (TS1 digest).
- `signature` = the event's `author_sig` (the DSSE Statement envelope).
- `signer_pubkey` = the actual public key that verified the signature. Because SSHSIG verify
  (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`) returns only pass/fail (NOT which key matched), determine it via a
  new `authorship.identify_signer(envelope, identity_id, *, repo_root) -> str | None` that
  iterates the identity's FULL keyring — ALL public keys, including REVOKED ones (so a valid
  signature by a since-revoked key is still identified, enabling the later
  `key_not_valid_at_era` classification) — verifying the envelope against each single-key
  trust root and returning the first that passes. **Single None-policy:** if `identify_signer`
  returns `None` (the signature verifies against NO key the identity ever held — a forged /
  foreign signature), STILL record a ledger entry (never omit — omitting would hide a forged
  event from the post-compaction merge-gate) with `signer_pubkey: null`; ledger verification
  (Section 4) classifies a null-`signer_pubkey` entry as `bad-signature`. The record always
  has exactly the five keys; `signer_pubkey` is a string or `null`.
- `position` = `{"commit_sha": <resolve_event_commit(...)>, "position": "<{ts}-{uuid}>"}` —
  the `position` string is the SAME `{timestamp}-{uuid}` value `verify_authorship_at_commit`
  already consumes for intra-commit ordering (NO separate integer index; the string ordering
  is the intra-commit index). `commit_sha` is resolved at compaction time.

### 4. Ledger verification (`verify_authorship.py::_ledger_events` + `_verify_signed`)
Rewrite `_ledger_events` to read the NEW fields (`content_hash`, `signature`, `signer_pubkey`, `position.commit_sha`, `position.position`) — not the old `author_id`/`author_sig`/`epoch`. For a ledger entry, verification is self-contained: crypto-verify the `signature` envelope against a ONE-key trust root built from `signer_pubkey`, check the Statement binds `content_hash`, and decide era from `position.commit_sha` against the SURVIVING snapshot keyring (retired KEY files folded into the same snapshot; `resolve_event_commit` still finds a retired file's ADD commit via `git log --diff-filter=A` across history) via `verify_authorship_at_commit`'s ancestry logic — emitting the same four-way verdict. A ledger entry with `signer_pubkey: null` is classified `bad-signature` directly (no key ever verified it). No raw event file needed.

### 5. Verdict vocabulary (NOT the verify-signature schema)
`verify_signature_result.schema.json` is the schema for the SEPARATE `rebar verify-signature` command (HMAC attestations: `unsigned|foreign_key|certified|mismatch`) — it is NOT touched. The `verify-authorship` verdicts are its own vocabulary (string constants in `verify_authorship.py`): `verified`, `unsigned`, `unknown-author`, `bad-signature`, and the NEW `key_not_valid_at_era`, with the display grouping documented in that module. (The epic AC's phrase "existing verify_signature_result verdicts" is read as the verdict-vocabulary style, not a literal edit to that unrelated command's schema — reconciled per plan-review.)

### 6. `create_placeholder`
Add `create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name, *, repo_root=None)` to `identity.py` as a thin idempotent alias over the delivered `ensure_identity_for`, and re-export it through the library facade chain so `rebar.create_placeholder(...)` is importable: add it to `_lib_writes.py` and to `rebar/__init__.py`'s `__all__`/exports alongside `ensure_identity_for`.

## Scope
In: the write-seam in-toto cutover, the merge-gate rewire to commit-ancestry + in-toto content-binding + the four-way `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict, the approved ledger schema + self-contained ledger verification, the `signer_pubkey`/`identify_signer` + `verify_authorship_any_key` helpers, and the `create_placeholder` alias + re-export. Out: authorship payload machinery (TS1, done); era model machinery (TS2, done); docs/ADR (TS4). NOTE: `verify_signature_result.schema.json` is deliberately NOT modified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A live signed event round-trips: with `identity.signing_key` set and a current
  identity holding a valid key, an event written through the seam is classified `verified`
  by `rebar verify-authorship` (proves the in-toto `_seam` stamping + the merge-gate in-toto
  content-binding + commit-ancestry verify are wired end-to-end).
- [ ] The SNAPSHOT authorship ledger records `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature,
  signer_pubkey, position}` (position = `{commit_sha, position:"<{ts}-{uuid}>"}`) per signed
  folded event; a round-trip test signs events, compacts (horizon=0, threshold=1), and
  asserts `verify-authorship --all` returns `verified` from the ledger ALONE (raw event
  files retired). A test also asserts the ledger record has exactly those five keys and that
  `signer_pubkey` equals the actual signing key.
- [ ] `verify-authorship` emits a distinct `key_not_valid_at_era` for an event whose
  signature is cryptographically valid by a key the identity holds but which was NOT valid at
  the event's commit (e.g. an event signed by a since-revoked key), distinct from
  `bad-signature` and `unknown-author` (test drives the CLI and asserts the verdict string).
- [ ] `bad-signature` is still emitted for a forged signature (verifies against no key the
  identity ever held) and for a content-binding mismatch (test).
- [ ] The `verify-authorship` verdict vocabulary exposes `key_not_valid_at_era` (a test
  asserts the constant / that the CLI can print it) and the module documents the
  `verified/unverified/unsigned` display grouping; `verify_signature_result.schema.json` is
  unchanged (a test asserts its enum is still `unsigned|foreign_key|certified|mismatch`).
- [ ] `rebar.create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name)` mints a keyless
  placeholder identity, is idempotent on repeat (returns the same identity), and is
  importable from the top-level `rebar` package (test).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (in-toto cutover: stamp author_sig via sign_event_authorship)
- `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` (_ScopedEvent epoch->commit_sha/position; in-toto content-binding; verify_authorship_at_commit; key_not_valid_at_era four-way verdict; read new ledger)
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (approved ledger schema + signer_pubkey via per-key identify)
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (verify_authorship_any_key + identify_signer helpers)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (create_placeholder alias over ensure_identity_for)
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (re-export create_placeholder)
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` (export create_placeholder for rebar.create_placeholder)
baseline.summary: transition: snapshot ledger schema + key_not_valid_at_era verdict (approved AC8/AC9)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

rebar's four-pass code-review system supports packaged criteria, while project criteria are declared in a repository overlay. Before this epic, a net-new project code-review criterion could be discovered by configuration but was dropped at the criterion-id resolver, Round-A fan-in, Pass-3 routing, eval/calibration surface, and CLI admission. The extension contract was also unproven in the deployed Gerrit review bot.

This epic repairs those seams, documents the contract, authors the first project criterion, and dogfoods it in advisory-only live Gerrit reviews. It supersedes the former umbrella `jira-reb-1001`, generic story `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, and bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8`.

## Delivered decomposition

The eight child tickets are dependency-ordered and closed:

1. `fc72-bf7e-7652-4228` — gate-key criterion-id resolver in
   `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py`.
2. `761e-5af2-ed57-408a` — Round-A fan-in and logical-id attribution in
   `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` and `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`.
3. `58ef-91fa-20c1-4f29` — repository-effective Pass-3 routing in
   `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py`.
4. `8153-e9b5-5706-49c8` — eval/calibration admission in
   `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` and `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`.
5. `41e2-a0a2-2db4-4847` — CLI admission in
   `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py`.
6. `19dd-7d89-972b-4274` — runtime contract in `docs/llm-framework.md`.
7. `225a-323c-a9f6-436b` — `project.review-phase-boundaries`, routing, and balanced eval corpus.
8. `9447-b31c-e0b7-446d` — advisory live-Gerrit dogfood, including the repaired
   repository-root seam and the cleaned final prompt revision.

Each seam child owns a disjoint production-file set. The shared `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` grows the end-to-end RED→GREEN proof across the stack.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar list --parent 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96` returns exactly the eight children above, each
  `closed` with a completion-verifier attestation.
- [ ] The five original drop-point categories are each owned by exactly one seam child: resolver
  (`fc72`), fan-in/attribution (`761e`), effective routing (`58ef`), eval/calibration (`8153`), and
  CLI admission (`41e2`); their production file-impact sets do not overlap.
- [ ] The no-overlay runtime preserves the ordered 13 built-ins, packaged Pass-3 dispositions, and
  default plan-review resolver mapping. Verify with
  `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k "resolver or fan_in or parity or routing"`.
- [ ] An active project code-review criterion runs once in Round A, retains its logical
  `criteria` id and physical `reviewer_id`, and uses repository-effective Pass-3 routing. Verify
  with the project-criteria unit tests and the live artifact cited on child `9447`.
- [ ] The eval/calibration API and CLI admit an active code-review-only project criterion while
  rejecting inactive or ambiguous project ids; the balanced
  `project.review-phase-boundaries` corpus and its prompt are present.
- [ ] The project-criterion runtime contract is documented in `docs/llm-framework.md`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Child `9447-b31c-e0b7-446d` is closed with a signed completion PASS;
  its final Gerrit change is merged, its live artifact has `coverage.llm_ran: true`, the FIRE
  directive is absent from the submitted revision, and routing remains threshold `0.90` with
  blocking disabled.
- [ ] The epic has `supersedes` edges to `jira-reb-1001`, `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, and
  `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8`, and all three tickets are `closed`.
baseline.summary: Thread project code-review criteria through the four-pass code-review seam

baseline.description:
## Problem
`reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot` is the last reconciler write that composes `git_adapter.add` + `git_adapter.commit` against the tickets tracker OUTSIDE the atomic locked commit+push transaction. Ticket 6454-d06e-7361-4e3d attempted the conversion and reverted it: the only offered seam, `rebar._store.push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch`, stages with `git add -A`, which sweeps in `.bridge_state/last-pass.json` — a per-pass timestamp the deliberate selective 5-file staging excludes. The tickets HEAD then advances on every idempotent pass and `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head` goes RED (reproduced in CI on Gerrit 1821 ps1 and locally).

Ticket 638a-3746-e58a-4929's R3 composition gate therefore lands with a durable reasoned `# raw-git-ok:` marker on that site. This ticket removes the marker by removing the reason for it.

## Approach (decided)
Extract the locked commit phase of `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` (exclude-lock-artifacts, write_lock, rebase guard, status, stage, commit) into a shared helper that takes an optional `paths` pathspec (`None` = today's `git add -A`; a sequence = `git status/add -- <paths>` scoped staging), and export it as `commit_tickets_branch(tracker, *, message, paths=None, strict=False, author_name=None, author_email=None)` — commit under the shared write lock, NO push. `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` keeps its exact current behavior (locked `-A` commit, then delivery) by calling the same helper then `push_tickets_branch`.

`_commit_binding_store_snapshot` then calls `commit_tickets_branch(tracker_dir, message=..., paths=<the 5 existing .bridge_state files>, strict=True)` instead of composing `git_adapter.add` + `diff_cached_names` + `commit`.

Classifications, explicit:
- **Push is OUT of scope and behavior is preserved**: today's site does not push; the new `commit_tickets_branch` never pushes. No caller of `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` changes behavior (same staging, same lock, same delivery).
- **Fail-open contract preserved**: `strict=True` makes any seam failure (stage/commit/lock-timeout/rebase-guard) raise `PushDeliveryError`, which the site's existing broad `except Exception` already converts into `return False` + stderr log + dedup'd `bridge_alerts` append — the exact contract `reconcile.py` depends on. Success paths (commit made, or nothing-to-commit) return normally → `True`.
- **Per-file idempotency (bug 1e08) preserved**: the pathspec-scoped `git status --porcelain -- <paths>` reports a change in ANY of the 5 named files individually (a retirement-only `bindings-retired.json` change stages and commits; no change in any of the 5 → no commit, HEAD unmoved), which is the property the basename check implemented.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `_commit_binding_store_snapshot` no longer calls `git_adapter.add`/`git_adapter.commit`; it goes through the shared locked seam (`rebar._store.push.commit_tickets_branch`), which does NOT push (today's no-push behavior preserved).
- [x] The committed file set is unchanged (the same 5 `.bridge_state` files, never `-A`): a dirty non-allowlisted tracker file (e.g. `.bridge_state/last-pass.json`) is not committed and does not advance HEAD on an otherwise-unchanged pass.
- [x] The fail-open bool + alert contract is unchanged: seam failure → `False` + stderr + dedup'd bridge_alerts entry (existing tests in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_commit_binding_store_failure.py stay green); success and nothing-to-commit → `True`.
- [x] `test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head` stays green, as do the retirement/rotation per-file idempotency tests (bug 1e08).
- [x] The `raw-git-ok` marker on `reconcile_helpers.py` is deleted and `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` still passes.
- [x] `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` callers see no behavior change (existing unit tests stay green).
baseline.summary: Give the tickets-branch commit seam a pathspec so the binding-store snapshot can leave raw git

baseline.description:
Add a `make worktree name=<branch>` target that creates a fresh git worktree branched from current `origin/main` and fully provisions its local env in one step — so agents and humans stop hand-running the multi-command worktree setup the repo's CLAUDE.md / docs/local-dev-env.md prescribe.

## Why
The repo mandates working in a fresh worktree branched from `origin/main` with its own local venv (never the main checkout, never a stale global build). Today that is a documented but manual sequence (`git fetch` → `git worktree add` → create venv → `make install`), which is error-prone and easy to shortcut. A single target makes the canonical setup one command, matches the repo's existing Makefile idiom, and needs no new per-developer dependency (git + python + the existing `make install`). This is the wrapper-command approach chosen over direnv: it matches "provision on creation" semantics, works identically for humans, agents, and non-interactive CI, and reuses the ONE canonical `make install` path rather than forking it.

## What
Add a `worktree` target to `Makefile` that:
- Requires a `name=<branch>` argument; prints usage and exits non-zero if absent.
- Creates the worktree at `../<name>` (overridable via `dir=<path>`), branched from
  freshly-fetched `origin/main` (`git fetch origin` then
  `git worktree add <dir> -b <name> origin/main`).
- Provisions the venv via the SAME sequence the docs bless and this change dogfoods:
  `python3 -m venv .venv` (seeds pip so the canonical installer works) then, with the
  venv active, `$(MAKE) install` (editable `.[dev]` install + `make hooks` wiring the
  pre-commit gate). No bespoke pip line — it delegates to the existing canonical path.
- Prints a final "activate with: cd <dir> && source .venv/bin/activate" hint.
- Is added to `.PHONY` and carries a `## ` help string so `make help` lists it.

The Gerrit `commit-msg` hook is inherited automatically (worktrees share the common git dir's hooks), so the target does not re-fetch it — a note in the recipe records why. Register the new target's purpose with a one-line mention in `docs/local-dev-env.md` so it is discoverable next to the manual sequence it replaces.

## Scope
- `Makefile`: new `worktree` target + `.PHONY` entry.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`: one line pointing at `make worktree name=<branch>` as the
  one-command form of the documented manual setup.
- Non-goal: direnv / auto-activation on `cd` (a different concern — ongoing activation,
  not creation-time provisioning); non-goal: a `post-checkout` hook; non-goal: removing
  the manual instructions (kept as the explanation of what the target automates).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make worktree` with NO `name=` prints a usage message and exits non-zero.
      Proving command: `make worktree 2>&1; test $? -ne 0 && echo USAGE-OK`
- [ ] `make worktree name=<tmp>` creates a worktree at `../<tmp>` on a new branch
      `<tmp>` whose HEAD equals current `origin/main`, containing a populated `.venv`
      with a working `rebar` on its path.
      Proving command (run against a throwaway name, then clean up):
      `make worktree name=__wt_probe && test -x ../__wt_probe/.venv/bin/rebar && ( cd ../__wt_probe && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD | grep -qx __wt_probe ) && echo CREATE-OK`
      Cleanup: `git worktree remove --force ../__wt_probe && git branch -D __wt_probe`
- [ ] The target is listed by `make help` (has a `## ` description) and is in `.PHONY`.
      Proving command: `make help | grep -q 'worktree' && grep -q '^\.PHONY:.*worktree' Makefile && echo HELP-OK`
- [ ] `docs/local-dev-env.md` references `make worktree name=` as the one-command setup.
      Proving command: `grep -q 'make worktree' docs/local-dev-env.md && echo DOC-OK`
- [ ] Existing gates stay green (Makefile is not Python, but the repo's checks must pass).
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck` both exit 0.
baseline.summary: Add 'make worktree name=<branch>' one-command worktree+venv bootstrap target

baseline.description:
## The defect

Two test sites outside the live-DC tier are the same **fail-OPEN** class as bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` / `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508`, under a different phrasing. Each spawns a REAL child with `subprocess.run`, never asserts a returncode, and its ONLY assertion is that some string is ABSENT from the captured output. A child killed by a signal writes nothing, so the absent-string assertion is trivially satisfied and the test reports GREEN for a run that never executed.

Proven mechanism (bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`, 4/4 deterministic): a child that SIGKILLs itself yields `returncode == -9` with `stdout == stderr == ""`.

### Site 1 — `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127`

`test_absent_floor_file_emits_no_workflow_error`. `_run_gate` (line ~54) is `subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", gate_script], capture_output=True)` with no `check=True` and no returncode assertion. The whole test body is three lines and its only assertion is:

    assert "::error::" not in (result.stdout + result.stderr)

A reaped or OOM-killed bash child gives empty streams, so the gate script never ran and the test still passes. This is a **success/health oracle** — the dangerous direction.

### Site 2 — `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:151`

`test_reconcile_is_routed_...` (the non-integration one). Real child via `_cli(...)`. No returncode assertion anywhere in the test; the sole assertion is:

    assert "unknown subcommand 'reconcile'" not in (cp.stdout + cp.stderr).lower()

Empty output from a signal-killed child satisfies it, so a never-started CLI reads as "the dispatcher routed correctly".

### Borderline (lower risk, worth a look)

`tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243` — `_run_redispatch` asserts `completed.returncode != 0`, which a `-9` / `137` exit ALSO satisfies, so the returncode check does not fully close the gap. It is a message-quality oracle on a deliberately-failing run, so the residual risk is low, but `!= 0` is the wrong shape for the same reason.

## Why it was not fixed in scope

Filed rather than fixed because both files sit outside the file lane of `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` (the live-DC test files plus their shared helper) and were held by other sessions at the time. They are also a different construct — an absent-string oracle over `stdout + stderr`, not the `assert "Traceback" not in cp.stderr` shape — so folding them in would have widened that change past what one review can carry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Neither site can pass on a signal-killed child: the returncode is asserted, not only the
      absence of a string in the captured output.
- [x] A RED test proves it for each site — the child forced to die on a signal (empty output)
      makes the assertion fail before the fix, and the failure names the signal after it.
- [x] `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243`'s `returncode != 0` is tightened or explicitly
      justified, since a signal kill satisfies `!= 0`.
- [x] Reuse `tests/_child_diag.py` (`child_failure_detail` / `assert_child_ran_clean`) rather
      than re-deriving the message, so every tier fails identically.
baseline.summary: Absent-string child oracles fail OPEN on a signal-killed child

## Why

## What — careful split along the comment-diff seam

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `outbound_comments.py` created (>100 LOC) holding the comment-diff cluster; `outbound_differ.py` imports it.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` drops BELOW 800 LOC and is REMOVED from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`.

## Context / Problem
At plan authoring (commit 0f5dbc88b, Ruff 0.15.19) the narrow RUF command `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 --statistics src/rebar tests` reported 142 actionable diagnostics (49 RUF059, 36 RUF022, 18 RUF005, 18 RUF012, 10 RUF043, 6 RUF023, 2 RUF028, and one each of RUF019, RUF046, RUF102). Those figures are dated observations, not the contract. The pinned Ruff is now `ruff==0.16.1` (`pyproject.toml`); the authoritative inventory is whatever that same narrow command reports against the **current** `origin/main` tip. Running the narrow census without ignoring RUF100 also surfaces RUF100 diagnostics that are narrow-selection artifacts (the valid `noqa` codes are outside that command's selected rules); they are not counted as remediation debt.

This story clears the live narrow-census RUF diagnostics (142 at plan authoring; use the current `origin/main` count) before selecting the family. RUF001, RUF002, and RUF003 remain deferred because many flagged Unicode symbols are intentional prose or UI content. True RUF100 findings are evaluated only with the final full configured rule set after RUF is selected; any suppression that is stale under that full configuration is removed.

## Dependencies and Ownership
This story depends on `28cd-d8f8-4456-482c`. The dependency is both ordering and shared-file ownership: the predecessor lands the ASYNC/DTZ `pyproject.toml` configuration and creates `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`; this story then edits the resulting configuration and extends that test. It does not create a competing version of the file.

## Approach
1. Extend `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` to require `RUF` in `[tool.ruff.lint].select`.
2. Add `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore = ["RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003"]` in `pyproject.toml`. The global deferral lives only in this exact key; do not introduce `extend-ignore` or RUF entries in `per-file-ignores`.
3. In the shared test, assert that the parsed `ignore` value is exactly the three-item deferral set and that `extend-ignore` is absent. Parse `tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores` and assert that no configured code equals `RUF` or starts with `RUF`. This deterministically prohibits broad or code-specific RUF per-file exemptions.
4. Use the pinned Ruff fixer only for safe mechanical edits, review every diff, then manually resolve remaining enabled RUF diagnostics across `src/rebar` and `tests`. The live narrow census against current `origin/main` is the starting inventory; the implementation records the post-fix per-code census on the ticket.
5. After RUF is in the global selection, run `ruff check src tests` and remove only RUF100 suppressions that are stale under that full configured rule set. Do not use the narrow-selection RUF100 count to drive removals.

Ruff security-family expansion and Semgrep expansion remain deferred and are already guarded by the predecessor's shared ratchet test; this story does not duplicate those orthogonal acceptance criteria.

Rejected: RUF per-file ignores, `extend-ignore`, Ruff S-family expansion, Semgrep expansion, and treating narrow-selection RUF100 output as actionable debt.

## Scope
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` (extend the file landed by 28cd)
- source and test files among the diagnostics reported live by the baseline command against current `origin/main`, limited to safe mechanical or behavior-preserving changes

## Testing / Verification
- Baseline reproduction: `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 --statistics src/rebar tests`
- Configuration and deferrals: `pytest -q tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`
- Enabled RUF diagnostics: `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 src/rebar tests`
- Full configured rule set including authoritative RUF100 evaluation: `ruff check src tests`
- Canonical lint: `make lint`
- Default tier: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The implementation begins from the live narrow-census inventory measured against current `origin/main` (the baseline command in Context) and changes only files reported by that live census.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `[tool.ruff.lint].select` contains the exact selector `RUF`.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore` is exactly `RUF001`, `RUF002`, and `RUF003`.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `[tool.ruff.lint]` has no `extend-ignore` key.
- [x] `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 src/rebar tests` exits 0.
- [x] `ruff check src tests` exits 0, proving RUF100 reports no stale `noqa` under the final full configured rule set.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` iterates every `tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores` code and fails if the code equals `RUF` or starts with `RUF`.
- [x] [operator-attested] The implementation records the post-remediation per-code RUF census on this ticket, including the authoritative RUF100 result from `ruff check src tests`.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` exits 0.

<!-- green-on-origin-main AC -->
- [x] After `git fetch origin`, `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 src/rebar tests` and `make lint` exit 0 against the **current** `origin/main`; any pre-existing RUF diagnostic on current `origin/main` (including drift-introduced since the measured commit) is resolved before the RUF ratchet is landed.

## Why
Workflow LLM output feeds DETERMINISTIC steps, so schema-conformance reliability is load-bearing. Agents frequently return non-conforming output; the current second-LLM-interpreter workaround is a recognized anti-pattern. Replace it with a deterministic-where-possible layered stack (research: docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/structured-output-research.md).

## What
Layered reliability stack: (1) provider-native CONSTRAINED decoding / strict json_schema where supported (OpenAI strict, Gemini responseSchema, Anthropic native structured outputs now GA) via Pydantic AI NativeOutput; PromptedOutput cross-provider; NOT forced-tool ToolOutput. (2) Deterministic tolerant parse of near-miss output via json-repair (no LLM). (3) Pydantic validation + normalizing validators, with numeric/length bounds in VALIDATORS not the JSON Schema (to stay inside Anthropic's strict-grammar subset). (4) Bounded SAME-model retry feeding the validation error back (retries={'output': 2}; default budget is 1). Handle Anthropic stop_reason in {refusal, max_tokens}; for steps needing extended thinking, SPLIT reasoning and structured extraction into two steps. Keep schemas LEAN (native constraint degrades on deeply-nested/hard schemas).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py, contracts.py, findings.py
- pyproject.toml (add json-repair)
Out: the runtime adapter itself (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Output via NativeOutput where supported, PromptedOutput cross-provider; forced-tool ToolOutput NOT used with extended thinking.
- [ ] json-repair tolerant parse + Pydantic validators (bounds in validators, not the schema); bounded retry feeds the validation error back.
- [ ] Anthropic stop_reason {refusal, max_tokens} handled; thinking steps split reasoning vs extraction; schemas kept lean.
- [ ] The second-interpreter LLM is removed; a structured-output validity eval (recall/false-accept) gates the change.
baseline.summary: Structured-output reliability stack (retire the second-interpreter LLM)

# The cutover withdrew a BLOCKING criterion's grounding tool, by prefix match, with no signal

## Context / Problem

Plan-review criterion **T1** (`facet: overlay-priorart`, `exec: AGENT`, `default_posture: **blocking**`) declares `"web": true` in the packaged routing registry (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`). Its reviewer prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T1.md`) instructs the model: *"when the web-search tool is offered, USE it to ground prior-art claims in real, current sources."* T1 is the bright-line overlay — it fires on external integration, unfamiliar dependency, security/auth, a novel architectural pattern, a perf/scalability target, or a migration.

The tool is attached only by this gate (`src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`, `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`):

    if not web or not resolved.startswith("anthropic"):
        return None

**Since the production review bot was cut over to Bedrock [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], `resolved` is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, which does not start with `anthropic`. So T1 now runs WITHOUT its grounding tool on every production plan review.** The live chain, each link verified: `criteria_routing.json` `"web": true` -> `criteria/model.py` `"web": bool(routing_entry.get("web", False))` -> `plan_review/passes.py` `web=agentic and any(bool(c.get("web")) for c in chunk)` -> `runner.py` `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities(resolved, web=req.web)` -> the prefix gate above.

## Why this matters

1. **It is a BLOCKING criterion.** T1 can block a plan. It now does so on weaker evidence — codebase
   and model knowledge instead of current sources — for exactly the plans that cross a bright-line.
2. **It is decided by PREFIX SHAPE, not capability.** The epic's standing rule is provider
   qualification by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, never prefix matching, with zero exceptions — enforced for the
   capabilities module by an attested guard. This site is the same anti-pattern in a different module,
   and the cutover is what made it bite: the identical MODEL (Claude) reached through a different
   PROVIDER loses a capability because of how its name is spelled.
3. **It is SILENT.** No warning is logged and the signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities`
   records `native_structured_output`, `prompt_cache_style`, `supports_temperature` and
   `supports_thinking` — but nothing about web search. So a reader of the verdict cannot tell that a
   declared grounding tool was withheld. This is the failure shape the epic kept hitting: the guard
   shares the bug's assumption.
4. **It contradicts the epic's own premise.** Epic 061c asserts `first_class = full fidelity`, and
   both Anthropic and Bedrock are first-class. This is a measurable fidelity difference between them
   that no acceptance criterion covers.

**Not a hallucination risk** — and this is the one piece of good news. T1's prompt handles absence explicitly: *"when it is not available, fall back to codebase and plan-text reasoning ... and do NOT fabricate web citations."* So the degradation is quiet quality loss, not invented sources.

## OPERATOR DECISION: web access is REQUIRED for T1 regardless of provider or model

This supersedes the branch this ticket was originally filed with. I had written that if Bedrock does not support Anthropic's server-side `web_search`, then returning `None` is CORRECT and the defect is merely that it is silent. **That is wrong.** The operator's requirement is that **T1 needs web access on EVERY provider and model.** A provider that cannot offer it is a capability gap rebar must CLOSE, not a difference rebar may document.

Two consequences follow, and the second is the harder one:

1. **The prefix gate goes regardless.** `resolved.startswith("anthropic")` cannot decide this, both
   because it is prefix matching (the epic's zero-exceptions rule) and because the answer it computes
   is no longer the question being asked.

2. **Provider-side-only is no longer a sufficient design.** The current implementation is deliberately
   provider-side: `plan_review_T1.md` and `anthropic_model.py` both state the tool is Anthropic's
   SERVER-SIDE `web_search`, "executed provider-side, no homegrown HTTP fetch tool" — an explicit
   decision to avoid rebar owning a fetch tool. If web access must hold for every provider, that
   decision must be REVISITED rather than worked around: where a provider offers a server-side tool,
   prefer it; where it does not, rebar must supply the access some other way. Whatever is chosen, it
   must satisfy the constraint the original design was protecting — the reviewer must not be handed an
   unbounded homegrown HTTP fetch capability without thinking about egress, caching and prompt-injection
   from fetched content. That tradeoff is the real work in this ticket and should not be skipped past.

STILL MEASURE BEDROCK FIRST — the measurement now selects the MECHANISM rather than deciding whether there is a bug: if Bedrock's Converse API can carry the server-side tool, that is the cheapest correct path for the current production provider and no rebar-side fetch tool is needed yet. If it cannot, the rebar-side path is required. Either way T1 ends up with web access.

ALSO REVISIT T1's PROMPT. It currently tells the reviewer the tool "MAY be offered on this run (it is provider-dependent...)" and to fall back to codebase reasoning when absent. Under this decision that conditional framing is wrong: web access is a guarantee for T1, so the prompt should assert it rather than hedge. The graceful-degradation clause protected against fabricated citations and should not be deleted carelessly — but it must stop describing absence as an expected state.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`, the prefix gate.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — most likely home for a profile-derived `supports_server_web_search`
  capability, alongside the existing `prompt_cache_style` / `native_structured_output` decisions.
- the `provider_provenance.capabilities` payload, so the outcome is observable in a signed verdict.

## Testing

- a test that with a `bedrock:`-qualified Claude model and `web=True`, the outcome matches the MEASURED
  Bedrock capability — and that the decision does not consult the provider-name string. Verify RED by
  reinstating a prefix match.
- a test that the signed verdict's provenance records whether server-side web search was attached, so
  the silent case cannot return. Verify RED by removing the field.
- record the Bedrock measurement itself (a real call with the capability requested) as the evidence for
  whichever branch the fix takes; "not supported" is an acceptable answer, an unmeasured assumption is
  not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] whether Bedrock's Converse API can carry Anthropic's server-side `web_search` is MEASURED and
      recorded, with the call and its outcome. This selects the mechanism; it does not decide whether
      there is a bug.
- [x] T1 has WEB ACCESS ON EVERY PROVIDER rebar can route it to, including Bedrock — verified by a run
      on each configured provider, not by inspection of the gate condition.
- [x] the web-access decision no longer consults a provider-name prefix; it derives from the model
      profile / capability registry, consistent with the epic's zero-exceptions rule. The attested
      guard `test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` is NOT weakened.
- [x] if a rebar-side mechanism is required for any provider, the egress / caching /
      prompt-injection-from-fetched-content tradeoff that the original provider-side-only design was
      protecting is addressed explicitly, not bypassed.
- [x] a signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities` records that web access WAS attached, so a
      future silent withdrawal is impossible to miss.
- [x] `plan_review_T1.md` no longer describes web access as provider-dependent or optional, while still
      forbidding fabricated citations.
- [x] tests pin the above and are each verified RED by mutation, including one that fails if the
      capability is withheld on a `bedrock:`-qualified model.
baseline.summary: Bedrock cutover silently removed server-side web search from blocking criterion T1, gated by provider-name prefix

# Shard the completion verifier's monolithic call into parallel per-criterion runs for large-AC closures

## Context

The completion-verifier gate's fast path is ONE monolithic agentic call (`CompletionAgentStep.run` → `RunnerAgentStep`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:536`). Telemetry from the latency investigation (bug `1e88`) shows this single call is the gate's wall-clock critical path: on a large epic it ran **48 turns / ~30k output tokens / ~468s**, decode-bound at ~60 tok/s. Output volume IS the wall-clock (corr(dur, output_tokens)=0.982).

When that one call exhausts its budget on a many-AC closure, a typed truncation (`LLMBudgetExhaustedError` / token-exhaustion `UnretryableOutputError` / `RunawayToolLoopError`) drops into `_recover()`, which **already** splits the work per criterion — a fresh agentic evidence run per checklist item — but runs them **SEQUENTIALLY** (`for index, criterion in enumerate(expected)`, `completion_recovery.py:583`), then a tool-free finalizer aggregates. Banking of incrementally-verified criteria across rounds already exists (story `2948`, closed).

So on exactly the closures that are slowest, we ALREADY fan out into N independent single-criterion agents — just one after another, on the slow path, AFTER paying for a doomed monolithic first pass. The provider, however, serves parallel calls essentially for free: the bug `1e88` micro-benchmark measured flat per-call latency (≤1.03x inflation) and linear aggregate throughput from concurrency 1→12 on Anthropic. **If we are already going to end up with multiple agents, run them in parallel.**

## Goal / approach (fidelity-preserving)

Two fidelity-neutral moves, in de-risk order:

1. **Parallelize the existing sequential recovery loop.** Each criterion's evidence run is an INDEPENDENT
   fresh-history agentic call with no cross-criterion state (bounds `_EVIDENCE_ITERATIONS=40`,
   `_EVIDENCE_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096`, `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16` are per-criterion and unchanged), so running
   them in a bounded thread pool is behaviour-identical — same prompts, same per-criterion outputs, same
   finalizer input, same verdict. Wall-clock for the recovery phase drops from Σ(criteria) toward
   max(criterion). This is the immediate win and mirrors the fidelity-neutral parallelization epic `c81c`
   does for plan-review's container fan-out.

2. **Shard PROACTIVELY up-front for closures predicted to exhaust**, skipping the wasted monolithic first
   pass. Instead of always trying one giant call and only sharding after it truncates, detect a large-AC /
   large-context closure and go straight to the parallel per-criterion (or per-criterion-bin) path. The
   shards become the unit of banking (`2948`), so a partial round still records verified criteria and only
   the unresolved shards re-run.

### When to shard — use historical exhaustion data (the crux)

Rather than guess a threshold, MINE THE HISTORY of when the verifier actually banks partial results and runs a second round. Every exhaustion emits a typed `gate_error_v1` / `CompletionRecoveryError` diagnostic (carrying `criteria_total`, `criteria_exhausted`, `requests`, `tool_calls`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`), and `.rebar/usage.jsonl` records `op=completion-verifier` rows with turns/output/finish per call. Join those to ticket AC-count and context size to answer: **at what AC count / evidence-char / context-size does the monolithic call start truncating?** That empirical knee — not a hand-picked constant — sets the proactive-shard trigger. Ship the trigger as config so it can be re-tuned as the corpus grows (current static bounds live at `completion_recovery.py:41` — `_MAX_CRITERIA=32`, `_MAX_CRITERION_CHARS`, `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS`).

### Concurrency must respect provider quota

Bug `1e88` also showed the ceiling is the provider ACCOUNT's throughput, not the code: a naive cap bump to 16 on Bedrock (while a second session shared the account) throttle-stalled 333s and failed. So the shard-pool concurrency must be a CONFIGURABLE cap (conservative default), with throttle-aware backoff/retry — which ties to bug `61d8` (Bedrock currently ignores `llm_retry_max_attempts`/`timeout_s`). Fix or account for that so a parallel burst degrades gracefully instead of failing the gate.

## Out of scope

- Changing any per-criterion prompt, tool set, iteration/output/tool-step budget, or the finalizer — those
  fix fidelity and must stay byte-identical.
- Reducing the verifier's output/turn budget to go faster (that is a fidelity tradeoff, tracked separately).
- The plan-review container fan-out (`c81c` owns that; this is the completion-verifier analog).
- Fixing the concurrency cache-write race (`c1fd`) — a prerequisite for raising ANY fan-out concurrency,
  linked as a blocker.

## Impacted files (indicative)

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — parallelize the `_recover()` per-criterion loop (bounded
  pool); add the proactive-shard entry that bypasses the monolithic primary for predicted-exhaust closures;
  make concurrency + shard-trigger configurable.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — config keys for shard concurrency cap and the exhaustion-prediction threshold.
- A small analysis script / test fixture that derives the threshold from `.rebar/usage.jsonl` + recovery
  diagnostics (historical mining).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The recovery per-criterion evidence loop runs in a BOUNDED thread pool instead of sequentially; the
      concurrency cap is configurable with a conservative default.
- [ ] Verdict and per-criterion findings are byte-identical to the sequential path on a fixture with >=8 ACs
      (fidelity: same prompts/outputs/finalizer input) — asserted by an offline/FakeRunner parity test.
- [ ] A closure predicted (from historical exhaustion data) to exceed the monolithic call's capacity shards
      up-front and never issues the doomed single call; a small closure keeps the one-call fast path.
- [ ] The shard trigger threshold is DERIVED from `.rebar/usage.jsonl` + recovery diagnostics (documented
      method + reproducible script), not a hand-picked constant, and is config-overridable.
- [ ] Parallel shards degrade gracefully under provider throttling (bounded cap + backoff/retry); a throttle
      does not fail the gate where the sequential path would have succeeded. Accounts for bug `61d8`.
- [ ] Shards are the unit of banking (`2948`): a partial round records verified criteria and only unresolved
      shards re-run.
- [ ] `make lint` + the completion-verifier test suite pass.

## Notes / provenance

Discovered from the latency investigation (bug `1e88`, lever L4 "parallelize the verifier"). The completion verifier is currently owned by a parallel session — coordinate before implementing. Depends on the concurrency cache-race fix `c1fd`.
baseline.summary: Shard completion verifier into parallel per-criterion runs for large-AC closures
