## Context / Problem
The closed development-process audit on bleakish-stational-cob proposed six improvements: escaped-defect metadata, deterministic plan preflight, completion-failure classification, risk-tiered review, proactive code-debt management, and broader maintainership/reviewer evidence. Before turning those proposals into new work, evaluate them against prior audits, janitor remediations, architecture decisions, and related implementation tickets. Prior decisions may be reconsidered only when their original rationale and the new evidence are both explicit.

## Approach
Search the canonical ticket/event history for each proposal and its underlying mechanisms. Inspect full ticket state, comments, dependencies, discovered work, and outcomes for relevant audits, janitor runs, design sessions, and implementation tickets. For each recommendation, record: prior effort or decision; why it was chosen; result or unresolved limitation; evidence from the 2026-08-15 frozen process audit that is genuinely new; and a disposition of reaffirm, refine, reconsider, or defer. Add durable comments and semantic links so future proposal work can recover this context without repeating the audit.

## Scope
- Tracker-only research and documentation; no repository files change.
- Source proposal: bleakish-stational-cob.
- Evidence: canonical rebar tickets, comments, relations, and relevant decision records referenced by those tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Each of the six recommendations is mapped to relevant prior audits, janitor work, decisions, and implementation tickets, including original rationale and observed outcome.
- [x] Each recommendation is assigned a supported disposition: reaffirm, refine, reconsider, or defer; any changed direction identifies the new evidence that warrants reconsideration.
- [x] The source audit and this evaluation carry durable comments with exact ticket aliases and material caveats.
- [x] This evaluation is linked to the source audit and materially relevant prior tickets using correct rebar relations; speculative keyword matches are excluded.
baseline.summary: Evaluate process recommendations against prior audits and decisions

baseline.description:
Mirror how validity is produced, but enforce independence STRUCTURALLY: score novelty in a
SEPARATE Pass-2 structured sub-call that ALONE receives the prior findings and answers a
small novelty sub-answer set ("does this finding correspond to a prior finding?"). The
existing verification sub-call (severity attributes + binary/validity) receives NO prior
findings, so the `verify.py:64` independence invariant (VERIFIER_RULES[0]) holds by
construction. Pass-1 stays unanchored.

This is NEW behavior (pure creation): `discriminates_novelty`, `NOVELTY_EXPECTS`, the
`novelty` contract, the novelty prompt, and the dedicated novelty eval spec do not exist
yet — none are edits to existing symbols.

## Why an LLM sub-call and not the deterministic `sidecar.norm_id` fingerprint

`sidecar.norm_id` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:119`) is an EXACT-match key (a
significant-token set + criteria): it collapses reordering/punctuation but a carryover
finding RE-PHRASED across a plan edit (different significant tokens) mints a different
`norm_id` and would slip through as "novel". The whole point of novelty is to catch the
SUBSTANTIVELY-same finding reworded between reviews, so an LLM matches-prior sub-call is the
right tool. `norm_id` remains the offline join key; novelty is the runtime carryover signal.
Independence is still enforced STRUCTURALLY (the separate sub-call), not by prompt assertion.

## Novelty sub-answer set + scoring arithmetic (canonical)

Novelty is the INVERSE of "matches a prior finding". The sub-call answers a small set of
factual **matches-prior** questions (yes / insufficient / no), each scored on the same
ordinal map Pass-3 uses for validity (`yes=1.0, insufficient=0.5, no=0.0`):

- Q1 `restates_prior_defect` — Does this finding restate the same underlying defect as a
  specific prior-review finding?
- Q2 `cites_prior_location` — Does it cite the same plan location/section as that prior finding?
- Q3 `matches_prior_fix` — Is its suggested remediation substantively the same as that prior
  finding's?

A named constant `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS = ("restates_prior_defect", "cites_prior_location",
"matches_prior_fix")` in `decide.py` (the analogue of `GRADED_BINARY`) anchors the
`novelty_model` fields to the scoring arithmetic so they can never name different questions.

`carryover_match = mean(answerable matches-prior sub-answers)` (a sub-answer is "answerable"
when it is one of yes/insufficient/no; a missing/blank one is skipped); **`novelty = 1 −
carryover_match`** ∈ [0,1]. High novelty (≈1.0) = no prior match (genuinely new); low novelty
(≈0.0) = carryover. If NO sub-answer is answerable, novelty defaults to **0.0** (carryover →
never dropped — the safe direction). The questions are FACTUAL (match-prior), never normative
("should I downrank"). Pass-3 maps novelty deterministically in task cc5b.

## The `novelty` contract (registered alongside `verification`)

A distinct registered structured-output contract — `novelty_model` in `verify.py`, registered
under the kernel name `novelty`, with `plan_review_novelty` registered as the plan-review
alias in `passes.py` (mirroring how `verification`/`plan_review_verification` pair). Per-item
fields: `index: int`, the three matches-prior sub-answers (default `"insufficient"`, mirroring
the verification Binary defaults), and `matched_prior_id: str` (default `""` — the prior
finding id this matched, or empty when there is no match). The existing `verification`
contract is NOT reused (it has no prior-findings input). There is no schema "prompt id" field —
the prompt is identified by its prompt-library id (`plan-review-novelty`), not a payload field.

## The sub-call mechanism + data-flow contract

`verify.py` gains `score_novelty(findings, *, prior_findings, run_chunk, …) -> {index:
novelty_float}` mirroring `verify_findings`: it injects the prior findings as context to the
SEPARATE novelty sub-call (the only call that sees them), reshapes by global index, and maps
each finding's sub-answers to a novelty via `decide.novelty(...)`. The returned
`{index: novelty}` map is what cc5b's Pass-3 consumes; an index absent from the map (the
finding had no novelty produced) is treated by cc5b as carryover (novelty 0.0). The
severity/validity sub-call and Pass-1 are NOT given the prior findings.

## Fallback (fail-safe — never silently suppress)

If the novelty sub-call errors, times out, or returns malformed/unparseable output, novelty
defaults to **0.0** for the affected findings (treated as carryover → enforced at the normal
threshold, NEVER dropped). A broken novelty signal can only make the gate STRICTER, never
suppress a finding. The fallback emits a WARN log (so an elevated fallback rate is observable)
and is covered by a FakeRunner test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_novelty.py` (a sub-call
that raises / returns junk → every novelty is 0.0).

## `discriminates_novelty` eval gate — in a DEDICATED spec (the bar; resolves the BLOCK)

The novelty sub-call uses its OWN prompt + contract, NOT the `plan-review-verifier` prompt — so
its eval cases and scorer go in a **dedicated** `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml`
keyed to `prompt: plan-review-novelty` (appending them to the verifier spec would score the
verifier prompt's output, which never carries novelty — the wrong artifact). Add a
`discriminates_novelty` deterministic scorer mirroring `discriminates_true_from_false` /
`discriminates_impact_levels` (`eval_scorers.py`): a PER-CASE boolean at the **0.5 midpoint** —
a `kind: novel` (`expect: high_novelty`) case must score novelty **≥ 0.5**; a `kind: carryover`
(`expect: low_novelty`) case **< 0.5**. The scorer reads the novelty score via a dedicated
`_novelty(out)` extractor (numeric `novelty`, else computed from the matches-prior sub-answers
via the shared `decide.novelty` arithmetic, so the scorer and the gate can never diverge).
Register `discriminates_novelty` in the `eval_scorers.REGISTRY` and add ≥ 3 labeled
(prior-finding, new-finding) carryover/novel pairs (both directions) to the dedicated spec.

`eval_scorers.ALLOWED_EXPECTS` is extended with `NOVELTY_EXPECTS = {high_novelty, low_novelty}`
AND `validate_dataset_and_gold` in `eval.py` gains a novelty-axis balance check analogous to
the validity/impact ones (if any `NOVELTY_EXPECTS` value is used, BOTH `high_novelty` and
`low_novelty` must be present), so `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` both accepts the cases and
still enforces a balanced discrimination set.

**The bar (numeric target):** the scorer is GATED by the spec-level convention already used by
the sibling discriminators — `gate: at_least(2)` over `epochs: 3` with `coverage_threshold: 0.8`
(i.e. every labeled novelty pair discriminated correctly at the 0.5 midpoint in ≥ 2 of 3
epochs). There is no separate AUC/F1 number: house style for deterministic discriminators is
the per-case 0.5 midpoint + the spec gate (the llm-judge `threshold:` field does NOT apply to
deterministic scorers). This eval bar is DISTINCT from the runtime drop threshold
`T_novel = 0.7` (task cc5b): 0.5 is "did the scorer separate novel from carryover at all"; 0.7
is "how novel must a finding be to be eligible for the Pass-3 drop".

## The evidence gate (enforcement lives in cc5b)

"cc5b must not activate the drop rule until this bar is met" is enforced in cc5b, not here: the
Pass-3 drop rule ships behind a config key that is **default-OFF** for v1 (expand-contract), so
the deterministic floor is inert until the novelty discriminator has cleared the bar and the
key is flipped. 150b's responsibility is to make the scorer + labeled set + the dedicated spec
exist and validate; cc5b consumes them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Novelty scored in a separate Pass-2 sub-call that alone sees prior findings (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py` `score_novelty`, re-exported in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py`)
- [ ] The severity/validity sub-call receives NO prior findings; Pass-1 receives none
- [ ] Novelty sub-answers are factual (match-prior), not "should I downrank"; a `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` constant in `decide.py` anchors the fields; `novelty = 1 − mean(answerable matches-prior sub-answers)` on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0` map; no answerable sub-answers → novelty 0.0
- [ ] Fail-safe fallback: novelty sub-call error/timeout/malformed → novelty = 0.0 (carryover; never dropped) + a WARN log; covered by a FakeRunner test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_novelty.py`
- [ ] A distinct registered `novelty` contract (`novelty_model` in `verify.py`; `plan_review_novelty` alias in `passes.py`): `index`, the three matches-prior sub-answers (default `insufficient`), `matched_prior_id` (default `""`). The `verification` contract is NOT reused
- [ ] `discriminates_novelty` scorer (per-case, 0.5 midpoint) + a dedicated `_novelty(out)` extractor + ≥ 3 carryover/novel labeled pairs in a DEDICATED `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml` (`prompt: plan-review-novelty`) + registered in `eval_scorers.REGISTRY` (NOT appended to `plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml`)
- [ ] `ALLOWED_EXPECTS` extended with `NOVELTY_EXPECTS = {high_novelty, low_novelty}` AND `validate_dataset_and_gold` in `eval.py` extended with a novelty-axis balance check (both poles required), so `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` accepts AND balances the new cases
- [ ] The bar is `gate: at_least(2)`/`epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8` on the novelty pairs (the framework idiom; NOT an AUC literal), distinct from the runtime `T_novel=0.7`
- [ ] The novelty scorer + dedicated spec exist and validate (`rebar prompt eval plan-review-novelty`); the drop rule remains inert (default-OFF, enforced in cc5b) until the bar is cleared — the evidence gate

## Data flow to downstream (cc5b)
`score_novelty` returns `{finding_index: novelty}` (∈ [0,1]); cc5b's Pass-3 reads it, treats an
absent index as carryover (0.0), and applies the deterministic floor. Novelty never re-enters
the severity/validity sub-call (independence). The structural-independence design decision is
recorded in the ADR + docs delivered by task 4cb9.
baseline.summary: Pass-2: emit a structured novelty sub-answer set (prior-findings grounded)

baseline.description:
# S4: Config-driven link-relation mapping, skip-not-approximate preserved

## Context / Problem

Epic 3d7a adds a config-driven mapping seam. S1 landed core `mapping_config.py` (`MappingLayer` with `link_map: Mapping[str,str]`, `SKIP="skip"`, `resolve_for_project`, `validate`, `Capability`). S2 made STATUS config-driven (`config.py:77`). S4 does the same for rebar-relation → Jira-link mapping, preserving "skip, don't approximate": map to a real declared project link type, or skip — never invent an approximate link. S4 is link-relation ONLY (priority is S5; type/parents out of scope).

Link emission has TWO halves in `outbound_links.py`, only on the UPDATE path (`outbound_mutation_builders.py:285`; creates emit no links):

- ADD — `_diff_links` (`outbound_links.py:34`): per local dep, calls
  `links.link_payload_for_relation(relation)` (`:83`) and skips on `None` (`:84`).
- REMOVE — `_diff_link_removals` (`outbound_links.py:120`): walks the REMOTE
  canonical set `links.map_remote_links(jira_fields)` — `(relation, other_key,
  opaque_vendor_type)` — emitting `{"action":"remove","type":opaque_vendor_type,...}`
  (`:150`) for a managed, locally-absent link, stopping the inbound differ re-adding a
  deliberate local unlink each pass (the churn).

CRITICAL for REMOVE: each remote link's `relation` is recovered from its ACTUAL remote vendor type by the BUILT-IN, config-unaware reverse map `link_direction.JIRA_LINK_TO_RELATION` via `resolve_inbound_link` (`link_direction.py:19,27`) — `{"Blocks":"blocks","Relates":"relates_to"}`. A type NOT in that map reverses to `relation=None`, so a REMAPPED (overridden) remote type is silently dropped unless attribution is config-aware — this story's core REMOVE fix.

Both `link_payload_for_relation` impls read built-in `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` directly in TWO backends: `adapters/jira/backend.py:323`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:527`. `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK: dict[str, tuple[str, bool]]` (`value_maps.py:104`): `blocks→(Blocks,False)`, `depends_on→(Blocks,True)`, `relates_to→(Relates,False)`; unsynced in `UNSYNCED_RELATIONS` (`value_maps.py:128`). TYPE MISMATCH: built-in payload is a `(link_type, swap)` TUPLE; the S1 `link_map` axis is flat `str→str`.

## Approach

Mirror S2's forward seam; apply ONE effective link map to ADD and REMOVE, with config-aware REMOVE attribution.

1. **`config.effective_link_map(project_key, root)`** (`config.py`, NEW), like
   `effective_status_map` (`config.py:77`). Add an adapter-free literal
   `local_to_jira_link` = `{"blocks":"Blocks","depends_on":"Blocks",
   "relates_to":"Relates"}` (link-TYPE only; parity-tested like `local_to_jira_status`).
   Build `builtin = mc.MappingLayer(link_map=local_to_jira_link)`,
   `mc.resolve_for_project`, `mc.validate(resolved, mc.Capability(has_link_types=True))`
   (fail-closed), return `resolved.link_map` **retaining `SKIP`** so a
   forced skip ≠ an absent key.

2. **One resolver, both directions.** Add `_effective_link_map_for(ticket, mapping,
   repo_root)` in `outbound_differ.py` (NEW, sibling of `_effective_status_map_for`,
   `:272`). Compute once at `outbound_mutation_builders.py:285`; pass the SAME
   `link_map: Mapping[str,str] | None = None` to BOTH diff funcs. Shared helper
   `_resolve_link(relation, links, link_map) -> tuple[str,bool] | None` unifies both.

3. **`_resolve_link`:** `override = link_map.get(relation)`; `override == SKIP` →
   `None`; `payload = links.link_payload_for_relation(relation)`; `override` a `str` →
   `(override, payload[1] if payload else False)` (overrides only link_type; built-in
   swap preserved, `False` default); else → `payload` (maybe `None` → skip).

   **ADD** (`_diff_links`): `_resolve_link`; `None` ⇒ `continue`; else emit
   `type=vendor_type, swap=swap`. No `[mapping]` ⇒ both paths byte-for-byte today.

   **REMOVE** (`_diff_link_removals`): config-aware attribution FIRST. Build
   `reverse = {v: k for k, v in link_map.items() if v != SKIP}`. For each canonical
   `(relation, other_key, opaque_vendor_type)`:
   - `relation is None` (built-in `JIRA_LINK_TO_RELATION` didn't know this remote
     type) ⇒ recover `relation = reverse.get(opaque_vendor_type)`; still `None` ⇒
     genuinely unmapped ⇒ `continue` (adopt). This stops a remapped link being dropped.
   - `_resolve_link(relation, ...)` is `None` (SKIP) ⇒ `continue` — suppress REMOVE (a
     skipped relation is neither added nor removed; no inbound re-add).
   - else keep/remove as today against `(relation, local_target)` in `local_deps` /
     `managed_refs`, emitting `type=opaque_vendor_type` — the ACTUAL remote type,
     which IS the overridden type when remapped (no re-substitution), so add
     and remove reference ONE type.

4. **Fail-closed on undeclared link type.** The S1 mechanism exists
   (`MappingLayer.link_types` `mapping_config.py:102`, `Capability.has_link_types`
   `:80`, `validate()`'s `_check_vocab(link_map, link_types)` `:359`) but `validate()`
   is not yet invoked. A project declares `[mapping.default] link_types = [...]`;
   `effective_link_map` calling `validate()` (NEW) raises `MappingConfigError` on a
   `link_map` value outside it. `SKIP` always allowed.

## Scope

- `config.py`: `local_to_jira_link` literal + `effective_link_map` (~130 LOC).
- `outbound_differ.py`: `_effective_link_map_for`.
- `outbound_links.py`: `link_map` arg + shared `_resolve_link` + config-aware
  `reverse` attribution on both diff funcs (~220 LOC).
- `outbound_mutation_builders.py`: compute + pass `link_map` at `:285`.
- Backends + `link_direction.py` UNCHANGED (config-awareness layers in the removal
  path; the built-in reverse map stays the direction-aware first attempt).
- NEW `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_link_mapping.py`.
- OUT of scope: parents (S7), priority (S5), type axis, inbound remap-awareness.
- All modules stay well under the 800-LOC hard cap.

## Testing

New `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_link_mapping.py` (`pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`), driving REAL entry points (`config.effective_link_map`, `_diff_links`, `_diff_link_removals`) via a tmp `rebar.toml` `[mapping]` block:

- `test_link_config_effect` — a `link_map` override (`relates_to = "Relationship"`)
  changes the ADD mutation's `type` while preserving built-in `swap`; AND on REMOVE, a
  managed, locally-absent remote link carrying "Relationship" is config-awarely
  attributed to `relates_to` (not dropped) and emits a remove with `type=
  "Relationship"`. No `[mapping]` ⇒ both paths unchanged.
- `test_link_skip_preserved` — a `"skip"` override (and an unsynced relation) emits NO
  ADD; the same skip suppresses the REMOVE — never added nor removed; no approximate
  link substituted.
- `test_link_undeclared_fails_closed` — a `link_map` value outside a declared
  `link_types` vocabulary makes `effective_link_map` raise `MappingConfigError`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The SAME effective `link_map` governs ADD and REMOVE via one `_resolve_link`;
      ADD composes override link_type + built-in swap; verified by
      `test_link_config_effect`.
- [x] Skip is symmetric: a `"skip"` override (and unsynced relations) suppress BOTH
      ADD and REMOVE — never added nor removed; verified by `test_link_skip_preserved`.
- [x] REMOVE attribution is config-aware: a remote link carrying an OVERRIDDEN vendor
      type is attributed via the inverted map, NOT spuriously dropped/adopted, and its
      remove targets that same overridden type; verified by `test_link_config_effect`.
- [x] Undeclared link type fails closed via `validate()`; verified by
      `test_link_undeclared_fails_closed`.
- [x] Both consumers (`jira/backend.py:323`, `jira_datacenter/backend.py:527`) route
      through the single `effective_link_map` seam; no `[mapping]` block leaves
      emission unchanged; a parity test keeps `config.local_to_jira_link` in lock-step
      with `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`'s link-type components.

Test tier: unit

baseline.description:
## Why
Job 1: refute an asserted absence. When a reviewer (plan or code) claims an import/symbol is hallucinated, this lane tries to DISPROVE it by resolving the reference against the repo — the highest-value false-positive reducer for hallucinated-symbol findings. It is confirm-only: `refuted` (found it) or `abstain`, never asserts absence.

## What
- A **deterministic T1 resolver** over a full repo checkout = a **universal-ctags** repo-wide tags index (164
  langs, no server, no build) + plain file-path existence. (grep-ast is NOT a repo-wide indexer — per-file
  AST-context grep only; spike `docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/` confirmed this — so it is at most an
  optional context-display helper, NOT the index.)
- **`refuted` is SCOPED to name-existence WITH AN AMBIGUITY+MEMBER GUARD** (spike E2: naive bare name-existence
  false-refutes a collision; the guard restores 0 false-refute). The resolution rule: a **dotted/member** reference
  (`foo.bar`) → `abstain` (member binding is T2); a name with **>1 definition** (collision/common name) →
  `abstain(ambiguous)`; a **unique, bare** symbol name (or an existing file path) → `refuted`. So "scope to
  name-existence" is necessary but NOT sufficient — refute only a *unique, bare, non-member* name; everything else
  abstains. Never asserts `absent`.
- **Language support (R-7):** ctags' 164 + tree-sitter-language-pack's ~306 grammars cover the common case (a
  COBOL repo resolves out of the box). For a truly unsupported language the PROJECT supplies a ctags optlib
  (`--langdef`/`--regex-<LANG>` / `--optlib-dir`, no recompile) or a tree-sitter custom grammar via a `.rebar/`
  config slot the resolver reads; an unconfigured language → `abstain(unsupported_lang)`.
- The **explicit reference-in schema** the review agent must emit: `{kind, name, in_file?, container?}` where the
  **closed set `kind ∈ {symbol, import, dependency, file, member}`** — `symbol`/`import`/`file` are refute-eligible
  by name/path existence, `dependency` routes to the T0 deps lane (S3), and `member` (a dotted `recv.attr`) is
  T1-abstain (T2 territory). The closed `kind` set is the integration contract; S5 EXPOSES it (does not redefine).
  Optional deterministic extraction FROM a diff/file is in scope; prose extraction is NOT.
- Tiered design: universal-ctags is the always-available floor. LSP/SCIP semantic resolution is **T2 — out of
  scope here**, deferred to `850f` (servers/builds, non-deterministic).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/resolve.py` (+ helpers); reuse `universal-ctags` (repo-wide tags) + tree-sitter for
  structural needs; build on S1's contract + harness. grep-ast optional (context display only).
- Avoid stack-graphs (archived). No language servers, no builds (those are T2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `refute_absence(reference)` returns `refuted` ONLY for a unique bare non-member name/path, else `abstain` (dotted→member-T2; >1 def→`ambiguous`); never asserts absence. Guard validated by spike E2 (naive=1 false-refute → guarded=0).
- [ ] Polyglot repo-wide symbol/file index via **universal-ctags**; per-language coverage recorded; unsupported lang → abstain.
- [ ] Project language-extensibility slot honored (ctags optlib / tree-sitter custom grammar from `.rebar/`); unconfigured language fails open.
- [ ] Reference-in schema with the closed `kind` set {symbol,import,dependency,file,member} defined + validated; optional deterministic code/diff reference extractor.
- [ ] Refutation yield + false-refute measured on a REAL multi-repo corpus (NOT a self-planted fixture; spike E3 = 88% yield / 0 false-refute on rebar's own source), collision + member cases asserting `abstain`; fail-open tested (no tool / parse error / timeout / unsupported lang → abstain).
baseline.summary: Engine A — refutation resolver (universal-ctags T1 floor) + reference-in schema

baseline.description:
## Context

Migrate eligible OpenAI providers to the pydantic-ai **Responses API** as a config cutover with a pre-v1 deprecation of the Chat-Completions fallback. The blocking research ticket `ageless-ferny-ugandakob` (b612-1edb-efa9-4c61, CLOSED) produced the capability matrix and the contract tests (`tests/unit/test_openai_responses_contract.py`, already landed and green for both prefixes). Its verdict, which this ticket implements verbatim:

- **Only hosted OpenAI (matrix row 1)** — bare `openai:`/inferred `gpt-*`/`o1`/`o3`/`chatgpt`,
  with NO custom endpoint — is Responses-ready under the pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.2.
- **Every other row is Chat-Completions-only or UNKNOWN** and stays on `openai-chat:`:
  custom `base_url` builder (row 2), per-candidate `endpoint` override (row 3), `gateway/openai`
  (4), `deepseek`/`grok`/`moonshotai`/`heroku`/`cerebras` (5-7), `xai`/`groq` (8, UNKNOWN),
  vendor-side `/v1/responses` (9, UNKNOWN/moot under the pin).
- The migration's edit-set is the **four constraint sites** the matrix named.

Operator decision (2026-08-19, recorded on this ticket): **config cutover APPROVED** with a per-provider fallback to `openai-chat:` that is **explicitly temporary** — it carries a deprecation notice and is **scheduled for removal before v1**.

## Design

**Default flip (the cutover).** Hosted OpenAI now resolves to `openai-responses:` by default. A custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (top-level `base_url`, per-class slot `endpoint`, or per-candidate `endpoint`) keeps resolving to `openai-chat:` — matrix rows 2-3: rebar's `_build_openai` registers only under `openai`/`openai-chat`, an `openai-responses:` string never reaches it, and vendor `/v1/responses` support for custom servers is UNKNOWN, so flipping a custom endpoint would silently ignore its `base_url`.

**The fallback IS the explicit `openai-chat:` qualifier** (or `provider = "openai-chat"`), now a DEPRECATED compatibility surface. It is per-provider/per-slot because each model-class slot, fallback candidate, or `cfg.model` names its own qualifier. Writing it for **hosted** OpenAI emits a once-per-run deprecation notice pointing to `openai-responses:`, registered in the central `rebar._deprecations` registry as `cfg:openai-chat` with `remove_in = "v1.0.0"` (the repo's single-sourced pre-v1 removal horizon `_deprecations._MAJOR`). Chat forced by a **custom endpoint** does NOT warn (it is a construction constraint, not a deprecated opt-in, and no Responses alternative exists for it).

Portability: this is a pure config-resolution/provider change with no CI-provider dependency; the deprecation horizon is a static repo constant, and all new tests run in-process against an `httpx.MockTransport` stub with no network or provider credentials.

## Edit-set (RED->GREEN)

1. `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — add `"openai-responses"` to `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` so
   `split_provider_qualifier`/`infer_provider` treat `openai-responses:` as a qualifier.
2. `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` — add `openai-responses` to the set
   `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` returns (a new `_EXTRA_KNOWN_PROVIDERS` frozenset for names
   `infer_provider` special-cases but `known_model_names()` omits), so
   `ProviderSession.is_resolvable("openai-responses")` is True and the runner leaves it a lazy
   string for pydantic-ai to build `OpenAIResponsesModel`. The rebar builder stays chat-only.
3. `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — add `"openai-responses": _resolve_openai` to
   `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` so capability resolution no longer degrades (native_structured_output
   parity with `openai-chat:`).
4. `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — `_resolve_target` grows an `endpoint: str | None = None`
   param; an `_openai_family_target(tail, requested, endpoint)` helper returns `openai-chat:` for
   an explicit `openai-chat` request or when an endpoint is present, else `openai-responses:`
   (keeps `_resolve_target` under the C901 ceiling). Thread `endpoint` from the callers that hold
   it: `resolve_class`/`resolve_fallback_chain` (slot/target endpoint), `primary_endpoint_for`,
   `fallback_targets_for`, `build_fallback_model` — so the identity-matching those functions do on
   `_resolve_target` output stays consistent with what `resolve_class` produced.
5. `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — `_pai_model`: explicit `openai-chat:` passes through;
   bare `openai:` resolves to `openai-chat:` when `cfg.base_url` is set, else `openai-responses:`.
6. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — after `resolved` and the effective `cfg.base_url` (incl. recovered
   slot endpoint) are known, emit the `cfg:openai-chat` notice once when `resolved` is hosted
   `openai-chat:` (starts with `openai-chat:` AND no `base_url`).
7. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — register the `cfg:openai-chat` scheduled deprecation.
8. Docs: `docs/config-reference.md` + `docs/llm-framework.md` — document the wire-semantic change,
   how to exercise the `openai-chat:` fallback, its deprecation and the `v1.0.0` removal target.

## Testing

- Update the intended behavioural-diff assertions (now `openai-responses:` for hosted openai):
  `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` (incl. the `_KNOWN_24`->`_KNOWN_25` drift set),
  `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_model_classes.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py`.
- New assertions: hosted `openai:`/`gpt-4o` -> `openai-responses:`; `openai:` + endpoint (top-level
  and per-slot) stays `openai-chat:`; explicit `openai-chat:` stays chat; `is_resolvable` and
  capabilities parity for `openai-responses:`; the deprecation notice fires once for hosted
  `openai-chat:` and NOT for endpoint-forced chat.
- Re-run the landed contract tests (already parameterized over both prefixes) as the wire-level
  behavioural diff.
- Gates: focused provider tests plus `make test`, `make lint`, `make typecheck` in this worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every provider the matrix marks Responses-ready (hosted OpenAI, row 1) resolves to
      `openai-responses:` explicitly; every retained `openai-chat:` path (custom endpoints, rows
      2-3; other vendors, rows 4-9) is justified by the cited matrix row.
- [x] The contract tests are re-run against the migrated paths and the behavioural diff is
      recorded (structured output, streaming, tool calls, retries, custom base URLs).
- [x] A per-provider fallback to `openai-chat:` exists, is documented, emits a deprecation notice,
      and has a named pre-v1 removal target (`v1.0.0`) recorded via the deprecation registry.
- [x] Configuration/migration docs explain the observable wire-semantic changes and how to
      exercise the fallback.
- [x] Focused provider tests plus `make test`, `make lint`, `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Migrate eligible OpenAI providers to the pydantic-ai Responses API (config cutover with pre-v1 deprecation)

Library `ready()` invokes `ready --json`, but the engine `ready` has no `--json` (only `--format {ids,llm}` and `--epic`), so `rebar.ready()` raises and the MCP `ready_tickets` tool errors on EVERY call. Reproduced empirically.

- Engine: src/rebar/_engine/ticket-ready.py:168-179 — argparse choices `ids`/`llm`, `--epic`; no `--json`.
- Library: src/rebar/__init__.py:316-318 — builds `["ready","--json"]`.
- Repro: `rebar ready --json` -> argparse exit 2 "unrecognized arguments: --json"; `rebar.ready()` -> RebarError(exit 2); MCP `ready_tickets` -> ToolError every call.

## Fix (engine-side — makes the already-written library call correct, and advances the --json epic)
- Add a `--json` mode to ticket-ready.py emitting a JSON ARRAY (decide + document: array of compiled ticket-state objects [consistent with list/search] vs array of ticket ids [matches the default `ids` semantics]). Reuse the existing reducer the `--format llm` path uses.
- Ensure `rebar ready --json`, library `ready()` (already passes --json), and MCP `ready_tickets` all return the structured list. Keep default (no flag) = id-list, and `--format llm` unchanged.
- Prefer NOT to change src/rebar/__init__.py or mcp_server.py (another fix owns those). If the library can't parse the engine output without an __init__.py change, note it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar ready --json` emits a valid JSON array (shape decided + documented)
- [ ] `rebar.ready()` returns the list (no longer raises); MCP `ready_tickets` returns it
- [ ] default id-list and `--format llm` outputs unchanged
- [ ] Tests cover `ready --json` (bash dispatcher tier) and library/MCP ready

baseline.description:
## Summary

Observed LIVE on the deployed bot (2026-07-13): another agent set Autosubmit+1 on a 2-change stack (#644,#645, 'speed up gerrit-verify'). Both were LLM+1/Verified+1/submittable at selection, but main advanced before the bot's submit, so ancestor-atomic submit hit Gerrit 409 'requires fast-forward'. The bot then **emitted AUTOLANDER_ERROR every poll cycle in an infinite loop** (dozens of identical errors), never converging: it did NOT successfully rebase-on-behalf, and it did NOT clear the stack's Autosubmit (both changes STILL show Autosubmit=+1), so it re-selected the same stale stack forever. This floods the rebar-autolander-errors alarm and starves the serial queue (nothing else lands). Mitigated by engaging the S5d emergency-stop sentinel (bot paused).

## Likely root cause(s)
1. The SUBMIT-first design expects a submit-409 (not-ff) to trigger a rebase-onto-tip (drive_to_submit). For this stale STACK, that rebase path did not run (or failed) and fell through to a loud AUTOLANDER_ERROR + re-select.
2. The hand-back that should remove Autosubmit on a failed drive did not clear the votes — plausibly because the votes were cast by ANOTHER account and RebarBotNava lacks permission to remove another user's label vote (Gerrit label-removal perms), so the 'hand back = remove Autosubmit' step silently fails and the change stays selectable. (Related to but distinct from 0d3e, which is about Autosubmit being dropped across the bot's OWN rebase.)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create a 2+ change stack, get it submittable (LLM+1/Verified+1).
2. Advance main so the stack is no longer a fast-forward.
3. Set Autosubmit+1 on the stack (as a non-bot account).
4. Observe the bot select it, submit → 409, and loop on AUTOLANDER_ERROR without rebasing or clearing Autosubmit.

Expected: on a submit-409 the bot rebases-on-behalf + re-CIs + submits; if it cannot (conflict / can't clear Autosubmit), it hands back ONCE (removes its selectability) and moves on — never an infinite error loop. Actual: infinite AUTOLANDER_ERROR loop; stack stuck; queue starved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A submit-409 (not-ff) on a selected stack deterministically routes to rebase-onto-tip (rebase-on-behalf) + fresh-Verified await + re-submit, OR a single clean hand-back — never a repeating error loop.
- [ ] The hand-back reliably makes the change non-selectable even when the Autosubmit vote was cast by another account (handle the label-removal permission case, or exclude a just-failed change from re-selection via the S3 marker/backoff).
- [ ] A regression test simulates the stale-stack submit-409 and asserts bounded outcomes (rebase-and-reland OR one hand-back), asserting NO unbounded AUTOLANDER_ERROR repetition.
- [ ] [operator-attested] After the fix deploys, a stale Autosubmit'd stack lands (or hands back once) without looping, and the alarm stays OK.
baseline.summary: Auto-lander loops on AUTOLANDER_ERROR for a stale submittable stack (submit-409 not rebased; hand-back doesn't clear others' Autosubmit)

baseline.description:
Make a stale clone's push **refuse** instead of silently re-unioning ~1 GiB of stripped history. This is the keystone that makes the reclaim safe, and it must be deployed everywhere before the window. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why a guard is needed at all, and why in two places
After the strip, `.bridge_state` still only appears from 2026-06-11, so the first **1,029 commits are byte-identical** and `merge-base HEAD origin/tickets` **SUCCEEDS** (measured). So `sync.py` does NOT take its unrelated-histories branch — it reaches the ordinary **diverged** path (`:100-112`) and unions normally. Quiescence does not close this.

And a guard in `sync.py` alone is **bypassed**: `push.py:203` and `:229` run an INDEPENDENT `git merge <remote>/<branch>` on non-fast-forward rejection and then re-push (<=3 attempts), never consulting `sync.py`. That is exactly the path a stale review-bot write takes. **[v2 CORRECTED — the earlier chain was wrong; plan-review caught it]** Verified chain: `voter.py:735 emit_code_review_artifact(...)` -> (within it) `rebar.create_ticket` -> `event_append.py:561 push.push_tickets_branch(...)` -> push rejected non-FF -> `push.py` merge -> retry **succeeds**. There is **no `push_after_commit` intermediary**: `push_after_commit` (`push.py:268`) is called only from `delete.py:337,397`, `compact.py:644,762` and `transition_close.py:757` — never from the create path. And `voter.py:735` is `emit_code_review_artifact(`, not `create_ticket`.

## Placement (precise — the wrong spot wedges every clone)
- Inside **`sync._union_merge`** (`sync.py:114`) — the sole shared callee of both `:97` and `:111`.
  **NOT** before the merge-base test at `:96`: that would also block the ff-adopt at `:101-104`,
  which is exactly how a merely-behind clone converges, wedging it permanently.
- Before **`push.py:203` and `:229`**.
- **NOT** at `lock.acquire()` (where `check_store_compat` already fires, `lock.py:296`): a blanket
  write block would also block the convergence operation, deadlocking the clone it rejects.

## Where the epoch lives
Add an `epoch` field to the **existing** `.store-compat.json` rather than a parallel marker. Verified safe: `compat.py`'s `_analyze` validates only `format_version` and `required_capabilities` via `.get()`, so **unknown keys are ignored** — an older binary neither crashes nor fails closed. Two precisions: `compat.write_compat_record` (`:184`) hardcodes the two keys, so a store it stamps is born epoch-absent (decide that deliberately); and `_record_path` reads only the **local worktree**, so the guard needs its own `git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json` reader for the other side.

## Expand/contract — the FULL state matrix (plan-review E2/T1 remediation)
The earlier wording said only "`absent == absent` => compatible, `absent vs present` => abort", which left two distinct absences conflated. Specify all of it. Two independent axes per side: the **record** (`.store-compat.json`) may be absent or present, and within a present record the **`epoch` field** may be absent or present.

| local | remote | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| record absent | record absent | **compatible** (pre-feature store both sides; union proceeds) |
| record absent | record present, epoch absent | **compatible** |
| record present, epoch absent | record present, epoch absent | **compatible** (today's state) |
| epoch present | epoch present, equal | **compatible** |
| epoch present | epoch present, different | **ABORT** |
| epoch absent | epoch present | **ABORT** (local predates the rewrite) |
| epoch present | epoch absent | **ABORT** (remote predates local; refuse rather than guess) |
| either side | record present but **corrupt/unparseable** | **ABORT** (never silently treat as absent — mirrors `compat.py`'s existing corrupt-record rule) |
| remote ref unreadable (`git show` non-zero) | — | **ABORT**, distinguished in the message from "file absent" |

Note the last two rows: `git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json` exits non-zero **both** when the file does not exist at that ref and when the ref itself cannot be read. These must be distinguished in the log message, because the remedies differ (re-clone vs fix the remote).

**Epoch value format (plan-review E2 remediation — previously unspecified).** `epoch` is a JSON **string**, opaque to comparison: compared for byte equality only, never ordered or parsed. Value = the ISO-8601 UTC instant of the rewrite plus a short random suffix (e.g. `"2026-08-14T09-31-07Z-4f2a"`), unique per rewrite and human-diagnosable in a log line. A non-string `epoch` (number, object, null) is treated as **corrupt** -> ABORT, matching `compat.py`'s existing type-strictness for `format_version`. Deliberately NOT a monotonic counter: ordering invites "newer is probably fine" reasoning, and the only safe response to any mismatch is refuse-and-re-clone.

The epoch **value** appears only in the reclaim's re-add commit. The epoch **value** appears only in the reclaim's re-add commit. That way pre-window clones (both absent) merge normally even holding unpushed work, while post-rewrite stale clones abort.

**The guard only binds binaries at or after this change** — older ones ignore the field. So the reclaim window additionally requires >=24 h plus an observed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run on a descendant SHA, and the review-bot convergence (A6-0b) stays in the protocol.

## Control flow at each guard site (plan-review G6 remediation)
`logger.warning` describes the *message*, not the *control flow* — and at the `push.py` sites both merges sit inside the `for attempt` retry loop, so warning-and-continuing would simply retry the push. Specify both sites explicitly:

- **`sync._union_merge`**: log and **return without merging**. `reconverge` is best-effort by
  contract (its sole caller `reads.ensure_fresh` swallows everything), so a no-op return is the
  correct degradation — the clone simply stays un-converged instead of unioning.
- **`push.py` (before the merges at the non-FF retry)**: log and **abort the retry loop
  immediately** — specifically **`return` out of `push_tickets_branch`, not `break`** (plan-review G6
  remediation): `break` would fall through to whatever follows the loop and could still report a
  completed push, whereas `return` exits with the push explicitly not-completed. Do not merge, do not
  re-push, do not consume further attempts. The push must
  surface as *not* completed so the existing `PUSH_PENDING` path (which `fsck` reports) is the
  operator-visible signal. Returning "success" would silently drop the local commits from the
  operator's view, and continuing the loop would burn attempts on a merge that must never happen.

## Message channel
`logger.warning`, **not** an exception: every caller of `sync.reconverge` is `reads.ensure_fresh` (`reads.py:255-262`), which wraps it in a bare `except Exception: pass` inside a second bare `except Exception: return`, so a raise is swallowed with **no output**. Visibility comes from the entrypoint handlers (`_cli/__init__.py:408`, `mcp_server.py:688`, `rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:438`), not Python's `lastResort` (`__init__.py:131` attaches a `NullHandler`, so lastResort never fires). Known gap: `sync.push=async` spawns the push with `stdout/stderr=DEVNULL` (`push.py:113-145`), so those clones get no message and rely on `fsck`'s `PUSH_PENDING`.

## Out of scope, declared
`fsck_recover.py` cherry-picks dangling ticket commits with no epoch awareness — it creates new commits rather than unioning a DAG, so blast radius is bounded. Also **not** covered: the CI bash unions at `reconcile-bridge.yml:321` and `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:439`, which are protected by the window protocol (workflows disabled + no in-flight run asserted), not by this guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A clone on a **stale epoch** attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites — asserted separately for `sync._union_merge` and for `push.py`'s non-FF retry.
      Tier: **integration** in two real temporary clones with divergent epochs. This is the RED case.
- [ ] Assert on the emitted **log record** (`caplog`), plus one **subprocess** run with
      `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` proving the message reaches a real operator's stderr.
      `sync.push=async` is excluded by design.
- [ ] At the `push.py` site the retry loop **terminates immediately** on epoch mismatch: exactly
      **zero** merge invocations and **zero** further push attempts, and the push reports
      not-completed so `fsck` surfaces `PUSH_PENDING`. Tier: **unit** with a counting shim on the git
      calls — the guard is a pure predicate plus a control-flow decision, so no real remote is needed;
      the earlier "integration" label contradicted its own unit proving command (plan-review COH).
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py -k push_retry -v`.
- [ ] At the `sync._union_merge` site the function **returns without merging** and the clone is left
      un-converged (not corrupted). Tier: **integration**.
- [ ] A merely-**behind** clone (matching epochs) still converges via ff-adopt, and a
      **strictly-ahead** clone still returns early — neither is blocked. Tier: **integration**. This
      is the negative control that catches the wedge-everything misplacement.
- [ ] **Every row of the state matrix** above is asserted, including the two distinct absences
      (record-absent vs record-present-epoch-absent) and the corrupt-record row. Tier: **unit**,
      table-driven over the matrix — one case per row, so a missing row fails the suite.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py -v`.
- [ ] `git show` failing because the **ref** is unreadable produces a different message than the file
      being **absent** at a readable ref. Tier: **unit** with two fixtures.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py -k remote_read -v`.
- [ ] An older binary reading a record that carries `epoch` does not error and does not fail closed.
      Tier: **unit** against `compat._analyze`.
- [ ] The remote side is read via `git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json`, not the local worktree.
      Tier: **unit** with a fixture where local and remote records differ.

## Files
`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`, `src/rebar/_store/sync.py`, `src/rebar/_store/push.py`, tests

Scope: M. No dependencies; must land and roll out before A6-1.
baseline.summary: A6-0a: fail-closed store-epoch guard at BOTH union sites (keystone for the reclaim)

## Why

The `optionality` workflow (lean-runtime / clean-core-wheel / per-extra / union checks) casts NO Gerrit `Verified` vote — only `gerrit-verify.yaml` does, and it installs `.[dev]` (heavy stack present), so the no-extras clean-wheel RUNTIME check never runs pre-merge. A module-scope heavy-import regression (pydantic_ai/httpx) recently reached main this way. The static AST guard already runs in Verified via `make test`; the runtime/packaging jobs do not. Cost to add: ~0 critical-path latency (32s parallel vs ~1235s macOS long pole), ~145 cheap Linux machine-seconds/run.

## What

Extract optionality's jobs into a `workflow_call` reusable workflow and invoke it from both the push/PR lane and the Verified lane, so a clean-wheel/packaging failure blocks the Verified vote. Incorporate the critical-review findings (mandatory items below).

## Scope

- New `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` (`on: workflow_call`, inputs for the checkout
  mode), `.github/actions/smart-checkout` composite, thin `optionality.yml` caller,
  `gerrit-verify.yaml` gains an `optionality` job + it is added to `vote`'s `needs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `optionality`'s jobs live in a reusable `workflow_call` workflow, invoked by both
      `optionality.yml` (push/PR, branch-head checkout) and `gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- [ ] The gerrit lane checks out the EXACT patchset via `checkout-gerrit-change-action`
      (never plain `actions/checkout`, which would resolve to `main` and false-PASS).
- [ ] The `optionality` job is added to `vote`'s `needs` so the run-level conclusion
      aggregation sees a terminal optionality result before Verified is cast.
- [ ] NO `secrets: inherit` on the reusable workflow; Gerrit values passed as plain
      inputs only (prevents fork-PR exposure of GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY via the PR trigger).
- [ ] The third-party `checkout-gerrit-change-action` is SHA-pinned to the same v1.0.2
      commit gerrit-verify uses.
- [ ] `_optionality.yml` declares `permissions: contents: read`; the optionality caller
      job is pure `uses:` (no `steps:`) and independent of clear-vote/require-ticket.
- [ ] Workflows parse/lint clean (actionlint if available) and the push-triggered
      optionality run passes on the change; gerrit-verify runs the optionality job and
      the Verified vote reflects it.
baseline.summary: Add optionality checks to the Gerrit Verified path via a workflow_call reusable workflow

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split llm/prompting/prompts.py (789 LOC) along its concern boundary

baseline.description:
## Context

Test isolation under ~90-worktree/xdist parallelism is 15.8% of the defect stream (R2S1). The harness root already exists and propagates: `tests/conftest.py:486-513` provides the session-scoped `_rebar_root_sandbox_repo` and an autouse fixture that `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_ROOT", ...)`, per-worker under xdist via `tmp_path_factory`. Propagation to children is by **environment inheritance**, so a test that builds its own `env=` dict from scratch silently drops `REBAR_ROOT` and the child falls back to the git toplevel of cwd — the real checkout.

What is missing is ENFORCEMENT: nothing stops a new unit-tier test from spawning a subprocess with its own ad-hoc temp/HOME/root, which is how the recent class instances arose (`82a0d5cd`: a `home=Path.home()` default reached transitively, resolving the operator's real home; `ef9e1d74`: a single subprocess wall-clock bound conflating a product deadline with machine slack). Precedent: pip's `pytest_collection_modifyitems` raising on forbidden patterns; Bazel's hermetic `TEST_TMPDIR` contract (12c) recorded as the escalation path.

## Approach

A fourth arm in the existing `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (`tests/conftest.py:220`), delegating to a **pure predicate** in a new `tests/_subprocess_isolation.py` — mirroring the `_live_jira_confinement` split, so the predicate is unit-testable without spawning pytest.

Detection is **AST, not regex**: resolve `ast.Call` sites whose callee binds to `subprocess.{run,Popen,check_output,check_call,call}`, `os.system`, `os.popen`, or `pytest.main`, resolving module aliases from the file's own imports. Regex is disqualified — a naive `run(` pattern matches 126 `asyncio.run` sites.

The census on the current tier is 866 spawn sites across 334 files, of which ~841 already take their root from the harness (`cwd=<fixture path>`, `git -C <fixture path>`, a positional `git init <tmp_path>`, `env=subprocess_env(...)`, or plain env inheritance). Only ~26 are hazards, in three shapes: an `env=` dict literal carrying neither `os.environ` nor `REBAR_ROOT` (3), `cwd=REPO_ROOT`/`git -C REPO_ROOT` (23), and one site reading the operator's `$HOME`.

**Bounding the check conservatively is a requirement, not a nicety.** Roughly 58 sites pass `env=<bare variable>` and are undecidable without a def-site trace; these are REPORTED, never failed — failing them would redden 42 files on day one. The sanctioned nested-pytest funnel `tests/_nested_pytest.py` and its four documented exceptions are exempt by name.

Failures raise `pytest.UsageError`, not `pytest.fail`: this arm can fire from the xdist controller, where a `pytest.fail` escapes as a 20-line `INTERNALERROR>` traceback — the precedent and its rationale are already recorded at `tests/conftest.py:264-274` ("a guard whose whole value is a clear message must not look like a crash").

The opt-out is `@pytest.mark.allow_unharnessed_subprocess("<reason>")`. `--strict-markers` validates only the marker NAME, so the mandatory-reason rule is enforced by the guard itself (empty/blank args fail collection) — the same "reason is mandatory" convention as `# read-via:` in `check_config_reads.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: collection fails with an instructive error naming the fixture to use, when a unit-tier test spawns a subprocess without taking its root from the harness. Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py`, which drives the predicate over a seeded violation fixture.
- [x] AC2: the full unit tier collects clean at introduction, with the ~26 hazard sites fixed or explicitly marked and no blanket opt-out. Verified by `pytest --collect-only -q tests/unit` exiting 0.
- [x] AC3: the guard raises `pytest.UsageError` (not `pytest.fail`) so an xdist-controller failure reads as a clean `ERROR:` banner. Verified by a test asserting the raised type.
- [x] AC4: the opt-out marker requires a non-blank reason string, and a bare or empty-reason marker fails collection. Verified by a test over both forms.
- [x] AC5: opt-out growth is greppable and countable, so the mechanism ratchet can see it. Verified by `grep -rn "allow_unharnessed_subprocess" tests/ | wc -l` returning the marked-site count.
- [x] AC6: statically undecidable `env=<bare variable>` sites are reported, not failed. Verified by a test asserting such a site yields a report entry and no collection failure.
- [x] AC7: the check and the marker are documented alongside the existing isolation helpers.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py -v` — the guard's own suite: seeded violation fires (AC1), `UsageError` type (AC3), marker reason required (AC4), undecidable site reported not failed (AC6). The predicate is exercised directly, so no nested pytest spawn is needed.
- `pytest --collect-only -q tests/unit` — proves the tier collects clean at introduction (AC2).
- `pytest -n 4 --collect-only -q tests/unit` — proves the controller path renders the message cleanly rather than as an INTERNALERROR (AC3).
- `grep -rn "allow_unharnessed_subprocess" tests/ | wc -l` — the countable opt-out census (AC5).
- `make lint && make typecheck` — house gates stay green.

## File impact

- `tests/_subprocess_isolation.py` (new; the pure AST predicate, unit-testable in isolation)
- `tests/conftest.py` (fourth arm in `pytest_collection_modifyitems`; register the marker in `pytest_configure`)
- `tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py` (new; seeded-violation RED proof and the marker/undecidable cases)
- the ~26 hazard sites fixed or marked (final set from the AST census)
- `docs/` (the testing/isolation section documenting the existing guards)
baseline.summary: Collection-time enforcement: unit-tier subprocess tests must take isolation roots from the harness

# S8 — Client walkthrough: self-host Gerrit + rebar review-bot on AWS to gate GitHub

## Why
A client wants the same setup we built in d251 — a self-hosted Gerrit server combined
with the rebar review-bot (which imports the rebar review kernel / `rebar.llm`, the
same library the `rebar-mcp` server exposes) — used to GATE commits to a GitHub repo:
GitHub `main` becomes a read-only mirror that only advances via Gerrit after the
deterministic `LLM-Review` vote passes. We need a reproducible, **secret-free**
walkthrough that lets a client replicate this code-review-enforcement topology on
their own AWS account + GitHub repo, distilled from the d251 artifacts (Terraform,
docker-compose, the Gerrit config scripts, and ADRs 0007-0014).

## What
- A new client-facing guide `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` that walks through, end to end:
  1. **Prerequisites** — AWS account + creds, a GitHub repo + an `Administration: write`
     token, a domain/DNS zone, Terraform >= 1.10, Anthropic API key.
  2. **Provision the AWS base** (Terraform `infra/`) — EC2 + EBS + EIP + DNS + IAM +
     the SSM SecureString parameter contract (`/rebar/prod/*`) — referencing ADR-0012.
  3. **Deploy Gerrit + the review-bot** (docker-compose behind nginx/TLS) — referencing
     ADR-0007 (receiver-not-MCP-over-HTTP) + ADR-0008 (SSM->.env secrets).
  4. **Configure the Gerrit project + `LLM-Review` label + submit requirement** —
     referencing ADR-0013.
  5. **Wire the review-bot identity + webhooks + events-log** — referencing ADR-0014
     (inbound auth) + ADR-0009 (the verdict->label pipe / `code_review_decision` seam).
  6. **Gerrit -> GitHub replication** (deploy key, non-force) — referencing ADR-0010.
  7. **Lock the GitHub repo** to the replication identity — referencing ADR-0011 + S6-pre.
  8. **Verify + operate** — the e2e check, the manual `/rerun`, the kill-switch, rollback.
  The guide uses the committed `infra/` scripts/config as the source of truth and shows
  the operator commands; it does NOT duplicate large config inline.
- **No secrets in committed docs.** All credentials are PLACEHOLDERS sourced from SSM /
  CI secrets (never literal). The guide explicitly calls out the secret-handling model.
- **Link from the existing install docs.** Add a link to `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`
  from the project's install documentation (README / docs index) as an OPTIONAL /
  ADVANCED step titled for "code-review enforcement (self-hosted Gerrit gating GitHub)".

## Scope
In: the `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` walkthrough, the link from the install docs, and a
no-secrets verification of all committed documentation. Out: any NEW infrastructure or
code (S8 reuses and references the d251 artifacts produced by S1-S7); per-client
customization beyond the walkthrough.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` exists and is a complete, ordered client walkthrough
      covering all eight steps above (provision -> deploy -> project/label/submit-req ->
      bot/webhooks/events-log -> replication -> GitHub lock -> verify/operate), each step
      referencing the relevant `infra/` artifact(s) and ADR(s).
- [ ] The new guide and ALL committed documentation in the repo contain NO secrets —
      only placeholders; credentials are sourced from SSM Parameter Store / CI secrets.
      Verified by a secret scan over the committed docs (and `infra/`).
- [ ] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` is linked from the existing install docs (README and/or
      the docs index) as an explicitly OPTIONAL / ADVANCED step for code-review
      enforcement (self-hosted Gerrit gating GitHub) — discoverable from the normal
      install path but not required for standard rebar use.
- [ ] The walkthrough's secret-handling section documents the SSM-SecureString -> ephemeral
      `.env` model (ADR-0008) and that no credential is ever committed.
baseline.summary: Client walkthrough: self-host Gerrit + rebar review-bot on AWS to gate GitHub

baseline.description:
Discovered while implementing e9d5-c850-d505-4a5a (typed reconciler mutation payload contracts, ADR 0107). Two producers construct (outbound, update) Mutation payloads with different shapes:

- differ.py's older _compute_mutations_emit_both path emits a flat,
  unwrapped "changed" dict directly as Mutation.payload.
- outbound_pass.py / binding_walk.py wrap the same information as
  {"changed_fields": {...}, "comments": [...], "labels": [...], "links": [...]}.

ADR 0107's typed OutboundUpdatePayload contract standardizes on the wrapped shape (changed_fields); the flat legacy shape from differ.py's older path would fail typed validation today. This is a pre-existing inconsistency, NOT introduced by e9d5 -- e9d5 only documents it (see the corpus README and e9d5's ticket comment recording approved intentional deltas) and does not reconcile it, since producer rewiring is ADR 0107's deferred "Cut" step and out of e9d5's own scope (AC7).

Suggested follow-up: decide (a) which shape is canonical going forward, and (b) migrate differ.py's _compute_mutations_emit_both to emit the wrapped changed_fields shape so both producers agree before any producer is rewired to construct OutboundUpdatePayload directly (that "Cut" step is a separate, later ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- A decision is recorded on which shape is canonical for (outbound, update)
  Mutation payloads.
- differ.py's _compute_mutations_emit_both and outbound_pass.py /
  binding_walk.py agree on payload shape, verified by a test asserting both
  producers emit the same normalized shape for an equivalent update.
baseline.summary: Reconcile dual outbound-update payload shapes (differ.py flat vs outbound_pass.py wrapped)

baseline.description:
## Summary

Gerrit's outbound email has never worked on the production box (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`). `/var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config` contains **no `[sendemail]` section at all**, so Gerrit falls back to its built-in default SMTP target of `localhost:25`. The official Gerrit container ships no MTA, nothing listens on that port, and every outbound notification therefore fails.

This is the single largest error signature in the Gerrit logs by an order of magnitude — **4,119 occurrences** across the retained history — and it is still firing today.

## Reproduction Steps

1. SSM onto `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (us-east-1).
2. `grep -A6 -iE '\[sendemail\]' /var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config` — no
   `[sendemail]` section exists.
3. Comment on, merge, abandon, or push a new patchset to any Gerrit change.
4. `grep 'Cannot email' /var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** either outbound mail is configured and succeeds, or it is
  explicitly disabled (`sendemail.enable = false`) so Gerrit does not attempt it
  and does not log an error.
- **Actual:** Gerrit attempts SMTP on every notification and fails with
  `Connection refused`, emitting a multi-line ERROR + stack trace each time.

## Evidence

Counts over the retained Gerrit logs (`/var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log*`, 2026-06-30 → 2026-07-30):

```
Mail Error: Connection refused ....................... 4119
"Cannot email ..." error lines ....................... 3713
  ERROR EmailReviewComments : Cannot email comments for N,N ......... 2812
  ERROR EmailMerge : Cannot email merged notification for N .........  840
  ERROR EmailNewPatchSet : Cannot send email for new patch set N,N ..  385
  ERROR AbandonOp : Cannot email update for change N ................   40
in the CURRENT (live) error_log alone ................  135
```

Verbatim, most recent occurrences observed 2026-07-30:

```
[2026-07-30T20:49:16.668Z] [SendEmail-1[send-email merged]] ERROR
  com.google.gerrit.server.submit.EmailMerge : Cannot email merged notification
  for 1057 [CONTEXT SUBMISSION_ID="1057-1785444..."]
com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused
    at com.google.gerrit.server.mail.send.SmtpEmailSender.open(SmtpEmailSender.java:457)

[2026-07-30T20:54:05.506Z] [SendEmail-1[send-email comments]] ERROR
  com.google.gerrit.server.change.EmailReviewComments : Cannot email comments
  for 1048,4 [CONTEXT SSH_SESSION="6e14303c" ...]
com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused
    at com.google.gerrit.server.mail.send.SmtpEmailSender.open(SmtpEmailSender.java:457)
```

Daily spread (non-exhaustive sample of rotations) shows it is continuous, not a burst: 06-30 → 2, 07-05 → 108, 07-10 → 230, 07-15 → 117, 07-20 → 17, 07-25 → 58, 07-28 → 56, 07-29 → 21, live log → 135.

## Why this was never caught

- No CloudWatch alarm covers Gerrit SMTP. The host probe publishes
  `voter_errors`, `deploy_errors`, `g2p_dispatch_errors`, `replication_errors`
  and `review_bot_merge_change_errors` to namespace `rebar/host`, but nothing
  counts email-send failures, so the `rebar-gerrit-*` alarm set stayed green
  throughout.
- The condition was noticed exactly once, in passing, and set aside without a
  ticket: a comment on story `9249` records "the gerrit log also carries a
  pre-existing SmtpEmailSender connect failure. That is unrelated to this story
  (no SMTP change here)". Correct in that narrow context, but no bug was filed.
- A search of all 1,584 tickets for `smtp` / `sendemail` / `Cannot email`
  returns that single `9249` comment and nothing else.

## Impact

- Reviewers and change owners receive **no** Gerrit notification of comments,
  merges, new patchsets, or abandons. Our flow is heavily bot-driven, so the
  functional impact may be small in practice — but that tradeoff has never been
  recorded as a decision anywhere.
- ~4,000 multi-line ERROR + stack-trace entries actively bury genuine errors in
  `error_log`, which measurably raised the cost of this very audit.
- Contrast with `c943`, where the decision *not* to ship voter logs to
  CloudWatch was deliberately recorded in `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`.
  Here there is no configuration and no recorded decision — only silent failure.

## Decision required

Two legitimate resolutions; this bug should pick one explicitly rather than leave the current silent-failure state:

- **(A) Wire up outbound mail** — configure `[sendemail]` against Amazon SES
  (secrets via SSM SecureString + the existing instance role, consistent with
  how `ci-gerrit-ssh-key` / `g2p-github-pat` are handled).
- **(B) Disable cleanly** — set `sendemail.enable = false` so Gerrit stops
  attempting delivery, and record the rationale in the runbook.

Research into how actively-maintained Gerrit deployments configure AWS mail is attached as a comment on this ticket to ground that choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision between (A) configure SES and (B) disable cleanly is made and
      recorded in `infra/runbooks/` (not only in this ticket).
- [ ] `gerrit.config` carries an explicit `[sendemail]` section reflecting that
      decision; the config is materialized by the deploy path so it survives a
      compose-up and an autodeploy roll-forward.
- [ ] After the change, a fresh comment/merge/patchset on a Gerrit change
      produces **zero** `Cannot email` / `Mail Error: Connection refused` lines
      in `/var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.
- [ ] If (A): a test message is demonstrably delivered end-to-end, and the SES
      sandbox/production-access state is recorded.
- [ ] If (B): the lost functionality is enumerated in the runbook so the choice
      is reversible with full information.
- [ ] Observability gap closed: either the host probe counts email-send failures
      into `rebar/host` with an alarm, or the runbook states why not (mirroring
      the `c943` precedent).
- [ ] File paths: `infra/gerrit/` (gerrit.config materialization),
      `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, `infra/runbooks/`.
baseline.summary: Gerrit outbound email has never been configured: no [sendemail] section, 4119 'Mail Error: Connection refused' since 2026-06-30 and still firing

Split out of chewed-illicit-blacklemur (b8f7-65be-ec00-4844). Distinct defect, distinct fix.

TEST: tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py::test_plan_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union (and its two siblings, test_code_review_* / test_completion_*, which share the same helper).

SIGNATURE: AssertionError: clones do not share a base

## Confirmed root cause

The failing assertion is a FIXTURE PRECONDITION, not the I1 append-only invariant under test. In `_assert_emit_is_append_only`, clone A pushes its padded sidecar base to origin/tickets and clone B is then expected to hold the same base. B's sync is driven only as an incidental side effect of a read:

    _git("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:tickets", cwd=tracker_a)
    _expire_sync_marker(tracker_b)
    _engine_run(repo_b, "list")          # <- the only thing that syncs B
    ...
    assert base_a == _sidecar_paths(tracker_b, ...), "clones do not share a base"

That read-freshness path is best-effort BY DESIGN. `rebar._engine_support.reads.ensure_fresh` is throttled by a /tmp marker, calls `reconverge` with a deliberately SHORT lock timeout, and swallows every failure ("a read must never fail because a fetch could not run"). So `list` returns 0 whether or not B pulled A's push. Under CI load (contended lock / slow runner) the reconverge is skipped or times out silently, B keeps its stale base, and the test fails while building its own setup. The append-only behaviour the test exists to prove is never reached, so the red is a false alarm that costs a Verified -1.

Reproduced deterministically on this checkout by forcing the incidental sync to be a no-op (`REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off`, which `ensure_fresh` honours): all three two-clone-union tests fail with exactly `AssertionError: clones do not share a base`. With the sync left enabled they pass. That isolates the precondition to the best-effort side effect and rules out a product defect in sidecar emit.

## Fix

Make the fixture ASSERT its precondition instead of relying on a side effect:

1. Add a `_sync_from_origin(tracker)` helper that fetches `origin tickets` and fast-forwards
   the tracker onto `FETCH_HEAD`, both with `check=True`, so a sync failure raises at its own
   call site as a setup error rather than surfacing later as a misleading invariant failure.
2. Replace `_expire_sync_marker(tracker_b)` + `_engine_run(repo_b, "list")` in
   `_assert_emit_is_append_only` with that explicit call.
3. Label the two setup assertions distinctly from the I1 invariant assertions so triage can
   tell a setup failure from a real append-only violation.
4. Document at the helper why the production read path must NOT be used to establish a
   fixture precondition.

Deterministic sync, not a retry loop. Content/ordering assertions only - no wall-clock or timing-budget assertions are added.

Scope: tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py only. No production code changes; the product behaviour under test is unchanged and still fully exercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: `_assert_emit_is_append_only` establishes clone B's shared base with an explicit
      checked `git fetch` + `git merge --ff-only`; it no longer calls `_engine_run(repo_b,
      "list")` or `_expire_sync_marker` to make the base converge.
- [x] AC2: The two shared-base preconditions are asserted with messages that identify them as
      SETUP failures, textually distinct from the I1 append-only invariant messages.
- [x] AC3: With the incidental read-sync disabled (`REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off`) all three
      `*_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union` tests PASS on the fixed code; on the pre-fix code the
      same command fails all three with `AssertionError: clones do not share a base`.
- [x] AC4: All three tests pass under the default environment, and the file adds no wall-clock
      or timing-budget assertion (assertions remain content/ordering facts).
- [x] AC5: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: De-flake sidecar two-clone union fixture sync race

## Why
Three lightweight, ADVISORY/observational reliability additions from the dso gap report (#7 FP ledger, #10 grounding-health telemetry, #12 approach-viability note). None ever changes the deterministic verdict or adds a BLOCK source; all are coverage/coaching signals for agent consumers.

## What
Concrete decisions (resolving the plan-review advisories — thresholds named, data-flow specified):

### #7 — fp:code-review ledger + compile step
- Convention doc `docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md` (the concrete artifact): a confirmed false
  positive / invalid finding from the code-review gate is recorded as a `bug`-typed rebar ticket
  tagged `fp:code-review`, whose body carries REQUIRED fields — the finding (criterion + finding
  text), the diff/context that triggered it, and a `root-cause` drawn from a CLOSED enum:
  `false-evidence`, `rubric-overapplication`, `hallucinated-gap`, `scope-mismatch`, `stale-baseline`.
- Light compile tooling `src/rebar/llm/code_review/fp_ledger.py`:
  `compile_fp_ledger(repo_root) -> list[dict]` reads open `fp:code-review`-tagged tickets and DRAFTS
  no-fire eval cases in the EXISTING eval-spec dataset shape (`{id, corpus: "fp-ledger",
  expect: "pass", mode: <root-cause>, diff: <context>}`, matching code-review-*.eval.yaml). It is
  IDEMPOTENT: a drafted ticket gets a `compiled` tag and is skipped on re-run (processed-cursor via
  tag). Per-ticket ERROR ISOLATION: a malformed/unparseable ticket is skipped + logged, never aborts
  the batch, and a rebar-store error surfaces as an empty draft-list (never raises into a caller).
  MANUAL to start (Rule-of-Three: the corpus feeds evals once ≥1 ticket exists; no auto-schedule).

### #10 — grounding-health telemetry + low-grounding note
- Named constant `NON_TRIVIAL_DIFF_LINES = 20` (module-level in `fp_ledger.py`'s sibling telemetry
  home / gate_dispatch): a diff is NON-TRIVIAL iff `changed_lines > NON_TRIVIAL_DIFF_LINES` OR
  `changed_files > 1`. Single decided value — not two open options.
- Extend `_attach_code_review_metrics` (gate_dispatch.py) `coverage["metrics"]` with:
  `findings_per_run` (len(blocking)+len(advisory)), `verify_requests` (sum of the agentic Pass-2
  verify step's `_usage.requests` — the SAME mechanism plan-review's `verify_requests` already uses,
  so per-agentic-pass request/tool-call counts ARE available), and `grounding_health` band
  (`"ok"` | `"low"`).
- LOW-GROUNDING NOTE: when the diff is NON-TRIVIAL and the agentic verify pass made ZERO requests
  (`verify_requests == 0`), set `grounding_health = "low"` and emit an advisory
  `coverage["grounding_note"]` naming the named threshold. NEVER blocks.

### #12 — approach-viability advisory note
- Named constants `MIN_SURVIVING_HIGH_PRIORITY = 3`, `MAX_PASS2_DROP_RATE = 0.5`.
- Deterministic post-Pass-3 signal (computed in `_attach_code_review_metrics` from the assembled
  verdict + recorder, so it is verdict-independent): if the surviving high-priority advisory count
  `>= MIN_SURVIVING_HIGH_PRIORITY` OR the Pass-2 drop rate `>= MAX_PASS2_DROP_RATE`
  (dropped / (dropped+surfaced+blocking), 0 when denominator 0), emit an advisory
  `coverage["approach_viability_note"]` for agent consumers. NEVER changes the verdict.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/fp_ledger.py` (new: constants + compile step), `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (`_attach_code_review_metrics` enrichment + the two notes), `docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md` (new). Unit tests for each. All advisory/observational — no verdict-path change, no new BLOCK source.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md` exists documenting: the `fp:code-review` tag, the required
      body fields, and the CLOSED `root-cause` enum (five values above).
- [ ] `compile_fp_ledger` drafts no-fire eval cases (existing fixture shape) from `fp:code-review`
      tickets, is idempotent (skips `compiled`-tagged), and isolates per-ticket errors — a unit test
      pins draft-shape, idempotency, and that a malformed ticket is skipped not raised.
- [ ] `coverage["metrics"]` carries `findings_per_run`, `verify_requests`, and `grounding_health`;
      the low-grounding note fires ONLY on a non-trivial diff with zero verify requests, using the
      named `NON_TRIVIAL_DIFF_LINES` constant; it never blocks (unit test).
- [ ] The approach-viability note fires on the named `MIN_SURVIVING_HIGH_PRIORITY` /
      `MAX_PASS2_DROP_RATE` thresholds and never changes the verdict (unit test asserts verdict
      unchanged with/without the note).
