# Unchanged-plan review reuse must replay the last review's full result, notated as reused

## Current behavior (evidence)

`rebar review-plan` short-circuits when nothing the review would read has changed (both paths bypassed by `--force`):

- PASS path: `idempotent_reuse` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:57-135, feature b3e5) reuses the still-valid certified attestation — but it SYNTHESIZES the returned verdict with EMPTY `blocking`/`advisory`/`coaching`/`indeterminate` lists and no counts, instead of replaying the stored REVIEW_RESULT sidecar content. The CLI (`_render_plan_review_text`, src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:407-427) then prints `PLAN REVIEW: PASS`, the "reused: existing attestation is still current — no LLM re-run (pass --force to re-review)" notation, and `blocking=0 advisory=0 …` — losing whatever advisory findings and coaching the last real review actually surfaced.
- BLOCK path: `verdict_reuse` (reuse.py:138-215, bug 7e77) already replays the stored blocking/advisory/coaching from the latest sidecar plus a reused notation — this is the desired shape.

## Requested behavior (operator, 2026-08-22)

When plan review refuses to re-run because the plan is unchanged since the last review, output THE RESULT OF THE LAST REVIEW, with a notation that it is the last review's result replayed against the unchanged plan — not a fresh review. The BLOCK path already conforms; close the PASS-path gap and make the notation state what it replayed.

## Scope

1. `idempotent_reuse`: when the reuse fires, read the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (it already reads it for the ticket-type check) and, when it is usable and corresponds to the same material fingerprint, populate the returned verdict's `advisory`, `coaching`, `indeterminate`, and `coverage.counts` from the stored result rather than empties. Keep the existing fail-open semantics: an unreadable/absent/mismatched sidecar degrades to the current empty-list behavior (the attestation, not the sidecar, is the validity authority — do not let a sidecar problem block a valid reuse). `blocking` stays empty on a PASS by construction; if the stored sidecar verdict contradicts (BLOCK stored but attestation valid), prefer current behavior and do not replay contradictory findings.
2. CLI notation (`_render_plan_review_text`): on either reuse path, the notation must make unmistakable that the rendered findings are the LAST review's result replayed because the plan/code are unchanged (not a fresh LLM run), and keep pointing at `--force` to re-review. Include the stored review's recency anchor if the sidecar carries one (e.g. its verified_at_sha / timestamp) so the reader can judge staleness; omit gracefully when absent.
3. JSON surface parity: the machine-readable result keeps `coverage.llm_ran=False` and the existing `idempotent_skip`/`verdict_reuse` flags; replayed findings appear in the same fields a fresh review would use. `runner="reused"` unchanged. MCP output schema must remain valid (`findings.validate_structured` already gates this — keep it passing).
4. Tests: RED first — a reuse-path test proving stored advisory/coaching are replayed on PASS reuse (currently empty), a fail-open test (sidecar unreadable → reuse still fires with empty lists), and a rendering test for the notation. Do not weaken existing b3e5/7e77 tests.

## Non-goals

- No change to WHEN reuse fires (validity rules, fingerprints, type-change invalidation stay exactly as-is).
- No change to `--force`, exit codes, signing, or sidecar emission (reuse still emits no new sidecar).
- No change to `review-plan --status`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] PASS reuse replays the stored sidecar's advisory/coaching/indeterminate + counts when the sidecar matches the current material fingerprint; degraded empty-list behavior preserved when it does not.
- [x] Both reuse paths render a notation stating the output is the last review's result replayed against an unchanged plan, with --force pointer.
- [x] `coverage.llm_ran=False` + reuse flags unchanged; structured validation passes.
- [x] New tests seen RED before the fix; existing reuse tests unweakened.
baseline.summary: Replay last review result on unchanged-plan reuse

# Publish the review policy: what the LLM-Review and Verified gates mean for contributors

## Why

rebar's blocking `LLM-Review` Gerrit label appears to be first-of-kind in public OSS: research (2024–2026) found no project documenting a blocking LLM merge vote — the Kubernetes AI-review policy (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/github-management/ai-code-review-tools.md) makes AI review advisory-only. Novelty raises the documentation bar. The document's SHAPE is convergent: Chromium's CQ doc (https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/infra/cq.md) and Zuul's gating doc (https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html) both name the labels, define each vote value, state bot-vs-human authority, and document escape hatches.

Why a separate doc rather than expanding CONTRIBUTING §2c: §2c is the in-flow quick reference; the policy doc carries the normative content (authority, dispute, bypass, responsibility) that outlives workflow edits and is linkable from every surface. Authority rule (the epic's single-source protocol, clarified): `docs/review-policy.md` is the sole authoritative DOCUMENT for vote semantics; its table's CONTENT is transcribed from the code (the enums below) — document-of-record and source-of-truth are different things and both are named here.

Sequencing note (resolves the file-existence review findings): `docs/your-first-change.md` does not exist at plan time — it is created by story **fat-leaflike-canary**, which this story `depends_on` (edge recorded in the store). The retarget edit to that file executes only after that story lands.

## What

New `docs/review-policy.md` (contributor-facing):

- The two required labels, described accurately:
  - `Verified` — CI on GitHub Actions via `gerrit-verify.yaml`. NOT described as just three make targets: the workflow additionally runs the rebar-ticket trailer check, module-size gate, prompt-index/env-registry drift gates, security-rules freshness, criteria-routing parity, public-types drift, `make config-check`, pip-audit, and unit + integration pytest tiers. The doc states: "locally approximate with `make lint && make typecheck && make test`; the authoritative list is the workflow file (linked)."
  - `LLM-Review` — what the bot reviews; only bots/admins vote either label (no self-approval, no self-verification).
- Vote-semantics table (Chromium style) transcribed from BOTH code sources: the five `_TAG_SUFFIXES` coverage-gap sub-reasons in `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` (gate-disabled, llm-unavailable, scanner, review-error, indeterminate), PLUS the merge-path tags emitted by `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`: the distinct `coverage-gap (merge-review)` veto (~line 160) and the `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix variant. Each row: what it means + the productive response (`finding` → fix and re-push; any `coverage-gap (…)` → infra veto, not your code, maintainer re-triggers; `Verified −1` → open the linked run; `recheck` for flakes). Drift-guard line in the doc: "if you see a tag not listed here, treat it as coverage-gap-class and ping the maintainer" (a CI drift gate tying doc to enums is out of scope, noted as future work).
- Bot vs human authority (Zuul's mechanical-enforcement framing): (a) the lead maintainer sets the rubric and can waive/override any finding; (b) dispute path — resolve the comment thread with written justification or raise to the maintainer, best-effort response within 5 business days (matching SECURITY.md's ack window); if unresolved, the maintainer's decision is final (solo-maintainer reality, stated plainly); (c) the gate supplements maintainer judgment; (d) bypasses are admin-only and auditable.
- Responsibility clause (Kubernetes norm, cited): the submitter must be able to personally explain their change, AI-assisted or not.
- One clarifying paragraph distinguishing THIS (code-review merge gate) from the plan-review ticket gate, linking docs/plan-review-gate.md.
- Framing recorded in the doc itself: the gate is "required-with-human-override"; the dispute path is v1 and will iterate with the first external contributor.

Links this story owns (ownership-inversion rule): add the review-policy link into CONTRIBUTING.md §2c (slimmed to summary + pointer; the full sub-reason enumeration moves out of §2c) and — after the dependency lands — retarget `docs/your-first-change.md`'s vote-semantics link from §2c to the new doc.

## Scope

IN: `docs/review-policy.md` (new), CONTRIBUTING §2c slim-down + pointer, tutorial link retarget (executes post fat-leaflike-canary). OUT: changing gate behavior/thresholds/criteria; a CI drift gate tying the doc to the enums (future work); the plan-review gate's own docs; Gerrit ACL changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/review-policy.md` present — prove, each as its own grep against the file: "LLM-Review"; "Verified"; "gate-disabled"; "llm-unavailable"; "scanner"; "review-error"; "indeterminate"; "merge-review"; "merge-change"; "recheck"; "5 business days"; "plan-review"; "override"; "dispute"; "bypass".
- [ ] Verified described via the workflow — prove: `grep -q "gerrit-verify" docs/review-policy.md` and `grep -qi "approximat" docs/review-policy.md` (the make targets labeled as local approximation).
- [ ] No-self-approval + maintainer-override stated — prove: `grep -qi "self-approv" docs/review-policy.md` and `grep -qi "waive\|override" docs/review-policy.md`.
- [ ] Single-source enforced — prove: `grep -q "review-policy" CONTRIBUTING.md` (pointer added) and `grep -c "llm-unavailable\|gate-disabled" CONTRIBUTING.md` = 0 after the slim-down (enumeration lives only in the policy doc); post-dependency, `grep -q "review-policy" docs/your-first-change.md`.
- [ ] Framing + iteration caveat in the doc — prove: `grep -qi "human-override" docs/review-policy.md` and `grep -qi "will iterate\|v1 of this policy" docs/review-policy.md`.
baseline.summary: Publish the review policy: what the LLM-Review and Verified gates mean for contributors

# `s3_doctor` sits outside rebar's self-healing git seam, so a transient object-DB read fails the heal

## Proven mechanism

Three CI occurrences (runs 31340000912, 31349549323, 31558315198 — three DIFFERENT sibling tests) fail identically:

    S3DoctorConflict: could not bundle merged tip <sha> for ref tickets: fatal: bad object HEAD

The investigation on this ticket established, by experiment against real git:

- `fatal: bad object` is git's `get_reference()` path — the name resolved to an OID but
  `parse_object()` returned NULL, i.e. **the object was unreadable at that instant**. An unborn
  or dangling HEAD produces `ambiguous argument`, never `bad object`; an empty or corrupt object
  emits extra `error:` lines the CI logs do not contain. So the object was ABSENT, not corrupt.
- The literal `HEAD` token in the message carries no information: run 31340000912 raised the
  same fault with the SHA named directly (`bad object ae7d19a6…`).
- The mechanism reproduces byte-for-byte by making the merge commit's object unreadable
  immediately before the bundle call.
- **`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`'s `_git` helper calls `gitutil.run_git` directly.** No retry
  wrapper is in that path at all — not `_with_index_lock_retry`, not
  `_with_transient_head_retry`, not the per-store advisory git-op lock. The whole `s3_doctor`
  module is the one store git caller OUTSIDE rebar's self-healing seam, while every other store
  write path routes through `gitutil.run_git_write` and self-heals exactly this class of
  runner-FS read blip.

The runner-side TRIGGER (what made the object briefly unreadable) remains unproven and is NOT in scope. What is in scope is the proven structural gap: the same fault class that the rest of the store rides out unassisted is fatal here, and it has now cost three review cycles.

## Scope — reuse the existing seam, do not grow a fourth private retry

1. Route `s3_doctor._git` through the existing `gitutil.run_git_write` seam instead of raw
   `run_git`, so it inherits the per-store advisory git-op lock, the bounded index/ref-lock
   retry, and the transient read-fault retry. `git bundle create` reads objects and writes a
   scratch file the caller re-creates and deletes; the other doctor invocations are reads,
   merges and scratch-ref updates. All satisfy the idempotency precondition
   `_with_transient_head_retry` documents.
2. Extend the existing transient-marker family in `gitutil` to the PROVEN missing-object
   signature (`bad object`) so the observed fault self-heals, keeping the marker set tight and
   greppable exactly as `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_MARKERS` is. No new retry loop, no new backoff policy,
   no new module — the existing wrapper gains one scoped marker.
3. Distinguish the failure in the raised error: `S3DoctorConflict`'s default hint ("tickets
   store heads conflict; run: rebar fsck-recover") misdescribes an object-DB read failure on a
   merge that never conflicted, and sends the operator to the wrong tool.

This is behavior-preserving hardening justified by recurrence: a success or any non-transient failure still returns at once, so a genuine error surfaces unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `s3_doctor._git` routes through `gitutil.run_git_write`; no raw `run_git` call remains in
      `s3_doctor`.
- [x] The proven `bad object` signature is retried by the existing transient-read wrapper in
      `gitutil`, scoped to that marker family — no new retry loop is introduced.
- [x] A test injects the transient deterministically (first bundle attempt fails with the exact
      CI signature, the identical retry succeeds) and asserts the heal completes losslessly.
      It fails before the change.
- [x] A non-transient git failure is still raised immediately, with no retry — pinned by a test,
      so the marker cannot mask a genuine error.
- [x] A bundle failure that survives the retries raises an error whose hint describes an
      object-DB read failure rather than a heads conflict.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the s3_doctor + gitutil test tiers pass.
baseline.summary: Flaky CI: s3_doctor heal test fails with 'fatal: bad object HEAD' when bundling the merged tip

# Exemplar remediation: llm/plan_review/ end-to-end + enable BLE001/T201 with shrinking allowlist

The reference PR. Its diff IS the convention — every other batch copies it. Do NOT parallelize this with the sweeps; it must land (and lock the lint) before they start. Depends on the logging substrate.

## What
- Remediate every broad-except in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` to the observability floor: log with
  `exc_info` OR carry a justified `# noqa: BLE001` (reason string required). Opportunistic narrowing only
  where a specific type is genuinely expected, with a test.
- Migrate `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` diagnostics in the package to the named logger.
- Enable ruff **BLE001** and **T201** (scoped) in `pyproject.toml` `[tool.ruff.lint]`, gated behind a
  `per-file-ignores` allowlist that exempts every not-yet-swept package (clone the shrinking-allowlist
  pattern from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`); `llm/plan_review/` is NOT in the allowlist.
- T201 scoping (corrected per plan-review G4): banned in library/core/MCP, but a `per-file-ignore` is needed
  for the legitimate-`print` surfaces — BOTH (a) the CLI presentation layer (`_cli`, `_commands`), where
  `print(json.dumps(...))` stdout output is the machine contract, AND (b) the reconciler subprocess
  (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/`), which legitimately prints operational `RECON:`/`ERROR:` lines to its OWN
  stderr (all 42 existing `# noqa: T201` sites live there, NOT in the CLI).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All broad-except sites in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` meet the observability floor; no unjustified
      `except ...: pass` remains.
- [ ] Stderr-diagnostic prints in the package are migrated to `logging.getLogger(__name__)`.

      packages; CI is green.
- [ ] `llm/plan_review/` is excluded from the allowlist (it is fully conformant).
- [ ] `make lint` + full test suite pass.

## Target
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — **786 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (14 lines of headroom).

Fourteen lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.

# Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

## Context / Problem

A `/rebar-implement` run of epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` landed five changes through every gate. **The gates performed to their design envelope.** Plan-review blocked infeasible mechanics (a tenacity-transport claim that cannot wrap boto3; an `isinstance` against a botocore-dependent class; a live canary path that would have made billable AWS calls on every CI run). The completion-verifier twice refused a close whose stated criteria had no test. Full-suite pre-flight caught cross-module regressions `tests/unit` missed.

Every one of those catches shares a property: **the ground truth lived in the repo**, where the reviewer's read/grep tools could reach it.

Four escapes got through, and they are one defect wearing different clothes — **a green signal whose measurement could not have observed the failure it claims to rule out**:

1. **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching and model-availability measurements were taken in account
   `579718921998` / `us-east-2` and recorded as settled fact; the project runs in `896586841071` / `us-east-1`
   (named by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`). No gate compares a claim's observation
   context against the project's environment. A human caught it by asking "is that this project's account?"
2. **Instruments that cannot observe the failure — twice, in the same investigation.** This escape is the
   epic's sharpest example precisely because the *first correction was also wrong*.

   **2a.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls validated a *scoped* IAM grant while running under an identity
   holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than production is structurally unable to
   fail, so its success carries **zero information**.

   **2b.** The prescribed remedy — `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against the role — then produced a
   confident, recorded, and **wrong** conclusion: that `bedrock:Converse` was the action to grant. The
   simulator answered exactly the question asked ("would this policy permit the action *named*
   `bedrock:Converse`?", legitimately no, since that action genuinely exists) but **not** the question that
   mattered ("which action does the Converse API actually *check*?"). Only a real call FROM the instance
   revealed the truth — `AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel` — meaning
   the ORIGINAL plan was right and the "fix" broke it, on a role feeding `eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`, a cutover
   with no fallback.

   The pair is the lesson: a wildcard identity could not fail, and a simulator could not fail *for the reason
   that mattered*. **Evidence is only as good as its ability to have come out the other way for the reason
   you care about** — and swapping one instrument for a more rigorous-sounding one does not establish that.
3. **Tests that cannot fail** — the code-side form of the same defect: a contrast case whose discriminating
   conjunct was never exercised, and an oracle asserting on an object where production passes a string.
   **Both WERE caught** (mutation testing; the LLM reviewer) precisely because they are repo-checkable. That
   contrast is the evidence for this epic's thesis.
4. **Confidence outrunning method**: "verified by reading" was a hand-picked grep that missed a dependency;
   "18/18 green" was reported while typecheck was red.

## Why 1 and 2 are structural, not a calibration miss

`verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all. Plan-review runs **before** the evidence exists, so it cannot audit a measurement not yet taken; the completion-verifier accepts `[operator-attested]` evidence **on trust by design** (ADR-0043). One gate cannot audit it, the other is designed not to. The in-flight T5c rewrite pushes grounding toward current code and IaC state but still cannot observe a live cloud account — nothing in the current design can, and nothing should try.

## Approach

Do **not** make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it. Detail lives in the child story; the shape is:

1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and
   privilege posture relative to production.
2. Enforce their **presence** deterministically, zero LLM, mirroring
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (DET-first doctrine).
3. Let an LLM criterion judge the *declaration* against repo facts — once provenance is text, "plan attests
   account X, IaC names account Y" becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**, which is exactly what the
   gate's strongest criteria already do well.
4. Land the generalized rule as an **advisory** criterion per ADR-0054; corpus replay decides promotion.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, recursive — the verifier's
  own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the instrument under
  suspicion.
- **Escape 4 as gate scope.** Reported-green-while-red is *reporting discipline*, already covered by the
  orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success. Filing it as a
  gate gap would be mis-attribution.
- **Wording changes alone.** The contract was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the defect. This is
  the same lesson as epic `9109-2ad9-2477-4cf6` (Serena tool-choice), which is why that epic's structural
  framing is the model here rather than its subject matter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking measurement provenance is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check
      (no LLM) — `det_measurement_provenance.py`, surfaced advisory through `p6_ac_quality`, landed in
      change 1423 with a mutation-tested oracle (breaking the binding rule, placeholder detection or enum
      membership each kills tests)
- [x] the new criterion ships **advisory** (ADR-0054) and rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, leaving the
      shipped default criteria set unchanged for other rebar clients
- [x] an ADR records the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes
- [x] the completion-verifier is NOT made to re-run world measurements — the rejected alternative stays
      rejected, and a test or grep demonstrates it

## Descoped to `98df-3528-9b1f-405a` (ridiculous-expert-mouse), filed as an `idea`

AC-1 originally also required the wrong-account escape to be **reproduced as a regression fixture** from the real `579718921998` vs `896586841071` case. That clause is NOT delivered and is NOT claimed as done.

Reproducing it means exercising the AGENT criterion's rule (a) semantically, which needs an eval corpus (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.eval.yaml`) plus a live run — the same behavioural half descoped from story `f161`. Both moved to `98df`, which also carries the rule (b)/(c)/(d) fixtures and the ADR-0054 corpus-replay false-positive rate that would justify promoting the criterion from advisory.

This epic therefore closes on its MECHANISM being delivered and proven — provenance is now forced into the record as text, deterministically enforced, and judged by a tool-enabled criterion — not on that criterion's firing behaviour having been calibrated. The distinction is safe because the criterion ships **advisory**: it cannot block any claim or close, so an uncalibrated advisory criterion is inert-but-useful rather than risky. Promotion is a separate ADR-0054 decision nobody has committed to, which is why `98df` is an `idea`.
baseline.summary: Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

## Context (parking lot — undesigned; do NOT dispatch)

The project auto-lander (epic f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af) is deliberately **Gerrit-specific, project-owned
infrastructure** — its agent-facing landing command lives in project tooling, NOT `rebar` core,
because landing/merge-queueing is platform-specific and not part of rebar's platform-agnostic
mission.

rebar's roadmap includes **code-review support on broader platforms** (GitHub without Gerrit,
GitLab, …). IF/when a **second** platform needs to land changes, generalize the *portable* part of
the auto-lander into a **provider-abstracted landing seam in `rebar` core**:

- A platform-neutral **`land → typed outcome` interface**, where the outcome enum
  (`merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed | review_failed`) is the platform-agnostic core.
- **Adapters** per platform own the status-reading + land-request specifics: Gerrit
  (votes/labels/`POST rebase`+submit), GitHub (checks + `mergeable_state` + merge queue), GitLab
  (`detailed_merge_status` + merge trains).
- The project auto-lander (f1fa) would refactor onto the Gerrit adapter with no behaviour change.

This is consistent with rebar's existing **provider-neutral direction** (identity + reconciler:
jira-accountId now, GitHub node-id later).

## Why this is an `idea`, not `open`

**YAGNI / de-frankenstein discipline.** There is **no second platform that needs to land yet**, so
building the abstraction now would be a speculative seam abstracted from a single implementation —
exactly the premature-generalization rebar avoids (cf. the identity epic cutting the keyless/Sigstore
seam until a real need existed). A Gerrit-shaped `rebar land` in core *today* is the premature
version of this. **Promote to `open` only when a concrete non-Gerrit landing requirement appears**
(likely alongside a broader-platform code-review/sync epic), at which point the two real
implementations justify the abstraction.

## Rough acceptance (when promoted — to be designed then)

- [ ] A provider-neutral landing interface in rebar defining the portable typed-outcome contract.
- [ ] At least two adapters (Gerrit + one of GitHub/GitLab) implementing land-request + status-read.
- [ ] The project auto-lander (f1fa) refactored onto the Gerrit adapter with no behaviour change.
- [ ] Driven by a real second-platform need — not built speculatively.
baseline.summary: Platform-agnostic landing provider-seam in rebar core (Gerrit/GitHub/GitLab adapters + portable outcome enum)

# Verifier paths resolve the standard class

## Context / Problem
Three separate code paths pick the verifier model, and all three break off the default provider:
- `review_kernel/verify.py:269` — `verifier_default if model == default_model else (model or
  verifier_default)`. Any non-default model (every Bedrock id) reads as an explicit operator choice,
  so the downgrade silently stops applying.
- `completion.py:332` — `if cfg.model == DEFAULT_MODEL: cfg = replace(cfg, model=...)`. Same inversion,
  separate path.
- `workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — declares no `model:` on any step, so all four code-review passes
  take `cfg.model` and it never downgrades at all. Its Pass-2 pins `temperature: 0` for greedy
  verification, so running it on the frontier model also loses determinism.

## Approach
Replace all three with a single resolution of the `standard` class. The equality test DISAPPEARS rather than being repaired: "the operator chose a verifier" is now expressed by configuring the `standard` slot, not by comparing `cfg.model` to a constant. One mechanism fixes three gates.

**Alternative rejected — fixing the equality rule in place.** It would need a new way to distinguish "operator override" from "provider change" when both arrive as `cfg.model`, and it would have to be repeated on all three paths.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — add `resolve_model_string(value)`: the ONE place that knows the
  reserved class vocabulary. Returns the resolved id for `trivial`/`standard`/`frontier`, and any
  other string UNCHANGED.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `resolve_model` calls it via a LAZY, function-level import. A
  module-level import is IMPOSSIBLE here: `model_classes` imports from `config`, and its docstring
  forbids the reverse. Function-level is the established pattern in this file already
  (`config.py:108`, `:566`, `:768`).
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py` — `resolve_verifier_model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — `_verifier_cfg` (line 46). A consumer the plan had NOT
  enumerated, with two further call sites at `xcheck.py:198` and `xcheck.py:336`.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — the parallel equality test at line 332.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — express the per-pass class as `model: standard`.
- `tests/unit/` — per-path resolution tests.

NOT in scope, and deliberately: the ladder path (`production_batch_runner.py:93`, `code_review/batch_runner.py:55`) is sibling task 7761. Both tickets call the SAME `resolve_model_string`, which is why the vocabulary lives in one function.

## Testing
Contract tier: the observable is which model id each pass resolves to under a given class config.
- each of the FOUR verifier paths resolves the `standard` class: `resolve_verifier_model`,
  `_verifier_cfg`, `completion.py`'s equality test, and code-review.yaml's verify step.
- with classes configured for a non-default provider, none of them falls back to the framework
  default (the regression this ticket exists for).
- code review's Pass-2 resolves `standard`, not `frontier`.
- a literal model id passed to `resolve_model_string` comes back UNCHANGED (the back-compat
  guarantee that keeps every existing workflow YAML working).

## MECHANISM (decided on parent eb58 — corrected; do not re-derive)

**A workflow step names a class by using the class name as its `model:` value.** The three class names are RESERVED VALUES in the EXISTING model-string space — no new `class:` key, no schema change. In YAML: `model: standard`.

**There is NO single interception point.** An earlier version of this plan claimed `config.resolve_model` was "the ONE funnel every step model passes through". That was wrong three ways, all verified in source:

1. `config.py` cannot import `model_classes` at module level — the dependency runs the other way and
   `model_classes`'s own docstring forbids the reverse.
2. `model_ladder` never reaches `resolve_model`: `production_batch_runner.py:93` does
   `dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=req.model_ladder[0])`.
3. The verifier paths never reach it either — `resolve_verifier_model` is its own path, as is
   `_verifier_cfg`.

So the shape is ONE FUNCTION, several CALL SITES:

    model_classes.resolve_model_string(value: str) -> str
        "trivial" | "standard" | "frontier"  ->  resolve via load_class_slots()
        anything else                        ->  return unchanged

This ticket wires the VERIFIER call sites; sibling 7761 wires the LADDER ones. Keeping the vocabulary in one function is what stops those two tickets from drifting apart.

REJECTED — a new `class:` key: forks a step schema `runs.py` documents as closed, and makes `model: standard` vs `class: standard` a silent ambiguity.

REJECTED — resolving at YAML load time: the mapping depends on process-scoped env/CLI layers, so it would freeze the wrong value in a long-lived process and be invisible to `provider_provenance`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts plan-review Pass-2/Pass-4 resolve the `standard` class
- [ ] a test asserts the completion verifier resolves the `standard` class
- [ ] a test asserts code-review's verify step resolves the `standard` class rather than `cfg.model`
- [ ] a test asserts that with classes configured for a non-default provider, no verifier path resolves
      a model belonging to a different provider
- [ ] `grep -rn "== DEFAULT_MODEL" src/rebar/llm/` returns no verifier-selection site

- [ ] a test asserts a workflow step whose `model:` is the literal string `standard` resolves to the
      configured standard class's model id, and that a step whose `model:` is a literal model id
      resolves to that id UNCHANGED (the byte-for-byte back-compat guarantee)
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier resolves the `standard` class REGARDLESS of what
      `cfg.model` is — including when `cfg.model` is a Bedrock id. MEASURED today:
      `resolve_verifier_model` downgrades ONLY on an exact match against the bare `claude-opus-4-8`,
      so even `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` (the SAME model, merely provider-qualified) silently keeps
      Pass-2 on opus. This criterion fails against the current implementation, so it cannot pass
      vacuously
- [ ] a test enumerates the consumers of `resolve_verifier_model` and asserts each resolves the
      standard class — `plan_review/__init__.py:_verifier_cfg` is one the plan had not enumerated
- [ ] a test asserts `resolve_model_string` returns a literal model id UNCHANGED, so existing
      workflow YAML keeps resolving byte-for-byte
- [ ] a test asserts `_verifier_cfg` resolves the standard class, exercised through its real callers
      at `xcheck.py:198` and `xcheck.py:336` rather than in isolation
baseline.summary: Verifier paths resolve the standard class

## Context / Problem

The inbound fetcher can only see one tracker project. `_build_snapshot` resolves a single `query_project` and builds one JQL pair — active and recent-done — from it (`fetcher.py:313-406`), then runs its three enrichment passes — parent, comment, issuelink maps — against that one project key (`fetcher.py:408-560`). A store that lists several projects in its mapping still ingests only one of them, and single-project enrichment would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one. Inbound-created tickets also never record which project they came from, so the `bridge_project`/`repos` fields added by cef7 stay unset on inbound tickets.

## Approach

**Fan out per project (fetcher.py).** Replace the single `query_project` with the store's project SET: `projects_store.read_projects(repo_root).keys()`. For EACH project, issue the existing `jqls_for(project)` pair AND run all three enrichment passes (`get_parent_map` / `get_comment_map` / `get_issuelinks_map`) scoped to that project key, merging every result into the ONE shared `snapshot` dict (deduped by the existing `seen_keys`). This reuses `jqls_for` and `_validate_project_key` unchanged, so bug 626d's JQL-injection guard keeps applying to every key with no new interpolation site, and the per-query truncation ceiling (`_ACLI_CEILING`, raising `SilentTruncationError`) stays scoped per project — a busy project cannot exhaust a shared budget on behalf of the others. When the mapping is unseeded (empty), fall back to the single `[query_project]` list so the exact pre-change query pair and single enrichment pass are issued — single-project behaviour is byte-for-byte untouched.

**Failure semantics across the fan-out.** Base-query exceptions (transport/network, malformed response, `SilentTruncationError`) propagate and fail the whole pass, exactly as today — fanning out multiplies failure points but each is fail-closed, so no partial snapshot is written. The three enrichment passes keep their existing per-pass fail-open degradation (log + continue), applied independently per project; a `BackendPaginationStallError` still re-raises past the handlers (a stalled pager is a truncated read).

**Record source project + default repos (apply_inbound_records.py).** Provenance needs NO new channel through the snapshot: the snapshot is keyed by jira key, `_apply_inbound_create` derives `jira_key = mutation.target`, and the CREATE writer `_inbound_create_write_create_event` ALREADY receives `jira_key` and `repo_root`. The source project IS `jira_key`'s prefix (`DIG-123` → `DIG`, the same `rsplit("-", 1)[0]` idiom the fetcher's parent-key derivation uses). A new leaf helper `projects_store.resolve_inbound_bridge_fields(jira_key, repo_root) -> dict` returns `{"bridge_project": <prefix>, "repos": mapping.projects.get(prefix, {}).get("repos", [])}`; the create site stamps both fields in ONE line — `create_data.update(...)` — beside the existing `creation_channel` stamp (`apply_inbound_records.py:221`). No signature change and no `apply_inbound.py` edit are required, and the net addition to `apply_inbound_records.py` (already 797 LOC, near the 800 cap) is the import + the update call — two lines, staying under the cap.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — fan out the base JQL pair AND all three
  enrichment passes once per configured project into the shared snapshot; per-project ceiling;
  unseeded-mapping fallback to the single configured project.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` — new `resolve_inbound_bridge_fields`
  leaf helper (derive source project from the jira key, default repos from that project's mapping
  entry).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — stamp `bridge_project` + `repos`
  at the CREATE write site via the helper (net +2 lines; module is near the size cap).
- tests under `tests/`.

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful verified fake fed production-shaped Jira fixtures. The fake must RECORD the queries and enrichment calls it issues, because "one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass per project" is itself the contract under test and is invisible to a result-only assertion.

- Happy path: a mapping with two projects issues exactly two JQL pairs and one enrichment pass per
  project (parent/comment/issuelink), and the merged snapshot carries issues AND enrichment data
  from BOTH projects.
- Postcondition: each inbound-created ticket records its source project in `bridge_project` and its
  `repos` equal that project's mapping entry; checked on tickets created from a two-project
  fixture.
- Ceiling is per project: one project exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` raises `SilentTruncationError`
  naming it, while a second under-limit project still ingests — proving the budget is not shared.
- Empty result: a listed project returning zero issues contributes nothing and does not fail the
  pass.
- Single-project regression: an unseeded mapping issues the identical query pair and single
  enrichment pass as before this change; checked by comparing recorded queries/calls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A two-project mapping issues one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink
      maps) per project in a single pass, with both projects' issues and enrichment data present in
      the merged snapshot; checked by a fake transport recording issued queries and enrichment
      calls and asserting the exact per-project counts and contents.
- [x] Each inbound-created ticket records its source project in `bridge_project` and the repos from
      that project's mapping entry in `repos`; checked by asserting both fields on tickets created
      from a two-project fixture.
- [x] The truncation ceiling applies per project, not as a shared budget; checked by a test where
      one project exceeds it (raising `SilentTruncationError`) and a second under-limit project
      still ingests successfully.
- [x] A single-project (unseeded) mapping issues an identical query pair and single enrichment pass
      to the pre-change behaviour; checked by a regression test comparing the recorded
      queries/calls.
- [x] A configured project returning zero issues does not fail the pass; checked by an
      empty-result fixture.
baseline.summary: Multi-project inbound fetch: per-project JQL fan-out and source-project recording

# Child bin-packing for container criteria (pack small children, preserve single-child fallback)

## Why
After merge, the container still makes one call per child. Many children are small — multiple WHOLE children fit
in one call. Packing them reduces calls further, and because G3/G4 are CROSS-CHILD criteria, seeing children
together can IMPROVE consistency detection. Large (parent+child) pairings must keep the single-child path
(ca03 window-fit guarantee).

## What
- Bin-pack whole children into one call up to a token budget = model-window x P8_HEADROOM - output reserve
  (reuse the existing `pair_tokens`/`budget` + P8 machinery). Each child stays WHOLE (never chunked — ca03).
- PRESERVE the single-child path when parent+child strains the window; a child that alone exceeds budget stays
  the existing "too-big -> reduce the ticket" failure finding.
- Structured per-child sections in the prompt + REQUIRED per-child output so per-child attention isn't lost.
- Gate behind an OFFLINE EVAL confirming no per-child attention/accuracy loss vs one-child-per-call.

## Scope
- In: the bin-packer; multi-child container prompt + required per-child output; single-child fallback; the eval.
- Out: merge (S4, dependency); the caching/parallel substrate (S1/S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Small children are packed into one call up to the window budget; each child whole (never chunked).
- [ ] A child whose (parent+child) strains the window keeps its own call; a single child exceeding budget yields
      the too-big failure finding.
- [ ] The prompt requires per-child output; an offline eval shows no per-child attention/accuracy loss vs one-per-call.
- [ ] Container call count drops below N for epics with small children; `make lint` + tests pass.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 5, MINOR 10, BLOCKER 3)
- Bin budget reuses `int(largest_window_tokens * P8_HEADROOM) - P8_OUTPUT_RESERVE_TOKENS` (pass1.py:57-59), summed
  over `parent + ALL packed children`; the single-child fallback (`pair_tokens > budget`) still fires for a lone
  oversized child -> the existing too-big failure finding, unchanged.
- Update the sizing.py container-cost projection for <N calls after packing.
- Fidelity gate = the S6 semantic eval harness (DEPENDS ON S6).
- [ ] Bin budget = parent + all packed children <= P8 window budget; a lone child exceeding it yields the existing
      too-big failure finding; each child whole (never chunked).
- [ ] sizing.py projection reflects the reduced (<N) call count after packing.
- [ ] The S6 fidelity harness shows packed-call findings within tolerance of one-child-per-call.

## CI/eval posture (S6)
- The S6 semantic fidelity eval is a HUMAN-REVIEWED development gate run before merge (live, opt-in), NOT a required/blocking CI check (non-deterministic). The offline eval-spec discipline check still runs on every PR.
baseline.summary: Child bin-packing for container criteria (pack small children, preserve single-child fallback)

`_engine_support/reads.py:133-137` and `:151-157` print to stderr and call `sys.exit(1)` when the repo root is not a git worktree. That function is reached from the library gate surface (`_lib_gates.py:42,68,83,109,118,163,210`) and thence from MCP (`_mcp_reads.py:212,218,224`).

Empirically proven during verification: a real in-memory FastMCP client was driven against a tool that exits this way. FastMCP catches `Exception` (`mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py:116`) and `SystemExit` is a `BaseException`, so the whole `anyio.run` dies — the MCP server PROCESS terminates rather than returning a tool error.

Trigger is narrow (REBAR_ROOT unset with a non-repo cwd, or the repo vanishing mid-session), but a leaf helper unilaterally deciding process lifetime for every embedding surface is the defect. The library contract is to raise `RebarError`.

Both remediation proposers converged: convert to a domain exception and map it to exit 1 at the CLI boundary ONLY, so the CLI's observable behaviour is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tracker_dir()` raises a rebar error instead of calling `sys.exit`
- [x] The CLI maps that error to exit 1 with the same message as today
- [x] A test asserts an MCP tool returns an error payload (not a dead server) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd
- [x] No `sys.exit` remains reachable from `_lib_*` or `_mcp_*`
baseline.summary: Remove sys.exit from the shared read core

## GHA reconcile-bridge-canary: inject signing key + flip committer email to bot

The canary writes non-exempt tickets via the normal `rebar` CLI (`rebar create bug` / `comment` / `transition` in `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`), so it will SIGN AUTOMATICALLY through `_seam.append_event` once the identity + key are configured — no code change needed here (unlike the reconciler). The Rebar Bot identity ticket already exists (task bffe: `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`), so git-email resolution to the bot works.

- **Secure key injection (concrete):** in a workflow step, `echo "::add-mask::$REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY"`
  first (so it can never surface in logs), then write it to a job-local file — e.g.
  `install -m 600 /dev/null "$RUNNER_TEMP/rebar-bot-signing-key"` then
  `printf '%s' "${{ secrets.REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY }}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/rebar-bot-signing-key"`
  (mode 0600) — and export `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` (or set `identity.signing_key`) to that
  path. The runner's `$RUNNER_TEMP` is discarded at job end.
- Set the canary's committer email to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` (from the current bridge
  default) so git-email resolution maps to the Rebar Bot identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` masks the secret (`::add-mask::`), writes it to a `0600` file under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, sets `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`/`identity.signing_key` to that path, and sets the committer email to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`; the key is never logged or committed.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A canary run (post-deploy; triggered via `workflow_dispatch` on `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`) creates a bug/comment/transition whose event is signed as Rebar Bot: capture the created ticket id from the run log and confirm `rebar verify-authorship` (or `rebar verify-identity`) reports it `verified` and attributed to identity `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`.
- [ ] No code change is introduced here (the CLI signs automatically via the seam); the key is never logged or committed.
baseline.summary: GHA reconcile-bridge-canary: inject signing key + flip committer email to bot

baseline.description:
# Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

## Context / Problem

A `/rebar-implement` run of epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` landed five changes through every gate. **The gates performed to their design envelope.** Plan-review blocked infeasible mechanics (a tenacity-transport claim that cannot wrap boto3; an `isinstance` against a botocore-dependent class; a live canary path that would have made billable AWS calls on every CI run). The completion-verifier twice refused a close whose stated criteria had no test. Full-suite pre-flight caught cross-module regressions `tests/unit` missed.

Every one of those catches shares a property: **the ground truth lived in the repo**, where the reviewer's read/grep tools could reach it.

Four escapes got through, and they are one defect wearing different clothes — **a green signal whose measurement could not have observed the failure it claims to rule out**:

1. **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching and model-availability measurements were taken in account
   `579718921998` / `us-east-2` and recorded as settled fact; the project runs in `896586841071` / `us-east-1`
   (named by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`). No gate compares a claim's observation
   context against the project's environment. A human caught it by asking "is that this project's account?"
2. **Instruments that cannot observe the failure — twice, in the same investigation.** This escape is the
   epic's sharpest example precisely because the *first correction was also wrong*.

   **2a.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls validated a *scoped* IAM grant while running under an identity
   holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than production is structurally unable to
   fail, so its success carries **zero information**.

   **2b.** The prescribed remedy — `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against the role — then produced a
   confident, recorded, and **wrong** conclusion: that `bedrock:Converse` was the action to grant. The
   simulator answered exactly the question asked ("would this policy permit the action *named*
   `bedrock:Converse`?", legitimately no, since that action genuinely exists) but **not** the question that
   mattered ("which action does the Converse API actually *check*?"). Only a real call FROM the instance
   revealed the truth — `AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel` — meaning
   the ORIGINAL plan was right and the "fix" broke it, on a role feeding `eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`, a cutover
   with no fallback.

   The pair is the lesson: a wildcard identity could not fail, and a simulator could not fail *for the reason
   that mattered*. **Evidence is only as good as its ability to have come out the other way for the reason
   you care about** — and swapping one instrument for a more rigorous-sounding one does not establish that.
3. **Tests that cannot fail** — the code-side form of the same defect: a contrast case whose discriminating
   conjunct was never exercised, and an oracle asserting on an object where production passes a string.
   **Both WERE caught** (mutation testing; the LLM reviewer) precisely because they are repo-checkable. That
   contrast is the evidence for this epic's thesis.
4. **Confidence outrunning method**: "verified by reading" was a hand-picked grep that missed a dependency;
   "18/18 green" was reported while typecheck was red.

## Why 1 and 2 are structural, not a calibration miss

`verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all. Plan-review runs **before** the evidence exists, so it cannot audit a measurement not yet taken; the completion-verifier accepts `[operator-attested]` evidence **on trust by design** (ADR-0043). One gate cannot audit it, the other is designed not to. The in-flight T5c rewrite pushes grounding toward current code and IaC state but still cannot observe a live cloud account — nothing in the current design can, and nothing should try.

## Approach

Do **not** make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it. Detail lives in the child story; the shape is:

1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and
   privilege posture relative to production.
2. Enforce their **presence** deterministically, zero LLM, mirroring
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (DET-first doctrine).
3. Let an LLM criterion judge the *declaration* against repo facts — once provenance is text, "plan attests
   account X, IaC names account Y" becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**, which is exactly what the
   gate's strongest criteria already do well.
4. Land the generalized rule as an **advisory** criterion per ADR-0054; corpus replay decides promotion.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, recursive — the verifier's
  own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the instrument under
  suspicion.
- **Escape 4 as gate scope.** Reported-green-while-red is *reporting discipline*, already covered by the
  orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success. Filing it as a
  gate gap would be mis-attribution.
- **Wording changes alone.** The contract was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the defect. This is
  the same lesson as epic `9109-2ad9-2477-4cf6` (Serena tool-choice), which is why that epic's structural
  framing is the model here rather than its subject matter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking measurement provenance is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check
      (no LLM) — `det_measurement_provenance.py`, surfaced advisory through `p6_ac_quality`, landed in
      change 1423 with a mutation-tested oracle (breaking the binding rule, placeholder detection or enum
      membership each kills tests)
- [x] the new criterion ships **advisory** (ADR-0054) and rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, leaving the
      shipped default criteria set unchanged for other rebar clients
- [x] an ADR records the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes
- [x] the completion-verifier is NOT made to re-run world measurements — the rejected alternative stays
      rejected, and a test or grep demonstrates it

## Descoped to `98df-3528-9b1f-405a` (ridiculous-expert-mouse), filed as an `idea`

AC-1 originally also required the wrong-account escape to be **reproduced as a regression fixture** from the real `579718921998` vs `896586841071` case. That clause is NOT delivered and is NOT claimed as done.

Reproducing it means exercising the AGENT criterion's rule (a) semantically, which needs an eval corpus (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.eval.yaml`) plus a live run — the same behavioural half descoped from story `f161`. Both moved to `98df`, which also carries the rule (b)/(c)/(d) fixtures and the ADR-0054 corpus-replay false-positive rate that would justify promoting the criterion from advisory.

This epic therefore closes on its MECHANISM being delivered and proven — provenance is now forced into the record as text, deterministically enforced, and judged by a tool-enabled criterion — not on that criterion's firing behaviour having been calibrated. The distinction is safe because the criterion ships **advisory**: it cannot block any claim or close, so an uncalibrated advisory criterion is inert-but-useful rather than risky. Promotion is a separate ADR-0054 decision nobody has committed to, which is why `98df` is an `idea`.
baseline.summary: Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

## Summary

Discovered while proving `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey` (e339-9709-15fe-419a). Independent of that ticket's FIT divergence: under `reconciler.rich_text_cutover = "cloud"` (this project's setting, `rebar.toml:87`) the outbound comment differ decodes the two sides of its body-equality key with DIFFERENT decoders, so a markdown comment WELL WITHIN the length limit never matches its own landed body.

- **Local side** — `_diff_comments` computes `codec.normalize_outbound(...)`. In rich mode
  `AdfCodec.normalize_outbound` is a markdown round trip, which ESCAPES markdown-active
  characters and rewrites autolinks.
- **Jira side** — `_normalize_comment_body` calls `inbound_mapper.normalize_rich_text`
  (`inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` -> `adf_to_text`), which does NOT escape.

## Runtime evidence

Driving the real `AdfCodec(rich=True)` and `_JiraInbound` on current main (worktree `fix-sakimonkey-dedupkey`), with an in-limit markdown body:

```
local key : '# Head\n\nSome *bold* text and a [link](<http://x>) plus `code`.\n\n- a\n- b'
landed key: '# Head\n\nSome *bold* text and a [link](http://x) plus `code`.\n\n- a\n- b'
EQUAL?    : False
```

The same asymmetry escapes the truncation notice: the local key carries `\[truncated by reconciler\]` where the landed body carries `[truncated by reconciler]`.

## Confirmed root cause (Phase 1, worktree fix-17c3)

Reproduced deterministically by capturing the real send path (`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`, only `_run_acli` stubbed): the landed wire is `to_wire(fit_preserving_marker(DECORATED body))`, and because the decoration `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` is an HTML comment, `markdown_to_adf`'s documented content-preservation fallback (`adf.py`, `markdown_to_adf`) degrades the WHOLE document to the plain `text_to_adf` encode. The Jira-side key decodes that wire with `adf_to_text` (no escaping). The local key instead round-trips the UNDECORATED body through `adf_to_markdown(markdown_to_adf(...))` (`outbound_comments.py`, `_diff_comments` `compare_body`), which both escapes markdown-active characters AND renders rich — two divergences from the landed form with one root cause: the two keys are produced by different decode compositions.

## Fix plan (one decoder)

In `_diff_comments`, derive the LOCAL key by predicting the exact wire the send path produces and decoding it with the SAME decoder already used on the fetched Jira side: `_normalize_comment_body(codec.to_wire(_decorate_outbound_comment(sanitizer.fit_comment(body))))` replacing `_normalize_comment_body(codec.normalize_outbound(sanitizer.fit_comment(body)))`. `to_wire` is already part of the `RichTextCodec` Protocol; `_IdentityCodec` grows an identity `to_wire` so the no-codec fallback is unchanged. Send-path behavior is NOT touched — this is key derivation only. Verified at runtime across the 8-cell matrix (cutover off/cloud x {in-limit md, over-length md, plain in-limit, oversize plain}): the new key equals the landed key in every cell; the old key diverges in 3 cloud cells; every cell where the old key already matched still matches (no loosening, no shifted in-limit plain key).

## Testing

- RED test first: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_comment_dedup_key_matches_send_fit.py`
  gains cases under `REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER=cloud` with an in-limit markdown body:
  the landed side CAPTURED from the real `add_comment` (only `_run_acli` stubbed, same pattern
  as the existing tests in that file), asserting `_diff_comments` emits no duplicate mutation
  (RED pre-fix) and that a genuinely new markdown comment is still emitted (counter-regression).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/ tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_dc_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`
- `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (no new/increased entries)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The differ's two comparison keys are produced by the same decode under every
      `rich_text_cutover` setting — verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_comment_dedup_key_matches_send_fit.py -q`.
- [x] A test drives an in-limit markdown comment through the differ with the cutover ON and
      asserts no duplicate mutation is emitted (RED on current code) — checked: run the new
      test at the pre-fix commit and observe the failure, then GREEN post-fix.
baseline.summary: Cloud comment dedup key is markdown-escaped on one side only

## Problem
An MCP `review_plan_start` job for ticket `unadhesive-erectable-axolotl` changed from `running` to `stale-running` without writing a readable `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar or a plan-review attestation.

## Observed
- Date: 2026-09-04.
- Job: `1788538783977524160-fd43d54af972425e89d256830684fdf6`.
- Initial `review_plan_start` returned a normal running handle.
- The first `gate_status` poll reported `running`, `findings.readable=false`, and an unsigned durable result.
- The next poll reported `stale-running`, `findings.reason=run-stale-running`, and no signature.
- An immediately preceding review job on the same ticket completed normally with a structural BLOCK.

## Expected
The async daemon records a terminal PASS/BLOCK/ERROR result and readable diagnostic evidence, or the MCP surface returns an actionable cause for the daemon death.

## Reproduction
Edit a plan after a structural plan-review BLOCK, call `review_plan_start` again for `origin/main`, and poll the returned job with `gate_status`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The daemon-death cause is reproducible or identified from durable evidence.
- [ ] A stale async gate records an actionable terminal error or recoverable diagnostic evidence.
- [ ] Regression coverage exercises the stale-running path without a billable external model call.

## Context
Change 1855 patchset 2 CI run 32130591202, Ubuntu Python 3.12 job 95691543683, passed 13,821 tests and then errored in `test_ledger_attribution_is_unchanged_by_the_batching`. The fixture diagnostics added by prior bug `warmthless-dermal-oropendola` captured the first actionable recurrence: `git merge -q --no-edit side` failed rc=128 because blob `66842fd006b2fdc95ff55a33a263f1cb216bc7d6` referenced by `1005-cccc2222-COMMENT.json` was missing. `git fsck --full` reported the same missing blob; `.git/objects/pack/tmp_pack_53R4Hl` existed with size 0. The current Gerrit patch only changes the Anthropic test isolation subprocess and does not touch this fixture or Git object operations.

## Plan
Run the full chronic-issue rebar-debug protocol with independent code-tracer, historical, and empirical investigators. Reproduce or deterministically force the object-loss mechanism, discriminate concurrent Git maintenance/repack from fixture logic and filesystem/environment causes, record a proven runtime RCA, then design a held-out RED oracle at the real Git seam. Only after the cause is proven, implement the smallest class-level repair, verify RED→GREEN with exact-defect mutation, run the affected fixture under CI-parity xdist stress, and sweep sibling Git-fixture operations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The exact missing-blob/tmp-pack failure is explained by a runtime-confirmed, cited mechanism.
- [ ] Competing fixture-content, hook, ref-resolution, environment, and filesystem hypotheses are explicitly confirmed or rejected.
- [ ] A held-out test deterministically fails through the real Git object-store seam before the repair and passes after it.
- [ ] Reintroducing the exact confirmed defect returns the held-out test to RED.
- [ ] The original authorship fixture passes under CI-parity xdist stress without weakening its ledger-attribution assertions.
- [ ] Sibling instances of the confirmed Git-operation pattern are swept and dispositioned.
- [ ] The final RCA, proof, scope/safety audit, and replication evidence are recorded on this ticket.
