Mirror inventory finding F11 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), LOW.

## Problem

- `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` `ROUTES` — the live route names
- `src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py:22` `_CROSS_SESSION_WARN_COMMANDS` — 14 hardcoded SPELLINGS, used at `:74`

All 14 are live route names today, so this is preventive. A route RENAME silently drops the warning: `:74` is `if name not in _CROSS_SESSION_WARN_COMMANDS`, so a stale spelling simply never matches and the cross-session warning disappears with nothing failing.

## Scope — what is and is not the mirror (epic AC2)

WHICH verbs warn cross-session is a DISTINCT CONCEPT: a policy subset, the same shape that makes `_NOT_CLAIMABLE_STATUSES` not a mirror. This ticket does not touch that judgement and must not change which commands warn.

The mirror is ONLY the SPELLINGS, which must be route names and are not enforced to be. This is the one CLI policy subset not folded into `derive_policy_sets` (`_registry.py:680`), where every other such subset already lives.

## Approach — add-route-flag

Give `Route` a `warn_cross_session` flag, set it on those 14 routes, and fold the set into `derive_policy_sets` beside its siblings. The spellings then ARE route names by construction, and a rename carries the flag automatically.

## The census test this change must update

`derive_policy_sets` has a key census that is pinned exactly: `tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py:81` asserts `set(derived) == set(_CENSUS_SETS)` against the hardcoded 17-name `_CENSUS_SETS` tuple at `:28`. Adding a derived key makes that assertion fail until the tuple names it, so this change MUST update that test — it is declared in `file_impact` for exactly that reason, and leaving it out is what would make the close gate refuse the ticket for going beyond the reviewed plan.

The new key is an OVERLAY set (its members already appear in a base set, like `_CONFIRM_SCOPE` and `_LEGACY_OUTPUT`), so it also belongs in the skip list inside `_all_current_spellings` (`:74`), which would otherwise double-count its members in the spelling census.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: the warn set is derived from `ROUTES` via `derive_policy_sets`; `_execute.py` no longer
      carries a spelling list. Verified by a test asserting the derived set is used and the literal
      is gone.
- [x] AC2: the membership is UNCHANGED — exactly the same 14 commands warn. Verified by a test
      pinning the derived set against the 14 names the literal carried, so the refactor cannot
      quietly change policy.
- [x] AC3: every warn-flagged name is a live route name. Verified by a test asserting the derived
      set is a subset of live `ROUTES` names, which is the property a hardcoded list could violate.
- [x] AC4: renaming a route carries its warning. Verified by a test that renames a flagged route in
      a synthetic registry and asserts the derived set follows the new name.
- [x] AC5: the `derive_policy_sets` key census still passes. Verified by
      `test_derive_covers_exactly_the_census_set_names` being green with the new key named in
      `_CENSUS_SETS`, and by the spelling census not double-counting the overlay members.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "registry or execute or cross_session or policy" -q` — AC1-AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Validate _CROSS_SESSION_WARN_COMMANDS spellings against ROUTES, or add a route flag (mirror F11)

baseline.description:
# Prompt caching writes on every gate call and is never read across calls: the marked prefix is not stable

## Observed — measured, with a control

Two `rebar review-plan` runs executed BACK TO BACK, seconds apart, well inside the ~5-minute cache TTL, on two DIFFERENT tickets (1c39 then 9baf), with REBAR_USAGE_LOG capturing every call. All calls on Bedrock via the project default. Per-call figures:

    pass                                RUN A in / write        RUN B in / write        RUN B read
    plan-reviewer (frontier/opus)        5286 / 2800             5394 / 2908             0
    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier    3809 / 1545             3872 / 1608             0
    plan-review-verifier                 7136 / 4871             7199 / 4934             0
    plan-review-coach                    1999 / 0                2062 / 0                0
    ticket-digest (trivial/haiku)        2131 / 0                2816 / 0                0
    TOTALS                               write 9216, read 0      write 9450, read 0

RUN B WROTE THE CACHE AGAIN INSTEAD OF READING IT. Every read is zero in both runs.

## The mechanism this points at

Each pass's cache-WRITE size tracks its input size almost exactly across the two runs (plan-reviewer 5286 -> 5394 input, 2800 -> 2908 write; verifier 7136 -> 7199 input, 4871 -> 4934 write). A cache prefix that were genuinely stable would produce the SAME marked prefix and therefore a hit on the second run. That the write grows in step with per-ticket input says the MARKED PREFIX ITSELF VARIES PER CALL — i.e. per-ticket content is landing ahead of the cache breakpoint, so the cache key is unique every time and can never be reused.

`capabilities.cache_settings_for` marks the INSTRUCTIONS plus tool definitions, and `structured_run.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` derives the marked size from the SYSTEM PROMPT. So the hypothesis to test first is that the rendered system prompt/instructions embed per-ticket material (the plan text, the ticket digest, or similar) rather than being invariant across runs.

## What is NOT the explanation — ruled out by evidence

* NOT "caching is off on Bedrock". Three of five passes write thousands of tokens per run, so the
  settings are emitted and the provider accepts them.
* NOT "the read path is broken". Intra-CALL reuse demonstrably works: the production review bot's
  multi-step agentic records read large caches within a single call — e.g. a code-review pass with
  steps=9/125 logged cache_read=386204 against in=430479, and another with steps=17/125 logged
  cache_read=493547. Those are steps 2..N reusing what step 1 wrote inside one conversation.
* NOT the sub-minimum-prefix condition for the three writing passes. That condition explains the
  two passes that write ZERO — coach (whole prompt small) and ticket-digest, where the diagnostic
  fired verbatim: "only 477 tokens sit ahead of the cache breakpoint, below this model's
  4096-token minimum, while 8634 of the 9111 billed input tokens ride AFTER it unmarked". It does
  not explain a pass that writes 4871 tokens and then never reads them.

## Why it costs money rather than being merely untidy

A cache write is billed at a PREMIUM over ordinary input; a read is billed at a steep discount. The current behaviour pays the premium on every gate call and collects the discount only within a single multi-step call. For single-step passes — which is every pass in a plan review, all five records show requests=1 — the write is pure loss: nothing ever reads it. Every plan review on this project pays roughly 9,000-11,000 premium-rate cache-write tokens for zero benefit.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` `cache_settings_for` — where the breakpoints are placed.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` and the ineffective-cache
  diagnostic — the estimate is the instrument that would have caught this and did not.
- whatever renders the plan-review system prompt / instructions, if that is where per-ticket
  content is crossing the breakpoint.

## Approach — investigate before changing anything

The first task is NOT a fix, it is to identify precisely which bytes sit ahead of the breakpoint and whether they vary per run. Capture the rendered system prompt for the same pass on two different tickets and diff them; the varying region is the defect's location. Only then decide whether the fix is to move per-ticket content behind the breakpoint (into the user message) or to split the instructions into an invariant prefix and a per-run suffix.

Do NOT "fix" this by disabling caching on single-step passes: that trades a real, measurable premium for giving up the cross-call discount entirely, and the cross-call discount is the larger prize once the prefix is stable. Note also that the existing diagnostic's advice — "the changeable thing is where the breakpoint sits, not the size of the prompt" — is exactly right here and was never triggered for the writing passes, so consider whether the predicate should also flag "wrote every call, never read".

## Testing

- an oracle that renders the same pass's marked prefix for two different tickets and asserts they
  are BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is the RED test: it should fail today. Verify RED before any fix.
- a live two-run oracle (the experiment above) asserting cache_read > 0 on the second run for at
  least the frontier pass, run inside the TTL.
- a guard that the ineffective-cache diagnostic fires when a pass writes on every call and never
  reads, so this class cannot recur silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the bytes that vary ahead of the cache breakpoint are identified and cited, with a diff of
      the rendered marked prefix for one pass across two different tickets.
- [x] the marked prefix for a given pass is byte-identical across tickets, pinned by a test
      verified RED against today's behaviour.
- [x] a second run of the same pass inside the cache TTL records cache_read > 0, evidenced by an
      actual usage-log capture rather than by inspection.
- [x] the diagnostic in `structured_run` also flags the write-every-call-never-read shape, so a
      regression is loud.
- [x] the cost change is stated with figures — premium-rate write tokens per review before and
      after — so the benefit is measured rather than asserted.
baseline.summary: Prompt cache is written on every call and never read across calls: the marked prefix varies per ticket

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:42` sets `BUGFIX_SIZE_THRESHOLD_NON_TEST_LINES = 150`. On Gerrit only, a change whose trailer resolves to a `bug` and whose diff exceeds 150 non-test lines must carry an acceptable plan-review attestation or the bot votes `LLM-Review -1` (`bugfix_size_gate.py:248-322`; docs `docs/plan-review-gate.md:1058`). A fix at or under the floor is never asked for a plan.

Measured by `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main` (all of `origin/main`):

- 644 bug-fix commits; 105 over the floor = 16.3% escalation.
- "This fix later introduced a bug" is labellable from the store's `caused_by` field (aggregated by `bug_trends.caused_by_fan_in`): 22 of the 644 name one.
- Size floor catches 10 of 22. Repeat-fix signal (a non-test file touched by >=2 other bug-fix commits on the base branch in the prior 7 days) catches 12 of 22 at 34.8% escalation (224/644). Union: 14 of 22 at 39.0%.
- Under the floor today: `8d862d1058` (bug `7084-4e33-e698-42dd`) is 127 non-test lines.

Pure git history plus ticket type — no path lists, no CI provider required (portability).

## Approach
New module `src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py`: `REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS = 7`, `REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR = 2`, `repeat_fix_escalates(paths, *, repo_root, base_ref, at) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]` (verdict + the priors the teaching finding names). Per non-test path it walks `git log --no-merges --since/--until <path>` on the base branch, counting commits whose message resolves to a `bug` ticket.

`apply_bugfix_size_gate` gains this order, which preserves the other pinned exemptions: (1) extract non-test paths, empty -> return with no reads; (2) escalate if `non_test_lines > 150` OR `repeat_fix_escalates(...)`, else return; (3) resolve ticket, require `ticket_type == "bug"`, classify attestation — unchanged.

## Constraints
- **The `review-plan` mirror is a no-op; NOT in scope.** `orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:191-211`) already returns True for a bug whose `file_impact` names ANY non-test path, which every repeat-fix bug does. The only bugs a mirror could newly escalate have empty/test-only `file_impact`, where the predicate cannot fire either. Its call sites `orchestrator.py:245` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:127` stay unchanged; the docs edit records this so it is not re-proposed.
- **A pinned invariant changes deliberately.** `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:304` (`test_under_threshold_diff_never_reads_the_store`) patches `ticket_for_commit_message`, `_load_ticket_state`, `classify_plan_review_attestation` to raise and asserts an under-floor diff leaves the verdict untouched — but the predicate must run on under-floor diffs. Rewrite it to the surviving invariant: an under-floor diff with no non-test files, or no repeat-fix hit, performs no attestation classification. `test_test_only_diff_is_exempt_even_when_huge` (`:320`) must pass unchanged.
- **`flagged` keeps meaning the size floor alone.** `--check-planning-corpus` (`scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py:180-191`) asserts the flagged set equals `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE` exactly, so the repeat-fix verdict is a NEW field beside `flagged`, never folded into it.
- **Additive coverage keys only.** `coverage["bugfix_size_gate"]` gains `escalation_reason` (`size`/`repeat-fix`/`size+repeat-fix`) and `repeat_fix_priors` as NEW keys, so the consumers need no edit: `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py:202-215` (imports `bucket_for_verdict`, `classify_plan_review_attestation`, `ticket_for_commit_message` by name) and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:345-347`.
- **Reuse the resolver.** Commit->ticket resolution exists at `bugfix_size_gate.py:138-151` and `metrics/blame.py:171`; call the former, do not add a third copy.
- **Patchable by name.** Reach the predicate through a module-level name in `bugfix_size_gate`, so the existing string-keyed `monkeypatch.setattr(bsg, "<name>", ...)` sites (`test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:210-224`, `:308-310`, no `raising=False`) can neutralise it.
- **Ratchets / fail-open.** `apply_bugfix_size_gate` scores C901 9 of 15 and the module is 322 of 800 lines, so extract the predicate evaluation into a helper. A git failure yields no escalation and no exception.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py` (new); `bugfix_size_gate.py`; `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` (add `--repeat-fix` and `--labels-from-caused-by`, importing the shipped predicate so the script cannot drift); `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (the section at `:1058` — there is no "escalation section" in that file); `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py`; `tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py` (new).

Reviewed, NOT changed: `orchestrator.py`, `workflow_ops.py`, `review_bot/retrigger.py`, `code_review/finalize.py`, `metrics/blame.py`.

## Testing
Fixture repo built in-test, not this repo's history. Escalates: two prior bug-trailer commits inside 7 days on a 20-line fix. Does not: one prior fix; two 8 days back; priors resolving to a non-bug ticket or to nothing; merge commits; a test-only diff (which also reads nothing). The floor still escalates alone; a git failure fails open.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Predicate + parameters ship in their own module. `grep -c "^REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS\|^REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR\|^def repeat_fix_escalates" src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py` prints `3` (anchored to the three DEFINITIONS; unanchored also counts their uses). Today the file is absent (exit 2).
- [x] New unit tests pass. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py -q` exits 0. Today pytest exits 4.
- [x] An under-floor repeat-fix is escalated. `tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py::test_repeat_fix_escalates_an_under_floor_bug_fix` asserts `verdict["coverage"]["bugfix_size_gate"]["escalation_reason"] == "repeat-fix"`. Today an under-floor diff writes no `coverage` entry (`bugfix_size_gate.py:262-263`).
- [x] Existing gate behaviour preserved. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py tests/unit/test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py -q` exits 0 (pinning; passes today, with the one test rewritten as above).
- [x] Backtest emits the repeat-fix verdict from the shipped predicate. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range HEAD~200..HEAD --repeat-fix --out /tmp/bt.json` exits 0 and `python -c "import json; c=json.load(open('/tmp/bt.json'))['commits']; assert c and all('repeat_fix' in r for r in c)"` exits 0. Today `--repeat-fix` is unrecognised (exit 2) and rows carry only `commit`/`ticket`/`non_test_lines`/`flagged`.
- [x] Backtest labels from the store and reports recall per predicate. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main --repeat-fix --labels-from-caused-by --out /tmp/bt_full.json` exits 0 and prints labelled-recall + escalation rate per predicate (2026-08-21: 22 labelled; floor 10/22 at 16.3%, repeat-fix 12/22 at 34.8%, union 14/22 at 39.0%). Today `--labels-from-caused-by` is unrecognised (exit 2). The command recomputes its own figures, so the criterion is that the summary exists and its floor row reconciles, not that the digits are frozen.
- [x] `flagged` still means the floor alone. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` reports `missed=[]; mechanical_fp=[]` — the flagged set is still exactly `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE`, which is the guard. Its other arm, `corpus=114 (want 113)` (exit 1), is a PRE-EXISTING drift reproduced unchanged on pristine `origin/main`; tracked separately, out of scope.
- [x] Docs record the predicate and why `review-plan` is not mirrored. `grep -c "repeat-fix" docs/plan-review-gate.md` prints >= `2`. Today `0`.
baseline.summary: Escalate repeat fixes to plan review: a file bug-fixed twice in the prior 7 days

baseline.description:
Remove the dead `SupportsIncremental` capability and its false docstring, so the reconciler backend port stops asserting a dispatch behaviour that does not exist.

## Context / Problem

`SupportsIncremental` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:545-553`) is a `@runtime_checkable` capability Protocol whose docstring asserts, in the present tense, a behaviour that is not implemented:

> Core uses an incremental fetch only when ``isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)``;
> otherwise it falls back to a full scan.

It has **zero implementers** and **zero dispatch**: no adapter defines `search_incremental`, and no `isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)` check exists anywhere in `src/` (confirmed by `grep -rn "SupportsIncremental" src/` — the only hits are the class itself and the module-docstring inventory at `_backend.py:11-19`). A tested, documented, maintained capability that is never invoked is a false-assurance signal: a reader auditing the backend port finds a "core uses this" promise the code never keeps.

This is the same defect class the sibling ticket `723f-c5b2-d83b-43cb` (closed, this epic) resolved — a docstring that "actively lies" about a zero-caller unit — and it resolved it by **deleting** the dead unit. No consumer needs an incremental fetch: the three tickets that `depends_on` this one (`0743`, `373f`, `fc0c`) are unrelated janitor items, and the reconciler's full-scan fetch (`fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot`) is the only fetch path in use.

## Approach

**Delete the dead declaration** so reality (a backend port with no incremental fetch) no longer needs a claim that contradicts it. This is the minimal, correctness-neutral remedy for a false-assurance finding and matches the epic's established handling of the identical defect class (`723f` deleted `bug_close_reason_ok` and the dead `_attestation` module). Because the capability has no dispatch and no implementers, removing it changes **no** externally observable reconciler behaviour — the full scan already runs unconditionally.

Two negative tests reference the Protocol and must be disposed of; both are safe to remove (removal-rationale, Chesterton's Fence):

- `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected`
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py:68-69`) guards that the isinstance
  **skip branch** detects a backend lacking a capability. Triggering scenario the fence protects:
  a backend that declines a capability must not be driven through it. That scenario stays covered
  after removal by `FakeBackend` declining `SupportsLinks` — `test_fake_backend_does_not_advertise_links`
  (`:33-34`) and `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability` (`:42-48`) exercise
  the same skip branch — so deleting the incremental-specific case drops **no unique** coverage.
- `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental`
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:85-89`) carries an explicit
  intent marker: its docstring says the assertion exists "to stop it being added by accident."
  With the `SupportsIncremental` Protocol itself removed, there is no capability to accidentally
  opt into, so the fence's purpose is fully subsumed by the deletion; the design rationale it
  recorded (no client need, and incremental fetch has its own correctness surface) is preserved in
  this ticket and in the ADR 0035 amendment below.

ADR 0035 names `SupportsIncremental` in exactly one place — the opt-in-capability prose paragraph `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md:191-195`, with the symbol on `:192` ("`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`"). That paragraph and the summary at `:259` also assert a "**three** opt-in capability Protocols" **count**, which becomes two once the capability is removed. ADRs are durable records, so this is an **amendment**, not a text deletion, using the repo's established `> **AMENDED by [rebar:<id>]**` convention already present in that file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — delete the `SupportsIncremental` class
  (`:545-553`) and drop `:class:\`SupportsIncremental\`` from the module-docstring opt-in inventory
  (`:11-19`), leaving `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py` — remove the `SupportsIncremental`
  import (`:16`) and delete `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` (`:68-69`); retain the
  `SupportsLinks` skip-path tests unchanged.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` — remove the
  `SupportsIncremental` import (`:35`) and delete `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental`
  (`:85-89`); retain `test_dc_backend_advertises_its_three_capabilities` (`:78-82`) unchanged.
- `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` — amend the opt-in-capability paragraph
  (`:191-195`, symbol at `:192`) and the "three ... capability Protocols" count at `:191` and
  `:259` via the `> **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]**` convention.

No adapter or fetcher file is touched: there is nothing to implement.

## Testing

This is a dead-code removal that adds no new runtime behaviour, so the verification is a regression check plus a coverage-preservation check, both at the in-process unit tier against the real Protocols and backends:

- **Regression oracle.** After the edits, the reconciler capability suite is green:
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`
  collects and passes with the two deleted tests gone and no import error for the removed symbol.
- **Coverage-preservation oracle (the fence).** `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability`
  still collects and passes, proving the isinstance skip branch — a backend declining a capability
  is not driven through it — remains covered by the retained `SupportsLinks` negative case.
- **Absence oracle.** `grep -rq "SupportsIncremental" src/ tests/` exits non-zero, proving the
  declaration and every test reference are gone (the only surviving reference is the amended ADR
  prose under `docs/`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `SupportsIncremental` class is removed from `_backend.py`
      (verified: `grep -rq "class SupportsIncremental" src/` exits non-zero — no match).
- [x] The `_backend.py` module-docstring opt-in-capability inventory (`:11-19`) no longer names
      `SupportsIncremental` and lists only `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments`
      (verified by reading the docstring).
- [x] `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` and the `SupportsIncremental` import are
      removed from `test_backend_capability.py`, and the retained skip-path tests
      `test_fake_backend_does_not_advertise_links` and
      `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability` still pass
      (verified: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py` is green).
- [x] `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental` and the `SupportsIncremental` import are
      removed from `test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`, and
      `test_dc_backend_advertises_its_three_capabilities` still passes
      (verified: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` is green).
- [x] ADR 0035's opt-in-capability paragraph (`:191-195`, symbol at `:192`) and its "three ...
      capability Protocols" count at `:191` and `:259` are amended via the
      `> **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]**` convention to record that `SupportsIncremental`
      was removed as a zero-implementer, unwired capability (count now two), with a one-line note
      that an updated-since fetch can be reintroduced from vendor support (Jira JQL `updated >`,
      GitHub `since=`, Linear `updatedAt`) if a measured bandwidth need later arises
      (verified by reading the amended ADR).
- [x] No reference to `SupportsIncremental` remains in `src/` or `tests/`
      (verified: `grep -rq "SupportsIncremental" src/ tests/` exits non-zero — no match; the only
      surviving reference is the amended ADR under `docs/`).
baseline.summary: Remove the dead SupportsIncremental capability (zero implementers, false docstring)

baseline.description:
RISK 3 (worst single unit). `reconcile_once()` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py:556-1315` is a ~760-LOC monolith coupling snapshot-load -> diff -> apply -> persist -> log plus corrupt-snapshot abort + OM->Mutation conversion. It is stable (not actively breaking) but untestable per-phase and the highest-touch reconciler file. Decompose IN-PLACE (the natural sub-blocks are below the 100-LOC file floor, so the module-size policy prescribes in-file helpers, NOT a new module).

## Why
No sub-phase can be tested or reused without invoking the whole orchestrator; 5-deep nested error handling lives in the spine. `_apply_batch` in applier.py (handled in the sibling Risk-2b ticket) is the related deep function.

## What — in-place helper extraction along existing seams
- Extract `_load_snapshots()`, `_run_differs()`, `_apply_mutations()`, `_persist_and_log()` as module-level (in-file) helpers; keep `reconcile_once()` as a thin sequencer that calls them in order.
- Lift `_handle_corrupt_snapshot()` out of the spine into its own helper.
- Preserve the single-pass IDEMPOTENT contract and the corrupt-snapshot abort semantics exactly.

## Scope
In: behavior-preserving in-place decomposition + per-phase unit tests now made possible. Out: creating a new file (sub-blocks are <100 LOC), changing the reconcile contract, touching the acli subprocess boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `reconcile_once()` body is a thin sequencer; the four phases + corrupt-snapshot handler are separate in-file helpers.
- [ ] At least the load/persist phases gain direct unit tests (previously impossible).
- [ ] reconcile.py stays in the allowlist if still >800, but `reconcile_once` itself is materially shorter and max nesting drops.
- [ ] Full reconcile idempotency + corrupt-snapshot-abort tests pass byte-for-byte.
baseline.summary: Risk 3: decompose reconcile_once() into in-place phase helpers

baseline.description:
# Land dependabot PRs #123 (actions bumps) and #124 (mcp 2.0 + ruff 0.16.1) through Gerrit

## Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot still opens PRs there (#123, #124), but they can never merge — the updates have to be re-landed as Gerrit changes and the PRs closed by hand. Two are open now:

* **PR #123 — github-actions group**: `actions/setup-python` 6 -> 7 (new pinned SHA
  `5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97`) across 13 workflow files, plus a re-pin of
  `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` v1.14.0 to SHA `dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33`
  (upstream re-tag; version unchanged). The change also updates the two `echo` allowlist
  lines (the pinned-action identity allowlist) that mirror those SHAs.
* **PR #124 — uv-lock group**: `mcp` 1.29.0 -> **2.0.0 (major)** — pyproject constraint
  loosened `>=1.28.1,<2` -> `<3` in both the `mcp` extra and the dev group, new transitive
  `mcp-types` package in `uv.lock` — and `ruff` `0.15.22` -> `0.16.1` (pinned in the dev
  group; ruff is what `make lint` and the pre-commit hook run).

The mcp major is the risk: `rebar-mcp` imports v1 API paths — `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` (mcp_server.py:570, scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:72), `mcp.server.auth.settings` / `mcp.server.auth.provider` (mcp_server.py:590, _mcp_auth.py:38), `mcp.server.transport_security` (mcp_server.py:512), `mcp.types.ToolAnnotations` (_mcp_models.py:287). Whether 2.0 keeps these paths as compat shims is exactly what the test suite must decide; the upstream migration guide lists every breaking change.

**P0 escalation (2026-08-02):** CI's gating `pip-audit` scan (\`_build-and-test.yml\` `pip-audit` job — part of every `Verified` run) now fails on **click 8.2.1 → PYSEC-2026-2132** (command injection in `click.edit()`; fix 8.3.3), which neither dependabot PR covers (click is a transitive-only dependency — not constrained in pyproject.toml, pinned only in `uv.lock`). Because the scan gates every Verified run, EVERY change is blocked until the fixed lock lands — so this ticket gains a Change 0 that must land FIRST. Change 0's own Verified run scans Change 0's own committed lock, so it can pass while everything else cannot; there is no circular block.

## What — three independently reviewable Gerrit changes

### Change 0 (P0, lands first) — click 8.3.3 lock bump

In the worktree: `uv lock --upgrade-package click` (expect click 8.2.1 -> >=8.3.3 in `uv.lock` only; pyproject.toml is untouched since click is transitive), `uv sync --all-extras`, then `pip-audit --desc` locally (must report no known vulnerabilities) and the targeted suite for the CLI surface that consumes click plus `make lint` / `make typecheck`. Push, wait for both votes (its Verified run proves the unblock), Submit.

All changes carry this ticket's trailer and land through the normal gate (`LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, then Submit). Apply each PR's diff verbatim (`gh pr diff N | git apply`), never retyped by hand, so the landed content is byte-identical to what dependabot proposed (SHA pins included).

### Change A — PR #123 (workflows)

Apply `/tmp`-fetched `gh pr diff 123` onto a fresh worktree at current main. 13 workflow files + the allowlist echo lines. No source code is touched; the `Verified` CI run on the Gerrit change itself exercises the bumped `setup-python@v7` on every job that uses it — that run IS the functional validation. Risk note: setup-python v7 migrated to ESM and requires a node24 runner (ubuntu-latest provides it); no inputs we use were removed (we do not pass `pip-install`).

### Change B — PR #124 (mcp 2.0 + ruff 0.16.1)

The `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` constraint has two consumers OUTSIDE pyproject.toml that PR #124's diff does not touch and this change must keep coherent:

* `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:105` installs `'mcp>=1.28.1,<2'` into a clean venv
  for the MCP-optionality job — on path 1 bump it to `,<3` in the same change (else CI
  exercises v1 while the package ships v2); on path 2 it stays `<2`, matching the kept
  pin.
* `docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md:28` records the `<2` pin and its
  rationale (DNS-rebinding fix GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f) — on path 1 amend the ADR text with
  a dated note that the ceiling moved to `<3` (the floor still covers the GHSA); on
  path 2 it stays accurate as written.

Apply `gh pr diff 124` (pyproject.toml + uv.lock) onto a fresh worktree, `uv sync --all-extras`, then decide on evidence:

1. **Compat shims hold** (expected path): the full test suite (`make test` — the MCP
   surface that imports the at-risk v1 paths is covered by
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp*.py` — nine modules incl. `test_mcp.py`,
   `test_mcp_http_transport.py`, and the five `test_mcp_auth*` modules — plus
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_workflow_mcp_schema.py`), `make
   lint` (now ruff 0.16.1), and `make typecheck` all pass — possibly after mechanical
   fixes (new ruff rules, import-path renames with 1:1 replacements, updated
   deprecation-warning filters). Mechanical fixes ride in the same change.
2. **Breakage is structural** (FastMCP/auth API gone or semantics changed): do NOT force
   the major through this ticket. Land the safe subset instead — ruff 0.16.1 bump +
   `uv.lock` refresh with mcp kept `<2` — comment the evidence (failing test names,
   import errors) on this ticket, and file a follow-up ticket for the mcp v2 migration
   linked `discovered_from` this one; PR #124 is then closed with a comment pointing at
   the landed subset + follow-up.

`ruff format --check` may newly fail on files 0.16.x formats differently; run `.venv/bin/ruff format src/ tests/ scripts/` and include the mechanical reformat in the change if so (it is what every subsequent commit's pre-commit hook will enforce).

### Closing the PRs

After each Gerrit change merges: `gh pr close <N> --comment "<landed as Gerrit change <url>; GitHub is a read-only mirror>"`. Dependabot sees the manifest change on the next mirror sync and stops re-opening.

## Scope

* IN: the two PR diffs, mechanical fixes needed to keep the gates green under the bumped
  ruff/mcp, closing PRs #123/#124 with provenance comments.
* OUT: any non-mechanical mcp v2 migration work (follow-up ticket if path 2 triggers);
  dependabot config changes; other open dependency updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC0 (P0): a Gerrit change bumping click to >=8.3.3 in uv.lock is merged FIRST; its CI run's pip-audit step passes (PYSEC-2026-2132 cleared), unblocking all other changes.
- [ ] AC1: A Gerrit change with PR #123's diff (13 workflows + allowlist echo lines,

## Problem

When a ticket description exceeds the 8,000-character plan-review admission limit, the only remediation offered is **decomposition**. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:347-350`:

```python
"suggested_fix": (
    f"Reduce the description to at most {desc_limit} characters, usually by splitting "
    "independent work into coherent child tickets."
),
```

That is the right advice when the **work** is too large. It is the wrong first advice when the **prose** is too large, which is the more common cause — and an author who follows it fragments a coherent unit of work for a reason that has nothing to do with its scope.

## Evidence

Measured on `darkish-enormous-raptors` (`76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5`), which hit the limit:

```
description at rejection : 7989 chars — 14 acceptance criteria, 105 lines of narrative prose
after rewriting prose out: 4440 chars — ALL 14 criteria retained, plus 9 required provenance lines
headroom under the limit : 3560 chars (44% spare)
```

**Nothing needed splitting.** The unit of work was one coherent cleanup with fourteen criteria. What exceeded the limit was method discussion, rationale, and conversational progression that belonged in ticket comments. Removing none of the commitments and none of the evidence — only relocating the narration — left 44% headroom.

Had the author followed the suggested fix literally, they would have split a single cleanup into child tickets to solve a formatting problem.

At least **two independent sessions hit this limit on 2026-08-20**, and both independently arrived at the same unsuggested remedy: move the narrative into a comment. Two sessions rediscovering the same fix that the message does not mention is the signal.

## Why this is a coaching defect and NOT a limit defect

Stated plainly, because this ticket replaces an earlier one of mine (`piecemeal-batiste-greatargus`, closed `not_a_bug`) that got this wrong:

**8,000 characters is ample for one ticket's worth of work** — roughly 1,200 words. A plan that cannot state its problem and its acceptance criteria in that space is either describing more than one unit of work or is padded. The limit is correct and should not move. The formatting requirements that share the budget (`provenance:` continuation lines) are also correct and fit comfortably.

The gap is that the message names one cause of over-length and one remedy, when there are two distinct causes with different remedies, and the more common one is unaddressed.

## Direction (not a prescription)

Distinguish the two cases and coach accordingly. The signal is already available: this same function computes `oversize signals` separately from `description_over_limit`, and its OTHER branch already suggests G5 decomposition for genuinely large units. So decomposition advice already has a home; the over-limit branch could instead coach on authoring:

- prefer concise language over narration;
- move conversational progression, method discussion, and rationale into ticket **comments** or a
  **session log** — the description carries the plan and its acceptance criteria;
- follow the packaged authoring guidance (`rebar explain plan`,
  `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`);
- and only split when the WORK is genuinely more than one unit — pointing at the oversize-signal
  branch rather than conflating the two.

Whether to keep any mention of splitting in this branch is a judgement call for the implementer; the defensible minimum is that it stops being the *only* suggestion.

## Relationship to other tickets

Same class as `bediasite-bilineate-stoat` (`fb8b-189d-97ab-4546`, closed): a gate message whose stated remedy under-serves the situation the author is actually in. That one was fixed by making the message name the consequence the author would otherwise discover the hard way. This is the same fix shape applied to a different message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The over-limit finding's `suggested_fix` names concision and relocating narration to comments
      or a session log as remedies, not only decomposition — verified by a test asserting the
      message content.
- [x] The message distinguishes CONTEXT that must stay (problem, constraints, acceptance
      criteria and their evidence — enough that a reader who has never seen the ticket can
      evaluate the plan) from NARRATION that should move to comments or a session log
      (investigation history, method discussion, conversational progression). Coaching that
      only says "be shorter" fails the completion verifier from the opposite direction and
      does not satisfy this criterion — verified by a test asserting both halves are named.
- [x] The message points at the packaged authoring guidance rather than restating it, so the advice
      cannot drift from the guide.
- [x] Decomposition advice remains available for the case it genuinely fits (a unit of work too
      large for one session) and is distinguishable from the over-length-prose case — verified by a
      test covering both branches.
- [x] The 8,000-character limit itself is UNCHANGED. This ticket does not raise it, and a change
      that raises it does not satisfy these criteria.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.
baseline.summary: Over-limit plan message suggests only decomposition, coaching authors to split coherent work when the real fix is concision

# Plan-review and completion-verifier gates run slowly (minutes-scale wall clock); latency is NOT explained by the Anthropic→Bedrock provider switch, but correlates in time with the LLM provider seam migration

## Context / Problem

Since the LLM provider seam migration cut the gates over to AWS Bedrock (epic [rebar:061c-ecd1-8967-4a76], ADR 0059 landed 2026-08-04 `d416ab9846`; production/local default set to Bedrock `5bc3a432d7`), the plan-review gate (`rebar review-plan`) and — by shared mechanism — the completion-verifier gate (`rebar verify-completion`) exhibit minutes-scale wall clock on real epics/stories. This ticket records the OBSERVED slowness and the result of a controlled provider A/B, so the next session working the gate does not re-derive it. **It is an investigation/observability bug: no fix is applied here** — a parallel session owns the completion-verifier remediation (worktrees `debug-completion-validator`, `impl-10ae-verifier-ctx`).

## Observed evidence (grounded in telemetry + tickets)

**1. In-band telemetry — `.rebar/usage.jsonl` (163 rows, 2026-08-06T20:32Z → 2026-08-07T01:27Z, `provider=bedrock` on EVERY row — i.e. entirely post-migration; the file is gitignored so no pre-migration Anthropic baseline was retained).** Per-op `duration_s`:

| op | n | median | p90 | max | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plan-review-verifier-agentic` | 6 | **182.2s** | 276.0s | **276.0s** | up to 19 requests, 463k input tokens in one call |
| `plan-reviewer` | 106 | 21.8s | 60.2s | 99.6s | agentic finder loops |
| `plan-novelty` | 3 | 6.0s | — | 10.0s | |
| `plan-review-coach` | 9 | 5.7s | — | 7.0s | single-turn |
| `ticket-digest` | 9 | 5.5s | — | 7.7s | single-turn |
| `overlap-judge` | 18 | 4.1s | — | 5.4s | single-turn |
| `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` | 9 | 1.5s | — | 2.6s | |

The cost concentrates in the **agentic** passes (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`, `plan-reviewer`): 75 of 163 calls issued >1 request; the worst issued 19 requests / 276s / 463k input tokens. The single-turn ops are all <8s.

**2. Controlled provider A/B on ONE plan (epic `992d-9d17-c6ac-4492`, same material, both providers via per-class `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` overrides; Anthropic key sourced from the operator env). This isolates provider from plan content.**

- **Single-shot floor ops are provider-identical** (same inputs, same cache behaviour):
  - `overlap-judge`: Bedrock median **5.06s** vs Anthropic **5.22s** (per-call: bed `[5.53,5.67,4.59,4.45]`, ant `[6.08,5.83,4.61,4.40]`); identical `input_tokens`≈4.8k and `cache_read`≈1.3k.
  - `ticket-digest`: Bedrock ~6.4s vs Anthropic ~4.8s.
- **Full agentic review wall clock (after remediating the P1 floor blocker so the review reaches
  the agentic passes):**
  - **Bedrock: 428.7s** (7.1 min), 13 LLM calls, 72 requests.
  - **Anthropic: 903.0s** (15.0 min), 21 LLM calls, 151 requests — i.e. Anthropic was *slower* on
    this sample.
  - `plan-review-verifier-agentic` per-request: Bedrock **31 req / 236.5s (7.6s/req)** vs Anthropic
    **25 req / 374.3s (15.0s/req)**.

**Conclusion of the A/B: provider raw latency does NOT account for the slowness.** On identical single-shot calls the two providers are within noise; on the agentic passes BOTH are minutes-scale, and in this sample Anthropic was slower overall. The dominant driver is the **agentic loop structure** — request count × monotonically growing context (the verifier-agentic call re-sent ~1.4M input tokens across its loop on both providers) — not the Anthropic→Bedrock switch. The migration correlation is **temporal** (the gates got slow right as the seam/agentic-verifier work shipped and Bedrock became default), not **provider-latency causal**.

**3. Shared mechanism ⇒ the completion verifier has the same exposure.** Plan-review's `plan-review-verifier-agentic` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:406` `execution_mode="agentic"`) and the completion verifier (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:594` `execution_mode="agentic"`, ops `completion-verifier-evidence` / `completion-verifier-finalizer`) run the SAME agentic runner with the same per-criterion context accumulation. So the completion verifier is expected to show the same minutes-scale profile even though it is absent from the current `usage.jsonl` window.

## Provider-specific aggravators observed (secondary, NOT the dominant cause)

These are real Bedrock-path degradations seen live during the runs, but the A/B shows they do not explain the bulk of the latency (Anthropic, which avoids them, was still slow):

- **Structured-output falls back to `PromptedOutput` on Bedrock** (bug 895c, `d8adf0f565`): the
  installed botocore cannot send Bedrock's `outputConfig`, so every contract (`TicketDigest`,
  `OverlapVerdictBatch`, `P1Output`, …) routes to prompted JSON and logs
  `parse_structured: multiple candidates validated … selecting the LAST` — extra generation +
  reparse on the Bedrock path only. (`>=1.43.64` restores native output; local env has an older
  botocore.)
- **Bedrock ignores `llm_retry_max_attempts` / `timeout_s`** (bug [rebar:61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289],
  `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` bare `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` — no
  `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no read timeout). Bedrock uses botocore stock retry defaults,
  which are neither configured nor observable, so a throttle-induced stall on the agentic loop is
  invisible and un-tunable.

## Why this is currently hard to see (observability gap)

Per-pass latency/cost telemetry (`coverage['metrics'] = {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls}`) is NOT emitted on the workflow plan-review gate — that regression is tracked open in task [rebar:4a40-ea6e-d3f7-4af7]. So the slowness above is only visible in the raw `usage.jsonl` sink, not in the signed sidecar an operator would read.

## Scope (for the eventual fix — NOT done here)

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — the agentic verifier/finder passes and their per-request
  context growth / request-limit envelope.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — the completion verifier's agentic passes (same
  mechanism; **owned by the parallel session**).
- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — botocore retry/timeout envelope (bug 61d8, already filed).
- botocore floor for native structured output (bug 895c).
- Restore per-pass latency telemetry on the workflow gate (task 4a40) so this is measured in-band.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Root cause of the agentic-pass wall-clock is stated as a specific changeable artifact (request
      count and/or unbounded context accumulation in the agentic runner), grounded in per-request
      telemetry — not attributed to provider raw latency, which the A/B here refutes.
- [x] [operator-attested][tracked:4a40] A repeatable measurement exists (per-pass `det_ms`/`llm_ms`/`total_ms`/`llm_calls` on the
      signed sidecar, via task 4a40) so a before/after can be asserted rather than eyeballed from
      `usage.jsonl`.
- [x] The provider A/B conclusion is preserved: an equivalent single-shot op is verified within-noise
      across Anthropic and Bedrock, and the agentic passes are shown minutes-scale on BOTH.
- [x] The completion-verifier remediation is cross-referenced (parallel session) so the shared
      agentic-runner fix is not duplicated or divergent.
baseline.summary: Plan-review and completion-verifier gates run minutes-scale; provider A/B refutes Anthropic->Bedrock as the cause (correlates in time with the LLM provider seam migration)

## Context / Problem
Upper-bound wall-clock assertions in tests are the proven CI flake class under runner contention (19d7, 5e94, edfe, 85c3). 15 sites scanned: 13 upper-bound in scope, 2 lower-bound out of scope; 11 currently unescaped. Detector prototype (regex + escapes) caught all, 0 FPs, and found one site manual scan missed (test_lock_stale_reclaim.py:127).

## Approach
DET BLOCKING code-review criterion scanning tests/** for upper-bound wall-clock asserts. Escapes: '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' line marker, or the existing perf-lane CI-exclusion guard '@pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("CI") == "true", ...)' on the test (the idiom the benchmark tests in tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py:245-249 already use — NOTE: the '@pytest.mark.benchmark' marker alone is NOT an escape — it is registered (pyproject.toml, informational) but no CI invocation filters it out (the suite runs -m 'not integration and not external'), so a benchmark-marked test still executes on CI; the skipif(CI) guard is what actually removes runner-contention flake risk). Migrations (proven by experiment): tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201 -> spy config._ordered_layers, the miss-path filesystem walk load_config only calls on a _RESULT_CACHE miss (reset_config_cache seam; regression sim caught 10/10); tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 -> exactly one pending_enrichment call + zero drain/spawn. Remaining 9 sites get markers with reasons. Optional follow-on: migrate reducer benchmarks to _api.replay_events spy to restore CI coverage (currently benchmark-skipped). Seed implementation from /tmp/exp4_detector.py; proxy rule: spy the MISS-PATH function, never tomllib (warm TOML cache evades parse spies). Self-exclusion: the detector's own unit-test file carries live upper-bound asserts as RED fixtures, so it is structurally excluded via the sibling guards' EXCLUDED_FILES idiom (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:57 — the exact failure b047 recorded when its fixtures self-tripped the comment-hygiene guard).

## Scope
- detector as DET code-review criterion (review-bot checkout) or CI lint per gate conventions
- tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201, tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 migrations
- markers on the 9 hang-guard sites

## Testing
Detector unit tests: unescaped upper-bound assert -> finding; hang-guard marker escape -> silent; skipif(CI) guard escape -> silent (bare '@pytest.mark.benchmark' without the skipif guard -> still a finding); lower-bound assert -> silent. Migrated tests: regression simulation goes RED (cache cleared per call / drain forced), warm path GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Detector blocks new unescaped upper-bound wall-clock asserts in tests/** with a teaching message naming both escapes (hang-guard marker; skipif-CI perf-lane guard).
- [x] Both migration sites assert counting proxies (miss-path spies), proven RED under regression simulation.
- [x] All remaining in-scope sites carry reasoned markers; detector run on the tree is clean.
- [x] Detector has unit tests covering fire, both escapes (marker; skipif-CI guard — and bare benchmark marker NOT escaping), and lower-bound exclusion.
baseline.summary: Wall-clock upper-bound assert detector (DET blocking code-review criterion) + 2 site migrations

# Outsider onboarding: a warm "your first change" tutorial layered on CONTRIBUTING.md

## Why

CONTRIBUTING.md §1–§3 already documents the external Gerrit path (GitHub OAuth, clone-from-Gerrit-as-origin, hook, refs/for/main, the two votes, the §2e submit-authorization callout) — the gap is not information but SHAPE: it is a complete reference, not a first-contact narrative, and nothing on GitHub funnels an outsider into it. Every surveyed Gerrit-keeping project ships a dedicated first-change tutorial distinct from the reference (Go's contribute guide, LibreOffice GetInvolved, Wikimedia Gerrit/Tutorial); JGit proves a web-OAuth Gerrit needs only a short one. This story adds the tutorial layer and the funnel links; it does NOT restructure CONTRIBUTING.md's reference content.

## What

- New `docs/your-first-change.md`, 800–1500 words (one authoritative range; target ~1000), Go's two-layer structure (one-time setup vs per-change loop), LibreOffice-warm tone, consistent with CONTRIBUTING.md §1–§2 (same commands, same remote naming — the outsider clone uses `origin` = Gerrit, so pushes are `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main`; never the internal dual-remote `gerrit` name):
  1. How review works here (3 sentences): Gerrit not PRs; two bot votes gate submit; GitHub is a mirror. For vote semantics, link CONTRIBUTING.md §2c now; the review-policy story (which depends on this one) will retarget that link to `docs/review-policy.md` when it lands — this tutorial does NOT duplicate the vote table (epic single-source rule).
  2. One-time setup (~5 min): sign in at rebar.solutions.navateam.com with GitHub OAuth → generate HTTP password (Settings → HTTP Credentials) → clone via the authenticated `/a/` URL → install the commit-msg hook (one sentence demystifying Change-Id). Include the two common account-setup failure states (OAuth loop / hook curl failing) as gotcha rows.
  3. Your first change: branch from main → commit with `git commit -s` (DCO sign-off; brief, links CONTRIBUTING's DCO section once the DCO story lands — until then links developercertificate.org) AND the `rebar-ticket:` trailer. The outsider ticket flow, specified in-scope (no deferral): open a GitHub issue describing the work; the maintainer files the rebar ticket and replies with the id to put in the trailer; for tiny fixes the shepherded-patch path (CONTRIBUTING) skips Gerrit entirely. → `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main` with the magic ref demystified → reading a −1: link the authoritative vote-semantics doc; summarize only "finding = fix and re-push; coverage-gap = infra, not your code; Verified −1 = CI, comment `recheck` for flakes" without enumerating sub-reasons (the enum lives in one place) → `git commit --amend --no-edit` + re-push → final step: "a maintainer submits once both votes are green — you don't need (and won't see) a Submit button until you're added to Contributors" (mirrors CONTRIBUTING §2e; no false promise the outsider lands it themselves).
  4. Gotchas table: missing Change-Id; pushed to `main` instead of `refs/for/main`; new commit instead of amend; missing sign-off; missing/unresolvable rebar-ticket trailer; CI flake; OAuth/hook setup failures.
  5. See-also → CONTRIBUTING.md as the full reference.
- CONTRIBUTING.md: light edits only — add a prominent link to the tutorial near the top ("first time? start here"); no restructuring (the reference is already externally accurate).
- `docs/README.md` (audience-indexed docs ToC): add the tutorial under the Contributor section.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`: add the tutorial link alongside the existing CONTRIBUTING pointer (the PR template is an outsider's first contact until the lockdown bot lands).

## Scope

IN: `docs/your-first-change.md` (new), CONTRIBUTING.md top-link, `docs/README.md` index entry, PR-template link. OUT: README.md front-door work (own story: README front door); restructuring CONTRIBUTING.md; the DCO section and shepherded-patch section (owned by the DCO and PR-posture stories, which add their own cross-links INTO this tutorial when they land — ownership-inversion rule); vote-semantics table (review-policy story); video/asciinema tutorials; changes to review gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/your-first-change.md` exists — prove: `wc -w docs/your-first-change.md` in [800, 1500]; covers the nine-beat sequence (account → credential → clone → hook → branch → signed commit w/ trailer → push refs/for → respond → amend/re-push) — prove: grep hits for `refs/for/main`, `commit-msg`, `--amend`, `commit -s`, `rebar-ticket:`.
- [ ] Zero Nava-internal references on the happy path — prove: `grep -cE "feature-branch-drivers|CLAUDE|dual-remote|push gerrit " docs/your-first-change.md` = 0 (the push remote is `origin`).
- [ ] The outsider ticket flow is actionable without sibling stories: the GitHub-issue → maintainer-files-ticket → trailer loop is fully described in this doc.
- [ ] Submit expectations match reality — prove: doc states a maintainer performs Submit for first-time contributors (no instruction that the outsider presses Submit).
- [ ] No duplicated vote table — prove: the doc links CONTRIBUTING §2c (or review-policy.md once retargeted) and does not enumerate coverage-gap sub-reasons.
- [ ] Funnel links present — prove, one grep PER FILE (multi-file grep -q passes if any one matches, so each is its own check): `grep -q "your-first-change" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "your-first-change" docs/README.md`; `grep -q "your-first-change" .github/pull_request_template.md`.
baseline.summary: Outsider onboarding: your-first-change tutorial, CONTRIBUTING restructure, README front door

## Context / Problem
Every **attested-source** LLM gate operation fails on the LIVE MCP server (`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, container `compose-mcp-1`, image `compose-mcp:9499312eb7b05dc3d75d39c23ab74a5b4afc26b5`).

Observed 2026-08-27 against the live endpoint:

```
review_plan       {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered"}
  -> Error executing tool review_plan: cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'.
review_plan       {"ticket_id": "...", "ref": "HEAD"}
  -> Error executing tool review_plan: cannot resolve ref 'HEAD' to a commit in '.'.
verify_completion {"ticket_id": "..."}
  -> Error executing tool verify_completion: cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'.
review_plan       {"ticket_id": "...", "source": "local"}   -> RUNS (P1/P2/P3 emitted)
```

## Mechanism
The container's repo root has **no git metadata at all**. Verified in-container:

```
$ docker exec compose-mcp-1 sh -c 'pwd; ls -d /app/.git; git -C /app rev-parse origin/main'
/app
ls: cannot access '/app/.git': No such file or directory
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

`docker inspect` confirms `WorkingDir=/app`, `Cmd=["rebar-mcp"]`, and the env carries `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` but **no `REBAR_ROOT`** — so the repo root resolves to the cwd `/app`, which is a plain source copy, not a work tree. The image ships `/app/.deployed_ref` (`d4a0a2a44 (feat/gerrit-ci-verified-gate)`) as a text marker instead of a real clone. `source=attested` pins a snapshot at `ref` against that root's object DB, so ref resolution fails before any LLM call.

The tracker itself is unaffected: it is an out-of-tree clone reached via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`, so all non-git tools (create/show/search/list/comment/edit/link/claim/transition) work.

## Impact
`attested` is the DEFAULT source for both gate ops, and a `local`-source verdict is never signed. So **no plan-review or completion attestation can be earned through the live MCP server**, and consequently no `task`/`story`/`epic` can be closed through it while `verify.require_plan_review_for_close` is on — the only remaining path is `--force`, which agents are prohibited from using. Reproduced live: probe task `ruby-griffinish-goitered` (`c67b-ece5-707e-460e`) is stuck `in_progress` with `plan-review close gate: unsigned: no certified plan-review attestation`, and the prescribed remedy (`review-plan`) is the very operation that cannot run.

## Reproduction
1. Call `review_plan` on any claimable ticket through the live MCP endpoint with default args.
2. Observe `cannot resolve ref 'origin/main' to a commit in '.'`.
3. Repeat with `source: "local"` and observe it runs.

## Fix

Provision a real repository for the gate ops to resolve against, and point the repo root at it.

**Why not the obvious alternatives.** Shipping `.git` in the image (removing the `.dockerignore:5` exclusion) bloats every layer and pins a main that goes stale the moment the image is built — the gates need a ref that tracks main, not a frozen one. Re-using the tickets clone at `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` is tempting since `MCP_TICKETS_URL` is the SAME repository, but it conflates the code root with the tracker: two different lifetimes, two different refspecs, and a reader can no longer tell which one a failure came from.

**Shape.** `provision_store` gains a sibling that clones the CODE side into `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` — `--filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch main`, so it is a blobless clone that fetches objects on demand rather than materializing the history — and `REBAR_ROOT` is set to it (compose env + `mcp_run_new`, which must stay in parity). That root carries `rebar.toml`, so config resolution moves from the source copy at `/app` to a real checkout, which is strictly better: the two agree today, and a real root is what the config seam expects.

**Ordering.** Like the tickets clone this is backgrounded, so it cannot block `exec` past the readiness deadline. Until it converges the gates fail exactly as they do today — no worse.

**Enforcement is OUT OF SCOPE** (operator ruling, 2026-08-27). This change makes the attested gates work; it does NOT add a deploy-time check that refuses to promote a container whose code root failed to resolve. A failed code clone therefore degrades to today's behaviour — the gates error — rather than blocking the deploy. That is a deliberate boundary, not an oversight: gating promotion on a backgrounded clone is what produced the rollback loop in `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel`, and re-introducing it here would trade one outage shape for another.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1: `review_plan` with default arguments against the deployed MCP server returns a plan-review verdict (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) rather than a ref-resolution error.
- [x] AC2: `verify_completion` with default arguments likewise returns a completion verdict.
- [x] AC3: A PASS from AC1 persists a signed plan-review attestation.
      OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: `foreign_key` is ACCEPTED as sufficient; `certified` is
      NOT required. Observed: the AC1 run returned `attestation.signed: true`, so the
      attestation IS produced and persisted; `plan_review_status(b928-3ab6-5985-417b)`
      through the deployed server then returns `verdict: foreign_key` because that
      environment holds no op-cert public key and so cannot certify its own signature.
      The original wording demanded `certified`; that is waived here. The missing public
      key remains tracked separately (`dire-expectable-terr…`, see Scope boundaries).
- [x] AC4: The deployed container exposes a git object DB for the repo root reachable by the gate ops (a real clone at the repo root, or an explicit `REBAR_ROOT` pointing at one), verified by `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/main` succeeding inside the container.

## Definition of Done
- [x] DD1: AC1-AC3 demonstrated against a deployed MCP server.

## Scope boundaries (operator rulings, 2026-08-27)

- **Enforcement is out of scope.** No deploy-time refusal; see the Fix section.
- **A shared op-cert is acceptable.** The server signing under the box's existing opcert
  environment (ADR 0104 §3, Option A) is the accepted design. The separate observation that
  the environment holds no public key, so `verify_signature` returns `foreign_key`, is tracked
  as `dire-expectable-terrapin` and is NOT in scope here.

- [x] **LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE.** `review_plan` called through the deployed endpoint returns a VERDICT rather than `cannot resolve ref ... in '.'`, and an attestation is persisted.
      OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: `scan_spec` is DROPPED from this criterion, and a
      persisted-but-`foreign_key` attestation is accepted in place of a certified one.
      Evidence recorded in the LIVE VALIDATION comment on this ticket: `review_plan`
      and `verify_completion` both returned real verdicts (PASS) through
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` against container
      `rebar-mcp-2dbdcc8abe2c-8093`, with `attestation.signed: true`.
      Evidence must be OBSERVED against the deployed server at
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` and recorded in a ticket comment naming
      the tool(s) called, the arguments, and the actual response. A passing local test is
      NOT sufficient, and neither is a merged change: the container must have redeployed
      and served the call. This exists because a fix here was previously reported complete
      on the strength of a merge while the deployed behaviour was still broken.
baseline.summary: Attested-source LLM gates are unusable on the deployed MCP server: the container repo root has no git metadata

## Context
The Gerrit Verify matrix runs the same default-tier marker selection on Ubuntu Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13. Every cell currently enables pytest-cov and independently enforces the same repository-wide fail-under floor. All three cells remain necessary for supported-Python behavioral and contractual compatibility, but tracing identical source on three cells adds runner occupancy without a distinct verdict. Production code has no sys.version_info or sys.version branches. The closed ropeable-hydrated-siskin ticket established the accepted precedent of retaining platform tests while collecting coverage only on a primary cell. Ubuntu Python 3.13 is the primary cell because it is the newest stable supported interpreter already paired with the sole macOS compatibility cell; retaining the gate there keeps the coverage verdict on the primary runtime while 3.11 and 3.12 remain behavioral-compatibility legs.

## Plan
- Measure instrumentation cost on the same checkout and host with identical tests/unit selection and worker count: one untimed warm-up, then A-B-B-A-A-B where A includes the production coverage flags and B omits only those flags. Report local_delta = median(A elapsed) - median(B elapsed).
- Record this change own pre-merge Verify run id, the Python 3.11 and 3.12 default-suite step durations, and the post-merge comparison formula on this ticket before close. The umbrella inedible-subsimious-brahmancow owns the same-session post-merge observation because GitHub resolves the reusable workflow from main during pre-merge workflow_dispatch. The umbrella remains open until it records the first post-merge run, each changed-cell delta = pre-merge step duration - post-merge step duration, and the sum of only Python 3.11 and 3.12 deltas as runner-seconds freed. Python 3.13 and macOS are unchanged controls. The report must label a one-run comparison as noisy and must not call summed parallel time critical-path wall time.
- Survey Django, NumPy, and SciPy current workflows and record each topology and any documented rationale as found. Consensus passes only if at least two selectively collect coverage on a primary or dedicated configuration while broader compatibility jobs run uninstrumented and none documents rejecting that practice for coverage or reliability. If the threshold fails, stop before Phase 2 and summarize the contrary evidence for the operator.
- Extend tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py with a workflow contract that expands the declared matrix. Prove all four cells retain both default and integration pytest tiers. Prove exactly Ubuntu Python 3.13 receives both coverage flags and the other three cells receive neither.
- Encode the condition with the non-empty coverage flag string in the truthy and-slot and the empty string only in the final or-slot. This explicitly avoids the GitHub Actions empty-string-falsy trap recorded on ropeable-hydrated-siskin. Defect-seed the prior all-Ubuntu condition and a zero-coverage condition; each must make the held-out contract RED before restoring GREEN.
- Update the coverage rationale comment in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml and the canonical topology in docs/coverage.md so both state that Ubuntu Python 3.13 alone collects branch coverage and enforces fail-under.
- Run focused workflow tests, lint, and typecheck; land through Gerrit. Back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring the prior all-Ubuntu coverage condition and three-cell documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The A-B-B-A-A-B experiment reports raw elapsed samples.
- [ ] The experiment reports local_delta using the stated median formula.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.11 retains the default-tier pytest step.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.11 retains the integration-tier pytest step.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.12 retains the default-tier pytest step.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.12 retains the integration-tier pytest step.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.13 retains the default-tier pytest step.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.13 retains the integration-tier pytest step.
- [ ] macOS Python 3.13 retains the default-tier pytest step.
- [ ] macOS Python 3.13 retains the integration-tier pytest step.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.13 collects branch coverage.
- [ ] Ubuntu Python 3.13 enforces the unchanged fail-under threshold.
- [ ] No other matrix cell receives a coverage flag.
- [ ] The workflow contract is observed RED with the prior all-Ubuntu coverage condition.
- [ ] The workflow contract is observed RED when no cell receives coverage.
- [ ] The survey records a current workflow URL and topology for each named project.
- [ ] The survey records any documented rejection found.
- [ ] The consensus decision applies the stated threshold to the recorded findings.
- [ ] Tracker history cites ropeable-hydrated-siskin and any prior rejection found.
- [ ] The workflow rationale comment describes the one-cell coverage topology.
- [ ] docs/coverage.md describes the one-cell coverage topology.
- [ ] Focused tests pass.
- [ ] Lint passes.
- [ ] Typecheck passes.
- [ ] Gerrit LLM-Review is +1 with zero unresolved comments.
- [ ] Gerrit Verified is +1 before merge.
- [ ] The pre-merge baseline run id and raw 3.11/3.12 default-suite step durations are recorded before close.
- [ ] The post-merge observation is explicitly tracked on inedible-subsimious-brahmancow.
- [ ] Back-out is documented as a Gerrit revert restoring the prior condition and topology text.

## The gap

S1 (`aa40`, change 2620) put the unreachable-scratch **refusal** in `gate_admission()`, which wraps plan-review and completion-verifier. That is where ADR 0112 places it, and S1 implements the ADR faithfully.

But the review-bot's per-review clone does **not** pass through `gate_admission()`. It is a plain `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reviewbot-")` in `voter._decision_for_review_target`, following `TMPDIR`. So on a **declared-but-unmounted** scratch volume, plan-review and completion-verifier correctly refuse while the review-bot keeps cloning onto the root filesystem, silently — precisely the outage epic `6202` exists to prevent. A partial refusal is arguably worse than none, because the loud half creates confidence the protection is in force.

This is a gap in the architecture, not a defect in S1.

## The trap (read change 2620 first)

An unmounted volume raises **nothing**: a mount point whose volume is absent is an ordinary, writable, empty directory, so a naive `mkdir(parents=True)` silently recreates state on root and every caller keeps working. S1's answer is two markers on two different filesystems — `.gate-scratch-required` on **root** beside the mount point (the declaration, survives an unmount) and `.gate-scratch-mounted` **on the volume** (the proof, vanishes with it). Only declaration-present + proof-absent refuses.

## Approach

1. **Share S1's check, do not reimplement it.** Promote the two-marker predicate inside
   `gate_admission._require_scratch_volume` to a public `scratch_unavailable_detail()` on
   `src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py` (that module is not in the pinned API-surface baseline, so this
   is not a public-surface change). `_require_scratch_volume` becomes a thin caller that raises
   `GateScratchUnavailableError`; the review-bot calls the same function. One predicate, one pair of
   marker constants, so enforcement and `observability.sh` monitoring cannot disagree.
2. **Guard the clone at the existing pre-clone admission seam.** `_decision_for_review_target`
   already refuses before cloning when the free-space floor is not met
   (`if not _review_clone_has_room(cfg): return _low_disk_decision(), ""`). Add the scratch check
   immediately **before** that, and before the `TemporaryDirectory`, so nothing is created on root.
   Ordering matters: on an unmounted volume the empty mount point usually **passes** the free-space
   floor, so the scratch check must run first.
3. **Reuse ADR 0069's existing deferral; invent nothing.** The refusal is returned as an
   adapter-shaped decision carrying the **existing** `low-disk` retryable gap reason, built by a new
   `low_disk.scratch_unavailable_decision()` sibling of `low_disk.decision()`. That reason is already
   in `adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS`, so under budget the voter defers vote-less
   (`REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED`), and it is already the **one** reason ADR 0069 carves out to a terminal
   no-vote on exhaustion (`REVIEW_LOW_DISK_DEFERRED_EXHAUSTED`, labels unchanged) rather than the
   fail-closed `-1`. A new gap reason would have to be added to that carve-out branch by hand and
   could regress into a false `LLM-Review -1` on a host condition; reusing the reason makes
   "never -1" structural. The distinct sub-condition is carried in the coverage block
   (`scratch_unavailable`, `scratch_path`) and in the operator-facing message, not in routing.

Out of scope: `infra/scripts/*` and `infra/terraform/*` (owned by story `9183`, in flight).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — With the declaration present on the root-side parent and the proof absent from the mount
      point, the review-bot clone path **refuses**: `review_and_vote` returns a coverage-gap result
      and `clone_change_ref` is never called. Proven with the real two-marker files on a temp
      "host", not by monkeypatching the predicate.
- [x] AC2 — The refusal is an ADR 0069 **retryable deferral**, never an `LLM-Review -1`: under
      budget the result is `status="deferred"` with no vote posted; with the budget exhausted the
      result is `status="deferred-exhausted"` with no vote posted, no `VOTER_ERROR`, and labels
      unchanged.
- [x] AC3 — **Absence assertion (defect-seeded).** With declaration present and proof absent, the
      clone path creates **nothing** on the underlying (root) directory: no `reviewbot-*` entry
      exists under it after the call. Modelled on S1's
      `test_the_refusal_creates_no_store_on_the_underlying_directory` — asserts the directory does
      not exist, not merely that an error was raised. RED first: with the guard removed the same
      test shows the clone landing there.
- [x] AC4 — **No-op preserved.** With no declaration present (the default, and every developer
      machine and CI runner), nothing changes: the clone proceeds and no refusal occurs. Also
      asserted for the proof-present/declaration-absent quadrant.
- [x] AC5 — Monitoring and enforcement read the **same** proof marker: the review-bot path resolves
      its markers from `gate_admission`'s own constants via the shared predicate (asserted by
      identity, not by string duplication), and `observability.sh` continues to name that same
      marker.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k scratch -q` — AC1-AC5 on
  the review-bot clone path (refusal, absence-on-root, deferred / deferred-exhausted vote-lessness,
  both no-op quadrants, shared-predicate identity).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py -q` — S1's
  suite still passes unchanged, proving the extraction is behaviour-preserving for the gates.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py -q` — no regression in the low-disk and admission paths that share the seam.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py -q` — the three gates invisible to `make lint` (run after `git add`).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.

## File impact

`src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py`, `src/rebar/review_bot/low_disk.py`, `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`, `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`, `tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py`.
baseline.summary: review-bot clone path bypasses the gate-scratch refusal: on a declared-but-unmounted volume it silently clones onto root while the gates correctly refuse
