## Problem (finding P0-2a — separate from the seam-conversion work)
projects_store.set_project (projects_store.py) accepts ANY string key with no validation: it does not call fetcher._validate_project_key, so a syntactically-invalid or malformed key (e.g. "le-g", "", "1x", a key with trailing whitespace) is written to projects.json and only fails much later, deep in the reconciler fan-out. A validation guard at write time would have rejected the malformed input that contributed to the incident class (05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27).

## Scope note
This is a NEW behavior (input validation), NOT a hand-rolled->seam conversion. Filed separately from ticket fea4 (pure seam conversion, now merged) so it can be approved on its own. It does NOT modify any shared seam and adds no facade. SYNTACTIC validation ONLY — NO live Jira/network call (existence validation is owned by the reconcile preflight, not here).

## Approach
set_project validates the key with the EXISTING fetcher._validate_project_key (import and reuse it — do NOT duplicate the _PROJECT_KEY_RE regex `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`) and rejects an invalid key with a clear error and NO file write, BEFORE the record is persisted/published. remove_project gets the same guard for symmetry (it can receive an unvalidated key). The validation slots in BEFORE B's fsutil.atomic_write + write_lock + commit_and_push_tickets_branch RMW, so a rejected key never persists or publishes. The new ValueError is mapped to a clean RebarError(returncode=2) at the _lib_ops seam (bridge_projects_set/remove) — the SAME error contract those consumers already handle for remove's absent-key KeyError — so both production consumers surface it cleanly: the CLI (_cli/_bridge_commands.py projects set/remove) catches RebarError and prints a non-zero error with no traceback, and the MCP write tools (_mcp_writes.py) raise that same RebarError (identical to remove's absent-key path, no MCP code change needed). No Jira-existence checking here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] set_project with an invalid key ("le-g", "", "1x", "LEG " trailing space) raises a
      clear error and writes NOTHING (projects.json unchanged / uncreated), verified by
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py -q`.
- [x] A valid key ("REB", "PROJ_2") is still accepted and written unchanged (B's
      atomic_write/lock/publish path preserved), verified by the same test module.
- [x] remove_project rejects an invalid key with the same guard, before any mutation.
- [x] Reuses fetcher._validate_project_key; no duplicated regex, no seam change, no
      network/Jira call added.
- [x] The invalid-key rejection surfaces as ONE clean RebarError(returncode=2) / non-zero
      error (no traceback) through the library, the CLI, and the MCP write tools, verified
      by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bridge_projects_surfaces_heldout.py
      tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_projects_heldout.py -q`.

## Testing
- RED-first unit tests in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py: each
  invalid key raises and leaves projects.json unwritten; a valid key still writes. Run
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ tests/scripts/bridge/ -q`.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean.

## Sequencing
Edits projects_store.py (+ _lib_ops.py if needed) + tests — same file as ticket fea4, now MERGED into origin/main, so this builds on B's seams. This change stacks on B.
baseline.summary: Validate project key at write time in projects_store.set_project (reuse _validate_project_key)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

CI runs the suite with `-n 3 --dist worksteal`, and the `lru_cache` on `_rendered()` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py:60` is process-local, so each xdist worker that lands one of its four consumers re-renders all 178 corpus bodies (~884 pandoc spawns). Measured on this worktree (macOS, pandoc 3.6.1 via `pypandoc-binary==1.15`):

* serial (`-p no:randomly`, no xdist): ONE test pays the fill —
  `test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained` 47.92s, the other three
  consumers ~0s. 135.09s wall, 38.10s user + 48.69s system.
* `-n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300`: THREE tests each pay a full fill —
  44.49s, 43.38s, 42.82s. 92.03s wall but 63.96s user + 79.50s system.

So the filed premise holds: three cache fills under `-n 3` versus one serially, about +56s of CPU burned re-deriving an identical, immutable artifact. On a 3-core macOS runner three concurrent 884-spawn pandoc storms also contend with the rest of the suite, which is what produced the 321.6s/495.6s aggregates cited on the parent audit.

A second duplication shows in the same runs: the three `test_dc_corpus_passes_two_to_five_are_byte_identical[...]` tests each recompute `first = render_markdown_to_wiki(body)` per body — bit-for-bit the pass-1 render `_rendered()` already holds. They cost 23.85s/25.93s/22.34s serially, about half of which is that recomputed pass 1.

## Approach

Replace the process-local `lru_cache` with a **session-scoped artifact shared across xdist workers on disk**, and have the fixed-point tests read pass 1 from it instead of recomputing it.

* A session-scoped fixture `corpus_pass1` resolves the shared directory as
  `tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent`. Under xdist a worker's basetemp is
  `pytest-<N>/popen-gw<K>`, so `.parent` is `pytest-<N>` — shared by every worker
  of THIS session and rotated by pytest between sessions: cross-worker sharing
  with no new dependency and no artifact that outlives the session.
* The artifact is **sharded per stratum** (one file per `code_arrow`/`table`/`prose`),
  and each worker probes the strata in an order rotated by its
  `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` index. That is a scheduling hint only — the lock still
  guarantees one computation per stratum — but it stops concurrent whole-corpus
  consumers from queueing on the same shard, so a cold session costs one stratum of
  wall time instead of the whole corpus.
* The artifact filename embeds a SHA-256 digest of the three corpus JSON files,
  the `wiki_render` module source, and the resolved pandoc executable path +
  size, so a corpus or renderer edit can never be served a stale render.
* Mutual exclusion uses `os.mkdir` on a sibling lock directory (atomic on POSIX
  and Windows, no new dependency): the winner renders, publishes via `os.replace`
  (atomic, so a visible artifact is always complete), and removes the lock in a
  `finally` block, retiring it on the success AND the error path. A loser that
  sees neither lock nor artifact re-enters the acquisition loop. **The loser's
  fallback deadline is 150s** — below the `--timeout=300` guard, with headroom
  over the fill — so a loser blocked on a crashed winner breaks the orphaned lock,
  renders locally, and still finishes inside the timeout instead of being killed
  by it: it degrades to today's per-worker behaviour rather than deadlocking.
* The four `_rendered()` consumers and the three fixed-point tests all take the
  fixture. The fixed-point tests keep their own pass-2 (and conditional pass-3)
  renders — that is real, non-duplicated coverage.

This fits because the render is a pure function of the inputs the digest pins, so sharing it weakens no assertion, and it targets the duplication directly rather than cutting corpus coverage, which the parent audit and the coordinating tickets refused. Caching pass 1 (not pass 2) keeps the largest test far below the hang guard instead of concentrating the whole corpus into one test.

## Scope

* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py` — replace the
  `lru_cache`d `_rendered()` (line 60) with the digest-keyed cross-worker
  artifact plus a session fixture; convert the four consumers
  (`test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained`,
  `test_dc_corpus_tables_survive_verbatim`,
  `test_dc_corpus_html_comments_survive_exactly`,
  `test_dc_corpus_coverage_ratios`) and the three
  `test_dc_corpus_passes_two_to_five_are_byte_identical` parametrizations to the
  fixture; update the module docstring's cost-discipline note.

No production file changes: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` is read (for its source bytes in the digest and via its existing public `render_markdown_to_wiki`/`code_fragments`) but not modified. Corpus fixtures under `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` are unchanged.

## Testing

The changed unit is itself the test module, so verification is by running it and comparing against the recorded baselines above:

* Happy path — `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py
  -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300 --durations=12`: all 11 tests still pass,
  and exactly one test shows a fill-sized duration while the other `_rendered()`
  consumers drop to well under a second.
* Serial path — the same module with no xdist still passes, proving the shared
  artifact degrades correctly when there is a single worker.
* Failure/edge path — a temporary local corpus mutation is confirmed to change the
  digest, forcing a fresh render instead of serving the previous artifact; and a
  temporary renderer defect that drops a protected code fragment is confirmed to
  still fail `test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained` through the cached
  path. Both mutations are reverted; neither is committed.
* Whole-suite regression — the CI pytest command is green.

No wall-clock or timing-budget assertion is added to any test; the savings are recorded as ticket-comment evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All 178 corpus bodies and every existing assertion (cardinality, secret
      scrub, protected excerpts, tables, HTML comments, determinism, fixed point,
      coverage ratios, non-vacuity) still run against real pandoc — verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py` reporting
      11 passed with no test skipped or deleted.
- [x] Under the exact `-n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300` command, each
      stratum's pass-1 render is computed exactly once per session: no worker shows
      a whole-corpus (>30s) fill, versus the three 42-45s fills measured today —
      recorded as a before/after ticket comment.
- [x] Aggregate per-test time for the module under that command is at least 40%
      below the 211s baseline recorded above, measured by summing `--durations=12`
      setup+call times and posted as a ticket comment.
- [x] Total CPU (user+system) for that command is below the 143s baseline recorded
      above, posted as a ticket comment.
- [x] No single test in the module exceeds 120s under `-n 3`, keeping clear of the
      300s hang guard — read off the same `--durations` output.
- [x] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` and
      `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/*.json` are byte-identical to `origin/main`,
      confirmed by `git diff --stat origin/main -- <those paths>` being empty.
- [x] A locally seeded corpus edit is shown to change the artifact digest and
      force a fresh render rather than serve the previous artifact — evidence in a
      ticket comment, mutation reverted.
- [x] A locally seeded protected-fragment break is shown to still fail
      `test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained` through the cached path —
      evidence in a ticket comment, mutation reverted.
- [x] The loser fallback deadline in the committed code is below the
      `--timeout=300` guard, confirmed by reading the constant in the diff.
baseline.summary: Wiki corpus cost cache is duplicated by every xdist worker

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The two weekly, canonical-repo-only GitHub Actions jobs that make **real, billable LLM calls** surface **no retrievable record of token usage**:

- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` → `external` job (weekly `cron "0 6 * * 1"`),
  runs `pytest -m external tests/external` (`external-integration.yml:30-136`).
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` → `eval-live` job (weekly `cron "0 7 * * 1"`),
  runs `ev.run_eval(pid, max_cases=cap)` over the eval specs (`prompt-eval.yml:79-100`).

Per-call usage is *already captured in code* — `PydanticAIRunner.run` computes `usage = _extract_usage(...)` (input/output/cache tokens + `requests`) at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:392,394`, logs one INFO line at `runner.py:452-470`, and attaches it as a private `result["_usage"] = usage` at `runner.py:486`. But that record never reaches either weekly job: the eval path (`ev.run_eval`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`) returns only `passed`/`coverage`/`junit` and drops `_usage`; the external `pytest` tier surfaces nothing; and the INFO log lines are swallowed because `src/rebar/__init__.py` attaches a `NullHandler` to the `rebar` logger and neither job calls `logging.basicConfig`. The only usage-bearing path, the `langfuse-trace` job, exports spans to an **ephemeral** Langfuse torn down with `docker compose ... down -v` each run, so nothing is retrievable afterward.

There is **no token→USD price table anywhere** in the codebase, so this ticket records **token usage** (input/output/cache tokens + request count), not a dollar figure.

Edit-set (all paths confirmed present unless marked *new*):
- *new* `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (720 LOC today; cap is 800 per `.github/module-size-limit.txt`)
- *new* `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py`
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml`
- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`

## Approach

Add one process-level usage sink at the **already-existing** `_usage` seam that is shared by both jobs (both go through `PydanticAIRunner.run`), so a single hook covers both without any per-test or per-eval plumbing.

1. New module `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py`:
   - `record(usage: dict, *, op: str) -> None` — when env var `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set to a
     path, append one JSON object per call (`op`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
     `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `requests`) as a line to that file (JSONL).
     No-op when the env var is unset. Best-effort: it wraps its file write in a `try/except`
     and never raises into the LLM call path (a telemetry sink must not break a run).
   - `summarize(path: str) -> str` — read the JSONL and return a Markdown summary: a totals
     row (summed tokens + total calls) plus a per-`op` breakdown table. A missing or empty
     file returns the single line `No LLM calls recorded.` (so a run with zero LLM calls still
     produces valid, honest summary output).
   - `__main__` CLI: `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize <path>` prints `summarize(path)`
     to stdout, for `>> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` in CI.
2. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — immediately after `result["_usage"] = usage` (`runner.py:486`),
   call `usage_log.record(usage, op=_call_label)` (module-level import). One statement; keeps
   `runner.py` well under the 800-LOC cap.
3. Both workflows (`prompt-eval.yml` `eval-live` job and `external-integration.yml` `external`
   job): set job env `REBAR_USAGE_LOG: ${{ runner.temp }}/usage.jsonl`; after the test/eval
   step (with `if: always()` so a test failure still reports spend), run
   `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize "$REBAR_USAGE_LOG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` and
   upload the raw JSONL via `actions/upload-artifact`. This gives both a human-glanceable job
   summary and a durable, machine-readable artifact.

Rejected alternatives: (a) persisting the `langfuse-trace` spans — requires standing up and retaining a Langfuse backend + secrets, far heavier than the ask and off the eval job's path entirely; (b) parsing the runner's INFO log lines out of pytest stdout — fragile and suppressed by the `NullHandler` today. The `_usage` seam is the one chokepoint already common to both jobs.

## Scope

- Recording is **token usage only** (input/output/cache tokens + request count). No dollar
  cost is computed — no price table exists in the repo, and adding one is out of scope.
- The sink is **opt-in via `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`**; default (env unset) behavior of the runner and
  of every existing caller is unchanged, so `make test` and normal library use are unaffected.
- Only the two weekly jobs set `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`; the PR/push and Verified lanes are untouched.
- No change to what tests/evals run, to gating, to `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES`, or to any provider
  credential handling.

## Testing

Offline unit tests only (no live LLM; consistent with the `not integration and not external` default suite). New `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py`:
- `record` appends one well-formed JSON line per call when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` points at a
  tmp_path file, and is a **no-op** when the env var is unset (assert no file created).
- `summarize` aggregates multiple recorded lines into correct totals and a per-`op` breakdown;
  a missing/empty file yields exactly `No LLM calls recorded.`
- Record-at-the-seam: drive `PydanticAIRunner.run` through the existing offline
  `FunctionModel` model-override path (with `pydantic_ai.models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False`,
  as in `tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py`) with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` set to a tmp file, and
  assert a JSONL line is appended — proving the runner call site fires without a live call.
- CLI: invoking `summarize` via the module entry point returns/prints the Markdown summary.

Workflow YAML edits are validated by `python -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(f))"` for each changed file (structural parse) in addition to the CI lint that already runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` exists exposing `record(usage, *, op)` and
      `summarize(path)` with the semantics above; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` passing.
- [ ] With `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` unset, `record(...)` writes no file and the runner path is
      unchanged; verified by the no-op unit test.
- [ ] `PydanticAIRunner.run` appends a usage record when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set; verified by
      the FunctionModel-override unit test asserting a JSONL line was written.
- [ ] `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize <path>` prints the Markdown totals + per-op
      table (or `No LLM calls recorded.` for an empty/missing file); verified by the CLI test.
- [ ] The `eval-live` job (`prompt-eval.yml`) and the `external` job
      (`external-integration.yml`) each set `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`, append `summarize` output to
      `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (`if: always()`), and upload the JSONL as an artifact; verified by
      `yaml.safe_load` of each file and grep for the three additions.
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` remains ≤ 800 LOC; verified by `wc -l`.
- [ ] `make test`, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` all pass locally; the change lands via
      Gerrit with `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`.
baseline.summary: Record token usage from the two weekly live-LLM jobs (external + eval-live)

## Context

`templates/rebar-usage.md` currently instructs every project to pass `--assignee <you>` and lists six link relations. The claim command already applies `ticket.default_assignee` when the option is omitted. A repository may leave that setting empty, in which case claim remains valid and records no assignee. An explicit value is an override and must be suitable for the configured Jira bridge when one is present. `templates/AGENTS.md` embeds a synchronized generated region from the usage template. Ticket bilingual-raptorial-furseal deliberately left these templates unchanged because adopter repositories may lack a default assignee. Tickets stun-wraith-conch, weariless-scrapable-mouse, isogonal-wedded-catfish, and dolorous-coverable-mice establish the current behavior and synchronized ownership.

## Plan

- Make the portable claim example omit `--assignee`.
- Explain the configured default and the valid unassigned result when no default exists.
- State the conditions for an explicit Jira-resolvable identity without assuming that every client repository uses Jira.
- Add `caused_by` to the link inventory.
- Add dependency-ordered plan review guidance that tells clients to review prerequisites before dependents.
- Synchronize the generated region in `templates/AGENTS.md` through the established template ownership mechanism.
- Preserve the existing byte-synchronization test and add focused behavior assertions.
- Exclude repository-specific Gerrit workflow guidance from the portable template.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The canonical template presents `rebar claim <id>` as the default command.
- [x] The template describes behavior when `ticket.default_assignee` is configured.
- [x] The template describes behavior when `ticket.default_assignee` is empty.
- [x] Explicit assignee guidance requires email or accountId only for a Jira-reconciled store when an override is intended.
- [x] The link inventory includes `caused_by`.
- [x] Plan review guidance requires prerequisites before dependents.
- [x] The canonical template contains no repository-specific Gerrit workflow guidance.
- [x] The generated region in `templates/AGENTS.md` matches `templates/rebar-usage.md`.
- [x] Focused template synchronization and behavior tests pass.

baseline.description:
## Context

Gerrit review of change 1536 confirmed the new locked commit-and-push entrypoint safely fails closed when local lock-artifact exclusion cannot be installed, and that the pre-lock update may append harmless duplicate exclude lines under concurrent first use. Preserve the shipped compatibility contract while tightening the local metadata update and its direct failure oracles.

## Current state (verified against origin/main cc69cc1179)

`_ignore_lock_artifacts` (src/rebar/_store/push.py:606-629) resolves `info/exclude`, reads it, computes the missing patterns, and appends them with a buffered `open(..., "a")` that can issue TWO writes (a leading newline, then the patterns). It is called at push.py:651, BEFORE the write lock is taken — deliberately, since the exclusion must exist before anything can stage — so two first-time callers genuinely race here.

Two racing buffered appends can interleave at the byte level and tear a pattern into a corrupt half-line (e.g. `.ticket-write.lo`), which would silently stop excluding the lock artifact. That is the real hazard; a duplicated WHOLE line is not.

Test coverage gaps in tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py (331 lines): the existing tests cover `git add` / `git commit` failure (line 190), lock failure (228), the recovery guard (156), push-only (259) and the CLI (277). Nothing directly covers the exclusion-write failure gate (push.py:651-655), the `git status` failure gate (push.py:673-678), or proves that lock artifacts stay out of a real commit.

## Plan

1. push.py `_ignore_lock_artifacts`: hoist the pattern tuple to a module constant and replace the
   buffered two-write append with a SINGLE `os.write` to an `O_WRONLY|O_APPEND` descriptor. POSIX
   applies that one write at end-of-file atomically, so a racing pair can no longer tear a
   pattern. Document in the docstring that a duplicated whole line remains possible and is the
   deliberate disposition — git applies a repeated exclude pattern identically, so the file stays
   semantically idempotent, and removing the duplicate would require a lock this function must
   not take (it runs before the write lock and stays outside the recovery guard, both unchanged).
   Do not change the read-failure disposition (`OSError` still returns False / fails closed).
   Scope note: single-write `O_APPEND` atomicity is a POSIX guarantee, which matches this
   project's declared support surface — pyproject.toml classifies it `Operating System :: POSIX`
   and `MacOS :: MacOS X` (no Windows classifier) and every CI job runs on `ubuntu-latest`. The
   docstring states that scope rather than implying a universal guarantee.
2. Tests, added to the held-out file:
   - exclusion-write failure, strict and default: force `_ignore_lock_artifacts` to fail and
     assert strict raises `PushDeliveryError` with reason `stage-failed` while default logs a
     warning and returns; the dirty content is retained and a clean retry commits and delivers.
   - `git status` failure, strict and default: same split, same retained-content + clean-retry
     oracle, reaching the push.py:673-678 branch specifically.
   - real legacy-tracker commit: with both lock artifacts present on disk, commit and assert via
     `git ls-tree -r` that neither `.ticket-write.lock` nor anything under `.ticket-write.lock.d/`
     entered the committed tree, and that a clean retry succeeds.
   - concurrent first use: run the exclude update from several workers against one fresh tracker
     and assert every line of `info/exclude` is a whole, intact pattern (no torn line) and both
     patterns are present.
3. Keep push.py within the 800-line module-size gate — it is at 789 today, so the change must be
   close to net-neutral.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py -q` (the held-out commit-and-push suite).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -k "push" -q` (the push-only compatibility suites).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.
- `awk 'END{print NR}' src/rebar/_store/push.py` stays at or below the 800 in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Concurrent first use cannot corrupt local exclude metadata on the supported POSIX platforms; duplicate-line disposition is documented or eliminated. Proved by the concurrent-first-use test asserting no torn line.
- [x] AC2 — Strict and default exclusion/status failures are directly covered with observable typed-error or warning/return outcomes. Proved by the four new failure tests (`stage-failed` reason vs caplog warning + return).
- [x] AC3 — A real legacy tracker commit proves lock artifacts are absent from the resulting commit and a clean retry succeeds. Proved by the `git ls-tree -r` oracle over the committed tree.
- [x] AC4 — Existing push-only and commit-and-push compatibility suites remain green, checked by the pytest commands above; `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass and push.py stays within the module-size gate.
baseline.summary: Harden lock-artifact exclusion metadata and failure coverage

baseline.description:
# Give Cloud the resilience and config-validation coverage DC gained

## Context

Epic e369 hardened the DC adapter against a real instance and produced a tier of coverage Cloud never had. Cloud's tests grew from INCIDENTS THAT HAPPENED; DC's grew from CONFIGURATIONS THAT DIFFER. The second kind generalises, and Cloud does not have it.

This story is the Cloud half of the parity work. It is lower priority than [rebar:0fad-59f7-1605-4377] (Cloud's unpaginated whole-project readers) because Cloud is the mature, live-exercised path — but each item below is a real asymmetry, not a symmetry exercise.

## The gaps, with what DC has for comparison

**1. No per-member 429 sweep.** DC's `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` walks EVERY mutating transport member and asserts each fails on the first 429 — because retrying a mutation on an HTTP error is the duplicate-issue class [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] fixed, and an enumeration is what stops a later-added mutation inheriting a retry by omission. Cloud has `test_retry_httperror.py` (5 tests) and one 429 path in `state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:352-368`, neither of which sweeps the member set.

**DC's property does NOT transfer uniformly, and assuming it does is the main risk in this item.** Cloud has no single choke point; its mutations traverse FOUR distinct 429 behaviours across two levels, all verified in the tree. Two are transport-level and DELIBERATELY OPPOSITE:

* **direct REST** (`AcliRestMixin._rest_urlopen_with_retry`) — "Does NOT retry on
  `urllib.error.HTTPError` (4xx / 5xx)" (`adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:50-52`). A 429 arrives as
  `urllib.error.HTTPError`. Here DC's property holds verbatim: exactly ONE attempt.
* **ACLI subprocess** (`acli_subprocess._run_acli`) — **already RETRIES a 429**, on purpose, via
  `_rate_limit_backoff` honouring `Retry-After`; `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff`
  (`state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:369`) asserts the call SUCCEEDS on retry. A 429 here is an
  exit code plus `429` in stderr, not an HTTP exception.

…and ABOVE both sits the reconciler's dispatch level, which is the part most likely to be missed — and it is itself SPLIT IN TWO:

* **the retrying dispatch wrapper** — `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
  (`dispatch_one.py:71`) catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and, when `exc.code == 429`, records
  `Retry-After` and RETRIES (`dispatch_one.py:115-118`). So a REST mutation that makes exactly one
  attempt when its transport method is called DIRECTLY is nevertheless retried when reached the way
  production reaches it.
* **the explicitly NON-retrying apply phases** — `dispatch_apply_phases`, whose module docstring
  states it owns "the phases that do NOT funnel their Jira writes through
  `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`". These include real mutations:
  `_update_one_apply_reporter` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:96`) and
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:147`, the single-attempt comment dispatch). A 429 here is a
  FOURTH behaviour — neither the subprocess backoff nor the dispatch-wrapper retry applies — and
  existing coverage (`test_comment_single_attempt.py`) pins attempt count for ONE member, not a
  sweep.

So "every mutating member fails on the first 429" is TRUE for a raw REST transport method called directly, TRUE again for the non-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` mutations, and FALSE for both the subprocess seam and anything routed through the retrying dispatch wrapper. **An attempt-count assertion is therefore meaningless unless it names the BOUNDARY it measures at.** Writing the DC assertion across all four would either fail immediately or pressure someone into deleting an intentional, tested backoff. This story must establish the split FIRST and assert a per-layer property — and it must not fold in a behaviour change (below).

**The two retries named above are KNOWN and DELIBERATE — they are not the bug trigger.** Both `_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff and `_call_with_retry`'s 429 branch are already implemented, tested and documented, so "a mutation is retried on a 429" is not by itself a finding; the enumeration will hit them by construction. The bug-filing trigger is NARROWER: a mutating member retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already explicitly tested and documented — an UNDOCUMENTED or newly-discovered retry path. That is the [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] duplicate class. If one is found, file a linked bug with the evidence and do NOT "fix" it inside this test story. Separately, if the enumeration shows a KNOWN retry applying to a mutation in a way nobody has evaluated for duplicate-write safety, record that assessment on this ticket — as a finding, not as a code change.

**2. No config-validation tier.** DC asserts a non-HTTPS base URL is rejected, that the insecure override warns, that malformed config propagates, and that a missing credential fails loudly rather than going anonymous (`test_jira_dc_config_settings.py`, `test_dc_pat_required_heldout.py` — the latter exists because bug cd78 was exactly a silent fall-back to ANONYMOUS access). Cloud has no equivalent. Whether Cloud CAN go anonymous is itself unestablished and worth answering.

**3. The probe's resolved-status set is not runtime-configurable.** `adapters/jira/probe.py:39` pins `frozenset({"Resolved","Done","Cancelled"})`; DC threads `resolved_statuses` from settings and tests it. Cloud's `probe_remote` also re-resolves env itself rather than using the transport's configured session.

**"Is it deliberate?" is already answered — do NOT re-open it.** `probe.py`'s module docstring (`:20-25`) states that J2 moved the pure classifier to `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` taking the status set as a PARAMETER, and that `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` "is Cloud/DIG's *configured value* (a self-hosted Data Center workflow can name its resolved states anything), so it stays defined here". So it is documented as deliberate at the definition site, and an AC satisfied by "document it" would be satisfied by doing nothing. The remaining OPEN question is narrower and is the only one this item answers: **does a Cloud deployment whose workflow uses non-standard resolved-status names need a runtime config hook** (as DC has), or is the per-deployment constant genuinely sufficient? Record THAT decision with its rationale; if a hook is needed, file it as its own ticket.

**4. `search_user_by_email` degradation is unasserted on DC** (the mirror-image item, kept here so the pair is not split). `outbound_assignee.py:33-37` resolves the user-search method by NAME STRING across three aliases; DC provides none of them, so `_bootstrap_account_id_via_user_search` returns `None` and the path degrades to string matching. That degradation is probably correct — DC has no accountId concept — but nothing asserts it, so an accidental rename on the Cloud side would look like the same silence.

## Approach

Take these in the order above; 1 and 2 carry the risk, 3 is an investigation that may produce a ticket rather than a test, 4 is a one-test pin.

**Port the PROPERTY, not the test — and note the property is PER-LAYER.** Cloud's retry lives in a different place from DC's, so a copied test would assert the wrong seam. What must survive the port is the ENUMERATION — that every mutating member is named explicitly, because an ellipsis is how the next mutation inherits a retry.

**Step 0 for item 1, before any test is written:** enumerate every mutating member of Cloud's transport and classify each on BOTH axes, by reading bodies rather than inferring from names:

1. **transport seam** — one of THREE: ACLI subprocess (`_run_acli`); pooled direct REST
   (`_rest_urlopen_with_retry` / `_direct_rest_post_raw` / `_direct_rest_put_raw`); or **bare
   `urllib.request.urlopen`**, which bypasses `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` entirely and therefore does
   not even inherit its transient-fault retry — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority`
   (`acli_cli_ops.py:396`, urlopen at `:437`) is a confirmed instance, reached in production because
   `AcliClient.update_issue` delegates to the free function `update_issue` (`acli.py:374`), which
   calls `update_priority` when `priority` is among the changed fields (`acli.py:180`). A member with
   more than one leg (e.g. a REST leg and a subprocess leg) is called out as such.
2. **dispatch level** — which of THREE the reconciler uses: the retrying wrapper
   `dispatch_one._call_with_retry` (`dispatch_one.py:71`), which adds a 429 retry ON TOP of
   whatever the seam does; the explicitly non-retrying apply phases in `dispatch_apply_phases`
   (`_update_one_apply_reporter:96`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments:147`); or no dispatch wrapper at
   all. Determine this by reading the call site, since the module split is by RETRY POLICY, so the
   answer is not inferable from the member's own body.

**Completeness check for the table, run and recorded alongside it** — the table gates the whole item, so its coverage must be demonstrated, not asserted. Enumerate the candidate surface with a concrete command and account for EVERY name it returns:

    git grep -nE "^(    )?def [_a-z]" -- \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py

Three things about that pattern are deliberate, and each one is a way the table can look complete while omitting a writer:

* it matches BOTH indented class methods AND module-level free functions;
* it includes `_`-PREFIXED names — `acli_graph._add_label_impl:144` and `_remove_label_impl:204` are
  mutating, as are the `_direct_rest_*` helpers in `acli_rest.py`, and a `def [a-z]` pattern would
  emit none of them, so the "every name it returns is classified" rule would be satisfied vacuously;
* `acli_cli_ops.py` is in the file list, because `AcliClient` delegates real mutations to free
  functions there (`create_issue:147`, `update_priority:396`, `add_comment:469`).

Record that raw output as a REPO ARTIFACT beside the table (in the sweep module's header comment, where the table lives) and mirror it onto the ticket. Every name in it is either classified in the table or explicitly marked NON-MUTATING with a one-line reason — no name may be silently absent. Cross-check the mutating set against DC's enumerated list in `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` and record any member DC sweeps that Cloud's table lacks, or vice versa, with the reason.

The table decides, per member, which property is asserted and at which boundary it is observed — and a member can legitimately have DIFFERENT correct answers at the two levels (one attempt raw, retried when dispatch-wrapped).

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — Cloud 429 sweep, Cloud config-validation tests, a DC
  user-search-degradation pin.
- an investigation note (or a linked bug) on the Cloud probe's hardcoded resolved statuses.
- the per-member seam classification table for item 1 (recorded on the ticket, not in code).
- No production change intended. Items 1 and 3 may each produce a linked BUG — item 1 only if a
  mutating member is retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already tested and
  documented (the two known deliberate retries do not count), item 3 if the hardcoded
  resolved-status set is an accident — and in both cases the fix is its own ticket, never folded in
  here.

## Testing

The 429 sweep must assert the ATTEMPT COUNT per member, not merely that an exception escaped — an implementation that retried and then re-raised satisfies a raises-only assertion having issued the write twice. This is the same correction being applied to DC's own sweep in [rebar:2944-dd3f-e982-4359]; do not copy that mistake forward.

**The instrument differs per seam, and a single patch point covers only half the members** — a sweep that patches `urllib.request.urlopen` is blind to subprocess mutations, and one that patches `acli_subprocess._run_acli` is blind to REST mutations, while either LOOKS complete because every member still raises. So:

* POOLED REST-seam members, called DIRECTLY on the transport (not through the dispatch wrapper) —
  observe attempts at the urlopen boundary; inject a 429 as `urllib.error.HTTPError`; assert EXACTLY
  ONE attempt (no retry), matching `acli_rest.py:50-52`.
* BARE-`urlopen` members — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority` (`:396`, urlopen at `:437`) bypasses
  `_rest_urlopen_with_retry`, so it has no retry of its own: assert EXACTLY ONE attempt there too.

  **One patch point covers both, and per-module patching is NOT a real isolation mechanism.** Both
  `acli_rest.py` (`:23`) and `acli_cli_ops.py` (`:24`) do `import urllib.request` — a MODULE-object
  binding — so both resolve `urlopen` at call time through the same shared `urllib.request` object.
  Patching it once affects both; `mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:160` already relies on
  exactly that, calling it "the process-wide `urllib.request.urlopen` (a shared singleton)". So
  patch it once and distinguish the seams by WHICH MEMBER was invoked and what the captured request
  looks like — not by which module the patch was applied through. Coverage of both seams must
  therefore be proven by ENUMERATION (every member in the table has a case) rather than by any
  assumed namespace separation.
* the DISPATCH-WRAPPED path — the same members reached through `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
  DO retry a 429 by design (`dispatch_one.py:115-118`). Assert the retry is bounded and honours
  `Retry-After`; do NOT assert one attempt here. This is the layer where "is a MUTATION being
  retried on a 429?" is actually decided, so it is the layer the bug-filing trigger below applies to.
* subprocess-seam members — observe attempts at the `_run_acli`/`Popen` boundary; inject a 429 as
  the exit-code + `429`-in-stderr shape the existing test uses; assert the OBSERVED, INTENDED
  behaviour (a bounded retry honouring `Retry-After`, per
  `state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:369`) rather than one attempt — and record whether that
  retry applies to a MUTATION, which is the bug-filing trigger above.

Each seam's sweep must be MUTATION-CHECKED at its own instrument: make one member issue an extra attempt at that boundary and confirm THAT seam's sweep goes red — proving the sweep is not blind to the half it is supposed to cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] every MUTATING Cloud transport member is enumerated explicitly — no ellipsis, no sampling —
      and classified on BOTH axes: transport seam (ACLI subprocess / pooled direct REST / bare
      `urllib.request.urlopen`) and dispatch
      level (retrying `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, the explicitly NON-retrying
      `dispatch_apply_phases` phases, or no wrapper). The table ALSO carries, for every member that
      reaches a mutation through a KNOWN deliberate retry (`dispatch_one._call_with_retry` or
      `_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff), a "Duplicate-write safe? [reason]" column recording the
      duplicate-write assessment for that member — so the assessment is a repo artifact, not a
      tracker-only note. The table lands as a REPO ARTIFACT — the sweep test module's own enumeration
      plus a header comment carrying the per-member classification and that duplicate-write-safety
      column, which is where a reviewer will look — and is mirrored onto this ticket
- [x] the table's COMPLETENESS is demonstrated, not asserted: the enumeration command from Step 0 is
      run, its raw output recorded beside the table, and every name it returns is either classified
      or marked NON-MUTATING with a reason — plus the DC cross-check for members present on one side
      and missing on the other
- [x] each POOLED-REST and each BARE-`urlopen` mutating member, invoked DIRECTLY on the transport, is
      asserted to make EXACTLY ONE attempt under a 429, observed at the shared process-wide
      `urllib.request.urlopen`, with one case PER MEMBER from the table — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority`
      explicitly among them
- [x] the DISPATCH-WRAPPED path is covered separately: reached through
      `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, a 429 IS retried by design (`dispatch_one.py:115-118`), so the
      assertion there is a BOUNDED retry honouring `Retry-After` — not one attempt
- [x] each subprocess-seam mutating member is asserted against its ACTUAL intended 429 behaviour —
      the bounded `Retry-After` backoff in `_run_acli` — observed at the `_run_acli` boundary. This
      criterion is NOT satisfied by asserting one attempt there, because
      `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff` proves the retry is deliberate
- [x] mutations reached through the NON-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` path
      (`_update_one_apply_reporter`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`) are asserted to make exactly
      one attempt under a 429 — extending `test_comment_single_attempt.py`'s single-member pin to
      the sweep
- [x] if a MUTATING member is retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already tested and
      documented, a linked bug is filed with the evidence. The two KNOWN deliberate retries
      (`_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff, `_call_with_retry`'s 429 branch) do NOT by themselves
      trigger a bug; where one applies to a mutation, the duplicate-write assessment is RECORDED in
      the sweep module's "Duplicate-write safe? [reason]" table column (the authoritative repo
      artifact) and mirrored onto this ticket — never ticket-only. This story changes NO retry
      behaviour either way
- [x] Cloud rejects a non-HTTPS base URL, or the test records that it deliberately does not
- [x] Cloud's behaviour on a MISSING credential is asserted: it must fail loudly, or the test pins
      that it does not and a bug is filed (this is bug cd78's shape on the other adapter)
- [x] the OPEN question on the Cloud probe's resolved-status set is answered: whether a Cloud
      deployment using non-standard resolved-status names needs a runtime config hook as DC has, or
      whether the per-deployment constant suffices. The DECIDING CRITERION is whether a Cloud
      deployment can rename its resolved-status workflow states WITHOUT a rebar code change: if
      `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` is compiled into the adapter and no per-tenant override path exists, a
      deployment with non-standard names is mis-probed and a runtime hook is warranted (file it);
      if such names cannot occur on Cloud (a documented workflow constraint) the constant suffices.
      The answer lands as a REPO ARTIFACT, not only a ticket comment — a comment at `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` in `adapters/jira/probe.py` recording the
      decision and citing this ticket id (plus the follow-up ticket id if a hook is needed) — so a
      reviewer can find it without the tracker. Re-documenting it as merely "deliberate" does NOT
      satisfy this: `probe.py:20-25` already says so, and an AC already true on an unmodified tree is
      not a criterion
- [x] a test pins that DC exposes none of `_USER_SEARCH_METHODS` and that the bootstrap degrades to
      the string-match path rather than raising
- [x] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED. "Mutation-checked" here means a CONCRETE MANUAL mutation,
      not a mutation-testing tool: for each new test, apply the named perturbation below, run that
      test module, record it RED with its pass/fail counts, revert, record it GREEN again. Both
      verdicts go in a REPO-VISIBLE place — the commit/Gerrit change description of the change that
      adds the tests, listing per test the mutation applied and the RED/GREEN pass-fail counts — as
      well as on this ticket, so the evidence is reviewable from the change itself and survives
      independently of the tracker. The named mutations are: for a REST-seam sweep, make one member retry
      once at the urlopen boundary (the `== 1` attempt assertion must go red); for a subprocess-seam
      sweep, SUPPRESS the retry outright — cap `_run_acli`'s attempt loop at one, or make it re-raise
      on a 429 exit without looping — so the ATTEMPT-COUNT assertion goes red. Note what does NOT
      work: making `_rate_limit_backoff` return `None` does not remove the retry at all, because
      `acli_subprocess.py:429` is
      `_backoff_sleep(rl_delay if rl_delay is not None else 2 ** (attempt + 1))` — a `None` merely
      swaps `Retry-After` for a uniform exponential delay and the call is still retried;
      for the non-HTTPS-URL test, FIRST establish whether Cloud has a scheme rejection at all —
      `_validate_reconci … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Cloud resilience + config-validation coverage, matching DC's

baseline.description:
## Context

Auditors need to review, for one work ticket, what the automated LLM review gates decided: the latest plan review, the completion-verification result, and the latest associated code review, alongside the ticket's current details — with the ability to navigate the history of plan and code reviews and to see each review's full four-pass breakdown (pass-1 findings, pass-2 verification, pass-3 determination with thresholds, pass-4 coaching). The audit data is made lossless and readable by the data-enrichment epic (a hard dependency; see the linked `depends_on` epic).

This epic delivers that as an OPTIONAL, disabled-by-default, read-only local web UI.

## Data contract (the named interface Epic 1 must expose)

This UI is a pure function of the enriched fields the data-enrichment epic (Epic 1) persists per finding and per criterion. The two epics share THIS named interface — Epic 1 delivers it (via story A's plan-review v2 `_slim`, story B's code-review v2 payload, and story C's completion `criteria[]`), Epic 2 consumes it. The minimal enriched field set is:

| Consumer (UI region)          | Source (Epic 1)                        | Required fields                                                                                                                              |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Finding-provenance (per finding) | plan-review v2 (story A) / code-review v2 (story B) | `finding`, `criteria`, `location`, `evidence`, `scenarios`, `impact`, `suggested_fix`, `verification`, `validity`, `priority`, `decision`, `reason`, `block_threshold`, `blocking_enabled` |
| Round history + convergence   | plan-/code-review sidecar history      | full retained per-round sidecars (newest-first) + each round's `coaching[]` (`{move_id, finding_refs}`)                                        |
| Threshold meter (per finding) | plan-/code-review v2                    | the finding's resolved (per-finding) `block_threshold` + `blocking_enabled` + `priority` + `decision`                                          |
| Completion panel (per criterion) | completion `criteria[]` (story C)     | `criteria[]` of `{criterion, met, citation, kind}` where `kind ∈ {codebase-verifiable, operator-attested}`                                     |

`block_threshold` is the PER-FINDING resolved value each finding was judged against (persisted by stories A/B), NOT a round-level scalar. The completion panel's per-criterion rows have NO source in the pre-enrichment completion verdict (findings are failures-only); they are PRODUCED by story C's `criteria[]`. This epic MUST NOT proceed to render a region until its Epic 1 field source has landed.

## Approach rationale

Server-rendered FastAPI + Jinja2, REUSING the `reviewbot` extra's already-shipped web stack rather than adding a second web framework, bound to loopback only, with no client build step. This fits a read-only, low-traffic, single-user audit view and reuses proven in-repo machinery (the reviewbot FastAPI app is the established "thin, lazily-imported, never-required-by-core" precedent). The alternative of a static HTML export was weighed and rejected for v1: the audit data is naturally navigable (history rounds, drill-in) and replay is cheap, which a point-in-time static dump serves poorly.

## Scope

- IN: the optional web-server surface (subcommand, config flag, `[ui]` extra, lazy import, loopback
  binding) and the per-ticket audit page rendering.
- OUT: any data-model/sidecar change (owned by the dependency epic — the Data-contract fields above
  are DELIVERED by Epic 1, not by this epic); network exposure / multi-user auth; write/edit actions
  (the UI is strictly read-only).

## Compatibility & rollback

The whole feature is default-off (`[ui] enabled = false`) and its web deps live in a new `nava-rebar[ui]` extra, lazy-imported — so it is inert when disabled and when the extra is absent. Rollback is turning the flag off / not installing the extra; no data or schema change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both child stories are closed.
- [ ] The page is navigable across the retained review history for BOTH plan review AND code review:
      an OLDER round (not just the latest) of EACH can be selected and its distinct content renders.
      Oracle: a live end-to-end test seeding ≥2 plan-review rounds AND ≥2 code-review rounds on one
      ticket, selecting the older round in each gate, and asserting each renders its (distinct from
      latest) content.
- [ ] With the feature enabled, `rebar audit serve` serves a ticket audit page showing the ticket
      details and the plan/completion/code panels with pass-1..4 detail, per-finding resolved
      thresholds, and the completion `criteria[]` rows. Oracle: a live end-to-end test that starts
      the server and asserts on the rendered response.
- [ ] With the feature disabled (default), no web dependency is imported and all existing commands
      behave unchanged. Oracle: a test asserting the server is not started and `import rebar` needs
      no web dep.
- [ ] A `rebar audit serve` subcommand starts a read-only web server, gated OFF by default, that renders
- [ ] With the feature disabled (default) and its extra not installed, rebar behaves exactly as today
baseline.summary: Ticket audit-trail UI (optional, disabled by default)

Independent seam review (2026-08-05) of the completion-recovery chain found: in `CompletionAgentStep._recover` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py), the prelude `ticket = _reads.show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=ctx.repo_root)` executes inside the `except LLMBudgetExhaustedError` handler but BEFORE the `try:` whose `except LLMError` is the only place `self.failure_diagnostic` is built. `show_ticket` raises `RebarError` (not LLMError) on a missing id or a store that fails to reduce; that raise escapes `_recover`, `_run_leaf` flattens it to StepResult(status="failed"), `failure_diagnostic` stays None, and `raise_completion_workflow_failure` takes the bare-LLMError branch: no gate error sidecar, no aggregate_* keys — the primary run's already-computed budget and repetition diagnostic is dropped in full. Total evidence loss on a narrow trigger.

## Plan
Move the prelude (at minimum the `show_ticket` call) inside the existing try so a prelude failure lands in the `stage="preflight"` arm, which already prefixes and preserves the primary diagnostic.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A `RebarError` raised by `show_ticket` during recovery produces a
      CompletionRecoveryError whose diagnostic carries the primary run's
      aggregate_* repetition/budget keys (unit test, held-out).
- [x] The gate-error sidecar is emitted on that path.
- [x] The happy path and the existing recovery-failure paths are unchanged
      (existing suite green).
baseline.summary: completion recovery prelude failure drops primary diagnostic

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Private aliases remain across plan-review orchestrator sizing/context/move registries, runner Anthropic/tool/structured-run names, workflow gate-dispatch recovery names, and `llm.config` gate-context names. `llm.usage_log.failure_usage` also misnames the neutral `run_shape` record and has live callers. The governing private-shim policy is the direct prerequisite ADR `earthen-wheat-chick`; the parent container is ordered after the LLM configuration-reader extraction.

## Approach

After the prerequisite ADR and configuration-reader extraction complete, migrate every consumer to `plan_review.sizing`, `context_assembly`, `passes`, `anthropic_model`, `runner_support`, `structured_run`, `workflow.plan_review_recovery`, and `llm.gate_context`. Rename `failure_usage` completely to `run_shape` and prove emitted dictionaries and durable JSONL rows are byte/field identical. Remove each old private binding only after semantic and raw dynamic/monkeypatch census is empty.

## Scope

- plan-review, runner, workflow-dispatch, and gate-context private re-exports
- usage-log implementation, callers, docs, experiment prose, and JSONL tests
- all source/test/string/dynamic/monkeypatch consumers

## Testing

Run focused plan-review/workflow/runner suites; compare old/new usage record dictionaries and JSONL rows across success and failure paths; run semantic and raw reference scans.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every enumerated old LLM/workflow private binding has no repository consumer and its named canonical owner is the sole binding.
- [ ] `failure_usage` is absent and `run_shape` owns all former behavior.
- [ ] Success and failure records retain byte/field-identical dictionaries and durable JSONL rows after the rename.
- [ ] Gate-context, plan-review recovery, runner, and workflow behavior remain covered by focused tests.
- [ ] Static, string, dynamic-import, `getattr`, and monkeypatch census proves old paths absent.
baseline.summary: Migrate and remove LLM, plan-review, and workflow internal shims

# The close gate offers `--force-close` as the remedy for a RESOURCE exhaustion

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a].

When completion verification fails for ANY reason, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:293-297` appends `Override with --force-close="<reason>".` to the error. That is correct for a verdict the operator wants to overrule. It is wrong for a **resource** failure, where no verdict exists at all.

A step-budget exhaustion is not a judgment that the work is incomplete — it is the gate failing to finish evaluating. Conflating the two points the operator at the one action the project forbids: a force-closed ticket is the unattested state epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] spent its whole cycle removing, and the reason [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260] and [rebar:0059-c7f0-cce1-4077] were reopened. Same shape as the certification trap in [rebar:738a-376e-4829-42ca]: two individually correct rules composing into a state whose only reachable exit is the forbidden one.

The remedy text itself was already narrowed once for this class — `close_gate_remedy` (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:522-550`) stops blaming a missing `[agents]` extra for a verifier that provably ran (bug d59e). This is the same correction one step further out: the `--force-close` sentence is appended unconditionally, after the remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a completion verification that fails from RESOURCE exhaustion (step budget / iteration cap)
      does not present `--force-close` as its remedy
- [ ] the message instead names the actionable next move for a resource failure and points at the
      recorded diagnostic
- [ ] a genuine FAIL verdict still offers `--force-close` exactly as today (regression pinned)
- [ ] a test asserts the two failure classes produce different remedy text
baseline.summary: Close gate offers --force-close as the remedy for a RESOURCE exhaustion, steering agents into the unattested state

## Context / Problem

Two backend-neutral core modules load Jira rich-text/limit modules by literal lazy-load key and run them unconditionally — for ANY configured backend:

- `outbound_comments.py:68` (`_ADF_KEY = "rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf"`, loaded at
  `:75-85`) and `outbound_comments.py:71` (`_COMMENT_LIMITS_KEY =
  "rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.comment_limits"`, loaded at `:88`) — comment-body
  formatting/truncation on the outbound comment-diff path.
- `inbound_translate.py:315` (`_ADF_KEY_APPLIER`, loaded at `:319-324`) —
  `_normalize_adf_body` decodes a raw ADF dict to text as defense-in-depth on the inbound
  apply path (bug 1bb2-5da5).

A GitHub/Linear backend would still have its comments ADF-encoded and Jira-limit-truncated. These literal keys are the last vendor reach-through in neutral core paths after the sibling stories land; epic bbf1's separation goal ("a second backend drops in behind the port") requires them behind the port.

## Approach

Route both modules through the port roles that already own these responsibilities:

- `FieldSanitizer` (already pinned in `_backend.py` as the vendor hard-limit defense, with the
  existing SEND-side `sanitize_comment(body: str) -> str`, which truncates AND logs a warning)
  gains ONE new method, `fit_comment(body: str) -> str` — a PURE fit-to-limit for the
  comment-DIFF comparison path (`outbound_comments.py:324`), delegating to
  `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`'s `truncate_comment_body` with NO warning (the compare
  path must not emit send-side warnings). `fit_comment` is the single, consistently-named
  comment-fit surface used throughout this plan; `adapters/jira/adf.py` provides only the
  DECODE (`adf_to_text`), which is served by `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` (below), NOT
  by the fit surface.
  `outbound_comments.py` resolves the configured backend's sanitizer via the registry seam
  (`select_backend(load_config())` — pattern proven at `outbound_differ.py:450-454`) instead
  of lazy-loading vendor modules, and the two literal keys at `outbound_comments.py:68,71`
  are deleted.
- `InboundMapper` gains `normalize_rich_text(body: Any) -> str` (Jira: `adf_to_text` for
  dicts, identity for strings — exactly today's `_normalize_adf_body`,
  `inbound_translate.py:349+`). `inbound_translate.py` calls the backend's inbound mapper;
  the literal key at `inbound_translate.py:315` is deleted. The defense-in-depth property
  (a raw vendor rich-text dict on the wire never reaches an EDIT event's `description`) is
  preserved backend-neutrally.
- Add a sweep case to `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`: no
  package-root core module contains the literal string `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"`,
  with a single recorded exemption for `inbound_fields.py:24` — that module IS the Jira
  `InboundMapper` implementation (delegated by `adapters/jira/backend.py:43-47`) that
  remains at the package root only for loader location-pinning reasons; its physical
  relocation is out of this epic's scope and tracked by follow-up ticket
  `556a-5a1f-adb3-4139` (linked `discovered_from` epic bbf1).

Rejected alternatives: (a) a new sixth role Protocol ("RichTextCodec") — YAGNI: FieldSanitizer already owns vendor-limit defense per its `_backend.py` docstring and InboundMapper already owns vendor→local payload translation; fewer than 3 call sites for a new role. (b) Leaving the lazy keys because "they are only strings, not imports" — the loader still executes vendor code on neutral paths for any backend, which is the substance of the leak.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (FieldSanitizer comment-fit surface; InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py (route via sanitizer; delete both literal keys)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py (route via inbound mapper; delete the literal key)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (implement the new members, delegating to adf/comment_limits)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py (Jira mapper: normalize_rich_text implementation)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (literal-key sweep with the recorded inbound_fields.py exemption)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (comment formatting/truncation + normalize_rich_text behavior tests)

## Testing

- Happy path: an outbound comment body formats and truncates byte-identically to today via
  the sanitizer route; a plain-string inbound description passes through
  `normalize_rich_text` unchanged.
- Failure/edge: an over-limit comment truncates with today's marker semantics; a raw ADF dict
  arriving on the inbound apply path is decoded to text and never written verbatim into an
  EDIT event (the bug 1bb2-5da5 regression case, now backend-neutral).
- Gate: the sweep case fails when any package-root core module (except the recorded
  `inbound_fields.py` exemption) contains the `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"` literal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `outbound_comments.py` and `inbound_translate.py` contain neither `adapters.jira`
      imports nor `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"` lazy-key literals — verified by the new
      sweep case in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`.
- [ ] Comment formatting/truncation and inbound rich-text normalization behave identically
      for Jira — verified by the behavior tests in Testing (including the 1bb2-5da5
      regression case).
- [ ] The sweep gate documents the single `inbound_fields.py` exemption with its rationale
      and the follow-up ticket id — verified by reading the gate test.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Plan-review remediation (drift re-review, G1G2 findings)

Three under-scoped consumer surfaces are pinned here so no lazy-key deletion orphans a caller:

1. **Outbound-comment ADF DECODE (`outbound_comments.py:134`).** `_normalize_comment_body`
   calls `adf.adf_to_text(body)` to DECODE a remote Jira ADF comment dict to comparable text on
   the comment-DIFF path (bug 85a1) — a decode, not a send-side fit/truncate. It routes through
   the backend's `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text(body)` (the SAME decode surface as the
   inbound apply path: `adf_to_text` for dicts, identity for strings). `normalize_rich_text`
   therefore serves BOTH the inbound apply path AND this outbound comment-diff decode;
   `FieldSanitizer.fit_comment(body)` (a pure fit-to-limit, delegating to
   `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`, no send-side warning) serves the `:324` compare-body
   truncation. `outbound_comments.py` obtains BOTH the sanitizer and the inbound mapper from the
   one `select_backend(load_config())` it resolves, and BOTH literal keys at `:68,71` are deleted.

2. **`inbound_translate`'s PUBLIC decode surface (`_normalize_adf_body`).** This function is
   re-exported by `applier.py` (`__all__` lines 322/326/361/367) and imported + called at three
   sites by `apply_inbound_records.py` (lines 35, 145, 268, 308). It therefore STAYS as
   inbound_translate's public function, re-implemented to route through the backend's
   `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text(body)` (resolved via `select_backend(load_config())`), so
   BOTH consumers keep working unchanged and the bug-1bb2-5da5 defense (a raw ADF dict never
   reaches an EDIT event `description`) stays intact and backend-neutral. Only the vendor
   internals `_ADF_KEY_APPLIER` (the literal), `_AdfModule_Applier`, and `_load_adf_module` are
   deleted from `inbound_translate.py`. Because `applier.py` re-exports those three now-deleted
   names, `applier.py` drops them from its `inbound_translate` import list and from `__all__`
   (keeping `_normalize_adf_body`); `apply_inbound_records.py` is untouched.

3. **Scope additions:** `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` (drop the three dead
   re-exports; keep `_normalize_adf_body`).

**AC3 restated machine-executably:** the single-`inbound_fields.py`-exemption sweep is verified by the test `test_no_root_core_module_carries_vendor_lazyload_literal` passing (green with exactly that one exemption) plus a companion `test_sweep_exemption_is_still_needed` asserting inbound_fields.py genuinely still carries the literal — both under `make test`, not by human inspection.

**Added acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The outbound-comment ADF decode at `_normalize_comment_body:134` routes through
      `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` (NOT orphaned by the `_ADF_KEY` deletion); comment-diff
      dedup normalizes ADF-dict bodies to text byte-identically — verified by a comment-diff test
      with an ADF-dict remote body.
- [ ] `inbound_translate._normalize_adf_body` STAYS importable and routes through the port;
      `applier.py` no longer imports/re-exports `_ADF_KEY_APPLIER`/`_AdfModule_Applier`/
      `_load_adf_module`; `apply_inbound_records.py`'s three call sites behave identically
      (ADF dict -> text) — verified by the behavior tests plus a green import of both modules.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 936 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Rich-text codec and comment limits behind the port: delete the adapters.jira lazy-key literals from core

## Why

Static wiring tests cannot prove that an LLM criterion distinguishes concrete breakage scenarios from harmless silence or valid project customization. A balanced, repeatable evaluation is needed before the blocking project criterion is considered ready.

## What

Add a project criterion evaluation corpus, add structural tests for that corpus, run the existing live evaluation runner, and tune only the project rubric if calibration exposes false positives or missed portability failures.

## Scope

In scope:

- `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`, only for calibration-driven rubric adjustments
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py`
- live evaluation of `project.portability`

Out of scope:

- core registry, verifier, or disposition changes
- coaching move behavior
- existing portability debt
- adding requirements for client-agnostic wording

## Approach

Use the existing project eval override path proven by `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/README.plan-review.md`: `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` resolves for logical criterion `project.portability`. Author this exact top-level contract:

- `prompt: plan-review-project-portability`
- `model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`
- `epochs: 3`
- `gate: at_least(2)`
- `coverage_threshold: 1.0`
- one deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer
- a balanced `dataset` plus a non-empty `gold_set`

The dataset contains exactly eight ids. Each must-fire case uses `expect: finding`, includes an inline `input` plan, and uses the existing `note` metadata field. The note is one non-empty string containing the exact labels `Plan citation:`, `Alternate shape:`, `Causal mechanism:`, and `Observable breakage:` with non-whitespace text after every label:

- `PORT-F1`: reusable core adds `rebar landing` with a Gerrit-only push flow; alternate clients do not use this repository policy.
- `PORT-F2`: reusable core adds Python-only review criteria; Java, Next.js, .NET, Ruby, and Terraform projects cannot apply them.
- `PORT-F3`: reusable execution requires the macOS `security` binary; Windows, Linux, and BSD fail before work begins.
- `PORT-F4`: remote MCP derives the target repo from `Path.cwd()` plus unrestricted local filesystem access; a server outside the checkout cannot find or read the project.

Each must-not-fire case uses `expect: pass`:

- `PORT-N1`: the plan is silent about portability and contains no incompatible mechanism.
- `PORT-N2`: Gerrit-specific coaching remains in `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json` project configuration.
- `PORT-N3`: an additive terminal-color feature is explicitly limited to the CLI and leaves library plus MCP behavior unchanged.
- `PORT-N4`: workspace discovery accepts an explicit path and uses portable standard-library filesystem operations.

The `gold_set` contains all eight cases. Each gold entry carries a non-empty `input` scenario description plus a matching `finding` or `pass` `label`. The `finding_contract` test loads the YAML directly and asserts every `PORT-F*` note is a string whose four exact labels are each followed by non-whitespace text; it does not rely on `validate_eval_spec` to interpret note content. Run each dataset case three times through `rebar criteria eval`. The release threshold is recall `1.0`, false-accept rate `0.0`, `agreement: 1.0`, per-case `stability >= 0.6666666667`, and Cohen kappa `>= 0.70`. Kappa is specifically `calibrate_criterion` expected-vs-observed fire/no-fire agreement over the eight dataset cases; it is not `judge_alignment` and requires no LLM-judge scorer. If the threshold is missed, revise only `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` and rerun; do not change the generic registry, Pass 2, or Pass 3. If any model call times out, returns an API error, or produces a partial result, do not attest the partial output. Make at most three complete-command attempts: wait 30 seconds before attempt two and 120 seconds before attempt three. If attempt three fails, stop, leave the criterion uncalibrated, and record each UTC failure time plus error summary on the ticket; a later execution must start a fresh three-attempt sequence.

`tests/unit/test_criteria_eval.py` is the prior art for project prompt-id mapping, injected calibration, metric keys, and N-run stability. The new structural tests use the real eval loader plus `validate_eval_spec`; they use an injected solve function for deterministic metric assertions and never make a billable call.

## Dependencies

Depends on the criterion-integration child because calibration executes the activated project criterion and its authored rubric.

## Test Strategy

Validate corpus structure deterministically, then use the live criterion evaluation command for semantic calibration. Record the model, timestamp, run count, and aggregate metrics on this ticket so the external LLM result is auditable by the completion gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The project eval override resolves from `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k override_resolution`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `prompt: plan-review-project-portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `epochs: 3` plus `gate: at_least(2)`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `coverage_threshold: 1.0`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares one deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The dataset contains exactly `PORT-F1` through `PORT-F4` with `expect: finding`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k balanced_corpus`.
- [ ] The dataset contains exactly `PORT-N1` through `PORT-N4` with `expect: pass`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k balanced_corpus`.
- [ ] Every must-fire case has a non-empty `note` whose four exact labels are followed by non-whitespace text. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k finding_contract`.
- [ ] The must-not-fire cases respectively cover silence, project configuration, explicit surface scoping, plus portable alternatives. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k negative_boundaries`.
- [ ] Every gold entry carries a non-empty `input` plus the expected `label`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k gold_set`.
- [ ] An injected perfect solve returns the exact metric mapping specified in the Approach. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k calibration_metrics`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] One complete CLI result satisfies the exact live threshold mapping in the Approach; a ticket comment records the command, model, UTC timestamp, run count, aggregate metrics, plus every case result. Prove with `.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval project.portability --runs 3 --output json`.
- [ ] No calibration change touches generic implementation under `src/rebar/`. Prove with `test -z "$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- src/rebar)"`.
- [ ] The final project rubric retains every structural marker specified by `immune-floury-toad`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py`.
baseline.summary: Calibrate the portability criterion
