## Summary

`rebar criteria eval <project.criterion>` (and the underlying `calibrate_criterion`) cannot run the LIVE calibration of any project criterion whose logical id contains the `project.` namespace dot, because the physical prompt-id → criterion-id round-trip is lossy.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Activate a project criterion via `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (e.g.
   `project.portability`, `exec: 1-TURN`) with a rubric prompt and an eval fixture
   at `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`.
2. Run `rebar criteria eval project.portability --runs 1 --output json`.

Expected: the criterion runs live over the dataset and prints calibration metrics.

Actual: exits non-zero with `ValueError: no eval solver for prompt 'plan-review-project-portability'` from `eval_solver.run_case`.

## Root Cause

`rebar.llm.evals.eval.calibrate_criterion` computes `prompt_id = criterion_prompt_id("project.portability")` = `plan-review-project-portability` (the forward map replaces `.`→`-`) to load the eval fixture (correct). But the default `_criterion_solver.solve(prompt_id, case)` passes that DASH prompt-id to `eval_solver.run_case`, which resolves the criterion via `_criterion_id(prompt_id)`: it strips the `plan-review-` prefix to `project-portability` (dash) and checks `cid in registry.by_id(repo_root)`. The registry is keyed by the LOGICAL id `project.portability` (dot), so the dash form is never found → `_criterion_id` returns None → `run_case` raises `no eval solver`. Built-in ids (no dot) round-trip fine; only namespaced `project.<name>` criteria break. Confirmed: `_criterion_id("plan-review-project-portability", root)` → None, while `_criterion_id("project.portability", root)` → "project.portability".

## Proposed Fix (one of)

- `_criterion_solver` / `calibrate_criterion`: resolve the criterion in `run_case` from
  the ORIGINAL logical `criterion_id` (dot), using the dash `prompt_id` only for
  `load_eval_spec`; or
- `eval_solver._criterion_id`: after stripping `plan-review-`, also try mapping a leading
  `project-<name>` back to `project.<name>` (the namespaced project-criterion inverse),
  since `<name>` has no dots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar criteria eval <project.criterion>` resolves and runs the project criterion's
      Pass-1 finder over its dataset (no `no eval solver` error), for a criterion whose
      logical id contains the `project.` namespace dot.
- [ ] A regression test drives `calibrate_criterion` (or `eval_solver.run_case`) for an
      activated `project.<name>` criterion with an injected/fake runner and asserts the
      criterion resolves (fires/does-not-fire per the fake), proving the physical→logical
      round-trip. File: `tests/unit/test_criteria_eval.py` (or a sibling).
- [ ] Built-in criterion calibration (e.g. `F1`) is unchanged (no regression).
baseline.summary: Live criteria-eval cannot resolve namespaced project criteria (dash/dot round-trip)

baseline.description:
## Context

The fixture-admission runner (`src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py`, epic REB-693 / 67aa) SCOPES OUT container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) as `container-material-unrecoverable`: the replay corpus (`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py`) persists a review's children as bare ticket-id STRINGS only (`_child_ids`), with no per-child title/description. But the LIVE plan-review container finder reads each child's full title/description at review time (`context_assembly.py` fetches every child via `show_ticket`), and G3's coverage-discharge cannot fire on a title-only roster (`container_stage.py`). So a container case rehydrated from the corpus would run the finder over an IMPOVERISHED roster — an admit/drift verdict UNFAITHFUL to history. `material_fingerprint` hashes children by id only (`material_diff.py`), so it cannot detect the loss.

## Approach

Extend the corpus sidecar row to persist per-child at-review `{canonical_id, title, description}` (reconstruct each child's title+description from its OWN event history at `review_ts`, reusing the `_reconstruct_material` machinery already used for the parent description), and rehydrate those into the `{ticket_id, title, description}` records the container finder consumes. When a child's at-review material is unrecoverable, withhold that case to drift as unrecoverable rather than running the finder over a degraded roster. Then REMOVE the container scope-out guard in `fixture_admission.run_admission` and re-run a live admission over G3/G4/decomp-shape to mint faithful specs.

## Scope

`corpus.py` (per-child material reconstruction + persistence), `fixture_admission.py` (drop the container scope-out once corpus is faithful), the container eval specs re-minted by a live run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The corpus sidecar row persists per-child `{canonical_id, title, description}` reconstructed at `review_ts`; a unit test over synthetic child histories asserts the reconstructed title/description match the child's state as of the review.
- [ ] The admission runner rehydrates container children WITH title/description and dispatches G3/G4 to the finder (no longer withheld as container-material-unrecoverable); a held-out test asserts a container must-fire case reproduces over the faithful roster.
- [ ] A child whose at-review material is unrecoverable withholds that case to drift as unrecoverable (not a degraded-roster finder call).
- [ ] A live admission run mints faithful G3/G4 specs; ledger records the spend ≤ cap.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`/`make typecheck`/`make test` pass; container specs re-minted faithfully.
baseline.summary: Persist per-child at-review material so container criteria (G3/G4) admit faithfully

baseline.description:
## Why

Both link bugs were invisible in telemetry: the batch outcome reports mutation-level `error=None` and "applied N of N" but never the per-sub-op counts, so a link/comment/label that silently no-ops (or fails non-fatally, logged only to stderr) leaves the pass green. The inbound applier already returns `links_applied`; the outbound batch path does not. Make a silent no-op fail loudly — safely.

## What

- Surface `links_applied`, `comments_applied`, `labels_applied` in the **structured outbound batch outcome** (queryable, not only logged) and the `RECON:` line — parity with the inbound applier's existing `links_applied`.
- Add a **silent-no-op canary**: when a mutation carries N sub-ops of a kind but `applied == 0`, that is a failure condition (`computed > 0 && applied == 0`), surfaced in the outcome/telemetry and asserted by a test that would have caught the link drop.
- **Rollout safety:** the fail-loud invariant lands **warn-first** — emit telemetry + a `WARNING` behind a flag/canary — and is promoted to hard-fail only after a baseline pass that emits zero such warnings. Reverting to warn is a flag flip, no other code change. This avoids hard-failing production syncs on a false positive.
- Sequencing: depends on story D (the single consolidated applier) so the counts come from one path.
- Out of scope (justified): making the threshold itself configurable — the simple `computed > 0 && applied == 0` invariant IS the contract; only enforce-vs-warn is flagged. A configurable threshold is YAGNI.

## Scope

- In: outcome/telemetry plumbing in `batch_dispatch.py` / `applier.py` / `reconcile.py`; the canary test; the warn-first flag.
- Out: the probe wiring (story F); applier consolidation (story D).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The structured outbound batch outcome and the `RECON:` line surface `links_applied`, `comments_applied`, `labels_applied`.
- [ ] A test asserts that a mutation with computed sub-ops > 0 but applied == 0 fails (reproduces what the link drop would have triggered).
- [ ] The fail-loud invariant rolls out warn-first (telemetry + `WARNING`) behind a flag; promotion to hard-fail and reversion to warn are a flag flip with no other code change.
- [ ] Sync semantics are otherwise unchanged (telemetry + guard only); the full reconciler suite is green.
- [ ] The canary asserts the count invariant, not specific log strings (anti-change-detector).
baseline.summary: Surface outbound sub-op telemetry + silent-no-op canary

baseline.description:
## What

Generate `docs/mcp-reference.md` from the MCP server's OWN registrars, correctly classified by gate, and gate it in CI. Mirrors the `gen_env_registry.py` generator + drift-gate pattern.

## Source of truth (verified — registration-time vs call-time gating)
The server (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py` `build_server()`) assembles THREE registrars:
- `register_read_tools` (`_mcp_reads.py`) — 23 tools, ALWAYS registered.
- `register_llm_tools` (`_mcp_llm.py`) — 6 tools, ALWAYS registered; gated at CALL time on
  `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`.
- `register_write_tools` (`_mcp_writes.py`) — 18 tools, CONDITIONALLY registered: returns
  early when `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` is truthy, so they are ABSENT from `list_tools()` in
  read-only mode. Totals verified: 47 tools (readonly off) / 29 (readonly on).

**Critical:** only `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` changes list membership. `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` are call-time only (tools always listed, refuse at call). So a naive single `list_tools()` in ambient env silently produces a PARTIAL reference. The generator MUST enumerate each registrar with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=0` so writes register.

## Classification rule (deterministic — registrar default + closed 3-entry special-case table)
There is NO per-tool gate attribute, and `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` do NOT map to the env gate. Classify by which registrar registers the tool, then apply the closed override table:
| Group (registrar) | Default gate | Special-case overrides |
|---|---|---|
| READS | none (always available) | `reconcile` -> mutating modes blocked by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` FIRST, then require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` (BOTH gate live mode; dry-run always works); `fsck` -> recover path gated by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` |
| LLM | `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (call-time) | `sign_review` -> `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` (HYBRID: in the LLM registrar but write-gated, makes no LLM call) |
| WRITES | `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` (registration-time; absent when readonly) | `run_workflow` -> write-gated by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` AND, for a non-dry-run workflow that HAS LLM steps, additionally gated at call time by `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (a second hybrid) |

This special-case table is CLOSED at FOUR entries (`reconcile`, `fsck`, `sign_review`, `run_workflow`); the generator carries them explicitly and a drift check asserts these four names still exist in their expected registrars, so a new hybrid is caught rather than silently misclassified. `sign_manifest` is a WRITE-registrar tool (not the LLM `sign_review` — do not conflate). Gate descriptions come from the `MCP_ENV_VARS` constant (`mcp_server.py`), the same source `rebar-mcp --help` uses, so the doc cannot drift from `--help`.

## Scope
- Add `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` (new): enumerate each registrar onto its own FastMCP
  with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=0` (writes register); read each tool's name + first-line summary
  (from `.description`); classify via the table above; emit `docs/mcp-reference.md` with a
  generated header and exactly THREE clearly-labeled gate-tier sections:
  **Read-only (always)**, **LLM-gated (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`)**, and
  **Write-gated (`REBAR_MCP_READONLY`)**. The three special cases are inline ANNOTATIONS,
  NOT separate sections: `reconcile` under Read-only annotated "live/mutating modes blocked by
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` and require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`"; `fsck` under Read-only annotated "recover path gated by
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`"; `sign_review` under Write-gated (NOT LLM-gated) annotated "hybrid: in the LLM registrar,
  write-gated"; `run_workflow` under Write-gated annotated "live LLM-step workflows also
  require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`". Include the `MCP_ENV_VARS` gate descriptions.
- `--check` drift mode + CI gate in BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND
  `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (the actual Verified gate; a parity test
  `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` enforces every `scripts/*.py` in test.yml also
  appears in gerrit-verify.yaml — omitting it breaks `make test`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` is generated (marked generated) from the live registrars and
      lists all 47 tools (23 read + 6 llm + 18 write).
- [ ] Tools are structurally separated into labeled sections by gate tier (NOT prose) — a
      Read-only section, an LLM-gated section, and a Write-gated section each exist (verify,
      prints nothing):
      `for s in 'Read-only' 'LLM-gated' 'Write-gated'; do grep -qi "$s" docs/mcp-reference.md || echo "NO SECTION $s"; done`
- [ ] The three special cases are correctly placed — DETERMINISTIC section-bounded proof
      (all three sub-checks print nothing). `sign_review` is in the Write-gated section and
      NOT in the LLM-gated section; `reconcile` is annotated jira-gated; `fsck` annotated
      readonly-recover:
      `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`
      then a held-out unit test asserts, using section-bounded slicing of
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` (awk from a tier heading to the next `## `): `sign_review` row
      is inside the Write-gated section and absent from the LLM-gated section; the `reconcile`

## Context
The 884-unit hardening oracle invokes production `_convert` once per unit. `_convert` currently resolves `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` on every invocation. A runtime trace on current origin/main d05bf2bc1be observed 100 Pandoc plus 102 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocesses for 100 conversions; resolving once at the render-pass boundary preserved identical outputs and reduced the trace to 100 Pandoc plus 3 one-time root probes. The prior 884-unit trace observed 1,770 total Popen calls (884 Pandoc + 886 root discovery). This is separate from the copied legacy oracle removed by absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl.

## Contract and prior disposition
- Preserve all real Pandoc calls, corpus units, byte expectations, timeout configurability, per-unit fallback, timeout, and process-group reap behavior.
- absolute-diplomatic-snowyowl approved immutable outputs only for the copied legacy side and retained all 884 real production conversions. harmless-wavy-osprey approved session-scoped sharing that reduced duplicate work, while coercive-paediatric-bug rejected parallelism that does not reduce aggregate runner usage. No tracker ticket rejects render-pass configuration injection.
- Full replacement of product Pandoc calls remains out of scope because ADR 0095 requires the real pinned boundary in every conversion assertion.

## OSS consensus research (2026-08-14)
All three surveyed projects are active, unarchived, and popular: Django (88,426 stars; pushed 2026-08-13) lazily resolves each setting and caches it in `LazySettings.__dict__`; Black (41,804 stars; pushed 2026-08-10) reads pyproject configuration at CLI setup and passes resolved `mode` into multi-file workers; pytest (14,416 stars; pushed 2026-08-12) exposes its resolved Config as a session-scoped `pytestconfig` fixture. Consensus is 3/3 for resolving loop/session invariants once and passing them to repeated work.

## Plan
1. Add a held-out behavioral oracle with three proven renderable units and assert exactly one `_pandoc_timeout()` resolution for the whole render pass.
2. Resolve timeout once in `render_markdown_to_wiki`; pass it through `_render_unit` and `_convert` using optional parameters so direct two-argument callers retain safe default behavior. The direct `_render_unit` caller at test_wiki_render_corpus.py:325 remains valid.
3. Update the two `_convert` monkeypatch stand-ins at test_wiki_render.py:268/278 to accept the optional argument supplied by the public render path.
4. In the 884-unit direct hardening loop, resolve timeout once outside the loop and pass it to `_convert`; keep exact expected bytes and all 884 real Pandoc invocations.
5. Run held-out RED -> fixer -> GREEN, defect-seeded RED, focused hardening/corpus tests, lint, typecheck, and paired subprocess/timing measurement. The fresh-process measurement must observe 884 Pandoc launches, exactly one timeout resolution, and at most 3 one-time Git-root probes.
6. Push through Gerrit; merge only after LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, no unresolved comments, then record CI and runner savings. Back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring per-call timeout resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A render pass with three renderable units calls `_pandoc_timeout()` exactly once.
- [ ] The hardening oracle launches all 884 real production Pandoc conversions.
- [ ] A fresh 884-unit trace launches at most 3 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` probes.
- [ ] Non-default timeout configuration remains observable between separate render passes.
- [ ] Per-unit timeout fallback behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Pandoc stdin and argv behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Byte-equivalence to all 884 immutable expected outputs remains covered.
- [ ] Whole-process-group reap behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Held-out RED/GREEN and exact defect-seeded RED are recorded.
- [ ] Before/after subprocess counts and wall time quantify savings without claiming more than the evidence.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, and typecheck pass.
- [ ] LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] Final report cites OSS sources and prior-ticket dispositions.

## Context / Problem

`tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py` cites "epic 3a03" in short, four-hex form at lines 10, 13, and 414. In this repository `3a03` resolves to `3a03-9863-542e-4ae1`, an unrelated closed bug about the `_no_repo_root_leaks` test-isolation guard. A reader following the citation lands on the wrong ticket, so the provenance of the ACLI contract-regression tests is effectively lost.

The verified source is the pre-extraction DSO epic `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f` (closed, 24 children, "level-triggered reconciler"), recorded in the DSO ticket-data mining report stored on the tickets branch under `63cc-ec94-4792-464b`. Evidence for that attribution:

- The citations arrived verbatim in `b534f47a7f` ("Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler
  into standalone rebar", 2026-06-08), so they name DSO ids, not rebar ids.
- The same file and `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py` cite
  sibling DSO bug ids in full form (`c916-74a1-ed06-40e4`, `4fa9-0846-519e-4c30`,
  `5010-1c6a-9387-4b5b`); none of them resolve in the rebar store either.
- `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f` is the only DSO-era id beginning `3a03` recorded anywhere in this
  repository's history, and it shares the prefix the author abbreviated.

The earlier hypothesis on this ticket that the source was rebar epic `3006-e198-13db-4e1f` is disproved: `3006` was created 2026-07-03, a month after the citations landed in this repository and six weeks after the 2026-05-24 ACLI audit they describe, and its plan never mentions ACLI. Citing it would substitute one wrong reference for another.

## Approach

Rewrite the three short `epic 3a03` citations to the full DSO id `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f`, labelled as a pre-extraction DSO ticket so no reader mistakes it for the rebar ticket that now owns the `3a03` prefix. This matches the full-id convention the surrounding code already uses for the sibling DSO bug ids, and it needs no new lookup table or doc. The edits are inside a module docstring and a comment banner only, so no test or assertion changes.

## Scope

- `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py` — lines 10, 13, and 414: replace
  the short `epic 3a03` citation with `pre-extraction DSO epic 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f`. No
  executable line, fixture, assertion, or test name changes.

No other file changes. The sibling short form `bug c916` on line 409 is left alone: it does not collide with any rebar ticket and its full id is already given on line 422.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -n "3a03" tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py` returns three
  lines, each containing the full id `3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f` and none containing a bare `3a03`
  short-form citation.
- [x] Each of the three corrected citations identifies the id as a pre-extraction DSO ticket,
  verified by reading lines 10, 13, and 414.
- [x] `git diff` for the change touches only comment and docstring lines in that one file,
  verified by inspecting the diff.
- [x] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py`
  passes with the same collected test count as before the edit.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass in the worktree.

baseline.description:
## Not the same bug as [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1] — do not fold them together

While proving 895c's root cause (Bedrock rejecting an over-complex structured-output grammar), a **second, distinct** LLM failure mode surfaced in the same logs and must not be attributed to it.

### The two are separable on three independent axes

| | 895c (schema complexity) | THIS bug (overlap-judge) |
|---|---|---|
| step | `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` | `overlap-judge` |
| duration | 180.6-185.9s (tight, 27 samples) | **312-381s** (different band) |
| `requests` recorded | **0** — no model request ever completed (pre-response 400) | **3** — real requests completed |

A pre-response 400 and a failure after three completed requests are different mechanisms. The duration bands do not overlap.

### What is known

* Recorded via the usage instrumentation landed by [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86]: 5 occurrences,
  312-381s, `requests=3`. Overall failure rate across that sample was 64 ok / 9 failed = 12.3%.
* Separately observed in `/tmp/03ef-review6.out`: `llm call [overlap-judge] ... model=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 FAILED in 0.4s: status_code: 401 ... 'API key is invalid.'` — a DIFFERENT overlap-judge failure again (direct-Anthropic auth), tracked separately.
* 895c's original report also noted `UnexpectedModelBehavior: Exceeded maximum output retries (2)`
  from the overlap judge — consistent with an output/validation failure rather than a request
  rejection.

### Why it matters

`overlap-judge` deduplicates findings across reviewers. When it fails the review still proceeds, so this degrades silently — the failure is not visible in the verdict.

## Resolution (premise resolved by the fix — closed `duplicate`)

Re-measured 2026-08-11 across all 17 local `usage.jsonl` logs (1638 `overlap-judge` records, 2026-08-06T20:35Z -> 2026-08-12T01:29Z). **The 312-381s / `requests=3` failure mode no longer occurs and is now structurally unreachable.** Commit `7fa8102477` (2026-08-08, ticket [rebar:22da-e9a6-63e7-49e5]) bounded the live `judge_batch` path with `output_token_limit=1024`, `structured_retry_limit=0`, `transport_attempt_limit=1`, `request_timeout_limit_s=60`.

Splitting failures by `output_tokens` separates two disjoint populations:

| population | n | `requests` | duration | last seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `output_tokens`=48000 (unbounded, this bug's signature) | 135 | 3 | 186.0-465.4s | **2026-08-10T17:39:48Z** |
| `output_tokens`=1024 (bounded by 7fa8102477) | 295 | 1 | **1.5-29.8s** | 2026-08-12T01:29Z |

Bounded-path failures above 120s: zero. In the 312-381s band: zero. Of the 149 `overlap-judge` calls after 2026-08-11T18:07Z, all 67 failures are bounded and the maximum duration across every call is 24.0s. The 2026-08-09/08-10 occurrences were stale checkouts and long-lived processes still running pre-fix code — independently confirmed by [rebar:3939-d68c-6e99-498d], which reached the identical 2026-08-10T17:39 cutoff from different data.

**The original Acceptance Criteria are void with the premise**, and are recorded here rather than left as unreachable checkboxes:

- **AC1/AC2 (mechanism, by measurement) — ANSWERED.** Output-retry exhaustion, not a provider-side
  timeout and not transport retry. Every long failure carries `finish_reason=length` and exactly
  48000 output tokens = 3 attempts (pydantic-ai `OUTPUT_RETRIES=2` default) x the 16000-token
  default cap; successful calls on the same path show 16091/16036/16323/16102/32035 output tokens,
  confirming the 16k-per-request ceiling. `model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` throughout,
  so distinct from the [rebar:2876-7958-8dee-4882] direct-Anthropic 401 misroute (0.2s) and from
  [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1]'s pre-response 400 (`requests`=0).
- **AC3 (effect on the verdict) — ANSWERED.** `judge_one` and `judge_batch` both swallow any
  exception and return `_ABSTAIN`, so an overlap-judge failure never fails a review: it silently
  disables cross-reviewer dedup for the affected pairs and duplicate findings survive into the
  verdict with no signal that dedup did not run. On the batch path the whole batch abstains
  together. The fix changed the cost of that failure (~$132 measured waste -> ~$0.02 each), not its
  semantics.
- **AC4 (regression test) — VOID.** `7fa8102477` landed its own coverage of the bounds
  (`tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` +141 lines, plus `test_runner_hardening.py` and
  `test_settings_builders_seam.py`). A test written for this ticket would pin the same seam.

Residual, non-blocking (inherited from 3939): a batch whose legitimate verdict exceeds 1024 output tokens now abstains — an overlap-recall loss worth revisiting only if drain-abstain rates grow. The live follow-on is [rebar:b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c] (a gate run does not warn when its running build is behind the base ref), which is what made these stale-build failures read as current.

## Testing

    python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl   # the recorded evidence
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q
baseline.summary: overlap-judge LLM calls fail at 312-381s with requests=3 — a SECOND failure mode, distinct from the schema-complexity 400

baseline.description:
Discovered while repairing binding-drift bug 8656-01fe-6f74-44c9 (unbound_jira REB-3510).

DEFECT: the inbound-create adopt path writes the Jira-side rebar-id:<local-id> label BEFORE the local CREATE event + binding are durably published to origin/tickets. When the pass's final tickets push is rejected (non-fast-forward) on an EPHEMERAL runner (GHA run 32602702883: 'final-push-rejected … 7 unpushed commits', runner destroyed), the local state is lost while the Jira label persists. Every automated healing path then stands down:
- binding_walk L10 guard skips adopt when the rebar-id label is present
- differ's bug-4354 suppression likewise stands down on the label
- BindingRecovery.recover_pending_bindings only walks state=='pending' store entries, which were lost with the runner

Result: a permanently stuck unbound_jira drift that only manual repair (or the fsck canary + human) can clear. This class will recur on any ephemeral-runner reconcile that loses its final push race.

## Chosen design (AC1): option (b) — recovery extension, mechanizing the manual repair

Codebase evaluation of the two AC1 options:

- (a) durable-publish-first ordering was evaluated and REJECTED as the load-bearing fix. The label write-back (`_inbound_create_writeback_jira`) runs per-mutation inside `_apply_batch`'s dispatch loop; deferring it until after the pass's final `commit_and_push_tickets_branch` would restructure the apply loop, widen the bug-4354 window (the label is the differ's within-pass and next-pass dedup signal), and STILL leave the mirror-image window (local published, label stamp lost). Notably, that mirror window is ALREADY healed idempotently today: the ticket-1577 dedup guard in `_apply_inbound_create` (binding present -> `dedup_skipped`) makes replay safe when local state survived. The one unhandled ordering is exactly its converse — label persisted, local state lost — so the symmetric completion of the existing idempotent-replay design is the recovery extension, not a reordering.
- (b) recovery extension is the load-bearing fix. This matches what mature OSS systems do for cross-system crash windows (transactional-outbox consumers, Debezium/Kafka Connect source connectors resuming idempotently from offsets, Temporal activity retries, Stripe idempotent replay): pair best-effort ordering with IDEMPOTENT RECOVERY keyed on a deterministic identity — here the deterministic inbound local id (`_jira_key_to_local_id`), which makes the replayed adopt converge on the same local id, binding, and (idempotent re-add) the same Jira label.

Implementation: the fix lands in `binding_walk.py`'s phase-1b unbound arm — the level-triggered walk that already re-considers every present-unbound key each pass and whose L10 guard comment already promises "binding recovery owns re-linking a marked-but-unstored key" (a promise nothing fulfills today). The L10 stand-down becomes conditional: when the unbound key's rebar-id marker set is exactly the DETERMINISTIC inbound id for that key (`jira-<key-lower>`), AND the binding store has no entry (pending or confirmed) for that id, AND a targeted local read (`local_reader`) finds no local ticket — i.e. the marked-but-unstored lost-adopt residue — the walk falls through to the ordinary classify->ADOPT machinery instead of standing down. The replayed adopt routes through the EXISTING `_apply_inbound_create` leaf unchanged (retired-skip gate, dedup guard, baseline seed, idempotent label write-back) and through the existing blast-radius breaker and census.

Safety scoping (why this cannot re-introduce L11 double-bind): a marker that does NOT equal the deterministic inbound id (a UUID from an outbound bind, a foreign `jira-dig-NNNN` ghost label, or multiple markers) keeps the unconditional stand-down — those are different drift classes owned by dd-5 conflict surfacing / fsck alert + human adjudication. A key whose marked id still has a store entry keeps the stand-down (pending-write-ahead recovery owns it). A key whose marked local ticket still exists keeps the stand-down (only the binding is missing — a store_integrity repair, not this class). A RETIRED key still routes to SKIP_RETIRED via the classifier and the leaf's gate #1.

`bridge_fsck` is deliberately untouched (AC3): its unbound_jira audit classifies present-unbound snapshot keys without consulting the label, so it keeps alerting on this class until the binding actually exists again — no suppression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Recovery extension per option (b): `binding_walk.py`'s unbound arm detects a marked-but-unstored key (rebar-id label equal to the deterministic inbound local id; no binding-store entry for that id; no local ticket) and replays the adopt through the existing inbound-create leaf, instead of standing down on the L10 guard. `compute_binding_walk_mutations` complexity does not increase (guard swapped one-for-one into a helper).
- [x] A RED-first regression test simulating the lost-final-push runner: runner 1 adopts (CREATE event + binding written, label stamped), the final push is rejected and ALL local state is discarded; runner 2 (fresh store, fresh tracker) sees the labeled snapshot — the walk emits the replay adopt and applying it re-materialises the local ticket + binding under the SAME deterministic local id with no duplicate label. Confirmed failing (walk stands down, adopted == []) before the fix.
- [x] Existing L10/L11 protections preserved: foreign/ghost markers, multi-marker keys, keys whose marked id still has a store entry, and keys whose marked local ticket still exists all keep standing down; retired keys still skip. Existing tests `test_class_b_labeled_key_not_double_bound` and `test_class_b_empty_rebar_id_marker_is_adopted` unchanged and green.
- [x] bridge fsck continues to alert unbound_jira on the class until healed — no suppression added anywhere (fsck code untouched; post-heal the key is bound so the alert clears by becoming true).

## Testing / Verification

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_binding_walk.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py -q` — new marked-but-unstored replay cells (walk-level + end-to-end two-runner replay) plus all existing class-A/B/C cells green.
- RED evidence recorded on the ticket: the new walk-level test fails on pre-fix code with `adopted == []` (stand-down on the label).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` (includes the complexity ratchet: new=0 increased=0) and `make typecheck` green.
- fsck behavior verified by reading `bridge_fsck.py`'s unbound_jira audit (label not consulted) — no code change there.

Evidence and full RCA on ticket 8656-01fe-6f74-44c9; repair precedent 16c1-0f0c.
baseline.summary: Reconcile stamps Jira rebar-id label before local adoption is durably published — push-rejected ephemeral runs strand unhealable unbound_jira drift

baseline.description:
## Why this exists

`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (`aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`) is the bug: the Jira reconcile bridge's PRIMARY comment-dedup skip — `binding_store.is_comment_mapped(local_comment_key)`, keyed on comment ID — was **inert in production**, because the `comment_ids` map in `.bridge_state/bindings.json` is empty:

```
bindings:     2475 entries
comment_ids:     0 entries
```

This ticket is not that bug. It is the question the bug raises: **how did a silently-inert primary guard survive review, tests, CI and production, and what would have caught it?**

## Why it is worth asking here specifically

Three properties make this a high-value escape to study, not a routine one:

1. **It was silent by construction.** `_record_comment_id`
   (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:309-334`) returns quietly on any of four guard conditions. Nothing
   logged, nothing raised, no metric moved. The system had no way to tell an operator that its
   primary dedup key had never been populated.
2. **A working fallback hid it.** The SECONDARY body-equality skip — described in-code as
   belt-and-suspenders for "a lost map write" — absorbed enough traffic that the failure looked
   like partial success rather than total failure of the primary path. Short comments deduped
   (REB-424: 22/25); only richly-formatted ones did not (REB-1861: 1/40). A degradation that
   correlates with content shape is exactly the kind that reads as flakiness.
3. **A prior fix in the same area did not surface it.** `florid-vigorous-urial`
   (`1f3d-cb66-d3fc-4356`) fixed 5000-cap comment inflation via pagination, and that fix is
   present and correct. It **hardened the fallback's inputs while the primary skip was already
   inert** — so the area had recent, competent attention that did not reveal the deeper problem.
   That is the most interesting fact here.

## Scope

This is an **escape analysis**, in the manner of `cranial-goodly-seahog`. It should produce findings and, where warranted, concrete detection proposals — NOT a re-fix of the bridge, which `aa7b` owns.

Questions to answer with evidence:

- **Detection.** What signal existed that a reasonable operator or test could have read? Was
  `comment_ids` ever non-empty — i.e. did this regress, or was it never populated? Git history on
  `.bridge_state/bindings.json` should settle that, and the answer changes the analysis
  completely.
- **Test gap.** Do the reconciler's tests exercise the primary ID skip at all, or do they pass a
  binding store that makes the fallback sufficient? A test that would still pass with
  `is_comment_mapped` hard-wired to `False` cannot detect this class.
- **Review gap.** Would any current plan-review or code-review criterion have flagged a
  silently-returning guard on a correctness-critical path? If not, is that a criterion worth
  proposing — bearing in mind the project's rule that a capability whose only trigger is a
  specific CI system is not portable (`project.portability`).
- **Observability gap.** Should a dedup map that is empty while its sibling map holds thousands
  of entries be an alertable invariant? This is the cheapest candidate remedy and should be
  evaluated on its merits rather than assumed.
- **Fallback design.** The general pattern — a secondary guard silently carrying a failed
  primary — is likely not unique to this file. Is it worth a targeted sweep?

## Testing / Verification

The deliverable is an analysis, so verification is reproducibility of each finding: the findings comment must quote the exact probe commands run and their raw output — the `git log`/`git show` commands over the `tickets` branch history of `.bridge_state/bindings.json` (populated-or-not per revision), the pytest invocation that demonstrates whether the named dedup tests pass with `is_comment_mapped` forced to `False` (run in this worktree's `.venv`), and the `rebar explain <criterion-id>` / `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` reads behind the review-gap conclusion. Any reader can re-run those commands and reproduce each classification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Established from evidence (git history of `.bridge_state/bindings.json` on the tickets
      branch) whether `comment_ids` was ever populated, so the escape is correctly classified
      as a regression versus never-worked — checked by reading the findings comment's quoted
      history probe.
- [x] [non-codebase] The test gap is characterised: named tests that cover the dedup path, and
      a demonstration of whether they would still pass with the primary skip disabled —
      checked by the quoted pytest run in the findings comment.
      provenance: environment=this worktree venv (pytest); principal=analysis agent; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=simulation — instrumented plugin forced is_comment_mapped False on every loaded BindingStore copy; 5 failed / 26 passed, plugin and command quoted in the findings comment.
- [x] [non-codebase] The review gap is characterised: whether any existing plan-review or
      code-review criterion addresses silently-inert guards, with the criterion ids checked —
      checked by the criterion-registry citations in the findings comment.
      provenance: environment=local worktree docs and git history; principal=analysis agent; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=static-analysis — criteria E4, T2, T3, T5b read from the registry; code-review fail-open rubric dated via git (4c57247ff88, post-escape); citations in the findings comment.
- [x] [non-codebase] At least one concrete, portable detection proposal is made — or a
      reasoned argument that none is worth its cost, which is an acceptable outcome if argued
      — checked by reading the findings comment; any gate/criterion change is filed for
      operator adjudication, not implemented.
      provenance: environment=rebar tracker; principal=analysis agent; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=static-analysis — in-process reconciler invariant alert proposed (operation-linked, no CI trigger) and filed as prissy-comic-koi; no criterion change proposed.
- [x] [non-codebase] Findings are recorded on this ticket; any proposed criterion or test work
      is filed as its own ticket linked `discovered_from` this one rather than implemented
      here — checked by the links on this ticket.
      provenance: environment=rebar tracker; principal=analysis agent; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — findings comment posted; prissy-comic-koi and vanitied-kitschy-mantis created and linked discovered_from this ticket via rebar CLI.

## Sequencing

Was blocked by `aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615` (now closed): its root-cause pass confirmed the mechanism — GUARD 3 of `_record_comment_id` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:328-330`) fires on every successful Cloud post because ACLI's batch mutation envelope carries no top-level `id`; guards 1/2/4 and the persistence path are healthy. That confirmed mechanism is the input this analysis builds on.
baseline.summary: Escape analysis: how a silently-inert primary dedup guard survived review, tests and months of production

baseline.description:
Split from silvern-dewy-damselfly (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843). OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-21, latest comment): option (a) approved — persist close provenance durably in the close STATUS event.

## Context / Problem

After a close whose completion-signature append failed, a later reader cannot tell that ticket apart from one closed with the gate off (damselfly reports the loss only in the returned payload — ephemeral). The gate's state at close time is read from config and discarded (`_completion_precheck`, `_commands/close_precheck.py`), so "closed with no attestation" collapses into ONE state: gate off, `--force` close, config-unreadable fail-open, `source == "local"` unattested close, `certifiable is False` withholding, and signature-append failure.

Landed prerequisites:

* steep-tired-whimbrel (f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe, CLOSED) — `gates.gate_enabled` returns the
  tri-state `GateState` (ENABLED / DISABLED / UNREADABLE); this plan CONSUMES it, never
  recomputes it.
* defiant-orthoclase-buck (055d-f176-8fcb-4ffe, CLOSED) — `force_close_reason` is persisted
  on the close STATUS event and folded; `force_bypassed` complements that durable reason.
* Owner for `not_applicable` (operator decision): set explicitly on the `idea -> closed`
  path in `transition_close.close_ticket`, which alone knows the gate never applied.

## Approach

Record on the `*->closed` STATUS event WHY a completion signature was or was not expected — in the SAME locked write that commits the close (`txn.transition_core`), so NO additional lock acquisition (an audit comment or second event would append through the very write-lock whose timeout causes the failure being recorded).

`completion_expectation` is a present-only string ENUM (a bool cannot separate the states the ACs demand), total over the close path:

| value | meaning at close time |
|---|---|
| `required` | the gate ran; a completion signature was expected |
| `disposition` | a qualifying administrative close: signed as a DISPOSITION, not a PASS |
| `gate_off` | a readable config had the gate off (DISABLED — a policy choice) |
| `gate_unreadable` | unreadable config, gate failed OPEN (UNREADABLE — a FAULT, not laundered into `gate_off`) |
| `force_bypassed` | the gate was ENABLED and `--force` skipped it (its reason is the sibling `force_close_reason`) |
| `local_source` | verdict `source == "local"`: verified but never signed |
| `not_certifiable` | `certifiable is False`: certification withheld |
| `not_applicable` | `idea -> closed`: a REJECT/DROP, not a completion |

The event records the EXPECTATION only, never the outcome — the STATUS commits BEFORE signing is attempted. A reader combines it with the durable attestation: `required` + attestation = closed and signed; `required` + none = **signature LOST**; `disposition` +/- attestation = disposition-signed / disposition-signature-lost; anything else = not expected, and the value says exactly why.

Precedence: the gate state resolves FIRST (matching `_completion_precheck`'s existing branch order) — `force_bypassed` is recorded only when the gate was ENABLED and `--force` skipped it. A forced close under a disabled/unreadable config records `gate_off`/`gate_unreadable` (no gate to bypass; a FAULT is never masked by a force); the force's reason stays durable in `force_close_reason` either way.

Computation and threading — NOT `verified_result` (None for force, gate-off, local and not-certifiable alike, so it conflates the very states this separates): `_completion_precheck` already visits every branch and now returns the PAIR `(verified_result, completion_expectation)`; a private in-repo seam — its direct callers and monkeypatch sites in tests are updated in the same change. `close_ticket` sets `not_applicable` on the `idea -> closed` branch it already owns and threads the value into `txn.transition_core`, which gains a keyword parameter and stamps it present-only next to `close_class` / `force_close_reason` (their exact precedent). Lifecycle-exempt types yield an empty expectation; their transition is refused before any event is written.

Reduced state: `_fold_close_metadata` (`reducer/_processors_status.py`) folds it on the winning `*->closed` edge under the same present-only + fork-winner-only rules as `close_class`; declared as a `$defs` enum in `schemas/common.schema.json`, referenced from `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `types.py` regenerated. `rebar show` and the MCP `fetch_ticket` surface it with no further wiring (open dicts).

Backward compatibility (docs/event-schema.md + docs/migrations.md): additive, reducer-known, present-only. A historical close event lacking the key reduces to state WITHOUT the key — absent = unknown/legacy, never guessed. No migration; older readers ignore the added key.

Complexity budget: `transition_core` (15) and `_completion_precheck` (15) sit at the ratchet threshold and `close_ticket` at its frozen ceiling (17); the new logic lands via behavior-preserving extraction along existing seams — never a baseline bump.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — return the pair; consume the tri-state; extract
  the gate-resolution head helper
* `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — unpack the pair; `not_applicable` on
  `idea -> closed`; thread into `transition_core`
* `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — accept and stamp the field on the `*->closed` STATUS event
  in the same locked write (extract the stamping cluster)
* `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` — fold on both `*->closed` edges
* `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`,
  `src/rebar/types.py` (regenerated) — declare the enum in reduced state
* `docs/event-schema.md` — document the STATUS close-metadata fields incl. the new one
* `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` (+ existing precheck/reducer test modules whose
  contracts change) — the ACs below

## Testing

Unit tests (happy + failure/edge): one close per enum value read back from REDUCED state; the three-way signed / signature-lost / gate-off separation; the single-lock assertion via a counting monkeypatch on `txn._acquire_write_lock`; `gate_unreadable` vs `gate_off`; and the degrade path — a legacy close event with no key reduces to state with the key ABSENT.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `completion_expectation` is written into the close STATUS event in the SAME locked
      write as the close — verified by a test asserting the write-lock is acquired exactly
      once during a close
- [x] A later reader, holding no lock and reading only reduced state, separates
      closed-and-signed (`required` + attestation) from closed-with-signature-lost
      (`required`, no attestation) from closed-with-gate-off (`gate_off`) — verified by a
      test closing one ticket each way and asserting all three read back distinctly
- [x] Each of `force_bypassed`, `local_source` and `not_certifiable` is recorded as ITSELF
      and never as `gate_off` — verified by a test per value
- [x] An unreadable config records `gate_unreadable`, never `gate_off` (a fault is not
      laundered into a policy choice) — verified by a test
- [x] A qualifying disposition close records `disposition`, distinct from `required` —
      verified by a test
- [x] `idea -> closed` records `not_applicable` (a REJECT/DROP is not a completion) —
      verified by a test
- [x] The expectation is computed independently of `verified_result`, so a `--force` close
      past an ENABLED gate records `force_bypassed`, never gate-off — and a forced close
      under a disabled config records `gate_off` (gate-state precedence, reason still in
      `force_close_reason`) — verified by a test of each
- [x] The field is documented in `docs/event-schema.md` and is present-only and
      backward-compatible: a legacy close event lacking it reduces to state with the key
      ABSENT (unknown, never guessed) — verified by a test replaying a legacy close event
baseline.summary: Closed-without-signature is not distinguishable from gate-off on read

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The project needs a repository-wide audit of documentation and source comments against the operator standards recorded below. Future developers and agents need an evidence-based remediation proposal before any project file changes are authorized.

## Audit standards

The standards baseline is the operator instruction dated 2026-08-20, preserved in this ticket through the following requirements.

- Prose must not use an em dash, en dash, spaced hyphen, semicolon, or a colon that connects or introduces a clause within a sentence.
- A colon may introduce a list of items or act as a structural label. Spoken narration must contain no colon.
- Hyphens are limited to compound words, technical names, identifiers, Markdown list bullets, table separators, horizontal rules, code operators, or SQL operators. A plain hyphen must not replace a dash.
- Every Markdown paragraph remains one logical line. Line breaks remain only where Markdown structure requires them.
- Writing uses a formal voice with precise verbs, complete sentences, no contractions, no colloquialisms, and no casual connectors.
- Filler or authenticity padding must be deleted. The prohibited filler list contains `real`, `actual`, `genuine`, `live` when used as a value adjective, `simply`, `just`, `quietly`, `seamlessly`, `robust`, `powerful`, `leverage`, `truly`, `in real time`, `concretely`, and `today` when used for emphasis rather than as a date.
- Authenticity padding phrases such as `not a placeholder`, `live for this run`, `the thing that matters`, or `this is not a mock` must not appear. Writing describes the mechanism or source instead of claiming authenticity.
- A noun remains unmodified unless an adjective selects one option from several.
- Tickets preserve the history of work for future developers or agents.
- ADRs preserve key decisions that introduce architectural invariants needing more visibility than tickets. Future developers or agents are their primary audience.
- Internal project documentation explains the current development processes, architecture, or codebase. It references tickets or ADRs when historical context is necessary instead of repeating material that has no future use.
- External documentation teaches clients who do not develop rebar or understand its internals. It uses concise language focused on using rebar.
- Shipped help follows the external documentation model. It supports discovery and directs users to relevant information shipped with rebar.
- Comments provide developer context required to understand code. Comments are not conversations, historical records, or restatements of the code. References to tickets or ADRs are encouraged when they supply necessary context.

## Approach

Build a complete textual-surface inventory from `rg --files`, file-type grouping, Python tokenization, and targeted searches. Apply the shard precedence rules below so each surface has one exploration owner. Compare factual claims with code, configuration, generated help sources, tests, ADRs, and relevant ticket history. Each agent returns a structured report to the root agent. The root agent alone appends report summaries to the session log. The separation between exploration and adversarial validation follows the sequence in `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md`. The content-specific shard map below is defined for this audit because that runbook uses code-health perspectives rather than documentation surfaces. Separate exploration owners reduce omissions within large surface families. The later challenge pass evaluates the complete set, which exposes cross-shard duplication, misplacement, unsupported claims, and coverage gaps.

## Exploration shard map

- **Shard A. Durable records plus internal documentation.** This shard owns ADRs, architecture documents, development process documents, contributor governance documents, research records, experiments, archives, design notes, infrastructure runbooks, test READMEs, and relevant ticket history. It owns each standalone document not assigned to shard B.
- **Shard B. External documentation plus shipped help.** This shard owns the root client overview, support or security guidance, user guides, command references, configuration references, integration setup, examples, templates, packaged guides, files under `src/rebar/_cli/help/`, client-facing CLI strings, client-facing MCP descriptions, and package documentation metadata.
- **Shard C. Developer comments plus embedded prose.** This shard owns comments or docstrings in source, scripts, tests, experiment code, workflows, configuration, and infrastructure. It also owns reviewer prompts, schema descriptions, error text, or other embedded prose not assigned to shard B.
- **Precedence rule.** A client-facing string belongs to shard B. A comment or docstring belongs to shard C. A standalone document belongs to shard A unless shard B names its audience as clients. The root coverage table records the owner of every surface group, so mixed files do not create overlapping review responsibility.

## Filtering pass

After consolidation, three agents receive the complete draft list. One challenges evidence plus factual accuracy. One challenges taxonomy, placement, completeness, plus duplication. One challenges punctuation, diction, paragraph shape, audience fit, plus concision. The root adjudicates each item as retained, revised, merged, or rejected.

## Scope

- Root contributor and client documents, package metadata, repository policies, templates, and workflow text.
- Internal documents under `docs/`, including ADRs and indexes.
- External documents, packaged guides, command help, MCP descriptions, examples, and other shipped user guidance.
- Developer comments and docstrings in maintained source, scripts, tests, and configuration files.
- Relevant ticket history needed to distinguish historical records from current-state documentation.
- Generated corpora, dependency content, caches, build output, wordlists, binary assets, and archived machine output receive inventory entries plus provenance checks rather than line-level prose review.
- Read-only repository inspection. No project file edits, gates, commits, or pushes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The inventory names every maintained surface in scope plus every explicit exclusion. Verification uses a session log coverage table.
- [ ] Every proposal cites a repository path, symbol, command output, ADR, or ticket as evidence. Verification uses the proposal evidence field.
- [ ] Every proposal names one target documentation type plus its audience. Verification uses the proposal classification fields.
- [ ] Every proposal states one remediation action plus one destination. Verification uses the proposal action fields.
- [ ] Every factual correction identifies the implementation, configuration, test, or effective help source used to establish expected behavior. Verification uses the proposal citations.
- [ ] Exploration agents inspect the three shard definitions. Verification uses one session log report for each shard.
- [ ] Filtering agents challenge every consolidated proposal for evidence quality, factual accuracy, completeness, placement, duplication, plus prose conformance. Verification assigns every draft item a retained, revised, merged, or rejected status.
- [ ] The final proposal text conforms to the audit standards in this ticket. Verification applies the pattern set `\x{2014}|\x{2013}|\x20\x2d\x20|\x3b|\x3a` plus manual diction review to the draft text before storage.
- [ ] No project file changes exist at handoff. Verification uses final worktree status plus diff checks.
- [ ] The filtered proposal appears in a ticket comment. Verification uses `rebar show minimum-rainy-fawn`.
- [ ] The filtered proposal appears in the operator response. Verification uses the completed response.
baseline.summary: Audit documentation taxonomy, prose, and comment quality

## Context
Record the approved RP-04 architecture before implementation. The completed research and probes live on `relevant-liberal-xantus` and in `.joe-janitor/rp04-secrets-research.md`, `.joe-janitor/rp04-composition-readback.md`, and `.joe-janitor/rp04-adr-research-critique.md`. This child is documentation-only and must not start RP-04 implementation.

## Deliverable
Create ADR 0098, `docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md`, using this repository's ADR format and generator. The ADR records one coherent decision: Rebar composes immutable non-secret operation configuration with separately owned provider-auth/runtime bindings at application boundaries. The slug avoids the generic word `bindings`, which would incorrectly classify the application-wide decision under the reconciler workstream. The generator has no generic operation-config keyword, so its current deterministic fallback is `Other decisions`; changing that classifier is outside this documentation-only ticket.

## Plan
1. Work from a fresh worktree at current `origin/main`; reserve ADR 0098 with the generated `.numbers/0098` marker.
2. Cite the completed primary-source and maintained-OSS research for Pydantic/PydanticAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, boto3/AWS, Git credential helpers/SSH, Jira integrations, CI secret injection, subprocess environments, and Rebar's current probes. Claims about dependency behavior must point to the exact source consulted.
3. Describe the current split authorities, trust boundaries, behavioral regressions, and why configuration and authentication are related at composition time but remain separate data/capability models.
4. Record the approved decisions: operation snapshot precedence/root rules and lifecycle; CLI/MCP/Python/service composition ownership; subsystem projections; provider-native pre-client auth/session injection into Rebar-owned factories; provider-specific `SecretStr`/`SecretBytes` static carriers; no universal secret broker/keyring/cloud-secret retrieval; subprocess environment rules without global mutation; restart/redeploy static rotation; SDK-owned refresh; fail-closed decision-bearing auth; and the optional observability exception.
5. Record op-cert startup composition: exactly one path or multiline value, validation before service work, process-owned 0700/0600 copy, context-local signer/principal/push policy, no application runtime SSM/boto3/region coupling, and deployment freedom to retain SSM-at-rest before injection. Amend only ADR 0049's per-job retrieval/composition detail; preserve its algorithm, trust-root/era, producer, and deployment storage choices.
6. Explain alternatives and rejection grounds: current ambient/per-consumer loading; one secret-provider/string lookup; application-owned SSM/keyring layer; aggressively restricted child environments; global `os.environ` overlays; public constructed-client/runner replacement; per-job op-cert retrieval; and hot rotation owned by Rebar.
7. State security limits/non-goals, migration and rollback, compatibility effects, explicit behavior changes, observability/provenance constraints, and implementation verification obligations. Relate ADRs 0008, 0014, 0041, 0046, 0049, 0050, 0059, and 0083 without claiming to supersede their unaffected decisions.
8. Regenerate `docs/adr/README.md` and `.numbers/0098`; make the minimal `docs/architecture.md` update appropriate for a proposed decision under this project's conventions.
9. Run ADR-number/index/docs checks. Then perform and publish the required numbered Draft Critique: uncited claims, internal inconsistencies, missing constraints, and conflicts with existing ADRs. Resolve any mechanical/document defects, but stop before HOLD/MERGE and request explicit maintainer approval.

## Verification
- `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check`
- `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`
- The repository's documentation/lint checks applicable to changed files.
- Deterministic searches confirm no placeholder sections or merge-conflict markers in the changed ADR artifacts.
- Read the rendered diff against the approved research and every related ADR named above.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] ADR 0098 exists in project-native format and accurately records the approved operation-snapshot, provider-auth/runtime-binding, subprocess, rotation, failure, observability, and op-cert decisions.
- [x] Every external dependency/OSS behavior claim has a specific primary or repository research citation; Rebar probe claims cite the recovery artifacts or durable research ticket.
- [x] Alternatives, consequences, security limitations/non-goals, explicit behavior changes, migration, rollback, and post-cutover compatibility are concrete enough that implementation stories need not invent architectural policy.
- [x] The ADR narrows ADR 0049 only at the per-job retrieval/composition seam and explicitly preserves all unaffected decisions; relationships to ADRs 0008, 0014, 0041, 0046, 0050, 0059, and 0083 are consistent.
- [x] `docs/adr/README.md` and `docs/adr/.numbers/0098` are generator-produced, collision-free, and pass their checks; `docs/architecture.md` points readers to the proposed decision without overstating implementation status.
- [x] The numbered Draft Critique is recorded on this ticket and identifies or explicitly clears uncited claims, inconsistencies, missing constraints, and ADR conflicts.
- [x] No RP-04 production code or implementation child stories were created before explicit maintainer authorization; Gerrit merge evidence is recorded on this ticket.
baseline.summary: Draft ADR 0098 for RP-04 composition and authentication boundaries

baseline.description:
## The assertion cannot pass, even when the code is correct

`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:317-319`) creates an issue directly on the DC harness, runs a `bootstrap-strict` pass, then asserts:

    tickets = rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=str(dc_rebar_repo))
    matched = [t for t in tickets if remote_key in json.dumps(t)]
    assert matched, f"no local ticket was created from DC issue {remote_key}; ..."

`remote_key` is the RAW Jira key (`RBJNAZV-1`). Two facts make the match impossible:

1. **The local id is LOWERCASED.** `_jira_key_to_local_id` (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`) returns
   `"jira-" + jira_key.lower()`, so the created ticket's id is `jira-rbjnazv-1`. The `in` test is
   case-sensitive.
2. **The ticket payload carries NO raw Jira key.** `_inbound_create_write_create_event`
   (`apply_inbound_records.py:183-212`) builds `create_data` from id / ticket_type / title /
   description / parent_id / tags / priority / assignee / creation_channel. The Jira key appears only
   as a TITLE FALLBACK (`fields.get("summary","") or jira_key`), so it is absent whenever the issue
   has a summary — as it does here ("J7 provenance oracle"). The binding is recorded separately, in
   the binding store (`_inbound_create_record_binding`), which `list_tickets` does not return.

Verified directly against the payload shape the inbound path writes:

    remote_key : RBJNAZV-1
    local_id   : jira-rbjnazv-1
    ticket json contains raw remote key? False

## Why this matters more than a broken test

Observed in GitHub Actions run 30651750699 (job "jira DC harness smoke"), where it is the ONLY failure — 1 failed, 14 passed — on the first run in which the harness got far enough to reach it (the PAT-cap fix [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] unblocked it).

The run reported `invariants: scanned=1` and `OK: applied 1 of 1 mutations`. The pass SAW the DC issue and applied a mutation. So the observable evidence is consistent with the inbound create having worked perfectly and the ORACLE being unable to see it.

**The consequence is that epic e369's headline acceptance criterion — "an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass" — is UNPROVEN, not disproven.** This test is the only thing currently asserting it, and it cannot distinguish "the ticket was created" from "the ticket was not created". Whichever the truth is, the oracle has to be fixed before the epic can make a claim either way. Do NOT read this failure as evidence that inbound is broken, and do NOT read a future green as evidence that it works until the assertion actually targets something the inbound path writes.

This is the THIRD oracle-that-cannot-pass found in this epic, after `_envelope()` being asserted on writing-mode passes (which emit no JSON — corrected under bda8). The pattern is consistent: the live tests were authored against an assumed output shape rather than the one the code emits, and the defects stayed invisible because an earlier failure aborted the run before the assertion was reached.

## Approach

Assert against what the inbound path ACTUALLY produces, and assert the binding too, so a pass is evidence of the round-trip rather than of a string appearing somewhere in a blob:

1. derive the expected local id with `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` and match on ticket `id`
   exactly — not a substring scan of `json.dumps`, which matches incidental occurrences and (as here)
   misses the real one;
2. additionally assert the BINDING maps that local id to `remote_key`, read from the binding store —
   this is where the DC↔local correspondence actually lives, and it is the property the headline AC
   is really about;
3. keep the existing `creation_channel == "jira"` assertion, which is correct and unaffected.

**Rejected: making the substring match case-insensitive.** It would make the test pass while leaving it a blob scan that could match on an unrelated field, and it would still not assert the binding — the thing that makes the local ticket genuinely correspond to the DC issue.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — the provenance test's assertions.

## Testing

The live DC harness job is the oracle. The fix is verified when that job reports the provenance test PASSING — and, because a green here would otherwise be indistinguishable from a weakened assertion, the new assertions must be shown to FAIL against a deliberately wrong local id (a unit-level check of the id derivation is enough for that half, since `_jira_key_to_local_id` is pure).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the provenance test matches the ticket by EXACT `id` equal to `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)`,
      not by a substring scan of `json.dumps(ticket)`
- [ ] the test additionally asserts the binding store maps that local id to `remote_key`
- [ ] a unit test asserts `_jira_key_to_local_id` lowercases and prefixes, so the derivation the live
      test depends on is pinned independently of the harness
- [ ] the live `jira DC harness smoke` job reports this test PASSING, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the epic's headline AC is only claimed after that green — and the ticket records that the prior
      failure was an oracle defect, so the run is not misread as a regression fix
baseline.summary: Live provenance oracle cannot pass: asserts the raw Jira key against a lowercased local id

baseline.description:
Move GET-rotation stamps into `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` so a later rollout step can remove them from the large sort-ordered `bindings.json`. A2-1 is the compatibility half: new binaries write both formats and read `max(new, legacy)`; A2-2 removes the legacy write after its observable rollout gate. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** contains the measured facts.

## Why

`set_last_get` stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit` (default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly 20 entries change per affected pass. The full A2 saving is realized only after A2-2 removes this scattered legacy write. During A2-1, dual-write is intentional compatibility cost: an old binary cannot read the sidecar, so it must still observe progress made by new binaries.

## Approach — compatibility first

Write every new stamp to the sidecar and the legacy inline field, and read the chronological `max(sidecar, legacy)`. Under mixed versions an old binary may advance only the inline field; `max()` ensures a following new binary does not use stale sidecar state. Conversely, dual-write ensures an old binary following a new one sees the new progress. Values are fixed-width zero-padded timestamps, so lexicographic `max()` is chronological.

Load legacy-only rotation state in memory and persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`. This covers all production save paths: end-of-pass persistence, the write-ahead saves in `dispatch_one.py`, and the recovery/retirement saves in `binding_store.py`. Saving unchanged canonical state must remain byte-stable. `reconcile-check` runs with `persist=False`, never reaches save, and must not create the sidecar.

Add `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE`, characterize its path, and include it in both `reconcile_helpers.py` explicit staging and basename membership checks. This is required because local reconciliation does not use `git add -A`. The existing `.gitattributes` glob covers the new file. Update the `_store/push.py` docstring that enumerates regenerable files.

`outbound_differ.py` is at the locked 800-line cap. Move the existing last-GET and best-effort bookkeeping wrappers across the new rotation seam so the module remains at or below the cap.

## Rollback

Reverting A2-1 is safe: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but every new-binary pass also advanced the inline legacy field. The orphaned sidecar is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Tier: integration in a real temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances identical selected-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Tier: integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Tier: real-git integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] Rotation order after an interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence matches the all-new sequence. Tier: integration; it must fail for either sidecar-first lookup or missing dual-write.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store yields identical rotation order. Tier: unit.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Tier: unit.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Tier: CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Tier: CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Tier: git-adapter characterization.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The `_store/push.py` regenerable-files documentation includes `get_rotation.json`. Tier: characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verify with the repository module-size gate.

## Files

`binding_store.py`, new `get_rotation.py`, `outbound_differ.py`, `git_adapter.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `_store/push.py` (docstring), focused tests.

Scope: M. Depends on closed A1.
baseline.summary: A2-1: move last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping into .bridge_state/get_rotation.json (write-new, read max(new, legacy))

baseline.description:
## Context
Production rich-text convergence mutates a binding entry reached through shallow `all_bindings()`, bypassing lifecycle policy. The public shallow query must remain compatible, but production needs a named mutation seam.

## Outcome
Add `BindingStore.note_rich_emit(local_id, wire)` or an equivalently narrow operation that owns hash/counter/save behavior and returns the current nonfatal missing-binding result. Do not cut over `apply_handlers.py` yet.

## Plan
1. Capture the current production sequence in a failing comparison test, including changed/unchanged wire hashes, counters, dirty/save gating, and missing binding.
2. Implement the operation through facade -> lifecycle -> repository while retaining the original dictionaries.
3. Keep `all_bindings()` copy depth and public signatures unchanged, but document the new method as the supported mutation seam.
4. Add a boundary test proving adapters and reconciler callers cannot obtain direct writable repository/lifecycle objects.

## Testing
Compare new-operation results and persisted bytes with the legacy mutation sequence for changed, unchanged, and missing cases.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Changed rich-emission wire data produces the same hash and counter as the legacy sequence, and the same persisted bytes once the pass's single save runs.
- [x] The operation performs NO save of its own on any path - changed, unchanged, or missing binding - matching the production caller, which mutates in place and relies on the pass's later unconditional save.
- [x] Missing bindings remain nonfatal with the current result.
- [x] `all_bindings()` remains shallow and every existing facade signature remains unchanged.
- [x] No production adapter receives direct repository or lifecycle mutation access.

## Out of scope
`apply_handlers.py` cutover belongs to RP-02 S3 after its RP-04 coordination condition.

## Correction: there is no per-emit save and no dirty-gating
An earlier draft attributed "save" and "dirty/save gating" behaviour to this operation and to the legacy sequence. Verified against the code: the production caller `apply_handlers._observe_rich_reemit` never calls `save()` - it mutates the live binding entry in place (reached today through the shallow `all_bindings()` query) and relies on the pass's later save. And `BindingStore.save()` is explicitly unconditional: no dirty-gating, no write elision.

So the narrow operation must NOT introduce a per-emit save; doing so would add write amplification the current path does not have, and would be a behaviour change in a slice whose whole point is parity. It mutates through lifecycle/repository and returns the count, plus a distinct nonfatal result for a missing binding. Byte equivalence is asserted by driving ONE save after the operation and comparing against the legacy sequence given the same save, not by counting saves per emit.

This is the same class of correction already applied twice in this epic (the non-existent double-bind safety-abort, and the comment map's "never remapped" claim): a documented behaviour that the code does not implement.
baseline.summary: RP-02 S2 T3 — Add the narrow rich-emission facade operation

baseline.description: Deferred hardening (accepted limitation, ADR 0046). The commit-ancestry key-validity model (attest/authorship.py verify_authorship_at_commit) defeats the direct revoked-key-reuse case (a new event descends the revocation commit, so a revoked key's revoke-commit is an ancestor and the key is excluded). Its integrity rests on the tickets-branch commit graph being append-only, which today is a CONTROL (Gerrit-authenticated, controlled-environment write access), not a cryptographic guarantee. gittuf shipped the same log-position model and still needed a monotonic policy counter (CVE-2026-44544); TUF hard-codes N+1 root versioning. Future hardening: (a) a regression test asserting a revoked-then-re-introduced key at a LATER ancestry position FAILS; (b) documented threat analysis of tickets-branch force-push/rewrite and the controls that bound it; (c) evaluate an explicit monotonic anti-rollback guard as defense-in-depth. Not scheduled.
baseline.summary: Cryptographic anti-rollback for commit-ancestry key validity (monotonic guard + regression test + tickets-branch-rewrite analysis)
