## Context / Problem

The inbound fetcher can only see one tracker project. `jqls_for(project)` builds exactly one pair of queries — active and recent-done — from a single key (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:78-90`), and `_validate_project_key` refuses an empty or malformed key outright rather than searching unscoped (`fetcher.py:63-75`, bug `626d`). A store that lists several projects in its mapping still ingests only one of them.

## Approach

Fan out: call the existing `jqls_for` once per project in the store mapping and union the results into the snapshot, rather than building a single `project IN (A,B)` query. Two concrete reasons. First, the per-query truncation ceiling (`_ACLI_CEILING = 1200` at `fetcher.py:91`, raising `SilentTruncationError`) stays scoped per project instead of becoming a shared budget that a single busy project could exhaust on behalf of the others. Second, it reuses `jqls_for` and `_validate_project_key` unchanged, so the JQL-injection guard that bug `626d` added keeps applying to every key with no new interpolation site.

Inbound-created tickets record their source project in `bridge_project` and get their `repos` defaulted from that project's mapping entry. The existing local-id derivation already encodes the project (`_jira_key_to_local_id`, `inbound_translate.py:120-124`, `DIG-123` → `jira-dig-123`), so ids stay unique across projects with no change; this story makes the association explicit on the ticket rather than only implicit in the id.

The CREATE event for an inbound ticket is written directly rather than through `create_core` (`apply_inbound_records.py:150-222`, which stamps `creation_channel` at `:221`), so the two new fields are stamped at that same site.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful verified fake fed production-shaped Jira fixtures. The fake must record the queries issued, because "one JQL pair per project" is itself the contract under test and is invisible to a result-only assertion.

- Happy path: a mapping with two projects issues exactly two query pairs — one per key — and the
  resulting snapshot contains issues from both.
- Postcondition: each ticket created from the fetch records the project its issue came from, and its
  `repos` equal that project's mapping entry.
- Edge: a project listed in the mapping that returns zero issues contributes nothing and does not
  fail the pass.
- Failure path: one project exceeding the per-query ceiling raises `SilentTruncationError` naming
  that project, and the ceiling is evaluated per project — a second project under the limit is not
  penalised by the first. This is the contrast case that proves the budget is not shared.
- Collateral invariant: a store whose mapping holds exactly one project issues the same query pair as
  before this change, so single-project behaviour is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mapping with two projects issues one JQL pair per project in a single pass; checked by a fake
      transport recording the issued queries and asserting the exact pair count and contents.
- [ ] Each inbound-created ticket records its source project and the repos from that project's
      mapping entry; checked by asserting both fields on tickets created from a two-project fixture.
- [ ] The truncation ceiling applies per project, not as a shared budget; checked by a test where one
      project exceeds it and a second under-limit project still ingests successfully.
- [ ] A single-project mapping issues an identical query pair to the pre-change behaviour; checked by
      a regression test comparing the recorded queries.
- [ ] A configured project returning zero issues does not fail the pass; checked by an empty-result
      fixture.
baseline.summary: Multi-project inbound fetch: per-project JQL fan-out and source-project recording

# Convergence rollout tail: Phase-3 consumer swap flip + live shadow-pass validation + capped live heal

## Summary
High-risk tail of the convergence rollout, carved from soar-quill-flare (7d23). Per epic adept-hedge-stain the AGENT (ACLI access) performs the live validation directly, with GUARANTEED cleanup of test artifacts in both live Jira and the local store (full-surface validation is centralized in sibling D1 close-ferreous-cardinal). The `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` workflow runs `rebar reconcile --mode live` every 20 min.

## What already landed (7d23, on main)
- Phase-1 baseline dual-write SHADOW (`baseline_shadow.py`) behind `reconciler.baseline_dual_write`, with per-pass
  `baseline_shadow_check` logging + `baseline_shadow_divergence` alert.
- Circuit breaker (`check_blast_radius`, default 0.10) before the first acting mutation.

## Remaining CODE
- [CODE] Phase-3 consumer swap: re-point `outbound_fields._local_matches_prev` (and its `outbound_differ` caller)
  from `prev_snapshot` to `BindingStore.get_baseline`, behind a NEW flag `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap`
  (bool, default false; add to `ReconcilerConfig` in `_config_schema.py`, distinct from `baseline_dual_write`).
  PRESERVE byte-for-byte: absent-baseline->local-wins; corrupt-store fail-closed abort. NOTE `get_baseline` returns
  None for a non-dict/absent entry, so map None -> the existing absent-baseline (local-wins) branch, and add an
  explicit corrupt-store detection (get_baseline cannot itself signal "corrupt") so fail-closed is preserved.
  Document the flag + flip procedure in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
- [CODE] RED-first direction-preservation property test running the SWAPPED consumer, covering the five mirrored
  fields as MAPPED (local title/description/priority/status/assignee <-> Jira summary/description/priority/status/
  assignee — reconcile the two field-name sets `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` and `baseline_shadow._MIRRORED_FIELDS`);
  name it distinctly from the existing `test_property_direction_preservation`.
- [CODE] Census key: expand-contract — emit BOTH `decision_census` and `binding_walk_census` for one release,
  migrate consumers to `decision_census`, then drop `binding_walk_census`. (Not a bare rename.)
- [CODE] classifier-vs-legacy divergence alerting: compare `classify()`'s per-binding decision against the
  PRODUCTION differ's action for that binding in the SAME pass, emitting `classifier_legacy_divergence`
  {classifier_count:int, legacy_count:int, divergent_pairs:list[str] of local_ids, pass_id:str}. If a per-binding
  production decision is not extractable for a given code path, scope the alert to the paths where it is and
  document the gap (do NOT invent a parallel legacy engine).

## Remaining OPERATIONAL (agent-run with ACLI; guaranteed cleanup)
- [OPERATIONAL] >=10 CONSECUTIVE clean shadow passes (`baseline_shadow_check` divergent==0) BEFORE flipping the flag.
  Streak is DERIVED from the sync-log history (query the last N `baseline_shadow_check` events), NOT an in-memory
  counter, so a fresh GHA process recomputes it; any divergent>0 OR a >20-min gap resets it and emits
  `baseline_shadow_divergence`. COORDINATION: A3's live remediation pauses the reconciler and will reset this streak
  — do NOT run A3's live pass during the streak window (sequence them).
- [OPERATIONAL] Capped live heal under bootstrap-strict incl. the GC-after-grace deletion (f8b5-2f30 -> REB-530).
  PRE-HEAL BACKUP covers BOTH sides: export affected Jira issue state (JSON via Jira API) AND tag the tickets branch
  (`git tag pre-heal-<date>`) so binding-store mutations are recoverable; if either backup fails, ABORT the heal.
  Store the artifacts in the workflow run artifacts (retention documented).
- [OPERATIONAL] Flip the flag only after BOTH gates. Rollback rehearsed: (a) revert the flag to false and confirm
  the reconciler reverts to `prev_snapshot` arbitration with no divergence, AND (b) force one `--mode dry-run` pass
  confirming zero mutations; record both workflow run-ids.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [CODE] `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap` flag added + documented in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`; `_local_matches_prev` reads `get_baseline` behind it; None->local-wins; corrupt-store fail-closed preserved (explicit detection).
- [ ] [CODE] RED-first direction-preservation property test (swapped consumer, five mapped fields) RED before, GREEN after.
- [ ] [CODE] Census emits both keys (expand-contract), consumers migrated to `decision_census`; `classifier_legacy_divergence` emitted with the typed fields above (or scoped+documented where per-binding legacy decisions aren't extractable).
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] >=10 consecutive clean shadow passes (log-derived streak, reset rule above) before the flip, NOT overlapping A3's live pass; evidence recorded.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Capped live heal with a bilateral pre-heal backup (Jira JSON + tickets-branch tag); heal aborts if either backup fails; artifacts stored.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Flip only after both gates; rollback rehearsed (flag-revert + dry-run run-ids recorded).

## Context / Problem

The `rebar-root-disk-pressure` CloudWatch alarm (root `/`, 30G, threshold 85%) sat in ALARM for ~39 hours on 2026-08-04/06: the review-bot host's root disk filled from ~48% to ~95% during an autodeploy build burst, then stayed pinned at 92-96% until the next real deploy finally reclaimed it. Root cause: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` reclaims docker garbage via `prune_docker_caches()` (builder prune `--keep-storage 5GB` + image prune) ONLY on the deploy and backoff paths. When `main` is quiescent, every ~2-min `rebar-autodeploy.timer` tick hits the "up to date … no-op" early exit (autodeploy.sh:228) and returns WITHOUT pruning, so nothing reclaims disk between deploys. This extends closed bug 7a41-95f4-c38c-4b5a (added the deploy-path prune) to cover the quiescent-main gap it left.

## Approach

Add a pressure-triggered, throttled reclaim to the autodeploy no-op path — the ideal hook because it fires every ~2 min exactly when no deploy is reclaiming, already holds the single-flight `flock` (autodeploy.sh:191), and already has `prune_docker_caches()` in scope. Reuse the exact root-disk-% computation from observability.sh:79 (`df --output=pcent /`).

1. Add tunables near `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP` (autodeploy.sh:~87): `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (default 80 — below the 85% alarm for hysteresis), `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` (default 600s throttle), `PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE` (default under `STATE_DIR`).
2. **Relocate `prune_docker_caches()` above the no-op exit.** It is currently defined at autodeploy.sh:245, which is AFTER the line-228 no-op exit; bash only makes a function callable once its `funcname() { … }` definition line has executed, so calling it from line 228 would fail with "command not found". Move the entire `prune_docker_caches()` definition up into the helper block near line ~150 (immediately below the new helpers in step 3), so it is defined before its FIRST use. Its existing callers stay valid because they all run later than line 150: `record_backoff_failure` (autodeploy.sh:261), the deploy-success path (autodeploy.sh:379), and the new line-228 call. Concrete resulting order: helpers/`prune_docker_caches`/`reclaim_under_pressure` at ~142-160 → single-flight + fetch (~191-224) → line-228 no-op exit calling `reclaim_under_pressure` → backoff/deploy paths (245+) that also call `prune_docker_caches`. `prune_docker_caches`' own body is unchanged (it uses only `docker`, `timeout`, `log`, `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP`, all available at that point).

3. Add two helpers in that same block (autodeploy.sh:~150): `root_disk_pct()` (the `df --output=pcent /` one-liner) and `reclaim_under_pressure()` which returns early unless `root_disk_pct >= DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`, enforces the min-interval throttle via the persisted timestamp file (atomic tmp+mv write), emits a countable `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` journal marker via the existing `marker()`, calls `prune_docker_caches` (now defined above it), and logs the before/after percentage. A prune failure only logs (never alters control flow), matching the deploy-path guarantees.
4. Call `reclaim_under_pressure` on the no-op early-exit line (autodeploy.sh:228), before the `log "up to date"; exit 0`.

Default threshold 80% with a flat floor plus the 10-min throttle (not a derivative/trend) is chosen deliberately: the throttle prevents per-tick churn and `prune_docker_caches` keeps a 5GB warm cache so back-to-back prunes are cheap no-ops; an absolute floor is simpler and less flappy than slope tracking. All new behavior is opt-outable via env overrides sourced from `/etc/rebar/autodeploy.env` (already sourced by the script), so no host redeploy is required to tune it.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — add the three tunables; relocate the existing `prune_docker_caches()` definition from line ~245 up into the helper block (~150) so it precedes the new line-228 call site (its body and its two existing call sites are otherwise unchanged); add the `root_disk_pct()` + `reclaim_under_pressure()` helpers; and add the single new call site on the no-op exit path (line 228). No change to the deploy/backoff prune BEHAVIOR, the drain/defer logic, or any journal-marker token except the new `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE`.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py` — new test module (new testable behavior): assert the reclaim fires when simulated disk% is at/above the threshold and no-ops below it, that the throttle suppresses a second prune inside the interval, and that a prune failure does not change the script's exit code. Stub `df` and `docker` via PATH shims / injected fakes, matching the existing `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*` harness style.

The new `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` marker is intentionally NOT wired to a new CloudWatch metric in this story (autodeploy still exits 0; the existing `root_disk_used_percent` alarm already covers the outcome). Wiring an observability delta metric for it is deferred as out of scope.

## Testing

- Happy path: with a `df` shim reporting 90% and a `docker` shim that records calls, running the no-op path invokes `prune_docker_caches` once and writes the timestamp file.
- Throttle/edge path: a second invocation within `PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL` does NOT invoke prune; an invocation with `df` reporting 70% (below threshold) does NOT invoke prune.
- Failure path: a `docker` shim that exits non-zero leaves the script's overall exit status at 0 (prune failure is non-fatal), and the pressure marker is still emitted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] On the autodeploy no-op tick, when root `/` usage is >= `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (default 80) and the throttle window has elapsed, `prune_docker_caches` runs — verified by `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py` happy-path assertion (docker-shim call recorded).
- [x] When root usage is below the threshold, or within the throttle window of the last pressure-prune, no prune runs — verified by the below-threshold and throttle assertions in the same test module.
- [x] A prune failure on the pressure path does not change autodeploy's exit code (stays 0) and only logs — verified by the failure-path assertion.
- [x] A countable `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` marker line (prefix `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE ` followed by the `marker()` JSON) is emitted to stderr exactly once per triggered pressure prune and zero times on the below-threshold and throttled paths — asserted by capturing the script's stderr in the test module and counting matches.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the new and existing `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_*` tests pass under the repo venv.
baseline.summary: autodeploy: pressure-triggered docker prune on the no-op tick to prevent root-disk-pressure

Move GET-rotation stamps into `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` so a later rollout step can remove them from the large sort-ordered `bindings.json`. A2-1 is the compatibility half: new binaries write both formats and read `max(new, legacy)`; A2-2 removes the legacy write after its observable rollout gate. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** contains the measured facts.

## Why

`set_last_get` stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit` (default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly 20 entries change per affected pass. The full A2 saving is realized only after A2-2 removes this scattered legacy write. During A2-1, dual-write is intentional compatibility cost: an old binary cannot read the sidecar, so it must still observe progress made by new binaries.

## Approach — compatibility first

Write every new stamp to the sidecar and the legacy inline field, and read the chronological `max(sidecar, legacy)`. Under mixed versions an old binary may advance only the inline field; `max()` ensures a following new binary does not use stale sidecar state. Conversely, dual-write ensures an old binary following a new one sees the new progress. Values are fixed-width zero-padded timestamps, so lexicographic `max()` is chronological.

Load legacy-only rotation state in memory and persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`. This covers all production save paths: end-of-pass persistence, the write-ahead saves in `dispatch_one.py`, and the recovery/retirement saves in `binding_store.py`. Saving unchanged canonical state must remain byte-stable. `reconcile-check` runs with `persist=False`, never reaches save, and must not create the sidecar.

Add `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE`, characterize its path, and include it in both `reconcile_helpers.py` explicit staging and basename membership checks. This is required because local reconciliation does not use `git add -A`. The existing `.gitattributes` glob covers the new file. Update the `_store/push.py` docstring that enumerates regenerable files.

`outbound_differ.py` is at the locked 800-line cap. Move the existing last-GET and best-effort bookkeeping wrappers across the new rotation seam so the module remains at or below the cap.

## Rollback

Reverting A2-1 is safe: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but every new-binary pass also advanced the inline legacy field. The orphaned sidecar is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Tier: integration in a real temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances identical selected-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Tier: integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Tier: real-git integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] Rotation order after an interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence matches the all-new sequence. Tier: integration; it must fail for either sidecar-first lookup or missing dual-write.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store yields identical rotation order. Tier: unit.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Tier: unit.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Tier: CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Tier: CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Tier: git-adapter characterization.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The `_store/push.py` regenerable-files documentation includes `get_rotation.json`. Tier: characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verify with the repository module-size gate.

## Files

`binding_store.py`, new `get_rotation.py`, `outbound_differ.py`, `git_adapter.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `_store/push.py` (docstring), focused tests.

Scope: M. Depends on closed A1.

baseline.description:
Add an atomic `idea` command on all three surfaces (CLI, MCP, library) that creates an `epic` in status `idea` in a single genesis CREATE event.

## Why

Capturing an idea must be one race-free operation. A create-then-transition path would momentarily leave the ticket in `open` (claimable by a parallel agent, the anti-pattern `claim` already forbids), so the idea must be born in `idea` via a single CREATE event. The command is intentionally light: title plus an optional description only.

## Prerequisite (depends on S1, 81b4-985e-b3e8-4026)

This story requires the status-vocabulary story to land FIRST: `idea` must be a recognized status value (added to the `TicketStatus` literal and to `_VALID_STATUSES`) before this command is coherent. Without S1, a created idea-status ticket is inconsistent with the type surface, and the transitions exercised by the end-to-end smoke test below (`transition idea open`, `transition idea closed`) are rejected by the existing `_validate_status` guard. A `depends_on` link to S1 is already recorded. This story's own deliverable — the command emitting a single CREATE event carrying `status=idea` for an `epic` — does not itself modify the status vocabulary; it consumes what S1 establishes.

## What

- Have `process_create` honor an optional `status` on the CREATE event, defaulting
  to `open` when absent — completing the one CREATE field the reducer does not
  currently read. The `idea` command is the sole producer of a non-`open` genesis
  status; no general `create --status` flag is added.
- Add the CLI command `rebar idea "<title>" [--description=…]` creating an `epic`
  in status `idea`.
- Add the MCP write tool `create_idea` with the same behavior.
- Add the library entry point `rebar.idea(...)` with the same behavior.
- Suppress the create-time "non-bug ticket lacks file_impact" stderr warning for
  idea-created epics.
- Document `rebar idea` / `create_idea` / `rebar.idea` in the command/tool
  references and note in `docs/event-schema.md` that a CREATE event may carry
  `status`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — `process_create` honors optional `status`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/idea.py` — new atomic CLI command.
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — `rebar.idea(...)` library entry point.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — `create_idea` MCP write tool.
- `docs/event-schema.md` and command/tool reference docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `process_create` sets `status` from the CREATE event data when present.
- [ ] `process_create` defaults `status` to `open` when the CREATE event omits it.
- [ ] `rebar idea "<title>"` creates a ticket of type `epic`.
- [ ] The ticket created by `rebar idea` has status `idea`.
- [ ] The ticket created by `rebar idea` is produced by a single CREATE event with
      no intervening STATUS event (test inspects the event log).
- [ ] `rebar idea "<title>" --description=TEXT` records TEXT as the description.
- [ ] The MCP `create_idea` tool creates an `epic` in status `idea` in one CREATE
      event.
- [ ] The library `rebar.idea(...)` creates an `epic` in status `idea` in one
      CREATE event.
- [ ] No surface gains a general `create --status` flag.
- [ ] The create-time file_impact stderr warning does not fire for a ticket created
      by `rebar idea`.
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` states that a CREATE event may carry `status`.
- [ ] The command/tool reference lists `rebar idea`, `create_idea`, and
      `rebar.idea`.
- [ ] After S1 (status vocabulary) and S2 (close-bypass) have landed, an
      end-to-end smoke test demonstrates the user-facing flow: `rebar idea`
      creates a ticket absent from `ready`/`next-batch`; `transition idea open`
      promotes it to claimable work; `transition idea closed` succeeds with no
      completion-gate error. (This AC is gated on the S1/S2 prerequisite above.)
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: Add atomic 'idea' command (CLI/MCP/library) creating an epic in status idea

baseline.description:
## Report

`scripts/canary_bridge.py:26` does a bare `import alert_dedup`. That only resolves when `scripts/` is already on `sys.path`. Running the affected test file on its own fails:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py -q
ERROR ...::test_every_bug_close_carries_valid_class[heartbeat-alert-_heartbeat_recovery_env]
  - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'alert_dedup'
ERROR ...::test_every_bug_close_carries_valid_class[binding-drift-alert-_drift_recovery_env]
  - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'alert_dedup'
1 passed, 2 errors
```

Reproduced on `origin/main` with the repo venv on PATH.

## Provenance — introduced today, not pre-existing

`scripts/alert_dedup.py` was ADDED by `0767c38ebb` (ticket 63e8, "route dependency advisories by lane"). That change correctly EXTRACTED the dedup helpers out of `canary_bridge.py` rather than duplicating them — the extraction was the right call — but it left the consumers importing the new module by bare name.

## Why it matters even though CI is green

CI's full run passes because `tests/scripts/conftest.py:32-38` inserts repo-root `scripts/` on `sys.path` at collection time, and that process-wide side effect leaks into every later-collected module in the same session — including `tests/unit/`, which has no such insert of its own. The failure only appears when the file is run as a SUBSET — which is what developers and agents do constantly while iterating. A test that passes in CI and fails when you run it directly trains people to distrust the suite.

## Chosen mechanism (AC2 decision, stated up front)

**An explicit `sys.path` insert of the script's own directory, immediately above the sibling import** — the pattern already established in this repo by `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:46-51`. Rationale, and why the two alternatives are rejected:

- *Package-relative import* — rejected. These modules are executed as standalone scripts by
  workflow YAML (`python scripts/canary_bridge.py heartbeat-alert …`,
  `scripts/dependency_audit.py gate`). A relative import raises
  `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` under that
  invocation, so it would trade a test-only failure for a production-canary failure.
- *Making `scripts/` a real package* — rejected. Adding `scripts/__init__.py` changes how
  every script in the directory is resolved by every existing caller (workflows, Makefile,
  pre-commit), which is a far larger blast radius than the defect, and is not
  behavior-preserving.

The chosen insert is invocation-independent: it derives the directory from `__file__`, so it holds under `python scripts/x.py`, `python -m pytest`, bare `pytest`, and `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` alike. It is idempotent (guarded by a membership check) and does not reorder any path entry that is already present.

## Sweep of sibling call sites (AC3)

Every bare import under `scripts/` of a module that lives in `scripts/` or `tests/`:

| Site | Status |
|---|---|
| `scripts/canary_bridge.py:26` `import alert_dedup` | **UNGUARDED — fix here** |
| `scripts/dependency_audit.py:50` `import alert_dedup` | **UNGUARDED — fix here** |
| `scripts/calibrate_completion_floor.py:24` `from gold_set_completion import …` | SAFE — line 22 explicitly inserts `tests/unit` derived from `__file__` immediately above it |
| `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:51` `import jira_dc_field_readiness` | SAFE — lines 46-48 insert `scripts/` from `__file__`; this is the precedent pattern |
| `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:59` `from _engine_path import engine_dir` | SAFE — lines 57-58 insert `tests/` from `__file__` |

The sweep is valid as of the sha it runs against and is re-run against merged `main` before push.

## Guard (AC4/AC5) — closing the other half of the class

Ticket `a371` (merged `1db88c92d7`) landed `tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py`, which AST-scans for `tests.`-rooted imports **under `tests/`**. It does not look at `scripts/`, so the class is only half-guarded. This adds the companion: `tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py`, same AST-scan shape, asserting that every bare import under `scripts/` naming a module that is only resolvable via a directory insert is preceded by that insert in the same file — plus a subprocess check that the affected test module collects when run alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1 — the reported repro passes standalone.**
  Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py -q` exits 0 with
  0 errors (repo venv on PATH, no wrapper).
- [x] **AC2 — the import is resolved by an explicit, invocation-independent mechanism.** Both
  fixed sites derive the directory from `__file__` and insert it idempotently above the
  import; neither relies on ambient `sys.path` ordering.
  Verify (asserts the insert itself, not merely the token `__file__`):
  `python -c "import sys; bad=[p for p in ['scripts/canary_bridge.py','scripts/dependency_audit.py'] for w in [open(p).read().split('import alert_dedup')[0]] if not ('sys.path.insert' in w and '__file__' in w)]; print(bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"`
  exits 0 and prints `[]`.
- [x] **AC3 — sibling call sites swept and classified.** The table above enumerates all five
  bare sibling-import sites and states which are safe and why.
  Verify (AST scan that distinguishes sibling imports from stdlib/third-party by resolving
  each imported top-level name against a real file under `scripts/` or `tests/**`, then
  compares the resulting set to the five documented rows — exits 0 and prints `OK` only on
  an exact match):
  `python -c "$(cat <<'PY'
import ast, pathlib, sys root = pathlib.Path('.') sib = {p.stem for p in root.glob('scripts/*.py')} | {p.stem for p in root.glob('tests/**/*.py')} found = set() for p in sorted(root.glob('scripts/*.py')):
    tree = ast.parse(p.read_text(), filename=str(p))
    for n in ast.walk(tree):
        names = [a.name for a in n.names] if isinstance(n, ast.Import) else (
            [n.module] if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom) and n.level == 0 and n.module else [])
        for m in names:
            if m.split('.')[0] in sib and m.split('.')[0] != p.stem:
                found.add(f"{p}:{n.lineno}:{m}")
expected = {
 'scripts/canary_bridge.py:__L__:alert_dedup',
 'scripts/dependency_audit.py:__L__:alert_dedup',
 'scripts/calibrate_completion_floor.py:__L__:gold_set_completion',
 'scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:__L__:jira_dc_field_readiness',
 'scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:__L__:_engine_path'}
norm = {':'.join([a, '__L__', c]) for a, _, c in (f.split(':') for f in found)} print(sorted(norm - expected) or 'OK'); sys.exit(1 if norm - expected else 0) PY )"`
  (line numbers are normalized out so the check survives the insert shifting them).
- [x] **AC4 — the a371 guard has a companion covering `scripts/`.**
  Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q` exits 0, and the
  new file exists.
- [x] **AC5 — the guard is proven RED against the defect.**
  Verify: reverting the `sys.path` insert in `scripts/canary_bridge.py` and re-running
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q` FAILS naming
  `scripts/canary_bridge.py`; restoring it makes it pass. Run this before landing and record
  the output in a ticket comment.
- [x] **AC6 — no behavior change and no regression.**
  Verify: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit tests/scripts -q`
  all pass.

## Out of scope

Any change to what `canary_bridge.py` or `dependency_audit.py` DO — this is an import- resolution repair only. No CLI surface, no argv, no output text changes.
baseline.summary: canary_bridge's bare 'import alert_dedup' resolves only when scripts/ is on sys.path; subset test runs error

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Code review has no criterion that owns correctness races. The security overlay covers only attacker-framed TOCTOU; the performance overlay covers only load-shaped concurrency (stampede, pool exhaustion); the base reviewer has no concurrency rubric. A traced corpus of four real production races in this repo shows the gap: `eclectic-spotted-barb` (detached drain child commits with a raw unlocked whole-index `git rm`+`commit`, racing locked `stage_and_commit` writers — introduced by 9ad46965bd), `fine-wisteria-solenodon` (fsck Check 3 reclaims `index.lock` via getmtime-then-remove TOCTOU — introduced by 56e130ff71), `greisen-draconian-annelid` (verify→sign reads HEAD twice; drift guard detects but closes unsigned anyway — introduced by 3938c7ed2d), and `fervid-boring-python` (CI bash retry with exponential backoff on a CAS race — introduced by ea79ecca7f). Siblings `malevolent-emigratory-umbrette` and `grassgreen-clotty-duck` are the same "unlocked twin" class, making it this codebase's modal race. Plan review already covers concurrency (T9 shared-state lifecycle, G6 mechanism correctness); code review does not.

## Approach

Add a `concurrency` Pass-1 specialist overlay to the four-pass code-review gate, following the established overlay invariants (rubric + FP guards carried in the overlay because Pass-2 is domain-blind; evidence-record contract; no model-emitted severity; empty findings expected). The rubric is lockset-first — the Eraser/RacerD "inconsistent synchronization discipline on the same resource" heuristic — because it is a citation lookup rather than an interleaving argument, so it stays reliable on less capable agents and decomposes into sub-claims the existing Pass-2 verifier disciplines already check (reachability-via-callers, prove-absence-by-searching). The overlay fires via a two-layer deterministic lexical trigger, mirroring RacerD's production precedent of a single lexical cue flipping on the analysis: a committed high-precision cross-stack token list (survey-grounded: Lu et al. ASPLOS'08, Tu et al. ASPLOS'19, RacerD trigger heuristic, CodeQL CERT packs; measured 14% fire rate over this repo's last 300 main commits), plus a project-extensible noisy tier in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` that rebar itself dogfoods (noisy tier measured +21%; it is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here). **Recall boundary (committed vs project tier), stated explicitly:** the committed high-precision tier is deliberately stack-agnostic and low-noise, so it fires only on hunks bearing an explicit synchronization primitive (thread/async/DB-lock/file-lock tokens) and DOES NOT fire on this codebase's MODAL unlocked-twin class — the raw `git rm`+`git commit` whole-index writes (`eclectic-spotted-barb`, `malevolent-emigratory-umbrette`, `grassgreen-clotty-duck`) and the `os.path.getmtime`-then-`os.remove` on `index.lock` reclaim (`fine-wisteria-solenodon`) carry no such token. Portable recall on that modal class is delivered NOT by the built-in but by the project-extensible noisy tier: a fresh project that installs the built-in overlay without adding its own `trigger_tokens` will not escalate its own git-index/lockfile unlocked-twin race, and is expected to layer its repo-specific vocabulary (as rebar itself dogfoods in the final child, e.g. `.lock`, `stage_and_commit`, `refs/reconciler/`). This is an accepted, documented recall boundary of the committed tier, not a defect — the two-tier split is the mechanism by which the built-in stays portable while this repo still catches its modal races. The overlay ships advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) per this repo's calibrate-then-flip precedent (`api-compat`, `tests`, `deletion-impact`); the blocking flip is explicitly out of scope pending calibration volume. Accepted v1 blind spots, documented rather than promised: no-twin races (the `greisen-draconian-annelid` twice-read-HEAD class) and CI-level CAS/backoff judgment (the `fervid-boring-python` class) — these are the lexical/judgment ceiling confirmed independently by the survey's blind-spot analysis.

## Child decomposition

Children deliver, respectively: the project-extensible trigger mechanism for built-in overlays (`trigger_tokens` + `applies_to` union consumed through effective routing); the overlay's Pass-1 reviewer prompt carrying the full rubric; the generic registration (overlay id, committed high-precision content trigger scanning added and removed lines, base-catalog escalation line, advisory routing entry); a standing eval spec distilled from the traced corpus (recall and no-fire families, including the deliberate check-then-act hard-FP control); and the rebar dogfood entry plus the two-layer trigger documentation. Dependencies: registration depends on the prompt existing (the workflow must never escalate to a dimension with no reviewer); the eval depends on the prompt; the dogfood depends on both the extension mechanism and the registered overlay id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A code-review run over a diff seeded with an unlocked-twin race surfaces a Pass-1 `concurrency` finding; checked by the standing eval `rebar prompt eval code-review-concurrency` passing its gate.
- [x] The `concurrency` overlay fires deterministically from diff content via the committed high-precision token trigger (added and removed lines), and appears in the base reviewer's overlay catalog for escalation; checked by unit tests over corpus-derived diff hunks. The committed-trigger unit tests NAME the coverage split: hunks bearing an explicit synchronization primitive (e.g. `Lock(`, `flock`, `RwLock`) fire the committed tier, while the unlocked-twin corpus hunks (raw `git rm`+`git commit`, `getmtime`+`os.remove` on `index.lock`) carry no committed token and are covered only by the project noisy tier — so the committed-tier test asserts the sync-primitive hunks fire and the project-tier config-effect test (AC#4) asserts the unlocked-twin vocabulary fires only under project routing.
- [x] A project can extend a built-in overlay's trigger vocabulary and `applies_to` globs through `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` without code changes; checked by unit tests with a project-overlay fixture.
- [x] rebar's own `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries the noisy-tier concurrency vocabulary as the documented worked example, and the two-layer trigger design is documented in `docs/llm-framework.md`; checked by a config-effect test proving a project token (`index.lock`) triggers the overlay under this repo's effective routing but not under committed-only routing.
- [x] The committed routing entry for `concurrency` is advisory (`block_threshold` 0.95, `blocking_enabled` false); checked by a unit assertion on `threshold_for("concurrency")`.
baseline.summary: Concurrency code-review overlay: lexical trigger, lockset-first rubric, project-extensible vocabulary

baseline.description:
# S3 — First-class AWS Bedrock provider (native, no gateway) with measured prompt caching

## Context / Problem

rebar has no Bedrock path. Our clients will reach Claude through Bedrock more often than through the direct Anthropic API, and PR #121's answer — front Bedrock with an OpenAI-compatible gateway — forces every operator to stand up and accredit a proxy, and gives up prompt caching, the retrying transport, and native structured output in the process.

## Approach

Register a `bedrock` builder in the provider factory [rebar:7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1] that constructs pydantic-ai's native `BedrockConverseModel` with a `BedrockProvider`, authenticating through the ambient AWS credential chain (instance role in production, `AWS_PROFILE`/env locally) — no rebar-managed key. Prompt caching is already selected by the `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` capability shipped in story f184, which sets **exactly two** keys — `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions`. An earlier draft of this plan named a third (`bedrock_cache_messages`); that is **rejected** for parity, because the direct-Anthropic path sets only the matching two and `AnthropicModelSettings.anthropic_cache_messages` is likewise left unset. Enabling message caching on Bedrock alone would make it cache MORE than Anthropic, which is a new behaviour with its own cost and TTL profile — a separate decision with its own measurement, not a third key smuggled in here. The parity bar in story 0d76 is measured against exactly these two keys. Ships as a new `[bedrock]` optional extra (`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`) so boto3 stays out of the default `[agents]` install; the builder raises a clear missing-extra error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

**Caching HAS been measured (real AWS, us-east-2, account 5797…98).** The measurement is done; this section records the results and the decisions they force, so no implementer has to guess. Oracle: the same request twice with a `cachePoint` after a ~4000-token stable system prefix, reading `cacheReadInputTokens` / `cacheWriteInputTokens` off the real Converse response.

1. **On-demand model ids are not invokable at all** in this account/region — both
   `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` and the older `anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` return
   `ValidationException: Invocation of model ID … with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request
   with the ID or ARN of an inference profile.` So this story's original on-demand-vs-profile comparison is
   moot: **only inference profiles work**, and rebar's documented default must be one.
2. **A regional inference profile DOES cache.** `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`: attempt 1
   `cache_write=4017, cache_read=0`; attempt 2 `cache_write=0, cache_read=4017`; reproducible across runs (a
   later run hit a still-warm cache, 5-minute TTL). This **refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381** for this
   model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce.
3. **Caching is MODEL-dependent and fails SILENTLY.** `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` and
   `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` both report `cache_read=0` AND `cache_write=0` on both
   attempts, billing the full 4029 input tokens every call — no error, no warning. A controlled same-model
   comparison (`us.` vs `global.`) showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the **model**, not the profile
   prefix. Silent full-price billing is the real hazard here.
4. `us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` with a `cachePoint` hard-fails:
   `AccessDeniedException: You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching.`

**Decision A — the default is `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`**, the verified-caching regional inference profile. Config accepts any profile id; this is what the docs recommend and what the parity story measures.

**Decision B — rebar must WARN when caching was requested but both counters are zero.** Because failure is silent, an operator otherwise pays full input price on every call forever with no signal.

**It cannot reuse `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, and that is the whole point of specifying it.** That guard fires on `requests > 0 AND input_tokens == 0 AND output_tokens == 0` — the zeroed-adapter case. The measured Bedrock failure is the opposite shape: `input_tokens=4029` (a perfectly healthy count) with `cache_read=0` and `cache_write=0`. The existing predicate never fires, so extending it would silently do nothing.

A SEPARATE helper is required, with this predicate:

    caching_requested AND usage.cache_read_tokens == 0 AND usage.cache_write_tokens == 0 AND usage.input_tokens > 0

- "caching_requested" is embodied by the existing local the runner already computes for the cache gate —
  `cache_settings is not None` (equivalently `caps.prompt_cache_style != "none"`). No new state is needed.
- It is invoked at the same seam as `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, i.e. after `_extract_usage()` on the success path,
  and is gated on `self._model_override is None` for the same reason that guard is (test doubles report no usage).
- WARNING level, observability only, NEVER blocking — an ineffective cache is a cost problem, not a correctness
  one, and must not fail a gate run.
- The message must name the model id and both counters, so the operator can act (switch to a
  measured-caching model id) rather than merely learn that something is wrong.

### Decision C — `temperature` is FATAL on Bedrock for some models (found by measurement, not in the original plan)

`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` with `temperature=0` returns **400 `ValidationException: temperature is deprecated for this model`**; the identical call without it succeeds. Reproduced through pydantic-ai as well: `BedrockConverseModel` + `BedrockModelSettings(temperature=0.0)` → `ModelHTTPError` 400.

This breaks rebar's gates on Bedrock, not just a corner case: `runner.py` sets `model_settings["temperature"]` whenever `cfg.temperature`/`req.config.temperature` is set, and the plan-review **Pass-2 verifiers deliberately send `temperature=0`** so re-verifying a finding does not resample. Critically, `_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings` exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's `models/anthropic.py`, **not** in `models/bedrock.py` — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully (warning: "Sampling parameters ['temperature'] are not supported … will be ignored") and the Bedrock path hard-fails.

**Decision: carry it as a capability — but f184's override table must first learn the MODEL NAME.**

An earlier draft of this decision said "add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock models". That is **not implementable as f184 shipped**, and the gap is worth stating precisely: f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates receive only the `ModelProfile`, and `BedrockModelProfile` carries **no per-model identifier** (verified: no model/name attribute on the profile object). So the only predicate expressible today is "is this Bedrock-hosted Claude", which would strip `temperature` from `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` too — the measured-good default — destroying exactly the greedy Pass-2 determinism this decision exists to protect.

So this story adds a SEPARATE, additive table rather than changing f184's contract. f184 is **closed and its plan-review attestation is signed**, and it defines its override predicates as `Callable[[ModelProfile], bool]`; widening that signature would silently redefine a shipped, signed contract from a downstream leaf. The rule is that the parent wins, so f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` and its `_is_claude` predicate are left **exactly** as shipped.

1. Add `supports_temperature: bool = True` to `ModelCapabilities`.
2. Add a **second, distinct** override table, `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES: dict[str, Mapping[str, object]]`,
   keyed on the **exact** model id, applied AFTER the profile-shaped overrides. The two tables encode genuinely
   different things and are better apart than merged: f184's keys on *capability shape* (what kind of model is
   this), this one keys on *a specific model's API defect* (this exact id rejects a parameter).
3. Keys are **exact-set membership, never prefix matching**. That is both cleaner — only model ids whose
   behaviour has actually been MEASURED get an entry, so the table never speculates — and it preserves f184's
   attested criterion that `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is empty.
4. **`capabilities_for()`'s BODY changes; its public signature does not.** An earlier draft said "no signature
   change is needed anywhere", which misleadingly implied no change at all. To be exact — the shipped body reads
   only `getattr(model_or_model_string, "profile", None)` and, for strings, `partition(":")`; it never touches
   `model_name`. The required edit, stated as control flow so nothing is left to inference:

   - the private helper becomes `_capabilities_from_profile(profile, model_id: str | None)` — a PRIVATE helper,
     so this is not the signed `_REBAR_OVERRIDES`/`capabilities_for` contract f184 attested;
   - **path 1 (model object):** `model_id = getattr(model_or_model_string, "model_name", None)` (verified: a
     `BedrockConverseModel` returns e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), passed alongside the profile;
   - **path 2 (model string):** the id is the value `partition(":")` ALREADY produces — reuse it, do not re-parse;
   - **path 3 (conservative fallback):** no id is available, so no model-id override applies — the conservative
     record is returned unchanged, exactly as today;
   - **ordering inside the helper:** derive the fields from the profile, apply f184's profile-shaped
     `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` first (unchanged, first-match-wins), THEN apply
     `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES.get(model_id, {})` on top, so an exact-id entry wins over a shape-based one.
     A model id absent from the table changes nothing.

   `capabilities_for()`'s own parameter list, and f184's predicate signature, both stay as shipped.
5. `runner.py` omits `temperature` from `model_settings` when the capability is False, logging once at INFO that
   it did and why.

**This is model-id matching, and that is deliberate, not a relapse.** The epic's criterion forbids selecting *provider behaviour* by matching a *provider-name* string; recording a known per-model API defect is a different thing, and it is what pydantic-ai itself does — its profile functions dispatch on `model_name` (`anthropic_model_profile(model_name)`), and upstream's own `anthropic_disallows_sampling_settings` flag exists for exactly this class of quirk on the Anthropic side.

**Honest limitation: the list will drift** as AWS deprecates sampling parameters on more models, and an unlisted-but-affected model still hard-fails. A denylist is chosen over an allowlist because an unknown-but-affected model then fails LOUDLY, whereas an allowlist would silently drop temperature from an unknown-but-fine model and let verdicts resample — a quiet correctness risk is worse than a loud configuration error.

#### The drift mitigation, specified (catch site, predicate, output)

An earlier draft promised to "translate a 400 naming a sampling parameter into an actionable error" without saying where or how, which is not implementable. Concretely:

**Catch site.** `runner.run()`'s existing `except Exception as exc` block (the one that wraps a systemic provider failure into `LLMUnavailableError`). The translation is attempted FIRST; only if it returns `None` does the existing `LLMUnavailableError` path run unchanged. Nothing else about that handler moves.

**Where the helper lives.** A new provider-AGNOSTIC function in the existing `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (already rebar's failure-classification seam):

    translate_sampling_parameter_rejection(exc, model_id: str) -> LLMConfigError | None

It must NOT live in the Bedrock leaf and must NOT introduce a provider-name branch in `runner.py` — the epic's criterion forbids that, and any provider could in principle reject a sampling parameter. It keys on the ERROR CONTENT, never on the provider name.

**Detection predicate**, grounded in the measured strings rather than invented. boto3 raises `ValidationException: The model returned the following errors: 'temperature' is deprecated for this model.`; through pydantic-ai the same failure surfaces as `ModelHTTPError: status_code: 400, model_name: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7, body: {'Error': {'Message': ...}}`. So the predicate is, on the exception or its `__cause__`:

- it looks like a client request rejection — `getattr(exc, "status_code", None) == 400` OR `"ValidationException"`
  appears in `str(exc)`; AND
- `str(exc)` mentions one of the sampling parameters rebar can send — `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`; AND
- it mentions a rejection word — `deprecated`, `not supported`, or `unsupported`.

All three conjuncts are required, so an unrelated 400 (a malformed request, a bad model id) is NOT swallowed and keeps its existing `LLMUnavailableError` classification.

**Output.** An `LLMConfigError` naming (a) the model id, (b) the offending parameter, and (c) BOTH remedies: add the id to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` with `supports_temperature=False`, or unset the temperature config. The whole point is that the operator learns what to change, not merely that something failed.

Rejected alternatives: dropping temperature on ALL Bedrock calls (loses Pass-2 greedy determinism on the measured-good default); catching the 400 and retrying without it (burns a billable, often multi-minute agentic call and keys on model-specific error text).

Note this also widens f184's signed capability record, which story 343b stamps into the verdict sidecar — doing it now is cheaper than after that payload shape is signed in the field. It directly de-risks story eb6e (the production review-bot cutover with no Anthropic fallback), which would otherwise hard-fail on such a model.

**Alternative rejected:** OpenAI-compatible gateway fronting Bedrock (PR #121). No proxy is needed for the native path, and the gateway path measurably loses caching and native structured output.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` (**new leaf**, mirroring `anthropic_model.py`) — the `bedrock` builder and
  its `BedrockProvider`/`BedrockConverseModel` construction. It does NOT go in `providers.py`: that file is at
  289 LOC against the **300-LOC cap that is an attested criterion of closed story 7468**, so the builder
  would breach a signed criterion. `providers.py` gains only the one-line registry entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — `supports_temperature` on the record plus a NEW exact-id
  `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` table (Decision C). f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicate signature and
  `_is_claude` are left UNCHANGED — that contract is closed and signed. The profile override for Bedrock-hosted Claude and the `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"`
  cache-settings selection are **ALREADY SHIPPED by closed story f184** — verify, do not re-add.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — omit `temperature` when the capability withdraws it, and add the Decision B
  cache-zero warning. **BLOCKED ON task `2682-b015-4fe5-4066` (the runner.py split), which MUST land first.**
  Both additions are strictly positive LOC and `runner.py` is at EXACTLY the 800-LOC hard cap, so there is no
  net-neutral way to make them: an earlier draft said "net-neutral or the split lands first" without naming
  a dependency, which left an implementer facing a signed-criterion conflict with no resolution. The split is
  now a recorded blocking edge, not an aspiration. Story `343b` (verdict provenance) needs the same headroom.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — Bedrock region + model-id/inference-profile config keys.
- `pyproject.toml` — a `[bedrock]` optional extra (`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`), AND that same extra added to
  the **`dev`** extra so this story's unit tests actually RUN in CI rather than skipping.

  The runtime posture is unchanged and that is the point: `[agents]` does not gain boto3, so
  `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still has no AWS dependency (an explicit AC below). But `BedrockConverseModel`
  and `BedrockModelSettings` are unimportable without it, so without the dev entry every builder-construction
  assertion would be `importorskip`-ed away in CI and the criteria would only ever be provable on a developer's
  machine. This is the SAME precedent story `dc0d` set for `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`, and the same one `mcp`
  already sets — an optional runtime extra that `dev` installs so its tests are real. Note most of this story's
  new logic (the `supports_temperature` override, the cache-zero warning, the 400 translation) is deliberately
  testable with profile STUBS and needs no boto3 at all; only construction does.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated.
- `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` (new); `tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py` (new, env-gated).

  **It MUST live under `tests/external/`, not a new `tests/live/`.** An earlier draft said `tests/live/`,
  which does not exist and would have been a live landmine: `tests/conftest.py` (a) auto-applies the
  `external` marker to every item under `tests/external/`, and (b) HARD-FAILS collection for any item marked
  `external` that lives outside it. A canary at `tests/live/` would therefore either be collected by the
  default CI selection (`-m "not integration and not external"`) and make billable AWS calls on every CI
  run, or — if marked `external` by hand — break collection for the WHOLE suite. Existing precedents to
  follow: `tests/external/test_completion_pass_live.py`, `tests/external/test_deps_live.py`.

## Testing

Two tiers, because the mechanism spans a pure construction path and a real external service.

- Unit (construction, mocked boto3 client): the builder produces a `BedrockConverseModel` whose settings carry
  **exactly the two** `bedrock_cache_*` keys the parity decision above fixes —
  `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` — and NOT `bedrock_cache_messages`; a plain on-demand id and an inference-profile ARN both construct; a missing
  `[bedrock]` extra raises `LLMConfigError` naming the install command. Contrast case: an `anthropic` model
  still gets `anthropic_cache_*`, never `bedrock_cache_*`.
- Live canary (env-gated, `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK=1`, skipped in default CI): issue the same cached-prefix request
  twice and assert `usage.cache_read_tokens > 0` on the second — the observable oracle for "caching works".
  Run it for both the on-demand id and the inference-profile ARN and record both results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<claude-id> rebar review-plan <ticket>` completes with a valid structured verdict
      against real Bedrock, output attached as a comment on this ticket
- [x] **MEASURED** — the cache canary result is recorded on this ticket: on-demand ids are not invokable at all
      here; `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` caches (`cache_write=4017` then `cache_read=4017`, reproducible);
      `us.`/`global.` opus-4-5 silently do not cache. rebar documents `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` as the
      default
- [ ] a test asserts rebar WARNS when caching was requested but both cache counters are zero (Decision B),
      since the failure is otherwise silent and bills full input every call
- [ ] a test asserts `temperature` is omitted for a model whose `supports_temperature` capability is False,
      and still sent for one where it is True (Decision C) — the contrast case
- [ ] unit tests pass with no AWS credentials present (boto3 client mocked), proving default CI is unaffected
- [ ] the live canary lives under `tests/external/` and is EXCLUDED by the default selection
      `-m "not integration and not external"` — verified by confirming the default suite's collected count is
      unchanged by its addition, so CI never makes a billable AWS call
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still installs without boto3 (`python -c "import boto3"` fails in that env)
- [ ] f184's shipped contract is untouched: `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates still take a single `ModelProfile`
      argument and `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is still empty
- [ ] a test asserts a provider error matching the MEASURED shape (400 / ValidationException + a sampling
      parameter name + a rejection word) becomes an `LLMConfigError` naming the model id, the parameter, and
      both remedies — and a CONTRAST case asserts an unrelated 400 still becomes `LLMUnavailableError`, so the
      translation cannot swallow unrelated failures
- [ ] `grep -n 'bedrock\|anthropic' src/rebar/llm/failure.py` shows no provider-name branch — the translation
      keys on error CONTENT only
- [ ] a test asserts the conservative-fallback path still returns the unchanged conservative record when no
      model id is available (the third path above), so adding the second table cannot alter it
- [ ] a test asserts an exact-id override WINS over a profile-shaped one for the same model (ordering)
- [ ] a t … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: S3 — first-class AWS Bedrock provider (native, no gateway) with measured prompt caching
