# Stale ticket snapshot in the completion verifier — CONFIRMED DEFECT (plus a second, independent bare-FAIL defect)

## Disposition

Hypothesis 1 (**staleness defect**) CONFIRMED; hypothesis 3 (**a non-itemized FAIL is indistinguishable from "no verdict obtainable"**) CONFIRMED as a SECOND, independent defect. Hypothesis 2 (deliberate anti-gaming snapshot) REJECTED: the pin is deliberate, but its documented purpose is reproducibility/signability and its docstring states the goal is to pin "the shared store, **not a stale local copy**" (`repo_snapshot.py:546-548`) — staleness is contrary to intent.

### Root cause 1 — the close path pins the ticket store with no fetch

`close_precheck` calls the verifier with `fetch=False` (`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:505-512`), justified in its own comment (`:502-504`) only for the CODE ref (`HEAD`, always local). `resolve_gate_handle` threads the same flag into the TICKET store pin (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:115`), and in `materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:568-576`) `fetch=False` skips `origin/tickets` and pins the main repo's local `refs/heads/tickets` — a mirror that only advances on fetch. `.tickets-tracker/` is a SEPARATE repository, so that mirror is arbitrarily stale (measured here: 6757 commits behind). Reproduced deterministically, no LLM call — `materialize_tickets(fetch=False)` then `show_ticket(cb91)` yields `{status: open, comments: 0}`, while `fetch=True` yields `{status: in_progress, comments: 2}`. That `status: open` + `comments: []` is verbatim what incident 1's stored `COMPLETION_VERDICT` cited as its authoritative evidence.

### Root cause 1b — the two halves of the gate read different stores

The fenced context given to the model comes from the LIVE store (`gate_ops.py:174,190`); the model's own `show_ticket` reads the PINNED snapshot (`runner.py:335-337`). The prompt labels that context `<untrusted_ticket_context>` and names `show_ticket` authoritative (`completion_verifier.md:26-28`), so the model correctly preferred the stale snapshot.

### Root cause 2 — a FAIL with no findings is fabricated, not reported

`reconcile_verdict` (`completion.py:454-467`) coerces any non-`PASS` verdict to `FAIL`, then, when `findings` is empty, SYNTHESIZES a placeholder criterion `(unspecified)` — exactly what incident 3's stored verdict shows. Unlike plan-review (unsigned `INDETERMINATE`, exit 2), completion verification cannot say "I could not obtain a verdict".

## Implementation plan

1. **Pin the ticket store at the LIVE store's own HEAD.** `materialize_tickets`
   (`repo_snapshot.py:534`) resolves the sha from the live tracker repo (`.tickets-tracker`) HEAD
   when present — the state every other rebar read sees — so the pin is current-at-close by
   construction and the gate's two halves stop disagreeing. Still immutable-by-sha and signable.
   `fetch` keeps its meaning ("may I touch the network?"), applied uniformly to every caller:
   - `fetch=True` (`review-plan` via `operations.py:203`, standalone `verify-completion`, MCP):
     force an UN-throttled reconverge of the tracker with `origin/tickets` (the `_store.sync`
     implementation `reads.ensure_fresh` uses, called so the <=1/min marker is bypassed).
     `reconverge` returns `None` on success AND on every failure, so it yields no usable signal;
     `materialize_tickets` confirms the outcome itself with `git -C <tracker> merge-base
     --is-ancestor <remote>/tickets HEAD`. Exit 0 (at-or-ahead) => pin tracker HEAD. Non-zero, or
     the fetch / `rev-parse <remote>/tickets` failing => fall back to today's exact behaviour,
     `resolve_ref(f"{remote}/tickets", fetch=True)`, so "no content visible today is lost" holds
     unconditionally, not only when a throttle window is open.
   - `fetch=False` (close path): pin tracker HEAD as-is — current-at-close, never the stale mirror.
   - Tracker absent (CI, checkout-less): unchanged `origin/tickets` -> local-branch chain.
2. **Give completion verification a "no verdict obtainable" channel.** Indeterminacy rides on a
   NEW framework-set boolean `verdict_obtainable`, NOT a third verdict token: the `{PASS, FAIL}`
   vocabulary, its normalizing validator, and fail-closed blocking stay intact, and no token can
   be coerced away. Touch points, all of them:
   - `reconcile_verdict` (`completion.py:442`) — the rule keys on FINDINGS, since `gate_ops`
     populates `result["criteria"]` before delegating here, so a genuine fault can arrive with a
     criteria manifest. For a non-PASS verdict with zero `findings`: if `criteria` holds any
     `met: false` entries, synthesize real findings FROM them (named criteria, NOT a fault); only
     when no unmet criterion is identifiable from either source, set `verdict_obtainable=false`
     and emit a finding saying no usable verdict was produced, replacing the fabricated
     `(unspecified)`. `verdict` stays `FAIL`, so every existing consumer still blocks.
   - `gate_ops.completion_reconcile` (`workflow/gate_ops.py:297`), the workflow close-gate path
     that also stamps `certifiable`: inherits the marker by delegating to `reconcile_verdict`;
     asserted by a test. Such a verdict is never certifiable and never signs, as any FAIL today.
   - `completion_sidecar` (`completion_sidecar.py:323`): the marker rides onto the durable record
     so a fault is queryable afterwards rather than looking like an unmet criterion.
   - `close_precheck.py:543`: check `verdict_obtainable` BEFORE the `!= PASS` branch and route it
     to a distinct message naming it a verifier fault, with retryable exit 11 instead of 1.
   - `_cli/_llm_commands.py:383-389` — the standalone `verify-completion` exit mapping, which
     today flattens every non-PASS verdict to exit 1: route `verdict_obtainable=false` to the same
     retryable exit 11 `_llm_error_exit_code` uses, so a fault is retryable from either entry
     point.
   - `schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json`: document the optional boolean.
3. **Fix the misleading wording at its real sites.** The "does not exist" phrasing is
   model-generated, so nothing is deleted from the prompt; instead (a) `completion_verifier.md`
   gains an instruction that an absence seen via `show_ticket` must be reported as "not visible in
   the ticket snapshot I read", never as a claim the record does not exist, and (b)
   `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE` (`completion.py:54`) is reworded to match.
4. **Document the ticket-store pin** in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` (today it covers only the
   code snapshot), cross-referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] The investigation is settled and durably recorded here: the
      `show_ticket` read path with its exact pin point, and the verdict (staleness defect, NOT a
      deliberate review-time snapshot). Evidence: the "Disposition" and "Root cause" sections of
      this description, each carrying file:line citations. Already satisfied by the text above;
      the remaining ACs are the code end-states.
- [x] The pinned ticket snapshot reflects the live store at close time, with a regression test
      that fails before the fix.
- [x] The `fetch=True` consumers are covered: a regression test proves a `fetch=True` snapshot
      still contains everything `origin/tickets` holds (including via the confirm-or-fall-back
      path). Tracker-repo-absent environments keep the existing resolution.
- [x] A non-PASS verdict from which no unmet criterion is identifiable sets
      `verdict_obtainable=false` and is reported as a verifier fault with a distinct message and
      retryable exit, not as a fabricated unmet criterion — with a regression test covering
      `reconcile_verdict` and the workflow path.
- [x] The unmet-criterion diagnostic distinguishes "not present" from "not visible in the
      snapshot read", and the ticket-store pin is documented in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier reads a stale ticket snapshot - bug or deliberate anti-gaming semantics? (2 recorded incidents)

# A rejected tickets-branch auto-push fails SILENTLY, and ticket event payloads are never scanned for secrets

Two hardening items carried forward from [rebar:94d0-5d19-2d06-4fa7] (closed). Its incident (live credentials in a ticket comment) is resolved -- credentials rotated, history scrubbed, branch pushing again -- but the two conditions that let it run for ~8 hours undetected are properties of the store, not of that incident, and remain.

## 1. A rejected auto-push is invisible to the agent that wrote

rebar's store auto-commits and auto-pushes every write to `sync.remote`. When that push is REJECTED, the write still succeeds locally and the command reports success.

Measured during the incident: 122 ticket commits accumulated locally over roughly eight hours while every push was rejected by GitHub push protection. Every `rebar comment`, `rebar transition` and `rebar create` in that window returned normally. The divergence was discovered only because an unrelated CI failure prompted a manual `git push`, which finally printed the rejection. Consequences observed: a Gerrit change could not pass its ticket gate because the ticket it referenced existed only locally; evidence recorded on epic children was invisible to CI and to every other agent session.

The store's whole premise is "every write is shared immediately" (`docs/concurrency.md`). A push that fails silently breaks that premise while preserving its appearance.

## 2. Ticket event payloads are never scanned for secrets

rebar runs `gitleaks` as its code-review secret gate, but that gate sees CODE. A ticket COMMENT is the one place an agent routinely pastes raw environment output. Nothing scans it on write.

## PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete -- see the RCA comment for full evidence)

Three mechanisms, each confirmed by DRIVING a real rejected push (local bare origin with a `pre-receive` hook exiting 1 with GH013-shaped stderr), reproduced independently twice.

**RC-1 (primary).** `src/rebar/_store/push.py:27` `_NON_FF = re.compile(r"non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first", re.IGNORECASE)` is the sole classifier splitting retriable non-fast-forward from terminal-report-with-stderr. Git's policy decline line `! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (pre-receive hook declined)` contains the bare token `rejected`, so `push.py:175` misroutes it onto the retry path, skipping the ONLY stderr-bearing log call (`push.py:176`), and exits at `push.py:296` with `"tickets branch push failed after %s retries"` -- retry count only. `run_git` DID capture the GH013 body (`gitutil.py:57-97`); it is discarded. Control experiment: a failure whose stderr lacks a non-ff token DOES print the full reason, proving the reason-bearing branch works and the rejected class specifically routes past it.

**RC-2.** `PUSH_PENDING` is computed at exactly one pull-only site (`_commands/fsck.py:365` `_tracker_sync_status`, called only from `fsck.py:203`) and is `is_issue=False` (`fsck.py:424-429`). No write path consults it, so the warning is byte-identical on write #1 and write #122 and nothing re-announces the growing backlog. This is the mechanism that explains eight hours.

**RC-3 (split out, see below).** On `sync.push=async` the push is a detached `Popen(..., stderr=DEVNULL)` (`push.py:128-141`) -- measured: exit 0, stderr COMPLETELY EMPTY. Library embedders get only the `NullHandler` (`rebar/__init__.py:131`). Under MCP the warning goes to the server's stderr, never into the tool result the writing agent reads.

**Prior art for the fix.** `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:723-747` (bug 4afc) already fixed this exact over-broad-`rejected`-substring class, with `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS = ("file exists", "hook declined", "internal server error", "rate limit")` and test `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`. `push.py` is the parallel surface that never got the rule.

## FIX PLAN (this ticket)

Scope is RC-1 + RC-2 -- both live on the same failure path in ONE file, `src/rebar/_store/push.py`.

1. Add a policy-rejection classifier beside `_NON_FF`, modelled on the trusted `_ref_lock.py`
   pattern: markers that name a NON-fast-forward cause (`hook declined`, `push declined`,
   `protected branch`, `rate limit`, `internal server error`, `permission denied`, `GH0`) mean
   the rejection is TERMINAL, not retriable. Such a push reports the reason immediately instead
   of burning three futile fetch+merge cycles.
2. Carry the git stderr tail into the terminal retries-exhausted warning at `push.py:296` so
   the failure self-identifies. The substring `failed after 3 retries` MUST be preserved --
   `tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py:198` and
   `tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py:216` assert it is absent in their
   scenarios, and rewording would silently weaken those negative assertions.
3. Include the unpushed-commit count (`origin/tickets..HEAD`) in the failure warning, so every
   subsequent write re-announces an ESCALATING backlog rather than an identical one-shot line.
   This is the "visible N-commits-unpushed state that subsequent commands report" the report
   asks for, and it is what breaks an eight-hour silence.

Constraint held throughout: "never fails the caller" is authoritative intent (`docs/concurrency.md:296-299`, `push.py:9-11` "ALWAYS returns None", `tests/unit/test_store.py:151,156`). The remedy is a SIGNAL, never an exception. No caller signature changes; every caller of `push_tickets_branch`/`push_after_commit` is a bare call whose result is already discarded, so the change has no behavioral dependents.

Test: a RED-first regression driving a REAL rejected push against a real local bare origin whose `pre-receive` hook declines -- asserting the surfaced warning names the reason and the backlog size, and that the write still succeeds. No mocks, no call counts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a rejected auto-push is surfaced to the writing caller rather than failing silently --
      the warning names the git rejection REASON and the number of unpushed commits
- [x] a test drives a REJECTED push (real git, real pre-receive decline) and asserts the caller
      sees it -- not a mock's call count
- [x] a policy rejection is not retried three times as if it were a non-fast-forward
- [x] the best-effort contract is preserved: the write still succeeds and the caller is not
      failed (regression-asserted)
- [x] [operator-attested] a recorded decision on scanning ticket event payloads for secrets on write -- including
      an explicit "no, and here is why" if that is the answer
baseline.summary: A rejected tickets-branch auto-push fails silently; ticket event payloads are never secret-scanned

## Context / Problem

RP-04's config-ownership drain reaches its final two rows. After C3f (`ed65`) drains the nine residual files, `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py` `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` holds exactly TWO rows, both on `_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_lifecycle.py`:

- `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` — the consecutive-404 absence-retire grace,
  read in `note_absent` via the local `_env_int` shim.
- `os.environ.get` — the raw ambient lookup inside that same `_env_int` parser.

Both were MOVED into `binding_lifecycle.py` from `binding_store.py` by RP-02 S2 (the absence policy travelled with them). RP-04 S7.3.a (ticket `6633`) closed having cut the reconciler CORE/JIRA reads but NOT these — its recorded file impact named the pre-move `binding_store.py`, so the moved reads fell through. Tracker `01d8` records the coupling but is bookkeeping-only (no file impact, out of the epic tree). This story is the executable drain that RP-02 S2's move left owing, and it is the LAST one before the whitelist is EMPTY.

## Key finding — the owned accessor already exists, exposed via the public facade

The cut is NOT a constructor-threading refactor. `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` (a composition root that owns env reads) ALREADY exposes `resolve_absent_retire_grace()` — "Owns the read for binding_store/binding_walk" — with byte-identical semantics to the local shim: raw `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` over the default `3`, clamped `>= 1`, malformed/absent → default. It is re-exported through the PUBLIC facade `rebar.config` (`config.py`: `from rebar._config_sources import resolve_absent_retire_grace as resolve_absent_retire_grace`), which is exactly how the sibling reconciler modules consume owned config (`fetcher.py`/`applier.py` use `from rebar.config import compose_config`/`repo_root_env`/`reconciler_repo_root`). So this is the established, in-process pattern — import the accessor from `rebar.config`, never from the private `_config_sources` module.

## Approach

1. In `binding_lifecycle.py::note_absent`, replace the
   `_env_int("RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE", _DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE, minimum=1)`
   call with `resolve_absent_retire_grace()` imported from the PUBLIC facade
   `from rebar.config import resolve_absent_retire_grace` (the same import
   direction `fetcher.py`/`applier.py` already use — no cycle).
2. Remove ONLY the now-dead `_env_int` helper (its single caller was that
   `note_absent` read), which eliminates the ambient `os.environ.get` read
   entirely. KEEP the `_DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` constant: it is a plain
   module constant (NOT an ambient read, so the gate never flagged it) and it
   has a live cross-module consumer — `binding_store.py` aliases it at import
   time (`_DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE = binding_lifecycle._DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE`)
   and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_no_resurrection_after_confirmed_delete_3b5f.py`
   reads that alias. It stays at `3`, agreeing with the accessor's default.
3. Remove BOTH `binding_lifecycle.py` rows from
   `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`. `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` is now EMPTY.

## Portability

The cut composes through an in-process owned accessor exposed on the public `rebar.config` facade; it has no CI-provider or external-service trigger. The config-ownership gate is a deterministic offline AST check. Works with any or no CI provider.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `note_absent`'s absence-retire grace is sourced from
  `resolve_absent_retire_grace()` imported from the public `rebar.config`
  facade; no ambient `os.environ` read or `_env_int`-style shim for it remains
  below the seam in `binding_lifecycle.py`.
- [x] The dead `_env_int` helper is removed (its only caller was rewired), so
  `binding_lifecycle.py` carries zero below-seam config/credential reads. The
  `_DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` constant is RETAINED (still aliased by
  `binding_store.py` and asserted by the resurrection test).
- [x] Both `binding_lifecycle.py` rows are removed from
  `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`, and `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` is now
  EMPTY (`[]`) — the whole-tree config-ownership drain is complete.
- [x] `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` reports zero findings with the
  whitelist empty.
- [x] Absence-retire behavior is byte-preserved: default 3, clamp `>= 1`,
  malformed/absent env → default; a set valid value is honored; a binding
  retires at exactly `grace` consecutive 404s.

## Testing / Verification

- Held-out oracle (RED-first before the cut): `python -m pytest
  tests/scripts/test_binding_lifecycle_grace_seam_clean_heldout.py -q` — asserts
  `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS == []`, the gate is clean for `binding_lifecycle.py`, no
  `_env_int` shim remains, and the grace behavior is byte-preserved.
- Config-ownership gate: `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` (exit 0).
- Module-size gate: `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ |
  xargs wc -l | awk '$2!="total" && $1>800'` (empty).
- Env-registry drift: `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check` (clean).
- Full pre-flight: `make lint && make typecheck`, plus the reconciler
  binding-lifecycle unit tests (`pytest -k "binding or resurrection"`).
baseline.summary: RP-04 C3g: cut binding_lifecycle absence-grace read (reach EMPTY)

## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` currently changes up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this deliberately covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

Author the behavioral oracle RED-first. Hold out the interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases from the implementer; expose only the basic dual-read happy path. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs is expected to advance and commit both rotation representations; claiming that such a pass makes no commit would contradict the required dual-write compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- new `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (docstring only)
- focused unit/integration/CLI tests

Estimated scope: M. Depends on closed A1 through the parent story.

baseline.description:
## Why

Every plan-review criterion that mentions the two headings POOLS them and applies ONE bar —
F1 reads "each acceptance/success criterion", G3 "each parent acceptance/success criterion",
G7 fetches "What/Scope/Success Criteria/Acceptance Criteria" as one contract. The dual
vocabulary is therefore noise in the rubrics: it suggests to the reviewing model a distinction
the criteria do not implement, and it is the source the generated criteria guide is built from.
This story removes it at the source.

## What

Rename Success Criteria -> Acceptance Criteria throughout the reviewer prompts and the criteria
routing index, then REGENERATE the criteria guide from them.

## Scope

Reviewer prompts (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`):
- `plan_review_F1.md:10` — "each acceptance/success criterion" -> "each acceptance criterion"
- `plan_review_G3.md:10` and `:12` — line 12 carries BOTH bare-`SC` tokens in the repo:
  "THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS" and "'SC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'"
- `plan_review_G5.md:19` ("a set of unrelated success criteria" — the decomposition tell,
  which DOES mean the ticket's criteria), `plan_review_G7.md:12` and `:16`,
  `plan_review_COH.md:10`, `plan_review_container.md:14`
- `completion_verifier.md:59` — the Epic bullet naming `## Success Criteria`

Routing index `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `check` strings at
`:544` (COH), `:830` (G3), `:908` (G7).

Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with
`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` — it is GENERATED and
carries a do-not-hand-edit banner; all 11 of its SC hits are downstream of the files above.

EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED — `plan_review_T2.md:10`. Its phrase is "a pilot with success metrics ...
or stated success criteria for a trial": generic English for the metrics that define whether an
EXPERIMENT succeeded, not the ticket heading. Renaming it to "acceptance criteria for a trial"
would change T2's meaning. This is the same false-positive class as `O-RAN-SC`; the site is
recorded here so a later sweep does not "fix" it.

OUT OF SCOPE: the `dod_uncertifiable` / "definition-of-done" wording in
`plan_review_verifier.md:81`, `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:87` and
`review_kernel/verify_models.py:231` — a related but distinct concept, tracked separately.

## Approach

Textual substitution in the listed files only. Two forms appear and both are handled:
the phrase "acceptance/success criteria|criterion" collapses to "acceptance criteria|criterion"
(not "acceptance/acceptance"), and standalone "Success Criteria" becomes "Acceptance Criteria".
G3's two bare-`SC` tokens are edited by hand, not by pattern, because `\bSC\b` also matches
`O-RAN-SC` elsewhere in the repo. Their exact replacements are:
`THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS` -> `THREE AC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS`, and
`'SC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'` ->
`'the AC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'`.

Editing `criteria_routing.json` rotates the `regver` criteria-registry stamp, which on TODAY's
`main` invalidates every outstanding plan-review attestation (632 tickets, ~40
open/in_progress) as `stale-regver`. Ticket `1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` (ADR 0053) grandfathers that
at the claim gate, and it HAS now merged — Gerrit change 962 landed as `095c4afef` and the
ticket is closed. This story's `depends_on 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` was a genuine MERGE-ORDER
constraint, not a preference: landing this rename first would have stranded ~40 in-flight
claims behind a full LLM re-review. That prerequisite is now SATISFIED, so the routing edit
is safe to make. (Status refreshed during implementation; the plan previously recorded 962
as still awaiting its votes.)

Once grandfathering has landed, the rotation is harmless at the claim gate (attestations stay
valid and report non-blocking `registry_drift`). It DOES still deny progressive drift-refresh
reuse, which is correct and expected.

## Testing

- Regenerate the guide and assert it is free of SC vocabulary (the regeneration is itself the
  check that the generator was run rather than the file hand-edited).
- `pytest tests/unit -k "criteria or routing or registry"` green.
- A test that captures `registry_version(None)` BEFORE applying the routing edit (from the
  pre-edit file content) and asserts it differs afterwards, so the rotation is proven by
  construction rather than compared against a literal that would rot the moment any other
  change touches `criteria_routing.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` returns matches ONLY at the three sites this
      story's Scope deliberately excludes, and no others — i.e. all 11 in-scope hits are gone.
      AMENDED during implementation: as originally written ("returns no matches") this criterion
      contradicted both this story's own Scope and its AC6. The three surviving hits are:
      `plan_review_T2.md:10` (generic English — "a pilot with metrics, or stated success criteria
      for a trial"; renaming it would change T2's meaning, and AC6 REQUIRES it to survive), and
      `plan_review_verifier.md:81` + `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:87`, which are the
      `dod_uncertifiable` "definition-of-done / success criterion" wording that Scope lists as
      OUT OF SCOPE (and that parent epic 1386 also excludes as a separate concept). Verify with
      `... | grep -v -e plan_review_T2.md -e plan_review_verifier.md -e plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`
      returning empty.
- [ ] `grep -noE "\bSCs?\b" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md` returns no matches (both
      bare tokens renamed).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is regenerated by the documented command, still
      carries its GENERATED banner, and `grep -niE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)"` on it returns
      EXACTLY ONE match — the T2 criterion's embedded prompt ("...stated success criteria for a
      trial"). AMENDED during implementation: "is empty" was unsatisfiable alongside AC6. The
      guide is a GENERATED snapshot of the registry and embeds each criterion's prompt verbatim,
      so T2's deliberately-excluded phrase necessarily echoes into it. Asserting exactly one
      match is strictly stronger than a bare exclusion: it also proves the phrase was carried
      through rather than silently dropped.
- [ ] Verified BEFORE the routing edit is made: `rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity`
      no longer returns a blocking `stale-regver` verdict on the branch point (i.e. ticket
      `1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` has merged), asserted by a check against the current checkout rather
      than assumed.
- [ ] A test proves `registry_version(None)` computed from the PRE-edit routing content differs
      from `registry_version(None)` computed after the edit — capturing both values at run time,
      asserting inequality, and hard-coding neither.
- [ ] `grep -n "success criteria" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` still returns its
      one match, proving the deliberately excluded pilot-metrics phrase was left intact.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Rename Success Criteria to Acceptance Criteria in reviewer prompts and criteria routing

baseline.description:
## Context
Follow-up to winning-endurant-xenops. Before the fold defer-guard lands, any fold that crossed an un-cited pre-snapshot orphan LAUNDERED it: the event file was retired and its uuid cited in source_event_uuids without its effect entering the compiled state. fsck reports clean on such tickets. The data is NOT lost — retired files are preserved and rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log replays the full log including .retired — but there is no DETECTION: finding historical laundering requires comparing each ticket's snapshot-compiled state against a full-log replay (expensive, so an opt-in deep check, e.g. fsck --deep or --verify-snapshots).
## Proposed direction
Opt-in fsck deep verification: for each ticket with a snapshot, replay full log (incl .retired) and diff against snapshot-compiled state; mismatch => LAUNDERED_SNAPSHOT finding routed to the existing rebuild door. Known live incidents: one (e27c orphan, healed pre-fold) — historical damage believed bounded.
## Out of scope
The forward-path defer guard (xenops).
baseline.summary: fsck deep check: detect historically laundered snapshots (cited-but-effect-missing)

## Context / Problem
`AGENTS.md` says launch-loaded guidance must stay lean and point to maintained documentation, but its background-process section embeds a dated incident narrative, operator recovery procedure, and detector explanation. Every agent pays that context cost even when it only needs the prevention contract.

## Approach
- Replace the long `AGENTS.md` section with a compact prevention contract retaining the safety invariants, bounded-spawn and process-group cleanup example, bounded-LLM-gate exemption, and a detailed-documentation pointer.
- Move incident evidence, detector interpretation, and operator recovery into `docs/orphaned-processes.md`; index it from `docs/README.md`.
- Update both the module docstring and runtime report in `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` to name `docs/orphaned-processes.md`.
- Assert that flagged-process runtime output contains `docs/orphaned-processes.md`.
- Preserve the commands and facts needed to prevent, detect, and reclaim orphaned processes.

## Scope
- `AGENTS.md`: compress the launch-loaded background-process rule.
- `docs/orphaned-processes.md`: own incident evidence, prevention rationale, detector interpretation, and operator recovery.
- `docs/README.md`: index the operations page.
- `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py`: replace both stale `AGENTS.md` recovery pointers.
- `tests/scripts/test_check_orphaned_load.py`: protect the runtime runbook reference.

## Testing
- Run `python scripts/check_docs_index.py`.
- Run focused documentation and orphan-detector tests.
- Run `make lint` with the worktree virtualenv first on PATH.
- Verify every moved invariant, command, and runbook reference remains reachable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The `AGENTS.md` background-process section contains no more than 35 physical source lines.
- [x] The compact section includes a wall-clock-bounded spawn plus process-group cleanup example.
- [x] The compact section states that no spawned process may reach PPID 1 and that each subagent must reap its own helpers.
- [x] The compact section prohibits unbounded busy loops without a wall-clock bound.
- [x] The compact section explicitly forbids applying timeouts to bounded LLM gate operations.
- [x] Dated incident evidence is absent from `AGENTS.md` and present in `docs/orphaned-processes.md`.
- [x] Orphan-detector interpretation and operator reclamation steps are absent from `AGENTS.md` and present in `docs/orphaned-processes.md`.
- [x] The Operations section of `docs/README.md` links `orphaned-processes.md` as the prevention, detection, and recovery procedure.
- [x] The detailed page documents bounded spawn, process-group cleanup, read-only detection, and confirmed reclamation commands.
- [x] Both recovery pointers in `scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` name `docs/orphaned-processes.md`.
- [x] A regression test proves flagged-process runtime output contains `docs/orphaned-processes.md`.
- [x] Documentation checks and focused tests pass.
- [x] `make lint` passes with the worktree virtualenv first on PATH.
- [x] [non-codebase] Gerrit reports `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved comments.
- [x] [non-codebase] The change is submitted to `main`.

## Verification
Count physical source lines from the background-process H2 heading through the line before the next H2; search for every preserved invariant, command, and runbook reference; run focused tests and lint; then confirm Gerrit labels and merged status before closing the ticket.
baseline.summary: Move orphan-process incident detail out of AGENTS.md

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The S3 ticket-store backend (parent epic) relies on the `awslabs/git-remote-s3` remote helper, which must be an **optional** dependency: core rebar stays lean (only pyyaml, jsonschema, referencing are hard deps — see `pyproject.toml` `[project.optional-dependencies]` and `src/rebar/_optional.py`), and only operators using S3 install it. The version matters: the multiple-bundles corruption the epic must prevent is *created* by a client without the `IfNoneMatch` per-ref lock; a live experiment this session verified `git-remote-s3` **0.3.2** carries that lock (its `acquire_lock` uses `IfNoneMatch="*"` with a TTL steal). So we need a declared extra AND a runtime probe that other children can call to prove the helper is present and new enough.

This story delivers only the **dependency plumbing and a pure availability guard** — no behavior is wired into init/push here (the preflight-enforcement child does that).

## Approach

Follow the existing optional-extra pattern exactly (verified against `src/rebar/_optional.py`: `EXTRAS` at line ~40, `_install_hint` at line 54 which emits `pip install 'nava-rebar[<extra>]'`, `guard_import(module, *, extra=...)` at line 83 which imports `module`):

1. In `pyproject.toml` `[project.optional-dependencies]`, add `s3 = ["git-remote-s3>=0.3.2"]`
   with a comment (mirroring the `mcp`/`agents` entries) noting it ships the remote helper
   and is never required by core rebar.
2. In `src/rebar/_optional.py`, add an `EXTRAS` entry
   `"s3": ("git_remote_s3", "<blurb>")`. The `git-remote-s3` distribution installs an
   **importable** package named `git_remote_s3` (the console script `git-remote-s3` is its
   entry point), so the existing import-based probe (`find_spec`/`extra_installed`) detects it
   correctly; rebar never calls the package's API, it only probes presence. A missing install
   therefore produces the standard one-line message
   `install it with:  pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'` via `_install_hint`/`guard_import`.
3. Add `require_s3_helper()` to `src/rebar/_optional.py` with a module-level
   `MIN_GIT_REMOTE_S3 = "0.3.2"`. It fails closed (raising `OptionalDependencyError` carrying
   the `_install_hint("s3")` string) unless BOTH hold:
   - the console script git invokes is on `PATH`: `shutil.which("git-remote-s3") is not None`
     (this is what git actually execs as the remote helper); and
   - the installed distribution meets the minimum: read
     `importlib.metadata.version("git-remote-s3")`, catching `PackageNotFoundError` and
     treating it as "not installed" (route to the same actionable error). Compare with a
     stdlib-only parser — split the version on `.`, take the leading run of digits of each of
     the first three components as ints, and compare that tuple to `(0, 3, 2)`. A version
     string whose leading component is non-numeric/unparseable is treated as **not** meeting
     the minimum (fail closed) rather than silently passing. `_optional.py` stays stdlib-only
     (no `packaging`, no import of `git_remote_s3`).

Rationale: reusing `_optional.py`'s single-chokepoint pattern keeps the "missing extra" experience consistent with every other rebar extra and keeps `import rebar` dependency-free, while a standalone `require_s3_helper()` gives the preflight and doctor children one tested seam to call rather than each re-implementing detection; checking both the `PATH` console script and the distribution version closes the gap where one is present without the other.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — add the `s3` optional-dependency entry.
- `src/rebar/_optional.py` — add the `s3` `EXTRAS` probe, `MIN_GIT_REMOTE_S3`, the
  stdlib-only version comparison, and `require_s3_helper()`.
- `tests/unit/test_s3_optional_guard.py` — new unit tests for `require_s3_helper()`.

No changes to store, config schema, or CLI behavior in this story.

## Testing

Tier: **pure-function / validation unit tests** (no git, no network — the guard is a PATH+version check; monkeypatch `shutil.which` and `importlib.metadata.version`). Oracles:
- Happy: `shutil.which` returns a path and `version(...)` returns `"0.3.2"` →
  `require_s3_helper()` returns success.
- Failure (script missing): `shutil.which` returns `None` → raises `OptionalDependencyError`
  whose message contains the exact string `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`.
- Failure (dist metadata missing): `version(...)` raises `PackageNotFoundError` → raises the
  same actionable error.
- Edge (too old): `version(...)` returns `"0.2.9"` → raises an error naming the `>=0.3.2`
  minimum.
- Edge (newer / suffixed): `version(...)` returns `"0.4.0"` → success; `"0.3.2.post1"` →
  success (leading numeric components parse to `(0,3,2)`).
- Edge (unparseable): `version(...)` returns `"unknown"` → fails closed (does not pass).
- `guard_import("git_remote_s3", extra="s3")` with the module absent → message contains
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pyproject.toml` declares `s3 = ["git-remote-s3>=0.3.2"]` under
      `[project.optional-dependencies]`; `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'` resolves the helper.
      Verified by a metadata check that the extra is listed.
- [x] `src/rebar/_optional.py` exposes `require_s3_helper()` and a `"s3"` `EXTRAS` probe;
      a missing install yields the standard one-line message containing the exact string
      `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`. Verified by the guard_import unit-test oracle.
- [x] `require_s3_helper()` returns success only when the `git-remote-s3` console script is on
      `PATH` and the distribution is `>=0.3.2`; it raises `OptionalDependencyError` (naming the
      `0.3.2` minimum and the install string) when the script is absent, the dist metadata is
      missing (`PackageNotFoundError`), the version is older, or the version is unparseable.
      Verified by the seven unit-test oracles above.
- [x] `_optional.py` remains stdlib-only (no `packaging`, no import of `git_remote_s3`).
      Verified by inspection and the module importing in a lean install.
baseline.summary: Declare the optional [s3] extra and a git-remote-s3 availability/version guard

baseline.description:
## Context

Discovered while adding the compact-worker leg to doctor's lock census (ticket bemused-painted-worm / 8a0d-96ca-a60e-4da6, merged as 8874ec98c7c). Snapshot GC's operation-linked trigger (a3da2f4cce) added a stamped worker lock at `<snapshot-store>/gc/worker.lock` (`rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger._WORKER_LOCK_NAME`), the same detached-background-worker shape as `.rebar/compact-worker.lock` — a lock most likely to be held by a process an operator cannot find with `ps`. `doctor_locks.scan_locks` censuses only tracker-adjacent locks, so a snapshot-GC worker that died between acquire and release leaves a stamped lock the one diagnostic built to answer "who holds what" cannot see.

## Decision

ADD the leg. The two design questions the ticket raised resolve cleanly:

1. **Staleness discipline IS the shared table.** `gc_trigger._acquire_worker_lock` uses
   `rebar._store.stamped_lock.stamped_file_lock` (the consolidation from story
   1cf6-f902-5bfa-438f), which writes the same v2 ownership stamp as the drain and
   compact-worker locks and adjudicates reclaim via
   `rebar._store.lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale`. So doctor's existing
   `_existence_report` — which decodes the v2 stamp and asks that same shared table — is
   exactly the right reader, no new staleness heuristic.
2. **Root derivation must be READ-ONLY.** The lock lives on the per-host snapshot store
   (`rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.store_root()`, `$REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` or
   `tempfile.gettempdir()`, dir `rebar-gate-snapshots`), NOT the tracker's `.rebar/`. But
   `store_root()` mkdirs+chmods the root and `gc_trigger._gc_dir` mkdirs `<store>/gc/` as
   side effects — a diagnostic pass must not create directories (the census's existing
   read-only guarantee: probing must never create what it probes). So the leg needs a
   non-creating derivation seam, added where each layer already owns its layout.

A store that does not exist yet reports the leg `free` — for an existence lock the file IS the lock, so an absent store trivially holds nothing; this matches how the drain and compact-worker legs report an absent lock file, and the row's note says the store may not exist yet.

## Approach

1. `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`: add `peek_store_root() -> Path` — the same
   base-resolution as `store_root()` (`config.resolve_gate_tmpdir()` or
   `tempfile.gettempdir()`, joined with `_STORE_DIRNAME`) WITHOUT mkdir/chmod; refactor
   `store_root()` to call it then create (behavior preserved).
2. `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py`: hoist the `"gc"` dirname into a `_GC_DIRNAME`
   constant used by `_gc_dir`, and add `worker_lock_probe_path() -> Path` returning
   `peek_store_root() / _GC_DIRNAME / _WORKER_LOCK_NAME` with no directory creation —
   gc_trigger owns the sidecar layout, so doctor does not re-derive it.
3. `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py`: add `LEG_SNAPSHOT_GC_WORKER = "snapshot-gc-worker"`
   as a sixth leg in `scan_locks`, built by the existing `_existence_report` on
   `worker_lock_probe_path()` (module imported lazily inside the leg lambda's scope so the
   census does not import the snapshot subsystem at module import). Note text: "no detached
   snapshot-GC worker holds the snapshot store's worker lock (per-host store; may not exist
   yet)". Update the module docstring: five → six legs, and a paragraph on the snapshot leg's
   DIFFERENT root (per-host store, not the tracker), same stamped shape/shared table.
   `scan_locks(tracker)` keeps its signature; the new leg is per-host and ignores the tracker
   argument — the docstring says so.
4. `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json`: add `"snapshot-gc-worker"` to the leg-name enum.
5. `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py`:
   - an autouse fixture pinning `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` to a per-test tmp dir, so the census's
     new host-global leg cannot leak REAL host state into any test in the module (the
     free-store census test and both doctor integration tests assert exact finding sets).
   - update `test_a_free_store_reports_every_leg_and_no_finding` to six legs; assert the
     snapshot leg is `free` with `holder is None` when the store does not exist, and that
     scanning did NOT create the store directory (the read-only guarantee for the new
     derivation).
   - `_plant_snapshot_gc_lock` helper writing a v2 stamp at
     `repo_snapshot.peek_store_root() / "gc" / "worker.lock"` (under the pinned tmp base);
     mirror the compact-worker tests: live holder → held/info, dead holder → stale finding
     via `lock_findings`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The snapshot-GC worker lock joins `rebar doctor`'s census as leg
      `snapshot-gc-worker`, derived from the per-host snapshot-store root without creating
      any directory.
- [x] The leg reports held-for / holder / staleness like the other stamped legs, with tests
      for held (live + dead holder) and free/absent store.
- [x] The dead-holder case is a stale-lock finding; a live holder is information; an absent
      store (or free lock) is no finding, and the doctor JSON schema admits the new leg name.

## Verify
- pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py tests/unit/test_snapshot_gc_trigger.py tests/unit/snapshot/test_repo_snapshot.py -x -q  (repo_snapshot tests live where they live; adjust path if the module sits directly under tests/unit)
- make lint; make typecheck; python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check
baseline.summary: doctor lock census has no snapshot-GC worker-lock leg

baseline.description:
Remove the refs that pin pre-rewrite history, and take a backup that lives outside the repo. Without this the reclaim lands at **167 MB instead of ~94 MiB**. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Measured: remote tag `pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` (`2a77dd48`) is an ancestor of `origin/tickets` and pins **22,317 commits / 63,202,159 bytes** of `.bridge_state`. A full clone fetches tags, so leaving it defeats most of the reclaim. It is absent from Gerrit and replication is `mirror = false`, so deletion sticks and will not be recreated. Also delete the host-local `pre-a3-remediation` tag (`0adbd40a`, ~64.8 MB reachable).

An **in-repo** archive branch or tag reclaims nothing — reachable objects are served and repacked forever (crates.io's receipts: 1.73 GB live index vs **6.94 GB** archive repo). So the backup must leave the repository: `git bundle create` from an **unfiltered** clone, stored off-repo, including the tag tips being deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `git ls-remote --heads --tags origin` (de-peeling `^{}` entries) is enumerated at run time and
      every ref whose ancestry intersects the old tip is listed. Do **not** hardcode a count — today
      it is 13 heads + 16 distinct tags. Tier: **repo-level script**.

baseline.description:
# An issue link DELETED in Jira is never removed from the local ticket (inbound)

Found while writing the row-11 inbound cell of the J11 mutation table (story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae), filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a product defect stops and reports. THIS TICKET NOW CARRIES THE FIX (reparented under epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling).

## Mechanism

The inbound link differ is ADD-ONLY, by construction and by its own docstring. `inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound` opens with "Reflect Jira issuelinks into rebar relations. ADD-only." and closes with "ADD-only (no REMOVE mutations)" (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py:380 and :396). It iterates the CURRENT `fields.issuelinks` and emits an add per unseen link; nothing walks the local deps looking for one whose Jira counterpart has gone.

So the flow is asymmetric: the OUTBOUND direction does have a removal path (`outbound_links._diff_link_removals`, which emits `{"action": "remove", "type":..., "to_key":..., "relation":...}`, outbound_links.py:120-175, applied via `delete_issue_link`), while the inbound direction has no counterpart. A link a human deletes in Jira stays on the rebar ticket forever, and no pass ever reports it.

## Why this is a gap and not merely a documented design choice

Story 5200's acceptance criteria define a 14-row mutation table with an explicit oracle per direction. Row 11's INBOUND oracle is "that link is ABSENT" from the local ticket. That row cannot pass while the differ is add-only, so the epic's comprehensiveness claim is not reachable without either implementing the removal or amending the AC. This ticket IMPLEMENTS THE REMOVAL; the Approach below resolves the evidence question (how we know the peer deleted a link rather than that we failed to observe it), which is the part that made this more than a guard removal.

Note the add-only choice is not obviously safe either: the same docstring's idempotency logic already skips an emit when "the counterpart is absent from the ACTIVE local set", i.e. the differ is willing to reason about absence — just not about the absence of the LINK.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` asserts the local dep is gone after the Jira link is deleted. It should go RED on the harness until this is addressed.

## Approach

Mirror the outbound removal path, but gate it — an inbound removal is a WRITE that destroys local data, so the whole design problem is establishing that the peer really DELETED the link rather than that we merely failed to see it.

1. **A new `_diff_link_removals_inbound` in `inbound_differ.py`**, the mirror of
   `outbound_links._diff_link_removals` (outbound_links.py:120-175). It walks the local `deps` and
   emits `{"action": "remove", "target_id": <local id>, "relation": <local relation>}` — inbound
   records carry `target_id` (a local id), not `to_key`. Build the OBSERVED peer link set through
   `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link`, NOT from raw Jira keys, so both sides are compared in local
   relation vocabulary; comparing raw keys makes an `inwardIssue`/`Blocks` link read as `depends_on`
   while the local dep is `blocks`, producing a spurious removal of a link that is still there.

2. **`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` must branch on `action`.** It currently reads
   `if entry.get("action") != "add": continue` (apply_inbound_records.py:560-562) and only ever calls
   `rebar.link`, so a removal record is silently discarded — a differ-only fix would ship the exact
   silent-failure class this epic exists to end. Removal applies via `rebar.unlink`.

### The five guards, and why each is load-bearing

- **G1 OBSERVED.** Emit only when `"issuelinks" in jira_fields` — key PRESENT, empty list allowed.
  `fetcher.py:592-596` sets that key only for entries `get_issuelinks_map` returned a list for, and the
  base search omits issuelinks entirely (bug 3f04), so key-presence is a reliable "enrichment reached
  this issue" marker. Both readers make an empty list authoritative rather than dropping the key
  (Cloud `acli_graph.get_issuelinks_map` records `result[key] = links` for any list "including the
  empty list — an authoritative 'no links'"; DC `transport.py:391-394` builds `{key: list(... or [])}`).
  `_snapshot_schema.py` is `total=False` and never injects `[]`. So key-absent covers exactly the
  unsafe cases — enrichment failed, HTTP 410, a fail-open partial map, the issue fell outside a
  truncated page, a cross-project bound issue, or a client with no `get_issuelinks_map` — and every one
  of those fails safe to NO REMOVAL.
  **`_diff_links_inbound:397` opens `jira_fields.get("issuelinks") or []`, which collapses
  observed-empty into unobserved. That line must NOT be reused on the removal path.**
- **G2 TARGET BOUND.** Require `binding_store.get_jira_key(target_id)` non-None. An unbound target
  could never have had a Jira link, so its absence proves nothing.
- **G3 MANAGED.** `should_propagate_removal(relation, target_id, local_ticket)` from
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs` — the same predicate the outbound parent/link gates consume, so a
  peer-created dep rebar never owned is not clobbered. It also excludes
  `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`discovered_from` for free, because `MANAGED_REF_KINDS` omits relations
  with no reliable peer link type; do NOT add a redundant filter for them.
- **G4 ARBITRATION — REWRITTEN AFTER THE LIVE ORACLE REFUTED THE FIRST VERSION. READ THIS CAREFULLY.**
  The FIRST version of this guard said: "never mirror a removal for a target the outbound side is adding
  this pass", on the reasoning that an outbound ADD means "being pushed" rather than "peer deleted it".
  **That reasoning is WRONG, and its failure is total.** When the peer deletes a link, the local dep still
  exists and the peer lacks it — which is EXACTLY the condition under which the outbound differ emits a
  link ADD. So on any bidirectional pass a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that target,
  and the guard therefore always suppressed the inbound REMOVE: **the feature could never fire.** Proven by
  harness run 30784592232 against main @ `de2f1ed87` (which CONTAINS change 1276):
  `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` stayed RED with "the Jira link was DELETED … but the local dep …
  still targets 'jira-rbjflfv-2'". The mutation ledger was green throughout, because
  `test_g4_outbound_add_this_pass_suppresses_the_removal` asserted the behaviour the plan specified — **a
  mutation ledger cannot catch a wrong SPECIFICATION.**

  **THE CORRECTED RULE: `managed_refs` decides PRECEDENCE between the two directions. It is not a second
  AND-gate beside G3.** The two differs disagree about one fact — local dep present, peer link absent — and
  exactly one must win:
    * ref **IS managed** (rebar pushed it at some point) + peer lacks it → **the peer DELETED it** → the
      inbound REMOVE wins, **and the outbound ADD for that pair must be suppressed.**
    * ref is **NOT managed** (never pushed) + peer lacks it → **we simply have not pushed it yet** → the
      outbound ADD wins and the inbound REMOVE is suppressed. This is the ONLY case the old G4 should have
      covered.
  Suppressing only the inbound side is NOT sufficient and must not be shipped: both differs run against
  the same pre-pass snapshot and then both apply, so inbound unlinking locally while outbound re-adds in
  Jira leaves the pass DIVERGENT and the next pass re-adopts the link inbound — churn, not convergence.
  **So `outbound_links.py` (or the shared suppression context) is in scope: this is arbitration across BOTH
  differs.**
  An outbound REMOVE for the same pair still suppresses the inbound removal (the two directions must not
  both act on one pair in a pass; deferring re-evaluates next pass rather than double-removing).
- **G5 RELATION MATCH AT APPLY.** `rebar.unlink(id1, id2, *, repo_root=None)` takes NO relation
  argument, and that is deliberate — `_commands/unlink.py`'s usage text says "pair-scoped, NO relation
  arg; removes the most-recent link between the pair", and `_get_link_info` returns the most recent
  net-active link. So if a pair holds two active relations and the peer dropped only one, a naive
  unlink can remove THE WRONG ONE — a link the peer still has. The apply step must confirm the pair's
  net-active relation MATCHES the vanished relation, and skip + log otherwise.

### G3's blind spot, stated plainly rather than papered over

`add_managed_ref` is folded by the **LINK-event** processor (`reducer/_processors.py:411`), so a ref becomes "managed" the instant it is created LOCALLY — it does NOT mean "we pushed it to the peer". `seed_managed_refs_from_current` compounds this for pre-feature tickets by seeding all current `deps` as managed. So G3 alone does not establish that the peer ever had the link. **Under the CORRECTED arbitration rule above, that is handled by precedence rather than by a second gate:** an UNMANAGED dep is never removed (the outbound ADD wins), so a brand-new local dep is safe by construction. What remains is the narrower case where `managed_refs` says managed but the ref was never actually pushed — chiefly `seed_managed_refs_from_current`, which marks a PRE-FEATURE ticket's CURRENT deps as managed. On such a ticket a never-pushed dep could be read as "the peer deleted it" and removed locally. That window is real and is recorded here deliberately; it is far narrower than the behaviour it replaces, which was that the feature never fired at all.

**The earlier text here claimed "G4 closes that in a healthy pass, because outbound emits a link ADD for exactly that dep and the suppression drops the removal." That sentence was the error** — it is precisely why the first implementation could never work, and it is retained in this form only so the mistake is legible rather than quietly overwritten.

**Alternative rejected: compare against the previous peer link set** (link present in the prior Jira snapshot, absent now = a real remote deletion). This is the textbook-correct signal and would retire G3's blind spot outright, but it is NOT available: as of `6cdd4b00d9` ("Narrow persisted Jira snapshot to key membership") `reconcile._write_prev_snapshot_key_set` persists `{jira_key: {}}` — key membership only, carrying no fields and therefore no issuelinks. Reaching for it means adding a new persisted artifact with its own migration and its own truncation semantics, which is a materially larger change than this defect warrants. Recorded so a future reader knows it was considered and why it was declined.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — the removal differ + G1/G2/G3, and making
  G4 deliberate. 718/800 LOC today; a ~50-line mirror lands ~770. If it would breach 800, shed weight
  into `link_direction.py` (59 LOC, already imported by both directions), never mechanically.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — action branch + `rebar.unlink` + G5.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py` (or the shared same-pass suppression context) —
  **ADDED after the live refutation:** the managed case must also suppress the OUTBOUND link ADD, or the
  pass ends divergent and churns. This is the arbitration half the original plan did not contemplate.
  579/800 LOC.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py` — OPTIONAL, only to add a `should_mirror_peer_removal` sibling
  sharing the `managed_ref_set()` read path. Mechanically the identical predicate, so it buys naming
  and a place to document that inbound needs more than the managed check. Skip it if the guards read
  clearly without it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** any fetcher or adapter change (the observed/unobserved distinction already
  survives); `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`, which another ticket owns.

## Acceptance criteria

**AMENDED after an operator ruling — see the AC AMENDMENT comment on this ticket for the full reasoning and the ecosystem research with sources.** The ruling was: research the ecosystem, build if it is a parity gap, defer if it is not commonly handled. It is NOT commonly handled (Aha! refuses deletion propagation outright citing inadvertent-data-loss risk; Asana<->Jira and Workfront<->Jira leave the far item in place; Exalate makes link sync opt-in scripted config), and it is NOT a Cloud/DC parity gap (shared core; Cloud never mirrored a peer deletion and has no equivalent cell). So removal-mirroring is DEFERRED and the criteria written around "the removal IS emitted" no longer describe what this ticket ships.

The original criteria are preserved verbatim below under RETIRED rather than deleted, so the decision is auditable.

### What this ticket actually shipped — the criteria that stand

- [x] the apply-layer DROP is fixed. `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` used to
      discard any non-`add` link record outright (`action != "add": continue`), so even a correct
      differ could not have worked. That branch + the `rebar.unlink` wiring landed in change 1276
      and is independently mutation-proven. This was a REAL defect and it is fixed
- [x] G1/G2/G3/G5 landed and are mutation-proven. They are dormant (nothing emits a removal for
      them to gate) but they are correct, and they are the guards a future implementation needs
- [x] the shipped semantics are STATED: local-wins-and-restore. A link deleted in Jira is re-added
      on the next pass — convergent, no local data destroyed, identical on both backends
- [x] the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is XFAIL with the full reason in the
      marker, `strict=False` so it fails LOUDLY as an xpass the moment a removal path starts
      working — NOT inverted and NOT deleted. Gerrit change 1303, MERGED as 29f9627128; verified on
      main: reason text present, strict=False, cell body unmodified
- [x] the ecosystem evidence is recorded, with sources, so this is not re-litigated from scratch
- [x] the refutation of the original design is recorded, with a probe — `managed_refs` cannot
      distinguish "a link we never pushed" from "a link the peer deleted"; the two states are
      IDENTICAL on every input the guards read. That finding stopped a second data-loss defect
      before it was written
- [x] the correct design is recorded WITH A WORKING TEMPLATE — change 1296 landed exactly this
      pattern for parents (a per-binding record of what the peer last had, advanced only on
      OBSERVATION), so whoever picks this up starts from shipped, reviewed code rather than from
      the refuted premise. `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs
- [x] `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap

### RETIRED — specify a feature deliberately NOT shipped

Recorded, not silently dropped. Every item below described emitting or gating a link REMOVAL, which this ticket no longer ships. The live cell still EXISTS and still RUNS (as an xfail); what changed is the product decision about what behaviour to ship, taken on ecosystem evidence plus a first-hand incident in which the identical inference destroyed 63 parent edges.

- ~~RETIRED~~ a link deleted in Jira is mirrored locally: the local dep is asserted POSITIVELY ABSENT after
      the pass, never "no exception was raised"
- ~~RETIRED~~ the removal record survives the apply layer end to end — differ emit → `run_differs` payload →
      `apply_inbound` → `rebar.unlink` → the dep is gone from the reduced ticket. A test that stops at
      the differ boundary does NOT satisfy this, because the record was silently dropped at
      `apply_inbound_records.py:560-562` and a differ-only oracle goes green while the store is untouched
- ~~RETIRED~~ G1: with the issue's `issuelinks` key ABSENT (unobserved — simulate the real truncation/fail-open
      shape, not a hand-deleted key if the real path differs), NO removal is emitted
- ~~RETIRED~~ G1: with `issuelinks` present and EMPTY (authoritative "no links"), the removal IS emitted
- ~~RETIRED~~ G2: an unbound target emits no removal
- ~~RETIRED~~ G3: a dep that is not in `managed_refs` emits no removal, so a peer-created dep is never clobbered
- ~~RETIRED~~ G4 arbitration, MANAGED case: a MANAGED dep whose peer link is gone emits the removal **even
      though the outbound side is adding that target this pass**, and the outbound ADD for that pair is
      SUPPRESSED. Assert BOTH halves — inbound removal present AND outbound add absent — because
      suppressing only one leaves the pass divergent and churning
- ~~RETIRED~~ G4 arbitration, UNMANAGED case: an UNMANAGED dep whose peer link is absent emits NO removal and the
      outbound ADD proceeds, asserted against `link_add_keys`
- ~~RETIRED~~ a test pins that the two arbitration branches are decided by `managed_refs` and NOT by the mere
      presence of an outbound add — i.e. flipping only the managed-ness of the ref flips which direction
      wins. This is the assertion whose absence let the first version ship broken
- ~~RETIRED~~ the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is GREEN on a harness run, and the run id is
      recorded here. **A green unit suite is explicitly NOT sufficient for this ticket** — the first
      version had a fully green, mutation-checked unit suite and did not work at all
- ~~RETIRED~~ G5: when the pair's net-active relation differs from the vanished relation, no unlink is
      performed and the skip is logged
- ~~RETIRED~~ steady state does not churn: a managed dep still present on the peer emits NO removal on
      repeated passes
- ~~RETIRED~~ every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the removal unconditional — a fix that emits removals with no guard passes
      the happy-path oracle while being a data-loss bug, so the guard oracles are the ones that
      actually protect the product
- ~~RETIRED~~ `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is
      unmodified, and turns GREEN on the harness once this lands
- ~~RETIRED~~ `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap
baseline.summary: Inbound link removal is never mirrored (inbound link differ is ADD-only)

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

## Problem

The `rebar-implement` skill (examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md) carries a "Model tiering" section that pins the implementer subagent to strong/standard/cheap model tiers to save tokens. This model-level gradient adds complexity (a tier table, per-dispatch tier-naming rules, a dedicated 4e-bis "Tier escalation" ladder, per-leaf tiering session-log requirements) for savings that only materialize on wide epics. We are removing it.

Separately, Phase 0's preflight hard-stops on any ticket with no children. That is too strict: a `story`/`task` with no children but a recorded file impact is already an executable code leaf — the file impact is exactly the acceptance the completion-verifier close gate needs. The skill should execute such a ticket as a single leaf instead of refusing it.

## Plan

1. Remove the model-level gradient: delete the "## Model tiering" section; strip tiering language
   from Phase 3 (non-code leaf), 4a, and 4d while PRESERVING the held-out discipline (the
   implementer stays a separate subagent, which never depended on tiering); rewrite 4e-bis from
   "Tier escalation" to a tier-free "Escalation — when re-dispatch isn't enough"; reground the
   Phase 5 residual-sweep example.
2. Allow a childless story/task with a recorded file impact to run as a single leaf: Phase 0
   recognizes two executable shapes (has children -> tree; childless story/task with non-empty
   `rebar get-file-impact` -> single leaf) and stops only when neither holds; add a Phase 2
   callout collapsing Phases 3/5/6 to one change; update the frontmatter description, Phase 0
   heading, and Reporting stop line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] No "Model tiering" section and no strong/standard/cheap model-tier references remain in
      SKILL.md. Proof: `! grep -niE 'model tiering|cheap.?tier|standard.?tier|strong.?tier' examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`
- [x] The held-out separation (a separate implementer subagent) is still stated in Phase 4.
      Proof: `grep -n 'separate' examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`
- [x] Phase 0 documents executing a childless story/task with a recorded file impact as a single
      code leaf, keyed on `rebar get-file-impact`. Proof:
      `grep -n 'get-file-impact' examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`
- [x] Frontmatter description, Phase 0 heading, Phase 2, and Reporting are consistent with both
      changes (checked: manual read of the four sections).

## Testing

Docs-only change to a Markdown skill file; no source code changes, so the CI `Verified` gate (`make lint && make typecheck && make test`) is unaffected and passes unchanged. Verify the acceptance criteria with the grep commands listed above, run from the worktree root.
