## Context / Problem
The MCP `review_plan` tool (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) derives whether it signs a plan-review attestation SOLELY from server read-only mode: it calls the library with `sign=not ro, emit_sidecar=not ro`. There is no caller-facing `sign` parameter, so an MCP client cannot request an explicit unsigned review the way a CLI caller can with `--no-sign` or a library caller can with `sign=False`. Conversely, when read-only mode DOES suppress signing, the returned verdict carries no machine-readable reason saying so — a client sees an unsigned PASS and cannot distinguish "policy suppressed the signature" from "signing failed".

Split out of epic 58f2-b6ed-363e-4608 (uninformed-aspiring-rhino) on 2026-07-24: the CLI and library boundaries of that epic are a test/help-hardening job, while this is a genuine public API change to a different boundary with tool-schema and generated-reference consequences.

## Expected Behavior
- MCP `review_plan` accepts `sign: bool = True`, matching the library default.
- An explicit `sign=False` runs the review without signing, and the result names the caller's
  opt-out as the unsigned reason.
- Read-only server mode continues to suppress signing regardless of the requested value, and
  the result carries a machine-readable unsigned reason identifying the read-only policy
  (distinct from the caller-opt-out reason and from a signing failure).
- The tool docstring states the sign-by-default contract and both unsigned exceptions.

## Approach
1. Add `sign: bool = True` to the MCP `review_plan` signature; pass `sign=sign and not ro`.
2. Introduce a machine-readable unsigned-reason field on the verdict distinguishing:
   `caller-opt-out`, `readonly-policy`, `not-signable` (BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/degraded/local),
   and `sign-failed`. Reuse the existing `signature.signed` boolean as the primary contract;
   the reason is additive, so existing consumers stay byte-compatible.
3. Update the tool docstring and regenerate `docs/mcp-reference.md`.

Rejected: inferring the reason client-side from the verdict shape — the read-only and not-signable cases are indistinguishable without server knowledge, which is the bug.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (unsigned-reason plumbing, if the reason is
  produced at the finalization seam rather than the MCP boundary)
- MCP surface tests for plan review
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` (generated tool inventory / outputSchema)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] MCP `review_plan` exposes `sign: bool = True`; a contract test proves the default
      persists an attestation and `sign=False` does not.
- [ ] With `sign=False`, the result carries a machine-readable unsigned reason identifying the
      caller opt-out; a test asserts the exact reason value.
- [ ] In read-only mode the result is unsigned regardless of the requested `sign` value and
      carries the read-only-policy reason, distinct from the caller-opt-out reason; a
      table-driven test covers (sign x readonly) combinations.
- [ ] A never-signable verdict (BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / degraded / local source) reports the
      not-signable reason rather than the opt-out or read-only reason.
- [ ] The MCP tool docstring states sign-by-default and names both unsigned exceptions;
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` regenerates cleanly and matches.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: MCP review_plan has no caller-facing sign opt-out and no machine-readable unsigned reason

## Context / Problem

`.provision.log` is written into a worktree when its venv is provisioned, but it is not listed in `.gitignore`. Because it is untracked-and-not-ignored, `git status --porcelain` is non-empty for the life of the worktree.

That is not merely cosmetic. The machine-local worktree GC (`com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc`) refuses to reclaim any worktree whose status is non-empty — the "no uncommitted work" safety guard. A provisioning artifact therefore pins a worktree permanently: it can never age out, and no amount of idleness makes it collectable. A 2026-08-06 audit of this checkout found 6 worktrees whose ONLY untracked file was `.provision.log`, plus the same guard firing on in-scope agent worktrees (`KEEP agent-a1bf191c510431899: dirty`).

The file is pure build/provisioning noise: it records the output of venv creation and the editable install. Nothing reads it after provisioning, and it is never intended to be committed.

## Approach

Add `.provision.log` to `.gitignore`, next to the other provisioning/rebuild noise entries (`.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`) so it sits with the artifacts it belongs to rather than at the end of the file.

An unanchored `.provision.log` pattern is deliberate: the file is written at whatever directory the provisioner runs in, so matching it at any depth is the intended behavior, consistent with how `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` are already written in this file.

This is a one-line mechanical change to a config file. It does not alter any Python source, any CLI behavior, or any gate.

## Scope

- `.gitignore` — add one entry.

No other file changes. No `src/rebar` change, so no test-file change is implied.

## Testing

No new testable behavior is added: `.gitignore` is consumed by git itself, not by any rebar code path, and no test imports or executes it. Verification is therefore direct observation of git's own behavior plus the repo's existing gates:

- `git check-ignore -v .provision.log` exits 0 and names the new `.gitignore` line
  (before the change it exits 1).
- With a `.provision.log` present in a clean worktree, `git status --porcelain` is empty
  (before the change it reports `?? .provision.log`).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass (enforced by the pre-commit hook).
- CI's `Verified` label on the Gerrit change is `+1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `.gitignore` contains a `.provision.log` entry; checked by
      `grep -c '^\.provision\.log$' .gitignore` returning 1.
- [x] `git check-ignore -v .provision.log` exits 0 and attributes the match to
      `.gitignore`.
- [x] In a clean checkout with a `.provision.log` file created, `git status --porcelain`
      produces no output.
- [x] No file other than `.gitignore` is modified by the change; checked by
      `git show --name-only` listing exactly that one path.
- [x] The change reaches `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on Gerrit and is submitted to
      `main`.
baseline.summary: gitignore: ignore .provision.log so a provisioning artifact cannot pin a worktree

baseline.description:
# Persist ticket digest as a REVIEW_RESULT-style sidecar (shared cache)

## Why
The digest is a billable LLM artifact we never want to recompute (~$1.90 to enrich the whole 793-ticket store — see epic experiment comment). Storing it in the SHARED store (auto-pushed) makes one client's enrichment a cache-hit for everyone. rebar's exact precedent is `REVIEW_RESULT`: a reducer-IGNORED, preserved-and-ignored, per-ticket LLM-derived sidecar with a schema sentinel + a `prune` retention. We mirror it.

## What — payload schema (fully specified)
A `TICKET_DIGEST` sidecar event. Its `data` payload: `{"schema": "ticket_digest_v1", "digest": {problem_keywords, component_or_area, key_entities, propositions}, "content_hash": "<hex>", "model": "<model-id>", "digest_hash_version": <int>}`. The `schema` sentinel `"ticket_digest_v1"` guards reads (mirrors REVIEW_RESULT keying on `payload['schema'] == 'plan_review_result_v1'`) so a foreign/older payload is skipped, not mis-parsed. `content_hash`, `model`, `digest_hash_version` are the three freshness tags (named fields in the payload).

## Content hash — a LOCAL, self-consistent normalizer (no cross-layer import)
`content_hash = sha256(_normalize_text(state))` where `_normalize_text(state)` is a small module-LOCAL function in `digest_sidecar.py` doing the canonical join (title + description + comment bodies, `"\n".join`, empties skipped). It is deliberately LOCAL and NOT an import of `rebar._engine_support.gates._ticket_text`: no `rebar.llm.*` module imports `_engine_support.gates` (that would be a layering violation — the same reason S5/`ee3d` inlines its own join), and the content hash is this story's OWN internal freshness key, so it need not be byte-identical to any other module's normalizer. What matters is INTERNAL consistency: the SAME `_normalize_text` is used both when writing (`emit`) and when checking freshness (read), so a hash computed at write equals the hash recomputed at read for unchanged state. `DIGEST_HASH_VERSION` (module constant in the sidecar) is bumped only if the hashed field-set ever changes, invalidating all cached digests deterministically. (No dependency on S5's inline join — S5 does not hash; only this story computes/consumes the content hash.)

## Freshness (computed on read, fail-closed)
The digest is CURRENT iff ALL of: stored `content_hash` == `sha256(_normalize_text(current))` (via the SAME local `_normalize_text` used at write), stored `model` == active model, stored `digest_hash_version` == current constant. Any mismatch → stale. If current state can't be read (partial read) → NOT-current (fail-closed; never falsely fresh).

## Scope (exact edit targets — every registry a new event type touches)
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py`: the `_cmd_show` freshness render (detailed below). (No `gates.py` edit — the content-hash normalizer is local to `digest_sidecar.py`, see Content hash.)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: add `"TICKET_DIGEST"` to the `EVENT_TYPES` write allow-list AND its enumerated string in the StoreError message (lines ~97-103).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`: add `"TICKET_DIGEST"` to `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` (NOT `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`) — preserved-and-ignored, never compacted into SNAPSHOT, no fsck WARN (mirrors REVIEW_RESULT).
- New `src/rebar/llm/overlap/__init__.py` (the package) + `src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py` with `emit(digest, ticket_id)` (appends + calls `prune`), `prune(ticket_id, keep=1)`, `latest_ticket_digest(ticket_id)` (guards on the `ticket_digest_v1` sentinel) — all modeled on `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`.
- `show` freshness render (CLI-show-ONLY — must NOT touch the library state shape):
  the parity invariant `test_show_list_search_share_one_shape`
  (`tests/interfaces/store/test_reducer_single_source.py:59`) asserts the **library** returns
  are identical — `set(rebar.show_ticket(id)) == set(list_tickets element) == set(search element)`
  and `show == lst == srch`. So `show_state`/`show_ticket` and `reducer/_present.py::public_state`
  (the SHARED key-stripping filter used by show/list/search/ready/MCP — NOT a show-only
  renderer) must be left untouched. The freshness flag ("present-fresh"|"present-stale"|"absent")
  is therefore added ONLY in the CLI show arm `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py::_cmd_show`
  (~line 144-171): after `state = show_state(...)`, `_cmd_show` computes freshness via
  `overlap.digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest(id)` + the freshness check and injects
  `digest_freshness` into the dict it prints (`json.dumps(state, ...)` and the `to_llm(state)`
  `--output llm` arm) — a CLI-presentation-only field that never enters the library
  `show_ticket`/`list`/`search` returns, so the parity invariant holds. No new field in
  `ticket_state.schema.json`; the digest stays a sidecar (like REVIEW_RESULT).
  `test_cmd_show_renders_freshness` asserts the CLI `show` stdout carries the flag;
  `test_library_shape_unchanged` asserts `show_ticket`/`list`/`search` still share one shape
  with a digest present (parity invariant held).
- Prune invocation: `emit` calls `prune(keep=1)` on every write — EXACTLY the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar pattern, nothing more. There is NO special archive/delete lazy-prune (that novel behavior is dropped: it has no `REVIEW_RESULT` prior art and `show_state` does not cleanly signal "gone" for archived tickets). An archived/deleted ticket's digest simply lingers as a harmless sidecar, bounded to ONE record per ticket by `keep=1`, and is never read into any hot path (like a stale REVIEW_RESULT). `latest_ticket_digest` does no existence check on the ticket.

## Dependencies
S1 (indecisive-callous-armyworm) — produces the `ticket_digest` payload. (The drain that decides to re-enrich lives in S4; this story owns only WRITE + READ + freshness of the sidecar, not the skip decision.)

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_ticket_digest_store.py`: `test_roundtrip`; `test_freshness_all_triggers` (stale on content-hash OR model OR digest_hash_version change); `test_hash_write_read_parity` (the content_hash written by `emit` equals the hash recomputed by the freshness check for UNCHANGED state — proving both paths call the SAME local `_normalize_text`; and an edit to title/description/comments flips it stale — proving the normalizer actually covers those fields); `test_fail_closed` (unreadable → not-current); `test_latest_wins` (two appends, latest-by-HLC); `test_older_binary_ignores` (fsck no WARN); `test_cmd_show_renders_freshness` (CLI `show` stdout carries the flag); `test_library_shape_unchanged` (show_ticket/list/search still share one shape with a digest present); `test_prune_keep1` (a second `emit` supersedes the first — exactly one `TICKET_DIGEST` retained per ticket).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `TICKET_DIGEST` write→`latest_ticket_digest` read roundtrip with the `ticket_digest_v1` sentinel guard; `pytest ...::test_roundtrip`.
- [ ] Freshness flips stale on ANY of content-hash / model / digest_hash_version mismatch; `::test_freshness_all_triggers`. The content_hash uses a LOCAL `_normalize_text` (no `gates` import); the write path and the freshness-check path use the SAME normalizer (write-hash == read-hash for unchanged state); `::test_hash_write_read_parity`.
- [ ] `TICKET_DIGEST` in `EVENT_TYPES` + `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` (not `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`); older binary preserves-and-ignores, no fsck WARN; `::test_older_binary_ignores`.
- [ ] Unreadable current state → NOT-current (fail-closed); `::test_fail_closed`.
- [ ] The CLI `show` stdout renders digest presence + freshness (not raw text) via `_cmd_show`; `::test_cmd_show_renders_freshness`. The library `show_ticket`/`list`/`search` returns still share one shape with a digest present (parity invariant `test_show_list_search_share_one_shape` untouched); `::test_library_shape_unchanged`. `emit` keeps exactly one `TICKET_DIGEST` per ticket (`prune(keep=1)`, REVIEW_RESULT pattern; no archive/delete special-casing); `::test_prune_keep1`.
baseline.summary: Persist ticket digest as a content-hash-keyed record on the ticket (shared cache)

baseline.description:
`rebar review-code --ref <sha> --source attested` accepts both values, forwards them through the library, and drops them at the shim. This is not merely unimplemented: `CodeReviewRequest` has a `source` field (`gate_dispatch.py:297`) that `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` consumes (`gate_dispatch.py:433`), so the caller's request is actively discarded at the seam.

`llm/code_review/shim.py:127-128` declares `ref`/`source`; the `CodeReviewRequest(...)` literal at `:146-158` omits them. `shim.py` never imports `gate_source`, and `_verdict_to_review_result` (`:79-104`) never stamps `source`/`verified_at_sha` — while `operations.py:242`, `completion.py:488`, `plan_review/__init__.py:473` and `spec_scan.py:69` all do.

`_mcp_llm.py:93-96` tells MCP callers that results carry `source`/`verified_at_sha`/`signable`. That is a false promise on the trust boundary that decides whether a code review can be signed: `--source attested` silently reviews the dirty working tree and yields an unsignable result, indistinguishable from a successful attested run.

Highest-scoring finding of the audit (validity 1.0, impact 0.92). Both remediation proposers converged on this approach independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `ref` and `source` are forwarded into the `CodeReviewRequest` literal
- [x] `_verdict_to_review_result` stamps `source` and `verified_at_sha`, matching the four sibling producers
- [x] A behavioural test covers each `source` value, not just the signature change
- [x] `_mcp_llm.py`'s documented promise is true of the returned result
baseline.summary: Wire code-review provenance: --ref/--source are dropped at the shim

baseline.description:
Run the one-time reclaim. **Do not start until A1-A5, A6-0a..0d and Epic B's B6 are closed**, and until A6-0a has been on `main` >=24 h with an observed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run on a descendant SHA (older binaries ignore the epoch field, so they would sail past the guard). session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Protocol
1. **Agent** disables `reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (`gh workflow disable`,
   which also blocks `workflow_dispatch` and therefore `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` self-redispatch);
   **asserts** no reconcile run is in progress (poll `gh run list`, not drain-and-hope); asserts the
   **Gerrit review queue is empty** — zero sessions stops new pushes, but a patchset pushed just
   before the window can still have its `LLM-Review` vote fire during it, and every vote writes a
   ticket; break-glasses `refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}` if held.
2. **Agent** pauses the AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` and the host LaunchAgents
   `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` (04:00) and `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update` (whose hourly
   rollback-guarded pipx reinstall could silently revert the global `rebar` to a pre-A6-0a build
   mid-window). **[operator-attested] Operator** confirms **zero active sessions** and all
   **`rebar-mcp` servers stopped** (a long-running MCP holds an in-process store handle and does not
   hot-reload). Gerrit needs no separate confirmation: every Gerrit push comes from a session.
3. **Agent** converges the local tracker (`fetch` + `reset --hard origin/tickets`, 0-ahead verified).
   This covers all 48 sibling worktrees at once — their `.tickets-tracker` are **symlinks to the one
   store**. The four other real trackers on the host point at different GitHub repos.
4. **Agent** deletes the pre-rewrite ref pins (A6-0d), runs the strip in a fresh **unfiltered** clone,
   verifies the pre-push assertions, and pushes with **`--force-with-lease`**.
5. **Agent** asserts non-resurrection: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is
   **false**, and no clone-fetched ref has the old tip as an ancestor.
6. **Agent** converges the review-bot clone over SSM (`fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets` on
   `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`). Reverts to **[operator-attested]** if the issued AWS
   credentials do not permit `ssm send-command` against `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`.
7. **Agent** lands the `enforce_since` re-pin through Gerrit, mapped via the commit-map.
   `rebar.toml:115` is the only literal SHA in the system; with `require_authenticated = false`
   (`:106`) `verify_authorship.py:531-550` returns early and never reads it, so there is **no CI
   deadlock** and the change lands normally. `verify.opcert_enforce_since` is unset.
8. **Agent** re-enables the GitHub workflows, the AWS timer, and both LaunchAgents.
9. **Agent** verifies the ACs below and **notifies the operator** that the tickets branch is
   available for sessions again.

## T11 migration-safety answers
- **Expand/contract:** yes — A6-0a's reader ships and is deployed before the epoch value exists.
- **Batching:** n/a, single atomic ref update.
- **Resumability: NONE, stated.** A force-push is not resumable. Mitigation: all correctness
  assertions run on the scratch clone **before** publishing, so a wrong graph never reaches origin;
  the push itself is atomic per-ref.
- **Dual-write window:** none — the store is quiesced; the epoch guard replaces dual-write as the
  stale-writer defence.
- **Rollback:** restore from the A6-0d bundle + `--force-with-lease` back to the old tip. Known
  limit: rollback re-diverges anything already converged, so consumers must be re-converged in the
  same order as the forward path. **No event bytes are ever altered** — only commit SHAs — so the
  rewrite itself cannot lose ticket data.
- **T4 destructiveness:** an irreversible force-push to the authoritative store of a live system,
  chosen deliberately to reclaim 92% of the branch, gated on operator-confirmed quiescence, an
  off-repo bundle, a fail-closed epoch guard, and pre-push assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB** (from 1.04 GiB; the measured strip
      result is ~94 MiB) and `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree.
      **Holds only because B6 landed first.** Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] Commit count and merge-commit count on `tickets` are **unchanged** versus the pre-rewrite
      recording (measured at window time, never hardcoded). Tier: **repo assertion**.
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <sha> --format json`, run pre-rewrite
      against the old SHA and post-rewrite against the mapped SHA: the **stderr summary counts** are
      identical AND the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` from the JSON report is
      identical **ignoring `commit`**. (JSON mode puts only the report array on stdout and the summary
      on stderr; the report lists only non-verified events; every `commit` is a rewritten SHA. The
      command **exits 1** when `enforced_not_verified > 0`, so do not require exit 0.) Tier: **CLI
      subprocess, both sides**.
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** and `size-pack` growth is **< 1 MB**. The ancestry assertion is
      what actually proves non-resurrection. Tier: **repo measurement after an observed vote**.
- [ ] No ref a default clone fetches has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier: `ls-remote` +
      `merge-base` loop, computed at window time.
- [ ] Operator confirmation of zero active sessions and stopped MCP servers is recorded as a comment
      before step 3. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] A reconciler pass completes green after step 8, and `rebar fsck` is clean. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
Operational — no `src/` changes. Uses the A6-0c script and A6-0d helpers; touches `rebar.toml` (`enforce_since`) via Gerrit in step 7.

Scope: M (operational). Depends on A5, A6-0b, A6-0c, A6-0d, and Epic B's B6.
baseline.summary: A6-1: execute the reclaim window (quiesced, guarded, agent-executed except the zero-sessions confirmation)

## Context / Problem
`scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` is wired into CI as its own step (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, "comment-hygiene gate") and is covered locally only by `tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py::test_the_real_tree_is_clean`, which runs in the **full** suite. It is **not** in `make lint`, so the local fast gate returns a clean verdict over trees CI rejects. Measured cost: bug 84c7 (change 1999) took a `Verified -1` for comment-hygiene findings `make lint` could not surface, wasting a full review cycle (two red jobs, the pytest one 15m09s with the hygiene guard as its only failure).

## Approach
Evidence gathered and recorded as a comment on this ticket resolves the ticket's option fork in favor of wiring the gate into `make lint`:
- The introducing ticket `b047-267f-3c3d-4374` shows **no deliberate intent** to keep the gate out of `make lint` — its plan wired the detector as a named CI step per the `scripts/check_*.py` guard convention and never discusses the local lint target.
- Measured runtime: ~4.9s warm on the full tree locally (`make lint` baseline 17.8s → ~22.7s). Acceptable next to the 15-minute CI cycle a miss costs, and squarely inside the documented env-var-drift-gate rationale already in the Makefile ("running it here makes the local verdict agree with CI instead of surfacing staleness only in the full suite").

So: add `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` to the `lint` target next to `scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check`, mirroring that gate's precedent exactly — the standalone CI step in `_build-and-test.yml` **stays** (its if-present guard correctly handles patchsets predating the gate; the small double-run in CI matches the env-registry precedent). Add a wiring test in `tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py` (the gate's own test module) asserting the `lint` target body invokes the script, using the `_lint_target_body` idiom from `tests/unit/test_config_gate_wiring_heldout.py`, plus a teeth case proving the assertion flips when the invocation is stripped from a synthetic Makefile copy.

## Scope
- `Makefile` — add the gate invocation (with a short rationale comment citing this ticket and the measured runtime) to the `lint` target.
- `tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py` — baseline wiring assertion + removal-teeth test.

## Testing
RED first: the new wiring test fails against the unedited Makefile. GREEN: it passes once the lint-target line lands. Edge/teeth: stripping the invocation from a synthetic Makefile copy flips the assertion (proves it is not vacuous). `make lint` (now including the gate), `make typecheck`, and the targeted test module all pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The introducing ticket `b047-267f-3c3d-4374` is checked for deliberate intent to keep the gate out of `make lint`, and the finding (none found) plus the measured runtime (~4.9s standalone; lint 17.8s → ~22.7s) are recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [x] `make lint` runs `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` in the `lint` target — verified by running `make lint` and by the new wiring test in `tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py`.
- [x] The wiring test has teeth: a synthetic Makefile with the invocation stripped fails the same assertion, and this is itself a passing test at HEAD.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py` pass locally.
baseline.summary: comment-hygiene gate is reachable locally only via the full suite, not make lint

## Context

Complete bridge portability across local shells, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments without breaking checked-out workflows or environments that still use the legacy reconcile vocabulary.

This story coordinates two independently releasable children:

1. A runner-neutral bridge entrypoint plus thin GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and GitLab wrappers.
2. Provider-neutral destructive-repair pause ownership for `fsck --repair` and `doctor --repair`.

The children are intentionally dependency-free. Their implementation ownership is otherwise non-overlapping; their additive release-note updates were developed and landed sequentially. Each child preserves old vocabulary, signatures, defaults, messages, exit behavior, and mutation boundaries while adding the new noun-based bridge route. They may be reviewed and submitted separately or shipped together after both gates are green.

GitHub-specific mirror health (`src/rebar/mirror_guard.py`) and optional GitHub step-summary reporting are outside bridge execution. They remain unchanged and are not evidence for or against the provider neutrality of the bridge runner.

## Plan

1. Review and claim each child independently.
2. Implement each child under RED-first held-out TDD.
3. Require `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved Gerrit comments before submission.
4. Verify legacy reconcile callers and checked-out workflows continue to operate.
5. Close this story after both children have landed and closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The runner-neutral bridge child is closed with its Gerrit change merged.
- [x] The provider-neutral destructive-repair child is closed with its Gerrit change merged.
- [x] Checked-out workflows that still invoke `rebar reconcile --mode ...` retain their behavior.
- [x] Environments using legacy reconcile modes retain their published defaults and exit behavior.
- [x] Local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare bridge execution use the packaged Python core in `src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py` through exactly `rebar bridge run`; no repository-local runner script is required.
- [x] `src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py` owns destructive-repair schedule safety through the provider-neutral durable gate lifecycle: it reads the existing pause snapshot, calls `set_pause`, and clears only its observed OID through `release(..., ref_lock.GATE_REF, ...)`.
- [x] `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` proves no GitHub CLI dependency: it rejects subprocess argv beginning with `gh`, runs destructive repair successfully, and asserts `gh_calls == []`.

## File impact

Owned by the two child tasks. This coordination story changes no files directly; its recorded file-impact paths are child-owned completion evidence supplied to the bounded close-gate prefetch.
baseline.summary: Make the bridge portable across local, GitHub, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments

## Context / Problem

Current-base archaeology shows that `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` (the `factories` map, ~lines 413-418) registers `review-code`, `review-plan`, and `sign-review`, but there is no bare `review` command anywhere in the registry. Two operational-guidance pages still misstate the current CLI contract:

- `AGENTS.md` (~lines 239-241) claims "the old single-pass `review` verb
  is deprecated and now forwards to `review-plan`" -- there is no such
  forwarding; the verb is gone, not deprecated-and-forwarding.
- `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` (line 3) claims the CLI forms are
  "`rebar review-plan`, `verify-completion`, `review`, `review-code`, and
  `scan-spec`, with `review` retained as an alias" -- no such alias exists.

`docs/exit-codes.md` does NOT contain a stale bare-`review` row: line 184 is the unrelated `identity` command row, and the file's full `review` table rows (192-199, 259-280) are all live (`review-code`, `review-plan`, `sign-review`, and the `--review` flag on `edit`/`claim`) -- there is no bare-`review` row to remove there. `docs/exit-codes.md` needs no edit for this ticket; it already has no stale bare-`review` claim.

Historical records also mention the removed command and must remain historical evidence, not be rewritten: `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:170` records a prior CLI/MCP mapping; `docs/release-notes.md:441` and `docs/output-schemas.md:263` expressly describe the surface as removed.

## Approach

Rewrite the stale `AGENTS.md` LLM-operations guidance and the stale `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` CLI-form list to describe only live commands: `review-plan`, `review-code`, `sign-review` where applicable, `verify-completion`, and `scan-spec`. Do not touch `docs/exit-codes.md` (it already carries no stale bare-`review` claim -- confirmed above). Do not alter the ADR or removal-history records. Do not add a command-reference generator and do not change the CLI registry: source inspection is the verification boundary, not an implementation target.

## Scope

- `AGENTS.md` -- remove or rewrite the stale claim that bare `review`
  is deprecated and forwards to `review-plan`.
- `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` -- remove bare `review` from its CLI
  forms list and delete the retained-alias claim.
- Read-only, no edit expected: `docs/exit-codes.md` (verify it still has
  no bare-`review` row/prose -- it already doesn't).
- Read-only historical records: `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md`,
  `docs/release-notes.md`, and `docs/output-schemas.md` retain accurate
  past/removal references.
- Read-only verification: `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` establishes the
  live command set.

## Testing

Run the existing documentation checks. Confirm the registry has no bare `review` route. Run `rg -n 'rebar review($|[^-])' AGENTS.md README.md docs`, then classify every residual hit: the only allowed historical hits are the ADR mapping row and the release-notes/output-schemas removed-surface records; any operational-guidance hit is a failure. Search the two edited operational pages for deprecated-forwarding and retained-alias wording.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Existing documentation checks pass without expanding

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

rebar has three detached-child spawn sites that are near-duplicates of one another:

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — the async branch of `push_tickets_branch`
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — `_spawn_detached_drain` (+ `_detach_kwargs`)
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` — `_spawn_detached_sweep` (+ `_detach_kwargs`)

Each independently repeats: the `parents[2]` PYTHONPATH bootstrap so a bare-python child can import rebar, the `-c` stub that re-inserts `src` and calls back into rebar, the platform detach flags, the stdio discipline, and the never-raise wrapper. The duplication is not accidental and it is documented in the code itself — `compact_trigger._detach_kwargs` says "mirroring :func:`rebar.llm.enrich_drain._detach_kwargs`", `_spawn_detached_sweep` says "Mirrors ``enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain``", and `enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain` says "Mirrors push.py's PYTHONPATH bootstrap".

## Why this matters — a defect has already propagated along this seam

Bug `3198-438c-72a5-470f` was a missing `cwd=` on the detached `Popen`: the child inherited the spawning command's working directory, and when that was a `make worktree` worktree since removed, the child died at `os.getcwd()`. It was present at ALL THREE sites, and it got there by deliberate imitation across three separate tickets:

- `57114212cf` (2026-06-12, pre-trailer) introduced the pattern in `push.py`;
- `c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135` copied it into the drain — its plan says outright "POSIX reuses
  push.py's approach (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`) + its PYTHONPATH bootstrap";
- `1fde-becd-942a-4351` copied it again into the compaction sweep.

One omission, replicated three times over two months, because "spawn a detached rebar child" has no single implementation to get right once. The next property this pattern needs — a signal handler, an env projection, a resource limit, an fd discipline — will propagate the same way.

## Scope (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)
- A single `spawn_detached(...)` in `src/rebar/_proc.py` (already the documented single source
  of truth for logic shared between detached spawn sites, and already home to
  `reap_process_group` and `detached_child_cwd`; it is a deliberate stdlib-only leaf with no
  `rebar.*` imports, which must be preserved). It would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the
  detach flags and the durable cwd, and it RE-RAISES on failure — the never-raise posture
  stays per-caller, because the three sites do not catch identically (push.py catches only
  `OSError`, logging `%r`; drain/sweep catch broad `Exception` with `exc_info=True`) and
  folding the catch into the helper would silently broaden push.py's exposure. Each caller
  keeps its existing `except` clause and its own log line, so the refactor changes no
  exception surface. Callers would supply the child
  entry point, their stderr sink, and their child ENV — env construction stays per-caller
  because it differs materially (push.py passes its secret-stripped
  `project_child_env(relationship="unrelated")` projection plus `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`,
  the drain/sweep pass a plain `{**os.environ}`); the helper only layers the PYTHONPATH
  bootstrap onto whatever env the caller provides, so consolidation cannot drop
  push.py's secret-stripping.
- The three call sites above collapse onto it.
- Test consumers of the per-site helpers move with them: 
  `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_windows_detach_kwargs` (and any other direct
  caller of a per-site `_detach_kwargs`) is rewritten against `_proc`'s platform seam —
  `_proc` exposes the detach-kwargs construction testably so the Windows branch keeps its
  API-derisked assertion — since the per-site helpers no longer exist.
- Related open question, deliberately NOT changed while fixing 3198: should
  `_config_sources.repo_root`'s final `Path.cwd()` fallback DEGRADE rather than raise? It was
  left raising on purpose — a silently-wrong repo root is worse than a loud failure, and the
  three detached children no longer reach it now that they get an explicit cwd. But the
  exposure survives for long-lived IN-PROCESS work, which cannot be given its own cwd: daemon
  threads at `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:575`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py:523`,
  `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:440`,
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_heartbeat.py:69`, and a reconciler that
  `src/rebar/config.py:516` says "can run as a daemon from anywhere". Decide that posture
  once, here, rather than per-site.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Exactly one implementation of "spawn a detached rebar child" exists; the three sites
      call it and none re-implements the bootstrap or the detach flags.
- [x] A STATIC test (source scan over `src/rebar`) enforces that the signature of a
      DETACHED-REBAR-CHILD spawn appears only in `_proc.py`: the Windows detach tokens
      (`DETACHED_PROCESS` / `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) and the bare-python re-entry bootstrap
      (the `-c` stub doing `sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[...])` back into `rebar.*`).
      A fourth un-exercised copy-paste site then fails the test rather than slipping
      past a runtime-only assertion. The three NON-detached `start_new_session` spawn
      sites (`grounding/harness.py`, `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`,
      `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — process-group reaping, not rebar
      re-entry) are out of scope and must stay untouched.
- [x] `_proc.py` remains a stdlib-only leaf with no `rebar.*` imports.
- [x] A recorded decision (accept or change) on `repo_root`'s cwd fallback for long-lived
      in-process callers — recorded as a comment on this ticket AND in the docstring at
      `_config_sources.repo_root` (verified by inspecting that location); if the decision is
      'change', the degraded fallback is implemented.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Observed while fixing `3198-438c-72a5-470f`. The cwd omission itself is fixed at all three sites; this is the structural reason it was three sites and not one.
baseline.summary: consolidate the three detached-spawn sites behind one helper

baseline.description:
## Problem

`infra/scripts/observability.sh` counts journal/log markers CUMULATIVELY — grep the whole journal for a token, publish `total - prev`, where `prev` is a persisted offset file. Six counters share the shape, and every one guards the negative case identically:

    new=$((total - prev))
    [ "$new" -lt 0 ] && new=$total

Verified present at §3 replication_errors, §4 voter_errors, §4c review_bot_merge_change_errors, §4d deploy_errors, §4e (the shared `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` helper, covering deploy_deferrals AND review_interrupts), and §4b g2p_dispatch_errors.

A negative delta happens only when the journal LOSES history it previously had — journald vacuuming by `SystemMaxUse`/`MaxRetentionSec`, a `journalctl --vacuum-*`, or the persistent journal being cleared. In exactly that case the guard republishes the ENTIRE remaining count as "new this interval", re-counting markers already counted and already alarmed on.

## Why it matters most for `review_interrupts`

`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts` (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) is `period=900, evaluation_periods=1, datapoints_to_alarm=1, threshold>0` — deliberately a single datapoint so the `signal-unavailable` case surfaces fast. One spurious republish therefore pages, and it pages pointing an investigator at journal history that was just deleted.

## NOT currently firing — latent, not the cause of anything observed

Measured on i-00880b2c7f13527c5 on 2026-08-12 while diagnosing [rebar:7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9]: journal total = 7, offset file = 7, journal reaches back to 2026-07-03. No rotation has occurred on this box yet. Filed because the hazard was ruled OUT by measurement, not design.

## Plan

Minimal, bash-delta-negative-to-flat. Do NOT add a boot-id/cursor state machine: that is real logic, and this repo prefers deleting bash over growing it (AGENTS.md strangler-fig). The correct fix is one token per site.

1. Replace the clamp at all six sites with `new=0`, i.e. treat lost history as
   already-counted. Rationale: the offset is monotonic evidence that those markers were
   already published. If the journal shrank, every surviving marker is at-or-older-than the
   ones we already counted, so republishing them is guaranteed double-counting; suppressing
   them under-counts at most the markers emitted inside the single rotating interval. For a
   1-datapoint pager, a missed count that the NEXT interval catches (the offset resets to the
   new smaller total, so genuinely-new markers after rotation still publish) is strictly
   better than a false page. The offset write is unchanged: `echo "$total" > offset` still
   runs on successful publish, so the counter re-bases to the shrunken journal in one interval.
2. State that rationale in the script as a single shared comment at §3 (the first site) and
   a one-line back-reference at the other sites — no duplicated prose.
3. Extend the existing bash-driven pytest harness
   `tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py`'s pattern with a new test module that
   drives the real script with a stubbed `journalctl`/`aws` and a PRE-SEEDED offset file
   LARGER than the stub's marker count (the shrinking-journal simulation), asserting the
   published value is 0 — not the total — for `review_interrupts` and every other counter.

No Python migration is warranted: after this change the counters are a subtraction and a clamp, not logic worth porting. A future time-windowed (`journalctl --since`) rewrite would delete the offset files entirely and IS the right shape, but it changes the metric's semantics under clock skew and is out of scope for a latent-hazard bugfix.

## Deployment

No manual box action. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` watches `OBS_PATHS` (`infra/scripts/observability.sh infra/scripts/install-observability.sh`) and re-runs the idempotent `install-observability.sh` on the box when either changes, re-materializing `/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh`. Landing on `main` ships it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: No `new=$total` (or per-site equivalent `*new=$*total`) clamp remains in
      `infra/scripts/observability.sh`; all six negative-delta guards assign 0. Verify:
      `grep -nE '(-lt 0 \])? *&& *[a-z]*new=\$[a-z]*total' infra/scripts/observability.sh`
      returns no matches.
- [x] AC2: A test drives the real script with an offset file seeded ABOVE the journal marker
      count and asserts the published `review_interrupts` value is `0`, covering every one of
      the six counters. Verify: the new test module passes and FAILS against the pre-fix
      script (checked by reverting the clamp locally once).
- [x] AC3: The chosen behaviour on lost history — suppress rather than republish — is stated
      with its rationale in a comment in `infra/scripts/observability.sh`.
- [x] AC4: Existing `tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py` and
      `tests/scripts/test_observability_exit.py` still pass (no regression to the
      publish-then-persist-offset contract).
baseline.summary: observability marker counters re-count on journal rotation, spuriously re-firing the 1-datapoint review-interrupts alarm

baseline.description:
A runaway/exhaustion-truncated completion-verifier run is dispositioned as a BLOCKING substantive FAIL (exit 1, requires --force) instead of the non-blocking, re-runnable INDETERMINATE fault the contract requires (bug 2a6f; 46a2; ed6d). Root cause confirmed (RCA comment). Two compounding seams downstream of a correctly-firing runaway guard, both from ticket 1d71-a76c-04f6-4642 (commit 6b318ffaec4a).

## Root cause (proven)
- Seam A (mint): `completion_verdict_assembly._restamp_marker` stamps the per-criterion
  insufficiency marker only when the criterion's BANK entry carries it; a criterion the abort
  truncated is NEVER banked (`entry is None`), so the marker is POPPED, minting a bare
  `met=false` indistinguishable from a positive refutation. The OMITTED-criterion branch of the
  same function already stamps un-banked criteria insufficient — the ECHO branch is
  inconsistent.
- Seam B (disposition): reconcile_verdict already derives the top-level
  `evidence_sufficient=False` marker on an insufficiency-only FAIL (since 1d71), but the close
  gate (`close_precheck`) and the standalone `verify-completion` verb (`_llm_commands`) still
  raise the fail-closed exit 1 for it. Only a `verdict_obtainable=False` fault (the no-criterion
  fault, bug 2a6f) currently takes the retryable exit-11 path.

## Approach (two behavior-preserving fixes; reuse the EXISTING evidence_sufficient marker)
- Fix A — `completion_verdict_assembly._restamp_marker`: a finalizer-echoed `met is False`
  record whose criterion has NO bank entry (`entry is None` — never evaluated/truncated) is
  stamped `evidence_sufficient=False`, making the echo branch consistent with the omitted
  branch. Keys STRICTLY on `entry is None`, NOT on any bank-entry evidence-cap `truncated`
  flag: a PRESENT markerless entry is a genuine refutation and stays bare (failures not masked).
- Fix B — a single shared pure helper `completion_fail_returncode(result)` (added to
  completion_reconcile, re-exported from `rebar.llm.completion`) returns the retryable 11 when
  the FAIL is a fault (`verdict_obtainable is False` OR `evidence_sufficient is False`), else 1.
  Both consumers call it, so their disposition is identical by construction. NO overload of
  `verdict_obtainable` (its schema stays the no-criterion fault); routed on the existing
  `evidence_sufficient` marker. The insufficiency-accurate close message already exists in
  `_verification_fail_message` — only the returncode changes.

## Impacted sites
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py — `_restamp_marker` (Fix A).
- src/rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py — new `completion_fail_returncode` helper (Fix B).
- src/rebar/llm/completion.py — re-export `completion_fail_returncode`.
- src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py — the generic completion-FAIL raise uses
  `completion_fail_returncode(result)` for its returncode (was hard-coded 1).
- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py — the `verify-completion` verb returns
  `completion_fail_returncode(result)` on a non-PASS (was hard-coded 1).
- src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json — update the `evidence_sufficient`
  description: its close/verb disposition is now the retryable exit-11 fault, not fail-closed.
- Unchanged consumer (noted for completeness): src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py already
  persists the top-level `evidence_sufficient` marker onto the durable record (since 1d71) — no
  new durable-record behavior.
- tests/ — new deterministic regression tests (no LLM).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] An insufficiency-only FAIL (top-level `evidence_sufficient=False`, incl. un-banked
  `met=false` echoes) disposes as retryable exit 11 via `completion_fail_returncode`; the
  ticket does not close.
- [x] A completed run with a genuinely-refuted criterion (met=false, no insufficiency marker)
  still disposes as exit 1 — genuine failures are not masked (dual assertion).
- [x] The pre-existing no-criterion fault (`verdict_obtainable=False`, 2a6f) still disposes
  exit 11 — undisturbed.
- [x] `merge_finalizer_with_bank` stamps `evidence_sufficient=False` on an un-banked
  `met=false` echo (entry is None), and leaves a present markerless entry bare.
- [x] `verdict_obtainable`'s schema/meaning is unchanged (no overload); `evidence_sufficient`
  schema doc updated to the retryable disposition.
- [x] Deterministic regression tests (no LLM) cover all; `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean;
  complexity ratchet not increased.

## Portability
No CI-provider coupling: pure in-process verdict reconciliation/assembly/disposition logic, exercised by deterministic unit tests that run under any/no CI provider.

## Test plan
Held-out RED oracle drives `merge_finalizer_with_bank` and the shared `completion_fail_returncode` helper on synthetic verdict/bank dicts; asserts the exit-11 insufficiency disposition, the preserved 2a6f exit-11 fault, and the non-masking exit-1 genuine block; mutation-check by restoring the pop / collapsing the helper to always-1.
baseline.summary: Completion-verifier close gate FAULTs: runaway read_file loop aborts evidence search, then reports the truncation as a blocking FAIL (3 'evidence gap' unmet criteria)

baseline.description:
## Summary
`rebar list --status=all` (or any invalid status value) silently returns an empty list instead of rejecting the value. An unrecognized filter value should be a loud error, not an empty result set.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar list --status=all` (all is not a valid status).
2. Observe: exit 0, output `[]`.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: non-zero exit + error naming the invalid status value and listing valid ones (open/in_progress/closed/blocked/deleted...).
- Actual: exit 0 with [] — indistinguishable from 'no tickets match'.

## Impact
Corrupted a real measurement during the 3006-e198 derisk experiments (an agent computed 614 false class-A drift candidates from the silently-empty list). Any agent or script filtering by a mistyped status silently operates on an empty world.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An invalid --status value exits non-zero with an error listing valid statuses.
- [ ] A test covers the invalid-status path (RED before fix).
- [ ] Valid statuses (and any 'all'-equivalent, if one is intended) are documented in `rebar list --help`.
baseline.summary: rebar list --status=<invalid> silently returns empty instead of erroring

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The 7–21 Aug 2026 defect review (221 bug tickets, 196 real, 56 git-dated to changes inside the window) found that every hotspot is the same decision written in two to seven places: a fix lands in one copy and its twin stays broken, so families arrive as three-ticket instalments (sidecar keying ×3, git_adapter by-path loads ×3, nested-pytest --basetemp ×3, comment key/send fit ×5, compaction ×6). The spawner consolidation (`c98d976199`) and its static guard `tests/unit/test_spawn_detached.py::test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc` showed the durable shape: one implementation plus a test that a second copy cannot merge (`7213e082b5` was caught by it two days later).

## Approach
Each child collapses one duplicated computation into one shared module, keeps every current behaviour pinned by the tests named in the child, and lands with a construct-uniqueness guard that asserts on the construct's distinctive atoms (not on internals), with an explicit `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker as `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` uses. Children are independent; order by blast radius (store paths and stamped lock first, merge recovery last).

## Guard-test construction rule (applies to every child; approved 2026-08-21)
A construct-uniqueness guard pins how MANY implementations exist, never how the one implementation works. Build it as `tests/unit/test_spawn_detached.py::test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc` is built:
1. Scan every file under `src/rebar` EXCEPT the owner module; refactoring inside the owner cannot fail the guard.
2. Match on the conjunction of atoms that constitute the construct (for example `os.O_EXCL` together with `stamped_file_is_stale`), or on an AST shape (call target plus argument position) as `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` does — never on a single common token such as `os.open` or `.lock`.
3. Provide a line marker with a mandatory reason (`# <construct>-ok: <why>`) for a legitimate second use, so the exception is visible in review instead of silently absent.
4. Where the construct has no distinctive atoms, assert the definition count of the named symbol instead (exactly one `def <name>` under `src/rebar`).
5. The guard proves uniqueness only. Behaviour preservation is proven by the pinning tests each child names, which must pass with no assertion edits.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_store/`, `src/rebar/_commands/` (transition/close/compaction), `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (outbound comments), `src/rebar/llm/` (runtime, failure, gate dispatch), `src/rebar/_mcp_*.py`, `tests/` helpers and guards, `.github/workflows/` (predates-gate guard).

## Acceptance Criteria

This epic carries **two child classes with different guarantees**, and the criteria below are scoped accordingly. The **consolidation children** — the fourteen named under "Child responsibilities" — collapse duplicated logic and are held to no-behaviour-change plus net-negative lines. The **hardening children** (`dormant-fibre-pterosaurs`, `tireless-ruinable-prairiedog`, `bold-abeyant-indri`, `amenable-befuddling-phoenix`, `nitro-zombie-mealworm`, `diabetic-inorganic-equine`, `emulsible-beneficent-caiman`, `compliable-evaluable-mamba`, `tectonic-toxophilic-limpet`) close the process gaps the same defect review found: they deliberately ADD behaviour and lines, so the two consolidation guarantees do not apply to them and they are governed by their own recorded criteria.

- [ ] Every duplicated computation inventoried in the review has exactly one implementation on `main`, each delivered by one consolidation child; checked by that child's construct-uniqueness test passing in the default `Verified` tier.
- [ ] No **consolidation** child changes a PINNED observable behaviour: the pinning tests each such child names pass unchanged (no edits to their assertions); checked by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` of each landed change showing only additions. Where collapsing copies also converges a latent divergence — a copy that lacked a fix its twins already carried — the child records that convergence explicitly in its own description and covers it with a new test; the guarantee is that no PINNED behaviour changes silently.
- [ ] The net non-test line count across the **consolidation** children's landed changes is negative; checked by summing `git show --numstat` over those children's trailer commits.
- [ ] Each **hardening** child meets its own recorded acceptance criteria; checked by that child's own close gate (completion verification + execution-phase plan review).
baseline.summary: Collapse duplicated logic into shared modules (fortnight defect review)

baseline.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230, store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88 commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py` 14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.** `_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3; `signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP 204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in `llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" — the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [ ] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [ ] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and "Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [ ] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [ ] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [ ] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.
baseline.summary: Comment triage: relocate history, rationale and contracts out of src

baseline.description:
# Refresh exact-pinned dev tooling: zizmor + ruff

Bump two exact `==` pins in `pyproject.toml`'s `[dev]` extra to current, un-yanked releases.

## Why
- **zizmor 1.27.0 is YANKED** for GHSA-f42p-wjw5-97qh (Moderate, CWE-532): 1.27.0 prints
  GitHub tokens (`GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN`) to stderr under `-v`/debug
  logging. Only 1.27.0 is affected; the fix is 1.28.0. rebar's `make lint` invokes `zizmor
  release.yml` with no verbose flag, so there is no live exposure, but pinning exactly to a
  security-yanked release is fragile (a stricter resolver / pruned cache can fail installs).
- **ruff 0.15.19 -> 0.15.22**: routine patch refresh to stay current on the format/lint pin
  (exact-pinned for local<->CI parity). No yank/security; grouped here as a low-risk sibling.

## Plan
1. `pyproject.toml`: change the pin line `zizmor==1.27.0` -> `zizmor==1.28.0`.
2. `pyproject.toml`: change the pin line `ruff==0.15.19` -> `ruff==0.15.22`.
3. Reinstall the dev extra so the worktree venv has the new tools.
4. Run `make lint`; if the newer ruff reformats anything, apply `ruff format` and include the
   diff so CI format-check stays green. Run `make typecheck`.
5. One commit, `rebar-ticket` trailer + DCO sign-off; push to Gerrit; land after
   `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`.

Note: the pin comment block above zizmor does not mention a specific version string, so no
comment edit is required — only the pin line itself changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `zizmor==1.28.0` — verify: `grep -c 'zizmor==1.28.0' pyproject.toml` returns 1 and `grep -c 'zizmor==1.27.0' pyproject.toml` returns 0.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `ruff==0.15.22` — verify: `grep -c 'ruff==0.15.22' pyproject.toml` returns 1 and `grep -c 'ruff==0.15.19' pyproject.toml` returns 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0 in the worktree venv (ruff check + format-check + zizmor + actionlint).
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0 in the worktree venv.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only `pyproject.toml` (plus any file ruff-format rewrote), no unrelated files.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The change is merged to `main` via Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` (evidence: the merged change's Gerrit vote record; out-of-session).
baseline.summary: Bump zizmor 1.27.0->1.28.0 (yanked/GHSA) and ruff 0.15.19->0.15.22

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The code-review `tests` overlay (blocking at 0.54 — `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json:110-121`) is selected only when a changed file matches its `applies_to` globs `**/test_*.py`, `**/*_test.py`, `**/tests/**` (`registry.glob_triggered_overlays`, `registry.py:340-356`). A change adding product logic and no test file never runs it unless the base reviewer happens to recommend it, and guard (vii) (`code-review-tests.md:97`) keeps a bare coverage-gap finding advisory.

Four changes adding declarations merged on `LLM-Review +1` with zero test files: Gerrit 388 (`d9e0f0e733`, 15 added `def`/`class` lines, new `git_adapter.py`), 1920 (`721cb7d6ac`, 3), 1737 (`1c2bf6e57b`, 22), 1703 (`83d91d488c`, 8). 388 later produced three bugs (`79c6-eaf3-38af-4ce9` + two siblings) — the `git_adapter` by-path-load family the epic names. Gerrit 1547 (`24917e843b`) is a NEGATIVE case: comment-only source delta, 0 added declarations. Approved in the 2026-08-21 fortnight defect review; diff-coverage was rejected — this project tests behaviour, not coverage %.

## Approach
Fire the overlay from the diff CONTENT, where the diff and the changed files are both known.
1. `content_triggered_overlays` (`registry.py:461`) takes `(diff_text, repo_root)` only and is
   path-blind by construction (every helper skips the `+++`/`---` headers), so the "no test file
   changed" half of the rule has no operand there. Add a keyword-only
   `changed_files: Sequence[str] = ()` (call sites stay positional) and pass the step's `changed`
   list at `workflow_ops.py:99`.
2. The detector is a NEW module-level helper (`_has_added_declaration`), NOT extra branches inside
   `content_triggered_overlays`: the complexity ratchet fails on `new>0` and may not be raised. It
   fires when, for some changed file, an ADDED (`+`) line matches
   the EXISTING polyglot `_REMOVED_DECL_RE` (`registry.py:399-412` — Python `def`/`class`, Go
   `func`, Rust `fn`, JS/TS `function`/arrow/`class`) and the NAME it declares is not also removed
   on a `-` line in that same file (per-file provenance from the `diff --git … b/<path>` headers,
   since the composed context interleaves files). `_REMOVED_DECL_RE` has no capture group, so the name comes from a
   SEPARATE regex over the matched line, spanning the same keywords (`def`/`class`/`fn`/`func`/
   `function`, `const`/`let`/`var`). NAMES, not line TEXT: an annotation-only rewrite that re-wraps
   a signature changes every declaration line's text while declaring nothing new. An ANONYMOUS
   declaration (`export default function (`) yields no name, so it cannot take part in the
   comparison and is SKIPPED — failing closed rather than firing on a rewrite; a recorded
   limitation. `tests` is then selected only if NO changed file matches the `tests` globs.
   Added DECLARATIONS only — branch-line ("a new `if`/`for`") detection is explicitly OUT, since
   no cited corpus case needs it; a follow-up may add it with its own case.
3. Portable by construction, not by CI: an in-process pure-text scan, identical under the library,
   CLI and remote-MCP harnesses and under any CI provider or none, assuming NO language and NO
   repository layout — no `src/**` predicate, no Python-only regex — so it fires for a Ruby, Java,
   Next.js or .NET target as for this one. Its only path predicates are the `tests` globs and a
   docs/data extension skip (`.md`/`.rst`/`.txt`/`.json`/`.yaml`/`.yml`/`.toml`/`.cfg`/`.ini`/
   `.lock`), so a fenced code block in a docs-only change cannot fire it.
4. A MOVE is not suppressed: the reviewed diff carries no `-M` (`assemble.py:230`), so a rename
   arrives as delete-in-A + add-in-B whose added names are new to B — 1920 and 1737 trigger.
5. The scanned text is the COMPOSED context: `overlay_union` receives
   `steps.assemble_diff.outputs.context` (`gates/code-review.yaml:63`, `:116`) — a changed-files
   list plus the diff truncated at `DIFF_CHAR_CAP = 60000` (`assemble.py:30`,
   `compose_diff_context:77-92`). Both shapes are tested; a declaration past the cap does not
   trigger (a recorded blind spot), while `changed_files` is truncation-proof — hence keying the
   rule's negative half on it. Accepted consequences: the `tests`-keyed Pass-4 coach moves
   (`moves.py:30`, `:75-82`) now offer on ordinary source changes, and each qualifying change
   costs one extra uncapped Round-A overlay call.
6. Narrow guard (vii) in `code-review-tests.md:97` so a coverage gap is blocking-eligible only when
   the finding concerns *newly introduced behaviour* AND names a *violating input*. No trigger
   provenance reaches the reviewer (`workflow_ops.py:61-65` supplies context/changed_files/
   scope_context only), so the prompt DEFINES both from the diff alone: behaviour is *newly
   introduced* when its implementing lines appear as ADDED (`+`) lines in the diff under review;
   behaviour reachable only through unadded lines is *pre-existing* and stays advisory; a *named
   violating input* is a concrete value, argument or call sequence stated verbatim in the finding
   that the added lines mishandle. ONE prompt serves both rounds, so this also narrows blocking
   eligibility for the existing glob-triggered population (0.54, 8.0% of changes) — intended; the
   corpus gains the pre-existing FP case.

## Scope
Under `src/rebar/llm/code_review/`: `registry.py` (594 lines, cap 800) — `changed_files` kwarg + `_has_added_declaration`; `workflow_ops.py` — pass `changed` at `:99`, refresh the step `description=` (`:70-86`); `criteria_routing.json` — `tests` `_comment` only, `applies_to` unchanged. Also `reviewers/code-review-tests.md` (guard (vii)) and `eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` (one recall + one FP case), both under `src/rebar/llm/`; new `tests/unit/test_code_review_tests_trigger.py` (`tests/unit/llm/` does not exist).

## Acceptance Criteria
Unless stated: `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_tests_trigger.py -q`.
- [x] A diff whose only addition is a function/method/class declaration, with no changed test file,
  selects `tests` from `content_triggered_overlays` and, through `overlay_union`, sets
  `include_tests` true — asserted on BOTH a raw diff and its `compose_diff_context` output.
- [x] Parametrised replay over synthetic diffs of each cited shape: SELECT for `d9e0f0e733` (new
  module, 15 added declarations), `721cb7d6ac` (moved declarations, 3), `1c2bf6e57b` (module split,
  22); DO NOT SELECT for `24917e843b` (comment-only source delta, 0 added declarations) or
  `83d91d488c` (annotation-only rewrite; all 8 added names also removed in the same file). An
  added ANONYMOUS declaration selects nothing.
- [x] Portability: an added declaration in a non-Python, non-`src/` file — a Go `func` under
  `internal/`, a TS `export function` under `app/`, a Ruby `class` under `lib/` — selects `tests`,
  while a docs-only diff whose markdown fence holds `def f():` and a config-only diff do NOT.
- [x] A test-file-only diff does not content-select it; a declaration *plus* a `tests/` file still
  selects it by glob (union, not replacement).
- [x] Guard (vii) defines newly-introduced-vs-pre-existing behaviour and "named violating input"
  in diff-decidable terms, with the Four-Criterion Test bullet unchanged; asserted via
  `prompts.get_prompt("code-review-tests")`.
- [x] The `overlay_union` step's `description=` names the added-declaration content trigger, not
  deletion-impact as the only one.
- [x] No regression, no baseline edit: `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py
  tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py
  tests/unit/test_criteria_vocabulary_reviewers.py -q` green with the first two unedited (35 tests),
  `python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` clean, and `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
  reporting `new=0 increased=0` with `registry.py` under `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
baseline.summary: Content-trigger the code-review tests overlay on new src behaviour with no test change
