# Project-supplied review criteria + project-invariant compliance (unified cross-gate registry)

## Context

rebar's review gates ship a fixed, built-in set of criteria. Client projects have their own
standards and invariants — naming, layering, banned APIs, architectural rules — the built-in
set can't express. This epic lets a **project supply its own review criteria** and declare
**architectural invariants** the gates check, **beyond** the built-in set.

**Cross-cutting:** it must serve **plan-review, code-review (`b744`), and any future
criteria-based gate** through **one shared registry**. (Spun out of `5fd2` as follow-on F8;
config-UX sibling `55de`/F5.)

**Posture (from `5fd2`, binding):** coach-not-block, advisory-by-default, **fail-open
(ironclad)**, polyglot / broad client base, convergent-by-construction, **reuse existing
machinery — no plugin system, no new DSL**.

## Design decisions (settled in brainstorm; see rationale comment)

1. **Unified criterion data model + shared registration/discovery/schema/eval plumbing;
   per-gate application** (gate-scoped routing inside the shared record; postures do NOT
   converge).
2. **Two authoring forms, no project code in the gate:** DET "invariants" = declarative
   pattern rules via the existing grounding scan facade; LLM criteria = prompt files.
3. **Any criterion (DET or LLM) may block** — `--force`-escapable, folds into the signed
   (kind-keyed) attestation coverage, can never rebind a built-in.
4. **Blocking is project-owned policy.** rebar surfaces the same eval/calibration instruments
   it uses on its built-ins; the maintainer decides blocking + threshold. Trust is theirs.
5. **Reuse existing formats** (prompt front-matter, the `criteria_routing.json` schema,
   Inspect-AI fixtures, the scan facade). No new formats.
6. **Explicit activation; presence != active.** Routing/threshold in a `.rebar/` overlay
   (§ Overlay schema); namespaced + additive; the overlay may re-tune or **disable** a
   built-in (recorded in coverage).
7. **Eval tooling in scope** = fixture/discrimination harness + calibration/agreement view.
   **Out** = REVIEW_RESULT FP-replay (F1; gate-agnostic, inherited later).
8. **An "invariant" is just a blocking criterion** (usually DET). One mechanism.
9. **Visual editor extended** to author project criteria (reuses `/library/create`).

## Overlay schema, activation & caching (clears E2/G6/T8)

- **File:** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, reusing each gate's packaged `criteria_routing.json`
  schema, keyed by gate:
  `{"plan_review": {"<id>": {…routing…}}, "code_review": {"<id>": {…}}, "activate": ["project.<name>", …]}`.
- **Per-criterion routing** reuses existing keys: plan-review `{exec, applies_at, block_threshold,
  default_posture, facet, checklist}`; code-review `{exec, applies_to (globs), block_threshold,
  blocking_enabled}`. (Note the deliberate posture divergence — plan-review derives blocking
  from `default_posture`; code-review uses an explicit `blocking_enabled`; the shared
  `threshold_for` must honor BOTH — do not "fix" the divergence.) **DET criteria also carry
  `fail_mode: open|closed`** (default `open` for project invariants; `closed` for the built-in
  security class) — see § DET-invariant scan scoping.
- **`exec` vocabulary:** `1-TURN` / `2-STEP` / `AGENT` (LLM tiers) or **`DET`** (pattern-rule
  invariant; code-review already uses `DET` inline). A **DET criterion has no prompt** — descriptor
  assembly must treat prompt resolution as OPTIONAL for `exec: DET` (today `_descriptor_from_prompt`
  unconditionally calls `get_prompt(...)` and raises if absent). A DET criterion's "rubric" is its
  detector rule id (`.rebar/detectors/`), not a `.md`; only its routing entry is required.
  **DET fallback descriptor shape** (a `_descriptor_from_prompt` DET branch that skips
  `get_prompt`): `name` = routing `name` or id; `scenario` = the detector rule's `message`/
  description from its `.rebar/detectors/<id>` envelope; `facet` = routing `facet` (default = id);
  `checklist` = empty. This is an expand-contract change (add the DET branch; existing prompt-backed
  callers unaffected).
- **Namespace / collision (load-time, located error):** a net-new project criterion id MUST be
  `project.<name>`-prefixed. An overlay entry keyed by an **un-prefixed built-in id** is a
  **re-tune/disable** of that built-in (allowed, §Design 6). A `project.`-prefixed id equal to a
  built-in id, or a duplicate project id, is **rejected at load** (a project id can never rebind
  a built-in).
- **Activation:** a criterion runs only if listed in `activate` (presence in the file ≠ active).
- **Discovery — `effective_criteria(repo_root)`** = `CANONICAL_LLM`/`OVERLAY_IDS` ∪ activated
  project ids (each resolved via `get_prompt(id, repo_root)` for its rubric + the overlay routing
  entry). Route it through **every** vocabulary site: plan-review `load_criteria`,
  `check_registry_coverage`, and the **workflow Pass-1 assemble op** (`workflow_ops` emits a
  sanitized `include_project_<name>` boolean — `.`→`_` — per activated project id as the
  coverage/routing record). **LANDED-DESIGN NOTE (ef7e):** the v3 `batch` schema is IMMUTABLE and
  the gate self-validates, so project criteria do NOT fan out via a new workflow field; instead the
  rebar-specific `ProductionBatchRunner` appends the `project.` subset of `route_criteria` to the
  finder set (built-ins keep their static YAML `criteria:` slots, unchanged). Code-review sites
  (`OVERLAY_IDS`, `routing_index`, `threshold_for`) are unified later, after b744 (story 5065).
- **Caching (clears G6 cache bug) — LANDED (ef7e):** `_routing_index()` stays `@lru_cache`d for the
  **packaged** index (immutable per binary); `effective_routing(repo_root)` / `load_criteria` are
  `@lru_cache(maxsize=128)` keyed by `(repo_root, sha256(overlay-bytes))` — a CONTENT signature
  (not mtime), so an overlay edit self-invalidates and cross-repo leakage is impossible;
  `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears them. A RED cross-repo-leak test proves it.

## Attestation & invalidation (clears G6/COH/E1; reuses kind-keyed attest infra)

- **`registry_version(repo_root=None)`** additionally hashes the `.rebar/` overlay when
  `repo_root` is given; thread `repo_root` through **every** caller — `claim_gate_check →
  compute_validity`, and also `drift_refresh_candidate` and `remediation_mode_candidate` (which
  call `registry_version()` today without it) — so activating/editing/disabling a criterion
  **invalidates a prior attestation at claim time** (today it hashes packaged routing only — the
  change does not invalidate).
- **Disable recorded in coverage:** a disabled built-in is listed in a `disabled_builtins: [ids]`
  field in the verdict `coverage` dict (and folded into the signed manifest) so the cert reflects
  reduced coverage rather than silent omission; the field is additive/expand-contract (absent on
  old certs).
- **Cross-gate:** applies to **any gate attestation backed by the shared registry** (plan-review
  now; code-review once it signs — see Migration; code-review signs nothing today).
- **Expand-contract / back-compat:** the new regver basis is additive; an existing attestation
  lacking it is treated as **stale → re-review**, never a crash. Overlay absent ⇒ regver == today
  (no invalidation churn).

## DET-invariant scan scoping & fail-open (clears COH)

- A DET invariant runs as a **whole-repo content scan** via the shared `grounding.engine_b.scan`.
  The **oracle always fails open** (engine binary absent / parse-error / timeout → `abstain`). The
  **consumer** then applies the criterion's **`fail_mode`**: `open` (default for project invariants)
  turns an abstain into a skip = PASS; `closed` (the built-in security class, via the existing
  `apply_failclosed`) turns an abstain into a BLOCK. So generalizing `code_review/detectors.py` =
  making its currently-hardcoded fail-closed behavior a per-criterion `fail_mode` that **defaults
  open** — the two behaviors are one code path parameterized by `fail_mode`, not a contradiction.
  Matches are **gate-scoped**: code-review filters matches to the **diff** (as
  `code_review/detectors.py` already does); plan-review has no diff, so a DET invariant checks the
  plan's declared intent and repo context — an invariant that inherently needs a diff is **N/A at
  plan time (fail-open)** and belongs to code-review.
- Because matches are gate-scoped (diff / plan), pre-existing whole-repo violations are **not**
  surfaced as new work — this is why **no baseline/grandfathering** is needed (reconciles the
  Out-of-scope note).
- **LLM fail-open:** an LLM criterion configured to block whose call errors/times out **fails
  open** (skipped, does not block) — same rule as DET.

- **`apply_failclosed` → `fail_mode` expand-contract (clears T4; story `7f0d`).** The generalization
  is backward-compatible, no flag-day: `apply_failclosed(...)` is KEPT as a thin wrapper that calls
  the new `apply_fail_mode(..., fail_mode="closed")` — so its **default stays `closed`** and every
  existing caller (`code_review/detectors.py`, the built-in security class) is byte-identical until
  explicitly migrated. `detectors.py` is then migrated to call the new function with the
  criterion's routing `fail_mode` (project invariants default `open`, security class `closed`); the
  old wrapper is deprecated and removed only after all callers pass an explicit `fail_mode`.
  **Rollback** = revert callers to the `apply_failclosed` wrapper (still `closed`). No caller's
  behavior changes silently.

## What exists vs. what we build (grounded to file:line, 2026-06-30; incl. b744 worktree)

**Already built (reuse):**
- **Shared three-pass kernel** `review_kernel/` (verify/decide/coach) — **both** gates already
  consume it (code-review via `code_review/workflow_ops.py`); the divergence-risky core is
  already unified.
- **A DET pattern-rule → finding consumer already exists:** `code_review/detectors.py` calls the
  shared `grounding.engine_b.scan` + `load_registry` (which already unions `.rebar/detectors/`) +
  `apply_failclosed` (consumer-side fail-CLOSED; oracle stays fail-OPEN). Generalizable — the only
  hardcoded bits are the `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix + 2 criterion mappings.
- **Per-criterion blocking is DONE:** `code_review/registry.threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3 +
  detector fail-closed.
- **Project extension points:** `.rebar/prompts/` (rubric override), `.rebar/<gate>_moves.json`
  (additive coach moves), `.rebar/detectors/` (project pattern rules), `.rebar/evals/` (fixtures).
- **Kind-keyed attestation infra** (`plan_review/attest.py`); Inspect-AI eval seam; discrimination
  scorers + Cohen's κ + parity metrics.

**Net-new (build):**
- **Open the closed criterion vocabularies** (`CANONICAL_LLM`, `OVERLAY_IDS`) via
  `effective_criteria(repo_root)` — THE precondition; a project criterion is silently skipped
  today regardless of overlay.
- **`.rebar/` routing overlay + activation + cache isolation** (§ Overlay schema).
- **A shared descriptor abstraction:** code-review has only `routing_index()` (raw routing), no
  `load_criteria`-style merged descriptor and no `facet/checklist/…`; unification introduces/
  generalizes one and reconciles the `blocking_enabled` vs `default_posture` postures + exec-tier-
  polymorphic (prompt-less DET vs LLM) criteria.
- **Generalize the DET-scan consumer** beyond the security prefix (data-driven criterion↔detector
  map) so arbitrary project invariants route; make the fail-open/closed behavior a per-criterion
  `fail_mode` (today `apply_failclosed` is hardcoded closed; default project invariants to open);
  expose to plan-review too.
- **Per-criterion eval runner** — `eval_solver.run_case` is a closed 3-id dispatch (raises
  otherwise) + a validate-only CLI; add a criterion-aware runner + a live CLI + the
  **calibration/agreement view** (rendering is net-new; κ/parity metrics exist).
- **Attestation port to code-review** + `registry_version(repo_root)` + disable-coverage +
  claim-gate invalidation (§ Attestation).
- **Editor live must-fire/must-not-fire preview** — a new **synchronous** editor endpoint
  `POST /criterion/preview` `{criterion_id | inline(prompt+routing), fixture}` →
  `{verdict: "fire"|"no-fire", finding?: <findings.py finding shape>, rationale: str}`, reusing
  the per-criterion eval runner behind the `agents` extra + credentials, with a **configurable
  timeout (default 60s)** (no prompt-execution endpoint exists today — the editor's `POST` set is
  `/save`, `/prompt/save`, `/validate`, `/library/create`). **Spike gate:** if a single sync
  preview does not return within the timeout on the reference model, fall back to an async
  job+poll shape rather than blocking the editor's `ThreadingHTTPServer` handler.
- **Routing derivation/validation pipeline** (`criteria_routing.json` is hand-maintained; no
  generator/drift gate).

## Migration & compatibility

- **Callsites** to route through `effective_criteria`: plan-review `load_criteria`,
  `check_registry_coverage`, `attest.registry_version`, `workflow_ops` vocab; code-review
  `OVERLAY_IDS`, `routing_index`, `threshold_for`.
- **Preserve the `review_code` / `code_review/shim.py` `review_result` return shape** — it is a
  back-compat surface consumed by MCP `review_code`, CLI `rebar review-code`, and the Gerrit
  `review_bot/adapter.py`.
- **Rollback = fail-open to packaged:** overlay absent ⇒ both gates behave exactly as today. The
  unification is expand-contract; a misbehaving unified registry falls back per-gate. The
  `registry_version` code change is itself expand-contract (old certs → stale, never crash).
- **Docs deliverable:** an ADR under `docs/adr/` (LANDED: `docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` for the plan-review slice) + a `CLAUDE.md` "project-supplied criteria"
  section document the unified registry contract, the overlay merge/activation semantics, and the
  attestation-invalidation protocol, plus a how-to for authoring/activating/eval'ing/blocking on a
  criterion (the concrete target for the docs AC).

## Build order (risk-ordered MVP; clears G5 thin-slice)

Prove the full loop on the riskiest piece first, then fan out:
1. **MVP slice — ✅ DONE (story `ef7e`, PR #103).** `effective_criteria`/`effective_routing`
   (content-hash cache isolation) → activate ONE project LLM criterion from the `.rebar/` overlay →
   `ProductionBatchRunner` fans it into Pass-1 → surfaces its finding; CI parity gate + ADR 0015.
   (The `registry_version`-reflects-the-overlay + attestation-invalidation half is split into story
   `08af`, step 6 below — this slice proved author→activate→run→surface.)
2. Generalize the DET-invariant scan consumer (data-driven map).
3. Per-criterion eval runner + calibration view.
4. Editor live-preview + authoring extension.
5. **Unify** plan-review + code-review registries into `rebar.llm.criteria` (after `b744` lands).

## Dependency

**Blocked on `b744`** (code-review; WS1–WS5 landed on `worktree-code-review-capability`, WS6 =
Gerrit voter pending). The `review_kernel` is already shared; the remaining fork is the
registry/descriptor + posture + vocabulary layer, unified after b744 lands (temporary
duplication accepted).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `effective_criteria(repo_root)` opens the closed vocabularies (`CANONICAL_LLM` +
      `OVERLAY_IDS`) so an activated project criterion is loaded/run by the gate; routed through
      every vocabulary callsite (see Migration).
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay per the § Overlay schema: gate-keyed, namespaced,
      explicit `activate` list, load-time collision/rebind rejection (a located error).
- [ ] Overlay merge is cache-isolated per repo (packaged index stays cached; overlay is not); a
      RED test proves no cross-repo routing leakage.
- [ ] The overlay may re-tune or disable a built-in; a disable is recorded in attestation coverage.
- [ ] Project DET pattern-rule invariants run through the generalized (data-driven)
      `engine_b.scan` consumer and surface as blocking-capable findings; fail-open on
      engine-binary-absent / parse-error / timeout per the criterion's `fail_mode` (default `open`
      → skip = PASS; security-class `closed` → block).
- [ ] Project LLM prompt criteria run through the shared registry with gate-scoped routing; an
      LLM-block criterion that errors fails open. … [truncated by reconciler]
- [ ] A project can add its own criteria (DET pattern-rules + LLM prompts) that run in plan-review,
- [ ] A project can declare architectural invariants (blocking DET criteria) the gates check.
- [ ] The project **owns blocking/threshold policy** per criterion, informed by the same
- [ ] **No project code executes in the gate**; unsupported stacks fail open.
baseline.summary: Project-supplied review criteria + project-invariant compliance (unified cross-gate registry)

baseline.description:
# Retire `rebar review`: alias the verb to `review-plan`, deprecate the library/MCP surfaces

## Context / Problem

`rebar review` runs a single-pass LLM ticket review that no longer earns its keep. Its CLI intercept (`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:477-478` → `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:148`) is the only first-class product surface it has; the MCP tool (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:46`) already refuses to run unless `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:69-72`); and the ground it covers is taken from above by the signed `review-plan` gate and from below by the LLM-free `clarity-check` / `check-ac` / `quality-check`.

**The operator has decided to retire it.** This ticket is the safe execution of that decision, not a re-evaluation. The people affected are agents and operators who read `rebar review` in `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md` and `AGENTS.md` and script it: today they are pointed at a command that is going away, and a naive alias would silently accept `--graph` and a positional `reviewer_id` that the target verb cannot honour, and would silently start writing a signed attestation where the old verb wrote nothing.

## Approach

Turn `rebar review` into a **loud deprecation shim over `review-plan`** that preserves the old verb's read-only, unsigned semantics, and deprecate — without deleting — the library and MCP surfaces. The library function is a public API (`rebar.llm.review_ticket`, exported at `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:46` and listed in `__all__` at `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:73`), so deleting it in the same change would be an unannounced breaking change for external importers; the announce-then-remove split is what makes the retirement safe.

The whole deprecation runs through the mechanism rebar already has: the central registry in `src/rebar/_deprecations.py`. `warn_deprecated()` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:310`) looks its key up in `REGISTRY` and **raises `KeyError`** when the surface is not catalogued, and `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py:126` source-scans for raw `is deprecated` / `DeprecationWarning` emissions that bypass the helper. A hand-rolled `sys.stderr.write` would fail CI, so routing through the registry is both the cheapest path and the enforced one. The registry already models the kinds needed — `_KINDS` is `{"env","cfg","cli","lib","mcp"}` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:44`).

### The five in-source call sites of `review_ticket`

Enumerated by grep over `src/rebar`, because the rest of the plan depends on the list being complete:

1. `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:192` — the CLI `_review` body (**replaced** by the shim).
2. `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:75` — the MCP tool body (**kept**; emits the `mcp` signal and calls the
   private impl).
3. `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:22` — a docstring example, not a call (**reworded**).
4. `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py:86` — the legacy leg of `diff_review_paths`, the
   parallel-run-and-diff harness declared at `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py:70` (**kept, must
   not warn**).
5. `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:310` — the eval harness's solver arm (**kept, must not
   warn**).

Sites 4 and 5 are internal harnesses, not user surfaces; a `DeprecationWarning` fired from them would be noise in eval output and, worse, would train readers to ignore the warning. So `review_ticket` splits into a private `_review_ticket_impl(...)` holding today's body, plus the public `review_ticket(...)` = emit the `lib` deprecation, then delegate. **Sites 2, 4 and 5 all call the private impl.** Site 2 is included deliberately: the MCP tool emits its own `mcp` signal, so if its body kept calling the public `review_ticket` a single tool invocation would fire two overlapping deprecation signals. One surface, one signal. This is a three-caller split, so it is the minimum structure that gets each warning onto exactly one boundary.

Outside `src/rebar`, roughly fourteen test call sites invoke the public `rebar.llm.review_ticket` directly (`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_ops_characterization.py:32,47,77`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py:100,124,148`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_budget.py:62,84`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py:666,715,735,746`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:122`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py:212`, plus `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py:180` and `tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py:417` on `operations.review_ticket`). **None of them need editing**: pytest is configured with only `addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"` and no `filterwarnings` key (`pyproject.toml:508-515`), so a `DeprecationWarning` is recorded, not raised. They are the coverage that proves the public op still behaves identically after the split, and they are run as-is (see Testing).

### The six moves

**1. `_review` becomes a forwarder.** `_review` (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:148-203`) keeps its own `argparse` parser so it can reject the two arguments that have no counterpart on the target verb, then calls `_review_plan(...)` (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:434`) and returns its exit code unchanged. `--output` / `--check` / `--ref` / `--source` exist on both verbs and are forwarded verbatim.

**2. The shim forwards `--no-sign`, so the bare verb keeps its read-only semantics.** This is the one behavioural trap in the alias: the old `rebar review <id>` wrote nothing, while `review-plan` signs an attestation that gates `claim`. `_review_plan` already exposes `--no-sign` (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:462`, threaded as `sign=not args.no_sign` at `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:521`), so the shim passes it unconditionally. A caller who scripted `rebar review <id>` therefore writes nothing, exactly as before, and earning an attestation stays an explicit `rebar review-plan <id>`. That removes the silent state side-effect instead of merely documenting it, and the rollback is the same one the whole change has: the deprecated surfaces still work, so reverting the shim commit restores the old verb.

The shim does **not** pass `--force`, and that leaves one behavioural divergence that is accepted and documented rather than papered over: `review-plan` fast-fails to `INDETERMINATE` (exit 2) with no LLM call on a ticket that is not claimable — `closed`/`idea`/`blocked`, or `open` but still blocked by an unclosed prerequisite — whereas the old verb would have run the model and returned findings. Worked example:

```
$ rebar review <a-closed-ticket>      # old: exit 0, findings JSON on stdout
$ rebar review <a-closed-ticket>      # new: exit 2, INDETERMINATE, no LLM call
$ echo $?
2
```

Auto-forwarding `--force` would be worse than the divergence: it would spend a full multi-pass gate run on a ticket the gate deliberately refuses, and `--force` is the audited escape hatch, not a default. The divergence is therefore stated in `rebar review --help` and asserted by a test, so a scripted caller sees exit 2 with an explanation instead of a mystery.

**3. `--graph` and a positional `reviewer_id` FAIL LOUDLY.** Both are declared on the current parser (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:163-172`) and neither exists on `review-plan`. Each is rejected with `parser.error(...)` — argparse exit code 2 — with a message naming what to use instead. Worked example, the exact required behaviour:

```
$ rebar review 316a --graph
rebar review: error: --graph is not supported by `rebar review-plan`, which reviews one
ticket. Review each ticket in dependency order instead.
$ echo $?
2
```

Silently accepting and discarding an argument that changes what the command means is the defect class this ticket exists to avoid.

**4. Register three deprecation rows** in `_ENTRIES` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:73`): a `cli` row for `rebar review`, a `lib` row for `rebar.llm.review_ticket`, and an `mcp` row for the `review_ticket` tool — all three replaced by the plan-review verb/tool. All three use `_scheduled(...)` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:62`), **not** `_permanent(...)`. The registry states the deciding rule at `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:88-99`: a *rename* of the same knob is permanent, while a **supersession by a different interface** is scheduled, because the old surface is meant to go away. `review` → `review-plan` is a supersession — the replacement signs, enforces a blocking floor, and fast-fails on a non-claimable ticket — so `_scheduled` applies, with its default `remove_in=_MAJOR` (`v1.0.0`, `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:48`). Emission channels follow the ones `warn_deprecated` documents per site type (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:326-334`): `via="stderr"` for the CLI parse-boundary signal, `via="warning"` (a `DeprecationWarning`) for the library entry point, and the default `via="log"` for the MCP tool.

**5. Keep the reviewer prompt and the two shared helpers.** `select_reviewers` and `assemble_context` (`src/rebar/llm/operations.py:25`) are untouched — `assemble_context` is a documented public entry point used by the completion gate. `ticket_quality.md` and its `"default": true` catalog entry (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json:79-91`) are **kept**: `default_reviewer_id()` raises `LLMError` when no catalog entry is marked default (`src/rebar/llm/operations.py:36-45`) and it is called from `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py:52`, so removing the default entry would break an unrelated caller. Only its `description` string — currently "The default reviewer for the `review` operation" (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json:82`) — is corrected to name the library op rather than the retired CLI verb.

**6. Repoint the output schema.** `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["review"]` maps to `REVIEW_RESULT` (`src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:303`) and is that schema's **only** wiring (`REVIEW_RESULT` appears at `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:61,110,303` and nowhere else). Once `rebar review` emits a plan-review verdict, that key maps to `PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT`, and `review_result` is re-wired under a synthetic `"review_ticket"` key for the surviving library/MCP surface — exactly the pattern already used for `"enrich"`, `"overlap_judge"` and `"review_code_gate"` (`src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:313-327`). Without that re-wiring the orphan guard in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py:38-49` fails.

## Scope

Source:

- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — `_review` becomes the forwarding shim (with `--no-sign` and
  the two hard rejections). The intercept at `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:477` keeps dispatching to
  it unchanged, so that file is not edited.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — three new `_scheduled` rows in `_ENTRIES`.
- `src/rebar/llm/operations.py` — split into `_review_ticket_impl` + a warning `review_ticket`.
- `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py` — line 86 calls `_review_ticket_impl`.
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` — line 310 calls `_review_ticket_impl`.
- `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py` — the module docstring (lines 4, 22) stops presenting `review_ticket`
  as the reference operation and points at the plan-review gate; the export itself stays.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py` — the `review_ticket` tool emits the `mcp` deprecation, calls
  `_review_ticket_impl` (so it does not also fire the `lib` warning), and its docstring names
  `review_plan` as the replacement; the tool stays registered.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` — the `ticket-quality` description string (line 82).
- `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` — `"review"` → `PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT`, plus the synthetic
  `"review_ticket"` → `REVIEW_RESULT` key.

Tests (every existing site that exercises the old CLI contract, found by grepping `tests` for `cli._review` and `main(["review"`):

- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_ref_source_surfaces.py` — `_MAPPING` (line 21) and the
  `cli._review` calls at lines 83-84, 139, 165, 169. The CLI-side ref/source assertion moves from
  the `review_ticket` capture to the `review_plan` capture; the MCP-side assertions over the
  `review_ticket` tool (lines 33-40) are unchanged, because the tool still exists.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py` — `main(["review","--check"])` (line 765) still
  works via the forwarded `--check`; `test_cli_review_with_fake_runner` (line 784) must now validate
  against `plan_review_verdict`, not `REVIEW_RESULT`; `test_cli_review_bad_reviewer_is_graceful`
  (line 802) passes a positional reviewer and must now expect exit 2 from the rejection.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:207` — `main(["review","--check"])`, forwarded.
- `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py` — coverage for the three new rows.
- `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` —
  `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN["llm/operations.py::review_ticket"]` (lines 265-270) and the docstring of
  `test_review_ticket_uses_the_operators_configured_model` (lines 167-172) justify the entry as
  "`rebar review`'s PRIMARY op call". After this change `rebar review` no longer calls it, so the
  registered reason is rewritten to justify the surviving library/MCP op. The entry and the test are
  **kept**, because the function is kept; the analysed site becomes `_review_ticket_impl`, so the
  key is renamed to match.
- `tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py` — new.

Docs:

- `docs/llm-framework.md` — the `rebar review` occurrences at lines 24-25, 148-152, 283-285, 390.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — the `review` row at line 478.
- `docs/output-schemas.md` — the `review` → `review_result` row at line 57 and the exemption
  paragraph at lines 173-179, both of which become false after move 6.
- `AGENTS.md` — the LLM-operations pointer at line 149, which lists `review` as an operation.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py`:

- **Happy path** — `cli._review([tid])` invokes the plan-review path (patched) and returns its exit
  code; the deprecation line is on stderr.
- **The no-sign contract** — the patched `review_plan` call records `sign=False`, proving the bare
  verb still writes no attestation, and records no `force` argument.
- **Non-claimable divergence** — `cli._review([closed_tid])` returns 2 and does not call the LLM,
  matching the documented fast-fail.
- **Edge / hard failure** — `cli._review([tid, "--graph"])` raises `SystemExit(2)` and its stderr
  names `review-plan`; likewise `cli._review([tid, "ticket-quality"])` for the positional
  `reviewer_id`. These are the two behaviours a silent alias would get wrong.
- **Registry** — `warn_deprecated("cli:rebar review")` returns a message rather than raising, and
  the same for the `lib` and `mcp` keys; a scheduled row's message contains "scheduled for removal"
  per `_message()` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:299-306`).
- **Library surface intact** — calling `rebar.llm.review_ticket` still works and emits a
  `DeprecationWarning` (`pytest.warns`), while `_review_ticket_impl` called directly emits none
  (`warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` is empty) — that pair is what keeps the MCP tool, the eval
  harness and the diff harness from double-signalling.

Regression suites this change can break, run explicitly: `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py`, `tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_ref_source_surfaces.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py`, `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`.

And, unedited, the fourteen existing direct callers of the public op listed in Approach — `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_ops_characterization.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_budget.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py` and `tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py` — which are the in-session proof that splitting `review_ticket` did not change its behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar review <id>` runs the plan-review gate and returns its exit code; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py::test_review_forwards_to_review_plan`.
- [x] The bare verb writes **no** attestation: the shim passes `sign=False` through to
      `review_plan`; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py::test_shim_forwards_no_sign`, which asserts the
      recorded kwarg is `sign=False`.
- [x] `rebar review <id> --graph` and `rebar review <id> <reviewer_id>` each exit **2** with a
      message containing the string `review-plan`, rather than being accepted and ignored; verified
      by `pytest tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py::test_graph_rejected` and
      `::test_positional_reviewer_rejected`.
- [x] Three rows — `cli:rebar review`, `lib:rebar.llm.review_ticket`, `mcp:review_ticket` — exist in
      `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY`, each with `permanent=False` and `remove_in == "v1.0.0"`;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py`, which also enforces that no
      emission site bypasses `warn_deprecated`.
- [x] `rebar.llm.review_ticket` still resolves and emits a `DeprecationWarning` when called, and the
      three internal call sites (`_mcp_llm.py:75`, `review_workflows.py:86`, `eval_solver.py:310`)
      emit none;
      verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py::test_public_warns_impl_is_silent`.
- [x] `rebar review --help` states the four differences a caller will notice — plan-review signs an
      attestation (which this shim suppresses with `--no-sign`), enforces a blocking floor,
      fast-fails with no LLM on a non-claimable ticket, and costs a multi-pass gate run; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py::test_help_states_the_behaviour_differences`,
      which asserts the help text contains all four anchors: `attestation`, `blocking`, `fast-fail` and
      `multi-pass`.
- [x] `rebar review <closed-or-blocked-id>` exits **2** without an LLM call and its stderr explains
      the fast-fail; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py::test_non_claimable_fast_fails`, which asserts the
      exit code is 2 and the patched runner recorded zero calls.
- [x] The fourteen existing direct callers of `rebar.llm.review_ticket` listed in Approach still
      pass **unedited**, proving the impl split is behaviour-preserving; verified by

The close-time gate + signing integration. Optional (`verify.require_completion_verification_for_close`, default off). On a non-force close: verify → close → **sign on PASS** (verify→close→sign ordering, BL-5); FAIL/missing-LLM → fail-closed block; `--force-close` → close without sign (withhold the confirmation).

## Scope (files)
- `src/rebar/config.py`: `VerifyConfig.require_completion_verification_for_close: bool=False` + `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer.
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`: factor `bug_close_reason_ok(reason)` shared predicate.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`: read ticket_type; `_completion_precheck` (outside lock; lazy `rebar.llm` import; `except Exception`→fail-closed; bug-reason precheck) BEFORE `transition_core`; sign via `signing.sign_manifest` AFTER a confirmed close; force-close skips verify+sign; update audit-comment wording.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] flag off → no verify call; flag on + PASS → close + SIGNATURE event (verify_signature==certified) AFTER the STATUS event
- [ ] FAIL → CommandError, no SIGNATURE, ticket stays open; missing-extra/any-exception → fail-closed block
- [ ] `--force-close` → closes, no SIGNATURE; ConcurrencyMismatch → no orphan SIGNATURE
- [ ] gate is alternatives-not-composed with `_signature_gate` (documented); when ENABLED but the LLM is unavailable it fails CLOSED; an UNREADABLE config fails this (opt-in) gate OFF with a warning — it must NOT preempt the signature gate or auto-enable across repos (refined during implementation; see commit)

baseline.description:
# S7 — End-to-end proof + backup/restore drill + monitoring + runbooks

## Why
Prove the whole gate works end-to-end and that freeze-and-restore is real. This is the
dogfood-readiness checkpoint for d251 (P1 integrity proven on a real change; P3 restore
proven). The full four-pass dogfood is b744-WS6.

## What
- **E2E proof:** push a change -> the bot reviews + votes `LLM-Review` -> submit
  (whole-topic) -> replicate -> the change appears on GitHub `main`; AND a direct GitHub
  push / PR-merge to `main` is rejected.
  - **`LLM-Review` label-integer vocabulary (so the e2e test can assert a concrete value).**
    The `LLM-Review` label gates CODE merges, so the review-bot casts it from the
    **CODE-review verdict** (`PASS`/`BLOCK`, see `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py`)
    of the change under review. The e2e test asserts the integer for a *passing*
    change. The mapping the test must assume: a passing CODE review votes **MAX** (the value
    `label:LLM-Review=MAX` resolves to in d251's `project.config` label range — the e2e
    test reads the achieved label value from Gerrit and asserts it equals that range's MAX,
    rather than hardcoding `+1` vs `+2`), which is what makes the change submit-enabling;
    a blocking CODE review casts a non-MAX value (the label's MIN, e.g. -1, fail-closed) so
    Gerrit refuses submit. The exact integers are pinned by d251's `project.config` label
    definition — this AC cross-references that, so the e2e test and the project config agree
    on MAX/MIN by construction rather than by a guessed literal.
  - **No-vote / blocked fallback (e2e harness robustness).** The e2e test script must
    bound the wait for the `LLM-Review` vote with an explicit timeout and must distinguish
    three terminal states: (a) **MAX vote + submit succeeds** = pass; (b) **non-MAX (MIN)
    vote** (a blocking CODE review, fail-closed) = "gate correctly blocked" (expected only in
    the negative-path sub-test, a failure in the positive path); (c) **no vote within the
    timeout** = "voter/harness failed" — surfaced as a distinct, non-ambiguous harness error,
    NOT silently conflated with a correctly-blocked change. This makes a model
    outage/timeout during the drill diagnosable rather than a hang.
- **Backup/restore — two snapshot tiers (reconciled).** (a) ROUTINE RPO safety net: DLM takes
  scheduled, **crash-consistent** EBS snapshots of the data volume — these are NOT
  application-quiesced, which is acceptable because Gerrit's NoteDb is git (crash-consistent and
  recoverable, `git fsck` on restore). (b) ON-DEMAND QUIESCED snapshot: before a PLANNED restore
  drill / upgrade / migration, briefly stop the Gerrit container (or set it read-only), take the
  snapshot, restart — so that restore source is application-consistent. `index/` + `cache/` are
  rebuildable and excluded from any `$site_path` archive. Run the restore-from-IaC drill (on a
  separate instance, per the safety bullet) and record the achieved RTO; merged code is always
  safe on GitHub (RPO = only in-flight reviews since the last snapshot, bounded by the DLM interval).
  - **RTO target (pre-stated, not circular).** A numeric **RTO target of ≤ 2 hours** is the
    pass/fail bound, agreed *before* the drill and documented in the restore runbook. The
    drill records the *achieved* RTO and passes only if it is within that 2-hour target
    (the target is the baseline; the achieved time is measured against it). 2 h is the
    starting target for this single-instance, IaC-rebuild + `$site_path`-restore topology;
    the runbook may revise it for a later drill, but a drill never sets its own target.
  - **Snapshot retention.** The DLM lifecycle policy carries a bounded retention
    (`retain_rule { count = N }`, default **N = 7**) and the `$site_path` snapshots carry an
    equivalent TTL/count so snapshots do not accumulate unbounded; the restore runbook states
    how to identify the latest valid snapshot for a drill.
  - **Restore-drill safety (non-destructive by construction).** The restore DRILL provisions
    a SEPARATE, throwaway instance + volume RESTORED FROM THE LATEST SNAPSHOT (a scratch
    Terraform workspace / a `-var` toggle) and verifies Gerrit boots and the data is intact
    THERE — the live production volume is never detached, mutated, or replaced during a drill,
    so a failed drill cannot endanger production. Defense-in-depth: the live data volume
    carries `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. **Back-out:** a failed drill is unwound by
    terminating the throwaway instance/volume (the live system is untouched). For the genuine
    disaster-recovery case (where you DO replace the live volume), the runbook documents a
    back-out — detach-but-RETAIN the old volume, attempt the restore, and re-attach the
    retained original at the same device path if the restore fails — performed only after a
    plan review that removes `prevent_destroy`.
- **Monitoring:** CloudWatch basic + an alarm on "gate down" (Gerrit/MCP unreachable) so an
  outage — which freezes `main` — is noticed.
  - **Probe mechanism (resolves the no-ALB / plain-EC2 gap).** Because d251 excludes an ALB,
    CloudWatch has no native HTTP-reachability metric for the on-box services. The plan pins
    one concrete mechanism: a **cron/systemd-timer health probe on the EC2 host** runs every
    60 s, curls Gerrit (`curl -sf http://localhost:8080/config/server/version`) and the MCP
    health endpoint, and publishes a binary custom metric via
    `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace Rebar/Gate --metric-name GerritReachable
    --value 1|0`. The `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` in `monitoring.tf` fires when
    `GerritReachable < 1` for **2 consecutive 60 s periods**, and sets
    **`treat_missing_data = breaching`** so that if the on-box probe itself stops publishing
    (e.g. the host crashed and the timer is dead) the alarm transitions to **ALARM**, not the
    CloudWatch default `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` — a host crash that silences the probe must raise
    an alert, not go unnoticed. This detects process/port-level gate-down (a Gerrit/MCP crash
    the probe can still report). **Host-crash backstop:** because a hard host failure also
    kills the probe, a second `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` on the EC2
    `StatusCheckFailed_System` / `StatusCheckFailed_Instance` metric (AWS-published, independent
    of the on-box probe) backs the probe alarm so a dead host is detected even if the
    `treat_missing_data` path were missed. Both alarms point at the same SNS topic. The probe
    script and the metric namespace/name are the explicit interface contract documented in the
    monitoring runbook so a Gerrit upgrade that moves the health path is a known, versioned
    change point.
  - **Notification delivery (so an outage is actually noticed).** The alarm's `alarm_actions`
    point at an **SNS topic** whose subscription endpoint is the team alert target
    (email/Slack/PagerDuty). The endpoint is stored in **SSM Parameter Store** (consistent
    with d251's secrets-at-boot pattern) and read via `data.aws_ssm_parameter` in
    `monitoring.tf` — not committed as a plaintext `.tfvars` value. An alarm with empty
    `alarm_actions` does not satisfy this story.
  - **IAM scope.** Enumerate the minimum IAM actions the new resources need — CloudWatch
    (`PutMetricAlarm`/`PutMetricData`/`DescribeAlarms`), DLM (the snapshot lifecycle role with
    `ec2:CreateSnapshot`/`ec2:DescribeVolumes` scoped to the data volume), SNS
    (`CreateTopic`/`Publish`) — scoped to the specific resources (no `cloudwatch:*`/`dlm:*`
    wildcards), added to the existing instance profile or a dedicated scoped DLM role.
- **Terraform state.** `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf` uses the **shared remote backend**
  established by the earlier infra stories (S3 state + DynamoDB locking, `us-east-1`), not
  local state, so concurrent applies during a drill cannot corrupt state; the runbook makes
  `terraform plan` (reviewed) a required step before `apply`.
- **Runbooks:** provision/restore + the one-minor-at-a-time Gerrit upgrade.
- **Sequencing (de-risk order).** Execute E2E proof first (validates the live gate) ->
  monitoring alarm (observability of that gate) -> restore drill (recoverability) ->
  runbooks (document the above); each step is evidence-gated on the previous.

## Scope
In: the e2e proof, the restore drill, monitoring, runbooks. Out: the full four-pass
dogfood (b744-WS6); choosing the *final* alarm threshold/period tuning and the *final*
RTO target beyond the stated starting values (operational tuning, left to the implementer
within the mechanism/bounds fixed here).

## Files
- `infra/runbooks/*.md` — provision/restore runbook (includes RTO target, snapshot
  identification, `prevent_destroy` handling, `terraform plan`-before-`apply`) and the
  one-minor-at-a-time Gerrit upgrade runbook (documents the probe health-endpoint contract).
- `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf` — CloudWatch alarm (`GerritReachable < 1` for 2 periods)
  + SNS topic/subscription (endpoint from SSM) + DLM snapshot lifecycle policy
  (`retain_rule.count = 7`) + scoped IAM; uses the shared S3+DynamoDB backend; adds/asserts
  `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` on the stateful data-volume resource.
- The host health-probe script (cron/systemd timer) publishing the `Rebar/Gate/GerritReachable`
  custom metric (co-located with the host provisioning assets).
- An e2e test script under `infra/tests/` (push->review->vote->submit->replicate assertion,
  the negative-path GitHub-direct-push-rejected assertion, the `LLM-Review`=MAX label-value
  assertion read against `project.config`, and the timeout/terminal-state fallback logic).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] E2E proof passes: a test change is reviewed + voted + submitted in Gerrit and appears on
      GitHub `main`; the e2e test asserts the cast `LLM-Review` value equals the label range's
      MAX (as defined in d251 `project.config`); a direct GitHub push / PR-merge to `main` is
      rejected. The test bounds the vote wait with a timeout and reports "no vote / harness
      failure" distinctly from "gate correctly blocked."
- [ ] A restore-from-backup drill succeeds on a SEPARATE throwaway instance/volume restored
      from the latest snapshot (the live production volume is never detached/mutated during the
      drill), within the **pre-stated ≤ 2-hour RTO target**, with the achieved RTO recorded;
      the drill's restore source is an ON-DEMAND QUIESCED snapshot (Gerrit briefly stopped/
      read-only before the snapshot) and excludes `index/` and `cache/`; routine RPO snapshots
      are scheduled crash-consistent DLM snapshots (git-recoverable via `fsck`) — the two tiers
      are reconciled, not contradictory; merged history is confirmed intact on GitHub. The live
      data volume carries `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`, and
      the restore runbook documents a back-out (terminate the throwaway on a failed drill; for
      real DR, detach-but-retain the original and re-attach on failure).
- [ ] A gate-down condition raises an alert: the host probe publishes the
      `Rebar/Gate/GerritReachable` custom metric, and the CloudWatch alarm fires
      (`GerritReachable < 1` for 2 consecutive periods) and delivers a notification via its
      SNS topic to the configured (SSM-sourced) endpoint — `alarm_actions` is non-empty and a
      simulated gate-down delivers an actual notification. The probe alarm sets
      `treat_missing_data = breaching`, and a simulated **host-down** (the probe stops
      publishing entirely, as in a host crash) also raises an alert — both via the probe
      alarm going to ALARM on missing data and via a dedicated EC2
      `StatusCheckFailed_System`/`StatusCheckFailed_Instance` alarm backstop — rather than
      sitting silently in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`.
- [ ] A DLM/`$site_path` snapshot retention policy is in effect (DLM `retain_rule.count`
      bounded; default 7) so snapshots do not accumulate unbounded, and IAM for the new
      monitoring/DLM/SNS resources is scoped to specific resources (no wildcard actions).
- [ ] Provision/restore + Gerrit upgrade runbooks exist under `infra/runbooks/`, documenting
      the RTO target, snapshot identification, the probe health-endpoint contract, the
      `prevent_destroy` removal procedure, and `terraform plan`-before-`apply` on the shared
      remote backend.

## Round-7 remediation
- **SNS alert endpoint SSM path (E2):** the SNS subscription endpoint is stored in SSM at **`/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint`** (read via `data.aws_ssm_parameter` in `monitoring.tf`, not a plaintext tfvar).
- **review_code decision rule (G6):** `rebar.llm.review_code()` returns a `review_result` (a `findings` list), NOT a verdict string. The receiver derives a binary decision: **BLOCK if any finding is at/above a configured blocking severity (default critical/high), else PASS** -> PASS->label MAX, BLOCK or error/no-result->-1 (fail-closed); the threshold is config-driven. b744-WS6 swaps in `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` (typed `{verdict: PASS|BLOCK}`), removing the derivation.
- [ ] `monitoring.tf` reads the SNS endpoint from SSM `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint`, and the e2e asserts the receiver's derived PASS/BLOCK decision maps to the LLM-Review MAX/non-MAX value.

## Round-12 addition (manual re-review / `/rerun` runbook)
S4b adds a token-authenticated manual re-review endpoint on the review-bot receiver
(`POST /rerun?change=<id>`, reached via nginx at `/review/rerun`) that FORCE re-reviews a
change — bypassing the dedup + existing-vote short-circuits — so an operator can recover a
change stuck at a fail-closed `-1` (e.g. from a transient LLM outage) WITHOUT amending the
patchset. It is still fail-closed (a rerun only requests a FRESH review; it can never force a
PASS). This MUST be clearly documented in S7's runbooks so a rebar developer/operator can find
it and use it.

Added AC:
- [ ] The `infra/runbooks/` runbooks include a clear, discoverable "manually re-run a review"
      section documenting the `/rerun` endpoint: WHERE it lives (the review-bot receiver, via
      nginx `/review/rerun`), HOW to call it (the exact authenticated `curl` with the
      `?token=` secret sourced from SSM `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` and the `change` id),
      WHEN to use it (recover a change stuck at a fail-closed `-1`; vs. the automatic 5-minute
      backfill reconciler which only re-reviews vote-LESS changes), and that it is fail-closed
      (requests a fresh review, never forces a PASS). Cross-referenced from ADR-0009.

## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-30 — internal sequencing + advisory fixes)
**Blocking — internal phasing (the story stays single, executed in verified phases):**
- **Phase A — live gate validation (e2e + monitoring):** prove the chain end-to-end
  (Gerrit review->vote->submit -> replicate), and stand up the CloudWatch alarms
  (GerritReachable gate-down + EC2 status-check host-down + SNS to the SSM alert-endpoint).
  Verified before Phase B.
- **Phase B — recoverability (backup/restore drill + runbooks):** the non-destructive EBS
  snapshot restore drill, and the runbooks (provision/restore, Gerrit upgrade, the `/rerun`
  manual re-review). Gated on Phase A green.
(Each phase is independently verifiable; this satisfies the structural-readiness concern without
splitting the ticket — the same phasing pattern used in S1/S2.)

**Advisory fixes folded in:**
- **Code-review verdict source (correction):** the PASS/BLOCK decision comes from S4b's
  `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py::code_review_decision` over `rebar.llm.review_code()`'s
  findings + the severity threshold (config `BLOCKING_SEVERITIES`, default {critical,high} in
  `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py`) — NOT a `decide.py`/`review_kernel`. b744-WS6 later swaps the
  internals behind the same adapter signature.
- **Replication BSL:** S7 relies on S5's already-proven Apache-2.0 core `replication` push plugin
  (cited in ADR-0010); no new license dependency in S7.
- **Snapshot retention ownership:** S1 OWNS the DLM policy (`retain_rule.count`=7, default) +
  the DLM role; S7 only ASSERTS/monitors it (no second DLM resource). `monitoring.tf` likewise
  only ASSERTS the data volume's `prevent_destroy` (S1 set it) — it does not manage the volume.
- **Probe deployment pinned:** the host health probe is `infra/scripts/observability.sh`,
  installed as the `rebar-observability.timer` systemd timer by
  `infra/scripts/install-observability.sh` (every 5 min) — already deployed in S2/S5.
- **Apply-prove-rollback scope (consistent with S6):** the operator chose apply-prove-rollback
  for the GitHub lock, so the e2e proof does NOT permanently advance `navapbc/rebar` `main` nor
  leave it locked. The full chain is proven on a TEST ref / transiently (Gerrit submit ->
  replicate -> appears on GitHub on a deletable test branch; the lock's direct-push/PR-merge
  rejection was already proven in S6). The main-advancing + permanent-lock cutover e2e is the
  documented cutover step (S6 runbook), deferred per the chosen scope.

baseline.description:
## Dependencies (STACKED — review with --ref HEAD)
Builds on **4e9d** (event `author_id`), **bde5** (`sign_authorship`/`verify_authorship`), **e165** (`verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`) — all committed on this branch, not yet on origin/main. Review with `--ref HEAD`.

## Context
Project-opt-in enforcement of authenticated authorship. The real control is a MERGE-GATE (CI-side verification, mirroring the `verify.require_ticket_for_commit` gate in `verify_commit.py`); the local write-gate is UX-only convenience. Replay NEVER rejects — a bad-signature event still folds — and snapshots carry folded identities+signatures so compacted signed events still verify.

## Why
Cryptographic authorship is only trustworthy if something verifies it before code lands. Enforcing at the merge-gate (not at replay) keeps the store always-readable (no clone can be bricked by an unverifiable event) while still blocking unauthenticated history from landing on the protected branch when a project opts in.

## What
### 1. Config `[identity]` section (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`)
- `identity.require_authenticated: bool = False` (default OFF; opt-in), with the same
  `_as_bool` coercion pattern as `verify.require_ticket_for_commit` (line 459).
- `identity.signing_key: str | None = None` — path to the local identity's SSH PRIVATE
  key used to sign events at write time (optional; unset → events are written unsigned).

### 2. Optional write-time event signing (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`)
In `append_event`, AFTER the attribution fields (4e9d) are stamped: when a current identity resolves AND `identity.signing_key` is configured, sign the event's CANONICAL bytes (`canonical.canonical_str(event-without-author_sig).encode()`) via `authorship.sign_authorship(payload, signing_key, principal=<author_id>)` and store the DSSE-encoded envelope as `author_sig` on the event envelope. Best-effort: no key / no identity → the event is written UNSIGNED (no `author_sig`). Signing must never break a write (a signing failure logs + writes unsigned). Sign at the SAME single seam; the canonical payload EXCLUDES `author_sig` itself (self-reference), mirroring the HMAC unsigned-hint pattern.

### 3. Write-gate (UX-only, fail-fast)
When `identity.require_authenticated` is ON and a write cannot be signed (no resolvable identity or no `signing_key`), `append_event` fails fast with a clear message directing the user to configure their identity/key. This is DOCUMENTED as UX-only — a local convenience that a determined user can bypass; it is NOT the security boundary. (Gate- and lifecycle-exempt types — session_log/code_review/identity — are exempt, like the other write gates.)

### 4. Merge-gate (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` + CLI `rebar verify-authorship`)
The real control, mirroring `verify_commit.py`. For the events introduced by a commit range (default: the range CI verifies) — or the whole store with `--all` — verify EACH mutating event: it must carry an `author_id` referencing an existing `identity`, and an `author_sig` that `verify_authorship_at_epoch(envelope, author_id, epoch_for_position(author_id, event_position))` (e165) reports verified. Flag each event with the CRYPTOGRAPHIC verdict (distinct from the reducer's presence counts): `verified` / `unsigned` (no author_sig) / `unknown-author` (author_id absent or not an identity) / `bad-signature` (present but fails verify). Exit non-zero (gate fail) when `require_authenticated` is on and ANY event is not `verified`; exit 0 when the config is off (advisory). CI runs it as the merge-gate.

### 5. Replay NEVER rejects (reducer records status; `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`)
The reducer folds a bad-signature / unsigned event into compiled state EXACTLY as today — it MUST NOT raise or drop the event. It additionally records a per-ticket PRESENCE summary — `state["authorship"] = {"signed": <count of events carrying an author_sig>, "unsigned": <count without>}` (deliberately NOT the word "verified": the reducer records PRESENCE only, never a live crypto check, to stay fast + deterministic; the cryptographic verdict — verified / bad-signature / unknown-author — is EXCLUSIVELY the merge-gate's job). Aggregation is unambiguous COUNTS, so a ticket with mixed signing coverage reports e.g. `{"signed":3,"unsigned":1}`. `show` surfaces the counts; `fsck` reports store-wide unsigned counts.

### 6. Snapshot carries folded signatures (`process_snapshot` / compact.py)
Compaction must PRESERVE each folded event's `author_id` + `author_sig` so a post- compaction `verify-authorship` still works. This is a `compact.py` change (NOT the reducer): `compact.py` composes the SNAPSHOT `compiled_state` (~lines 178-213), so it independently SCANS the folded event files it is absorbing and builds an `authorship_ledger` = the list of `{event_uuid, author_id, author_sig, epoch}` tuples, storing it under the SNAPSHOT's `compiled_state["authorship_ledger"]`. It must survive `_snapshot_strip_keys` and be rebuilt identically by `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`. `verify-authorship` reads the ledger when the raw event files are gone. A round-trip test signs events, compacts, and re-verifies from the snapshot's ledger.

## Scope
In: the config keys, optional write-time signing, the UX write-gate, the `verify-authorship` merge-gate command, the reducer status-record (never-reject), and snapshot authorship-ledger preservation + surfacing in show/fsck. Out: the actual CI YAML wiring (an operator step; documented in 4b5b), key distribution/rotation (e165).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `identity.require_authenticated` ON, `rebar verify-authorship` FLAGS an
  unsigned event and an unknown-author event and exits non-zero (merge-gate); the local
  write-gate fails fast on an unsignable write; a test asserts both, and that with the
  config OFF verify-authorship is advisory (exit 0).
- [ ] Replay never rejects: an event with a BAD `author_sig` still folds into compiled
  state (the ticket reduces, status unchanged) — a test reduces a tampered-signature
  event and asserts the state is intact; `show` surfaces the ticket's authorship status
  and `fsck` surfaces an unsigned/unverified count.
- [ ] Snapshot round-trip: signed events compacted into a SNAPSHOT still verify — a test
  signs events, compacts the ticket, and asserts `verify-authorship` (reading the
  snapshot's authorship_ledger) still reports them verified.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (identity.require_authenticated + identity.signing_key)
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (optional write-time author_sig signing + UX write-gate)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain` starts the detached drain child with `subprocess.Popen([...], env=..., stdin=..., stdout=..., stderr=log_fh, **_detach_kwargs())` — with **no `cwd=`**. The child therefore inherits the parent's working directory.

rebar's own workflow creates short-lived worktrees and removes them (`make worktree` / `git worktree remove`). When a write from inside such a worktree spawns a drain child and the worktree is later removed, the child's inherited cwd no longer exists. `queue.claim` calls `_tracker(repo_root)` -> `config.tracker_dir` -> `_config_sources.repo_root` -> `Path.cwd()`, and `os.getcwd()` raises:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

The drain aborts before claiming anything.

## Evidence (2026-08-20, this repo's own store)

`.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log` carries this traceback for **four distinct removed worktrees**:

```
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-ci-latency-debug
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-structured-duplicates
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-zizmor-online
/Users/joeoakhart/split-config-writer
```

The store currently holds **3 permanently pending enrichment entries** that never drain:

```
8625-7bea-67db-4cdc   9305-b42c-3262-4c58   e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2
```

Notably these are also the three largest ticket directories in the store (870 / 747 / 621 event files) — the most re-certified tickets, so the ones most often re-enqueued.

## Why this matters beyond a failed drain

It defeats the fix for `moist-short-lionfish` (958e-f4b3-275c-4154). That bug makes the write-path drain gate O(1) via a marker recording "nothing can be pending before T". The fast path is only reachable when the queue is genuinely quiet — correctly so, since a marker must never be able to hide real work. With entries wedged pending forever, the gate keeps doing the full O(ticket-count) store walk on every write and the 20 ms budget warning keeps firing, even with 958e landed. So 958e's acceptance criterion "the WARNING no longer fires on an ordinary write" is not observable on this store until this is fixed.

## Approach (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)

Pass an explicit, known-good `cwd` to the detached child rather than inheriting one that may be gone — the tracker's parent (the repo root) is already computed by `_rebar_dir(tracker)` and is the natural choice. Consider also whether `_config_sources.repo_root`'s `Path.cwd()` fallback should degrade rather than raise, since any detached/daemonised caller has the same exposure.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` (`_spawn_detached_drain`)
- possibly `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` (`repo_root`'s cwd fallback)
- tests under `tests/unit/`

## Testing
- A test that spawns the drain child from a directory that is removed before the child resolves
  the tracker, and asserts the drain still claims and processes the entry.
- A test pinning that the child is launched with an explicit `cwd` that does not depend on the
  caller's.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A detached drain child started from a since-removed worktree still resolves the tracker
      and drains.
- [x] The three wedged entries above drain (or an equivalent reproduction does).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while debugging 958e-f4b3-275c-4154 (moist-short-lionfish) — the reason that bug's fix cannot be observed end-to-end on this store. Out of that ticket's scope (different file, different mechanism), filed rather than folded in.
baseline.summary: detached drain child inherits a removed worktree's cwd and dies at getcwd()

## Context / Problem
Operators need an authoritative configuration precedence/source/lifecycle reference and a security reference that stay byte-current with the config schema and the deprecation/secret-name registries rather than drifting by hand. The existing `docs/config.md` is a 648-line HAND-AUTHORED operator doc (rationale, precedence narrative, a `## Config-key inventory`, a `### Secrets` list, the `## ticket.default_assignee` section, a fail-loud tombstone-registry section, stable anchor slugs) with many in-repo consumers: content-asserting tests (`test_snapshot_docs.py`, `test_session_id.py`, `test_structured_run.py`, `test_harness_provenance.py`, `test_session_shims.py`, `test_agents_claim_assignee_guidance.py`, `test_build_drift.py`, `test_llm_model_env_removal.py`), anchor deep links (`AGENTS.md#ticketdefault_assignee`, `docs/reuse-surface.md#rebar_operation_snapshot_shadow`, `docs/concurrency.md#config-key-inventory`),. Byte-generating into `config.md` would strand these consumers.

## Outcome
A new `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` generates a NEW standalone, fully-generated `docs/config-reference.md` (the machine-current, registry-derived precedence/source/lifecycle reference) and a NEW indexed `docs/security.md`. Its concrete inputs are three symbols: the typed config schema `rebar._config_schema` (keys/types/defaults), `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` + `rebar._deprecations.tombstones()` filtered to `kind=="cfg"` (the per-key LIFECYCLE/deprecation/removal column — a NEW cfg-channel derivation modelled on how `gen_env_registry.py` reads `kind=="env"` entries), and `rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES` (the secret-name inventory). There is no discrete "ownership registry" (ownership is a DERIVED AST classification in `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`); the generator does NOT read it. `docs/config.md` is LEFT ENTIRELY UNCHANGED, so all its consumers stay intact by construction. Non-registry-derivable narrative topics named by the epic (precedence rule, observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, native refresh) are supplied VERBATIM from a curated template constant in the generator, not synthesized. `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation reference the new docs. A newline-normalizing `--check` drift mode, gated by a pytest suite (run under `make test`, no CI dependency), fails when either generated doc is stale.

## Plan
1. Add `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` (modelled on `gen_env_registry.py`/`gen_cli_reference.py`): read `rebar._config_schema` (keys/types/defaults), `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` + `rebar._deprecations.tombstones()` (`kind=="cfg"` → lifecycle column), and `rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES` (secret-name inventory), and render (a) registry-derived tables and (b) the curated template constant (the precedence/observability/subprocess/behavior-delta/native-refresh narrative, verbatim) into fully-generated `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md`. Both are generated whole (no partial-region markers — new generator-owned files). Each carries a top-of-file markdown banner within its first 8 lines containing the word "generated" AND the exact command `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, per `test_generated_surface_markers.py::test_text_surface_carries_a_banner`. The generator exposes `main(["--check"])` returning 0 when the committed docs match and nonzero on drift (as `gen_cli_reference.py`/`gen_env_registry.py` do).
2. Create `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md`; update `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation. Register BOTH docs in the parity gate: add each (→ `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`) to the `GENERATED` map in `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py`, AND add a matching row for each to the `### Generated — never edit these by hand` TABLE in `docs/README.md` — the table row set must EQUAL `GENERATED`+`GATED_HAND_AUTHORED` (`test_readme_table_matches_registry`), so the prose nav link is not sufficient. Do NOT modify `docs/config.md`.
3. Add pytest suite `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` (modelled on `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`) that asserts `gen.main(["--check"]) == 0` on the committed docs and drives the topic/preservation/newline coverage below. This is the DRIFT GATE and it runs under `make test` — portable, no CI provider required; `--check` compares with newline normalization (universal-newline / text-mode read, not raw byte compare) so a CRLF autocrlf checkout does not false-fail.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Drift: a deliberate edit to either generated file makes `gen.main(["--check"])` return nonzero; regenerating clears it.
- Preservation (by construction): `docs/config.md` is byte-unchanged, proven by a test asserting the generator/`--check` never target `config.md`; its content-asserting suites named in Context continue to pass.
- Topic coverage: a test asserts that, across `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md` together, a heading/anchor exists for every entry in an explicit REQUIRED_TOPICS list — precedence, source, lifecycle, restart/redeploy rotation, native refresh, observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, MCP/CLI exposure — failing if any is missing.
- Newline safety: a regression test feeds CRLF-encoded checked-out content while the generator emits LF and asserts `--check` reports NO drift.
- Parity gate: `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` passes — each new doc carries its self-announcing banner (`test_text_surface_carries_a_banner`) and the `docs/README.md` table row set equals the registry (`test_readme_table_matches_registry`).
- Portability: the generator and its `--check` drift gate run under `make test` with no CI provider present.

## Compatibility / rollback
Docs-and-tooling only; no product-behavior change. `docs/config.md` and all its consumers are untouched. Rollback removes the generator (with its `--check` mode), the curated template constant, `docs/config-reference.md`, `docs/security.md`, `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py`, the two `GENERATED`-map/README-table registrations, and reverts the two navigation edits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` generates `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md` whole from `rebar._config_schema`, `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY`+`tombstones()` (cfg lifecycle), and `rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES`, plus a curated template constant, and never writes `docs/config.md`.
- [x] `docs/config.md` is byte-unchanged and all its enumerated consumers remain intact (its content-asserting suites pass; its anchor slugs still resolve), proven by a test that the generator/`--check` do not target `config.md`.
- [x] Across `docs/config-reference.md` and `docs/security.md`, an anchor exists for every topic in the REQUIRED_TOPICS list (precedence, source, lifecycle, restart/redeploy rotation, native refresh, observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, MCP/CLI exposure), proven by a topic-coverage test.
- [x] `docs/config-reference.md` carries a top-of-file banner (within its first 8 lines) naming `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, and `docs/security.md` carries the same, satisfying `test_generated_surface_markers.py::test_text_surface_carries_a_banner`.
- [x] Both new docs are registered in the `GENERATED` map of `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` and in the `docs/README.md` `### Generated — never edit these by hand` table, so `test_readme_table_matches_registry` passes.
- [x] `gen.main(["--check"])` returns 0 on committed docs and nonzero on a stale doc, is exercised by `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` under `make test` with no CI dependency, and does NOT false-fail on a CRLF checkout (newline-normalized comparison).
- [x] `docs/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` navigation reference the new docs.
baseline.summary: RP-04 S7.4 — Generate config/security/operator docs from registries + drift check

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Every other story in this epic is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake transport. That is the right tier for each of them, but it cannot exercise the failure modes that only appear against a real tracker: actual JQL evaluation over two projects, real per-project permissions and key allocation, real issue creation, and — the one that matters most — whether a pass scoped to one project can contaminate another. A multi-project bridge that is wrong in that direction writes real issues into the wrong project, which is expensive to detect and worse to undo. This story is the justified live canary the shared test-design standard allows for external-service mapping, run once the functionality is otherwise complete.

## Approach

Rehearse the whole feature live, against an **isolated store copy**, with dry-run gating at every step.

**Isolation comes first.** The rehearsal never runs against the production tickets branch. A copy of the tickets branch is published to an encrypted S3 remote — the capability delivered by epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`, which is why this epic depends on it — and the rehearsal store points its `sync.remote` at that copy. Before any mutating command, the harness asserts the configured remote is the S3 copy and not the production remote, and aborts otherwise. This is a precondition assertion, not a comment: it runs first and fails the test if the store is misconfigured.

**Dry-run gating is the contamination control.** Each scenario runs `bridge preview` first and asserts the previewed mutation set contains **only** targets in the intended project, with an empty intersection against every other configured project. Only then does `bridge sync` run. A preview that names a target outside the intended project fails the scenario before anything is written — which is the same fail-closed posture as the cross-project guard, applied at the harness level.

**Project configuration.** The mapping is loaded with the two live Jira Cloud projects, `REB` and `DIG`, plus dummy projects that exist only in the mapping and never in Jira — these exercise the "configured but empty" and "unknown to the tracker" paths without consuming real projects. Repo configurations deliberately vary: one project mapped to a single repo, one mapped to two repos, and one mapped to none, so the defaulting behaviour is observed across all three shapes rather than only the common one.

**Cleanup is designed in, not bolted on.** Every issue the rehearsal creates carries a run-scoped label. Cleanup is a single JQL sweep over that label across both live projects, and the run is not considered finished until a follow-up query for the label returns zero issues in each project. The label is generated per run so a failed earlier run cannot cause a later one to delete issues it did not create.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_multi_project/` (new) — the rehearsal harness and its scenarios
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — the operator runbook for performing and cleaning up the rehearsal

## Testing

Tier: a live end-to-end rehearsal against real Jira Cloud, which the shared standard permits for external-service mapping when a fake cannot reach the mechanism — here, genuine cross-project isolation. It is gated to an opt-in external suite so ordinary CI never touches live Jira.

Scenarios, each preview-gated then applied:

- **Inbound from both projects.** An issue created in `REB` and one in `DIG` are both ingested in a
  single pass; each resulting ticket records the project it came from and the repos mapped to that
  project.
- **Outbound to both projects.** Two rebar tickets, one per project, each land as an issue in their
  own project and nowhere else.
- **Not-synced.** A ticket with an explicit empty project produces no issue in either project, and no
  outbound mutation naming it appears in the preview.
- **Legacy resolution.** A ticket with the project field absent syncs to the recorded legacy default
  and to no other project.
- **Repo-config variety, both directions.** Inbound tickets from the single-repo, two-repo and
  zero-repo projects receive exactly those repo lists; outbound tickets created under each config
  reach the correct project regardless of their repos value, confirming repos never influences
  routing.
- **Contamination guard, the negative control.** An update aimed at a project absent from the mapping
  raises `CrossProjectTargetError` in preview and writes nothing — verified by querying both live
  projects afterwards and confirming no issue changed.
- **Promote-only.** Setting a project on an unbound ticket then syncing creates the issue; attempting
  to change a bound ticket's project is refused and the existing binding is unchanged.
- **Capability stamp.** With two projects in the mapping, `.store-compat.json` carries
  `multi-project-bridge`, and a binary lacking that capability refuses to write to the rehearsal
  store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The rehearsal aborts before any mutation if the configured remote is not the S3 store copy;
      checked by pointing it at a non-S3 remote and asserting it exits non-zero having written
      nothing.
- [ ] Issues created in `REB` and `DIG` are both ingested in one pass with the correct source project
      and repos recorded; checked by querying both live projects and asserting both tickets' fields.
- [ ] Rebar-created tickets targeting each project land in that project only; checked by querying
      both projects and asserting each issue exists in exactly one.
- [ ] A ticket with an explicit empty project creates no issue in either project; checked by a
      post-run query of both projects for the run label finding no issue for it.
- [ ] All three repo configurations produce the expected repos on inbound tickets and correct routing
      on outbound ones; checked per configuration.
- [ ] An update targeting an unmapped project is refused in preview and changes nothing live; checked
      by comparing both projects' issue state before and after.
- [ ] Every scenario's preview contained only targets in its intended project; checked by asserting
      an empty intersection against every other configured project for each preview.
- [ ] All issues created by the run are removed and a JQL query for the run label returns zero
      results in both `REB` and `DIG`; checked as the final step of the run.
baseline.summary: Live multi-project rehearsal against REB and DIG on an isolated S3 store copy
