baseline.description:
# P1.1 — Structured query: field predicates, OR, negation, --sort

## Context (problem + research)

rebar `search` is whitespace-split, case-insensitive **AND of substrings** with a few fixed flags (`reducer/search.py:search_states(states, query, *, status, ticket_type, has_tag)`, confirmed by EXP-R10). No OR, no field-scoped predicates (`assignee:`, `priority:<2`), no caller-controlled sort, no saved queries. Agents post-filter in their own code, fragmenting behavior. Comparable trackers expose richer query: Fossil offers SQL report queries; git-bug a `status:open label:x sort:` query language. This is a read-only, low-risk, high-daily-value upgrade (I3-clean — no writes).

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP8: a ~40-line parser does field predicates + `OR` + negation + degrade-to-
  substring (unknown `field:` -> literal substring, no crash).
- EXP-R10 (real code): confirmed the real `search_states` and
  `apply_ticket_filters(results, *, type_filter, status_filter, parent_filter,
  tag_filter, priority_filter, without_*...)` signatures — the integration seams.

## What / Implementation detail

1. New `reducer/_query.py` parser: tokenize; recognize `field:value`
   (`status:`, `type:`, `priority:` incl. `<`/`>`, `assignee:`, `tag:`,
   `parent:`) with exact match (tag = set membership; parent accepts id OR alias,
   resolved to full id before matching), leading `-`/`not:` negation, and **comma-OR
   within a field** (`status:open,in_progress`) as the only OR mechanism in v1 — there
   is NO bare `OR` keyword (a literal `OR` degrades to a substring). `priority:` uses
   GitHub range operators `<`,`<=`,`>`,`>=`,`n..m`. Free text still matches the existing
   `_haystack`. Unknown `field:` -> literal substring.
2. Expose one `match_predicate(state, field, op, value)` in `reducer/_filters.py`
   shared by `_query.py` and `apply_ticket_filters` (one comparison vocabulary).
3. `--sort/-s` in `_engine_support/reads.py` + `_reads.py`: keys
   `priority|created|updated|id|status`, `-key` descending; default sort unchanged
   so goldens hold. **Do not** touch `reducer/_sort.py` (that is event replay order,
   not presentation sort).
4. Parity across CLI (`--sort`, help texts), library (`sort=` kwarg), MCP
   (`sort` + bumped inputSchema).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reducer/_query.py` parser (predicates, comma-OR, negation, substring fallback) + unit tests
- [ ] `updated_at` computed during replay as running max(created_at, every replayed event ts); set on the reduced dict; `process_snapshot` re-seeds the max from the SNAPSHOT `compacted_at` (replay skips pre-snapshot events)
- [ ] `compact.py` strips `updated_at` from the reduced dict BEFORE serializing `compiled_state`; SNAPSHOT event bytes byte-identical with/without the change (canonical-bytes parity test holds) — no SCHEMA_VERSION bump, no new event type
- [ ] latest-event-ts accumulator added to the replay loop; compacted-then-untouched ticket asserts `updated_at == compacted_at`
- [ ] None-last `(is_none, value)` tuple sort key applies to ALL sort keys incl `created`/`updated` (never `key or 0`)
- [ ] shared `match_predicate` in `_filters.py` used by both query and filters
- [ ] `--sort` on list/search/ready (CLI), `sort=` (library), `sort` (MCP inputSchema)
- [ ] parity test across all three interfaces + a sorted-list golden
- [ ] back-compat: plain substring search byte-identical to current output

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.1).
- [ ] `search "status:open,in_progress priority:<2 assignee:alice"` (comma-OR within a
- [ ] A plain `search "login"` returns byte-identical results to today (back-compat).
- [ ] No event-schema change; no SCHEMA_VERSION bump.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The completion-verification close gate still fails to close legitimately complete tickets: the verifier agent trips the runaway-tool-loop guard (RunawayToolLoopError) while re-reading evidence files, the gate aborts, and authors are pushed toward `--force` — the exact symptom bug 46a2-9c1a-d855-4706 set out to eliminate.

Prior art (this plan builds ON it, not around it): epic 9b71 shipped the windowed distinct-ratio runaway guard (breaker/detector). Epic 10ae/story 2948 then shipped three levers in src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py: (1) completion-policy evidence banking, (2) a path-normalized read_file memo (`_memo_toolsets`) that reads a whole file once and serves subsequent range requests by slicing the cache, (3) large-file summarize/cap handling. The loop persisted DESPITE the memo layer.

Root cause (confirmed by reading the live composition in agent_call.py): the guard sits OUTERMOST (layer-order pinned Guard→Memo→Steering), so it observes every call BEFORE the memo layer answers it. A memo-SERVED repeat — free, harmless, exactly what lever 2 was built to produce — is therefore still counted as loop evidence by the guard's distinct-ratio window. Lever 2 made repeats cheap; the guard still punishes them: the two shipped fixes fight each other. Secondary defect in the same composition: reads past the cached window fall back to uncached exact-range reads, so long files degrade the ratio further.

## Approach
Recompose guard and memo via a SHARED ledger instead of reordering layers (the completion policy sits between them and must keep seeing calls). New module src/rebar/llm/runaway_guard.py: `ToolCallLedger` tracks observed vs EXECUTED calls plus a served-streak; the memo layer calls `record_executed` on EVERY path that reaches a wrapped tool — concretely five record sites: (1) non-allowlisted passthrough, (2) exact-signature cache miss, (3) read_file with unparseable path (path=None passthrough), (4) read_file first-read whole-file fetch (this record also covers the same invocation's past-window exact-range fallback for a >cap file), (5) repeat read_file past a truncated cache window (uncached exact-range fallback). Cache-served paths never record, so only they can extend the served-streak. The guard becomes two arms: (arm 1) the distinct-ratio computed over the EXECUTED stream only — memo-served repeats are no longer loop evidence; (arm 2) a served-streak backstop that still bounds a pure cache-served loop after a FULL window of consecutive zero-execution calls (checked at call entry, before increment). Guard stays outermost; layer order unchanged; completion policy unaffected. Governance-notice loops (policy answers without delegating) stay bounded by arm 2 since policy responses never reset the streak.

Out of scope, filed as follow-up when this lands: tri-state evidence banking (BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE banks met=false at search exhaustion — should bank insufficient_evidence), to be linked discovered_from this bug.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runaway_guard.py (new) — ToolCallLedger + two-arm guard.
- src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py — memo layer records executed work into the ledger (4 sites); build_agent_kwargs creates one ledger per call and passes it to both layers; old in-file guard removed.
- tests/unit/test_agent_call_memo_nudge.py — recomposition coverage, incl. a parametrized test that each execution site resets the served-streak.
- tests/unit/test_agent_call_runaway_guard_c827.py — held-out end-to-end guard oracle (PydanticAIRunner/build_agent_kwargs): stays green unchanged — its looping tools return "Error:"-prefixed strings, which the memo never caches, so observed==executed and the ratio arm still trips exactly as pinned.

## Testing
- Regression (withheld oracle, proven to FAIL on the old guard): a verifier pattern of 2 cached re-reads per novel call (i%3) must NOT trip the guard — memo-served repeats are not loop evidence for the ratio arm.
- Backstop: a pure cache-served loop (zero execution for a full window) still trips, with the served-streak message text distinguishing the arm.
- Non-allowlisted looping tool still trips the ratio arm (passthrough calls are executed work).
- Error-looping allowlisted tool (responses never cached) still trips the ratio arm.
- Layer-order test keeps pinning Guard→Memo→Steering.
- Per-site streak reset: a parametrized test drives each of the five record sites inside a cache-served streak and asserts the streak resets (no false arm-2 trip on real work), covering the truncated-window fallback branch inside a loop.
- End-to-end: the c827 held-out oracle module runs unchanged and green (ratio-arm trip semantics, abort-before-budget, k-cycle detection preserved).
- Manual mutation pass over the new module and the five record_executed sites; every mutant killed (mutation testing already surfaced and filled 2 gaps: non-allowlisted loop, error-looping exact-sig path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A verifier run that re-reads memoized evidence files completes without RunawayToolLoopError; checked by test_memo_served_repeats_are_not_loop_evidence_for_the_ratio_arm (fails on pre-fix code).
- [x] A genuine loop — non-allowlisted repeat, error-looping tool, or pure cache-served spin — is still bounded; checked by the three trip tests (both arms).
- [x] Layer order and completion-policy visibility unchanged; checked by the existing layer-order test staying green.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the LLM-area test suite green; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier still loops on repeated file reads, blocking legitimate closes despite the runaway-guard fix (incomplete fix of brusque-tippable-sunbittern)

## Context / Problem

`adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.add_comment` is the only `--json` consumer in that module that returns raw `json.loads(result.stdout)` straight to its caller (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:549-550`). Every sibling normalizes or verifies the payload first: `get_comments` -> `_parse_paginated_comments`, `_parse_acli_comments` (normalizes bare list / wrapped dict / unrecognised shape), `get_issue` (unwraps `issues[0]`, raises when absent), `create_issue` -> `_verify_created_issue` (raises loudly when no key, `acli_cli_ops.py:40`).

Because `add_comment` skips that idiom, it hands its caller ACLI's batch mutation envelope (`{"results": [...], "totalCount": N, "successCount": N}`) while its declared type (`_backend.py:585`: `add_comment(...) -> dict[str, Any]`) and its consumer (`dispatch_apply_phases._record_comment_id`, which reads `result.get("id")`) treat it as a created comment resource. That gap is exactly what let bug `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (`aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`) ship: `_record_comment_id` read `result["id"]`, got `None` on every Cloud post, and silently no-opped — re-posting ~205 comments an hour until REB-1861 hit Jira's 5000-comment cap. The aa7b fix made `_record_comment_id` tolerant (records `UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID` when no id), but the transport boundary itself still returns the semantically-wrong shape, and `results[].id` (the WORK ITEM key) remains a trap for any future consumer.

## Approach

Normalize at the transport boundary, mirroring the sibling idiom:

1. Add a module-level helper `_parse_comment_created(stdout: str) -> dict[str, Any]` in
   `acli_cli_ops.py`, called by `add_comment` in place of raw `json.loads`:
   - A dict WITHOUT the batch-envelope markers (`results` / `successCount`) is a comment
     resource (the DC/REST-shaped `{"id": "10001"}` that
     `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py:52` pins) — returned
     verbatim. Assume any non-envelope dict is a resource (default; no shape allowlist).
   - The batch envelope is returned as an honest comment-resource-shaped dict
     `{"id": None, "acli_envelope": <parsed>}`: explicit `id: None` because ACLI echoes no
     comment id, envelope preserved under a clearly-named key so `results[].id` (the WORK
     ITEM key, not a comment id) can never be mistaken for one. FAILURE envelopes never reach
     the normalizer: `acli_subprocess._run_acli` already raises `AcliMutationError` via
     `_check_mutation_failure` (`acli_subprocess.py:299-345`, bug 44de).
   - Any other shape (bare list, scalar, non-JSON handled by json.loads raising) raises
     `RuntimeError` naming the payload, mirroring `_verify_created_issue`'s loud failure.
2. Update the `acli_result` fixture assertions in
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_comment_id_acli_envelope.py` (which currently pin
   the raw-envelope passthrough) to the normalized contract; its four dedup tests must keep
   passing unchanged (the recording path still stores `UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID`).
3. Commit a RECORDED real ACLI comment-create payload: the failure envelope captured live
   today against acli 1.3.19 via the safe probe
   `acli jira workitem comment create --key NONEXIST-999999 --json` (exit=0,
   `successCount: 0`, `results[0].id == "NONEXIST-999999"` — no mutation performed). Embed it
   as a constant with a provenance note and assert `_check_mutation_failure` raises
   `AcliMutationError` on it, plus normalizer unit tests against the already-recorded SUCCESS
   envelope (verified live against acli 1.3.19 by fix 8d98c298fa8).
4. Audit the remaining `--json` mutation wrappers for raw passthrough —
   `acli_cli_ops.create_issue` paths (`_create_issue_no_json`, `_create_from_json_payload`),
   `update_priority` (REST, no JSON return), `get_issue`, `get_comments`, and the
   module-level `acli.update_issue` (`acli.py:211` returns `json.loads(result.stdout)` raw
   for `workitem edit`) — and record the findings as a comment on this ticket; file a
   `discovered_from` ticket for any consumer-reachable hazard found.
5. Touch up the `_record_comment_id` docstring (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:311`) so its
   description of the Cloud transport's return matches the normalized shape.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` — add
  `_parse_comment_created`; `add_comment` routes through it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_comment_id_acli_envelope.py` — update fixture
  assertions to the normalized contract; add recorded failure-envelope constant + tests.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py` — docstring-only update to
  `_record_comment_id`.

## Testing

- Happy path: the recorded SUCCESS envelope driven through the real
  `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` (stubbed at the `_run_acli` seam, as the existing fixture does)
  returns `{"id": None, "acli_envelope": <envelope>}`; the DC/REST-shaped `{"id": "10001"}`
  passes through verbatim (existing `test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py` assertion keeps
  passing).
- Failure/edge: the RECORDED failure envelope raises `AcliMutationError` in
  `_check_mutation_failure`; a bare-list payload makes `_parse_comment_created` raise
  `RuntimeError`.
- Regression: all four existing dedup tests in `test_comment_id_acli_envelope.py` pass with
  the normalized fixture (recording stores `UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID`; re-diff emits nothing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `add_comment` no longer returns the raw batch envelope: SUCCESS envelope ->
      `{"id": None, "acli_envelope": ...}`, resource-shaped payload -> verbatim, unrecognized
      shape -> `RuntimeError` — checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_comment_id_acli_envelope.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py`.
- [x] At least one test asserts against a RECORDED real ACLI comment-create payload (the
      live-captured failure envelope with its provenance note) rather than an invented one —
      checked by reading the committed constant's provenance comment and running its test.
- [x] The remaining `acli_cli_ops` `--json` mutation wrappers (and `acli.update_issue`) are
      audited for raw passthrough and the finding is recorded as a comment on this ticket —
      checked by the comment's presence on the ticket.
baseline.summary: ACLI add_comment returns the raw batch envelope, not a comment resource

baseline.description:
# Cluster 2 — unify the two `_advisory_lock` backoff functions into one parameterized helper

## What

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py` contains two structurally identical jittered-exponential-backoff functions — both compute `min(base * factor**i, cap) * uniform(1 - jitter, 1 + jitter)` — that differ only in their constants:

- `_compute_backoff_seconds(retry_index)` — `_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS=0.2`, `_BACKOFF_FACTOR=2.0`,
  `_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=5.0`, `_BACKOFF_JITTER_FRACTION=0.3` (used by `acquire_pass_lock`, budget
  `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT=5`).
- `_cas_backoff_seconds(retry_index)` — `_CAS_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS=0.05`, factor `_BACKOFF_FACTOR`
  (=2.0, already shared), `_CAS_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=1.0`, `_CAS_BACKOFF_JITTER_FRACTION=0.3` (used by
  `_cas_advance_with_retry`, budget `_CAS_RETRY_BUDGET=8`).

Collapse the shared math into ONE parameterized pure function `_jittered_backoff(retry_index, *, base, factor, cap, jitter_fraction)` that performs exactly one `random.uniform` call (preserving the RNG draw count/order, so a seeded sequence is identical). Keep `_compute_backoff_seconds` / `_cas_backoff_seconds` as thin wrappers that bind their respective constants, so the two call sites and the two retry **budgets** are unchanged. This is the single genuine in-file duplication identified by the audit; the other retry sites solve different problems and are intentionally left bespoke (see parent epic `civil-marlin-flare`).

## Why

One backoff formula in one place is observable and tunable; two hand-copied copies drift silently. Behavior is preserved exactly — both budgets keep their constants and the formula is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py` has a single parameterized backoff
      function; `_compute_backoff_seconds` and `_cas_backoff_seconds` are removed (or become trivial
      wrappers binding their constants), with no remaining duplicated `base*factor**i`/jitter math.
- [ ] Both call sites (`acquire_pass_lock`, `_cas_advance_with_retry`) produce the same backoff
      schedule as before for their respective constants; the two retry budgets are unchanged.
- [ ] The existing jitter test
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_retry_jitter.py` still passes (extend it
      if needed to cover both constant sets through the unified function).
- [ ] No universal `retry()` helper or new `_retry.py` module is introduced; the change stays inside
      `_advisory_lock.py`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make test` pass; net LOC for the module does not increase.
baseline.summary: Cluster 2: unify the two _advisory_lock backoff functions into one parameterized helper

## Context and confirmed root cause

The accepted benchmark on closed ticket left-changeful-mamba deliberately requires 3,000 tickets, 6,000 events, exactly 24 batched commits, and >=10x commit-count reduction. It is the integration-tier long pole at 93-108s on current macOS jobs. N, event count, commit/crash safety, platform cells, and coverage are locked.

A full N=3000 cProfile on current origin/main confirmed two dynamic bulk-path defects:
- rebar._commands._seam.append_event calls author(), which executes git config user.name once per envelope. The benchmark made 6,000 calls; _git_config consumed 47.79s cumulative and subprocess.run 59.54s.
- event_append.batch_stage_and_commit prepares a chunk by calling staging.stage_event for every not-yet-published CREATE. stage_event calls sweep_stale_staging for each new ticket, so the benchmark made 3,000 sweeps and 375,876 staging-owner checks, consuming 15.94s. Within a batch, the same staging root is rescanned while earlier prepared items remain unpublished.

Controlled identical-harness A/B, preserving 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, and 29 total commits (5 init + the locked 24 import delta):
- current collaborators with counting wrappers: 77.231s, 6,001 git-config reads, 3,000 sweeps;
- only git-config and sweep replaced by side-effect-free logical collaborators: 16.404s, same state and commits.
That 60.8s delta discriminates these mechanisms from event serialization/commit count as the dominant avoidable cost.

## OSS comparison and prior decisions

Git's maintained fast-import backend reads one stream and writes repository objects/refs in bulk (git/git@745601a, Documentation/git-fast-import.adoc#L14-L29). The relevant consensus is amortizing repeat setup/scans inside a bulk boundary, not replacing rebar's event validation or crash-safe commits with git fast-import.

Tracker cross-check: left-changeful-mamba locks N=3000, 6,000 events, 24 commits, >=10x reduction, rollback, and crash-resume. coercive-paediatric-bug rejects extra workers/shards that increase runner-minutes. No ticket rejects batch-scoped identity lookup or one stale-staging sweep per batch; interactive per-write behavior remains unchanged.

## Plan

1. In src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py add an explicit contextvar-scoped author cache. Outside that context author() retains the existing per-call git-config read. The cache is keyed by fallback so git-config-less Unknown/unknown parity remains. It is nestable and reset in finally. Do not extend the existing module-global _ATTRIBUTION_CACHE: that cache owns user.email/identity invalidation across independent writes, whereas user.name must remain live for independent interactive writes and be frozen only inside one explicit import context. Document the distinct lifetimes beside both caches.
2. In src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py enter that author-cache context for the whole import composition. Every imported envelope therefore uses the author value observed once at import start; no cache survives the call, thread/task, or pytest session. Event bytes and attribution fields are otherwise unchanged.
3. In src/rebar/_store/staging.py add a keyword-only sweep_stale=True parameter to stage_event. The default preserves every direct/reconciler caller. In src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py thread the same defaulted parameter through _prepare_event; stage_and_commit keeps the default.
4. In src/rebar/_store/event_append.py keep streaming validation/preparation and a local swept_stale flag. For each item call _prepare_event(..., sweep_stale=not swept_stale); after the first returned StagedEvent has staging_dir set (proving the validated item took the new-ticket branch and performed the sweep), set swept_stale=True for the rest of that bounded batch. Thus empty and existing-ticket-only batches add no sweep, a new-ticket batch sweeps exactly once, invalid input still fails before any new sweep, and materialization/generator semantics remain unchanged. Atomic staging/publish, rollback, lock, and commit behavior remain unchanged.
5. Strengthen the existing N=3000 integration benchmark with deterministic counters: one user.name lookup for the import and one stale sweep per CREATE chunk; derive the expected count from the already-computed locked import commit formula (expected / 2), not a second hardcoded chunk-size literal, never wall-clock thresholds. Add focused unit coverage that empty batches do not sweep, existing-ticket-only batches do not introduce a new sweep, new-ticket batches sweep once, direct stage_event still sweeps, fallback-sensitive author caching is scoped, and interactive writes remain uncached.
6. RED first on the current mechanisms, hold the oracle out from the fixer, then GREEN. Re-seed each defect independently (remove author cache; restore per-item sweep) and prove the corresponding assertion returns RED. Refactoring-only renames must remain green.
7. Re-run the identical N=3000 harness/profile on the same host and report wall/call-count deltas. Run import batching/idempotency/crash-resume/rollback, atomic ticket-dir/store tests, lint, typecheck, and the full pytest selection.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: left-changeful-mamba plus tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py require N=3000, 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe commits, >=10x reduction, complete created/comment counts, rollback and resume; this ticket requires eliminating redundant bulk setup without changing those contracts. trigger_preconditions: a fresh git-backed store importing 3,000 synthetic CREATE+comment records through public rebar.import_tickets. production_path: rebar.import_tickets -> import_ndjson.import_tickets -> _seam.append_event/finalize_event -> event_append.batch_stage_and_commit -> event_prepare._prepare_event -> staging.stage_event. test_tier: real temporary-git integration for the locked import contract plus focused unit tests for cache/sweep lifecycle. observable_postcondition: identical logical state and 24 import commits; exactly one user.name lookup per import; stale sweeps equal half of the test's already-computed expected import commits (12 for N=3000 today, one per CREATE chunk); single/direct writes retain their existing lookup/sweep behavior. negative_control: interactive writes remain one commit and one live author lookup per event; existing-ticket-only/empty batches do not gain stale-sweep work. collateral_invariants: same event bytes/author fallback semantics, clean index, no lost/duplicate events, same warnings and provenance. recovery: injected later-chunk commit failure resumes to all tickets exactly once. ci_gate: integration pytest job and full Gerrit Verified gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Summary

`fsck` is a DIAGNOSTIC tool: finding problems is its purpose and its success condition. The MCP tool nevertheless converts a completed report into `command_failed`, so the caller receives an error object with the entire report stuffed into a message STRING rather than a structured result.

## Mechanism

- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:242-243` — the CLI exits non-zero when `issue_count > 0`.
  **Correct; NOT the defect.**
- `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:347-353` — calls `fsck_cli([])` (TEXT mode, so it never asks for the
  JSON the CLI can already produce) and raises `RebarError(f"rebar fsck failed (exit {rc}): ...")`
  on ANY non-zero rc, flattening the report into an exception message. **This is the defect.**
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:385,396` — `def fsck(...) -> str` (so no `outputSchema`) returning
  `rebar.fsck(...)`, so that raise reaches the client as
  `{"error":"command_failed","exit_code":1,"message":"<whole report>"}`.

Verified: on a store with findings, `rebar fsck --output json` returns rc 1 AND a structured `{"issues":[{"kind","ticket_id","detail"}],"fixed":[],"issue_count":2}` — while `rebar.fsck()` raises on the same store. The structure exists one layer down and is discarded.

## What is EXPECTED and what is the BUG

**Expected: the CLI exiting non-zero on findings.** Conventional for an integrity checker (`git fsck`, `fsck(8)`); scripts depend on it. Not a defect. **The bug is the library/MCP layer treating that as a FAILED CALL.**

## Two commands, two contracts

`fsck` and `fsck-recover` are DIFFERENT operations and must not share a reader:

| | `fsck` (scan) | `fsck-recover` |
|---|---|---|
| output | tagged `KIND:` lines; has `--output json` | plain-English NARRATIVE; no JSON mode |
| exit 0 | clean | nothing to do / recovered |
| exit 1 | issues found (completed) | attempted but nothing recovered (completed) |
| exit 2 | usage / uninitialised store | fatal (no tracker / bad args) |

Sources: `_commands/fsck.py:17-18,242-243`; `_commands/fsck_recover.py:9-11,200-320`. An uninitialised store exits **1**, not 2 (`_missing_tracker_result`, `fsck.py:246-268`), and in JSON mode emits a payload byte-identical to a clean store.

## Plan

1. **`src/rebar/_lib_reads.py` — new `fsck_report(*, recover=False, report_only=False,
   repo_root=None) -> dict`**, a thin dispatcher over two private readers with SEPARATE
   exit-code contracts:
   - `_fsck_scan_report` — passes `--output=json` so the canonical shape comes from the CLI's own
     transform (text and JSON cannot drift). Returns
     `{issues, fixed, issue_count, returncode, mode: "scan", report: None}` for a completed run
     (exit 0 or 1). Raises on exit outside `(0, 1)`, and — SCAN ONLY — on exit 1 with an empty
     `issues[]`, which is unreachable for a real scan (the exit derives from the COUNTED tally
     while `issues[]` is the superset of every emitted `KIND:` line) and therefore identifies the
     uninitialised/unscannable store. Without it the function would report a store it never read
     as clean.
   - `_fsck_recover_report` — captures the narrative VERBATIM into `report` and never runs it
     through the scan's line transform (which would scrape `{"kind": "warn"}` entries out of the
     narrative's `WARN:` prose and discard the rest). Returns
     `{mode: "recover", report, issues: [], fixed: [], issue_count: 0, returncode}` for exit 0 or
     1; raises on exit 2. It must NOT inherit the scan's exit-1 rule — recover's exit 1 is a
     completed recovery.
   - `mode` is the discriminator, so a recover result can never be misread as a clean scan.
2. **`rebar.fsck()` is left exactly as it is** — `-> str`, raising on non-zero. It has ~10
   existing callers across `tests/interfaces/**` that assert on its string return.
3. **`src/rebar/_mcp_models.py` — add `FsckOut`** mirroring `src/rebar/schemas/fsck.schema.json`
   (which ALREADY EXISTS, registered as `schemas.FSCK`), following the `_Out` /
   `ClarityResultOut` / `BridgeFsckOut` pattern, incl. `mode` and `report`.
4. **`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — `fsck` returns `FsckOut`** built from `rebar.fsck_report()`, so
   the tool advertises an `outputSchema` like every read tool registered around it. `recover` and
   `report_only`/`REBAR_MCP_READONLY` handling is unchanged. One tool, one schema, two modes.
5. **`src/rebar/schemas/fsck.schema.json`** — declare `returncode`, `mode` and `report` as
   OPTIONAL (kept out of `required` so the CLI's own `--output json` payload still validates
   unchanged), and register `FsckOut -> fsck` in `check_mcp_models.MODEL_SCHEMAS`.
6. **AC4 (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py`)** — `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` stops incrementing the
   issue counter; the line and its `issues[]` entry are unchanged. Reasoning in the AC4 comment.
7. **Docs**: `docs/user-guide.md` (never-counted class, beside the `TRACKER_DIRTY_TMP_EVENT`
   precedent), `docs/concurrency.md` I8, and `docs/output-schemas.md` (the MCP `fsck` outputSchema
   exemption is no longer true).

## Test plan

RED first, held out from the implementer: `tests/interfaces/facades/test_fsck_structured_326f.py` asserts the MCP-layer call returns an enumerable structured result rather than raising; that a run which could not HAPPEN still raises and is distinguishable; that `rebar.fsck()` and the CLI exit are unchanged; that `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` is emitted but not counted; and — covering the paths whose absence let a blocker through review — that the RECOVER path preserves its narrative, invents no findings from its `WARN:` prose, treats exit 1 as a completed recovery, still raises on exit 2, and that the scan's `rc not in (0, 1)` branch raises. Mutation-checked by re-seeding each confirmed defect (including routing recover back through the transform, and applying the scan's exit-1 rule to recover) and confirming RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The MCP `fsck` tool returns a STRUCTURED result (findings enumerable by kind and ticket)
      for a completed run, whatever the findings, and advertises an `outputSchema`.
- [x] A genuine execution failure (fsck could not run) remains distinguishable from a completed
      run that found issues, on BOTH the scan and recover paths, whose exit-code vocabularies
      differ.
- [x] The recover path is represented as the distinct operation it is: its narrative is preserved
      verbatim and never parsed as a scan report.
- [x] The CLI's non-zero-on-findings exit is PRESERVED — scripts depend on it; only the
      library/MCP surfacing changes.
- [x] `rebar.fsck()`'s existing `-> str`/raise contract is unchanged for its existing callers.
- [x] Decided and recorded whether self-resolved `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` entries count toward the
      failure exit; the CLI's exit reflects that decision.

- [x] [non-codebase] **LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE.** `fsck` called through the deployed endpoint returns a STRUCTURED result with enumerable findings, not `command_failed`.
      provenance: environment=deployed container rebar-mcp-6fe5c0d54574-8093 serving https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp; principal=MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CODEX bearer; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — fsck returned a STRUCTURED result with keys issues/fixed/issue_count/returncode/mode/report (issue_count=14, mode=scan) and no command_failed envelope. The caller-visible shape of a deployed tool is not determinable from source.
      Evidence must be OBSERVED against the deployed server at
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` and recorded in a ticket comment naming
      the tool(s) called, the arguments, and the actual response. A passing local test does not satisfy it, and neither does a merged change: the container must have redeployed
      and served the call. This exists because a fix here was previously reported complete
      on the strength of a merge while the deployed behaviour was still broken.
baseline.summary: MCP fsck turns a SUCCESSFUL diagnostic report into a tool error, so the report is unusable

baseline.description:
## Summary

On 2026-09-02 the `rebar-gerrit` host (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, us-east-1) filled its 30-GiB gp3 root volume and took **Gerrit fully offline for ~5 hours** (~02:05–07:10 PDT). This is the FOURTH root-disk-pressure incident in a month and the FIRST to cause a complete outage: previous incidents degraded the review bot, this one killed the service, the SSM agent, and the metrics publisher simultaneously.

Two distinct defects. The second is new and is the reason nobody was paged.

## Defect 1 — root disk fills faster than reclaim frees it

Root reached **29 GiB used of 30 GiB**. Every prior mitigation has reduced the rate without bounding the ceiling, so the disk still reaches 100%.

## Defect 2 (NEW, and the reason this became a 5-hour outage) — the disk alarm RESET ITSELF TO OK as the host died

`rebar-root-disk-pressure` is configured:

* metric `rebar/host` `root_disk_used_percent`, threshold **> 85%**
* **EvaluationPeriods = 3**
* **TreatMissingData = `notBreaching`**

The metric is published BY AN AGENT ON THE HOST THAT IS RUNNING OUT OF DISK. Observed series (30-min max):

```
2026-09-01T23:03  92
2026-09-01T23:33  94      <- breaching (>85)
2026-09-02T00:03  92
2026-09-02T00:33  91
2026-09-02T01:03  92
2026-09-02T01:33  90      <- LAST DATAPOINT EVER
(no data thereafter)
```

`GerritReachable` stops at the same timestamp. The publisher died with the host.

Because the disk was breaching but had not yet accumulated **3** breaching periods, and because missing data is treated as **notBreaching**, the alarm did not fire — it transitioned **to `OK` at 01:45:10**, i.e. it went GREEN at the exact moment the host became unreachable, and is STILL green now. The only thing that fired was `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` (a black-box reachability probe) at 02:05.

This is the classic dead-man's-switch inversion: for a metric published by the failing host, "no data" is the strongest possible evidence of the condition, and this configuration reads it as the absence of the condition. `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` has the SAME `notBreaching` setting and the same inversion.

## Why the prior fixes did not hold

Chronology (all on this host, all root disk unless noted):

* **2026-08-04/06** — `sour-plugugly-rhino` (28f9-535c-ce9c-4583): root 48% -> 95%, pinned 92–96% for ~39h. Fix: pressure-triggered `docker prune` on the autodeploy no-op tick.
* **2026-08-17** — `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` (3a52-2d79-320d-4fed): root 71% -> 90%, review-bot unhealthy. Title records this as happening **"after automated-reclaim mitigation"** — the Aug-4 prune did not prevent it.
* **2026-08-26** — `/var/gerrit` DATA volume fill; remediation task `scowlful-bovine-dragonfly` (3e92-b7f4-dede-4c17) is **still OPEN**.
* **2026-08-29/30** — `beton-naval-eyas` (2f46-6871-796f-41c9): correlated autodeploy alarms on this host.
* **2026-09-01 (yesterday)** — `preodorous-temporary-piglet` (3cef-c948-68ba-40fd): root 91–95%, review clones hit ENOSPC, change 2481 burned its retry budget into a **spurious `LLM-Review -1`**.
* **2026-09-02 (today)** — full outage, ~5h.

Reclaim has been made *faster* and *more triggered* each round, but nothing has ever bounded the CEILING, and no alarm survives the host it monitors.

## Recovery performed (an UNWEDGE, not a fix)

1. Snapshot `snap-06f35ff3a20fe4a73` of root `vol-0270fcf13709cf472`.
2. `modify-volume` root **30 -> 60 GiB**.
3. Reboot; AL2023 cloud-init `growpart` expanded partition + filesystem at boot.
4. Verified: `/dev/nvme0n1p1 60G 29G 32G 48% /`; Gerrit HTTP 200 and SSM `Online` at 07:10 PDT.

**The 29 GiB of content is UNCHANGED — this only bought headroom.** At the observed fill rate the larger disk postpones recurrence, it does not prevent it. Growing the volume must not be recorded as the resolution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 [non-codebase]: `rebar-root-disk-pressure` and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` no longer treat missing data as healthy — `TreatMissingData` becomes `breaching` (or `missing`), so a host that stops publishing raises rather than clears. Verified by `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` showing the new setting, and by an induced publish-stop raising the alarm.
- [x] AC2 [non-codebase] [REWRITTEN 2026-09-02 — the original premise was refuted by measurement; see the correction comment on this ticket]: the disk alarm RE-ENTERS alarm when the publisher dies, instead of self-clearing to OK and staying there. Original AC2 asked for "an alarm that would have fired on the 2026-09-01T23:33 94% datapoint"; that is unsatisfiable, because the raw 300s series has no 23:33 datapoint (the 94 reading is at 23:40) and the alarm had ALREADY been in continuous ALARM since 22:32 PDT under BOTH the old and new configuration, so nothing "fires on" it. What the fix actually buys, and what this AC now requires, is that after the last real datapoint at 01:40 the alarm returns to ALARM on missing data rather than remaining OK through the outage. Verified by replaying the recorded series against the live configuration (Maximum / 300s / evaluation_periods 3 / datapoints_to_alarm 2 / threshold 85 / GreaterThanThreshold / treat_missing_data breaching): window [01:40 real 85 = not breaching, 01:45 missing -> breaching, 01:50 missing -> breaching] gives 2 of 3, so ALARM at ~01:55:10 PDT — versus never under the old configuration. The replay is validated against real alarm history, predicting the 01:45 OK (actual 01:45:10) and the 22:30 ALARM (actual 22:32).
- [x] AC3: the top consumer of the 29 GiB root working set is identified and named with measured byte totals (the `du`/`docker system df` breakdown could not be captured during recovery because SSM invocations hung on the loaded box).
- [ ] AC4: root usage has a bounded CEILING, not merely a faster reclaim — a mechanism that cannot exceed a configured high-water mark regardless of build burst rate. Verified by a test or simulation driving the documented fill rate and showing usage plateaus below the bound.
- [x] AC5: the still-open `/var/gerrit` remediation `scowlful-bovine-dragonfly` is either completed or explicitly superseded by this ticket's fix, so the data volume is not left with the same unbounded shape.
- [x] AC6 [non-codebase]: an operator runbook entry covers "host is wedged and SSM is ConnectionLost", recording the shell-free recovery path used here (snapshot -> modify-volume -> reboot -> cloud-init growpart) and stating explicitly that it is an unwedge requiring a follow-up reclaim.

## Notes

- The EC2 status checks stayed `ok` throughout: the hypervisor and instance networking were healthy, so instance-check alarms cannot detect this class.
- The instance is `unlimited` burstable with ~440 CPU credits and 0 surplus, so CPU throttling was ruled out as a cause.
- TCP 443 stayed OPEN while HTTP returned 504 then timed out — the reverse proxy survived while its upstream died, which is why black-box probes saw a slow failure rather than a refusal.

## Completion evidence (2026-09-03)

- **AC2** — MET. Replayed the recorded series against the live configuration (Maximum / 300s / evaluation_periods 3 / datapoints_to_alarm 2 / threshold 85 / GreaterThanThreshold / treat_missing_data breaching). Window [01:40 real 85 = not breaching, 01:45 missing -> breaching, 01:50 missing -> breaching] gives 2 of 3, so ALARM at ~01:55:10 PDT versus never under the old configuration. The replay model is validated against real alarm history: it predicts the 01:45 OK (actual 01:45:10) and the 22:30 ALARM (actual 22:32).
- **AC3** — MET. Root 28G: /var 26G, of which /var/lib/docker 17G (overlay2 16G across 67 layer directories), /var/tmp 3.6G, /var/log 1.8G (journal 1.7G). Docker's own accounting claimed ~9.5 GB with ZERO dangling images, so ~6.5 GB was orphaned overlay2 layer state prune cannot reach — which is why four rounds of prune-based mitigation never held.
- **AC5** — MET, by doing the work inside this ticket per the operator's decision. Gerrit change 2586 (MERGED) adds a `/var/gerrit` non-`site` debris census publishing `rebar/host:data_disk_debris_bytes`, and alarm `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-debris` (1 GiB, 2-of-3, breaching), **now APPLIED and live in production reading 0 bytes**. Plus runbook `infra/runbooks/gerrit-data-volume-reclaim.md` and a pointer from review-bot-ops.md. The enforceable half is detection; the evidence-location policy is advisory and labelled as such in the tree, because rebar cannot stop a shell on the box writing where it likes.
- **AC6** — MET. Gerrit change 2549 (MERGED) adds `infra/runbooks/gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md`, leading with the UNWEDGE-not-a-fix framing and the 29-GiB-before/29-GiB-after argument, plus a cross-reference from review-bot-ops.md. The root volume id was verified against the live API before landing, since the data volume id is hardcoded in sibling runbooks and the two are dangerous to confuse.

## The two ACs that remain, and why

- **AC1** — HALF met. `describe-alarms` confirms both disk alarms are live at `treat_missing_data = breaching` (root_disk_pressure 300/3/2, gerrit_data_disk_high 300/3/2). The second half asks for an INDUCED publish-stop raising the alarm, which is a deliberate production test: stopping the publisher stops ALL host metrics, so it would drive roughly twelve alarms into ALARM and page for a non-incident. Awaiting an operator decision on whether to run it, or to accept the AC2 replay — which proves the missing-data semantics against real recorded data — as sufficient.
- **AC4** — NOT met, and owned elsewhere by design. The bounded ceiling is Defect 1, which the operator-approved plan decomposed into epic `6202-e1c7-c57f-4897` (endowed-upset-scaup); that epic's own description states "Defect 2 stays on that bug and was fixed/landed/applied live. This epic is Defect 1." The epic is open, linked, and still has NO CHILDREN. Awaiting an operator decision on whether this ticket closes on Defect 2 with AC4 recorded as epic-owned, or stays open until 6202 delivers.

## AC1 evidence — operator accepted replay in place of an induced publish-stop (2026-09-03)

The setting half was already confirmed live: `describe-alarms` shows `rebar-root-disk-pressure` and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` both at `treat_missing_data = breaching`, 300s / 3 periods / 2 datapoints.

The behaviour half is proven by REPLAY rather than by inducing a publisher stop. Operator decision: replay accepted. The reasoning, recorded because it generalises:

- An induced publish-stop stops ALL host metrics, so it drives roughly twelve alarms into ALARM and pages for a non-incident. The cost is real and the information gained is small.
- The replay is deterministic, repeatable, and covers a window chosen to include the worst churn on record rather than whichever period happens to elapse.
- Replaying 24h of each alarm's own recorded series against its live configuration produced **zero transitions caused by missing data** across all twelve, while correctly reproducing the three genuine breaching events (mirror_out_of_sync x3, review_interrupts_bound_exceeded x2, deploy_errors during the febd build failures). Every 300s alarm saw 27 missing periods in that window — the jitter is real, and it was absorbed.
- For this ticket's own alarm specifically, the earlier replay showed `rebar-root-disk-pressure` re-entering ALARM at ~01:55:10 PDT on missing data under the new configuration, versus never under the old one — with the replay model validated against real history (it predicts the actual 01:45:10 OK and the actual 22:32 ALARM).

The operator's standing principle behind this: **an acceptance criterion that depends on time passing is defective.** Verifying that a fix is live and remediates behaviour should be designed as a real-time activity. Waiting samples whichever day elapses, proves nothing about a worse one, cannot be re-run, and — as the bff5 replay showed — would not even have distinguished a flap from a true positive without doing this analysis anyway.
baseline.summary: [root-disk-pressure] rebar-gerrit root disk fills to 100% and takes Gerrit fully offline; the disk alarm resets to OK when the publishing host dies

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`AcliClient.search_issues` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:398-453`) memoizes its full result set per JQL string in `self._search_cache` — an unbounded dict with no TTL and no invalidation anywhere in the class — and it caches negative (empty) answers too. The docstring scopes the cache to "avoid redundant fetches when the caller paginates", but nothing enforces that scope: any caller that re-asks the same JQL over time on one client gets a permanently stale answer. Proven root cause of bug d30c (dutiable-shaded-honeyeater), where an index-visibility poll re-issued two constant JQLs on one client and only the first attempt ever reached Jira. The only correct handling in the tree reaches into the private attribute from outside the class: `access_check.py:176-178` does `cache.pop(jql, None)` before each retry, and the d30c fix (`tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` `_fresh_search`, ~:393-416) copies that reach-in. The freshness invariant is undocumented, unenforced, and satisfied only by encapsulation violations.

## Approach

1. **Establish client lifetime and document it at the cache definition.** Evidence already
   read from the tree: `reconcile_helpers.bind_operation_runtime`
   (`reconcile_helpers.py:675`) composes "the ONE operation runtime for this pass" per pass;
   `_backend_registry.select_backend` (`_backend_registry.py:60-76`) constructs a fresh
   backend on every call (no caching); the production entrypoint runs one
   `reconcile.reconcile_once` per process invocation (`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:450`).
   So an `AcliClient` — and its `_search_cache` — lives at most ONE reconcile pass. Record
   this at the cache definition in `acli.py` and in the audit comment on this ticket.
2. **Add the supported freshness door**: an `AcliClient.invalidate_search_cache(jql: str |
   None = None)` method — evicts the one JQL entry when given, clears the whole memo when
   `None`. Chosen over a `fresh=True` kwarg because it is purely additive (no
   `search_issues` signature change on the transport port, `_backend.py`) and matches the
   evict-then-search shape both existing call sites already use. Move `self._search_cache`
   initialization into `AcliClient.__init__` so the method needs no `hasattr` dance (and
   `search_issues` drops its lazy-init branch — a complexity improvement).
3. **Migrate both reach-in sites onto the door**: `access_check.py:176-178` and
   `_fresh_search` in `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` call
   `invalidate_search_cache(jql)` via a callable-guarded lookup (both sites accept arbitrary
   client classes/stubs today, so the guarded lookup preserves that tolerance while using
   the supported name).
4. **Document the negative-caching hazard** in the `search_issues` docstring: negative
   (empty) results are cached; a caller that re-asks the same JQL for freshness must call
   `invalidate_search_cache` first.
5. **Audit `binding_recovery.py:342-346`**: the pending-recovery loop issues each
   `labels = "rebar-id:<local_id>"` JQL once per pending id per pass (the hyphen fallback is
   a distinct JQL string), and its `search_miss_count` corroboration accumulates ACROSS
   passes — where each pass constructs a fresh client (step 1), so repeated misses are
   genuinely fresh queries and `_MISSES_BEFORE_UNBIND` cannot be satisfied by replays of one
   cached answer. Record this proof in the ticket comment and in the cache-definition note.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py` — init cache in `__init__`, add
  `invalidate_search_cache`, document lifetime + negative caching in the docstrings.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py` — migrate the JQL retry loop's
  reach-in onto `invalidate_search_cache`.
- `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` — migrate `_fresh_search` onto
  `invalidate_search_cache`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_search_cache_freshness.py` — new unit tests for the
  memo + door.

## Testing

Unit tests (new file, subprocess stubbed at the `AcliClient._run` seam, counting invocations):

- Happy: two `search_issues` calls with the same JQL run ONE subprocess (pins the existing
  memo, including a negative first answer staying cached).
- Freshness door: `invalidate_search_cache(jql)` then re-search re-runs the subprocess and
  returns the refreshed answer (a negative-to-positive flip becomes visible — the d30c
  class).
- Full clear: `invalidate_search_cache()` empties the memo for all JQLs.
- Edge: invalidating a never-searched JQL is a no-op (no raise, memo unchanged).

Existing coverage guards the migrations: the access-check retry loop and live-E2E poll tests keep passing with the reach-in replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `AcliClient` lifetime question is answered (one pass per instance in production)
      and documented at the cache definition in `acli.py` — checked by reading the committed
      docstring/comment citing `bind_operation_runtime` and `select_backend`.
- [x] `invalidate_search_cache(jql=None)` exists and `access_check.py` plus the d30c E2E
      poll use it instead of popping `_search_cache` directly — checked by
      `grep -rn "_search_cache" src tests` showing no reach-in outside `acli.py`, and by
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_search_cache_freshness.py`.
- [x] The `search_issues` docstring states that negative results are cached and repeat-query
      callers must invalidate first — checked by reading the docstring.
- [x] `binding_recovery.py:342-346` is audited: the proof that per-pass client construction
      makes cross-pass miss corroboration fresh is recorded as a comment on this ticket —
      checked by the comment's presence.
baseline.summary: Give AcliClient's per-JQL search memo a supported freshness door (it caches negatives forever)

# Live DC harness (rendered HTML) + cross-repo contract test

## Context / Problem
The DC codec is validated offline against pandoc's jira reader as a proxy, but the real Jira DC wiki renderer and Jira's own storage canonicalization differ from pandoc and cannot be modeled offline — that gap is the residual risk this story closes. The repo already runs live DC testing with a Dockerized Jira 8.17.1 instance in GitHub Actions (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`), so this extends that harness rather than building a new one. Separately, the sibling repo `agentic-dev-platform` imports the `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` seam from this package, so changing its behavior must be guarded by a contract test.

This story is the LIVE proof of the state-based echo-safety and settled-conflict behavior that `5c0e` (DC render robustness) and `3388` (cutover + echo suppression + local-wins conflict) deliver; it depends on both.

## Approach
Extend the existing Docker DC harness with a rich-text test that:
- renders a representative body and pushes it via the real API
  (`rebar.edit_ticket(local_id, repo_root=repo, description=value)`, the pattern
  already used by `_out_description` in
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`), and asserts **rendered HTML**
  through `?expand=renderedFields` — not just the wiki source via `?fields=description`
  — so we verify what Jira actually interprets (`*foo*`→bold, `h1.`→heading,
  `{code}`→macro). No `renderedFields`/`expand=` assertion exists in the harness
  today, so this is a genuinely new fidelity check.
- runs a second reconcile pass to assert **state-based echo-safety end-to-end** (the
  landed rich body decodes to a value the differ recognizes as unchanged → no
  re-push), exercising `3388`'s once-only-upgrade-then-converge path against the real
  renderer.
- performs a **both-sides concurrent edit** to assert `3388`'s settled conflict
  behavior with the precondition that policy actually requires. The
  `outbound-field-conflict` alert fires ONLY on a both-sides divergence
  (`local != baseline` AND `remote != baseline`, `outbound_field_diff.py:354-362`); a
  bare Jira-side edit with local unchanged is instead suppressed by the
  directionality guard (`_suppressed_by_inbound`) and mirrored inbound (Jira-wins)
  with NO conflict alert. So the live scenario is: (1) push a body and let a pass
  converge so a baseline is recorded; (2) make a **rebar-side** edit to the
  description AND a **Jira-side** edit to the same field before the next pass;
  (3) assert the next pass emits rebar's body (**local-wins**) and records the
  deduped `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description` bridge alert — the remote value
  is recorded, never silently destroyed (NOT a novel LWW clock; this is the a713 +
  `3388` policy proven live, mirroring `3388`'s `test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`
  precondition).

Gate it with the harness's existing skip markers (absent-harness / absent-extra) and the session-scoped PAT the harness already provisions. Add a contract test that pins the public shape/behavior of `normalize_rich_text` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py:134`, exposed as `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text`) so a change that would break the `agentic-dev-platform` import fails here first.

## Scope
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — new rich-text live test module (render+push,
  `?expand=renderedFields` HTML assertions, 2nd-pass echo, both-sides-concurrent-edit
  local-wins + conflict-alert assertion), reusing the existing conftest
  fixtures/skip markers.
- CI workflow for the DC harness job — ensure the new test runs in the existing
  amd64 Docker job (no new job).
- `tests/` — cross-repo `normalize_rich_text` contract test.

## Testing
- Live render fidelity: a pushed rich body's `renderedFields` HTML contains the
  expected bold/heading/code-macro markup (skipped when the harness/extra is absent).
- Live echo-safety: a second reconcile pass against the live instance pushes no
  description change (upgrade-then-converge holds against the real renderer).
- Live conflict: with a converged baseline, a **both-sides** edit (rebar-side AND
  Jira-side to the description) before the next pass keeps rebar's body and raises the
  deduped `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description` alert (remote value recorded,
  not clobbered); a bare Jira-only edit is NOT asserted as a conflict (it is
  Jira-wins inbound).
- Contract: `normalize_rich_text` accepts the documented inputs and returns the
  documented type/shape; a signature/behavior change fails
  `test_normalize_rich_text_contract`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [operator-attested] [x] The Docker DC harness has a rich-text test asserting rendered HTML via
  `?expand=renderedFields` (not just wiki source), covering bold/heading/code-macro;
  verified by the test running in the existing DC-harness CI job.
- [operator-attested] [x] The live test asserts state-based echo-safety across a second pass (no re-push)
  AND `3388`'s settled local-wins + `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert under the
  required **both-sides** precondition (converged baseline, then a rebar-side AND a
  Jira-side edit to the description → local-wins emit + deduped
  `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description`, remote value recorded, not silently
  destroyed); verified by the same live test.
- [x] A cross-repo contract test pins `normalize_rich_text`
  (`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text`) back-compat so a breaking change fails here
  first; verified by `test_normalize_rich_text_contract`.
baseline.summary: Live DC harness (rendered HTML) + cross-repo contract test

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` — **790 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (10 lines of headroom).

Ten lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split llm/workflow/executor.py (790 LOC) along its concern boundary

`bridge_fsck` reads `prev_snapshot.json` off disk as its offline Jira oracle and uses the **field values**, so narrowing prev to a key-set (A4-2) would silently degrade its drift classification. Fence it first. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why first
`bridge_fsck.py:306-308` loads the file as `jira_snapshot` and passes `fields=jira_snapshot[key]` into `ObservedJira.PRESENT` at `:344` and `:380`. With `{}` entries, membership still works but every field-based classification degrades. This is an **out-of-band consumer of the file itself**, not of `ctx.prev_snapshot`, so no test that exercises `reconcile_once` would catch it. It reads the **working tree**, so it is unaffected by clone filters.

## Approach
Make the field-dependence explicit: classify on membership where that is sufficient, and where a field value is genuinely required, report the classification as **indeterminate** rather than inferring from an empty dict. Do not silently treat absent fields as absent values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Against a **key-set** prev fixture (`{jira_key: {}}`), `bridge_fsck` drift classification is
      identical to its classification against the equivalent full-payload fixture for every case that
      does not require a field value, and reports **indeterminate** (never a false drift) for cases
      that do. Tier: **unit** with paired fixtures.
- [ ] Against a full-payload prev, behaviour is byte-identical to today (no regression for the
      pre-A4-2 world). Tier: **unit** golden comparison.
- [ ] `rebar bridge-fsck` exit code and JSON shape are unchanged for both fixtures. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py`, tests

Scope: S. No dependencies (independent of A1/A2/A3).
baseline.summary: A4-1: fence bridge_fsck's offline drift oracle before prev_snapshot is narrowed

## Context
433c requires AC boxes checked before close; but checking a box edits the description, and material_fingerprint (llm/plan_review/pass1.py) hashes the raw description — so the required box-flip trips stale-material in validate_attestation (attest.py) and forces a fresh LLM review before EVERY close. Observed on all four closes of d3ed/433c/9d07/a584. Checkbox STATE is progress metadata (verified independently by the completion verifier); the ITEM TEXT is the material.

## Approach
Normalize checkbox state before hashing in material_fingerprint: case-insensitive `- [x]`/`- [X]` → `- [ ]` (also `*` bullets), line-anchored, so flipping a box never changes the fingerprint while ANY text change still does. Single seam: both the plan-review close gate and the completion-verifier staleness check recompute through material_fingerprint via current_material_fingerprint.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py (material_fingerprint: normalize description basis)
- tests: unit on fingerprint invariance + a close-gate-level regression

## Testing
RED first: fingerprint(desc with [ ]) == fingerprint(desc with [x]) fails today; any non-checkbox text edit still changes the fingerprint; validate_attestation no longer returns stale-material after a pure box flip.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Flipping any AC box (either direction, x or X, - or * bullet) leaves the material fingerprint unchanged.
- [x] Any other description edit still changes the fingerprint (staleness preserved).
- [x] A signed plan-review attestation stays valid across a pure box-flip edit (no stale-material at close).
- [x] Existing attestations signed on unchecked descriptions remain valid for checked descriptions (normalization is backward-compatible by construction).
baseline.summary: AC checkbox flips invalidate plan-review attestation (stale-material on every close)

# Four-pass review KERNEL: extract the shared evidence → verify → decide → coach framework (plan-review as reference)

## Context

Industry practice and 2025–2026 research converge on a **multi-pass** LLM review: a finder
surfaces cited EVIDENCE against a locked rubric (no model-emitted severity/confidence); a
SEPARATE verifier validates each finding via atomic, independent binary sub-questions; a
DETERMINISTIC policy (not the model) decides severity and blocking; and an affirmative COACH
maps the surviving advisories to a locked move registry. That is **four passes** (the coach is
Pass-4, demonstrated by plan-review) — the framework's name is updated from three-pass to
four-pass.

The framework is no longer hypothetical. The **plan-review gate (epic `5fd2`)** realized the
full four-pass concretely and runs it in production as the *sole* plan-review gate on the v3
workflow engine: Pass-1 finder (evidence contract `{finding, criteria[], evidence[],
scenarios[], impact}`), Pass-2 verifier (severity attributes + a typed binary sub-answer set),
Pass-3 deterministic `pass3_decide`, Pass-4 coach (move registry, rendered deterministically).
Recent work hardened it further (a non-frontier verifier-model default, token-budget verify
chunking, the coach gated on surviving>0). BUT that implementation lives INSIDE
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — it is **not a shared kernel**. A second review surface (the
code-review capability, epic `b744`) would otherwise COPY the passes, forking the verification
vocabulary and the deterministic decision math — exactly the silent-drift class this repo
already paid for once (the retired bespoke vs workflow verify divergence).

This epic **extracts** the value-bearing, divergence-dangerous passes into a reusable kernel
that both gates consume, so the decision core and the binary vocabulary cannot fork.

## Supersedes the prior three-pass epic (`9da1`)

This replaces "Realign rebar reviews to three-pass; migrate existing reviewers" because the
scope changed on three counts:
1. It is **four** passes (the coach pass), not three.
2. "Migrate the existing reviewers" is dropped: `src/rebar/llm/code_review.py` is a throwaway
   DEMO, not a migration target — real code review is epic `b744`, which CONSUMES this kernel.
3. The framework is already built (in plan-review), so the work is **extraction + a clean
   consumer seam**, not a from-scratch build. The old epic's 10 overlay-catalog comments are
   inputs to `b744`, not to this epic's deliverable.

## What the kernel is — and is NOT

**SHARED (extract into the kernel — domain-agnostic, divergence-dangerous):**
- **Pass-2** finding-verifier: operates on a findings list + a domain context; emits per finding
  `{severity_attributes, binary}`. Owns the single `verification` output contract (the binary
  sub-question vocabulary + the severity-attribute enums) and the verify orchestration already
  built for plan-review (token-budget chunking, merge-by-global-index, the verifier-model
  default).
- **Pass-3** deterministic decision: the one `pass3_decide` (+ math: validity from the graded
  binary fraction; impact from the ordinal-mapped severity attributes; the conditional
  cited-reference veto; per-criterion thresholds, parameterized).
- **Pass-4** coach MECHANISM: move-selection → deterministic template render → the bounded
  noun-phrase subject validator → the no-free-prose discipline → gate-on-surviving>0; plus a
  pluggable move-registry SCHEMA.

**NOT shared (already reusable / engine-provided):**
- Pass-1 criteria→batch orchestration — the `ProductionBatchRunner` already does token/budget
  finder batching; the workflow `batch` step already aggregates. Not re-abstracted.
- The workflow shell (steps/branch/batch/`RunnerAgentStep`/`gate_dispatch`) — the v3 engine
  already provides it; each gate keeps a thin workflow.

**Per-gate PLUG-INS (the consumer seam):** criteria + routing, finder prompts, the
domain-context assembler (plan text vs diff), the verify-prompt preamble, and the move-catalog
CONTENT (planning moves vs code moves).

## Enforcement — keep reuse honest WITHOUT making the workflow system brittle

Enforce STRUCTURE mechanically and BEHAVIOR via evals; never enforce prompt *text* via a lint
(an anti-pattern — DSPy / Guardrails / Instructor / promptfoo all enforce typed contracts +
output/behavior, not prompt-string greps):
- **Vocabulary** → ONE registered `verification` schema. Validate via the existing TOLERANT
  stack (json-repair + bounded retry + pydantic-ai native outputs) and DEGRADE to INDETERMINATE
  on an unparseable turn — never hard-crash a gate. Keep the schema small/flat (the
  reliability cost of strict validation is the failure mode to avoid).
- **Decision interpretation** → ONE `pass3_decide` function (thresholds parameterized per
  criterion).
- **Soft prompt rules** (atomicity; independence — don't show the finding's own conclusion;
  allow "insufficient"; verdict-with-citation-NOT-fix) → a canonical RULES SCAFFOLD + kernel
  doc for discoverability, ENFORCED by BEHAVIORAL evals (deterministic FakeRunner assertions on
  the gate path in CI + a small GATED live eval kept OFF the blocking CI path). **No
  prompt-marker lint** (explicitly rejected as brittle/gameable).
- **Move registry** → registered schema + load-time validation, with a `triggers`/applies_when
  applicability field.
- **Drift** → reuse the existing contract / derived-prompt-index drift gate (it keys on the
  output CONTRACT, not on prompt wording).

## Out of scope (decisions recorded, not deliverables)

- **Completion verifier stays single-pass.** It is already binary-per-given-criterion; a full
  independent verify pass ≈2× the agentic cost for a small, unmeasured accuracy gain. The one
  cheap lever (the binary/independence discipline in-prompt) was applied separately, not here.
- The throwaway `code_review.py` demo reviewers (real code review = `b744`).
- Threshold/severity calibration (separately deferred; thresholds start high → mostly advisory).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A shared kernel module (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`) houses: Pass-2
      `verify_findings(findings, *, context, model, headroom)`, the registered `verification`
      contract, Pass-3 `pass3_decide` (+ math, per-criterion thresholds parameterized), and the
      Pass-4 coach mechanism + move-registry schema.
- [ ] The plan-review gate consumes the kernel for Pass-2/3/4; an offline (FakeRunner) test
      asserts the produced verdict is unchanged vs the pre-extraction behavior (reuse, not fork).
- [ ] The `verification` contract is the single source of the binary-question vocabulary +
      severity-attribute enums; validation uses json-repair + bounded retry and DEGRADES to
      INDETERMINATE (never crashes a gate) on an unparseable turn.
- [ ] The move-registry schema includes a `triggers`/applies_when field; coach move-selection
      applies a DETERMINISTIC applicability filter, then the LLM picks among the applicable moves
      (closing the prior wholly-LLM-delegated selection gap).
- [ ] A canonical verifier-rules scaffold + kernel doc record the soft prompt rules; a
      BEHAVIORAL eval (offline FakeRunner on the gate path; a small gated live eval off the
      blocking CI path) verifies the rules are obeyed. NO prompt-marker lint is added.
- [ ] A documented consumer seam enumerates the per-gate plug-points (criteria, finder prompts,
      domain-context assembler, verify preamble, move-catalog) that `b744` consumes; this epic
      `blocks` `b744`.
- [ ] Out-of-scope decisions are recorded (completion verifier single-pass + rationale;
      throwaway code_review.py not migrated; calibration deferred).
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
- [ ] A shared four-pass kernel module exists (Pass-2 verifier + `verification` contract; Pass-3
- [ ] The plan-review gate is rewired to CONSUME the kernel for Pass-2/3/4 with NO behavior change
- [ ] A documented consumer SEAM (the per-gate plug-points + the rules scaffold) that `b744` builds
- [ ] Enforcement is structural (schemas) + behavioral (evals), with no prompt-text lint;
baseline.summary: Four-pass review kernel: extract the shared evidence->verify->decide->coach framework (plan-review as reference)

## Context / Problem
After operation-family cutovers, leaving generic `_call_with_retry`, `_best_effort`, duck-typed production dispatch, or legacy write routes active would preserve retry multiplication and allow future code to bypass the coordinator. Preview/log consumers also need a stable versioned contract for lifecycle and deferred outcomes before expand can contract.

## Outcome
Finish the expand/contract migration: route every supported live mutation through typed plans/coordinator/adapters, remove obsolete physical-retry and write fallbacks, fail loudly for unsupported production paths, and seal manifests, logs, pass cursor/tallies, documentation, and local verified-fake validation. Preserve existing mutation shape while making lifecycle/retry/fuse outcomes explicit and observable.

## Plan
1. Inventory every Cloud/DC mutation leaf and prove it reaches the typed coordinator. Remove generic whole-operation retry, `_best_effort` write swallowing, production class-name/duck fallbacks, and duplicate SDK/adapter retry owners.
2. Keep compatibility only at serialized/public read boundaries. An unsupported live action raises a typed pre-effect error; tests may use explicit fakes implementing the declared protocol.
3. Finalize versioned preview/manifest sections for lifecycle intents, logical/physical attempts, delay source/value, budgets, scope, disposition, `retry_not_before`, fuse state, and exact per-ticket/pass outcomes. Redact secrets and bound diagnostic size.
4. Advance cursor/baseline/binding state only for proven postconditions. Deferred, failed, skipped, and commit-unknown work remains eligible for later re-observation and is never reported as applied.
5. Add ADR/docs for retry ownership, failure taxonomy, scoped fuse, label-first create containment, explicit behavior deltas, expand/contract rollback, and future adapter obligations. Run portable verified-fake Cloud/DC end-to-end tests; retain bounded live probes as optional operator evidence.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- A dispatch census test enumerates every `MutationDirection`/`MutationAction` and provider route, asserting one typed owner or an intentional pre-effect unsupported error.
- End-to-end fake Cloud/DC passes cover mixed success, transient recovery, long-delay deferral, permanent ticket failure, auth/provider stop, fuse open/reset, create containment, restart, and delivery failure.
- Golden preview/log/manifest tests pin existing mutation fields plus additive versioned sections, redaction, bounded diagnostics, and exact tally/exit semantics.
- Static/string and runtime poison tests fail if removed legacy helpers or hidden retries are reachable from production.

## Compatibility / rollback
Contract only after shadow parity and each family cutover test passes. A pre-contract release can revert per-family routing; after removal, rollback is a code revert that re-observes remote state and never compensates by deleting successful Jira work. Stored ticket/binding/event formats are unchanged; additive manifest fields are versioned and ignorable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A route census proves every supported Cloud/DC mutation uses exactly one typed coordinator/adapter path and no hidden SDK, generic wrapper, `_best_effort`, or duck-typed production fallback remains reachable.
- [x] Unsupported production actions fail before local/remote effects with a typed provider-neutral error.
- [x] Preview, manifest, and logs preserve existing mutation fields and add versioned redacted logical-attempt, lifecycle, delay/budget, disposition, fuse, and `retry_not_before` data.
- [x] Cursor, baseline, and binding state advance only for proven postconditions; deferred/failed/skipped/commit-unknown work is never counted as applied and remains recoverable next pass.
- [x] Portable verified-fake Cloud/DC end-to-end suites cover the approved taxonomy, retry envelope, fuse, create containment, restart, and partial-outcome behavior without external credentials.
- [x] ADR and operator docs record ownership, intentional behavior changes, future adapter contract, no-dual-write cutover, and rollback that never deletes successful Jira work.

## Inherited invariant — pre-observation repair boundary (folded in from insectile-modest-martin, 2026-08-19)

Operator decision: `insectile-modest-martin` (d7b9-ac42) is CLOSED and its requirement now lives here. This ticket edits `reconcile.py`, which sits at **799 of the 800-line cap**, so it must perform a behaviour-preserving extraction (extract along an existing call-graph seam; NEVER raise the limit). That extraction must preserve one specific ordering invariant that is easy to break silently.

**The invariant.** The call `binding_store.repair_at_write_boundary(persist=persist, scoped=bool(scoped_ids))` must remain:

- **AFTER** the under-lock staleness validation (`ensure_selection_current`) — a pass whose
  selection is stale has not established that its view is current and has no standing to repair; and
- **BEFORE** the pass's first remote issue fetch (`fetcher.fetch_snapshot` / `compute_snapshot`).

The pre-observation half is the one with teeth. A durable tombstone is authoritative retirement intent. A pass that fetched first could observe the retired issue answer 200 and then complete that issue's retirement in the same breath as fresh evidence that it is alive; repairing first keeps the recorded decision from racing a later observation. **Move the call after the fetch and the repair still runs, still writes correct-looking bytes, and is silently wrong.**

`run_differs.py` is specifically NOT an alternative home: `reconcile._load_snapshots` performs the first remote fetch inside itself, and both `bind_operation_runtime` and `run_differs()` run after it returns, so no position inside `run_differs.py` can precede remote observation. Recorded in ADR 0099.

**The two tests that are the only guard** (both drive or name `_load_snapshots` directly, so an extraction that renames or re-splits that phase WILL force someone to touch them) — in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_recovery_write_boundary.py`:

- `test_repair_runs_before_the_first_remote_observation` — the behavioural oracle; drives the real
  load phase with an event recorder and asserts the repair event precedes the fetch event.
- `test_the_repair_is_invoked_from_reconcile_and_not_from_run_differs` — a structural anchor.

The tempting shortcut under time pressure is to relax the assertion rather than re-anchor it. **Relaxing it is the thing to avoid.**

### Additional acceptance criteria (inherited)
- [x] After this change to `reconcile.py`, the repair call still runs after the under-lock staleness
      gate and before the pass's first remote issue fetch.
- [x] `test_repair_runs_before_the_first_remote_observation` still fails when the call is moved to a
      post-fetch position — demonstrated by SEEDING that move and observing RED, not merely by the
      suite being green.
- [x] If the load phase is renamed or re-split, the boundary tests are RE-ANCHORED to the new
      structure rather than relaxed, and the ordering assertion survives in a form that still
      discriminates.
- [x] `reconcile.py` remains within the 800-line cap without raising the limit.
- [x] ADR 0099's invocation-boundary section is updated if the realized position changes shape.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S5 — Complete coordinator cutover and remove legacy write fallbacks
