# J3 — Pin a `RichTextCodec` contract (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

Rich-text encoding is one of the three real differences between Jira Cloud and Data Center: Cloud's REST v3 requires Atlassian Document Format (a nested JSON document; sending a plain string returns 400), while DC's REST v2 carries descriptions and comment bodies as plain text / wiki markup. Today ADF is hardwired into the Cloud path — `adapters/jira/adf.py` provides `fit_text_to_adf_limit` and the decode, and `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72`'s `map_fields_to_remote` calls `outbound_fields._load_adf()` inline. PR #120's answer was to copy that whole method and change the single ADF line, which is the duplication this epic exists to prevent.

## Approach

Define a `RichTextCodec` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with two operations: `fit_outbound` (fit a local string to the deployment's rich-text limit, returning the deployment's wire shape) and `decode_inbound` (turn a wire body into plain text). Provide two implementations — `AdfCodec`, which delegates to the existing `adapters/jira/adf.py` with no logic change, and `WikiTextCodec`, a character-count fit plus an identity decode.

The shared `map_fields_to_remote` then takes the codec as a constructor dependency, so exactly one implementation of the mapping exists and the ADF-vs-wiki difference is a parameter. The same codec is the dependency J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] injects into the relocated `_sanitize_description`, whose `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call IS this seam — so if J2 lands first with a minimal `Callable[[str], str]` fit function as a placeholder, this story widens that placeholder to the full `RichTextCodec` and re-points the sanitizer at it. Either landing order works; what must not happen is `jira_family/` importing the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py` directly. Cloud is constructed with `AdfCodec` and its behavior is unchanged, proven by J1's pinned oracles [rebar:acb2-1823-2f0d-415b].

**Alternative rejected:** a boolean or enum flag (`use_adf=True`) threaded through the mapper. It puts the branch back inside the shared code, grows a branch per deployment type, and gives the codec no place to own its own limit constant.

**Alternative rejected:** copying `map_fields_to_remote` per adapter (PR #120). One line differs; the other thirty drift.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (new) — the Protocol + `WikiTextCodec`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py` — wrapped by `AdfCodec`, logic unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` — the shared mapper takes the codec.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier for each codec (pure transforms) plus a contract test run against BOTH implementations, since the point of the story is that they are interchangeable behind one Protocol.

- shared contract, parameterized over both codecs: a short string round-trips through
  `fit_outbound` → `decode_inbound` to itself; an over-limit string is fitted to at most the limit and its
  decode is a prefix of the original.
- Cloud-specific: `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` produces the same ADF document the current
  `fit_text_to_adf_limit` produces for the same input — asserted against J1's pinned value.
- DC-specific: `WikiTextCodec` truncates at its character limit and marks the truncation; `decode_inbound`
  returns `""` for `None` and passes a string through unchanged.
- contrast case: a non-`str` value is passed through untouched by both codecs rather than coerced, matching the
  current mapper's behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test runs against both `AdfCodec` and `WikiTextCodec` and passes for each
- [ ] `AdfCodec` output for the J1-pinned input equals the J1-pinned expected ADF document
- [ ] `grep -rn '_load_adf\|fit_text_to_adf_limit' src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` shows those names
      reached only from inside `AdfCodec`
- [ ] exactly one definition of `map_fields_to_remote` exists in the tree
baseline.summary: J3 — pin a RichTextCodec contract (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for Data Center)

## Symptom

No workflow step runs `npx playwright install chromium`, so the `browser_runner` fixture self-skips on "Chromium unavailable" in CI. **The browser test tier never actually runs there.**

Surfaced while implementing bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`; pre-existing and untouched by that change.

## Why this matters more than a normal skip

A skipped tier is indistinguishable from a passing one in the summary line. CI reports green, and the green is partly vacuous — nobody is told that a whole class of assertions never executed. That is the same failure shape as two other defects found on 2026-09-04:

- `9a17`: provisioning cost was charged to a test budget, and the resulting worker kill reported as a
  crash rather than a timeout — the true cause was invisible in the summary.
- `90c7`: the `scanner-integration` job was added and **never ran** on the change that introduced it,
  yet that change still received `Verified +1`. A vote was cast on a job that did not execute.

In all three the gate said "fine" while not actually checking. This ticket is the mildest of the three, but it is the same class: **absence of execution reported as success.**

Note also that change 2600 moved `playwright` to `optionalDependencies` and provisions with `--omit=optional` for selections containing no browser test. That is correct and deliberate — it cut the cold install from 15 packages / 30M to 11 / 12M. It does mean the browser path now needs provisioning *explicitly* when it is wanted, rather than arriving incidentally.

## What needs deciding, and it is a real fork

Either:
- **(a) Run the tier in CI** — add a browser-provisioning step (`npx playwright install chromium`,
  plus its OS dependencies) so `browser_runner` actually executes. Costs CI minutes and adds a
  download to the critical path; the browser binary is large and would want caching.
- **(b) Keep it skipped, but make the skip LOUD and INTENTIONAL** — assert somewhere that the tier is
  deliberately not run in CI, so the skip is a recorded decision rather than an accident, and a
  future reader is not misled into thinking browser behaviour is covered.

**(b) is not a lesser option** and may well be right: the tier may be genuinely local-only by design. What is not acceptable is the current state, where the skip is silent and looks like coverage.

Whichever is chosen must respect `project.portability` (a blocking plan-review criterion): the behaviour cannot depend on a specific CI provider. A developer with no CI must get the same, comprehensible result.

## Acceptance criteria

Deterministic, verifiable in one run.

1. The disposition is explicit and recorded in the tree: either the tier runs in CI, or a test/assert
   states that it is deliberately skipped there and why.
2. If (a): `browser_runner` tests actually execute in CI — demonstrated by a run where they report as
   passed rather than skipped, and the browser download is cached rather than fetched every run.
3. If (b): a check fails if the tier is silently skipped **without** the recorded opt-out — i.e. the
   skip cannot revert to being accidental. Demonstrate by removing the marker and observing RED.
4. Either way, the summary a reader sees distinguishes "this tier was deliberately not run" from
   "this tier passed". No configuration where absence of execution is indistinguishable from success.
5. Portable: the chosen behaviour works in a checkout with no CI provider.

## File impact

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, `tests/e2e/conftest.py` (the `browser_runner` fixture and its skip reason), possibly `Makefile` and `tests/e2e/js/package.json`.
baseline.summary: browser_runner tier never executes in CI: chromium is never installed, so the tier silently self-skips and the green is partly vacuous

# Live rich-text cutover + state echo suppression + concurrency conflict safety

## Context / Problem
Cut the live Cloud and DC send paths to the rich codecs (needs `e59d`, `271c`). DC's codec is lossy/one-way, so `decode(encode(x))==x` cannot gate loops; echo suppression is by **state**: current Jira value vs last-synced baseline (ADR 0026; `binding_store.get_baseline`/`set_baseline`; `_BASELINE_FIELDS` in `peer_state.py`).

**Reused unchanged:** the ADR-0026/d6bd baseline diff (`get_baseline` via `InboundMapper`, `outbound_field_diff.py`; `description` in `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`, via `_compute_field_changes`); once-only re-emit convergence needs the codec law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (`test_rich_text_codec.py`, a32a) plus round-trip idempotence. **The non-idempotent tail is bounded.** Consecutiveness is PERSISTED, not inferred: the inline binding record carries a change-gated `rich_reemit` counter beside `rich_sha`, incremented when a field is emitted with `rich_sha` unchanged and reset to 0 when `rich_sha` changes or the baseline refreshes — so it stays 0 (no churn) on healthy bodies. At `rich_reemit == RICH_REEMIT_OBSERVE_AT` do ONE post-push GET and overlay it via `binding_store.merge_baseline`, so `_advance_baselines` REMAINS the sole baseline writer. The GET lives in `apply_handlers.handle_update`. Comment dedup intact.

## The live cutover
- **Cloud:** point the four `AdfCodec` ops at `adf.py`'s Markdown-aware fns
  (`to_wire→markdown_to_adf`, `decode_inbound→adf_to_markdown`,
  `normalize_outbound→adf_to_markdown∘markdown_to_adf`, `fit_outbound→fit_markdown_to_adf_limit`)
  + whole-codec plain-text fallback; pin test `test_rich_text_codec.py:198/205/207/208`. Reroute:
  encode `adapters/jira/acli.py`, `acli_cli_ops.py`; fit `jira_fields.py`; compares
  `adf.normalize_description`/`adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` (`outbound_fields.py`,
  `inbound_differ.py`) — **send-fit and compare-fit must be one transform**.
- **DC:** `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` delegates to `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki` (`271c`);
  **redefine `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`**, restoring the
  codec law. Send composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))` (`outbound_mapper.py`) →
  rendered wiki on `issue.update(fields=…)`. **TWO other DC send sites:**
  `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`) AND
  `_issues._translate_create_fields` (via `_description_codec()`) — BOTH must compose
  `to_wire(fit_outbound(...))` or they ship un-rendered Markdown on CREATE while updates ship
  rendered wiki. Retarget the DC pin tests.

## Design decisions
1. **Two DISTINCT compares — do not collapse.** *Emit (`outbound_field_diff.py:288`),
   local-vs-REMOTE — UNCHANGED:* `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local))` vs
   `canonical_remote["description"]` = `decode_inbound(remote_wire)`
   (`inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local`); both decoded → lossy round-trip cancels; an
   un-normalized remote forces the one-time legacy re-emit (`outbound_fields.py:586`).
   *Baseline (`_suppressed_by_inbound` `:323`, `_local_matches_baseline` `:464`) — LOCAL side
   normalized:* raw local Markdown vs `decode(baseline_wire)` differ → "local changed" every
   pass; route the local side through `RichTextCodec.normalize_outbound` (`decode∘to_wire`, via
   `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote`), sole normalizer.
   `_remote_matches_baseline` (`:399`) — UNCHANGED.
2. **Concurrent both-sides edit — unchanged (a713 local-wins).** Both differing from
   `baseline` → `outbound_field_diff.py:450-457` appends `(jira_key, fname)` to
   `conflict_sink`; `run_differs.py:_emit_outbound_field_alerts` (`:97`) emits the deduped
   alert. Emit stays local-wins; inbound description stays **additive**
   (`conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES`, `resolve_additive`).
3. **Shared-op side effect.** The redefinition also reaches the DC comment-diff dedup key
   (`outbound_comments._diff_comments` via `_resolve_codec`); that path keeps the
   identity/plain normalizer UNCHANGED.
4. **Origin-gating + churn.** Updates fire only when `local != baseline`, so a Jira-authored
   construct (panel/mention/date, decoded by `adf.py`) survives an edit-free pass.
   Store a change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) **inline** in the
   binding (0.07 KB/version; a per-pass timestamp reproduced `0303`'s 12.62 KB anti-pattern);
   the compare never writes back.

## Scope (IN)
- `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` (+ fallback), `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`, Cloud
  consumer sites above, `backend.py` (`:57`) CREATE path — gated.
- **Cutover flag (NEW config, defaults OFF):** `reconciler.rich_text_cutover`
  (`off`|`cloud`|`dc`|`both`) across the standard four-file surface (`_config_schema.py`,
  `_config_sources.py`, `tests/golden/config_surface.json`, `docs/config.md`). Gates both send
  paths; off = plain/identity wire (the rollback). Enable per client, Cloud then DC, after canary.
- `binding_store.py` inline `rich_sha`; `outbound_field_diff.py` (`:323`, `:464`) local-side normalize
  only (`:292`, `_apply_mutations` untouched); tests under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`.

## Scope (OUT)
- No new three-way merge, LWW clock, conflict sink or parallel `norm()`; no change to
  `FIELD_CLASSES`/`_field_contract` or `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`; comment
  rendering and the DC dedup-key migration (`789c`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Cloud: a converted ADF description posts once; a second pass emits zero updates
  (`test_cloud_cutover_sends_structured_adf` + `test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes`).
- [x] DC: `issue.update(fields=…)` gets rendered wiki, not raw Markdown; a second pass emits
  zero updates (`test_dc_cutover_sends_rendered_wiki` +
  `test_cutover_does_not_mass_rewrite_already_synced_bodies`).
- [x] TWO distinct compares: emit on the plain inbound-decoded remote; baseline compares'
  LOCAL side through `normalize_outbound` to match `decode(baseline_wire)`; a no-edit body stays
  suppressed across passes, a rebar edit shows changed, a legacy body upgrades once then
  converges (`test_lossy_baseline_compare_local_normalized`, `test_legacy_body_upgrades_once`,
  `test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes`).
- [x] The `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` redefinition leaves the DC comment-diff dedup key
  unshifted; comment-diff converges with no duplicate re-post
  (`test_diff_comments_cutover_neutral.py`, all 4 tests).
- [x] Outbound fires only on a rebar-originated change (`local != baseline`); the baseline
  advances via `_advance_baselines`; a benign re-canonicalization converges in one re-emit, no
  re-GET (`test_echo_rebar_origin_only`, `test_recanonicalization_converges_within_one_reemit`).
- [x] A Jira-authored construct (panel/mention/date) survives a later rebar pass under
  origin-gating (`test_jira_native_construct_survives_an_edit_free_pass`).
- [x] A concurrent both-sides body edit keeps rebar's body (local-wins) AND raises the
  `outbound-field-conflict` alert, recording the remote value (`test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`).
- [x] An inline change-gated 8-byte `rich_sha` is stored, no per-pass timestamp, changing 0
  entries on a no-op pass; ≤0.07 KB/version asserted on the serialized per-binding delta
  (`test_rich_reemit_state.py`). NOTE: no "git-delta harness" exists in the repo; the byte-level
  assertion measures the same quantity.
- [x] Flag-gated, defaults OFF (opt-in per client, not a 100%-traffic flip), reverting to the
  plain/identity wire when off (`test_cutover_defaults_off`,
  `test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain`).
- [x] With the marklas extra absent, the cutover path emits the plain-text ADF wire (today's
  behaviour), raising nothing; verified by `test_cloud_functions_degrade_without_marklas`
  (`rich=True`, `adf._marklas` stubbed to None) and `test_dc_degrades_without_pandoc`.
baseline.summary: State-based echo suppression + LWW conflict safety

# Committed store compatibility record with a fail-closed capability gate

Introduce a committed store-level compatibility record (`format_version` + `required_capabilities`) that a v1.0 binary reads before any mutating or externally-publishing operation, failing closed on an unknown version or required capability while keeping reads and diagnostics available. (Readiness Finding 2 — verified VALID against `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/{compact,fsck,init}.py`, `docs/migrations.md`.)

## Why

rebar's migration mechanism is an idempotent desired-state ensure-registry, not an ordered ledger: `run_ensures` runs every unit under the write lock, converts exceptions to `failed`, and **returns normally** (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` docstring "Never raises"; init/boot never abort). Event compatibility is preserve-and-ignore: unknown event types are skipped in replay (`reducer/_replay.py:195-196`) and omitted from the compaction fold but kept on disk (`_commands/compact.py:179-195`), and `fsck` emits an informational WARN that does not increment `issue_count` or stop operation (`_commands/fsck.py:229-252`, which itself notes "a reconcile host on an old binary may push stale state").

This forward-compat is correct for *optional additive* data — it prevents an old compactor from deleting new bytes. But there is **no committed store-format-version or required-capability record** (confirmed absent; `SCHEMA_VERSION` is a stamp, never compared to fail closed). So an old binary computes state that omits the unknown event and can then emit a new event, compact, evaluate close/verify policy, or push a stale field to Jira from that incomplete state. `docs/migrations.md` explicitly files the "A-tier ledger + committed store-format version that fails closed" under future work. **The reader must ship in v1.0**: an already-installed v1.0 binary cannot be taught later to inspect a record whose existence and semantics were not defined in v1.0 — so to ever mark a store as requiring a post-v1.0 capability, v1.0 must already know how to detect and refuse unknown required capabilities.

## What

Adopt git's repository-format-version pattern (`core.repositoryformatversion` + `extensions.*`: an implementation that does not understand the advertised format or a required extension must not operate, because continuing can produce incorrect results or lose data), and git's staged rollout (teach readers first, make writing opt-in, default later):

- **The record.** Add a committed store-level record, minimally
  `{"format_version": 1, "required_capabilities": []}`, at a fixed store path (e.g.
  `.store-compat.json`). It is **committed to the `tickets` branch** (not
  git-ignored) — it is the shared fact the gate reads. Write it with the store's
  standard write-to-tempfile-then-atomic-rename pattern so a partial/interrupted
  write never leaves a truncated file.
- **Recognised-capability vocabulary.** The new module exports
  `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset()` — the set of capability strings
  **this** binary understands. The gate blocks when any entry in a record's
  `required_capabilities` is not in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. Future capabilities are
  added to this set only when the feature that consumes them ships (git
  `extensions.*` semantics).
- **The gate error.** The module exports `StoreIncompatibleError(Exception)`, raised
  by the gate; entry-point callers convert it to the existing `CommandError` /
  non-zero exit path (as other gate errors do), with a message naming the
  unsupported version/capability.
- **Four record states (explicit).** (1) **Absent** → implicit legacy format
  version 0, compatible / pass-through, NOT blocked. (2) **Present + compatible** →
  pass. (3) **Present + incompatible** (unknown `format_version` or a
  `required_capabilities` entry ∉ `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`) → **fail-closed**. (4)
  **Present + unreadable/corrupt** (JSON parse error, truncation, permission denied)
  → **fail-closed** with a diagnostic message naming the parse error and the record
  path (a corrupt record is NOT treated as absent — that would silently bypass the
  gate).
- **Expand phase (writing the record into pre-v1.0 stores).** Every store created by
  a pre-v1.0 build is state (1). An idempotent ensure unit (School B) writes the
  record at the current version when absent, at init / fsck-repair / MCP-boot.
  **Because `run_ensures` is fail-silent** (a `LockTimeout` silently skips the whole
  sweep; exceptions become `failed` and it returns normally), the covered-write path
  must not *depend* on the ensure sweep having run: the gate treats absent as
  pass-through regardless, and the record is written opportunistically. So a missed
  sweep never blocks writes — it only defers stamping the record to a later covered
  operation. **absent = legacy/needs-migration, not blocked; present-incompatible or
  corrupt = blocked.**
- **Gate at the true structural choke point, NOT by enumerating call-sites.** "No
  mutation without the gate" must not rest on a hand-maintained list a future path can
  bypass. The single convergence point for **all lock-based store mutations** is
  **`lock.acquire()` in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`** — both the `write_lock()` context
  manager AND the direct callers that bypass it (`txn.py`'s `_acquire_write_lock` for
  claim/transition, `compact.py:167`/`:415`, `fsck.py:419`) call `acquire()`. Insert
  the `check_store_compat()` gate **inside `lock.acquire()`**, after `canonical_tracker()`
  resolves the path and before the fcntl/mkdir legs — so every lock-holding path
  (context-manager and raw-handle) is covered by one insertion point, with no
  enumeration. **Gate ALL `lock.acquire()` unconditionally — no `read_only` parameter
  needed.** The diagnostic exemption is already **structural**: `fsck`'s diagnostic
  path reads ticket data **without acquiring the lock at all**, so it is inherently
  ungated and stays available; only `fsck`'s **repair** path (which *does* call
  `lock.acquire()` at `fsck.py:419`), and `compact.py`/`txn.py`, hold the lock and are
  therefore gated. This is simpler and less error-prone than a read/write-intent flag.
- **Two paths do NOT go through `lock.acquire()` and each gets its own explicit gate:**
  1. **`fsck_recover.py`** performs raw `git cherry-pick`/`rebase --continue`/`merge
     --abort` via its `_git()` helper with **no locking at all** — so it is genuinely
     un-gated by the lock choke point. Add an explicit `check_store_compat(tracker_dir)`
     at the top of `fsck_recover_cli` before any mutation. (Wrapping the mutation block
     in `write_lock` too would additionally close a real pre-existing concurrency gap,
     but at minimum the explicit gate is required.)
  2. **Outbound Jira publish** — the push/reconcile side effect is a **remote API
     call**, not a lock-held write. Jira writes are scattered
     (`create_issue`/`update_issue`/`delete_issue`/`add_comment` across
     `apply_outbound.py` + `dispatch_one.py`), but they all funnel once per pass
     through **`reconcile._apply_mutations()`** (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py`,
     which calls `applier.apply(...)`). Gate there, **after the `persist=True` check**
     (so dry-run / reconcile-check / cap-0 no-write passes are excluded) and before
     `applier.apply()` — mirroring the existing fail-closed cross-project guard
     precedent at `applier.py:637-652` ("refuse BEFORE issuing any Jira write … abort
     the whole pass, no partial writes"). **Use the reconciler's own tracker path**
     (`repo_root / ".tickets-tracker"`, hardcoded at `reconcile.py:133/670`), NOT
     `config.tracker_dir()`, since the reconciler resolves the store directly.
- **Completeness is CI-enforced.** A coverage test/lint greps the tree for **both**
  `lock.acquire(` and `write_lock(` (and asserts each routes through the gate) plus
  asserts `fsck_recover_cli` calls `check_store_compat` — so a new un-gated write path,
  in any of the acquisition forms, fails CI rather than relying on this prose list.
- **Read/diagnostic allowance.** Under an incompatible/corrupt record, the read-only
  commands — `fsck` (diagnostic mode), `show`, `list`, `search` — stay available
  (exit 0) and report the unsupported version/capability (structured, machine-checkable
  output). `fsck`'s **repair** mode (write-intent) is gated like any other mutation.
- **Rollback safety (decided, then proven).** Post-rollback the committed
  `.store-compat.json` remains on the `tickets` branch unchanged, and a pre-v1.0 binary
  **ignores it** (ignored-unknown → rollback-safe): `.store-compat.json` is a *new*
  file at a path no pre-v1.0 code reads — pre-v1.0 replay/compaction/fsck open only
  event files and the known metadata files (`.env-id`, `.gitignore`, etc.), never this
  name — so there is no parse-and-error path. This is the committed design position
  (not a deferral), and the **hard rollback test below is its empirical proof** (git-
  stash the gate code, run `rebar fsck` against a store containing `.store-compat.json`,
  assert operable + file byte-unchanged). The delete-`.store-compat.json` recovery is
  documented as belt-and-suspenders only.
- **Scope boundary.** Keep the ensure-registry for convergent check-then-act repairs.
  Do **not** build the ordered ledger here — only the record + reader gate. Clarify
  the relationship to `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `reducer/_version.py` (it stays the
  event-schema discriminator; `format_version` is the new store-format gate — state
  whether they move together or independently).

## Scope

- New module under `src/rebar/_store/` for the compatibility record + gate, exporting
  `StoreIncompatibleError`, `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`, and `check_store_compat()`.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — insert the gate inside `lock.acquire()` (the single
  convergence point for `write_lock()` + all direct `lock.acquire()` callers:
  `txn.py`, `compact.py:167`/`:415`, `fsck.py:419`), gating every acquisition
  unconditionally (fsck diagnostic holds no lock → structurally exempt).
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` — explicit `check_store_compat()` before its
  raw-git mutation (it holds no lock, so the `lock.acquire()` gate does not cover it).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — `check_store_compat(repo_root/".tickets-tracker")`
  at the top of `_apply_mutations()` after the `persist=True` check (the single
  per-pass chokepoint for both write paths; excludes dry-run/cap-0 passes).
- A coverage test/lint grepping `lock.acquire(` + `write_lock(` + `fsck_recover`'s check.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` — relate `format_version` to the existing
  preserve-and-ignore `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` machinery and to `SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (optional-additive events stay preserve-and-ignore; a required capability is the
  new fail-closed path).
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — the ensure unit that writes the record when absent.
- `docs/migrations.md` — document the record, the four states, the fail-closed
  semantics, the absent-record upgrade path, and the concrete rollback state.
- Interface tests extending `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py`.
- Out of scope: the ordered migration ledger; changing any existing event-replay
  behaviour for currently-known types.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A committed store compatibility record (`format_version` +
  `required_capabilities`) is created at init at a fixed path, written atomically
  (tempfile + rename), and read by a gate function that raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError`; the module exports `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str]`.
- [ ] An **absent** record (pre-v1.0 store) is treated as legacy format version 0 /
  compatible (pass-through, not blocked), and the ensure unit idempotently writes the
  record on the next init / fsck-repair / MCP-boot — verified by a test that opens a
  record-less store with a v1.0 build, confirms it operates, and confirms the record
  is then present (upgrade-in-place, no manual step); the test also confirms a missed
  ensure sweep does not block writes — by monkeypatching `run_ensures` to raise
  `LockTimeout` (or return a `failed` outcome) and asserting a subsequent write still
  succeeds (the gate treats the still-absent record as pass-through).
- [ ] The gate is inserted inside `lock.acquire()` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, after
  path resolution, before fcntl/mkdir) and gates **every** acquisition unconditionally
  — `write_lock()` context-manager callers AND direct `lock.acquire()` callers
  (`txn.py`, `compact.py`, `fsck.py:419` repair) — by one insertion point; `fsck`
  diagnostic holds no lock so it is structurally exempt. Plus an explicit
  `check_store_compat()` at the top of `fsck_recover_cli` (raw-git, no-lock mutation)
  and at the top of `reconcile._apply_mutations()` after the `persist=True` check
  (before `applier.apply()`, using `repo_root/".tickets-tracker"`) for the outbound
  Jira push. It raises `StoreIncompatibleError` (→ non-zero exit) before any side
  effect when the record is **present but incompatible**. Verified by (a) a test in
  `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py` writing a record
  with a `required_capabilities` entry ∉ `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` (e.g. `["unknown-v99"]`)
  and driving a lock-held mutation (store files byte-unchanged), an `fsck_recover`
  invocation, and a reconcile pass (mock Jira adapter records zero calls); and (b) a
  coverage test/lint that greps the tree for **both** `lock.acquire(` and `write_lock(`
  and for `fsck_recover_cli`'s + `_apply_mutations`'s `check_store_compat` call,
  asserting each routes through the
  gate — so a new un-gated write path in any acquisition form fails CI.
- [ ] A **corrupt/unreadable** record (truncated JSON / parse error) is treated as
  fail-closed (NOT as absent) with a diagnostic naming the parse error and path —
  verified by a test writing a truncated record and asserting a mutating entry point
  is blocked.
- [ ] A rollback **test** (hard requirement) simulates a pre-v1.0 binary by invoking
  the store layer with the gate patched out (monkeypatch `check_store_compat` to a
  no-op, emulating code that predates it) against a store carrying the committed
  `.store-compat.json`, and asserts **operable** = `rebar list`/`fsck` exit 0 AND a
  normal write (e.g. `comment`) succeeds, and the `.store-compat.json` file is
  byte-unchanged afterward (proving upgrade-in-place won't brick a pre-v1.0 clone). The
  ignored-unknown guarantee and the delete-`.store-compat.json` compensating path are
  also documented in `docs/migrations.md`.
- [ ] Under an incompatible/corrupt record, the read-only commands `fsck` (diagnostic
  mode), `show`, `list`, and `search` exit with the read-allowed code (0) and their
  structured output / stderr (WARNING+) contains the unsupported version/capability
  identifier — while `fsck` **repair** mode (write-intent) exits non-zero — verified by
  a test asserting the exact field via `jq -e` / an anchored regex and the repair-mode
  non-zero exit.
- [ ] Optional additive (unknown-but-not-*required*) events retain today's
  preserve-and-ignore behaviour — the existing forward-compat contract tests still
  pass, and a new test proves a *required* capability fails closed while an *optional*
  additive event does not.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` documents the record, the four states, the fail-closed
  gate, the deployment-order rationale (why the reader ships in v1.0), and the
  concrete rollback state.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass, and the change lands via the
  Gerrit two-vote gate.

# Optional authentication for the rebar MCP server (OAuth 2.1 Resource-Server model)

## Context

`rebar-mcp` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP("rebar")`) is today **stdio-only**: `build_server().run()` is called with no transport argument. It has **no HTTP transport and no per-request/session plumbing**. Per the MCP authorization spec, authentication is an **HTTP-transport concern** — stdio servers *should not* authenticate (credentials come from the environment). rebar has deliberately kept MCP stdio-only and met every remote need with separate FastAPI library-mode services (the Gerrit `review_bot`, the in-flight op-cert service), so **nothing consumes rebar-mcp over the network today** (Gerrit and GitHub Actions use the rebar library/CLI in-process, per ADR-0007).

This epic adds an **optional** capability: rebar-mcp can serve over HTTP and require authentication, acting as an **OAuth 2.1 Resource Server** that validates inbound bearer tokens and advertises RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata. The capability is generic (provider-agnostic) so any organization can front it with its own identity provider — it is **not** coupled to this project's dev auth model. Design-of-record: session log `emanatory-confounded-dodo` plus the higher-effort coherence/peer/security review pass captured in the same log.

## Why (beneficiary + problem)

**Beneficiary:** an operator/organization (including rebar itself, as future follow-on) that wants to expose rebar MCP tools to remote MCP clients (Claude Code / an IDE / a CI job) over the network instead of a local stdio subprocess. **Problem today:** there is no HTTP transport and no authentication, so a shared/hosted rebar store cannot be reached by a remote MCP client without exposing it unauthenticated. This epic makes a remote rebar-mcp endpoint possible and safe to require auth on, verified locally.

## Approach & rationale (positive)

Build rebar's **own** token verifiers against the **official `mcp` SDK's `TokenVerifier` seam** (`mcp.server.auth.provider.TokenVerifier.verify_token(token) -> AccessToken | None`), wired via `FastMCP(token_verifier=…, auth=AuthSettings(…))`, and serve the optional Streamable-HTTP transport the SDK already provides. rebar is a **Resource Server only** — it validates tokens and advertises discovery metadata; it is **not** an Authorization Server and does **not** implement Dynamic Client Registration (identity is delegated to the deploying org's IdP).

**Why this fits:** (a) the official SDK — already a dependency — provides the `TokenVerifier` seam, `AuthSettings`, RFC 9728 metadata routes, `TransportSecuritySettings`, and Streamable-HTTP transport natively; the verifiers are small modules on a stable, blessed seam. (b) It is the mainstream self-hosted path (GitHub, Grafana, Neon, GitLab, and the SDK's own `simple-auth` example build auth on the official SDK; GitHub's remote server likewise delegates identity and does not do DCR). (c) It avoids the standalone `fastmcp` framework, whose `server.auth` module is semver-exempt and has had multiple CVEs. (d) It keeps every line under rebar's own tests/CI/version control.

**RS-only + no-DCR is defensible, not a usability gap.** Claude Code / Claude.ai do not *require* DCR: they auto-discover via the RFC 9728 PRM rebar serves (pointing at the org IdP), and when the IdP lacks anonymous DCR (Entra, Cognito, default Keycloak/Auth0/Okta) the user falls back to first-class **manual `--client-id`/`--client-secret`** or a **static bearer `--header`** — both of which rebar's PRM + static verifier serve directly. S7 documents these three connection paths.

## Security (this epic crosses a trust boundary — the core of the plan)

Enabling HTTP exposes rebar-mcp to **lower-trust network actors**. The posture is first-class and propagated to every child:

- **Authentication is the deliverable.** With auth enabled, every request is admitted only on a
  validated bearer token; an unauthenticated request receives **401 + `WWW-Authenticate`** with the
  RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` URL. Identity is delegated to the org IdP; rebar mints no tokens.
- **The composite verifier is the single audience/fail-closed choke point.** The SDK does **not**
  validate token audience and `AccessToken.resource` defaults to `None`, so there is no SDK
  backstop. Therefore the **composite** re-validates every returned token: it rejects unless
  `AccessToken.resource` is present **and** equals the single configured `auth_resource_server_url`
  (RFC 8707). Every verifier — including static and trusted-proxy, which have no natural token
  audience — must populate `.resource` explicitly. A verifier cannot bypass the audience check.
- **One resource, one audience.** There is a single `auth_resource_server_url`; it is what the PRM
  advertises AND the audience every verifier validates against — they are never independent.
- **Fail-closed everywhere:** any verifier that raises is logged and treated as **non-acceptance**
  (never acceptance); if no verifier returns a valid, audience-matching token the request is denied
  (401). Misconfigured auth, an unknown `auth_strategies` entry, `auth_enabled=true` with an empty
  composite, or auth-enabled-over-HTTP with no verifier wired all **refuse to start**. An HTTP
  transport with auth disabled refuses to start unless `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP` is set.
- **Transport hardening:** DNS-rebinding/`Origin` protection on by default with explicit loopback
  defaults; loopback bind by default; a non-loopback bind requires explicit host/origin allowlists
  AND an explicit TLS-at-edge acknowledgment (bearer tokens/secrets must never cross the network in
  cleartext). Discovery URLs derive from the configured `auth_resource_server_url` (validated https
  for non-loopback), not the request scheme — the behind-a-proxy correctness fix.
- **No token passthrough** to any upstream (confused-deputy prohibition); tokens/secrets never
  logged (a redaction layer is required and tested).
- **Authenticated ≠ authorized (named residual).** Any authenticated principal wields rebar's full
  ambient authority (writes auto-push; `reconcile live` uses rebar's own git/Jira creds) gated only
  by server-level `required_scopes` and the existing `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`/`ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`/
  `ALLOW_LLM` env gates — which now also gate remote actors. Per-tool scope→capability authorization
  is deferred and documented as a residual risk. Rate-limiting/brute-force protection is delegated
  to the edge proxy in v1, with mandated high-entropy static tokens; documented as a residual.

## Scope

**In scope:** an optional Streamable-HTTP transport; a provider-agnostic auth framework (composite `TokenVerifier` that is the single audience/fail-closed choke point + config-driven selection) shipping five verifiers (static bearer, JWKS/JWT, RFC 7662 introspection, trusted-proxy passthrough, pluggable custom); RFC 9728 metadata + 401; the security/transport hardening above; local verification (pytest); docs + an ADR; config/manifest updates (`McpConfig`, `MCP_ENV_VARS`, `server.json`, regenerated `mcp-reference.md`/`env-vars.md`).

**Out of scope (explicit):** deploying an authenticated endpoint on AWS / `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` and any Gerrit/CI reconfiguration (Gerrit and CI do not use MCP — deliberate follow-on); rebar acting as an Authorization Server / DCR / token issuance; per-tool scope→capability authorization (server-level `required_scopes` only); rate-limiting inside rebar (edge-proxy responsibility in v1); GitHub-**user** and Gerrit authentication (neither is an OAuth token issuer — only a deploying org's proxy/custom concern). stdio remains the default transport and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories (S1–S7) are closed.
- [ ] `rebar-mcp` serves over an optional Streamable-HTTP transport while stdio remains the default
      and default behavior is byte-unchanged when the new flat `mcp.*` keys are unset (observable:
      the existing `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` stdio suite still passes).
- [ ] With auth enabled, the local suite demonstrates 401-without-token (with a `WWW-Authenticate`
      header carrying the RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` URL), a served PRM document, 200-with-valid-
      token, 403-insufficient-scope, and rejection of a token whose `resource` ≠ `auth_resource_server_url`
      enforced at the composite.
- [ ] All five verifier modes (static, JWKS/JWT, introspection, trusted-proxy, custom) are
      selectable via the flat `mcp.auth_strategies` list / `REBAR_MCP_*` env vars, each has passing
      tests, and each populates `AccessToken.resource` so the composite audience check applies.
- [ ] Fail-closed startup is tested: unknown `auth_strategies` entry, `auth_enabled` with an empty
      composite, auth-enabled HTTP with no verifier wired, and HTTP with auth disabled and no
      `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP` all refuse to start.
- [ ] New flat config keys and env vars are reflected in `MCP_ENV_VARS` and `server.json` (the CI
      manifest drift gate `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes) and in regenerated
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` / `docs/env-vars.md`.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-auth.md` and an ADR document the resource-server-only model, the composite audience
      choke point, the five verifier modes, the security posture (incl. the authenticated≠authorized
      residual and rate-limiting delegation), the behind-a-proxy deployment (TLS + allowlists +
      discovery URLs), and the three interactive-client connection paths.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the final integrated branch.
- [ ] A rebar-mcp operator can run the server over HTTP with authentication **required**, using any of
- [ ] The trust-boundary guarantees hold and are demonstrated locally: unauthenticated → 401 +
- [ ] Misconfiguration and downgrade are fail-closed: unknown strategy, empty composite with auth on,
- [ ] A third-party operator can connect an interactive Claude client (documented paths) and the design

## Testing strategy (children carry the tiers/oracles)

Verification is entirely local (no AWS). Each verifier is unit-tested against its own real logic (valid/invalid/audience/expiry/algorithm-confusion/rotation/fail-closed/header-spoofing cases), and the HTTP+auth surface is integration-tested by driving the SDK's Streamable-HTTP ASGI entrypoint with an in-process `httpx` `ASGITransport` client (asserting HTTP status, the `WWW-Authenticate` header, and the served PRM document). Each child story names its test tier and observable oracle.

## Compatibility & rollback

Purely **additive**: stdio stays the default, auth is off by default, all new behavior is gated behind new, unset-by-default flat `mcp.*` keys, so existing stdio deployments and the existing MCP tests are unaffected. The dependency changes are pinning `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` (the v2-alpha renames the SDK surface; 1.28.1 is at/above the DNS-rebinding fix) and adding `pyjwt[crypto]` for the JWKS verifier. Rollback is config-level: leave the new keys unset (or `mcp.transport=stdio`) for exactly today's behavior.
baseline.summary: Optional authentication for the rebar MCP server (OAuth 2.1 Resource-Server model)

# 88d9's inbound parent-clear is unreachable in a bidirectional pass: outbound re-pushes the parent and inbound discards its own clear

A parent cleared on the Jira side is never cleared locally. The inbound clear that ticket 88d9 built is COMPUTED and then DISCARDED within the same pass, so `.parent_id` survives indefinitely on a child whose remote parent is gone.

## Proven RED-first, not inferred

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_clear_bidirectional_37e7.py` wires the REAL outbound differ into the REAL inbound differ the way `run_differs` does — deliberately NOT a hand-built outbound entry, which is the flaw that hid this. Two cells, first run, no setup fighting:

    test_real_outbound_differ_emits_a_parent_write_for_the_deparented_child   PASSED
    test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass                     FAILED

      outbound fields for DC-1: {'parent': 'DC-2'}
      inbound fields for DC-1:  {}
      inbound items suppressed by outbound context: 1
      RECON: outbound_update key=DC-1 changed=[parent] comments=0 labels=0 links=0

`suppressed == 1` is the smoking gun: inbound computed exactly one item — the clear — and it was thrown away.

## Mechanism, both steps read from source

1. **Outbound re-pushes the parent.** `outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent` resolves the
   bound epic parent; `canonical_remote["remote_parent_id"]` is now `None`; they differ, so the
   local-wins branch emits `changed["parent"] = <parent key>`. Crucially `parent` is NOT in
   `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`, so no baseline arbitration ever defers to inbound on this field.
2. **Inbound discards its own clear.** `inbound_differ` canonicalizes the outbound `parent` to
   `parent_id`, then the contradiction filter drops every key already present in the outbound
   entry — including the clear it just computed.

The clear's precondition (Jira has no parent, local does) is IDENTICAL to the outbound re-push's precondition. So for any parent rebar can resolve outbound — bound, and epic-typed per bug 8b25's guard — 88d9's clear can never fire in a bidirectional pass.

## Why the existing 88d9 suite is green

Every 88d9 acceptance cell passes `outbound_mutations=None`. The single cell that DOES supply outbound context — `test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear` — hand-builds a fake outbound entry and asserts the suppression as DESIRED behaviour. It never asks whether the real outbound differ produces that mutation in the clear scenario. It always does.

That is this epic's signature failure shape one level up: not a vacuous oracle, but a REAL oracle asserting the wrong thing because its input was fabricated rather than produced.

## Scope

Confirmed for the EPIC-parent case, which is the normal one on Data Center. For a non-epic local parent `_resolve_local_parent` omits the parent entirely, outbound emits nothing, and the suppression cannot fire — that is the separate situation [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] covers.

## Blast radius beyond DC

The suppression lives in the SHARED differ layer, not in a vendor adapter, so Jira Cloud is implicated on the same code path wherever a parent is cleared remotely while the local parent still resolves. Not yet observed there — recorded as a question, not a claim.

## Proposed fix (from the trace, not yet implemented)

Give the outbound parent branch the directionality guard the mirrored fields already have, reusing 88d9's own evidence channel: before emitting a parent SET, suppress when `local_parent` is truthy, `remote_parent` is falsy, AND `binding_store.get_peer_parent(local_id) == local_parent` — i.e. the peer de-parented since our last observation while local stood still, which is exactly the case `diff_inbound_parent` exists to handle. `get_peer_parent` must stay getattr-guarded, and its absence must fall through to today's local-wins push.

Guard 4 (`test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear`) then needs restating as "an outbound push suppresses the clear ONLY when local re-set the parent", rather than unconditionally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass` is GREEN
- [x] a local parent that was genuinely re-set still wins outbound — the fix must not invert
      into "remote always wins", which would silently drop real local intent
- [x] `test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_round_trips` is GREEN on a live harness run,
      with the run id recorded
- [x] the reworded guard 4 asserts suppression only for the local-re-set case
baseline.summary: 88d9's inbound parent-clear is unreachable in a bidirectional pass: outbound re-pushes the parent and inbound discards its own clear

## Why

Outbound link sync broke because production routes outbound updates through the **batch** applier (`batch_dispatch.update_one` + `_mutation_to_batch_dict`), while the link/comment/label features and their tests lived in the **typed-leaf** applier `apply_outbound._apply_outbound_update` — which production does not execute. Capabilities had to be re-added to the batch path one bug at a time (parent 8b25, comments 87e4, links 3f04). Two parallel outbound appliers guarantee the next capability will drift the same way.

## What

- Collapse outbound application to **one** path. Either delete the dead typed leaf `_apply_outbound_update` (and its now-misleading tests), or make it the single production path and route the batch dispatch through it — chosen so there is no separately-tested parallel that production skips.
- Retarget the existing typed-leaf tests at the surviving production path.
- Add **one** test that drives a multi-sub-op outbound UPDATE — scalar fields + comments + labels + links + parent together — through the production path in a single mutation (the sub-ops were only ever tested in isolation, in separate files).
- **Safety (rollout):** verify behavioral parity BEFORE deleting the retired path — assert the surviving path applies every sub-op the retired path did (fields, comments, labels, links, parent), so the deletion cannot silently drop a capability.

## Scope

- In: applier consolidation in `apply_outbound.py` / `batch_dispatch.py` / `applier.py`; the combined multi-sub-op test; the parity check.
- Out: sub-op telemetry (story E).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Exactly one outbound applier path remains in production; the retired path is deleted (no dead, separately-tested applier code).
- [ ] Behavioral parity is verified — the surviving path applies every sub-op the retired path did — before the retired path is deleted.
- [ ] A single test drives fields + comments + labels + links + parent through the production path in one UPDATE and asserts each sub-op took effect.
- [ ] No capability regresses; the full reconciler suite is green.
- [ ] The combined test asserts effects (sub-op outcomes), never interaction/mock-call-counts.
baseline.summary: Collapse the dual outbound applier paths to one production path

## Problem
A misleading error code is a significant failure mode: it causes LLM/agent consumers to make erroneous assumptions and act on a wrong diagnosis (e.g. "the AI provider is down" when the real fault is bad input or a missing asset). Recent bugs are all instances of ONE systemic pattern: the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` fallthrough in the `error_code_for` classifier mislabels non-availability failures.

## Goal
Systematically audit EVERY error-code / classification surface so each returned code accurately and specifically describes the actual condition, and no failure degrades to a misleading catch-all.

## Reconciled taxonomy (RESOLVED — supersedes the pre-dbca brief)
Epic dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d has since LANDED (closed; commits ae4f6c1a, f854924b) and already reclassified the workflow caller-input family with FINER, more descriptive codes than a broad `command_failed`. Per the operator descriptiveness bar a finer accurate code is strictly better, so dbca's answer is preserved, not competed with. The authoritative target for this epic is therefore:
- `LLMUnavailableError` / `LLMConfigError` -> `llm_unavailable` (genuine availability faults only).
- `LLMRunnerError` subtree (`LLMBudgetExhaustedError`, `ContextWindowExceededError`, `LLMInputRejectedError`, `RunawayToolLoopError`, `StructuredOutputError`/`UnretryableOutputError`/`CompletionRecoveryError`) -> `command_failed` (the residual mislabel this epic fixes).
- dbca workflow caller-input subtree (`WorkflowNotFoundError` -> `not_found`; `WorkflowParseError`/`WorkflowValidationError`/`WorkflowVersionError`/`WorkflowUnknownStepError` -> `invalid_input`) -> PRESERVED UNTOUCHED.
- bare `WorkflowError` base + bare `LLMError` -> `llm_unavailable` (dbca's pinned catch-all; the still-open escalated ticket 551b owns any future change to the bare-base editor/missing-bundle code — this epic does NOT pre-decide it).
Discriminate by exception TYPE, not by phase. Do NOT revert dbca. Do NOT invent new fine-grained error codes beyond what a consumer demonstrably needs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `error_code_for` (src/rebar/_errors.py) routes the `LLMRunnerError` subtree to `command_failed` while keeping `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError` -> `llm_unavailable`, and leaves dbca's workflow caller-input taxonomy (`not_found`/`invalid_input`) and the bare `WorkflowError`/`LLMError` catch-all (`llm_unavailable`) untouched (child f75f-5509-10c0-4430).
- [x] `_structured_llm_failure` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py) derives its top-level `error` field via `error_code_for(exc)` instead of hardcoding `llm_unavailable`, across all 4 MCP gate tools, so both dbca's finer codes and the LLMRunnerError routing apply uniformly (child fbc0-ee15-9d69-49ae).
- [x] The `render_workflow` MCP tool surfaces the `WorkflowError` caller-input family as `not_found`/`invalid_input` (NOT `llm_unavailable`) — already proven observably by the landed dbca contract tests (tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py). 7d47-2131-42bd-4832 is therefore closed as SUPERSEDED by dbca; no `command_failed` is re-asserted for that family.
- [x] `pinned_ticket_read_failed` is registered in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (child 0aee-a70d-045b-48a1).
- [x] The gate-degrade `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean is True only for genuine `LLMUnavailableError` outages; `LLMInputRejectedError` instead sets a distinct `input_rejected` signal (via a shared `failure.degrade_cause_flags` helper applied in BOTH degrade builders — `gate_dispatch.py` and `plan_review_recovery.py`), and the three readers (`plan_review/drift_floor.py`, `plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `review_bot/adapter.py`) are updated to read it. No broad `degraded` category (child 5f96-25aa-af9d-4f57).
- [x] A prevention guardrail lands: an exhaustive `exception -> code` contract test over the `LLMError` subclass tree asserting the RECONCILED taxonomy above (availability -> `llm_unavailable`; `LLMRunnerError` subtree -> `command_failed`; dbca workflow subtree -> `not_found`/`invalid_input`; bare bases -> `llm_unavailable`), plus a vocabulary-closure test asserting every code any producer can emit is in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (pins 0aee).
- [x] [non-codebase] Every change lands via Gerrit with `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`, carries a `rebar-ticket` trailer + DCO sign-off, and children are closed bottom-up.
  provenance: environment=gerrit@rebar.solutions.navateam.com + github-actions-ci; principal=rebar review-bot (LLM-Review) and CI Verified bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit changes 2413/2415 merged to main and 2416/2418/2419 each carry Verified +1 and LLM-Review +1 (confirmed via live Gerrit REST /detail), every commit carries a rebar-ticket trailer + DCO Signed-off-by, and children f75f/fbc0/7d47/0aee/5f96 were closed bottom-up before this epic close.

## Scope (surfaces enumerated by the audit)
- `error_code_for` mapping (`src/rebar/_errors.py`) — the residual blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch 7 (branch 6 workflow classification already handled by dbca).
- `_structured_llm_failure` (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) across the 4 MCP gate tools.
- The gate-degrade `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean (`gate_dispatch.py` + `plan_review_recovery.py`) and its three readers.
- Top-level `_errors.py` `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` vocabulary contract.

## Constraints
Remediation lands via Gerrit per AGENTS.md. No --force. Gates run unbounded. dbca (landed) is preserved, not reverted. 551b remains OPEN and owns the bare-`WorkflowError`-base editor/missing-bundle decision — this epic explicitly does not resolve it.
baseline.summary: Audit all error codes for descriptiveness; eliminate misleading classifications

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/drift_floor.py:126` (`drift_floor_candidate`) computes the drift-refresh eligibility `code_drifted` reason as:

```python
signed_sha = signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(manifest)   # the GATE-REF sha at review time
current_sha = signing.head_sha(_config.repo_root(repo_root))    # git rev-parse HEAD of the working tree
reasons["code_drifted"] = bool(signed_sha) and bool(current_sha) and current_sha != "unknown" and signed_sha != current_sha
```

This is the SAME defect class as bug `1137-8215-ec04-4ca0` (seaworthy-revengeful-blobfish): it compares the signed **gate-ref** sha (`verified_at_sha`) against `git rev-parse HEAD` of whatever working tree the evaluator sits in. Its own comment states it "mirrors compute_validity's unscoped whole-HEAD 'stale-head' trigger anchor **exactly**" — and 1137's fix corrected compute_validity's unscoped trigger to resolve the CURRENT gate ref (via `resolve_ref(default_ref, working, fetch=False)`, `source=local`/legacy tolerant, fail-closed on unresolvable). This site was NOT updated, so it now DIVERGES from the invariant its comment asserts.

## Impact (why this is P3, not P2)
Unlike 1137 this does NOT block claims. `drift_floor_candidate` is the drift-refresh REUSE floor: a spurious `code_drifted=True` only DENIES cheap-refresh eligibility, forcing a (safe but wasteful) FULL re-review, and makes `_drifted_paths(signed_sha, current_sha)` diff the gate-ref sha against a FOREIGN commit (bogus drifted-file lists). Conservative/wasteful, not incorrect-blocking.

## Non-trivial subtlety (DO NOT fix blind)
drift_floor's failure semantics DIFFER from attest.py's: `code_drifted` guards `current_sha != "unknown"`, so an UNRESOLVABLE current sha reads as NOT drifted → **fail-OPEN** (would reuse a possibly-stale review). attest.py fails CLOSED on the same condition. A correct fix must resolve the current gate-ref sha AND handle resolution failure so it does not introduce a fail-open drift-refresh reuse. This needs its own RED->GREEN test (attested manifest, origin/main unmoved, foreign working-tree HEAD -> code_drifted must be False/eligible; gate ref moved -> code_drifted True; gate ref unresolvable -> conservative not-eligible).

## Suggested approach
Mirror 1137's attest.py fix: resolve `resolve_ref(gate_source.default_ref(working), working, fetch=False)` for attested manifests (source=local / no-verified_at_sha keep head_sha), and map a SnapshotError to a conservative not-eligible outcome (NOT eligible), preserving drift_floor's fail-safe direction. Consider a shared helper with attest.py's `_unscoped_head_drift` so the documented mirror invariant holds by construction.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `drift_floor_candidate` resolves the CURRENT gate ref (not working-tree HEAD) for attested manifests.
- [ ] source=local and no-verified_at_sha manifests keep the working-tree basis (unchanged).
- [ ] Gate-ref resolution failure yields a CONSERVATIVE not-eligible outcome (no fail-open reuse).
- [ ] RED->GREEN test proves the foreign-working-tree false-drift is gone and moved/unresolvable ref semantics preserved.
- [ ] Mirror invariant with compute_validity's unscoped trigger restored (ideally a shared helper).
baseline.summary: drift_floor_candidate reads working-tree HEAD, not the gate ref, for attested code-drift eligibility (1137 sibling)

baseline.description:
## Context
ADR 0051 / bug 88eb landed FOREGROUND auto-gc on the tickets worktree (fixes the
detached-maintenance corruption). Measured safe on the current 184k-object store
(~1-2s routine, ~8-9s worst-case). But the git `gc` maintenance task does a FULL
repack whose cost scales with TOTAL store size, so the worst-case foreground pause
grows as the store grows, eventually approaching the 60s write-lock budget.

## Idea — strictly-better posture: bound each foreground maintenance run to O(new objects)
Replace the size-scaling `gc` task with git's incremental maintenance tasks, kept
foreground (serialized under the write lock, preserving the ADR 0051 safety):

- Disable the `gc` task (`maintenance.gc.enabled=false` / keep `gc.auto=0` semantics).
- Enable **`loose-objects`** — packs NEW loose objects into a fresh `loose-*.pack`
  (default batch 50k), and does NOT rewrite existing packs or the multi-pack-index.
- Enable **`incremental-repack`** — geometric, auto-sized batch capped at 2 GB
  (git commit a13e3d0), so a run "never" repacks the whole store in one shot.
- Optional (Gitaly's further win): pack loose objects into a fresh pack WITHOUT
  updating the MIDX (the residual O(size) cost), consolidate geometrically only
  occasionally.

## Prior art (see bug 88eb research)
- Microsoft Scalar: `gc.auto=0` + background `loose-objects`/`incremental-repack` via
  `git maintenance` (docs/advanced.md).
- GitLab/Gitaly: geometric repacking + time-based full repack + loose-object packing
  that never updates the MIDX (13s -> 174ms).
- git's own `git maintenance` "incremental" strategy: runs loose-objects +
  incremental-repack, never the gc task, and sets maintenance.auto=false.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The tickets worktree runs incremental maintenance (loose-objects +
  geometric incremental-repack), foreground, with the full `gc` task disabled.
- [ ] Measured foreground-maintenance pause stays bounded (~1-2s) as the store grows
  well past ~500k objects (proving command: the gc-latency measurement harness).
- [ ] No regression to the 88eb corruption fix (concurrency test stays green on git 2.54).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated; ADR 0051's "escape hatch / scale-up" section points here.
baseline.summary: Bound foreground git-maintenance to O(new objects): disable the gc task, use loose-objects + geometric incremental-repack

# Concurrent review-plan silently drops the plan-review attestation: enrich_drain._prune_queue_events uses an unlocked whole-index git commit that races locked store writes

## Summary

Under `[agents]`, every `review-plan` finish triggers the opportunistic enrichment drain, whose `rebar.llm.enrich_drain._prune_queue_events` (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:191-207`) stages and commits with a **raw, unlocked, whole-index** `git rm` + `git commit` — taking neither the unified store write lock nor a commit pathspec. Running in the detached drain child concurrently with a review's locked `stage_and_commit` writes, it drops the concurrent writer's event, so a PASS review leaves NO persisted attestation (and no observability sidecar).

This is the un-hardened twin of bug `malevolent-emigratory-umbrette`, whose fix routed the two sibling prunes (`plan_review/sidecar.py:94`, `overlap/digest_sidecar.py:141`) through the locked, pathspec-scoped `event_append.delete_events`; the enrich-queue prune was missed.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Concurrently run `rebar review-plan` on several DIFFERENT tickets (separate processes), with the
   `[agents]` extra + a real key (so the enrichment drain is live).
2. Some PASS reviews return `sidecar_emitted=False` and `verify-signature` → "unsigned — ticket has
   no signature", despite a PASS verdict. Serial runs persist fine.

Confirmed by an isolated-store experiment (remote OFF, so branch-divergence is excluded): 6 locked `append_event` writers vs 4 processes calling the real `_prune_queue_events` produced 33/360 writes raising `git commit failed while holding lock` ("nothing to commit" — the writer's staged blob was swept into the prune's whole-index commit — and "cannot lock ref 'HEAD': is at X but expected Y"), with all 33 blobs left IN HEAD but UNLINKED from the worktree (sweep-and-strand); worktree-listing readers then report them absent.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** a concurrent write is serialized by the single store write lock (invariant I5); a
  committed event is durable and visible to readers. "A push failure never fails the write — the
  commit stays local" (CLAUDE.md). A PASS review persists a claimable attestation.
- **Actual:** the unlocked prune committer sweeps/orphans a concurrent locked write; the review's
  own commit fails (swallowed by `sidecar.emit` → `sidecar_emitted=False` and by
  `attest.sign_plan_review` → unsigned), and the swept blob is unlinked from the worktree.

## Root Cause

`_prune_queue_events` performs a store write OUTSIDE the unified write lock with a whole-index commit, contrary to `event_append.delete_events`'s contract (`event_append.py:302-307`) and the I5 single-lock invariant (`_store/lock.py:1-24`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:_prune_queue_events` no longer runs a raw unlocked `git rm` /
  whole-index `git commit`; it routes through the locked, pathspec-scoped
  `event_append.delete_events` (mirroring `plan_review/sidecar.py:prune`).
  - Proving: `rg -n 'subprocess.run.*git' src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` shows no raw `git commit`
    in `_prune_queue_events`; `rg -n 'delete_events' src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` present.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the race (RED before the fix) and passes after: concurrent
  locked writes + the drain-queue prune leave zero dropped/stranded events.
  - Proving: the new test in `tests/` fails on `origin/main` and passes with the fix; `make test` green.
- [ ] A sibling sweep confirms no other unlocked `git commit` store-write remains outside the
  locked path.
  - Proving: `rg -n "git.*commit" src/rebar --glob '*.py'` reviewed; any raw store-commit routes
    through the locked path or is justified.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass — CI's `Verified` gate green on the landed change (external CI state; attested by a comment citing the change + vote + merge).
baseline.summary: Concurrent review-plan silently drops the plan-review attestation: enrich_drain._prune_queue_events uses an unlocked whole-index git commit that races locked store writes

## Context / Problem
Normal compaction (`compact_txn._compact_locked`, `compact_txn.py:522-654`), the fsck rebuild (`compact_rebuild.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`, `compact_rebuild.py:107-238`) and crash recovery (`compact_recovery.py:128-202`) each re-derive the same decisions in their own code:

* **candidate listing** — `compact_txn._parse_candidate_events` (196-223) vs
  `compact_rebuild._partition_rebuild_sources` (59-84) vs `compact._foldable_event_count`
  (`compact.py:176-225`): three hand-rolled `listdir` + dotfile/`-SYNC.json` filters + JSON
  parses.
* **the "is this a SNAPSHOT file" test** — `compact_txn._is_snapshot_path` (226-228),
  re-inlined at `compact_txn.py:633-637` (the source-uuid filter added by bug
  `privileged-nephelite-colt` / `aea0`), and spelled a third way at `compact_rebuild.py:75-79`.
* **the SNAPSHOT envelope** — `compact_txn._build_snapshot_event` (297-326) vs the inline copy
  at `compact_rebuild.py:164-195`; the former's docstring already admits it is "mirroring" the
  latter. `"source_event_uuids":` and `"compacted_at":` appear as dict keys in exactly these
  two places.
* **the `*.retired` rename-back rule** — `compact_txn._retire_folded_sources` (329-397),
  `compact_txn._rollback_fold` (418-454) and `compact_recovery._revert_partial_fold` (128-164)
  each restore sources, then remove the uncommitted SNAPSHOT *only* when every reverse-rename
  succeeded (the data-loss guard from bug `compulsory-pernickety-mantis` / `e72e`), and two of
  them also `git reset` the ticket dir. `os.rename(retired, ...)` appears three times.
* **the commit step** — `compact_txn._commit_compaction` (401-415) vs
  `compact_rebuild._commit_rebuild` (88-103): the same `add -A <id>/` → `diff --cached --quiet`
  → `commit --no-verify -m` skeleton, differing only in message and error handling.
* **the two-arm "needs folding" rule** — `compact._scan_snapshot_state` (228-283) vs
  `compact_trigger.ticket_needs_folding` (88-117), including the `any(n.endswith(
  "-SNAPSHOT.json") ...)` probe in both.

Open story `plush-excessive-willet` (snapshot as derived cache) is a later design change this planner makes cheaper; it does not overlap.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_commands/compact_plan.py` — no I/O policy of its own, only the shared derivations — and route the three paths through it:

* `Candidate` (frozen dataclass: `path`, `name`, `uuid`, `timestamp`, `event_type`, with
  `is_snapshot` / `is_active` / `is_known_type`) and
  `list_candidates(ticket_dir, *, include_retired=False)`.
* `is_snapshot_event_file(name)` and `source_uuids_of(candidates)` — the `aea0` exclusion rule
  in one place.
* `has_snapshot(ticket_dir, *, default)` and `needs_folding(foldable, has_snap, threshold)`.
* `build_snapshot_event(tracker, ticket_dir, compiled_state, source_uuids, snapshot_ts)`
  returning `(event, final_path)`; `git_author()` moves here with it.
* `restore_retired(originals) -> bool`, `discard_uncommitted_snapshot(path)`,
  `unstage_ticket_dir(tracker, ticket_id)` — the rename-back rule and its data-loss guard.
* `commit_ticket_dir(tracker, ticket_id, message) -> tuple[bool, str]`; each caller keeps its
  own reaction (`compact_txn` writes the stderr line and returns 1; `compact_rebuild` ignores).

**Deliberately NOT consolidated.** `compact_rebuild`'s forward retire loop (`compact_rebuild.py:198-205`) keeps its per-file tolerance and its `.snapshot-rebuild.bak` idempotent-restart crash model. Giving it the fold's abort-and-roll-back semantics would change observable behaviour on a repair path (today a rename failure is logged and the rebuild still succeeds), and bug `e72e` scoped its journal/rollback design to the fold, not to the rebuild. The intent journal, `.bak` sentinel and in-process abort seams are unchanged; fsck remains the sole owner of mixed state (`compact_recovery.py:22-26`).

**Recorded convergence.** `_partition_rebuild_sources` filters only dotfiles and `-SYNC.json`, so a stray non-event file in a ticket dir (no `.json` suffix) was cited in `source_event_uuids` and renamed to `*.retired`. `list_candidates` requires the `.json` (or `.json.retired`) suffix that the other two scans already required. This is the one behaviour that converges; it is covered by a new test and is not pinned by any existing test.

## Guard construction
`compact_plan._offending_line(line)` (mirroring `rebar._store.paths._offending_line`) flags a line outside the owner that either writes a SNAPSHOT-envelope key (`source_event_uuids` or `compacted_at` in dict-KEY position — the call-target/argument-position shape the epic rule sanctions) or performs the retired rename-back (`os.rename(` with `retired` in first-argument position). A `# compact-plan-ok: <reason>` marker excuses a line; a bare marker is itself an offence. `tests/unit/commands/test_compact_plan.py` scans every `src/rebar/**/*.py` except the owner, and unit-tests `_offending_line` in both directions.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_commands/compact_plan.py` (new), `compact_txn.py`, `compact_rebuild.py`, `compact_recovery.py`, `compact.py`, `compact_trigger.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_compact_plan.py` (new). `_compact_locked` and `compact_all_cli` sit at their C901 ceilings, so edits there are subtractive only.

## Testing
Happy path: a normal fold and a rebuild over the same ticket directory produce SNAPSHOT events whose `source_event_uuids` agree, and both envelopes carry the same key set. Edge: a stray non-`.json` file is neither cited nor retired by the rebuild. Guard: the tree scan plus the four `_offending_line` direction tests. Pinning (must pass with no assertion edits): `tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_process_death.py` (real SIGKILL at the rename barrier), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_rollback_recovery.py`, `tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_rebuild_counter_b2bb.py` (`_REBUILD_COUNT` stays in `compact_rebuild`), `tests/unit/test_compact_all_selection.py`, `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A normal fold and a rebuild over the same ticket directory agree on
      `source_event_uuids`; checked by the new equivalence test in
      `tests/unit/commands/test_compact_plan.py`.
- [x] No second SNAPSHOT-envelope builder or retired rename-back exists under `src/rebar`
      outside `compact_plan.py`, and an unmarked copy fails while a reasoned
      `# compact-plan-ok:` marker excuses it; checked by the guard tests.
- [x] A rebuild over a ticket dir holding a stray non-`.json` file leaves that file in place
      and excludes it from `source_event_uuids` (the recorded convergence); checked by the new
      edge test.
- [x] The pinning suites listed above pass with no assertion edits, and
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`;
      checked by running both.

## Close verification (orphan takeover, 2026-08-22)
Commit 6a5a9f98011 merged to main (verified at 8a036765705). All 4 ACs verified: tests/unit/commands/test_compact_plan.py 15/15 pass (equivalence, guard, stray-file edge tests included); no second SNAPSHOT builder (guard tests green); complexity check new=0 increased=0. Boxes checked with this evidence.
baseline.summary: compact_plan: one candidate/source/envelope/retire planner for normal, rebuild and recovery compaction
