# S5 — Signed verdicts stamp provider, endpoint, tier, and effective capabilities

## Context / Problem

A signed gate verdict records only a model string. THREE sites write it: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:629`, `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:206,223`, and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:105` each write `"model": verdict.get("model")`. That string is the resolved `provider:model`, so a verdict produced behind an opaque gateway still claims it came from `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`. Once rebar supports two first-class providers and a best-effort tier, a consumer cannot tell a Bedrock-backed verdict from an Ollama-backed one, even though rebar signs both.

## Approach

Keep the existing `model` string field untouched and **add** a sibling `provider_provenance` object: `{provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, capabilities}`. `endpoint_host` records the host only (never a full URL, never credentials); `tier` is `first_class` or `best_effort`; `capabilities` is the effective record from S2 [rebar:f184-a5f1-f181-4700]. Verdicts still sign on every tier — a contributor running Ollama can still exercise the gates, which matters for the OSS on-ramp — but a consumer now has the lever to reject an off-tier verdict.

Additive-only is deliberate: it makes this a **backward-compatible** payload change, so an older reader ignores the new key and no store-compatibility capability gate or migration is required. Readers that want the provenance treat its absence as "unknown, legacy".

**Alternative rejected:** refusing to sign off-tier verdicts. It gives a stronger guarantee but breaks local development without a first-class provider key, which weakens exactly the contributor on-ramp `docs/plan-review-gate.md` depends on.

**Alternative rejected:** replacing the `model` string with the structured object. That is a breaking payload change requiring a compatibility gate and a migration for zero added information.

**Where the record is assembled, and why NOT in `providers.py`.** An earlier draft of this plan said `providers.py` would 'expose the provenance record from the factory'. That is impossible AND unnecessary:

- IMPOSSIBLE: `ProviderSession.provider_factory` is the `(str) -> Provider` hook handed to pydantic-ai's
  `infer_model`. Its return type is fixed by that contract, so it has no channel to hand anything else back to
  the caller. This is the SAME limitation the module already documents for the retrying httpx client (which is
  why builders append to `self._closeables` instead of returning it).
- UNNECESSARY: `runner.run()` ALREADY holds every field, in one scope — `resolved = _pai_model(cfg)`
  (`runner.py:273`) gives the provider-qualified model, `_provider_name` (`:294`) the provider,
  `caps = capabilities_for(...)` (`:357`) the effective capability record, and `cfg.base_url` the endpoint.
  Nothing needs to travel back from the factory at all.

So the runner assembles the record from data it already has, via a helper in `capabilities.py` (277 LOC, the roomiest candidate; `runner.py` is at 698 against the 800 cap, so the runner-side change stays a call, not an inline block). `providers.py` — at 299 against the <300 cap that is an ATTESTED criterion of closed story 7468 — is left untouched, which removes that constraint from this story entirely.

**Reuse the already-computed capability record, do not recompute it.** `runner.py:357` resolves `caps` ONCE per run, and the model-object-vs-string distinction there is load-bearing (it caused a prior regression). Provenance must stamp THAT record; calling `capabilities_for` a second time can silently diverge from the record that actually drove the run.

**`endpoint_host` uses `urlparse(base_url).hostname`, never `.netloc`.** `.hostname` strips userinfo; `.netloc` RETAINS `user:secret@`. Note `runner.py:650` uses `.netloc` — harmless there (a truthiness check) but the wrong accessor to copy here. This is the mechanism behind the security oracle below.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — assemble the provenance record. It takes PRIMITIVES
  (`provider: str`, `model: str`, `base_url: str | None`, `caps: ModelCapabilities`) and returns the record.
  It must NOT take `LLMConfig` or a provider object: this module is a declared LEAF whose docstring states it
  imports nothing from `runner`/`providers` and keeps `import rebar.llm` stdlib-only.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — call that assembler and thread the record alongside `ran_model`.
- **`src/rebar/llm/providers.py` is NOT modified** (see Approach).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — populate it alongside `ran_model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` (`:629`), `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` (`:206,223`),
  and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` (`:105`) — the CODE-REVIEW gate's verdict payload. It was
  missing from an earlier draft of this Scope and is the most consequential of the three for this epic:
  code review is the gate being cut over to Bedrock [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], so a consumer trying to
  tell a Bedrock-backed LLM-Review vote from an Anthropic-backed one reads THIS payload. Leaving it out
  would have shipped provenance to the two gates that need it least.
- `docs/event-schema.md` — document the additive field.
- `tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract tier: the mechanism is a producer/consumer shape agreement across a signed, persisted payload, so the test feeds a real runner result into the real sidecar writer and reads the persisted record back.

- happy path: a Bedrock run persists `provider_provenance.tier == "first_class"` and `provider == "bedrock"`.
- best-effort path: a run with `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` persists `tier == "best_effort"` and the endpoint host.
- collateral invariant: the pre-existing `model` string field is byte-identical to what it was before this
  change, and the signature over the payload still verifies.
- security oracle (negative control): given a `base_url` containing credentials
  (`https://user:secret@host/v1`), the persisted `endpoint_host` is `host` and the persisted payload contains
  neither `secret` nor the api_key anywhere.
- backward compatibility: a sidecar payload written WITHOUT the new key still loads and verifies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts no credential material from `base_url` or `api_key` appears anywhere in the persisted
      sidecar payload
- [ ] a test asserts a legacy payload lacking `provider_provenance` still loads and its signature verifies
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar review-plan` on a real ticket writes a sidecar whose `provider_provenance.tier` matches the
      configured provider, shown in the ticket comment
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` documents the field as additive and optional
baseline.summary: S5 — signed verdicts stamp provider, endpoint, tier, and effective capabilities

baseline.description:
## Problem
Reclaim/concurrency integration fixtures create bare repositories, then invoke Git with the bare repository as `cwd` but without an explicit `--git-dir`. On hosts configured with `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, fixture setup fails before test bodies run:

- `git config gc.autoDetach false` -> `fatal: not in a git directory` (exit 128)
- `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/tickets` -> `fatal: cannot use bare repository ... (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')` (exit 128)

The same errors reproduce from pristine `origin/main`; the failing tests import no force/transition/claim code. Linux CI currently uses Git defaults and therefore does not expose the failure, but the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. Treat agents dismissing reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.

## Safety constraints
Be very cautious about Git configuration. Do not change, unset, or weaken host, global, system, or repository safety settings as remediation. Perform ticket and commit archaeology before proposing a fix so prior bare-repository safety fixes or contracts are not regressed. Prefer explicit, command-scoped repository targeting if the evidence supports it. Do not mask unrelated Git failures.

## Investigation plan
1. Inventory every affected reclaim/concurrency fixture command and the helper/call chain that creates and initializes bare repositories.
2. Search tickets and Git history for prior bare-repository, `safe.bareRepository`, `--git-dir`, fixture, and repository-isolation fixes; record the intended contracts and regression risks.
3. Reproduce from a fresh `origin/main` worktree using isolated command-scoped configuration that sets `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, without mutating host/global Git configuration. Include the default-config run as a negative control.
4. Use runtime evidence to confirm whether implicit repository discovery from a bare-repository `cwd` is the complete mechanism for both failures and rule out venv or product-code explanations.
5. After a proven RCA and legitimacy/caller-dependency checks, design a held-out RED oracle covering both failing command shapes and their observable fixture outcome.
6. Repair only the confirmed mechanism. Evaluate explicit `--git-dir` or an equivalent command-scoped invocation; do not change Git safety settings.
7. Prove GREEN, re-seed the exact defect to prove the oracle returns RED, and rerun the original report under both explicit-safe and default Git configurations.
8. Run focused reclaim/concurrency suites locally and through the normal CI matrix, plus lint/typecheck/complexity gates as applicable. Sweep semantically for sibling bare-repository commands using the same unsafe invocation pattern.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Exact affected fixture commands and call paths are inventoried with citations.
- [x] Relevant tickets and commits are archaeologically reviewed, with prior contracts and regression risks recorded.
- [x] The failure is reproduced on pristine `origin/main` using isolated command-scoped `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, without changing host/global Git settings.
- [x] A default-Git-config negative control demonstrates the environmental trigger while preserving the conclusion that local test portability is a repository responsibility.
- [x] A runtime-confirmed RCA explains both fixture setup failures and rules out venv and unrelated product-code causes.
- [x] A held-out final-form oracle is observed RED before the repair and covers both `git config` and `git symbolic-ref` bare-repository initialization paths.
- [x] The repair explicitly targets the bare repository (for example with `--git-dir`, if archaeology and experiments validate it) and does not weaken any Git safety setting.
- [x] The held-out oracle is GREEN after repair and returns RED when the exact implicit-discovery defect is reintroduced.
- [x] Focused reclaim/concurrency tests pass locally under both explicit-safe and default Git configurations and pass in the normal CI matrix.
- [x] Unrelated Git errors remain visible; no broad exception swallowing, retries, skips, xfails, or test weakening are introduced.
- [x] A semantic sibling sweep covers other bare-repository fixture invocations and dispositions every confirmed instance.
baseline.summary: Bare-repository fixtures fail under safe.bareRepository=explicit

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`clarity_check` can return `verdict: "fail"` while its own reported evidence says the ticket passed, and its MCP output carries no field that explains why. A caller sees `score >= threshold` next to `verdict: fail` and has nothing to act on.

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server, on probe ticket `ruby-griffinish-goitered` (`c67b-ece5-707e-460e`):

```
clarity_check {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered"}
  -> {"score": 6, "verdict": "fail", "threshold": 5, "passed": false}
```

6 >= 5, yet `fail`. The description at that moment had an `## Acceptance Criteria` section whose items were plain `- AC1: ...` bullets rather than `- [ ]` checkboxes. After rewriting the same ticket's ACs as checkboxes, the identical call returned `{"score": 7, "verdict": "pass", "threshold": 5, "passed": true}` — confirming the failure came from the structural floor, not the score.

## Mechanism
`src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:165-169`

```python
score = _clarity_score(description, ticket_type)
floor = evaluate_plan_clarity(description)
if score >= threshold and floor.passes:
    return {"score": score, "verdict": "pass", "threshold": threshold}, 0
return {"score": score, "verdict": "fail", "threshold": threshold}, 1
```

The verdict is a conjunction of two independent conditions, but only the score half is returned. `PlanClarityFloor` (`src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py:44-56`) already carries the exact evidence — `ac_items`, `empty_ac_items`, `sentinel_assignments`, `unchecked_ac_lines` — and all of it is discarded here.

The MCP output model has no place to put it either: `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:162-166`

```python
class ClarityResultOut(_Out):
    score: int
    verdict: str
    threshold: int
    passed: bool | None = None
```

Note the library's own read-error branch (`src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:49-52`) DOES return a `reason`, so the field exists on the failure path that cannot happen in normal use and is missing on the one that can.

## Impact
`clarity_check` is a read-only gate tool agents use to decide whether a plan is dispatchable. On the common failure (bulleted instead of checkbox ACs, or a `TBD`/`TODO` sentinel in a value position) it returns a self-contradictory result with no remediation signal, so the caller must guess or re-derive the floor. The related `check_ac` returns a `reason` string in exactly this situation, so the two sibling gates are inconsistent.

## Reproduction
1. Create a ticket whose description scores at or above the clarity threshold but whose
   `## Acceptance Criteria` items are plain `-` bullets, not `- [ ]` checkboxes.
2. Call `clarity_check` on it.
3. Observe `verdict: "fail"` with `score >= threshold` and no explanatory field.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1: `clarity_check_compute` returns a `reason` naming which condition failed — the score floor, or the structural floor — and, for the structural floor, which defect (missing checklist, empty AC item, or unresolved sentinel with its line).
- [x] AC2: `ClarityResultOut` carries that `reason` so it survives to MCP callers.
- [x] AC3: A pass still returns `verdict: "pass"` with the existing shape; the added field is additive and does not break existing consumers.
- [x] AC4: A regression test asserts that a description with `score >= threshold` and non-checkbox ACs yields `verdict: "fail"` with a non-empty `reason` naming the structural floor.
- [x] AC5: A regression test asserts a below-threshold description yields a `reason` naming the score.

## Definition of Done
- [x] DD1: AC1-AC3 implemented; AC4 and AC5 tests pass.
- [x] DD2: `docs/mcp-reference.md` regenerated if the tool summary changes.
baseline.summary: clarity_check returns verdict=fail with score >= threshold and no reason, hiding the structural-floor cause

# Live-store remediation: drive fsck to zero (safe, reversible, batched, committed)

## Why
`rebar fsck` on the live store = 2422 SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT + 11 ORPHAN_EVENT + 1 MISSING_CREATE. Fix #1 stopped new corruption; this cleans the backlog. DESTRUCTIVE on a live, git-backed shared store — safety is first-class. Consumes NEW sibling deliverables: A1 (tricolour-head-ratfish) ADDS the `.retired` rename + `RETIRED_SUFFIX` + retire helper; A2 (glandulous-potent-waxwing) ADDS the `include_retired` rebuild path. depends_on A1+A2.

## Repair per fault class
- SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT (2422): a folded source file STILL PRESENT (listed in `source_event_uuids`, never deleted).
  Repair = call A1's retire helper to rename each still-present listed source to `.retired`. NOT a rebuild.
- ORPHAN_EVENT (11): a pre-snapshot event absent from `source_event_uuids`. Routed BY EVENT TYPE (see policy):
  AUTO-RECOVER types -> A2's `reduce_ticket(..., include_retired=True)` rebuild; HUMAN-TRIAGE types -> surfaced,
  NOT auto-rebuilt (the rebuild would pick an order that may be wrong).
- MISSING_CREATE (1): `fsck --repair` logs it, no automatic write; human triage.

## Orphan disposition (a CODE constant, not just prose)
Define two sets in code (enumerating ALL KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES so none is unclassified):
- AUTO-RECOVER (additive/commutative): COMMENT, LINK, UNLINK, TAG_DELTA, COMMITS, BRIDGE_ALERT, REVERT.
- HUMAN-TRIAGE (order-sensitive): STATUS, EDIT, FILE_IMPACT, VERIFY_COMMANDS, SIGNATURE, WORKFLOW_RUN,
  WORKFLOW_STEP, ARCHIVED. Decisions recorded in the PR / a linked ops doc.

## Safety
- GIT-AWARE writes: the tracker is a git worktree. Each batch commits+pushes:
  `git -C <tracker> add -A && git -C <tracker> commit -m 'a3-remediation: batch N/M' && git -C <tracker> push`.
  If a push FAILS (conflict/network/reject), ABORT the run and surface the error — do NOT continue; the pre-tag
  enables rollback. BEFORE any write: `git -C <tracker> tag pre-a3-remediation <oid>`; rollback = `git reset --hard
  pre-a3-remediation && git push --force-with-lease`.
- Dry-run FIRST: `fsck --repair --dry-run` prints per-ticket before/after diff + dispositions, writes NOTHING
  (a test asserts zero file writes + zero commits); the live run is gated on human review.
- Reconciler pause: disable the `reconcile-bridge.yml` GHA schedule for the window via the GitHub API/CLI
  (`gh workflow disable reconcile-bridge.yml`), verify no pass is mid-flight, and RE-ENABLE in a `finally`/failsafe
  (auto re-enable after N minutes or on repair-process exit) so a crash never leaves it disabled. (The pass-lock
  `refs/reconciler/lock` is a leased CAS lock and would expire, so it is NOT the pause mechanism.) Manual writers
  hold off (documented); the batched+committed+pre-tagged design makes a stray write recoverable.
- Idempotent/resumable: fsck itself is the AUTHORITATIVE resumability check (re-run repairs only tickets fsck still
  flags). A per-ticket `.a3-repaired` marker is a LOCAL, gitignored optimization only. Per-snapshot rewrite uses the
  EXISTING `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` (not hand-rolled). The SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT rename + rebuild hold the
  store write-lock for the per-ticket critical section (no TOCTOU with a concurrent writer). Per-ticket failure
  logs+skips (no batch abort). Batched `--limit=200`, wait >=30s between.

## Scope
`_commands/fsck.py` ONLY (`--repair`/`--dry-run`/`--limit`, per-batch git commit+push, disposition constants, per-snapshot `fsutil.atomic_write`, local marker, write-lock critical section; update the `fsck --help` golden files `tests/golden/cli_help/fsck__help.out` + the `-h` variant). This ticket does NOT edit `compact.py` (A1 owns all compact.py changes) — it CALLS A1's retire helper and A2's `include_retired` rebuild. Gated on RC1 fix #1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `fsck --repair --dry-run` prints per-ticket before/after + dispositions; a test asserts ZERO file writes and ZERO commits in dry-run.
- [ ] Live repair commits+pushes each batch; a push failure ABORTS + surfaces the error; pre-tag created; rollback rehearsed on a fixture (post-rollback store == pre-tag state).
- [ ] Reconciler paused by `gh workflow disable` (verified no in-flight pass), re-enabled in a failsafe `finally`.
- [ ] Orphan disposition is a code constant covering ALL KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES; AUTO-RECOVER rebuilt, HUMAN-TRIAGE surfaced (not auto-rebuilt); tested.
- [ ] Resumability via fsck re-check; `.a3-repaired` marker local/gitignored; per-snapshot rewrite uses `fsutil.atomic_write`; write-lock held per ticket; crash-before-marker is safe (test).
- [ ] Synthetic-fixture unit tests: SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT / ORPHAN_EVENT (both dispositions) / MISSING_CREATE (incl. `.retired`) repair correctly.
- [ ] Live store reaches 0 UNRESOLVED faults (triaged+documented orphans count as resolved); before/after counts recorded.
baseline.summary: Live-store corruption remediation: drive fsck to zero

baseline.description:
Discovered while implementing 03ef-6fb5-158b-4abd (scheduled mirror main CI).

## Context

Before 03ef, `codeql.yml` ran on every push to `main` PLUS a weekly schedule, and its own comment described the weekly cron as catching "advisories that land between pushes" — i.e. the push trigger was the primary scan of new code and the schedule was the backstop for newly published advisories.

03ef dropped the push trigger from every workflow so the mirror's `main` CI reports branch health on a schedule rather than per-commit. CodeQL was NOT moved onto the new 6-hourly tick at that time; the workflow header asserted that a 6-hourly cadence would be "a 28x increase nobody asked for". That left the weekly cron as CodeQL's PRIMARY scan of newly-landed code rather than a between-pushes backstop, so a newly-introduced SAST finding could sit unscanned for up to 7 days.

## The decision (made by the operator — settled, not open)

**CodeQL moves to the 6-hourly tick.** The operator's instruction, verbatim: "CodeQL should be running every 6 hours, which is the cadence I specified for scheduled CI to replace push on main."

Reasoning recorded:

* The 6-hourly tick was specified as the **replacement for push-on-main**. CodeQL's original
  design ran it on every push to `main`; leaving it weekly silently *reduced* its coverage of
  newly-landed code rather than preserving it. Joining the tick restores the intended posture.
* The "28x cost increase" rationale in the current header **does not apply**: `navapbc/rebar`
  is a **public** repository, and both CodeQL and GitHub Actions minutes are **free** for public
  repos. The frequency argument was therefore not a billing constraint.
* Worst-case exposure for a newly-introduced SAST finding drops from 7 days to 6 hours.

## Implementation plan

1. `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`
   * Replace the weekly cron `23 4 * * 1` with a 6-hourly cron **`35 */6 * * *`**. The minute is
     off-the-hour (never `0`/`30`) and **distinct from every sibling lane** — `test.yml` is `41`,
     `optionality.yml` is `47`, `verify-identity.yml` is `53` — so the four branch-health lanes
     stay staggered on a 6-minute spacing (35/41/47/53) and none of them pile onto the hour
     boundary that GitHub's scheduler congests.
   * Rewrite the header comment. It currently asserts CodeQL deliberately does NOT join the
     6-hourly tick and cites a 28x cost increase; both statements become **false** with this
     change. A stale comment contradicting the config it sits above is itself a defect.
   * Everything else is unchanged: no `push` trigger is reintroduced, `workflow_dispatch` stays,
     permissions/concurrency/matrix/steps untouched.

2. `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` — existing coverage pins the OLD cadence and will
   go red. **Retarget it; do not delete it.**
   * Move `codeql.yml` out of the `_OWN_CADENCE` map (which asserts a lane keeps a slower cron
     AND carries no `*/6` cron) and into the 6-hourly cohort.
   * Because CodeQL — unlike the other three lanes — has **no push trigger at all**, it cannot
     join the `_SIX_HOURLY` tuple wholesale: that tuple also drives the "push CI for non-main
     branches is preserved" case, which CodeQL would fail. Introduce a separate
     schedule-only cohort so the cadence assertion covers CodeQL while the push-preservation
     assertion does not.
   * Keep every assertion that still holds: CodeQL runs on **no** push to `main`, and CodeQL
     keeps `workflow_dispatch` (both driven by `_NO_MAIN_PUSH`, which must still include it).
   * Add cover for the staggering invariant the operator specified: the 6-hourly lanes use
     **distinct** off-the-hour minutes.
   * Update the module docstring, which currently states the CodeQL scan "stays weekly".

## Out of scope (explicitly not touched)

`gerrit-verify.yaml`, both reconcilers, `external-integration.yml`, `mirror-guard.yml`, every `_*.yml` reusable, `prompt-eval.yml` (billable live-LLM tier — stays weekly), and `terraform-drift.yml` (stays daily).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The cadence question is decided explicitly, with the reasoning recorded (above).
- [x] `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` schedules `35 */6 * * *` and no longer carries `23 4 * * 1`.
- [x] `codeql.yml`'s header comment states the new rationale and no longer asserts that CodeQL
      stays off the 6-hourly tick or that the cadence is a cost tradeoff.
- [x] `codeql.yml` still has no `push` trigger and still has `workflow_dispatch`.
- [x] The four 6-hourly lanes (`test.yml`, `optionality.yml`, `verify-identity.yml`,
      `codeql.yml`) use distinct, off-the-hour minutes.

baseline.description:
Found in ticket 18a4's Phase-1 investigation.

DEFECT. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` carries the structural guard `test_no_search_issues_call_relies_on_the_default_page_size`, whose stated job is "THE CRITERION THAT CONVERTS 'I fixed two' INTO 'a fourth cannot be added silently'": it AST-scans for any `search_issues(...)` call that omits an explicit result cap (which would take `max_results=50` and silently truncate past 50 issues).

It scans exactly ONE file -- `_TRANSPORT_SRC`, i.e. `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (test file line ~31).

Ticket 465d's one-module-per-capability split then moved the pager and every `search_issues` call OUT of `transport.py` (the pager now lives in `_base.py`; the single-page primitive in `_issues.py:262`). MEASURED on origin/main at fc705c64410: an AST walk of `transport.py` finds **0** `search_issues` calls. The guard now scans a file that no longer contains the construct it polices, so it passes unconditionally and would not notice a fifth unpaginated caller added anywhere in the DC adapter.

This is a rotted guard, not a missing one -- and pointedly so: its own sibling test's docstring says "A structural test that cannot fail is decoration -- and this one exists precisely because the previous audit of this seam under-counted."

PROPOSED FIX: widen the scan from the single `transport.py` path to every `*.py` in `adapters/jira_datacenter/`, and add a teeth test proving the widened predicate actually reaches `_base.py` and `_issues.py`. Pre-checked: both current call sites pass an explicit cap (`_base.py:148` `maxResults=page_size`, `_issues.py:262` `maxResults=max_results`), so widening should go green immediately -- confirm rather than assume. Consider whether the same rot hit other single-file AST guards that 465d's split moved code out from.

NOT folded into 18a4 deliberately: 465d owns the module re-architecture whose split caused this, and the repair changes a pre-existing guard's SCOPE (which can surface unrelated offenders), so it is its own reviewable unit.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] The guard scans every module in `adapters/jira_datacenter/`, not just `transport.py`
- [x] A teeth test proves the widened predicate reports a synthetic uncapped call in a
      NON-transport.py module (so it cannot silently rot the same way again)
- [x] Audit and report whether any other single-file AST guard was emptied by 465d's split

---

## PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (Phase 1 confirmed — see RCA comment for the full experiment log)

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:31-34` binds `_TRANSPORT_SRC` to the single hardcoded path `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`, and `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` `ast.parse()`s exactly that one file. Commit `4213081d23` ("Split DC transport into capability mixins", rebar-ticket 465d) moved both `search_issues` call sites out of `transport.py` (they were at transport.py:365 and :406 before the split) into `_issues.py` and `_base.py`, and its own message states "Pure text move: no test edited" — the hardcoded scan path was never moved with the code. Measured at HEAD: an AST walk of `transport.py` finds **0** `search_issues` call nodes, and the live predicate returns `[]`, so `assert not offenders` is unconditionally true.

## PLAN (mechanical; test-only, no runtime behaviour change)

1. **Widen the scan.** Replace `_TRANSPORT_SRC` with `_DC_ADAPTER_DIR`
   (`adapters/jira_datacenter/`) and have `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` walk
   every `*.py` in it, reporting offenders as `<module>.py:<line>` so a failure names the
   file. Keep the existing `src=` override parameter so the current teeth test is unaffected.
2. **Add a non-vacuity assertion.** The guard must also assert the widened scan observed a
   NON-ZERO number of `search_issues` call sites. This is the anti-rot repair proper: if a
   future move empties the directory again, the suite goes RED instead of silently disarming.
   Without this, criterion 1 alone leaves the same rot possible one directory up.
3. **Add a teeth test for the widened predicate** proving it reports a synthetic uncapped
   call attributed to a NON-`transport.py` module, so the directory walk (not just the
   string-source path) is exercised.
4. **Audit** the rest of `tests/` for other single-file AST/structural guards emptied by
   465d's split and report the finding on this ticket.

Pre-measured: both live call sites already pass an explicit cap (`_base.py:172` `maxResults=page_size`; `_issues.py:262` `maxResults=max_results`) and every other module in the directory has zero calls, so the widened guard goes green immediately. No `src/` file is modified.

### file_impact (declared)
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` (the only file changed)

### Verification
- `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` — full module green
- RED proof: the non-vacuity assertion fails against the current single-file scan before the fix
- Mutation check: re-pin the scan to `transport.py` only -> the non-vacuity test returns RED
- `make lint` + `make typecheck`

### Out of scope / explicitly NOT changed
- The DC pager's behaviour, page-size handling, and offset-stall logic (18a4) are untouched.
- No change to any `src/` module; this ticket only restores a guard's scope.
baseline.summary: DC pagination structural guard went VACUOUS after 465d's module split

baseline.description:
## Problem

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` recreates the `compose-review-bot-1` container whenever `main` advances and the bot's source changed. It does NOT drain in-flight reviews first, so recreation stops uvicorn and KILLS whatever code review is running. Because a full code review takes far longer than the gap between deploys during a landing burst, reviews can be killed before they ever vote — and the gate LIVE-LOCKS: no change gets an `LLM-Review` vote, so nothing can submit, which is indistinguishable from an outage.

## MEASURED, live, on 2026-08-03 (account 896586841071, instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

SEVEN recreations in 90 minutes, from `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy`:
    16:23:05, 16:41:17, 16:48:22, 17:10:06, 17:14:46, 17:29:50, 17:49:28
    => gaps of 18, 7, 22, 4, 15, 20 minutes

A full code review, from the bot's own logs, is SEVEN passes and takes ~10 MINUTES:
    code-review-base 94.6s / 103.5s / 134.9s · code-review-tests 92.3s / 125.3s
    code-review-scope-intent 29.1s / 101.0s · code-review-api-compat 96.7s / 114.1s
    code-review-verify 80.9s / 137.6s · plus deletion-impact, phase-boundaries, coach
    >1,000,000 input tokens per change (LLM_TOKEN_USAGE: input 1,010,039, cache_read 883,980)

FOUR of the six gaps are SHORTER than one review. The interruption was observed directly in the log — passes running, then `INFO: Shutting down` / `Application shutdown complete` / `Finished server process [1]`, mid-review.

USER-VISIBLE IMPACT observed at the time: changes 1302 (`Verified +1` at 17:24) and 1303 (`Verified +1` at 17:32) both sat with `LLM-Review = 0` for 20-35 minutes, unsubmittable.

## Why NO ALARM FIRED — this is the part that matters

The bot is HEALTHY by every signal the monitoring has:
  - `docker inspect`: `running`, `restarts=0`
  - every deploy logged `{"event":"autodeploy","msg":"review-bot redeployed + healthy"}`
  - ZERO `VOTER_ERROR` lines, so `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` (monitoring_s4b.tf) stayed `OK`
  - all 11 CloudWatch alarms `OK` throughout
A killed review emits NO `VOTER_ERROR`, because nothing failed — the process was asked to stop. So the fail-closed voter path never runs and the alarm that eb6e's rollback plan depends on cannot see this failure mode AT ALL. **The gate can be fully live-locked while every health signal reads green.**

## Why this is not self-evidently benign

Interrupted reviews ARE retried by the reconciler, so the system self-heals ONCE deploys stop. The defect is that it cannot converge while deploys keep arriving faster than reviews complete — and a landing burst is exactly when the gate is most needed. Convergence depends on the burst ending, not on any bound in the deploy path.

## Relevance to the Bedrock cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]

eb6e removes the cross-provider fallback and names the `VOTER_ERROR` CloudWatch alarm as its safety net. This bug shows a live-lock the gate can enter that the alarm provably does not observe, so that safety net has a blind spot independent of provider. Worth resolving, or at least recording, before the cutover relies on it.

## Approach

Make recreation wait for in-flight work, rather than making reviews survive recreation. Options to weigh:
  (a) DRAIN: before `docker compose up -d`, poll a bot endpoint for in-flight review count and wait up to
      a bounded timeout; recreate immediately when idle. Needs an endpoint exposing that count.
  (b) DEFER: if the bot reports busy, skip this deploy cycle and retry on the next timer tick (~2 min).
      Simplest, and autodeploy is already an idempotent oneshot timer, so skipping is natural.
  (c) COALESCE: debounce — require N seconds of no new `main` commits before deploying, so a burst
      produces one deploy instead of seven.
(b) and (c) compose well and need no new bot surface. Whatever is chosen, bound the wait so a permanently busy bot cannot block deploys forever, and LOG the deferral so a skipped deploy is visible rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A deploy that would interrupt an in-flight review is DEFERRED or DRAINED rather than recreating the
      container mid-review, proven by a test or a scripted simulation of the busy case.
- [x] The deferral/drain is BOUNDED, so a permanently-busy bot cannot block deploys indefinitely, and the
      bound is stated with its rationale.
- [x] A deferred deploy is LOGGED and visible (journald + the autodeploy metric), so a skipped cycle can
      never be mistaken for no change having landed.
- [x] The interrupted-review failure mode becomes OBSERVABLE: either it emits a countable marker that an
      alarm can watch, or the gap is explicitly recorded as accepted with its reasoning — the current
      state, where a fully live-locked gate leaves every health signal green, is what this criterion
      exists to end.
- [x] A landing BURST is covered, not just a single deploy: a simulation with commits arriving faster than
      one review completes ends with the review voting rather than being killed repeatedly.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Autodeploy recreates the review-bot mid-review, so a landing burst live-locks the LLM-Review gate

## Why

The additive-attestations rollout (epic dark-acme-lumen) kept a legacy single-slot `state['signature']` mirror alongside the authoritative kind-keyed `state['attestations']` map — the *expand* half of an expand/contract. This ticket ships the *contract* half: stop carrying the mirror in new SNAPSHOTs. Dropping it is a one-way door (a pre-attestations clone reads `state['signature']` and has no map to fall back to), so it is gated on a readiness condition, made fully reversible by config, and documented.

## What (ordered so no reader ever sees a stripped mirror)

1. **ADD a NEW helper** `signing.most_recent_attestation(state)` (does not exist today; this
   ticket creates it). Semantics: return the record with the greatest `signed_at` from
   `state['attestations']` (ties → last processed, matching the legacy mirror's
   last-writer-wins); fall back to `state['signature']` only when the map is absent/empty.
   This reproduces the mirror's "latest signature of any kind" from the authoritative map.
2. **Migrate all three in-tree mirror readers to call that helper** (so they no longer read
   `state['signature']` directly), done BEFORE step 3 so a stripped mirror is never observed:
   `signing._record_for_kind` (kind=None verify-latest path), `_engine_support/validate.py`
   (`signature_findings` — same "most-recent record, verify_record it" semantics, now
   map-sourced), and `_commands/txn.py:_signature_gate` (line 362, require_signature_for_close).
   Because `attestations` is always present on a post-feature snapshot (and old snapshots are
   folded into it on read), every migrated reader still finds the record after the drop.
3. **Only then drop the mirror on the write side:** `compact.py` strips the legacy `signature`
   key from a SNAPSHOT's compiled_state (normal-compaction AND fsck-rebuild paths), gated by a
   NEW `compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror` config flag (default `false` = drop).
4. Keep the read-side fold-in (`_processors.py`) so pre-map snapshots still upgrade on read.
5. Document the readiness gate, rollback, and target version.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`, `src/rebar/signing.py`, `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `docs/migrations.md`, tests under `tests/unit/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] Readiness gate satisfied before the mirror is dropped: no
  pre-attestations clone/reconcile-host that reads `state['signature']` remains live. Evidence:
  this fleet auto-updates hourly to origin/main (so no pre-attestations binary is live), and
  the gate + upgrade-first ordering is documented in docs/migrations.md "Legacy
  signature-mirror retirement". Recorded as a ticket attestation.
- [ ] Rollback + named target version: the drop is reversible with NO code downgrade — setting
  `compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror = true` (env `REBAR_COMPACT_EMIT_LEGACY_SIGNATURE_MIRROR`)
  re-emits the mirror on the next compaction. Named rollback target: that flag on the 0.7.x
  line (introduced after 0.7.1). Documented in docs/migrations.md; verified by a unit test that
  the rollback flag keeps `signature` in the snapshot.
- [ ] Contract: a new SNAPSHOT's compiled_state contains `attestations` but NOT the legacy
  `signature` mirror (default flag), and docs note the field retired. Verified by unit tests
  in `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py` covering: (a) the strip default drops
  `signature` and the rollback flag keeps it; (b) `most_recent_attestation` resolves the
  latest-by-signed_at record from the map (this is the SINGLE accessor all three migrated
  readers — `signing._record_for_kind` kind=None, `validate.py:signature_findings`,
  `txn.py:_signature_gate` — now call, so one accessor test covers all three call sites);
  (c) a mirror-less snapshot round-trips through `process_snapshot` and still resolves via the
  map; (d) the legacy-mirror fallback when the map is absent. docs/migrations.md documents the
  retirement.

## Verification

- `make lint && make typecheck` pass; `pytest tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py`
  and the signing/attestation suites (test_signing, test_attestations_reducer,
  test_attestation_verify, lifecycle/test_signature) pass with no regressions.
baseline.summary: Contract phase: drop the legacy signature SNAPSHOT mirror (post-upgrade)

baseline.description:
## Problem

`acli` (the Atlassian CLI) is a hard runtime prerequisite for rebar's Jira **Cloud** paths, and nothing at install time says so.

- It is invoked as a bare binary resolved from `PATH`: `_DEFAULT_ACLI_CMD: list[str] = ["acli"]` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:32`), used throughout `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py`.
- It **cannot** be a Python dependency — it is an external binary — so no extra can pull it in.
- The Jira-related extras declare only Python packages: `jira-datacenter = ["jira>=3.8,<4"]` and `adf = ["marklas", "mistune"]`. There is **no** extra for the Cloud/acli path at all, and no extra mentions the binary.
- It IS documented in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` (pinned version + sha256, download URL) — but in a **CI-setup** context (`gh variable set ACLI_VERSION`), not as a prerequisite for someone installing the package.

**Consequence.** A user installs a Jira extra, gets a successful install, and then every Jira-mutating operation fails at runtime with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'`. That errno names a file, not a missing dependency, and gives no install instruction — so the user has no path from the failure to the fix.

Observed 2026-08-28 on the deployed box: with credentials finally reaching the container, `bridge_check_access` returned `{"verdict":"FAIL","steps":[{"step":"STEP_CREATE","reason":"exception","detail":"[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"}]}`. The box case is filed separately as `royalistic-gorgeable-norwayrat` (54e6-ecb0-10c7-451f) — this ticket is the **package-level** sibling: the same gap as it reaches anyone who installs rebar.

## Why it matters for the release

Documentation and error messages ship. Telling a user to `pip install nava-rebar[...]` for Jira and leaving them to discover an undocumented binary via an errno is a defect in the installed product, not in our deployment.

## Two parts, both wanted

**1. Document it.** State `acli` as a prerequisite wherever the Jira extras are described (extras documentation, install docs, and the packaging metadata description if extras are listed there), with an install pointer. Say plainly WHICH paths need it: the Cloud adapter needs `acli`; the Data Center adapter uses the `jira` Python library and does not.

**2. Fail usefully.** Replace the bare `FileNotFoundError` with a typed, actionable failure at the point of use or in a preflight: name the missing binary, say it is required for Jira Cloud operations, and point at the install docs. `access_check` already fail-closes with typed verdicts (`missing_credentials`, `missing_project`), so a `missing_acli` verdict fits the existing shape rather than inventing one. This is the same principle just landed on `potential-powellite-mouflon` (dbca): a caller-visible failure should carry the class that tells the caller what to do.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The Jira extras' documentation names `acli` as a required external binary for the Cloud path, with an install pointer, and states that the Data Center path does not need it. (README.md prerequisite bullet, docs/jira-sync-setup.md non-container note, pyproject.toml `[jira-datacenter]`-exempt comment — Gerrit 2397, MERGED.)
- [x] A missing `acli` produces a typed, actionable failure naming the binary and the remedy — not a bare `[Errno 2]`. (`AcliNotInstalledError` raised at the `_run_acli` Popen site / `require_acli` preflight, message names `acli`, Cloud, and docs/jira-sync-setup.md; subclasses `FileNotFoundError` so existing handlers still catch it.)
- [x] The typed failure is distinguishable from `missing_credentials` and `missing_project`, so a caller can tell "not installed" from "not configured". (Held-out test `test_missing_binary_vs_missing_credentials_are_distinct` proves the three states yield three distinct results; scope boundary respects ac93 which owns the access_check verdict mapping.)
- [x] The Data Center path is demonstrably unaffected — it must not acquire a dependency on `acli`. (`test_data_center_path_does_not_import_acli_transport` guard; DC uses the `jira` REST client and never spawns acli.)

## Testing

- Drive the failure with `acli` genuinely absent from `PATH` (manipulate `PATH`, do not monkeypatch the check away) and assert the typed code and message content.
- **Anchor against vacuity:** a test asserting "an error was raised" passes for the WRONG error, which is the defect being fixed. Assert the specific code, and prove the three states are distinguished from each other — missing-binary vs missing-credentials vs missing-project must produce three different results, not merely three failures.
- Add a positive control: with a stub `acli` on `PATH`, the preflight passes — otherwise the check could be unconditionally failing and the test would not notice.
- Mutation-check: collapse the new code into the existing ones and confirm the discrimination test fails.
baseline.summary: acli is an undeclared, undocumented runtime prerequisite of the Jira extras: install succeeds, then every Cloud path dies with a bare errno

baseline.description:
Discovered while fixing dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d (potential-powellite-mouflon). This ticket is now **scoped to the one reachable, unambiguous site**; the two design-decision siblings were split out (see "Split-out siblings" below), following the /rebar-debug escalate-design-decisions guard.

## Problem (in scope)
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py:541` raises a **bare** `WorkflowError("unknown scripted step {name!r} (not in the step registry)")`. Because `WorkflowError` subclasses `LLMError`, `error_code_for` (`src/rebar/_errors.py`, branch 7) maps it to `llm_unavailable`. An unknown scripted `uses:` step is a caller/plan-authoring fault, not an LLM outage.

## Mechanism / reachability (proven — see Phase-1 RCA + CORRECTION comments)
- The linter (`lint_refs.py`) validates step shape/fields but NOT scripted-step registry membership, so an unknown `uses:` name passes lint and is only caught at execute time by this raise.
- **CORRECTED (latency finding):** the raise is caught by the interpreter (`interpreter.py:509-511` `except Exception` around `_dispatch`) and folded into a failed `StepResult` string — the exception TYPE is discarded. A runtime oracle (instrumented `error_code_for` + a real `run_workflow` with an unknown `uses:`) confirmed `error_code_for` is **never** invoked during the run. So the misclassification is a **latent** static property of `error_code_for`, with no observable `llm_unavailable` on any live surface today. The fix is a contract-completeness correction of the classifier (defense-in-depth), matching exactly how dbca handled the sibling subtypes.

## Contract violated
dbca established the per-subclass taxonomy: a workflow that WAS found but is invalid (parse/lint/migrate) is caller `invalid_input`; only the bare execute base stays `llm_unavailable` (protects genuine execute-time outages, dbca AC3). An unknown `uses:` step is a found-but-invalid workflow — the same class as `WorkflowValidationError`→`invalid_input`. dbca's own suite asserts `error_code_for(...)` directly for these subtypes, so classifier correctness is a directly-testable project contract. `invalid_input` is already in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` (no new vocabulary).

## Fix plan (IMPLEMENTED — landed as Gerrit change 2395, merged f854924b1bc4)
1. `src/rebar/llm/errors.py`: add `WorkflowUnknownStepError(WorkflowError)` — message passthrough, mirroring `WorkflowNotFoundError`.
2. `src/rebar/_errors.py`: add `WorkflowUnknownStepError` to the `invalid_input` group in `_workflow_caller_code` (extends the existing isinstance tuple — no new branch, no complexity increase). Docstrings updated.
3. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py`: raise `WorkflowUnknownStepError(...)` instead of the bare base, message preserved; import it.
4. Held-out regression `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_35ab.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1: An unknown scripted `uses:` step (executor.py:541) classifies as `invalid_input`, not `llm_unavailable`, via `error_code_for` and the `_structured_llm_failure` LLM-tier surface. — Evidence: `test_unknown_step_error_classifies_as_invalid_input`, `test_unknown_step_error_structured_llm_failure_is_invalid_input`, and the white-box `test_dispatch_unknown_step_raises_unknown_step_error` (the raise site now raises the subtype). All GREEN.
- [x] AC2: The bare `WorkflowError` execute base and genuine LLM outages (`LLMUnavailableError`, `LLMError`) still classify as `llm_unavailable` (dbca AC3 preserved). — Evidence: `test_execute_base_and_outages_still_llm_unavailable` GREEN; full dbca suite still passes.
- [x] AC3: The emitted code is a member of `rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`; no new vocabulary added. — Evidence: tests assert `code in rebar.KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`; `invalid_input` already existed.
- [x] AC4: Held-out RED→GREEN regression test asserts on the error CODE (not message text) and had teeth (mutation returns it to RED). — Evidence: RED first (missing type), GREEN after fix; two sandboxed mutations (revert raise site → `WorkflowError`; drop from invalid_input tuple) each returned the oracle to RED (`invalid_input`→`llm_unavailable` observed).

## Split-out siblings (escalated design decisions — NOT in this ticket)
- **551b-1a30-ac2b-4127** (sanidine-cilium-eland): editor.py:475 missing-bundle `WorkflowError`. CLI-only (not MCP-exposed; the CLI prints the raw message and never classifies), so not observably misclassified; correct code needs a NEW-vocabulary design decision the operator directed to escalate.
- **73d8-4871-1b49-4047** (brainy-convulsant-unicorn): `ExpressionError` (execute-time workflow wiring) also classifies as `llm_unavailable`; whether to reclassify an execute-time expression fault is a design decision.

Origin: caused_by 8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239 (blanket LLMError→llm_unavailable), class plan_defect — same as dbca.

## Why

Two regexes key on the `## Success Criteria` heading and one scope extractor lists it. They are the only code that READS the heading to make a decision, so until they change the heading remains load-bearing and the store migration cannot be verified. (One further site, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:308`, WRITES the heading into generated eval fixtures; that is a producer, not a reader, and belongs to the eval-specs story — this story does not depend on it and its AC greps deliberately do not cover it.) `_count_ac_items` already counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under `## Acceptance Criteria`, so criteria written under SC never reach the P1 blocking floor and can never carry the `[operator-attested]` tag — collapsing the two TIGHTENS the gate.

## What

Point the heading-reading code at `## Acceptance Criteria`, and update the test fixtures that embed `## Success Criteria` in ticket descriptions.

## Scope

Code:
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:136` — the epic branch of `_clarity_score`, currently
  `+2` for `^##\s+Success Criteria`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:227` — the deliberate copy of that heuristic used for
  P1 coverage (non-blocking); the two must stay in lockstep, which the module comments require.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py:253` — `_SCOPE_HEADINGS`, which lists
  `"## success criteria"` alongside `"## acceptance criteria"`; drop the SC entry.

Test fixtures embedding the heading:
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_rubric_consistency.py:4,36`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py:48`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree.py:28`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree_heldout.py:22`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_story_epic.py:29`
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py:219,293,356,407,425,465`
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py:108`

OUT OF SCOPE: removing `clarity-check` entirely (separately planned). This story only stops it keying on the SC heading.

## Approach

In both `_clarity_score` copies the epic branch REPOINTS its `+2` from `^##\s+Success Criteria` to `^##\s+Acceptance Criteria`. Because AC is already a universal blocking floor, the bonus becomes automatic and the epic branch stops discriminating. That is accepted deliberately: clarity-check is a dead metric already slated for removal, and the alternative is worse.

The arithmetic, measured against the real `_clarity_score` rather than estimated. The epic fixture in `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` scores 6 today (heading +1, len>=200 +1, len>=500 +1, bullet +1, SC +2 ... minus length, netting 6 at 440 chars). With the SC block removed and the bonus DROPPED it scores 4 at 412 chars — below the default threshold of 5, so `test_clarity_pass_implies_check_ac_pass[epic]` goes RED and would need the fixture padded past 500 chars to compensate. With the bonus REPOINTED it scores 6, unchanged.

Dropping the bonus would also lower every real epic in the store by 2, risking a live clarity-check regression across the 108 migrated tickets for the sake of a metric being deleted. Repointing avoids both the fixture fragility and that regression, so it is the chosen route.

`_SCOPE_HEADINGS` loses `"## success criteria"`; `"## acceptance criteria"` already covers the collapsed vocabulary.

Fixtures that carry BOTH headings drop the SC block; fixtures carrying SC as their only criteria block have it renamed to `## Acceptance Criteria` with its bullets converted to `- [ ]` items so they still satisfy the P1 floor.

## Testing

- `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` is the invariant that a clarity-PASS implies a check-ac
  PASS; it must stay green with the epic fixture no longer carrying SC.
- `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle tests/interfaces/store tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` green.
- A new case pinning that an epic carrying `## Acceptance Criteria` plus `## Context` (the two
  remaining epic signals) passes BOTH `clarity-check` and `check-ac`. The fixture deliberately
  keeps `## Context` so the case tests the AC repoint rather than the degenerate
  zero-heading-signal path.
- An assertion of the score itself (`_clarity_score(fixture, "epic") == 6`), so a future change
  to the weights fails loudly here instead of silently drifting the epic fixture under the
  threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn "Success Criteria" src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py` returns no matches.
- [ ] The two `_clarity_score` copies remain textually in lockstep (verified by diffing the two
      epic branches), preserving the invariant their comments assert.
- [ ] No *fixture* under `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, `tests/interfaces/store/` or
      `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` still describes a ticket using
      `## Success Criteria`. Verified by
      `grep -rn '## Success Criteria' <those paths> --exclude=test_criteria_heading_collapse.py`
      returning no matches. AMENDED during implementation: as originally written this was a
      blanket string prohibition, which is unsatisfiable alongside the epic's own design —
      sibling story 5f4d requires the reintroduction guard be "proven by a test that injects
      one", so the epic MUST contain a file carrying the literal heading. This story's new
      contract test `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` is that
      file: every occurrence is a negative-case probe demonstrating the heading is inert
      (one of them, L144, asserts its ABSENCE from the code-review scope context). The
      criterion's intent — no fixture corpus carries SC as live plan vocabulary — is met in
      full. 5f4d's allowlist must cover that file; a note is recorded on 5f4d.
- [ ] A new test asserts an epic whose description carries `## Acceptance Criteria` and
      `## Context` passes both `clarity-check` and `check-ac` (exit 0 each), and that
      `_clarity_score(fixture, "epic")` equals 6 — the same score the fixture earns today, so
      the repoint is proven score-neutral rather than assumed.
- [ ] The epic fixture in `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` needs NO length padding to stay
      green, confirming the repoint (not a drop) was implemented.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Point heading-detection code and its test corpus at Acceptance Criteria

baseline.description:
## Finding

Canonical contributor guidance hardcodes a specific maintainer/bot DCO identity even though project contribution policy requires contributors to sign with their own real configured identity.

## Evidence

- `AGENTS.md:124-169` documents the Gerrit workflow and currently prescribes `Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>`.
- `.agents/rules/rebar.md:28-34` repeats the same personal bot identity.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:198-214` requires a real contributor name and email for DCO sign-off.

## Remediation

Make the canonical guidance identity-neutral: contributors and agents use the real name and email configured for the actor performing the commit (`git config user.name` / `git config user.email`). Retain Joe Oakhart's bot identity only in narrowly scoped automation guidance for a workflow that actually runs as that bot.

Cascade flag: documentation-only contract change; verify all imported/copied agent guidance (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/*.md`, and any other contributor-facing guidance under `docs/`) so contradictory instructions do not remain. Automation-owned paths (`infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/fixtures/`) and experiment corpora (`docs/experiments/`) legitimately reference the bot identity and are explicitly out of scope for the sweep and for the consistency check below.

Add a deterministic consistency check: a `make lint`-integrated grep step (e.g. a target in the `Makefile`, or a script under `scripts/` invoked from `make lint`) that runs `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md' CONTRIBUTING.md ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' ':(exclude)docs/experiments/**'` (the `:(glob)` pathspec magic makes `**` recurse into subdirectories under `docs/`; the `:(exclude)` pathspec drops `docs/experiments/` from the scan) and fails the build if it finds any match. `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, and `tests/` are excluded by construction because they are not passed as pathspecs. Document, next to the check, which file owns it and that `infra/`/`.github/workflows/`/`tests/`/`docs/experiments/` are the intentional exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` tells contributors and agents to verify `git config user.name` and `git config user.email` and to sign off with that configured real identity. Verify: `grep -q 'git config user.name' AGENTS.md && grep -q 'git config user.email' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] `.agents/rules/rebar.md` and any derived guidance no longer instruct every actor to use Joe Oakhart's bot identity. Verify: `! git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- '.agents/rules/*.md' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Any retained Joe-specific identity is explicitly scoped to the automation that owns it (e.g. `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) and is not presented as general contributor guidance. Verify: `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart'` returns matches ONLY under `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/`, or `docs/experiments/`; any match outside those prefixes fails the check.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md`, canonical agent guidance, and generated/imported guidance describe one consistent DCO contract, defined concretely as: all three name "the committer's own configured git identity (`git config user.name`/`user.email`)" as the sign-off source, and none of them names a specific third party (Joe Oakhart or otherwise) as the required sign-off for general contributions. Verify: `for f in CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md .agents/rules/rebar.md; do grep -q "configured git identity" "$f" || exit 1; done` exits 0 (each file must contain the phrase, or the loop exits non-zero on the first miss), AND `git grep -l 'Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md'` returns no results.
- [ ] A deterministic consistency check exists and fails the build on a reintroduced hardcoded personal sign-off: implemented as a `make lint`-integrated grep step (script or Makefile target) running `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md' CONTRIBUTING.md ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' ':(exclude)docs/experiments/**'` (the `:(glob)` magic recurses into `docs/adr/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/migrations/`, `docs/calibration/`, etc.; `:(exclude)` drops `docs/experiments/`; `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/` are excluded by not being passed as pathspecs) and fails the build (non-zero exit) if `git grep` finds any match. Verify: the new check's script/target exists, running it against the post-change guidance files exits 0, and running it against a scratch copy with the hardcoded string reinjected exits non-zero.
baseline.summary: Make contributor sign-off guidance identity-neutral

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
In `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, the `golden-path` job executes `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq && jq --version` unconditionally on every run. On standard GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` runners, `jq` is already pre-installed out of the box, making the 15–30s `apt-get update` call redundant overhead.

## Approach
Use a conditional check `type jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || (sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq) && jq --version`. This evaluates `type jq` in <0.001s and skips `apt-get update` when `jq` is present, while safely falling back to package installation if executed on a minimal runner environment lacking `jq`.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (`golden-path` job step)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` uses a conditional fallback check for `jq` installation in the `golden-path` job step.
- [x] `make lint` (ruff + actionlint + zizmor) passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` passes.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes all 17 tests.
baseline.summary: Avoid redundant apt-get update in gerrit-verify golden-path step when jq is present

baseline.description:
## Summary

Sibling sweep of bug 5546 (rebar-debug Step 7). 5546's root cause is a repeatable pattern, not a one-off: **a bare `git fetch <remote> <branch>` whose result is then consumed as `<remote>/<branch>`.** A bare fetch always writes FETCH_HEAD but only *opportunistically* writes `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` — and only when the remote's CONFIGURED refspec covers that branch. Under a narrow refspec (`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, which is what `git clone --single-branch` AND `actions/checkout` produce by default) the ref is never written, or — worse, when it already exists — never UPDATED, so the consumer silently reads a missing or STALE ref.

5546 fixed the `sync.py` instance. Two live instances remain; both were confirmed semantically (read in context), not by string match.

## Sibling 1 — `src/rebar/_store/push.py:182`

```python
_git(base_path, "fetch", remote, branch)          # :182  bare fetch
...
merge = _git(base_path, "merge", remote_ref, ...) # :202  consumes f"{remote}/{branch}"
```

This is the non-fast-forward retry loop. Under a narrow refspec the merge target is missing or stale, so the merge cannot absorb what actually rejected the push and **every retry re-pushes the same rejected history until the budget is exhausted.**

## Sibling 2 — `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:286,309` (and the canary at :424,:436)

```sh
git fetch origin tickets || true                      # :286
ahead=$(git rev-list --count origin/tickets..HEAD ...) # :287  consumes origin/tickets
...
git fetch origin tickets 2>&1 || ...                  # :309  inside the retry loop
```

Note the SAME workflow already uses the correct explicit form at line 115 (`git fetch origin '+tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets'`), as does `verify-identity.yml:55` — so these sites are internally inconsistent, which is good evidence they are an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

**This is a strong candidate root cause for bug 449f-f9bf-be90-47fe** (and for the Reconcile Bridge push-rejection evidence recorded in 5546's own comment thread: 4 runs on 2026-07-30 exhausting a 5-retry budget with `! [rejected] HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)`). Because line 115 creates `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` earlier in the job, the later bare fetches at :286/:309 leave it STALE rather than absent — so `rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD` and the reconcile merge both operate on a snapshot that never advances, and the retry loop provably cannot converge no matter how large the budget. That mechanism has NOT yet been experimentally confirmed against a real runner; it is a cited hypothesis, and confirming or rejecting it is the first task here.

## Deliberately NOT siblings (checked and cleared)

- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:70,87` — bare fetch, then consumes
  `review/<branch>` / `tickets/<branch>`. Same shape, but the workspace is built by
  `git init` + `git remote add`, which installs the DEFAULT WILDCARD refspec, so the
  branch is always covered. Not reachable.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:347`, `review_bot/gerrit_client.py:335`,
  `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:115`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:86`,
  `verify-identity.yml:55` — already use an explicit refspec. Correct as written.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:375` — a genuine instance, but bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220
  already owns and fixes it. Excluded to avoid a conflicting edit.

## Why filed rather than folded into 5546

5546's authorized surface was `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` + its tests. `push.py` and the CI workflows are separate blast radii — the workflow change in particular needs a real runner to verify — so they get their own reviewable change rather than riding along.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 449f hypothesis above is experimentally confirmed or rejected against a real
      narrow-refspec checkout; if confirmed, 449f is linked to this ticket.
- [ ] `push.py`'s retry-loop fetch uses an explicit refspec, with a test proving the
      non-fast-forward retry loop converges under a narrow clone refspec (it currently
      cannot).
- [ ] The reconcile-bridge workflows' bare `git fetch origin tickets` sites use the
      explicit refspec already used at line 115 of the same file.
- [ ] A guard (lint rule, test, or reviewer-facing note) prevents the bare-fetch form
      from being reintroduced.
baseline.summary: sibling sweep of 5546: bare git fetch leaves <remote>/<branch> missing or stale in push.py and the reconcile-bridge workflows

## Parity sibling discovered by the rebar-debug sweep of `254e-1770-854b-47a2`

While fixing the Anthropic LLM transport's zero/expired-`Retry-After` herd vector (254e), the Step-7 parity census found the **same class-B vector** on a parallel, non-LLM surface: the Jira reconciler's 429 backoff. This is filed (not fixed in 254e) because 254e's operator-approved scope is explicitly **Anthropic-only** ("Bedrock path untouched; Anthropic-only change") and the reconciler is a separate subsystem (ADR 0036, its own MAX_BACKOFF/attempt policy).

### The finding
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py` `parse_retry_after()` returns `secs if secs >= 0 else None` — so a `Retry-After: 0` parses to **`0.0`**, not `None`. Callers then honor it as an immediate retry:
- `dispatch_apply_phases.py` `_call_with_retry`: `delay = min(MAX_BACKOFF_S, retry_after)` -> `min(60, 0.0) = 0.0` -> `time.sleep(0.0)` -> immediate replay.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` `_rate_limit_delay`: `min(MAX_BACKOFF_S, 0.0 * (1+jitter)) = 0.0` (the `is not None` guard passes for `0.0`).
- `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py` `_rate_limit_backoff`: the `\d+(\.\d+)?` regex matches `0` -> `min(0.0, MAX) = 0.0`.

Across concurrent reconcilers hitting the SAME Jira instance, a server-sent `Retry-After: 0` synchronizes an immediate replay — the identical thundering-herd class B that 254e fixes for Anthropic.

### NOT present here (unlike Anthropic)
The class-A vector (non-jittered no-`Retry-After` fallback) is **absent**: all three reconciler adapters already jitter their no-header fallback (`2**(attempt+1)+random.random()` / `+uniform(0,1)` / `retry_after*(1+random*0.2)`). Only the zero-guard (class B) is missing.

### Proposed fix (single-source, low blast radius)
Change `parse_retry_after` to treat a non-positive value as absent: `return secs if secs > 0 else None` (0/negative -> `None` -> the already-jittered fallback). This fixes all three callers at the shared parser. Confirm the DC/acli inline parses agree (acli regex could also be tightened to ignore a `0`). Add a RED test asserting a `Retry-After: 0` yields the jittered fallback (`> 0`), not `sleep(0)`, per the same held-out RED->GREEN discipline used in 254e.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `parse_retry_after("0")` (and `"0.0"`) returns `None`, so callers use the jittered fallback; a held-out unit test asserts the resulting reconciler backoff delay is `> 0`.
- [ ] A positive `Retry-After` (e.g. `"2"`) is still honored (regression guard), capped at `MAX_BACKOFF_S`.
- [ ] The no-`Retry-After` jittered fallback in all three adapters is unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; lands via Gerrit.

## Testing
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit -k "retry_after or reconciler_retry" -q` (new/updated held-out tests over `parse_retry_after` and `_call_with_retry`).
- Full gate: `make lint && make typecheck && make test`.
baseline.summary: Reconciler backoff: parse_retry_after treats Retry-After: 0 as an immediate retry (zero-guard parity with the Anthropic transport)

baseline.description:
`bridge_fsck` reads `prev_snapshot.json` off disk as its offline Jira oracle and uses the **field values**, so narrowing prev to a key-set (A4-2) would silently degrade its drift classification. Fence it first. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why first
`bridge_fsck.py:306-308` loads the file as `jira_snapshot` and passes `fields=jira_snapshot[key]` into `ObservedJira.PRESENT` at `:344` and `:380`. With `{}` entries, membership still works but every field-based classification degrades. This is an **out-of-band consumer of the file itself**, not of `ctx.prev_snapshot`, so no test that exercises `reconcile_once` would catch it. It reads the **working tree**, so it is unaffected by clone filters.

## Approach
Make the field-dependence explicit: classify on membership where that is sufficient, and where a field value is genuinely required, report the classification as **indeterminate** rather than inferring from an empty dict. Do not silently treat absent fields as absent values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Against a **key-set** prev fixture (`{jira_key: {}}`), `bridge_fsck` drift classification is
      identical to its classification against the equivalent full-payload fixture for every case that
      does not require a field value, and reports **indeterminate** (never a false drift) for cases
      that do. Tier: **unit** with paired fixtures.
- [ ] Against a full-payload prev, behaviour is byte-identical to today (no regression for the
      pre-A4-2 world). Tier: **unit** golden comparison.
- [ ] `rebar bridge-fsck` exit code and JSON shape are unchanged for both fixtures. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py`, tests

Scope: S. No dependencies (independent of A1/A2/A3).
baseline.summary: A4-1: fence bridge_fsck's offline drift oracle before prev_snapshot is narrowed

baseline.description:
## Context
While revalidating `epidemic-chocolaty-imago` at `origin/main` `813baac9b01524a024523a8516d563b17f395358`, `rebar review-plan` failed closed before model execution: `git fetch from origin timed out after 300s`. GitHub authentication and ref discovery were healthy: `git ls-remote --heads origin main` completed in 1.09s.

The code checkout configures `remote.origin.fetch=+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`. `rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.resolve_ref` always calls `fetch_origin` without a ref before resolution, and materialized attested review sets `blobless=False`; production therefore runs an unfiltered `git fetch origin` across every configured head. This repository deliberately keeps code on `main` and the large ticket store on `tickets` at the same remote, so a review of `origin/main` pulls the unrelated tickets history into the code checkout common object database. At reproduction time that shared database reported 117 packs, 8,758,551 packed objects, and 11.55 GiB of pack storage, plus interrupted temporary packs.

A controlled reproduction of the exact unfiltered general fetch remained active for more than one minute and was stopped after proving the transfer shape. A separate disposable clone configured by `git clone --single-branch --branch main --filter=blob:none` had only `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, completed in 22 seconds, and the same attested plan review completed with a signed PASS at the exact upstream SHA. This excludes missing credentials, an unreachable remote, ticket material, and the model runner.

## Relationship to existing repairs
`agrologic-oval-bobolink` proves that ref-updating fetches also require common-directory coordination and bounded recovery. Its scope preserves tracker sync’s explicit tickets refspec and addresses concurrent compare-and-swap races; it does not prevent the snapshot layer from fetching unrelated heads or transferring an oversized branch. This bug is complementary, not a duplicate. Do not weaken that ticket’s coordination requirements, remove tracker sync’s explicit tickets refspec, reintroduce a size gate, or make ordinary reviews depend on a tickets-store budget.

## Remediation constraints
Resolve and materialize only the requested gate ref while preserving freshness for moving branches/tags and support for explicit reachable SHAs. An unfiltered materialization may fetch all objects reachable from the selected ref, but must not update or transfer unrelated remote heads. Preserve fail-closed attested semantics, credential-safe errors, noninteractive authentication, partial-clone correctness, and the common-directory coordination/recovery contract tracked by `agrologic-oval-bobolink`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reviewing `origin/main` against a remote that also has a much larger `tickets` head fetches/materializes `main` without updating `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` or transferring objects reachable only from `tickets`.
- [ ] Moving branch and tag refs are refreshed before resolution, and an explicit reachable SHA remains supported with a descriptive fail-closed error when the server refuses the want.
- [ ] `blobless=False` obtains every blob needed to materialize the selected commit in one bounded path without latching an ordinary clone into an unusable promisor state.
- [ ] Snapshot fetches retain common-Git-directory coordination and bounded recovery from `agrologic-oval-bobolink`; network I/O does not take the ticket write lock.
- [ ] Deterministic local-repository tests include an oversized unrelated branch and prove selected-ref transfer/ref-update isolation before and after the fix.
- [ ] Existing plan-review, completion-verifier, code-review, tag, SHA, partial-clone, authentication, timeout, and narrow-tracker-sync tests remain green.
- [ ] Concurrency/snapshot documentation explains selected-ref fetch scope and its distinction from tracker synchronization.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.
baseline.summary: Attested snapshot fetch pulls unrelated oversized tickets branch

# Gerrit change descriptions show line breaks at fixed-width intervals

## Context / Problem

Reported alongside bug 4e21 (Jira descriptions rendering a break at the end of every soft-wrapped line). The reporter observes a similar-looking line-break problem on Gerrit change descriptions.

## What has already been ruled out

Bug 4e21's fix does NOT address this. That fix changes `text_to_adf` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py`, which lives in the Jira adapter and is reachable only from the Jira REST v3 payload builders (`adapters/jira/acli.py:201`, `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:369`) plus the three description compare sites. Nothing under `src/rebar/review_bot/` or the Gerrit client imports it. A search of `src/rebar/review_bot/` and `src/rebar/llm/` for `textwrap` or any reflow helper found no matches, so rebar does not appear to be injecting these breaks in code.

## Working hypothesis (NOT yet confirmed — this is the work)

A Gerrit "change description" is the git commit message. Gerrit renders commit messages as preformatted fixed-width text and preserves the author's newlines verbatim. Commit-message bodies are conventionally hard-wrapped at ~72 columns (git's own norm), so the breaks may be authored rather than injected, which would make this intended behavior rather than a defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Obtain a concrete example Gerrit change whose description renders wrongly, and record the change number.
- Determine whether the newlines are present in the commit message object itself (`git cat-file commit <sha>`) or introduced by a rebar/review-bot code path.
- Classify explicitly: defect vs intended-behavior vs authoring convention. If intended, close as not-a-bug with the citation and, if useful, document the commit-message wrapping convention instead.
- Only if it is a genuine injection defect: fix under RED->GREEN discipline.

## Notes

Filed at the reporter's request during the 4e21 session and deliberately scoped OUT of that session. Not yet reproduced or confirmed as a defect.
baseline.summary: Gerrit change descriptions show fixed-width line breaks (investigate; may be authoring convention)
