## Context / Problem

Operator ruling received (see comment): **"Unreadable config should result in an error."** This settles the question this ticket was filed to carry — the opt-in `verify.*` gates must NOT keep failing OPEN on an unreadable config, and must NOT fail closed into a blocked-`unavailable` verdict either. An unreadable/corrupt `rebar.toml` is a FAULT the operator must see and fix; today `gate_enabled` (`_commands/gates.py`) swallows the `ConfigError` into `GateState.UNREADABLE`, prints one stderr warning, and the gated operation silently proceeds as if the gate were off.

## Approach

Raise the error at the SOURCE, so every gate consumer gets the new posture without per-caller re-implementation:

1. `gates.gate_enabled` stops catching `ConfigError` into `GateState.UNREADABLE`. On an
   unreadable config it raises a `ConfigError` (chained `from` the parse fault) naming the
   gate label, the ticket, and the underlying parse error — the existing typed config-fault
   family, so callers and tests can catch it precisely.
2. `GateState.UNREADABLE` is removed (it becomes unreachable); `GateState` keeps
   `ENABLED`/`DISABLED` and its `__bool__` so the ~15 test modules that monkeypatch
   `gate_enabled` with a plain bool keep working. The `unreadable` skip verdict branch in
   `close_plan_review_gate_check` is removed (dead); the `gate_ran` stamp and predicate
   stay (still distinguish the `disabled` skip from a gate that ran).
3. The `extra` parameter of `gate_enabled` (a warning-suffix clause) is dropped with the
   warning it decorated; both call sites passing it are updated.
4. CLI surfacing: `_cli/__init__.py main()` gains an `except ConfigError` boundary
   (alongside `RemovedInputError`/`TrackerRootError`) printing `Error: <msg>` to stderr
   with exit 1, so the new error is a clean operator-facing failure, not a traceback —
   the same rendering `main()` already gives a `ConfigError` from `-c` overrides.
5. Docs updated to the new contract: `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (the "unreadable config
   fails this opt-in gate off with a warning" paragraph), `docs/config.md` bullet 6
   ("Loud, not silent"), `docs/llm-framework.md`'s matching sentence.

### Caller sweep (every `gate_enabled` consumer, per c504977aef's RCA)

- `gates.close_plan_review_gate_check` (plan-review close gate) — PROPAGATES. Called
  pre-lock by `transition_close`, so the error is raised BEFORE `txn.transition_core`
  takes the write lock; the b8841ae695 property (an unreadable config does no work under
  the lock) is preserved and stays tested. The in-lock recheck closure is only installed
  after a pre-lock check that RAN. Precision on the rare pre-lock→lock window (the config
  turns unreadable AFTER a passing pre-lock check): the locked recheck's `ConfigError` is
  re-typed by `transition_core`'s fail-closed boundary (`txn.py`: `except Exception →
  CommandError(f"Error: {exc}", returncode=1) from None`), so THAT path aborts loudly as
  a `CommandError` carrying the parse-fault text in its message — exit 1, close refused —
  but NOT as the typed, chained `ConfigError` and NOT via the CLI `ConfigError` boundary.
  That is deliberate: `transition_core`'s re-wrap is its existing fail-closed contract
  for the write path and is out of scope here; the typed, chained `ConfigError`
  guarantee (AC1/AC2) applies to the pre-lock and claim paths, which are the paths an
  unreadable-at-operation-start config actually takes.
- `gates._plan_review_gate_applies` → `plan_review_precheck` (claim + `transition open
  in_progress`) and `claim.py` stage-1 `--review` sensing — PROPAGATES: starting work on
  an unreadable config fails loudly.
- `close_precheck._completion_precheck` (completion close gate) — PROPAGATES: the close
  fails loudly before any billable verifier work.
- `gates.description_cap_warning` — DELIBERATE CATCH, kept: its `except Exception →
  None` guards an advisory-only notice emitted after a write has already committed
  (documented in its docstring and pinned by
  `test_description_cap_warning.py::test_an_unreadable_cap_never_disturbs_the_write`).
  The ruling scopes the error to gate resolution of gated operations; the completed
  write must not be disturbed, and the actual claim of that ticket still errors.

Read-only ops (`list`, `show`, `search`) do not resolve gates and are unaffected — the error is scoped to gate resolution, exactly as the ruling demands.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py` — the raise, `GateState` narrowing, docstrings.
- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — call-site signature + comment.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — comment describing the recheck-install
  condition (behavioural text references the retired unreadable skip).
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — the `ConfigError` boundary in `main()`.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/config.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md` — contract text.
- Tests: rewrite `tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_ran_predicate_2091.py` (unreadable arm),
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py`; new RED module
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_unreadable_config_errors_39f8.py`.

## Testing

RED before GREEN (the new module fails on current main, passes after):

- Happy/failure pair at the function: readable-on → `ENABLED`, readable-off →
  `DISABLED`; malformed `rebar.toml` → `ConfigError` raised, message names the gate
  label, the ticket id, and the parse fault.
- End-to-end failure paths: with a malformed `rebar.toml`, (a) `rebar.claim` fails
  loudly naming the config fault and the ticket stays `open`; (b) a close via
  `rebar.transition(in_progress→closed)` fails loudly BEFORE the write lock (the ticket
  stays `in_progress`, no status event is appended, and the in-lock recheck is never
  invoked — the b8841ae695 no-work-under-the-lock property, retargeted from "silently
  proceeds" to "errors first").
- Invariance guards: `disabled` skip verdict, `gate_ran` stamp semantics, and bool
  monkeypatch compatibility unchanged.
- Full gates: `make lint`, targeted pytest for the modules above, `make typecheck`,
  complexity ratchet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With a malformed `rebar.toml`, `gate_enabled` raises `ConfigError` (chained from
  the parse fault, message naming gate + ticket + fault) instead of returning a state —
  checked by `tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py`.
- [x] With a malformed `rebar.toml`, a claim fails loudly with that error (exit ≠ 0 on
  the CLI, typed raise in the library) leaving the ticket `open` — checked by
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_unreadable_config_errors_39f8.py`.
- [x] With a malformed `rebar.toml`, a close fails loudly with that error leaving the
  ticket `in_progress` — checked by the same new test module.
- [x] The close-path error is raised BEFORE the write lock; no config read or gate work
  happens under the lock on the unreadable path — checked by the rewritten
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py`.
- [x] A readable config's behaviour is byte-identical (`ENABLED`/`DISABLED` resolution,
  the `disabled` skip verdict, the `gate_ran` stamp, bool monkeypatch compatibility) —
  checked by the existing gate test suites staying green.
- [x] `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/config.md`, and `docs/llm-framework.md` state
  the new contract (unreadable config ⇒ error; never a silent skip, never a fake
  `disabled`) — checked by reading the three updated sections.
baseline.summary: Operator ruling: should the opt-in verify.* gates keep failing OPEN on an unreadable config?

baseline.description:
## Context

Discovered while widening the MCP model/schema drift gate for mirror F5 (`62eb-5e6f-512a-420d`). That gate's registry covered 11 of 32 public `*Out` models. Deriving the registry — every model whose `<snake_case>.schema.json` exists — brings 9 more models under the check, and four of them are ALREADY DRIFTED.

## The measured gap: 41 undeclared schema properties

- **CreateResultOut** (create_result.schema.json) — 1: `title`
- **GateResultOut** (gate_result.schema.json) — 5: `ac_items`, `criteria_count`, `file_impact`, `keyword_count`, `line_count`
- **NextBatchOut** (next_batch.schema.json) — 12: `available_pool`, `batch`, `batch_size`, `epic_title`, `skipped_blocked`, `skipped_blocked_story`, `skipped_design_awaiting`, `skipped_in_progress`, `skipped_manual_awaiting`, `skipped_needs_planning`, `skipped_overlap`, `tasks`
- **TicketStateOut** (ticket_state.schema.json) — 23: `attestations`, `author`, `bridge_alerts`, `bridge_project`, `close_class`, `close_reason`, `completion_expectation`, `created_at`, `creation_channel`, `creation_channel_inferred`, `detected_by`, `env_id`, `force_close_reason`, `last_reopened_at`, `preconditions_summary`, `repos`, `reverts`, `source_author`, `source_created_at`, `source_env`, `source_id`, `updated_at`, `verify_commands`

## Why this is separate from F5

F5 fixes the GATE — it makes the check enum-aware and derives its registry so nothing can be silently omitted again. Closing these 41 gaps is a different change with a different risk profile: `_mcp_models` supplies the MCP tools' published `outputSchema`, so declaring a field CHANGES THE WIRE CONTRACT clients read. That deserves its own review rather than riding along inside a gate refactor.

F5 therefore baselines these four models as declared exceptions naming THIS ticket, so the gate is green at rest while any NEW omission fails. Standard ratchet shape, the same one `check_complexity_baseline.py` and `check_mechanism_delta.py` use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: each of the four models declares the properties its canonical schema defines, or the
      schema is corrected where the property is genuinely not part of that payload. Verified by
      the drift gate reporting zero missing declarations for them with their baseline entries
      REMOVED.
- [x] AC2: the baseline exception entries added by F5 are deleted, not merely emptied, so the
      gate's exception map returns to naming only genuine permissive omissions. Verified by
      grepping the gate for this ticket id and finding none.
- [x] AC3: any property deliberately NOT declared carries a stated reason in the gate's
      permissive-omissions map. Verified by reading each remaining entry.
- [x] AC4 [non-codebase]: the wire-contract impact is stated — for each newly declared field,
      whether MCP clients could already observe it in practice. Verified by a comment on this
      ticket recording the assessment.

## Testing

- `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` — zero drift with the baseline removed.
- `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_model_schema_drift_heldout.py -q`.

## Completion evidence (2026-09-03) — Gerrit change 2556 MERGED

- **AC1** — 39 of the 41 properties are declared on `CreateResultOut`, `GateResultOut`, `NextBatchOut` and `TicketStateOut`; the remaining 2 are permissive omissions with stated reasons (AC3). `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check` reports "MCP model schema drift gate OK — no missing declarations" with the baseline removed. The property list was derived authoritatively by running `find_drift()` with `BASELINED_OMISSIONS` monkeypatched empty, and matched exactly.
- **AC2** — `BASELINED_OMISSIONS` is DELETED, not emptied: the dict, its comment block, and its merge line in `find_drift` are all gone. `grep -c "BASELINED_OMISSIONS\|3a02" src/rebar/schemas/check_mcp_models.py` returns **0**.
- **AC3** — two deliberate omissions, each with a reason in the permissive-omissions map. `CreateResultOut.title`: only the CLI's `create --output json` emits it (`_commands/composer.py:481`); every MCP create tool returns `rebar.create_ticket(return_alias=True)`, which drops title — declaring it would advertise a permanently-null title on a ticket that always has one. `NextBatchOut.tasks`: belongs to the CLI-only `next-batch --limit=0` reduced variant (`_engine_support/next_batch.py:559`); the library/MCP path emits `batch` and never `tasks`.
- **AC4** — wire-contract impact assessed and recorded in a comment on this ticket. **All 39 newly declared fields were ALREADY on the wire** as undeclared `extra="allow"` pass-throughs, verified against this store's real tickets plus a union over 200 closed ones, so the change DOCUMENTS AN EXISTING SHAPE rather than altering what clients receive. That is a materially lower risk profile than F5 assumed when it deferred them.

Hazard surfaced and handled during implementation: declaring an optional pydantic field makes it EMIT, and 15 of the properties have canonical types admitting no null, so a naive declaration made real payloads violate their own schema (8 contract tests caught it). A new `_OmitUnsetOut` base pops never-set fields at serialization, so the declaration appears in `outputSchema` while the emitted bytes are unchanged. Timestamps are typed `int | str | None` rather than bare `int`, because `js_safe_result` would otherwise coerce them to a lossy number on FastMCP re-validation (bug 6fe7).
baseline.summary: MCP output models under-declare 41 canonical schema properties across four models

baseline.description:
## What

The test repo-isolation guard `_no_repo_root_leaks` (`tests/conftest.py:157-181`) only diffs the **top-level** entries of `REPO_ROOT` (`set(os.listdir(_REPO_ROOT))` before vs after each test). It is therefore **blind to a test leaking state INTO a pre-existing top-level directory** — most importantly `.rebar/` (this checkout dogfoods rebar, so `.rebar/` always exists locally). A test that writes `.rebar/run_snapshots/<sha>` adds no *new* top-level entry, so the guard passes locally — while a fresh CI checkout (no `.rebar/`) sees the SAME write *create* `.rebar` and flags it. This is a false-green/false-red split between local and CI.

## Why

This is the exact gap that hid the `test_sweep_removes_readonly_snapshot_tree` leak (fixed in `fc792e4f`): the test snapshotted into `cwd = REPO_ROOT`'s `.rebar/`, which was invisible to the top-level guard locally but failed CI's clean checkout. The guard's job is to catch tests that escape their sandbox; right now it catches only the subset that create a *new top-level* entry, giving false confidence locally.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Ensure `REPO_ROOT/.rebar/` exists (it does in any checkout that has run rebar).
2. Add a test that writes a file under `REPO_ROOT/.rebar/` (e.g. `(_REPO_ROOT /
   ".rebar" / "leaked.txt").write_text("x")`) without using `tmp_path`.
3. Run it **locally**: the `_no_repo_root_leaks` guard does NOT fail it (the new file
   is inside the pre-existing `.rebar/`, so the top-level `os.listdir` diff is empty).
4. Run it on a **fresh checkout** (no `.rebar/`): the write creates `.rebar/` → the
   top-level diff flags `['.rebar']` → the test fails.

**Expected:** a test that writes anywhere under `REPO_ROOT` it didn't create is flagged **locally**, regardless of whether the containing dir pre-existed. **Actual:** leaks into a pre-existing top-level dir (`.rebar/`, etc.) pass locally and only surface (if at all) on a clean CI checkout.

## Proposed improvement

Extend the guard to detect new entries created **inside** the volatile pre-existing dirs, not just at the top level — while staying cheap and not flagging dirs with legitimate per-test churn:

- Snapshot a deeper path set for the known cache/state dirs that tests must NOT touch
  in `REPO_ROOT` — at minimum `.rebar/` (one level: `{f".rebar/{e}" for e in
  os.listdir(REPO_ROOT/'.rebar')}`), diffed before/after alongside the top-level set.
  Optionally generalize to a bounded recursive walk that **excludes** the dirs with
  legitimate churn (`.git/`, `.tickets-tracker/`, `.venv/`, caches) so it stays fast.
- Keep the existing best-effort cleanup of leaked paths, extended to the deeper set.
- (Belt-and-suspenders, optional) add a CI/local parity note or a `make` target that
  runs a representative slice in a throwaway checkout, so the local↔CI environment gap
  (pre-existing `.rebar`, installed extras, filesystem) is exercised before push.

The underlying test bug is already fixed; this ticket hardens the *guard* so the next such leak fails locally instead of only in CI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_no_repo_root_leaks` flags a test that creates a new entry under a pre-existing
  `REPO_ROOT/.rebar/` (verified by a self-test that deliberately leaks into `.rebar/`
  and asserts the guard fails it) — even when `.rebar/` pre-exists.
- [ ] The guard still passes the full existing suite (no false positives from dirs with
  legitimate per-test churn — `.git/`, `.tickets-tracker/`, etc. remain excluded).
- [ ] The check stays inexpensive (no full-repo recursive walk of large dirs; scoped to
  the known state dirs or a bounded/excluded walk).
- [ ] Leaked deeper paths are cleaned up (best-effort) as the top-level ones already are.
</content>
baseline.summary: test isolation guard _no_repo_root_leaks misses leaks into pre-existing top-level dirs (e.g. .rebar/)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

ADR 0098 defines one immutable non-secret `OperationSnapshot` per operation. Today CLI and shared command-write entry points still call `emit_shadow_snapshot()`, while store/config helpers can resolve ambient state independently. The reconciler runtime already demonstrates snapshot-derived bindings; reuse that pattern.

This story cuts ordinary CLI, MCP/Python command, and store-opening operations over. LLM-specific resolution is the dependent follow-up.

## Approach

- Census the command/store consumers and identify the public composition boundaries for CLI, MCP, and Python.
- Compose exactly once after input parsing and before lock/network/write, then pass focused immutable projections/context through shared command/store seams.
- Preserve explicit-input > environment > project > user > schema precedence and independent repository-root selection from ADR 0098.
- Add consumer-level metamorphic and effect-spy tests.
- Remove migrated shadow calls and ambient reloads; extend the existing ownership checker with red-proven detections rather than a second registry.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_operation_config.py` and `src/rebar/config.py` — existing composer/projections and approved compatibility boundary.
- `src/rebar/_cli/`, `src/rebar/_commands/`, `src/rebar/_store/`, and MCP command entry modules — compose once and thread focused context.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/` and focused config/store/CLI/MCP tests.
- `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and its exact exception registry.

## Testing

Happy path: equivalent CLI, MCP, and Python operations resolve one identical snapshot and produce existing effects. Metamorphic edge: mutate environment, selected files, and CWD after capture; the active operation remains unchanged and the next operation changes. Failure edge: malformed selected configuration causes zero lock, subprocess, network, or store effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Representative CLI, MCP, and Python ticket/store reads and writes each compose one snapshot/context, proven by call-count tests through production entry points. Proven by `test_operation_snapshot_authoritative_binding.py`'s compose-once/reentrancy tests (CLI `_main_dispatch`, command-write `append_event`, and the new `bind_operation_snapshot_for_tools` MCP proxy all bind exactly one snapshot per outer call and reuse it for nested seams).
- [x] Given environment/config/CWD mutation after composition, the active operation's selected tracker directory, branch, remote, and observable effects remain unchanged; a new operation observes the change. Push mode is a documented, tested exception: it stays LIVE per-call because `_io/import_ndjson.py` toggles `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH` mid-bulk-import and `test_c3b_push_defer_coupling_heldout.py` depends on that live read continuing to work — freezing push mode would silently break that existing, in-scope-adjacent coupling. The new tests assert this carve-out explicitly (push mode observes the mutation even inside a bound operation) so the exception is enforced, not merely asserted in prose.
- [x] Explicit operation input remains authoritative and malformed selected config fails before lock, subprocess, network, or store write; the binding itself fails OPEN (never raises) so an operation that doesn't need config keeps working. Proven by the AC3 override/bypass tests (`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` env override and an explicit different-repo root both bypass the binding) and the fail-open litmus test (a real `ConfigError`-raising project config still lets `bridge setup --reset` succeed with rc=0, and the composition failure is logged with a redacted exception type name only).
- [x] Store helpers receive focused projections/context and do not call `load_config`, environment, or CWD beneath the approved boundary. `tracker_dir`/`tickets_branch`/`tickets_remote` in `config.py` now consult the bound snapshot via `_bound_snapshot_for_root` before falling back to `load_config`; `check_config_ownership.py` continues to run clean with the pre-existing exception registry untouched (zero new entries).
- [x] Migrated `emit_shadow_snapshot` calls and compatibility resolution branches are deleted, with no stored ticket/event/bridge format change. All 33 `_shadow("mcp.read.xxx")` and 23 `_shadow("mcp.write.xxx")` call sites (plus the `_shadow` import) were deleted from `_mcp_reads.py`/`_mcp_writes.py`; the CLI's and command-write seam's shadow calls were replaced with the authoritative binding. No event/ticket/bridge schema was touched. `_mcp_llm.py`, `_lib_ops.py`, and the reconciler `__main__.py` deliberately keep their shadow calls (out of scope — LLM-specific resolution is ticket ec44's follow-up), confirmed via `test_single_definition_helpers.py`'s updated assertions.
- [x] The structural ownership checker catches a synthetic below-boundary ambient read and has zero new legacy exceptions. `check_config_ownership.py` and its exception registry were not modified by this change (confirmed via `git diff` on the commit); the pre-existing `test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` continues to prove the checker's detection, and `check_config_ownership.py` runs clean against the new code with no new exceptions added.
- [x] Existing config, tracker layout, concurrency, CLI/MCP/library parity, lint, typecheck, and default suites pass. `make lint` and `make typecheck` are fully green. `make test` is green except 8 pre-existing baseline failures (`test_atomic_completion_close.py` x5, `test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated`, `test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` x2) confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this change via `git stash` comparison (identical failures with and without this ticket's implementation).
baseline.summary: Make OperationSnapshot authoritative for CLI, command, and store operations

baseline.description:
## Why

The `rebar.*` library facade returns plain `dict`/`list` shapes with no named,
documented return contract, so published-library consumers cannot tell which keys
are guaranteed or get type-checker support. The review flagged this as the main
library-API gap. rebar's public contract is *already* the canonical JSON Schemas
in `src/rebar/schemas/` (loaded via `rebar.schemas.load`/`names`/`OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`),
and it already has a derived-artifact + CI drift-gate pattern (the prompt-index
gate: regenerate-in-place then `git diff --exit-code`) to keep derived artifacts
in sync. Pydantic is deliberately NOT a core dependency (core is
`pyyaml`/`jsonschema`/`referencing`), so runtime models are off the table.

## What

Give the schema-backed subset of the `rebar.*` facade a typed return contract
**additively and statically**, via schema-derived `TypedDict`s generated from the
canonical JSON Schemas. **Zero runtime change** — returns stay plain dicts;
existing callers are untouched.

### Design decisions (resolving plan-review findings)

- **`additionalProperties: true` (BLOCKING G6).** Every public output schema is
  *open* ("unknown properties allowed so the event-sourced shape can evolve").
  TypedDict cannot express arbitrary extra keys, so we generate **closed
  TypedDicts that name the documented/guaranteed contract**: schema-`required`
  keys are normal fields; non-required keys are wrapped in `typing.NotRequired[…]`
  (PEP 655, available in stdlib `typing` on our `requires-python = ">=3.11"`),
  with `total=True`. This preserves the "required fields are present" guarantee
  (unlike the blanket `total=False` used by the hand-authored
  `_snapshot_schema.py` precedent) while marking optional keys. The runtime dicts
  remain open; that openness is documented in the generated module docstring and
  each class docstring — reading undocumented extra keys is outside the typed
  contract by design.

- **Generator: a small custom in-repo generator, not an off-the-shelf tool
  (T1/T2/T3/E2).** We write `src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py` (a `python -m
  rebar.schemas.gen_types` entry-point, mirroring `regenerate_prompt_index`)
  rather than adopting `datamodel-code-generator`, because (a) rebar avoids adding
  dependencies, and (b) our schemas use cross-file `$ref` into
  `common.schema.json#/$defs/*`, `["string","null"]` unions, and draft-2020-12 —
  constructs off-the-shelf generators support only partially. A focused generator
  handling exactly the constructs present (object `properties`/`required`,
  `["T","null"]`→`T | None`, arrays, `$ref` to `common.schema.json#/$defs/*`
  resolved to shared generated TypedDicts, enum `$ref`→`Literal[…]`) is simpler
  and dependency-free. It resolves the `from` reserved-word key (transition_result)
  via the functional `TypedDict("TransitionResult", {…})` form. Output is written
  deterministically (stable key order + trailing newline) so the diff-gate is
  stable.

- **Enum vocabulary only from formal `enum`/enum-`$ref` (T6/T8).** Where a value
  vocabulary lives only in a schema `description` string (e.g. `workflow_run`
  `status`), the generator emits `str`, not `Literal` — Literal comes only from a
  formal `enum` constraint or a `$ref` to an enum def (`ticket_status`,
  `ticket_type`, `priority`). This limitation is documented; we do not over-promise
  Literal unions.

- **Scope = the schema-backed facade subset, enumerated (advisory 1/14).** We
  generate + annotate for the public functions whose return shape has a canonical
  entry in `rebar.schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`: `transition`/`reopen`
  (`transition_result`), `claim` (`claim_result`), `create_ticket` dict form
  (`create_result`), `clarity_check` (`clarity_result`), `check_ac`/`quality_check`
  (`gate_result`), `validate` (`validate_report`), `get_file_impact`
  (`file_impact`), `get_verify_commands` (`verify_commands`), `grounding_info`,
  `sign_manifest` (`sign_result`), `verify_signature` (`verify_signature_result`),
  `show_ticket`/`list_tickets`/`search`/`ready`/`recent_session_logs`
  (`ticket_state`), `get_workflow_status`/`get_workflow_result` (`workflow_run`),
  `deps` (`deps_graph`), `next_batch` (`next_batch`), `summary` (`summary`),
  `list_epics` (`list_epics`), `bridge_fsck` (`bridge_fsck`). **Explicitly OUT of
  the generated set** (no canonical output schema — annotated `dict[str, Any]`,
  unchanged, and listed as out-of-scope): `append_session_log`,
  `start_session_log`, `attach_commits`, `export_tickets`, `import_tickets`,
  `reconcile`, and `run_workflow` (its `_result_dict` shape differs from the
  `workflow_run` schema). `fsck` returns captured `str` (unchanged).

- **`create_ticket` polymorphism (advisory 2).** `create_ticket` returns `str`
  (bare id) by default and a dict when `return_alias=True`. We add `@overload`s
  keyed on the `return_alias` literal (`Literal[False] -> str`,
  `Literal[True] -> CreateResult`) so existing `tid = rebar.create_ticket(...)`
  callers keep `str` and no spurious mypy error is introduced.

- **Type-checker gate = mypy only (advisory 9).** The gated checker is `make
  typecheck` (mypy over `src/rebar`); pyright is not a CI gate here, so AC claims
  mypy only (the generated TypedDicts are pyright-compatible, but only mypy is
  enforced).

- **Exceptions: promote exactly `RebarError` + `ConcurrencyError` (advisory
  13/15).** These two (already in `rebar.__all__`, defined in `rebar/_errors.py`)
  are the stable public exception surface; `SigningError` stays internal (wrapped
  into `RebarError`). No others promoted. Documented in `docs/reuse-surface.md`
  (or the README library section) with their `.returncode`/`.stderr` contract.

- **ADR + docs (advisory 8/16).** Add a short ADR under `docs/adr/` capturing the
  static-only, schema-derived, custom-generator, no-Pydantic decision and its
  trade-offs; add a README/usage note pointing consumers at `from rebar.types
  import …` and the exception surface.

## Scope

Schema-derived TypedDicts (`src/rebar/types.py`, generated) + the generator
(`src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py`) + a CI drift-gate (in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`, mirroring the prompt-index gate) + facade return
annotations in `src/rebar/__init__.py` + exception docs + an ADR. Static-typing
only: NO Pydantic/dataclass runtime models, NO new core runtime dependency, NO
change to any return value. Pairs with the API-stability matrix story (830d, the
Python-facade row).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/types.py` holds `TypedDict`s generated from the canonical JSON

## Why

The task-decomposition SOTA report (epic 6982, §5 of docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md;
prior art T1: CodePlan's layer-cake antipattern, claude-task-master's DAG ordering, Kiro's
"waves") identifies two recurring **decomposition-SHAPE smells** in CONTAINER plans (a parent
split into children) that the existing container criteria G3 (child-coverage) and G4
(child-consistency) do NOT target:

- **layer-cake split** — children partitioned by ARCHITECTURAL LAYER (a "DB/schema" child, a
  "service/API" child, a "frontend/UI" child) instead of vertical, independently-shippable
  slices. Each child is un-demoable alone and the integration risk is deferred to the end.
  G3 (does the union cover the parent's ACs?) and G4 (7 cross-child interaction modes) both pass
  a layer-cake — coverage is complete and the layers are individually consistent; the DEFECT is
  the partition axis itself.
- **consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge** — a child NAMES/CONSUMES an artifact a SIBLING
  produces (its output file, schema, event, symbol), yet there is NO ordering dependency
  (depends_on/blocks) between them, so a parallel-agent scheduler can start the consumer before
  the producer exists. G4's "dependency gap"/"ordering violation" modes are broad and
  benign-filtered; this is the specific, high-signal producer→consumer-without-edge shape.

Both are SHAPE properties of the (parent, children) decomposition — not coverage, not code
grounding. This story ships one focused advisory container criterion for exactly that surface.

## What

Add one new **advisory, AGENT-tier, CONTAINER** plan-review criterion, id `decomp-shape`
(facet `container`, like G3/G4 — NOT codebase-grounding), that audits the (parent, children,
sibling-roster) decomposition for the two smells above. It runs on the EXISTING container
fan-out — no new pass, no new engine construct:

- **Mechanism seam (cited).** Container criteria are pulled out of the normal agent path and run
  via the dedicated per-child loop: `CONTAINER_CRITERIA = ("G3", "G4")` at
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:43` (partitioned at pass1.py:373-374), dispatched by
  `passes.pass1_container(...)` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:357` — which builds the
  combined rubric from the `criteria` list (`rubric = "\n\n".join(_criterion_block(c) ...)`,
  passes.py:387), validates model self-reported attribution against `valid_ids`
  (passes.py:381, 428), and hands the finder parent + whole children + the complete sibling
  roster. Adding `decomp-shape` to `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` fans it out through that same seam with
  per-criterion + per-child attribution; nothing else changes.
- **Registration seam.** A packaged built-in LLM criterion must be added to
  `registry.CANONICAL_LLM` and `registry.AGENT_TIER` (like G3/G4; NOT `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` — its
  facet is `container`, not codebase-grounding), be given a routing entry in
  `criteria_routing.json` (`exec:AGENT`, `facet:container`, `applies_at.scope:["container"]`,
  `default_posture:"advisory"`, `block_threshold:0.95`), a rubric prompt at
  `reviewers/plan_review_decomp_shape.md` (front-matter `title`→guide name, body→scenario), and a
  regenerated `## decomp-shape` guide section — else `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` flags
  ORPHAN and CI fails (the bit that hit R2/b080), and `validate_criteria_guide()` flags the
  missing section.
- **Two criterion-local checklist sub-answers** (gated-then-detected): `has_container_decomposition`
  (GATE — parent has >=2 children forming a decomposition; `no` -> not-applicable -> PASS) and
  `decomposition_shape_sound` (`no` when a layer-cake partition OR a
  consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge is present — the finding).
- **Bounded sanity harness.** Container criteria are NOT runnable over the inline-text eval path
  today (`eval_solver._run_criterion_case` raises for `cid in CONTAINER_CRITERIA`,
  eval_solver.py:105). This story extends that arm to run a container criterion via
  `pass1_container` when the fixture carries a `children:` list — a small, contained enhancement
  that makes `decomp-shape` (and G3/G4) calibratable through `rebar criteria eval`, keeping the
  sanity run bounded to one live container call per fixture.

It ships **advisory posture (never blocks)** — its permanent posture per this epic's operator
direction. Promotion to blocking is a **future dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change**,
DOUBLE-gated: (1) the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder (`criterion_effectiveness.py`)
must show it earns its blocks (high `detection_proxy`, low `blocking_fp_proxy`, sufficient
sample) AND (2) E6's judge order-stability must improve above floor — E6's order-shuffle
reliability FAILED (fleiss_kappa=0.55 < 0.6 floor, raw=0.7 < 0.8; e6_summary.json), which is a
declared R3 PREREQUISITE FAILURE (e6_judge_reliability.py:672): an order-sensitive judge makes a
BLOCKING container verdict untrustworthy, so blocking-promotion is deferred until order-stability
clears floor. Advisory shipping is unaffected — a non-blocking coaching nudge is safe under
judge instability.

## Scope

IN: the criterion + its routing/registry/rubric/guide, the eval_solver container-arm extension,
the bounded sanity fixtures + committed result, deterministic unit tests, and the promotion-gate
documentation note. OUT: any blocking promotion (future dogfood-gated), the E2/E3 mutant corpus
(permanently rejected on cost; sanity uses hand-authored fixtures), dogfood-accumulation waits.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `.../criteria_routing.json`, `.../pass1.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_decomp_shape.md`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py`,
`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`,
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml`,
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/decomp_shape_sanity.json`,
`tests/unit/test_decomp_shape_criterion.py`, `tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py`,
`docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `decomp-shape` is REGISTERED as an advisory, AGENT-tier CONTAINER criterion and is
  non-orphan. Proof: `python -c "import json; from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry as r;
  from rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1 import CONTAINER_CRITERIA; assert 'decomp-shape' in
  r.CANONICAL_LLM and 'decomp-shape' in r.AGENT_TIER and 'decomp-shape' not in r.CODEBASE_GROUNDED;
  assert r.validate_packaged_routing()==[]; assert 'decomp-shape' in CONTAINER_CRITERIA;
  e=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json'))['decomp-shape']; assert
  e['exec']=='AGENT' and e['facet']=='container' and e['default_posture']=='advisory';
  print('OK')"` prints OK, and `rebar explain decomp-shape` exits 0 with a `## decomp-shape`
  section (`validate_criteria_guide()==[]`).
- [ ] Deterministic (no-LLM) unit tests for the non-LLM logic pass — registration invariants,
  routing/finding shape (advisory, container facet, scope), prompt-contract front-matter +
  sub-answer keys, the eval_solver container-arm (a fake runner threads through `pass1_container`),
  the eval-fixture shape, and zero-wiring auto-inclusion into the effectiveness recorder. Proof:
  `pytest tests/unit/test_decomp_shape_criterion.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] Bounded sanity check committed: hand-authored fixtures — one known layer-cake container
  plan + one known consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge plan (must-fire), plus vertical-slice
  and well-ordered containers (must-not-fire) — the criterion FIRES on both positives and is
  CLEAN on the negatives. Proof: `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/decomp_shape_sanity.json`
  preserves the raw per-case `rebar criteria eval decomp-shape --output json` output and records
  recall over the positives (target 1.0) and false-accept over the negatives; any negative fire
  is ADVISORY (never blocks), recorded as a promotion-gate FP signal. <=8 live single-criterion
  container runs total; NO E2/E3 corpus, NO batch eval.
- [ ] The criterion auto-flows into the standing recorder. Proof: a unit assertion feeds one
  synthetic firing row through `criterion_effectiveness.firings_from_review` /
  `compute_effectiveness` and asserts `decomp-shape` is auto-included with ZERO per-criterion
  wiring (the id appears in the `--report` metrics map).
- [ ] The advisory->blocking promotion gate is documented, citing d8a5's protocol in
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder + advisory->blocking
  promotion gate", and NOTING that E6's order-sensitivity (fleiss_kappa=0.55 < floor) defers
  blocking-promotion until order-stability clears floor (a second gate on top of dogfood
  effectiveness). Proof: the section names `decomp-shape` and the E6 order-stability prerequisite.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The change is landed on main: `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` and
  submitted (Gerrit), attested in-session.
baseline.summary: R3: decomposition-shape container criterion (advisory-only; blocking-promotion dogfood+E6-gated)

## Summary
The four LLM sidecar retention prunes bypass rebar's canonical locked event-write path. Each `prune()` runs raw `git rm` + a whole-index `git commit` (no pathspec) via `subprocess.run`, WITHOUT acquiring `write_lock`, WITHOUT rebase-guard, and WITHOUT the shared index-lock retry/self-heal. This races normal ticket writes in the shared tracker worktree.

Affected sites (near-identical copy-paste):
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` `prune`
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` `prune`
- `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` `prune`
- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py` `prune`

Contrast the canonical writer `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:stage_and_commit`, which holds `write_lock`, checks rebase state, does a path-limited add, retries index-lock failures, and cleans staged residue. event_append even warns (line ~263) that a whole-index commit "could sweep unrelated staged residue in under THIS write's message" — the prunes reintroduce exactly that, outside the lock.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run an LLM gate (plan-review / completion-verify / code-review) whose sidecar
   emit triggers `prune()` on a ticket with > RETAIN_PER_TICKET sidecar events.
2. Concurrently run a normal ticket write (claim/transition/comment) on the same
   tracker so its `git add` (holding write_lock) overlaps the prune's lock-free
   `git commit`.

Expected: retention prune is serialized with every other store write; it commits only its own deletions and never observes/writes another writer's staged state.

Actual: the prune's whole-index `git commit` can commit a concurrent writer's staged event under a `prune:` message, causing the original writer's commit to report a false failure (its `_unstage`+`_silent_unlink` then removes an already-committed event from the worktree, diverging worktree from HEAD). Under index.lock contention the prune instead fails outright (best-effort swallowed), making retention unreliable in the multi-agent workload.

## Fix (Option B — narrow lock-respecting delete helper)
Add ONE `delete_events(tracker, relpaths, commit_msg)` primitive in `event_append` that acquires `write_lock`, checks the rebase guard, `git rm`s the given paths, commits PATHSPEC-SCOPED (`git commit -- <paths>`, not whole-index), and routes git through the shared index-lock retry. Route all four prunes through it. Keep the helper NARROW (delete-events-under-lock, not a general locked-git facade) and preserve each caller's best-effort try/except so a failed prune never fails the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single `delete_events`-style helper exists in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`
      that acquires `write_lock`, checks the rebase guard, and routes git through the
      shared index-lock retry.
- [ ] The helper's `git commit` is pathspec-scoped to the deleted paths (cannot
      sweep unrelated staged residue), and it cleans up on failure.
- [ ] All four sidecar `prune()`s (`plan_review/sidecar.py`, `code_review/sidecar.py`,
      `completion_sidecar.py`, `overlap/digest_sidecar.py`) call the helper instead of
      raw `subprocess.run(["git", ... "rm"/"commit"])`.
- [ ] Each caller retains its best-effort exception-swallowing posture (a failed
      prune never fails the gate).
- [ ] A unit/interface test covers the helper: it deletes only the named events,
      commits under the lock, and does not sweep an unrelated staged file in the index.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass; the change lands via Gerrit
      with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Sidecar retention prunes bypass the canonical locked write path (unlocked git rm+commit races store writes)

## Context / Problem

Their consumers are internal source or test/monkeypatch paths; no public wire or persisted-data contract requires them. The governing ADR is delivered by earthen-wheat-chick.

## Approach

## Scope

- every source/test/patch/dynamic consumer

## Testing

Run targeted CLI/help, security-detector, graph/reducer, and grounding suites plus semantic and raw reference censuses.

## Acceptance Criteria

baseline.description:
## Context

`rebar-root-disk-pressure` went ALARM 2026-08-17 21:51 PDT (OK 22:12) on `rebar-gerrit` (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, 30-GiB gp3 root). Root usage climbed 71% @20:55 → 90% @21:55/22:00, then dropped to 48% @22:05; `reviewbot_healthy` dipped to 0 at 22:05.

## Phase 1: COMPLETE — root cause proven

Full evidence in the "Phase 1 EXIT" comment (experiments, CloudWatch series, citations). Summary:

- **REJECTED — "autodeploy prunes Docker caches too late."** Build artifacts cannot appear
  without a build; 10 of 12 build-free intervals still grew (median +1.12, max +3.93 GiB/h).
  The 12.6-GiB reclaim exceeds the whole 5 GB buildkit ceiling. `prune_docker_caches` cannot
  reclaim a **running** container's writable layer at all.
- **CONFIRMED (RC-B, this ticket) — the janitor's reclaim triggers are unreachable here.**
  `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:53` `DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES = 2 GiB` is an **absolute**,
  disk-size-blind floor: on a 30-GiB root it is crossed only at **93.3% used**, above the 85%
  alarm (`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:226`) and above the 90% peak reached.
  Driving the real `run_gc()` with injected free space gives **0 evictions at 85% and at 90%
  used**; first eviction only past 93.3%. The 7-day cold-trim (`janitor.py:55`) exceeds the
  container's lifetime (23 recreations in 4 days). The janitor *is* started
  (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136`) and correctly evicted nothing.
- **CONFIRMED (RC-A, split to `smart-disloyal-naga`) — the growth source.** Every review
  materializes a full ~620 MiB / 69,984-file copy of the ticket tree
  (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` → `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`), keyed on a tip
  that advanced 1,374 times in the 10-hour window with consecutive commits differing by 1 file.

The store sits on the 30-GiB root because `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` is unset everywhere, so `store_root()` (`repo_snapshot.py:113`) falls through to `tempfile.gettempdir()` = the container writable layer. The 48% floor and the 22:05 health dip are one event: the deploy recreating the container and destroying that layer.

## Scope of THIS ticket

RC-B only — make reclaim engage **before** the alarm floor. RC-A is `smart-disloyal-naga`; the missing byte-total backstop and `add_bytes` accounting are `itchy-arbored-peccary`.

## Plan

Add a **volume-relative** headroom term to the janitor's free-space trigger so the watermark cannot sit above the alarm floor on a small volume, plus hysteresis so a pass reclaims past the trigger instead of re-firing every 300 s. Both new values are **integers** so they survive the existing int-only config seam (`_snapshot_int` coerces with `int()`, and `JanitorConfig`'s fields and `_default_tunables()` are `dict[str, int]`) — a float fraction would truncate to 0 and silently disable the fix.

1. `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` — add `DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT = 0` and
   `free_watermark_pct: int` (whole percent of the volume; `0` = relative term off) to
   `JanitorConfig` + `_default_tunables()`. Add a module-level
   `RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT = 5` constant — a fixed internal margin, not an operator knob,
   matching how `DEFAULT_GRACE_SECONDS` / `DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` are handled. In
   `_gc_pass`, take `total = shutil.disk_usage(root).total` and compute:
   - `trigger = max(free_watermark_bytes, total * free_watermark_pct // 100)`
   - `target  = max(free_watermark_bytes, total * (free_watermark_pct + RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT) // 100)`

   Evict when `free < trigger`, and once triggered keep evicting until `free >= target`. The
   grace window and `_is_entry`'s `tickets-` recognition are untouched.

   Worked example, 30-GiB root, `free_watermark_pct = 20`: `trigger` = 6.0 GiB free (80% used),
   `target` = 7.5 GiB free (75% used). Both sit below the 85% alarm floor (4.5 GiB free), which
   is what AC4 requires. With `free_watermark_pct = 0` the arithmetic collapses to
   `max(2 GiB, 0)` = today's behaviour exactly.

2. `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — resolve `free_watermark_pct` through the existing
   `resolve_janitor_tunables` int path (`REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT` > `[snapshot]` table >
   default `0`). No new float helper is needed.
3. `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — set `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT: "20"` on the
   `review-bot` service, the pattern already used for `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` and
   `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`. 20 is `autodeploy.sh:110`'s `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80` expressed as headroom,
   chosen there as below the 85% alarm for hysteresis.
4. `docs/config.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`, `docs/env-vars.md` — document the one new
   knob and the fixed margin.
5. `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py` — the RED oracle.

### Design decision for review: what should `free_watermark_pct` default to?

- **Option A (this plan) — default `0` (off), set to `20` for the review-bot host in compose.**
  No behaviour change for any existing rebar user; fixes this host. Cost: the defect stays
  latent for other deployments on small volumes.
- **Option B — default `20`.** Removes the defect for every deployment. Cost: on a large volume
  that is >80% full for unrelated reasons, `_gc_pass` would evict the whole store every pass
  without reaching the target. Bounding how much such a pass evicts needs the store's real
  size — exactly the accounting `itchy-arbored-peccary` restores, so Option B should follow it.

## Testing

Run from the worktree venv (`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" ...`).

- **RED oracle** — `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py -q`. New cases drive the real
  `janitor.run_gc()` with `free_bytes` injected for a 30-GiB volume (`total` stubbed via
  `shutil.disk_usage`): at 85% used (4.50 GiB free) and at 90% used (3.00 GiB free) the pass
  MUST evict a non-grace entry. Against current code both evict 0 — the observed RED. A
  hysteresis case asserts the pass continues to the 7.5-GiB-free target rather than stopping
  at the 6.0-GiB trigger; a grace case asserts an entry touched inside `grace_seconds` is still
  skipped. A `free_watermark_pct=0` case asserts today's behaviour is unchanged.
- **Exact-defect mutation** — reset the compose/config `free_watermark_pct` to 0 (restoring
  the absolute-only watermark) and re-run the module: the new cases MUST return to RED.
- **Config seam** — `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py -k tunable -q`, covering
  `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT=20` surviving int resolution (not truncating to 0).
- **Docs pin** — `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_docs.py -q`.
- **No regression** — `pytest tests/unit -q`; `make lint`; `make typecheck`; `make config-check`.
- **Post-deploy (operator, read-only)** — `rebar/host:root_disk_used_percent` shows reclaim
  events with peaks under 85%, where the pre-fix series peaked at 90% (2026-08-17) and 87%
  (2026-08-18).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A faithful local reproduction identifies the dominant disk consumer and the component
      responsible for the 90%→48% reclaim.
- [x] A discriminating runtime experiment proves the root cause and rules out the surviving
      Docker-vs-snapshot alternative.
- [x] A test is observed RED on the proven mechanism, GREEN after repair, then RED again under
      the exact-defect mutation — proved by `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py -q`.
- [x] The repaired path reclaims before a 30-GiB root crosses the 85% alarm floor — proved by
      the 4.50-GiB-free case evicting.
- [x] The repaired path reclaims with hysteresis — proved by the hysteresis case asserting
      reclaim continues to the 7.5-GiB-free target, not stopping at the 6.0-GiB trigger.
- [x] Live/grace snapshot entries are preserved — proved by the grace-window case.
- [x] Existing fail-safe deploy/review semantics remain intact — proved by `pytest tests/unit -q`
      green (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` is absent from this ticket's file impact).
- [x] Documentation is updated — proved by `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_docs.py -q` green.
baseline.summary: [root-disk-pressure] Root disk reaches 90% and review-bot drops unhealthy after automated-reclaim mitigation

## Observation
After bug 84c7 removed the four ghost rows, **all 9 remaining `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` rows declare an empty prefix**. `_rebar_env: (0, "REBAR_")` was the only row that ever used the second tuple element, and its helper was drained out of the tree by the RP-04 cutover (`d361eb28e4`).

The prefix is still applied at `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` `_scan_call` (`reads.setdefault(prefix + lit, ...)`) and at `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` `_helper_access` (`return self._resolved_env(node, prefix + lit)`).

## Why it matters
The feature has **zero production users and zero live end-to-end coverage**, and its only historical coverage passed for the wrong reason (see the 84c7 comment correction). An unused-but-wired feature in two CI gate scripts is a maintenance hazard: it cannot rot visibly, only silently.

## Decision (operator ruling, recorded in comments)
**Remove the prefix field from both consumers**, simplifying both tables to a bare int (`helper name -> 0-indexed position of the env-name argument`). Rationale: no live row uses a prefix, the 84c7-era held-out assertion is vacuous with every live prefix empty, and repo policy prefers deleting unused code over testing an unused feature. A future prefixed helper can re-add the field together with real coverage.

Scope:
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`: `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` becomes `dict[str, int]`; `_scan_call`
  stops applying a prefix and `_call_key_expr` reads the bare int instead of subscripting
  `[0]` on the row (the third live consumer of the tuple shape).
- `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`: `_helper_access` stops applying a prefix.
- Tests touching the tuple shape updated:
  `test_known_env_helper_call_resolves_and_fires` in
  `tests/scripts/test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` is rewritten fully off the tuple
  (the line-99 `(pos, prefix)` destructuring becomes a bare-int read, the line-104
  `prefix + "SOME_KNOB"` assertion becomes a plain `"SOME_KNOB"` assertion, and the
  line-96 comment stops describing a prefix); the ghost-row literal `(0, "")` in
  `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py` becomes `0`; the `registered[name][0]`
  subscripts (lines 106/108) in `tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py` become
  bare-int reads.
- `docs/env-vars.md` regenerates byte-identical (no live row used a prefix).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The prefix field is removed from `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` in both consumers and the
      `prefix + lit` application code is gone from `_scan_call` and `_helper_access`.

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — **793 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (7 lines of headroom).

Seven lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.

- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria

`rebar review-plan` reports `signature` present (the JSON `signature` field is non-null, and batch tooling reads `signed=True`) even when the **verdict is BLOCK**. The documented contract is that it "signs a plan-review attestation on a **non-blocking PASS**" — so a BLOCK verdict should NOT carry a passing signed attestation. Either the signing-on-BLOCK is a bug, or the `signature` field means something other than "passing attestation"; either way it is misleading, because the signature is meant to be the trustworthy proof-of-PASS that downstream gates (the claim gate) and CI rely on. A consumer that checks "is there a signature?" to decide claimability would be misled by a signed BLOCK.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Author a ticket whose plan trips a blocking criterion (or use any ticket the four-pass gate
   BLOCKs).
2. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json` (default source = attested, signing on).
3. Inspect the result JSON: `verdict` and `signature`.

## Expected
- On `verdict == BLOCK`, no passing attestation is signed — `signature` is null/absent (or the
  field is unambiguously labeled as a non-passing attestation), so "has signature" reliably
  means "passed".

## Actual
- Observed repeatedly this session: tickets with `verdict=BLOCK` returned `signature` populated
  (`signed=True`). Concretely, Round-2/3/4 runs on the S4/S6/S7 d251 children showed e.g.
  `s6: BLOCK block=6 ... signed=True` and `s4: BLOCK block=2 ... signed=True` — a signature on a
  BLOCK.

## Notes
- Inferred from the JSON `signature` field, not the signing internals — possible the field is
  populated-but-not-a-passing-attestation; that distinction is exactly what's unclear and should
  be made explicit. Surfaced while dogfooding the plan-review gate on epic d251 (alto-fruit-punch).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar review-plan <id>` on a BLOCK verdict does NOT emit a passing signed attestation
      (either `signature` is null/absent on BLOCK, or the field/type is explicitly distinct from
      a passing attestation and documented as such).
- [x] `verify_signature` / the claim gate cannot be satisfied by an attestation produced on a
      BLOCK verdict (a BLOCKed plan is never claimable on the strength of its signature).
- [x] The behavior is documented (docs/plan-review-gate.md): exactly when a signature is emitted
      and what its presence guarantees.
- [x] A regression test asserts: BLOCK verdict -> no passing signature; PASS verdict -> signature present.

## 2026-08-08 resolution and duplicate consolidation

Duplicate closed report: `c494-eb77-60da-47dd`; the landing commit cites this ticket as the canonical report.

Fresh resolution experiment on current `origin/main`: the plan-review gate tests for BLOCK and PASS signature behavior report `3 passed`. They prove a BLOCK carries no passing signature or satisfiable claim attestation, while PASS carries a valid signature. The documented `signature.signed` contract—not object presence—is the boolean of record. The original reported behavior is no longer occurring.
baseline.summary: plan-review: signed attestation emitted on BLOCK verdict (signature should mean PASS)

# The attested `<700` headroom target no longer matches its baseline

## What happened

Rebasing the LLM-provider-seam stack onto current `origin/main` turned `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap` RED:

```
AssertionError: runner.py is 713 LOC; the split must bring it under 700 so
adding a line is not a build break
```

**This is not a regression in the split.** Measured on the rebased stack:

| | LOC |
|---|---|
| `runner.py` on `origin/main` (no split) | **798** |
| `runner.py` on the stack (2682's split applied) | **713** |
| 2682's attested target | **< 700** |

The split still removes 85 lines. What changed is the BASELINE: when 2682 was authored, main's `runner.py` was ~698 and the split produced 655. Main has since grown it by ~100 lines (server-side web search for bug ff64, usage-log provider stamping, and others), so replaying the same split now lands at 713.

## Why it cannot simply be forced under 700

Two candidate seams exist, and BOTH are pinned by the test suite as deliberate monkeypatch seams — moving either would require ~15 test edits across 9 files, which is precisely what 2682 was careful to avoid (its criterion was ZERO test edits):

- `_import_pydantic_ai` — `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_import_pydantic_ai", ...)` in `test_llm_temperature.py`, `test_llm_timeouts.py`, `test_llm_provider_factory.py`, `test_agent_build_invariants.py`, `test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` (x2), `test_bedrock_provider.py`, `test_web_tool_gating.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py`.
- `_pai_check_config` — imported directly from `rebar.llm.runner` in `test_openai_compatible_provider.py` (x3).
- `_check_tool_capability` / `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` — 7 references in `test_agent_build_invariants.py`, including `runner_mod._TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED.clear()` as a MODULE ATTRIBUTE. Moving it saves only ~17 lines and would need a re-export shim to land at ~698 — a 2-line margin achieved mechanically, which the module-size policy explicitly forbids ("never mechanically to hit a number").

## The decision this needs

The test's STATED intent — "runner.py must stop sitting ON the 800 gate, not merely pass it" — is arguably satisfied at 713, which has 87 lines of headroom against the hard cap. But 700 is an ATTESTED acceptance criterion of CLOSED story 2682, so changing it is not a unilateral call.

Options, none of which should be taken silently:

1. **Do the seam work properly** — extract the preflight/import cluster (`_import_pydantic_ai` + `_pai_check_config`, ~40 LOC) into its own module and update the ~15 monkeypatch sites to target the new module. Real headroom (~676), but a genuine refactor with suite-wide reach.
2. **Re-derive the target from the current baseline** and record why, acknowledging that 2682's number was calibrated against a main that no longer exists. This changes a closed story's attested criterion and should be explicit, not incidental.
3. **Push back on main's growth of `runner.py`** — 798 LOC with a 800 cap means main itself is now one line from a build break, which is the deeper problem this surfaced.

Option 3 is worth noting independently: **`runner.py` on `origin/main` is at 798/800.** Whatever is decided here, main has two lines of headroom in its single busiest module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a decision is recorded on this ticket naming which option was taken and why
- [ ] `test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap` passes on a stack rebased onto current `origin/main`, without a re-export shim introduced solely to satisfy the count
- [ ] if the target is changed, the new number is justified against the CURRENT `origin/main` baseline and the change is cross-referenced from closed story 2682
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes on the rebased stack, evidenced by the pytest summary in a comment
baseline.summary: 2682's runner.py <700 target is unreachable after main grew runner.py to 798

## Summary
The mirror-guard workflow fails on every evaluation: permissions declares 'administration: read', which is NOT a valid GITHUB_TOKEN workflow-permission scope, so the workflow fails schema validation and no jobs run (0-job 'startup failure'). Even if valid, its ruleset-drift check needs a GitHub token with administration:read (a fine-grained PAT), which org policy won't grant the default token.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Push to main (or trigger mirror-guard).
2. Observe: run created with 0 jobs, conclusion=failure, 'log not found'.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: mirror-guard runs and verifies Gerrit->GitHub replication using the default token.
- Actual: workflow fails validation (invalid permission key) and never runs.

## Fix
Scope the Actions workflow to the REPLICATION check only (rebar.mirror_guard --replication), which needs no admin token (fetch_github_main_sha treats the token as optional; Gerrit read is anonymous). Drop the ruleset-drift check from this workflow and remove the invalid administration:read permission, so it runs on the default GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: read) with no PAT.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mirror-guard.yml permissions contains no invalid keys (drops administration:read; keeps contents: read).
- [ ] The workflow runs 'rebar.mirror_guard --replication' (no ruleset check), needing no fine-grained PAT.
- [ ] mirror-guard is green on main (replication in sync) without any new secret.
baseline.summary: mirror-guard CI red: invalid administration:read permission + PAT-only ruleset check

# PR posture on the GitHub mirror: welcome-bot redirect + shepherded-patch intake (with pre-flight experiments)

## Why

PRs opened against the mirror can never merge (today a repository ruleset rejects merges; PRs would sit open and unanswered — the posture universally condemned across peers: Gerrit's own mirror with rotting PRs, pre-archive AOSP). Peers split: Chromium/Qt/torvalds flipped GitHub's native Feb-2026 `has_pull_requests: false` setting (zero-cost but silent); LibreOffice/Wikimedia/OpenDev bot-close with a warm redirect. For a project that wants to convert drive-bys into repeat contributors, research recommends keeping PRs ENABLED as an intake channel: a bot answers instantly and the maintainer converts worthwhile patches to Gerrit (Wikimedia's "ask someone to convert" path).

## What

Decision (record as ADR `docs/adr/0037-oss-contribution-intake-posture.md`, covering: PR posture chosen + rejected alternatives incl. native disable and GerritBot-style auto-import; revisit trigger = PR volume exceeding solo-shepherd capacity): keep PRs ENABLED + auto-answer bot.

- Add `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` using dessant/repo-lockdown **SHA-pinned with a trailing version comment** (repo convention per gerrit-verify.yaml: "All third-party actions are SHA-pinned"; resolve the current v5.x release SHA at execution, e.g. `dessant/repo-lockdown@<sha> # v5.0.2`). Trigger: `pull_request_target: types: [opened, reopened]` (`reopened` closes Wikimedia's reopen loophole, T374157). Explicit least-privilege block: `permissions: { pull-requests: write }` (nothing else — `pull_request_target` runs with an elevated token on fork PRs; issues are real intake here, so the workflow must NOT touch issues: no `issues:` events, no issue inputs). `close-pr: true`, `lock-pr: false` (LibreOffice pattern — thread stays open). **Exempt `dependabot[bot]`** (job-level `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'`): the release-hygiene story configures Dependabot whose PRs are advisory notifications that a maintainer converts to Gerrit changes — the bot must not close them. Verify the v5 input key names against the action's manifest (action.yml) at execution; a renamed input fails silently.
- Comment message per the convergent five-part skeleton: thank by name; "read-only mirror, PRs can't merge here — this close is automatic, nothing is wrong with your change"; deep-link Gerrit (GitHub OAuth sign-in) + `docs/your-first-change.md` (exists before this lands — this story depends_on the onboarding story); shepherded-patch escape hatch; warm tone.
- Publish the shepherded-patch policy in CONTRIBUTING.md (new section; Qt's voice — allowed, explicitly slower, best-effort): contributor runs `git commit -s` (their own DCO sign-off — required; see the DCO section) then attaches `git format-patch -1` output to a GitHub issue (plain diff acceptable with name/email to credit); maintainer applies with `git am` (author = contributor, committer = shepherd), adds their own `Signed-off-by` and the `rebar-ticket:` trailer via amend (message-only; authorship untouched), pushes `refs/for/main`, drives review; `Co-authored-by:` when substantially rewritten. If E2 (below) finds Forge Author NOT grantable, the policy text instead promises `Co-authored-by:` credit — the section is written after E2 resolves.
- Update the GitHub repo description: "Read-only mirror — code review at https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com".

Pre-flight experiments (complete BEFORE the workflow lands; record each outcome as a ticket comment AND fold consequences into the affected artifact):
- [E1] Scratch-repo test of `has_pull_requests: false` fork-side UX — documents the rejected alternative in the ADR.
- [E2] Admin read of Gerrit ACLs (JoeOakhartNava identity) on the live server + `infra/gerrit/project.config`: is Forge Author granted to Registered Users on the rebar project? If not, add the grant via the declarative config path or downgrade the authorship promise (go/no-go feeds the policy text above).
- [E3] Audit ALL `.github/workflows/*` for `pull_request`/`pull_request_target` event dependencies — known set today: test.yml, optionality.yml, eval.yml, eval-plan-review-container.yml (enumerate at execution with `grep -l "pull_request" .github/workflows/*`); confirm none is broken by bot-closed fork PRs (they run on PR events but fork PRs being closed quickly may cancel runs — acceptable; record). Any real breakage found is fixed in this story or ticketed via discovered_from.
- [E4] Confirm the `rebar-ticket:` trailer policy for shepherded patches (default: shepherd creates/uses a ticket and amends the trailer in) and cross-check it against the onboarding tutorial's outsider-ticket flow.

Note: maintainer-opened test PRs are NOT exempted from the bot — a closed test PR is precisely the verification (AC1); no exemption logic.

## Scope

IN: lockdown workflow + message text, CONTRIBUTING.md shepherded-patch section, repo description, ADR 0037, experiments E1–E4. OUT: GerritBot-style automatic PR→Gerrit import — non-goal recorded in ADR 0037: only Go operates one; the gerrit github-pullrequest plugin is dormant; even at Go's scale bridged PRs merge at ~34% vs ~78% native (golang discussion #61182). Also OUT: issue lockdown (Issues are real intake), changes to the merge-blocking ruleset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test PR from a non-collaborator fork receives the comment and is closed (not locked) — prove: the test PR's timeline shows the bot comment + closed state; a REOPENED test PR is re-closed (covers the `reopened` type).
- [ ] Message content check — prove by grep of the workflow file: contains "read-only mirror", "nothing is wrong with your change", a link to `docs/your-first-change.md`, a link to https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com, and the patch-fallback offer; contains none of "rejected", "not accepted", "closed as invalid".
- [ ] Workflow hardening — prove: `lockdown.yml` has a `permissions:` block granting only `pull-requests: write`; the action ref matches `@[0-9a-f]{40} # v` (SHA-pinned); input keys verified against the pinned action.yml.
- [ ] Dependabot exemption present — prove: `grep -q "dependabot" .github/workflows/lockdown.yml`; a Dependabot-authored PR (or a simulated actor test) is NOT closed by the bot.
- [ ] E1–E4 outcomes recorded as ticket comments; E2's go/no-go reflected in the CONTRIBUTING policy text; E3 breakage (if any) fixed or ticketed.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md shepherded-patch section present with all four required elements — prove, each individually against the section: `grep -q "format-patch" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "Signed-off-by" CONTRIBUTING.md` (both-trailer DCO handling); `grep -qi "author" CONTRIBUTING.md` reflecting the E2 outcome (either `git am` authorship preservation or `Co-authored-by` fallback — whichever E2 selected); `grep -q "rebar-ticket" CONTRIBUTING.md` (trailer policy); `grep -qi "best-effort" CONTRIBUTING.md` (caveat).
- [ ] ADR 0037 committed covering posture decision, native-disable rejection (E1 evidence), GerritBot non-goal, revisit trigger. Repo description updated — prove: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar --jq .description` contains "read-only" or "mirror".
baseline.summary: PR posture on the GitHub mirror: welcome-bot redirect + shepherded-patch intake (pre-flight experiments)
