# The `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain is a documented subsystem with no live producer

## Status

DISCOVERED while fixing d103-c3f8-2fbc-4c97 / 727f-b351-59ba-4b3b. Not a regression those fixes introduced - it predates them and neither changes it. Filed so it is not lost.

## What is unreachable

`differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` is the only producer of `(inbound, probe)` mutations. It iterates `local_state` looking for entries carrying a bound `jira_key` field. Its sole production caller, `run_differs`, passes `prev_snapshot` - a FETCHED Jira snapshot, whose entries never carry `jira_key` (`fetcher.py`, and the contract shape in `_snapshot_schema.py`). The loop therefore never emits, and everything downstream of it is dead in production:

* `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` in `run_differs.py`
* `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeResult`, `ProbeBranch`)
* the router `route_inbound_probe` — which lives in `reconcile_helpers.py` and is re-exported at
  `reconcile.py:66`, NOT in `inbound_probe.py` as an earlier draft of this section claimed
* `backend.probe_remote` / the `SupportsAbsenceProbe` capability

Confirmed empirically: fed a realistic fetched-snapshot pair, `compute_mutations` emits only `jira_new`, `unbound_local` and `field_drift`. The only fixture in the repo that supplies a `jira_key`-bearing `local_state` is `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`.

## Why it matters

This is the mechanism ADR 0028 para 2 relies on to tell "deleted" from "aged out of the fetch window" - deletion is proven only by a bounded direct GET returning 404. With no live producer, that discrimination is never exercised in production.

The live DC cell that once asserted the probe WAS re-oracled, but the inherited wording for it was wrong and is corrected here (see CITATION-3B5F-D). The rename `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe` -> `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown` landed in commit `ae009443a9`, whose subject is `b9b8: mirror a Jira-side title edit inbound`. It was BUNDLED INTO b9b8's commit, not part of b9b8's scope (b9b8 is a title-mirroring bug in `outbound_field_diff.py:38-45`). The cell today asserts the ADR 0028 para 1 observable and PASSED live in harness run 30933704255.

## What is NOT the fix

Do NOT re-enable the arm by making `run_differs` pass a `jira_key`-bearing local_state without also removing `reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` in the SAME change. That suppression exists only because the caller passes the legacy `(prev, curr)` pair; migrating the caller makes the suppressed emissions correct again, and leaving both in place would silently drop real work.

## OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-04): once an issue is deleted in Jira, it shouldn't be resurrected.

This settles the question DECISION-3B5F-C escalated, and it widens the ticket: rebar resurrects TODAY, on a delay, through a path no ticket has examined.

**Measured, not assumed** (real `BindingStore`): 3 consecutive confirmed-404 `note_absent` calls retire the binding; `_retire` (`binding_store.py:564-577`) pops the entry from BOTH `bindings` and `reverse`; `get_jira_key` then returns `None`, so the local ticket is UNBOUND; and `outbound_differ.py:502-513` emits an outbound CREATE for any unbound local ticket. A fresh Jira issue therefore replaces the deliberately-deleted one about 3 passes later.

Prior art agrees with the ruling: Unito will not recreate deleted work items, "assuming that once a work item is deleted, you don't want it back", explicitly to stop flows re-creating things you wanted gone; Kubernetes reconcilers treat a missing object with `IgnoreNotFound` and never resurrect.

**`is_retired` does not prevent this.** It exists (`binding_store.py:612`) and is consulted at `outbound_differ.py:590`, but only to keep retired keys OUT of the GET-probe candidate list. It is keyed by `jira_key`, and the unbound-create arm has no retired check at all.

## Plan

**A0. Define the escape hatch - it does not exist yet.** There is NO un-retire API: `is_retired` reads (`binding_store.py:612`), `clear_absent` only resets the 404 counter (`:589`), and `_retire` (`:564`) is private and one-way. A tombstone would be permanent with no route out but hand-editing `.bridge_state/bindings-retired.json`. So this adds `BindingStore.unretire(jira_key)`: drop the key from the retired set and file so the next pass treats the ticket as ordinary unbound work. The suppression message names this call.

**A. Tombstone a confirmed-deleted pairing so it is never re-created.**
1. Add `BindingStore.is_retired_local(local_id) -> bool` - a reverse lookup over the retired entries
   (`bindings-retired.json` is keyed by `jira_key` and carries `local_id`, so only the accessor is
   missing). Same duck-typed/fail-open tolerance as `outbound_differ._is_retired`.
2. Guard the unbound-create arm at `outbound_differ.py:510-513`: a local ticket with NO live binding
   but WITH a retired one was previously paired with a remote that returned a confirmed 404 - skip the
   create. A never-bound ticket still creates normally; that distinction is the whole point.
3. Make it VISIBLE: a bridge alert / sync-log line naming the local id and the retired key, and naming
   `unretire` as the route back.

**B. Delete the dead legacy probe arm:** the producer `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, `route_inbound_probe` (`reconcile_helpers.py`) and its re-export at `reconcile.py:66`.

**B2. THE CONSUMER INVENTORY — every module that exercises a removed symbol.** A prior revision of this plan named only the fixture-only test, which under-declared the blast radius: eight further modules reference these symbols directly and would break unaddressed. `review-plan` blocked on exactly that, correctly. The complete set, and the disposition of each:

*Deleted* (the module's whole subject is the removed chain):
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py` — the only fixture supplying a
  `jira_key`-bearing `local_state`, i.e. a synthetic input the real caller never produces
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_inbound_probe_dispatch.py` — exercises
  `route_inbound_probe` across all branches

*Updated* (the module has a legitimate wider subject; only the dead-chain assertions go, and a comment records the removal so the next reader is not left guessing):
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py` — called
  `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` directly
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py` — likewise
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_snapshot_differ_stale_local_state.py` — asserted the
  dispatch as a stubbed phase

Source modules carrying the removals besides the four named above: `reconcile.py` (re-export), `typed_dispatch.py`, `applier.py`, `apply_inbound.py`, `_backend.py`, `inbound_probe.py` (dormancy note only).

**B1. SCOPE BOUNDARY - the port capability stays, as a reasoned exclusion.** `inbound_probe.py`, `backend.probe_remote` and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` also lose their only consumer, but removing DC's `probe_remote` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:213-229`) removes DC's only import of the shared `classify_probe_response`, leaving it used by Cloud alone (`adapters/jira/probe.py:85,98,100`) - which weakens **epic e369 AC5**, whose claim is that the probe classifier has one implementation in `jira_family` imported by BOTH backends. Trading an epic-level AC to delete a dormant Protocol is a separate decision; recorded as dormant with a follow-up.

**C. Do NOT restore same-pass re-create - and REMOVE its implementation rather than orphaning it.** An earlier draft kept `_apply_inbound_delete` "for a possible re-wire"; `review-plan` blocked that as leaving a removed producer's consumer behind, and under the ruling the objection is stronger than the reviewer put it: `create_after_hard_delete` (`apply_inbound.py:220`) is not merely unreachable, it is now UNWANTED - it IS the resurrection ruled against. So the leaf goes: `_apply_inbound_delete` (`apply_inbound.py:175-284`), its `("inbound","delete")` entry (`typed_dispatch.py:92`), the `_apply_inbound_probe` marker leaf and its `applier.py` registration, and the `create_after_hard_delete` consumption at `applier.py:452`. No half-wired resurrection path remains.

**C1. Plan C's consumer inventory.** Removing the leaf orphans its builders, so they go too: `_build_hard_delete_recreate` and the `pending_hard_delete_creates` plumbing, plus `reconcile_helpers._audit_log_probe`. Test consumers:

*Deleted*: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_hard_delete_recreate.py` — its entire subject is the same-pass re-create this ruling forbids.

*Updated*: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py` (asserted `create_after_hard_delete`) and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_leaves_effect_matrix.py` (asserted the `(inbound,probe)` marker leaf via `_drive_inbound_probe`).

*Updated (a THIRD guard, found by CI not by my grep)*: `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_post_deletion_linkage.py` pins the exact `(direction, action)` pairs as a LITERAL `EXPECTED_LEAF_PAIRS` frozenset, so removing the two inbound leaves is registry DRIFT to it. The two pairs are dropped from that pinned set with the reason recorded inline; the guard still pins the remaining pairs, so an ACCIDENTAL drop still fails. It was missed locally because the file lives under `tests/integration/` but is NOT marked `integration`, and CI selects by MARKER (`pytest -m "not integration and not external"`) — so a path-based local run (`pytest tests/unit`) cannot see it. Reproduce with the marker selection.

*Deliberately NOT modified*: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier.py` and `apply/test_applier_direction_guard.py` iterate the `_LEAVES` registry and cross-check it against `mutation._VALID_COMBINATIONS`. They keep passing unmodified because they assert `_LEAVES` ⊆ `_VALID_COMBINATIONS`, not the converse. **Known loose end, stated rather than hidden:** `_VALID_COMBINATIONS` still permits `(inbound, delete)` and `(inbound, probe)`, so such a mutation would now raise `UnknownActionError` at dispatch rather than being rejected up front. Narrowing the allowlist is deliberately out of scope here — it would change a shared validation contract this ticket did not review — and it is recorded so a reviewer agrees to it rather than discovers it.

**D. `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` STAYS.** The caller is unchanged, so the suppression is exactly as correct as today. (The "what is NOT the fix" trap applies to the WIRE option, not taken.)

**E. Correct ADR 0028.** Its Consequences assert c244 re-creates a hard-deleted issue in the same pass. That is false today and, under this ruling, no longer desired. Replace with tombstone semantics and note that absence-vs-deletion discrimination lives in `outbound_differ` + `binding_walk`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Establish whether the absence-probe path is still wanted, or whether ADR 0028 para 2's
      direct-GET confirmation has since been implemented elsewhere. **ANSWERED** — implemented twice
      and both live: `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` (L13) and `binding_walk.py:187-196` (ADR para 4),
      called at `run_differs.py:222` / `:257`. Verified live on DC: Row 14
      `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown` PASSED in harness run 30933704255.
- [x] ~~a RED-first test proving `(inbound, probe)` is produced from the real production call path~~ —
      **MOOT** under the operator ruling; no producer is to be created.
- [x] the dead chain is removed: `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`,
      `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, `route_inbound_probe`, and the fixture-only
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`
- [x] RED-first: a local ticket whose binding was retired on a confirmed 404 gets NO outbound create —
      the test FAILS before the guard exists and PASSES after, checked by running it at both commits
- [x] a never-bound local ticket STILL gets its outbound create, asserted in the same test module so
      the guard cannot suppress ordinary creation
- [x] the suppression is observable (bridge alert or sync-log line) naming the local id and the retired
      key, and the message names `BindingStore.unretire(<jira_key>)` as the route to re-enable creation
- [x] `BindingStore.unretire(jira_key)` exists, drops the key from BOTH the in-memory retired set and
      `bindings-retired.json`, and a test proves the local ticket is created again on the next pass —
      so the tombstone is reversible by a documented call rather than by hand-editing state
- [x] the dormant port capability (`probe_remote` / `SupportsAbsenceProbe` / `inbound_probe.py`) is
      recorded as dormant with a follow-up ticket, and the reason it is not removed here (epic e369
      AC5's both-backends claim on `classify_probe_response`) is stated
- [x] `BindingStore.is_retired_local(local_id)` tolerates legacy/duck-typed stores the way
      `outbound_differ._is_retired` does — asserted with a stub store lacking the method
- [x] the resurrection implementation is removed, not orphaned: `_apply_inbound_delete`, the
      `("inbound","delete")` typed_dispatch entry, the `_apply_inbound_probe` marker leaf, and the
      `create_after_hard_delete` consumption in `applier.py` — verified by the suite passing with them
      gone and a grep showing no remaining reference
- [x] ADR 0028's c244 Consequence is corrected to describe tombstone semantics
- [x] `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` is still present and still consulted — asserted, so
      the WIRE trap cannot be entered by accident

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler -q                    # the reconciler tier
    pytest tests/unit -q                                     # full unit suite (no regressions)
    make lint && make typecheck

The RED-first proof for the tombstone guard is run explicitly at two commits: the test is added first and must FAIL against the pre-guard tree, then PASS once the guard lands. A guard asserted without a demonstrated RED is unverified, and this one suppresses work — the failure mode of a wrong guard is silently not creating issues, which no green suite would surface.

Removal of the dead chain is proved by the suite continuing to pass with the producer, the dispatch arm and the router gone — plus a grep confirming no remaining `(inbound, probe)` producer, since the dynamic loader means an import-graph check alone would miss a string-loaded module.
baseline.summary: Inbound-probe dispatch chain has no live producer

## Target

Seven lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Context / Problem

AGENTS.md's "Module-size policy (when editing rebar itself)" section prominently documents the 800-LOC module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`) but says NOTHING about its sibling CI gate: the shrink-only C901 cyclomatic-complexity ratchet (`.github/complexity-baseline.json`, McCabe max-complexity 15, enforced by `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` as part of `make lint`).

The ratchet fails the build whenever a function gains NEW debt or grows PAST its recorded per-symbol ceiling. This is exactly the failure mode of routine work like adding a CLI flag or a guard clause (added branches -> increased complexity), so an agent that adds a couple of flags to an existing command (e.g. create_cli/edit_cli) hits it predictably. Because it is a structural gate the behavioral test oracle cannot see, an implementer/orchestrator only discovers it at pre-flight, forcing an unplanned behavior-preserving extraction pass.

Discovered while implementing story cef7 (bridge_project/repos create+edit flags): the flag/guard additions pushed create_core (23>21), create_cli (26>22), edit_core (24>21) past ceiling and made edit_cli (16) new, failing `make lint` although the change was under the 800 LOC cap and lint/typecheck were otherwise clean.

## Approach

Add a short paragraph to AGENTS.md's Module-size policy section (or an adjacent "Structural gates" note) surfacing the complexity ratchet next to the LOC cap: what it is, that it is part of `make lint`, that it is shrink-only (fails on new/increased debt, ceilings in `.github/complexity-baseline.json`, threshold 15 in pyproject `[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]`), that the fix is behavior-preserving extraction (never bumping the baseline), and how to inspect it (`ruff check --select C901 <file>` / `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`). Cross-reference from the rebar-implement skill's 'ship the constraints the oracle cannot see' step so implementer briefs quote it alongside the module-size limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AGENTS.md surfaces the C901 shrink-only complexity ratchet in/next to the Module-size policy section, naming the gate command, the baseline file, the threshold source, and the extraction-not-baseline-bump remedy.
- [x] The note explains it runs under `make lint` and blocks CI like the module-size gate.
- [x] A one-line pointer is added so a reader knows how to census offenders (`ruff check --select C901`).
baseline.summary: Surface the shrink-only C901 complexity ratchet in AGENTS.md alongside the module-size cap

## Summary
`AcliClient.set_relationship(from, to)` emitted `jira link create --out from --in to`, but
ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED vs the naive reading: `--out X --in Y --type Blocks`
creates "Y blocks X" (the `--in` issue is the blocker). So every reconciler-written link was
reversed. This stayed hidden because (a) rebar reads links direction-agnostically, (b) most
links were adopted from Jira rather than written by us, and (c) the tests never asserted
absolute direction.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create Jira issues X, Y. Call `set_relationship(X, Y, "Blocks")`.
2. Observe Jira shows "Y blocks X" (expected "X blocks Y"). (Live-validated 2026-07-16.)
3. Consequence via the applier: `A blocks B` -> Jira "B blocks A" (reversed); `A depends_on B`
   -> after c8ed added the applier swap, Jira "A blocks B" (reversed).

**Expected:** `A blocks B` -> "A blocks B"; `A depends_on B` -> "B blocks A".
**Actual:** both reversed (blocks reversed since outbound link sync shipped; depends_on
reversed by c8ed, which added the correct applier swap but on top of the inverted primitive).

## Root Cause
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_graph.py::set_relationship` maps `from_key`->`--out`,
`to_key`->`--in`, which is backwards. Fix: emit `--out to_key --in from_key` so the link reads
"from blocks to". With c8ed's applier swap + the relation map, BOTH relations then write the
correct direction. Live-validated end-to-end via the differ+applier (blocks->"A blocks B",
depends_on->"B blocks A").

## Why the tests missed it
The live E2E round-trip (`tests/external/test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`) checked only that a
Blocks link existed in EITHER direction and that outbound<->inbound AGREE (a consistency check
that holds even when reversed), and never covered `depends_on`. Unit tests stub
`set_relationship`, so they cannot see the flag order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `set_relationship(from, to)` emits `--out to --in from`; a unit test pins the flag order.
- [ ] A live E2E test asserts ABSOLUTE direction for BOTH `blocks` and `depends_on`.
- [ ] Live-validated: blocks->"A blocks B", depends_on->"B blocks A" through rebar's code paths.
- [ ] [operator-attested] the ~96 reversed `blocks` links (and any c8ed-reversed depends_on) are repaired in live Jira.
baseline.summary: Outbound Jira links written REVERSED: set_relationship passes ACLI --out/--in backwards

## Summary

`resolve_project` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py`) collapses the tri-state `bridge_project` field's **`None` "absent/legacy" sentinel** into the same branch as the explicit `""` "never-sync" value, so a legacy ticket (no `bridge_project` flag) is **suppressed from outbound create** instead of routing to `legacy_default`. This is the direct cause of live DC rehearsal scenario 4 (`test_absent_project_resolves_to_legacy_default`) failing with `assert 0 == 1` — the legacy-default ticket never lands in the legacy project.

## Proven root cause (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete)

`create_ticket` with no `bridge_project` stores `bridge_project: None` (present-but-null, seeded by the reducer `_state.py:58`), NOT an absent key. `resolve_project`'s `if not value: return None` lumps that `None` absent/legacy sentinel with `""` never-sync, and its `if "bridge_project" not in ticket` branch is dead because the reducer ALWAYS materializes the key — so `legacy_default` never fires for the cohort it exists to serve.

The authoritative **cef7 tri-state contract** (`src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:53-58`) states `bridge_project` is seeded `None` as the deliberate "absent/legacy" sentinel; `""` is explicit never-sync; a non-empty string is the sync target. `None` must route to `legacy_default`. Runtime-confirmed: `resolve_project({"bridge_project": None}, ld="LEG")` → `None` (vs. explicit `"LEG"` → `"LEG"`); the outbound create gate (`outbound_differ.py:584`) `if not target: return` then drops the create. Confirmed original (not regression) via `git blame a22e6f3642`.

## Fix plan

Rewrite `resolve_project` to honor the tri-state explicitly (and update its docstring to document the present-but-null `None` sentinel):

    value = ticket.get("bridge_project")
    if value is None:      # absent key OR the None absent/legacy sentinel
        return mapping.legacy_default or None
    if value == "":        # explicit never-sync
        return None
    return value

## Blast radius / caller-dependency sweep (gate CLEARED)

Single production caller: `outbound_differ.py:584` — the malfunctioning create gate itself, which expects the contract-correct target. No existing test pins `None`->None; all existing tests (`{}`->legacy_default, `""`->None, empty-legacy->None) stay green. The only behavior change is the previously-untested `{"bridge_project": None}` case, changing toward the cef7 contract. The outbound create is double-guarded — it fires only when the mapping is seeded AND `legacy_default` is both set and a key in the mapping — i.e. exactly the designed cef7 legacy migration. No behavioral dependency on the buggy path found; gate clears without escalation.

## Testing

- Held-out RED unit test added to `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py`,
  verified RED before the fix and GREEN after; teeth proven by a defect-seeded mutation that
  returns it to RED. Proof command:
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py -q`.
- Full projects-store + ensure-mapping suites stay green:
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_happy.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py -q`.
- Live DC rehearsal proven end-to-end in CI via the `Live External Integration` workflow:
  `pytest tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` with `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Held-out RED unit test `resolve_project({"bridge_project": None}, ld=X) == X` seen RED
      before the fix and GREEN after, teeth verified by defect-seeded mutation
      (`pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_projects_store_heldout.py -q`).

## Context / Problem
Entering the review-bot ASGI lifespan from an ordinary test started the real backfill reconciler and snapshot janitor, while shutdown inherited the production 1200-second queue-drain default. The idiomatic TestClient lifespan path could therefore turn a unit test into a long-running background sweep or hang. The production behavior is intentional and unchanged: src/rebar/review_bot/config.py defines DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS = 1200, and shutdown_drain_seconds() accepts a positive SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS override.

## Delivered Approach
- tests/conftest.py now uses the root autouse fixture _bound_review_bot_shutdown_drain to set SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS=1.0 for every test and registers the real_reconcile_loop marker.
- tests/unit/test_review_bot.py now uses the module-autouse fixture _safe_review_bot_lifespan_defaults to replace reconcile.reconcile_loop and rebar._snapshot.start_background_janitor during ordinary tests. Marked tests bypass only the reconciler replacement; the unrelated filesystem janitor remains stubbed.
- test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs exercises TestClient against the real application lifespan without local reconciler or janitor setup and asserts the exact 1.0-second test drain.
- test_lifespan_can_opt_into_the_real_reconcile_loop uses the marker plus an observable reconcile_once fake to prove the production reconcile_loop remains available.
- The five previously duplicated or specialized string-patch sites within tests/unit/test_review_bot.py were classified: identical setup was removed, test_lifespan_starts_and_stops_snapshot_janitor retains its observable janitor fake, and test_lifespan_cancel_await_is_bounded_for_a_task_slow_to_cancel retains its slow-reconciler fault injection.
- The repo-wide string census also found tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py. Its test-specific reconcile_loop and worker replacements are intentionally retained because they model a queued manual-rerun shutdown path outside the module fixture's scope; its 0.1-second override keeps that deliberate non-task-done queue control fast while proving local overrides take precedence.
- No production files changed.

## Verification
- RED: test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs initially observed 1200.0 instead of the required test-only 1.0.
- Focused lifespan contracts passed 8 tests; tests/unit/test_review_bot.py passed 86 tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every pytest test receives the exact SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS=1.0 baseline through _bound_review_bot_shutdown_drain; verified by test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs and the focused review-bot tests.

baseline.description:
# Reduce the macOS pytest cell to a platform-compatibility subset

## Context / Problem
The Gerrit Verified Gate's critical path is the macOS pytest cell. It runs the FULL default suite plus the integration tier, while every other gate job finishes by ~20 min. Measured over four recent successful runs the macOS py3.13 cell is ~2140-2486s and is the sole long pole (gate ~43 min). On the IDENTICAL test selection the macOS runner is ~3.7x slower per test than Ubuntu (macOS ~2140s vs Ubuntu ~572-595s), attributable to per-test process-spawn + git-store fixture overhead — the CPU-bound AST/policy scanners are equal/faster on macOS. Running full breadth on the slow runner buys latency, not confidence.

## Approach
Keep the full suite on Linux (Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 unchanged) and reduce the macOS cell to the tests whose behaviour genuinely differs between Darwin and Linux: file locking (flock/fcntl/ mkdir), atomic directory/rename, subprocess timeout (gtimeout vs timeout), and cross-process git contention. macOS keeps its existing `integration` tier step (cross-process concurrency end-to-end) and runs a new `platform_compat`-marked subset in place of the full default suite. Selection is centralised in ONE auditable place — a path-keyed auto-marker in tests/conftest.py — rather than per-file markers, so the macOS suite cannot silently drift. This fits the goal of cutting CI runtime without cutting confidence: Linux still runs everything.

## Scope
- pyproject.toml — register a `platform_compat` marker in the `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`
  `markers` list (the block currently ends at the `e2e:` entry).
- tests/conftest.py — extend the existing `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook (which already
  auto-applies the `external` marker by path) to also apply `platform_compat` by path, driven by
  a documented `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS` tuple (store/lock/atomic/timeout/snapshot/
  contention seams).
- .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml — change the `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS` env expression
  (currently the two-branch ternary at the "Run the default suite" step) so the macOS cell
  selects `platform_compat and not external`; Ubuntu keeps its existing selection. The macOS
  integration-tier step is unchanged.
- tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py — update
  `test_repo_policy_nodes_run_only_in_the_existing_primary_cell` (its regex hardcodes the old
  two-branch `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS`) for the new three-branch expression, and add a guard that
  the macOS subset still collects the core OS-sensitive files.

## Testing
- Collect and run `-m "platform_compat and not external"` locally; confirm it selects the
  store-lock / timeout / snapshot / contention tests and passes.
- Run tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py (the CI-shape guard) to green.
- A new guard test asserts a representative set of platform-sensitive files (store lock,
  stamped_lock, timeout_budget, repo_snapshot, event_append_index_lock, atomic_ticket_dir_create)
  collect under the marker, so pattern drift fails loudly rather than silently emptying the macOS
  suite (the failure path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A `platform_compat` marker is registered in pyproject.toml and `pytest -m platform_compat`
      collects a non-empty set (verified by collection + the new parity guard test).
- [x] tests/conftest.py auto-applies `platform_compat` by path via
      `_PLATFORM_COMPAT_PATH_FRAGMENTS`, and the macOS `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS` branch in
      _build-and-test.yml is `platform_compat and not external` (verified by
      test_repo_policy_nodes_run_only_in_the_existing_primary_cell).
- [x] The Ubuntu default-suite selection is unchanged — the primary/non-primary branches still
      read `not integration and not external` and `... and not repo_policy` (verified by the same
      parity test).
- [x] tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py passes in full.
- [x] The platform_compat subset runs green locally via
      `pytest -m "platform_compat and not external and not integration"`.
baseline.summary: Reduce the macOS pytest cell to a platform-compatibility subset

baseline.description:
`rebar review-plan` (the four-pass plan-review gate) is **non-deterministic and mis-calibrated**
as a gate: the same ticket re-reviewed gives different PASS/BLOCK verdicts and a different finding
set each run, the advisory batch is a near-constant ~10 regardless of plan quality, and almost
every finding is tagged `severity=critical` while remaining non-blocking. The Pass-1 finder
recall is stochastic, so "PASS" is not reproducible for the same input — which undermines a gate
whose contract is "must PASS before you can claim." (The finding CONTENT is consistently high
quality; this bug is about stability/calibration, not correctness.)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json` on a well-formed ticket; note `verdict` + the
   `blocking`/`advisory` arrays.
2. Without changing the ticket (or after a change that only ADDS detail/hardening), re-run.
3. Compare verdicts, finding counts, and which findings appear.

## Expected
- The verdict is reproducible for the same input (same ticket -> same PASS/BLOCK), and finding
  count/severity reflect actual plan quality (a strong plan yields fewer/lower-severity findings
  than a weak one).

## Actual (observed across ~29 runs this session on epic d251 + its children)
- **Non-reproducible verdicts.** S4/S6/S7 went `PASS -> BLOCK` after remediations that only added
  hardening, and each re-run surfaced DIFFERENT blocking findings; S6's block count was
  non-monotonic across rounds: `0 -> 3 -> 1 -> 6`. The same plan can pass for one run and block
  for the next.
- **Fixed-size advisory batch.** Almost every ticket, every round, returned ~10 advisories
  (`P/10a` near-uniformly; one ticket once at 8) — reads as a target/cap, not a measurement, so
  advisory volume does not discriminate plan quality.
- **Severity inflation.** Most advisories are `severity=critical` (e.g. epic 10/10, S3 10/10)
  yet non-blocking (`reason: default-advisory`) — "critical but doesn't block" is incoherent and
  makes severity useless for triage.
- **Weak cross-criterion dedup.** A single root issue surfaced as multiple findings under
  different criteria (e.g. S1's `use_lockfile`/TF>=1.10 issue appeared 4x under T1/T3/E2/G6),
  inflating the count.

## Impact
"Re-run until it passes" (the gate protocol) assumes convergence that doesn't hold: remediating
the cited block can surface new, unrelated blocks, so a good-faith author may not reach a stable
PASS. Two agents reviewing the same ticket can get different claimability.

## Notes
- Likely root: Pass-3 (decide) is deterministic GIVEN the findings, but Pass-1 (finder) recall is
  stochastic, so determinism is only conditional on a non-deterministic input. The fixed-~10 and
  all-critical patterns suggest finder prompt/threshold calibration. Surfaced dogfooding d251.
- Separate, more clear-cut bug filed for signed-on-BLOCK.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Re-running `review-plan` on an unchanged ticket yields a stable verdict (PASS stays PASS;
      no spurious PASS<->BLOCK flips) — e.g. via seeding/caching the finder, lowered temperature,
      or a deterministic finder pass, measured over N repeat runs.
- [ ] Advisory count reflects actual issues found (not a near-constant ~10); document/justify any
      cap and surface when findings were truncated.
- [ ] Severity is calibrated so `critical` implies blocking (or the block thresholds are aligned
      so a wall of "critical" advisories cannot coexist with a clean PASS); severity becomes
      usable for triage.
- [ ] Cross-criterion dedup collapses one root issue reported under multiple criteria into a
      single finding.
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents the determinism guarantees and the calibration of
      severity vs. blocking thresholds.
baseline.summary: plan-review: non-deterministic verdict + mis-calibrated findings (fixed ~10 advisories, all 'critical', PASS<->BLOCK flips)

## Why

The README is a thorough ~31KB reference (Why / Requirements / Install / CLI /
Python / MCP / Config / Tests) but has **no short tutorial** — Install jumps
straight into reference-style command docs. A newcomer has no golden path from
zero to a working first flow. Meanwhile `rebar --help` already emits a full,
authoritative command index backed by 40 per-command help files, so a separate
"cheat sheet" would only duplicate it and invite drift.

## What

Add a single, single-sourced `## Quickstart` section near the top of `README.md`:

- Install (one canonical line) -> `rebar init` -> create a first ticket ->
  `ready` / `claim` -> close, showing **expected output** at each step.
- A minimal "point an agent at it" example (the MCP one-liner) so the agent path
  is visible.
- Uses only the ~6 core commands inline and **defers the full command list to
  `rebar --help`** rather than re-listing commands.

## Scope

`README.md` only (one new section + a link to it from the top). Explicitly NOT a
separate cheat-sheet doc and NOT a duplicate command index — `rebar --help` +
the `_cli/help/*.txt` files remain the authoritative command reference. Keep it
short (a screenful).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `README.md` has a `## Quickstart` section near the top with an
  install -> first-ticket -> first-agent-flow walkthrough and expected output.
- [ ] It shows only the core commands inline and points to `rebar --help` for the
  full list (no re-listed command index, no separate cheat-sheet file).
- [ ] The commands shown are copy-pasteable and correct against the current CLI.
- [ ] A top-of-README link points to the Quickstart.
baseline.summary: Add a single-sourced README Quickstart (golden path; defers to rebar --help)

## Context
The default suite runs about 13,255 tests. The autouse _no_repo_commits guard calls git rev-parse HEAD before and after every test. On macOS, 1,000 direct head() probes averaged 7.826ms, projecting 207.4 runner-seconds / 69.1 three-worker wall-seconds per full job. A same-host A-B-B-A experiment over 895 tests measured baseline 51.81s and 56.70s versus 49.22s and 49.21s when only this guard was bypassed: median saving 5.04s (9.3%), projecting about 75s at full-suite scale. The session-wide dirty-tree backstop remains separate. No matching performance ticket was found; closed renderer ticket ashy-waterlog-hamadryas mentions the guard only as failure attribution, not optimization.

## Plan
- Preserve the exact per-test contract: detect a checkout HEAD move, name the responsible test, retain the current allow_repo_writes escape, and retain the session dirty-tree backstop.
- Replace two per-test Git processes with an in-process HEAD fingerprint after one-time per-worker discovery of the worktree Git directory/common directory. Cover symbolic loose refs, packed refs, detached HEAD, and linked worktrees; fall back safely when metadata is unreadable.
- Inventory callers and string-based references before changing the shared primitive.
- Write RED behavioral tests for unchanged HEAD, same-branch commit, detached commit, packed-ref-to-loose transition, linked-worktree commit, and exact test attribution. Add a subprocess spy proving steady-state per-test checks launch no Git process.
- Compare the approach with test-isolation/checkout-integrity practice in at least three popular actively maintained OSS projects. Implement only if at least two-thirds use the practice and none documents rejecting it for coverage/reliability; otherwise return the research for operator disposition.
- Repeat the 895-test A-B-B-A experiment and report full-suite projected plus observed savings without weakening any test selection or assertion.
- Land through Gerrit; back out with a Gerrit revert if any supported Git layout regresses or CI savings fail to reproduce.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Same-branch, detached-HEAD, packed-ref, and linked-worktree HEAD moves are detected by behavioral tests.
- [ ] An unchanged HEAD produces no false positive.
- [ ] The failing test remains individually named and allow_repo_writes retains its existing behavior.
- [ ] Steady-state before/after checks execute no Git subprocess per test after one-time worker initialization.
- [ ] The session dirty-tree backstop and all existing repo-isolation tests remain enabled.
- [ ] Three named active OSS projects are compared and the consensus decision is recorded against the standing approval rule.
- [ ] Paired timing shows a positive median wall-time reduction on the same 895-test slice and reports the full-suite projection.
- [ ] Focused tests, full lint, and typecheck pass.
- [ ] Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 are recorded before merge.
- [ ] The first post-merge full-route macOS observation is recorded before close.
baseline.summary: Eliminate per-test Git subprocesses from repo-isolation guard

## Summary

Surfaced immediately AFTER fixing the completion-verifier observed_upsert kwarg TypeError (ticket 9c7c-4844-f53c-4eac, Gerrit 1805, merged). With the signature drift fixed, the completion verifier now runs to a verdict on the bedrock arm, and a DIFFERENT, pre-existing behavioral assertion in the same test fails:

    tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py::test_dense_completion_banks_and_terminates_in_two_of_three_trials

Live run 31870102530 ('Live External Integration', bedrock arm 94977302870): 1 failed, 17 passed. The failure:

    AssertionError: dense completion banking successes=0/3
    trials = [{'banked': 5, 'verdict': 'PASS', 'error': None, 'calls_at_bank': [11, 11, 11, 11, 11], 'evidence_calls': 11}, ...x3]

All 3 trials reached a valid PASS verdict with error=None (the TypeError is gone), banking all 5 criteria — but `_bounded_bank_gaps` (test helper) requires each criterion's FIRST tool-sourced bank to fall within <=3 filesystem-evidence calls of the previous (`all(gap <= 3)`). On this run the bedrock model (bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6) gathered all 11 evidence-tool calls up front, then bulk-banked all 5 criteria at once (calls_at_bank=[11,11,11,11,11] -> gaps=[11,0,0,0,0], first gap 11 > 3), in all 3 trials. So 0/3 met the incremental-banking oracle; the test needs >=2/3.

## Why this is distinct

- This test is bedrock-PINNED (`_MODEL = 'bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6'`, decorated `@skip_unless_provider('bedrock')`), so it only runs on the bedrock arm; the anthropic/openai arms skip it. It is the sole oracle for incremental/bounded banking.
- The 9c7c fix (thread upsert **kwargs through the observation stub) only OBSERVES banking; it does not change model behavior or the banking counters. The failing assertion is about WHEN the model interleaves the record tool with evidence gathering.

## Root cause (to investigate)

Either (a) genuine model-behavior variance/flakiness on bedrock (the model now front-loads evidence gathering and bulk-banks, so the <=3 bounded-gap oracle no longer holds on bedrock), or (b) a real regression in the banking prompt / bounded-search interleaving that suppresses incremental banking. Investigate whether the bulk-bank pattern is stable across reruns (flaky vs deterministic), compare to the last known-green bedrock run, and inspect the completion-verifier banking prompt / bounded-fallback for changes that could have shifted the model from incremental to bulk banking. Decide whether to fix the interleaving behavior or relax/rescope the `_bounded_bank_gaps` oracle for bedrock.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Determine whether the bulk-bank pattern is deterministic or flaky on the bedrock arm (rerun evidence).
- [ ] Either restore incremental banking (gaps <= 3) so >=2/3 trials pass, or rescope/relax the oracle with a documented rationale.
- [ ] test_dense_completion_banks_and_terminates_in_two_of_three_trials passes on the bedrock arm of Live External Integration.

## Testing

- Repeated workflow_dispatch of 'Live External Integration' (bedrock arm) to characterize variance.
- pytest -m 'external' tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py on bedrock creds.
baseline.summary: Bedrock completion eval: dense banking not incremental (_bounded_bank_gaps 0/3)

baseline.description:
## Why
`rebar review-code` (the local/coding-agent path) reviews a diff but persists NOTHING — only the Gerrit voter emits a `code_review` artifact. Without a local artifact there is no per-session memory for the region-gated novelty floor (blameless-grindable-noctule) to converge against. This story makes local `review-code` emit a session-keyed `code_review` artifact, reusing the payload/reader shape from revenued-thickset-dassie.

## What
- **Resolve the local memory key.** Use the centralized
  `rebar._commands.session_id.resolve_session_id()` (precedence: `REBAR_SESSION_ID` →
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` → `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` → `SESSION_ID`; validated shared-across-subagents,
  unique-per-parallel-session).
  - **Fallback (approach A):** when it returns `None` (bare/headless, no SessionStart shim), mint a
    per-invocation `uuid4` (do NOT persist a shared file). This guarantees ISOLATION — no
    local→Gerrit bleed and no cross-session contamination — at the cost of making local convergence
    intentionally INERT for a bare invocation (each run gets a fresh key, so the reader finds no
    prior). Genuine per-session convergence arrives wherever a session lifecycle exists (native
    harness var or a SessionStart shim exporting `REBAR_SESSION_ID`).
- **Set `session_id` on the verdict.** The local path sets `verdict["session_id"] = session_key` so
  the payload (revenued-thickset-dassie's `build_payload`, which reads `verdict.get("session_id")`)
  carries it top-level. The typed memory key for the reader is `session:<session_key>`.
- **Wire the local gate entry to emit + persist.** Thread the resolved key down the local call chain
  `_review_code → shim.review_code → gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` and emit a session-keyed
  artifact:
  - **Signature changes (in scope):** add `target_ticket: str | None = None` and
    `session_id: str | None = None` parameters to `code_review/shim.py::review_code(...)`, AND add a
    `session_id: str | None = None` field to the `CodeReviewRequest` dataclass in `gate_dispatch.py`
    (alongside the existing `target_ticket`). The shim forwards both onto
    `CodeReviewRequest(target_ticket=…, session_id=…, …)`. Without these the resolved key cannot
    reach the emit path.
  - **Create-or-reuse idempotency (session key = stable convergence point).** Before emitting, a
    local-emit helper resolves ONE artifact ticket per session key, mirroring
    `voter.emit_code_review_artifact` (voter.py ~199–220) EXACTLY:
    `title = f"code-review: session:{session_key}"`; scan
    `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review", repo_root=repo_root)` for a title match and REUSE
    that artifact id; else `rebar.create_ticket("code_review", title, …)`. Then `sidecar.emit(verdict,
    target_ticket=artifact_id, …)`. So two sequential local reviews under one session id append
    sidecar events to the SAME artifact (AC4) instead of duplicating.
  - **`relates_to` link (best-effort).** Link the artifact `relates_to` the work ticket resolved
    from the head commit's `rebar-ticket:` trailer (via the existing `extract_ticket_refs` +
    `resolve_ticket_id`, exactly as `voter.emit_code_review_artifact` does) for searchability. No new
    `--ticket` CLI flag is added (out of scope). A trailerless/unresolved/ticketless review STILL
    persists (memory is keyed by session, not by ticket) — the only degradation is no cross-run
    match when the key differs; a missing/unresolved link is logged, never fails the review.
  - **Best-effort throughout:** artifact create/reuse/emit/link failures are logged and swallowed —
    they must NEVER fail the review (mirrors the voter + sidecar posture).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` (`_review_code`: resolve key, thread it down),
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py` (`review_code`: add `target_ticket`/`session_id` params),
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (local-emit helper: create-or-reuse the session artifact
  + set `verdict["session_id"]`).
- Depends on the payload shape + reader (revenued-thickset-dassie) — specifically `build_payload`
  reading `verdict.get("session_id")`, which lands with c639; this story is reviewed/implemented
  AFTER c639 is committed on the stack, so that dependency exists in the tree.
- OUT of scope: the Gerrit voter path (already emits; inherits the payload extension); the
  region_gated_floor consumer (blameless-grindable-noctule).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Local `rebar review-code` emits a `code_review` artifact keyed `session:<id>` carrying the
      reviewed-file `deps` map and a top-level `session_id`.
- [ ] The session key = `resolve_session_id()`; when `None`, a per-invocation `uuid4` is used (no
      shared-file persistence), making bare-invocation local convergence intentionally inert.
- [ ] `shim.review_code` gains `target_ticket` + `session_id` parameters and `CodeReviewRequest`
      gains a `session_id` field, both forwarded, so the local path can supply the artifact anchor
      and session key.
- [ ] Create-or-reuse idempotency: two sequential local reviews under ONE session id append to the
      SAME artifact (title `code-review: session:{id}`), not duplicate tickets.
- [ ] The artifact `relates_to`-links the ticket resolved from the head commit's `rebar-ticket:`
      trailer when one resolves; a trailerless/unresolved review still persists (keyed by session)
      and never fails the review (no new `--ticket` flag).
- [ ] Tests: a local review with a set `REBAR_SESSION_ID` emits/reuses one session-keyed artifact
      across two runs; a bare review (no session var) mints a uuid key and still persists; artifact
      failures never fail the review.
baseline.summary: Persist a code_review artifact for local rebar review-code + session keying (uuid fallback)

baseline.description:
## What
Read-only derivations over the existing gate sidecars for gate-economics + env-diagnosis metrics: an LLM cost proxy (`llm_calls`, latency) from the plan/code-review sidecars, cost-per-accepted-change, first-pass verification, and env-diagnosis intervals (`gate_error_v1` ERROR → next PASS). All read-only; nothing is written.

## Data-access ground truth (the plan is built on this)
- **Only `REVIEW_RESULT` (`plan_review_result_v2`) carries a `metrics` block** — `{det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls, claim_path}` (`plan_review/sidecar.py:496-497`). **`COMPLETION_VERDICT` carries NO metrics block** (verified in `completion_sidecar.py:182-219`; neither the pass nor fail branch has `llm_calls`). So all `llm_calls`/latency derivations read `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics` ONLY — the completion sidecar is used for the pass/fail *outcome*, never for cost.
- **"Accepted change"** is defined precisely: a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` record (`SCHEMA_PASS`, `completion_sidecar.py:29`) on a ticket — i.e. the completion (close) gate PASSED. This is NOT a plan-review PASS (`plan_review_result_v2` with `verdict=="PASS"`), which only clears the *claim* gate and does not mean the ticket closed. The reader distinguishes the two by schema.
- Sidecars are reducer-ignored. **This reader uses a single RAW ordered scan** of each ticket's `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` and `*-COMPLETION_VERDICT.json` event files (resolve dir via `tracker_dir`+`resolve_ticket_dir_name`; sort by the ns-epoch filename prefix / `event_sort_key`; `json.load`; read `event["data"]` + `event["timestamp"]`). The schema-guarded helpers are NOT used for counting, because `latest_pass_record` returns only the single most-recent PASS (`completion_sidecar.py:137`) and `all_review_results` hard-filters to `plan_review_result_v1/v2` — neither can COUNT completion passes nor surface `gate_error_v1`. A record's kind is read off `data.schema` / `data.verdict`: `plan_review_result_v2` (verdict PASS/BLOCK/FAIL) with a `metrics` block; `completion_verifier_pass_v1` / `_fail_v1`; and `gate_error_v1` (verdict ERROR, carries a `gate` field). The raw scan sees ALL of them on the stream in order.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py` — new: reader over the sidecars, registered into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py`.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_sidecar_metrics.py` — new.

## Metric definitions
- **llm_call_proxy / latency** — sum `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics.llm_calls` (and latency fields) over the range. `source="sidecar"`.
- **cost_per_accepted_change** — summed `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics.llm_calls` divided by the count of `completion_verifier_pass_v1` records (accepted closes) in range; returns `None` (→ `Unavailable`) when there are zero accepted closes (no division by zero).
- **first_pass_verification** — fraction of tickets whose FIRST `COMPLETION_VERDICT` record is a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` (passed on the first verification attempt).
- **first_pass_verification** — fraction of tickets whose FIRST `COMPLETION_VERDICT` record (oldest-first by filename order) is a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` (passed on the first close-verification attempt). Reads the raw COMPLETION_VERDICT files per ticket in chronological order and inspects the earliest one's schema.
- **env_diagnosis_interval** — pair each `gate_error_v1` ERROR record with the next PASS record **for the SAME gate** on that ticket's stream. Because plan-review and code-review both write to `REVIEW_RESULT`, pairing matches on the ERROR record's `gate` field (`plan_review`/`code_review`/`completion`) against the next same-gate PASS (a `plan_review_result_v2`/code-review PASS for those gates, a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` for completion) — NOT merely the next PASS on the stream. The interval = PASS `timestamp` − ERROR `timestamp`; an ERROR with no following same-gate PASS is an open (unclosed) diagnosis interval.

## Approach
Pure read-side derivations over sidecars that already persist per-run metrics, verdicts, and (via ticket 8bc5) the additive ERROR outcome. `confidence="high"`; `is_authoritative("sidecar")` is True. Nothing is written.

## Tests
- Unit (real sidecar fixtures written to a temp store): cost-per-accepted-change over 3 REVIEW_RESULT runs (llm_calls 2+3+4=9) with 1 `completion_verifier_pass_v1` returns 9; with 0 accepted returns `None`. An ERROR record paired with a later PASS on the same ticket yields an interval equal to the fixture timestamp delta; an ERROR with no PASS yields an open interval.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_sidecar_metrics.py` passes: a `gate_error_v1` ERROR row paired with a later PASS on the same ticket yields a diagnosis-interval duration equal to the fixture timestamp delta (`assert dur == expected`).
- [ ] cost_per_accepted_change over a fixture of 3 REVIEW_RESULT runs summing `llm_calls==9` with exactly 1 `completion_verifier_pass_v1` returns 9; a fixture with 0 accepted closes returns `None` (→ `Unavailable`, no ZeroDivisionError) — both asserted.
- [ ] the cost derivations read `llm_calls` ONLY from `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics` (never from COMPLETION_VERDICT, which has none) — asserted by a fixture whose COMPLETION_VERDICT records carry no metrics yet cost is still computed from the REVIEW_RESULT runs.
- [ ] `first_pass_verification` over a fixture of 3 tickets where 2 have their EARLIEST `COMPLETION_VERDICT` record as `completion_verifier_pass_v1` and 1 has an earliest `completion_verifier_fail_v1` returns 2/3 — asserted numerically (proves the oldest-first COMPLETION_VERDICT scan).
- [ ] `env_diagnosis_interval` pairs a `gate_error_v1` ERROR (gate=`plan_review`) with the next `plan_review` PASS and NOT with an interleaved `completion` PASS on the same REVIEW_RESULT/COMPLETION_VERDICT streams — asserted (proves the gate-field match).
- [ ] the metrics register into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py` with `source="sidecar"` (authoritative) — asserted.
baseline.summary: Gate-sidecar reader (gate-economics + env-diagnosis metrics)

## Context / Problem

The CLI and MCP still accepted caller-selected reviewer input at `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/llm.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, and `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, while `src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py` ignored it and let the four-pass code-review gate select overlays internally. Callers could believe they chose reviewers even though the gate owned that decision.

## Approach

Remove reviewer-selection input from the CLI parser, CLI dispatch, MCP method/schema, and the keyword-only Python signature. Keep gate-owned overlay selection and the output `reviewers` field that reports which reviewers actually ran. Treat this as an intentional pre-1.0 breaking change with no deprecation shim.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_cli/help/review-code.txt`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/mcp-reference.md`, `docs/adr/0075-retire-single-pass-code-review.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` restate the new contract
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_ops_characterization.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_help_writing_guidelines_jerboa.py`, `tests/unit/test_advanced_cli_parsers.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_provenance_heldout_2d1c.py`, `tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json`, `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py`, and `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py` pin the input removal while preserving output reviewers reporting

Cascade flag: true. Recensus CLI, MCP, library, generated-doc, and test-fixture callers.

## Testing

Exercise CLI parse failure on the removed flag, absence of forwarded `reviewers` kwargs, Python signature rejection, output `reviewers` preservation, CLI/help drift checks, MCP/library parity, and the default `make test` selector with only the known baseline lifecycle failure accepted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] CLI `--reviewer`, MCP `review_code.reviewers`, and Python `reviewers=` inputs are absent from their contracts.
- [x] Old calls fail at parsing, schema, or signature validation before a billable model call.
- [x] Gate-owned reviewer selection remains and result `reviewers` accurately reports reviewers that ran.
- [x] Docs, generated help/reference, and parity baselines state the pre-1.0 breaking replacement: omit selection and inspect result reviewers.
baseline.summary: Remove caller-selected reviewer inputs from code review contracts

## Why
Nothing currently checks the DIFF against its ticket. plan-review checks the plan; completion-verifier checks at close; a diff-time scope check is complementary and catches scope drift in the change itself.

## What
New scope-intent overlay, content-triggered when >=1 ticket resolves from the commit's rebar-ticket: trailer. Grounded prerequisites from plan review:
- REGISTER `scope-intent` in the closed OVERLAY_IDS tuple in registry.py (unknown ids are dropped).
- assemble_diff (assemble.py) does NOT currently read the rebar-ticket: trailer; add trailer parsing via
  extract_ticket_refs (supports multiple ids: multiple trailer lines AND whitespace-separated tokens) and
  assemble the referenced tickets' scope/AC as this overlay's context.
- Ticket-blindness is NOT free: ticket_context is threaded into the shared reviewer_input, so keeping base
  + other overlays ticket-blind requires explicit plumbing (gate ticket context to the scope-intent
  overlay only; do not leak it to the others). Verify with a test.
Checks the diff against the UNION of all referenced tickets so legitimate multi-ticket commits don't produce false scope findings. Reuses plan-review's scope-intent criterion vocabulary. Advisory.

## Scope
reviewers/code-review-scope-intent.md, registry.py (OVERLAY_IDS + content trigger), assemble.py (trailer read + ticket-context assembly), criteria_routing.json (SHARED — coordinate with C, F).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scope-intent` in OVERLAY_IDS; overlay fires only when a ticket resolves from the trailer.
- [ ] assemble_diff reads the trailer (all ids) and assembles union scope context.
- [ ] A test proves base + other overlays receive NO ticket context (ticket-blind).
- [ ] A multi-ticket commit naming all its tickets produces no false scope-drift finding (eval).
- [ ] Overlay is advisory.

## Data-flow: commit message -> scope-intent overlay (resolves plan-review G6)
The trailer lives in the COMMIT MESSAGE, which is not part of the diff text, so it must be plumbed end-to-end (default "" everywhere → overlay simply does not fire when absent, per the AC):
- `assemble.py`: `assemble_diff_context(...)` gains `commit_message: str = ""`. It calls
  `extract_ticket_refs(commit_message)`; for each resolved trailer ticket it loads that ticket's
  scope/AC and assembles a UNION scope-context string, exposed as a SEPARATE context field consumed
  ONLY by the scope-intent overlay (base + other overlays stay ticket-blind — assert this).
- `assemble_diff_input` schema: add optional `commit_message`.
- `gates/code-review.yaml`: thread `commit_message` into the `assemble_diff` step; the scope-intent
  overlay's `ticket_context` includes the union scope-context.
- `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict(...)`: accept + forward `commit_message` (default "").
- Call sites (`shim.review_code`, `review_bot/voter.py`): pass the change's commit message when
  available (Gerrit change commit body), default "" otherwise.
scope-intent is content-triggered (fires only when ≥1 trailer ticket resolves) and ADVISORY.

## Per-overlay context injection (resolves plan-review G6, batch-runner tension)
CodeReviewBatchRunner today injects one shared `_context` (the diff) into every overlay (`batch_runner.py:58`). scope-intent needs a DIFFERENT ticket_context (the union ticket scope). Resolve by extending the batch runner, not by polluting the shared context:
- `CodeReviewBatchRunner.__init__` gains `context_overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None` (prompt_id ->
  ticket_context). In `run`, when an overlay's `prompt_id` is in `context_overrides`, inject that string
  as its `ticket_context`; every other overlay keeps the shared diff `_context` (base + others stay
  ticket-blind — assert it in a test).
- `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` builds `context_overrides={"code-review-scope-intent":
  <union_scope_context>}` ONLY when the commit-message trailers resolve ≥1 ticket (else omit → overlay
  inert), using the union-scope string assembled in assemble.py.
This is additive and default-None, so existing single-context behaviour is unchanged.
baseline.summary: Scope-intent overlay (diff vs union of trailer tickets)

## Context
The real ref-backed reconcile-check continuity test exposed that Mode inherits str. functools.total_ordering does not replace rich comparison methods inherited from str, so Mode.__gt__ remains lexical instead of rank-based. As a result Mode.BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE > Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK is false and check_phase_gate fails to block higher modes when the stored gate is reconcile-check.

## Approach
- Make every Mode rich comparison use the existing _ORDERED rank contract instead of inherited string lexical ordering.
- Preserve equality, enum values, MODE_CAPS, from_str, and the five-mode ordering.
- Extend the existing mode contract tests to exercise natural operators across the full five-mode order.
- Reuse the real ref-backed test on parent 2c87 to prove reconcile-check blocks a higher mode while allowing the equal target.

## Testing
Run the focused mode and advisory-lock suites, then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Mode rich comparisons follow reconcile-check < dry-run < bootstrap-strict < bootstrap-throttle < live for all operators.
- [x] The real ref-backed reconcile-check gate round trip blocks bootstrap-throttle and allows reconcile-check.
- [x] Existing mode strings, MODE_CAPS, from_str behavior, and legacy comparisons remain unchanged.
- [x] Focused tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Compatibility and rollback
This repairs the advertised rank semantics without changing persisted values or vocabulary. Reverting restores the lexical-comparison defect but does not require data migration.
baseline.summary: Fix rank ordering for str-backed reconciler modes

## Summary
Sub-effort (c) of story fatty-cipher-range. The event log is the wire format between clones running DIFFERENT rebar versions; declare it versioned and pin forward compatibility for unknown event types.

## Semantics decision (recorded — resolves the "preserved-and-ignored" ambiguity)
- "Ignored": replay skips unknown event_type values WITHOUT error (this is already the behavior — _processors.py:414 — pin it with a test, including that the ticket remains fully readable).
- "Preserved" means at the FILE level, not state level: unknown-type event FILES must survive untouched. The critical case is COMPACTION: rebar compact must NOT absorb or delete unknown-type events into a SNAPSHOT (else a newer clone's data is destroyed by an older clone's compaction). Verify what ticket-compact.sh does with unknown types today; if it absorbs/deletes them, THAT is the code fix in this ticket.
- NO new VERSION event type, no version negotiation. SCHEMA_VERSION constant in ticket_reducer (new _version.py or __init__) + version declaration in docs/event-schema.md.

## Suggested RED test
tests/interfaces/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py: write an event with event_type=FUTURE_TYPE into a ticket dir -> reduce_ticket succeeds, state readable; then run compaction over that ticket -> the FUTURE_TYPE event file still exists on disk afterward and replay still succeeds. RED if compaction destroys it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SCHEMA_VERSION constant + versioned docs/event-schema.md
- [ ] Unknown-type replay tolerance pinned by test
- [ ] Compaction proven (or fixed) to preserve unknown-type event files

## Summary

On 2026-09-01 the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on `rebar-gerrit` fail-closed reviews because root disk reached 91-95%; review clones/materializations hit ENOSPC and surfaced as `coverage-gap (review-error)`. Change 2481 exhausted its retry budget to a spurious LLM-Review -1. Recovery required manual `docker builder prune -f` without `--keep-storage`, proving automated prune could not reclaim below its 5GB build-cache floor. Operator approved implementing fixes A+B.

## Root cause

1. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` always runs `docker builder prune -f --keep-storage "$BUILD_CACHE_KEEP"`, even on acute pressure/no-op tick paths. At 5.244GB cache, automated prune freed ~0.
2. The review hot path starts clones/materializations without checking free disk first. `voter.py` clones into `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reviewbot-")` on the root temp volume; `repo_snapshot.py` materializes into the snapshot-store volume.

## Approved implementation plan

### A. Acute pressure reclaim tier

Keep normal warm-cache behavior unchanged. Add `DISK_PRESSURE_HARD_PCT` default 90, above soft `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80`. When root used-% is at/above hard threshold, `prune_docker_caches()` escalates BuildKit reclaim to `docker builder prune -f` with keep->0 (no `--keep-storage`), best-effort/non-fatal and `timeout 120` bounded like existing docker calls. Measure before/after root filesystem bytes and log bytes actually freed; success evidence is `bytes_freed > 0`, not invocation.

### B. Low-disk admission control

Add target-path free-space helper in `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` (`shutil.disk_usage(path)`) and `REBAR_GATE_MIN_FREE_GIB` default 2. This is a hard pre-clone admission floor; existing janitor watermarks remain cleanup targets.

Check target volume before cloning/materializing:

- In `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`, before `TemporaryDirectory` / `gc.clone_change_ref`, measure `tempfile.gettempdir()`.
- In `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` / `src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py`, measure the snapshot-store path before attested snapshot clone/materialize.

Represent low disk explicitly. Snapshot admission raises a dedicated `LowDiskError` (or returns an equivalent low-disk sentinel) with target path/free/floor. `gate_source.py` maps that condition into structured coverage as `coverage["low_disk"] = True` and preserves details; `adapter._coverage_gap_reason` gains a first branch `if coverage.get("low_disk"): return "low-disk"`. Do not let low disk fall through to generic `review-error`.

For the Gerrit voter pre-clone guard, synthesize a decision with `verdict="BLOCK"`, `gap_reason="low-disk"`, and first line `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (low-disk)] ...`. Define `_TAG_SUFFIXES["low-disk"] = "BLOCK — coverage-gap (low-disk)"`; add `low-disk` to `adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS`; keep `retrigger.py` parsing the existing `coverage-gap (<reason>)` grammar.

In `_handle_retryable_gap`, add explicit low-disk semantics. Under budget it defers vote-less like existing ADR 0069 retryable gaps. At/over the low-disk budget it returns `deferred_result` with a terminal status such as `deferred-exhausted`, `gap_reason="low-disk"`, writes/logs an operator-visible neutral Gerrit comment/status explaining low disk exhausted retry holdback and that a `recheck`/new patchset will retry after disk remediation, but leaves labels unchanged: no `LLM-Review -1`, no `append_retries_exhausted_note`, no `VOTER_ERROR`. This converges safely by making the change non-submittable due to missing LLM vote while avoiding a false code veto; explicit recheck/new patchset remains the recovery path after the host is healthy. Existing exhaustion behavior for non-low-disk review errors/coverage gaps is unchanged. Document in ADR 0069, ADR 0077, `docs/review-policy.md`, and `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Hard-pressure reclaim: root used-% >= `DISK_PRESSURE_HARD_PCT` with enough reclaimable build-cache excess causes emergency keep->0 builder prune, logs/measures `bytes_freed > 0`, and fixture returns below soft `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`; proof in `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py` and/or `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py`.
- [x] Warm-cache regression: below `DISK_PRESSURE_HARD_PCT`, `prune_docker_caches()` still uses `--keep-storage "$BUILD_CACHE_KEEP"`; proof in `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py`.
- [x] Review-bot low-disk admission: below `REBAR_GATE_MIN_FREE_GIB` on `tempfile.gettempdir()`, `voter.py` does not create the clone and defers retryably/vote-less through ADR 0069; proof by focused voter test asserting no clone/vote.
- [x] Exhausted low-disk budget: labels remain unchanged/no `LLM-Review -1`, with a neutral operator-visible exhausted-deferral result recoverable by recheck/new patchset; proof contrasts `low-disk` with `review-error` exhaustion.
- [x] Snapshot low-disk admission: below `REBAR_GATE_MIN_FREE_GIB` on the snapshot-store volume, materialization aborts before clone with `coverage["low_disk"]` -> `gap_reason="low-disk"`; proof around `repo_snapshot.py` / `gate_source.py` / adapter coverage routing.
- [x] Distinct semantics: literal suffix `BLOCK — coverage-gap (low-disk)` and routing tests distinguish low-disk from genuine coverage/review errors.
- [x] Portability: all reclaim/admission logic is in-process/operation-linked, with no CI-provider dependency.

## Testing / Verification

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest <focused low-disk review admission/voter tests> -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## File impact

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`; `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py`; `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_disk_pressure.py`; `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py`; `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`; `src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py`; `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`; `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`; `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py`; `docs/review-policy.md`; `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`; `docs/adr/0069-retryable-coverage-gap-bounded-deferral.md`; `docs/adr/0077-code-review-voter-four-pass-rewire.md`; focused tests.
baseline.summary: Disk-pressure reclaim cannot reach the build-cache floor under acute pressure, and the review clone path has no near-full admission control — review-bot fail-closes again

## What
The `mcp_registry` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` failed on the v0.7.1 tag (Actions run 28806482655): the MCP Registry validates that the PyPI package exists, and returned `PyPI package 'nava-rebar' not found (status: 404)` because it ran in the seconds right after the PyPI publish, before PyPI served the new version. A manual re-run of the failed job succeeded once PyPI had propagated.

## Why
A release must not require a human to notice the failure and re-run the job. The job should absorb the propagation lag itself.

## Fix (in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `mcp_registry` job)
- Before publishing, **poll PyPI** for the tagged version
  (`https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/<version>/json` until HTTP 200, bounded ~5 min)
  so the registry's package-ownership check resolves against a live version.
- Wrap `mcp-publisher publish` in a **bounded retry** (a few attempts with backoff)
  that is idempotency-safe: on a failed attempt, if the version is already present in
  the registry, treat it as success (so a retry after a partial publish does not fail).
- Derive the version from the tag (`${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v}` / `github.ref_name`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `mcp_registry` waits for PyPI to serve the tagged version before `mcp-publisher publish`.
- [ ] `mcp-publisher publish` is retried on failure with a bounded number of attempts and backoff.
- [ ] The retry treats an already-published version (present in the registry) as success.
- [ ] The workflow YAML parses (validated with a YAML loader).
- [ ] The change lands on main through Gerrit (LLM-Review + Verified green).
baseline.summary: release.yml: harden mcp_registry against PyPI-propagation race (wait + idempotent retry)

# S3 — Install gerrit-to-platform in the Gerrit container

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
`gerrit-to-platform` (g2p) is the bridge that `workflow_dispatch`es the GitHub Actions CI on
`patchset-created` / `comment-added` and is the production-proven Gerrit→GitHub-Actions pattern.
The Gerrit `hooks` plugin execs `$site/hooks/*` **from inside the container**, so g2p and its
Python interpreter MUST live in the container — a host-side g2p (hooks symlinked into a
bind-mount) is broken because the container process cannot resolve a host interpreter path.

## What
Extend the Gerrit image with Python ≥3.11 + g2p; enable the `hooks` + `replication` Gerrit
**core** plugins (bundled in `gerrit.war`; no external download/sha256 — unlike the non-core
`events-log`/`oauth`); establish the hook symlinks at container start; configure g2p. Record the
g2p adoption + in-container runtime decision as an ADR.

## Scope
- Extend the Gerrit image (`FROM gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`) — a Dockerfile under
  `infra/compose/` — with Python ≥3.11 + `pip install gerrit-to-platform`.
- Enable core plugins (`infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md`); container-start hook-symlink step;
  `gerrit_to_platform.ini` + `replication.config` symlink + `recheck → verify` mapping.
- New ADR. Depends on S2 (replication) + S4 (the PAT via the container-env secret path).
- Out of scope: the workflow (S5), credential provisioning internals (S4), the gate (S1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Extend the Gerrit image (`FROM gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`) with Python ≥3.11 +
      `pip install gerrit-to-platform`, so the in-container hook exec resolves its interpreter
      (host-side placement is rejected — the `hooks` plugin execs `$site/hooks/*` in the container).
- [ ] Enable the `hooks` + `replication` **core** plugins (from `gerrit.war` via `init
      --install-plugin` / copy — no download or sha256 pin) and list them in
      `infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md`.
- [ ] At container start, symlink the `patchset-created` / `comment-added` / `change-merged`
      console-script hooks into the volume-mounted `$site/hooks/`, pointing at the in-container g2p
      paths (image-build-time symlinks are shadowed by the volume mount).
- [ ] Write `gerrit_to_platform.ini` (GitHub PAT sourced via the container-env path from S4 —
      `fetch-secrets.sh` → compose `.env`; no plaintext on disk) + the `replication.config` symlink
      + the `recheck → verify` mapping.
- [ ] Coexistence proof: push a test patchset and observe BOTH the review-bot webhook `LLM-Review`
      vote AND the g2p `workflow_dispatch` fire on the same event.
- [ ] Write an ADR recording **g2p adoption** as the Gerrit→GitHub-Actions bridge + the
      in-container runtime decision.
baseline.summary: S3 — Install gerrit-to-platform on the Gerrit host

## Why
The plan-review gate shipped advisory-by-default with uniform thresholds
(block_threshold=0.95, default_posture=advisory for all 32 criteria) so it could
not block during calibration. We have now dogfooded enough to calibrate per-criterion
defaults from real data: 167 REVIEW_RESULT sidecars / 106 tickets / 1,329 findings.

## What
Derive per-criterion (default_posture, block_threshold) defaults from the dogfooded
REVIEW_RESULT corpus, using two reliability signals:
- Verifier-refutation (dense form): per-criterion `validity` distribution, P(dropped),
  P(indeterminate), and the per-binary-subquestion "no" profile. (The literal `dropped`
  outcome alone is too sparse — 18 total — so use continuous validity.)
- Voluntary revision-response: a material_fingerprint change between consecutive reviews
  of a ticket = a genuine revision. Exact finding-id survival is CONFOUNDED by finder
  text-churn (~100% false "resolution" for LLM criteria vs 13% for the one deterministic
  criterion P6), so attribute revisions at criterion-load-delta granularity, not exact id.
- Fire-rate denominator from coverage.routing (which criteria ran per review).

## Scope
1. Sidecar enrichment (APPROVED, must stay UX-invisible to library/MCP/CLI): persist
   fields that make the revision signal cleanly measurable going forward (normalized
   finding id + location), without changing the surfaced verdict shape.
2. Offline calibration analysis over the sidecars -> per-criterion reliability profile +
   proposed (posture, threshold).
3. Step 5 = INTERACTIVE review with the user for borderline / low-sample criteria
   (block vs advisory) — some may be clear blockers despite small n.
4. Apply agreed thresholds to src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json
   (block_threshold + default_posture per criterion; registry reads it directly).
5. Step 7 validation: run plan-review with the new thresholds on 20 randomly-sampled
   tickets that historically had high finding counts or overlay triggers. If any BLOCK,
   discuss with the user; otherwise the plan is approved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sidecar enrichment lands with a test proving the surfaced verdict (library/MCP/CLI
      return shapes) is byte-unchanged — enrichment is observability-only.
- [ ] A reproducible offline calibration script reads the sidecars and emits a
      per-criterion table: n, mean validity, P(dropped), P(indeterminate), revision-response
      (criterion-load-delta), fire-rate, and a proposed (posture, threshold).
- [ ] Step 5 interactive decision is recorded (which criteria flip to blocking and at what
      threshold, which stay advisory, and the rationale per criterion).
- [ ] criteria_routing.json updated to the agreed per-criterion defaults; lint + the
      plan-review unit tests pass.
- [ ] Step 7: 20 sampled tickets re-reviewed under the new thresholds; the block outcomes
      are reported. Zero unexpected blocks => approved; any block => discussed.
baseline.summary: Calibrate plan-review per-criterion block thresholds from dogfooded REVIEW_RESULT data
