## Context / Problem

Under heavy multi-session load (~20 concurrent rebar CLI processes sharing the one tracker), `rebar show airborne-wellloved-kingfisher` (epic 2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a, 23 children) produced ZERO output for >200 s across two attempts (killed at 75 s and 211 s), while `rebar list --parent 2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a` — a strictly larger payload (778.6 KB) — completed in ~67 s, and every invocation logged `rebar.llm.enrich_drain` gate-check overruns (339-3589 ms vs a 20 ms budget). Root cause is CONFIRMED (see the RCA comment, 2026-08-22): the default `rebar show` arm attaches `plan_review_health` (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:206), whose pin derivation calls, per plan-material pin, `current_material_fingerprint_impl` → `live_material_children` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:299) → `_reads.list_tickets(parent=<pin>)` → `reduce_all_tickets` — a FULL-STORE reduction per pin, ×4 for stale pins via `_legacy_material_ok` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:679). Measured on the real store (5247 tickets): 89 full-store scans, 466,983 single-ticket reduces, 745 s for ONE `plan_review_health` call; `list --parent` does exactly 1 scan (9.1 s in the same window). The enrich-drain gate overrun is a separate, bounded mechanism split out to 6148-5d81-8e80-41e8 (linked discovered_from).

## Approach

Collapse the O(pins × 4) full-store scans to one shared snapshot per derivation, without changing any verdict semantics. Add a ContextVar-scoped child-index snapshot to `rebar.llm.plan_review.relation_snapshot`: a context manager (`material_child_index()`) that, while active, makes `live_material_children` answer from a parent_id→children index built ONCE from a single unfiltered `_reads.list_tickets(include_archived=True, …)` pass (same `counts_as_plan_material_child` filtering as today, relation_snapshot.py:273-299, so per-parent results are byte-identical). Activation is idempotent (an outer context wins). `derive_plan_material_pin_health` (attest.py:54) opens the context around its `derive_health` call — covering the per-pin fingerprints AND the in-frame `_legacy_material_ok` recomputes — and `plan_review_health` (src/rebar/audit/read.py:58) opens it around the verify+compute_validity pair so the whole show-side derivation shares one snapshot. This fits the problem because the 89 scans are provably identical-argument `reduce_all_tickets` calls within one derivation (RCA experiment: 89 × 5247 = 466,983 reduces, exact); a bounded read-scoped snapshot also gives all pins one consistent store view instead of 89 slightly different ones. No caching survives the call; gates (claim/close/bugfix-size) keep their exact result contract and merely stop rescanning — all `compute_validity` callers consume the result dict only (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py:141, src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:244, src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:255, src/rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py:110). The test seam `attest.current_material_fingerprint` (monkeypatched by tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py, test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py) is untouched.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py — add the `material_child_index()` context
  manager + index-aware fast path in `live_material_children`.
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py — `derive_plan_material_pin_health` opens the context.
- src/rebar/audit/read.py — `plan_review_health` opens the context around its
  verify+compute_validity block.
- tests/unit/test_pin_health_store_scan_count.py — new regression test (RED first).

## Testing

RED-first regression test (tests/unit/test_pin_health_store_scan_count.py): build a scratch store (git init + `rebar.init_repo`, the tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py `repo` fixture pattern), create an epic with 4 children plus filler tickets, then call `compute_validity` with a constructed plan-review attestation carrying 1 pin vs 4 pins (all with non-matching fingerprints, forcing the ×4 legacy path) while counting `rebar._engine_support.reads.reduce_all_tickets` invocations via a monkeypatch wrapper. Failure path (today, RED): the 4-pin run performs strictly more full-store reductions than the 1-pin run (O(pins)). Happy path (after the fix, GREEN): both runs perform the same, constant number of full-store reductions, and per-pin `live_material_children` results are identical with and without the snapshot context (equality assertion — the no-drift check). Existing suites must stay green: tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py, tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py, tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Root cause confirmed via /rebar-debug (mechanism at file:line, discriminating experiment
      run, caused_by attributed) — DONE, recorded in the RCA comment (89-scan arithmetic match,
      faulthandler stacks, caused_by cb6b-24b4-1056-4ee6 linked).
- [x] The new scan-count test proves full-store reductions per `compute_validity` call do not
      grow with pin count (seen RED before the fix, GREEN after; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_pin_health_store_scan_count.py`).
- [x] `plan_review_health` on epic 2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a against the real store completes in the
      same order of magnitude as one `rebar list --parent 2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a` (checked by
      re-running the RCA's instrumented timing: scan count drops from 89 to ≤2, wall time from
      ~745 s to within ~10x of the single-scan list time in the same load window).
- [x] Verdict-preservation: tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py,
      tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py and
      tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py pass unchanged (checked by pytest).
- [x] The enrich-drain gate-check overrun has a recorded disposition: mechanism + rationale in
      this ticket's RCA comment, contract decision tracked in 6148-5d81-8e80-41e8
      (discovered_from-linked) — no silent steady state.
baseline.summary: rebar show stalls indefinitely on an epic under concurrent store load while list --parent completes

# Generic, config-driven mapping seam for per-project tracker workflow variance

## Context / Problem

rebar's reconciler hardcodes how its model maps onto a target Jira project's model, so a project whose workflow lacks an analogous concept cannot be supported without a core edit — the anti-pattern this epic exists to remove (core rebar must stay project-agnostic; a single project's states/types must never be named in shipped code). The mappings live in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` (`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`, `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `UNSYNCED_RELATIONS`) and are duplicated in `config.py` (`local_to_jira_status`, `jira_to_local_status`, `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`) and `inbound_fields.py` (`_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`, `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`). A live probe of the REB project (Jira Cloud) confirms the variance is real: REB has a `Blocked` status and an `Initiative` issue type at `hierarchyLevel` 2 above `Epic` at 1, and no `Supersedes` link type.

The felt need spans four target axes — **status, ticket type, permissible transitions, and permissible parent relationships** — plus two hardcoded sibling value axes (**link relations, priority**) and the **required-create-fields** gotcha that hard-fails `create` on a mandatory custom field.

## Approach

Introduce a **provider-neutral, config-driven mapping seam** read from hand-editable `rebar.toml`/`[tool.rebar]` config (rebar's config surface per `docs/config.md`), with the current hardcoded maps preserved as the **built-in default** (lowest precedence). Config is layered: built-in default → config `default` block → per-project overlay (`projects.<JIRA_KEY>`), deep-merged per key so an override changes only the keys it names. The seam is factored onto rebar's existing vendor-adapter boundary (`docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`, amended by `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md`; `_backend.py` `select_backend` / `OutboundMapper`/`InboundMapper`): a **provider-neutral core** owns the schema, the layered merge, fail-closed validation, the mapping-application semantics, and a **capability descriptor** (which axes a target has); a **Jira adapter** supplies the built-in defaults, the live probe, and the capability values. No other provider is built here; neutrality is structural, so a future adapter reuses the core untouched.

For target concepts with no analogue, the seam offers four provider-neutral answers, each building on existing rebar primitives (`rebar-status:` labels, `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`, the per-hop `transition_issue_by_name` call), while S6's replay algorithm itself is new code: **map** to a chosen value; **collapse** (non-injective, e.g. `epic→Initiative`) made round-trip-safe by a `rebar-type:` label symmetric with today's `rebar-status:` labels; **skip** (type-granular whole-ticket exclusion, extending `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`); or **drift** with a warning (unrepresentable statuses/transitions/parents diverge and are recorded, never silently forced). Non-allowed **transitions** additionally attempt **replay**: S6 adds **new** dispatcher logic that derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's **core STATUS event log** (per-ticket status-change events already persisted by the core; the reconciler stores no hop history of its own), anchors on Jira's current status, and re-attempts each intermediate hop through that existing single-hop primitive **exactly once each, in recorded order**, aborting to **drift** on the first hop the target rejects (no retries, no self-invented hops) — so replay is bounded by the finite recorded hop sequence. When no recorded trail survives — e.g. a **compacted** ticket whose STATUS events are folded into a snapshot that keeps only the final status — replay is not applicable and the failed transition degrades to the pre-S6 per-mutation soft-fail backstop (never inventing hops). Non-representable **parents** additionally leave an echo-safe **breadcrumb comment** naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key. rebar's own transitions and hierarchy are never restricted by a target's rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A project whose config declares no overrides syncs **byte-for-identical** to
  today's behavior — verified by the existing reconciler suite passing unchanged and a
  test asserting the composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants.
- [x] A per-project overlay changes only the keys it names, layering over the `default`
  block which layers over the built-in default — verified by a config-effect contrast
  test (default vs. overlaid value produce different observable outbound mappings).
- [x] Every mapping axis (status, type, link relation, priority) is driven by the
  config seam rather than a hardcoded literal, with the built-in default as fallback —
  verified by tests that a non-default config value reaches the outbound/inbound differ.
- [x] A rebar type with no target analogue can be **collapsed** (round-trip-safe via a
  `rebar-type:` label) or **skipped** (whole-ticket), and an unmapped-non-skipped type
  **fails closed at config load** — verified per child.
- [x] A non-allowed **transition** is attempted by **replay** of rebar's recorded hops
  and, failing that (or when no recorded trail survives, e.g. a compacted ticket),
  **drifts** — never restricting rebar's local
  transitions — verified per child.
- [x] A non-representable **parent** drifts and leaves an **echo-safe breadcrumb**
  naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key — verified per child.
- [x] Required-field create failures are prevented by a per-project
  `create_defaults` block — verified per child.
- [x] A `rebar bridge suggest-mapping` command interrogates a live target and emits
  suggested config for every offline-discoverable axis, flagging transitions as
  best-effort — verified per child.
- [x] `rebar doctor` detects Jira-compat config problems (offline validation failures
  and live-drift against the target) — verified per child.
- [x] The mapping core is **provider-neutral**: the schema, layered merge, validation,
  application semantics, and capability descriptor contain no Jira-specific literal;
  Jira specifics live only in the adapter — verified by a test that the core modules
  neither import the Jira adapter nor carry Jira value literals.

## Child decomposition (each criterion maps to ≥1 child; responsibilities do not overlap)

- **S1 — Config schema + layered-merge core + capability descriptor** delivers the
  provider-neutral foundation, layering, fail-closed validation framework, and the
  neutrality guarantee.
- **S2 — Status mapping via the seam** retires the three hardcoded status copies to the
  seam, default-preserving.
- **S3 — Type mapping: collapse + `rebar-type:` label + operator skip** delivers the
  no-analogue-type answers and load-time fail-closed on undecided types.
- **S4 — Link-relation mapping** retires
  `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`/`UNSYNCED_RELATIONS` (skip-not-approximate preserved).
- **S5 — Priority mapping + `create_defaults` injection** retires
  `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` to the seam (map-or-drift soft field) and injects
  per-project create_defaults to prevent required-field create failures.
- **S6 — Transition replay** adds a **new** direct→replay→drift fallback to the
  dispatcher, deriving the hop sequence from the core per-ticket STATUS event log
  (drift when that trail is absent, e.g. compaction).
- **S7 — Parent breadcrumb comment** adds the echo-safe nearest-represented-ancestor
  breadcrumb on parent drift.
- **S8 — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping` command** interrogates a live target and emits
  suggested config (the verb is `suggest-mapping`, not `probe`, which collides with the
  retired `bridge-probe` alias).
- **S9 — Docs + `project.portability`** documents the seam + portability guard.
- **S10 — Jira-compat config diagnostics in `doctor`** detects offline-invalid config
  and live-drift.
baseline.summary: Generic, config-driven mapping seam for per-project tracker workflow variance (Jira first)

baseline.description:
## Summary

Extend the attestation-reuse pattern (already implemented for the completion-verification close gate) to the **code-review** gate, and make reuse **identity-scoped**: an environment must reuse a stored review/completion attestation ONLY when that attestation was minted by the SAME signing identity the environment itself signs with. As part of this, evaluate extracting a **shared reuse seam** that both the completion gate and the code-review gate call, instead of two parallel implementations.

Discovered while implementing standalone completion-verifier recording + close-time reuse (`transition_close.record_completion_verdict` + `close_autoresume._reusable_attested_pass`).

## Motivation

- Completion verification already supports: a standalone `verify-completion` run RECORDS a
  signed `completion-verifier` op-cert on the ticket, and a later same-`--ref` close REUSES it
  instead of firing a duplicate (billable) verifier run
  (`close_autoresume._reusable_attested_pass`). Code review (`review-code` / the code-review
  gate) has no equivalent reuse, so identical reviews are re-run across environments.
- Reuse across environments with DIFFERENT signing certificates is unsafe. Example: a
  developer-local `review-code` signs with a local key; the AWS review bot signs with a
  distinct certificate. The AWS bot must NOT treat the local attestation as its own — reuse
  must require that the stored attestation's signing identity matches the CONSUMING
  environment's configured signing identity. Otherwise one environment silently inherits
  another's trust boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The code-review gate reuses a still-current, same-`ref` code-review attestation instead
      of re-running the LLM review, mirroring `close_autoresume._reusable_attested_pass`
      (stricter than validity-on-read: explicit authenticated SHA + material fingerprint that
      still match the review input; legacy/malformed/stale/unreadable → full review).
- [ ] Reuse (for BOTH completion and code-review) is IDENTITY-SCOPED: a stored attestation is
      reused only when its signing identity (the op-cert principal / key fingerprint) equals the
      consuming environment's configured signing identity. A mismatch (e.g. local cert vs. AWS
      bot cert) falls through to a fresh signed run under the consuming environment's own
      identity. This is covered by a test that seeds an attestation under identity A and proves
      an environment configured with identity B does NOT reuse it.
- [ ] A DESIGN DECISION is recorded (ADR or ticket comment) on whether to extract a shared
      reuse seam consumed by both gates. If extracted, both the completion close gate and the
      code-review gate call it, with no behavior change to the existing completion reuse (its
      current tests still pass); if NOT extracted, the rejection rationale is documented.
- [ ] Standalone `review-code` RECORDS its result on the ticket (signs the reusable
      code-review attestation on an attested pass + emits the sidecar), symmetric with
      standalone `verify-completion` and `review-plan`, gated by an explicit opt-out
      (`--no-sign`) and never signing a `local`/uncertifiable verdict.
- [ ] Portability preserved: reuse and identity-scoping have an operation-linked / in-process
      basis and are not tied to any single CI provider (`project.portability`).

## Notes / pointers

- Completion reuse consumer: `src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py`
  (`_reusable_attested_pass`).
- Completion recording producer: `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`
  (`record_completion_verdict`, `sign_completion_verdict`).
- Identity/attestation internals: `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py`, `src/rebar/signing.py`,
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (`_authoritative_*`, `current_material_fingerprint`).
- Code-review gate: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/`, MCP/CLI `review-code`.
- The identity check likely reads the op-cert principal/key-fingerprint from the signed DSSE
  predicate and compares to the environment's resolved signing binding (see the op-cert service
  startup binding, `opcert_service/`).
baseline.summary: Identity-scoped attestation reuse for the code-review gate (shared reuse seam)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`import rebar` callers get a return value, not a terminal, so the first-class way to raise a non-fatal warning is Python's **`warnings`** subsystem (not `logging`, which the brainstorm rejected). This story emits a `warnings.warn` of a dedicated category from single-ticket library functions when the detector fires. Depends on the merged detector (`cross_session_warning_for`) and reducer clearing: a ticket not `in_progress` has no holder, so the detector returns `None` and nothing is emitted.

## Approach

Add a new module `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` defining `class CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)` and a best-effort helper `emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None)`, and re-export the category as `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` so callers can filter/escalate it. The module also exposes a `suppress_cross_session_warning()` context manager (holds the same guard) so an outer surface that already advises stops the library channel from doubling it.

The helper mirrors the CLI's `_maybe_warn_cross_session`: it calls the merged detector `cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` and, on a non-`None` string, calls `warnings.warn(msg, CrossSessionWarning)`; on `None` it does nothing. Two properties:

- **Best-effort — never breaks the call.** The body is wrapped in
  `try/except Exception: pass`; the operation always proceeds, no warning on failure.
- **Re-entrancy-guarded.** The detector (`_commands/cross_session.py`) itself calls public
  `show_ticket`, so a naive emit on `show_ticket` would recurse. A module-level
  `contextvars.ContextVar` (`_EMITTING`, default `False`) makes the helper a no-op while an
  emit is in progress (returns if set, else sets/runs/resets in `finally`), so exactly one
  warning fires per top-level call. The detector is **not** modified.

Each single-ticket public entry point calls `emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` **before** returning (for writes, before the mutation, so the holder is read pre-mutation — matching CLI/MCP). **No return type changes.** Covered public functions (from `src/rebar/__init__.py`) are enumerated per file in Scope; `quality_check` is **out of scope** — absent from the CLI allowlist, deferred on MCP (S4).

`link`/`unlink` warn for the **primary endpoint `id1`** only, matching CLI (S3)/MCP (S4). Bulk reads (`list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`, `next_batch`) do **not** warn. `claim` raises `ConcurrencyError` on an `in_progress` ticket before any warning path.
### Surface layering (single-emit dedup)

The CLI and MCP surfaces call these same library functions, so a naive library emit doubles the advisory each already carries (CLI stderr `WARN:`; MCP `cross_session_warning` field). Dedup keeps exactly one advisory per operation per surface:

- **CLI** (`src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py`) — `execute()` runs `_maybe_warn_cross_session` (the
  allowlist single source) **and** handler dispatch inside `suppress_cross_session_warning()`,
  so the library `CrossSessionWarning` is suppressed and the CLI's `WARN:` line is the only
  CLI advisory.
- **MCP** (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) — `build_server()` registers read/write tools through
  `suppress_library_double_advisory(mcp)` (in `_lib_warn.py`), a proxy that runs each tool
  handler (sync + `async`) inside `suppress_cross_session_warning()`, so the response field is
  the only MCP advisory WITHOUT a process-global filter (which would over-silence the library
  `CrossSessionWarning` for unrelated `import rebar` callers sharing the server process).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` (**new**) — `CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)`, best-effort
  re-entrancy-guarded `emit_cross_session_warning`, `suppress_cross_session_warning`, and the
  `suppress_library_double_advisory(mcp)` MCP proxy (scopes suppression per tool handler).
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — re-export `CrossSessionWarning` (import + `__all__`).
- `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py` — emit in `show_ticket`, `deps`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — emit in `transition` (before the mutation); `reopen`
  delegates to it, so it does not emit separately (no double warning).
- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` — emit in `comment`, `edit_ticket`, `link` (`id1`),

- `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` — emit in `set_file_impact`, `declare_no_file_impact`,

- `src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py` — hold `suppress_cross_session_warning()` across detection +

- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` — `build_server()` wraps read/write tool registration with the
  `suppress_library_double_advisory` proxy (scoped per-handler suppression; no global filter).
- `src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py` — `cross_session_warning_for` reads the config toggle
  and acting session BEFORE the `show_ticket` reduce, short-circuiting (skipping the reduce and
  cache write) when the feature is disabled or the session is unknown.
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — document `rebar.CrossSessionWarning`.
- `tests/unit/test_cross_session_lib.py` (**new**) — the library-surface oracle.
- `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` — refresh for the new `CrossSessionWarning` export.

Tier: **in-process unit test** with stdlib `warnings` capture (`pytest.warns` / `catch_warnings(record=True)`). Real temporary tracker; acting session via `REBAR_SESSION_ID` (monkeypatch). Claim as holder A, then act as B.

- B vs A-held: `show_ticket` and `comment` each emit one warning naming A; write applies.
- Write + two-endpoint: `transition` and `link` (holder A on `id1`) each emit one for `id1`.
- Negative control (same session A): none. Bulk (`list_tickets`/`ready` as B): none.
- Unset `REBAR_SESSION_ID`: none. Category is `isinstance(..., CrossSessionWarning)`.
- Re-entrancy: exactly one per top-level `show_ticket`. Best-effort: detector raises -> call

  2=double); reopen delegates to transition (one). CLI dedup: one `WARN:` per command.

- [x] Same-session A negative control emits none; `list_tickets()`/`ready()` as B emit none.
- [x] With `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits none.
- [x] The emitted warning is `isinstance(..., rebar.CrossSessionWarning)` (subclass of

- [x] Re-entrancy: one `CrossSessionWarning` per top-level `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` despite

- [x] Best-effort: when `cross_session_warning_for` raises, the library call returns normally

- [x] Single-emit dedup: a warning CLI command (e.g. `link`) writes exactly one `WARN:` line,
  not doubled by the library channel (`test_cross_session_cli.py` `count(...) == 1`).

Run the ADR-0036-mandated version-segmented threshold replay for the plan-v2 impact model ("calibration 3") and adjudicate current blocking thresholds against it. Calibration 2 (2026-07-08) lowered six criteria 0.70->0.60 adjudicated against the OLD mean impact model; the plan-v2 severity-first MAX model with the 0.85 hard-override floor (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py::impact_plan) shipped the same day and has never been replayed. The block-rate rise (~25% pre-cal-2 to 52-67% after) was measured in the d195 calibration analysis and is recorded in the comments of ticket 0730-6ceb-88c3-430c (analysis task) and epic d195's evidence trail - that analysis is the grounded source for the motivation numbers. This ticket produces the evidence base; threshold changes are applied here only if the replay warrants them per the decision rule below. The dependent floor-split story that consumes this ticket's AC4 evidence is large-sleepful-needlefish (7d91-55fc-e07c-4101), already linked depends_on this ticket.

## What
- Corpus pre-check (already performed, recorded here for reproducibility): the sidecar corpus at .tickets-tracker/*/*-REVIEW_RESULT.json holds 2059 sidecars: 1007 tagged impact_model_version=plan-v2, 835 untagged (pre-tagging), 150 code-v3, 67 code-v2. GO/NO-GO floor: proceed iff the plan-v2 segment has >=500 sidecars AND >=5 non-DET criteria reach the script's MIN_N=25 finding floor; otherwise stop and record a low-power decision on this ticket. (The >=500 pre-check already passes; MIN_N coverage is confirmed from the replay output itself.)
- Extend docs/experiments/calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py so load() counts skipped sidecars by reason (different-version vs untagged) and main() prints the skipped remainder alongside the segment size - the script currently discards non-matching sidecars silently, so AC1's "skipped remainder" needs this counter. Land this script change (plus the calibration record, below) via Gerrit.
- Run `python docs/experiments/calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py --impact-model-version plan-v2` from the main checkout (where .tickets-tracker lives) and record its full output as a comment on this ticket.
- Adjudicate each non-DET blocking-tier criterion (current tiers: 0.60 for the six cal-2 criteria; 0.70 for T1, T8, G1G2; 0.75 for E4) against the replay proposal using this decision rule: (a) script class LOW-DATA (n<25) -> KEEP current, record low-data; (b) script class FP-PRONE (mean validity <0.45 or P(indeterminate)>0.20) -> DEMOTE to advisory OR raise threshold to >=0.90, choose and record which; (c) script class BLOCK-ELIGIBLE -> adopt max(0.5, p90 rounded to nearest 0.05) when it differs from the current threshold by >=0.05 in either direction (this is the raise path when p90 > current+0.05 and the lower path when p90 < current-0.05), else KEEP; (d) script class ADVISORY-KEEP on a currently-blocking criterion -> KEEP threshold but record the borderline signals for calibration 4. Every decision cites the criterion's replay row (n, validity, rev_rr, p90, fire rate).
- Record the adjudication durably: append a "Calibration 3 (plan-v2 segmented replay)" section to docs/experiments/plan-review-threshold-calibration.md with the replay table, per-criterion decisions, and rationale - landed in the same Gerrit change as the script counter (and any warranted criteria_routing.json threshold edits). The edit target for threshold values is src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (NOT src/rebar/llm/criteria/, which holds only the resolver machinery).
- Floor-attribution analysis for the dependent story: over the plan-v2 segment's decision==block findings, recompute impact_plan from each finding's persisted verification.severity_attributes with the hard-override floor disabled; a block is "floor-driven" iff the floorless impact falls below the finding's persisted block_threshold while the floored impact met it. Report the floor-driven count/share overall and for ac_unverifiable-bearing findings specifically. Classify the ac_unverifiable!=none floor-driven findings' finding text into missing_oracle (text asserts no verification method exists) / underspecified_oracle (text demands a more specific command, file, or expected value for a check that exists) / ambiguous, classifying all of them when <=100 else a seed-42 random sample of 100, and report all three proportions. Record this as a comment on story 7d91-55fc-e07c-4101.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A comment on this ticket records the segmented replay's full output including the segment's sidecar/ticket/finding counts AND the skipped-remainder counts by reason (different-version vs untagged), produced by the extended script.
- [ ] A comment on this ticket records the adjudication: every non-DET blocking-tier criterion mapped from current threshold to a KEEP/RAISE/LOWER/DEMOTE decision via the decision rule above, each citing its replay row signals.
- [ ] The Gerrit change containing the script skipped-counter and the "Calibration 3" section of docs/experiments/plan-review-threshold-calibration.md (plus criteria_routing.json threshold edits iff the adjudication warrants any; the no-change case is stated explicitly in that doc section) is MERGED (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
- [ ] A comment on story 7d91-55fc-e07c-4101 records the floor-attribution analysis: floor-driven block count/share (overall and ac_unverifiable-specific) and the missing_oracle/underspecified_oracle/ambiguous proportions with the sample-size rule stated above.

baseline.description: Discovered during 2dcb-5468. The runaway guard correctly aborts a genuine loop of identical repeated read_file calls (24x in the incident), but nothing steers the model to STOP re-reading before the abort: agent_call.py memo returns cached content plus a passive nudge, cache-hit repeats are not counted toward the runaway window, and no ModelRetry-style hard steer is raised on the Nth identical call. The run burns its budget and truncates its evidence bank, and a fresh re-run can loop again, hurting exit-11 re-run convergence. OSS pydantic-ai practice: raise ModelRetry/ToolFailed on repeated identical tool calls; UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit); prepare_tools/tool_choice=none for tool-free finalization on budget exhaustion. Separate hardening from the 2dcb-5468 misclassification fix; reduces loop frequency / improves convergence but not required for that fault's correctness.
baseline.summary: Runaway/duplicate read_file loop in completion verifier is not steered to stop

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py` module docstring only;

## Context

A related-material pin can be rejected as stale solely because the fingerprint algorithm changed, even though the related ticket's material did not. Historical pin 6b113a084820af9d exactly matches the post-330c/pre-2be7 recomputation of the current prerequisite, while the latest generation yields bbe91c054a677441.

## Proven root cause

`pin_health.derive_health` compares pins only with the latest fingerprint. The plan-review wrapper supplies no compatibility check, although `attest._legacy_material_ok` already recognizes both supported historical full-hash generations for the subject's own material. The prerequisite had no post-review events; wrong-target and genuine-material-drift rivals were rejected. An unmatched hash control remains stale.

Original epic `jira-reb-1160` defines actual related-material drift as the invalidation boundary. Story `convulsive-calx-yearling` requires recovery when review-time related material remains current. `ethnogenic-forbidden-umbrette` requires genuine dependency edits to invalidate unconditionally.

## Repair plan

- Extend related-pin health with a narrowly scoped compatibility predicate supplied by the attestation layer.
- Classify a mismatched latest fingerprint as current only when recomputing the current related ticket under a supported historical full-fingerprint generation exactly matches the signed pin.
- Preserve current-fingerprint reporting, malformed/missing classifications, enforcement semantics, and genuine unmatched drift.
- Add a held-out ephemeral-store unit oracle at the real attestation-to-pin-health seam.

## Testing

- Run `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_generation_3e0f.py tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_health.py tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_health_heldout.py`.
- Run `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An unchanged related ticket pinned with the post-330c/pre-2be7 fingerprint is classified current, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_generation_3e0f.py`.
- [x] A semantic edit makes that same historical pin stale, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_generation_3e0f.py`.
- [x] An arbitrary unmatched valid hash remains stale, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_material_pin_generation_3e0f.py`.
- [x] Latest-generation, malformed, missing, advisory, and enforced health behavior remains compatible, checked by the focused pin-health suite.
- [x] The held-out oracle is RED before the fix, GREEN after the fix, and RED again when historical compatibility is removed.

## Context / Problem
Code review currently combines workflow-authored built-in criteria with an unconditional project Round-A fan-in and packaged-only overlay/detector selection. This ignores effective disables/retunes, omits activated project DET criteria, ignores project file applicability and explicit dollar budgets, and aborts without partial results when one criterion fails. The approved RP-06 policy corrects these behaviors while preserving hard-won code-review topology and output contracts.

## Approach
Add a code-review strategy adapter that compiles `DiscoveryStagePlan` units from the immutable `CriteriaSnapshot` delivered by S1 and executes them through the shared kernel delivered by S2. Round A keeps the base reviewer and each selected built-in/project criterion exactly once. Project LLM criteria select by effective globs; effective disabled or non-applicable criteria execute zero times with stored reason provenance. Project DET criteria remain outside the LLM fan-in and execute through the detector selector from the same snapshot. Round B remains the existing one-hop, capped base-reviewer recommendation path.

Preserve the authored `code-review.yaml` topology, base-reviewer summary/recommendations payload, per-overlay context overrides, prompt contracts, model-ladder resolution, sequential scheduling, and absence of code-review checkpoints. Code review retains no implicit dollar cap; every positive authored `usd_budget` is enforced and shed units are recorded. Zero remains schema-invalid.

After RP-01 exhausts one local criterion call, retain successes and continue independent criteria. A real blocking finding wins `BLOCK`; otherwise missing blocking-capable coverage returns unsigned `INDETERMINATE`; advisory-only missing coverage may still `PASS`. Systemic configuration/provider setup and cancellation behavior remains fail-safe. Persist the versioned safe discovery trace in the internal code-review journal/sidecar, never in the normal review response or status projection.

During expand-contract, compute the legacy and new deterministic projections from the same calls and record comparison mismatches without issuing duplicate model calls. Approved differences are limited to effective disable/retune, project DET inclusion, project applicability, explicit budget enforcement, and the approved partial-failure verdict policy.

## Testing
Use real workflow producer-to-consumer tests with a stateful fake only at the external model boundary. The oracle is the final typed verdict, exact selected call ids/order, internal trace, and unchanged public response shape. Negative controls pin the base reviewer, one-hop Round B, sequential execution, no checkpoint writes, and no-project-overlay behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A docs-only diff skips a project criterion scoped to `src/**`, while a matching diff runs it exactly once in Round A; both outcomes are recorded internally without adding trace fields to the review response.
- [x] Effective built-in disable/retune and activated project DET fixtures drive actual code-review selection from one snapshot rather than packaged routing.
- [x] Base-reviewer summary/recommendations, one-hop capped Round B, per-overlay context, model/mode, sequential order, authored YAML topology, and no-checkpoint behavior match the pre-cutover contract when no approved delta applies.
- [x] A positive authored `usd_budget` sheds over-budget units before calls, omission stays uncapped, and zero is rejected by workflow validation.
- [x] With one exhausted local failure, later independent criteria execute and earlier successes survive; dependency-blocked units skip, blocking-capable missing coverage yields `INDETERMINATE` unless a real block exists, and advisory-only missing coverage may pass.
- [x] Systemic setup/configuration failure and cancellation stop remaining work with exact usage accounting and no signed or hollow pass.
- [x] Shadow contract tests use one observed call set and report no differences outside the approved delta allowlist; code-review response and status schemas remain narrow and backward-compatible.
baseline.summary: RP-06 S3 — Cut code review over to effective shared discovery

## Summary

`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref origin/main` resolves the ref MORE THAN ONCE during a close. If `origin/main` advances between the verification step and the signing step, completion verification PASSES against the first sha and the signer then REFUSES to attest, because the state it is asked to sign has drifted from the state that was verified.

The close SUCCEEDS. The ticket reaches `closed` with `class` recorded and no error is printed. What is silently missing is the completion-verifier attestation.

## Observed

Closing `cutprice-untameable-stork` (326f-595a-088b-40a5):

- verification ran against `6fe5c0d54574`
- `origin/main` advanced to `d44bd253ee44` mid-run
- verification PASSED; the signer refused the drifted state
- result: `status=closed`, `close_class=preexisting`, **no completion-verifier signature**

Nothing in the output flags the gap. It is only visible if you go looking for the attestation.

## Why it matters

The attestation is the durable evidence that a close was earned rather than asserted. A close that passes verification but silently loses its signature is indistinguishable, after the fact, from one that was never verified — which is precisely the property the gate exists to provide.

The window is not narrow in practice: a completion-verified close takes 9-11 minutes, and on a repo with active CI and multiple agents `origin/main` moves several times an hour. This session alone moved main a dozen times.

## Mechanism (hypothesis — not yet proven)

Two independent resolutions of the same symbolic ref, with a multi-minute LLM verification between them. A single resolve-once-then-reuse would remove the race. I have NOT read the close path to confirm where the second resolution happens; whoever picks this up should.

## Workaround, and why it is not a fix

Pass an immutable sha:

    SHA=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
    rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --class <c> --ref "$SHA"

That works, but it requires every caller to know the hazard. The documented guidance and the tool's own help present `--ref origin/main` as ordinary usage, and the CLI close gate's DEFAULT (worktree HEAD) has the same shape — a HEAD that moves mid-run would race identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A symbolic `--ref` is resolved ONCE at the close boundary and the resolved sha REPLACES
      the argument, so verification, snapshot materialisation, the drift guard and signing all
      see the same immutable commit (`_pin_completion_ref`, `transition_close.py:135`, rebound
      by the caller at `:618`).
- [x] If the verified and signing shas ever disagree, the close emits a loud stderr warning
      naming BOTH shas and the exact remediation, and refuses to attest stale state
      (`transition_close.py:402-411`).
      OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: a warning is SUFFICIENT. The close is deliberately NOT
      required to exit non-zero, because that would change the contract for every existing
      caller (scripts, the library facade, and the MCP surface all expect exit 0 today). The
      original wording asked the close to FAIL; it warns and succeeds, and that is accepted.
      Note the drift branch is now near-unreachable: the pin removes the symbolic-ref split,
      and 4de6 already pinned the default HEAD target.
- [x] A close that cannot obtain an attestation says so on stderr, naming the cause and how to
      certify. The machine-readable `completion_signature` marker is already present on the
      library, JSON and MCP surfaces. The residual — the default CLI *text* output on stdout
      not inspecting that marker — is tracked separately as `faulty-floppy-kob`
      (`4c28-0883-bf98-424b`), filed from this investigation.
- [x] A regression test drives a close with `--ref` advancing MID-RUN and asserts the close
      lands SIGNED and bound to the verified tree
      (`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_symbolic_ref_pins_3e21.py`); seeding the defect
      back returns it to RED.

## Found by

A close performed during this session; the missing signature was noticed only because the closing agent checked for it explicitly. Recorded because the failure is silent by construction.
baseline.summary: Close gate races on a moving --ref: verification passes at one sha, signing refuses at another

Importing `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` fails at line ~38 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler.outbound_comments'`, surfacing as a pytest COLLECTION ERROR on `tests/scripts/reducer/test_managed_refs.py` during a full-suite run. Discovered while landing the open-bugs batch (reducer-cache / linter / perf / reconcile-test fixes).

## Reproduction Steps

1. Fresh venv on current main: `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e '.[dev]'`.
2. `.venv/bin/pytest tests/scripts/reducer/test_managed_refs.py -q` (or a full-suite run).

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** the module imports and the test collects/runs (or skips) cleanly.
- **Actual:** `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler.outbound_comments'` raised from `outbound_differ.py`, erroring the whole test module at collection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `import rebar_reconciler.outbound_differ` succeeds (no ModuleNotFoundError) on a fresh install from main.
- [x] The symbols the importer needs (e.g. `_normalize_comment_body`) resolve to their real definition location; the import points at the correct module.
- [x] `tests/scripts/reducer/test_managed_refs.py` collects and runs (passes/skips) rather than erroring at import.
- [x] A regression test guards the import/collection so the breakage cannot silently recur.
- [x] No regression in `tests/scripts/reducer/`.
baseline.summary: outbound_differ imports a missing rebar_reconciler.outbound_comments module (collection error in test_managed_refs)

## Summary

Found by the Step 7 (Axis 1 construct) sibling sweep while fixing `satiated-activated-aardwolf` (5524-e353-2e2d-4dbe). Same detect-only drift class as `CONFIG_PATHS`, but on the gerrit deploy-key materializer, which was overlooked when `materialize-g2p-config.sh` was added to `CONFIG_PATHS`.

`infra/gerrit/materialize-deploy-key.sh` is an SSM→file materializer (it puts the replication deploy key into the gerrit user's dir), a direct sibling of `infra/gerrit/materialize-g2p-config.sh`. `materialize-g2p-config.sh` IS enumerated in `CONFIG_PATHS` (detect-only, `reason=config_manual`); `materialize-deploy-key.sh` is in **no** manifest. So a merged change to the deploy-key materializer rsyncs to `/opt/rebar` and silently does nothing — the same drift class `CONFIG_PATHS` detect-only was created to make visible.

## Class-level plan (PRIMARY ticket for the manifest-omission class)

This ticket is the primary for a ONE class-level change fixing both confirmed instances of the class "an infra SOURCE that affects the running environment is absent from every path manifest in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, so a merged change to it drifts silently". The change touches ONLY `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (two manifest additions) plus the new/extended regression tests. Sibling ticket `5d4c-a25b-b612-4aca` (broke-choleric-hound) is fixed in the same change.

Both instances proven at runtime with a discriminating contrast against the sibling source that IS in the manifest (see RCA comments on each ticket).

## Acceptance criteria (both instances are criteria)

- [ ] **Instance 1 (this ticket, DETECT-ONLY):** `infra/gerrit/materialize-deploy-key.sh` is enumerated in `CONFIG_PATHS` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, so a deploy-key-materializer-only change emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=config_manual` (parity with `materialize-g2p-config.sh`). Applying it touches gerrit — the same operator-judgement boundary as the rest of `CONFIG_PATHS` — so signal only, no auto-reload.
- [ ] **Instance 2 (sibling 5d4c, APPLY-PARITY):** `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` is enumerated in `MCP_PATHS`, so an entrypoint-source-only change rebuilds the MCP image via the EXISTING blue-green mcp deploy path (ADR 0079 v1 mcp auto-apply scope; reuse the existing path exactly — no new apply semantics).
- [ ] RED→GREEN regression test per instance (held out from the fixer), mirroring `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py` (instance 1) and `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` (instance 2), each shown RED first and with mutation teeth (empty the manifest entry → back to RED).
- [ ] `observability.sh` already counts the `config_manual` signal (it counts every `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {` regardless of reason) — verified, no observability change needed.
- [ ] `make lint` (incl. shellcheck) + full `tests/scripts` suite green.

## Structural guard (decided separately — NOT in this change)

A structural manifest-completeness guard for this class is being evaluated separately and is intentionally out of scope here. This change closes the two confirmed instances; any further same-class instances found are enumerated in the final report, not filed, per the sweep-containment directive.

## Evidence

- `CONFIG_PATHS='… infra/gerrit/materialize-g2p-config.sh …'` includes the g2p materializer but NOT `materialize-deploy-key.sh`.
- `grep -oE "^[A-Z_]+_PATHS='[^']*'" infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh | grep materialize-deploy-key` → no match.
- Runtime: deploy-key-materializer-only change → NO signal; g2p-materializer-only change → `config_manual` fires.

## Context / Problem
A container ticket (epic/story with children) rarely declares its own `file_impact`, so its plan-review attestation's signed dependency set is empty and the code-drift gate falls back to whole-HEAD invalidation (ADR 0002 decision 5): ANY commit — however unrelated — invalidates the container's attestation, forcing a re-review or drift-refresh on every merge. This is the container-scale form of the over-invalidation ADR 0002 was written to fix, and a real gate-economics drag under the parallel epic/child workflow where the base ref moves constantly.

The scope a container plan actually reasons about is its children's declared scope. The invalidation lattice for inheritance already exists: `material_fingerprint` (pass1.py:551) hashes a ticket's description + file_impact + child ids, and a container review pins each DIRECT child's material fingerprint into the signed manifest — so a child editing its file_impact (or a child being added/removed) already invalidates the container's attestation via pin/material drift, forcing a re-review that recomputes any inherited union. Inheritance therefore cannot go silently stale one level deep. It does NOT hold for grandchildren (a child's fingerprint covers grandchild IDS only, not grandchild file_impact), which is why inheritance is DIRECT CHILDREN ONLY — deeper drift is covered by the deeper tickets' own attestations, mirroring the review model (reviews pin direct dependencies; dependency-order review covers each tier).

Depends on 72d9-8fbd (athletic-esthetical-polecat) landing first: before that fix, scoped dependency sets are inert in attested mode, so giving containers a non-empty set would move them OFF the only working invalidation (whole-HEAD) onto a broken path.

## Approach
1. In `dependency_hashes` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py): when the reviewed ticket
   has children, compute the candidate union = own `file_impact` ∪ review citations ∪ the
   union of DIRECT children's `file_impact`. Apply the POISON RULE: if any non-closed direct
   child has an empty `file_impact`, do NOT inherit — keep the pre-change set (own ∪
   citations; empty ⇒ whole-HEAD fallback), preserving fail-closed for undeclared scope.
   Closed children neither contribute files nor poison (their work is delivered; ADR 0024's
   completion floor deliberately stops re-litigating it, and their files' later churn belongs
   to other tickets). NO new store reads: the orchestrator already fetches every direct
   child whole (`orchestrator.assemble_context` -> `ctx.children`, each carrying status and
   file_impact), so thread that list through as an optional parameter —
   `_run_plan_review` passes `ctx.children` to `attest.sign_plan_review(children=...)`,
   which forwards to `dependency_hashes(children=...)` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py
   and attest.py gain the threading; manifest.py consumes it). This also avoids any
   tickets-root ambiguity in attested mode (the child states were read from the pinned
   ticket snapshot by the same review run). `children=None` (default — e.g. the resign
   recovery path, which has no assembled context) means NO inheritance: the dep set stays
   the pre-change own-impact ∪ citations, which is the conservative direction (an empty set
   falls back to whole-HEAD invalidation), and the drift-refresh path re-hashes the PRIOR
   signed dep set so an inherited scope survives refresh unchanged.
2. Extend P9 (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py, `p9_file_impact_coverage`): containers
   currently auto-pass. Keep passing when inheritance is effective (every non-closed direct
   child declares file_impact, and there is at least one). Surface an ADVISORY (never
   blocking) on a container whose inheritance is poisoned, naming the children with empty
   file_impact, so authors see exactly why the epic stays on whole-HEAD invalidation. Leaf
   behavior unchanged.
3. Document: docs/plan-review-gate.md (scoped-drift paragraph: containers inherit direct
   children's declared impact under the poison rule) and a short amendment note in
   docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md decision 5.
Rejected: recursive (whole-subtree) inheritance — the pin lattice only self-heals one level deep, so a grandchild file_impact edit would leave a recursively-computed union silently stale. Rejected: inheriting a partial union when some children lack file_impact — that flips the empty-set fallback from fail-closed to fail-open for exactly the undeclared portion.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py (dependency_hashes + a small child-union helper)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py (thread
  ctx.children through sign_plan_review into dependency_hashes; no new store reads)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py (P9 container extension)
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py
- tests/unit/test_plan_review.py (the existing P9 unit tests pin the old container auto-pass
  and must be updated to the new container semantics)
- docs/plan-review-gate.md, docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md

## Testing
Interface tests in tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py against a tmp repo with the suite's attested/ref=HEAD default, committing drift via the existing `_commit_all` helper: container+children fixtures asserting the signed manifest's `dep` paths (inherited union, poison rule, closed-child exclusion), claim-gate outcomes (unrelated commit keeps the claim open; a committed change to a child-declared file blocks the claim naming drift), the child-file_impact-edit → container pin invalidation property, and DET-floor unit assertions for the P9 container advisory. In tests/unit/test_plan_review.py, replace test_p9_not_applicable_for_container (which asserts the old unconditional container pass) with three container cases: effective inheritance passes, a non-closed impact-less child yields the poisoning advisory naming the child id, and a closed impact-less child does not poison; leaf cases unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A container whose non-closed direct children all declare non-empty file_impact signs a
      dependency set equal to own file_impact ∪ citations ∪ the children's union — asserted
      by parsing `dep` lines from the signed manifest in an interface test.
- [ ] Poison rule: if any non-closed direct child has empty file_impact, the signed set is
      unchanged from pre-change behavior (empty ⇒ whole-HEAD fallback applies) — asserted by
      manifest inspection plus a claim blocked after an unrelated commit.
- [ ] Closed children neither contribute paths nor poison the union — asserted with a fixture
      containing one closed impact-less child.
- [ ] With inheritance effective: an unrelated committed change does NOT invalidate the
      container attestation (claim succeeds); a committed change to a child-declared file
      DOES (claim blocked, reason names drift) — both asserted via rebar.claim.
- [ ] A child editing its file_impact after the container review invalidates the container's
      attestation (pin/material drift) — asserted via claim_gate_check.
- [ ] P9: a container with poisoned inheritance yields an advisory naming the offending
      child id(s); a container with effective inheritance passes; leaf behavior is unchanged —
      asserted in DET-floor tests.
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md and ADR 0002 describe container inheritance and the poison
      rule.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Container plan-review drift scope inherits direct children's file_impact

# Close the Cloud <-> Data Center reconciler test-parity gaps

## Why this exists

Two Jira adapters now sit behind one backend port, and they were hardened at different times by different means:

* **Cloud** (`adapters/jira/`, ACLI-based) is the historically battle-tested path. Years of
  production incidents produced byte-for-byte characterization pins, ADF depth tests, comment and
  description length-convergence suites, and a large applier/differ corpus.
* **Data Center** (`adapters/jira_datacenter/`, pycontribs-based) was written and tested intensively
  during epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb], which drove it against a real Dockerized instance. That
  work produced things Cloud never had: multi-page pagination proofs, a 429/`Retry-After` matrix,
  TLS and credential validation, a live 49-cell harness suite, and a structural anti-regression
  guard.

**The gaps therefore run in BOTH directions, and that is the point of this epic.** A parity audit commissioned while closing e369 found Cloud-only coverage that DC lacks AND DC-only coverage that Cloud lacks — and the second direction contains the single highest-risk finding, because Cloud's whole-project readers have never been tested past one page while DC's have.

## The governing insight

Every defect e369 found in the DC adapter was an OPERATIONAL EDGE that only appears against a differently-configured instance: index lag, server-side page caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen configuration, workflow transition naming. None was an architectural flaw. The same class of edge exists on Cloud and is simply untested there, because Cloud's coverage grew from *incidents that happened* rather than from *configurations that differ*.

So this epic is not "make the two suites look alike". It is: **for each behaviour the two adapters share, the harder-won test should exist on both sides**, and where a SHARED module is exercised through only one adapter, a regression must not be able to reach production for the other.

## Scope

Test-tier work plus the small production changes that untested duplication forces (one map is genuinely duplicated and must be single-sourced before it can be guarded). No behaviour change to either adapter is intended; where a test reveals one is needed, that becomes its own bug ticket rather than being folded in silently.

## Out of scope

Adding coverage for behaviours only one adapter HAS (Cloud's ADF codec depth, DC's TLS/PAT handling) — those are legitimate asymmetries, not gaps. Promoting `_engine` through the mypy strictness ratchet. Any change to the backend port's shape.

## Provenance

Commissioned during epic e369's closeout. Every finding below was verified against the tree before being written down — the audit was treated as a lead, not as evidence.

## PRIORITY FRAMING (operator direction, 2026-08-02) — READ THIS BEFORE PICKING UP A CHILD

The top priority is **shipping defect-free Jira Data Center functionality.** This epic is a *related* priority precisely because parity is what gives confidence that the DC feature is defect-free — it is instrumental to the goal, not adjacent to it.

That ranks the two directions differently, and the ranking should drive which child you take:

* **DC-DIRECTION GAPS COME FIRST.** `cedc` (DC characterization) and `79d5` (DC length convergence
  + the comment ceiling) are the ones that directly buy confidence in what is being shipped. DC's
  values have never been pinned; its contract test asserts SHAPE only and would pass with every
  value wrong. Until those land, "the DC adapter is defect-free" rests on the live harness alone,
  and the live harness only covers the configurations that one default-configured instance happens
  to have.
* **BOTH-DIRECTION items rank with them** where they touch DC: `bd9e` (the duplicated ticket-type
  map is read by DC's create path) and `2944` (several of the tests that cannot fail are DC tests,
  so they are confidence we do not actually have).
* **CLOUD-DIRECTION GAPS RANK BELOW.** `0fad` and `2127` harden the mature, live-exercised Cloud
  path. They are real and worth doing — `0fad` in particular is a genuine latent truncation risk —
  but they do not serve the DC-confidence goal, and they must not gate it. `0fad` was moved out of
  epic e369 for exactly this reason and dropped to P2 under this framing.

**Do not read "parity" as "make the two suites symmetrical."** The goal is confidence in the DC feature. Where an asymmetry is legitimate (Cloud's ADF depth, DC's TLS/PAT handling) closing it buys nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e` is closed: DC's create-path field values, both sanitizer boundaries,
      the identity label form, and all four probe branches are pinned BY VALUE, and the shared
      `map_fields_to_remote` body is exercised through `WikiTextCodec` as well as `AdfCodec`
- [x] `79d5-63c7-5f31-48a7` is closed: an oversized DC comment AND an oversized DC description each
      converge across TWO passes (pass 2 plans nothing for that ticket), and the DC comment
      ceiling's PROVENANCE is cited in the source at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding
      — naming `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519 — so the constant reads as a
      decision rather than an assumption. (The ceiling is no longer unknown: it was established from
      Jira's `jpm.xml`, whose property description covers Comments as well as Description; that it
      is admin-configurable is tracked separately as `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` and does NOT gate this
      epic.) Verified by reading the cited comment in the diff
- [x] `bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8` is closed: exactly ONE dict literal defines the local->Jira ticket-type
      map within `adapters/`, and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` carries an assertion that
      fails the build if a second copy appears — the same guard shape the status and priority maps
      already have
- [x] `2944-dd3f-e982-4359` is closed: each of the five enumerated vacuous tests either asserts the
      contract its own docstring names or is renamed to what it actually pins; none is merely
      deleted, because the docstring's intent is the valuable part
- [x] [operator-attested] every pin or rewrite added under this epic is MUTATION-CHECKED — the
      mutation applied and the resulting verdict recorded as a comment on the owning child ticket. A
      pin nobody has seen fail is not evidence. Copied terminal output showing the mutated code and
      the resulting FAIL, pasted as a child-ticket comment, satisfies this criterion; it is attested
      rather than CI-checkable because a mutation is applied and reverted in a working tree and
      therefore leaves no repo artifact to inspect
- [x] where the two adapters CORRECTLY diverge, the expectation carries a DIFFERENT value per
      vendor rather than asserting sameness. Checked positively rather than as a negative property:
      the parametrized characterization suite must contain at least one case for EACH known
      divergence — (a) rich text, ADF vs wiki markup, and (b) identity form, Cloud `accountId` vs
      DC `name` — in which the Cloud and DC parameters carry DIFFERENT expected values, and both
      cases pass. Verifiable by reading the parametrize table in the diff and by running those
      cases; a reviewer can confirm it without re-deriving which behaviours diverge, because the
      two are enumerated here
- [x] `test_backend_characterization.py`'s pre-existing Cloud assertions still pass UNEDITED, so
      Cloud's incident-hardened safety net is intact rather than loosened to fit DC
baseline.summary: Close the Cloud<->DC reconciler test-parity gaps

## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` currently changes up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this deliberately covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

Author the behavioral oracle RED-first. Hold out the interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases from the implementer; expose only the basic dual-read happy path. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs is expected to advance and commit both rotation representations; claiming that such a pass makes no commit would contradict the required dual-write compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- new `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (docstring only)
- focused unit/integration/CLI tests

Estimated scope: M. Depends on closed A1 through the parent story.
baseline.summary: A2-1 implementation: extract and persist GET-rotation sidecar

# Container eval fixtures without a `children` payload cannot be run by `run_case`

## Problem

`eval_solver._run_criterion_case` raises for a CONTAINER criterion (G3 / G4 / decomp-shape) whose case carries no non-empty `children` list — the criterion runs `pass1_container` over a (parent, children, sibling-roster) decomposition, not inline text. ALL 12 cases in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carry only `input` (the parent plan) and no `children`, so none can be executed through `run_case`. `plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` cases DO carry `children` and are the working precedent.

## Evidence (measured, story 0d76)

In the live provider-parity run, `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` and `G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer-rebar` raised `ValueError: container criterion 'G3' needs a non-empty children list in the eval fixture` on BOTH arms at ALL 3 epochs, before any model call, on both class slots. They contributed nothing but error counts. `provider_parity._runnable` now excludes them, so the parity corpus is 28 items rather than 30. (Only those two surface because `select_corpus` takes the FIRST gold-block and FIRST gold-advisory case per spec; the other ten are equally unrunnable.)

## The decision, and why it is already settled by the project's own record

The original AC asked whether to add `children` payloads or to document the cases as runnable only through `pass1_container` directly. The repo already answers this, so this ticket does NOT re-open it:

- `eval_solver._run_criterion_case` states the contract in its own comment: *"A container
  criterion with no `children` payload is a **fixture error**, not a silent pass."* The raise is
  deliberately loud precisely so the fixture gets fixed.
- `plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml` is the same kind of spec with the payload present, and
  documents the shape in its header: *"Container criteria run over a (parent, children)
  decomposition, so each case carries the parent plan as `input` and the children as a
  `children:` list."*
- `_run_criterion_case` drives the SAME `pass1_container` fan-out the real gate uses, so a
  `children`-carrying fixture IS the "runnable through `pass1_container`" path — the second
  option is not a different capability, only a decision to leave the corpus smaller.

So: add the payloads. No new capability, no contract change, no code change.

## Approach

Add a `children:` list to each of the 12 cases in `plan-review-container.eval.yaml`, each entry `{ticket_id, title, description}`, matching the decomp-shape shape exactly.

The children are **transcribed, not invented**: every case's existing `input` prose already names its child set (e.g. `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar`: "Its children cover the importer, the API, and the UI — but NO child addresses idempotency"; `G4-R-ordering-violation-snap`: "Child A deletes the legacy payments column; child B still reads it"). Each `children` list makes exactly those children explicit and adds nothing the `input` does not already assert, so the gold label (`expect`) of every case is unchanged by construction.

`sibling_roster` is deliberately NOT pinned per case: `_run_criterion_case` falls back to `build_sibling_roster(children)`, the ONE shared builder, so eval fixtures see the same roster shape production does.

No source change: `provider_parity._runnable` already admits any container case with a non-empty `children` list, so `eligible_cases` picks the fixed cases up unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` — add `children:` to all 12 dataset
  cases. `prompt`, `model`, `epochs`, `gate`, `scorers`, `tolerance`, every `input`, every
  `expect`/`criterion`/`corpus`/`note`/`mode`, and the whole `gold_set` are UNCHANGED.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` — `test_container_cases_without_a_children_payload_are_excluded`
  ends with `assert all(i.spec != "plan-review-container" for i in pp.eligible_cases())`, using
  the container spec as the witness that the exclusion rule is non-vacuous. Once the fixtures are
  fixed that witness is false. The RULE stays pinned (the `_runnable` unit assertions in the same
  test already prove it non-vacuously on synthetic cases); only the stale witness line is
  replaced by its inverse — that the container spec is now eligible.

## Testing

- The load-bearing assertion is that every container case in `eligible_cases()` carries a
  non-empty `children` payload AND that the container spec is now represented — i.e. the ticket's
  own AC becomes an executable test rather than a manual check. This is added to
  `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` in place of the stale witness line.
- A fixture-shape test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` pins that EVERY dataset case in
  `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries a non-empty `children` list whose entries each have
  `ticket_id`/`title`/`description` — so a future case added without a payload fails CI instead
  of silently dropping out of the corpus (which is exactly how this bug went unnoticed).
- No live model call is needed: `_runnable` / `eligible_cases` / spec loading are all offline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every dataset case in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries a
      non-empty `children:` list whose entries each have `ticket_id`, `title` and `description`;
      pinned by a new test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` that fails if any case lacks
      one.
- [x] `provider_parity.eligible_cases()` picks the container cases up with NO change to
      `src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py` or `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py`; verified
      by `git diff --stat` showing neither file modified, and by a test asserting
      `any(i.spec == "plan-review-container" for i in pp.eligible_cases())`.
- [x] The container spec contributes its first gold-block and first gold-advisory case again, so
      `select_corpus(eligible_cases())` grows by exactly 2. MEASURED on this base: eligible
      128 -> 140, corpus 26 -> 28. (The recorded "28 -> 30" totals predate unrelated changes to
      the spec set; the +2 delta is the invariant, and is what the test asserts. See the ticket
      comment recording this measurement.)
- [x] Every container item in `eligible_cases()` satisfies `item.case["children"]`; the existing
      exclusion RULE remains pinned by the `_runnable` assertions
      (`not _runnable("G3", {"input": ...})`, `_runnable("G3", {"children": [...]})`).
- [x] Each case's `expect` label is unchanged and each `children` list is entailed by that case's
      existing `input` prose (no new scenario invented); reviewable by diffing that no `input`,
      `expect`, `criterion`, or `gold_set` line changed.
- [x] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green with the worktree venv on PATH.

# Prevent a recurrence of the 2026-08-26 `/var/gerrit` disk-fill from investigation evidence

## Why
The acute `/var/gerrit` disk-fill incident (`wakeful-ordinary-chicken` / `5a05`) was dominated by one-off investigation evidence written to the Gerrit data volume: `/var/gerrit/rebar-quiet-window-evidence/` held two `epoch-probe-20260826T*` dumps of about 5.2G each (~11G total, 65% of used space). They were reclaimed with operator approval on 2026-08-30, taking `/var/gerrit` from 37% to 15%. Nothing currently prevents similar debris from landing on the data volume again, and the runbook coverage is root-volume-heavy.

This is the carried-over `/var/gerrit` sibling for disk-ceiling epic `endowed-upset-scaup` (`6202-e1c7-c57f-4897`). It is linked to that epic with `relates_to` rather than as a blocking edge so the ADR/scratch/root-accumulator stories remain claimable; the epic acceptance criteria require this ticket to be resolved or explicitly dispositioned before epic close.

## What
Add policy/guarding and runbook coverage so investigation/probe evidence does not accumulate on `/var/gerrit`. Establish the approved evidence/scratch location (prefer the new bounded gate scratch path once S1 lands, or another explicitly capped temporary location) and document how to reclaim `/var/gerrit` data-volume headroom safely.

## Scope
In scope: `/var/gerrit` data-volume runbook, guard/policy for probe evidence paths, optional metric/check for non-`site/` debris, and local tests if code changes are required. Out of scope: root-volume Docker/journald/tmp/container caps and gate scratch EBS provisioning, which are tracked by sibling stories under `endowed-upset-scaup`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Investigation/probe output does not land on the Gerrit data volume (`/var/gerrit`) without an explicit, bounded, documented exception.
- [ ] A guard, check, or loud failure path prevents or flags probe output under `/var/gerrit` before it can silently accumulate.
- [ ] Probe artifacts are bounded at spawn or stored under a capped scratch location so they self-clean rather than accumulate.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` documents `/var/gerrit` data-disk reclaim/headroom diagnosis and safe remediation, not only root-volume Docker prunes.
- [ ] Optional non-`site/` `/var/gerrit` debris metric/alarm is either implemented or explicitly rejected with rationale in the ticket/runbook.
- [ ] Portability criterion: any guard/check uses host-level scripts/runbooks and local validation, not a GitHub-only CI trigger.

## Notes / scope boundary
The slower data-disk growth driver from tickets-branch enrichment fan-out/blob-inclusive store remains separate work tracked by `4520`/`536b`/`0754`; do not duplicate that here.
baseline.summary: Prevent investigation evidence on /var/gerrit + add data-disk reclaim runbook
