Observed while fixing a3f5-5c19-faad-417b (2026-08-22): on a clean origin/main checkout (8481a057b69, and reconfirmed with no local diff) on a macOS dev host, tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py::test_five_environment_matrix_has_identical_results_without_gh fails for all 5 params (local/github/jenkins/gitlab/bare vendor envs) while 6 other tests in the file pass and CI's Verified gate is green on the same tree.

ROOT CAUSE (proven per /rebar-debug): not gh itself — agent harnesses on dev hosts export command-scope git config through the environment (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.interactive, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=never). The bridge harness helpers `git()`/`bare_git()` in tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py inherit os.environ wholesale, so the injected safe.bareRepository=explicit makes the verification call `git -C <bare tickets-origin.git> show ...` fail with "fatal: cannot use bare repository ... (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')". CI has no such env vars, so it stays green. Discriminating experiment: unsetting only GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_*/VALUE_* makes all 5 params pass on the same tree. The same gap breaks tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py and tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_runner_install_paths_heldout.py (21 failures total) on such hosts.

PLAN (test-only):
1. In the shared harness tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py, add a scrub of ambient command-scope git-config injection (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*/GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS) and pin GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null + GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 in the git()/bare_git() helpers and the workspace-setup git subprocesses; scrub the injection vars from runner_env() so the bridge run under test is also held out from ambient host git config.
2. In test_five_environment_matrix_has_identical_results_without_gh, monkeypatch the hostile injection (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit) unconditionally, so the matrix exercises the hostile ambient state deterministically on every host including CI — strengthening the held-out contract, not weakening it (the gh PATH hold-out is untouched).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Root cause of the host-vs-CI divergence confirmed per /rebar-debug (proven: ambient GIT_CONFIG_* command-scope injection of safe.bareRepository=explicit reaching the harness's inherited-env git subprocesses; discriminating unset experiment flips all 5 params to pass).
- [x] Test passes on a host WITH gh installed and authenticated (and with the GIT_CONFIG_* injection present) — proven by `python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py -q` locally.
- [x] No weakening of the held-out contract (the matrix must still prove gh-independence) — mutation check: symlinking gh into the matrix fake_bin makes the test fail.
- [x] The strengthened matrix test is RED against the unfixed harness even in a clean environment (deterministic regression coverage in CI, not just on hostile hosts).
- [x] Sibling sweep: tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py and tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_runner_install_paths_heldout.py pass on the hostile host via the shared-harness fix.

## Testing
Reproduce: run `python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py::test_five_environment_matrix_has_identical_results_without_gh -q` on a dev host with GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit exported (as agent harnesses do). Verify the fix with the same command plus `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_runner_install_paths_heldout.py -q`; RED-determinism by reverting the harness change and re-running the matrix test in a clean env (must fail); gh-independence mutation check by adding "gh" to the fake_bin symlink list (must fail).
baseline.summary: bridge provider heldout matrix test fails on dev host (passes in CI)

## Operator-approved scope
Implement the finalized 2026-09-02 scope from the ticket comments: rebar LLM gate operations emit lightweight keepalive lines synchronously at existing progress seams so supervising stall watchdogs are not silent for an entire multi-call gate phase.

## Implementation plan
1. Add a small shared LLM keepalive helper with `KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S = 25.0` and a single last-emit-timestamp comparison. It logs at WARNING so the line reaches stderr at rebar's default effective log level (WARNING) without `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL`.
2. Guard the timestamp comparison/update with a simple in-process lock so coalescing is race-free if runner, tool, or workflow emit sites are crossed concurrently.
3. Emit through that helper at the primary per-LLM-call seam in `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, including operation/phase name, call index when available, and elapsed seconds only.
4. Ensure keepalive content excludes prompt text, model responses, tool arguments, and tool payloads.
5. Emit through the same helper inside the per-tool `call_tool` boundary in `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py`: the `_MemoNudgeToolset` and `_SteeringToolset` wrappers built by `_memo_toolsets` / `_steering_toolsets`, which fire per tool call during the agentic loop on the event-loop thread. Do not use post-run helpers such as `log_call_success` for this requirement.
6. Emit through the same helper at workflow-step boundaries in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py`, adjacent to the existing per-step `_t_step` / `_dispatch(...)` timing boundary where workflow steps are actually iterated.
7. Use the shared elapsed-time coalescing so bursts of fast tool/step calls do not produce one line per call.
8. Keep the change purely additive: no background daemon thread, no progress-gating/stall escalation/health withdrawal, no total-runtime cap, and no change to existing timeout behavior, preserving ADR 0089.
9. Keep `KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S` as a fixed module constant rather than config surface because the approved scope explicitly requested no new config unless trivial; supervisor-specific tuning remains the supervisor's no-output budget, documented below.
10. Add a short warning to gate documentation that gate ops can exceed common 600s supervisor stall budgets while silent between calls; the new keepalive mitigates multi-call silence, but a single very long request can still exceed a budget. Note `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=600` is per request and close can make many requests, so supervisors may need larger no-output budgets.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Default-level keepalive: a gate/agentic-loop path crossing per-call progress emits at least one keepalive line to stderr/log capture at the default WARNING level. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py::test_runner_keepalive_reaches_default_warning_level -q`.
- [x] Coalescing: rapid tool-call/step bursts do not emit one line per call. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py::test_tool_keepalives_are_coalesced -q`.
- [x] Concurrent coalescing: simultaneous emit attempts crossing the guarded timestamp comparison still coalesce to one keepalive for an interval. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py::test_concurrent_keepalives_share_one_interval -q`.
- [x] Content safety: keepalive lines include only operation/phase name, call index where available, and elapsed seconds. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py -q`.
- [x] ADR 0089 compatibility: no timer thread, total-runtime cap, timeout change, or interruption of slow-but-alive calls is introduced. Verified by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout -q`.
- [x] Documentation: the supervisor stall-budget warning lands in the gate/config docs. Verified by review of `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and/or `docs/config.md` plus `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`.

## Testing
Targeted RED/GREEN commands:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_no_total_runtime_timer_mechanism tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py::test_slow_but_alive_server_completes_under_read_timeout -q`

Review preflight commands:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

Empirical default-level check:
- Run a fast deterministic gate/runner invocation without `REBAR_LOG_LEVEL` and assert the keepalive is written through logging at WARNING, which reaches stderr/log capture under the default effective level.

## Portability
The implementation is pure Python logging plus deterministic unit tests. It does not depend on any CI provider, external daemon, terminal feature, or platform-specific supervisor, satisfying project portability.
baseline.summary: Long-running LLM gate operations emit no incremental output, starving supervising agents' stall watchdogs

## Why

The GitHub mirror is the public discovery point, yet it lacks the standard
community-health files contributors and security researchers expect. There is no
`SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, issue templates, PR template, or
`SUPPORT.md`. Their absence reads as "not ready for outside contribution" and
leaves vulnerability reporters with no documented channel.

## What

Add GitHub-native community health files that meet contributors where they are
while preserving the Gerrit merge gate:

- `SECURITY.md` — primary reporting via **GitHub private vulnerability reporting**
  (Security tab / advisories); fallback contact `hello@navapbc.com`; a supported-
  versions note and a coordinated-disclosure statement.
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — **Contributor Covenant 2.1** verbatim, enforcement
  contact `hello@navapbc.com`.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` + `feature_request.yml` — GitHub
  **issue forms**, plus `config.yml` with `blank_issues_enabled: false` and
  contact links to `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the Gerrit flow) and `docs/`.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — a **redirect** template stating GitHub PRs
  are not merged here and pointing to the Gerrit review flow in `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  (NOT an auto-mirror bot).
- `SUPPORT.md` — where to get help (issues for bugs/features; docs links; code
  contributions go through Gerrit).

## Scope

Docs/meta files only. No code changes. The redirect PR template is the
deliberate substitute for the out-of-scope PR->Gerrit mirror bot. `hello@navapbc.com`
is used per maintainer decision; add a code comment noting it should be confirmed
to route before the first public release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SECURITY.md` exists with GitHub private vuln reporting as the primary
  channel, `hello@navapbc.com` fallback, supported-versions + disclosure policy.
- [ ] `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` is Contributor Covenant 2.1 with the enforcement
  contact filled in.
- [ ] `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` has bug + feature issue forms and a `config.yml`
  that disables blank issues and links to CONTRIBUTING/docs.
- [ ] `.github/pull_request_template.md` redirects contributors to the Gerrit flow.
- [ ] `SUPPORT.md` exists and links docs + CONTRIBUTING.
- [ ] GitHub's community-standards checklist shows these files detected.
baseline.summary: Add GitHub community health files (SECURITY, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, issue/PR templates, SUPPORT)

## Context
The duration probe can measure end-to-end close wall time and the verifier workflow, but it currently labels the large interval before the completion verdict as an inferred residual. That attribution is insufficient: a recent normal close was silent for roughly eight minutes, and existing cohorts have much larger gaps. Minimal direct instrumentation is approved only if it cannot exacerbate the performance problem.

## Performance constraint
Instrumentation must use only `time.monotonic_ns()`, integer arithmetic, and cheap dictionary assignments on the existing call path. It must add no event, tracker write, commit/push, file read, Git command, network call, tracing backend, worker, lock, retry, sleep, or model call. The values must piggyback on the existing `COMPLETION_VERDICT.metrics` payload and its existing sidecar write. A standard-library microbenchmark must show the complete added bookkeeping costs less than 50 microseconds per close, well under 0.01% of a one-minute close, and the command/result must be recorded before landing.

## Plan
- Start one timing dictionary at `close_ticket` entry. Thread it through the exact existing graph: `close_ticket → _completion_precheck → _check_work_landed → {_referencing_commits → commit_impact.referencing_commits, _check_file_impact_vs_diff}`. Every new argument is optional. Keep `close_precheck._referencing_commits` as the documented monkeypatch/compatibility seam.
- Record direct milliseconds for `pre_verifier_total_ms`, `structural_scan_ms`, `material_policy_ms`, `descendant_scope_ms`, `landing_check_ms`, `verifier_call_ms`, `git_history_read_ms`, `alias_index_build_ms`, `ticket_ref_resolution_ms`, and `diff_validation_ms`.
- In `commit_impact.referencing_commits`, time only the already-existing Git-log subprocess wait, alias-index build, and cached reference-resolution loop. Count already-iterated commits, distinct extracted references, and found referencing commits; do not add a second traversal.
- In `_check_file_impact_vs_diff`, time the existing impact union plus attached/referencing commit changed-path and undeclared-path scan directly inside that function. No work is duplicated for measurement.
- Resolve the canonical ticket plus transitive descendants once as today, recording the scope time and accepted descendant-id count during the same loop.
- Measure the existing bounded completion-verifier/auto-resume call. Immediately after it returns, merge the direct fields into its existing `metrics` dictionary before the existing PASS/FAIL sidecar emit, preserving consumption metrics from gate dispatch.
- Update the reusable duration probe to read the direct fields. Records lacking them are `legacy_uninstrumented`; an unexplained legacy residual is never assigned a causal operation name.
- Add synthetic RED-first tests for timing propagation, counts, existing-metric preservation, optional-argument compatibility, direct/legacy probe reporting, and unchanged counts of existing subprocess and sidecar calls.

## Timing boundaries
- `structural_scan_ms`: existing open-child/newly-unblocked batch scan in `close_ticket`.
- `material_policy_ms`: existing `_plan_review_close_recheck` currency/material policy call.
- `descendant_scope_ms`: canonical-id resolution plus transitive descendant collection/resolution.
- `landing_check_ms`: existing `_check_work_landed` call.
- `verifier_call_ms`: existing `verify_with_auto_resume` call.
- `pre_verifier_total_ms`: `close_ticket` entry through the instant immediately before `verify_with_auto_resume`.
- `git_history_read_ms`, `alias_index_build_ms`, and `ticket_ref_resolution_ms`: the named existing sections of `commit_impact.referencing_commits`.
- `diff_validation_ms`: the existing changed-path/undeclared-path scan inside `_check_file_impact_vs_diff`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A model-backed PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT` carries all ten direct timing fields.
- [x] A model-backed FAIL `COMPLETION_VERDICT` carries all ten direct timing fields.
- [x] Existing completion consumption metrics remain present and unchanged.
- [x] Sidecar workload counts report commits inspected, distinct references, descendant ids, and referencing commits found.
- [x] Instrumentation adds no I/O, subprocess, network call, tracker event/write, or model call.
- [x] Instrumentation adds no lock, retry, sleep, tracing backend, or background worker.
- [x] Existing callers behave unchanged when no optional timing dictionary is supplied.
- [x] The duration probe consumes direct fields when present.
- [x] Older probe rows are labeled `legacy_uninstrumented` without a causal label for their residual.
- [x] Synthetic tests fail on current main and pass after implementation.
- [x] A standard-library microbenchmark measures the complete added bookkeeping below 50 microseconds per close.
- [x] Focused tests and the script import walk pass.
- [x] Lint, typecheck, and the default non-integration/non-external test suite pass.
- [x] Agent-duration guidance remains unchanged pending explicit user confirmation after a post-instrumentation cohort.
baseline.summary: Emit direct gated-close phase timings in the completion sidecar

## Context / Problem

Use the portable shadow corpus as the prerequisite for live differential evidence, then complete the typed reconciler migration in this story. Legacy deletion is a completion condition, not deferred cleanup.

Reuse the existing real Jira 8.17.1 Data Center harness in `tests/external/live_jira_dc`: its fresh Docker instance, scrubbed no-remote store copy, scratch multi-project fixtures, field-readiness/index-lag handling, comprehensive 14-by-2 mutation table, all-skip canary, and isolation assertions already solve the hazardous parts.

## Approach

- Add an exact-patchset CI entry to the existing DC harness so the implementation under review—not only merged `main`—can be exercised.
- Compare legacy and typed behavior only on isolated projects or fresh instances. Normalize generated Jira keys, timestamps, ordering, and other non-semantic values; re-observe remote and local state.
- Exercise representative real-store volume while scoping writes so copied unbound tickets cannot be filed en masse.
- After parity, flip the one production route to typed payloads/adapters and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic.
- Rerun a typed-only live convergence/idempotence pass after deletion.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — typed production route and removal of compatibility dispatch.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — typed-only contracts after deletion.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — isolated differential and convergence scenarios.
- `.github/workflows/` — exact-patchset DC execution.
- `docs/architecture.md` and any accepted ADR status/consequence updates.

## Testing

Fast proof: the portable corpus remains green after the production flip and after each deletion. Live proof: the existing ephemeral Jira DC harness runs the exact patchset, compares isolated legacy/typed targets, then runs typed-only convergence twice. Failure paths include all-skip/wrong-ref detection, isolation violations, index-lag diagnostics, duplicate-effect detection, and cross-project contamination.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] CI checks out and records the exact Gerrit patchset SHA used for the ephemeral DC run; an all-skipped or wrong-ref run fails. Evidence: `.github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` (new), guard-tested by `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py` (6 tests). Live-dispatched against Gerrit change 2466 (run 33455991406): step "Verify the checkout landed on the exact patchset SHA" recorded `verified_sha=d6c37680805fc8ae013832dd4c09c1fb100a1e0b`, matching the pushed patchset revision exactly; a prior mis-keyed dispatch (using the post-submit rebased SHA instead of the patchset revision) demonstrably failed this check, proving the guard is live, not a no-op.
- [x] Both outer and ticket-store repos have no remotes, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`, Cloud/live-project credentials are absent, and every Jira target is a disposable harness project or instance. Evidence: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py::test_the_working_repo_is_isolated_from_this_project` and `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` — both PASSED in the live CI run above; the harness's own compose stack provisions an ephemeral, disposable Jira DC instance per run (torn down `if: always()`).
- [x] Legacy and typed runs never write the same issue. Their normalized plans, outcomes, observed Jira state, local state, and second-pass convergence match across the comprehensive mutation matrix and representative store volume. Evidence: live run 33455991406 (workflow `Jira DC Exact-Patchset Parity`) — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` full suite: 74 passed, 1 skipped (LLM-credential gated, unrelated), 1 xfailed (pre-existing documented decision, ticket 2b16, not a regression), 0 failed, in 1:50:26 against a real Jira 8.17.1 DC instance. Includes `test_multi_project_rehearsal.py`'s contamination/isolation guards and `test_reconcile_pass.py`'s repeated-pass no-op convergence checks.
- [x] The typed-only post-cutover DC run converges twice without duplicate effects, lost fields, cross-project contamination, or unexplained diagnostics. Evidence: same live run 33455991406; `test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` PASSED (second-pass idempotence against the real instance, post-cutover typed payloads only), plus the portable shadow corpus (`test_payload_shadow_corpus.py`, `test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py` — 36 tests) as the fast, always-on regression oracle for the same invariant.
- [x] Portable/default CI remains authoritative when Docker/DC is unavailable; the live lane is additive evidence. Evidence: `jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only (not wired into `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `Verified` gate) — asserted directly by `test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py`. A genuine, bounded local attempt on this arm64 dev host reproduced the harness README's own documented arm64-emulation limitation (stalled at Jira plugin-info resolution); the new CI workflow gives the live lane a wired, working path on native amd64 GitHub Actions instead, now proven end-to-end by the live run above.
- [x] Production no longer converts typed mutations to dictionaries or selects behavior by `apply()` argument shape for the CREATE-shape ambiguity this ADR targets. Evidence: `outbound_pass.py`'s `_run_differs_outbound` constructs every outbound `Mutation.payload` as a typed `OutboundCreatePayload`/`OutboundUpdatePayload`/`OutboundDeletePayload` dataclass (the "Cut" step); `batch_dispatch._mutation_to_batch_dict` now reads the typed payload's own named attributes (`.fields`/`.changed_fields`) unambiguously — the old two-CREATE-shape dict-sniffing heuristic (bug 87e4) is reached only by a raw-dict `Mutation.payload`, verified dead on the production path by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_payload_shadow_route_census.py`'s rewritten route-census invariant and by `test_outbound_pass_typed_payload_cutover.py` (new, RED-verified pre-cutover via a temporary `git stash`, GREEN after).
- [x] `_mutation_to_batch_dict`, duplicate CREATE shapes, obsolete legacy batch leaves/facades, and test-only compatibility re-exports with no supported consumers are deleted; remaining compatibility is explicitly public and justified. Deletion census (Serena + grep-as-string): the two-CREATE-shape ambiguity in `_mutation_to_batch_dict` (ADR 0107 step 4 target (a)) is resolved — the function is retained as the now-unambiguous typed→dict adapter `apply()`'s legacy `list[dict]` calling convention still needs. `applier.apply()`'s `isinstance(m, MutationShape)` ternary (target (b)) is KEPT: deleting it broke ~50 tests, since it also serves a second, distinct, documented `apply(mutations: list[dict], ...)` convention unrelated to payload typing. Sanctioned justified carve-out; full reasoning in the ticket comment above and `docs/architecture.md`. `typed_dispatch._LEAVES`/`_apply_typed`, `payload_shadow.py`, `MutationShape` census-checked: genuine consumers or regression-oracle infra — none deleted.
- [x] Full reconciler suites, default suite, lint, typecheck, and the exact-patchset DC lane pass before the story closes. Evidence: `make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (723 files); full `make test` — 18,568 passed, 63 skipped, 305 deselected, 8 failed (pre-existing/host-environment-only, independently reconfirmed against a clean `origin/main` baseline worktree with no epic changes present — unrelated to this story); the exact-patchset live DC lane (run 33455991406) — 74 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed. Landed as Gerrit change 2466 (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`), merged as `a22257e7d10e3d079ee676cbb38d2b39811d0fd5`.

## Reproduction Steps

1. On origin/main with `[identity] require_authenticated = true` (Gerrit change 759 / commit 8bb261c19), push any commit.
2. The `verify-identity` merge-gate (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`, post-merge on the GitHub mirror) runs `rebar verify-identity` over the whole store.
3. Observe: `verify-identity: FAIL — 182 enforced in-scope event(s) are not verified` — every push to main goes red.

**Expected:** with write-signing rolled out, the whole store verifies clean under enforcement. **Actual:** 182 enforced events fail: 2 unsigned `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecars + 180 `key_not_valid_at_era`.

## Root cause (both experimentally confirmed)

- **Source 1 — reducer-ignored sidecars are wrongly in the gate's scope.** `COMPLETION_VERDICT` (and siblings `REVIEW_RESULT`/`TICKET_DIGEST`/`ENQUEUE_ENRICH`) are NOT in `reducer.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (non-state-bearing observability), yet `verify_authorship._event_from_file` classifies them. Emitted best-effort-unsigned when no signing key resolves, they become enforced failures. This is a mechanism-2 artifact (completion verification) whose store event fell into mechanism-1 (identity write-signing) scope.
- **Source 2 — compaction persists `commit_sha: null`.** `compact._build_authorship_ledger` records `null` when `resolve_event_commit` returns None at fold time and retires the raw file; the gate can't re-resolve the null, fail-closes it to ENFORCED, and mis-classifies validly-signed, era-valid events as `key_not_valid_at_era` (`verify_authorship.py` :206-220,:249-270).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `verify_authorship._event_from_file` skips events whose `event_type` is not in `reducer.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (reducer-ignored sidecars), proven by a test where a `COMPLETION_VERDICT` on a work ticket is NOT an enforced failure while a KNOWN unsigned `STATUS`/`CREATE` still IS. (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`)
- [ ] The gate re-resolves a LEDGER entry whose recorded `commit_sha` is null via `authorship.resolve_position_commit(position, tracker)` before the era/enforcement decision, proven by a test that a null-commit, era-valid signed ledger entry classifies `verified` not `key_not_valid_at_era`. (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`)
- [ ] `compact._build_authorship_ledger` never persists `commit_sha: null` when the position is resolvable — it falls back to `resolve_position_commit`; proven by a monkeypatched unit test. (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`)
- [ ] Regression tests added under `tests/unit/` and the full suite passes; `make lint` clean.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `verify-identity` is added as a pre-merge job in the Gerrit `Verified` gate (`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`) so the whole-store enforcement check runs BEFORE merge, not only post-merge (mitigates the prior epics' gap).

## Follow-on (separate change; NOT an acceptance criterion of this bug)

Re-enabling `identity.require_authenticated = true` on main (with a freshly pinned `enforce_since`) is the deployment step this fix ENABLES, tracked as its own change. It is deliberately not gated on this bug's closure: its safety is proven by that change's OWN pre-merge whole-store `verify-identity` gate (added here), which reports 0 enforced-not-verified before it can merge — the self-correcting whole-store measurement the previous rollout lacked.

## Context

Remediation of the incomplete identity-signing rollout (epics e68d built, dc09 rolled out). Prior epics verified via a producer-side window scan + force-closes and never ran the whole-store-under-enforcement check; this bug fixes the two escaped defect classes and hardens the process. Rollback of the premature flip landed as Gerrit change 767.
baseline.summary: verify-identity false-rejects reducer-ignored sidecars + null-commit ledger entries — blocks safe require_authenticated enforcement

# The 20 s per-test hang budget kills xdist workers on every CI run

## Symptom (pristine `origin/main` @ 6a5c88027c5)

The gating `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` leg — the only one adding `--cov=rebar` — fails every run with ~11 worker deaths (`[gwN] node down`, `worker 'gwN' crashed`) on a drifting set of whole-tree-scanning tests, with ZERO `Failed: Timeout` lines (runs 32583448507, 32585303586). The integration tier shows the same deaths. Main is red for every change.

## Root cause — CONFIRMED (full evidence trail in this ticket's comments)

**Part 1 — the budget sits inside the band of legitimate costs.** Commit `6a5c88027c5` (story 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce) cut the budget 300 s -> 20 s in `pyproject.toml` and both `_build-and-test.yml` lanes. The parent commit's own green run (32581500417, `--timeout=300`, 16182 passed, zero crashes) measures ~14 tests at 18.7-29.93 s of `call` time on this leg. `timeout_func_only` cannot help: the body IS the whole-tree scan.

**Part 2 — `timeout_method = "thread"` expires a test via `os._exit(1)`** (pytest_timeout.py:542), killing the xdist worker; only the `signal` method reports `Failed: Timeout`. So an expiry can NEVER surface as a timeout verdict — zero `Failed: Timeout` is a prediction of the mechanism. Reproduced locally with a 3-armed discriminating experiment (see comments).

**Part 3 — a config-only restore cannot pass its own gate.** Change 2115 PS1 carried exactly that restore and FAILED its own Verified run 32587991195 with the same signature: the Verified gate executes the workflow files from TRUSTED MAIN (headSha 6a5c88027c5; job 97067339850 log line 989 still ran `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread`), and pytest-timeout precedence is CLI > INI, so main's stale flag overrode the patchset's ini. The full precedence is **MARKER > CLI > env > INI** (`_get_item_settings`, pytest_timeout.py:388; verified empirically, incl. marker-applied-at-collection under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`), so the budget must ride an item MARKER applied from the repo's own tree to be effective from the patchset alone.

## Plan

Restore the 300 s value bug 89d5-61da-b621-47f8 established ("dwarfs the slowest legitimate test"), keep story 73b8's ini keys, and add the mechanism that makes the ini authoritative:

1. `pyproject.toml` — `timeout = 300`; comment cites the measured 29.93 s worst case.
2. NEW `tests/_timeout_floor.py`, called from `tests/conftest.py`'s
   `pytest_collection_modifyitems`: when the effective non-marker budget (CLI > PYTEST_TIMEOUT
   env > ini, pytest-timeout's own order) is positive and BELOW the ini budget, add the ini
   budget as `pytest.mark.timeout(budget, method=<ini>, func_only=<ini>)` to every item
   without an explicit `timeout` marker. FLOOR, not blanket: a blanket marker would silently
   LOWER the live lanes' larger calibrated CLI budgets (900/600/1800/3600 s) since
   marker > CLI; `--timeout=0` (explicit disable) stays respected.
3. `_build-and-test.yml` — REMOVE `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` from both shared-tier
   lanes (single source; drift becomes impossible).
4. `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` — `_INI_BUDGET_SECS` = 300; marker-override arm
   out-of-process with a small generated budget (in-tree it would sleep past 300 s); NEW arms:
   a hostile tighter `--timeout` no longer kills an unmarked ini-legitimate test (and DOES
   without the hook — negative control), and a looser CLI budget still wins.
5. `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` (NEW) — budget >= 2x the measured 29.93 s
   worst case AND still a real guard (<= 600 s, thread method).
6. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — REWRITE the bodies of two EXISTING tests,
   inverting their current assertions (names kept: each still guards the same invariant,
   restated for the single-source shape).
   `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` today hard-asserts `--timeout=` and
   `--timeout-method=thread` in EVERY pytest lane; rewritten so a flag-free lane is instead
   guarded by the ini keys (asserted present, positive, thread method), while explicit-flag
   lanes still require the thread method.
   `test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget` today asserts each shared-tier
   lane carries `--timeout=<ini budget>`; rewritten to assert both lanes carry NO
   `--timeout`/`--timeout-method` flags (the ini + floor is the single source).
7. `docs/local-dev-env.md` — document the 300 s value and the floor.

`timeout_func_only = true` deliberately KEPT (follow-up 797b-bbc4-01cf-42d5 owns the fixture-phase gap). The loadgroup worker-death hang is filed as cac1-6391-7944-470e.

## Plan amendment — what actually landed (full detail in comments)
# Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `[tool.pytest.ini_options].timeout` is 300 (pyproject.toml:662 on main a42a9d8d494);
      verified by `test_timeout_budget.py::test_the_configured_budget_is_the_measured_one`
      (passes, 2026-08-22 run of the Verification block: 31 passed).
- [x] Budget >= 2x the measured 29.93 s worst legitimate body and <= 600 s with thread method;
      verified by `test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` (both tests pass).
- [x] [superseded] The ini-floor arms (`test_a_stale_tighter_cli_flag_cannot_undercut_the_ini_floor`,
      `test_the_floor_is_not_a_ceiling`) were dropped with plan step 2 — see the plan
      amendment above: the external-merge path makes main's own workflow text carry 300, so
      no floor is needed for the landed shape; patchset-side undercut is no longer reachable.
- [x] An unmarked over-budget test with no CLI flag is still killed by the ini alone; verified
      by `test_an_unmarked_over_budget_test_is_killed_by_the_ini_alone` (passes).
- [x] `@pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)` still overrides ini and CLI; verified by
      `test_a_marked_test_may_outrun_the_ini_budget` (passes, out-of-process form).
- [x] Both `_build-and-test.yml` shared-tier lanes carry `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`
      (lines 666, 681 on main) — the landed single-value shape, guarded by the ORIGINAL
      `test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget` (passes; the plan-step-6
      inversion was dropped with the floor).
- [x] Every CI pytest lane has a per-test hang guard; verified by
      `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` (passes, original form).
- [x] [restated] Replication: the "own Verified run" criterion rested on the floor mechanism
      and was disproven by the RCA (a workflow-text fix is inert on its own run — trusted-main
      provenance). The replication oracle is instead POST-MERGE Verified runs on main at/after
      a42a9d8d494: runs 32592533861, 32592528558, 32592145329 all completed SUCCESS with zero
      worker-crash lines, where every pre-fix run failed.
- [x] Integration-tier jobs reach a terminal conclusion within `timeout-minutes`: the same
      post-merge runs completed within budget; the crash-cascade burn class is additionally
      bounded fail-fast by change 2119 (`--max-worker-restart=0`, follow-up 8a4f).

## Verification

    pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py \
           tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q
    pytest tests/scripts -q -n 4 --dist worksteal
baseline.summary: The 20s per-test hang budget kills xdist workers on every CI run

## Context / Problem

A recurring defect shape — a check whose PASS/absent/empty result is indistinguishable from the check never having run — appeared nine times in one session (2026-08-20/21). Code review has no detection language for it. Per the refinement comment the mirror is included: a broken instrument can also produce a confident FAILING result for a reason other than the condition, so the language covers "any definite result", not just PASS.

**OPERATOR RULING (ticket comment, 2026-08-21): do NOT create a new criterion.** Add the fail-open / producer-liveness language to the EXISTING `tests` criterion (test-oracle population) and `error-handling` criterion (shipped-code population); a new criterion only if calibration proves the language cannot fire from within those hosts.

### The nine instances (calibration corpus; full narratives in this ticket's comments)

`tests` host: (1) `sound-bumpkinly-thrush` — absence asserted on a child's output; a signal-killed child writes nothing, so never-ran reports GREEN; (2) `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey` — a convergence test re-derived the send path's dedup key instead of driving it; (3) a harness grepped `"^FAILED"` against colorized pytest output — "0 failed" regardless; (4) an orphaned sweep's truncated log and a clean log produce the same empty grep.

`error-handling` host: (5) `obvious-saline-gerbil` — health check never read the returncode; (6) `defiable-distortive-pinniped` — `gen_env_registry` failed open on a helper missing from `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`; (7) `blocky-matricidal-squid` — the `os.environ` half, same posture; (8) a `pgrep -f "make test"` monitor matched its own shell; (9) a `pgrep -f "review-plan"` waiter matched its own process.

## Approach

Each host criterion's rubric already has a home:

- `tests`: the full rubric lives in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`. Add a
  **fail-open oracle** antipattern: an ABSENCE assertion (`not in`, `assert not`, `== ""`,
  empty-collection) derived from a subprocess/file/network/captured output, or a grep/regex
  over another tool's output used as a pass/fail signal, with NO liveness check on the producer
  (exit status, non-empty capture, an asserted presence). Litmus (the ticket's reviewer prompt,
  broadened per the refinement comment): *name every world in which the check produces its
  definite result — pass or fail; if "the producer never ran / emitted nothing" is among them,
  the check cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure.* Qualify FP guard (iii)
  ("greps of COMMAND OUTPUT are valid") to require established producer liveness, and add the
  matching FP guard for absence assertions preceded by a liveness assertion.
- `error-handling` is a BASE-REVIEWER dimension (per its criteria_routing.json `_comment`), so
  its language goes in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` §"Surface grounded
  findings": a short fail-open paragraph naming the shipped-code triggers — a silent
  lookup/membership MISS path, a subprocess check that never reads the returncode, a
  `pgrep`/`pkill` pattern that can match the matching process itself, any best-effort check
  whose failure is invisible — with the same litmus and the uniform remediation (assert the
  producer RAN before trusting any absence derived from it). The paragraph instructs the base
  reviewer to TAG such findings `error-handling` (routing hosts them @0.50), and delimits
  against the security overlay's same-named "fail-open error handling" antipattern
  (code-review-security.md): security-consequence fail-open (authz/validation fallback) stays
  with security; this language covers checks/oracles/health probes whose failure is invisible.
- Registry record: extend the `_comment` of the `tests` and `error-handling` entries in
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (this ticket + trigger list + placement
  ruling). No posture/threshold/blocking values change.
- Calibration corpus: add the nine instances as seeded-diff recall cases (pre-fix,
  `expect: finding`) each paired with a post-fix no-fire case (`expect: pass`) — 1–4 in
  `code-review-tests.eval.yaml`, 5–9 in `code-review-base.eval.yaml` (dso house style).
- Docs: code-review criteria have no per-criterion `rebar explain <id>` section (`_explain` in
  `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` covers plan-review criteria + guides only); the code-review
  author surface is `rebar explain review` (`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`).
  Default taken (see fork-record comment): document the pattern there with two worked examples
  (instances 1 and 6).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` — fail-open oracle antipattern + FP guard.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — error-handling fail-open paragraph.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` — `_comment` provenance only.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` — 4 recall + 4 no-fire cases.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-base.eval.yaml` — 5 recall + 5 no-fire cases.
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — pattern + two worked examples.

## Testing

- Offline (no model): `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py` — both extended specs must
  stay strict-clean (`validate_eval_spec(strict=True)`, registered scorers, every case has a
  `diff`).
- Live calibration replay (bedrock via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`): run each of the 18 new cases
  through its Pass-1 prompt via `rebar.llm.evals.eval_solver.run_case` (`code-review-tests` for
  1–4, `code-review-base` for 5–9). Each seeded pre-fix diff is MINIMAL — the fail-open defect
  is the only defect in it — so a grounded finding on it is attributable by construction.
  Decision rule: a pre-fix case passes iff it yields ≥1 finding AND the finding's quoted claim
  names the seeded fail-open defect (the quote is copied into the calibration comment, so the
  attribution is auditable); a pre-fix case whose only findings are about something else counts
  as a MISS. A post-fix case passes iff it yields ZERO findings (the `code_review_no_fire`
  presence/absence rule). If a post-fix case fires an UNRELATED finding, the seeded diff
  carries an incidental defect — revise the diff to remove it (keeping the liveness fix
  intact) and re-run until zero-finding; if the finding IS about producer liveness, the
  seeded fix is wrong — correct it and re-run. Every revision + final per-case result is
  recorded in the calibration comment.
- FP posture: both hosts are ALREADY blocking (`tests` @0.54, `error-handling` @0.50) so no
  advisory ramp applies; the FP measurement is the 9 post-fix no-fire cases plus the specs'
  standing no-fire families staying silent in the same replay. Record both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `code-review-tests.md` names the fail-open oracle antipattern with the producer-liveness
      litmus and matching FP guard; checked by `rg fail-open` on the file.
- [x] `code-review-base.md` carries the error-handling fail-open language (silent lookup miss,
      unchecked returncode, pgrep self-match, invisible best-effort failure); checked by
      `rg fail-open` on the file.
- [x] The `tests` and `error-handling` `_comment` fields in
      `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` record the triggers + this ticket; no
      routing VALUE changes (checked by diff).
- [x] Calibration: all 9 pre-fix cases yield ≥1 finding whose quoted claim names the seeded
      fail-open defect, and all 9 post-fix cases yield ZERO findings (with the unrelated-fire
      fallback protocol above); per-case quotes + results recorded as a ticket comment.
- [x] FP posture recorded in the same comment (hosts already blocking; standing no-fire
      families silent).
- [x] `rebar explain review` documents the pattern with ≥2 worked examples; checked by
      `rebar explain review | rg -c "fail-open"` ≥ 1 plus reading the examples.
- [x] Eval specs strict-clean offline; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py`.
baseline.summary: Code review has no criterion for fail-open checks, whose pass result is indistinguishable from never having run

# Establish a consistent, observable error-handling convention (remediation-led) + enable BLE001

## Context

A codebase-health audit (joe-janitor, 2026-06-24) found ~199 `except Exception`/`except BaseException` sites in `src/rebar` (~96 already `# noqa: BLE001`-justified, ~100 unguarded), ~104 scattered `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` diagnostics, and `logging` used in only a handful of modules with **no handler configured anywhere**. Each agent session invented its own swallow style (`pass`, silent fallback, ad-hoc stderr print), so unintended swallows hide real failures with no operator signal — a cross-session-inconsistency smell.

**This epic is remediation-led: the primary deliverable is remediated code that SETS the pattern, not a design-decision document.** The convention is established by an exemplar remediation (working code other batches copy) plus a CI lint gate, not by prose. This was decided after researching rebar's actual peers (basic-memory, the `modelcontextprotocol/servers` reference servers, mcp-atlassian) and the MCP framework itself — the chosen convention is deliberately boring and uses no novel/rarely-used elements.

## The convention (demonstrated by the exemplar, enforced by lint)

- **MCP surface:** don't catch-and-return error dicts — just `raise`; the MCP framework converts a raised
  exception into an `isError` tool result and keeps the connection alive. Use `ToolError` for intentional,
  clean client-facing messages (e.g. `ConcurrencyError`, validation).
- **CLI surface:** a base `RebarError` caught at the boundary maps to an exit code (already in place;
  `ConcurrencyError` -> exit 10).
- **Library:** named `logging.getLogger(__name__)` under the `rebar` root + a `NullHandler` in
  `__init__.py`; the CLI and MCP entrypoints each install a **stderr** `StreamHandler`.
- **Best-effort case:** inline narrow-and-log — **no shared helper** (peers don't have one; a helper would
  be novel). `try/except <type>: logger.warning(..., exc_info=True)`.
- **Terminal state = observability floor:** every broad catch must either log with `exc_info` OR carry a
  justified `# noqa: BLE001` (reason string required). Narrowing is opportunistic, with tests; fail-open /
  body-inspecting / public-API sites stay broad-but-logged.
- **Enforcement:** ruff **BLE001** (blind-except) and **T201** (print, scoped: banned in library/core/MCP,
  allowed in the CLI presentation layer) enabled in CI, gated behind a *shrinking* `per-file-ignores`
  allowlist (the existing `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` strangler pattern).

## stdout is sacred (the load-bearing constraint)

CLI *data* `print(json.dumps(...))` on stdout is a machine contract (the reconciler `json.loads` it at `reconcile.py:472`) and MCP-over-stdio reserves stdout for JSON-RPC framing. Only **stderr diagnostics** migrate to the logger; stdout data prints stay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The logging substrate exists (named loggers + `NullHandler` + stderr handler at both entrypoints) and
      a stdout-purity contract test guards the CLI data contract.
- [ ] An exemplar package (`llm/plan_review/`) is fully remediated to the convention and is the reference
      others copy; BLE001 + scoped T201 are enabled with a shrinking allowlist.
- [ ] The ~100 unguarded broad-except sites are remediated to the observability floor in batches (log with
      `exc_info` or justified `# noqa: BLE001`); no silent `except ...: pass` remains without justification.
- [ ] Where opportunistic narrowing surfaced a previously-hidden bug, it is fixed with a regression test;
      if no batch surfaced one, the close-out records that explicitly (so AC4 is not vacuously satisfied).
- [ ] The convention is durably documented in `CLAUDE.md` / a contributing doc (not only in the exemplar
      code + lint), so the rationale (raise-don't-catch on MCP, stdout-sacred, noqa-with-reason) survives.
- [ ] The allowlist is emptied; `make lint` + the full test suite pass; child tasks are parented here with
      file-impact set.
- [ ] One observable, lint-enforced way to do error handling across rebar's library / CLI / MCP surfaces.
- [ ] Failures that used to vanish silently are now observable on a stderr logger; `KeyboardInterrupt` /
- [ ] A future joe-janitor audit finds no unguarded blind-except cluster; new unguarded blind-excepts / stray
baseline.summary: Consistent error-handling pattern + eliminate unguarded except Exception

# The DC harness project has NO 'Epic' issue type, so the epic-parent path cannot be tested live

## Evidence

Harness run **30857265932** (main @ `b301e7513d`, i.e. WITH change 1311), `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link`:

    SETUP FAILED (not a rebar defect): project RBJSXPQ offers no 'Epic' issue type
    (has ['Sub-task', 'Task'])

`collected=58`, 6 failed / 51 passed / 1 xfailed.

The cell reported SETUP FAILED distinctly rather than as an ambiguous red — that branch was written for exactly this case — so the diagnosis cost nothing. But the consequence is real.

## What this blocks

The scratch project is created from whichever template the DC image ships, and that template offers only `Sub-task` and `Task`. **No Epic issue type means no Epic Link relationship can be created**, so on this harness:

 * [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] **AC1 cannot be arbitrated.** Change 1311's Epic Link write is
   unexercised live — the cell cannot reach the code. This is the THIRD distinct reason that AC has
   gone unproven (first the emit/apply gates were disjoint, then the greenhopper route 404'd, now
   the fixture cannot build the fixture).
 * [rebar:9bb9-56a3-e9c0-46e9] **AC3 likewise** — the read side cannot be proven for the epic case
   either, for the same reason.

Both changes are unit-proven and neither is live-proven. Given 1276, 1288 and 1302 each shipped mutation-proven and wrong, that is exactly the gap this epic exists to close.

## Why this is a harness defect, not a product one

Nothing about rebar is implicated. `_seed_epic` correctly discovers the project's issue types rather than hardcoding `Epic` (the same discipline `_subtask_type_name` follows), and correctly reports SETUP rather than blaming the transport. The gap is that the harness provisions a project which cannot express the relationship under test.

## Candidate fixes, cheapest first — none yet verified

 1. **Create the scratch project from a Jira SOFTWARE template** rather than whatever the image
    defaults to. Epic ships with the Software templates; the Core/Business ones do not carry it.
    `conftest.py:359` already records a prior attempt at pinning a template
    (`com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira:gh-simplified-kanban-classic`), so the machinery and the prior art
    both exist — check why that pin is not in force.
 2. **Add the Epic issue type to the project's issue-type scheme** after creation, via REST.
 3. **Provision a second project** from a Software template solely for the epic cells.

Option 1 is the obvious first try given the existing comment, but the template list an image offers is version-specific and must be READ from the instance, not assumed — the same lesson `_seed_epic` already encodes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the harness project (or a project the epic cells use) offers an `Epic` issue type, discovered
      from the instance rather than assumed
- [x] `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` EXECUTES — it reaches its assertions
      instead of reporting SETUP FAILED — on a harness run, with the run id recorded
- [x] whichever template or scheme change is made is discovered/verified at runtime, so a future DC
      image that ships a different template set fails loudly rather than silently reverting to a
      project without Epic
- [x] the canary line still shows `skipped` at its expected baseline — this must not be "fixed" by
      skipping the cell
baseline.summary: DC harness project has no Epic issue type, so the epic-parent path cannot be tested live

## Context / Problem

Best-effort tickets-branch push failures that are EXPECTED and AUTO-HANDLED are surfaced to agent-visible stderr at WARNING with wording that primes LLM agent sessions to assume the store is broken. Two 2026-08-21 session reports (~12 concurrent writers) show agents halting work to inspect `push.py` for a state that heals on the next successful write. Operator ruling (2026-08-21): "If these issues are expected and handled automatically, we need to stop surfacing them to sessions because it primes them to assume there's an issue and burn tokens investigating." Ruling update (2026-08-21): "We should suppress the message under normal load. This is noise, not an outage signal." — so under normal load (ordinary contention losses, transient transport retries, the routine unpushed-backlog suffix) the messages are suppressed from agent-visible output entirely (DEBUG at most), and a merely non-zero or shared backlog count is NOT an outage signal.

## Offending messages (all logger.warning, agent-visible)

1. `push.py:342` — "tickets branch push failed after 3 retries: <raw git stderr><suffix>" after
   losing a CONTENTION race; raw git stderr pattern-matches corruption to an LLM (`unable to
   update local ref`, `! [rejected]`). The sibling terminal site `push.py:323` "terminal push
   failed after recovery" is the same lost-contention outcome, same treatment.
2. `push_classify.py:225` — "transient transport fault (attempt x/y), retrying" — the code is
   already retrying itself; pure worry-bait.
3. `push_state.py:148` `unpushed_summary` — the "(N unpushed commits on origin/tickets..HEAD)"
   suffix: "HEAD" is the TRACKER's HEAD but a session reads it as its code worktree HEAD; the
   count escalates across ALL concurrent sessions; nothing states the self-healing contract.

## What must STAY loud (bug 2a76's rationale is still valid)

- Policy declines (hook declined, GH013, branch protection) — permanent, operator-actionable.
- Strict-mode callers — PushDeliveryError already raises; unchanged.
- A PERSISTENT/GROWING backlog — fsck PUSH_PENDING and the durable rebar-push-pending marker
  are the operator channels; a terminal failure with a PROVEN-growing count stays WARNING.

## Approach

Logging/wording only — no change to push behavior, classification, retries, or the durable marker. The first landing (Gerrit 2017, 8c71e91a54) did steps 1–2 and demoted the expected paths to INFO; the ruling update reopens this to demote them further, INFO → DEBUG (steps 3–5 as now worded). Encode expected-and-self-healing vs operator-actionable at the reporting seam (`push_classify`):

1. (LANDED in 2017) `push_state.unpushed_summary` names the tickets branch explicitly (no
   bare `..HEAD`) and states the self-healing contract: committed locally, publish on the
   next successful push. The suffix stays factual for policy declines — the "no action
   needed" clause is appended only on the demoted path (pt 3).
2. (LANDED in 2017) `push_state.backlog_grew(tracker, remote_ref)` — read-only compare of
   the current `unpushed_count` against the previous push-pending marker's `unpushed` count
   (no new persistent state). Ambiguity resolves to False — growth must be PROVEN before a
   report escalates to operator-loud.
3. `_terminal_severity` in `push_classify` (landed in 2017) returns (log level, backlog
   suffix) for a terminal best-effort push failure: WARNING for a policy decline in the
   terminal stderr or a proven-growing backlog stays; THIS change lowers the otherwise branch
   from INFO to DEBUG, keeping the appended "expected under concurrent tickets writers — no
   action needed" clause. Still called BEFORE `_raise_if_strict` records the new marker.
4. The two terminal lost-contention sites in `push.py` already log via
   `logger.log(level, ...)` from that helper (landed in 2017) — no push.py change needed; the
   pinned literals "failed after %s retries" / "terminal push failed after recovery" and the
   epoch-guard negative assertions stay honored.
5. Demote every mid-retry transient-transport notice from INFO (post-2017) to DEBUG, keeping
   the "retrying automatically, no action needed" wording: `_retry_transport_or_stop` in
   `push_classify` plus the recovery-leg notices in `push_recovery.py` (merge-leg, fetch-leg).
   The TERMINAL transport/policy warnings stay WARNING (bug 2a76 / f61c rationale).

Tests pinning the post-2017 level are retargeted in the same change: `test_push_strict.py` (mid-retry capture level) and the quiet-suite level assertions.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_store/push_classify.py — mid-retry demotion to DEBUG; terminal-severity helper
  returns DEBUG for the expected case (was INFO after the first landing).
- src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py — demote the merge-leg and fetch-leg mid-retry
  transient-transport notices to DEBUG (same class, same wording contract).
- tests/unit/test_push_expected_contention_quiet.py — retarget: expected-case silence at INFO
  and above + worry-free wording + growing-backlog escalation + no bare `..HEAD`.
- tests/unit/test_push_strict.py — retarget the mid-retry level pin to DEBUG.
- push.py / push_state.py / test_push_strict_happy.py / test_push_rejection_surfacing.py —
  unchanged this round (their 2017 state already satisfies the ACs).

## Testing

RED→GREEN (the retargeted tests fail on current main, pass after the fix), all caplog-level assertions on the `rebar._store` loggers:

- Expected case: a retry-exhausted lost contention race (every push non-fast-forward-rejected,
  recovery merges clean, no prior marker) emits NO record at INFO or above; a DEBUG record
  carries "failed after N retries", names the tickets branch, and states "expected under
  concurrent" + "no action needed"; no message contains bare `..HEAD`.
- Mid-retry transient transport notice is captured at DEBUG, below INFO.
- Growing backlog: with a prior marker recording a smaller `unpushed` count, the same terminal
  contention failure logs at WARNING (the sanctioned escalation).
- Preserved loud cases: the existing real-git policy-decline suite
  (test_push_rejection_surfacing) still passes at WARNING with reason + backlog count; strict
  callers still raise PushDeliveryError (test_push_strict / test_push_strict_happy).

Verification: targeted pytest on the push/epoch-guard suites (tests/unit/test_push_*.py, test_epoch_guard_matrix.py, tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py, tests/unit/test_commit_and_push*, tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py), then `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A lost contention race on a best-effort write emits NOTHING at INFO or above (DEBUG at
      most), while the state remains observable via push_status()/fsck PUSH_PENDING/marker.
      Checked by the new caplog test (no records >= INFO) plus the marker/fsck suites green.
- [x] Mid-retry transient transport messages (push_classify + both push_recovery legs) are
      DEBUG or below. Checked by caplog levels in test_push_strict.py and the new suite.
- [x] Every remaining backlog message names the tickets branch explicitly (no bare `..HEAD`),
      with the self-healing contract stated in the message text. Checked by wording assertions
      on the emitted records and the strict-message pins.
- [x] Policy declines, strict failures, and a proven-GROWING backlog remain WARNING/raise,
      byte-compatible where tests pin them (reason token, GH013 passthrough, backlog count).
      Checked by test_push_rejection_surfacing and test_push_strict staying green.
- [x] Tests pin expected-case silence at INFO and above, worry-free wording, plus the
      preserved loud cases. Checked RED on current main, GREEN after the fix.
baseline.summary: Expected tickets-push contention warnings prime agent sessions to investigate non-issues

## Context
Agent guidance needs evidence-based duration expectations for `review-plan` and `verify-completion`. Existing logs, sidecars, ticket histories, and the `rebar metrics` gate-economics lens may contain usable wall-clock observations, but their coverage and populations must be validated before documenting a range. Prior closed bug `exultant-neofascist-bluegill` established minutes-scale latency and investigated provider causality; this task measures current empirical percentiles.

## Scope
Read-only analysis. Do not modify agent guidance or production files. Present the statistics and the proposed documentation range to the user, then wait for explicit confirmation before creating or executing any documentation-change task.

## Plan
1. Inventory available duration sources: gate sidecars, usage/event logs, ticket details/comments, and `rebar metrics` gate-economics output. Identify which records measure complete end-to-end wall time versus LLM-only or partial phases.
2. Define reproducible populations for plan-review and completion-verifier runs, recording the observation window, success/failure inclusion policy, workflow/provider-era filters, deduplication rules, and sample sizes. Prefer complete attested end-to-end runs; report sensitivity or limitations where coverage differs.
3. Extract durations without mutating the tracker or repository, cross-check overlapping sources, and investigate outliers or malformed records before excluding them.
4. Compute p50, p90, and p99 using an explicitly stated percentile method. Report raw values in seconds and human-readable minutes.
5. Compute the requested expectation interval as `(p50 * 1.20)` through `(p90 * 1.20)` separately for each operation, plus a defensible rounded wording proposal.
6. Record commands, source locations, population rules, statistics, and limitations on this ticket. Present the results to the user and stop for confirmation; do not edit guidance in this task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Plan-review p50, p90, and p99 durations are reported with sample size, observation window, and source provenance.
- [x] Completion-verifier p50, p90, and p99 durations are reported with sample size, observation window, and source provenance.
- [x] The percentile algorithm, inclusion/exclusion rules, deduplication, and known coverage limitations are explicit.
- [x] `rebar metrics` output is evaluated and either reconciled with the independent extraction or documented as insufficient.
- [x] The proposed range for each operation is calculated from p50 + 20% through p90 + 20%, with both exact and rounded values.
- [x] Findings and reproducible evidence are recorded on the ticket.
- [x] No repository or guidance files are modified.
- [x] The user is asked to confirm the proposed wording/ranges before any documentation update.
baseline.summary: Quantify plan-review and completion-verifier duration percentiles

baseline.description:
## Why

The compaction fold claims an all-or-none contract (invariant I1): snapshot written first, sources renamed to `*.retired`, and on failure every completed rename reversed and the snapshot removed. But in `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (~lines 235-247) the rollback path only *logs* a failed reverse-rename and continues, then unconditionally removes the snapshot and returns failure. Because normal replay excludes `*.retired` (`src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py`), a source that failed to restore becomes invisible with no snapshot left to carry its folded effect — silent, undetectable data loss that violates the stated contract.

## What

Chosen approach (committed — not "retain OR sentinel"): **retain the snapshot.** The snapshot already carries the folded effect of every source, so keeping it is the minimal change and needs no new on-disk artifact. On any reverse-rename failure during rollback, skip the `os.remove(snapshot)` step, emit an explicit `rollback incomplete; run fsck` diagnostic, and return failure.

Key realization from the fsck code: with the snapshot retained, the residual mixed state is **already detectable and repairable by existing fsck** — no new issue kind is needed:
- A source that WAS reversed back to an active `.json` is a UUID in the snapshot's
  `source_event_uuids` whose active file "still exists" → the existing
  `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` check (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:302`) fires, and it is
  already in the `--repair-snapshots` rebuild trigger (`fsck.py:191`).
- A source that failed to reverse stays `*.retired` and folded in the snapshot — i.e. the
  normal healthy compacted state; no false positive (crucially, this means the detection
  does NOT fire on healthy fully-compacted tickets).
So this story's only production change is: **do not delete the snapshot** in the rollback-failure branch (plus the diagnostic). The existing `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` + `--repair-snapshots` path already reconciles the mixed state (confirmed against `fsck.py`), so **no fsck code change is expected**.

Two correctness facts, confirmed against the code (correcting earlier drafts):
- **Repair mechanism is REBUILD, not retire-only.** `--repair-snapshots` routes a
  `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` finding to `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:193-195`, `compact.py:289`), which WRITES A NEW SNAPSHOT
  from the full ordered log and retires the live raws. So the repair test must assert a
  new `*-SNAPSHOT.json` IS written and the formerly-active source IS renamed to
  `*.retired`, and a follow-up `fsck` exits 0 — NOT "no new snapshot written."
- **Reads are already safe in the mixed window (no double-count).** The reversed-to-active
  source keeps its ORIGINAL (old) filename, so it sorts BEFORE the retained snapshot;
  normal replay short-circuits on the snapshot and skips all pre-snapshot events
  (`src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, `_cache.py:110-113` positional skip), so the folded event
  is not re-applied. The mixed state is therefore read-correct BEFORE repair; the
  `rollback incomplete` diagnostic tells the operator to run `fsck --repair-snapshots` to
  NORMALIZE the hygiene inconsistency (`SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`), not because reads are
  wrong.
- **Durability of the decision.** Add an architectural comment at the retained-snapshot
  branch in `compact.py` explaining WHY the snapshot is intentionally not removed (so a
  future refactor doesn't "fix" it back into the data-loss hazard), and note the
  compact→fsck recovery contract in the concurrency docs.

- Add fault-injection tests (currently the negative suite injects only at
  `compact.lock.acquire` and `compact._git`, never in the rename loop).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (rollback-failure branch: retain snapshot + diagnostic)
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` (verify the existing `_check_snapshot`/`_scan` +
  `--repair-snapshots` rebuild covers the mixed state; extend only if a gap is found)
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` (new fault-injection tests)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Forward-rename fault test: inject `OSError` on the 2nd/3rd forward `os.rename`;
      assert nonzero exit, no active snapshot, every original filename restored, no
      stray `*.retired`, reduced state deep-equal to pre-compaction, clean `fsck`, and
      an idempotent re-compaction.
- [ ] Reverse-rename fault test: inject a forward failure AND a reverse-rename failure
      (so at least one source is reversed-to-active and at least one stays `*.retired`);
      assert the snapshot is NOT deleted, a recoverable diagnostic is emitted, and no
      source data is lost.
- [ ] In the mixed state BEFORE repair, a read is correct: the reducer's event-UUID set +
      payloads deep-equal the pre-compaction reduced state (the snapshot's positional skip
      excludes the reversed-to-active source; no double-count). The `rollback incomplete`
      diagnostic directs the operator to run `fsck --repair-snapshots`.
- [ ] `fsck` (no flag) reports `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` for the reversed-to-active
      source in that mixed state (existing detection), and does NOT flag a healthy
      fully-compacted ticket.
- [ ] `fsck --repair-snapshots` reconciles by REBUILDING via
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`: assert a NEW `*-SNAPSHOT.json` is written, the
      formerly-active source is renamed to `*.retired`, a follow-up `fsck` exits 0, and
      the reduced state is unchanged (deep-equal to pre-repair).
- [ ] An architectural comment in `compact.py` documents why the snapshot is retained on
      rollback failure, and the compact→fsck recovery contract is noted in
      `docs/concurrency.md`.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Fix compaction rollback-failure atomicity hazard + rename fault-injection tests

## Why
Epic AC1 requires a **write-time guard that rejects private-key material in an identity event**. The delivered `identity` create path (ddbe / change 558) passes `keys` straight onto the CREATE event with no check, so a user could accidentally commit an SSH PRIVATE key into the always-readable, replicated tickets store — a real (if narrow) footgun. The epic completion-verifier flagged this as unmet. (Remediation of epic gnu-whale-ichor to full AC coverage; see session_log fanatical-gentling-bushbaby.)

## What
Add a shared guard `reject_private_key_material(values: list[str])` in `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` that raises `CommandError` if any value contains a private-key PEM/OpenSSH header — matching (case-insensitive) any of: `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN DSA PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`, `-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----` (i.e. the generic `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` family). Call it:
- in `create_identity_core` on the `keys` list BEFORE `create_core` appends the CREATE
  event (no event written on rejection);
- in `add_identity_key` on the `public_key` BEFORE the KEY_ADD event is appended.
A legitimate authorized-keys public line (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`) passes unchanged.

## Scope
In: the `reject_private_key_material` guard + its two call sites (identity CREATE keys[] and KEY_ADD public_key). Out: any other behavior. The guard function lives in the ddbe commit (558); the `add_identity_key` call site lives in the e165 commit (563) — both are amended (the guard fn is defined in 558, so 563 can call it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `create_identity(name, email, keys=[<a string containing "BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE
  KEY">])` raises (CommandError/RebarError) and appends NO event (store unchanged); a test
  asserts the raise and that no identity was created.
- [ ] `add_identity_key(identity, <a private-key string>)` raises and appends no KEY_ADD
  event (test).
- [ ] A normal authorized-keys public line (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`) is accepted by both
  `create_identity(keys=[…])` and `add_identity_key` (test).
- [ ] The guard matches the common private-key header family case-insensitively
  (parametrized test over the RSA/EC/DSA/OPENSSH/PKCS8/ENCRYPTED headers).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (reject_private_key_material guard + create/key-add call sites)
baseline.summary: identity: reject private-key material at the identity write-gate (epic AC1)

# WS-DOC — docs/workflow-engine.md (intended use, for two audiences)

## Why

The workflow engine (epic a88f, closed; rebuilt under e6d9) has no canonical project
doc describing its INTENDED USE. Knowledge is scattered across README, docs/llm-framework.md,
CLAUDE.md, and closed tickets. New users and maintainers have no single anchor.

## What

Author `docs/workflow-engine.md` as the canonical anchor the review epics (5fd2/9da1)
point at. It MUST serve two distinct audiences and clearly separate them:
- a CLIENT / operator who will mostly RUN workflows and gates, not edit them;
- a REBAR DEV who authors/edits workflows, prompts, criteria, and evals.

## Scope

- When to use a workflow vs a bespoke op; the YAML DSL + schema; author/validate/render/run.
- Scripted vs agentic steps; the agent-vs-single-turn bright line.
- The three-tier (three-pass) LLM-review gating pattern (evidence -> binary-verify -> deterministic gate).
- The prompt-library + eval seam, including the two-tier eval model (deterministic gate every PR;
  LLM-judge tier off the PR critical path) and how the live tier is triggered + cost/fork-safety rails
  (reflects WS-EVAL-EXISTING as built).
- Prompt-authoring guidance for reviewer criteria (the research-backed do/don't list from the epic body).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/workflow-engine.md` exists and is linked from README + CLAUDE.md doc index.
- [ ] A clear CLIENT-vs-DEV split: a client can find run/use guidance without wading through authoring internals; a dev finds the authoring + eval surface.
- [ ] Documents the YAML DSL, scripted vs agentic steps, the agent-vs-single-turn bright line, and the three-pass gating pattern.
- [ ] Documents the eval seam: two-tier model, how to author a spec, how the live tier is triggered, cost + fork-safety rails (consistent with WS-EVAL-EXISTING).
- [ ] No contradiction with docs/llm-framework.md / docs/plan-review-gate.md (cross-link, don't duplicate).
baseline.summary: WS-DOC: author docs/workflow-engine.md (client vs dev audiences)

## Target
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — **799 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (1 lines of headroom).

One line of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split _engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py (799 LOC) along its concern boundary
