## The gap AS FILED — refuted before implementing

`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` was reported to match wrapper calls only by bare callable name, so that `core._git("commit", ...)` — an attribute on a module object passed in as a parameter — would escape it. **That is not the case.** `_ScopeLinter._wrapper_name` has carried an `ast.Attribute` branch (`func.attr in WRAPPER_NAMES`) alongside the `ast.Name` branch since the gate's first commit, 6739ea54fa ("d37e: lint gates raw git writes to seams"), confirmed by `git log -S'isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in WRAPPER_NAMES'`.

A synthetic probe (`/tmp/rebar-4073-9d4f-c644-44a9/probe`, `--report`) shows `core._git(root, ["commit", ...])`, `mod.run_git(root, ["add", "-A"])`, `core._git(root, *argv)`, `core.sub._git(...)` and `self._git(...)` ALL firing, `check` exiting 1, and `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` silencing the attribute form exactly as it silences the bare form. Full evidence is in the ticket comment.

`_ref_lock_push.py` has no hits for a different reason: its one wrapper call (`push_lease_cas`, line 116) passes `push`, which is not in `MUTATION_VERBS` (`{add, commit, rm, mv, reset, update-ref, checkout, clean}`). The gate saw the call and resolved its argv — it correctly declined to fire. `src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py` does not exist yet anywhere in the tree.

## What is actually wrong

The BEHAVIOUR is right; the EVIDENCE for it is missing. All 8 R2 tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` use the bare-name form (`test_wrapper_literal_mutation_verb_fires` through `test_sibling_wrapper_names_not_in_name_set`); not one exercises an attribute receiver, and the module docstring says only "BY NAME". Untested, undocumented coverage is coverage that reads as absent — which is how this bug came to be filed. Left alone it will be re-filed, and worse, a future refactor of `_wrapper_name` can delete the branch with every test still green.

## Change

Two files, no detection-logic change (a detection change would be wrong — the detection is correct):

1. `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` — a new R2 sub-section pinning the attribute form:
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_form_mutation_verb_fires` — `core._git(...)` / `core.run_git(...)`
     with a literal mutation verb each fire `wrapper-git-mutation`.
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_receiver_shape_does_not_matter` — `self._git(...)`, a nested
     receiver `core.inner._git(...)`, and an imported-module receiver `_ref_lock._git(...)` all
     fire, proving the match is on the attribute and not on any particular receiver shape.
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_form_opaque_argv_fires_and_marker_silences` — `core._git(root,
     *args)` fires the fail-closed `unresolvable-argv-wrapper`, and the SAME line with
     `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` is clean. This is the ACs' "existing exemption mechanics must keep
     working" requirement, on the attribute form.
   - `test_attribute_form_push_lease_cas_shape_does_not_fire` — the real `push_lease_cas` argv
     shape plus an attribute-form read (`rev-parse`) stay clean, pinning the disposition so the
     absence of a marker on `_ref_lock_push.py` reads as resolved rather than as a blind spot.
2. `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — the module docstring's R2 bullet gains the explicit
   statement that the name comes from the CALLABLE, so an attribute call is matched by its
   attribute whatever the receiver, and names the late-binding `core`-passing idiom as the
   reason that matters. Docstring only; `_wrapper_name`, `MUTATION_VERBS`, `WRAPPER_NAMES`,
   `_check_wrapper_call` and every marker path are untouched.

## Deliberately NOT done

Adding `push` to `MUTATION_VERBS` would make `_ref_lock_push.py` fire. That is a real but DIFFERENT question — what "mutation" means for a gate whose stated policy is local store writes (`git add/commit/rm`) — and it would flood every legitimate `git_adapter` and sync push site. Recorded in the ticket comment rather than smuggled in under a detection-blind-spot premise.

## Verification

- Mutation check (already run): deleting the two-line `ast.Attribute` branch from
  `_wrapper_name` turns exactly the three new detection tests RED (31 passed, 3 failed);
  restoring it returns 34 passed. The new tests therefore pin the branch rather than merely
  co-exist with it.
- Whole-repo re-run of the gate after the change: `python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py`
  exits 0 and `--report` yields the same 123-hit inventory as before, so no new hits need
  triage and no legitimate site needs a new marker (the change adds no detection).
- Full local gate set before push: every `scripts/check_*.py`, the generators' no-diff check,
  `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the CI pytest selection
  (`-m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300`), and
  `tests/integration` explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Attribute-form calls whose attribute is in `WRAPPER_NAMES` resolve: confirmed
      already true, with the reason and the probe evidence recorded on the ticket, and the
      coverage stated in the gate's own module docstring so it is no longer implicit.
- [x] AC2 — `_ref_lock_push.py` is explicitly dispositioned (seen, argv resolved, correctly
      not fired because `push` is not a mutation verb; no marker warranted) and the
      `push_recovery.py` half is recorded as moot (the file does not exist).
- [x] AC3 — Four tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` pin attribute-form detection,
      receiver-shape independence, fail-closed opaque forwarding, and marker sanctioning; three
      of them are shown to fail when the `ast.Attribute` branch is removed.
baseline.summary: check_raw_git_writes misses attribute-form git wrapper calls

## Summary

Current `origin/main` already contains the bug-2f46 core decoupling: `run_http_with_grace` drives certified-op drain through `InFlightGauge`/`drain_then_exit` and gives uvicorn a separate short graceful-shutdown timeout. This ticket closes the approved 2026-09-01 DECISION by making that separation explicit and durable for the parentless 40a7 bug: name the uvicorn timer as a transport backstop, set its concrete default to 30 seconds, preserve compatibility for existing callers, and add direct tests for the two shutdown directions the incident requires.

The certified-op drain grace remains `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 1200`. That value is the primary drain deadline for in-flight certified ops and is enforced by `drain_then_exit`; it is not uvicorn's `timeout_graceful_shutdown`.

Deadline-elapse disposition: if the certified-op drain deadline expires while the gauge is still busy, the retiring process sets `server.should_exit`; uvicorn begins graceful shutdown and the in-flight client receives the terminal shutdown/connection disposition from the transport. That is distinct from the idle path, where `should_exit` is set only after the gauge is already idle and uvicorn's short backstop sweeps idle held-open streams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` exports `DEFAULT_UVICORN_BACKSTOP_SECONDS = 30` as the named uvicorn transport backstop.
- [x] Existing imports of `DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS` remain compatible as an alias for the new backstop constant.
- [x] `run_http_with_grace` passes uvicorn `timeout_graceful_shutdown=int(uvicorn_backstop_seconds)` instead of using the certified-op `grace_seconds` value.
- [x] `run_http_with_grace` preserves the existing keyword `uvicorn_graceful_seconds` as a backward-compatible override for callers while documenting `uvicorn_backstop_seconds` as the preferred name.
- [x] `drain_then_exit` still uses `grace_seconds` as the certified-op drain deadline.
- [x] The SIGTERM handler calls `gauge.begin_draining()` immediately when retirement starts.
- [x] The SIGTERM handler sets `server.should_exit` only after the gauge is idle or the certified-op drain deadline elapses.
- [x] An idle-gauge retirement test proves `server.should_exit` is set immediately/quickly with `grace_seconds=1200`, demonstrating the early-exit path is well under the certified-op grace.
- [x] A busy-gauge retirement test injects a small `grace_seconds` and a shorter uvicorn backstop value and proves `server.should_exit` is not set until the gauge drains or the injected certified-op deadline elapses, so the short uvicorn backstop does not cut short an in-flight certified op.
- [x] The change is self-contained in in-process MCP shutdown logic and does not depend on any CI provider or deployment-specific external service.

## Testing

- Focused: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py -k "mcp_retirement or run_http_with_grace or drain_then_exit or sigterm"`
- Lint: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`
- Typecheck: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`
- Gerrit: land only after `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved comments.
baseline.summary: mcp retirement should codify a short uvicorn backstop separate from certified-op drain grace

## Why

Epic `850f` needs a place for a T2 semantic backend to plug in and be reported, without touching the
deterministic T1 lane or any consumer. Today `TIER_T2` exists in the closed tier vocabulary but is
never emitted, and member/dotted references abstain inline in `resolve.refute_absence`. This story
adds the opt-in, default-off seam and wiring; S3 adds the actual pyright backend behind it. Shipping
the seam separately keeps the seam change regression-safe and independently reviewable.

## What

- New module `src/rebar/grounding/semantic.py` (stdlib-only, import-clean) exposing:
  - `T2_BACKENDS: tuple[str, ...] = ()` initially — the closed set of selectable backend names. (S3
    adds `"pyright"`.) An unknown/empty selection fails open to disabled.
  - `refute_semantic(reference, *, repo_root, config, timeout=None, cache=None) -> dict | None` —
    returns a normalized `TIER_T2` evidence record (`refuted`/`abstain`) or `None` meaning "T2 declined
    to run; keep the caller's T1 record". With no registered backend it returns `None` (default-off).
    `cache` is a **caller-owned** optional mapping (mirrors T1's `index` param) for reusing one
    backend invocation across many references in a single review — no module-global mutable state, so
    no cross-thread concern.
  - `available_backends() -> list[dict]` — `[{name, available, version}]` for each name in
    `T2_BACKENDS`, each probed fail-open (empty while `T2_BACKENDS` is empty).
- Extend `GroundingConfig` + `load_config` in `resolve.py` with three `.rebar/grounding.toml`
  `[grounding]` keys (all default-off / safe):
  - `t2_enabled: bool = False`, `t2_backend: str | None = None`, `t2_timeout_seconds: float = 30.0`.
    Invalid types/values fail open to the default (never a raise), consistent with the existing loader.
- Wire escalation in `oracle.refute_absence` (the single consumer entry): after the T1/deps lane
  returns, if the record is an `abstain` on a `member`/dotted reference or a not-found bare
  `symbol`/`import`, call `semantic.refute_semantic(...)`; a returned `refuted@T2` replaces the T1
  abstain, otherwise the T1 record is returned unchanged. `resolve.refute_absence` is **not** modified
  (T2 stays out of the deterministic T1 lane).
- Extend `oracle._backend_availability()` to append `*semantic.available_backends()` so
  `grounding_info` reports T2 backends.

## Scope

In scope: `semantic.py`, the config keys, the `oracle` escalation + availability wiring, and unit
tests. Out of scope: the pyright backend itself and its extra/docs (S3). While `T2_BACKENDS` is empty
the seam is fully inert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/grounding/semantic.py` exists exposing `refute_semantic`, `available_backends`, and
      `T2_BACKENDS`.
- [ ] `semantic.py` is stdlib-only: `tests/unit/grounding/test_non_adoption.py` still passes
      (the import-purity guarantee holds).
- [ ] `GroundingConfig`/`load_config` expose `t2_enabled` (bool, default False), `t2_backend`
      (str|None, default None), and `t2_timeout_seconds` (float, default 30.0).
- [ ] Each new config key fails open to its default on malformed input (a test feeds a malformed
      `.rebar/grounding.toml` and asserts the defaults, with no raise).
- [ ] `oracle.refute_absence` escalates member/dotted and not-found-symbol abstains to
      `refute_semantic`.
- [ ] `oracle.refute_absence` returns `refute_semantic`'s `refuted@T2` when produced, otherwise the
      unchanged T1 record.
- [ ] `resolve.refute_absence` is unmodified (verified by diff review — the T1 lane stays out of T2).
- [ ] `oracle._backend_availability()` includes the T2 backends reported by `available_backends()`.
- [ ] `grounding_info()` output validates against `grounding_info.schema.json` after the change.
- [ ] Default-off regression: a test in `tests/unit/grounding/` asserts that with `t2_enabled=False`
      (empty `T2_BACKENDS`) `oracle.refute_absence` returns the pre-change evidence for a member/dotted
      reference (still `abstain` at `TIER_T1`).
- [ ] A seam-dispatch test using an in-test fake backend (monkeypatched into `T2_BACKENDS` +
      `refute_semantic`) shows a `refuted@T2` record replaces the T1 abstain.
- [ ] That `refuted@T2` record validates against `grounding.schema.json`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/grounding/` exits 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
baseline.summary: T2 grounding S2: pluggable semantic seam (refute_semantic + config + oracle escalation, default-off)

# WS6 — Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review

## Why
Epic `d251` (AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP) **shipped and merged** — including S4b's complete review-bot:
`src/rebar/review_bot/` (receiver `app.py`, `voter.py`, `gerrit_client.py`, `dedup.py`,
`reconcile.py`) plus the **verdict→label seam `adapter.code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root,
ref) → {decision, message, findings}`**. That seam is currently implemented over the OLD
single-pass `rebar.llm.review_code(...)` + a blocking-severity heuristic — a deliberate "proven
pipe" placeholder. `adapter.py`'s own docstring says: *"b744-WS6 will REIMPLEMENT this same
signature over `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` — drop-in, with no caller change."*

WS6 is exactly that swap: make Gerrit's `LLM-Review` vote driven by **our new four-pass code
review** (the deterministic Pass-3 blocker), not the single-pass demo.

## Realignment (2026-06-30) — supersedes the earlier standalone-package plan
The pre-merge WS6 plan (a NEW `src/rebar/gerrit/` voter package + REST client + patchset handler)
is **retired as redundant**: d251 already ships all of that in `src/rebar/review_bot/`. WS6 must
NOT build a parallel package — it CONSUMES the shipped receiver and swaps only the decision engine
behind the existing seam. The live dogfood is split out to WS6-b (`0da5`); the GitHub cutover to
WS7.

## What
- **Rewrite `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`'s `code_review_decision`** over
  `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` (the typed `PASS`/`BLOCK`/`INDETERMINATE` verdict):
  - keep the signature + return shape (`{decision, message, findings}`, plus an additive
    `coverage_gap` flag) so `voter.py` is unchanged;
  - map the verdict fail-closed (below); the four-pass gate's own Pass-3 thresholds
    (`criteria_routing.json`) decide PASS vs BLOCK, so the adapter no longer applies the
    `blocking_severities` severity heuristic (it becomes vestigial for this path);
  - review the receiver's cloned working tree by passing `repo_root` (the security detectors scan
    the changed files there) + the fetched `diff_text`.
- **Add an `enabled: bool | None = None` override to `produce_code_review_verdict`** so the adapter
  can pass `enabled=True` (force-enable): the code-review gate is OFF by default
  (`verify.enable_code_review`), but voter activation is itself the authoritative gate, so the
  per-repo flag would otherwise leave every change with the inert disabled verdict. (ADR 0015.)
- **Update `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`** adapter tests to drive the four-pass verdict (mock
  `produce_code_review_verdict`) instead of `review_code`.
- **ADR 0015** records the seam reimplementation + the force-enable rationale + the fail-closed
  vote mapping + the coverage-gap message distinction.

## Vote mapping (fail-closed; the gate's Pass-3 owns PASS/BLOCK)
`produce_code_review_verdict` emits three verdicts (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) plus an inert
disabled verdict. The adapter collapses them to the receiver's PASS/BLOCK (the voter then casts
`llm_review_max_value` / `llm_review_block_value` from `ReceiverConfig`):

| verdict / state | adapter decision | note |
|---|---|---|
| PASS + full coverage | PASS | advisory findings are surfaced in the message, non-blocking |
| BLOCK (blocking findings) | BLOCK | real finding (`coverage_gap=False`) |
| INDETERMINATE (LLM outage) | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap |
| PASS but `coverage.enabled==false` (inert) | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`gate-disabled`) — defense-in-depth |
| fail-closed security-scanner abstain | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`scanner`) |
| ANY exception / bad shape | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`review-error`) |

## Distinct coverage-gap message (infra vs code)
The vote comment (`ReviewInput.message`, posted by the receiver's `post_vote`) begins with a
machine-parseable tag so an INFRA `-1` is unmistakable from a real-finding `-1`:
`[LLM-Review: PASS]`, `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, and
`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (<gate-disabled|llm-unavailable|scanner|review-error>)]`. The
`coverage_gap` sub-reason is derived deterministically from `verdict.coverage`
(`enabled==false` → gate-disabled; `llm_unavailable` → llm-unavailable; a `security_detectors`
note with `reason=='fail-closed-abstain'` → scanner). A real secret MATCH
(`reason=='detector-finding'`) is a finding, NOT a coverage gap.

## Scope
- IN: the `adapter.py` reimplementation, the `produce_code_review_verdict` `enabled` override, the
  updated `test_review_bot.py` adapter tests, ADR 0015.
- OUT: the receiver/voter/gerrit_client/reconciler (d251 shipped them — unchanged); the live
  end-to-end dogfood (WS6-b, gated on the deployed env); the GitHub cutover (WS7).

## Dependencies
- CONSUMES d251's shipped `review_bot` package + the provisioned `LLM-Review` label / value
  mapping (`ReceiverConfig`). depends_on WS4 (98ff, closed) for `produce_code_review_verdict`.
- No live env needed: the adapter is fully verifiable offline (mock the verdict; the receiver's
  own tests already stub Gerrit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `review_bot/adapter.py`'s `code_review_decision` is reimplemented over `produce_code_review_verdict` with `enabled=True`; the signature + `{decision, message, findings}` return shape are unchanged (the voter is not touched).
- [ ] Vote mapping is exhaustive + fail-closed over PASS / BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / inert-disabled / scanner-abstain / exception; a test asserts each → the correct decision, and that an inert-disabled verdict never yields PASS.
- [ ] `produce_code_review_verdict` gains an `enabled: bool | None = None` override (default None = read config); a test asserts `enabled=True` forces the gate to run even when `verify.enable_code_review=false`.
- [ ] The vote message distinguishes a coverage-gap `-1` (sub-reason gate-disabled / llm-unavailable / scanner / review-error) from a real-finding `-1`, via the documented first-line tag; a test asserts the PASS tag, the finding tag, and each coverage-gap sub-reason.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` adapter tests are updated to the four-pass verdict (mock `produce_code_review_verdict`); the full `pytest -k review_bot` suite passes; ruff + mypy clean.
- [ ] ADR 0015 records the seam reimplementation, the force-enable rationale, the fail-closed vote mapping, and the coverage-gap message vocabulary.
baseline.summary: WS6: Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review

## Silent data loss in the store under concurrent write + in-flight review

**Evidence is SECONDHAND** — reported by the session working [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86], not reproduced by the filing session. Filed anyway because it is silent DATA LOSS in the ticket store, which is the system of record for every agent.

### What was observed

1. A `rebar edit --description` succeeded and was **verified by read-back at 14,997 chars**.
2. A subsequent `rebar show` returned **10,582 chars** — an OLDER revision. Nothing reported an
   error; no conflict, no `ConcurrencyError`, no exit 10.
3. The agent's next read-modify-write then grafted new edits onto that stale text, **corrupting an
   acceptance criterion** by splicing two unrelated fragments:

       - [ ] a gate run persists `finish_reason` (recorded for triage, deliberately not rendered) (the windowed distinct-ratio that
             rebar ticket 70bc establishes is computable from the record)

4. Only a further read-back caught it. The agent rebuilt from a saved good revision and verified
   the restore (15,666 chars, all markers present).

### The reporter's hypothesis (unproven)

The ticket was being edited **while its own `rebar review-plan` was running**, and a review emits its own `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar events (`sidecar_emitted: true`). Store reconvergence between the two writers is the suspected cause. Corroborating signal: a later write to the same ticket with **no review in flight** stayed intact.

### Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

* **Optimistic concurrency did not fire.** The documented protection is a `ConcurrencyError`/exit 10
  on a conflicting write. Here the write reported success, verified on read-back, and was then
  silently rolled back — which is the one failure mode the concurrency design is supposed to make
  impossible.
* **Read-back verification is not sufficient**, which invalidates the standard mitigation every
  agent is told to use. The read-back PASSED and the data was still lost afterwards.
* The practical rule that emerged ("never write to a ticket while its own review is running") is an
  undocumented landmine, and it conflicts with the normal remediate-then-review loop the plan-review
  gate asks authors to perform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the interaction is REPRODUCED deterministically (concurrent `rebar edit` + an in-flight
      review emitting sidecar events on the same ticket), or the hypothesis is falsified and the
      real trigger identified — the current evidence is a single secondhand observation
- [ ] it is established why optimistic concurrency did not reject the losing write; a silent
      last-writer-wins rollback on a ticket description is either a bug in the conflict detection
      or an undocumented property of sidecar reconvergence
- [ ] a write that will be discarded FAILS LOUDLY (`ConcurrencyError`/exit 10) rather than
      reporting success and reverting afterwards
- [ ] a regression test drives the concurrent-writer path and asserts the losing write is rejected,
      not silently dropped

## Context / Problem
`correctness` and `edge-cases` are BASE-REVIEWER dimensions — the base reviewer's evidence contract names them (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md:33-34`) and they are NOT in the closed `OVERLAY_IDS` tuple (`llm/code_review/registry.py:38-54`). Neither has a routing entry in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (22 keys today, one of them `_comment`), so every finding tagged with them resolves through the unknown-criterion default — `block_threshold` 0.95, not blocking (`llm/criteria/model.py:68-88`, constant `registry.py:148`). `concurrency` IS routed, but advisory: `"block_threshold": 0.95`, `"blocking_enabled": false`.

`regression` (0.54), `error-handling` (0.50), `api-compat` (0.51), `deletion-impact` (0.60) and `tests` (0.54) already block. `correctness` (n=909) and `edge-cases` (n=618) are the two largest un-routed dimensions in the code-v3 corpus, ranked 3rd and 4th by volume in `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md`. That document's 2026 adjudication held them advisory on a *rev_rr* argument, without ever measuring their block-impact at 0.54; this story measures it and routes them on the number.

**Measured** (author run, `--tracker` at a checkout's `.tickets-tracker`; 1262 code-v3 changes):

| criterion | thr | surviving | would-block | changes hit | % of all changes | mean validity | val<0.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| correctness | 0.54 | 715 | 62 | 51 | 4.04% | 1.00 | 0 |
| edge-cases | 0.54 | 485 | 27 | 22 | 1.74% | 0.99 | 0 |
| concurrency | 0.54 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0.00% | n/a | 0 |

**Corrections to the originating claim.** The claim that the escaped bug at `c3aec3eae6` produced a `correctness`/`edge-cases` finding at priority 0.60 is FALSE against the committed corpus: that change's stored code-v3 sidecar carries the finding on `["correctness","maintainability"]` at priority **0.3857 / validity 0.714**, so a 0.54 flip does NOT recall it. `d2dea317ec` has NO code-v3 sidecar at all, so no recall claim is measurable for it. Recall of those two changes is therefore dropped as a justification; the flip rests on the precision/friction profile above.

## Approach
1. Add a `--block-impact CRIT=THR` mode to `docs/experiments/calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py`
   that prints exactly the columns of the document's existing block-impact table
   (`code-review-threshold-calibration.md:121-137`), so those numbers become reproducible instead
   of hand-computed. The existing default output is unchanged.
2. Record the measured rows in `code-review-threshold-calibration.md` under a new heading
   `## Code-v4 friction replay at 0.54 (correctness, edge-cases, concurrency)`, one machine-parseable
   table row per criterion carrying its `% of all changes` and a `flip` / `hold` decision.
3. Route `correctness` and `edge-cases` in `criteria_routing.json` as base-reviewer rows shaped
   like `regression` (`"exec": "AGENT"`, `"applies_to": []` — both inert for a base dimension; only
   `default_posture`/`block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` are consulted), at
   `blocking`/`0.54`/`true`, since each measured at or under the **8.0%** operator-accepted budget
   recorded in the `tests` entry's `_comment` (`criteria_routing.json:111`). `concurrency` stays
   advisory: 1 surviving finding is below the calibration script's own `MIN_N = 25` power floor.
4. Replace the hard-coded `_BLOCKING_SET` literal in
   `docs/experiments/replay_code_v4_would_block.py` with a set derived from
   `registry.routing_index()` filtered on `blocking_enabled`, so its printed summary cannot drift
   from the posture it actually applies via `threshold_for`.

## Constraints
- The corpus is NOT committed (`replay_code_v4_would_block.py:16-18`). The measurement runs once by
  the author; only its OUTPUT lands. Every check below is corpus-free, offline and
  CI-provider-agnostic (`project.portability`): the new test reads the packaged JSON and the
  document, and `replay_code_v4_would_block.py` with no `--tracker` runs a self-check that exits 0.
- Adding routing keys widens the canonical vocabulary: the gate registers
  `canonical=lambda: frozenset(routing_index())` (`registry.py:167-171`), so
  `registry.effective_criteria()` grows by these two ids. Intended, and asserted.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` re-tunes `code_review.concurrency` (`trigger_tokens`,
  `applies_to` only). `criteria.overlay.effective_routing` merges an un-prefixed built-in id over
  the packaged entry field-by-field (`llm/criteria/overlay.py:320-362`), so it cannot clobber a
  packaged posture. No overlay edit; asserted.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`, `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md`, `docs/experiments/calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py`, `docs/experiments/replay_code_v4_would_block.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_routing.py` (new).

## Testing
The new test is corpus-free. It parses the packaged routing and the new document table and asserts the routing/document agreement, the numeric budget bound, the vocabulary widening, the overlay non-clobber, and the routing-derived replay blocking set. Existing `test_code_review_ws5.py`, `test_code_review_nit_routing.py`, `test_code_review_blocking_replay.py`, `test_criteria_snapshot.py`, `test_code_review_project_criteria.py` must pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `correctness` and `edge-cases` each have an explicit routing entry in the packaged
  `criteria_routing.json` and appear in `registry.effective_criteria()`; verified by
  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_criteria_routing.py -q`
  (the file does not exist today, so the command errors now).
- [x] For EVERY criterion whose packaged entry has `blocking_enabled: true` and which the new
  document table lists, the table's `% of all changes` parses as a number **<= 8.0**; and every
  criterion the table marks `hold` has `blocking_enabled: false`. Verified by the numeric-budget
  assertion in the same pytest run, which fails if a listed blocking row exceeds 8.0.
- [x] `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md` carries the new section; verified by
  `grep -c "^## Code-v4 friction replay at 0.54" docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md`
  printing `1` (it prints `0` today).
- [x] The `--block-impact` mode computes each column correctly; verified corpus-free by a unit
  test that feeds `block_impact()` a synthetic in-memory corpus with known priorities and asserts
  the resulting `would_block`, `changes_hit`, `of_all_changes` and `mean_validity` values.
- [x] The mode degrades safely with no corpus; verified by
  `.venv/bin/python docs/experiments/calibrate_code_review_thresholds.py --block-impact correctness=0.54 --tracker /nonexistent`
  exiting 0 (an empty corpus prints a zero-row table rather than dividing by zero).
- [x] `replay_code_v4_would_block.py` no longer hard-codes its blocking set; verified by
  `grep -c "^_BLOCKING_SET = (" docs/experiments/replay_code_v4_would_block.py` printing `0`
  (it prints `1` today).
- [x] That script still exits 0 with no corpus; verified by
  `.venv/bin/python docs/experiments/replay_code_v4_would_block.py` exiting 0.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`958e-f4b3-275c-4154` made the write-path drain gate O(1) on a **quiet** store by caching "nothing can be pending before T" in `.rebar/enrich-gate.json`. The marker is only ever *written* on a scan that found nothing:

```python
# src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:374-377
if out:
    _clear_gate_marker(tracker)
else:
    _write_gate_marker(tracker, now_ns, soonest)
```

So a **single** pending entry is enough to disable the fast path for the entire store, and every subsequent write pays a full walk of every ticket directory until the pending set empties again.

## Measured (2026-08-21, synthetic stores, marker forced cold)

| store size | pending | gate ms |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 1 | 116.9 |
| 1000 | 500 | 157.1 |
| 1000 | 1000 | 206.5 |
| 4000 | 1 | 560.3 |
| 4000 | 500 | 572.3 |
| 4000 | 0 | cold 525.7, **warm 0.110** |

- Cost is **linear in store size** (x4 tickets -> x3.6-4.8) and only weakly sensitive to backlog
  depth (x500 depth -> x1.34; x1000 -> x1.77).
- **Depth 1 already costs the full scan.** The trigger is binary, not proportional.
- The marker, when it engages, is ~4,800x faster (0.110 ms vs 525.7 ms).

On the live 4,938-ticket store this is 1,200-1,330 ms per write.

## Approach

Generalize the gate marker from "the whole store is quiet" to "everything OUTSIDE this recorded live set is quiet" — the set-valued form of f400's open question #3 ("nothing pending before index N", but keyed on the queue's real membership rather than a sort boundary). Concretely:

- `_write_gate_marker` records a third field, `live`: the ticket ids that had a live queue
  entry (enqueued, no later DONE) when the full scan ran. The full scan now ALWAYS writes
  the marker — the `if out: _clear_gate_marker(...)` branch (queue.py:374-377) goes away.
  With a non-empty pending set, `next_eligible_ns` is <= now by construction (a pending
  entry's eligible instant is its soak deadline, already past), so the marker never claims
  quiet for a noisy store.
- `_read_gate_marker` validates `live` (a list of strings, or absent/None from an older
  marker) and reports the whole marker untrusted on any wrong type, exactly like the
  existing fields — untrusted degrades to the full scan, the pre-existing behaviour.
- `pending_enrichment` gains a middle path: a TTL-fresh, non-future marker that does not
  prove quiet but carries a `live` list scopes the walk to reducing ONLY those tickets
  (`reduce_ticket` per live id — real per-entry reductions, so time-driven transitions:
  soak deadlines passing and leases expiring are still answered honestly). The full
  `os.listdir` walk remains the fallback for no/untrusted/expired markers. The per-entry
  scan loop — including the f400 `(not_before_ns, ticket id)` service-order sort — is
  extracted into ONE helper that both the full walk and the scoped walk call, so the scoped
  path returns exactly the order the full walk would for the same store state (the sort key
  IS the drain service order; f400's starvation fix must hold in precisely this backlog
  regime), and no function crosses the McCabe ceiling.
- Scoped probes do NOT rewrite the marker. Within a marker's lifetime the live set cannot
  grow (every queue append still clears the marker — rule 2 unchanged), and NOT refreshing
  `written_ns` preserves rule 3: the TTL still bounds the time since the last FULL walk, so
  the accepted append-during-scan race keeps exactly today's bound.

Honesty analysis (rule 1): the marker still only ever asserts ABSENCE of pending work — a quiet store, or quiet-outside-the-live-set. Pending verdicts always come from reducing real queue events; a stale or wrong marker can defer a drain (TTL-bounded, as today) but can never manufacture a pending ticket. The three-rule block comment (queue.py:232-254) is updated to document the live-set form and the previously undocumented never-writes branch's replacement.

Cost: a probe on a store with a standing backlog drops from O(store) (full walk, ~1.2 s at 4,938 tickets) to O(live set) reductions; the quiet fast path stays O(1). This preserves c1de's quiet-case 20 ms budget scope; the noisy-case cost now scales with the backlog, not the store.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py` — marker read/write/validation (`_read_gate_marker`'s
  widened return tuple; its only other caller, the former `_gate_marker_says_quiet`, is
  inlined into `pending_enrichment` — the sole call site — and deleted),
  `pending_enrichment` scoped-scan path + extracted scan helper, block-comment update.
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_queue.py` — new tests below; the 9 existing marker tests must
  pass unchanged (they pin the quiet path, TTL, invalidation, and corruption handling).

No other module changes: `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` and `drain` consume `pending_enrichment` unchanged; the marker file name, location (`.rebar` sidecar via `StorePaths`), TTL constant, and clear-on-append call sites are untouched.

## Testing

RED first (fails on current code), all counted by instrumenting `reduce_ticket` (`_count_reductions`), never wall clock (`check_wall_clock_asserts`):

- A store with a PERMANENTLY non-empty pending set (one eligible entry that is never
  claimed or done), parametrized over store sizes 4 and 40: after one cold scan, a repeat
  probe reduces exactly the live entries (1), independent of store size, and still returns
  the pending id. (RED: current code clears the marker and reduces all N every probe.)
- New-enqueue visibility through the scoped path: with a backlog marker standing, enqueue a
  second ticket with soak 0 — the append clears the marker, and the next probe returns both
  ids (never hides the newcomer behind the live set).
- TTL still bounds the scoped path: scoped probes do not refresh `written_ns` — a probe
  past the TTL performs a full walk again (reduction count == store size, and the marker is
  re-established by that walk).
- `live`-field validation: a marker whose `live` is wrong-typed (a string; a list with a
  non-string) is untrusted and degrades to the full scan, still returning the pending id.
- Time-driven transitions through the scoped path: a soaking live entry becomes pending
  once its deadline passes, and a claimed live entry becomes reclaimable at lease expiry,
  both answered from scoped reductions without a full walk.
- Ordering parity: on a store with several pending entries with distinct `not_before_ns`,
  the scoped-path result equals the full-walk result for the same store state — same ids,
  same `(not_before_ns, id)` order (the f400 service-order contract).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A store with a standing non-empty pending set does not pay a full store walk on every write.
- [x] The marker still only ever asserts absence of pending work (for the whole store or for
      everything outside its recorded live set); a pending verdict always comes from reducing
      real queue events.
- [x] Every queue append still invalidates the marker.
- [x] The marker is still TTL-bounded, with the TTL measured from the last full walk (scoped
      probes never refresh it).
- [x] A test seeds a store with a **permanently non-empty** pending set and pins the gate cost
      (by probe/syscall count, not wall clock — `check_wall_clock_asserts`).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit sweep are green.


## Scope note (post-land cleanup)

Commit 57f4ab26f5 accidentally included the scratch file `.review-out.txt` (review-plan output swept in by `git add -A`). It is inert (no runtime/test behavior) and is deleted by follow-up Gerrit change 2105 on this same ticket. `file_impact` declares it for the completion gate.
baseline.summary: enrich gate marker is all-or-nothing: one pending entry disables the O(1) fast path store-wide

baseline.description:
## Summary

The plan-review gate's **deterministic Layer-1 floor** admitted a ticket that violates two of its own blocking checks, while blocking two sibling tickets of the SAME shape in the same minutes.

## Evidence

Three children of epic `undamaged-murderous-horse` (f79d-0d71-0fd7-439f) were filed by the same sweep, in the same format: a bare prose finding with **no `##` headings at all and zero `- [ ]` checkboxes**.

All three were reviewed concurrently at ~11:56-12:02 PDT on 2026-09-02, same store, same build:

| ticket | shape at review | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `refutable-goosebumpy-opossum` (545a-4db5-3a64-42d9) | bare prose, 0 headings, 0 checkboxes | **BLOCK** |
| `misandrous-defaceable-zenaida` (0d3c-ff25-5317-4d73) | bare prose, 0 headings, 0 checkboxes | **BLOCK** |
| `classical-grey-ayeaye` (fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad) | bare prose, 0 headings, 0 checkboxes | **PASS + signed** |

Both BLOCKs cite the floor verbatim:

- "The ticket fails the deterministic readiness floor: no standard `## Acceptance Criteria` checklist."
- "The plan states no verification: no Testing/Verification section and no acceptance criterion names a proving command or verification step."

`classical-grey-ayeaye` satisfies NEITHER condition and was nonetheless signed. Its result carries `coverage.llm_ran: true` and `source: attested`, so this was a full review, NOT a short-circuit reuse of an older attestation and not a cached verdict.

Reproduce the shape difference:

    rebar show classical-grey-ayeaye   # 0 headings, 0 checkboxes -> PASS
    rebar show <either sibling>        # same shape at review time -> BLOCK

(The two siblings now show 5 checkboxes because they were rewritten IN RESPONSE to the block; the store's event history holds their pre-rewrite descriptions.)

## Phase 1 confirmed RCA and repair plan

The CREATE events in `.tickets-tracker/{545a-4db5-3a64-42d9,0d3c-ff25-5317-4d73,fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad}` hold the review-time bare descriptions. Direct runtime calls to `det_floor.run_det_floor(PlanContext(...))` over those exact descriptions all produce P1 and P10 blocking findings. Driving the production workflow precheck over the same three descriptions explains the divergence: task tickets keep P1/P10 in `det_blocking` and return terminal BLOCK, while ordinary bug tickets go through `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py::plan_review_precheck`'s lightweight bug-tier branch, where P1/P10 are moved from `det_blocking` to `det_advisory`; the later LLM tier can then return PASS and sign. The responsible path is the bug-tier DET downgrade in `plan_review_precheck`, not nondeterministic parsing, batching, or model sampling.

Minimal fix: keep the lightweight bug review tier for well-formed ordinary bugs, but preserve P1/P10 readiness-floor failures (and existing P4 description-limit failures) as authoritative DET blocks before any LLM pass. Non-readiness DET findings remain advisory in the bug tier. Documentation is updated only to match the restored contract.

Regression plan:

- Direct-floor unit coverage proves all three exact pre-rewrite descriptions trip P1/P10.
- Production `plan_review_precheck` coverage proves all three exact descriptions short-circuit to BLOCK, including the `classical-grey-ayeaye` bug fixture.
- The same test runs the collection in normal and reversed order to prove order independence.
- Existing well-formed bug-tier tests prove a clean bug still runs the substantive lightweight advisory LLM tier and is not restored to bare exemption.
- Mutation check reintroduces the P1/P10 downgrade and confirms the held-out regression test returns RED.

## Why it matters

1. **A signed attestation is the artifact the claim gate consumes.** A plan admitted without
   acceptance criteria produces a certified claim for work whose completion cannot later be
   verified — the completion verifier reads those criteria. The close then fails for a ticket
   whose plan the gate itself certified as ready, which is where I hit it.
2. **"Deterministic" is the floor's whole selling point.** Layer 1 exists so a structural defect
   is caught identically every time, before any model judgment. If it is order-, batch-, or
   model-dependent, an author cannot tell a real structural gap from a coin flip, and the
   documented revise -> review -> claim loop stops converging.
3. It silently weakens every downstream gate that assumes a reviewed plan has criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: the floor's `## Acceptance Criteria` check and its Testing/Verification check produce
      the SAME verdict for the same description text, independent of concurrency, batching, or
      model sampling. Verified by a test feeding the three descriptions above through the floor
      directly and asserting all three BLOCK, and by driving the production precheck path to prove
      no later LLM path can discard those P1/P10 blocks.
- [x] AC2: a regression test pins the exact `classical-grey-ayeaye` pre-rewrite description (from
      the store's event history) as a BLOCK case, so this specific admission cannot recur.
- [x] AC3: the root cause is identified and named — whether the floor is bypassed on some path,
      evaluated non-deterministically, or its result discarded when a later pass returns PASS.
      Verified by the fix citing the responsible code path.
- [x] AC4 [non-codebase]: if any other signed attestation in the store was minted over a plan
      lacking acceptance criteria, those tickets are listed in a comment so their claims can be
      re-reviewed rather than silently trusted.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py -k "plan_review_bug_floor" -q` — direct-floor and production-precheck regression/determinism tests over the three pre-rewrite descriptions.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py tests/unit/test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py tests/unit/workflow/test_det_short_circuit.py -q` — preserves bug-tier, escalation, and DET short-circuit behavior.
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
- `rebar explain plan` remains accurate about what the floor requires.
baseline.summary: Plan-review deterministic floor is not deterministic: an AC-less, Testing-less plan was signed while two identical siblings were blocked

Scope: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` (95 files, 27,284 LOC, 42% comment density). ~970 lines leave — the largest shard.

Dominant category: 28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines), already single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, AGENTS.md and ADR 0058.

Four new ADRs proposed, each consolidating an argument restated 4-8 times: field-convergence fit-then-normalize (8 sites); pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers (3 independent arguments, 3 prior incidents); unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps. Plus amendments to ADR 0028, 0055 §(g), 0031, 0035.

Verified stale: `_backend_registry.py:3` 'STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented' while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; the S3/S4-not-landed notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`.

Headroom: `_ref_lock.py` 1 -> ~21, `dispatch_one.py` 14 -> ~57, `inbound_differ.py` 18 -> ~66, `binding_store.py` 18 -> ~33, `fetcher.py` 29 -> ~80.

This subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured external-API facts that cannot be re-derived from code. The do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G1G2/G6)

### 1. The dominant-category count was wrong — re-measured

The body claims "28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines)". That is not borne out by the tree. Measured over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

    $ grep -rn "RELOCATED VERBATIM" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # 6 sites, ALL under adapters/jira_datacenter/
    $ grep -rniE "800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # a SEPARATE, smaller set (transport.py, retry.py, transitions.py)
    $ grep -rliE "RELOCATED VERBATIM|800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" ... | wc -l
    10                      # 10 distinct files carry EITHER marker

No single site carries the quoted combined marker. The two families are disjoint, and neither is close to 28. The real figure is **~12 occurrences across 10 files**, not 28.

**Consequence for the shard's headline yield.** The "~970 lines leave" estimate was built on the inflated count for its largest single category. That estimate is therefore UNRELIABLE and must not be treated as a target. The implementer MEASURES the actual recoverable total and records it on this ticket; the number is an output of the work, not an input to it. Do not manufacture relocations to reach ~970.

### 2. Write-ordering must cover the ADRs, not just `do_not_move`

The plan requires the `do_not_move` list to be appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands, but says nothing about ordering for the four proposed new ADRs (field-convergence fit-then-normalize; pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers; unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps) or the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035.

Those ADRs are the single-source DESTINATIONS for the arguments currently restated 4-8 times. If a comment citing "see ADR NNNN" is collapsed before ADR NNNN exists, the citation dangles and the argument is simply LOST — which is the opposite of relocation and is not recoverable from the diff by a later reader.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] The shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it
      is collapsed or deleted — destination first, then the relocation
- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination; nothing is deleted
      without a destination that already exists
- [ ] The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the
      unreliable ~970 estimate. The measured marker counts (6 RELOCATED VERBATIM, 6 cap mentions,
      10 files) are the corrected baseline
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are CORRECTED where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete — specifically `_backend_registry.py`'s "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be
      implemented" (false: `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules) and the S3/S4-not-landed
      notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay VERBATIM (this subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured facts that cannot be
      re-derived from code — the do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard)
- [ ] No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged

## Summary

The `langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)` job of the `external-integration` workflow has been broken since the d6d1 cutover (2026-06-22) and tests behavior that no longer exists. Two independent breakages:

1. **Readiness probe imports an uninstalled SDK.** `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:128`
   runs `from langfuse import get_client; assert get_client().auth_check()`, but the `langfuse`
   Python SDK was dropped from `[agents]` in c282b2950. `pip install -e '.[dev]'` no longer
   installs it, so all 24 readiness iterations raise `ModuleNotFoundError` — hidden by
   `2>/dev/null`, masquerading as "Langfuse project did not initialize in time".

2. **Test asserts a removed trace_id round-trip.** `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py:100` asserts
   `result["trace_id"]` is truthy and fetches `GET /api/public/traces/{id}`. The runner now
   hardcodes `trace_id=None` (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:391); the SDK trace-id capture was deleted
   in 2e9bd4205 when tracing became write-only OTLP export (src/rebar/llm/tracing.py). Also the
   job never installs `[tracing]`, so `setup_tracing` no-ops and no spans are exported at all.

## Decision (user, 2026-07-09)

Rewrite the job to validate CURRENT behavior (write-only OTLP span export to Langfuse), not the removed SDK trace_id round-trip.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Trigger the `external-integration` workflow (langfuse-trace job).
2. Observe "Wait for Langfuse to be ready" time out after 120s ("project did not initialize in time").

Expected: readiness passes; a review run's OTLP spans land in Langfuse and the test confirms it. Actual: readiness fails on a hidden ModuleNotFoundError; the test would fail on the None trace_id anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Readiness probe no longer imports the langfuse SDK; uses a REST check (e.g. `curl -fsS -u pk:sk .../api/public/projects`) and does not mask stderr.
- [ ] The langfuse-trace job installs the `[tracing]` extra so OTLP export actually fires.
- [ ] `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py` asserts OTLP spans for a review run are ingested by Langfuse (fetched via REST), with no reliance on a runner-surfaced `trace_id`.
- [ ] Verified end-to-end: the rewritten test passes against the docker-compose.langfuse.yml stack with a real review call, and the external-integration GitHub Action's langfuse-trace job runs successfully.
baseline.summary: langfuse-trace job tests removed behavior + readiness probe imports uninstalled SDK

## Context

A documentation audit (final unified report, evaluated at commit `2272d68ca` = `origin/main`) surfaced front-door defects and factual drift in rebar's docs. Every finding was re-validated against `origin/main` before filing this epic; one audit finding (that `docs/config.md` mis-describes the config-file format) was **REFUTED** — the loader matches the doc exactly — and is deliberately excluded.

Our audiences are human clients, LLM clients, human contributors, and LLM contributors. The two highest-leverage moves are (a) fixing the immediate defects that break onboarding/trust, and (b) adding cheap **drift-proofing** so the same class of staleness cannot silently return — the true lever on maintenance burden.

### Validated findings this epic remediates
- P0: README `session-log` syntax is invalid (missing subcommand); README quickstart
  is not actually one ticket end-to-end (hard-coded `reel-lot-tea`, separate Python
  ticket, MCP shows config only).
- P1: dependency count + `mcp` floor wrong in README and `docs/config.md` (truth: 3
  base deps, `mcp>=1.9`); `docs/output-schemas.md` points at a moved source path and
  describes a removed bash shell-out; stale bash-engine language in CI comments +
  `leaf.py`.
- P2: `docs/README.md` index is incomplete (4 unlinked living docs) and mixes living
  references with historical evidence.

### Reuse note (avoids duplicate work)
- `scripts/probe-rebar.sh` already implements the full install→…→close golden path;
  it just is not wired into CI.
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` + its CI drift gate is a proven **generator +
  drift-gate** pattern to template for new generated references.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tickets are closed (each with green CI / `Verified +1`).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the assembled stack. This
      aggregate integration check is owned at the EPIC level (not any single child):
      the executor runs it on the full assembled stack before landing, as the
      parent-level close gate.
- [ ] The refuted config-format finding is NOT acted on (no spurious change).
- [ ] Lower-value inventory work (Python-API / config-key) is captured as an `idea`,
      not shipped speculatively.
- [ ] The golden-path CI gate runs the **literal commands extracted from the README quickstart fenced block** (not merely an independent probe with its own syntax), so a wrong command *printed* in the README — e.g. the `session-log` missing its `append` verb — fails the build. This is the mechanism that makes command *text* rot (not just executability) a hard CI failure, and doubles as the end-to-end new-user onboarding validation (CI follows the README exactly as a cold reader would).
- [ ] Docs-index completeness/drift fails the build (docs-index CI gate `f088`): every
      living/normative `docs/*.md` is linked from the index, and the relative links
      the remediation touches (index entries + inbound links to docs relocated under
      `docs/archive/` by `9d81`) resolve. Scope is bounded to index completeness and
      the links this epic manages — it is the enforcement arm of the P2 finding, not a
      general site-wide linter.
- [ ] Generated CLI + MCP references drift-gate against their live registries.

### Drift-proofing mechanism — how command *text* rot fails the build (closes G6/F4)
The audit gap is that testing command *executability* (running `probe-rebar.sh`, which uses its own internally-correct syntax) does NOT catch a wrong command *printed in the README*. So the golden-path gate (ticket `contained-dendritic-angora`/0435) is scoped to **extract the fenced command block(s) from the README quickstart and execute those exact lines** in a throwaway repo. A stale/invalid README command then exits non-zero and fails CI. This is both the text-accuracy drift guard (G6) and the concrete end-to-end onboarding validation (F4): a new user copy-pasting the README is exactly what CI now does.

### Shared-file edit ordering (closes P5)
Several children edit `README.md` (session-log fix `a41f`, quickstart repair `b55f`, dep-count `319a`, catalog-trim `b5a4`). These are **serialized through the review stack in dependency order** — each change is built on the prior one (a41f → b55f → 319a → … → b5a4), so there is no concurrent same-file edit; `b5a4` additionally `depends_on` the generated-reference tickets (`e866`, `235a`) it links to. The stack order IS the observable ordering proxy: a later change rebases on the earlier landed change, never races it.

The SAME single-linear-stack serialization covers the other shared files: `.github/workflows/test.yml` (edited by `0435`, `e205`, `e866`, `235a`, `f088`) and `docs/README.md` (edited by `9d81`, `6755`) are each modified by exactly one change at a time in stack order — every change is built on the prior landed one, so there is never a concurrent same-file edit to reconcile. Execution is a single agent driving one relation-chain, so the dependency order and the stack order are the same total order.
- [ ] Every validated defect above is corrected against `origin/main`.
- [ ] New CI gates make quickstart-command rot and docs-index drift fail the build
- [ ] The docs index is complete and clearly separates living reference from historical
- [ ] Volatile command/tool surfaces move toward generated references so they cannot go
baseline.summary: Documentation remediation: fix front-door defects, drift-proof the docs, clarify taxonomy

baseline.description:
# Close-workflow contract architecture — deferred design record

## Status

Captured as an **idea**, not an implementation plan. RP04 was rejected from the 2026-08-29 Janitor pass by maintainer direction on 2026-08-30. Do not decompose, claim, or implement this work until the idea is deliberately promoted after its blocking architecture decision is resolved.

Origin: Janitor audit `literal-subaverage-dartfrog` (`673c-f602-748b-4b90`), audited snapshot `9a94ef9737fbdf070ae314bba6e797319aee2301`, report `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-29.md`.

## Finding

The close path has accumulated a behavior-bearing parameter train across transition dispatch, structural/gate checks, receipt preparation, atomic publication, candidate delivery, and public-result adaptation. Its values come from materially different authorities and have different freshness, mutability, ownership, and consumer lifetimes. Passing them as one flat set makes stale observations look like current proof, runtime capabilities look like values, and outputs look like operation inputs.

Evidence at the audited snapshot includes:

- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:284-314,373-393` — validation/no-op ordering and generic dispatch into the close-named path.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:568-633` — graph observations, ref pinning, ticket reduction, and plan-review guard occur at different times.
- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:682-691` — disposition evidence is selected during precheck.
- `src/rebar/_commands/completion_bundle.py:68-114,339-350` — atomic selection and a mid-operation `sync.push` reread.
- `src/rebar/_commands/completion_txn.py:121-194` — locked HLC/authorship/finalization and hard-coded `in_progress -> closed` publication.
- `src/rebar/_commands/completion_delivery.py:616-627` — delivery rereads configuration again.
- `docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md:81-112` versus `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:218-238` — one operation snapshot conflicts with D8's live mid-run policy check.

At that snapshot, `transition.py`, `transition_close.py`, and `close_precheck.py` were each approximately 795–797 lines, leaving no room to layer another context object under the 800-line module cap.

## Design progression

1. **Original RP04:** construct one immutable close-publication context and carry it through validate, prepare, publish, and deliver while re-splitting the close modules.
2. **Source-oriented refinement:** distinguish caller-supplied close intent, configuration-derived policy, close-process observations/decisions, publication artifacts, outputs, and live runtime resources. Grouping by source is appropriate at ingress; grouping by phase, lifetime, and consumer is required for derived state.
3. **First independent codebase review:** separate `CloseRequest`, focused policy projection, evidence decision, atomic/legacy staging, receipt-validated publication base, and outcomes; preserve public generic transition APIs, transaction ownership, deep immutability, and dynamic compatibility seams.
4. **Second adversarial Python review:** verdict **accept with changes; not implementation-ready**. It rejected a broad `ClosePreflight`, a decorative `LegacyClosePlan`, and plan-owned `EventProvenance`; required a factory-proven atomic edge, separate gate/delivery policies, single lexical ownership of the mutable candidate resource, and an explicit resolution of the two competing configuration authorities.

## Current candidate boundary model

```text
CloseRequest                         normalized caller intent
CloseGatePolicy                     projection of one OperationSnapshot
CompletionDeliveryPolicy            separate projection of that snapshot
runtime capabilities                verifier/store/signer/Git/clock/finalizer
          |
          v
CloseEvidenceDecision
          |
          +-- legacy close function
          |
          +-- factory-only AtomicCertifiedCompletionClosePlan
                         |
                         v
             per-attempt _ValidatedPublicationBase
                         |
                         v
             context-managed CompletionCandidate
                         |
                         v
              DeliveryOutcome -> CloseOutcome
```

Candidate rules:

- Construct `CloseRequest` only after transition validation and same-status no-op handling, and only for a real close.
- Treat target `closed` as implicit. Idea rejection remains derived from ticket status rather than caller-selected command type.
- Derive separate `CloseGatePolicy` and `CompletionDeliveryPolicy` values from one authoritative operation snapshot.
- Keep verifier, signer, finalizer, repository, Git, clock, identity, metrics, and the disposable candidate outside immutable data contracts.
- Represent evidence as a typed decision union while retaining existing durable verdict/signature payloads as recursively frozen mappings.
- Permit `AtomicCertifiedCompletionClosePlan` construction only for non-forced, certifiable, receipt-bearing, attested `in_progress -> closed` decisions whose requested and receipt-observed status and code basis agree.
- Factory-produce the per-attempt publication base after receipt replay and bind both the tickets OID and exact receipt digest.
- Keep final HLC ordering, authorship, and finalizer execution under the write lock.
- Recheck freshness-sensitive structural guards under lock or against a validated tickets OID; pre-lock graph observations are not proof.
- Make `CompletionCandidate` a mutable context-managed resource with one lexical owner. Model delivery state with an enum and derive retry/idempotence properties.
- Keep the legacy path as an ordinary function. Preserve CLI/library/MCP schemas, signer/re-export and monkeypatch seams, force/idea/disposition ordering, atomicity/idempotence, and pre-lock malformed-config failure.
- Extract existing call-graph units rather than adding branches to the three near-cap modules.

## Blocking architecture decision

Choose exactly one configuration authority before promotion:

1. **Recommended:** make the operation's immutable `OperationSnapshot` authoritative for close gate and delivery policy, then update the superseded ADR 0005 D8 wording, documentation, and tests; or
2. Record a narrow superseding ADR exception that deliberately permits a live policy reread and precisely defines which values may change mid-operation.

The implementation must not silently combine selection from configuration version A, transaction validation from version B, and delivery from version C.

## Promotion bar

Before this idea can become executable work:

- Resolve and record the ADR 0098 / ADR 0005 D8 authority decision.
- Re-audit the current close path and any store/runtime binding delivered since the audited snapshot.
- Demonstrate that each proposed type enforces a real invariant or crosses a real module/lifetime boundary.
- Provide a behavior-preserving migration that keeps public and dynamic compatibility seams.
- Include regression coverage for no-op, idea/force/disposition precedence, direct-close fallback, snapshot mutation, ticket/store drift, digest mismatch, retries, ambiguous delivery, and candidate cleanup.
- Include mutation tests for atomic-edge selection, digest matching, cleanup, gate precedence, locked guards, idempotence, and delivery-state derivation.
- Fit the module-size and complexity ratchets through call-graph extraction.

## Janitor disposition

Rejected from RP04 for this Janitor pass and excluded from Janitor Cleanup ticketization. This is a deferral for unresolved architecture and scope, **not** a known-fine blessing and not a conclusion that the finding is invalid.
baseline.summary: Decompose the close workflow into authority- and lifetime-correct contracts

## Context
Organic Gerrit Verify run 31846417650 emitted 260 fixture_setup spans over 1 second totaling 380.393 aggregate worker-seconds. Excluding the separately proven 35-second editor DNS delay, the largest module totals were: tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py 28.998s / 23 setups; tests/interfaces/queries/test_list_filters.py 25.856s / 17; tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py 19.230s / 7; tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py 16.486s / 11; and tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py 12.846s / 9. Closed precedent peculiar-calmy-bubblefish proved that a session template plus isolated per-test copies reduced tests/interfaces wall time from 270.7s to 186.5s (31%) while running nine more tests, and explicitly deferred roughly 20 module-local fixtures as the larger remaining win.

## Phase 1 plan
- Trace each measured >1s setup to its exact fixture and separate from-scratch git/rebar store initialization, fixture copying/fix-up, test-body work, and runner variance with setup-only timing plus runtime instrumentation.
- Test the dynamic hypothesis that the five modules repeatedly build equivalent virgin git-backed stores. Confirm only where the same initialized precondition recurs; reject template reuse for fixtures whose setup semantics intentionally vary or whose contract is initialization itself.
- Search ticket history for prior acceptance/rejection and compare the remediation with at least three popular, actively maintained OSS projects using session-scoped expensive templates with isolated per-test copy/reset. Apply the parent ticket consensus rule: at least two-thirds use the practice and none documents rejecting it for coverage/reliability.

## Phase 2 plan (only after confirmed RCA and consensus)
- Add or extend one uniquely named test helper at an existing call-graph seam; use session/worker-local templates and per-test copies only for confirmed equivalent fixtures.
- Preserve the safety contracts established by peculiar-calmy-bubblefish: rewrite both linked-worktree pointers, reject bare git worktree repair, allocate a per-test gate snapshot directory, regenerate environment/signing identity, reset module caches, keep the template virgin, and retain deliberate from-scratch initialization/recovery tests.
- Prove RED->GREEN with durable isolation sentinels before migrating consumers. Do not remove, skip, sample, xfail, or weaken any behavioral assertion.
- Run every affected module, full owning tiers, the full default/integration selectors, lint, typecheck, and workflow guards. Measure paired before/after setup and wall time under the same environment and report runner-seconds saved without claiming critical-path savings from aggregate fixture time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every targeted setup is attributed to a specific fixture operation with a focused measured baseline.
- [x] The confirmed RCA includes a runtime experiment that discriminates repeated equivalent store construction from test-body work and unavoidable per-test semantics.
- [x] Tracker history and at least three popular actively maintained OSS projects are cited; consensus is evaluated by the parent rule.
- [x] Only fixtures proven equivalent are migrated; initialization/recovery contracts continue to build from scratch.
- [x] Collected/passed test counts and all pre-existing assertions are preserved or increased.
- [x] Per-test copies cannot share ticket refs, linked-worktree paths, gate snapshots, environment IDs, signing keys, module caches, or mutable config state.
- [x] Durable sentinels fail for stale half-rewritten pointers, bare worktree repair, shared refs, shared identity/signing state, and non-virgin templates.
- [x] A defect-seeded mutation of each newly relied-on isolation fix returns the relevant sentinel to RED.
- [x] Paired before/after setup and module/tier wall-time measurements quantify runner-seconds saved.
- [x] Full affected tiers plus default/integration selectors, lint, typecheck, and workflow guards pass.
- [x] The Gerrit change receives LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and merges before closure.

## Back-out
Revert the Gerrit change to restore per-test from-scratch fixture construction; no product behavior or coverage destination changes.
baseline.summary: Eliminate repeated git-store construction in measured long-pole fixtures
