## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` previously changed up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

The behavioral oracle was authored RED-first. The interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases were held out from the implementer; only the basic dual-read happy path was exposed. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs advances and commits both rotation representations during the compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py`
- `docs/env-vars.md`
- focused unit/integration/CLI tests

Landed as Gerrit 1295 / `e9a25ab84729be0bc9769614f8faa637a1411fac`.

## Why
Tier E is the LAST tier of the bash->Python strangler-fig migration (story adult-oxide-slave, 8784-c2d7-c395-4478). Tiers A-D are DONE/retired; Python is the sole live impl for reads, leaf writes, compute, and the write/sync core. The story's end-state AC is literally "no _engine/*.sh": one implementation + three facades (lib/CLI/MCP), zero standalone shell tests, no embedded heredocs.

Grounding against the live tree (2026-06-12) shows this requires porting ~20 STILL-LIVE bash commands the dispatcher routes to (init, fsck, fsck-recover, transition, reopen, claim, compact, compact-all, scratch, clarity-check, check-ac, quality-check, summary, exists, resolve, format, list-descendants, delete, get-file-impact, get-verify-commands, bridge-status, purge-bridge) -- not just deleting dead wrappers -- plus rewiring the reconciler off the compat shims + engine_env, relocating ticket_txn.py off the bare _engine/event_append.py, deleting the dispatcher + compat shims, and translating all 107 .sh test files to pytest. Tier E has NO kill-switch; rollback is git revert. Clusters:

- E5c: relocate ticket_txn.py; delete the bare _engine/event_append.py.
- E6: rewire remaining compat-shim importers; delete the shims; assert-gone tests.
- E7: delete the dispatcher _engine/rebar + engine_env/PYTHONPATH machinery + engine_dir zipimport
  assertion + jq prereq + flock(1)/mkdir discovery; retire machinery tests in the same commit.
- E8: translate the 107 .sh suites to pytest; delete suite-engine.sh/assert.sh/collector.
- E9: docs (architecture.md offender table -> empty; bash-migration.md §7 DONE) + exhaustive
  live-dogfood validation + soak-evidence comment + close adult-oxide-slave.

## Scope
The whole remaining bash engine, one command/cluster at a time over multiple sessions; each cluster independently green + revertible. NOT in scope: store/locking/event-schema changes (ratified sound); dropping the dual-leg mkdir lock (release-level follow-up, see Tier D note).

## Acceptance Criteria

baseline.description:
# Config-driven status mapping (map-or-drift, round-trip via rebar-status labels)

## Context / Problem

Status mapping is hardcoded: outbound reads built-in `local_to_jira_status` at CREATE/UPDATE; inbound inverts built-in `jira_to_local_status`, preferring a `rebar-status:<local>` label hardcoded to `blocked`/`cancelled`. A project needing a remap/collapse has no echo-safe path. Make it config-driven on the S1 core: **map-or-drift** (never coerce); remap/collapse round-trips via `rebar-status:`.

## Dependency (prerequisite ticket)

On the S1 mapping core **[rebar:bfe7-0900-c3d1-4141]** (merged): `mapping_config` provides `load_mapping_config(root=None)` + `resolve_for_project(config, key, *, builtin) -> MappingLayer` (merges `builtin ← default ← projects.<KEY>`; `.status_map` local→Jira, `SKIP`=drop, ABSENT=drift). `local_to_jira_status` is the `builtin`, so no `[mapping]` ⇒ effective map = today's default.

## Approach — one FORWARD seam; inbound stays reverse-map-free

Only **outbound (forward)** becomes per-project; inbound needs no reverse map/project key (the `rebar-status:` label makes every non-built-in status self-describing).

1. **`config.py` — forward resolution.** Add
   `effective_status_map(project_key, root=None) -> dict[str,str]` = `load_mapping_config(root)` +
   `resolve_for_project(builtin=local_to_jira_status)`. The literal stays the parity-tested
   fallback; `mapping_config` imported LAZILY (config.py stays stdlib-only).

2. **Outbound consumers read the resolved map via the `OutboundMapper` Protocol.**
   `outbound_differ._effective_status_map_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)` resolves the ticket's
   project (`projects_store.resolve_project`) and calls
   `config.effective_status_map(project_key, root=repo_root)` — the `[mapping]` overlay is read
   from the STORE ROOT (not the CWD, mirroring fetcher/preflight), threaded via a new
   `OutboundDiffConfig.repo_root` populated in `run_differs`. The effective `status_map` (optional;
   `None`→built-in) flows into both Protocol methods — `map_local_to_remote` (CREATE) and
   `map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE, via `compute_update_fields`); `_backend.py` + the two wrappers
   gain the param. Shared map-or-drift lives in `outbound_mapper.resolve_outbound_status`, reached
   by the UPDATE mapper (Cloud+DC) and both CREATE builders. `acli.transition_issue` is NOT
   threaded (gets the already-mapped name).

3. **Drift = leave Jira as-is, never a per-mutation failure.** Decided ONLY in the mapper: with
   no entry for a local status it **omits the `status` field** (Jira unchanged) + a drift alert
   (deduped per-status per-process so it doesn't re-flood stderr each pass), replacing today's
   `.get(status,"To Do")` coerce. `preflight_status_mapping` runs AFTER the mapper
   (`reconcile.py:485`): a drift carries no `status`, but a config REMAP emits a config-only Jira
   NAME absent from the BUILT-IN keys∪values it tolerates → spurious warning. Widen it (and the
   fetcher, step 5) to built-in ∪ a **NEW S2** `mapping_config.declared_status_names` (from
   `reconcile.py:485` `repo_root`).

4. **Generalised `rebar-status:` round-trip (built-in-reverse stamp rule).** Outbound
   (`outbound_labels`): `target = forward.get(local)` (GUARDED `.get`, never a subscript). A
   DRIFTED local (no target) → **no label**. Else stamp `rebar-status:<local>` **iff
   `config.jira_to_local_status.get(target) != local`**. On the built-in map this selects
   {blocked, cancelled} (`deleted` is lossy but excluded upstream via `excluded_statuses`) —
   default stamping preserved. Under ANY config remap/collapse, every status whose Jira target
   isn't the built-in canonical name for `<local>` is labelled → inbound recovers it. Inbound:
   parse the `rebar-status:<local>` suffix, validating `<local>` against a vocabulary DERIVED from
   `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` values ∪ `deleted` (cannot drift from a parallel literal) via one shared
   helper; the plain `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS.get()` fallback stays correct since every non-built-in
   status is labelled. (Malformed `[mapping]` fails closed via S1's `MappingConfigError`.)

5. **Fetcher known-set widened.** `fetcher._known_jira_statuses` today reads only built-in
   `jira_to_local_status` keys → a config-only status trips a spurious "no reconciler mapping"
   warning. Widen to built-in ∪ `mapping_config.declared_status_names` (from `repo_root`).

## Scope (files)

- `config.py` — `effective_status_map` (forward, lazy `mapping_config`).
- `outbound_differ.py` — `_effective_status_map_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)`; `OutboundDiffConfig.repo_root`; thread `status_map` into CREATE/UPDATE + label diff.
- `run_differs.py` — populate `OutboundDiffConfig.repo_root` from the pass `repo_root`.- `outbound_field_diff.py` — `compute_update_fields` forwards `status_map`.
- `_backend.py` — `OutboundMapper` Protocol: OPTIONAL `status_map` (default None) on both map methods.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — wrappers forward `status_map`; DC `_map_local_to_dc_fields` uses it (DC CREATE) w/ drift-omit.
- `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py` — shared `resolve_outbound_status` (map-or-drift, deduped alert); `map_fields_to_remote` (UPDATE).
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — `_map_local_to_jira_fields` (Cloud CREATE), drift-omit.
- `outbound_labels.py` — built-in-reverse stamp rule keyed on `config.jira_to_local_status` (guarded).
- `inbound_fields.py` — generalised `rebar-status:<local>` recovery via a DERIVED vocab (shared helper).
- `inbound_translate.py` / `apply_inbound_events.py` / `inbound_differ.py` — shared helper (retire `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL`); `_LOCAL_STATUS_VALUES` re-uses the derived vocab.
- `applier.py` — re-export shared helper in `__all__`.
- `mapping_config.py` — **add NEW** `declared_status_names(config)`: every Jira status NAME declared across config (`status_map` values ∪ `statuses`).
- `fetcher.py` — widen `_known_jira_statuses` to built-in ∪ config-declared names.
- `reconcile_helpers.py` — widen `preflight_status_mapping` set (optional `repo_root`).
- `reconcile.py` — thread `repo_root` into the `preflight_status_mapping` call.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` (new).

## Testing

Tier **in-process unit** — pure over the resolved map; tests hit REAL entry points; alerts are non-fatal stderr via `capsys`.


## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Effective forward map = `local_to_jira_status` ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>` via S1
  `resolve_for_project`; a non-default overlay changes the outbound target through the real mapper
  — `test_status_config_effect`.
- [x] An unmapped status **drifts**: the mutation omits `status` (Jira unchanged) + a non-fatal
  warning, never skipped nor a failure — `test_unmapped_status_drifts`; the drift alert is deduped
  per-status per-process — `test_drift_warning_deduped_within_pass`.
- [x] A config remap AND a collapsed pair (OTHER than blocked/cancelled) round-trip losslessly via
  `rebar-status:<local>` labels, recovered inbound without a reverse map —
  `test_status_remap_roundtrip`/`test_status_collapse_roundtrip`.
- [x] The `outbound_differ` seam resolves the per-project map and reads `[mapping]` from the
  `repo_root`, not the CWD — `test_effective_status_map_for_resolves_project`,
  `test_effective_status_map_for_honors_repo_root`.
- [x] A config-only/remapped Jira status is tolerated by BOTH the fetcher known-set AND the
  post-mapper `preflight_status_mapping` — `test_fetcher_known_includes_config`,
  `test_preflight_tolerates_config_remap`.
- [x] The duplicated `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` literal is retired for a shared helper
  (re-exported in `applier.__all__`) whose recovery vocab is DERIVED (not a divergent literal),
  covering every local status the stamp rule can emit — `test_status_label_helper_single_source`,
  `test_recovery_vocab_covers_every_local_status`.
- [x] `value_maps`↔`config` parity tests in `state/test_config.py` stay green.
baseline.summary: Config-driven status mapping (map-or-drift, collapse round-trip via rebar-status labels)

## Problem

A provider 400 meaning "your input is too big" surfaces to the caller as `LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed` — provider-outage semantics for a deterministic, caller-fixable input problem. The caller cannot tell "retry later, the provider is down" from "shrink your input, this will never succeed".

Observed (scripted `ModelHTTPError`, offline):

```
ModelHTTPError(400, "prompt is too long: 206826 tokens > 200000 maximum")
  -> LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed
```

## Why this is a defect, not a design gap

rebar **already computes the correct classification**. `run_failure.py:152` holds `CHANGE_INPUT` with `retryable=False` at the moment it wraps the error — and then wraps it in a type whose name and message assert the opposite. Only the *type* is wrong; no new measurement, estimator, calibration, or classification work is required.

Confirmed adjacent behaviour, so the blast radius is understood: there is **no** transport retry (400 is absent from `_RETRY_STATUSES`) and **no** fallback (`CHANGE_INPUT` is excluded), so nothing today depends on this presenting as an outage. But plan-review's size ladder burns a full failed round-trip per rung against an error it cannot recognise as terminal-for-this-input.

## Scope — deliberately narrow

This is a **type/message correction at an existing classification site**, not a new guard.

Explicitly OUT of scope: any pre-flight measurement of the outgoing request. That is the shared-seam design change tracked by `undamaged-adolescent-sable` (`f79d-e364-5fdb-417d`), which needs a token estimator and a calibration decision this ticket does not touch. This fix acts only AFTER the provider has answered, so it is a **complement, not a substitute** — it cannot satisfy that ticket's "before the provider call" requirement and does not claim to.

Also out of scope: widening which HTTP statuses are classified `CHANGE_INPUT`. Use the classification already computed at the wrap site; do not add new ones.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A provider 400 already classified `CHANGE_INPUT` at the wrap site raises an error whose
      type and message identify it as a caller-fixable input problem, not a provider outage —
      verified by a test scripting such an error offline and asserting on the raised type
- [x] The raised type remains a subclass of `LLMError`, so the 13 existing broad handlers keep
      catching it — verified by a test asserting the subclass relationship
- [x] A genuine provider outage (a 5xx, or a transport failure) still raises
      `LLMUnavailableError` — verified by a test, so the change discriminates rather than
      relabelling everything
- [x] No change to `_RETRY_STATUSES` or to fallback eligibility — verified by a test pinning
      that a `CHANGE_INPUT` 400 is still neither retried nor failed over
baseline.summary: A CHANGE_INPUT 400 is raised as LLMUnavailableError, so a caller-fixable input problem reads as a provider outage

## Target
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — **799 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (1 lines of headroom).

One line of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.

- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.

- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

# Rotate the compromised GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN — BLOCKED on deploying the 66af fix to prod first

## Why this exists
66af (Gerrit 1384, MERGED) fixes the review-bot logging the webhook token in plaintext. Its AC5 mandates the already-leaked token be rotated AND that the rotation be "TRACKED SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY". This ticket is that record.

## Decisive finding (do NOT rotate before deploying)
The 66af code is merged to main but NOT deployed to the prod box (i-00880b2c7f13527c5). Verified inside the running container `compose-review-bot-1` (image built 2026-08-04T11:07Z, BEFORE 1384 merged ~12:47):
  - review_bot/config.py: TokenRedactingFilter  -> 0 (absent)
  - review_bot/app.py:    X-Rebar-Token          -> 0 (absent)
  - review_bot/app.py:243  token = request.query_params.get("token", "")  <-- still URL-sourced
So the bot still takes the token from `?token=` and uvicorn access-logs it in clear text. Rotating now would re-leak the NEW token the moment Gerrit's webhook/`/rerun` next calls it — exactly the runbook's forbidden precondition ("the code fix must land BEFORE rotation").

## Also: the token is a SHARED secret (ADR-0014)
`/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` is simultaneously (a) the bot's Gerrit HTTP basic-auth password (outbound REST/voting), (b) the inbound webhook `?token=`/`X-Rebar-Token` secret, and (c) the container `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` env. A bare `aws ssm put-parameter` DESYNCS these and breaks the LLM-Review gate. The canonical atomic tool is `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (gerrit set-account new password + SSM overwrite + re-render/push webhooks.config to refs/meta/config).

## Correct sequence (coordinated deploy-then-rotate; brief review-bot bounce)
1. Deploy current origin/main (with 66af) to the box: rebuild the `compose-review-bot` image
   from current main + `docker compose up -d` recreate; re-render webhooks.config to the
   X-Rebar-Token HEADER form via the updated service-user.sh. This removes the leaky URL path.
2. Rotate: run `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` -> new 256-bit token set as the bot's Gerrit HTTP
   password, overwritten into SSM, and substituted into webhooks.config (pushed to
   refs/meta/config).
3. Restart the review-bot container so it loads the new GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN (fetch-secrets.sh ->
   .env -> compose up -d).
4. Verify end-to-end: inbound webhook triggers a review (or `/rerun`), AND an outbound
   LLM-Review vote succeeds (outbound basic-auth works). Update any operator-local git
   credential caches to the new token.
5. Prefer a quiet window AFTER in-flight changes 1376 (9305) and 1386 (1dbe) have landed — both
   depend on the LLM-Review bot and would be disrupted by the bounce.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [operator-attested] 66af code deployed to the prod box; running container confirmed to source the token from
      the X-Rebar-Token header and to carry TokenRedactingFilter (no `?token=` URL read).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Token rotated via service-user.sh: new value is the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, in SSM,
      and in the pushed webhooks.config; old (compromised) value no longer accepted.
- [ ] [operator-attested] review-bot restarted and verified: an inbound webhook/`/rerun` triggers a review AND an
      outbound LLM-Review vote lands with the new credential.
- [x] [operator-attested] Rotation recorded as DONE here (not assumed), and 66af AC5 checked off / closed.

## Security note
Until step 2 completes, the previously-logged token remains COMPROMISED and valid. Treat as an open credential exposure.
baseline.summary: Rotate compromised GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN (deploy 66af first)

baseline.description:
## Summary
When a synced local ticket is archived or moved to status `deleted`, its bound Jira issue is left live (e.g. "To Do") indefinitely. The reconciler's outbound diff never sees these tickets, so no transition/close/unbind is ever emitted. Proven on REB-464/456/465/466/457 (bound to locally archived/deleted test tickets), all still "To Do" in Jira.

## Root Cause (two filter layers, an unintended gap)
- Layer 1 (archived): the reconciler builds its local snapshot via `rebar list --full` (`reconcile.py:455`) with no `--include-archived`; `reducer/_api.py:234` drops `archived=True`. Archived tickets never enter the diff.
- Layer 2 (deleted): deleted-status tickets survive the snapshot but are skipped in the differ loop (`outbound_differ.py:537-540`, `excluded_statuses={archived,deleted}`).
- Smoking gun: `outbound_fields.py:94` maps `"deleted" -> "Done"` (propagation is INTENDED) but the `:539` skip fires before that mapping runs (`:636`) — intended behaviour rendered dead code. `OutboundMutation` declares a `"delete"` action (`outbound_differ.py:245`) but nothing ever constructs one. Not a deliberate "never mutate Jira" policy: `closed -> Done` propagates normally.
- Runtime proof: `rebar list --full` returns 0 for the archived id vs 1 with `--include-archived`; a `reconcile --mode dry-run` (249 mutations over 606 issues) plans nothing for any of these keys.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Sync a local ticket to Jira (binding confirmed).
2. Archive it, or transition it to `deleted` locally.
3. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run`.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: local archival/deletion of a bound ticket drives its Jira issue to a terminal status (Done) and/or retires the binding, within one pass.
- Actual: no mutation is planned; the Jira issue is stranded live forever.

## Proposed design (perf-safe, binding-driven)
Drive terminal-transition detection from the BINDING STORE, not a full archived-ticket scan, so cost scales with the number of *synced* tickets (~606), never with the total number of archived tickets:
- Each pass compute `missing = bindings.keys() - active_snapshot_ids` (synced tickets that fell out of the active view = just archived/deleted). Cheap set-diff over ~606 bindings.
- For only those ids, do a targeted state read and emit the already-wired terminal transition (`deleted`/`archived -> Done`) via `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` + `_diff_fields`.
- Idempotency: once Jira == Done the field-diff is empty (near-zero steady-state cost); optionally retire the binding after the terminal transition so it leaves the working set. Per-pass cost = O(newly-archived-since-last-pass), shrinking to zero — never O(all-archived). Do NOT switch the full snapshot to `--include-archived`.
- Unifies with the class-C binding GC (same binding-store iteration).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A locally archived or deleted ticket bound to a Jira issue drives that issue to a terminal Jira status (Done), or unbinds it, within one reconcile pass.
- [ ] Detection is bounded by #bindings / #newly-archived, not total archived-ticket count (no full `--include-archived` snapshot per pass); documented with a perf note/test.
- [ ] The dead `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS["deleted"]="Done"` mapping becomes reachable (or is replaced by an explicit terminal-transition path).
- [ ] A test binds a ticket, archives/deletes it locally, runs a pass, and asserts the Jira issue transitions to Done (RED before fix).
- [ ] The concrete drift (REB-464/456/465/466/457) reconciles after the fix.

## Notes
Discovered comparing Jira REB vs the local store. All current instances are "delete me" test tickets, but the mechanism affects any real archived (or closed-then-archived) ticket. `bridge_fsck` does not detect this (see the class-D ticket). Files: `outbound_differ.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `reconcile.py`, `reducer/_api.py`.

## Guardrails (must-preserve — prior-art + archaeology; folds in the corrected plan)
Approved policy: local archive/delete drives the Jira issue to a terminal status (Done). But:
- [ ] Drive the terminal transition from the per-binding BASELINE + binding-store walk, NOT from snapshot membership; act only on a CONFIRMED terminal/404 (grace-counted), never on snapshot-absence (L13/L16/L17).
- [ ] Close the bidir loop: add `archived` to the reverse status map AND the single-pass bidir suppression, so inbound reading Jira `Done` does not flip local `archived -> closed` (L21/L3; `inbound_translate.py:121`). Today `archived` maps nowhere on the reverse path.
- [ ] Gate the whole class behind the circuit breaker (refuse a pass that would terminal-transition/retire > N% of bindings) [prior art: Argo `allowEmpty`].
- [ ] Preserve `note_absent` grace + reversible retirement (L14/L15); a local-archive retirement must not corrupt the `absent_404_count` machinery.
- [ ] Unify with class C (13eb): one binding-store loop heals terminal transitions and GCs dead bindings.
- [ ] Parity is proven by the CONVERGENCE property (re-reconcile after the heal yields zero actions), not by an enumerated case.

## Implementation contract (foundation-first — read before coding)
DEPENDS ON amiss-bun-wince (baf7): do NOT hand-roll a detection path. This bug is the `TERMINAL_TRANSITION` Decision cell of `classify()` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/classify.py) plus its apply handler.
1. Detection: the level-triggered binding-store walk (all_bindings()) classifies each bound pair; a pair whose LOCAL ticket is archived or status=deleted while ObservedJira=PRESENT with Jira status != Done yields `TERMINAL_TRANSITION`. Read the local ticket's true state with a targeted read (`rebar show`-equivalent library call), NOT by adding --include-archived to the snapshot (see the perf note: 120 archived tickets exist, only 6 are bound).
2. Apply: emit the already-mapped transition via `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` ("deleted"->"Done"; add "archived"->"Done") through the existing outbound mutation dispatch (typed_dispatch/apply_outbound) — construct a normal status-transition mutation; do NOT invent a new mutation type.
3. ADR 0029 #2 is a HARD PREREQUISITE in this ticket: add `archived` to the reverse status map (inbound_translate.py `_status_maps` region) so inbound Jira `Done` on a locally-archived ticket KEEPS local archived (never flips it to closed), and add the archived case to the L3 single-pass suppression map (inbound_differ.py). RED test first: archive locally -> 1 pass -> Jira Done -> next inbound pass -> local STILL archived; assert stability over 3 simulated passes.
4. Circuit breaker: TERMINAL_TRANSITION is an acting kind — it is automatically counted by check_blast_radius (foundation); no extra work beyond NOT bypassing the apply-path breaker.
5. Live acceptance cells: REB-464/456/465/466/457 (verified still 'To Do' on 2026-07-03) transition to Done; census on the following pass shows 0 acting for this class.
Files: classify.py (cell), outbound_fields.py (status map + reachability of the dead deleted->Done mapping), inbound_translate.py + inbound_differ.py (reverse map + L3), apply_outbound.py/typed_dispatch.py (handler), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ + diffing/.
baseline.summary: Reconciler never propagates local archive/delete to the bound Jira issue (stranded live issues)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A top-level command cannot truthfully declare one required package extra. Optionality varies by nested mode, workflow contents, analyzer, renderer, or selected provider. Enforcing extras during route discovery would hide stable verbs and break lean diagnostic paths; converting every missing dependency to an error would regress intentional unavailable, abstain, and fallback behavior.

## Approach
Create a stdlib-only semantic capability registry independent of the command registry. Each immutable record names a semantic key, packaging extra, and missing posture. The initial complete runtime census is:

- `agent_runtime → agents/error`, `audit_ui → ui/error`, `bedrock_provider → bedrock/error`, `jira_datacenter → jira-datacenter/error`, and `s3_remote → s3/error`;
- `metrics_lizard → metrics/unavailable` and `pricing → pricing/unavailable`;
- `grounding_structural → grounding/abstain` and `grounding_t2 → grounding-t2/abstain`;
- `cloud_adf → adf/fallback`, `datacenter_wiki → wiki/fallback`, and `trace_export → tracing/fallback`;
- separate-entrypoint `mcp_server → mcp/error` and `review_bot → reviewbot/error`, reusable without adding CLI verbs.

`dev` is packaging/development metadata and is not a runtime capability. Validate that every capability references a declared packaging extra, every route's possible capability name exists, and no probe imports the optional package.

Expose a narrow shared error helper for `error` capabilities. Invoke it only after existing handlers/factories parse the selected mode/backend: `audit show` before `audit serve`; status/check/dry-run paths before live agent work; provider selection before Bedrock/Jira DC/S3 client construction. For `unavailable`, `abstain`, and `fallback`, domain components retain control of result payloads and logging; they may consult registry metadata/install hints but the registry never manufactures their domain result.

## Compatibility and Rollback
Preserve existing exact install guidance, exit/error types, and degraded output shapes. Stable verbs and top-level help never depend on installed extras. Existing `_optional.require_extra` and `guard_import` remain compatibility surfaces during expansion and delegate to the new semantic seam where applicable. Rollback restores those direct calls; no persisted data changes.

## Testing
Use unit tests for capability validation and shared error text. Use clean no-extras subprocess/production-path tests for each posture and contrast mode: lean `audit show` versus selected `audit serve`; review/workflow diagnostics versus live agent construction; unselected versus selected Bedrock/Jira DC/S3; metrics/pricing unavailable; grounding abstain; ADF/wiki/tracing fallback. Block heavy modules in `sys.modules` and import hooks during registry/help construction. Separate `rebar-mcp` and review-bot entrypoint smoke tests assert their packaging capabilities without adding CLI routes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every initial semantic capability above validates against one declared packaging extra and one typed missing posture without importing its probe module.
- [x] Stable commands and top-level help remain present in a no-extras wheel; only the selected capability boundary emits an actionable error for `error` postures.
- [x] Lean diagnostic/read/dry-run modes execute without requiring sibling live capabilities, including `audit show` and non-agent review/workflow paths.
- [x] Metrics/pricing unavailable, grounding abstain, ADF/wiki/tracing fallback, and selected provider errors retain their existing domain output, exception, stream, and exit contracts.
- [x] `rebar-mcp` and review-bot remain separate entry points and can consume capability metadata without appearing in the top-level route registry.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The bridge has nowhere to record which tracker projects a store syncs, nor which repos each project's tickets belong to. Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` needs that mapping to be a property of the **store** rather than of any one repo, because `.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json` is shared by every repo using the store: if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would see the other's projects as vanished from the remote and diff them as deletions.

## Approach

Add `.bridge_state/projects.json` beside the committed bridge state already there (`bindings.json`, `get_rotation.json`, `prev_snapshot.json` — all present on the `tickets` branch), owned by a new `projects_store.py` module rather than by extending `binding_store.py`. The two records have very different write cadences, and keeping them separate means an operator editing the mapping never rewrites the large bindings record.

Record shape:

```json
{"version": 1, "legacy_default": "REB", "projects": {"REB": {"repos": ["rebar"]}}}
```

The `projects` key set **is** the store's sync list, so there is no second list to keep in agreement. `legacy_default` is the project that tickets predating this epic resolve to.

This choice sits well with ADR 0060 ("Keep bridge state committed, but make its formats cheap"): that ADR's constraint is per-pass churn on the tickets branch — it measured 12.79 KB per changed `bindings.json` version and ~4.5 MB/day for `prev_snapshot.json`. The mapping changes only on an operator edit, so it adds no per-pass growth at all.

Surface it as `bridge projects` under the verb group established by story `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a` (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py`), with the library and MCP parity epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3` requires of every bridge verb. The bridge library surface is `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py` (`bridge_fsck` at `:75`). The MCP layer is split by mutation, not by feature: `register_read_tools` (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:36`) hosts tools annotated `_ANN["READ_ONLY"]` — where the existing `bridge_fsck` tool lives at `:259` — while `register_write_tools` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:33`) hosts mutating tools, and `mcp_server.py:663` registers both. The `projects` verbs therefore split across both modules: `list` is a read tool, `set` and `remove` are write tools. Sub-verbs: `list`, `set <KEY> --repos a,b`, `remove <KEY>`. `set` on a key that is already present **replaces** that key's repos list rather than merging into it, so the command is idempotent and a repo is removed by re-issuing `set` without it.

The bridge group's help is a **pinned byte-exact contract**, not generated text: the group listing lives in `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` (which today names only `preview` and `sync` at lines 5-7) and is served verbatim by `_help.subcommand_help` (`src/rebar/_cli/_help.py:52`), while the parser hardcodes the verb set a second time as `metavar="{preview,sync}"` (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:52-53`). Adding a verb therefore means editing three places, not one; omitting either of the two help sites ships a group whose own help does not mention the command it just gained.

The module exposes two functions so that I/O and rule are separable: `load_mapping(repo_root)` reads and validates the record, and `resolve_project(ticket, mapping) -> str | None` is a pure function over an already-loaded mapping, which keeps the tri-state rule unit-testable without a store on disk.

**Read behaviour when the record is missing or bad** follows the precedent `compat.py` already sets for `.store-compat.json` (`docs/migrations.md:155-165`): an **absent** record is legal and reads as an empty mapping with a `legacy_default` of `None`, while a **malformed** one raises rather than being silently treated as absent — a corrupt record must never degrade into a permissive default. Absent is legal because the record is seeded by an ensure unit that runs at init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot; until it does, every ticket resolves to `None` and nothing syncs, which is the fail-safe direction — the bridge writes nothing rather than writing somewhere wrong.

`resolve_project` implements the tri-state rule so the inbound and outbound stories consume one implementation instead of each re-deriving it. The states map to concrete return values:

| ticket `bridge_project` | returns | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| key absent from state | the mapping's `legacy_default` (a `str`) | legacy ticket, predates this epic |
| `""` (explicit empty) | `None` | deliberately not synced |
| `"REB"` | `"REB"` | sync into that project |

`None` is the not-synced sentinel, so every consumer branches on a single defined value: callers treat `None` as "emit no mutation for this ticket" and any non-`None` result as a project key safe to target. A `legacy_default` that is itself empty — a store whose backend had no configured project — also yields `None`, so an unconfigured store degrades to "nothing syncs" rather than to a malformed query.

`--repos` is **required** on `set`; omitting the flag is an argument error and exits non-zero. `--repos ""` is the explicit way to store an empty list, which keeps "no default repo" a deliberate statement rather than an accident of a forgotten flag.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` — the subcommand, and the hardcoded `metavar` verb set at `:52-53`
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` — the pinned byte-exact group help listing
- `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — the `list` read tool
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — the `set` and `remove` write tools
- tests under `tests/`

This story owns the mapping module; the parent epic's file impact is updated to name `projects_store.py` rather than `binding_store.py`, so parent and child agree that the mapping does not extend the bindings record.

`_mcp_writes.py` is the one file this story shares with its sibling that adds the ticket create arguments. The overlap is forced by the codebase's own read/write registrar split rather than chosen, and it is safe because that sibling `depends_on` this story: the two are strictly ordered and can never be edited concurrently. Introducing a third MCP module purely to avoid the shared file would break the established registrar convention for no benefit.

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's CLI row — a real CLI subprocess with a persisted-state assertion — because the mechanism spans argument parsing, the on-disk JSON record, and exit codes; an in-process unit test would not cross the parsing or exit-code components.

- Happy path: `bridge projects set REB --repos rebar` in a fresh store, then `bridge projects list`
  returns the entry and `.bridge_state/projects.json` on disk contains it.
- Cross-surface contract test: an entry written through the library surface is read back byte-equal
  through the CLI and through MCP — proving one record, not three parallel stores.
- Failure path: `bridge projects remove NOPE` on a store without that key exits non-zero, names the
  key, and leaves the record byte-unchanged.
- Edge: `set REB --repos` with an empty list is accepted and stores `[]` — a project with no default
  repo is legal, not an error.
- Replace-not-merge: `set REB --repos a,b` followed by `set REB --repos a` stores exactly `["a"]`,
  proving the second call replaced rather than merged.
- Pinned help: `rebar bridge` with no verb, and `rebar help bridge`, both render text naming
  `projects`, and the argparse `metavar` matches the pinned listing — asserted against the file so a
  future verb cannot drift the two apart silently.
- Collateral invariant: after any mapping write, `bindings.json` and `prev_snapshot.json` hash
  identically to before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects set|list|remove` exist under the bridge verb group and operate on
      `.bridge_state/projects.json`; checked by a CLI subprocess test asserting the on-disk record
      after each verb.
- [ ] The library and MCP surfaces read and write the same record as the CLI; checked by a test that
      writes through one surface and reads the identical entry through the other two.
- [ ] `resolve_project` returns the `legacy_default` string for an absent field, `None` for an
      explicit empty value, and the key itself for a set value, and returns `None` when the
      `legacy_default` is itself empty; checked by a parameterized unit test asserting the exact
      return value for all four cases.
- [ ] `set` without `--repos` is an argument error exiting non-zero, while `--repos ""` stores `[]`;
      checked by a paired CLI subprocess test.
- [ ] An absent record reads as an empty mapping with a `None` legacy default while a malformed one
      raises; checked by a paired test over a store with no record and one with truncated JSON.
- [ ] `list` is registered as a read tool and `set`/`remove` as write tools; checked by asserting
      `list` carries the READ_ONLY annotation and that `set`/`remove` are registered by
      `register_write_tools`.
- [ ] A mapping write leaves `bindings.json` and `prev_snapshot.json` byte-identical; checked by
      hashing both before and after in the CLI test.
- [ ] `remove` of an unknown key exits non-zero and mutates nothing; checked in the same test.
- [ ] `set` on an already-present key replaces its repos list rather than merging; checked by
      asserting the stored list equals exactly the second call's argument.
- [ ] The pinned group help in `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` and the parser `metavar` both name
      `projects`; checked by a test asserting the rendered `rebar bridge` help contains the verb and
      that the pinned file and the `metavar` verb set agree.
baseline.summary: bridge projects: store-level project-to-repos mapping and its CLI, library and MCP surface

baseline.description:
## Summary

The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow fails in production on a recurring basis — **22 failed runs between 2026-07-23T20:29Z and 2026-07-30T22:14Z** — and **7 of those failures landed AFTER the most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix**, including two in the very `refs/reconciler/lock` subsystem that fix repaired.

Individual failures are self-healing (a later scheduled run succeeds), which is why they have never been ticketed: the heartbeat canary only files a ticket when staleness exceeds its 2h threshold (it did so once, `4b5c`). The remaining failures are invisible.

## Timing investigation vs commit history

**Most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix:** `7c763f1a7` — *"a4b2: prune an orphaned local pass-lock ref"*, authored 2026-07-27 23:20:41 -0700 = **2026-07-28T06:20:41Z**. Ticket `a4b2` (*Stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently*) is a **bug** and its fix is specifically about the pass-lock ref lifecycle.

Every later commit touching `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` is J-series Jira Data Center *story* work (`62d9`, `0a94`, `aac8`, `9fd4`), not a bug fix. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge*.yml` has no commit since `5623a2496` (`0e15`, 2026-07-19); `src/rebar/_store/push.py` / `sync.py` have none since `27e1165cd` (2026-07-17).

**Failures after that fix (7):**

| When (UTC) | Run | Failing step |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-29T15:27:11Z | 30465914822 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T00:45:55Z | 30503669644 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T03:06:34Z | 30510284129 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T05:02:44Z | 30515516036 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T19:46:26Z | 30576272914 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T20:29:25Z | 30579382013 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T22:03:07Z | 30585738860 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |

**Rate before vs after the fix** (same workflow, contiguous windows):

```
PRE-FIX  2026-07-23T20:29 -> 2026-07-28T06:20 : 955 runs, 815 success,  15 failure, 124 cancelled  (1.57% fail)
POST-FIX 2026-07-28T06:20 -> 2026-07-30T22:14 : 549 runs, 460 success,   7 failure,  81 cancelled  (1.28% fail)
```

The failure rate is essentially unchanged, and the lock/lease failure mode recurs after a lock-specific fix. `a4b2` addressed a *local* stranded ref wedging local passes; it did not address CI-side lease loss under contention. **This bug is therefore NOT a regression of `a4b2` and not a claim that `a4b2` is wrong — it is the residual, separate problem `a4b2` did not cover.**

## Three distinct failure modes observed post-fix

**(1) Pass-lock lease lost mid-pass** — 2 runs (30576272914, 30579382013):

```
ref-lock renew: refs/reconciler/lock CAS rejected — lease lost/stolen
  (held 52b2181c53bacdfc7c6d4623afbd5d5ec6f6b0ff)
ERROR: reconcile heartbeat lost the lease (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting pass
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: pass lock lease lost mid-pass (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting
```

Aborting on lease loss is correct-by-design (`2711`: "heartbeat loses lease mid-pass -> pass aborts, no double-run"), but the abort surfaces as a hard workflow failure (exit 1) rather than a benign skip.

**(2) Push to `origin/tickets` rejected after 5 retries** — 4 runs:

```
Push rejected (attempt 4):
 ! [rejected]            HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have
Push failed after 5 retries. Last stderr: ...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Concurrent writers keep advancing `origin/tickets` faster than the retry budget.

**(3) Unhandled `HTTP Error 404` from the reconcile pass** — 1 run (30465914822, 2026-07-29T15:34:55Z):

```
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
```

Preceded in the same run by repeated (non-fatal) warnings:

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records: _apply_inbound_update: rebar.link failed for
  761e-5af2-ed57-408a -> 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 (blocks): RebarError('rebar link failed (exit 1):
  Error: ERROR: redundant link — ... are in a direct parent-child relationship')
```

A bare 404 escaping as an unhandled exception is the least explained of the three and may be a genuine gap rather than contention.

## Adjacent signal: cancellation volume

124 pre-fix + 81 post-fix runs were **cancelled** (~15% of all runs), consistent with heavy schedule/dispatch overlap. High overlap is the plausible common driver behind both mode (1) and mode (2), so it is included here as evidence rather than as a separate ticket.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** contention between overlapping reconciler runs is absorbed
  (backoff, longer retry budget, or a clean no-op exit), so a run that loses a
  race does not turn the workflow red; genuinely unhandled errors (mode 3) fail
  loudly and distinguishably.
- **Actual:** ~1.3% of runs fail, in three different ways that are
  indistinguishable at the workflow level, none individually tracked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the three modes is classified as either *benign contention*
      (should exit non-red / be absorbed) or *a real fault* (should stay red),
      with the decision recorded.
- [ ] Mode (1): losing the pass lock to a legitimate concurrent holder no longer
      produces a red run; a genuine lock fault still does.
- [ ] Mode (2): the `origin/tickets` push either succeeds under normal
      contention (adequate retry/backoff, or fetch-rebase-retry) or exits
      non-red when it has provably lost a benign race.
- [ ] Mode (3): the `HTTP Error 404` path is root-caused and either handled with
      a specific error or reported with enough context to identify the
      failing request.
- [x] Post-fix verification. The `>= 500 runs` population gate originally written
      here is **WAIVED by operator decision (2026-07-31)**: at ~215 Reconcile Bridge
      runs/day it is wall-clock-bound at ~2.3 days, and it adds no evidence about the
      MECHANISM beyond what the oracles already prove. Replaced by, and satisfied by:
      (a) each fixed mode proven RED-first against an oracle held out from the
          implementing agent, then mutation-checked by re-seeding the exact defect —
          mode 1 returns `assert 1 == 75`, mode 3's create/delete 404 escapes again;
      (b) the post-fix sample that actually exists at close, recorded plainly:
          **7 Reconcile Bridge runs** since the fix landed (6 success, 1 cancelled,
          0 failures). Seven runs is a small sample and is explicitly NOT claimed as
          proof the failure has stopped — it is on the record so the number is stated
          rather than implied. Sustained-absence evidence, if wanted, needs the
          wall-clock this waiver declines to spend.
- [ ] Cancellation rate is either explained as expected or reduced.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (pass lock / reconcile_once error
      handling).

## Investigation provenance

Found during a cross-source audit of AWS, Gerrit and GitHub Actions logs for errors not tracked as bugs (2026-07-30). Run inventory: 2,598 Actions runs over 2026-07-23 → 2026-07-30 pulled via the Actions API; failure classification from per-job step conclusions and job logs.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge fails ~1.3% of runs in three modes (lock-lease loss, tickets push rejected, unhandled 404) — 7 recurrences after the a4b2 pass-lock fix

## Why

The concurrency contract promises compaction is recoverable if the process dies after the snapshot is written and partway through source retirement. Existing tests only monkeypatch Python exceptions (which still run `except`/cleanup code) or construct orphan states by hand — none kill an actual compactor process. `SIGKILL` runs none of the rollback, lock-release, cache-cleanup, or git-staging code, so the real process-death durability contract (including lock reclamation and a dirty tracker worktree left between snapshot write and commit) is unproven.

## What

- Add a deterministic subprocess test that kills a real `rebar compact` process
  mid-retirement and verifies recovery from a fresh CLI process.
- Use a test-only failpoint / filesystem barrier to pause after the first source
  rename, rather than a timing-based race window.

## Scope

- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` (new process-death test)
- Possibly a small test-only failpoint hook in `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`
  (guarded so it is inert in production).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test seeds foldable events, launches `rebar compact` in a subprocess, pauses after
      the first source rename via a barrier, and `SIGKILL`s it.
- [ ] From a fresh CLI process: the write lock is recoverable, the ticket reads at its
      exact pre-crash semantic state, no source UUID is lost, `fsck` returns the
      documented clean/repairable result, and re-running compaction is idempotent or
      performs the documented repair (after which `fsck` is clean).
- [ ] The test is deterministic (no reliance on a narrow timing window).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Add real compactor process-death (SIGKILL) recovery test

## Why

The author-facing guides are the ONLY place the SC/AC split was ever described as a real
distinction — `rebar explain plan` currently tells container authors they need
`## Success Criteria` on top of the universal `## Acceptance Criteria` floor. That prose is the
source of the divergence this epic removes; leaving it in place after the gates change would
instruct authors to write a heading nothing reads.

## What

Rewrite the author guide and user docs for the collapsed vocabulary, including the leaf/container
section rule that motivated the split.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:58,76` — the leaf-vs-container section rule
  ("Container ... needs `## Success Criteria`" and "Containers additionally: `## Success
  Criteria` + the child decomposition"). Both must be restated so containers are described by
  what actually differs: they still need `## Acceptance Criteria`, plus a child decomposition
  that COVERS it (G3), and they defer testing to children.
- `docs/user-guide.md:219,230`
- `docs/llm-framework.md:407`

## Approach

Rewrite rather than substitute. A literal rename of line 58 would read "Container needs
`## Acceptance Criteria`", which is true of every ticket and so says nothing — the container
guidance has to be re-expressed as the decomposition/coverage requirement. This is the one place
in the epic where the edit is editorial rather than mechanical.

Note the guide is packaged and surfaced by `rebar explain plan`, so it is a shipped artifact,
not just documentation.

## Testing

- `rebar explain plan` renders the updated guide with no SC vocabulary.
- `pytest tests -k "guide or explain"` green.
- Manual read-through that the container guidance still tells an author what containers need
  DIFFERENTLY from leaves (coverage + decomposition), i.e. the section did not become vacuous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/_guides/ docs/user-guide.md docs/llm-framework.md` returns no matches.
- [ ] `rebar explain plan` exits 0 and its output contains no SC vocabulary.
- [ ] The guide's leaf-vs-container section still states a container-specific requirement
      (child decomposition covering the parent's acceptance criteria, testing deferred to
      children) rather than collapsing to "containers need Acceptance Criteria".
- [ ] `make lint` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Rewrite author guide and user docs for the collapsed criteria vocabulary

## Context
The architecture is well documented and selected seams have strong bespoke AST negative controls, but there is no repository-wide dependency contract for stable package layers. This leaves new cross-layer imports and cycles outside the specifically protected seams detectable only by review.

## Plan
- Derive a deliberately small layer model from docs/architecture.md and current package ownership.
- Encode allowed dependency directions with an import-graph or contract checker.
- Add known-positive and known-negative fixtures so the checker cannot pass vacuously.
- Gate only stable boundaries; retain specialized Jira-family and optionality checks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Stable package layers and permitted dependency directions are documented with rationale.
- [ ] A deterministic repository check rejects a synthetic forbidden edge and accepts a permitted edge.
- [ ] The check covers production imports without treating facade or documented lazy-import seams as accidental cycles.
- [ ] CI runs the contract check and reports actionable offending edges.
- [ ] Existing specialized boundary checks remain green and non-duplicative.
baseline.summary: Define repository-wide package dependency contracts for stable rebar layers

baseline.description:
## Summary

The in-process library read path (`rebar._reads`) has **no initialization guard**, so every read against a repo whose tracker directory does not exist returns an EMPTY result with no error. The CLI read path guards this exact condition (`_engine_support/reads_cli.py:340-342` -> "ticket system not initialized", exit 1), and the library WRITE path guards it too (`_store/event_prepare.py:99-102`), but the library/MCP READ path does not.

Because the MCP read tools delegate straight to the library (`_mcp_reads.py:295` -> `rebar.list_tickets`), an MCP client pointed at a host with a missing store is told "there are no tickets" instead of "this store is not initialized".

## Impact (observed in production)

The deployed rebar MCP server at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` has no `/app/.tickets-tracker`. It reports "Connected" and answers:

- `list_tickets` / `search` / `ready_tickets` -> `[]`   (silent)
- `show_ticket <real alias>`                  -> "ticket_not_found"  (loud but WRONG cause)
- `fsck`                                      -> "ticket system not initialized (/app/.tickets-tracker not found)"  (correct)

An agent following the repo's MCP-first tracker rule therefore sees an empty tracker, concludes no ticket exists for its work, and files duplicates -- the precise silent-data-hiding failure mode already recorded as a defect for the store-divergence case in bug bilingual-capitalist-caecilian ("Silent data-hiding: no error is surfaced to the operator; the store simply looks empty") and for the filter case in bug spiny-ferry-ripen.

## Authoritative sources violated

- `docs/mcp-reference.md:7` -- MCP faults are surfaced as distinct error codes "instead of
  silently resolving to a fallback", so "a driving agent can tell a broken config from a
  deliberate policy refusal". `[]` for a missing store defeats exactly this.
- Surface parity: the CLI (`reads_cli.py:340`) and library writes (`event_prepare.py:99`)
  both raise on this condition; library reads alone do not.

## Root cause

`_reads.py` resolves the tracker through `_tracker()` (`_reads.py:31-33`) and never checks that the directory exists; all 8 read entries funnel through it unguarded.

Origin: commit 7d53bc5b43b7 (2026-06-09, "#2 Steps 0/2/3") introduced the in-process read path, stating it replicated "each shim's exact contract" while explicitly noting the in-process reads "do not run the dispatcher's `_ensure_initialized`". Its parity test covered an *empty* store but never an *uninitialized* one; that test was later deleted as "now-moot" by 28406790c61e. Ticket: tend-tomb-doe (df9b-663a-98ed-4dc4), whose own scope was "Map in-process exceptions to existing RebarError shapes" + "parity tests green both ways".

## Reproduction (purely local, no network)

    tmp=$(mktemp -d); cd "$tmp"; git init -q .
    python3 -c "import rebar; print(rebar.list_tickets(repo_root='$tmp'))"   # -> []      (silent)
    python3 -c "import rebar; rebar.create_ticket('task','x',repo_root='$tmp')"  # -> RebarError: not initialized
    rebar list                                                              # -> Error: not initialized, exit 1

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A library read (`list_tickets`, `search`, `recent_session_logs`) against a repo with no
      tracker directory raises the same not-initialized `RebarError` the write path raises,
      instead of returning `[]`.
- [x] `show_ticket` against an uninitialized store reports the store as uninitialized rather
      than the misleading "Ticket '<id>' not found".
- [x] The corresponding MCP read tools surface that fault as a machine-readable error
      envelope, not an empty array.
- [x] An INITIALIZED-but-empty store still returns `[]` with no error (no regression).
- [x] Regression coverage asserts read/write parity on an uninitialized store.

## Scope of the read/write agreement — the predicates DIFFER, deliberately

Earlier wording in this plan claimed "read/write parity" without qualification. That overstates it, and plan review was right to block on the claim. Stated precisely:

Reads and writes now agree that an **ABSENT tracker directory** is an error. They deliberately do NOT agree about a directory that EXISTS but is not a git repo:

    write path   _store/event_prepare.py   isdir(tracker) AND exists(tracker/.git)
    CLI reads    _engine_support/reads_cli.py:340,384   isdir(tracker) only
    library reads  _reads._tracker (this change)        isdir(tracker) only

The read guard matches the CLI READ path, not the write path, and that is the correct target: the defect was that library reads disagreed with CLI reads. Adopting the write predicate would make library reads STRICTER than CLI reads — trading one asymmetry for a new one — and would break a live, supported case.

Verified empirically on a tracker whose `.git` was removed (the shape a `git archive` of the orphan `tickets` branch produces, documented in `tests/unit/test_store_copy_needs_env_id.py`):

    tracker dir exists: True | .git present: False
      READ  -> 1 ticket(s): reads WORK
      WRITE -> refused: "ticket system not initialized"

So reads on a `.git`-less store are working behavior that real fixtures depend on, not an oversight. The write path's extra `.git` check guards event APPENDS (provenance stamping) and has no read-side analogue.

The regression test is named for what it actually asserts — `test_reads_and_writes_agree_that_an_absent_store_is_an_error` — i.e. the absent-directory case only. No test claims the broader parity.
baseline.summary: Library and MCP reads mask an uninitialized store as an empty one (list/search/ready return [] instead of erroring)

## Context / Problem
Fourteen call sites in `src/rebar/llm` hand-build the SAME single-turn structured request shape: `mode="structured"` + `output_schema=<name>` + `execution_mode="single_turn"`, with `system_prompt` / `instructions` / `config` / `reviewers`. Verified on the tree: `overlap/judge.py:163,203`, `enrich.py:183`, `epic_bug_screen.py:266`, `evals/eval_solver.py:167`, `plan_review/__init__.py:172`, `plan_review/prerequisites.py:231`, `plan_review/xcheck.py:199,337`, `plan_review/completion_subcall.py:193`, `plan_review/passes.py:469,582`, `workflow/completion_recovery.py:404`, `code_review/workflow_ops.py:612`.

Two consequences of the copy-paste:

1. `RunRequest`'s own contract (`runner.py:96-100`) says a `single_turn` request must also carry
   `mode="structured"` + `output_schema` "so the two stay consistent" — but nothing enforces it;
   it is re-asserted by hand fourteen times.
2. The bounding decision is invisible. Only ONE of the fourteen declares any of the four
   lowering-only seams (`output_token_limit` / `structured_retry_limit` /
   `transport_attempt_limit` / `request_timeout_limit_s`): `judge_batch` (judge.py:211-214), and
   only `completion_recovery.py:413` sets a token cap. Confirmed by
   `grep -rn "output_token_limit=\|structured_retry_limit=\|transport_attempt_limit=\|request_timeout_limit_s=" src/rebar`.
   Omission is silent, so an unbounded site reads exactly like a deliberately-unbounded one.
   That is the shape of bug `leathery-druidic-nurseshark` (22da): it bounded `judge_batch` and
   the identical `judge_one` block four lines up stayed unbounded, unnoticed for days.

Not in scope, deliberately:
- **Bounding any site.** Every site keeps its CURRENT effective bounds. In particular
  `judge_one` stays unbounded: `kaolinite-head-wildebeest` (3939) closed `not_a_bug` on the
  grounds that `judge_one` has no production caller, and this story does not reopen it.
- **Model-class binding.** That is bug `afeb`'s mechanism (`cfg = replace(cfg, model=...)`)
  with its own oracle in `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`; folding a `model_class`
  argument into the builder would CHANGE the model at the sites that deliberately inherit.
- **`build_usage_limits` / `iteration_limit_for`.** `build_usage_limits` returning the BARE
  `req_limit` is deliberate and documented (`structured_run.py:427-432`, RP-01 S2): telemetry
  and `completion_banking.iteration_limit_for`'s `2*B` inverse both read the bare base, and the
  retry allowance is an addend only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`. There is no drift to
  fix. A single-turn run makes one model call with `tools=[]`, so `iteration_limit` is a no-op
  for it and the builder does not expose it.

## Approach
One shared constructor for the shape; the bounds decision becomes a REQUIRED argument.

1. `structured_run.py` (leaf module): add a frozen dataclass `SingleTurnBounds` with four
   fields and **no defaults** — `output_tokens`, `timeout_s`, `structured_retries`,
   `transport_attempts`, each `int | None`. `None` means "inherit run-wide policy", which is
   what an omitted seam does today (every seam is lowering-only: `runner._effective_config`
   `min()`s timeout/transport, `structured_run.output_retry_allowance` `min()`s retries).
2. `runner.py`: add `RunRequest.for_structured(*, system_prompt, instructions, config,
   reviewers, output_schema, bounds, target=None)` — keyword-only, `bounds` required — which
   fixes `mode="structured"` and `execution_mode="single_turn"` and maps `bounds` onto the four
   `RunRequest` fields. Add `RunRequest.INHERIT_POLICY: ClassVar[SingleTurnBounds]`, the named
   all-`None` value, so a site that inherits says so in one greppable token and needs no new
   import.
3. Adopt at all fourteen sites. Thirteen pass `bounds=RunRequest.INHERIT_POLICY`; `judge_batch`
   passes its existing four values; `completion_recovery.py:404` passes its token cap with the
   other three `None`. Byte-identical resulting `RunRequest` at every site.
4. Extend the existing site oracle. `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py::_run_request_sites`
   matches only `node.func.id == "RunRequest"`, so after adoption it would stop seeing fourteen
   sites and FAIL OPEN. Teach it to accept `RunRequest.for_structured` as well. The frozen
   `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` table (24 entries, its keys, config expressions and verdicts)
   is UNCHANGED — the `config=` expression at each site is untouched — so this is an
   oracle-scope repair, not an assertion edit.

## Guard construction
Per the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module (`runner.py`) exempt; match the AST conjunction that constitutes the construct — a direct `RunRequest(...)` call carrying BOTH `execution_mode="single_turn"` and `mode="structured"` — never a single token; escape marker `# single-turn-structured-ok: <reason>` with a mandatory non-empty reason, as `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` uses; behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`, the fourteen call sites above, `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` (oracle scope only), `tests/unit/test_run_request_builder.py` (new).

Line delta: adoption removes one line per site (two keywords out, one `bounds=` in); the shared builder plus dataclass add roughly thirty. This child is about line-neutral, not net-negative; the epic's net-negative criterion is a SUM over its consolidation children.

## Testing
- Builder unit tests: `for_structured` returns `mode="structured"` /
  `execution_mode="single_turn"`; each `SingleTurnBounds` field lands on its `RunRequest` field;
  `INHERIT_POLICY` leaves all four `None`.
- Edge: `for_structured(...)` without `bounds` raises `TypeError`; `SingleTurnBounds(...)`
  missing any field raises `TypeError`.
- Guard test (AST, `src/rebar` minus `runner.py`) with a marker-honouring escape and a test
  that an unreasoned marker does not excuse a site.
- Pinning, unchanged assertions: `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` (site table), `tests/unit/test_enrich.py`,
  `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No file under `src/rebar` except `runner.py` constructs a `RunRequest` carrying both
      `execution_mode="single_turn"` and `mode="structured"` without a reasoned
      `# single-turn-structured-ok:` marker; checked by the new guard test.
- [x] Calling `RunRequest.for_structured` without `bounds`, and `SingleTurnBounds` with any
      field missing, both raise `TypeError`; checked by the builder edge tests.
- [x] `_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES` still lists all 24 sites with the same keys, config
      expressions and verdicts after adoption; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`.
- [x] The pinning suites above pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest`.
baseline.summary: RunRequest.for_structured builder with required bounds for single-turn LLM calls

## Context

Bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events breaks the event store's append-only union invariant. Independently valid stale clones can then produce delete/modify conflicts instead of reconverging without history loss.

Gerrit change 989, commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d, removed queue and digest pruning and added a real two-clone regression proving both histories survive and merge cleanly. That was the required correctness and recovery fix.

Removing pruning creates a deliberate long-term retention problem. Each successful enrichment cycle normally appends ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST events; retries or claim races can append more. At the 2026-07-27 measurement, the live tickets tree contained 1,198 such files totaling about 1.23 MB: roughly 5.5% of tracker files and 0.5% of tracker bytes.

Queue reduction reads accumulated per-ticket event history, pending-work discovery scans every ticket directory, and latest-digest lookup enumerates the ticket directory. Without retention, live file/inode counts and these O(history) scans grow linearly, increasing clone, checkout, index, merge-tree, and operational costs. The former deletion scheme bounded only the live tree; deleted blobs remained in earlier Git history, so it never truly bounded repository storage.

Existing follow-up task 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d records the initial retention design work. This epic preserves the broader architectural context and is intentionally out of scope for the current session.

## Long-term objective

Design and land merge-safe retention, compaction, or archival semantics that bound hot/live tracker cost while preserving cross-clone convergence, crash recovery, auditability, and every independently committed event or a lossless compacted representation. Physical deletion or rename of committed UUID events is not an acceptable solution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current queue and digest growth rates and read/clone/index costs are measured with deterministic benchmarks.
- [ ] The chosen design bounds hot/live event lookup and working-tree growth without rewriting or deleting independently committed UUID events.
- [ ] Real two-clone stale-history tests prove independent retention operations reconverge cleanly and preserve all logical state.
- [ ] Crash recovery, claim leasing, latest-digest selection, auditability, and migration/rollback behavior are documented and tested.
- [ ] Operational rollout includes monitoring and a safe migration for existing unbounded histories.
- [ ] The relationship between live-tree retention and Git object/history storage is documented so the design does not claim storage reclamation it does not provide.

## Related evidence

- Closed root-cause bug: 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282
- Existing retention-design task: 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d
- Correctness fix: Gerrit change 989 / commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d
baseline.summary: Bound tracker growth without deleting committed event history

# `binding_store.py` is at 787/800 — extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster

Raised by the operator while reviewing change 1296 (ticket 88d9): "We're adding a lot to binding_store.py. Should we split that out to preemptively avoid the 800 LOC cap?" Measured rather than estimated: the file was **749** LOC, 1296 takes it to **787**, and the cap is **800**. Thirteen lines of headroom, and the CI module-size gate fails the build when ANY `src/rebar` file exceeds the cap — so the next contributor to touch this file breaks the build, having added nothing wrong.

Deliberately NOT done inside 1296: that change is a data-loss fix that needed to land promptly, and bundling a structural refactor into it would have made it slower to review and harder to reason about. The docstrings added there were tightened instead (795 -> 787) to buy immediate headroom.

## The seam, which already exists

`binding_store.py` holds two distinct concerns:

1. **binding lifecycle** — bind / confirm / unbind, absence + rekey handling, GC/retire grace, the
   immutable numeric Jira id (bug 7c26). This is the bulk of the file.
2. **last-synced PEER STATE** — the ADR-0026 three-way-merge baseline (`get_baseline`, `set_baseline`,
   `seed_baselines_from_snapshot`, `_BASELINE_FIELDS`) plus the peer-parent evidence channel added by
   1296 (`get_peer_parent`, `set_peer_parent`). Together ~130 LOC with docstrings — comfortably over
   the policy's 100-LOC floor for a new module, and a genuine cohesive concern: "what did the peer
   look like the last time we successfully looked".

Concern 2 has its own ADR, its own absence semantics ("an ABSENT baseline is VALID and degrades to local-wins"), and its own advance site in the pass (`reconcile._advance_baselines` / `_advance_peer_parent`). Its consumers are `outbound_field_diff`, `binding_walk` and now `inbound_fields` — none of which touch binding lifecycle.

## What makes this non-trivial, stated honestly

These are METHODS on `BindingStore`, not free functions, so this is not a file move. Extraction means either module-level helpers taking the entry dict (the store keeps thin delegating methods, so no caller changes) or a mixin. The first is preferable — it keeps the public surface identical, so every existing call site and every test double stays valid, and it makes the peer-state functions directly unit-testable without constructing a store.

Per the module-size policy this must be split ALONG THE SEAM ABOVE and not mechanically to hit a number, and the new module must not fall under 100 LOC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `binding_store.py` is under 700 LOC, and the new module is over 100
- [x] `BindingStore`'s public surface is UNCHANGED — no call site and no test double is edited to
      accommodate the split, asserted by the fact that the reconciler suites pass untouched
- [x] the peer-state functions are directly unit-testable without constructing a `BindingStore`, and
      at least one new test does so (otherwise the extraction bought nothing)
- [x] `_BASELINE_FIELDS` moves WITH the cluster, and `outbound_field_diff` / `binding_walk` /
      `inbound_fields` still resolve their reads (a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket)
- [x] the absence semantics survive the move verbatim: absent baseline degrades to local-wins, absent
      peer parent degrades to NO CLEAR. A test pins each, because these are the properties that make
      the cluster safe and a refactor is exactly when they get quietly dropped
- [x] the module-size gate passes, and the full reconciler unit + integration suites pass
baseline.summary: binding_store.py is at 787/800: extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster
