## Context / Problem
Automated bug filers can spam duplicates, file on single flakes, or silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces). The audit surface is the THREE existing filers — no new filer is built; this ticket HARDENS what exists and documents the contract for future filers: the heartbeat-alert filer (scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:197) and the binding-drift-alert filer (cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:350) — canary_bridge.py has exactly these two create sites, verified by inventory —, plus `_file_conflict_bug_ticket` in the reconciler applier (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:135, called at :522), which today files one bug per unresolved (local, Jira) conflict with no dedup key, no template contract, and no empty-detail abort.

## Approach
Per OSS practice (PyTorch DISABLED-test bot, Flutter flake bot, Sentry fingerprinting, Alertmanager 'for:'): dedup via a stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day; templated body (check name, first-red time, run URL, failing-output tail, workflow path) with abort-if-empty-detail; recovery comment on green with close left to agents is documented in the CONTRACT as the default for future filers whose bugs carry investigation value; it is NOT retrofitted anywhere in this ticket. The two canary_bridge filers ALREADY auto-close their alert ticket on green via `rebar transition open closed --force-close` (cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:247-262, cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:398-410) — that existing recovery contract is KEPT AS-IS (pure state alerts, nothing to investigate once green); the audit records this divergence and its rationale in the table rather than retrofitting agent-close onto them. Pattern elements apply per-site by SEMANTIC FIT, recorded in the audit table: the N>=2 consecutive-red threshold applies only where a derivable red/green run signal exists: the HEARTBEAT filer only — its stale check fails the canary run (the 'Fail job on stale' step), so the workflow's previous run conclusion carries the signal. The BINDING-DRIFT filer gets NO threshold, with rationale recorded: its oracle never fails the run (conclusion carries no drift signal), and drift is PERSISTENT state, not a flake — it cannot self-heal between runs, so first-observation filing is correct and dedup + daily accumulation already bound spam; the conflict filer has no cycle semantics, so it gets dedup (stable tag derived from the conflict identity: local id + jira key), template, abort-if-empty, and detected_by — not the threshold. CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE: no new state store — the workflow's own run history is the durable state. On red, the filer queries the same workflow's previous completed run conclusion (gh api repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs?status=completed&per_page=2, excluding the current run); previous-also-red => threshold met; previous-green-or-absent => first red, no ticket. Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path regardless of threshold. ACCUMULATION DEDUP ('max one accumulation comment/day'): derived from the target ticket's OWN comment history — the accumulation comment opens with a stable marker line; the filer reads the ticket (rebar show --output json), finds the newest marker-bearing comment, and skips if it is <24h old. The ticket store IS the durable state; no new store, and the */20 cron cannot spam. First-red time in the template = the previous red run's timestamp. WORKFLOW THREADING (scope): the consuming alert steps in .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml today pass only STALE/RUN_URL/DRIFT_* env; the heartbeat alert step's run-history query additionally needs GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (already used by other steps in that workflow), the repo (github.repository), and the workflow file id (the literal filename) threaded as step env — enumerated as workflow edits in scope, heartbeat step only. The contract doc records the same recipe for future filers with run-conclusion signals. LIFECYCLE: green with no open tagged ticket (single flake that never crossed the threshold) => recovery path no-ops on the empty has-tag search — stated as an invariant and unit-tested. USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS: (a) audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit the fitting pattern elements; (b) document the bug-creation contract for automation — exact rebar create args, exit codes, dedup search command, REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var — so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create.

## Scope
- canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic (coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py `_file_conflict_bug_ticket`: dedup tag + template + abort-if-empty + detected_by (no threshold — no red/green cycle)
- docs: bug-creation contract page
- audit table of every auto-file site in the change description, with a per-site row: which pattern elements apply and why

## Testing
Heartbeat-filer unit tests: first red -> no ticket; second consecutive red -> one ticket with template fields; third red same day -> accumulation comment, not a new ticket; second accumulation within 24h -> skipped (marker-line dedup); green with open ticket -> existing auto-close path preserved (transition open closed --force-close, unchanged); green with NO open ticket -> no-op, exit 0; empty detail -> abort with loud log, no hollow ticket; previous-run query failure -> treated as first red (fail toward not filing, loud log). Binding-drift tests: first observed drift -> one ticket (no threshold, rationale in table); repeat drift -> accumulation not duplicate; green -> existing auto-close preserved. Conflict-filer tests: same conflict twice -> one ticket + one accumulation comment; distinct conflicts -> distinct tickets; empty conflict detail -> abort.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All three audited auto-file sites use the fitting dedup+template pattern elements (audit table enumerates sites x elements with rationale, including the kept auto-close divergence and the binding-drift no-threshold rationale).
- [x] Heartbeat consecutive-red threshold implemented via workflow run-history query; no new state store introduced; single flake files nothing.
- [x] Bug-creation contract documented and referenced by every filer.
- [x] Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above, including the green-with-no-ticket no-op and the query-failure arm.
- [x] detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).
baseline.summary: Auto-bug-filer hardening: dedup pattern, all-site audit, contract doc

## Summary
rebar's LLM runner inherits `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the environment, so when a local
Claude-Code payload-optimizing proxy (headroom, `http://127.0.0.1:8787`) is enabled, ALL
of rebar's agentic LLM calls are routed through it. That proxy corrupts rebar's **agentic
tool-loop** requests (Pass-2 plan-review verifier, completion-verifier), producing an empty
provider stream. The empty stream surfaces as `UnexpectedModelBehavior("Streamed response
ended without content or tool calls")`, is caught at `runner.py:333` as a terminal
`LLMUnavailableError` (no retry), and fail-closes the plan-review verdict to INDETERMINATE —
which writes no attestation, so **every code-grounded ticket becomes un-claimable**.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Enable headroom (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787`).
2. `rebar review-plan <code-grounded-epic>` (e.g. ac1b-cef3-35c8-415f).
3. Observe `coverage.verify_failed=True`, `coverage.metrics.verify_requests=0`,
   `coverage.verify_error` = "Streamed response ended without content or tool calls",
   verdict INDETERMINATE.

Expected: verify completes; verdict PASS/BLOCK on the plan's merits.
Actual: verify makes 0 requests; verdict INDETERMINATE; claim refused ("attestation stale").

Discriminating proof: `env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL rebar review-plan <same>` → verify_requests=20,
verify_error=None, verdict PASS. Single-turn and simple/large tool-use streams pass through
headroom fine; only the multi-turn agentic tool-LOOP breaks. RTK (bash hook) is not involved.

## Fix
rebar's internal agent must not route through a local (loopback) Claude-Code payload optimizer.
When the resolved model is Anthropic and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a loopback host, build the
Anthropic model with a provider pinned to the direct public API (bypassing the local proxy).
Respect non-loopback gateways (untouched). Opt out with `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY=1`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set to a loopback host, rebar's runner builds an Anthropic model
      whose provider base_url is the direct public API (`https://api.anthropic.com`), not the loopback.
- [ ] A non-loopback `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (a real gateway) is respected (passed through unchanged).
- [ ] `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY=1` opts back in (no bypass) for users who intend the local proxy.
- [ ] Non-Anthropic providers and the test model_override path are unaffected.
- [ ] Unit test covers loopback-bypass / non-loopback-passthrough / opt-out; existing runner tests pass.
- [ ] Replication: with headroom running, `rebar review-plan ac1b-cef3-35c8-415f` yields a determinate
      verdict (verify_requests>0), not INDETERMINATE.
baseline.summary: runner routes agentic LLM calls through local headroom proxy -> empty stream -> INDETERMINATE

## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'you're authorized to configure our bridge to run hourly instead of continuously for this project in order to free the runner.'

The config half is done: `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` was flipped true -> false at 2026-08-13T14:59Z, so the self-re-dispatch chain stops after its in-flight pass and the runner slot frees. The bridge now runs solely on `reconcile-bridge.yml`'s cron, which change 1726 (f59a-2d16-68c5-450c) just set to a uniform 40-minute three-entry schedule. Operator intent here is HOURLY, so that block is now wrong and over-elaborate — the three-entry spelling existed only because cron cannot express 40 minutes in one entry.

## Approach
1. **The schedule** — replace the three entries in `reconcile-bridge.yml` with the single entry `23 * * * *`. Off-:00 deliberately: GitHub's scheduler is best-effort and most contended at the top of the hour, so an on-:00 entry is likeliest to be delayed or dropped. `workflow_dispatch` stays (manual runs); AC1's "no other trigger" is about automatic firing.
2. **The cadence test** — `test_bridge_backstop_fires_on_a_uniform_40_minute_cadence` (added by 1726) derives the day's fire times from the cron entries and asserts every consecutive gap, wrapping past midnight. Keep that machinery — it catches what a literal pin cannot — and retarget it: rename to `..._on_a_uniform_hourly_cadence`, assert the gap set is exactly `{60}`, and add two assertions the hourly form makes meaningful: exactly ONE schedule entry (the three-entry workaround must not survive as dead weight) and a non-zero minute (the off-:00 hygiene, otherwise unenforced). `_cron_field_matches` is unchanged.
3. **Pinned literals** — `_UNCHANGED_CRONS`, `test_reconcilers_keep_their_own_schedules_and_never_cancel`, and `test_github_schedule_and_continuous_redispatch_remain_compatible` each pin 1726's three-entry list; all take the single hourly entry. The canary's `0 */2 * * *` pin is unchanged — it stays 2-hourly per pittabird.
4. **Jenkinsfile** — the three-line `cron('''…''')` block collapses to `cron('23 * * * *')`, its 40-minute comment rewritten.
5. **Canary staleness arithmetic** — the canary header derives its window as "3x cadence". At 40 min the floor was 2h against a 4h window; hourly it becomes 3h, still inside 4h, so **the window does not change** — only the sentence naming 40 minutes. `canary_bridge.py`'s alert body "bridge cadence: 40 minutes" becomes "hourly". This is the one place the change could silently create false alarms, so it is checked, not assumed.
6. **The CloudWatch alarm — a real break, not a comment** — `monitoring_bridge.tf`'s `bridge_run_failures` alarm is `Sum`, `period = 3600`, `threshold = 1`, `GreaterThanThreshold`: "two failed passes in one hour" (its comment still says the bridge "runs every ~20 minutes"). Hourly, at most ONE pass falls in a bucket, so the Sum can never exceed 1 and **the alarm becomes structurally unfirable** — the silent monitoring regression it exists to prevent (the 2026-08-12 token expiry that produced no signal). Retune to keep the intent (a blip stays quiet, a sustained failure pages): keep `period = 3600`, set `threshold = 0`, `evaluation_periods = 2`, `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` — two CONSECUTIVE hourly buckets each with a failed pass. A healthy pass publishes 0, failing `> 0` and breaking the streak, so single flakes stay quiet. Detection latency ~40 min -> ~2h; update the description and both cadence comments.
   **Apply consequence, stated not discovered:** `terraform-drift.yml` runs `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` on `infra/terraform/**` changes and FAILS on a non-empty plan, so this leaves Terraform Drift red until an operator applies it — called out on the ticket at landing so the apply is sequenced, not discovered as a mystery red.
7. **Comments and docs** — every remaining "40-minute"/"40 min": the bridge header, schedule comment, re-dispatch backstop references and `::warning::` string; the `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` and `test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` docstrings; and `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — cadence table, the "…40-minute floor" heading plus its three anchor links, its bullets, and the latency note recording the new **1 hour** worst case.

1726's chain-pacing step stays: gated on `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS`, now false, so it is inert here — but this file is a client-copied TEMPLATE and an adopter may still opt in. Deleting a working opt-in mechanism is not what "run hourly for this project" asks for.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` — single hourly cron + comment rewrites.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` — staleness arithmetic sentence only.
- `Jenkinsfile` — single hourly cron.
- `scripts/canary_bridge.py` — alert-body cadence string.
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — cadence table, heading + anchors, 1h latency note.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_bridge.tf` — retune `bridge_run_failures` to stay firable hourly.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` — retargeted cadence test, literal pin, docstring.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py` — pins.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` — docstring.

## Testing
- **Happy path:** the retargeted cadence test derives fire times from the workflow's own cron and asserts the gap set is exactly `{60}` — a property, not a literal echo. The three pins assert the single-entry list.
- **Edge / regression:** the same test asserts one schedule entry and a non-zero minute, so neither a reintroduced multi-entry block nor an on-:00 drift passes silently. Both are checked by mutating the workflow locally (a second entry; minute 0) and confirming the test fails before reverting.
- **Alarm arithmetic:** confirm by hand that one failed pass in an hour does NOT breach (one bucket, two consecutive required) and two consecutive failing hours DOES — so the retune preserves the quiet-on-a-blip intent, not merely firability.
- **False-alarm check:** confirm the canary arithmetic still holds — 3 x 60 min = 3h floor inside the unchanged 4h window — and that `tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge*.py` and `test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py` pass unchanged (they set `ALERT_WINDOW_HOURS` explicitly).
- **Gates:** the `check_*` gates, generator no-diff, `make lint` (actionlint parses the workflow), `make typecheck`, the CI unit selection, and `tests/integration`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `reconcile-bridge.yml` has exactly one `schedule:` entry, `23 * * * *`, and no other automatic trigger; `workflow_dispatch` remains for manual runs.
- [x] The cadence test derives the schedule and asserts a uniform 60-minute gap, a single entry, and a non-zero minute; the mutation checks in Testing confirm it fails on a second entry and on an on-:00 minute.
- [x] The three pinned cron literals, `Jenkinsfile`, `scripts/canary_bridge.py`, and every workflow/test comment are updated so that NOTHING still asserts a 40-minute bridge cadence. Remaining '40 min' text is allowed only where explicitly historical — why the retired three-entry form existed, or what the detection latency moved FROM — each checked by hand. `tests/unit/test_bridge_output_parsing.py:6` ('a 40-minute scheduled live job') is out of scope: it describes the external live-DC harness job, not the bridge.
- [x] The `bridge_run_failures` alarm can still fire hourly (`threshold = 0`, `evaluation_periods = 2`, `datapoints_to_alarm = 2`), its description and comments name the ~2h detection latency, and the ticket records that a `terraform apply` is required and Terraform Drift stays red until it happens.
- [x] `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` records the 1-hour worst-case latency and its cadence table reads hourly; the canary stays 2-hourly, window unchanged at 4h, arithmetic sentence corrected.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the CI unit selection, and `tests/integration` are green.
baseline.summary: Bridge schedule to hourly now that continuous is off

## What
When `rebar create` makes a work ticket whose type is **not** `bug`/`session_log`
(i.e. `task`/`story`/`epic`), print a **stderr warning** that no `file_impact` was
recorded, nudging the author to run `set-file-impact` before the plan-review gate.
This surfaces the plan-review **file-impact-coverage (P9)** requirement *early*, at
create time, instead of only when `review-plan` runs — so it can be fixed before a
full review round (the churn seen on ticket f112, re-reviewed after file_impact was added).

## Why
`file_impact` cannot be supplied at create time (only via a later `set-file-impact`),
and the P9 detector (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:645`, `applicable = not
ctx.children`) flags any leaf work ticket lacking it. `bug`/`session_log` are gate-
exempt upstream (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:540`), so the warning mirrors that exemption.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` `create_cli()`: after a successful create, if
  `ticket_type not in ("bug", "session_log")`, emit
  `print("Warning: no file_impact recorded ...", file=sys.stderr)` (matches existing
  `Warning:`-to-stderr convention in transition.py/txn.py/unlink.py).
- Keep stdout pure (created alias/id line unchanged); warning goes to stderr only.
- Not in scope: a `--file-impact` create flag or MCP structured warning (follow-ups).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar create task "x"` with no file_impact prints a `Warning:` line to **stderr** naming the id and pointing at `set-file-impact`; stdout stays pure (alias/id line only).
- [ ] `rebar create bug "x"` and `rebar create session_log ...` print **no** such warning.
- [ ] A test in `tests/integration/test_stdout_purity.py` (or equivalent) asserts the stderr warning for `task` and its absence for `bug`.
- [ ] `make lint` and the touched tests pass.
baseline.summary: create: warn on stderr when a non-bug ticket is created without file_impact

# Wire run_eval (Inspect Task) + eval-live CI (2.5)

## What

Replace the `run_eval()` NotImplementedError with a native live eval loop (Inspect AI is intentionally NOT used — agentic ops don't fit its single-completion solver model; see the rationale comment in eval.py):
dataset -> solver (task 2.2) -> generator call -> scorers (registry, task 2.1) ->
epochs/at_least(k)/coverage/judge_alignment(kappa over gold_set) -> JUnit via to_junit.
Behind the `eval` extra (guard_import). Then wire `.github/workflows/eval.yml`
`eval-live` to actually run for all specs, with community-standard CI + cost rails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `run_eval()` runs a real live eval for any dataset-bearing spec (no longer raises NotImplementedError) via a native loop over the eval solver that reuses the discipline primitives (at_least(k)/coverage/JUnit/registry); the live runner is gated by the `agents` extra; Inspect AI is intentionally not used (rationale in eval.py); offline discipline functions remain the pinned logic.
- [ ] Deterministic scorers gate; llm-judge reports; coverage + kappa applied; JUnit emitted.
- [ ] `eval-live` triggers on workflow_dispatch + weekly schedule (job `if:` includes 'schedule'), `continue-on-error: true` (non-blocking), and `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`. Cost rails: cases run SEQUENTIALLY (run_eval has no model fan-out; concurrency 1 under the workflow cap), a per-run case ceiling via `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES` (passed to `run_eval(max_cases=...)`), and `actions/cache` on the pip cache (the native loop has no promptfoo response-cache dir to cache).
- [ ] Fork-safe: live calls never run on fork PRs/Dependabot; no pull_request_target checking out fork code; spend-cap guidance documented.
- [ ] `eval-discipline` remains the only required PR check (zero-cost).
baseline.summary: Wire run_eval (Inspect) + eval-live CI (2.5)

## Why

The floor must key on VERIFIED delivery, never bare `closed` status — otherwise a force-closed or
abandoned child would launder un-validated work past scrutiny, and a stale closed ticket can hard-
block the epic review (observed in practice).

## What

Add a `delivered_now(child, epic, repo_root)` helper (in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`,
reusing the `compute_validity(sig, child_state, 'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read check used INSIDE `_child_closure_findings` in `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — note that fn is a DEFICIT detector (returns findings for children LACKING delivery), so we reuse its validity CALL applied to children whose status IS closed, NOT the fn itself) that returns True iff
the child is `closed` AND holds a completion-verifier attestation that is VALID on read
(`compute_validity(..., "completion-verifier")` — so drift-stale / force-closed / unsigned all read
false), OR child B is superseded by a SIBLING A (same parent; direction B superseded_by A) that is itself a live vehicle (delivered-now OR open/in_progress, not force-closed/abandoned) (read the
`supersedes`/`duplicates` links via `src/rebar/__init__.py`; verify shared parent so work that left
the epic does not count as delivered). Recomputed each run. In-progress / abandoned / force-closed
children return False -> stay in scope.

## Scope

- IN: the `delivered_now` predicate + its sibling-supersede check + validity-on-read reuse.
- OUT: the Pass-3 wiring (separate story); the Pass-2 sub-call (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `delivered_now` is True for a closed child with a VALID completion attestation; False for force-closed, unsigned, drift-stale, in-progress, and abandoned children.
- [ ] `delivered_now` treats B as delivered-elsewhere ONLY when a SIBLING A (same parent) supersedes B (direction: B superseded_by A) AND A is a live in-epic vehicle (delivered-now OR active open/in_progress); False when A is not a sibling or is itself force-closed/abandoned (closes the supersede-direction + replacement-not-done gap).
- [ ] The predicate reuses the `compute_validity(..., 'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read call (NOT the deficit-detector `_child_closure_findings` itself), applied to closed children, and is recomputed per run (no persisted state).
- [ ] Unit tests cover attested / force-closed / drift-stale / supersede-sibling / supersede-nonsibling / in-progress cases.

## Supersede mechanism (concrete artifact)

The supersede relationship is the structured `supersedes` LINK RELATION (one of rebar's six link
relations) — an auditable, event-sourced graph edge in the ticket's deps, NOT a free-text note,
tag, or naming convention. `delivered_now` reads it via `rebar.show`/`ticket_deps`: child B is
delivered-elsewhere iff a SIBLING A (same `parent_id`) has an `A supersedes B` edge (equivalently B
`superseded_by` A) AND A is a live in-epic vehicle (delivered-now OR open/in_progress). Because the
edge is a structured graph relation (not unsigned prose) AND the superseding sibling A stays in
review scope, this is NOT the unsigned/gameable suppression the Alternatives reject: no coverage is
removed (A is still reviewed), and the security/contract preserve-set (T5c/T10) is never dropped
regardless of supersede — so a manipulated edge cannot launder a security finding.

## Acceptance Criteria (mechanism)

- [ ] The supersede signal is the structured `supersedes` link relation read from the child's deps (named artifact), not a note/tag/convention.
- [ ] A test asserts the security/contract preserve-set is never dropped even when a supersede edge is present (no laundering).

## Acceptance Criteria (reopen semantics)

- [ ] A PARENT epic reopen does NOT un-deliver its closed children: ADR 0009 keys on each ticket's OWN `last_reopened_at`, so only a CHILD's own reopen invalidates that child's completion attestation. Closed children remain `delivered-now` across a parent reopen; a reopened child flips to not-delivered and its findings resurface.
baseline.summary: delivered-now predicate: reuse completion attestation (validity-on-read) + in-epic sibling supersede

## Why
Implementing this epic's session-provenance fold (`_fold_claimed_session`, stories 68ef + c557) added the claiming-session/harness fold to `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`, which was already at EXACTLY the 800-LOC module-size soft cap on `main`. The additions pushed it to 832, tripping the CI module-size gate. Rather than allowlist it (grow the grandfathered over-cap set), split the file along the clean seam that already exists: the per-event **processors** vs the two-pass **replay engine**.

## What
- **New module `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py`** — move the replay ENGINE out of
  `_processors.py`: `scan_for_latest_snapshot`, `_ReplayCtx`, the flat `_EVENT_HANDLERS`
  dispatch table, and `replay_events`. This is a one-way dependency (the engine imports the
  `process_*` processors; the processors never call the engine), so it is a clean seam.
- **`_processors.py`** keeps ONLY the per-event `process_*` fold functions; drop the
  now-unused imports (`Callable`, `NamedTuple`, `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`, `TAG_DELTA` — all were
  used solely by the engine/handler-table). Result: `_processors.py` drops from 832 to ~652
  LOC, back under the 800 soft cap with no allowlist change.
- **Importers** — `reducer/_api.py` and `reducer/__init__.py` import `replay_events` /
  `scan_for_latest_snapshot` from `._replay` instead of `._processors` (and the `__init__`
  module docstring's provenance note is updated).
- **Test** — `tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_tag_delta.py::test_downgraded_clone_preserves_and_ignores`
  monkeypatches `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` / `TAG_DELTA`; retarget those patches from `_processors`
  to `_replay` (the module the replay loop now reads them from).
- Pure move — NO behavior change; the reducer's public API (`reduce_ticket`, `replay_events`,
  `scan_for_latest_snapshot`, the `process_*` functions) is unchanged.

## Scope
- IN: the file move (`_replay.py`), the `_processors.py` trim + import cleanup, the two
  importer updates, and the one test monkeypatch retarget.
- OUT: any behavior change; further reducer decomposition; the session-provenance feature
  itself (stories 68ef / c557 / 199b).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` is under the 800-LOC soft cap (no allowlist/ceilings
      entry added). Proof: `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py)" -lt 800 ]` exits 0
      (the file prints fewer than 800 lines).
- [ ] `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` exists and holds all four engine symbols: `replay_events`,
      `scan_for_latest_snapshot`, `_ReplayCtx`, and `_EVENT_HANDLERS`. Proof: each of
      `grep -q "def replay_events"`, `grep -q "def scan_for_latest_snapshot"`,
      `grep -q "class _ReplayCtx"`, and `grep -q "_EVENT_HANDLERS"` on
      `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` succeeds.
- [ ] The public reducer API still imports and works: `replay_events` /
      `scan_for_latest_snapshot` resolve from `rebar.reducer`, and `reduce_ticket` is unchanged.
      Proof: `python -c "from rebar.reducer import replay_events, scan_for_latest_snapshot, reduce_ticket"`.
- [ ] The module-size CONTRACT test passes (no over-cap drift). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py -q`.
- [ ] The reducer test suite (incl. the retargeted downgraded-clone test) stays green. Proof:
      `pytest tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_tag_delta.py -q` and the full
      `tests/scripts/reducer/` directory.

## Depends on
- (none — a mechanical extraction; lands as the BASE of the session-provenance stack so the
  fold-bearing commits stay under the cap.)

## Context / Problem
After Gerrit 1796, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` sits at 800 LOC (the absolute CI module-size cap) and `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` at 799. Any edit to either must extract first or the module-size gate fails. Each module carries several distinct concerns. Operator direction: remediate BOTH architecturally — separate concerns into modules with clear contractual boundaries, not a mechanical split to duck under the cap.

## Concern map (from the real call graph, verified by Serena refs + grep string sweep)
`completion.py` (800) holds four concerns: (1) operation orchestration — `verify_completion`/`_verify_completion_inner`/`_verifier_model_for_completion`/`verify_step_floor` (consumers: `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:38`, `workflow/completion_banking.py:38`, `workflow/gate_dispatch.py`); (2) deterministic child-closure gate — `child_closure_findings`/`_uncertified_child_ids`/`build_child_closure_evidence` (consumer: `workflow/gate_ops.py:61,224`); (3) epic-close bug-screen deterministic layer — `EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_CEILING`, `_epic_subtree_states`, `_open_bugs`, `_first_in_progress_ns`, `epic_bug_floor_findings`, `epic_bug_candidates` (consumers: `gate_ops.py:64`, `epic_bug_screen.py:267-275`, whose docstring already describes these as the screen's DET stages 1-2); (4) verdict reconciliation — remediation constants, `reconcile_verdict` + fault/insufficiency helpers, `deterministic_child_failure`. `completion_recovery.py` (799) holds three: (5) criteria surface + admission bounds + coverage contract — `explicit_completion_criteria`, `physical_context_ceiling`, `_validate_recovery_inputs`, `_validate_coverage`, the checkbox regexes and `_MAX_*` bounds; (6) failure taxonomy — `_normalized_finish_reason`, `_is_token_exhaustion`, `_bounded_diagnostic`, `raise_completion_workflow_failure`; (7) recovery orchestration — `CompletionAgentStep` (primary run + banked successors + finalization).

## Approach — target modules and their contracts
Behavior-preserving moves along the existing seams above; no signature or logic changes. Keep documented public seams stable via re-export; move internal consumers to the new homes.
- `rebar/llm/completion.py` (~250 LOC): OWNS the completion-verification operation (entry `verify_completion`, model/budget tuning `verify_step_floor`/`_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX`/`_verifier_model_for_completion`) and REMAINS the stable public seam its `__all__` documents: re-exports `child_closure_findings`, `build_child_closure_evidence`, `deterministic_child_failure`, `reconcile_verdict`, `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE`, and `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_REMEDIATION` (imported by name at `tests/unit/workflow/test_insufficient_evidence_marker.py:315`) — so `gate_ops` imports and `monkeypatch` strings on `rebar.llm.completion.*` (e.g. `tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py:209`) stay valid unchanged.
- NEW `rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py` (~210): OWNS the deterministic child-closure invariant + evidence block (concern 2). Exposes `child_closure_findings`, `build_child_closure_evidence`.
- NEW `rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py` (~290): OWNS verdict normalization + remediation (concern 4): `reconcile_verdict`, `_findings_from_criteria`, `_is_no_verdict_fault`, `_insufficiency_only`, `NO_VERDICT_CRITERION`, both remediation constants, and `deterministic_child_failure` (the no-LLM FAIL verdict).
- `rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py` (297 → ~460): ABSORBS concern 3 so the entire epic bug screen (DET floor, DET candidate filter, LLM screen) is one module; `gate_ops.py:64` and `epic_bug_screen.py:267-275` switch to local/`epic_bug_screen` imports. The epic_bug_* symbols are NOT re-exported from completion.py, so EVERY `completion.epic_bug_*` reader in `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py` repoints to `epic_bug_screen`: direct attribute-call sites at lines 79, 94, 103, 112, 120, 129, 136, 238 AND monkeypatch targets at 230 (`EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_CEILING`) and 450 (`epic_bug_floor_findings`) — import/alias switch only.
- NEW `rebar/llm/workflow/completion_criteria.py` (~240): OWNS concern 5 — what counts as a completion criterion, the recovery admission bounds, and the full-coverage contract.
- NEW `rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` (~230): OWNS concern 6 — typed exhaustion classification, bounded allowlisted diagnostics, and workflow-failure finalization.
- `rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` (~420): keeps `CompletionAgentStep` + finalizer constants; re-exports `explicit_completion_criteria`, `raise_completion_workflow_failure` (its documented `__all__`) AND `physical_context_ceiling` — so `gate_dispatch.py:669`, `completion_prefetch.py:214`, the patch string `test_completion_prefetch.py:120`, and every `_cr.physical_context_ceiling` module-alias read (`test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py:66`, `test_completion_token_recovery.py:312`, `test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py:94-97`, `test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py:57,220`) stay valid unchanged. Underscore-helper module-alias reads repoint to `completion_criteria`: `_validate_recovery_inputs` (`test_completion_recovery_contract.py`, `test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py:112-137`), `_validate_coverage` (`test_completion_recovery_contract.py`, `test_completion_banking.py:219-239`, `test_insufficient_evidence_marker.py:288-296`), `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (`test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py:190-191`).
Caller updates: `completion.py:758` prelude imports and doc cross-references. Tests get import-path and monkeypatch-target updates ONLY; zero assertion changes. Riskiest assumption: every moved symbol stays patchable where its runtime caller reads it. Cheapest falsifier, run FIRST per move: grep the moved name as a string across src+tests (monkeypatch/patch/importlib/getattr).

## Scope
Edit: `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`, `src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py`. Create: `src/rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_criteria.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py`. Test import/patch-target updates in `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py` and the recovery suites that import underscore helpers (`test_completion_recovery_contract.py`, `test_completion_recovery_context_product_bound.py`, `test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py`, `test_completion_banking.py`, `test_insufficient_evidence_marker.py`).

## Testing
Mechanical, behavior-preserving refactor — no new testable behavior; the existing suites are the oracle, unmodified except import paths/patch targets: `pytest tests/unit/workflow tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py tests/unit/test_agent_call_runaway_guard_c827.py tests/interfaces`; `make lint` (complexity ratchet must report new=0 increased=0) and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every touched/created module ends 200-500 LOC (hard: none > 700, none < 100); checked by `wc -l` on the nine modules above.
- [x] Decomposition plan (concern map + module contracts) recorded on this ticket before implementation; checked: this description section + a summarizing ticket comment exist.
- [x] Zero behavior change: the suites named in Testing pass with no assertion edits (import-path/monkeypatch-target updates only); checked by running them green.
- [x] Every moved symbol's dotted name swept as a string across src+tests with no orphaned patch targets; checked: grep for each old dotted path returns only intentionally-kept re-export seams.
- [x] `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0; module-size check green (all `src/rebar` files ≤ 800).
- [x] Change pushed to Gerrit carrying trailer `rebar-ticket: 45c1-513b-d97a-46d3`; checked by the created change number (submit/close deferred to the operator per instructions).

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Existing stores — including client deployments — have no `.bridge_state/projects.json` and no `bridge_project` on any ticket. Without a migration they read every ticket as absent-project with no recorded legacy default for the resolver to fall back to, so a store that syncs today stops syncing on upgrade.

## Prerequisites (substrate, from cited deps — already `depends_on` edges)

- `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]` — the projects-mapping store `projects_store.py`: the
  `.bridge_state/projects.json` record (`{version, legacy_default, projects}`), `load_mapping`, the
  `Mapping` dataclass, the tri-state resolver `resolve_project` (absent field → `legacy_default`;
  `""` → `None`; key → verbatim), and `set_project`/`read_projects`.
- `[rebar:67f9-4a07-9667-446a]` — registers `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
  (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`), so
  a store may stamp it and still pass its own compat gate.

`Backend.project` (`_backend.py:598-605`, the effective write/create scope) is pre-existing.

## Approach

Ship the migration as ensure units on the idempotent registry (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `REGISTRY_IDS` `:66`, `_registry()` `:82`) — rebar's sanctioned seam (`docs/migrations.md:40-56`; the ordered School-A ledger is deliberately not built, `:14-16`). Units run at init/re-init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot (`:57-65`), so a client store converges with no operator action.

**No ticket events.** An EDIT-per-ticket migration would be a four-figure event write under the store lock, and MCP-boot runs the sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended (`:63-65`) — so it would silently skip at one entry point and converge unpredictably. Instead the unit records `legacy_default` once, and `resolve_project` `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]` treats every absent-field ticket as belonging to it. One small write migrates the whole store.

Two units, both check-then-act and safe to re-run:

1. **Seed the mapping.** If `.bridge_state/projects.json` `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]` is absent, write it with
   `legacy_default` and a single `projects` entry from `Backend.project` (`_backend.py:598-605`); if
   present, return `ok` and write nothing. Tree-check the committed
   `tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json` blob before committing so a converged store makes zero commits
   (`docs/migrations.md:45-46`).
2. **Converge the capability stamp (backstop, NOT the trigger).** Per the parent epic 0e68, the
   *authoritative* `multi-project-bridge` stamp is written by the `bridge projects` set/remove write
   path — the stamp and the mapping mutation land in the SAME tracker commit (one atomic publish). This
   ensure unit is only a **convergence backstop for residual divergence**: when the mapping already
   holds more than one project but `.store-compat.json`'s `required_capabilities` lacks
   `multi-project-bridge` (a legacy store, or a crash between the write path's two writes), it adds the
   token; a single-project store is never stamped and stays usable by older binaries. It is
   level-triggered on the mapping state and decoupled from *how* the store became multi-project, and is
   never the primary trigger — the seed above only ever makes a **one-project** mapping, so this unit
   never fires from the same sweep's seed. The token is registered in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` by
   prerequisite `[rebar:67f9-4a07-9667-446a]` (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`, the `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`
   frozenset), so a stamped store still passes `check_store_compat` on this binary — this story makes
   **no** `compat.py` edit, and a test asserts a two-project stamped store passes the gate.

Ids are new and never reused (`docs/migrations.md:50-51`).

**Unit bodies live in a new `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py`**, not `init.py` (where the six existing units live, e.g. `_store_compat_unit` `:509`). `init.py` is **758 lines** — ~42 under the 800-line gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so this is a **cohesion** choice, not size-forced: the projects migration is distinct from init's `.gitignore`/`.gitattributes` constants. `ensures.py` (257 lines) gains only its two registry entries.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` (new) — both unit bodies
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — two `REGISTRY_IDS` entries + two `_registry()` mappings
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_ensures.py` — update the hardcoded `expected` id-set literal in
  `test_registry_id_set_is_frozen` (`:57`, the six existing ids) to add the two new ids so the
  registry-agreement test passes
- `docs/migrations.md` — document the two units and the `multi-project-bridge` token's meaning for
  other binaries/operators (it gates `.store-compat.json` compatibility)
- `tests/integration/test_ensure_project_mapping.py` (new) — the behavioural oracle below

## Testing

Real temp git repos and refs (the shared standard's git row) — the units commit to `tickets` and the zero-commit-when-converged property is only observable against real refs.

- Happy path: sweeping a no-mapping store creates one whose `legacy_default` equals the backend
  project, and every ticket resolves to it via `resolve_project`.
- Load-bearing: the sweep writes **zero ticket events** — assert the event-file set is identical before
  and after (distinguishes this from an EDIT-per-ticket migration).
- Idempotence: a second sweep returns `ok` for both units and the tickets-branch tip SHA is unchanged.
- Conditional stamp (contrast pair): one-project → `required_capabilities` empty; two-project → exactly
  `multi-project-bridge`. The one-project half proves the stamp is genuinely conditional.
- Compat-gate safety: a two-project stamped store still passes `check_store_compat` on this binary.
- Failure path: a raising unit is recorded `failed` and does not abort the sweep or caller.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A no-mapping store gains one whose `legacy_default` equals the configured backend project;
      real-git test reads the seeded record.
- [x] Every absent-`bridge_project` ticket resolves to that default via `resolve_project`
      `[rebar:c927-0a68-4465-42a2]`; same test.
- [x] The sweep writes zero ticket events; the event-file set is identical before and after.
- [x] A second sweep returns `ok` for both units.
- [x] A second sweep leaves the tickets-branch tip SHA unchanged (compared across two sweeps).
- [x] A one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; real-git test.
- [x] A two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge`; real-git test.
- [x] A two-project stamped store still passes `check_store_compat` on this binary; test invokes the
      gate.
- [x] The two new ids are added to `REGISTRY_IDS`.
- [x] The two new ids are mapped in `_registry()`.
- [x] The two new ids are added to the `expected` literal in `test_registry_id_set_is_frozen`
      (`test_ensures.py:57`) so that test passes.
- [x] A raising unit is recorded `failed` and does not abort the sweep or caller; test monkeypatches a
      raising unit into `_registry()`.
- [x] `docs/migrations.md` documents the two ensure units and the `multi-project-bridge` token's
      compat meaning for other binaries/operators (that it gates `.store-compat.json` compatibility).
baseline.summary: Legacy-store migration: ensure units seeding the project mapping without writing ticket events

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at **800 lines against the hard 800-line cap** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which the CI module-size gate enforces with no allowlist. It is one line from red: the next change to any public library write verb fails the build. The sibling story adding two optional `create_ticket` arguments must widen two `@overload` signatures, the implementation, and their docstrings — it cannot land until this is relieved. This ticket buys that headroom by concern, not by line count.

## Approach

`_lib_writes` is the **aggregation point for every public library write**, so it grows on two axes: a new verb appends a wrapper, and an existing verb gaining an argument widens one in place. The facade split (S3/4532) cut the library **by direction** — writes vs reads vs gates vs ops — and that axis is exhausted: the write half alone carries seven concerns. The durable fix is to cut it **by concern**, per the `fsck` split (`defaceable-icy-antelope`), which took two cuts out of one 800-line file.

The seven concerns present today:

1. **Genesis** — `init_repo`, `create_ticket` (two `@overload`s + impl), `idea`.
2. **Identity & key material** — `create_identity`, `ensure_identity_for`, `create_placeholder`,
   `add_identity_key`, `revoke_identity_key`, `use_identity`, `resolve_current_identity`; all
   delegate to `rebar._commands.identity`, none touches ticket state.
3. **Status lifecycle** — `transition`, `claim`, `reopen`. The only place in the module that
   raises `ConcurrencyError`.
4. **Leaf mutations** — `_python_leaf` and its seven in-module callers `comment`, `edit_ticket`,
   `link`, `unlink`, `tag`, `untag`, `archive`.
5. **Session logs** — `append_session_log`, `start_session_log`; own `CommandError` mapping,
   NOT routed through `_python_leaf`.
6. **Store maintenance** — `compact`, `attach_commits`.
7. **Signing** — `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, delegating to `rebar.signing`.

**Two cuts**, mirroring `fsck`:

- **`_lib_mutations.py`** takes 4+5+6. Anchored on the `_python_leaf` call graph: one adapter,
  seven callers, all inside the block, nothing else in this module calling it. Stated honestly,
  5 and 6 **ride along** as the contiguous remainder of the post-genesis mutation surface, not
  because they call `_python_leaf`; the strict call-graph subset is ~130 lines and
  non-contiguous, forcing a scattered cut near the 100-line floor.
- **`_lib_identity.py`** takes 2+7 — the non-ticket, key-material surface. Identities own
  OpenSSH key lines, `use_identity`/`resolve_current_identity` select the current one, and
  signing binds a manifest to the environment key. Stated honestly, signing is ~52 lines and
  **cannot stand alone** under the 100-line floor; identity is the nearest concern by shape,
  and the module already banners signing apart from the write path.
- **`_lib_writes.py` keeps 1+3** — genesis and the status state machine.

The plan of record extracted only 4+5+6 and left `_lib_writes` at ~544 — sound at 778, but at 800 that lands **above** the 200-500 target band on a file that grew 22 lines in weeks. Hence two cuts.

Moved names are **re-exported** from `_lib_writes` with `# noqa: F401`, exactly as `fsck.py` re-exports from `fsck_scan`/`fsck_tracker_health`. That leaves `__init__.py` and `_lib_gates.py` **untouched**, so every `rebar.<name>` and `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` path survives — a smaller diff than re-pointing consumers.

**The pre-move surface, reconciled.** `_lib_writes` has 29 `def` statements = **27 distinct names** plus the two extra `@overload` stubs of `create_ticket`. `__init__.py` re-exports **all 27**, so the facade surface and the definition set coincide — no name defined here is omitted from the facade. `_python_leaf` is one of the 27: it resolves as **`rebar._python_leaf`** (its own `_python_leaf as _python_leaf` alias in `__init__.py`) *and* as `rebar._lib_writes._python_leaf`, the form `_lib_gates.py` imports. The 27 partition across the concerns above as 3 + 7 + 3 + 8 (leaf mutations, counting `_python_leaf`) + 2 + 2 + 2. Dependency direction is one-way — `_lib_writes` imports both new modules, neither imports back — so there is no cycle.

This is **behaviour-preserving**: bodies relocate byte-identically; no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` (new) — concerns 4+5+6
- `src/rebar/_lib_identity.py` (new) — concerns 2+7
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — keeps 1+3, gains the two re-export blocks

`__init__.py`, `_lib_gates.py`, and everything under `tests/` are deliberately **not** touched. The reference audit supports that: the only real-code importers of `_lib_writes` are `_lib_gates.py` (`_python_leaf`) and `__init__.py` (the 27-name re-export), and the string pass (`monkeypatch.setattr` / `getattr` / `importlib`) finds **zero** `_lib_writes` attribute references — every test patch targets the `rebar` facade or `rebar.signing`, both preserved.

`.github/complexity-baseline.json` holds **zero** entries for `_lib_writes.py`, so no moved symbol carries accepted debt and the `--lock` re-key hazard that cast `Verified -1` on the `fsck` change cannot arise. The baseline is therefore not in scope.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing with **no test file edited**. The specific risk is the **public API surface**, since all 27 names are re-exported as `rebar.<name>` and `_lib_gates` depends on `_python_leaf` at three call sites — a silently dropped re-export would still leave the suite green wherever the facade is imported lazily. Checked by name:

- every name previously importable as `rebar.<name>` still resolves after the move, asserted
  name by name against the pre-move list;
- `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` still resolves for all moved names, which is what makes
  `_lib_gates` and any `monkeypatch` target survive;
- the three modules import cleanly in **either** order, catching a cycle introduced by the
  re-export direction.

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the size oracle and needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_lib_writes.py` is at or below 450 lines; checked by
      `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_writes.py)" -le 450 ]` exiting 0.
- [x] `_lib_mutations.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`.
- [x] `_lib_identity.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_identity.py`.
- [x] The repo's size oracle still passes; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` exiting 0.
- [x] All 27 names still resolve on the facade as `rebar.<name>` — 26 public wrappers plus
      `rebar._python_leaf`; checked by a script asserting `hasattr(rebar, n)` for every name in
      the pre-move list, exiting non-zero on the first miss.
- [x] All 27 names still resolve as `rebar._lib_writes.<name>`, which is the form
      `_lib_gates.py` imports; checked by the same assert-and-exit script against
      `rebar._lib_writes`.
- [x] `src/rebar/__init__.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` are unchanged; checked by
      `git diff --exit-code HEAD~1 -- src/rebar/__init__.py src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` exiting 0.
- [x] No file under `tests/` is changed; checked by `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 -- tests/`
      producing empty output.
- [x] The three modules import cleanly in any order; checked by two fresh interpreters, one
      importing `_lib_identity`, `_lib_mutations`, `_lib_writes` in that order and one in
      reverse, both exiting 0.
- [x] `make lint` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [x] [operator-attested] The CI test selection passes; checked by
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exiting 0.
- [x] `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` reports no new entries; checked by running
      it with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=navapbc/rebar` and confirming exit 0.
baseline.summary: Split _lib_writes by concern into mutations and identity

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
When a ticket's acceptance criteria stop matching reality, the completion-verification close
gate blocks the close and there is no obvious sanctioned way forward. Agents reach for
`--force-close` (which closes WITHOUT verification, leaving an uncertified ticket) or for
`--ref <old-commit>` (which verifies against the tree where the criteria still held).

**Decision (2026-07-24): both of those are the WRONG answer for stale criteria.**

Closing against criteria that no longer describe the work leaves inaccurate state in the
ticket system. The ticket permanently claims something that is not true of the codebase — and
the ticket store is the shared, durable record other agents read. A close that "passed" by
pointing at an old commit is a close whose criteria still lie.

**The correct path is: EDIT the ticket so its criteria are accurate, re-pass the plan-review
gate, then close against the corrected criteria.** The criteria end up true, the close is
genuinely verified, and the record is accurate.

This ticket is therefore a DOCUMENTATION fix, not a feature. It was originally scoped toward
building an auditable "criterion disposition" record (moot / invalidated / superseded) with
cited evidence and provenance. That is deliberately REJECTED as overbuilt for a single bug
report: it adds a whole audited sub-system to avoid an edit that authors should be making
anyway.

## Worked example (the case that prompted this)
`86a5-9221-0037-4e38`'s criteria grepped `docs/passing-code-review.md`. A later commit
(c2bfbe217) moved that guide into the package, leaving the old path a stub — so the criteria
became false. It was closed with `--ref f90850861`, the commit where the work landed, which
PASSED verification but left the ticket asserting a file check that no longer holds. Under this
decision the right move was to edit the criteria to name
`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, re-pass plan review, and close.

## Out of scope (explicitly not building)
- An auditable criterion-disposition record (moot / invalidated-by-fix / superseded).
- An automation-owned closure path for bot-filed alert tickets.
- Any change to `--force-close`, which remains the escape hatch for a human operator's
  judgment call and correctly leaves the ticket unsigned.

## Known related gap (NOT fixed here)
Closing an epic whose plan review predates a criteria-registry change is blocked by the
plan-review close gate's `stale-regver` check, forcing a full billable re-review of an
already-executed plan. Hit twice on 2026-07-24 (86a5 and 58f2). Recorded here so it is not
lost; it needs its own ticket if it keeps costing.

## Scope
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — a short subsection under the completion close gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states that when acceptance criteria no longer match reality
      the fix is to EDIT the ticket, re-pass plan review, then close against the corrected
      criteria; verified by
      `grep -q 'criteria no longer match' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The same passage says explicitly that closing against stale criteria — whether via
      `--force-close` or by pointing `--ref` at an older commit — leaves inaccurate state in
      the ticket system and is not the remedy; verified by
      `grep -q 'inaccurate state' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The addition is SHORT (a single subsection, not a new document or a new mechanism).
- [ ] `make lint` and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier has no legitimate close path when acceptance criteria are invalidated by the fix or are auto-generated/unverifiable

baseline.description:
## Problem

AGENTS.md carries two pieces of guidance that read as contradictory when an agent is about to run a gate:

- **"Bound every background process you spawn"** says to bound helpers AT SPAWN in wall-clock
  time (`timeout 120 …`), because an unbounded busy loop reparents to PID 1 and runs for days.
- **"Gate duration expectations"** says `review-plan` takes 15-20 minutes and a
  completion-verifier close 9-11 minutes.

An agent that reads the first rule and then backgrounds a `review-plan` will put a `timeout` on it. That is the wrong move and it is expensive: the gate is a billable multi-call LLM run, so truncating it wastes the whole call, produces no verdict, and — worse — the truncation is easy to misread as a gate failure rather than a bound the agent imposed on itself.

I nearly did exactly this in the session that filed this ticket, and the operator corrected it: "Don't bound the background helper at spawn. 15-20 minutes is a guideline, not a hard limit."

## Why the two rules do not actually conflict

The bounding rule targets an **unbounded** workload — `while True: pass`, `yes > /dev/null` — which has no reason to stop and no natural end. A gate run is a **bounded** workload that simply takes a long time: it terminates on its own with a verdict. The section already says "Prefer a bounded workload to an unbounded one. A loop that counts to a fixed bound and exits cannot leak; only an infinite one can." A gate is that bounded workload. The guidance is right; it just never says so where an agent about to run a gate will look.

## Fix

State the carve-out in the bounding section itself, and make the duration line say that the figures are guidelines rather than ceilings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The bounding section explicitly excludes long-running gate/LLM operations from the
      at-spawn `timeout` rule, and says why (bounded workload, terminates on its own).
- [ ] The duration line states the figures are guidelines, not limits, and that a gate may
      legitimately exceed them.
- [ ] The carve-out names the concrete failure it prevents: a truncated gate wastes a billable
      run and reads as a gate failure.

## Verification

    grep -n "gate" AGENTS.md   # the carve-out appears in the bounding section
baseline.summary: AGENTS.md: the at-spawn bounding rule reads as applying to gate runs, which would truncate them

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split llm/prompting/prompts.py (789 LOC) along its concern boundary

baseline.description:
# Re-architect the DC transport along CAPABILITY seams, so it stops needing rescue splits

## Why now (operator-approved as a separate change)

`transport.py` is at **799/800**. The next parent-related change cannot land. This is the fourth time in one day the file has forced prose-trimming to fit: 756 → 780 (1302) → 794 → 781 (1305) → 799 (1311 + 9bb9). Each rescue bought a few lines and none addressed why growth keeps landing here.

## The diagnosis: the previous splits were REACTIVE, so they did not change where code goes

Two extractions already happened, both under cap pressure, both along whatever seam was nearest:

    retry.py        258 LOC   retry policy + error translation   (story S1 of b586)
    transitions.py  166 LOC   transition resolution + routing
    transport.py    799 LOC   EVERYTHING ELSE

`transport.py` re-exports the extracted names as a facade, so from a caller's view nothing moved. Critically, **neither split gave a NEW operation an obvious home**. A new capability still has exactly one plausible destination — the god file — so the file re-grows to the cap and the cycle repeats. b586's own lesson (S1 mechanical relocation passed plan review FIRST TRY where the combined ticket took ten rounds) was about splitting *a change*; it did not fix the module's shape.

## The insight: the right seam ALREADY EXISTS and is not being used

`_backend.py` defines the capability Protocols this class implements — `TicketTransport`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsAbsenceProbe`. Those ARE the module's natural boundaries, and the class already satisfies them. The file is organised by nothing; the contract is organised by capability. Aligning the two means every future operation has a determined home: *"which capability is this?"* answers *"which file does it go in?"*

## Proposed architecture — capability mixins composed by a thin transport

Reading the current method inventory, the clusters are clean and already disjoint:

    _base.py        ~120   shared plumbing: __init__, _client, _unwrap, _call_logged,
                           _user_attr, _paged_search  (the mixins' common substrate)
    _issues.py      ~180   create_issue, get_issue, get_issue_by_rest, update_issue,
                           delete_issue, search_issues
    _hierarchy.py   ~150   set_parent, _resolve_epic_link_field_id, get_parent_map
                           <- where 39c1 / 9bb9 / future parent work LANDS
    _links.py       ~120   set_relationship, get_issue_links, get_issuelinks_map,
                           delete_issue_link
    _comments.py    ~100   add_comment, get_comments, get_comment_map
    _people.py      ~130   _assign, set_reporter, validate_assignee_exists
    _properties.py  ~110   _put_property, set_issue_property, set_entity_property
    transport.py    ~150   the composition root: class JiraDataCenterTransport(...mixins),
                           build_client_from_settings, _jira_client_class, __all__ facade
    (retry.py, transitions.py unchanged)

Every unit lands in the **200–500 target band or just under**, and none is a sub-100-LOC fragment — the two failure modes the module-size policy names.

**`JiraDataCenterTransport` remains ONE class**, composed from mixins, so `isinstance` against the Protocols, `assert_transport_conforms`, and every caller and test keep working with no edit. That is what makes this a *mechanical relocation* rather than a redesign — and, per b586's evidence, what makes it reviewable in one pass.

## Why mixins rather than delegation or free functions

Delegation (`self._issues.create_issue(...)`) would change the call shape at every site and break Protocol conformance. Free functions taking a client would lose the shared cache (`_epic_link_field_id`) and the `_call_logged` wrapper. Mixins keep one object, one cache, one `self`, and move only the *text*. The cost is that mypy needs the shared attributes declared on a base — hence `_base.py` rather than bare mixins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] behaviour is UNCHANGED: this is a relocation. No test assertion is edited, and the full
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` suite (2105 at time of filing) passes untouched
- [x] `JiraDataCenterTransport` remains a single class satisfying the same Protocols —
      `assert_transport_conforms` and the shape contract `tests/_jira_shape_contract.py` pass unedited
- [x] the `transport.<name>` facade still resolves for every currently re-exported name, so
      `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` and friends pass UNEDITED (the reason `__all__` exists)
- [x] every resulting module is between 100 and 500 LOC; none exceeds the 800 cap
- [x] `_resolve_epic_link_field_id` has exactly ONE definition after the move — the duplication
      9bb9 deliberately avoided must not be reintroduced by the split
- [x] a short note in the package docstring states the organising principle (one module per
      capability Protocol) so the NEXT operation has a determined home rather than defaulting here
- [x] done as its own change, landing BEFORE further parent work, per the operator's approval

## Explicitly out of scope

Changing any behaviour, touching `retry.py`/`transitions.py`, or altering the Protocols themselves.
baseline.summary: Re-architect the DC transport along capability seams to stop chronic cap-driven splits

## Why
The reconcile-bridge outage (bug 8002-a92f-0999-45dd) was an *unparseable* workflow: `f2bde8d3b5` put `${{ runner.temp }}` in a job-level `env:` of `reconcile-bridge.yml` (and its canary) — a GitHub Actions startup failure (0 jobs) that stopped Jira sync for ~2 days. **CI never caught it** because `make lint` (the gate the Gerrit `Verified` vote runs) scopes actionlint to `release.yml` ONLY (`Makefile`, `RELEASE_WORKFLOW`; comment line 101: "Scoped to release.yml — NOT repo-wide"). Every other workflow — including the bridge + canary — is unvalidated, so an invalid-workflow change merges green and silently disables the workflow.

## What
Widen the CI **actionlint** coverage in `make lint` from `release.yml` to **all** `.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}`, so a parse-error / bad-context change is blocked at the `Verified` gate. Cost is zero today: `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml` already exits 0 with 0 findings (post-8002-fix). **zizmor stays scoped to `release.yml`** — widening the security audit is a separate concern, out of scope.

## Scope
- `Makefile` lint target: invoke actionlint over ALL workflows (actionlint auto-discovers
  `.github/workflows` when given no path arg), keeping `zizmor $(RELEASE_WORKFLOW)` unchanged
  and preserving the macOS-skip + pinned-binary install logic. Update the actionlint-scope
  comments (lines ~19, 97, 101, 107, 115) that say "release.yml only"/"NOT repo-wide" so they
  describe the widened actionlint scope (noting zizmor remains release.yml-scoped).
- `docs/releasing.md:129`: correct "zizmor + actionlint scoped to `release.yml`" →
  "zizmor scoped to `release.yml`; actionlint covers all workflows".
- `tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_scope.py` (new): assert the Makefile lint recipe runs
  actionlint over all workflows (not `$(RELEASE_WORKFLOW)`-only), guarding a silent re-narrow.

## How it is guarded (accurate — corrects the prior plan)
Both `gerrit-verify.yaml:303` (pre-merge Verified) and `test.yml:55` (post-merge branch CI) run `make lint`, so widening the Makefile target covers both legs automatically; a reintroduced bad workflow fails that `make lint` step. NOTE: the existing `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` only asserts both legs invoke the *string* `make lint` — it does NOT verify actionlint's scope, so it is NOT the guard for this change. The new `test_ci_actionlint_scope.py` is that guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make lint` runs actionlint against every `.github/workflows/*.yml`/`*.yaml`, not just
  `release.yml`. Proof: `sed -n '/^lint:/,/^actionlint-bin:/p' Makefile` shows the actionlint
  invocation is not restricted to `$(RELEASE_WORKFLOW)`.
- [ ] `make lint` passes on the current tree. Proof: `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] Reintroducing a `${{ runner.temp }}` job-level env into any workflow makes `make lint`
  FAIL for the runner-context reason. Proof: add the line, run `make lint` → non-zero exit
  citing `runner`, then `git checkout` to revert.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the Makefile actionlints all workflows and fails if re-scoped
  to `release.yml` only. Proof: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_scope.py -q`.
- [ ] No stale "actionlint scoped to release.yml" wording remains. Proof:
  `grep -rniE 'actionlint[^.]*scoped to .?release\.yml|actionlint[^.]*release\.yml only' Makefile docs/`
  returns nothing (accurate zizmor-scoped references may remain).
baseline.summary: Harden CI: extend actionlint coverage to ALL workflows (not just release.yml) — the gap that let the reconcile-bridge startup failure merge
