baseline.description:
## Summary

`_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:723` over-matches, so several push failures that are **not** compare-and-swap mismatches are classified as one — which the ref-lock reports as "lease lost/stolen". The same branch discards the git stderr, so a production occurrence cannot be diagnosed after the fact.

Found while root-causing bug `449f-f9bf-be90-47fe`. Filed separately because fixing it changes lock classification semantics, and (see below) the very logging gap it creates is why we cannot yet prove it has fired in production.

## The code

```python
# A rejected ``--force-with-lease`` prints "stale info" (the lease mismatch) or a
# "! [rejected]" / "cannot lock ref" line — distinct from a genuine transport
# failure ("Authentication failed", "Could not resolve host"), which we do NOT
# classify as a CAS mismatch (fail-closed).
_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS = ("stale info", "rejected", "cannot lock ref")
```

`_push_lease_cas` (`:726-747`) lowercases stderr, substring-matches those markers, and on a hit raises a synthetic `CalledProcessError(128, ["git","update-ref",ref])` that `_cas_once` reads as a CAS mismatch and `renew` (`:570-572`) converts to `LeaseLostError` -> heartbeat abort -> pass abort.

## Evidence — runtime, driving `_push_lease_cas` with real git stderr strings

```
genuine CAS mismatch (stale info)              CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- correct
server-side concurrent ref lock (NOT CAS)      CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
remote internal rejection (NOT CAS)            CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
pre-receive hook declined (NOT CAS)            CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
GitHub secondary rate limit (NOT CAS)          CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
transport: auth failed                         fail-closed                  <- correct
transport: host unresolved                     fail-closed                  <- correct
```

The strings used are real git output shapes, e.g. `error: cannot lock ref 'refs/reconciler/lock': Unable to create '...lock': File exists.` and `! [remote rejected] refs/reconciler/lock (pre-receive hook declined)`.

`"rejected"` in particular matches `! [remote rejected]`, which git emits for hook declines, quota/rate-limit rejections, and server-side errors — none of which mean the lease moved.

## The contract this violates

The module's own comment at `_ref_lock.py:719-722` promises the opposite: a genuine transport failure "we do NOT classify as a CAS mismatch (fail-closed)". ADR 0031 (`docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md:66,92`) states the same in its "Three exit-128 outcomes, one classifier" section. ADR 0031:189-190 additionally asserts "a **live** holder is never stolen (regression-tested)".

## The compounding defect — the evidence is thrown away

The classified branch (`:743-745`) raises **without logging**. The fail-closed branch below it (`:746-752`) *does* log the stderr. So the one path that makes a consequential claim ("your lease was stolen") is the one that keeps no evidence for it.

Concrete cost: `Reconcile Bridge` runs 30576272914 and 30579382013 (2026-07-30) aborted on `LeaseLostError`. Both landed ~86s into the pass, on the **second** heartbeat tick (lease 120s, interval 40s), and `renew`'s pre-CAS `read()` — which force-fetches from origin — saw the ref still at our own oid immediately before the push CAS failed. No other run logged a steal, and the workflow's `concurrency: reconcile-bridge` group serializes passes. That pattern is suspicious but **unprovable either way**, because the stderr that would settle it was discarded.

## Why this is filed, not fixed inline

Narrowing the markers changes what the lock treats as contention versus fault, on `acquire` / `release` / `renew` / `steal` alike. That is a real blast radius, and the occurrence rate is currently unmeasurable. The right order is: restore the evidence first, then narrow once a real sample exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The CAS-mismatch branch logs the git stderr (and the ref + expected oid) before
      raising, at a level that survives into CI logs — so the next occurrence is
      diagnosable. This alone is low-risk and should land first.
- [ ] On `LeaseLostError`, the holder additionally records what the remote ref
      actually was (e.g. an `ls-remote` of the lock ref plus the holder recorded in
      the lock blob), so "stolen by whom" is answerable rather than inferred.
- [ ] The marker set no longer classifies non-CAS rejections (hook decline, server
      ref-lock contention, rate limit, internal error) as a lease mismatch, with a
      unit test driving the real stderr shapes above and asserting the split. RED
      first against the current list.
- [ ] Fail-closed behaviour for genuine transport failures (auth, DNS) is unchanged
      and still covered.
- [ ] With the logging in place, state whether the two 2026-07-30 lease losses were
      genuine takeovers or spurious classifications — or, if no new occurrence has
      been captured, say so explicitly rather than closing on inference.
- [ ] File paths: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` (lines 715-752,
      and the `renew`/`LeaseLostError` path around 559-601).
baseline.summary: _PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS misclassifies non-CAS push failures as a stolen lease, and discards the stderr that would prove it

baseline.description:
## What

Running a workflow against a **non-existent target ticket id** silently creates a
phantom, CREATE-less ticket directory in the store. The workflow recorder appends
`WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP` events to the target ticket's directory **without first
verifying the ticket exists**, and the store's commit path does
`os.makedirs(ticket_dir, exist_ok=True)` — so the events land in a brand-new directory
that has no `CREATE` event. The result is a "ghost" ticket that `fsck` flags as
`MISSING_CREATE` forever (it is excluded from `list` as an error-state, so it is easy to
miss until a store-health check trips on it).

This was discovered during the 0.5.2 release dogfood: an orphan dir
`31c6-d82c-44a5-4953` held a single `_fake: true` `WORKFLOW_STEP` (a FakeRunner run,
epic a88f) and no CREATE — it was the sole `MISSING_CREATE` fsck finding in the real
store (since cleaned up).

## Reproduction Steps

1. In an initialized store, run a workflow targeting a ticket id that does **not** exist,
   e.g. library `rebar.run_workflow(<wf>, ticket_id="no-such-ticket")` (or the CLI/MCP
   `run_workflow` equivalent), with the FakeRunner so no LLM is needed.
2. `rebar fsck`.

**Expected:** the run **fails fast** with a clear "ticket … not found / has no CREATE"
error and writes **no** event files — no directory is created for a bogus id (same
contract leaf writes already enforce).
**Actual:** the run proceeds and writes `WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP` events into a new
`no-such-ticket/` directory with no CREATE; `fsck` then reports
`MISSING_CREATE: no-such-ticket — no CREATE event found` permanently.

## Root cause (citations)

- `rebar.llm.workflow.runs.run_workflow` (`runs.py:169-192`) takes `ticket_id`, calls
  `record_run_location`, and passes `target_ticket=ticket_id` to the executor **without
  validating the ticket resolves / is not a ghost**.
- `executor.TicketEventRecorder._append` (`executor.py:233`) writes each
  `WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP` via `_seam.append_event(self.ticket, …)`.
- `_seam.append_event` (`_commands/_seam.py:151-187`) composes the envelope and commits
  through `_store.event_append.write_and_push` — it does **not** call
  `_seam.require_not_ghost`, and `stage_and_commit` does `os.makedirs(ticket_dir,
  exist_ok=True)`, so a non-existent target id materializes a CREATE-less dir.
- Contrast: the leaf-write commands (comment/edit/tag/…) call
  `_seam.require_not_ghost(ticket_id, tracker)` (`_seam.py:70-83`) BEFORE appending,
  precisely to refuse writing onto a ticket that was never created. The workflow
  recorder is missing that guard.

## Proposed fix

Validate the target ticket up front, before the first `WORKFLOW_RUN` write:

- In `run_workflow` (the entry point), when `ticket_id` is provided, resolve it and run
  the ghost check (`_seam.require_id` + `_seam.require_not_ghost`, or the library
  equivalent) and fail fast with a clear error if it does not exist — BEFORE
  `record_run_location` / starting the run, so no partial state is written.
- Optionally add the same `require_not_ghost` guard in `TicketEventRecorder` (or its
  first `_append`) as defense-in-depth for any other caller that constructs a recorder
  with a bogus target.
- Do not auto-create the ticket; recording run-state onto a non-existent ticket is a
  caller error, mirroring the leaf-write contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `run_workflow` (library + CLI + MCP) against a non-existent `ticket_id` fails fast
  with a clear "ticket not found / has no CREATE" error and writes **zero** event files —
  no phantom directory is created.
- [ ] `run_workflow` against a real, existing ticket records `WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP`
  exactly as before (no regression to the happy path or to `dry_run`).
- [ ] `fsck` stays clean after running workflows (no new `MISSING_CREATE`).
- [ ] A regression test exercises the non-existent-ticket case (asserts the fail-fast
  error AND that no `<bogus-id>/` directory was created).
</content>
baseline.summary: workflow engine records WORKFLOW_RUN/STEP to a non-existent target ticket -> phantom CREATE-less dir (fsck MISSING_CREATE)

baseline.description:
## Context

S1 produces a rewritten below-horizon baseline on a shadow clone. This story builds the **publish-swap** that would replace the published `tickets` history with that baseline — as a per-backend adapter over one precondition ("replace iff the remote is unchanged since T0, else abort+retry") — plus the rollback re-convergence design. It STOPS before executing any real swap.

## Scope

- **git ref remotes** (bare/GitHub/Gerrit): swap via `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/tickets:T0` (old→new ref CAS).
- **S3 `git-remote-s3` backend (ADR 0093):** there is NO atomic ref CAS. The helper stores one git bundle per push, and the non-interactive auto-doctor (`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`) folds divergent heads by lossless 2-parent merges and NEVER discards a head — so a normally-pushed rewrite would be MERGED BACK (resurrected). Implement an EXCLUSIVE offline bundle-set replacement under the per-ref push-lock: assert the head set equals T0 (the CAS precondition), back up the bundle set to a rollback key prefix, write ONE rewritten bundle, delete the originals — bypassing the auto-doctor.
- **Rollback re-convergence (plan-review advisory #4):** design and document the path for clients that already reconciled onto the rewritten baseline (new SHAs) BEFORE a rollback — after rollback they point at a baseline graph the remote no longer has. Specify how they re-converge (e.g. treat the restored pre-reclaim ref as authoritative and force-override per the C3 stale-clone protocol).

## Out of scope

Executing a swap against any real `tickets` remote — that is a separate human go/no-go after the S3 dry-run. Everything here is validated against throwaway remotes/fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The git-ref adapter swaps via `--force-with-lease` and ABORTS (no write) when the remote moved since T0, verified on a throwaway bare remote.
- [ ] The S3 adapter performs an exclusive push-locked bundle-set replacement that asserts the T0 head set, backs up bundles to a rollback prefix, writes one rewritten bundle, deletes originals, and does NOT trigger an auto-doctor merge — verified on a fake-S3 fixture.
- [ ] A backup ref / rollback bundle prefix is captured before the first destructive step in each adapter.
- [ ] The rollback re-convergence path for already-reconciled clients is documented and covered by a reconvergence fixture (a client on the rewritten baseline is force-overridden back onto the restored ref).
- [ ] [non-codebase] No real `tickets` remote is swapped by this story.

## Portability

Both adapters use either core-git ref primitives or the store's existing S3 seam; no single-CI-provider dependence.
baseline.summary: S2: per-backend publish-swap (git-ref CAS + S3 bundle replacement) + rollback re-convergence

## Why
Make prompts contract-bearing palette citizens like scripted ops, and represent the single_turn vs agentic distinction precisely so the runner can be written without inventing protocol.

## What
- `execution_mode` is a CLOSED enum `{single_turn, agentic}` on the PROMPT front-matter (NOT the
  workflow IR; it is DISTINCT from the existing step `mode:[findings,structured,text]`, which controls
  output shaping and is unchanged). Document the relationship between the two fields.
- Runner DISPATCH protocol (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` + `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py`
  RunnerAgentStep): `agentic` = the current pydantic_ai tool-using path (unchanged). `single_turn` =
  ONE `pydantic_ai` model call with NO tools; the resolved prompt is rendered with the step's `with:`
  inputs marshaled as template variables; the model is asked for structured output validated against
  the prompt's `outputs` contract (reuse the existing structured-output stack); no tool loop.
- Surface the resolved prompt's consumes/produces/description in the inspector (reuse S0's path).
- `outputs` contract change on an override/variant is BREAKING: `validate` flags override-vs-builtin drift.

## Scope
In: enum + runner dispatch (both modes) + prompt-contract surfacing + drift flag. Out: deep/runtime validation (S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `execution_mode` is a `{single_turn,agentic}` enum on prompt front-matter, documented as distinct from step `mode`.
- [ ] `single_turn` runs exactly one model call with zero tools and returns output validated against the prompt's `outputs` contract; `agentic` is the unchanged tool-using path; both covered by tests.
- [ ] An agent step surfaces its prompt's contract in the inspector.
- [ ] `validate` flags an override/variant that changes a prompt's `outputs` contract.
- [ ] A live `single_turn` prompt produces structured output validated against its `outputs` contract.
- [ ] A prompt that LACKS `execution_mode` defaults to `agentic` (back-compat) — tested; the field is otherwise the closed `{single_turn,agentic}` enum, and S3's migration stamps it explicitly on existing prompts.
baseline.summary: Prompt contracts in IR/runner + execution_mode + inspector surfacing

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Agents file bugs outside an epic's hierarchy during epic execution and deem them out-of-scope/pre-existing even when they are defects in the epic's own deliverable; the direct-children close gate cannot see them. Event-precise backtest over 56 analyzable epic closes: 2 real at-close escapes (30a2 token-bin scaling under the token-reduction epic a492; 5b09 artifact persistence under 119f), and legitimate deferrals that must NOT block (30d3 proven-pre-existing fsck diagnostics; e6a0 filed-49s-before-close architectural follow-up, later its own epic; c8ed bug supersedes an investigation epic). 'Open linked bug' alone is not the discriminator — causation is. Incentive risk: the check keys on voluntary links; blocking legitimate deferrals teaches agents to stop linking.

## Approach
Three stages at epic close (verify-completion, epic path only):
1. DET floor: any OPEN/IN_PROGRESS bug with caused_by -> epic or any descendant = deterministic block (like the direct-children gate, completion.py ~:90). Reverse-edge read primitive, concretely: caused_by is DIRECTIONAL, stored on the BUG's own compiled deps[] with no reciprocal on the epic side — so the floor (and the stage-2 filter) enumerate open/in_progress bugs via the list-tickets read and scan each bug's deps[] for edges whose target resolves into the epic-subtree id set; the epic's own deps[] cannot supply these edges. Semantically unambiguous; 0 historical FPs; teaches: fix it, re-parent it, or dispute the link. Known-limited standalone coverage (caused_by edges are mostly auto-derived at a bug's own close, so open orphans rarely carry one) — the floor is the cheap deterministic tier; coverage of unlinked orphans comes from stages 2-3.
2. DET candidate filter for the screen: status in {open,in_progress} AND type=bug AND (created after the epic's FIRST in_progress transition OR linked any-relation/any-depth to the epic subtree, both directions). Timing-anchor read primitive: the first open->in_progress STATUS event from the epic's event directory, read WITH retired tombstones (the event_metrics._event_files idiom, include_retired=True — snapshot compaction folds old events, so the compiled state alone cannot supply it). Fallback when NO in_progress event exists at all (epic closed straight from open, or predates the workflow): anchor on the epic's creation timestamp — wider window, safe direction (over-inclusion only feeds the cheap screen). Backtested fan-out: median 3, p90 11, max 24 (descriptive, not a bound). Enforced screen ceiling: at most 32 candidates are evaluated per close — linked-to-subtree candidates first, then by created timestamp descending — and any remainder is recorded in the sidecar tally as an unevaluated-overflow count (visible to the operator, never silently dropped). Commit-relation criterion evaluated and REJECTED: 0 unique catches, 2 FPs, 58% of bug-cited SHAs already unresolvable (Gerrit rebase rot), and comment-hygiene work drains SHA citations from bug bodies going forward.
3. Haiku relevance screen: single-turn per candidate, forced choice {A: describes a defect in something this epic changed/built or behavior its AC claims; B: same subsystem, pre-existing or adjacent; C: unrelated} + one-line citation. Epic material (title/description/AC/children titles) in the system prompt for prompt caching; one warm call then parallel fan-out, reusing the warm-then-fan-out orchestration pattern of plan_review/pass1.py (extract the shared helper only if it lifts cleanly; otherwise mirror the pattern with a citation comment — no speculative refactor of pass1). MUST ride the model-class config + shared cache settings (bug afeb-bc04: hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass model-class config — do not add another instance; bug 7a79: 4096-token cache floor means small epics may not cache — acceptable, haiku is cheap uncached).
Forward A-verdicts to the completion verifier as compact evidence: title + screen citation + ticket id (~40 tokens each), cap 8 with titles-only overflow count. Forwarding path, concretely: the compact candidate block is appended INSIDE the fenced context assembled by completion_precheck (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:45, via operations.assemble_context) as a clearly-delimited 'unresolved bug candidates' section — no completion_precheck_output schema change. The verifier's native read-only show_ticket tool retrieves detail on demand — no context squeeze, no new plumbing. Screen output contract follows the overlap_verdict idiom (contracts.py:175): a prompt file with `outputs:` naming a new epic_bug_screen_verdict schema registered in contracts.py — forced choice A/B/C + one-line citation — with a normalizing validator; no hand-rolled JSON parsing. The validator's normalization DEFAULT is C (unrelated): any out-of-vocabulary, malformed, or missing verdict coerces to the non-surfacing value, mirroring overlap_verdict's safe default (related_distinct) — a garbled screen output degrades open and never fabricates an A-candidate. Verifier directive (landed as an edit to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md, where the adjudication rule lives next to the context it reads): block only a defect-in-deliverable with NO recorded disposition. A disposition SATISFIES via store-grounded signals the verifier checks through show_ticket — (a) a supersedes or duplicates link (either direction) connecting the bug to the epic subtree or to a named successor ticket, or (b) a reasoned pre-existence/deferral assertion in the bug's description or comments, judged for substance (a bare 'out of scope' does not qualify). close_class NEVER satisfies (it exists only on closed bugs; candidates are open/in_progress by construction). Fixture mapping: c8ed satisfies via (a) (carries a real supersedes link to the investigation epic); 30d3 via (b) (description proves pre-existence); e6a0 via (b) (its supersession exists ONLY as comment prose — 'Superseded by epic 4702-a55c-7aeb-445a…' — with no supersedes/duplicates link; store verified). Prose-only supersession is intentionally handled by (b), not (a): (a) is the link-shaped fast path, (b) is the substance-judged prose path, and e6a0 proves the common case where agents record supersession in prose without linking. This protects the linking incentive. Record the full screen tally (per-bug verdict + citation) in the completion sidecar for audit and live FN calibration. Screen failure degrades open (log + skip), never blocks the close by itself; the DET floor is the hard tier. --force-close remains the operator escape hatch.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/completion.py (DET floor beside the direct-children gate; candidate filter)
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py (completion_precheck: (i) the DET-floor ENFORCEMENT short-circuit, mirroring the unclosed-child gate at ~:63-74 — an open/in_progress caused_by bug returns run_verify=False + precheck_failed=True + a deterministic FAIL verdict (same shape as deterministic_child_failure), NO LLM call; (ii) append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change)
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md (adjudication directive + disposition rule)
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/epic_bug_screen.md (new prompt, `outputs: epic_bug_screen_verdict`) + the full three-file overlap_verdict registration idiom: src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (response model + normalizing validator), src/rebar/schemas/epic_bug_screen_verdict.schema.json (the JSON schema), and src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py (EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_VERDICT constant + __all__ + prompt->schema map entry, mirroring OVERLAP_VERDICT at ~:130/:318)
- new module for the screen (module-size policy: keep completion.py under cap), e.g. src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py
- src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py (screen tally recording)
- docs/plan-review-gate.md (close-gate section) + docs/llm-framework.md
- tests: unit for filter + floor + forwarding cap; regression fixtures below

## Testing
Regression set from the event-precise backtest — must-block: 30a2-4f2a, 5b09-4f3d (real at-close deliverable defects). Must-pass: 30d3-eaf0 (description proves pre-existence), e6a0-ba9b (disposition trail: filed then superseded by epic 4702), c8ed-d52d (supersedes an investigation epic — investigate/file/close is correct). Documented-unreachable, assert NOT flagged: 5e94-3841 (created 13 days post-close), 22f5-5a48 (fixed during epic, 2h before close). DET floor unit tests: open caused_by bug blocks; closed caused_by bug passes; discovered_from alone does not trip the floor. Filter unit tests: timing window uses FIRST in_progress transition; any-depth link traversal both directions. Screen: fan-out cap, warm-then-parallel ordering, degrade-open on model failure, tally lands in sidecar. All regression/unit tests are LLM-free at BOTH tiers: the screen runs through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map, AND the verifier decision path is faked/stubbed — automated must-block fixtures assert the DET-floor short-circuit (caused_by cases) or assert UP TO the forwarded candidate block (content + cap + overflow in the assembled fenced context); automated must-pass fixtures assert no floor trip and correct candidate forwarding. The REAL verifier's store-grounded disposition adjudication (30a2+5b09 block; 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass) is proven exclusively in the [operator-attested] live calibration AC — matching the repo's LLM-test idiom; the live haiku path likewise runs only in that calibration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] DET caused_by floor blocks epic close with an open/in_progress caused_by bug in the subtree, with a teaching message (fix / re-parent / dispute link).
- [x] Candidate filter implements exactly: open|in_progress bugs AND (created-after-first-in_progress OR linked-any-relation-any-depth); commit-relation is NOT implemented.
- [x] Screen rides model-class config + shared cache settings (no hand-built client), forced-choice output with citation, parallel after cache warm.
- [x] Verifier receives at most 8 compact candidates (title+citation+id) + overflow count inside the precheck-assembled fenced context (verified by a forwarding unit test on the assembled string).
- [x] Verifier adjudicates via show_ticket on demand and blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects per the store-grounded disposition rule — (a) supersedes/duplicates link, or (b) reasoned pre-existence/supersession prose; never close_class (verified by the must-block/must-pass regression fixtures).
- [x] Screen verdict rides a registered output schema + normalizing validator (overlap_verdict idiom); verifier directive text lands in completion_verifier.md.
- [x] Screen tally recorded in the completion sidecar, including the unevaluated-overflow count when the 32-candidate screen ceiling truncates; screen failure degrades open with a logged reason.
- [x] Full regression set above encoded as tests (must-block, must-pass, not-flagged).
- [x] docs/plan-review-gate.md close-gate section documents the three-stage gate (DET floor, candidate filter, screen + disposition rule) and docs/llm-framework.md references the epic_bug_screen prompt/schema.
- [x] [operator-attested] One live calibration run over the regression fixtures recorded on this ticket: (i) per-bug haiku A/B/C tally with timestamp, proving the real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path end-to-end, AND (ii) the verifier's block/pass outcome per fixture through the REAL disposition rule (live run 2026-08-03: 30a2 block; 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass; 5b09 pass — original must-block adjudication corrected against snapshot evidence of pre-close production recovery, see calibration comment); automated tests stay on the fake verdict map.
baseline.summary: Epic-close bug gate: DET caused_by floor + filtered haiku relevance screen + verifier adjudication

## Why / Summary

The inbound link differ maps Jira `Blocks` issuelinks to the INVERTED rebar relation (`blocks`<->`depends_on`). Latent since f6687adf4 (2026-06-15); UNMASKED when the outbound direction fix (6b25dbead/43d154523) corrected the write path — the two inversions had been cancelling on round-trip. Result: ~815 inbound link applies/pass are cycle-rejected by rebar's guard, and the reconciler never converges.

## Root cause (proven, LIVE-validated)

- `_diff_links_inbound` (inbound_differ.py:519-527) AND `_diff_link_removals`
  (outbound_links.py:198-203) both invert inward/outward -> relation.
- LIVE Jira ground truth: REB-458 ("0250 blocks ba7e") carries `outwardIssue: REB-461`
  with `type.outward == "blocks"`. So **outwardIssue+Blocks => rebar `blocks`;
  inwardIssue+Blocks => rebar `depends_on`.** The code does the OPPOSITE (verified by
  running the current `_diff_links_inbound` on real REB-461 JSON — it emits the
  cycle-causing inverse).

## Chronic-pattern guardrails (this fix MUST NOT repeat prior failures)

Prior link fixes (3f04, c8ed, 3b86) each corrected ONE seam and were validated by a ROUND-TRIP / self-consistency oracle that is invariant under double inversion — so the mirror stayed broken and every audit read through the inversion. This fix must:

- [ ] Fix BOTH mirror sites in lockstep (inbound add AND removal path).
- [ ] UNIFY the duplicated direction logic into ONE helper (the inward/outward->relation
      mapping is copy-pasted in inbound_differ.py and outbound_links.py; `_JIRA_LINK_TO_RELATION`
      is re-declared in acli_graph.py:53, inbound_differ.py:459). One source of truth so the
      next inversion cannot reappear on an untouched copy.
- [ ] Assert ABSOLUTE direction pinned to a captured LIVE-JIRA ground-truth fixture
      (real REB-458/461 issuelinks JSON), NOT round-trip agreement. A test that asserts
      "outbound<->inbound agree" is banned here — it passes on inverted code.

## The completeness requirement (a pure branch-swap is NOT sufficient)

Measured on 17 real tickets: a pure swap eliminates the 30 cycle-rejections but then emits ~all MIRROR-adds (the counterpart already owns the edge; ~400 spurious deps store-wide). The fix must add INVERSE-AWARE CROSS-TICKET dedup: emit an inbound link only if the edge X<->Y is absent in rebar in EITHER equivalent form (X has (blocks,Y) OR Y has (depends_on,X); and the relates_to symmetric case). `compute_inbound_mutations` already receives `local_tickets_by_id`, so the counterpart's deps are available.

- [ ] The dedup map MUST include the FULL local set (incl. archived tickets) — a residual
      mirror to archived cf10 in the live prototype was ONLY a map-exclusion artifact;
      cf10 owns the inverse edge. Verify `local_tickets_by_id` completeness or the fix
      re-emits mirrors to archived counterparts.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Local ticket A has dep `A blocks B`; both bound to Jira; outbound has (correctly)
   written REB-A outward Blocks -> REB-B.
2. Run inbound diff (or a reconcile pass).
3. Observe: inbound emits `A depends_on B` (inverted) -> rebar cycle-guard rejects it
   ("would create a cycle"). Expected: 0 inbound emits (edge already synced).

- Expected: inbound emits 0 link mutations for an already-synced link (either direction).
- Actual: inbound emits the inverted relation, cycle-rejected every pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `_diff_links_inbound` unit test on the CAPTURED LIVE REB-458 issuelinks JSON
      (outwardIssue Blocks) asserts relation == `blocks`; on REB-461 JSON (inwardIssue
      Blocks) asserts relation == `depends_on`. RED on current code. Proving command:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/ -k link_direction -q`.
- [ ] A `_diff_links_inbound` test with the counterpart owning the inverse edge asserts
      0 emitted mutations (inverse-aware dedup). RED on a pure-swap fix.
- [ ] The removal-path mirror (`_diff_link_removals`) has an equivalent absolute-direction
      test. RED on current code.
- [ ] Existing tests that encode the reversed convention (test_reconcile_roundtrip.py:522,
      test_link_dedup.py:198) are corrected to the live-Jira shape and pass.
- [ ] LIVE fix-verification (pre-land): the fixed inbound differ, run against real REB
      issuelinks for the ~815 affected pairs, emits 0 cycle-rejecting mutations and 0
      mirror-adds (prototype already validated: converges to 0 with the full local map).
- [ ] `make test` passes; no new external dependency.

## Notes
P2 of epic 58b0. Blocked-independent of P1. The observability promotion (separate child) should land AFTER this so the reconciler isn't flipped to fail-loud while this noise exists.
baseline.summary: Inbound link differ inverts blocks<->depends_on (unmasked by outbound fix); needs inverse-aware cross-ticket dedup

## Dependencies (STACKED — review with --ref HEAD)
Documents the whole identity epic shipped by ddbe/4e9d/bde5/e165/264f/2f13/3183 (all committed on this branch). Review with `--ref HEAD`.

## Context
Document the authenticated-identity model end-to-end so operators and agents can adopt it, and record the load-bearing architectural decisions as an ADR.

## What
### 1. `docs/identity.md` — the identity model end-to-end
A new operator/agent guide covering, with concrete `rebar identity …` examples:
- **The `identity` entity** (`src/rebar/…`): a gate/graph/Jira-sync-exempt ticket-type
  (like `session_log`) holding name, email, `{provider, external_id}` mappings, and
  public keys; the `.rebar/current_identity` self-identity pointer.
- **Tiers**: real identities vs. `placeholder` ghosts (inbound-minted, idempotently
  upgraded) — how to tell them apart (`is_placeholder`) and how ghosts get promoted.
- **Event attribution**: every local event carries denormalized `author`/`author_email`
  + optional `author_id`; replay back-compat.
- **Authorship attestation** (`rebar.authorship.v1`): SSHSIG over the foundation attest
  substrate; trust root = the identity's in-band keys.
- **Key rotation / era-scoping**: TOFU genesis, signed add/revoke, epoch-scoped validity
  (`identity key add|revoke`), and WHY validity is merged-log-position (epoch) not
  wall-clock.
- **Provider-neutral Jira mapping**: outbound assignee/reporter by opaque accountId, the
  `/user/search` bootstrap, and the **Modify-Reporter** permission constraint +
  documented degradation.
- **Opt-in enforcement**: `identity.require_authenticated`, the write-gate, and the
  crucial **"the merge-gate is the control; the local write-gate is UX-only"** caveat;
  replay-never-rejects; `rebar verify-authorship`.

### 2. ADR `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md`
Records the load-bearing decisions and their rationale/alternatives:
- **git-bug-style entity**: identity as a first-class event-sourced ticket entity
  (reusing the exempt-type substrate) rather than a side table.
- **Opaque-id keying**: mappings keyed on the provider's stable opaque id, NEVER email.
- **In-band TOFU**: trust-on-first-use genesis keys carried in-band on the identity,
  with a signed rotation chain (filling git-bug's IsProtected), and era-scoped validity.

### 3. Docs index
Add `docs/identity.md` (and the ADR per the ADR-dir convention) to the docs index so the docs-index completeness gate stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/identity.md` exists and covers ALL of: the identity model, tiers, opt-in
  enforcement + the merge-gate-is-the-control caveat, Jira accountId mapping +
  Modify-Reporter constraint, key-rotation/era-scoping, and the provider-neutral seam.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md` exists and records the git-bug-entity,
  opaque-id-keying, and in-band-TOFU decisions (context / decision / consequences).
- [ ] The docs-index completeness gate passes (`python scripts/check_docs_index.py
  --check` exits 0) with the new docs indexed.

## file_impact
- `docs/identity.md` (new operator/agent guide)
- `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md` (new ADR)
- the docs index file (add the new docs so check_docs_index passes)

## Context / Problem

A convergence test that RE-DERIVES what the send path does — instead of DRIVING the send path and capturing what it produced — measures the helper it named, not the convergence it claims. It stays green when the send path drifts, which is the only failure it exists to catch. This happened twice in the same module:

1. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` modelled
   the landed Jira body as `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(emitted_body)`. When
   `emersed-specific-mutt` moved the Cloud send path onto `AdfCodec.fit_outbound`, the model
   went stale and the test kept passing while live convergence was broken (bug
   `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey`, 836 unmarked duplicate comments in live Jira).
2. The first draft of that bug's own fix re-derived the send side as
   `fit_preserving_marker(_decorate_outbound_comment(body), codec.fit_outbound)` — a copy of
   the composition under test — and passed Gerrit CI with `Verified +1`. Seeding the exact
   original mistake back into `add_comment` left it GREEN (8 passed re-derived vs 2 failed
   captured, recorded in this ticket's history).

The concrete test defect is already fixed: commit `103729e90c` landed `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_comment_dedup_key_matches_send_fit.py`, whose `_send` helper captures the `--body` argument from a real `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` call with only `acli_subprocess._run_acli` stubbed. What remains is guardrail work: nothing in the repo tells the next test author which of the two shapes is correct — `make lint`, the complexity ratchet and code review all passed the re-derived version.

## Approach

Record the rule in the shared test-design standard — the guidance test authors are already directed to at oracle-design time (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:627` and `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md:214` both point at `test-design.md` in their skill directory) — rather than inventing a new document. Add a titled paragraph to `examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md` §4 "Trigger the mechanism; assert the contract" (the section that governs what an oracle may assert, and one of the sections that "apply to every test" per the scale-ceremony rule, so no section renumbering is needed): in a convergence/agreement test, the side of the assertion that represents an external effect must be CAPTURED from the real call site — drive the production entry point with only the irreducible boundary stubbed and capture what it handed the boundary — never RE-DERIVED by recomposing the helpers that call site uses today. Use the two instances above as the compact worked example (stale re-derived model vs. the landed captured `--body` oracle). Then sync the byte-identical per-skill copies exactly per `examples/agent-skills/README.md` §"The shared test-design standard" (`cp` canonical over `rebar-debug`/`rebar-implement`/`rebar-brainstorm` copies); the existing gating test `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` enforces the sync.

For the mechanical-check AC, evaluate the proposed lint (flag a test that imports the same fit/encode helper the module under test uses on both sides of an equality assertion) against the current tree and record the verdict as a comment on this ticket. Default decision: do NOT add it — 17 test files under `tests/` already import `fit_outbound`/`truncate_comment_body`/`fit_preserving_marker`, and the legitimate characterization shape (e.g. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_backend_characterization.py` deliberately pins `fit_comment` equal to the send-path fit by calling both helpers) is syntactically identical to the defective shape; whether one assertion side "represents an external effect" is intent, not syntax, so the check cannot be written without flagging the sanctioned tests. The comment records the survey numbers so the decision is auditable.

## Scope

- `examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md` — add the capture-don't-re-derive rule +
  worked example to §4 (canonical copy).
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/test-design.md` — byte-identical sync of the canonical.
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/test-design.md` — byte-identical sync.
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-brainstorm/test-design.md` — byte-identical sync.

## Testing

Documentation-only change — no new testable runtime behavior. The one existing gating test that covers this edit is the copy-sync guard: `pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` must pass (it fails if any per-skill copy diverges from the canonical file). `make lint` and `make typecheck` run as usual.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md` §4 states the rule — the external-effect
      side of a convergence assertion is captured from the real call site, not recomputed
      from the helpers that call site uses — and names both worked examples from this ticket
      (the stale `truncate_comment_body` model and the captured `--body` oracle that replaced
      it). Check: `grep -n "re-derive" examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md` hits
      inside §4 and a read of the paragraph confirms both examples.
- [x] All three consuming skill copies are byte-identical to the canonical file. Check:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` passes.
- [x] The mechanical-check evaluation is recorded as a comment on this ticket: the decision
      (add / don't add) plus the false-positive evidence (the survey counts of legitimate
      tests importing the shared fit helpers). Check: `rebar show` on this ticket shows the
      comment.
baseline.summary: Convergence tests re-derive the send path instead of driving it

Scope: `src/rebar/llm/**` excluding plan_review and workflow — the package root plus code_review, prompting, review_kernel, evals, criteria, overlap. ~218 lines leave.

Contains the repo's #1 hotspot: `runner.py` 797/800, 88 commits, 12 in five days, with a 371-line method at its C901 ceiling. Recovering ~45 lines takes headroom from 3 to ~48 — roughly 4-5 stories of runway WITHOUT another split. ADR 0056 measured prose at 40% of `run()` and 50% of its pre-call region.

A self-contradicting module: THREE sites assert Anthropic 400s when extended thinking meets a native output constraint, while `structured.py:228-238` — 210 lines below one of them, in the same file — explicitly calls that 'a stale rationale' and 'a relic'.

A dead field found via its own comment: `runner.py:94-97` says `extra_tools` 'is always None in practice'; grep confirms no caller sets it. Delete the field, not the comment.

Confirmed exemplar for the maintainer's original finding: `capabilities.py:166-198` is structurally a complete ADR (security posture for a BLOCKING gate, three numbered bounds, an explicitly accepted limitation on domain controls) and NO ADR in the 83-file corpus mentions web search in any form.

85 lines are free wins — history already citing b690, b300, 2682, 3a98, 7a79, e3cd, 8455. `providers.py:3-16` duplicates ADR 0059 §1 verbatim including its file:line citations.

capabilities.py:295-316 is a matrix that cost real AWS accounts to produce and says so; capabilities.py:269-281 carries a rejected-alternative warning sitting exactly where the next reader would reintroduce it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim
## CORRECTION (plan defect + plan-review preempt, parent 373f disposition vocabulary)

The plan's `extra_tools` premise is FALSE and would cause a regression if executed literally. `extra_tools` is LIVE, not dead: `llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:469,665` set it (the token-recovery record tool, story 2948), `llm/workflow/runs.py` threads it end-to-end, and `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py:491` asserts `captured.get("extra_tools")` ("the record tool is still wired"). The STALE unit is the `runner.py` comment claiming it "is always None in practice" — that is CORRECTED in place; the field is DO_NOT_MOVE (load-bearing). Superseding ACs below encode this and the 373f disposition rules.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one parent-373f
      label: RELOCATE (to an ADR / docs / ticket, reduced to a one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP,
      DO_NOT_MOVE, or CORRECT-IN-PLACE.
- [x] Decision rule CORRECT-vs-DELETE: a comment documenting CURRENT runtime behavior / a live
      invariant is CORRECTED in place; a comment is DELETED only when the thing it describes no
      longer exists (artifact removed, or superseded). Every DELETE records its reason
      (referenced-artifact-gone / superseded) in the commit body or a ticket comment.
- [x] `runner.py` `extra_tools` field is KEPT (DO_NOT_MOVE — load-bearing via
      completion_recovery/runs.py/tests); its stale "always None in practice" comment is
      CORRECTED to reflect the story-2948 record-tool wiring (or deleted as superseded), with the
      reason recorded. The field and its two call sites are NOT removed.
- [x] The three sites asserting an Anthropic-400 on extended-thinking + native-output-constraint
      vs `structured.py:228-238` calling that rationale "stale"/"a relic" are RECONCILED
      conservatively: determine which matches current runtime and CORRECT the stale side in
      place; if the truth is not determinable from the code without behavior risk, KEEP both
      verbatim (DO_NOT_MOVE) and file a `discovered_from` ticket rather than guess. No
      load-bearing invariant is deleted on uncertainty.
- [x] The web-search capability security-posture block (`capabilities.py:166-198` — a structurally
      complete ADR: BLOCKING-gate posture, three numbered bounds, an accepted limitation) is

baseline.description:
# Re-home the outbound parent-CLEAR live cell to the Epic Link path

`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is one of three permanent reds in the live DC suite. It clears a **sub-task's** `fields.parent`, which Data Center will not do. Its INBOUND twin was already re-homed to the Epic Link by ticket 37e7's approved ruling; the outbound twin never was.

## The three reds are three DIFFERENT problems, not one

That reframing is the finding — treating them as one platform limitation is what kept them together in red.

| cell | real blocker | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` | the cell picked a sub-task; the Epic Link path is reachable | **this ticket** |
| `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | rebar must do the write and DC accepts-and-ignores it — unreachable, and its coverage is already green elsewhere | `xfail(strict=True)` |
| `test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | the DC-side reparent is only SETUP; the subject is rebar's inbound pass | re-target to adoption |

The outbound-set behaviour rebar can actually deliver is already pinned green by `test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored`, so `xfail(strict=True)` there loses no coverage — and an xpass would FAIL the suite, a stronger signal than today's permanent red.

## Why the Epic Link clear is believed reachable (source-verified)

 * `_resolve_local_parent` returns `(True, None)` for a locally-detached ticket regardless of
   parent type — the epic-only guard suppresses *sets*, not *clears*.
 * `fetcher.merge_parent_map` overlays `client.get_parent_map()`, and 9bb9 taught DC's
   `get_parent_map` to fall back to the Epic Link — so a standard issue under an epic yields a
   truthy `remote_parent_id` and the clear is observable outbound.
 * `set_parent` for a non-sub-task writes `{epic_link_field_id: None}` — the same path as a set.

Two gates the cell must be built around, or it will fail for the wrong reason:
 1. `should_propagate_removal` requires the ref to be MANAGED — so the cell must have **rebar**
    set the Epic Link in a priming pass, not create it Jira-side.
 2. `_peer_removed_the_parent` (339a) short-circuits on a truthy remote parent, so it does not
    interfere.

## THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN

**Whether `{epic_link_field_id: None}` actually clears on DC 8.17.1 is UNTESTED.** The capability map measured that WRITING the Epic Link works (req-0040/0041); clearing it was never probed. Do not write the cell before this is answered — that is exactly how changes 1276, 1288 and 1302 each shipped merged, mutation-proven and wrong.

A targeted, deterministic probe is added by this ticket: `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` + `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml`. It is NOT the capability map — no LLM, no agent, four predetermined REST calls — so it settles the question without re-running or churning the map's committed answers.

## A related gap this surfaced

`set_parent`'s **non-sub-task branch has no read-back verification**, unlike the sub-task branch that 1a9f added. If the Epic Link clear silently no-ops, that is invisible today. Worth closing regardless of the probe's answer, though the probe's result decides whether adding it makes `set_parent` start refusing epic-parent clears (correct, and the same move 1a9f made).

## Ruled out, with evidence — do not re-investigate

 * **screen provisioning for `parent`** — REFUTED. `OrderableField` is defined as "fields able to
   be placed on screens" and Jira Server 8.x has NO Parent implementation of it; `parent` is
   absent from `/rest/api/2/field` (JRASERVER-47377, closed unfixed). It cannot be screened. This
   does not contradict the map's screen-gating finding, which was about a field that EXISTS.
 * **sub-task ⟷ standard conversion via REST** — no such endpoint in the 8.17.0 reference
   (JRASERVER-27893 open since 2012; the adjacent issuetype-change request closed Won't Do).
 * **bulk edit / `/issue/move` / `overrideScreenSecurity`** — none exist on DC 8.x
   (`/subtask/move` is sibling REORDERING); `overrideScreenSecurity` occurs zero times in the
   8.17/8.22/9.4/9.12 references — Cloud-and-app-only.
 * **delete-and-recreate** — rejected: new key, lost history, and a broken binding.

## STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-04) — the blocking unknown is ANSWERED and one AC is SUPERSEDED

**The probe is no longer needed to proceed.** Two cells that PASSED in live run `30951453979` already answer whether `{epic_link: null}` clears on DC: `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link` (whose final assertion is `set_parent(child, None)` then `assert not cleared`) and `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`. **It clears.** So AC2 is the live branch and AC3's "if it does NOT clear" branch is moot. Recorded in `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` with the run id.

**AC4 (xfail) is SUPERSEDED by the operator ruling on [rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223] (2026-08-04):** "resolve the failures; do NOT delete, skip, or `xfail` any cell." `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` is therefore NOT xfailed — it is re-homed under 9f26 to the claim nothing currently asserts (an unrepresentable parent must produce a durable bridge alert rather than being silently dropped). That is a stronger outcome than an xfail: a permanent red becomes a green assertion about behaviour rebar owns.

**Scope of this ticket is now test-only:** re-home `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` to the Epic Link clear, priming the parent through a LOCAL rebar edit so `should_propagate_removal` sees a MANAGED ref. The `set_parent` non-sub-task read-back gap this ticket correctly identified is real but is NOT currently masking anything (the Epic Link round-trips green in both directions), so it is left out to keep the diff narrow — a recorded decision, not an oversight.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the probe runs in CI and its verdict on `{epic_link: null}` is recorded here
- [x] if it CLEARS: `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is re-homed to the Epic Link path
      (rebar-set parent in a priming pass) and is GREEN on a live run, with the run id recorded
- [x] if it does NOT clear: that is a product defect — file it, and add the missing read-back to
      `set_parent`'s non-sub-task branch so it stops reporting a no-op as success
- [x] `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` is `xfail(strict=True)` with a reason citing
      the measured platform limitation
- [x] no cell is weakened to pass — no skips, no deleted assertions, no round-trip loosened

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Replaying a candidate change tells you *what would change*, not whether it is *better*. The store already carries outcome signals needing no LLM/human labeling: revise→re-review pairs, verdict flips on byte-identical material (the reviewer-noise floor), bug closes with `close_class=plan_defect`, `caused_by` links, PASS-then-completion-FAIL tickets, reopens.

`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py` (celestine-treasonous-ewe, closed): `build_corpus(store_roots, *, cache_dir) -> manifest` recovers `plan_review_result_v1/v2` sidecars, verifies material, writes `cache_dir / f"{manifest['content_hash']}.jsonl"` — one JSON line per VERIFIED row ONLY, fields `store, ticket_id, review_event_ts, review_event_uuid, schema, verdict, ticket_type, description, file_impact, file_impact_scope, no_file_impact_reason, children, material_fingerprint, verified, generation, reconstructed, ran_model`. No per-ticket rows in the manifest itself.

`corpus._enumerate_event_blobs` applies NO content-type filter — it returns EVERY event blob, deduped by `(ticket_id, uuid)`. `_CONTENT_TYPES` filtering happens one layer up, in `corpus._load_ticket_events`. A caller wanting other kinds (STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT) filters `_enumerate_event_blobs`'s own output by `kind`.

Every event `ts` is a `time.time_ns()` NANOSECOND epoch value; convert with `datetime.fromtimestamp(ts / 1e9, tz=timezone.utc)`, matching `rebar_reconciler/conflict_bug_filing.py:119`.

STATUS events carry `data = {status, current_status, ...}`. `clean_close`'s timestamp is the `ts` of the MOST RECENT STATUS event with `data["status"] == "closed"`. A `COMPLETION_VERDICT` event's TYPE covers BOTH outcomes — `data.schema == "completion_verifier_fail_v1"` marks FAIL, `"completion_verifier_pass_v1"` marks PASS — filter on `data.schema`, not the event kind.

Each surfaced finding carries `criteria: list[str]` (may name >1 criterion, e.g. `["E2","T8"]`).

`config.tracker_dir_override()` reads `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`, winning verbatim over any config. `caused_by` is an OUTBOUND edge on the SOURCE (bug) pointing at TARGET (culprit); inbound only on the culprit (`include_inbound=True`).

`mine_outcome_corpus.py` (docs-tree, not importable from `src/`) defines `reopen_count`/`force_close`/`completion_verifier_fail_count` as pure functions over a per-ticket event dict.

## Approach

Build `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py`:

- **Corpus identity + ticket population**: `corpus.build_corpus(store_roots, cache_dir=...)`; `manifest["content_hash"]` is the hash labels key to. Read `cache_dir / f"{content_hash}.jsonl"` for `(store, ticket_id)` pairs, `review_event_ts`/`review_event_uuid`/`verdict`/`material_fingerprint` — the single driver for every label; unverified rows never enter labels. Refuses (raises, naming both hashes) on a hash mismatch against a supplied `labels-<hash>.jsonl`.
- **Finding-level source (verified-only)**: per cache row's `review_event_uuid`, re-read that SAME `REVIEW_RESULT` blob's `data` via `corpus._enumerate_event_blobs` + `_batch_cat` (matched by uuid). Filter `findings` to `sidecar.surfaced_findings(data)` before any `norm_id` join.
- **Ticket-level event source (multi-store, env override)**: per `store_name, tracker_git_root` in `store_roots`, temporarily set `os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = tracker_git_root` (restored `finally`) around `show_ticket(ticket_id, include_inbound=True)`. `reopen_count`/`force_close`/`completion_verifier_fail_count` REIMPLEMENTED in `labels.py` (mirroring the miner), fed by `corpus._enumerate_event_blobs` filtered to `kind in {STATUS, COMMENT, COMPLETION_VERDICT}` then `_batch_cat`; `completion_verifier_fail_count` further filters to `data.schema == "completion_verifier_fail_v1"`. Same STATUS events supply `clean_close`'s timestamp.
- **Ticket-level labels**: `escaped_defect(X)` = (a) `X.close_class == "plan_defect"` OR (b) `X.inbound_deps` has `relation == "caused_by"`. `completion_failed_after_pass(X)`: a PASS cache row at ns-ts T AND a `completion_verifier_fail_v1` event with `ts > T`. `reopened` (`reopen_count > 0`); `escape_signals(X) = escaped_defect OR completion_failed_after_pass OR reopened OR force_close`; `clean_close` = closed AND NOT escape_signals AND `(now - datetime.fromtimestamp(latest_close_ts / 1e9, tz=timezone.utc)).days >= CLEAN_CLOSE_MIN_DAYS` (constant, default 7). Each label carries source event id(s).
- **Finding-level labels**: per ticket's cache rows ordered by ts, each CONSECUTIVE pair (k, k+1) with differing `material_fingerprint`. Finding `f` in k: `f.norm_id` also in k+1 → `persisted`; absent from k+1 → `resolved_by_author`. New in k+1 → neither. `noise_flip` only over IDENTICAL-material pairs, comparing `verdict`.
- **Noise floor**: (a) verdict flip rate; (b) per-criterion churn — a finding's `norm_id` is a member of EVERY criterion in its `criteria` list; `churn(c) = 1 - jaccard(S_k(c), S_{k+1}(c))`; published figure = mean over every criterion observed, plus per-criterion breakdown. (c) per-question Pass-2 agreement — `verification = {"binary": {...}, "severity_attributes": {...}}`; flatten as `"binary.<key>"`/`"severity_attributes.<key>"`; compare keys present in both findings; agreement = matches/total, pooled, with comparison count.
- Output `labels-<content_hash>.jsonl` + Markdown report, joined to `content_hash`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py` (new)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/labels-report-<date>.md` (new)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_labels.py` (new)

## Testing

Unit: five-ticket synthetic corpus exercising each label — a bug via `close_class`, a separate origin via `inbound_deps`; `completion_failed_after_pass` true only for a `completion_verifier_fail_v1` event after a PASS (not for `pass_v1`); `clean_close` false when any escape signal fires, using the LATEST close STATUS ts converted from ns; finding present-then-absent → `resolved_by_author`; present-in-both → `persisted`; new → neither; a two-criteria finding contributes to both churn sets; identical-material flip via `noise_flip` only; a permanently-dropped finding excluded from the join; per-question agreement over nested `verification` (one match, one mismatch → 0.5); an UNVERIFIED row never reaches a label. Empty corpus → empty report. Stale-hash file refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every review/finding in the verified corpus carries the labels above, with source event ids. Evidence: `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_labels.py` (75/75, mutation-verified) proves every label-derivation rule; `build_labels` was additionally run end-to-end against a real 40-ticket subset of the "rebar" tracker (11 verified rows / 9 tickets), producing a committed `labels-b3784f0609e3d7f7dcd5a20f2d83081bc37c31dfddd62e2bf8f0baeb3eed8ad6.jsonl` + report -- this caught a real production-data bug (explicit-null `verification`, fixed with a regression test). A full-corpus (~6400-ticket) run is DEFERRED follow-up: each ticket needs its own `show_ticket` call, too slow at that scale under the store's current activity (confirmed per-call cost, not lock contention, since an isolated local clone made no difference).
- [x] The noise floor is published with the identical-material pair count. Evidence: unit tests for each metric, plus the committed subset report's pair-label section (2 differing-material pairs in the 40-ticket subset; `noise_flip` itself is unit-tested directly since the subset had no identical-material pair).
- [x] Labels are keyed to `corpus.build_corpus(...)["content_hash"]`; the loader raises on a stale hash. Evidence: `test_load_labels_refuses_a_stale_hash`; the committed report's filename embeds its content hash.
- [x] No LLM calls. Evidence: all tests and the real subset run used zero provider credentials; the module makes no LLM/network calls anywhere.

## The defect

`tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone` fails against a real, installed jscpd. The adapter reports `duplication["clones"] == 0` for a fixture that contains two byte-identical files, so the assertion `result.duplication["clones"] >= 1` fails.

    assert 0 >= 1

## Why this is being filed now

This failure was one of the two used as evidence in bug a5f5 (`make worktree` provisioned its venv from ambient python3, so worktrees ran Python 3.14 while CI tested 3.11-3.13). a5f5's acceptance criteria required re-checking both on an in-matrix interpreter, because every prior observation of them had been on an untested Python and nobody could say which were artifacts.

Re-checked on Python 3.12.13 as part of landing a5f5:

- `tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`
  -> PASSES. It was an artifact of the untested interpreter, and needs no ticket.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone`
  -> STILL FAILS. So it is genuinely unrelated to the Python revision.

## Environment

    jscpd     5.0.14  (/opt/homebrew/bin/jscpd)
    python    3.12.13 (in-matrix)

The test is a live-tool test: it is skipped when jscpd is absent, so CI (which does not install the Node toolchain) never runs it. It only fires for developers who have jscpd on PATH for `rebar metrics`, which is why it has gone unattributed.

## Likely direction, not yet confirmed

jscpd 5.x is a major version ahead of whatever the adapter was written against; the most likely cause is a changed report shape or changed default thresholds (`--min-lines` / `--min-tokens`) so the fixture's clone falls under the detection floor. Confirm before fixing — this ticket records the observation, not a diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Root cause established: adapter contract vs jscpd 5.x behaviour, with evidence.
- [x] `test_live_clone` passes against the installed jscpd, or the adapter's supported jscpd
      range is declared and the test skips outside it (loudly, naming the range) rather than
      failing.
- [x] `rebar metrics` duplication is confirmed to report real clones on jscpd 5.x, not silently
      zero — a metric that reads 0 when it means "I cannot tell" is worse than `unavailable`.

## Provenance

Discovered from a5f5 while satisfying its "re-check on an in-matrix interpreter" criterion.
baseline.summary: jscpd 5.x live-clone detection returns 0 clones, so test_live_clone fails against a real jscpd

## Concept
Add a first-class research ticket type for durable, lifecycle-managed investigation work that does not modify the codebase and should not pay software-delivery gate costs. It fills the gap between ephemeral/session-oriented session_log records and implementation-bearing task, story, bug, and epic tickets.

## Proposed semantics
- research tickets use the ordinary open -> in_progress -> closed lifecycle.
- research tickets cannot be created in or transitioned to idea status.
- plan review is inapplicable and cannot be invoked for research tickets.
- completion verification is inapplicable and cannot be invoked for research tickets.
- file impact and verification-command metadata cannot be set on research tickets.
- research tickets cannot have a parent and cannot be made a child through parent-setting or child hierarchy links.
- research tickets may use non-hierarchical links to other tickets so evidence, discoveries, and resulting implementation work remain connected.
- research tickets appear in list/search/show operations and normal direct-id lookups.
- research tickets are excluded from ready and next-batch because those commands enumerate executable implementation work.
- research tickets retain comments, assignee/claim state, tags, priority, authorship, bridge-safe identity, and the normal audit history needed for collaborative investigation.

## Safety boundary
This type is not a gate bypass for code-changing work. The product should define and enforce that a research ticket cannot declare file impact, carry implementation completion evidence, or serve as the claimed work item for a code commit. Research findings that authorize repository changes must create or promote separate ordinary gated tickets and link them to the research ticket.

## Design work before promotion
- Define the canonical event/schema representation, public Python type, CLI/MCP surface, reducer validation, transition matrix, and compatibility behavior for older readers.
- Decide which existing non-hierarchical relations are allowed and reject every hierarchy-forming path consistently, including inverse link forms.
- Define whether claim is allowed directly from open and how default assignee/session ownership works.
- Define search/list filters and bridge/Jira representation without letting reconciled Jira hierarchy imply a local parent.
- Add cross-surface behavioral tests proving plan-review, completion-verifier, file-impact, parent, ready, and next-batch prohibitions and proving normal lifecycle/search/link behavior.
- Document when to use research versus session_log versus task/story/bug/epic.

## Intended outcome
Investigations such as architecture research, historical CI-log analysis, OSS prior-art studies, and empirical probes get a durable collaborative work record with an honest lifecycle, while implementation tickets retain the full plan-review, file-impact, and completion-verification discipline.
baseline.summary: Add a lightweight research ticket type

The AWS review-bot holds a persistent tickets clone that a redeploy does not refresh, and it writes on every Gerrit vote. Give it diverged-detection, and fix the deploy path so the change actually reaches the box. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Its clone lives on an EBS-backed external volume (`docker-compose.yml:127`, `external: true`) cloned once behind `if [ ! -d .git ]` (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:117`, itself nested inside `if [ -n "${REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT:-}" ]` at `:112`), so a redeploy does **not** converge it. It writes a `code_review` ticket and auto-pushes on **every** vote (`voter.py:260-343`, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`) — event-driven, not scheduled, so pausing AWS *schedules* does not stop it.

This is **new code, not a predicate fix**: `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` currently does only `git config user.email/user.name` (`:52-53`) then `run_ensures` (`:59`) — no fetch, no reset, no ancestry test. Note its invocation at `Dockerfile.reviewbot:125` sits OUTSIDE the PAT block, so new logic there runs even with the PAT unset.

**Chicken-and-egg:** `autodeploy.sh:186`'s rsync — which is what refreshes the box's copy of these scripts — runs only when `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS` changed (`:55` = `src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot pyproject.toml infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`). A commit touching only these two scripts would never reach the box. So this must land in the **same change** as an `src/rebar/` edit (A6-0a qualifies).

## Approach
1. Add diverged-detection to `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`: if `HEAD` is not an ancestor of
   `origin/tickets` and not strictly ahead, `fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets`. Safe because the
   bot never holds unpushed work (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`).
2. Add `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` to `autodeploy.sh:55`'s `BOT_PATHS`, so future
   edits to it deploy at all.

Vote safety is already guaranteed and must not regress: `voter.py:698` records the vote **before** `emit_code_review_artifact` (`:735`), and that call is wrapped in `except Exception` -> `_artifact_emit_error` + `logger.warning` + `return None` (`:368-371`) — documented as "the vote is already cast, so this never fails the review". A store failure cannot wedge the `LLM-Review` gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a clone diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared tip), the script re-converges it to
      `origin/tickets` and leaves no local commits. Tier: **shell integration** against two real
      temporary repos.
- [ ] Given an up-to-date or merely-behind clone, the script makes **no** destructive change
      (negative control). Tier: **shell integration**.
- [ ] With `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` unset, the new logic still executes (it sits outside the PAT
      block). Tier: **shell integration** with the env var unset.
- [ ] `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` appears in `autodeploy.sh`'s `BOT_PATHS`. Verify:
      grep assertion in a test.
- [ ] A rebar store write failure inside the bot still leaves the vote cast (regression guard). Tier:
      **unit** on `emit_code_review_artifact` with an injected store failure.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0a (and must ship in the same change as an `src/rebar/` edit).
baseline.summary: A6-0b: make the review-bot's tickets clone self-converge, and fix its deploy trigger

## Summary
A vanished git object poisons the SHARED index and CASCADES: `git commit` (whole-index) fails `error: invalid object <sha> for '<path>'` / `error: Error building trees`, and because the failed commit leaves the poisoned entry staged, EVERY subsequent write's commit fails identically until the index is reset. This is the residual behind the enrich-prune concurrency flake after Mode A (4f8d) and Mode B (ac26) were fixed (CI: `lost=28..50 swallowed_write_raises=28..50`, all on ONE object). Genesis: a loose object that vanishes between `git add` and `git commit` (a background gc repack, or a partial/interrupted object write under CI FS/memory pressure).

## Reproduction Steps
1. Baseline commit so HEAD exists. 2. Stage an event file, then delete its loose object
   (`objects/xx/rest`) — a vanished object. 3. A NEW rebar write's whole-index commit builds a
   tree from the index and fails `invalid object … Error building trees`; the next write
   fails identically (proven cascade — `tests/.../test_event_append_transient_retry.py`).

**Expected:** a locked write self-heals and no write is lost. **Actual (pre-fix):** the poison persists (the per-path `_unstage` clears the CURRENT write's path, never the earlier poison's) and wedges every later commit.

## Root Cause
`git write-tree` verifies each index blob EXISTS; a missing one fails the tree build. The failed commit leaves the poisoned entry in the index. rebar's existing recovery only unstages the current write's path, so a cross-path poison is never cleared → cascade.

## Fix
`event_append._recover_from_invalid_object`: on the `invalid object`/`Error building trees` signature, `git read-tree HEAD` (reset the WHOLE index to HEAD — drops the poison regardless of path; worktree untouched), re-`git add` this write's file(s) — regenerating a missing object from the intact worktree file — and retry the commit. Non-destructive on a false positive; bounded (one recovery attempt); emits a WARNING naming any orphaned worktree path. Verified accepted pattern (git-annex regenerates its index identically); vetted by an adversarial code review (APPROVE) and a prior-art sweep (acceptable-with-caveats, all met).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A cross-path vanished-object poison self-heals instead of cascading; a subsequent write
  also succeeds (RED test `test_cross_path_poisoned_index_self_heals`, mutation-checked).
- [ ] A write whose OWN object vanished regenerates it and commits
  (`test_own_vanished_object_is_regenerated`).
- [ ] The heal logs a WARNING naming any orphaned worktree path (observability guardrail).
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` pass; the enrich-prune concurrency test passes; no
  existing store test weakened.
baseline.summary: Vanished git object poisons the shared index and cascades all writes (enrich-prune Mode D)

## Summary

When a completion-verified close commits but fails to obtain its `completion-verifier` attestation, the CLI's **default (text) output** says nothing about it. It prints only:

    transitioned <id>: in_progress -> closed; unblocked: none

Split out of `rookie-fickle-hydra` (3e21-4c5b-3e0d-4e23) so that bug can stay scoped to its proven root cause (a symbolic `--ref` resolved twice). This is the separate REPORTING limb.

## What already exists — this is a narrow residual, not the whole gap

Bug `silvern-dewy-damselfly` (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843) already delivered the machine-readable marker. `completion_signature {signed, cause, error}` — with the closed cause vocabulary `signed` / `material_drifted` / `sign_failed` / `force_bypassed` — reaches:

- the library: `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:385-386` (`rebar.transition()` return)
- the CLI JSON branch: `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:637-638` (`--output json`)
- MCP `transition_ticket`, which forwards the library result

and a warning is written to stderr on both failure branches (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:363-372` for drift, `:383-392` for a signing error).

What is NOT covered is the **default text branch**, `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:641-647`, which never inspects `result["completion_signature"]`. A human — or an agent reading the success line and not stderr — sees an unqualified success.

## Why it still matters

The attestation is the durable evidence that the close was earned. Its absence propagates: `src/rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py:185-205` classifies a closed-but-uncertified child as `uncertified` with the detail "its subtree is unattested, so the parent closes WITHOUT certification" — so one silently unsigned child close costs its parent story/epic its certification too. A reader who never learns the first close was unsigned cannot connect the two.

## Explicitly NOT in scope: a nonzero exit code

`f4cf` recorded this decision and it stands. `docs/exit-codes.md` declares the contract frozen as of the 2026-06-09 window, pinned by `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`, with the table at `:158` fixing `transition` at 0/1/10 — a new code is additive-only in a future window, a release decision. Reusing exit 1 would be actively harmful: agents read 1 as "the transition failed" and re-run it, which then exits 10 (already closed), trading a silent loss for a louder wrong answer. This ticket is about the text output only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] When `completion_signature` is present and `cause != "signed"`, the default text output
      names the outcome on the same success line (or an adjacent line) — the ticket closed AND
      whether it carries an attestation — verified by a test per cause in the vocabulary.
- [x] A close that signs normally, a non-close transition, and `idea -> closed` (which carries no
      `completion_signature` key at all) print exactly what they print today — verified by tests.
- [x] Exit code remains 0 on every path — verified by a test pinning that decision.
- [x] `--output json` output is unchanged.

## Found by

Root-cause investigation of `rookie-fickle-hydra`. That bug's own AC3 ("A close that cannot obtain an attestation says so in its output") is already met for library / JSON / MCP consumers and unmet only here, which is why the residual is split out rather than folded in.
baseline.summary: A close that lands without its completion attestation is silent in the CLI's default text output

# `read_file` silently reads to EOF when `line_end < line_start`

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a] and deliberately left out of that fix's scope to keep its review surface to one function.

`read_file` (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`) computes `hi = line_end if line_end and line_end >= lo else len(lines)`. An INVERTED range — `line_end` below `line_start` — therefore falls back to "read to EOF" (capped at `_READ_MAX_LINES`) rather than reporting that the request was malformed. The agent asked for a 30-line window and silently received a 259-line one.

Observed live: the looping verifier in bf31 issued `read_file(<path>, line_start=115, line_end=30)` **31 times**, each returning the same 11,000-char blob. The malformed range was not the cause of that loop, but it is the same class of defect as the one bf31 fixed — a tool answering a request it did not actually perform, with no signal that it substituted something else.

Note the deliberate, documented case that must be preserved: `line_end=0` means "read to EOF" and is part of the tool's contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `read_file` with `line_end < line_start` (and `line_end != 0`) returns an explicit `Error: ...`
      naming the malformed range, instead of silently reading to EOF
- [x] `line_end == 0` still means "read to EOF, capped" — the documented behaviour is unchanged
      (regression pinned)
- [x] a normal `line_start <= line_end` window is unchanged
- [x] the docstring states the malformed-range behaviour, since Pydantic AI passes it to the agent
      as the tool contract (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:46`)
baseline.summary: read_file silently reads to EOF when line_end < line_start instead of reporting the malformed range
