baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar review-plan --source local` is documented — in the CLI's own generated help — as "local: read the in-place checkout (dirty allowed, **never signs**)". It signs.

A local-source PASS mints a fully CERTIFIED, CLAIM-VALID plan-review attestation. Probed on origin/main (20ae67c61):

    signed=True source='local' verified_at_sha=None
    claim_gate_check -> ok=True reason='certified plan-review attestation'
    rebar claim       -> succeeds, ticket goes in_progress

That is a gate-integrity hole, not just a help-text drift. `--source local` reads the IN-PLACE working tree, uncommitted edits included. So an agent can review a plan against code that exists only in its dirty worktree and earn a claim attestation that binds `verified_at_sha=None` — no committed SHA at all. The attested-snapshot discipline the claim gate is built on (review a snapshot pinned at a ref, bind that SHA, re-hash the SAME basis at claim time) is bypassed.

Discovered while writing boundary regression tests for epic 58f2-b6ed-363e-4608 (uninformed-aspiring-rhino), whose AC5 asserts "unattested local-source results remain unsigned". They do not. Either the AC is wrong or the code is; this ticket resolves which.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Enable the claim gate: `[verify] require_plan_review_for_claim = true`.
2. Create an open, non-exempt ticket with a reviewable plan.
3. `rebar review-plan <id> --source local` (or library `review_plan(..., source="local")`)
   with a runner that yields a clean PASS.
4. Inspect the verdict: `signature.signed` is `True`, `verified_at_sha` is `None`.
5. `rebar claim <id>` — succeeds.

## Expected Behavior
One of the two, decided deliberately:
- **(A) Honor the documented contract:** a `source=local` review NEVER signs. It returns a
  PASS with `signature.signed=False` and a machine-readable unsigned reason naming the
  local-source policy. The claim gate stays unsatisfied.
- **(B) Change the contract:** local-source signing is intentional; then the help, the
  guides, and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` must say so, and the attestation must still bind a
  committed SHA rather than `None`.

(A) is the recommendation: the whole point of `verified_at_sha` is that the claim gate re-hashes the same committed basis, which a dirty worktree cannot provide.

## Actual Behavior
`source=local` signs a certified attestation with `verified_at_sha=None`, and the claim gate accepts it.

## Approach
1. Add the local-source guard at the shared sign-on-PASS finalization seam in
   `rebar.llm.plan_review` (NOT at each caller), alongside the existing non-PASS/degraded
   refusals in `attest.sign_plan_review`.
2. Surface a machine-readable unsigned reason so a caller can tell "policy declined to sign"
   from "signing failed".
3. Pin it with a table-driven never-sign test covering BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / degraded /
   local-source / explicit `sign=False`.
4. Audit whether any existing attestation in the store was minted from a local-source review
   (`verified_at_sha is None` is the tell) and decide whether to invalidate.

Rejected: fixing only the help text — that documents a gate bypass instead of closing it.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `source=local` PASS returns `signature.signed is False` and a machine-readable
      unsigned reason naming the local-source policy; an interface test asserts both.
- [ ] After a `source=local` PASS, `attest.claim_gate_check(...)` reports `ok=False` and a
      subsequent `rebar claim` is BLOCKED (exit 1) with the ticket still `open`.
- [ ] `test_pass_verdict_carries_a_passing_signature` (which today reviews with
      `source="local"` and asserts a signature) is updated to use the attested source, so the
      suite no longer encodes the bypass as expected behavior.
- [ ] A table-driven never-sign test covers BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, local-source, and
      explicit `sign=False`.
- [ ] No signed attestation can carry `verified_at_sha=None`; a test asserts the invariant.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states the local-source never-signs rule.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: review-plan --source local mints a claim-valid attestation despite documented 'never signs'

baseline.description:
Move GET-rotation stamps into `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` so a later rollout step can remove them from the large sort-ordered `bindings.json`. A2-1 is the compatibility half: new binaries write both formats and read `max(new, legacy)`; A2-2 removes the legacy write after its observable rollout gate. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** contains the measured facts.

## Why

`set_last_get` stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit` (default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly 20 entries change per affected pass. The full A2 saving is realized only after A2-2 removes this scattered legacy write. During A2-1, dual-write is intentional compatibility cost: an old binary cannot read the sidecar, so it must still observe progress made by new binaries.

## Approach — compatibility first

Write every new stamp to the sidecar and the legacy inline field, and read the chronological `max(sidecar, legacy)`. Under mixed versions an old binary may advance only the inline field; `max()` ensures a following new binary does not use stale sidecar state. Conversely, dual-write ensures an old binary following a new one sees the new progress. Values are fixed-width zero-padded timestamps, so lexicographic `max()` is chronological.

Load legacy-only rotation state in memory and persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`. This covers all production save paths: end-of-pass persistence, the write-ahead saves in `dispatch_one.py`, and the recovery/retirement saves in `binding_store.py`. Saving unchanged canonical state must remain byte-stable. `reconcile-check` runs with `persist=False`, never reaches save, and must not create the sidecar.

Add `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE`, characterize its path, and include it in both `reconcile_helpers.py` explicit staging and basename membership checks. This is required because local reconciliation does not use `git add -A`. The existing `.gitattributes` glob covers the new file. Update the `_store/push.py` docstring that enumerates regenerable files.

`outbound_differ.py` is at the locked 800-line cap. Move the existing last-GET and best-effort bookkeeping wrappers across the new rotation seam so the module remains at or below the cap.

## Rollback

Reverting A2-1 is safe: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but every new-binary pass also advanced the inline legacy field. The orphaned sidecar is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Tier: integration in a real temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances identical selected-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Tier: integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Tier: real-git integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] Rotation order after an interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence matches the all-new sequence. Tier: integration; it must fail for either sidecar-first lookup or missing dual-write.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store yields identical rotation order. Tier: unit.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Tier: unit.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Tier: CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Tier: CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Tier: git-adapter characterization.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The `_store/push.py` regenerable-files documentation includes `get_rotation.json`. Tier: characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verify with the repository module-size gate.

## Files

`binding_store.py`, new `get_rotation.py`, `outbound_differ.py`, `git_adapter.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `_store/push.py` (docstring), focused tests.

Scope: M. Depends on closed A1.
baseline.summary: A2-1: move last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping into .bridge_state/get_rotation.json (write-new, read max(new, legacy))

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
On 2026-08-12 a session was blocked on the tickets write lock for 15+ minutes: a `transition ... closed` (pid 61327) held both legs of the store write lock (`.ticket-write.lock` and `.ticket-write.lock.d`) for the whole LLM completion verification. rebar had NO diagnostic surface for this — the operator had to `ls` the lock dir and `cat` the owner stamp by hand to learn who held it and whether that process was still alive. `rebar doctor` today only audits blocking links, so an operator facing a wedged store has nothing to run.

The lock-hold defect itself is bug `sunlit-cynical-ray` (84af-8d4f-bc1c-41b9), fixed in parallel. This ticket is the OBSERVABILITY half and does not change locking behaviour: even after 84af lands, a held or orphaned lock still needs to be inspectable.

## Approach
Add a read-only lock-health section to `rebar doctor`. All the primitives already exist and are REUSED, not re-derived:

- `rebar._store.lock.write_lock_is_busy` — the existing zero-deadline both-legs probe.
  Its immediate-probe technique (fcntl `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`, `mkdir`, give straight back)
  is what the per-leg probes use, so held/free is answered without waiting.
- `rebar._store.lock_owner._parse_v2_stamp` / `_describe_stamped_pid` /
  `_mkdir_lock_age_s` — the v2 owner stamp (host/ns/pid/start), the same-host-only
  liveness verdict (`live` / `not-running` / `unprobeable (...)`), and the hold age.
- `rebar._store.lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale(lock_dir, fcntl_held=False)` — the SOLE
  staleness authority. No second heuristic is written; the pid-recycle qualification and
  the wall-clock ceiling from the existing decision table are inherited as-is.
  `fcntl_held=False` because doctor holds nothing.

Legs reported: the tracker's fcntl leg `.ticket-write.lock`, the tracker's mkdir leg `.ticket-write.lock.d`, `.rebar/hlc.lock` (fcntl, probed the same non-blocking way), and `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` (an `O_EXCL` existence lock, so held == file exists). The drain lock carries no owner stamp; its staleness is reported as `not-assessable` rather than guessed at, because inventing a heuristic for it is exactly what this plan forbids.

Doctor is READ-ONLY here: nothing is reclaimed or deleted, and `--repair` does not touch locks (its repair loop iterates only the link findings list, which lock results never join). A held lock with a live holder is INFO. A lock the shared staleness function calls stale is a FINDING and joins doctor's existing exit-code rule (exit 1 when anything is outstanding, 0 otherwise).

Because `_commands/doctor.py` is a link-audit module, the lock checks land in a new sibling module `_commands/doctor_locks.py` along the existing command-module seam (the same split `fsck.py`/`fsck_repair.py` uses); `doctor.py` calls one entry point and renders the result.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` (new) — leg probes, stamp decode, report + finding
  construction, text rendering.
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — call the scan, add `locks` / `lock_findings` to the
  JSON envelope and the text output, fold lock findings into the exit code.
- `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json` — describe the two new keys.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — document the lock section under `rebar doctor`.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py` (or a new sibling test module) — the tests below.

## Testing
- Happy path: a free store reports every leg `free`, no lock findings, exit unchanged (0).
- Held-and-healthy: holding the real write lock via `lock.write_lock`, doctor reports the
  mkdir leg held, names host/pid from the stamp, reports a non-negative hold age and a
  live pid state, and produces NO finding (INFO only) — so exit stays 0.
- Stale/dead holder: a mkdir lock dir stamped with a v2 stamp for a dead pid on this host
  produces a `stale-lock` finding and exit 1.
- Unreadable/absent stamp: a lock dir with no owner file reports `unknown (no ownership
  stamp)` and does not crash; a `.rebar` dir that does not exist reports the two `.rebar`
  legs as absent rather than raising.
- Read-only guarantee: after a doctor run over a held lock, the lock dir, its owner file
  and the drain lock file all still exist byte-identical (doctor never reclaims).
- JSON contract: `--output json` validates against the updated doctor schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar doctor` reports, for each of the four legs, held/free (or absent), and for
      the mkdir leg the v2 stamp fields host/ns/pid/start, holder liveness, and hold age —
      verified by the held-and-healthy test asserting those fields in `--output json`.
- [x] Holder liveness is same-host only: a stamp from another host identity or another pid
      namespace reports an `unprobeable (...)` verdict, never a pid guess — verified by a
      test stamping a foreign host identity.
- [x] Staleness comes only from `lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale`; a grep of the new module
      shows no second staleness heuristic (no independent age threshold, no independent pid
      probe used to decide stale).
- [x] A dead-holder lock yields a finding and `rebar doctor` exits 1; a live-holder lock
      yields no finding and exits 0 — verified by the two tests above.
- [x] Doctor never mutates lock state: the read-only test shows lock dir, owner file and
      drain lock file unchanged after a run, and `--repair` performs no lock action.
- [x] `--output json` matches `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json` and
      `docs/cli-reference.md` documents the lock section — verified by the schema test and
      the docs diff.
- [x] All `src/rebar` files stay under the 800-LOC module cap (module-size gate green).
baseline.summary: doctor: lock health checks (held/free, holder liveness, hold age, staleness)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`binding_store.py` is at the 800-line hard boundary because file loading, unknown-field preservation, tempfile cleanup, JSON encoding, GET-rotation ordering, retired-state replacement, and alert persistence live beside identity policy. Moving those branches without direct byte/fault oracles could turn known recoverable partial states into silent data loss.

## Outcome
Extract a private `BindingRepository`/unit-of-work behind the unchanged public `BindingStore` facade. The repository owns paths and the original dictionaries, returns open typed views over those same dictionaries, and preserves every existing load/save byte and exception contract. `peer_state.py` and `get_rotation.py` remain independent owners. Record the internal ownership and recovery/cutover constraints in the binding-lifecycle ADR.

## Plan
1. Add a cohesive repository module for live, retired, rotation, and alert paths; current load/corruption rules; JSON tempfiles; per-file `os.replace`; and dirty/change gating. Do not introduce a multi-file atomicity claim.
2. Move persistence calls behind facade delegates without changing `BindingStore` construction, loader, public signatures, shared inner dictionaries, or caller-visible exceptions.
3. Preserve rotation-before-live order and the inline rotation floor, retired-first move ordering, best-effort alert writes, and exact sorted/indented/newline serialization.
4. Keep tickets publication in `reconcile_helpers.py` as an external five-file allowlisted seam. Add no broad staging and no publish at each local checkpoint.
5. Add an ADR that distinguishes repository unit-of-work durability from tickets publication and records the later exact-match recovery boundary.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- A direct-repository suite loads legacy/unknown-field fixtures and asserts byte-equal round trips and no eager rewrite.
- Failure cuts inject tempfile, rotation replace, retired replace, live replace, alert write, and selective commit failures. Oracles are exact surviving files/bytes, raised versus swallowed outcome, alert/tally, and unchanged HEAD where applicable.
- Public-facade regressions assert pending/confirmed/reverse lookup and the current shallow `all_bindings()` compatibility.
- Existing GET-rotation and selective-publication suites remain the cross-seam oracle.

## Compatibility / rollback
This is an internal delegation only. Reverting the facade delegation restores the previous implementation over identical files. No format migration, eager rewrite, public import change, deep copy, general journal, or `git add -A` is permitted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Given legacy records and unknown fields, direct repository and public-facade load/save preserve semantic fields and exact sorted/indented/trailing-newline bytes without an eager write.
- [x] Given each named fault cut, tests observe the documented old/new file combination and the same raise/swallow/alert behavior as before extraction.
- [x] GET rotation is durably attempted before live replacement; a failed sidecar save retains the newest inline floor and a later retry converges.
- [x] `BindingStore` import, constructor, loader, signatures, shared inner-entry behavior, and existing peer/get-rotation delegates remain compatible.
- [x] Tickets publication still stages only the existing five bridge-state files and an unchanged pass creates no commit.
- [x] The ADR states repository ownership, ordered partial-state behavior, selective publication, rollback, and the no-journal/no-format-migration decision.
baseline.summary: RP-02 S1 — Extract the byte-preserving binding repository

# Enforce the 50/72 commit-message rule with a local commit-msg hook

## Context / Problem

Gerrit renders a change description as preformatted text and preserves the author's newlines, so the wrapping a commit lands with is exactly what reviewers read (and what `git log` shows in an 80-column terminal). Gerrit's bundled `commit-message-length-validator` only WARNS (`warning: subject >50 characters`, `warning: too many message lines longer than 72 characters; manually wrap lines`), which is trivially ignored — and nothing in this repo checked it.

Result: commit bodies on `main` are split between hard-wrapped (72-79 col) and single-paragraph (129-286 col) styles. Measured with the new checker against the last 40 commits on origin/main: 5 pass, 35 fail, with failures like 177, 183, 222 and 223-char body lines. That inconsistency is what made the wrapping look like something rebar was doing to the text (investigated under ticket 368a, closed not_a_bug).

Research basis — all four major Gerrit-based projects mandate the same rule, and none avoids the line breaks:
- Go: "The text should be wrapped at around 72 columns" + "Don't use HTML, Markdown, or any other markup language."
- Chromium: "Long lines should be wrapped to 72 columns for easier log message viewing in terminals."
- ChromiumOS: "Wrap the body text to 72 characters so that `git log` looks nice"; subject ~60, 72 hard limit.
- Android: "Provide a long description that hard-wraps at 72 characters maximum"; subject 50 max.

## Approach

Enforce locally at commit time (operator's explicit choice: pre-commit framework, NOT CI).

- `scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py` — check-only checker for the 50/72 rule, matching the repo's existing `scripts/check_*.py` convention. Never rewrites the message; it names the offending lines.
- Wired as a `commit-message-wrap` hook in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` at the **commit-msg** stage. It cannot run at the `pre-commit` stage because the commit message does not exist yet. `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]` installs both.
- `make hooks` now verifies BOTH hooks landed AND that Gerrit's Change-Id stamping survived.

Carve-outs (wrapping these would break them): trailers (`rebar-ticket:`, `Change-Id:`, `Signed-off-by:`), `TAG=` lines, fenced code blocks, indented literal blocks, table rows, and lines whose length comes from a single unsplittable atomic token (URL, path, dotted identifier). Comment lines and the `git commit --verbose` diff are ignored.

## Critical risk handled: Gerrit's commit-msg hook

Gerrit's own `commit-msg` hook (which stamps `Change-Id`) already owns that slot. `pre-commit install` defaults to MIGRATION mode, preserving the existing hook as `commit-msg.legacy` and running both. Verified empirically in a throwaway repo: a conforming commit still received its `Change-Id`; an over-long body was rejected and no commit was created. `pre-commit install -f/--overwrite` would delete Gerrit's hook and break every push — documented as a do-not-do in the config, the Makefile, and CONTRIBUTING.md, and `make hooks` warns if the Change-Id chain is missing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A commit whose body has a line over 72 columns is REJECTED locally, with output naming each offending line and its length.
- [ ] A commit whose subject exceeds 50 columns is REJECTED locally.
- [ ] A conforming commit succeeds AND still receives its Gerrit `Change-Id` trailer (Gerrit's hook is chained as `commit-msg.legacy`, not clobbered).
- [ ] A body line is EXEMPT from the 72-column check when any of these detection rules matches (each stated as the exact rule an executor implements):
  - [ ] **Trailer** — the stripped line matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s` (e.g. `rebar-ticket:`, `Change-Id:`, `Signed-off-by:`).
  - [ ] **Tag** — the stripped line matches `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=` (e.g. `BUG=`, `TEST=`).
  - [ ] **Fenced block** — the line lies between two lines matching `^\s*```{3}`; the fence marker TOGGLES, so prose after a closing fence is checked again.
  - [ ] **Indented literal block** — the RAW line begins with exactly 4+ spaces or a tab, i.e. `line.startswith(("    ", "\t"))`. A 1-3 space indent is NOT exempt.
  - [ ] **Table row** — the stripped line begins with `|`.
  - [ ] **Atomic token** — the line contains a whitespace-delimited token longer than 72 chars, EVERY such over-long token matches `://|[/\\]|\w[._-]\w` (a URL scheme, a path separator, or a dotted/underscored/hyphenated identifier), AND the rest of the stripped line (its length minus the longest such token) is itself <= 72. A 73+ char run of ordinary characters is NOT exempt.
- [ ] git's own scaffolding produces no false positives: comment (`#`) lines and the `git commit --verbose` diff below the `>8` marker are ignored.
- [ ] The checker never mutates the commit message (check-only, matching the repo's stated pre-commit policy).
- [ ] `.pre-commit-config.yaml` gains a top-level `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]` key, so the EXISTING bare `pre-commit install` in `make hooks` (which passes no `--hook-type`) installs both hook types with no flag change.
- [ ] The `hooks:` target in `Makefile` is MODIFIED to add the two new verification branches described below; it currently verifies only the `pre-commit` hook file and must not be left as-is.
- [ ] `make hooks` EXITS NON-ZERO when either the `pre-commit` or the `commit-msg` hook file is absent after install.
- [ ] `make hooks` prints a WARNING (and still exits zero) when no `Change-Id` stamping is found in `commit-msg` or `commit-msg.legacy`, since Gerrit's hook is fetched separately and its absence must not block wiring the local gates.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md documents the enforcement, the exemption list, why the hook runs at the commit-msg stage, and the never-run-`pre-commit install -f` warning.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the rule, every carve-out, the fence-toggle case, and the CLI exit codes.

## Notes / scope

Local guardrail only — bypassable with `git commit --no-verify`, and CI does NOT check wrapping (deliberate: the operator chose pre-commit over CI). Existing history is not rewritten; the gate applies to new commits only.
baseline.summary: Enforce the 50/72 commit-message rule with a local commit-msg hook

## Context

The review bot's reported token totals are incomplete: the Pass-1 finder batch does not surface its usage on the batch step output, so the finalize step has nothing to fold in and the CloudWatch totals under-report every code review by the whole Pass-1 finder leg.

**This ticket is now scoped to the CODE-REVIEW half only.** The plan-review half of the original scope already landed under ticket `d52a`: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:684` sets `coverage["usage"] = aggregate_usage(call_records)`, and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:199` surfaces it as `"_usage": coverage.get("usage") or aggregate_usage([])`. Re-scoped 2026-08-09 after a status audit found that half delivered and this half untouched; do not re-do the plan-review work.

What remains, verified outstanding on `origin/main`:

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py:130` emits `outputs={"findings", "criteria_count",
  "batch_plan"}` — there is no `usage` key anywhere in the file.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:139-141` carries a present-tense comment recording the gap
  ("the Pass-1 finder batch does not surface `_usage` on its step output (follow-up)"), which is
  now this ticket and becomes stale the moment it is fixed.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:169-172` ALREADY folds `_usage` into the totals when a step
  emits it, so the consuming side needs no change — this is an emit-side fix.

## Plan

Mirror the shape `d52a` established on the plan-review side rather than inventing a second convention: aggregate the Pass-1 finder call records in the code-review batch runner and emit them under the same `_usage` step-output key `finalize.py` already reads. Then delete the stale follow-up comment in `finalize.py`, because a comment describing a closed gap is worse than none.

Keep the change emit-side only. Do not modify `finalize.py`'s folding arithmetic — it is already correct and covered; touching it would widen the blast radius for no gain.

## Testing

A code-review finalize unit test that asserts the finder-batch usage reaches the folded totals: it must FAIL before the emit change (the key is absent, so the fold contributes zero) and pass after. Assert on the folded total rather than on the presence of the key, so the test proves the number is actually complete rather than that a dict has a key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` emits Pass-1 finder token usage on its batch step
      output under the same `_usage` key that `finalize.py:169-172` already consumes.
- [x] The aggregation uses the same helper and shape as the plan-review side established by `d52a`,
      so the two paths do not diverge into two conventions.
- [x] The stale gap comment at `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:139-141` is removed.
- [x] A held-out unit test asserts the finder-batch usage is included in the finalized code-review
      totals, verified RED before the emit change and GREEN after.
- [x] `finalize.py`'s existing folding arithmetic is unchanged, and the existing code-review
      finalize tests pass unmodified.
baseline.summary: code-review: surface Pass-1 finder token usage on the batch step output

# Idea: self-hosted Renovate on Gerrit — peer-pattern dependency updates through the two gates

Captured 2026-07-09 during the OSS v1.0.0 front-door research (epic breaded-ammonitic-elephant). The APPROVED v1.0 design is Dependabot advisory PRs on the GitHub mirror (github-actions ecosystem only, monthly; PRs are unmergeable notifications the maintainer lands via Gerrit; lockdown bot exempts dependabot[bot]) — see story cardiac-lush-chihuahua. This idea records the researched alternative that would eliminate that departure from the Gerrit-peer pattern, for possible post-1.0 adoption.

## The finding

Renovate (Mend.io — the leading cross-platform dependency bot; what ruff/uv use) has a native self-hosted Gerrit platform (`platform=gerrit`, all Gerrit 3.x): it pushes each dependency bump directly as a **Gerrit Change** — no GitHub PRs — so updates flow through the same `LLM-Review` + `Verified` gates as human changes. That is the Wikimedia-LibraryUpgrader / OpenStack-requirements-bot pattern, off the shelf, and it matches rebar's dogfooding ethos (the dependency bot is just another contributor under the two-vote merge policy).

- Docs: https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/gerrit/ and https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/platform/
- Mechanics: Gerrit bot account + HTTP credentials; SSH cloning supported (discussion #39625); metadata via a `Renovate-Branch` commit footer (needs Gerrit ≥3.6, satisfied); `autoApprove` exists but would stay OFF (our gates vote); `statusCheckNames` can map Renovate checks (e.g. minimumReleaseAge) onto Gerrit labels.

## Why it was NOT chosen for v1.0 (the blockers to re-evaluate)

1. **Experimental platform status**: Renovate's Gerrit support is officially experimental — maintainers deprioritize Gerrit issues and allow breaking changes in minor releases. Re-evaluate when it is declared stable.
2. **Ops cost**: Renovate is a CLI needing a scheduled runner (cron GitHub Action or the Gerrit host) plus credentials — a new moving part vs zero-ops Dependabot; disproportionate for a monthly, github-actions-only update stream.
3. **`rebar-ticket:` trailer integration**: the Verified gate requires a resolving rebar-ticket trailer on every commit; Renovate has a known open issue with commit trailers via `commitBody` on Gerrit (https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/33306). Adoption needs one of: a working trailer config, a standing "dependency updates" ticket baked into the commit template, or a narrow bot exemption in the require-ticket check.
4. No Dependency Dashboard on Gerrit (built on Issues) — cosmetic at this scale.

## Promotion sketch (if/when picked up)

- Trial on a scratch Gerrit project first: bot account, `platform=gerrit`, github-actions manager only; verify trailer handling end-to-end through both gates; verify the LLM-Review bot behaves sanely on bot-authored changes.
- If adopted: retire the Dependabot advisory-PR flow (delete .github/dependabot.yml or reduce to security-alerts posture), remove the lockdown-bot dependabot exemption, and update the decision records in docs/releasing.md + the dependabot.yml rationale that story cardiac-lush-chihuahua created.
- Revisit triggers: Renovate Gerrit platform declared stable; dependency-update volume growing beyond monthly-actions-only (e.g. a committed uv.lock); the advisory-PR flow proving annoying in practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] (To be designed at promotion — this is a parked idea, not dispatchable work.)
baseline.summary: Self-hosted Renovate on Gerrit: peer-pattern dependency updates through the two gates (post-1.0)

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at **800 lines against the hard 800-line cap** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which the CI module-size gate enforces with no allowlist. It is one line from red: the next change to any public library write verb fails the build. The sibling story adding two optional `create_ticket` arguments must widen two `@overload` signatures, the implementation, and their docstrings — it cannot land until this is relieved. This ticket buys that headroom by concern, not by line count.

## Approach

`_lib_writes` is the **aggregation point for every public library write**, so it grows on two axes: a new verb appends a wrapper, and an existing verb gaining an argument widens one in place. The facade split (S3/4532) cut the library **by direction** — writes vs reads vs gates vs ops — and that axis is exhausted: the write half alone carries seven concerns. The durable fix is to cut it **by concern**, per the `fsck` split (`defaceable-icy-antelope`), which took two cuts out of one 800-line file.

The seven concerns present today:

1. **Genesis** — `init_repo`, `create_ticket` (two `@overload`s + impl), `idea`.
2. **Identity & key material** — `create_identity`, `ensure_identity_for`, `create_placeholder`,
   `add_identity_key`, `revoke_identity_key`, `use_identity`, `resolve_current_identity`; all
   delegate to `rebar._commands.identity`, none touches ticket state.
3. **Status lifecycle** — `transition`, `claim`, `reopen`. The only place in the module that
   raises `ConcurrencyError`.
4. **Leaf mutations** — `_python_leaf` and its seven in-module callers `comment`, `edit_ticket`,
   `link`, `unlink`, `tag`, `untag`, `archive`.
5. **Session logs** — `append_session_log`, `start_session_log`; own `CommandError` mapping,
   NOT routed through `_python_leaf`.
6. **Store maintenance** — `compact`, `attach_commits`.
7. **Signing** — `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, delegating to `rebar.signing`.

**Two cuts**, mirroring `fsck`:

- **`_lib_mutations.py`** takes 4+5+6. Anchored on the `_python_leaf` call graph: one adapter,
  seven callers, all inside the block, nothing else in this module calling it. Stated honestly,
  5 and 6 **ride along** as the contiguous remainder of the post-genesis mutation surface, not
  because they call `_python_leaf`; the strict call-graph subset is ~130 lines and
  non-contiguous, forcing a scattered cut near the 100-line floor.
- **`_lib_identity.py`** takes 2+7 — the non-ticket, key-material surface. Identities own
  OpenSSH key lines, `use_identity`/`resolve_current_identity` select the current one, and
  signing binds a manifest to the environment key. Stated honestly, signing is ~52 lines and
  **cannot stand alone** under the 100-line floor; identity is the nearest concern by shape,
  and the module already banners signing apart from the write path.
- **`_lib_writes.py` keeps 1+3** — genesis and the status state machine.

The plan of record extracted only 4+5+6 and left `_lib_writes` at ~544 — sound at 778, but at 800 that lands **above** the 200-500 target band on a file that grew 22 lines in weeks. Hence two cuts.

Moved names are **re-exported** from `_lib_writes` with `# noqa: F401`, exactly as `fsck.py` re-exports from `fsck_scan`/`fsck_tracker_health`. That leaves `__init__.py` and `_lib_gates.py` **untouched**, so every `rebar.<name>` and `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` path survives — a smaller diff than re-pointing consumers.

**The pre-move surface, reconciled.** `_lib_writes` has 29 `def` statements = **27 distinct names** plus the two extra `@overload` stubs of `create_ticket`. `__init__.py` re-exports **all 27**, so the facade surface and the definition set coincide — no name defined here is omitted from the facade. `_python_leaf` is one of the 27: it resolves as **`rebar._python_leaf`** (its own `_python_leaf as _python_leaf` alias in `__init__.py`) *and* as `rebar._lib_writes._python_leaf`, the form `_lib_gates.py` imports. The 27 partition across the concerns above as 3 + 7 + 3 + 8 (leaf mutations, counting `_python_leaf`) + 2 + 2 + 2. Dependency direction is one-way — `_lib_writes` imports both new modules, neither imports back — so there is no cycle.

This is **behaviour-preserving**: bodies relocate byte-identically; no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` (new) — concerns 4+5+6
- `src/rebar/_lib_identity.py` (new) — concerns 2+7
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — keeps 1+3, gains the two re-export blocks

`__init__.py`, `_lib_gates.py`, and everything under `tests/` are deliberately **not** touched. The reference audit supports that: the only real-code importers of `_lib_writes` are `_lib_gates.py` (`_python_leaf`) and `__init__.py` (the 27-name re-export), and the string pass (`monkeypatch.setattr` / `getattr` / `importlib`) finds **zero** `_lib_writes` attribute references — every test patch targets the `rebar` facade or `rebar.signing`, both preserved.

`.github/complexity-baseline.json` holds **zero** entries for `_lib_writes.py`, so no moved symbol carries accepted debt and the `--lock` re-key hazard that cast `Verified -1` on the `fsck` change cannot arise. The baseline is therefore not in scope.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing with **no test file edited**. The specific risk is the **public API surface**, since all 27 names are re-exported as `rebar.<name>` and `_lib_gates` depends on `_python_leaf` at three call sites — a silently dropped re-export would still leave the suite green wherever the facade is imported lazily. Checked by name:

- every name previously importable as `rebar.<name>` still resolves after the move, asserted
  name by name against the pre-move list;
- `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` still resolves for all moved names, which is what makes
  `_lib_gates` and any `monkeypatch` target survive;
- the three modules import cleanly in **either** order, catching a cycle introduced by the
  re-export direction.

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the size oracle and needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_lib_writes.py` is at or below 450 lines; checked by
      `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_writes.py)" -le 450 ]` exiting 0.
- [ ] `_lib_mutations.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`.
- [ ] `_lib_identity.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_identity.py`.
- [ ] The repo's size oracle still passes; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve on the facade as `rebar.<name>` — 26 public wrappers plus
      `rebar._python_leaf`; checked by a script asserting `hasattr(rebar, n)` for every name in
      the pre-move list, exiting non-zero on the first miss.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve as `rebar._lib_writes.<name>`, which is the form
      `_lib_gates.py` imports; checked by the same assert-and-exit script against
      `rebar._lib_writes`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/__init__.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` are unchanged; checked by
      `git diff --exit-code HEAD~1 -- src/rebar/__init__.py src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] No file under `tests/` is changed; checked by `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 -- tests/`
      producing empty output.
- [ ] The three modules import cleanly in any order; checked by two fresh interpreters, one
      importing `_lib_identity`, `_lib_mutations`, `_lib_writes` in that order and one in
      reverse, both exiting 0.
- [ ] `make lint` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [ ] The CI test selection passes; checked by
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exiting 0.
- [ ] `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` reports no new entries; checked by running
      it with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=navapbc/rebar` and confirming exit 0.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the _python_leaf mutation block from _lib_writes.py into _lib_mutations.py

## Context / Problem

`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` runs its live tier on a weekly cron across every dataset-bearing spec, bounded only by `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES: "12"` per spec, with no dollar ceiling in that lane (its comment: "Hard dollar caps live at the provider dashboard").

Letting the criteria covered by this epic join that sweep would multiply its per-run call count several-fold every week, in perpetuity, and would grow again with each criterion added later. The cron is also the wrong instrument for these fixtures: they exist to catch a criterion-rubric regression, and a rubric regression arrives with a commit rather than with the passage of time.

## Approach

Execute a criterion's fixtures when that criterion's rubric changes.

The selection is a rebar operation, not a CI feature: a shared engine function (`src/rebar/llm/evals/changed_criteria.py`) maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it. It does NOT reimplement the criterion→rubric-path rule: it REUSES the prior-art primitive `rebar.llm.evals.fixture_selection.rubric_path(criterion_id, *, repo_root, gate_key='plan_review')`, which already resolves a logical id through `criterion_prompt_id` and `get_prompt`'s override-wins ordering. For every id in `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` it resolves `rubric_path`, makes it repo-relative, and intersects that set with the changed files. This mirrors the code-review precedent `code_review.registry.glob_triggered_overlays` / `project_criterion_applies`, which likewise map a `changed_files` set to criterion ids.

**Both rubric storage conventions are covered because `rubric_path` resolves both** — the packaged `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md` and a `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md` project override (which wins). A changed path of rubric shape that maps to no effective criterion's resolved rubric is UNMAPPED: named on stderr rather than skipped, selection still exits 0.

**Range → changed files** reuses the existing `git diff --name-only <ref>..HEAD` plumbing shape already in the repo (`plan_review.drift_floor._drifted_paths`), not a second convention.

**CLI surface and the argparse contract.** The existing `criteria eval` verb takes a REQUIRED positional `criterion_id` and returns exit 2 when it is empty/missing (`docs/exit-codes.md`). This story makes the positional OPTIONAL and MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with a new `--changed-since <ref>` flag: exactly one of {positional id, `--changed-since <ref>`} must be given. The bare `criteria eval` with NEITHER still returns 2, so the documented "empty or missing id → 2" contract is preserved for that form. `docs/exit-codes.md` is updated in the same change to document the new mode: `criteria eval --changed-since <ref>` prints the selected criterion ids (sorted, one per line) and exits 0; an unmappable rubric-shaped path is named on stderr and still exits 0.

**Select-then-run.** The positional `criteria eval <id>` form is unchanged (always live). The new `--changed-since` form prints the selection unconditionally, then runs each selected criterion live ONLY when the `agents` extra + credentials are present; with no model configured it is selection-only and issues no model call (a non-rubric range exits 0 with no model call).

**Portability.** The trigger is operation-linked: a developer (or a no-CI project) runs the command locally against any git range and gets the same selection; the workflow job is a thin caller. The command shells out to nothing POSIX-specific and takes its repo root from the existing resolution path.

**CI trigger classification and ref derivation.** The new job is added to `prompt-eval.yml`. The `pull_request` trigger is INCLUDED (a rubric edit arrives on a PR — the case this job exists for) passing `--changed-since ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`; the `push` trigger is INCLUDED for ordinary branches (passing `--changed-since ${{ github.event.before }}`) and EXCLUDED for `main`, `feature/**` and `tickets` via the existing `branches-ignore`; the weekly `schedule` trigger is EXCLUDED for the new job — the point of this child. No trigger is NO_FILTER. The job is non-blocking (`continue-on-error`) and same-repo-only.

## Scope

The shared changed-rubric selection function (reusing `rubric_path`), its CLI flag with the optional/mutually-exclusive positional, the `docs/exit-codes.md` update, and the workflow job that calls it. The existing weekly live sweep keeps its current spec set.

## Non-goals

- Changing the weekly cron's behavior for the specs it already covers.
- Making the new job a required or blocking check; it stays non-blocking like the existing
  live tier.
- Any dollar-ceiling mechanism inside GitHub Actions.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive: one new engine function, one new CLI flag (the positional becomes optional but the existing `criteria eval <id>` invocation is byte-compatible), one `docs/exit-codes.md` row update, one new workflow job. The offline tier (the only required check) and the weekly live tier are untouched. Back-out is deleting the job, the flag, and the doc row; no persisted state, no format change.

## Testing

A real CLI subprocess against seeded temporary git repositories exercises the selection across a rubric-touching range, a non-rubric range, and an unmappable rubric path (the subprocess tier is required for the argument parsing, git range resolution and exit codes). A unit test covers the workflow's resolved spec list; the existing actionlint node covers workflow validity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A range touching `plan_review_T8.md` and `plan_review_G6.md` selects exactly the
      criterion ids `T8` and `G6`; verified by a `pytest` subprocess test asserting the
      printed selection against a seeded temporary repository.
- [x] A range touching no rubric file selects nothing, exits `0`, and issues no model call;
      verified by the same subprocess test asserting an empty selection and `exit code` 0
      with no model configured.
- [x] A rubric path matching no registry criterion is named on stderr rather than skipped
      silently, and selection still exits `0`; verified by `pytest` asserting the warning text
      for a seeded `plan_review_bogus.md`.
- [x] `criteria eval` with NEITHER a positional id NOR `--changed-since` still exits `2`,
      preserving the documented contract; verified by `pytest` asserting exit code 2.
- [x] Wiring the change-triggered live-eval path for this epic's criteria does NOT enroll
      them into the weekly live sweep: after this change the weekly sweep's resolved spec
      list still excludes the epic's prompt ids (they run on rubric change only, never on the
      weekly cron), so the new path adds a trigger without widening the weekly sweep; verified
      by `pytest` asserting the intersection of the epic's prompt ids and the weekly sweep's
      resolved spec is empty.
- [x] When the `--changed-since` ref range is uncomputable — a branch's first push, where
      `github.event.before` is the all-zeros SHA — selection treats it as 'no prior ref',
      selects nothing, exits `0`, and notes it on stderr rather than crashing on `git diff`;
      verified by `pytest` (`test_first_push_zero_sha_ref_selects_nothing_without_crashing`).
- [x] The command produces a selection with no CI environment variables set; verified by a
      `pytest` subprocess test run with a cleared environment.
- [x] The workflow file passes the repository's existing actionlint check; verified by
      `pytest` over that node.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a rubric-touching range selects only the affected criteria; a non-rubric range selects none; `docs/exit-codes.md` documents the new mode.

## Budget

**Hard cap $25**, covering verification runs while developing this child. Steady-state cost afterwards is zero unless a rubric changes, at which point one criterion runs.

The MCP tool and the Python library both pass a ticket_id to `validate`, but the engine `validate` is REPO-WIDE and rejects positionals. Reproduced empirically.

- Engine: src/rebar/_engine/validate-issues.sh:81-84 — catch-all `*) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1`.
- Library: src/rebar/__init__.py:197-203 — `validate(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None)` builds `["validate", ticket_id, "--json"]`. Signature REQUIRES ticket_id (cannot be called id-less -> TypeError).
- MCP: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:153-156 — `validate(ticket_id: str) -> dict`.
- Repro: `rebar validate <id>` -> `Unknown option: <id>`, exit 1; `rebar.validate('<id>')` -> {'output':'Unknown option: <id>','exit_code':1}; `rebar.validate()` -> TypeError.

## Fix
- Library: make validate repo-wide (no ticket_id); call `["validate","--json"]`; parse stdout JSON into the report dict. NOTE: validate's nonzero exit is score-encoded (exit = 5 - score), NOT an error — do not raise on nonzero; return the report.
- MCP: drop the ticket_id param (`def validate() -> dict`); update docstring.
- Update any existing tests that call validate with an id.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar.validate()` (no id) returns the repo-wide report dict {score,critical_issues,major_issues,minor_issues,warnings,suggestions}
- [ ] MCP `validate` tool takes no ticket_id and returns the report
- [ ] Score-encoded nonzero exit does not raise / is not treated as failure
- [ ] Test covers library + MCP repo-wide validate; existing id-passing tests updated
baseline.summary: validate() passes ticket_id but engine validate is repo-wide (lib + MCP broken)

Change 330c (commit 9ba1e90e3c, "box flips no longer stale attestations") normalizes AC checkbox STATE (case-insensitive x, - or * bullets, line-anchored) to '[ ]' before hashing the material fingerprint, so flipping boxes at close no longer stales a plan-review attestation or the completion-verifier staleness check. The commit touched only src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py + tests — no documentation.

docs/plan-review-gate.md still teaches the OLD behavior:

- §"Attestation, freshness & invalidation" (~L469): "the bound material fingerprint matches the current ticket — a material edit (description/AC/file-impact/decomposition) invalidates it. (Tags/comments/links/assignee are not material and do not invalidate.)" — a reader concludes any description edit, including box flips, invalidates. Checkbox-state flips are now explicitly NOT material.

baseline.description:
# J11 — Prove bidirectional reconciliation live, against a realistic store

## Why this exists

Epic e369's headline AC is:

> [operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira instance ... at
> least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass, and one local edit
> appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions

It is NOT met, and the way it failed is instructive. CI run 30637886718 reported:

    invariants: scanned=0 filed=0
    OK: steady-state pass converged
    RECON: outbound_differ total=0   inbound_differ total=0

**Scanned zero.** The pass converged because there was nothing to reconcile. That proves the reconciler runs cleanly against an EMPTY instance — it does not prove data moves. On an empty store 'converged' and 'works' are indistinguishable, and only one of them is the criterion. Closing the epic on that output would have been the fifth instance in this epic of green-but-broken.

The existing live module builds its store with the `rebar_repo` fixture: `rebar.init_repo()` on an empty temp dir. Nothing to sync, so nothing syncs.

## Approach

Run the live verification against a COPY OF THIS PROJECT'S ACTUAL TICKET STORE, so the pass sees realistic volume, ticket shapes, link graphs, comment histories and field values — the conditions that surface ordering and field-mapping defects an empty store cannot. (Deliberately NOT "pagination": that is a property of the REMOTE issue count, not of the local store, and is exercised by seeding the harness — see the volume bullet below. An earlier draft listed it here and contradicted that bullet.)

### Isolation is the first requirement, not an afterthought

rebar AUTO-COMMITS and AUTO-PUSHES ticket events to `sync.remote`. A copy of this project's store that retained its configuration could push test mutations back at the real project. Defence in depth, in priority order:

1. **A SEPARATE REPO WITH NO REMOTES — the primary mechanism.** The CI job `git init`s a fresh repo
   and copies the ticket-store content in. It never adds `origin`, so there is physically
   nowhere to push, independent of any config or env value. This is stronger than a flag
   because it cannot be defeated by a mis-read setting.
   **HOW the content is obtained, because it is NOT in a normal checkout:** `.tickets-tracker/` is
   GITIGNORED (`.gitignore:9`) and the store lives on the ORPHAN `tickets` branch, which
   `actions/checkout` does not fetch. The job must explicitly `git fetch origin tickets` in the
   SOURCE checkout and materialise that tree, then `git init` + commit it in the destination.
   Copying the workspace directory would copy nothing.
   **EXTRACT INTO `.tickets-tracker/`, NOT INTO THE REPO ROOT — an earlier draft's command was
   wrong and would have produced a store the reconciler cannot see.** The orphan `tickets` branch
   holds the ticket files AND `.bridge_state` at ITS OWN ROOT (`git ls-tree origin/tickets` shows
   `.bridge_state`, `.store-compat.json`, and bare ticket-id entries such as `003a-09ae-9983-4007`),
   whereas the reconciler reads `tracker_dir = repo_root / ".tickets-tracker"` (`reconcile.py:265`).
   Extracting to the root therefore lands every ticket one directory ABOVE where the pass looks,
   so the pass sees NO LOCAL TICKETS — a store that is empty as far as the reconciler is
   concerned, reproduced by the setup rather than by the product. (Note this does NOT surface as
   `scanned=0`: that number counts REMOTE Jira issues, not local tickets — see the store-copy AC.
   It is caught by the ticket-count check, which is why that check reads the filesystem.)
   The command is:
       mkdir -p <fresh repo>/.tickets-tracker
       git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x -C <fresh repo>/.tickets-tracker
   and the fixture must ASSERT the layout after extraction (ticket files exist under
   `.tickets-tracker/`) rather than trust the redirection.
   **THE WORKING REPO ALSO NEEDS A CONFIG, and it has none — it is a fresh `git init`.** The copied
   tree carries tickets, not reconciler settings, so the fixture must WRITE a `rebar.toml` into the
   fresh repo containing `[reconciler]` with `base_url = "http://localhost:2990/jira"` (plus the
   project key and `allow_insecure = true`, since the harness serves plain http). That written file is
   also what the `base_url` AC below inspects — the check and the setup must name the same file, or
   the check passes by finding nothing.
2. `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` as a second, independent layer (`sync.push` accepts `always|async|off`;
   the env override is authoritative).
   **Do NOT assert on `sync.remote`.** It defaults to `"origin"` (`_config_schema.py:307`) whether or
   not such a remote exists, so "sync.remote is empty" is neither achievable nor meaningful — and
   setting it empty to satisfy a check would give false confidence while changing nothing. The
   assertion that carries real weight is that `git remote` in the working repo returns NOTHING.
3. The reconciler config points ONLY at the harness (`reconciler.base_url` = the container). No Cloud
   credentials are present in the job environment at all — no `JIRA_URL`, no `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, no
   `acli` auth — so the Cloud path cannot be driven even by accident.
4. **The isolation is ASSERTED, not assumed.** A test fails the job if `git remote` returns anything in
   the working repo. (NOT on `sync.remote` — see layer 2: it defaults to `"origin"` regardless, so
   that assertion can never pass and would only invite someone to weaken it.) Safety that is not
   tested is an intention.

### The copy must be SCRUBBED of Jira IDs and reconciler artifacts

Isolation stops ticket events ESCAPING. It does not stop the reconciler forming an intent to WRITE to a production issue key. The scrub is an independent layer and both are required.

Enumerated against this project's REAL tickets branch, not assumed:

    .bridge_state/bindings.json
    .bridge_state/bindings-retired.json
    .bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json
    .bridge_state.bak-retarget/bindings.json
    .bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json

Two traps a naive scrub falls into:

* **`.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` also holds real bindings.** It is a backup left by a past project
  retarget. Deleting `.bridge_state/` by name removes the live set and leaves a SECOND full set of
  production Jira bindings in the copy. Match the pattern `.bridge_state*`, and assert none survive —
  do not delete a hardcoded list. The existence of this directory is itself proof that the artifact
  set drifts over time, so the scrub must ENUMERATE the copied tree.
* **`prev_snapshot.json` must still be scrubbed — but it is NOT detectable from mutation counts,
  and two earlier drafts of this plan got that wrong in opposite directions.** It is the OUTBOUND
  field-change baseline (`OutboundDiffConfig.prev_snapshot`, consumed in
  `outbound_differ.compute_outbound_mutations`), NOT an inbound create/delete trigger: the inbound
  and legacy differs decide creates from the CURRENT snapshot. So a leftover production copy does
  not drive mass DELETION — that much an earlier draft got right.
  What that draft then got WRONG is the claim that it produces a wave of spurious outbound UPDATEs
  that the run can detect. It cannot, and the reason is mechanical: `outbound_differ.py:518-520`
  branches on `binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id)`, and `None` routes to the CREATE path — an
  UPDATE is only ever emitted for a ticket that HAS a binding. The scrub removes `bindings.json`,
  so no ticket has one, so a `prev_snapshot.json` surviving ON ITS OWN emits nothing at all.
  **Therefore it is caught DIRECTLY, by the scrub-completeness criterion asserting `.bridge_state*`
  is absent — an observation of the file itself, not an inference from mutation counts.** See the
  zero-counts AC for the full derivation; this bullet and that AC must agree, and an earlier
  revision left them contradicting each other.

### The DC-side mutation suite

Comprehensive mutations applied to the HARNESS instance (never a real Jira), each asserted to round-trip against a NAMED per-mutation oracle (the table in the acceptance criteria gives the proving read for every cell), so the bridge is exercised rather than merely started. The ONE exception is `set_parent`'s epic case, which by design does not round-trip and is asserted directly against the transport — stated here as well as in the ACs so the two cannot drift:

* **inbound (DC -> local), fourteen mutations:** create issue; edit summary; edit description;
  transition status; add label; remove label; add comment; assign; unassign; create issue link;
  delete issue link; set sub-task parent; clear parent; delete issue (absence probe).
  **`edit comment` is deliberately NOT in this list.** An earlier draft required it in both
  directions. The reconciler has no edit-comment mutation type and `JiraDataCenterTransport` has no
  `update_comment`, so it specified a capability that does not exist. If comment editing is wanted it
  is a separate feature story, not a verification criterion.
* **outbound (local -> DC), enumerated rather than described as "the mirror set":** create ticket ->
  issue; edit title -> summary; edit description; transition status; add label; remove label; add
  comment; set assignee; clear assignee; create link; delete link; set parent; clear parent; delete
  ticket. Fourteen, matching the inbound list one-for-one — `set_parent`'s epic case is expected to
  raise `NotImplementedError` (see bda8's triage), asserted **directly against the transport**
  (`with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError): transport.set_parent(...)`), NOT through the reconciler
  subprocess. `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent` catches `Exception` (dispatch_one.py:564) and
  only logs, so the exception is SWALLOWED inside a pass: no traceback, unchanged return code, and
  therefore indistinguishable on the subprocess streams from a mutation that succeeded. Routing that
  assertion through the subprocess would make it untestable by construction — the same
  swallowed-exception trap that let J9's twelve missing members pass 1600 tests.
* **volume — and note WHAT drives it.** Pagination is a property of the REMOTE issue count, not of
  the local store copy. The store copy buys realistic local volume, ticket shapes and link graphs;
  it does NOT exercise paging at all. To exercise paging the suite must CREATE issues in the harness.
  Procedure, because guessing the cap is how truncation stays hidden: first READ the instance's
  effective page size (issue a `search_issues` with a high `maxResults` and observe what the server
  actually returns — Jira 8.17.1 defaults to 50, but `jira.search.views.default.max` is
  server-configurable and the server silently truncates), then seed at least `2 * observed + 1`
  issues so at least three pages are required. Assert the observed cap in the test output so a
  future instance change is visible rather than silent.
* **idempotence:** an immediately repeated pass after each direction writes nothing.

### Sequence: a thin slice BEFORE the comprehensive suite

The riskiest unknown is not any individual mutation — it is whether the copied-and-scrubbed store drives a live pass at all. So land a vertical slice first: fetch + scrub + isolation assertions, ONE inbound round-trip (create in DC, assert it appears locally) and ONE outbound round-trip (edit locally, assert it appears in DC). Only once that is green in CI does the full mutation suite go in. Building all thirteen mutations against an unproven harness path risks debugging thirteen failures that share one root cause.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` — the `jira-dc-harness` job gains the store-copy step
  (fresh `git init`, no remote) and the isolation assertions.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — the mutation suite and its fixtures; a `dc_mutations` helper that
  applies each DC-side change through the real transport.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md` — document the isolation contract and WHY (auto-push).

**NOT in scope:** any change that could write to this project's Jira or its tickets branch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the working repo in CI has NO git remote, asserted by a test that FAILS the job otherwise —
      this is the primary isolation and it must be verified, not assumed
- [x] `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` is asserted in the same test as the no-remote check
- [x] no Cloud credential is present in the job environment, asserted by test
- [x] the store under test is a COPY of this project's real ticket store, proved by COUNTING
      LOCAL TICKETS DIRECTLY — not by the pass's `scanned` number.
      **THIS AC PREVIOUSLY MEASURED THE WRONG SIDE OF THE BRIDGE, and correcting it also corrects
      this epic's founding diagnosis.** `scanned` is `len(curr_snapshot)` (`run_differs.py:282`),
      and `curr_snapshot` is `fetcher.compute_snapshot(...)` (`reconcile.py:286`) — the normalized
      **JIRA** snapshot, i.e. the count of REMOTE issues fetched from the harness. It says nothing
      whatever about how many LOCAL tickets the copied store holds. The isolated harness starts
      with no issues, so a pass run before any DC seeding reports zero no matter how large the copy
      is; the old AC would have failed on a perfectly good store, and could never have proved the
      thing it was written to prove.
      This also means the epic's original reading of the earlier failing run was wrong. That run's
      `scanned=0` was recorded (handoff #4) as "it converged because the STORE was EMPTY". On this
      code it means the HARNESS had no issues — a remote-side fact. The local store may well have
      been fine. The conclusion drawn from it (that a pass over an empty input proves nothing)
      still stands; the mechanism attributed to it does not.
      **THE CORRECT OBSERVABLE — count the copy, on the filesystem, before any pass runs.** Assert
      that the number of ticket entries under `<working repo>/.tickets-tracker/` equals the number
      on the fetched `tickets` branch (`git ls-tree --name-only FETCH_HEAD`, excluding the dot-files
      `.bridge_state*`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `.store-compat.json`, `.ticket-write.lock`),
      and that it is > 0. Comparing the two counts rather than asserting a bare floor is what makes
      this catch a PARTIAL extraction, which a `> 0` check would wave through.
      Keep the remote-side number too, but label it honestly: after the pagination cells seed the
      harness, the same line reports how many issues the fetch actually saw, and that is the
      truncation signal the seeding criterion already owns. Where to read it, since it is not in the
      JSON envelope and two earlier revisions of this AC got the stream and the wording wrong:
      `run_differs.py:270-283` branches on
      `skip_invariant_filing = (not persist) or bool(filter_local_ids)`:
        * DRY-RUN takes the SKIP branch — `persist` is False because `MODE_CAPS[DRY_RUN] == 0`
          (`reconcile.py:218-222`) — and prints to STDERR (so no-write mode keeps STDOUT a pure
          JSON payload):
              invariants: skipped (no-write mode, <N> issues in snapshot)
          There is NO `scanned=` line in this mode at all.
        * A FILTERED pass — what the mutation cells use — hits the SAME skip branch (the gate is
          `(not persist) or bool(filter_local_ids)`) and prints
          `invariants: skipped (filtered pass, <N> issues in snapshot)` to STDERR.
        * The `scanned=<N> filed=<M> (cap=5)` line on STDOUT is emitted ONLY by an UNFILTERED
          WRITING pass — which this plan never runs (see the scoping note: unfiltered passes are
          dry-run only). It is documented here so a future reader does not go looking for that
          line in this suite's output and conclude something is broken when it is simply absent.
      Do not read `.scanned` from the envelope; there is no such key. The sibling `filed` counts
      INVARIANT-VIOLATION tickets, not tickets filed from DC issues, so `filed=0` is not evidence
      about inbound either way.
- [x] the scrub matches `.bridge_state*` as a GLOB and a test asserts ZERO binding or snapshot
      artifacts survive anywhere in the copied tree — derived by enumerating the tree, not from a
      hardcoded list
- [x] a test asserts the `.bridge_state*` scrub is COMPLETE — nothing matching `.bridge_state*`
      survives anywhere under the copied tracker dir, so a partially-scrubbed tree fails the job.
      NOT "the copied store holds no production Jira key reference", which an earlier draft required
      and which is MECHANICALLY UNACHIEVABLE: ticket event files under `.tickets-tracker/`
      legitimately embed `jira_key` values from prior Cloud syncs, the scrub correctly leaves that
      historical data intact (only BINDINGS drive remote writes — `binding_store.py:113`), so a
      whole-tree scan for production keys would ALWAYS hit and could never pass
- [x] the first pass plans EXACTLY ZERO deletion mutations AND EXACTLY ZERO outbound UPDATE
      mutations, both read from the `--mode dry-run` JSON envelope on stdout (the no-write branch at
      `__main__.py:445-452` is the one that emits JSON; writing modes emit only an `OK:` line, so
      dry-run is what makes these counts observable at all).
      **THE EXACT KEYS, so the assertion needs no guesswork.** The envelope is the whole result
      dict (`reconcile.py:690-709`). The per-mutation plan is the top-level `plan` array, built by
      `_build_plan_entries` (`reconcile_helpers.py:450-480`), whose entries are exactly
      `{direction, action, target, local_id}`. `direction` is `MutationDirection` (`"inbound"` |
      `"outbound"`) and `action` is `MutationAction` (`"create"` | `"update"` | `"delete"` |
      `"probe"` | `"clean_label"` | `"repair_property"` | `"conflict"`) — both `StrEnum`, so they
      serialize as those literal strings (`mutation.py:17-29`). The two assertions are therefore:
          jq -e '[.plan[] | select(.action == "delete")] | length == 0'
          jq -e '[.plan[] | select(.direction == "outbound" and .action == "update")] | length == 0'
      Read the envelope from STDOUT ONLY: the human-readable `OK: dry-run computed …` line goes to
      STDERR precisely so it cannot corrupt the JSON, so the test must not merge the two streams.
      **BOTH COUNTS ARE ZERO, and an earlier draft's rationale for a non-zero tolerance was
      MECHANICALLY WRONG — corrected here from the code rather than softened.** That draft said
      `< 10` outbound UPDATEs independently detects a surviving `prev_snapshot.json` while the
      deletion count stays at a reassuring zero. It cannot. `outbound_differ.py:518-520` branches
      on `binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id)`: `None` routes to the CREATE path, so an UPDATE is
      only ever emitted for a ticket that HAS a binding. The scrub removes `bindings.json`, so no
      ticket has one, so a `prev_snapshot.json` that survives on its own produces NO outbound
      updates whatsoever — the assertion it was supposed to catch that failure with is blind to it.
      What the two assertions actually do:
        * ZERO deletions catches a surviving `bindings.json` — its production keys do n … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: J11 — prove the epic's headline live: real store copy, comprehensive DC mutations, hard isolation

baseline.description:
## Context

Mutation testing should protect changed behavioral cores, but the historical whole-file counts are stale. A pinned mutmut 3.7.0 probe found 814 mutants in `signing.py` versus 491 in the old record, including both equivalent survivors and real contract gaps. Enforcing the old ceilings would block unrelated work; accepting all current survivors would normalize defects. The approved rollout therefore starts with evidence gathering and promotes each shard only when its results and runtime justify stronger enforcement.

## Plan

Use `.github/mutation-shards.toml` as the sole source for shard mappings, reviewed equivalent fingerprints, explicit timeout inputs, and an explicit per-shard enforcement mode:

- `advisory`: run head mutation evidence and publish every outcome. Existing survivors, `no tests`, and timeouts are nonblocking mutation-quality findings. Missing, zero-mutant, incomplete, or unrecognized evidence blocks, as do configuration, selection, execution, and artifact-contract failures, because usable evidence was not produced.
- `ratchet`: compare fresh base/head archives. For AST-identical functions, preserve unchanged legacy survivors and `no tests` outcomes. Block killed mutants that disappear or become survived, timed out, incomplete, or `no tests`; block new survivors, timeouts, and incomplete statuses. Report newly introduced `no tests` without blocking because mutmut cannot reliably attribute subprocess tests. Added or edited functions must kill every mutant unless a survivor matches an individually reviewed equivalent fingerprint; `no tests` remains report-only in ratchet.
- `strict`: apply the changed-function rule to the entire shard. Every mutant must be killed or individually fingerprinted as equivalent; `no tests`, timeouts, incomplete statuses, and zero mutants block. Strict promotion therefore requires direct in-process mutation coverage.

Start all legacy shards as advisory. Promote a shard to ratchet only after three successful base/head pilot runs show stable mappings and a maximum runtime of 24 minutes or less inside its 30-minute job. If a shard cannot meet that threshold, narrow it to proven function patterns before promotion. Promote it to strict only after legacy non-killed outcomes are remediated or individually reviewed. Mode changes are small manifest reviews; there is no fuzzy severity classification.

A selector inspects `HEAD^..HEAD`, including both sides of renames. Mapped source, test, or support changes select their shards; mutation-infrastructure changes select all. Unmapped changed Python tests are reported as advisory findings. Unresolved refs or diffs fail; an empty selection is an explicit successful skip. The reusable workflow emits selector JSON and creates one matrix job per selected shard, so every shard has its own 30-minute cap. Advisory evaluates head only; ratchet evaluates fresh base and head archives; strict evaluates complete head evidence plus the regression evidence required by the driver.

For each archive the driver synthesizes `[tool.mutmut]` from the canonical manifest before execution. The repository does not retain a second global `[tool.mutmut]` shard mapping. The manifest pins `timeout_constant = 1.0` and `timeout_multiplier = 15.0`; mutmut therefore gives each mutant a wall limit of `(estimated selected-test runtime + 1 second) * 15`, while the workflow independently caps the shard job at 30 minutes. Each job uses Python 3.12, pinned `mutmut==3.7.0`, `--max-children 1`, and selected clean-test preflight. Dependency downloads may be cached; mutation verdict state may not. Gerrit checks out the exact patchset and includes mutation in `vote.needs`; the push/PR lane mirrors it. A weekly/manual sweep selects every shard through the same selector and matrix.

Mutation-result reruns are diagnostic only and cannot turn red green. Only independently identified setup failures may retry. Raw logs, survivor diffs and fingerprints, and a structured summary publish for every driver outcome. Documentation describes the live manifest policy and promotion process and removes stale score or budget tables. A contract test reads the documentation, asserts the required policy sections and mode names, and asserts the historical score-table heading is absent. The existing two-vote rollback runbook remains the emergency recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Selection maps changed source, test, support, and global inputs to the expected shard set.
- [x] Selection keeps both sides of renames and deletions, reports unmatched Python tests, returns an explicit empty selection, fails unresolved refs, and emits selector JSON for targeted or all-shard runs.
- [x] Manifest loading accepts only `advisory`, `ratchet`, or `strict`, emits the pinned timeout values into each archive config, and no duplicate repository mutmut mapping remains.
- [x] Advisory returns success for survived, `no tests`, and timeout mutation-quality findings while returning failure for missing, zero-mutant, incomplete, or unrecognized evidence and configuration or execution errors.
- [x] Ratchet preserves unchanged legacy survivors and `no tests` and reports newly introduced `no tests` without blocking.
- [x] Ratchet blocks killed regressions, missing killed mutants, new survivors, timeouts, and incomplete statuses; added or edited functions require killed mutants or individually reviewed equivalent fingerprints except that `no tests` is report-only.
- [x] Strict requires every mutant to be killed or individually fingerprinted and blocks every `no tests`, timeout, incomplete status, and zero-mutant run.
- [x] Execution uses fresh archives, restores no verdict cache, pins runtime and concurrency, runs clean-test preflight, generates archive-local config, and always writes structured evidence.
- [x] Workflows use selector-derived per-shard matrix jobs with a 30-minute limit each, exact Gerrit patchset checkout, `vote.needs`, push/PR parity, weekly/manual all-shard selection, cancellation, and always-published artifacts.
- [x] A real compact-policy smoke run passes from fresh base/head archives.
- [x] The documentation contract test proves the phased modes, deterministic promotion evidence, false-positive policy, cadence, manifest authority, and absence of stale score or budget tables.

## Verification

    pytest -q tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
    python scripts/mutation_gate.py smoke --shard compact-policy --base HEAD^ --head HEAD
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    make config-check
    make lint
    make typecheck

## Primary evidence

Current primary-source examples: Instructor uses a pinned bounded shard with explicit exceptions; DataDog maps changed tests to source and compares base/head; PostHog gates a targeted PR shard; Trailmark cancels superseded runs and always reports; GeoParquet schedules broad mutation, fails on missing evidence, retries setup only, and publishes artifacts. The pinned mutmut 3.7.0 probe verifies `run --help` exposes `--max-children`; `configuration.py` defaults and fingerprints `timeout_constant=1.0` and `timeout_multiplier=15.0`; `__main__.py` derives the wall limit from those values, maps exit codes to every consumed status, and produces survivor output with `difflib.unified_diff`. The real repository probe and corrections are recorded in concise ticket comments.
