# J4 — Pin a `UserIdentityModel` contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

User identity is the second real Cloud/DC difference. Jira Cloud identifies users by opaque `accountId` (username and userkey were removed for GDPR); Data Center identifies them by `name`. This leaks into two places in the Cloud adapter: `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee`, which returns `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` and encodes the 3-state account-resolution fast-path the core diff consults (ADR 0035 §(d) canonical-comparison corollary), and the transport's create/update assignee payload shape.

PR #120 handled this by copying `resolve_assignee` and hardcoding `is_account_id=False`, and its copy consulted `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` — an attribute nothing ever sets, so its entire authoritative branch was unreachable and DC would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. That is not a cosmetic bug: a permanently non-authoritative assignee resolution makes the outbound diff re-emit assignee changes it can never converge, which is the churn class epic `ace2` was created to fix.

## Approach

Define a `UserIdentityModel` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `resolve(local_value, remote_identity)` returning the existing `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` tuple, and `to_payload(value)` returning the deployment's assignee field shape. Two implementations: `AccountIdIdentity` (Cloud — the current behavior verbatim, `{"accountId": …}`) and `NameIdentity` (DC — resolves through the DC user-search endpoint, `{"name": …}`).

`NameIdentity` performs a **real** lookup against DC's user-search endpoint rather than echoing the local value, so it can return `authoritative=True` and the diff converges. Its resolver is injected at construction from the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], not discovered via `getattr`, so there is no unreachable branch.

**Alternative rejected:** DC returns the local value with `authoritative=False` always (PR #120's effective behavior). It compiles and passes shallow tests while guaranteeing assignee-diff churn on every pass.

**Alternative rejected:** normalizing both to a single "user reference" string. The core diff's 3-state fast-path genuinely needs to know whether the value is an accountId, so flattening it would push the branch back into core.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — Cloud constructed with `AccountIdIdentity`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_model.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier with a stateful fake resolver for the lookup (the irreducible external boundary), plus a shared contract test over both implementations, since the 3-state contract must hold identically for each.

- shared contract, parameterized over both models: an empty local value yields
  `("", False, <model default>)`; a value that resolves to the SAME identity the remote already has yields
  `(None, True, …)` (converged, nothing to emit); a value resolving to a different identity yields that
  identity with `authoritative=True`.
- Cloud-specific: the resolved value is an accountId and `is_account_id is True`; payload is `{"accountId": …}`.
- DC-specific: the resolved value is a username and `is_account_id is False`; payload is `{"name": …}`.
- failure path: an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (the neutral base at
  `_backend.py:48`) rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value.
- regression oracle for PR #120's defect: a test asserts that for a resolvable assignee, DC returns
  `authoritative=True` — this test fails against the `getattr`-based implementation.
- contrast case: an unassigned local value yields the documented desired-unassigned state, not a lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test covers all three resolution states for both identity models
- [ ] a test asserts DC returns `authoritative=True` for a resolvable assignee (the anti-churn oracle)
- [ ] a test asserts an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for both models
- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` returns nothing — no `getattr`-discovered collaborator anywhere
- [ ] J1's pinned Cloud assignee behavior is unchanged (`make test` green with those assertions unmodified)
baseline.summary: J4 — pin a UserIdentityModel contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## What

Introduce the low-level **bare-ref CAS lock primitive** the reconciler pass-lock and phase-gate
will sit on. Ref -> blob, so it never lives in the tickets working tree and is never union-merged.
No reconciler wiring yet (C3). Also **prove the remote feasibility** the whole design rests on.

- **AC0 feasibility spike (do this first — it gates the rest):** prove a non-branch
  `refs/reconciler/*` ref pointing at a **blob** round-trips (push + fetch) through the `origin`
  GitHub remote using the CI `GITHUB_TOKEN` (contents:write). If GitHub rejects it, fall back to
  ref -> tiny-commit and record that in the ADR (fallback fully specified under Design decisions).
  Document the working refspec.
- New module `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` exposing `acquire`/`release`/`read`
  over a configurable ref name (`refs/reconciler/lock`, `refs/reconciler/gate` share one schema).
- **Blob = newline-terminated UTF-8 JSON** `{holder, lease_secs, heartbeat_ns, fence}`, clock from
  `time.time_ns()` (NOT `rebar._store.hlc` — that fcntl cache orders ticket events, wrong tool).
  `heartbeat_ns` is the acquisition/renew anchor; `fence` is a monotonic **progress-witness /
  generation counter** (seeded to 0 on first acquire; C2 increments it on renew/steal) — not a full
  fencing token. Decode of a corrupt/partial/empty blob **fails closed**: `read` raises a named
  `RefLockCorruptError` and callers treat "cannot parse" as HELD, never free.
- **Blob creation:** `git hash-object -w --stdin` plants the blob and yields the OID, THEN
  `git update-ref <ref> <oid> <old>`: **create-only CAS acquire** uses old = 40 zeros; **release
  deletes the ref** (`git update-ref -d <ref> <old-oid>`) with old = the exact observed OID. A
  release whose CAS sees a different oid (someone else now owns it) is a benign **idempotent success**,
  not an error.
- **Reuse the real CAS helper** `_cas_advance_with_retry` (`_advisory_lock.py:447-487`), NOT a
  second primitive. Its discriminator `_is_cas_mismatch` (`_advisory_lock.py:415`, hard-coding
  `'refs/heads/tickets'` at line 425) is **generalized to accept the ref name** so a CAS exit-128 on
  `refs/reconciler/*` is classified correctly (exact seam under Design decisions). Reuse, do not
  duplicate the classifier.
- **Acquire vs release retry semantics differ** (so the reused retry loop must be told which path it
  is on): a create-only **acquire** CAS exit-128 means "lock already held" — definitive, **not
  retried**. A **release** CAS exit-128 (ref already gone / owned by another) is a benign **idempotent
  success**, not retried. **Steal**-CAS (C2) exit-128 is the single-winner race — the loser stops and
  does not re-acquire. Only genuinely transient CAS races are retried via `_cas_advance_with_retry`.
- No lease-expiry/steal logic here (that is C2); a plain `acquire` fails if the ref already exists.
- Add structured log emission for acquire-failure (already held) and release on a stale oid.
- Record the bare-ref-lock design decision (schema, CAS contract, remote refspec, operator runbook)
  in a new ADR under `docs/adr/` (extended by later children).

**Why a ref lock at all (vs the workflow's `concurrency:` group in `reconcile-bridge.yml`)?**
GitHub Actions `concurrency:` only serializes runs *within one repo's workflow*; a manually-invoked
pass, a cron on a different runner, or a second clone bypasses it entirely. The ref lock is a
cross-invocation, workflow-independent guard anchored on the shared remote — the workflow group and
the ref lock are complementary, not redundant.

## Design decisions (resolves plan-review ambiguities; binding on the implementation)

1. **`_is_cas_mismatch` seam (backward-compatible).** Add an optional `ref_name: str =
   "refs/heads/tickets"` parameter; the default preserves every existing call site verbatim. Thread
   the ref name through the one internal use (`_advisory_lock.py:469`) and update the one external
   call site (`_advisory_lock.py:585`) to pass `ref_name="refs/heads/tickets"` explicitly. No new
   shared module: `_ref_lock.py` imports `_cas_advance_with_retry` / `_is_cas_mismatch` from its
   sibling `_advisory_lock.py` (two call sites is below rule-of-three; C4 leaves these helpers in
   place). The coupling is documented in the ADR.
2. **Three distinct exit-128 outcomes without duplicating the classifier.** Factor a
   `_cas_once(...) -> bool` helper (True = CAS succeeded; False = CAS old-oid mismatch; re-raises any
   non-mismatch `CalledProcessError`). `_cas_advance_with_retry` becomes `_cas_once` in the retry
   loop (behaviour unchanged). `acquire` maps False -> raise `RefLockHeldError` (definitive, no
   retry); `release` maps False -> return (idempotent success); C2's steal maps False -> "lost the
   race", stop.
3. **`RefLockCorruptError(ValueError)`** is defined in `_ref_lock.py` and raised by `read` on any of:
   empty / non-UTF-8 bytes; invalid JSON; a missing `holder`/`lease_secs`/`heartbeat_ns`/`fence`
   field; `fence` not a non-negative int; `lease_secs` not a positive number. It carries the raw
   bytes for debugging. Callers treat it (and any read failure) as HELD, never free.
4. **`fence` in C1.** `acquire` writes `fence=0` unconditionally (create-only CAS guarantees no prior
   blob survived); `release` neither reads nor mutates `fence` (it deletes the ref). All `fence`
   increment / renew / steal logic is C2.
5. **Distributed CAS via an optional `remote`.** `acquire`/`release`/`read` take an optional
   `remote` argument. When `remote is None` (unit tests / local) they use a pure local
   `git update-ref` CAS. When a remote is given they use the network-CAS equivalent —
   `git fetch <remote> <ref>:<ref>` to sync, then `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<old-oid>`
   (explicit lease-ref form, never bare) — which is exactly the old-oid CAS on the authoritative
   remote. The reconciler passes `remote="origin"`; wiring that call and the workflow fetch refspec
   are C3. AC0 proves the remote path's refspec.
6. **Subprocess timeouts.** Every `subprocess.run` in `_ref_lock.py` sets `timeout=` — 5 s for local
   object/ref ops, 30 s for remote push/fetch — and a timeout raises `RefLockTimeoutError` (a
   fail-closed condition; callers treat it as "cannot determine state" = HELD). Values recorded in
   the ADR.
7. **AC0 ref->tiny-commit fallback (fully specified).** If GitHub rejects a blob-pointing ref, the
   ref points instead at a tiny commit whose tree holds a single `lock.json` with the same schema;
   `read` retrieves it via `git cat-file blob <ref>:lock.json` (commit case) vs `git cat-file blob
   <ref>` (blob case), selected by `git cat-file -t <ref>`; `git hash-object -w` still plants the
   payload. The CAS (create-only / observed-oid) is identical. The ADR records which path GitHub
   accepted.
8. **Operator break-glass.** The ADR carries a runbook: clear a wedged lock with
   `git push origin :refs/reconciler/lock` (remote) or `git update-ref -d refs/reconciler/lock`
   (local). C2's lease expiry makes this rarely necessary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC0: a proving command/test demonstrates `refs/reconciler/*` (ref -> blob) push+fetch through
      the `origin` GitHub remote with the CI token; the working refspec (and the fully-specified
      ref->commit fallback) is documented in the ADR.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` provides `acquire`/`release`/`read` over a
      configurable ref and an optional `remote`; acquire is create-only CAS (old=zeros), release is
      observed-oid CAS; blob is created via `git hash-object -w` before `update-ref` / push.
- [ ] Blob is UTF-8 JSON `{holder, lease_secs, heartbeat_ns, fence}` (`time.time_ns()`, `fence=0` on
      acquire); `read` of a corrupt/empty blob raises `RefLockCorruptError` and callers treat it as
      HELD (fail-closed), never free; the corrupt conditions in Design decision 3 are each covered.
- [ ] The CAS reuses `_cas_advance_with_retry` / `_is_cas_mismatch` (`_advisory_lock.py:447-487,415`)
      via the `_cas_once` seam; `_is_cas_mismatch` gains a `ref_name` param defaulting to
      `refs/heads/tickets` (existing call sites unchanged); acquire exit-128 ("held") is NOT retried,
      release exit-128 is idempotent success, and C2's steal exit-128 is single-winner-loss.
- [ ] Subprocess calls in `_ref_lock.py` carry timeouts (5 s local / 30 s remote) and a timeout
      raises `RefLockTimeoutError` (treated as HELD).
- [ ] Structured logs are emitted for acquire-already-held and stale-oid release.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: acquire on a free ref; second concurrent acquire fails (already exists);
      `read` on present vs absent ref (defined contract); release requires the correct old oid and a
      stale-oid release is idempotent success; corrupt-blob decode fails closed; and a parametrized
      regression that `_is_cas_mismatch` still classifies exit-128 on `refs/heads/tickets` unchanged
      AND classifies exit-128 on `refs/reconciler/lock`.
- [ ] The bare-ref-lock decision (schema, CAS contract, remote refspec, fallback, timeouts, operator
      runbook) is captured in a new `docs/adr/` entry. Non-integration suite green.
baseline.summary: Ref-lock primitive: bare-ref CAS acquire/release + lock-blob schema

baseline.description:
## Problem

`_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` maps the `gemini` prefix to the provider name `google_genai`, but no runtime registry knows that name, so any bare `gemini-*` model id resolves to a provider that cannot be constructed and dies at call time.

Reproduced on this base (worktree at `origin/main`, `d72c477`):

    infer_provider('gemini-2.5-pro')                 -> 'google_genai'
    'google_genai' in _pydantic_ai_known_providers() -> False
    'google_genai' in KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES           -> False
    ProviderSession(LLMConfig())._builders           -> ['anthropic', 'bedrock']
    ProviderSession.is_resolvable('google_genai')    -> False
    ProviderSession.provider_factory('google_genai') -> LLMConfigError:
        unknown provider 'google_genai'; registered providers: ['anthropic', 'bedrock']

pydantic-ai 1.107.1 recognises `google`, `google-cloud`, `google-gla`, `google-vertex`, `vertexai` and `gateway/google-cloud`. It does NOT recognise `google_genai`.

### Which path actually breaks

There are two composition sites, and only one of them is broken — this matters for where the test goes:

- `anthropic_model._pai_model()` (used by `runner.run()` for a BARE `cfg.model`) passes the inferred
  name through a second, private table, `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX`, which happens to translate
  `google_genai -> google-gla`. That path accidentally survives.
- `model_classes._resolve_target()` — the model-class / ladder path (`trivial = { model =
  "gemini-2.5-pro" }`, fallback chains, `resolve_model_string`) — uses `infer_provider`'s result
  VERBATIM and composes `google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro`. `_pai_model` then returns that string
  unchanged because it is already qualified, and provider construction raises. This is the
  end-to-end failure and is what the RED test must exercise.

The failure is at CALL time, not config time: an operator who configures a `gemini-*` model gets a plausible-looking config that fails only when a gate actually runs.

## Design decision

**Map `gemini` to `google`.** `google` is pydantic-ai's current canonical provider name for the Gemini Developer API; `google:gemini-*` ids appear directly in `known_model_names()`, and `google` is already a member of both `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` and `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()`, so `ProviderSession.is_resolvable('google')` is True and the model is left on the existing deferred lazy-string path (rebar registers no builder for it, exactly as for `openai` without a `base_url`). Building it still requires the optional `google-genai` package, and pydantic-ai's own ImportError already names the extra to install — that is the same contract every other delegate provider has, not a new failure mode.

Rejected alternatives:

- `google-gla` / `google-vertex` / `vertexai` — resolvable, but pydantic-ai 1.107.1 emits a
  deprecation warning for these prefixes and removes them in v2.0, so choosing one would
  re-introduce a scheduled break.
- Dropping the `gemini` prefix entirely so a bare `gemini-*` id fails at config time — this yields a
  WORSE outcome for an operator who has the Google extra installed: a model that pydantic-ai can
  serve today would stop being usable via a bare id.
- Adding `google_genai` to `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` (what 7b22's plan proposes for a back-compat test)
  — rejected: it makes a name that neither pydantic-ai nor rebar can build a first-class member, and
  `ProviderSession` would still refuse it. 7b22 must not lock that choice in.

`anthropic_model._PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` is deliberately NOT touched. Its `google_genai` key becomes unreachable from inference but is still a valid explicit-`model_provider` back-compat shim, and `capabilities.py` documents its `google-gla` output as load-bearing. Changing it is a separate concern from making the inference table agree with the registries.

## Changes

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES`: `("gemini", "google_genai")` becomes
  `("gemini", "google")`; update the two comments that restate the old mapping (the
  `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` preamble and the `LLMConfig.model_provider` comment).
- `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` — replace `test_the_inference_path_is_not_validated`
  (which pins the defect as deliberately out of scope) with the fixed expectation; add the
  whole-table invariant and the regression pins.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py` — `test_infer_provider` pins
  `infer_provider("gemini-2.5-pro") == "google_genai"`; update to the resolvable name.

## Test plan

1. RED first, on the end-to-end mechanism: assert
   `model_classes._resolve_target("gemini-2.5-pro", None)` composes a provider string that
   `ProviderSession(LLMConfig()).is_resolvable(...)` accepts. On unfixed code this fails with
   `google_genai`.
2. AC2 invariant, parameterized over the WHOLE `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` table (not just the gemini
   entry): every mapped provider name is in `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` or in
   `ProviderSession._builders`, so a future added prefix cannot reintroduce the class of defect.
3. AC3 regression pins: `claude-* -> anthropic`, `gpt-*/chatgpt-* -> openai`, an already-qualified
   `google-gla:gemini-2.5-flash` still passes through unchanged, an unknown id still infers `None`.
4. Mutation-check in both directions: revert the one-line production change and confirm the new
   tests go RED; restore and confirm GREEN.
5. Gates by exit code: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default `pytest` selection.

## Risk and rollback

One-line data change in a lookup table plus test updates; no control flow changes. Blast radius is limited to model ids that begin with `gemini`, which today cannot work at all. Rollback is reverting the single commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A bare `gemini-*` model id resolves, through both `infer_provider` and
  `model_classes._resolve_target`, to a provider name that `ProviderSession.is_resolvable` accepts.
- AC2: No value in `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` maps to a provider name absent from both
  `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` and `ProviderSession._builders`. A test pins this for the WHOLE
  table, not just the gemini entry, so the next added prefix cannot reintroduce the class of defect.

baseline.description:
# Doctor: mapping-config diagnostics with offline-always / live-drift-degrades portability

## Context / Problem

The mapping seam (S1–S8) adds a hand-editable `[mapping]` config surface. Two failure classes need surfacing before a reconcile silently drifts:

- **Internally-invalid config** — already fail-closed via `MappingConfigError`: a non-integer
  `hierarchy` / malformed block fail at LOAD; out-of-vocabulary and unmapped-non-skipped values
  fail in the `config` resolvers. Doctor surfaces these as **error** findings.
- **Live drift** — internally valid but disagreeing with live Jira (a mapped status/type/link
  Jira dropped). Surface when Jira is reachable; degrade cleanly when not.

`rebar doctor` is the existing diagnostic home, so extend it. It must stay portable: it runs where the optional **`jira-datacenter`** extra is absent and no credentials are set — offline checks always run; the live-drift check degrades to an `unavailable` finding, mirroring `rebar metrics` (`docs/user-guide.md`).

## Approach

Add a mapping-diagnostics function to `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, wired into `scan`. Mapping findings go in their **own list** (as for scan-dirty/lock reports), are rendered and folded into the exit code, and kept **out of** `run_repair`'s iteration — so `doctor.scan()`'s blocking-edge finding contract (and `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`) is unchanged.

- **Offline checks (always run, stdlib-only, no Jira import):** first call
  `mapping_config.load_mapping_config` inside `try/except MappingConfigError` — a load-time
  failure (non-integer hierarchy, or a malformed axis/vocabulary block) becomes one **error**
  finding whose `detail` is the `MappingConfigError` message verbatim — it already frames the key
  in either prefix format (`[mapping.<where>]:` for axis/hierarchy/layer, `[mapping].<where>:`
  for vocabulary), so no brittle parsing — and the per-key pass is skipped. On a successful load, enumerate `config.projects` **union the default layer** and, per
  key, run the provider-neutral `config` resolvers — `effective_status_map`, `effective_type_map`,
  `assert_type_decisions_complete`, `effective_link_map` — which inject the built-in
  `MappingLayer` + `Capability`, import `mapping_config` lazily, and are stdlib-only at import
  (never `adapters.jira*`); a resolve-time `MappingConfigError` (out-of-vocabulary,
  unmapped-non-skipped) → an **error** finding naming the key (non-zero exit). On the same per-key pass, one genuinely *soft* problem — an all-empty `projects.<KEY>` block
  (likely a stub) — is a **warning** naming the key, not an error.
- **Live-drift check (best-effort, degrades):** run only when the `jira-datacenter` extra is
  importable — gated through `rebar._optional.capability_installed("jira_datacenter")` — AND
  credentials resolve. On the available path, reuse S8's read-only probe reader
  (`mapping_probe.build_probe`) and diff configured vs observed vocabulary, one finding per
  divergence on the axes the reader observes — **status, type, link** (a configured value absent
  from Jira's set).
  Hierarchy is deliberately **excluded** from the live diff: `build_probe` resolves Data Center,
  where `mapping_probe._hierarchy` is always empty (`hierarchyLevel` is Cloud-only) — so a
  hierarchy divergence is structurally undetectable here (offline hierarchy validity still
  covered above). When the
  extra is absent, OR the resolved PAT is empty (`JIRA_PAT` unset — `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings`
  returns `pat=""`), OR settings resolution raises `ConfigError` (fail-loud on a malformed
  `[tool.rebar.reconciler]`), OR the probe
  transport raises or times out (the probe call runs under a doctor-side bounded wall-clock
  timeout — a daemon worker thread with `result(timeout=…)`, bound a module constant (default
  10s), since S8's `build_client_from_settings` sets none; a timed-out thread is abandoned and
  doctor returns promptly with `unavailable`), emit a single `unavailable` finding
  ("live mapping-drift check skipped: <reason>") and return success — never raise. The Jira import
  and probe construction happen lazily behind the guard, wrapped so every degradation cause
  folds into the one `unavailable` finding.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — new mapping-diagnostics function (own findings list); the
  `capability_installed("jira_datacenter")` guard and lazy Jira import.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — document the offline error/warning findings and the `unavailable`
  live-drift convention.
- Reuses S1's `mapping_config` (via `config` resolvers) and S8's `mapping_probe.build_probe`.
- Out of scope: `--repair` for mapping config (report-only); Jira as a hard doctor dependency;
  the live-drift **true path against real Jira** — transport is S8's proven read-only probe
  reader (covered by S8), so this child proves the diff logic via an injected vocabulary and
  treats the real-transport path as not-applicable.

## Testing

- **Unit (offline tier), no Jira import:** temp config with (a) valid mapping → no findings;
  (b) each error-class problem — a load-time one in each message format (non-integer hierarchy
  `[mapping.<where>]:`, and a malformed vocabulary list `[mapping].<where>:`) and a resolve-time
  one (out-of-vocabulary value, unmapped-non-skipped type) → an **error** finding whose detail
  carries the key + non-zero exit; (c) an all-empty `projects.<KEY>` block → a **warning**. Asserts
  no `adapters.jira` import on this path. Oracle: finding list + exit code.
- **Unit (portability tier):** force the guard false (monkeypatch `capability_installed` for
  `"jira_datacenter"`) → exactly one `unavailable` finding, success exit, no Jira import. Oracle:
  the single finding + zero exit.
- **Unit (degradation causes):** guard true; drive each cause — empty resolved PAT, a
  `ConfigError` from settings resolution, and a slow/hanging probe reader exceeding the
  doctor-side timeout — each folds into one `unavailable` finding with the matching reason +
  success exit. Oracle: the finding + reason + zero exit.
- **Unit (live-drift tier), injected transport:** inject a fake probe reader whose vocabulary
  diverges on status, type, and link → one drift finding per divergence naming the axis + absent
  value. No live Jira. Oracle: the per-axis finding set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar doctor` on a valid `[mapping]` config with the `jira-datacenter` extra absent
  succeeds and emits exactly one `unavailable` live-drift finding — portability-tier test (guard
  forced false via `capability_installed`, no Jira import, zero exit).
- [x] Each offline error-class problem yields an **error** finding whose detail carries the key
  + non-zero exit: both load-error message formats (non-integer hierarchy `[mapping.<where>]:`
  and malformed vocabulary `[mapping].<where>:`) surfaced verbatim, plus the resolve-time errors
  (out-of-vocabulary value, unmapped-non-skipped type) reached by enumerating `config.projects`
  + the default layer per key — offline-tier test asserting the `MappingConfigError`-derived
  finding.
- [x] An all-empty `projects.<KEY>` stub yields a **warning** finding naming the key (not an
  error, not a non-zero exit) — offline-tier test.
- [x] Each degradation cause — extra absent, empty resolved PAT (`JIRA_PAT` unset), a
  `ConfigError` from settings resolution, and a slow/hanging probe exceeding the doctor-side
  timeout — folds into a single `unavailable` finding + reason + success exit — portability and
  degradation-cause tests.
- [x] With a fake probe reader injected, each configured-vs-observed divergence on status, type,
  and link yields a drift finding naming the axis + absent value — live-drift-tier test.
  Hierarchy is excluded by design (the reused Data Center probe never observes `hierarchyLevel`).
- [x] `docs/user-guide.md` documents the new mapping diagnostics.

All four tiers run in-process, no live Jira, no specific CI provider — satisfying `project.portability`.
baseline.summary: Doctor: mapping-config diagnostics with offline-always / live-drift-degrades portability

baseline.description:
## Problem
`git commit --amend -F <file>` (and `-m`) REPLACES the entire commit message, dropping the `Change-Id` trailer. Gerrit's `commit-msg` hook then stamps a NEW Change-Id, so the next push creates a SECOND Gerrit change instead of a new patchset on the existing one. The original change is left orphaned and must be abandoned by hand.

This happened TWICE in one session (2026-08-19), producing abandoned duplicates Gerrit 1921 and
1926. Both agents recovered — restored the original Change-Id, re-pushed as a new patchset, and
abandoned the duplicate — so the cost is cleanup and reviewer confusion rather than lost work.

## A hook CANNOT fix this — measured, not assumed
`prepare-commit-msg` looked like the natural home (this repo already uses it as a clone-local rail that blocks commits on `main`, and `--no-verify` does not bypass it). It does not work. Measured directly in a throwaway repo:

| invocation | hook receives |
|---|---|
| `git commit --amend --no-edit` | `source='commit'  sha='HEAD'` — detectable |
| `git commit --amend -F <file>` | `source='message' sha=''` — **identical to a fresh `-F` commit** |

Git does not tell the hook that an `-F` amend is an amend, so the hook cannot distinguish "amending, preserve the Change-Id" from "new commit, stamp one". Gerrit's own `commit-msg` hook is no help either: by design it only ADDS a Change-Id when absent and does nothing when one is present.

Nor does the server catch it. Gerrit rejects the same Change-Id in multiple changes and multiple Change-Id lines, but a commit carrying a FRESH Change-Id is indistinguishable from a legitimate new change — which is exactly why both incidents produced silent duplicates rather than a push rejection.

## How the Gerrit ecosystem actually solves it (prior art)
Every large Gerrit project removes the failure mode by ensuring contributors never hand-run `git commit --amend` + `git push refs/for/*`:

| project | wrapper |
|---|---|
| Go | `git codereview change` — creates a new commit, or amends the existing one PRESERVING the Change-Id |
| OpenStack / OpenDev | `git-review` (`git review`) |
| Android | `repo upload` |
| Chromium | `git cl upload` (depot_tools) |

The documented backstop is a prohibition: OpenStack's contributor guide states plainly not to use `-m` to supply a commit message, because it overrides the previous message and regenerates the Change-Id. `-F` behaves identically.

**No major Gerrit project implements a hook or pre-push guard for this.** They make the failure UNREACHABLE rather than DETECTABLE.

## Scope
Follow the prior art. Add a thin wrapper and make it the documented path.

1. A `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` target (thin script if the Makefile recipe gets unwieldy) that
   amends HEAD with the contents of FILE while CARRYING FORWARD the existing `Change-Id` trailer
   from the current HEAD message. If HEAD has no Change-Id, it must fail loudly rather than
   silently amending — a missing trailer means the commit-msg hook is not installed, which is its
   own problem (`make hooks`).
2. Update `AGENTS.md` line ~280, which currently reads
   "Iterate on findings with `git commit --amend --no-edit` (keep the `Change-Id`) + re-push",
   to also name `make amend-msg FILE=…` as the path for a REWRITTEN message, and to state
   explicitly that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate change.

**EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — do not build:** a `pre-push` hook, a reflog-based Change-Id comparison, or any other novel guard. A reflog rail was designed and REJECTED for this ticket: no project in the ecosystem does it, so we would be maintaining a bespoke hook with no prior art to borrow from when it misfires, to detect a failure the wrapper prevents outright.

## Why this matters more here than upstream
Those projects' contributors are humans using `$EDITOR`, where the pull toward `-m`/`-F` is weak. rebar's contributors are largely AGENTS composing raw git commands, for whom `-F` is the natural way to write a multi-line message without shell-quoting pain. The remedy transfers; the incentive to bypass it is stronger, which is why the wrapper must be the DOCUMENTED DEFAULT rather than merely available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` amends HEAD with FILE's contents and the resulting commit
      carries the SAME `Change-Id` as before the amend — proven by a test that captures the
      Change-Id before and after and asserts equality.
- [x] The same test proves the naive form still loses it: `git commit --amend -F <file>` on the
      same fixture yields a DIFFERENT (or absent) Change-Id. Without this contrast the first
      criterion can pass vacuously.
- [x] `make amend-msg` fails loudly and non-zero when HEAD carries no `Change-Id`, rather than
      producing a commit that will be stamped with a fresh one.
- [x] `AGENTS.md` names `make amend-msg` as the path for a rewritten commit message and states
      that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate Gerrit change.
- [x] No `pre-push` hook, reflog comparison, or other guard is added.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Provenance
Filed 2026-08-19 after two duplicate changes (Gerrit 1921, 1926) in one session. The hook-based approach was investigated and empirically disproved before filing; the wrapper approach follows Go, OpenStack, Android and Chromium practice.
baseline.summary: Add make amend-msg wrapper so amending a commit cannot drop its Change-Id

## Why
S2 (urge-brook-plume) named a `merge_change_409_guard` journald event in its plan's What section for the review-bot's merge-change path. S2 implemented the guard STRUCTURALLY — a merge revision (>= 2 parents) cannot use Gerrit's bare `/patch` endpoint (it returns HTTP 409 'Revision has too many parents'), so voter.review_and_vote branches on `is_merge` BEFORE any diff fetch and routes merges through the auto-merge-delta path (`_assemble_merge_diff`) instead of `gc.get_patch` (src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:393 vs :426; unit test asserts get_patch_calls==0 on merges). BUT the named observability event was NEVER emitted (`grep merge_change_409_guard src/` = 0 hits) — so the guard fires silently. S2's completion verifier flagged this as a valid gap; it was deferred to this follow-up.

## What
- Emit a structured `merge_change_409_guard` journald event (via the voter's `_emit`, same shape as `merge_detection`/`merge_change_review`) at the point the code enters the is_merge branch and deliberately avoids the bare `/patch` (which would 409 on a merge). Carry change_id, revision_id, parent_count.
- It fires ONLY on merges (is_merge True) — distinct from `merge_detection` (which logs is_merge for EVERY change).
- Document it in infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md's merge-change ops signals list.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `merge_change_409_guard` structured event is emitted when the review-bot takes the merge path (is_merge, avoiding the bare /patch 409)
- [ ] The event does NOT fire on a non-merge change (guard is merge-specific)
- [ ] A unit test asserts the event fires on a merge and is absent on a non-merge (src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py path via tests/unit/test_review_bot.py)
- [ ] Documented in infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md merge-change ops signals
baseline.summary: Emit merge_change_409_guard event on merge-change 409 guard path (S2 follow-up)

## Context / Problem

Bedrock Converse `outputConfig` (native structured output) is rejected CLIENT-SIDE by the currently locked botocore 1.40.61 (`ParamValidationError` before any network call — measured, E1 experiment recorded on the selection bug ticket). The wire feature needs botocore >= 1.43. The lock sits at 1.40.61 because of the declared extras diamond: `[eval]` -> inspect-ai -> aioboto3 -> aiobotocore caps `boto3 < 1.40.62`, while `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]` (pyproject.toml:250) wants newer; the `[tool.uv]` conflicts block (pyproject.toml, ~line 261) already forks eval vs bedrock/dev resolution to keep both installable.

## Approach

Add an explicit floor `botocore>=1.43.0` (and matching `boto3>=1.43.0`) alongside the `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]` dependency in pyproject.toml, then `uv lock`. Assumption stated as default: the existing conflict forks absorb the eval cap exactly as they do today (eval and bedrock never co-resolve); if the lock proves unresolvable, the fallback is scoping the floor to the bedrock-carrying extra only. No source change; the capability rows story is what makes the new wire feature reachable — this ticket is purely the SDK floor.

Purely mechanical dependency bump: no new testable behavior, so no Testing section (the existing suite gates regressions).

## Scope

- pyproject.toml — the floor declaration
- uv.lock — regenerated

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `uv lock` succeeds with the existing `[tool.uv]` conflicts block unchanged — checked by
      the lock command exiting 0 in-session.
- [x] The dev/bedrock resolution contains botocore >= 1.43 — checked by `uv tree` (or
      `uv pip list`) output recorded in the commit/ticket showing the resolved version.
- [x] The eval fork still resolves (`uv sync --extra eval` exits 0) — checked in-session.
- [x] `make test` passes on the new lock — checked by the CI-gating suite before push.
baseline.summary: Raise the Bedrock SDK floor to botocore >= 1.43 for outputConfig

baseline.description:
## Why this exists

Surfaced while diagnosing 7084 (store write-lock hold duration). Two questions the operator asked led here: whether each worktree could get its own clone of the `tickets` branch and let git resolve on push, and how compaction conflicts could self-heal given that compaction is deterministic.

**What we found about today's behaviour.** Three mechanisms cover parallel clients, and only two are policies:
1. **Event appends need no policy.** The tickets-branch `.gitattributes` says so outright — 'uuid-named ticket dirs never collide, so they never need a merge policy'. Files are `{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json` under per-ticket dirs, so concurrent appends are disjoint paths that merge trivially.
2. **Shared mutable root files use `merge=ours`** (`.bridge_state/* merge=ours`), with the committed rationale that these are 'per-pass derived CACHES the reconciler rebuilds, not ticket events' — keep ours, let the next pass rebuild the loser. The same file records that `merge=union` is WRONG there because it line-unions JSON into invalid JSON.
3. **Compaction renames have NO handling at all.** No rename/`.retired` logic exists anywhere in the push path. Locally the race is PREVENTED rather than resolved: every worktree resolves to ONE store via `lock.canonical_tracker`, so the write lock serialises all local writers. ACROSS CLONES (the GitHub Actions reconciler vs a local agent) a concurrent compaction of the same ticket lands in the push path's terminal branch — '# Real content conflict — retry won't help, but continue so _MAX_RETRIES is honored' — which aborts the merge, warns, exhausts retries, and leaves the push PENDING for a human.

This is also why the per-worktree-clone idea was rejected: it would convert case 3 from a PREVENTED race into an UNHANDLED one, at the frequency of every pair of parallel agents rather than the rare cross-clone case.

## The idea

The SNAPSHOT and its `.retired` renames are DERIVED from the event log; the event log is the source of truth. A derived cache does not need to be merged — it needs to be REGENERATED.

On a compaction conflict:
* take the UNION of live (non-retired) events from both sides,
* DISCARD both snapshots,
* let the next compaction pass rebuild from the merged event set.

**Why this is provably lossless:** uncompacted state is always semantically valid — compaction is a space optimisation, not a state change. So the resolution direction is always RESURRECT, never RETIRE. The worst outcome is redundant work on a later pass; the failure mode is disk, never correctness.

This is the same policy already applied to `.bridge_state/*`, applied to the one remaining artifact in the store that is not conflict-free by construction.

## Prior art (researched 2026-08-07)

**git-bug — the closest domain match — solved this by removing the need to merge, not by merging better.** It is a distributed, offline-first issue tracker embedded in git: the same shape as rebar (tickets in git, multiple clients, offline edits, sync by push/pull). It uses LAMPORT TIMESTAMPS plus an OPERATION-BASED data model so concurrent edits from multiple remotes merge without conflicts and without manual resolution, and it stores data as git OBJECTS under a ref namespace (`refs/bugs`) rather than worktree files — so git's file-merge semantics never apply. rebar is already most of the way there: append-only event log plus an HLC (same family as Lamport clocks), and ticket e3d0 already cites the 'git-bug operationPack pattern'. The SNAPSHOT is our only non-conflict-free artifact.

**Nix content-addressed derivations — the cautionary tale for the alternative we considered first.** Content-addressing the snapshot (naming it by a hash of the folded event set so identical folds collide harmlessly) was our initial preference. Nix's CA derivations (RFC 0062) make the same bet and remain EXPERIMENTAL and opt-in years later — stabilisation ~65% as of March 2026. The blockers transfer directly: determinism does not hold in practice ('ghc is deterministic only disabling the parallel building i.e. passing -j1'), and divergent realisations poison the cache — their handling 'just forbids fetching a path if the local system has a different realisation for the same drv output ... can result in a totally useless binary cache in some pathological cases'. That is our failure mode exactly: two byte-different artifacts each claiming to be the same logical snapshot, with NO RULE to choose between them, which is worse than the conflict because both look correct.

**Where content-addressing succeeds, nothing is ever merged.** Bazel's remote CAS, OCI layers and git's own object database are all content-addressed and all successful — and in every one the artifacts are IMMUTABLE and simply coexist. Content addressing solves IDENTITY and DEDUPLICATION, not CONFLICT RESOLUTION.

**Conclusion:** derived-cache regeneration is the primary move. Content-addressing the snapshot is a COMPLEMENTARY dedup win — it removes the spurious case (two clients folding an identical event set) but leaves the real one (divergent fold sets) untouched, since different inputs legitimately hash differently and both land.

## The hazard any design must respect

Resolution must be ATOMIC OVER THE PAIR — the SNAPSHOT together with its `.retired` renames. A per-file `merge=ours` would happily take OUR snapshot alongside THEIR retirements, dropping events our snapshot never folded. A `.gitattributes` line therefore CANNOT express this; it needs a custom merge driver or a post-merge repair that reasons about the pair.

## What a plan would need to establish

- Where the resolution lives: a custom git merge driver, or a post-merge repair step in the push/reconverge path.
- How a compaction conflict is reliably RECOGNISED as such, versus any other content conflict.
- How the live event set is reconstructed when both sides retired different subsets — including un-retiring events the other side folded that we did not.
- That the reducer tolerates a ticket with many events and NO snapshot (it should — that is simply the pre-compaction state), proven by test rather than assumed.
- The interaction with `compact.py:150`'s mid-retirement crash window (SNAPSHOT written, retirement incomplete) — whether the same recovery machinery covers both, since they are the same class of half-applied compaction.
- Whether CENTRALISING compaction to a single writer is cheaper than resolving the conflict at all, which would make this moot.
- Whether determinism is worth PROVING regardless (ordering, parallelism, float/dict serialisation), since `compact.py:138` already strips `updated_at` — one key is not a proof, and the answer gates whether content-addressing is worth adding as the complementary win.

## Note on urgency

Not urgent. The local race is prevented by the shared store and the write lock; only the cross-clone case is exposed, and it degrades to a pending push rather than data loss. This should be judged on its own merits, not as a prerequisite for 7084's lock-duration work (R1/R3/R5), which is independent.
baseline.summary: Treat the compaction SNAPSHOT as a derived cache: regenerate on conflict instead of merging it

baseline.description:
## Why
Compaction preserves folded events as `*.retired` (I1, epic b306) permanently, so tombstones + the whole per-event commit/tree history accumulate on `tickets`. This blocks health-lane bug `defensive-buckskin-rhino` (`a453-193b-2864-451b`): the blobless CI checkout pack is ~481 MiB vs a deliberate 100 MiB budget (`verify-identity.yml:47`). `git gc`/repack does NOT shrink it (proven). The only lever is reducing reachable commit/tree objects on `tickets` history — causally-safe history reclamation, which needs the causal-stability proof this epic owns.

## Operator decision (2026-08-24, comments)
**Option 2 (remote-anchored horizon) + stale-clone forced override**, N=30d; residual loss of a >N-day-drifted clone's divergent work is ACCEPTED.

## Design + proof (full detail in the DESIGN + PROOF comment)
Boundary C1–C5: an event is reclaimable iff (C1) folded by a committed SNAPSHOT, (C2) that fold reachable on the sync remote's `tickets` ref ≥ N days, (C3) stale clones (>N days) forced to reset to remote, (C4) its signature is carried in the SNAPSHOT `authorship_ledger` OR `identity.enforce_since` is re-anchored to grandfather it, (C5) no unfolded state depends on it (I9). Under C1–C5: no still-observable state changes, no signature verification breaks, no resurrection.

Measured (origin/tickets): 235,482 commits, 408,295 trees, ZERO blobs blobless; trees ≈95% of bytes; root tree 270 KB × 6,008 flat ticket dirs re-emitted per commit; ~69% derived enrichment/digest churn; ~14K commits/day.

## Quantified win — insufficient alone
`.retired` files are blobs; the guarded pack is blobless ⇒ `.retired` GC shrinks it ~0. The lever is collapsing per-event history into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints below the horizon. Max safe win N=30d ≈ 365–380 MiB; N=7d ≈ 200–215 MiB; ≤100 MiB needs an unsafe <4-day horizon. **A temporary budget-raise bridge (W3) is unavoidable**, paired with structural fixes (out of scope, `discovered_from` this epic): W1 batch the enrichment/digest write lane; W2 shard the flat ticket dirs to shrink root-tree churn.

## Mechanism (portable, out-of-band; NO CI-provider dependence)
Offline reclamation in a disposable clone (I9b isolation), never interactive, never under the store lock:
- **S1** remote-anchored eligibility — pure git reachability + timestamps.
- **S2** coalesce to a re-signed baseline checkpoint = compacted as-of-horizon state + carried authorship_ledger; re-anchor `enforce_since` to the baseline. Broadened from `.retired`-only to commit/tree reclamation.
- **S3** stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect.
- **S0** ADR: amend §I1 permanent-retention doctrine; prove I1–I9 under the horizon with the accepted >N-day loss.

## Feasibility (resolves the surfaced questions)
**Publish-swap = a per-backend adapter over ONE precondition ("replace published history iff remote unchanged since T0, else abort+retry"); no clone registry, no hold-open window (G6/T1/T3).** All clones auto-push to the ONE `sync.remote` (the single choke point). Adapter per backend: (a) git ref remotes (bare/GitHub/Gerrit) — `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/tickets:T0`, the same old→new ref CAS ADR 0031 uses. (b) S3 `git-remote-s3` backend (ADR 0093) has NO ref CAS — it stores bundle-per-push and its non-interactive auto-doctor (`s3_doctor.py`) folds divergent heads by lossless merge and NEVER discards a head, so a normally-pushed rewrite would be MERGED BACK (resurrected). So on S3 the reclaim is an EXCLUSIVE offline bundle-set replacement: under git-remote-s3's per-ref push-lock, enumerate bundles (`get_bundles_for_ref`), assert the head set == T0 (the CAS precondition), back up the bundle set to a rollback prefix, write ONE rewritten bundle and delete the originals — deliberately BYPASSING the auto-doctor. No acknowledged write is lost (a changed head set aborts+retries). Clients reconcile post-swap by EVENT-FILE REPLAY onto the baseline (append-only files, not history merge); >N-day offline clones lose divergent work (accepted). **Ledger reconciliation (G6):** the authorship_ledger keys on the stable `position` (`{ts}-{uuid}`), invariant across the rewrite; only the resolved `position.commit_sha` annotation and `enforce_since` (a ref) change. The same S2 pass re-resolves `position→commit_sha` in the NEW graph, rewrites the SNAPSHOT ledger annotations, and re-anchors `enforce_since` to the baseline — so `verify_authorship_at_commit`'s ancestry era-check evaluates consistently within one graph (in-horizon events verify against it; pre-baseline events grandfathered). **Rewrite primitive = core-git (T3):** emit new history with `git fast-import` (or `git mktree`/`commit-tree`) — ships with git, no `git filter-repo` (not vendored); preflight asserts `git fast-import --version`.

## Risk / rollback
A rewrite changes every commit SHA ⇒ every clone/worktree diverges (non-FF update of a shared auto-pushed branch); the CAS/exclusive-replace precondition bounds in-flight loss to the accepted >N-day case. Rollback: immutable backup ref `refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date>` (or the S3 rollback bundle prefix) before the swap; stage on a shadow branch verified by `rebar fsck` + full-log replay + `verify-authorship`; the swap is one revertible step; never prune the backup until a green Verify Authorship Identity run + full reconcile.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Causal-stability boundary C1–C5 specified with citations.
- [ ] C1–C5 proven to preserve still-observable ticket state (reads reduce from the SNAPSHOT).
- [ ] C1–C5 proven to preserve signature/authorship verification.
- [ ] C1–C5 proven to prevent resurrection across all clone states, incl. a <N-day clone with unpushed writes.
- [ ] Publish-swap precondition realized as a git-ref CAS on git remotes.
- [ ] Publish-swap realized as an exclusive push-locked bundle-set replacement (auto-doctor bypassed) on the S3 backend.
- [ ] Ledger `position→commit_sha` re-resolution plus `enforce_since` re-anchor specified so authorship verifies on the rewritten graph.
- [ ] History-rewrite primitive named as core-git and its portability resolved.
- [ ] Pack-shrink quantified from measured object composition against the 100 MiB budget.
- [ ] Coalescing shown insufficient alone at any safe horizon.
- [ ] W3 budget-bridge value identified as the near-term unblock.
- [ ] W1/W2 structural follow-ups identified as the durable fix.
- [ ] Risk assessment plus rollback (backup ref, shadow-branch stage) designed.
- [ ] Escalated to a human for approval before any destructive/history-rewriting action.

## Deferred child-slice work (S0–S3 — NOT implemented here; only after approval)
- [ ] S0 ADR: §I1 doctrine amended; I1–I9 proven under horizon plus override; accepted >N-day loss stated.
- [ ] S1 eligibility algorithm implemented (remote-reachable ≥ N days; recent excluded; portable).
- [ ] S2 coalescing prototyped on a DISPOSABLE SHADOW CLONE (never pushed); fsck/replay/verify-authorship clean on that shadow branch; two-clone resurrection test.
- [ ] S3 stale-clone override enforced on reconnect.
- [ ] docs/concurrency.md §I1 moved to 'implemented'; residual pack size quantified; W3 set; W1/W2 filed.

## HARD STOP (this design slice only)
DESIGN + PROOF only: no history rewrite / force-push / destructive reclaim executed; none of the deferred S0–S3 items done here. All S0–S3 implementation (incl. the S2 shadow-clone prototype) happens in later child slices AFTER human approval, and never mutates origin/tickets or the Gerrit box until the approved staged rollout. Escalated to the orchestrator for human approval before any destructive action.
baseline.summary: Remote-anchored retired-event GC + stale-clone override (N-day horizon)

## Why

rebar's `_store/lock.py` mkdir-lock reclamation (`_mkdir_lock_is_stale`) is deliberately conservative: every branch that cannot POSITIVELY prove the owner is a dead same-host process returns `False` (never reclaim) — the "refuse without proof" contract of bug yaw-gravel-linen. 304e (castoff-tigerseye-ammonite) fixed ONE instance of the resulting failure — a container recreate making a same-host orphan look foreign — but left the CLASS open: an absent/unreadable owner stamp, a malformed v2 stamp, a genuinely foreign-host stamp on a shared filesystem, or a cross-namespace stamp seen without the fcntl proof all still wedge the store PERMANENTLY, exactly as the 2026-07-31 production incident did (review-bot boot 62s vs a 30s health check).

The 9305 OSS research (rec #1, highest value, fully backed) prescribes the missing piece: a wall-clock AGE CEILING, following git gc's gc.pid 12h precedent (builtin/gc.c) — a stamp we cannot prove orphaned is respected UNTIL a generous ceiling, then reclaimed, so the store can never wedge forever. rebar holds the write lock only for a single event append (seconds), so the ceiling can be far tighter than git's 12h.

## What / Approach

Add `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` (1 hour) and reclaim a contended mkdir lock, even without proof of death, once its lock-dir mtime (the acquisition time; the stamp is never refreshed) exceeds the ceiling — but ONLY on the branches that today refuse for LACK of a liveness signal: absent/unreadable stamp, malformed v2 stamp, foreign host identity, cross-namespace without the fcntl proof, and non-numeric pid.

The ceiling must NOT override a positive `pid alive` probe. Per the research's own rule — "if you ever break a lock, do it under a conservative fail-closed guard PLUS a wall-clock backstop, NEVER ON A TIMER ALONE" — a branch where `os.kill(pid,0)` says the owner is alive keeps returning `False` regardless of age. The macOS "pid alive but start-time unconfirmable" gap is a SEPARATE research recommendation (#6, start-time fallback) and is explicitly out of scope here.

Reclaiming an unprovable-but-aged lock is noteworthy, so `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` logs the holder stamp and the dir age at WARNING (research rec #8, "report the holder"), turning a silent 60s wedge into an observable, attributable reclaim.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — the ceiling constant, an age helper, the age backstop on the
  refuse-without-proof branches, and holder-disclosure logging on reclaim.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py` — new.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An aged-out mkdir lock with an ABSENT/unreadable owner stamp is reclaimed (was permanent):
      `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` returns True once the dir mtime exceeds the ceiling, and `acquire`
      succeeds promptly.
- [ ] An aged-out FOREIGN-host v2 stamp and an aged-out MALFORMED v2 stamp are likewise reclaimed,
      while the SAME stamps with a fresh mtime are still refused — proving only age, not identity,
      changed the decision.
- [ ] SAFETY: a lock whose stamped pid is a LIVE same-host, same-namespace, start-time-matching
      owner is NEVER reclaimed even when its mtime exceeds the ceiling (proof of life beats age).
- [ ] SAFETY: a lock whose pid probes ALIVE but whose start time is unconfirmable is NOT reclaimed
      by the ceiling (the "never on a timer alone" boundary; macOS start-time is rec #6, not here).
- [ ] `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` emits a WARNING naming the reclaimed owner stamp and the dir age.
- [ ] The existing lock suites (`test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`, `test_lock_container_recreate.py`)
      still pass unchanged — fresh (non-aged) orphans keep their current behaviour.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Age ceiling on refuse-without-proof mkdir-lock branches: close the permanent-wedge class (9305 rec #1)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Pass 2 (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`, questions in `verify_models.py`, prompts `reviewers/plan_review_verifier*.md`, `temperature: 0`, standard class = Sonnet on Bedrock) is the cheapest LLM pass. A question/prompt change can be measured by re-verifying the *stored* Pass-1 findings and comparing to the stored answers.

**Production input, byte-identical — exact seam call.** `verify.finding_listing(batch)` renders ONLY `claim`/`criteria`/`evidence`/`impact` per finding — NOT `location`. `verify_findings(findings, *, context, run_chunk, window_tokens, est_tokens, headroom=...)` is called with `window_tokens=sizing.largest_window_tokens(model)` and `est_tokens=det_floor.est_tokens`, matching production's `sizing.verify_request_chunks` wrapper. `RunRequest.for_structured(..., bounds=RunRequest.INHERIT_POLICY)` is the repo-wide ratchet for single-turn structured calls.

**Model pinning follows the parity prerequisite exactly.** `run_tier1`/`build_candidate_runner` call `parity.resolve_pinned_model("pass2")` (per `efd4-847d-f7ad-47bc`'s fallback-free pinning contract) and construct `LLMConfig(model=pinned.model_id, repo_path=pinned.config_root, temperature=0.0)` — `repo_path=pinned.config_root` is exactly the ephemeral fallback-free config `fallback_targets_for` resolves against, so `PydanticAIRunner.run` never re-derives an Anthropic-direct fallback chain or collapses `prompt_cache_style`. The real commissioning run's ledger row shows `cache_write_tokens: 356518` (nonzero), empirically confirming caching stayed effective under this pinning.

**Missing-answer handling.** A finding absent from the candidate result or in `omitted` is excluded from κ/agreement with a reported per-question "no-answer" count, split per axis (binary vs severity attributes) so a question that is no-answer for EVERY finding still surfaces in the report instead of being silently dropped.

**Ledger — flat per-sample.** `ledger.reserve(ledger.estimate("tier1", n))` gates every run before any call; the fixed `PER_SAMPLE_ESTIMATE_USD["tier1"] = 0.5` pre-flight estimate ($30 for N=60) is intentionally conservative versus the real measured $6.72 (~$0.112/sample) — the estimate is a pre-flight ceiling, not a prediction, and stays well inside the $170 available budget either way.

**Tier1's `VerifierCandidate`** (new, distinct from Pass-3's `Candidate`/`CANDIDATES`) resolves a prompt-path override (`None` = production's shipped prompt).

**Distribution shift**: impact uses its closed categorical vocabulary as bins; validity/priority (continuous [0,1] scalars) are binned into 10 fixed equal-width buckets. Per-bucket count delta + total variation distance, per stratum and overall.

## Approach

`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier1.py`, `sampling.py`, `verifier_candidates.py`: stratified sample (verdict/leaf-container/finding-count/store/impact_model_version strata, seed-deterministic, `verified` rows only, standard-class `ran_model` only) → ledger pre-flight → replay each sampled review through the candidate verifier via the byte-identical production seam, model pinned per `parity.resolve_pinned_model("pass2")` → per-question κ/agreement + distribution shift → hand to Tier-0 for downstream metrics. `__main__.py` gained a `tier1` subparser; `eval_solver.py` gained the verifier `run_case` arm.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier1.py`, `sampling.py`, `verifier_candidates.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/__main__.py` (edited)
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` (edited)
- `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` (edited — registered the two new RunRequest sites)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/tier1-current-ddc8fb442281.md` (generated, committed)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/ledger.jsonl` (real commissioning-run row, committed)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_tier1.py` (new, 24 tests)

## Testing

24 unit tests, mutation-tested (no-answer exclusion, distribution-shift bucketing, ledger pre-flight-before-any-call ordering, run_id path-sanitization, the per-question-agreement fully-no-answer surfacing fix). Landed via Gerrit changes 2433 (main harness, 5 patchsets — CI's `RunRequest.for_structured` ratchet + a real per-question-agreement bug caught by LLM-Review, both fixed) and 2440 (real commissioning report + ledger.jsonl + a report-filename cosmetic fix). Live commissioning run: N=60, seed=0, reproduction candidate (`VerifierCandidate(prompt_path=None)`), pinned via `parity.resolve_pinned_model("pass2")`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay tier1 --n 60` over the real corpus produced per-question agreement (with no-answer counts) and distribution shift for a stratified sample of 60/60 requested; checked by `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/tier1-current-ddc8fb442281.md`.
- [x] The reproduction run (`VerifierCandidate(prompt_path=None)`) is recorded with its per-question agreement as the Pass-2 noise floor; checked by the same report (e.g. `absence_confirmed_in_context`: raw=0.735 kappa=0.582 n=328 no_answer=20).
- [x] Every call was priced via `ledger.estimate("tier1", n)`/`ledger.reserve`, used the Bedrock standard-class model id pinned via `parity.resolve_pinned_model("pass2")`, and stayed cache-effective (`cache_write_tokens: 356518` > 0); checked by the ledger.jsonl row: `{"run_id": "tier1-current-ddc8fb442281", "tier": "tier1", "sample_n": 60, "models": {"pass2": "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"}, "usd": 6.72}`.
- [x] Commissioning spend for this ticket ≤ $40; actual real spend $6.72 (622413 input / 265196 output / 356518 cache-write tokens), well under the cap; checked by the ledger.jsonl row above.
- [x] Unit tests pass in `make test` (24/24 passing; full CI `Verified` gate green on both Gerrit changes).
baseline.summary: Tier-1 harness: replay Pass-2 impact/validity questions on stored Pass-1 findings (Sonnet via Bedrock, budgeted)

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` measures **771 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that fans the fetch out over several projects rewrites the query construction in `_build_snapshot` and will not fit in 29 lines.

## Approach

Extract the pagination cluster into a new `fetch_paging.py`: `_ACLI_CEILING` and `SilentTruncationError` (`:99-120`), `_extract_issues` (`:251-262`), `_iter_pages` (`:265-390`) and `collect` (`:392-399`).

The call chain is genuine and self-contained: `collect` calls `_iter_pages` (`:397`), which calls `_extract_issues` (`:296`) and raises `SilentTruncationError` (`:308,343,355`) against `_ACLI_CEILING` (`:354`). Nothing in the cluster calls back upward; `_build_snapshot` reaches it only through `_iter_pages` (`:554`). The new module's complete import list is `annotations` and a `TYPE_CHECKING` import of `TicketTransport` — the pagination code is otherwise pure.

This extraction is well matched to the incoming change, which rewrites the `queries` tuple at `_build_snapshot:548-554` into a per-project loop over `jqls_for` — all of which stays in `fetcher.py`.

**Three things must stay resident**, and getting any of them wrong breaks tests silently:

- `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (`:105`) stays — `_build_snapshot:550` uses it. Only `_ACLI_CEILING` moves.
- `_load_acli` and `_load_alert_store` stay — they carry **25** and **3** `patch.object(fetcher, ...)`
  sites respectively, and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move. Both are called
  from `_build_snapshot` (`:523,536`), which stays, so no patch site is disturbed.
- `fetcher.py` re-exports **all four** moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`,
  `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` — because every one of them is reached as an attribute
  of `fetcher` by existing tests, and an attribute access does not follow a moved symbol:
  - `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py:118,139`), plus further
    `fetcher._iter_pages` / `fetcher.collect` accesses in the same file and in
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py`;
  - `fetcher.SilentTruncationError`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_pagination_jql.py:133,165`) as well as the
    explicit `from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import SilentTruncationError` at
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:32`;
  - `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` (`test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:149`), which reads the constant
    directly to size its fixture. This one is easy to miss precisely because the constant looks
    private and unshared.

The re-export keeps roughly 48 existing references green across six test modules. Note that the two production mentions of `fetcher._iter_pages` — `_backend.py:62` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:139,153` — are **docstring prose** recording bug history, not runtime references, so no production module needs an edit.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~195 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — drops to ~606 lines, plus a re-export block

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. The risks are attribute presence and patch survival, so both are asserted rather than assumed:

- Attribute-surface assertion: `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
  both hold after the move, and `SilentTruncationError` still imports from `fetcher`.
- Patch survival: the tests that `patch.object(fetcher, "_load_acli")` and `"_load_alert_store"` pass
  unedited, proving those symbols stayed resident and are still resolved from `fetcher`'s globals.
- Truncation behaviour preserved: a fixture exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` still raises
  `SilentTruncationError` through the real `collect → _iter_pages` path — the contract most at risk
  from moving the constant away from its raiser.
- One-way import: `fetch_paging` must not import `fetcher`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fetcher.py` and `fetch_paging.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the module-size
      gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] All four moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`, `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` —
      still resolve as attributes of `fetcher`; checked by a test asserting each by attribute access,
      which covers the two existing `hasattr` assertions and the direct `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` read.
- [ ] `_load_acli`, `_load_alert_store` and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` remain defined in `fetcher.py`;
      checked by asserting each is in that module's own namespace, not merely importable.
- [ ] A fixture exceeding the ceiling still raises `SilentTruncationError` via the real paging path;
      checked by the existing pagination held-out test running unedited.
- [ ] `fetch_paging.py` does not import `fetcher`; checked by a test importing the two modules in
      both orders and asserting `fetcher` is absent from `fetch_paging`'s imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the pagination cluster from fetcher.py into fetch_paging.py

## What
Add tests proving a fresh `rebar init` honors a custom `tracker.dir` and `tracker.branch` end-to-end, plus a regression test that defaults reproduce today's behavior, and an `fsck` WARN when the configured branch/dir does not match what is actually mounted.

- e2e/init test: configure custom dir + branch in `[tool.rebar]`, run `init`, assert the
  orphan branch is created under the custom name, the worktree/symlink uses the custom dir,
  it is gitignored, and create/list/show round-trip.

## Summary
The reconciler resolves a ticket's `assignee` to a Jira user on TWO divergent code paths, producing inconsistent results for the same input. An UPDATE strictly resolves the assignee (exact / unique-normalized accountId, else unassign); a CREATE sends the **raw** local string to ACLI/Jira with no resolution, so Jira fuzzy-matches or applies a project-default assignee. Same local value `"joe"` therefore yields different outcomes depending on path.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Local ticket with `assignee="joe"` (not a unique Jira identity — e.g. 3 "Joe"s exist).
2. **CREATE path** (new issue): reconcile creates the Jira issue. **Actual:** Jira assigns it to `joeoakhart@navapbc.com` (fuzzy/default fallback) — a *wrong* user.
3. **UPDATE path** (already-bound, Jira unassigned): reconcile diffs assignee. **Actual:** `"joe"` is unmappable → issue left unassigned (and inbound later clears the local value).

**Expected:** both paths apply the SAME resolution policy: resolve `"joe"` → unique accountId if one exists, otherwise leave unassigned — never silently mis-assign to a fuzzy/default user.

## Root Cause
- **CREATE does NOT validate.** `acli.py:297-298` extracts the raw assignee; `acli_cli_ops.py:241-243` (non-JSON) and `:367-368` (JSON) pass the raw string straight to ACLI. No `validate_assignee_exists` call. ACLI/Jira then fuzzy-resolves or defaults.
- **UPDATE DOES validate.** `acli.py:347-349` calls `validate_assignee_exists()` before mutating; the diff resolver `outbound_differ.py:506-535` + `outbound_fields.py:372-390` map unmappable → unassign (`""`). Strict matcher: `acli.py:517-606`.

## Proposed Unification
Add ONE shared resolver consumed by both paths:
- New `AcliClient.resolve_assignee_for_mutation(assignee, *, issue_key=None, project_key=None) -> (accountId|None, authoritative: bool)` that wraps `validate_assignee_exists` and classifies the outcome: resolved accountId; `AssigneeNotFoundError` → `(None, authoritative=True)` (definitively unmappable → unassign); transient/API error → `(None, authoritative=False)` (do NOT unassign — preserve, let next pass retry). Preserve the `(acct, authoritative)` tuple rather than collapsing to a bare string, so a transient REST failure never spuriously unassigns.
- **CREATE** (`create_issue`, no issue key yet) resolves with `project_key=<project>`: resolved accountId → include in payload; unmappable → omit (leave unassigned); transient → omit (avoid mis-assign).
- **UPDATE** (`update_issue`, has issue key) resolves with `issue_key=<key>` via the same method.
- The diff-side `_assignee_resolver` collapses to a thin wrapper over the shared method (single source of truth).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CREATE and UPDATE route assignee resolution through ONE shared method; identical input yields identical Jira outcome.
- [ ] An ambiguous/unmappable assignee (e.g. `"joe"`) is left UNASSIGNED on both paths — never fuzzy-matched or defaulted to an unrelated user.
- [ ] A uniquely-resolvable assignee (exact email/accountId/displayName, or unique normalized variant) is assigned identically on both paths.
- [ ] Transient resolution failures do NOT unassign (authoritative=False is preserved end-to-end); only authoritative AssigneeNotFoundError unassigns.
- [ ] CREATE uses project-scope resolution (no issue_key yet); `validate_assignee_exists` already accepts `project_key`.
- [ ] Tests: CREATE+UPDATE parity for ambiguous, exact, unique-normalized, and transient-error cases.

## Affected Files (initial)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli.py` (`create_issue`, `update_issue`, new shared resolver, `validate_assignee_exists`)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_cli_ops.py` (CREATE raw-string call sites)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` / `outbound_fields.py` (diff resolver → wrapper)
baseline.summary: Unify assignee resolution across CREATE and UPDATE reconciler paths (CREATE bypasses validate_assignee_exists -> fuzzy/default mis-assignment)

## Context / Problem
Two grounded code-review false negatives (escaped-bug deep-dive on cranial-goodly-seahog; user-approved design 2026-08-18, recorded verbatim in this ticket's comments) drove an approved three-part change set: citric-preregal-ladybird — a deletion-impact/api-compat finding naming the removed PUBLIC API `rebar.llm.review_ticket` plus a concrete broken external test scored impact 0.30, below the approved deletion-impact@0.60 / api-compat@0.51 blocking flips; brattish-ladyish-jaguar — a pass-2 recall failure on a workflow-YAML artifact. The approved set: (a1) churn/freq_mult amplify-only, never suppress, and never dampen a SERIOUS-tier binary; (a2) version-signal gating of `unversioned_published_contract_break`; (proposal-3) a pass-2 removed-public-symbol sub-question keyed on the EXPORT (not a cited caller) feeding a targeted impact boost.

STATUS OF a1: already landed on main by code-v4 (commit 61d50b0513, ticket 7f9f-05f4-796a-4c63): the debt-lane churn amplifier is [1.0,1.5] (amplify-only) and the serious-maint lane is undamped, pinned by tests/unit/test_impact_code.py (test_serious_maint_undamped_by_churn, test_debt_churn_zero_is_amplifier_one_not_half, test_freq_mult_cold_vs_hot). For a1 this ticket only corrects the stale "churn 0 => freq_mult 0.5" comment in workflow_ops.py.

## Approach
Implement a2 + proposal-3 on top of code-v4, each behavior change RED first (a test proving the current wrong score / missing gating) then GREEN:

- a2 (pass-2 classification gating): redefine `unversioned_published_contract_break` in BOTH pass-2 surfaces — the pydantic field description (verify_models.py CodeSeverityAttrs) and the code-review-verify.md prompt bullet — as TRUE only when the published-contract break LACKS a version/deprecation signal (a major version bump, a deprecation cycle, or a CHANGELOG breaking-change entry); a MANAGED removal (any such signal present) is FALSE.
- proposal-3 (pass-2 sub-question + deterministic boost): add two abstain-safe booleans to CodeSeverityAttrs — `removed_public_symbol` (TRUE when the finding cites a symbol this diff REMOVES whose name was reachable from the public API: `__all__`/re-export, a CLI command, or an MCP tool; detection keyed on the EXPORT, never on a cited caller — the absence of an internal caller does not prove an external API unused) and `version_signal_present` (TRUE when the removal carries one of the a2 signals). `decide.impact_code`'s serious-maint lane gains the derived contribution: `removed_public_symbol AND NOT version_signal_present` => the 0.9 unversioned-contract-break tier. Both fields default False, so an older/absent verifier ABSTAINS (no boost, never suppression); the boost is amplify-only — it can never lower an existing score. Bump sidecar IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION code-v4 -> code-v5 (impact semantics changed; sidecars segment by version), updating the exact-string version pins in tests.
- Eval spec: add one fire case (unmanaged removal of an exported public symbol) and one no-fire case (managed removal with a deprecation cycle + CHANGELOG breaking-change entry) to code-review-verify.eval.yaml, offline-validated by the existing spec-discipline tests.
- Interpretation note (recorded deliberately): the operator scope comment says the boost targets findings "that cite a REMOVED public symbol together with a named broken caller"; the user-approved design comment explicitly keys detection on the EXPORT, "NOT on a cited caller". The design comment wins — a named broken caller is NOT required for the boost. Assume this default unless the operator overrides it.

The pass-3 validity<0.5 hard-drop stays impact-blind, exactly as the approved design states (the brattish lever is pass-2 recall, addressed by the prompt/labeling changes above; no decider change here).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py — a2-gated `unversioned_published_contract_break` description; 2 new CodeSeverityAttrs booleans
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py — impact_code serious-maint boost path (code-v5)
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-verify.md — gated bullet + removed-public-symbol sub-question guidance
- src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py — IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION "code-v5"
- src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py — correct the stale freq_mult-0.5 comment (a1 residue)
- src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-verify.eval.yaml — fire/no-fire removal dataset cases
- tests/unit/test_impact_code.py — boost/abstain/managed-removal tests + the citric-preregal-ladybird replay
- tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py — version pin -> code-v5
- tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py — prompt/description text pins for a2 + proposal-3

## Testing
Happy path: `impact_code({"removed_public_symbol": True}) == 0.72` (0.9 serious tier x 0.8 non-silent amp) and the citric-preregal-ladybird replay attrs (capability_degraded + reachable_path_without_automated_coverage + trigger_likelihood rare + removed_public_symbol) score >= 0.60, clearing the deletion-impact@0.60 / api-compat@0.51 flips end-to-end through the packaged routing. Failure/edge paths: a managed removal (`version_signal_present: True`) gets NO boost and scores exactly as before the change; empty attrs still score 0.0 (abstain); `version_signal_present` alone changes nothing; the boost never lowers a score that other lanes already earned. Prompt/model text pins assert the version-signal gating and the export-keyed sub-question wording on both pass-2 surfaces. Offline eval-spec validation covers the new dataset cases. Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_code.py tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `impact_code({"removed_public_symbol": True}) == 0.72` and the citric-preregal-ladybird replay scores >= 0.60 through the real packaged routing — checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_code.py`.
- [x] A managed removal never trips the boost: the same attrs with `version_signal_present: True` score exactly the pre-change value, and empty attrs still score 0.0 — checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_code.py`.
- [x] `unversioned_published_contract_break` is version-signal-gated on BOTH pass-2 surfaces (field description + prompt bullet name the major-bump / deprecation-cycle / CHANGELOG-breaking-change signals and the managed-removal=>FALSE rule) — checked by the text pins in `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py`.
- [x] The verify prompt carries the removed-public-symbol sub-question keyed on the EXPORT (`__all__`/re-export, CLI command, MCP tool), explicitly not on a cited caller — checked by the text pins in `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py`.
- [x] IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION == "code-v5" and code-review-verify.eval.yaml gains one fire + one no-fire removal case that pass strict offline spec validation — checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py`.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass in the worktree — checked by running them.
baseline.summary: Apply approved code-review impact-model fixes: amplify-only freq_mult, version-signal gating, and deletion-impact/api-compat impact boost
