## Context / Problem

rebar is a concurrency-heavy project (multi-process writers over a git-backed store, file locks, detached children, CI-level push contention), which makes it both the ideal dogfood target and the worst case for trigger over-fire. Measured over the last 300 non-merge `origin/main` commits by replaying each commit's diff through `content_triggered_overlays` (committed-only vs. with the noisy tier; reproducible — the measurement script is recorded on the session log and in the commit message): the committed high-precision tier fires on 13.3% of diffs (40/300); the noisy tier (`.lock`, `retry`, `Popen`, `fork`, …) adds a further 22.0% (66/300), for 35.3% combined. Three of the four traced corpus bugs (`fine-wisteria-solenodon` via the `.lock` token on `index.lock`, `fervid-boring-python` via `retry`, `eclectic-spotted-barb` via `Popen`) trigger only through noisy-tier vocabulary — so for THIS repo the noisy tier is load-bearing, and per the parent epic's decided design it lives in the project overlay, not the committed list. Nothing currently documents the two-layer trigger design for other projects to copy.

## Approach

Two deliverables. (1) Add a `concurrency` entry to the `code_review` section of this repo's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` using the project-extension mechanism delivered by the prerequisite story: `trigger_tokens` `[".lock", "retry", "Popen", "setsid", "fork", "stage_and_commit", "push_tickets_branch", "refs/reconciler/"]` (carrying ONLY these two additive keys — `concurrency` is a built-in overlay id, so `effective_routing` merges the entry per-key over the committed routing; a posture/threshold key would silently re-tune the overlay. `start_new_session` and `index.lock` were dropped in code review as redundant — the former is already a committed token, the latter is subsumed by the `.lock` substring) and `applies_to` `["**/_store/**", "**/lock*", "**/enrich_drain*", ".github/workflows/**"]`. (2) Document the two-layer trigger design in `docs/llm-framework.md` adjacent to the existing code-review routing material (the routing/prompt/eval pointer block around docs/llm-framework.md:661): the committed high-precision tier and its survey grounding, the project noisy tier and how a project adds vocabulary, the measured fire-rate tradeoff (13.3% committed vs +22.0% noisy on this repo, with the reproducible measurement method), and this repo's entry as the worked example. Positive rationale: the dogfood entry is load-bearing (it is what makes the corpus bugs trigger here) and doubles as documentation-by-example, the same way this repo's `project.portability` and `project.engine-layer-enforcement` entries demo the plan-review project overlay.

## Scope

- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — the `code_review.concurrency` project entry.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — the two-layer trigger section.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py` — the config-effect case below (module created by the prerequisite trigger-extension story).

## Testing

Config-effect contrast (shared test-design standard §6), unit tier: one test proving the project entry changes behavior through the REAL read path — a fixture diff containing `index.lock` (a project token deliberately absent from the committed high-precision list) fires the `concurrency` overlay when `content_triggered_overlays` runs with `repo_root` = this checkout, and does NOT fire under committed-only routing (no `repo_root` / a bare tmp root). A test that only parsed the JSON would miss the read-but-miswired class; this asserts the observable outcome differs across the two routing states.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries the `code_review.concurrency` entry with the tokens and globs listed in the Approach; checked by reading the file.
- [x] Config-effect test: a diff containing `index.lock` fires `concurrency` under this repo's effective routing and not under committed-only routing; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py`.
- [x] `docs/llm-framework.md` documents the two tiers, the fire-rate measurement, and how a project adds vocabulary, using this repo's entry as the worked example; checked by reading the section.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the targeted pytest module pass. [non-codebase]
baseline.summary: Dogfood: rebar project trigger vocabulary + two-layer trigger docs

baseline.description:
# Workflow engine: conditional overlays (via if:) + delegating batch step

## Context

Split out of soupy-spool-revel (6f2d) per the brainstorm (session logs boom-demon-jug ad3f + woody-meat-seize). The e6d9 engine (declarative IR + thin worklist interpreter, run-state on the git event log; step kinds uses/prompt/branch/loop/map + bounded-concurrent map fan-out) is closed. To express a reusable 4-pass LLM-review pipeline ON the engine (epic B migrates plan-review + completion-verification), the engine needs support for (1) conditional criterion INCLUSION and (2) budgeted BATCH orchestration. This epic adds ONLY that, engine-only (no plan-review coupling). A prior-art survey (Argo/Step Functions/dbt/LangGraph/Airflow/Dagster/Temporal) + a code investigation grounded the design.

## The two concepts (one already exists, one is genuinely new)

1. **Conditional overlay = the EXISTING `if:` skip-guard (do NOT add a new field).** Code investigation
   found the engine ALREADY does per-step conditional inclusion: the v1 `if:` skip-guard (retained in
   v2; interpreter.py _guard_scoped) evaluates a predicate over run-start-journaled inputs + recorded
   prior outputs, is replay-deterministic (no live-store access), records a durable `skipped` event,
   and fails closed. So overlays ADOPT `if:`. The deliberately-CLOSED expression grammar (lint_refs.py
   _ALLOWED_EXPR; pinned by the v2 schema `expression`  — no operators/regex/functions) is the only
   gap: it can branch on a boolean in scope but cannot COMPUTE one. The clean design (keeping the grammar
   tiny + injection-safe) is a DETERMINISTIC scripted PRECOMPUTE step that turns each overlay trigger
   (has-children, has-linked-session-log, keyword/trigger match over a text input) into a boolean output
   the criterion's `if:` references; plus optionally journaling the resolved included-set at run-start
   for coverage. NO new IR field is added.

2. **Batch orchestration = a THIN delegating step (genuinely new).** No surveyed engine makes adaptive
   cost-budgeted batching first-class — it is app code everywhere — and encoding it in the IR would break
   the replay invariant (batch composition depends on a runtime token estimate + which call hit a context
   limit, so its control state is a recorded DECISION-TREE, not a function of outputs). So the IR gains a
   thin `batch` step declaring only params (group, usd_budget, model_ladder); a batch-RUNNER (behind a
   seam) does the adaptive packing / token-estimation / context-limit fallback / model-escalation /
   shed-to-INDETERMINATE / fingerprint-checkpoint and JOURNALS its batch-plan + fallback as OPAQUE events
   the interpreter stores but never interprets. Epic A ships the seam + a reference default runner; epic
   B supplies the production runner (extracting the gate's sizing.py) behind this seam.

## Scope (engine-only)

- Overlay-via-`if:`: a deterministic trigger-precompute scripted step + a documented precompute-then-`if:`
  pattern + optional run-start journaling of the resolved included-set. The expression grammar is UNCHANGED.
- The `batch` step kind: schema/JSON Schema + the batch-runner SEAM + a reference default runner + the
  journaled batch-plan/fallback event vocabulary + interpreter wiring (store the opaque plan, do not interpret).
- A THROWAWAY demo workflow exercising an `if:`-gated (overlay) step + a `batch` step end-to-end (dry-run
  via FakeAgentRunner), removed by epic B; retained meanwhile as the visual-editing refinement sample.
- VISUAL EDITING in the workflow editor for the batch step (NEW) and the `if:` overlay predicate (EXISTING
  — confirm/extend the editor renders + edits `if:` and supports add/remove of a conditionally-included prompt).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Overlays adopt `if:` (no new IR field): a deterministic precompute scripted step computes overlay-
      trigger booleans (has-children, has-linked-session-log, text/keyword trigger match) as step outputs;
      a criterion gated by `if: ${{ steps.<triggers>.outputs.<name> }}` is included when truthy and skipped
      (durable event) when falsy; the expression grammar is NOT extended. (A1)
- [ ] Replay determinism for inclusion: a mid-run store edit does not change the included/skipped outcome
      (read from the run-start journal, not live state); the resolved included-set is observable for coverage
      (journaled at run-start OR documented as recovered from skip statuses — decide + record). (A1)
- [ ] A `batch` step kind exists with declarative params (group/usd_budget/model_ladder), a batch-runner
      SEAM + a reference default runner; the runner journals its batch-plan + fallback as OPAQUE events the
      interpreter STORES but never branches on (a test asserts this); replay reads the recorded plan. (A2)
- [ ] The Burr-tripwire stays green (no asyncio/threading leaks outside the confined fan-out). (A2)
- [ ] A throwaway demo workflow exercises an `if:`-gated overlay step + a `batch` step end-to-end under the
      FakeAgentRunner (offline, no live calls), with a test; it is clearly labeled disposable. (A3)
- [ ] The workflow visual editor renders/edits the `batch` step and the `if:` overlay predicate, and
      supports add/remove of a conditionally-included prompt. (A4)
- [ ] make lint + the full test suite pass.
- [ ] The engine expresses conditional criterion inclusion (via `if:` + a precompute pattern) and budgeted
- [ ] A demo proves both offline; the batch step + the `if:` overlay are visually editable.
baseline.summary: Workflow engine: first-class conditional overlays + delegating batch step (engine-only; + throwaway demo + visual editing)

baseline.description:
## Summary

`autodeploy.sh` keeps ONE piece of global state for TWO independently-deploying components (the review-bot and the mcp blue-green target). Split out of `cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95` with the operator's approval: that ticket scopes the review-bot DEFERRAL so control reaches the mcp block; this one makes the state each component depends on per-component.

Four rounds of code review on the combined change each found the same defect shape, each fix exposing the next. They are one concern and belong in one ticket.

## The three couplings

**Completion.** `deployed-sha` is written once, at the footer, so ANY early exit loses the completion of whichever component DID deploy, and the next tick redeploys it. A review-bot redeploy stop-and-drains the container, killing an in-flight review (bug 34cd) — the exact harm the drain gate exists to prevent, arriving from the other direction.

**Failure.** `record_backoff_failure` writes ONE `deploy-backoff` keyed on the global `$TARGET`, and the top-level gate exits the whole script on it. On `main` it is called from BOTH blocks (~5 sites in the bot block, ~10 in the mcp block), so an mcp failure throttles the BOT and a bot failure suppresses mcp.

**Incompleteness.** A component skipped by an open backoff window has not deployed, but nothing records that, so the footer stamps `$TARGET` into its marker for a deploy that never ran. The next tick then computes no delta and drops the pending change PERMANENTLY.

## Shape of the fix

- `mcp-deployed-sha` and `bot-deployed-sha`, each written the moment that component completes,
  with each component's delta gate RE-POINTED to diff from its own marker rather than the
  global `$DEPLOYED` baseline. An absent or unparseable marker falls back to `$DEPLOYED`.
  The global `deployed-sha` KEEPS its existing role unchanged: it is the TICK-level record,
  advanced only at the footer and only on a tick that completed, and it still drives the
  top-level "up to date; no-op" early exit (`if [ "$TARGET" = "$DEPLOYED" ]`). It is not
  removed and not split — the component markers are added ALONGSIDE it. On a complete tick the
  footer ALSO stamps both component markers. Those two writes are not in conflict: the
  mid-tick write records a component that actually DEPLOYED, and the footer write is an
  idempotent top-up covering the component that was a NO-OP this tick (nothing changed under
  its trigger paths), so it is never left behind the global marker. For a component that
  already deployed, the footer rewrites the same value. On an INCOMPLETE tick the guard exits
  before the footer, so the only markers written are the mid-tick ones for components that
  genuinely deployed — which is precisely the asymmetry per-component state exists to record. `$DEPLOYED` also remains the fallback baseline for a component whose marker is
  absent or unparseable, which is what makes the first tick after upgrade behave as today.

- A separate `mcp-deploy-backoff` recorder; the existing file then records bot failures only,
  which is what makes it safe to move its gate off the top of the script. Each gate sits with
  the component it throttles and skips that component instead of exiting the tick.
- `bot_incomplete` / `mcp_incomplete`, honoured by the footer guard, so a backoff-skip with a
  delta still pending never records completion. Each gate tests the DELTA before the window, so
  "nothing to do" stays distinguishable from "skipped with work pending".
- Both recorders keep emitting the `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker. That token — not the reason
  string — is what the alarm counts: `infra/scripts/observability.sh:230` does a bare
  `grep -cE '^AUTODEPLOY_ERROR \{'` over the unit journal and publishes the count as
  `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (`:240`, §4d). It never parses the reason, so alarm continuity is
  preserved by continuing to emit the marker at all. The reason stays `deploy_failed` and
  gains a `component=mcp` marker for OPERATOR legibility — telling the two paths apart when
  reading the journal — not for the metric.

## Consumers outside autodeploy.sh

The marker's only non-test consumer is `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (§4d, lines 230/240), which counts `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` occurrences into `rebar/host:deploy_errors`. It is deliberately kept distinct from the deferral and retire-cap tokens (`:259-260`, `:282`, `:338`) so routine deferrals and retire-caps never inflate that alarm — this change adds no new token, so that separation is unchanged. Test consumers of the marker: `test_autodeploy_review_drain.py`, `test_autodeploy_health_gate.py`, `test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py`, `test_observability_marker_anchor_8c2f.py`.

The one test consumer of the shared STATE FILE is `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py:86`, which reads `state/deploy-backoff` after a REVIEW-BOT failure. That file keeps its name and keeps recording bot failures, so the test needs no change and continues to pass unmodified — verified, 4 passed. Only the mcp block's failures move to the new file, and no existing test reads that path. Had the split renamed `deploy-backoff` instead of narrowing what writes to it, this consumer would have broken silently; narrowing rather than renaming is what avoids that.

## Boundary correction (2026-08-27)

The mcp completion marker (`mcp-deployed-sha` and re-pointing the mcp delta gate to it) has MOVED to `cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95`. Code review showed the original boundary was wrong: without that marker, cf34's fix re-triggers a full blue-green cutover on every tick of a deferral episode, so making the mcp path REACHABLE on a deferred tick and keeping it from redeploying every deferred tick are one concern and belong in one change. This ticket keeps the BOT-side marker, the scoped backoffs, and the incompleteness flags.

## Deliberately out of scope

A bot FATAL path still exits the tick, so mcp misses that single tick, after which the bot is in backoff and skipped and mcp proceeds. Bounding it to one tick is enough; making the bot's fatal paths return rather than exit is a larger restructure of a live deploy script.

## Acceptance criteria

All six mutation-checked: removing the behaviour each guards returns its test to RED.

- [x] An mcp failure does not write the SHARED backoff.
      Proof: `test_mcp_failure_on_a_deferred_tick_does_not_backoff_the_bot`
- [x] An mcp failure does not cause the review-bot to redeploy on later ticks.
      Proof: `test_a_failed_mcp_deploy_does_not_redeploy_the_bot_every_tick`
- [x] A component skipped by its own backoff window is not recorded as deployed (both halves).
      Proof: `test_bot_backoff_tick_does_not_record_the_bot_as_deployed`,
      `test_mcp_backoff_tick_does_not_record_mcp_as_deployed`
- [x] An open backoff window with NO pending delta is not reported as a skip.
      Proof: `test_an_open_bot_backoff_with_no_pending_delta_is_not_reported_as_a_skip`
- [x] An mcp backoff throttles mcp while the review-bot still deploys on the same tick.
      Proof: `test_mcp_backoff_throttles_only_mcp_and_lets_the_bot_deploy` — mutating the mcp
      recorder to also poison the shared backoff kills it on the bot assertion specifically.
- [x] mcp failures still emit an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, so `deploy_errors`
      (`observability.sh:230,240`) counts them as before, and the reason names `component=mcp`.
      Proof: `test_mcp_failure_keeps_the_deploy_failed_metric_and_names_the_component`


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/ -q -p no:randomly

Each new test is mutation-checked: removing the behaviour it guards returns it to RED.
baseline.summary: autodeploy keeps one global state for two independent components: per-component completion, backoff, and incompleteness

# Jira DC hardening — follow-on to e369

## Context

Epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] delivered Jira Server/Data Center support and met its operator-approved exit bar. This epic holds the DC work that delivery DISCOVERED, which is hardening rather than the feature itself. Operator decision 2026-08-05: let e369 close, harden here.

## What is in scope — all three children CLOSED, all three changes MERGED to main

* [rebar:4a6d-5bbc-44f4-4a56] (bug) — the capability-map channel reports rather than fails, so a run
  made before any Software project exists silently writes a WRONG Epic-field contract. Its ORIGINAL
  fix (a pre-run `await_required_fields` gate) was REFUTED in triage; re-scoped to post-run
  validation by operator decision 2026-08-12 option (a). **Change 1642 → `f487b62b3c`.**
* [rebar:a3fa-e8d4-f4aa-4b51] (bug) — capability call sites are cast but not runtime-guarded, so a
  non-capable transport fails silently. **Change 1634 → `671fa77c88`.**
* [rebar:f020-0960-2c42-4d61] (task) — the dormant absence-probe port; ruled **DELETE**.
  **Change 1645 → `b95c097fd4`.**

Full delivery evidence, the three AC amendments and their rationale, and the artifact index for the `[operator-attested]` criteria are in this ticket's comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py` refuses to vouch for an Epic-field report it cannot
      verify: it validates AFTER the agent run (never a pre-run `await_required_fields`, which bug
      941b banned) and exits non-zero with the verdict in `run_metadata.json`. Commit `f487b62b3c`
- [x] a unit test pins a system-only field inventory as not-ready on that surface, so the refusal is
      proven by a test rather than by configuration —
      `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`
- [x] **AMENDED** — the four capability call sites are runtime-guarded, and capability-ABSENT vs
      capability-RAISED are reported distinctly on the existing `bridge_alerts` channel rather than
      swallowed. *Replaces "fails loudly rather than silently": the operator ruling on a3fa is
      distinct reporting, NOT a hard failure on absence.* Commit `671fa77c88`
- [x] **AMENDED (guard shape)** — the guard is `isinstance`-primary with a `hasattr` fallback, a
      documented divergence from ADR-0083's isinstance-only guidance, because Python 3.12's
      `getattr_static` would declare a `__getattr__`-proxying transport non-capable. Follow-up
      [rebar:5c21-f24a-f7f8-4a55]
- [x] [operator-attested] f020's DELETE ruling is executed and recorded with its reason, including
      its effect on e369 AC5 (`classify_probe_response` dropped from the shared-unit list; e369
      amended). The ruling lives in ticket comments, outside the repo. Commit `b95c097fd4`
- [x] [operator-attested] this epic's changes did not regress the live DC harness. *Replaces "still
      GREEN (0 failed cells)": the harness was ALREADY red before these changes landed, from commit
      `c87afedba8`, now fixed by `b13173bb7d` under [rebar:9590-34f5-21a8-41fc], which carries the
      re-green bar.* Run evidence lives in GitHub Actions
- [x] [operator-attested] no cell was deleted, skipped or `xfail`ed to reach green. The harness holds
      exactly one `xfail`, introduced by `29f9627128` and owned by ticket 2b16 — none of this epic's
      three commits

## Testing

    gh workflow run "Live External Integration" --ref main
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 -q; make lint typecheck
baseline.summary: Jira DC hardening — follow-on to e369 (readiness parity, capability guards, dormant port)

baseline.description:
Run the one-time reclaim. **Do not start until A1-A5, A6-0a..0d and Epic B's B6 are closed**, and until A6-0a has been on `main` >=24 h with an observed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run on a descendant SHA (older binaries ignore the epoch field, so they would sail past the guard). session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Protocol
1. **Agent** disables `reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (`gh workflow disable`,
   which also blocks `workflow_dispatch` and therefore `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` self-redispatch);
   **asserts** no reconcile run is in progress (poll `gh run list`, not drain-and-hope); asserts the
   **Gerrit review queue is empty** — zero sessions stops new pushes, but a patchset pushed just
   before the window can still have its `LLM-Review` vote fire during it, and every vote writes a
   ticket; break-glasses `refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}` if held.
2. **Agent** pauses the AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` and the host LaunchAgents
   `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` (04:00) and `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update` (whose hourly
   rollback-guarded pipx reinstall could silently revert the global `rebar` to a pre-A6-0a build
   mid-window). **[operator-attested] Operator** confirms **zero active sessions** and all
   **`rebar-mcp` servers stopped** (a long-running MCP holds an in-process store handle and does not
   hot-reload). Gerrit needs no separate confirmation: every Gerrit push comes from a session.
3. **Agent** converges the local tracker (`fetch` + `reset --hard origin/tickets`, 0-ahead verified).
   This covers all 48 sibling worktrees at once — their `.tickets-tracker` are **symlinks to the one
   store**. The four other real trackers on the host point at different GitHub repos.
4. **Agent** deletes the pre-rewrite ref pins (A6-0d), runs the strip in a fresh **unfiltered** clone,
   verifies the pre-push assertions, and pushes with **`--force-with-lease`**.
5. **Agent** asserts non-resurrection: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is
   **false**, and no clone-fetched ref has the old tip as an ancestor.
6. **Agent** converges the review-bot clone over SSM (`fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets` on
   `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`). Reverts to **[operator-attested]** if the issued AWS
   credentials do not permit `ssm send-command` against `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`.
7. **Agent** lands the `enforce_since` re-pin through Gerrit, mapped via the commit-map.
   `rebar.toml:115` is the only literal SHA in the system; with `require_authenticated = false`
   (`:106`) `verify_authorship.py:531-550` returns early and never reads it, so there is **no CI
   deadlock** and the change lands normally. `verify.opcert_enforce_since` is unset.
8. **Agent** re-enables the GitHub workflows, the AWS timer, and both LaunchAgents.
9. **Agent** verifies the ACs below and **notifies the operator** that the tickets branch is
   available for sessions again.

## T11 migration-safety answers
- **Expand/contract:** yes — A6-0a's reader ships and is deployed before the epoch value exists.
- **Batching:** n/a, single atomic ref update.
- **Resumability: NONE, stated.** A force-push is not resumable. Mitigation: all correctness
  assertions run on the scratch clone **before** publishing, so a wrong graph never reaches origin;
  the push itself is atomic per-ref.
- **Dual-write window:** none — the store is quiesced; the epoch guard replaces dual-write as the
  stale-writer defence.
- **Rollback:** restore from the A6-0d bundle + `--force-with-lease` back to the old tip. Known
  limit: rollback re-diverges anything already converged, so consumers must be re-converged in the
  same order as the forward path. **No event bytes are ever altered** — only commit SHAs — so the
  rewrite itself cannot lose ticket data.
- **T4 destructiveness:** an irreversible force-push to the authoritative store of a live system,
  chosen deliberately to reclaim 92% of the branch, gated on operator-confirmed quiescence, an
  off-repo bundle, a fail-closed epoch guard, and pre-push assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB** (from 1.04 GiB; the measured strip
      result is ~94 MiB) and `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree.
      **Holds only because B6 landed first.** Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] Commit count and merge-commit count on `tickets` are **unchanged** versus the pre-rewrite
      recording (measured at window time, never hardcoded). Tier: **repo assertion**.
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <sha> --format json`, run pre-rewrite
      against the old SHA and post-rewrite against the mapped SHA: the **stderr summary counts** are
      identical AND the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` from the JSON report is
      identical **ignoring `commit`**. (JSON mode puts only the report array on stdout and the summary
      on stderr; the report lists only non-verified events; every `commit` is a rewritten SHA. The
      command **exits 1** when `enforced_not_verified > 0`, so do not require exit 0.) Tier: **CLI
      subprocess, both sides**.
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** and `size-pack` growth is **< 1 MB**. The ancestry assertion is
      what actually proves non-resurrection. Tier: **repo measurement after an observed vote**.
- [ ] No ref a default clone fetches has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier: `ls-remote` +
      `merge-base` loop, computed at window time.
- [ ] Operator confirmation of zero active sessions and stopped MCP servers is recorded as a comment
      before step 3. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] A reconciler pass completes green after step 8, and `rebar fsck` is clean. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
Operational — no `src/` changes. Uses the A6-0c script and A6-0d helpers; touches `rebar.toml` (`enforce_since`) via Gerrit in step 7.

Scope: M (operational). Depends on A5, A6-0b, A6-0c, A6-0d, and Epic B's B6.
baseline.summary: A6-1: execute the reclaim window (quiesced, guarded, agent-executed except the zero-sessions confirmation)

## Context
With an out-of-worktree `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` and a code worktree at a commit carrying the ticket trailer, `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` correctly resolved the trailer but CLI `rebar transition ... closed --ref HEAD` falsely reported that no commit referenced the ticket. `close_precheck.py` derived `code_root = os.path.dirname(tracker)`, so a tracker override made it scan the checkout containing tracker storage instead of the current code worktree. The public library call succeeded when passed the actual repo root, proving the defect and workaround.

## Plan
- Add a regression test with a code worktree and a separate custom tracker directory.
- Resolve the code root from the explicit/current repository context while continuing to resolve ticket state from `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`.
- Preserve the fail-fast no-referencing-commit behavior and default in-repo tracker behavior.
- Run RED to GREEN, defect-seeded mutation, focused lifecycle tests, gates, and Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CLI close with an out-of-worktree `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` finds a matching trailer reachable from the current code worktree HEAD.
- [x] A true missing referencing commit still fails before the completion LLM call.
- [x] Default in-repo tracker behavior is unchanged.
- [x] The regression test is RED before the fix and GREEN after reintroducing the correct code-root seam.
- [x] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, LLM-Review +1, and Verified +1 pass before merge.
baseline.summary: CLI close precheck misroots code repo for custom tracker directories

baseline.description:
## Context

`fixture_selection.select_candidates` groups a criterion's matched findings by `norm_id` and also compares finding `norm_id` sets across a ticket's successive reviews. On the REAL committed plan-review corpus these paths raise `KeyError: 'norm_id'`. `select_from_corpus` reconstructs findings from every `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar event across ALL committed history (`_review_findings` -> `corpus._load_ticket_events`, keyed by review-event uuid). The `norm_id` field is emitted by the sidecar `_slim` projection UNCONDITIONALLY — current `_slim` (`sidecar.py:664`, `"norm_id": norm_id(f)`) writes it for every finding regardless of tier, and `norm_id()` (`sidecar.py:311-319`) never returns None. That line was ADDED by commit `314e4191c826` (2026-06-29). Sidecar events committed BEFORE that commit predate the field, so their reconstructed findings carry no `norm_id` key at all — the crash is a schema-VINTAGE gap in historical records, NOT current `_slim` tier behavior.

Evidence (scan of the tickets tracker via `_review_findings`, recorded here as the `[non-codebase]` provenance attestation for this root-cause claim): 1437 of 79914 criterion-naming findings lack a `norm_id` key; ALL 1437 have a review-event timestamp before 2026-06-29 and ZERO are after; they span BOTH tiers (LLM 1299, DET 138). The vintage cutoff matches commit `314e4191c826` exactly. The first such finding aborts the whole candidate-selection pass, so the fixture-mining pipeline (epic 65dd-e93b-666a-4caa) cannot run over real history at all — it blocks ticket 67aa's live admission run (AC10).

A norm-less finding is subscripted `finding["norm_id"]` at SIX sites reached from `select_candidates`: the `_fire_rows` grouping (`fixture_selection.py:234`) AND — via `_author_response_norm_ids` -> `classify_finding_survival` — `labels.py:167,169`, plus `_criterion_sets`/churn `labels.py:184,220,221`. A fix scoped to `_fire_rows` alone would leave the `classify_finding_survival` path (reached whenever a ticket has two reviews with differing `material_fingerprint`) still crashing.

## Approach

Normalize norm-less findings out ONCE at the `select_candidates` entry — the single point every eligible review passes through before ANY norm-keyed consumer. At the top of `select_candidates`, rebuild each review as `{**review, "findings": [f for f in review["findings"] if f.get("norm_id") is not None]}`, then proceed unchanged. Because `_eligible_reviews`, `_fire_rows`, `_no_fire_rows`, and `_author_response_norm_ids` all derive from this list, the single normalization covers all six subscript sites — and it protects BOTH the public `select_candidates` (direct callers / tests) and `select_from_corpus` (which calls it).

Rationale for the entry-boundary normalization over scattered per-consumer defensive reads: a finding with no `norm_id` has no stable cross-review identity, so it cannot participate in ANY norm-keyed operation (reproduction-consensus grouping, author-response survival, or per-criterion churn) — excluding it once at the entry is both the minimal single-point fix and semantically correct. For every norm-BEARING finding the normalized lists are byte-identical to today, so all existing selection behavior is unchanged. No change to `labels.py` is needed: the boundary keeps norm-less findings from ever reaching it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `select_candidates` no longer raises `KeyError: 'norm_id'` when an eligible review's findings
      include a criterion-naming finding with no `norm_id` key, exercised through BOTH norm-keyed
      paths: `_fire_rows` grouping AND the `_author_response_norm_ids` -> `classify_finding_survival`
      survival path (two reviews of one ticket with differing `material_fingerprint`, at least one
      norm-less finding) — the run returns rows without error (`pytest`).
- [x] A finding lacking `norm_id` contributes NO candidate and does not perturb the candidates
      produced by norm-bearing findings for the same criterion: the emitted rows for an eligible
      set containing a norm-less finding equal the rows produced when that finding is absent
      (`pytest`).
- [x] Existing norm-bearing selection behavior is unchanged: the module's current
      `test_fixture_selection` suite still passes (`pytest`).
- [x] Selection remains deterministic — two `select_candidates` runs over the same eligible set
      return byte-identical manifest rows (`pytest`).

## Definition of Done

`make lint` / `make typecheck` / targeted `pytest` pass; the fix lands through Gerrit (`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`); the fixture-mining selection pass runs over the real corpus without the `norm_id` KeyError.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py` — normalize norm-less findings out at the
  `select_candidates` entry (single point; covers `_fire_rows` + the `classify_finding_survival`
  and churn paths in `labels.py`).
- `tests/unit/test_fixture_selection.py` — held-out regression: a norm-less finding routed
  through both the fire-grouping and the author-response/survival paths.
baseline.summary: fixture_selection._fire_rows KeyError on findings without norm_id blocks real-corpus selection

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Long-running MCP and review-bot processes mix startup deployment policy with per-operation config and ambient auth reads. Static Gerrit/GitHub/LLM/telemetry material can change underneath an in-progress operation or be reread inconsistently. RP-04 requires restart/redeploy rotation for static bindings while preserving request-scoped inbound auth and SDK-native refresh.

## Outcome
Compose non-secret startup policy and live runtime bindings once when MCP/review-bot services start; create a fresh non-secret `OperationSnapshot` for each operation/request. Review-bot Gerrit/GitHub/LLM capabilities are typed and adapter-local. Inbound MCP bearer tokens remain transient request context, never config. Optional Langfuse/OTLP setup remains fail-open/no-op and cannot change the underlying operation result.

## Plan
1. Update MCP construction so deployment/startup config is captured once, each tool call composes its own S1 operation snapshot, and existing OAuth/JWKS/introspection/proxy verification stays request-scoped under ADR 0050.
2. Update review-bot config/app/Gerrit client to compose static provider bindings at startup, validate decision-bearing auth before accepting a job/webhook, and pass S4 `LLMRuntime` plus focused Git/Gerrit policy into each operation. Do not expose stronger server identity through CLI/MCP inputs.
3. Bind Langfuse/OTLP once at startup using provider-specific static input. Missing/partial/rejected telemetry disables telemetry with a redacted diagnostic and no operation-result change; security/load-bearing auth remains fail-closed.
4. Document and test rotation: changing static env/file material does not rebind a running process; a restarted process observes it; revoked old auth fails without principal fallback; official refreshable capabilities may refresh in process.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Service/component tests run two operations around environment/file mutation and assert static runtime identity is unchanged while operation-scoped non-secret config is freshly composed where intended.
- MCP auth interface suites prove inbound tokens die with the request and never enter startup/operation snapshots, logs, caches, schemas, or subprocess environments.
- Review-bot verified-fake tests cover valid/missing/conflicting/revoked Gerrit/GitHub auth, webhook acceptance, one selected integration, LLM runtime forwarding, and no fallback principal.
- Observability tests use partial/rejected credentials and exporter failure; the exact operation result remains equal and only telemetry is disabled.
- [operator-attested] AWS review-bot deploy/E2E canary records change/run ids, startup binding kinds, vote/result, retry counts, timestamp, and redacted diagnostics.

## Compatibility / rollback
During expansion, service constructors accept optional runtime bindings and may use the legacy startup composition facade. Rollback before cutover selects that facade and restarts/redeploys. MCP wire/tool schemas, webhook auth protocol, Gerrit vote schema, and LLM result schemas remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] MCP and review-bot tests prove startup bindings stay stable across ambient mutation while each new operation receives the intended fresh non-secret snapshot.
- [x] MCP inbound bearer/OAuth material remains request-local and absent from startup/operation snapshots, serialization, logs, caches, child environments, and tool schemas.
- [x] Review-bot decision-bearing auth is validated before job/provider work, only the selected integration is constructed, and revoked/missing/conflicting auth never falls back to another principal.
- [x] Static binding replacement is observed only after process restart/redeploy; native refreshable capability behavior remains SDK-owned.
- [x] Partial/rejected Langfuse/OTLP auth disables telemetry without changing the underlying operation result, while security/load-bearing auth remains fail-closed.
- [x] [operator-attested] The AWS review-bot deploy/E2E canary passes and records the required redacted provenance.
  provenance: environment=AWS-hosted rebar review bot + GitHub Actions CI; principal=review-bot production principal (deployed) + CI reconciler; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit 1861 PS4 (147caa1ebe): the AWS-hosted rebar review bot processed this change end-to-end (event->clone->review->signed vote) and cast LLM-Review +1, and CI cast Verified +1 running the S5 held-out oracle over the NEW startup-binding/decision-auth/runtime-forwarding code; startup binding kinds = all-None ambient LLMRuntime (SDK-owned creds) + non-secret Gerrit/GitHub/LLM ReceiverConfig policy; vote/result = LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1 / PASS; retries = 0; redacted diagnostics = none; no token/credential material recorded; full evidence in the operator-attestation comment on this ticket.
baseline.summary: RP-04 S5 — Bind MCP and review-bot config/auth at startup

## Summary
A Jira issue created directly in Jira (no rebar binding) is never adopted into the local store at steady state. Proven: REB-532 ("EXPERIMENT (delete me): assignee clobber repro", Bug, To Do) is fetched every pass but has no binding and no local ticket.

## Root Cause (edge-triggered adoption + prev_snapshot as a false "handled" proxy)
- REB-532 IS fetched — the inbound JQL has no rebar-label filter (`fetcher.py:67-79`).
- The binding-aware `inbound_differ.compute_inbound_mutations` skips any unbound issue by design (`inbound_differ.py:719-722`, docstring `:4-6` "local is source of truth"); it only emits `update`, never `create`.
- Inbound-CREATE lives only in `differ.compute_mutations`, which production calls as `compute_mutations(prev_snapshot, curr_snapshot)` — BOTH Jira snapshots (`reconcile.py:901-903`). Create fires only for a key in `curr` but NOT `prev` (`differ.py:457-469`) = "new since last pass".
- `prev_snapshot` means "seen in a prior fetch", used as a proxy for "already handled" — but it is NOT "bound to a local ticket". `reconcile.py:1407` advances prev via `shutil.copy2(curr, prev)` UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of whether adoption actually landed. So once REB-532 is in prev it is in both snapshots -> present-in-both (field-drift) branch -> never re-adopted. There is NO level-triggered reconvergence that asks "fetched key has no binding -> adopt".
- Runtime proof: `compute_mutations(prev={}, curr={REB-532}) -> 1 inbound create`; `compute_mutations(prev={REB-532}, curr={REB-532}) -> 0`.

## Why the test suite misses it
- The differ unit tests model `compute_mutations(arg1, arg2)` as `(local_state, jira_state)` (`test_differ.py:1-13`), so an unbound issue is always absent from arg1 and create always fires — validating a contract production does NOT use.
- Every adoption test uses `local={}` (empty prev) incl. the closest-named `test_unbound_jira_issue_without_rebar_id_label_still_creates` (`test_differ.py:542`).
- The only two-pass integration test binds everything in pass 1 (`test_reconcile_idempotency.py:268,291`), so the "in prev but still unbound" state is never constructed; the unconditional `copy2` at `reconcile.py:1407` is untested.
- `inbound_differ` tests assert unbound issues are ignored (`test_inbound_differ.py:112`), entrenching the skip.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create an issue directly in Jira REB (no rebar-id), e.g. REB-532.
2. Let >= 2 reconcile passes run (so it enters prev_snapshot).
3. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run` and search the plan for the issue.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: a Jira-native issue is adopted into the local store (a `jira-*` local ticket + confirmed binding) and stays converged.
- Actual: it is fetched but never adopted; permanently orphaned in Jira.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A Jira-native issue with no binding is adopted into local within one pass, regardless of whether it is already in `prev_snapshot` (level-triggered, not just edge-triggered) — without re-deriving all historical creates every pass (respect the prev_snapshot perf optimisation).
- [ ] `prev_snapshot` advance (`reconcile.py:1407`) no longer marks an issue "handled" when adoption did not actually bind it (decouple prev-advance from adoption success), OR a binding-aware reconvergence adopts unbound fetched issues.
- [ ] A RED test constructs the failing state: the SAME key present in both `prev_snapshot` and `curr_snapshot` with NO binding, then asserts it is adopted.
- [ ] REB-532 is adopted (or explicitly excluded as a test artifact) after the fix.

## Notes
Discovered comparing Jira REB vs local. Files: `differ.py`, `inbound_differ.py`, `reconcile.py`, `fetcher.py`, `apply_inbound.py`; tests under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/`, `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/`.

## Guardrails (must-preserve — prior-art + archaeology; folds in the corrected plan)
Approved policy: ADOPT unbound Jira-native issues (test-ticket hygiene is the creator's responsibility). But adoption is gated:
- [ ] Adoption MUST consult `bindings-retired.json` (`is_retired`) so a locally-archived-then-retired issue is not resurrected into a delete/re-adopt loop (interacts with C's GC).
- [ ] Run the rebar-id label audit (L9) and the label-derived-binding suppression (L10, bug 4354) FIRST: an issue already carrying a `rebar-id:`/`rebar-id-` label is bound — adopting it double-writes identity and recreates the phantom `jira-dig-NNNN` + ghost-label defect and can trip the double-bind quarantine (L11).
- [ ] Seed the per-binding BASELINE from the adopted issue's fields on bind, so the first outbound diff is EMPTY (echo suppression, L2).
- [ ] Adoption `create + bind` is keyed on the external id (idempotency/dedup key) so two overlapping passes cannot create duplicate local items before the binding lands [prior art: K8s read-all-then-write].
- [ ] Level-triggered: `unbound = fetched_keys - bound_keys` each pass (replaces the `prev_snapshot` edge-trigger), so a failed adoption re-fires until it binds. Do NOT rely on `prev_snapshot` for the trigger.
- [ ] Proven by the convergence property with an issue present in BOTH prev/curr snapshots and unbound (the exact steady-state cell the current suite never constructs).

## Implementation contract (foundation-first — read before coding)
DEPENDS ON amiss-bun-wince (baf7): this bug is the `ADOPT` / `SKIP_RETIRED` Decision cells of `classify()` plus the gated adopt handler. The trigger is LEVEL-based: `unbound = fetched_keys - bound_jira_keys` computed EVERY pass from the binding store — prev_snapshot plays NO role in the trigger (its unconditional advance at pass end stays as-is for now; the rollout ticket owns its future).
Adoption handler ORDER (ADR 0027 #4 — each step has an existing helper; do not reimplement):
1. `BindingStore.is_retired(jira_key)` -> Decision SKIP_RETIRED (prevents the delete/re-adopt loop with the GC bug 13eb).
2. rebar-id label audit (rebar_id_audit.py, L9) + label-derived-binding suppression (differ.py L10 region): an issue already carrying rebar-id:/rebar-id- is BOUND — route to binding repair, never double-create (the phantom jira-dig-NNNN defect).
3. Create local ticket + bind keyed on the EXTERNAL id (idempotency: a second overlapping pass must no-op); use the existing bind_pending -> create -> marker -> bind_confirm write-ahead protocol (binding_store.py docstring).
4. Immediately `set_baseline(local_id, adopted_fields)` (foundation method) so the FIRST outbound diff is empty — echo suppression per ADR 0027 #4c / ADR 0029 #3.
RED test (the exact cell today's suite never constructs): SAME key in prev_snapshot AND curr_snapshot, no binding -> assert ADOPT fires. Plus: retired key -> SKIP_RETIRED; labeled key -> no double-bind (L11 quarantine NOT tripped).
Live acceptance cell: REB-532 adopted (or explicitly archived in Jira as a test artifact — decide and record in a closing comment).
Files: classify.py (cells), apply_inbound.py or a new adopt handler beside dispatch_one.py, binding_store.py (consume, don't modify), fetcher.py (no changes — JQL already fetches unbound), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ + diffing/ + integration two-pass test.
baseline.summary: Reconciler never adopts a Jira-native issue at steady state (edge-triggered inbound-create + prev_snapshot proxy)

baseline.description:
Workflow gate ops re-resolve `LLMConfig.from_env()` independently instead of receiving the caller's resolved config, producing a DOCUMENTED correctness divergence: a library caller passing an explicit non-default `config=` has it honored for the LLM calls but the workflow verdict's `model`/`runner` fields still reflect the env config (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:78-79`).

## Why
Config resolution is a cross-cutting concern that should resolve once per run, not once per op. The current scatter silently ignores part of a caller's explicit configuration — a reliability/correctness gap for library/MCP consumers.

## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:113,329`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:60,104`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:89` — stop calling `LLMConfig.from_env(...)` per op.
- Resolve `cfg` once at the run boundary (`gate_dispatch.produce_*` / `review_plan`) and pass the `runner`/`model` identity into the ops as workflow `inputs` (the pattern already used for `ticket_id`), so ops read it from `ctx.inputs` rather than re-deriving from env. Keep `StepContext` config-agnostic (`executor.py:107-120`).

## Scope
In: single-resolution + thread model/runner identity through inputs; remove the documented divergence note. Out: redesigning `StepContext` to carry the full `LLMConfig` type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A caller passing an explicit `config=` sees that model/runner reflected in BOTH the LLM calls and the verdict's `model`/`runner` fields.
- [ ] No op calls `LLMConfig.from_env()` after the run boundary resolves it.
- [ ] The divergence caveat at `plan_review/__init__.py:78-79` is removed (no longer true).
- [ ] Existing plan-review/completion gate tests still pass.
baseline.summary: Honor caller's explicit LLMConfig in workflow gate ops

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps
1. Configure a Jira project whose workflow has a status with no entry in the reconciler's `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` map (e.g. a custom state like "In UAT").
2. Move a Jira issue bound to a **closed** local ticket into that unmapped status.
3. Run a reconcile pass with inbound sync enabled.

**Expected:** the unmapped status is skipped (local status left untouched) and the unmapped status is surfaced as a deduped bridge alert. **Actual (before fix):** `inbound_differ._map_jira_to_local_fields` did `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS.get(status_raw, "open")` — the `"open"` default silently REOPENED the closed local ticket. This class of bug bit once before (ticket 929a). Audit Reliability finding #7 (MEDIUM).

## Why it matters
Reopening closed work corrupts board state, re-enters tickets into ready/next-batch dispatch, and invalidates the meaning of completion attestations — all with no operator signal.

## What / files
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py`: `_map_jira_to_local_fields` no longer defaults an unmapped status to `"open"` — it OMITS the status field from the mapped dict when the Jira status has no `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` entry and no `rebar-status:` label. `_diff_jira_vs_local` skips the status field when it is absent from the mapped dict, so no status change is emitted (no silent reopen).
- Observability reuses the EXISTING fetcher alert: `fetcher.py` already emits a deduped `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` bridge alert (built from the same `config.jira_to_local_status` mapping) for any unmapped status seen in a snapshot — so no second, redundant alert is added in the differ (alert at fetch, skip at diff is the correct split).
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`: documents the skip + existing-alert behaviour for unmapped inbound statuses.

## Scope
In: inbound_differ.py skip logic, docs. Out: adding a redundant differ-side alert (the fetcher already alerts); changing any existing status mapping; the `idea↔IDEA` round-trip must stay unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An inbound Jira status with no mapping is skipped (no local status change) — a closed bound local ticket stays closed
- [ ] The unmapped status is surfaced via the existing deduped `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` bridge alert (no silent handling)
- [ ] Regression test: an unmapped inbound status against a **closed** bound local ticket emits no status change (`"status" not in changed`); mapped statuses (incl. `IDEA→idea`, `Done→closed`) still flow
- [ ] `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` documents the skip + alert behaviour
- [ ] Existing reconciler/bridge suites stay green; `make test` green
baseline.summary: Unmapped inbound Jira status defaults to open — can silently reopen closed local tickets

baseline.description:
## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `itchy-arbored-peccary` (3907-0110-7688-43bd), while verifying a handed-in claim that the janitor had no caller. It has one — but exactly one.

## Context / Problem

`start_background_janitor` has a single production invocation: the review-bot's FastAPI lifespan (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136`). So the janitor — the ONLY thing that reclaims `$REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR/rebar-gate-snapshots` — runs only inside the long-lived review-bot server process. Every other host that resolves an attested gate (a developer laptop running `rebar review-plan` / `review-code` / `verify-completion`, a CI runner, any library embedding that is not the review-bot app) populates the snapshot store and never reclaims it. Measured on one developer host: 64,021 entries, 47.24 GiB, nothing ever reclaimed. Bug 3907 fixed the *policy* (the `max_bytes` byte-total cap); this ticket is the *cadence* — on a non-review-bot host there is no pass to apply the policy.

## Operator ruling (design constraint)

Recorded verbatim in the comment below: an operation-linked GC trigger is acceptable, BUT it must avoid the long-lock pitfall we hit before (bug `0d15-59a4` — a sweep holding the ticket store lock for minutes), by using the same pattern that fixed it: a near-free in-process check on the tail of the operation, heavy work in a DETACHED child, stamp/lock sidecars for cadence and single-flight.

## Approach

Mirror `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` — the compaction sweep's operation-linked trigger, the pattern that fixed 0d15-59a4 — applied to the EXISTING snapshot-GC policy (`janitor.run_gc`: hysteretic watermark, grace window, cold-trim, `max_bytes` backstop).

New module `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py`:

- **Sidecars keyed on the snapshot store root** (`<store>/gc/last-pass.stamp` and
  `<store>/gc/worker.lock`), not on any repo/worktree path — the store is per-host and
  already canonical, so two worktrees of one repo share one clock and one lock (the
  dae7f62696 discipline, applied where this store actually lives).
- **`maybe_gc(repo_root)` — the operation-linked trigger.** Called on the tail of gate
  resolution (`gate_source.resolve_gate_handle`, the single choke point every attested gate
  op flows through — review-plan, verify-completion, review-code, scan-spec, workflows), for
  attested handles only. Its decision is O(1): one `stat` of the stamp (a02eedbb6e's marker
  fast-path discipline — no store enumeration, nothing that grows with entry count) against
  the janitor's existing `interval_seconds` cadence knob (`<= 0` disables the trigger). It
  takes NO ticket-store lock — it never imports or touches `rebar._store.lock` — and never
  raises (never fails the gate that triggered it).
- **Detached child** (`_spawn_detached_gc`, mirroring `_spawn_detached_sweep`): PYTHONPATH
  bootstrap, stdio to a log under `<store>/gc/`, durable cwd anchored at the snapshot store
  root (the d575600381 concern: never inherit an ephemeral worktree cwd), POSIX-only v1
  (win32 no-op, exactly like compact_trigger and enrich_drain).
- **Single-flight**: the trigger probes `worker.lock` (an `O_EXCL` file carrying the v2
  owner stamp, adjudicated by `lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale` — pid-recycle
  qualification and stale reclamation inherited, not re-invented) before spawning, and the
  child re-acquires it for real. `run_gc` additionally holds its own non-blocking `flock` on
  `<store>/gc/lock`, so overlap with the review-bot's resident janitor is harmless by
  construction (the loser returns `skipped="locked"`).
- **The stamp records only an actual pass** (the `run_sweep` lesson: a stand-aside must not
  reset the clock): the child stamps `last-pass.stamp` only when `run_gc` ran
  (`skipped is None`). The review-bot's resident janitor is untouched and keeps running;
  because its passes go through the same `run_gc`, hosts where it runs simply see fresh
  passes and the op-linked trigger stays quiet.

ADR 0005 D5 ("never invoked from populate/read") holds in spirit and is amended with a note: the trigger check on the gate-resolution tail is one stat, and the pass itself runs in a detached child off every hot path.

Portability (`project.portability`): the trigger is operation-linked and in-process — it requires no CI provider, no cron, no daemon; the review-bot's resident thread remains a supplementary cadence, not the floor.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py` (new): stamp/lock sidecar helpers, `maybe_gc`,
  `_spawn_detached_gc`, `run_detached` (the child entry point).
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/__init__.py`: export `maybe_gc`.
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py`: call `maybe_gc` on the tail of `resolve_gate_handle`
  (attested handles only, never-raise).
- `tests/unit/test_snapshot_gc_trigger.py` (new).
- `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`: document when a pass runs on a non-review-bot host and how
  an operator forces one (run the trigger's child entry point / set the interval).
- `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md`: D5 amendment note.

## Testing

RED-first (tests written and failing before the implementation), mirroring `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py`'s style (monkeypatched spawn capture; fake-`Popen` argv capture for the detach contract):

- **Trigger fires**: with a stale/missing stamp, `maybe_gc` spawns the detached GC; a
  gate-resolution wiring test asserts `resolve_gate_handle` invokes the trigger for an
  attested handle and not for a local one.
- **Near-free + lock-free on the quiet path**: with a fresh stamp, `maybe_gc` performs no
  directory enumeration of the store (does not scale with entry count) and touches no
  ticket-store lock (the store-lock acquire is patched to fail loudly).
- **Single-flight under contention**: a held `worker.lock` suppresses the spawn; a live
  lock is respected, a provably-stale one is reclaimed; overlap with a concurrent `run_gc`
  degrades to `skipped="locked"`.
- **Reclamation on a simulated non-review-bot host (the headline AC)**: a store with a cold
  entry and no resident janitor, spawn patched to run the child entry point inline →
  the entry is evicted and the stamp records the pass; a second immediate trigger stays
  quiet (failure/empty path: fresh stamp → no spawn, nothing evicted).
- **Detach contract**: fake `Popen` captures argv/kwargs — the child is handed the resolved
  store root, cwd is the durable store root, stdio is detached.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A host that runs attested gates WITHOUT the review-bot server reclaims its snapshot
      store: a gate resolution on a due stamp spawns a detached `run_gc` pass.
- [x] The trigger check is O(1) on the quiet path — no store enumeration, no ticket-store
      lock, never raises into the gate — and the GC pass itself runs in a detached child
      off the gate's critical path (ADR 0005 D5 amended with the reasoning).
- [x] The trigger is operation-linked and in-process — not dependent on any CI provider,
      cron, or daemon (`project.portability`).
- [x] Single-flight across simultaneous hosts/worktrees: stamped worker-lock sidecar +
      `run_gc`'s existing gc flock; double-running with the review-bot's resident janitor
      is harmless (`skipped="locked"`), and the resident janitor is not regressed.
- [x] A test observes reclamation happening on a simulated non-review-bot host — RED before
      the change, GREEN after.
- [x] `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` documents when a pass runs and how an operator forces
      one.
baseline.summary: Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host's store is append-only

baseline.description:
Jira reconciler silently fails to sync comments and inbound links while reporting `converged` — three distinct defects, all hidden behind a pass that counts failed sub-operations toward "applied N of N" and exits 0.

## Context

Investigation (/rebar-debug, 2026-07-17) established that status/existence sync is healthy (0 drift across ~1200 tickets), but three field-level sync paths are broken and invisible:

- **Comment sync (P1):** `get_comments()` returns only the first 50 of N comments
  (no `--paginate`), so outbound dedup re-posts the rest every pass. 13 tickets have
  been inflated to Jira's 5000-comment hard cap (local truth: 22-76 comments each);
  further adds fail `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and are swallowed.
- **Inbound link direction (P2):** `_diff_links_inbound` (inbound_differ.py:519-527)
  AND `_diff_link_removals` (outbound_links.py:198-203) both invert the
  inward/outward -> blocks/depends_on mapping. Latent since 2026-06-15 (`f6687adf4`);
  UNMASKED when the outbound direction fix landed (`6b25dbead`/`43d154523`, 07-16/17)
  — the two inversions previously cancelled on round-trip. Now ~815 inbound link
  applies/pass are cycle-rejected by rebar's guard.
- **Observability (meta):** a pass with failed sub-ops still prints `applied N of N`
  / exits 0 / logs `converged`. The `RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP` flag (default off)
  exists but is not enabled; swallowed comment failures land in `comment_errors` and
  are never counted as failures.

## Jira cleanup safety plan (T4 — destructive-step rollback)

The comment de-duplication is IRREVERSIBLE (Jira comment deletion cannot be undone via API). It is a deliberate, justified destructive step (the tickets are permanently unable to sync until duplicates are purged), executed only with these guardrails:

- [ ] **Pre-deletion backup:** export the FULL comment payload (id, body, author,
      created) for all 13 tickets to a versioned JSON artifact BEFORE any deletion, so
      any comment can be re-created if needed.
- [ ] **Dry-run first:** the cleanup script has a `--dry-run` (default) mode that
      lists exactly which comment IDs would be deleted and which one canonical copy of
      each distinct body is kept; a human reviews the dry-run diff before `--execute`.
- [ ] **Keep-one dedup rule:** for each distinct normalized body, keep the OLDEST
      copy (lowest created) and delete the rest; never delete a body with only one copy.
      Only delete comments authored by the bridge bot identity (never human comments).
- [ ] **Idempotent + resumable:** re-running is safe; on partial failure, re-run
      `--dry-run` to see the remaining duplicates and resume. Deletions are logged
      (ticket, comment id, body hash) to an artifact as they happen.
- [ ] **Sequencing:** run ONLY after P1 is deployed to main, else the buggy
      reconciler re-inflates duplicates within minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child tickets (P1, P2, observability, test-hardening, Jira-cleanup) are closed.
- [ ] A reconcile pass shows 0 comment-cap failures and 0 inbound link
      cycle-rejections for the previously-affected tickets.
- [ ] The cleanup backup artifact + dry-run log exist before any live deletion.
- [ ] P1: outbound comment sync is idempotent — a steady-state pass emits 0 comment
- [ ] P2: an inbound Jira `Blocks` link round-trips to the correct rebar relation
- [ ] Observability: a pass with any silent sub-op no-op reports failure (non-zero
- [ ] Test hardening: unit + integration + E2E coverage added for all three failure
- [ ] Jira data cleanup: the 13 capped tickets are de-duplicated so new comments can
baseline.summary: Jira reconciler: silent comment + inbound-link sync failures

baseline.description:
## Symptom

Gerrit change 1416 (ticket fd30) earned `LLM-Review +1` but `Verified -1`. The failing step was `Git version floor gate` in `build-and-test / pytest`, with:

    ##[error]missing .github/git-version-floor.txt (the single source of the Git version floor)

The change touched only `Makefile`, `docs/local-dev-env.md` and `docs/user-guide.md` -- nothing related to git versions.

## Root cause

`.github/git-version-floor.txt` was introduced by ticket 980d ('declare and enforce the Git 2.38+ floor'). The Gerrit Verified lane takes the workflow **definition** from the target branch (main, which now has the gate) but checks out the **change's tree** (which predates the file). So the gate runs against a tree that cannot contain its own input.

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` already documents this exact hazard and its remedy under ticket ee2a -- the 'Definition-vs-tree skew guard': a new gate step that consumes a repo file must skip, with a log line, when that file is absent from the checked-out tree, then re-enforce on rebase and on every post-merge change. The `raw-git-write` gate implements it. The Git version floor gate does not.

## Impact

Every open change whose base predates 980d gets a spurious `Verified -1` and must rebase, even when its diff is unrelated. This is noise that trains agents and humans to treat `Verified -1` as 'probably just rebase', which erodes the value of the gate.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the floor gate's step in the same if-present guard the raw-git-write gate uses: when `.github/git-version-floor.txt` is not in the checked-out tree, echo a skip line and pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Git version floor gate skips (with a log line) when `.github/git-version-floor.txt` is
      absent from the checked-out tree, and enforces normally when present.
- [ ] A change based before 980d no longer earns `Verified -1` for this reason.
- [ ] A survey of other gate steps added since ee2a confirms each either consumes no repo file or
      carries the guard.
baseline.summary: Git version floor gate lacks the ee2a if-present guard, so it fails every change based before 980d

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Plan review and code review currently make discovery decisions through partially independent registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, and failure paths. This lets one review schedule disabled built-ins, omit activated project DET criteria, ignore project applicability or an authored budget, and mistake failed work for a successful checkpoint. The recovered RP-06 design and the completed research on `rubellite-secondary-cub` establish that these are policy-ownership defects, not merely duplicated code.

The durable intent sources are session log `supporting-chummy-snake`, recovery ticket `irascible-clueless-basenji`, and the approved decisions recorded on `rubellite-secondary-cub`. RP-01 remains authoritative for request-local provider retry, context, output-size, and structured-output behavior; this epic does not create another provider retry loop or truncate authoritative review input.

## Outcome and Architecture
Implement one review-discovery architecture:

`CriteriaSnapshot -> gate-owned strategy -> DiscoveryStagePlan -> shared executor -> DiscoveryStageResult -> gate-owned verdict policy`

One immutable repository-bound effective-policy snapshot includes built-ins, project LLM criteria, project DET criteria, routing, prompts, posture, applicability, and a digest. Gate strategies retain their own context and topology rules. The shared executor owns typed unit outcomes, usage, budget enforcement, cancellation, and success-only checkpoint mechanics; it does not choose applicability, truncate inputs, retry provider turns, or decide a gate verdict.

The final failure policy continues independent work after RP-01 exhausts a local operation, retains successful findings, skips dependency-blocked work with provenance, and returns unsigned `INDETERMINATE` when blocking-capable coverage is missing unless a real blocking finding takes precedence. Advisory-only gaps may still pass. Systemic configuration, cancellation, deterministic-floor, and whole-tier failure behavior remains fail-safe.

## Required Behavior
- Project code-review LLM criteria require a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative globs; `["**"]` means repository-wide. Migrate `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]` without changing its current membership, and as part of that migration audit and update any documentation, examples, or config references that cite the old empty-list (`[]`) glob semantics so none remain stale after the explicit-repository-wide convention lands.
- Built-in criteria retain their established secondary-trigger semantics, project DET remains detector-selected, and plan-review project criteria retain `applies_at` and `trigger` semantics.
- Positive explicit `usd_budget` values are authoritative on both gates. For code review, omission is uncapped. For plan review, omission preserves the existing plan-review budget policy: the current authored/default per-review budget cap continues to apply (omission is not uncapped for plan review), so this epic changes no plan-review budget-omission behavior. On both gates zero remains invalid and never acts as a disable switch.
- Preserve code review sequential execution, no code-review checkpoints, base-reviewer payloads, one-hop Round B, and authored YAML/BPMN topology.
- Preserve plan review chunking, concurrency, cache warming, checkpointing, container/prerequisite stages, and cancellation behavior while moving to a new digest-complete success-only checkpoint namespace. Legacy checkpoints never seed the new path.
- Persist a versioned typed discovery trace for retry, audit, and diagnostics. Review and review-status responses remain narrow end-result contracts and do not expose per-unit debugging detail, raw prompts, ticket content, provider payloads, or secrets.
- Add `rebar review-plan --retry`: only the literal latest completed `INDETERMINATE` review with retryable missing calls is eligible; reuse content-identical successes, retry only missing calls, and grant each explicit retry a fresh attempt budget. Changed or unreadable lineage refuses with zero calls. `--retry` is incompatible with `--force`, `--status`, and `--check`, while `--no-sign` remains compatible.
- Document `--retry` in canonical CLI help, generated command reference, the user guide, the plan-review gate guide, and exit-code guidance.
- The workflow editor shows editable Authored Workflow separately from read-only Effective Policy.

## Migration and Rollback
Use expand-contract without duplicate model calls: compute the legacy and new deterministic projections from the same observed calls, compare selection/order/context/model/budget/posture/usage/checkpoint decisions, and allow only approved deltas. Keep the legacy projection non-default during the compatibility window so a code revert can restore it; do not add an operator configuration flag solely for rollback. New code ignores legacy checkpoint envelopes, and old code ignores the new namespace.

## Testing
Each child begins with the smallest RED oracle that crosses its real seam: in-process policy and executor tests, real producer-to-consumer contract tests for journals and verdicts, real CLI subprocess tests for `--retry`, workflow-editor tests for authored/effective separation, and a final live review exercise because this epic cuts over production LLM paths. Stateful fault tests assert exact partial results, collateral state, and clean retry behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Both review gates derive selection from one immutable effective-policy snapshot, including effective built-in retunes/disables and activated project LLM/DET criteria.
- [x] The shared discovery executor emits typed success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, and cancelled outcomes; only success/resumed outcomes can seed the new checkpoint namespace.
- [x] Code review preserves its scheduler, base-reviewer, topology, and narrow response contracts while enforcing approved applicability, budget, and partial-failure behavior.
- [x] Plan review preserves its scheduler, cache, topology, and narrow response contracts while using digest-complete journals and approved partial-failure behavior.
- [x] `rebar review-plan --retry` reuses eligible successes, retries only missing work with a fresh budget, refuses all stale/ineligible lineages before any model call, and is documented on every canonical operator surface.
- [x] The workflow editor separates editable Authored Workflow from read-only Effective Policy and rejects an empty project code-review LLM glob list with the `["**"]` remedy.
- [x] Cross-gate shadow traces show only approved behavior deltas, and a live end-to-end exercise proves the defaulted discovery paths against a real supported provider before the epic closes.
baseline.summary: RP-06 — Unified effective-policy discovery for review gates

## Problem

The Jira API-token outage took the Reconcile Bridge down and produced **zero CloudWatch signal**. The bridge runs on GitHub Actions, not on the monitored host, so nothing in `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (the host probe that publishes every `rebar/host` metric) can see it. Its only failure surface today is `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:264-279` ("Notify on bridge failure"), which writes a step summary and an `::error` annotation — visible only to someone already looking at the run. GitHub Actions *can* publish to CloudWatch; nothing in this repo does it yet.

## Design

**(a) Publish the metric from the workflow.** Add to the `reconcile` job in `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`:

- `id-token: write` at **job** level (the workflow-level block at :58-60 is `contents: write` +
  `actions: write`; job-level is where `structured-output-baseline.yml:39-41` puts it for the
  same reason).
- an OIDC credential step mirroring `structured-output-baseline.yml:60-67`
  (`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6`, `role-to-assume` + `aws-region` from repo
  `vars`), gated on `always()` so it is present on both the success and failure paths, and on
  the canonical repo + the var being set so forks and unconfigured checkouts skip it.
- `bridge_run_failures = 1` on `if: failure()`, and `= 0` on `if: success()`, both
  `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace rebar/host --metric-name bridge_run_failures
  --unit Count --value <n>`, dimensionless on both sides (`monitoring_s4b.tf`: a dimension on
  only one side silently unmatches the alarm).

*Why publish 0 on success rather than relying on missing-data semantics:* with `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` a failure-only metric would alarm correctly, but the metric would be absent whenever things are healthy — indistinguishable from "the publisher itself is broken/unauthorized", and the alarm would sit in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` rather than `OK`. The success-path 0 makes the *publisher* continuously observable, matching the existing host probe, which publishes `gerrit_healthy`/`reviewbot_healthy` as 0-or-1 every tick rather than only on failure (`observability.sh:45-51`). Telemetry steps are `continue-on-error` so a metric publish can never fail an otherwise-converged reconcile pass.

**(b) IAM.** Do **not** widen `rebar-terraform-plan` (`iam.tf:144-199`, `ReadOnlyAccess` + `kms:Decrypt` — it is the drift-detection role and single-owner) and do not widen the Bedrock CI role. Add a **new** narrowly-scoped role in `infra/terraform`, reusing the repo's existing OIDC pattern: trust `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` (`oidc.tf:14`) with the same `aud = sts.amazonaws.com` + `sub` StringLike `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` conditions, and one inline policy granting **only** `cloudwatch:PutMetricData`, constrained by the standard `cloudwatch:namespace` StringEquals condition to `rebar/host`. PutMetricData takes no resource ARN, so the namespace condition is what makes it narrow.

**(c) Alarm.** A new CloudWatch alarm on `rebar/host:bridge_run_failures`, styled on the `rebar-autodeploy-*` alarms (`monitoring_autodeploy.tf:113-150`): `Sum`, dimensionless, `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`, SNS `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`, description naming the runbook action (open the workflow run; check Jira token validity). Cadence differs deliberately from the autodeploy 900s/threshold-0: the bridge runs every ~20 min, so a single failed pass is routinely a transient network/API blip, while the token outage was sustained. `period = 3600` with `threshold = 1` / `GreaterThanThreshold` alarms on the **second** failed pass within an hour — a flake stays quiet, a real outage pages within ~40 minutes.

## Testing

- `actionlint .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` and `zizmor .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`
  (workflow edits are gated on both in CI).
- `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` (validate previously caught
  an over-cap `alarm_description`; the 1024-char limit applies).
- `pytest tests/scripts -q` for the unchanged script suites (no regression from the workflow edit).
- The apply itself is operator-run; post-apply proof is
  `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names rebar-bridge-run-failures` returning the alarm.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `reconcile-bridge.yml` publishes `rebar/host:bridge_run_failures` = 1 on `if: failure()` and
      0 on `if: success()`, authenticated by OIDC via repo `vars`, skipped outside the canonical
      repo, and `continue-on-error` so telemetry cannot fail a converged pass. Checked:
      `actionlint` + `zizmor` clean on the edited workflow.
- [x] A new IAM role in `infra/terraform` grants exactly `cloudwatch:PutMetricData` conditioned on
      `cloudwatch:namespace = rebar/host`, federating the existing
      `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github`. Checked: no diff widens `rebar-terraform-plan` or
      the Bedrock CI role (`git diff` touches neither).
- [x] An `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` on the new metric exists, dimensionless, with
      `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`, SNS `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`, and a description
      naming the runbook action (open the workflow run; check Jira token validity). Checked:
      `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` pass.
- [x] Change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
- [x] The operator has run `terraform apply` for the new role + alarm and the alarm exists in
      CloudWatch. **This AC is the operator's apply; the implementing agent cannot satisfy it.**
      Checked: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names rebar-bridge-run-failures`.
baseline.summary: Publish bridge run failures to CloudWatch and alarm
