## Context / Problem

The deterministic Pass 3 of code-review ignores project routing. `code_review_decide` passes `registry.threshold_for` as a bare callable and calls `registry.nit_suppressed_criteria()` with no arguments (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:419,427`), so both read the **packaged** routing map and a project overlay's threshold / blocking / nit-suppression re-tunes are dropped — even though those resolvers already accept an optional routing map (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:309-343`) and `registry.effective_routing(repo_root)` already exists on `origin/main` (`registry.py:171-176`). Third of five seams (root cause on superseded bug 8a4b).

## Approach

Pure wiring — thread the repository-effective routing map into the two Pass-3 resolvers:

- In `code_review_decide`, compute `routing = registry.effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)`
  (`ctx.repo_root` is already used in this function at `workflow_ops.py:414`).
- Bind that map into the `threshold_for` callable handed to `pass3_over_findings` (e.g.
  `functools.partial(registry.threshold_for, routing_map=routing)`), and pass it to
  `registry.nit_suppressed_criteria(routing)`.

No `registry.py` change is needed — the optional `routing_map` parameters landed with story 5065, and `effective_routing` is on `origin/main` today (cited above).

**Rejected alternative.** Re-implementing routing resolution inside `workflow_ops` — the shared resolvers already exist and are the single source of truth; duplicating them would diverge from plan-review's routing semantics.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — thread `effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)` into the
  Pass-3 `threshold_for` binding and `nit_suppressed_criteria` call.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` — extend this shared test file (a new file
  first created earlier in the stack; this ticket appends its Pass-3 routing cases). This ticket
  **depends on** child 2 `[rebar:761e-5af2-ed57-408a]`, which will introduce both the synthetic-repo
  fixture and the logical `project.<name>` attribution on code-review findings; the Pass-3 tests
  here consume a finding carrying that logical id.

## Testing

- Happy path (routing): a synthetic repo re-tunes `project.foo` (lower block threshold + blocking,
  and separately `nit_suppressed`); assert Pass 3 blocks / demotes the project finding per the
  **project** routing, not the packaged default. The routed finding carries the logical
  `project.foo` id that child 2 `[rebar:761e-5af2-ed57-408a]` will attribute.
- Parity: with no overlay, Pass-3 dispositions are byte-identical to today (packaged-default path).

Tier: unit; feeds deterministic findings (carrying logical `project.foo`) through `code_review_decide` with a synthetic effective routing — no LLM.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Project routing (threshold / blocking / nit-suppression) governs the deterministic Pass 3
      for a project finding; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k routing`.
- [ ] With no overlay, Pass-3 dispositions are unchanged (parity); verified by the same `-k routing`
      selector asserting the packaged-default path.
baseline.summary: Thread repository-effective routing into code-review Pass 3

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
An LLM plan review can consume the full model cost, return `PASS`, and still leave the reviewed ticket without a signed plan-review attestation unless signing was separately requested. That discards the review's durable gate artifact: the subsequent claim path cannot distinguish the paid, passing review from no review at all and may require another billable run or a manual recovery step.

The intended contract is already stated by the dedicated `rebar review-plan` documentation and library docstring: a non-blocking PASS signs the plan-review attestation consumed by the claim gate. All public routes that perform the same billable plan review must converge on one default: sign a fresh attestation after PASS. Deliberately skipping the signature must be explicit, visible, and exceptional.

**Scope decision (2026-07-24): MCP is OUT of scope for this epic.** The MCP `review_plan` tool derives signing from server read-only mode (`sign=not ro`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) and exposes no caller-facing `sign` parameter. Adding one — plus the machine-readable read-only unsigned reason — is a distinct public-contract change to a different boundary, with its own generated-reference and tool-schema consequences. It is split out rather than carried here. This epic now covers the **CLI** and **library** plan-review boundaries only.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create or select an open, non-exempt ticket with a reviewable plan and no current plan-review attestation.
2. Run the plan-review operation through a public plan-review route without an explicit no-sign option.
3. Allow the LLM review to complete with verdict `PASS`.
4. Run `rebar verify-signature <ticket-id> --output json`.
5. Observe that verification reports the ticket as unsigned even though the full review cost was incurred and no opt-out was requested.

## Expected Behavior
Every mutating public plan-review entry point signs and persists a plan-review attestation by default when the final verdict is a signable, non-degraded `PASS`. The attestation binds the reviewed material fingerprint and verified source SHA exactly as the claim gate expects.

Skipping signing requires an explicit opt-out at the relevant boundary: `--no-sign` for CLI use, `sign=False` for library use. The output clearly states whether the attestation was signed and, when deliberately skipped, why.

## Actual Behavior
The default behavior is correct on the CLI and library routes, but nothing at the real parser/API boundary PINS it: a future refactor could silently flip the default with no test failing. The signing default is therefore an undefended invariant rather than a defect in itself.

## Approach
1. Inventory the CLI dispatcher, the dedicated `review-plan` command, and the library `review_plan` call paths and identify where the default changes or the signing wrapper is bypassed.
2. Route every mutating plan-review surface through the same sign-on-PASS finalization seam. Keep the structural guards that prohibit signatures for BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, local/unattested-source, and otherwise non-signable results.
3. Make deliberate unsigned execution explicit at each public boundary. CLI exposes `--no-sign`; the library exposes `sign=False`.
4. Preserve idempotent reuse of an already-current attestation. A default invocation should neither rerun the LLM nor emit a duplicate signature when the claim gate already accepts the current attestation.
5. Preserve signing-failure behavior: a PASS whose signature persistence was attempted but failed is not reported as ordinary success. It returns the established retryable failure disposition and points to the non-LLM `sign-review` recovery path when the PASS sidecar remains current.
6. Update user, CLI, and LLM-framework documentation so the default, opt-out syntax, non-signable verdicts, and recovery behavior match the implementation.

Rejected: leaving signing opt-in to avoid ticket writes. The review is already a gate operation whose purpose is to produce the claim-consumable attestation; callers needing a pure read have an explicit no-sign mechanism. Rejected: signing BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, or local-source results, because those are not certifiable PASS outcomes. Rejected (2026-07-24): carrying the MCP `sign` opt-out here — see the scope decision above.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`
- plan-review dispatcher/finalization modules found during the call-path inventory
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`
- library surface tests for plan review
- `docs/cli-reference.md`
- `docs/user-guide.md`
- `docs/llm-framework.md`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`

Explicitly NOT in scope: `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, MCP surface tests, and generated MCP reference inputs/outputs.

## Testing / Verification
- Unit tests cover sign-on-PASS and never-sign verdict/source guards at the shared finalization seam.
- CLI tests exercise default signing and explicit `--no-sign` through the actual argument parser and dispatcher.
- Library contract tests exercise default `sign=True` and explicit `sign=False`.
- An end-to-end lifecycle test runs a passing plan review through the real CLI route, verifies the resulting signature, and then proves the claim gate accepts it without a second LLM call.
- Documentation/help drift checks pin the default and every supported opt-out/recovery path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A non-exempt ticket receiving a non-degraded PASS through each mutating public plan-review entry point (CLI `review-plan`, library `review_plan`) gets a persisted plan-review attestation by default; interface tests verify the attestation is present and claim-valid.
- [ ] An end-to-end lifecycle test invokes the real CLI `review-plan` route without an opt-out, verifies the attestation matches the current material fingerprint, and proves a subsequent `rebar claim` succeeds without another LLM call.
      (Note: the epic's original wording named an "affected `rebar review` plan route". No such
      route exists — `rebar review` is the separate `review_ticket` op, `_cli/__init__.py:413` —
      so the e2e was written against the real `review-plan` CLI route.)
- [ ] CLI unsigned execution requires the explicit `--no-sign` flag; parser tests prove omission signs and presence deliberately skips signing.
- [ ] Library unsigned execution requires explicit `sign=False`; contract tests prove the default is `sign=True`.
- [ ] BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, and degraded results remain unsigned, and explicit `sign=False`
      withholds the signature; table-driven tests verify each guard, including a direct
      `attest.sign_plan_review` refusal test so the guard is pinned at the artifact that owns
      it rather than at one caller.
      **Scope amendment (2026-07-24, audited):** this criterion originally also asserted that
      *exempt* and *unattested local-source* results remain unsigned. Investigation proved
      BOTH assert behavior that does not hold on current main, and each is a defect in its own
      right rather than missing coverage of this epic's invariant. They are DELEGATED, not
      dropped:
      - `--source local` signs a claim-valid attestation with `verified_at_sha=None` ->
        5128-0856-d80f-4eb6 (melancholy-firstborn-shihtzu). Root cause proven; repair blocked
        on a suite-wide decision (the offline suite defaults to `source=local`).
      - a `bug` returns `runner='pydantic_ai'`, runs a full review and signs, so the
        `runner != "exempt"` guard never engages -> 26a4-a0e8-e539-464d (quibbling-bionic-olm).
      Pinning either as-is would have encoded a defect as expected behavior.
- [ ] A PASS with an attempted signature-persistence failure returns the established retryable nonzero disposition and identifies `sign-review` as the recovery path; `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py` verifies the behavior.
- [ ] Re-running the default operation with a current claim-valid attestation reuses it without an LLM call or duplicate signature event; an interface test verifies both conditions.
- [ ] `rebar review-plan --help` states that PASS signs by default and names the explicit unsigned exception; a help drift test verifies the generated text.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` accurately describe sign-on-PASS, explicit opt-out, never-sign outcomes, and `sign-review` recovery; documentation checks pass.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Plan review PASS does not sign an attestation by default on every public route

baseline.description:
## Context

Replace GitHub-only `gh workflow disable/enable` safety around destructive repair with durable, provider-neutral pause ownership. Preserve both `rebar fsck --repair` and `rebar doctor --repair` without changing their public vocabulary, existing repair effects, or non-repair behavior.

Use the durable `refs/reconciler/gate` control shipped by story `1104`. Add `read_pause_with_oid(...) -> tuple[dict[str, object], str] | None` to read one ref OID and decode the pause document from that same object. Preserve existing `read_pause(...)` callers by delegating to the new seam and discarding only the OID.

The repair sequence is fail-closed:

1. Resolve `who` through `identity._git_email(repo_root)`. Missing identity aborts before any pause
   write or repair with `Error: <surface> repair requires a configured git user.email`.
2. Read the durable gate. Any pre-existing pause is foreign; abort without clearing it.
3. Generate `repair:<surface>:<uuid4>` once. CAS-write it and record ownership only after success.
4. Run the existing provider-neutral `refs/reconciler/lock` in-flight check. HELD, corrupt, timeout,
   transport failure, authentication failure, or uncertainty aborts the repair.
5. Run the existing repair only after both safety checks succeed.
6. In `finally`, reread pause document and OID as one snapshot. Clear only if its reason equals this
   invocation's token. Pass that observed OID to the existing `release(..., oid=observed_oid)` CAS.

A missing, replaced, or changed pause after ownership is an error. Do not recreate it. Do not clear another actor's pause. Do not retry against a fresh OID. A clear failure leaves the bridge paused for explicit operator recovery. This keeps the currently working GitHub safety behavior while also covering local, Jenkins, GitLab, and bare environments without a `gh` binary.

## Plan

1. Inventory both repair surfaces and dynamic/string references to existing pause helpers.
2. Add RED-first backend tests for the one-snapshot pause/OID read and legacy read compatibility.
3. Add RED-first public command tests for ownership, lock uncertainty, mutation, and cleanup.
4. Physically hold out edge and end-to-end tests from the implementation worker.
5. Implement one shared repair-owned pause context used by fsck and doctor.
6. Remove the GitHub CLI workflow-disable/enable dependency from destructive repair.
7. Update release notes with the provider-neutral safety contract and operator recovery behavior.
8. Run focused tests, lint, typecheck, module-size, and full project gates.

This composes pause acquisition, lock inspection, destructive mutation, and CAS cleanup, so reuse the existing shared concurrency fixtures where applicable. Add a two-clone contention regression for ownership replacement during repair; do not build a bespoke contention harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_ref_lock.read_pause_with_oid` reads the pause ref OID exactly once.
- [x] `_ref_lock.read_pause_with_oid` decodes the document from that observed OID.
- [x] Existing `_ref_lock.read_pause` behavior remains compatible.
- [x] `fsck --repair` uses the durable pause ref before destructive mutation.
- [x] `doctor --repair` uses the same repair-owned pause contract.
- [x] Neither repair surface requires a `gh` binary.
- [x] Missing git email aborts before pause creation.
- [x] Missing git email aborts before destructive mutation.
- [x] A pre-existing pause aborts repair.
- [x] A pre-existing pause is never cleared by repair.
- [x] Pause creation uncertainty aborts repair.
- [x] A held reconciler lock aborts repair.
- [x] A corrupt or indeterminate reconciler lock aborts repair.
- [x] Lock transport or authentication uncertainty aborts repair.
- [x] Destructive mutation begins only after this invocation owns the pause.
- [x] Destructive mutation begins only after the lock check reports safe.
- [x] Successful cleanup compares the pause reason to the invocation token.
- [x] Successful cleanup deletes by the same observed OID used for the reason check.
- [x] A missing pause during cleanup returns nonzero without recreating it.
- [x] A replaced or changed pause is never cleared.
- [x] A cleanup CAS miss is surfaced without retrying against a new OID.
- [x] A cleanup failure leaves the durable pause for operator recovery.
- [x] A bare-remote test proves canonical sync is blocked while repair owns the pause.
- [x] Local, GHA-shaped, Jenkins-shaped, GitLab-shaped, and bare invocations share pause behavior.
- [x] A two-clone test proves ownership replacement cannot clear another actor's pause.
- [x] Existing fsck repair postconditions remain unchanged after safe entry.
- [x] Existing doctor repair postconditions remain unchanged after safe entry.
- [x] Non-repair fsck and doctor behavior remains unchanged.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_ref_backend.py`
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py`
- focused new fsck/doctor repair ownership tests
- `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`
- `docs/release-notes.md`
baseline.summary: Make destructive repair pause ownership provider-neutral

baseline.description:
Store the baseline in the projection the comparison already computes: `description` as `normalize_rich_text(raw)`, `status`/`priority` as `.name`. Expected ~-66% on an **18.3 MB** (18,257,550-byte) file. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why this is safe without a comparator change
`outbound_field_diff.py:187,196` canonicalize BOTH sides at **read** time via `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` (docstring `:183`: "storage stays vendor-shaped, mapped at READ time only"), and both canonicalizers are idempotent on already-normalized values: `normalize_rich_text` (`inbound_fields.py:136-145`) returns `adf_to_text(body)` for dicts and `str(body)` otherwise; `_extract_jira_field_value` (`:92-96`) reads `name`/`displayName` for dicts and passes strings through. So ADF-dict and plain-text baselines canonicalize identically and a mixed store needs no new comparator. This also makes the change **revert-safe** — a normalized-string baseline round-trips unchanged through pre-A3 code.

CORRECTION carried forward: an earlier framing rested on `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields`, which have **zero production callers**. Validate against the live path only.

## Why assignee is EXCLUDED — data loss, not conflict noise
`_assignee_candidates` (`outbound_field_diff.py:56-67`) builds its match set from the scalar **plus every non-None identity form**, and `_suppressed_by_inbound` (`:250-256`) routes assignee through `_assignee_matches`. Collapsing three identity forms to one string shrinks that candidate set and loses inbound-directionality suppression, so local-wins **silently clobbers a concurrent remote assignee edit**. (The strict `assignee_identity` equality at `:390-394` is the lesser, secondary effect.) Keep assignee raw.

## Trap to pin
Store exactly `normalize_rich_text(raw)` — any other text extraction (fit/truncate/strip variants) diverges from what the same ADF decodes to on the read path and fabricates a permanent diff.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the **same
      verdict** as its normalized-string equivalent. Tier: **integration** through the real
      production comparison path. **This test does not exist today** —
      `test_binding_baseline.py:36-59` and `test_baseline_arbitration.py:91` use flat strings only, so
      a no-op-on-strings normalizer would leave them green while proving nothing. This is the RED case.
- [ ] The direction-preservation suite, extended with assignee shape cases (email / accountId /
      displayName), passes unchanged — proving assignee arbitration is untouched. Tier: **property/unit**.
- [ ] Baseline entries for `description`/`status`/`priority` are scalars after one pass; `assignee`
      remains a dict. Tier: **integration** asserting stored shapes.
- [ ] A corpus diff over real bindings shows **zero mutation delta** before vs after normalization.
      Tier: **repo-level corpus script**.
- [ ] `bindings.json` size drops by >=50%. Verify: byte comparison before/after one full pass.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py`

Scope: S-M. Depends on A2-1.

## Summary

`_decorate_outbound_comment` (`outbound_comments.py`) appends `RECONCILER_MARKER` AFTER the comment body. The outbound comment-limit truncation (`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`, `_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX = \" … [truncated by reconciler]\"`) then cuts the composed text at the 32767-char limit, which removes the trailing marker paragraph.

## Impact

A comment whose body exceeds the limit lands in Jira with NO marker. That comment is then:
- unrecognisable as the reconciler's own echo on the inbound side (the loop-breaker at `inbound_collection_diffs.py` tests for the marker in the body text), and
- unrecognisable to any tooling that identifies bot-authored comments by the marker.

## Evidence (live)

Found during the duplicate-comment cleanup (`darkish-enormous-raptors` / `76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5`). 836 Jira comments across REB-1567 (418), REB-1931 (278) and REB-2605 (140) are marker-less. Each is authored by the bridge bot accountId `712020:6471376f-4e5e-4ed2-8c05-330827bc387e`, is exactly 32767 rendered chars, ends in `_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX`, and repeats ~139 times identically. They had to be excluded from the marker-based cleanup as non-candidates.

## Expected vs Actual

- Expected: every outbound comment carries the marker regardless of body length.
- Actual: any comment over the limit loses it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Outbound truncation reserves room for the marker — truncate the BODY to (limit - len(marker) - len(suffix)) and append the marker after truncating, so the composed text is <= the limit AND ends with the marker.
- [x] Unit test: a body longer than the limit produces an outbound payload that is <= the limit and whose rendered text contains RECONCILER_MARKER. RED on current code.
- [x] Unit test: the truncation suffix is still present on a truncated body (the existing truncation contract is not broken).
baseline.summary: Outbound comment truncation drops the RECONCILER_MARKER, defeating the loop-breaker for >32767-char comments

## Context
Operator-specified (2026-08-12, verbatim): "The 8k cap should be pulling from a config key, defaulting to 8k. When a ticket is saved with a description over the configured cap (create or edit) and the plan review gate is enabled for the project (claim will fail without a passing review), we should display a warning at the time of save to give the client a heads-up that they'll need to edit the description. This provides a more immediate feedback loop instead of waiting for someone to try to run plan review."

Background: the plan-review admission guard (landed as 7cf80009d9) fast-fails reviews on descriptions over the limit. Tonight FOUR agents hit it blind at review time (8,001 / 8,001 / 8,180 / three children at 11k-22k) - the late feedback loop is measured waste.

## Correction to AC1 (recorded after code inspection)
AC1 is ALREADY SATISFIED on main by 7cf80009d9: the cap is the config key `verify.max_ticket_description_chars` (default 8000, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`), read by the review guard (`llm/plan_review/det_floor.py::_description_limit`, P4) and by the completion precheck (`llm/workflow/gate_ops.py`). No NEW key is introduced; the save-time warning becomes a THIRD reader of that same key, preserving single-sourcing. Scope of this ticket is therefore AC2-AC5 plus a test pinning the shared source.

## Implementation plan

1. `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py` (242 LOC, the single home of gate enablement) - add
   `description_cap_warning(description, ticket_type, *, ticket_id, repo_root) -> str | None`.
   It loads config once for `verify.max_ticket_description_chars`, returns None when the
   description is within the cap, and otherwise reuses the CLAIM path's existing probe
   `_plan_review_gate_applies()` (which wraps `gate_enabled("require_plan_review_for_claim")`
   and the `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` tuple) - no new probe invented. Returns None when
   the gate is off/exempt. Message states actual length, the cap, and that claim requires a
   passing plan review which refuses admission until the description is shortened. It never
   raises: any unexpected error returns None (the warning must never affect the write).

2. `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` - compute the warning AFTER the CREATE/EDIT event is
   appended (so the write is never altered or blocked) and return it:
   - `create_core` adds `"description_warning"` to its returned dict.
   - `edit_core` returns `str | None` instead of None (only when a description field was
     written); ticket type is read from compiled state / the edited `ticket_type` field.
   - `create_cli` / `edit_cli` print `Warning: <msg>` to **stderr** (the established CLI
     channel, mirroring the existing no-file_impact nudge in `create_cli`), stdout stays
     pure in both text and json modes, exit code stays 0.

3. `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` - `create_ticket` and `edit_ticket` emit the warning through
   the **rebar logger** (`logging.getLogger(__name__).warning`), the documented library
   channel (`_logging.py`; the `rebar` root carries a NullHandler, so an embedding caller
   opts in, and the CLI/MCP stderr handlers show it). `edit_ticket`'s return type widens
   from `None` to `str | None` (additive: None when there is no warning) so a programmatic
   caller can surface it - the same reasoning already documented on `link()`.
   `create_ticket(return_alias=True)` carries `description_warning` in its dict.

4. `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` + `_mcp_models.py` - surface it as a RESULT FIELD, exactly the
   `push_status` precedent (an MCP client reads only the tool result): add optional
   `description_warning: str | None = None` to `CreateResultOut` and `WriteAckOut` (both
   already `extra="allow"`, so this is a strict superset of today's shape), thread it from
   `create_ticket` and `edit_ticket`.

5. `docs/config.md` - extend the existing `verify.max_ticket_description_chars` entry to
   record that create/edit warn at save time when the value is exceeded and the claim gate
   is on. No new key, so no env-registry regeneration.

## Testing
Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_description_cap_warning.py tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py -q`, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`. New tests in `tests/unit/test_description_cap_warning.py`:
- over-cap + gate ON warns, on create and on edit, per surface: CLI stderr (capsys), library
  logger (caplog), MCP result field.
- over-cap + gate OFF: silent on all three.
- under-cap (and exactly at the cap - 8000 allowed, 8001 warns): silent.
- exempt ticket type (bug) with gate on: silent.
- config key respected: a non-default `verify.max_ticket_description_chars` moves the
  threshold, and the default is 8000; a test pins that the warning and the review guard
  read the SAME key.
- the write still succeeds and is unaltered when warning (ticket description round-trips).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1 - The admission cap reads from a config key defaulting to 8000, and the review guard and the new save-time warning read the SAME key (single source). (Key pre-exists: `verify.max_ticket_description_chars`.)
- [x] AC2 - On `create` and `edit` (CLI, library, MCP), when the saved description exceeds the configured cap AND the plan-review claim gate is enabled, a warning is emitted at save time stating the length, the cap, and that claim will require a passing review which refuses admission until the description is shortened. The save still succeeds.
- [x] AC3 - No warning when the gate is disabled, or when the description is within the cap; the warning never blocks or alters the write.
- [x] AC4 [operator-attested] - Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_description_cap_warning.py`: tests cover: over-cap+gate-on warns (create and edit, each surface's channel - CLI stderr, library logger, MCP result field); over-cap+gate-off silent; under-cap silent; config key respected and default correct.
- [x] AC5 [operator-attested] - docs/config.md documents the save-time warning; verified by `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/unit/test_description_cap_warning.py tests/unit/test_ticket_description_limit.py`.
baseline.summary: Config-driven description cap with save-time warning

## Problem

All four `AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT` / `bound-exceeded` firings on 2026-08-12 missed the `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` bound by a hair: `deferred_for` = 1810s, 1820s, 1810s, 1930s against a 1800s bound — overshoots of 10s, 20s, 10s and 130s. Each one killed an in-flight LLM-Review (the backfill reconciler retries it, but the gate stalls meanwhile), and they fired at ~10x the normal rate during a 60+-merge landing burst. The bound is sized for a steady-state review queue and is marginally too small for a burst; a bound that misses by 10s buys nothing that a slightly larger bound would not have caught for free.

## Where it lives

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:70-82` — the rationale comment + `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX="${DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX:-1800}"`.
  Commit 34cd pinned 1800s as **1.5x** `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (`DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
  = 1200`, `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:31`).
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py:399-420` —
  `test_defer_bound_default_outlasts_the_apps_own_per_review_cap` reads the shell default out of
  the script and asserts it against the app constant, so the two cannot drift. It currently pins
  the weaker `bound >= 1x` relationship.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:133` — an alarm-cadence comment restating `1800s`.

## Decision

Raise the default to **2400s = 2.0x `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`**, and tighten the pinned test from `>= 1x` to `>= 2x` so the new relationship is enforced rather than merely commented.

Why 2400 and not more: 2400s clears the worst observed overshoot (1930s) by 470s — ~3.6x the 130s miss — so all four firings would have deferred to completion. Why bounded at all: the saturated-trace analysis on `greasy-plucky-piranha` showed that under *sustained* pipelining an unbounded raise does not prevent the kill, it only defers it, while a deploy that never lands is its own outage. Anchoring the bound to a fixed multiple of the app's own per-review cap keeps it self-adjusting (raising `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` drags the bound with it, enforced by the test) instead of being a free-floating literal.

No terraform resource changes — the terraform edit here is comment-only, so nothing in this ticket requires an operator apply.

## The counter-argument, and why the raise is still bounded

`greasy-plucky-piranha` (7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9) closed with an explicit "I would not raise the bound". Its trace of the 03:03:04Z episode showed `in_flight` oscillating 2 -> 1 -> 2 and **never reaching 0 across 30 continuous minutes**: no single review outlived `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, the bound was outlasted by ordinary *pipelining*. Under that saturation a larger bound only defers the same kill. Tonight's sweep (`childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet` b902-18af-14ed-4da1, comment 12) presents only the terminal markers, not per-episode `in_flight` traces, so whether the four Aug-12 episodes were saturated the same way is **unestablished**.

This ticket therefore does not claim to fix saturated episodes. It claims the narrower thing the data does support: four firings missed by 10-130s, and a bound at 2.0x rather than 1.5x the per-review cap absorbs those margins. Where an episode really is saturated, 2400s defers the kill by 600s and no more — which is precisely why the raise is a fixed multiple of the app's cap and not an unbounded one. The underlying residue piranha carried forward (34cd's rationale treats a *concurrent gauge* as if it were a single-review timer) is NOT closed by this ticket and remains open on 7b4a's discovered_from chain.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q` — the pinned-relationship test and the
  full drain suite (the burst/bound scenarios drive the real script).
- `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` (comment-only change, but the
  gates still run).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` default is `2400` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:82`, its rationale
      comment rewritten to state the 2.0x relationship and cite the 2026-08-12 overshoot data
      (1810/1820/1810/1930s against a 1800s bound). Checked: `grep DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX:- infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`.
- [x] `test_defer_bound_default_outlasts_the_apps_own_per_review_cap` asserts
      `bound >= 2 * DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` — updated deliberately, not deleted — with the
      docstring carrying the rationale. Checked:
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q` passes.
- [x] The restated `1800s` figure in `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:133` reads 2400s.
      Checked: `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` pass; no resource attribute changes,
      so `terraform plan` is a no-op and **no operator apply is required for this ticket**.
- [x] Change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Raise the autodeploy deferral bound to 2x the review cap

# The parity flip/agreement criteria are gold-blind, so a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate

## Context / Problem

Criterion (b) of the parity bar has two parts, and BOTH compare the two arms to each other without ever consulting the gold label that the same corpus carries:

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `agreement = _rate(pairs, lambda p: p[0].decision == p[1].decision)`
* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `decision_flips = ... a.decision != b.decision` (gold pairs are
  selected on `a.label`, but the label is never used in the COMPARISON)

Recall and false-accept in the same function DO consult `label`. So the bar already knows which arm is right on every gold item, and criterion (b) deliberately throws that away.

Consequence, measured on the recorded live Bedrock run (`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`, re-scored offline with zero model calls after the 62ac false-accept fix): all THREE decision flips across both slots are cases where the CANDIDATE (Bedrock) matches gold and the BASELINE (direct Anthropic) does not.

| slot | case | spec | gold | v1 Anthropic | v2 Bedrock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard | R-drop-column-no-backfill | code-review-db-migrations | block | advisory | **block** |
| frontier | FP-rename-all-callsites-updated | code-review-api-compat | advisory | block | **advisory** |
| frontier | FP-create-index-concurrently | code-review-db-migrations | advisory | block | **advisory** |

Bedrock is correct in 3 of 3. The bar reports these as "decision-level flip(s) on the gold set (must be 0)" — the criterion documented as never acceptable because "it changes what ships".

The same three disagreements also drive the only other remaining failure: frontier verdict agreement 0.929. At the scored corpus size of n=28, the 0.95 floor tolerates at most ONE disagreement anywhere in the corpus (27/28 = 0.964 passes, 26/28 = 0.929 fails), so the agreement failure is not independent evidence — it is the same two cases counted again.

## Why it matters

This is a gating criterion on rebar's non-inferiority bar. As written it can fail a strictly better candidate. It is the sibling of bug 62ac (the inverted false-accept metric): both come from a metric that measures the wrong direction of the same underlying quantity. 62ac is fixed; this one is not, and it is now the sole remaining blocker on the Bedrock parity slots.

Note this ticket does NOT propose relaxing the bar to let Bedrock pass. It proposes that the criterion measure what it claims to measure — a regression in what ships — which requires consulting gold on a gold-labelled corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Decide and document whether criterion (b) should distinguish a gold-IMPROVING flip from a
      gold-REGRESSING one on gold-labelled items, and whether the agreement floor should be
      computed over non-gold items only (where no ground truth exists) or left as is.
- [x] If a change is made, a test pins the direction: a candidate that flips a gold item TOWARD
      the gold label is scored differently from one that flips it AWAY.
- [x] The recorded provider-parity results are re-scored offline against whatever bar results,
      with zero model calls, and the per-slot verdict recorded.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: parity flip + agreement criteria are gold-blind: a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate than the baseline

## Why

`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (~line 112) validates titles with `if not title:`, which is falsy only for the empty string — a whitespace-only title such as `"   "` is truthy and is accepted. Per the decision for this epic, whitespace-only titles must be rejected. Separately, cross-facade parity tests use only simple ASCII values, and the create path's empty/`>255` title rejection has code enforcement but only an edit-path test, leaving input-handling contracts thinly covered.

## What

Committed policy decisions (so the test oracle is unambiguous):
- **Whitespace validation:** reject a title iff `title.strip()` is empty (covers `""`,
  spaces, tabs, newlines). A title with surrounding whitespace but real content (e.g.
  `"  hi  "`) is ACCEPTED and **stored as-is** — validation must not silently mutate the
  value, so round-trip assertions expect the original bytes back.
- **Unicode normalization:** **preserve as-is (byte-identical round-trip); do NOT
  normalize** — with ONE documented pre-existing exception: `create_core`/`edit_core`
  already substitute `U+2192 (→)` → `->` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:121` and
  `:385`). That substitution is OUT OF SCOPE for this story and is retained; U+2192 is
  therefore EXCLUDED from the byte-identity corpus (or included only as an explicit
  "documented normalization" case asserting `→` becomes `->`). Composed (NFC) and
  decomposed (NFD) forms of the same string are otherwise treated as distinct values,
  each round-tripping unchanged — the oracle is per-form byte-identity, not cross-form
  equality.
- **Rejection identity (across facades):** "rejected identically" does NOT mean an
  identical wire representation — it means all three facades reject with the SAME
  human-readable message substring on their facade-appropriate surface: CLI → nonzero
  exit + message on stderr; library → `CommandError` (or the documented exception type)
  carrying the message; MCP → an error result carrying the message. The shared invariant
  is the message + "all three reject," not a shared exit code.

Then:
- Reject whitespace-only titles consistently across the CLI, library, and MCP
  create/edit surfaces.
- Add a create-path test for empty and `>255`-char title rejection.
- Add a curated cross-facade text corpus for values representable through all three
  facades; handle argv-impossible values (NUL) in library/MCP tests only.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (title validation)
- `tests/interfaces/facades/` (corpus + create-path validation tests)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A whitespace-only title (spaces/tabs/newlines) is rejected on create AND edit
      across CLI, library, and MCP, with a clear error.
- [ ] Create-path tests assert rejection of an empty title and a `>255`-char title.
- [ ] A title with surrounding whitespace + content (`"  hi  "`) is accepted and stored
      byte-identically (no silent trimming).
- [ ] A shared corpus (leading `-`/`--`, quotes, backslashes, LF/CRLF, emoji/non-BMP,
      NFC and NFD forms of one string as SEPARATE byte-identity cases, and a string of
      ≥1000 characters) round-trips byte-identically — EXCEPT U+2192, handled per the
      documented `→`→`->` exception — or is rejected identically (per the rejection-
      identity definition above) across all three facades; persisted/replayed content and
      structured output are asserted, with no stdout/stderr contamination.
- [ ] NUL / other argv-impossible values are covered via library/MCP tests only.
- [ ] Breaking-change handling: this is a user-visible tightening (callers passing
      whitespace previously succeeded). Document a back-out/expand-contract note. Run a
      concrete one-off store scan run pre-merge:
      `rebar list --output json | jq -e '[.[] | select(.title | test("^[[:space:]]*$"))] | length == 0'`
      (exit 0 = zero whitespace-only titles → no migration needed). If it exits nonzero,
      file a migration sub-task before landing.
- [ ] User-facing docs updated with concrete, grep-able artifacts: a `CHANGELOG.md` entry
      mentioning the whitespace-title rejection (`grep -qi 'whitespace' CHANGELOG.md`) and
      the CLI `create`/`edit` help text updated to state the non-empty-after-trim rule
      (verifiable by `rebar create --help` containing the rule).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Reject whitespace-only titles + create-path validation + cross-facade text corpus

# A dedicated `parent` verb, with `--force`

Raised while repairing an incident (88d9-fe42-e50f-4067) in which a reconcile pass cleared the `parent_id` of 63 tickets. Every prior parent was recoverable from the event log, but rebar had **no supported way to write most of them back**. Filed as an idea by operator direction: out of scope for that session.

## The gap

Hierarchy is edited only as a side effect of `edit`:

* `edit --parent` is the ONLY reparent path. There is no `parent` / `move` / `reparent` verb, and
  `link`/`unlink` cover the six link RELATIONS, not containment.
* `edit` has no `--force`, so the `--parent` cascade's refusal
  (`_commands/composer.py:503-513`, "cannot re-parent to closed ticket") is absolute.
* `rebar revert <ticket> <uuid>` does not help: `process_revert`
  (`reducer/_processors.py:456-488`) only appends to `state["reverts"]`; its sole state effect is
  un-archiving on REVERT-of-ARCHIVED. Reverting the offending EDIT leaves `parent_id` empty.
* `fsck-recover` is git-level dangling-write recovery, not semantic repair.
* `rebar.edit_ticket` shells out to the same CLI, so the library inherits the guard.

Net: the reconciler can DESTROY a parent edge automatically, but an operator cannot RESTORE one when the parent is closed — and the store has no supported route back to a state it previously held. The documented workaround ("reopen the parent first") means, at incident scale, reopening ~20 epics and re-closing them, which re-runs the LLM completion gate on already-signed closes and risks leaving a previously-closed epic open.

In this incident 61 of 63 affected tickets were closed and the current state was ACCEPTED by the operator on that basis; only the two non-closed tickets were repaired, and they were repairable precisely because their parents were still `open` / `in_progress`.

## Shape

A first-class `parent` verb owning containment, rather than a field on `edit`:

    rebar parent <child> <parent> [--force]
    rebar parent <child> --detach

with `--force` scoped to bypass ONLY a positively-known closed/inactive parent. Deliberately still enforced under `--force`: the parent must exist, no self-parent, no cycle, and the fail-closed branch for an UNVERIFIABLE status (`--force` overrides a KNOWN-closed parent, never an UNKNOWN one). Follows rebar's existing idiom (`claim --force`, `transition --force-close`): explicit intent, audited, never implicit.

Worth considering alongside it: whether `--force` should require a reason string (as `--force-close` does) so a hierarchy override leaves the same audit quality as a gate override.

## Why an idea rather than a bug

The capability gap is real but it only bites during repair of a defect that should not recur — the inbound parent clear that caused this incident was reverted, and its root cause (deciding a peer deletion from `managed_refs`, which cannot prove the peer ever had the ref) is being fixed separately. So this is a resilience/ergonomics improvement to reach for deliberately, not an urgent fix.
baseline.summary: Add a dedicated parent verb with --force, so a destroyed hierarchy is repairable

## Discovered from bug e548-5b35-7eb8-4727 (bolstered-afraid-ichidna)

While root-causing e548 it was proven that the failing test is **invisible to CI**, which is how the breaking change earned `Verified +1`.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py` guards the review-bot test with
  `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")`. Whole files do the same at module scope, e.g.
  `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py:20-21`.
- **No CI lane ever installs fastapi.** All three install steps in
  `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (lines 70, 219, 295) run
  `uv sync --locked --extra dev`. The `dev` extra contains no fastapi (verified by parsing
  pyproject: `dev has fastapi? False`); fastapi lives only in the `reviewbot` and `ui` extras
  (`pyproject.toml:93`, `:100`).
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:169` lists the isolation `specs=(...)` as
  agents / eval / tracing / grounding / metrics / mcp / union — **`reviewbot` is absent** — and
  that lane runs an import probe only, never pytest.
- Reproduced: `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra agents` then running the suite reports
  `SKIPPED [1] tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py:148: could not import 'fastapi'`.

## Why it matters

Every `rebar.review_bot` and `rebar.opcert_service` test — including SECURITY guards (the `/rerun` 502 stack-trace-exposure guard, the `X-Opcert-Guard` 403 auth guard, the 66af token redaction suite) — silently no-ops in CI. A change can break all of them and still be `Verified +1`. This directly contradicts the stated invariant in the `_optionality.yml:163-168` comment: "the isolation set is every key of `_optional.EXTRAS` — so a newly declared extra cannot ship with ZERO CI".

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A CI lane installs the `reviewbot` extra and RUNS the tests it unlocks (not just an import probe)
- [x] Proven by seeding a deliberate break in a review-bot test and observing CI go red
- [x] Consider a guard that fails the build when a `pytest.importorskip` skip is unlocked by no lane

## Resolution (change 1486, merged as 604e4e5d67)

- AC1: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` pytest job now installs
  `--extra dev --extra reviewbot --extra ui` and RUNS the suite; GH Actions run
  31178210685 is green on all four cells with the 38 tests executing.
- AC2: proven in the faithful form — with fastapi uninstalled,
  test_review_bot_token_redaction.py reports `4 skipped` today and `4 failed`
  under the guard; test_opcert_service_app.py goes from a whole-module skip to a
  collection ERROR. `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS=1` is set on both CI pytest steps, so
  the same loss in CI is a red build.
- AC3: implemented as tests/_extra_guard.py + tests/unit/test_extra_coverage_guard.py
  (a guard on tests NOT RUNNING, not on an extra being named in a workflow file).
baseline.summary: review-bot + opcert tests are permanently SKIPPED in CI: no lane installs the reviewbot extra

## Context
Maintained guidance conflates generic HMAC manifest signatures with current plan-review and completion-verifier operation certificates. ADR 0044 defines the DSSE and SSHSIG substrate. ADR 0049 defines asymmetric, environment-attributed operation certificates and legacy compatibility.

## Plan
- Use the existing file-impact set as the positive edit scope: `README.md`, `docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, and `docs/sample-ticket-log.jsonl`.
- Classify each gate-adjacent signature statement in those files as current operation-certificate guidance, generic HMAC manifest/API guidance, legacy HMAC compatibility, or historical migration evidence.
- Make every current plan-review or completion-verifier statement identify all four implemented facts: a DSSE envelope, SSHSIG signing, an Ed25519 key, and environment-attributed signer identity.
- Make every legacy HMAC compatibility statement say that the record remains readable but cannot certify a current gated operation.
- Preserve generic HMAC manifest-signing guidance for other consumers. In `docs/reuse-surface.md`, change only incorrect gate-consumer attribution while retaining the source-contract statements pinned by `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`, including the generic `sign_manifest` API and hex-HMAC `compute_signature` result.
- Preserve ADR and migration history. Keep `src/rebar/_cli/help/sign.txt` and `docs/llm-framework.md` unchanged because their current statements are accurate.
- Use a one-time repository search plus an auditable per-file classification comment to detect omissions. This is review evidence, not a persistent string gate or mechanical prose-quality policy.
- Do not add mechanical writing enforcement. Do not change the Markdown-only reduced test policy.

## Verification
- Run `rg -n "HMAC|DSSE|SSHSIG|operation[- ]certificate" README.md docs src/rebar/_cli/help/sign.txt`, classify every gate-adjacent hit, and record the path plus classification in a ticket comment. Any hit outside the positive edit set must be recorded as accurate, historical, excluded, or follow-up scope before completion.
- Review `git diff -- README.md docs/manifest-signing.md docs/event-schema.md docs/reuse-surface.md docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md docs/plan-review-gate.md docs/sample-ticket-log.jsonl` against the four-fact current-certificate checklist and the explicit non-certifying legacy-HMAC checklist. Record the completed checklist in the ticket comment rather than adding an automated wording gate.
- Run `python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check` to prove documentation links and index entries remain valid.

- Run `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py -q` to prove current and legacy signing lifecycle contracts remain green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every changed current-gate statement identifies DSSE, SSHSIG, Ed25519, and environment attribution.
- [x] Every changed legacy-HMAC statement explicitly says it cannot certify current gated operations.
- [x] Generic HMAC manifest/API statements retain their implemented non-gate meaning.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Create is the highest-risk operation: a timeout or local key-persistence failure can leave a real Jira issue without durable local identity, and replay can duplicate it. Existing write-ahead pending/keyed recovery contains many cases, but lifecycle writes occur across handlers rather than as plan intents. The new coordinator must use RP-02s single facade/recovery seam without inventing another identity owner.

## Outcome
Make the coordinator authoritative for outbound and inbound create plus their binding lifecycle intents. Preserve pre-create pending durability and index-lag grace. After Jira returns a key, attach the canonical `rebar-id:<local_id>` label first, attempt the optional entity property second, then persist/confirm through RP-02. If any containment/persistence step fails, safety-abort with the known key and never delete the successful Jira issue.

## Plan
1. Execute the plans pending-binding intent durably before any create call. A failure here makes zero provider calls and returns an item-scoped persistence failure.
2. Send create once within the shared logical budget. On commit-unknown timeout, re-observe only through replay-safe identity/query seams and otherwise defer; never blind-replay.
3. Once a key is returned, add the canonical label first. Treat the entity property as optional enrichment whose unsupported/permission failure is visible but cannot erase the label floor.
4. Persist the known key and confirmation through the RP-02 facade/repository unit-of-work. On failure, return a typed known-key safety abort; later keyed/keyless recovery converges without a duplicate.
5. Execute other lifecycle intents only after their remote postcondition is proven. Preserve create-before-link and hierarchy deferral, tombstone suppression, filtered/read-only behavior, and exact per-ticket tallies.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Failure cuts run before pending save, during create disconnect/timeout, after returned key, during label/property, and during known-key live replacement. Oracles include provider call count, remote labels/properties, exact local bytes, terminal disposition, and next-pass recovery.
- Duplicate probes run the whole crash/restart sequence twice for Cloud/DC fakes and assert one Jira issue.
- Index-lag fixtures retain the three-miss plus 3600-second conjunction and keyed recovery performs zero search.
- Dependency tests prove links/children wait for a proven create and independent tickets continue.

## Compatibility / rollback
Cut over create as one operation family; never run legacy and coordinator creates together. Before contract removal, a flag can return future creates to legacy behavior. Rollback never deletes remote issues. The explicit approved behavior change is label-first/property-second containment before local confirmation; preview/stored mutation shape remains compatible.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A failed pre-create pending save produces zero Jira calls and an item-scoped persistence outcome.
- [x] After a returned Jira key, the canonical label is attempted before optional property and local confirmation; every failure reports the known key without deleting the issue.
- [x] Create timeout/connection-loss cases never blind-replay; observation or a deferred pending record prevents duplicate creation across restart.
- [x] Cloud/DC crash-restart fixtures produce exactly one remote issue and converge to one confirmed forward/reverse binding.
- [x] Keyed recovery performs no search; keyless negative search requires both three misses and 3600 seconds; per-entry recovery failure does not stop unrelated tickets.
- [x] Lifecycle intents execute only after proven remote postconditions, while tombstones, filters, read-only modes, hierarchy, and create-before-link rules remain effective.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S4 — Coordinate create and binding lifecycle with label-first containment

# Live DC suite: residual assertions that cannot fail, or that can pass vacuously

## Provenance

Found by an independent verification pass over story `5200-e04e-246e-4aae`'s 18 acceptance criteria, commissioned while closing epic e369. Three findings from that pass were repaired immediately because they undermined the story's own evidence (the vacuous `08-assign` cell, the missing row-1 outbound cell, and the pagination precondition measured with the code under test). **These are the residual ones**, separated because none of them affects confidence in DC PRODUCT behaviour — they weaken the suite's self-protection, not its verdict on the bridge. Recorded rather than fixed inline so closing e369 was not gated on test-hardening that proves nothing new about Data Center.

## Finding A — three isolation assertions assert their own fixture's setup

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py`:

* `:87` asserts `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH == "off"`, but the `dc_store_copy_repo` fixture does
  `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_SYNC_PUSH", "off")` at `conftest.py:620`. The CI job env sets only
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` (`external-integration.yml:323-337`).
* `:88-92` loops `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN` — the IDENTICAL three names the
  fixture `monkeypatch.delenv`s at `conftest.py:624-625`. It is structurally impossible for this to
  detect a Cloud credential in the JOB environment, which is what its criterion claims it checks, and it
  does not cover other plausible names (`JIRA_TOKEN`, `JIRA_URL`).
* `test_dc_mutations.py:1696-1728` collects every `base_url = "..."` in the copied tree and asserts the
  set equals `{BASE}` — but the only file in the copy carrying a `base_url` is the `rebar.toml` the
  fixture itself wrote from `_BASE` (`conftest.py:607-617`), and `_BASE`/`BASE` are the same expression.
  It compares the fixture against itself, so it cannot detect the stray production URL it exists to
  catch.

**The isolation itself is REAL** — the fixture does set the env var and does delete the credentials — so these have genuine value as regression guards ON THE FIXTURE. The defect is that they claim more reach than they have, and a reader auditing "is the live suite safe against touching production?" would take false assurance from them.

## Finding B — two absence assertions read a FILTERED plan with no positive control

* idempotence, `test_dc_mutations.py:1782` — concludes from `mine == []`
* row-14 inbound, `test_dc_mutations.py:1382` — concludes from `not teardown`

Both derive a negative from an EMPTY filtered dry-run plan. Story 5200 already burned a cycle on `--filter-local-ids` being a post-filter that matched nothing ("1640 mutations computed, 0 match filter", recorded in that ticket's comment 4). Under that failure mode both assertions pass vacuously while proving nothing. Neither cell has a positive control demonstrating the filter CAN surface an entry for its own pair. Row 14 is partly protected by a second, positive assertion (the local ticket survives with a non-teardown status); idempotence has no such backstop.

## Finding C — smaller shape issues, same family

* `_out_status` (`test_dc_mutations.py:439-445`) mutates CONDITIONALLY (`if current != "in_progress"`),
  so on an already-`in_progress` ticket it would assert a state it did not create. Harmless today (an
  imported DC issue lands `open`), but it is the same "the oracle may be checking pre-existing state"
  shape as the `08-assign` vacuity that was just repaired.
* Row 3 (description, both directions) uses `in` containment where the criterion says the path EQUALS
  the value.
* Return codes and stderr are checked unevenly: the writing passes assert `"Traceback" not in
  cp.stderr` at 26 sites, but the mutation cells never check the return code, and the dry-run passes in
  `_plan_entries_for`, the pagination cell and the row-14 cell do not check `stderr` at all.
* `.signing-key`, `.opcert-key` and `.opcert-key.pub` are present in the copied tracker and are not part
  of the `.bridge_state*` scrub. Not covered by any criterion; noted because the copy is a throwaway
  that CI writes to.

## Why this is worth doing (and why it is not urgent)

The operator's standing priority is that DC/Cloud test parity is what gives confidence the DC feature is defect-free. An assertion that cannot fail contributes nothing to that confidence while LOOKING like it does — and this epic has repeatedly proved that the cost is real, not theoretical: a vacuous assignee oracle reported green for months and, once repaired, immediately surfaced product defect 8d68. So the class deserves closing. It is not urgent because each item here is a self-protection gap rather than a gap in what the suite says about Data Center.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Finding A: each of the three assertions either exercises a value the fixture did NOT author, or is
      re-labelled in code and docstring as a fixture regression guard — the overclaiming wording is the
      defect, so an honest narrowing is an acceptable fix, but it must be explicit
- [x] Finding A: the credential check no longer shares a hardcoded name list with the fixture that
      deletes them (derive one from the other, or assert over a broader documented set including
      `JIRA_TOKEN`)
- [x] Finding B: the idempotence cell gains a POSITIVE control proving `--filter-local-ids` can surface
      an entry for its own pair, so an empty filtered plan cannot be mistaken for convergence
- [x] Finding B: the same positive-control property is asserted for the row-14 inbound cell, or that
      cell's existing positive assertion is documented as the backstop and shown sufficient
- [x] Finding C: `_out_status` establishes the pre-state it needs rather than mutating conditionally
- [x] every change is MUTATION-CHECKED — for an assertion whose whole defect is that it cannot fail, a
      fix without a demonstrated RED is unverifiable by construction, and the verdicts are recorded here
- [x] no live cell is weakened or skipped, and the live suite's collected count does not drop (a dropped
      cell silently leaves the `_live_jira_ready` canary, the failure change 1203 had to repair)

## All criteria met — see VERDICTS-59B2-A (Gerrit 1372, merged; live run 30944241768)

Finding A: the credential check now asserts over the environment the fixture INHERITED (recorded before it mutated anything), so it exercises a value the fixture did not author; `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH` is honestly re-labelled as a fixture guard; one shared `CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_VARS` definition, broadened to include `JIRA_TOKEN`/`JIRA_URL`; the `base_url` collector gained a decoy positive control.

Finding B: BOTH idempotence cells got the positive control — the ticket named only one, and the second was found by the guard that pairs control-count to verdict-count. Row 14 establishes reach before the delete and records why the surviving-ticket assertion is not a sufficient backstop.

Finding C: `_out_status` always transitions and refuses a wrong pre-state loudly.

AC6: four repo-only oracles mutation-checked with a demonstrated RED; the two live positive controls assert NON-emptiness, which is trivially falsifiable, and both returned non-empty against the real filter in the live run — the boundary is stated rather than a mutation check being claimed.

AC7: collected 61 -> 63 with `skipped` 0 in both runs. Nothing was weakened or left the canary.
baseline.summary: Live DC suite: residual assertions that cannot fail or pass vacuously (isolation, filtered-plan absence)

## Why

The E1-verified miss class (epic 6982, §5 of docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md;
runs/README.md §"3 MISSED asserted-capability cases") is: **a plan asserts that an existing,
NAMED module provides (or lacks) a capability, and the assertion is false against the code** —
so the executing agent builds on a capability that isn't there, or rebuilds one that already
is. The three verified misses:

- `dc58` — the plan's sign step used a helper `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` does not have
  (signing lives in `rebar.signing`; completion.py:350 only *references* the close gate's
  signing). Pipeline was redesigned mid-flight.
- `db7b` — the plan proposed bounding the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar via event **compaction**, but
  by rebar's own contract compaction folds ONLY `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (`_commands/compact.py:206`)
  and REVIEW_RESULT is reducer-ignored, so compaction never absorbs it. Retention is instead a
  dedicated `sidecar.prune` (`llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:72`).
- `5886` — the plan proposed a NEW unmapped-Jira-status alert that `fetcher.py` already emits
  (`_flag_unmapped_statuses` → `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status`, fetcher.py:219). The bug was
  gate-exempt, so nobody looked.

E4 (assumption/premise verification, blocking) probes assertions broadly but MISSED all three:
the named module EXISTS, so E4's existence check passes; the defect is the finer-grained
**capability-surface** mismatch (module present, specific capability absent — or present when
the plan says absent). This story ships a focused probe for exactly that surface.

## What

Add one new **advisory, code-grounded, AGENT-tier** plan-review criterion, id
`asserted-capability`, in the G6/E4 rubric family (facet `codebase-grounding`), that fires when
a plan makes a **capability-surface claim about a named module/symbol that it relies on**, and
that claim is refuted by the code. Two symmetric directions (one concern — capability claims
about named modules must be grounded):

- (A) plan asserts named module M PROVIDES capability C, but M lacks C (dc58, db7b);
- (B) plan asserts capability C is ABSENT / must be built, but M already provides C (5886).

**Mechanism (grounded against `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`).** The probe plugs into the EXISTING
generic pass machinery — no core pass change. Pass-1 runs it as one agentic finder
(`passes.pass1_chunk(..., agentic=True)`, dispatched because its exec tier is `AGENT`;
eval_solver.py:112-113 and pass1.py:3 "one agent per code-grounding criterion"). The finder
greps/reads the repo (and `resolve_symbol` for installed deps) to confirm the module's actual
capability surface. Pass-2 verifier grades its two criterion-local binary sub-answers; Pass-3
computes validity×impact deterministically; Pass-4 coaches surviving advisories. It ships
**advisory posture (never blocks)** — registry entry `default_posture: "advisory"`.

**Registration seam.** Because it is a packaged built-in LLM criterion it must be added to
`registry.CANONICAL_LLM` (registry.py:79), `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` (:66), and `AGENT_TIER` (:72),
given a routing entry in `criteria_routing.json`, a rubric prompt at
`reviewers/plan_review_asserted_capability.md`, and a regenerated `## asserted-capability`
guide section — else `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` (:430) flags it ORPHAN and CI fails
(the exact failure that bit R2/b080), and `validate_criteria_guide()` (:530) flags a missing
section.

**Prior art.** This extends the SAME four-pass finder/verifier/decide/coach machinery already
used by A1/E4/G6/removal-rationale (see docs/plan-review-gate.md); `removal-rationale` (the
removal-side code-grounded advisory dual of A1) is the direct structural precedent for a
gated-then-grounded two-sub-answer code criterion. No new pass, no new engine construct.

**Effectiveness measurement is future dogfood, not a blocking AC.** The just-landed standing
recorder `criterion_effectiveness.py` (commit 0d695be47, d8a5) AUTO-INCLUDES every criterion id
it sees, so `asserted-capability` accrues `detection_proxy` / `blocking_fp_proxy` from real
reviews with ZERO per-criterion wiring. The advisory→blocking promotion gate is the protocol
d8a5 documented in docs/plan-review-gate.md §"Standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder +
advisory→blocking promotion gate"; this story cites it, it is not gated on accumulation time.

## Scope

- IN: the new criterion (registry + routing + rubric + guide), deterministic unit tests, a
  committed `criteria eval` fixture set + its result artifact (the bounded sanity check).
- OUT: promotion to blocking (future dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change per the cited
  promotion gate); any E2/E3 batch eval (permanently rejected on cost); changing E4/A1.
- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `.../criteria_routing.json`,
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_asserted_capability.md`,
  `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` (regenerated),
  `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-asserted-capability.eval.yaml`,
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/asserted_capability_sanity.json`,
  `tests/unit/test_asserted_capability_criterion.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The criterion is REGISTERED advisory and non-orphan. Proof:
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry as r; assert 'asserted-capability' in r.CANONICAL_LLM; assert 'asserted-capability' in r.CODEBASE_GROUNDED and 'asserted-capability' in r.AGENT_TIER; assert r.validate_packaged_routing()==[]; import json; e=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json'))['asserted-capability']; assert e['default_posture']=='advisory' and e['exec']=='AGENT' and e['facet']=='codebase-grounding'; print('OK')"`
  prints `OK`.
- [ ] The rubric prompt loads and the guide has its section. Proof:
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry as r; assert '## asserted-capability' in open('docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md').read(); print(r.explain_criterion('asserted-capability')[:40])"`
  prints a non-empty section head; and `rebar explain asserted-capability` exits 0.
- [ ] Deterministic unit tests for the non-LLM logic (registration invariants, routing/finding
  shape, prompt-contract sub-answer keys) pass. Proof:
  `pytest tests/unit/test_asserted_capability_criterion.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] Bounded sanity check committed: a `criteria eval` fixture set with the 3 E1-verified misses
  (dc58/db7b/5886, reconstructed to their original false-asserting plan text, grounded against
  current modules) as must-fire and 3 clean plans as must-not-fire. The committed result
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/asserted_capability_sanity.json` shows the probe FIRES
  on >=2 of 3 misses (report §6 R1 threshold; observed 3/3, stability 1.0) and that any clean-plan
  fire is ADVISORY (never blocks) and is recorded as the promotion-gate FP signal. Proof: the JSON
  records `recall_over_misses>=0.66` (observed 1.0), preserves the raw per-case
  `rebar criteria eval asserted-capability --output json` output, and records
  `false_accept_over_clean` (observed 0.33 = one advisory false-fire on the no-claim control N1,
  a non-blocking dogfood datapoint given advisory posture — the exact signal the advisory→blocking
  promotion gate exists to watch). (6 live single-criterion runs total; NO E2/E3 corpus, NO batch
  eval.)
- [ ] The criterion auto-flows into the standing recorder. Proof:
  `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/criterion_effectiveness.py --report` (or a
  targeted unit assertion on `compute_effectiveness`) yields output in which
  `asserted-capability` appears once it has a firing — verified by a unit test feeding one
  synthetic firing row through `firings_from_review`/`compute_effectiveness` and asserting the
  id is auto-included (zero per-criterion wiring).
- [ ] The advisory→blocking promotion gate is documented and cited: docs/plan-review-gate.md's
  §"Standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder + advisory→blocking promotion gate" (added by
  d8a5) is the authority; this criterion's rubric/guide state it ships advisory and promotion is
  a future dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change. Proof: `grep -n "advisory" ` on the
  rubric shows the advisory posture note.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Landed through Gerrit: change carries `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`
  and is submitted to main; `make lint && make typecheck && make test` are green on the change.
  Evidence recorded on this ticket (change number, merge commit, vote outcomes) — verified by
  attestation, not an in-session repo check.
baseline.summary: R1: asserted-capability grounding probe (G6/E4 rubric family, gated on E2+E3)

# /var/gerrit data disk filled and has stayed near-full; review-bot went unhealthy

## Impact (stated first)
The Gerrit/review-bot box (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, region us-east-1) suffered a box-wide disk-fill starting **2026-08-26 ~15:00 PDT**. The `/var/gerrit` data disk jumped from a ~55–59% baseline to **93–95% within ~6h and has NOT recovered** — it is still **94%** and the alarm `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` is **still in ALARM** at the time of this sweep (2026-08-29 10:00 PDT). During the fill, `rebar/host:reviewbot_healthy` **dropped to 0** (unhealthy) for two multi-hour windows, so LLM-Review capacity was degraded. Gerrit itself stayed up (`gerrit_healthy`=1, `Rebar/Gate:GerritReachable`=1 throughout).

## Evidence — CloudWatch (namespace rebar/host, InstanceId i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

### `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` alarm
- `describe-alarm-history`: **OK -> ALARM at 2026-08-26T17:55:32 PDT**; no return-to-OK since.
- StateReason: "1 datapoint [88.0 (27/08/26 00:50Z)] >= threshold (85.0)".

### `disk_used_percent` mount=/var/gerrit (Maximum/hour, PDT)
- Baseline: 52% (08-25 17:00) rising slowly to 59% (08-26 14:00).
- **Sharp climb**: 08-26 15:00 = 64% -> 16:00 = 81% -> 17:00 = **88%** -> 18:00-20:00 = 89% ->
  21:00 = **93%**.
- **Plateau, unrecovered**: 93-95% continuously from 08-26 21:00 through 08-29 10:00
  (latest datapoint **94%**). Trend: plateaued high, not draining.

### `reviewbot_healthy` (Min/hour = 0 means unhealthy) — service impact
- **0** for 08-26 15:00,16:00,17:00,18:00,20:00,21:00 PDT (coincides with the data-disk climb).
- **0** again for 08-28 16:00-20:00 PDT (coincides with the root-disk thrash + deploy backpressure below).

### Correlated root-disk pressure on the same box (30-GiB gp3 root, `root_disk_used_percent`)
- `rebar-root-disk-pressure` **flapped into ALARM ~18 times** 08-26 20:41 -> 08-28 10:45 PDT.
- Root usage oscillated 76-**98%** (peaks: 98% @08-26 15:00, 98% @08-28 01:00), then relaxed
  to ~72-82% after 08-28 11:00.
- `disk_pressure_prunes` ran **continuously ~5-6/hour for ~24h** (08-27 10:00 -> 08-28 10:00 PDT)
  — the automated reclaim was working overtime and the root disk still sat near-full, matching
  the "reclaim frees nothing" symptom of the closed root-disk tickets.

### Downstream backpressure (08-28 16:00-20:00 PDT, review-bot unhealthy again)
- `deploy_errors`: Sum=1 at 08-28 16:00 and 17:00 PDT -> `rebar-autodeploy-errors` ALARM
  17:07->17:47 PDT.
- `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded`: 08-28 16:00, 18:00, 19:00 (alarm flapped 3x);
  `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable`: 08-28 17:00 (alarm 17:07->17:22).
- `deploy_deferrals` climbed to Max 19-20/period on 08-28 evening — autodeploy repeatedly
  deferred, consistent with disk pressure + in-flight reviews.
  (Caveat: some marker-delta counters can over-report on a cold-start republish per closed
  bug e2a6 widespread-zealous-narwhal; but the co-timed `reviewbot_healthy`=0 and root-disk
  peaks make a real backpressure episode the stronger reading.)

## Likely common cause (hypothesis)
A large repository/pack growth landed on the box around 08-26 15:00 PDT, filling both `/var/gerrit` and root simultaneously. This is corroborated by CI's repo-growth guard tripping the same day: `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` step **"Fail closed if the blobless checkout pack exceeds its limit"** (`REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB`, git `size-pack`), plus the mirror pack-size limits. Candidate on-disk consumers to confirm on the box: git repo/pack growth under `/var/gerrit` (tickets-branch and mirrors), Gerrit review artifacts/caches, docker layers/build cache, and journald/logs.

## What this ticket is NOT (dedup)
- No existing ticket covers the **`/var/gerrit` data disk** mount; all prior disk tickets are
  the **root** volume or docker cache (3a52 masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle, 9bc0
  taurine-smiling-hamadryad, 7a41 forgivable-nerdy-genet — all closed). The data-disk high +
  sustained-non-recovery is a distinct, currently-active condition.
- The 08-28 root-disk flapping recurs the closed root-disk-pressure symptom (3a52); linked
  relates_to for context rather than as this ticket's headline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] Identify what consumed `/var/gerrit` on 08-26 (du breakdown on the box:
      git/packs vs review artifacts vs docker vs logs) and confirm/deny the pack-growth
      hypothesis. — DONE (SSM du breakdowns in comments): the acute consumers were operational
      evidence debris, NOT git-store pack growth — 30G of retired divergent ticket clones
      (`retired-ticket-clones/`) + ~11G of one-off Aug-26 investigation probes
      (`rebar-quiet-window-evidence/` epoch-probe dirs, 5.2G each). Pack-growth hypothesis
      DENIED for the acute fill: the served Gerrit repo `site/git/rebar.git` was only ~475M and
      well-packed.
      provenance: environment=aws-prod/i-00880b2c7f13527c5 us-east-1; principal=ops-sweep via SSM RunShellScript (operator-approved); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read-only SSM `du`/`df` on the live Gerrit box; evidence lives off the codebase snapshot.
- [x] [non-codebase] Reclaim or grow `/var/gerrit` so `disk_used_percent` returns below the 85%
      threshold and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` clears. — DONE (operator-approved SSM reclaim):
      stopgap removed the 30G retired clones (95%→36%), then the 2026-08-30 evidence-debris
      reclaim removed `rebar-quiet-window-evidence/` (37%→15%, ~11.9G freed). Alarm
      `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` = OK since 2026-08-29T13:35 PDT and stayed OK.
      provenance: environment=aws-prod/i-00880b2c7f13527c5 us-east-1; principal=ops-sweep via SSM RunShellScript (operator approvals "Approved for 1a" / "5a05 approved"); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `rm -rf` of retired clones + evidence dirs then `df`; CloudWatch alarm-history confirms ALARM→OK; off-snapshot evidence.
- [x] [non-codebase] Confirm `reviewbot_healthy` returns to steady 1 and stays there. — DONE:
      review-bot / Gerrit / mcp / opcert containers all Up and healthy post-reclaim; Gerrit HTTP
      200; in-window ops sweep (2026-08-29→08-30) recorded no further data-disk firings and
      sustained OK.
      provenance: environment=aws-prod/i-00880b2c7f13527c5 us-east-1; principal=ops-sweep via SSM + CloudWatch; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — live container status + Gerrit HTTP probe + CloudWatch `reviewbot_healthy`/alarm reads; off-snapshot evidence.
- [x] [non-codebase] Add a guard/headroom or growth alarm so a repeat pack-growth event does not
