## Context / Problem

The Gerrit Verified gate executes workflow files from TRUSTED MAIN, not the patchset (proven on change 2115 PS1: its own run 32587991195 still executed main's stale `--timeout=20`, headSha 6a5c88027c5). pytest-timeout precedence is marker > CLI > `PYTEST_TIMEOUT` env > ini (`get_env_settings` / `_get_item_settings` in `pytest_timeout.py`), so the `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` CLI flags on `_build-and-test.yml`'s two shared-tier lanes (the default-suite and integration `run:` commands) permanently shadow any future per-test-budget change carried in `pyproject.toml`: a budget fix can never be exercised by its own Verified run — the class of failure that made 2115 PS1 fail its own gate. Bug `3fa7-94ba-42aa-4623` was ultimately landed by an operator-cast Verified+1, which is not a repeatable path.

## Approach

Single-source the shared-tier budget: REMOVE the `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` CLI flags from both `_build-and-test.yml` lanes and let `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` (`timeout = 300`, `timeout_method = "thread"`, at `pyproject.toml:662-663`) govern. This is the ecosystem-standard shape — scikit-learn, pandas and numpy pass no `--timeout` on their CI pytest command lines; the budget lives in config. With the flags gone, a patchset that changes the ini budget IS exercised by its own Verified run, because the ini travels with the patchset while workflow files come from trusted main.

Effective budgets do not change: the lanes ran at CLI `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` and the ini already carries the identical values, so removal only moves authority (the before/after is documented in the commit message). The eleven other `--timeout=` lanes (external-integration, optionality, eval-discipline, test.yml, structured-output-baseline) keep their own larger calibrated CLI budgets — they drive live services, clean-venv installs and eval sweeps, and several run outside this repo's rootdir where the ini is not in play.

The previously drafted conftest-floor mechanism (branch `preserve/timeout-floor-hardening`, commit `b38bf9a4748`) is rejected and does not land: pytest-timeout resolves `config._env_timeout` at session start read-only, so a conftest floor has no supported hook point and no OSS precedent. That branch is mined for its reusable test assets only (the parity-contract rewrites and the lane-flag removals); its `tests/_timeout_floor.py`, conftest hook, and docs floor section are discarded, and the branch (local-only; it has no `origin` ref) is deleted after mining.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — remove `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`
  from the default-suite and integration `run:` commands; rewrite the adjacent hang-guard
  comments to say the budget lives in the ini and these lanes are deliberately flag-free.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — rewrite
  `test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget` to assert the two shared-tier
  lanes carry NO `--timeout`/`--timeout-method` flags (and that the ini budget is present and
  positive, since it becomes their only guard); update
  `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` so a lane may satisfy the guard by
  inheriting the asserted-real ini keys (budget positive, `thread` method) instead of an
  explicit flag, while a lane that DOES set a flag must still use the `thread` method.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — update the sentence stating the two lanes are "held equal to the
  ini value" to say they are held flag-free (single-sourced from the ini).

## Testing

RED-first: the rewritten parity contract asserting no `--timeout`/`--timeout-method` on the shared-tier lanes is the oracle — it fails against the current workflow (flags present) and passes after the removal. The hang-guard sweep keeps its negative power: it still requires every other pytest lane to carry an explicit budget flag with the `thread` method, and the ini fallback it now accepts for flag-free lanes is asserted real (`timeout` positive, `timeout_method = "thread"`) rather than assumed. An unmarked hung test remains bounded: the out-of-process negative arms in `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` prove the ini keys alone expire a hung body, setup, and teardown. `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the targeted suites (`pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py`) run green before push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Neither `_build-and-test.yml` shared-tier lane passes `--timeout` or `--timeout-method`
      on its pytest command line; checked by the rewritten parity contract failing if a flag
      reappears.
- [x] The ini remains the lanes' real guard: the parity contracts assert
      `[tool.pytest.ini_options].timeout` is present and positive and `timeout_method` is
      `thread`, and the existing out-of-process negative arms in `test_timeout_budget.py`
      prove those keys alone expire a hung test (no weakening of the hang guard).
- [x] The hang-guard sweep still requires an explicit `--timeout` flag (with
      `--timeout-method=thread`) on every pytest lane outside `_build-and-test.yml`; checked
      by `test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard` passing over the unchanged
      eleven calibrated lanes.
- [x] The effective shared-tier budget is unchanged (300 s, thread method, before and after);
      documented in the commit message and checked by the ini config arm in
      `test_timeout_budget.py` still pinning `timeout = 300`.
- [x] Branch `preserve/timeout-floor-hardening` is deleted after mining (local `git branch -D`;
      it has no `origin` ref, verified via `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/preserve/*'`);
      recorded in this ticket's close evidence.
baseline.summary: Single-source the shared-tier hang budget in the ini; remove the CI CLI --timeout flags

## Why
Workflows must be git-tracked text agents and humans can edit with clean diffs; the format and its validation are the foundation everything else builds on.

## What
- Define a coordinate-free GitHub-Actions-style `steps:` YAML DSL with a versioned JSON Schema.
- Add a reference-integrity linter (dangling input/output refs), YAML 1.2 safe-load, a closed
  expression allow-list, a secret scan, and a schema_version read-time up-conversion shim.
- Ship `rebar workflow new` / `validate` / `--dry-run` (FakeRunner, no tokens).

## Scope
- In: schema, linter, safety, scaffolding, validate, schema versioning/migration.
- Out: execution (WS-C); rendering (WS-I).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] JSON Schema + reference-integrity linter with located, actionable error messages.
- [ ] YAML 1.2 safe-loader; schema_version typed string; anchors/merge-keys rejected; size cap.
- [ ] Expression allow-list; linter forbids raw ${{}} in prompt/command fields; post-substitution re-validation.
- [ ] Secret scan gate on .rebar/workflows/*.yaml.
- [ ] schema_version up-conversion is a read-time chained vN->v(N+1) shim (never in-place rewrite) with a lossless round-trip test per shim.
- [ ] A schema_version newer than the running rebar is a hard "upgrade rebar" error.
- [ ] One immutable version-pinned JSON Schema per version at a stable $id (additionalProperties:false).
- [ ] `rebar workflow new/validate/--dry-run` working, with a worked 3-step example.

baseline.description:
## Why

Story 1 invalidates a plan-review attestation when the code it was grounded against drifts, and falls back to a FULL re-review (~all criteria, billable, minutes) to re-earn it. But most drift is **immaterial to the plan** — the changed code doesn't break any assumption the plan relies on. Paying for a full re-review in that common case is wasteful.

The original idea (re-run only the "code-grounded" criteria and reuse the rest) is **unsound** as the codebase stands: tools are gated by `execution_mode`, not per-criterion, so ALL 12 agentic criteria (incl. `G3/G4` and the `T*` overlays) can read code — there is no enforced code-blind subset to safely reuse. (The `registry.py` comment claiming "only these 4 grep — the orchestrator enforces it" is inaccurate; see Notes.)

Instead, use a **progressive (tripwire) re-review**: on drift, run ONE focused probe — "is the plan still accurate with respect to the (now-changed) codebase?" — and only escalate to a full re-review if it finds something. Soundness comes from the probe (a dedicated check confirms immateriality), not from reusing a subset of stale findings, so the partition problem disappears.

## What

When a claim is blocked by **code drift** (Story 1's per-path hash mismatch) AND a prior PASSing plan-review attestation exists whose only staleness is code drift (ticket material unchanged):

1. **Probe** — run the codebase-accuracy check against the CURRENT working tree: the existing
   `E4` (assumption/premise verification — forced codebase probe) and `G1G2` (edit-set/consumer
   accuracy), the two criteria whose whole job is "does the plan match the actual code." Hint them
   with the drifted dependency paths so the probe focuses on what changed.
2. **Clean probe → refresh, don't re-review.** If the probe yields no blocking/material findings, the
   drift did not invalidate the plan: REUSE the prior verdict wholesale and re-sign the attestation
   with the CURRENT dependency-file hashes (a "refreshed" attestation), recording provenance
   (`refreshed-from` the prior signature + the probe outcome). One/two agentic calls instead of the
   full criteria set.
3. **Probe finds something → full re-review.** Escalate to the existing full review path (Story 1's
   fallback); the plan genuinely needs re-examination.

The reuse is **whole-verdict, gated by the probe** — never a per-criterion or per-finding subset — so there is no per-finding "code-hash vintage" and no chained-finding attestation to design; the refreshed attestation is just a fresh signature over the prior verdict + the new dependency map.

### Fail-safe to FULL re-review

- The probe errors / is INDETERMINATE / the LLM is unavailable.
- Registry or criteria-contract **version skew** between the prior signing and now (the probe's
  meaning may have changed).
- No reusable prior verdict (e.g. the prior attestation predates this mechanism, or material also
  changed — that's a material-edit invalidation, handled by Story 1 / `dead-stalk-chasm`).

### Explicitly descoped (superseded by the progressive design)

- Per-criterion finding reuse based on a "code-blind" partition (unsound — no enforced partition).
- Per-finding code-hash vintage; chained per-finding attestation. Replaced by whole-verdict reuse +
  a refreshed signature.
- Observed read-set capture; `>N files` fallback (already rejected in the brainstorm).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — the progressive path: detect a drift-only re-review
  with a reusable prior verdict, run the `E4`(+`G1G2`) probe, branch reuse-vs-full.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — "refresh" an attestation: re-sign a prior verdict with the
  current dependency-hash map + `refreshed-from` provenance; expose the prior verdict/manifest read.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` / `registry.py` — run just the probe criteria as a focused
  pass (reuse existing `E4`/`G1G2`); no new criterion text required for v1.
- Tests under the plan-review suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a drift-only re-review with a reusable prior PASS, the probe (`E4`[+`G1G2`]) runs against the
      current code; a CLEAN probe refreshes the attestation (prior verdict re-signed with the current
      dependency hashes + `refreshed-from` provenance) WITHOUT running the full criteria set.
- [ ] A probe that surfaces a blocking/material finding escalates to a FULL re-review (no silent
      reuse); the refreshed attestation is never issued in that case.
- [ ] Fail-safe to FULL re-review on: probe error/indeterminate/LLM-unavailable, registry/criteria
      version skew, or no reusable prior verdict.
- [ ] The refreshed attestation is a valid plan-review attestation (claim succeeds after a clean
      refresh) and is externally CI-verifiable; its provenance records it was a drift-refresh.
- [ ] Soundness: the reuse is whole-verdict gated by the probe — NO per-criterion/per-finding subset
      reuse (documented), so the unenforced code-blind partition is not relied upon.
- [ ] Measurement: report the cost (tokens/latency) of the probe-only refresh vs a full re-review on
      a representative immaterial drift, before enabling the progressive path by default.
- [ ] Tested: immaterial drift (touch a dependency file in a way that doesn't break the plan) →
      probe clean → refresh → claim succeeds; material drift (change a cited premise) → probe finds →
      full re-review; version skew / no-prior-verdict → full re-review.

## Notes

The `registry.py` `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` comment ("only these AGENT-tier criteria grep ... the orchestrator enforces it — no other criterion greps") is inaccurate — agentic tooling is granted by `execution_mode`, not per criterion, so every AGENT-tier criterion can read code. This design does NOT depend on that invariant; the comment should be corrected (small doc fix, here or a follow-up).
baseline.summary: Narrowed delta-re-review on code drift: re-run only the enforced code-grounded criteria with a chained attestation

baseline.description:
# Stage-1 BM25F candidate generation over digests + graph-exclusion filter

## Why
Stage 1 narrows a few hundred tickets to ~20 candidates cheaply and deterministically, no LLM/embeddings, and must NOT surface a ticket's own already-related work (parents/children/siblings/linked) — the top source of "related-but-distinct" false flags. DERISKED (epic experiment comment): digest-BM25F recall@20 = 1.0 on 8 paraphrase pairs, STABLE 60→200 corpus; single-query latency 0.69 ms at 800 digests (~14× under budget) — so brute-force is correct and no ANN/vector-DB is needed.

## What
- Brute-force BM25F "More Like This" over `ticket_digest` records (S2). Bespoke ~40 LOC: `rank-bm25` provides only UNWEIGHTED BM25, but we need per-field weighting; at n<1000 bespoke is trivial and avoids a dependency (the recall+latency spikes validate this choice). Field weights are a module-level constant `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` in `retrieve.py` (`problem_keywords` 3.0, `component_or_area` 3.0, `key_entities` 1.0, `propositions` 1.0) — a stable algorithmic choice, deliberately NOT a config knob (a dict-typed config value has no `from_env` resolution helper, and BM25F weights do not need per-invocation tuning; if they ever do, that is a separate `_llm_json` helper story). Tokenize lowercased on non-alphanumeric, drop stopwords + corpus-boilerplate via `overlap_max_doc_freq`. Returns a typed `OverlapCandidate` `[{ticket_id, score, matched_terms}]` (the interface S7 consumes — stated so S7 isn't blind to it). Query side = the query ticket's freshly-extracted digest, passed by the caller.
- **Graph exclusion** BEFORE scoring: new helper `src/rebar/llm/overlap/graph.py::related_ticket_ids(ticket_id, tracker) -> set[str]` that loads states ONCE via `_load_all_states(tracker)` (the same helper `descendants.py` uses) and derives all four relation sets from that one dict: descendants (BFS on `parent_id`, or by calling `descendants.list_descendants(ticket_id, tracker)` and flattening its type-bucketed id lists — NOT by sharing its internal snapshot, which it does not expose), ancestors (walk `parent_id` up), siblings (same `parent_id`; a root ticket with no parent has NO siblings — handled explicitly), and linked tickets in BOTH directions (scan all tickets' `deps` for any edge whose source OR target is `ticket_id` — an incoming `blocks`/`depends_on` from another ticket is not in this ticket's own `deps`, so outgoing-only would miss it). It does NOT refactor `next_batch.py`. At n<1000 one state load is sub-ms (latency spike).
- Cold/stale: corpus tickets whose digest is absent or stale (S2 freshness: content-hash/model/version mismatch — not an age threshold) are SKIPPED; the skip-count is logged so a cold run is distinguishable from a healthy one.
- Overlap floor: a `min_should_match` fraction (default 0.15 of query terms) below which a candidate is not returned; `retrieve()` returns `[]` when nothing clears the floor.
- Errors: any graph-read/scoring exception is caught, logged, returns `[]` (never blocks review_plan).

## Config (LLMConfig, not VerifyConfig) — with explicit `from_env` wiring
Three SCALAR tunables on `LLMConfig` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`); field weights are a constant (see What), NOT config:
- `overlap_k: int = 20`
- `overlap_max_doc_freq: float = 0.5` (ignore terms appearing in >50% of digests)
- `overlap_min_should_match: float = 0.15`

**`LLMConfig.from_env()` MUST be edited** (it explicitly constructs `LLMConfig(...)` with every field read via a helper — a new dataclass field not read there stays at its default and is silently un-tunable). Add module constants `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_K = 20`, `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ = 0.5`, `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH = 0.15`; add the three dataclass fields; and in `from_env`'s `return cls(...)` add:
- `overlap_k=_llm_int(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_K", "overlap_k", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_K)`
- `overlap_max_doc_freq=_llm_float(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ", "overlap_max_doc_freq", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ)`
- `overlap_min_should_match=_llm_float(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH", "overlap_min_should_match", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH)`

`_llm_int` exists (`config.py:388`); `_llm_float` does NOT — add it in `config.py` mirroring `_llm_int` (env > `rebar -c llm.*` > `[tool.rebar.llm]` file > default, parsing via `float()` with a clean fallback on ValueError). This is the only non-scalar-free helper needed (no dict keys remain). `_config_schema.py` reserves the `llm.*` layer, so these are NOT on `VerifyConfig`.

## Dependencies
S1 (`ticket_digest` schema/fields), S2 (digest store + freshness). Digest fields are DEFINED in S1.

## Scope
- New `src/rebar/llm/overlap/retrieve.py` (BM25F + `OverlapCandidate` + `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` constant) and `src/rebar/llm/overlap/graph.py` (`related_ticket_ids`).
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: add `_llm_float` helper, the three `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_*` constants, the three `LLMConfig` fields, and the three `from_env()` reads (enumerated above).
- OUT: judge (S6), wiring (S7). Interface for S7: `retrieve(query_digest, corpus, exclude:set[str]) -> list[OverlapCandidate]`.

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_overlap_retrieve.py`: `test_topk` (order); `test_perf` (<10 ms at 300 digests); `test_graph_exclusion` (parents/children/siblings/linked dropped; root-ticket-no-siblings edge); `test_cold_skip` (absent/stale skipped + count logged); `test_boilerplate` (shared boilerplate ≠ match); `test_floor_empty` (nothing clears min_should_match → `[]`); `test_error_empty` (graph error → `[]`, no raise); `test_config` — sets `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_K`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` in the env, calls `LLMConfig.from_env()`, and asserts the three fields resolve to the env values (proving `from_env` wiring, not just dataclass defaults); `test_field_weights_constant` (retrieve uses the `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` constant).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Returns top-K (default 20) `OverlapCandidate`s by field-weighted BM25F, <10 ms at ~300 digests; `pytest ...::{test_topk,test_perf}`.
- [ ] Candidates EXCLUDE the query's parents/children/siblings/linked via `related_ticket_ids(ticket_id, tracker)` (reusing `descendants.list_descendants`); root-with-no-parent has no siblings; `::test_graph_exclusion`.
- [ ] Absent/stale digests skipped, skip-count logged; `::test_cold_skip`. Boilerplate doesn't drive matches; `::test_boilerplate`.
- [ ] `min_should_match` floor returns `[]` when unmet; a graph/scoring error returns `[]` (never blocks); `::{test_floor_empty,test_error_empty}`.
- [ ] `overlap_k`, `overlap_max_doc_freq`, `overlap_min_should_match` are read from the env by `LLMConfig.from_env()` (explicit wiring, `_llm_float` added for the floats); field weights are the `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` constant, not config; `::test_config`, `::test_field_weights_constant`.
baseline.summary: Stage-1 BM25F candidate generation over digests + graph-exclusion filter

# Land dependabot PRs #129 + #130 as ONE Gerrit change (setup-uv v10 + uv-lock botocore/json-repair)

## Context / Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot PRs never merge there; content is re-applied locally and landed via Gerrit, then the PRs are commented/closed. Per operator directive these two open dependabot PRs are grouped into a SINGLE ticket and a SINGLE Gerrit change (one commit touching both the CI-action pin and the lockfile — the shared "dependency housekeeping" lane):

* PR #129 (`dependabot/github_actions/github-actions-fa3bf1173d`, github-actions
  group): `astral-sh/setup-uv` v9.0.0 (`c771a70e…`) -> v10.0.0 (`ae62891f…`),
  19 pinned-SHA references across 11 workflow files. VALIDITY: v10 is a major
  bump; its ONLY breaking change disables the cache for `enable-cache: auto` on
  `pull_request_target` / `workflow_run` / `release` events (cache-poisoning
  hardening, astral-sh/setup-uv#984). EVERY rebar usage passes
  `enable-cache: true` explicitly (never `auto`), so that change does not alter
  our behavior; the `version`/`version-file` additions are opt-in and unused.
  Dependabot pins the exact v10.0.0 commit SHA, so the bump is reproducible.

* PR #130 (`dependabot/uv/uv-lock-434831ba27`, uv-lock group): two lock-only
  patch bumps —
  - `botocore` 1.43.69 -> 1.43.70 (patch) — SAFE. Routine service-model update;
    consumed via lazy imports only (`bedrock_model.py`, `structured.py`,
    `remote_cert.py`). pyproject floor `botocore>=1.43.0` already admits it and
    boto3's botocore range (`<1.44`) accepts it, so boto3 need not move.
  - `json-repair` 0.63.0 -> 0.63.1 (patch) — SAFE. `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`
    calls `repair_json(cand, return_objects=True[, schema=…])`; the called API is
    unchanged across the patch. Floor `json-repair>=0.61` already admits it.
  The PR also carries uv's lockfile-format churn: `revision = 2 -> 3` and an
  httpcore2 marker simplification (dependabot ran a newer uv). Both are
  format/resolver byproducts, not dependency changes; `uv lock --check` on main
  already passes latest-uv, so revision is not load-bearing — but we reproduce
  the PR faithfully by regenerating with a recent uv.

## Approach

In a fresh worktree branched from `origin/main` (venv on PATH):

1. NO pyproject.toml edit — all bumps are admitted by existing constraints
   (setup-uv is a SHA pin in workflow YAML, not a pyproject dep; botocore /
   json-repair floors listed above; no exact pins exist for either).
2. setup-uv: replace every `astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e…  # v9.0.0` with
   `astral-sh/setup-uv@ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d  # v10.0.0`
   across the 11 workflow files (19 sites) via an exact-string sed; verify 0
   remaining v9 SHAs and 19 v10 SHAs.
3. uv-lock: install a recent uv in the worktree, then
   `uv lock --upgrade-package botocore --upgrade-package json-repair`. If uv
   resolves PAST the PR's reviewed versions (per the #128 precedent it did),
   re-lock with exact `==1.43.70` / `==0.63.1` pins so the landed lock matches
   the certified scope; the newer patches arrive in the next dependabot round.
   Then `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra agents` so gates run against the
   bumped tree. Verify `git diff uv.lock` moved only botocore/json-repair (plus
   uv's transitive/format bookkeeping) — no other version churn.
4. Gates: YAML-parse the 11 changed workflow files; `uv lock --check`;
   `make lint`; `make typecheck`; targeted usage-surface tests
   (`pytest tests/unit/test_structured.py tests/unit/test_silent_success.py`
   for json-repair; `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` for the botocore lazy
   import — run whichever exist). Full `pytest tests/unit` is CI's job; CI
   Verified +1 is the authoritative full-suite gate.
5. ONE commit (subject <=50 chars, body wrapped at 72) with trailer
   `rebar-ticket: <this ticket's full canonical id>` + DCO `-s`;
   `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`. Leave the ticket in_progress for the
   bots; the change is submitted only after LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.
6. Comment on BOTH PR #129 and PR #130 pointing at the single Gerrit change and
   noting they were grouped; leave the PRs open for dependabot/operator to close
   once the mirror updates.

## STOP / defer rule (explicit fallback done-state)

If a package bump fails its targeted tests or lint/typecheck in step 4: drop ONLY that package (re-lock from a clean `git checkout uv.lock` with the remaining package), record the failure evidence as a ticket comment, and land the remaining safe content. If setup-uv v10 fails a workflow-parse or a real usage incompatibility surfaces, drop the actions bump and land the lock subset (or vice-versa) — the two halves are independent. The fallback done-state: the ticket closes legitimately with the landed subset, provided every dropped item has a recorded-on-ticket failure reason.

## Out of scope

* Any src/rebar or test code change — nothing in these deltas requires one.
* boto3 / mcp / any other dependency bump not in PR #129 or #130.
* pyproject.toml constraint edits and `.github/complexity-baseline.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: on the landed change, all 19 setup-uv references read the v10.0.0 SHA
  `ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d` across the 11 workflow files, zero
  v9 SHAs remain, and all 11 changed workflow files still parse as valid YAML.
- [x] AC2: `uv.lock` records botocore 1.43.70 and json-repair 0.63.1 (or a
  documented STOP-rule subset), pyproject.toml is unchanged, and
  `uv lock --check` exits 0.
- [x] AC3: `make lint` + `make typecheck` exit 0 and the targeted usage-surface
  tests pass against the bumped tree.
- [x] AC4: the change lands through Gerrit as a SINGLE change with a
  `rebar-ticket:` trailer for this ticket's full canonical id + DCO sign-off,
  after LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.
- [x] AC5: both PR #129 and PR #130 carry a comment pointing at the single
  grouped Gerrit change; both left open for the mirror/dependabot to close.
- [x] AC6 (fallback): every item dropped under the STOP rule has a ticket
  comment recording the concrete failure evidence and the re-lock excluding it
  (vacuously satisfied when everything lands).
baseline.summary: Land dependabot PRs #129 + #130 as one Gerrit change (setup-uv v10 + uv-lock botocore/json-repair)

## Summary
Cut the 0.10.1 patch release of rebar per docs/releasing.md. This is a fix/patch bump from 0.10.0, covering the ~36 commits landed on main since v0.10.0 (reconciler Backend-port scalar surfaces, plan-review/close-gate hardening, code-health analyzers scc/lizard/jscpd, review-bot token accounting, and assorted fixes).

## Plan
1. Fresh worktree from origin/main (git worktree add / make worktree).
2. Bump versions in lockstep: pyproject.toml [project].version; server.json top-level version AND every packages[].version -> 0.10.1. server.json has exactly ONE packages[] entry, so a correct bump yields two 0.10.1 occurrences in that file. The release authorize job runs release_guards.py version-lockstep and fails the build on any mismatch.
3. CHANGELOG.md: prepend the [0.10.1] section via 'make changelog VERSION=v0.10.1', hand-curate the generated top section, add the [0.10.1] compare-link footer.
4. Local gates, run with the worktree venv on PATH: 'make lint && make typecheck && make test', then build+validate the artifact metadata exactly as the runbook (docs/releasing.md L259) and release.yml specify: 'python -m build && python -m twine check dist/*'. twine is not a dev extra in pyproject; invoke it as the CI lock does via 'pipx run twine check dist/*' (or 'uvx twine check dist/*') if 'python -m twine' is absent in the worktree venv, so the glob-targeted metadata check actually runs against the built wheel+sdist.
5. Commit with 'rebar-ticket: zincoid-panoramic-eeve' + DCO sign-off trailers; push 'git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main'; earn LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1; then Submit (POST /a/changes/<n>/submit as RebarBotNava).
6. Fast-forward the worktree to merged main; dispatch the release from main: 'gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f version=0.10.1' and approve the pypi environment deployment when prompted (required-reviewers gate). PyPI is immutable — if the published artifact is defective, yank it and ship 0.10.2.
7. Verify the channels with the proving commands below.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Version-lockstep holds: 'grep -c 0.10.1 pyproject.toml' >=1 and 'grep -c 0.10.1 server.json' == 2 (top-level + the single packages[] entry) on the release commit; equivalently release_guards.py version-lockstep passes in the authorize job.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md carries a curated release section: 'grep -E "^## \[0\.10\.1\]" CHANGELOG.md' matches.
- [ ] Release commit landed on main through Gerrit with both gate votes green: the Gerrit change shows LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 and status MERGED, and 'git log origin/main --oneline | grep -i "release 0.10.1"' finds it.
- [ ] [operator-attested] 0.10.1 published to PyPI: 'curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/json | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"info\"][\"version\"])"' prints 0.10.1.
- [ ] [operator-attested] v0.10.1 tag + GitHub Release created at the released main SHA: 'gh release view v0.10.1 --json tagName,targetCommitish,isLatest' shows the tag, marked Latest.

## Out of scope / automated follow-ups (no executor action required)
- Homebrew tap self-bump (navapbc/homebrew-rebar autobump.yml, scheduled every 6h) and the MCP-registry publish job (mcp_registry in release.yml, needs: publish) run automatically after publish; verifying them is not a release-blocking acceptance criterion for this ticket.

## Attestation evidence
- The above acceptance criteria are proven in-session by the quoted shell/gh/curl commands whose outputs are recorded as comments on this ticket, plus the Gerrit change number and its +1/+1 vote outcome and MERGED status.

# Bring provider configs under version control + repo-wide CLAUDE.md reference sweep

## Why

Once `AGENTS.md` is canonical, two things must happen so the migration ships to other providers and clones: (1) the committed-tree references to `CLAUDE.md` must move to the new structure, and (2) the provider-config scaffolding must be **committed** — a spike found that `.codex/config.toml` and `.agents/rules/rebar.md` are **untracked, locally `.git/info/exclude`d files on one machine** (`git ls-files` returns nothing for them), so today no other clone or provider sees them.

## What

A `git grep 'CLAUDE\.md'` over tracked files gives the complete surface (24 refs). Ownership is split, and this story owns a defined subset:

- **This story updates** (CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md or the new docs home): `CONTRIBUTING.md:570`,
  `README.md:354`, `rebar.toml:3`, `docs/architecture.md:65,233`, `docs/api-stability.md:25`,
  `docs/exit-codes.md:43`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:484`, `docs/llm-framework.md:462`,
  `docs/releasing.md:250`, `docs/workflow-editor.md:160`, `docs/workflow-engine.md:29`,
  `docs/adr/0043-…:121`, `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md:462,467`,
  `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh:130`, and the plan-review criteria
  text in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:407`,
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5e.md:10`, plus the prose comment in
  `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:307`. (The rename breaks zero code — every `src/` hit is a
  prose comment; the unrelated `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var does not match `CLAUDE.md`.)
- **Owned by other stories (out of scope here):** `docs/event-schema.md:46` (S1 replaces that
  pointer) and `examples/claude-skills/{rebar-implement/SKILL.md,rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md}`
  (S5 repoints them).
- **Deliberately NOT changed:** `CHANGELOG.md` (3 hits) — a changelog is a historical record of
  past changes made when the file *was* `CLAUDE.md`; rewriting it would falsify history.
- **Commit the Codex config:** bring `.codex/config.toml` under version control (`git add -f`,
  it is currently locally excluded) pointing at `AGENTS.md`, comment updated to the completed state.
- **Commit the generic rules file:** bring `.agents/rules/rebar.md` under version control as a
  concise distillation that **references `AGENTS.md`** as the source of truth (Antigravity
  `.agents/rules/*` does not support `@`-imports, so a short reference-and-summary, not a symlink).
- **Per-tool pointers:** record the decision on optional `.github/copilot-instructions.md` /
  `.cursor/rules` / Gemini config. Default: **defer to a follow-up** (none added here).

## Scope

In: the ~17 owned files listed above, `.codex/config.toml`, `.agents/rules/rebar.md`. Out: files owned by S1/S5, `CHANGELOG.md`, the root-file/template changes. **Depends on S1, S2, S3** (S1 and S5 must land their reference updates for the global tree to be clean; S2 must create `AGENTS.md`). Rollback: `git revert` — docs/config/text only, no data migration.

## Assumption (flag for override)

The epic's goal (guidance *available to* Codex/Cursor/Antigravity) is only met if the provider configs are committed, so this story brings `.codex/` and `.agents/` into version control. If the team wants provider configs to stay per-developer/local, drop those two bullets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] This story's 17 owned files carry no `CLAUDE.md` reference (verifiable on this story alone;
  the thin `CLAUDE.md` pointer, historical `CHANGELOG.md`, and the S1-/S5-owned files are excluded
  because they are out of this story's scope).
  - Proving: `[ "$(git grep -c 'CLAUDE\.md' -- ':!CLAUDE.md' ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!docs/event-schema.md' ':!examples' ':!docs/experiments' | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s+0}')" = 0 ]`
- [ ] The plan-review criteria text (both the `src/rebar/llm` files and the
  `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` mirror) references `AGENTS.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`.
  - Proving: `[ "$(git grep -c 'CLAUDE\.md' -- src/rebar/llm docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s+0}')" = 0 ]`
- [ ] `.codex/config.toml` is git-tracked and points at `AGENTS.md`.
  - Proving: `[ -n "$(git ls-files .codex/config.toml)" ] && git grep -q 'AGENTS.md' -- .codex/config.toml`
- [ ] `.agents/rules/rebar.md` is git-tracked and references `AGENTS.md` as the source of truth.
  - Proving: `[ -n "$(git ls-files .agents/rules/rebar.md)" ] && git grep -q 'AGENTS.md' -- .agents/rules/rebar.md`
- [ ] [operator-attested] The per-tool-pointer decision (default: defer) is recorded as a comment
  on this ticket citing the choice.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass and the module-size CI gate is green.
  - Proving: `make lint && make test`
baseline.summary: Retarget provider shims to AGENTS.md + repo-wide reference sweep + optional per-tool pointers

## Discovered from

Step 7 sibling sweep during rebar-debug on bug `smart-disloyal-naga` (8386-a512-4815-4e6b). Same construct, different entry kind. Confirmed semantically (by reading the code path, not a string match) and then observed at runtime.

## Problem

Bug 8386 fixed the write amplification on `tickets-<sha>` entries by hardlinking unchanged blobs against a verified neighbouring entry. The **code** entry path has exactly the same construct and was deliberately left out of that fix's scope.

`materialize` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`, the `cache.acquire` populate branch) builds `<store>/<sha>` with the same `_materialize_tree` — `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index --all --force` — so every blob is written fresh, with no hardlink and no delta against an adjacent entry.

**Observed at runtime** (scratch store, 40-file tree, 4 successive `cache.acquire` calls each after a commit touching ONE file):

    code entries: 4 resolutions -> files=170 distinct_bytes=385118 one_tree~96240 (4.00x)

Charging each `(st_dev, st_ino)` exactly once, four adjacent-SHA resolutions cost **4.00x one tree** — identical to the pre-fix tickets number, i.e. zero sharing.

## Why it was scoped out of 8386, and why it is still worth doing

Weaker in the field than the tickets case, on two counts: the code tree is ~41.6 MiB / 3,131 files against the ticket store's ~620 MiB / 69,984 blobs (15x smaller), and the default code ref `origin/main` genuinely does have key reuse — it moves per merge, and concurrent gates collapse onto one SHA, which is the case ADR 0005 D2 was written for. That is why the tickets key was the acute problem and this one is not.

It is still real: this host holds **29,450 code entries**, and `--ref HEAD` (the documented way to review committed-but-unlanded code) makes the key move per commit, which is the fast-moving regime the ADR's reuse assumption does not cover.

Held out of 8386 on blast radius, not on doubt: code snapshots are the **attestation basis for signed verdicts**, so changing how they are built deserves its own review rather than riding along with a ticket-store performance fix.

## What makes this cheap now

8386 landed `src/rebar/_snapshot/delta_tree.py` as a **generic** donor-selection + hardlink-clone
+ delta-apply helper that takes the source repo, the target sha, and a destination. It was
written not to depend on anything ticket-specific. Wiring the code path through it should be small; the work is in the review and the test, not the algorithm.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `materialize`'s populate branch reuses unchanged blobs from a verified neighbouring code
      entry, or the decision not to is recorded with its reasoning.
- [x] A test observes the amplification RED (N adjacent-SHA code resolutions consume ~N trees)
      and GREEN after (~1 tree), asserting distinct-inode bytes rather than wall-clock.
- [x] Each entry still byte-matches the committed tree at its own SHA, and the LFS-pointer and
      submodule caveat sidecars are still computed correctly for a delta-built entry.
- [x] The attestation argument is stated explicitly: sharing storage must not weaken the claim
      that `<store>/<sha>` is the tree at `<sha>`.
baseline.summary: Code snapshot entries have the same no-sharing write amplification as the ticket entries

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`verify.enable_code_review` (default False — src/rebar/_config_schema.py:191, parsed in src/rebar/_config_sections.py:26) is wired as an ENABLEMENT switch for the whole code-review capability, not an ENFORCEMENT switch for the gate. `gate_dispatch.code_review_enabled()` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:273) is consulted at the top of `rebar.llm.code_review.shim.review_code()` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py:168), and when the flag is off a MANUAL, explicit invocation — the CLI `rebar review-code`, the library `review_code()`, the MCP `review_code` tool — does zero work and returns the inert `_disabled_review_result()` ("code-review capability disabled (verify.enable_code_review is off).", empty findings, UNPINNED provenance).

Why this is wrong:
- An explicit manual invocation IS the operator's statement of intent. Gating it on a config var conflates two different questions: "should code review run when asked?" (always yes — the user asked) and "should code review be ENFORCED as a blocking gate in automated flows?" (the thing a config knob should decide).
- AGENTS.md and `rebar explain review` tell authors to "preview the review locally with `rebar review-code` before you push". On any checkout that has not flipped `verify.enable_code_review`, that documented flow silently returns an empty PASS-looking verdict — a trap: the author believes their change was reviewed clean when nothing ran.
- The workaround inside rebar itself proves the design smell: the review-bot adapter must FORCE-ENABLE the capability to do its job (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:16, `request.enabled` override at gate_dispatch.py:373).
- Sibling gates already model this correctly: the criteria-registry posture distinguishes per-criterion `blocking_enabled` (src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:62) — i.e., enforcement — from the operation being invocable at all.

## Approach (direction, refine at claim time)
Repurpose the config axis from enablement to enforcement:
- A manual/explicit `review-code` invocation (CLI, library, MCP) always runs the four-pass gate — no config precondition beyond a working LLM config.
- The config knob (renamed or reinterpreted, e.g. `verify.enforce_code_review` / gate-posture semantics) decides only whether automated flows treat code-review as a required/blocking gate (voter posture, workflow dispatch), preserving today's off-by-default ENFORCEMENT.
- Keep the inert-empty-result shape for automated dispatch paths when enforcement is off, so existing pipelines that probe the gate cheaply do not start paying LLM costs.
- Decide the compatibility story for the existing `verify.enable_code_review` key explicitly (tombstone-warn or alias), matching the deprecation conventions used for prior config-key removals.

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py — drop the enabled() precondition from the manual entrypoint
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py — split enforcement posture from invocability
- src/rebar/_config_schema.py — enforcement-semantics key (+ compat handling for enable_code_review)
- src/rebar/_config_sections.py — parse the new/renamed key
- src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py — remove the force-enable workaround
- docs/config.md — document enforcement semantics

## Scope narrowed by operator ruling (2026-08-21, recorded in comments)
"review-code should not require a config key to be active. It should operate comparably to plan review: a config key controls whether it is REQUIRED, not whether it is AVAILABLE. Making it required is out of scope for this bug; dropping the config key gating availability is approved." The enforcement-repurposing items below are therefore struck from this bug's scope; only the availability-gate removal lands here (Gerrit change 2010, commit a1a6a151bc).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar review-code` on a checkout with no code-review config key set runs the four-pass gate and returns real findings (not the inert "capability disabled" result).
- [x] The library `review_code()` and MCP `review_code` tool behave identically to the CLI in that respect.
- [x] A config knob still exists that controls whether AUTOMATED dispatch runs the code-review gate, default off, and automated dispatch honors it: `verify.enable_code_review` (src/rebar/_config_schema.py) is consulted by `_code_review_preflight` when a `CodeReviewRequest` leaves `enabled=None` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py), pinned by tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py::test_produce_verdict_disabled_is_inert_and_makes_zero_llm_calls and tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py::test_disabled_code_review_never_invokes_runner. (Per the operator ruling, REPURPOSING it into a blocking-enforcement knob is out of scope for this bug.)
- [x] The review-bot adapter (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py) keeps its explicit `enabled=True` — per the operator ruling and the 2026-08-17 escalation comment, receiver deployment is its enforcement control — and its module docstring now documents that this is the same intent-is-authoritative semantics as the explicit surface, not a workaround.
- [x] The `verify.enable_code_review` key is neither renamed nor deprecated (struck per the operator ruling — no compatibility disposition is needed): it keeps its current meaning for `enabled=None` dispatch callers, documented at its declaration in src/rebar/_config_schema.py and in `code_review_enabled`'s docstring (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py).
- [x] The `rebar explain review` guide and llm-framework/config docs describe the availability semantics (explicit invocation always runs; the key gates only `enabled=None` dispatch). docs/config.md carries no entry for this key; the generated docs/config-reference.md row remains accurate unchanged.
baseline.summary: Code-review config gates enablement, not enforcement: manual rebar review-code silently returns an inert empty verdict unless verify.enable_code_review is set

baseline.description:
## Context
F12 (story 65c9, "Complete registry-backed CLI help discovery") committed one help artifact for every visible route that is not retired and generates the CLI reference from those artifacts. Manual review found writing-guideline violations in the help that F12 newly exposed. The affected output inherits parser descriptions and option help strings that predate the documentation policy. Violations occur in help for `verify-completion`, `sign-review`, `explain`, `review-plan`, `review-code`, `scan-spec`, `verify-identity`, `verify-authorship`, `verify-opcert`, `verify-commit-ticket`, `enrich`, `trusted-env`, and `remote-cert`, and in the aggregated `overview.txt` summaries. F08A and F10 do not provide general coverage for parser-owned CLI help. The operator rejected character restrictions and other mechanical prose enforcement.

The writing rules that the affected text breaks are defined in `docs/documentation-policy.md` under "Writing rules": no em dash or en dash, no semicolon, no clause-joining colon, no spaced-hyphen connector used as a dash, formal complete sentences for an external audience, and the banned-word list.

## Scope
The scope is exactly the parser-owned help that F12 newly committed (the 21 artifacts added in commit `131e75a`) that carries a violation, corrected at the maintained parser source, plus the two generated projections (`overview.txt` and `docs/cli-reference.md`). Help that predates F12 and was already exposed is out of scope. Usage strings, metavar tokens, option flag names, exit codes, and configuration keys are technical identifiers and stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Source-to-artifact trace
Each violating generated line is corrected at its maintained source:
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/llm.py` owns the descriptions and option help for `review-code`, `scan-spec`, `verify-completion`, `explain`, `review-plan`, `sign-review`, and the shared `_add_ref_source` helper (`--ref` / `--source`).
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/verify.py` owns `verify-opcert`, `verify-identity` / `verify-authorship`, and `verify-commit-ticket`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/enrich.py` owns the `enrich` `mode` help.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/certs.py` owns the `trusted-env` positional and `--root` help.
- `src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py` module docstring is used verbatim as the `remote-cert` description.
The committed `src/rebar/_cli/help/*.txt` artifacts and `docs/cli-reference.md` are regenerated from these sources by the existing generators; they are never hand-edited.

## Implementation plan
1. Rewrite the parser descriptions and option help strings above for an external user audience: replace em/en dashes and clause-joining colons with complete sentences, remove semicolons, remove banned words and all-caps emphasis padding, and keep each Markdown/paragraph line as one logical line. Preserve command meaning, argparse behavior, technical identifiers, config keys, flag names, and exit codes exactly.
2. Regenerate the committed help with `python scripts/gen_cli_help.py` and the CLI reference with `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`.
3. Verify no drift with `python scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check` and `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check`.

## Testing approach
Portability: all validation runs through repository scripts and pytest with no dependency on any specific CI provider.
- The existing drift checks (`scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check`, `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check`, and `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py`) prove the committed artifacts stay byte-current with the parser sources after the rewrite.
- Add one focused content-specific contract test, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_help_writing_guidelines_jerboa.py`, that asserts the specific corrected wording of the affected commands (positive assertions on the rewritten phrasing plus the absence of the exact constructs that were removed from those named commands). This is a narrow behavior test over the affected commands, not a repository-wide character gate, banned-word scanner, or punctuation scanner.

No mechanical character or prose enforcement gate is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The affected committed help and CLI reference prose conforms to the project writing guidelines.
- [x] Each changed generated line is corrected at its maintained parser source.
- [x] Command semantics, syntax, technical identifiers, and exit behavior remain unchanged.
- [x] The help and CLI-reference drift checks pass (`gen_cli_help.py --check`, `gen_cli_reference.py --check`).
- [x] Focused CLI help contracts pass.
- [x] No mechanical character or prose enforcement is introduced.
baseline.summary: F20 align generated CLI help with documentation writing guidelines

## Why
The GitHub CodeQL "Security and quality" scan flags `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` in `docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/runtime_pydanticai_poc.py` (code-scanning alerts 3 and 4). That file is a hand-run proof-of-concept: it is not packaged (the wheel/sdist ship only `src/rebar` — `pyproject.toml:213`), is on no `import rebar` path, and never runs in production. The findings are false positives (they log public provider-name strings such as "anthropic"/"openai", not secrets). The individual alerts have been dismissed, but any code under `docs/` keeps generating recurring scan noise on every push. The advanced-setup CodeQL workflow (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`) currently passes no config, so nothing is excluded.

## What
Add a CodeQL config file that excludes `docs/**` from analysis and wire it into the workflow, so the exclusion is durable (survives future `docs/experiments` additions) rather than relying on per-alert dismissals.
- New file `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` with `paths-ignore: ["docs/**"]`.
- Edit `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: pass `config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` to the
  `github/codeql-action/init` step. No change to the default query suite (only path scoping).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` exists and its `paths-ignore` list covers `docs/**`.
- [ ] The CodeQL workflow `init` step (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`) references that config via `config-file:`.
- [ ] `python -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml')); assert 'docs/**' in d['paths-ignore']"` exits 0 (config parses and contains the exclusion).
- [ ] No file under `src/rebar` is modified in this change (config/workflow only, so no runtime behavior change) — verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main` listing only `.github/` paths.

## Verification
- `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml'))"` — config is valid YAML.
- `grep -q 'config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml' .github/workflows/codeql.yml` — wiring present.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main` — shows only `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` and `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`.

## Out of scope
- The 27 valid `py/path-injection` findings and the `py/stack-trace-exposure` finding (alert 27): those
  need real code fixes and are tracked separately.

## Problem

`tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py::test_code_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union` failed CI on the checked `git push origin HEAD:tickets` in `_assert_emit_is_append_only` (currently line 1738), costing Gerrit change 1655 a spurious `Verified -1`.

## The filed premise is FALSIFIED (evidence in comments)

Filed hypothesis: a lost CAS / non-fast-forward between two clones racing the push leg. The job's captured log disproves it. The push was rejected by the RECEIVING repository with `unresolved deltas left after unpacking`, `remote unpack failed: unpack-objects abnormal exit`, and `refs/heads/tickets does not point to a valid object!` — the remote rejected the pack as an unpacker error. There is no `non-fast-forward`, no `cannot lock ref`, and no OOM/signal anywhere in the job. The same warning repeats 18 times with a monotonically climbing unpushed-commit counter, so the fixture's bare `remote.git` was already missing objects from the FIRST emit push onward: the remote was corrupt before any assertion ran.

This is object loss inside the fixture's own remote, not a ref race between the two clones. The earlier sibling occurrence failed differently (an empty clone-B event set, root-caused and fixed by willing-cellular-carp), so the two are distinct mechanisms.

## Root cause

Three facts compose:

1. `two_clones` creates the bare remote with a plain `git init --bare` (line 216) and never
   configures it.
2. `_make_repo` clones that local path with no `--no-hardlinks` (line 66), so repo A/B
   `.git/objects` are HARDLINKED to `remote.git/objects`, and `.tickets-tracker` is a linked
   worktree sharing repo A's object database (`_commands/init.py:381`).
3. rebar's gc-config ensure unit (`_commands/init.py:112-155`) deliberately re-enables
   auto-gc but forces it FOREGROUND (`gc.autoDetach=false`, `maintenance.autoDetach=false`),
   precisely because a DETACHED background gc/maintenance repacking an object database
   outside the write lock corrupts the store (bug 88eb, ADR 0051; `_store/sync.py:17-26`).

That pinning reaches the tracker and its enclosing clone. It does NOT reach the bare remote. `remote.git` is therefore the one repository in the fixture whose `receive-pack` runs `git gc --auto` at git's defaults — DETACHED — after each of the ~50 emit pushes, repacking and pruning its object store concurrently with the next incoming push. git-clone(1) also warns that local hardlink clones can race with concurrent modification of the source repository, which is exactly the shape here.

## Scope

Fixture/test-only; no `src/rebar` behaviour change. Fixing it at the remote-creation and clone sites covers all 16 `push … HEAD:tickets` sites in this file at once.

Reconciled with depraved-frowzy-trout: that audit classified read-sync preconditions (`_expire_sync_marker` to `_sync_from_origin`). It did not classify push sites, so there is no kept-as-fail-fast decision being overturned here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — The fixture's bare remote is pinned to the same no-detached-upkeep posture rebar
      pins on trackers, and the clones no longer hardlink its object store. The reason is
      recorded at the fixture with the bug 88eb / ADR 0051 reference.
- [x] AC2 — A regression test asserts that posture on the fixture's remote, so a future
      fixture that drops the pin fails deterministically here rather than rarely in CI.
- [x] AC3 — Fail-fast preserved: a genuinely failing push still fails. Proven by a test that
      makes the remote reject a push and asserts the fixture's push path still raises. No
      retry, no swallowed error, and no wall-clock bound is introduced.
- [x] AC4 [operator-attested] — The affected file passes at least 20 consecutive runs under CI's settings
      (`-n 4 --dist loadgroup`), with the evidence recorded in a comment.
- [x] AC5 [operator-attested] — `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Two-clone sidecar fixture races on the tickets push leg

baseline.description:
## Problem

Change 1996 (`02f71da097`, RP-05 S5) added two steps to `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` that invoke repository files, **without the if-present guard this repo mandates for exactly this case**:

```yaml
- name: parser-derived docs are byte-current on the lean wheel
  run: |
    /tmp/clean/bin/python scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check
    /tmp/clean/bin/python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check

- name: clean-wheel distribution + every-help-form byte contract (portable pytest)
  run: |
    /tmp/clean/bin/python -m pytest ... tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py -rs
```

`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py` was **created by that same commit** (141 lines, new file).

## Mechanism

Gerrit's verify job takes the workflow **DEFINITION** from the target branch but checks out the **CHANGE'S** tree. So a step added on `main` runs against every open change whose base predates it. The test file is absent in those trees, pytest collects nothing, and exits 4:

```
collected 0 items
============================ no tests ran in 0.01s ============================
##[error]Process completed with exit code 4.
```

That is a `Verified -1` caused by the gate, not by the change under review.

## Measured blast radius — 3 open changes, all innocent

Failing the identical job at 34-47s, none of them touching the CLI registry or packaging:

| change | subject |
|---|---|
| 1997 | Resolve access-check client seam at call time |
| 1998 | Stop absent-string child oracles failing open |
| 1999 | Fail closed on stale KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS rows |

`main` itself is green: "Optional-Dependency Isolation (mirror)" and the full "Test Suite (mirror)" both succeeded, and the whole job reproduces clean locally against `origin/main` in a no-extras venv (`rebar --help` exit 0; agents-absent assertion OK; 17 passed).

## The remedy already exists in this repo

This hazard is documented (ticket `ee2a`, bug `1909-c1a7-9f20-440f`) and every other script-invoking gate step carries the guard. From `_build-and-test.yml`:

```yaml
- name: comment-hygiene gate
  run: |
    if [ ! -f scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py ]; then
      echo "not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping;" \
           "the gate re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change"
      exit 0
    fi
    python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py
```

The Verified-gate parity gate and the raw-git-write gate use the same shape. The two new optionality steps are the outliers.

## Why this is a defect and not a nuisance

A gate that reds a change for a reason unrelated to the change **trains reviewers to discount the gate**. That is the failure mode `recheck` discipline exists to prevent: once a `-1` can mean "your base is old", every `-1` becomes ambiguous, and the two-vote gate loses its meaning as evidence. The cost is already visible — three unrelated changes, each of whose authors must otherwise investigate a failure that is not theirs.

## Scope

Add the established if-present guard to the two new steps. Match the existing wording so the skip is self-explaining.

Explicitly OUT of scope: changing what the steps check, weakening either `--check`, or altering the distribution contract. The steps are correct; only their unguarded invocation is wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Both new steps skip with an explanatory message when their target file is absent from the
      checked-out tree, matching the existing guard wording — verified by a test or a CI dry-run
      against a tree lacking the file
- [x] Both steps still run and still fail on a tree that DOES contain the file, so the guard
      cannot be satisfied by simply never running — verified by a positive case
- [x] A change based on pre-`02f71da097` `main` passes the optionality lane — verified against
      one of 1997/1998/1999 before their rebase, or an equivalent reconstruction
baseline.summary: New optionality gate steps lack the if-present guard, so every open change with an older base fails Verified

## Context / Problem

Originally an evidence + proposal ticket for an additive-obligation parity criterion (P0-P3). The operator rulings recorded in this ticket's comments (2026-08-21) narrowed the executable scope, and this description now reflects only that approved scope:

- **P2 — APPROVED, no replay necessary:** widen plan-review overlay T13's trigger lexicon from
  *prohibition* to *obligation*. Operator expectation on record: the phrasing seems specific
  enough that it will provide minimal value — implement as the cheap prompt edit it is.
- **P1 — ASSESSMENT ONLY, no implementation:** measure whether the recommended
  content-triggered widening of `surface-parity` (plus the NDJSON/import channel) would have
  yielded historical false positives, before any adoption decision.
- **P0 (import-integrity) — DEFERRED:** pending separate operator confirmation of the
  deterministic CI import-walk alternative. Not touched here.
- **P3 (`project.obligation-parity` overlay) and ci-gate-compat — REJECTED:** not touched;
  the ci-gate-compat decline is being recorded in the gap-analysis doc under ticket 0778-b9c8.

The full original evidence (samples, base rates, prior art) is preserved verbatim in the first comment on this ticket.

## Approach

**P2 (the code change).** T13's rubric body is the packaged prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T13.md` (trigger lexicon at lines 12-14 currently lists prohibition verbs only: "block", "reject", "require … before", "enforce", "must pass", "cannot merge until", "deny", "fail the build if"); its router applicability text is the `"T13"` entry in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (line 1108, trigger: "plan NEWLY FORBIDS a previously-permitted action"). Widen both from prohibition-only to obligation: the overlay also applies when the plan ADDS a new obligation — a contract, invariant, schema field, required argument, or a second site that must stay in step — that existing sites now owe. Keep the MIGRATED/EXEMPTED/UNCOVERED classification, the fail-open abstain rule, and the advisory posture/threshold unchanged. The deterministic pre-gate in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_gate_rules.py` gains a second alternation branch carrying the additive-obligation lexicon (per the Gerrit LLM-Review reachability finding on change 2035: additive-only phrasings otherwise never reach the router); the audit-verbatim enforcement branch (ticket 696a) stays byte-for-byte, and fires-side unit coverage is added. Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with its generator (`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide`, implemented at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_guide.py:48`) — never hand-edit the guide.

**P1 (analysis, no code).** Enumerate historical commits in a recent window (target: the last ~60 days or ~40 qualifying commits, whichever bounds first) that changed CLI argument/guard surfaces under `src/rebar/_cli/` — i.e. commits the widened content-triggered surface-parity would have TRIGGERED on. For each, determine ground truth from the diff and surrounding history: did the MCP or NDJSON/import surface genuinely owe a matching update, and was it updated? Classify each would-be finding TP/FP, report the FP rate, and compare against the ~90%-`none` omitted-scope-site precedent already cited in this ticket. Judgment + git evidence only — no paid LLM review replays. Record the result as a ticket comment prefixed "P1 FP ASSESSMENT:" with trigger count, TP/FP split, and an adopt/narrow/reject recommendation.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T13.md` — widen title/trigger paragraph wording from
  prohibition-only to obligation
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `"T13"` trigger text and checklist
  wording widened to match
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — regenerated output only
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_gate_rules.py` — additive-obligation alternation branch on
  the T13 pre-gate (review-driven; audit-verbatim branch unchanged)
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_criterion_gates.py` — fires-side coverage for that branch

No other files change; P0/P3/ci-gate-compat artifacts are untouched.

## Testing

Prompt-content change with existing coverage: `tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py` (`test_g5_prohibition`) asserts the MIGRATED/EXEMPTED/UNCOVERED enums remain in the prompt and the T13 eval cases stay wired; `tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_criterion_gates.py` covers the untouched deterministic pre-gate; the guide-parity validation (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/guide_parity.py`) fails if the regenerated guide diverges from the registry. Run those targeted tests plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`. Default: no new tests — the edit adds no new runtime behavior (assume this unless an existing test fails).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] T13's rubric applies to newly ADDED obligations, not only prohibitions; checked by
      `grep -c obligation src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T13.md` returning >= 1 and the
      trigger paragraph naming additive obligation examples.
- [x] The routing entry matches the widened applicability; checked by `rebar explain T13`
      showing the obligation wording.
- [x] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is generator output; checked by re-running the
      generator and `git diff --exit-code docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` passing.
- [x] Targeted tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` pass in the worktree venv.
- [x] The P2 commit carries the `rebar-ticket: 5bca-4ca9-3dc8-4abd` trailer and is pushed to
      Gerrit `refs/for/main`; checked by the Gerrit change existing with both gate votes
      requested (landing is gated on `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`).
- [x] A "P1 FP ASSESSMENT:" comment is recorded on this ticket with trigger count, TP/FP
      split, FP rate vs the ~90%-`none` precedent, and a recommendation; checked by
      `rebar show 5bca-4ca9`.
- [x] The diff touches only the five Scope paths (P0 deferred, P3/ci-gate-compat rejected);
      checked by `git show --stat` on the P2 commit.

## Verification

`make lint`, `make typecheck`, targeted pytest above, generator idempotence check, and the two Gerrit gate votes on the pushed change (change 2035). Adjudication is complete: P0 is resolved by operator ruling as the deterministic CI import-walk, built separately under ticket 37b9-fa7e — not this ticket's work; P3 and ci-gate-compat are REJECTED (rulings on record in comments). With the P2 change landed and the P1 FP assessment recorded, this story's evidence + proposal + ruling promise is fulfilled and the ticket closes.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Scheduled Mirror Guard run 32567576681 (2026-08-22T10:25:45Z) failed its replication check — Gerrit main SHA != GitHub main SHA — during a heavy merge burst; the next scheduled run (32568260546, +16 min) passed. The mirror was trailing by minutes: expected, self-healing replication lag, not an outage. A red run on main for this primes agents/operators to investigate a non-issue (same noise class as the 3ff9-a8f0 operator ruling: "suppress under normal load — noise, not outage signal").

RCA (see the Phase 1 comment on this ticket, confirmed at runtime): `replication_verdict` (src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:44-73) reports instantaneous SHA equality by design — its own docstring (lines 47-50, shipped in introducing commit d96628c9dca) states transient divergence (~15s post-submit) is expected and "the *alarm's* evaluation window (sustained divergence) absorbs transient lag". The secondary watcher implements that window (infra/terraform/monitoring_ws7.tf:40-44: 2x5-min sustained, "so the normal ~15s post-submit replication lag never pages"). The primary watcher (.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml) never got one: it runs `python -m rebar.mirror_guard --replication` once and fails on a single instantaneous sample. Classification: incomplete-implementation — the designed lag-absorption was never built on the workflow surface. caused_by: a774-5ca9-3a80-4f6d (scope-of-work; the omission shipped with a774's own commit d96628c9dca).

## Approach
Give the guard an in-process, scheduler-agnostic evaluation window in `src/rebar/mirror_guard.py` (this satisfies project.portability: the tolerance lives in the module, not in any CI provider's retry/state machinery — comparing against the previous run via the Actions API was rejected as GitHub-specific with no portable fallback). This approach fits because it implements exactly the absorption the module's own docstring already delegates to the alarm layer, using the same "sustained divergence" semantics the sibling CloudWatch alarm already encodes:

- Keep `replication_verdict(gerrit_sha, github_sha)` unchanged (it correctly reports the instantaneous truth; its contractual schema test at tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py:104 is superset-pinned `set(v) >= {...}`).
- Add a persistence wrapper `replication_check_with_lag_tolerance(fetch_pair, *, attempts=3, delay_seconds=45.0, sleep=time.sleep) -> dict`: fetch (gerrit_sha, github_sha); if the sample is in sync OR a SHA is missing, return that verdict immediately (one fetch, zero sleeps — the common healthy case pays nothing; missing-SHA keeps today's immediate-failure behavior). On divergence, sleep `delay_seconds` and re-sample, up to `attempts` total samples; return healthy the moment a sample converges (annotated `"samples": n`, reason "transient replication lag, converged"). If all samples diverge, return the last unhealthy verdict with `"samples"` and a reason distinguishing a static GitHub tip ("replication stalled") from a moving-but-not-converged tip. Any non-converged outcome still fails — strictly no weakening: today's failure set minus lag-that-converges-within-the-window. A GitHub-ahead/foreign divergence (true invariant breach) never converges to the Gerrit SHA, so it still fails every run.
- `run()` (src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:184, existing symbol confirmed by reading the tree) gains keyword params `lag_attempts: int = 3`, `lag_delay_seconds: float = 45.0`, `sleep=time.sleep` and drives the replication check through the wrapper; fetch exceptions keep propagating to the existing except -> exit 2 path. Defaults: 3 samples x 45s spacing (~90s window, ~6x the documented ~15s expected lag) unless flags say otherwise.
- `main()` gains `--lag-attempts` / `--lag-delay` flags wired to those params (defaults as above).
- `.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml`: header comment updated to state the new semantics (fails when divergence persists across the in-run window; transient post-submit lag self-clears) — no functional workflow change.
- Module docstring updated: the CLI itself now provides the alarm-layer evaluation window portably; the CloudWatch alarm remains the secondary sustained-divergence pager.
- Keep every touched function under the McCabe ceiling (wrapper is a small loop; run() gains no branches beyond the call swap).

## Scope
- src/rebar/mirror_guard.py — persistence wrapper, run()/main() params + flags, docstring.
- tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py — new behavioral tests for the tolerance window; update `test_run_divergence_exit_1` (line 141) to inject a no-op sleep so it exercises the persistent-divergence path without real sleeping (assertion `code == 1` unchanged).
- .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml — header comment only.

## Testing
All unit-level, monkeypatched fetchers, injected no-op sleep — no network, no real sleeping (the suite's socket guard already forbids network):
- Happy path: first sample in sync -> healthy, exactly 1 fetch and 0 sleep calls (counted via the injected fakes).
- Bug reproduction (RED first): fetch sequence diverged -> converged; today this exits 1 (single sample), after the fix it is healthy / exit 0 with reason noting convergence.
- Failure path kept loud: all samples diverged with static GitHub tip -> unhealthy, exit 1, reason names stalled replication and sample count.
- Failure path kept loud (ahead/foreign): all samples diverged with a moving, never-converging GitHub tip -> unhealthy, exit 1.
- Edge: missing SHA on first sample -> immediate unhealthy verdict, no re-sampling.
- Contractual: existing schema/exit-code tests still pass unchanged (schema is superset-pinned).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A fetch sequence [diverged, in-sync] through `run(check_replication=True, ...)` with injected no-op sleep returns exit code 0 and a healthy replication verdict (new unit test, seen RED on unfixed code first).
- [x] A fetch sequence of 3 diverged samples with a static GitHub SHA returns exit code 1 with a reason containing "stalled" and `samples == 3` (new unit test).
- [x] A fetch sequence of 3 diverged samples with a moving, never-converging GitHub SHA returns exit code 1 (new unit test — GitHub-ahead stays loud).
- [x] An in-sync first sample performs exactly one fetch-pair call and zero sleep calls (new unit test).
- [x] A missing-SHA first sample returns unhealthy immediately without re-sampling (new unit test).
- [x] Full tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py passes; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0, increased=0) all pass in the worktree venv.
- [x] .github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml header describes the persistence semantics (comment-only change, verified by reading the diff).
baseline.summary: Mirror Guard replication check alarms on single-sample expected lag

Store the baseline in the projection the comparison already computes: `description` as `normalize_rich_text(raw)`, `status`/`priority` as `.name`. Expected ~-66% on an **18.3 MB** (18,257,550-byte) file. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why this is safe without a comparator change
`outbound_field_diff.py:187,196` canonicalize BOTH sides at **read** time via `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` (docstring `:183`: "storage stays vendor-shaped, mapped at READ time only"), and both canonicalizers are idempotent on already-normalized values: `normalize_rich_text` (`inbound_fields.py:136-145`) returns `adf_to_text(body)` for dicts and `str(body)` otherwise; `_extract_jira_field_value` (`:92-96`) reads `name`/`displayName` for dicts and passes strings through. So ADF-dict and plain-text baselines canonicalize identically and a mixed store needs no new comparator. This also makes the change **revert-safe** — a normalized-string baseline round-trips unchanged through pre-A3 code.

CORRECTION carried forward: an earlier framing rested on `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields`, which have **zero production callers**. Validate against the live path only.

## Why assignee is EXCLUDED — data loss, not conflict noise
`_assignee_candidates` (`outbound_field_diff.py:56-67`) builds its match set from the scalar **plus every non-None identity form**, and `_suppressed_by_inbound` (`:250-256`) routes assignee through `_assignee_matches`. Collapsing three identity forms to one string shrinks that candidate set and loses inbound-directionality suppression, so local-wins **silently clobbers a concurrent remote assignee edit**. (The strict `assignee_identity` equality at `:390-394` is the lesser, secondary effect.) Keep assignee raw.

## Trap to pin
Store exactly `normalize_rich_text(raw)` — any other text extraction (fit/truncate/strip variants) diverges from what the same ADF decodes to on the read path and fabricates a permanent diff.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the **same
      verdict** as its normalized-string equivalent. Tier: **integration** through the real
      production comparison path. **This test does not exist today** —
      `test_binding_baseline.py:36-59` and `test_baseline_arbitration.py:91` use flat strings only, so
      a no-op-on-strings normalizer would leave them green while proving nothing. This is the RED case.
- [ ] The direction-preservation suite, extended with assignee shape cases (email / accountId /
      displayName), passes unchanged — proving assignee arbitration is untouched. Tier: **property/unit**.
- [ ] Baseline entries for `description`/`status`/`priority` are scalars after one pass; `assignee`
      remains a dict. Tier: **integration** asserting stored shapes.
- [ ] A corpus diff over real bindings shows **zero mutation delta** before vs after normalization.
      Tier: **repo-level corpus script**.
- [ ] `bindings.json` size drops by >=50%. Verify: byte comparison before/after one full pass.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py`

Scope: S-M. Depends on A2-1.
baseline.summary: A3: text-normalize baseline description/status/priority in set_baseline (assignee deliberately excluded)
