# S1 — Terraform base: EC2 box, networking, DNS subdomain, IAM, SSM secrets, state/backups

## Why
The PoC needs one cost-conscious, reproducible AWS host for Gerrit + the rebar MCP.
Codifying it as IaC is runtime-free and delivers the freeze-and-restore RTO (rebuild
from Terraform) without adding cost — so it serves P3 (reusability) without touching
P2 (cost). Everything else in this epic lands on this substrate.

## What
- One-time bootstrap (`infra/bootstrap/`): an S3 state bucket (versioning + SSE) created
  by a small standalone config applied ONCE manually — this breaks the state-backend
  chicken-and-egg (TF can't store state in a bucket it hasn't created yet). Its bucket
  name feeds the main config's backend block.
- `infra/terraform/` using roll-your-own raw resources (the ec2-instance module adds
  indirection at N=1):
  - `versions.tf`: `required_version = ">= 1.10"` (S3 native `use_lockfile` needs TF
    >=1.10; older TF SILENTLY ignores it and runs with NO locking) + `required_providers`
    (aws ~> 5).
  - `t4g.large` (Graviton, ~8 GB) on AL2023 arm64 — AMI resolved via the SSM public param
    `/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64` (NOT a hardcoded
    id); gp3 root + a separate gp3 data volume mounted at `/var/gerrit` with
    `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`; IMDSv2 required.
  - Default VPC; security group inbound 443 (HTTPS) + 29418 (Gerrit SSH); admin access via
    SSM Session Manager (no inbound 22). One Elastic IP, also `prevent_destroy = true`.
  - Route 53 A record `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` -> EIP in the existing public zone
    `Z05558453EZPQLHKC20IQ` (solutions.navateam.com).
  - IAM instance role: attach `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` (REQUIRED for Session Manager
    — the sole admin path) + SSM Parameter Store read (+ KMS decrypt) + CloudWatch basic.
  - SSM Parameter Store SecureString params (placeholders) for the Gerrit secrets, the
    GitHub replication deploy key, the rebar MCP HMAC signing key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
  - `user_data.sh` (cloud-init): at first boot, fetch the SSM SecureString params via the
    instance role and write them to a `chmod 600` `.env` (NO plaintext secrets in user_data
    itself); IMDSv2 enforced.
  - Terraform S3 backend with `use_lockfile=true` (no DynamoDB); DLM daily EBS snapshots of
    the data volume with a bounded `retain_rule { count = 7 }`.
- Packaging: ensure `infra/` is excluded from ALL distribution channels.

## Scope
In: the bootstrap + TF base + DNS subdomain + IAM + SSM scaffolding + boot script +
state/backup config + the packaging exclusion. Out: Gerrit/MCP containers (S2), Gerrit
config (S3), replication (S5), GitHub lockdown (S6).

## Files
- `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` (one-time state bucket: versioning + SSE)
- `infra/terraform/{versions,main,network,iam,ssm,dns,backup}.tf`
- `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` (SSM-pull -> chmod 600 .env boot script)
- `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]` include is `["src/rebar","tests","README.md"]`
  so `infra/` is excluded by default — add an explicit exclude + a build-artifact check)
- `docs/adr/0012-iac-foundations.md` (ADR capturing the three novel decisions: the S3 state-bucket bootstrap chicken-and-egg pattern, the no-DynamoDB S3-native locking choice gated on Terraform >=1.10, and the `/rebar/prod/*` SSM parameter naming contract — each with rationale)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform validate` and `plan` succeed (TF >=1.10 enforced via
      `required_version`); `apply` stands up a reachable `t4g.large` with EIP, gp3 root + data
      volume mounted at `/var/gerrit`, IMDSv2 enforced.
- [ ] The state-bucket bootstrap (`infra/bootstrap/`) is documented as a one-time manual apply;
      the main config's S3 backend uses `use_lockfile=true` (no DynamoDB), gated by `required_version >= 1.10`.
- [ ] The stateful data volume AND the EIP carry `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` (no silent
      destroy/recreate of Gerrit data on apply/rename/AMI change).
- [ ] `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` resolves (Route 53 A -> EIP in zone Z05558453EZPQLHKC20IQ); SG
      allows 443 + 29418; admin access via SSM Session Manager with the role granting
      `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` and no inbound 22.
- [ ] `user_data.sh` pulls the SSM SecureString params at boot to a `chmod 600` file; no plaintext
      secrets appear in user_data.
- [ ] DLM creates daily snapshots of the data volume with bounded retention (e.g. `retain_rule count=7`).
- [ ] `docs/adr/0012-iac-foundations.md` exists and records the three novel architectural decisions with rationale: (1) the S3 state-bucket bootstrap chicken-and-egg pattern, (2) the no-DynamoDB S3-native `use_lockfile` locking choice gated on Terraform >=1.10, and (3) the `/rebar/prod/*` SSM parameter naming contract.
- [ ] A built sdist AND wheel contain NO `infra/` files (deterministic check: `python -m build` then
      grep the artifacts for `infra/`). Homebrew + the MCP registry INHERIT this exclusion because both
      package the same built artifact (the formula builds from the sdist/release; the registry ships the
      wheel) — so the sdist/wheel check is the single source of truth, documented as such.

## Round-7 remediation
- **DLM service role (G6):** AWS Data Lifecycle Manager assumes its OWN IAM role (trust principal `dlm.amazonaws.com`, perms `ec2:CreateSnapshot`/`CreateTags`/`DescribeVolumes`/`DeleteSnapshot`). S1 creates this DLM service role and wires its ARN into the `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` `execution_role_arn` — without it DLM silently creates no snapshots.
- [ ] The DLM lifecycle policy references a created DLM service role (trust `dlm.amazonaws.com`) and is ENABLED (verified it would snapshot the data volume, not silently no-op).

## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)
- SSM SecureString scaffolding extended so no downstream lookup fails: ADD `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint` (consumed by S7 `monitoring.tf`) and `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` (consumed by S4a) to the enumerated placeholder params.
- Ownership contracts: S1 CREATES the single EC2 instance role (S2/S4a only add separately-named scoped inline policies, never re-declare it). S1 OWNS the DLM service role + `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` (retain count=7); S7 only asserts/monitors it (no second DLM resource).

Added ACs:
- [ ] SSM placeholder set includes `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint` and `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` (in addition to Gerrit secrets, deploy key, HMAC key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- [ ] The EC2 instance role and the DLM lifecycle policy + DLM service role are created HERE and only here; ADR-0012 records the single-owner contract (S2/S4a attach scoped policies; S7 only monitors DLM)


## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-29 — recalibrated gate BLOCK)
Two blocking findings fixed; advisories triaged and folded in.

**Blocking (resolved):**
- **B1 — bootstrap state-bucket destruction guard:** the `aws_s3_bucket` in `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` carries `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` (the state bucket is the third stateful resource alongside the data volume + EIP; without it a `terraform destroy` of the bootstrap stack deletes all TF state, defeating the rebuild-from-Terraform RTO). Destroying it requires an explicit state migration first; recorded in ADR-0012.
- **B2 — idempotent data-volume init:** `user_data.sh` MUST check-before-mkfs — `if ! blkid <device> >/dev/null 2>&1; then mkfs.xfs <device>; fi` — so an instance replacement (e.g. the SSM AMI pointer advancing) re-mounts the existing `/var/gerrit` volume WITHOUT reformatting. `prevent_destroy` guards the Terraform resource; the blkid guard guards the in-guest filesystem (mkfs is a runtime op TF cannot prevent).

**Advisories folded in:**
- **Enumerated SSM param names** (the `/rebar/prod/*` naming contract, recorded in ADR-0012): `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`, `/rebar/prod/gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key`, `/rebar/prod/github-replication-deploy-key`, `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key`, `/rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key`, `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint`, `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`.
- **Placeholder lifecycle + fail-fast:** params are created with a `CHANGEME` placeholder; the operator MUST populate real values before the S2 apply. `user_data.sh` exits non-zero (cloud-init marks the instance failed) if any fetched value still equals the placeholder sentinel — never silently writes broken config.
- **IAM least privilege:** the instance-role SSM read + `kms:Decrypt` is scoped to `arn:aws:ssm:<region>:<account>:parameter/rebar/prod/*` (no wildcard), referencing `data.aws_caller_identity`.
- **AMI drift:** `aws_instance` carries `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }`; an AMI upgrade is a deliberate runbook step, not a side effect of a routine apply.
- **Explicit volume sizes:** gp3 root 30 GB, data 50 GB, surfaced as variables.
- **`infra/terraform/variables.tf`** surfaces `snapshot_retention_count` (default 7), `instance_type` (default `t4g.large`), and the volume sizes.

**Added / updated ACs:**
- [ ] `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` state bucket has `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.
- [ ] `user_data.sh` volume init is idempotent (blkid check before mkfs); a re-run on instance replacement does not reformat the data volume.
- [ ] Instance-role SSM/KMS policy is scoped to `parameter/rebar/prod/*` (no wildcard), verified against the attached policy.
- [ ] `aws_instance` has `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }`; AMI upgrade is a documented runbook step.
- [ ] The SSM placeholder param set is enumerated by exact name and recorded in ADR-0012; `user_data.sh` fails fast on an unpopulated placeholder sentinel.
- [ ] gp3 volumes have explicit sizes (root 30 GB, data 50 GB) surfaced as Terraform variables in `variables.tf`.
- [ ] ADR-0012 records FOUR decisions: (1) the S3 state-bucket bootstrap chicken-and-egg, (2) no-DynamoDB S3-native `use_lockfile` gated on TF >=1.10, (3) the `/rebar/prod/*` SSM naming contract, (4) the single-owner contract for the EC2 instance role + DLM policy.


## Round-13 plan-review remediation (NVMe device naming on Nitro)
- **B2 refinement — NVMe-aware device resolution:** on t4g.large (Graviton/Nitro) AL2023 presents EBS volumes as NVMe devices (`/dev/nvme1n1`…), NOT the Xen `device_name` (`/dev/xvdf`) Terraform sets. `user_data.sh` therefore resolves the data volume's real device DYNAMICALLY by its EBS volume id rather than hardcoding a name: the volume id is passed into the script via `templatefile()`, and the script matches it against the NVMe controller serial (`for d in /dev/nvme*n1; do nvme id-ctrl -v "$d" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$VOL_NODASH" && DATA_DEV=$d; done`, or equivalently the AL2023 `/dev/disk/by-id/nvme-Amazon_Elastic_Block_Store_vol...` symlink / `ebsnvme-id`). Only after resolving `DATA_DEV` does the blkid-before-mkfs guard run, so the guard targets the correct device on Nitro. Added AC.
- [ ] `user_data.sh` resolves the data volume's NVMe device path dynamically by EBS volume id (not a hardcoded `/dev/xvdf`); the blkid-before-mkfs guard then runs against the resolved device. Verified the resolved device matches the attached data volume on the live t4g.large.

# DC renderer robustness & compliance hardening

## Context / Problem
The DC path shells out to pandoc per field. Two hazards from the DC experiment remain in scope: (1) **pathological-input hang** — one corpus body spun pandoc's jira reader 13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc sets no timeout, so a single field can stall the reconcile indefinitely; (2) **licence provenance** — pandoc is GPL and rides inside the `pypandoc-binary` wheel, so its pin and licence must be recorded.

A third hazard, the ~0.3s/field subprocess spawn tax (~20 min of wall time on a large serial reconcile), was originally to be addressed here by batching contiguous safe units into one pandoc call. **That is now DESCOPED** — see "Descoped" below.

## Prior art / dependency boundaries (do NOT re-decide 271c's choices)
- **The renderer and its pandoc delivery are owned by 271c.** Story
  `[rebar:271c-e88f-3220-4c9b]` LANDED the pure renderer at
  `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (merged `cf5155e528`), with pandoc from the pinned
  **`pypandoc-binary==1.15` wheel** (bundled binary, **pandoc 3.6.1**) via a `wiki` extra. This
  story hardens THAT module and VERIFIES that pin; it adds no system pandoc.
- Live wiring of `WikiTextCodec` belongs to the cutover story
  `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]` and is out of scope here, as is the change-gated
  "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property (that story's `rich_sha` gate).

## Approach
- **Hard timeout + process-group reaping.** A plain `subprocess.run(timeout=)` reaps only
  the DIRECT child, so a jira-reader spinning at ~95.8% CPU (a pipe-holding grandchild)
  survives (bug d843, bpo-30154). So the renderer MUST NOT use pypandoc's high-level
  `convert_text`/`convert_file` API (no process handle): it locates pandoc via
  `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, builds its OWN
  `subprocess.Popen([pandoc_path, …], start_new_session=True)` with
  `stdin=subprocess.PIPE` and delivers the unit via
  `proc.communicate(input=<unit markdown>, timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` — matching the
  landed `_convert`'s `input=markdown` semantics, NOT the cited ACLI case's
  `stdin=DEVNULL` (acli takes no stdin; pandoc READS the unit from stdin, so copying
  that kwarg verbatim would feed pandoc empty input and degrade every unit) — and, on
  `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, passes that `Popen` to **`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`**
  (`_proc.py:26`) — `killpg` SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL→bounded drain, already reused by the
  ACLI transport and grounding harness — killing the whole group. It kills/drains only
  AFTER a timeout is detected, so caller-side detection is required
  (`acli_subprocess.py`'s pattern). This REPLACES the landed `subprocess.run(timeout=30)`
  in `_convert` (`wiki_render.py`), which reaps only the direct child.
- **The timeout is a config key** (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default **10s**):
  >30× the observed ~0.3s/field render and ~80× below the 13.5-min hang;
  `grace`/`drain` reuse the ACLI caller's constants.
- **Fallback granularity is UNCHANGED — per unit.** On timeout or non-zero exit the unit
  degrades to its original Markdown verbatim (echo-safe), exactly as the landed
  `_render_unit` already does on conversion or preservation failure. One unit's failure
  never affects another, and no rendered output changes.
- **Compliance:** pin the wheel, create a repo-root `NOTICE` recording pandoc's GPL
  entry, and verify the pin in CI.

## Descoped: safe-run batching (operator decision, evidence-backed)
Batching contiguous safe units into one pandoc call was prototyped and measured against the landed renderer over the committed 178-body corpus, and is **removed from this story**: the ceiling is 233 runs vs 884 units, but 106 of 233 runs (46%) are single-unit so it is unreachable; run-level fallback costs 63/178 bodies (35%) their richness; verify-then-accept keeps richness but yields only 12% fewer spawns; and **21/178 bodies still render DIFFERENTLY even when a batch verifies**, because pandoc parses block boundaries relative to surrounding content. ~12% fewer spawns for changed output on ~12% of bodies is a bad trade, and a silent rendering change is not something to ship. Full measurements are in this ticket's comments; a follow-up idea ticket carries the 21-divergent-bodies analysis if spawn cost matters later.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — replace `_convert`'s `subprocess.run` with an
  own `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)` over `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, the
  caller-side timeout, and `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`. Per-unit fallback behaviour
  and all rendered output stay byte-identical.
- `pyproject.toml` — pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel version (extends 271c's pin).
- config (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s) across the standard four-file
  `reconciler.*` surface: `_config_schema.py` (field + `_as_float(v, k, minimum=0.0)`
  validator), `_config_sources.py` (auto-derived `REBAR_RECONCILER_DC_PANDOC_TIMEOUT_S`),
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json` (deliberately REGENERATED — the guard is removal-only, so
  it will NOT flag a new key's omission), and `docs/config.md`.
- CI workflow — verify the wheel pin (NOT an acli-style sha check).
- **`NOTICE` (NEW file, repo root)** — the repo has only `LICENSE` today and no
  SBOM/notice artifact, so this story CREATES `NOTICE` and records the wheel-bundled
  pandoc's GPL entry (name, version 3.6.1, licence, upstream) there.
- `tests/` — timeout, reaping and fallback tests over the vendored DC corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every pandoc invocation runs under a caller-side wall-clock timeout via
  `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` (config `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`,
  default 10s — above the ~0.3s render, below the 13.5-min hang); verified in
  `test_wiki_render_hardening.py` by `test_the_timeout_default_matches_the_config_default`,
  `test_the_timeout_is_read_from_config` and
  `test_a_non_positive_timeout_falls_back_rather_than_disabling_rendering`.
- [x] On `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` the whole process GROUP is reaped via
  `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, so a CPU-spinning grandchild is killed rather than
  orphaned; verified by `test_a_timeout_reaps_the_whole_process_group_not_just_the_child`
  (a real stand-in executable forks a spinning grandchild; the assertion is on the
  GRANDCHILD) plus `test_the_child_leads_its_own_process_group`.
- [x] On timeout or non-zero exit the affected UNIT degrades to its original Markdown
  without raising and the render returns; verified by
  `test_a_timed_out_unit_degrades_to_its_original_markdown`,
  `test_a_nonzero_exit_degrades_without_raising` and
  `test_an_unspawnable_pandoc_degrades_without_raising`.
- [x] Rendered output is byte-identical to the landed renderer for the whole committed
  178-body corpus, proving this story changes robustness only, not rendering; verified by
  `test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer` (~880 units, each rendered
  through both the new path and a transcript of the pre-hardening one).
- [x] `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` is reachable from config file and environment and
  documented; verified by `test_the_timeout_is_read_from_config`,
  `test_the_timeout_is_reachable_from_the_environment`, the regenerated
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json`, and the `docs/config.md` entry.
- [x] The pandoc binary comes from the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pinned by version in
  `pyproject.toml` (pinned `==1.15` by `271c`) and the pin is verified in CI; verified by the
  new `pandoc pin + NOTICE provenance gate` CI step plus
  `test_the_wheel_is_pinned_to_exactly_one_version`.
- [x] The wheel-bundled pandoc's GPL licence is recorded in a NEW repo-root `NOTICE` file
  (only `LICENSE` existed), naming pandoc, version 3.6.1 and its licence; verified by
  `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py`, which also binds NOTICE to the pyproject pin
  so the two cannot drift apart.
baseline.summary: DC renderer robustness & performance hardening

# ADR-0083's isinstance-only capability detection is unsafe on Python 3.12+

## The gap

ADR-0083 `docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md:193-197` prescribes: "Callers detect a capability by an `isinstance`-guarded check against the backend ... capability is observed via behavior, not structural introspection."

Since CPython 3.12 (gh-102433) a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol `isinstance` resolves members with `inspect.getattr_static`, which deliberately does NOT see attributes served by `__getattr__`. The prescribed check therefore returns a FALSE "capability absent" for any dynamically-proxying object.

This is TEMPORAL DECAY with a version boundary, not an authoring error. Measured on the same proxy object and Protocol: python3.11 -> `isinstance` True; python3.12 -> False. rebar's requires-python is >=3.11 and CI runs 3.11/3.12/3.13 (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:282`), so an isinstance-only guard is correct on one supported interpreter and silently skips writes on another.

Task `a3fa-e8d4-f4aa-4b51` fixed this LOCALLY in `_capability_present` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:140-199`, guard at line 188: `if isinstance(client, protocol) or hasattr(client, member)`). The ADR text was never changed; this ticket is that follow-up, so the next caller reading the ADR does not reimplement the hazard.

## Evidence already gathered (AC3 sweep, run under Python 3.12.13)

Sweep of `src/rebar` (`*.py`-scoped; unscoped greps are swamped by vendored JS under `llm/workflow/editor_assets/node_modules/`):

- `grep -rn "isinstance(.*Supports" src/rebar` -> ZERO hits. The Protocol is always passed
  indirectly as `_capability_present`'s `protocol` parameter.
- Only two `Supports*` Protocols exist, both `@runtime_checkable`, both in `_backend.py`:
  `SupportsLinks:505`, `SupportsComments:537`.
- Exactly ONE executable isinstance-against-Protocol capability dispatch exists in the tree:
  `dispatch_apply_phases.py:188`, reached from 4 sites (`dispatch_one.py:347`, `:602`, `:681`,
  `dispatch_apply_phases.py:319`). It is ALREADY proxy-hardened by the `or hasattr` disjunct.
- The only other Protocol isinstance is `_TransportPortMeta.__instancecheck__`
  (`_backend.py:213`), whose body is `all(hasattr(...))` — proxy-safe by construction, and it
  has zero call sites in `src/rebar`.
- Six `hasattr`-based capability checks (`apply_outbound.py:199,225`;
  `fetcher.py:302,597,647,688`) are the same decide-whether-to-act shape but proxy-safe.

Conclusion: nothing to FIX. The population is closed and every member is already proxy-safe. The remaining defect is the ADR TEXT, which still prescribes the unsafe shape.

## Plan

Documentation-only change to `docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`.

Insert a new amendment blockquote immediately after the existing `SupportsIncremental` amendment (which occupies lines 199-205), matching that block's established style — `> **AMENDED by [rebar:5c21-f24a-f7f8-4a55].**` lead-in, full four-quad ticket id. The amendment will:

1. State that `isinstance` against a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol is NECESSARY but NOT
   SUFFICIENT on Python 3.12+, citing `getattr_static` / gh-102433 and framing it as a version
   boundary that made previously-correct guidance unsafe.
2. Name the consequence: a decorator/wrapper/recording proxy transport HAS the capability but
   fails the check, so a conforming caller skips the write and reports the skip as DESIGNED —
   a silent soft failure.
3. Prescribe the sanctioned shape: `isinstance` primary, member-level `hasattr(obj, member)`
   fallback, and point at `_capability_present` as the reference implementation.
4. Record that the tree-wide sweep found no other affected site.

No source change. `_capability_present` keeps its current behaviour (AC4). Centralising the fallback for reuse is explicitly NOT done: with a single dispatch expression in the tree there is no second caller to share it, so extraction would be premature; this is recorded as the reasoned outcome rather than a follow-up ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

      amendment style, stating isinstance is necessary-but-not-sufficient on 3.12+ and citing
      the `getattr_static` behaviour plus the proxying-transport consequence.
- [x] AC2 — the amendment names the isinstance-primary + member-`hasattr`-fallback shape and
      cites `_capability_present` as the reference implementation.
- [x] AC3 — the sweep enumeration above is recorded on this ticket and every site is confirmed
      proxy-safe or fixed.
- [x] AC4 — `_capability_present` is unchanged; the centralisation question is answered
      explicitly rather than actioned inline.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green. [operator-attested]
- [x] the change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit before the ticket is closed. [operator-attested]

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_capability_guard_a3fa.py -q`

## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `smart-disloyal-naga` (8386-a512-4815-4e6b), via an independent write-safety audit of the materialized ticket-store entry. Not a root cause of 8386; a separate defect found while proving that one.

## Problem

`<store>/tickets-<sha>/` is documented and treated as an **immutable, content-addressed** entry (ADR 0005 D2). It is not. Every `show_ticket` read through the pinned root writes a derived reducer cache **inside the entry**:

`reducer/_api.py:221` -> `write_cache(cache_path, ...)` with `cache_path = os.path.join(ticket_dir, ".cache.json")` (`reducer/_cache.py:196`, published at `:146` via `atomic_write`). A second site, `reducer/_processors.py:58`, writes the same file on the corrupt-CREATE replay path.

**Measured on this host:** one live entry (`tickets-00b00a6ee3e2b6c0ebb667c044eb303ccf2ba3e3`) holds **4,844 `.cache.json` files**, every one with an mtime newer than the entry directory itself — i.e. created by reads after materialization, not by `checkout-index`. They are gitignored on the tickets branch, so they are absent from the committed tree and are purely post-build artifacts.

## Why it matters

1. **The immutability premise is false**, and other code is entitled to rely on it. Bug 8386's
   fix now hardlinks unchanged blobs between adjacent entries; it is safe only because
   `atomic_write` publishes by `os.replace` (`_store/fsutil.py:96`) rather than writing in
   place. That is an incidental property of one line, not an enforced invariant. If that line
   ever becomes a plain `open(path, "w")`, every entry sharing the inode is silently corrupted.
2. **It already breaks the reverify pass.** `janitor.reverify_entry` (`janitor.py:249-277`)
   records a TOFU digest over the entry's contents at first sight. Reads keep adding
   `.cache.json` files afterwards, so a baseline taken before the first read makes the entry
   look **corrupt** on the next pass and evicts it. Opt-in today (`reverify_seconds > 0`), which
   is the only reason this has not bitten.
3. It inflates the store, which is the parent bug's whole subject: ~4.8k extra files per entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Reading a ticket through a pinned snapshot root does not write into the snapshot entry
      (e.g. the reducer cache is disabled, or redirected outside the entry, when the tracker
      root is a snapshot).
- [x] A test observes the write RED (a materialized entry's file set changes after a read) and
      GREEN after the fix.
- [x] The rename-over contract in `_store/fsutil.py` is pinned by a test, or the entry is made
      genuinely read-only, so a future in-place write cannot silently corrupt shared inodes.
- [x] ADR 0005's immutability claim is either enforced or amended to describe reality.
baseline.summary: Snapshot entries are not immutable: every ticket read writes .cache.json inside them

## Problem

On 2026-08-31 (~17:30-18:00 PDT), three consecutive MCP log_session writes failed with: `flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: host=boot-bf4c34b1-475c-4363-8ff6-aada80c3c3ab pid=49003 start=19655570 held=155-174s pid_state=live op=compact-sweep)`.

Executed incident evidence:
- `ps -p 49003` on the operator host found no process.
- `lsof /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` found no holder.
- `held=` values were non-monotonic with constant `start`, consistent with a stale stamp.
- Immediate local CLI `rebar session-log append` on the shared checkout succeeded, so this is specific to the MCP write path / MCP tracker clone.

## Confirmed root cause

MCP `log_session` uses the shared write-lock path: MCP tool -> `rebar.append_session_log` -> `session_log.append` -> `append_event` -> `lock.write_lock`. `lock.acquire` first obtains the kernel `.ticket-write.lock` fcntl leg, then polls the mkdir stamp dir `.ticket-write.lock.d`; on timeout it renders `.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` through `describe_lock_holder`.

The stale mkdir owner stamp is treated as authoritative for the whole write timeout even after the waiter has acquired the kernel fcntl leg. For same-host/same-namespace v2 stamps, `_stamp_is_stale` probes the pid. If `_pid_alive(pid)` is true but `_process_start_time(pid)` is unavailable, it waits for the 1h stale ceiling. That fixed the unbounded wedge in `larval-tribal-tigermoth`, but the 1h ceiling exceeds MCP/write request budgets, so every MCP write can still burn its full timeout while the kernel lock is free.

Diagnostics have a matching gap: `_describe_stamped_pid` reports bare `_pid_alive(pid)` as `pid_state=live` without start-time corroboration, so a recycled/unqualified pid number is presented as a live holder even though it does not prove the stamped compact-sweep owner exists.

## Runtime proof

In `/Users/joeoakhart/storelock-fix`, an isolated scratch repo forged `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d/owner` as a same-host `op=compact-sweep` v2 stamp. The experiment first acquired `.ticket-write.lock` with nonblocking `fcntl`, proving the kernel lock was free, then drove real in-process FastMCP `log_session`. Instrumentation showed `_acquire_fcntl` succeeded, `_pid_alive(49003)` returned true, `_process_start_time(49003)` returned `None`, and the tool timed out with `pid_state=live`. A real MCP `rebar-log_session` call in this session timed out, while local CLI append immediately created `oxymoronic-ammonic-bats`; the shared checkout had no `.ticket-write.lock.d`, so the deployed MCP server is using a different tracker path/clone than the local CLI.

## Defect attribution

`caused_by`: `larval-tribal-tigermoth` (`ab00-1407-2da3-42fd`) by plan-defect/omission. That fix explicitly considered immediate reclaim when the fcntl leg is held and deliberately left it out; this incident proves the deferred case is necessary for MCP/write budgets. Close with `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=larval-tribal-tigermoth`.

## Fix plan

Edit `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` for the shared decision/diagnostic contract. Update all exact/string consumers of `_describe_stamped_pid` as needed: `src/rebar/_store/staging.py` (behavioral abandonment decision), `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` (drain-lock holder phrase), and `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` (operator-facing pid_state/detail). Add regression tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] MCP `log_session` with a forged same-host compact-sweep mkdir owner stamp returns without `LockTimeout` under a 1s lock budget; verified by `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py -q`.
- [x] The MCP regression test proves the free kernel fcntl leg was acquired before stale mkdir reclaim; verified by `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py -q`.
- [x] A same-host v2 stamp whose pid probe is unqualified is stale immediately when `fcntl_held=True`; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [x] The same unqualified stamp remains refused while fresh when `fcntl_held=False`; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [x] Holder diagnostics do not render an unqualified pid-number match as `pid_state=live`; verified by `tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py`.
- [x] Holder diagnostics render a corroborated matching start time as `pid_state=live`; verified by `tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py`.
- [x] Holder diagnostics render a differing known start time as a recycled/not-owner pid; verified by `tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py`.
- [x] Existing lock tests still pass for corroborated-live owners; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [x] Existing lock tests still pass for foreign-host stamps; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [x] Existing lock tests still pass for malformed stamps; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [x] Existing lock tests still pass for aged unprovable stamps; verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py -q`.
- [x] Step-7 parity census is posted as a ticket comment enumerating CLI, MCP/API, library facade, automated callers, dual-direction diagnostics, reconciler ref lock, and heartbeat/stamped-file locks; verified by ticket comment before close.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py -q`
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py tests/interfaces/store/test_atomic_ticket_dir_create_021d.py -q`
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
- Ticket comment containing the Step-7 parity census before close.
baseline.summary: MCP server write path wedged: dead compact-sweep holder (pid 49003) reported pid_state=live, all writes time out at 181s

## Problem

Pinning uv (bug 56b7-b21a-c8ab-4afc) removed the VERSION-RESOLUTION manifest fetch, but CI still makes one network call to `raw.githubusercontent.com` per job, so the `##[error]fetch failed` failure mode that killed run 33214025855 is still reachable.

Verified on run 33230196661 (change 2367 patchset 1), five jobs sampled, all identical:

    Found version for uv in /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/pyproject.toml: 0.12.7
    Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson ...
    Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7

The version came from the local pin — no `Could not determine uv version` line — and the manifest was fetched anyway.

## Root cause

`setup-uv` has a SECOND, independent manifest consumer. `setupUv` (`src/setup-uv.ts`) calls `tryGetFromToolCache`; on a miss it calls `downloadVersion`, whose first statement is:

    const artifact = await getArtifact(version, arch, platform, manifestUrl);   // src/download/download-version.ts:42

The manifest supplies the download URL and sha256, so it is fetched unconditionally regardless of how the version was resolved. A GitHub-hosted runner starts each job with an empty uv tool cache, so the miss is guaranteed. This is unchanged in v10.0.1, the newest release. A committed local manifest does not help: `fetchManifestResponse` uses Node `fetch()`, which rejects `file:` URLs, and `manifest-file` is documented as a URL.

## Candidate approaches (choose ONE during planning; none is pre-selected here)

- Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with `actions/cache` keyed on the pinned version, so `tryGetFromToolCache` hits and `downloadVersion` never runs. Trades a raw.githubusercontent.com dependency for a GitHub-cache-service dependency, which is a different and better-instrumented failure domain — but it is still a network dependency, so state that honestly rather than claiming zero.
- Install uv without the action (direct download from `releases.astral.sh` at the pinned version with a committed sha256, mirroring the `acli` precedent in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`). Removes the manifest entirely; costs the action's caching and PATH wiring, which would have to be reimplemented at 25 call sites or in one composite action.
- Upstream a change to `astral-sh/setup-uv` that skips `getArtifact` when the version is exact and the checksum is already in `KNOWN_CHECKSUMS`, then bump the pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A real CI log for the change contains the liveness anchor `Successfully installed uv version <pinned>` AND zero occurrences of `Fetching manifest data`; both greps recorded verbatim on this ticket. The anchor is asserted FIRST — a zero-match grep alone is also produced by an empty log or a skipped step, which is how an empty `gh run view --job=N --log` scored a clean vacuous pass during 56b7's verification.
- [x] The installed uv version in that same log still equals the pin in `pyproject.toml`, so the fix does not silently change which uv runs.
- [x] Whatever residual network dependency the chosen approach retains is named explicitly in the change description; the change does not claim 'no network dependency' unless the log shows zero external fetches in the install path.
baseline.summary: setup-uv fetches the version manifest for the artifact URL on every job even when uv is pinned

## Context / Problem

Pass 3 (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py`: `validity()`, `impact_plan()`, `pass3_decide`, `pass3_over_findings`) is deterministic; every input is in the v2 sidecar (`sidecar.py:702-703` persists per-finding `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` losslessly). `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` proves the replay works but is a one-off script with hardcoded baselines.

`orchestrator.pass3_over_findings(findings, verifs, *, execution_review=False)` (`orchestrator.py:662-711`) is the REAL LIVE path: `_threshold_for` special-cases `"prerequisite-consistency" -> (0.60, True)`, else resolves live via `_criteria.threshold_for(criteria, crit_by_id, gate="plan_review")`, bumps `block_threshold = max(bt, 0.80)` when `execution_review and blocking_enabled`; applies `_restrict_on_target_veto_to_grounded` under `if execution_review:` (line 698) before delegating.

**`execution_review` recovery — exact call.** `sidecar.parse_review_phase_metadata(payload)` returns `{"phase": "planning"|"execution", "priority_floor": ...}` (raises `SidecarReviewPhaseError` on a malformed payload, guarded to a `"planning"` default). Threaded into BOTH `pass3_decide` (for `replayed-stored`) and `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings` (for `live-baseline`).

**Registry drift is distinct from `impact_model_version`.** Thresholds live in `criteria_routing.json`, governed by `regver`. Tier-0 computes THREE things per finding: **stored**, **replayed-stored** (persisted threshold/posture, must equal `stored`), **live-baseline** (`orchestrator.pass3_over_findings`, may differ on registry drift).

**Candidate** diffed against **live-baseline**, via `candidates/__init__.py`'s `CANDIDATES` registry (`overlay` + `impact_fn`), mirroring `_threshold_for` + the on-target-veto restriction against the overlay-merged registry.

**Era-correct impact model (landed as a follow-up fix after real-corpus validation).** `replayed_stored_decision`'s self-check must use the impact model IN EFFECT when a row was judged, not always the current one: `impact_fn_for_row(data)` selects `legacy_v4_baseline.legacy_impact_plan` for any row whose `impact_model_version` isn't the current `sidecar.IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` ("plan-v5") — the shipped `decide.impact_plan` scores pre-v5 ordinal grades as 0.0, silently collapsing old findings' impact otherwise.

**Post-verdict floors not replayable from the sidecar alone are reported separately, not counted as mismatches** (also a real-corpus finding): a finding whose stored `reason == "prerequisite-coverage-indeterminate"` was reclassified by a review-level prerequisite-coverage override whose input isn't persisted per-finding.

**Per-finding, not just per-row, threshold gating** (also a real-corpus finding): `replay_row` excludes an individual finding lacking a numeric persisted `block_threshold` (e.g. a DET-tier finding Pass-3 never scored) from every lens, rather than falling back to a fabricated default threshold for it.

Ticket-level labels (`labels.py`, closed) need `show_ticket` per ticket — too slow at full-corpus scale. Label-proxy metrics: SEPARATE, OPTIONAL, only over a supplied `labels-<hash>.jsonl`.

**Friction rate**: `count(findings where live-baseline is non-blocking AND candidate is blocking) / count(all findings scored)`.

## Approach

`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/`: `legacy_v4_baseline.py` (relocated plan-v4 `classify`/`RULES`/`legacy_impact_plan` from `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py`, which now imports them), `candidates/__init__.py` (`Candidate` overlay registry), `tier0.py` (the replay harness: `execution_review_for`, `impact_fn_for_row`, `mirrored_threshold_for`, `replayed_stored_decision`, `live_baseline_decisions`, `candidate_decisions`, `sidecar_data_for_row`/`build_event_index` (full-body re-read matched by `(store, ticket_id, review_event_uuid)` — store-scoped to avoid a cross-store UUID collision), `replay_row`, `flip_matrix`, `label_proxy_metrics`, `run_tier0`), `report.py` (Markdown), `__main__.py` (`python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay tier0 --candidate <name> [--labels <path>]`).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier0.py`, `legacy_v4_baseline.py`, `candidates/__init__.py`, `report.py`, `__main__.py` (new)
- `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` (edited — imports relocated names)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/tier0-*.md` (generated, committed)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_tier0.py` (new, 34 tests)

## Testing

34 unit tests: identity/mirroring invariants (candidate `"current"` == live-baseline, overlay flips boundary findings, `prerequisite-consistency` special case, `execution_review` bump, on-target-veto grounded-cohort restriction), the self-check invariant (`replayed-stored` == `stored`, including execution-phase drops and the 0.80 bump), the era-correct impact-model selection (with a regression test proving the WRONG-era formula collapses the same finding), the per-finding threshold-gating fix (a regression test with a mixed DET+Pass-3 finding row), the prerequisite-coverage exclusion, flip-matrix arithmetic (friction rate, relief count, registry drift) on known-ratio fixtures, label-proxy metrics on a known confusion matrix, `run_tier0` integration against a real git tracker (incl. a real `labels_path` round-trip via `labels.build_labels`). Mutation-tested `execution_review`'s threshold bump, the friction-rate/relief-count split, `impact_fn_for_row`'s era branch, and the per-finding threshold filter — each negated condition drove a held-out test RED, then was restored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay tier0 --candidate current` over the real corpus (3758 reviews, 35082 scored findings) reports zero `replayed-stored` vs `stored` mismatches for plan-v4 and plan-v5 rows (34653 of 35082 findings, 98.8%); a residual of 429 mismatches (1.2%) is confined entirely to plan-v2/plan-v3, the corpus's two oldest schema generations, which predate this harness's documented plan-v4 baseline scope and are deferred follow-up work (mirroring `labels.py`'s precedent of honestly scoping real-data evidence); checked by the committed report `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/tier0-current-04e25807671d.md`.
- [x] Replaying the plan-v4->plan-v5 change (via the relocated `legacy_v4_baseline` module) reproduces its documented direction and approximate magnitude; checked against `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` running unchanged post-extraction (verified manually: `old=4485 new=4833 lost=47 gained=395`, matching pre-extraction output).
- [x] The report separately states registry-drift flips (659) and candidate-induced flips (0, since `--candidate current` carries no overlay), plus friction rate and per-criterion deltas; checked by inspection of the committed report.
- [x] IF a labels file is supplied, the report additionally contains `blocking_agreement_rate`, `proxy_precision`, `proxy_recall`, and `coverage_fraction`; checked by `test_run_tier0_labels_path_populates_label_proxy_metrics` (integration test with a real labels file).
- [x] The Pass-3 replay itself completes in under 5 minutes on this laptop over the real corpus (measured: 4:50-4:58), with zero LLM calls and no provider credentials required; checked by timing the committed report's generation.
- [x] Unit tests pass in `make test` (34/34 passing).
baseline.summary: Tier-0 harness: replay Pass-3 calculation, thresholds and routing overlays over the whole corpus (zero LLM)

## Summary

Found by the Step 7 (Axis 1 construct) sibling sweep while fixing `satiated-activated-aardwolf` (5524-e353-2e2d-4dbe). Same broad drift class — a source that affects the running environment is absent from every autodeploy path manifest — but a **different surface and disposition**, so it is filed rather than folded into the detect-only 5524 fix.

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` is the MCP container ENTRYPOINT: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` does `COPY . /app` then `RUN install -m 0755 /app/infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh` and `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh"]`. It is baked into the image at build time.

`autodeploy.sh`'s `MCP_PATHS='src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml'` does **not** include `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh`, and it is in no other manifest. So a merged change to ONLY `mcp-entrypoint.sh` triggers no MCP rebuild — the running container keeps the stale entrypoint. Unlike the host-nginx materializers (5524, detect-only because applying means `nginx -s reload`), applying THIS is an ordinary MCP image rebuild, which is already inside the mcp target's v1 auto-apply scope.

## Evidence

- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:91,147,150` — `COPY . /app`; installs `mcp-entrypoint.sh` to `/usr/local/bin`; sets it as `ENTRYPOINT`.
- `grep -oE "^[A-Z_]+_PATHS='[^']*'" infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh | grep mcp-entrypoint` → no match (absent from every manifest).

## Suggested disposition (apply-parity, NOT detect-only)

Add `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` to `MCP_PATHS` so an entrypoint-source change rebuilds the MCP image via the existing blue-green mcp deploy path (this is apply, not signal — distinct from the ADR 0079 v1→v2 host-nginx reload boundary that kept 5524 detect-only). Add regression coverage mirroring `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_signals_nginx_materializer.py` / the mcp-delta tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` is enumerated in `MCP_PATHS` (or otherwise triggers an MCP rebuild) so an entrypoint-source change is applied, not silently dropped.
- [x] Regression test drives `autodeploy.sh` under a git shim where only `mcp-entrypoint.sh` changed and asserts the MCP deploy path fires.
baseline.summary: Autodeploy never rebuilds the MCP image on an mcp-entrypoint.sh source change — baked into the image but absent from MCP_PATHS (silent-drift sibling of 5524)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

CLI users need to see the cross-session warning inline. rebar already has a stderr `WARN:`/`WARNING:` convention that leaves stdout and exit codes untouched (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:99` `warn_secret_screen_refused`; the fsck `WARN:` lines in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py`). This story emits that warning for CLI commands that target **one specific ticket**, and — per the brainstorm scope — **never** for bulk reads (`list` / `search` / `ready` / `next-batch`).

Depends on the detector (`cross_session_warning_for`, sibling story) and on the reducer clearing (so a non-`in_progress` ticket has no holder and never warns).

## Approach

Define the single-ticket-targeted CLI command set as an **explicit, data-driven allowlist** (a frozenset in the CLI dispatch layer) rather than inferring it, so bulk-read commands are excluded by construction. The set covers single-ticket reads and mutations, using the exact command spellings registered in `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py`'s `_CORE_FACTORIES`: `show`, `comment`, `edit`, `transition`, `reopen`, `tag`, `untag`, `set-file-impact`, `deps`, `archive`, `check-ac`, `clarity-check`, `link`, `unlink`. (There is no separate `declare-no-file-impact` CLI command — the no-impact form is `set-file-impact <id> --none`, already covered by `set-file-impact`.) It excludes `list`, `search`, `ready`, `next-batch`, and `create` (no pre-existing target). For `link` / `unlink` (two endpoints) the warning is computed for the **primary** ticket argument (`id1`) only.

At the point where each allowlisted single-ticket CLI command has resolved its ticket id, call `cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=...)`; when it returns a string, `sys.stderr.write("WARN: " + msg + "\n")` **before** performing the operation, so the warning is visible even if the op itself is quiet. stdout content and the process exit code are unchanged. `claim` is intentionally **not** in the set: claiming an `in_progress` ticket already fails with `ConcurrencyError`/exit 10 before any warning path (`docs/concurrency.md`).

The emit is **best-effort and must never break the command**: `cross_session_warning_for` performs a state read, so wrap it so that any exception it raises (corrupt/absent/locked state) is swallowed and the command proceeds unwarned — the warning is advisory, never a gate on the underlying operation. The gate that decides whether to emit is the **allowlist frozenset keyed by the resolved command name**, evaluated at the dispatch layer — not a single shared id-resolution helper. `require_id` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:157`) is only *one* of the id-resolution paths (some reads such as `show`/`deps` and the gate commands resolve their id on their own arm), so the implementation confirms each allowlisted command's resolved-id point during implementation and emits there; the frozenset membership check — not a `require_id` call — is what excludes bulk commands.

The warning is computed from the ticket state **at operation time** (before a mutation applies), so e.g. a `transition <id> in_progress closed` run by another session warns about holder A and *then* clears the provenance — the read precedes the write.

## Scope

- The CLI dispatch layer under `src/rebar/_cli/` — define the allowlist frozenset (keyed by
  the command spellings in `_registry.py`'s `_CORE_FACTORIES`) and add the stderr emit at
  each allowlisted command's resolved-id point (which may be `require_id`,
  `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:157`, or a command's own id-resolution arm). Confirm the
  exact per-command insertion point by reading the dispatch during implementation; the
  allowlist frozenset is the single source of "which commands warn".
- `docs/user-guide.md` — a short note that single-ticket CLI commands warn on stderr when
  another session holds the ticket, and that bulk commands do not.

## Testing

Tier: **real CLI subprocess + persisted-state assertion** (test-design §3 "CLI parsing, streams, env, exit codes" — the mechanism crosses argv parsing, env-var session resolution, and stderr). Use a real temporary tracker; set `REBAR_SESSION_ID` per invocation to model distinct sessions.

- Claim a ticket with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=A` (so `claimed_session=A`). Run `rebar show <id>`
  and `rebar comment <id> "x"` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=B`: assert **stderr** contains `WARN:`
  and the holder id `A`, stdout is the normal output, and exit code is `0`.
- Negative control (same session): the same commands with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=A` emit **no**
  `WARN:` line (exit 0).
- Bulk exclusion: `rebar list` (and `rebar ready`) with `REBAR_SESSION_ID=B` emit **no**
  `WARN:` line even though the store contains A's `in_progress` ticket.
- Unset-id silence: `rebar show <id>` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset emits no `WARN:` line.
- `link` primary-endpoint: `rebar link <id1> <id2> ...` as session B, with A holding `id1`,
  emits a single `WARN:` naming holder `A` computed for the **primary** `id1` (not `id2`).
- Defect-seeded: temporarily point the emit at the wrong ticket / drop the allowlist guard
  and show the bulk-exclusion and holder-id assertions go RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With ticket held by session A, `rebar show <id>` and `rebar comment <id> ...` run as
  session B print a `WARN:` line naming holder `A` to **stderr**, with unchanged stdout and
  exit code 0 (checked by a CLI subprocess test under `make test`).
- [x] Negative control: the same commands as session A print no `WARN:` line (checked by the
  same test asserting stderr has no `WARN:`).
- [x] `rebar list` and `rebar ready` as session B print no cross-session `WARN:` line even
  with A's `in_progress` ticket present (checked by a bulk-exclusion assertion).
- [x] `rebar show <id>` with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset prints no `WARN:` line (checked by an
  unset-id assertion).
- [x] `rebar link <id1> <id2>` as session B, with A holding `id1`, prints a single `WARN:`
  naming holder `A` computed for the **primary** `id1` only (checked by a link
  primary-endpoint assertion in the CLI subprocess test).
- [x] The stderr emit is best-effort: when `cross_session_warning_for` raises (corrupt /
  absent / locked state), the command still completes normally and unwarned — the warning
  never gates the underlying operation (checked by a test that forces the detector to raise
  and asserts the command's exit code and stdout are unchanged with no `WARN:` line).
- [x] `docs/user-guide.md` documents the CLI stderr warning and the bulk exclusion (checked:
  `grep -n "another session" docs/user-guide.md` matches).
baseline.summary: CLI: emit cross-session WARN on stderr for single-ticket commands

baseline.description:
## Why
Report §5.2 found 4/8 tickets with persisted reviews were CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED: the gate raised the right advisory, but the author applied it only AFTER claim — advisory latency, not blindness. Authors defer advisories because nothing ranks which surviving advisories are worth applying *now* vs safe to defer. A deterministic triage of the round's surviving advisories is pure coaching (the reviewer never writes the plan) and carries no detection risk, so per the epic gate table it ships first with **no eval gate** — validated post-ship by dogfooding via R7's advisory-application-latency metric.

## What
Add a **deterministic advisory-triage stage** to the Pass-4 coach path of the plan-review gate. It runs AFTER Pass-3 has decided findings and split them into blocking vs surviving (advisory), and it partitions the round's surviving **advisory** findings into two buckets — `apply-now` and `defer` — using ONLY fields already recorded on each decided finding. It emits NO new LLM judgment (no model call) and no free prose; it renders from a locked format, so the same decided-finding set produces byte-identical output.

**Output shape (structured, returned — not persisted).** The stage produces a structured `triage` array, one entry per surviving advisory finding: `{"id": str, "criteria": list[str], "priority": float, "block_threshold": float, "bucket": "apply-now"|"defer", "reason": str}` (`reason` is `""` for `apply-now`). This array is attached to the returned verdict as a **top-level key `verdict["triage"]`** — the `plan_review_verdict` output schema has `additionalProperties: true`, so it validates with no schema change — so the agent sees it at review time. It is **NOT** added to the persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar: `sidecar.build_payload` enumerates coaching-note fields explicitly, and R7's dogfood metrics derive advisory *application* from post-claim outcomes joined to findings by `criteria`, not from a stored triage stamp — so persistence is unnecessary and `build_payload` stays unchanged. No Markdown, no config flag.

**Mechanism choice (rationale).** It is NOT an entry in the Pass-4 `MOVE_REGISTRY` (in `passes.py`, re-exported by `orchestrator.py`). The registry schema (`review_kernel/coach.py` `MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA`) is a *per-finding* `{subject}`-placeholder template the LLM fills; a single `{subject}` substitution cannot express a ranked two-bucket split across all surviving advisories. So the triage is a small pure function on the plan-review Pass-4 path — blast radius stays inside plan-review; the shared kernel coach mechanism and its notes are unchanged.

**The ranking rule (fully specified, grounded in real fields).** Every decided finding carries `priority` (= `validity × impact`, float in [0,1], always present — `review_kernel/decide.py`, and set to 0.4 for DET-tier advisories in `orchestrator.py`). `block_threshold` is present on LLM-decided findings (resolved by `decide.py`; 0.60 via plan-review's `criteria_routing.json` routing, not `decide.py`'s 0.95 `DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`); DET-tier advisories stamped by `partition_findings` (`orchestrator.py`) do **not** carry it, so `triage_advisories` reads it as `f.get("block_threshold", DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD)` — the 0.95 default applies when absent (already imported in `passes.py`), under which a DET advisory (priority 0.4) buckets `defer`. No other field is used — there is NO "remediation-mode carryover status" field on Pass-4 findings.

- **Bucketing.** An advisory is `apply-now` iff `priority >= block_threshold - APPLY_NOW_MARGIN`
  (it came within the margin of blocking → highest value to apply now); else `defer`.
  `APPLY_NOW_MARGIN` is a named module constant, default **0.10**.
- **Ordering (total, deterministic → byte-identical).** The `triage` array is sorted by
  `priority` DESC, then by `criteria[0]` (the first element of the finding's `criteria` list;
  a finding with empty `criteria` sorts last via a fixed sentinel `"~"`) ASC, then by `id` ASC.
- **Defer reason.** Built only from the finding's own numbers, e.g.
  `deferred: priority 0.32 is 0.28 below its 0.60 block line` — fixed words + recorded numbers,
  no LLM prose, non-prescriptive.
- **Eligibility.** Only findings with `decision == "advisory"` are triaged. Blocking findings
  must be remediated regardless and are excluded (this is why R6 is advisory-only).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — the deterministic `triage_advisories(surviving)` pure
  function (bucketing + ordering + defer-reason via a locked format) and the `APPLY_NOW_MARGIN`
  constant.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` — in the `plan_review_coach` step (the sole live
  verdict-assembly path; the older bespoke `_run_passes` path was retired in epic
  solid-timer-unison), invoke `triage_advisories` on the surviving advisory findings and set
  `verdict["triage"]` before the closing `validate_structured(verdict, _OUTPUT_SCHEMA)` return.
  The two `gate_dispatch.py` recovery paths (`_recover_plan_review_coach_failure`,
  `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure`) assemble DEGRADED verdicts when a pass fails and have no
  decided advisories to triage, so they are out of scope — a recovered verdict simply omits
  `triage`. No other returned-result consumer changes.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py` — unit tests (see ACs).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — document the triage stage, ranking rule, and R7 dogfood
  expectation.
- NOT touched: `sidecar.py` / the `plan_review_result_v2` schema (triage is returned, not
  persisted) and `review_kernel/coach.py` (kernel mechanism unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `triage_advisories` returns byte-identical output across two runs on the same fixed
      advisory set, and every `reason` string matches the locked format (only fixed tokens +
      recorded numeric fields — no LLM/prescriptive prose). Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k determinism -q`.
- [ ] Boundary bucketing: an advisory with `priority == block_threshold - APPLY_NOW_MARGIN` is
      `apply-now`; one epsilon below is `defer` (parametrized). Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k boundary -q`.
- [ ] The `triage` array is ordered by `priority` DESC, then `criteria[0]` ASC (empty→`"~"`),
      then `id` ASC — a test with deliberate priority ties and a multi-element / empty
      `criteria` pins the exact order. Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k ordering -q`.
- [ ] Only `decision == "advisory"` findings appear in the array; blocking findings are
      excluded, and every surviving advisory appears exactly once (including advisories that
      mapped to no coach move). Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k advisory_only -q`.
- [ ] Integration: the returned plan-review verdict carries the `triage` array as top-level
      `verdict["triage"]`, equal to `triage_advisories(surviving)` for that run (a test drives the
      `plan_review_coach` step with fixture findings and asserts `verdict["triage"]`).
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k integration -q`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the triage stage, its ranking rule (the
      `APPLY_NOW_MARGIN` default, the ordering, and the defer-reason format), and the R7 dogfood
      expectation. Proving command:
      `grep -q "APPLY_NOW_MARGIN" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "apply-now" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "defer" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "R7" docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] Landed through Gerrit directly in the packaged Pass-4 coach path — no config flag;
      `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.
baseline.summary: R6: advisory-triage coaching move (pass-4 registry, ship-first)

## Context
The generated configuration reference enumerates key, type, default, and lifecycle data from typed dataclass fields but provides no public setting descriptions. It cannot serve as the external settings contract until each emitted key explains its user-visible effect. The parent ticket [rebar:66c6-2fe5-4850-4297] authorizes this Description-column enrichment as corrective follow-on scope beyond the closed generator baseline. Generated ownership remains unchanged.

## Plan
- Add concise `public_description` metadata to every dataclass field emitted through `_SECTION_CLASSES`, co-located with each field so generator introspection remains the single source of truth and a sidecar description registry cannot drift.
- Treat `public_description` as the authoritative external setting prose. Existing code comments remain internal implementation notes rather than a second generated contract.
- Preserve field types, defaults, factories, coercion, and runtime behavior.
- Extend `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` to require nonempty description metadata and render a Description column.
- Fail generation when an emitted field lacks a description.
- Regenerate `docs/config-reference.md`.
- Add focused tests for complete metadata, table escaping, generated drift, and an injected missing or empty description that fails with the offending key named.
- Review every generated Description cell against its key plus adjacent Type, Default, and Lifecycle cells. Require a user-visible effect or operational consequence rather than a restatement, then record the reviewer identity, UTC timestamp, and completed row-by-row result in a ticket comment.
- Keep `src/rebar` modules below the absolute 800-line limit. Use an existing configuration-section seam if an extraction is required.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py tests/unit/test_config_typed.py tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py -q`

## Summary

Re-running `rebar review-plan` on the **already-signed, unchanged** auto-lander epic `f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af` (and its story S1 `843b-801f-9ef9-442d`) produced a stream of **invalid blocking findings** and **non-convergent** behaviour: the plan had been signed CLEAN (`blocking: 0, advisory: 2`) at HEAD `2272d68`, and re-review at a later HEAD `6244666` — with **no change to the plan**, only `main` advancing — returned `BLOCK` (`blocking: 1, advisory: 13`). Remediating the findings then *increased* the finding count and *spawned new blocks*. The gate never converged; the epic could only be claimed via `--force`.

This bug documents each invalid/problematic finding with full context, its triggering criterion, its round-over-round progression, and — crucially — **which stage of the review pipeline (finding discovery / validation assessment / impact assessment) should have caught it and why.** It is the raw material for calibrating the plan-review gate so an already-signed plan is not re-blocked by non-deterministic false positives at a drifted HEAD.

## The review pipeline (stage vocabulary used below)

`review-plan` produces a verdict through three conceptual stages. Each invalid finding below is attributed to the stage that should have filtered it:

1. **Finding discovery** — generation of candidate findings from the plan + graph. A finding
   whose premise is *contradicted by text present in the plan* should never be emitted here.
2. **Validation assessment** — deciding whether a candidate is *real*. A candidate that is
   contradicted by (a) the plan itself, (b) a sibling finding in the same verdict, or (c) the
   ticket's own recorded comment trail should be dropped as not-real here.
3. **Impact assessment** — scoring severity and deriving block-vs-advisory. A finding whose
   remedy is deferred/operator-attested/implementation-stage should not score at the blocking
   tier here.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Take a plan that has a valid, signed `plan-review` attestation (`blocking: 0`).
2. Let `main` advance so the attestation reads *stale* (HEAD-relative staleness) without
   editing the ticket.
3. Run `rebar review-plan <id>` again. Observe a materially different verdict — new blocking
   findings that were not present in the signing review, including at least one whose fix is
   already in the plan text.
4. Remediate a flagged advisory (e.g. "name the missing edit target in Scope"). Re-run the
   review. Observe that the remediation *introduces new blocking findings* (it now demands an
   AC + proving command for the thing you just added to Scope).

**Expected:** re-reviewing an unchanged, previously-signed plan at a drifted HEAD yields a substantively stable verdict (still a PASS, or at most the same findings). Findings whose premise is present-and-contradicted in the plan are dropped in validation. Remediating an advisory does not manufacture new blocks.

**Actual:** the verdict flips PASS→BLOCK with no plan change; a blocking finding re-appears verbatim after its fix is demonstrably present; two findings in the same verdict contradict each other; and advisory remediation cascades into new blocks. The gate does not converge.

---

## A. Invalid BLOCKING findings

### A1 — Epic: "pre-cutover snapshot never captured / not stored" (FALSE POSITIVE)
- **Criteria:** `E2`, `F1`. **Impact:** 0.85 (blocking). **Rounds:** raised r1 → remediated
  (AC added naming actor, artifact, location, timing) → **re-raised VERBATIM r2**.
- **Finding text:** *"The security-invariants AC requires 'a GET /projects/rebar/access diff
  vs the pre-cutover snapshot,' but the plan never tasks anyone with capturing the pre-cutover
  snapshot before the label is deployed, nor where it is stored."*
- **Why invalid:** after r1 the plan literally contained: *"Pre-cutover access baseline
  (captured by S1 843b, BEFORE the label is pushed): save the current `GET
  /a/projects/rebar/access` response to `infra/gerrit/access-snapshot-pre-autolander.json`
  and commit it in the same change."* This names the **actor** (S1), the **artifact/location**
  (the JSON file), and the **timing** (before cutover, same change) — exactly the three things
  the finding claims are absent. The finding offered **no `checklist_item` fix** (it had
  nothing to suggest because the fix was already present).
- **Stage that should have caught it:** **Validation assessment.** A validation pass that
  re-reads the plan for the finding's own premise would find the contradicting text and drop
  the candidate. Secondarily **finding discovery** should not regenerate a finding whose
  subject string is present in the plan.
- **Damning corroboration:** the SAME r2 verdict contains advisory A-adv "the parent
  **explicitly assigns capture to S1**" (see B2 below). One verdict simultaneously asserts
  "no one is tasked with capture" (blocking) and "the parent explicitly assigns capture to S1"
  (advisory). A validation stage that cross-checked findings against each other would have
  killed one of them.

### A2 — S1: "setup-project.sh has no AC / no proving command" and "line-148 commit message not updated" (REMEDIATION-INDUCED)
- **Criteria:** `E6`/`F1` and `G1G2`. **Impact:** 0.85 each (blocking). **Rounds:** absent r1 →
  **created by remediating epic advisory A-#6** ("add `setup-project.sh` to the plan's edit
  targets"). I added a Scope sentence naming `setup-project.sh`; r2 then blocked because that
  Scope deliverable had no matching AC/proving command.
- **Why problematic:** this is the **remediation cascade** — acting on a low-impact advisory
  manufactured two *blocking* findings. A gate that turns "you should also mention X" into "X
  is now a blocking deliverable with no AC" cannot converge: every remediation widens the
  surface faster than it closes it. (These two were legitimately fixable and I fixed them with
  one AC + `grep -F 'Autosubmit' infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`; the DEFECT is that the gate
  created them from an advisory in the first place.)
- **Stage that should have caught it:** **Impact assessment.** A newly-named, secondary
  audit-trail touch (a commit-message string) is not a blocking-tier gap; it is advisory at
  most. Escalating it to `blocking` (0.85) is impact inflation.

---

## B. Invalid / non-material ADVISORY findings

### B1 — Epic A8: "sibling tickets touch the same file with no ordering edge"
- **Criteria:** `P5`. **Impact:** 0.4. **Fix offered:** none.
- **Why invalid:** `infra/autolander/loop.py` is co-edited by S2a/S2b/S2c **by deliberate
  decomposition** (S2 was split into three tasks precisely to keep each unit loadable — the
  module-size ethos), and real ordering edges DO exist (`38be depends_on 89f9` and `08e1`).
  The premise ("no ordering edge") is false, and the pattern it flags is the intended design.
- **Stage:** **Validation assessment** — a dependency-graph read disproves "no ordering edge."

### B2 — Epic A9 / S1 A7: "Acceptance-criteria / definition-of-done quality issues"
- **Criteria:** `P6`. **Impact:** 0.4. **Fix offered:** none. **Rounds:** present both rounds.
- **Why invalid:** contentless. No specific AC is named, no defect is described, no remediation
  is suggested. It is un-actionable by construction — the agent cannot act on "quality issues."
- **Stage:** **Finding discovery** should not emit a finding with an empty body and no
  `checklist_item`; a finding with no actionable content is noise, not signal.

### B3 — Epic A12: "`POST /changes/{id}/rebase:chain` endpoint unverified"
- **Criteria:** `T3`. **Impact:** 0.0. **Fix offered:** add a live API probe.
- **Why invalid:** this exact claim was **already litigated and rejected in the ticket's own
  comment trail** — the epic records: *"Verified against the Gerrit REST API docs: `POST
  /changes/{change-id}/rebase:chain` DOES exist (3.6+, so the 3.14.1 instance has it) — the
  review's own advisory T3 concedes this."* The gate re-surfaced a settled, fact-checked
  point that a prior review round had already conceded.
- **Stage:** **Validation assessment** — the ticket comment trail is in scope for the review
  and directly refutes the finding. Re-raising conceded fact is a validation miss.

### B4 — Epic A11 & A13: "`rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader` trailer-preservation unverified"
- **Criteria:** `T1`, `T3`. **Impact:** 0.0 (both). **Fix offered:** add a probe/smoke test.
- **Why non-material:** these ask for *implementation-stage verification* of a documented
  Gerrit flag. The plan already routes that verification into child ACs — S2a carries an
  "uploader/trailer-preservation test" and S5b carries a "synthetic scratch-ref smoke change."
  The plan does not need to re-prove a library capability at plan-review time.
- **Stage:** **Impact assessment** correctly scored these 0.0 (non-blocking), but they were
  still surfaced as duplicated findings (A11 and A13 are the same claim). **Finding discovery**
  should de-duplicate; a 0.0-impact, already-covered concern is noise.

### B5 — Epic A14: "S5 should formally `depends_on` S3, not merely 'Uses S3'"
- **Criteria:** `G4`. **Impact:** 0.0.
- **Why non-material:** S5 already documents "Uses S3's outcome marker," S5 is gated behind S2,
  and S3 completes in the same topological tier. The distinction between a `Uses` note and a
  formal `depends_on` here is cosmetic and impact-0.0 by the reviewer's own scoring.
- **Stage:** **Impact assessment** (correctly 0.0) — but flagging it at all, given it is
  cosmetic, is discovery noise.

### B6 — S1 A4/A5/A6/A8/A9/A11: "pin curl/auth/jq/rollback into the plan ACs"
- **Criteria:** `T3`, `E6`, `T5b`, `T5c`. **Impact:** 0.85 down to 0.0.
- **Why non-material:** these demand that the plan AC embed the exact `curl` command, auth
  mechanism, `jq` assertion, HTTP-200 check, and rollback procedure for the **operator cutover**
  (`GET /a/projects/rebar/labels/...`, `GET /a/projects/rebar/access`). That cutover is an
  **operator-attested** step (ADR-0043) whose evidence is a recorded attestation, not an
  in-session command. Mechanical proving-commands belong in the cutover script/runbook, not the
  plan AC.
- **Stage:** **Impact assessment.** The gate does not distinguish codebase-verifiable ACs from
  operator-attested ones (ADR-0043); it applies the "every AC needs an in-session proving
  command" rule uniformly, inflating operator-runbook granularity to 0.85 blocking-adjacent.

### B7 — S1 A12: "no RETIRE path for the Autosubmit label"
- **Criteria:** `T9`. **Impact:** 0.0.
- **Why invalid:** demanding a feature-retirement procedure for a label being *introduced* is
  YAGNI/scope creep. The label ships with a documented back-out note already; a full retire
  runbook is out of scope for the introduction story.
- **Stage:** **Validation assessment** (scope check) should recognise retire-path demands on an
  introduction ticket as out-of-scope, not a plan gap.

---

## C. Cross-cutting review-gate defects (the root causes)

1. **Non-determinism across HEAD drift (the core bug).** The epic was signed CLEAN
   (`blocking: 0`) at `2272d68`; the identical plan re-reviewed at `6244666` returned
   `blocking: 1, advisory: 13`. No plan change occurred — only `main` advanced. Re-review of an
   unchanged plan must be substantively stable; it is not. This is what forces the entire
   re-claim treadmill.
2. **Verbatim re-block after a demonstrated fix (A1).** Validation does not re-read the plan for
   a finding's own premise before re-emitting it.
3. **Intra-verdict self-contradiction (A1 blocking vs its advisory twin).** Findings within one
   verdict are not cross-checked for consistency.
4. **Remediation-induced finding cascade (A2).** Acting on a low-impact advisory manufactures
   new blocking findings, so the finding count rises with each remediation round and the gate
   never converges.
5. **Uniform proving-command demand ignores ADR-0043 (B6).** Operator-attested ACs are scored
   as if they need in-session mechanical commands.
6. **Contentless and duplicated findings (B2, B4).** Findings with empty bodies / no
   `checklist_item`, and duplicate findings, pass discovery.
7. **Hard-override mis-classification is the blocking amplifier (root cause of the 0.85s).**
   Per the impact model shipped in closed story `0858-facb-6901-4781` (under closed epic
   `4cc3-23c9-b062-41ac`), a finding tagged with any of {AC-unverifiable, DoD-uncertifiable,
   undecomposed, divergent-implementation} gets `impact_sev` **force-set to ≥ 0.85** (a hard
   override, bypassing the severity MAX). Nearly every invalid finding above lands at exactly
   **0.85** — i.e. the validation stage mis-tagged a false-positive/non-material finding into
   a hard-override axis (chiefly "AC-unverifiable"), which then mechanically escalated it to
   the blocking tier. The override is doing its job; the DEFECT is upstream — validation
   assigns the hard-override axis to findings that are not actually AC-unverifiable (the AC is
   present, or the "unverifiable" step is operator-attested per ADR-0043). **Fixing validation
   mis-tagging is higher-leverage than re-tuning the threshold**, because the override
   deliberately ignores the threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Finding discovery drops (or does not emit) any candidate finding whose subject text is
      **present and contradicted** in the plan body; a regression fixture reproduces epic A1
      (snapshot AC present) and asserts no such block is emitted.
- [ ] Validation assessment cross-checks findings **within a single verdict** for mutual
      contradiction and drops the weaker/contradicted one; a fixture reproduces the A1
      blocking-vs-advisory contradiction and asserts at most one survives.
- [ ] Validation assessment consults the ticket's **recorded comment trail** and drops a
      finding that re-litigates a point the trail already resolved; a fixture reproduces B3
      (`rebase:chain` conceded in-trail) and asserts it is dropped.
- [ ] Impact assessment distinguishes **operator-attested** criteria (ADR-0043) from
      codebase-verifiable ones and does NOT demand an in-session proving command for the former;
      a fixture reproduces B6 and asserts those findings are not scored at the blocking tier.
- [ ] Finding discovery **de-duplicates** findings and suppresses contentless findings (empty
      body / no `checklist_item`); a fixture reproduces B2/B4.
- [ ] **Re-review stability (the headline criterion):** re-running `review-plan` on an
      unchanged, previously-signed plan at a drifted HEAD yields a verdict with **no NEW
      blocking findings** relative to the signing review; a fixture (sign at HEAD-A, advance to
      HEAD-B with no ticket edit, re-review) asserts the block set does not grow.
- [ ] A short design note (or ADR) records the "remediation cascade" anti-pattern (acting on an
      advisory must not manufacture a block) and the re-review-stability contract.

## Notes / provenance

Surfaced while executing the auto-lander epic `f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af` under `/rebar-implement`: every one of its 13 live tickets was signed at `2272d68` and went stale when `main` advanced, so each claim required a fresh review, exposing the non-convergence. Full per-finding triage and the force-claim justifications are recorded on session log `547b-4aca-0076-4a36`.

**Related prior work (both CLOSED):** epic `4cc3-23c9-b062-41ac` "Review-gate impact redesign
+ threshold re-tune (plan-review + code-review)" and its story `0858-facb-6901-4781`
"Plan-review impact redesign: severity-first MAX + hard override + detection amplifier" — this bug is a follow-on defect against that same subsystem (see cross-cutting defect #7: the hard-override from `0858` is what force-escalates the mis-validated findings to 0.85). Linked `relates_to 4cc3` and `discovered_from f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af`.
baseline.summary: Plan-review gate: non-convergent re-review of an already-signed plan at drifted HEAD emits invalid blocking findings (auto-lander epic f1fa)
