## Scope (revised 2026-08-13; operator-approved exception to the LOC-remediation freeze)

Re-measured on `origin/main` @ `2af5a4c773`: 435 `src/rebar` `*.py` files, **46 over 700 LOC**, 7 at 796-800. The two this story named at 799 (`_ref_lock.py`, `init.py`) are now 730/758; `_config_schema.py` 677 and `fsck.py` 301 also landed. Worst now: `pass1.py` **800**, `_lib_writes.py` **800** (in flight as Gerrit 1737 — OUT OF SCOPE), `completion_banking.py` 799, `_store/push.py` **799**, `signing.py` 798, `binding_store.py` 798, `apply_inbound_records.py` 797, `runner.py` 796.

This story does **not** drain all 46: per epic `broke-boarish-hagfish` the object is the RECURRENCE pattern, not the population. Three changes, one per file-cluster, as a small stack: the two files at/one-line-from the cap not already in flight, plus the leading indicator this story's last AC asks for. `signing.py` was mapped too and deferred to a `discovered_from` record (see comments): its `_baked_commit_sha` patch-target/consumer pair forces a test edit.

---

## Change 1 — `llm/plan_review/pass1.py` 800 -> ~510

Four fused concerns: (a) the **container (G3/G4) pairing stage**, (b) the driver `run_pass1`, (c) ISF/context blob builders (~95 LOC), (d) usage aggregation + material fingerprint (~110). Only (a) is large enough to extract without breaching the 100-LOC floor; (c) and (d) stay with their nearest collaborator.

**Extract to `llm/plan_review/container_stage.py` (~300 LOC):** `CONTAINER_CRITERIA`, `_CONTAINER_MAX_WORKERS`, `_too_big_finding`, `build_sibling_roster`, `_timed_pairing`, `_run_container`. Seam: `_run_container` has exactly ONE call site (`run_pass1`'s `if container and ctx.has_children:` branch); `_timed_pairing`, `_too_big_finding` and `_CONTAINER_MAX_WORKERS` are called from nowhere but `_run_container`. That call site is the seam a previous author already cut and stopped at — the shape `defaceable-icy-antelope` found in `fsck.py`.

**`_submit_ctx` moves to `generation.py`**, not to the new module: it is shared by BOTH `_run_container` and `run_pass1`, so leaving it in `pass1.py` would force `container_stage -> pass1` and cycle. `generation.py` is the right home because the worker `_submit_ctx` launches calls `generation.review_cancelled()`, and the `_CANCEL_SCOPE` ContextVar that reads is defined in `generation.py:120` — that is the generation-owned state `copy_context()` must capture. (The gate-session vars `_submit_ctx` also carries, `_in_gate_session` / `_active_code_root`, live in `llm/gate_context.py`, not here; they are captured generically.) `generation.py`'s docstring already names `pass1._submit_ctx`. Direction stays one-way: `pass1 -> container_stage -> generation`. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` is re-derived in `container_stage.py` from `capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` — the same single source `pass1.py` reads, not a second literal.

Compatibility (semantic search AND string grep, both run): `orchestrator.py` imports `CONTAINER_CRITERIA`, `_run_container`, `_ticket_graph_blob`, `material_fingerprint` from `.pass1`; `provider_parity.py` imports `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` — both preserved by re-export. The ONLY symbol patched on the `pass1` module is `_shed_to_budget` (`test_plan_review.py:2049`), whose consumer `run_pass1` STAYS, so the flamingo trap does not arise; `_submit_ctx`, `_run_container` and `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` are patched nowhere. Two source-text tests are satisfied by the re-export lines themselves: `test_container_roster.py::test_roster_builder_single_sourced` and `test_cache_floor_warning.py`. The only complexity-baseline key for this file is `pass1.py::run_pass1` (20), which does NOT move: no new key, no re-key.

## Change 2 — `_store/push.py` 799 -> ~500

Concerns: (A) `_git`/`_GIT_TIMEOUT` 15 LOC, (B) **stash / dirty-tree recovery** 126, (C) **non-fast-forward recovery** 166, (D) `_push_mode` 15, (E) S3 preflight 30, (F) commit path 114, (G) entry/driver/CLI 330. B and C form ONE subtree whose only edge into the rest is `push_tickets_branch`'s single call to `_recover_non_fast_forward`; every other member (`_stash_create`, `_restore_stash`, `_resolve_conflicted_apply`, `_recover_dirty_merge`, `_merge_with_transport_retry`, `_merge_remote_under_lock`, `_fetch_for_recovery`) has one caller, inside the subtree. **Extract B+C + `_PUSH_MERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to `_store/push_recovery.py` (~345 LOC).** A/D/E are far under the 100-LOC floor, staying with `push_tickets_branch`; F is deliberately NOT cut — 114 LOC barely clears the floor and would need a second late-binding seam for no headroom gain.

The hazard: `push._git` is monkeypatched at ~25 sites across 10 test modules and 8 of the 9 moved functions call it. A module-level `from .push import _git` in the extracted file would both cycle and bind pre-patch, silently running REAL git while tests assert on a fake. Remedy is the project's own established pattern, `_ref_lock_push.py`: each moved entry point takes the calling module as its first `core` parameter and resolves `core._git` and `core.logger` at call time. `_git`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and `logger` all stay in `push.py`, so `push_state.py`'s `from rebar._store.push import _git`, the `rebar._store.push` logger-name assertions in 6 test modules (including the store-epoch warning emitted from the MOVED `_merge_remote_under_lock`), and `_bridge_runner.py`'s `python -m rebar._store.push` keep working unchanged. `push_recovery.py` imports nothing from `push.py` — one-way.

`test_push_shared_stash_2fa6.py` calls `_push._recover_dirty_merge(...)` directly with `push._git` patched; it gets a two-line delegating shim in `push.py`, not a test edit. `compat` / `lock` stay imported AS MODULES on both sides so their patch sites survive. `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has zero keys for `push.py`.

## Change 3 — surface the leading indicator that already exists

Do NOT build a second indicator (per the 2026-08-05 comment): `near_cap_count` is computed and reports 37, but only someone running `rebar metrics` ever sees it. The CI **Module-size gate** already computes per-file LOC for every file it measures. Append to that same step a NON-BLOCKING pass emitting one `::warning::` per `src/rebar` file within a headroom band of the locked cap, exiting 0 regardless. Reuses the gate's own `find | wc -l` — no second definition of the rule, no new file, no new failure mode, band derived from the locked limit. One edit: the gate lives only in the reusable `_build-and-test.yml`, which both `gerrit-verify.yaml` and `test.yml` call. Policy note in `docs/architecture.md`.

## Verification, per change, before push

Full CI-parity suite (`-m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300`) plus `tests/integration`, with **test-count parity** against the parent commit per split; every `check_*.py` gate; every `gen_*.py` generator re-run with no diff; `make lint`; `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pass1.py` <= 550 LOC; `container_stage.py` in [100, 500]; `generation.py` <= 500.
- [x] `push.py` <= 550 LOC; `push_recovery.py` in [100, 500]. No file created by this story is
      under 100 LOC or over 550.
- [x] `pass1.<symbol>` / `push.<symbol>` attribute access preserved for every symbol named
      above; `orchestrator.py`, `provider_parity.py`, `push_state.py`, `_bridge_runner.py` and
      `_init_probe.py` byte-unchanged.
- [x] Zero test files edited by Changes 1 and 2; test-count parity demonstrated per change.
- [x] `check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` OK on each change; the baseline file unmodified.
- [x] The CI module-size gate emits a non-blocking near-cap warning listing every file in the
      headroom band, and still passes when that list is non-empty.
- [x] `docs/architecture.md` records both splits and the near-cap warning.
- [x] [operator-attested] Each change earns `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` and is submitted
      before this ticket closes; the Gerrit change numbers are recorded as ticket comments.
baseline.summary: Module-size headroom is exhausted repo-wide: 40 files over 700 LOC, three within two lines of the hard cap

## Summary
tests/external/test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py::test_link_sync_differ_apply_roundtrip_live fails on main with:
  AttributeError: 'StubBindingStore' object has no attribute 'get_baseline'
The reconciler per-binding-baseline path was finalized (baseline rollout flags retired, e.g. c4d58a306), so outbound_fields.py:418 now ALWAYS calls binding_store.get_baseline(local_id) (comment at :410). The integration-tier stubs were updated with get_baseline, but the external-tier StubBindingStore (tests/external/test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py:126) was missed — the one sibling not updated.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run the external-integration workflow on main (workflow_dispatch). Observed run 29303295904 (2026-07-14): '1 failed, 24 passed' — only test_link_sync_differ_apply_roundtrip_live fails on the missing-attribute AttributeError.
Expected: the external stub implements the BindingStore.get_baseline(local_id)->dict|None contract; absent baseline returns None (local-wins, ADR 0026 §2), matching the stub's pre-flag behavior. Actual: the stub lacks the method; the outbound arbitration path AttributeErrors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] StubBindingStore in tests/external/test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py implements get_baseline(local_id)->dict|None matching binding_store.BindingStore.get_baseline (return None = no last-synced baseline).
- [ ] [operator-attested] external-integration workflow re-run on main is green (test_link_sync_differ_apply_roundtrip_live passes) — live-Jira tier, verified by a workflow re-run.
- [ ] No other external/integration BindingStore stub is left missing get_baseline where the outbound arbitration path exercises it (sibling sweep: integration stubs already updated; only this external one was missed).

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`BindingStore` is the authoritative local-id ↔ Jira identity aggregate and must remain so, but its 799-line module now owns byte persistence, live/reverse lifecycle policy, retirement, recovery, peer-state delegates, comment identity, and GET rotation. New safety rules have no cohesive owner, and production code mutates an inner entry returned by the shallow `all_bindings()` compatibility query. A mechanical split could regress hard-won crash, index-lag, identity, serialization, and selective-publication behavior.

## Outcome
Keep one public `BindingStore` facade and existing import/method compatibility while extracting three internal owners: a byte-preserving repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, and incomplete-operation recovery. Typed views remain open over the original dictionaries so unknown fields and exact JSON behavior survive. Add the approved journal-free retirement completion rule: a durable tombstone is authoritative intent, and a live forward/reverse pair is removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree. Only explicit `unretire` revokes that intent; automatic liveness observations never resurrect a tombstoned identity.

## Delivery slices
1. Extract repository/unit-of-work persistence behind the facade with byte, fault-cut, corruption, rotation-order, and selective-publication regression oracles; establish ADR 0099 with the complete approved target design.
2. Extract lifecycle policy and add narrow facade operations so new production code no longer needs mutation-through-query while `all_bindings()` remains shallow-compatible.
3. Extract recovery, cut the live caller to the narrow mutation seam, complete exact-match interrupted retirements before remote issue observation, and finalize ADR 0099 to describe the realized behavior.

## Architectural constraints
- Preserve `peer_state.py`, `get_rotation.py`, pending → confirmed → reversible retired lifecycle, numeric-ID re-key, comment identity, and the existing five-file selective tickets publication.
- Preserve unknown fields, `indent=2`, sorted keys, trailing newline, legacy additive reads, and unchanged-pass byte/HEAD idempotency.
- Corrupt live state still fails closed; retired/rotation/alert/commit failure behavior changes only when this plan names it.
- Construction, load, check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered operations do not perform recovery writes.
- Live recovery runs after configuration snapshot/preflight and exclusive lock/staleness validation but before remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation. This ordering prevents an upgraded pass from interleaving new liveness evidence with completion.
- In a historical overlap, stale `absent_404_count`, automatic 200/`clear_absent`, or same-key confirm cannot revoke the durable tombstone; only explicit `unretire` removes it and thereby eliminates the completion candidate.
- No general journal, format migration, eager rewrite, broad `git add -A`, deep-copy change to `all_bindings()`, or new identity writer.

## Compatibility / rollback
Each slice is an internal facade delegation with unchanged stored formats and public signatures. A slice can be reverted independently to the preceding facade implementation. The exact-match repair is additive and idempotent: disabling its pre-observation live-operation call restores the prior detectable overlap without rewriting coherent stores. Rollback never deletes a remote issue or implies automatic unretire.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Existing `BindingStore` imports, signatures, shallow `all_bindings()` behavior, unknown-field preservation, and exact serialization remain compatible through direct-loader and public-facade tests.
- [x] Repository fault-cut tests preserve current rotation-before-live ordering, per-file atomic replacement, selective five-file publication, and explicit failure outcomes.
- [x] Lifecycle tests preserve both-index identity guards, pending/confirmed/retired rules, 404 grace/reset, immutable-ID re-key, tombstone suppression/unretire, and append-only comment identity.
- [x] Recovery tests prove keyed/keyless create recovery and exact-match retirement completion are idempotent; repair runs before remote observation, identities must agree, and ambiguity/replace failure safety-aborts.
- [x] Automatic liveness signals do not override durable retirement intent; explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone and prevents completion.
- [x] Load/check/dry-run/preview/selection/filtered tests prove zero recovery writes; only a validated write-bearing operation may repair an interrupted retirement.
- [x] ADR 0099 identifies preserved behavior, the intentional repair behavior, explicit-unretire reversal, pre-observation ordering, rollback, and the prohibition on broad tickets-branch staging.
baseline.summary: RP-02 — Decompose binding persistence, lifecycle, and recovery behind BindingStore
tune snapshot-janitor watermark for the 30G root box (2GiB engages only at ~93%, above the 85% alarm)

# Finish ADR 0056: extract build_agent_kwargs and the post-call telemetry from run()

## Context / Problem

`PydanticAIRunner.run()` is the last un-decomposed stretch of ADR 0056 (`docs/adr/0056-decompose-pydantic-ai-runner-run.md`). Earlier stories in epic 061c landed the first three of the ADR's four named extractions — `interpret_failure` (e6bd), `build_model_settings` / `build_usage_limits` (8229), and the `with ProviderSession(cfg)` guard. The fourth, `build_agent_kwargs`, plus the post-call telemetry block the ADR's Consequences section names by name, are still inline.

MEASURED on this branch (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, worktree `feat/5e75-adr0056`):

- `runner.py` was **699 LOC** when this ticket was written, one line under a `runner.py < 700`
  assertion then present in `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py`. SUPERSEDED: that assertion
  has since been REMOVED under ticket db7f / ADR 0058, which makes
  `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (800) the sole authoritative ceiling. The one-line-headroom
  urgency is therefore gone; it is recorded here only as the original motivation.
- `PydanticAIRunner.run()` spans `runner.py:259-600` = **342 lines**, still 49% of the file and
  far from ADR 0056's projected 60-90.

The problem is the one-line headroom, and the people with it are every contributor who has to touch the runner next (task cb6f and the provider-seam epic both queue lines into this cluster).

## Approach

Extract three inline blocks out of `run()` into ONE new sibling module, `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py`, as plain functions with explicit parameters (ADR 0056 decision 3; no carrier object — no signature reaches the ADR's ~6-parameter threshold for one).

This is a **pure relocation**: no renamed public symbol, no changed signature crossing a module boundary, no logic "improved" in transit, no comment losing a measured fact, a bug/story id, a `file:line`, or a stated invariant (the constraint this ticket inherits from 7f86).

**1. `build_agent_kwargs(cfg, req, tools, toolsets, *, model_settings, web_caps) -> dict`**

Today three separated statements all write the SAME `kwargs` dict that is handed to `Agent(model, **kwargs)` at `runner.py:481` and to `_pai_structured(...)` at `runner.py:496-498`:

- `runner.py:371-382` — the `tool_step_limit` rewrite of `tools`/`toolsets` into a filtered
  `FunctionToolset` (its only purpose is to produce the two values the dict then stores).
- `runner.py:384-392` — the base dict (`system_prompt`, `tools`, `toolsets`, `tool_timeout`).
- `runner.py:436-437` — `kwargs["capabilities"] = web_caps`.
- `runner.py:460-461` — `kwargs["model_settings"] = model_settings`.

The seam is real and already exists in the data flow: `tools`/`toolsets` are read nowhere in `run()` after `runner.py:382` except by the dict at `384-387`, and `kwargs` is read nowhere between its construction at `384` and its two consumers at `481`/`497`. So the four fragments collapse into one call sited where the last of them stands today, with no statement crossing another statement's read or write. `build_agent_kwargs` also consumes the output of `build_model_settings` (`runner.py:441-443`), which ADR 0056 already extracted — the two are adjacent links in one chain, which is why the ADR names them together in decision 3.

`web_caps` is passed IN rather than computed inside, deliberately: `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` is a `runner` module global reachable by `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, ...)`, and moving its CALL SITE into another module would silently defeat any such patch (the hazard ADR 0056's Consequences section records). Keeping the call at `runner.py:433-435` means **zero monkeypatch repoints are required by this change** — verified against the patch inventory below.

**2. `log_call_success(usage, *, call_label, execution_mode, ran_model, req_limit, eff_max_iter, started_at)`**

`runner.py:547-565` — the 19-line success-path `logger.info` with the step-usage counters. This is the block ADR 0056's Consequences section names as one of the two reasons its earlier ~250/~15 projection was wrong.

It is extracted **in place**, called from `runner.py:547`, NOT folded together with the spend record below. `_findings.finalize_outcome` at `runner.py:566-578` can raise (schema validation); today the "ok" line is already emitted when it does. Moving the log after finalization would lose that line on a finalization failure — a behaviour change, which a pure refactor may not make.

**3. `record_call_spend(usage, *, call_label, ran_model)`**

`runner.py:583-599` — the `usage_log.active_step()` / `usage_log.record(...)` spend row. Same post-call telemetry concern, same `usage`/`call_label`/`ran_model` inputs as (2); it stays a separate function only because it must stay on the far side of `finalize_outcome`. Its `infer_provider(ran_model)` call moves with it, and `infer_provider` is then dropped from `runner.py:38`'s import — confirmed unused elsewhere in `runner.py` and imported from `runner` by no module or test (`grep -rn "runner import.*infer_provider" src/ tests/ docs/` is empty).

### Why a NEW module and not `structured_run.py`

The ticket's original scope line named `structured_run.py` as the destination. That is not viable, and the evidence is in-repo: `structured_run.py` is **491 LOC** and `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py:59` asserts `100 <= loc < 500` on it (AGENTS.md's 200-500 target band). It has **9 lines of headroom** — it cannot absorb a ~130-line extraction without either failing that assertion or forcing an edit to a structural guard another story just wrote.

`agent_call.py` is sized honestly rather than to clear a floor: the relocated source is 62 lines of `runner.py` today (22 + 2 + 2 + 19 + 17), and signatures, contract docstrings, imports and the module docstring bring it to roughly 130-150 — inside AGENTS.md's 200-500 target's lower half and clear of the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor with real content, not padding.

Its cohesion is stated plainly rather than overclaimed: the three functions do **not** call each other. What binds them is that they are the edges of exactly one Agent call — the kwargs handed to `Agent(...)`, and the two records emitted after it returns — and they share `run()`'s locals (`usage`, `ran_model`, `call_label`, `req_limit`, `eff_max_iter`). `structured_run.py` keeps its own distinct job (driving the structured-output retry loop and computing settings) and is not edited at all by this change.

`agent_call.py` is a LEAF on the same rule as `structured_run.py`: it imports nothing from `runner` at runtime; the one `RunRequest` annotation is deferred via `from __future__ import annotations` + `TYPE_CHECKING`, so `import rebar.llm` stays stdlib-only.

### Monkeypatch-hazard audit (the constraint 7f86 flagged as LIVE)

The full inventory of `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, ...)` targets in the suite is `_import_pydantic_ai`, `capabilities_for`, `ProviderSession`, `build_usage_limits`, `_pai_structured`, `_pai_model`, `cache_settings_for`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, and `get_runner`. **Every one of them stays a `runner` module global under this plan** — none is called from inside a relocated block, and `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` is kept at its current call site precisely to preserve that. So this change requires **zero** repoints, and the ADR's "each repoint lands in the same commit" rule is satisfied vacuously.

`tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:332-334` asserts `"signal.alarm" not in inspect.getsource(runner_mod)` and `"Timer(" not in ...`; removing lines only narrows that negative-space guard, so it stays green.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — remove the four `kwargs` fragments and the two telemetry blocks;
  add the three calls and one import; drop the now-unused `infer_provider` import.
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — NEW; the three extracted functions.
- `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` — NEW; the structural seam test, following the convention
  of `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py` and `tests/unit/test_interpret_failure_seam.py`.

No other file changes. `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` is NOT edited.

## Testing

A relocation adds no behaviour, so the real regression net is the **existing suite passing unedited** — no assertion weakened, skipped, deleted, or adjusted. The baseline pass count is recorded before the first edit and must match after.

The new seam test asserts the structure the move has to preserve, and covers a failure/edge path rather than the happy path only:

- Happy path: `build_agent_kwargs` with `tool_step_limit=None` returns `tools`/`toolsets`
  unchanged and `tool_timeout == float(cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s)`; worked example — with
  `cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s = 77` and `tools=[t]`, the result is
  `{"system_prompt": ..., "tools": [t], "toolsets": [], "tool_timeout": 77.0}`.
- Edge: with `tool_step_limit=3` and a non-empty `tools`, the result has `tools == []` and every
  entry of `toolsets` filtered — the convergence-boundary rewrite, whose absence would silently
  un-bound a tool loop.
- Edge: `model_settings=None`/falsy and `web_caps=None` omit the `"model_settings"` and
  `"capabilities"` keys entirely (the "byte-identical for a non-anthropic request" invariant at
  `runner.py:430-432`).
- Edge: `log_call_success` on an empty `usage` dict emits its line with zeroed counters and does
  not raise (`usage` is `{}` whenever the call failed before usage extraction).
- Structural: `agent_call.py >= 100` (the anti-fragmentation floor; NO upper ceiling on
  `runner.py` — see ADR 0058), and `agent_call.py` has no
  runtime import of `runner` (AST-checked, same method as
  `test_structured_run_seam.py::test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_agent_kwargs` exists in `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` as a plain function with
      explicit parameters and no carrier object, and `runner.py` builds the Agent kwargs by
      calling it — verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` and by
      `grep -c 'kwargs: dict\[str, Any\] = {' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returning 0.
- [ ] The success-path `logger.info` telemetry block and the `usage_log.record` spend block are
      both out of `run()` and in `agent_call.py` as `log_call_success` / `record_call_spend` —
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py`.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` asserts that `agent_call.py` clears the 100-LOC
      anti-fragmentation floor — verified by that test passing. It must NOT assert any upper LOC
      ceiling on `runner.py`: ADR 0058 makes `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (800) the SOLE
      authoritative ceiling, enforced by the CI module-size gate and mirrored in-process by
      `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, which reads that same file. Per-file ceilings
      asserted in seam tests were removed under ticket db7f as overreach — they invert governance
      (the tightest bound becomes an unlocked literal) and fail mid-refactor by construction.
      Narrowed from the original "under 700 LOC AND ..." wording after ADR 0058 landed; the
      floor half is retained because it is the opposite check and catches what the cap cannot.
- [ ] The full default selection
      (`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal -q`) passes with a pass
      count at least the pre-change baseline and zero failures, with **no existing test edited** —
      verified by diffing the recorded baseline count against the post-change count and by
      `git diff --stat` showing no modified file under `tests/` (only the new seam test added).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` both exit 0.
- [ ] No relocated comment lost a measured number, a `file:line`, a bug/story/epic id, a named
      failure mode, or a stated invariant — verified by `git show --stat` plus reading the moved
      comment blocks against their originals in the diff.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The before/after LOC for `runner.py` AND for the `PydanticAIRunner.run()`
      METHOD BODY are recorded in the commit message. Tagged because the completion verifier reads
      repository files only and cannot read git history; the method figure is tracked separately
      because it is the number ADR 0056 has twice under-projected (260, then 310, MEASURED 323
      after 7f86, 342 today). Evidence recorded on the ticket: a comment quoting both figures and
      the commit SHA that carries them.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Zero monkeypatch repoints were required, and the commit message says so
      with the reason (no relocated block calls a patched `runner` global). Evidence recorded on
      the ticket: a comment naming the audited target list and the commit SHA.
baseline.summary: Finish ADR 0056: extract build_agent_kwargs and the telemetry block from run()

## Why
Prove the entire architecture end-to-end on the SMALLEST unit before generalizing: a schema registry holding input+output contracts, a step DECLARING a contract, the editor SURFACING it, and validation CONSUMING it. This is the walking skeleton that validates the epic's central claim ("every step kind advertises input/output contract + description, consumed by the editor") on one scripted op, so design flaws surface in week 1 rather than after the whole model is built.

## What
- Extend the existing schema registry (`src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` `registry()`/`validator()`,
  already `referencing.Registry` + `Draft202012Validator`, 2020-12) so it ALSO resolves INPUT
  schemas by name. Author one input schema file for `fetch_ticket`.
- Add a `StepContract` (`{input_schema, output_schema, description}`) and extend the
  `@register_step` decorator (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py`) to accept
  `input_schema=`/`output_schema=`/`description=`; attach it to `fetch_ticket` in
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/steps.py`. Expose a lookup `contract_for(step_name)`.
- Editor inspector (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` + `editor_assets/`): for a selected node,
  render its CONSUMES (input contract fields) / PRODUCES (output contract fields) + description,
  READ-ONLY.
- Validation (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint_refs.py`): a `with:` field mapped to
  `${{ steps.A.outputs.foo }}` is checked that A's output contract declares `foo` (NAME-EXISTENCE
  only here); recognize a distinct `${{ inputs.* }}` namespace for engine-injected vars
  (ticket_id/ticket_context/repo_path) and do NOT flag those.

## Scope
In: the four layers above wired through `fetch_ticket` only. Out: other ops (S1), prompts (S4), deep/runtime validation (S5), authoring/write-back (S6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `fetch_ticket` declares input+output schema names + description via `@register_step`, resolvable from the registry.
- [ ] The editor inspector shows that op's consumes/produces/description (read-only) for a selected node.
- [ ] `lint_refs` flags a `with:` ref to a non-existent upstream output field; `${{ inputs.* }}` is not flagged.
- [ ] An end-to-end test loads a fixture workflow using `fetch_ticket` and asserts: inspector contract output + lint catches a bad ref + passes a good ref.
- [ ] `lint_refs` treats an upstream step that lacks an output contract as UNKNOWN/skip (never a false error) — required since only `fetch_ticket` is annotated in this slice.
- [ ] The engine-injected `${{ inputs.* }}` var set (ticket_id/ticket_context/repo_path) is defined as a SINGLE named constant (the source of truth), not hardcoded inline.
- [ ] The inspector shows a defined empty/no-contract state (not a crash) for a node with no declared contract or when nothing is selected.
- [ ] The `fetch_ticket` input schema lives at a defined registry path (e.g. `src/rebar/schemas/fetch_ticket_input.schema.json`) and resolves by name.
baseline.summary: Walking skeleton: contract -> inspector -> validation on one scripted op (end-to-end)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Three unit tests sleep through real production backoff, so CI pays wall-clock for delays that are pure logic. Confirmed against current main in this worktree:

* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py:44` declares
  `sleep_fn=time.sleep` — an IMPORT-BOUND default, evaluated once at def time.
  `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py:286` does
  `mock.patch("time.sleep")  # avoid real delay`, which rebinds the attribute on
  the `time` module and therefore cannot reach the already-captured default. The
  probe's JQL retry then really sleeps `JQL_RETRY_SLEEP=5` five times
  (`JQL_RETRY_COUNT=6`, `access_check.py:12-13,104-112`) = 25s, matching the
  filed 25.3s.
* `scripts/dependency_audit.py:194` has the same shape,
  `sleeper: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep`, and
  `tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py:319` patches `mod.time.sleep` — again
  too late. `run_pip_audit` sleeps `attempt * 5` for attempts 1 and 2
  (`dependency_audit.py:215-216`) = 5s + 10s = 15s, matching the filed 15.0s.
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_stale_binding_404.py:236`
  (`test_non_404_http_error_still_propagates`) patches nothing at all. It drives
  `_call_with_retry` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:74`),
  whose HTTPError-5xx branch sleeps `2**(attempt+1) + random.random()`
  (line 129) for three retries = ~2+4+8 plus jitter ≈ 14-17s, matching the
  filed 15.8s.

So the premise holds for all three, and the two "patched" tests were silently no-ops — the comment `# avoid real delay` was already false.

## Approach

Late-bind the two import-bound defaults, and make all three tests use a RECORDING sleeper that asserts the logical schedule.

* In `access_check.run_access_check` and `dependency_audit.run_pip_audit`, change
  the default from `time.sleep` to `None` and resolve
  `sleep_fn = time.sleep if sleep_fn is None else sleep_fn` in the body. Production
  behaviour is byte-identical: both parameters are keyword-only, no caller in the
  tree passes them (`_lib_ops.py:303` and `jira-capability-probe.py:34` are the only
  `run_access_check` call sites, neither passes `sleep_fn`), and an unpassed argument
  still resolves to `time.sleep` — only WHEN it resolves moves, from import time to
  call time, which is what makes the seam patchable at all.
* Each of the three tests replaces its ineffective (or absent) patch with a sleeper
  that appends the requested delay to a list and returns immediately, then asserts
  the recorded schedule: `[5, 5, 5, 5, 5]` for the probe, `[5, 10]` for the audit,
  and three HTTPError backoffs for the 500 test. `dispatch_apply_phases.py:132`
  calls a bare `time.sleep(delay)` resolved at call time, so the 500 test needs only
  a `monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", recorder)` — no production change there.

Asserting the recorded schedule IS the required guard: if a future change re-binds the seam early, or a new call path bypasses it, the recorder stays empty and the assertion fails loudly, rather than the test merely getting slow again. That is a stronger guard than checking wall time, and it adds no timing-budget assertion.

Late-binding is preferred over threading an explicit sleeper down from `main`, because the probe is executed as a script through `run_access_check()` with no injection point, so a caller-supplied sleeper could not reach it without changing the probe's public entry shape.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py` — late-bind `sleep_fn`.
* `scripts/dependency_audit.py` — late-bind `sleeper`.
* `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` — recording sleeper +
  schedule assertion in `test_probe_retries_jql_search_three_times`.
* `tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py` — recording sleeper + schedule
  assertion in `test_gate_reports_db_unreachable_as_infrastructure`.
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_stale_binding_404.py` —
  recording sleeper + schedule assertion in
  `test_non_404_http_error_still_propagates`.

`dispatch_apply_phases.py` is read but NOT modified; its bare `time.sleep` is already a working seam.

## Testing

* Happy path — each of the three tests still asserts exactly what it asserted
  before (6 `search_issues` calls; 3 `pip-audit` attempts with the INFRASTRUCTURE
  message; `pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError)` on the 500), and now
  additionally asserts its logical delay schedule.
* Failure/edge path — the guard is proven by seeding: reverting
  `access_check.py` to the import-bound default is confirmed to make the probe
  test FAIL on the empty recorder (not merely run slowly), and the same for
  `dependency_audit.py`. Both seeds reverted; neither committed.
* Production-behaviour check — `run_access_check` and `run_pip_audit` called
  without a sleeper still resolve to `time.sleep`, confirmed by a direct
  interpreter check of the resolved default rather than by sleeping.
* Whole-suite regression — the CI pytest command is green.

No wall-clock or timing-budget assertion is added; savings go in ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `test_probe_retries_jql_search_three_times` still asserts
      `search_issues.call_count == 6` AND asserts the recorded delays are five
      5-second entries, with no real sleep — verified by the test passing in
      under 2s where it took ~25s.
- [x] `test_gate_reports_db_unreachable_as_infrastructure` still asserts rc 1,
      `INFRASTRUCTURE issue`, `recheck`, and three `pip-audit` attempts, AND
      asserts recorded delays `[5, 10]` — verified by the test passing in under
      2s where it took ~15s.
- [x] `test_non_404_http_error_still_propagates` still raises
      `urllib.error.HTTPError` after retry exhaustion AND asserts three recorded
      backoff delays — verified by the test passing in under 2s where it took
      ~15s.
- [x] Production retry counts, delay schedules, exception types and messages are
      unchanged: the only production edits are the two default values moving from
      `time.sleep` to `None` with an equivalent in-body resolution, shown by
      `git diff` on the two production files being exactly that.
- [x] Each of the three tests fails (not merely slows) when its seam is reverted
      to the import-bound default — recorded as a ticket comment with the seeded
      failure output, seeds reverted.
- [x] Before/after wall-clock for the three tests is recorded as a ticket comment,
      measured with `pytest --durations`.
baseline.summary: Unit tests execute production retry sleeps through import-bound defaults

baseline.description:
## Summary

The deployed MCP server has NO Jira credentials, so `bridge_check_access` (and every other live bridge operation) fails immediately.

## Observed

    bridge_check_access -> {"error":"command_failed", "exit_code":2,
      "message":"bridge access check requires JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, and JIRA_API_TOKEN"}

## Established by inspection

- **No Jira leaf existed.** Neither `fetch-secrets.sh` nor `infra/terraform/ssm.tf` had one, so
  this is an ABSENT capability, not a broken one.
- **The three credential VALUES were seeded OUT OF BAND by an operator** (AWS CLI, not terraform):
  `/rebar/prod/jira-url` (String), `jira-user` (String), `jira-api-token` (SecureString). Terraform
  does not have them in state, which the plan must handle.
- **A FOURTH input is required for a live verdict: `JIRA_PROJECT`.**
  `access_check._resolve_probe_scope` fails closed with `reason=missing_project`, and
  `rebar.config.resolve_jira_probe_scope` reads the ENVIRONMENT ONLY — the committed
  `rebar.toml` `[jira] project = "REB"` never reaches the probe. Wiring only the three credentials
  would move the failure from `missing_credentials` to `missing_project` without reaching a
  verdict. It is NON-SECRET, so it is wired as a fourth PLAIN leaf.
- **Preserve the var/secret split, do not flatten it.** GitHub Actions models `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`
  as non-secret `vars.*` and only `JIRA_API_TOKEN` as a `secrets.*`
  (`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:122-126`); rebar's `_child_env.py` registry agrees, listing
  `JIRA_API_TOKEN` as the sole jira secret. Only the token warrants a SecureString.

## Work

1. **`ssm.tf` — declare the four leaves with the type split.** `jira-api-token` joins
   `local.rebar_secret_params` (SecureString); `jira-url`/`jira-user` go in a new plain `String`
   resource. Both keep the repo's operator-seeded precedent (`value = "CHANGEME"` +
   `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`), so terraform owns existence and type but never the
   value, and each gets a terraform `import` block to adopt the out-of-band parameter — without
   which the next apply dies on `ParameterAlreadyExists`. `jira-project` is the exception: a public
   identifier, so FULLY terraform-managed (real value, no `ignore_changes`, no import), with a test
   pinning it equal to `rebar.toml`.
2. **`fetch-secrets.sh` — read and emit all four, SOFT.** Never the fail-fast `get_param`, which
   exits 1 and writes no `.env` at all. The token uses `get_param_optional`; the three Strings use a
   new `get_param_optional_plain` that OMITS `--with-decryption`, honouring the split at the read.
3. **Carry them via the `.env`, NOT via `-e`.** Compose already has `env_file: .env` and
   `mcp_run_new` already has `--env-file`. Spelling them as `-e JIRA_URL=${JIRA_URL:-}` would
   resolve EMPTY in the deploy shell and CLOBBER the real value, so all four join `_ENV_FILE_ONLY`
   in `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — the existing `MCP_TICKETS_PAT` mechanism,
   reused.
4. **Failure posture: SOFT DEGRADE, deliberately.** Jira credentials are an OUTBOUND integration
   credential, so their absence cannot yield an unauthenticated endpoint (unlike
   `mcp-static-tokens.json`, which fails CLOSED). The container boots, the endpoint stays up, and
   only the bridge tools report unavailable.
5. **Tests** pin the leaf types and import adoption, the `.env` emission and decryption posture, the
   compose/`mcp_run_new` parity, and the soft degrade.

**Status: IMPLEMENTED AND LANDED** as `ab885cef6986` (Gerrit change 2279, MERGED). Verification evidence is in this ticket's comments.

## Explicitly OUT of scope

Changing the bridge code path. `_lib_ops.bridge_check_access` (`src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:362-368`) already raises a TYPED `RebarError(returncode=2)` naming all three missing variables. That IS the soft degrade at the tool boundary: one tool reports a clear, typed "these are required" error while the server keeps serving every other tool. Converting it into a non-raising "not configured" verdict would change the library/MCP contract and its output schema, which is a separate ticket, not part of wiring the credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria

      declared in `ssm.tf` with that type split, the three operator-seeded ones adopted by import

- [x] `ssm.tf`'s `jira-project` value equals `rebar.toml`'s `[jira] project`, asserted by test, so

- [x] The four variables reach the mcp container in BOTH the compose boot path and the
      blue-green `mcp_run_new` path, asserted by the existing
      `test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service` parity oracle via `_ENV_FILE_ONLY`.
- [x] Absent or blank credentials do NOT abort `fetch-secrets.sh` and do NOT take the endpoint
      down: the stack boots, and `bridge_check_access` surfaces its existing typed exit-2 error
      naming the missing variables. (Asserted in-session by test, no live Jira needed.)
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `shellcheck` on the touched shell, and the infra/compose
      test suites all pass.
- [x] No credential value is logged, printed, or written into the repo or into terraform.
- [x] [non-codebase] `bridge_check_access` returns its live typed verdict from the deployed MCP
      container and is no longer blocked on credentials. Both preconditions the original wording
      named are met: terraform created `/rebar/prod/jira-project`, and the container carries all
      four values. The probe scope RESOLVES instead of failing closed, and the verdict's only
      failing step is the absent `acli` transport binary, filed as `royalistic-gorgeable-norwayrat`
      — a distinct defect this fix unmasked, not a credential or project-scope fault.
      provenance: environment=AWS prod EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 us-east-1, MCP container rebar-mcp-25ea12c200ae-8092 running build 25ea12c200ae which contains the fix ab885cef6986; principal=IAM user joe_frontier issuing SSM RunShellScript, Jira reached as the container's own JIRA_USER identity; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — one real rebar.bridge_check_access() call in the deployed container against production Jira project REB, anchored by a corrupted-token negative control returning 401 and a before/after JQL census confirming nothing was left behind

baseline.description:
## Why
The live Jira/LLM external tier (`tests/external/`) runs only on `workflow_dispatch` (`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`), which sets `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` and maps `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` but **no `JIRA_*` secrets** and does **not install the `acli` binary** — and `test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py::_live_jira_ready()` gates on BOTH (`creds and shutil.which("acli")`). So the live Jira round-trip can only ever SKIP: Jira API/SDK drift merges through normal CI with no real integration signal, and nothing fails a run in which the whole external tier silently skips. VALIDATED.

Correction to the earlier framing: the live test is NOT read-only — it calls `create_issue` twice + `set_relationship`, then in a `try/finally` deletes every artifact it created (links then issues). It makes REAL, self-cleaning Jira mutations against whatever project the creds point at, so it requires a DEDICATED disposable test project, not a shared one.

## What
1. **Workflow** (`external-integration.yml`): add an `on.schedule` trigger with the exact cron
   `0 6 * * 1` (Mondays 06:00 UTC, weekly) alongside `workflow_dispatch`, and MIRROR the
   established `reconcile-bridge.yml` convention
   EXACTLY (not an ad-hoc variant):
   - Jira env, sourced the SAME way reconcile-bridge does: `JIRA_URL: ${{ vars.JIRA_URL }}`,
     `JIRA_USER: ${{ vars.JIRA_USER }}` (repo VARIABLES, not secrets), and
     `JIRA_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_API_TOKEN }}` (the only secret), and `JIRA_PROJECT: ${{ vars.JIRA_PROJECT }}` (the live Jira tests read it for the target project).
   - the `acli` install, reusing reconcile-bridge's THREE companion steps verbatim in shape:
     the `cache-acli` cache step, the `Download + verify + install acli` step (pinned
     `vars.ACLI_VERSION` + `vars.ACLI_SHA256`, sha256-checked), AND the `Add acli to PATH and
     authenticate` step exactly as reconcile-bridge does it: `sudo ln -sf "$HOME/.acli/acli"
     /usr/local/bin/acli` (symlink the binary into the on-PATH `/usr/local/bin`, NOT
     `$GITHUB_PATH`), then `echo "$JIRA_API_TOKEN" | acli jira auth login --site "$JIRA_URL"
     --email "$JIRA_USER" --token`. Without this step `shutil.which("acli")` and the live auth
     both fail, so the Jira tests still skip.
2. **Fail-on-all-skip Jira canary** — deterministic, marker-based (NOT skip-string matching,
   which is fragile across the tier's many distinct skip reasons), and SELF-MAINTAINING (no
   hardcoded module list, so a future Jira module is auto-covered). All Jira live modules share
   one gate signature: a module-level `_live_jira_ready()` + `_skip = skipif(not
   _live_jira_ready(), …)` (currently `test_link_sync_live.py`, `test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`,
   `test_reconcile_live.py`, `test_verified_fake_contract_live.py`, but the hook keys off the
   signature, not this list).
   - Register a `jira_live` marker (pyproject `[tool.pytest.ini_options].markers`).
   - In `tests/external/conftest.py`, a `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook AUTO-APPLIES the
     `jira_live` marker to every collected item whose `item.module` defines `_live_jira_ready`
     (i.e. every Jira-gated module, present or future) — no per-file `@pytest.mark` edits, no
     enumeration to drift.
   - A `pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus)` hook (which sets a nonzero `session.exitstatus` to fail the run) that, when
     `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` is truthy, REPORTS the `jira_live` executed-vs-skipped counts and
     FAILS the session (nonzero exit) iff ≥1 `jira_live` test was COLLECTED but ZERO executed
     (passed or failed) — exactly the "Jira secrets/acli missing, no real signal" condition.
     Membership is the marker (deterministic), so unrelated always-on tests
     (`test_model_requests_enabled`, `test_deps_live`) neither mask nor trip it.
   - When `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` is unset (the default suite, tier inert via the opt-in guard),
     the hook is a no-op.
3. **Tests**:
   - a behavioral test of the fail-on-all-skip hook over SIMULATED session reports: a session
     where all `jira_live` tests skipped (with `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`) makes the hook signal
     failure; a session where ≥1 `jira_live` test executed passes; and an unset
     `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` is a no-op. (Drive the hook function directly with constructed
     report objects — no live creds needed.)
   - a config-as-artifact test asserting `external-integration.yml` declares an `on.schedule`
     trigger, maps `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN` into the external job env, AND
     installs `acli` / puts it on PATH (a drift guard mirroring the repo's YAML-artifact tests).

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` — schedule + JIRA_* env + acli install/PATH/auth.
- `pyproject.toml` — register the `jira_live` pytest marker.
- `tests/external/conftest.py` — register-free auto-marking (`pytest_collection_modifyitems`
  keyed on `_live_jira_ready`) + the marker-scoped fail-on-all-skip session hook + report.
- A test module (e.g. `tests/unit/test_external_canary.py`) — the hook behavior + workflow wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The workflow declares `on.schedule` with cron `0 6 * * 1`; sources `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_PROJECT`
      from `vars.*` and `JIRA_API_TOKEN` from `secrets.*` (matching reconcile-bridge.yml); and
      installs `acli` + symlinks it onto PATH + authenticates (the cache / download-verify-install
      / add-to-PATH-and-authenticate steps). A config-as-artifact test pins the cron, the Jira
      env wiring, and the acli PATH/auth step.
- [ ] A `jira_live` marker is registered and AUTO-APPLIED (via a collection hook keyed on
      `_live_jira_ready`) to every Jira-gated live module; the
      conftest hook FAILS an external session (with `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`) iff ≥1 `jira_live`
      test was collected but zero executed (all skipped), PASSES when a `jira_live` test
      executed, and is a no-op when `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` is unset — asserted by a behavioral
      test driving the hook over constructed report objects.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The operator configures the `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER` repo VARIABLES,
      the `JIRA_API_TOKEN` SECRET, and the `ACLI_VERSION`/`ACLI_SHA256` repo variables, and
      provisions a DEDICATED disposable Jira test project (these require GitHub repo-admin + a
      Jira project and cannot be done from the code change). CONCRETE evidence to record as a
      comment on this ticket: the URL of a manual `workflow_dispatch` run of the
      `external-integration` workflow whose `external` job is GREEN with the live Jira
      round-trip test EXECUTED (passed, not skipped) — i.e. the fail-on-all-skip canary did NOT
      fire — plus the run id/timestamp. A blank "done" without that run URL does not satisfy it.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` green.

baseline.description:
## Problem (PROVEN, not inferred)

`apply_inbound_records.py` derives the inbound identity provider AND creation channel from the configured backend's vendor string:

    vendor = select_backend(load_config()).vendor          # 'jira-datacenter' for DC
    rebar.ensure_identity_for(vendor, account_id, ..., creation_channel=vendor)

But the store vocabulary does not contain that value:

    CREATION_CHANNELS = frozenset({'cli', 'mcp', 'python', 'jira', 'import', 'unknown'})

Measured directly against a scratch repo:

    creation_channel='jira'            ext=acct-cloud -> returned '4802-2404-6de4-4167'
    creation_channel='jira-datacenter' ext=acct-dc    -> RAISED ValueError:
        invalid creation_channel 'jira-datacenter'; must be one of
        ['cli', 'import', 'jira', 'mcp', 'python']

(The failure only appears on a FRESH mint — an existing (provider, external_id) mapping is reused idempotently and never reaches validation, which is why a naive probe shows a false pass.)

## Why it is SILENT — the part that makes this dangerous

The call is wrapped in:

    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply
        logger.debug('inbound: could not ensure identity for jira accountId %r', ...)

So on a Data Center deployment EVERY inbound ghost-identity mint fails, is swallowed, and is reported only at DEBUG. The reconcile pass still converges and reports success. This is precisely the failure mode epic e369's AC6 exists to catch: a swallowed exception can still converge, so convergence is not evidence of correctness.

Consequence: DC inbound assignees never get identities minted, so assignee resolution degrades silently on every DC pass.

## Why it is newly reachable

Before story J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1], `reconciler.backend` was validated as `_as_choice(v, k, {'jira'})`, so config could NEVER select the DC backend and `select_backend(load_config()).vendor` could never return 'jira-datacenter'. J7 widens that choice set — which is what ACTIVATES this path. The defect is latent on main today and becomes live the moment a DC deployment is configured.

## Also inconsistent WITHIN the same module

The ticket-creation path a few lines below already hard-codes the family channel:

    create_data['creation_channel'] = validate_creation_channel('jira')

So the ticket gets 'jira' while the identity path tries 'jira-datacenter'. One of the two is wrong; per epic e369's shared-identity decision (DC-created tickets carry the SHARED 'jira' creation channel and the deployment is distinguished by RemoteRef.instance, so nothing in the store vocabulary forks per deployment), the ticket path is right and the identity path is the bug.

## Proposed fix (NOT to widen the vocabulary)

Map the backend vendor to its FAMILY channel at this call site, so both jira and jira-datacenter mint under the shared 'jira' provider/channel. Adding 'jira-datacenter' to CREATION_CHANNELS is the WRONG fix: it forks the store vocabulary per deployment, contradicting the epic's decision and dragging in a migration + compatibility gate that the epic explicitly avoids. It would also fragment identity across deployments (a Cloud and a DC identity for the same human).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] an inbound apply under the DC backend mints a ghost identity successfully, asserted by a test
      that FAILS on today's code
- [ ] the identity is minted under the shared 'jira' provider/channel, matching the ticket path
- [ ] a test asserts the failure is not merely swallowed — i.e. the mint is observed to SUCCEED,
      not that no exception escaped
- [ ] CREATION_CHANNELS is UNCHANGED (no per-deployment vocabulary fork, no migration)
baseline.summary: DC inbound identity mint fails silently: 'jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel

## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` currently changes up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this deliberately covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

Author the behavioral oracle RED-first. Hold out the interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases from the implementer; expose only the basic dual-read happy path. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs is expected to advance and commit both rotation representations; claiming that such a pass makes no commit would contradict the required dual-write compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- new `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (docstring only)
- focused unit/integration/CLI tests

Estimated scope: M. Depends on closed A1 through the parent story.
baseline.summary: A2-1 implementation: extract and persist GET-rotation sidecar

baseline.description:
## Finding (audit of epic 3405-c0b7)
**Site:** the gate degrade producers in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` (via the `except (LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError)` arm at line 203), `_degraded_code_review_verdict` (line ~336 sets `"llm_unavailable": True`), and the completion-verdict degrade. They emit `coverage.llm_unavailable = True`.

**Problem:** the arm catches `(LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError)` together (comment at line 203 folds `LLMInputRejectedError`, bug 43d4, into "the mid-run infra outage" arm). So when the cause is an INPUT REJECTION (oversized/malformed prompt, content-policy refusal), the verdict still carries `coverage.llm_unavailable=True`. The field's docstring admits the name is overloaded to mean "no provider record accompanies this verdict" (degraded), NOT literally "the provider is down".

**Wrong signal:** `coverage.llm_unavailable=True` for a non-availability fault. `resolution_fields(outcome)` DOES ride the truthful `resolution_class` (CHANGE_INPUT) alongside, so the disposition is recoverable — but the boolean's NAME misreports the cause.

**Consumers that branch on the boolean:** `plan_review/drift_floor.py:202`, `plan_review/orchestrator.py:468`, `review_bot/adapter.py:114`.

**Observable vs latent:** OBSERVABLE — on every degraded gate verdict JSON and to the three consumers above.

**Proposed fix (needs decision):** behavior-change / rename — either split the flag (a neutral `degraded` / `no_provider_record` boolean vs a strict `llm_unavailable` reserved for real outages) or have consumers/readers key off `resolution_class` instead of the overloaded boolean. Affects the verdict contract and three consumers → **escalate**.

**caused_by / class:** the same "input-rejection framed as provider outage" pattern; origin 8a31 / bug 43d4.

## Operator decision (approved: Option B)
Split the overloaded `coverage.llm_unavailable` boolean: keep it True ONLY for genuine availability outages; add a distinct `input_rejected` signal for `LLMInputRejectedError`. Do NOT introduce a broad `degraded`/`no_provider_record` category (operator explicitly rejected it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A single source-of-truth helper `degrade_cause_flags(error)` in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` returns mutually-exclusive coverage flags — `input_rejected=True` for `LLMInputRejectedError`, else `llm_unavailable=True` (real outages and the string-error degrade tail).
- [x] Both degrade builders emit the split signal through that helper: `_degraded_code_review_verdict` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`) and `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py`).
- [x] The three readers honor the split: `plan_review/drift_floor.py` (veto branch), `plan_review/orchestrator.py` (maps `input_rejected` to INDETERMINATE), and `review_bot/adapter.py` (non-retryable `input-rejected` coverage-gap reason, deliberately NOT in `RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS` — a deterministic input rejection is an honest fail-closed veto, not a deferred retry).
- [x] `coverage.llm_unavailable` is no longer True for an input-rejection fault; the new `input_rejected` flag carries it instead, preserving real-outage behavior unchanged.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_coverage_input_rejected_5f96.py tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_coverage_input_rejected_5f96_heldout.py -q`

baseline.description:
Store the baseline in the projection the live comparison already computes: `description` as `normalize_rich_text(raw)`, and `status`/`priority` as the Jira field's `name` string (for example, `"In Progress"` and `"High"`, never local-mapped values such as `"in_progress"` or `1`). Expected reduction is approximately 66% on the measured 18,257,550-byte predecessor file. Measured-facts trail: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4**; do not re-derive it.

## Why this is safe without a comparator change

`outbound_field_diff.py:188,197` canonicalize the remote and baseline sides through `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` (the docstring at `:183` says storage stays vendor-shaped and mapping happens at read time). `normalize_rich_text` converts an ADF dict through `adf_to_text` and passes a string through unchanged. For priority/status, `map_remote_to_local` extracts the Jira `name` through `_extract_jira_field_value`, then keys `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_PRIORITY` or `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` on that exact name; status also honors a `rebar-status:` label branch, which is absent from baselines. Therefore exact Jira-name scalars such as `"High"` and `"In Progress"` and their vendor dicts reach the same live comparison values. The pre-A3 reader also accepts the scalar form, which is the rollback seam.

An earlier plan incorrectly cited `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields`; they have no production callers. All behavioral oracles below cross the live `compute_update_fields` path instead.

## Why assignee is excluded

`_assignee_candidates` in `outbound_field_diff.py` builds a candidate set from the scalar plus every non-None identity form, and `_suppressed_by_inbound` routes assignee through `_assignee_matches`. Collapsing the vendor dict to one string would remove identity forms and could make local-wins overwrite a concurrent remote assignee edit. The implementation must preserve the assignee value, presence bit, and dict/scalar/null shape exactly.

## Implementation steps and exact oracles

1. In `inbound_fields.py`, add one projection helper used only by baseline writes. It returns
   `normalize_rich_text(value)` for `description`; the exact Jira `name` string for
   `status` and `priority`; and the input unchanged for every other field. It is idempotent for
   already-scalar values and preserves field absence.
2. In `BindingStore.set_baseline`, retain the existing mirrored-field allowlist and write-when-equal
   guard, but project each present field through that helper before equality comparison and storage.
   Do not project `summary` or `assignee`, and do not add a migration pass or comparator change.
3. Happy-path unit oracle:
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py::test_set_baseline_normalizes_vendor_text_shapes_but_keeps_assignee_raw`
   writes an ADF description plus Jira status/priority dicts through a real `BindingStore` and
   asserts the exact persisted baseline is description `"hello baseline"`, priority `"High"`,
   status `"In Progress"`, with the complete three-identity assignee dict unchanged.
4. Held-out live-comparison oracle:
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py` creates two real
   `BindingStore` instances, one from ADF/Jira dict values and one from their scalar equivalents.
   It calls `compute_update_fields` with the real `JiraBackend` inbound/outbound mappers and asserts
   both exact results are `{}` and the stored baselines are equal. The same file parameterizes
   exactly three local assignee identities (`ada@example.test`, `acct-ada`, `Ada Lovelace`); for
   each, Jira carries a different assignee and the oracle asserts no outbound field is emitted and
   the complete baseline assignee dict remains unchanged. A partial-input case asserts idempotence
   and that absent summary/assignee fields remain absent.
5. Stateful integration oracle:
   `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_normalization.py` initializes a real temporary
   git repository, binds one Jira key, and runs `_advance_baselines` with ADF/Jira-shaped data. It
   asserts the exact serialized baseline contains scalar description/status/priority and the raw
   assignee dict. It commits that state, runs the same production seam with scalar equivalents, and
   asserts byte-identical `bindings.json` plus a clean git worktree. Production imports remain
   inside the test function so full-suite collection first establishes the unit test package's
   shared namespace; the collect-only command below guards this order-dependent contract.
6. The existing inbound-adopt test in
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py` asserts that the dynamic baseline
   seeding caller persists exact Jira name strings and preserves raw assignee data.
7. Repository corpus oracle:
   `scripts/measure_baseline_normalization.py` loads every baseline from the named tickets ref and
   obtains local tickets through `rebar.reduce_all_tickets`. For each local id, **mutation outcome**
   is the exact JSON-comparable object `{fields, conflicts, dropped}` returned by the live
   `compute_update_fields` path and its sinks. **Mutation delta** is the count of local ids for which
   that complete object differs between the raw-baseline store and the normalized-baseline store;
   success requires a count of zero, not a similarity score or manual inspection. The forward run
   uses current code. The rollback run exports the named pre-A3 revision with `git archive` and runs
   its code in a separate subprocess with that revision first on `PYTHONPATH`, preventing module
   cache aliasing. The command exits nonzero unless every stored baseline is compared, both delta
   counts are zero, missing/error counts are zero, assignee deltas are zero, and serialized bytes
   fall by at least 50%.

## Testing

Run from this isolated A3 worktree with its `.venv` first on `PATH`:

```sh
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py \
  tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_normalization.py

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q --collect-only

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/measure_baseline_normalization.py \
  --store-ref da937e47068898ed3fc6feae09acdfea963e1dd3 \
  --pre-a3-ref 550442ae58864f6f32b76ba78172251ba3119bb8

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q \
  tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys \
  tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py::test_check_mode_clean_against_committed_tree

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test
```

The pinned corpus command must report 1,774/1,774 baselines compared, zero forward mutation deltas, zero rollback mutation deltas, zero missing/errors, zero assignee deltas, and at least 50% size reduction. Repeat with `--store-ref origin/tickets` immediately before review upload to detect new incompatible rows. `docs/experiments/bridge-state-baseline-normalization.md` records the pinned inputs, exact result, test contract card, and reproduction command.

## Rollback and stop conditions

- Before merge, any held-out failure, corpus delta, missing/error row, assignee delta, size reduction
  below 50%, collection failure, or repository gate failure blocks upload/merge. Production remains
  unchanged.
- After merge, an unexpected production mutation verdict or reconcile error is attributable to A3
  only after the same input succeeds under the parent of the A3 merge and fails under the A3 merge.
  On that contrast, disable both reconcile workflows immediately and poll until no run is active.
  Keep them disabled while rollback is reviewed; do not attempt a live data rewrite.
- Create a Gerrit revert of the single A3 change from a fresh worktree, retain the A3 ticket trailer
  and DCO sign-off, and do not submit until `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved comment.
  If the revert cannot clear those gates, reconciliation stays disabled and the incident remains
  operator-visible; do not bypass either gate.
- Before re-enabling, run the committed A3 corpus harness against the then-current `origin/tickets`
  with `--pre-a3-ref` set to the parent of the A3 merge and require zero rollback mutation deltas,
  zero missing/errors, and zero assignee deltas. Then require one successful reconcile workflow run
  at a SHA descending from the revert merge. Existing scalar rows remain; the pre-A3 reader accepts
  both scalar and vendor dicts, so no lossy denormalization or backup restore is attempted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] The dict-shaped baseline and scalar equivalent produce the exact same live
      `compute_update_fields` verdict through real Jira mappers. Prove with the held-out test file
      and focused pytest command above.
- [x] [code-verifiable] All three assignee identity forms (email, accountId, displayName) preserve
      inbound-direction suppression and the raw baseline assignee dict. Prove with the three-case
      parameterization in the held-out test file.
- [x] [code-verifiable] One real baseline-advance pass stores scalar description/status/priority,
      exactly `"In Progress"` and `"High"`, while assignee remains a dict; an equivalent second pass
      is byte-stable and leaves git clean. Prove with the integration test above.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The pinned full-corpus command reports zero forward mutation deltas as
      operationally defined above, complete coverage, and no errors.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The same command reports zero rollback mutation deltas under separately
      exported pre-A3 code, proving the old reader accepts the normalized store.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The corpus command reports at least 50% serialized-size reduction and zero
      assignee shape/value deltas.

## Files

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py`, `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_normalization.py`, `scripts/measure_baseline_normalization.py`, and `docs/experiments/bridge-state-baseline-normalization.md`, and `docs/env-vars.md` (mechanically regenerated registry after binding_store.py line shifts).

Scope: S-M. Depends on closed A2-1 ticket `9594-1f1c-bcd1-4774` only for sequencing and the already-landed committed-format state; A3 consumes no new A2-1 symbol.
