## Context / Problem

At audited code snapshot `9a94ef9737fbdf070ae314bba6e797319aee2301`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py:166-352` `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` accepts 24 loose values spanning remote observation, transport, binding state, mapping policy, diagnostics, and mutation output. Related field-diff seams accept 14 and 11 values at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:235-475`.

Brant's typed-payload stories make mutation outputs discriminated by direction/action, but output typing alone does not guarantee that producer construction stops threading the current loose dependency bundle. Adding another mapping axis, sink, collaborator, or policy otherwise continues to require synchronized edits across builder, caller, and helper boundaries.

Provenance: janitor finding A04 (validity 1.00, impact 0.92), discovered during `literal-subaverage-dartfrog`. Commit `52d9e5f34ea3` extracted the builder for module headroom but did not decide its input ownership.

## Approach / End State

- Start from the accepted contract and typed payload union produced by
  `scummy-ultrashort-tuatara` and `earthborn-statuelike-boutu`.
- Re-census the current producer and successor seams after the typed implementation lands. If the
  cited 24-value seam has already been eliminated, record the evidence and do not create substitute
  work.
- Otherwise divide construction along the existing observation-resolution, canonical-diff,
  comment/label/link assembly, and typed-mutation construction seams so each stage receives only
  the data and collaborators it owns.
- Reuse RP-03's `Observation` / `TicketPlan`, Brant's payload contracts, and existing runtime
  bindings. A small typed request is acceptable only when its fields form one cohesive invariant;
  do not wrap the same loose bundle in a generic context, option bag, or
  `Mapping[str, Any]`.
- Keep production on the pre-cutover route in this story. `single-vast-roan` remains the owner of
  production flip and legacy-dispatch deletion.

`cascade_flag=true`: census callers, string imports, monkeypatch targets, compatibility re-exports, standalone file loading, manifests, and Cloud/DC adapter projections before changing the seam.

## Sequencing

This story starts after `earthborn-statuelike-boutu` lands the types and portable parity oracle. It must close before `single-vast-roan` flips production and deletes the legacy route.

## Testing

Use Brant's portable synthetic/scrubbed replay corpus as the main behavior oracle. Existing Cloud/DC verified-fake contracts, mutation tests, effect spies, deterministic traces, module-size, complexity, lint, and typecheck gates remain green. No live Jira or production dual-send is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A post-`earthborn-statuelike-boutu` census records the surviving mutation producers,
      callers, dynamic consumers, and the disposition of the cited 24/14/11-value seams.
      Evidence: census comment posted before any refactoring confirmed the 24/14/11-value
      seams were NOT eliminated by `earthborn-statuelike-boutu` (zero references to
      `Observation`/`TicketPlan`/`mutation_payloads`/`payload_shadow` in
      `outbound_differ.py`/`outbound_mutation_builders.py`/`outbound_field_diff.py`); a
      follow-up comment records the ADR-0107-driven disposition actually implemented.
- [x] No surviving production or shadow mutation producer retains the current 24-value loose bundle
      or merely hides it inside a generic context, option bag, or `Mapping[str, Any]`.
      Evidence: merged commit `b0239e04aacc` (Gerrit change 2456) converges
      `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` (11 -> 7 params) and
      `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` (24 -> 10 params) onto the EXISTING
      `OutboundDiffConfig` (extended with 7 pass-scoped fields), per ADR 0107 §"Disposition
      of the 23/14/11-parameter producer seams (AC7)", which explicitly rejects a new
      generic context/options bag — an initial draft that introduced one
      (`OutboundMutationContext`/`OutboundMutationSinks`) was caught in review-against-ADR
      and reverted before landing.
- [x] Observation resolution, canonical diff, ancillary-operation assembly, and typed mutation
      construction each receive only cohesive owned inputs; Brant/RP-03 domain types are reused
      rather than duplicated.
      Evidence: pass-scoped values live on `OutboundDiffConfig` (the pre-existing cohesive
      owner for this exact class of input, per its own docstring); Backend-port
      collaborators (`binding_store`, `outbound_mapper`, `inbound_mapper`,
      `assignee_resolver`) stay separate, explicit, narrow parameters per ADR 0107 point 3.
      Full `TicketPlan` population for the outbound path (the ADR's aspirational per-ticket
      grouping) was deliberately NOT attempted: `ticket_plan.py`/`observation.py` are not in
      this ticket's declared file_impact, and `jira_snapshot`/`local_parents`/
      `local_ticket_types` are genuinely pass-invariant rather than per-ticket, so they went
      onto `OutboundDiffConfig` instead — documented as an intentional, honest deviation, not
      silently skipped.
- [x] Retry, idempotency, fuse, and transport-resource ownership remain exactly where ADR 0103 and
      the existing runtime seams place them; no second owner is introduced.
      Evidence: this story touched only `outbound_differ.py` and
      `outbound_mutation_builders.py`'s parameter-threading; no retry/idempotency/fuse/transport
      code paths were modified — `client` continues to be read from the same origin
      (now via `config.client`, a pre-existing field, rather than a redundant separate
      parameter).
- [x] The portable legacy/typed corpus has zero unexplained trace or modeled-state deltas, and effect
      spies prove this story adds no production write route or dual-send path.
      Evidence: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` + `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/` +
      held-out seam/adapter-contract tests: 3831 passed, 1 skipped, zero regressions. Full
      `make test`: 18419 passed, 63 skipped; the only "failed"/"error" results traced to (a)
      8 pre-existing environment-specific failures reproduced identically on a clean stash of
      `origin/main` before this change, and (b) 3 false positives from a leftover local
      scratch file picked up by unrelated repo-hygiene checks, which pass cleanly once removed.
      No production routing changed (behavior-preserving refactor only).
- [x] Semantic and string/dynamic-reference censuses find no stale supported import, monkeypatch,
      manifest, or adapter consumer after the change.
      Evidence: repo-wide grep for `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` /
      `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` / `OutboundMutationContext` / `OutboundMutationSinks`
      / `OutboundDiffConfig` across `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` found zero stale references
      after the change (no test imports/monkeypatches these builder functions by name; the
      only non-code reference is a documentation string in
      `tests/fixtures/reconciler/payload_corpus/v1/scenarios.json`, unaffected by a signature
      change).
- [x] Focused reconciler suites, verified Cloud/DC fake contracts, module-size and complexity gates,
      lint, and typecheck pass without weakened assertions.
      Evidence: `make lint`, `make typecheck` clean; `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`:
      `active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10` (unchanged). Module sizes after change:
      `outbound_differ.py` 654 LOC, `outbound_mutation_builders.py` 386 LOC,
      `outbound_field_diff.py` 558 LOC (untouched) — all well within the 800-LOC cap.
- [x] Production cutover and legacy deletion remain unimplemented here and explicitly owned by
      `single-vast-roan`.
      Evidence: no changes to production routing/dispatch selection in this story; `3f27-cb3c-8023-4f57`
      (alias `single-vast-roan`) was not touched.

## Problem (parity sibling of the tickets-branch invariant violation)
`alert_store._atomic_write` (`alert_store.py:84`) hand-rolls `tempfile` + `os.replace` instead of the shared `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` seam — the same hand-rolled-vs-shared-seam class as `projects_store` (ticket `fea4-f98c-f1a2-4168`, LANDED). This ticket converts that one writer to the authoritative shared seam.

## Scope note — binding-snapshot conversion was ATTEMPTED and REVERTED (behavior-preserving boundary)
The original plan for this parity sweep also proposed routing `reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot` through `push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch` (which stages with `git add -A`). That conversion is **intentionally NOT part of the landed change.** A first patchset that did it FAILED CI: `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head` went red — on an unchanged second reconcile pass the binding bytes are byte-identical and `mutation_count == 0`, yet git HEAD advanced. Root cause: the seam's `git add -A` widening sweeps in OTHER per-pass `.bridge_state` state files (rotation / last-pass / peer_confirmations markers) that the original selective 5-file staging deliberately excluded, so a redundant commit is created and reconcile idempotency is broken. That is a real behavioral change, which falls OUTSIDE the approved scope ("call the authoritative seam AS-IS, only where it is behavior-preserving"). The binding-snapshot path therefore keeps its original selective-staging raw-git implementation unchanged. Only the `alert_store` conversion (below), which is genuinely behavior-preserving, landed.

## Use the EXISTING seam (NO new facade, NO redesign) — same as ticket fea4
`rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` — the shared crash-atomic write.

## Approach — alert_store._atomic_write -> fsutil.atomic_write (RESIDENCY = LOCAL SCRATCH)
`alert_store` writes to `repo_root/bridge_state/bridge_alerts` (NO dot), which `.gitignore` (`bridge_state/`) ignores and which is NOT tracked on the tickets branch (only the dotted `.bridge_state/*` is). So the alert files are local scratch: `fsutil.atomic_write` ALONE is correct — NO publish/commit path is added.
- The current `_atomic_write` does `parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` before writing;
  `fsutil.atomic_write` does NOT create the destination directory. KEEP an explicit
  `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` immediately before the call, then
  `fsutil.atomic_write(path, content, permissions=0o600, fsync=True)` to preserve exact
  serialized bytes, mode `0o600` (mkstemp default, no chmod today), and fsync-before-replace
  durability.

## Constraints — BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING
No functional change beyond seam adoption: same on-disk alert bytes/mode, same missing-parent handling. Reuse the existing seam ONLY; add no helper.

## Testing / Verification
- RED-first byte-identity test that `fsutil.atomic_write` produces the same file contents and
  `0o600` mode as the removed hand-rolled path, and that the write succeeds when the parent dir
  does not pre-exist (guards the retained `mkdir`).
- Reconcile idempotency remains green (proving the binding-snapshot path was left unchanged):
  `python -m pytest tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py -q`.
- Proving commands (all must pass): `make lint`; `make typecheck`;
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -q` (modulo the known-unrelated
  `state/test_ref_lock.py::test_ac0_blob_ref_roundtrips_through_remote` flake).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `alert_store._atomic_write` is replaced by `fsutil.atomic_write` with a retained
      `parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`; residency determined = local scratch
      (documented); no publish path; exact bytes + `0o600` mode + fsync preserved.
      Verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_alert_store_atomic_write.py -q`.
- [x] The binding-snapshot commit path is left UNCHANGED (raw selective-staging), so reconcile
      idempotency is preserved (no redundant commit on an unchanged second pass).
      Verified by `python -m pytest tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head -q`.
- [x] No functional/behavioral change beyond the alert_store seam adoption.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -q`
      all pass (modulo the known-unrelated `state/test_ref_lock.py` flake).

## Sequencing
Depends on fea4 (LANDED). Edits `alert_store.py` (+ its test) only — disjoint from A/C/D.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Once a store actually syncs more than one tracker project, an older rebar binary reading it is dangerous rather than merely limited: it would fetch only its single configured project, see every other project's bound tickets as having no corresponding remote issue, and create duplicate issues in the wrong project. There is a shipped mechanism for exactly this — `.store-compat.json` with a fail-closed read (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`) — but `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is still an empty frozenset (`compat.py:60`), so no capability has ever been declared through it.

## Approach

Register `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. That single addition is what makes a binary able to *recognise* the capability; a binary that predates it hits the "required capability this binary does not provide" branch and raises `StoreIncompatibleError`, refusing writes rather than corrupting the store (`docs/migrations.md:158-165`).

This is the expand half of the expand/contract rollout `docs/migrations.md:138-149` describes: teach binaries to read and fail closed **before** anything writes the requirement. Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story, so shipping it changes no behaviour for any existing store. The conditional stamp lands separately, which is why the two are ordered rather than combined.

Reads deliberately stay available: the gate is on the write lock only (`docs/migrations.md:174-178`), so `list`/`show`/`search` keep working against a store an old binary may not write, and `fsck` surfaces the condition as a structured `compat_error` without changing its exit code.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's pure-branch row: an in-process unit test against the real classification function, since the mechanism is entirely a validation branch with no I/O of its own — plus one real-store test for the write-gate, because the gate fires inside lock acquisition and a unit test would not cross that component.

- Happy path: a record declaring `multi-project-bridge` classifies as compatible on a binary that
  registers it.
- Contrast case: a record declaring an unregistered capability name still raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError` — proving the registration widened the known set by exactly one entry and
  did not disable the check.
- Absent-record regression: a store with no `.store-compat.json` still passes through as implicit
  legacy, so pre-feature stores are unaffected.
- Write-gate path: a store whose record declares an unknown capability refuses a write through the
  real lock acquisition, while `list`/`show` against the same store still succeed. The read half is
  the contrast case that proves the gate is scoped to writes.
- Corrupt-record path: a malformed record still raises rather than being treated as absent, which is
  the bypass the gate is designed to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `multi-project-bridge` is in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` and a record declaring it classifies as
      compatible; checked by a unit test over the classification function.
- [ ] A record declaring an unregistered capability still raises `StoreIncompatibleError`; checked by
      the paired negative case.
- [ ] A store with no compat record still passes through as implicit legacy; checked by an
      absent-record regression test.
- [ ] A store declaring an unknown capability refuses writes while reads still succeed; checked by a
      real-store test exercising the write lock and a read command against the same store.
- [ ] A corrupt record raises rather than being treated as absent; checked by a malformed-record test.
baseline.summary: Register the multi-project-bridge store-compat capability (expand half)

baseline.description:
With a key-set prev, keys present in both prev and curr route to `_compute_mutations_emit_both` with an empty `local_fields`, producing ~516 mutations per pass that are provably inert but not free. Skip them. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Each inert mutation still traverses `_apply_one`, which calls `_recheck_drift` -> `concurrency.snapshot_head(repo_root)` — **a `git rev-parse` subprocess per mutation**. So ~516 extra git invocations per pass, ~516 `RECON: batch_outcome` stderr lines, ~516 outcome records in the manifest, and an inflated `mutation_count` so a converged pass reports 516 instead of 0. It also enlarges the HEAD-drift window. Under `BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` (cap 10) or `BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE` (cap 100) these compete for cap slots with genuine work (`apply_planning.py:90-101`) and can starve it — production defaults to `LIVE` (cap `None`), so that risk is latent, not live.

## Approach
Short-circuit `_compute_mutations_emit_both` when `local_fields` is falsy, or equivalently skip the `_emit` at `differ.py:590` when the resolved `changed` dict contains no field that survives `_mutation_to_batch_dict`. ~5 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With a key-set prev over a real corpus, `(outbound, update)` mutations with an empty effective
      payload are **0** (down from ~516). Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations` + the corpus script.
- [ ] Mutations with a genuine non-empty effective payload are still emitted unchanged — the
      negative control. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `mutation_count` on a converged pass is 0. Tier: **integration** asserting the pass record.
- [ ] `git rev-parse` invocation count per pass drops correspondingly. Tier: **integration** with a
      counting shim.

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/differ.py`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A4-2.

baseline.description:
## Suspected sibling of 7dea-2f00-db57-4a96 (completion-cache shared-tmp collision)

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py::save_checkpoint` writes `tmp = d / f'.tmp-{envelope.digest}.json'` then `tmp.replace(path)`, where `_checkpoint_dir` is `.rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket_id>` — keyed by ticket only, NOT run-scoped. Two concurrent plan-review workers saving a checkpoint for the SAME (ticket, digest) therefore target the SAME temp file: both write it, both call `tmp.replace(path)`, and the second raises `FileNotFoundError` (the first replace consumed the temp), which the outer `except Exception: return False` swallows — a silently lost checkpoint. This is the exact construct proven in 7dea (shared deterministic temp name + concurrent writers), in a different subsystem.

## Mandatory reproduction before remediation
Mirror 7dea's experiment: drive two concurrent save_checkpoint writers for the same ticket+digest with a barrier forcing both temp writes before either replace; capture each writer's return value, suppressed exceptions, final JSON validity, and orphaned temp files. Include a cross-process case.

## Remediation if reproduced
Same fix shape as 7dea: unique same-directory temp via a stdlib tempfile primitive (`tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d, ...)`), retain atomic replace onto the shared final `<digest>.json`, and bounded cleanup of only the writer's own temp on failure. No contract/output change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A deterministic two-writer experiment proves or falsifies the collision (thread + cross-process).
- [ ] If reproduced, a RED regression test fails against the shared `.tmp-<digest>.json` implementation before the fix.
- [ ] If reproduced, writers use unique same-directory temp paths and atomically replace the shared final key; concurrent stress leaves one valid record, no partial, no residue.
- [ ] If falsified, no production change; close with the falsifying evidence.
baseline.summary: plan-review checkpoint save_checkpoint shares a .tmp-<digest>.json path across concurrent same-ticket writers

baseline.description:
`scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` exits 1 on current `origin/main`:

```
planning-corpus check: corpus=114 (want 113); missed=[]; mechanical_fp=[]; FAIL
```

Reproduced UNCHANGED on a pristine detached worktree at `origin/main` (with the tracker symlinked in), so this is not caused by ticket 1dd5's change: the flagged set is still exactly `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE` (`missed=[]`, `mechanical_fp=[]`); only the corpus SIZE arm fails.

## Context / Problem

Root cause shape: the corpus is described in the module docstring as 'pinned and reproducible', but it is re-derived at run time from LIVE ticket state — the ancestors of `PLANNING_CORPUS_BOUNDARY` whose subject prefix resolves to a ticket whose CURRENT `ticket_type` is `bug` (`_resolve_bug_ticket` -> `_ticket_type`). Reclassifying any historical ticket to/from `bug`, or adding a ticket that changes short-prefix resolution, moves the count. `PLANNING_CORPUS_SIZE = 113` is therefore a constant asserted against a moving derivation.

Nothing in CI or the test suite runs this script, so the drift went unnoticed.

## Approach

Pin the corpus by IDENTITY, not count: replace `PLANNING_CORPUS_SIZE = 113` with a `PLANNING_CORPUS_COMMITS` frozenset of the exact 113 commit SHAs the planning analysis adjudicated (recovered by re-running the derivation in `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` `main()` against the tracker's historical state at the pin commit 1920dc9fe559 / tickets branch 94ec395ee9b2, via the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` override in `src/rebar/config.py:tracker_dir`). In `--check-planning-corpus` mode, iterate those pinned SHAs directly (measuring each with the existing `_measure`) instead of re-deriving membership from live ticket state; assert the measured set's identity equals the pin and the flagged set equals `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE` exactly. Per-row ticket labels stay best-effort resolved for the artifact only — they no longer gate. This fits the problem because the adjudication was a one-time, hand-reviewed judgment over a fixed commit set; identity pinning is the only assertion shape immune to tracker churn. Align the module docstring so 'pinned and reproducible' matches what the code actually does.

## Scope

- `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` — pin the 113 SHAs, derive check-mode rows from the pin, align the docstring.

## Testing

Mechanical constant + control-flow change to a standalone analysis script that nothing in CI or the test suite imports; the executable proof is the script's own check mode: `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` exits 0 (happy path), and the check still fails (exit 1) if the flagged set diverges from `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE` — verified by inspection of the retained assertion arm.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` exits 0 on `origin/main`, OR the size assertion is replaced by one that does not depend on live ticket state (e.g. pin the 113 SHAs, not the count). Checked by running the command in the worktree and observing exit 0.
- [x] The decision is recorded in the script's docstring so the 'pinned and reproducible' claim matches what the code does. Checked by reading the updated docstring.
baseline.summary: backtest --check-planning-corpus pin drifts: corpus=114, want 113

## Target
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — **800 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (0 lines of headroom).

This file is AT the cap. Any edit at all currently fails CI.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [x] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [x] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [x] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [x] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

baseline.description:
## Why

A re-fired container review re-litigates delivered AC (false BLOCKs / stale coaching). We need a
deterministic gate that drops those findings without hiding anything live — mirroring the novelty
floor (ADR 0008) and drift-refresh (ADR 0002).

## What

Add a third Pass-3 floor in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (`pass3_decide`) that, using the
completion sub-answers (story: Pass-2 sub-call) and the delivered-now predicate (story:
delivered-now), DROPS a finding iff ALL hold: attribution = a delivered-now child AND
containment = limited-to-closed AND layer = plan-semantics AND priority (validity x impact) < floor
AND the criterion is NOT in the always-preserve set (config-backed `verify.completion_preserve_criteria`; default the registered security overlay T5c + contract criterion T10). Recompute every run (never persist a drop). Record each
drop to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`sidecar.py`) joinable by finding id. Gate behind a
`verify.completion_floor_active` evidence-gate flag + a `verify.completion_priority_floor` in
`src/rebar/config.py` (VerifyConfig), defaulting inert — the total back-out, exactly like the
novelty flags.

## Scope

- IN: the Pass-3 drop predicate; the config keys; sidecar `floored` recording; the deterministic
  aggregation of the three sub-answers + priority + structural criterion class.
- OUT: the sub-questions themselves (separate story); the delivered-now predicate (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pass3_decide` drops iff attribution=delivered-now AND containment=limited-to-closed AND layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND the finding's criterion is NOT in the always-preserve set; all other combinations keep.
- [ ] Suppression is inert unless `verify.completion_floor_active` is true; `verify.completion_priority_floor` is configurable (mirrors `novelty_priority_floor`).
- [ ] Every drop is written to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (joinable by finding id) and is recomputed each run (no persisted suppression).
- [ ] The always-preserve set is CONFIG-BACKED (`verify.completion_preserve_criteria`) referencing REGISTERED criterion IDs — default {T5c security overlay, T10 endpoint/interface contract}; adding privacy/compliance is a config change, not code (T8/T5e).
- [ ] Completion drops carry a distinct `drop_reason="completion"` in the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (vs novelty `"novelty"` / normal), so `plan_review_result_v1` offline joins never collide (G6).
- [ ] A finding on a preserve-set (T5c/T10) criterion is never dropped regardless of the other axes.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the truth table (each single-condition flip preserves the finding).

## Worked example (suppression boundary)

Epic mid-flight; child X = closed+attested, child Y = open.
- "X's AC wording for step 3 is ambiguous" -> attribution=X(delivered-now), containment=limited-to-closed, layer=plan-semantics, priority<floor, criterion=COH -> DROPPED (settled plan text).
- "X's step-3 mechanism conflicts with Y's planned approach" -> containment=spans-open -> KEPT.
- "X's delivered contract omits an error field consumers rely on" -> layer=delivered-functionality -> KEPT.
- "X's endpoint has no auth" (T5c) -> criterion in {security} veto -> KEPT regardless of the other axes.
- If X was force-closed (not attested) -> delivered-now=False -> every finding on X KEPT.

## Acceptance Criteria (durable record + invariants)

- [ ] A durable ADR `docs/adr/0024-completion-aware-container-plan-review.md` codifies the contracts: the three-field sub-answer schema + closed enums, the `delivered-now` predicate, the completion-floor drop rule + config knobs, and the sidecar `drop_reason` field (inline AC + session log are not the durable record).
- [ ] The Pass-3 floor consumes the exact enum value `containment=="limited-to-closed"` (no value drift vs the sub-call).

## Acceptance Criteria (sidecar schema + ADR cross-refs)

- [ ] `_slim()` in `sidecar.py` gains a `drop_reason` field (enum {`null`, `"completion"`, `"novelty"`}): `null` for surfaced/normal findings, `"completion"` for completion-floor drops, `"novelty"` for novelty-floor drops; it lives in the per-finding slim payload and is the join key that disambiguates the two floors offline.
- [ ] ADR 0008 (novelty floor) and ADR 0002 (drift-refresh path) are updated with a cross-reference to ADR 0024 so the three Pass-3 floors/paths are documented as one coherent set (no standalone/misleading floor reference).
baseline.summary: Pass-3 completion floor: deterministic drop of delivered re-litigation + config evidence-gate

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Measurement 50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92 found the recorded caused_by edges cannot be partitioned into blame-derived guesses vs explicitly supplied attributions: `_apply_caused_by` (src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py) writes both origins through `_write_link_event` with no provenance field, so on read a guessed edge is indistinguishable from a proven one and the escaped-defect consumers (`rebar metrics` bug_trends lens, the epic-close caused_by floor) weight them identically. The operator accepted this proposal — see the OPERATOR DECISION comment on this ticket — so this ticket now implements the marker. It builds directly on the merged caused_by target validation (change 2125, ticket 77e7-1eec-7b52-46ed).

## Approach

Add an OPTIONAL `provenance` field to the caused_by LINK event payload, value `"derived"` (blame auto-derivation) or `"explicit"` (operator/agent-supplied). Old events carry no field and read as unknown — no migration is needed: the dep schema (`common.schema.json` `$defs/dep`) already allows additional properties, and the reducer surfaces the field present-only (the same pattern as the comment `source_*` provenance fields).

- `rebar.graph._links._write_link_event` gains an optional `provenance` parameter, included in
  the LINK event data only when set.
- `transition_close._apply_caused_by` passes `"explicit"` when the close carried a non-empty
  `--caused-by`, `"derived"` when the culprit came from `blame.derive_caused_by`. No change to
  the deriver's fail-closed behaviour (the strict-majority abstention stays as designed).
- `add_dependency` (the `rebar link` path shared by CLI/library/MCP) marks caused_by writes
  `"explicit"` — a linked attribution is supplied by the caller, never blame-derived. Other
  relations are unchanged (no field written).
- `reducer/_processors.py process_link` copies `provenance` onto the dep entry present-only,
  so replay of old unmarked events yields the exact prior dep shape.
- `common.schema.json` documents the optional enum on the dep def.
- `rebar metrics`: bug_trends rows carry per-edge provenance and a new STOCK dimension
  `bug_caused_by_provenance` reports the explicit/derived/unknown edge counts, so escape-rate
  consumers can weight proven attributions above guessed ones. `bug_caused_by_fan_in` keeps
  its existing shape.

## Scope

- src/rebar/graph/_links.py — `_write_link_event` provenance param; `add_dependency` marks
  caused_by explicit.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py — `_apply_caused_by` selects derived vs explicit.
- src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py — `process_link` surfaces the field present-only.
- src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json — optional `provenance` property on the dep def.
- src/rebar/metrics/bug_trends.py — per-edge provenance in rows + the
  `bug_caused_by_provenance` dimension.
- docs/event-schema.md, docs/user-guide.md — document the marker and the new dimension.
- tests/unit/test_caused_by_provenance.py (new) — write-site and replay coverage.
- tests/unit/metrics/test_bug_trends.py — the new dimension's derivation.

## Testing

Unit tests, written RED-first: (1) a bug close with an EMPTY `--caused-by` and a stubbed blame culprit writes the edge with provenance `"derived"`; (2) a close with an explicit `--caused-by` writes `"explicit"`; (3) `rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by` writes `"explicit"`; (4) legacy/failure path — replay of a pre-marker LINK event (no field) reduces to a dep entry WITHOUT a provenance key (shape unchanged, reduction succeeds), and blame returning no culprit still writes nothing; (5) `bug_caused_by_provenance` counts explicit/derived/unknown edges and returns None when no caused_by edges exist (the unavailable/empty path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both transition_close write origins populate the marker: unit tests assert `"derived"`
      on the blame path and `"explicit"` on the `--caused-by` path.
- [x] `rebar link … caused_by` marks `"explicit"`: unit test asserts the dep entry's field.
- [x] Old unmarked events read as unknown: a replay unit test shows the dep entry carries no
      provenance key and reduction succeeds unchanged.
- [x] `rebar metrics` distinguishes supplied vs derived edges: the bug_trends lens gains
      `bug_caused_by_provenance` with explicit/derived/unknown counts, asserted by unit test.
- [x] docs/event-schema.md documents the marker and docs/user-guide.md lists the new
      dimension: verified by reading the landed diff.
baseline.summary: Proposal: provenance marker (derived vs explicit) on caused_by link events

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Operator ruling (recorded in comments, 2026-08-22): option (b) approved. The 0707 dense-banking eval (`tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py`) is re-scoped to SYSTEM-level boundedness: the oracle counts durable banking events regardless of actor — genuine model `record_criterion_verdict` upserts AND the policy's silent bounded-fallback insufficiency snapshots — and asserts progress is durably banked at bounded evidence-response intervals. No steering nudge is added to production; the model's voluntary banking cadence is explicitly no longer the measured contract.

Why: commit e1352535ace (ticket dd41-239d-6e09-4a86) deliberately let batched governed evidence reads execute and removed the COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE pressure that had made the model interleave genuine records. Post-merge run 32575679530 proved the system bound still holds (the policy's per-criterion 3-response fallbacks fire on schedule, source="fallback", snapshots one response low per the documented ordering caveat: 2/5/8), but the eval's observer counts only source=="tool" writes, so the model's genuine first banks at responses [6,7,8,9,9] fail the 3-response bound 3/3 deterministically. The observer's actor filter is the last stale facet of the pre-dd41 contract.

## Approach

Test-only change; no production code. In the shared seam `tests/_bank_observer.py`, re-scope `make_observed_upsert`'s bookkeeping from `source == "tool"` to any durable run-time bank write regardless of source, EXCLUDING cache seeds (`seeded=True` marks pre-run cache seeding, not run progress). Keep the bounded-gap oracle (`bounded_bank_gaps`) unchanged — it already bounds first-bank gaps in evidence responses. Update the module docstring, the eval's docstring, and the oracle regression's docstring to name the ruled contract (system-level boundedness, operator ruling on this ticket). Update the unit regressions:

- `tests/unit/test_completion_bank_observer_forwarding.py`: the first-write bookkeeping test now
  asserts a fallback-sourced write IS recorded and a seeded write is NOT.
- `tests/unit/test_completion_banking_oracle.py`: add a GREEN case proving a fallback-only
  transcript (model never records; the REAL policy fail-closes every criterion at its
  per-criterion 3-response boundary, observed snapshots [2,5,8,11,14]) passes the oracle; add a
  RED case proving the oracle in final form REJECTS a genuinely-unbounded system (fallback
  disabled via a no-op fallback_record, model banks only after 6 evidence responses →
  first gap > 3); add a replay of the live run-32575679530 shape (silent fallbacks + genuine
  records from response 6) proving it is GREEN under the ruled scope.

Validation limit: the live bedrock arm cannot run locally. Local validation is the stub replay through the REAL `wrap_completion_evidence_policy` (the proven [2/5/8] fallback snapshot schedule gives gaps within bound 3). Live confirmation lands on the next scheduled/dispatched external-integration run.

## Scope

- tests/_bank_observer.py
- tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py
- tests/unit/test_completion_banking_oracle.py
- tests/unit/test_completion_bank_observer_forwarding.py

## Testing

`python -m pytest tests/unit/test_completion_banking_oracle.py tests/unit/test_completion_bank_observer_forwarding.py -q` in the worktree venv; external module collects cleanly. Strict test-modification order: the revised oracle+observer are seen RED in final form against a genuinely-unbounded transcript (no-op fallback, late model banks) before the change counts; mutation check re-runs the GREEN fallback-only case with the gap bound dropped to confirm teeth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `make_observed_upsert` records the first durable bank write of each criterion regardless
  of `source`, excluding `seeded=True` cache seeds, verified by the updated forwarding
  regression.
- [x] A fallback-only transcript through the REAL policy (snapshots [2,5,8,11,14]) PASSES the
  oracle, and the live run-32575679530 shape (fallbacks at 2/5 + genuine records from response

baseline.description:
Build the one-time strip as a committed operational script, and prove it on a scratch clone before any window. **No new dependency**: `git-filter-repo` is deliberately not used. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why stock plumbing
`git fast-export --no-data --signed-tags=strip --export-marks=old.marks tickets` | filter | `git fast-import --export-marks=new.marks`. Verified on the real branch: the stream carries `M 100644 <sha> <path>` with **zero** inline blob data (26 MB stream for ~49,900 commits), so the filter is line-oriented text processing that never moves the ~1 GiB. No `deleteall`; no tags in a branch export (so `--signed-tags=strip` is a harmless no-op); merges ride `merge :n`; **empty commits are kept**, so DAG topology and every file's introduction point survive — which is exactly what ancestry-based authorship verification needs. filter-repo would prune them and reshape the graph.

**Proven result:** 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%), all commits and all merge commits preserved, HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths, ~30 s end to end.

## Required corrections (each was a real defect found in review)
1. Must run in a fresh **UNFILTERED** clone — `fast-import` hard-fails `fatal: blob not found` in a
   `blob:none` partial clone, and this host's `origin` is one.
2. Strip **both** `.bridge_state/` **and** `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` prefixes — B6 removes the
   latter at HEAD only; its 33 MB stays in history.
3. **Derive the re-add set DYNAMICALLY** — `git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state/` —
   never a hardcoded list. It is three files today but **A2-1 adds `get_rotation.json`**, so at window
   time it is four; a hardcoded list would fail the tree-identity assertion.
4. The filter must be **`data <n>`-length-aware**, not `grep -v`: commit messages live inside `data`
   blocks. (Today 0 of ~49,900 messages begin with `M `/`D `, but the script must not rely on that.)
5. Push with **`--force-with-lease`**, never `--force` — the remote tip moves constantly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a scratch unfiltered clone, the script produces a rewritten branch whose **commit count and
      merge-commit count are unchanged** (measured at run time, not hardcoded). Tier: **repo-level
      assertion in the dry-run harness**.
- [ ] `rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree}` **equals** the old tip tree after the dynamic re-add. Tier:
      **repo-level assertion**. This is the "not one byte of live content changed" invariant.
- [ ] The re-add set is discovered from `ls-tree`, proven by a fixture where a 4th `.bridge_state`
      file exists. Tier: **integration** with a synthetic 4-file store.
- [ ] Pack size drops to <=15% of the original. Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] The filter preserves a commit message that begins with `M ` (adversarial fixture). Tier:
      **unit** on the stream filter.
- [ ] The script refuses to run in a partial clone, with a clear message. Tier: **integration**
      against a `--filter=blob:none` clone.
- [ ] All assertions run **before** any push; the script has no push step of its own.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reclaim-bridge-history.sh` (or `.py`), dry-run harness, tests

Scope: M. No code dependencies; must exist before A6-1.
baseline.summary: A6-0c: build and dry-run the history-strip script using stock git plumbing

baseline.description:
## Refuted premise (as originally filed)

Filed as: current `origin/main` fails the locked complexity gate because `close_ticket` in `transition_close.py` reports 19 against a recorded ceiling of 17, to be fixed by extracting along a seam.

**That is false, and the suggested remedy would have changed working code without unblocking anyone.** Verified:

* main tip `07e76a1ce3`: ruff reports `close_ticket` at **17**, and
  `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records **17**. `--check` on a clean checkout returns
  `active=60 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
* the sha in the report, `104dc4e10a`: code **19**, recorded ceiling **19**.

Neither tree contains a 19-vs-17 mismatch. There is nothing in `close_ticket` to extract.

## The real defect

CI runs `--lock`, not `--check`. `lock_against_base` (`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:455`) compares the CHANGE's baseline against **main TIP**: a REMOVED entry or a LOWERED ceiling is allowed; a RAISED ceiling or a NEW entry is a violation needing an administrator.

Change 1673 (merged `8f6b6c9356`) extracted the signing tail from `close_ticket`, taking it 19 -> 17, and drained the stale baseline entry 19 -> 17. Lowering is allowed, so it passed. But every OPEN change whose tree still carries the pre-1673 baseline now presents ceiling 19 against main's 17 — which the lock reads as RAISING it.

**Verbatim reproduction.** Feeding main-tip ceilings as `base` and `104dc4e10a`'s as `branch` into `lock_against_base` returns exactly one violation:

```
ceiling RAISED for 'src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py::close_ticket': 17 -> 19 —
an administrator must override the gate to raise a ceiling
```

That is the reported symptom, verbatim. The same call with a rebased branch returns ZERO.

So the gate cannot distinguish "this branch RAISED a ceiling" from "main LOWERED it underneath an un-rebased branch". It blames the branch for a change main made. This is not specific to 1673: **every future ceiling reduction on main will break the fleet identically**, so the shrink-only ratchet currently punishes the shrinking it exists to reward. A change that never touches the baseline is still hit, because it still carries the old FILE.

Immediate operational unblock (no code, no admin): affected changes REBASE onto current main.

## Direction

Compare the branch against **`merge-base(main, HEAD)`** rather than main tip, so only entries the BRANCH itself changed can violate.

* `_fetch_base_ceilings_from_main` (`:494`) currently fetches `--depth=1`, which is too
  shallow to compute a merge base. Fetch main with enough history, and if the local checkout
  is shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`) deepen it before retrying.
* Read the baseline at the merge-base commit and use it as `base`. `lock_against_base`'s rules
  are unchanged — only the base it is given changes.
* **Fallback direction matters.** If a merge base still cannot be computed, fall back to
  today's main-tip comparison with an explicit note. That fallback is STRICTER, never looser:
  it can only over-report, so an unavailable merge base can never let a genuine ceiling raise
  through. Fail-closed posture is preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An un-rebased branch carrying the pre-reduction baseline PASSES the lock after main
      lowers a ceiling — verified by a test reproducing exactly that scenario
- [x] A branch that genuinely RAISES a ceiling relative to its merge base still FAILS —
      verified by a test
- [x] A branch that adds a NEW entry still FAILS — verified by a test
- [x] A ceiling LOWERED or an entry REMOVED by the branch still passes — verified by a test
- [x] When no merge base can be computed the gate falls back to the main-tip comparison and
      says so, never silently passing a genuine raise — verified by a test
baseline.summary: complexity lock compares against main tip instead of merge base, so ceiling reductions on main break every un-rebased branch

**Licensed outcome, reverified against the CURRENT tree (post-prerequisite):** the prerequisite [rebar:patriotic-valued-hog] already concluded, with a full effect/resource boundary timeline and consumer census, that "no restructuring of `run()`'s ownership is warranted right now" — every extracted concern already has exactly one owner in `agent_call.py`/`providers.py`/ `model_classes.py`/`structured_run.py`/`runner_support.py`, and `run()`'s remaining lines are irreducible orchestration glue, not a movable cluster. **fe75 disposition:** the prerequisite's research also found one genuine gap — a raise inside `_findings.finalize_outcome` (runner.py, outside both the `ProviderSession` `with`-block and the failure-accounting `try/except`) skips `record_call_spend`/`interpret_failure`/ `step_failures.record`. ## Acceptance Criteria

## Why
The "select prompts AND scripted ops / author in place" half of the vision: compose by selecting from a typed palette, and author new prompts in the UI.

## What
- TYPED PALETTE / INSERTION: insert a new step by selecting EITHER a scripted op OR a prompt from a
  typed palette (grouped by category/contract), surfaced via editor endpoints
  (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py`, `editor_assets/`). Selecting a scripted op sets `uses:`;
  selecting a prompt sets `prompt:`. (This delivers the success-criterion's "scripted ops from a typed
  palette", not only the prompt library.)
- PROMPT LIBRARY: dropdown listing built-in + project prompts (from the derived index + project dir).
- CREATE a new prompt and EDIT prompt text in the UI. On Save, write-back AUTO-DETECTS a writable
  `nava-rebar` source checkout (pyproject `[project].name == nava-rebar` AND a writable
  `src/rebar/llm/...` path -> edit the packaged `.md`) else writes a `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` project
  override; SHOW the resolved target path before Save. Writes are ATOMIC (write-temp + rename) through
  S2's canonical writer, and creating/editing a prompt REGENERATES the derived index.
- NON-HAPPY PATHS (explicit): refuse + clear error when NEITHER a writable source checkout NOR a
  writable project dir exists; id COLLISION on create-new (refuse/confirm-overwrite); discarding
  unsaved edits; an empty/invalid prompt id.
- Round-trip golden tests prove no corruption on authored/edited prompts.

## Scope
In: typed palette (op+prompt insertion) + library + create/edit + atomic write-back + non-happy-paths + index regen + tests. Out: properties-panel structured fields (S8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The typed palette inserts a scripted op (sets `uses:`) AND a prompt (sets `prompt:`); the prompt dropdown lists built-in + project prompts.
- [ ] Create-new + edit-text persist via S2's writer with an ATOMIC write; write-back target auto-detected and the resolved path shown; packaged write refused when read-only.
- [ ] Non-happy paths handled: neither-location-writable error, id collision, discard-unsaved, invalid id — each surfaces a clear error (no silent corruption); round-trip tests pass.
- [ ] Authoring/editing a prompt regenerates the derived index (no stale index).
- [ ] A browser e2e exercises palette insert (op + prompt) / create / edit / Save.
- [ ] The palette groups by the CLOSED category vocabulary from the prompt model (review/verifier/transform/code/exploration); the insertion mechanism is specified (a bpmn-js palette/context-pad entry or a custom insertion panel) and inserts a valid `uses:`/`prompt:` step.
baseline.summary: Editor prompt library + authoring/write-back (select + create + edit in place)

## Context / Problem
The workflow editor currently presents authored YAML/BPMN configuration without a trustworthy view of the effective criteria policy derived from built-ins plus project overlays. RP-06 adds an immutable derived policy and an explicit project applicability rule; exposing derived state as if it were editable topology would create a second policy authority and make misconfiguration difficult to diagnose.

## Approach
Extend the workflow-editor server to obtain the S1 `CriteriaSnapshot` for the selected repository and expose a narrow, read-only Effective Policy view. Keep Authored Workflow as the only editable YAML/BPMN topology. The effective view shows snapshot digest/source, criterion id, gate, execution tier, effective posture/threshold, applicability summary, enabled/disabled state, and a concise derived reason. It never serializes edits back into workflow or project routing.

At authoring/save validation, a new `project.*` code-review LLM criterion must have a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative `applies_to` globs. The editor rejects an empty/missing selector with the exact `["**"]` repository-wide remedy. Built-in entries, project DET criteria, and plan-review criteria retain their distinct trigger authoring controls and are not forced through this field.

Keep stored execution trace and per-call debugging detail out of the editor response. The Effective Policy panel is configuration provenance, not a review-result/status viewer. Repository or validation errors fail the save or mark the effective view unavailable with a located, actionable message; they do not silently display packaged defaults as effective policy.

## Rationale and Compatibility
A read-only projection makes the centralized pattern visible while preserving one authored source of topology. Older workflow files remain readable. The UI and server add fields without rewriting saved YAML/BPMN, and rollback removes the panel/endpoint while leaving authored artifacts unchanged.

## Testing
Use server contract tests with real overlay/snapshot compilation and focused editor DOM/state tests. The oracle is the serialized authored document remaining byte-equivalent while the read-only view changes with project policy. Negative controls cover built-in empty trigger semantics, project DET, and plan review. Error fixtures prove unavailable policy is explicit and save validation is fail-loud.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The editor renders distinct Authored Workflow and read-only Effective Policy sections, and no action in the effective section mutates or serializes YAML/BPMN.
- [x] Effective Policy data comes from the repository-bound `CriteriaSnapshot` and displays digest/source plus concise criterion gate, tier, posture, applicability, and enabled/disabled provenance.
- [x] Creating or saving a project code-review LLM criterion with missing, empty, non-list, or blank globs is refused with the criterion location and `use ["**"] for repository-wide` remedy.
- [x] Built-in secondary triggers, project DET selector controls, and plan-review `applies_at`/`trigger` authoring remain valid negative controls and are not subjected to the project-LLM glob rule.
- [x] A snapshot load/validation failure marks Effective Policy unavailable with an actionable located error and never substitutes packaged defaults or permits an invalid save.
- [x] Server and editor tests prove policy changes update only the derived view while authored workflow round-trips byte-equivalently.
- [x] Editor payloads contain no per-unit discovery trace, raw prompt/context body, provider response, or secret.
baseline.summary: RP-06 S6 — Separate authored workflow from effective review policy

## Context
ADR 0100 makes the immutable route registry and parser factories authoritative for command identity, grammar, and committed help. Twenty-one visible pure-intercept routes support `rebar <command> --help` but remain absent from overview help and fail under `rebar help <command>`. The `identity` child parsers disable their own help actions, so `rebar identity create --help` reaches top-level usage and exits with an error.

## Plan
- Make the help-backed predicate exactly `not route.hidden and not route.retired` in `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py`, and `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py`. Do not add route metadata.
- Add nonblank parser descriptions to `reconcile.build`, `enrich.build`, `identity.build`, and `certs.build_trusted_env` so route-owned summaries populate overview help.
- Move `_unwrap_usage` and `_collapse_metavars` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` into `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`. Apply usage unwrapping only to intercept routes without explicit parser usage. Apply metavar normalization to intercept option lines before byte normalization. Preserve the explicit multiline `trusted-env` usage.
- Expand the generator census through its public entry point. Do not test the private `_expected` helper. Generate one committed artifact for each newly help-backed route and regenerate `overview.txt`.
- Widen top-level help pre-scan to every live visible route. Keep `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS` exactly `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, and `workflow` so nonleading child help reaches the owning parser or handler.
- Enable help on the `identity create`, `identity use`, and `identity key` child parsers. Prove that each child returns child usage and exits successfully.
- Keep the explicit `config validate --help` contract because `config validate` is handler-dispatched and has no populated argparse subparser action.
- Keep parser-introspective nested-family coverage for argparse-backed families. Assert that the derived family set matches runtime ownership, then exercise each child-help path. Keep the 42-subprocess all-route contract in the held-out outer oracle.
- Delete `_render_intercept` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`. Make CLI reference generation consume `subcommand_help(route.name)` for every documented route. Update the two legacy expectations in `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`.
- Correct comments and docstrings that claim intercept routes lack committed help. The affected paths include `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`, `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_workflow_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_parser_formatter_pinned.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_central_mount_gate_ad9f.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_registry_cutover_s6.py`, and `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`.
- Update affected expectations in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py` and `tests/interfaces/facades/test_intercept_registry_cutover_s6_heldout.py`.
- Retain `_OVERVIEW_OMIT` as exactly `bridge-fsck` and `bridge-probe`. Retain the test allowlist as exactly `help`, `bridge-fsck`, and `bridge-probe`.
- Keep `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_parser_formatter_pinned.py` scoped away from pure-intercept parsers because generator normalization permits those parsers to retain the standard library formatter.
- Regenerate package help and the CLI reference through their existing generators. The Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 CI cells must pass the help drift check against the same committed bytes.
- Do not add another router, parser, help source, mechanical writing-policy gate, or change to the Markdown-only reduced test policy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every live visible route outside the documented omit set appears exactly once in overview help.
- [x] `rebar help <command>` succeeds for every canonical pure-intercept route returned by the registry.
- [x] The pure-intercept help contract proves that no command handler executes.
- [x] The pure-intercept help contract proves that no ticket store is mounted or created.
- [x] `rebar help <command>` returns the matching committed artifact bytes.
- [x] Top-level `rebar <command> --help` returns the matching committed artifact bytes.
- [x] Every pure-intercept parser factory supplies a nonblank overview description.
- [x] The committed `trusted-env` usage banner preserves separate `add` and `revoke` lines.
- [x] Each CLI-reference pure-intercept syntax block equals the matching committed artifact.
- [x] A repository-wide semantic and string search reports zero `_render_intercept` references.
- [x] All four help-backed census sites use the live-visible predicate.
- [x] The exact overview exemptions remain `help`, `bridge-fsck`, and `bridge-probe`.
- [x] Hidden aliases and retired spellings remain absent from overview discovery.
- [x] `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS` equals `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, and `workflow`.
- [x] Every parser-introspectable nested family returns child-parser usage for each child.
- [x] `rebar identity create --help`, `rebar identity use --help`, and `rebar identity key --help` return their child usage and exit successfully.
- [x] `rebar config validate --help` reaches `build_validate` and returns validate child help.
- [x] Comments and test docstrings describe committed help ownership accurately.
- [x] The help drift check passes on supported Python versions.
- [x] The CLI-reference drift check passes.
- [x] No competing routing, parser, or help mechanism is introduced.
- [x] No mechanical writing enforcement is introduced.
- [x] The Markdown-only reduced test policy remains unchanged.

## CI gate remediation
- Classify the generated `jira-onboard` artifact and overview entry as compatibility surfaces. ADR 0100 records `jira-onboard` as a compatibility shim with a distinct historical invocation. The approved F12 acceptance criteria require the overview omit set to remain unchanged.
- Register the existing `review_result` schema for `scan-spec`.
- Add JSON schemas for the stable `config` and `sign-review` output contracts.
- Extend the CLI output contract test with offline drivers for `config` and `sign-review`.
- Add a reason-bearing CLI driver exemption map in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py` for `review-code`, `review-plan`, `scan-spec`, and `verify-completion` because they invoke model operations. Wire the map into driver classification, require a nonblank reason for every entry, reject stale entries, and reject overlap with offline drivers. The guard documentation permits explicit exemptions, but the current CLI guard does not implement this facility.
- Correct schema registry comments that depend on intercept routes lacking committed help.
- Document the added schemas in the external output catalog.

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Retained compatibility spellings are categorized without removing them from generated help.
- [x] Every newly discovered output advertiser has a registered schema.
- [x] Offline output advertisers are exercised against their registered schemas.
- [x] Every model-backed driver exemption has a nonblank reason.
- [x] The fixture-store contract test does not invoke model-backed output advertisers.
- [x] The three CI regressions reproduce red before remediation and pass afterward.

## Context / Problem

`outbound_field_diff.py` wires the live account-search resolver into the outbound mapper by **setting an attribute on it**:

    outbound_mapper._assignee_resolver = lambda lv: assignee_resolver(lv, jira_key)

wrapped in a `try/except (AttributeError, TypeError): pass`. Consumers then **discover** it with `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` and silently fall back to a non-authoritative result when it is absent.

This is a collaborator passed by side-channel rather than by contract, and it has three concrete costs:

1. **It fails silently.** If the injection ever stops happening — a mapper that forbids attribute assignment
   hits the bare `except ...: pass` — every assignee resolution degrades to `authoritative=False`. That is not
   cosmetic: a permanently non-authoritative assignee makes the outbound diff re-emit an assignee change it can
   never converge, the churn class epic `ace2` exists to fix.
2. **It hid a real bug in review.** GitHub PR #120's proposed Data Center adapter copied the `getattr` line
   into a class where nothing ever set the attribute, so its ENTIRE authoritative branch was dead code and DC
   would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. A typed constructor parameter makes that
   failure impossible to write.
3. **It is invisible to the type checker.** Each assignment needs `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` because the
   attribute is on no Protocol, so mypy cannot see the dependency at all.

## The FULL live site list (re-enumerated against this tree)

The Data Center adapter has since MERGED, so the blast radius is wider than "one injection + one getattr". `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` currently matches, in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

| # | site | role |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `outbound_field_diff.py:270` | core injection (`try/except`, per-`jira_key` closure) |
| 2 | `adapters/jira/backend.py:111` | Cloud `_JiraOutbound.resolve_assignee` getattr discovery |
| 3 | `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:118` | **DC** `_DCOutbound.resolve_assignee` getattr discovery |
| 4 | `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:331` | **DC** `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` injection onto `self.outbound`, `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` |
| — | `adapters/jira/backend.py:105,115`, `jira_datacenter/backend.py:115,324`, `jira_datacenter/_people.py:50` | docstrings that describe the attribute |
| — | `outbound_differ.py:384` | an UNRELATED local function that happens to share the name; leave it (renaming it is churn, and it is a nested `def`, not an attribute) |

Two implementers of the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` therefore have to change, not one: `adapters/jira/backend.py:92` (Cloud) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:109` (DC).

The two injections have DIFFERENT lifecycles, which is the one thing that needs a decision rather than a transcription:

- the core injection (#1) is built per remote key inside `compute_update_fields` and is the resolver the
  differ means to use;
- DC's (#4) is bound once in the backend constructor to the `jira.JIRA` client
  (`lambda name: _search_users_by_username(client, name)`), with no `jira_key`.

Today the core injection **overwrites** DC's constructor one whenever the differ runs, so "core wins, constructor is the fallback" is not a new policy — it is exactly the current behaviour, and the explicit form must preserve it.

Also note the call site is NOT where the injection is: `resolve_assignee` is invoked at `outbound_field_diff.py:398` inside `diff_canonical_fields`, a function that today receives no resolver. `compute_update_fields` (the injection point) calls it at line ~271, so the resolver has to be threaded through that hop as well.

## Approach

Thread the resolver **explicitly** instead of by attribute:

1. Widen the neutral port `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` in `_backend.py` with a keyword-only,
   defaulted `assignee_resolver` parameter, so the dependency appears in the contract and is typechecked.
2. Widen BOTH implementers to accept and forward it:
   - Cloud `adapters/jira/backend.py` → `AccountIdIdentity(resolver=assignee_resolver)`, deleting the getattr;
   - DC `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` → `NameIdentity(resolver=...)`, deleting the getattr.
3. Give DC's `_DCOutbound` a declared, typed constructor parameter for its client-bound resolver, and have
   `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` pass it there — deleting the `self.outbound._assignee_resolver = ...`
   assignment and its `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`. `resolve_assignee` prefers the explicit parameter and
   falls back to the constructor-supplied one, which reproduces today's overwrite semantics exactly.
4. Thread the resolver from `compute_update_fields` through `diff_canonical_fields` to the
   `resolve_assignee` call, and delete the attribute-injection block (and its `try/except ... : pass`).
5. Update the four/five docstrings that describe the attribute, and the test doubles that implement
   `resolve_assignee` so they accept the new keyword.
6. Keep every observable resolution outcome identical — this is plumbing.

### What "resolver absent" means, explicitly

The new parameter's default is `assignee_resolver=None`, and `None` keeps its CURRENT documented meaning: "no live account search is available on this path", which the identity models already define as the permissive, non-authoritative string match — `AccountIdIdentity(resolver=None).resolve("a@x.com", {"account_id": "acct-9"}) == ("a@x.com", False, False)`, pinned today by `test_user_identity_heldout.test_cloud_with_no_resolver_keeps_the_permissive_fallback`. The change is not the VALUE but its provenance: absence becomes a **declared default on the contract** that a caller chooses, instead of the invisible outcome of an injection that silently did not happen. Nothing raises, and no outcome moves.

## Why this is a separate ticket

Discovered while implementing story J4 [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], whose plan asserted the attribute was never set (true of PR #120, not of this tree) and whose AC4 asked for `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` to return nothing. Satisfying that literally means changing the **backend-neutral port signature**, which affects every backend — a materially wider blast radius than J4's three-file scope, and precisely the kind of core-risking change epic e369 deliberately sequenced away from the Data Center delivery path. J4 instead guarantees the property where it matters (the new identity models take the resolver as an explicit parameter and contain no `getattr` discovery at all) and defers this core cleanup here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` matches nothing except the unrelated local function in
      `outbound_differ.py`, and no `getattr(..., "_assignee_resolver", ...)` remains anywhere — in
      particular all four sites above are gone
- [x] the resolver is a declared parameter on the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` contract in
      `_backend.py`, and on BOTH implementers (Cloud and DC)
- [x] no `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` remains at either wiring site, and `make typecheck` passes
- [x] the six-state parity oracle in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_heldout.py`
      (`_CLOUD_STATES` × `test_account_id_identity_matches_the_live_cloud_backend_state_for_state`)
      still passes and still compares the live backend against the live identity model. Its ONE line
      that builds `expected` by attribute-injection (`backend.outbound._assignee_resolver = ...`,
      line ~148) necessarily becomes the explicit parameter pass — that seam is what this ticket
      deletes, so the oracle cannot be literally byte-unmodified. Its six states, its expectations,
      and its live-vs-live construction stay exactly as they are; only the injection line changes
      form. Every OTHER assertion about `resolve_assignee`
      (`state/test_canonical_mapper_surface.py`, `test_backend_characterization.py`,
      `test_dc_backend_characterization.py`) passes UNMODIFIED
- [x] a test proves the degradation path is gone: with the resolver absent, the behavior is the documented
      explicit default rather than a silent non-authoritative fallback
- [x] a test proves DC still resolves authoritatively through its constructor-supplied resolver, and that a
      core-supplied resolver takes precedence over it (today's overwrite semantics, preserved)
baseline.summary: Replace the outbound mapper's _assignee_resolver attribute-injection with explicit parameter passing

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Plan-review criterion prompts ship with no behavioral regression oracle. Of the 50 plan-review criteria returned by `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')`, only 12 have an eval spec across `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` and `.rebar/evals/`. A contributor editing any of the other rubrics under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` learns nothing if the edit reintroduces a false positive or drops a catch. ADR 0109 delivered a way to MEASURE a proposed change (the three-tier replay harness); it did not deliver an assertion of any criterion's required behavior on concrete material.

The material already exists. The committed manifest `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json` records 6,482 sidecar rows (`verified_ratio` 0.9568), and `plan_replay/corpus.py` reconstructs each row's at-review plan text. `plan_review/sidecar.py` retains, per finding, the `criteria` list, `cohort` (`sidecar.py:667-672`), `norm_id`, `decision`, and `decision_margin` — enough to state, for a real plan, which criteria fired, and — via the per-finding `cohort` set — which criteria were routed yet stayed silent.

## Approach

Mine that corpus offline into per-criterion fire/no-fire eval fixtures on real plans, and admit a fixture only after it reproduces against current code.

**No-fire evidence predicate.** The sidecar persists only findings that FIRED, so silence is an ABSENCE inference, never on its own a valid `expect: pass` case: silence from the criterion never being routed to that plan is indistinguishable from silence from finding nothing. The selector admits a plan as no-fire evidence for criterion C only when C appears in the `cohort` set of some finding recorded for that plan (`sidecar.py:667-672`, proving C was routed) AND no finding on that plan cites C; a row with a MISSING `cohort` key is treated as unknown and skipped, never emitted as `expect: pass` (the sidecar contract: missing cohort is unknown, never an empty set). No-fire reproduction consensus ranges over the equal-`material_fingerprint` reviews meeting this predicate; the selector owns it, the emitter transcribes it.

**Only inline-runnable criteria are mined.** `eval_solver.py:100-140` has three runner paths: generic criteria run over inline plan text, `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` (G3/G4/decomp-shape) require a `children` payload, and ISF RAISES on any inline fixture. Both non-inline classes still carry a `cohort` tag, so the selector EXCLUDES them from inline mining and the self-healing loop files an `unreliable-criterion:` ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each; the admission runner treats a fixture whose finder rejects its shape as WITHHELD-with-reason, never a hard error.

This fits because the fixture is what the existing machinery already consumes: `rebar criteria eval` runs a criterion's cases through its real Pass-1 finder (`eval_solver.py:139-142`) via the validated `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml` seam (`eval.py:69-78`). A fixture adds zero production tokens, cannot bias a live review, and composes with the ADR 0109 harness rather than duplicating it.

This epic REPLACES its earlier R-4 framing (examples injected into reviewer prompts): the Pass-1 rubric is assembled into `instructions` AFTER the cache breakpoint (`pass1.py:283-298`), so prompt-resident examples re-bill on every chunk forever, and a false positive used as both prompt example and eval case makes the eval measure nothing.

## Non-goals

- Injecting anything into reviewer prompts. No file under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`
  changes in this epic.
- Fixtures for criteria that already have a spec. `eval.py:69-78` resolves a project spec
  as a REPLACEMENT for the packaged one, so writing one there would delete the packaged
  cases.
- Shipping rebar's fixtures as packaged core for other projects. The tooling is the reusable
  artifact; a project overriding criteria owns its own evals, as it already owns its tests.
- Closing the drift the admission run discovers. Each entry becomes a follow-on ticket
  linked `discovered_from` this epic.
- Per-finding true/false-positive labelling or human adjudication (the 2026-07-16 attempt
  was invalidated at ~79% contaminated labels,
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/README.md:112-118`; not retried here).
- Restructuring the prompt cache so eval prefixes become cacheable.

## Budget

Epic ceiling **$450** including a $75 reserve, enforced by the parameterized ledger and allocated per child: ledger $0, selector $0, emitter $0, admission runner $250, change-triggered execution $25, self-healing loop $100, ADR/docs $0. The admission bootstrap central estimate is $112 (band $68-$229) at the per-call rates in `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/ledger.jsonl`. Steady-state cost after this epic is zero unless a rubric changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A no-fire (`expect: pass`) case for criterion C is emitted only when C is in the
      `cohort` set of some finding on that plan AND no finding on that plan cites C; a row
      with a missing `cohort` key is skipped, never emitted; verified by `pytest` over a
      synthetic corpus with an in-cohort silent plan (emitted), a never-in-cohort plan
      (skipped), a missing-cohort row (skipped), and a container/ISF-class criterion
      (excluded from inline mining).
- [x] Every plan-review criterion that `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')`
      reports and that had no eval spec when this epic opened either has a spec file under
      `.rebar/evals/`, or an open ticket titled `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`
      recording why it has none; verified by a script that sets the routing key set against
      `ls .rebar/evals/ src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` and the open-ticket titles, and exits
      non-zero if any criterion is in neither set.
- [x] No fixture enters `.rebar/evals/` without having reproduced against current code, and
      the candidates that failed to reproduce are recorded with both their historical and
      observed behavior; verified by the committed drift report plus the admission run's
      admitted/withheld counts.
- [x] A criterion's fixtures execute when that criterion's rubric file changes, and the
      criteria covered by this epic do not join the existing weekly live sweep; verified by
      `grep` of the resolved weekly spec list showing none of the new prompt ids.
- [x] A run whose pre-flight estimate would exceed the epic ceiling is refused before it
      issues any model call; verified by `pytest` over the ledger refusal test.
- [x] No file under `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` is modified by this epic; verified by
      `git diff --stat origin/main..HEAD -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` producing no output.
- [x] The mining and admission protocol is recorded as an ADR under `docs/adr/` and
      referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`; verified by `grep -q` for the ADR filename
      in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Child decomposition

Each acceptance criterion above is owned by at least one child, non-overlapping:

- No-fire predicate AC -> the selector (owns/applies the cohort + no-finding predicate) and
  the emitter (transcribes no-fire candidates to `expect: pass`).
- Coverage AC -> the selector (trustworthy candidates), the emitter (validated specs) and
  the admission runner (writes survivors); residual gaps + container/ISF criteria -> the
  self-healing loop, which files the `unreliable-criterion:` tickets.
- Reproduction/drift AC -> the admission runner.
- Change-triggered execution AC -> the change-triggered execution child.
- Budget-refusal AC -> the ledger parameterization child, consumed by the admission runner.
- Untouched-prompts AC -> a constraint on every child; no child edits a rubric.
- ADR AC -> the ADR and docs child.

Ordering: selector -> emitter; emitter + ledger -> admission runner; admission runner -> change-triggered execution + self-healing loop; ADR/docs lands last.
baseline.summary: Plan-review per-criterion regression fixtures mined from the review sidecar record (R-4)

## What

`transition <id> open in_progress` currently bypasses the plan-review claim gate that `claim` enforces. Starting work via a plain transition should apply the SAME validation (require a certified plan-review attestation, or `--force` with an audit note). The gate logic, today living in `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py::_plan_review_precheck`, must be consolidated into a single shared method that both the claim path and the transition path call — so the two cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The plan-review gate validation lives in ONE method (consolidated out of `claim.py` into a shared home, e.g. `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`).
- [ ] `claim_compute` calls the consolidated method (behavior unchanged; existing claim-gate tests still pass).
- [ ] `transition_compute` calls the consolidated method when transitioning `open -> in_progress`, blocking (fail-closed) on a missing/stale attestation when the gate is enabled, and exempting bug/session_log.
- [ ] `--force` (with audit comment) bypasses the gate on the transition path, mirroring claim.
- [ ] New tests cover the transition open->in_progress gate (blocked / force-bypass / bug-exempt / earned-attestation-succeeds).
baseline.summary: Apply plan-review gate to open->in_progress transition; consolidate claim/transition gate logic
