## Why
A senior-SDET-quality review of the test suite, run as an iterative loop, is the closing quality gate for the post-migration hardening.

## What
- Run an opus subagent primed as an SDET to review the project's testing (coverage adequacy, assertion quality, isolation, flakiness, fixture design, seam organization, contract coverage across the 3 interfaces, CI wiring).
- Remediate every important/critical finding.
- Repeat the review→remediate loop until a review returns NO important/critical findings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] At least one opus SDET-primed review performed and its findings recorded
- [ ] All important/critical findings remediated (with tests/changes referenced)
- [ ] Review loop repeated until a clean pass (no important/critical findings)
- [ ] Suite green locally + CI after remediation
baseline.summary: Opus SDET review loop: review tests, remediate important/critical findings, repeat until clean

RP-04 is not complete while these ambient reads sit below the approved composition/credential/backend seams enforced by `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`. Parent: 075b-1479-dcb7-40ab.

Affected files (relative to `src/rebar/`):

Their `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` entries are removed. `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` reports zero findings for these paths with those entries gone and no path-glob exception. No stored ticket/event/binding format changes. A legacy facade is removed only after its focused suite passes; until then rollback selects the facade.

- [x] The `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` entries for these files are removed from `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`, and `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` passes with no path-glob exception (proven by the held-out `test_reconciler_engine_seam_clean_heldout.py`).
- [x] The subsystem behavioral suites (tests/interfaces/store, tests/integration reconciler suites, tests/unit/rebar_reconciler) pass after the cutover; redacted operation-snapshot fingerprints / provider-neutral outcomes are unchanged except recorded approved deltas.

## Context / Problem

Private re-exports, wrappers, and alias assignments survive after ownership moved elsewhere. Their only beneficiaries are repository imports, strings, and monkeypatch targets, so they create a second binding without protecting a public compatibility contract. The approved policy requires every such consumer to migrate and prohibits new internal-only shims.

## Approach

A prerequisite ADR establishes the boundary and enforcement policy. After it merges, disjoint children migrate all source, tests, dynamic imports, string lookups, and monkeypatch consumers by subsystem and delete the old binding. Public facades, MCP wire schemas, event readers, and persisted-data migrations remain separate contracts.

## Child Decomposition

- The ADR child performs RESEARCH, DRAFT, HOLD, and MERGE for the no-internal-shim rule.
- Core/reconciler, CLI/security/graph/grounding, and LLM/workflow/MCP-model children own disjoint migration censuses.
- The LLM/workflow shard also owns approved SDC3 alias migrations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A merged ADR defines one canonical binding after private moves, atomic consumer migration, valid exceptions, and recurrence prevention.
- [ ] Every enumerated internal shim has its semantic/static and string/dynamic/monkeypatch consumers moved to its canonical owner.
- [ ] No old private binding remains solely for internal compatibility.
- [ ] Deliberate public facades, wire schemas, event readers, and persisted-data migrations retain their independently specified contracts.
baseline.summary: Eliminate internal-only compatibility shims under an ADR-governed policy

# Create canonical AGENTS.md (rebar dev guide) + reduce CLAUDE.md to a thin @AGENTS.md pointer

## Why

`AGENTS.md` is read natively by Codex, Cursor, Copilot's coding agent, Zed, Windsurf, Amp, Factory, Jules, Devin, RooCode, and Cline — so one canonical `AGENTS.md` covers the ecosystem, and Claude Code is bridged by a one-line import. This also fixes the size/duplication anti-pattern: sections that duplicate a `docs/` file become one-line pointers.

## What

Author a lean `AGENTS.md` at the repo root that keeps rebar-INTERNAL developer specifics inline and replaces every already-documented topic with a one-line `docs/…md` pointer. Then reduce `CLAUDE.md` to a single `@AGENTS.md` import plus an optional `## Claude Code` section.

- **INLINE (kept in full):** intro; the record-work/claim-before-you-work operating rules; the
  parallel-agent loop; env bootstrap (`make install`/`make hooks`); module-size policy; Serena
  navigation; a **condensed** Git/Gerrit section; a 6-line library snippet.
- **POINTER (one line each), to EXISTING docs:** gate protocols → `docs/plan-review-gate.md`;
  quality gates + ticket template + project criteria → `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`; MCP
  tool set → `docs/mcp-reference.md`; store-shares-writes + parent-first cascade →
  `docs/concurrency.md`; ticket model → `docs/ticket-model.md` (created by S1); session logs →
  `docs/event-schema.md` + `docs/user-guide.md`; library reference → `docs/reuse-surface.md`; the
  LLM agent-operations topic → `docs/llm-framework.md`; the completion close-gate →
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. These are POINTERS only — this story writes no content into those
  docs (their content already exists; the two "stowaway" topics currently mixed into CLAUDE.md's
  Session-logs heading are simply not carried into AGENTS.md).

## Scope

In: new `AGENTS.md`, rewritten `CLAUDE.md`. No writes to any `docs/*` file (pointers only). Out: `CLAUDE.local.md` (S3), the shim/reference sweep (S6), and code. **Depends on S1** (already linked `depends_on`): `docs/ticket-model.md` must exist before `AGENTS.md` points at it. Rollback is a plain `git revert` (docs/text only).

## Design decisions (spike-validated)

- The `@AGENTS.md` import is PROVEN in Claude Code 2.1.211 (headless canary + official docs
  recommend exactly `@AGENTS.md` + `## Claude Code`); no symlink fallback.
- Imports "load at launch" and do not reduce context, so the token win comes from de-dup into docs
  and **AGENTS.md must itself be lean.** A grounded estimate puts a complete lean file at ~152
  lines and ≤ 200 only if the Git/Gerrit section is condensed to agent-actionable rules and defers
  the full recipe to `CONTRIBUTING.md` (verbatim Gerrit → ~215-230, which misses the target).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` exists at repo root and is ≤ 200 lines.
  - Proving: `test -f AGENTS.md && [ "$(wc -l < AGENTS.md)" -le 200 ]`
- [ ] The Git/Gerrit section is condensed (≤ ~55 lines) and defers the full recipe to
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
  - Proving: `rg -q 'CONTRIBUTING.md' AGENTS.md`; reviewer confirms the section ≤ 55 lines.
- [ ] Each already-documented topic is a one-line pointer, not a restated section.

baseline.description:
## Context

When the plan-review claim gate re-fires on a CONTAINER ticket (epic/story with children) that is
mid-execution, it reviews the plan as if FRESH — blind to which children are already delivered. It
then re-litigates acceptance criteria already shipped by closed+attested children: false BLOCKs and
coaching to tighten AC that is done, plus a slow whole-context review of settled work.

Re-fires are legitimate but infrequent — a paused epic reopened (ADR 0009 invalidates an
attestation signed before the reopen), or a material course-correction to the epic plan
(material-fingerprint invalidation). The claim CASCADE is not the driver (it only fires while the
parent is `open`). Code-drift invalidation is INTENTIONAL and unchanged (a container's plan is
reviewed against codebase state — G6 runs at container scope): this epic changes only what a
re-fired review DOES, not when it fires.

## What we build

A deterministic Pass-3 "completion floor" (third floor beside the novelty floor ADR 0008 and the
drift-refresh path ADR 0002), fed by a separate `plan_review_completion` Pass-2 sub-call (mirroring
`plan_review_novelty`) that answers three atomic orthogonal sub-questions per finding: ATTRIBUTION
(which closed child), CONTAINMENT (limited vs spans open), LAYER (plan-semantics vs
delivered-functionality). Pass-1 stays completion-blind (full recall); the coach is unchanged.

## Scope

- IN: the Pass-2 completion sub-call + three sub-questions; the Pass-3 completion floor + config
  evidence-gate + priority floor; the delivered-now predicate (attestation reuse + in-epic sibling
  supersede); sidecar recording; calibration gold-set + tests.
- OUT (deferred, separate epics): partial-completion attestation for in-progress children; a
  structured `resolution` enum on `close`; the sidecar re-injection queue; an optional second LAYER
  binary. In-progress children stay FULLY in scope in v1.

## Alternatives considered

- (a) Exempt epics from the claim gate — REJECTED: discards the container security review ADR 0016
  added (a container epic that stands up infrastructure would go unreviewed).
- (b) Completion-aware container review — CHOSEN; hybrid = (b) + keying on VERIFIED delivery
  (completion attestation) + in-epic sibling supersede.
- Decomposition-drift-only freshness (never invalidate a container on code drift) — REJECTED:
  code-drift invalidation is intentional; a container's plan IS reviewed vs codebase state (G6 runs
  at container scope).
- A single composite predicate instead of three sub-questions — REJECTED: attribution / containment
  / layer are orthogonal (identity / spatial scope / artifact layer); folding them loses the
  distinctions and re-couples model category + severity error.
- Hide delivered children / review only open children — REJECTED: blinds coherence + security to
  delivered<->open interactions; we FREEZE delivered children as visible context, not hide them.
- Tag- or progress-note-based suppression — REJECTED: unsigned + gameable (prompt-injection surface
  into a security-sensitive gate); we key on the signed completion attestation.
- Run the completion-verifier to drive scoping — REJECTED: FAIL-by-construction mid-flight + signing
  ambiguity (needs a third attestation kind); we READ the attestation closed children already carry.
- Reuse the novelty sub-answer mechanism (add the three completion questions to NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS)
  instead of a parallel sub-call — REJECTED: completion keys on a DIFFERENT context input (the
  delivered-children manifest) than novelty (prior findings), so a separate sub-call preserves the
  Pass-1 independence invariant by construction; they share the kernel sub-answer machinery, not context.

## Acceptance Criteria

Decision (recorded, not a forward deliverable): option (b)/hybrid chosen — see the decision comment, '## Alternatives considered', and the completion session log.
- [ ] A separate `plan_review_completion` Pass-2 sub-call (mirroring `plan_review_novelty`) emits, per finding, {attribution, containment, layer} with fail-safe values (insufficient/n/a/spans-open/delivered-functionality all keep).
- [ ] Pass-3 completion floor drops a finding iff attribution=delivered-now-child AND containment=limited AND layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND criterion not in {security,contract}; gated behind an evidence-gate flag + configurable priority floor (mirroring the novelty floor).
- [ ] `delivered-now` = valid completion attestation (validity-on-read, reusing the `_child_closure_findings` predicate) OR superseded by a sibling under the same parent; force-closed/abandoned/in-progress children are NOT delivered and stay in scope.
- [ ] Drops recorded to the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (joinable, observable) and recomputed every run (a reopened/un-delivered child auto-resurfaces its findings).
- [ ] A durable ADR (`docs/adr/0020-completion-aware-container-plan-review.md`) codifies the new contracts (sub-call schema + closed enums, delivered-now predicate, completion floor + config, sidecar drop_reason) — inline AC + session log are not the durable record.
- [ ] Tests: a partially-complete epic review drops delivered plan-semantics findings yet preserves (a) a delivered child's delivered-functionality/security finding, (b) a finding spanning an open sibling, (c) all findings on a force-closed child; plus a calibration gold-set of must-never-suppress cases.
- [ ] A re-fired container review does not re-litigate delivered AC: findings limited to a
- [ ] Suppression is deterministic in Pass-3, keyed on VERIFIED delivery (completion attestation or
- [ ] No change to WHEN a review is invalidated (code-drift stays), no `close`-op change, no new
baseline.summary: Completion-aware plan-review for container tickets (epics/stories with children)

baseline.description:
# The shared webhook/rerun secret is written to journald in every access-log line

## Context / Problem

The review-bot receiver is a uvicorn app, and uvicorn's default access log records the full request line INCLUDING THE QUERY STRING. Both authenticated endpoints take their secret as a QUERY PARAMETER (`?token=...`), so every request writes the secret to stderr -> journald in clear text:

    INFO:  127.0.0.1:34184 - "POST /rerun?token=<the actual secret>&change=1323 HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted
    INFO:  172.21.0.4:33070 - "POST /webhook?token=<the actual secret> HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted

Observed directly in the production container's journal (`journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1`).

## Why it matters

* **The secret is the auth for both endpoints.** `config.py:239` is
  `webhook_token = os.environ.get("WEBHOOK_TOKEN", "").strip() or bot_token`, and this
  container sets no `WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, so the webhook token IS `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` — the
  review bot's Gerrit credential. Anything that can read the journal therefore learns a
  credential that can both drive reviews AND act as the bot against Gerrit.
* **The blast radius is wider than the box.** journald content flows into anything that reads
  it: `infra/scripts/observability.sh` greps the same journal, operators paste log excerpts into
  tickets and chat, and any future log-shipping would carry the secret off-host. It also means
  the secret cannot be treated as unexposed after any incident that involved sharing logs.
* **It is a fail-open exposure, not a fail-closed one:** nothing errors, nothing alarms, and the
  endpoint keeps working — so there is no signal that would ever surface it.

DISCOVERED the hard way: an agent grepping the journal for `/rerun` activity while working [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] surfaced the token into a session transcript. That is the failure mode — the secret is sitting in the most-grepped log on the box.

**This ticket does not fix the exposure that already happened.** The token in the journal (and anywhere journal excerpts have been shared) must be treated as compromised and ROTATED independently of the code fix. Rotation alone is also not sufficient: without the fix, the new token is logged the moment it is first used.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — the `/webhook` and `/rerun` handlers and/or the uvicorn
  logging configuration (`configure_logging`).
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — the `uvicorn` invocation, if the access-log format or
  its disabling belongs there.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the `/rerun` recipe currently instructs the operator to
  put the token in a URL, which is what puts it in the log; and a rotation note.

## Approach (options, with the tradeoff stated)

1. **Move the secret out of the query string** — accept it as a header (e.g. `X-Rebar-Token`) or
   in the POST body. Cleanest: access logs record the request line, not headers. But
   `/webhook` is called BY GERRIT, so the Gerrit-side webhook configuration must be able to
   send it — check what the `webhook` plugin supports before assuming a header is expressible.
   `/rerun` is operator-driven and can move to a header immediately regardless.
2. **Scrub the access log** — install a uvicorn log filter that redacts `token=[^&]*`. Keeps the
   URL shape, protects the value, and covers BOTH endpoints even if Gerrit cannot send a header.
   Weaker in principle (the secret still transits a URL, so it can leak via any other component
   that logs URLs) but it is the only option that works without a Gerrit-side change.
3. Do both: header for `/rerun`, redaction filter as the backstop for `/webhook`.

Do NOT simply disable the access log — it is load-bearing for debugging and for the `observability.sh` greps.

## Testing

The oracle must assert on the EMITTED LOG LINE, not on the handler's behaviour, because the handler is already correct — it is the logging that leaks:

- drive a request carrying a known sentinel token through the app with `caplog` (or a captured
  uvicorn handler) and assert the sentinel does NOT appear in any emitted record, while the
  route and status DO;
- verify RED by reverting the fix and observing the sentinel reappear;
- if a header is adopted, a second test that a query-string token is REJECTED (or at least not
  logged), so the old path cannot quietly persist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the webhook/rerun secret no longer appears in any log record the receiver emits, proven by
      a test that asserts on the emitted log line with a sentinel value and is verified RED by
      reverting the fix.
- [x] the mechanism is stated in the code where the choice is made (header vs redaction filter),
      including WHY — so a future change does not reintroduce the query-string form as a
      convenience.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`'s `/rerun` recipe no longer instructs the operator to
      put the token in a URL, and carries a note that the previous token must be treated as
      compromised and rotated.
- [x] the access log still records route and status for both endpoints (the observability greps
      and debugging value are not sacrificed to fix this).
- [x] ROTATION IS TRACKED SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY: the currently-logged token is rotated, and
      that rotation is recorded as done rather than assumed, since the code fix does not
      un-leak what is already in journald.
baseline.summary: Review-bot logs the webhook token in plaintext on every /webhook and /rerun request

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`_pai_structured` creates fresh Agent runs for prompted-output recovery, so output attempts can reset the request budget and history is assembled outside Pydantic (`structured_run.py:87-178`). The RP-01 contract instead composes the S1 output-policy adapter [rebar:grazeable-preferred-bumblebee] (landed: `src/rebar/llm/pai_output.py`; review `--ref HEAD`) in one Agent operation, preserving every authoritative input and stored response.

## Approach
Replace the manual attempt scheduler with one Pydantic `Agent` run composing the S1 adapter (`pai_output.output_function` as `output_type=TextOutput(fn)`) with two new seams from `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py`:

1. **Wire-context projection — a pydantic-ai `history_processors` `HistoryProcessor`.** The Agent-level `history_processors=[proc]` seam runs a callable before each request returning a wire COPY without mutating stored state, so `result.all_messages()` keeps full history regardless of wire omissions. It puts a failed `ModelResponse` on the retry wire ONLY when, for every viable candidate, that response's own `response.usage.input_tokens + output_tokens` (the tokens it already billed) plus `effective_max_tokens` fits `model_classes.own_window_tokens(candidate)`; else it omits that response WHOLE (never partially; missing/zero usage → omit). Authoritative input alone over the window (`input_tokens + effective_max_tokens > window`, nothing added) fails closed with the new typed `ContextWindowExceededError` — never shortened.

2. **Truncation reclassification — a concision-aware operation guard.** Guard attachment is PER OUTPUT MODE. On the PROMPTED branch ONLY (`output_type=TextOutput(fn)`), `pai_retry` supplies its own `after_model_request` capability in place of `pai_output.guard_capability()`; the NativeOutput branch keeps `pai_output.guard_capability()` unchanged (terminal). `guard_capability`'s contract for other callers is likewise UNCHANGED until S5 cutover. Because the shared classifiers only RAISE (never return a reason), the guard does a read-only two-layer read for the truncation subset ONLY — `finish_reason` OR raw `provider_details['finish_reason']` in {`length`,`max_tokens`} (two layers, mirroring check_response, so a provider_details-only truncation #5221 is caught): (a) on a truncation signal it raises, before parsing, `pydantic_ai.ModelRetry("Make your response as concise as possible while fulfilling the prompt and output format requirements.")` — bounded, in-run; (b) else it delegates to the SAME S1 logic — `check_response`: re-raise terminal `UnretryableOutputError` (refusal/`content_filter`), translate retryable `StructuredOutputError` (`error`) into `ModelRetry`. The shared `structured.py` tables are NOT modified (read, never mutated).

3. **One shared request budget, one shared retry counter.** `build_usage_limits` sets the operation-wide `UsageLimits.request_limit` = base allowance (`ceil(eff_max_iter/2)`) PLUS the configured output-retry allowance, computed once, NO per-attempt reset. The RETURNED `req_limit` (telemetry + `completion_banking.iteration_limit_for`) stays the BARE base, so the `2×B` inverse stays exact; the allowance is an addend only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`. The allowance N (`structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES`=2, lowered by `req.structured_retry_limit`) seeds BOTH `retries={"output": N}` AND the `request_limit` addend from ONE value, so the request budget can NEVER trip before the output-retry counter. That the concision `ModelRetry` (capability hook) and the parse/validation `ModelRetry` (`TextOutput` fn) share ONE counter is pinned BEHAVIORALLY by the limit-matrix oracle (pass at N, abort at N−1), not any private symbol. On exhaustion pydantic-ai raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior` ("Exceeded maximum output retries"), translated to a rebar-typed `UnretryableOutputError`.

**NativeOutput preserved.** `structured.output_mode`'s NativeOutput (constrained-decoding) selection and its documented bug-895c grammar-compilation fallback to the prompted path are kept UNCHANGED: the NativeOutput branch runs as the same bounded operation (`output_type=NativeOutput`), sharing the wire projection and the one output-retry counter, but attaching `pai_output.guard_capability()` — NOT the concision guard. Concision applies ONLY to the prompted branch — a fixed decoding grammar (not verbosity) drives a native turn's size, so a truncated native turn stays TERMINAL via `guard_capability`/`check_response`. Only the manual for-loop is replaced — not mode selection, the 895c fallback, or native terminal truncation.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py` — new: (a) the `HistoryProcessor` wire projection (fit decision + non-mutating whole-response include/omit) and (b) the concision-aware guard (see Approach §2). Docstring records the combined-allowance derivation. No provider selection, usage projection, or persistence.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — replace the manual `_pai_structured` attempt scheduling with one Agent operation; extend `build_usage_limits` to derive the combined `request_limit` (base + output allowance) with no counter reset (this is where `req_limit` is computed, not `agent_call.py`).
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — thread the two seams and `retries={"output": allowance}` into `build_agent_kwargs` (wiring only; does not compute the allowance).
- `src/rebar/llm/errors.py` — add `ContextWindowExceededError(LLMRunnerError)` for authoritative-input overflow.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — compose the helper without exceeding the 800-line cap.
- `tests/unit/test_structured_run.py`, `test_runner_pydantic_budget.py`, `test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, plus the two seams pinning the CONSTRUCTED `request_limit` — `test_settings_builders_seam.py` and `test_llm_failure_matrix.py::test_runner_computes_derived_usage_limits` (both move `ceil(mi/2)`→base+allowance) — operation/history/limit contracts.

**Consumers of the `ceil(x/2)` budget shape** (sweep of `build_usage_limits`): `completion_banking.iteration_limit_for` (`2×B`) and `plan_recovery_pool` (`ceil(floor/2)`) both stay exact because `build_usage_limits` keeps RETURNING the bare base `req_limit`; the allowance lives only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`. A source-census test pins both encodings as authoritative (full sweep + pydantic-ai grounding in ticket comment).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Invalid-then-valid output completes in one Agent run reporting exactly two requests under one shared `UsageLimits`; verified by real-`FunctionModel` tests.
- [x] A complete 5,000-char failed response is on the retry wire only when the full request plus output reserve provably fits (`input_tokens + effective_max_tokens <= window` for every candidate); verified by a fit test.
- [x] When it does not fit — or the count is unknown — zero chars of it reach the wire while `all_messages()` retains all 5,000; verified by omit + unknown-count tests.
- [x] Authoritative-input overflow raises `ContextWindowExceededError` with no shortening of system/user/tool content; verified by an oversize-input test.
- [x] `length`/`max_tokens` consumes at most the shared output-retry allowance and sends exactly the concision instruction from Approach §2; verified by success + exhaustion cases.
- [x] Refusal/content-filter stays terminal after one model call, triggering neither output retry nor fallback (an in-run `ModelRetry` never reaches `fallback_on`); verified by call- and candidate-count assertions.
- [x] The NativeOutput branch still selects via `output_mode`, runs under the shared bounded operation with `pai_output.guard_capability()` attached (NOT the concision guard), keeps truncation TERMINAL (no concision retry), and preserves the bug-895c grammar-compilation fallback to the prompted path; verified by native-run and 895c-fallback tests.
- [x] The combined allowance is documented in the `pai_retry.py` docstring, and no per-attempt reset path remains; verified by that docstring plus a source-census and budget test.
baseline.summary: RP-01 S2 — Run structured-output recovery as one bounded Agent operation

## What
Prove the batch write reduces commit count and does not break crash-resume: a before/after commit-count benchmark on a synthetic many-event import, plus rollback + crash-resume tests. **Depends on B1 (890d) and B2 (6386)** — the primitive and the importer adoption must exist.

## Why
Batching changes commit granularity (N events per commit). We must demonstrate the win (commit-count reduction) and prove the safety properties: all-or-nothing per commit, and that a crash mid-batch plus the `source_id` re-scan resumes cleanly. NOTE: the importer's existing LINE parsing is fail-open (a malformed NDJSON line is skipped); the whole-chunk rollback proven here is a property of the BATCH PRIMITIVE (`batch_stage_and_commit`) — one event that fails validation inside a chunk rolls back that chunk's already-staged events — not of the importer's line parser.

## Scope
- Benchmark test: build a synthetic N=3000 NDJSON where each ticket has 1 CREATE + 1 comment
  and no parents/file-impact/verify/links/statuses (so only Pass 1 and Pass 2d carry events),
  run `import_tickets`, and assert the commit-count DELTA (`int(subprocess.run(["git","-C",
  tracker,"rev-list","--count","HEAD"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)` after − before)
  == `2*ceil(3000/256)` (=24), >=10x fewer than the ~6000 per-event commits.
- Malformed-event-mid-chunk test (batch primitive level): a chunk containing one event that
  fails validation triggers whole-chunk rollback — assert index clean (`git diff --cached
  --name-only` empty) AND commit count unchanged (`git rev-list --count HEAD`), and no
  chunk event files left on disk.
- Crash-resume test: simulate a crash before a chunk's `git commit` (e.g. monkeypatch the
  commit to raise after staging); assert the store is left whole-commit-or-none, then re-run
  the import and assert the `source_id` re-scan skips committed events and re-emits the rest.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Benchmark test asserts the commit-count DELTA (`git rev-list --count HEAD` after − before; baseline `init_repo` commits excluded via the delta) == `2*ceil(3000/256)` (=24) for a synthetic N=3000 CREATE+comment import, >=10x fewer than the ~6000 per-event commits
- [ ] Malformed-event-mid-chunk test: a chunk containing an event dict that fails the primitive's validation (invalid `event_type` / missing `uuid`) rolls the whole chunk back — assert BOTH `git diff --cached --name-only` is empty (index clean, no phantom staged blob) AND `git rev-list --count HEAD` is unchanged from before the failed flush (proving no commit was written), and none of the chunk's event files exist on disk
- [ ] Crash-resume test on a CREATE-only synthetic file (N=1000 tickets, so Pass 1 is the only batched pass and committed-event count == committed-ticket count): monkeypatch `event_append.subprocess.run` so `git commit` succeeds for the first K=2 256-chunks then raises after staging on the 3rd chunk. Assert (i) whole-commit-or-none: `git diff --cached --name-only` empty (B1's rollback ran) and `rebar.list_tickets` count == exactly 512 (no partial chunk); undo the monkeypatch and re-run the same import and assert (ii) `rebar.list_tickets` returns all 1000 tickets exactly once (no duplicates/losses) and (iii) the re-run adds exactly `ceil(488/256)=2` chunks' worth of commits (`git rev-list --count HEAD` delta), proving the source_id re-scan skipped the 512 already-committed tickets
- [ ] Named regression suites green (verified paths): `tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_reducer_single_source.py` + `tests/unit/test_reducer_status_fork_record.py` (replay), `tests/unit/test_sync_union_recovery.py` + `tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py` (union-merge convergence), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` + `tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py` + `tests/unit/test_snapshot_cache.py` (SNAPSHOT compaction)
- [ ] `make test` green
baseline.summary: B4: commit-count benchmark + crash-resume/rollback tests for batched writes

## Context

Run the rebar-janitor codebase-health pipeline against the current rebar repository as a deliberate maintenance pause. This is a read-only audit of product code: the deliverables are durable audit artifacts, a human-approved remediation plan, and tracker tickets. No production or test code will be changed.

## Scope

Inspect the repository for code debt, code and architectural smells, separation-of-concerns problems, spent optionality, documentation gaps, oversized units, weak test oracles, AI-generated-code and security smells, and temporal decay. Weight recently changed regions while covering the full codebase. Consult prior janitor artifacts, tickets, ADRs, and commit history so intentional decisions are not mistaken for defects.

This repository's established artifact location is `.joe-janitor/`: `docs/documentation-policy.md` explicitly recognizes that tree, and `.joe-janitor/tools.md` already contains the durable playbook. Reuse that location rather than the generic skill default.

## Plan

1. Discovery: fan out one concern per independent agent, shard comment and test-suite review by subsystem, and pool path:line-cited findings without severity or confidence.
2. Verification: independently blue-team each finding, establish reachable harm, check prior decisions and known-fine entries, apply the skill's fixed validity and impact floors, and persist the audit record plus reusable tool playbook.
3. Remediation: obtain two blind proposals per survivor from asymmetric evidence bases (community practice versus project record), converge at move/end-state level, and research divergences.
4. Approval: present the Remediation Plan one item at a time for human approve/refine/reject decisions; record explicit known-fine blessings only when given.
5. Ticketization: first search for a matching current Janitor Cleanup epic and children; create only missing tracker records. Approved work becomes actionable child tickets with acceptance criteria, provenance, dependencies, and file impact.

Any failed discovery shard remains an explicit coverage gap and prevents Phase 1 completion. Audit artifact updates preserve existing content and ticketization searches before creating records so a resumed run does not silently lose coverage or duplicate work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Discovery covers every concern required by the rebar-janitor skill.
- [ ] Every discovery candidate has an exact path:line citation.
- [ ] Discovery candidates contain no severity or confidence score.
- [ ] Independent verification records validity for every candidate it processes.
- [ ] Independent verification records impact and a reachable-harm statement for every candidate it processes.
- [ ] Independent verification records prior-decision and known-fine handling.
- [ ] Candidates below validity 0.75 are dropped.
- [ ] Candidates below impact 0.5 are dropped.
- [ ] The dated audit record is persisted at `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-29.md`.
- [ ] The reusable command and pattern playbook is appended at `.joe-janitor/tools.md`.
- [ ] The audit report records commands and tuned thresholds.
- [ ] The audit report records survivors, dropped candidates, and their evidence-backed disposition.
- [ ] Every surviving finding receives two blind asymmetric-evidence remediation proposals.
- [ ] Every divergent proposal pair is researched before its item enters the Remediation Plan.
- [ ] Each remediation item receives an explicit user approve, refine, or reject decision before ticket creation.
- [ ] Approved work is filed as child tickets under a current Janitor Cleanup epic.
- [ ] Each created child is linked back to this audit ticket.
- [ ] No production code, tests, configuration, or documentation outside `.joe-janitor/` and the tracker is modified.
baseline.summary: Run codebase-health janitor audit — 2026-08-29

## Context / Problem
Inert-config class (281f, 9d7a family): a typed schema field ships with zero cfg.<section>.<field> read sites outside schema/config plumbing, so the knob silently does nothing. Env vars are already covered by the docs/env-vars.md drift gate; schema fields have no equivalent.

## Approach
Deterministic AST-level check: for each field in _config_schema.py, require >=1 attribute-read site outside the schema/config plumbing modules.

Detection shape (decisive, receiver-agnostic): an ast.Attribute node in Load context whose terminal attribute name equals the field name — matching ONLY on the final `.field` segment, never on a receiver spelling. This deliberately matches every real read shape in src/: `load_config().mcp.readonly`, `config.load_config(root).verify.overlap_enabled`, a section object bound to a local (`mcp_cfg.auth_introspection_endpoint`), `self.config.<section>.<field>`, or any alias. Trade-off, stated openly: terminal-name matching is permissive — an unrelated object's same-named attribute also counts, silently keeping the gate quiet. That failure mode is fail-QUIET (a rare shadowed name suppresses a firing), never a false fire on a live field; zero-reference firing stays sound because a field with literally no `.field` attribute read anywhere cannot be read. Same-named-field collisions across sections are likewise fail-quiet and accepted. Dynamic reads (getattr dispatch) are invisible to the AST walk by design — that is exactly what the marker is for. Escape hatch: '# read-via: <path-or-reason>' comment on the field for indirect reads (getattr dispatch, client-project-only knobs) — pointer required, not a bare boolean. Fires ONLY on zero references (the bug condition), so refactors that move reads cannot FP. Failing message teaches the escape and cites in-file examples. Wire into CI alongside existing gates.

## Scope
- new check script (AST walk over src/rebar) + CI wiring
- '# read-via:' markers for any legitimately indirect current fields (enumerate at implementation; expected small)

## Testing
Unit: field with a read passes; field with zero reads fails naming the field; read-via marker with pointer passes; marker without pointer fails. Full-tree run clean at merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CI fails when any schema field has zero read sites and no read-via marker; message teaches remediation.
- [x] Marker requires a pointer/reason; bare markers rejected.
- [x] Zero-reference-only firing (no change-detector behavior on refactors).
- [x] Tree clean at landing with justified markers only.
baseline.summary: Config-is-read DET check: every _config_schema.py field must have a read site

baseline.description:
# S2 — honour `Retry-After` on 429, scoped to IDEMPOTENT READS

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260] (ten BLOCK rounds; full record on that ticket). S2 is the POLICY half; [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] (S1) was the mechanical relocation that made room for it. **S1 HAS LANDED** — Gerrit 1179, on `main` as commit `529e802da0`. `transport.py` is now 683 lines (117 of headroom under the locked 800 cap) and the retry cluster lives in `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`. **Every line citation in this plan was re-probed against that post-S1 tree**; the previous revision's citations were taken pre-S1 and were all stale, which is what a round of review correctly caught.

Jira Data Center has built-in rate limiting (8.6+, **DC only**, **OFF BY DEFAULT** — an admin enables it), a per-user token bucket. rebar's DC transport does not handle it: `_with_connection_retry` retries only connection-level faults and its docstring states that `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` — any HTTP 4xx/5xx — is NOT in the retry set, so a 429 propagates as a hard failure on the first occurrence, on an instance that was merely asking rebar to slow down.

Two constraints shape the whole fix:
1. **A static pacing policy is NOT implementable.** The limit is admin-configured and may be absent
   entirely (pre-8.6, Server, or simply disabled), so honour headers WHEN PRESENT and degrade
   gracefully when absent.
2. **Atlassian prescribes `Retry-After` PLUS up to 20% jitter**, which differs from ADR-0036's
   backoff curve (designed for transient connectivity, where the server offers no guidance).
   Jitter is not decoration: every rebar instance hitting the same bucket would otherwise retry in
   lockstep.

**VERIFY THE NUMBERS BEFORE BUILDING TO THEM** — "off by default", "8.6+" and "retry-after + 20% jitter" come from OSS research with Atlassian citations, not from testing, and that research retracted two of its other claims on a second pass.

## Approach

**Reuse what exists — do not build a third `Retry-After` implementation.** `_errors.parse_retry_after()` and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` already exist, `dispatch_one.py:41` already imports both, and `dispatch_one.py:148-172` is ALREADY a 429-honouring retry path for the REST transport. Read that path first and mirror it; a second parser is the finding that opened round 1.

**MIRROR IT, BUT NOT EXACTLY — one deliberate divergence, stated so it is not read as a slip.** That existing path applies `min(MAX_BACKOFF_S, retry_after)` with **no jitter** on the `Retry-After` branch (it jitters only the ADR-0036 curve, `dispatch_one.py:167-169`). Atlassian prescribes `Retry-After` PLUS up to 20% jitter for the DC token bucket, so this story's 429 branch jitters where the existing one does not. Reuse the PARSER and the CONSTANT; do not copy the delay arithmetic verbatim.

**SCOPE THE RETRY TO IDEMPOTENT READS. This is the load-bearing constraint.** `_with_connection_retry` is the single choke point for ALL 15 transport call sites INCLUDING `create_issue`, `add_comment` and `add_label`, and its docstring already records why JIRAError is unretried: "retrying a mutation on an HTTP error risks duplicates". Retrying 429s there would **reintroduce the duplicate-issue class [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] just fixed** — a 429 can arrive after the server began the write, and nothing in the response distinguishes that from rejection at the gate. So: per-CALL opt-in, **defaulting to OFF**, so a mutation added later cannot inherit the retry by omission.

**THE OPT-IN HAS TO REACH THE RETRY LAYER THROUGH TWO DISTINCT PATHS, NOT ONE.** A previous revision threaded the flag through `_call_logged` alone and was blocked for it; the correction is recorded here because the gap is invisible unless the call sites are read individually:

  * PATH A — `_paged_search` -> `_call_logged` -> `_with_connection_retry`. `_paged_search`
    (`transport.py:315`) issues its search through `_call_logged` (`transport.py:165`), which today
    calls `_with_connection_retry(fn)` with **no keyword argument at all**. So `_call_logged` is an
    EDIT TARGET, not merely a conduit: it must accept `rate_limit_retry` and forward it. Omitting
    it makes the flag a no-op that still type-checks.
  * PATH B — a DIRECT `_with_connection_retry` call that bypasses `_call_logged` entirely.
    `get_comment_map` fetches comments **one request per issue** at `transport.py:367`
    (`_with_connection_retry(lambda k=key: self._client.comments(k))`). That is the
    HIGHEST-VOLUME read in a pass and therefore the single most likely thing to trip a token
    bucket — and it is precisely the call PATH A does not reach. It opts in directly.

Getting only PATH A would ship a rate-limit fix that misses the read most likely to be rate limited, while every test written against `_paged_search` passed.

**WHAT ESCAPES WHEN THE CAP IS EXHAUSTED.** `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, never the raw `JIRAError`. This is not a preference: it is what the boundary already does. `_with_connection_retry` (now `retry.py:121`) catches the library error types and raises `_as_backend_http_error(exc) from exc`, which reads `.status_code` into `BackendHTTPError.code` using urllib's spelling SO THAT the core's existing `except urllib.error.HTTPError` branches classify a DC failure exactly as they classify a Cloud one. Leaking `JIRAError` past that boundary is the actual regression risk here, and J10 pinned the neutral exception contract precisely to stop it. (A library error with no usable status degrades to `code=0`, which no core branch mistakes for a 404 or a success.)

## Scope

Four files' worth of edits, and the opted-in read call sites are ENUMERATED HERE — this is the single enumeration in the document, and Testing and the ACs refer back to it rather than restating it. (The previous revision had Scope defer to Testing while Testing deferred to Scope, so neither listed anything; that circularity was a blocking finding.)

- `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — `_with_connection_retry` gains
  `rate_limit_retry: bool = False`; the 429 branch, `Retry-After` parsing, jitter-then-clamp.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`:
  - `_call_logged` (`:165`) — gains `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` and FORWARDS it. Without this
    edit the flag cannot reach the retry layer from `_paged_search` at all.
  - `_paged_search` (`:315`) — gains `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` and forwards it to
    `_call_logged`. It **accepts and forwards**; it does NOT pass `True` unconditionally.

**THE OPTED-IN READ CALL SITES — FOUR, exhaustively** (line numbers probed on `main` at `529e802da0`, i.e. post-S1):
  1. `get_issuelinks_map` -> `self._paged_search(...)` at `transport.py:349` — passes `True`.
  2. `get_comment_map` -> `self._paged_search(...)` at `transport.py:363` — passes `True`.
  3. `get_comment_map`'s inner PER-ISSUE comment fetch at `transport.py:367` — a direct
     `_with_connection_retry` call (PATH B above) — passes `True`.
  4. `get_parent_map` -> `self._paged_search(query, fields="parent")` at `transport.py:461` —
     passes `True`.

**NOT in scope:** any mutation call site; any change to ADR-0036's connectivity backoff curve; any read not in the list of four above (every other read keeps today's behaviour, which is what the default-OFF flag guarantees).

## Testing

* **the cap-exhaustion contract** — a client that returns 429 forever: assert the escaping
  exception is `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, AND assert `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` does
  NOT escape. A test that only checks "it raised" passes while the vendor type leaks.
* **`Retry-After` is honoured when present** — the sleep is driven by the header, not the ADR-0036
  curve; jitter is applied and the result is CLAMPED to `MAX_BACKOFF_S`.
* **absent header degrades gracefully** — no header (limiter off / pre-8.6 / Server) behaves exactly
  as today.
* **MUTATIONS DO NOT RETRY, enumerated rather than sampled** — assert one 429 fails immediately for
  EVERY non-opting mutation member of the transport. Enumerate them explicitly; an ellipsis is how
  a later-added mutation silently inherits the retry.
* **the opt-in defaults to OFF** — a call that does not pass the flag does not retry a 429.
* **BOTH PATHS carry the flag** — one test per path, because they fail independently: a
  `_paged_search`-driven read (PATH A, exercising the `_call_logged` forward) and
  `get_comment_map`'s per-issue fetch (PATH B, the direct call). A single test over
  `_paged_search` would pass while the highest-volume read remained unprotected.
* **`_call_logged` still forwards nothing by default** — its existing callers (every other
  transport member) must be unaffected, asserted rather than assumed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] (S1) has LANDED — Gerrit 1179, `main` commit `529e802da0`;
      `transport.py` 789 -> 683 lines, `retry.py` created at 162 lines
- [ ] a 429 with a `Retry-After` header is retried on an opted-in READ, with jitter applied and the
      delay clamped to `MAX_BACKOFF_S`, asserted numerically
- [ ] `_errors.parse_retry_after` and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` are REUSED — a test or the diff shows
      no second parser and no second constant
- [ ] cap exhaustion raises `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, and a test asserts `JIRAError`
      does not escape the adapter boundary
- [ ] EVERY mutation call site still fails on the FIRST 429 — asserted per member over an explicit
      enumeration of the transport's mutation members, not a sample
- [ ] the opt-in parameter defaults to OFF on `_with_connection_retry`, on `_call_logged` and on
      `_paged_search`, asserted, so a future call inherits no retry by omission
- [ ] `_call_logged` ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS `rate_limit_retry`. This is an EDIT, not a pass-through
      that already works: today it calls `_with_connection_retry(fn)` with no keyword argument, so
      without this change the flag is a no-op that still type-checks
- [ ] `_paged_search` ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` — it does NOT pass
      `True` unconditionally. The decision, not a requirement to decide: an unconditional `True`
      would silently grant retry to every FUTURE caller of the helper, the same "inherits by
      omission" hazard the per-call opt-in exists to prevent
- [ ] ALL FOUR opted-in read call sites listed in Scope pass `True`, asserted PER SITE — including
      `get_comment_map`'s inner per-issue fetch, which does NOT route through `_paged_search` or
      `_call_logged` and is the highest-volume read in a pass
- [ ] the three researched numbers (DC-only, 8.6+, off-by-default; retry-after + up to 20% jitter)
      are each either confirmed against the target DC version or explicitly marked unverified
baseline.summary: S2 — honour Retry-After on 429, scoped to idempotent reads

baseline.description:
# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: E1 — Force measurement provenance into attested evidence

baseline.description:
## Finding

Future ChatGPT sessions may have the GitHub connector and repository visibility but lack a local clone, direct Gerrit access, shell network access, or a mounted Rebar tracker. Existing general agent guidance does not explain how to recognize this environment, what operations remain safe, or when ticket creation cannot be completed natively.

## Evidence

- `AGENTS.md:27-45` requires work to be found, created, claimed, and recorded in Rebar before implementation.
- `AGENTS.md:124-131` states that GitHub is a read-only mirror and all code changes land through Gerrit.
- `templates/rebar-usage.md:18-30` requires search-before-create and native Rebar create/claim/link commands.
- `docs/concurrency.md:21-26` defines the tracker as a dedicated orphan `tickets` branch with append-only event files.
- `docs/concurrency.md:171-176` requires all writes to use the lock-guarded append/commit path; raw hand-authored tracker mutations are unsafe.
- `docs/import-export.md:52-64` documents `rebar import` as the only sanctioned bulk-ingest path: it composes ordinary events through the normal locked write path (no raw-event injection), consumes NDJSON (`src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`), assigns fresh local ids/HLC timestamps, and is idempotent by `source_id` (the imported line's own `ticket_id` becomes the created ticket's `source_id`).
- `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s `required` array is `["schema_version", "ticket_id", "ticket_type", "title", "status"]`. **`rebar import` does not JSON-Schema-validate against this file** — `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` (lines 221-225) checks only `ticket_id`/`ticket_type` directly and, if either is missing, **silently skips the record with a logged warning** (`warn(f"skipping record without ticket_id/ticket_type: ...")`) via a bare `continue` — it does not raise, and does not check `schema_version`/`status`/`title` at all. The `skipped` counter (line 205, incremented at line 227) counts ONLY already-imported records (`sid in seen_source`) — a missing-`ticket_id`/`ticket_type` record is warned about but does **not** increment `skipped`; it is invisible to the return summary's counters and detectable only via the `warnings` list. A fallback payload missing a required field is therefore silently dropped on import (surfaced only in `warnings`, not in any counter), not rejected with an error.
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` documents the `create_ticket` MCP tool's input schema (title, ticket_type, description, parent_id, etc.).

## Remediation

Add concise ChatGPT-specific guidance that teaches sessions to detect connector-limited execution, prefer the installed native Rebar CLI/MCP when a valid tracker worktree exists, respect the GitHub-read-only/Gerrit workflow, and avoid inventing tracker state or substituting GitHub Issues. Define a safe fallback that prepares fully formed ticket content and reports the exact missing capability rather than claiming tickets were created. Document the exceptional import path for appending CLI-generated NDJSON without hand-authoring or mutating existing events.

**Capability check and decision rule (resolves T8 findings):** the environment capability check enumerates six dimensions — local checkout, native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` binary, tracker worktree (a directory containing a valid `tickets` branch checkout, confirmed via `rebar exists <known-id>` or equivalent), network/remote access, GitHub connector, and Gerrit availability. "Native ticket creation is impossible" is defined precisely as: **the tracker-worktree dimension fails** (no accessible `tickets` branch checkout) **AND** **the network/remote dimension fails or the native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` binary is unavailable** — i.e., the session cannot reach a real store through either the CLI, the MCP server, or a git-remote clone/fetch. Any other combination of capability failures does not trigger the fallback; the guidance must state this rule explicitly so an executor does not need to infer it.

**Fallback payload schema (resolves T8 finding on AC6, and round-2 findings G6/T1):** the reviewable ticket payload MUST conform to `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s actual `required` array — `schema_version`, `ticket_id`, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status` — plus `description` (including a `## Acceptance Criteria` block) and `parent_id` if applicable. This resolves an apparent conflict: a never-yet-created ticket has no rebar-assigned id, but the schema's `ticket_id` is **not** a rebar-assigned id here — it is a **provenance id the agent generates itself** (a stable UUID4), which becomes the imported ticket's `source_id` on `rebar import` (per `docs/import-export.md`'s idempotent-by-`source_id` behavior) — re-running the same fallback payload through `rebar import` later is then a no-op, not a duplicate. The guidance must state each field's fallback value precisely: `schema_version: 1`, `ticket_id: <agent-generated UUID4, becomes source_id on import>`, `status: "open"`, `ticket_type`/`title`/`description` from the ticket content, `parent_id` if applicable — the same shape produced by `rebar export` and consumed by `rebar import`, so a maintainer can review it and optionally ingest it via `rebar import` without hand-transcription.

**Exceptional import mechanism (resolves E4 and G6 findings on AC7):** the only sanctioned exceptional import path is `rebar import` (or the library's `rebar.import_tickets()`), which is the native locked write path already documented in `docs/import-export.md` — never raw event-file injection and never a GitHub Contents API write to the `tickets` branch. The guidance must state precisely what this path does, not assert unverified behavior: it accepts NDJSON compiled-state projections conforming to the fallback payload schema above (not raw event files), assigns fresh local ids and HLC timestamps to each ticket (source provenance preserved via `source_id`/`source_created_at`/`source_author`), and is idempotent by `source_id`. Before invoking it, the operator confirms the target branch is current (`git fetch` + `rebar exists <known-id>` against the intended tracker) and runs `rebar import --dry-run` first — but the guidance must state its actual, narrower guarantee precisely: in dry-run mode (`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` ~lines 144-161), a record missing `ticket_id`/`ticket_type` hits a bare `continue` with **no counter increment and no warning at all** (the `warnings` list is never populated in the dry-run branch); only already-imported records (a `source_id` already present in the target) increment `skipped`. So a malformed record is invisible to `would_create`/`skipped` individually, but **is** detectable by comparing `would_create + skipped` against the total NDJSON line/record count: any shortfall is exactly the count of malformed (missing `ticket_id`/`ticket_type`) records, since those are the only category dry-run drops without incrementing either counter. Afterward, the operator runs `rebar validate` (or `rebar fsck`) against the tracker to confirm store integrity.

Cascade flag: guidance must remain consistent with Rebar's append-only, optimistic-concurrency, and native-command invariants; it must not normalize direct contents-API writes as the ordinary workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ChatGPT-specific guidance file or clearly labeled section is discoverable from `AGENTS.md` without bloating the canonical startup context. Verify: `grep -qi 'chatgpt' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Guidance includes an environment capability check covering local checkout, native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp`, tracker worktree, network/remote access, GitHub connector, and Gerrit availability. Verify: `grep -qi 'tracker worktree' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'gerrit' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance states that the GitHub repository is a read-only mirror for code changes and that GitHub Issues are not a substitute for the Rebar tracker. Verify: `grep -qi 'read-only mirror' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance requires search-before-create and native parent/child creation whenever the live tracker is accessible. Verify: `grep -qi 'search-before-create' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance prohibits hand-authoring, modifying, or deleting event files and explains the append-only reason. Verify: `grep -qi 'append-only' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance defines precisely when native ticket creation counts as "impossible" (the tracker-worktree-and-network/binary decision rule above) and, in that case, requires producing a reviewable ticket payload conforming to `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s required fields (`schema_version: 1`, an agent-generated UUID4 `ticket_id`, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status: "open"`, plus `description` with an Acceptance Criteria block and `parent_id` if applicable) plus a transparent capability-gap report, without claiming persistence occurred. Verify: `grep -qi 'export.schema.json' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'schema_version' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] The documented exceptional import mechanism names `rebar import` (or `rebar.import_tickets()`) as the only sanctioned path — never raw event-file injection or Contents API writes — states it accepts NDJSON (not raw events), assigns fresh local ids/HLC timestamps, correctly describes missing-`ticket_id`/`ticket_type` records as silently skipped with NO warning and NO counter increment in `--dry-run` mode specifically (only already-imported records increment `skipped` there), recommends detecting malformed records via a `would_create + skipped == total record count` comparison, requires confirming the target branch head before invocation, and requires running `rebar validate` or `rebar fsck` afterward. Verify: `grep -qi 'rebar import' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'rebar validate\|rebar fsck' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'dry-run' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] A lightweight documentation test (`tests/unit/test_chatgpt_guide_links.py`) asserts each of the following specific invariants against `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md` and `AGENTS.md`, and exits 0 only if ALL hold:
  1. `AGENTS.md` links to `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md` (discoverability).
  2. The guide does not recommend GitHub Issues as a substitute for the Rebar tracker (no phrase matching "github issues" co-occurring with "instead of"/"substitute for"/"in place of" the tracker).
  3. The guide does not describe a direct GitHub Contents-API write to the `tickets` branch as a sanctioned or normal path (no phrase pairing "contents api" with "tickets branch" in an affirmative/how-to context).
  4. The guide names `rebar import` (not a raw event-file write) as the only sanctioned exceptional ingest mechanism.
  5. The guide's fallback-payload field list matches `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s actual `required` array (`schema_version`, `ticket_id`, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status`).
baseline.summary: Document safe ChatGPT workflows for connector-limited Rebar environments
