## Why

Workflow-vs-bespoke parity nit found in tepid-bus-pomp review: bespoke `pass4_coach` returns `[]` with
NO LLM call when there are 0 surviving advisories; the workflow ALWAYS runs the `coach_notes` prompt
step, so a clean PASS (0 advisories) still makes one wasted coach LLM call (and a coach listing over an
empty set). Pre-dates B5 — the coach step has always run since B2. Gate it to match bespoke.

## What

- Gate the workflow `coach_notes` prompt step on `surviving > 0` (a `when:` condition) so a PASS with 0
  surviving advisories makes no coach LLM call.
- Keep the `coach_inputs` / `coach` ops behaving correctly (empty coaching list) when skipped.

## Scope

In scope: the `when:` gate on the `coach_notes` step in
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` (both the agentic and single-turn branches) and a test
asserting the coach call count is 0 on a 0-surviving PASS. Out of scope: WS1 migration, WS2 model/editor,
WS3 chunking. This story is independent of the others and can land in parallel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The workflow `coach_notes` step is gated on `surviving > 0` (in both the agentic and single-turn
      branches).
- [ ] A PASS with 0 surviving advisories makes no coach LLM call; a test asserts the call count is 0.
- [ ] A PASS/BLOCK with ≥1 surviving advisory still runs the coach step (no regression).
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: WS4: Gate workflow coach_notes on surviving>0 (bespoke parity, no coach call on clean PASS)

## Context

Sibling-emitted candidate fixture specs assert a criterion should fire or stay silent for a real plan — from history, not current code. One run cannot settle it — byte-identical material flipped verdict in 208 of 551 pairs, so shipped specs use `epochs: 3`/`gate: at_least(2)`.

## Approach

**Rehydrate, then run.** The selector manifest lists candidates per criterion, each carrying `direction` (fire/no_fire) and a `review_event_uuid` — the join key to the review sidecar (`fixture_selection.py` schema, shared with the emitter prerequisite). A candidate's emitter `input` is a model-free provenance descriptor, NOT plan text, so the finder never runs on it. It loads the sidecar corpus the selector used (`corpus.build_corpus`, persisting verified rows of at-review material keyed by `review_event_uuid`; `corpus.py:_build_sidecar_row`), and REHYDRATES each case's finder input from the matched row: `description` as plan text. Container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) are SCOPED OUT before any finder call (see Non-goals): the corpus persists `children` as bare ticket-id strings only. A candidate resolving to no verified row is withheld to drift as unrecoverable material (no finder call). It runs the criterion's current Pass-1 finder via `eval_solver.run_case(...)` (`eval_solver.py:322`) with `case["input"]` the rehydrated material (not `calibrate_criterion`). Each case runs three times; `_fired(verdict)` (a finding present) is the observed verdict; a case matching its `expect` (`finding`/`pass`) in ≥2 of 3 runs REPRODUCES (current code still agrees with history).

**Disposition.** A reproducing case is kept; a non-reproducing one is withheld to a drift report at `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/fixtures/drift-report.md` (criterion, case id, predicted vs observed, originating review `(ticket_id, review_event_uuid)`). To write a spec the runner reuses the emitter's strict-only skeleton (`prompt`, `model`, `epochs`, `gate`, `coverage_threshold`, `scorers`) UNCHANGED, and rebuilds `dataset` + `gold_set` (1:1) from only the reproducing cases, each case's `input` the runnable rehydrated material. The spec is written to `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml` via a temp file + atomic `os.replace` only when the filtered dataset is balanced (both sides non-empty), `gold_set` non-empty, and `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` returns zero errors; else withheld. The runner returns an in-memory summary (admitted/withheld ids, drift, spend); only the drift report and admitted specs are written.

**No-shadowing guard.** A user `.rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml` WINS over a packaged built-in at load, so the runner SKIPS any criterion packaged in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`.

**Budget enforcement.** Before each criterion the run pre-flights `ledger.reserve(estimate_usd, cap_usd=250.0, reserve_usd=0.0)` against this epic's ledger `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/fixtures/ledger.jsonl` (reserve_usd=0 ⇒ ceiling $250), then `finalize()`s priced ACTUAL usage. After each `finalize` the run re-reads cumulative spend and halts FATALLY before the next criterion if it meets/exceeds `cap_usd`, so $250 bounds finalized spend. The estimate tier follows `exec` routing (`criteria.effective_routing`, ADR 0033): AGENT→`criteria-eval-agent`, else `criteria-eval-cheap`; `exec: DET` out of scope. Model parity pinned to production Pass-1 (ADR 0109).

**Failure disposition.** Per criterion the two writes are STRICTLY ORDERED — atomic spec `os.replace` FIRST, ledger `finalize()` SECOND — with the ledger the sole resume oracle: a criterion is done iff its stable `run_id = f"admission-{prompt_id}"` is in the ledger. Crash before the ledger row ⇒ resume re-derives, overwriting the orphan spec; crash after ⇒ the spec exists. A transient model/transport error is RETRYABLE (3×, exp backoff 1s/2s/4s); on exhaustion the criterion is left incomplete (no ledger row; run continues). Both a `reserve` `BudgetExceeded` and the post-`finalize` cap breach are FATAL, stopping with finalized criteria admitted; `reconcile` recharges no recorded `run_id`.

## Scope

The admission runner, its rehydration/disposition logic, the drift-report writer, and the `.rebar/evals/` specs.

## Non-goals

Container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) are OUT of the runner: the corpus persists children as bare ids (no per-child title/description), so a rehydrated container case scores the finder over an impoverished roster — UNFAITHFUL to the historical review (whose finder read full child state), and `material_fingerprint` (children hashed by id) cannot detect the loss. Each is withheld `container-material-unrecoverable` pending faithful per-child capture (follow-up ticket). Repairing drift (each entry becomes a ticket linked `discovered_from` the epic); editing `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`; scheduling re-runs (the self-healing loop owns it).

## Testing

Unit tests drive disposition with a scripted stub solver and stub sidecar index (no model); the live run covers the real path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A must-fire case whose `review_event_uuid` resolves to a sidecar row runs the finder on that
      row's rehydrated `description`, not the descriptor; scripted (fire, fire, silent) it is admitted
      with that material as its `input` (`pytest`).
- [x] A must-fire case scripted (fire, silent, silent) is withheld with a drift entry
      (its originating review `(ticket_id, review_event_uuid)`); a case whose `review_event_uuid`
      matches no verified row is likewise withheld as unrecoverable material, no finder call
      (`pytest`).
- [x] With the ledger at the ceiling, the first `reserve` raises `BudgetExceeded` and a
      call-counting stub reports `0` model calls (`pytest`).
- [x] When a finalized criterion's ACTUAL spend reaches/passes `cap_usd`, the run halts before the
      next criterion (the breaching one stays admitted); `pytest` prices rows above the estimate.
- [x] Every written spec passes the real `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` over each file
      (`pytest`).
- [x] A criterion matching a packaged built-in in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` is skipped while a
      same-id `.rebar/evals/` prior artifact is NOT; `pytest` asserts written and packaged basenames are
      disjoint and the seeded id was processed.
- [x] A criterion writes no `.eval.yaml` when its reproducing cases leave one side empty (drifting
      its cases) or when a case raises before all finish (no partial file) (`pytest`).
- [x] Resume is crash-consistent (`pytest`): a re-run recharges no finalized criterion (`reconcile`
      returns the existing row, zero new calls); a spec file with no ledger row (crash between
      writes) is re-derived to one ledger row.
- [x] On a transient model/transport error the finder is retried 3×, then the criterion is left
      incomplete (no `.eval.yaml`, no ledger row) and the run continues (`pytest`, a stub raising
      transient errors).
- [x] [non-codebase] A live admission run has completed over the full candidate set with the Pass-1
      model pinned to its production class, and this epic's ledger records total spend >0 and ≤250.0
      with a per-pass model id on every row.
      provenance: environment=dev workstation, production Bedrock chain (bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8); principal=RebarBotNava <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — production Pass-1 at parity; ledger $11.65, 15 admitted rows (G3/G4 withheld container-material-unrecoverable).
- [x] [non-codebase] Each drift-report entry has a ticket linked `discovered_from` the parent epic.
      provenance: environment=production rebar tickets store; principal=RebarBotNava <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — 71 tickets linked discovered_from the epic.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`/`make typecheck`/`make test` pass; live run completed; drift report and admitted specs committed; ledger spend ≤ $250.

## Target
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — **786 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (14 lines of headroom).

Fourteen lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split _commands/init.py (786 LOC) along its concern boundary

## Context
The coordinator and fuse remain inert until non-create families route through them. Cutover must preserve independent work, explicitly defer matching plans, and prove the new fuse would not have prematurely stopped historical successful or partially successful jobs.

## Outcome
Make typed coordination authoritative for non-create families behind an internal per-family rollback selector, persist explicit deferral metadata, add the new endpoint-failure scoped fuse (retaining the blast-radius mass-mutation guard `classify.check_blast_radius`), and emit exact pass outcomes.

## Plan
1. Venue-gate verified-fake Cloud/DC summary behavior, then change the internal operation-family default from legacy to coordinator; never dual-send.
2. Route update, delete, probe, clean-label, repair-property, and conflict plans through coordinator/fuse. Preserve successful effects and recover rollback by re-observation.
3. Defer remaining matching plans with scope/reason/`retry_not_before`; let independent scopes continue.
4. Preserve exact applied/failed/deferred/skipped/recovered tallies and nonzero degraded-pass signaling.
5. Replay the sanitized 1,200-run completed GitHub Actions slice. Count only normalized terminal outcomes, never warning/grep text, and prove zero premature termination of observed successful/partial work.

## Testing
Verified-fake batches assert wire order/call ceilings/tallies/logs/exit. Historical replay names any counterfactual stop and blocks if it predates observed later success.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Each non-create family has one coordinator route and one internal legacy rollback value with no dual-send.
- [x] Venue-gated Cloud/DC verified fakes pass before the coordinator default changes.
- [x] Matching remaining work is deferred with exact scope, reason, and `retry_not_before`, while independent scopes continue.
- [x] Applied, failed, deferred, skipped, and recovered tallies plus degraded exit status are exact.
- [x] Migrated families route failure fusing through the new endpoint-failure scoped fuse; legacy ad-hoc retry nesting is unreachable for them and the blast-radius mass-mutation guard remains in force.
- [x] Historical replay of the completed 1,200-run slice shows zero premature stop before observed successful or partially successful work.

## Out of scope
Create coordination remains S4; final legacy removal remains S5.
## Impacted sites (existing dispatch seams the cutover rewires)
Routes the S3 T1 coordinator + T2 fuse into real non-create dispatch behind the landed per-family selector; additive, never dual-send. (Wiring detail: see "Reuse the landed cutover surface" below.)
- `applier.py` (**784 LOC — 16 under the 800 cap; MUST NOT grow past 800**): `_apply_batch` (:538)/`_apply_one` (:727) dispatch non-create families today. Gains ONLY a thin per-family route branch; net-new adapter lands in `batch_dispatch.py`.
- `dispatch_apply_phases.py` (694): legacy ad-hoc nested `_call_with_retry` (:76) becomes UNREACHABLE for migrated families (they fuse through `pass_fuse` via `coordinate_and_fuse`).
- `batch_dispatch.py` (361): landed cutover surface (`route_for`/`coordinate_and_fuse`/`CutoverReport`/`build_pass_tally`) — consumed and extended with the guard-hosting `execute` adapter + outcome→manifest mapper.
- `coordinator.py`/`pass_fuse.py` (S3 T1/T2), `classify.check_blast_radius` (blast-radius guard, DISTINCT from the fuse, retained in force AC5) — consumed as-is.
- `tests/fixtures/reconciler/rp03_fuse_completed_slice.json`: sanitized synthetic 1,200-run completed slice; replay counts only normalized terminal outcomes and shows zero premature stop (AC6).

Create coordination (S4) and final legacy removal (S5) stay out of scope.

## Guard preservation on the coordinator route (G6)
`coordinator.coordinate(ticket_plans, *, execute, locate, budget_factory)` is a PURE decision core (zero I/O, no clock); its injected `execute(plan, mutation)` closure is the SOLE side-effect channel, invoked ONCE per mutation in dependency order. Every legacy `_apply_batch` guard is preserved by hosting it at the SAME point relative to each physical invocation — none is lost to the pure core.

Per-mutation guards → inside the `execute` closure, before each dispatch (same order as the legacy loop, applier.py:658-662):
- Lost-lease `abort_check()` (applier.py:660): called FIRST in the closure — a lost ref-lock lease still raises `ReconcileLockLost` before any routed mutation issues.
- HEAD-drift recheck (`_recheck_drift`, applier.py:697 via :662): the closure re-pins HEAD + runs the same benign-tolerant check before each mutation; hostile drift still raises `HeadDriftError`. Head-pin state threads through the closure, not the core.
- rebar-id audit: the closure delegates each op to the existing per-call `dispatch_one`, which stamps the `rebar-id:<local_id>` label (dispatch_one.py:153/:247) — provenance unchanged.

Batch-precondition guards → on the full migrated set BEFORE `coordinate()`, fail-closed, exactly as `_apply_batch` today (applier.py:631):
- Cross-project guard (bug 626d, `_cross_project_targets` applier.py:231 via :631): offender refusal runs before any mutation issues; a cross-project target still fails closed.
- Blast-radius guard (`classify.check_blast_radius`): retained unchanged — DISTINCT from the fuse (AC5).

The core owns ONLY bucketing, dependency ordering, scope isolation and re-observation recovery; all imperative safety I/O stays in the closure/preconditions.

## Reuse the landed cutover surface (no new module)
The live reroute REUSES the already-landed pipeline in `batch_dispatch.py` — it adds NO parallel module. Enumerated landed surface consumed as-is:
- `route_for` (batch_dispatch.py:197): the per-family `coordinator|legacy` selector (non-create families default coordinator; `legacy` is the internal rollback value, AC1); the branch calls it.
- `coordinate_and_fuse` (batch_dispatch.py:294): accepts the injected `execute` closure, runs `coordinator.coordinate` then folds terminal outcomes through `pass_fuse`, returning `CutoverReport` (outcomes + five-bucket `tallies` + `fuse_decisions` + `degraded`). The reroute calls THIS; it is not reimplemented.
- `CutoverOutcome`/`CutoverReport`/`_fuse_one` (batch_dispatch.py:221/:235/:256) and `build_pass_tally` (:345): consumed for the outcome→live-tally/manifest mapping.

Net-new wiring (small, lands in batch_dispatch.py at 361 LOC — ample headroom — NOT applier.py):
1. An `execute(plan, mutation)` adapter builder that hosts the per-mutation `abort_check()` + HEAD-drift recheck (threading head-pin/concurrency/repo_root state) and delegates each physical op to the existing per-call dispatch (`dispatch_one`), preserving the `rebar-id:<local_id>` audit stamp.
2. A `CutoverReport`→manifest/five-bucket-tally mapper feeding the existing LIVE degraded-exit machinery (via `derive_pass_tally`).
`applier.py` `_apply_batch` gains ONLY a thin per-family branch: after the resident cross-project (bug 626d) + blast-radius batch preconditions, migrated families dispatch via `coordinate_and_fuse` with the adapter; non-migrated/create stay on the verbatim legacy loop. applier.py stays <800 LOC.

## Deferral metadata consumer + retirement
The fuse and its open scopes are PER-PASS, in-memory, zeroed each `reconcile_once` (S3 T2 contract) — deferral state is NOT persisted cross-process. A `scope_deferred` plan is simply not applied this pass; `scope`/`reason`/`retry_not_before` ride the deferral metadata as observability + the next pass's normal eligibility hint. The CONSUMER is the next reconcile pass's standard pending-work scan, which re-derives the plan from the store and re-evaluates it fresh; RETIREMENT is automatic (the in-memory scope evaporates at pass end). No new durable queue or cross-pass reader is introduced (that stays S4/S5 scope).
baseline.summary: RP-03 S3 T3 — Cut over non-create routing with exact deferral and tally semantics

baseline.description:
## Context
Investigation absurd-zoometric-bobwhite measured 229,222,450 bytes of repeated comment bodies embedded in active and retired snapshots. Current compaction (`compact_plan.needs_folding`) writes the complete reduced ticket state whenever foldable active events exceed the fixed threshold of 10 (`compact.threshold`), then permanently retains the prior snapshot and folded sources append-only (I1, `*.retired`). For a large state that keeps growing, this creates superlinear retained snapshot bytes even after the producer defect stops.

This work must preserve the concurrency and recovery contracts established by ADR 0035 and the out-of-band compaction sweep: conservative fold horizon, rebuild-on-stray, first-snapshot backfill, deterministic replay, authorship-ledger preservation, crash recovery, and two-clone merge-as-union safety. It is research first; no production cadence change is authorized until the findings are reviewed and any required ADR completes RESEARCH -> DRAFT -> HOLD -> MERGE.

## Plan
- Build a deterministic large-ticket benchmark that separates source-event bytes, active-snapshot bytes, retired-snapshot bytes, snapshot count, and replay latency under the current fixed threshold.
- Compare the current policy against a geometric schedule and a byte/replay-cost-aware schedule on the identical workload.
- Evaluate every candidate against ADR 0035, the six-hour out-of-band sweep, mixed-version rollback, crash recovery, and stale two-clone reconvergence.
- Recommend a concrete trigger and numeric growth/read-cost targets, with rejected alternatives and unresolved assumptions explicit.
- Record findings on the ticket and, if a cadence change is warranted, recommend an ADR and decompose implementation into independently reviewable tasks (a separate discovered_from ticket); do not implement here.

## Testing / Verification
- The deterministic benchmark is archived as a ticket comment and run with `python bench_snapshot_cadence.py` (worktree venv). Verification is the printed table: the fixed-count control must show retired-snapshot bytes growing quadratically (double the events -> ~4x bytes) while the geometric and byte-cost candidates stay linear.
- Contract findings are verified by tracing each candidate through `compact_plan.needs_folding` / `compact_txn` and ADR 0035, confirming the cadence changes only the WHEN trigger and not snapshot placement, `source_event_uuids`, retire/restore, or replay: `checked: code-read of src/rebar/_commands/compact_plan.py and compact_txn.py against docs/adr/0035-rc2b-snapshot-horizon-safe-replay.md`.
- Deliverable completeness is verified by confirming every acceptance criterion below has an explicit finding recorded in the ticket comments: `checked: rebar show melancholy-couped-turkey` lists the findings comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The benchmark (`python bench_snapshot_cadence.py`) reproduces full-state snapshot amplification under the fixed-threshold control and reports source-event bytes, active-snapshot bytes, retired-snapshot bytes, snapshot count, and replay latency.
- [x] Fixed-count, geometric, and byte/replay-cost-aware candidates are each measured on the identical fixture and workload, with their five measures recorded.
- [x] Each candidate has an explicit pass/fail finding for conservative-horizon behavior.
- [x] Each candidate has an explicit pass/fail finding for rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, mixed-version rollback, and two-clone union convergence.
- [x] The recommendation states the exact trigger, the configuration/migration behavior, the expected asymptotic bound, and the measured bound.
- [x] No production implementation begins in this ticket; if a cadence change is warranted, an ADR is recommended and implementation is decomposed into a linked discovered_from ticket.

## Context / Problem

Once a store actually syncs more than one tracker project, an older rebar binary reading it is dangerous rather than merely limited: it would fetch only its single configured project, see every other project's bound tickets as having no corresponding remote issue, and create duplicate issues in the wrong project. There is a shipped mechanism for exactly this — `.store-compat.json` with a fail-closed read (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`) — but `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is still an empty frozenset (`compat.py:60`), so no capability has ever been declared through it.

## Approach

Register `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. That single addition is what makes a binary able to *recognise* the capability; a binary that predates it hits the "required capability this binary does not provide" branch and raises `StoreIncompatibleError`, refusing writes rather than corrupting the store (`docs/migrations.md:158-165`).

This is the expand half of the expand/contract rollout `docs/migrations.md:138-149` describes: teach binaries to read and fail closed **before** anything writes the requirement. Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story, so shipping it changes no behaviour for any existing store. The conditional stamp lands separately, which is why the two are ordered rather than combined.

Reads deliberately stay available: the gate is on the write lock only (`docs/migrations.md:174-178`), so `list`/`show`/`search` keep working against a store an old binary may not write, and `fsck` surfaces the condition as a structured `compat_error` without changing its exit code.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's pure-branch row: an in-process unit test against the real classification function, since the mechanism is entirely a validation branch with no I/O of its own — plus one real-store test for the write-gate, because the gate fires inside lock acquisition and a unit test would not cross that component.

- Happy path: a record declaring `multi-project-bridge` classifies as compatible on a binary that
  registers it.
- Contrast case: a record declaring an unregistered capability name still raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError` — proving the registration widened the known set by exactly one entry and
  did not disable the check.
- Absent-record regression: a store with no `.store-compat.json` still passes through as implicit
  legacy, so pre-feature stores are unaffected.
- Write-gate path: a store whose record declares an unknown capability refuses a write through the
  real lock acquisition, while `list`/`show` against the same store still succeed. The read half is
  the contrast case that proves the gate is scoped to writes.
- Corrupt-record path: a malformed record still raises rather than being treated as absent, which is
  the bypass the gate is designed to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `multi-project-bridge` is in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` and a record declaring it classifies as
      compatible; checked by a unit test over the classification function.
- [x] A record declaring an unregistered capability still raises `StoreIncompatibleError`; checked by
      the paired negative case.
- [x] A store with no compat record still passes through as implicit legacy; checked by an
      absent-record regression test.
- [x] A store declaring an unknown capability refuses writes while reads still succeed; checked by a
      real-store test exercising the write lock and a read command against the same store.
- [x] A corrupt record raises rather than being treated as absent; checked by a malformed-record test.
baseline.summary: Register the multi-project-bridge store-compat capability (expand half)

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` measures **771 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that fans the fetch out over several projects rewrites the query construction in `_build_snapshot` and will not fit in 29 lines.

## Approach

Extract the pagination cluster into a new `fetch_paging.py`: `_ACLI_CEILING` and `SilentTruncationError` (`:99-120`), `_extract_issues` (`:251-262`), `_iter_pages` (`:265-390`) and `collect` (`:392-399`).

The call chain is genuine and self-contained: `collect` calls `_iter_pages` (`:397`), which calls `_extract_issues` (`:296`) and raises `SilentTruncationError` (`:308,343,355`) against `_ACLI_CEILING` (`:354`). Nothing in the cluster calls back upward; `_build_snapshot` reaches it only through `_iter_pages` (`:554`). The new module's complete import list is `annotations` and a `TYPE_CHECKING` import of `TicketTransport` — the pagination code is otherwise pure.

This extraction is well matched to the incoming change, which rewrites the `queries` tuple at `_build_snapshot:548-554` into a per-project loop over `jqls_for` — all of which stays in `fetcher.py`.

**Three things must stay resident**, and getting any of them wrong breaks tests silently:

- `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (`:105`) stays — `_build_snapshot:550` uses it. Only `_ACLI_CEILING` moves.
- `_load_acli` and `_load_alert_store` stay — they carry **25** and **3** `patch.object(fetcher, ...)`
  sites respectively, and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move. Both are called
  from `_build_snapshot` (`:523,536`), which stays, so no patch site is disturbed.
- `fetcher.py` re-exports **all four** moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`,
  `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` — because every one of them is reached as an attribute
  of `fetcher` by existing tests, and an attribute access does not follow a moved symbol:
  - `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py:118,139`), plus further
    `fetcher._iter_pages` / `fetcher.collect` accesses in the same file and in
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py`;
  - `fetcher.SilentTruncationError`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_pagination_jql.py:133,165`) as well as the
    explicit `from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import SilentTruncationError` at
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:32`;
  - `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` (`test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:149`), which reads the constant
    directly to size its fixture. This one is easy to miss precisely because the constant looks
    private and unshared.

The re-export keeps roughly 48 existing references green across six test modules. Note that the two production mentions of `fetcher._iter_pages` — `_backend.py:62` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:139,153` — are **docstring prose** recording bug history, not runtime references, so no production module needs an edit.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~195 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — drops to ~606 lines, plus a re-export block

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. The risks are attribute presence and patch survival, so both are asserted rather than assumed:

- Attribute-surface assertion: `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
  both hold after the move, and `SilentTruncationError` still imports from `fetcher`.
- Patch survival: the tests that `patch.object(fetcher, "_load_acli")` and `"_load_alert_store"` pass
  unedited, proving those symbols stayed resident and are still resolved from `fetcher`'s globals.
- Truncation behaviour preserved: a fixture exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` still raises
  `SilentTruncationError` through the real `collect → _iter_pages` path — the contract most at risk
  from moving the constant away from its raiser.
- One-way import: `fetch_paging` must not import `fetcher`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fetcher.py` and `fetch_paging.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the module-size
      gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] All four moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`, `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` —
      still resolve as attributes of `fetcher`; checked by a test asserting each by attribute access,
      which covers the two existing `hasattr` assertions and the direct `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` read.
- [ ] `_load_acli`, `_load_alert_store` and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` remain defined in `fetcher.py`;
      checked by asserting each is in that module's own namespace, not merely importable.
- [ ] A fixture exceeding the ceiling still raises `SilentTruncationError` via the real paging path;
      checked by the existing pagination held-out test running unedited.
- [ ] `fetch_paging.py` does not import `fetcher`; checked by a test importing the two modules in
      both orders and asserting `fetcher` is absent from `fetch_paging`'s imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the pagination cluster from fetcher.py into fetch_paging.py

baseline.description:
## Context

The `tickets` pack grows because enrichment writeback emits separate git commits that each re-emit the root tree. S1 reclaims historical churn; W1 reduces new post-enrich finalize churn at the source.

## Scope

Batch only the post-enrich finalize events for one successful enrichment item: `TICKET_DIGEST` + `DONE_ENRICH` collapse from two commits to one commit/root-tree re-emission. `CLAIM_ENRICH` remains its own committed and auto-pushed event, visible before the LLM/enrich call, because `_live_drainer_ids`, `_MAX_CONCURRENT_DRAINERS`, and `queue.claim()` arbitrate cross-clone drainers by reading committed post-enqueue `CLAIM_ENRICH` events. `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` remains unchanged as an earlier lifecycle event.

Preserve observable ticket state, event semantics, per-event signing/verifiability, and optimistic-concurrency guarantees. Batch the git commit only; each event remains its own event file with its own authorship material.

## Out of scope

History reclaim (S1); event schema changes; queue claim arbitration changes; drainer concurrency-cap changes; enqueue timing changes; folding `CLAIM_ENRICH` into a batch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The post-enrich finalize events (`TICKET_DIGEST` + `DONE_ENRICH`) for a single successful enrichment item collapse into ONE commit/root-tree re-emission on a fixture; `CLAIM_ENRICH` remains a separate committed event for cross-clone drainer arbitration.
- [x] Observable reduced ticket state is unchanged vs the pre-batch behavior (public-reader/reducer fixture passes).
- [x] Each batched event retains its individual signature and passes `rebar verify-authorship`.
- [x] Optimistic-concurrency / audit guarantees are preserved: existing drainer arbitration and concurrency tests pass, and `CLAIM_ENRICH` stays visible before enrichment.
- [x] Commits-per-enrich-burst and per-burst root-tree re-emissions drop from CLAIM + DIGEST + DONE (3 commits) to CLAIM + batched-finalize (2 commits); `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` remains a separate earlier lifecycle event.

## Portability

Pure library/store change; no dependence on any single CI provider.

## Implementation plan (2026-09-01, narrowed by operator decision)

### Worked example

For an already-soaked queued ticket, drain currently emits committed `CLAIM_ENRICH`, then after the LLM returns emits committed `TICKET_DIGEST`, then committed `DONE_ENRICH`. W1 keeps CLAIM exactly as-is. The normal-path finalize lane composes `TICKET_DIGEST {schema, digest, content_hash, model, digest_hash_version}` and `DONE_ENRICH {ticket_id}` as separate signed events but flushes them through one batch commit.

Partial-failure example: if digest event composition/signing is refused and `digest_sidecar.emit()` returns `False`, `queue.mark_done()` is still called exactly as current code does. The batch buffer contains whatever the existing helpers successfully composed (DONE only in that example) and flushes that. If the batch commit itself fails after events were composed, the helper logs and falls back to the existing sequential direct calls in order (`digest_sidecar.emit()` then `queue.mark_done()` outside the sink). This preserves the previous best-effort failure posture; the optimization is the normal successful path, not a new durability contract under store faults.

### Mechanism

1. In `rebar.llm.enrich_drain._finalize_claims`, replace the success path's two independent normal writes with an enrichment-local helper that opens `_commands._seam.batch_sink`, calls `digest_sidecar.emit(...)` and `queue.mark_done(...)` in the same order and with the same ignored return-value contract as today, then flushes the buffered events with `_store.event_append.batch_write_and_push()`.
2. Preserve helper best-effort semantics: composition/signing failures are swallowed by existing helpers; the following helper call still runs; an empty buffer returns without a commit. Batch commit failures degrade to the old sequential direct write path after rollback, with a warning.
3. Do not change `queue.enqueue`, `queue.claim`, `queue.mark_done`, `digest_sidecar.emit`, event schema, `_live_drainer_ids`, `_MAX_CONCURRENT_DRAINERS`, or queue reducers. The public event stream after successful finalize still contains the same `TICKET_DIGEST` and `DONE_ENRICH` events in order; only the wrapping git commit count changes.
4. Leave permanent-rejection tombstones and stale-writeback re-enqueue behavior unchanged. CLAIM remains outside the batch by design and visible before enrichment.

### Alternatives considered

A. Batch only the post-enrich finalize pair: chosen by the operator on 2026-09-01. B. Batch CLAIM with finalize using local reservations: rejected because committed CLAIM events are the cross-clone coordination contract. C. Hold the drain advisory lock across the LLM: rejected because existing concurrency work requires enrichment outside the advisory lock. D. Make the finalize pair strictly atomic with no fallback: rejected because W1 should not change best-effort store-fault behavior.

### Test plan / RED-first oracle

- Add a fixture test in `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`: enqueue a ticket, record tracker commit count, run one drain, and assert exactly two new commits: one containing `CLAIM_ENRICH`, and one containing both `TICKET_DIGEST` and `DONE_ENRICH`.
- Assert public postconditions in that fixture: digest present/fresh, queue `done == True`, `pending == False`, and sidecar events do not alter schema-visible ticket state.
- Run fixture-appropriate `rebar verify-authorship` after batched finalize to prove each batched event retains individual signing/verifiability.
- Run existing arbitration/concurrency tests, especially `test_concurrent_drains_make_zero_duplicate_llm_calls`, to prove `CLAIM_ENRICH` visibility is unchanged.
- Add a targeted partial-failure unit test by monkeypatching the batch flush to raise after buffered composition, asserting the old direct helper calls are invoked in order as fallback.
- Preflight with targeted pytest first, then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate before push.

### Surface-parity census

CLI command: in scope through `rebar enrich --drain`/`cmd_enrich` because it routes to `enrich_drain.drain`. MCP/API: no separate schema change; enrichment callers share the same library drain core, accepted residual gap unless a direct MCP enrich surface appears. Library facade: in scope through direct `enrich_drain.drain`, `queue`, and `digest_sidecar` fixture tests. Automated callers: in scope because `_store.event_append.write_and_push -> _maybe_enrich_drain -> maybe_drain -> drain` remains the automated path, with CLAIM still committed before enrichment. Read/dual direction: in scope through `latest_ticket_digest`, `freshness`, `queue.reduce_ticket`, and `pending_enrichment`; reducer-visible ticket state stays unchanged.

### Acceptance mapping

AC1/AC5: commit-count/root-tree tests showing CLAIM remains separate while finalize pair is one commit. AC2: public reducer/reader postconditions. AC3: authorship verification on the fixture. AC4: unchanged public queue contracts plus existing drain concurrency tests and fallback-order coverage.
baseline.summary: W1: batch enrichment quartet + digest into one write lane (cut ~14K commits/day at source)

## Summary

Split out of `e668-b496-e264-4283` per its plan review (finding G5: that ticket bundled two independently-releasable outcomes). This is the static half.

On 2026-08-26 a pytest test `subprocess`-exec'd a real shell script that performs `rm -rf "$dir"/*`, with the path variable set to `""`. The glob expanded to `rm -rf /*` and destroyed `/opt/homebrew` and every Homebrew-installed app in `/Applications`. The deeper defect is that a test asserting *"the guard rejects an unsafe path"* was able to delete anything at all: asserting on **what would have been deleted** is a strictly better oracle than observing a wiped directory.

The specific offending test is not on `main` (it lives on the unmerged `fix-mcp-clone-blocks-boot` branch), so this gates the **class** rather than that one file — consistent with how `check_raw_git_writes.py` and `check_wall_clock_asserts.py` already work in this repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A gate flags a test that `subprocess`-execs a shell script containing an
      unguarded destructive deletion (`rm -rf` against an interpolated variable).
      Verified by `python scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py`.
- [x] The gate passes a test whose script routes deletion through an injectable seam
      such as `"${RM_CMD:-rm}"`, so the recommended remediation is not itself flagged.
      Verified by a passing fixture in
      `tests/scripts/test_check_destructive_test_exec.py`.
- [x] The gate passes a script whose deletion is guarded by `: "${dir:?}"` plus an
      explicit deny-list, so hardened call sites are not flagged.
- [x] The gate reports `path:line` for each finding and exits non-zero, matching the
      output shape of `check_raw_git_writes.py`.
- [x] The gate runs in `make lint`. Verified by `make lint`.
- [x] Enforcement is in `make lint` (invoked by both the pre-commit hook and CI), not
      a CI-provider-specific step (`project.portability`).

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_check_destructive_test_exec.py` — flags the unguarded
  shape, passes the seamed shape, passes the `${dir:?}`-guarded shape.
- `make lint` — the gate is wired and the current tree is clean.
- `make typecheck` and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` — green.

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion above is checked by the command it names.
- The current tree passes the new gate, or each pre-existing finding is fixed or
  carries a targeted justification comment.

## Notes

Sibling of `e668-b496-e264-4283` (the OS sandbox, the dynamic half). This gate is static analysis and cannot stop a mutation at runtime — the sandbox is the load-bearing control; this catches the pattern before it lands.

## Summary
The tickets-branch push-retry logic resolves a non-fast-forward push with a "stash → merge → pop" dance, but the `git stash pop` is run **unconditionally and its return code is never checked**. When the stashed working-tree copy of a tracked bridge-state file (`.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json`, `.bridge_state/bindings.json`) conflicts with the freshly-merged upstream copy, the pop leaves **git conflict markers in the working tree and an unmerged (`UU`) index entry**. Nothing detects or repairs this, so the corruption is silently committed/left behind and wedges two subsystems:
- **Reconcile**: the read-side guard fail-closes every pass ("prev_snapshot.json is corrupt or contains git conflict markers … Aborting reconcile pass").
- **All store writes**: `git commit` refuses to commit with an unmerged path, surfacing to users as `git commit failed while holding lock` on any `rebar` write (claim/edit/transition/archive/…).

Observed live this session: a concurrent reconciler push-retry left `.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json` with `<<<<<<< Updated upstream` / `>>>>>>> Stashed changes` markers (stages 1/2/3 in the index). HEAD’s committed copy was clean — the corruption was purely the un-popped stash conflict in the worktree+index. `rebar archive` failed with `git commit failed while holding lock` until I restored the file to HEAD.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Have a local tickets worktree with modified, tracked `.bridge_state/*` files (normal reconciler state) AND an `origin/tickets` that is ahead and also touched those same files.
2. Trigger a write that auto-pushes (any `rebar` write) so the non-fast-forward push-retry path runs: merge fails "dirty working tree" → `git stash push` → `git merge` (updates `.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json` from upstream) → `git stash pop`.
3. The pop conflicts on `prev_snapshot.json` (both sides changed it).

**Expected:** the push-retry either resolves the bridge-state file deterministically (those files are reconciler-regenerable) or fails cleanly, leaving the worktree/index in a consistent, writable, reconcile-able state.

**Actual:** conflict markers + an unmerged `UU` index entry are left in `prev_snapshot.json`. Reconcile fail-closes on every subsequent pass, and every `rebar` store write fails with `git commit failed while holding lock`. Manual recovery is required (restore the file to HEAD, or delete it to force a full re-fetch).

## Root Cause
`src/rebar/_store/push.py:158-180` — the dirty-working-tree branch (bug 12a6): `git stash push` (160), `git merge` post-stash (166-173), then `git stash pop --quiet` at **line 174 with the comment "pop unconditionally"**. The pop’s return code is never inspected; a conflicting pop applies-with-conflict, keeps the stash, and leaves markers + an unmerged index. The `merge2.returncode` check (175) aborts only `merge2`, not a conflicted pop, and the clean-`merge2` path just `continue`s — so a successful merge2 + conflicting pop produces silent corruption.

Downstream guards behave correctly but only as fail-closed detectors, not repair:
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py:733-785` aborts the pass on a corrupt/conflict-marked `prev_snapshot.json` (SAFETY INVARIANT) — correct, but leaves reconcile wedged with only a manual-recovery message.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py:104` is the same corruption class for `bindings.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The push-retry stash-pop checks its result; a conflicting pop is detected and resolved (or the operation fails cleanly) — never silently leaving conflict markers / an unmerged index in `.bridge_state/*`.
- [ ] Because `.bridge_state/*` are reconciler-regenerable, the resolution should deterministically take one side (e.g. reset those paths to the merged HEAD / `--theirs`) and drop the stash, rather than leaving an unmerged entry.
- [ ] After a push-retry that hit a bridge-state conflict, the tickets worktree is left writable (no `UU`) and reconcile-able (valid JSON), with no manual intervention.
- [ ] A store write that encounters a pre-existing unmerged `.bridge_state/*` index entry self-heals (or fails with an actionable, non-cryptic error) instead of the bare `git commit failed while holding lock`.
- [ ] Regression test simulating a stash-pop conflict on `prev_snapshot.json` during push-retry asserts the worktree/index end consistent and both reconcile + the next store write succeed.

## Affected Files (initial)
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (`_push_tickets_branch` retry loop, stash→merge→pop)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` (prev_snapshot read guard — consider auto-recovery)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` (same corruption class for bindings.json)
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (the commit-under-lock path that surfaces the unmerged-index failure)
baseline.summary: Push-retry stash-pop leaves conflict markers in .bridge_state/*, wedging reconcile (fail-closed) AND all store writes

## Why
Intent-source fidelity (ISF) is the approved criterion that catches silent descoping of an EXTERNALLY-expressed
requirement (the gate's plan-internal blind spot). It has distinct mechanics, so it gets its own child.

## What
- Build ISF: a single-turn / 2-STEP, FRONTIER-model criterion, FED the linked session log + the pre-resolved
  ticket graph (NOT agent/tool-using); fires ONLY when the ticket is linked to a session log.
- Size handling: if the linked log exceeds the escalated context window, run ISF against a SUMMARY of the log,
  RECORD that a summary was used, and carry REDUCED CONFIDENCE (supporting context only — never the plan).
- Validate against the eval suite: recall (catches a seeded silently-dropped requirement), false-fire
  (no finding when the plan honors the intent or a requirement was descoped WITH a stated rationale).

## Scope
- The criterion + its session-log feeding/summary-fallback; validation via the eval suite (`7284`). THIS child
  OWNS the ISF criterion build (criterion + prompt + session-log gating); `7284` owns the eval suite/harness and
  adds ISF's eval cases — no duplication (see the `relates_to` link).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ISF implemented per its descriptor (single-turn/2-STEP, fed session log + ticket graph, NOT agent); fires only when a session log is linked.
- [ ] Oversized-log fallback: documented SUMMARY + reduced confidence (never summarizes the plan).
- [ ] Validated on labeled cases: catches a silently-descoped requirement (recall); no false-fire on honored/justified-descope plans.
baseline.summary: Intent-source-fidelity (ISF) criterion: build + validate

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

**This is a DIAGNOSABILITY fix, not a correctness one. The behaviour is already safe.** Read this first so nobody later mistakes it for another fail-open: bug `505d-b2c5-734f-47d9` made the claim gate fail CLOSED on a degraded basis, so whichever way the resolution fails the gate now refuses to certify. Nothing here changes a verdict. What is left is that an operator reading the box's logs cannot tell WHICH failure happened.

`gate_ref_hash_basis()` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py`, added by 505d) wraps the whole resolution in one broad `except Exception` and emits a single message:

    current gate-ref snapshot unavailable; hashing the working tree

Two materially different faults collapse into that one line:

1. **The ref does not resolve** — `resolve_ref(...)` raises `SnapshotRefError`. Benign and
   expected in an ephemeral clone: the review-bot's `clone_change_ref` does `git init` +
   `git fetch <url> <patchset-ref>` and configures no `origin` remote at all, so this fires
   on 100% of review-bot runs. It is NOT actionable.
2. **The ref resolved but the snapshot could not be materialized** — `_cache.acquire(...)`
   raises. On the box's blobless checkout this is the interesting case:
   `repo_snapshot._ensure_blobs_present` is documented "Deliberately BEST-EFFORT and silent
   on failure", so a failed blob top-up plus a failed lazy fetch surfaces here. Disk
   pressure, a corrupt or evicted cache entry, and a lock timeout land here too. This IS
   actionable.

Case 1 is routine noise; case 2 means the box cannot read the tree its gates are supposed to verify against. Today they are indistinguishable without attaching a debugger, so triage has to guess — and because case 1 is so loud, case 2 is easy to dismiss as more of the same.

## Expected Behavior

The log distinguishes the two, and the distinction is available to a caller that wants to report it. An unresolvable ref stays a low-noise, expected outcome; a materialization failure is identifiable as a distinct, operator-actionable fault.

## Approach

Keep it small. Inside `gate_ref_hash_basis` only:

1. Split the single `try` so `resolve_ref` and `_cache.acquire` are caught separately, and
   emit a distinct message for each (naming the ref in both cases; naming the resolved SHA
   in the materialization case).
2. Narrow the catches to what those calls actually raise (`SnapshotRefError` /
   `SnapshotFetchError` for the ref arm), keeping a broad backstop so the function retains
   its never-raises contract — that contract is load-bearing and must not regress.
3. Optionally record which of the two occurred on `GateRefBasis` (e.g. a `cause` field), so
   the claim gate's denial reason can say "could not be resolved" vs "could not be
   materialized". Only if it stays cheap; the log split is the required part.

## Out of scope

- Any change to WHETHER the basis degrades, or to the fail-closed guard 505d added.
- Any change to `_hash_basis`'s signature, contract, or working-tree fallback (ADR 0002; the
  operator-approved decision on `72d9-8fbd-3a9e-48a6`).

- Any new verdict literal. `bugfix_size_gate.KNOWN_VERDICTS` stays untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unresolvable gate ref and a failed snapshot materialization emit DISTINCT log
      messages, each naming the ref (and the materialization case naming the resolved SHA).
- [ ] `gate_ref_hash_basis` still never raises, and still returns the working-tree path with
      `degraded=True` for BOTH faults — the 505d fail-closed behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `source=local` is still not reported as degraded.
- [ ] A test drives both arms separately and asserts the two are distinguishable (the
      materialization arm by making `_cache.acquire` fail with the ref resolvable, so it is
      not merely the ref arm again).
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ref_coherence.py` stays green unchanged, including
      `test_attested_claim_gate_refuses_to_certify_when_the_gate_ref_is_unresolvable`.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default pytest suite exit zero.

baseline.description:
Mirror inventory finding F2 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), MEDIUM.

## Problem

The op-cert kind vocabulary has three masters:

- `src/rebar/signing.py:115` `OPCERT_KINDS` — canonical, and already EXPORTED in `__all__` at `:76`
- `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:38` `VALID_KINDS` — the same two, hand-copied
- `src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py:24` `_VALID_KINDS` — the same two again, plus a prose copy
  in `_USAGE` at `:23`

Neither consumer imports the exported name, and both gate client REQUEST VALIDATION: a kind present in `OPCERT_KINDS` but missing from a consumer's copy is silently rejected as invalid. Churn is low — ADR 0049 fixes the count at two — which is precisely why a miss would sit unnoticed.

## The consumers, and why a naive import would be WRONG

`OPCERT_KINDS` is a `frozenset` — UNORDERED. Both copies are ordered TUPLES, and three consumers depend on that:

- `_cli/_parsers/advanced/certs.py:51` — `choices=remote_cert._VALID_KINDS`. argparse renders
  `choices` into help and into its error text, so a frozenset makes both non-deterministic.
- `opcert_service/app.py:222` — `f"kind must be one of {list(jobs.VALID_KINDS)}"`, an
  order-visible API error message.
- `opcert_service/__init__.py:14,18` — re-exports `VALID_KINDS` in `__all__`. It is PUBLIC
  API, so changing its type is a breaking change independent of ordering.

(`app.py:217` is a membership test and is indifferent.)

## Approach — generate-from-canonical, preserving type and order

Both copies become `tuple(sorted(OPCERT_KINDS))`. Sorted order is `("completion-verifier", "plan-review")` — byte-identical to what both copies hold today, so every consumer above sees exactly what it sees now, while the MEMBERSHIP stops being a hand-copy. `_USAGE` prose is generated from the same tuple.

Deriving a frozenset here would have been the wrong fix, and that is the substance of this ticket: the canonical value and its consumers disagree about whether order is part of the fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: both copies are derived from `signing.OPCERT_KINDS` and neither re-lists the kinds.
      Verified by a test asserting each equals `tuple(sorted(OPCERT_KINDS))` and the literals are gone.
- [x] AC1b: both remain ORDERED TUPLES with their current order, so argparse `choices`, the
      `app.py:222` error message and the `opcert_service.__all__` export are unchanged. Verified by
      a test asserting the exact tuple value and its type.
- [x] AC2: `remote_cert`'s `_USAGE` names exactly the canonical kinds, generated not re-typed.
      Verified by a test comparing the usage text against the set.
- [x] AC3: a kind added to `OPCERT_KINDS` is accepted by both consumers with no further edit.
      Verified by a test that patches the canonical set and asserts both validators follow.
- [x] AC4: an unknown kind is still rejected at both sites. Verified by explicit rejection tests.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "opcert or remote_cert or signing" -q` — AC1-AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Single-source the op-cert kinds across signing, opcert_service and remote_cert (mirror F2)

Coupled to E5c: relocate the ticket_txn.py locked critical section into the rebar package so transition/claim run in-process without putting the engine dir on sys.path (test_engine_dir guard). Touches the single locked write path + the optimistic-concurrency exit-10 contract. Plan opus-reviewed (REVISE -> 11 revisions folded in). No bash deleted (back-loads to E7/E8). No kill-switch; rollback = git revert.

## What
Per-command pattern (E0-E2): characterize bash arm -> port reusing rebar.* (one source for error strings) -> route argparse in-process + rewire library off _run -> dual-run byte-parity test (tests/interfaces/test_e3_*.py) -> green commit + child ticket. Sub-commits:

  + hand-rolled rename/add/commit under ONE lock-hold (NOT stage_and_commit: re-locks per event +
  sorted bytes). Preserve json.dump(ensure_ascii=False). Convert sys.exit/stderr -> return + typed
  exceptions; old _engine/ticket_txn.py becomes a thin shim re-exiting 10/1/2. Preserve dual-leg
  fcntl+mkdir lock (stiff-mop-lane fix). Golden-bytes test (STATUS + CLAIM, before/after identical).
- Port ticket-unblock.py batch-close/newly_unblocked -> rebar/graph/_unblock.py (faithful: exclude

- claim: over claim_core; reproduce _emit_error_envelope stderr (ticket_not_found/concurrency_conflict/

Fold in: git config user.name -> "Unknown" fallback parity; 2-arg autodetect + =/space flag variants in parity scenarios; close bug stiff-mop-lane via preserved dual-leg lock.

## Why
The pattern only pays off if future sessions can discover and reuse it. A first-class doc is how the next agent adds an ensure correctly, understands the invariants, and knows the accepted trade-offs and the A-tier future.

## What
Write `docs/migrations.md` AND add a link to it from the docs index and CLAUDE.md. Cover: how to add an ensure unit (append to the `ensures.py` registry with a stable id + a check-then-act callable returning ok/changed/failed); the entry points (init/re-init, `rebar fsck --repair`, MCP server startup — all reconcile unconditionally under the write lock); the applied-set `.ensure-applied` marker + the `.ensure-hinted` rate-limited pending-hint; the marker-gates-hint-never-repair invariant; the hot-path performance contract (no sweep on writes; ≤1 marker read/process); the ACCEPTED long-lived-MCP trade-off (converges at boot, does not re-sweep mid-life — drift caught at next `fsck --repair`); and the A-tier future (committed store-format version + ordered ledger, fail-closed on too-new) with the committed-version recommendation. Use gc-config as the worked reference unit.

## Scope

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` documents adding an ensure unit (registry + stable id + check-then-act + typed result) with gc-config as the worked reference
- [ ] Documents the entry points, `.ensure-applied` + `.ensure-hinted`, the pending-hint, and the marker-gates-hint-never-repair invariant

baseline.description:
## Why
The core deliverable of the epic: an `in_progress` ticket should carry the coding-agent session that STARTED it, end-to-end (written on the STATUS event AND folded into compiled state), additively — without disturbing `assignee` / `author`, and byte-identical to today when no session id is present. Recording without folding produces no observable outcome, so both halves ship together.

## What
- **Write (`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`).** In `claim_core` and `transition_core`, when the
  event is an `open -> in_progress` STATUS, call the shared `resolve_session_id()` (story
  6014) via a small `_stamp_session(status_data)` helper; when it returns non-None, add
  `data["session"]`. When None, OMIT the key entirely so the event bytes are identical to the
  pre-feature path. Stamp on ANY `open -> in_progress` STATUS — the `claim` command AND a
  bare `transition <id> open in_progress` (including the parent-first cascade) — not just
  `claim`.
- **Fold (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`).** In `process_status`, a
  `_fold_claimed_session(state, data)` helper sets `state["claimed_session"] = data.get("session")`
  on the `open -> in_progress` edge (`current_status == "open" and status == "in_progress"`).
  It is invoked ONLY in the two branches that APPLY this event's status — the normal-update
  branch and the fork-WINNER branch — and NEVER in the branch where the existing chain wins,
  so a losing concurrent claim never overwrites the winner's session (epic advisory G6/T8).
  The edge condition reads the **incoming event's** `data.get("current_status")` and
  `data.get("status")` — NOT the post-update `state["status"]` (already mutated to
  `in_progress` by the time the helper runs) — so in the fork-winner branch it still keys on
  the event's declared `open -> in_progress` edge, never firing for a `<other> -> in_progress`
  winner (advisory T8).
  `claimed_session` records the session of the CURRENT claim episode (mirrors `assignee`): a
  session-less re-claim folds `None`, deliberately CLEARING any stale prior id so the field
  never mis-attributes the current in_progress slot to a past session (advisory T9). A later
  non-claim edge (e.g. `blocked -> in_progress`) leaves it untouched.
- **Initial-state default (`src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`).** Add `claimed_session: None` to
  `make_initial_state()` (mirrors `assignee`), so a fresh event-replay always carries the key
  (value `None`) rather than key-absent.
- **Compiled-state schema (`src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`).** Add a
  `claimed_session: {type: [string, null]}` property beside `assignee` so the new public
  compiled-state field is enumerated in the schema.
- **Interim key-presence contract (until S3).** A snapshot persisted BEFORE this stack lacks
  `claimed_session` entirely, so during the coexistence window a snapshot-served state may be
  key-absent while a fresh-replay state is `None`. Consumers MUST therefore read via
  `state.get("claimed_session")` (tolerating both); S3 (199b) adds the snapshot-restore default
  + compaction round-trip that closes the window. This story does not claim key-presence for
  pre-existing snapshots.
- **Forward/back-compat.** `data["session"]` is an additive data key; a reducer build without
  the fold ignores unknown data keys (it only reads `data.get("status")` / `current_status`),
  so an older clone tolerates the event. Absent-session events are byte-identical to today.
- **Dependency.** The shared `resolve_session_id()` is story 6014, landed as the BASE COMMIT
  of this stacked change series; this story is plan-reviewed with `--ref HEAD` so the review
  snapshot includes it.

## Scope
- IN: the write stamp (both cores) + the reducer fold + the `make_initial_state` default +
  the `ticket_state.schema.json` property + unit/integration tests (present,
  absent/byte-identical, bare-transition, fork-winner gating, forward-compat tolerance,
  session-less stale-clear, initial-state default).
- OUT: snapshot/compaction default + pretty read surface + MCP outputSchema (S3 / 199b);
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`/`CODEX_THREAD_ID` + harness provenance (S5 / c557); capture hooks
  (S4 / S6). The shared resolver itself is story 6014 (already landed as this stack's base).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Claiming with a session env var set records `claimed_session` in compiled state.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k claim_records -q`.
- [ ] Claiming with NO session env var set folds `claimed_session` to `None` (key-present,
      consistent with the initial-state default) AND the written STATUS event carries no
      `session` key (byte-identical no-session event path). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k absent -q` asserts
      `state["claimed_session"] is None` AND `"session" not in` the STATUS event's `data`.
- [ ] A bare `transition <id> open in_progress` records it too (cascade parents included).
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k transition -q`.
- [ ] Fork-winner gating: when two competing `open -> in_progress` STATUS events carry
      DIFFERENT session ids, compiled `claimed_session` equals the lexical-UUID WINNER's
      session (never the loser's). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k fork -q` replays both events in BOTH
      orders and asserts the winner's session each time.
- [ ] Forward-compat: `process_status` folds a STATUS whose `data` carries both `session` and
      an arbitrary UNKNOWN extra key without error, and the unknown key does not enter state
      (proxy for an older clone tolerating the additive key). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k forward_compat -q`.
- [ ] Stale-clear (T9): a later `open -> in_progress` claim carrying NO session folds
      `claimed_session` back to `None` (never leaves a stale prior id). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k session_less_reclaim -q`.
- [ ] `make_initial_state()` defaults `claimed_session` to `None` (key-present). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py -k initial_state -q`.
- [ ] `ticket_state.schema.json` enumerates `claimed_session` as `[string, null]`. Proof:
      `grep -n '"claimed_session"' src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`.

## Depends on
- S1 (shared resolver `resolve_session_id`) — landed as the base of this stack.
baseline.summary: Record the claiming session id on open->in_progress (claim + bare transition)

baseline.description:
Add an `mcp` autodeploy target to `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` implementing the ADR 0079 amendment's blue-green pointer-swap, so on-box `rebar-mcp` tracks `origin/main` without killing an in-flight certified op (eliminates bug 7b4a). Scope: MCP deploy path only (edge = esok, secrets = avians); no new timer (existing `rebar-autodeploy.timer`→`.service`).

## Approach (blue-green, ADR deft-evolutive-mosasaur / 0079)
Model on the LOCAL `origin/main` updater (`sticky-genetic-narwhal`): immutable release + atomic pointer swap + graceful retire, NOT stop-and-drain. On MCP source change:
1. Build + tag immutable `compose-mcp:<target-sha>` (`docker compose build mcp`).
2. **Memory pre-check BEFORE the 2x overlap** (t4g.large 8 GiB): `MemAvailable` (`/proc/meminfo`,
   MB) `< MCP_MEM_MIN_MB` (default 1024) ABORTS — `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT`, backoff, no second
   container. Unreadable fails OPEN; `MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB` overrides for tests.
3. Start a NEW container alongside old via **`docker run -d`** on a FREE A/B host port (see Run
   mechanism).
4. Health-check the NEW `/health` 200 within `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` (default 120). On failure:
   `docker rm -f` new, leave OLD include UNCHANGED, `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` `mcp-unhealthy`, backoff,
   exit 1.
5. **Atomically flip the nginx `/mcp/` upstream**: back up the include, write
   `server 127.0.0.1:<newport>;` to a dotfile temp NOT matching the `mcp-upstream*.conf` glob,
   `mv` (atomic rename) over `/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf`, `nginx -t`, `nginx -s reload`. On
   failure: RESTORE backup, `docker rm -f` new, backoff, exit 1. DONE at the reload.
6. **Retire the OLD container**, retaining newest `MCP_RELEASES_KEEP` (default 1). Teardown is a
   GRACEFUL `docker stop --time 1260` (SIGTERM), which triggers the container's OWN bounded
   self-drain (`_mcp_health.run_http_with_grace`: stop intake, wait `in_flight`→0 up to
   `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`=1200s, exit; compose `stop_grace_period`=1260s) — NEVER
   `docker rm -f`/SIGKILL a serving container, so no in-flight certified op is killed. The stop is issued
   in the BACKGROUND so the tick never waits on drain; exited containers are then `docker rm`'d
   and their A/B ports freed. If the managed count exceeds `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`
   (default 3) — too many still draining/holding ports — emit `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` instead
   of forcing (also the port-exhaustion guard). Since `autodeploy.sh` exits
   early when up-to-date, also run `mcp_retire_sweep` on the no-op tick so exited containers are
   reaped as they drain.

## Run mechanism + managed set
`docker compose up mcp` pins `8091` and would collide, so the NEW container starts via **`docker run -d`** from `compose-mcp:<sha>` (helper `mcp_run_new`) on a FREE blue-green HOST port `-p 127.0.0.1:<newport>:8091` (container port stays 8091): `newport` = whichever of `MCP_PORT_A=8092`/`MCP_PORT_B=8093` is NOT currently bound by a managed container (8091 is RESERVED for the compose-original). If BOTH A and B are bound by un-reclaimable containers, the deploy does NOT start a colliding 3rd — it emits `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` + backoff and starts nothing. So managed ports = EXACTLY {8091,8092,8093} = `MCP_RELEASES_CAP=3` (cap = port pool). `mcp_run_new` reproduces the compose `mcp:` service EXACTLY — `--env-file .env`, every `REBAR_MCP_*`/`REBAR_OPCERT_*` var with compose's literal `${VAR:-default}` values (`docker run` does NOT interpolate), the two `:ro` secret mounts, `--restart always`, `--stop-timeout 1260`; the compose-parity oracle pins this set. The managed MCP set (sweep/cap counts it) = names matching `MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX` (`rebar-mcp`) OR `MCP_COMPOSE_CONTAINER` (`compose-mcp-1`); at boot `compose-up.sh` brings up `compose-mcp-1` on 8091 (seed include→8091), retired gracefully like any other (autodeploy never `docker compose up mcp`).

## Change detection + blast radius
`MCP_PATHS='src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml'` — esok's canonical `mcp:` compose-comment set. Diffed `deployed..target` it triggers ONLY `mcp`; `src/rebar`+`docker-compose.yml` are shared with `BOT_PATHS`, so a shared change triggers BOTH targets in independent `if changed` blocks. `gerrit` untouched (gerrit-id assert). `flock` still serializes.

## Failure + backoff
The `mcp` branch failure is FATAL like `review-bot` (`record_backoff_failure` + `exit 1`), so `deployed-sha` is not advanced and the deploy retries next tick. For a shared change review-bot runs first; its idempotent rebuild just repeats until mcp also succeeds.

## Alerting (marker → observability → CloudWatch → SNS; NO direct SNS publish)
autodeploy.sh has no `sns:Publish` path and must not gain one. Like every existing autodeploy alert: a countable `marker AUTODEPLOY_MCP_* {json}` → `observability.sh` `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` → a dimensionless `rebar/host` metric → a terraform `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` → `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn`. Adds tokens `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`
+ `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` (distinct from `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`); two marker-delta calls (+ offset
files) → `rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap` + `rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort`; two alarms mirroring `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`'s 900s/2-of-4/Sum>0/notBreaching shape.

## Portability (`project.portability`)
Trigger is the on-box systemd/launchd timer polling the git mirror — operation-linked, not CI; flip/retire run in-process. Works with any/no CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Tier: **real subprocess/bash integration, temp git repos + fake docker/nginx**. Tests stub
  the box binaries onto PATH and run the REAL `autodeploy.sh` in `tests/scripts/`. Oracles:
  - Change detection (REAL temp git repo, two commits, asserted via the docker call log): an
    MCP-only change (touch `Dockerfile.mcp`) triggers `mcp` and NO review-bot/gerrit rebuild; a
    review-bot-only change (`Dockerfile.reviewbot`) does the inverse; a shared `src/rebar` change
    triggers BOTH independently.
  - Cutover order start-new → health → flip → retire (via the call log); returns success
    WITHOUT waiting on `in_flight` (with `in_flight>0` on OLD it still flips and exits 0).
  - Retire is GRACEFUL: the OLD container is torn down with `docker stop` (SIGTERM self-drain),
    NEVER `docker rm -f`; an `in_flight>0` OLD container is `docker stop`'d (drains, not
    SIGKILLed) and the deploy returns before its drain finishes; over `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`
    `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` is emitted with no forced kill.
  - Port exhaustion: with BOTH A and B bound by `in_flight>0` containers, a new MCP change does
    NOT `docker run -p` on an occupied port (no 3rd container); `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`
    emitted, backoff recorded.
  - Memory pre-check: `MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB < MCP_MEM_MIN_MB` ABORTS — no second container started,
    `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` emitted, backoff recorded, include unchanged.
  - Health-check OR nginx reload failure leaves the OLD include byte-identical
    (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`, backoff, `deployed-sha` not advanced); a retry next healthy tick flips it.
  - `gerrit` container id UNCHANGED across an mcp deploy (blast radius).
  - Compose parity: a test parses the `mcp:` service in `docker-compose.yml` and asserts
    `mcp_run_new`'s `docker run` env keys+values and `:ro` mounts match it — drift guard, since
    `/health` is auth-independent and cannot catch a wrong `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_*`/`ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
- [x] observability.sh publishes `rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap` + `rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort`; two
  terraform CloudWatch alarms route them to `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn` (mirror
  `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`).

## Compat / rollback
Additive (new `if changed "$MCP_PATHS"` block + no-op sweep); other targets unchanged (existing autodeploy tests stay green); ADRs 0079/0104 document it. Rollback = revert the additions AND reset the include to `server 127.0.0.1:8091;` (edge points back at compose-managed 8091).

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur, esok.
