baseline.description:
Evidence-backed proposals to cut LLM token spend without weakening the gates. Full analysis in the session that filed this ticket; headline evidence:

EVIDENCE (rebar tickets branch, Jun 23-Jul 29): 2,683 plan reviews / 779 tickets (mean 3.4, 71% re-runs, ~66k LLM calls, ~319 LLM-hours). Challenge repo (sec-semantic-layer, wk of 07-22): 545 reviews / 121 tickets, 70% needed 2+. Re-run causes (rebar store): 57% BLOCK->revise (intended), 22% staleness (13% self-edit-after-PASS, dep/base/registry drift), ~12% pure waste (117 unrevised-BLOCK retries, 114 identical-material re-runs incl. PASS<->BLOCK flapping on identical fingerprint+sha).

Already fixed upstream (do NOT redo): depends_on INDETERMINATE envelope bug (60a0eab88, 966f7cff3); container over-invalidation (f0cf30a0e); registry grandfathering (ADR 0053); trivial-rebase carry (ADR 0041); artifact dedupe (1bed2f0cd); temp-0 Pass-2 verifier (dcfcb15b4); prompt caching; budget cap+shedding; checkpointing; idempotent skip; --status; sign-review; claimability fast-fail; drift-refresh probe.

PROPOSALS (no model changes):
1. Fix the edit&&review-plan write race (EDIT commit lands after REVIEW_RESULT, voiding the fingerprint; only doc-warnings + resign rescue exist today). Sign on current-material==reviewed-material regardless of event order, or provide an atomic verb.
2. Deterministic verdict reuse for identical fingerprint+sha when last verdict was BLOCK (idempotent skip covers only valid PASS). Kills unrevised-BLOCK retries and makes verdict flapping cost-free (~3k calls in-store).
3. review-at-claim discipline: run review-plan only immediately before claim (a claim --review combined verb; next-batch aware). 245 self-edit-after-PASS re-runs + ~10.3k calls spent on never-landed tickets.
4. Author-side deterministic preflight for the chronic blockers: P6 ac-quality failed in 456/540 challenge reviews; G6/G1G2/E4 + specification-by-example dominate BLOCKs. A zero-LLM lint (existing _lib_gates checks) surfaced pre-review would shorten the 57% BLOCK->revise loop.
5. Close the Pass-1 usage-log gap (ed8c747e8 notes it) + real price table (COST_AGENT_USD=0.12 is a hard-coded guess) so the USD cap reflects reality.
6. Demote AGENT-exec criteria to 1-TURN where the ADR-0054 corpus replay shows tool exploration never changed the finding: 18 AGENT criteria at ~20x 1-TURN cost dominate per-review spend (~26.5 calls/review).
7. Optional, validate first: extend temperature-0 (or warm-then-fan-out caching) to Pass-1 finders; flapping on identical material observed (epic bbf1: PASS,PASS,PASS,BLOCK,PASS).

Explicitly NOT proposed: model swaps (context-window/capability changes alter gate behavior; ladder + sonnet verifier already tuned).
baseline.summary: Token-usage reduction proposals for the LLM gates (evidence-backed, 2026-07-29 analysis)

baseline.description:
## Discovered from
bug `conversant-cepivorous-mastiff` (0449-cf75-bb4b-41fd), which widened `claim` to accept a `blocked` source status.

## Problem
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py` lists `blocked` in `_NOT_CLAIMABLE_STATUSES`, so `review-plan` on a blocked ticket fast-fails INDETERMINATE with the reason 'not claimable: status is "blocked", not "open"'. That premise is now false: `claim` accepts `blocked`.

Residual gap: a gated `task`/`story`/`epic` sitting in `blocked` with a MISSING or STALE plan-review attestation cannot earn a fresh one — `claim` refuses on the gate, and `review-plan` refuses to run. `--force` is the only lever.

## Why it was NOT fixed under the parent bug
The blocked fast-fail is **documented intended behavior** in three places — `AGENTS.md` L129, `docs/user-guide.md` L338, `docs/workflow-engine.md` L34-35 — so changing it is a plan-review gate design decision with a doc-contract change, not a defect repair.

## Scope if taken
Remove `blocked` from `_NOT_CLAIMABLE_STATUSES`, correct the reason string (it asserts 'not open'), and update the three docs. Keep `closed`/`idea` fast-failing.
baseline.summary: review-plan fast-fails on blocked, so a resumable blocked ticket cannot refresh a stale claim attestation

baseline.description:
Run the one-time reclaim. **Do not start until A1-A5, A6-0a..0d and Epic B's B6 are closed**, A6-0b records a successful deployment/runtime receipt for the live review bot, and a completed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run has a `github.sha` descending from the A6-0a merge. The epoch-blind writer risk is closed by direct runtime proofs under quiescence, not by elapsed time. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Protocol
1. **Agent** disables `reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (`gh workflow disable`,
   which also blocks `workflow_dispatch` and therefore `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` self-redispatch);
   **asserts** no reconcile run is in progress (poll `gh run list`, not drain-and-hope); polls the
   deployed review-bot `/health` until `in_flight == 0` and runs an authenticated Gerrit query for
   `status:open -label:LLM-Review`, requiring no current patchset that is still awaiting its vote.
   Zero sessions stops new pushes, but a patchset pushed just before the window can otherwise have
   its vote fire during it, and every vote writes a ticket; break-glasses
   `refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}` if held.
2. **Agent** pauses the AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` and the host LaunchAgents
   `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` (04:00) and `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`. It explicitly
   refreshes the host `rebar` installation from a descendant of the A6-0a merge, records the
   executable path and version/source, and executes an epoch-mismatch refusal probe with that exact
   runtime against temporary real clones. It also records the completed descendant
   `reconcile-bridge.yml` run and successful `git merge-base --is-ancestor` result. These direct
   observations replace the former 24-hour proxy and prevent the hourly updater from reverting the
   binary mid-window. **[operator-attested] Operator** confirms **zero active sessions** and all
   **`rebar-mcp` servers stopped** (a long-running MCP holds an in-process store handle and does
   not hot-reload). Gerrit needs no separate confirmation: every Gerrit push comes from a session.
3. **Agent** converges the local tracker (`fetch` + `reset --hard origin/tickets`, 0-ahead verified).
   This covers all 48 sibling worktrees at once — their `.tickets-tracker` are **symlinks to the one
   store**. The four other real trackers on the host point at different GitHub repos.
4. **Agent** deletes the pre-rewrite ref pins (A6-0d), runs the strip in a fresh **unfiltered** clone,
   verifies the pre-push assertions, and pushes with **`--force-with-lease`**.
5. **Agent** asserts non-resurrection: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is
   **false**, and no clone-fetched ref has the old tip as an ancestor.
6. **Agent** converges the review-bot clone over SSM (`fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets` on
   `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`). Reverts to **[operator-attested]** if the issued AWS
   credentials do not permit `ssm send-command` against `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`.
7. **Agent** lands the `enforce_since` re-pin through Gerrit, mapped via the commit-map.
   The re-pinned key is `[identity].enforce_since` at `rebar.toml:115`, the only literal SHA in the
   system. With `require_authenticated = false` (`:106`) `verify_authorship.py:531-550` returns
   early and never reads it, so there is **no CI deadlock** and the change lands normally. The
   separate `[verify].opcert_enforce_since` key is unset.
8. **Agent** treats the Gerrit re-pin's review-bot vote as the deterministic first post-window
   write: records its change/patchset and vote timestamp, fetches `origin/tickets`, asserts
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is false, and measures `size-pack`
   growth from the immediate post-rewrite baseline as < 1 MB.
9. **Agent** re-enables the GitHub workflows, the AWS timer, and both LaunchAgents.
10. **Agent** verifies the ACs below and **notifies the operator** that the tickets branch is
    available for sessions again.

## T11 migration-safety answers
- **Expand/contract:** yes — A6-0a's reader ships before the epoch value exists; the descendant
  workflow run, live review-bot refusal probe, and exact host-runtime refusal probe prove deployment
  directly while every writer is quiesced.
- **Batching:** n/a, single atomic ref update.
- **Resumability: NONE, stated.** A force-push is not resumable. Mitigation: all correctness
  assertions run on the scratch clone **before** publishing, so a wrong graph never reaches origin;
  the push itself is atomic per-ref.
- **Dual-write window:** none — the store is quiesced; the epoch guard replaces dual-write as the
  stale-writer defence.
- **Rollback:** restore from the A6-0d bundle + `--force-with-lease` back to the old tip. Known
  limit: rollback re-diverges anything already converged, so consumers must be re-converged in the
  same order as the forward path. **No event bytes are ever altered** — only commit SHAs — so the
  rewrite itself cannot lose ticket data.
- **T4 destructiveness:** an irreversible force-push to the authoritative store of a live system,
  chosen deliberately to reclaim 92% of the branch, gated on operator-confirmed quiescence, an
  off-repo bundle, a fail-closed epoch guard, and pre-push assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] The A6-0a merge SHA, a completed descendant
      `reconcile-bridge.yml` run id, and successful ancestry result are recorded before publication.
- [x] [operator-attested] A6-0b records the deployed review-bot SHA or image digest plus a live
      epoch-mismatch refusal result from that runtime.
- [x] [operator-attested] The explicitly refreshed host executable path/version and its successful
      epoch-mismatch refusal result are recorded before publication.
- [x] [operator-attested] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB** (from 1.04 GiB; the measured strip
      result is ~94 MiB) and `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree.
      **Holds only because B6 landed first.** Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [x] [operator-attested] Commit count and merge-commit count on `tickets` are **unchanged** versus the pre-rewrite
      recording (measured at window time, never hardcoded). Tier: **repo assertion**.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <sha> --format json`, run pre-rewrite
      against the old SHA and post-rewrite against the mapped SHA: the **stderr summary counts** are
      identical AND the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` from the JSON report is
      identical **ignoring `commit`**. (JSON mode puts only the report array on stdout and the summary
      on stderr; the report lists only non-verified events; every `commit` is a rewritten SHA. The
      command **exits 1** when `enforced_not_verified > 0`, so do not require exit 0.) Tier: **CLI
      subprocess, both sides**.
- [x] [operator-attested] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** and `size-pack` growth is **< 1 MB**. The ancestry assertion is
      what actually proves non-resurrection. Tier: **repo measurement after an observed vote**.
- [x] [operator-attested] No ref a default clone fetches has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier: `ls-remote` +
      `merge-base` loop, computed at window time.
- [x] [operator-attested] Operator confirmation of zero active sessions and stopped MCP servers is
      recorded as a comment before step 3.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The landed `rebar.toml` `identity.enforce_since` value equals the
      mapped post-rewrite SHA derived from the pre-window pin.
- [x] [operator-attested] Post-enable reconciliation is validated by either a green reconcile-bridge.yml run or, during a GitHub Actions outage, an operator-approved production-equivalent signed CLI sequence: pre-live dry-run with zero mutation/recovery failures; live pass(es) exit 0 with every Jira batch error=None and silent_noop=[]; persisted state is pushed; final dry-run has zero mutation/recovery failures; and the canary classifier reports drift_total=0. Tier: **CLI subprocess**.
- [x] [operator-attested] `rebar fsck` is clean after step 9. Tier: **CLI subprocess**.

## Files
Operational — no `src/` changes. Uses the A6-0c script and A6-0d helpers; touches `rebar.toml` (`identity.enforce_since`) via Gerrit in step 7.

Scope: M (operational). Direct dependencies: A5, A6-0b (which depends on A6-0a), A6-0c, and A6-0d. A1-A4 and Epic B's B6 are transitive/epic start gates and must also be closed.

baseline.description:
Integrate the task-decomposition SOTA research (docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md, commit 143d5074e, ticket englacial-communal-conure/d39b) into the plan-review gate: validate each recommendation experimentally with evals FIRST, implement only behind its results gate, then dogfood in production review. Per operator direction (2026-07-15): no A/B testing - validation is eval-based (the E-gates below), post-ship observation is dogfooding via R7 instrumentation, and the approach must be clearly documented at every step.

## Context
GATE TERMS: each child R1-R7 story carries its own falsifiable pass/fail thresholds (drawn from the report's section-6 experiment table) INSIDE its Acceptance Criteria - the child ACs are the authoritative 'gate rows'; this epic does not duplicate the numbers. R6 is the one deliberate exception: a deterministic pass-4 coaching move with no detection behavior ships first with no eval gate (validated by dogfooding via R7 metrics). Experiment ids follow the report's numbering; E4 (the in-situ A/B experiment) is deliberately DROPPED per the operator's no-A/B directive, which is why the experiment set is E1/E2/E3/E5/E6. INCONCLUSIVE-GATE RULE: an experiment that fails its own validity gate (e.g. E1 kappa < 0.7) or returns an ambiguous result gets at most ONE documented re-run with changed method; if still not clearly passing, every dependent R-story closes deferred with the results recorded - ambiguity never rounds up to a pass. ORDERING: first wave after E1 is R7 + R6 (instrumentation and the no-gate move), so dogfood monitoring exists before any detection change lands; R2/R3/R4 each touch criteria_routing.json and land serially in any order (file-impact keeps them out of one batch); R1 does not depend on R5 (the probe is effective without the kernel sub-answer; R5 strengthens its verification later); R5's IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump is coordinated at claim time with the floor-split story's own potential bump so the corpus segments cleanly (one bump train, never two half-bumps). The report's §5 mined this store's own history: post-claim description edits on 16/505 claimed work tickets (3.2%), 15 substantive; of 8 with persisted reviews, 3 were review MISSES sharing one defect class (plan asserts a capability an existing module lacks: dc58, db7b, 5886) and 4 were advisories applied only post-claim (latency, not blindness). Small n: 3/8 identifies the defect CLASS (binomial 95% CI 9-76%), it is not a precise miss rate - child E1 re-verifies these claims before anything depends on them. §6 defines R1-R7, each with a falsifiable experiment. Implementation targets: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/ (orchestrator, det_floor.py, passes.py, criteria_routing.json), src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/ (SHARED with code-review - R5 requires the E5 non-regression gate), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_*.md. Calibration assets in docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/ are extended, not replaced. This epic runs alongside the calibration-3 line (task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly, story large-sleepful-needlefish); implementation children that touch criteria_routing.json/review_kernel sequence after the floor-split story to avoid file conflicts.

## Acceptance Criteria
> RECONCILED AT CLOSE (2026-07-19). The original ACs below tracked the ORIGINAL plan (batch evals + inter-rater kappa). Several were changed by explicit, OPERATOR-APPROVED cost decisions during execution: the batch-eval gating strategy was retired in favor of an advisory-first + standing-dogfood strategy, the finding-adjudication/kappa corpus was descoped, and the expensive E2/E3 LLM batch baselines were permanently rejected on cost and superseded by story d8a5. Each AC is restated to reflect what was actually delivered, honestly noting the deferrals/descopes and their rationale. All 13 children are closed.

- [x] **E1 outcome corpus frozen** — the plan-review OUTCOME corpus IS frozen + committed under docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/ with a versioned README (628 rows, event-mined; landed via Gerrit 740+744). **DESCOPED (operator-approved):** the finding-adjudication corpus + inter-rater κ≥0.7 gate were invalidated (tool-less, plan-truncated labeling ~79% contaminated vs the whole-plan/code-grounded/agentic production gate) and descoped; the independent human-adjudicated gold set is parked as idea e59d-c078-724d-46e5 (relates_to this epic). Recorded on E1/e95e. The INCONCLUSIVE-GATE RULE's 'E1 κ<0.7' example is moot (κ descoped).

- [x] **Each experiment child closed with a docs writeup — with an operator-approved rescope of E2/E3.** E1 (e95e) ✔, E6 (a880) ✔, E5 (5342) ✔ (byte-identical cross-gate replay writeup) closed with committed docs/experiments/ artifacts. **E2 (d125) / E3 (def5) RESCOPED (operator-approved, cost):** their deterministic corpus/harness were built as WIP, but the expensive LLM batch baseline was PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost and SUPERSEDED by story d8a5 (`criterion_effectiveness.py`, change #798) — a zero-LLM sidecar-native effectiveness recorder that supplies the same detection/blocking-FP evidence continuously in production. Batch mining was also confirmed dead on its own terms (only ~4 plan-v3 baselines exist vs the ~200 the counterfactual replay assumed). E2/E3 closed on that basis with the result recorded, not as a passed batch-eval gate.

- [x] **Each recommendation R1–R7 landed through Gerrit + closed signed — with R1/R3/R4 re-planned advisory-first.** All of R1 (59b7), R2 (b080), R3 (3a27), R4 (03a9), R5 (ea39), R6 (5dac), R7 (b1a4) landed through Gerrit and closed. **STRATEGY CHANGE (operator-approved):** because the E2/E3 batch-eval gate was rejected, R1/R3/R4 were re-planned **advisory-first** rather than batch-eval-gated: each ships in **advisory posture** (never blocks a plan), passes a bounded ≤~8-run sanity check, and is auto-monitored by d8a5's standing dogfood effectiveness recorder, with the advisory→blocking **promotion gate** documented (a criterion only promotes on accumulated dogfood evidence). The original intent — 'no detection-bearing recommendation implemented without its eval gate' — is met by advisory-safety (no blocking risk pre-evidence) + standing dogfood monitoring, NOT by pre-ship batch evals. R6 shipped ship-first as planned (deterministic rendering + validator compliance); R2/R5 landed per their own child gate terms.

- [x] **Landed changes in the packaged registry, no config-flag, R7 dogfood documented, docs/plan-review-gate.md updated.** SATISFIED as-is: advisory criteria live directly in the packaged `criteria_routing.json` + `CANONICAL_LLM` (no config-flag or overlay gating); d8a5's standing effectiveness recorder + the advisory→blocking promotion-gate protocol are documented in docs/plan-review-gate.md.

NOTE — the batch-eval → advisory-first + standing-dogfood pivot AND the E2/E3 batch-baseline deferral were **operator-approved cost decisions** (LLM spend minimized, human-adjudication time over budget). They replace, rather than fail, the original batch-eval-gated plan.

### Original Acceptance Criteria (pre-reconciliation, for audit)
- [ ] E1 ground-truth corpora are frozen and committed under docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/ with a versioned README (outcome corpus + finding-adjudication corpus, inter-rater kappa >= 0.7 recorded).
- [ ] Each experiment child (E1, E2, E3, E5, E6 - no E4, see Context) is closed with its results committed as a docs/experiments/ writeup (the repo artifact is the criterion; ticket comments mirror it).
- [ ] Each recommendation child (R1-R7) is either landed through Gerrit with its own AC gate terms demonstrably passed (R6's terms are ship-first: deterministic rendering + validator compliance), or closed/deferred with the failing result recorded - no detection-bearing recommendation implemented without its eval gate.
- [ ] All landed criteria/rubric changes are incorporated directly into the packaged registry/rubrics (no config-flag or overlay gating), with R7 dogfood monitoring documented, and docs/plan-review-gate.md updated to match.
- [ ] Every implemented recommendation has a committed docs/experiments/ writeup showing its gate row passed before implementation; every rejected/deferred recommendation has the failing result recorded.
- [ ] The gate ships with no blocking-FP regression: validated changes are incorporated DIRECTLY into the packaged review process (no config-flag or overlay gating - operator direction 2026-07-15); new criteria enter at advisory POSTURE first where their child's gate terms say so, with R7 dogfood monitoring: when a criterion's trailing blocking-FP proxy exceeds 10% (the **blocking-FP proxy** for a criterion is the fraction of that criterion's BLOCKING findings, over a trailing window of reviews, that are subsequently adjudicated false-positive / not-block-worthy — measured by R7's instrumentation against E1's committed finding-adjudication ground-truth corpus; 10% is the demotion threshold), its registry posture is demoted to advisory by an ordinary criteria_routing.json change (precedent: calibration 3 demoted T5e to advisory on FP evidence, task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly; T3/T10 are the precedent for keeping routinely-ignored criteria non-blocking in the first place).
- [ ] The plan-review methodology remains documented: docs/plan-review-gate.md reflects every landed change.

baseline.description:
## Context and confirmed RCA

Gerrit Verify run 31874837464 completed in 29m11s with macOS at 27m38s. macOS spent 20.88s in test_hook_falls_back_to_git_when_env_unset, 16.38s setting up build-provenance artifacts, 10.69s rebuilding from sdist, plus 8.98s in a blank-env build. Ubuntu repeats these builds in three Python cells. Local profiling showed the fallback exports the 3,019-file / 42.4MB checkout although hatch_build.py resolves one SHA then writes src/rebar/_build_info.py: git add costs 1.37-1.53s; python -m build costs 3.85-4.32s. A same-hook minimal package preserved the exact SHA while reducing paired totals from 6.30/9.26s to 2.66/5.43s.

The exact -n 3 --dist worksteal selector proved built_artifacts initializes on three workers, each paying 6.60-6.74s setup. This is a bounded contributor, not the cause of multi-minute host variation. The pre-repair selected-six serial baseline is 18.23s.

Live run 31874837464 received patchset 9aecb53e and checked it out, but artifact-probe built with trusted-main GITHUB_SHA 7d908fb. Truthiness-only probes accepted the wrong nonempty COMMIT, violating ducal-statuelike-ladybird exact-source identity.

## Ticket and OSS research

No prior rejection exists. ducal-statuelike-ladybird requires real sdist/wheel exact provenance. square-tragic-llama accepts a minimal Git fixture retaining exact fallback SHA plus shallow-source control. despotic-dorsal-greatdane approves immutable artifact reuse but stops at per-worker scope. cryptic-damp-panda identifies repeated package builds as coverage-neutral residual work.

Four popular active projects use this placement: pytest 68308aa has one Ubuntu package job before its matrix; pip f399c371 has packaging jobs outside Unix/Python tests; Poetry 92b74dc has one Ubuntu build/install smoke job outside its OS/Python matrix; Pydantic 02c5c975 has a dedicated Ubuntu distribution build outside its matrix. This is 4/4 consensus for one full-package integration job plus lighter behavioral probes in the broad matrix. Rebar remains stricter by retaining real isolated PEP 517 sdist-to-wheel execution through the production hook in every cell.

## Plan

1. Freeze RED workflow plus build-hook contracts. The workflow oracle rejects GITHUB_SHA, requires git rev-parse --short HEAD after final checkout, then requires exact equality from installed wheel plus sdist. Build-hook oracles retain env SHA, preserved sdist SHA, git fallback SHA, blank-env failure.
2. Create one shared fixture around checkout-current hatch_build.py plus the src/rebar/_build_info.py boundary. Migrate all whole-tree forms: _clean_tree, _self_contained_checkout, and the inline git archive plus tar extraction in test_hook_fails_when_rebar_build_commit_empty. Re-derive completeness by string-sweeping git archive and tar extraction in build-semantics tests. The direct full-Rebar WheelBuilder content test remains intentional.
3. The fixture creates a tiny Hatch package, copies production hatch_build.py, declares it as the real custom hook, provides src/rebar/__init__.py at the production target, initializes Git, then commits only that tree. The hook writes and force-includes src/rebar/_build_info.py into sdist plus wheel, exercising preserve-existing through the real archive boundary. Default PEP 517 isolation remains; Hatchling, Git, archive creation, and wheel inspection are not mocked.
4. Convert repeated semantics tests in test_attestation_signing.py plus test_build_provenance.py to the fixture. Retain every named assertion, the no-git helper branch, direct full-package content test, and shallow-source control.
5. Keep the full-Rebar replay in shared _artifact-probe.yml, serving test.yml branch-head checkout plus gerrit-verify.yaml patchset checkout. Compute REBAR_EXPECTED_COMMIT using git rev-parse --short HEAD after either final checkout. Build with that value. Require exact equality for wheel plus install-from-sdist. Preserve import, CLI, schema, packaging, and vote-gating probes.
6. Seed the wrong-SHA defect, a whole-tree fixture regression, and one precedence defect. Each oracle must return RED before restoration. Record focused serial plus exact-xdist timings against pre-repair 18.23s selected-six serial and 6.60-6.74s per-worker setup baselines. Timing quantifies runner work but is evidence only, not a retention gate, because host variation dominates wall-clock.
7. Run focused tests, workflow consumers, make lint, typecheck, plus full default/integration selectors. Push immediately through Gerrit without a control-only run. Record hosted macOS plus Ubuntu durations from that treatment.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: ducal-statuelike-ladybird requires real sdist-to-wheel provenance, exact env/git fallback, blank-env failure, sdist preservation, plus exact source identity; both workflow consumers must build their final checkout. trigger_preconditions: each matrix cell runs production hatch_build.py through isolated PEP 517 on the minimal package; artifact-probe has completed its final checkout. production_path: copied production hatch_build.py resolves, writes, then force-includes COMMIT during sdist plus wheel builds; artifact-probe builds then installs full distributions. test_tier: minimal real-build probes across every current OS/Python cell plus one full-project artifact integration job per workflow lane. observable_postcondition: existing semantics remain; full artifacts equal the short SHA of final checkout. negative_control: wrong nonempty SHA fails; blank env fails; no-git/no-bake remains None; shallow source remains supported. collateral_invariants: no selector, assertion, isolation mode, worker, platform, Python cell, coverage, mutation, probe, runner, or vote dependency is removed. ci_gate: focused serial/xdist tests, workflow contracts, make lint, make typecheck, Gerrit Verified, LLM-Review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every OS/Python cell executes a real isolated sdist-to-wheel build through production hatch_build.py on the minimal fixture.
- [ ] The env-override probe requires the exact supplied SHA.
- [ ] The install-from-sdist probe requires the exact preserved SHA.
- [ ] The git-fallback probe requires the exact committed fixture SHA.
- [ ] The blank-env probe requires a nonzero real-build exit.
- [ ] No hook-semantics test retains _clean_tree, _self_contained_checkout, or inline git-archive materialization.
- [ ] A repository string sweep finds no other full-checkout archive in hook-semantics fixtures.
- [ ] Both artifact workflow lanes derive expected SHA after final checkout.
- [ ] The installed full-Rebar wheel equals expected SHA.
- [ ] The installed full-Rebar sdist equals expected SHA.
- [ ] A wrong nonempty full-artifact SHA fails the workflow oracle.
- [ ] The direct full-Rebar WheelBuilder content test remains enabled.
- [ ] The shallow-source negative control remains enabled.
- [ ] The OS/Python matrix remains unchanged.
- [ ] Pytest selectors, xdist workers, coverage, plus mutation remain unchanged.
- [ ] Artifact import, CLI, schema, plus vote-gating probes remain unchanged.
- [ ] A precedence mutation returns the build-hook oracle to RED.
- [ ] Focused serial plus exact-xdist timings are recorded against the 18.23s serial and 6.60-6.74s per-worker setup baselines as non-gating evidence.
- [ ] The first hosted treatment records macOS plus all Ubuntu job/test durations.
- [ ] Gerrit records LLM-Review +1 before merge.
- [ ] Gerrit records Verified +1 before merge.
- [ ] Gerrit records zero unresolved comments before merge.

baseline.description:
## What happened

A story that was legitimately SUPERSEDED cannot be closed by any non-`--force` path, because two mechanisms contradict each other:

1. `rebar transition <id> open closed --class=superseded`, with a **live `supersedes` link**
   already recorded, is refused:

   > `plan-review close gate: unsigned: no certified plan-review attestation. Run rebar
   > review-plan <id> separately, then retry close.`

2. `rebar review-plan <id>` on that same ticket **cannot pass** — and correctly so. The reviewer
   returns BLOCK with three critical `G1G2` findings whose substance is *"the described edit
   target content does not exist / the test you plan to write already exists"*:

   > "The guide lines the plan names as needing cut-over already contain `[non-codebase]` …"
   > "that test already asserts `[non-codebase]` is present"
   > "AC4's 'NEW negative test' already exists as `test_legacy_alias_stays_undocumented`"

That is precisely what "superseded" MEANS: another change already delivered this plan's work. The gate demands an attestation that the ticket is, by construction, unable to earn — the more correctly it is superseded, the more certainly its review blocks.

## Why the existing escape does not cover it

`rebar transition --help` states that an administrative disposition skips **completion verification** when its evidence holds (a live `duplicates`/`supersedes` link, or a required close reason). That evidence was present here. But the skip does not extend to the **plan-review close gate** (`require_plan_review_for_close`), which still demands a certified attestation, so the administrative path is blocked anyway.

The only remaining route is `--force=<reason>`, which AGENTS.md explicitly reserves for a human operator's judgment call and which deliberately records **no signed attestation**. So every superseded ticket permanently degrades the audit trail, for a disposition that is administrative and evidence-backed rather than a bypass of real verification.

## Reproduction

1. Create stories A and B; give B a plan whose work A will absorb.
2. Land A, implementing everything B planned.
3. `rebar link A B supersedes` (evidence for the administrative disposition).
4. `rebar transition B open closed --class=superseded` → refused, `plan-review close gate: unsigned`.
5. `rebar review-plan B` → BLOCK, findings all of the form "this work already exists".
6. Goto 4. There is no non-`--force` exit.

## Suggested direction (not a prescription)

The administrative dispositions that already skip completion verification on live-link evidence (`superseded`, `duplicate`) are candidates for skipping the plan-review close gate on the SAME evidence. The gate exists to certify that work about to be done, or just done, was reviewed — neither applies to a ticket whose work was delivered elsewhere and which is being closed as a bookkeeping act.

`obsolete`/`wontfix` (reason-required rather than link-backed) may warrant different treatment; this ticket is only about the link-backed dispositions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A ticket with a live `supersedes` (or `duplicates`) link can be closed under its matching
      `--class` without `--force` and without a plan-review attestation.
- [x] The close still refuses when the claimed evidence is absent — no live link means no skip.
- [x] The resulting close is distinguishable in the audit trail from a `--force` close (it is an
      evidence-backed disposition, not an unaudited bypass).
- [x] A test drives the six-step reproduction above and asserts step 4 succeeds.
baseline.summary: Superseded tickets cannot be closed: plan-review close gate demands an attestation they cannot earn

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` measures **771 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that fans the fetch out over several projects rewrites the query construction in `_build_snapshot` and will not fit in 29 lines.

## Approach

Extract the pagination cluster into a new `fetch_paging.py`: `_ACLI_CEILING` and `SilentTruncationError` (`:99-120`), `_extract_issues` (`:251-262`), `_iter_pages` (`:265-390`) and `collect` (`:392-399`).

The call chain is genuine and self-contained: `collect` calls `_iter_pages` (`:397`), which calls `_extract_issues` (`:296`) and raises `SilentTruncationError` (`:308,343,355`) against `_ACLI_CEILING` (`:354`). Nothing in the cluster calls back upward; `_build_snapshot` reaches it only through `_iter_pages` (`:554`). The new module's complete import list is `annotations` and a `TYPE_CHECKING` import of `TicketTransport` — the pagination code is otherwise pure.

This extraction is well matched to the incoming change, which rewrites the `queries` tuple at `_build_snapshot:548-554` into a per-project loop over `jqls_for` — all of which stays in `fetcher.py`.

**Three things must stay resident**, and getting any of them wrong breaks tests silently:

- `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (`:105`) stays — `_build_snapshot:550` uses it. Only `_ACLI_CEILING` moves.
- `_load_acli` and `_load_alert_store` stay — they carry **25** and **3** `patch.object(fetcher, ...)`
  sites respectively, and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move. Both are called
  from `_build_snapshot` (`:523,536`), which stays, so no patch site is disturbed.
- `fetcher.py` re-exports **all four** moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`,
  `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` — because every one of them is reached as an attribute
  of `fetcher` by existing tests, and an attribute access does not follow a moved symbol:
  - `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py:118,139`), plus further
    `fetcher._iter_pages` / `fetcher.collect` accesses in the same file and in
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py`;
  - `fetcher.SilentTruncationError`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_pagination_jql.py:133,165`) as well as the
    explicit `from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import SilentTruncationError` at
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:32`;
  - `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` (`test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:149`), which reads the constant
    directly to size its fixture. This one is easy to miss precisely because the constant looks
    private and unshared.

The re-export keeps roughly 48 existing references green across six test modules. Note that the two production mentions of `fetcher._iter_pages` — `_backend.py:62` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:139,153` — are **docstring prose** recording bug history, not runtime references, so no production module needs an edit.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~195 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — drops to ~606 lines, plus a re-export block

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. The risks are attribute presence and patch survival, so both are asserted rather than assumed:

- Attribute-surface assertion: `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
  both hold after the move, and `SilentTruncationError` still imports from `fetcher`.
- Patch survival: the tests that `patch.object(fetcher, "_load_acli")` and `"_load_alert_store"` pass
  unedited, proving those symbols stayed resident and are still resolved from `fetcher`'s globals.
- Truncation behaviour preserved: a fixture exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` still raises
  `SilentTruncationError` through the real `collect → _iter_pages` path — the contract most at risk
  from moving the constant away from its raiser.
- One-way import: `fetch_paging` must not import `fetcher`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fetcher.py` and `fetch_paging.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the module-size
      gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] All four moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`, `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` —
      still resolve as attributes of `fetcher`; checked by a test asserting each by attribute access,
      which covers the two existing `hasattr` assertions and the direct `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` read.
- [ ] `_load_acli`, `_load_alert_store` and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` remain defined in `fetcher.py`;
      checked by asserting each is in that module's own namespace, not merely importable.
- [ ] A fixture exceeding the ceiling still raises `SilentTruncationError` via the real paging path;
      checked by the existing pagination held-out test running unedited.
- [ ] `fetch_paging.py` does not import `fetcher`; checked by a test importing the two modules in
      both orders and asserting `fetcher` is absent from `fetch_paging`'s imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the pagination cluster from fetcher.py into fetch_paging.py

## Context / Problem
S2-S5 establish parser-derived help, lazy execution, semantic capabilities, and downstream contracts while retaining derived compatibility exports for safe expansion. RP-05 remains incomplete while the facade or handlers expose parallel policy sets, explicit selection ladders, imperative duplicate grammars, hand-authored usage tables, or manual documentation censuses that future commands can update instead of the authorities.

## Approach
Perform the contract phase after S2-S5 pass.

1. Use semantic navigation plus repository-wide string scans to inventory every reference/patch/import of old policy names, ladder helpers, command registries, parser loops, help-text authorities, and generator compatibility data.
2. Move remaining consumers to route/capability/parser APIs. Delete the 19 policy/census objects, explicit intercept selection ladder, derived compatibility exports, docs-only/manual syntax tables, and command-handler imperative grammars superseded by S2 factories.
3. Preserve specialized handler modules and the selected handler's S2 parser ownership; do not fold domain execution or build a root argparse tree in the facade.
4. Run whole-route and whole-parser shadow comparison immediately before deletion. Fail on any delta except the approved help/overview normalization.
5. Run both generators twice and `--check`; assert every runtime parser ref has exactly the expected committed artifact and reference section.
6. Keep all source modules below 800 lines, split only on existing call-graph seams, and create no file under 100 lines.
7. Document the completed migration and code-only back-out. No ticket/event/bridge/binding migration or cleanup runs.

The positive rationale is to leave one writable route authority, one semantic capability authority, and one runtime-used argparse grammar per command. This removes migration scaffolding rather than adding a feature flag.

## Compatibility and Rollback
All hard-won parser/help/mount/init/output/bridge/optionality/degradation tests remain authoritative. Deltas are limited to S2's approved help/overview change. Before contraction, rollback uses compatibility exports; after contraction, reverting code plus generated artifacts restores the old route because no stored format changed.

## Testing
Run focused real subprocess suites for help/mount/argv/output/aliases/retired commands and selected capabilities, both generator checks, lean/full-extra contracts, and repository lint/type/module-size/complexity gates. Add negative scans proving old policy symbols, imperative command-grammar authorities, curated intercept tables, and retired tokens are absent while registered compatibility spellings remain. The full suite is collateral evidence, not a substitute for behavioral oracles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No shipped source, generator, test, or active documentation reads/patches retired policy sets, selection ladders, compatibility censuses, docs-only syntax tables, or superseded imperative command grammars.
- [x] Every command has exactly one registered runtime-used argparse factory and generated help artifact mapping; both generator `--check` commands pass on a second render.
- [x] Whole-route/parser shadow comparison reports no unapproved delta in identity, mount/init, argv, diagnostics, confirmation/output, streams, exit codes, aliases, or capability posture.
- [x] Approved help/overview behavior and all execution/degradation contracts pass through real subprocess and production-path tests after compatibility exports are removed.
- [x] Module-size, complexity, lint, and type gates pass with no mechanically split file under 100 lines.
- [x] Migration docs state the completed contract and code/artifact rollback, and no persisted ticket/event/bridge/binding format or data changes.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S6 — Complete CLI registry cutover and retire duplicate route authorities

baseline.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230, store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88 commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py` 14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.** `_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3; `signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP 204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in `llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" — the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [ ] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [ ] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and "Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [ ] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [ ] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [ ] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.
baseline.summary: Comment triage: relocate history, rationale and contracts out of src

## Problem

Surfaced while fixing `anatomical-arbored-oyster` (e3e0-2e7c-b280-4b4a). With the floor leg's build `TypeError` removed, `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` runs the unit tier and emits teardown ERRORs:

```
ERROR at teardown of test_link_success_noop_and_unlink_lines
Failed: New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.pytest_cache']
tests/conftest.py:379: Failed
```

## Root cause (confirmed)

`tests/conftest.py`'s `_no_repo_root_leaks` guard diffs REPO_ROOT's top-level entries around each test and `pytest.fail`s on any new entry, exempting only coverage.py data files (`_is_coverage_artifact`). `.pytest_cache/` — gitignored (`.gitignore:7`) and written by the pytest framework, not by a test body — was never exempted, so when the floor-leg pytest materializes `.pytest_cache` under REPO_ROOT during a test's wall-clock window (despite `-p no:cacheprovider`) the guard trips at teardown. It is the identical class the guard already treats as non-leaks for coverage. Omission, not regression; change 2420 (`47713c44`) merely EXPOSED it by unblocking the floor unit tier.

## Fix (landed — Gerrit change 2427, MERGED)

Generalized the exemption to the gitignored tool-cache class via a new `_is_framework_artifact` predicate over `_TOOLING_CACHE_ARTIFACTS` = {`.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.mutmut-cache`, `__pycache__`}. Genuine pollution (any other new entry) still fails and is still named. Regression tests drive the REAL guard (`tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py`): `.pytest_cache` passes; the full exempt class passes against a pinned contract list (teeth: dropping a name → RED); a real leak beside `.pytest_cache` still fails and names only the leak.

## Evidence
- Mirror run 33299427686: `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` job 99224621821 — multiple `ERROR at teardown ... New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.pytest_cache']`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The floor `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` leg has no `.pytest_cache` REPO_ROOT-pollution teardown errors. — `.pytest_cache` is now exempt from `_no_repo_root_leaks` (verified: guard passes with `.pytest_cache` present; regression test `test_leak_guard_exempts_pytest_cache`).
- [x] The pollution guard's treatment of `.pytest_cache` is portable (no dependence on a specific pytest version or CI provider). — Exemption is a static name allowlist in conftest (`_TOOLING_CACHE_ARTIFACTS`); no pytest-version- or CI-provider-specific trigger. Verified+1 across ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS py3.13 on change 2427.
baseline.summary: Floor sweep: conftest REPO_ROOT pollution guard trips on .pytest_cache teardown errors

baseline.description:
## Context

Cumulative error counters in infra/scripts/observability.sh persist an acknowledgement offset before CloudWatch accepts the matching datapoint. A transient put-metric-data failure therefore causes the next interval to compute zero from an already-advanced baseline, permanently losing the positive delta. The same copied construct affects seven metric streams across six code shapes, including the G2P block omitted from the original five-site census.

## Proven root cause

Each affected block writes total to its offset file before running aws cloudwatch put-metric-data. Whole-script runtime probes showed offset 2/source 7/failing AWS becomes offset 7, and the next successful run publishes 0 rather than 5 for every stream. Removing only error suppression does not recover the count. Original feature stories explicitly require these observed failures to publish metrics and trip alarms.

## Repair plan

- Reorder each of the six concrete publish shapes so the matching offset advances only after a successful CloudWatch call. Cover replication, voter, merge-change, deploy, both shared autodeploy-marker streams, and G2P.
- Preserve the script systemd exit-0 contract and existing logging behavior: AWS failure stays best-effort for the overall probe, but the failed metric remains unacknowledged.
- Keep zero-delta publication behavior unchanged; a successful zero publish may acknowledge the observed total. Preserve reset handling where total below offset retries total.
- Add a whole-script PATH-shim regression oracle that drives the real script, fails each targeted AWS metric once, proves the offset is byte-identical after failure, then proves a successful retry publishes the accumulated delta and advances the offset. Include zero/reset controls and both shared-helper metrics.

## Testing

- Run `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py tests/scripts/test_observability_exit.py`.
- Run `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All seven cumulative counter streams advance their offset only after the matching successful AWS publication, checked by the whole-script test.
- [x] A failed publication leaves the targeted offset byte-identical, checked for every stream by the whole-script test.
- [x] A subsequent successful run publishes the accumulated delta and then advances the offset, checked for every stream.
- [x] Reset handling retries the reset total after failure, and zero-delta behavior remains compatible.
- [x] observability.sh still exits zero when an individual AWS publication fails and on a healthy run.
- [x] The held-out oracle is observed RED before the fix, GREEN after the fix, and RED again under the original pre-acknowledgement mutation.
- [x] Repository lint and typecheck gates pass.
baseline.summary: observability.sh advances its metric offset before the CloudWatch publish, so a transient put-metric-data failure permanently loses that interval's count

baseline.description:
Discovered during the DC<->Cloud test-parity re-audit (epic 3e73-72b5-cff2-40f0).

DC pins the empty-outbound-assignee behaviour POSITIVELY: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_unassign_751e.py::test_empty_outbound_assignee_actually_unassigns` and `::test_unassign_co_submitted_with_an_editable_field_does_both`.

Cloud has the implementation (bug 85a1, `AcliClient.update_issue` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`: an assignee in `(None, "")` is POPPED and routed to `self.unassign_issue(...)` instead of being sent to ACLI as `--assignee ""`, which ACLI silently no-ops), but the only Cloud test is NEGATIVE (`mutate/test_assignee_validation.py::test_update_issue_transient_error_propagates_does_not_unassign`). Nothing asserts the positive path, so a regression that re-forwards `--assignee ""` — the exact silent-success defect 85a1 fixed — would keep every Cloud test green.

Scope: TEST-ONLY. Behaviour-preserving; no production file is modified. The new test drives the real `AcliClient.update_issue` with `unassign_issue` recorded on a fake and `acli_subprocess._run_acli` stubbed (deterministic, no subprocess, no network).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] New file `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_unassign_6a74.py` exists and contains the
      Cloud characterization, with a docstring naming the DC tests it mirrors.
- [x] A test asserts that `AcliClient.update_issue(key, assignee="")` calls `unassign_issue(key)`
      exactly once AND spawns no `workitem edit` subprocess (no editable field remains).
- [x] The same assertion holds for `assignee=None` (both empty sentinels are covered).
- [x] A test asserts the co-submit case: `update_issue(key, assignee="", summary="new summary")`
      calls `unassign_issue(key)` once AND emits a `workitem edit` argv carrying `--summary
      "new summary"` and NO `--assignee` flag — i.e. both halves apply and the empty string never
      reaches ACLI.
- [x] A contrast test asserts a NON-empty assignee still takes the validate-then-edit path:
      `unassign_issue` is not called and `--assignee` IS present in the argv.
- [x] No file under `src/` changes (verified: `git diff --stat` touches only `tests/`).

## Testing

- [x] Proof: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_unassign_6a74.py -q` passes.
- [x] Proof: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass from the worktree venv.
- [x] Proof: the characterization is falsifiable — checked by temporarily removing the empty-assignee
      branch locally and confirming the new tests FAIL, then reverting.
baseline.summary: Cloud empty-assignee unassign characterization (positive parity with DC test_dc_unassign_751e)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The inbound fetcher can only see one tracker project. `jqls_for(project)` builds exactly one pair of queries — active and recent-done — from a single key (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:78-90`), and `_validate_project_key` refuses an empty or malformed key outright rather than searching unscoped (`fetcher.py:63-75`, bug `626d`). A store that lists several projects in its mapping still ingests only one of them.

## Approach

Fan out: call the existing `jqls_for` once per project in the store mapping and union the results into the snapshot, rather than building a single `project IN (A,B)` query. Two concrete reasons. First, the per-query truncation ceiling (`_ACLI_CEILING = 1200` at `fetcher.py:91`, raising `SilentTruncationError`) stays scoped per project instead of becoming a shared budget that a single busy project could exhaust on behalf of the others. Second, it reuses `jqls_for` and `_validate_project_key` unchanged, so the JQL-injection guard that bug `626d` added keeps applying to every key with no new interpolation site.

Inbound-created tickets record their source project in `bridge_project` and get their `repos` defaulted from that project's mapping entry. The existing local-id derivation already encodes the project (`_jira_key_to_local_id`, `inbound_translate.py:120-124`, `DIG-123` → `jira-dig-123`), so ids stay unique across projects with no change; this story makes the association explicit on the ticket rather than only implicit in the id.

The CREATE event for an inbound ticket is written directly rather than through `create_core` (`apply_inbound_records.py:150-222`, which stamps `creation_channel` at `:221`), so the two new fields are stamped at that same site.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful verified fake fed production-shaped Jira fixtures. The fake must record the queries issued, because "one JQL pair per project" is itself the contract under test and is invisible to a result-only assertion.

- Happy path: a mapping with two projects issues exactly two query pairs — one per key — and the
  resulting snapshot contains issues from both.
- Postcondition: each ticket created from the fetch records the project its issue came from, and its
  `repos` equal that project's mapping entry.
- Edge: a project listed in the mapping that returns zero issues contributes nothing and does not
  fail the pass.
- Failure path: one project exceeding the per-query ceiling raises `SilentTruncationError` naming
  that project, and the ceiling is evaluated per project — a second project under the limit is not
  penalised by the first. This is the contrast case that proves the budget is not shared.
- Collateral invariant: a store whose mapping holds exactly one project issues the same query pair as
  before this change, so single-project behaviour is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mapping with two projects issues one JQL pair per project in a single pass; checked by a fake
      transport recording the issued queries and asserting the exact pair count and contents.
- [ ] Each inbound-created ticket records its source project and the repos from that project's
      mapping entry; checked by asserting both fields on tickets created from a two-project fixture.
- [ ] The truncation ceiling applies per project, not as a shared budget; checked by a test where one
      project exceeds it and a second under-limit project still ingests successfully.
- [ ] A single-project mapping issues an identical query pair to the pre-change behaviour; checked by
      a regression test comparing the recorded queries.
- [ ] A configured project returning zero issues does not fail the pass; checked by an empty-result
      fixture.
baseline.summary: Multi-project inbound fetch: per-project JQL fan-out and source-project recording

baseline.description:
# `recheck-review` should accept a `bugfix-size-attestation` block once the ticket carries a current attestation

## The gap, hit for real

`retrigger.py:194` refuses `recheck-review` for ANY current-revision `finding` state, on the reasoning that "the fix for a finding is amend + re-push, not a retry" (module docstring, `retrigger.py:15-19`). That is right for a code veto. It is **wrong for `bugfix-size-attestation`**, whose remedy is not a code change at all: the fix is to write the plan into the TICKET and run `rebar review-plan <id>`.

Observed on Gerrit change **1378** (bug `738a-376e-4829-42ca`):

```
[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]
rebar code review found 1 blocking issue(s):
- (bugfix-size-attestation) ... 162 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but
  bug 738a-376e-4829-42ca has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; ...)
```

The attestation was then earned (`review-plan 738a` -> PASS, signed; verified `certified` / `valid: true`). The finding was therefore **stale**, but:

* `recheck-review` refused it as a "REAL FINDING";
* a no-code-change patchset **copies the -1 forward** (label copy condition
  `changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR ... TRIVIAL_REBASE`), so re-pushing the same tree does not clear it.

So the only route was to invent a code change purely to force a re-review. That is exactly the churn-for-the-bot the gate should never require, and it pressures a contributor into cosmetic edits to an already-reviewed change.

## Why accepting this case is SAFE

The module's own security argument already covers it (`retrigger.py:15-19`): a re-review "can only produce a fresh fail-closed verdict, never mint an unearned PASS". Refusing `finding` is a churn-control measure, not a safety boundary. If the attestation is genuinely still missing, the fresh review simply re-blocks.

## Design — both inputs stay PRIVILEGED-SIDE

The module's invariant is that eligibility is decided from durable Gerrit state, "never from anything the requesting comment says" (`retrigger.py:13-14`). This condition honours that: it reads the **bot's own** vote message plus the **ticket store**. Nothing from the requesting comment is consulted.

1. When the current state is `finding`, read the bot's own latest vote message on the current
   revision and require its HEADER count to be exactly one:
   `rebar code review found 1 blocking issue(s):`.

   **The header count is load-bearing and the finding LIST is not trustworthy for this.**
   `adapter.py:129-139` renders only the first **10** findings as `- (<criterion>) ...` lines and then
   appends `N additional blocking finding(s) omitted from this summary.` So "the rendered lines contain
   only bugfix-size-attestation" does NOT imply it is the only blocking finding — a mixed block could be
   unlocked by truncation. The header states the TOTAL (`len(blocking)`), so requiring exactly 1 closes
   that hole regardless of rendering. (Each finding's detail is also clipped at 240 chars,
   `adapter.py:133`, which is the second reason not to parse semantics out of the detail text.)
2. Require the single rendered `- (<criterion>)` line's criterion id to be exactly
   `bugfix-size-attestation`.
3. Resolve the ticket id from the CHANGE'S COMMIT MESSAGE via the gate's own resolver
   `ticket_for_commit_message(commit_message, repo_root=...)` — **not** from the finding text. This is
   how `apply_bugfix_size_gate` itself picks the ticket, so the two cannot disagree, and it sidesteps
   the 240-char detail clipping entirely rather than relying on the id happening to land inside it.
4. Re-classify with the gate's OWN privileged-side verifier,
   `bugfix_size_gate.classify_plan_review_attestation(ticket_id)` — the full chain (op-cert decode ->
   keyring verify at the storage anchor -> `compute_validity`) — and accept only when
   `bugfix_size_gate.bucket_for_verdict(verdict) == "accepted"`
   (`ACCEPTED_VERDICTS = {certified, stale-code, stale-head}`).
5. **Every failure path REFUSES** (fail-closed): header absent or count != 1, criterion line absent or
   not the expected id, commit message unavailable, ticket id unresolvable, classifier raising, or any
   non-`accepted` bucket. A parse that cannot establish the precondition is not evidence the
   precondition holds.

Reusing the gate's own classifier and bucketing is deliberate: a second, independent notion of "acceptable attestation" in the retrigger path would drift from the gate that produced the finding.

## What must still refuse

* any block whose findings are not exactly `{bugfix-size-attestation}`;
* an attestation that is absent, `stale-material`, `mismatch`, `invalid`, or otherwise in
  `FLAG_VERDICTS` — otherwise a contributor could attest, then edit the plan, and unlock a re-review
  on an attestation that no longer covers the plan;
* an `infra` verdict (`unavailable` / `error`) must NOT auto-accept via this new arm — it is not
  evidence the attestation exists. (It remains eligible through the pre-existing coverage-gap arm if
  the bot itself tagged a coverage gap.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `recheck-review` is ACCEPTED when the current revision's block is exactly the
      `bugfix-size-attestation` finding AND the named ticket's plan-review attestation buckets as
      `accepted` — proven RED-first, since the current code refuses every `finding`
- [x] a block containing `bugfix-size-attestation` PLUS any other blocking finding is still REFUSED
- [x] a `bugfix-size-attestation` block whose ticket attestation is absent or `stale-material` is
      still REFUSED, with the observed verdict named in the refusal reply
- [x] an `infra` verdict (`unavailable` / `error`) does not accept through this arm
- [x] eligibility reads only the bot's own vote message and the ticket store — asserted by a test that
      puts a forged criterion id and ticket id in the REQUESTING COMMENT and confirms it is ignored
- [x] the retrigger path still writes no vote (the existing no-`labels` invariant holds)
- [x] `classify_plan_review_attestation` / `bucket_for_verdict` are REUSED, not reimplemented —
      asserted by a test that monkeypatches the gate's classifier and observes the retrigger honour it
- [x] a block whose HEADER count is > 1 is REFUSED even when the only rendered `- (...)` line is
      `bugfix-size-attestation` — the truncation case, asserted with a synthetic 12-finding message
- [x] every parse failure refuses: missing header, unparseable count, missing criterion line,
      unresolvable ticket id, classifier exception — each asserted, not assumed
- [x] the ticket id comes from the commit-message trailer via `ticket_for_commit_message`, NOT from the
      finding detail text — asserted by a test whose finding text names a DIFFERENT ticket than the
      trailer, confirming the trailer wins
- [x] the refusal message for a genuine code finding is unchanged

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit -k "retrigger or recheck_review or bugfix_size" -q
    make lint && make typecheck

RED-first is load-bearing here: the accept path must be shown to fail against today's code (which refuses every `finding`) before the condition is added, or the test proves nothing. The forged-comment test is the security assertion — it is the one that would catch a future refactor that starts trusting the requesting comment for the criterion id or the ticket id.
baseline.summary: recheck-review should accept a bugfix-size-attestation block once the ticket carries a current plan-review attestation

# op-cert: docs + ADR (env-attribution, postures, integrity, producer signing, HMAC removal)

## Context
Document the operation-certificate model and its security contract as a named ADR artifact `docs/adr/NNNN-opcert-asymmetric.md` (pick the next free ADR number), cross-referencing ADR 0046 (security posture; L2 no-transparency-log and L4 single-environment/no-threshold are op-cert-scoped). The ADR documents the **settled** model from the epic's two design-resolution sections, including the round-6 producer-signing resolution: uniform producer signing (every environment signs with its own auto-generated Ed25519 key at `<tracker>/.opcert-key`; the trusted server is an ordinary environment whose key is pinned out-of-band and which fetches authoritative state), per-kind native verdict vocabularies with the transport-status/verdict split in the remote job API, signer identity as deployment config (no repo-config `env_id` key; consumer policy = `verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since`; client routing = `verify.opcert_remote_url`), the cost-verified runtime choice — the existing trusted VM (compose service) behind an API Gateway HTTP API SigV4 front with an async job API (Lambda and a dedicated Fargate stack rejected, with reasons incl. the zero-fixed-monthly-cost constraint), the stateless store-read-only server (client persists the self-authenticating envelope), and HMAC removal via expand-contract (`docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/NNNN-opcert-asymmetric.md` exists and is non-empty, covering: the
      environment-attribution model, low/high-security postures, the authoritative-state-fetch
      integrity requirement, the out-of-band trust root (`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`),
      merge-gate enforcement, the authoritative era anchor (storage-position key validity; rotation-with-pin vs kill-switch revocation), uniform producer signing + local key provenance, the trusted-server
      runtime + async job API + stateless/read-only posture, and HMAC removal + migration.
- [ ] The ADR cross-references ADR 0046 and contains the strings `rebar.opcert.v1`,
      `trusted_environments.yaml`, and `ADR 0046`; a test asserts the file exists, is non-empty,
      and contains those strings.
baseline.summary: op-cert: docs + ADR (env-attribution, postures, integrity, HMAC removal)
