# Populate `RemoteRef` on the inbound path, and correct what it actually protects

## Context / Problem

`RemoteRef` — the backend-neutral identity value `{vendor, instance, remote_id}` defined at `_backend.py:81` — is **never constructed in production code**. Re-verified against the current tree, not taken from the original report: in `src/` there is only the frozen dataclass, its docstring, and one comment in `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:206`. Every construction is in tests (`backend_support.py:228`, `test_backend_contract.py:96-97`).

Its `instance` field is documented as naming "the concrete deployment (e.g. a Jira site / project host) so two instances of the same vendor never collide". Nothing populates it, so that sentence describes an intention rather than a behaviour.

This surfaced in J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1], whose AC required asserting "a populated `RemoteRef.instance`" on a DC-created ticket. That assertion was not satisfiable against any reconcile pass, so J7's AC was narrowed to the provenance that IS observable (creation_channel + local-id prefix) and this ticket was filed for the remainder.

## The decision this plan makes

The original draft said "needs design, not just implementation" and left the `instance` source open. It is decided here, because a plan that defers its central choice cannot be implemented from.

**`instance` is derived from the CONFIGURED base URL** — normalised (scheme dropped, host lowercased, default port dropped, trailing slash dropped, context path retained, since DC is commonly served at `/jira`). It is available wherever a backend is constructed (`JiraDataCenterSettings.url`, `settings.py:45`, itself `reconciler.base_url`), needs no extra REST round-trip, and requires no operator action.

**The stability objection is real and is answered by SCOPE, not by cleverness.** The draft warned that "if `instance` is derived from a mutable base URL, an operator moving their instance silently re-identifies every ticket". That is true of a PERSISTED key. It is not true here for one reason only, and the reason is sufficient on its own: **this story does not persist a `RemoteRef` anywhere.** It is an in-memory value returned by a port member. Nothing on disk carries it, so a URL change re-labels nothing.

A PREVIOUS REVISION ALSO CLAIMED "bindings already key on the issue's immutable numeric id — 7c26 changed exactly that". **That claim was WRONG and is withdrawn**, verified in `binding_store.py` rather than argued: the binding's primary key is still the Jira KEY (`entry["jira_key"]`, and the reverse index is `reverse[jira_key]`). 7c26 was ADDITIVE — it added `record_jira_id`/`get_jira_id` as a supplemental fallback that `note_absent_or_rekey` uses to RE-KEY an entry after a 404. The argument above never needed that claim, so it is removed rather than repaired. **This story does NOT make it a persisted key, and says so in BOTH ADRs (0055 and 0035).** Any future story that persists a `RemoteRef` inherits the stability problem and must solve it there (the candidate is an operator-set opaque id, or the instance's own server id — neither is needed for in-memory use, and adding either now would be unused configuration).

## THE CORRECTION THIS TICKET ACTUALLY DELIVERS — the collision claim is FALSE as written

Verified in source rather than reasoned about, and it changes the ticket's conclusion:

* `vendor` ALREADY separates the deployments. Cloud's backend sets `vendor = "jira"`
  (`adapters/jira/backend.py:142`); DC's sets `vendor = "jira-datacenter"`
  (`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:200`). So Cloud-vs-DC never needed `instance`; what
  `instance` disambiguates is TWO DEPLOYMENTS OF THE SAME VENDOR — e.g. two DC instances.
* **Populating `instance` does NOT prevent the collision the docstring claims it prevents.** The
  colliding value is the LOCAL TICKET ID, and `_jira_key_to_local_id`
  (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`) is `"jira-" + jira_key.lower()` — it takes the Jira key and
  NOTHING else. Two DC deployments that each have a project `DIG` both mint `jira-dig-123` for
  their own issue 123, whatever `RemoteRef.instance` says. The field cannot fix that, because
  nothing consults it when the local id is minted.

So AC4 of this ticket ("e369's shared-identity claim is either satisfied or its ADR amended to match reality") resolves to **AMEND BOTH ADRs** — 0055 and 0035, enumerated in Scope. Making the local id instance-aware would change the id scheme for every existing Jira-sourced ticket — a breaking, store-wide migration that is not this ticket and must not be smuggled into it.

## Approach — and THE RECEIVER, which the first revision left unnamed

Round 1 was BLOCKED, correctly and twice, on the same hole: it said "construct a `RemoteRef` on the inbound path" without naming where the value GOES. With no receiver the construction is a local variable that is immediately discarded — a no-op that adds a line and changes nothing — and the "assert on the object the pass actually built" criterion is unsatisfiable by construction, because nothing exposes it. The correction:

**THE RECEIVER IS A `remote_ref()` MEMBER ON THE `Backend` PORT, and the codebase already told us so.** The test double has implemented exactly this method since J7 — `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py:227-228`: `def remote_ref(self, remote_id: str) -> RemoteRef: return RemoteRef(vendor=self.vendor, instance="test", remote_id=remote_id)`. The FAKE satisfies a port member that the PORT never declared and no real backend implements. That asymmetry is the actual defect underneath this ticket: the contract tests pass against a fake that is strictly more capable than production.

So:
1. DECLARE `remote_ref(self, remote_id: str) -> RemoteRef` on the `Backend` Protocol.
2. IMPLEMENT it on both concrete backends, returning a `RemoteRef` built from an `instance` value
   the backend was GIVEN AT CONSTRUCTION — not one it resolves when called.
   **`remote_ref()` MUST NOT call `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` / `resolve_jira_settings()`
   at call time**, and this is a hard constraint rather than a style preference:
     * `JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__` takes `(transport, client=None)` and receives NO settings,
       so a call-time resolve reaches into ambient config. The contract test constructs backends
       with a `FakeTransport` and no config context, so it would fail for an environment reason
       having nothing to do with what it asserts.
     * this codebase has already been bitten by exactly that shape. A settings-resolving PROPERTY
       earned a `Verified -1` on change cd78: Python 3.12 changed runtime-checkable `Protocol`
       `isinstance` from `hasattr` to `inspect.getattr_static`, so a property that RAISES breaks
       `isinstance` on CI's 3.11 while passing locally on 3.13. The remedy adopted then was to move
       the resolution to the build site, and the same remedy applies here.
   So the backends take the value as a constructor parameter (defaulting to empty), and the
   `build_backend` factories — which already call `resolve_*_settings()` and therefore already hold
   `settings.url` — pass it in. The derivation itself is a small pure helper (the only logic in
   this story).
3. The backend method IS the observable. Assertions read what a real backend returns, which is a
   value that exists in production rather than one a test built.

**NO INVENTED CONSUMER.** Nothing in the pass consumes a `RemoteRef` today, and this story does NOT wire a call into the inbound path just to have one. Threading a value through a code path that does not use it would be ceremony that reads as coverage — the reviewer's point restated in the opposite direction. The deliverable is that the port vocabulary becomes REAL and populated on both backends; a consumer arrives with the story that needs one.

**THIS CHANGES AN ORIGINAL AC, deliberately, and the reason is recorded.** The ticket as filed said "a reconcile pass constructs a RemoteRef". Against the current code that is not satisfiable without adding a consumer that has no purpose, so the criterion is restated as "both real backends return a populated `RemoteRef` through a declared port member, asserted against the real backend". The ticket's own text called its scope a "sketch [that] needs design, not just implementation", and its plan has never been certified, so these are draft criteria being settled rather than settled criteria being reopened.

## Scope

- `rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — DECLARE `remote_ref()` on the `Backend` Protocol, and correct
  `RemoteRef`'s docstring. NO change to `RemoteRef`'s FIELDS (it is a frozen value type with a
  passing contract test; changing its shape is out of scope).
- both concrete backends (`adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`) —
  IMPLEMENT `remote_ref()`, and accept the `instance` value as a CONSTRUCTOR parameter.
- both `build_backend` factories — pass `settings.url` in (they already resolve settings).
- a new pure `instance`-normalisation helper + unit tests.
- the ADRs amended per the section above — BOTH files that carry the claim, named rather than
  gestured at: `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` (its ":146" line calls `RemoteRef.instance`
  "INTENDED design, not an existing mechanism", and its ":317" open-issue entry says it "remains
  unbuilt", citing this ticket) and `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`, which
  introduces `RemoteRef`. Amending only one leaves the other asserting the opposite.

**NOT in scope:** wiring a `remote_ref()` call into the inbound path or any other pass (no consumer exists; see Approach); changing `_jira_key_to_local_id` or the local-id scheme (a breaking store-wide migration); persisting `RemoteRef` anywhere; any new config key.

## Testing

* the normalisation helper is unit-tested directly: two DIFFERENT deployment URLs give DIFFERENT
  `instance` values, and two spellings of the SAME deployment (trailing slash, upper-case host,
  explicit default port) give the SAME one. The second half is the one that matters — a helper that
  merely returns the URL passes the first half trivially.
* BOTH REAL BACKENDS return a `RemoteRef` with a non-empty `instance` from `remote_ref()`,
  asserted against a real backend object rather than the fake — the fake has implemented this
  method all along, so a test that only exercises the fake would pass today, before any change.
* the contract test constructs those backends with NO ambient config, passing the `instance`
  EXPLICITLY, and still passes — which is what proves `remote_ref()` reads constructor state
  rather than resolving settings at call time. If it needs a config fixture, the constraint above
  has been violated. A second construction WITHOUT the argument must return the empty default,
  distinguishing "used what it was given" from "found a value elsewhere".
* two backends configured at different base URLs produce `RemoteRef`s that are NOT equal, and two
  configured at the same URL produce equal ones (`RemoteRef` is frozen and value-equal, which
  `test_backend_contract.py:96-97` already pins).
* a REGRESSION GUARD for the correction above: a test asserting that two deployments sharing a
  project key DO still mint the same local id, with a docstring naming this as known and bounded.
  Pinning the limitation stops a later reader assuming `instance` solved it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a pure helper derives `instance` from a base URL; different deployments differ, and
      equivalent spellings of one deployment (trailing slash / case / default port) agree
- [ ] `Backend` DECLARES `remote_ref()`, both concrete backends IMPLEMENT it, and each returns a
      `RemoteRef` whose `vendor` and `remote_id` are correct and whose `instance` is EXACTLY THE
      VALUE THE CONSTRUCTOR WAS GIVEN — asserted against the REAL backends, constructed in the test
      with an EXPLICIT instance argument and no ambient config. There is no tension between "no
      config" and "non-empty instance": the value is non-empty BECAUSE the test passes one in, and
      that is precisely what proves `remote_ref()` reads its constructor state rather than
      resolving settings. A backend constructed WITHOUT the argument returns the empty default,
      which is also asserted — so the test distinguishes "took the injected value" from "found one
      somewhere else". (This restates the ticket's original "a reconcile pass constructs a
      RemoteRef": nothing consumes one, so satisfying that literally would mean adding a
      purposeless consumer. Reasoning in Approach.)
- [ ] two backends at different base URLs yield unequal `RemoteRef`s for the same `remote_id`
- [ ] the chosen `instance` source is documented, INCLUDING what happens when the base URL changes,
      and including that this story does not persist a `RemoteRef` anywhere — which is the whole
      reason a URL change re-labels nothing on disk
- [ ] BOTH ADRs named in Scope (0055 and 0035) and `RemoteRef`'s docstring are AMENDED to state
      that `instance` does NOT prevent
      local-id collision between two same-vendor deployments — `_jira_key_to_local_id` derives the
      id from the Jira key alone — and that `vendor` already separates Cloud from DC
- [ ] a test pins that known limitation, so it cannot be silently assumed fixed
- [ ] no new operator-facing config key is introduced, `_jira_key_to_local_id` is unchanged, and no
      `remote_ref()` call is added to any pass (the port member is the deliverable; a consumer is not)
- [ ] `remote_ref()` resolves NO configuration when called — the `instance` value arrives via the
      constructor from the `build_backend` factory, and the contract test constructs both real
      backends with no config context to prove it
- [ ] the contract test covers `remote_ref()` for the REAL backends, closing the gap where
      `backend_support.FakeBackend` implemented a port member production did not
baseline.summary: Populate RemoteRef on the inbound path so deployment identity is observable

baseline.description:
## The hazard, and it already caused a live incident

`git stash` writes to the SHARED git common dir, not to the worktree. On this host there are roughly 30 worktrees with multiple agents working concurrently, so the stash is a single global stack that every agent pushes to and pops from.

Two agents stashing at overlapping times will pop EACH OTHER'S uncommitted work into the wrong worktree.

## Confirmed incident 2026-08-05

An agent working bug c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af used `git stash` twice to check whether a test failure was pre-existing. On the second use a concurrent agent's stash operation interleaved, and it popped the OTHER agent's changes into its worktree while its own went to theirs.

It recovered only because it happened to hold out-of-band copies. The displaced work was preserved two ways and is STILL SITTING THERE at time of filing:

    stash@{0}: On fix-c5b3-scc-byfile: RECOVERED measurement-provenance work
               (ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance) displaced into worktree
               fix-c5b3-scc-byfile by a shared-stash race;
               backup at /tmp/RECOVERED-stash-race

ACTION NEEDED INDEPENDENT OF THIS BUG: that is another session's work on ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance. Whoever owns it likely does not know it was displaced. It should be returned to its owner before anything prunes the stash or clears /tmp.

## Why this is a rebar problem and not just a git fact

rebar's own guidance actively produces the conditions for it. AGENTS.md mandates working in fresh worktrees, and `make worktree` makes spinning them up a single command. The parallel-agent workflow is a documented, encouraged pattern. So the project tells agents to run many worktrees in parallel while `git stash` — a reflex command for "let me check this against a clean tree" — is silently global across all of them.

The failure is also SILENT and DESTRUCTIVE: `git stash pop` succeeds, the wrong files appear, and nothing indicates the content came from another worktree. An agent that then commits has committed someone else's work; an agent whose changes vanished may conclude its edits were never made.

## What agents should do instead (all worktree-local)

- A throwaway worktree for the clean-tree comparison:
  `git worktree add /tmp/<unique> origin/main --detach`
- `git archive <ref>` to materialize a specific tree shape (ticket 7e90's agent did exactly
  this successfully to reproduce a pre-gate `.github/` layout).
- `git diff > /tmp/<unique>.patch` + `git checkout -- <paths>`, re-applied with `git apply`.
- Plain file copies inside the agent's own worktree directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AGENTS.md states plainly that `git stash` is UNSAFE in this repo's parallel-worktree
      workflow, with the worktree-local alternatives above, sited where an agent reaching for
      stash will actually see it (near the worktree/parallel-agent guidance, not an appendix).
- [ ] The reason is given, not just the prohibition — an agent that understands the stash is
      global will generalize; one told a bare rule will work around it.
- [ ] Consider a mechanical block rather than relying on agents reading docs: evaluate whether
      a pre-commit or wrapper can refuse `git stash` when more than one worktree exists, and
      either implement it or record why not.
- [ ] The displaced ADR 0061 work above is returned to its owner or confirmed no longer needed,
      and the stash entry and /tmp backup are cleaned up only after that.
- [ ] Sweep for other git commands with the same shared-common-dir property and document any
      found (hooks are already known-shared — bug 84aa records a worktree-wide hook clobber
      from the same root cause, which suggests this class is recurring).

## Provenance

Reported by the agent that hit it while working c5b3. Bug 84aa is prior art for the same class: hooks live in the shared common dir, so installing one from a linked worktree clobbered it for every worktree at once.
baseline.summary: git stash is SHARED across all worktrees, so parallel agents silently swap each other's uncommitted work

baseline.description:
## Why

Epic 3156 required a **visual-editor UX** for authoring project criteria (story 6e31). That UX is
BROKEN for the primary case — authoring a NET-NEW criterion — so the deliverable's user experience
fails a round trip:

- A project criterion MUST be `project.<name>`-prefixed (the overlay namespace that guarantees a
  project criterion can never rebind a built-in — ef7e/ADR 0015).
- Its rubric is a prompt stored at `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md`, and `get_prompt` /
  `create_prompt` derive that filename from the criterion id as `plan-review-<id>`.
- But `prompt_library._validate_id` → `prompt_authoring._valid_id` enforces `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*`
  — **no `.`** (a filename-safety rule: a `.` would let an id masquerade as a `<id>.<variant>.md`
  overlay and enables traversal). So `plan-review-project.foo` is rejected at author time, AND
  `.rebar/prompts/` would mis-read a dotted stem as a variant overlay.

Net effect: the editor can RE-TUNE a built-in (id `F1`) but CANNOT author a net-new `project.<name>`
criterion end-to-end — the exact thing project-supplied criteria exist for. 6e31 currently
validate-then-rollback-rejects the attempt with a clean 400, so it never persists a broken overlay,
but the UX still dead-ends. This must be remediated for the editor UX to actually work.

## What — decouple the logical id from the physical filename (the Semgrep/npm/Python pattern)

Popular, actively-maintained tools NEVER force a namespaced logical id to also be a raw filename;
they decouple via ONE deterministic mapping:
- **Semgrep**: the dotted rule `id` is a metadata field, decoupled from the file name.
- **npm**: `@scope/name` → a deterministic path `node_modules/@scope/name/`.
- **Python**: `a.b.c` → `a/b/c.py` (dots → path separators).

Apply the same here. The criterion id stays `project.<name>` (dotted) EVERYWHERE it matters
(overlay key, `activate`, routing, no-rebind collision check, the `.`→`_` workflow-output-key
sanitization). Only the RUBRIC's physical storage is decoupled, via a SINGLE canonical function:

- Add `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id) -> str` (one source of truth): a built-in `<id>` →
  `plan-review-<id>` (unchanged); a `project.<name>` → `plan-review-project-<name>` (`.`→`-`), a
  filesystem-safe, `_valid_id`-valid prompt id. Injective because a project name is constrained to
  a DOT-FREE charset (exactly one namespace dot) — validate this in `_validate_routing_entry` /
  the namespace check so `project.a-b` and any dotted variant can never collide.
- Route BOTH sides through it so they can never diverge:
  - descriptor resolution: `criteria.model.build_descriptor` / `plan_review.registry` resolve a
    project criterion's rubric via `get_prompt(criterion_prompt_id(cid), repo_root=...)` (not the
    raw `plan-review-<cid>`);
  - editor authoring: `criterion_preview.author_criterion_overlay` writes the rubric via
    `create_prompt(criterion_prompt_id(cid), ...)` (now a valid id → passes `_valid_id`), then the
    atomic overlay routing+activate write keyed by the dotted `project.<name>` id.
- `enumerate_library` / `_user_prompt_ids`: a `plan-review-project-<name>.md` stem has no `.`, so it
  is enumerated normally (no variant-overlay mis-read). No change needed beyond using the sanitized
  filename.

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py` (or a small shared `ids.py`) — `criterion_prompt_id`;
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` + `src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py` (descriptor rubric
  resolution); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py` (authoring writes via the mapping);
  `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` or `_validate_routing_entry` (constrain project name to
  dot-free); the editor UI (`editor_assets/src/rebarProvider.jsx`) so the authoring form derives +
  shows the resulting criterion id.
- **No back-compat burden (just-shipped feature):** project criteria shipped in ef7e days ago with
  no external data/users, so backward compatibility is NOT a requirement — the sanitized form is
  simply THE form. One clean code path (no dotted-`get_prompt` fallback). The ef7e/overlay TEST
  FIXTURES that hand-place a dotted `plan-review-project.no_print.md` are just rewritten to the
  sanitized `project.no-print` → `plan-review-project-no-print.md` — a free edit, not a migration.
  Built-in prompt-id resolution is unchanged only because there is no reason to touch it, not for
  compat.
- **Project-name charset (RESOLVED):** a project criterion name follows the SAME rule as any prompt
  id — `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*` (alnum + dash; NO dots, NO underscores) — with exactly ONE
  namespace dot in the full id (`project.<name>`). This makes `criterion_prompt_id` a total,
  injective, filesystem-safe map (`.`→`-` on the single namespace dot). A name containing `.` or
  `_` (or otherwise not matching the charset) is a LOCATED error at overlay load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single canonical `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)` maps `project.<name>` →
      `plan-review-project-<name>` (filesystem-safe, passes `_valid_id`) and a built-in `<id>` →
      `plan-review-<id>` (unchanged); it is the ONLY id→prompt-filename derivation, used by BOTH
      descriptor resolution and editor authoring.
- [ ] A net-new `project.<name>` criterion can be authored end-to-end via the editor
      (`create_prompt` no longer rejects it) AND then loaded/run by the gate (`load_criteria`
      resolves its rubric) — a test proves the full author→activate→load→run round trip.
- [ ] Project names are constrained to a dot-free charset (one namespace dot) so the id→prompt-id
      map is injective; a name with a `.` is a located error.
- [ ] `criterion_prompt_id` is total + injective: a built-in `<id>` → `plan-review-<id>` and a
      `project.<name>` → ONLY `plan-review-project-<name>` (no dotted fallback); a dotted/underscored
      project name is a located error. (Back-compat is not a requirement — one clean path.)
- [ ] The editor authoring form surfaces the resulting criterion id (`project.<name>`) so the user
      sees what will be created; a net-new author no longer dead-ends at a 400.


## The dotted criterion id flows through explicitly (remediation, run 2)

The mapping `criterion_prompt_id` is ONE-WAY (`project.foo` → `plan-review-project-foo`); it is NOT
reversible (a name may contain dashes, so `plan-review-project-foo-bar` can't be un-split to a unique
dotted id). Therefore the DOTTED criterion id (`project.foo`) is the primary key and must be carried
explicitly — never reverse-derived from the sanitized prompt id:
- The editor authoring form has an explicit **criterion-id field** whose value IS the dotted id
  (`project.<name>`); the `/library/create` POST body carries BOTH `id` = the dotted criterion id AND
  the `routing` object. (Today `_library_create` strips `plan-review-` off the prompt id to recover
  `cid` — that path only works for built-ins; for a project criterion the dotted id comes from the
  form field, not from un-stripping.)
- `author_criterion_overlay(criterion_id, routing, *, repo_root)` takes the DOTTED `criterion_id` as
  its primary argument. It computes `prompt_id = criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)` for the
  `create_prompt(prompt_id, rubric)` write, and keys the overlay `plan_review[criterion_id]` +
  `activate` entries by the DOTTED id. So the sanitized prompt filename is derived once, forward-only;
  the dotted id is authoritative for the overlay + activation.
- `write_criterion_overlay(repo_root, criterion_id, routing)` likewise keys by the dotted id.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation addition, run 2)

- [ ] The dotted criterion id (`project.<name>`) is passed EXPLICITLY through authoring (the editor
      form's id field → `/library/create` body → `author_criterion_overlay(criterion_id=...)`), never
      reverse-derived from the sanitized prompt id; the overlay entry + `activate` are keyed by the
      dotted id while the rubric is written at `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)`.


## Call-site responsibility (remediation, run 3 — the single wiring table)

Exactly one site applies `criterion_prompt_id`; every site's job is pinned:

1. **Editor form** (`rebarProvider.jsx`): the id field's value IS the dotted criterion id
   (`project.<name>`). POST `/library/create` body = `{id: "project.<name>", kind: "criterion",
   body: <rubric md>, routing: {...}}`.
2. **`editor._library_create`** (the orchestrator): for `kind == "criterion"` with a `routing`, it
   (a) computes `prompt_id = criteria.ids.criterion_prompt_id(id)`; (b) calls
   `create_prompt(prompt_id, body, repo_root=...)` — THIS is the ONE place `criterion_prompt_id` is
   applied before `create_prompt`, so the sanitized (valid) id reaches the write path; (c) calls
   `write_criterion_overlay(repo_root, criterion_id=id, routing)` keyed by the DOTTED id (routing +
   `activate`). Order is prompt-first (a failed overlay leaves an inactive, harmless prompt), and the
   overlay write is the existing atomic validate-then-rollback.
3. **`author_criterion_overlay`** is RENAMED/refocused to take the dotted `criterion_id` (not a
   prompt id) — it no longer strips `plan-review-` to recover the id (that path only worked for
   built-ins and can't recover a dotted id from the sanitized one). It delegates the routing+activate
   write to `write_criterion_overlay(repo_root, criterion_id, routing)`.
4. **Descriptor resolution** (`plan_review/registry._get_prompt` at registry.py:236 + the shared
   `criteria.model.build_descriptor` prompt path): resolve a criterion's rubric via
   `get_prompt(criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id), repo_root=...)` instead of the raw
   `f"plan-review-{cid}"` — so a `project.<name>` reads `plan-review-project-<name>.md`.
5. **`criterion_prompt_id`** lives in a new tiny `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py` (the single source),
   imported by both the editor authoring path and the descriptor path so they can never diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation addition, run 3)

- [ ] `criterion_prompt_id` is applied at exactly ONE pre-`create_prompt` site
      (`editor._library_create` for authoring) and at the descriptor-resolution site
      (`registry._get_prompt` / `build_descriptor`); a test authors `project.<name>` via
      `/library/create` and asserts the rubric lands at `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`
      AND `load_criteria` resolves it.
baseline.summary: Editor round-trip for net-new project criteria: decouple criterion id from rubric filename (project.<name> can't be authored — create_prompt forbids '.')

## Summary
The MCP blue-green autodeploy emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {reason: deploy_failed}` (→ `rebar/host:deploy_errors`, which pages the `rebar-autodeploy-errors` alarm) on TWO conditions that are *documented as routine, non-error backoffs that must be kept OUT of deploy_errors*: `port-exhausted` (retire-cap) and low-memory abort. This false-pages the general "deploys are failing" alarm during a normal landing burst, when the deploy is in fact correctly, safely deferring.

## Evidence (live, 2026-08-30 ~03:33–04:05 UTC on i-00880b2c7f13527c5)
During a burst of merges, both blue/green MCP ports (8092/8093) were held by un-reaped containers still in their 21-min graceful drain (`docker stop --time 1260`). Each deploy tick logged BOTH markers for the same event:
```
AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP {reason: port-exhausted, ...}
AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {reason: deploy_failed, detail: component=mcp target=... fail#1..4 backoff=60s..480s}
```
`rebar-autodeploy-errors` (deploy_errors, Sum>0 / 4 periods) and `rebar-autodeploy-mcp-retire-cap` BOTH went ALARM. It self-resolved (~04:15). No outage — MCP served the old build throughout; only the cutover was delayed.

## Root cause
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`: `record_mcp_backoff_failure` (~L668) calls `err deploy_failed "component=mcp ..."` → emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` → inflates `deploy_errors`. It is invoked on the two routine backoff paths — low-mem abort (~L915, after `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT`) and port-exhausted (~L924, after `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`). This contradicts the documented contract in `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (~L284-291, L355): the retire-cap and mem-abort markers are "each kept out of AUTODEPLOY_ERROR so a routine retire-cap / memory abort never inflates deploy_errors." The sustained case is already covered by the dedicated `mcp_retire_cap` / `mcp_mem_abort` alarms. Introduced by the blue-green commit `2a0a4b19f2ab` (ticket 6964), which shipped both the contract and the violating code — an internally-inconsistent plan (`plan_defect`).

## Standing intent — this is a fix, not a behavior decision
The intended behavior is documented in observability.sh. The code simply doesn't match it. No ADR / design decision required.

## Fix
Factor the backoff-timer bookkeeping (write `$MCP_BACKOFF_FILE` + prune) out of the `err deploy_failed` emission via a shared `schedule_mcp_backoff` helper. Add a `record_mcp_routine_backoff` variant (schedule + log, no `err deploy_failed`) and switch the two routine paths to it. Genuine-failure paths (build/tag/run/unhealthy/handshake/flip) keep `record_mcp_backoff_failure` and still page. The throttle still applies on all paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A routine `port-exhausted` (retire-cap) backoff does NOT emit `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/deploy_failed` and does NOT increment `deploy_errors`; the `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` marker + `mcp_retire_cap` metric remain the signal.
- [x] A routine low-memory abort likewise does NOT inflate `deploy_errors`; `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` + `mcp_mem_abort` remain the signal.
- [x] GENUINE MCP deploy failures (build-failed, tag-failed, run-failed, unhealthy, handshake, flip) STILL emit `deploy_failed` and page `deploy_errors` (no regression to real-failure alarming).
- [x] The mcp backoff throttle (timer/prune) still applies on the routine paths so ticks don't hammer during a drain — only the erroneous deploy_errors emission is removed (the `mcp-deploy-backoff` file is still written).
- [x] A regression test asserts the observable outcome: the retire-cap/mem-abort paths emit their own marker but NOT `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`, while a real failure emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — includes new `test_port_exhausted_routine_backoff_does_not_inflate_deploy_errors` and `test_low_memory_routine_backoff_does_not_inflate_deploy_errors` (assert routine marker present, no `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/deploy_failed`, throttle file still written), plus existing `test_mcp_failure_keeps_the_deploy_failed_metric_and_names_the_component` and `test_unhealthy_new_container_leaves_old_upstream_current` (genuine failures still emit `deploy_failed`).
- Verified: `make lint` (shellcheck), `make typecheck`, `make test` all green. Mutation check: reintroducing `record_mcp_backoff_failure` on the routine sites returns both new tests to RED.

## Notes
Checked for duplication against the blue-green target ticket (6964) and the graceful-drain-contract bug (b580) — not duplicates. The plan-review overlap detector flags shared artifact `record_mcp_backoff_failure` with e1d9 (handshake gate, already landed in origin/main) and the held-back sibling `prespinal-gem-kinkajou` (dbf0); this change edits disjoint lines (function def + the two routine call sites) and lands first in the autodeploy.sh cluster.
baseline.summary: Autodeploy MCP routine backoff (retire-cap port-exhausted / mem-abort) inflates deploy_errors, false-paging the general deploy alarm

# Directory reorg + TicketQuery for the list_tickets 14-param replication

## Context
Two independent maintainability items from the 2026-07-02 audit, grouped under one ticket. They
share no code and land as SEPARATE Gerrit changes (each carries this ticket's trailer):
- **Part B (TicketQuery)** — collapse the ~14-filter replication that `list_tickets` threads across
  6 sites down to 3 boundary signatures + one dataclass.
- **Part A (dir reorg)** — group two flat packages into subpackages along existing prefix seams
  (reorg only, no file-splitting): the root `llm/` (normal imports; low risk) and the reconciler
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (48 flat files; **path-loaded**, higher risk — see the note).

## Part B — TicketQuery (do first; contained)
`list_tickets` replicates the same ~14 filter params across 6 sites:
1. `src/rebar/__init__.py` — public facade `list_tickets` (scalar API; KEEP signature)
2. `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` — MCP tool `list_tickets` (tool schema; KEEP signature)
3. `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py` `_cmd_list` (argv contract; KEEP)
4. `src/rebar/_reads.py` `list_tickets` (internal pass-through — COLLAPSE)
5. `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` `list_states` (filter core — COLLAPSE)
6. `src/rebar/reducer/_filters.py` `apply_ticket_filters` (7-param subset — partial)
Introduce a `TicketQuery` dataclass built at the 3 public boundaries and threaded inward via
`**asdict` / a `to_engine_kwargs()` that owns the `full`→`include_body` rename and None→"" coercion.
A new filter then touches 3 sites, not 6. Public + MCP + CLI signatures unchanged.

## Part A.1 — llm/ reorg (low risk)
Group by existing prefix seam (normal imports; update import paths only):
- `prompting/`: `prompts.py`, `prompt_library.py`, `prompts_frontmatter.py`
- `evals/`: `eval.py`, `eval_scorers.py`, `eval_solver.py` (fold in the existing `eval_specs/`)

## Part A.2 — reconciler reorg (HIGH RISK — path-loaded, subprocess-isolated)
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/` is NOT normal-imported: `__main__.py` loads siblings via
`spec_from_file_location` under **flat** dotted keys `rebar_reconciler.<name>`, computing
`Path(__file__).parent / f"{name}.py"`. ~15 sibling-load sites duplicate this, tests **pre-seed
`sys.modules` with these exact flat keys** as patch() targets, and Python 3.14 dataclass resolution
requires each `@dataclass` module's `__module__` to match its sys.modules key. Grouping into
`acli/`/`outbound/`/`inbound/` breaks every one of these unless the key + relative-path computation
and all pre-seeding tests are updated in lockstep. This package is subprocess-isolated (absent from
the import SCC), so the reorg yields tidiness only — no import-health benefit. Sequence LAST; if the
risk/benefit proves unfavorable, surface the tradeoff rather than force it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `TicketQuery` threaded through `_reads.list_tickets` + `list_states` (+ `apply_ticket_filters` where applicable); a new filter touches 3 sites not 6; public + MCP + CLI scalar signatures unchanged; tests green.
- [ ] `llm/` grouped into `prompting/` + `evals/`; imports updated; suites green.
- [ ] Reconciler grouped into `acli/`/`outbound/`/`inbound/` with the path-loader keys + relative paths + sys.modules-preseeding tests updated in lockstep and the subprocess boundary intact; suites green — OR the reorg is descoped with the risk/benefit tradeoff recorded and agreed.
- [ ] Each part lands as its own Gerrit change; `make lint` + `make check` + full suite green; commits carry `rebar-ticket:` trailers.

baseline.description:
## Summary

The blue-green autodeploy of the `mcp` target is crash-looping on a fail-closed auth check, and the box is currently serving a **hand-patched container whose fix is not in git**. The next successful deploy will revert that patch and re-break the service.

`rebar-autodeploy-errors` is IN ALARM (confirmed 2026-08-25 via `describe-alarms`, us-east-1).

## Evidence

Verbatim from SSM invocation `0d3b8b4b` (2026-08-25T16:37:45Z):

    rebar._mcp_auth.AuthConfigError: static tokens file '/run/secrets/mcp-static-tokens.json' defines no tokens
      File "/app/src/rebar/mcp_server.py", line 774, in main
        server = build_server(cfg)
      File "/app/src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py", line 725, in _load_static_tokens

This is the documented fail-closed posture at `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:367-371`.

Consequence, from invocation `448230fe`:

    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "mcp-unhealthy", "detail": "new mcp container rebar-mcp-d49466b5e960-8092 failed /health within 120s; removing it, leaving the OLD upstream live"}
    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "deploy_failed", "detail": "target=d49466b5e960... fail#9 backoff=900s"}

An operator recovered manually at 16:55Z by injecting `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL` via `env_file` and running `compose recreate` (invocation `d1d2ce4a` — "HEALTHY at t=8", "Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8091"). A live probe confirms `GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` returns `HTTP 401 invalid_token`, so it is serving.

## Why this is urgent

1. The running config is out-of-band. The `env_file` injection is not committed, so it is one
   successful autodeploy away from being lost.
2. The deployed code is stale: the box serves `d49466b5e960`, four commits behind `main` HEAD at
   the time of investigation.
3. `fail#9 backoff=900s` means the loop is still retrying and still failing.

This is INDEPENDENT of the missing-tickets-store defect — it explains why the deployed code is stale, not why `fsck` reports an uninitialized store. Neither causes the other.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Revised** — the original set rested on a premise since retracted (see below).

The original AC1 asked that "the operator's manual REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL fix be captured in git so a deploy reproduces it rather than reverting it". That criterion is VOID: the value was already supplied from git by BOTH `docker-compose.yml` and `mcp_run_new`, each with the same default, and `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` already pinned it. The operator's hand-added `.env` line was redundant, not load-bearing, and there was nothing to capture. See the "CORRECTION #2" comment. Ticking it would have claimed work that was never needed.

The real, single defect and its criteria:

- [x] The mcp blue-green deploy path re-materializes its SSM-sourced secrets before starting the
      replacement container, so a rotated credential reaches it without a manual operator run.
      Delivered: `fetch-secrets.sh` is invoked in the mcp block of `autodeploy.sh`, before the
      build and well before `mcp_run_new`.
- [x] The refresh is FAIL-FAST with the same semantics as the review-bot path: an SSM error
      aborts the deploy while the OLD container is still serving, rather than replacing a
      working container using stale secrets. Delivered: `mcp-secrets-fetch-failed`.
- [x] A secrets-refresh failure is distinguishable in the error signal from a generic
      `mcp-unhealthy`. Delivered: its own named reason, asserted by
      `test_secrets_fetch_failure_aborts_before_touching_the_live_upstream`.
- [x] Regression coverage pins the ORDERING that makes it safe (refresh strictly before the new
      container starts), and the structural check pins that the call exists at all:
      `test_mcp_bluegreen_refreshes_ssm_secrets_before_starting_the_new_container`.
- [x] `rebar-autodeploy-errors` is OK **and the fix has actually deployed**. MET 2026-08-27.
      This criterion deliberately did NOT accept a green alarm as evidence: the alarm needs
      3-of-4 900s datapoints, so an isolated failure cannot trip it by construction. The
      evidence is therefore the raw event count and the running script, not the alarm:
      - `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy.service --since '24 hours ago' | grep -c AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`
        => **0**, across **63** successful ticks in the same window.
      - The box reports `up to date (634826846f97)`, and
        `git merge-base --is-ancestor 30d7059f632d 634826846f97` succeeds — so the merged
        secrets-refresh fix IS the autodeploy.sh actually executing on those 63 ticks.
      - `rebar-autodeploy.timer`: `active` / `enabled`, 2-minute cadence, last run 18:06:33Z.
      The timer state matters because the alarm went OK at 04:57Z while the timer was DISABLED
      for ~21h — zero errors because nothing ran. That green was an artifact; this one is not,
      and the distinction is why the criterion was written to require the fix RUNNING.

## Completion evidence (merged origin/main 30d7059f632d)

Landed as Gerrit 2230 with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Both new tests were mutation-checked: removing the `fetch-secrets.sh` call turns each RED, and restoring it turns them GREEN.
baseline.summary: mcp autodeploy crash-loops on AuthConfigError and the live fix is un-versioned (rebar-autodeploy-errors in ALARM)

## Why

The plan-review gate is a 742-LOC bespoke orchestrator (`orchestrator.py`, ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out) + a 663-LOC pass system (`passes.py`), running its 4-pass pipeline OFF the unified workflow engine. To converge on one substrate (and gain the visual editor + parity tooling), the pipeline must be re-expressed as a declarative engine workflow. The criteria-rubric prompts and pass-system prompts ALREADY exist as `.md` files in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/` (`plan-review-finder`/`-verifier`/`-coach`/`-isf-finder`/`-container` + 33 criterion rubrics), so this is WIRING existing prompts into a workflow, not authoring prompts.

## What

Author a v3 engine workflow (e.g. `.rebar/workflows/plan-review.yaml`) that expresses the pipeline using existing step kinds + epic A's constructs: a `uses` DET precheck wrapping `det_floor.py` (P1–P9; only P1/P5/P8 block) → an `overlay_triggers` precompute resolving the T1–T12 overlays + proportionate-scrutiny filter → `batch` finders over the routed criteria (using B1's production batch-runner) → an aggregate `prompt` verify (Pass-2, ONE call) → a `uses`/`branch` deterministic decide (Pass-3) → a `prompt` coach (Pass-4). The criteria list + their `when` overlays are assembled from `registry.py` at workflow-render time (the deterministic `_criterion_block()` assembly stays deterministic).

## Scope

- The `plan-review` workflow YAML + any new `uses` ops it needs (DET-precheck wrapper, registry→
  criteria assembly, decide, coach rendering) registered with input/output contracts.
- Reference existing library prompt ids; do NOT inline prompt text.
- Depends on B1 (production batch-runner). This story delivers the workflow + ops that PRODUCE a
  plan_review_verdict-shaped result OFFLINE (FakeAgentRunner); live cutover + signing is B5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A v3 `plan-review` engine workflow expresses DET precheck (`uses`) → overlay resolution →
      `batch` finders → aggregate `prompt` verify (one call) → `uses`/`branch` decide → `prompt`
      coach, referencing existing `reviewers/*.md` prompt ids.
- [ ] The Pass-1 criteria + their overlay `when` predicates are assembled from `registry.py`
      deterministically at render time; the production batch-runner (B1) drives the `batch` step.
- [ ] The workflow validates + lints clean and runs end-to-end OFFLINE (FakeAgentRunner) producing
      a plan_review_verdict-shaped result; a test exercises it.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: B2: plan-review as an engine workflow (DET precheck -> batch finders -> verify -> decide -> coach)

baseline.description:
## Why
`test_code_review_ws5.py::test_security_rule_yaml_files_are_present_and_nonempty` (`:36-39`) only checks one file is non-empty and greps another for the substrings `rebar.builtin.security.` and `rules:`. Invalid YAML, duplicate ids, malformed rule objects, wrong severities, or an unusable pattern all satisfy it. VALIDATED.

## Definitions (make the ACs concrete)
- **Rule family** = one vendored security-rule YAML file under
  `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/builtin/`. There are three security families:
  `security_iac_public_exposure.yaml`, `security_owasp_cwe.yaml`,
  `security_secrets_gitleaks.yaml`.
- **Loaded via the production loader** = through `rebar.grounding.detectors.registry`
  (`load_registry` / the file-level `_detectors_from_file`), which returns `Detector`
  objects (id, backend, namespace, envelope, rule) — NOT hand-parsed YAML.
- **Fails closed (observable)** = malformed vendored data never silently produces a usable
  detector. Two distinct, correctly-scoped observations:
  - **Invalid YAML (file-level):** the whole file yields ZERO detectors AND a recorded reason
    (`_detectors_from_file` returns `([], "parse_error")`; `Registry.parse_drops` carries the
    file-level drop) — the loss is SURFACED.
  - **A rule missing its `id` (rule-level):** that rule is simply ABSENT from the returned
    detectors (a per-rule silent skip in `_detector_from_rule`) while the file's other rules
    still load. There is NO `parse_drops` entry for a per-rule skip (parse_drops is file-level
    only); the observable is the detector's absence, not a recorded drop.

## What
Replace the substring/presence assertions with loader-based behavioral checks. Two production loader seams are used (both are the real code `load_registry` runs — no hand-parsing): `load_registry()` (loads the real built-in dir) for the POSITIVE assertions, and the file-level `registry._detectors_from_file(path) -> (detectors, reason)` for the FAIL-CLOSED case against a temp malformed file (`load_registry` hardcodes `_builtin_dir()`, so a temp dir is fed to the file-level loader instead).

1. Positive: call `load_registry()` and, for each of the three security families, assert the
   EXACT set of detector ids contributed by that family, their `backend`, and their declared
   severity (from the rule/envelope metadata) — pinning the real loaded contract, not a
   substring. (Match detectors to a family by their `source_path` / id namespace.)
2. Fail-closed (observable loss, never a silent working detector), via
   `_detectors_from_file(temp_path)`:
   - **Broken YAML:** a temp file with invalid YAML returns `([], "parse_error")` — ZERO
     detectors AND a non-None reason (the drop is surfaced, per the loader's documented
     fail-open-with-reason contract), so a downstream pin/expected-id check would catch it.
   - **Rule with no `id`:** a temp file that copies a family but REMOVES one rule's `id`
     yields detectors for the file's OTHER (well-formed) rules but NOT for the id-less one —
     rule-level fail-closed: `_detector_from_rule` never manufactures a detector from a rule
     lacking a usable id. (Assert the id-less rule's would-be detector is absent while its
     siblings load.)
3. Keep a fast presence/freshness guard ONLY if explicitly labeled as such (not the coverage
   claim).

Note: matcher EXECUTION (running opengrep/ast-grep against positive/negative code snippets) is NOT asserted here because it requires the external backend binary, which is not guaranteed in unit CI; this ticket pins the loaded rule CONTRACT (ids/backends/severities) and the fail-closed loader behavior, which are the untested gaps. (Matcher execution is exercised elsewhere where the backend is available.)

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py` — loader-based id/backend/severity assertions + the
  fail-closed malformed-data test.
- `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/builtin/` — reference only (validated, not modified).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For each of the three security families, the test loads it via the production
      `load_registry` and asserts the exact detector ids, their backends, and their severities.
- [ ] A fail-closed test feeds malformed vendored data through `_detectors_from_file`: broken
      YAML yields `([], "parse_error")` (zero detectors + recorded reason); a rule with no `id`
      is ABSENT from the returned detectors while the file's well-formed sibling rules still
      load (a per-rule silent skip — NOT a `parse_drops` entry, which is file-level only).
- [ ] The old substring/presence-only assertion is removed (or explicitly relabeled as a fast
      freshness guard, distinct from the coverage claim).
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Validate vendored security-rule YAML through the production loader with fixtures

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A rebar ticket carries no record of which tracker project it syncs into, nor which repos it belongs to. The current ticket state fields are seeded in `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:29-81` and declared in `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`; neither includes a project. Today the project is only implicit — recoverable from a bound issue's key prefix in `bindings.json`, and absent entirely for a ticket that has never been bound. Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` needs it explicit, because a ticket that is deliberately not synced has no binding to infer from.

## Approach

Add two ticket state fields together, in one edit set: `bridge_project` (string) and `repos` (list of strings). They are one story rather than two because a field is not usable without its write path, and splitting them would put two children on `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`.

`bridge_project` is **tri-state**, mirroring the established `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths pattern (`docs/ticket-model.md:210-212`): absent means legacy, an explicit empty string means never sync, and a key means sync there. The three states are distinguished so a pre-feature store is not read as "every ticket is unsynced". Resolution of the absent state is not implemented here — it belongs to `resolve_project` in the mapping module.

Both fields are written into the CREATE event data by `create_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:169-220`), projected by the reducer, and seeded in `make_initial_state`. Create-time arguments `--bridge-project` and `--repos` are added to all three write surfaces — CLI (`composer.create_cli`), library (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:79-135`), and MCP (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:47-70`). Note the CLI flag loop rejects unknown options strictly (`composer.py:287-291`), so the new flags must be registered there or they are hard errors.

`bridge_project` is **promote-only**: setting it on a ticket with no binding is allowed, changing it on a ticket that already holds one is refused. That keeps the change free of any issue-move or unbind/rebind machinery. `repos` stays freely editable — it never reaches the tracker, so there is no binding to invalidate.

No schema version bump: `docs/event-schema.md:124-150` states additive fields on an existing event type do not require one. Types are generated from the schemas (`reducer/_state.py:11-13`), so the generator is re-run.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard: a producer/consumer contract test for the event→state path (real CREATE event fed through the real reducer, no stubbing), plus a real CLI subprocess test for the argument parsing, since the strict unknown-option rejection is itself part of the mechanism.

- Happy path: `create task "t" --bridge-project REB --repos rebar,api` produces a ticket whose state
  shows `bridge_project == "REB"` and `repos == ["rebar", "api"]` after a full replay.
- Three-state coverage: a ticket created without the flag replays with the field **absent**; one
  created with an explicit empty value replays with `""`. These must be distinguishable — asserting
  the absent case is not merely falsy is the point of the test.
- Cross-surface parity: the same ticket shape results from the CLI, the library, and MCP.
- Failure path: an edit setting `bridge_project` on a ticket that already holds a binding is refused
  with a non-zero exit and the stored value is unchanged; the same edit on an unbound ticket succeeds.
- Collateral invariant: replaying a ticket created before this change yields identical state apart
  from the two new keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge_project` and `repos` are declared in the ticket state schema, seeded in
      `make_initial_state`, and projected by the reducer; checked by a replay test asserting both on
      a freshly created ticket.
- [ ] `--bridge-project` and `--repos` exist on the CLI, library and MCP create paths and produce
      identical state; checked by a per-surface test comparing the resulting ticket state.
- [ ] The absent, explicit-empty, and set states are distinguishable after replay; checked by a
      parameterized test asserting each of the three separately.
- [ ] Setting `bridge_project` on a bound ticket is refused while setting it on an unbound ticket
      succeeds; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] A ticket created before this change replays to the same state apart from the new keys; checked
      by a fixture-based regression test.
baseline.summary: Ticket fields: tri-state bridge_project and repos, with create-time arguments on all three write surfaces

## Context / Problem

Only two subprocess-heavy interface regressions are duplicated: `test_blame_autoderives_single_culprit` and `test_ambiguous_blame_draws_no_autolink` at `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py:66-118` and `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive_heldout.py:58-117`. This is hardening work, not a production-defect fix: keeping both copies increases CI time and makes later contract changes require parallel edits.

The held-out module is not wholesale duplicate code. It must retain `test_library_facade_threads_caused_by` at lines 45-55, which covers the Python facade's `caused_by` forwarding, and `test_user_guide_has_blame_hunt_advisory` at lines 120-130. The canonical module likewise retains its separate CLI explicit-`--caused-by` test at lines 37-57.

## Approach

Keep the canonical two auto-derivation regressions as the sole coverage of their single-culprit and ambiguous-blame behaviors. Delete only their held-out copies. Retain the two held-out boundary tests and the canonical explicit-flag test unchanged. Then remove only imports and private helpers made unreachable by deleting the duplicated held-out tests; do not parameterize across the facade, CLI-explicit, or documentation boundaries.

## Scope

- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py` — canonical duplicate coverage remains unchanged
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive_heldout.py` — remove only the two duplicate test bodies and any now-unreachable test helpers/imports

## Testing

Collect and run both modules before and after the change. Verify one collected instance each of the single-culprit and ambiguous-blame test names, plus the retained facade, explicit-flag, and user-guide-advisory tests. Run the focused interface suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `test_blame_autoderives_single_culprit` and `test_ambiguous_blame_draws_no_autolink` remain in the canonical module and are removed only from the held-out module. Verified: canonical module has both at lines 69/96; heldout module's `grep ^def test_` shows neither present.
- [x] The held-out module retains `test_library_facade_threads_caused_by` and `test_user_guide_has_blame_hunt_advisory`; the canonical module retains `test_explicit_caused_by_on_bug_close`. Verified: all three present at their expected locations.
- [x] Any held-out imports or private helpers that become unreachable after those two removals are deleted, with no remaining test referencing them. Verified during implementation; heldout module retains only what its 2 remaining tests need.
- [x] Focused collection reports exactly one instance of each auto-derivation regression and reports all three distinct boundary tests. Verified: `pytest --collect-only` on both modules together reports exactly 5 tests, one instance each.
- [x] Both lifecycle test modules and the focused interface suite pass. Verified: both modules pass directly; full `tests/interfaces` suite (2313 tests) passes excluding 3 files with pre-existing environmental failures confirmed unrelated to this change (reproduced on a clean origin/main checkout). Committed b53677968c4e714fa20a0da7bf4b9a2728af0b24, pushed as Gerrit change 2538 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).

baseline.description:
## Why
rebar's mutating verbs follow the Unix rule of silence: `link`, `unlink`, `comment`, `tag`, `edit`, `set-file-impact` exit 0 with empty stdout on success. Observed cost (2026-08-14, bug clubby-circular-halicore): success and silent idempotent no-op are indistinguishable on stdout, so agents run a second `rebar show` per mutation to verify their own write; one agent misread silent success as failure, filed a spurious bug, and retried. Modern CLI practice (clig.dev; kubectl/git/gh/terraform) confirms every state change on stdout; the confirmation belongs in the mutation's own output.

## Scope
- **IN**: `_WRITES_FULL` (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:125) + `_LIFECYCLE` (:114). Verbs that already print — `create`, `idea`, `revert`, `claim`, `session-log`, `transition` (emits `UNBLOCKED: ...` transition.py:628, `Reverted event ...` :463, though not the from->to itself) — are NORMALIZED to the same message contract (operator-approved 2026-08-14): the line keeps every datum it prints today (ids/aliases are consumed by scripts — no information loss) restated in the step-1 style, e.g. `created <alias> (<id>)`, `claimed <alias>: open -> in_progress (assignee <who>)`, Old->new mappings documented in the change + regenerated cli-reference.
- **OUT**: MCP tools (outputSchemas already confirm), doctor/fsck/compact/bridge/tracker-maintenance (own reporting), config-key equivalent of --quiet.

## Plan
1. **Uniform message contract.** Success: one stdout line `<past-tense-verb> <args-summary>` built only from CLI args + the seam's outcome (no follow-up store read): `linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`, `unlinked <src> -/-> <target> (<relation>)`, `comment added to <alias>`, `tagged <alias>: +<tag>`, `untagged <alias>: -<tag>`, `edited <alias>: <field-names>` (comma-joined names of fields the invocation set, e.g. `edited x: description, priority` — names only, never values), `impact set on <alias>: <n> paths`, `archived <alias>`, `verify-commands set on <alias>: <n>`, `commits attached to <alias>: <n>`, `reopened <alias>: closed -> open`. transition's normalized line is `transitioned <alias>: <from> -> <to>; unblocked: <ids|none>` — the UNBLOCKED datum is preserved inside the line, not dropped. No-op (where the seam reports one): `no change: <specific reason>` — e.g. `no change: already linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`, `no change: tag <tag> already on <alias>`. Exit 0 both ways.
2. **Per-verb outcome signal, existing contracts preserved.** Confirm each core seam's ACTUAL return contract before touching it (Serena + string grep), then extend compatibly:
   - Seams returning `None` with no consumers gain a small outcome return (wrote/noop + detail).
   - Seams whose return IS consumed — e.g. `add_dependency` returns `dict | None` (REDIRECT record), propagated by `link_core` and consumed by the MCP/library facade — are NOT changed; the CLI derives the confirmation from what the seam exposes, adding a parallel channel only if the existing signal cannot distinguish wrote-vs-noop, never altering the consumed value's type or meaning.
   - Verbs with no idempotent no-op path (e.g. `comment` always writes) get success lines only; an inventory table in the change classifies each verb.
3. **Global output flags pre-extracted at the top-level router** (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py) BEFORE any partition dispatch — required because the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaf verbs (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands — `_REGISTRY` is defined in src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:41, dispatched from the `_cli/__init__.py` router) treat any option-looking token as a usage error and never call parse_output. Pre-extraction strips BOTH global flags from argv once, uniformly for every verb (operator-approved 2026-08-14):
   - `--quiet`/`-q`: suppresses confirmation lines only; errors/exit codes untouched.
   - `--output <mode>`/`-o <mode>`: PROMOTED from per-verb parse_output handling to the same top-level extraction, so every in-scope verb (including `_REGISTRY` leaves) gains `--output json`. Verbs already accepting it keep identical behavior (same modes, same JSON shapes); newly-covered verbs emit ONE uniform mutation envelope — {"outcome": "<verb-past>"|"noop", "subject": <alias/edge>, "detail": <str>} (kubectl-Status-style; bespoke per-verb schemas are deliberately NOT designed here) — documented as pre-1.0-unstable in cli-reference. `--quiet` + `--output json` together: JSON still prints (quiet governs the text confirmation channel only).
   Extraction is position-independent but never consumes tokens after `--` or verb-argument values (tested: a comment body containing "--quiet" is preserved).
4. **Channel discipline:** confirmations print only in text mode. Under `--output json` stdout is exclusively the JSON document; the outcome rides as a structured field.
5. **REDIRECT reconciliation:** `link` already prints a machine-readable redirect record as raw JSON to stdout on write and no-op paths (`_emit_redirect`, src/rebar/graph/_links.py:220 — an existing CLI contract), PRESERVED byte-identical; when a redirect record is printed in text mode, no additional text confirmation line is added on top (one result on stdout per invocation, no mixed text+JSON). The record is MACHINE DATA, not a confirmation line: `--quiet` never suppresses it (quiet governs only the step-1 text lines), so `link --quiet` on a redirect path still emits the record byte-identical. Under --output json the record nests as an envelope field; golden tests pin both paths.
6. **stdout/stderr split:** confirmations to stdout (the command's result); warnings/logs stay on stderr. Exit codes unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Every verb in `_WRITES_FULL` + `_LIFECYCLE` that is silent today prints the step-1 success line on a successful write (edit's line lists exactly the field names passed on that invocation, no values); per-verb tests assert the exact line and that no additional store read/reduce builds it (call-count or monkeypatch assertion on the reduce path).
- [x] Every verb whose seam reports an idempotent no-op prints the `no change: ...` form, exits 0, writes no event (store-event count asserted); the change includes the inventory table classifying each verb (no-op-capable vs always-writes), and re-link of an identical active edge is among the tested no-ops.
- [x] Already-printing verbs (create, idea, revert, claim, session-log, transition) are normalized to the shared contract with zero information loss: for each, a test asserts the new line contains every datum the old line carried, and the change description lists each old->new mapping. reopen (silent today) gains a step-1 line.

## Context / Problem
119 `*/.archived` and 126 `*/.write.lock` files are tracked in the tickets branch HEAD — committed before `.gitignore` gained the `*/.archived` and `*/.write.lock` patterns (both present in the tracker's .gitignore today; verified by `git check-ignore`). gitignore never un-tracks already-tracked files, so routine marker churn (archive/unarchive, compaction retiring markers) surfaces as tracked working-tree deletions: it dirties `git status`, breaks the strict head check in rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py::tracker_head_sha (every plan-review/close attestation fails with store-read-failure), and feeds reconverge merge-abort variant (b) (see parent epic and bug e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73). Both markers are derived local caches: archival's source of truth is ARCHIVED events (reducer/_api.py already filters archived tickets out of compiled state at the end of its list path, and clears stale markers), and `.write.lock` is a transient fcntl handle target (reducer/marker.py).

## Approach
Add one new ensure unit to the idempotent ensure-registry (rebar._store.ensures.REGISTRY_IDS + implementation in rebar._commands.init, the established pattern for store-config convergence — the registry runs all units under the store write lock and a converged store makes zero commits). Unit `untrack-runtime-markers`: check = `git ls-files -- '*/.archived' '*/.write.lock'` empty (cheap, one git call); act = `git rm --cached --quiet` those paths in batches + one commit through the store seam. Worktree copies are untouched, so local cache behavior is unchanged on the machine that runs it. Peers merging the untrack commit have git delete their worktree marker copies (tracked-unmodified files follow the tree deletion) — that is safe for correctness because listing excludes archived tickets from compiled state, and the marker is only a fast-path; to restore the fast-path, make the reader self-heal: in reducer/_api.py's list path, when a reduced ticket's compiled state says archived but the `.archived` marker file is absent, re-materialize it via reducer.marker.write_marker (mirror of the existing stale-marker clearing in the same function). Riskiest assumption tested first: that `git rm --cached` + commit on the tickets branch merges cleanly into a peer whose worktree still has the files — covered by the first unit test (fixture with two clones) before wiring the ensure unit into the registry.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_store/ensures.py — add `untrack-runtime-markers` to REGISTRY_IDS and the registry map.
- src/rebar/_commands/init.py — the unit implementation (check-then-act, batched `git rm --cached`, one commit).
- src/rebar/reducer/_api.py — re-materialize a missing `.archived` marker when compiled state is archived (self-healing cache; mirrors the existing stale-marker clear).
- tests/unit/test_ensures_untrack_markers.py (new) — unit + two-clone merge test.
- docs/migrations.md — one paragraph documenting the unit.

## Testing
- Happy path: fixture tracker with tracked `*/.archived` + `*/.write.lock`; run the ensure; assert `git ls-files` empty, worktree files still present, exactly one commit made, second run makes zero commits (idempotent).
- Peer path: second clone merges the untrack commit; assert its worktree markers are deleted by the merge, `git status` clean, and a subsequent list re-materializes `.archived` for net-archived tickets while excluding them from default output.
- Edge: store with nothing tracked (fresh init) — unit reports ok, zero commits; a ticket dir with marker but no ARCHIVED event — marker cleared (existing behavior preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] After `run_ensures` on a store seeded with tracked markers, `git ls-files -- '*/.archived' '*/.write.lock'` is empty and re-running makes zero commits; checked by the new unit test.
- [x] Deleting or creating a marker in the worktree no longer appears in `git status --porcelain`; checked in the same test after the unit runs.
- [x] A net-archived ticket with a missing marker is excluded from default `list` output AND its marker is re-created by that list call; checked by the peer-path test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
baseline.summary: Untrack per-ticket runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) from the tickets branch via an ensure unit; reader self-heals the marker cache

## Summary (RESOLVED — see resolution note)

SITE: `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` `run_sweep(tracker)` — the detached-child compaction entry point formerly composed its config root as `repo_root = os.path.dirname(tracker)`, sanctioned `# repo-root-ok:` in the config-root guard (`scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py`) as the ONE deferred CONFIG-ROOT site of the auspicial-friended-merganser class.

CONTEXT: split off from auspicial-friended-merganser (2ec7-be89-9b01-496a), which fixed the 8 clean `dirname(tracker)`-as-config-root sites. `run_sweep` is spawned with cwd == the canonical STORE and inherits only `tracker`; auspicial DEFERRED this site because the detached child needs a DURABLE code root.

IMPACT (milder than the parent's AC#1): on a relocated store (`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` — the deployed MCP topology, store `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, code `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`) `run_sweep` read DEFAULT compaction config (threshold 10, 1800 s horizon) instead of the project's `[compact]` block — folding the right tickets by the WRONG rule. No gate was disabled.

## RESOLUTION — fixed on origin/main by Gerrit 2344 (`c68cc1de3185`)

This bug is FIXED and MERGED. `c68cc1de3185` ("Resolve the sweep's code root, not compose it", Gerrit 2344, carrying `rebar-ticket: 6bf1-326b-7404-4034`) merged with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` and is an ancestor of current `origin/main`.

The landed fix calls the bare `config.repo_root_or_none()` in the child (`compact_trigger.py` `run_sweep`, `repo_root = _cfg.repo_root_or_none()`), and removes the `# repo-root-ok:` sanction. One resolver covers BOTH supported topologies:

- **Deployment** (relocated store): `REBAR_ROOT` is exported unconditionally and names the provisioned checkout `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`, so the `REBAR_ROOT` arm resolves the real code root.
- **Local `make worktree`** (co-located store): the git-toplevel arm reads a cwd that `_proc.detached_child_cwd` has already anchored at the canonical store's parent — the durable main checkout, not the ephemeral worktree. `None` (nothing resolved) passes through as the discover sentinel.

This design has a strictly WIDER correctness envelope than the alternative `dirname(canonical tracker)` fallback once considered here: it is correct when EITHER `REBAR_ROOT` is set OR the cwd is inside the checkout, whereas `dirname(canonical tracker)` regresses the relocated-store + `REBAR_ROOT`-unset + cwd-in-checkout case back to the original bug (measured; see ticket comments). Rejected alternatives in the landed change: threading the resolved root through the spawn contract (re-runs the durability class of bugs 3198/93a9), and `snapshot_repo_root()` (snapshot-only `"."` fallback).

## Acceptance Criteria (met by Gerrit 2344 / `c68cc1de3185`)

- [x] AC#1 — `run_sweep` resolves the code/config root independent of store location, via `config.repo_root_or_none()`, with no spawn-contract change and no new parameter.
- [x] AC#2 — On a relocated store with a non-default `[compact]` block, `run_sweep` honours it (RED->GREEN), AND the root it hands `compact_all_cli` IS the resolved code root, pinned at the seam. Config driven by a `rebar.toml` FILE, not env.
- [x] AC#3 — The `# repo-root-ok:` sanction is removed, leaving the guard allowlist with ZERO deferred config-root sites (only `_store/sync.py`'s store-repo ref reads remain). `python scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` exits 0.
- [x] AC#4 — Both precedence arms are exercised, including a test that unsets `REBAR_ROOT` so the git-toplevel arm is covered, not just the deployed arm.
- [x] AC#5 — A config-effect contrast: the same store/ticket fold NOTHING under a `[compact]` block whose horizon holds the events back, with a LIVENESS check on the sweep's return code (`run_sweep` swallows exceptions, so an absent snapshot would otherwise be satisfied by a crash).
- [x] AC#6 — Caused-by attribution: same origin class as the parent (`dirname(tracker)`-as-config-root construct), written by `d2dea317ec94` (rebar-ticket `1fde-becd-942a-4351`), recorded as a `caused_by` link.

## Testing (as landed in Gerrit 2344)

The merged change carries the `run_sweep` fold + seam tests, the `REBAR_ROOT`-unset arm test, the folds-nothing + liveness contrast, and the guard self-test asserting no deferred config-root site; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the module-size gate and the complexity ratchet stay clean.

Note: an earlier revision of this description (during a parallel remediation attempt) mandated a `compaction_child_repo_root` resolver; that approach was abandoned (Gerrit 2352, ABANDONED) because it would have reverted the strictly-better merged fix. See ticket comments for the full trail.
baseline.summary: run_sweep detached child derives repo_root from os.path.dirname(tracker), ignoring relocated-store config

# The issuelinks snapshot-enrichment merge is inline, so its guard test hand-mirrors it and will drift

## The problem

`fetcher.py:592-596` merges `client.get_issuelinks_map()` into the snapshot inline inside `fetch_snapshot`. There is no named, directly-callable helper, so a unit test cannot exercise the real merge without standing up a whole fetcher.

Change 1276 (bug `2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9`) therefore had to reproduce it as `_enrich_like_fetcher`, a byte-faithful HAND COPY that quotes the original. Its implementing agent flagged this itself as the weakest link in the change, and it is right to be worried:

**What that copy guards is not cosmetic.** 2b16's guard **G1** decides whether an inbound link REMOVAL may fire, by distinguishing "the peer was queried and has no links" (`"issuelinks"` key PRESENT, possibly an empty list) from "we never observed this issue's links" (key ABSENT — enrichment failed, HTTP 410, a fail-open partial map, or the issue fell outside a truncated page). If the production merge ever changes so that key-presence stops meaning "observed", **G1 silently stops protecting and the removal path starts deleting local deps from truncated reads** — while the hand copy keeps the test green.

This epic has already fixed THREE silent-truncation defects in this exact data path (change 1105; `9263-b404-cb6c-463f`; `deac-4f5a-856a-49bd`, measured losing 92% of a snapshot). Turning those READ bugs into a WRITE bug is the worst outcome available here, and a drifting test copy is precisely how it would happen without anyone noticing.

## Note on scope

Bug `88d9-fe42-e50f-4067` carries an acceptance criterion to extract the sibling **parent** enrichment merge for the same reason, so the pattern will already exist when this is picked up — this ticket is the **issuelinks** half. Do them the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the issuelinks enrichment merge is a named, directly-callable helper, and `fetch_snapshot` calls it
      rather than inlining it — behaviour-preserving, pinned by a characterization assertion taken BEFORE
      the extraction
- [x] 2b16's `_enrich_like_fetcher` hand copy is DELETED and its test drives the real helper
- [x] a test asserts the property G1 depends on: an issue observed with zero links yields the
      `"issuelinks"` key PRESENT (empty list), and an issue the map never mentioned yields the key ABSENT
- [x] mutation-checked: changing the merge so an unobserved issue gains an empty `issuelinks` list must
      turn a test RED, because that is the exact drift that would disarm G1
baseline.summary: Extract the issuelinks snapshot-enrichment merge so 2b16's G1 guard test stops hand-mirroring it
