# Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

## Context / Problem

CMS and similar federal clients run **self-hosted Jira Data Center**, which rebar cannot reconcile against. DC differs from Cloud on three axes: REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies instead of v3 + ADF, Personal Access Token bearer auth instead of the ACLI subprocess, and name-based user identity instead of `accountId`.

GitHub PR #120 proposed a second adapter package for this. It rides ADR 0035's `Backend` port correctly, but it reaches into `adapters/jira/` privates (`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, `_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `classify_probe_response`) and forks `map_fields_to_remote` as a verbatim copy of `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` with one line changed. That creates a de facto "Jira family" layer with no contract: `adapters/jira/` becomes simultaneously a concrete backend and a shared library, with nothing pinning what is shared and nothing stopping a Cloud change from breaking DC.

## Approach

Make the Jira family an **explicit sub-seam** rather than an accident, in an order that never puts the live-validated Cloud path at risk.

1. **Freeze Cloud first.** Extend the existing held-out characterization tests
   (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`) to pin the current outputs of every unit
   about to move, so any behavior change during extraction fails a pinned oracle.
2. **Extract a `adapters/jira_family/` shared layer** — and re-point the Cloud adapter at it. Cloud's ACLI
   transport is not touched at all.

   **Only non-location-pinned symbols may physically move.** ADR 0035 §(a) pins `adf.py`,
   `outbound_fields.py`, and `comment_limits.py` as **Jira-coupled *and* location-pinned**: they are loaded by
   filename relative to `_PACKAGE_DIR` (via `_loader.lazy_load(` / `_load_sibling_keyed(` /
   `spec_from_file_location(`), so physically moving them breaks the dynamic loader unless the loader is taught
   the new sub-package in the same change — deferred to ADR 0035's Phase 2, explicitly **out of scope here**.
   **Location-pinned means "cannot change path" — NOT "cannot be edited."** Editing a pinned module's
   *contents* (e.g. replacing a dict literal with an import) is safe and is how the pinned units get
   single-sourced; only *relocating* the file breaks the loader.

   **Move by SYMBOL, not by file.** `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` cannot relocate wholesale: it imports
   `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from the pinned `adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
   `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from the pinned `comment_limits.py` (used by
   `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the whole file would point `jira_family/` at `adapters/jira/` — the exact
   dependency inversion the import contract in §6 forbids. So the file is split by symbol, and the two coupled
   sanitizers are **parameterized by the contracts this epic already introduces** rather than importing a
   vendor module: `_sanitize_description` takes the `RichTextCodec` (its `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the
   rich-text seam), and comment truncation takes the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract. Cloud
   constructs those contract objects in `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC
   constructs wiki-markup/plain-text equivalents. `jira_family/` imports neither.

   Concretely, of the six symbols PR #120 reached for:
   - **Movable to `jira_family/` in this epic:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
     and `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` (all in `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`, not location-pinned and not
     ADF/limit-coupled), `classify_probe_response` (`adapters/jira/probe.py`, not location-pinned), and the new
     `RichTextCodec` / `UserIdentityModel` contract objects.
   - **Moves to `jira_family/` only in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and
     `_sanitize_comment` — same observable behavior, but the ADF/limit dependency arrives as an injected
     contract instead of a direct import of a pinned module.

   - **Stays put (path-wise):** `_map_local_to_jira_fields` in the pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`,
     and the ADF encoder in the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. These are shared **by dependency-inverting
     instead of moving**: the pinned module is parameterized by the `jira_family` contracts (it imports *from*
     `jira_family/`, never the reverse), so DC reuses one implementation without any file relocating and
     without the loader changing. Any story that would *move* a pinned file must instead stop and record the
     blocker.

   One more unit needs parameterizing rather than sharing verbatim: `classify_probe_response` hardcodes
   `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})`. Those are Cloud/DIG workflow state
   names; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything. So the classifier moves to
   `jira_family/` taking the resolved-status set **as a parameter**, with Cloud passing today's frozenset
   (pinned unchanged by J1's oracle) and DC passing its own configured set. Sharing it with the Cloud names
   baked in would silently misclassify a DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED` when it is in fact resolved.
   The DC set is **operator-configured** via a `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config key (a list of workflow
   state names), defaulting to the same `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset so an operator whose workflow
   uses the conventional names configures nothing. Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not
   made configurable by this change.

   **The value maps are a special case — they are ALREADY duplicated, and this epic must not preserve the
   duplication.** There are today **three** independently-referenced copies of the local→Jira status map (and
   two of the priority map):
   - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the
     ACLI transport (`acli.py:69-70,143,171`; `acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354`).
   - `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (pinned): `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by
     the `Backend` port via `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
   - `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`: `local_to_jira_status` — the engine-level config copy.

   They have **already drifted**: `outbound_fields` and `config.py` both carry a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the
   `jira_fields` copy lacks. So simply moving the `jira_fields` copy to `jira_family/` would leave Cloud's
   backend still reading a second copy — the exact "two places" the epic exists to eliminate. This epic
   consolidates the two `adapters/` copies; `config.py`'s is folded in by bug `fe15` (its call sites are
   engine-level config, a wider blast radius than this epic's seam).

   **Resolution: `adapters/jira_family/` holds the ONE definition of each value map. Both current copies are
   deleted and replaced by imports from it** — `jira_fields.py` (whose map literals move out, the file itself
   staying put for its ADF/limit-coupled sanitizers) and `outbound_fields.py` (pinned, so it stays at its path
   but its dict literals become an import). After this,
   grep finds exactly one dict literal per map, reachable from the ACLI transport, the Cloud backend port, and
   the DC backend alike.

   The `deleted`-key drift **must be decided in J2**, because a single unified dict cannot preserve two
   callers that currently disagree. J2 adopts `"deleted": "Done"` — the value **two of the three** existing
   copies already use (`outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status`).
   The ACLI-side omission produces `"Deleted"` via a `.title()` fallback, which is not a state in the live DIG
   workflow, so Jira would reject that transition: a latent bug, not behavior to preserve. This is the one
   declared observable change in an otherwise behavior-preserving extraction, pinned by its own test. Bug
   `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) keeps the remainder: the missing ACLI-side
   characterization pins and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.
3. **Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts**: a `RichTextCodec` (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for
   DC) and a `UserIdentityModel` (`accountId` for Cloud, `name` for DC). Cloud is parameterized by its existing
   behavior; DC is a different configuration, not a fork.
4. **DC transport builds on the maintained `pycontribs/jira` library**, gated behind a `[jira-datacenter]`
   extra and imported lazily, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract and the battle-tested Cloud path are
   both untouched.
5. **Verify against a real Jira.** Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026, so the oracle
   is a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK at `localhost:2990` — the same approach pycontribs/jira itself
   uses in its `tests/conftest.py`.
6. **Keep the new boundary structurally enforced, not conventional.** The drift this epic exists to prevent can
   recur the moment a contributor adds Cloud-specific logic to the shared layer. So the seam ships with a
   machine-checked import contract (an `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml`, or an equivalent CI grep
   check): only `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` may import `adapters/jira_family/`, and
   `jira_family/` may import neither of them.
7. **Security posture for the DC connection.** Self-hosted DC is frequently served over plain HTTP inside
   corporate networks, which would put ticket bodies and the PAT on the wire in cleartext. The DC backend
   therefore **requires `https`** for `reconciler.base_url` and rejects a non-TLS URL unless an explicit
   `allow_insecure = true` override is set (which logs a warning). Operator docs state the least-privilege
   expectation: a **dedicated service account** whose PAT is scoped to only the projects rebar reconciles
   (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments / Link Issues on those projects), never an
   admin-level token.

   **Certificate verification stays ON.** Self-hosted DC commonly presents a self-signed or internal-CA
   certificate, and the tempting fix — disabling verification — turns the `https` requirement into theatre. So
   the DC transport never sets `verify=False`: an operator with an internal CA points rebar at their CA bundle
   (a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client), and
   a verification failure surfaces as a clear error naming the CA-bundle setting rather than being silently
   downgraded. `allow_insecure` governs the URL *scheme* only; it does NOT relax certificate checking.

   **The J5 harness is the intended `allow_insecure` case, not an exception to it.** The Dockerized Jira serves
   plain `http://localhost:2990/jira`, so every live test against it sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and
   asserts the warning is emitted. That is deliberate: it means the loopback-only test path exercises the
   override rather than bypassing the validator, and the validator's reject-by-default branch is covered by a
   unit test with a non-loopback `http://` URL. The override is **not** narrowed to loopback — an operator on a
   private network is a real use case — but the warning text names the cleartext risk.

**Provenance decision.** DC and Cloud share the single `jira` creation channel, `jira-` local-id prefix, and `jira_key` binding; deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this. They are the same vendor. Generalizing the store vocabulary is epic `be74`'s work, where a genuinely different vendor (GitHub) makes it necessary; doing it here would mean a store migration for no user-visible benefit.

**Alternative rejected: PR #120's separate adapter package.** Two copies of the field maps and sanitizers drift, and cross-adapter private imports are a dependency direction ADR 0035 never sanctioned.

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib REST client.** PR #120's client is competent, but pycontribs/jira already absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks that thousands of users have found. Confining it to an opt-in extra keeps the cost off every rebar install.

**Alternative rejected: `atlassian-python-api`.** It was surveyed in ADR 0004 and does support DC with PAT auth, but `pycontribs/jira` is the better fit here for two reasons: it ships the Dockerized-Jira-SDK test harness pattern this epic adopts as its verification oracle (its own `tests/conftest.py`), and its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object. Either would work; picking one and confining it to an opt-in extra is what matters.

**Alternative rejected: generalizing `jira_key` / the `jira-` prefix / the channel vocabulary now.** That is epic `be74`'s spine and touches 50+ binding-store sites; pulling it forward delays the CMS delivery for no behavioral gain.

**Alternative rejected: moving the location-pinned modules now.** Relocating `outbound_fields.py` / `adf.py` into `jira_family/` would be the tidier file layout, but it requires teaching the dynamic loader the new sub-package and re-targeting every `mock.patch("rebar_reconciler.<mod>.<attr>")` site in the suite (ADR 0035 §(a)–(b)). That is ADR 0035's Phase 2; doing it here would couple a live-Cloud-risking refactor to a delivery epic for no DC-visible benefit. Dependency inversion gets the same single-implementation guarantee at a fraction of the risk.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new), `adapters/jira/`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (new).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen `reconciler.backend` (**owned by J7**), add the TLS/`allow_insecure`
  validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (**owned by J6**). Split deliberately: J6 lands the
  DC connection settings with the transport that consumes them; J7 lands the backend-choice widening with the
  assembly that makes the choice valid.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra, and the import contract.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`, `test_backend_contract.py`.
- A new ADR amending ADR 0035.
- **Out of scope:** relocating any location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`,
  `comment_limits.py`) or touching `_loader.py` — ADR 0035 Phase 2 owns that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit
- [ ] `test_backend_contract.py`'s backend fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes for it
- [ ] an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon
- [ ] [operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at
      `localhost:2990`, selected by `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` with `reconciler.base_url`
      pointing at that instance: at least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound
      pass, and one local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions
      in the reconcile log
- [ ] No mapping logic exists in two places: the field/value maps, the label sanitizer, the link-relation
      vocabulary, the probe classifier, the rich-text codec, and the user-identity model each have exactly one
      implementation reachable by both backends — `adapters/jira_datacenter/` defines none of its own and
      imports each from `adapters/jira_family/` (or, for the location-pinned modules, consumes the pinned
      module parameterized by a `jira_family` contract). Enforced by the machine-checked import contract, which
      fails CI on a violation
- [ ] The Cloud adapter's observable behavior is unchanged: characterization oracles pinning every unit that
      moves or is re-pointed were committed **before** the extraction change was pushed for review (the oracle
      change's Gerrit number recorded on the extraction story), and the full oracle set passes against the
      post-extraction Cloud adapter
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` is exercised by the backend-agnostic contract suite, not only by adapter-local tests.
- [ ] Installing rebar without the `[jira-datacenter]` extra pulls in no new dependency — `pip install
      nava-rebar` then `pip list` shows no `jira` package and `import rebar` still works — **and the existing
      clean-core CI check enforces it**: `jira` is added to the absent-module list in
      `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` (today it checks only `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`,
      `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`, so without this the guarantee has no CI teeth).
- [ ] No location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `comment_limits.py`) changed path, and
      `_loader.py` is untouched — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main` on the landed stack (their
      *contents* may change to import from `jira_family/`; only a rename is forbidden)
- [ ] Exactly one dict literal defines the local→Jira status map and one the priority map **within
      `adapters/`** — the pre-existing `jira_fields` / `outbound_fields` duplicate pair is gone, and the ACLI
      transport, the Cloud backend port, and the DC backend all read the single `jira_family` definition
      (verified by grep for the map literals under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/`).
      `rebar_reconciler/config.py`'s third copy is the ONE knowingly-remaining literal outside `adapters/`,
      deferred to bug `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` because its call sites are engine-level config with a wider blast
      radius than this seam — so the grep is scoped to `adapters/`, not the whole engine
- [ ] The DC backend rejects a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` unless `allow_insecure = true` is set, warns
      when the override is used, and never disables TLS certificate verification
- [ ] The operator docs state the least-privilege service-account/PAT scope and how to point rebar at an
      internal CA bundle
baseline.summary: Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

baseline.description:
## Context

The Jira reconciler coordinates concurrent passes across clones (local + the GitHub-Actions
reconcile bridge) with a **pass-lock** and a **phase-gate**. Today both are **working-tree files
committed to the shared `tickets` orphan branch**: `.reconciler-pass-lock` and
`.reconciler-phase-gate` (`_advisory_lock.py:69-70`), written by `acquire_pass_lock`
(`_advisory_lock.py:243`), released by `release_pass_lock` (`:302`), orchestrated in
`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:373-447`. The body is `pass_id\ntimestamp_ns`.

Two problems with a tree-committed lock:

1. **It rides the `merge=ours` band-aid.** `.reconciler-*` is matched by the `merge=ours` driver
   in the tickets-branch `.gitattributes` (`_commands/init.py:57`; `.bridge_state/*` is line 56).
   Two clones that touch the lock on diverged histories reconverge by silently keeping one side.
2. **No self-healing.** No lease/heartbeat/steal. A pass that **crashes while holding the lock**
   leaves a stale file that clears only on the next clean run. The current mitigation is the
   `b859-8fa1` **retry band-aid** (`_advisory_lock.py:73-89, 263-291`).

**Recent ground truth.** `feat/reconcile-continuous-loop` is **merged to main** (flag-gated on the
`RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` GitHub Variable, default off) and explicitly relies on "concurrency + the
reconciler pass-lock" to prevent overlapping passes — it is the contention amplifier this epic
hardens against.

This epic is the **WS-2 (coordination) half** of the former "conflict-free reconciler state" epic;
WS-1 (event-sourcing the binding *data*) was dropped because the closed epic *Level-triggered
bridge convergence* (`3006-e198-13db-4e1f`, ADRs 0026-0029 + the `8de5` classifier/canary) already
made binding drift detected and self-healing and `bindings.json` is a derived cache.

**Framed as an EFFICIENCY lock, not a correctness lock.** Reconcile passes are idempotent; the
lock avoids wasted overlapping work. A rare double-acquire degrades to two idempotent passes
(tolerated by the `3006` `classify()` matrix + acting-fraction breaker), never to corruption.

## Design (WS-2 — self-healing ref-lock)

- Move pass-lock and phase-gate OFF the working tree into **bare git refs** `refs/reconciler/lock`
  and `refs/reconciler/gate` (ref -> blob), so they are never in the tickets tree, never
  union-merged, never subject to `merge=ours`. Authoritative on `origin` (the `sync.remote`).
- **Blob = newline-terminated UTF-8 JSON** `{holder, lease_secs, heartbeat_ns, fence}`. Decode of
  a corrupt/partial blob **fails closed** (a contender that cannot parse treats the lock as HELD,
  never free). Clock source is plain `time.time_ns()` — **not** `rebar._store.hlc` (that fcntl
  cache is for ticket-event ordering, the wrong tool for a lease).
- **Blob creation:** `git hash-object -w --stdin` to plant the blob, then a **CAS** on the ref:
  `git update-ref <ref> <new-oid> <old>` (acquire old = 40 zeros = create-only; release/steal old =
  the exact observed oid). Reuse the existing CAS retry helper `_cas_advance_with_retry`
  (`_advisory_lock.py:447-487`); its discriminator `_is_cas_mismatch` (`:415`, line 425) hard-codes
  `refs/heads/tickets` and must be generalized to accept the ref name.
- **Relative-duration, skew-proof lease (DynamoDB-lock-client pattern):** a contender does NOT
  compare clocks across clones. It records `(observed_oid, fence)`, waits one lease interval on its
  OWN clock, re-reads; if `fence` and oid are unchanged, the holder made no progress for a full
  lease -> dead -> **CAS-break against `observed_oid`**. The CAS guarantees a double-break race
  resolves to **exactly one winner** (the loser observes CAS failure and does NOT also acquire).
  `fence` is the progress witness + fencing token, bumped on every acquire/renew/steal.
- **Lease + heartbeat:** default lease **120 s**, heartbeat every **~lease/3**, both configurable
  via a new `[reconciler]` config key `lock_lease_secs` (which **replaces** the retired
  `lock_max_retries`). Because a pass can run 10-60 min, the holder renews from a **daemon thread**
  started on acquire; a renewal-CAS failure (`LeaseLostError`) sets a `lock_lost`
  `threading.Event` that the pass polls at per-ticket checkpoints and, when set, raises
  `ReconcileLockLost` to abort (idempotent -> safe re-run). Heartbeat git ops touch only
  `refs/reconciler/lock`, disjoint from tickets-branch writes.
- **Phase-gate** uses the **same** blob schema + CAS discipline as the lock (not operator-freeform).
- **Expand-contract cutover:** a `[reconciler] lock_backend = file | ref` switch lets the ref
  backend land alongside the file backend (C3) and the file backend + `merge=ours` + `b859` band-aid
  be removed only after the ref backend is proven (C4) — a clean rollback path.
- **Remote feasibility is load-bearing and unproven:** whether GitHub accepts push/fetch of a
  non-branch `refs/reconciler/*` ref pointing at a **blob** (with the CI `GITHUB_TOKEN`) is verified
  FIRST (C1 AC0); the contingency if it does not is ref -> tiny-commit instead of ref -> blob.

Out of scope: `.ticket-write.lock` (`_store/lock.py`, a local fcntl lock for single-host ticket
writes) — a separate mechanism, not cross-clone pass coordination. And all of WS-1 (binding data).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pass-lock and phase-gate live in `refs/reconciler/*` (bare ref -> blob, not in the working
      tree, not union-merged); acquire is create-only CAS, release/steal is observed-oid CAS
      (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` + `_advisory_lock.py` + `rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`).
- [ ] Blob is UTF-8 JSON `{holder, lease_secs, heartbeat_ns, fence}` (`time.time_ns()` clock);
      corrupt/partial decode fails closed (treated as HELD, never free).
- [ ] Stale-lock self-heal via relative-duration lease (no cross-clone clock compare): a contender
      CAS-breaks only after observing no `fence`/oid progress across one locally-measured lease; a
      double-break race resolves to exactly one winner (regression test). Holder renews at ~lease/3
      from a daemon thread; a lost-lease renewal aborts the pass.
- [ ] `lock_backend = file | ref` switch enables an expand-contract cutover; the ref-lock design +
      rollback path are recorded in a new ADR under `docs/adr/`.
- [ ] `.reconciler-*` removed from the `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` (`_commands/init.py:57`, via a
      migration that also updates already-initialized trackers) and from
      `tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py`; `.bridge_state/*` left intact; no
      `.reconciler-*` file is committed to the tickets branch (regression test).
- [ ] The `b859-8fa1` retry band-aid (`_advisory_lock.py:73-89, 263-291`) and its now-dead helpers
      (`_resolve_retry_budget`, `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, `_compute_backoff_seconds`) + config
      key `lock_max_retries` (`_config_schema.py:334,445`) + env aliases + their tests are removed.
- [ ] Reconcile-pass idempotency asserted by a named double-acquire convergence test; the existing
      ref-CAS primitive is reused (not duplicated). Full non-integration suite green.
- [ ] The reconciler coordinates concurrent passes with **zero coordination state in the tickets
- [ ] The `merge=ours` policy no longer covers any live coordination state (`.bridge_state/*` unchanged).
- [ ] The design + its rollback path are captured in an ADR.
baseline.summary: Self-healing Jira-reconciler pass-lock: move pass-lock/phase-gate off the tickets branch into refs/reconciler/* (retire merge=ours + b859 retry band-aid)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The multi-project model changes things a reader currently learns from the docs as single-project facts: `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:74` presents `project` as one config line and has no section on multiple projects, `docs/config.md:216-260` documents the `[jira]` block as a single scalar project, and `docs/migrations.md` describes the ensure registry without the two units this epic adds. A user upgrading a client store also needs to know what the new `required_capabilities` entry means for older binaries in their fleet. None of that is documented by the implementation stories, which own code and tests only.

## Approach

Document the shipped behaviour and record the architectural decision. The ADR is warranted rather than decorative because two decisions here are load-bearing, non-obvious, and expensive to reverse: that the project set is a property of the **store** rather than of a repo, and that the legacy migration writes **no ticket events**. Both were chosen against plausible alternatives — per-repo project lists and an EDIT-per-ticket backfill — and a future reader who does not know why will be tempted back toward them.

The ADR is `docs/adr/0062-*` — the next number after `0061-measurement-provenance-in-attested-evidence.md`. It records the shared-`prev_snapshot` reasoning for store ownership, the short-lock-budget reasoning for the event-free migration, and the conditional-stamp reasoning for compatibility. It also notes the relationship to ADR 0060, whose churn constraint the mapping satisfies by construction.

Documentation updates cover the mapping and its `bridge projects` verb, the tri-state project field, the repos field, the two ensure units, and the upgrade note for fleets running mixed binary versions.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0062-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` (new)
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
- `docs/config.md`
- `docs/migrations.md`
- `docs/user-guide.md`
- `docs/ticket-model.md`

## Testing

No `## Testing` section beyond this note: this story adds no testable behaviour — it is documentation and an ADR, which `rebar explain plan` names as a legitimately test-free change class. Verification is by the repository's existing documentation gates rather than by new tests, and the acceptance criteria below name the command that checks each claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0062-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` exists and records the store-ownership,
      event-free-migration, and conditional-stamp decisions with their rejected alternatives; checked
      by reading the file and confirming each of the three decisions names what it was chosen over.
- [ ] The Jira sync and config docs describe the project mapping and no longer present a single
      scalar project as the only option; checked by confirming no remaining passage states the
      single-project constraint as current behaviour.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` lists both new ensure units alongside the existing built-ins; checked by
      confirming each registered id appears in the doc.
- [ ] The docs state what the `multi-project-bridge` capability means for an older binary and what an
      operator does about it; checked by confirming the upgrade note names both the fail-closed
      behaviour and the remedy.
- [ ] The generated CLI reference includes `bridge projects`; checked by running the repository's
      documentation generation and confirming the verb appears without a manual edit.
baseline.summary: Document the multi-project model and record ADR 0062

baseline.description:
Move the GET-rotation stamp out of `bindings.json` so the file stops changing on passes with no real change. After A1 this is what collapses the **version count** (20 of 40 sampled revisions become byte-identical), taking the combined saving to **12.8x**. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`set_last_get` (`binding_store.py:459-464`) stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit` (default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly **20 entries change per pass**. So with A1 alone the file still changes every pass and the version count stays ~180/day; only the delta shrinks. Losing rotation state is harmless — it just resets ordering, and the existing wrappers at `outbound_differ.py:167-172` are already fail-open.

## Approach — compatibility first
Write the new file, read `max(new, legacy)`, and **keep writing the legacy field**. Deletion is a separate ticket (A2-2).

`max()`, not new-then-old: under mixed versions an old binary advances the in-line field but cannot write the new file, so a first-wins read would take the **stale** value; since rotation sorts on it (`outbound_differ.py:607`), recently-probed keys would sort first and the rest would starve. Values are fixed-width zero-padded (`2026-07-29T21-46-44`), so lexicographic `max()` is chronological, and `_last_get_pass` returns `""` on absence — the lexicographic minimum — so after A2-2 `max(new, "")` degenerates cleanly to `new`.

**Migrate in memory on load; persist only inside `save()` / the `if persist:` block** (`reconcile.py:547-549`). Adding a file IS a write, and `__main__.py:106` `_run_reconcile_check` ("read-only") reaches `load_binding_store` at `:152`. Not an ensure unit: `run_ensures` holds the store filesystem lock (`ensures.py:155`), disjoint from `refs/reconciler/lock`, and `BindingStore.save()` takes no lock and is a whole-file `os.replace` — an ensure unit would introduce a clobber race that does not exist today.

**Module-size constraint:** `outbound_differ.py` is at **exactly 800 LOC**, the locked cap. This change must be **net-negative** there — move `_last_get_pass` (`:155-163`) and `_set_last_get` (`:166-172`) into the new rotation module; the two call sites (`:607`, `:704`) are one-for-one substitutions.

**Staging:** add `get_rotation.json` to `reconcile_helpers.py:206`'s `_rel_files` AND the basename check at `:227-230`, or it is never committed **locally** (GHA's `git add -A` would mask the omission). `.gitattributes` is a glob (`.bridge_state/* merge=ours`) so the new file is covered. Update `push.py:76`'s docstring, which names the regenerable files explicitly.

## Rollback
Reverting is safe: readers fall back to the in-line field, which this change never stops writing, so rotation order survives and the orphaned file is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The byte-identical/no-commit assertion from A1 **still holds when <=20 absent-key GETs occur in
      a pass**. Tier: **integration** in a real temporary git repo.
- [ ] `get_rotation.json` is **staged and committed locally** (asserted in a real temporary git repo,
      since GHA's `git add -A` would mask a staging omission). Tier: **integration**.
- [ ] Rotation order after an **interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence** matches the
      all-new sequence. Tier: **integration**. This is the RED case for the `max()` rule — a
      first-wins read fails it.
- [ ] A legacy store with in-line stamps only yields identical rotation order. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty). Tier: **CLI subprocess** + worktree assertion.
- [ ] `wc -l src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` is **<=800**. Verify: the
      module-size gate in `_build-and-test.yml` passes.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, new rotation module under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, `outbound_differ.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `_store/push.py` (docstring), tests

Scope: M. Depends on A1.
baseline.summary: A2-1: move last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping into .bridge_state/get_rotation.json (write-new, read max(new, legacy))

baseline.description:
Operator-approved early removal (pre-1.0 breaking pass #3), 2026-08-12. Source: the DEPRECATION REMOVAL-READINESS SURVEY, comment #11 on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1), Tier 2 item 3. Operator ruling (verbatim): "The two best candidates and the one ready now are all approved for removal." Third and last change of the pass, after checked-unhelpful-tanager and priceless-charred-fruitbat.

## What

Remove the deprecated bare env var `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` (deprecated 1fbfb5c691, shipped v0.11.0; ADR 0057). The per-class `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]` slots are the interface; the bare scalar is a SUPERSESSION with a migration window that the operator has now closed early.

## SCOPE NARROWING — the config key `[tool.rebar.llm].model` STAYS

The survey framed this as "REBAR_LLM_MODEL / llm.model". Evidence says only the ENV VAR is removable, and that matches the registry, whose single row (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:101`) is env-only:

- `rebar.toml` sets `[tool.rebar.llm].model` deliberately and load-bearingly (it pins the provider so provider inference cannot leak to a non-Bedrock default).
- `LLMConfig.model` is read widely across the runtime and is the value model-class resolution falls back to.
- `docs/config.md:320` documents `model` as a live key; only its "env `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`" annotation goes.

So this ticket removes ONE env channel and leaves the config key, the CLI `-c llm.model` override, and the per-step `model:` workflow override untouched.

## Scope (current main)

- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:92-101` — delete the `_scheduled("env", "REBAR_LLM_MODEL", …)` row and its explanatory comment block; append this removal to the historical-record NOTE.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:~249` — ADD the tombstone `_tomb("env", "REBAR_LLM_MODEL", "the [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] slots", "error")`, directly mirroring the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` row at :249.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py:529-536` — wire the new tombstone check next to the existing `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` check in `LLMConfig.from_env`, the same fail-loud placement (a retired LLM knob fails only when the LLM stack loads; `RemovedInputError` is a `BaseException` so the broad `except Exception` in this method cannot swallow it).
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py:581-597` — delete the warn-when-set block; `:599` — stop reading the env for `model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py:373` — `_llm_str` gains `env_name: str | None`, skipping the env read when `None`, so `model` resolves CLI > config table > default with no env channel.
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:230-250` — delete `_deprecated_bare_model()`; drop the `fallback_default` rung so class precedence becomes CLI > per-class env > config table > built-in default (`:183-189` comment updated).

### Prose/comment sites in `src/` that name the variable (all must move, or AC-1 cannot pass)

`src/rebar/llm/config.py:10` (module env table), `:285` (the `resolve_model` docstring describing `cfg.model` as folding the env read — FACTUALLY FALSE post-removal), `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:70` (says a non-default `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` still wins — also FACTUALLY FALSE post-removal), `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py:14` (a historical sizing anecdote; reword to past tense, it is a record of why a change was unlandable).

### Test consumers (the blocking risk: they set the env and go through `LLMConfig.from_env`)

After the tombstone lands, ANY test that sets `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` and builds an `LLMConfig` will RAISE `RemovedInputError` instead of resolving. All 15 files that reference the variable must be retargeted to `[tool.rebar.llm].model`, a per-class `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL`, or the `-c llm.model` override: `tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_deprecation.py` (retargeted to assert the fail-loud tombstone), `test_config_llm.py`, `test_ci_provider_matrix.py`, `test_llm_config_pointer.py`, `test_project_default_provider.py`, `test_llm_config_gate_root.py`, `test_gate_context_seam.py`, `test_bedrock_provider.py`, `test_openai_compatible_provider.py`, `test_reviewbot_bedrock_cutover.py`, `test_code_review_per_pass_classes.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_usage_attribution.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_scoped_ticket_tool.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py`.

### `infra/` (operator-facing, hand-written)

`infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:334-339` tells operators not to reach for the alias and names `model_classes._deprecated_bare_model`, a symbol this change deletes; `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:170-178` explains why the variable is deliberately not set. Both are reworded to "removed", not "deprecated".

## Registry/tombstone treatment (mirrors precedent)

Deleted row + historical NOTE is the DE7 / ticket-5899 shape. UNLIKE removal #2, this one DOES take a tombstone: the tombstone registry covers `env`/`cfg`/`file` inputs, and the closest precedent — `_tomb("env", "REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS", "REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS", "error")`, also a superseded LLM knob checked in `llm.config.from_env` — is `behavior="error"`. Fail-loud is right here because silently ignoring a still-set `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` would quietly change which model every operation runs, i.e. cost and quality, with no signal. Record "operator-approved early removal (pre-1.0 pass #3), 2026-08-12".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The env var is gone from the resolver and from every prose site that described it as live; checked: `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL src/rebar` matches ONLY the tombstone row in `_deprecations.py`, its `from_env` check, and the historical-record NOTE (a raw grep, since env names are string literals the LSP cannot resolve).
- [x] A still-set `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` FAILS LOUD with the migration message rather than being ignored; checked: `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=x rebar review-plan --check` exits non-zero naming the model_classes slots.
- [x] `[tool.rebar.llm].model`, `-c llm.model` and the per-step `model:` override all still resolve; proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_llm.py`.
- [x] The deprecation row is deleted and the tombstone added; proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py`.
- [x] `docs/env-vars.md` is REGENERATED, not hand-edited, and no longer lists the variable; checked: `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py && git diff --exit-code docs/env-vars.md`.
- [x] Hand-written docs and operator material drop the variable: `docs/config.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/llm-example-configs.md`, `docs/local-dev-env.md`, `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/workflow-authoring-v2.md`, `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`, `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`. ADR 0057 stays as historical record.
- [x] No test sets the removed env and then builds an `LLMConfig` (which would now raise); proven by the full `pytest` suite passing.
- [x] `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` record the removal in the prior passes' table format.
- [x] Gates green; checked: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full `pytest` suite.

## Testing

- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — the commit gate.
- `pytest` (full suite); `tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_deprecation.py` covers the deprecation being removed and is retargeted to the tombstone's fail-loud behaviour.
- `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py && git diff --exit-code docs/env-vars.md` — the CI env-registry drift gate.
- `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL src tests docs infra` — raw grep for the string-literal env name, including the operator-facing `infra/` runbook and compose file.
baseline.summary: Remove the deprecated REBAR_LLM_MODEL env var

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Compaction can leave the tracker working tree dirty (untracked `SNAPSHOT.json` / `*.retired` regenerated by a peer clone and pushed to origin). The next reconverge runs `git merge origin/tickets` in `src/rebar/_store/sync.py::_union_merge`; because origin now wants to CREATE those same paths, git aborts with *"untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge."* The handler is abort-only (`sync.py:191-197`) and push-recovery cannot clear untracked files (`push_recovery.py`: `git reset --hard` is tracked-only; `_stash_create` omits `-u`). Every retry re-aborts → the store wedges, stranding local commits off origin. Proven end to end (RCA comment on this ticket; runtime repro `/tmp/mergerepro`).

## Fix (primary — breaks the wedge at the proven site)
Make the union merge self-heal the ONE recoverable abort class: untracked paths that origin is about to introduce. In `_union_merge`, when `git merge` fails, detect the "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the exact paths git names. Relocate ONLY those named untracked paths into a quarantine directory under the git common dir (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/`, OUTSIDE any worktree so they cannot re-collide), then retry the merge once.
- On retry success: origin's authoritative committed versions are now present; the union keeps
  both parents, so no local commit is orphaned. Quarantine is retained as a safety copy (not
  deleted inline).
- On any other failure or a genuine content conflict: fall back to today's behavior exactly —
  `git merge --abort`, keep local, log the `rebar fsck-recover` hint.

### Why this is safe / non-destructive
- Only the paths git explicitly names are moved, and that error names ONLY files that already
  exist on origin (that is WHY they collide) — i.e. regenerable compaction artifacts.
- `.tmp-event-*` real uncommitted event-appends live at the tracker ROOT and do not exist on
  origin, so git never names them → they are never quarantined.
- Files are MOVED, never deleted, so even a mistaken selection loses nothing.

## Portability
In-process; uses only local `git`. No CI-provider trigger, no network dependency — the recovery runs wherever reconverge runs (satisfies `project.portability`).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` — add untracked-collision quarantine+retry to `_union_merge`; add a
  small parser for the git error's path list and a quarantine helper.
- `tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py` (new) — RED→GREEN coverage.

## Test plan (RED→GREEN, held-out oracle)
1. RED: construct a tracker whose HEAD lacks a path that `origin/tickets` adds, and place that
   same path as an UNTRACKED file in the working tree; call the reconverge entry; assert it
   currently raises/leaves HEAD un-merged (the abort). Confirm it fails for the untracked-overwrite
   reason (not an unrelated error).
2. GREEN after fix: same fixture → merge completes, HEAD contains both parents, the local-only
   commit remains reachable, and the quarantined copy exists.
3. Mutation check: re-introduce the abort-only handler (skip the quarantine) → test returns RED.
4. Refactoring litmus: assertions are on observable git state (HEAD parents, reachability, files),
   not private names.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A reconverge whose union merge would abort ONLY on origin-introduced untracked paths now
      completes, keeping both parents; no local commit orphaned.
- [x] A genuine content conflict still aborts, keeps local, and hints `rebar fsck-recover`
      (unchanged behavior).
- [x] `.tmp-event-*` and any untracked path NOT named by git are left untouched.
- [x] New unit test is legitimately RED before the fix and GREEN after; mutation returns it to RED.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; change lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND
      Verified +1) before this ticket closes.

## Defense-in-depth (separate follow-up, linked discovered_from)
Make compaction crash-atomic (roll back the dirty tree if the detached sweep dies before commit) so the dirty state is not produced in the first place. Not required to stop the loss — the reconverge self-heal above already breaks the wedge — so tracked as a linked follow-up, not this ticket's scope.
baseline.summary: Compaction leaves tracker working tree dirty; reconverge union-merge then wedges store (untracked-overwrite abort), stranding local ticket events off origin

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` and `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` declare `trace_id` as `["string","null"]`, described as "Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled", but `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` hardcodes `None` at every site emitting it. No per-run identity exists, so a verdict cannot name its run and no header can carry a run-stable value.

## Approach

Mint one identity per gate run at the two boundaries that already resolve the run's config once: `workflow/gate_dispatch.py:167` (plan-review, `ctx.ticket_id` in scope) and `:762` (completion-verifier). Both open `gate_config(cfg)`, whose contextvar every op reads via `resolve_gate_config` (`config.py:99-107`). Attach with `dataclasses.replace(cfg, ...)` before `gate_config(cfg)`, never mutating the caller's object.

Three values: `trace_id` (32 lowercase hex — the active OpenTelemetry span's trace id when one is recording, else `secrets.token_hex(16)`), `ticket_id` (the boundary's own), and `operation` (`"review-plan"` or `"verify-completion"` — rebar's canonical verb names, so the vocabulary matches the CLI and docs). No `run_id`: `trace_id` already identifies the run. `ticket_id` and `operation` are minted here because the boundary is the only place they are knowable; their consumer is `26ae-041f-dcc4-4279`'s `${run:...}` vocabulary, and criteria below cover them.

32-hex is W3C trace-id format, which Langfuse v3+ requires. Reading a live span's id is correct when an enclosing span exists and free when none does — but it does NOT by itself align the header with rebar's exported spans: rebar opens no root span, so at the boundary nothing is normally recording and the value is minted, while `tracing.py`'s per-candidate spans open later inside each model request, each its own trace root. That alignment needs the run-level root span, which is out of scope. One consequence to accept: under a coarse enclosing span, several gate runs inherit one id and Langfuse will show them as a single trace. Langfuse's model groups related units by session, not by a shared trace id, so the run-level span is what fixes this properly. Random per run, not derived from the ticket: a derived value would merge every re-review into one trace.

The value reaches pool workers unchanged via `generation._submit_ctx` (`copy_context().run`, `generation.py:154-165`), used by `pass1.py:426-427` and `container_stage.py:260`.

Read `req.config.trace_id` at **all three** `runner.py` sites hardcoding `None`:

- `:254` — `FakeRunner.run`'s `mode == "structured"` branch, comment "Structured mode (e.g.
  verify_completion)". The completion verifier is structured-mode, so its fake verdict returns
  here, not `:259`; omitting it makes the completion criterion below unsatisfiable.
- `:259` — `FakeRunner.run`'s findings branch.
- `:719` — the real runner.

The two `FakeRunner` branches are selected by `req.mode`, so testing one says nothing about the other. The seam is `req.config`: the gate config arrives as `RunRequest(config=...)` (`operations.py:209-212`) and `FakeRunner` holds no instance config, reaching configuration only via `req.config` (`repo_path` at `:264`). Derivations like `max_output_cfg` use `dataclasses.replace`, so the identity rides through.

Both schema descriptions are restated in the same change so the contract cannot contradict the emitted value: "per-gate-run correlation id (32 lowercase hex); null for deterministic or fallback verdicts and standalone ops" — deliberately not "present inside any gate run". Other emitters run inside a gate scope with no LLM call (`workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py:153`, `completion_reconcile.py:252`, `workflow/completion_failures.py:98`), and `spec_scan.py:138` is not a gate op; all stay `None` and are out of scope, since a deterministic verdict has no gateway request behind it.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the identity fields on `LLMConfig`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — mint at both run boundaries.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — read `req.config.trace_id` at `:254`, `:259`, `:719`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `tests/unit/test_run_correlation.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: in-process unit tests plus schema validation — contextvar propagation and verdict field population both run for real in-process; no subprocess or network boundary.

- Happy path: within one scope every `resolve_gate_config()` read returns the same `trace_id`.
- Edge: two scopes differ; the value is `None` outside any gate run.
- Concurrency: a value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's.
- Real-runner path: `:719` driven through `PydanticAIRunner.run` with the offline
  `model_override` TestModel harness — every other verdict assertion is satisfiable through
  `FakeRunner`, leaving `:719` otherwise unproven.
- Both gate surfaces: each produces a verdict carrying the run's `trace_id`, validated against
  its own schema.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Inside one gate run `resolve_gate_config().trace_id` is identical across repeated reads;
      checked by asserting equality across three reads in one scope.
- [x] Absent an enclosing recording span, two gate runs produce different `trace_id` values;
      checked by a test over two scopes with no tracer configured. The qualifier is load-
      bearing: under one coarse caller-owned span (a CI wrapper, an auto-instrumented host)
      every run inside it reads that span's id, so the values legitimately match.
- [x] `trace_id` is 32 lowercase hex; checked by `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", value)`.
- [x] With a recording OpenTelemetry span active, `trace_id` equals that span's trace id as 32
      hex; checked by a test starting a real span and comparing.
- [x] With no span recording, `trace_id` is freshly minted; checked by asserting two runs differ
      with no tracer configured.
- [x] A value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's.
- [x] Within a gate scope `resolve_gate_config().ticket_id` and `.operation` equal what the
      boundary minted them from, with `operation` equal to `review-plan` and
      `verify-completion` respectively; checked for each boundary.
- [x] A plan-review verdict carries the run's `trace_id` and validates against
      `review_result.schema.json`.
- [x] A completion-verifier verdict produced in a completion-verifier scope carries that run's
      `trace_id` and validates against `completion_verdict.schema.json`.
- [x] A verdict produced through the real runner site `:719` carries `req.config.trace_id`;
      checked by driving `PydanticAIRunner.run` with the offline `model_override` harness, so no
      `FakeRunner` branch can satisfy it.
- [x] Both schema descriptions state the correlation id in 32-hex shape and the
      deterministic/fallback exemption, with no residual Langfuse claim and no "present inside
      any gate run" wording; checked by a grep over both files.
- [x] A deterministic completion verdict produced inside a gate scope still carries
      `trace_id: null`; checked by driving the deterministic child-closure path.
- [x] The identity survives a per-request config derivation; checked by asserting
      `max_output_cfg(cfg).trace_id == cfg.trace_id`.
- [x] Outside any gate run the identity is `None` and verdicts are unchanged.
baseline.summary: Mint a per-gate-run correlation identity and populate the verdict trace_id

baseline.description:
# Operation certificates — asymmetric + environment-attributed + per-project required-environment

## Context
rebar's operation certificates (plan-review and completion-verifier verdicts) are today **local self-attestations**: signed with a per-clone **symmetric HMAC secret** and verified only by the same clone (`foreign_key` if verified elsewhere — `src/rebar/signing.py`). Nothing at merge (Gerrit `Verified` / CI) re-verifies them, so they are local discipline, **not enforceable controls**, and no third party can verify one without the forge-capable secret. This epic migrates operation-certs to **asymmetric** signatures on the attestation foundation, **attributes** each to the signing **environment** (verify-by-anyone against that environment's public key), and lets a project **optionally require** a certificate from a specific trusted environment. **Beneficiary:** high-assurance projects that need a gate verdict they can trust was not forged by the developer who wanted to pass it — while low-security projects keep the fast local-report behavior. This epic delivers the end state in which **both** signature types are asymmetric.

> **Prerequisites shipped (drift note, 2026-07-13).** Both prerequisite epics have landed on `main`:
> the **foundation** epic (`2fd4` / brilliant-curly-songbird) shipped the attestation substrate at
> `src/rebar/attest/` (DSSE+PAE `dsse.py`, the source-pinned per-kind `POLICY` table in `registry.py`,
> the SSHSIG scheme `sshsig.py`, and HMAC-as-legacy `hmac_legacy.py`); the **identity** epic
> (`e68d` / gnu-whale-ichor) shipped an authenticated-authorship **merge-gate CI job**
> (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`, which walks the *merged log* and grandfathers via
> `ENFORCE_SINCE`), an in-toto **merged-log ledger**, and **era-scoped commit-ancestry key validity**
> (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`: validity as commit-ancestry positions
> `added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit`, compared with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; verdict
> `key_not_valid_at_era` is already in `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json`). This
> epic was planned before those landed and originally described building the merge-gate, ledger, and
> era-scoped rotation itself. It now **reuses** that shipped machinery rather than building parallel
> copies — see the reuse notes inline below and the proposal comment on this epic.

## Approach (and why)
- **Environment-attributed, asymmetric op-certs.** Any environment signs with its own asymmetric
  Ed25519 key via the foundation's substrate (namespace `rebar.opcert.v1`); the certificate
  attributes to that environment and is verifiable by anyone against its public key. This matches
  the existing per-environment model (a dev machine and a shared server are both "environments")
  and restores the clean two-actor split (op-cert = **environment**; authorship = person, the
  identity epic). The two kinds stay **orthogonal in actor and threat model** — different key,
  trust-root, and namespace, so a signature is never valid across kinds — but the identity epic has
  since **shipped**, so this epic now **reuses** its delivered machinery (the `verify-identity`
  merge-gate CI job, the merged-log ledger, and the era-scoped commit-ancestry key-validity *rule*
  in `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`) rather than building parallel copies. "Independent" here means
  the dependency is never inverted — op-certs are signed by environment keys, never by identity/person
  keys — **not** that no code is shared.
- **Per-project optional requirement.** A project pins trusted-environment public keys
  **out-of-band** (a Gerrit-protected / CI config path, **never** the auto-pushed tickets branch)
  and may require a specific environment's certificate for a gate. Low-security default: any/local
  certificate is a **process record**, not a control. High-security: the **merge gate** (Gerrit/CI)
  verifies the required environment's signature over the merged log. (Op-cert trust roots are
  **out-of-band and high-authority** — deliberately unlike the identity epic's in-band TOFU authorship
  keys; this distinction is preserved and is the reason op-cert cannot simply inherit identity's trust
  model wholesale even while it reuses identity's era/merged-log plumbing.)
- **Trusted remote execution for high assurance.** To obtain a required-environment certificate, a
  developer routes the gate operation to a trusted `rebar-mcp` server (e.g. on AWS) that runs the
  verifier and signs. **Integrity requirement (load-bearing):** that server MUST fetch the
  authoritative state itself (ticket state from the tickets branch; code at the specific commit from
  the review remote) and run the gate on THAT — never on client-provided inputs — or the signature
  certifies a lie. This is a security/latency tradeoff the project opts into; the default local path
  stays **offline and never wedges** a rebar operation.
- **Verify against the pinned key, not the claimed key_id.** "Require environment E" verifies the
  signature against E's out-of-band-pinned public key; the DSSE keyid is an unauthenticated hint.
  Certificates bind `{ticket id, material fingerprint, merged-log position}` so they cannot be
  replayed onto another ticket / stale state. The merged-log position is a **`main` commit SHA**
  (the commit at which the trusted environment ran the gate); there is no `intra_idx` symbol — the
  substrate's only intra-commit tiebreak is the event's `{timestamp}-{uuid}` position, which does
  not apply to op-cert's explicit-SHA model.
- **HMAC removal (contract phase).** Once op-certs verify asymmetrically, the legacy HMAC scheme
  (`src/rebar/attest/hmac_legacy.py`, registered in the foundation's `attest/registry.py` `POLICY`
  table) is removed — completing the migration begun in the foundation epic. Authorship already signs
  asymmetrically (identity epic), so plan-review / completion-verifier op-certs are the last remaining
  HMAC consumers.

## Trust config & era-validity protocol (design resolution, 2026-07-13)
This section resolves the concrete mechanics the plan previously left abstract (epic plan-review BLOCK, findings E2/F1/G6/T1/T8). It is the single schema children 368c/42d1/4214/ee0b/8f1d all read.

- **Trust config file.** Trusted-environment public keys are pinned in a **YAML** file at
  **`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`** (repo-root, resolved relative to the review remote's
  checkout). This path is **out-of-band**: it lives on the code branch (`main`, Gerrit-gated +
  CODEOWNERS-protected), **never** on the auto-pushed `tickets` branch. An absent file means "no
  required environment" — the low-security default (local certs are records, not controls).
- **Schema.**
  ```yaml
  environments:
    - env_id: "<string>"            # logical environment name; MUST equal the DSSE principal (keyid)
      keys:
        - public_key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…"   # one OpenSSH ed25519 authorized-keys line
          added_at_commit: "<git-sha-on-main>"      # era start: the main commit at/after which this key is valid
          revoked_at_commit: "<git-sha-on-main>|null"  # era end (null = still valid)
  ```
  `require_environment` (per-gate) names one `env_id` that must produce the certificate.
- **Why explicit SHAs, not tickets-branch positions.** The identity epic's era mechanism resolves a
  key's add/revoke *position* to a commit by globbing `<ticket_dir>/<position>-*.json` **on the
  tickets branch** (`authorship.resolve_event_commit`). Environment keys are **not** on the tickets
  branch, so `resolve_event_commit` / `_keyring_for` **cannot** be reused verbatim. Instead the
  config records `added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit` as **explicit git SHAs on `main`**. What is
  reused is the **era-validity *rule*** — the `git merge-base --is-ancestor` ancestry comparison and
  the `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict — factored so both authorship (position→commit) and op-cert
  (explicit-commit) call one shared ancestry predicate. Children 368c must reuse the *rule/verdict*,
  not the event-file resolver.
- **Era-validity decision rule.** An op-cert binds a **merged-log position** = the `main` commit `P`
  at which the trusted environment ran the gate (the subject's bound commit). A config key is
  **valid at `P`** iff `git merge-base --is-ancestor(added_at_commit, P)` is true AND
  (`revoked_at_commit is None` OR `git merge-base --is-ancestor(revoked_at_commit, P)` is false). A
  certificate verifies iff **some** currently-valid key for the required `env_id` verifies its
  signature (overlapping rotation windows are permitted, exactly as authorship allows). A cert whose
  only matching key is past its rotation surfaces the shared `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict.
  Revoked keys are **retained in the config keyring** (with `revoked_at_commit` set) so the
  two-phase check's "any historical key" pass can still recognize a signature by a since-rotated
  key and classify it `key_not_valid_at_era` rather than `mismatch`.

## Scope
- **In:** asymmetric environment-signed op-certs on the foundation's substrate; the out-of-band
  `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` environment public-key trust config; per-project optional
  required-environment policy; merge-gate verification (a CI lane added to / mirroring the shipped
  `verify-identity.yaml` gate, **extending** its merged-log walk rather than a fresh walker); the
  trusted `rebar-mcp` remote-execution path that fetches authoritative state; certificate subject
  binding + explicit-SHA env-key era rotation (**reusing the identity epic's commit-ancestry
  validity *rule/verdict***); removal of the legacy HMAC scheme with an expand-contract migration;
  IaC for the trusted MCP-server deployment (IAM SigV4 endpoint auth, least-privilege IAM, Ed25519 key in SSM Parameter Store (SecureString));
  docs + ADR.
- **Out:** the signing substrate itself (foundation epic); person/authorship signing (identity
  epic); the merge-gate walker / ledger / era-validity *rule* itself (identity epic — this epic
  *reuses* it); transparency-log / keyless follow-ons; threshold/multi-sig (deferred idea 5100).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Operation certificates are produced/verified via the foundation's substrate with an Ed25519
      environment key (namespace `rebar.opcert.v1`), registered as a new kind in the
      `src/rebar/attest/registry.py` `POLICY` table alongside the foundation's HMAC-legacy and the
      identity epic's `rebar.authorship.v1`; a test asserts a certificate signed by environment E
      verifies against E's public key and fails against a different key.
- [ ] A project config pins trusted-environment public keys in the out-of-band, review-gated file
      **`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`** (schema in "Trust config & era-validity protocol";
      NOT the tickets branch); a test asserts a certificate from an environment not in the pinned
      set fails the required-environment check, and that the check verifies against the pinned key,
      not the certificate's self-claimed `key_id`.
- [ ] A merge-gate CI job verifies the required-environment certificate over the merged log and
      fails when a ticket that must carry one does not; it **extends the shipped `verify-identity.yaml`
      merge-gate** (same merged-log walk + `ENFORCE_SINCE`-style grandfathering) rather than a
      parallel job; a fixture demonstrates a missing/foreign certificate fails the job. CI-trigger
      audit: enumerate the `on:` triggers of `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` (the gate the
      op-cert lane is added to) and classify each as INCLUDED (the op-cert check runs under that
      trigger) or NO_FILTER (no `paths`/`branches` filter on that trigger excludes an op-cert-bearing
      change); a comment records the classification so no merge path silently skips the gate.
- [ ] Certificates bind `{ticket id, material fingerprint, merged-log position (a `main` commit SHA)}`;
      a test asserts a certificate cannot be replayed onto a different ticket or a mutated state.
      Environment-key rotation uses **explicit-SHA** era-scoped validity per the "Trust config &
      era-validity protocol" (`added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit` in the trust config, compared
      with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` against the cert's bound `main` commit), **reusing the
      commit-ancestry era *rule* and the `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict already in
      `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` (shipped by the identity epic)** — not
      the tickets-branch `resolve_event_commit` resolver; a test asserts a certificate from a key
      valid at its era verifies while one past its rotation surfaces `key_not_valid_at_era`.
- [ ] The trusted remote path fetches ticket state and code-at-commit from authoritative remotes
      itself and runs the gate on that; a test asserts a client-supplied doctored input does NOT
      change the signed verdict. **Transport:** the existing `rebar-mcp` server is stdio-only and is
      NOT network-exposed; the trusted remote path is a **library-mode HTTP service** (rebar imported
      as a library, mirroring the proven `review_bot` pattern — no stdio-MCP transport work) fronted
      by **AWS API Gateway**, which is the SigV4 integration point. The AWS infra authenticates the
      endpoint via **AWS IAM (SigV4-signed requests) restricted to a named admin role**, over TLS;
      declares least-privilege IAM for the signing-key read + repo read; and stores the **Ed25519
      signing key material in AWS SSM Parameter Store as a SecureString (AWS-managed KMS key at rest; the free mechanism rebar already uses for /rebar/prod/* secrets)** — the server
      performs SSHSIG signing itself with that key. (NOT AWS KMS managed signing: KMS asymmetric
      SIGN_VERIFY supports only ECDSA/RSA, not Ed25519, so "KMS" here means envelope-encryption of
      the secret, not the signing operation.) The default **local path stays the offline stdio
      `rebar-mcp` and never wedges an op.**
- [ ] The legacy HMAC scheme is removed; a test asserts no code path signs or accepts an HMAC
      operation-cert. A named migration artifact **`docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`** exists
      documenting the expand-contract cutover window / re-issue procedure (a test asserts the file
      exists, is non-empty, and describes the expand→contract phases — an `## Expand` and a
      `## Contract` section — so the cutover procedure is present, not effort-framed), rather than a
      flag-day break. Rollback:
      the required-environment policy is opt-in and defaults off (absent
      `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` / no `require_environment`); disabling it reverts to local
      behavior.
- [ ] Docs + ADR: a named ADR artifact `docs/adr/NNNN-opcert-asymmetric.md` exists documenting the
      environment-attribution model, low/high-security postures, the authoritative-state-fetch
      integrity requirement, out-of-band trust root, merge-gate enforcement, and HMAC removal +
      migration, and cross-references ADR 0046 (security posture; L2/L4 are op-cert-scoped). A test
      asserts the ADR file exists, is non-empty, and contains the strings `rebar.opcert.v1`,
      `trusted_environments.yaml`, and `ADR 0046`.
- [ ] Operation certificates are asymmetric and verifiable by any third party against the signing
- [ ] A project can require a certificate from a specific trusted environment for a gate; the merge gate
- [ ] The trusted environment's certificate reflects the authoritative state it fetched itself, not
- [ ] The legacy HMAC scheme is removed; both operation-cert and authorship signatures are asymmetric.
- [ ] The default (low-security, local, offline) path never requires network and never wedges an op.

## Intended decomposition (children)
1. Asymmetric environment-signed op-cert kind on the foundation's substrate (+ subject binding
   + explicit-SHA env-key era rotation, folded in from former task 5893) — a new `rebar.opcert.v1`
   kind in `attest/registry.py`'s `POLICY` table; reuses the era-validity *rule/verdict*, not the
   tickets-branch event resolver.
2. Out-of-band `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` key config + required-environment policy +
   verify-against-pinned-key.
3. Merge-gate verification CI job over the merged log (+ new-prohibition consumer scan, CI-trigger
   audit) — **extend the shipped `verify-identity` gate; do not stand up a parallel merged-log walker.**
4. Trusted `rebar-mcp` remote-execution path that fetches authoritative state + its AWS infra (IAM SigV4 endpoint auth, least-privilege IAM, Ed25519 key in SSM Parameter Store (SecureString)).
5. ~~Env-key era-scoped rotation~~ — **folded into child 1** (former task 5893, dropped as
   superseded).
6. HMAC removal (contract) + expand-contract migration artifact (`docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`).
7. Docs + ADR.

## Prior art / grounding
DSSE (keyid is an unauthenticated hint — verify against pinned keys); OpenSSH `allowed_signers` validity intervals; git SSH-signing trust-file model; RFC 8725 (alg-confusion); key-transparency lineage (equivocation) noted as a later option. Depends on the foundation epic's substrate (`src/rebar/attest/`, shipped). Reuses the identity epic's shipped merge-gate (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`), merged-log ledger, and commit-ancestry era-validity *rule* (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`).

## Producer-signing & compute-runtime design resolution (2026-07-13, round-6 convergence)

This section resolves the remaining design forks that blocked ee0b/8f1d plan-review convergence (rounds 1–5): the producer-signing seam, double-signing, verdict-vocabulary normalization, the compute runtime, and signer identity. It is the single schema the remaining children (the producer-seam story, ee0b, the IaC/deploy story, 8f1d, 6a89) all read. It supersedes the "Intended decomposition" list above for the not-yet-built half.

- **Uniform producer signing (the 8f1d fork, resolved: fork A).** Every environment holds its own
  Ed25519 op-cert key and the **gate producers themselves** mint `rebar.opcert.v1` certs: the
  plan-review sign step (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` `sign_plan_review`, today →
  `signing.sign_manifest` HMAC) and the close-gate sign step
  (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` `_sign` path, today → `signing.sign_manifest` HMAC)
  are repointed at `signing.sign_opcert_manifest`. A local cert is a **process record** (exactly
  today's HMAC semantics, but verifiable-by-anyone against the environment's public key); a
  **trusted** cert is the same artifact signed by an environment whose key is pinned in
  `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`. **The trusted server is not a special signer** — what makes
  it trusted is (a) its pinned key and (b) its operational property of fetching authoritative
  state. Fork B (local gates stop signing entirely) is rejected: it would strip the claim/close
  gates' local-tamper evidence and make low-security attestations trivially forgeable (worse than
  HMAC today).
- **Double-signing dissolves by construction.** One signature per verdict, minted by the gate
  producer with the ambient environment key. The remote handler (ee0b) never signs separately and
  never passes `sign=False` — it invokes the same library gate, which signs with the server's key
  because the server is the ambient environment. The HMAC environment key is never provisioned in
  the server.
- **Local key provenance.** Per-environment **passphrase-free Ed25519 keypair** auto-generated on
  first signing use at `<tracker>/.opcert-key` / `.opcert-key.pub` (`ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N ""`,
  0600, git-ignored) — mirroring the HMAC `.signing-key` genesis it replaces. The DSSE
  principal/keyid defaults to the environment's existing `env_id`; `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`
  overrides (deployment config). If `ssh-keygen` (OpenSSH ≥ 8.9) is unavailable, signing degrades
  to the existing in-band `{signed: false, error: …}` record — a local op never wedges; a project
  whose gate *requires* the signature then blocks at the gate with a clear
  install-OpenSSH remediation. … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Operation certificates — asymmetric + environment-attributed + per-project required-environment

# Split `_ref_lock.py` — it is pinned at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap

## Why this exists

Discovered while fixing bug `freeborn-dizzy-raven` (ebee-e959-8015-4e02), whose fix added two markers to `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py`. The file was at 799 lines and the CI module-size gate hard-fails any `src/rebar` file over 800 (no allowlist), so a two-line change did not fit. The fix landed by appending the markers in one `+=` statement, leaving the file at **exactly 800**. That is a spent margin: the next change to this module, of any size, cannot land without splitting it first.

## Two traps that sank a previous attempt (recorded, not hypothetical)

1. **`rebar._engine` is not an importable package.** `from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.X
   import ...` fails at collection with `ModuleNotFoundError`. Reconciler modules load siblings
   through the `_loader.py` `lazy_load(<key>, "<file>.py")` seam (`_ref_lock` already pulls
   `_advisory_lock` that way). Any split MUST go through that seam.
2. **Tests bind to module identity.**
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py` does
   `monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_git", ...)` and then calls
   `_ref_lock._push_lease_cas(...)`. Two loader keys mean two module objects, so a naively
   moved `_push_lease_cas` resolves `_git` from the child module and the patch misses. Its
   `caplog` assertions then fail too — same root cause, not an independent logger-name trap
   (they assert on record *messages*, not logger names). Keep the log emitting on the
   `rebar_reconciler._ref_lock` logger anyway, so operator-facing evidence is unchanged.

## Seam

Move the tail cluster (currently lines ~709-800, ~92 LOC) to a sibling `_ref_lock_push.py`: `_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS`, `_LEASE_MISMATCH_MARKER`, `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS`, `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr`, `_push_lease_cas`, `_push_cas`, `_push_delete_cas`. It is a real unit: *decide whether a rejected ref push means the lease moved, and issue the lease pushes that ask the question*. Nothing outside `_ref_lock.py` references these names except the one test above.

### Rewiring — all three moved entry points keep 4/5-arg wrappers in `_ref_lock.py`

`_push_cas` and `_push_delete_cas` are called from code that **stays** in `_ref_lock.py`:

- `_ref_lock.py:393` — `_push_cas(repo_root, ref, oid, _ZERO_OID, remote)` in `acquire`'s `_plant()`
- `_ref_lock.py:476` — `_push_cas(repo_root, ref, new_oid, old_oid, remote)` in `_cas_advance`'s `_do()`
- `_ref_lock.py:422` — `_push_delete_cas(repo_root, ref, oid, remote)` in `release`'s `_delete()`

If those three bare calls are left resolving nothing, the remote acquire/release/advance paths raise `NameError`. So the parent does **not** move the names away; it re-binds them. Worked example of the parent side after the split:

```python
_push = lazy_load("rebar_reconciler_ref_lock_push", "_ref_lock_push.py")
_is_cas_mismatch_stderr = _push.is_cas_mismatch_stderr


def _push_lease_cas(repo_root: Path, ref: str, old_oid: str, remote: str, refspec: str) -> None:
    _push.push_lease_cas(sys.modules[__name__], repo_root, ref, old_oid, remote, refspec)


def _push_cas(repo_root: Path, ref: str, new_oid: str, old_oid: str, remote: str) -> None:
    _push_lease_cas(repo_root, ref, old_oid, remote, f"{new_oid}:{ref}")


def _push_delete_cas(repo_root: Path, ref: str, old_oid: str, remote: str) -> None:
    _push_lease_cas(repo_root, ref, old_oid, remote, f":{ref}")
```

Consequences that make this the chosen shape rather than a re-export:

- The three call sites at :393, :422 and :476 are **unchanged** — same names, same arity.
- The child never imports the parent; the parent hands `sys.modules[__name__]` down as an
  explicit `core` argument, so there is no import cycle and no second module object.
- The child reads `core._git`, `core._REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS` and `core.logger` at **call time**,
  so `monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_git", ...)` is seen, and the CAS verdict still logs on
  the `rebar_reconciler._ref_lock` logger.
- Line budget: -92 moved, +~14 wrappers, so `_ref_lock.py` lands near 722.

The module docstring explaining the CAS-vs-server-fault distinction (the subject of bugs 4afc and ebee) carries the new file over the 100-LOC floor.

### Verification of the rewire, in-session

- `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -q` — exercises `acquire`/`release`/`renew` over the
  remote path, so a broken :393/:422/:476 binding fails here rather than in production.
- `python -c "from rebar_reconciler import _ref_lock; [getattr(_ref_lock, n) for n in
  ('_push_cas','_push_delete_cas','_push_lease_cas','_is_cas_mismatch_stderr')]"` — proves each
  name is still resolvable at the original module path.
- `grep -rn --include=*.py "_push_cas\|_push_delete_cas" src` returns only `_ref_lock.py`
  wrapper definitions/call sites and `_ref_lock_push.py` definitions — no orphan reference.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: `_ref_lock.py` <= 730 LOC (real margin under the 800 cap); `_ref_lock_push.py`
  >= 100 LOC and under the cap.
- [x] AC2: `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- [x] AC3: `test_ref_lock_push_classification.py` passes with its behavioural assertions
  untouched.
- [x] AC4: a test proves `monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_git", ...)` still intercepts the
  moved lease-push functions.
- [x] AC4b: a test proves the CAS-mismatch verdict still logs on the
  `rebar_reconciler._ref_lock` logger.
- [x] AC4c: `_push_cas`, `_push_delete_cas`, `_push_lease_cas` and `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr`
  are all still resolvable as attributes of `rebar_reconciler._ref_lock`, and the call sites at
  `_ref_lock.py` :393, :422 and :476 are byte-identical to their pre-split form.
- [x] AC5: CAS classification contract unchanged — `stale info` stays conclusive, the
  subtractive veto markers still win, ambiguity still fails closed (bugs 4afc, ebee).
- [x] AC6: `make lint` passes.
- [x] AC6b: `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] AC6c: the complexity ratchet passes with no new debt.
baseline.summary: Split _ref_lock.py — pinned at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap, so the next change of any size cannot land
