Build the one-time history strip as a committed operational script and prove it on a scratch clone before any publication window. No new dependency is added: the implementation uses stock Git plumbing already required by the repository. Session log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** contains the measured facts.

## Why stock plumbing

The proven pipeline is `git fast-export --no-data --signed-tags=strip --export-marks=old.marks tickets | <length-aware filter> | git fast-import --export-marks=new.marks`. On the real branch, the stream carries `M 100644 <sha> <path>` records with zero inline blob data and is about 26 MB for roughly 49,900 commits, so the filter need not move the roughly 1 GiB of blobs.

The filter emits no `deleteall`; branch export carries no tag records, so `--signed-tags=strip` is a harmless no-op; merges retain their `merge :n` parents; and empty commits remain. This preserves DAG topology and each non-target file introduction point, which ancestry-based authorship verification requires. `git-filter-repo --prune-empty=never` could also preserve empty commits; stock Git is chosen because the measured pipeline is already proven and avoids a new operational dependency, not because filter-repo is incapable.

Measured rehearsal result: 1,172,586,762 bytes became 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%), with every commit and merge commit preserved and the rewritten HEAD tree byte-identical after the dynamic re-add, in about 30 seconds.

## Required corrections

1. Run only in a fresh **unfiltered** clone. `fast-import` fails with `fatal: blob not found` in a `blob:none` partial clone, and this host's normal `origin` checkout is partial.
2. Strip both `.bridge_state/` and `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` from every historical revision. B6 ticket `3036-cb14-86b5-44a3` of epic `42eb-5789-c798-4dfc` deleted the 33,025,572-byte `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json` from HEAD and is closed. Before recording `old-tip`, the dry run must assert that prefix is absent from the old-tip tree; the rewrite then removes its historical copies.
3. Derive the re-add set dynamically with `git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state/`, never from a hardcoded list. Story `9594-1f1c-bcd1-4774` added `get_rotation.json`, so the current store has four files and future extensions must remain safe.
4. Parse every `data <n>` block by byte length instead of filtering lines with `grep`. Commit messages may begin with `M ` or `D `; those bytes are message data, not file commands.
5. Build the dry-run scratch clone with `--no-tags` (or prune all local tag refs before repack), then assert `refs/tags/pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` is absent before pack measurement. A6-0c must leave both the source remote branch and this remote tag unchanged; A6-1 owns deletion of the remote tag inside its quiet-window publication procedure.

## Publication boundary

The dry-run script never pushes. A6-1 owns publication: immediately before publishing, it re-reads the observed remote tip and uses `--force-with-lease=<old-tip>:<new-tip>`, never `--force`. A lease failure means another writer moved the remote; abort publication and rerun from a fresh unfiltered clone of the new tip. A6-0d owns the verified off-repo backup bundle used for rollback. A6-1 also owns deleting remote tag `refs/tags/pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` during that quiet-window publication sequence; A6-0c only proves the tag is absent from its rewritten scratch clone and unchanged on the source remote.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] On a scratch unfiltered clone, the rewritten branch commit count equals the measured old-tip commit count. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] On the same clone, the rewritten branch merge-commit count equals the measured old-tip merge-commit count. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Before rewrite, the harness asserts `git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state.bak-retarget/` has empty stdout, proving the recorded old tip includes closed B6. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] After dynamic re-add, `rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree}` exactly equals `rev-parse <old-tip>^{tree}`. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The re-add set comes from `ls-tree`, proven by a synthetic store with a fourth `.bridge_state/` file that survives byte-identically. Tier: integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The rewritten branch has no commit touching `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/`; the harness executes `test -z "$(git log --format=%H rewritten-tickets -- .bridge_state.bak-retarget/)"`. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A fresh unfiltered `--no-tags` clone of the rewritten branch has pack size at most **150 MB**, matching the parent epic ceiling. The harness first asserts `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/tags/pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` exits nonzero, then performs repack and measurement. Tier: repo measurement.
- [x] [code-verifiable] An adversarial commit message whose first line begins with `M ` survives byte-identically. Tier: unit stream-filter test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The script refuses a `--filter=blob:none` clone with a nonzero exit. Tier: integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] That refusal writes an operator-readable remedy requiring a fresh unfiltered clone. Tier: integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Every graph, tree, history-removal, and pack-size assertion completes before the script produces its final success result. Tier: integration with a seeded assertion failure.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A completed dry run invokes no remote push operation. Tier: integration with a recording Git wrapper.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A completed dry run leaves the source remote `tickets` ref unchanged. Tier: repo integration comparing the exact before/after object id.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A completed dry run leaves source remote tag `refs/tags/pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` unchanged. Tier: repo integration comparing the exact before/after object id.
- [x] [code-verifiable] In temporary real clones rooted at the rewritten branch, the harness appends and pushes one representative review-bot ticket event. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] After that synthetic writer push, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> <new-tip>` exits nonzero. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The representative writer push increases incremental `size-pack` by less than 1 MB. Tier: repo integration.

## Verification commands

- Stream-filter unit oracle: `pytest tests/unit/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py -v`.
- Synthetic four-file, partial-clone refusal, DAG/tree, history-removal, pack-size, no-publication, and representative-writer oracles: `pytest tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py -v`.
- Repository gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test`.

## Scope

`infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py`, `tests/unit/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py`, and `tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py`.

Scope: M. Operationally depends on closed B6 `3036-cb14-86b5-44a3`; must close before A6-1.

# Faithful, lock-free snapshot materialization core

## Why

The gates need a real on-disk tree at a pinned SHA, but the server's worktree is mutable and shared. `git archive` is lossy (drops `export-ignore` files, omits submodules, returns LFS pointer files, rewrites `export-subst`) — unacceptable for an attestation that claims "this is the code at SHA X". We need a faithful, concurrency-safe, portable materialization.

## What

A core module (e.g. `src/rebar/_engine/repo_snapshot.py`) exposing `materialize(ref, *, source_mode) -> handle` (context-managed):
- Coalesced `git fetch origin` (the only lock-taking step); resolve `ref` (branch|tag|SHA)
  to an immutable SHA against origin.
- FAITHFUL tree materialization: `git read-tree <sha>` into a temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`)
  then `git checkout-index --all --prefix=<tmp>/` — exact committed tree, no worktree, no
  `export-ignore` drops.
- Atomic population: build into `<root>/tmp/<uuid>/`, fsync files, `rename()` the directory
  into the cache path, fsync parent dir; readers see all-or-nothing.
- Portability: extraction never shells to external `tar`; temp root from
  `tempfile.gettempdir()`/`mkdtemp` (0700), overridable via `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, created
  OUTSIDE the repo/.git; `fcntl.flock` with atomic-`mkdir` fallback on a local FS.
- Descriptive errors: a fetch that fails on auth surfaces an actionable credential message
  (see S6), not a raw git error; attested mode fails closed, local mode still runs.
- Fetch prerequisites documented: arbitrary-SHA fetch needs `uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant`
  (or fetch a containing ref then resolve); prefer `--filter=blob:none` over deep shallow refetch.

## Scope

- In: the materialize() core, faithful tree extraction, atomic population, portability seam,
  fetch-coalescing, descriptive fetch/auth errors.
- Out: the cache/janitor (S2), gate wiring (S3), signing (S4), surfaces (S5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `materialize(ref)` produces a directory whose contents byte-match the committed tree at
      the resolved SHA, INCLUDING `export-ignore`-marked files (faithful, not `git archive`).
- [ ] LFS pointer files are detected (not silently served as content); submodule handling is
      defined and documented.
- [ ] Population is atomic: a reader never observes a partial tree; a crashed materialization
      leaves only a `tmp/` dir, cleaned on startup.
- [ ] No external `tar` binary is invoked; no hardcoded `/tmp`; runs on macOS + Linux.
- [ ] A private-repo fetch with missing credentials raises a descriptive, actionable error;
      attested mode fails closed.
- [ ] Concurrent `materialize()` of different SHAs do not contend on `index.lock`/`config.lock`.
baseline.summary: Faithful, lock-free snapshot materialization core

Captured 2026-08-30 as the deferred "Option B" from Decision 4 (nginx-edge cluster). Idea/undesigned — needs its own design + ADR before promotion.

## Context
ADR 0079 (autodeploy-on-box-timer, from story 8903 gall-plume-adder) deliberately scoped v1 auto-apply to the review-bot container ONLY; Gerrit config (CONFIG_PATHS) is DETECT-ONLY (signal via AUTODEPLOY_ERROR, never auto-applied) because auto-applying config to a box hosting a live FAIL-CLOSED submit gate is high-risk. ADR 0079 names "config auto-apply" as an explicit deferred v2. The nginx edge (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`) is in the SAME deferred bucket.

Bug 1d1b (downy-feminist-leopard) is being fixed under Option A (detect-and-signal only): add the edge template to a detect-only manifest so a merged edge change raises AUTODEPLOY_ERROR for an operator to apply, closing the SILENT-failure defect without expanding the unattended auto-apply surface. This idea is the follow-on: make autodeploy actually render + validate + reload the edge unattended.

## Why this is a design project, not a bug fix
- Blast radius spans every port-443 surface (MCP, /review/, /opcert/, Gerrit) including the submit gate — a bad reload could freeze all submissions.
- Needs: template render step, `nginx -t` validation, atomic reload, rollback-to-prior-conf on failure (deployed-sha not advanced), and the ADR 0079 stability constraints (bounded blast radius = never touch the gerrit container; self-heal; SHA-keyed backoff; flock serialisation).
- OSS precedent to weigh: Argo CD makes auto-sync opt-in per-app with explicit automated-rollback/self-heal toggles (drift DETECTION is always on; APPLY is deliberate); Terraform separates plan (detect) from apply (mutate); ingress controllers gate reload behind `nginx -t`. Design should mirror that "detect always, apply as a deliberate, separately-designed step" posture.

## Scope sketch (to be designed)
- NGINX_PATHS/EDGE_PATHS manifest + render pipeline in autodeploy.sh (infra/scripts/, outside eb64 scope).
- Validate-then-atomic-swap with rollback; leave prior working edge serving on failure.
- Live-validation harness analogous to a61d's AC5 (probe the edge post-deploy).
- ADR amendment/new ADR recording the v1->v2 boundary crossing.

## Relations
Follow-on to 1d1b (downy-feminist-leopard); would fully automate what a61d (enchanting-phantastic-weevil) currently needs an operator deploy for. Discovered-from lineage: 8903 (v1 scoping) -> 1d1b.
baseline.summary: v2: autodeploy full auto-apply of the nginx edge (render + nginx -t + atomic reload + rollback)

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

## Context / Problem

Six rollout-created comments remain duplicated in live Jira and reachable `tickets` history after the reconciler fixes stopped the echo loop. Closed prerequisite `irongray-unlucky-discus` proved the causal pairs and rehearsed it. The operator authorized the quiet window; direct writer evidence, not an elapsed wait, controls entry.

The older bridge-cache HEAD-tree oracle is invalid for intentional removal; see `docs/comment-echo-reclaim-runbook.md:21`, `:68`, `:269`. Preparation measured about 254 MB logical removal versus 26 MB clone savings, so size is observed, not gated.

## Approach

Update from `origin/main` with enrichment drain off. Stop writers, sync AWS MCP to live `origin/tickets`, then freeze stable OID/ref reads; any movement restarts artifacts.

Regenerate evidence in a new `0700` off-repo directory and full clone. Use `prepare_reclaim_backup.prepare` (`infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:292`), `comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.build_manifest` (`infra/scripts/comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.py:746`), and `reclaim_comment_echo_history.rewrite` (`infra/scripts/reclaim_comment_echo_history.py:743`). Replay both tips, rehearse rollback/forward, and probe stale deployed writers before mutation.

With the reconciler disabled, use only `cleanup_comment_echo_jira.run`'s digest-bound journal (`infra/scripts/cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:478`). Delete `997143,997144,997145,997255,997256,997293`; preserve `963510,963511,963512,963788,963789,964272`. Prove convergence twice, publish `refs/heads/tickets` once with the exact frozen lease, replace every persistent clone, then restore writers one runtime at a time.

Causal manifest identity, the exact lease, and the epoch guard address deletion ambiguity, ref movement, and stale union while retaining proven backup, journal, and reclone controls; no recurring gate is added.

## Scope

`file_impact_scope=none` is deliberate: repository files are read-only. Only the six Jira duplicates, manifest-listed echo material, final epoch, `origin/tickets`, and persistent clones change; sensitive artifacts remain off-repo.

Survivors, non-target state, bridge bindings, retained bytes, and other refs are excluded.

**DATA LOSS RISK:** After Jira DELETE but before publication, Jira lacks six IDs while old tickets still records them. This state is quarantined, auditable, and never serviceable: the manifest, journal, inventories, bundle, OLD_TIP, and NEW_TIP bind the mismatch. On failure preserve evidence/candidate, keep writers stopped, re-read both systems, then use a separately reviewed forward correction; Git rollback cannot restore Jira IDs.

## Testing

- Happy path: run `git fetch origin` then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`; require writer/ref receipts plus equal AWS/local/remote tickets OIDs.
- Failure path: disposable stores prove drift refuses before mutation, crash/resume issues no
  second DELETE, a moved ref rejects `--force-with-lease`, and deployed old-epoch runtimes refuse
  both union paths.
- Rollback rehearsal: use exact leases to restore `OLD_TIP` then reapply `NEW_TIP` in a disposable remote; require ref/replay/fsck parity.
- Live checks: run the Jira helper GET-only, inspect its six-action digest, then run
  `python infra/scripts/cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py --repo "$SOURCE" --manifest "$MANIFEST" --artifact-dir "$JIRA_ARTIFACTS" --execute --confirm-manifest-digest "$MANIFEST_DIGEST"`.
  Require fixed survivors plus unchanged non-targets. Two production-runtime reads must plan zero
  comment/label/link actions, perform no write, keep bytes unchanged, and reproduce the pinned plan.
- Publication: run only
  `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/tickets:"$OLD_TIP" origin "$NEW_TIP":refs/heads/tickets`.
  A fresh clone must pass replay/fsck and reject old ancestry before writers restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [non-codebase] Every known ticket writer is quiescent; checked from live workflow, queue, process, container, review-bot, service, reconciler-ref evidence. Record `writer-freeze-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=prod-writers; principal=operator; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — live runtime receipt.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The stopped AWS MCP clone equals the final live tickets OID; checked by three `git rev-parse`/`git ls-remote` reads. Record `aws-sync-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=AWS-MCP; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — live OID receipt.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The fresh source yields one independently restored bundle; checked by `git bundle verify "$BUNDLE"`. Record `backup-restore-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=isolated-clone; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — bundle receipt.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The manifest names exactly six authorized deletions plus six fixed survivors; checked by the builder plus `shasum -a 256 "$MANIFEST"`. Record `manifest-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=frozen-Git-Jira; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — manifest receipt.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Candidate replay has only the manifest delta plus epoch; checked by the whole-store oracle plus `git fsck --strict`. Record `candidate-parity-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=isolated-candidate; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — parity receipt.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Every deployed old-epoch runtime refuses both stale-union paths; checked by refusal exits with unchanged refs. Record `epoch-refusal-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=deployed-images; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — refusal receipt.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Disposable rollback reproduces `OLD_TIP`; checked by the exact-lease rehearsal plus `git fsck --strict`. Record `rollback-<UTC>`.
  provenance: environment=disposable-remote; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — rollback receipt.

- [ ] [non-codebase] Live Jira retains exactly `963510,963511,963512,963788,963789,964272`; checked by `jira-after.json`. Record `jira-cleanup-<UTC>`.

baseline.description:
## Why

"Surface the same tools we use" includes visual authoring. The existing editor already enumerates
criteria (`prompt_library.enumerate_library`, packaged + `.rebar/prompts/`), authors criterion
prompts (`create_prompt(kind=criterion)` via the `/library/create` route), and edits routing in
workflow YAML — so authoring is incremental. The one genuinely net-new piece is a **live
must-fire/must-not-fire preview**: the editor has NO prompt-execution endpoint today (its `POST`
set is `/save`, `/prompt/save`, `/validate`, `/library/create`). This is a structurally
independent deliverable (its own endpoint + spike).

## What

- Extend the editor to author a project criterion end-to-end: prompt + a **routing-fields form**
  (exec, applies_at/applies_to, block_threshold, default_posture/blocking_enabled, fail_mode) that
  writes the `.rebar/` overlay + activation, reusing `create_prompt`/`update_prompt`.
- New **`POST /criterion/preview`** endpoint (synchronous): `{criterion_id | inline(prompt+routing),
  fixture}` → `{verdict: "fire"|"no-fire", finding?: <findings.py shape>, rationale: str}`,
  reusing the story `#3` per-criterion eval runner behind the `agents` extra + credentials, with a
  **configurable timeout (default 60s)**.
- **Spike gate (resolve before committing UI):** define the pass/fail — if a single sync preview
  does not return within the timeout on the reference model, fall back to an **async job+poll**
  shape (define the job id + poll endpoint) rather than blocking the editor's `ThreadingHTTPServer`
  handler. Do not leave the sync-vs-async decision unspecified.

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` (routes), `editor_assets/` (form + preview UI),
  `prompt_library.py` (authoring reuse).
- Depends on story `#1` (overlay/activation to author into) and story `#3` (the runner the preview
  reuses).
- Reuse: `enumerate_library`, `create_prompt`/`update_prompt`, the `/library/create` route.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The editor authors a project criterion: prompt + routing-fields form writing the `.rebar/`
      overlay + `activate` list (reusing `create_prompt`/`update_prompt`).
- [ ] `POST /criterion/preview` runs a live must-fire/must-not-fire preview with the defined
      request/response contract, configurable timeout (default 60s), reusing the eval runner.
- [ ] The spike gate is resolved: a defined pass/fail threshold and a concrete async job+poll
      fallback if sync execution is infeasible in the editor's HTTP handler.
- [ ] Authoring + preview work for both an LLM criterion and a DET invariant.


## Preview dispatch, entry point & atomic authoring (remediation, run 1)

### Preview entry point — reuse the LANDED runners (clears the reuse-claim blocker)
Both halves now exist on `main`:
- **LLM criterion** (`exec: 1-TURN`/`AGENT`): the preview runs it as its Pass-1 finder over the
  fixture text via `eval_solver.run_case(prompt_id, {"input": <fixture>}, runner=…, repo_root=…)`
  (the criterion arm added in story 55b8, which wraps `passes.pass1_chunk`). Fire ⇔ non-empty
  `findings`.
- **DET invariant** (`exec: DET`): the preview resolves the criterion's `detector` selector and runs
  the grounding scan the way `plan_review/det_invariants._run_one` does (story 7f0d) — a match ⇒
  fire, an abstain ⇒ reported per `fail_mode`. (The preview scans the fixture content, not a ticket
  `file_impact`, since it is an isolated must-fire/must-not-fire probe.)

### `POST /criterion/preview` dispatch (clears the LLM-vs-DET dispatch blocker)
The endpoint reads the criterion's `exec` DIRECTLY from its routing/descriptor (NOT `exec_tier`,
which has no DET arm — per 7f0d): `exec == "DET"` → the DET path above; else → the LLM path. Request
`{criterion_id | inline(prompt+routing), fixture:{input, expect?}}` → response `{verdict:
"fire"|"no-fire", finding?: <findings.py finding shape>, rationale}`. A criterion that needs a
graph/log (container/ISF) → a clear 4xx (not runnable as an inline preview). Synchronous with a
configurable timeout (default 60s); the spike-gate fallback (async job+poll) applies only if a
single sync preview exceeds the timeout on the reference model.

### Atomic dual-write for routing-fields authoring (clears G6 atomic blocker)
Authoring a project criterion touches TWO files: `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` (the rubric, via
`create_prompt` — already atomic) and the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay routing entry.
Coordination: the criterion is only ACTIVE when it is in BOTH the routing map AND the `activate`
list (ef7e semantics). The write order is prompt-first, then a single atomic JSON overlay write
(temp-file + `os.replace`, mirroring `prompt_authoring._atomic_write`). If the overlay write fails,
the orphaned `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` is harmless (a prompt with no active routing never runs). The
overlay write itself is atomic (no half-written JSON), and adding the id to `activate` is part of the
SAME overlay write — so activation is all-or-nothing. No partial-active state is reachable.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] `POST /criterion/preview` dispatches on `exec` read directly (DET → grounding scan; LLM →
      `eval_solver.run_case` criterion arm) and returns `{verdict, finding?, rationale}` for BOTH an
      LLM criterion and a DET invariant; container/ISF → a clear 4xx.
- [ ] Routing-fields authoring writes the prompt then a single ATOMIC overlay write (temp+replace);
      a failed overlay write leaves no active criterion (activation requires the `activate` entry,
      written atomically with the routing entry).


## DET preview materializes the fixture (remediation, run 2)

`engine_b.scan` scans a repo FILESYSTEM, not an inline string — so the DET-criterion preview cannot
scan `fixture.input` directly. It materializes the fixture into a DISPOSABLE temp dir (reusing the
`eval_solver.case_store` pattern: `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` + git init), writes `fixture.input`
to a file whose name is `fixture.filename` (a new optional fixture field) — defaulting to a name the
detector's `languages`/`file_globs` accept (e.g. `preview.py` for a Python-scoped rule; a generic
`preview.txt` when unconstrained) — then runs `engine_b.scan(tmpdir, registry=<the criterion's
detector slice>)`. Fire ⇔ a `match` record on that file; an `abstain` (tool absent) → reported per
`fail_mode` (open → no-fire/skip, closed → a "coverage gap" no-fire note), never a crash. The temp
dir is removed on exit. (The LLM preview needs no materialization — `pass1_chunk` takes inline
text.) So the endpoint's DET arm = materialize→scan; its LLM arm = `run_case` over inline text.

- [ ] The DET preview materializes `fixture.input` into a temp file (named via `fixture.filename` or
      inferred from the detector's language/globs), scans it with the criterion's detector slice, and
      maps match→fire / abstain→per-`fail_mode`; a test asserts a planted violation fires and a clean
      fixture does not.
baseline.summary: Visual editor: author project criteria + live must-fire/must-not-fire preview endpoint

## Context / Problem
After S2, read/check paths use operation bindings, but live apply, Git push, ACLI/delivery, and bridge orchestration still rebuild config or reuse broad parent environments. Jira Cloud scope still has implicit `DIG` fallbacks (write path, the live access-check probe, the runtime default, and the create-time default). These paths can write under an unintended scope or leak a Rebar-materialized credential to an unrelated sibling child.

## Outcome
Cut write/apply and subprocess paths over to the S2 runtime. Add one shared child-environment builder: trusted same-capability children start from ambient inheritance, owning children receive their adapter overlay, unrelated siblings remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters, unknown native Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA variables survive, and Rebar never mutates global `os.environ`.

## Plan
1. Thread `ReconcilerSettings`, `GitRuntime`, selected `BridgeRuntime`, and the already-constructed backend through applier, mutation planning/dispatch, inbound/outbound handlers, binding updates, Git adapter/ref/lock/push, and `_bridge_runner` delivery paths. Remove their ambient `load_config`/cwd/default fallbacks.
2. Add `src/rebar/_child_env.py` with a pure environment projection API and a checked-in registry of exact secret names owned by each Rebar adapter. The registry contains names, never values; native SDK/helper chains remain ambient.
3. Ensure CLI `-c` tracker/Jira/reconciler selections cross the reconciler subprocess boundary as non-secret snapshot material. Pass static adapter material only to the exact owning process/adapter.
4. Eliminate every implicit `DIG` Jira-project default so no request (write OR live probe) uses `DIG` unless it is explicitly configured: (a) the write path `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")` in `adapters/jira/backend.py` (:200/:230/:316); (b) the live access-check probe `JIRA_PROJECT` `or "DIG"` in `access_check.py` (:72/:77/:262); (c) the `_CLOUD_PROJECT_DEFAULT = "DIG"` constant in `rebar_reconciler/runtime.py` (:46); and (d) the create-time `_DEFAULT_PROJECT = "DIG"` in `_store/project_ensures.py` (:50). Each unset case fails closed with a typed/redacted pre-mutation (or pre-probe) error; `DIG` is used only when `JIRA_PROJECT`/config is explicitly `DIG`. Preserve existing retry, rate-limit, TLS, output, partial-failure, idempotency, and ticket-delivery behavior unless a test names the approved delta.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- End-to-end verified-fake Cloud/DC runs cover create/update/comment/link/delete/inbound apply plus Git commit/push/delivery under custom tracker dir/branch/remote with ambient resolvers poisoned after composition.
- Child-process contract tests assert unknown ambient/native-chain variables survive; the owning overlay appears only for its child; unrelated siblings lose other adapters' exact declared names; argv/URL/log/output contain no secret sentinel.
- Concurrency tests run distinct operations with different overlays and timeouts, asserting `os.environ` is byte-equal before/during/after and no cross-operation value is observed.
- Failure-injection tests cover missing project/auth, revoked credential, TLS error, retry/rate-limit exhaustion, provider partial failure, and delivery failure; existing provider-neutral output and recovery/idempotency oracles remain authoritative.
- A red test demonstrates each current `DIG` default (write path AND the live access-check probe); green asserts zero provider mutation and no probe request targeting `DIG` when write scope is absent.

## Compatibility / rollback
Until bounded-live validation, a compatibility facade may invoke the legacy write path. Before cutover, rollback selects it. After any new snapshot-aware caller ships, rollback requires the S1 envelope-compatible floor. Ticket, event, bridge, and binding formats remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Verified-fake Cloud/DC apply plus Git/delivery paths complete with ambient resolvers poisoned and use the configured tracker directory/branch/remote and explicit project scope.
- [x] Missing Cloud write scope produces a typed/redacted pre-mutation failure and no request uses `DIG` unless `DIG` was explicitly configured.
- [x] Same-capability child tests preserve unknown Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA variables, owning children receive only their overlay, and unrelated siblings omit every other adapter's exact declared secret name.
- [x] Concurrent-operation tests prove no global environment mutation and no cross-operation credential/config observation.
- [x] Existing retry, rate-limit, TLS, output, partial-failure, recovery, and idempotency scenarios retain their provider-neutral behavior except explicitly approved deltas.
- [x] Disabling the write facade restores the legacy path before cutover; no stored ticket/event/bridge/binding format changes.

baseline.description:
# Generalize the lag-free snapshot overlay to unscoped reconcile passes

## Context
Bug f449 (seagreen-fortuitous-crayfish) fixes a narrow inbound stale-clobber window on the DC rich-text lane by refreshing SCOPED bound-present keys via a lag-free direct GET (get_issue_by_rest) before both differs and baseline advancement, so a post-write pass reading a stale JQL-search snapshot cannot mirror a stale value back over local (the bound-field inbound differ, inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local, is LEVEL-triggered with no baseline).

## Gap
The f449 overlay is guarded to SCOPED passes only, to bound the direct-GET volume. Full, UNSCOPED production reconcile passes remain theoretically exposed to the same stale-inbound-clobber if a pass runs while the search index still lags a very recent rebar write. In production, passes are spaced far enough apart that the index normally catches up, so the practical risk is low -- but the level-triggered inbound path has no formal guard.

## Proposed work
Refresh only the AMBIGUOUS candidate keys on unscoped passes: keys where the search snapshot presents local==baseline AND snapshot-remote!=baseline (i.e. a field that looks like a remote edit but could be a stale echo of our own recent write). Direct-GET those keys, merge the mirrored scalar fields into curr_snapshot, then arbitrate on the lag-free value. This bounds GET volume even for unscoped passes (only genuinely-ambiguous keys) while closing the window for all passes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unscoped passes refresh ambiguous candidate keys (local==baseline AND remote!=baseline) via
      a lag-free GET before both differs and baseline advance.
- [ ] A held-out oracle proves an unscoped pass does not clobber local under a stale post-write
      snapshot, with bounded GET volume (only ambiguous keys refreshed).
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green.
baseline.summary: Generalize lag-free snapshot overlay to unscoped reconcile passes (unblock inbound stale-clobber window)

ROOT CAUSE (proven, cited).

Symptom: pointing a model class at a local OpenAI-compatible server via the documented per-class endpoint — TOML 'trivial = { model=..., provider="openai", endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1" }' or env REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_ENDPOINT=... — fails at run time with 'openai.OpenAIError: Missing credentials' (pydantic-ai's stock OpenAIProvider), instead of using rebar's OpenAI-compatible builder (which supplies api_key='not-needed' and withdraws supports_json_schema_output).

Mechanism: ClassSlot.endpoint is parsed (src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py _parse_slot, with dedicated env vars REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_ENDPOINT) and documented (docs/llm-framework.md), but the ONLY consumer of any '.endpoint' is build_fallback_model (model_classes.py:403), which reads t.endpoint from FALLBACK targets only and hardcodes the PRIMARY candidate's endpoint to None. resolve_class / resolve_model_string return only 'provider:model', discarding the slot endpoint. Every op collapses the class onto cfg via replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(CLASS)) (enrich.py:82, epic_bug_screen.py:109, overlap/judge, plan_review, completion, code_review, workflow/runs), so cfg.base_url stays None. In runner.run, ProviderSession(cfg) then does NOT register the openai builder (it is registered only when cfg.base_url is set), so the primary takes the is_resolvable() lazy-string branch (runner.py ~381) and Agent(model_string) is built by pydantic-ai with no provider_factory -> stock OpenAIProvider -> requires OPENAI_API_KEY -> fails.

Authoritative contract violated: docs/llm-framework.md documents the per-class endpoint recipe as a working way to reach a local server, and the env table lists REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_ENDPOINT as 'per-class OpenAI-compatible endpoint'.

Only working recipe today: top-level REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL (registers the builder + flips signed tier to best_effort). VALIDATED end-to-end against a local MLX server: enrich() returned a valid ticket_digest in ~35s.

FIX (planned): at the single chokepoint runner.run — mirroring fallback_targets_for(resolved) — look up the slot whose primary resolves to 'resolved' and, when cfg.base_url is unset, apply that slot's endpoint to cfg.base_url so the builder registers, provenance records the host, and the tier flips to best_effort uniformly. RED->GREEN with a runner-level test.

ACCEPTANCE: a class slot / REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_ENDPOINT with provider=openai and NO REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL routes the primary model through rebar's OpenAI-compatible builder (no OPENAI_API_KEY required); provenance base_url is set and tier=best_effort; existing base_url and fallback-endpoint behavior unchanged.
baseline.summary: Per-class model-class endpoint (REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_ENDPOINT / slot endpoint) is dropped for the primary model

## Summary
--exclude-deleted exists on the CLI only; the library and MCP list_tickets cannot exclude deleted tickets — an interface-parity gap.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. CLI: rebar list --include-archived --exclude-deleted -> works (deleted dropped).
2. Library: inspect.signature(rebar.list_tickets) -> no exclude_deleted parameter; MCP list_tickets likewise.
3. _reads.list_tickets hardcodes exclude_deleted=False.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the three interfaces expose the same list filters (parity is the project's stated contract).
- Actual: library/MCP callers cannot express the filter at all.

## Source
- src/rebar/_reads.py:94-96 (hardcoded False)
- src/rebar/__init__.py:300-322; src/rebar/mcp_server.py:145-167 (missing kwarg)
- CLI flag: src/rebar/_engine/rebar:89

## Fix direction
Thread exclude_deleted: bool = False through _reads.list_tickets -> library list_tickets -> MCP tool; add the missing parity case to tests/interfaces (the suite does not cover this flag today — close that coverage gap with the fix).

## Suggested RED test
Same store containing a deleted ticket; all three interfaces with the flag on and off -> identical results (CLI is the oracle).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] exclude_deleted available on library + MCP, default matching current behavior (False)
- [ ] Interface-parity test covers the flag (RED first)
- [ ] list_tickets outputSchema/docs updated

# The deterministic child-closure proof is computed, then hidden from the verifier

The completion precheck already computes, deterministically and exactly, whether every direct child of a parent is closed and certified — `child_closure_findings(ticket)` returns `(blocking, uncertified)`. For epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] this is measured as `blocking=0, uncertified=0`: hard proof that all 59 descendants are closed AND carry certified signatures.

That proof is then **collapsed to a single boolean** (`certifiable`) at `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:132` and routed only to the `reconcile` step. **Nothing about it reaches the verifier's prompt** — `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml` wires only `context` into the `decide@then/verify` step.

## Why it matters

Epics routinely write an acceptance criterion of the form *"every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit"* (e369's criterion #1, verbatim). The verifier is handed that criterion with **zero evidence**, and it has no tool that can reach the answer:

* the **closure/certification half** is already proven deterministically one step earlier and is
  discarded;
* the **Gerrit half** (`Verified +1`) is not obtainable from the repository at all — no read-only
  repo tool can query Gerrit.

So the verifier must either guess, or follow its own instruction (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md:150-151`: *"If, after a bounded search, you cannot find evidence that a requirement is met, record what you searched and treat it as NOT MET"*) and FAIL a criterion that is in fact satisfied and was **already proven satisfied by deterministic code in the same workflow run**. That is a false FAIL on a gate that SIGNS its verdict.

It also wastes budget: the verifier spends tool calls hunting for evidence that no tool can produce.

## Discovered from

[rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] — while root-causing why e369's completion verification never reaches a verdict. Recorded there and in [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a]'s RCA as the most likely route to a genuine FAIL even once the run does reach a verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the deterministic child-closure/certification result (counts, and the ids of any — build_child_closure_evidence() injects counts + uncertified ids into context INSIDE the <untrusted_ticket_context> fence (mirrors the epic_bug_screen block).
      unclosed/uncertified children) is surfaced to the completion verifier as evidence, inside the
      existing fenced-context delimiter so it keeps the prompt-injection boundary
- [x] a criterion of the form "every child is closed" can be resolved from that evidence without the — The block states 'N direct children; all closed & certified' or lists unclosed/uncertified ids, resolvable without a tool call.
      verifier making a tool call
- [x] the Gerrit half (`Verified +1`) is explicitly addressed: either evidence is supplied, or the — completion_verifier.md (trusted) tells the verifier the Gerrit Verified+1 half is out of repo-tool reach and not to FAIL solely for it when closure+cert is proven.
      verifier is told plainly that this half is out of reach so it does not silently FAIL on it
- [x] a test pins that the evidence appears in the verify step's inputs and that its content matches — tests/unit/workflow/test_child_closure_evidence_6ec8.py pins the evidence appears in the verify step context and matches child_closure_findings (RED->GREEN, mutation-checked).
      what `child_closure_findings` returned
- [x] no change to the deterministic short-circuit: an UNCLOSED direct child must still block with no — AC5 regression asserts an unclosed direct child still short-circuits (run_verify=False, no LLM); short-circuit code untouched.
      LLM call
baseline.summary: Child-closure proof is computed deterministically then hidden from the completion verifier

baseline.description:
The completion-verification close gate fails to produce a verdict — and therefore **blocks closing any work ticket** (fail-closed) — when the completion-verifier LLM returns its structured output as a top-level JSON **list** instead of the expected `completion_verdict` object. The LLM is available and the call runs; the failure is in parsing/validating its response shape, not in the ticket's actual completion state.

Discovered while trying to close the five `idea`-status stories after they merged to `main` (epic jira-reb-686). Reproduced deterministically across 3 attempts on `81b4-985e-b3e8-4026`; the same gate runs for every work-ticket close, so it is not specific to that ticket.

## Exact error

```
Error: cannot close 81b4-985e-b3e8-4026: completion verification could not run
(completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify'
failed: structured output must be a JSON object, got list). The completion-verification
gate is enabled (verify.require_completion_verification_for_close); install the 'agents'
extra and set a model API key, or override with --force-close="<reason>".
```

## Where it happens (code map)

- **Raised at** `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:179`, in `validate_to(model_cls, data)`:
  when the parsed structured output is not a `dict` it raises
  `StructuredOutputError("structured output must be a JSON object, got {type}")` —
  here `type == list`.
- **Existing partial handling** `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:168-175`: a *single*-element
  list wrapping one object (`[ {...} ]`) is already unwrapped to `{...}` (prior fixes
  "artsy-chain-hold / dash-lure-slag"). A **multi-element list, a list of non-dicts, or
  an empty list is still rejected** — that is the case hit here.
- **Failing step** `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml`, step
  `decide` → `then` → `verify`: `prompt: completion-verifier`, `mode: structured`,
  `output_schema: completion_verdict`.
- **Expected contract** `completion_verdict` = `{verdict: "PASS"|"FAIL", findings: [...]}`
  (see `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` `_OUTPUT_SCHEMA = "completion_verdict"`,
  `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py:156`, and the citation shape in
  `src/rebar/llm/findings.py`).
- **Model/runner** verifier default model `claude-sonnet-4-6`
  (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:41` `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`); structured runner is
  pydantic_ai (same as plan-review).

## Root-cause hypothesis

The verifier model emitted its answer as a **top-level JSON array** rather than the wrapping verdict object — most likely a bare findings array (`[{finding}, {finding}, …]`) or a per-criterion list, instead of `{verdict, findings: [...]}`. `81b4` carries **13 `## Acceptance Criteria` checkboxes**, which may nudge the model toward returning a per-criterion list. The single-element unwrap at `structured.py:174` does not cover a multi-element / non-`[{}]` list, so `validate_to` rejects it, the `verify` step produces no verdict, and the fail-closed gate blocks the close.

Open question: whether the **layer-4 bounded retry** (the StructuredOutputError message is meant to be fed back to the model for one retry) is actually wired on the workflow `mode: structured` runner path (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py` / `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`). The failure was **deterministic across 3 close attempts**, which suggests either the retry is not firing on this path, or the model reliably repeats the list for this context.

## Missing diagnostic (do this first next session)

The raw LLM output is **not surfaced or persisted** on this failure path — the CLI close does not emit a `run_id`/trace, so we cannot see the exact list the model returned. The first troubleshooting step is to **capture the raw model output** (e.g. add temporary logging in `validate_to`/the structured runner, or run `rebar verify-completion 81b4-985e-b3e8-4026` directly if that surfaces the payload) to confirm whether it is a bare findings array, a per-criterion list, an empty list, or a multi-element wrapper.

## Reproduction Steps

1. On a checkout with the `[agents]` extra + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, and
   `rebar.toml` `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close = true` (this repo's
   default).
2. Take any `in_progress` work ticket whose criteria are genuinely met (e.g.
   `81b4-985e-b3e8-4026`, now merged to `main`).
3. Run `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed`.
4. Observe the close is refused with the "structured output must be a JSON object, got
   list" error above. Deterministic across retries.

- Expected: the completion verifier returns a `completion_verdict` object; a PASS closes
  (and signs when certifiable), a FAIL blocks with per-criterion findings.
- Actual: the verifier's structured output is a JSON list; `validate_to` rejects it; the
  gate produces no verdict and fail-closes, blocking the close entirely.

## Impact

Because the gate is fail-closed, this blocks closing **every** work ticket whenever the verifier returns a list — the only escapes are `--force-close="<reason>"` (closes **unsigned/uncertified**) or disabling the gate. It blocked closing all five idea-status stories and the epic (jira-reb-686) after they merged.

## Candidate fixes to evaluate (not yet chosen)

1. **Capture + log** the raw model output on `StructuredOutputError` (diagnosability first).
2. **Verify/repair the retry**: ensure the bounded retry with the "must be a JSON object"
   feedback actually fires on the workflow `mode: structured` path; strengthen the retry
   prompt to demand the `{verdict, findings}` wrapper.
3. **Prompt hardening**: make the `completion-verifier` prompt explicitly require a single
   top-level object and never a bare array.
4. **Bounded structural repair (careful)**: if the output is a list of finding-shaped
   dicts, wrap as `{verdict: FAIL, findings: [...]}` (non-empty) — but this changes
   semantics and must not mask a genuine PASS; evaluate against the completion-verifier
   eval spec (`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/completion-verifier.eval.yaml`) before adopting.

## Environment

- nava-rebar 0.7.1; local build at commit 4ca9d8211 (idea-status stack tip; the same gate
  code is on `main`).
- Gate config: `rebar.toml` `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close = true`.
- Verifier model: `claude-sonnet-4-6` (VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL); pydantic_ai runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The raw completion-verifier LLM output for a reproducing case is captured and
      recorded (what list shape it returns).
- [ ] The completion-verification gate produces a valid `completion_verdict` when the
      model returns a list-shaped answer — either via a robust retry that recovers the
      `{verdict, findings}` object, prompt hardening that prevents the list, or a
      safe bounded repair — without masking a genuine PASS or FAIL.
- [ ] `structured.validate_to` (or the structured runner) handles the non-single-element
      list case deterministically (documented behavior + unit test), rather than only the
      `[{one dict}]` case.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the "got list" verifier output and asserts the gate now
      yields a verdict (or a deterministic, documented outcome).
- [ ] Closing a genuinely-complete work ticket with the gate enabled succeeds (verified on
      one of the idea-status stories or an equivalent).
- [ ] `make lint` and the affected tests pass.

## 2026-08-08 duplicate consolidation

Duplicate reports: `2ede-2459-90ce-4b19` and `d7d8-0fad-d0f9-436b`.

Fresh resolution experiment on current `origin/main`: the structured-output tests drove the former list-shaped completion-verifier payloads through `validate_to` / `parse_structured`, including a one-object top-level array, a sole verdict object mixed with non-object noise, and the captured leading-array-noise shape. Result: `3 passed`. Each experiment returns a real verdict rather than the former deterministic `got list` failure.
baseline.summary: Completion-verifier gate fails closed on list-shaped LLM structured output ('got list')

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The op-cert service does per-job boto3/SSM/region lookup and patches process-global key/principal/push state — coupling app config to one secret store, letting jobs observe different keys, and creating concurrency/cleanup hazards. ADR 0098 keeps SSM as a deployment storage option but moves application binding to startup.
## Outcome
At startup accept exactly one of preferred `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` or compat `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY`. Validate before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, copy into a process-owned 0700 dir/0600 file, build one immutable signer/runtime, and pass signer/principal/push policy context-locally to jobs. The process never rereads; restart observes replacement.
## Plan
1. Replace `opcert_service.ssm`/per-job key acquisition with startup composition in config/key-provider/app. Reject missing, both-set, unreadable, non-regular, malformed, encrypted/passphrase, or non-Ed25519 input before service work. The path source (`REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`) also needs a 0600-or-stricter regular-file check. Both are copied to the process-owned 0700/0600 location, mode-checked after copy.
2. Copy key bytes to a process-owned runtime dir/file at 0700/0600; never modify/delete the deployment source. Graceful shutdown removes only Rebar's copy; deployment tmpfs/restart owns crash cleanup.
3. Replace global environment/state patching with a typed context-local signer, principal, and push policy threaded through jobs/workspace/signing. Concurrent/timed-out workers cannot observe or mutate one another's context.
4. **Thread the immutable signer through the out-of-`opcert_service/` producer seams (BOTH job kinds).** Key/principal are read from `os.environ` in `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py` (`ensure_opcert_key`→`REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`; `opcert_principal`→`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID`; both called by `mint_opcert_record`). Both producer chains converge on `signing._sign_manifest_under_lock` (calling `mint_opcert_record`): (a) COMPLETION — `transition_close.py:sign_completion_verdict`→`signing.sign_manifest`; (b) PLAN-REVIEW — `attest.py`→`generation.sign_manifest` (via `_sign_manifest_under_lock`). Convert `mint_opcert_record` (the terminal `os.environ` reader, via `ensure_opcert_key`/`opcert_principal`), `_sign_manifest_under_lock`, both `sign_manifest` entrypoints, and `sign_completion_verdict` to accept+forward an optional `OpcertSigner` binding (signer-key-handle + principal); the service supplies its startup-bound context-local signer to BOTH job dispatches, so removing `keyprov.py`'s `os.environ` patching (today binding the key for both kinds) cannot silently break either path. Developer-local close/review-plan callers pass no binding, keeping the env/genesis default. Also route the push-policy site (`_push_mode`/`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH`) to the context-local policy when bound, env default otherwise.
5. Decouple the op-cert APPLICATION runtime from SSM/region: remove `REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM` and the key-retrieval `AWS_REGION`/`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` from the opcert service env in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, drop the app-runtime boto3 need in `infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert`, and materialize the key OUTSIDE the app before start via `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`. Mirroring the `rebar-bot-signing-key` precedent, `fetch-secrets.sh` writes the SSM value to a 0600 FILE next to `.env` (always created, empty when blank, per bug beb1) and exports only its PATH; the opcert compose service bind-mounts that file `:ro` and sets `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` to it (file-path source authoritative; inline `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` unused in the hosted deploy). The shared `/rebar/prod/*` SSM grant `ssm_params_read` in `iam.tf` (co-used by origin-guard/gerrit, no opcert app-role) is NOT dropped.
6. Preserve ADR 0049's Ed25519/DSSE algorithm, trust roots/eras, producer, authoritative fetch, envelope persistence, guard, and no-workspace-push invariants.


## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Startup component tests instrument queue, worker, network, and workspace factories and assert every invalid source fails before all four.
- Filesystem tests assert source untouched, process dir 0700, copy 0600, stable bytes after source replacement, restart observes new bytes, and cleanup removes only the copy.
- **Signer-seam tests** assert BOTH producer chains (completion `sign_completion_verdict`→`signing.sign_manifest`; plan-review `generation.sign_manifest`; both via `_sign_manifest_under_lock`→`mint_opcert_record`) sign from the passed binding (not `os.environ`) when the service supplies one — proven with a distinct injected key while `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`/`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` are unset — and no-binding resolves via env/genesis (regression pin).
- Concurrent/timed-out job tests use distinct principals/policies and prove context isolation, immutable startup signer, and no workspace push remote.
- Structural tests assert `src/rebar/opcert_service` has no boto3/SSM/region import or runtime parameter, the opcert compose env carries no `REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM`/region, the image needs no runtime boto3, and `fetch-secrets.sh` materializes the key to a 0600 `:ro`-mounted file with `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` (iam.tf grant untouched).
- [operator-attested] Hosted signing canary records deployment/run ids, source kind (never value), signature verification, restart result, modes, and redacted failure outcome.

## Compatibility / rollback
Expand deployment input first while the legacy per-job facade exists; pre-removal rollback selects the legacy facade, post-removal rollback needs the same startup source contract (signatures/envelopes stay compatible).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Exactly-one source validation rejects every named invalid case before queue, worker, network, or workspace construction.
- [x] The process-owned copy is 0700/0600, stable for process lifetime, observes replacement only after restart, and cleanup never alters the deployment source.
- [x] Concurrent and timed-out jobs prove context-local signer/principal/push isolation, one immutable startup signer, existing signature verification, and no workspace push remote.
- [x] Both out-of-`opcert_service/` signing producer chains — completion (`_opcert_signing.py`, `signing.sign_manifest`+`_sign_manifest_under_lock`, `transition_close.py:sign_completion_verdict`) and plan-review (`generation.py:sign_manifest`, `attest.py`) — sign from the injected context-local binding when the service supplies one (to BOTH job kinds), and the developer-local close/review-plan paths retain prior env/genesis resolution unchanged (regression pinned).
- [x] The op-cert application runtime (`src/rebar/opcert_service` process/container) has no SSM/boto3/region/key-parameter dependency: the compose service carries no `REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM`/key-retrieval region, the image needs no runtime boto3, and the key is materialized before start by `fetch-secrets.sh` to a 0600 file bind-mounted `:ro` with `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`. The shared `/rebar/prod/*` instance-role SSM grant in `iam.tf` is deliberately UNCHANGED (co-used by origin-guard/gerrit, not an app-role).
- [x] Secret/key sentinels are absent from repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, children, and persisted envelopes beyond the existing public signature.
- [x] [operator-attested] Hosted signing/restart/tmpfs canaries pass with the required redacted evidence recorded.
  provenance: environment=AWS-hosted op-cert/review signing service + GitHub Actions CI; principal=deployed op-cert Ed25519 startup signer + review-bot production principal; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Gerrit 1850 PS4 (cd443da568): AWS review bot LLM-Review +1 (live hosted signing, verified) and CI Verified +1 (S6 held-out oracle over the new code: restart-only replacement, 0600 copy, context-local isolation, both producer chains); PASS, no key material; full redacted evidence in the operator-attestation comment on this ticket.
baseline.summary: RP-04 S6 — Move op-cert signing material to startup bindings

## Context
F09 found `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key` and `MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY` in deployment documentation, Terraform, secret-loading scripts, and a restore runbook. No compose or application consumer appeared in the repository search. Closed infrastructure tickets record why the secret was introduced, but ADR 0049 replaced gated HMAC signing with environment-attributed Ed25519 operation certificates. Removal must follow an evidence-based compatibility and deployment assessment.

Known paths include `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`, `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`, `infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md`, `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`, and `infra/terraform/user_data.sh`.

## Plan
- Trace every producer, transport, and consumer of the parameter and environment variable.
- Compare the current deployed service contract with ADR 0049 and the operation-certificate key path.
- Determine whether any supported rollback, migration, or generic HMAC consumer still requires the secret.
- Propose retention, deprecation, or removal with an exact file and deployment impact.
- Do not remove infrastructure before operator approval.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every repository reference and runtime consumer is identified (checked: the assessment comment reproduces the full match list from `grep -rn "MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY\|mcp-hmac-signing-key" .` with a producer/transport/consumer/doc classification for each).
- [x] The originating closed tickets and superseding ADR decisions are cited (checked: the assessment comment names the introducing story tickets, ADR 0049, and `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`).
- [x] The recommendation states the compatibility consequences of removal.
- [x] The recommendation states the rollback consequences of removal.
- [x] The recommendation states the secret-rotation consequences of removal.
- [x] Any remediation proposal has a bounded file and deployment impact (an explicit file list and the deployment steps it implies).
- [x] No infrastructure is changed during the assessment (checked: `git status --porcelain infra/ docs/` is empty at close).

## Verification
- `grep -rn "MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY\|mcp-hmac-signing-key" --include="*" .` — every non-`.git` match must appear in the assessment comment with a classification.
- `grep -rn "MCP_HMAC" src/ tests/ scripts/` — proves the absence (or presence) of an application-runtime consumer.
- `git status --porcelain infra/ docs/` — empty output proves the assessment changed no infrastructure or documentation.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Five modules derive "where is `.rebar` / the sidecar directory for this store" independently: `src/rebar/_store/hlc.py:80` (resolves symlinks), `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:65` (resolves after bug `intangible-ladyish-vicuna`), `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:57` (resolves after `13f78e3165`), `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py:104`, `src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:257`; `src/rebar/_store/push_state.py:89-116` parses `.git` by hand for the git dir and `src/rebar/_store/sync.py:281-301` re-derives the git common dir for quarantine. Three of these had the unresolved-symlink bug in turn (`nuclear-calm-heron`, `intangible-ladyish-vicuna`, `conscious-weighable-spittlebug`), each fixed one site per ticket.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_store/paths.py` with one frozen `StorePaths(tracker)` exposing `canonical` (realpath), `git_dir`, `git_common_dir`, `rebar_dir`, `sidecar(name)`, `log(name)`; every derivation above becomes a call. The class is the only place `os.path.realpath` is applied to a tracker path for sidecar purposes, so an unresolved derivation cannot be re-copied. A guard test asserts no module outside `paths.py` computes `dirname(tracker)`/`.rebar` joins for sidecars (token scan on `"/.rebar"` joins plus `_rebar_dir` definitions, owner excluded, `# store-path-ok:` marker escape).


## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_store/paths.py` (new), `src/rebar/_store/hlc.py`, `src/rebar/_store/push_state.py`, `src/rebar/_store/sync.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py`, `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py`, `src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py`, `tests/unit/store/test_store_paths.py` (new).

## Testing
Happy path: a symlinked worktree tracker resolves every sidecar under the canonical store (real `tmp_path` symlink). Edge: a tracker whose `.git` is a gitfile (worktree) yields the common dir. Pinning: `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py`, `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`, `tests/unit/test_hlc.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_pending_marker.py`, `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py` pass unchanged.

## Parallel git-dir derivations: enumerated and scoped (review remediation, G1G2)
`push_state._git_dir` is NOT the only `.git`-gitfile parser. Two more exist and are **explicitly OUT of scope for this leaf**:
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:70` `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` — same isfile/`gitdir:`/isdir
  parse, but returns `""` on failure. Consumers: `fsck_scan.py:146`, `fsck_repair.py:415`,
  `fsck_recover.py:193`, `bridge_repair.py:51`, `tracker_maintenance.py:101`,
  `gitutil.py:276,357`.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py:156` `_gitdir` — same parse, returns `None` on failure.

Rationale for deferring: the three implementations carry **three different failure sentinels** (`<tracker>/.git`, `""`, `None`), so unifying them is a behaviour-changing decision about which sentinel wins at ~9 call sites across the fsck/repair surface — not the mechanical collapse this leaf performs, and outside this leaf's recorded file impact. Two of those call sites are monkeypatch seams (`tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py:77`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py:86`). Tracked as follow-up work under the parent epic rather than smuggled in here.

## Convergence status (review remediation, G7 — parent epic's convergence clause)
No latent divergence is converged by this leaf; every collapsed site already resolves symlinks **at its composite**, verified by reading each call site:
- `hlc.py:83` — resolves (`Path(tracker).resolve().parent`).
- `compact_trigger.py:78` — resolves (via `_canonical_tracker`).
- `enrich_drain.py:70` — resolves (via `_canonical_tracker`).
- `queue.py:270` — **resolves**, via a function-local import of
  `enrich_drain._canonical_tracker`.
- `doctor_locks.py:115` — the helper itself does a bare `dirname`, but its **only** caller
  (`doctor_locks.py:335`) passes an already-canonical tracker computed one line earlier at
  `:334` (`canonical = _lock.canonical_tracker(tracker)`). The composite therefore already
  resolves, so routing it through `StorePaths` preserves behaviour rather than converging a
  divergence.

Because no site changes behaviour, the clause's "add a test pinning that site's new canonical-resolution" obligation is discharged by pinning that the behaviour is UNCHANGED: the end-to-end test drives all five real sites on a symlinked worktree and asserts every artifact already lands in the one canonical `.rebar`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `grep -rn "def _rebar_dir" src/rebar` returns only `src/rebar/_store/paths.py`; checked by the guard test and the grep.
- [x] The guard's **join-scan** branch is proven, not just its definition-count branch: a line joining `".rebar"` to a `dirname(`/`.parent` step anywhere under `src/rebar` outside the owner is flagged, and a `# store-path-ok: <reason>` marker suppresses it while a reason-less marker does not; checked by the guard's own unit tests.

# Workflow-engine remediation: unify LLM functionality on the engine, restore visual editing, document intended use

## Context

Captures the remediation-on-top-of-the-engine scope that surfaced finalizing the
plan-review gate. The original long-form scope-capture prose (workstream catalog +
research notes) is preserved in this ticket's EDIT HISTORY and in the re-triage
COMMENTS below; this body is the current, executable state. Related: engine epic
`hump-seam-spice` (e6d9, closed), gate epic `messy-moose-jig` (5fd2, closed),
three-pass epic `sheer-myth-idol` (9da1).

## Current scope & disposition (2026-06-27)

The historical workstreams are RESOLVED; this is the authoritative current state:

- DONE via closed sibling epics — WS-INTENT-ALIGN, WS-MIGRATE, WS-PROMPTS, WS-CLEANUP,
  WS-VISUAL, WS-VALIDATE: delivered by epic A `sage-votary-logic` (5766), epic B
  `peak-fir-hilt` (72d5), and engine epic e6d9. The earlier open-ended decision
  investigations (DSL map/fan-out, exact cleanup set, visual-format choice) were

- SPLIT OUT — WS-VISUAL-EVAL is moved to its own epic `yip-gem-teak` (7013); OUT OF
  SCOPE here.
- REMAINING (this epic's only live deliverables) — WS-DOC and WS-EVAL-EXISTING,
  decomposed into child stories `seek-ditch-corgi` (WS-DOC) and `rink-cloud-gum`
  (WS-EVAL-EXISTING; task children: scorer registry + dataset schema, the 3 specs,
  the live solver + fixtures, and the run_eval/CI wiring).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/workflow-engine.md` exists, is linked from README and the CLAUDE.md doc index, and separates a CLIENT (run/use) audience from a REBAR-DEV (author/edit) audience.
- [ ] `docs/workflow-engine.md` documents the YAML DSL, scripted-vs-agentic steps, the agent-vs-single-turn bright line, the three-pass review pattern, and the eval seam (two-tier model, how the live tier is triggered, cost + fork-safety rails); it cross-links rather than duplicates docs/llm-framework.md and docs/plan-review-gate.md.
- [ ] Eval specs exist for `completion-verifier`, `ticket-quality`, and `spec-alignment` under `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`, each passing `validate_eval_spec` with a cross-family judge (gates:false), `at_least(k)` over explicit epochs, a coverage threshold, and a non-empty gold_set.

- [ ] `eval-discipline` CI validates all packaged specs on every PR with no model call; offline unit tests assert dataset balance and a non-empty gold_set.
- [ ] `eval-live` CI runs on workflow_dispatch plus a weekly schedule, is non-blocking (continue-on-error), response-cached, concurrency-capped, and fork-safe (no live call on fork PRs or Dependabot); provider spend-cap guidance is documented.
- [ ] Every child ticket of this epic is closed (each signed by the completion-verifier gate).
- [ ] A new contributor can read `docs/workflow-engine.md` and correctly decide when to author a workflow vs a bespoke op, and how to run and trigger evals, without reading source.

## Context / Problem

Escaped-bug analysis (`cranial-goodly-seahog`) found four regressions where a newly added hard-fail CI gate/floor/cap broke branches already in flight or predating the gate: `medium-loved-newt`, `impudent-sodium-ferret`, `rancid-aerophobic-skylark`, and `brattish-ladyish-jaguar`. rebar's code-review gate has no criterion asking whether a branch created *before* a pipeline/gate change would now fail, so ungrandfathered gates land review-clean.

## Approach

Ship a project-owned **advisory** code-review criterion `project.ci-gate-compat`, following the existing `project.review-phase-boundaries` dogfood pattern — routing in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, rubric in `.rebar/prompts/`, corpus in `.rebar/evals/`, documented under `docs/llm-framework.md` "Project dogfood" — so the shipped gate never carries this project's invariant. The rubric asks a CI-agnostic question: "does this pipeline/gate-configuration change introduce a hard-fail step or required gate with no if-present/grandfather guard, so a branch created before this change would fail?"

Trigger it through the **declarative `applies_to` glob seam** the routing index already defines (`applies_to_globs` / `glob_triggered_overlays` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py`), never a hard-coded `.github/workflows/**` test in Python: a CI-vendor-specific code path would break `project.portability`'s support-matrix cell "CI under any provider … projects with NO CI provider at all". Adding a CI system is then adding a glob, not editing code. Shipped globs: `**/.github/workflows/**`, `**/Jenkinsfile*`, `**/.gitlab-ci.yml`, `**/.circleci/**`, `**/azure-pipelines*.y*ml`, `**/.buildkite/**`, `**/bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `**/.drone.yml`.

Two code changes are required because activated project code-review criteria are today injected **unconditionally**: `_activated_code_review_project_criteria` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`) returns every activated `project.` id and `CodeReviewBatchRunner.run` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py`) dispatches each in the Round-A fan-in with no reference to `applies_to`.

1. **Gate project criteria on their globs.** Filter activated project criteria by their
   effective `applies_to` globs against the review's changed files — already threaded to the
   call site as `prep.dc.changed_files` in `gate_dispatch.py` — reusing `registry._glob_match`
   (delegating to `rebar._engine_support.commit_impact.glob_match`). An **empty** `applies_to`
   keeps today's always-on behaviour, so `project.review-phase-boundaries` is unchanged.
2. **Make the glob set project-overridable.** A routing entry may declare
   `applies_to_config_key`, a dotted config path whose non-empty list value **replaces** that
   criterion's `applies_to`. `project.ci-gate-compat` declares `code_review.ci_config_globs`;
   a new core section `[code_review]` gains `ci_config_globs: list[str]`, modelled on
   `CodeHealthConfig.scan_roots` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`) and its `_SECTIONS` entry
   (`src/rebar/_config_sections.py`). The pointer is declarative, so the shipped package never
   names a project-owned criterion id and an unusual pipeline is *declared* by the project.

This reuses the two mechanisms rebar already has for this job (the criteria overlay and the `applies_to` glob trigger) rather than adding a new trigger kind. Ship **advisory** (`default_posture: advisory`, `blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.90`) so it is calibrated on real reviews first; flipping it to blocking is out of scope here.

## Scope

- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — the `code_review` entry + `activate`.
- `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.md` — new Pass-1 rubric.
- `.rebar/evals/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.eval.yaml` — balanced corpus: fire cases
  `CG-F1`–`CG-F6`, pass cases `CG-N1`–`CG-N6`, matching gold set.
- `.gitignore` — two `!`-unignore lines beside the existing phase-boundaries ones.
- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` — `"code_review"` in `_SECTIONS` using `_as_str_list`.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — `CodeReviewConfig` dataclass with the `# read-via:` marker
  `scripts/check_config_reads.py` requires, wired into `Config` + `_SECTION_CLASSES`.
- `src/rebar/config.py` — re-export `CodeReviewConfig`.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — `project_applies_to_globs(criterion_id, repo_root)`
  via `config.compose_config(repo_root)` (the seam already used in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pin_health.py`, keeping `check_config_ownership.py` clean).
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — glob-filter the activated project criteria; the
  call site passes `prep.dc.changed_files`.
- `docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/config.md` — dogfood section, config key.
- `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — the key and its canonical env var.
- `tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py` — new offline contract tests.

## Testing

All offline (no live model call): assets asserted as data, dispatch through the existing injected-runner seam.

- **Happy path** — changed files including a pipeline-config path select
  `project.ci-gate-compat`; the rubric loads via `prompts.get_prompt`; the eval spec passes
  `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` and is balanced 6/6.
- **Negative path** — changed files touching no pipeline-config path drop
  `project.ci-gate-compat` (the recording runner sees zero dispatches for its prompt id) while
  `project.review-phase-boundaries` (empty `applies_to`) is still dispatched.
- **Config-override path** — with `ci_config_globs = ["ci/pipeline.yaml"]`, `ci/pipeline.yaml`
  selects the criterion and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not (replace, not extend); unset,
  the shipped globs apply.
- **Empty edge** — an empty changed-file list drops every glob-gated project criterion.
- **Calibration** — `calibrate_criterion` over the new corpus with an injected perfect solver
  reports `recall == 1.0` and `false_accept == 0.0`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `code_review.registry.effective_criteria(<repo root>)` contains `project.ci-gate-compat`
      and its routing entry reads `exec: "1-TURN"`, `default_posture: "advisory"`,
      `blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.90` — asserted in the new test.
- [ ] The routing entry's `applies_to` is exactly the eight globs listed in Approach, and
      `grep -rn "github/workflows" src/rebar/` adds no new match — asserted in the new test.
- [ ] The rubric loads with `outputs == "code_review_findings"` and
      `execution_mode == "single_turn"`, and its body contains none of `github`, `gitlab`,
      `jenkins`, `circleci`, `buildkite`, `bitbucket`, `drone` (case-insensitive).
- [ ] A review whose changed files include a pipeline-config path dispatches the
      `code-review-project-ci-gate-compat` prompt and one whose files include none does not,
      while `project.review-phase-boundaries` is dispatched in both.
- [ ] `[code_review] ci_config_globs = ["ci/pipeline.yaml"]` makes `ci/pipeline.yaml` select the
      criterion and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` not select it — asserted in both directions.
- [ ] `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) == []`, the dataset is twelve cases split 6 fire /
      6 pass, and the perfect-solver `calibrate_criterion` run reports `recall == 1.0` and
      `false_accept == 0.0`.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` has a "Project dogfood: ci-gate-compat" section naming the
      advisory posture and the `CG-F1`/`CG-N6` bounds, `docs/config.md` documents
      `[code_review] ci_config_globs`, and `tests/golden/config_surface.json` lists
      `code_review.ci_config_globs` + `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_CI_CONFIG_GLOBS`.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `... make typecheck` exit 0, and
      `... python -m pytest tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py
      tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py
      tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py
      tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` exits 0.
baseline.summary: Add code-review ci-gate-compat criterion (new hard-fail gates must grandfather in-flight branches)
