## Problem
The reconciler active-set query hardcodes status != "Done" as the only Done-equivalent (fetcher.py jql_active / jql_done_recent). The code comment admits it: "A project whose workflow adds another closed-equivalent status would need this to move to statusCategory != \"Done\"". Against a live CLIENT Jira whose workflow uses Closed / Resolved / Cancelled (common), issues in those statuses are NOT "Done", so:
- jql_active pulls Closed/Resolved issues into the active working set -> the reconciler
  treats resolved issues as active and may push outbound mutations at them.
- jql_done_recent misses them, so they never populate the recent-Done snapshot.
This mis-scopes the entire active set for any non-DIG/REB workflow.

## Approach
Switch the Done predicate from the literal status = "Done" to Jira's status CATEGORY: statusCategory = Done / statusCategory != Done, which is workflow-agnostic (every Jira status maps to one of To Do / In Progress / Done categories, including custom Closed/ Resolved/Cancelled statuses which map to the Done category). Keep the JQL builders' per-project scoping and _validate_project_key unchanged. Verify ACLI/JQL supports statusCategory (it does on both Cloud and DC).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] jql_active excludes any status in the Done statusCategory (not just literal "Done").
      Verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/ -q`.
- [x] jql_done_recent selects the Done statusCategory, ORDER BY updated DESC, cap preserved.
      Verified by the same test command.
- [x] Single-project + multi-project fan-out unchanged otherwise; DIG/REB (To Do/In Progress/
      Done only) behavior is identical. Verified by the same test command.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/ tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py -q`
  — JQL-builder unit tests assert the statusCategory predicate on jql_active / jql_done_recent
  for single- and multi-project fan-out (no live Jira; JQL strings asserted directly).
  RED first: a test encoding a client workflow with a "Resolved" status shows the OLD
  `status != "Done"` query would include Resolved in the active set (bug), and the NEW
  `statusCategory != Done` query excludes it.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_paging_split.py -q` — guards the
  650-line fetcher.py size target.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` from the worktree.

## Sequencing
Edits fetcher.py jql builders AND tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetch_multi_project.py (plus the fetch/ and orchestrate/ JQL-string tests), which ticket A also edits — this ticket is SEQUENCED AFTER ticket A (a01d). Rebased onto A's landed change.
baseline.summary: Reconciler: scope active/done by statusCategory not literal status=Done (support Closed/Resolved client workflows)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

An MCP client cannot see CLI stderr, so the cross-session warning must ride in the **structured tool response** of single-ticket MCP tools. rebar already carries exactly this kind of advisory in structured responses: `WriteAckOut.description_warning` (`src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:212`, populated via `_ack(..., description_warning=...)` at `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:60`). This story mirrors that pattern with a dedicated cross-session field on the single-ticket write and read responses, and leaves bulk-read tools untouched.

Depends on the detector (`cross_session_warning_for`, sibling story) and the reducer clearing.

## Approach

Add a `cross_session_warning: str | None = None` field to the response models used by single-ticket MCP tools: `WriteAckOut` (`src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:196`) for single-ticket writes, and `TicketStateOut` (the model `show_ticket` returns, `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:221`) for the single-ticket read. Populate it from `cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, ...)` in the corresponding single-ticket handlers in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` / `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` (extend the shared `_ack` helper to accept and thread the value, matching how `description_warning` is threaded). Because the field defaults to `None`, the `outputSchema` gains an optional property and existing clients are unaffected (additive, back-compatible).

**Compute the warning BEFORE the underlying mutation runs.** The advisory must reflect the ticket state **at operation time**, so each handler calls `cross_session_warning_for` first (reading the live holder), then performs `rebar.<op>(...)`, then attaches the pre-computed string to its response. Reading after the mutation would, for a state-changing op, race the very field (`claimed_session`) the warning is about.

The single-ticket MCP tools whose response model carries the field via `_ack` / `TicketStateOut` are: the read `show_ticket` (`TicketStateOut`) and the writes `comment_ticket`, `edit_ticket`, `tag_ticket`, `untag_ticket`, `set_file_impact`, `set_verify_commands`, `archive_ticket`, `link_tickets` (primary `id1`), `unlink_tickets` (primary `id1`) — all of which build their ack through the shared `_ack` helper.

**`transition_ticket` and `reopen_ticket` are also covered** — they are the core single-ticket lifecycle mutations, so epic AC3 ("single-ticket-targeted operations on MCP") requires them. They return the raw engine result `dict` (`{ticket_id, from, to, newly_unblocked}`) rather than `WriteAckOut`, so the warning rides as an **additive `cross_session_warning` key on that dict** (present only when non-`None`; computed before the transition applies). This is additive and back-compatible — existing keys are untouched.

The bulk read tools — `list_tickets`, `search`, `ready_tickets`, `next_batch` — do **not** populate the field. `claim_ticket` is excluded for the same reason as the CLI story (an already-`in_progress` ticket fails the atomic claim before any warning).

**Accepted scope limits (documented, follow-up filed as `discovered_from` this story).** `check_ac` and `quality_check` return `GateResultOut` — they are `READ_ONLY` gate-verdict tools, not the mutation the feature targets, and they share one model with unrelated tooling; `declare_no_file_impact` returns a bare `"ok"` `str` whose schema would have to change type (a breaking, non-additive change). These three are deferred to the follow-up; the CLI surface already warns on the corresponding verbs, so the signal is not lost system-wide.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py` — add `cross_session_warning: str | None = None` to
  `WriteAckOut` and `TicketStateOut`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — thread the value through `_ack` and populate it (computed
  before the mutation) in the single-ticket `WriteAckOut` write handlers; add the additive
  `cross_session_warning` key to the `transition_ticket` and `reopen_ticket` dict returns.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — populate it in the `show_ticket` handler.
- `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` — add the generated note describing the new optional field
  (the source of truth for `docs/mcp-reference.md`, which a CI stale-doc gate checks).
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` — document the new optional response field on the single-ticket
  tools (including the additive dict key on transition/reopen) and the deferred trio.

## Testing

Tier: **contract test** — drive the real MCP handler functions in-process and assert on the validated response model (test-design §3 "producer/consumer shape mismatch": the real handler produces the model through real `model_validate`). Use a real temporary tracker and set the acting session via `REBAR_SESSION_ID`.

- With a ticket held by session A and acting session B, call the `show_ticket` handler and a
  single-ticket write handler (e.g. `comment_ticket`); assert the returned model's
  `cross_session_warning` is a non-empty string naming holder `A`.
- With an A-held ticket, call `transition_ticket` as session B (e.g. `in_progress ->
  blocked`); assert the returned **dict** carries a `cross_session_warning` key naming holder
  `A`, and that the transition still applied (the mutation is not gated by the warning).
- Negative control (same session): acting as A, assert `cross_session_warning is None` (model
  field) and that the `transition_ticket` dict omits the key (or maps it to `None`).
- Bulk exclusion: the `list_tickets` / `ready_tickets` responses have no populated
  cross-session field for A's `in_progress` ticket.
- Unset-id silence: with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, the single-ticket handlers return
  `cross_session_warning is None` (and the transition dict omits the key).
- Schema check: the tool's advertised `outputSchema` includes the optional
  `cross_session_warning` property (asserted against the generated schema), and a default
  response (no mismatch) still validates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `show_ticket` and a single-ticket write handler (`comment_ticket`) return a model
  whose `cross_session_warning` names holder `A` when acting as session B against an
  A-held ticket (checked by an in-process MCP contract test under `make test`).
- [x] `transition_ticket` as session B against an A-held ticket returns a dict carrying a
  `cross_session_warning` key naming holder `A`, and the transition still applies (checked by
  an in-process contract test asserting both the key and the post-transition state).
- [x] Negative control: acting as session A, `cross_session_warning is None` on the model
  handlers and the `transition_ticket` dict does not carry a non-`None` warning (checked by
  the same test).
- [x] `list_tickets` / `ready_tickets` responses do not populate a cross-session warning for
  A's `in_progress` ticket (checked by a bulk-exclusion assertion).
- [x] With `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, single-ticket handlers return `cross_session_warning is
  None` (checked by an unset-id assertion).
- [x] `WriteAckOut` and `TicketStateOut` `outputSchema` expose the optional
  `cross_session_warning` property and existing (unset) responses still validate (checked by
  a schema/model-validation assertion).
- [x] `docs/mcp-reference.md` documents the field (checked: `grep -n "cross_session_warning"
  docs/mcp-reference.md` matches).
baseline.summary: MCP: carry cross_session_warning in single-ticket tool responses

## Context / Problem
Five approved prose upgrades to the implement-side skill and the shared test-design doc, targeting the largest escape classes: parity siblings at build time, config read-but-miswired, op-level contention semantics, gate findings fixed without oracle upgrades, and known gaps evaporating at close. (Bug-trend review changes 18-22; enforcement twins deliberately not proposed where FP modes dominate.)

## Approach
All prose, no new gate machinery: (18) SKILL.md 4a surface-parity census, defined self-contained here (no equivalent exists yet in rebar-debug to inherit; sibling ticket 78f1 adds the debug-side analog independently): when the change touches one of several parallel surfaces, enumerate five slots — CLI / MCP-API / library-facade / automated-callers / dual-direction (reconcile read+write) — each slot dispositioned in-scope-and-proven-through-that-surface or out-of-scope-with-reason (feeds the Phase-5 sweep). (19) test-design.md §6 config-effect contrast: for each config key the change reads or should read, one test proving the key CHANGES BEHAVIOR through the real read path (default vs non-default contrast), not merely that a value is parsed — targets the read-but-miswired class (9d7a: honored by MCP server, ignored by comment tool). (20-prose) SKILL.md contention triggers, narrowed to op-level semantics (case c): if the change (i) composes >=2 locked operations or check-then-act across store reads/writes, (ii) adds its own retry/backoff/reclamation logic, or (iii) introduces a cache/snapshot over store state — add contention cases to the EXISTING shared suites by shape: composed/check-then-act writes -> tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py (two_clones fixture); write-storm/retry-reclamation -> tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py (storm suite); read-integrity-under-contention (shape iii, the ed2b class) -> tests/interfaces/store/test_reads_under_sync_contention.py via the shared tests/interfaces/store/sync_contention_harness.py. 'Never a bespoke harness' means reuse these shared fixtures/harnesses — it does not claim no read-contention harness exists. Changes riding existing seams (single locked op) are exempt. (21) SKILL.md 4g gate-finding oracle upgrade: a behavioral gate finding gets a RED test FIRST in the same amended change, then the fix; non-behavioral (naming/docs/style) fixed directly — exemption stated to prevent change-detector tests. (22) Phase 5 + Reporting residual-gap disposition sweep over an enumerable source checklist (4a census out-of-scope slots, 4b exclusions, 4e-bis compromises, deferred 4g advisories): each item filed (ticket + discovered_from) / accepted-with-reason / fixed; 'none' legitimate.

## Scope
- examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md (4a, contention trigger block, 4g, Phase 5, Reporting)
- examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md §6 (+ sync of per-skill copies enforced by tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py)

## Testing
Prose-only: skill sync test must stay green (test_skill_shared_sync.py); dry-run read-through of the census + contention triggers against two historical bugs (9d7a config-miswire; ed2b pagination-under-writes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All five prose blocks landed at the named anchors; no new gate machinery introduced.
- [x] Contention trigger text scopes to the three case-c shapes and routes each shape to its existing shared suite by path (two_clones / storm / reads-under-sync-contention harness).
- [x] Shared test-design.md copies in sync (test green).
- [x] Census slots and disposition checklist use forced-artifact wording (in-scope-proven / out-of-scope-reason / filed / accepted / fixed).

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The ownership-direction gate `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` (created by slice C1, ticket 29a9-3cf7-3ded-42d8) and the existing field-consumption gate `scripts/check_config_reads.py` are only useful if they run on every change through a portable trigger that needs NO CI provider, with CI as a mirror. Today `scripts/check_config_reads.py` runs ONLY as a standalone "Config-read gate" step in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (wrapped in the ee2a if-present tree-skew guard), and `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` runs nowhere. rebar must work with diverse CI providers or no CI provider, so the primary trigger must be the portable local `make lint` path.

## Outcome
The `lint` target in `Makefile` runs BOTH `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and `python scripts/check_config_reads.py`. Because CI already runs `make lint` (the `_SHARED_GATE_SIGNATURES` "make lint" entry, asserted present in `_build-and-test.yml` by `test_ci_workflow_parity.py`), CI runs both gates THROUGH that one `make lint` step — so the now-redundant standalone "Config-read gate" workflow step is REMOVED (its coverage moves to `make lint`), which also eliminates the double-run that would occur if both the standalone step and `make lint` invoked the field-consumption gate.

## Design decisions (resolving the double-run / lost-skip-guard tension)
1. **Single source = `make lint`.** Both gate invocations live in exactly one place: the
   `lint` target. CI inherits them via its existing `make lint` step; no CI step invokes
   either gate directly, so neither gate runs twice per job.
2. **The ee2a if-present guard is no longer needed and is dropped with the standalone
   step.** That guard let a Gerrit patchset predating `check_config_reads.py` pass. Under
   `make lint` the equivalent protection is INHERENT: CI runs the PATCHSET's own `Makefile`,
   and a patchset predating this slice has a `Makefile` without these invocation lines, so
   `make lint` simply does not run the gates — no missing-file failure, and the gate
   re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change. This is strictly MORE portable
   (operation-linked to `make lint`, not CI-only).
3. **The existing CI-wiring guard is re-anchored, not duplicated.**
   `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py::test_ci_wires_the_gate` currently
   greps `_build-and-test.yml` for `check_config_reads.py`; since the invocation moves out
   of the workflow into `make lint`, that test is updated to assert the `Makefile` `lint`
   target wires the field-consumption gate (it would otherwise red on the removed step).

## Plan
1. Add `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and `python scripts/check_config_reads.py`
   to the `lint` target in `Makefile`.
2. Remove the standalone "Config-read gate" step (and its ee2a if-present guard) from
   `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`.
3. Re-anchor `test_check_config_reads_heldout.py::test_ci_wires_the_gate` to assert the
   `Makefile` `lint` target contains `check_config_reads.py`.
4. Extend `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`: assert the `Makefile` `lint` target
   contains BOTH gate invocations AND that CI still runs `make lint` (the existing shared
   signature) — so removing either gate line from the Makefile, or removing `make lint`
   from the workflow, fails the parity check (fed synthetic edited copies).

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- A parity test asserts that removing the ownership-gate invocation from a synthetic copy
  of the Makefile `lint` target fails the check, and likewise for the field-consumption
  gate; and that a synthetic workflow copy dropping `make lint` fails (so CI cannot silently
  stop running the gates it inherits).
- `make lint` executes both gates and remains green on the current tree (with C1's
  populated legacy-exception set).
- The gates run under `make lint` with NO CI provider present (portable path), proving the
  trigger is operation-linked, not CI-only.
- The re-anchored `test_ci_wires_the_gate` passes against the Makefile.

## Dependency
Depends on slice C1 (ticket 29a9-3cf7-3ded-42d8), which creates `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and its legacy-exception set; AC3's greenness on the current tree requires C1's exception set. The `depends_on` edge C2->C1 is recorded.

## Compatibility / rollback
Wiring-only; no product-code change. Rollback restores the standalone workflow step, reverts the Makefile additions, and restores the original `test_ci_wires_the_gate` anchor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The `Makefile` `lint` target executes both the ownership-direction gate
  (`scripts/check_config_ownership.py`) and the field-consumption gate
  (`scripts/check_config_reads.py`); CI runs both through its existing `make lint` step, and
  the standalone "Config-read gate" workflow step is removed (no double-run).
- [x] The workflow-parity tests fail if either gate invocation is removed from the Makefile
  `lint` target, or if `make lint` is removed from the workflow.
- [x] `test_check_config_reads_heldout.py::test_ci_wires_the_gate` is re-anchored to the
  Makefile and passes.
- [x] `make lint` runs both gates with no CI provider present (portable/no-CI path) and
  remains green on the current tree.
baseline.summary: RP-04 S7.2 — Wire ownership + field-consumption gates into make lint + CI parity

baseline.description:
# A bug closed as a DUPLICATE withholds its parent's certification forever, with no non-force remedy

## The two halves of the gate disagree

**The close path grants dispositions an exemption.** `_commands/transition_close.py:253-260`:

> A duplicate / not-a-bug / escalated bug with a durable replacement relation is a disposition, not
> a claim that this ticket's acceptance criteria were implemented. Skip the completion-only checks
> (including file-impact and the billable verifier) [...]

So `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class duplicate` returns exit 0 and mints **no** `completion-verifier` attestation. That is correct and deliberate: a duplicate never claimed to implement its own ACs, so verifying its completion would be meaningless (and billable).

**The certification path does not honor that exemption.** `llm/completion.py:170-199` (`child_closure_findings`) requires a valid `completion-verifier` attestation on **every** closed direct child, with no disposition branch. A disposition-closed child therefore lands in `uncertified`, and `gate_ops.py:131`'s `certifiable = not uncertified` withholds the parent's signature.

## Why this is a trap, not merely an inconvenience

The two rules are each individually right and compose into a state with **no non-force exit**:

* the child cannot earn an attestation — reopening and re-closing takes the same exemption branch
  every time, so the outcome is identical on every attempt;
* `--force-close` produces exactly the uncertified state the operator ruling prohibits;
* the only other escapes are dishonest: pick a close class that is not the true disposition, delete
  the true `duplicates` link, or de-parent the child so it leaves `children`. Each makes the tree
  certify by misrepresenting it.

## Live instance, with the substance intact

Epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb` (Jira DC support). Child `0059-c7f0-cce1-4077` is a true duplicate of `23ed-de0a-765b-49aa` — the same defect diagnosed to its actual cause, fixed and merged as change
1124. Measured just now:

```
child_closure_findings('e369-a449-4773-48fb')
  UNCERTIFIED: child 0059 is closed but its completion closure is not certified/valid
               (signature: unsigned)
verify_signature('23ed-de0a-765b-49aa', kind='completion-verifier') -> certified
```

**The replacement is certified AND is a direct sibling under the same epic.** So the work IS attested inside this tree; the gate simply will not look through the `duplicates` edge to find it. The epic is denied certification over a bookkeeping gap, not a missing verification.

## Candidate remedy — NOT to be applied without an operator ruling

Teach `child_closure_findings` the same disposition branch the close path already has: when a closed child carries a disposition class (`duplicate` / `not_a_bug` / `escalated`) **and** a net-active replacement link to a live ticket, resolve certification **through** that link — certified iff the replacement's own closure is certified-and-valid — rather than demanding an attestation the child is exempt from producing. `_has_live_replacement_link` already implements the predicate, so both halves could share one definition instead of drifting.

**Why this is an operator ruling and not an agent's call:** it changes when a parent close is certifiable, which is gate semantics — the same class of decision as the degrade-open remedy on [rebar:1019-e1e9-5117-4795] and [rebar:2a76]. A wrong call here either keeps blocking honest closes or lets an unattested subtree certify by pointing at an unrelated ticket. Recording it rather than fixing it unilaterally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the operator rules on whether disposition-closed children resolve certification through their
      replacement link, or must remain uncertified by design — **RULED: attest them.**
- [x] `child_closure_findings` and the close gate share ONE definition of "disposition with a live
      replacement": `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` is asserted equal to
      `close_precheck._NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` — verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py`
- [x] a disposition close MINTS a `completion-verifier` attestation, and its manifest does NOT claim a
      completion PASS that never happened (it reads `DISPOSITION <class>` + the replacement id)
- [x] the negative case still holds: NO live replacement link ⇒ no attestation, so the close keeps
      normal verification and `--class duplicate` cannot become a bypass
- [x] `--force-close` remains UNSIGNED — its guard runs before the disposition branch, mutation-checked
      by reverting the guard's position and observing the test fail
- [x] the wiring is exercised through the REAL `_completion_precheck`, not only the module in isolation
      (the call site moved during bug 74a3's split; a piece-only suite stayed green through the move)
- [x] end-to-end: `verify_signature(0059, kind="completion-verifier")` returns `certified` and epic
      e369's uncertified descendant count drops from 2 to 1

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py -q      # 17 passed
    pytest tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py \
           tests/unit/test_transition_close.py -q                        # 59 passed
    make lint && make typecheck                                          # clean

Mutation checks performed (a guard asserted without a demonstrated RED is unverified):

* force-close ordering — moved `if force_close: return None` AFTER the disposition branch;
  `test_a_force_close_is_still_never_signed_even_for_a_linked_duplicate` FAILS. Restored: passes.
* call-site wiring — reverted the disposition branch to `return None`;
  `test_the_precheck_ACTUALLY_returns_the_disposition_verdict` FAILS. Restored: passes.

End-to-end verification was run against the real store (reopen → claim → close `--class duplicate`), producing the manifest recorded in the FIXED-738A-B comment.
baseline.summary: Certification path ignores the disposition exemption: a duplicate-closed child withholds its parent's signature with no non-force remedy

## Problem
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py` recognises only a closed set of environment-read forms when it scans `src/rebar` to build `docs/env-vars.md`. At `scripts/gen_env_registry.py:98` it matches `func.attr == "get"` (plus the `os.environ[...]` subscript and `os.getenv` forms). Any OTHER expression that reads an environment variable is invisible to it.

The consequence is silent documentation loss on a refactor that looks entirely harmless. Changing

```python
value = os.environ.get("REBAR_SOMETHING")
```

to

```python
value = os.environ.pop("REBAR_SOMETHING", None)
```

still reads the variable, but the generator no longer sees it, so the key DISAPPEARS from `docs/env-vars.md`. Nothing about the edit signals that documentation was dropped.

## Evidence
Observed 2026-08-20 while implementing `illusory-patronal-giraffe` (op-cert credential hardening). The natural implementation of that ticket was exactly the `get` -> `pop` swap. It silently reduced the generated registry from **161 keys to 160**, dropping `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` — the very variable the change was about.

The implementer worked around it rather than absorbing a generator fix: the read stays an `os.environ.get` with a literal key, and the pop is a SEPARATE statement. That is the correct scope call for that ticket and it is not in question here — but it leaves the generator blind spot in place, and the next person to write a `pop`-based read will hit it without the same luck.

## Why the current gate does not protect you
`make lint` does NOT catch this. The staleness check only fires in the full suite, via `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys`.

So the feedback loop is: make a reasonable one-token edit, see `make lint` pass locally, and learn about the dropped documentation from CI — or not at all, if the same change happens to regenerate the file. This is the same shape as the complexity-ratchet divergence recorded on `dystopian-bardlike-basil`: a local gate that is weaker than CI, teaching contributors to trust a signal that does not hold.

## Investigation before choosing a remedy
Establish first which env-read forms actually occur, or plausibly could, in `src/rebar` — `pop`, `setdefault`, an `os.environ` alias bound to a local name, a `dict(os.environ)` copy, indirect reads through a helper. The remedy should be sized to what the codebase realistically uses, not to every expression Python permits.

Candidate approaches, to be decided on evidence:
- Widen the recogniser to the read-bearing method set (`get`, `pop`, `setdefault`, …) rather than
  the single `get`.
- Make an UNRECOGNISED `os.environ` attribute access a loud generator error rather than a silent
  skip, so a novel form fails the build instead of quietly dropping a key. This is the fail-closed
  option and is likely stronger than enumerating methods, since it catches forms nobody predicted.
- Have `make lint` run the generator's `--check` so the local and CI verdicts agree.

The second and third are complementary: fail-closed recognition plus a local gate that actually reports it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A `pop`-based environment read in `src/rebar` is REGISTERED in `docs/env-vars.md` — proven by
      a test that performs the read one way, regenerates, and asserts the key is present; and that
      FAILS against today's generator.
- [x] An `os.environ` access the recogniser does not understand causes a LOUD failure (generator
      error or a failing check), not a silent omission. Proven with a deliberately novel form.
- [x] The local and CI verdicts agree: a tree whose generated registry is stale fails
      `make lint`, not only the full suite. If that is judged too slow for the lint path, record
      why and name where the earlier signal comes from instead.
- [x] `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` remains present in `docs/env-vars.md` (key count does not regress
      from 161), guarding the specific instance that exposed this.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` pass, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.

## Provenance
Discovered 2026-08-20 during `illusory-patronal-giraffe`; the generator behaviour at `scripts/gen_env_registry.py:98` and the 161→160 key drop were both observed directly, not inferred.
baseline.summary: gen_env_registry recognises only os.environ.get, so a pop-based read silently drops its key from docs/env-vars.md

baseline.description:
Normalize the force-bypass surface so `--force[=<reason>]` is the single approved pattern across `transition` and `claim`, consistently across the externally-exposed surfaces (CLI + library) AND the internal module/method naming, and remove the redundant `force_close`.

Operator rulings (2026-08-18): `--force[=<reason>]` is the universal approved pattern — the audit reason is tightly coupled to the force operation, so it rides on `--force`, NOT a separate `--reason`; `force_close` is to be removed; blast radius is limited to `transition` + `claim` (tracker-maintenance / init / gates keep their own `--force` conventions and are out of scope).

## Context / Problem
`claim` already has the target shape: lib `claim(force: str | None = None)` where the value IS the audit reason (bare CLI `--force` -> "(no reason given)", `--force=<reason>` -> that reason). `transition` diverges: lib `transition(force: bool, reason: str, force_close: str | None)` splits the one concept across a bool `force`, a separate `reason`, and a redundant `force_close` str; and the transition CLI additionally lets `--reason` stand in as the force-bypass audit note (transition.py help ~lines 42-46, 59-63) — a coupling `claim` does not have. Internally the single concept "the force-bypass reason" is spelled four ways: `force_reason` (CLI `_parse_flags`), `force_close` (lib param), `force_close_reason` (txn.py plumbing + a PERSISTED `status_data` key), and `force_plan_review` (claim_compute).

## Approach
Make `transition` match `claim`'s canonical shape and unify the internal names.
- Lib: change `transition` to `force: str | None = None` (the audit reason; None = not forcing; any string incl. "(no reason given)" = force, bypassing whichever gate THIS transition hits — start-work OR completion-verify close). REMOVE the `force: bool` and `force_close` params. `reason` remains ONLY for its close_reason role (reason-required non-force closes); it no longer doubles as the force-bypass note.
- Migration: a legacy `rebar.transition(force_close="<r>")` call WARNs via the sanctioned lib-kind deprecation alias (rebar._deprecations `_KINDS` includes `lib`) and maps to `force="<r>"`; a legacy `force=True` maps to `force="(no reason given)"`.
- CLI (transition.py): keep the `--force[=<reason>]` shape (already present); the force note comes from `--force=<reason>` else "(no reason given)" — DROP the `--reason` fallback for the force note so it matches `claim` (reason stays for close_reason only). Bare `--force` -> "(no reason given)" exactly as `claim`.
- Internal naming: unify the IN-MEMORY spelling of the concept to `force_reason` across transition (`_parse_flags`, `transition_compute`, the txn.py param) and claim (`claim_compute`'s `force_plan_review` -> `force_reason`), with no behavior change. KEEP the PERSISTED `status_data["force_close_reason"]` key name unchanged — it is durable reduced state; renaming it is an event-schema migration and is out of scope. Add a short comment noting the persisted key is intentionally retained.
- Reducer/schema (reducer/_processors_status.py, schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, types.py) UNCHANGED: historical events (incl. the `force_close_reason` status field) keep reducing to the same state.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_lib_writes.py — `transition`: `force: str | None`, drop `force: bool` + `force_close`; deprecation-map legacy force_close/force(bool) via _deprecations.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition.py — map `--force[=<reason>]` -> `force` str; drop the `--reason`-as-force-note fallback; adopt the unified `force_reason` name; update usage/help text.
- src/rebar/_commands/txn.py — thread the unified `force_reason` in-memory name; RETAIN the persisted `force_close_reason` status key.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py, close_precheck.py — key the close bypass on `force is not None` (was `force_close`), recording the force reason as the audit note.
- src/rebar/_commands/claim.py + claim_compute — rename `force_plan_review` -> `force_reason` (internal only); the `claim` lib shape is already correct.
- src/rebar/_deprecations.py — register the lib `force_close`/`force(bool)` deprecation alias.
- Guidance/help text for transition + claim IS in scope: src/rebar/_commands/gates.py (~302-303) currently prints TWO spellings in one override hint — `claim --force="<reason>"` AND the decoupled `transition --force --reason="<reason>"`; unify BOTH to `--force[=<reason>]`. Reconcile the txn.py override hints (~554, 602, 618: `--force="<reason>"`) and the transition.py usage/help so every transition/claim guidance string shows only the `--force[=<reason>]` pattern (no `--reason`-as-force-note wording).
- OUT OF SCOPE: tracker-maintenance, init, and the gates break-glass `--force` conventions for OTHER commands; the MCP surface (sibling scratchy-leprous-galago); the argparse refactor (sibling churlish-fruited-dassie).

## Testing
- `transition ... --force` (bare) bypasses the gate with note "(no reason given)"; `--force="x"` records "x"; byte-identical to `claim --force` / `--force=x` (interface tests on BOTH verbs assert the same fallback).
- `transition ... closed --force` bypasses the completion-verify/signature close gate (same closed-without-signature outcome as today's force-close); `--reason` on a force close is NOT used as the force note (behavior-change test).
- `rebar.transition(force_close="x")` and `rebar.transition(force=True)` WARN via _deprecations and behave as `force="x"` / `force="(no reason given)"` (unit tests).
- A historical event carrying `force_close_reason` still reduces to the identical ticket state (reducer fixture test).

## Acceptance Criteria

## Context / Problem
Twenty-seven bugs in the fortnight defect review were tests that could not fail or that burned CI time: absent-string subprocess oracles with no return-code check (`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`, `1241-b83c-f8c7-40bf`), a test burning the full 120 s Jira readiness budget per xdist worker (`e394-9433-c839-4c9f`), a timeout oracle expiring after its watchdog fires (`9bb7-4430-1202-4d93`). All closed.

State of the tree:

- `pytest-timeout==2.4.0` is pinned at `pyproject.toml:251`.
- `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` sets `addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"` but no `timeout` / `timeout_method` / `timeout_func_only`, so `make test` and bare local `pytest` have no per-test budget. Only 4 `@pytest.mark.timeout` marks exist tree-wide (`test_review_bot.py:1806`; `test_opcert_service_app.py:158,206,268`).
- The budget lives only on CI command lines: `_build-and-test.yml:658` (default tier) and `:673` (integration tier), both `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`.
- Ruff 0.16.3 selects `E,F,W,I,UP,B,BLE001,T201,SIM115,ASYNC,DTZ,RUF` with `ignore = ["RUF001","RUF002","RUF003"]`; no `PLW1510`, no `PT`. `make lint` runs `ruff check $(sources)`, `sources = src tests scripts` (`Makefile:13`).
- `scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py` and `check_raw_git_writes.py` exist, run in CI only (`_build-and-test.yml:181-198`), are absent from `make lint`, and both exit 0 today.

Backlog (`ruff check --statistics src tests scripts`): **PLW1510 = 336, zero fixes even under `--unsafe-fixes`**; **PT = 1811**, only 37 safely auto-fixable — PT018 1513, PT011 84, PT019 69, PT006 57, PT001 37, PT022 19, PT017 15, PT007 7, PT013 4, PT008 2, PT021 2, PT012 1, PT028 1.

Runtime: `pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal -q --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` ran 11 m 16 s, 5097 passed, **zero** `Failed: Timeout` (the 6 failures + 4 errors were the environmental "repo HEAD moved" guard). The `timeout=120..300` values in test sources are subprocess ceilings, not durations: the unit tier already fits inside 20 s. The integration tier is not yet measured.

Operator decision (2026-08-21): adopt only common practice in maintained OSS projects; a 20 s per-test budget with an explicit override for tests that must be slow.

## Approach
1. **Ruff, per code.** Add the eleven codes in the first AC's selector to `[tool.ruff.lint] select` — 481 findings, cleared here. `PT018`/`PT011`/`PT019` (1666) are deliberately NOT selected; the `select` comment says so in place. PLW1510 is cleared with explicit `check=False` where the call already inspects `returncode`, `check=True` only where an unchecked non-zero exit is a bug.
2. **Local budget in the ini.** Add the three keys in the fourth AC to `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`.
3. **Mark the slow integration tests.** Measure that tier at `--timeout=20`, then give each over-budget test `@pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)` with a one-line comment naming why. No exemption without a comment.
4. **Lower, do not drop, the CI flags.** `_build-and-test.yml:658` and `:673` go `--timeout=300` -> `20`, keeping `--timeout-method=thread`.
5. **Drift guard.** One new assertion in `test_ci_workflow_parity.py`: the `--timeout=` on those two steps equals the ini `timeout`.
6. **`make lint` reachability.** Append both hygiene scripts to the `lint` recipe, as `check_comment_hygiene.py` was by task `2d9a-78c5-5f87-4a22`. No `if [ -f ]` guard: `make lint` runs the patchset's own Makefile.

Not adopted (no maintained tool does it): lints for subprocess `timeout=`, `sleep` budgets, `os.environ.copy()`, `sys.modules` writes, foreign `.git/` writes.

## Constraints
- **PT codes go in `select`, never `ignore`.** `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py:73` (`test_ruff_ignore_is_exactly_the_ruf_unicode_deferral`) asserts `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore == ["RUF001","RUF002","RUF003"]` exactly, and `test_ruff_lint_has_no_extend_ignore` forbids `extend-ignore`, so selecting a family then silencing most of it fails CI. Per-code selection is the project's own precedent: the `[tool.ruff.lint]` comment records "We take SIM115 only, not the wider SIM group".
- **`--timeout=` must not be removed from any workflow.** `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:718` (`test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`) sweeps every workflow pytest step and requires both `--timeout=` and `--timeout-method=thread` (`89d5-61da-b621-47f8`, `d835-1846-95d1-4d84`). Dropping them so the ini applies turns that guard red.
- **Eleven other `--timeout=` lanes stay untouched**, each calibrated for external / live-service / eval suites that run for minutes: `external-integration.yml:245,405,514,625,765`, `_optionality.yml:140,165`, `_eval-discipline.yml:74`, `test.yml:144`, `structured-output-baseline.yml:117`.
- **PLW1510 is not test-only.** 318 of the 336 sit under `src` + `tests`; `make lint` covers all three trees.
- **The ini mechanism is verified**, so only the marking sweep is open: the three keys are real `parser.addini` options in pytest-timeout 2.4.0, and on this venv they time out an unmarked 25 s test under `--strict-config` and pass the same test marked `timeout(60, func_only=True)`.
- Marking precedes lowering: step 3 before step 4.

## Scope
`pyproject.toml` (ruff `select`; pytest ini keys); `Makefile` (`lint`); `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (`:658`, `:673`); `tests/**` + `src/**` + `scripts/**` (the PLW1510 and selected-PT backlog); `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` (drift assertion); `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` (new); `docs/local-dev-env.md` (budget + override).

Reviewed, NOT changed: `test_ruff_ratchet.py`; the nine other workflow lanes; the two hygiene scripts.

## Testing
`tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` holds both arms: a ~25 s test marked `timeout(60, func_only=True)` that passes, and a negative arm running `pytest` on a generated temp test in a subprocess with no `--timeout`, asserting a `Timeout` failure (a permanently red test cannot be committed). Pinning: `test_ruff_ratchet.py`, `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` and the two hygiene-lint tests stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
All commands run from the worktree with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"` prepended.
- [x] The adopted codes are clean tree-wide. `ruff check --select PLW1510,PT001,PT006,PT007,PT008,PT012,PT013,PT017,PT021,PT022,PT028 src tests scripts` exits 0; today it exits 1 with 481 findings.
- [x] They are configured, not passed ad hoc. `python -c "import tomllib; s=tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['tool']['ruff']['lint']['select']; assert 'PLW1510' in s and 'PT001' in s"` exits 0. Today: `AssertionError`.
- [x] `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore` is unchanged. `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py -q` exits 0 (pinning).
- [x] The budget lives in the ini. `python -c "import tomllib; p=tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['tool']['pytest']['ini_options']; assert p['timeout']==20 and p['timeout_method']=='thread' and p['timeout_func_only'] is True"` exits 0. Today: `KeyError: 'timeout'`.
- [x] Both budget arms hold under the ini alone. `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py -q` exits 0. Today pytest exits 4.
- [x] The two CI lanes carry the ini budget and keep their hang guard. `grep -c -- "--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread" .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` prints `2` (today `0`), and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q` exits 0 with the drift assertion in place.
- [x] `make lint` reaches both hygiene checks. `make -n lint | grep -c "check_wall_clock_asserts.py\|check_raw_git_writes.py"` prints `2`; today `0`.
- [x] The default tier stays clean under the budget. `python -m pytest -m unit -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` reports no `Failed: Timeout` (pinning; measured clean 2026-08-21 at an explicit `--timeout=20`).
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
baseline.summary: Adopt standard test-hygiene tooling: ruff PLW1510 + PT, pytest-timeout 20 s budget with marker override, hygiene checks in make lint

## Summary

The `Reconciler Heartbeat Canary` workflow (`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`)
fails on every run whenever `bridge-fsck` reports binding drift, because its
`Open binding-drift alert` step calls `rebar create` (a write) but the store was
never write-initialized in CI — so the write seam rejects it.

## Reproduction Steps

1. In a fresh checkout, mount the tickets branch with a bare
   `git worktree add -B tickets .tickets-tracker origin/tickets` (as the canary does)
   — this does NOT create `.tickets-tracker/.env-id`.
2. Run any rebar write, e.g. `rebar create bug "x"`.

- **Expected:** the write succeeds and a ticket is created.
- **Actual:** `Error: ticket system not initialized. Run 'ticket init' first.` (exit 1),
  raised by the write seam at `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:180`, which refuses to
  append any event unless `.tickets-tracker/.env-id` exists. `.env-id` is git-ignored,
  never committed to the `tickets` branch, and is created only by `rebar init`.

## Root Cause

The canary's `Mount tickets branch as a worktree` step does a bare `git worktree add`
and never runs `rebar init`, so `.env-id` is absent. It was latent until the
binding-drift alerting step (commit `dc01c11fe`) added the first `rebar create` the
canary actually exercises; it fires whenever `bridge-fsck` sees drift. The documented
headless-CI provisioning path (`docs/architecture.md`) is `rebar init` — idempotent,
non-interactive, attaches to the existing `origin/tickets`, and seeds `.env-id`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `rebar init` step is added to `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` after the store is
      mounted and rebar is installed, so `.env-id` is seeded before any rebar write.
- [ ] The canary's `rebar create` / `rebar comment` / `rebar transition` write steps no
      longer fail with "ticket system not initialized".
- [ ] The step is idempotent and non-interactive (safe on every scheduled run).
- [ ] Change is pushed to Gerrit `refs/for/main` with a `rebar-ticket:` trailer.
baseline.summary: canary: rebar create fails 'ticket system not initialized' — mount step never seeds .env-id

## Site
`ExpressionError(WorkflowError)` is defined at `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py:251` and raised from workflow execute-time expression resolution (`interpreter.py` and `executor.py`) for wiring/state faults: input not set, no such step output, loop/map var out of scope, missing secret/env, or unresolvable `${{ }}` expression.

## Symptom
`error_code_for(ExpressionError(...))` currently reaches the broad `LLMError`/`WorkflowError` branch and returns `llm_unavailable`. That asserts a provider outage for a caller/state wiring fault and encourages retries that will not self-heal.

## Operator decision
Latest DECISION NEEDED comment (operator-approved 2026-09-01) supersedes the earlier `expression_unresolved` option for this ticket: reclassify `ExpressionError -> invalid_input`, matching prior bug 35ab (executor unknown-step -> invalid_input) and dbca (parse/lint -> invalid_input). Give `ExpressionError` an explicit `error_code = "invalid_input"` so the mapping is honest regardless of branch order. Preserve dbca AC3 by ensuring genuine execute-time LLM outages still map to `llm_unavailable` through the true outage type/wrapper path. Implement this with ce6b's umbrella narrowing as one coherent change.

## Symptom

Five tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` fail locally for any developer whose git config sets `safe.bareRepository = explicit`. They pass under git's default (`all`), which is what CI uses, so **CI can never exercise this path**. All five fail identically — not an assertion, a `CalledProcessError` from the test helper: `Command '['git', '-C', '.../tickets-remote.git', 'ls-tree', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 128`.

## Root cause

`git` refuses to **discover** a bare repository via `-C` / cwd when `safe.bareRepository=explicit`; it accepts one named by a top-level `--git-dir`. Exit 128 is a refusal to open the repository at all, *before* any ref lookup:

```
git -C <bare>  -> fatal: cannot use bare repository '<bare>' (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')
git --git-dir <bare>  -> exit 0
```

The offending helper is `_git` at `test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46`, which hardcodes `["git", "-C", str(repo), *args]`. The bare remote is built in `_ticket_remote` (:97-117) and read at **:401, :402, :415, :423, :435, :455, :493, :576** — eight sites across the five failing tests.

Two claims in the original report are wrong: the `refs/heads/tickets` ref EXISTS (git never gets as far as looking it up), and git 2.55.0 is a red herring — `safe.bareRepository` shipped in git 2.38.0 with these exact semantics.

## This is a recurrence of a class already fixed

Closed ticket `3476-4472-3407-4246` (`embolismic-adverse-dragon`) records the policy verbatim: "the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. **Treat agents dismissing reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.**" It converted 13 files from `git -C <bare>` to `git --git-dir <bare>` and added the held-out oracle `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py`.

**Why this file escaped the guard:** that oracle pins a **hardcoded allowlist** of 3 fixture nodes (`_FIXTURE_NODES`). `test_atomic_completion_close.py` was added on 2026-08-25 by commit `1cb1cdd25aff` — four days *after* the guard landed — and reintroduced the banned construct. There is no static sweep either, so the guard only checks three files that were already fixed and cannot fail when a new file reintroduces the defect. **That allowlist is why this is the second occurrence, and leaving it is why there would be a third.**

## Plan

1. **Point fix.** Add a sibling helper `_bare_git(remote, *args)` that addresses the bare remote
   with a top-level `--git-dir`, and route only the bare-remote call sites through it. `_git` is
   also used on **non-bare** worktrees (`tracker`, `writer`, `tmp_path` for `init`/`clone`), so a
   blanket `-C` -> `--git-dir` swap is wrong. This is the shape ticket 3476 already established in
   the integration fixtures (`_bare_git` beside `_git`).
2. **Close the oracle gap with a tree-derived sweep, inside the guard that failed.** Delete the
   hand-maintained `_FIXTURE_NODES` allowlist from
   `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py` and replace it with an
   AST sweep over every `tests/**/*.py`. Per module it derives the identifiers bound to a bare
   repository:
   - the last path operand after a `--bare` token (`git init --bare <dir>`, and
     `git clone --bare <src> <dst>`, whose *source* must not be marked);
   - the directory the call runs in when the flag takes no operand (`_git(remote, "init", "-q",
     "--bare")`, the shape the already-fixed integration fixtures use);
   - a name bound by a bare-repository factory: a `bare`-named creator taking only paths
     (`init_bare_remote(remote)`), or a same-module helper that creates a bare repository **and
     returns it** — tracked by return POSITION (`return remote, writer` marks only the first
     element; a helper returning the *worktree* marks nothing) and applied to the **caller's
     binding name**, so a rename (`origin, scribe = _ticket_remote(...)`) is covered;
   - the **argument passed at a parameter position** that the callee marks bare in its own body,
     which covers `_publish_ticket_store(repo, remote)` by dataflow rather than by the caller
     happening to spell the name the same way.
   Marking is otherwise module-scoped by identifier, covering the same flows a second way. Then
   flag any `-C` invocation targeting a marked name — direct, or through a module-local helper
   that forwards its first parameter to `-C`. Two calls are **exempt**: one carrying the inline
   `-c safe.bareRepository=all` opt-in, the deliberate escape ticket 3476 preserved in
   `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py` (it passes under the strict config today);
   and the **creating** call, since `git -C <dir> init --bare` runs before `<dir>` is a repository.
   Self-test the detector on synthetic offending / renamed-binding / parameter-passed / escaped
   modules, and pin the git behaviour the rule encodes, so neither can rot into a tautology.
3. **Why not a `scripts/check_*.py`.** That is the repo's usual shape for a static sweep and was
   the intended home, but `scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py` names every `scripts/check_*.py`
   a `ci_gate` **by its path**, and `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` asserts `new=0` and
   `set(baseline) == live` **regardless of any `# mechanism-ok:` marker** — so a new gate script
   cannot land without an operator running `--lock`. Repairing the existing guard adds no
   mechanism, is the narrower change, and keeps enforcement on the suite CI already runs (a
   portable trigger needing no CI provider of its own).
4. Fix every site the sweep flags, so the guard is green on landing: 12 sites in 2 files — 8 in
   the file under fix and 4 in `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`, whose
   `test_fresh_clone_json_exposes_allocation_without_a_policy_verdict` and
   `test_invalid_configured_branch_cleans_only_its_temporary_child` fail under the strict config
   today for exactly the same reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file setting safe.bareRepository=explicit> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` exits 0 with 17 passed (today: 5 failed, 12 passed).
- [x] The same file still passes under default git config (17 passed), and the full `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle` run still passes.
- [x] `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` passes under the strict config too (today: 2 failed, 5 passed) and under the default config.
- [x] The sweep reports nothing on the fixed tree; reintroducing the `git -C <bare-repo>` construct anywhere under `tests/` makes it fail. Demonstrated by temporarily reverting one call site, observing the guard go RED, and restoring it.
- [x] The guard's coverage is derived from the tree, not from a hand-maintained file allowlist: `_FIXTURE_NODES` is gone, and a new bare-fixture test using `git -C <bare>` fails the gate with no registration step.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` all pass, with **no new mechanism registered** — no `# mechanism-ok:` marker needed and no baseline edited.

## Testing

- RED first: `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$STRICT GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 python -m pytest <file> -q` must show `5 failed, 12 passed` before the fix and `17 passed` after, and `2 failed, 5 passed` -> `7 passed` for `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- Default-config runs of both files, plus `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle -q`.
- Guard: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py -q`, plus a mutation run with one call site reverted to `_git(remote, ...)` proving it goes RED.
- Ratchets: `make lint` (module-size, complexity, mechanism-delta), `make typecheck`, and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q` (which `make lint` does NOT cover).
baseline.summary: Bare-repo test fixtures regress: git -C <bare> in test_atomic_completion_close.py fails under safe.bareRepository=explicit (guard's hardcoded allowlist missed it)

## Completion state

This workflow migration is complete. Gerrit changes 1538, 1540, and 1541 are merged. The current tree is the intended post-migration state:

- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml delegates one strict synchronous commit-and-push action to the core bridge runner while preserving the exact bot identity and commit subject.
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml delegates one strict synchronous push-only action to rebar._store.push.
- Both workflow-local CAS loops and the reconciler raw-git exemption are absent.
- Core owns retry/CAS recovery and workflow calls remain red on exhausted delivery.

Graduate `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` off the module-size allowlist (currently ~886 LOC, soft cap 800) by extracting a cohesive cluster of the NON-retrying `update_one` apply phases into a new leaf sibling `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py`.

## Seam

`update_one` is a thin sequencer over per-phase helpers. The phases split cleanly into two groups: those that funnel Jira writes through the shared `_call_with_retry` backoff hub, and those that do NOT. The retrying phases (`_update_one_apply_parent`, `_update_one_scalar_update`, `_update_one_dispatch_labels`, `_update_one_dispatch_links`) STAY in `dispatch_one` alongside `_call_with_retry` itself. The NON-retrying phases MOVE to the new leaf: `_OUTBOUND_BATCH_ALLOWLIST`, `_jira_account_id_for`, `_load_alert_store`, `_record_reporter_alert`, `_update_one_apply_reporter`, `_update_one_filter_fields`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (~132 LOC). None of these touch `_call_with_retry`, so the new module is a true LEAF (it imports nothing from `dispatch_one`; its only cross-module uses are lazy in-function imports of `rebar`, `rebar._commands.identity`, and `rebar_reconciler._loader`). `dispatch_one` re-imports the 3 phase functions (`_update_one_apply_reporter`, `_update_one_filter_fields`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`) so `update_one`'s bare-name calls and `dispatch_one.<phase>` attribute access keep resolving.

## Deviation from the architecture.md remedy row

The current `docs/architecture.md` offenders row for this file names its next seam as extracting `_update_one_apply_parent` (plus the assignee sentinel pop) into `dispatch_apply_phases.py`. That named symbol CANNOT move cleanly: `_update_one_apply_parent` calls the shared `_call_with_retry` hub (`_call_with_retry(client.set_parent, ...)`), so moving it would force the leaf to import `_call_with_retry` back from `dispatch_one` and create a bidirectional dependency. This ticket therefore takes a different, code-accurate seam — the "non-retrying apply phases" grouping above — which keeps the new file a strict leaf. The arch.md row is superseded; this ticket DELETES that remedy row (the file graduates off the gate entirely). This ticket does NOT claim arch.md already records this exact seam.

This is a pure/mechanical refactor: no signature or logic changes, symbols are moved verbatim and re-exported. E5 testing-plan is not-applicable — the existing test suite is the oracle. The one required test edit repoints `test_identity_264f_reporter.py`'s `monkeypatch.setattr(dispatch, "_record_reporter_alert", ...)` to the leaf module (the symbol moves there), while the direct `dispatch._update_one_apply_reporter(...)` calls keep working via the re-export.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Land dependabot PR #125 (uv-lock group) through Gerrit — zizmor 1.29.0 only

## Context / Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror for this project: dependabot keeps opening dependency PRs there, but they can never merge — the content has to be re-applied locally and landed as a Gerrit change, then the PR closed by hand. PR #125 ("deps: bump the uv-lock group across 1 directory with 2 updates") is open now and proposes two bumps:

* `zizmor` `1.28.0` -> `1.29.0` — pinned EXACTLY in the `dev` group for local<->CI parity;
  `make lint` runs `zizmor .github/workflows/release.yml`.
* `mcp` `1.29.0` -> `2.0.0` (major), with the pyproject ceiling loosened `<2` -> `<3` in
  both the `mcp` and `dev` extras.

The `mcp` half is a re-proposal of what dependabot already asked for in the now-closed PR
#124. That was investigated under ticket 1dfd (entodermic-dizzying-pikeperch) and rejected
on evidence: mcp 2.0 removes the `mcp.server.fastmcp` module (verified `ModuleNotFoundError`), which `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:570` and `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:72` import. Other v1 import paths in the same subsystem are separately at risk under 2.0 — `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:512` (`mcp.server.transport_security`), `:590` (`mcp.server.auth.settings`), `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:38` (`mcp.server.auth.provider`), and `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:291` (`mcp.types`). That migration is structural work and is already tracked as its own open ticket, 732b-51df-acf2-477b (bared-nickel-insect), "Migrate MCP server to mcp 2.0 (fastmcp removal)". Nothing about PR #125 changes that finding, so re-litigating it here would duplicate 732b.

## Approach

Land the **safe subset** of PR #125 — the `zizmor` bump alone — and leave the `mcp` ceiling at `<2` so the resolver keeps `mcp` 1.29.0. This is the same path-2 decision rule that ticket 1dfd already applied to the identical `mcp` proposal, so the two tickets stay consistent rather than contradicting each other.

Concretely, in a fresh worktree branched from current `origin/main`:

1. Edit `pyproject.toml`: `"zizmor==1.28.0"` -> `"zizmor==1.29.0"` in the `dev` group. The
   exact pin (not a floor) is deliberate and documented in the surrounding comment; keep it
   exact.
2. Refresh the lock with `uv lock --upgrade-package zizmor` so `uv.lock` is regenerated by
   uv rather than hand-edited. CI gates on `uv lock --check` (`_build-and-test.yml:67`), so
   the committed lock must be exactly what uv produces for the edited pyproject.
3. Do NOT touch the `mcp` constraints, `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`, or ADR 0050 —
   those are 732b's edit-set.
4. Verify, commit with a `rebar-ticket:` trailer + DCO sign-off, push to
   `refs/for/main`, land on `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, then close PR #125 with a
   comment naming the merged commit and pointing the `mcp` half at 732b.

Assume the zizmor bump is clean unless `make lint` says otherwise: zizmor tightens and adds audits across releases, so if 1.29.0 reports a NEW finding on `release.yml`, fix that finding in this change (that is exactly what the exact pin exists to surface).

## Scope

* `pyproject.toml` — the single `zizmor==` pin in the `dev` dependency group.
* `uv.lock` — the regenerated `zizmor` package entry (version, sdist, wheels) plus whatever
  incidental churn `uv lock` emits.
* OUT: the `mcp` 1.29.0 -> 2.0.0 bump and its `<2` -> `<3` ceiling move (deferred to 732b);
  `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`; ADR 0050; dependabot configuration; any other open
  dependency update; `src/` and `tests/` (no source change is expected).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `pyproject.toml` contains `"zizmor==1.29.0"` and still contains `mcp>=1.28.1,<2`
  in both the `mcp` extra and the `dev` group — checked with
  `grep -nE 'zizmor==|mcp>=' pyproject.toml`.
- [x] AC2: `uv.lock` records `zizmor` at `1.29.0` and `mcp` at `1.29.0` — checked with
  `grep -A1 -E '^name = "(zizmor|mcp)"$' uv.lock` — and `uv lock --check` exits 0, proving
  the committed lock matches the edited pyproject (the same gate CI runs).
- [x] AC3: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` exits 0 in the worktree, proving
  zizmor 1.29.0 reports no finding on `release.yml`; `make typecheck` and the test suite
  also exit 0.
- [x] AC4: A Gerrit change carrying this diff is merged into `main` with `LLM-Review +1`
  and `Verified +1` — checked by `git log origin/main` showing the commit with this
  ticket's `rebar-ticket:` trailer.
- [x] AC5: GitHub PR #125 is in state `CLOSED` — checked with
  `gh pr view 125 --json state --jq '.state' | grep -qx CLOSED`.
- [x] AC6: PR #125 carries a closing comment that names the merged Gerrit commit sha and
  points the `mcp` 2.0 half at ticket 732b — checked with
  `gh pr view 125 --json comments --jq '.comments[].body' | grep -q 732b` and the same
  pipeline `| grep -q "4bce6a3cca435f9d52dbe2e1969dd08cab605e29"`, both exiting 0.


## Outcome

Landed as Gerrit change 1483 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1483), merged to `main` as `4bce6a3cca435f9d52dbe2e1969dd08cab605e29` with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`. PR #125 is CLOSED with a provenance comment. The `mcp` 2.0 half was not landed and remains tracked by ticket `732b-51df-acf2-477b`. Full per-AC evidence is in this ticket's comments.
baseline.summary: Land dependabot PR #125 through Gerrit: zizmor 1.29.0 (mcp 2.0 deferred to 732b)

# S1 — One provider factory behind pydantic-ai's `infer_model(provider_factory=…)`

## Context / Problem

Provider construction is an inline special case. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:268` reads `if self._model_override is None and resolved.startswith("anthropic"):` and builds the retrying Anthropic client in the middle of `run()`. Any second provider (Bedrock, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) has to add another branch in the same place, which is how PR #121 was written. There is no single place that answers "how is a Provider constructed for provider X".

## Approach

Introduce `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` holding a **per-run `ProviderSession`**: an object constructed once per `run()` from the `LLMConfig`, exposing `provider_factory` — a callable matching pydantic-ai's `infer_model(model_str, provider_factory=…)` hook signature `(str) -> Provider` — plus a registry mapping provider name to a builder. Upstream directs user-configurable-provider apps to exactly this hook (pydantic-ai#1343) rather than patching `infer_provider`, so rebar depends on a supported contract.

**Client teardown is the reason this is a session object, not a bare function.** The hook's return type carries a `Provider` only, with no channel for the retrying `httpx.AsyncClient` that `anthropic_model._build_retrying_anthropic_model` currently returns as the second element of a tuple (`runner.py:283`) and that `runner.py:446-452` closes in a `finally` block. `ProviderSession` owns that lifecycle instead: each builder that constructs an `httpx.AsyncClient` appends it to the session's private `_closeables` list, and `ProviderSession.close()` closes them all. `run()` wraps its body in the session as a context manager, so the existing `finally`-block teardown becomes the session's `__exit__` and the ad-hoc `_http_client` local disappears. One session per `run()` call, never shared across runs or threads, so the list needs no locking.

The Anthropic construction moves verbatim into an `anthropic` builder that still calls `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, keeping the tenacity transport, the `max_retries=0` guard, the loopback-proxy bypass (`anthropic_model.py:60`) and the per-request `httpx.Timeout` unchanged; the builder unpacks the existing `(model, client)` tuple, registers the client with the session, and returns the provider. `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`'s own signature is unchanged, so the two tests that import it directly (`tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:33`, `tests/unit/test_transport_retry.py:28`) keep working — but they import it via `rebar.llm.runner`, so those two import sites move to `rebar.llm.anthropic_model` in this change. `_pai_model` (`anthropic_model.py:159`) remains the model-string resolver and is not touched.

This story is a **pure relocation with no behavior change** — it lands the seam before any new provider uses it, so the Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible stories are additive registrations rather than surgery on `run()`.

**Alternative rejected:** a chain of `elif` branches in `run()` (PR #121's shape). It keeps provider knowledge smeared across the runner, makes each new provider a diff to the hottest function in the module, and leaves no place to attach the capability lookups S2 needs.

**Alternative rejected:** a bare `build_model(resolved, cfg) -> (Model, Closeable | None)` helper that bypasses `infer_model` entirely. It solves teardown just as well but abandons the upstream hook, so rebar would own provider-string resolution forever instead of inheriting it.

**Alternative rejected:** passing a mutable out-parameter (e.g. a one-element list) into the factory closure to smuggle the client back. It works but is an unnamed side channel with no ownership story, and it would have to be repeated for every future closeable resource.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` (new) — `ProviderSession`, the builder registry, the `anthropic` builder.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — replace the `:268` branch with the session's factory; the `:446-452` teardown
  becomes the session context manager's exit.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — unchanged behavior; imported by the new builder.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py` (`:33`), `tests/unit/test_transport_retry.py` (`:28`) — update the import
  site of `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` from `rebar.llm.runner` to `rebar.llm.anthropic_model`.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract test tier (producer/consumer through the real seam): the factory is the producer and `run()` the consumer, so a unit test on the registry alone is insufficient — the assertion must be that `run()` obtains its provider through the session and that the session closes what it opened.

- happy path: with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`, the model `run()` builds is an `AnthropicModel`
  whose httpx client carries an `AsyncTenacityTransport` and whose `AsyncAnthropic.max_retries == 0`.
- resource oracle (the defect this design exists to prevent): after `run()` returns, every `httpx.AsyncClient`
  the session constructed reports closed — asserted on the real client object, not on a call count. A second
  assertion covers the exception path: `run()` raising still closes the client.
- failure path: an unregistered provider name raises `LLMConfigError` naming the registered providers, not a
  `KeyError`.
- negative control: the `model_override` test path bypasses the factory entirely, constructs no client, and the
  session closes nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -n 'startswith("anthropic")' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returns nothing
- [ ] the full existing suite passes unchanged (`make test`), evidencing no behavior change
- [ ] a test asserts `run()` sources its provider from `ProviderSession.provider_factory`, and that an unknown
      provider raises `LLMConfigError` listing registered names
- [ ] a test asserts every client the session opened is closed after `run()` returns **and** after `run()`
      raises, checked on the real client object's closed state
- [ ] a test asserts the `model_override` path builds no client and the session closes nothing (negative control)
- [ ] `grep -rn '_build_retrying_anthropic_model' tests/` shows both import sites resolving to
      `rebar.llm.anthropic_model`, and `make test` passes
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` is under 300 LOC and imports nothing from `runner` (leaf module, matching the
      `anthropic_model.py` convention)
baseline.summary: S1 — one provider factory behind pydantic-ai infer_model(provider_factory=…)

baseline.description:
## Problem
`tests/conftest.py`'s autouse `_no_repo_root_leaks` fixture (line 297) **deletes files it did not create**, using a before/after directory snapshot that cannot distinguish a leaking test from a concurrent process making a legitimate write.

```python
before = _repo_leak_snapshot(_REPO_ROOT)          # :300
...
after = _repo_leak_snapshot(_REPO_ROOT)           # :304
leaked = {name for name in (after - before) if not _is_coverage_artifact(name)}
for name in sorted(leaked, key=len, reverse=True):
    target = _REPO_ROOT / name
    if target.is_dir():
        shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)  # :313
    else:
        target.unlink()                            # :316
```

Anything that appears under `_REPO_ROOT` between the two snapshots is deleted. The fixture's own comment says cleanup is "best-effort" and suppresses `OSError` so a race cannot mask the real failure — sound reasoning for the leak it was built to catch, but it means a deletion that hits an unintended target is **silent**.

## Why this is dangerous in THIS repository specifically
rebar's ticket store lives **under the repo root** (`.tickets-*`), and rebar writes to it constantly — every `comment`, `edit`, `set-file-impact`, `claim`, `transition`. This project also runs many agents concurrently, each in its own worktree but frequently issuing `rebar` commands while a suite runs. A tracker write landing under a worktree's `_REPO_ROOT` during a test is, to this fixture, indistinguishable from a leak — and gets deleted.

This is not theoretical. Multiple agents in the 2026-08-19/20 session reported this guard firing because of concurrent `rebar` writes, e.g. "one leak guard tripped because a `rebar transition` wrote `.rebar/workflow_runs` mid-run", and "`.tickets-tracker` written under that same worktree root mid-run". Every one of those reports was treated as harmless noise. The deletion half was noticed only when one agent read the fixture and observed that it **removes** what it flags — so running rebar tracker writes during a suite in the same worktree is *actively unsafe, not merely noisy*.

## Bounding the damage honestly
Ticket events auto-commit and auto-push to `sync.remote` on write, so an event that completed its push survives on the remote even if the local file is deleted. The exposure is the window between the write landing on disk and its push completing — plus any local-only state the fixture removes (`.rebar/workflow_runs` and similar are not ticket events and have no remote copy).

So this is not "the tracker gets destroyed". It is: a test fixture can silently delete another process's files, in a repo whose primary datastore lives at that path, with no attribution check and suppressed errors. The blast radius is bounded by the auto-push, not by the fixture's design.

## The design gap
The fixture asks "what appeared under REPO_ROOT during this test?" when the question it needs is "what did THIS TEST create?". A snapshot diff cannot answer the second in the presence of any other writer.

Candidate remedies, to be decided on evidence rather than assumed:
- **Attribute before deleting** — only remove paths the test's own process created, or that match
  the known leak shapes, rather than any diff entry.
- **Fail without deleting** — the `pytest.fail()` already surfaces the leak; deletion is a
  convenience. Removing it converts a silent data-loss risk into a loud, harmless failure. The
  burden of proof should be on keeping the deletion, not on removing it.
- **Exclude the datastore** — never delete under `.tickets-*` / `.rebar/`, on the grounds that no
  legitimate test leak lives there and every legitimate concurrent write does.
- **Detect concurrent writers** and skip cleanup when one is active.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A concurrent, legitimate write under `_REPO_ROOT` during a test run is NOT deleted — proven by
      a test that writes from a separate process mid-test and asserts the file survives.
- [x] The fixture still catches the leak it exists for: a test that genuinely leaks into REPO_ROOT
      still FAILS. Prove it by seeding a leaking test and observing the failure, so this does not
      become a silent weakening of the guard.
- [x] If deletion is retained in any form, deletions are ATTRIBUTED (the fixture can say why it
      believes it created each removed path) and are no longer silent on error.
- [x] Guidance records whether running `rebar` commands against a worktree while its suite runs is
      supported. If it is not, say so in `docs/local-dev-env.md` — several agents did it all session
      believing the resulting errors were cosmetic.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.

## Provenance
Fixture behaviour read directly at `tests/conftest.py:296-320` on origin/main; the concurrent-write reports are from four separate agents' own logs during the 2026-08-19/20 session. Surfaced by the implementer on `dirt-prior-falcon`, which flagged the deletion rather than absorbing it.
baseline.summary: Leak-guard fixture deletes files it did not create, including concurrent tracker writes under REPO_ROOT

# transition_close.py is 803/800 LOC on main — the locked module-size gate fails EVERY patchset

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` sits at 803 LOC on current `origin/main` (f70e5d21 and descendants), over the locked 800-LOC hard cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The CI module-size gate runs on every patchset's tree, so every new Gerrit change based on main now gets `Verified -1` regardless of its own diff — observed live on change 1374 (bug 1019's fix): `803 src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` was the only gate failure. Recent merges grew the file past the cap (a submit race let the overage land). This blocks all landing work until the file is split.

## Approach

Split along the existing call-graph seam: the completion-PREcheck cluster — `_is_live_ticket`, `_has_live_replacement_link`, `_referencing_commit_exists`, and `_completion_precheck` — is a self-contained group (the first three are called only by `_completion_precheck` and each other; nothing else in the file calls into them) of ~335 LOC. Move it verbatim into a new module `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` (well over the 100-LOC floor; the remainder of `transition_close.py` lands ~470 LOC, inside the 200-500 target). No behavior change: pure move plus imports.

Compatibility seams preserved exactly:

- `transition_close` re-imports `_completion_precheck` and
  `_referencing_commit_exists` (`from rebar._commands.close_precheck import
  _completion_precheck as _completion_precheck, ...`), so
  `close_ticket`'s call site still reads the `transition_close` module global —
  existing tests that `monkeypatch.setattr(transition_close,
  "_completion_precheck", ...)` and the direct test import
  `from rebar._commands.transition_close import _referencing_commit_exists`
  keep working unmodified. No test file changes are expected.
- `sign_completion_verdict`, `close_ticket`, `_short_head` (the other
  externally referenced names) stay where they are.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — new module (the moved cluster).
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — remove the moved code, add the
  re-import.

## Testing

Pure mechanical move — no new testable behavior, so no new tests. The move is verified by the existing suites that drive the moved code through both entry points staying green: `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` (close gate, attested signing, idea bypass, subtree), `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` (direct `_referencing_commit_exists` import), `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py`
+ `test_close_gate_bound_*` / `test_close_gate_step_budget_*` (direct
`_tc._completion_precheck` calls), and `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py`. Gate compliance is verified by `wc -l` ≤ 800 on both files and CI's own module-size gate going green on the change's patchset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` is ≤ 800 LOC (target ≤ 500) —
      checked by `wc -l` locally and the CI module-size gate passing on the
      change's patchset.
- [x] the new `close_precheck.py` is ≥ 100 LOC and contains the moved cluster
      unchanged in behavior — checked by `wc -l` and the existing close-gate
      suites passing with zero test-file edits.
- [x] `monkeypatch.setattr(transition_close, "_completion_precheck", ...)`
      seams and the `_referencing_commit_exists` direct import keep working —
      checked by `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` and
      `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` passing unmodified.
