baseline.description:
Three values that are accepted by a signature and then never read. All three were confirmed against the code during the 2026-08-05/06 janitor run; the approved remediation is deletion in every case, because each "wire it up" alternative requires inventing a capability no caller has asked for.

**a. `timeout_s` — `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:71`**

`_call_with_retry(fn, *args, timeout_s: int = 30, max_retries: int = 3, **kwargs)` declares, defaults and documents `timeout_s` ("Per-call timeout in seconds (currently advisory for stub-based callers)", `:86`) but the body never reads it. Six call sites in `apply_outbound.py` (`:101`, `:109`, `:180`, `:202`, `:227`); none passes it.

The defect is not inertness. Because `timeout_s` is a *named* keyword-only parameter in front of `**kwargs`, a caller who passes `timeout_s=60` intending it for the wrapped Jira client has it **swallowed by the wrapper instead of forwarded**. This wrapper is on the path for every Jira write. Deleting the parameter restores the natural behaviour: `timeout_s` flows through `**kwargs` to `fn`.

**b. `run_eval(dirty=True)` — `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:626`**

Declared, never read in the body; no caller in `src/` or `tests/` passes it (five `run_eval(` call sites, all in `tests/unit/test_eval.py`). The boolean falsely implies the eval-provenance source can be switched.

**c. Two permanently-`Unavailable` metric seeds — `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py:136-158`**

`module_size_trend` and `commit_cadence_trend` both carry `compute=_no_data_yet`, which returns `None`, so `evaluate` always yields `Unavailable`. `accruing_since` is `2026-07-18` with no data source landed. `git_metrics.register()` registers six entirely different ids (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`, `churn`, `refactor_to_addition_ratio`), so nothing currently competes for these ids.

The latent trap: every registrar appends under `if spec.id not in existing` (`git_metrics.py:277`, `event_metrics.py:367`, `bug_trends.py:337`). A future real implementation of `module_size_trend` would find the seed already holding the id and be **silently skipped** — no error, no warning, and the metric would keep reporting `Unavailable`. Deleting the seeds frees both ids so a real spec registers cleanly.

`tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics_heldout.py:138-142` (`test_trend_unavailable`) asserts the placeholder stays `Unavailable` — a change-detector test pinning a stub in place. It goes with them.

Note: no consumer of the two metric ids was found outside the registry and that test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `timeout_s` is removed from `_call_with_retry`'s signature and its docstring `Args:` entry;
      a caller passing `timeout_s=` now reaches `fn` through `**kwargs`
- [x] `dirty` is removed from `run_eval`'s signature
- [x] The `module_size_trend` and `commit_cadence_trend` specs are removed from `REGISTRY`, and
      `_no_data_yet` goes too if it has no remaining user
- [x] `test_trend_unavailable` is removed
- [x] `rebar metrics` output no longer advertises two ids that can never carry a value
- [x] No behavior change to Jira retry/backoff, eval runs, or any metric that reports real data
baseline.summary: Delete three accepted-then-ignored values: timeout_s, run_eval(dirty=), two metric seeds

## Summary

The "Live External Integration" workflow (external-integration.yml) has 4 failing job lanes — `external LLM (live anthropic)`, `external LLM (live openai)`, `external LLM (live bedrock)`, and `langfuse tracing round-trip` — all failing with:

    AttributeError: module 'rebar.llm' has no attribute 'review_ticket'

## Root cause (proven)

The public `rebar.llm.review_ticket()` API was REMOVED in a pre-1.0 breaking pass (deprecated v0.11.0, removed 2026-08-12; CHANGELOG.md:121, docs/release-notes.md:72 maps it -> `rebar.llm.review_plan()`). `rebar.llm` now exposes `review_plan` / `review_code`, no `review_ticket`. That removal epic's AC said "the rest [of the 19 referencing test files] are retargeted to the surviving review-plan/engine paths" — but TWO EXTERNAL live-test modules were missed:

- `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py:80` (`test_pydantic_review_ticket_opus`) —
  run by the external-llm lanes via `pytest -m "external and llm_live" tests/external`.
- `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py:151` — run by the langfuse lane via
  `pytest -m external tests/external/test_llm_trace.py`.

These modules are marked `external` and are EXCLUDED from the standard Gerrit Verified gate (which collects+skips external tests), so the removal epic's `pytest` run never exercised them and the regression was invisible until a live `workflow_dispatch` run. Discovered during the 368f Jira-DC harness live run (run 31853325667).

## Fix is NOT a mechanical rename

The old call `llm.review_ticket(epic, "ticket-quality", repo_root=..., config=...)` differs from the replacement `review_plan(ticket_id, *, ref=None, source=None, repo_root=None, config=None, ...)`:
- `review_plan` has NO positional `"ticket-quality"` graph-target-kind argument.
- `review_plan` returns a `PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT`, but both tests validate `schemas.REVIEW_RESULT`
  and assert `result["runner"]`, `result["model"]`, `result["findings"]`.

So retargeting requires an author decision (review_plan vs review_code) plus adapted assertions/schema. Both external modules must move to a surviving API with the correct result contract, not a blind s/review_ticket/review_plan/.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `grep -rn "review_ticket" tests/external` shows no call to the removed public API (the
      surviving `operations._review_ticket_impl` engine symbol is a different thing and may stay).
- [x] `test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py` and `test_llm_trace.py` are retargeted to a surviving
      public op (`review_plan` or `review_code`) with assertions/schema matching that op's
      actual result contract.
- [x] A live `workflow_dispatch` of "Live External Integration" shows the `external LLM (*)`
      and `langfuse tracing round-trip` lanes GREEN (or the retarget is validated equivalently).

## Testing

- `pytest -m "external and llm_live" tests/external` and
  `pytest -m external tests/external/test_llm_trace.py` (require live LLM creds).
- A `workflow_dispatch` of "Live External Integration" is the authoritative check.


## Resolution evidence

- Retargeted both modules to `rebar.llm.review_code` (surviving REVIEW_RESULT op) in Gerrit
  change 1800, merged as `d38eb1c7a1`. `review_plan` was rejected — it returns a
  PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT with no top-level `findings`, so it cannot satisfy either test.
- `grep -rn "review_ticket" tests/external` now returns only doc/comment mentions and a
  cross-reference to `test_llm_live.test_live_review_ticket`; no call to the removed public API.
- Verified live: `test_pydantic_review_code_opus` PASSED on the bedrock arm locally (60s), and
  the authoritative workflow_dispatch run 31856166064 shows `external LLM (live anthropic)`,
  `external LLM (live openai)`, and `langfuse tracing round-trip` GREEN — all running the
  retargeted tests. ZERO `review_ticket`/`no attribute` errors on any arm (original regression
  gone). The `external LLM (live bedrock)` arm's lone red is an UNRELATED completion-verifier
  defect (`observed_upsert() got an unexpected keyword argument 'evidence_sufficient'` in
  `test_completion_banking_behavior_0707`; 17 passed / 1 failed), filed as
  `ulcerative-confined-blacklemur` (9c7c-4844-f53c-4eac) and linked `discovered_from`.
baseline.summary: External live tests call removed rebar.llm.review_ticket -> 4 CI lanes fail

# Outbound clear-assignee cannot unassign on Jira Data Center

Found while writing the row-9 outbound cell of the J11 mutation table (story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae). NOT fixed here — filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a product defect stops and reports.

## Mechanism (proven by code path, three links in a chain)

1. The differ's desired value for an EMPTY local assignee is the EMPTY STRING, not
   None: `outbound_differ._assignee_resolver` returns `("", True, False)` when
   `not assignee` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:504-505).
   `assignee` is in `_OUTBOUND_BATCH_ALLOWLIST`
   (dispatch_apply_phases.py:46), so it reaches `client.update_issue(key,
   assignee="")`.

2. The DC transport forwards that empty string VERBATIM to the vendor library.
   `JiraDataCenterTransport.update_issue` pops `assignee` and calls
   `self._assign(remote_id, assignee)` whenever the key is present — there is no
   empty-value branch (adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:281-287, 290-303).
   `_assign` calls `self._client.assign_issue(remote_id, "")`.

3. pycontribs/jira treats ONLY None / -1 / "-1" as Unassigned. In jira 3.10.5,
   `JIRA._get_user_id` starts `if user in (None, -1, "-1"): return user` and
   otherwise runs `search_users(user="", maxResults=20)`, raising
   `JIRAError("No matching user found for: ''")` when that returns nothing — and
   when it returns something, it assigns THAT arbitrary user. So the empty string
   is not an unassign instruction on this path at all.

## Cloud already has the fix; DC never got its half

This is bug 85a1's defect class, unported. The Cloud transport routes an empty/None assignee through `unassign_issue` instead of passing it on, with the reason recorded inline: "Bug 85a1 (Fix D7): assignee=None/empty is routed through `unassign_issue` (REST PUT /assignee with `{"accountId": null}`) rather than passed to ACLI as `--assignee ""`, which ACLI silently no-ops" (adapters/jira/acli.py:342-345, guard at :357-359).

The shape is identical to bug d067 (the status-to-transition seam existed on Cloud and Data Center simply never got its half), which the DC `update_issue` docstring itself records at transport.py:265-275.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_unassign_round_trips` asserts `fields.assignee` is null on the DC issue after a local assignee clear converges. It should go RED on the harness until this is fixed.

## Suggested fix

Give the DC transport the same empty-assignee branch Cloud has: in `_assign`, map a falsy assignee to `None` before calling `assign_issue` (pycontribs then PUTs `{"name": null}`, which is DC's unassign), rather than letting `""` reach `_get_user_id`.
baseline.summary: DC outbound clear-assignee never unassigns (empty string reaches assign_issue)

baseline.description:
## What

Add **lease-based self-healing** on top of the C1 ref-lock primitive so a crashed pass-holder
never wedges the reconciler beyond one lease interval. Builds directly on C1.

**Depends on: 524d-00fa-66ef-4432 (C1).** C1 delivers the `_ref_lock.py` module, the blob schema
(`heartbeat_ns`, `fence`), the `acquire`/`release`/`read` API, and the CAS helpers. **This child
ADDS `renew()` plus the lease-expiry/steal logic to that module** — it is not standalone and C1
must be merged first. (`renew()` is introduced here, not in C1.)

- **Relative-duration, skew-proof lease (DynamoDB-lock-client pattern):** expiry is NOT a
  cross-clone timestamp comparison. A contender records `(observed_oid, fence)`, waits one lease
  interval measured on its **own** clock, re-reads; if `fence` and the ref oid are unchanged, the
  holder made no progress for a full lease -> considered dead. This is why the stored `heartbeat_ns`
  is only diagnostic and the design is skew-proof.
- **`renew()`** (heartbeat) CAS-updates the blob's `heartbeat_ns` and increments `fence`
  (`fence += 1`) while the holder still owns the ref (old = observed oid). `fence` is a **monotonic
  progress-witness / generation counter** — it is the signal the expiry rule reads; it is NOT a
  full fencing token handed to the protected resource (no stale-writer rejection is claimed).
- **CAS-break-on-expiry:** a contender may steal **only** an expired lease, by CAS-replacing the
  blob against the exact observed OID. Because the steal is a compare-and-swap on the observed oid,
  a **double-break race resolves to exactly one winner** — the loser's CAS fails, it backs off and
  does NOT also acquire.
- **Lease + cadence config:** default lease **120 s**, heartbeat interval **`max(1, lease // 3)`**
  seconds (integer floor, not a vague `~lease/3`), read from a new `[reconciler]` key
  `lock_lease_secs`. Registering that key is C3's job (the `_config_schema.py` wiring lands with the
  `lock_backend` switch); here it is consumed with a safe default so C2 is testable standalone.
- **`renew()` failure contract:** a rejected renewal CAS means the lease was lost/stolen. `renew()`
  raises a **named exception** (e.g. `LeaseLostError`) — it does NOT silently retry into another
  holder's lock. The orchestrator (C3) turns that exception into a pass-abort.
- Structured log emission for lease-steal, renewal-failure, and expiry-detection events.
- Lives in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` (extends C1); no reconciler
  orchestration wiring (that is C3). Extend the C1 ADR with the lease/heartbeat/fence contract.

## Design decisions (resolves plan-review ambiguities; binding on the implementation)

1. **API surface added to `_ref_lock.py`.** `renew(repo_root, ref, *, oid, remote=None) -> str`;
   and the steal is split into a **testable core** `try_break_if_stale(repo_root, ref, *, first,
   holder, remote=None) -> str | None` plus a convenience `steal(repo_root, ref, *, holder,
   remote=None, sleep_fn=time.sleep) -> str | None` that does observe -> `sleep_fn(first.lease_secs)`
   -> `try_break_if_stale`. The one-lease wait is injected via `sleep_fn` so unit tests exercise the
   CAS/expiry logic **without real time**; a short configured lease also keeps any live test fast.
2. **`renew()` contract.** Reads the current state; if the ref is absent or no longer points at
   `oid` -> `LeaseLostError` (no CAS attempted). Otherwise it CAS-updates the blob to
   `{holder, lease_secs (unchanged), heartbeat_ns=time.time_ns(), fence+1}` against `oid` (via the
   shared `_cas_once` seam / `--force-with-lease` on the remote path); a rejected CAS ->
   `LeaseLostError`. Returns the new oid the caller threads into the next `renew`. It NEVER retries
   into another holder's lock.
3. **Steal contract.** `try_break_if_stale` takes the `first` observation and re-reads: if the ref
   is now free (`None`) or its `(oid, fence)` changed -> returns `None` (the holder released or made
   progress = live, never stolen). Otherwise it CAS-replaces the blob against `first.oid` with
   `{holder=<contender>, lease_secs=first.lease_secs, heartbeat_ns=now, fence=first.fence + 1}`; a
   rejected CAS (lost the single-winner race) -> `None`. It never steals a **free** ref (that is
   `acquire`) and never steals a **live/renewing** holder.
4. **Fail-closed during steal/renew.** A `RefLockCorruptError` / `RefLockTimeoutError` from any read
   in the steal/renew path propagates (fail-closed = treat as HELD); a contender never steals on an
   unreadable blob.
5. **Lease constants.** `DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS = 120` and `heartbeat_interval(lease) -> max(1,
   int(lease // 3))` live in `_ref_lock.py`; C3 wires `[reconciler] lock_lease_secs` into the
   `acquire` call. `lease_secs` is carried IN the blob, so a contender waits the **holder's** lease,
   not its own — the skew-proof relative-duration rule.
6. **Structured logs.** Emit on lease-steal (won a break), expiry-detection (no `(oid, fence)`
   progress across one lease), and renewal-failure (`LeaseLostError`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_ref_lock.py` gains `renew()` (owner-only CAS-update of `heartbeat_ns`, `fence += 1`, against
      the held oid) and a lease-expiry evaluation using observed-no-progress-over-one-locally-measured
      -lease, not an absolute cross-clone clock diff; `renew()` on a lost/stolen lease raises
      `LeaseLostError` (no silent retry) and returns the new oid on success.
- [ ] A contender CAS-breaks only an expired lease (no `fence`/oid progress across one lease); a
      live, heartbeating holder is never stolen from (regression test); a free ref is never "stolen"
      (that path is `acquire`).
- [ ] Double-break race: two contenders race to steal one expired lock (both call
      `try_break_if_stale` against the same `first`); exactly one wins, the other observes CAS
      failure and returns `None` (does NOT acquire) — single-winner regression test.
- [ ] Lease = `[reconciler] lock_lease_secs` (default `DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS = 120`), heartbeat interval
      `heartbeat_interval(lease) = max(1, lease // 3)`, not hardcoded at the call sites; the one-lease
      wait is injectable (`sleep_fn`) so tests need no real sleep.
- [ ] A corrupt/unreadable blob encountered during steal/renew fails closed (treated as HELD), never
      stolen.
- [ ] Lease-steal / renewal-failure / expiry-detection events emit structured logs; the C1 ADR is
      extended with the lease/heartbeat/fence contract. Non-integration suite green.
baseline.summary: Lease + heartbeat + CAS-break-on-stale self-healing (single-winner)

# Committed store compatibility record with a fail-closed capability gate

Introduce a committed store-level compatibility record (`format_version` + `required_capabilities`) that a v1.0 binary reads before any mutating or externally-publishing operation, failing closed on an unknown version or required capability while keeping reads and diagnostics available. (Readiness Finding 2 — verified VALID against `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/{compact,fsck,init}.py`, `docs/migrations.md`.)

## Why

rebar's migration mechanism is an idempotent desired-state ensure-registry, not an ordered ledger: `run_ensures` runs every unit under the write lock, converts exceptions to `failed`, and **returns normally** (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` docstring "Never raises"; init/boot never abort). Event compatibility is preserve-and-ignore: unknown event types are skipped in replay (`reducer/_replay.py:195-196`) and omitted from the compaction fold but kept on disk (`_commands/compact.py:179-195`), and `fsck` emits an informational WARN that does not increment `issue_count` or stop operation (`_commands/fsck.py:229-252`, which itself notes "a reconcile host on an old binary may push stale state").

This forward-compat is correct for *optional additive* data — it prevents an old compactor from deleting new bytes. But there is **no committed store-format-version or required-capability record** (confirmed absent; `SCHEMA_VERSION` is a stamp, never compared to fail closed). So an old binary computes state that omits the unknown event and can then emit a new event, compact, evaluate close/verify policy, or push a stale field to Jira from that incomplete state. `docs/migrations.md` explicitly files the "A-tier ledger + committed store-format version that fails closed" under future work. **The reader must ship in v1.0**: an already-installed v1.0 binary cannot be taught later to inspect a record whose existence and semantics were not defined in v1.0 — so to ever mark a store as requiring a post-v1.0 capability, v1.0 must already know how to detect and refuse unknown required capabilities.

## What

Adopt git's repository-format-version pattern (`core.repositoryformatversion` + `extensions.*`: an implementation that does not understand the advertised format or a required extension must not operate, because continuing can produce incorrect results or lose data), and git's staged rollout (teach readers first, make writing opt-in, default later):

- **The record.** Add a committed store-level record, minimally
  `{"format_version": 1, "required_capabilities": []}`, at a fixed store path (e.g.
  `.store-compat.json`). It is **committed to the `tickets` branch** (not
  git-ignored) — it is the shared fact the gate reads. Write it with the store's
  standard write-to-tempfile-then-atomic-rename pattern so a partial/interrupted
  write never leaves a truncated file.
- **Recognised-capability vocabulary.** The new module exports
  `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset()` — the set of capability strings
  **this** binary understands. The gate blocks when any entry in a record's
  `required_capabilities` is not in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. Future capabilities are
  added to this set only when the feature that consumes them ships (git
  `extensions.*` semantics).
- **The gate error.** The module exports `StoreIncompatibleError(Exception)`, raised
  by the gate; entry-point callers convert it to the existing `CommandError` /
  non-zero exit path (as other gate errors do), with a message naming the
  unsupported version/capability.
- **Four record states (explicit).** (1) **Absent** → implicit legacy format
  version 0, compatible / pass-through, NOT blocked. (2) **Present + compatible** →
  pass. (3) **Present + incompatible** (unknown `format_version` or a
  `required_capabilities` entry ∉ `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`) → **fail-closed**. (4)
  **Present + unreadable/corrupt** (JSON parse error, truncation, permission denied)
  → **fail-closed** with a diagnostic message naming the parse error and the record
  path (a corrupt record is NOT treated as absent — that would silently bypass the
  gate).
- **Expand phase (writing the record into pre-v1.0 stores).** Every store created by
  a pre-v1.0 build is state (1). An idempotent ensure unit (School B) writes the
  record at the current version when absent, at init / fsck-repair / MCP-boot.
  **Because `run_ensures` is fail-silent** (a `LockTimeout` silently skips the whole
  sweep; exceptions become `failed` and it returns normally), the covered-write path
  must not *depend* on the ensure sweep having run: the gate treats absent as
  pass-through regardless, and the record is written opportunistically. So a missed
  sweep never blocks writes — it only defers stamping the record to a later covered
  operation. **absent = legacy/needs-migration, not blocked; present-incompatible or
  corrupt = blocked.**
- **Gate at the true structural choke point, NOT by enumerating call-sites.** "No
  mutation without the gate" must not rest on a hand-maintained list a future path can
  bypass. The single convergence point for **all lock-based store mutations** is
  **`lock.acquire()` in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`** — both the `write_lock()` context
  manager AND the direct callers that bypass it (`txn.py`'s `_acquire_write_lock` for
  claim/transition, `compact.py:167`/`:415`, `fsck.py:419`) call `acquire()`. Insert
  the `check_store_compat()` gate **inside `lock.acquire()`**, after `canonical_tracker()`
  resolves the path and before the fcntl/mkdir legs — so every lock-holding path
  (context-manager and raw-handle) is covered by one insertion point, with no
  enumeration. **Gate ALL `lock.acquire()` unconditionally — no `read_only` parameter
  needed.** The diagnostic exemption is already **structural**: `fsck`'s diagnostic
  path reads ticket data **without acquiring the lock at all**, so it is inherently
  ungated and stays available; only `fsck`'s **repair** path (which *does* call
  `lock.acquire()` at `fsck.py:419`), and `compact.py`/`txn.py`, hold the lock and are
  therefore gated. This is simpler and less error-prone than a read/write-intent flag.
- **Two paths do NOT go through `lock.acquire()` and each gets its own explicit gate:**
  1. **`fsck_recover.py`** performs raw `git cherry-pick`/`rebase --continue`/`merge
     --abort` via its `_git()` helper with **no locking at all** — so it is genuinely
     un-gated by the lock choke point. Add an explicit `check_store_compat(tracker_dir)`
     at the top of `fsck_recover_cli` before any mutation. (Wrapping the mutation block
     in `write_lock` too would additionally close a real pre-existing concurrency gap,
     but at minimum the explicit gate is required.)
  2. **Outbound Jira publish** — the push/reconcile side effect is a **remote API
     call**, not a lock-held write. Jira writes are scattered
     (`create_issue`/`update_issue`/`delete_issue`/`add_comment` across
     `apply_outbound.py` + `dispatch_one.py`), but they all funnel once per pass
     through **`reconcile._apply_mutations()`** (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py`,
     which calls `applier.apply(...)`). Gate there, **after the `persist=True` check**
     (so dry-run / reconcile-check / cap-0 no-write passes are excluded) and before
     `applier.apply()` — mirroring the existing fail-closed cross-project guard
     precedent at `applier.py:637-652` ("refuse BEFORE issuing any Jira write … abort
     the whole pass, no partial writes"). **Use the reconciler's own tracker path**
     (`repo_root / ".tickets-tracker"`, hardcoded at `reconcile.py:133/670`), NOT
     `config.tracker_dir()`, since the reconciler resolves the store directly.
- **Completeness is CI-enforced.** A coverage test/lint greps the tree for **both**
  `lock.acquire(` and `write_lock(` (and asserts each routes through the gate) plus
  asserts `fsck_recover_cli` calls `check_store_compat` — so a new un-gated write path,
  in any of the acquisition forms, fails CI rather than relying on this prose list.
- **Read/diagnostic allowance.** Under an incompatible/corrupt record, the read-only
  commands — `fsck` (diagnostic mode), `show`, `list`, `search` — stay available
  (exit 0) and report the unsupported version/capability (structured, machine-checkable
  output). `fsck`'s **repair** mode (write-intent) is gated like any other mutation.
- **Rollback safety (decided, then proven).** Post-rollback the committed
  `.store-compat.json` remains on the `tickets` branch unchanged, and a pre-v1.0 binary
  **ignores it** (ignored-unknown → rollback-safe): `.store-compat.json` is a *new*
  file at a path no pre-v1.0 code reads — pre-v1.0 replay/compaction/fsck open only
  event files and the known metadata files (`.env-id`, `.gitignore`, etc.), never this
  name — so there is no parse-and-error path. This is the committed design position
  (not a deferral), and the **hard rollback test below is its empirical proof** (git-
  stash the gate code, run `rebar fsck` against a store containing `.store-compat.json`,
  assert operable + file byte-unchanged). The delete-`.store-compat.json` recovery is
  documented as belt-and-suspenders only.
- **Scope boundary.** Keep the ensure-registry for convergent check-then-act repairs.
  Do **not** build the ordered ledger here — only the record + reader gate. Clarify
  the relationship to `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `reducer/_version.py` (it stays the
  event-schema discriminator; `format_version` is the new store-format gate — state
  whether they move together or independently).

## Scope

- New module under `src/rebar/_store/` for the compatibility record + gate, exporting
  `StoreIncompatibleError`, `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`, and `check_store_compat()`.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — insert the gate inside `lock.acquire()` (the single
  convergence point for `write_lock()` + all direct `lock.acquire()` callers:
  `txn.py`, `compact.py:167`/`:415`, `fsck.py:419`), gating every acquisition
  unconditionally (fsck diagnostic holds no lock → structurally exempt).
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` — explicit `check_store_compat()` before its
  raw-git mutation (it holds no lock, so the `lock.acquire()` gate does not cover it).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — `check_store_compat(repo_root/".tickets-tracker")`
  at the top of `_apply_mutations()` after the `persist=True` check (the single
  per-pass chokepoint for both write paths; excludes dry-run/cap-0 passes).
- A coverage test/lint grepping `lock.acquire(` + `write_lock(` + `fsck_recover`'s check.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` — relate `format_version` to the existing
  preserve-and-ignore `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` machinery and to `SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (optional-additive events stay preserve-and-ignore; a required capability is the
  new fail-closed path).
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — the ensure unit that writes the record when absent.
- `docs/migrations.md` — document the record, the four states, the fail-closed
  semantics, the absent-record upgrade path, and the concrete rollback state.
- Interface tests extending `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py`.
- Out of scope: the ordered migration ledger; changing any existing event-replay
  behaviour for currently-known types.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A committed store compatibility record (`format_version` +
  `required_capabilities`) is created at init at a fixed path, written atomically
  (tempfile + rename), and read by a gate function that raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError`; the module exports `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str]`.
- [ ] An **absent** record (pre-v1.0 store) is treated as legacy format version 0 /
  compatible (pass-through, not blocked), and the ensure unit idempotently writes the
  record on the next init / fsck-repair / MCP-boot — verified by a test that opens a
  record-less store with a v1.0 build, confirms it operates, and confirms the record
  is then present (upgrade-in-place, no manual step); the test also confirms a missed
  ensure sweep does not block writes — by monkeypatching `run_ensures` to raise
  `LockTimeout` (or return a `failed` outcome) and asserting a subsequent write still
  succeeds (the gate treats the still-absent record as pass-through).
- [ ] The gate is inserted inside `lock.acquire()` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, after
  path resolution, before fcntl/mkdir) and gates **every** acquisition unconditionally
  — `write_lock()` context-manager callers AND direct `lock.acquire()` callers
  (`txn.py`, `compact.py`, `fsck.py:419` repair) — by one insertion point; `fsck`
  diagnostic holds no lock so it is structurally exempt. Plus an explicit
  `check_store_compat()` at the top of `fsck_recover_cli` (raw-git, no-lock mutation)
  and at the top of `reconcile._apply_mutations()` after the `persist=True` check
  (before `applier.apply()`, using `repo_root/".tickets-tracker"`) for the outbound
  Jira push. It raises `StoreIncompatibleError` (→ non-zero exit) before any side
  effect when the record is **present but incompatible**. Verified by (a) a test in
  `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py` writing a record
  with a `required_capabilities` entry ∉ `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` (e.g. `["unknown-v99"]`)
  and driving a lock-held mutation (store files byte-unchanged), an `fsck_recover`
  invocation, and a reconcile pass (mock Jira adapter records zero calls); and (b) a
  coverage test/lint that greps the tree for **both** `lock.acquire(` and `write_lock(`
  and for `fsck_recover_cli`'s + `_apply_mutations`'s `check_store_compat` call,
  asserting each routes through the
  gate — so a new un-gated write path in any acquisition form fails CI.
- [ ] A **corrupt/unreadable** record (truncated JSON / parse error) is treated as
  fail-closed (NOT as absent) with a diagnostic naming the parse error and path —
  verified by a test writing a truncated record and asserting a mutating entry point
  is blocked.
- [ ] A rollback **test** (hard requirement) simulates a pre-v1.0 binary by invoking
  the store layer with the gate patched out (monkeypatch `check_store_compat` to a
  no-op, emulating code that predates it) against a store carrying the committed
  `.store-compat.json`, and asserts **operable** = `rebar list`/`fsck` exit 0 AND a
  normal write (e.g. `comment`) succeeds, and the `.store-compat.json` file is
  byte-unchanged afterward (proving upgrade-in-place won't brick a pre-v1.0 clone). The
  ignored-unknown guarantee and the delete-`.store-compat.json` compensating path are
  also documented in `docs/migrations.md`.
- [ ] Under an incompatible/corrupt record, the read-only commands `fsck` (diagnostic
  mode), `show`, `list`, and `search` exit with the read-allowed code (0) and their
  structured output / stderr (WARNING+) contains the unsupported version/capability
  identifier — while `fsck` **repair** mode (write-intent) exits non-zero — verified by
  a test asserting the exact field via `jq -e` / an anchored regex and the repair-mode
  non-zero exit.
- [ ] Optional additive (unknown-but-not-*required*) events retain today's
  preserve-and-ignore behaviour — the existing forward-compat contract tests still
  pass, and a new test proves a *required* capability fails closed while an *optional*
  additive event does not.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` documents the record, the four states, the fail-closed
  gate, the deployment-order rationale (why the reader ships in v1.0), and the
  concrete rollback state.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass, and the change lands via the
  Gerrit two-vote gate.
baseline.summary: Committed store compatibility record with a fail-closed capability gate

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`ticket_planner.py:74-82,192` recognizes `requires_create` and `requires_parent`, but production outbound CREATEs never carry either value. The current emission path is `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` in `outbound_mutation_builders.py:122-173`, then `outbound_pass.py:257-269`, which converts the raw `OutboundMutation` to a typed `Mutation` whose `target` is `om.local_id`. `OutboundCreatePayload` has no prerequisite fields, so metadata added only to the raw builder would be lost before the planner sees it.

The planner is not yet authoritative for CREATEs. `batch_dispatch.reroute_migrated_plans` deliberately excludes create actions, and `create_route` coordinates only one create/containment sequence. The live batch consumption point is `apply_handlers.handle_create` (with the sibling typed-create route in `apply_outbound.py`); `create_route.should_hold_dependent` currently has no production caller. Thus ordering requires a new per-pass create scheduler at the batch sequencer, not a claim that the existing single-create coordinator already orders parent and child creates.

## Approach

Use local ticket IDs for all prerequisite and provider identities. An outbound create has `Mutation.target == om.local_id`, which is also its `TicketPlan.identity`; a prerequisite must never name a Jira key for an unbound ticket.

Derive a prerequisite only for a real local parent/create edge in `outbound_mutation_builders`, carry it on `OutboundMutation`, and model it explicitly on `OutboundCreatePayload`. Preserve it in the `outbound_pass` conversion as top-level mapping metadata visible to `ticket_planner._collect_dependencies`. `batch_dispatch._mutation_to_batch_dict` must exclude this scheduler-only metadata from Jira vendor fields.

Add a focused per-pass create-scheduling seam, owned by the batch application path, for homogeneous outbound-create `TicketPlan`s. It receives the finalized plans and their legacy batch mutations, uses the existing planner dependency order, and dispatches each selected create through the existing `apply_handlers.handle_create` → `create_route` path exactly once. It translates the selected route’s terminal result into a provider outcome: only a confirmed create whose containment releases dependents marks its local ID successful; permanent, `commit_unknown`, budget-deferred, or unconfirmed containment outcomes hold dependents as `dependency_deferred`. It records those outcomes in the existing manifest/tally shape, removes only consumed creates from the following legacy loop, and leaves mixed/non-create plans on their established paths.

Refactor the batch create adapter and the typed `apply_outbound` create adapter to expose the same structured create-route completion signal (`confirmed` / `dependents_released`) without a second Jira call or a second routing selector. This keeps `create_route` the owner of one-create persistence, containment, and rollback selection while the new scheduler owns only inter-create ordering.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — raw `OutboundMutation` prerequisite carrier
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py` — derive parent/create prerequisite local IDs
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_pass.py` and `mutation_payloads.py` — preserve typed payload metadata and its mapping round trip
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/ticket_planner.py` — retain/document local-ID dependency and provider semantics
- a new create-ordering sibling (or equivalent focused existing-seam extraction) plus `applier.py` — schedule eligible create plans before the legacy mutation loop and preserve manifest/tally accounting
- `apply_handlers.py`, `create_route.py`, and `apply_outbound.py` — expose and consume the single create-route completion signal at both live create consumption points
- `batch_dispatch.py` — batch projection and removal of scheduler-only metadata from Jira fields
- focused outbound-payload, planner, create-scheduler, handler/route, and operation-coordinator tests

## Testing

Exercise the full builder → typed payload → planner → per-pass create-scheduler → `handle_create`/`create_route` path with parent and child initially unbound. Cover confirmed parent success, permanent failure, `commit_unknown`, budget defer, unconfirmed containment, an already-bound parent, an unknown local parent, unrelated creates, and the vendor-field boundary. Assert local IDs—not Jira keys—at every provider/dependency edge, exactly one create-route execution per selected mutation, and no duplicate dispatch through the legacy loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The create builder emits a prerequisite only for a real local parent/create edge, using the parent local ticket ID and never inventing a Jira key for an unbound parent.
- [x] The raw `OutboundMutation`, `OutboundCreatePayload`, and `outbound_pass` conversion preserve each prerequisite as planner-visible metadata; `_mutation_to_batch_dict` excludes it from Jira vendor fields.
- [x] Each provider create has `Mutation.target` equal to the local ID advertised to dependents, and planner tests prove that this identity resolves without a local-ID↔Jira-key conversion.
- [x] The batch sequencer selects eligible homogeneous outbound-create plans, executes them in planner dependency order through `apply_handlers.handle_create` and the single selected `create_route`, then removes only those executed/deferred creates from the legacy loop.
- [x] A confirmed parent create releases its child only after the parent’s matching local-ID-to-Jira binding and containment are confirmed; the child is dispatched once through the same route.
- [x] A permanent failure, `commit_unknown`, REST-budget defer, or unconfirmed containment holds the dependent as `dependency_deferred` and makes no child vendor-create call.
- [x] The batch and typed create adapters expose equivalent `confirmed`/`dependents_released` completion signals without dual-send or a second route selector.
- [x] An already-bound parent local ID satisfies the dependency without a new parent create; an unknown local parent ID is `dependency_deferred`; unrelated creates retain their existing behavior.
- [x] Focused payload, planner, scheduler, handler/route, and operation-coordinator suites pass.
baseline.summary: Emit and enforce reconciliation create-order dependency metadata

APPROVED (operator sign-off recorded 2026-07-24). Add a new Pass-4 coach move for T15 findings. Existing moves 1 (spike), 4 (riskiest-assumption test), and 7 (thin vertical slice) are adjacent but none captures the T15 remedy. The move is deliberately distinct from move 1: spike is a PLANNING-TIME experiment before plan approval that proves a mechanism or syntax and yields a decision; out-of-loop proof is an EXECUTION-TIME step the plan itself includes to prove the actual implementation works before it enters the slow delivery loop.

Move id 15 was available when this story was approved, but it has since landed as `sample, not the population` under closed ticket `amoral-natatorial-dog`. Preserve that shipped move unchanged and allocate the next free built-in id, 16, to this approved move.

## Work
- Add key `16` to `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` `MOVE_REGISTRY` with name `out-of-loop proof`, the approved template below verbatim, and `applies_when: ["T15"]`:

  `Build an out-of-loop proof of {subject} into the plan — an execution step that confirms the implementation works via the fastest local run or manual probe against the real target, before it is committed to the slow delivery loop.`
- Preserve move 15 and every other existing registry entry unchanged.
- Add the matching move-16 row to the mirrored coaching table in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- Add `out-of-loop proof` to the remaining registered moves in `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`, describing it as an execution step before the slow delivery loop rather than a planning-time spike.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `MOVE_REGISTRY["16"]` contains the approved template verbatim.
- [x] The move-16 template contains exactly one `{subject}` placeholder.

- [x] The author guide distinguishes move 16 as an execution-time step from the planning-time `spike` move.
- [x] The focused plan-review and review-kernel suites pass with the new scoped move.

## Testing
- Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py tests/unit/test_guides.py -q`.
- Run `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry validate-routing`.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Every change to the plan-review gate — a Pass-1 criterion prompt, a Pass-2 impact/validity question, a Pass-3 formula or threshold — lands on a handful of live dogfood reviews. No standing instrument answers "did this change make the gate better or worse?" before it ships; the prior calibration epic (`pastoral-aquatic-viper`, 6982) rejected live A/B batches on cost and parked the human gold set. The work is scattered across six epics and several orphan stories (`jira-reb-529`, `jira-reb-1589`, `fort-wisp-wren`, `spin-cub-usher`, `ridiculous-expert-mouse`, `auspicious-torrid-curlew`). This epic unifies them behind one harness.

The instrument already mostly exists as data. The live rebar store holds ~4,300 `plan_review_result_v2` sidecars on ~1,280 tickets (2026-06-27 → now; ~2,000 older ones pruned from the tree but recoverable from `origin/tickets` history) and `~/legacy-modernization-navigator` holds 74 more. Each v2 sidecar retains the raw Pass-1 findings, the complete Pass-2 answer vector, and the Pass-3 outputs (validity, impact, priority, `block_threshold`, decision). The reviewed plan text is not stored but is reconstructable from ticket `EDIT`/`SNAPSHOT` history and matchable against the stored `material_fingerprint` — a hash over a NORMALIZED, PARTIAL basis (description with checkbox-state/whitespace normalized away, file_impact, sorted child ids), so a match establishes normalized-material equivalence, not byte-exact text reconstruction. The store also carries free outcome labels: 2,483 revise→re-review pairs, 208 verdict flips on byte-identical material (the reviewer-noise floor), 84 `plan_defect` bug closes, 89 `caused_by` links, 199 plan-PASS→completion-FAIL tickets, 18 reopens.

## Approach

Three eval tiers, ordered by cost, each measuring one pass in isolation while holding the others fixed:

- **Tier 0 — Pass-3 replay (zero LLM).** Re-run `review_kernel.decide.pass3_decide` (and the post-verdict floors) over the whole corpus with a candidate formula/threshold/routing overlay; diff against stored decisions. Generalises `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` and `docs/experiments/calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py`. Runs on every proposal, unlimited.
- **Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay (Sonnet, ~$0.5/review uncached).** Re-run the verifier with candidate questions/prompt on the *stored* Pass-1 findings plus reconstructed plan text via the `verify_findings(run_chunk=…)` seam; score per-question agreement against stored answers, then feed Tier 0. The model re-run consumes the same normalized material the corpus builder reconstructs — normalized-basis equivalence is what the replay needs, not byte-exact text.
- **Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay (Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached, plus a Tier-1 run on the new findings).** Re-run finders with candidate criteria on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets); compare finding sets by `norm_id`/criterion; single-criterion mode (~$0.17/call) for per-criterion edits.

Non-negotiable invariants, enforced by the harness rather than by convention:

1. **Hard budget.** A committed ledger tracks every eval call priced via `genai-prices`; every run pre-flights a cost estimate and refuses to start if projected spend would exceed the remaining allocation. Epic-wide cap is **$200** total with a $30 reserve; commissioning spend is planned at ≤$120. Per-proposal costs are published.
2. **Model parity.** Every LLM re-run uses the exact production model class for that pass (frontier Opus for Pass 1, standard Sonnet for Pass 2) through **Bedrock only**, on a homogeneous provider chain (mixed Bedrock+Anthropic silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost). The harness records the per-pass model id in every result, refuses to diff runs whose per-pass model ids differ, and refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's `provider_provenance.ran_model`. Substituting a cheaper model to save budget is forbidden.
3. **Offline first.** Tier 0 and all label joins are pure functions of the frozen corpus; no proposal may be assessed on a live-only signal. Consistent with ADR 0054 and with 6982's rejection of live A/B.
4. **Noise-aware acceptance.** A change is reported as regressing/improving only when its label-proxy deltas exceed the noise band measured from identical-material flips and the Tier-1 reproduction run; otherwise "indistinguishable".

## Scope

New package `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` (corpus, labels, tier runners, ledger, report) with a `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay` entry; frozen corpus manifest + ledger + reports under `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/`; an ADR and a contributor guide section; fixes to `usage_log` ticket attribution. No CI provider dependency — everything runs locally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A frozen, versioned replay corpus exists covering both stores, with at-review plan text reconstructed and material-fingerprint-equivalent (normalized basis, full legacy generation ladder — see `celestine-treasonous-ewe`) for a majority of v2 sidecars; the builder reports the observed ratio without a hard threshold here — that ratio feeds `expectable-clownlike-ynambu` to decide if/where a floor is warranted; verified by the manifest's coverage counts and `verified_ratio`.
- [x] Outcome labels and a reviewer-noise floor are computed from the corpus with no LLM calls and joined to every review/finding; verified by a labels report listing counts per label source.
- [x] A Pass-3 change (formula, threshold, routing overlay) can be assessed over the entire corpus with zero LLM calls, producing a diff report (verdict flips, per-criterion deltas, label-proxy precision/recall, friction rate); verified by replaying current code against itself with zero diffs and replaying a known historical threshold change reproducing its documented effect.
- [x] A Pass-2 change can be assessed on a stratified sample using stored Pass-1 findings, with per-question agreement vs stored answers and downstream Tier-0 metrics; verified by a reproduction run whose agreement establishes the noise floor.
- [x] A Pass-1 change can be assessed on a fixed stratified sample with finding-set comparison by `norm_id`/criterion and downstream Tier-1/Tier-0 metrics; verified by one baseline sample run.
- [x] Every LLM eval call is priced and written to a committed ledger; a run whose pre-flight estimate exceeds remaining allocation is refused; total ledger spend at epic close is ≤ $200; verified by the ledger file and a test of the refusal path.
- [x] Every eval result records the per-pass model id; the harness refuses to diff results with differing model ids and refuses to run a pass on a model other than its production class via Bedrock; verified by unit tests and the ledger showing only Bedrock Opus/Sonnet ids.
- [x] Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call); verified from the usage log.
- [x] A contributor-facing protocol (ADR + docs) states which tier a proposal needs, the required report artifact, and the noise-band acceptance rule; verified by the docs landing and being referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Child decomposition

Corpus (1) → labels/noise floor (2) → Tier-0 (3) → Tier-1 (4) → Tier-2 (5) → ledger + model-parity + Bedrock chain (6-8, incl. the usage-log bug) → protocol ADR + docs (9). Folded in: `ridiculous-expert-mouse` (Tier-2 single-criterion consumer), `auspicious-torrid-curlew` (Tier-0-mined deterministic-floor candidates), `brutal-idiocratic-rodent` (deferred human-gold enrichment). `jira-reb-529` superseded (recorded-LLM-response mocking is infeasible; sidecar-replay delivers its intent). `jira-reb-1589`/`fort-wisp-wren` are downstream consumers; `spin-cub-usher`/`yip-gem-teak` are related but out of scope.

## Non-goals

Changing any production criterion, question, or threshold; a full human-adjudicated gold set; live A/B in the production gate.
baseline.summary: Plan-review process regression harness: replayable corpus + tiered evals under a hard $200 Bedrock budget

baseline.description:
## Why
The gate returns FINDINGS (what's wrong) but never coaches a productive MOVE (here's a play to address this class) — so a caller's next revision isn't primed with best practice. This Pass-4 "coach" adds affirmative, forward coaching over the surviving findings: it primes the caller toward a de-risking/clarifying move, without handing a ready-made solution. It is ADVISORY (never blocks) and is the shared coaching layer for `9da1` too.

## What
- A **single-turn, structured-output LLM call (NOT an agent, no tooling)** — the same cheap shape as the Pass-2
  aggregate verifier — running AFTER Pass-3 over ONLY the surviving (advisory, not-dropped) findings.
- It does TWO things only: (a) map each finding to a `move_id` from the fixed MOVE REGISTRY, (b) extract a short
  `subject` noun-phrase (what the move targets, drawn from the finding) that is VALIDATED by a deterministic
  SUBJECT VALIDATOR (v1 default: bounded = ≤ 8 words / ≤ 60 chars; REJECT if it contains code tokens — backticks,
  parentheses, `;`/`=`, or an `import`/`def`/`class` keyword — or a leading imperative verb; on REJECT, emit NO
  coaching for that finding — best-effort drop, never a retry-into-prose loop). Output schema:
  `[{move_id, subject, finding_refs[]}]`, CLUSTERED by move. The LLM authors NO free prose.
- **Deterministic rendering:** the coaching note is rendered from the move's LOCKED template + `subject`; the
  "name-the-move-not-the-answer" property is baked into the human-authored template, not the LLM's judgment.
- **MOVE REGISTRY (declarative, project-extensible — same pattern as the criteria/detector registries):** each
  move = `{id, triggers (criteria/finding-class), template, source}`. v1 moves: 1 spike/tracer-bullet ·
  2 prior-art/OSS-research/build-vs-buy · 3 pre-mortem · 4 riskiest-assumption-test · 5 weigh-alternatives
  (set-based) · 6 specification-by-example (observable "done") · 7 thin-vertical-slice · 8 ADR/one-way-door ·
  9 plan-the-verification · 11 propagate-revisions-to-children (fires when the ticket has children) ·
  12 generalize-the-finding-across-the-work (fires per review). Templates are IMPERATIVE actionable guidance.
- **C1-C4 authoring guardrails (LLM-recipient, positive-by-construction):** C1 actionable GUIDANCE (a move to
  pursue), NOT executable code/commands or the solution — enforced by the SUBJECT VALIDATOR above (not merely the
  template), since `subject` is the one free-text field the template interpolates; C2 reference findings BY ID, never restated;
  C3 select-from-registry + fill-subject (template enforces); C4 cap/cluster/front-load.
- **Caller-visible finding `id` contract:** the stable per-finding `id` is MINTED by the orchestrator (`ca03`)
  at result assembly (the content fingerprint) — its SOLE owner; this coach CONSUMES it (`finding_refs` point at
  that id) and the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`db7b`) records the same id; findings + coaching ship in ONE result
  so the reference resolves locally (no circular alignment).

## Scope
- INPUT is the CAPPED surfaced advisory set (Pass-3 surfaces the top-N advisory by priority score, config
  default 10); BLOCKING findings are surfaced UNCAPPED and may also be coached. The coach never alters the cap or
  the block decision.
- `src/rebar/` (in the gate's review pipeline) + a move-registry prompt-library entry. Reuses the rebar.llm
  single-turn structured-output path. Advisory only — coaching never affects the block/advisory decision (Pass-3).
- Grounded in LLM-feedback research (external-grounded feedback > self-reflection — Huang/DeepMind; anti-
  sycophancy; lost-in-the-middle; specific-actionable > Socratic). NOT human-pedagogy (no productive-struggle).
- Project-extensible: a project may add its own moves to the registry. Convergence expected in ~2-3 revisions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single-turn structured-output call over the surviving (advisory) findings; emits `{move_id, subject, finding_refs}` clustered by move; the LLM authors no free prose.
- [ ] Move registry (declarative, project-extensible) with moves 1-9,11,12 and LOCKED imperative templates; rendering is deterministic from template + subject.
- [ ] C1-C4 guardrails enforced by construction — INCLUDING a SUBJECT VALIDATOR (bounded noun-phrase; code/imperative/solution rejected) so C1 holds mechanically, not just via the template; plus reference-by-id, select-from-registry, cap/cluster/front-load.
- [ ] Coaching `finding_refs` reference the stable per-finding `id` MINTED by the orchestrator (`ca03`) at assembly (this coach is a CONSUMER, not the owner); findings + coaching ship in one result so the reference resolves locally.
- [ ] Advisory only — coaching never blocks and never alters the Pass-3 decision. Shared with `9da1`.
- [ ] Tested: finding→move mapping on a labelled set; deterministic render; reference resolution; a finding matching no move yields no coaching (best-effort).
baseline.summary: Pass-4 affirmative coach: single-turn structured-output coaching pass + move registry

## Why
`test_completion_floor_e2e.py::test_non_regression_floor_is_review_only` (`:178-198`) asserts, via `inspect.getsource` over the floor functions, that tokens like `sign_manifest`, `transition`, `reopen(` are ABSENT from their source, and that `completion_floor` does not appear in `rebar.llm.completion`. A pure change-detector: a rename / helper / indirect call evades it, and it exercises no runtime behavior. VALIDATED.

Context on what is testable: the floor's DECISION logic (which findings drop / are preserved / resurface on reopen) is ALREADY behaviorally covered by the sibling tests in this file (`test_floor_drops_and_preserves_per_gold_labels`, `test_floor_inactive_is_byte_identical`, `test_reopen_resurfaces_dropped_finding`). And `_apply_completion_floor_to_verdict` is a PURE verdict→verdict transform (no `repo_root`, no store/LLM I/O), so "it doesn't sign/transition" cannot be shown by a store snapshot or by spying a close-path function it structurally never calls — those tests are vacuous. The genuine, non-vacuous, non-duplicative behavioral content the old test was reaching for is the floor's **observable purity contract**: it only re-partitions findings and never emits any signing/attestation side-output.

## What
Replace the source-token test with a behavioral **purity-contract** test that runs the real floor over the existing gold fixture (a case that drops a finding) and asserts on OBSERVABLE state:
1. **Findings conserved (no create/lose/rewrite):** the multiset of finding ids across
   `advisory ∪ dropped` after the floor equals the set before — the floor only moves findings
   between the two lists (this is the observable analogue of "never signs/transitions/reopens";
   a floor that fabricated or dropped-without-recording a finding would fail it).
2. **No signing/attestation side-output:** the returned/mutated verdict grows NO
   `signature` / `attestation` / `attestations` key, and no new attestation KIND — the floor's
   only additions are the `dropped` list and the `coverage` narrowing annotation. (Assert the
   set of top-level verdict keys added by the floor ⊆ {`dropped`, and coverage sub-keys}.)
3. **Inputs not mutated:** the `cmap` argument and each finding's own content dict are unchanged
   by identity/value — the floor re-partitions list membership only, it does not rewrite the
   caller's inputs. (Deep-copy the inputs before the call; assert equal after.)
4. Keep the genuine artifact-contract assertion `attest._MANIFEST_PREFIX == "plan-review"`
   (no NEW attestation kind exists) — a real invariant, not a source grep.

Delete the `inspect.getsource` token-absence assertions (for the floor functions and for `rebar.llm.completion`). The confinement-of-the-floor-to-plan-review property is NOT asserted behaviorally, because it is a negative over a pure, structurally-separated function (any such test is vacuous against the current code); it is left to the module structure, and this ticket converts the false-confidence source grep into the real, observable purity assertions above.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_completion_floor_e2e.py` — replace `test_non_regression_floor_is_review_only`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A behavioral test runs the floor over the gold fixture and asserts findings are CONSERVED
      (the id set across `advisory ∪ dropped` is identical before/after — nothing fabricated or
      silently lost).
- [ ] The test asserts the floor adds NO `signature`/`attestation`/`attestations` key to the
      verdict (its only additions are `dropped` + the coverage narrowing).
- [ ] The test asserts the floor does not mutate its `cmap` input or the finding content dicts
      (pure re-partition) — verified against deep copies taken before the call.
- [ ] No `inspect.getsource` token-absence assertion remains; the
      `attest._MANIFEST_PREFIX == "plan-review"` artifact contract is retained.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Replace completion-floor review-only source-token test with a spy-based side-effect test

## Context / Problem
`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` prints only aggregate counts on a failing check (e.g. `active=41 new=2 increased=1 stale=7`). It never names the offending symbols, their files, current McCabe scores, or the baseline ceiling/threshold they breached. Diagnosing a CI failure (e.g. Gerrit run 32914110990) currently requires a separate local no-cache Ruff census plus manual baseline comparison — especially poor in resource-constrained CI-only workflows. Split out from bug 0ab0-6754-cc72-4d8c, which the operator classified not_a_bug: the terse output is the documented, --help-surfaced, unit-tested contract (module 'Exit-code contract' docstring + test_help_documents_contracts), so this is an approved ENHANCEMENT, not a defect.

## Plan
- Preserve the existing compact counter summary line (`active=<A> new=<N> increased=<I> stale=<S>`) byte-for-byte so anything parsing it today keeps working.
- On a FAILING `--check` (new>0 or increased>0), after the summary emit additive, deterministic per-symbol detail lines:
  - one line per `new` symbol: `  new       <file>::<symbol> score=<n> threshold=<15>`.
  - one line per `increased` symbol: `  increased <file>::<symbol> score=<n> ceiling=<c>`.
- Detail lines are stable-sorted (by key) within each group.
- Keep passing and stale-only output compact — NO detail lines when there is no regression.
- Do NOT alter the pass/fail gate logic (has_regression / exit codes) — formatting only over already-computed data; scanner/gate runtime unchanged.
- Update the module 'Exit-code contract' docstring accordingly.
- Add focused unit coverage for detail values, ordering, and absence-on-pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A failing `--check` names every `new` symbol with file::symbol, current score, and the allowed threshold.
- [x] A failing `--check` names every `increased` symbol with file::symbol, current score, and baseline ceiling.
- [x] Detail lines are stable-sorted and appear together with the existing summary line, which is unchanged.
- [x] A passing or stale-only check retains compact output with no violation detail lines.
- [x] Pass/fail gate logic and exit codes are unchanged.
- [x] Focused tests plus `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Diagnostics: surface per-symbol detail on complexity-baseline --check failure

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — **789 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (11 lines of headroom).

Eleven lines of headroom. Prompt text and prompt-assembly logic are often separable concerns here, but confirm against the call graph.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split llm/prompting/prompts.py (789 LOC) along its concern boundary

## Context
Discovered while landing abasic-doddering-harrier. Annotating `repo_root` parameters caused formatter-required wrapping and moved `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` from 784 to 793 LOC against the hard 800 cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The prior change is correct and merged; this task buys back module-size headroom through a behavior-preserving split.

Re-wrapping is not an alternative because `ruff format --check` enforces the current layout. Raising the cap is prohibited by project policy.

## Plan
- Create `src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py` for the existing git-ancestry/commit-resolution cluster: `resolve_event_commit`, `resolve_position_commit`, `build_ticket_position_commit_map`, `build_introducing_commit_map`, and `build_position_commit_map`. This is an existing call-graph seam of roughly 330 LOC, so the new module is above the 100-LOC floor while `authorship.py` returns to the 200-500 target band.
- Import and re-export all five names from `authorship_resolution.py` in `authorship.py`, preserving the current `rebar.attest.authorship.<name>` paths used by production callers and tests.
- Preserve the established subprocess monkeypatch seam explicitly without an import-time cycle. Each moved function that invokes git performs a lazy in-function `import rebar.attest.authorship as _authorship` immediately before the call, then uses `_authorship.subprocess.run(...)`. `authorship_resolution.py` has no top-level import back to `authorship.py`; the lazy lookup occurs only after package initialization and mirrors the existing lazy `tracker_dir` import pattern. Therefore `monkeypatch.setattr(authorship, "subprocess", ...)` still intercepts every moved git path. This is compatibility indirection only; git arguments, branches, timeouts, fallbacks, return values, and exception handling remain unchanged.
- Preserve the internal spy path explicitly: `verify_authorship_at_commit._resolve` remains in `authorship.py` and continues its module-global lookup of `resolve_event_commit`. The module-level imported binding is the re-export, and replacing `authorship.resolve_event_commit` updates that same module dictionary entry, so existing counting spies remain observable.
- Use Serena `find_referencing_symbols` on all five definitions, then use repository-wide `rg` for string-based `setattr`/`getattr`/parametrization sites that the LSP cannot resolve. The semantic census confirms production callers in `opcert.py`, `verify_authorship.py`, `verify_opcert.py`, `compact_txn.py`, and `compact.py`; direct test/helper callers include the authorship resolver/batching/performance suites, `_opcert_helpers.py`, and `test_opcert_storage.py`. The string sweep covers monkeypatch consumers in `test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py`, `test_authorship_resolver_git_flags.py`, `test_authorship_resolver_git_flags_heldout.py`, `test_identity_perf_1cc0.py`, `test_identity_ts2_09f9_heldout.py`, `test_verify_identity_a2c7_perf.py`, `test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py`, `test_compact_sweep_perf.py`, plus the integration bulk-parity test.
- Move code without changing decision logic. The only edited lookup is the lazy compatibility indirection required to preserve the existing subprocess test seam.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/attest/authorship.py)" -le 500` exits 0.
- [x] `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py)" -ge 100` exits 0.

- [x] `pytest -q tests/unit/test_authorship_resolver_git_flags.py tests/unit/test_authorship_resolver_git_flags_heldout.py tests/integration/test_authorship_resolver_bulk_parity.py` passes, proving the `authorship.subprocess` monkeypatch still intercepts every moved resolver path.
- [x] `pytest -q tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py tests/unit/test_identity_perf_1cc0.py tests/unit/test_identity_ts2_09f9_heldout.py tests/unit/test_verify_identity_a2c7_perf.py tests/unit/test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py tests/unit/test_opcert_storage.py` passes, proving `authorship.<name>` consumers still exercise the re-exported production paths.
- [x] `mypy src/rebar/attest --disallow-untyped-defs` reports no errors.
- [x] `test "$(grep -rhE ":\s*Any\b|->\s*Any\b" src/rebar/attest/*.py | wc -l | tr -d " ")" -eq 2` exits 0, preserving the two explicit trust-root boundary annotations.
- [x] `make lint` passes.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`CodeReviewBatchRunner.run` iterates only the static `req.criteria` list and stamps each finding
with `reviewer_id = prompt_id` and no logical criterion id
(`src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py:49,79`). The code-review gate YAML injects only the 13
built-in overlays (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml:77-94,109-126`), so an activated
project criterion never enters Round A/B and, even if it did, its findings could not be attributed
to `project.<name>`. Plan-review already solves the related dynamic-membership problem at runtime
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:206-225`). Code review differs because its
single runner serves both `round_a` and `round_b`; project fan-in must therefore be explicitly
once-only. This is the second of five seams (root cause on superseded bug 8a4b).

## Approach

Add a Round-A-only project-criteria input to the existing code-review runner:

- At the code-review batch assembly point in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (where
  `CodeReviewBatchRunner` is constructed around `gate_dispatch.py:643-645` and `repo_root` is
  available as `request.repo_root`), read `registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)` plus
  `registry.effective_routing(repo_root)`. Select active `project.` ids whose routing entry has
  `exec: LLM`; DET-tier project criteria remain outside this LLM finder path. Resolve each physical
  prompt with `criterion_prompt_id(cid, gate_key="code_review")`
  `[rebar:fc72-bf7e-7652-4228]` and build entries carrying both `prompt` and logical `criterion_id`.
- Extend `CodeReviewBatchRunner.__init__` with an additive default-empty `project_criteria` tuple.
  `run()` combines `req.criteria` with those entries only when `req.step_id == "round_a"`; for
  `round_b` it uses only `req.criteria`. The runner instance may therefore serve both YAML batch
  steps without double execution. Activated project criteria are deliberately once-per-review
  opt-ins rather than recommendation/glob-driven built-ins, so they run in Round A and do not
  consume or bypass the Round-B escalation cap of three. No seen-set or cross-run mutable state is
  used, keeping retries/replays deterministic.
- When a project entry emits findings, preserve any model-emitted `criteria` tags and append the
  logical `criterion_id` once if absent; keep the existing physical `reviewer_id` provenance.
- If an activated project criterion prompt is missing or malformed, fail loudly with a located
  `LLMError` naming the logical criterion and expected
  `.rebar/prompts/<physical-prompt-id>.md` path. Errors reading or validating
  `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` are not swallowed or degraded to built-ins: the shared criteria
  loader error propagates, so invalid project configuration cannot silently disable review.

**Rejected alternatives.** Adding static project slots to `code-review.yaml` cannot work because
project ids are repository-specific. Appending project entries to every `BatchRunRequest` would
execute them in both rounds. A mutable seen-set would make retries and replay depend on call order.
The Round-A-only branch on the stable YAML step id is explicit, stateless, and testable.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — assemble active LLM project entries and pass them to
  the runner.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` — accept project entries; inject them in Round A
  only; append logical criteria ids; raise a located prompt error.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` — extend the shared file; add a synthetic repo
  fixture that activates `project.foo` and writes
  `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-foo.md`, reused by later children.

`BatchRunRequest`, the workflow interpreter, YAML membership, Pass-3 routing, and the Round-B cap
are unchanged. Pass-3 project posture is owned by dependent child 58ef.

## Testing

- Happy path plus workflow boundary (`fan_in`): run the real two-round workflow with a stub finder;
  `project.foo` executes exactly once in `round_a`, never in `round_b`, and every emitted finding
  retains existing tags plus logical id `project.foo`.
- Direct runner edge: invoking a `round_b` request with project entries configured does not append
  or execute them; replaying a `round_a` request produces the same once-per-call plan without
  retained mutable state.
- Parity: an overlay-absent repo produces the same ordered built-in Round-A/Round-B requests and
  findings as before; no project entries are present.
- Config error (`missing`): active `project.foo` with no prompt raises a located `LLMError` naming
  both `project.foo` and `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-foo.md`.

Tier: unit plus an offline workflow integration using the real interpreter and stubbed agent calls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An activated LLM-tier project criterion executes exactly once across the complete Round-A +
      Round-B workflow, in Round A, and each finding preserves prior tags while carrying logical
      `project.<name>`; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k fan_in`.
- [ ] An overlay-absent repo yields the unchanged ordered built-in batches and findings; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k parity`.
- [ ] A project criterion with a missing prompt raises a located `LLMError` naming the criterion and
      expected path; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k missing`.
baseline.summary: Fan project criteria into Round A/B and attribute logical ids

baseline.description:
## Why
Beyond Claude Code (S4) and OpenCode, the portable `REBAR_SESSION_ID` / `AI_AGENT` provenance must be populated by each harness's own mechanism or the feature no-ops there. This story ships copy-paste capture shims for **Codex CLI** and **Cursor** cloud agents.

**Design correction (the epic's S6 premise was partly wrong — verified against vendor docs).** The epic sketched "a Codex SessionStart hook exports `REBAR_SESSION_ID`" and "a Cursor start-script exports `REBAR_SESSION_ID`", but:
- A Codex `SessionStart` hook **cannot export env vars** into the shell commands Codex later runs
  (a hook's only structured effect is `additionalContext`) — there is no `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`
  equivalent. Codex also exposes **no readable session-id env var** (rollout files live at
  `~/.codex/sessions/…/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl`). Source:
  https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference + /codex/hooks.
- Cursor's `.cursor/environment.json` has **no `env` field**, and Cursor exposes no readable
  session/agent-id env var; the first-class env mechanism is the dashboard **Secrets** tab.
  Source: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/setup + the environment.schema.json.

So both shims reliably set the **harness TAG** (`AI_AGENT`) via each harness's real injection point, and DOCUMENT the session-id limitation (set `REBAR_SESSION_ID` via profile / Secrets when a value is available). A Codex/Cursor `rebar claim` then records `claim_harness` even when the session id is not natively capturable.

## What
- **Codex (`scripts/session-shims/codex-config.toml`).** A `~/.codex/config.toml` fragment using
  `shell_environment_policy.set = { AI_AGENT = "codex" }` — the one reliable static injection
  point (applied to every Codex subprocess). Comments document that hooks can't export env, the
  rollout-file location, and the `experimental_use_profile` route for `REBAR_SESSION_ID`
  (`experimental_use_profile = true`, a documented `shell_environment_policy` bool per the cited
  Codex config reference, sources the user's shell profile into subprocesses).
- **Cursor (`scripts/session-shims/cursor-environment.json` + `cursor-provenance.sh`).** An
  example `.cursor/environment.json` whose `install` command runs `cursor-provenance.sh`, which
  idempotently (guarded by `grep -qF`) appends `export AI_AGENT=cursor` to the ephemeral,
  single-session cloud-agent VM's shell profile — specifically `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile`
  (the default login/interactive-shell rc files; creating an empty one if absent). Both files
  document the Secrets-tab path for `REBAR_SESSION_ID` and that the G3 not-in-profile caveat
  does not apply to a throwaway VM. Fail-safe (`exit 0`).
- **Docs (`docs/session-id-shims.md`).** New "Codex CLI" and "Cursor cloud agents" sections with
  the real mechanisms, the limitations, and the cited vendor source URLs.

## Scope
- IN: the Codex `config.toml` fragment, the Cursor `environment.json` + `cursor-provenance.sh`,
  the two new `docs/session-id-shims.md` sections, and a NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_shims.py`
  (valid TOML/JSON/shell; the harness tag is set; Cursor idempotency; docs document both with
  citations).
- OUT: Gemini CLI / other harnesses (follow-up); the record/read core (S1-S3, S5); the Claude
  Code shim (S4). Dynamic per-session-id capture for Codex/Cursor is not possible from these
  harnesses today and is explicitly documented as a limitation, not delivered.

## Acceptance Criteria
(All proofs are in a NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_shims.py` — the existing `test_session_shims.py` is S4's; S6 does not modify it.)
- [ ] `scripts/session-shims/codex-config.toml` is valid TOML and sets
      `shell_environment_policy.set.AI_AGENT == "codex"` (asserted by `tomllib.loads`). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_shims.py -k codex -q`.
- [ ] `scripts/session-shims/cursor-environment.json` is valid JSON whose `install` runs

      (`~/.bashrc` AND `~/.profile`) — idempotent, no accumulation in either. Proof:

- [ ] `docs/session-id-shims.md` documents both harnesses' real mechanism + limitation with

Keep verbose `session_log` bodies out of the dependency-graph and store-health hot paths, and out of default `list`, while keeping them in `search` and `show`.

## Why

`reduce_all_tickets()` compiles full bodies with no lazy-loading and backs `ready`, `next_batch`, `deps`, `validate`, and `list`. Verbose logs must not tax those. The requester chose "searchable, hidden from list": logs appear in keyword `search` and `show` but nowhere that would slow the constant graph/health work.

## What

- Add an `exclude_ticket_types` (or `exclude_session_logs`) parameter to
  `reduce_all_tickets()` in `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, mirroring the existing
  `exclude_archived` / `exclude_deleted` pattern.
- Default it on for graph/health callers: `src/rebar/graph/_ready.py`
  (`find_ready_tickets`), `src/rebar/graph/_graph.py` (`build_dep_graph`),
  `src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` (`compute`), and
  `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py` (`validate_state` health checks).
- Exclude `session_log` from default `list` (surface only on explicit
  `--type=session_log`) in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` /
  `src/rebar/reducer/_filters.py`.
- Keep `session_log` in the `search` corpus (`src/rebar/reducer/search.py`) and in
  `show` (single-ticket reduce path unchanged).

## Scope

Read-path visibility and graph/health isolation only. The recent-logs command is a separate story.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ready`, `next_batch`, `deps`, and `validate` never include `session_log`
      tickets and their timings are unaffected by log count/size (asserted).
- [ ] Default `list` omits `session_log`; `list --type=session_log` returns them.
- [ ] `search <keywords>` matches `session_log` bodies; `show` returns a
      `session_log` fully.
- [ ] `validate` does not flag `session_log` tickets as orphaned/empty/etc.
- [ ] Tests assert both the exclusions and the inclusions.
baseline.summary: Isolate session_log from graph/health compile paths and default list
