## Context / Problem

`caused_by` is the store's only machine-readable causation edge and it is not trustworthy: `rebar link <bug> <target> caused_by` accepts ANY target, so `rebar metrics` (`bug_caused_by_fan_in`) and the epic-close `caused_by` floor reason over edges nobody validated. The most-linked target today is a misattribution whose "children" are unrelated CI items.

Verified against `origin/main` first: `rebar link` validates only relation grammar, cycles, the redundant-link guard and the closed-source guard (`graph/_links.py:add_dependency`), and has NO `--force`. The "does a commit reference this ticket?" scan exists exactly once, privately, as `_referencing_commits` in `_commands/close_precheck.py`; its `[]` return conflates "scanned, none found" with "no git history".

## Approach

1. Hoist the trailer/subject scan into the existing shared module
   `_engine_support/commit_impact.py` as `referencing_commits(ids, tracker, repo_root)`
   returning `list[str] | None`, `None` = "git history unreadable" — the same `None`-vs-`[]`
   distinction `changed_paths` there already uses. `close_precheck._referencing_commits`
   becomes a thin `... or []` delegate KEEPING ITS NAME (a string monkeypatch target in
   `tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py`); `_referencing_commit_exists` — re-exported by
   `transition_close` and asserted directly in `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` — still
   delegates to it, so both keep their current contracts.
2. Add ONE predicate `caused_by_refusal(target_id, relation, tracker, code_root) -> str | None`
   in `_commands/link_revert.py`. BOTH `link_core` (the write) and `_link_dry_run` (the
   preview) call it: `_link_dry_run` does not route through `link_core`, so a shared
   predicate — not a shared code path — is what stops the preview drifting from the refusal.
3. The rule: for `caused_by`, the RESOLVED TARGET must have >=1 referencing commit — the
   target ITSELF, not its descendants, because `caused_by` must name the specific change that
   introduced the defect and crediting an epic through its children is the exact
   misattribution this story exists to stop. `caused_by` is never hierarchy-promoted, so the
   resolved target is the requested one.
4. Command layer, not `add_dependency`: `rebar.graph` is the store layer, runs NO git and
   takes no `repo_root` (only `tracker_dir`), and `link_core` is its only functional caller.
   Both callers resolve the CODE root as `config.repo_root(repo_root)` and pass THAT — never
   the tracker dir, which an absolute `tracker.dir` can relocate — mirroring close_precheck's
   `code_root`/`tracker` split.
5. Unverifiable is NOT invalid: `None` from the scan (no code repo / no commits) allows the
   link. A refusal must mean "this target has no commit", never "this clone has no history".
6. Escape hatch `--force[=<reason>]` on the CLI, `force=` on library and MCP, spelled as
   `claim --force`. Its parser moves to `_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:extract_force` and
   `claim._parse_force` delegates, so the CLAIM-STYLE spelling has one implementation shared
   by claim and link. `transition._extract_force` and `tracker_maintenance` keep theirs:
   transition's bare `--force` yields `''`, not `'(no reason given)'` — a different contract.
7. Reconciler: `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:337` applies arbitrary
   inbound relations through `rebar.link` and fails open, so a peer-authored `caused_by` whose
   commit lives only in another clone would be dropped and recorded as an impossible link.
   That call passes `force="inbound reconcile: peer-authored edge"`; sync is unchanged.
8. Oracle: a `"link"` branch in `write_parity_contract.execute()` (and `Case.op`), plus `link`
   on the Adapter protocol and all three adapters changed from `(a, b, relation) -> None` to
   `(a, b, relation, *, force=None) -> Outcome`. `adapter.link` IS called, at
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py:147` (`test_deps_parity`), which discards the
   return; that file joins Scope and gains `assert adapter.link(a, b, "blocks")`.
9. `SKILL.md`: the rule governs the `rebar link ... caused_by` form (CLI/library/MCP) ONLY —
   the close's `--caused-by=<id>` flag writes via `transition_close._apply_caused_by` and is
   NOT gated. Say that at the early-link instruction (~L598-607) AND at the Omission case
   (~L633-644), whose scope-of-work story/epic target is commit-less by construction, with
   the worked example `rebar link <bug> <story> caused_by --force="scope-of-work attribution:
   the story that should have covered this case has no introducing commit"` plus a note to
   repeat that reason in the RCA. Unattributable still leaves the link unset.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt`, `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`, `tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py` (new), `tests/interfaces/adapters.py`, `tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`, `docs/ticket-model.md`, `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`.

## Explicitly OUT of scope

The original plan's `introducing_sha` field + `rebar fsck` date check and the "attach the 196-row corpus" criterion are cut and re-filed as a follow-up linked `discovered_from`: no surface writes `introducing_sha` so it would land dead; `fsck` is a STORE-integrity walker that must run where no code repo exists; the corpus is absent from the repo.

## Testing

New `tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py`, over a store whose code repo has real commits: happy path (a target carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer commit links); refusal (the error names the target and `--force`; `show_ticket(...)["deps"]` unchanged); `force="..."` records the edge; `relates_to`/`blocks` to the same target unaffected; a commit-less code repo allows the link; `--dry-run` prints "Would reject" and writes nothing; `close_precheck._referencing_commits` still resolves by name and still returns `[]`.

Pinning: `tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py`, `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py`, `tests/unit/test_caused_by_dedup_10d0.py`, `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py`, `tests/unit/test_close_gate_*.py`, `tests/unit/test_claim_*.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_parity.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A `caused_by` link to a commit-less target is refused identically on library, CLI and
      MCP, `force` bypassing it on all three; two new `op="link"` rows make
      `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py -q` cover it.
- [x] The refusal names the target and the escape hatch, leaves the store unwritten, previews
      under `--dry-run`, and allows a commit-less code repo; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py -q`.
- [x] The scan has ONE implementation:
      `test $(grep -cE '%H%x1f' src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py) -eq 0`.
- [x] The delegate keeps its name:
      `test $(grep -cE '^def _referencing_commits' src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py) -eq 1`.
- [x] The close gate is behaviour-identical:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py tests/unit/test_transition_close.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -q`.
- [x] Docs state the rule: `grep -q 'referencing commit' docs/ticket-model.md` (absent today).
- [x] SKILL.md carries the forced-link example:
      `test $(grep -c 'scope-of-work attribution' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md) -eq 1`.
- [x] Gates green: `make lint`; `make typecheck`;
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting `new=0 increased=0`.
baseline.summary: Refuse a caused_by link whose target has no referencing commit

baseline.description:
# The pass that GENERATES blocking findings moves to the cheapest model the moment b690 lands

## Severity framing

This is not a cost or consistency issue. **Pass-1 of plan-review is the finder** — it produces the findings that become blocking and gate every `claim`. Moving it to a weaker model makes the gate QUIETLY MORE PERMISSIVE, and there is no alarm for "the review was weaker than it should have been". `b690`'s change is `LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1` and green on every offline test, because **none of this risk is test-detectable**: the offline suite substitutes `FunctionModel`/`FakeRunner` for exactly the thing that changes, which is WHICH MODEL a live gate calls.

## The mechanism, verified end to end

Under this repo's actual config there is **no `model_classes` table anywhere** (no `[llm]` in `rebar.toml`, no `[tool.rebar…]` LLM keys in `pyproject.toml`, no `.rebar/config.conf`, no `REBAR_LLM_*` in shell rc / LaunchAgents / CI), so classes take built-in defaults:

    trivial -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5   standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   LLMConfig.from_env().model -> claude-opus-4-8

**Crucially, plan-review's runner floor is NOT `cfg.model`.** `plan_review/__init__.py:609` calls `produce_plan_review_verdict(ctx, _verifier_cfg(cfg), …)`, so the whole run's `runner._config.model` is `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. Then:

1. `gate_dispatch.py:163` builds `ProductionBatchRunner(runner=get_runner(_verifier_cfg(cfg)))`
   → floor = sonnet.
2. `production_batch_runner.run` does `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0]))`
   → `plan-review.yaml:62-65` rung 0 is `trivial` → **haiku**.
3. `pass1.py:484` → `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` → `passes.pass1_chunk` builds
   `RunRequest(..., config=cfg)` (`passes.py:319-330`).
4. **PRE-b690** the runner opened `cfg = self._config` and DISCARDED `req.config` → Pass-1 actually
   ran on **sonnet**. **POST-b690** it honours the declaration and runs on **haiku**.

Measured:

    gate runner floor model  : anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    Pass-1 batch cfg.model   : anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5
    PRE-b690  effective model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    POST-b690 effective model: anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5

**The smoking gun that this was never intended-and-tested:** `origin/main`'s own `_verifier_cfg` docstring asserts "The Pass-1 finder is unaffected: it runs the YAML `model_ladder` via the ProductionBatchRunner, not `cfg.model`." **That comment is FALSE on main**, and `b690` is what makes it true. `git log -L62,66` on `plan-review.yaml` shows Pass-1 has declared the cheapest rung since the workflow was born (originally the literal `claude-haiku-4-5`) and has **never once actually run on it**.

## Why the ladder does not save it

`pass1_with_ladder` escalates on a **context-limit signal** — it is a SIZE ladder, not a quality ladder (its own docstring says so). A plan that fits haiku's 200k window stays on haiku forever. Some Pass-1 chunks also run `execution_mode="agentic"` (code-grounding with tool calls), where the drop from sonnet to haiku is a large capability change, not a marginal one.

Secondary effect on the prerequisite finder (`registry.py:361-367` gives it `"default_posture": "blocking"`): `pack_prerequisite_bins(..., model=cfg.model)` now packs for haiku's 200k instead of sonnet's 1M, so context-limit escalation genuinely fires where it previously could not. Escalation does work (`models_at_or_above('claude-haiku-4-5')` → `['claude-haiku-4-5','claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-opus-4-8']`), but the first attempt is a real downgrade and every attempt burns tokens.

## Why it is silent rather than loud

The gates fail CLOSED on errors — `attest_gate.py:112-125` blocks a claim on a missing/stale attestation, and an LLM outage degrades to INDETERMINATE → no signature → claim blocked. That is the loud path and it is fine. **This is the other kind:** a haiku Pass-1 that surfaces fewer grounded findings yields a **PASS**, which gets signed, and the claim proceeds. The sidecar records only the VERIFIER's model (`data.model`), never Pass-1's, so it is invisible in the artifacts too.

## An asymmetry worth deciding on

Code-review's Pass-1 finder declares **`frontier`** (`code-review.yaml`, landed by 3768). Plan-review's Pass-1 declares **`trivial`**. Both are finders that generate blocking findings. That asymmetry may be deliberate, but it has never been effective, so it has never been evaluated.

## The decision, made by the operator and confirmed by archaeology

**Pass-1 (the finder) runs on `frontier`/opus. Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach run on `standard`/sonnet.** That split is what `_verifier_cfg` was written to express, and its own docstring already asserts it ("The Pass-1 finder is unaffected"). The docstring has simply been false since 2026-06-27.

This is a RESTORATION, not a new preference. The sidecar record shows 115 plan reviews generating findings on opus up to 2026-06-27, then zero ever since — a total changeover one day after `4beec08a4` introduced the verifier downgrade and accidentally applied it to the whole run. See the archaeology comment for the day-by-day table.

**b690 is the ENABLER.** Until it landed, `PydanticAIRunner.run` discarded `req.config`, so NO ladder rung could influence Pass-1 at all. With b690, the declaration is finally reachable — and it says `trivial`, which is why the regression would deepen rather than heal on its own.

**The change:** `plan-review.yaml`'s `model_ladder` entry rung `trivial` -> `frontier`. `standard` would freeze the regression; `trivial` would deepen it.

Note that with rung 0 at `frontier`, `models_at_or_above(opus)` returns just `[opus]`, so model escalation becomes a no-op. That costs nothing: sonnet and opus share the same 1M window, so the only size-meaningful step was ever haiku->sonnet, and the size handling that matters (batch -> one-criterion-per-call -> the P8 too-big finding) is independent of the model rungs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `plan-review.yaml`'s Pass-1 `model_ladder` entry rung is `frontier`, so findings generate on
      opus as they did before 2026-06-27
- [ ] Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach remain on the verifier model (`standard`/sonnet) — this ticket
      must not disturb the downgrade that `_verifier_cfg` correctly applies to them
- [ ] a test asserts the EFFECTIVE model of Pass-1 at the seam that decides it
      (`ProductionBatchRunner` -> `run_pass1` -> `pass1_chunk`, i.e. the model reaching the runner),
      so a future change cannot silently move the finder again. Asserting the YAML text is NOT
      sufficient — the YAML has said `trivial` for five weeks while sonnet actually ran
- [ ] a test asserts Pass-1 and Pass-2 resolve to DIFFERENT models under the default config, since
      the defect was precisely the two collapsing onto one
- [ ] `_verifier_cfg`'s docstring claim that "the Pass-1 finder is unaffected" is either true after
      this change or corrected — it must not remain a false assertion in the code
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real plan-review run after the change records opus for the Pass-1 finder,
      cited from `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-step attribution (which story b690 made possible)
- [ ] the prerequisite finder's bin packing is checked against opus's window, since
      `pack_prerequisite_bins` sizes to `cfg.model`

## Notes

Found by an independent landing-safety assessment of the epic stack, NOT by the offline suite — which is green at the stack tip and cannot see this. `b690` itself is closed and correct in its own terms: it made declarations effective. This ticket is about one declaration that turns out to be wrong.
baseline.summary: b690 silently downgrades the plan-review Pass-1 finder from sonnet to haiku, weakening the claim gate that generates blocking findings

baseline.description:
Build the one-time strip as a committed operational script, and prove it on a scratch clone before any window. **No new dependency**: `git-filter-repo` is deliberately not used. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why stock plumbing
`git fast-export --no-data --signed-tags=strip --export-marks=old.marks tickets` | filter | `git fast-import --export-marks=new.marks`. Verified on the real branch: the stream carries `M 100644 <sha> <path>` with **zero** inline blob data (26 MB stream for ~49,900 commits), so the filter is line-oriented text processing that never moves the ~1 GiB. No `deleteall`; no tags in a branch export (so `--signed-tags=strip` is a harmless no-op); merges ride `merge :n`; **empty commits are kept**, so DAG topology and every file's introduction point survive — which is exactly what ancestry-based authorship verification needs. filter-repo would prune them and reshape the graph.

**Proven result:** 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%), all commits and all merge commits preserved, HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths, ~30 s end to end.

## Required corrections (each was a real defect found in review)
1. Must run in a fresh **UNFILTERED** clone — `fast-import` hard-fails `fatal: blob not found` in a
   `blob:none` partial clone, and this host's `origin` is one.
2. Strip **both** `.bridge_state/` **and** `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` prefixes — B6 removes the
   latter at HEAD only; its 33 MB stays in history.
3. **Derive the re-add set DYNAMICALLY** — `git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state/` —
   never a hardcoded list. It is three files today but **A2-1 adds `get_rotation.json`**, so at window
   time it is four; a hardcoded list would fail the tree-identity assertion.
4. The filter must be **`data <n>`-length-aware**, not `grep -v`: commit messages live inside `data`
   blocks. (Today 0 of ~49,900 messages begin with `M `/`D `, but the script must not rely on that.)
5. Push with **`--force-with-lease`**, never `--force` — the remote tip moves constantly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a scratch unfiltered clone, the script produces a rewritten branch whose **commit count and
      merge-commit count are unchanged** (measured at run time, not hardcoded). Tier: **repo-level
      assertion in the dry-run harness**.
- [ ] `rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree}` **equals** the old tip tree after the dynamic re-add. Tier:
      **repo-level assertion**. This is the "not one byte of live content changed" invariant.
- [ ] The re-add set is discovered from `ls-tree`, proven by a fixture where a 4th `.bridge_state`
      file exists. Tier: **integration** with a synthetic 4-file store.
- [ ] Pack size drops to <=15% of the original. Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] The filter preserves a commit message that begins with `M ` (adversarial fixture). Tier:
      **unit** on the stream filter.
- [ ] The script refuses to run in a partial clone, with a clear message. Tier: **integration**
      against a `--filter=blob:none` clone.
- [ ] All assertions run **before** any push; the script has no push step of its own.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reclaim-bridge-history.sh` (or `.py`), dry-run harness, tests

Scope: M. No code dependencies; must exist before A6-1.
baseline.summary: A6-0c: build and dry-run the history-strip script using stock git plumbing

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Three agents on 2026-08-05 reported contradictory answers to "does ticking an AC checkbox invalidate a plan-review attestation?". The contradiction is a DIAGNOSTIC defect, not a behavioral one, and the empirical answer is now settled (see Findings). Every attestation staleness message today names a fixed, partly-fictional list of inputs, so a reader cannot tell which input actually changed and hunts for an edit that could never have been the cause. The operator has approved fixing this broadly: wherever rebar reports an attestation error, it must say WHAT CHANGED. That approval covers this ticket's whole scope, including the additive manifest change described below.

## Findings that fix the scope (verified in this checkout)

- The material basis is a SINGLE composite sha256, built in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` `material_fingerprint()` over exactly four keys —
  `ticket_id`, `description`, `file_impact`, `children` — plus `file_impact_scope` when the
  scope is `none`. Verified by reading `pass1.py:750-777`.
- AC checkbox STATE is normalized out of that basis by
  `pass1.py::_normalize_checkbox_state` (`pass1.py:741-747`, bug 330c). Ticking `- [ ]` to
  `- [x]` therefore does NOT invalidate an attestation. Confirmed by running
  `material_fingerprint` over a tick-only description pair: the hashes are equal.
- "AC" is NOT a basis component. Acceptance criteria live inside `description`. Every current
  message says "description/AC/file_impact/children", naming an input that does not exist.
- A pre-330c attestation hashed the RAW description, so after a tick neither the normalized
  recompute nor the `attest.py::_legacy_material_ok` grandfather (`attest.py:614-631`) can
  match, and it reads `stale-material` with no component actually edited. This is the residual
  cause the current message hides, and it reconciles observation 3 in the original report.
- `children` is derived from OTHER tickets' `parent_id` at read time
  (`relation_snapshot.py::live_material_children`), not from this ticket's own event log.
- The signed manifest ALREADY carries per-child/prerequisite pins —
  `plan-material-pin: <role> <id> <fingerprint>` parsed by `manifest.py::manifest_pins`
  (`manifest.py:428-457`) — so the signed child-id set is recoverable from any pinned
  attestation without any schema change.

## Approach

Add per-component fingerprints to the signed manifest and diff them component-wise on read.

Concretely:

1. New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` holding two functions.
   `material_components(ctx)` returns `{name: hash16}` for each basis key, hashing exactly the
   same per-key values `material_fingerprint` already feeds into the composite (so the two can
   never disagree). `explain_material_change(attestation, ticket_id, repo_root)` returns a
   compact human string naming the components that differ.
2. `manifest.py::build_manifest` emits one additive, deterministic line per component:
   `material-part: <name> <hash16>`, sorted by name. `manifest.py` gains
   `manifest_material_parts()` to parse them back. The lines are additive, so an existing
   verifier ignores them and a pre-change manifest simply parses to `{}`. The prefix cannot
   collide with `manifest_material()`, which matches `startswith("material:")`.
3. `attest.py::compute_validity` calls `explain_material_change` for BOTH `stale-material`
   returns (plan-review at `attest.py:588-601` and completion-verifier at `attest.py:527-538`)
   and puts the named components in `reason`. It also names the reopen timestamp on
   `stale-reopened` and keeps the already-specific `stale-code` / `stale-head` wording (both
   already name the drifted paths / the two SHAs).
4. `attest_gate.py::claim_gate_check`'s `unsigned` message (`attest_gate.py:121-126`) states
   both remedies, because rebar cannot distinguish "never reviewed" from "review PASSed but
   signing aborted": run `rebar review-plan <id>`, or `rebar sign-review <id>` if a review
   already passed. `claim_gate_check` already forwards `compute_validity`'s `reason` verbatim,
   and `_commands/transition_close.py::_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error` and
   `_commands/claim.py` render that same string, so fixing the source fixes the claim gate, the
   close gate and `review-plan --status` together.
5. The sites that re-word or drop the reason instead of forwarding it are pointed at the same
   helper or made to carry the data they already hold:
   - `generation.py:265-269` and `resign.py:198-208` — replace the fixed list with the named
     components.
   - `generation.py:270-273` — "a dependency's plan material changed since the review" names no
     dependency, although the changed pin set is in hand; `resign.py:262-270` already names the
     ids, so this one is brought to parity.
   - `completion.py:178` — a child's closure-validity detail is currently
     `f"signature: {sig.get('verdict')}"`, dropping the reason that explains it; it forwards the
     reason too.
   - `_cli/_llm_commands.py:118-141` — a `plan_review_sign_aborted` signing failure currently
     renders the generic "run `rebar sign-review`" advice, which is wrong for the
     `store-read-failure` reason (a re-sign hits the same unreadable read). It gets its own
     branch naming the reason and the correct remedy.
   - `attest_gate.py:166-167` — the docstring's verdict vocabulary omits `not-closed`,
     `malformed-phase`, `incompatible-phase` and the `stale-pin-*` values; corrected so the
     documented list matches what `compute_validity` can actually return.

   These were found by an exhaustive sweep of every attestation refusal surface. Surfaces
   deliberately left unchanged because they already forward the reason verbatim:
   `_commands/gates.py::_claim_gate_reason`, `_commands/transition_close.py`, and
   `llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`. `attest/opcert.py` and `signing.py` are also left
   alone: their verdicts are cryptographic (`mismatch` / `foreign_key`), not staleness, and
   already name the two keys or ids that differ.

Why this approach: the composite hash is one-way, so naming a changed component requires the old per-component values, and the only trustworthy source for them is the SIGNED manifest — anything reconstructed at read time could disagree with what the reviewer actually saw. The alternative of replaying the event store to `signed_at` is rejected: `children` comes from other tickets' state, so it would need a whole-store replay, and compaction squashes exactly the old events where legacy attestations live. Adding the parts to the manifest is additive, authenticated by the existing HMAC, and deterministic (no timestamps), so re-signing stays reproducible.

Attestations signed before this change carry no `material-part:` lines. For them `explain_material_change` degrades in two useful steps rather than falling back to the old fixed list: it uses the signed `plan-material-pin:` child ids to report a `children` add/remove diff when one exists, and when no component difference can be named it says so plainly and points at the pre-330c normalization basis as the likely cause, with the remedy.

No gate outcome changes: every edit is inside the `reason` string of an already-failing branch, or is a new additive manifest line. No branch condition, threshold or verdict value is touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` (new) — component hashing + the diff/explain
  helper.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — emit and parse `material-part:` lines.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — component-named `stale-material` reasons (both
  kinds); timestamp-named `stale-reopened`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` — actionable `unsigned` message.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — forward the child-closure validity reason, not just the
  verdict.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — a dedicated render branch for a `plan_review_sign_aborted`
  signing failure that names the reason and the correct remedy.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — state plainly that ticking a checkbox is attestation-safe, and
  document the component-named staleness reasons.
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` (new) — the tests below.

`pass1.py` is at 776 of the 800-line cap, so the new hashing helper goes in `material_diff.py` and `pass1.py` is not touched.

## Testing

- Happy path: an attestation whose `file_impact` changed reports a reason containing
  `file_impact` and NOT `description` or `children`; likewise a description-only edit and a
  children-only edit, one test each.
- Checkbox pin (330c): an attestation over a description whose boxes are then ticked reports
  `certified`, not `stale-material` — pinning the normalization that is currently only implicit.
- Legacy/grandfather regression: a pre-330c attestation (raw-description basis) over an
  unchanged ticket still reports `certified`, and one that cannot be grandfathered reports the
  "no component differs" wording rather than a spurious component name.
- Edge: an attestation with no `material-part:` lines and no pins still produces an actionable
  reason and never raises.
- Gate-outcome invariance: for each of the stale verdicts, assert `valid is False` and the
  `verdict` value is unchanged from the current code — the same inputs are still refused.
- The full existing suites `tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_material_grandfather_96d1.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` and `tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py`
  pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `material_diff.material_components(ctx)` returns a per-component hash map whose keys are
      exactly the `material_fingerprint` basis keys; verified by a test that asserts the key set
      matches and that changing one component changes only that component's hash.
- [ ] `build_manifest` emits sorted `material-part: <name> <hash16>` lines and
      `manifest_material_parts()` round-trips them; verified by a test asserting the round-trip
      and that a manifest without the lines parses to `{}`.
- [ ] A `stale-material` reason from `compute_validity` NAMES the differing component(s) with a
      compact magnitude (for example `file_impact: 13 -> 16 paths`) and does not contain the
      string `description/AC/file_impact/children`; verified by one test per component, plus a
      repo-wide grep asserting that literal no longer appears in `src/`.
- [ ] Ticking checkboxes only leaves the verdict `certified`; verified by a test that signs over
      an unticked description, ticks every box, and asserts `compute_validity` returns
      `verdict == "certified"`.
- [ ] A pre-330c (raw-description) attestation over an unchanged ticket still returns
      `certified`, and an un-grandfatherable one returns a reason that says no component differs
      rather than naming a component; verified by two tests.
- [ ] `stale-reopened` names the reopen timestamp and `unsigned` names both `review-plan` and
      `sign-review` remedies; verified by asserting those substrings in the reasons.
- [ ] A `plan_review_sign_aborted` signing failure renders its reason (for example
      `store-read-failure`) and does NOT advise `sign-review`; verified by a test that feeds a
      verdict carrying that event to the renderer and asserts both facts.
- [ ] A dependency-material change from `generation.py` names the changed dependency ticket
      ids, matching `resign.py`'s existing wording; verified by asserting the ids appear in the
      raised message.
- [ ] No gate outcome changes: for every branch touched, a test asserts the same
      `(valid, verdict)` pair as before, and `pytest tests/unit tests/integration` passes.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states plainly that ticking an AC checkbox is
      attestation-safe; verified by a grep for that statement in the file.

## Provenance

Three independent agent reports on 2026-08-05, recorded in the original description above. Related: bug 858c-786a-13be-4332 (the close gate cannot express an N/A criterion).
baseline.summary: Whether ticking an AC checkbox invalidates a plan-review attestation is inconsistent across tickets

baseline.description:
## Symptom
A `preview` route pass, and a legacy `--mode dry-run` pass, perform REMOTE Jira writes during pending-binding recovery. Both modes are documented and reported as no-write.

## Evidence (verified by reading the spine)
- `run_differs.py` guards the recovery call with exactly ONE condition, `if not scoped_ids` (where `scoped_ids = ctx.filter_local_ids or ctx.selection_ids`). There is no `persist` / `no_write` / mode condition on it.
- The client it is handed is the real configured transport: `outbound_diff_client = backend.transport`, and `_load_reconcile_backend()` calls `select_backend(load_config())` unconditionally — there is no dry-run branch that substitutes a no-op transport.
- The keyed-pending branch of `recover_pending_bindings` then calls `client.add_label(key, "rebar-id:<local_id>")` and `client.set_entity_property(key, "local_id", <local_id>)`. Those are mutations of the remote issue.
- For contrast, the sibling invariant-filing gate in the same function DOES compose both axes: `skip_invariant_filing = (not persist) or bool(scoped_ids)`. So the omission on the recovery call is asymmetric with the code beside it.

Net effect: `persist=False` suppresses the local binding-store `save()` (it sits inside `reconcile.py`'s `if persist:` block), so the LOCAL side of recovery is correctly not persisted — but the REMOTE label/entity-property writes still go out. A preview therefore mutates Jira and then throws away the local record of having done so, which is also the least recoverable combination.

## Why this was not fixed in RP-02 S3
RP-02 S3 adds a NEW recovery operation (interrupted-retirement completion) and gates it on `persist and not scoped_ids`. It deliberately does NOT change the pre-existing create-recovery gate: that is a behaviour change to load-bearing anti-duplicate machinery, outside an extraction-plus-addition slice, and S3 T1 carries an explicit acceptance criterion that the create-recovery gate is pinned unchanged. The real behaviour is pinned by test, and the correction is filed here.

## Judgement needed before fixing
This is not a one-line gate addition, because there is a real argument on both sides:
- Suppressing recovery on a preview keeps the promise that preview never mutates.
- Recovery exists to prevent duplicate Jira issues after a crash. A preview that skips it is harmless, but an operator who only ever runs preview would never recover a keyed-pending binding.

The likely correct answer is to suppress the REMOTE writes on a no-write pass while still reporting what recovery WOULD do, matching how the rest of preview behaves. That needs its own plan and its own oracles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A `preview` pass performs zero remote `add_label` / `set_entity_property` calls from pending-binding recovery.
- [x] A legacy `--mode dry-run` pass performs zero such remote calls.
- [x] A live pass's recovery behaviour is unchanged, including the keyed-pending no-search rule and the three-miss plus 3600-second keyless conjunction.
- [x] The chosen disposition (suppress silently vs. report-what-would-happen) is recorded with its rationale.
- [x] A regression test drives a no-write pass with a keyed-pending binding and asserts zero remote identity writes.

## Fix plan & chosen disposition (AC#4)
**Disposition: suppress the remote recovery writes silently on a no-write pass.** This matches how the rest of preview/dry-run behaves (it suppresses all other remote mutations without a separate 'would-do' report), and it keeps the change minimal and symmetric with the sibling gates in the same function (`skip_invariant_filing = (not persist) or bool(scoped_ids)`) and RP-02 S3's `repair_at_write_boundary(persist=, scoped=)`. A full 'report-what-recovery-would-do' surface is a larger observability feature and is out of scope for this contract-restoration bug.

**Change:** in `run_differs._run_differs_outbound`, change the recovery gate from `if not scoped_ids:` to `if ctx.persist and not scoped_ids:`. `ctx.persist` is already available (used elsewhere in the module). Live full passes (persist=True, unscoped) are unchanged; preview and legacy `--mode dry-run` (persist=False) now perform zero remote add_label/set_entity_property from recovery. Scoped passes remain suppressed as before.

**Testing:** a new unit test drives `_run_differs_outbound` with a keyed-pending binding on a no-write (persist=False) pass and asserts zero remote identity writes; a companion assertion confirms a live (persist=True) pass still triggers recovery (mutation-checked by reverting the `ctx.persist and` clause -> RED).
baseline.summary: Preview and dry-run passes perform remote Jira writes during pending-binding recovery

## What
DEPRECATE list-epics in favor of generic list/query, by first EXPANDING the generic list filters to cover what list-epics filters by, then making list-epics a deprecating alias.

list-epics' filters/criteria all derive from the same reducer+graph the generic reads use; only the FILTER EXPOSURE is missing from generic list. So:

1. Expand generic 'list' filters (reads.py list_states + ticket_reads CLI + library list_tickets + MCP list tool):
   - --min-children=N : tickets with >= N non-deleted direct children (child count via parent_id over reduced state).
   - --unblocked / --blocked : filter by blocking state (reuse rebar.graph find_ready_tickets / all_blockers_closed).
   These are universal filters, useful beyond epics.
2. Deprecate list-epics: emit a deprecation warning at every surface (CLI stderr, library DeprecationWarning, MCP tool description) steering to 'rebar list --type=epic --status=open,in_progress [--unblocked] [--min-children=N]'.
3. FOR NOW keep list-epics' current behavior + output ({p0_bugs,epics} envelope, child counts) intact so the MCP outputSchema + consumers don't break; the bespoke ticket-list-epics.sh (453 LOC) is removed in a later step once consumers migrate.

p0_bugs is a separable bug metric ('list --type=bug --priority=0'); not part of the generic list expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] generic 'list' gains --min-children + --unblocked/--blocked at CLI + library + MCP (parity with list-epics' filter criteria)
- [ ] new filters covered by tests (dual-impl where relevant)
- [ ] list-epics emits a deprecation warning at CLI (stderr) + library + MCP, steering to generic list; behavior/output otherwise unchanged
- [ ] existing list-epics suites still green (behavior preserved); deprecation warning does not pollute stdout/JSON
- [ ] docs note the deprecation + the new generic filters

baseline.description:
# S2 — Deploy Gerrit + review-bot receiver (docker-compose) behind nginx + TLS

## Why
Run Gerrit and the **review-bot webhook receiver** as the two containers on the box, reachable
over HTTPS at `rebar.solutions.navateam.com`. Gerrit needs a `%2F`-safe reverse proxy — the
community uses nginx/Apache, NOT Caddy (Caddy URL-decodes paths by default with no global
switch, which breaks Gerrit's change/project screens; no confirmed Caddy+Gerrit recipe exists).
This is the bottom layer of the d251 "proven pipe": Gerrit serving, the receiver reachable over
HTTP, TLS terminated, secrets from SSM. NOTE (peer-pattern correction): Gerrit POSTs webhook
JSON, not MCP protocol — so the right component is a thin HTTP **webhook receiver that IMPORTS
the review kernel as a library**, NOT the stdio rebar-MCP server exposed over HTTP (a FastMCP
HTTP transport would reject a Gerrit webhook by spec; `streamable-http` is a red herring here).

## What
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:
  - official `gerritcodereview/gerrit` pinned to a PATCH tag (e.g. `3.14.1`) with persistent
    volumes (git/index/cache/etc/db on the data volume) + the two-step init. DERISK NOTE (E4):
    bare minor tags `3.14`/`3.13` do NOT exist on Docker Hub; pin a published patch tag
    (`3.14.1`/`3.13.7`/`3.12.8`), all of which publish arm64 manifests.
  - the **review-bot container** (signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sourced from SSM into the boot
    `.env` — see secrets bullet; write-gating as needed); both `restart: unless-stopped`, pinned
    tags. The receiver calls the `rebar.llm` library functions DIRECTLY, so the LLM review path is
    enabled simply by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` being present + the `[agents]` extra being installed —
    there is NO separate allow-flag for direct library calls (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` gates only the
    stdio MCP server's tool wrappers, which this receiver does not use, so it is intentionally not
    set).
  - the Gerrit data volume is declared **`external: true`** (created once, outside compose) so a
    stray `docker compose down -v` cannot destroy git/NoteDb/index state. S2 only DECLARES this
    external data volume; volume snapshotting + retention is owned by **S7's DLM daily-snapshot
    policy** (see S7), and the restore procedure is in the runbook. Freeze-and-restore (the d251
    recovery posture, no break-glass v1) operates against the snapshots S7 manages.
- **Review-bot webhook receiver (in-scope S2 deliverable).** The second container is a thin
  **webhook->review->vote receiver** (an ASGI/FastAPI service under `src/rebar/review_bot/`)
  that IMPORTS the review kernel as a library and exposes a plain HTTP endpoint Gerrit's
  `webhooks` plugin POSTs to. This is deliberately NOT the stdio rebar-MCP server over HTTP
  (Gerrit speaks webhooks, not MCP JSON-RPC; an MCP HTTP transport would reject the request).
  The stdio MCP server is unchanged and remains for agent use only. The receiver binds
  `0.0.0.0:<PORT>` (default `8000`); nginx routes
  `location /review/ { proxy_pass http://review-bot:<PORT>/; }`. Decision recorded in
  `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`.
- `gerrit.config`: `container.heapLimit=2g` with `core.packedGitLimit` budgeted INSIDE the heap
  (~512m-1g), NoteDb, `canonicalWebUrl=https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/`, sshd/httpd thread
  caps + `sshd.batchThreads` to avoid parallel-clone OOM.
- nginx + certbot (Let's Encrypt) terminating TLS on 443: route Gerrit (`%2F`-safe: `proxy_pass`
  with no path) and the receiver (`location /review/`) behind the one cert; Gerrit SSH on 29418.
- **certbot renewal lifecycle.** Initial issuance AND renewal: a systemd timer (or cron) runs
  `certbot renew` twice daily with a deploy-hook that reloads nginx; nginx serves an
  `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location (webroot) so HTTP-01 renewal succeeds. Installed by
  the bootstrap script.
- **secrets bootstrap (SSM -> ephemeral `.env`).** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` runs
  `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` for the signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (via the
  **instance role**, no static keys) and writes a root-only (`0600`) `.env` that compose reads,
  BEFORE `docker compose up`. The `.env` is gitignored + ephemeral (regenerated each boot, never
  committed); the script is idempotent and **aborts** if SSM is unreachable (never reuses a
  stale `.env`). Recorded in `docs/adr/0008-secrets-source-ssm.md`.
- **IAM instance role (least privilege).** Grants `ssm:GetParameter`/`GetParameters` scoped to
  the project parameter-path prefix only (e.g.
  `arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:896586841071:parameter/rebar/prod/*`) plus `kms:Decrypt` on the
  SecureString key — no wildcard. Defined in the infra IaC.
- **observability (minimal).** Both containers log via `journald`; a health probe hits `/` and
  the receiver `/review/` health path; a disk-usage alarm guards the Gerrit data volume.

## Scope
In: containers, the external Gerrit data volume DECLARATION, base `gerrit.config`,
nginx+TLS+certbot renewal, the review-bot receiver HTTP surface + hosting, SSM->.env secrets
bootstrap, the SSM IAM instance role, minimal logging/health/disk observability. Out: Gerrit
project/label/submit-req (S3); the bot identity + event wiring + the receiver's review/vote
LOGIC (S4 — S2 stands up the *service*, S4 wires its behavior); replication (S5); the data
volume's snapshot + retention policy (S7's DLM daily-snapshot policy owns it — S2 only declares
the volume).

## Files
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/compose/gerrit.config`, `infra/nginx/*.conf`
  (incl. the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location and the `location /review/` upstream)
- `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (SSM -> ephemeral `.env`), bootstrap scripts under `infra/`
  (install the certbot-renew timer, the health/disk checks)
- `src/rebar/review_bot/` (the webhook-receiver ASGI service — skeleton/health endpoint in S2;
  review+vote behavior in S4)
- `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`, `docs/adr/0008-secrets-source-ssm.md`
- `.gitignore` (ensure `infra/compose/.env` is ignored)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gerrit is reachable at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` with a valid Let's Encrypt cert.
- [ ] A Gerrit change screen / a project path containing `%2F` renders correctly (encoded-slash round-trip verified end-to-end through nginx).
- [ ] certbot renewal is automated: the timer/cron is installed + enabled, the nginx `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location serves the HTTP-01 challenge, and `certbot renew --dry-run` succeeds and reloads nginx via the deploy-hook.
- [ ] Gerrit SSH clone works on 29418 and the admin account is bootstrapped.
- [ ] Gerrit data persists across `docker compose down/up` and an instance reboot; the data volume is `external: true` so `docker compose down -v` does not destroy it. (Snapshot + retention of this volume is owned by S7, not S2.)
- [ ] The review-bot webhook receiver (a plain HTTP service importing the review kernel as a library, NOT the stdio MCP over HTTP) is reachable through nginx at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/` — a POST reaches the receiver process (not a 502); the decision is recorded in `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`.
- [ ] The review-bot container's signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are sourced from SSM at boot by `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` into a `0600`, gitignored, ephemeral `.env` (never baked into the image/compose, never committed); the script authenticates via the instance role, is idempotent, and aborts if SSM is unreachable. The receiver's LLM review path is enabled by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + the `[agents]` extra alone (no `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` flag, which gates only the stdio MCP server, is set).
- [ ] The SSM IAM instance role grants `GetParameter`/`GetParameters` scoped to `parameter/rebar/prod/*` only (no wildcard), verified against the attached policy.
- [ ] Both containers log to `journald`; a health probe covers `/` and `/review/`, and a disk-usage alarm covers the Gerrit data volume.
- [ ] Gerrit runs a supported version at an EXISTING arm64 patch tag (e.g. `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`; a bare minor tag like `3.14` is NOT used — it doesn't exist), with `heapLimit=2g` and `packedGitLimit` budgeted within it.

## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-30 — recalibrated gate BLOCK + critical advisories)

**Blocking — internal sequencing (phased build, each phase verified before the next):**
- **Phase 1 (riskiest first):** Gerrit `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1` (arm64) container up with the external data volume + base `gerrit.config`; reachable over plain HTTP through nginx (no TLS yet); `%2F`-encoded path round-trips. Proves the arm64 image + the `%2F`-safe proxy before anything else is layered on.
- **Phase 2:** nginx TLS via certbot (Let's Encrypt) on 443 + the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` webroot + the twice-daily `certbot renew` timer with the nginx-reload deploy-hook; `certbot renew --dry-run` green.
- **Phase 3:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (SSM->ephemeral 0600 `.env`) via the instance role + the scoped IAM policy attachment (S2's separately-named inline policy on the S1-owned role).
- **Phase 4:** the review-bot receiver container reachable through nginx at `/review/` (skeleton + health only — review/vote LOGIC is S4b).
- **Phase 5:** observability (journald, `/` + `/review/` health probes, data-volume disk alarm).

**Critical advisories folded in:**
- **`webhooks` plugin is NOT bundled in the official image (seam to S4a):** S2 stands up the *service* only. The Gerrit site's `plugins/` dir is a bind-mount/volume path so a version-matched (3.14.1) `webhooks` + `events-log` plugin jar can be dropped in; ACTUAL plugin install + wiring is **S4a**. S2 verifies only that the site supports dropping plugin jars (the plugins dir is writable + on the persistent volume). No S2 AC depends on webhooks delivering events.
- **Receiver framework dependency (was absent):** add a `reviewbot` optional extra to `pyproject.toml` = `fastapi` + `uvicorn[standard]`. The receiver container builds via `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` (`pip install .[agents,reviewbot]`). The stdio MCP server is untouched.
- **Dockerfile added** to Files: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`.
- **`core.packedGitLimit` is OFF-HEAP (correction):** JGit's `core.packedGitLimit` is the mmap'd packfile budget, sized against TOTAL RAM, NOT inside the Java heap. Config: `container.heapLimit=2g` (on-heap) + `core.packedGitLimit` ~1g budgeted against the ~8 GB box RAM ALONGSIDE (not within) the heap, leaving headroom for the OS + the receiver container.
- **`fetch-secrets.sh` explicit SSM-leaf -> env mapping** (the 7 params S1 created): `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`->`GERRIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key`->`GERRIT_SSH_HOST_ED25519_KEY`, `github-replication-deploy-key`->`GITHUB_REPLICATION_DEPLOY_KEY`, `mcp-hmac-signing-key`->`MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`, `anthropic-api-key`->`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `alert-endpoint`->`ALERT_ENDPOINT`, `gerrit-bot-token`->`GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN`. (Same contract as S1's user_data.sh; S2 sources only the subset the containers need.)
- **LLM path enablement:** the receiver's LLM review path is enabled by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + the `[agents]` extra ALONE — `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (which gates only the stdio MCP server) is intentionally NOT set.
- **External volume creation step:** the Gerrit data volume is a Docker `external: true` volume backed by the `/var/gerrit` EBS mount; `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` (the boot orchestrator) runs `docker volume create --driver local --opt type=none --opt o=bind --opt device=/var/gerrit gerrit_data` (idempotent) BEFORE `docker compose up`, so a stray `docker compose down -v` cannot destroy it.
- **Port single-source:** the receiver port is one env var `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` (default 8000) in the `.env`; compose and the nginx upstream both read it (nginx via an envsubst-templated conf at boot), so the two can't drift.

**Added / updated ACs:**
- [ ] The build is phased (Phase 1 Gerrit+HTTP -> 2 TLS -> 3 secrets/IAM -> 4 receiver -> 5 observability); Phase 1 reachability is proven before TLS is layered on.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` declares a `reviewbot` extra (fastapi + uvicorn); `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` builds the receiver via `.[agents,reviewbot]`.
- [ ] `gerrit.config` sets `container.heapLimit=2g` (on-heap) and `core.packedGitLimit` as a SEPARATE off-heap budget (~1g) sized against box RAM, NOT inside the heap.
- [ ] `fetch-secrets.sh` maps the enumerated `/rebar/prod/*` leaves to the documented env-var names, writes a 0600 ephemeral `.env`, authenticates via the instance role, is idempotent, and aborts if SSM is unreachable.
- [ ] The Gerrit data volume is created as an `external` bind volume on `/var/gerrit` by `compose-up.sh` before `docker compose up`; `docker compose down -v` does not destroy it.
- [ ] The receiver port is single-sourced (`REVIEW_BOT_PORT`) and consumed by both compose and the nginx `/review/` upstream.

## Context
The completed Gerrit Verified latency RCA optimized the macOS completion path, but Ubuntu jobs still occupy scarce org-wide runners for 11-14 minutes and contribute to queue contention. Follow-up questions identify three candidate levers: replace repeated Pandoc corpus rendering with static expected results plus a smaller boundary test, remove redundant work from the exhaustive 1,440-minute bridge cadence proof, and move genuinely live Jira DC coverage out of the per-change hot path while retaining fast unit coverage. This work must preserve behavioral coverage and must not use extra parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner usage.

## Plan
- Build a dated Ubuntu runner-time dossier from final post-remediation run 31752047186, pytest duration logs, workflow routing, and focused local runtime experiments.
- For Pandoc and render_unit, map every current assertion to the code boundary it exercises; compare static golden fixtures, a bounded real-Pandoc contract sample, and full-corpus external execution using defect-seeded experiments to detect any coverage loss.
- For the bridge cadence test, discriminate between the cost of the 1,440 arithmetic checks and invariant workflow YAML I/O; prefer hoisting invariant I/O if it preserves the exhaustive proof.
- Inventory expensive Jira DC/default-tier tests, identify which require a real Jira or external binary, and map them to faster existing or new unit contracts before proposing any lane move.
- Compare each candidate with current practice in popular actively maintained OSS projects and search tracker history for prior acceptance or rejection.
- Record a confirmed RCA and measured runner-time/wall-time savings. Create linked implementation tickets only for remediations that preserve coverage; under the operator standing approval, implement those matching OSS consensus through Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every Ubuntu operation or test phase over 30 seconds in the final sample is attributed to a specific mechanism and measured with a focused baseline.
- [ ] Pandoc corpus, render_unit, bridge cadence, and Jira DC lane-move proposals each have an assertion-level coverage map and an A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] Each proposal cites tracker history and practices from popular actively maintained OSS projects.
- [ ] No accepted remediation removes an assertion, behavioral equivalence class, OS/Python cell, or external boundary; moved coverage has an explicit destination and schedule.
- [ ] Runner-minute and expected queue-pressure savings are quantified without counting parallel matrix time as critical-path wall time.
- [ ] Every consensus-backed remediation is implemented on a linked ticket, passes repository gates and Gerrit LLM-Review +1 plus Verified +1, and merges before this task closes.
- [ ] Non-consensus or coverage-risking proposals are summarized with evidence and left for operator disposition.
baseline.summary: Reduce Ubuntu CI runner occupancy without losing test coverage

baseline.description:
# Comment sync (append-only) with persistent Jira-comment-ID map

## Context / Problem
Comment sync identifies comments by **body equality** (normalized-text key in `_diff_comments`), so same-text comments collide and an edited body looks new. Semantics are **append-only**: mirror comment *creation* both ways, never edits or deletes. This story also **owns the DC comment-diff dedup-key migration `3388` deferred here**: `3388` moved `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to the rendering form for descriptions but left the comment-diff path on the identity normalizer (a32a `_resolve_codec` seam, default `_IdentityCodec`). Flipping that path to the real codec, and keeping comment-diff convergent when it renders rich, is this story's job.

## Approach
**1. Identity = local comment key + returned Jira ID, not body.** Local key = the COMMENT event's **HLC `timestamp`** (unique, monotonic; already on the compiled entry at `reducer/_processors.py:349`). Persist a **`local_comment_key (HLC) → Jira comment ID`** map in binding state: outbound, an unmapped key is created in Jira and its returned ID recorded; inbound, mirror Jira comments whose IDs are not map values (entries carry `jira_comment_id`, bug 85a1). **Append-only**: no rebar edit/delete pushed to Jira, no Jira edit/delete applied to rebar; a mapped key/ID is never re-synced. The map is change-gated, one fixed-shape entry per comment.

**1a. Capture the returned ID at both enactment sites**, discarded today. It rides only on `SupportsComments.add_comment`'s returned `{"id": …}` dict (protocol `_backend.py:540`; Cloud `backend.py:275`, DC `jira_datacenter/backend.py:462` delegate to the transport; Cloud transport `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` returns `json.loads(result.stdout)` at `:515`). So (i) the local key rides ON the mutation entry as `"local_comment_key": <HLC>`; (ii) `binding_store` reaches both loops: `create_one` has it, and a new optional `binding_store` param on `update_one` → `_update_one_dispatch_comments` is fed by `handle_update`/`_apply_outbound_update` (the latter via `_apply_typed`'s var-kw). Failures stay non-fatal (`comment_errors` unchanged). **Crash-durability**: `record_comment_id` `save()`s immediately on the `add_comment` return (write-ahead).

**1b. Two identity stores, one authoritative per DIRECTION, never crossed.** `jira_comment_id` (bug 85a1) is authoritative for INBOUND-origin comments, the map for OUTBOUND-origin. **Outbound**: skip when EITHER the HLC key is mapped OR the comment carries a `jira_comment_id`; the normalized-body test is DEMOTED, not removed, to a secondary skip against a lost map write. ID identity is the PRIMARY outbound guard; the `RECONCILER_MARKER` exclusion stands. **Inbound**: `_diff_comments_inbound` (`inbound_differ.py:280`) is UNCHANGED, never receives the map; its loop-breakers stand (`RECONCILER_MARKER` bodies, ids matching a local `jira_comment_id`).

**2. Render bodies through the codec; migrate the dedup key.** Outbound bodies render through the `RichTextCodec.to_wire` seam descriptions use (`AdfCodec.to_wire` Cloud, `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` DC after `3388`). The Cloud comment path lacks an encode step: `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` (`:492`) sends `--body <str>` (`:510-511`) unencoded.

**`--body` accepts ADF, and fit BEFORE encode (Cloud, load-bearing).** `acli jira workitem comment create --help` documents `-b, --body string   Comment body in plain text or Atlassian Document Format (ADF)` (probed read-only on installed acli, exit 0, no Jira mutation), so `--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))` is supported like `--description`. Today `add_comment` runs the plaintext guard `_sanitize_comment(body)` (`:502`); it must NOT run on serialized ADF (far longer than its text, so truncation mismeasures length and can slice JSON mid-structure → a payload ACLI rejects). Correct order, mirroring `AdfCodec.fit_outbound`: **fit the TEXT first** (`AdfCodec(rich=...).fit_outbound(body)` → `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit`, bounding `len(json.dumps(markdown_to_adf(...)))`), **then** `json.dumps(to_wire(fitted))`. The plaintext truncation applies only on the plain branch (DC / rich `off`). DC `to_wire` returns `str`, so DC `--body` stays plain wiki. Codec built as `backend.py:52,64` do — `AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())`, so `rich_text_cutover` (`3388`, ships `off`) governs rendering. Then **flip the a32a injection** (`_diff_comments`'s `_resolve_codec`) from `_IdentityCodec` to the real codec so the local dedup key (via `normalize_outbound`) matches the landed wire.

Depends on `e59d`/`271c`/`3388` shipping first.

## Scope
Engine paths under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:
- `binding_store.py` — the map + `record_comment_id(...)` write-ahead writer.
- `outbound_comments.py` — skip logic (1b); append `"local_comment_key"`; flip
  `_resolve_codec` to the real codec.
- `outbound_differ.py` — `compute_outbound_mutations` threads `binding_store` +
  `RichTextCodec` into `_diff_comments`.
- `dispatch_one.py` — `create_one` records the id; `update_one` gains optional `binding_store`.
- `dispatch_apply_phases.py` — `_update_one_dispatch_comments` records the id.
- `apply_handlers.py` / `apply_outbound.py` — thread `ctx.binding_store` through
  `handle_update` / `_apply_outbound_update` (from `_apply_typed`'s var-kw).
- `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` `add_comment` (`:492`) — Cloud ADF encode
  (fit-then-encode per Approach 2), guarded by `AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())`.
- `reducer/_processors.py` — HLC key (`:349`); `jira_comment_id` (`:354-356`) unchanged.
- `inbound_differ._diff_comments_inbound` (`:280`) — **UNCHANGED, not in the edit set**.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Identity is the persistent COMMENT-HLC → Jira-comment-ID map, not the normalized-body
  key; verified by `test_comment_duplicate_bodies_distinct_ids`.
- [x] The returned `add_comment` `{"id": …}` is captured at both enactment sites
  (`create_one`; `update_one`→`_update_one_dispatch_comments` via `handle_update` /
  `_apply_outbound_update`) and persisted against the entry's `local_comment_key` via
  `record_comment_id` on Cloud (acli) and DC; verified by
  `test_comment_id_captured_and_persisted`.
- [x] Inbound-origin `jira_comment_id` (bug 85a1) and the outbound map are each
  authoritative for their own direction and never compete: the inbound differ is unchanged
  (ONLY `RECONCILER_MARKER` / `jira_comment_id`); the outbound differ skips when EITHER the
  key is mapped OR a `jira_comment_id` is present; verified by
  `test_comment_bidirectional_identity_no_double_sync`.
- [x] Comment sync is append-only both directions — new comments mirror once, edits/deletes skipped; verified by `test_comment_append_only`.
- [x] Outbound bodies render through `RichTextCodec.to_wire`: the Cloud ADF encode on the
  real create surface (`--body json.dumps(to_wire(fitted))`; `--body` confirmed by
  `acli jira workitem comment create --help` to accept ADF), fit-then-encode ordering (rich
  fit measures the wire BEFORE `json.dumps`; the plaintext `_sanitize_comment` guard never
  truncates serialized JSON), and the a32a `_resolve_codec` injection
  migrated to the real codec; verified by `test_comment_rendered_through_codec`,
  `test_comment_dedup_key_uses_real_codec`, `test_comment_adf_encode_fits_before_serialize`.
- [x] After migration, DC comment-diff converges with zero duplicate re-post; verified by
  `test_dc_comment_diff_converges_after_migration`.
- [x] A repeat reconcile pass creates no duplicate comments; verified by `test_comment_sync_idempotent`.
- [x] Crash-durability: `record_comment_id` `save()`s immediately on the successful
  `add_comment` return and the demoted body-equality test stays a secondary skip, so a lost
  map write does not re-post; verified by
  `test_comment_crash_between_add_and_map_save_no_duplicate`.
- [x] The comment-ID map is change-gated, no per-pass churn; verified by `test_comment_map_no_churn_on_no_new_comment_pass`.
baseline.summary: Comment sync (append-only) with persistent Jira-comment-ID map

Scope: `src/rebar/llm/**` excluding plan_review and workflow — the package root plus code_review, prompting, review_kernel, evals, criteria, overlap. ~218 lines leave.

Contains the repo's #1 hotspot: `runner.py` 797/800, 88 commits, 12 in five days, with a 371-line method at its C901 ceiling. Recovering ~45 lines takes headroom from 3 to ~48 — roughly 4-5 stories of runway WITHOUT another split. ADR 0056 measured prose at 40% of `run()` and 50% of its pre-call region.

A self-contradicting module: THREE sites assert Anthropic 400s when extended thinking meets a native output constraint, while `structured.py:228-238` — 210 lines below one of them, in the same file — explicitly calls that 'a stale rationale' and 'a relic'.

A dead field found via its own comment: `runner.py:94-97` says `extra_tools` 'is always None in practice'; grep confirms no caller sets it. Delete the field, not the comment.

Confirmed exemplar for the maintainer's original finding: `capabilities.py:166-198` is structurally a complete ADR (security posture for a BLOCKING gate, three numbered bounds, an explicitly accepted limitation on domain controls) and NO ADR in the 83-file corpus mentions web search in any form.

85 lines are free wins — history already citing b690, b300, 2682, 3a98, 7a79, e3cd, 8455. `providers.py:3-16` duplicates ADR 0059 §1 verbatim including its file:line citations.

capabilities.py:295-316 is a matrix that cost real AWS accounts to produce and says so; capabilities.py:269-281 carries a rejected-alternative warning sitting exactly where the next reader would reintroduce it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim
## CORRECTION (plan defect + plan-review preempt, parent 373f disposition vocabulary)

The plan's `extra_tools` premise is FALSE and would cause a regression if executed literally. `extra_tools` is LIVE, not dead: `llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:469,665` set it (the token-recovery record tool, story 2948), `llm/workflow/runs.py` threads it end-to-end, and `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py:491` asserts `captured.get("extra_tools")` ("the record tool is still wired"). The STALE unit is the `runner.py` comment claiming it "is always None in practice" — that is CORRECTED in place; the field is DO_NOT_MOVE (load-bearing). Superseding ACs below encode this and the 373f disposition rules.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one parent-373f
      label: RELOCATE (to an ADR / docs / ticket, reduced to a one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP,
      DO_NOT_MOVE, or CORRECT-IN-PLACE.
- [x] Decision rule CORRECT-vs-DELETE: a comment documenting CURRENT runtime behavior / a live
      invariant is CORRECTED in place; a comment is DELETED only when the thing it describes no
      longer exists (artifact removed, or superseded). Every DELETE records its reason
      (referenced-artifact-gone / superseded) in the commit body or a ticket comment.
- [x] `runner.py` `extra_tools` field is KEPT (DO_NOT_MOVE — load-bearing via
      completion_recovery/runs.py/tests); its stale "always None in practice" comment is
      CORRECTED to reflect the story-2948 record-tool wiring (or deleted as superseded), with the
      reason recorded. The field and its two call sites are NOT removed.
- [x] The three sites asserting an Anthropic-400 on extended-thinking + native-output-constraint
      vs `structured.py:228-238` calling that rationale "stale"/"a relic" are RECONCILED
      conservatively: determine which matches current runtime and CORRECT the stale side in
      place; if the truth is not determinable from the code without behavior risk, KEEP both
      verbatim (DO_NOT_MOVE) and file a `discovered_from` ticket rather than guess. No
      load-bearing invariant is deleted on uncertainty.
- [x] The web-search capability security-posture block (`capabilities.py:166-198` — a structurally
      complete ADR: BLOCKING-gate posture, three numbered bounds, an accepted limitation) is
      RELOCATED into a NEW ADR with a unique unused number (>= 0063), which EXISTS and is
      committed BEFORE the source comment is collapsed to a one-line citation.
- [x] Measured-fact and anti-refactor comments stay VERBATIM (DO_NOT_MOVE): the AWS-cost capability
      matrix (`capabilities.py:295-316`) and the rejected-alternative warning
      (`capabilities.py:269-281`). `providers.py:3-16` duplicating ADR 0059 §1 verbatim is
      collapsed to a one-line citation.
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands;
      lint/type pragmas (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and
      test-introspected docstrings are DO_NOT_MOVE.
- [x] The actual recovered comment-line count is measured (by diff) and recorded on this ticket

## Context / Problem
The debug skill reads prior tickets but never writes back (reads from a well it never fills); Step 7 sweeps by construct only (parity siblings are ABSENCES invisible to grep); Reporting lets residual fragility evaporate. Approved changes 14+15+16 from the bug-trend review.

## Approach
(14) Writebacks: Phase-1-exit RCA comment (root cause + discriminating evidence); Reporting summary comment (cause/proof/test/fix/siblings/replication); not-a-bug classification comment + cited source; Step-7 siblings filed via create + discovered_from encoded DIRECTLY in the skill (no AGENTS.md reference — client projects may lack it). Tracker discriminator, stated inline in the skill: the tracker the debug session is already operating within — the one that produced or holds the ticket under debug — is "the project's own mandated tracker" and receives the prescribed writebacks un-gated; ANY other tracker is third-party and stays approval-gated. The existing approval-gate paragraph (SKILL.md "Seek explicit user approval… writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers") is explicitly amended in the same change with a carve-out sentence so the prescribed own-tracker writebacks do not contradict it; all other tracker mutations remain gated. (15) Step 7 second sweep axis (construct search unchanged), decomposed into 4 forced-artifact questions: NAME THE RULE (operation+property, must not name the fixed site); CHANNEL CENSUS (fixed 5-slot checklist: CLI / MCP-API / library-facade / automated-callers / dual-direction, plus caller-set derivation — a surface absent from the shared core's callers is the parity signature); PER-SURFACE PROBE (cite path:line or MISSING); DISPOSITION (RED-test fix or ticket + discovered_from). Step 7's entry trigger is amended to the OR of the two axis triggers: enter when the root cause is a repeatable construct pattern (axis 1, existing wording) OR when the fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces (axis 2 — a parity sibling is an absence, present even for one-off constructs); each axis then runs only under its own condition. (16) Reporting item 'Residual risk & prevention': per observed-with-citation fragility, forced disposition — ticket filed (may propose structural guard) / accepted with reason / fixed in scope; 'none observed' legitimate; prose only, no new ticket-system structures.

## Scope
- examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md (single real file; ~35-45 lines total). SKILL.md has no symlink or synced copy — only shared/test-design.md is cp-synced across skills, and that file is untouched here.

## Testing
Prose-only skill change: no code tests. Validation = the existing skill sync gate (tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py, which covers shared/test-design.md only) run as a regression check confirming this change does not perturb the synced set, and a dry-run read-through against the 4-question artifacts on one historical bug (4b59 link-direction class).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All four writebacks encoded at their lifecycle points, with the inline own-tracker-vs-third-party discriminator AND the approval-gate paragraph amended with the matching carve-out (no contradiction between the two sections).
- [x] Step 7 carries both axes with the 4-question decomposition and forced artifacts, and its entry trigger is the OR of the two axis conditions.
- [x] Reporting carries the residual-risk disposition item with 'none observed' legitimate.
- [x] No references to AGENTS.md; discovered_from linkage stated inline.

## Context / Problem

The principal-engineer Janitor audit at snapshot `9a94ef9737fbdf070ae314bba6e797319aee2301` verified maintainability, oracle, documentation, compatibility, and dead-code findings that passed the fixed validity and impact floors and were approved by the maintainer. The audit itself changed no product code; this epic delivers the approved cleanup before further feature work consumes the recovered headroom.

Authoritative evidence and dispositions are in `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-29.md` and audit ticket `literal-subaverage-dartfrog`.

## Approach

Deliver each approved remediation through a non-overlapping child whose plan owns its cited files and regression contracts. Structural extractions follow existing call-graph seams. Public removals state their replacement and breaking-change impact. Internal-only shim removal is gated by a prerequisite ADR and migrates every static, dynamic, string, test, and monkeypatch consumer before deletion. Reconciler compatibility removal is separately dependency-ordered so persisted state and live lock/exit contracts are migrated before old routes disappear.

## Child Decomposition

- Structural-headroom children own RP01, RP07, and RP13.
- Behavioral-oracle and CI children own RP05, RP06, RP09, RP14, RP16, RP19, RP29, RP31, RP33, and RP36.
- Adapter and documentation children own RP10, RP20, RP21, RP22, RP23, RP24, RP28, and RP35.
- Public-deprecation and compatibility children own RP18, RP27, scheduled removals, config aliases, CLI aliases, the reconcile family, Python/MCP aliases, and MCP model re-exports.
- The internal-shim container owns the prerequisite ADR and disjoint implementation shards, including SDC3.

Observed while running the CI marker selection for bug 941b-f049-5f29-4410 (rebar-debug residual-risk sweep). NOT caused by that change.

## Reproduce

    pytest -m 'not integration and not external' -n 4 --dist worksteal -q

fails with:

    tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py:109: AssertionError
    assert engine_b.BACKEND_METRIC in table
    AssertionError: assert 'metric' in {'opengrep': {'ran': 1, 'skipped': 5,
      'reasons': Counter({'unsupported_lang': 5})}, 'ast-grep': {'ran': 1,
      'skipped': 0, 'reasons': Counter()}}

## Proof it is pre-existing, not a regression from 941b

Run against a CLEAN worktree detached at origin/main (d68907dbe2), with none of 941b's edits present: the same cell fails identically (1 failed in 9.35s). So the reconstructed coverage table is keyed by BACKEND NAMES ('opengrep', 'ast-grep') where the test expects `engine_b.BACKEND_METRIC` ('metric') — the reconstruction and the assertion disagree about the table's key space.

## Why it matters

The CI marker suite is the gate agents are told to run before pushing. A cell that is red at HEAD trains every subsequent agent to read a red suite as normal, which is how a genuine regression gets waved through.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the disagreement is resolved at its source: either the reconstruction emits the metric
      key the test asserts, or the test asserts the backend-name key space the reconstruction
      actually produces — with the choice justified against which key space callers consume
- [ ] `pytest -m 'not integration and not external'` is green at HEAD

## Context
Gerrit Verify uses same-change concurrency with cancel-in-progress=true, but the docs-only routing change 6f4123678c added job-level always() predicates to seven full-route jobs. GitHub re-evaluates those predicates during cancellation; because they remain true, stale matrix/reusable jobs are not canceled. In run pair 31834162663 -> 31834896849, the predecessor consumed 1,785 runner-seconds after the replacement existed and delayed successor job creation by 1,510 seconds.

The existing docs-only contract must remain fail closed: a classifier failure still launches the full fallback route and remains a blocking result. A superseding-patchset cancellation is a different state and must not launch or preserve stale full-route work.

## Plan
- Add a focused workflow-contract regression that is RED on the current job predicates and separately proves both branches: cancellation makes every full-route job ineligible; classifier failure while not canceled keeps every full-route job eligible.
