# Decide the provider qualifier by registry membership, not prefix shape

## Context / Problem

Parent bug `03b0` fixed a real outage-shaped defect: a canonical Bedrock model id (`anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`) contains a colon in its version suffix, so a `":" in model` test read it as "already provider-qualified" and silently discarded the operator's configured `provider = "bedrock"`. That fix shipped a SHAPE test — a pre-colon prefix counts as a provider only if it matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$` (identifier-like, crucially no dots, since Bedrock ids are dotted). It lives at `src/rebar/llm/config.py:192` (`_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE`) and is applied at `src/rebar/llm/config.py:203` inside `split_provider_qualifier`.

The shape test works for the ids we have, but it answers the wrong question. It asks "does this prefix LOOK like a provider name?" when the answer needed is "IS this prefix a provider name?". Two consequences are live today, both confirmed by running the tree:

- A typo'd configured provider is accepted at config-resolution time:
  `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")` returns `'bedrok:claude-opus-4-8'`. Config
  resolution runs in `rebar` commands that never reach an LLM, so the mistake is only reported much
  later, at provider construction (`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:180`), if it is reached at all.
- Any future model id whose pre-colon prefix happens to be a lowercase dotless identifier would be
  silently promoted to a "provider". Bedrock ids are dotted today by AWS convention, not by
  contract — the same shape assumption that produced `03b0`.

`03b0` cannot close until this is settled, so it is on the epic's critical path.

The decision (already taken, not reopened here): decide qualification by membership in a known- provider registry, which is what every comparable project does — LangChain's `model.split(":", 1)[0] in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`, LiteLLM's `model.split("/", 1)[0] in litellm.provider_list`, pydantic-ai's `infer_provider_class` raising `Unknown provider: …`. The separator stays `:`.

## Approach

Replace `_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE` with a module-level `frozenset[str]` named `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, and make `split_provider_qualifier` test membership in it.

The set is a literal of plain strings — no imports, no lazy loading, no registry object. This is the design move LangChain and LiteLLM both make: separate "which names are providers" (a static set of strings) from "what implements them" (resolved downstream by `ProviderSession`). It fits here for a concrete reason: `split_provider_qualifier` runs during config resolution, where the optional `[agents]` extra may not be importable at all, and the `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` module docstring (lines 27-30) states the constraint the module already lives under — heavy libraries are imported inside the functions that need them "so `import rebar.llm` stays stdlib-only". A literal string set satisfies that with nothing lazy to get wrong; `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py:51` already enforces the property.

**Contents of the set — 24 names, NO EXCEPTIONS.** Exactly the names `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` returns today (`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:54`): `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `cerebras`, `cohere`, `deepseek`, `gateway/anthropic`, `gateway/bedrock`, `gateway/google-cloud`, `gateway/groq`, `gateway/openai`, `google`, `google-cloud`, `google-gla`, `google-vertex`, `grok`, `groq`, `heroku`, `huggingface`, `mistral`, `moonshotai`, `openai`, `openai-chat`, `vertexai`, `xai`. Verified against the installed runtime: the set difference in both directions is empty.

rebar's own builder names — `anthropic`, `bedrock`, and `openai` when `base_url` is set (`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:106` and `:118`) — are all already among those 24, so they add no name. They are named here because the drift test pins them.

**No name is grandfathered in.** An earlier draft of this plan admitted `google_genai` because the inference table emits it and a test pinned it. That is rejected. The deciding evidence, from probing the installed pydantic-ai (1.107.1) directly:

    infer_model("test")                      -> TestModel
    infer_model("test:foo")                  -> ValueError: Unknown provider: test
    infer_model("notaprovider:foo")          -> ValueError: Unknown provider: notaprovider
    infer_model("google_genai:gemini-2.0")   -> ValueError: Unknown provider: google_genai
    infer_model("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8") -> AnthropicModel

Upstream already does exactly what this story proposes — registry membership, hard-rejecting an unknown provider qualifier — and it rejects BOTH `test` and `google_genai`. `test` is not a provider in pydantic-ai at all: it is the special bare model string that instantiates `TestModel`. Granting either name membership would make rebar MORE permissive than the library it wraps, which is backwards for a thin provider seam. Note also that no member of the 24 contains an underscore; `google_genai` is not merely unregistered, it does not match the shape real provider names take.

Five members contain a slash (`gateway/anthropic`, `gateway/bedrock`, `gateway/google-cloud`, `gateway/groq`, `gateway/openai`) and so are REJECTED by today's shape regex. Membership therefore widens as well as narrows: those names start splitting correctly. That is a fix, not a regression, and no existing test pins the old rejection.

**Two paths, deliberately different, because they are different questions.**

1. *An inline prefix in a model string* — `split_provider_qualifier` returns `(prefix, rest)` when
   `prefix` is a member, and `(None, model)` otherwise. It does **not** raise on a non-member. This
   is load-bearing: raising on every unrecognized prefix would break the very ids `03b0` fixed,
   because `"anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0".partition(":")` yields the prefix
   `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1`, which is by construction not a provider name. Falling
   back to "not qualified" is the only answer that keeps a colon-bearing model id intact. This
   matches the OpenRouter precedent upstream: strict on a configured provider, permissive on an
   unrecognized inline prefix.

2. *An explicitly configured provider* — `_resolve_target(model, provider)`
   (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:224`) validates `provider` against the same set and raises
   `LLMConfigError` naming the offending value and listing the valid ones, before composing
   anything. This is the capability the shape test cannot provide, and the one the motivating
   `bedrok` case needs: the operator's typo is reported where the operator made it, during config
   resolution, instead of surviving into a composed target string.

An inline typo (`bedrok:claude-opus-4-8`) is unchanged by this work: it becomes unqualified, no inference prefix matches it, `_resolve_target` returns it verbatim, and the existing typed `LLMConfigError("unknown provider 'bedrok'; registered providers: …")` at `src/rebar/llm/providers.py:180` fires at construction. Adding a second diagnostic for it here would duplicate that error, so it is deliberately not added.

**Fan-in consequence: `infer_provider` returns None for a non-member inline prefix.** Because `infer_provider` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:213`) delegates to `split_provider_qualifier`, dropping `test` from the set changes its result for a synthetic model double: `infer_provider("test:FunctionModel")` goes from `'test'` to `None`. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:596` stamps `provider=infer_provider(ran_model)` into the usage log, so two existing assertions change. `None` is the more truthful telemetry — there is no provider behind a `FunctionModel` double, and `"test"` was a fabricated value produced only by the shape regex accepting an arbitrary identifier. These are updated to the new expected value, not weakened or deleted. rebar's `test:` fixtures keep working because they use `FakeRunner`/`_Recorder` and never reach `infer_model`; the strings still resolve verbatim through `_resolve_target` (no inference prefix matches them), so only the recorded `provider` field changes.

**Drift.** The static set and the runtime registries can diverge when pydantic-ai adds a provider. Rather than couple the config layer to the optional package, a test (guarded by `pytest.importorskip("pydantic_ai")`, the pattern already used at `tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py:32`) asserts that every name in `ProviderSession._builders` and every name in `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` is present in `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`. The assertion is one-directional (runtime names are a subset of the static set) so that a future rebar builder for a name pydantic-ai does not enumerate is not a failure; with zero exceptions the two sets are in fact equal today, and the exact-24 literal test pins that. A pydantic-ai upgrade that adds a provider fails that test loudly here, instead of silently in an operator's config.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — delete `_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE` (line 192), add the
  `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` frozenset, switch the test in `split_provider_qualifier` (line 203) to
  membership, replace the comment block at lines 183-191 that explains the shape rationale, and drop
  the now-unused `import re` (line 39 — line 192 is its only use, so ruff F401 fails otherwise).
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — validate the explicitly configured `provider` in
  `_resolve_target` (line 224) against `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`; update its docstring, which currently
  cites the shape decision.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` — new cases (below), plus ONE existing case updated: the
  `"google_genai:gemini-2.0"  # ...or an underscore` parametrization at line 72 feeds
  `test_an_already_qualified_string_is_returned_unchanged` (line 75), whose line 77 asserts
  `_resolve_target(already, "google_genai") == already`. Under membership that now correctly raises
  `LLMConfigError`. No member of the 24 contains an underscore, so the property that case was
  pinning ("a provider name may contain an underscore") is not true of any real provider. It is
  replaced by a slashed member (`gateway/openai:gpt-4o`), which pins the same structural class — a
  provider name carrying a non-alphanumeric character round-trips — with a name that actually
  exists. `google_genai` gains a new case asserting its NEW behaviour (unqualified), so coverage of
  the string is strengthened, not dropped. Line 79 of that test
  (`_resolve_target(already, None) == already`) passes unchanged for every case including the
  replacement.
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` — line 330 asserts `rows[0]["provider"] == "test"`; becomes
  `is None` per the fan-in consequence above.
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py` — line 121 asserts `row["provider"] == "test"` on the
  failure-row path; same change.
- `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` — the comment at lines 43-45 states "`test:` survives
  `split_provider_qualifier` as a provider qualifier", which stops being true. The strings still
  resolve unchanged (no inference prefix matches `test:…`, so `_resolve_target` returns them
  verbatim), so only the comment's reasoning changes, not the assertions.

The fan-in blast radius is exactly those two usage-log files, verified by grep: a `provider == "test"` assertion appears nowhere else in `tests/`. The three other files carrying `test:` model literals — `tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_step_model_attribution.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_usage_attribution.py` and `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` — contain no `provider` assertion at all.

Out of scope, stated so it is not read as an omission:

- **The bare-name inference table.** `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:169`) maps
  `gemini` to `google_genai`, so `_resolve_target("gemini-2.5-pro", None)` still yields
  `'google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro'`, which no builder and no pydantic-ai name can construct, so it
  dies at `src/rebar/llm/providers.py:180`. This change validates only the EXPLICITLY CONFIGURED
  provider, never the inferred one, so that path is untouched and behaves identically before and
  after. It is a pre-existing defect filed on its own ticket. Validating inferred providers here
  would fold an unrelated bug fix into this change.
- **`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`** — its `":" in model` splits (lines 101-102) are eval-only
  scoring helpers, not qualification deciders, and `03b0` deliberately left them alone. Unchanged
  here for the same reason.
- **The guard order** — checking an explicitly configured provider before scanning the model string
  at all — already landed in `03b0` and is untouched.
- **Changing the separator.** `:` stays. pydantic-ai's own `KnownModelName` contains two-colon
  entries (`bedrock:anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`), so "provider, first colon, then a
  model name that may itself contain colons" is our runtime's grammar.

## Testing

In `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` unless noted.

- **Happy path** — `split_provider_qualifier("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` returns
  `("anthropic", "claude-opus-4-8")`; a configured provider composes
  `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "anthropic") == "anthropic:claude-opus-4-8"`.
- **The existing suite** — every other case in the file (lines 45, 49, 55, 94, 99, 122, 126, 138,
  150 and 156) keeps passing with no edits, including both canonical Bedrock shapes — versioned
  (`anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`) and the unversioned alias. The single edited case is
  the line-72 parametrization documented in Scope.
- **Failure path (the new capability)** — `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")` raises
  `LLMConfigError`; the message contains `bedrok` and at least one valid name.
- **Edge: unknown inline prefix** — `split_provider_qualifier("bedrok:claude-opus-4-8")` returns
  `(None, "bedrok:claude-opus-4-8")` and does not raise.
- **Edge: dotted multi-colon prefix** — `split_provider_qualifier("anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-
  20251001-v1:0")` returns `(None, <the whole id>)`, the property that makes path 1 safe.
- **Edge: a slashed member** — `split_provider_qualifier("gateway/openai:gpt-4o")` returns
  `("gateway/openai", "gpt-4o")`, the case the shape regex rejected.
- **The two de-registered names** — `split_provider_qualifier("test:FunctionModel")` and
  `split_provider_qualifier("google_genai:gemini-2.0")` each return `(None, <the whole string>)`,
  and `infer_provider` returns `None` for both. This pins the decision that neither name is
  grandfathered.
- **Back-compat enumeration** — a parametrized case over every one of the 24 names asserting
  `split_provider_qualifier(f"{name}:some-model") == (name, "some-model")`.
- **Drift** — the `importorskip`-guarded subset test described in Approach.
- **Fan-in** — `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` and `tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py` assert
  the recorded `provider` is `None` for a `FunctionModel` double.
- **No new optional import** — `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` continues to pass unchanged,
  which is what proves the set imported nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE` no longer exists anywhere in the tree; verified by
      `! grep -rq "_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE" src/ tests/` exiting 0.
- [ ] Neither decider module re-introduces a raw colon test; verified by
      `! grep -rq '":" in model' src/rebar/llm/config.py src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` exiting 0
      (scoped to the two decider modules — `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:101-102` legitimately
      contains that substring and is out of scope).
- [ ] `_resolve_target` and `infer_provider` each still call `split_provider_qualifier` (they do
      today at `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:239`/`:251` and `src/rebar/llm/config.py:213`).
- [ ] `import re` is gone from `src/rebar/llm/config.py`; verified by
      `! grep -q "^import re$" src/rebar/llm/config.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `split_provider_qualifier` decides by membership in the module-level `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`
      frozenset literal in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, and that set is exactly the 24 names listed in
      Approach; verified by a test asserting
      `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES == frozenset({<the 24 literals>})`.
- [ ] Neither `test` nor `google_genai` is a member; verified by a test asserting both are absent
      from `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`, that `split_provider_qualifier` returns `(None, <input>)` for
      `"test:FunctionModel"` and `"google_genai:gemini-2.0"`, and that `infer_provider` returns
      `None` for both.
- [ ] The change pulls in no optional import; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py::test_lean_workflow_runtime_pulls_no_heavy_stack`
      passing (it fails if `import rebar.llm` pulls `pydantic_ai` or `httpx`).
- [ ] A configured provider that is not a member raises `LLMConfigError` naming it and listing valid
      names; verified by a new test asserting `_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")` raises
      and that `"bedrok"` appears in the message.
- [ ] An unknown INLINE prefix does not raise and is treated as unqualified; verified by a new test
      asserting
      `split_provider_qualifier("bedrok:claude-opus-4-8") == (None, "bedrok:claude-opus-4-8")`.
- [ ] Back-compat is enumerated, not assumed: a parametrized test covers all 24 names and asserts
      each still splits as a qualifier.
- [ ] The static set cannot silently drift from the runtime registries; verified by a new
      `importorskip("pydantic_ai")` test asserting every key of `ProviderSession._builders` (built
      with `base_url` set, so `openai` is registered) and every member of
      `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` is in `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES`.
- [ ] Both canonical Bedrock id shapes still resolve with a configured provider; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] The usage-log fan-in is updated, not weakened: `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` and
      `tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py` assert the recorded `provider` `is None` (not
      `is not None`, and not deleted) for a `FunctionModel` double.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py
      tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py
      tests/unit/test_usage_log.py tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py
      tests/unit/test_model_classes.py` exits 0.
- [ ] The full default selection `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exits 0.
baseline.summary: Decide the provider qualifier by registry membership, not prefix shape, matching OSS consensus

## Why

Debugging-orchestration sessions periodically sweep for AWS + GitHub Actions errors "since the last sweep." Passing the last-sweep timeline across sessions needs a durable, zero-noise carrier. We already use a dedicated long-lived `session_log` ticket (`tomophobic-stilllife-mayfly` / `b2dc-b1ab-0bd9-47f6`, tagged `ops-sweep`) as an append-only ledger, but the convention is undocumented, so future sessions cannot reliably discover or extend it. `session_log` is the right carrier precisely because it is excluded from default `list`, `ready`/`next-batch`, and graph-health, and never syncs to Jira — an always-open ledger creates zero work-queue noise.

## What

Document the "ops error-sweep ledger" convention in the docs and add a one-line pointer in AGENTS.md so debug sessions discover it. This is a DOCS-ONLY change — no source or test code is touched.

- `docs/user-guide.md`: add a new subsection (e.g. "### Ops error-sweep ledger") in/after
  the existing "## Session logs" section, matching that section's concise, example-driven
  style. Cover: the ledger is a `session_log` ticket (and why — queue/graph/Jira
  exclusion); the current ledger id/alias + `ops-sweep` tag; discovery via
  `rebar search "ops-sweep"`; the newest comment / `SWEEP <ISO-8601> | window <start>..<end>`
  header convention and next-window rule; appending with `rebar comment <ledger-id>` (NOT
  `session-log append`, which is session-keyed and auto-rotates); linking filed tickets
  with `rebar link <filed> <ledger-id> relates_to` (non-blocking relations only); and how
  to recreate the ledger (`session-log start` + `tag ... ops-sweep`), with the tag+search
  as the durable anchor.
- `AGENTS.md`: extend ONLY the existing one-line "Session logs" pointer bullet under
  "Where to read" to mention the ops error-sweep ledger convention. Keep it a pointer, not
  restated content (AGENTS.md policy: already-documented topics are one-line pointers into
  docs/).

## Scope

- Files: `docs/user-guide.md` (new subsection), `AGENTS.md` (one-line pointer extension).
- Out of scope: any code/test change; restating the full convention in AGENTS.md.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/user-guide.md` has a new subsection under "## Session logs" documenting the
      ops error-sweep ledger convention accurately: session_log rationale, ledger id/alias
      + `ops-sweep` tag, discovery via search, the `SWEEP ... | window ...` header +
      next-window rule, append via `rebar comment` (not `session-log append`), link via
      `relates_to`, and recreation via `session-log start` + tag.
- [x] `AGENTS.md`'s existing "Session logs" pointer bullet is extended by one line/clause
      to mention the ops error-sweep ledger convention — a pointer only, no restated body.
- [x] The convention text matches the mechanics in docs/event-schema.md ("The session_log
      ticket type") and docs/user-guide.md ("Session logs") — no contradictions.
- [x] `make lint` passes; no new tooling added; no source/test files changed.
baseline.summary: Document the ops error-sweep ledger convention (session_log-based)

baseline.description:
## Impact, stated first

`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts` — the paging alarm that bug [rebar:34cd-1a7c-b9b1-4b05] created specifically so the LLM-Review live-lock could never again be invisible — **fired three times in the last seven days**, most recently **2026-08-11T20:05 PDT**, i.e. during the current landing burst. Each firing means an in-flight LLM-Review was killed by a container recreation.

By 34cd design that is the alarm doing its job. The reason it is worth a ticket is that **firing is supposed to be the exceptional case**, reachable (per 34cd) only by "a chronically busy bot" — and three firings in a week says the exceptional case is now routine.

Found by an automated ops error sweep of AWS CloudWatch (account 896586841071, us-east-1) over 2026-08-05T00:00Z -> 2026-08-12T04:00Z. No open ticket covers this; 34cd is closed, and [rebar:9ec0-02b2-8494-4ea5] (in_progress) covers only the *shutdown-side* half — manual restart, reboot, autodeploy rollback — which is a different trigger from the one seen here.

## Occurrences (rebar/host:review_interrupts, Sum > 0)

- 2026-08-07 04:33 PDT
- 2026-08-07 05:55 PDT
- 2026-08-11 20:05 PDT

Alarm state history confirms each as a full OK -> ALARM -> OK episode, self-clearing in ~15 minutes.

## The deferral run-up is the interesting part

`rebar/host:deploy_deferrals` immediately before the 2026-08-11 interrupt:

    2026-08-11 19:00 PDT   11 deferrals
    2026-08-11 20:00 PDT    3 deferrals
    2026-08-11 20:05 PDT    -> review_interrupts = 1

The autodeploy tick is ~2 minutes, so 11 deferrals in the 19:00 hour is roughly 22 minutes of continuous deferring, continuing into the next hour until the interrupt lands. `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` is **1800s (30 min)**. The run-up therefore matches the **`bound-exceeded`** path: the bot stayed busy long enough to spend the entire bound, after which autodeploy proceeds and kills the review. The 2026-08-07 firings show the same shape (13 deferrals at 04:00 -> interrupt 04:33; 15 deferrals at 05:00 -> interrupt 05:55).

## Stated uncertainty — this is an inference, not a reading

`rebar/host:review_interrupts` is published with **no dimensions**, so the metric cannot distinguish the two reasons the marker is emitted: `bound-exceeded` (chronically busy) versus `signal-unavailable` (the `/health` `in_flight` signal was unreadable and the deploy proceeded blind). The deferral run-up above is strong circumstantial evidence for `bound-exceeded`, but **confirming it requires `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` on the box**, which this sweep did not have access to. That check should be step one.

The distinction matters a great deal, because the two readings imply opposite fixes: `bound-exceeded` means reviews are queueing faster than they complete and the bound is correctly bounding a real overload; `signal-unavailable` means the drain check itself is broken and **every** deploy has been running blind — which would be a silent regression of 34cd rather than its intended behavior.

## Why not just raise DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX

Recording this so it is not the reflexive first move: 34cd chose 1800s deliberately as 1.5x the app-side `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (1200s) ceiling, with a test asserting `bound >= REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to keep the two in lockstep. Raising it would trade a killed review for a longer deploy stall, and if the true cause is `signal-unavailable` the bound is not involved at all and raising it would change nothing while appearing to.

## Secondary observation, same hour

`rebar/host:mirror_out_of_sync` also recorded a datapoint at 2026-08-11 20:00 PDT (and on 08-04, 08-05, 08-07 x2). These are isolated single datapoints that never breached `rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync`, so no alarm fired — consistent with brief Gerrit->GitHub replication lag rather than a stuck mirror. Noted for correlation only; not claimed as related.

## Acceptance Criteria

All four are resolved. The disposition is DIAGNOSIS + NO ACTION on autodeploy behaviour; what remains is carried by two linked child tickets, not by this one.

- [x] The reason field behind each firing is read from `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` and
      recorded here: **`bound-exceeded`, all of them** (4 firings, not 3 — see below).
      Read via SSM RunShellScript on i-00880b2c7f13527c5; full evidence in the verdict comment.
- [x] If `signal-unavailable`: **NOT APPLICABLE — ruled out by measurement.** The token appears
      ZERO times in the entire unit journal back to 2026-07-03. 34cd's drain check is healthy
      and has not regressed; the `/health` `in_flight` probe needs no repair.
- [x] If `bound-exceeded`: decision recorded. **A landing burst that outlasts the 30-minute
      bound is ACCEPTED as steady state.** Operator disposition, 2026-08-12: take no action on
      autodeploy behaviour. Do NOT raise `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` (34cd pinned it to 1.5x
      `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` under a test, and the saturated trace indicates a larger bound
      would only defer the same kill). Interrupted reviews are retried by the backfill
      reconciler, so this is not an outage. The alarm is firing CORRECTLY on real events.
      Pager-noise retune is deliberately NOT undertaken now: revisit only if the noise becomes
      a problem in practice.
- [x] `review_interrupts` dimensionality: **carried forward, not dropped.** Split out as
      [rebar:613a-e3f4-14a6-45a3] (dowdy-antarctic-junco), linked `discovered_from` this
      ticket. It is observability-only but is a Terraform alarm-contract change requiring an
      operator `terraform apply`, so it is sequenced separately rather than closed here.

## Disposition (2026-08-12)

**Verdict (a): TRUE POSITIVES.** Every firing is a genuine, distinct interrupt; the alarm and the drain check are both working as designed. Two corrections to this ticket as filed:

1. **There were FOUR firings, not three.** `2026-08-12T03:59:33Z` landed 27 seconds inside the
   sweep's closing boundary and was missed. It came ~56 min after the third, i.e. a second full
   1800s bound spent back-to-back.
2. **The root cause is sharper than "a chronically busy bot".** 34cd justified the 1800s bound
   on the premise that `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200` means `in_flight` necessarily reaches 0
   within it. That holds per-review and fails in aggregate: `in_flight` is a CONCURRENT gauge,
   and the episode trace shows it oscillating 2->1->2 across 30 unbroken minutes without ever
   reaching 0. Reviews completed normally throughout; none outlived its timeout. The bound is
   not defeated by a stuck review — it is outlasted by ordinary pipelining. So "reachable only
   by a chronically busy bot" is literally true but does not imply the rarity it was taken to
   imply.

A metric artifact was considered and EXCLUDED by measurement (journal total 7 = offset file 7, journal intact to 2026-07-03, every datapoint matching a distinct journal line). The latent rotation double-count hazard found while excluding it is filed as [rebar:2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2] (affluent-conveyable-dromedary), linked `discovered_from`.

No code was changed, and nothing was mutated on the box or in AWS (read-only `journalctl`, `cat`, `grep`, and `get-metric-statistics` only).

## Notes

Filed by an automated ops error sweep. No file_impact is recorded and none is expected: the outcome is a diagnosis plus a recorded no-action decision, with all implementation residue moved to the two linked child tickets above.

baseline.description:
Follow-up from d19d LLM-Review (Gerrit change 1776, advisory comments — d19d landed with LLM-Review +1). Hardens the many-to-many outbound path for the four advisory findings below. None are live-behaviour regressions (the create-path resolution is gated on a seeded mapping), so this is defensive alignment + test depth.

## Problem

1. **(correctness) Case-sensitivity mismatch on the create path.** `outbound_differ._compute_outbound_create_mutation` suppresses a create with `target not in mapping.projects` — a **case-SENSITIVE** membership test (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:585`). The applier's cross-project guard normalizes both sides to uppercase (`apply_inbound_records`/`applier._cross_project_targets`, `applier.py:247-262` `.upper()`). A `bridge_project` differing only in case from the mapping key (`"b"` vs `"B"`) is suppressed on the create path yet passes the applier guard — the two paths disagree. Jira keys are canonically uppercase so it does not fire in practice, but the paths must agree.
2. **(tests) Applier guard store-loading wiring is not exercised end-to-end.** The many-to-many guard branch `list(read_projects(repo_root).keys()) or _project` (`applier.py:618`) is only unit-tested at the pure-helper level (`_cross_project_targets` with a literal set). The store-loading path through the caller (`apply()` reading a seeded `projects.json`) has no test.
3. **(tests) The `run_differs` load_mapping seam has no fail-closed test.** `_run_differs_outbound` threads `projects_store.load_mapping(repo_root)` into the outbound diff (`run_differs.py:471`); the contract is that a MALFORMED `projects.json` fails closed (ValueError aborts the pass). `load_mapping`'s ValueError is unit-tested in isolation, but nothing proves `run_differs` lets it propagate through the seam.
4. **(low priority, accept + document) The mapping is read twice per pass** — `load_mapping` in the outbound seam (create resolution) and `read_projects` in the applier guard. A mid-pass `projects.json` change could make them disagree. Accepted: `projects.json` writes are rare operator CLI actions and a pass is a short single window; document the assumption rather than thread one read through.

## Approach

**Finding 1 (fix, `outbound_differ.py`).** Make the create-path membership test case-insensitive and align it with the applier's normalization. Resolve the ticket's target, then match it against the mapping keys case-insensitively; when it matches, stamp the **canonical mapping key** (not the raw `bridge_project` case) so the transport routes to the real project key. When it does not match (stale/typo binding) or the ticket is not synced, emit no create — the existing suppression contract. Replace:

```python
target = projects_store.resolve_project(ticket, mapping)
if not target or target not in mapping.projects:
    return
create_fields[_BRIDGE_TARGET_PROJECT_KEY] = target
```

with a case-insensitive canonical-key lookup (`next((k for k in mapping.projects if k.upper() == target.upper()), None)`), stamping the canonical key.

**Finding 2 (test, `test_applier_cross_project_guard.py`).** Add an integration test that writes a seeded `projects.json` (two projects) under `tmp_path`'s `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/` and drives `applier.apply()` (repo_root=tmp_path) with an update whose key is foreign to the seeded set — asserting the guard refuses before any write — and a companion asserting a key IN the seeded set is allowed. This exercises the real `read_projects(repo_root)` store-loading wiring through the caller, not the pure helper.

**Finding 3 (test, `test_outbound_multi_project.py`).** Add a `run_differs`-seam test: write a MALFORMED `projects.json` under `tmp_path`, build a minimal ctx (scoped pass so binding recovery is skipped, empty `local_tickets`), call `run_differs._run_differs_outbound(ctx, [], backend)`, and assert it raises `ValueError` — proving the seam threads `load_mapping(repo_root)` and fails closed rather than degrading silently.

**Finding 4 (document).** Add a short code comment at the outbound seam noting the two-read single-pass-window assumption is accepted (rare CLI writes); no behaviour change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The create-path membership check in `outbound_differ.py` is case-insensitive; a ticket whose `bridge_project` matches a mapping key case-insensitively (e.g. `"b"` vs key `"B"`) emits a create stamped with the canonical mapping key, and a genuinely-absent project still suppresses the create. Proven by a held-out RED test in `test_outbound_multi_project.py`.
- [x] An integration test in `test_applier_cross_project_guard.py` seeds `projects.json` and drives `apply()` through the store-loading guard wiring (foreign key refused, member key allowed).
- [x] A `run_differs`-seam test proves a malformed `projects.json` aborts the outbound phase with `ValueError` (fail-closed).
- [x] Finding 4 is documented as accepted at the outbound seam (comment); no behaviour change.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the touched reconciler test modules pass.
baseline.summary: M2M outbound: case-insensitive project membership + guard-wiring test depth

Scope: `src/rebar/_commands/**`, `_cli/**`, `_engine_support/**`, `_io/**`. ~205 lines leave.

Largest cluster, unanticipated: the bash dispatcher is GONE (no `*.sh`, no `ticket_txn.py`) yet ~16 module docstrings still narrate 'Ports ticket-X.sh', 'byte-parity with the dispatcher arm', 'Tier E cutover', 'until E7'. ~126 lines, confirmed stale rather than merely historical. `docs/bash-migration.md` is the existing home.

Verified stale and confirmed individually: `_commands/txn.py:3-8` cites a shim that does not exist; `_engine_support/reads.py:15-19` states a false reason for the module's location; `_commands/leaf.py:9-12` says tag/untag/archive are 'tracked as child tickets' while all three are defined in that same file; `_engine_support/__init__.py:7-9` cites compat shims that do not exist; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side 'lands in a later sub-task' six lines above the line importing it; `_cli/_help.py:3-8` is truncated mid-clause (introduced by 3a53e202a7).

`_engine_support/reads_cli.py` explains the same unknown-option rule in five near-identical blocks — a ->CODE fix (extract one helper) rather than a comment edit.

Headroom: `_commands/init.py` 799 -> ~782 (18 lines of margin), `_cli/_llm_commands.py` 789 -> ~778 (22) — both WITHOUT any code extraction. The module-size pressure in these two files is partly caused by comments explaining previous module-size splits.

New ADR proposed: 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation' — a prior-art survey (git-bug/git-appraise vs git-issue/bugs-everywhere/Fossil) stated in four places.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria F1/E6)

AC3/AC4 rested on a subjective correct-vs-delete judgment with no decision rule or observable check. Superseded below with the parent 373f disposition vocabulary and a recorded-reason rule for every deletion.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one of the parent
      373f labels: RELOCATE (to docs/bash-migration.md, an ADR, or a ticket, reduced to a
      one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE, or CORRECT-IN-PLACE.
- [x] Decision rule for CORRECT-vs-DELETE: a stale comment that documents CURRENT runtime
      behavior / a live invariant is CORRECTED in place; a comment is DELETED only when the thing
      it describes no longer exists (referenced artifact removed, or the statement is superseded).
      For each DELETE, the reason (referenced-artifact-gone / superseded) is stated in the commit
      body or a ticket comment, so no comment documenting current behavior is removed without a
      recorded reason.
- [x] The dead bash-dispatcher narration (~16 module docstrings citing 'Ports ticket-X.sh',
      'byte-parity with the dispatcher arm', 'Tier E cutover', 'until E7' — the bash dispatcher
      and ticket_txn.py no longer exist) is relocated to docs/bash-migration.md where still
      useful, or deleted as stale with the reason recorded.
- [x] The individually-confirmed stale comments are CORRECTED or DELETED per the rule above:
      `_commands/txn.py:3-8` (cites a non-existent shim), `_engine_support/reads.py:15-19`
      (false location reason), `_commands/leaf.py:9-12` (tag/untag/archive defined in-file, not
      'tracked as child tickets'), `_engine_support/__init__.py:7-9` (non-existent compat shims),
      `_io/__init__.py:14` (contradicted 6 lines below), `_cli/_help.py:3-8` (truncated clause).
- [x] The `_engine_support/reads_cli.py` five near-identical unknown-option blocks are collapsed
      to one shared helper (behavior-preserving), verified by the existing CLI tests.
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands;
      lint/type pragmas (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and
      test-introspected docstrings are DO_NOT_MOVE.
- [x] Any new ADR (e.g. 'Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation') EXISTS and is
      committed before any comment citing it is collapsed.
- [x] The actual recovered comment-line count is measured (by diff) and recorded on this ticket
      as an output, not a target.
- [x] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass unchanged.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Cloud and Jira DC currently nest retries across subprocess, SDK, wrapper, and reconciler layers. A non-idempotent ticket write can therefore exceed a predictable request budget or be replayed after an ambiguous commit. This task defines the provider-neutral logical-operation contract before either adapter changes.

## Approach
Create immutable operation/outcome values plus one fake-clock retry-budget owner in the reconciler domain. Adapter layers report one physical invocation at a time; they do not sleep or replay. This keeps the approved retry envelope in one place while preserving the additive-jitter behavior already accepted in ADR 0084.

The contract is exact:
- `logical_id` is one canonical UUID string generated once per logical operation, retained across every invocation or observation.
- `Disposition` has exactly `applied`, `already_satisfied`, `recovered`, `retryable_deferred`, `commit_unknown`, `permanent_failure`, `exhausted_transient`, `dependency_deferred`, `scope_deferred`, `safety_aborted`, `skipped`.
- `FailureScope` has exactly `none`, `ticket`, `endpoint`, `tenant`, `provider`, `global`.
- `ReplaySafety` has exactly `not_applicable`, `safe`, `observe_first`, `forbidden`.
- `DelaySource` has exactly `none`, `fallback_jitter`, `provider`, `fuse`.
- Enum values serialize as the lowercase strings above. Invocation/request totals are non-negative integers. Durations serialize as integer milliseconds. `retry_not_before` is UTC RFC 3339 with `Z`.
- Canonical bytes route through `rebar._store.canonical.canonical_bytes` with its default `ascii_only=False`; no inline JSON serializer is added. Equivalent outcomes therefore produce byte-identical sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON.
- `invocation_count` is the number already executed, ranging from 0 through 3. `retry_index` is zero-based: index 0 selects `[2s,3s)` while index 1 selects `[4s,5s)` using `2**(retry_index+1)+U[0,1)`.
- Diagnostic entries are chronological immutable mappings. Only `stage`, `category`, `status_code`, `provider_code`, `retry_after_ms`, `message` are admitted; optional absent keys are omitted. Raw headers, request/response bodies, credentials, ticket content are never admitted. Message redaction calls the public `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` seam with only the `message` key, then applies this contract size bound. Each message is capped after redaction at 512 Unicode code points: an overlong value becomes its first 511 code points plus `…`.
- The outcome holds at most eight diagnostic entries. Eight or fewer remain unchanged. On overflow, retain the first seven; entry eight is exactly `stage=diagnostic`, `category=truncated`, `message=dropped=N`, with other optional keys absent. Worked example: nine inputs serialize entry eight as `{"category":"truncated","message":"dropped=2","stage":"diagnostic"}` because inputs eight plus nine were omitted.
- The budget permits at most three physical invocations, at most 15,000 ms cumulative sleep. An authoritative provider delay is a lower bound, never shortened. If the next required delay cannot fit, return `retry_not_before` without sleeping or incrementing invocation/request totals.
- After an ambiguous write, observe the desired primary-store postcondition before replay. Observed desired state produces `recovered`. Conclusive old state may replay if budget remains. Failed or inconclusive observation produces non-replaying `commit_unknown` with `ReplaySafety.forbidden`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/operation_outcome.py` — immutable provider-neutral values, bounded diagnostics, canonical serialization via the existing store seam.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/retry_budget.py` — sole three-invocation, 15-second fake-clock budget.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_operation_retry_budget.py` — deterministic contract, bounds, schedule, deadline, ambiguity tables.
- `docs/adr/0103-reconciler-operation-coordination.md` — provisional ownership/recovery decision.
- `docs/adr/README.md` — ADR index entry.

Grounding: `docs/adr/0084-acli-429-rate-limit-backoff.md` plus `acli_subprocess.py::_rate_limit_backoff` establish the existing additive-jitter formula. `docs/adr/0041-llm-diagnostic-sanitization.md` plus `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` establish allowlist-first redaction. Inspection shows that sanitizer does not enforce the ADR size promise, so this operation contract adds only its own size bound. `rebar._store.canonical.canonical_bytes` is the existing single canonical-JSON seam already used by reconciler modules.

## Testing
Use injected UUID, jitter, fake clock values. Table tests cover every enum member, canonical byte serialization, Unicode truncation, diagnostic overflow, all budget boundaries, provider delays that fit or exceed the remaining sleep budget, every ambiguity branch. Poison sleepers plus invocation counters prove rejected delays or `commit_unknown` perform no hidden work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The outcome field types expose exactly the enum member sets listed above; verified by exhaustive enum contract tests.
- [x] Equivalent outcome values serialize through `canonical_bytes` to byte-identical compact UTF-8 JSON; verified by byte fixtures containing non-ASCII text.
- [x] Diagnostic construction drops every field outside the six-key allowlist; verified with headers, bodies, credentials, ticket content.
- [x] Diagnostic messages use the centralized redaction seam before persistence; verified with every ADR 0041 credential/PII pattern.
- [x] Diagnostic truncation matches the 512-code-point rule plus the exact nine-input sentinel example; verified by Unicode boundary tables.
- [x] One canonical logical id remains stable across three physical invocations; verified by an injected-UUID sequence.
- [x] Invocation/request totals include only executed work; verified by counters on success, rejection, ambiguity paths.
- [x] No schedule permits a fourth physical invocation; verified by an exhaustion table.
- [x] No schedule permits cumulative sleep above 15,000 ms; verified at exact plus one-millisecond-over boundaries.
- [x] Zero-based retry indexes produce `[2s,3s)` then `[4s,5s)` with no third sleep; verified at deterministic jitter endpoints.
- [x] A fitting authoritative provider delay remains the sleep lower bound; verified with fake-clock tables.
- [x] An over-budget provider delay returns `retry_not_before` without hidden work; verified by poison sleeper/counter assertions.
- [x] Observed desired state returns `recovered`; verified by the desired-state ambiguity case.
- [x] Conclusive old state replays only within remaining budget; verified by within-budget/exhausted tables.
- [x] Failed or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`; verified by failure/inconclusive tables.
- [x] Time-dependent tests complete with zero wall-clock sleep; verified by the injected fake clock.
- [x] ADR 0103 records retry ownership, Jira non-idempotency, observe-before-replay, lifecycle owners, selected-route-only deltas, rollback, the ADR 0087 retry-ownership delta, desired-state deltas from ADRs 0004, 0026, and 0029, retained ADR 0084 additive jitter, and rejection of full/decorrelated jitter for only two bounded sleeps; verified by ADR numbering/index tests plus document inspection.

## Out of scope
Cloud/DC adapter execution, legacy dispatch integration, fuse consumption, production cutover are later tasks.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S1 T1 — Define the logical-operation outcome and retry budget

baseline.description:
## Summary

`tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py::test_tree_listed_ticket_blob_missing_from_object_database_fails_closed` fails intermittently on CI:

```
tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py:642: AssertionError: assert False
```

Line 642 is a SETUP precondition, not the behaviour under test:

```python
loose_object = object_root / blob_oid[:2] / blob_oid[2:]
assert loose_object.is_file()      # <-- fails here
loose_object.unlink()
```

The test wants to delete a ticket blob from the object database and assert the pinned view fails closed. To do that it assumes the blob is stored as a LOOSE object at `objects/ab/cdef…`. That is an implementation detail of git's storage, not a guarantee.

## Probable mechanism

If git packs the object before line 642, the loose path does not exist and the assertion fails — before the test ever exercises the missing-object path it exists to cover. Auto gc is a plausible trigger: `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` records that rebar deliberately **no longer sets `gc.auto=0`** ("This reachability guarantee is why rebar no longer needs ``gc.auto=0``"), so a `git gc --auto` may run after a commit and pack loose objects once the loose-object count crosses its threshold. Object counts differ between a fresh CI store and a developer's, which fits a failure that reproduces on CI but not locally.

Stated as probable rather than proven: the packing was not reproduced locally, and the diagnosis rests on the assertion's dependency on loose storage plus the removal of the `gc.auto=0` pin.

## Why it matters beyond the noise

The assertion that fails is scaffolding. When it trips, the test reports a failure while the behaviour it guards — the pinned view failing closed on a missing object — was never executed. A green run of this test also does not prove much on any store where the object happened to be packed, since the test would have failed rather than adapted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The test no longer depends on the blob being LOOSE, and covers each storage shape
      with a route appropriate to it. No skip: a skipped case exercises nothing, which is
      the gap this ticket closes rather than relocates.
      - LOOSE: delete the loose object file.
      - PACKED: induce packing DETERMINISTICALLY and surgically — write a pack
        containing ONLY the target blob (`git pack-objects` fed that one oid), delete
        the loose copy, assert `git cat-file -e` still resolves it (so it is genuinely
        readable only from the pack), then delete that pack. `git gc` is not used: it is
        threshold-dependent, so it cannot deterministically induce the shape.
- [x] The packed route leaves the commit and trees READABLE. Removing a whole repack
      would drop them too, and the view would then raise for a missing tree rather than
      for the target blob — passing for the wrong reason. Verified by asserting the
      error names the ticket's own `*-CREATE.json` path, not merely the generic
      "missing Git object" phrase.
- [x] The behaviour under test still runs: the pinned view is asserted to fail closed on
      a missing object. Verified by re-introducing the missing-object condition and
      observing `PinnedTicketViewError`.
- [x] The fix is proven against BOTH storage shapes — object loose, and object packed —
      rather than only the one a developer happens to have.

## Definition of Done

- The test cannot fail on its own setup precondition.
- Both storage shapes exercised.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Observed on Gerrit change 2311 (ubuntu-latest, py3.12) while landing `baf9-eea0`. The same run passed py3.11 and py3.13 on identical code, and the test passed locally on three consecutive runs plus a full-file run, which is what points at storage state rather than the change under review. 2311 touches docs and sandbox warning text only — nothing in the ticket store or pinned view.
baseline.summary: Pinned-view test fails on its own loose-object precondition

baseline.description:
## Context
The planner must be compared with legacy decisions before it gains authority. Preview consumers require the existing mutation array and canonical hash to remain stable while lifecycle intent data is additive and versioned.

## Outcome
Run `TicketPlan` generation in shadow, compare its mutations/dispositions with legacy output, and add a versioned lifecycle-intents preview section that old consumers can ignore.

## Plan
1. Feed the same frozen observation to legacy differ and shadow planner. Fail tests on unexplained mutation or disposition divergence and name approved deltas.
2. Extend preview/manifest rendering with an ADDITIVE versioned lifecycle-intents section under a new top-level key, leaving every existing key and the mutation array bytes untouched. Preserve the existing mutation array bytes and `serialize_manifest` canonical hash exactly.
3. Ensure construction, check, dry-run, and shadow modes perform zero repository saves, ticket writes, Jira calls, or subprocess launches.
4. Add golden fixtures covering normal, deferred dependency, filtered, tombstoned, and partial-snapshot plans.

## Impacted sites (existing construction/consumer surface)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/manifest_renderer.py` — `render_plan` / `render_dry_run_or_strict` / `render_throttle`: gain ONE additive top-level `lifecycle_intents` section keyed off the shadow `ticket_plans`; the existing mutation array and every existing key are emitted byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_planning.py:167` — the consumer that lazy-loads the renderer (`renderer_mod = _load_manifest_renderer()`): passes the shadow plans through to the renderer additively; no existing behavior changes.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mutation.py` — `serialize_manifest` (the canonical mutation-array manifest + sha256): NOT modified; a golden test pins its bytes/hash to prove the additive section does not perturb it.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/ticket_planner.py` — pure `plan_pass` shadow plans are the parity source; a new PURE parity helper compares shadow mutations/dispositions against the legacy mutation list and returns named deltas (zero I/O).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py:285` — the shadow construction site (`ctx.observation, ctx.ticket_plans = ticket_planner.plan_pass(...)`): stays a pure, additive, effect-free shadow attach; parity comparison reads `ctx.mutations` (legacy) vs `ctx.ticket_plans` (shadow) without writes.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_ticket_plan_shadow.py` — held-out oracle extended with parity + additive-section + byte-stability + zero-I/O golden tests.

## Testing
Golden and poison tests pin old fields/hashes, the additive section, parity diagnostics, and zero I/O.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Shadow mutations match legacy behavior for the ticket-sourced corpus except explicitly named approved deltas.
- [x] Shadow dispositions match legacy behavior for the ticket-sourced corpus except explicitly named approved deltas.
- [x] Preview preserves the existing mutation array bytes exactly.
- [x] Preview preserves the existing `serialize_manifest` canonical hash exactly.
- [x] Preview adds one versioned lifecycle-intents section that legacy consumers may ignore.
- [x] Construction, check, dry-run, and shadow paths perform zero repository/provider/subprocess writes.
- [x] A parity failure identifies the ticket identity, the observation version, and the differing plan fields, with no unbounded or secret content.

## Out of scope
Production coordinator authority remains RP-03 S3.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S2 T3 — Shadow plans through additive preview output

baseline.description:
Two cheap, decoupled wins split out of the `doctor`/`fsck`/`validate` consolidation. The consolidation itself is already tracked on epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` and is NOT duplicated here.

**1. `validate --fix` is advertised in three places and does nothing.** `validate.py:361-362` is literally `elif arg == "--fix": pass  # accepted, no-op (the bash --fix path is unimplemented)`. It is documented in `--help` (`validate.py:342`), in `docs/cli-reference.md:458`, AND printed at runtime as the suggested remedy (`validate.py:309`, `:322`: "Run with `--fix` to attempt automatic repairs (interactive)"). A user following the tool's own advice gets nothing, silently.

Maintainer decision: remove it. `doctor` is the path for fixing.

**2. `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` sends agents to the wrong command.** It says to run "`rebar validate` (or `rebar fsck`) against the tracker to confirm store integrity" — but store integrity is `fsck`'s job and is not something `validate` checks at all. `fsck` reads bytes and git refs; `validate` reads reduced ticket semantics. They are cleanly disjoint.

Investigation confirmed the ambiguity has already cost real work: two epics (`dabb` and `18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb`) were independently filed scoping the same `doctor` command, and `18ae` was closed as a duplicate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `--fix` is removed from `validate`'s parser, `--help`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, and both runtime hints
- [x] `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` names the correct command for store integrity
- [x] Epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` is updated with this audit's findings (capability matrix, the no-op, the usage evidence that `doctor` is invoked by nothing)

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criterion G1G2) — the edit set was under-enumerated

"Advertised in three places" was wrong. Verified against the tree, `--fix` is advertised at FOUR independent sites, plus the two runtime hints:

1. `src/rebar/_cli/help/validate.txt:1` — the `--help` usage line (the SOURCE of the generated doc)
2. `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt:23` — the `rebar` overview listing
3. `README.md:370` — the flag list in the validate paragraph
4. `docs/cli-reference.md:458` — GENERATED from the help text; must be REGENERATED
   (`python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`), never hand-edited, or the CI drift gate rejects it
5. `validate.py:309` and `:322` — the runtime "Run with `--fix` to attempt automatic repairs
   (interactive)" hints
6. `validate.py:361-362` — the parser arm itself (`elif arg == "--fix": pass`)

`README.md` is additionally covered by `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py`, so the README edit must keep that gate green.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] `--fix` is removed from `validate`'s parser (`validate.py:361-362`)
- [x] `--fix` is removed from ALL FOUR advertisement sites: `_cli/help/validate.txt`,
      `_cli/help/overview.txt`, `README.md`, and `docs/cli-reference.md` (the last REGENERATED via
      `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, with `--check` clean)
- [x] Both runtime hints (`validate.py:309`, `:322`) no longer suggest `--fix`; they point at
      `doctor`, which is the path for fixing
- [x] Passing `--fix` is REFUSED rather than silently accepted, via validate's existing
      unknown-option fall-through: stderr `Unknown option: --fix` and **exit 1**
- [x] `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` both pass
- [x] `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md:91` names `fsck` (store integrity), not `validate`
- [x] Epic `dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6` is updated with this audit's findings (capability matrix, the
      no-op, the usage evidence that `doctor` is invoked by nothing)


## CORRECTION 3 (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G6) — the exit code was wrong

Correction 2 above asserted `--fix` would be refused with "exit 2, unknown option". That is mechanically wrong and was my error, not the ticket's. Verified empirically:

    $ rebar validate --bogus-option ; echo $?
    Unknown option: --bogus-option
    1

`_engine_support/validate.py`'s unknown-argument fall-through (the `else` arm) prints `Unknown option: ...` and returns **1**. Exit 2 comes only from the `--output` parser (`OutputFormatError`), which `--fix` never reaches. Deleting the `elif arg == "--fix": pass` arm therefore yields exit 1 from the existing else-branch — no new code is needed to refuse it, and no exit-code change should be attempted as part of this ticket.


## CORRECTION 4 (plan-review BLOCK, criteria G1G2) — the in-file `_HELP` string

Corrections 1-3 still missed the `_HELP` literal INSIDE `_engine_support/validate.py`, which advertises `--fix` at two lines. Verified:

    validate.py:337  _HELP = """Usage: rebar validate [--quick] [--full] [--fix] ...
    validate.py:342    --fix          Attempt to automatically fix issues (interactive)

That is a SIXTH advertisement site (distinct from `_cli/help/validate.txt`, which is the packaged help text). The complete removal set is therefore:

1. `_engine_support/validate.py:337` — `_HELP` usage line
2. `_engine_support/validate.py:342` — `_HELP` option description
3. `_engine_support/validate.py:309`, `:322` — the two runtime "Run with `--fix`" hints
4. `_engine_support/validate.py:361-362` — the parser arm itself
5. `_cli/help/validate.txt:1` — packaged help usage line
6. `_cli/help/overview.txt:23` — overview listing
7. `README.md:370` — flag list
8. `docs/cli-reference.md:458` — GENERATED; regenerate, never hand-edit

The lesson for the implementer: `grep -rn -- '--fix'` across `src/ docs/ README.md` is the check, not a curated list. The final AC below requires exactly that grep to come back clean.

## Acceptance Criteria (FINAL — supersedes all lists above)

- [x] `grep -rn -- '--fix' src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py src/rebar/_cli/help/ README.md
      docs/cli-reference.md` returns NO advertisement of a validate `--fix` flag
- [x] The parser arm is deleted, so `--fix` falls through to the existing unknown-option handler:
      stderr `Unknown option: --fix`, **exit 1** (NOT exit 2 — exit 2 comes only from the
      `--output` parser, which `--fix` never reaches)
- [x] Both runtime hints point at `doctor`, which is the path for fixing
- [x] `docs/cli-reference.md` is REGENERATED (`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`), `--check` clean
- [x] `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` passes

## Context
Two store identifiers are currently fixed: the worktree/symlink dir `.tickets-tracker` (env-overridable via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` but NOT via project TOML) and the orphan **branch name** `tickets` (hardcoded in ~20 git invocations, no override at all). Make both overridable through project config, defaulting to the current values so every existing repo is unaffected.

## Proposed design
Add a typed `tracker` config section in `src/rebar/config.py` so the auto-derived env names line up with the established ones:
- `tracker.dir = ".tickets-tracker"`  -> auto-env `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` (already the canonical override; keep `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` as legacy alias).
- `tracker.branch = "tickets"`        -> auto-env `REBAR_TRACKER_BRANCH`.
Register in `_SECTION_CLASSES`, `_SECTIONS` (coercers: dir = relative-safe path; branch = valid git ref via a small validator), and `TrackerConfig` dataclass on `Config`.

Introduce a single resolver `tickets_branch(root=None)` next to `tracker_dir()`, and ROUTE BOTH through the resolved typed Config (full precedence: `-c` flag > env > project > user > default), not env-only. `tracker_dir()` currently consults env only (config.py:81-87) — it must read resolved config like the branch resolver.

## Call sites to migrate off the literals
- Branch `tickets` / `origin/tickets` (replace with `tickets_branch()` + f"origin/{branch}"):
  - `_commands/init.py` (lines ~272-295, 281): orphan/worktree creation, fetch, mount.
  - `_store/sync.py` (read reconverge, ~83-153) and `_store/push.py` (push refspec line 112, merge ~124-165).
  - `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_concurrency.py:56`, `_advisory_lock.py:498,533`.
  - `_engine_support/reads.py:187` (rev-parse verify).
  - `_commands/fsck.py:227-236` (PUSH_PENDING vs origin/<branch>).
- Worktree dir `.tickets-tracker` (replace with `tracker_dir()` / its basename):
  - The DUPLICATE `tracker_dir()` in `_engine_support/reads.py:99-149` must be unified with / kept in sync with `config.tracker_dir()`. NOTE: that copy is NOT a pure resolver — it also runs a git work-tree validation gate (`rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`); preserve that on unification (keep it, or split path-resolution from validation explicitly), don't silently drop it.
  - `_commands/init.py:152,199,418,461-469`: dir creation, the git `_exclude` it writes, the symlink name, the worktree-path resolver. The exclude must use the resolved basename so a custom dir is auto-gitignored.

## Constraints / decisions
- Defaults unchanged; pure additive. Existing repos and `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` keep working.
- Project config (committed `[tool.rebar]` in pyproject.toml / rebar.toml) is the right layer for branch name so all clones of one repo agree; the discovery walk stops at `.git` so it resolves at the repo root before the worktree exists.
- OUT OF SCOPE: renaming an EXISTING store (that is a migration). Both values are read at `init` time and thereafter; document that changing them on an initialized repo orphans the old branch/dir and is not auto-migrated. fsck SHOULD warn if a configured branch/dir does not match what is mounted — comparing the precedence-resolved config ("configured") against the actual checked-out branch + worktree/symlink target ("mounted", via `git worktree list` / the symlink).
- Validate branch against `git check-ref-format`-style rules (reject spaces, `..`, leading `-`, `~^:?*[`, trailing `/` or `.lock`). Validate `dir` shape too: a safe relative path (no absolute / `..` traversal) unless supplied via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tracker.dir` and `tracker.branch` exist as typed config keys with the precedence chain and appear in `rebar config` output + docs/config.md.
- [ ] A single `tracker_dir()` and a new `tickets_branch()` resolver are the only sources of these values; the duplicate resolver is removed/unified **with its git work-tree validation gate preserved** (see Constraints).
- [ ] All git invocations listed above use the resolvers (no remaining `"tickets"` / `.tickets-tracker` literals in code paths).
- [ ] `rebar init` honors both on a fresh repo: custom branch + custom dir create + mount + gitignore correctly; round-trips through a **write+sync** path (create -> push/pull or reconcile dry-run -> read-back), not just create/list/show.
- [ ] Defaults reproduce todays behavior byte-for-byte (regression tests green).
- [ ] Branch-name validation rejects invalid refs with a clear ConfigError.
- [ ] `dir`-shape validation rejects unsafe paths (absolute / `..` traversal) with a clear ConfigError.
- [ ] Docs updated: README storage section + docs/config.md + docs/architecture.md note configurability.

- [ ] The orphan / no-auto-migrate behavior (changing dir/branch on an initialized repo) is explicitly DOCUMENTED (plan body mentioned it; now an AC pins it).

## Suggested child tasks
1. config: add TrackerConfig section + coercers + branch-ref AND dir-shape validators + docs (config.md, README storage section, architecture.md; incl. the orphan/no-auto-migrate note).
2. resolvers: add tickets_branch(); route tracker_dir() through resolved config; unify the _engine_support duplicate.
3. migrate branch call sites (init/sync/push/reconciler/fsck/reads).
4. migrate worktree-dir call sites (init exclude/symlink/path resolver).
5. tests: custom dir+branch init e2e exercising a write+sync round-trip; validator accept/reject; regression test defaults; fsck mismatch warning (runnable under `pytest -m "not integration"`).

# Bindings key on the Jira KEY, which changes when an issue moves project

## Context / Problem

A Jira issue's KEY changes when it is moved between projects; its numeric `id` never does. Old keys are normally stacked in the `moved_issue_key` table so the old key still resolves — but a Data-Center-specific Atlassian KB documents that third-party apps moving issues via workflow post-functions, automations or scheduled routines can FAIL to update that table, after which the old key stops resolving entirely.

rebar's bindings are keyed on the KEY, and pervasively so — not just `get_jira_key`/`get_local_id`, but the `reverse` index, `note_absent`, `_retire`, `clear_absent` and `set_last_get` all take a `jira_key`. So a moved issue can silently detach: the binding points at a key that no longer resolves, the absence probe reads it as gone, and the local ticket is orphaned from an issue that still exists.

**What is NOT established, and must not be built on.** An earlier research pass asserted that `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns 200 with a body carrying the NEW key. That was retracted on a second pass and is unverified: the KB does not state whether a stale key yields 200-with-new-key, 301 or 404. The remediation below is deliberately chosen to be correct under ALL THREE readings, so this story does not block on settling it — but it is still settled here, as evidence, because two passes disagreed and the next reader deserves the answer.

## Approach

**Record the numeric `id` alongside the key on every binding, and resolve by `id` when a key lookup misses — re-keying the binding to the issue's current key when it does.**

This is deliberately ADDITIVE rather than a re-keying of the store, and that choice is the whole design decision:

* the binding store is SHARED WITH CLOUD. Changing the store's identity from key to id would rewrite
  the `reverse` index and every absence/retirement/last-get path for both vendors — a large blast
  radius on the live Cloud bridge to fix a DC-specific detachment. Additive id-capture leaves every
  existing key-keyed path behaving exactly as today.
* it is correct under all three unresolved readings of what a stale key returns. If the old key still
  resolves (200, with or without the new key in the body) nothing changes and the fallback never
  fires. If it 404s, the id fallback recovers the binding. No detection heuristic depends on the
  unverified behaviour.
* it degrades safely on a store written before this change: an entry with no recorded `id` simply has
  no fallback and behaves exactly as it does today. No migration is required, and the id is captured
  opportunistically on the next successful read of that issue.

Concretely: `bind_confirm` and `record_pending_key` accept and persist an optional `jira_id`; a `get_jira_id(local_id)` accessor is added; and the absence probe, before concluding an issue is gone, retries the lookup by recorded `id` and — on a hit whose key differs — updates the binding's key (maintaining the `reverse` index) and treats the issue as PRESENT rather than absent.

**Rejected: re-keying the binding store on the numeric id.** It is the "cleaner" answer and it is what the original ticket proposed, but it changes shared Cloud-facing identity semantics, rewrites the reverse index and every `jira_key`-taking method, and requires a store migration — all to reach the same end state this achieves additively. If DC experience later shows the fallback firing routinely, re-keying becomes a justified follow-up with evidence behind it.

**Rejected: detecting a move by parsing the old key's GET response.** That is precisely the mechanism two research passes disagreed about. Building on it would make the fix depend on unverified behaviour.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — persist and expose `jira_id`; re-key on an
  id-resolved move.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — capture the numeric id
  on reads (it is already present in the unwrapped REST payload as `id`).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — the harness experiment recording what a stale key actually returns.

## Testing

* **the binding survives a move** — a fake client where the issue's key changes and the OLD key 404s,
  while the recorded numeric id still resolves: assert the binding is preserved, re-keyed to the new
  key, and NOT retired by the absence probe. This is the defect, so it is asserted end-to-end rather
  than by inspecting the entry.
* **the `reverse` index follows the re-key** — the old key no longer maps to the local id and the new
  one does. A stale reverse entry would re-detach on the next pass.
* **a pre-existing binding with no recorded id** behaves exactly as today (no fallback, no crash),
  so the change is safe on an unmigrated store.
* **the fallback does not fire when the key still resolves** — asserted by a client that fails the
  test if the id lookup is attempted, since a fallback firing on the happy path would double every
  absence probe's cost.
* **live** — record what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns on DC 8.17.1 after a real move,
  as evidence, since two research passes disagreed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a binding whose issue moved project SURVIVES: with the old key 404ing and the recorded numeric
      id resolving, the binding is preserved and re-keyed to the current key, asserted by a test that
      FAILS against the current code
- [ ] the absence probe does NOT retire an issue that is reachable by its recorded id — the specific
      silent detachment this ticket exists to stop
- [ ] the `reverse` index is updated in the same operation as the re-key, asserted, so the old key
      stops resolving to the local id
- [ ] bindings written BEFORE this change (no `jira_id`) continue to work unchanged, with no
      migration step, asserted by a test over a legacy-shaped entry
- [ ] the id fallback is NOT attempted while the key resolves normally, asserted by a client that
      fails if it is called — the happy path must not pay for the recovery path
- [ ] Cloud behaviour is unchanged: no existing `jira_key`-taking method changes signature or
      semantics, verified by reading the diff, since this store is shared
- [ ] [operator-attested] what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns for a moved issue on DC 8.17.1
      (status, and whether the body carries the new key) is RECORDED on this ticket as evidence — two
      research passes disagreed and the answer must stop being folklore. The fix does not depend on
      the answer; this criterion exists to settle it
baseline.summary: Bindings key on the Jira KEY, which changes when an issue moves project

The LLM completion verifier is budget-impractical for code-heavy, multi-criteria tickets.

## Context
Discovered dogfooding the close gate on this feature's own epic + workstreams. On a faster, decisive model (sonnet) a FOCUSED ticket (≈2 small AC) converges in ~12s, but a code-heavy workstream whose AC reference large files (e.g. WS-3: ~4 AC across `_cli/__init__.py` ~1000 lines, `mcp_server.py`, test files) does NOT converge even at recursion_limit=500 / ~560s. The agent reads many large files / searches across criteria; there is no cheap shortcut to verifying implementation-completeness of a code-heavy ticket. With the gate enabled, such tickets currently can't be closed without a very high REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or `--force-close`.

## Candidate directions
- A lightweight repo-map / orientation (tree-sitter/PageRank à la Aider) so the agent reads less.
- Stronger budget steering (hard tool-call cap) and/or summarized-file reads.
- The framework-wide AutoStrategy/ProviderStrategy migration (separate follow-up) for cheaper structured output.
- Per-ticket file-impact hints (`set_file_impact`) to focus the agent on the relevant files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A code-heavy multi-criteria workstream ticket verifies (PASS/FAIL) within a practical
      budget/latency on the default verifier model. MET: the ToolStrategy root-cause fix (ticket
      `c7c5`) moved WS-3 from a timeout at recursion_limit=500 (~560s) to a **78s PASS** via
      `output_strategy='extract'`. `sonnet` is the decisive default; `opus` over-explores.
- [x] A decision is recorded on how to make the gate practical for code-heavy tickets.
      REMEDIATED 2026-08-07 — the original wording offered three options (raise the default budget,
      add a repo-map, scope the gate to focused tickets) and the actual answer was NONE of them: the
      convergence failure was root-caused and fixed outright, so no budget was raised, no repo-map was
      built, and the gate's scope was not narrowed. The criterion is rewritten to state what was
      genuinely decided rather than force-closing past an option list that reality overtook.

## Follow-on work — owned elsewhere

Three OPTIONAL optimizations surfaced by the prior-art research are explicitly NOT part of this ticket and are owned by another session under a separate ticket:
* per-criterion fan-out (LangGraph Send + a deterministic reducer),
* per-criterion context PRE-SELECTION (Aider repo-map / FastContext line-ranges) so the agent does not
  hunt through large files,
* small bounded per-unit budgets.

None of them blocks anything: the practical-budget problem this ticket was filed for is solved.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier: efficiency for code-heavy tickets (budget limit)

baseline.description:
## Why
The coach's move catalog must offer the right remediation. Two dso lessons need moves: pre-existing issues should become follow-on tickets (pairs with rebar's discovered_from), and change-detector tests must be DELETED, not re-pinned to new source text.

## What
Add two Pass-4 coach moves to `MOVE_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` (and thus `.rebar/code_review_moves.json`-overridable): `file-follow-on-ticket` (subject = the pre-existing/ out-of-scope issue; template guidance to file a `discovered_from` follow-on ticket) and `delete-bad-test` (subject = the change-detector/tautological test; template guidance to DELETE it, not re-pin it to the new source text). Deterministic `{subject}` templates; the LLM only picks the move name + names the subject.

### applies_when gating — DATA-FLOW (resolves plan-review G6 block f6f98d71)
The `applies_when` vocabulary is the CLOSED set `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` (`review_kernel.validate_move_registry`), and a move is offered by Pass-4 ONLY when its `applies_when` overlaps `active_triggers`, where `active_triggers = {c for f in surfaced for c in f.get("criteria", [])}` (`workflow_ops.py` `code_review_coach_inputs` / `code_review_coach`, ~line 342). Those `criteria` values are the overlay ids the reviewers emit (OVERLAY_IDS). Therefore a NOVEL tag (e.g. `"pre-existing"` / `"change-detector"`) would NEVER enter `active_triggers`, so a move keyed on it would register but never fire (dead move). We DELIBERATELY DO NOT extend the vocabulary. Instead we key on EXISTING overlay ids already emitted as `criteria`:
- `delete-bad-test` → `applies_when: ["tests"]`. A change-detector/tautological/over-mocking test finding
  arrives under the `tests` overlay criterion, so the move is offered whenever a surviving `tests` finding
  exists. Its `name`/`template` make it the obvious pick for a change-detector finding (vs re-pinning), and
  it sits alongside the existing `add-regression-test` move so the LLM selects delete — not "improve the
  test" — for a change-detector subject.
- `file-follow-on-ticket` → `applies_when: ["always"]`. A pre-existing/out-of-scope finding can surface
  under ANY overlay criterion, so the move is always offered; the LLM picks it when the surviving finding
  is about a pre-existing issue (subject = that issue), and the template instructs filing a
  `discovered_from` ticket rather than fixing it in-scope.

No new `applies_when` vocabulary value is introduced; both moves key on values already in the closed set, so both pass `validate_move_registry` subject-validation and actually enter `active_triggers`.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` (MOVE_REGISTRY entries) + a unit test. No verdict-path change; the coach prompt (`code-review-coach.md`) already picks the single most useful applicable move, so no prompt change is required beyond the moves being offered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `file-follow-on-ticket` and `delete-bad-test` moves exist in `MOVE_REGISTRY` with deterministic
      `{subject}` templates and pass `validate_move_registry` (built-in, strict).
- [ ] Each move's `applies_when` uses ONLY existing `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` values (`delete-bad-test` →
      `["tests"]`, `file-follow-on-ticket` → `["always"]`), so the move actually enters `active_triggers`
      and is OFFERED by `code_review_coach_inputs` for the intended criteria (proven by a unit test using
      `review_kernel.applicable_moves`).
- [ ] For a surviving finding tagged `criteria: ["tests"]`, `delete-bad-test` is among the applicable moves
      (the change-detector remediation), distinct from the "improve/add test" moves; a unit test pins this.
baseline.summary: Coach moves: file-follow-on-ticket + delete-bad-test
