## Problem

`rebar fsck` reports 8 stray top-level directories in the tickets tracker (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker`), each flagged twice — once as `MISSING_CREATE` (no CREATE event found) and once inside the single `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH` finding:

    0efe-9207-2706-43a3  2021-2ef0-e36f-44fc  6f8a-45e5-d9ec-402c  a109-e758-71bb-4371
    afe5-db0b-e9c5-45d8  c827-81ee-a592-4d27  d052-ad3f-23c1-4511  fa38-670c-d8fc-4c22

Baseline: `fsck complete: 16 issues found` = 8 MISSING_CREATE + 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED
+ 1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH.

## Evidence (pre-removal triage)

All 8 are empty directories (`ls -A` returns nothing), none is committed (`git ls-tree HEAD <dir>` empty for all 8), `git status --porcelain` in the tracker is clean because git cannot track empty directories, and `rebar exists <id>` returns exit 1 for all 8. `lsof +D` on the tracker shows no process holding a file under any of the 8. Directory mtimes span 2026-08-10 11:05 to 2026-08-12 12:52 — all far outside the ~30-minute live-writer window (triage run 2026-08-12 17:59 PDT). `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` independently reports `unpushed ticket commits: 0` and exactly these 8 as `foreign top-level paths`, so `--clean` will not refuse and the break-glass `--force` is NOT needed. `rebar review-plan` itself logs each one as "debris of an interrupted write; safe to delete".

## Likely cause

`os.makedirs(ticket_dir)` succeeded and the process died before the first event was atomically renamed in — agents interrupted mid-write by host sleeps, session-limit kills, and shell-cap timeouts across the active fleet.

## How `--clean` actually behaves (correcting an earlier draft of this plan)

`rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` is ALL-OR-NOTHING over the foreign set: `src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py` iterates `for name in foreign:` and calls `shutil.rmtree(full)` on every entry that `fsck.foreign_store_path_list` returned, with no per-directory filter and no CLI surface for passing a subset. The guards below therefore do NOT select what the tool deletes — they are a precondition on running it at all. Consequently the guard set is applied as an equality check: immediately before the write, `--status`'s foreign list must be exactly the 8 triaged ids. If it lists any 9th path, or any triaged directory has become non-empty, the run is ABORTED and reported rather than narrowed — because there is no way to narrow it. This also bounds the check-then-act (TOCTOU) window to the gap between that `--status` and the `--clean`, seconds apart.

## Relationship to 043f-3336-d5de-45be (closed)

That bug made the plan-relation reducer TOLERATE event-less directories and explicitly rejected writer-side cleanup, because an automatic rmdir races a concurrent session's in-flight write ("tolerate, never tidy"). This ticket does not reintroduce automatic cleanup: it is a one-off operator-initiated sweep whose guards are precisely the evidence an automatic writer-side rmdir could never establish.

## Plan (minimal, deterministic — five guards, all-or-nothing)

Per directory: (1) empty; (2) uncommitted; (3) `rebar exists <id>` exits 1; (4) no open file handle under it; (5) mtime older than 30 minutes. Then the run-level gate: `--status` foreign list equals the 8 triaged ids exactly. All six conditions hold -> run `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` (backup ref before first write, refusal on unpushed ticket commits, durable audit). Any condition fails -> make NO writes and report back. No raw git in the tracker, no stash. `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` (benign, auto-resolved) and `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` (known by-design flag from change 1638) are out of scope and must not be touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: A per-directory triage verdict for all 8 directories is recorded as a comment on
      this ticket, each citing the five guards. Verified by `rebar show 7c6e-4b8a-59c5-46db`
      showing a comment naming all 8 ids with a verdict each.
- [x] AC2: Immediately before any write, `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` is re-run and
      its `foreign top-level paths` list is asserted byte-equal to the 8 triaged ids;
      on any mismatch the sweep is aborted with no writes and the mismatch recorded.
      Verified by the recorded `--status` output in a ticket comment.
- [x] AC3: Given AC2's equality assertion held, `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` is run
      and exits 0 having printed a backup ref, and afterwards
      `rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` prints 0.
      If AC2's assertion failed instead, this criterion is satisfied by recording the abort
      and making no writes.
- [x] AC4: No committed ticket data is modified. Verified by capturing
      `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` before and after and asserting the two are
      byte-identical, and by `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` staying empty.

## Testing

A store data operation, so verification is by command exit code and before/after diff rather than by unit test:

1. Before: `rebar fsck 2>&1 | tail -1` (record issue count);
   `git -C /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` (record sha).
2. Per-directory guards: `ls -A <dir>` empty; `git ls-tree HEAD <dir>` empty;
   `rebar exists <id>` exit 1; `lsof +D` naming no file under it; mtime > 30 min old.
3. Run-level gate: `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` foreign list == the 8 ids exactly.
4. Act: `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` — must exit 0 and print a backup ref.
5. After: `rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` must print 0;
   `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD` must equal the step-1 sha;
   `git -C .tickets-tracker status --porcelain` must be empty.
baseline.summary: Sweep interrupted-ticket-write debris: 8 uncommitted stray ticket dirs in the tracker

baseline.description:
## Why

The code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`code_review_result_v1`) persists only the SURFACED findings — the `blocking`, `advisory`, and `coaching` buckets — and omits the `dropped` and `indeterminate` findings that Pass-3 produced. It also does not persist the numeric `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` each finding was judged against. So "the complete Pass-1 finding list" is not recoverable for a code review, unlike plan review.

## Dependency

This story **depends on 4e19** (plan-review lossless v2), which lands first in the stack and makes the SHARED review kernel stamp the resolved boundary on every decided finding: `pass3_decide` returns `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` and `pass3_over_findings` merges them, so every code-review finding (via `code_review_decide`) already carries them by the time this story runs. 4e19 also adds those two fields (plus `evidence`/`scenarios`) to the plan-review `_slim`, so the two sidecars **converge** in shape — this story does not introduce a field plan-review lacks.

## What

Extend the code-review sidecar to `code_review_result_v2`, pooling the four buckets the code-review gate actually produces — `blocking`, `advisory` (surfaced), `dropped`, `indeterminate` — with each finding's full Pass-2 `verification` and Pass-3 determination (`decision`/`priority`/…), plus the resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` (stamped by the 4e19 kernel change). There is **no `overflow` bucket** in code review: unlike plan-review (which applies an advisory cap that spills to `overflow`), `code_review_decide` partitions only into `{blocking, surfaced, dropped, indeterminate}` and the code-review verdict schema has no `overflow` property.

## Scope

The `dropped`/`indeterminate` buckets are computed by `code_review_decide` but are **not** currently forwarded to the terminal verdict — `code_review_coach` assembles only `{verdict, blocking, advisory, coaching, coverage}`, and `apply_region_gated_floor` only appends its own novelty-floor drops post-hoc. So the wiring must be extended:

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — in the `verdict` step's `with:` block, pass
  `dropped: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.dropped }}` and
  `indeterminate: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.indeterminate }}` (alongside the existing `blocking`
  and `surfaced`).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — `code_review_coach` accepts `dropped`/
  `indeterminate` inputs and includes them in its returned verdict dict; update its
  `code_review_coach_input`/`_output` schemas to allow the two new (optional) arrays.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — bump `SCHEMA` to `code_review_result_v2`; in
  `build_payload`, add `dropped`/`indeterminate` (norm-id-stamped, like `blocking`/`advisory`), each
  finding retaining its `verification`/`decision`/`block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled`; KEEP the
  separate `blocking`/`advisory` lists (so the surfaced reader is unchanged) and the change metadata
  (`change_id`/`revision`/`change_fingerprint`) + `deps`. `_latest_payload_with_ts` and
  `latest_code_review_result` accept BOTH `code_review_result_v1` and `_v2` (replace the
  `== SCHEMA` guard with membership in `{v1, v2}`), so old records still read and the surfaced
  reader keeps returning the `blocking + advisory` union.

Code-review findings carry no `evidence`/`scenarios` (those are plan-review Pass-1 fields); this story does not persist them for code review.

## Enumerated consumers to update

- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py:210` asserts `payload["schema"] == "code_review_result_v1"`
  on a fresh emit; update it to `_v2` (the schema bumped).
- `docs/experiments/derive_code_review_threshold.py` is a jq/offline consumer that filters on
  `code_review_result_v1`; note that it should accept `_v2` too (or is left as historical — out of
  this story's code scope, flagged for the reader).

## Compatibility & rollback

`v1` code-review sidecars remain readable (new buckets absent → default to `[]`). The novelty-floor reader that consumes surfaced findings keeps returning the `blocking + advisory` union, so region-gating is unaffected. No backfill. Reverting bumps `SCHEMA` back to `v1` and stops writing the `dropped`/`indeterminate` buckets; already-written `v2` records stay readable because the reader still accepts both schemas (the reader change is independently safe to keep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_payload` produces a `code_review_result_v2` payload that pools `blocking`, `advisory`,
      `dropped`, and `indeterminate`, each finding retaining its `verification`, Pass-3 `decision`,
      and resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` plus a `norm_id`. Oracle: a unit test driving
      `build_payload` with a verdict containing all four buckets and asserting on the payload JSON.
- [ ] `code_review_coach` forwards `dropped`/`indeterminate` from the decide step into the terminal
      verdict dict. Oracle: a contract test calling the `code_review_coach` op with those inputs and
      asserting they appear in the returned verdict.
- [ ] `latest_code_review_result` reads both a `v1` and a `v2` code-review sidecar. Oracle: a unit
      test with one hand-written record of each schema.
- [ ] The novelty-floor surfaced-findings reader returns exactly the `blocking + advisory` union
      from a `v2` payload, unchanged vs an equivalent `v1` payload. Oracle: a unit test comparing the
      two.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: code-review sidecar -> lossless v2 (all buckets + thresholds)

# terraform-drift check permanently red: opcert_admin trust-policy phantom drift

## Context / proven root cause
The `terraform-drift` GitHub Actions check has failed on every run against `origin/main` since opcert.tf landed (commit f78940a43, 2026-07-15). The check runs `terraform plan` over `infra/terraform/` with NO variable inputs (.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml:61). `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin`'s assume_role_policy derives its principals from `var.opcert_admin_principal_arns` (opcert.tf:138), which defaults to `[]` (opcert.tf:29). The live role was applied with the operator-supplied account-root principal (`arn:aws:iam::896586841071:root`, per the documented deploy pattern opcert.tf:26 / opcert-plan-assertions.sh:22). So every plan renders an EMPTY principal and diffs it against live's account-root principal:

    # aws_iam_role.opcert_admin will be updated in-place
      ~ Principal = { ~ AWS = "arn:aws:iam::896586841071:root" -> [] }
    Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.   -> exit 2 -> check FAILS

This is an un-reconcilable phantom (applying the committed default would remove the principal), so it permanently reds the daily drift sweep and masks any real future drift.

## Defect
Asymmetry inside opcert.tf: the sibling operator-seeded SSM KEY param carries `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` (opcert.tf:57-59) precisely so plan/apply never diff on an operator-owned value — but the equally operator-supplied trust principal was not given the same guard.

## Plan (fix direction: ignore_changes — user-approved)
Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy] }` to `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin`. Terraform still creates the role; the operator owns the trust list out-of-band (honors the documented "operator supplies principals at deploy" intent and mirrors the key-param precedent). This suppresses the phantom diff at PLAN time — no terraform apply required.

## Acceptance criteria (measurable)
1. `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin` in infra/terraform/opcert.tf declares
   `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy] }`.
2. A hermetic source-contract test in tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py asserts (1)
   and was seen RED before the fix, GREEN after (with a mutation check returning it to RED).
3. `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass on the edited module.
4. No existing opcert infra test is weakened; full unit suite for the file passes.

## Verify command
    cd /Users/joeoakhart/fix-opcert-drift-ignore-changes
    ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py -q
    cd infra/terraform && terraform fmt -check && terraform validate
baseline.summary: terraform-drift check permanently red: opcert_admin trust-policy phantom drift

# The global rebar build is 4 days stale, and it SILENTLY disables the LLM tier of plan review

## Context / Problem
This machine's global `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` is supposed to track `origin/main` HOURLY via a rollback-guarded LaunchAgent (documented in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`). IT HAS NOT RUN SINCE 2026-07-27 17:10 — measured from the mtime of `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar/lib/python3.14/site-packages/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py`, and corroborated by the venv directory's own mtime. Today is 2026-07-31, so the global build is ~4 days behind main.

**THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT DEGRADATION OF THE REVIEW GATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING.** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries `activate` as a DICT (scoped per review type), which main's overlay parser accepts — `git show origin/main:src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py | grep "must be a list of ids"` returns NOTHING. The stale global build predates that: its overlay.py DOES contain that check and raises `CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. Support landed in `f3dbe32b0b` (2026-07-27, "3ba4: Scope project criteria by review type") and `7f4c650114` (2026-07-28).

MEASURED consequence of running `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` with the global build in this repo:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay .../.rebar/criteria_routing.json:
                  'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command EXITS 2 and emits a sidecar. It does not present as a broken install; it presents as a plan that could not be reviewed. The DET tier still runs and reports pass/fail per criterion, so the output looks substantive. An operator or agent reading that verdict would reasonably conclude the TICKET is the problem. **No LLM review happened at all.**

The worktree build parses the same file fine — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 effective criteria — so this is purely the stale global install, not a repo defect.

## Why this matters beyond one command
AGENTS.md already warns to run the repo checkout's build rather than a stale global install, and gives the reason as "silently ignores newer config keys". This incident shows the consequence is worse than ignoring a key: an unrelated-looking INDETERMINATE on the claim gate. Any agent that trusts `which rebar` gets it. The MCP server is affected the same way and, per the local docs, will not hot-reload.

## Approach
Two separable pieces:
 1. DIAGNOSE why the LaunchAgent stopped. Check `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
    for its last exit status, and the agent's own log, before forcing a sync. A rollback-guarded updater
    that silently gave up 4 days ago has its own failure to explain — forcing a sync hides the evidence.
    Force it only after capturing that state:
    `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`.
 2. MAKE THE STALENESS LOUD rather than silent. A gate run whose LLM tier dies on a CONFIG-PARSE error
    from the installed build is not the same as an LLM outage, and collapsing both into
    `llm_unavailable` + INDETERMINATE is what made this cost time. A `CriteriaError` while loading the
    overlay is a CONFIGURATION fault: it should surface distinctly (its own verdict reason or a loud
    warning naming the installed build's version), so the reader is pointed at the install rather than
    at the plan.

## Scope
- The LaunchAgent / updater: diagnosis first, then a sync.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — distinguish a config-parse failure from an LLM outage in the verdict's
  `llm_error` / reason surfacing.
- Possibly a startup or gate-time warning when the running build's commit is far behind the repo's.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion below is verifiable IN-SESSION by a probe, experiment, or test — no criterion defers to a future change.

ALL OF THEM ARE TAGGED [operator-attested], and that is a statement of fact rather than a way around the gate: the completion verifier reads REPOSITORY FILES ONLY, while every probe here observes machine-local operational state — a launchd exit code, a pipx venv's recorded backend, `command -v uv` under a given PATH, the contents of ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log. NO repository file can record any of it, because THE FIX ITSELF TOUCHES NO REPOSITORY FILE (it is one line of a script under ~/.local/bin plus recreating a venv). The observed outputs are pasted verbatim in the evidence comment on this ticket so the attestation is checkable rather than merely asserted. The code hardening that was previously bundled here (reporting an overlay `CriteriaError` distinctly from an LLM outage, and naming the installed build as the suspect) has been SPLIT OUT to its own ticket, because it is a repo change with its own review and must not hold this environment repair open.

- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE A, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: `~/.local/bin/uv` (0.7.18) shadowed `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`
      (0.12.0) on the updater's PATH. Probe: under the script's ORIGINAL PATH order,
      `command -v uv` resolves the 0.7.18 binary; under the fixed order it resolves 0.12.0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE B, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: the pipx venv was pinned to the pip backend, which pipx
      will not override. Probe: `pipx_metadata.json` recorded `backend = pip` before and records
      `backend = uv` after; and `pipx install --force --backend uv` against the OLD venv was
      demonstrably IGNORED (same `resolution-too-deep`, metadata unchanged).
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE UPDATER COMPLETES: a run exits 0 and `last-good.sha` advances off the Jul-17 commit
      (`4dd9172b9`) to the current tip of `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IT WORKS UNDER LAUNCHD, NOT JUST BY HAND: `launchctl kickstart -k` the agent and then
      `launchctl print` reports `last exit code = 0`. This is the criterion that matters — every
      by-hand run inherits the operator's rich shell environment, whereas launchd supplies a minimal
      one, so a by-hand pass does not prove the scheduled job works.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE INSTALL PATH ITSELF IS EXERCISED UNDER LAUNCHD, not just the no-op branch: with
      `last-good.sha` temporarily rewound, a launchd-triggered run performs a real install and
      advances it again (restore the true sha afterwards). Without this, a green kickstart only
      proves the `no change` early-exit.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IDEMPOTENCE: an immediately following run is a no-op — it logs `no change (already on <sha>)`
      and exits 0 rather than reinstalling.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE MUTATION BITES: restoring the original PATH order reproduces the exact
      `pipx needs uv>=0.9.17` failure, proving the one-line fix is load-bearing and not incidental.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS GONE: the GLOBAL build parses the dict-shaped `activate` in
      `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns the full criteria
      set where it previously raised `CriteriaError`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE GATE ACTUALLY RUNS ON THE GLOBAL BUILD: a real `rebar review-plan` invoked with the GLOBAL
      build reaches the LLM tier (`llm_ran: true`), not merely a successful criteria parse. This is
      the end-to-end form of the reported failure, whose signature was `llm_ran: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE SMOKE-TEST/ROLLBACK GUARD IS INTACT: the script's post-install smoke test still gates
      `last-good.sha`, evidenced by the smoke commands exiting 0 against the freshly installed build.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE KNOWLEDGE IS RECORDED where the next person will look: the local runbook documents that
      PATH order is load-bearing, that `uv` is a hard requirement (so `--backend pip` is NOT a valid
      workaround for this package), that an existing venv pins its backend, and that `update.log` —
      not the 0-byte launchd logs — is the diagnostic file.
baseline.summary: Global rebar build 4 days stale: silently disables the LLM tier of plan review

# P2.1 — Hybrid Logical Clock for event ordering (skew-immune replay)

**Correctness backbone.** Closes the one architectural gap a distributed tracker
should not ship without; P2.3 rides its total order.

## Context (problem + research)

rebar orders replay by the `${timestamp_ns}` filename prefix; invariant I8 admits
EDIT/COMMENT interleaving is "best-effort" under clock skew (only STATUS forks are
skew-independent, UUID-keyed at `reducer/_processors.py:78-120`). Two agents on
skewed clocks editing the same field resolve by last *wall-clock* writer -> silent
clobber. **git-bug solves exactly this with a persisted Lamport clock**
(`util/lamport/*`, `clocks/<name>`): a single `uint64`, advanced monotonically,
**re-seeded by witnessing max over history**; the local file is a disposable
cache, the authoritative value rides in git. Replay orders by logical time then a
content-id tiebreak. Radicle uses the same family (causal DAG + actor-id tiebreak).

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP1: `time_ns()` is 19 digits until ~year 2286; equal-width ints sort identically
  as strings and ints; string sort only breaks across DIFFERING widths -> stay 19-digit.
- EXP4: 2400 concurrent flock'd `next_tick()` ticks — all unique/monotonic/19-digit.
- EXP4b: with **no cache file**, `next_tick_for_ticket()` still issues a tick >
  `max(prefix)`, 19-digit -> the cache is reconstructable (git-bug's model).
- EXP-jq: the prefix is >2^53; jq rounds it -> **no jq/arithmetic may ever touch it**
  (reinforces P1.0's one-Python-serializer rule).
- EXP-R2 (real code): `event_sort_key` ts segment is `str` today; int-order ==
  string-order on real filenames; malformed names take the fallback -> change is safe.

## What / Implementation detail

1. New `rebar._store.hlc.next_tick()` = single monotonic integer
   `max(hlc.state, max(prefix of TARGET TICKET's events after sync), time_ns()) + 1`,
   RMW under a **local** `.rebar/hlc.lock` (held only inside the call -> no ordering
   hazard with the write lock). `.rebar/hlc.state` is a **disposable cache**
   (gitignored, I3/I7); correctness is re-derived from the durable log, so a
   missing/stale/raced cache is still correct.
2. Thread it through the four live timestamp seams: `_commands/_seam.py:153`,
   `ticket_txn.py` (STATUS/claim), reconciler `inbound_translate`, and
   `ticket-compact.sh` (via `python3 -m rebar._store.hlc next`). Add an injectable
   `REBAR_HLC_NOW` for the skewed-clock test.
3. Change `reducer/_sort.py:event_sort_key` (line 21) to `int(ts_segment)` (malformed
   fallback), keeping the `(ts, type_order, name)` tuple + LINK<UNLINK tiebreak;
   align the other prefix sorts (`graph/_links.py:53`, `_commands/unlink.py:47`,
   bare `sorted()` STATUS scans at `ticket_txn.py:187/318`). Keep the UUID tiebreak
   (git-bug: logical-time then content-id).
4. Bump `reducer/_version.py:SCHEMA_VERSION` -> 2. Single-integer encoding keeps
   width at 19 digits, so older clones still string-compare correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar._store.hlc.next_tick()` (single-int, local-lock RMW, witness max(prefix), injectable clock)
- [ ] threaded through all four live timestamp seams (incl. bash via `python3 -m`)
- [ ] `event_sort_key` + the 3 other prefix sorts use integer comparison; UUID tiebreak kept
- [ ] SCHEMA_VERSION -> 2; event-schema.md updated
- [ ] NEW skewed-clock EDIT/COMMENT convergence regression (merged red-first), width-comparator + forward-compat tests
- [ ] staged behind `REBAR_HLC` with kill-switch for one release

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P2.1).
- [ ] A NEW skewed-clock regression (two clones, injected skew) shows EDIT/COMMENT
- [ ] Width-comparator test: legacy 19-digit and new names sort into one global order.
- [ ] v1-reducer replay of a v2 store still yields a valid state (forward-compat).
baseline.summary: P2.1 — Hybrid Logical Clock for event ordering (skew-immune replay)

## Context
The OS/Python-invariant complexity-baseline lock currently runs inside every test-matrix cell in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: Ubuntu costs 52/54/55s and macOS costs 45s. The same commit has already been checked out in the single Ubuntu lint job. Running the policy there once preserves the gate while eliminating four duplicate invocations and their fetch/merge-base work, estimated at about 154 net runner-seconds per Verified run. CPython and Django use dedicated single lint jobs; Rust and Kubernetes use dedicated tidy/verify surfaces. No rejection was found; `humble-cinnamoned-mussel` fixed lock correctness but did not require matrix duplication.

## Plan
- Strengthen workflow policy tests to require exactly one complexity-lock invocation, in the single lint job, and to prohibit it in the OS/Python test matrix.
- Move the existing unchanged script invocation and definition-vs-tree guard from `jobs.test` to `jobs.lint`.
- Run held-out RED→GREEN, a duplicate-invocation mutation, workflow/config tests, repository gates, and compare CI job timing after Gerrit upload. Back-out is a Gerrit revert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` executes exactly once for a Verified change.
- [ ] The invocation is a blocking step in the single lint job and is absent from the test matrix.
- [ ] The existing fail-closed and definition-vs-tree-skew behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] A workflow unit oracle fails on the current four-matrix-invocation placement and on any future duplicate placement.
- [ ] Reintroducing the matrix invocation returns the held-out oracle to RED.

baseline.description:
## Context

The plan-review gate's re-review of an *edited* plan does not converge: each remediation
round can surface new issues in previously-clean criteria, expanding scope every run and
creating a non-terminating loop that drives cost, wall-clock, and agent non-compliance.
This is distinct from run-over-run reproducibility on fixed input (the LLM-as-judge
self-consistency problem); the plan legitimately changed, so feedback *should* differ. The
problem we solve: a remediation re-review should confirm the surfaced issues were resolved
**without** introducing different, lower-stakes issues that restart the loop.

Prior conversation rejected three approaches: per-diff-region scoping (new section-diffing
machinery), skip-clean-criteria reuse (unsound — reuses absence-of-finding, freezes
high-stakes defects an edit introduces), and the whole-verdict probe (too coarse). This
epic captures the chosen approach. Relates to the plan-review epic `5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa`.
It is decomposed into 6 child tasks (see "Decomposition" below).

## Terminology (canonical)

- **impact** — the verifier's coarse severity-attribute score in [0,1] (`decide.impact`).
- **validity** — the graded fraction of the Pass-2 binary sub-answers in [0,1].
- **priority** — `validity × impact` (the existing Pass-3 score; the drop axis).
- **novelty score** — a new [0,1] score derived deterministically from a new Pass-2
  novelty sub-answer set (see below); high = "not present in the prior review".
- **carryover finding** — a current finding matching a prior-review finding (low novelty).

## What (the chosen design)

A **rising-floor remediation re-review**: run the FULL criteria set every time (no skipped
criteria, no Pass-1 anchoring → full recall), and on a remediation re-review apply a
deterministic Pass-3 floor that drops only **novel, low-priority** findings.

- **Full Pass-1, unanchored.** Every applicable criterion runs; the finder never sees prior
  findings (avoids the sycophancy/anchoring the research documents). High-priority defects
  an edit introduces are still found — nothing is frozen.
- **Novelty as a narrow-question score, in a SEPARATE Pass-2 sub-call.** Novelty is scored
  by a DISTINCT structured sub-call that ALONE receives the prior findings and answers a
  small novelty sub-answer set ("does this finding correspond to a prior finding?"). The
  existing verification sub-call (severity attributes + the binary/validity sub-answers)
  receives **NO** prior findings, so the `verify.py` independence invariant
  (VERIFIER_RULES[0]) is enforced *structurally*, not by prompt assertion — mirroring the
  Pass-1 isolation. Pass-3 maps the novelty sub-answers to a deterministic novelty score,
  exactly as it maps the binary sub-answers to validity. The sub-answers are factual **matches-prior** questions (same defect / same location / same fix as a specific prior finding?) on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0` map; **`novelty = 1 − mean(matches-prior sub-answers)`** (high novelty = no prior match). Fail-safe: a failed/malformed novelty sub-call defaults novelty to 0.0 (carryover → never dropped). Full set + arithmetic on task 150b. The sub-answers are factual
  **matches-prior** questions (does this restate the same defect / cite the same location /
  suggest the same fix as a specific prior finding?) on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0`
  map; **`novelty = 1 − mean(matches-prior sub-answers)`** (high novelty = no prior match).
  Fail-safe: a failed/malformed novelty sub-call defaults novelty to 0.0 (carryover → never
  dropped). Full set + arithmetic live on task 150b.
- **Deterministic rising floor (Pass-3).** A finding is dropped iff novelty ≥ `T_novel` AND
  `priority < floor`. Carryover findings (low novelty) use the normal threshold and must
  still be resolved. A novel high-priority finding (high impact × high validity) is
  preserved (and may block). The whole policy is deterministic — no LLM holistic severity.
- **Freshness window = remediation-mode gate.** The floor applies only when: config enabled,
  plan changed, code unchanged since baseline, registry unchanged, a prior sidecar (with
  finding text) is available, and the last review (full OR partial) is within the window
  (default 60 min). **Each review resets the window**, so the loop persists across a series
  of edits while the agent is actively iterating; it lapses to a normal full (un-floored)
  review only after the agent goes idle past the window. Code-changed / both-drifted → full
  review (`drift_refresh` untouched — out of scope). **Back-out:** setting the config key off
  restores byte-identical full-review behavior.

## Narrowed-verdict / sidecar schema

- The verdict's `coverage` records `narrowed: true`, `floored_criteria`, and the floored
  finding ids when the rising floor was applied (absent/false on a normal review).
- Dropped novel findings are written to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (not the surfaced
  verdict), joinable by `norm_id`, so suppression is always observable.

## Defaults & calibration (falsifiable)

- Starting defaults (tunable): `T_novel = 0.7`; `priority floor = the p40 impact percentile
  of the 245-event corpus × validity` (≈ the "below major" band). Both are *derived*, not
  guessed: `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` prints the percentile inputs.
- The novelty scorer must clear an **evidence gate** BEFORE the Pass-3 drop rule is activated.
  The bar is concrete and uses the framework's existing idiom (NOT an invented AUC/F1): a
  `discriminates_novelty` deterministic scorer (per-case, **0.5 midpoint** — `kind: novel`
  scores novelty ≥ 0.5, `kind: carryover` < 0.5, mirroring `discriminates_true_from_false` /
  `discriminates_impact_levels`) gated at the spec level by **`gate: at_least(2)` over
  `epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8`** on ≥ 3 labeled novel/carryover pairs (task 150b).
- **Three distinct numbers (do not conflate):** (a) the **runtime drop threshold
  `T_novel = 0.7`** — Pass-3 drops a finding only if novelty ≥ 0.7 (and priority < floor),
  config-overridable; (b) the **eval discrimination floor 0.5** — the per-case midpoint the
  `discriminates_novelty` scorer separates novel from carryover at; (c) the **eval bar** —
  the spec gate `at_least(2)/epochs:3` + `coverage_threshold:0.8` the scorer must clear before
  the drop rule activates. 0.7 is "how novel to be droppable"; 0.5/the gate is "did the scorer
  prove it can tell novel from carryover at all".

## Within-session suppression (deliberate, honest bound)

Because the window resets on each review, a novel low-priority finding can be re-floored
every round while the agent keeps iterating — within-session suppression is **intentionally
unbounded** (the chosen persistence behavior). It is bounded only by: the idle-lapse window,
carryover findings still being enforced at the normal bar, and every dropped finding being
recorded in the sidecar. Optional future safety valve: a `max_consecutive_narrowed_rounds`
cap that forces a full un-floored review. (No unsound *coverage* accumulates — Pass-1 always
runs the full criteria set; only the surfacing of novel low-priority findings is suppressed.)

## Empirical grounding (established)

- 245 `REVIEW_RESULT` events / 2,571 findings: the verifier's impact axis already
  discriminates (15% critical, 40% none, mean impact 0.43; attributes spread sensibly) — so
  impact discrimination is not a blocker; the floor has real spread to act on.
- The impact prompt nonetheless gives the severity attributes zero anchoring (vs rich
  guidance for validity) → tightening it is a robustness item, not a blocker.

## Already landed (observability foundation)

- `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` — repeatable corpus distribution report.
- `discriminates_impact_levels` eval scorer + `high_impact`/`low_impact` dataset pairs on
  `plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml`.

## Decomposition (6 child tasks)

1. Persist finding text in the sidecar + latest-sidecar reader (foundation).
2. Pass-2 novelty sub-answers in a SEPARATE sub-call + a `discriminates_novelty` eval gate.
3. Pass-3 novelty score + rising-floor drop rule (depends on 2; gated by the eval bar).
4. Remediation-mode gate: freshness window + preconditions + wiring (depends on 1).
5. Tighten the verifier impact prompt (robustness; verified by the impact eval).
6. Docs + ADR + offline convergence tests (depends on 3, 4).

## Scope

- IN: full-run + deterministic rising floor; separate-sub-call novelty scoring + its eval
  gate; freshness-window remediation-mode gating; sidecar finding-text persistence;
  impact-prompt tightening; config keys; docs + ADR.
- OUT: the code-drift `drift_refresh` path (unchanged); per-diff-region scoping;
  skip-clean-criteria reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Sidecar `_slim` persists `finding`, `suggested_fix`, `checklist_item` (sidecar event
      only; surfaced verdict shape byte-unchanged); a latest-sidecar reader exists; the
      `RETAIN_PER_TICKET` retention bound is respected.
- [ ] Pass-2 scores novelty in a SEPARATE structured sub-call that alone receives prior
      findings; the severity/validity sub-call receives none (independence enforced
      structurally). Pass-1 receives no prior findings.
- [ ] A `discriminates_novelty` eval scorer (per-case, 0.5 midpoint) + ≥ 3 labeled
      carryover/novel pairs land on a DEDICATED `plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml` (keyed to the
      `plan-review-novelty` prompt — NOT the verifier spec, where the scorer would grade the
      wrong artifact; this dedicated-spec correction was mandated by child 150b's plan review);
      its bar is
      `gate: at_least(2)`/`epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8` (NOT an AUC literal),
      distinct from the runtime `T_novel=0.7`; the scorer clears that bar before the Pass-3
      drop rule is activated (the evidence gate).
- [ ] Pass-3: deterministic novelty score; drop iff novelty ≥ `T_novel` AND priority < floor;
      carryover → normal threshold; novel high-priority → preserved; dropped → sidecar.
- [ ] Defaults committed: `T_novel = 0.7` and the priority floor at the stated corpus
      percentile (config-overridable); the distribution script prints the inputs.
- [ ] Remediation-mode gate: config key (**default-OFF** for v1, expand-contract rollout) +
      window minutes (default 60, measured from the last review of any kind and reset each
      review); code-unchanged precondition via `verified_at_sha` equality (prior manifest vs
      current run); both-drifted → full review; key off/absent restores byte-identical full review.
- [ ] Coverage on a narrowed verdict sets `narrowed: true` + `floored_criteria` + floored
      finding ids; dropped novel findings are written to the sidecar.
- [ ] Impact-prompt tightening is verified by the `discriminates_impact_levels` eval scoring
      at or above its threshold on the existing high/low pairs (not an effort claim).
- [ ] Offline FakeRunner tests: convergence on a remediation edit; each precondition fallback
      to a byte-identical full review; novel high-priority preserved; carryover enforced.
- [ ] Docs: a `docs/plan-review-gate.md` section AND an ADR under `docs/adr/` recording the
      chosen design, the three rejected alternatives, and the invariants (Pass-1 unanchored;
      novelty in a separate Pass-2 sub-call; drop decision deterministic in Pass-3).
- [ ] A remediation re-review (pure plan edit, code unchanged, within window) runs the full
- [ ] Severity/validity independence is enforced structurally (novelty in a separate Pass-2
- [ ] Any precondition failing → byte-identical full review; `drift_refresh` behavior unchanged.

## Out of scope / explicitly deferred

- Any change to the code-drift `drift_refresh` path.
- A `max_consecutive_narrowed_rounds` cap on within-session suppression (optional future
  safety valve; the chosen design accepts unbounded within-session suppression while the
  agent is actively iterating).
baseline.summary: Convergent plan-edit re-review: full-run + deterministic rising floor

baseline.description:
## Finding (audit of epic 3405-c0b7)
**Site:** `render_workflow` MCP read tool (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:557`) → `rebar.llm.workflow.render.render_workflow` → `runs.load_workflow_doc`. **Surfacing:** `mcp_server.build_server` calls `install_error_guard(mcp)` (mcp_server.py:692) BEFORE registering the read tools (704). So when `render_workflow` is called on a missing / malformed / too-new workflow file, the raised `WorkflowParseError` / `WorkflowValidationError` / `WorkflowVersionError` (all `WorkflowError` → `LLMError` subclasses) propagates into the guard `_envelope_error` (`_mcp_errors.py:77`), which calls `error_code_for(exc)`. Branch 6 of `error_code_for` (`src/rebar/_errors.py:130`) maps every `LLMError` to `llm_unavailable`.

**Exception type:** WorkflowParseError / WorkflowValidationError / WorkflowVersionError. **Wrong code:** `llm_unavailable` ("the AI provider is down"). **Correct/desired:** a workflow-file fault (missing / malformed / unsupported-version) — NOT a provider outage. There is no existing vocabulary code that fits precisely (`invalid_input` does not exist in this tree; `command_failed` would be honest-but-lossy).

**Observable vs latent:** OBSERVABLE — this is the live MCP manifestation of the SAME blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch that 551b (editor missing-bundle, logged CLI-only/latent) and 73d8 (ExpressionError, execute-time run-state) describe. It shows the branch is not purely latent: a read-only, always-registered MCP tool emits the misleading code today.

**Proposed fix (needs decision):** needs-new-vocabulary OR reuse. Minimal de-risk with existing vocab: route the `WorkflowError` family off `llm_unavailable` (e.g. to `command_failed`) so a bad workflow file stops claiming an outage. Richer fix: add a `workflow_invalid` / `workflow_not_found` code. Because 73d8/551b already hold the "which code for a workflow fault" design decision open (dbca AC3 deliberately kept execute-time WorkflowError on the LLM base to protect genuine outages), this is **escalate** — but the render_workflow path is LOAD-time, not execute-time, which strengthens the case that at least parse/validation faults should not be `llm_unavailable`.

**caused_by / class:** the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` branch (origin 8a31); relates to 551b, 73d8.
baseline.summary: render_workflow MCP tool surfaces WorkflowError family as llm_unavailable (observable manifestation of the blanket branch)

baseline.description:
Move the GET-rotation stamp out of `bindings.json` so the file stops changing on passes with no real change. After A1 this is what collapses the **version count** (20 of 40 sampled revisions become byte-identical), taking the combined saving to **12.8x**. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`set_last_get` (`binding_store.py:459-464`) stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit` (default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly **20 entries change per pass**. So with A1 alone the file still changes every pass and the version count stays ~180/day; only the delta shrinks. Losing rotation state is harmless — it just resets ordering, and the existing wrappers at `outbound_differ.py:167-172` are already fail-open.

## Approach — compatibility first
Write the new file, read `max(new, legacy)`, and **keep writing the legacy field**. Deletion is a separate ticket (A2-2).

`max()`, not new-then-old: under mixed versions an old binary advances the in-line field but cannot write the new file, so a first-wins read would take the **stale** value; since rotation sorts on it (`outbound_differ.py:607`), recently-probed keys would sort first and the rest would starve. Values are fixed-width zero-padded (`2026-07-29T21-46-44`), so lexicographic `max()` is chronological, and `_last_get_pass` returns `""` on absence — the lexicographic minimum — so after A2-2 `max(new, "")` degenerates cleanly to `new`.

**Migrate in memory on load; persist only inside `save()` / the `if persist:` block** (`reconcile.py:547-549`). Adding a file IS a write, and `__main__.py:106` `_run_reconcile_check` ("read-only") reaches `load_binding_store` at `:152`. Not an ensure unit: `run_ensures` holds the store filesystem lock (`ensures.py:155`), disjoint from `refs/reconciler/lock`, and `BindingStore.save()` takes no lock and is a whole-file `os.replace` — an ensure unit would introduce a clobber race that does not exist today.

**Module-size constraint:** `outbound_differ.py` is at **exactly 800 LOC**, the locked cap. This change must be **net-negative** there — move `_last_get_pass` (`:155-163`) and `_set_last_get` (`:166-172`) into the new rotation module; the two call sites (`:607`, `:704`) are one-for-one substitutions.

**Staging:** add `get_rotation.json` to `reconcile_helpers.py:206`'s `_rel_files` AND the basename check at `:227-230`, or it is never committed **locally** (GHA's `git add -A` would mask the omission). `.gitattributes` is a glob (`.bridge_state/* merge=ours`) so the new file is covered. Update `push.py:76`'s docstring, which names the regenerable files explicitly.

## Rollback
Reverting is safe: readers fall back to the in-line field, which this change never stops writing, so rotation order survives and the orphaned file is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The byte-identical/no-commit assertion from A1 **still holds when <=20 absent-key GETs occur in
      a pass**. Tier: **integration** in a real temporary git repo.
- [ ] `get_rotation.json` is **staged and committed locally** (asserted in a real temporary git repo,
      since GHA's `git add -A` would mask a staging omission). Tier: **integration**.
- [ ] Rotation order after an **interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence** matches the
      all-new sequence. Tier: **integration**. This is the RED case for the `max()` rule — a
      first-wins read fails it.
- [ ] A legacy store with in-line stamps only yields identical rotation order. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty). Tier: **CLI subprocess** + worktree assertion.
- [ ] `wc -l src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` is **<=800**. Verify: the
      module-size gate in `_build-and-test.yml` passes.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, new rotation module under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, `outbound_differ.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `_store/push.py` (docstring), tests

Scope: M. Depends on A1.
baseline.summary: A2-1: move last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping into .bridge_state/get_rotation.json (write-new, read max(new, legacy))

baseline.description:
## Why
LangChain/LangGraph is heavy (~80-110 deps) and its sole original justification (native Langfuse tracing) is obsolete. Pydantic AI is provider-agnostic (the cross-provider hard requirement) at ~half the deps. Validated by docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/runtime_pydanticai_poc.py.

## What
Implement a PydanticAIRunner behind the existing Runner protocol: single-turn LLM calls AND tool-using agents with filesystem + MCP (stdio/http) + custom rebar-operation tools; no per-provider code (provider chosen by config/model string). Keep FakeRunner. Parallel-run-and-diff against LangGraphRunner on the corpuses before any cutover.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py (PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam)
- pyproject.toml [agents] (add pydantic-ai-slim extras)
Out: dropping LangGraph (separate story); the structured-output stack (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PydanticAIRunner implements run/preflight behind the Runner seam; FakeRunner unaffected.
- [ ] Tools wired: filesystem, MCP (stdio + http), and custom rebar-op tools.
- [ ] No per-provider code; provider selected via config/model string (Anthropic primary).
- [ ] Parallel-run-and-diff vs LangGraphRunner meets the DEFINED PARITY BAR on the corpuses before any cutover. Parity = NON-INFERIORITY, not byte-identity (outputs are LLM-driven, so exact equality is incoherent). On the standing eval corpus (DSO + snap + rebar tickets), same model + decoding params, N>=3 repeats: (a) structured-output validity v2 >= v1 (target >=99% valid parses, no regression); (b) per-criterion verdict agreement >= 95% AND zero decision-level flips (block/advisory/dropped) on the gold set; (c) recall and false-accept each within +/-2pp of v1 (non-inferiority margin, paired test); (d) runtime error/timeout rate v2 <= v1; (e) cost/latency recorded (informational, non-gating). The LangGraph drop (d6d1) is blocked until this bar is met.
baseline.summary: Provider-agnostic Pydantic AI runtime behind the Runner seam

Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`, `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py --check`.

baseline.description:
## Why
The plan-v2 impact model floors four failure-mode axes at 0.85 (above every blocking threshold) whenever the axis is non-none at ANY grade - the floor is grade-blind. Calibration 3 (task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly; evidence comment on this story, 2026-07-15) measured the consequence on the plan-v2 segment: 35.5% of ALL blocking findings (807/2271) are floor-driven (would not block without the override), ac_unverifiable alone is 48.9% of the floor-driven set, 52/100 of a classified sample fired at grade=low, and the oracle-kind classification split 56% underspecified_oracle / 37% broken-oracle-shaped / 7% missing_oracle. The dominant floor-driven class is "a check exists, the plan just doesn't spell out the exact command/file/value" - a refinement demand that today auto-blocks with the same force as a genuinely untestable criterion. This story splits the axis so severity follows the actual defect.

## What
Replace the binary-ish ac_unverifiable severity grading with a THREE-value oracle-kind grade in the plan-review verification model, assigned explicitly by the pass-2 verifier (the calibration-3 evidence motivates three, not two - a broken oracle is not a refinement):
- missing_oracle: no verification method exists or could exist as the criterion is phrased (7% of sample) - KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor.
- broken_oracle: a stated proving command/symbol/count is factually wrong - nonexistent path, wrong CLI, contradictory assertion - so the stated verification CANNOT pass (37% of sample) - KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor (the check is protective; these are real plan defects).
- underspecified_oracle: a check exists or is clearly constructible; the finding demands the exact command/file/expected value (56% of sample) - scores BELOW the lowest blocking threshold in force after calibration 3 (0.60), i.e. maps to an impact contribution <= 0.55, so it surfaces and is coached but never auto-blocks.
BOTH verifier prompts define the three grades with one worked example each drawn from the calibration-3 classified sample (the gate YAML routes to TWO prompt files: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md AND plan_review_verifier_agentic.md - both change in lockstep). SCORING MECHANICS (exact decide.py change): impact_plan currently scores all seven axes through the shared ordinal map _SEV01 ({none,low,medium,high}) in TWO generic loops - the contribs list comprehension over _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES and the has_override any() over _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES. ac_unverifiable is REMOVED from both generic loops and special-cased: (1) contribs = [_SEV01.get(attrs.get(a), 0.0) for a in _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES if a != "ac_unverifiable"] + [ORACLE_GRADE01.get(attrs.get("ac_unverifiable"), 0.0)]; (2) has_override = any(_SEV01.get(attrs.get(a), 0.0) > 0.0 for a in _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES if a != "ac_unverifiable") or attrs.get("ac_unverifiable") in ("broken_oracle", "missing_oracle"). ORACLE_GRADE01 = {"none": 0.0, "underspecified_oracle": UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB, "broken_oracle": 1.0, "missing_oracle": 1.0} with UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB = 0.55 defined as a named module constant whose comment states its invariant (strictly below the lowest blocking threshold in criteria_routing.json), and a unit test asserts UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB < min(block_threshold over blocking-posture criteria) so a future threshold recalibration below 0.55 fails loudly instead of silently re-enabling blocks. An unknown/legacy grade string maps to 0.0 via .get() default in plan-v3 scoring - legacy records are never scored with plan-v3 code anyway (segmentation, below). The other six axes keep _SEV01 and the any-non-none override unchanged. WRITE-TIME ENFORCEMENT (the concrete mechanism): src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py owns PlanSeverityAttrs; its ac_unverifiable field changes from the ordinal type to Literal["none", "underspecified_oracle", "broken_oracle", "missing_oracle"], so Pydantic strict validation rejects out-of-vocabulary grades at verification-parse time - that field is the closed-set gate the ACs pin. OPERATOR-ATTESTED ENRICH: workflow_ops.enrich_operator_attested's guard changes from `not in (None, "", "none")` to the explicit clearable set `in ("missing_oracle", "underspecified_oracle")` (clears to "none" when attested evidence satisfies the criterion - the recorded attestation IS the oracle) while broken_oracle is never cleared (a factually wrong stated command is not cured by an attestation) - this file is in Scope and the asymmetry is pinned by test. BACK-COMPAT: the closed-set validation applies to NEW plan-v3 verifications at parse time; already-stored plan-v2 sidecars keep their legacy {low,medium,high} grades and are read as-is - every calibration/replay consumer segments by impact_model_version (ADR 0036), so old records are never scored with new semantics - and this is pinned by a TEST (a plan-v2 fixture sidecar with grade "low" round-trips unmodified through latest_review_result/all_review_results). The sidecar SCHEMA id stays plan_review_result_v2: the payload shape (keys, nesting) is unchanged - only the value vocabulary of one severity-attribute field changes - so the schema-string guard in the readers keeps matching; IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION (plan-v3) is the segmentation key for the semantics change. ROLLBACK: the version bump makes back-out clean - reverting the change restores plan-v2 semantics and the corpora stay segmented; no expand-contract migration is needed because sidecars are immutable records, not migrated state. IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bumps plan-v2 -> plan-v3 in the same change. The other three override axes (dod_uncertifiable, undecomposed, divergent_implementation) keep their ordinal vocabulary and any-non-none floor, untouched in this story (their grade mix is unmeasured; calibration 4 scope).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py: ORACLE_GRADE01 + UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB constants; ac_unverifiable excluded from both generic _SEV01 loops and special-cased per the exact change spec above.
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py: PlanSeverityAttrs.ac_unverifiable becomes the closed Literal grade type (the write-time enforcement mechanism).
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py: enrich_operator_attested vocabulary update (clears missing/underspecified on attestation, never broken_oracle).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md AND plan_review_verifier_agentic.md: three-grade definitions + one worked example each; the plan-review verification output schema accepts exactly {none, underspecified_oracle, broken_oracle, missing_oracle} for the axis and rejects anything else at write time.
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py: IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump to plan-v3; the grade persists in verification.severity_attributes as today (values change, key stays).
- Unit tests: tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py (replace old low/medium/high ac_unverifiable pins with the three-grade pins; keep other-axis pins), tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py (plan-v2 -> plan-v3 assertion), tests/unit/_audit_page_helpers.py (hardcoded plan-v2 string updated), new pins for: schema acceptance AND rejection of an invalid grade, sidecar persistence, the enrich asymmetry, the UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB < min(blocking thresholds) invariant, and the plan-v2 legacy-fixture read-as-is round-trip.
- docs/plan-review-gate.md: the floor description updated to the graded rule with the back-compat note.
- Coordination: story ea39 (R5 kernel sub-answer, epic pastoral-aquatic-viper) also plans a version bump and depends_on this story - if both land close together the bumps compose (v3 then v4), never merge into one ambiguous version.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The verification model accepts exactly the closed grade set {none, underspecified_oracle, broken_oracle, missing_oracle} for ac_unverifiable on new plan-v3 verifications - pinned by BOTH an acceptance test and a rejection test for an out-of-vocabulary grade - and both verifier prompts (single-turn + agentic) define each grade with one worked example.
- [ ] Impact scoring pinned by unit tests: missing_oracle and broken_oracle findings floor at >= 0.85; underspecified_oracle findings score <= 0.55 (below the 0.60 lowest blocking threshold) and never trigger the hard floor; the other three override axes floor unchanged.
- [ ] IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION is plan-v3 in the same change (test_impact_model_versioning.py updated), the grade persists per finding in the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (pinned by test), legacy plan-v2 records are read as-is (segmentation by version is the back-compat mechanism, asserted in the doc note), and enrich_operator_attested clears missing/underspecified but never broken_oracle (pinned by test).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents the three-grade rule citing the calibration-3 evidence comment on this story, and the change is MERGED through Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).

## Context
The research phase (see the 2026-08-16 decision brief comment) measured 11 OpenGrep detectors declared across only 5 YAML source files, while `_run_opengrep` in `src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py` ran `semgrep --validate --config <source>` once per Detector even though `--validate` checks the entire source file. Matched two-call experiment: 26.025s -> 14.135s median (validation subprocesses 22 -> 10), with exact evidence-output equality.

Operator ratification (2026-08-22, recorded in the design-decision comment): implement ONLY option (a) — call-local deduplication of OpenGrep configuration validation within a single `_run_opengrep` invocation. Pure waste-removal; no behavior or boundary change; no persistent or cross-scan caching. Option (b), cross-worker scan-result reuse, is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and is filed as a separate `idea` ticket linked `discovered_from` this one (stale-result risk if the tree changes mid-run; xdist fixtures are worker-local). The gw0-crash datum is covered by the CI-timeout lane; nothing filed for it here.

## Plan
- Add a unit test (RED first) proving `--validate` runs exactly once per unique detector `source_path` within one `_run_opengrep` call.
- Add a companion test locking the quarantine contract: a shared source that fails validation fans `invalid_detector` out to every detector declared from it.
- Implement a call-local `dict[str, RunResult]` keyed by `source_path` inside `_run_opengrep`, fanning each cached validation result out to that source's detectors. Scan execution, SARIF normalization, and coverage records unchanged.
- Run lint (incl. complexity ratchet), typecheck, and the grounding test modules.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Within a single `_run_opengrep` invocation, `--validate` is invoked exactly once per unique detector `source_path`; checked by `test_opengrep_validation_runs_once_per_source_file` (written RED first against the pre-change code).
- [x] A shared-source validation failure still quarantines EVERY detector from that source as `invalid_detector` with the per-detector detail; checked by `test_opengrep_shared_source_validation_failure_fans_out_to_every_detector`.
- [x] The cache is call-local only — no module-level, persistent, or cross-scan state is introduced; checked by code inspection of `_run_opengrep`.
- [x] No scanner invocation is removed or mocked in production code; scan execution, output normalization, and coverage records are unchanged; checked by the existing `test_engine_b.py`, `test_conformance.py`, and `test_coverage_reconstruction.py` suites passing.
- [x] Option (b) cross-worker scan-result reuse is filed as a separate `idea` ticket linked `discovered_from` this ticket, capturing the caching-boundary/stale-result design question.
- [x] Lint, format, complexity ratchet (`new=0 increased=0`), and mypy are green in the worktree venv.

## Verification
- `pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_engine_b.py -q` (includes the two new tests).
- `pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_conformance.py tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py -q`.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.

## What

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A plan review that trips a provider context limit escalates the Pass-1 finder onto a model the run was never configured for. On a run whose model is provider-qualified for anything other than the provider inferred from the model NAME — a Bedrock deployment being the live case — the recovery path silently relocates the call to direct Anthropic: a hard failure in a provider-isolated container, or unbudgeted spend wherever an Anthropic key happens to exist. This is the founding defect of epic 061c on a second, independent code path: the ENTRY rung was routed through the model-class vocabulary, the ESCALATION rungs were not.

Confirmed by running the function on this tree with no class table configured:

    models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")
      -> ["claude-opus-4-8"]        # bare, direct-Anthropic-inferring

## Root cause

`_rung_target` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:332-359`) decides a rung's escalation target by comparing the RUNG's own provider-inferred form against that rung's class resolution:

    resolved = resolve_model_string(class_name)       # sizing.py:354
    provider = infer_provider(bare)                   # sizing.py:355
    own = f"{provider}:{bare}" if provider else bare  # sizing.py:356
    return bare if resolved == own else resolved      # sizing.py:357

Both sides of that comparison are derived from the ladder constant. **The model the run is actually on is never an input.** So whenever the class table has not been retargeted the equality holds and the rung degrades to `MODEL_LADDER`'s bare Anthropic family name (`sizing.py:99-103`), discarding whatever provider qualifier `cfg.model` carried. `models_at_or_above` (`sizing.py:362-376`) hands those targets to the escalation loop, which assigns them straight onto the run config at `sizing.py:427-431`:

    for model in models_at_or_above(cfg.model):
        passes.pass1_chunk(runner, replace(cfg, model=model), ...)

Two consequences, both reproduced against the current tree:

1. A Bedrock-qualified primary escalates to a bare Anthropic id (transcript above).
   `cfg.model_provider` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:391`) is left untouched by `replace`, so a run
   that qualified through that field instead composes an id like `bedrock:claude-opus-4-8`,
   which is not a valid Bedrock model id.
2. The Pass-1 entry rung names `frontier` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:76`, resolved
   at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:97-100`), so
   `models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` returns the single-element list
   `["claude-opus-4-8"]`. The substitution therefore executes on the COMMON one-criterion retry,
   before any escalation is needed — it is not confined to a rare deep-escalation case.

When a class table IS configured for another provider the current code is already correct (`models_at_or_above` returns the Bedrock ladder, asserted at `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204-212`). The live gap is the UNCONFIGURED-table plus provider-qualified-`cfg.model` combination, which no test covers.

## Approach

Make the rung target a function of the model the run is on, and make the unnameable case fail SAFE instead of crossing providers.

`models_at_or_above` already holds the primary, so thread it into `_rung_target`. Resolve the rung through its model class exactly as today, then compare the RUN's provider (`infer_provider(primary)`) with the TARGET's provider (`infer_provider(target)`):

- providers agree, or either is undeterminable -> return today's value byte-for-byte;
- providers differ and the rung is the PRIMARY's OWN rung -> return `primary` verbatim, so the
  same-model one-criterion retry still runs on the operator's model (that retry is the step that
  most often succeeds, since one criterion is a far smaller prompt than the batch);
- providers differ on a HIGHER rung -> drop the rung. The class vocabulary is the only thing
  that can name that rung in the run's provider and it has not been configured, so there is no
  honest target. Escalation stops and the existing too-big failure finding
  (`sizing.py:450-471`) reports it — a visible outcome instead of a silent provider jump.

The rule applies only on the branch that LOCATED a start rung (`sizing.py:373-375`). The no-match fallback (`sizing.py:376`) is left exactly as today, because without a located start rung there is no "primary's own rung" to preserve; see Scope for why that branch is out of scope.

Why this approach fits: the defect is that a decision about the CURRENT run is made from module constants alone, so the fix is to give the decision the run's model — the smallest input that makes the question answerable. It keeps the model-class vocabulary as the single source of escalation targets (the epic's rule) while preserving the byte-for-byte back-compat that the docstring at `sizing.py:335-347` exists to protect, so no existing caller's strings change.

Deliberately NOT changed: on an unqualified or Anthropic-qualified primary the target stays the bare form (`anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` -> `claude-opus-4-8`). That substitution is byte-different but provider-identical. The harm was never the bare FORM; it was the provider CHANGE, and the provider-agreement rule is what removes that. Preserving the bare form is the back-compat contract that keeps `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150` and `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271` passing unmodified.

`MODEL_LADDER` also keeps its bare family names. It carries two roles and only one moves: it is also the WINDOW table that `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`) reads by substring match (`if name in model`), which is why `sizing.py:319-324` records that class names in that table would make every window lookup miss. Escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary; escalation WINDOWS stay keyed on concrete model families. That separates the two orderings the constant conflates without splitting the constant.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — `_rung_target` takes the primary model as an argument
  and applies the provider-agreement rule; `models_at_or_above` passes it on the located-start-rung
  branch. No other function in the file changes.
- `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` — new cases (see Testing). This is the existing home of
  the ladder's model-class contract, holding both the byte-for-byte control (lines 256-271) and
  the configured-Bedrock case (lines 204-212) this change must not disturb.

Explicitly OUT of scope, to be raised as a separate ticket: `models_at_or_above` locates the START rung by substring-matching `MODEL_LADDER`'s Anthropic family names against the primary (`sizing.py:373-374`), so a primary from another model family falls through to the whole ladder beginning at the trivial rung — confirmed on this tree: `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` returns all three Anthropic rungs, so a context-limit escalation would DOWNGRADE the window. `largest_window_tokens` has the matching gap, returning the ladder maximum (1,000,000) for that same primary. That is a different mechanism — rung LOCATION, not rung TARGET — and this change leaves it byte-for-byte as it is.

## Testing

New cases in `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py`, using its existing `no_classes` and `_set_class_table` fixtures.

- **The defect, on the escalation path itself** — not on `models_at_or_above` in isolation. Drive
  `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` with a stub runner whose first (batch) call raises a context-limit
  error (`is_context_limit_error`, `sizing.py:300-316`, matches the substring
  `"prompt is too long"`) and a `cfg` whose model is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`
  with no class table. Assert the `cfg.model` observed by the one-criterion retry call is that
  exact string. This is the case an entry-rung test structurally cannot catch, which is why the
  defect survived the entry-rung fix.
- **Worked example, unit level** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")` returns
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0"]`. Today it returns `["claude-opus-4-8"]`.
- **Edge, higher rungs are dropped rather than crossed** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` returns exactly
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]`, and no returned element contains
  `claude-sonnet` or `claude-opus`.
- **Edge, escalation still reports the size failure** — the same Bedrock-haiku primary under a
  runner that raises a context-limit error at every attempt still yields the existing `_too_big`
  failure finding (`sizing.py:450-471`) rather than an empty result or a raised exception.
- **Back-compat controls, kept passing unmodified** — the byte-for-byte case
  (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271`, covering bare rungs, `None`, and
  `"some-unknown-model"`), the order case (lines 275-299), the configured-Bedrock case
  (lines 204-212), and `orchestrator._models_at_or_above`'s literal assertions
  (`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no model-class table configured and a primary of
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`, the model that reaches `passes.pass1_chunk` on
      the one-criterion retry is that same string; verified by the new `pass1_with_ladder` test
      asserting the observed `cfg.model`, which fails against the current tree.
- [ ] No escalation target is returned whose inferred provider differs from the primary's
      inferred provider when both are determinable; verified by a test asserting
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` equals
      `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]` under the `no_classes` fixture.
- [ ] Dropping unnameable higher rungs does not turn escalation into a crash or a silent empty
      result: the all-attempts-fail case still produces the `_too_big` failure finding; verified
      by the new failure-path test asserting `finding["_too_big"] is True`.
- [ ] Escalation targets still come from the model-class vocabulary when a class table IS
      configured; verified by `test_models_at_or_above_stays_on_bedrock_for_a_bedrock_primary`
      (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204`) passing unmodified.
- [ ] The window sizes that drive the escalation DECISION are unchanged; verified by `git diff`
      showing no change to `MODEL_LADDER` (`sizing.py:99-103`) or `largest_window_tokens`
      (`sizing.py:137-146`).
- [ ] Back-compat: with no class table configured, every escalation target for an unqualified or
      Anthropic-qualified primary is today's value byte-for-byte, including the
      `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` common path that yields bare `claude-opus-4-8`; verified by
      `test_models_at_or_above_returns_todays_bare_ids_with_no_classes_configured` and
      `test_models_at_or_above_escalation_order_is_unchanged` passing unmodified.
- [ ] The out-of-scope start-rung behaviour is untouched:
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` still returns the three bare
      Anthropic rungs; verified by a pinning test asserting that exact list.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` passes, and
      `make lint` and `make typecheck` are clean.
baseline.summary: Pass-1 context-limit escalation sets a BARE Anthropic model id, bypassing the model-class table

## Suspected defect
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py` currently writes every concurrent producer for the same ticket and criterion through `<criterion-hash>.tmp`, then calls `os.replace` onto `<criterion-hash>.json`. The module claims last-write-wins safety, but the shared temporary pathname creates a plausible race: one writer can replace or overwrite the other writer's temporary file, and the outer best-effort exception handler can hide a lost cache write. This is a collision potential identified by source inspection, not a reproduced user-visible failure. It MUST be experimentally verified before any production change.

## Mandatory reproduction before remediation
1. Drive two independent writers for the same ticket and criterion with distinct, internally identifiable payloads. Use barriers around temporary-file write and `os.replace` so the overlap is deterministic; include a cross-process case because separate verifier processes share the cache directory.
2. Record each writer's return value, exceptions before best-effort suppression, final JSON validity/content, and leftover temporary files. Distinguish harmless last-write-wins from a missing replace, payload cross-talk, invalid JSON, or silently lost cache population.
3. If all forced interleavings are safe under the supported filesystems, record the falsification and close this bug without changing the writer. If an unsafe interleaving exists, preserve it as the failing regression test before remediation.

## Remediation constraints if reproduced
- Give every writer a unique temporary file in the destination directory (run id, UUID, or a secure same-directory temporary-file primitive), then retain atomic `os.replace` onto the shared final cache key.
- A crash or failed replace must not leave a partial final JSON document; bounded cleanup may remove only that writer's own temporary file.
- Cache failure remains an accelerator miss and must never alter the completion verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A deterministic two-writer experiment proves or falsifies the collision across both thread/task and cross-process execution. [non-codebase] REPRODUCED: barrier-forced experiment, 50/50 collisions in BOTH thread and cross-process (spawn) modes; evidence in the Phase-1 RCA comment.
- [x] The experiment captures suppressed exceptions, writer results, final payload identity/JSON validity, and orphaned temporary files for each forced interleaving. [non-codebase] Captured per interleaving: writer result ok/raised+type, suppressed FileNotFoundError, final JSON valid (winner's record), no leftover .tmp; see RCA + final-report comments.
- [x] If reproduced, a regression test fails against the shared `<criterion-hash>.tmp` implementation before the fix. [non-codebase] RED-first: tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verdict_cache.py::test_concurrent_persist_for_same_criterion_loses_no_writer failed {A:0,B:1} pre-fix and under defect-seeded mutation (sandboxed); GREEN post-fix.
- [x] If reproduced, writers use unique same-directory temporary paths and atomically replace the common final cache key without cross-writer cleanup. Fix in src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_cache.py: tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=key, suffix='.tmp') then os.replace onto the shared <hash>.json; failure removes only the writer's own temp.
- [x] Concurrent stress leaves one complete valid final record, no partial record, and no effect on the verifier verdict. The committed regression test asserts both concurrent writers persist (return 1), the final <hash>.json is one valid complete record, and no .tmp residue remains; cache failure stays a best-effort accelerator miss (returns 0), never altering the verdict.
- [x] If the experiment falsifies the hypothesis, no production behavior is changed and the ticket closes with the falsifying evidence. [non-codebase] N/A — the hypothesis was REPRODUCED (not falsified), so the remediation branch applied; recorded for completeness.
baseline.summary: Parallel completion-cache writers may collide on a shared criterion .tmp path
