Make `idea` a first-class ticket status and keep it out of the automated work-dispatch surfaces.

## Why

`idea` must exist as a legal status before any other part of the feature (gate bypass, Jira mapping, the `idea` command) is meaningful. It also must never be treated as dispatchable work: an idea is captured-but-undesigned, so it must not surface in `ready` or `next-batch`.

Why a first-class status rather than a tag on an `open` ticket: a status gives structural unclaimability. `claim_core` accepts only tickets whose status is `open`, so an `idea`-status ticket is unreachable by the claim primitive with no extra filtering — whereas a tagged-`open` ticket stays claimable via `claim <id>` and leaves a genesis window where it is `open` before the tag is applied.

Prerequisite: this story is foundational — the other four child stories (eced-c6b8-7461-48a0, 1982-bf75-0f28-4e91, 6173-32ea-1fc0-4f04, 2918-24c8-4c2a-4e10) depend on the `idea` status value existing, so this story should land first.

## What

- Add `idea` to the canonical enum source `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`
  (`$defs/ticket_status`), then regenerate the `TicketStatus` literal with
  `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` (the literal is a generated artifact guarded
  by a CI drift-gate — editing `types.py` by hand would fail the gate).
- Add `idea` to the transition validator so transitions into and out of `idea`
  are legal (no prohibited edges — clients drive their own workflow).
- Add `idea` to the accepted `list --status` filter set.
- Keep `idea` OUT of the "open-ish" sets that feed dispatch, so exclusion from
  `ready`/`next-batch` is achieved by omission, not by new filter code.
- Confirm `search` returns `idea` tickets (the search path is not status-filtered;
  add a regression test).
- Document the `idea` status AND its lifecycle in the committed `CLAUDE.md`:
  eligible transitions, the `idea → closed` reject/drop bypass, the `validate`
  exemptions, and the Jira `IDEA` mapping prerequisite.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` — canonical `ticket_status` enum source.
- `src/rebar/types.py` — regenerated `TicketStatus` literal (via `gen_types`).
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — `_VALID_STATUSES`.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py` — `list --status` accepted set.
- `src/rebar/graph/_ready.py` — verify `idea` is absent from `_OPEN_STATUSES`.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` — verify `idea` is absent from the
  `open,in_progress` candidate filter.
- `CLAUDE.md` — status + full-lifecycle documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `idea` is present in `common.schema.json` `$defs/ticket_status`.
- [ ] `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` regenerates `types.py` and the CI
      drift-gate passes with `idea` in the `TicketStatus` literal.
- [ ] `transition <id> open idea` succeeds with exit 0.
- [ ] `transition <id> idea open` succeeds with exit 0.
- [ ] `transition <id> idea in_progress` succeeds with exit 0.
- [ ] `rebar list --status=idea` returns tickets whose status is `idea`.
- [ ] `rebar list --status=idea` excludes tickets whose status is not `idea`.
- [ ] `rebar ready` never returns a ticket whose status is `idea` (test-verified).
- [ ] `rebar next-batch <epic>` never returns a ticket whose status is `idea`
      (test-verified).
- [ ] `rebar search <term>` returns a matching `idea` ticket (test-verified).
- [ ] The committed `CLAUDE.md` documents the `idea` status and its lifecycle
      (transitions, close-bypass, validate exemptions, Jira prerequisite).
- [ ] The full test suite passes with all five sibling changes integrated (this
      foundational story owns the integrated-suite check).
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: Add 'idea' as a first-class status excluded from ready/next-batch

baseline.description:
## Context

With an UNDECLARED `file_impact`, currency falls back to invalidating on ANY code-SHA change — a fail-safe measured to over-trigger: 307 of 1,457 full re-reviews (21%) ran on byte-identical material, 171 from base-SHA drift alone (b902-18af-14ed-4da1). Allowing drift without re-review, and requiring file_impact universally, are both rejected; this scopes the fail-safe instead, EXTENDING ADR-0002's per-path machinery rather than adding a parallel trigger.

## (a) Record the read-set inside the signed material

**Source.** `usage_log.run_shape` emits `distinct_fetches`: `{"tool","target"}` records where `fetch_target` returns the `path` arg for `read_file`/`list_directory`, the query STRING for `search_files`. **Normalization.** New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/read_set.py` reduces `distinct_fetches` to the read-set, in order:

1. **Tool filter** — keep ONLY `tool == "read_file"`. `search_files` targets are query strings; `list_directory` targets are directories `_hash_file` cannot hash — dropped, not expanded (which would import unread files).
2. **Root resolution** — resolve a relative target against the hash root `_hash_basis(repo_root)` (the pinned-SHA snapshot when attested, else the checkout); an absolute target is used as-is.
3. **Containment** — `os.path.realpath`, then DROP anything not under that root (discards `../` escapes and outside-repo absolutes).
4. **Repo-relative POSIX form** — `os.path.relpath` + `PurePath.as_posix()`, stripping `./` and collapsing `.`/`..`.
5. **Existence filter** — DROP anything not an existing regular file. A mistyped read contributed no content, so baking `_ABSENT_HASH` would let an unrelated later file creation invalidate.
6. **Dedupe + sort** — `./src/x.py` and `src/x.py` collapse to one; the manifest stays reproducible.

**Plumbing.** `distinct_fetches` does not reach signing today: `sizing.usage_record` keeps only criteria/requests/token fields, and `_attach_plan_review_metrics` reads only `requests`. Three additive edits: `usage_record` passes it through; `pass1.aggregate_usage` unions the per-call lists (dedup on `(tool,target)`); `_attach_plan_review_metrics` unions every LLM step's, normalizes, and writes `coverage["read_set"]` + `read_set_recorded`.

`read_set_recorded` is set ONLY when a fetch was OBSERVED and survived normalization. An empty observation is deliberately NOT read as "the review verifiably read nothing": a runner reporting no fetch telemetry is indistinguishable from one that opened no files, so the stronger reading would scope fail-OPEN.

**Signed record.** `build_manifest` gains sorted `read-path: <path>` lines plus a `read-set: <count>` marker, emitted only when recorded. The signature binds the whole manifest, so a modified read-set fails verification → `verdict="unsigned"` → invalidate.

## (b) Feed the read-set into the ADR-0002 dependency set

Scoping applies ONLY where ADR 0002 leaves a hole — all four must hold: the pre-existing set (declared `file_impact` ∪ cited paths ∪ inherited child impact) is EMPTY; the container poison rule is NOT in effect; the ticket's scope is UNDECLARED (not an authenticated `none`); a read-set was recorded. Then `dependency_hashes` composes **read-set ∪ expanded blast-radius entries** with the SAME machinery. The re-hash loop's STRUCTURE is unchanged — it still iterates exactly the entries recorded at signing — but each entry now DISPATCHES (below).

Each precondition is load-bearing. Adding the blast radius to an ALREADY-scoped set would only widen it and re-create the false positive this ticket removes (an unrelated `rebar.toml` commit would invalidate a container scoped to its child's files). A poisoned container is fail-CLOSED at whole-HEAD, since any partial scope is fail-OPEN for the child's undeclared impact. And an authenticated `none` is today fully EXEMPT from drift (`compute_validity` skips even the head check); scoping it yields a non-empty set that `classify_file_scope` reclassifies `none`→`paths`, so a previously exempt attestation would START invalidating — the opposite of the goal.

**Blast radius:** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, `rebar.toml`, `src/rebar/llm/criteria/**`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/*.yaml`. (`criteria/**` holds the threshold resolver and overlay-merge core, which change outcomes with no rubric edit.)


Because the check iterates recorded entries, each glob is handled two ways at ATTESTATION time:

- **Expansion** — sorted `glob.glob(root_dir=base, recursive=True)`, regular files only; each match becomes an **ordinary** `dep <sha256> <path>` line, so content drift names the exact file.
- **Membership digest** — the glob PATTERN is recorded as a dep entry whose digest is sha256 of its sorted, newline-joined match list, closing the addition/deletion blind spot: a rubric added after signing has no baked per-file hash but moves the digest; a deleted member moves both it and its own entry.

Both sides route through ONE helper, `read_set.hash_dep_entry(entry, base=...)`, dispatching on a glob metacharacter (`*`, `?`, `[`): glob → membership digest, plain path → `_hash_file` (so pre-81ca manifests re-hash byte-identically). THREE call sites convert: `dependency_hashes`, `attest._rehash`, and the INLINE `_hash_file(p, base=base)` in `compute_validity`'s DEFAULT loop — distinct from `_rehash`. Missing the third would hash a glob PATTERN as a literal filename to `_ABSENT_HASH`, mismatching the signed digest and invalidating on every claim.

**Fail-safes** (each falls back to invalidate-on-any-change — empty dep set → whole-HEAD): no recorded read-set (pre-change attestation, no agentic pass, no observed fetch); verification failure, including a tampered read-set; a raise during basis resolution or expansion, which `dependency_hashes` catches and logs.

## (c) Report the basis

`build_manifest` records one authenticated `currency-basis: file_impact | read-set | fail-safe` line chosen at sign time. `plan_review_status` (no LLM / no network) reads it off the signed manifest; a legacy manifest without it derives `file_impact` when dep lines exist, else `fail-safe`. The `--status` text renderer prints it; JSON carries the same key. ADR 0002 gains an addendum recording the read-set field, the preconditions, the composition rule, and the membership digest.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The signed manifest records the normalized read paths when fetches were observed, is absent otherwise, and a modified read-set cannot survive verification. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_attest_drift.py -k "read_set" -x -q` — pinning the field, the normalization cases (non-`read_file` dropped, `./` collapsed, outside-repo and nonexistent dropped, deduped), and tamper.
- [x] With an otherwise-empty UNDECLARED set and a moved SHA, currency reuses the ADR-0002 content-hash check over read-set ∪ blast radius: an untouched set stays current, a touched path invalidates, a file ADDED under a glob invalidates via the membership digest, and an already-scoped, poisoned, or declared-`none` set never gains the blast radius. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_attest_drift.py -k "no_file_impact or blast_radius or already_scoped or poisoned or exemption" -x -q`.
- [x] Unverifiable read-set, pre-change attestations lacking the field, and expansion failure each fall back to invalidate-on-any-change. Verify: `... -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_attest_drift.py -k "fallback" -x -q`.
- [x] `rebar review-plan <id> --status` reports the basis (file_impact | read-set | fail-safe) in text and JSON. Verify: `... -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_attest_drift.py -k "currency_basis" -x -q`.
- [x] ADR 0002 documents the read-set field, composition rule, and membership digest. Verify: `grep -n "read-set" docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md`.
baseline.summary: Scope no-file-impact SHA-drift invalidation to the review read-set and cited paths (approved design a+b)

## Context

The Cloud rate-limit sweep intentionally covers four transport-surface modules under `adapters/jira/`. Its `_step0_names()` input is hardcoded, so a classified mutating method can be renamed or moved into an unswept sibling module without the completeness assertion noticing. A package-wide glob was evaluated and rejected because it would redefine the sweep from the transport surface to the entire Jira package and require policy classification of 90 unrelated members.

Current measurement finds exactly two definitions outside the swept modules whose names are in `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`: `backend.py::set_relationship` and `backend.py::add_comment`. Both are pure, same-name `self.transport` delegations. The unswept package set also includes `acli_subprocess.py` and `jira_fields.py`; neither currently collides with the classified mutating names.

## Operator decision

Implement option B: retain the explicit transport file list and add a strict anti-drift guard over every other Python module in `adapters/jira/`. A classified mutating name is allowed outside the sweep only when its body is a pure same-name transport delegation with unchanged arguments. Reject package-wide globbing.

## Plan

- Make the four swept transport paths an explicit named constant used by `_step0_names()`.
- Parse every other Jira adapter Python module with `ast` and identify functions whose names collide with `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`.
- Accept only the deliberately narrow facade shape already used by `backend.py`: one return statement calling `self.transport.<same_name>` with the declared arguments forwarded unchanged. Any guard, retry, logging, argument transform, extra statement, or non-transport target fails.
- Add a test proving the current two backend facades are the only accepted collisions and a mutation-style fixture proving an unswept non-facade `add_comment` turns the guard red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The existing transport sweep remains scoped to the same four modules; no package-wide glob widens the 429 policy surface.
- [x] An anti-drift assertion scans every other `adapters/jira/*.py` module, including `acli_subprocess.py` and `jira_fields.py`, for names in `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`.
- [x] The only allowed collision shape is a pure same-name `self.transport` delegation with arguments forwarded unchanged.
- [x] The current `backend.py::set_relationship` and `backend.py::add_comment` facades pass the guard.
- [x] A new or moved unswept definition using a classified mutating name fails unless it is that exact pure-facade shape.
- [x] The focused Cloud rate-limit sweep passes without changing production code.
baseline.summary: Rate-limit sweep's Cloud file list is hardcoded, not derived (8a5e F7)

# Provider-generic agent guidance: AGENTS.md migration, doc de-dup, client template, portable skills

## Context

Our agent guidance is Claude-locked and bloated. `CLAUDE.md` is 665 lines and duplicates large parts of `docs/` (an established anti-pattern — the file loads every session, and past a threshold it degrades instruction-following). `CLAUDE.local.md` mixes genuinely machine/operator-local content with generally-applicable project rules copied from `CLAUDE.md`. And the guidance is readable only by Claude Code, while `AGENTS.md` is now the de-facto cross-vendor standard (OpenAI 2025 → donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic/OpenAI/Block, Dec 2025) read natively by Codex, Cursor, Copilot's coding agent, Zed, Windsurf, Amp, Factory, Jules, Devin, RooCode, and Cline.

The repo is already ~30% migrated (`.agents/rules/rebar.md`, `.agents/mcp_config.json`, `.codex/config.toml` with a "migrate CLAUDE.md" shim comment, `docs/session-id-shims.md`, and `examples/claude-skills/` reframed as retargetable). This epic finishes that migration.

**Locked decisions (design session):** (1) `AGENTS.md` becomes the canonical root file; a thin `CLAUDE.md` bridges Claude Code via a one-line `@AGENTS.md` import; the duplicated bulk is reduced to one-line pointers into `docs/`. (2) A shipped `templates/AGENTS.md` carries the portable "how to drive rebar" guidance for client projects, kept in sync with the authoritative docs by a test. (3) Example skills stay in the SKILL.md format (now a cross-provider open standard) but are de-branded and generalized. See the design-of-record session log for the full research basis (AGENTS.md governance, provider matrix, OSS patterns, anti-patterns).

**Key insight:** "CLAUDE.md duplicates docs" and "separate rebar's guide from a client template" are the same fix — push the portable rebar-usage guidance into `docs/` as the single source of truth, and have thin, audience-specific files point at it. rebar's own `AGENTS.md` keeps only rebar-internal dev specifics inline (Gerrit split-remote, module-size policy, Serena, local-dev-env, worktree/venv, CI-before-close, signing).

## Scope

In: the root guidance files, `docs/` homes for CLAUDE.md-native content, the `.codex`/`.agents` shims, `examples/` skills, a client template + drift test, and a repo-wide reference sweep. Out: changing rebar's runtime behavior, the Gerrit/CI landing flow itself, or Jira sync.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories are closed and their changes are landed on `main`.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` exists at the repo root and is the canonical guidance file; `CLAUDE.md` is a
  thin `@AGENTS.md` pointer (plus only Claude-only notes).
  - Proving: `test -f AGENTS.md && rg -c '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md`
- [ ] `templates/AGENTS.md` (client-usable, provider-neutral) exists and a drift-guard test
  keeps it in sync with the authoritative source.
  - Proving: `test -f templates/AGENTS.md && make test`
- [ ] The example skills directory is provider-neutral (renamed from `examples/claude-skills`)
  and `make lint && make test` pass on the merged result.
  - Proving: `rg -l 'examples/claude-skills' . | wc -l` returns 0
- [ ] Any supported harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) picks up rebar's dev guidance from a
- [ ] The root guidance file is lean (target ≤ ~200 lines) and duplicates no doc that already has
- [ ] A client project adopting rebar can copy one provider-neutral template to teach its own
- [ ] No guidance is lost in the move — every rule removed from `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE.local.md` has
baseline.summary: Provider-generic agent guidance: AGENTS.md migration, doc de-dup, client template, portable skills

baseline.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in **bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json` (1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40 consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x), and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git — an earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and dropped re-homing it off-branch (WS-1) because the convergence loop already self-heals binding drift. So the levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included (child A6) under an operator-approved quiescence protocol. Its mechanics are **proven, not theoretical**: `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` on the real branch produced 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%) with all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges preserved and the HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths. Stock git plumbing only — `git-filter-repo` is deliberately **not** used: it is an unwanted core dependency and it prunes empty commits, which would reshape the DAG that ancestry-based authorship verification walks.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` + write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`
2. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; read `max(new, legacy)`
3. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority (exclude `assignee`)
4. **A2-2** delete the legacy in-line `last_get_pass` field (gated on writer rollout)
5. **A4-1/2/3** `bridge_fsck` fence, then `prev_snapshot` -> key-set, then branch-3 empty-payload skip
6. **A5** ADR covering all three committed-format changes
7. **A6** one-time reclaim under the quiescence protocol (LAST; requires A1-A5 and Epic B's B6)

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes to a shared store file, each with a stated boundary. A2-1 is reversible (it never stops writing the legacy field). A3 is reversible because the read path canonicalizes both shapes idempotently. A2-2 and A4-2 are the irreversible steps: A2-2 is gated on observed writer rollout; reverting A4-2 requires the reverse-direction corpus diff recorded first. A6 is gated on an off-repo backup bundle plus a fail-closed epoch guard, and its resumability is explicitly **none** — mitigated by running every correctness assertion on a scratch clone before anything is published.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline today 12.79 KB.
      Verify: the measurement script recorded in the child ticket.
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: integration against a stateful fake asserting
      file bytes and commit count, not call counts.
- [ ] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference to it remains. Verify: `grep -r baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty) — the read-only path must not persist a migration.
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the same
      verdict as its normalized-string equivalent. This test does not exist today; the existing
      cells use flat strings only, so a no-op-on-strings normalizer would pass while proving
      nothing. Tier: integration through the real production comparison path.
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over >=4 real snapshot pairs shows zero
      difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect, **and** the reverse-direction
      diff is recorded as the A4-2 rollback artifact.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` is **<=800 LOC** after the rotation extraction (it is at exactly 800
      today; the locked module-size gate fails the build on 801).
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB**, `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded
      pre-rewrite tip tree, and commit and merge-commit counts are unchanged (measured at window
      time, not hardcoded).
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** (the assertion that actually proves non-resurrection) and
      `size-pack` growth is <1 MB.
- [ ] A clone on a stale epoch attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites (`sync._union_merge` and `push.py`'s non-FF retry). Tier: integration in two
      real temporary clones with divergent epochs.
- [ ] An ADR exists enumerating all three committed-format changes, the mixed-version protocol, the
      A2-2 gate, and each rollback boundary.
- [ ] The off-repo backup bundle exists and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] Operator has confirmed zero active sessions and all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped before the
      reclaim window. **[operator-attested]**
baseline.summary: Bound tickets-store growth: make the committed .bridge_state cache cheap + one-time reclaim of the spent ~1 GiB

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Research handoff, not a claim on the work: **a parallel session currently owns CI performance, the Python-version matrix and 3.14 adoption.** This task records a comparison of rebar's Gerrit Verified gate against five actively-maintained Python projects (Django, Pydantic, pytest, urllib3, cryptography — all with commits in the 10–22 Aug 2026 window) so the findings are not lost, and so the owner can take what fits.

**Verified against current `origin/main`, not the older commit the study cited:**
- `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, but the blocking matrix stops at **3.13**
  (`_build-and-test.yml:307-315`: `ubuntu-latest`/`macos-latest` × 3.11/3.12/3.13, with macOS
  3.11 and 3.12 excluded — so macOS runs 3.13 only, giving 4 cells).
- `codeql.yml:20-26` triggers on **`schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only** — no
  `pull_request`/`workflow_call`, so CodeQL structurally CANNOT gate a Gerrit merge.
- Zizmor is scoped to `release.yml` (`Makefile:243-244`, which says widening it "is separate
  work"); actionlint does cover all workflows, but it checks syntax, not supply chain.

## What rebar already matches or exceeds
Worth stating so this is not read as a deficit list: exact Gerrit patchset checkout with fail-closed voting, ruff/mypy/pre-commit/ShellCheck/actionlint/lockfile validation, severity-aware dependency audit, four test tiers, per-test and whole-job timeouts, targeted mutation testing, per-extra and no-extra install isolation, wheel/sdist provenance probes, Dependabot, trusted publishing, PEP 740 attestations, and documentation/schema/complexity/ module-size drift gates. Several of these exceed the comparison set.

## Approved direction (from the CI owner)
- Gerrit Verified gate tests the **oldest and newest supported** versions; intermediate
  versions move to the **scheduled sweep against main**.
- **macOS stays on the hot path but scoped to compatibility tests**; Ubuntu runs the full
  suite.
- **Windows is a candidate for the scheduled sweep** — coverage without hot-path latency.

## Findings, ordered by value per minute of added latency
**Zero added hot-path latency:**
1. **Widen Zizmor beyond `release.yml`.** It already runs under `make lint`; the scope is a
   Makefile argument. Gerrit Verified holds the SSH credential that casts the authoritative
   vote, so its own workflow is the one most worth auditing.
2. **SHA-pin third-party actions.** `gerrit-verify.yaml` states actions are SHA-pinned while
   using mutable `@v7` refs; `_build-and-test.yml` uses `actions/checkout@v7` and
   `actions/setup-python@v7`. Either pin them or correct the comment — a false claim in a
   security-relevant file is worse than an accurate absence.
3. **`twine check dist/*` in `_artifact-probe.yml`.** The probe already builds and installs
   distributions; metadata validation currently waits until release. Seconds, pre-merge.

**Scheduled sweep, no hot-path cost:** intermediate Python versions (3.12/3.13), Windows, 3.15-dev and free-threaded 3.14t as non-blocking, dependency lower-bound resolution (the lock proves ONE resolution works, not that the declared floors do), external documentation link checking, and the full macOS suite.

**Needs a latency decision, so flagged rather than recommended:** running CodeQL on the exact Gerrit refspec and adding it to `vote.needs`. Today a CodeQL-detectable defect can earn `Verified +1`. urllib3 runs it per-PR. This is the one item that genuinely adds pre-merge minutes; whether that trade is worth it is the owner's call, not this ticket's.

**Deferred with reasoning:** raising the 70% branch-coverage floor toward the 100% that urllib3 and cryptography enforce. rebar's targeted mutation testing is stronger evidence than raw coverage, and forcing a global percentage buys low-value tests. Diff coverage on changed lines is the better first step. Downstream-consumer testing is premature until public integrations exist.

## Scope
No files. This is a research record for the CI owner; any implementation belongs in tickets they raise, sized against their own latency budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [non-codebase] The CI owner has seen this record and each finding is dispositioned —
      adopted, deferred with a reason, or rejected with a reason; checked by a comment here
      naming the disposition of each numbered item.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Any adopted item exists as its own ticket with its own acceptance
      criteria; checked by links from this ticket.
baseline.summary: OSS CI-practice comparison: research handoff for the CI owner

baseline.description:
Add a code-review **surface-parity** overlay: a Pass-1 specialist reviewer for the four-pass code-review gate that flags when a write-op's parameter / guard / required-field surface changes on ONE adapter (lib `_lib_writes.py`, CLI `_commands/`, MCP `_mcp_writes.py`) without the sibling surfaces being updated in lockstep. This is the STATIC code-review complement to the runtime behavioral conformance oracle landed under topaz-blubbery-mice: the oracle proves parity at test time; this overlay coaches an author (at review time) toward parity BEFORE the code lands, catching the escaped-bug class recorded on cranial-goodly-seahog (a guard/arg added to one entry point and not mirrored to its siblings; worst case halfwhite-chordal-stonefly had 9 prior PASS reviews with zero findings).

Advisory-first (blocking_enabled=false): a divergence is a coach-not-block finding, verified in Pass-2 and decided in Pass-3. A DELIBERATE divergence the author justifies must NOT fire (the reviewer prompt carries that false-positive guard).

## Approach

Model it on the existing GLOB-triggered overlays (api-compat, security): the overlay fires when the diff touches a known write-surface adapter file, and the LLM reviewer judges whether an actual param/guard/required-field surface changed and whether the sibling adapters were updated in lockstep. No change to `registry.content_triggered_overlays` is needed; glob routing via `applies_to` keeps the overlay inert on unrelated diffs.

1. New packaged reviewer prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-surface-parity.md`
   (front-matter `dimension: code-review-surface-parity`,
   `langfuse_prompt: rebar-code-review-surface-parity`, `outputs: code_review_findings`,
   `execution_mode: agentic`, `category: code-review-pass`), matching the deletion-impact /
   api-compat contract (evidence-record findings, `criteria: ["surface-parity"]`, no
   model-emitted severity). The prompt enumerates the three write surfaces, tells the reviewer
   to Grep the sibling adapters for the changed param/guard, and carries the false-positive
   guards (deliberate justified divergence; a purely internal refactor changing no
   caller-visible surface; an adapter-bound param such as `_creation_channel` / `return_alias` /
   `source` / `repo_root` that is intentionally not caller-visible).
2. Add `"surface-parity"` to `OVERLAY_IDS` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` (closed
   enum; comment it glob-triggered, advisory).
3. Add the routing entry to `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`:
   `exec: AGENT`, `applies_to` globbing the write-surface adapters
   (`**/_commands/**`, `**/_lib_writes.py`, `**/_mcp_writes.py`), `default_posture: advisory`,
   `block_threshold: 0.95`, `blocking_enabled: false`, `_comment` citing this ticket.
4. Wire the overlay into the four-pass gate topology so the finder is actually DISPATCHED:
   - `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — add a `- `surface-parity` — …` bullet to
     the FIXED overlay catalog (base reviewer's `recommend_overlays` escalation list). A strict
     no-drift test (`test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids`) requires the catalog
     to EXACTLY equal `OVERLAY_IDS`, so this edit is mandatory the moment the id is added.
   - `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — add a
     `{ prompt: code-review-surface-parity, when: "${{ steps.triggers.outputs.include_surface_parity }}" }`
     entry to the `round_a` batch and its
     `steps.union.outputs.include_surface_parity` twin to the `round_b` batch, mirroring the
     two existing `code-review-deletion-impact` entries. Without this the `include_surface_parity`
     glob flag flips but no finder runs.
5. `reviewers/index.json` needs NO change: overlay prompts (category `code-review-pass`,
   `is_reviewer` false) are excluded from the selection catalog, so
   `prompts.regenerate_prompt_index()` is a no-op — the drift gate stays green because the
   prompt is correctly ABSENT (like every sibling overlay), not registered.

## Portability

The overlay is part of rebar's IN-PROCESS code-review gate (`rebar review-code` / `produce_code_review_verdict`); it runs via the same library entry point on every platform with NO dependency on any specific CI provider (identical with a diverse CI provider or no CI provider). Registration is data + a packaged prompt, loaded in-process. This satisfies `project.portability`.

## Scope

- ADD reviewer prompt `code-review-surface-parity.md`.
- EDIT `registry.py` (`OVERLAY_IDS`), `criteria_routing.json` (routing entry),
  `code-review-base.md` (catalog bullet), `code-review.yaml` (round_a + round_b finder).
- index.json is NOT touched (overlays are excluded from the catalog; regen is a no-op).
- ADD tests (see Testing).

OUT OF SCOPE: flipping the overlay to blocking (advisory-first by design; a later calibration ticket may promote it, mirroring cranial-goodly-seahog); any change to the runtime oracle (topaz); any change to the write adapters themselves (scratchy/blusterous own those).

## Testing

- Unit: assert `"surface-parity"` is a member of `OVERLAY_IDS` and that
  `registry.routing_index()["surface-parity"]` has the expected shape
  (`exec == "AGENT"`, advisory, `blocking_enabled is False`, `block_threshold == 0.95`, and the
  three write-surface globs present).
- Unit: assert `registry.threshold_for(["surface-parity"])` resolves to `(0.95, False)`
  (advisory, non-blocking) — it does NOT join the approved blocking set.
- Unit: assert the glob routing FIRES the overlay for a changed
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` (and `_mcp_writes.py`) and stays inert for an unrelated
  file (e.g. a docs-only change), via the existing overlay-selection seam
  (`overlay_union` / `workflow_ops`).
- Drift: assert the base-reviewer catalog stays in lockstep with `OVERLAY_IDS`
  (`test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids` passes with the new bullet).
- Workflow: assert the `code-review-surface-parity` finder is actually DISPATCHED in the
  `round_a` batch for a changed `src/rebar/_commands/*.py` (not merely that the
  `include_surface_parity` flag flips), mirroring the deletion-impact workflow test.
- Drift: assert `reviewers/index.json` is UNCHANGED — the overlay (category
  `code-review-pass`) is excluded from the catalog, so regen output is byte-identical and the
  drift gate passes as a no-op.
- `make lint` + `make typecheck` green; the complexity ratchet unaffected (no function grows).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A new `surface-parity` overlay exists in the code-review gate: `"surface-parity"` is a
      member of `OVERLAY_IDS` and has a routing entry in `criteria_routing.json`.
- [x] The overlay is GLOB-triggered on the three write-surface adapters
      (`_commands/`, `_lib_writes.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`) and stays inert on unrelated diffs, and
      is WIRED into the round_a/round_b batches of the code-review gate so the finder is actually
      dispatched (not just an unused include flag).
- [x] The base-reviewer overlay catalog (`code-review-base.md`) lists `surface-parity`, keep
      `test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids` green.
- [x] The overlay is ADVISORY (`blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.95`);
      `threshold_for(["surface-parity"])` == `(0.95, False)` and it is NOT in the approved
      blocking set.
- [x] A packaged reviewer prompt `code-review-surface-parity.md` exists (deletion-impact/api-
      compat contract); `reviewers/index.json` stays UNCHANGED (overlays excluded), drift gate a
      no-op.
- [x] The reviewer prompt carries the false-positive guards (deliberate justified divergence;
      adapter-bound non-caller-visible params; internal-only refactors) so a compliant lockstep
      change or a justified divergence returns no finding.
- [x] Unit tests in `tests/unit/test_code_review_surface_parity.py` assert the overlay
      membership, routing, glob firing on each write adapter, and round_a/round_b dispatch.
baseline.summary: Add code-review surface-parity criterion (CLI <-> MCP <-> import-format lockstep)

baseline.description:
## Context
The shared review kernel's impact() (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:111) computes impact = mean(max(prod_impact,debt_impact), blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility), each axis mapped none/local/low/easy=0.33 .. high/system/hard=1.0. This model was implicitly shaped by PLAN-REVIEW and mis-measures CODE-REVIEW findings.

Evidence (same model, two populations):
- PLAN-REVIEW would-block (n=921): prod_impact high=59%, blast module+=98%, likelihood high=78%, reversibility moderate/hard=84% -> impact 0.78+. Fits: plan-review findings are production/design-CONSEQUENCE shaped.
- CODE-REVIEW (n=31 live re-runs): prod_impact none/low=96% (0% high), reversibility easy=93%, blast local/module, debt_impact never high -> impact capped ~0.25-0.60. A feature silently dead in prod (untested wiring) scores prod_impact=none, impact=0.415 — overlapping the doc-nit band, so NO threshold separates landmines from nits.

## Why diverge (do NOT share the plan-review model — sibling of c34d, kept separate)
The two gates measure different things with different needs:
- Plan-review impact = production/design consequence of shipping a flawed PLAN. prod_impact / blast / likelihood / reversibility-of-the-approach are the right axes.
- Code-review impact = long-term MAINTAINABILITY / latent-regression risk of a DIFF. Dominant axis should be tech-debt / detection-gap, NOT immediate production blast. reversibility-of-the-change is not merely irrelevant but INVERTED here — a detection gap that is easy to reverse yet easy to miss (a missing test) is HIGH risk, but the model scores easy-reversibility as LOW impact. 93% of code-review findings hit that floor.
Forcing both through one production-severity model means code-review can never score its own high-value findings above its own nits.

## Directions (design later)
- A code-review-specific impact model: debt/maintainability severity primary (allow high/critical); a detection-gap / latent-regression axis (does this create a future SILENT failure?); blast measured on the FUTURE-change surface (how much future work does this booby-trap); DROP or invert reversibility for detection-gap findings.
- Keep the shared decide.py kernel but DISPATCH impact() per-gate (mirrors how threshold_for already dispatches per-gate in criteria/model.py), so plan-review keeps its production-severity model unchanged and code-review gets a maintainability model.
- Re-derive/validate from the code-review corpus once LLM blocking is trialed.

## Relationship
Sibling of c34d (neat-sooty-termite = PLAN-REVIEW impact aggregation / mean-dilution). Deliberately SEPARATE tickets: the models diverge. This ticket is the code-review-gate impact model; c34d is the plan-review-gate aggregation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Parking-lot idea; not scheduled. Revisit alongside introducing any code-review LLM blocking (the DET new-behavior-without-test gate is the near-term substitute that sidesteps the scalar).
baseline.summary: Code-review needs its OWN impact model — production-severity axes mis-measure maintainability/detection-gap findings

baseline.description:
# Extract build_model_settings() and build_usage_limits()

ADR 0056 decision 3, SECOND extraction. Sequenced after the except-spine extraction because both edit run(); there is no logical dependency between them.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/runner.py -> two plain functions with EXPLICIT parameters:
      build_model_settings(cfg, req, caps, resolved, cache_settings, *, model_override) -> dict
      build_usage_limits(cfg, req, UsageLimits) -> tuple[UsageLimits, int, int]
          returning exactly (usage_limits, req_limit, eff_max_iter)
  covering max_tokens, timeout, temperature (incl. the withdrawal matrix), max_iterations and the
  per-run request ceiling.
- tests/unit/
- tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py  (REQUIRED — see "the seam guard has no teeth by default")

### `build_usage_limits` MUST RETURN THE TWO COUNTERS, NOT JUST THE LIMITS OBJECT

`run()` needs `req_limit` AND `eff_max_iter` as independent locals AFTER the call, so a bare `-> tuple` leaves the unpacking contract undefined. MEASURED uses at HEAD: both are read at runner.py:542-543 to build `FailureContext(...)` — the carrier task e6bd introduced for `interpret_failure` — and again at runner.py:572-573 in the success telemetry log.

`eff_max_iter` CANNOT be recovered from the returned `UsageLimits`: only `max(8, eff_max_iter)` is stored there, as `tool_calls_limit` (runner.py:479), and `max()` is not invertible — for any `eff_max_iter <= 8` the original value is unrecoverable. `req_limit` happens to equal `usage_limits.request_limit`, but reaching back into the object to re-derive one of the two while the other must be returned anyway is worse than returning both.

Return `(usage_limits, req_limit, eff_max_iter)`.

### `cache_settings` MUST BE A PARAMETER — do not recompute it

MEASURED: the extracted region's FIRST line is `model_settings = dict(cache_settings) if cache_settings is not None else {}` (runner.py:408), and `cache_settings` is computed 27 lines EARLIER, at runner.py:381, as `cache_settings = None if self._model_override else cache_settings_for(caps)`.

So it is an INPUT to this region, not something the region derives. An implementer given the older signature has only two exits and both are wrong: invent an undocumented parameter, or recompute `cache_settings_for(caps)` inside `structured_run`. The recompute is the dangerous one — it drops the `self._model_override` guard, silently re-enabling cache settings on the offline TestModel path that this plan (and the comment at runner.py:373) requires to keep them None. It would also re-introduce a `cache_settings_for` call site in the leaf module.

Pass it in. This makes 5 positional parameters plus one keyword-only; ADR 0056's "carrier above ~6" threshold is advisory and is NOT tripped here.

NOTE: the line numbers above were taken BEFORE task e6bd landed in the stack. e6bd removed the except spine and tightened comment wording in run(), so re-locate the region by content, not by these offsets.

## Destination and its headroom (do not create a new file)

The themed module already exists: `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`. It is the run-execution cluster and is where e6bd put `interpret_failure`. MEASURED after e6bd: it is 373 LOC, and `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py` asserts `100 <= loc < 500`. So this extraction has roughly 125 lines of headroom there. If both functions plus their travelling comments would breach 500, split along a real seam into a second themed module at or above the 100-LOC floor — do NOT trim the comments to fit (see "Honest accounting").

## THE LEAF-INVARIANT TRAP — build_model_settings must be PURE

MEASURED: `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` is defined at `runner.py:64` and mutated inside the temperature block (`if resolved not in _TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED: _TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED.add(resolved)`), which sits INSIDE the region this ticket extracts.

`structured_run.py` is a LEAF, and that is ENFORCED, not conventional: `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner` walks the AST and fails on any runtime `import runner` (only a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded annotation import is allowed). A naive move therefore has two bad exits:

* move the block but keep referencing the set -> `structured_run` needs a runtime import of `runner`
  -> the leaf test FAILS;
* move the SET too -> `runner.py:64`'s own reference breaks, and so does the test-side `.clear()`
  through the import alias.

**REQUIRED SHAPE: `build_model_settings(...)` returns the computed `model_settings` dict and performs NO side effect. The dedup-logging `if ... .add(resolved)` stays INLINE in `run()`, beside the set it mutates.** Do not "solve" this with a lazy import, a callback parameter, or by relocating the set. The extraction is still worth doing without those two lines.

## Explicitly NOT a frozen carrier object

ADR 0056 rejects the `ResolvedCall` dataclass an earlier draft proposed. Two of its seven fields (model_settings, provenance) are mutated after construction -- task cc33 writes provider_provenance["ran_model"] AFTER the finally block -- so the freeze would be decorative exactly where it matters, at a cost of ~30-40 lines of replace() ceremony to relocate ~113 lines of code. Use explicit parameters; introduce a carrier only if a signature exceeds ~6 parameters.

## Honest accounting

This region is 50% comment: ~80 lines is ~36 lines of executable code. The comments TRAVEL WITH the code -- they are the temperature-deprecation matrix and the per-request-vs-config precedence rationale, and they are the reason the region is readable at all. Do not strip them to hit a number. Per AGENTS.md, do not create a module under 100 LOC by splitting: group these into ONE themed module rather than a file per function.

Wording MAY be tightened where a sentence carries no fact, but never drop a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a bug/story/epic id, a named failure mode, or a stated invariant. Deleting documentation to satisfy a size guard is the "raise the cap" anti-pattern ADR 0056 rejects by name.

## Monkeypatch repoints — measure, do NOT assume zero

e6bd owned ZERO repoints, but that was MEASURED for the except spine specifically and does not transfer. Whichever of `cache_settings_for`, `_pai_model`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url` fall inside the settings block this ticket actually moves must be repointed IN THE SAME COMMIT. Re-importing a moved name back into `runner` fixes `from … import` callers but NOT `monkeypatch.setattr` patches, which rebind `runner`'s global while the extracted function resolves through its own module globals — so "I re-exported it" is never evidence a repoint was unneeded. Run the full suite and repoint what breaks.

## Testing

Unit tier, no network -- pure given cfg/req/caps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts temperature is WITHDRAWN for a caps record with supports_temperature False and
      RETAINED when True -- the negative control is what stops a "withdraw always" implementation passing
- [ ] a test asserts a per-request output cap can only RAISE the configured floor, never lower it
- [ ] a test asserts a per-request step budget likewise only raises
- [ ] `build_model_settings` performs no side effect: the `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` mutation
      still happens in `run()`, and `test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner` passes
- [ ] the extracted module is at or above the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor, and
      `structured_run.py` remains under 500 LOC
- [ ] the durable end-state: `wc -l src/rebar/llm/runner.py` at this commit is under 700. This is
      machine-enforced, not a promise —
      `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap`
      fails otherwise, and `Verified` is cast per patchset
      (`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` checks out `refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P`), so a red
      ancestor blocks the whole relation chain
- [ ] [operator-attested] the commit message carries the measurement in a GREPPABLE form — two lines matching
      `runner.py before: <N>` and `runner.py after: <M>`, with M < N and M < 700. Verify with:
      `git log -1 --format=%B <sha> | grep -E 'runner\.py (before|after): [0-9]+'`
      (an outcome a reviewer can check from the artifact, not an unverifiable process step).
      TAGGED [operator-attested] because the evidence lives in GIT HISTORY, which the completion
      verifier cannot read - it has repository FILE tools only. docs/plan-review-gate.md's
      operator-attested lint exists for exactly this class and warns it "makes the completion
      verifier hunt for code proof that cannot exist and burn a close-gate cycle". It did not fire
      here because naming a proving command (`git log ... | grep ...`) trips the lint's
      codebase-verifiable SUPPRESSION co-signal - git history reads as in-repo but is not.
      The machine-enforced half of this measurement is the SEPARATE criterion above (wc -l < 700),
      which the verifier CAN and DID confirm at 647.
- [ ] the seam guard actually covers the new move: `build_model_settings` and `build_usage_limits`
      are added to BOTH hardcoded symbol lists in `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py` — the
      `for name in (...)` tuple in `test_moved_symbols_are_importable_from_the_new_module` and the
      `defined & {...}` set literal in `test_runner_no_longer_defines_the_moved_symbols`. Without
      this the guard silently passes while asserting nothing about either new function
- [ ] `python -c "from rebar.llm.structured_run import build_model_settings, build_usage_limits"`
      succeeds, and neither name is still defined in runner.py (the moved-not-copied contrast)
- [ ] any monkeypatch target that moved is repointed IN THE SAME COMMIT and named in the message
baseline.summary: Extract build_model_settings() and build_usage_limits()

## Why

The live e2e probe encoded the inbound-comment bug as EXPECTED behavior (`Phase3.verify-inbound-comments-gap … NOT-SYNCED`, and would have FAILED if comments synced), so the defect was undetectable; no probe round-trips relationships at all; and the probes are manual, not in CI. A probe that locks a bug in as "expected" is worse than no probe.

## What

- A **hermetic bidirectional round-trip assertion** — using story A's fixtures/fake through the production path — for comments, issue-links (both directions), and parent, runnable in CI without live Jira.
- **De-encode the "expected-bug" guards**: convert probe assertions that lock in a current gap (e.g. `Phase3.verify-inbound-comments-gap NOT-SYNCED`) into `xfail`/fail-when-the-gap-closes, so a fix is detected rather than rejected. Audit `scripts/jira-pressure-test/*.sh` for every `NOT-SYNCED`/"as expected" guard.
- A documented (optionally scheduled) live round-trip variant for the directions that truly need real Jira, kept off the default suite so it never flakes CI.

## Scope

- In: the hermetic round-trip test; the probe de-encoding audit; the live-variant doc.
- Out: the producer↔consumer schema/contract (story B).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A hermetic test asserts bidirectional round-trip of comments, links, and parent through the production path (no live Jira needed).
- [ ] Every probe assertion that encodes a current bug as "expected/NOT-SYNCED" is converted to fail-when-the-gap-closes (xfail) or removed; none silently passes on a defect.
- [ ] The hermetic round-trip runs in CI; any live variant is opt-in/scheduled and documented.
- [ ] Assertions check round-trip outcomes, not whole-blob equality (anti-change-detector).
baseline.summary: Honest bidirectional round-trip probe; de-encode 'expected-bug' guards

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The close-reason and force plumbing is computed independently on each surface: the "reason persists only on a REASON_REQUIRED class without force" rule lives at `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:584`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:318`, and `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:357-362`; the `"(no reason given)"` placeholder at `transition.py:388`, `claim.py:38`, `_lib_writes.py:412`; one datum travels as `force_reason` → `force_close` → `force_close_reason` across three files. The CLI refuses an inadmissible reason while the library silently discards it, and MCP `transition_ticket` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:224-232`) does not expose `reason` at all — the strict-xfail row in `tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py:34-35,193` (bug `scratchy-leprous-galago`). Bug `defiant-orthoclase-buck` was the datum accepted under one name and never read.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_commands/transition_request.py` with a frozen `TransitionRequest(ticket_id, current, target, close_class, reason, force, caused_by, ref)` exposing `force_note`, `close_reason`, and `reason_refusal()`. All three surfaces construct it; `txn.transition_core` and `close_ticket` read the properties. MCP `transition_ticket` gains `reason` by constructing the same object, which flips the strict-xfail to a pass and forces its removal. Guard: the placeholder literal and the REASON_REQUIRED admission test appear only in `transition_request.py`.


## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_commands/transition_request.py` (new), `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py`, `tests/unit/commands/test_transition_request.py` (new).

## Testing
Happy path: each surface closing a REASON_REQUIRED class with a reason persists it. Edge: a reason on a non-reason class is refused identically on CLI, lib, and MCP (the parity oracle row). Pinning: `tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`, `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py`, `tests/unit/test_administrative_close_dispositions.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` pass unchanged except the removed xfail marker.


## The `(no reason given)` oracle, corrected (review remediation)
The earlier AC-2 demanded `grep -rn "no reason given" src/rebar` return exactly ONE file. That cannot pass, and should not: the literal occurs **15 times across 5 files**, and only **5 are code** —
- code: `_lib_writes.py:247`, `_lib_writes.py:412`, `_commands/transition.py:396`,
  `_commands/claim.py:43`, `_commands/claim.py:46`
- prose: `_deprecations.py:100` (a comment), `_lib_writes.py:235,238,278,385`,
  `transition.py:65,264,343,390` (docstrings and help text that legitimately NAME the value
  they document).

A guard that forbade documentation from naming the placeholder would be deleted the first time someone wrote a docstring. So the construct is the **production of the value**, not the mention of it: the placeholder becomes a single named constant on the value object (`TransitionRequest.NO_REASON_GIVEN`), and the guard asserts the string LITERAL is assigned in exactly one place under `src/rebar`, with a `# force-reason-ok: <why>` escape. Docstrings and comments are out of the scan by construction (the scan looks for the literal in an assignment or return expression, not anywhere in the line), so prose stays free.

`src/rebar/_commands/claim.py` IS added to Scope (two code sites above). `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` is NOT added to Scope: its occurrence is a comment, and under the corrected oracle it needs no change.

## Convergence decision (REQUIRED before implementation)
The three copies are not interchangeable and **no merge leaves every pinning test green**. For an inadmissible reason the CLI **refuses** (exit 1, `transition.py:569-587`; pinned by `test_administrative_close_dispositions.py:343,:352`) while the library **silently discards** it (returns 0, `_lib_writes.py:314-337`; pinned by `test_library_close_reason_is_gated_on_the_admitting_class:262-289`).

**Decision: converge on REFUSE.** Accepting a datum and never reading it is the exact defect class of bug `defiant-orthoclase-buck` (`txn.py:263-273`), which this ticket's Context cites. The library therefore gains a rejection it did not have, and `test_library_close_reason_is_gated_on_the_admitting_class` is updated to assert the refusal instead of the silent discard — a **sanctioned assertion edit**, recorded here under the parent epic's convergence clause rather than made silently.

The library also gains the CLI's `target_status == "closed"` term, absent from `admits_close_reason` and today saved only by a downstream guard (`txn.py:280-281`).

## Traps the implementation must not spring
1. **Never let the `(no reason given)` placeholder reach `close_disposition.verdict`.** It fails
   closed on an empty reason (`close_disposition.py:200-201`); a normalised placeholder there turns
   an UNJUSTIFIED disposition into a SIGNED one.
2. **Do not move the `""`->placeholder normalisation relative to the refusal check.** A bare
   `--force` yields `force_reason=""`, which is FALSY at `txn.py:232`; it works only because
   `_force_note` normalises before `close_ticket`. A lazy `force_note` flips a bare-force close
   from accepted to refused.
3. **`close_reason`, `force_note` and `reason_refusal()` stay three INDEPENDENT accessors.** Force
   DISQUALIFIES the reason upstream but SATISFIES the reason-requirement at `txn.py:232`.
4. **`_lib_writes.transition(force_close=)` is a deprecated PUBLIC alias**; `close_ticket(force_close=)`
   is an internal hop name. Same spelling, unrelated — a mechanical rename retires the shim.
5. Three tests pin NAMES/SOURCE TEXT and break on a signature change alone:
   `test_transition_core_does_not_accept_a_parameter_it_discards` (inspect.getsource),
   `test_adapter_bound_internals_are_not_contract_params`, and the
   `transition.transition_compute` spy reading `kwargs["close_reason"]`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One `TransitionRequest` carries the close-reason/force rule for CLI, library and MCP; checked by the guard test and the pinning suites.
- [ ] The `"(no reason given)"` placeholder is PRODUCED in exactly one place: a single named constant on the value object, with every one of the five current code sites (`_lib_writes.py:247,412`, `_commands/transition.py:396`, `_commands/claim.py:43,46`) reading it; checked by a guard asserting the string literal appears in exactly one PRODUCING expression under (assignment, return OR call-argument — `_lib_writes.py:412` produces it as a keyword-argument value, which an assignment/return-only scan misses) `src/rebar`, owner-exempt, with a `# force-reason-ok: <why>` escape whose reason is mandatory. **Docstrings, comments and help text that NAME the placeholder are explicitly out of the scan and must keep working** — there are ten such mentions and forbidding them would get the guard deleted.
- [ ] Pinning suites pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest` and `git diff --stat`.
- [ ] The library refuses an inadmissible reason exactly as the CLI does, and MCP does too; checked by the write-parity oracle with the `reason-close-obsolete` row passing on all three adapters and its strict-xfail marker deleted.
- [ ] A bare `--force` close of a reason-required class is still ACCEPTED; checked by a test driving `--class=obsolete --force` with no value.
- [ ] The placeholder never reaches `close_disposition.verdict`; checked by a test asserting an empty reason still yields no signed disposition.
baseline.summary: TransitionRequest value object: one close-reason/force rule across CLI, library and MCP

## Context / Problem
Every rebar LLM operation (review-plan, verify-completion, gated close) fails with "no AWS region could be resolved" in any shell where only AWS_REGION is exported — the standard region variable modern AWS tooling sets (CLI v2 docs, SDKs) and what operators export in their shell profiles. Observed 2026-08-14: a login shell exports AWS_REGION=us-west-2; every subagent/tool shell inherits it; rebar's bedrock provider still refuses to run until REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION is manually injected per command.

Root cause: `build_bedrock_provider` (src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:99) passes only `cfg.bedrock_region_name` to `boto3.session.Session(region_name=...)` and otherwise delegates region resolution entirely to botocore, and botocore 1.43.62 does not consult AWS_REGION (measured; pinned by tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:704 `test_aws_region_alone_resolves_nothing_and_still_raises`). Effective order today: REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION -> AWS_DEFAULT_REGION (via botocore) -> profile config; AWS_REGION is never consulted. The error message (bedrock_model.py:110-118) documents the trap in a long "AWS_REGION alone does NOT resolve" paragraph instead of closing it. Correction to this plan's earlier draft: provider provenance records NO region today for ANY source — `provenance_for` (src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:554) has no region field, so this fix ADDS region recording rather than extending an existing one.

## Approach
Close the trap in rebar's own layer instead of waiting on botocore: a small pure resolver plus an explicit `region_name=` to the boto3 session makes botocore's AWS_REGION quirk irrelevant, preserves the no-invented-default-region policy, and gives provenance one source of truth.

1. New pure function `resolve_bedrock_region(bedrock_region_name: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]` in src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py returning `(region, source)`. Chain and the EXACT `source` string returned (and recorded verbatim as `region_source`): configured `bedrock_region_name` (REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION / `[tool.rebar.llm].bedrock_region_name`) -> `"REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION"`; env AWS_DEFAULT_REGION -> `"AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"`; env AWS_REGION -> `"AWS_REGION"`; nothing set -> `(None, None)`, meaning boto3's own resolution (active profile) applies, unchanged. Worked example: with AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=eu-west-1 and AWS_REGION=us-west-2 both set and no rebar knob, the resolver returns `("eu-west-1", "AWS_DEFAULT_REGION")`. Empty-string env values are treated as unset (botocore parity).
2. `build_bedrock_provider` calls it and passes the resolved region explicitly to `boto3.session.Session(region_name=...)`. The existing no-region LLMConfigError precheck stays, but its message is rewritten to name the full chain (REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION > AWS_DEFAULT_REGION > AWS_REGION > profile) and DROP the now-moot AWS_REGION-does-not-work paragraph; the IMDS note stays. Docstring MEASURED paragraphs are updated the same way.
3. Provenance: `provenance_for` (src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:554) gains an optional `bedrock_region_name` kwarg; when `provider == "bedrock"` it calls `resolve_bedrock_region` (lazy import; pure and stdlib-only — no boto3 enters this signed-record path) and, when the chain resolves, records additive keys `region` + `region_source` in `provider_provenance`. Both keys are absent when boto3's ambient profile resolution applies — rebar cannot observe that value at this seam without importing boto3, and synthesising it would place an unverified fact into a signed record (same rule as `endpoint_host`). The runner call site (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:450) threads `bedrock_region_name=cfg.bedrock_region_name` (+1 line; runner.py is 796 lines against the 800 cap — verified it fits, and no new branch lands there so the C901 ratchet is untouched).
4. Docs: docs/llm-framework.md:191-197 region bullet + :390 env-table row, docs/local-dev-env.md:288 region bullet. Infra runbooks keep their dated MEASURED records (historical evidence, still true of botocore).

Riskiest assumption: passing `region_name=` explicitly bypasses botocore's AWS_REGION quirk. Cheapest falsifier first: the spy-session mechanism already proves `Session(region_name=...)` reaches the client (tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:773), and the new AWS_REGION-alone test is written RED-first against current behavior before any src change.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py — resolver, explicit region_name, new error text, docstrings
- src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py — provenance_for records region + region_source
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py — thread cfg.bedrock_region_name into provenance_for (+1 line)
- tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py — precedence test, AWS_REGION-alone-now-works (rewrites the 4e71 oracle at :704, which pins the old raise), error-message assertions
- tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py — region/region_source recording + absence cases
- docs/llm-framework.md, docs/local-dev-env.md — region guidance

## Testing
Withheld-oracle TDD: each new test is written and shown RED against the unfixed tree first.
- Happy path: with only AWS_REGION=us-west-2 (AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION unset; spy boto3 session), `build_bedrock_provider` builds and the session receives `region_name="us-west-2"` (checked via the existing `_spy_boto_session` recorder).
- Precedence: one test sets all three sources to distinct regions and strips them pairwise, pinning REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION beats AWS_DEFAULT_REGION beats AWS_REGION.
- Failure path: no region anywhere still raises LLMConfigError; the message names all of REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_REGION, and no longer contains the stale "does NOT resolve" guidance (asserted on the message).
- Provenance: `provenance_for(provider="bedrock", ...)` records region + region_source per source; both keys absent for non-bedrock providers and when nothing in rebar's chain resolves.
- Ambient-profile fallback: the existing `test_an_ambient_boto3_region_is_still_honoured` stays green (no invented default).
- Mutation testing on `resolve_bedrock_region` (hand-mutants: reorder the chain, drop a var, invert empty-string handling, swap a source label); kill rate reported as a ticket comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] With only AWS_REGION set, `build_bedrock_provider` resolves that region and passes it explicitly to the boto3 session; checked by the new spy-session unit test in tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py.
- [x] Resolution order pinned by a passing precedence test: REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION > AWS_DEFAULT_REGION > AWS_REGION > profile fallback (ambient-profile test still green).
- [x] Resolved region + region_source recorded in `provider_provenance` for bedrock runs when rebar's chain resolves; absent otherwise; checked by new tests in tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py.
- [x] The no-region error message names the full chain and the stale AWS_REGION warning is gone (message-assertion test); docs/llm-framework.md and docs/local-dev-env.md region guidance updated to match.
- [x] Hand-mutant kill rate on `resolve_bedrock_region` reported as a ticket comment; target 100%.
- [x] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean (CI gate ran them on the merged change).
- [x] [operator-attested] Lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
  provenance: environment=Gerrit+GitHub Actions; principal=session operator (git-credential REST); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — /a/changes/1798/detail showed LLM-Review +1, Verified +1; MERGED as 951fda9448 on origin/main.
baseline.summary: Bedrock region resolution ignores AWS_REGION, the standard env var operators actually set

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:94-112` schedules three public removals: the Python-library `rebar.transition(force_close=...)` keyword, boolean `rebar.transition(force=True)`, and explicit hosted-OpenAI `openai-chat:` model selection. Closed migration `blusterous-earthly-kitten` established the temporary warning mappings; this ticket is the scheduled retirement, not a duplicate. These registry-adjacent removals are intentionally one pre-1.0 release increment: one compatibility deadline, one breaking-change notice, and separate subsystem-specific test coverage.

## End State

The Python library accepts only a reason-bearing string `force="<reason>"`. `force_close` or boolean `force=True` fail at the library boundary with `force="<reason>"` named as the replacement. Hosted model selection accepts `openai-responses:<model>`. Both live hosted-resolution paths reject explicit `openai-chat:`. Custom OpenAI-compatible `base_url` selection retains its Chat Completions dialect.

## Implementation Plan

1. Retire library mappings in `_lib_writes` plus `_deprecations`. Do not add an environment or configuration tombstone: these are callable inputs, so validation belongs at the Python boundary.
2. Regenerate the API snapshot plus MCP-library parity manifest after the library signature changes.
3. Retire hosted explicit `openai-chat:` in `_resolve_target` plus `_pai_model`/`_openai_wire_prefix`. Preserve custom-endpoint routing. Migrate hosted `gpt-5.4*` inventory to `openai-responses:`.
4. Retarget each test that currently preserves hosted `openai-chat:` to a hosted rejection assertion. Retain each custom-endpoint Chat assertion.
5. Regenerate `docs/config-reference.md` via `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`. Migrate all maintained hosted examples plus workflow-schema descriptions to `openai-responses:`.
6. Replace the two legacy warn-and-map tests in `test_force_unification_blusterous.py` with rejection tests. Retarget each behavior-preserving caller in `test_completion_gate.py`, `test_ac_checkbox_precheck_heldout.py`, `test_attestations_integration.py`, `test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py`, `test_attested_close_guard_e2e.py`, and `test_transition_open_children.py` to `force="<reason>"`.
7. Update maintained release/API guidance. Preserve historical `force_close_reason` durable state.

## File Impact

- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — retired library inputs
- `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`, `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` — generated public signature snapshot
- `tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json`, `scripts/check_mcp_library_parity.py` — retired library-only parity divergence
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py`, `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`, `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml` — hosted resolution plus deployed model inventory
- `tests/unit/test_openai_responses_migration.py`, `test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, `test_llm_capabilities.py`, `test_model_classes.py`, `test_openai_compatible_provider.py`, `test_provider_qualifier.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py` — hosted rejection plus custom-endpoint preservation
- `docs/config-reference.md`, `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` — cfg-kind output
- `docs/llm-example-configs.md`, `docs/workflow-authoring-v2.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, `src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v1.schema.json`, `workflow.v2.schema.json`, `workflow.v3.schema.json` — maintained hosted examples
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_force_unification_blusterous.py`, `test_completion_gate.py`, `test_ac_checkbox_precheck_heldout.py`, `test_attestations_integration.py`, `test_plan_review_close_gate_lifecycle.py`, `test_attested_close_guard_e2e.py`, `test_transition_open_children.py` — rejection migration plus canonical callers
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md` — breaking-release guidance

## Acceptance Criteria
