## Goal

Remove the legacy `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` CLI/direct-engine command and its `.bridge_state/reconcile-check.json` status artifact without breaking the canonical bridge surfaces that replaced its observables.

Replacement is distributed:
- `rebar bridge preview` is the live Jira-vs-local differ/proposed-change observable.
- `rebar bridge fsck --output json` is the offline orphan/unbound/binding-drift audit observable.
- `rebar bridge status --json` remains the status surface, but no longer reads stale `reconcile-check.json`.

Preserve `_ref_lock.py` pause sentinel `gated_mode == "reconcile-check"`: it is read back at runtime via `Mode.from_str` in `_advisory_lock._mode_blocks`, so `Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK` MUST stay in the enum/`_ORDERED` or a paused repo silently stops blocking. Remove only the CLI command, not the internal mode.

## Scope

- `_bridge_runner.py`: repoint retained `reconcile-check` profile to `rebar bridge preview`, not fsck.
- `_cli/_registry.py`, `_cli/_parsers/advanced/reconcile.py`, `_cli/help/reconcile.txt`: remove top-level `rebar reconcile`, `--mode reconcile-check`, and `--filter-local-ids` CLI surface.
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`: delete `_run_reconcile_check`, its JSON writer, dispatch branch, and CLI-only `filter_local_ids` handoff.
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py`: remove legacy-route parsing; keep canonical `preview`/`sync`.
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py`: RETAIN `Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK` + its `_ORDERED`/`MODE_CAPS` entries (load-bearing for the advisory-lock pause gate via `Mode.from_str("reconcile-check")`); only revise the docstring wording that describes it as the removed CLI command.
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_preflight.py`: remove reconcile-check no-write logic/wording.
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py`: remove `_read_reconcile_diagnostics()` and `snapshot()["reconcile_diagnostics"]`.
- `_mcp_models.py`, `schemas/bridge_status.schema.json`, `types.py`: remove `reconcile_diagnostics` from BridgeStatus model/schema/types so MCP no longer advertises a producerless field.
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_check.py`: delete orphaned legacy report module.
- Update stale reconcile-check wording in `binding_recovery.py`, `binding_walk.py`, `fetcher.py`, `get_rotation.py`, `load_phase.py`, `pass_support.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, and `ticket_planner.py`.
- Update workflow/probe/docs/changelog references that instruct `reconcile-check`, using preview for live discrepancy checks and fsck for offline orphan/unbound audits.
- Tests (enum retained, so all `Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK` references stay valid — only removed-symbol consumers change): DELETE the `reconcile_check.py`-module tests `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_check{,_canonical,_canonical_heldout,_bindings_dict}.py` (they exercise the removed `_run_reconcile_check`/`reconcile_check.reconcile_check()`); migrate `test_reconcile_filter.py` (drop `--filter-local-ids` `main()` parsing; keep engine plumbing). Grep the reconciler test tree for the removed symbols and fix any remaining consumer (leave enum/sentinel references intact). Add BridgeStatus model/schema-parity + preview-probe coverage. `make test` is an AC.

## Design Decisions

1. `bridge fsck` is not the sole replacement: it is offline and exits 1 on findings, whereas legacy reconcile-check exited 0.
2. `_bridge_runner.MODE_COMMANDS["reconcile-check"]` maps to `rebar bridge preview`, whose canonical route emits JSON on stdout and `BRIDGE_STATE: <state>` on stderr with 0/1/2 exit semantics.
3. After `_run_reconcile_check` is deleted, no canonical writer refreshes `.bridge_state/reconcile-check.json`; remove all status/model/schema readers instead of creating a new writer.
4. Remove `BridgeStatusOut.reconcile_diagnostics` in `_mcp_models.py`; schema drift will not catch an extra permissive model field, so add explicit MCP/schema parity coverage.
5. Pressure probes must stop grepping legacy prose (`0 discrepancies`, `discrepancy`, `mismatch`). Run canonical `preview --only ... --repo-root ...`, preserve the exit code, parse the final stdout JSON, and pass only when `route=="preview"`, `mutation_count==0`, and `plan` contains no entry for the probe key/local id.
6. Keep `_ref_lock.py` pause sentinel `reconcile-check` byte-for-byte, AND keep `Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK` in the enum/`_ORDERED`/`MODE_CAPS`: the sentinel is decoded back through `Mode.from_str` by `_advisory_lock._mode_blocks`, so removing the enum would make `from_str("reconcile-check")` raise and the pause gate fail open.
7. Do not remove dead internal `filter_local_ids` plumbing beyond CLI surface; follow-up `f8c4-ac9b-42c5-4bb0` owns that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_mode.py` proves `Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK` + its `_ORDERED`/`MODE_CAPS` entries are RETAINED and `Mode.from_str("reconcile-check")` still round-trips (pause gate intact); ordering works.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py` proves `--mode reconcile-check` rejects and `_run_reconcile_check` is not dispatched.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py tests/unit/workflow/test_bridge_provider_wrappers_heldout.py` proves the retained runner profile invokes `bridge preview`, not fsck, and preserves delivery semantics.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_binding_drift.py` proves orphaned bindings/Jira and unbound local/Jira remain in `bridge fsck --output json`.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_status_heldout.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_status_relocated_store.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic_heldout.py tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_model_schema_drift_heldout.py` proves BridgeStatus library/MCP/schema/types no longer expose `reconcile_diagnostics`.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/scripts/test_jira_pressure_probe_preview_assertions_heldout.py` proves both pressure probes migrated from legacy prose greps to preview JSON assertions on `route`, `mutation_count`, and absence of probe targets in `plan`.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_ref_backend.py` proves pause documents still preserve `gated_mode == "reconcile-check"`.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_reconcile_check_cli_removal_heldout.py` proves removed CLI spelling is rejected and remaining `reconcile-check` hits are only pause-sentinel or historical/changelog references.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` passes.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test` passes.

## Testing

Held-out oracles: `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_reconcile_check_cli_removal_heldout.py` (CLI-removal + residual-hit audit) and `tests/scripts/test_jira_pressure_probe_preview_assertions_heldout.py` (both probes migrated per Design Decision 5: scoped `preview --only ...` JSON parsing on `route`/`mutation_count`/`plan`, exit code preserved, no legacy prose greps). All proving commands are enumerated under Acceptance Criteria.

## Out of scope

- Do not edit `_lib_ops.py` or `_mcp_reads.py`; c195 already removed Python/MCP `rebar.reconcile(mode=...)`.
- Do not remove engine `filter_local_ids` plumbing beyond CLI surface; `f8c4-ac9b-42c5-4bb0` owns it.
- Do not change `_ref_lock.py` pause sentinel bytes/schema.
- Do not change canonical preview/sync/fsck/status semantics except removing stale status diagnostics.
- Do not run plan-review, claim, close, or force any ticket for this work.

## Context / Problem

The multi-project model changes things a reader currently learns from the docs as single-project facts: `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:74` presents `project` as one config line and has no section on multiple projects, `docs/config.md:216-260` documents the `[jira]` block as a single scalar project, and `docs/migrations.md` describes the ensure registry without the two units this epic adds. A user upgrading a client store also needs to know what the new `required_capabilities` entry means for older binaries in their fleet. None of that is documented by the implementation stories, which own code and tests only.

## Approach

Document the shipped behaviour and record the architectural decision. The ADR is warranted rather than decorative because two decisions here are load-bearing, non-obvious, and expensive to reverse: that the project set is a property of the **store** rather than of a repo, and that the legacy migration writes **no ticket events**. Both were chosen against plausible alternatives — per-repo project lists and an EDIT-per-ticket backfill — and a future reader who does not know why will be tempted back toward them.

The ADR is `docs/adr/0062-*` — the next number after `0061-measurement-provenance-in-attested-evidence.md`. It records the shared-`prev_snapshot` reasoning for store ownership, the short-lock-budget reasoning for the event-free migration, and the conditional-stamp reasoning for compatibility. It also notes the relationship to ADR 0060, whose churn constraint the mapping satisfies by construction.

Documentation updates cover the mapping and its `bridge projects` verb, the tri-state project field, the repos field, the two ensure units, and the upgrade note for fleets running mixed binary versions.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0062-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` (new)
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
- `docs/config.md`
- `docs/migrations.md`
- `docs/user-guide.md`
- `docs/ticket-model.md`

## Testing

No `## Testing` section beyond this note: this story adds no testable behaviour — it is documentation and an ADR, which `rebar explain plan` names as a legitimately test-free change class. Verification is by the repository's existing documentation gates rather than by new tests, and the acceptance criteria below name the command that checks each claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0062-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` exists and records the store-ownership,
      event-free-migration, and conditional-stamp decisions with their rejected alternatives; checked
      by reading the file and confirming each of the three decisions names what it was chosen over.
- [ ] The Jira sync and config docs describe the project mapping and no longer present a single
      scalar project as the only option; checked by confirming no remaining passage states the
      single-project constraint as current behaviour.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` lists both new ensure units alongside the existing built-ins; checked by
      confirming each registered id appears in the doc.
- [ ] The docs state what the `multi-project-bridge` capability means for an older binary and what an
      operator does about it; checked by confirming the upgrade note names both the fail-closed
      behaviour and the remedy.
- [ ] The generated CLI reference includes `bridge projects`; checked by running the repository's
      documentation generation and confirming the verb appears without a manual edit.
baseline.summary: Document the multi-project model and record ADR 0062

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Stores that already exist — including client deployments, not just this one — have no `.bridge_state/projects.json` and no `bridge_project` on any ticket. Without a migration those stores would read every ticket as having an absent project, and there would be no recorded legacy default for the resolver to fall back to, so a store that syncs perfectly today would stop syncing on upgrade.

## Approach

Ship the migration as ensure units on the existing idempotent registry (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `REGISTRY_IDS` at `:66`, `_registry()` at `:82`), which is rebar's sanctioned seam: `docs/migrations.md:40-56` describes adding a unit, and the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built (`docs/migrations.md:14-16`). Units run at init/re-init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot (`docs/migrations.md:57-65`), so a client store converges without any operator action.

**The migration writes no ticket events.** A unit emitting an EDIT per ticket would be a four-figure event write under the store write lock on a store this size, and the MCP-boot entry point runs the sweep on a deliberately short lock budget and skips when contended (`docs/migrations.md:63-65`) — so an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points and converge unpredictably. Instead the unit records `legacy_default` once in the mapping, and the tri-state resolver treats every ticket with an absent field as belonging to it. One small write migrates the whole store.

Two units, both check-then-act and both safe to re-run:

1. **Seed the mapping.** If `.bridge_state/projects.json` is absent, write it with `legacy_default`
   and a single `projects` entry taken from the backend's configured project
   (`Backend.project`, documented as the effective write/create scope at `_backend.py:610-632`). If
   the record already exists, return `ok` and write nothing. Tree-check before committing so a
   converged store makes zero git commits, as `docs/migrations.md:45-46` requires of commit units.
2. **Stamp the capability.** When — and only when — the mapping holds more than one project, add
   `multi-project-bridge` to `.store-compat.json`'s `required_capabilities`. A single-project store is
   never stamped and stays usable by older binaries.

Ids are new and never reused, per `docs/migrations.md:50-51`.

**Where the unit bodies live.** The existing six units are implemented in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (for example `_store_compat_unit` at `:528`) and referenced from `_registry()` (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:93`). This story deliberately does **not** follow that placement: at the time of writing `_commands/init.py` measures 799 lines against the repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so adding two unit bodies there would fail CI on a limit that has no allowlist escape hatch. Because `_registry()` maps an id to any callable, the two new units live in their own `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` and are referenced from `ensures.py` — which is 253 lines and gains only its two registry entries. This keeps the change inside the gate without refactoring an unrelated 799-line module as a precondition.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` (new) — both unit bodies
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — two `REGISTRY_IDS` entries and two `_registry()` mappings
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's git row — real temporary git repositories and refs — because the units commit to the `tickets` branch and the zero-commit-when-converged property is only observable against real refs.

- Happy path: sweeping a store with no mapping creates one whose `legacy_default` equals the
  configured backend project, and every existing ticket resolves to it.
- The load-bearing assertion: the sweep writes **zero ticket events**. Assert the store's event count
  and the set of event files are identical before and after — this is what distinguishes this design
  from an EDIT-per-ticket migration.
- Idempotence: a second sweep on a converged store returns `ok` for both units and makes zero new git
  commits (assert the branch tip SHA is unchanged, not merely that no error was raised).
- Conditional stamp, as a contrast pair: a one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; a
  two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge`. The one-project half proves the stamp is
  genuinely conditional rather than unconditional.
- Failure path: a unit raising is recorded as `failed` and does not abort the sweep or the caller, per
  the registry's skip-and-continue contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A store with no mapping gains one whose legacy default is the configured backend project, and
      every pre-existing ticket resolves to it; checked by a real-git test asserting the record and
      the resolution.
- [ ] The sweep writes zero ticket events; checked by asserting the event file set is identical
      before and after.
- [ ] A second sweep returns `ok` for both units and leaves the tickets-branch tip SHA unchanged;
      checked by comparing the SHA across two sweeps.
- [ ] The capability is stamped only when the mapping holds more than one project; checked by a
      paired test over a one-project and a two-project mapping.
- [ ] Both unit ids are registered in `REGISTRY_IDS` and mapped in `_registry()`; checked by the
      existing registry-agreement test, which fails if they disagree.
baseline.summary: Legacy-store migration: ensure units seeding the project mapping without writing ticket events

baseline.description:
## Summary

Characterize — and, only if a gap is confirmed, detect — the **refusal-as-content** failure mode in rebar's LLM structured-output path: a provider content-policy refusal returned as a normal-looking TEXT/verdict rather than raising, so an LLM gate (review / verify-completion / plan-review) could read a refusal as a valid result.

## Why (background)

pydantic-ai **#5221** (+ fix PR **#6167**) reports that a content-policy refusal can come back as a plain text part with `response.status='incomplete'` / `incomplete_details.reason= 'content_filter'` and NO structured refusal object. pydantic-ai's own agent loop only raises `ContentFilterError` when the parts are **empty**, so a refusal-as-content (non-empty `TextPart`) is returned to the caller as normal output.

**Note on provider:** #5221 is about **OpenAI** (`finish_reason='content_filter'`), not Anthropic — this ticket's title conflates them. rebar runs Anthropic (`claude-*`), where the analogous signal is `stop_reason="refusal"` (see `src/rebar/llm/errors.py:40`, `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:231`). The failure *shape* (a refusal surfaced as content) is provider-independent; the characterization must confirm which signals Anthropic-via-pydantic-ai actually emits for a refusal.

**rebar already has a partial defense** (from closed story 978d, `jade`-adjacent silent-success work): `structured.check_stop_reason(stop_reason)` (`src/rebar/llm/structured.py:249`) raises `UnretryableOutputError` on `{refusal, max_tokens, length, content_filter}`, and the runner calls it on BOTH output paths (`runner.py:519` PromptedOutput, `runner.py:539` NativeOutput) reading `run_result.response.finish_reason`. So IF pydantic-ai reliably surfaces `finish_reason`/`stop_reason` for a refusal-as-content turn, rebar already fails closed. The open question this ticket answers is whether that signal is reliably present, or whether a refusal can slip through with an unset/`stop` finish_reason.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Construct (or capture via a cassette) a pydantic-ai `ModelResponse` representing an
   Anthropic refusal-as-content turn: a non-empty `TextPart` carrying refusal prose. Vary the
   `finish_reason`/`stop_reason` across `{"refusal", None, "stop", "content_filter"}`.
2. Drive it through rebar's structured path (`runner.py` NativeOutput + PromptedOutput →
   `structured.check_stop_reason`) for a gated op (e.g. `verify_completion`).
3. Observe whether rebar RAISES (`UnretryableOutputError`) or returns the refusal prose as a
   (hollow but valid-looking) verdict.

- **Expected:** any refusal-as-content turn fails closed — rebar raises a typed refusal error
  and never returns the refusal as a usable verdict/review result.
- **Actual (to be characterized):** unknown. If `finish_reason` is reliably `refusal`/
  `content_filter`, `check_stop_reason` already catches it (no gap). If a refusal can arrive
  with `finish_reason` unset/`stop`, the refusal prose is returned as content — the #5221 gap
  reproduced in rebar.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Characterized:** a documented determination (a comment/artifact on this ticket, plus a
  reproduction test) of whether rebar's structured path is vulnerable to refusal-as-content —
  i.e., whether a refusal turn can be returned as a non-empty valid-looking result that
  `check_stop_reason` does NOT catch. Cites pydantic-ai #5221 / #6167 and the exact rebar code
  path (`structured.check_stop_reason`, `runner.py:519/539`).
- [ ] **If a gap is confirmed:** add a content-level guard (in `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`
  and/or `runner.py`) that recognizes a refusal-as-content response **independent of
  finish_reason** and raises the existing `UnretryableOutputError` (fail-closed), so a refusal
  can never be returned as a valid verdict/review. Covered by a unit test that simulates a
  refusal-as-content `ModelResponse` with an unset finish_reason and asserts it raises.
- [ ] **If NO gap** (the finish_reason/stop_reason signal is reliably present for our provider
  and `check_stop_reason` already fails closed): document why, add a **regression test** that
  pins that a refusal-as-content turn raises (so a future pydantic-ai/provider change can't
  silently reopen the gap), and close as characterized-not-vulnerable.
- [ ] File paths: `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`, `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`,
  `src/rebar/llm/errors.py`; tests under `tests/unit/`.

## Notes / decisions to confirm on review

- Desired posture is **fail-closed** (a refusal → typed error, never a PASS) per the user's
  earlier direction. Confirm this over warn-only or retry.
- Scope is the structured/verdict path (the LLM gates). Non-structured/free-text LLM calls (if
  any) are out of scope unless the characterization shows they share the defect.
baseline.summary: Characterize + detect refusal-as-content in the structured-output path (pydantic-ai #5221)

# Add deterministic public-exposure signals to the code-review security overlay (publicly-exposed-without-auth)

## Context
Follow-up to a278. Plan-review reasons over PROSE, so it cannot do true reachability analysis; the
deterministic "is this publicly exposed?" signals belong to the **code-review** gate, which sees the
actual `*.tf` / docker-compose diff. This adds tfsec/Checkov-**aligned** detectors that flag a network
service exposed to untrusted networks — the code-level counterpart to a278's T10 plan-level
`endpoint_access_contract`.

## Design decisions (resolving the review BLOCK)
- **Native opengrep rules, tfsec/Checkov-ALIGNED (not integrated).** There is no tfsec/Checkov
  integration seam in the grounding layer (the `sarif` backend is hardwired to gitleaks). So the
  detectors are authored as native opengrep rules under
  `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/builtin/security_iac_public_exposure.yaml`, each citing the
  equivalent tfsec / Checkov rule id in its message/metadata (e.g. tfsec `aws-vpc-no-public-ingress-sgr`,
  Checkov `CKV_AWS_260`). opengrep runs via the `semgrep` fallback binary already on PATH.
- **Deny-by-default EXPOSURE signal, NOT a deterministic auth-correlation.** A single opengrep rule
  cannot reliably prove "no authenticating gateway fronts this" (the gateway/mesh/network-policy may
  live outside the diff). So the detector fires on the deterministic EXPOSURE signal only and its
  message states the deny-by-default obligation ("public exposure — verify an authenticating gateway /
  mTLS / network policy fronts this"). Auth-absence is the reviewer's judgement, cued by the finding,
  not a separate deterministic match.
- **ADVISORY, not a hard block (new dedicated `exec: "DET"` criterion).** The detectors are filed under
  a NEW criterion `public-exposure-without-auth` with its own detector id-prefix
  (`rebar.builtin.iac.public-exposure.`), NOT under the fail-closed `high-critical-security` prefix.
  Posture is `blocking_enabled: false` / `fail_mode: "open"`: a match is surfaced as an advisory
  coverage finding, never an auto-BLOCK — so "boundary controls outside the diff" are weighed by the
  reviewer, and FP-guarded cases are "lower severity, not a hard block", exactly as the AC requires.
- **FP guards are pattern exclusions.** The rules match only unambiguous public exposure literals
  (`0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`, `associate_public_ip_address = true`, `internal = false` on an `aws_lb`, a
  `0.0.0.0:` host-published compose port). Private-CIDR (`10.0.0.0/8`, `192.168.0.0/16`), loopback
  (`127.0.0.1`), unix-socket, and `internal = true` do NOT match — so they are never flagged.
- **engine_b applicability fix (mandatory).** `engine_b._LANG_EXTENSIONS` has no `terraform`/`yaml`
  entry, so a detector declaring `languages: [terraform]` is skipped as `unsupported_lang`. Add
  `terraform`/`hcl` → `.tf`/`.tfvars` and `yaml` → `.yml`/`.yaml` mappings.
- **Data-driven wiring (story 7f0d).** Do NOT edit `code_review/detectors.py` (the consumer is
  data-driven since 7f0d); the new criterion is picked up from its routing `detector` selector. The
  new criterion's `applies_to` includes docker-compose globs (the `iac` glob list omits them).

## Reproduction Steps
1. A diff opens a security-group ingress `0.0.0.0/0` (or `::/0`) to a service port, gives an instance a
   public IP, stands up an internet-facing LB, or publishes a container port on `0.0.0.0`.
2. The current code-review security overlay does not deterministically flag that public exposure.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a deterministic advisory finding on a publicly-reachable service in the diff, cueing the
  reviewer to verify authentication/gateway.
- **Actual:** no such deterministic signal exists in the code-review gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/builtin/security_iac_public_exposure.yaml` adds opengrep rules under
      the `rebar.builtin.iac.public-exposure.` id-prefix (dimension `has_iac`) detecting, on the diff:
      SG/firewall ingress open to `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`; `associate_public_ip_address = true`; an
      internet-facing LB (`internal = false` on `aws_lb`); a non-loopback (`0.0.0.0:`) host-published
      docker-compose port. Each rule cites its tfsec / Checkov analog.
- [ ] Deny-by-default framing: each finding's message names the exposure and the obligation to verify an
      authenticating gateway / mTLS / network policy (the auth-absence cue), without asserting a
      deterministic auth-correlation the rule cannot prove.
- [ ] FP guards (pattern exclusions): private-CIDR-sourced ingress, loopback/unix-socket binds, and
      `internal = true` LBs do NOT match. Posture is ADVISORY (`blocking_enabled: false`,
      `fail_mode: "open"`) — a match surfaces as a coverage finding, never an auto-BLOCK, so boundary
      controls outside the diff are the reviewer's call.
- [ ] `engine_b._LANG_EXTENSIONS` gains `terraform`/`hcl` → `.tf`/`.tfvars` and `yaml` → `.yml`/`.yaml`
      so the new detectors are applicable; a new `public-exposure-without-auth` `exec: "DET"` entry in
      `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` selects the id-prefix and globs `*.tf` /
      `*.tfvars` / `docker-compose*.y*ml` / `**/compose*.y*ml` (compose globs the `iac` list omits).
- [ ] Unit tests: (positive) the new detectors register on the opengrep backend and a real semgrep run
      matches a `0.0.0.0/0` ingress + a public-IP + a public-LB + a `0.0.0.0:` compose bind; (negative) a
      private-CIDR / loopback / `internal = true` fixture yields NO match; and `apply_failclosed` keeps
      the verdict PASS (advisory, non-blocking) on a match for this criterion. `make lint` green.
baseline.summary: Deterministic public-exposure-without-auth detectors in the code-review security overlay (tfsec/Checkov-style)

baseline.description:
## Why

`nava-rebar` ships as both an application and a library at v0.6.0, but there is
no published statement of what "0.x" means for each surface. SemVer only
communicates compatibility if consumers know which APIs are stable. Today a user
cannot tell whether a CLI flag, a JSON-schema field, a `rebar.*` function, an
MCP tool signature, an event format, or a config key is safe to depend on.

## What

Add `docs/api-stability.md` publishing a stability matrix across every public
surface, and link it from the README and CONTRIBUTING:

- **CLI command names/options** — stable after 1.0; deprecation before removal.
- **`--output json` schemas** — the strongest contract; versioned, backward
  compatible.
- **Python `rebar.*` facade** — the documented stable subset (pairs with the
  typed-models story); internals (`_`-prefixed) are private.
- **MCP tool names / input+output schemas** — stable subset, deprecations
  mirrored from the CLI.
- **Event schema** — forward-compatible wire format, `SCHEMA_VERSION`-gated
  (preserve-and-ignore for unknown event types).
- **Config keys** — deprecate aliases with a documented removal window.

State the pre-1.0 caveat explicitly (everything may change before 1.0 except the
surfaces called out as the strongest contracts).

## Scope

One doc (`docs/api-stability.md`) + links from README/CONTRIBUTING. Describes
intended policy; does not itself change any API. Reference the real mechanisms
that already exist (`reducer/_version.py` `SCHEMA_VERSION`, the JSON Schemas in
`schemas/`, the `_`-private convention).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/api-stability.md` exists with a per-surface matrix covering CLI, JSON
  schemas, Python facade, MCP tools, event schema, and config keys.
- [ ] It names JSON output schemas + event wire format as the strongest contracts
  and states the pre-1.0 caveat.
- [ ] It documents the deprecation policy (deprecate-before-remove, removal
  window) for CLI/config.
- [ ] README and CONTRIBUTING link to it.
baseline.summary: Publish an API-stability matrix doc across CLI/schemas/Python/MCP/events/config

## Target
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — **786 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (14 lines of headroom).

Fourteen lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

## Suspected defect
A source-path audit at code revision d49466b5e960 suggests that one completion operation may combine code evidence read from the immutable tree selected by `--ref` with prefetch, deterministic checks, or later signing inputs rooted at the live checkout. This is a hypothesis from control-flow inspection, not a demonstrated failure. It MUST be verified experimentally before any production change.

The public contract is that checks which judge the implementation are based on the code revision supplied by `--ref`. Comparisons against live state can be valid for drift detection, ancestry, optimistic concurrency, or publication safety, but live checkout content must not become verdict evidence for a `--ref`-targeted run.

## Mandatory reproduction before remediation
1. Build a disposable Git fixture with revisions A and B whose source, referencing commit evidence, and a prefetched file deliberately disagree. Keep the live checkout at B and invoke the real completion path with `--ref A`.
2. Instrument or spy on every code-root/ref input used by context assembly, completion prefetch, deterministic commit/file checks, verifier tools, drift checks, and completion-signature material. Record the resolved OID and classify each read as verdict evidence, ticket-state evidence, or an intentional live-state comparison.
3. Prove whether all verdict-bearing code reads resolve to A. If they do, record the falsification and close this bug without a speculative refactor. If any verdict-bearing read resolves to B, preserve the failing experiment as the regression test before changing code.

## Remediation constraints if reproduced
- Thread one explicit pinned-code handle/OID through every verdict-bearing path; do not let a generic `repo_root` silently select live code.
- Keep intentional live comparisons explicit and one-way: they may reject/retry stale work, but may not contribute evidence that makes a criterion pass or fail.
- Bind `verified_at_sha` and the completion signature to the same A selected by `--ref`.
- Cover a moving branch name as well as a concrete SHA, resolving the name once at operation start.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A deterministic divergent-A/B experiment proves or falsifies the suspected mixed-root behavior through the real completion orchestration path. (Held-out oracle `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch_pinned_root_831f.py` drives the REAL `gate_source.gate_read_root(attested A)` + `assemble_prefetch(repo_root=live B)` path; Phase-1 runtime experiment reproduced the same via the real orchestration. PROVED (not falsified): prefetch read B.)
- [x] The evidence records the resolved OID and purpose of every code read used by prefetch, deterministic checks, agent file tools, drift comparison, and signing. (RCA comment classifies each: prefetch working-tree reads -> now the pinned snapshot A (was live B, the leak); reconcile citations -> A via `cfg.repo_path` at `gate_ops.py:290`; agent read_file/search_files -> A via `use_code_root(handle.path)`/`cfg.repo_path`; `referencing_commit_diffs` -> immutable-by-SHA object read (not live checkout evidence); drift guard -> one-way live comparison, not verdict evidence; signing -> `verified_at_sha`=`handle.sha`=A.)
- [x] If reproduced, a regression test fails before the fix when live=B and `--ref=A`, then passes only when every verdict-bearing check uses A. (Same held-out test: verified RED at buggy HEAD (prefetch carried `LIVE_B_CONTENT`), GREEN after the re-root fix; mutation-checked -- re-seeding the exact defect on both `_read_body` and `_discover_test_globs` re-roots turns it RED.)
- [x] Intentional live-state comparisons are named and tested to fail closed or retry without becoming verdict evidence. (The transition-close drift/stale guard is the sole intentional live comparison: it compares live HEAD/ref against the pinned `verified_at_sha` to reject/retry stale work and never feeds verdict evidence -- covered by `tests/unit/test_attested_close_guard.py`. The fix does not touch it; audit confirmed it stays one-way.)
- [x] The emitted `verified_at_sha` and signed completion manifest equal A. (`gate_source.annotate_result` binds `result["verified_at_sha"] = handle.sha` (=A) and marks the run `signable` only when attested + pinned SHA -- `src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:232`; provenance covered by `tests/unit/test_code_review_provenance.py`. Already correct; audit-confirmed, unchanged by this fix.)
- [x] If the experiment falsifies the hypothesis, no production behavior is changed and the ticket closes with the falsifying evidence. (Inapplicable branch: the experiment CONFIRMED the hypothesis rather than falsifying it, so the "no production change" path was not taken; the localized re-root fix landed instead. Recorded for completeness.)
baseline.summary: --ref-targeted completion may mix pinned code with live-checkout inputs

## Why
`run_git` (`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:26-61`) is characterized only through callers that monkeypatch it (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_git_adapter_characterization.py:48-57`); the real wrapper's own branches are never exercised directly. Signature: `run_git(cwd, *args, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=None, env=None, input_data=None)`. VALIDATED.

Separately, a latent contract hole was confirmed by direct probe: calling `run_git(..., input_data=b"...")` with the default `text=True` raises a confusing `AttributeError: 'bytes' object has no attribute 'encode'` from deep inside `subprocess`, even though the signature advertises `input_data: str | bytes | None`. The wrapper should turn this unsupported combination into a clear, actionable error rather than an opaque stdlib AttributeError.

## What
1. Add a focused contract test matrix in a NEW file `tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py` that
   invokes the REAL `run_git` (no monkeypatching of the wrapper) against a throwaway git repo
   created in a tmp dir, asserting each documented branch (see AC).
2. Narrow the `input_data` contract in `run_git`: when `input_data` is `bytes` and `text=True`
   (the default), raise a clear `TypeError` naming the fix (binary stdin requires `text=False`),
   instead of letting subprocess raise the opaque `AttributeError`. Update the docstring to
   state the narrowed contract. `str` stdin with `text=True` (the only combination any current
   caller uses) is unchanged.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — add the `bytes` + `text=True` guard in `run_git`; document it.
- `tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py` — new direct contract matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `cwd=None` omits the `-C` prefix (argv starts `git <args>`); a path-like `cwd` inserts
      `-C <cwd>` (argv starts `git -C <cwd> <args>`) — asserted by observing behavior against a
      real repo (e.g. `rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to the given repo only when `-C` is
      applied).
- [ ] `check=True` on a failing git command raises `subprocess.CalledProcessError`; `check=False`
      returns a `CompletedProcess` with the non-zero `returncode` instead.
- [ ] `timeout` on a command that exceeds it propagates `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`.
- [ ] `env` fully REPLACES the environment (a var present in the parent but absent from `env`
      is not visible to git), asserted via a git command that reads an env var.
- [ ] `input_data` (str) is forwarded to git's stdin (e.g. `hash-object --stdin` returns the
      hash of the piped content).
- [ ] `input_data=bytes` with `text=True` raises a clear `TypeError` (the narrowed contract),
      NOT the opaque stdlib `AttributeError`; a test pins this behavior.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Add a direct contract test matrix for the shared run_git wrapper

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
`BindingStore`/`BindingRepository` lifecycle alerts are documented as "deduped": `BindingRepository.alert()` (ported verbatim from `BindingStore._alert`) calls `alert_store.is_deduped(key, repo_root)` before appending, and the retired-file-corrupt docstring says corruption "degrades to an empty set + a deduped alert".

The suppression can never fire. `alert_store.is_deduped` computes `ts = rec.get("timestamp_ns", 0)` and tests `now - ts <= window_ns` (24h). The record these callers build is `{**record, "key": key, "resolved": False}` — it has no `timestamp_ns`, and `alert_store.append` does not add one. So `ts` defaults to 0, `now - 0` vastly exceeds the window, the check returns False, and every pass appends another record.

## Evidence
Found while extracting `BindingRepository` (RP-02 S1 T1, vivacious-widish-indianabat). A differential probe constructed both `BindingStore` and `BindingRepository` twice over the same corrupt `bindings-retired.json`: both produced 2 `binding-retired-file-corrupt` records, neither carrying `timestamp_ns`. Behavior is identical pre- and post-extraction, so this is a pre-existing defect, not a regression.

RP-02 S1 T1 deliberately PINNED the real behavior rather than fixing it, because that slice was a byte-for-byte extraction forbidden from changing behavior. See `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_repository.py::test_corrupt_retired_alert_routes_through_the_dedup_check_per_pass`, whose docstring records the reasoning.

## Impact
A persistently corrupt retired file, a repeatedly-retired binding, or any recurring lifecycle condition appends one alert per pass indefinitely, so the operator surface fills with duplicates and the 24h dedup window is decorative. Alerts are append-only JSONL in the git-ignored local `bridge_state/bridge_alerts` tree, so this is noise and unbounded local growth rather than data loss.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Determine the intended owner of `timestamp_ns` — the caller building the record, or `alert_store.append` stamping it centrally for every caller — and record the choice.
- [x] A second occurrence of the same alert key within the window appends no second record, proven through the real `BindingStore`/`BindingRepository` path, not a stubbed `is_deduped`.
- [x] An occurrence OUTSIDE the window still appends, so the fix does not silence a genuinely recurring condition forever.
- [x] Records already on disk without `timestamp_ns` remain readable (the absent field must not start throwing).
- [x] Update `test_corrupt_retired_alert_routes_through_the_dedup_check_per_pass`, which currently asserts the 2-record status quo, and drop the note in its docstring.
- [x] Audit the other `alert()` call sites for the same omission.

## Fix plan (AC#1 owner decision) — /rebar-debug Phase 1 complete

**Owner of `timestamp_ns`: `alert_store.append` (central stamping).** Evidence: a repo-wide audit of every `alert_store.append` caller shows all but one already stamp `timestamp_ns` themselves (apply_handlers.py:386/537, dispatch_apply_phases.py:250, fetcher.py:229/573, invariant_sink.py:139/203, pass_io.py:118/177, reconcile_helpers.py:278, reconcile.py:414, run_differs.py:114/151). The SOLE omission is `BindingRepository.alert()` (binding_repository.py:304 builds `{**record, "key": key, "resolved": False}` with no timestamp), which serves binding_lifecycle.py's four `_repo.alert(...)` calls (253/343/400/417). Rather than patch the one caller and leave `append` fragile for the next forgetful one, stamp centrally in `append`: `record = {"timestamp_ns": time.time_ns(), **record}` — a caller-supplied value WINS (spread after the default), so the dozen existing stampers are byte-for-byte unchanged and only the alert() path gains the field. This eliminates the whole latent class, satisfying AC#6 structurally.

**AC mapping:**
- AC#1 owner decision: central in `append` (documented above).
- AC#2 dedup fires: two `BindingRepository(tracker)` passes over a corrupt retired file now
  append ONE `binding-retired-file-corrupt` record (was two), proven through the real path.
- AC#3 outside-window still appends: a stored record whose `timestamp_ns` is older than the
  24h window does not suppress — `is_deduped` returns False, so a genuinely recurring
  condition is not silenced forever.
- AC#4 old records readable: `is_deduped` already does `rec.get("timestamp_ns", 0)`; a
  pre-existing record without the field yields ts=0 (outside window) and never throws —
  unchanged, asserted by a regression test.
- AC#5: rewrite `test_corrupt_retired_alert_routes_through_the_dedup_check_per_pass` to assert
  ONE record carrying `timestamp_ns`, and drop its status-quo docstring note.
- AC#6 audit: done above — central stamping covers every call site.

**Blast radius:** non-test code = `alert_store.append` (one line). Tests: rewrite the pinned test + add AC#3/AC#4 coverage. Behaviour change is additive (a field appears on records that lacked it) and gated by preserve-if-present, so no existing stamper changes.
baseline.summary: Binding lifecycle alerts never dedupe - records omit timestamp_ns

baseline.description:
## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` (3a52-2d79-320d-4fed), root cause RC-A. See that ticket's "Phase 1 EXIT" comment for the full evidence trail.

## Problem

`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` calls `materialize_tickets(...)` on every attested gate resolution. `materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`) content-addresses the entry as `<store>/tickets-<sha>` and builds it with `_materialize_tree` (`:373-410`, `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index`) — every file written fresh, with no hardlinking, no delta against a neighbouring entry, and no per-review release (`SnapshotHandle._cleanup` at `:199` is never assigned by any producer).

The key is the live tickets-branch tip: `_pin_tickets_sha` (`:534-609`) resolves the tracker via `config.tracker_dir()`, and `tracker_dir_override()` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:65-79`) returns `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` verbatim.

Measured on `origin/tickets`:

- **69,984 blobs**, ≈620 MiB (~800 MiB allocated). The code snapshot alongside it is
  41.6 MiB / 3,131 files — **15x smaller**.
- **1,374 commits** in a 10-hour window (2026-08-17 18:00 → 2026-08-18 04:00 PDT): the tip
  moves every ~26 seconds.
- each of the last 5 consecutive tickets commits changed **exactly 1 file**.

So a one-file delta produces a fresh 620 MiB copy — roughly 10^5x write amplification — on a key with effectively **zero reuse**. The review-bot's own `code_review` artifact write (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`, `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:120`) guarantees the ref advances between reviews even if nothing else in the fleet were writing.

On the review-bot host this modelled 2.5-10 GiB/h of root-disk growth; the measured rate during the 2026-08-17 incident was 4.4 GiB/h.

## Why this is a defect

`docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md` D2 rests on "an immutable SHA is a perfect cache key", which holds only for keys with **reuse**. This key has none, so the structure behaves as an append-only log of full copies rather than the bounded, reclaimable cache the ADR describes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A review no longer writes a full copy of the ticket tree when the previous entry differs
      by a handful of files (hardlink/reflink against the prior entry, materialize only the
      paths the gate actually reads, or pin a coarser/stabler key) — with the chosen approach
      justified against ADR 0005's integrity guarantees.
- [x] A test observes the amplification RED (N reviews across N adjacent tickets SHAs consume
      ~1 tree, not N trees) and GREEN after the repair.
- [x] `materialize_tickets` participates in the store's byte accounting (see the sibling
      ticket) so the entries it creates are visible to any size-based reclaim.
- [x] ADR 0005 / `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` updated to state the key-reuse assumption and how
      the tickets key satisfies it.
baseline.summary: Gate snapshot store copies the whole ~620 MiB ticket tree per review on a cache key with no reuse

baseline.description:
# Two more outbound-parent surfaces drop a hierarchy edit with no durable record

Found by the Step 7 parity census while fixing [rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223], which closed the same gap on the UPDATE emit path. Filed rather than fixed in place because both slots are outside 9f26's declared `file_impact` and reach into the Cloud/ACLI adapters — a separate blast radius that deserves its own attestation.

## The rule, stated without naming the site 9f26 fixed

**An outbound parent that cannot reach the tracker must leave a durable, operator-visible record (a `bridge_alerts` entry), not merely a log line.** This is the project's own contract, cited at `pass_io.py:113-118` ("a log line is not a signal: the pass still exits 0 and nothing durable says the hierarchy diverged") and `dispatch_one.py:561-564` ("Warn-and-continue alone is why 'the parent never reached the tracker' stayed invisible through five instances of this class"). Ticket 39c1 wired it into ONE of the four surfaces that can drop a parent.

## Channel census — four surfaces, two still MISSING

| # | surface | rule holds? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent` (UPDATE emit) | **HOLDS** — closed by 9f26; records `(jira_key, "parent")` on `dropped_field_sink`, which `run_differs._emit_outbound_field_alerts:98` turns into a deduped `outbound-field-dropped` alert |
| 2 | `adapters/jira/outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields:145-156` (CREATE emit) | **MISSING** — the same unconditional non-epic guard, but its only signal is `logger.debug`, which no operator sees and no test asserts |
| 3 | `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent:523-601` (UPDATE apply) | HOLDS — all three alert kinds |
| 4 | `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops._attach_parent_guarded:136-143` (create-then-attach fallback) | **MISSING** — swallows HTTP 400 with a WARNING and returns; no `record_parent_divergence` |

Slot 2 matters because a ticket CREATED with a non-epic parent loses the hierarchy at birth, which is harder to notice than losing it on an edit. Slot 4 matters because it is the only path where Jira actively REJECTED the parent and rebar still reports the create as successful.

## A second finding worth its own decision

The 8b25 hierarchy guard is **unconditional** (`outbound_field_diff.py:138-139` and `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:145-147`), and `outbound_field_diff.py:122-123` advertises "no vendor dependency" — but its stated rationale is vendor-specific: `dispatch_one.py:554-556` scopes it to "**this next-gen project**", where Jira 400s a non-epic parent. On Data Center a sub-task's parent is legitimately a standard issue and DC does **not** 400 it — it accept-and-ignores (capability map req-0056/0058). `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:276-291` restates the rule as a universal "standard project" constraint and never mentions Data Center. So the guard may be suppressing a shape whose justification does not hold on DC. 9f26 deliberately did NOT lift it — suppressing is still the right call for DC (the write would be silently ignored) — but the doc/code divergence should be resolved rather than left for the next reader to rediscover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] slot 2 records a durable bridge alert (not `logger.debug`) when a CREATE drops a non-epic
      parent, reusing the existing `dropped_field_sink` -> `outbound-field-dropped` channel
- [x] slot 4 calls `record_parent_divergence` on its 400-skip, under the existing
      `outbound-parent-rejected` kind
- [x] each is proven RED first: a test that fails for the missing signal before the change
- [x] the bound/unbound distinction 9f26 established is preserved — an UNBOUND parent must stay
      silent, because it converges on a later pass and alerting on it is churn
- [x] `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:276-291` states whether the epic-only parent rule is Cloud-specific,
      and the guard's comments agree with the doc
---

# Fix plan (rebar-debug Phase 1 exit, 2026-08-05)

Both silences were re-proven at runtime with positive controls before any code was written — see the Phase 1 comment on this ticket. The repair reuses 9f26's mechanism verbatim; it does NOT invent a second one.

## Slot 2 — CREATE emit: reporter reports, caller judges

9f26's split is the pattern: `_resolve_local_parent` gained a `suppressed_out` list and reports the key it WOULD have emitted, judging nothing, because only the caller can see the remote snapshot; the caller (`diff_canonical_fields`) owns the convergence comparison. Slot 2 gets the identical shape:

1. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields` gains a keyword-only
   `suppressed_out: list[str] | None = None`. On the 8b25 non-epic branch it appends
   `binding_store.get_jira_key(local_parent_id)` — **only when that key is truthy**, so an UNBOUND
   parent stays silent (it converges on a later pass; alerting on it is churn). The returned dict is
   byte-identical, so nothing rebar sends to Jira changes.
2. `_backend.OutboundMapper.map_local_to_remote` gains the same optional keyword; Cloud's
   `_JiraOutbound` forwards it; DC's `_DCOutbound` accepts and ignores it (DC's
   `_map_local_to_dc_fields` never maps a parent at all, so DC has no suppression to report and its
   behaviour is unchanged).
3. `outbound_differ._compute_outbound_create_mutation` receives `dropped_field_sink`, passes a fresh
   list, and appends `(local_id, "parent")` when it is non-empty — the EXISTING channel
   `run_differs._emit_outbound_field_alerts:101` already turns into a deduped
   `outbound-field-dropped` bridge alert. The identifier is the LOCAL id because a create has no
   Jira key yet by construction.

**Why no convergence gate here, and why the tests still vary that axis.** At CREATE the issue does not exist on the tracker, so there is no remote parent to already hold — the drop is unconditionally a real loss. The converged-vs-divergent axis is therefore protected on the UPDATE side instead: the UPDATE caller (`_diff_fields`) passes NO `suppressed_out`, so it cannot alert, and a test pins that a bound non-epic parent the tracker ALREADY carries produces no `parent` drop. That is the exact defect a sibling change shipped past two green gates because its fixture hardcoded `remote_parent_id: None`.

## Slot 4 — ACLI attach fallback

`acli_cli_ops._attach_parent_guarded`'s 400 arm calls `pass_io.record_parent_divergence("outbound-parent-rejected", child_key, None, parent_key, exc)` alongside the existing WARNING — the same kind and the same helper `dispatch_one.py:571-580` uses for the identical shape. `local_id` is `None` because the transport boundary does not carry it. The helper is fail-open by construction (it swallows every exception), so observability cannot cost a create that would otherwise land. The 400 is still swallowed and the create still returns — the only delta is a local jsonl append.

## The doc/code divergence (AC5)

`docs/jira-sync-setup.md` states the epic-only parent rule as a universal "standard project" constraint and never mentions Data Center. The rule as IMPLEMENTED is unconditional and stays that way — 9f26 deliberately did not lift it, because on DC the write would be silently accept-and-ignored (capability map req-0056/req-0058), which is worse than suppressing. The doc gains a Data Center paragraph saying exactly that: same outcome, different reason (Cloud 400s it; DC accepts and ignores it), so the guard is correct on both and is deliberately not vendor-conditional. `dispatch_one.py`'s "this next-gen project" phrasing is corrected to agree.

## Acceptance / verification

- RED first for each slot, proven failing for the missing signal before any fix exists.
- Mutation checks that vary converged-vs-divergent, and bound-vs-unbound.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and CI's own selection
  `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q`.
- No Cloud-observable behaviour change: no outbound payload, no request, and no return value on
  either surface differs.

## The exact call sites the `suppressed_out` thread touches (worked example)

The keyword is added to a Protocol, so every implementation and every call site is enumerated here rather than left for the implementer to discover:

1. **The CREATE arm must forward the sink.** `outbound_differ._compute_outbound_mutations` already
   holds `dropped_field_sink` in scope (`outbound_differ.py:439`) and passes it to the UPDATE arm
   (`outbound_differ.py:541`, `dropped_field_sink=dropped_field_sink`) — but the CREATE call at
   `outbound_differ.py:511` does NOT, and `_compute_outbound_create_mutation`'s signature
   (`outbound_differ.py:597-599`) has no such parameter. Both must change, mirroring the UPDATE arm;
   without it the appended `(local_id, "parent")` never reaches `_emit_outbound_field_alerts`.
2. **Three test doubles implement `map_local_to_remote` with FIXED signatures ending at
   `emit_detach_clear=False` and no `**kwargs`**, so each raises `TypeError` the moment the differ
   passes the new keyword. All three are inside CI's own selection and all three must gain
   `suppressed_out: list[str] | None = None` (accepted and ignored):
   - `_RecordingOutboundMapper` — `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:263`
   - `_FakeOutbound` — `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py:154`
   - `PassthroughOutbound` — `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_canonical_outbound_equivalence.py:151`
3. The two production implementations are `_JiraOutbound.map_local_to_remote`
   (`adapters/jira/backend.py:63`, forwards it) and `_DCOutbound.map_local_to_remote`
   (`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:86`, accepts and ignores it).

Worked example, end to end. Local parent `P` is a `task` bound to `RBJ-1`; unbound local child `C` has `parent_id=P`. `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` allocates `suppressed: list[str] = []` and calls `outbound_mapper.map_local_to_remote(ticket, binding_store=…, local_ticket_types=…, suppressed_out=suppressed)`. Cloud's `_map_local_to_jira_fields` hits the 8b25 non-epic branch, looks up `binding_store.get_jira_key("P") -> "RBJ-1"`, appends `"RBJ-1"` to `suppressed`, and returns the same dict it returns today (no `parent` key). The caller sees `suppressed` non-empty and appends `("C", "parent")` to `dropped_field_sink`, which `run_differs._emit_outbound_field_alerts:101` turns into the deduped alert `outbound-field-dropped:C:parent`. Change `P` to an `epic` and `suppressed` stays empty and `fields["parent"] == "RBJ-1"`; leave `P` unbound and the non-epic branch appends nothing because `get_jira_key` returns `None`.

### Slot 4 import direction — deliberate, and lazy

`record_parent_divergence` is imported LAZILY inside `_attach_parent_guarded` (function scope), not at module scope, matching the module's existing in-function `import logging as _logging`. Recording at the adapter boundary is the correct site, not a layering shortcut: this 400 is raised by `client.set_parent` INSIDE the ACLI create-then-attach sequence and is swallowed there, so no core call site ever observes it — `create_issue` returns the created issue and reports success. `pass_io` is vendor-neutral (stdlib-only imports; no `adapters` dependency), so the edge introduces no cycle.
baseline.summary: Outbound parent: the CREATE emit and the ACLI attach fallback still drop a hierarchy edit silently

baseline.description:
## Goal
Make the `code_health` metric lens portable to non-Python client projects by replacing rebar-specific, Python-only readers with a configurable, per-project **code-analyzer** built on actively-maintained polyglot OSS tools. Ship the analyzer + its tool dependencies as an **optional `[metrics]` extra** so rebar core gains no new hard dependencies.

## Why
Audit finding (portability review): of 15 registered metrics, only the `code_health` lens is truly language-coupled. `module_size_distribution` / `cap_change_events` / module-size seeds hardcode `src/rebar/**/*.py`, LOC-of-.py, and `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (a rebar governance artifact). Used as-is by a client they DON'T fail loudly — they either fabricate authoritative-labeled zeros (scan an absent path -> {count:0,max_loc:0} at confidence=high) or leak a raw FileNotFoundError as the 'unavailable' reason. Ticket-derived (agent_process) and git-delta (churn/refactor_ratio) metrics are already language-agnostic and stay in core.

## Recommended default stack (deterministic, no network, permissive licenses, verified actively-maintained 2026)
- **scc** (MIT, Go) — LOC + fast size/DRYness + approx complexity + COCOMO. v4.x, 8.5k stars.
- **lizard** (MIT, Python) — TRUE cyclomatic complexity (CCN) + token/param counts across ~25 languages. v1.23 (2026). Already a rebar dev/backfill dep.
- **jscpd** (MIT) — duplication/clone detection, 223 formats, Rabin-Karp. v5. Already a rebar dep.
- (rust-code-analysis has richer metrics — cognitive/Halstead/MI — but is STALE, last release 2023; not adopted.)

## Design
- Define an analyzer interface: `analyze(repo_root, languages) -> {loc, complexity, duplication}`, shelling out to the configured tool(s); deterministic, no LLM.
- Per-project config selects tool + thresholds; the rebar module-size CAP becomes one optional policy layered on the generic LOC signal (not hardcoded).
- **Hard fallback contract:** if no analyzer is configured for the client's language, emit a genuine `Unavailable("no analyzer configured for <lang>")` — NEVER scan a hardcoded path, NEVER fabricate zeros, NEVER leak an errno as a reason. (Fixes the silent-misleading-data mode found in the audit.)
- Package tools + analyzer under an optional `[metrics]` extra; core install stays dependency-free and degrades to Unavailable when the extra is absent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `code_health` metrics computed via the analyzer stack (scc/lizard/jscpd) for a Python client AND at least one non-Python client (e.g. Go or TS).
- [ ] Zero new HARD deps in rebar core; analyzer + tools live behind `pip install rebar[metrics]`; core-only install reports code_health as Unavailable with a clear reason.
- [ ] No hardcoded `src/rebar` / `.github/module-size-limit.txt`; scan root + size policy are per-project config.
- [ ] Missing analyzer/tool -> honest `Unavailable`, never fabricated zeros and never a leaked exception string.
- [ ] Module-size cap re-expressed as an optional policy over the LOC signal.
- [ ] Docs (reuse-surface, user-guide) describe the extra, config, and the fallback contract.

## Out of scope
- Polyglot **dependency-graph** analysis — tracked separately as an idea (no mature drop-in polyglot tool exists; needs per-language adapters or tree-sitter/stack-graphs/SCIP). Explicitly NOT part of this epic.
baseline.summary: Code-health metrics: adopt polyglot analyzer stack (scc/lizard/jscpd) behind a [metrics] extra

## Context / Problem
Acceptance criteria that merely restate a GENERIC development-process gate — one CI or rebar already enforces MECHANICALLY for every ticket regardless of subject — add no signal the completion verifier can act on. Examples seen in real tickets: "all child tickets are closed" (rebar's open-children guard enforces this structurally), "all tests pass" / "CI is green" (CI's Verified gate), "plan review passes" (the rebar/Gerrit plan-review gate). Such an AC would read identically on an ARBITRARY unrelated ticket. It cannot be truthfully evaluated by the completion verifier as ticket-specific work, wastes verifier effort, and can mislead it into gating close on a tautology. Plan review is the right place to catch these: an author-facing finding at plan time keeps them out of the accepted AC set, so the completion verifier is left with only ACs that meaningfully represent the delivered work.

No existing criterion covers this. `evidence-kind` classifies WHERE an AC's proof lives (codebase vs operator-attested) and would even ACCEPT "all tests pass" if tagged `[operator-attested]`; `E2` judges ambiguity; `ac-satisfiability` judges joint satisfiability; `E1` judges coverage/duplication. None asks whether an AC is a redundant mechanical gate.

## Approach
Add ONE new plan-review LLM criterion, `ac-process-gate`, via the established built-in-criterion pattern (mirrors `necessity`, epic 6982/R4) — a 1-TURN, non-code-grounded, single-turn plan-text judgment, shipped ADVISORY (author-coaching) with promotion to blocking left as the documented dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change in docs/plan-review-gate.md, exactly like the R1/R3/R4 family. The criterion visits every acceptance-criterion checkbox and FIRES on an AC whose ENTIRE completion predicate is a generic, ticket-agnostic process/tooling gate CI or rebar enforces for every ticket (children-closed; tests/CI/build/lint/typecheck pass; plan-review passes; completion-verifier passes; change merged/landed; commit-trailer/DCO present). It ACCEPTS (no finding) an AC that names or turns on THIS ticket's SPECIFIC deliverable — the artifact, behavior, contract, test, doc, config, or criterion the ticket produces — EVEN when tests/CI/plan-review are its subject (e.g. "E2E tests are written covering feature X", "the plan-review criteria are updated to the new rubric Y"). Discriminator/litmus: would this exact AC read and be satisfied IDENTICALLY on an arbitrary unrelated ticket? Yes -> generic gate -> FIRE; names/depends-on this ticket's specific deliverable -> PASS. Anti-FP: err toward SILENCE; an AC carrying any ticket-specific deliverable content passes.

Wiring follows the packaged pattern with no new machinery: (a) a rubric prompt file loaded by the existing da27 prompt library; (b) a routing entry in the packaged routing index; (c) membership in `CANONICAL_LLM`; (d) the regenerated tracked guide; (e) a committed bounded-sanity eval spec (the R4-style proving artifact). The criterion is in-process plan-review logic with no CI-provider trigger, so it is portable across environments with any or no CI provider.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_ac_process_gate.md` (NEW) — the rubric prompt (front-matter contract + discrimination body).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — add the `ac-process-gate` routing entry (exec/facet/applies_at/posture/checklist).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `ac-process-gate` to `CANONICAL_LLM` (NOT to `CODEBASE_GROUNDED`/`AGENT_TIER`).
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — regenerated (adds the `## ac-process-gate` section); regenerate-in-place, not hand-edited.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-ac-process-gate.eval.yaml` (NEW) — the committed bounded-sanity fire/no-fire corpus.
- `tests/unit/test_ac_process_gate_criterion.py` (NEW) — deterministic registration/routing/front-matter/guide/eval-shape invariants.

## Testing
- The new deterministic unit module pins: canonical/1-TURN/not-grounded registration; non-orphan advisory routing with the container+leaf scope and the two-key checklist; the prompt front-matter contract; the regenerated guide section (`validate_criteria_guide == []`); the eval-spec shape (>=2 fire, >=2 no-fire, <=8 cases); and zero-wiring effectiveness-recorder auto-inclusion.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the focused unit module run clean; the packaged-routing and criteria-guide parity gates stay green.
- Live bounded-sanity: `rebar criteria eval ac-process-gate --output json` fires on the process-gate ACs and passes the deliverable ACs; the result is committed as the run artifact.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A new plan-review criterion id `ac-process-gate` is a member of `registry.CANONICAL_LLM` and is absent from both `registry.CODEBASE_GROUNDED` and `registry.AGENT_TIER`, so `registry.exec_tier` resolves it to `1-TURN`.
- [x] `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` returns `[]` with the new criterion present, i.e. `criteria_routing.json` carries an `ac-process-gate` entry whose `exec` is `1-TURN`, `default_posture` is `advisory`, `facet` is `ac-text-quality`, and `applies_at.scope` is `["container","leaf"]`.
- [x] The `ac-process-gate` routing checklist has exactly two criterion-local sub-answers: a gate key that is not-applicable->PASS when the plan has no acceptance-criterion checkboxes, and a judgment key deciding whether each AC is a ticket-specific deliverable rather than a generic mechanical gate.
- [x] `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_ac_process_gate.md` exists with front-matter `execution_mode: single_turn`, `category: plan-review-criterion`, and `dimension: ac-text-quality`, and its body both documents the ADVISORY posture and references `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [x] The rubric body enumerates the reject-set (children-closed; tests/CI/build/lint pass; plan-review passes; completion-verifier passes; merged/landed; commit-trailer/DCO) and the accept-set (an AC naming this ticket's specific deliverable, e.g. tests written covering a named feature, or a named criterion/rubric update), and states the "reads identically on an arbitrary unrelated ticket" litmus and the err-toward-silence anti-false-positive rule.
- [x] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` contains a `## ac-process-gate` section and `registry.validate_criteria_guide(<checkout>)` returns `[]`; `registry.explain_criterion("ac-process-gate")` starts with `## ac-process-gate`.
- [x] `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-ac-process-gate.eval.yaml` declares `prompt: plan-review-ac-process-gate` and a dataset of at most 8 cases with at least two `expect: finding` process-gate-AC positives and at least two `expect: pass` deliverable-AC negatives.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_ac_process_gate_criterion.py` asserts the registration, routing, checklist, front-matter, guide-section, eval-spec-shape, and effectiveness-recorder-auto-inclusion invariants above (existence and content of these invariants, independent of any CI run).
- [x] [operator-attested] The live bounded-sanity eval (`rebar criteria eval ac-process-gate`) is run and its JSON result committed as `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/ac_process_gate_sanity.json`, with every must-fire case surfacing an `ac-process-gate` finding and every must-not-fire case surfacing none.
  provenance: environment=rebar repo worktree (impl-ac-process-gate) with live AWS Bedrock access; principal=RebarBotNava (joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the eval invokes the same Bedrock plan-review model production plan-review uses over the committed fire/no-fire corpus; result kappa=1.0 committed as the run artifact.
baseline.summary: Plan-review criterion: flag mechanical process-gate ACs

## Context

Parent epic `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb`; depends on S1 (`248f-ac00-18db-4259`), which adds the peer-confirmation store and records a confirmation when WE push a link. This story adds the second, independent evidence source: a link observed in an authoritative remote snapshot is peer-confirmed even if this clone never pushed it (peer-created links, links pushed before the store existed, links pushed by another clone).

The epic's binding constraint: **a partial / paginated / failed / stale read is NON-EVIDENCE** — it can neither confirm nor deny. rebar already has exactly this completeness signal, and this story consumes it rather than inventing one. `fetcher.py::merge_issuelinks_map` writes the per-issue `issuelinks` key ONLY on an authoritative read — an absent key means UNOBSERVED (truncated page walk, HTTP 410, failed enrichment, a backend without `get_issuelinks_map`), while `[]` means authoritatively-empty. This is the same G1 signal the inbound removal differ already depends on. `BackendPaginationStallError` re-raises rather than degrading, so a stalled pager never reaches this code as a complete read.

There is no snapshot revision counter in the codebase; `pass_id` is the only handle (epic comment D3), so records store `confirmed_pass`, not an ordered revision. No ordering logic is built on it.

## Scope

- `peer_confirmations.py` — add
  `confirm_from_snapshot(store, curr_snapshot, binding_store, pass_id) -> int`, returning the
  number of records written.
  - Iterate `curr_snapshot` entries. **Process an entry ONLY if `"issuelinks" in entry`** — an
    absent key is UNOBSERVED and must be skipped whole. Use the `in` test, never
    `entry.get("issuelinks") or []`, which collapses observed-empty into unobserved (the exact
    trap `inbound_differ.py`'s G1 docstring warns about).
  - Source local id is `binding_store.get_local_id(jira_key)`; skip the entry when it is None.
  - For each raw link entry use `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link(link)` to get
    `(other_key, relation)` in LOCAL relation vocabulary, then
    `binding_store.get_local_id(other_key)` for the target. Skip entries where either is None.
    `resolve_inbound_link` is used directly rather than `observed_peer_deps` because the latter
    returns only `(relation, target)` and DISCARDS the vendor link id this story must persist.
  - Record each as `direction="snapshot"`, `source="snapshot"`, `link_id=link.get("id")`,
    `confirmed_pass=pass_id`.
- `reconcile.py::_persist_and_log` — call it inside the existing `if persist:` block, as a
  sibling of the `_advance_baselines(binding_store, ctx.curr_snapshot, ctx.synced_fields)` call
  and BEFORE `binding_store.save()`, wrapped in the same fail-open `try/except Exception` shape
  that call already uses (log to stderr, never break a sync pass). Then `store.save()`.
- Confirmation is monotonic and additive: observing a link confirms it; NOT observing it never
  un-confirms. Un-confirmation is deliberately excluded — it would reintroduce "absence is
  evidence", the exact failure the epic forbids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 A snapshot entry with `issuelinks` present and a bound link produces a record with
      `direction="snapshot"`, `source="snapshot"`, `link_id` from the raw entry's `id`, and the
      current `pass_id`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k observed`.
- [x] AC2 A snapshot entry with the `issuelinks` key ABSENT produces NO record for that issue,
      even when the link is present and managed locally. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k unobserved`.
- [x] AC3 An authoritative `issuelinks: []` produces no record and does NOT remove or invalidate
      an existing confirmation. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k empty_authoritative`.
- [x] AC4 A link whose source or target key is unbound is skipped — no record, no raise. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k unbound`.
- [x] AC5 Relation mapping goes through `link_direction`, so an INWARD `Blocks` entry is recorded
      under `depends_on`, not `blocks`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k direction`.
- [x] AC6 An exception raised inside snapshot confirmation is logged and the reconcile pass still
      completes and persists (injected raising store). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k fail_open`.
- [x] AC7 In no-write mode (`persist` False) no confirmation is written. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k nowrite`.
- [x] AC8 Every edited module stays under the 800-line cap. Proof: `bash -c 'git archive HEAD |
      tar -xO src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py | wc -l'` per edited file, < 800.
- [x] AC9 Gates green. Proof: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0,
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` exit 0.

## Testing

- New suite `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py` covering the
  observed / unobserved / authoritative-empty trichotomy, unbound source and target, inward
  direction mapping, fail-open behavior, and the no-write path.
- Regression: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` — this story is
  additive and must not change any differ or apply behavior.

## Out of scope
