## Context / Problem

`docs/plan-review-gate.md` (~lines 534-540) states a bug is NOT exempt from plan review in general -- it gets a light advisory-only tier -- while `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:45`'s `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` makes `bug` exempt from the CLAIM-time gate specifically. Lines 1577-1578 and 1598 clarify these are separate axes ("The claim-time exemption is untouched"), but the guide never states the operational SEQUENCE an author should follow: claim a bug without plan review to perform root-cause analysis (RCA) first, then -- once RCA yields an implementation plan and file impact for a complex remediation -- get that plan LLM-reviewed before implementation begins. Absent that explicit sequence, the two true (and non-contradictory) statements read as if a bug is either always exempt or never exempt, depending which passage is read.

## Approach

Correct the maintained guide directly at the claim-time-exemption / bug-tier passage (~lines 534-540, 1577-1578, 1598). State the sequence explicitly: a bug may be claimed without plan review to perform RCA; after RCA, a complex bug with an implementation plan and recorded file impact must receive LLM plan review (an explicit review-plan run on the bug, which yields a real -- non-exempt -- verdict per the existing bug tier / blast-radius escalation) before remediation begins. Preserve the existing behavioral code/tests (gates.py, the bug review tier, blast-radius escalation) as authority; do not change their behavior.

## Scope

- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
- `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py` and `tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py`
  as behavior evidence/checks (read-only verification, not behavior
  changes)

## Testing

Run focused bug-review tier tests and add/update a documentation assertion that distinguishes claim-time exemption (CLI, always) from implementation-time plan review (LLM, required post-RCA for complex bugs).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The guide states a bug may be claimed without plan review
      specifically to perform RCA. Verified: new paragraph added at ~line 540.
- [x] The guide states a complex bug -- one with an implementation plan
      and recorded file impact after RCA -- must receive LLM plan review
      before implementation begins. Verified: same paragraph states the post-RCA requirement explicitly.
- [x] The guide does not imply every bug needs review before claim, nor
      that complex-bug remediation is permanently exempt from LLM review.
      Verified: the paragraph explicitly distinguishes the two axes.
- [x] Focused bug-review tier tests and a new documentation-content check
      pass. Verified: tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py (7) + new tests/unit/test_bug_claim_rca_sequence_docs.py (6) -- 13 pass together. Committed 1052f711f40a, pushed as Gerrit change 2544.
baseline.summary: Document bug claim exemption and post-RCA complex-bug plan review

`docs/adr/0004:43-48` asserts the snapshot-entry shape "has a single source of truth... Both the fetcher's output and the differs' expectations target it. When a new field is added to the snapshot, update the schema first." Nothing enforces that.

`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_snapshot_schema.py` (228 LOC) is imported by NO production module; the intended producer `fetcher.py` never imports it. The originating story declared `fetcher.py (producer validates vs schema)` as file impact; that wiring never landed.

The schema encodes a `parent` present-vs-absent distinction that gates an inbound CLEAR — a data-destroying path whose own history contains a revert titled "Revert the inbound parent clear: it destroys data."

Refined during approval: rather than a bespoke contract test, move the contract into `src/rebar/schemas/` where ~90 sibling schemas already live, loaded via `schemas.load()` and validated with `jsonschema` on a `Draft202012Validator`, with a generated TypedDict layer under a CI drift gate (`python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`, `_build-and-test.yml:545`). The snapshot contract is the odd one out — a hand-rolled Python module outside that machinery, which is *why* nothing enforces it while 90 siblings are enforced automatically.

Real fetcher output exists for fixtures: `bridge_state/snapshots/` holds 548 files spanning 2026-06-11..06-29 with fully-populated entries. It is gitignored and contains PII (`emailAddress`, `displayName`, `accountId`), so a small redacted fixture must be derived into the tracked `tests/fixtures/jira/`, covering all three observed shapes: populated, `parent`-absent, and horizon-trimmed-empty.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The snapshot-entry contract lives in `src/rebar/schemas/` and is loadable via `schemas.load()`
- [x] It is covered by the existing generated-types drift gate rather than a one-off check
- [x] A redacted fixture in `tests/fixtures/jira/` covers populated, `parent`-absent, and empty shapes
- [x] A fetcher field change that diverges from the contract fails CI
- [x] ADR 0004 describes the enforcement that actually exists
baseline.summary: Enforce the snapshot-entry contract through the schemas drift gate

baseline.description:
## Experiment: harness-parity oracle for completion verification (PoC, throwaway)
Operator hypothesis: completion verification is conceptually simple and works exceptionally well as a plain subagent in an agent harness with free tools; the unreliability (false rejections, insufficiency loops) lives in OUR in-process scaffolding (step budget, structured tool surface, mid-loop output contract), not in the task. This PoC measures that directly: same corpus, production verifier vs a minimal harness agent.

## Arms
- **Arm A (control): production in-process verifier** — `verify-completion` runs on the corpus tickets with the SAME harness seams the filter experiment (fabulous-lowborn-guanaco) proved: isolated per-run verdict-cache namespaces (monkeypatch `cache_dir`, completion_verdict_cache.py:59), `source='local'`/signable=false, run from a throwaway worktree's git-ignored `.expscratch/`. WHERE the guanaco control arm's transcripts are reusable (same ticket, same tree/ref, per-AC verdicts recorded), REUSE them as Arm A data instead of paying for new runs; rerun only for pairing gaps.
- **Arm B (treatment): minimal harness agent** — for each corpus ticket, a FRESH local harness subagent (Copilot CLI task agent; free, non-Bedrock) receives ONLY: the ticket's AC list verbatim, the worktree path at the pinned ref, and the instruction to verify each AC and emit JSON `{ac, verdict: PASS|FAIL|INSUFFICIENT, citations[], reason}` with file:line evidence — INSUFFICIENT is the mandatory abstain state for an AC whose evidence is not reachable with repository tools (e.g. an external-system or runtime-outcome claim); the agent must never coerce such an AC to PASS or FAIL. No rebar tooling, no step budget, no structured tool surface — plain grep/read/test-run freedom. One subagent per ticket per rep (not per AC — per-criterion fan-out was already implemented, measured, and removed for exploding cost per ticket 12b7's FORCE_CLOSE record; this experiment must not resurrect it).

## Corpus
Reuse the guanaco corpus verbatim for cross-experiment comparability: 45c1 (bettong, task, 6 ACs), 3388 (shrew, story, 10 ACs), 0e68 (wildebeast, epic, 7 ACs + 14 children), each with its in-harness adversarial variant (5 planted-unmet ACs citing symbols proven absent at ref). Ground truth: real variants = all-PASS; adversarial planted ACs = FAIL. Known Arm-A noise: guanaco observed 2 agentic false-FAILs in one epic run and 35↔55 step variance.

## Arm A rejection mapping (per AC)
Arm A per-AC outcomes come from the verifier's reconciled structured result: an AC counts as a REJECTION iff its final verdict is unmet. Among unmet ACs, classify insufficiency by the framework-derived `evidence_sufficient: false` marker (completion_reconcile.py:198-210 — model-minted markers are stripped, so this is trustworthy), the same predicate `_insufficiency_only` reuses (completion_reconcile.py:115). Report Arm A false-FAILs (unmet, evidence deemed sufficient) and evidence-insufficient unmets separately; BOTH count toward Arm A's rejection total in the decision rule.

## Arm B output validation & fallback
After each Arm B run: assert the emitted JSON parses and contains EXACTLY one entry per AC, matched by verbatim AC id/text. On parse failure or missing ACs, retry the subagent once with the same frozen prompt. If still malformed/incomplete: record every missing AC as INSUFFICIENT flagged `harness_error` (counted as rejections for the decision rule — harness fragility is a legitimate strike against Arm B, and this fail-closed rule mirrors production's per-criterion coverage check, completion_criteria.py:162). A crashed/hung subagent (no output) = one rerun; if it crashes again the rep is recorded FAILED (excluded from wall-time medians, included in the report). Validation outcomes (clean / retried / harness_error / failed-rep counts) are part of the metrics table.

## Metrics (per arm, per ticket, per rep)
False-PASS count (critical, per planted AC; an INSUFFICIENT on a planted AC is NOT a false-PASS); rejection count on real ACs = false-FAIL + INSUFFICIENT (both block a close in production, so both count toward the pain-point metric, reported separately); per-AC agreement with ground truth; wall time; Arm A Bedrock spend (tokens + $); Arm B local-harness turn/tool-call counts (cost qualitative — local harness is free per operator).

## Budget & reps
Bedrock cap **$20 total** (operator-approved) for Arm A reruns — track cumulative spend per run and STOP dispatching Arm A runs at the cap (reuse + partial pairing is an acceptable degraded result; report what was covered). Arm B is uncapped in dollars (local harness free) but capped at 2 reps/ticket-variant. Target: 2 reps per ticket-variant per arm; degrade to 1 rep on the epic if spend requires.

## Predeclared decision rule
**GO** (pursue an external-harness verifier seam in production design, feeding viral-peppy-lowchen) iff, aggregated over the corpus: (i) Arm B false-PASS = 0, AND (ii) Arm B total rejections on real ACs (false-FAIL + INSUFFICIENT) strictly < Arm A total rejections on real ACs (its false-FAILs + evidence-insufficient verdicts), AND (iii) Arm B median wall time ≤ 2× Arm A. Anything else = NO-GO or INDETERMINATE (state which and why). Apply verbatim; no post-hoc rule edits.

## Non-goals
Production integration (design goes to lowchen); per-AC fan-out (12b7); prompt engineering beyond the fixed minimal Arm-B instruction (one prompt, frozen before the first run, included in the report); closing this ticket (left in_progress for operator review).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Arm B prompt frozen and recorded on this ticket BEFORE the first Arm B run.
- [x] All 6 corpus ticket-variants exercised in both arms (reuse counted for Arm A), ≥1 rep each, with per-AC verdict tables.
- [x] Metrics table posted as a comment on this ticket AND on viral-peppy-lowchen: false-PASS/false-FAIL per arm, agreement, wall time, Arm A spend vs the $20 cap.
- [x] Predeclared GO/NO-GO rule applied verbatim with the arithmetic shown.
- [x] Zero Gerrit pushes; all runs source=local; harness confined to a git-ignored `.expscratch/`; Bedrock spend ≤ $20 documented.
baseline.summary: Experiment: harness-parity oracle — production verifier vs minimal free-tool harness agent (PoC)

baseline.description:
## What
`rebar review-code` assembles its diff with a TWO-dot range `git diff base..head` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py`). When `head` is behind `base` (reviewing a PR branch not caught up to `origin/main`), a two-dot diff shows `head` relative to base's CURRENT tip, so every commit merged into `base` since the branch point appears as a spurious deletion. This inflates the review with a revert of unrelated work and produces phantom-deletion findings that cite real line numbers but describe changes the PR never made. Reported upstream from a client project: a 7-file PR reviewed as 11 files with ~720 phantom deletions; 3 of 5 findings were artifacts.

## Approach
Switch both diff invocations in `assemble_diff_context` from `base..head` to the THREE-dot `base...head` (merge-base) form, matching git's own PR-review convention. Three-dot diffs `head` against the merge-base of base and head, excluding unrelated commits on `base` after the branch point. The change is limited to the `diff_text is None` git path; the supplied-`diff_text` offline seam is unaffected.

## Scope / files
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py` — two `_git` diff calls (`diff` and `diff --name-only`).
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_assemble.py` — new behavioral regression test.

## Acceptance criteria
- A branch behind its base reviews ONLY the branch's own changed files; commits merged into base
  after the branch point are not surfaced as deletions.
- New regression test `test_diff_is_merge_base_three_dot_not_two_dot` builds a real repo with a
  branch behind main and asserts `changed_files == ["feat.py"]` (no phantom `other.py`); it fails
  under two-dot and passes under three-dot.
- lint, typecheck, and the assemble test module stay green.

## Out of scope
Run-to-run non-determinism and the supply-chain/severity findings from the same upstream report are tracked separately.
baseline.summary: code-review --base uses two-dot diff; reviewing a branch behind base surfaces phantom deletions

baseline.description:
The AWS review-bot holds a persistent tickets clone that a redeploy does not refresh, and it writes on every Gerrit vote. Give it diverged-detection, and fix the deploy path so the change actually reaches the box. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Its clone lives on an EBS-backed external volume (`docker-compose.yml:127`, `external: true`) cloned once behind `if [ ! -d .git ]` (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:117`, itself nested inside `if [ -n "${REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT:-}" ]` at `:112`), so a redeploy does **not** converge it. It writes a `code_review` ticket and auto-pushes on **every** vote (`voter.py:260-343`, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`) — event-driven, not scheduled, so pausing AWS *schedules* does not stop it.

This is **new code, not a predicate fix**: `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` currently does only `git config user.email/user.name` (`:52-53`) then `run_ensures` (`:59`) — no fetch, no reset, no ancestry test. Note its invocation at `Dockerfile.reviewbot:125` sits OUTSIDE the PAT block, so new logic there runs even with the PAT unset.

**Chicken-and-egg:** `autodeploy.sh:186`'s rsync — which is what refreshes the box's copy of these scripts — runs only when `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS` changed (`:55` = `src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot pyproject.toml infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`). A commit touching only these two scripts would never reach the box. So this must land in the **same change** as an `src/rebar/` edit (A6-0a qualifies).

## Approach
1. Add diverged-detection to `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`: if `HEAD` is not an ancestor of
   `origin/tickets` and not strictly ahead, `fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets`. Safe because the
   bot never holds unpushed work (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`).
2. Add `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` to `autodeploy.sh:55`'s `BOT_PATHS`, so future
   edits to it deploy at all.

Vote safety is already guaranteed and must not regress: `voter.py:698` records the vote **before** `emit_code_review_artifact` (`:735`), and that call is wrapped in `except Exception` -> `_artifact_emit_error` + `logger.warning` + `return None` (`:368-371`) — documented as "the vote is already cast, so this never fails the review". A store failure cannot wedge the `LLM-Review` gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a clone diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared tip), the script re-converges it to
      `origin/tickets` and leaves no local commits. Tier: **shell integration** against two real
      temporary repos.
- [ ] Given an up-to-date or merely-behind clone, the script makes **no** destructive change
      (negative control). Tier: **shell integration**.
- [ ] With `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` unset, the new logic still executes (it sits outside the PAT
      block). Tier: **shell integration** with the env var unset.
- [ ] `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` appears in `autodeploy.sh`'s `BOT_PATHS`. Verify:
      grep assertion in a test.
- [ ] A rebar store write failure inside the bot still leaves the vote cast (regression guard). Tier:
      **unit** on `emit_code_review_artifact` with an injected store failure.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0a (and must ship in the same change as an `src/rebar/` edit).
baseline.summary: A6-0b: make the review-bot's tickets clone self-converge, and fix its deploy trigger

## Context / Problem
Running `uv` in this checkout generates a `uv.lock` at the repo root that shows up as an untracked file. rebar deliberately keeps core dependencies unpinned (`>=`), and `.github/dependabot.yml` states a `uv` ecosystem block should be added only "if a uv.lock is ever committed" — so the lockfile is a per-developer artifact that must not be tracked.

## Approach
Add a `uv.lock` entry to `.gitignore` with an explanatory comment matching the file's existing commented style, placed alongside the other per-developer tooling ignore rules (e.g. `.serena/`, `.tokensave/`). No dependency-manifest change — core deps stay unpinned `>=` by design; this only stops an already-uncommitted artifact from appearing as untracked.

## Scope
- `.gitignore` — add a commented `uv.lock` ignore rule.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.gitignore` contains a `uv.lock` rule; verified by `git check-ignore uv.lock` printing `uv.lock` and exiting 0.
- [ ] A stray root `uv.lock` no longer appears in `git status --porcelain`.
- [ ] No other tracked files change; verified by `git diff --stat` on the change showing only `.gitignore`.
baseline.summary: Ignore per-developer uv.lock in .gitignore

baseline.description:
## The defect

The close precheck requires EVERY `- [ ]` acceptance criterion to be ticked before a ticket can close. It has no way to record that a criterion is NOT APPLICABLE.

This breaks on any ticket whose ACs are branch-exclusive — the common "decide X, then: if A do this / if B do that" shape, where satisfying one branch necessarily means the other is never performed.

## Confirmed instance 2026-08-05

Bug `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1` asked for an operator decision (honor the inert `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` field, or remove it) and carried both outcomes as ACs:

    - [ ] If HONORED: structural metric evaluation is gated on it, with a test proving ...
    - [ ] If REMOVED: the field, its coercion row and its config-surface entries go ...

The operator chose REMOVE. The implementing agent therefore could not satisfy the HONORED branch — by construction, not by omission. The close gate refused the close until that box was ticked, so the agent ticked a criterion describing work it had deliberately not done, and posted a comment stating the tick means N/A rather than done. It did NOT use `--force-close`, which was the right call.

Ticket authorship is a contributing cause and worth saying plainly: whoever writes a decide-then-branch ticket creates this trap. But the gate offering no expression for N/A is what converts an awkward ticket into a false record.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating

A ticked AC is load-bearing evidence in this system. The close gate reads it, the completion verifier reasons over it, and reviewers treat it as an assertion that the work was done. Once agents learn that ticking can mean "not applicable", the signal degrades for every ticket, not just branch-exclusive ones — and the degradation is invisible, because a ticked box looks identical either way.

The `[operator-attested]` tag already establishes the precedent that a criterion can be satisfied by something other than in-repo work. This is the same shape: a criterion that is legitimately not code-verifiable, for a different reason.

## Candidate approaches (weigh; not prescribed)

1. An explicit marker, e.g. `- [x] [n/a: <reason>]` or `- [~]`, that the precheck accepts and
   that records WHY. Mirrors `[operator-attested]`, so the vocabulary stays consistent.
2. Structured branch groups, so ACs can be declared mutually exclusive and the gate requires
   exactly one branch satisfied.
3. Author-side only: forbid branch-exclusive ACs and require the decision to be made before the
   ACs are written. Cheapest, but relies on discipline and does not help tickets already filed.

Option 3 alone is insufficient — the decide-then-branch shape is genuinely useful when a ticket is filed before the operator has ruled, which is exactly how a573 and dce2 were written.

## Acceptance Criteria (rescoped 2026-08-07 to the refined ruling)

N/A eligibility keys off the CLOSE DISPOSITION, not off the individual criterion. A ticket claiming COMPLETION keeps today's strict behaviour; a ticket closing as a terminal disposition (won't-fix, obsolete, not-a-bug, duplicate) has no applicable AC scan.

- [ ] The set of close classes that make the AC scan INAPPLICABLE is decided and named explicitly.
      `--class` already exists on bug closes (regression, plan_defect, env_integration, flaky,
      preexisting, not_a_bug, duplicate, escalated, undetermined); state which of these are terminal
      dispositions, and whether a won't-fix / obsolete class needs adding — 3b92 had no honest class
      to use and was force-closed as a result
- [ ] Closing under a terminal-disposition class does NOT run the unchecked-AC precheck, and records
      the class as the reason the criteria were not evaluated
- [ ] Closing as COMPLETED is UNCHANGED: an unmet criterion still fails the close, and the remedy is
      still to remediate the criterion. A test pins that this path did not weaken
- [ ] A test proves a terminal-disposition close succeeds with unchecked criteria present AND that the
      same ticket closing as completed still fails
- [ ] `--force-close` is no longer the routine answer for an obsolete ticket; the CLI message on a
      failed close points at the class mechanism rather than straight at the override (this is the
      steering defect 218e reports separately)
- [ ] Non-bug types (task, story, epic) are covered too, or their exclusion is stated with a reason —
      3b92, 5dd2, e5ec, 39c5 and 83f2 were all tasks, and all were force-closed
- [ ] The distinction is documented where AC authors will see it, alongside `[operator-attested]`

## Out of scope

A PER-CRITERION N/A marker. That was the original request and it is rejected: on a ticket claiming completion, a criterion nobody can satisfy means the plan was written wrong, and letting an author mark it N/A converts that signal into a checkbox. The disposition-level mechanism above solves the genuine case without opening that door.
baseline.summary: The close gate cannot express an N/A acceptance criterion, so mutually-exclusive ACs force a false tick

baseline.description:
# S5 — Trusted-proxy passthrough verifier

## Why
Many organizations terminate authentication at an edge proxy / gateway (oauth2-proxy, API Gateway, ALB) and want the backend to trust the already-authenticated identity — and it is the only in-scope path for identity systems that are not token issuers (e.g. GitHub-user via oauth2-proxy). This verifier lets rebar delegate auth to that fronting proxy safely, through the SAME composite contract as token verifiers.

## What
Add a **trusted-proxy** mode to `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, activated by including `proxy` in the `mcp.auth_strategies` list (the strategy-selection config key **introduced by S2**, this story's dependency — not a pre-existing seam), with flat config keys it registers: `auth_proxy_secret_env` (NAME of an env var holding the proxy shared secret — no plaintext secret in config), `auth_proxy_secret_header` (default `x-proxy-auth`), `auth_proxy_identity_header` (default `x-forwarded-user`), and `auth_proxy_scopes` (comma-separated fixed scope set granted to proxy-authenticated principals; OPTIONAL, defaults to an EMPTY set — a proxy-authenticated principal then holds no scopes and is denied 403 by any non-empty `auth_required_scopes` until scopes are configured). It comprises a small ASGI middleware plus a `TokenVerifier`-shaped component so that proxy identity flows through the **same composite**, not around it:
- The **middleware** runs before the MCP app: it validates the shared-secret header (constant-time)
  and, only if valid, extracts the identity header into a request-scoped principal; otherwise it
  strips it. It **strips the entire `X-Forwarded-*` family** (and the configured identity/secret
  headers) from any inbound request that does not present the valid secret, normalizing header-name
  case and underscore/dash variants to defeat smuggling.
- The **verifier** turns that verified request-scoped identity into an `AccessToken` with
  `client_id`=the identity, `scopes`=`auth_proxy_scopes`, and **`resource=auth_resource_server_url`**
  so it passes the composite audience check exactly like a token verifier. If no verified proxy
  identity is present it returns None (composite falls through / denies) — it never accepts on a
  missing/invalid secret.
- **Ordering:** the proxy verifier participates in the composite `auth_strategies` order like any
  other; a bare request with no valid proxy identity is not accepted by it, so a co-configured bearer
  verifier still gets its turn. Adds the `auth_proxy_*` fields to `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`); their derived `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_PROXY_*` env-var names go in `MCP_ENV_VARS` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) + `server.json`; `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (docs regenerated by S7).

## Approach & rationale
Implement the oauth2-proxy-blessed trusted-header pattern, and route the result through the composite (not around it) so the single audience/fail-closed choke point (S2) still applies. Bind HTTP to loopback (S1 default) so only the proxy can reach the server; require a proxy shared secret; strip any inbound identity/forwarded headers unless the secret is valid. This is the documented mitigation for the forwarded-header-spoofing class (oauth2-proxy CVE-2026-40575 / CVE-2025-64484). A tiny ASGI middleware is the right seam because forwarded identity lives on headers the token-only `verify_token` seam does not see.

## Scope
The trusted-proxy verifier + its header-guard middleware only, on the S2 seam. Subset of the epic. Depends on S2. Independent of S3/S4/S6.

## Security
Boundary-crossing and itself a spoofing surface. Hard requirements:
- **Loopback bind** is the intended deployment (S1 default); a non-loopback bind is governed by S1's
  existing non-loopback gate (both allowlists + TLS-at-edge ack) — no new bind key.
- **Operator prerequisite (documented, loud):** the fronting proxy MUST overwrite/strip all
  client-supplied identity and forwarded headers before adding its own; rebar additionally strips the
  entire `X-Forwarded-*` family on its side unless the shared secret validates.
- The env var named by `auth_proxy_secret_env` MUST be present and non-empty at startup or the proxy
  verifier refuses to start (fail-closed).
- The shared secret proves "from the proxy," not identity authenticity — so identity is trusted ONLY
  when the secret validates AND the header survived rebar's strip-then-repopulate; a constant-time
  compare gates it; header-name normalization defeats underscore/case smuggling.
- The minted `AccessToken` carries `resource=auth_resource_server_url`, so it is still subject to the
  composite audience check; fail-closed (no valid secret → no identity → 401).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `auth_proxy_*` config fields exist in `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']` (`_config_schema.py`);
      their derived `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_PROXY_*` env-var names are in `MCP_ENV_VARS` (`mcp_server.py`) +
      `server.json`; and `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (observable oracle: manifest drift
      test green; both files contain the new env-var names). Docs regenerated by S7.
- [ ] Unit test (tier: unit — the ASGI middleware + verifier exercised directly) asserts: with a
      valid `auth_proxy_secret` header, the identity header yields an `AccessToken` whose
      `client_id`=identity, `scopes`=`auth_proxy_scopes`, and `resource==auth_resource_server_url`;
      without the secret, the identity header is stripped and the request is unauthenticated (401).
- [ ] Unit test asserts a client cannot spoof identity: sending `x-forwarded-user` (or the
      underscore/case variants `X_Forwarded_User`, `X-FORWARDED-USER`) directly WITHOUT the valid
      secret is stripped and never trusted; and that the entire `X-Forwarded-*` family is stripped in
      that case (negative controls for each variant).
- [ ] Unit test asserts the verifier refuses to start when the env var named by `auth_proxy_secret_env`
      is absent or empty (observable oracle: startup raises a clear message).
- [ ] Unit test asserts `auth_proxy_scopes` defaults to an empty set when unset, so a valid proxy
      principal holds no scopes and is denied 403 by a non-empty `auth_required_scopes` (observable
      oracle: 403 with empty proxy scopes vs 200 once the required scope is granted).
- [ ] Integration test (httpx `ASGITransport`) asserts an authenticated proxy request (valid secret +
      identity header) → 200, and that the proxy-minted token still passes the composite audience
      check; a bare request → 401.
- [ ] Integration test asserts composition: with `auth_strategies=proxy,static`, a request with no
      proxy identity but a valid static token still succeeds (proxy verifier returns None, static
      accepts) — observable oracle: 200.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive, opt-in via the `proxy` strategy. No change to other verifiers or the stdio path.

baseline.description:
The snapshot janitor never garbage-collects the new pinned ticket-store cache entries (`<store>/tickets-<sha>/`) introduced in PR #67, so they accumulate unboundedly as the `tickets` branch changes — a local-disk leak in the gate snapshot cache. They are also absent from the janitor's byte-total accounting.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run the plan-review / completion gates repeatedly while the `tickets` branch HEAD changes between runs (normal: every ticket write advances it).
2. Each distinct tickets SHA materializes a fresh `<store>/tickets-<sha>/.tickets-tracker/` copy of the whole ticket store.
3. Inspect the snapshot store (`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` / `store_root()`): the `tickets-<sha>` dirs accumulate and are never evicted.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the janitor evicts stale `tickets-<sha>` entries by the same grace/LRU/size policy it applies to code-snapshot `<sha>` entries, and counts them in the byte total.
- Actual: `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:_is_entry` treats an entry as `all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in name)` — the `tickets-` prefix is non-hex, so `_is_entry("tickets-<sha>")` is False. `_entries()` therefore excludes them: they are never evicted (leak) and never counted (under-reported cache size).

## Root Cause
`_is_entry` (janitor.py) recognizes only all-hex directory names; PR #67's `tickets-<sha>` entries don't match.

## Fix direction
Extend `_is_entry` to also recognize `tickets-<40hex>` (e.g. accept names matching `^(tickets-)?[0-9a-f]{40}$`), so `_entries()` includes them for eviction + accounting. Verify `_evict`/`_remove_sidecars` behave for a `tickets-`-named entry (no caveats sidecar — the unlink is try/except, harmless). Add a janitor test that a stale `tickets-<sha>` entry is evicted past the grace window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_is_entry` returns True for a `tickets-<40hex>` dir; `_entries()` includes it.
- [ ] The janitor evicts a stale `tickets-<sha>` entry (past grace) and counts it in the byte total.
- [ ] A regression test covers eviction + accounting of a `tickets-<sha>` entry.
- [ ] Code-snapshot `<sha>` entry handling is unchanged.
- [ ] Fix lands via PR to main.
baseline.summary: snapshot janitor leaks pinned ticket-store entries (tickets-<sha> not GC'd)

baseline.description:
## Context
Pure mutation plans still need to represent binding lifecycle decisions and prerequisite ordering without performing effects. Selection, filters, mode caps, and safety limits must exclude work before intents are eligible.

## Outcome
Add versioned lifecycle intents and explicit inter-ticket dependencies to `TicketPlan`, and apply every global selection/limit before any lifecycle or remote effect.

## Plan
1. Model bind, confirm, re-key, retire, baseline, and comment-identity changes as versioned intents only. Each intent's `version` is the enclosing frozen `Observation.version` identity from S2 T1 (its `ObservationVersion` — the content-hash `fingerprint` plus `pass_id`); intents carry no independent counter, so pure oracle tables assert `intent.version == observation.version` exactly.
2. Encode create-before-link and parent-before-child prerequisites. A blocked prerequisite yields a deferred disposition carrying reason `dependency_deferred` and emits no out-of-order mutation.
3. Move selection, filter, mode cap, and global safety limit decisions into pre-effect planning, each recording a distinguishable deferral reason (see "Dispositions" below).
4. Cover tombstones, pending/index lag, moved keys, impossible links, partial snapshots, and filtered passes with ticket-sourced tables, each mapping to a deterministic disposition + reason.

## Dispositions (deferral reason vocabulary)
`PlanDisposition` keeps `mutate`/`defer`/`noop`; a deferred/excluded plan additionally records a `defer_reason` drawn from the existing apply-layer `operation_outcome.Disposition` names, so each AC outcome family is separately assertable:
- blocked prerequisite (create-before-link / parent-before-child) -> `dependency_deferred`
- selection / filter exclusion -> `scope_deferred`
- mode cap / global safety limit exclusion -> `safety_aborted`
- tombstone / index-lag / moved-key / impossible-link / partial-snapshot -> `skipped`

## Impacted sites (existing construction/consumer surface)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/ticket_plan.py` — `TicketPlan` value type: gains versioned lifecycle-intent and inter-ticket-dependency fields plus the `defer_reason` field (kept frozen, provider-neutral, open payload).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/ticket_planner.py` — `plan_pass` (currently groups mutations by target only, ticket_planner.py:110-126): gains intent/dependency derivation and pre-effect selection/filter/mode-cap/limit exclusion with reason tagging. Stays pure (zero I/O).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py:285` — the shadow construction site `ctx.observation, ctx.ticket_plans = ticket_planner.plan_pass(... selection=..., limits=..., mode=...)`. **In scope:** it adopts the new pre-effect selection/filter/mode-cap/limit behavior and the widened `TicketPlan` surface by calling the updated `plan_pass`; it already forwards `selection`/`limits`/`mode`, so any `plan_pass` signature change is reflected at this call site. It remains a pure, additive shadow attach performing no effects.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_ticket_plan_shadow.py` — held-out oracle extended for intents/dependencies/pre-effect exclusion.

## Testing
Pure tables assert exact intent values (including `version == observation.version`), dependency edges, and per-family `(disposition, defer_reason)` pairs, and poison repository/provider writes. Ordering tests vary each limit independently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every named binding change is represented as a lifecycle intent whose `version` equals the enclosing `Observation.version` identity.
- [x] No lifecycle intent performs any write during planning (all repository/provider write seams poisoned).
- [x] Create-before-link prerequisites are explicit plan dependencies.
- [x] Parent-before-child prerequisites are explicit plan dependencies.
- [x] Blocked prerequisites produce deferred plans tagged `dependency_deferred`.
- [x] Blocked prerequisites emit no out-of-order mutation.
- [x] Selection and filter exclusion produce plans tagged `scope_deferred` before any intent or remote effect is eligible.
- [x] Mode cap and global safety limit exclusion produce plans tagged `safety_aborted` before any intent or remote effect is eligible.
- [x] Ticket-sourced tombstone, index-lag, move, impossible-link, and partial-snapshot cases produce deterministic `skipped` dispositions.

## Out of scope
Preview output rendering and production coordinator execution. The `run_differs.py:285` shadow construction site is in scope only for adopting the updated `plan_pass` signature/semantics (above); it does not gain preview rendering or effectful execution.

# restore_deleted_sources misses deletions a PATH-scoped walk would find

## Corrected diagnosis (the original filing was wrong)
This bug was filed claiming plain `git log` skips MERGE commits, so a deletion reaching HEAD through a merge was invisible. That is FALSE. Measured on the live store against ticket f130's lost EDIT (a440f6d5-6aa1-4669-9908-5fb955ad6a53, which carried that ticket's 2719-char description):

    git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/                          -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D --full-history -- <tid>/           -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D -m -- <tid>/                       -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D --diff-merges=first-parent -- ...  -> 0 hits
    git log --all --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/                    -> 0 hits
    git log --all --diff-filter=D        (no pathspec)         -> 0 hits
    git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/*<uuid>*                  -> 1 hit

Every merge-diff mode and `--all` changes nothing. ONLY narrowing the pathspec from the DIRECTORY to the FILE (or a per-uuid glob) finds it. So this is a pathspec-SCOPE effect under git's path history simplification — not merge-diff display, and not reachability. The fix the original acceptance criteria implied (add a diff-merges mode) would have shipped without fixing anything.

## Impact
`restore_deleted_sources` enumerates deletions with ONE ticket-scoped `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- <tid>/` pass. Anything that walk misses stays unrecoverable and the ticket keeps a SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES finding permanently. Observed on f130 during the b636 remediation; recovered by hand at the time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A targeted per-uuid fallback (`git log --diff-filter=D -- <tid>/*<uuid>*`) recovers
      sources the directory-scoped walk misses.
- [x] The fallback is BOUNDED to the uuids the snapshot still cites as absent after the cheap
      pass — a glob pathspec walks full history per uuid and is markedly slower (one probe
      command timed out at 10 minutes).
- [x] NEWEST-deletion-wins is preserved in the fallback (git streams newest-first, first hit
      wins), matching `_deleted_history`.
- [x] Held-out test: the fallback recovers an event when the directory-scoped walk is stubbed
      empty. Verified RED (fails with the fallback call removed) then GREEN.
- [x] Module-size: `fsck_repair` was at its 800-line cap, so the restore cluster
      (`_deleted_history`, `_deleted_path_for_uuid`, `_uuid_fallback`,
      `restore_deleted_sources`, `rebuild_with_restore`) moves to a new `fsck_restore` leaf —
      633/204 lines, both inside the 100-800 band. `fsck_repair` owns snapshot-source
      ACCOUNTING and the repair decision; `fsck_restore` owns recovering the bytes.
      `fsck_repair` re-exports the public names; `fsck_restore` imports
      `snapshot_missing_sources` lazily so the two do not form a cycle. Neither moved function
      carries a complexity-baseline entry, so the split adds none.
baseline.summary: restore_deleted_sources misses events deleted in a merge commit (git log --diff-filter=D skips merges)

baseline.description:
## Symptom

`sweep (macos, full suite)` fails on `main` at `6b034b9f8224` (run `33846424069`). The job has no `continue-on-error` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:370-373`), so it reddens the branch head.

```
19243 passed, 72 skipped, 422 warnings, 1 error in 2687.89s (0:44:47)
ERROR tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py::test_provisioning_installs_then_builds_and_leaves_the_bundle_in_place
  - subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['git', '-C', '/Users/runner/work/rebar/rebar', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD']'
    timed out after 5 seconds
```

The test itself PASSES. The error is in the autouse `_no_repo_commits` guard's post-test probe (`tests/conftest.py:774` -> `tests/_isolation.py:68,39`).

## Root cause (established, not assumed)

The cause is **runner contention**, not a leaked process/handle, and not the named test.

1. The premise that this test provisions a real Node toolchain is **false**. It drives a shell
   **stub** `npm` (`_SUCCEEDS`: `mkdir -p node_modules; exit 0`) under `tmp_path`. It is one of the
   cheapest tests in the file. There is no real `npm ci`/esbuild child to leak.
2. `git rev-parse HEAD` reads `.git/HEAD` plus refs and takes **no lock**. No leaked handle or child
   process can serialize against it, so the leaked-handle reading has no mechanism.
3. A patched clock is ruled out: CPython binds `from time import monotonic as _time` in
   `subprocess`, so `subprocess.run`'s timeout check is immune to a `time.monotonic` patch.
4. A leaked `PATH` is ruled out experimentally: `monkeypatch` (function-scoped, non-autouse) is
   finalized BEFORE the autouse guard's post-yield, so the probe runs with the session `PATH`.
5. `Popen: returncode: -9` shows the child was alive and killed by the timeout -- it was running,
   not wedged on a git-specific resource.
6. The same run emitted **400** `[rebar-ci-timing]` warnings (threshold 1.0s), topping out at
   `built_distributions fixture_setup elapsed=4.562s` on a different worker. Ordinary fixture setup
   on this runner reaches **91% of the probe's fixed 5s bound**.

So the defect is the **bound**, not the test: `GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5` is a single-sample fixed bound on a read-only idempotent probe that runs ~19,000 times under `-n 3` on a 45-minute macOS runner. 5s sits inside that runner's observed latency distribution, so the guard reports an infrastructure stall as a test ERROR.

## Approach

Make the probe **resilient**, not lenient. `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are read-only and idempotent, so a `TimeoutExpired` may simply be re-sampled: retry the probe up to `GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS` times, with no sleep between attempts -- the elapsed per-attempt timeout is itself the backoff, and adding a sleep would re-introduce the patched-`time.sleep` hazard that `_stable_subprocess_time` exists to avoid.

A **persistent** timeout still raises, unchanged. That is deliberate: `_isolation.head` already re-raises `TimeoutExpired` so the guard fails loudly rather than silently ceasing to detect a HEAD move, and that property must survive -- it is the "absence of execution reported as success" trap. The change absorbs a **transient** stall and leaves the **persistent** failure loud.

Explicitly not doing: skipping or marking the test on macOS (the test is innocent, and a skip would hide it), and not merely raising the per-attempt timeout (a re-exec is strictly better than a longer wait on one possibly-starved process).

## Scope

- `tests/_isolation.py` -- `_run_git_probe` gains the bounded retry and `GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS`.
- `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py` -- the `_blocking_git` shim gains the ability to block
  every probe from a given call onward (persistent) as well as exactly one (transient), plus the new
  tests below.

No `src/` change. `tests/conftest.py` and `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` are NOT modified: the guard's caller and the innocent test both stay as they are.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py` -- the guard's self-test suite, including:
  - a NEW test that a **transient** probe stall (one blocked call, then a responsive git) is
    absorbed and `head()` returns the correct sha -- RED before the fix (`TimeoutExpired`), green
    after;
  - the EXISTING `test_commit_guard_fails_explicitly_when_head_times_out` and
    `test_session_finish_fails_explicitly_when_porcelain_times_out`, re-pointed at a **persistent**
    block, proving the guard still fails loudly and has not been silently weakened;
  - the EXISTING `test_head_detects_a_commit` and `test_guard_fails_a_test_that_commits`, proving a
    real HEAD move is still detected.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck`.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`.
- `workflow_dispatch` of `test.yml` on the fix branch, proving `sweep (macos, full suite)` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The cause is established with quoted evidence that distinguishes contention from a leaked
      process or handle, with the rejected reading ruled out by mechanism rather than by assumption.
- [x] A transient probe stall no longer errors the test that happens to be running: a defect-seeded
      reproduction fails RED before the change and passes after.
- [x] The guard is not weakened -- a real HEAD move is still detected and still fails the test, and
      a **persistent** probe timeout still raises loudly rather than silently passing, each proven by
      a test that fails if the property is removed.
- [x] The failing e2e test is not skipped, marked, or excluded on macOS; it is left untouched.
- [x] `sweep (macos, full suite)` passes in a `workflow_dispatch` run of `test.yml` against the fix.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the mechanism-delta, predates-gate-parity and api-surface
      gate tests all pass.
baseline.summary: sweep (macos, full suite) fails on main: teardown git-HEAD probe errors after the e2e toolchain provisioning test added by 2600

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (the two `record()` call sites around the structured and agentic run paths, plus the `_call_label` fallback at runner.py:590) reads `req.target.get("ticket_id")` when building the usage-log row, but every producer of `target` writes the plural key `ticket_ids` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` and `src/rebar/llm/operations.py`). Result: 0 of the ~11,900 rows in `.rebar/usage.jsonl` carry a ticket, so per-ticket (and therefore per-review) cost attribution from the usage log is impossible, and `docs/llm-framework.md`'s claim that rows carry `ticket` is false. The eval ledger needs per-run attribution and this is the cheapest fix on that path.

## Approach

At all three read sites (the two `record()` call sites and the `_call_label` fallback at runner.py:590), read `ticket = target.get("ticket_ids")` and take `ticket = ticket_ids[0] if ticket_ids else None` — producers always write `ticket_ids` as a list (possibly empty), never omit the key, so the empty-list case is the real path to handle, not a missing key. Drop the backward-compat read of the singular `"ticket_id"` key: no producer writes it, so it is a dead shim with no live consumer. Correct the doc sentence in `docs/llm-framework.md`. If a run's `ticket_ids` has more than one element (a multi-ticket/graph run), only the first is attributed to the usage row — this is a known simplification, not full multi-ticket attribution; that is out of scope here.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (three read sites: both `record()` call sites and `_call_label`)
- `docs/llm-framework.md`
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` (or the existing runner usage test)

## Testing

Unit: a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[id]` yields a usage row with `ticket == id`; a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[id_a, id_b]` yields `ticket == id_a` (first-element rule, pinned by test); a request whose target carries `ticket_ids=[]` (the real empty-list producer path) yields `ticket=None`; a request whose target omits `ticket_ids` entirely also yields `ticket=None`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] New usage-log rows produced by a gate session carry the ticket id; checked by running one `review-plan` locally (or the Tier-1 commissioning run) and inspecting the rows. VERIFIED live in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`: rows from the `magnesian-subjective-ocelot` (efd4-847d-f7ad-47bc) review-plan run at 2026-08-30T01:33-01:35 UTC carry `"ticket": "efd4-847d-f7ad-47bc"` on `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier`/`plan-review-verifier-agentic`/`plan-review-coach` rows.
- [x] The regression test above passes in `make test`. VERIFIED: `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` (23/23) and `tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py` (all) pass; `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean.
- [x] `docs/llm-framework.md` describes the actual field. VERIFIED: `docs/llm-framework.md:540-542` describes `ticket` as populated from the first element of `ticket_ids`, absent when empty/missing.
baseline.summary: usage_log rows never carry a ticket id: runner reads target["ticket_id"] but producers write "ticket_ids"

# S9 — ADR + documentation for the provider seam and the two-tier support policy

## Context / Problem

After S1–S8 rebar has a provider seam, a tier policy, a Bedrock path, and tier-stamped verdicts — none of it written down. `docs/llm-framework.md:121-143` still describes provider support as "pydantic-ai resolves the provider from the model string" with no mention of tiers, Bedrock, or what a best-effort provider means for a signed verdict, and its `:131-133` local-server recipe describes behavior that only becomes true in S4. Without a recorded decision, the next Bedrock/gateway request reopens the same argument as a one-off, which is the failure mode this epic exists to end.

## Approach

Write one ADR recording the decisions and, importantly, the rejected alternatives with their evidence: the seam is pydantic-ai's `provider_factory` hook and capabilities come from `ModelProfile`; two support tiers with Anthropic and Bedrock first-class; native Bedrock rather than a gateway; LiteLLM rejected as an in-process dependency but reachable as a proxy; verdicts sign on every tier but stamp the tier. Then bring `docs/llm-framework.md` in line with what the code now does, including the Bedrock recipe, the tier table, and what tier means for an attestation consumer.

The ADR also records the two operational findings this epic turned up, so they are not rediscovered: the IMDS hop-limit constraint and its containment [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67], and the measured relationship between cross-region inference profiles and prompt caching [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].

**Alternative rejected:** documenting in `docs/llm-framework.md` only. That records the *what* but not the *why*, and rebar's ADR set is where rejected alternatives live — without them the LiteLLM and gateway options get re-proposed.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/00NN-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md` (new).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — the provider section (`:121-143`) and the env table (`:224-226`).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated.
- `README.md` — one line if the provider story is summarized there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the ADR exists, is `Accepted`, and names each rejected alternative (in-process LiteLLM, gateway-fronted
      Bedrock, refuse-to-sign off-tier, Bedrock API key in SSM, cross-provider fallback) with the evidence that
      rejected it
- [x] [operator-attested] every runnable command in `docs/llm-framework.md`'s provider section has been executed and produced the
      documented result, confirmed in a ticket comment
- [x] the docs state, for each tier, what is guaranteed (tests, parity) and what a consumer can infer from a
      verdict's stamped tier
- [x] [operator-attested] the documented generator produces NO diff to `docs/env-vars.md`, evidenced by the
      command and its empty-diff output quoted in a comment
baseline.summary: S9 — ADR + documentation for the provider seam and the two-tier support policy

baseline.description:
# Continuous auto-deploy: the running Gerrit environment reflects `main` without manual deploy or restart

## Why
Landing a change on `main` does NOT update the running environment. The **review-bot container's code**, the site `replication.config`, and the g2p config all require a MANUAL deploy (SSM / setup-*.sh) and sometimes a restart, causing drift + toil: epic 88ab S2's merge-review code landed on `main` but the running `compose-review-bot-1` still runs the pre-S2 image; the S3 `replication.config` fix had to be hand-applied via SSM. The deployed environment must AUTO-REFLECT `main` shortly after a change lands — WITHOUT ever destabilising the LIVE gate that contributors depend on to review + submit.

## What
### Trigger — RESOLVED: a systemd timer on the Gerrit host (option a; NOT GitHub Actions→SSM)
`rebar-autodeploy.timer` (every 2 min) runs `rebar-autodeploy.service` (oneshot). RATIONALE for the on-box timer over a GitHub-Actions `deploy.yml`→SSM: (1) NO new trust surface — the box already has an instance role and reads the PUBLIC mirror READ-ONLY (no GitHub→AWS OIDC/`ssm:SendCommand` grant, which would make the GH runner a lateral-movement path into the box); (2) self-contained + simplest to back out; (3) ~2-min poll latency is fine for a deploy loop.

### Deploy script (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, idempotent, flock-guarded)
- **flock** `/var/lib/rebar/deploy.lock` (`-n`) — overlapping fires skip; a long deploy is never re-entered.
- **deployed-sha** `/var/lib/rebar/deployed-sha`: on FIRST run (absent) INITIALIZE to the box's
  current HEAD WITHOUT deploying (adopt current state); write atomically (`mv` tmp) ONLY after success.
- **What to deploy (safety):** fetch `origin/main` from the mirror. The mirror's `main` only advances
  via Gerrit SUBMIT (post two-vote gate) → its tip is Verified BY CONSTRUCTION; deploy ONLY that tip,
  never an arbitrary ref. No-op when `origin/main == deployed-sha`.
- **Change detection (path-set per component):** `git diff --name-only deployed-sha..origin/main` ∩ a
  component manifest: review-bot (`src/rebar/**`, `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, `pyproject.toml`,
  `docker-compose.yml`), replication (`replication.config`), g2p (`gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`,
  `materialize-g2p-config.sh`).
- **Per-component apply (only if changed):** review-bot → `docker tag` current image `:prev`, then
  `docker compose up -d --build review-bot`; replication → re-materialise + autoReload (no restart);
  g2p → `materialize-g2p-config.sh`.
- **SCOPE BOUNDARY (v1):** covers review-bot container + replication.config + g2p config. `refs/meta/config`
  (project.config) is OUT of v1 (rare, security-sensitive, needs an operator-only Gerrit admin key):
  a change is DETECTED + signalled (metric + log), never auto-applied. Retry transient git/docker
  failures 3× w/ backoff; persistent failure → fail-safe (leave prior state + marker).

### Stability — live-pipeline safety (the load-bearing section)
The gate is FAIL-CLOSED: no LLM-Review vote ⇒ no submit. So a bad or careless deploy can FREEZE the whole pipeline. Hardening:
1. **Blast radius is bounded by construction.** Auto-deploy NEVER touches the `gerrit` container and
   NEVER modifies `refs/meta/config` (the labels/submit-rules/ACLs). `docker compose` is invoked with
   the EXPLICIT `review-bot` service only (never a bare `up` that could recreate `gerrit`); a guard
   asserts the `gerrit` container id is unchanged across the deploy. Gate INTEGRITY is thus not
   alterable by this mechanism — only the bot's code + replication/g2p config move.
2. **No Gerrit restart, ever.** Config changes use `autoReload` (replication) / materialise (g2p); only
   the review-bot CONTAINER restarts, and only when its code changed. Gerrit availability is untouched.
3. **In-flight reviews are delayed, not lost.** A bot restart drops in-flight webhook processing, but
   the EXISTING reconciler-backfill (events-log cursor) re-reviews any change missed during the
   restart window — so a contributor's vote is at most DELAYED by one restart, never dropped. The
   post-deploy health check confirms the reconciler loop is live.
4. **A broken bot deploy self-heals (never freezes the gate).** After `up -d --build`, an END-TO-END
   health check (30s timeout) verifies the bot is actually able to review (receiver `/health` + a
   probe that the review path is functional), NOT merely that the process is up. On failure →
   IMMEDIATE rollback to the `:prev` image + `up -d` + error marker; deployed-sha is NOT advanced. Max
   gate-frozen window = the health-check timeout, then service is restored to the known-good image.
5. **Circuit-breaker (no thrash on the live pipeline).** A per-target-SHA consecutive-failure counter:
   after 2 failed deploy attempts of the SAME `origin/main` tip, auto-deploy DISABLES itself
   (stop-file) + pages — it does NOT re-attempt the bad SHA every 2 min. An operator clears the
   stop-file after fixing forward. (Because the gate is fail-closed, thrashing restarts would be worse
   than pausing on a known-good image.)
6. **Config validated BEFORE it touches the running Gerrit.** replication.config / g2p config are
   parse-checked (`git config -f … --list`; g2p ini schema) BEFORE apply; a malformed config is
   SKIPPED (prior config retained) + alarmed — a bad config never breaks live replication/CI dispatch.
7. **Post-deploy pipeline-health gate.** deployed-sha advances only after a post-deploy check confirms
   the end-to-end gate still works (bot health OK; a canary confirms review + CI dispatch paths).

### Observability + back-out
Structured deploy log (from→to SHA + components) + `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (host-probe grep of an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, mirroring voter_errors) + a CloudWatch alarm w/ SNS action; the circuit-breaker stop-file is itself alarmed. Back-out: `systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer`; the manual path (compose-up.sh / setup-*.sh) is unchanged.

## Scope
The deploy orchestrator + systemd timer/service + stability guards + observability/back-out on the existing compose stack. Reuses the idempotent setup/materialise appliers. refs/meta/config auto-apply deferred (detect + signal). No change to gate semantics (S1/S2) or the feature-branch flow (88ab).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A change landing on `main` (post-gate + replicated) makes the running env reflect it with NO
      manual action, ≤ 5 min; live-measured latency recorded
- [ ] Idempotent + change-detected: a no-change run is a no-op; a relevant change re-applies ONLY the
      changed component(s) — verified for review-bot code, replication.config, and g2p separately
- [ ] review-bot rebuilt/restarted ONLY when its source-set changed (a docs-only `main` change does
      NOT rebuild it); after a code change the running bot reflects it end-to-end (a merge change gets
      the S2 merge-change tag from the auto-deployed bot)
- [ ] STABILITY — blast radius: the `gerrit` container is provably untouched across a deploy;
      `refs/meta/config` is never auto-modified; no Gerrit restart occurs (verified)
- [ ] STABILITY — self-heal: a deliberately-broken review-bot image triggers the health check to FAIL
      and rolls back to `:prev` (gate restored); deployed-sha not advanced (proven live)
- [ ] STABILITY — circuit-breaker: 2 consecutive failed deploys of a SHA DISABLE auto-deploy + alarm
      (no thrash); malformed replication/g2p config is rejected pre-apply (prior config retained)
- [ ] STABILITY — in-flight: a review dropped by the restart window is recovered by the reconciler
      backfill (delayed, not lost) — demonstrated
- [ ] Concurrency: overlapping fires serialized by flock; deployed-sha written atomically only on success
- [ ] project.config changes DETECTED + signalled (metric + log), not attempted (documented boundary)
- [ ] Deploy log + `deploy_errors` metric + alarm applied; back-out (disable the timer) tested; manual
      path still works
- [ ] Live-verified end-to-end on the running box (a real `main` change auto-deploys within the window)
baseline.summary: Continuous auto-deploy: running Gerrit environment reflects main without manual deploy or restart

Author ADR 0106 defining **remote-anchored below-horizon HISTORY reclamation** whose PRIMARY lever is **commit/tree collapse** (retired-event GC is a secondary companion, not the pack lever), and promote docs/concurrency.md §I1 'permanent retention' (epic b306) from a follow-up note to an implemented+cross-referenced model. This ADR is the causal-stability contract that unblocks S1-S3. (ADR number 0106 — 0105 was taken by an unrelated ADR that landed on origin/main.)

Scope (docs-only): the horizon config key (default 30d, portable, no CI-provider dependency); the remote-reachability computation (collapse checkpoint reachable from the sync remote's tickets ref for >= N days); the stale-clone detection + FORCED remote-override protocol on reconnect (a clone whose last convergence is older than N days overrides local with remote rather than reintroducing pre-collapse history by rebase); the **C1-C5 causal-stability boundary at the commit/tree-rewrite level**; SNAPSHOT authorship_ledger carriage AND enforce_since re-anchor (both applied) for signature/authorship verifiability; the portable rewrite primitive and per-backend publish-swap; and a proof that invariants I1-I9 still hold. State the accepted residual: a >N-day-drifted clone's divergent local work is discarded. (Re-scoped 2026-08-29 from '.retired-only' to the commit/tree-collapse lever - see epic comment 'Child-roster re-scope'.)

Note: ADR numbering is a bijection — the ADR file is paired with a `docs/adr/.numbers/0106` marker and the generated `docs/adr/README.md` index, both DERIVED by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py` from `docs/adr/*.md` and checked by `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` + `gen_adr_index.py --check` in the CI docs-gates action (`.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml`), NOT in `make lint`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` exists with the ADR shape (`# ADR 0106:`
  title, `- **Status:**`, `## Context`, `## Decision`, `## Consequences`).
- [x] The ADR defines the N-day horizon as a portable config key (default 30d, with a stated rationale)
  and NO single-CI-provider trigger (the `project.portability` criterion applies).
- [x] The ADR specifies remote-reachability (collapse checkpoint reachable from the sync remote tickets
  ref for >= N days) and the stale-clone FORCED remote-override protocol on reconnect.
- [x] The ADR states the C1-C5 causal-stability boundary at the commit/tree-rewrite level and how
  signature/authorship verifiability is preserved (SNAPSHOT authorship_ledger carriage AND enforce_since
  re-anchor, both applied).
- [x] The ADR names the history-rewrite primitive as core-git (`git fast-import` / `mktree`+`commit-tree`,
  NO third-party `git filter-repo`) and, per backend, the publish-swap: git-ref `--force-with-lease` CAS
  for git remotes, and an exclusive push-locked bundle-set replacement bypassing the `git-remote-s3`
  auto-doctor for the S3 backend — citing the auto-doctor never-discard-a-head resurrection hazard
  (ADR 0093 / `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`) and proving its bypass safe under C1-C5.
- [x] The ADR proves invariants I1-I9 hold under reclamation and names the accepted residual
  (a >N-day-drifted clone's divergent local work is discarded).
- [x] The ADR-number bijection artifacts are regenerated: `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py` creates the
  `docs/adr/.numbers/0106` marker (content = the ADR filename) and adds a 0106 entry to the generated
  `docs/adr/README.md` index; no ADR cross-reference dangles.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` §I1 is promoted from 'follow-up' to implemented and cross-references ADR 0106.

## Verification
- `grep -n '^# ADR 0106:' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` and
  `grep -n '^## \(Context\|Decision\|Consequences\)' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md`
  confirm the ADR shape and title.
- `grep -nE 'I[1-9]' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` (I1-I9 proof present),
  `grep -nE 'C1|C5' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` (C1-C5 boundary present),
  `grep -n 'ADR 0093\|s3_doctor' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` (S3 hazard cited),
  `grep -n 'force-with-lease' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` (git-ref CAS named),
  `grep -n 'discard' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` (accepted residual stated).
- `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py` then `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` and
  `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` pass (marker `docs/adr/.numbers/0106` present, README
  regenerated, bijection intact).
- `grep -n 'ADR 0106\|implemented' docs/concurrency.md` confirms the §I1 promotion + cross-reference;
  `grep -n '0106' docs/adr/README.md` confirms the index entry.
- `make lint` passes (ruff/format only); `rebar review-plan unlikely-zealous-skua` re-run confirms the
  plan is admissible.
baseline.summary: ADR: remote-anchored retired-event GC + stale-clone override (N-day horizon)

baseline.description:
Run the one-time reclaim. **Do not start until A1-A5, A6-0a..0d and Epic B's B6 are closed**, and until A6-0a has been on `main` >=24 h with an observed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run on a descendant SHA (older binaries ignore the epoch field, so they would sail past the guard). session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Protocol
1. **Agent** disables `reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (`gh workflow disable`,
   which also blocks `workflow_dispatch` and therefore `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` self-redispatch);
   **asserts** no reconcile run is in progress (poll `gh run list`, not drain-and-hope); asserts the
   **Gerrit review queue is empty** — zero sessions stops new pushes, but a patchset pushed just
   before the window can still have its `LLM-Review` vote fire during it, and every vote writes a
   ticket; break-glasses `refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}` if held.
2. **Agent** pauses the AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` and the host LaunchAgents
   `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` (04:00) and `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update` (whose hourly
   rollback-guarded pipx reinstall could silently revert the global `rebar` to a pre-A6-0a build
   mid-window). **[operator-attested] Operator** confirms **zero active sessions** and all
   **`rebar-mcp` servers stopped** (a long-running MCP holds an in-process store handle and does not
   hot-reload). Gerrit needs no separate confirmation: every Gerrit push comes from a session.
3. **Agent** converges the local tracker (`fetch` + `reset --hard origin/tickets`, 0-ahead verified).
   This covers all 48 sibling worktrees at once — their `.tickets-tracker` are **symlinks to the one
   store**. The four other real trackers on the host point at different GitHub repos.
4. **Agent** deletes the pre-rewrite ref pins (A6-0d), runs the strip in a fresh **unfiltered** clone,
   verifies the pre-push assertions, and pushes with **`--force-with-lease`**.
5. **Agent** asserts non-resurrection: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is
   **false**, and no clone-fetched ref has the old tip as an ancestor.
6. **Agent** converges the review-bot clone over SSM (`fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets` on
   `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`). Reverts to **[operator-attested]** if the issued AWS
   credentials do not permit `ssm send-command` against `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`.
7. **Agent** lands the `enforce_since` re-pin through Gerrit, mapped via the commit-map.
   `rebar.toml:115` is the only literal SHA in the system; with `require_authenticated = false`
   (`:106`) `verify_authorship.py:531-550` returns early and never reads it, so there is **no CI
   deadlock** and the change lands normally. `verify.opcert_enforce_since` is unset.
8. **Agent** re-enables the GitHub workflows, the AWS timer, and both LaunchAgents.
9. **Agent** verifies the ACs below and **notifies the operator** that the tickets branch is
   available for sessions again.

## T11 migration-safety answers
- **Expand/contract:** yes — A6-0a's reader ships and is deployed before the epoch value exists.
- **Batching:** n/a, single atomic ref update.
- **Resumability: NONE, stated.** A force-push is not resumable. Mitigation: all correctness
  assertions run on the scratch clone **before** publishing, so a wrong graph never reaches origin;
  the push itself is atomic per-ref.
- **Dual-write window:** none — the store is quiesced; the epoch guard replaces dual-write as the
  stale-writer defence.
- **Rollback:** restore from the A6-0d bundle + `--force-with-lease` back to the old tip. Known
  limit: rollback re-diverges anything already converged, so consumers must be re-converged in the
  same order as the forward path. **No event bytes are ever altered** — only commit SHAs — so the
  rewrite itself cannot lose ticket data.
- **T4 destructiveness:** an irreversible force-push to the authoritative store of a live system,
  chosen deliberately to reclaim 92% of the branch, gated on operator-confirmed quiescence, an
  off-repo bundle, a fail-closed epoch guard, and pre-push assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB** (from 1.04 GiB; the measured strip
      result is ~94 MiB) and `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree.
      **Holds only because B6 landed first.** Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] Commit count and merge-commit count on `tickets` are **unchanged** versus the pre-rewrite
      recording (measured at window time, never hardcoded). Tier: **repo assertion**.
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <sha> --format json`, run pre-rewrite
      against the old SHA and post-rewrite against the mapped SHA: the **stderr summary counts** are
      identical AND the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` from the JSON report is
      identical **ignoring `commit`**. (JSON mode puts only the report array on stdout and the summary
      on stderr; the report lists only non-verified events; every `commit` is a rewritten SHA. The
      command **exits 1** when `enforced_not_verified > 0`, so do not require exit 0.) Tier: **CLI
      subprocess, both sides**.
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** and `size-pack` growth is **< 1 MB**. The ancestry assertion is
      what actually proves non-resurrection. Tier: **repo measurement after an observed vote**.
- [ ] No ref a default clone fetches has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier: `ls-remote` +
      `merge-base` loop, computed at window time.
- [ ] Operator confirmation of zero active sessions and stopped MCP servers is recorded as a comment
      before step 3. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] A reconciler pass completes green after step 8, and `rebar fsck` is clean. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
Operational — no `src/` changes. Uses the A6-0c script and A6-0d helpers; touches `rebar.toml` (`enforce_since`) via Gerrit in step 7.

Scope: M (operational). Depends on A5, A6-0b, A6-0c, A6-0d, and Epic B's B6.
baseline.summary: A6-1: execute the reclaim window (quiesced, guarded, agent-executed except the zero-sessions confirmation)

## Context / Problem
`rebar review-code` runs the same four-pass reviewer the Gerrit bot casts `LLM-Review`
with, so an author can preview code-review findings locally before pushing — the exact
analog of `rebar review-plan` for the plan gate. But the code-review on-ramp never
mentions it: the plan-review author can discover their local self-check, the code-review
author cannot. This closes that discoverability asymmetry so both gates read symmetrically.

## Approach
Surface `rebar review-code` in the same three places plan review's local self-check is
surfaced: the author on-ramp (`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, printed by `rebar explain
review`), the docs index (`docs/README.md`), and the canonical `AGENTS.md` pointer.
Rejected: adding a new `rebar explain` topic for local code review — the existing `review`
guide is the right home, and a second topic would fragment the on-ramp rather than fix
discoverability.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md  (new "Preview the review locally" section, intro cross-link, loop-diagram preview step)
- docs/README.md               (index entry mentions the local preview)
- AGENTS.md                    (code-review pointer names `rebar review-code`)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` has a "Preview the review locally" section teaching
      `rebar review-code`, incl. the `[agents]` extra and `REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW`
      enabling requirement; verified by
      `grep -q 'REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md && grep -q '## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.
- [ ] The loop diagram in `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` shows the optional local
      `rebar review-code` preview step; verified by
      `grep -q 'rebar review-code — optional local preview' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.
- [ ] The `docs/README.md` passing-code-review index entry names `rebar review-code`;
      verified by `grep -A2 'passing-code-review.md)\*\*' docs/README.md | grep -q 'rebar review-code'`.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` code-review pointer names `rebar review-code`; verified by
      `grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] The intro anchor link resolves to the new section heading (GitHub-generated anchor
      `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push` matches the heading text); verified by
      `grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.

## Criteria correction (2026-07-24)
The criteria above originally named `docs/passing-code-review.md`. Commit c2bfbe217
("package author guides in-package so `rebar explain` works from any directory") later moved
the guide to `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` and left the old path a pointer stub,
which made every grep in this ticket false even though the work was delivered and is intact at
the new path.

This ticket was first closed with `--ref f90850861` (the commit the work landed in). That
verified, but it left the criteria asserting checks that no longer hold — inaccurate state in
the shared ticket store. Per the remedy now documented in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
("When the acceptance criteria no longer match reality", ticket 4636-432a-1871-4d74), the
criteria have been corrected to name the guide's real location and the ticket re-closed against
them. The delivered content is unchanged; only the paths in the criteria moved.
baseline.summary: Make local code review as discoverable as plan review

baseline.description: Implement the NEW code-review attestation once its ADR (refutable-meaningful-borzoi) is accepted. review-code RECORDS/SIGNS a reusable code-review op-cert bound to the ADR-defined diff/ref material fingerprint and ticket binding; the merge gate CONSUMES it per the ADR's trust-boundary ruling (whether/where a reused attestation may satisfy LLM-Review +1). Reuses the shared seam from citreous-arboreous-coral. BLOCKED until the ADR lands — the op-cert kind, material fingerprint, ticket binding, and merge-vote policy are all ADR outputs. Independently verifiable: sign a review, reuse it on an unchanged ref (accept), mutate the ref (reject).
baseline.summary: Code-review op-cert: producer (review-code signs) + consumer (merge-gate reuse)
