## Summary
`test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` fails on git 2.54 CI (Linux, all Python tiers) with `error: invalid object <sha> ... error: Error building trees` — a writer's locked `append_event` commit fails, is swallowed, and the write is lost (`lost == swallowed_write_raises`, counts vary 17..232/250).

## Proven root cause (confirmed by reproduction + forensics)
The tickets store is a linked git worktree (`.tickets-tracker`) that SHARES the parent repo's object database. On git >= 2.47, `git commit` triggers `git maintenance run --auto --detach` — a DETACHED background process that runs `git repack -d -l --cruft --write-midx`. Under concurrent writes, MULTIPLE such detached maintenance processes run OUTSIDE rebar's write lock, racing the concurrent writers and each other, and corrupt the shared object DB (missing/dangling objects; hundreds of `tmp_pack_*` garbage files). git's own docs warn a concurrent `git gc` "may corrupt the repository"; plain gc/maintenance-detach does not take the object-db lock. Directly observed: 4+ concurrent `git maintenance run --auto --detach -> git repack --cruft` processes live during the failure, while rebar's own write lock shows 0 overlaps (it serializes its own git perfectly — the corruption is 100% from git's detached maintenance escaping the lock).

## Why prior fixes did not resolve it
- WU-1 (epic 97e7) unset `gc.auto` + set `gc.autoDetach=true`, trusting "stock git gc is
  safe by construction" — that reasoning covers only SERIAL reachability, never a CONCURRENT
  background repack racing in-flight writes.
- 4c1c's `_recover_from_invalid_object` heal treats the downstream symptom (poisoned index)
  and cannot recover a HEAD-referenced missing object (read-tree HEAD re-poisons).
- `gc.auto=0` does NOT disable it: git >= 2.47 uses `git maintenance run --auto` (gated by
  `maintenance.auto`), not the legacy `git gc --auto`.

## Evidence
- git 2.47.3 -> 0 repro; git 2.54.0 -> reproduces (Docker, isolated).
- Diagnostic: zero-concurrency / writers-only / single-pair all PASS; only the full
  concurrent config fails, with live detached maintenance repack processes captured.
- Prior art: git-gc/git-maintenance docs; ArgoCD #25101 (identical: git 2.47 detached
  maintenance escaping a lock on a shared git dir); GitLab/Gitaly `gc.auto=0`; Homebrew
  `gc.autoDetach=false`.

## Fix direction (pending final experimental confirmation)
Disable background auto-maintenance on the tickets worktree — `maintenance.auto=false` (+ `gc.auto=0`, + `*.autoDetach=false` defense-in-depth) — so no detached maintenance can race writers; PRESERVE WU-1's bounded-growth by running gc/maintenance SERIALIZED under rebar's write lock (`git maintenance run --task=gc`). Confirm `maintenance.auto=false` vs foreground `autoDetach=false` empirically before choosing.

## Reproduction Steps
1. On git 2.54, init a rebar store; run 5 writer procs (SIGNATURE/REVIEW_RESULT bursts) +
   4 pruner procs (enqueue + `_prune_queue_events`) concurrently against it.
2. Observe some writers' `append_event` fail with `invalid object ... Error building trees`
   and background `git maintenance run --auto --detach` processes running.
- Expected: no writes lost. Actual: writes lost (corrupted shared object DB).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_gc_config_unit` disables background auto-maintenance (`maintenance.auto=false` +
  `gc.auto=0`) so no detached `git maintenance`/`git gc` can run concurrently with writers;
  proven by a test asserting the store's effective config after `init`.
- [ ] Bounded-growth (WU-1) preserved via a serialized-under-write-lock gc/maintenance path,
  OR an explicit, documented decision to defer it.
- [ ] `test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` re-enabled (skip
  removed) and green on the git-2.54 CI matrix (proving command: that test on CI).
- [ ] gc-config + ensure-drift-matrix tests updated to the new posture; docs (sync.py,
  concurrency.md, init.py `_gc_config_unit`) corrected to state that concurrent background
  maintenance is unsafe.
baseline.summary: enrich-prune flake root cause: git>=2.47 detached 'git maintenance run --auto' corrupts the shared tickets-worktree object DB

baseline.description:
# Continuous auto-deploy: the running Gerrit environment reflects `main` without manual deploy or restart

## Why
Landing a change on `main` does NOT update the running environment: the review-bot container's code,
`replication.config`, and g2p config need a MANUAL deploy (SSM / setup-*.sh) + sometimes a restart.
This drifts + toils (S2's merge-review code landed but the running bot is pre-S2; the S3 replication
fix was hand-applied). The environment must AUTO-REFLECT `main` — without ever destabilising the
LIVE, FAIL-CLOSED gate (no LLM-Review vote ⇒ no submit; a bad deploy could freeze all submissions).

## What
- **Trigger (RESOLVED): on-box systemd timer** `rebar-autodeploy.timer` (2-min) → `.service` oneshot
  running `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`. Chosen over a GitHub-Actions→SSM `deploy.yml` because it adds
  NO GitHub→AWS trust surface (no OIDC/`ssm:SendCommand` grant that would make the GH runner a
  lateral-movement path); the box already reads the PUBLIC mirror read-only + has an instance role.
- **Loop:** `flock -n` guard; fetch `origin/main`; no-op when `== deployed-sha`
  (`/var/lib/rebar/deployed-sha`, initialised to current HEAD on first run WITHOUT deploying, written
  atomically only on success). Deploy ONLY the mirror `main` tip (Verified-by-construction: it only
  advances via Gerrit submit). Change-detect per component via `git diff --name-only
  deployed-sha..origin/main` ∩ a path manifest (review-bot: src/rebar/**, Dockerfile.reviewbot,
  pyproject, docker-compose; replication: replication.config; g2p: ini + materialize script).
- **Apply only what changed (v1 = review-bot ONLY):** review-bot → tag current image `:prev`, sync
  source (see Box-adaptation), `docker compose build && up -d review-bot`. **replication/g2p AND
  `refs/meta/config` are DETECT-ONLY in v1** — a change is signalled (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`), never
  auto-applied (their correct apply needs a live-site copy + SSM PAT re-fetch whose failure modes must
  not sit in the unattended path guarding a fail-closed gate; v2 follow-up). See Box-adaptation §3.

## Stability — live-pipeline safety (load-bearing)
1. **Bounded blast radius:** never touch the `gerrit` container (explicit `review-bot` service target
   + a post-deploy assert the gerrit container id is unchanged); never modify `refs/meta/config` (gate
   labels/rules/ACLs). No Gerrit restart — only the bot container restarts, only on a code change.
2. **In-flight reviews delayed, not lost:** a restart drops in-flight webhooks, but the existing
   reconciler-backfill re-reviews them; the post-deploy health check confirms the reconciler is live.
3. **Self-heal, never freeze the gate:** after `up -d`, an END-TO-END health check (30s timeout —
   liveness: process up + `/health` 200) gates success; on failure → immediate
   rollback to `:prev` + `up -d`; deployed-sha NOT advanced. Max frozen window = the health timeout.
4. **Failure handling = capped exponential backoff, NOT hard-disable** (mature-OSS consensus: Flux
   retryInterval/backoff; Argo CD retry backoff duration/factor/maxDuration; k8s controller-runtime
   ItemExponentialFailureRateLimiter 5ms→1000s; systemd v254 RestartSteps/RestartMaxDelaySec):
   - rollback keeps last-known-good RUNNING; retry the deploy with backoff base 60s, factor 2, cap
     15m — never auto-disable the loop (a hard-disable strands the env stale until a human acts).
   - **SHA-keyed reset (Argo CD's rule):** persist last-attempted-SHA + failure count; a NEW
     `origin/main` tip RESETS the backoff to base (a fix-forward deploys promptly); a known-bad SHA is
     not re-attempted faster than the cap (no thrash) and is never permanently blacklisted.
   - **Outer storm guard:** systemd `StartLimitIntervalSec`/`StartLimitBurst` on the RUNNING bot
     service catches a crash-looping container (→ failed, needs `reset-failed`) — reserved for the
     pathological case, NOT the primary retry path.
5. **Config validated before it touches Gerrit:** parse-check replication/g2p config pre-apply; a
   malformed config is skipped (prior retained) + alarmed. (Belt-and-suspenders to AC below.)

## Defense-in-depth: a CI gate that rejects malformed config (so it never reaches `main`)
`make config-check` — parse-validate every infra config: `git config -f {replication,project}.config
--list`; python configparser on the g2p ini template; `docker compose config -q`; `bash -n` on
`infra/**/*.sh`. Wired into `test.yml` (⇒ runs in `gerrit-verify` ⇒ the `Verified` gate), so a
malformed config FAILS CI and can NEVER land on `main` — the auto-deploy never encounters one at
runtime (the runtime pre-apply check in Stability §5 is the belt-and-suspenders for a direct box edit).

## Observability + back-out
Structured deploy log (from→to SHA + components) + `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (host-probe grep of an
`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, mirroring voter_errors) + a CloudWatch alarm w/ SNS action; the
backoff/failure state is alarmed. Back-out: `systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer`; the
manual path (compose-up.sh / setup-*.sh) is unchanged.

## Scope
Deploy orchestrator + systemd units + stability guards + the CI config-check + observability/back-out
on the existing compose stack. Reuses the idempotent setup/materialise appliers. refs/meta/config
auto-apply deferred (detect + signal). No change to gate semantics (S1/S2) or the 88ab flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A post-gate `main` change auto-reflects on the box (no manual action) ≤ 5 min; latency
      live-measured. Idempotent: a no-change run is a no-op; a change re-applies ONLY the changed
      component(s) — verified for review-bot code; a replication.config / g2p / refs-meta change emits
      `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` and is NOT auto-applied in v1 (detect-only)
- [ ] review-bot rebuilt/restarted ONLY on a source-set change (docs-only change ⇒ no rebuild); after
      a code change the running bot reflects it end-to-end (a merge change gets the S2 merge tag)
- [ ] Blast radius: the `gerrit` container is provably untouched; `refs/meta/config` never
      auto-modified; no Gerrit restart. project.config changes are detected + signalled, not attempted
- [ ] Self-heal: a deliberately-broken bot image FAILS the health check ⇒ rollback to `:prev` (gate
      restored), deployed-sha not advanced (proven live)
- [ ] Failure backoff: repeated failure uses capped exponential backoff (base 60s→cap 15m), keeps
      last-known-good running, and a NEW `main` SHA resets the backoff (fix-forward deploys promptly);
      the loop never auto-disables; the systemd StartLimit storm-guard is in place
- [ ] CI config-gate: `make config-check` runs in `test.yml`/`gerrit-verify` and FAILS on a
      deliberately-malformed config (proven) — a malformed config cannot reach `main`
- [ ] flock serializes overlapping fires; deploy log + `deploy_errors` metric + alarm applied;
      back-out (disable timer) tested; manual path still works; live end-to-end auto-deploy verified

## Box-adaptation of the deploy mechanism (grounded in live box i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

Live SSM inspection changed two assumptions in v1–v4, so the mechanism is adapted and v1's
**auto-apply surface is narrowed to the review-bot container only** (config = detect+signal).
The safety guarantees (blast radius, self-heal, backoff, config-check-at-CI, flock) are unchanged.

### Observed box facts (SSM)
- `/opt/rebar` is a plain **copy** of the repo root — NOT a git checkout (no `.git`; uid 502; a
  `.deployed_ref` marker). It is the compose `build.context` (`../..`) for both services; review-bot
  bakes source at **build** time (no source bind-mount), so a rebuild picks up new code.
- Real compose working dir: `/opt/rebar/infra/compose` (services `gerrit`, `review-bot`).
- The ONLY runtime state under `/opt/rebar` is `infra/compose/.env` (SSM-sourced secrets, git-ignored,
  0600, regenerated at boot by `fetch-secrets.sh`). All Docker state lives OUTSIDE `/opt/rebar` —
  named volumes (`gerrit_git`/`gerrit_index`/…) + bind mounts under `/var/gerrit/*` — so a source
  resync cannot touch it. systemd 252. review-bot health `http://localhost:8000/health` → `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Adapted mechanism
1. **Mirror clone (self-bootstrapping).** autodeploy maintains its own **regular** git clone at
   `MIRROR_DIR=/var/lib/rebar/mirror` — `git clone https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` (public HTTPS,
   no auth; a *regular* clone, NOT `--mirror`/`--bare`, so `origin/main` resolves for the diff/rev-parse
   ops). autodeploy self-bootstraps it if absent and **aborts if the remote is not `https://`** (supply-
   chain guard). ALL git ops — fetch `--prune`, `rev-parse origin/main`, the
   `git diff --name-only deployed..target` component change-detection, checkout of the target — run there.
2. **Source sync = `rsync -a --delete $MIRROR_DIR/ /opt/rebar/`** with hard excludes protecting runtime
   state: `--exclude '/.git'`, `--exclude 'infra/compose/.env'`, `--exclude '/.deployed_ref'`, plus the
   dev/state set (`.venv .terraform .serena .claude .tickets-tracker`). `.env` + Docker volumes are never
   touched; ownership kept 502:502.
3. **Apply — review-bot ONLY (v1 narrowed).** On a review-bot source-set change
   (`src/rebar/** infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot infra/compose/docker-compose.yml pyproject.toml`):
   tag current image `:prev` (guarded — skip if none, first-build has no rollback target), `docker compose
   build review-bot && up -d review-bot` in `/opt/rebar/infra/compose`, END-TO-END health-gate (liveness:
   process up + `/health` 200), rollback to `:prev` on failure, blast-radius assert (gerrit container id
   unchanged), `docker image prune -f`. **replication.config, g2p, and refs/meta/config are DETECT-ONLY in
   v1** — a change is signalled (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker) for a manual operator apply, never auto-applied.
   Rationale: their correct apply needs live-site copy (`/var/gerrit/site/etc/…`) and an SSM PAT re-fetch
   (`materialize-g2p-config.sh`) whose failure modes should not sit in the unattended path guarding a
   fail-closed gate; they are rare and already hand-applied. Auto-apply of config is a documented v2 follow-up.
4. **State/backoff unchanged.** `deployed-sha`/backoff/first-run-adopt as in v1; first run seeds the marker
   from `/opt/rebar/.deployed_ref` if present (else the mirror tip), still WITHOUT deploying. A persistent
   **git-fetch failure is instrumented** (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR fetch_failed`) so a stalled mirror alarms.

### systemd + installer + scope additions
- **systemd fix:** `ExecStart=/opt/rebar/infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (not `/opt/rebar/src/…`),
  `DEPLOY_REPO=/opt/rebar`, add `MIRROR_DIR=/var/lib/rebar/mirror`.
- **`infra/scripts/install-autodeploy.sh`** (new; mirrors `install-observability.sh`): self-bootstraps the
  mirror clone, installs the `.service`+`.timer` unit files, `daemon-reload`. **Ships the timer DISABLED**
  (staged rollout: enable only after a manual dry-run passes).
- The health check is a **liveness** probe (process up + `/health` 200), not a deep readiness check — the
  AC wording is narrowed accordingly.

### Additional acceptance criteria (box-adaptation)
- [ ] autodeploy syncs source into the copy-based `/opt/rebar` via a self-bootstrapping regular mirror
      clone (HTTPS-enforced) + `rsync --delete` with excludes; a live resync provably leaves
      `infra/compose/.env` byte-identical and the `gerrit` container + Docker volumes untouched
- [ ] v1 auto-applies review-bot ONLY; a replication/g2p/`refs/meta/config` change is detected + signalled
      (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`), never auto-applied
- [ ] `install-autodeploy.sh` installs units with the **timer disabled**; a manual dry-run
      (`systemctl start rebar-autodeploy.service`) applies a real `main` advance end-to-end on the box
      (review-bot rebuilt from synced source, health OK), evidenced by the deploy log SHA transition
baseline.summary: Continuous auto-deploy: running Gerrit environment reflects main without manual deploy or restart

## Context
F12 verification on commit 8a036765705f5ef0e7db4fa21e0926e51d15bafd exposed a long-running `test_resign_routes_through_pin_collecting_sign_path`. An isolated run on current `origin/main` commit 51621917bfc635d7673cb0519a400afda12eb2cb reproduced the delay. The test body reported PASS after 201.81 seconds. The process exited after 524.52 seconds. Pytest attributed 5.15 seconds to setup and 0.06 seconds to teardown. A one-second process sample during the remaining post-PASS interval showed recursive filesystem deletion dominated by `unlinkat` and `rmdir`.

Closed tickets `grindable-deviant-angwantibo` and `asbestos-popular-tench` repaired omitted private `--basetemp` arguments in nested pytest children. This reproduction occurs in an ordinary test session and needs separate lifecycle tracing. Active ticket `famished-disgustful-gypsymoth` changes timeout coverage for fixture phases. Active ticket `expectable-slowwitted-squeaker` covers a local Git child timeout. Neither ticket records this test or its post-PASS deletion interval.

## Plan
- Reproduce the delay in an isolated current-main worktree and capture phase timings, the active temporary path, file counts, allocated bytes, and a Python stack during the post-PASS interval.
- Trace the fixture and pytest lifecycle that creates and removes the snapshot tree.
- Distinguish test-call snapshot materialization cost, session-finish cleanup cost, shared temporary-root cleanup, and host filesystem contention with discriminating experiments.
- Determine whether pending Gerrit change 2141 guards the affected phase or only changes the terminal failure mode.
- Establish the intended behavior from the maintained timeout and test-runtime policy.
- Confirm the root cause and defect origin before proposing any repair.
- If a repair is warranted, update this ticket with the fix plan and file impact, obtain a current plan review, and prove the repair with a RED-first held-out oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A current-main reproduction records call time, total time, and the post-PASS stack.
- [x] Runtime evidence identifies the lifecycle phase and the changeable artifact responsible for the delay.
- [x] Discriminating experiments reject the surviving alternative explanations.
- [x] The relationship to `grindable-deviant-angwantibo`, `asbestos-popular-tench`, `famished-disgustful-gypsymoth`, and `expectable-slowwitted-squeaker` is recorded.
- [x] The defect origin is proven or the RCA records the completed unattributable search.
- [x] The RCA is recorded before any repair begins.
- [x] Any repair uses a RED-first oracle, preserves unrelated test behavior, and passes its declared verification.
baseline.summary: pytest session cleanup spends minutes deleting plan-review snapshot tree

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Every other story in this epic is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake transport. That is the right tier for each of them, but it cannot exercise the failure modes that only appear against a real tracker: actual JQL evaluation over two projects, real per-project permissions and key allocation, real issue creation, and — the one that matters most — whether a pass scoped to one project can contaminate another. A multi-project bridge that is wrong in that direction writes real issues into the wrong project, which is expensive to detect and worse to undo. This story is the justified live canary the shared test-design standard allows for external-service mapping, run once the functionality is otherwise complete.

## Approach

Rehearse the whole feature live, against an **isolated store copy**, with dry-run gating at every step.

**Isolation comes first.** The rehearsal never runs against the production tickets branch. A copy of the tickets branch is published to an encrypted S3 remote — the capability delivered by epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`, which is why this epic depends on it — and the rehearsal store points its `sync.remote` at that copy. Before any mutating command, the harness asserts the configured remote is the S3 copy and not the production remote, and aborts otherwise. This is a precondition assertion, not a comment: it runs first and fails the test if the store is misconfigured.

**Dry-run gating is the contamination control.** Each scenario runs `bridge preview` first and asserts the previewed mutation set contains **only** targets in the intended project, with an empty intersection against every other configured project. Only then does `bridge sync` run. A preview that names a target outside the intended project fails the scenario before anything is written — which is the same fail-closed posture as the cross-project guard, applied at the harness level.

**Project configuration.** The mapping is loaded with the two live Jira Cloud projects, `REB` and `DIG`, plus dummy projects that exist only in the mapping and never in Jira — these exercise the "configured but empty" and "unknown to the tracker" paths without consuming real projects. Repo configurations deliberately vary: one project mapped to a single repo, one mapped to two repos, and one mapped to none, so the defaulting behaviour is observed across all three shapes rather than only the common one.

**Cleanup is designed in, not bolted on.** Every issue the rehearsal creates carries a run-scoped label. Cleanup is a single JQL sweep over that label across both live projects, and the run is not considered finished until a follow-up query for the label returns zero issues in each project. The label is generated per run so a failed earlier run cannot cause a later one to delete issues it did not create.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_multi_project/` (new) — the rehearsal harness and its scenarios
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — the operator runbook for performing and cleaning up the rehearsal

## Testing

Tier: a live end-to-end rehearsal against real Jira Cloud, which the shared standard permits for external-service mapping when a fake cannot reach the mechanism — here, genuine cross-project isolation. It is gated to an opt-in external suite so ordinary CI never touches live Jira.

Scenarios, each preview-gated then applied:

- **Inbound from both projects.** An issue created in `REB` and one in `DIG` are both ingested in a
  single pass; each resulting ticket records the project it came from and the repos mapped to that
  project.
- **Outbound to both projects.** Two rebar tickets, one per project, each land as an issue in their
  own project and nowhere else.
- **Not-synced.** A ticket with an explicit empty project produces no issue in either project, and no
  outbound mutation naming it appears in the preview.
- **Legacy resolution.** A ticket with the project field absent syncs to the recorded legacy default
  and to no other project.
- **Repo-config variety, both directions.** Inbound tickets from the single-repo, two-repo and
  zero-repo projects receive exactly those repo lists; outbound tickets created under each config
  reach the correct project regardless of their repos value, confirming repos never influences
  routing.
- **Contamination guard, the negative control.** An update aimed at a project absent from the mapping
  raises `CrossProjectTargetError` in preview and writes nothing — verified by querying both live
  projects afterwards and confirming no issue changed.
- **Promote-only.** Setting a project on an unbound ticket then syncing creates the issue; attempting
  to change a bound ticket's project is refused and the existing binding is unchanged.
- **Capability stamp.** With two projects in the mapping, `.store-compat.json` carries
  `multi-project-bridge`, and a binary lacking that capability refuses to write to the rehearsal
  store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The rehearsal aborts before any mutation if the configured remote is not the S3 store copy;
      checked by pointing it at a non-S3 remote and asserting it exits non-zero having written
      nothing.
- [ ] Issues created in `REB` and `DIG` are both ingested in one pass with the correct source project
      and repos recorded; checked by querying both live projects and asserting both tickets' fields.
- [ ] Rebar-created tickets targeting each project land in that project only; checked by querying
      both projects and asserting each issue exists in exactly one.
- [ ] A ticket with an explicit empty project creates no issue in either project; checked by a
      post-run query of both projects for the run label finding no issue for it.
- [ ] All three repo configurations produce the expected repos on inbound tickets and correct routing
      on outbound ones; checked per configuration.
- [ ] An update targeting an unmapped project is refused in preview and changes nothing live; checked
      by comparing both projects' issue state before and after.
- [ ] Every scenario's preview contained only targets in its intended project; checked by asserting
      an empty intersection against every other configured project for each preview.
- [ ] All issues created by the run are removed and a JQL query for the run label returns zero
      results in both `REB` and `DIG`; checked as the final step of the run.
baseline.summary: Live multi-project rehearsal against REB and DIG on an isolated S3 store copy

baseline.description:
## What
Add `batch_stage_and_commit(tracker, items)` (and a batched `write_and_push` variant) to `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: commit MANY events under ONE write-lock acquire + ONE `git commit`, all-or-nothing. `items` is a sequence of `(ticket_id, event_dict)`.

## Why
The single-event write path (`stage_and_commit`) commits one git graph per event (~3.3 commits/event). The write lock (`_store/lock.py`) is NOT re-entrant, so a caller cannot loop `stage_and_commit` under one lock. A dedicated batch primitive is the seam bulk callers (the importer, B2) use to collapse N commits into 1. Batching is invariant-safe because replay/dedup/union-merge/SNAPSHOT-compaction key off each event's per-event UUID, not commit boundaries (each event stays its own I2 uuid-named file).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` only. Single-event `stage_and_commit`/`write_and_push`
  behavior unchanged (the reversibility guarantee).
- Validate + canonical-stage every event BEFORE taking the lock; then under ONE lock:
  atomic-rename each temp into `{ticket}/{ts}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json`, one `git add`, ONE
  `git commit`.
- All-or-nothing rollback: any failure (validation, rename, add, non-recoverable commit)
  unstages AND unlinks ALL already-placed paths, not just the failing one.
- Generalize `_recover_from_unmerged` to re-add the FULL batch path list on retry.
- Empty batch = no-op (no lock, no commit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `batch_stage_and_commit(tracker, items)` in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: one lock acquire, N I2 uuid-named files, exactly one commit; returns the event count
- [ ] `batch_write_and_push` variant: batch commit then ONE best-effort push
- [ ] All-or-nothing rollback on validation / rename / `git add` / non-recoverable `git commit` failure: every already-renamed path unstaged from the index AND unlinked from disk
- [ ] `_recover_from_unmerged` (bug 6818 UU self-heal) re-adds the full batch path list on retry — a batched commit self-heals a pre-existing unmerged `.bridge_state/*`
- [ ] Empty batch is a no-op (no lock taken, no commit made)
- [ ] Single-event `stage_and_commit`/`write_and_push` path unchanged; existing regression tests (`tests/unit/test_store_write_index_reset_on_failure.py`, `tests/unit/test_store_write_unmerged_recovery.py`) stay green
- [ ] New unit tests in `tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py` cover: N-in-one-commit, canonical-byte parity vs single path, empty no-op, validation/commit rollback, next-write-uncontaminated, UU self-heal
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all green
baseline.summary: B1: batch_stage_and_commit — batched-commit write primitive in _store

baseline.description:
Store only the SET of Jira keys seen last pass instead of the full ACLI payload. prev_snapshot is **228.1 MB / 4.5 MB per day** — the largest term after A1. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Measured effect
Over the newest **400 real revisions**: **218 of 399** consecutive pairs have an **identical key set** (so they become byte-identical and produce no commit at all), and when it changes the mean symmetric difference is **1.78 keys**. Key-set payload at HEAD is **19,960 bytes** vs a **27.1 MB** full payload.

## Why this is safe — gate G1 was cleared empirically, not by reasoning
A corpus mutation-diff ran the real differ over **four real snapshot pairs** with full prev vs key-set prev and found **zero difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect**. The feared `_compute_mutations_emit_both` field-clearing does not reach Jira: `_mutation_to_batch_dict` reads `payload["changed_fields"]` for updates, which branch-3 never sets, so `fields` collapses to `{}` and `update_issue(key)` short-circuits at `acli.py:181-185` with zero subprocess and zero network.

**It also removes a latent bug.** With today's full prev, keys in prev-but-not-curr emit `(outbound, create)` carrying the departed issue's raw field blob — and that payload shape DOES reach `create_one`. Corpus: **973-998 spurious Jira creates** whenever the fetch window shrinks or the project is re-targeted. A key-set emits none.

Shape constraint: store a **dict** `{jira_key: {}}`, not a `set` — `check_dual_identity_complete` and `_emit_both`'s `local_state[key] or {}` guards assume dict entries.

## Rollback (mandatory artifact)
The G1 corpus diff ran **forward only**. Before merging, run it **backward** (key-set -> full, the revert direction) and record the result. Deleting `prev_snapshot.json` is **not** a safe default escape hatch: an empty prev is exactly what made the differ re-derive 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`), because `differ.py:455-490` emits an inbound CREATE for every curr-only key unless a `rebar-id:` label suppresses it — bound pairs are safe, unbound in-window keys are not. If deletion is ever used, it MUST be followed by a cap-0/no-write pass proving zero inbound creates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over **>=4 real snapshot pairs** shows **zero
      difference** in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect. Tier: **repo-level corpus
      script** committed under the experiments path.
- [ ] The **reverse-direction** diff (key-set -> full) is recorded on this ticket as the rollback
      artifact, showing the revert path emits no unexpected inbound creates. Tier: **repo-level
      corpus script**.
- [ ] Branch-2 regression is gone: with a key-set prev and >=900 prev-only keys, **zero**
      `(outbound, create)` mutations are emitted. Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations`.
- [ ] `check_dual_identity_complete` and the binding-walk adopt-skip set behave identically with
      `{}` entries. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] prev_snapshot at HEAD is <=64 KB after one pass. Verify: byte measurement.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` (prev persist), `run_differs.py`, tests, corpus script

Scope: M. Depends on A4-1.
baseline.summary: A4-2: narrow prev_snapshot.json to a bare key-set {jira_key: {}}

baseline.description:
## Why
Existing stores must learn they are behind the registry without hot-path cost — Rails `CheckPending` for a School-B registry: compare the applied-set to the registry ids, nudge on write activity, cheaply, rate-limited, never breaking a write.

## What
WS1 landed the registry as `rebar._store.ensures` and exports, on that module: `REGISTRY_IDS` (the frozen id tuple), `registry_ids() -> frozenset[str]`, `applied_ids(tracker) -> set[str]` (parses `.ensure-applied`, degrading absent/garbage/non-list → empty set), and `APPLIED_MARKER` (`.ensure-applied`). WS2 adds the write-path pending-nudge to THAT module (no new module) plus the `EnsureConfig` config section.

**Pending computation (compute-once, per process).** Add `maybe_emit_pending_hint(tracker)` to `rebar._store.ensures`. It computes `pending = registry_ids() - applied_ids(tracker)` and caches the resulting SET of pending ids in a module-level dict keyed by the canonical tracker path — so `.ensure-applied` is read AT MOST ONCE per store per process (a converged store caches the empty set and every later write is O(1), zero further reads). The cache holds the id SET (not a bare boolean) precisely so the emitted hint can NAME the pending units. When `.ensure-applied` is absent/unreadable/garbage, `applied_ids` returns the empty set so `pending` = all registry ids (a pre-feature store is genuinely behind) — the hint fires, but the rate-limit bounds it to ≤1 per interval so there is no per-write spam.

**Where it hooks (single choke point).** Call `maybe_emit_pending_hint` best-effort at the end of `event_append.write_and_push` (after a successful commit+push). Covered via `write_and_push`: `_seam.append_event` (comment/tag/edit/link/set_*/sign) and the `composer` create/edit/revert path (which call `append_event` → `write_and_push`). We hook ONLY `write_and_push`, NOT `_seam.append_event` (which itself calls `write_and_push`), so there is no double-firing. Best-effort, NOT universal — the ACCEPTED GAP set commits inline (raw `git commit`, NOT through `write_and_push`) and is intentionally NOT hooked: `claim` (`txn.claim_core` + `push_after_commit`), `transition`/close (`txn.transition_core` + `push_after_commit`), `compact.py`, `delete.py`, plus the ensure units themselves and `fsck --repair` batches. A rate-limited nudge is not a correctness mechanism, and these mutators still surface pending state on the NEXT covered write. Pure reads (list/show/…) never touch the hook.

**Emission + rate-limit.** Emit a single WARNING that names the pending unit ids and points to `rebar fsck --repair` (the EXISTING heal verb — WS3 folds the ensure-sweep into it), but only when `pending` is non-empty AND the last-hinted timestamp in `.ensure-hinted` is older than the configured interval. Reading `.ensure-hinted` is symmetric with `.ensure-applied`: an absent OR unparseable/garbage `.ensure-hinted` is treated as "never hinted" (`last = None`), so the hint fires (and then writes a fresh timestamp) rather than being silently suppressed. On a decision to hint, rewrite `.ensure-hinted` with the current time via `fsutil.atomic_write` (temp-in-same-dir + os.replace — same helper WS1 uses for `.ensure-applied`). `.ensure-hinted` (WS2-owned, git-ignored: ADD to `_GITIGNORE` at init.py:38-48) holds a single timestamp. A fresh auto-init'd worktree already has a current `.ensure-applied` (WS1 wrote it), so `pending` is empty and it NEVER hints.

**Config.** Add an `EnsureConfig` section to `_config_schema.py` (`ensure.hint_interval_secs`=86400, `ensure.hint_enabled`=true) with the full scaffolding: the `@dataclass EnsureConfig`, an entry in `_SECTION_CLASSES`, coercers in `_SECTIONS` (`_as_int(minimum=0)` / `_as_bool`), an `ensure` field on `Config`, and a re-export from `config.py`. Adding the section to `_SECTIONS` is automatically picked up by `config._env_signature()` (which iterates `_SECTIONS`) so the env layer + cache key work with no further edits. The hint reads these via `config.load_config(...).ensure`.

**Env-var documentation decision.** The env overrides are auto-derived by `config._canonical_env_name` as `REBAR_ENSURE_HINT_INTERVAL_SECS` / `REBAR_ENSURE_HINT_ENABLED` — no per-key entry needed. These names are built DYNAMICALLY (never appear as a literal `os.environ["…"]`), and `docs/env-vars.md` is GENERATED by `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, whose AST scanner only captures literal `os.environ`/ `os.getenv` reads. So the ensure env vars are (a) NOT captured by the drift gate and (b) `docs/env-vars.md` must NOT be hand-edited (the gate would regenerate it and fail on the diff). The `[ensure]` section and its two env overrides are documented in `docs/config.md` instead (WS4 also covers them in `docs/migrations.md`). No generated file is edited.

**Fail-silent.** `maybe_emit_pending_hint` swallows ALL of its own exceptions — including a lazy-import ImportError/SyntaxError from `rebar._store.ensures` / `rebar.config` — behind a debug log, so a write NEVER fails because of it. There is no import cycle: `event_append` lazy-imports `ensures` inside `write_and_push` (module load order unaffected), and `ensures` never imports `event_append`. A rare double-hint under parallel agents (two processes both past the interval) is accepted.

## Scope
In: `maybe_emit_pending_hint` in `rebar._store.ensures` (compute-once pending-set cache, rate-limit via `.ensure-hinted` + `fsutil.atomic_write`), the best-effort `write_and_push` hook (lazy import, fail-silent), the `.ensure-hinted` `_GITIGNORE` entry, `EnsureConfig` scaffolding, and the `[ensure]` docs in `docs/config.md`. Out: `run_ensures()` + `.ensure-applied` format/write (WS1), `fsck --repair` fold + `ensures: N/M` line (WS3), `docs/migrations.md` (WS4), the exhaustive hot-path/idempotency suite (WS5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `maybe_emit_pending_hint(tracker)` computes `pending = registry_ids() - applied_ids(tracker)` and caches the pending id SET once per process per canonical tracker; a converged store reads `.ensure-applied` at most once and does zero further reads on subsequent writes (verified by test (e): a spy on `applied_ids` shows exactly one read across two hint calls on the same tracker)
- [ ] `.ensure-hinted` read degrades symmetrically to `.ensure-applied`: an absent or unparseable/garbage marker is treated as "never hinted" so the hint fires (not silently suppressed), then a fresh timestamp is written
- [ ] The hook is called best-effort only from `event_append.write_and_push` (covering `_seam.append_event` leaf writes and the composer create/edit/revert path, which funnel through it); `_seam.append_event` is NOT separately hooked (no double-fire); the accepted-gap inline committers (claim/transition via `txn.*_core`+`push_after_commit`, compact, delete) are NOT hooked and this is documented; pure reads are untouched
- [ ] The WARNING names the pending unit ids and points to `rebar fsck --repair`, rate-limited via `.ensure-hinted` (written with `fsutil.atomic_write`; added to `_GITIGNORE`) using `ensure.hint_interval_secs` (86400s); suppressible via `ensure.hint_enabled` and its auto-derived env override `REBAR_ENSURE_HINT_ENABLED` (no generated-file edits; `docs/env-vars.md` untouched)
- [ ] `EnsureConfig` scaffolding complete (`@dataclass EnsureConfig` + `_SECTION_CLASSES['ensure']` + `_SECTIONS['ensure']` coercers + `Config.ensure` + `config.py` re-export); the `[ensure]` section + its two env vars are documented in `docs/config.md`
- [ ] The hook swallows all its own exceptions incl. lazy-import failures (debug-logged) so a write never fails; there is no import cycle between `event_append` and `rebar._store.ensures`
- [ ] WS2 owns four concrete tests: (a) a pending store (empty/absent `.ensure-applied`) emits exactly one WARNING naming pending units + `rebar fsck --repair`, and re-emits only after the interval; (b) a fresh auto-init'd worktree (current `.ensure-applied`) emits NO warning; (c) `ensure.hint_enabled=false` suppresses the warning even when pending; (d) fail-silent — when the pending computation raises (e.g. `applied_ids` patched to raise), `maybe_emit_pending_hint` swallows it (no exception propagates) and a real `write_and_push` still commits successfully with the hook installed (covering AC5); (e) read-dedup — a spy/counter on `applied_ids` shows exactly one read across two `maybe_emit_pending_hint` calls on the same tracker (covering the ≤1-read cache claim)

# Plan-review Pass-2 `prerequisite_verify` fails on Bedrock "Grammar compilation timed out"

## The defect (root cause PROVEN — see the RCA comments)

[rebar:18ae-27e9-b651-4b71] (commit `6c8daf7945`, 2026-08-05 00:48) added an exact-model-id row to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` in `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py`:

    "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6": {"native_structured_output": True, ...}

That row is applied AFTER the `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` family rule (`_is_claude -> False`) and therefore wins, flipping this model from `PromptedOutput` to `NativeOutput`. rebar consequently began sending Bedrock a JSON Schema for constrained decoding. Anthropic compiles that schema into a grammar and enforces a documented **180-second compilation timeout** plus complexity caps (**24 optional parameters**, 16 union-typed). rebar's verification contracts carry **22-36 optional parameters** — every field declares a `default=`, so every field is optional in JSON Schema — and the compile exceeds the ceiling. Bedrock returns HTTP 400 `ValidationException`, either "Grammar compilation timed out" (~185s) or "Schema is too complex" (~50-60s).

Result: the Pass-2 verify step cannot run, every finding degrades to `no-verification`, the review lands INDETERMINATE and unsigned, and the ticket cannot be claimed.

**Scale:** 27 live 400s across ~9 review targets; zero before 00:48. Affects BOTH gates — plan-review (`plan_review_verification`, 31 optionals) and the Gerrit `LLM-Review` code-review gate (`code_review_verification`, 36 optionals, pinned `model: standard` = sonnet-4-6 at `gates/code-review.yaml`).

Measured (live, us-east-1, serial, one variable at a time):

    review_result             10 optional  NATIVE  OK      14.0s
    completion_verdict        14 optional  NATIVE  OK      29.0s
    verification              22 optional  NATIVE  FAIL   185.3s   <- fails UNDER the documented cap
    plan_review_verification  31 optional  NATIVE  FAIL   185.4s
    code_review_verification  36 optional  NATIVE  FAIL   185.4s
    plan_review_verification  (same, PROMPTED)     OK      11.2s   <- the remedy works today
    plan_review_verification  descriptions stripped (8719->2403 B), NATIVE  FAIL  59.8s

## Approach

The fix is to stop sending a grammar the provider cannot compile, and to say so clearly when we do. Three parts, all inside the existing seams — no new subsystem.

**1. Gate native selection on schema complexity (`src/rebar/llm/structured.py`).** `output_mode(model_cls, caps, thinking=...)` already receives the contract class, so the decision belongs there and no signature changes.

**The count MUST recurse — this is the load-bearing detail.** The reproducing contracts' 22/31/36 optional parameters are NOT top-level properties: `VerificationOutput` has exactly ONE top-level property (`verifications`, a list), and the optional fields live inside `$defs` (`Verification`, `PlanSeverityAttrs`, `Binary`), reached through `items` and nested `properties`. A predicate that counted only top-level properties would score every one of these contracts at 0-1 and downgrade NOTHING, silently reproducing the bug while appearing to fix it.

So the predicate walks the RESOLVED schema: it dereferences/expands `$defs`, descends through `items` and nested object `properties`, and at EVERY object node counts each property absent from THAT node's own `required` list (optional), plus each property carrying `anyOf`/`oneOf` or a list-valued `type` (union). Correctness is pinned by reproduction: the walker must return exactly `review_result 10`, `completion_verdict 14`, `verification 22`, `plan_review_verification 31`, `code_review_verification 36` — the live registry counts measured above.

`output_mode` returns `PromptedOutput` above the bound even when `caps.native_structured_output` is True. Bound: **16 optional / 12 union**, module constants with the measurement table cited beside them. 16 sits inside the measured gap (14 = largest PASS, 22 = smallest FAIL), nearer the PASS side so a contract that grows one field does not silently cross it; deliberately BELOW Anthropic's published 24 because `verification` proves the published number under-predicts. It is a BOUND, not a disable: across the live registry it downgrades exactly the three measured-failing contracts and leaves the other 16 native.

**1b. Also gate on whether the STACK can send a native constraint at all (variant B).** Measured after this plan was first written: on botocore 1.40.61 (the main checkout) boto3 rejects the request CLIENT-SIDE in 0.0s — `Unknown parameter in input: "outputConfig"` — for EVERY contract however small (`ticket_digest` is 722 bytes). That is the same root cause hitting a different wall, and it is size-independent, so the complexity bound cannot catch it. `output_mode` therefore checks stack support FIRST (a cached, never-raising introspection of the Bedrock Converse operation's input shape, scoped to Bedrock via the capability record's own `prompt_cache_style`, failing closed to `PromptedOutput` when support cannot be shown) and only then applies the complexity bound.

This mirrors the prevailing OSS pattern: langchain-aws defaults `method="function_calling"` and makes native `json_schema` opt-in; instructor, llama_index, DSPy and BAML likewise do not send a native grammar by default. It also restores rebar's own pre-18ae posture for the contracts that need it, WITHOUT reverting 18ae's measured benefit for small contracts.

**2. Classify the rejection distinctly (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py`).** Add `translate_schema_complexity_rejection(exc, model_id)` returning a typed error, mirroring the existing `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` (`failure.py:371`) exactly — same conjunctive shape (`status_code == 400` or `ValidationException` in text, AND a documented phrase from a small closed set), same "tried FIRST in the broad except" wiring in `structured_run.py`. The message names the model, the contract, and the remedy. This is what stops a schema-complexity rejection being reported as an opaque provider outage (AC1).

**3. Fall back rather than fail closed (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`, minimal).** In `_pai_structured`, when the NativeOutput branch raises and `translate_schema_complexity_rejection` recognises it, log loudly and retry ONCE on the existing PROMPTED branch (proven to work: 11.2s). The fallback is never silent — it logs at WARNING and the classified cause is attached — which answers the strongest objection to auto-fallback (TanStack/ai
#682 stripped theirs partly because it hid the signal). Kept small because this module is at
750/800 LOC: the predicate and message live in the two modules above, not here.

Retry-without-change is deliberately NOT used: the rejection is a deterministic property of the request (27 identical failures), so a plain retry burns another ~185s and fails again.

## Non-goals (explicit)

* **AC3 — partial credit for a failed verify: WON'T FIX** (operator decision, 2026-08-05). The
  degrade is deliberate: `plan_review_recovery` preserves Pass-1 findings and routes them through
  `pass3_decide(None)`, the kernel's documented no-verification degrade, stamping
  `verify_failed: True`. Signing over unverified findings would weaken what a plan-review
  attestation means. Fixing the routing removes the trigger instead.
* **Not reverting 18ae's row.** Native output demonstrably works for small contracts on this model
  (14.0s / 29.0s measured) and 18ae's tests pin it; the row is not wrong, its scope is — it asserts
  a model fact where the real constraint is per-schema.
* **Not restructuring the verification contracts.** Making their fields `required` would reduce
  optionality, but the defaults are load-bearing (an older/absent verifier must ABSTAIN, per
  `verify_models.py`). That is a contract change, not a bug fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a Bedrock/Anthropic schema-complexity rejection (`Grammar compilation timed out` /
      `Schema is too complex`, 400 `ValidationException`) is classified DISTINCTLY and is not
      surfaced as a generic provider outage; the operator message names the model and the contract
- [x] `output_mode` returns `PromptedOutput` for a contract whose optional-parameter count exceeds
      the measured bound, even when the model's capability record says native is available
- [x] the plan-review Pass-2 verify step completes against `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`
      for the `plan_review_verification` contract (31 optionals) that reproduces the failure today
- [x] the same protection covers the code-review gate's `code_review_verification` contract (36
      optionals), which is pinned to the same model class and fails identically
- [x] a regression test drives the classification path with a SIMULATED provider
      grammar-compilation rejection and asserts it is not reported as an outage (no live call)
- [x] a test pins `output_mode`'s complexity gate with a fixture that varies BOTH poles — a
      small contract still routes NativeOutput on a native-capable model, a large one routes
      PromptedOutput — so the test cannot pass vacuously
- [x] 18ae's existing pins still pass: the measured small-contract cells keep NativeOutput

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_structured.py tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py -q
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
    make lint && make typecheck
    # live replication of the original report:
    rebar review-plan 895c-3eb2-043a-4de1

## Evidence

RCA + measurements in this ticket's comments. Logs: `/tmp/rp3.log`, `/tmp/rp4.log`, `/tmp/c827-planreview{,2}.log`, `/tmp/4ca2_rev*_err.log`, `/tmp/03ef-review4.out` ("Schema is too complex"), `/tmp/rp94a3c.log`. Discovered while attempting to earn the claim attestation for [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e].
baseline.summary: Plan-review Pass-2 verify fails on Bedrock 'Grammar compilation timed out', degrading every finding to INDETERMINATE

## Context / Problem

An `s3://` ticket-store remote is only safe with a `git-remote-s3` helper that has the `IfNoneMatch` per-ref lock: a live experiment this session proved that a client **without** that lock is exactly what leaves two `<sha>.bundle` files for one ref, producing the multiple-bundles corruption that makes the store unclonable. Today nothing stops rebar from driving an `s3://` remote with a missing or too-old helper — the failure would surface later as silent store corruption rather than at the point of misconfiguration.

The sibling story ("Declare the optional [s3] extra…", now landed) provides `require_s3_helper()` in `src/rebar/_optional.py`, which confirms the helper is on `PATH` and `>=0.3.2`, raising `OptionalDependencyError` (message naming `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'` and the `>=0.3.2` minimum) otherwise. This story **wires that guard in** so any store operation that would drive an `s3://` remote fails closed early with that actionable message.

## Approach

Detect "S3 mode" by the **remote URL scheme** — no new config key (reuse the existing `sync.remote`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` `SyncConfig.remote`). Treat a remote as S3 mode iff its resolved URL starts with `s3://` or `s3+zip://` (git-remote-s3's own schemes).

Add one small internal preflight helper in `src/rebar/_store/push.py`, `_require_s3_helper_if_s3_url(remote_url: str) -> None`, that takes an already-resolved remote URL string and, when it starts with `s3://`/`s3+zip://`, calls `rebar._optional.require_s3_helper()` and lets its `OptionalDependencyError` propagate; for any other scheme (or an empty string) it is a no-op. Taking the URL as an argument keeps it pure and lets each call site reuse the resolution it *already* performs — no new gitutil shell-out is added (the review flagged `resolve_remote_url` as redundant with the existing seams below).

**The best-effort contract, resolved explicitly.** `push_tickets_branch` is best-effort by default (returns `None` on delivery failure; raises `PushDeliveryError` only when `strict=True`), and it has **two** auto-push callers: `write_and_push` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`, the append-event family) calls it **without** a try/except, and `push_after_commit` (`src/rebar/_store/push.py`, the inline-commit paths — `transition`/`reopen`/`claim`/`compact`/`delete`) wraps it in a best-effort `except Exception` that must be made to **re-raise** `OptionalDependencyError` so it does not swallow the deliberate S3 fail-closed override. A missing/too-old S3 helper is **not** a transient delivery hiccup to swallow — it is a hard misconfiguration that must halt loudly to prevent the unlocked push that corrupts the store. So the S3 preflight raises `OptionalDependencyError` **unconditionally, independent of `strict`**, deliberately overriding best-effort. Because `write_and_push` does not catch it, the raise propagates and aborts the write with the actionable message and a non-zero exit; the local commit `stage_and_commit` already made is durable, and only the corrupting push is prevented (the store stays locally consistent and `fsck` surfaces `PUSH_PENDING`). This deliberate exception to the best-effort contract is the intended fail-closed behavior the AC requires.

Call sites, all keyed off the **already-resolved** URL (no second resolution):

- **`push.py` synchronous (`always`) path** — `push_tickets_branch` already resolves the
  configured remote's URL at `src/rebar/_store/push.py:418`
  (`remote_url = _git(base_path, "remote", "get-url", remote)`). Immediately after that
  resolution succeeds (i.e. after the existing `returncode != 0` / `remote-not-found` skip at
  lines ~419-426, so an **unresolvable/unset remote keeps its existing best-effort skip and is
  NOT treated as S3**), call `_require_s3_helper_if_s3_url(remote_url.stdout.strip())` before
  the push retry loop.
- **`push.py` `async` arm** — before it detaches the synchronous child (lines ~361-401),
  resolve the configured remote URL the same way and call the preflight, so an async-mode
  misconfiguration also fails fast **in the parent** (surfacing the message) rather than only
  inside the detached child whose stderr is discarded. The `off` arm is left untouched (it
  never pushes, so there is no corruption risk and no helper requirement).
- **`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` init/mount** — in `_mount_or_create_branch` (line ~383),
  after `remote_name = tickets_remote(repo)` is resolved, resolve its URL with the module's
  existing `_git(repo, "remote", "get-url", remote_name)` and call the same preflight, so a
  misconfigured `s3://` remote is caught at setup, not at first write.

Rationale: keying off the URL scheme reuses the field git-remote-s3 already keys off, needs zero schema/migration work, and keeps the blast radius to `s3://`/`s3+zip://` remotes only; guarding at init (fail-fast at config time) plus both push arms (belt-and-suspenders on the hot write path) funnels every path through the single tested `require_s3_helper()` seam.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — add `_require_s3_helper_if_s3_url()`; call it in the synchronous
  `always` path (after the existing URL resolution at line ~418) and in the `async` arm before
  detaching. No new remote-URL resolution is introduced (the line-418 `_git ... remote get-url`
  is reused).
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — call the preflight in `_mount_or_create_branch` after the
  remote name is resolved, using the module's existing `_git` shell-out.
- `tests/` — CLI/subprocess tests for the fail-closed and no-op behavior.

Explicitly **not** in scope: no new helper in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` (the existing `_git ... remote get-url` at `push.py:418` and init.py's `_git` are reused); no config schema change.

## Testing

Tier: **CLI subprocess** against a real temporary git repo configured with an `s3://` `sync.remote` (no AWS calls needed — the guard fails before any network I/O). Oracles:
- Failure (helper missing, init): with `git-remote-s3` not on `PATH` and `sync.remote` an
  `s3://` URL, `rebar init` exits non-zero and prints the message naming
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`.
- Failure (helper missing, push): the same configuration on a synchronous write/push path
  exits non-zero with the same actionable message.
- Edge (helper too old): monkeypatch the version probe to `0.2.9` → same fail-closed message
  naming the `>=0.3.2` minimum, on both init and push.
- Edge (`s3+zip://` scheme): with an `s3+zip://` `sync.remote` and the helper absent, init/push
  fail closed identically (the scheme is treated as S3 mode).
- Happy / no-regression (non-S3 remote): with a `file://` or GitHub-style remote, the preflight
  is a no-op and init/push succeed with **no** helper installed and no behavior change.
- No-regression (unresolvable remote): with `sync.remote` naming a remote that does not exist
  (`git remote get-url` fails), the push path keeps its existing best-effort `remote-not-found`
  skip and does **not** raise the S3 error (the missing URL is not misread as S3 mode).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With `sync.remote` pointing at an `s3://` URL and the helper absent, store init and the
      synchronous push path both **exit non-zero** with a single actionable message naming
      `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`. The preflight raises `OptionalDependencyError`
      **unconditionally** (independent of `push_tickets_branch`'s best-effort `strict` flag),
      propagating through the uncaught `write_and_push` call and the `OptionalDependencyError` re-raise in `push_after_commit`. Verified by the init and push
      CLI-subprocess failure oracles.
- [x] With the helper present but below `0.3.2`, the same paths fail closed naming the
      `>=0.3.2` minimum. Verified by the too-old edge oracle.
- [x] An `s3+zip://` `sync.remote` is treated as S3 mode and fails closed identically when the
      helper is absent. Verified by the `s3+zip://` edge oracle.
- [x] With a non-`s3://`/`s3+zip://` `sync.remote`, the preflight is a no-op: init and push
      succeed with no helper installed and no behavior change; and a remote whose URL cannot be
      resolved keeps the existing best-effort `remote-not-found` skip (it is not misread as S3).
      Verified by the no-regression and unresolvable-remote oracles.
- [x] S3 mode is detected purely from the remote URL scheme (no new config key added) and no
      new remote-URL resolution seam is introduced — the existing `_git ... remote get-url` at
      `push.py:418` and init.py's `_git` are reused. Verified by inspection and by the config
      schema being unchanged in this story.
baseline.summary: Fail closed when an s3:// ticket remote is used without a locking git-remote-s3 helper

## Observed signal
Error sweep window 2026-08-30T21:20:00-07:00..2026-09-01T11:58:00-07:00 (2026-08-31T04:20:00Z..2026-09-01T18:58:00Z) found GitHub Actions run 33455923923 (`Jira DC Exact-Patchset Parity`, workflow_dispatch, triggered by JoeOakhartNava) failed before executing the live DC parity body.

Failing job: `jira DC exact-patchset parity (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)` at step `Verify the checkout landed on the exact patchset SHA`.

Error: `checked-out HEAD (d6c37680805fc8ae013832dd4c09c1fb100a1e0b) does not match the requested Gerrit patchset revision (a22257e7d10e3d079ee676cbb38d2b39811d0fd5) — refusing to run the DC lane against the wrong ref.`

## Confirmed root cause
Gerrit change 2466 patchset 1 (`refs/changes/66/2466/1`) resolves to `d6c37680805fc8ae013832dd4c09c1fb100a1e0b`; patchset 2/current resolves to `a22257e7d10e3d079ee676cbb38d2b39811d0fd5`. Run 33455923923 combined the patchset-1 refspec with the patchset-2 revision. The pinned `checkout-gerrit-change-action` first checks out its `ref` default (`github.sha`) but then fetches `GERRIT_REFSPEC` and unconditionally checks out `FETCH_HEAD`, so the workflow landed on the stale refspec commit and only the later guard detected the mismatch.

The guard's fail-closed behavior is correct. The defect is that `.github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` delegates the final checkout to a refspec-first third-party action even though this lane's authoritative requested commit is the `(GERRIT_REFSPEC, GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION)` pair.

## Fix implemented
Gerrit change 2508 landed as `a85cb4781845ccf0d8c0375adce9a01391ba4bc8` and replaced only this workflow's first checkout step with explicit shell plumbing equivalent to the pinned action's fetch protocol, but with the missing SHA validation inserted before checkout. This is not a new protocol: the pinned action source at `lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action@f87b90a3370e62dad310797fedc7fd3700c75832` defines `fetch_from_gerrit()` as `git fetch ${{ inputs.gerrit-url }}/${{ inputs.gerrit-project }} ${{ inputs.gerrit-refspec }}`, and run 33455923923 shows the workflow supplied `gerrit-url: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com` plus `gerrit-project: rebar`, so the fallback URL form is `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar`. The action fetches the GitHub mirror through `origin`; the workflow now recreates that source explicitly as `https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git` in the initialized workspace.

Implemented behavior:

1. Initialize a git repository in the empty runner workspace and add `origin=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git`.
2. Fetch `GERRIT_REFSPEC` into `FETCH_HEAD` from `origin`; if that fails, fetch the same refspec from `https://${{ vars.GERRIT_SERVER }}/${{ inputs.GERRIT_PROJECT }}`. Do not check out either fetch result yet.
3. If neither fetch succeeds, fail with a clear error naming both attempted sources and the refspec.
4. Compare `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD^{commit}` to `GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION`; if they differ, fail with a clear dispatch-input error naming the refspec SHA and expected SHA. This is the repaired form of run 33455923923.
5. Only after the fetch/refspec SHA matches, check out `GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` explicitly in detached HEAD mode and verify `git rev-parse HEAD` equals it before any Python/Jira DC setup or live DC operation runs.

`tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py` now executes the embedded workflow checkout script against temporary git remotes and covers the success path, mirror-to-Gerrit fallback path, stale refspec/revision mismatch path, and unfetchable-refspec path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The Jira DC exact-patchset parity workflow checks out the exact requested Gerrit patchset SHA before any live DC operation runs; checked by `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py tests/unit/test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py -q`, `actionlint .github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml`, Gerrit `Verified+1`, and the existing `HEAD == GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` guard embedded in the workflow.
- [x] If the requested patchset refspec cannot be fetched from either the GitHub mirror or Gerrit fallback, the workflow fails with a clear fetch/input error rather than landing on a different commit; checked by a focused temporary-git test in `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py`.
- [x] The workflow records enough evidence for a future CI dispatch to prove the live Data Center lane ran from `HEAD == expected_sha`; in-session completion rests on AC1/AC2 plus Gerrit review/Verified results, and the future live dispatch evidence is a GitHub Actions run id whose summary lists the verified SHA.

## Context
Maintained guidance conflates generic HMAC manifest signatures with current plan-review and completion-verifier operation certificates. ADR 0044 defines the DSSE and SSHSIG substrate. ADR 0049 defines asymmetric, environment-attributed operation certificates and legacy compatibility.

## Plan
- Use the existing file-impact set as the positive edit scope: `README.md`, `docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, and `docs/sample-ticket-log.jsonl`.
- Classify each gate-adjacent signature statement in those files as current operation-certificate guidance, generic HMAC manifest/API guidance, legacy HMAC compatibility, or historical migration evidence.
- Make every current plan-review or completion-verifier statement identify all four implemented facts: a DSSE envelope, SSHSIG signing, an Ed25519 key, and environment-attributed signer identity.
- Make every legacy HMAC compatibility statement say that the record remains readable but cannot certify a current gated operation.
- Preserve generic HMAC manifest-signing guidance for other consumers. In `docs/reuse-surface.md`, change only incorrect gate-consumer attribution while retaining the source-contract statements pinned by `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`, including the generic `sign_manifest` API and hex-HMAC `compute_signature` result.
- Preserve ADR and migration history. Keep `src/rebar/_cli/help/sign.txt` and `docs/llm-framework.md` unchanged because their current statements are accurate.
- Use a one-time repository search plus an auditable per-file classification comment to detect omissions. This is review evidence, not a persistent string gate or mechanical prose-quality policy.
- Do not add mechanical writing enforcement. Do not change the Markdown-only reduced test policy.

## Verification
- Run `rg -n "HMAC|DSSE|SSHSIG|operation[- ]certificate" README.md docs src/rebar/_cli/help/sign.txt`, classify every gate-adjacent hit, and record the path plus classification in a ticket comment. Any hit outside the positive edit set must be recorded as accurate, historical, excluded, or follow-up scope before completion.
- Review `git diff -- README.md docs/manifest-signing.md docs/event-schema.md docs/reuse-surface.md docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md docs/plan-review-gate.md docs/sample-ticket-log.jsonl` against the four-fact current-certificate checklist and the explicit non-certifying legacy-HMAC checklist. Record the completed checklist in the ticket comment rather than adding an automated wording gate.
- Run `python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check` to prove documentation links and index entries remain valid.
- Run `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py -q` to prove reusable generic-HMAC API documentation still matches the source contract.
- Run `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py -q` to prove current and legacy signing lifecycle contracts remain green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every changed current-gate statement identifies DSSE, SSHSIG, Ed25519, and environment attribution.
- [x] Every changed legacy-HMAC statement explicitly says it cannot certify current gated operations.
- [x] Generic HMAC manifest/API statements retain their implemented non-gate meaning.
- [x] A ticket comment classifies every gate-adjacent search hit by path and consumer role.
- [x] ADR and migration history remains intact.
- [x] `src/rebar/_cli/help/sign.txt` remains unchanged.
- [x] `docs/llm-framework.md` remains unchanged.
- [x] All commands in `## Verification` pass or produce the recorded classification evidence.
- [x] No persistent mechanical writing-enforcement check is introduced.
- [x] The Markdown-only reduced test policy remains unchanged.

baseline.description:
On every autodeploy restart the review-bot silently abandons acknowledged-but-unreviewed webhooks (the in-memory review queue is dropped), so changes stall until the slow backfill reconciler catches up — and the reconciler itself can be frozen indefinitely by one hung review. Drain the queue on graceful shutdown and give backfill reviews the same per-review timeout the live worker has.

## Why
The review queue is an in-memory `asyncio.Queue` (`app.py:107`). `POST /webhook` enqueues and returns `202 {"queued": true}` — a promise to process the event. But the lifespan shutdown (`app.py:127-134`) **cancels the worker without draining the queue**, so on the hourly autodeploy restart (ADR-0026) any enqueued-but-unreviewed event is lost, and any in-flight review is cancelled. Recovery falls entirely to the reconcile backfill, which is slow (300s interval; sequential full-LLM-review per change; cursor advanced only at end-of-pass, `reconcile.py:221`). This was observed live: an autodeploy at ~22:53Z dropped a batch of in-flight webhooks (changes 716-723) that then took ~25 min to drain. Separately, the worker wraps each review in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout)` (`app.py:153`) but `reconcile_once` calls `review_and_vote` with NO timeout (`reconcile.py:215`) — so a single hung backfill review would freeze ALL backfill indefinitely (the safety-net has no safety-net).

## What
1. **Graceful drain (app.py lifespan):** in the shutdown `finally`, BEFORE cancelling the
   worker, `await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS)` (suppressing
   TimeoutError) so queued events are processed by the still-running worker before exit;
   anything not drained in the window still falls to the reconciler (fail-safe, not fail-lose).
   `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` from env (default 45).
2. **stop_grace_period (docker-compose.yml):** set the review-bot service `stop_grace_period`
   to 60s so Docker's SIGTERM→SIGKILL window is long enough for the drain to run (default 10s
   would SIGKILL mid-drain).
3. **Reconciler timeout parity (reconcile.py):** wrap the `review_and_vote` call in
   `reconcile_once` in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=<review_timeout>)`; on TimeoutError emit a
   greppable marker and CONTINUE to the next candidate (never freeze the loop). Share the
   timeout value with the worker (factor `review_timeout_seconds()` so both read the same
   `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`: drain in lifespan `finally`; `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` helper.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py`: per-review `wait_for` + timeout marker + continue.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py` (or a small shared helper): `review_timeout_seconds()` used
  by both app and reconcile (DRY; avoids an app<->reconcile import cycle).
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: `stop_grace_period: 60s` on `review-bot`.
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`: RED tests for the drain and the reconciler timeout.
- Non-goal: replacing the in-memory queue with a persistent/disk-backed queue (heavier; the
  reconciler remains the ultimate recovery path — chosen approach per operator direction).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On lifespan shutdown with items still queued, the items are drained (processed by the
      worker) rather than dropped; before the fix they are dropped.
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k shutdown_drain -q`
      passes and is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] The drain is bounded: if draining exceeds `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS`, shutdown still
      completes (does not hang) and remaining items are left for the reconciler.
      Proving command: a test with a slow/blocking worker asserts shutdown returns within the
      bound.
- [ ] `reconcile_once` does not hang on a review that never returns: a review exceeding the
      timeout is abandoned, a marker is emitted, and the loop proceeds to the next candidate.
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k reconcile_timeout -q`
      passes and is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` sets `stop_grace_period` on the review-bot service.
      Proving command: `python -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('infra/compose/docker-compose.yml')); assert d['services']['review-bot'].get('stop_grace_period')"`
- [ ] Existing gates stay green.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q` all exit 0.
baseline.summary: review-bot: drain review queue on shutdown + reconciler per-review timeout (deploy resilience)

baseline.description:
# The `Verified` gate's `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)` cell hangs after ~99% of the suite and is cancelled at the 60-minute job timeout

## Symptom

The cell prints progress normally for ~10 minutes, reaches `[ 99%]` with **zero** `F`/`E` markers, and then emits nothing at all until GitHub kills it:

    2026-08-07T17:04:16.9396830Z ....................................... [ 99%]
    2026-08-07T17:55:12.0420609Z ##[error]The operation was canceled.

`timeout-minutes: 60` is set on the `test` job in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`. The CI bot reads the cancellation as a failure and votes `Verified -1` + `Code-Review -1`, so an otherwise-green change cannot land.

## Not change-specific

Seen on at least two unrelated changes on 2026-08-07:

* change 1505 (`9fb3`), three consecutive runs — 31194624887, 31199714760, 31206898501 —
  including one run **after** a rebase onto `origin/main` @ 9532650f24.
* run 31208164115, a different change, same signature: `[ 99%]` then
  `The operation was canceled.`

The other matrix cells (ubuntu py3.12, ubuntu py3.13, macos py3.13) complete the same selection in 11-21 minutes on those same runs, so it is specific to the ubuntu/py3.11 cell.

Counting the progress dots on run 31199714760's cell: 11160 of ~11215 tests had reported before the silence, so roughly the last ~55 tests are where it stalls. It is a hang in the test tail, not in coverage combining or teardown after the run.

## Does not reproduce locally

On macOS with the CI-faithful configuration — `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra reviewbot --extra ui --python 3.11`, then `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS=1 pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q -p no:cacheprovider --durations=25 --cov=rebar` — the suite finishes in 15:00 with 11196 passed, 19 skipped, exit 0. So the trigger involves the Linux runner (4 vCPU, `fcntl.flock`-backed store locking) rather than the interpreter version alone.

## Why it matters

Every change in flight can be blocked by a red `Verified` that reflects no real defect, and the only workaround is to keep posting `recheck` until a run happens to get through. That is the same class of problem as a gating advisory failure: the gate stops discriminating.

## Suggested first moves

- Add `-v` (or `--timeout` via `pytest-timeout`) to the ubuntu cells so the hanging test
  names itself instead of being invisible behind `-q` dots.
- Suspect first the store's write-lock paths (`fcntl.flock` + `mkdir`) and any test that
  shells out to `rebar` as a subprocess, since a blocked lock acquire is the shape that
  produces exactly this silence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] the hanging test (or the blocking call) is named, with a CI log line or a local
      reproduction showing it stalled
- [x] [operator-attested] the ubuntu py3.11 cell completes within the 60-minute job timeout on three
      consecutive Verified runs
- [x] whatever makes the hang diagnosable (a per-test timeout, `-v`, or a faulthandler
      dump) is committed, so a recurrence names itself instead of going silent
baseline.summary: CI: the ubuntu-latest/py3.11 pytest cell hangs at 99% and is killed by the 60-minute job timeout
