## Context
Independent review of ticket 5f4d found two non-blocking hardening gaps in scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py. A file containing invalid UTF-8 is skipped wholesale (`except UnicodeDecodeError: continue`), so a source file can evade the guard by carrying one bad byte. Separately, an unallowlisted match prints the complete raw source line, so a very long line or embedded control characters land unescaped in CI logs.

## Plan
- Define a source-ish text extension set (`.py`, `.md`, `.json`, `.yaml`/`.yml`, `.toml`) that
  must FAIL CLOSED on a decode error, while every other extension stays tolerated so genuine
  binaries do not produce false positives.
- Bound and escape diagnostic excerpts: escape non-printable characters and cap the escaped excerpt at
  200 characters (`MAX_EXCERPT_CHARS = 200`), with an explicit truncation marker.
- Add behavioral tests for invalid-byte source input, invalid-byte binary input, and
  hostile (long / control-character) matching lines.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py -q` — new cases: an
  undecodable `.py` exits 1 naming the file, an undecodable `.bin` exits 0, and a long
  control-character line is emitted escaped and truncated.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — the guard is itself part of the `make lint` gate, so a
  clean run proves the real repository still scans clean.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Known text files cannot evade the vocabulary guard by containing an invalid UTF-8 byte:
      verified by a test asserting exit 1 and the offending path in stderr.
- [x] Binary files remain safely ignored without false positives: verified by a test asserting
      exit 0 for an undecodable non-source extension.
- [x] Diagnostics escape control characters and cap source excerpts at 200 characters: verified by a test asserting no raw control byte and a truncation marker in stderr.
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py -q` and `make lint` pass.
baseline.summary: Harden vocabulary guard decoding and diagnostics

baseline.description:
# A destroyed parent edge cannot be restored: no supported route re-parents to a closed parent

## Impact, and why this is filed as a defect rather than an enhancement

The reconciler cleared the `parent_id` of 63 tickets (see 88d9-fe42-e50f-4067 for that incident). Every prior parent is recoverable from the event log, but **rebar cannot write them back**: 61 of the 63 parents are closed, and `rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent` validation cascade (`_commands/composer.py:503-513`): "cannot re-parent to closed ticket '<id>'. Reopen the parent first".

So the tool can destroy a parent edge automatically but cannot restore one, and the store has no supported path back to a state it was previously in. That is the defect.

## All four candidate routes were checked, not assumed

* `edit --parent` is the ONLY reparent path — there is no `parent` / `move` / `reparent` command, and
  `link`/`unlink` cover the six link relations, not hierarchy.
* `edit` has NO `--force`: zero mentions in its help output, and `force` does not appear anywhere in
  `_commands/composer.py`.
* `rebar revert <ticket> <uuid>` does NOT restore state. `process_revert`
  (`reducer/_processors.py:456-488`) appends a record to `state["reverts"]`; its only state effect is
  un-archiving on REVERT-of-ARCHIVED. Reverting the offending EDIT logs the revert and leaves
  `parent_id` empty.
* `fsck-recover` is git-level dangling-write recovery, not semantic repair.
* `rebar.edit_ticket` shells out to the same CLI, so the library path hits the same guard.

## Why the documented workaround is not acceptable here

"Reopen the parent first" means, at this scale: reopen ~20 epics, re-parent their children, then re-close each. Re-closing runs the LLM completion-verification gate (`require_completion_verification_for_close = true`) ~20 times and writes fresh STATUS + COMPLETION_VERDICT events onto already-signed closes. A single gate failure leaves a previously-closed epic OPEN — a second visible regression introduced while repairing the first. Rewriting the close records of 20 completed epics to work around a missing flag is a symptom-level workaround.

## Approach

Add `--force` to `edit`, scoped to bypass **only** the closed-parent status check. Follows rebar's existing `--force` idiom (`claim --force`, `transition --force-close`): explicit operator intent, never implicit.

Deliberately still enforced under `--force`:
* the parent must EXIST (`resolve_ticket_id` + directory check),
* a ticket may not be its own parent,
* the cycle walk (a `--force` that could build a cycle would corrupt the hierarchy, which is a
  different and worse failure than the one being repaired),
* the `status == ""` fail-closed branch (an unverifiable parent stays refused — `--force` overrides a
  KNOWN-closed parent, never an UNKNOWN one).

Only the `status not in ("open", "in_progress")` refusal for a status that is positively known becomes overridable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `edit --parent=<closed ticket> --force` succeeds and the child's `parent_id` is the closed
      parent, asserted on the REDUCED ticket, not on the command's exit code
- [ ] without `--force` the same command still FAILS with the existing message, so the guard is not
      weakened for ordinary use
- [ ] `--force` does NOT bypass: a non-existent parent, self-parent, a cycle, or the `status == ""`
      fail-closed branch — one test per case, each asserting the specific error
- [ ] the flag is rejected/ignored coherently when `--parent` is absent (it has no other meaning)
- [ ] `--force` usage is discoverable: it appears in `edit`'s usage/help text
- [ ] every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the bypass UNCONDITIONAL — an unconditional bypass passes the happy-path
      oracle while silently removing the guard for every caller, so the still-refused cases are the
      oracles that protect the product
- [ ] the 63 recorded parent edges are restored and verified by re-reading the reduced tickets, with
      the count confirmed against the manifest
baseline.summary: edit cannot restore a parent edge onto a closed parent, so a destroyed hierarchy is unrepairable

baseline.description: Escaped-bug analysis (ticket cranial-goodly-seahog) found ~4 regressions in a class current code-review criteria miss entirely: import/packaging resolution breakage that passes in-tree but fails under real import order / sys.path. baseline.description:
The unit test `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_open_children.py::test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated` fails INTERMITTENTLY in CI with `rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar transition failed (exit 2): Error: git operation failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD`. It is NOT a CI-vs-Gerrit drift (Gerrit's Verified gate runs the identical pytest matrix, so it fails there too) — it is test-isolation / concurrency flakiness under pytest-xdist (`-n 4 --dist worksteal`), where a temp git store is exercised before its initial commit exists (unborn HEAD), so a `rebar transition` git op hits `could not parse HEAD`.

Discovered while resolving bug `pillared-doddering-fawn` (the deterministic `no-commit-to-branch` CI-drift red). Filed separately because it is a different failure CLASS (flaky test, not drift) and out of scope for that change.

## Evidence
- run 29470200567: FAILED on cell `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.12)` only (py3.11,
  py3.13, macOS all PASSED). `1 failed, 6171 passed` — the single failure is this test.
- run 29468054945: FAILED on cell `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` instead; py3.12
  PASSED that run. i.e. the failing cell MOVES run-to-run → non-deterministic.
- Failing assertion context: the test drives `rebar transition` on a store with
  child tickets; the git op raises `fatal: could not parse HEAD`.

## Reproduction Steps
- [ ] Run the interface suite under xdist repeatedly:
      `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_open_children.py -n 4 --dist worksteal -q`
      (and/or the full interface tier) enough times to surface the intermittent failure.
- [ ] Observe an occasional `git operation failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD` from
      `rebar transition` in `test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated`.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the test passes deterministically on every cell / every run (a fresh test
  store always has a parseable HEAD before a transition git op runs).
- Actual: it fails on ~1 random matrix cell per run with `could not parse HEAD`,
  reddening branch CI (and it would redden the Verified gate too).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root-cause the `could not parse HEAD` (the test-fixture git-store setup that
      leaves HEAD unborn / races the initial commit under xdist worker parallelism),
      cited to the fixture/code (`path:line`).
- [ ] Fix so the test store always has a committed HEAD before any `rebar transition`
      git op, under xdist parallelism (e.g. ensure the fixture commits an initial
      state / is isolated per worker).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Demonstrate stability: the test passes across repeated xdist runs (quantified,
      e.g. 50/50 green) — a single green run does not close a flake.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make test` (or the interface tier) green on all matrix cells.
baseline.summary: Flaky test: test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated fails intermittently with 'could not parse HEAD' under xdist

# The step-budget repetition diagnostic is computed, then dropped

## Context / Problem

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a]. The reported symptom was "the gate cannot be tuned because it cannot be observed" — no partial verdict, no count of anything, just a bare budget number. The diagnostic that answers it **already exists** and is thrown away one frame from the surface.

`interpret_failure` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:75-103`) builds `budget_diag` via `usage_log.failure_usage`, which reduces every tool call to a `(tool_name, sha256(args)[:8])` signature and summarizes it — `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`. That is precisely the loop-vs-explore discriminator, and it is attached as `budget_err.diagnostic`.

It then goes nowhere. `emit_gate_error` is only called by `raise_completion_workflow_failure` when `failure_diagnostic` is truthy (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:373-403`), and `failure_diagnostic` is set ONLY inside `CompletionAgentStep._recover` — which a budget exhaustion never reaches (the sibling [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911] fixes reachability). So **no `gate_error_v1` sidecar is written** and the CLI message carries none of it. In the instrumented reproduction the propagated exception reached the caller with `diagnostic: null`.

Two operators burned ~50 minutes each escalating the budget 480 -> 1600 against a constraint that was never a budget (and ticket 46a2-9c1a-d855-4706 records a third: 480 -> 1200, same result). The measurement that would have said so in one line was computed on the first run and discarded.

## Approach

Wire the already-computed diagnostic through the two drops. First, `CompletionAgentStep` records the caught exception's `.diagnostic` onto `self.failure_diagnostic` when it enters recovery (fd84 adds the budget entry edge; this ticket makes the diagnostic it carries survive), so `raise_completion_workflow_failure` — whose sidecar emission and `CompletionRecoveryError` path already exist and are keyed on a truthy `failure_diagnostic` — emits the `gate_error_v1` sidecar carrying the repetition counters. The carry path is NOT automatic: the caught exception's `.diagnostic` is filtered through `_bounded_diagnostic` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py`), whose `allowed` allowlist strips `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls` and `distinct_ratio_window` today — and whose scalar-only merge guard would drop the list-valued `top_repeated_tool_calls` even if allowlisted. This ticket widens that allowlist with those four repetition keys and relaxes the scalar-only guard for exactly `top_repeated_tool_calls` (a bounded list of `{signature, count}` dicts — hashed signatures, no prompts or arguments), so the summary survives both the recovery-exception merge and the primary-exception merge ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], landed, established that carry). On the budget path the counters ride the PRIMARY exception, and every primary-diagnostic key is re-prefixed `aggregate_` before landing on `failure_diagnostic` — so the sidecar carries them as `aggregate_tool_calls_distinct`, `aggregate_max_consecutive_repeat`, `aggregate_top_repeated_tool_calls`, `aggregate_distinct_ratio_window`. `format_repetition` reads the BARE key names, so `raise_completion_workflow_failure` builds its render input by projecting the prefix off first — `{k.removeprefix("aggregate_"): v for k, v in diag.items() if k.startswith("aggregate_")}` — and passes that projection to `format_repetition`; the sidecar itself keeps the `aggregate_`-prefixed names unchanged. Second, the operator-facing close-gate failure message renders the distinct-vs-total counts (via the existing `usage_log.format_repetition` renderer, which already formats exactly these fields) so "it looped" is distinguishable from "it ran out of room" without reading a log. No new computation: every value is already produced by `usage_log.failure_usage`; this ticket widens the diagnostic filter to stop dropping it and renders it.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — `_bounded_diagnostic`: extend the `allowed`
  allowlist with `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`,
  `distinct_ratio_window`, and permit the list-typed `top_repeated_tool_calls` through `merge()`
  (all other keys stay scalar-only); in `raise_completion_workflow_failure`, project the
  `aggregate_`-prefixed keys back to bare names and render that projection through
  `usage_log.format_repetition` into the raised message.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py` — the tests below.

Out of scope: making budget exhaustion reach this code at all ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], landed: budget exhaustions now enter `_recover` and set `failure_diagnostic`); computing the detector's new field ([rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0], landed: `failure_usage` now emits `distinct_ratio_window`). This ticket carries both through the `_bounded_diagnostic` filter that currently strips them.

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py -q

Happy path: a budget exhaustion whose recovery also fails emits a `gate_error_v1` sidecar populated with the repetition counters. Edge: a failure with NO diagnostic (the pre-existing bare path) still raises `LLMError` exactly as today (regression-pinned). Privacy: the sidecar payload carries no prompts, tool arguments, or response text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a step-budget exhaustion whose recovery also fails writes a `gate_error_v1` sidecar carrying
      the repetition summary under the `aggregate_`-prefixed names the primary-exception merge
      produces (`aggregate_requests`, `aggregate_tool_calls`, `aggregate_tool_calls_distinct`,
      `aggregate_max_consecutive_repeat`, `aggregate_top_repeated_tool_calls`,
      `aggregate_distinct_ratio_window`) — i.e. the `_bounded_diagnostic` allowlist passes these
      keys and the list-valued `top_repeated_tool_calls` survives the merge; verified by a test
      asserting the sidecar is emitted and those keys are populated
- [x] the operator-facing close-gate failure message includes the distinct-vs-total tool-call counts
      rendered from the `aggregate_`-prefix-stripped projection (so `format_repetition`'s bare-key
      lookups resolve to the actual numbers, never `None`), making "it looped" distinguishable from
      "it ran out of room" without reading a log; verified by a test asserting the raised error's
      message contains the concrete counts (e.g. `30 distinct / 253 calls`), not `None`
- [x] the sidecar payload stays free of prompts, tool arguments and response text (the existing
      privacy contract in `usage_log.failure_usage` is preserved); verified by a test asserting only
      hashed signatures and counters appear
- [x] a failure without any diagnostic still raises the current bare `LLMError` unchanged (no
      manufactured empty sidecar); regression-pinned by a test
baseline.summary: Step-budget repetition diagnostic is computed then dropped: no gate_error_v1 sidecar, no counters in the operator message

## Summary

`rebar claim` records **no assignee** on the deployed MCP server instead of the configured `ticket.default_assignee`. `_config_default_assignee` infers the config root as the TRACKER'S PARENT directory — an assumption that holds only when the tracker lives inside the repo.

    # src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:84
    return config.compose_config(root=os.path.dirname(tracker)).ticket.default_assignee or ""

In a checkout the tracker is `<repo>/.tickets-tracker`, so the parent IS the repo root and `rebar.toml` is found. The MCP server sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, whose parent `/var/gerrit/site` contains no `rebar.toml`. The lookup returns `""`, and the claim records an empty assignee.

The `except Exception: return ""` guard ("a malformed config must never break a claim") means this degrades **silently** — no warning, no error, just a ticket with no owner.

## Proven on the live box (2026-08-26, container `compose-mcp-1`)

Same call, two roots:

    CWD = /app
    compose_config(root=None)                    -> 'joeoakhart@navapbc.com'
    compose_config(root=dirname(REBAR_TRACKER_DIR)) -> ''
    tracker_dir(None)                            -> /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets

    $ ls /var/gerrit/site/rebar.toml   -> No such file or directory
    $ ls /app/rebar.toml               -> 14163 bytes
    $ echo $REBAR_DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE     -> <unset>   (env override does not rescue it)

The env-override path (`REBAR_DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE`, `_config_sources.py:316`) is not set in the mcp compose service, so nothing masks the bad root.

## Why this is the only site

`compose_config(root=os.path.dirname(` appears exactly once in `src/rebar` — this line. Every other caller passes a real `repo_root` (`_engine_support/gates.py:154`, `reads.py:118,186,347`, `verify_opcert.py:117`). `claim.py` is the outlier, and its own docstring asserts the assumption it violates: "Read from the repo root (the tracker's parent)".

The MCP write path supplies no `repo_root` at all (`_mcp_writes.py` has no such reference), so `repo_root` is `None` there — and `compose_config(root=None)` resolves correctly from CWD `/app`. That is what makes the fix a deletion rather than an addition.

## Fix

Resolve config the way every other caller does — pass `repo_root` through (including `None`) instead of substituting the tracker's parent:

    def _config_default_assignee(repo_root=None) -> str:
        try:
            return config.compose_config(root=repo_root).ticket.default_assignee or ""
        except Exception:
            return ""

`repo_root` is already in scope at the call site (`claim.py:175`, same function that computes `tracker = config.tracker_dir(repo_root)` at `:154`). In a checkout this resolves the same `rebar.toml` as today, so CLI behaviour is unchanged; on the box it finds `/app/rebar.toml`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A claim whose tracker sits OUTSIDE the repo resolves `ticket.default_assignee` from the
      repo root, not from the tracker's parent.
      Proof: `test_default_assignee_resolves_when_the_tracker_lives_outside_the_repo`
- [x] A claim in an ordinary checkout resolves the same value it does today — no behaviour
      change. Proof: the seven pre-existing tests in `test_claim_default_assignee.py` pass
      unmodified.
- [x] An explicit `--assignee` still wins over the default, and an explicit `--assignee ""`
      still clears it. Proof: `test_explicit_assignee_wins_over_default`,
      `test_explicit_empty_clears_no_fallback`
- [x] Regression coverage fails if the root reverts to `os.path.dirname(tracker)`.
      Proof: mutation-checked — restoring the old root turns the new test RED.
- [x] The PLAN-REVIEW GATE also resolves its config root correctly on a relocated store.
      Added after code review found the same root inference feeding
      `plan_review_precheck` / `_plan_review_gate_applies`: for a gate flag an empty config
      reads as OFF, so the start-work gate silently STOPPED APPLYING on the deployed server.
      Proof: `test_plan_review_gate_still_applies_when_the_tracker_lives_outside_the_repo`;
      restoring the old root produces `DID NOT RAISE`.


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -k "default_assignee or claim_assignee" -q -p no:randomly
baseline.summary: claim records no assignee when the tracker lives outside the repo: default_assignee is resolved from the tracker's parent

So this slice is (1) explicit TEST COVERAGE pinning that identity-scoping invariant (a local-dev cert is rejected by the AWS bot and vice-versa), (2) documentation of the guarantee, and (3) the shared reuse SEAM (vaquita AC#3) factored so the future code-review reuse can share it. Does NOT change the trust model. If the ADR (refutable-meaningful-borzoi) picks a different identity notion than env_id/principal, fold that in. Independently verifiable: tests + docs only.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Since 2026-08-23 the `tickets` event-sourced branch's commit rate jumped ~10x (~1.5-3K/day to 15-23K/day); ~88% of the surge is the enrichment quartet (ENQUEUE_ENRICH / CLAIM_ENRICH / DONE_ENRICH + TICKET_DIGEST). Runtime-proven root cause (this session): the drain self-heal `enrich_drain._stale_digest_ids` re-enqueues **every** ticket whose cached digest is `present-stale` on **every** drain, with `soak_min=0` and no per-ticket rate limit. So ordinary comment/edit/reconcile churn re-enriches a ticket once per content drift (measured: 1,239 tickets ~15x each). Correctness fix `be8a0c0` (bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282) had removed the only growth bound (`_prune_queue_events` + digest `prune(keep=1)`) for a valid union-merge reason, so each re-fire's 4 events are now retained permanently -> unbounded fan-out. Downstream operational impact: /var/gerrit disk-fill (wakeful-ordinary-chicken 5a05). Scope here is PREVENTION only (not history reclamation, which is polite-antivirus-bedbug 536b).

## Approach

Add a per-ticket **re-enrichment debounce** to the self-heal path only. `_stale_digest_ids` skips a present-stale ticket whose most recent enrichment (latest `DONE_ENRICH` event timestamp) is younger than a configurable window `overlap_reenrich_debounce_min` (default 1440 min = 24h). A slightly-stale dedup digest is an acceptable overlap hint until the window elapses; the next drain after it elapses re-enriches, so digests stay eventually-fresh. This bounds re-firing to at most one cycle per ticket per window regardless of drift volume, and it deletes **no** committed event, so it preserves the append-only union-merge invariant that 8185/4520 require (physical deletion is explicitly disallowed). First-time enrichment (no prior `DONE_ENRICH`), the certification->enqueue primary path, and explicit re-certification are all untouched (they do not pass through the self-heal). Default 1440 assumes a day of digest staleness is acceptable for dedup; operators tune via the env knob.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` - add `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_REENRICH_DEBOUNCE_MIN = 1440`, `overlap_reenrich_debounce_min: int` field, and the `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_REENRICH_DEBOUNCE_MIN` read in `from_env` (mirrors `overlap_soak_min`).
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` - `_stale_digest_ids` gains a debounce filter keyed on the latest `DONE_ENRICH` timestamp (`queue._latest(dir, DONE)`); `_collect_claims` passes `now` and the window (ns). A `debounce=0` value disables the filter (pre-fix behavior).
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` - RED->GREEN debounce unit tests.
- `docs/env-vars.md` - regenerated via `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` (CI drift gate).

## Testing

- Happy path (the bound): a ticket enriched once, then drifting N times within the window, produces 0 additional re-enrichment cycles (was N) and its `DONE_ENRICH` count stays 1.
- Boundary: a present-stale ticket whose last enrichment predates the window IS re-enriched (drain `now` driven past the window) -> digest becomes `present-fresh`.
- First-time: a ticket with no prior `DONE_ENRICH` is never debounced (processed on first drain).
- Disabled: `overlap_reenrich_debounce_min = 0` restores the exact pre-fix behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_stale_digest_ids` skips a present-stale ticket whose latest `DONE_ENRICH` is within `overlap_reenrich_debounce_min`; verified by a unit test asserting N in-window drifts produce 0 re-enrichment cycles (test seen RED before the change). DONE: `test_reenrich_debounce_bounds_the_self_heal_fanout` (RED pre-fix = 6 DONE_ENRICH, GREEN post-fix = 1).
- [x] A present-stale ticket whose last enrichment predates the window IS re-enriched; verified by a unit test that drives drain `now` past the window and asserts the digest becomes `present-fresh`. DONE: `test_reenrich_debounce_allows_reenrichment_after_the_window`.
- [x] First-time enrichment is unaffected: a ticket with no prior `DONE_ENRICH` is never debounced; verified by a unit test (first-time coverage in the debounce test block).
- [x] `overlap_reenrich_debounce_min` is a config knob (default + dataclass field + env read) reachable via `LLMConfig.from_env`, and `docs/env-vars.md` is regenerated so the CI drift gate is green. DONE: `config.py` (DEFAULT_OVERLAP_REENRICH_DEBOUNCE_MIN=1440, field, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_REENRICH_DEBOUNCE_MIN` in from_env); env-vars.md regenerated.
- [x] No committed UUID event is deleted or renamed by the change (the union-merge invariant from 8185/4520 is preserved); verified by inspection (debounce only skips an enqueue; deletes nothing) and by the concurrency/union-merge regression suite staying green (37 passed).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and targeted `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` pass. DONE: lint green (complexity new=0/increased=0, module-size 799<800), typecheck clean, 55 unit tests pass; merged as Gerrit 2386 with Verified +1.
baseline.summary: Debounce enrichment self-heal re-firing to bound tracker fan-out (no event deletion)

## Symptom

2026-08-12T23:07:07Z rebar-gerrit-voter-errors and 23:07:18Z rebar-review-bot-merge-change-errors both went OK -> ALARM, each on exactly 1 datapoint in the 23:06Z probe minute, and both returned to OK at 23:13Z.

NO voter error and NO merge-change error occurred. Both counts came from a SINGLE journal line at 2026-08-12T23:02:26Z which is the review-bot's own LLM code-review analysis prose, verbatim (CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1):

    ...mits matching markers for every target (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, AUTODEPLOY_ERROR,
    AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED, gerrit_to_platform error, both interrupt reasons) and REPL_LOG is
    populated. The rolled-up review_interrupts per_interval=2 arithmetic is consistent
    (total 14 seeded, next run +2)

The reviewer was reviewing a change to infra/scripts/observability.sh itself (the cold-start seeding fix for widespread-zealous-narwhal / e2a6-9ee4-8d5c-4290), so it enumerated the marker tokens as prose. The probe then counted that prose as two errors.

## Mechanism

infra/scripts/observability.sh section 4 and section 4c count markers with an UNANCHORED grep over the review-bot container's journal:

    vtotal=$(journalctl CONTAINER_NAME="$VOTER_CONTAINER" --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE 'VOTER_ERROR')
    mtotal=$(journalctl CONTAINER_NAME="$VOTER_CONTAINER" --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE 'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR')

The pattern matches the token ANYWHERE in a line. The review-bot writes its LLM output to the same journal stream, so any review whose text mentions a marker name is counted as an occurrence of that marker. The probe cannot distinguish its own alarm vocabulary from an actual error.

## Evidence that the counted line is not a real marker

Full-journal counts, real markers are emitted at line start under -o cat:

    VOTER_ERROR        line-start (real): 221    substring-anywhere: 222   offset file: 222
    MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line-start (real):   0    substring-anywhere:   1   offset file:   1

So exactly one of the 222 counted voter errors is the false match, and the merge-change counter has NEVER seen a real error in the entire retained journal — its only count in history is this false positive, which is what fired its alarm.

Review-bot health across the window contradicts any real failure: voter_voted events at 23:05:08Z, 23:13:04Z and 23:19:38Z, i.e. the bot was voting normally before, during and after. There is no Gerrit 4xx/5xx, no 409 and no conflict of any kind in the window.

## Classification

FALSE POSITIVE, and the alarm is not at fault: both alarms are correct to fire on a nonzero count. The count was fabricated by the probe. Do not tune the alarms.

## Why this recurs and is getting worse

The trigger is a review that discusses observability.sh or the marker vocabulary. The fleet is actively landing changes to observability.sh right now (the narwhal cold-start fix), so every further review of that file is likely to re-fire these two alarms. It is self-referential: the observability code's own review trips its own alarms. It also silently corrupts the offset files (voter offset is now 222 against 221 real markers), so the counters permanently carry the inflation.

Same false-positive FAMILY as widespread-zealous-narwhal (probe publishes counts for non-events) but a DISTINCT mechanism: that one is an absent-offset cold start, this one is an over-broad pattern matching the token as data. Both live in infra/scripts/observability.sh.

## Suggested fix direction (not prescriptive)

Anchor the match to the marker's actual emission shape rather than a bare substring. Evidence says real markers begin the message (221/221 line-start under -o cat), so '^VOTER_ERROR' / '^MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR' would exclude the prose case. A structural match on the emitted record would be sturdier still. Whatever is chosen must be applied to every marker counter that reads a stream the LLM also writes to, and the same question should be asked of the AUTODEPLOY_* counters, whose journal is not currently LLM-written but which share the unanchored shape. Consider also whether the inflated offsets should be corrected or simply left to age out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A journal line containing a marker token as prose (not at the emission position) is NOT counted. Verify: test feeding the verbatim 23:02:26Z line to the voter and merge counters yields 0.
- [x] A genuine marker line is still counted. Verify: test with a real-shaped VOTER_ERROR and MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line yields 1 each.
- [x] The tightened pattern is applied to every counter reading an LLM-written stream (sections 4 and 4c at minimum), and the AUTODEPLOY_* counters are audited for the same shape.

## Verification

Discovered by ops sweep of AWS alarm firings; full evidence trail on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1). All investigation read-only (CloudWatch describe/get + SSM read-only journalctl); nothing mutated in AWS or on the box.
## Implementation plan (on top of the narwhal cold-start fix, change 1686)

### Anchor to the marker's emitted RECORD shape, not the bare token

Every countable marker is emitted as `<TOKEN> {json}` at the START of the journal message — `voter.py` (`"VOTER_ERROR " + json.dumps(record)` printed to stderr, same for `MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR`) and `autodeploy.sh` `marker()` (`printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "<json>" >&2`). Under `journalctl -o cat` that is line-start, a space, then `{`. So the pattern becomes `^<TOKEN> \{` — the ticket's "structural match on the emitted record", which excludes prose naming the token both mid-line AND at line start. Evidence agrees the anchor keeps every real marker: line-start count 221 == real count 221 (bare substring counted 222).

Sites in `infra/scripts/observability.sh`:
- §4 `voter_errors`: `'VOTER_ERROR'` -> `'^VOTER_ERROR \{'`
- §4c `review_bot_merge_change_errors`: `'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR'` -> `'^MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR \{'`
- §4d `deploy_errors`: `'AUTODEPLOY_ERROR'` -> `'^AUTODEPLOY_ERROR \{'`
- §4e the four `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` call sites: `^AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED \{`,
  `^AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT \{`, and the two reason-scoped patterns gain the same prefix.
  The anchor goes at the CALL SITES; the helper's first argument stays a plain ERE.

### Audited, deliberately NOT anchored

§3 `replication_errors` (Gerrit's `replication_log`) and §4b `g2p_dispatch_errors` (Gerrit container journal): neither stream is LLM-written, and both match free-form phrases (`Giving up`, `[ERROR]`, `failed to dispatch`) that are not line-anchored records, so an anchor would drop real failures. Recorded as a comment at each site.

### Tests — tests/scripts/test_observability_marker_anchor_8c2f.py

Same stub harness as `test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py` (journalctl stub cats a file).

1. `test_prose_naming_a_marker_is_not_counted` — journal holds the VERBATIM 2026-08-12T23:02:26Z
   review-bot line naming `VOTER_ERROR` / `MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR` / `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` /
   `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED` / both interrupt reasons as prose. Every marker metric publishes 0.
2. `test_real_markers_are_still_counted` — one genuine `<TOKEN> {json}` line per marker publishes 1
   (2 for the rolled-up `review_interrupts`, which matches both reason lines).
3. `test_line_start_prose_without_a_record_is_not_counted` — line-start prose publishes 0.
4. `test_inflated_offset_self_heals` — offset 222 against 221 real markers publishes 0 and re-bases
   to 221, showing the false counts already banked need no manual correction (bug
   2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2's clamp).

RED-verified against the current tree first.

### Deploy and residue

No manual box action: autodeploy.sh watches `OBS_PATHS`. The inflated offsets (voter 222 vs 221 real, merge 1 vs 0) self-heal on the first probe run after this lands — the count drops, the negative-delta clamp publishes 0, and the offset re-bases.

### Out of scope

Alarm thresholds (correct as written); autodeploy.sh's `capture_bot_logs` redaction.
baseline.summary: observability.sh counts UNANCHORED marker substrings in the review-bot journal, so the bot's own LLM review text naming VOTER_ERROR / MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR fires false alarms

# J8 — ADR amending 0035: the Jira-family sub-seam, shared provenance, and the DC horizon

## Context / Problem

ADR 0035 §6 states that "the first real second backend is out of scope for this ADR and is tracked separately by epic `be74-7832-03a8-48ac`" — the GitHub adapter. This epic lands a different second backend first, and it introduces a structure ADR 0035 does not describe: a `jira_family` layer between the neutral core and a concrete adapter, with two contracts (`RichTextCodec`, `UserIdentityModel`) parameterizing it. It also makes a provenance decision — that the Jira family shares one `jira` creation channel and `jira-` id prefix, with deployments distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance` — which is precisely the decision PR #120 would have made silently by inheriting the hardcoded literal `validate_creation_channel("jira")` — today at `apply_inbound_records.py:211`, not :163 as an earlier draft of this plan said. Story J9's identity fix shifted it, and line 163 now holds an unrelated tag list-comprehension. CITE THE SYMBOL, not a line number: this plan has already gone stale against this exact file once. And it adds rebar's first third-party runtime dependency in the reconciler, confined to an extra.

Left unrecorded, each of these gets re-litigated the next time a Jira-like tracker appears.

## Approach

Write one ADR that amends 0035 rather than replacing it, recording: the `adapters/jira_family/` layer and why the seam is now two levels for one vendor family; the two parameterizing contracts; the shared-`jira` provenance decision and explicitly what it defers to epic `be74` (generalizing `jira_key`, the `jira-` prefix, and the channel vocabulary when a genuinely different vendor lands); the `pycontribs/jira` dependency, why it is extra-gated, and why the Cloud ACLI path was deliberately not migrated onto it; and the Docker harness as the verification oracle given that DC trial licenses ended in March 2026 and no official DC OpenAPI spec exists.

The ADR states the **horizon** plainly: Data Center goes read-only on 28 March 2029 and receives no new features today, so this is a deliberately time-boxed investment for existing self-hosted clients, and the durable asset is the family seam rather than the DC adapter. That framing is what tells a future maintainer whether to extend this code or retire it.

The ADR must ALSO record two findings this epic produced by execution, both already evidenced on this ticket's comments — they are properties of the SEAM, not of the DC adapter, so epic `be74` (GitHub Issues) inherits them:

* **The port did not state what the core requires.** `TicketTransport` declares SIX members while the
  core reaches for TWENTY-ONE distinct transport members (an earlier draft said fifteen — that was a
  call-form-only AST scan; counting EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver finds
  six more, because the reconciler routinely passes methods as values, e.g.
  `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)`); TWELVE were absent from the DC transport and
  declared on no Protocol at all. The consequence was measured, not theorised: a DC writing reconcile
  pass crashed (`set_entity_property`) while `isinstance(backend, Backend)`, the backend contract
  suite, and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green. So ADR 0035's "the contract suite certifies a
  backend" holds ONLY as far as the port is complete — and, per [rebar:cc77-8120-bcc6-47e8], only as
  far as the transport parameters are TYPED, since an unannotated `client` makes the gap invisible to
  mypy. State that conditionality plainly. Tracked by [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5] and
  [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]; the exception half is [rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052].
* **`RemoteRef.instance` is NOT built.** The ADR must NOT assert that deployments *are* distinguished
  by it as though that were existing reality. `RemoteRef` is never constructed in production code —
  `src/` holds only the frozen dataclass definition and docstrings; the only constructions in the repo
  are two test helpers. State it as the INTENDED design with the gap named and tracked
  ([rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]), or a future reader will build on a field nothing populates.

**Alternative rejected:** documenting only in `docs/architecture.md`. rebar's ADR set is where rejected alternatives live; without them the fork-per-deployment and hand-rolled-client options get re-proposed.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` (new — 0055 is the next free number; 0054 is taken by
  `0054-data-driven-calibration-no-costly-llm-assessments.md`).
  **Numbering caution:** THREE existing files share the number 0035 —
  `0035-rc2b-snapshot-horizon-safe-replay.md`, `0035-code-review-two-lane-tier-tagged-impact.md`, and
  `0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`. This story amends the THIRD. Every reference must cite the
  FILENAME; a bare "ADR 0035" is ambiguous in this repo.
- `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` — a pointer noting the amendment and correcting §6's
  "first real second backend" statement.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/user-guide.md` — the `reconciler.backend` choice and the DC extra.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated for `JIRA_PAT`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` states the DC least-privilege expectation: a dedicated service account whose PAT is
      scoped to only the reconciled projects (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments /
      Link Issues), never an admin token — and documents `allow_insecure` as cleartext-only-if-you-must, the
      `ca_bundle` key for internal-CA certificates, and `resolved_statuses` for workflows that do not use the
      conventional Resolved/Done/Cancelled state names (epic AC13)
- [ ] the ADR exists, is `Accepted`, and records each rejected alternative (fork-per-deployment, hand-rolled
      stdlib client, generalizing the store vocabulary now, migrating Cloud onto pycontribs) with its reason
- [ ] ADR 0035 carries a pointer to the amendment, and **all THREE stale statements** are corrected —
      not just Decision item 6. The claim that the first real second backend is out of scope appears
      at `:111` (layout-diagram comment `<backend-x>/  # future second backend`), `:204-205` (prose),
      and `:236-237` (Decision item 6). All three are falsified because this epic landed Jira Data
      Center AHEAD of the GitHub adapter `be74` was reserved for; correcting only one leaves two
      readers misinformed
- [ ] the ADR records the OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]: the seam ARCHITECTURE
      converged with what mature Jira integrations do (a maintained client library rather than
      hand-rolled REST, PAT bearer auth, an ephemeral containerised instance as the oracle), and every
      gap found was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES that only appear against a differently-configured
      instance — index lag, server-side pagination caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen
      configuration, project moves. State that pattern, because it tells the next backend author where
      to look
- [ ] the ADR states the March 2029 DC read-only date and what it implies for future investment in this adapter
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` documents selecting the DC backend and installing the extra, and the documented
      commands have been executed against the J5 harness
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` documents the `reconciler.backend` choice and the `jira-datacenter` extra
      (it mentions neither today) — it is a Scope deliverable and was previously uncovered by any AC
- [ ] the ADR records that ADR 0035's "the contract suite certifies a backend" claim is CONDITIONAL on
      the port being complete and typed, citing the measured evidence (6 declared vs TWENTY-ONE called, 12
      absent, a live crash while every static signal was green). The figure is 21, not 15: a
      call-form-only AST scan finds 15 and misses six members the reconciler reaches for as VALUES
      (e.g. `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)`). An earlier draft of this AC
      carried the stale 15 while the Context above already said 21
- [ ] the ADR describes `RemoteRef.instance` as INTENDED design with its gap named and ticketed, NOT as
      an existing mechanism — `grep -rn "RemoteRef(" src/` returns nothing, and the ADR must not
      contradict that
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` regenerates with no diff

## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` currently changes up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this deliberately covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

Author the behavioral oracle RED-first. Hold out the interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases from the implementer; expose only the basic dual-read happy path. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs is expected to advance and commit both rotation representations; claiming that such a pass makes no commit would contradict the required dual-write compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- new `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (docstring only)
- focused unit/integration/CLI tests

Estimated scope: M. Depends on closed A1 through the parent story.

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` — **790 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (10 lines of headroom).

Ten lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [x] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [x] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED. BOUNDED EXCEPTION: a
      purely mechanical `<file>:<line>` prose citation inside a test docstring or assertion MESSAGE
      may be repointed when the move shifts the line it names. That is non-behavioural (it changes
      no assertion, no fixture and no import) and is NOT evidence of a bad seam; any change to an
      assertion, fixture, import or expected value IS, and means stop and reconsider the seam.
- [x] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0` and `increased=0`.
- [x] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

## Chosen seam (derived from the call graph, 2026-08-19)

**Concern boundary: the step-kind I/O CONTRACT MODEL (declaration + static compatibility) vs the RUN ENGINE (control flow, expression resolution, dispatch, recording).** The two clusters in `executor.py` share no call edges.

*Cluster 1 (moves)* - `StepContract`, `STEP_CONTRACTS`, `contract_for`, `input_schema_for`, `shallow_contract_check` -> `_schema_is_opaque` / `_field_is_opaque` / `_primitive_kinds`, `_SHALLOW_COMBINATORS`. Internal edges only (`input_schema_for` -> `contract_for` -> `STEP_CONTRACTS`). Consumers are the STATIC / edit-time surface: `editor.py`, `editor_contracts.py`, `lint_refs.py`, and the interpreter's pre-dispatch input validation.

*Cluster 2 (stays)* - `new_run_id`, `_capture_nondeterminism`, `StepContext`, `StepResult`, `ScriptedStep`, `STEP_REGISTRY`, `register_step`, `RunState`, `RunResult`, the expression resolver, `static_order` / `_terminal_step` / `_guard_passes`, `run_workflow`, `_dispatch`, `_step_record`, the snapshot TTL sweep.

The run loop NEVER calls cluster 1. The only cross-seam edge is `register_step` writing `STEP_CONTRACTS`, so cluster 1 moves to a new `step_contracts.py` and `executor.py` imports it - one direction, no cycle. Same pattern as this file's two prior splits (`recorder.py`, `runners.py`): move the cluster, re-export the public names so every import point is unchanged.

### The COMPLETE re-export surface (one line per moved symbol)
`executor.py` re-binds at module scope EVERY cluster-1 symbol any consumer imports from `rebar.llm.workflow.executor`:
- `StepContract` - constructed by `register_step`; already in `executor.__all__`.
- `STEP_CONTRACTS` - written by `register_step`; imported by `tests/unit/workflow/test_contracts.py:18`.
- `contract_for` - `test_contracts.py:18`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_scripted_steps.py:16`; already in `__all__`.
- `shallow_contract_check` - `tests/unit/workflow/test_validation_depth.py:15`; already in `__all__`.

Worked example: `test_contracts.py:18` reads `from rebar.llm.workflow.executor import STEP_CONTRACTS, STEP_REGISTRY, contract_for`. After the move `executor.py` carries `from .step_contracts import STEP_CONTRACTS, StepContract, contract_for, shallow_contract_check` at module scope and `STEP_REGISTRY` never leaves executor, so that exact line resolves unchanged and the file is not edited. `STEP_CONTRACTS` binds the SAME dict object in both modules, so `register_step`'s writes stay visible through either name.

`input_schema_for` is the one moved symbol with no import from `executor` outside `src` - its only consumers are the function-local imports at `editor.py:168` and `interpreter.py:76` (verified by `grep -rn input_schema_for` over the tree) - so it is repointed at `step_contracts`, not re-exported. The private helpers have no consumer outside the moved cluster.

### Why the OTHER candidate clusters must NOT move
- **Expression resolution** carries the ONE `# read-via:` line budgeted to
  `llm/workflow/executor.py` in `tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py` (`_MARKER_BUDGET`,
  exact count 1). Moving it turns that budget RED.
- **`run_workflow`** is a live `monkeypatch.setattr` target (`test_code_review_gate_session.py`,
  `test_code_review_provenance.py`, `test_plan_review_cancel.py`).
- **`StepContext` / `StepResult` / `STEP_REGISTRY`** are read as MODULE ATTRIBUTES (`_ex.X`) across
  ~50 test modules, so nothing that binds to the module object moves.
- The Burr tripwire scans `executor.py` + `interpreter.py` for banned imports and the trigger-list
  prose; the moved cluster has no control flow and no third-party imports and the docstring stays,
  so the tripwire keeps its intended scope unchanged.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has ZERO entries keyed to `llm/workflow/executor.py`, so no
  baselined symbol is relocated (checked before choosing the seam).

### Expected shape
`executor.py` ~790 -> ~655 LOC (below the 720 near-cap band); new `src/rebar/llm/workflow/step_contracts.py` ~190 LOC (over the 100-LOC floor). Moved bodies are byte-identical apart from imports.

### Verification (each command exits non-zero on failure)
- `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py)" -le 720`
- `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/workflow/step_contracts.py)" -ge 100`
- `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt`
- `pytest -m "not integration and not external" tests/unit/workflow tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_scripted_steps.py`
- `make lint`; `make typecheck`; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
- Reference sweep: Serena `find_referencing_symbols` per moved symbol PLUS
  `grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' --include='*.md' .` for each name AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib); no site may still expect a symbol at its OLD home.
baseline.summary: Split llm/workflow/executor.py (790 LOC) along its concern boundary

## Context

Observed 2026-07-10 during the adept-hedge-stain epic close-out: `rebar fsck` reported 14 issues (later 17 after more write activity) — MISSING_CREATE + ORPHAN_EVENT ('pre-snapshot event not captured in source_event_uuids'). This ticket's original open question was whether those were (a) false positives from binary/store version skew (an older binary misreading newer ENQUEUE_ENRICH-era events) or (b) genuine faults.

## RESOLVED (2026-07-11)

The ENQUEUE_ENRICH-introducing change has **already merged to main** (current binary = main 2d1524ad8; `rebar fsck` prints `ensures: 5/5 applied` with NO "store contains events newer than binary" WARN), so AC1's gate is satisfied and the classification can be made from the current binary. Re-running fsck from that binary, the faults **persist** — so they are **NOT version-skew false positives**. They are real, but BENIGN, artifacts (full forensic classification recorded as a comment on this ticket and on 115b):

- **13 ORPHAN_EVENT** — benign snapshot-staleness from a distributed compaction-vs-reconciler
  write race (the Jira reconciler writes an assignee EDIT; a compaction in a different clone
  snapshots before observing it; the reconciler re-emits an identical EDIT after the snapshot
  which drives live state). Live status/assignee verified correct for all 13.
- **4 MISSING_CREATE** — local-only phantom dirs (0 tracked files, not in HEAD, no structural
  refs); 110e is a local duplicate of the tracked epic 6d0d.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] Re-run `rebar fsck` with the ENQUEUE_ENRICH-era binary against the live store and record
  the counts on this ticket. (DONE: 13 ORPHAN_EVENT + 4 MISSING_CREATE, `ensures: 5/5 applied`.)
- [ ] [operator-attested] Classify each fault as version-skew artifact vs real. (DONE: none are version-skew — they
  persist under the current binary; classified real-but-benign per the forensic comment.)
- [ ] [operator-attested] Remediate the real faults with A3-safe tooling (NOT `fsck --repair-snapshots`, which
  rebuilds from the full log and previously corrupted 11/13 statuses): retire each orphan EDIT
  file (`.json` -> `.json.retired`, which fsck skips) and delete the 4 local phantom dirs, then
  confirm `rebar fsck` reports zero ORPHAN_EVENT + zero MISSING_CREATE with no ticket's
  status/assignee changed. (This is the shared remediation tracked jointly with 115b.)

## Notes

- Root cause of the recurring orphan race (compaction snapshotting before observing a remote
  reconciler write) is a separate durable-fix follow-up, out of scope for this classify-and-
  remediate-to-zero ticket.

Scope: root-level `src/rebar/*.py` plus `attest/`, `metrics/`, `review_bot/`, `opcert_service/`, `audit/`, `grounding/`, `_guides/`. ~180 lines leave of 7,248 comment lines (2.5%) — this scope is in good health and the yield is concentrated, not diffuse.

SURFACED A LIVE DEFECT, filed separately: `_mcp_models.BridgeFsckOut` omits `binding_drift`, so the MCP outputSchema under-declares a field `bridge_fsck.py:217` always returns. The comment at `_mcp_models.py:31-34` claiming 'the cross-interface schema tests pin both to the canonical schema' is FALSE — those model names appear zero times in tests/. That false assurance is why the drift went unnoticed.

Two prior leads resolved AGAINST the hypothesis and belong in do_not_move: `_mcp_llm.py`'s 121 docstring lines are the literal wire-visible MCP tool descriptions FastMCP publishes to clients — API surface, not narration, zero recoverable. Caveat that bounds this shard: 280 of `_config_schema.py`'s 792 lines are comments, and for many keys they are the ONLY documentation — `docs/config.md` has zero coverage for `completion_floor_active`, `comment_max_chars`, `auth_proxy_secret_env`. ## Context / Problem

Closing a large epic runs the completion-verifier close gate, whose final `decide@then/verify` step makes an LLM (Bedrock `converse`) call. On epic `3d7a-7795-efde-4df7` (REB-3233, 13 children) the gate ran ~40 minutes and then FAULTED — it produced **neither PASS nor FAIL/BLOCK**, but an error:

```
cannot close 3d7a-7795-efde-4df7: completion verification could not run
(completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict:
 step 'decide@then/verify' failed: the LLM provider call failed:
 Read timeout on endpoint URL:
 "https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6/converse").
```

This is a fault in the gate itself: a transient/among-oversized provider Read timeout is surfaced as "could not run / no verdict", so a legitimate close cannot complete without `--force`. Reproduced deterministically: three consecutive close attempts on this epic all faulted identically (~40+ min each, EXIT 1).

`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:271` classifies `httpx.ReadTimeout` (`httpx.TimeoutException`) as `WAIT_AND_RETRY`, and `config.py` documents a retry policy over transient timeouts — yet the gate still terminated with no verdict via `completion_failures.py:232` ("... did not produce a verdict"). So either the verifier's decide-step path does not apply the retry, retries are exhausted because each attempt sends an oversized accumulated context that itself read-times-out, or the effective per-request timeout is too low for a large-AC epic-close verification.

This defect class has rich history (verifier sharding `12b7`, banked/resumable AC verification `2948`, context reworks `10ae`, step-budget loops `46a2`/`3211`, `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` wiring `02cd`, Bedrock provider seam+timeout `061c`, gates running minutes-scale `1e88`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A transient provider Read timeout during the completion verifier's
  `decide@then/verify` step no longer terminates the gate with "could not run / no
  verdict"; it is handled per the WAIT_AND_RETRY classification (bounded retry) OR
  the verification work is bounded so a single call cannot exceed the provider read
  timeout — root cause to be confirmed by /rebar-debug before the fix. Proven by a
  RED→GREEN test that exercises the confirmed mechanism.
- [x] A large-epic close (many children / large AC set) completes through the gate
  without a raw provider read-timeout fault, or degrades to an actionable verdict
  rather than an un-actionable "could not run".

## Testing

- [x] A unit/integration test reproduces the faulting path (verifier decide step
  raising `httpx.ReadTimeout`) and asserts the post-fix behavior (bounded retry
  and/or bounded context / actionable outcome), seen RED before the fix and GREEN
  after, with a mutation check.
baseline.summary: Completion-verifier close gate faults (no verdict) on a Bedrock Read timeout during decide@then/verify for large-epic closes

## Context / Problem

The Janitor approval for parent story 038d authorizes removing eight long-lived env/config aliases instead of keeping them as permanent ergonomic renames. That approval explicitly chose **clean removal for simplification (no expected clients)**: follow-on work must remove the alias declarations and active parsing/warning paths, not convert these aliases to fail-loud tombstones. Before code or published docs change, the project needs an ADR that records the approval, names each canonical replacement, defines the removal order for the dependent chain, and distinguishes this pre-1.0 operator-approved cleanup from the stronger public/wire/persisted-data compatibility contracts.

## Approach

Allocate the next ADR number through `docs/adr/.numbers`, write the ADR in the standard house style, and record the governing policy for this chain:

| Removed alias | Canonical replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `REBAR_NO_SYNC` | `REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off` |
| `COMPACT_THRESHOLD` | `REBAR_COMPACT_THRESHOLD` |
| `SCRATCH_BASE_DIR` | `REBAR_SCRATCH_BASE_DIR` |
| `REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT` | `REBAR_JIRA_CLI_TIMEOUT` |
| `RECONCILER_ABSENT_GET_BUDGET` | `REBAR_RECONCILER_DELETION_PROBE_LIMIT` |
| `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE=warn` | `REBAR_UNSAFE_ID_GUARD_BYPASS=true` |
| `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` | `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS` |
| `verify.overlap_enabled` | `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` |

The ADR must cite the current authoritative code locations (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py`, `src/rebar/_config_sources.py`, and `src/rebar/_config_sections.py`) for the live aliases and cite the 038d operator approval for the clean-removal rationale. It should call out `REBAR_NO_SYNC` and `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` as transformed-semantics aliases (inverse pull and id-guard bypass) that need explicit migration text, while still applying the same clean-removal policy to the remaining inert renames. It must define the dependency order: this ADR first, then 7370 removes/tombstones only as directed by the implementation plan, then 038d removes live aliases, then 1a63 publishes docs/release notes.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/.numbers`
- new ADR under `docs/adr/`

## Testing

Run `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`, `python scripts/check_docs_index.py`, and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`. Also verify with grep that `docs/api-stability.md` references ADR 0115 and still separately documents the strong public/wire/persisted-data contracts (`--output json` schemas, MCP schemas, event schema, public Python facade, and persisted-data migrations/readers) so this config-alias cleanup is not over-applied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ADR is Accepted, uses the generator-assigned ADR number, and cites the 038d operator approval as clean removal for simplification with no expected clients.
- [ ] The ADR records all eight removed aliases and their canonical replacements exactly as listed in the plan table.
- [ ] The ADR explains that follow-on implementation removes alias declarations and active parsing/warning paths rather than preserving these aliases as permanent aliases or converting them into fail-loud tombstones.
- [ ] The ADR calls out `REBAR_NO_SYNC` and `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` as transformed-semantics aliases requiring explicit migration text.
- [ ] The ADR distinguishes this pre-1.0 config/env alias cleanup from public/wire/persisted-data compatibility contracts.
- [ ] `docs/api-stability.md` contains a minimal cross-reference to ADR 0115 and still documents the separate strong contracts for JSON/MCP schemas, the event schema, the public Python facade, and persisted-data compatibility.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`, `python scripts/check_docs_index.py`, and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` pass.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Teams running several tracker projects against one codebase (or several repos against one ticket store) cannot use the bridge: it is hard-wired to exactly one project at three points — `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`_config_schema.py`), the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one (`fetcher.jqls_for`), and the applier aborts a pass when any outbound mutation targets a key outside that project (`applier.CrossProjectTargetError`). The only escape is the destructive one-way `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`. Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff` and taken as a dependency, not duplicated here.

(Full original description with line-anchored citations preserved verbatim as a ticket comment, 2026-08-13.)

## Approach

Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects. Each ticket records the project it syncs into and the repos it belongs to.

The STORE owns the project set — `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the tickets branch beside `bindings.json`/`prev_snapshot.json`. Reason (mechanical): `prev_snapshot.json` is last-known-remote state; if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would diff the other's projects as remote deletions. A store-owned project set removes that failure mode by construction and leaves no per-repo list to disagree.

Built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`) and the backend-neutral port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)`, `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`. `Backend.project` ("the backend's effective write/create project scope") is the per-repo default for rebar-created tickets; no new config key; generalizes beyond Jira.

Migration writes NO events. The ticket project field is tri-state — absent=legacy, explicit-empty= never sync, explicit key=sync there — mirroring `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths (`docs/ticket-model.md`). Absent resolves against the legacy default recorded in the mapping, seeded by an idempotent check-then-act ensure unit (`docs/migrations.md`, the sanctioned seam; the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built). A per-ticket EDIT migration was rejected: four-figure event writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot entry runs the ensure sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended — an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + the ensure seed. Delivers migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`. Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces; promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out + snapshot union; per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project. Delivers two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create; guard relaxed from single project to set membership. Delivers explicit-project + guard criteria.
- **Store-compat capability stamp** — conditional `required_capabilities` entry + fail-closed read. Delivers final criterion.
- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: rehearse against two live Jira Cloud projects on an
  isolated tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`,
  hence the depends_on); dry-run-gated, all created issues removed. Fixtures cannot reach the
  cross-project contamination failure mode this validates.
- **Module-size relief** — several files this feature edits sit within ~30 lines of the 800 hard cap.
  Behaviour-preserving extractions along existing seams, each ordered ahead of the story needing room;
  they deliver no epic criterion (preconditions; their own criteria are unchanged suite + measured LOC).

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive at every layer. Absent project = legacy; a pre-feature store behaves as today, no operator action. A single-project store never receives the capability stamp, so older binaries keep working; only a genuinely multi-project store fails closed on them — the intended protection (an older binary would fetch its one project, see other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicates in the wrong project). Rollback is per-change on Gerrit; the mapping and capability entry are inert to older binaries apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to implicit-legacy with the idempotent ensure re-stamping on the next covered write.
baseline.summary: Many-to-many tracker projects: per-ticket bridge project + repo association over one shared store

## Context

The one confirmed ungated representation mirror (12a Part 1): `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` + `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` gate the library's public surface, and `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` generates docs from the MCP registrar — but nothing cross-checks the MCP tool surface against the library facade, so the two can drift silently (the S1 sample's live example: MCP tool signatures diverging from the library surface). Precedent: Kubernetes `hack/verify-generated.sh` (regen-in-isolated-worktree + diff); the repo's own generated-registry pattern.

## Approach

Introspect the MCP registrar's tool inventory (names, parameters, defaults) and the library facade functions they wrap; emit a normalized parity manifest; a `--check` mode diffs against the committed manifest and fails on divergence, wired into `make lint`. Regeneration documented in the script's --help. Where a tool intentionally diverges from the facade (e.g., enumerated MCP params vs **fields passthrough — the known edit_ticket case), the manifest records the divergence explicitly so drift is still caught relative to the declared shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: a script produces a normalized MCP↔library parity manifest and `--check` fails (exit != 0) when either side drifts from the committed manifest.
- [x] AC2: `make lint` runs the check; a seeded mismatch (test fixture) proves it fires RED.
- [x] AC3: intentional divergences are declared in the manifest with a reason field, and an undeclared divergence still fails.
- [x] AC4: regeneration is one documented command; docs updated where the sibling generators are documented.

## File impact

- scripts/check_mcp_library_parity.py (new; or extend gen_api_surface.py — decide at implementation against the existing script's structure)
- tests/unit/test_mcp_library_parity.py (new)

# S1 — Gerrit gate config: `Verified` label + two-vote submit requirement

Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).

## Why
The gate today is a single vote (`LLM-Review` only). Adding an independent CI vote requires a
`Verified` label plus a submit requirement that demands it, mirroring the existing `LLM-Review`
label/SR pattern in `infra/gerrit/project.config`.

## What
Add the `Verified` label + submit-requirement + voting ACL, and record the gate-architecture
change (two independent votes) as an ADR superseding/amending ADR-0013.

## Scope
- `infra/gerrit/project.config` (label + submit-requirement + `label-Verified` ACL).
- New ADR superseding/amending ADR-0013; update the gate section of `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`.
- **The submit-requirement ACTIVATION is deferred** until the voter is proven (done in S6) — this
  story authors the config; S6 flips it on. Out of scope: the workflow, g2p, credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add `[label "Verified"]` (function `NoBlock`, values -1/0/+1, `defaultValue = 0`,
      `copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`) to `infra/gerrit/project.config`, mirroring the
      `LLM-Review` label block.
- [ ] Add `[submit-requirement "Verified"] submittableIf = label:Verified=MAX` and grant the CI
      service-account group `label-Verified = -1..+1` (Service Users only; devs cannot self-vote).
- [ ] The intended final gate is `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND label:Verified=MAX AND -has:unresolved`;
      the `Verified` submit-requirement is left inactive/enforcement-deferred until S6 proves the
      voter (avoids blocking all submits during rollout).
- [ ] Write an ADR that supersedes/amends **ADR-0013** documenting the two-independent-vote gate.
