Add plan-review criterion T15 "overlay-derisk" so plans prove risky runtime mechanisms via a fast out-of-loop experiment BEFORE committing them into a slow, codified delivery loop (CI/CD, IaC apply, provisioning pipeline). Motivation: on infra epics, basic failures (a service that won't boot, a credential that doesn't authorize, a dependency that won't connect, a readiness check that never passes) are discovered only at the END of a long delivery cycle. No existing criterion rewards front-loading those checks into a cheap local run or a manual probe against the real target. This is a CORE built-in change (not project-specific), stack-agnostic (no hardcoded Terraform/docker), routed by the self-gating Pass-1 finder like the other Txx overlays.

## The finalized T15 rubric (design of record)

OVERLAY — apply only when ALL of the following hold; else PASS not-applicable.
- S1 Codified loop? the mechanism is delivered/validated by pushing through an automated pipeline or an environment/infrastructure apply, not by running or unit-testing code directly.
- S2 Slow or costly pass? one pass through that loop is slow (minutes-to-hours) or otherwise costly to run.
- S3 Runtime-only correctness? the change introduces behavior whose correctness only resolves when it actually runs in a realistic environment (boots, authenticates, connects, is authorized, passes readiness) — unreachable by static/unit checks.

When applicable, report a finding for each check not satisfied:
- (a) RISK NAMED — the plan identifies the specific mechanism(s) confirmable only by completing the full loop.
- (b) FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF — for each named risk, the plan commits to proving it via the fastest feedback path available for that mechanism, outside the slow loop: running the unit locally/emulated where feasible, OR a manual experiment directly against the real target (an interactive call, a one-off CLI/console action, a probe script, a throwaway resource) where local reproduction isn't possible. The experiment is concrete and returns a verdict in minutes, not a delivery cycle. An unnamed "we'll verify" / "we'll check after deploy" does not satisfy it.
- (c) PROVE-THEN-CODIFY — the cheap experiment comes before committing the mechanism into the slow loop, so the loop validates an already-proven mechanism.
- (d) SCOPED CLEANUP — throwaway experiments are cleaned up afterward, with teardown that removes ONLY the artifacts the experiment itself created (the records a probe inserted, the scratch resource it spun up) and touches nothing pre-existing, shared, or persistent; a cleanup step that could delete, reset, or truncate a resource the experiment did not create (e.g. dropping an existing table or wiping a bucket to "reset" it) fails this check.

ANTI-FP: a manual experiment against the real target is a fully valid proof — never penalize choosing it over local reproduction; many stacks cannot be reproduced locally. A mechanism already proven elsewhere in the codebase needn't be re-proven.

Facet ~ empirical / approach-soundness; exec AGENT (it ground-checks that the named mechanism and named experiment are real/plausible against the codebase). Posture (advisory vs blocking) and block_threshold are NOT decided here — set by the normal registry/review process.

## Required companion change: T10 boundary partition
The de-risk (transient experiment) phase and T10's production-hardening phase must not overlap; there is no runtime cross-criterion suppression by design. Fix by partitioning in T10's own rubric text — add a scope clause: "This overlay evaluates the DURABLE infrastructure — the IaC/config that persists. Transient, throwaway experiments used to de-risk a mechanism before committing it — their creation, isolation, and teardown — are out of scope here." (T10 does NOT name T15 or any other overlay.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] all child tickets are closed
- [x] `rebar explain T15` renders the criterion with its descriptive name (not the bare id), and
      `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` regenerates
      `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with a T15 section, with the criteria-guide and registry
      validators passing
- [x] the writing-a-passing-plan guide instructs authors to de-risk out-of-loop before slow delivery loops,
      evidenced by the T15 guidance appearing in `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`
- [x] the coach-move decision (add or reject the proposed out-of-loop-proof move) is recorded on this epic
      as a comment naming the decision and its rationale
- [x] T10's rubric and regenerated criteria-guide section contain the scope clause partitioning durable infrastructure from transient de-risk experiments. Verify: `python -c "from pathlib import Path; phrase='This overlay evaluates the DURABLE infrastructure'; assert phrase in Path('src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md').read_text(); assert phrase in Path('docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md').read_text()"` exits 0.
baseline.summary: Add plan-review criterion T15 (overlay-derisk): prove risky mechanisms out-of-loop before slow delivery loops

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` requires a plan-review attestation for a bug fix over 150 non-test lines. When the attestation classification itself raises (`classify_plan_review_attestation` catches every exception and returns `verdict: "error"`), `apply_bugfix_size_gate` maps INFRA to an **advisory** finding (module docstring: "Fail-open on infrastructure") and the change keeps `LLM-Review +1`. An infrastructure fault therefore produces the same outcome as a satisfied gate.

## Reproduction
- Gerrit change 1369 (`73abb5805f`, trailer ticket e39f, type bug, 525 non-test lines) merged on `LLM-Review +1` with 0 blocking / 2 advisory findings; the REVIEW_RESULT coverage records the bugfix-size gate as `error`. The ticket `asbestos-lithe-kouprey` (b6e1-c217-8cd3-4446) was later filed against that change.
- Unit: make `_load_ticket_state` raise inside `classify_plan_review_attestation`; `apply_bugfix_size_gate` leaves `verdict` unchanged from PASS.

## Expected
An infrastructure error in a blocking gate abstains instead of passing: the verdict becomes INDETERMINATE, with the classification error surfaced in the coverage record (`coverage.bugfix_size_gate.verdict == "error"`). Downstream (existing behaviour, unchanged by this fix): the review-bot adapter maps a non-PASS verdict with no blocking findings to the `indeterminate` coverage gap and the voter casts the fail-closed `-1` tagged as infrastructure — never a `+1` — so an unclassifiable oversized bug fix can no longer merge on the gate's silence. This is the same fail-closed-on-infra posture the codebase already established (bug 3fce: an unreadable ruling is an error, never a silent degrade; WS5 `detectors.apply_failclosed`).

## Approach
Change only the INFRA arm of `apply_bugfix_size_gate`: instead of appending an advisory finding, set `verdict["verdict"] = "INDETERMINATE"` (never downgrading an existing BLOCK). The coverage entry (already written for every bucket) keeps carrying the `error` verdict and reason, so the bot's infra-recovery/retrigger loop can observe why. Leave the `flag` (BLOCK) and `accepted` (no-op) arms, the ≤150-line no-op, and the missing-trailer no-op unchanged. Update the module docstring (`Fail-open on infrastructure` → fail-closed abstain), `bucket_for_verdict`'s docstring, and the stale caller comment in `finalize.py`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` — the INFRA arm + docstrings.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py` — the call-site comment only.
- `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py` — new RED test for the INDETERMINATE outcome; rewrite the two tests that encoded the old fail-open behaviour (`test_infra_or_unknown_classification_is_advisory_never_blocks`, `test_classifier_exception_degrades_to_advisory`); a guard test that an already-BLOCK verdict is not downgraded.

## Testing
- RED first: classification error on a >150-line non-test bug-fix diff yields `verdict == "INDETERMINATE"`, a coverage entry `bugfix_size_gate.verdict == "error"` / `bucket == "infra"`, and no advisory or blocking finding that reads as a pass.
- Edge: an infra classification when the verdict is already BLOCK leaves BLOCK in place.
- Unchanged behaviour: `unsigned`/`stale-material` still BLOCK, accepted verdicts still no-op, under-floor and test-only diffs never read the store.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A classification error (both the classifier's own `error` verdict and an exception escaping to the gate's outer handler) on an over-floor bug fix produces an INDETERMINATE review verdict, not PASS; checked by the new unit tests in `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py`.
- [x] An infra classification never downgrades an existing BLOCK verdict; checked by a new unit test.
- [x] Existing tests for `unsigned`, certified/stale-code/stale-head, under-floor, test-only, non-bug, and unresolvable-ticket behaviour pass unchanged; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py`.
- [x] The Gerrit voter's existing INDETERMINATE handling (terminal fail-closed `-1`, no `+1`) is unchanged; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k indeterminate`.

## Verification
`pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k "bugfix_size or indeterminate"`; `make lint`; `make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: bugfix-size attestation gate degrades to advisory on classification error, so an infra fault passes the change

baseline.description:
Provision the per-client bearer PATs the `static` verifier authenticates (ADR deft-evolutive-mosasaur) and the repo-root local-only client-credential config the epic asks for, treated like every other box secret: SSM-sourced, materialized on-box, gitignored, never committed. Single concern: the credential material + its safe delivery — client-side config wiring is olm.

## Approach + rationale (SSM-materialize, NOT rsync — gotcha f600)
The `.env` on the box is rsync-EXCLUDED, so a rotated SSM secret never reaches the box via source sync. The bearer PATs must therefore be materialized on the box from SSM at deploy time, exactly like the existing `opcert-guard.map.conf` materialization pattern (a separate SSM-sourced file that nginx/the app reads), NOT baked into the rsync'd tree. A pure value-rotation (no git change) does NOT advance `main`, so autodeploy no-ops on it — rotation is operator-driven (re-materialize + reload), which the runbook must state. Because the `static` verifier loads its token set ONCE at `__init__` (`StaticBearerVerifier.__init__` → `_load_static_tokens`; no per-request re-read), "reload" here means RECONSTRUCTING the verifier — i.e. restarting/replacing the `rebar-mcp` process/container (the ADR 0104 blue-green swap) — NOT merely rewriting the tokens file; an operator who only re-materializes the file sees NO effect. The runbook states this explicitly.
- Terraform SSM params for the per-client PATs (one per client: copilot/codex/claude) under the
  existing `/rebar/prod/` prefix; `fetch-secrets.sh` wiring to materialize them on the box.
- The `static` verifier's accepted-token set is sourced from those materialized secrets. Transform
  (named so the slice is unambiguous): `fetch-secrets.sh` materializes each per-client PAT from SSM
  into the on-box container env source (`.env`, 0600, rsync-excluded) as
  `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_{COPILOT,CODEX,CLAUDE}`, and emits the tokens JSON the verifier reads
  (`infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json`, `mcp.auth_static_tokens_file`) whose records reference
  those env vars via **`token_env`** — NEVER a plaintext `token` and NEVER the raw PAT inside the
  tokens file (ADR 0050 §4 / ADR 0104: the server holds only SHA-256 digests, supplied via env-var
  NAMES, never literals; `_parse_static_record` rejects a plaintext `token`). The tokens file is
  ALWAYS created even when a slot is blank (bug beb1: a missing bind-mount source becomes a
  directory).
- A **repo-root local-only** client-credential config TEMPLATE (committed placeholder-only) —
  `mcp-clients.local.example.json` — that renders to a real gitignored file `mcp-clients.local.json`
  (`.gitignore` pattern `/mcp-clients.local.json`), so an operator wiring a client has a documented
  shape but no secret is ever committed.
- Enumerated gitignore/rsync edits so the materialized artifacts are BOTH gitignored and
  rsync-protected (mirroring the `.env` precedent): add `infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json` (and
  its `.*` temp variants) plus `/mcp-clients.local.json` to the root `.gitignore`, and add
  `--exclude 'infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json'` to `autodeploy.sh` RSYNC_EXCLUDES (~line 163),
  so a value-only re-materialize is never clobbered by `rsync --delete`.
- Blank-slot behavior: `fetch-secrets.sh` OMITS the `token_env` record for any client whose
  `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_*` slot is unset/empty (so `_parse_static_record` never sees an empty `token_env`
  and cannot fail the whole verifier). The file is still ALWAYS created (beb1); when ALL slots are
  blank it is `{"tokens": []}`, and the `static` verifier then fails-closed at startup
  (`_load_static_tokens` raises "defines no tokens") — the intended state until an operator
  populates at least one PAT.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Tier: **real file/CLI + a committed-secret guard test** (test-design §3 CLI + §6 contrast). Oracles:
  - The gitignored real credential path `mcp-clients.local.json` is matched by `.gitignore` and a
    guard test asserts `git check-ignore` returns it AND that no file in the tree contains a real PAT
    pattern (the negative control: the committed template `mcp-clients.local.example.json` with a
    placeholder passes; a planted real-looking secret fails). Proof:
    `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k guard`.
  - `fetch-secrets.sh` materializes the per-client PATs from SSM: the raw value lands ONLY in the
    0600 rsync-excluded env source (`.env` as `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_*`), and the tokens JSON the `static`
    verifier reads (`mcp-static-tokens.json`) references it via `token_env` (never a plaintext
    `token`, never the raw value in the tokens file). Oracle: with a stubbed SSM/aws sink feeding a
    known value → the materialized env source contains the value AND the tokens file loads via the
    real `_load_static_tokens`/`_parse_static_record` path (token_env records); both files are
    gitignored (NOT under the rsync'd tree), and the tokens file is created even when a slot is
    blank (beb1). Proof: `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k materialize`.
  - Config-effect contrast (§6): the `static` verifier (`StaticBearerVerifier` over the materialized
    tokens file with the per-client env var set) accepts a request bearing a materialized PAT and
    rejects an unknown token (401) through the real `_load_static_tokens` read path. Proof:
    `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k verifier`.
- [x] The runbook documents operator-driven rotation (re-materialize + restart/replace the
  `rebar-mcp` process/container so the verifier re-reads the tokens file; autodeploy no-ops on a
  value-only rotation). Proof: checked via `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k runbook`
  asserting `infra/runbooks/mcp-client-pats.md` documents the re-materialize + reload (restart)
  rotation and that a file-only rewrite has no effect on a running verifier.

## Testing
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py` — the guard, materialization, verifier-contrast,
  and runbook oracles above (RED-first; the ACs are the oracle).
- `make lint && make typecheck` — gate the new Python test module + touched sources.

## Compat / rollback
Additive (new SSM params + materialization). Rollback = remove the params + materialization step; no existing secret path changes. Never commits a secret (enforced by the guard test above).

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur (ADR fixes the auth mode = static bearer). Blocks: unmythical-uninspired-olm (client configs need the PAT values).
baseline.summary: MCP client credential handling: SSM-sourced local-only config template + gitignore

## Why
Operator direction (2026-08-15): approach viral-peppy-lowchen (b4be-0ed8-22cb-4b01) as an EXPERIMENT before any production design. Experience says a pure evidence-prepacked single-pass verifier yields false-positive REJECTIONS whenever the prepack is imperfect — and a perfect prepack over natural-language prose ACs is unrealistic. Operator counter-proposal to test: use the single pass as a FILTER that may only PASS or ABSTAIN per criterion (never reject), then run the existing agentic verifier scoped to the remaining criteria — narrowing agentic work, not eliminating it. Structural consequence: false-positive rejection is impossible by construction; the residual risks to MEASURE are false-positive PASSes and insufficient coverage (filter abstains so often it saves nothing).

## Protocol (rapid PoC — throwaway harness, no production code)
1. Corpus: select >=3 real CLOSED tickets with large surfaces (description near the 8000-char cap, >=6 prose ACs, comments; at least one with children), e.g. the tapeworm CLI-normalization ticket (7998 chars) and the bettong decomposition ticket. Ground truth for these = all ACs met (they passed the close gate). Add >=3 ADVERSARIAL variants: copies (in-harness, not written to the store) with 1-2 ACs edited to be genuinely unmet (reference a symbol/behavior that does not exist at the verified ref). Ground truth = those ACs unmet.
2. Prepack builder (harness script): per AC, deterministically assemble evidence — file_impact paths + their content slices, grep hits for symbols/strings the AC names, referencing commits + diffs, test names/results where cited. Cap per-AC pack size; record pack-build failures honestly (missing evidence -> thin pack, NOT a synthesized one).
3. Filter pass: ONE LLM call, no tools: given ticket text + per-AC packs, emit per AC either PASS(with citations) or ABSTAIN. The contract forbids FAIL.
4. Fallback: run the existing agentic verifier scoped to the ABSTAINed ACs via the ticket-load seam: `verify_completion` loads the root ticket through `_reads.show_ticket` (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:197); the harness monkeypatches that read (the standard unit-suite technique) to return the real ticket with its Acceptance Criteria block REDUCED to the abstained ACs. Criteria enumeration (`explicit_completion_criteria`, completion_criteria.py:45) and the step floor (completion.py:212-237, keyed on checkbox count) both derive from that text, so the budget narrows automatically — that IS the mechanism under test. Read-only --source local, never signs.
4b. Comparability: the pure-agentic control runs the SAME harness (same monkeypatch machinery, un-reduced ticket, same ref, same config) so fixed overheads cancel; the cost delta is reported as (filter LLM call + narrowed agentic run) vs (full agentic run), each with its own auto-derived floor. Child-closure/precheck asymmetries are avoided by corpus selection: childless tickets verify identically in both arms; the one with-children ticket is reported separately with this caveat stated.
5. Metrics table (the deliverable): filter coverage (%% ACs PASSed at step 3), false-PASS count on adversarial unmet ACs (MUST be 0 for the design to survive), agentic steps/tokens/wall-time for step 4 vs a pure-agentic control run of the same ticket, per-ticket totals.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no src/rebar changes).
- [x] >=3 real large closed tickets + >=3 adversarial variants run end-to-end through filter+fallback AND a pure-agentic control.
- [x] Metrics table posted as a comment on THIS ticket and on viral-peppy-lowchen: coverage, false-PASS count, cost deltas.
- [x] Verdict comment: does filter+fallback beat pure-agentic on cost WITHOUT any false PASS? Include failure modes observed and a go/no-go recommendation for productizing.
- [x] No store writes beyond ticket comments; no signatures minted (--source local only).
baseline.summary: Experiment: prepack single-pass FILTER + narrowed agentic fallback (lowchen PoC)

baseline.description:
# Stage-2 bounded LLM pairwise overlap judge (advisory findings + suggested link commands)

## Why
Precision lives in stage 2, not in a similarity threshold. The recall spike (epic experiment comment) showed retrieval recall is excellent BUT flagged precision-at-scale as the residual risk (same model produces query+doc digests → vocabularies converge → near-duplicates converge too). This judge IS that precision mitigation: a bounded LLM pairwise classifier over the ~K stage-1 candidates.

## What — output schema (fully specified, DIRECTED)
Output `overlap_verdict` (register in `contracts.py`): `{relation: enum, shared_artifact: string|null, confidence: number, abstain: bool}`, `relation ∈ {duplicates, supersedes, depends_on, related_distinct, unrelated}` (CLOSED). The judge is prompted with an ORDERED pair (First, Second) and its `relation` is read DIRECTIONALLY as "First `relation` Second" (e.g. `supersedes` ⇒ "First supersedes Second"; `depends_on` ⇒ "First depends_on Second"). Only `duplicates|supersedes|depends_on` are surfaceable; the `rebar link` relation set is the 6 built-ins (`blocks, depends_on, relates_to, duplicates, supersedes, discovered_from`) — the judge only ever emits the three surfaceable ones.
- Both orderings run: ordering-1 = (Q=query, C=candidate) → r1 = "Q r1 C"; ordering-2 = (C, Q) → r2 = "C r2 Q". AGGREGATION (fail-safe toward "distinct"; each side must cite a non-null `shared_artifact` and both `confidence >= overlap_conf_threshold`, else downgrade to `related_distinct`, not surfaced; an `abstain:true` in EITHER ordering also downgrades and consumes no surface slot):
  - **`duplicates` (symmetric):** surface iff r1 == r2 == `duplicates`.
  - **`supersedes`/`depends_on` (DIRECTIONAL):** surface iff exactly ONE ordering asserts the directional relation and the other is DIRECTION-CONSISTENT (not the same label pointing the other way). Concretely, r1 ∈ {supersedes,depends_on} is surfaced as "Q r1 C" only if r2 does NOT assert the reciprocal "C r1 Q" (r2 ∈ {related_distinct, unrelated, or the inverse}). If BOTH orderings assert the same directional label with opposite subjects (r1="Q supersedes C" AND r2="C supersedes Q"), that is a self-contradiction → downgrade to `related_distinct` (not surfaced). This resolves the inverted-`link_command` ambiguity: the surfaced direction is taken from the single ordering that consistently asserts it.
- Surface ≤ `overlap_surface_cap` (default 3) highest-confidence results: `{source_id, target_id, relation, shared_artifact, confidence, link_command}`. The `link_command` uses the DIRECTED pair: for a directional relation, `rebar link <source_id> <target_id> <relation>` where (source→target) is the asserting ordering's (First→Second) — so "Q supersedes C" ⇒ `rebar link Q C supersedes` and "C supersedes Q" ⇒ `rebar link C Q supersedes` (never both). For symmetric `duplicates`, canonicalize the pair by sorted ticket-id so the command is deterministic: `rebar link <min(Q,C)> <max(Q,C)> duplicates`.
- K candidates → 2K judge calls (both orderings), flat in corpus size.
- Errors: LLM timeout/error/malformed output on a candidate → treated as `abstain` (dropped), logged; never raises to the caller.

## Config (LLMConfig, not VerifyConfig) — with explicit `from_env` wiring
`overlap_conf_threshold: float = 0.7`, `overlap_surface_cap: int = 3` on `LLMConfig` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`) — LLM tunables; `_config_schema.py` reserves `llm.*`, so NOT `VerifyConfig`. **`from_env()` MUST be edited** (it constructs `LLMConfig(...)` reading every field via a helper): add module constants `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD = 0.7` / `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP = 3`, the two dataclass fields, and in `from_env`'s `return cls(...)`:
- `overlap_conf_threshold=_llm_float(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD", "overlap_conf_threshold", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD)`
- `overlap_surface_cap=_llm_int(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP", "overlap_surface_cap", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP)`

(`_llm_float` is added by S2 wood-heedless-sheldrake, a sibling — if S2 has not landed in the stack yet, this story adds it, mirroring `_llm_int`.)

## Dependencies
S5 (`OverlapCandidate` interface + query/corpus digests). Consumed by S7. (S5 is a sibling story; a codebase grep won't find `OverlapCandidate` until it lands.)

## Scope
- New `src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py` + rubric prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/overlap_judge.md` (`execution_mode: single_turn`, `outputs: overlap_verdict`, `category: overlap`) whose body MUST encode: the CLOSED 5-value `relation` classification ({duplicates, supersedes, depends_on, related_distinct, unrelated} — only the first three surfaceable), the require-a-cited-shared-artifact gate, the both-orderings instruction, and the abstain-when-unsure criterion.
- `overlap_verdict` schema `src/rebar/schemas/overlap_verdict.schema.json` + `register_contract("overlap_verdict", <builder>)` at the bottom of `contracts.py` (co-located with `response_model_for`, guaranteeing registration before use). WIRE the schema in `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` (`OVERLAP_VERDICT = "overlap_verdict"`, `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["overlap_judge"] = OVERLAP_VERDICT`, add to `__all__`) so `test_every_schema_file_is_wired` passes.
- **Deliverable — labeled fixtures:** `tests/fixtures/overlap_pairs/` with ≥12 labeled pairs (each `{a_digest, b_digest, gold_relation}`), COMMITTED as part of this story (consumed by `test_judge_precision_recall`).
- Config field wiring in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` (enumerated above).
- OUT: retrieval (S5), wiring (S7).

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` (FakeRunner): `test_agree` (both agree+artifact → surfaced); `test_disagree_downgrade`; `test_requires_artifact` (null artifact → not surfaced); `test_abstain_dropped` (no slot consumed); `test_cap` (≤ surface_cap); `test_link_command` (valid relation string); `test_directional_link_command` (for `supersedes`/`depends_on`, the emitted `link_command` uses the asserting ordering's source→target direction — `rebar link Q C supersedes` NOT `C Q`; and a both-orderings-same-directional-label contradiction downgrades to `related_distinct`); `test_duplicates_canonical` (`duplicates` command uses sorted-id pair, deterministic); `test_llm_error_abstain` (no raise); `test_config` (sets `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP`, asserts `LLMConfig.from_env()` resolves both from the env — proving `from_env` wiring, not just defaults).
- Precision/recall check as a PYTEST FIXTURE test (NOT the prompt-eval harness — no registered scorer exists for the `overlap_verdict` shape): `test_judge_precision_recall` (a deterministic UNIT test: a FakeRunner returns canned per-pair `overlap_verdict`s over a LABELED fixture of ≥12 pairs at `tests/fixtures/overlap_pairs/`, no live LLM) computes precision AND recall and asserts precision ≥0.8 AND recall ≥0.6 (the recall floor stops an abstain-everything judge from trivially passing). Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py::test_judge_precision_recall`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Judges both orderings, aggregates by the stated rule; `pytest ...::{test_agree,test_disagree_downgrade}`.
- [ ] Surfaces only with a non-null `shared_artifact`, else `related_distinct`; `::test_requires_artifact`. Abstain drops without consuming a slot; `::test_abstain_dropped`.
- [ ] ≤ `overlap_surface_cap` (default 3) findings, each `{source_id, target_id, relation∈{duplicates,supersedes,depends_on}, shared_artifact, confidence, link_command}`; the `link_command` is DIRECTED correctly (directional relation uses the asserting ordering's source→target; `duplicates` uses sorted-id canonical pair); `::{test_cap,test_link_command,test_directional_link_command,test_duplicates_canonical}`.
- [ ] LLM error on a candidate → abstain, logged, no raise; `::test_llm_error_abstain`.
- [ ] Fixture test `test_judge_precision_recall` (≥12 labeled pairs) asserts precision ≥0.8 AND recall ≥0.6; `::test_judge_precision_recall`.
- [ ] `overlap_conf_threshold` (0.7) and `overlap_surface_cap` (3) are read from the env by `LLMConfig.from_env()` (explicit wiring, `_llm_float` for the threshold); `::test_config`.
baseline.summary: Stage-2 bounded LLM pairwise overlap judge (advisory findings + suggested link commands)

## Problem

The config-root guard flags `os.path.dirname(tracker)` but **does NOT flag** `os.path.dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)`. Both compose the repo/config root from the store path — the precise construct the guard exists to eliminate — but only the first is detected.

Measured on 2026-08-28 while adjudicating `scathing-custommade-bobcat` (6bf1-326b-7404-4034): both forms were placed in one file under `src/`; the guard flagged the bare form and passed the `.canonical` form.

## Why this matters more than a missed lint

The guard is what makes an acceptance criterion like 6bf1 AC#3 ("ZERO deferred config-root sites") meaningful. A construct the guard cannot see would sit in the tree **unflagged**, while that AC truthfully reports zero — so the criterion would pass while the defect class it protects is present. A guard with a blind spot is worse than a missing guard, because it converts an unchecked assumption into a checked-looking one.

This is not hypothetical: a concurrently-proposed redesign of `run_sweep` used exactly `dirname(canonical tracker)` as its fallback arm and would have entered the tree unsanctioned.

## Mechanism

By its own docstring the detector matches the bare name, `*.tracker_dir()`, and `str()`-wrapped forms, and deliberately does **not** unwrap the `realpath`/`abspath` family. `StorePaths(...).canonical` is in that unwrapped family. The guard remedy text already names `config.repo_root_or_none()` as the sanctioned fix, so the intended contract is clear; the detector simply does not cover this spelling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guard flags `os.path.dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)` in a file under `src/`.
- [ ] The guard flags the equivalent `realpath`/`abspath`-wrapped spellings of the same composition, or the decision to exclude each is recorded in the guard docstring with its reason.
- [ ] No existing sanctioned site newly fails: the guard still exits 0 on the current tree, or every new finding is triaged and either fixed or sanctioned.
- [ ] The detector change is proven non-vacuous: a seeded positive is flagged AND the clean tree passes, so the test cannot pass by never running.

## Testing

- Add a guard self-test that seeds each newly-covered spelling and asserts a finding, plus a negative control asserting the clean tree passes.
- Mutation-check: disable the new matching arm and confirm the seeded case survives (proving the assertion is load-bearing). Verify the seed actually applied — anchor the edit to a line start, since a replace that lands in a comment produces a mutant that was never seeded.
- Run the full guard over the repo and record the before/after finding counts.
baseline.summary: Config-root guard misses dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical), the exact construct it exists to catch

baseline.description:
The AWS review-bot holds a persistent tickets clone that a redeploy does not refresh, and it writes on every Gerrit vote. Give it diverged-detection, and fix the deploy path so the change actually reaches the box. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Its clone lives on an EBS-backed external volume (`docker-compose.yml:127`, `external: true`) cloned once behind `if [ ! -d .git ]` (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:117`, itself nested inside `if [ -n "${REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT:-}" ]` at `:112`), so a redeploy does **not** converge it. It writes a `code_review` ticket and auto-pushes on **every** vote (`voter.py:260-343`, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`) — event-driven, not scheduled, so pausing AWS *schedules* does not stop it.

This is **new code, not a predicate fix**: `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` currently does only `git config user.email/user.name` (`:52-53`) then `run_ensures` (`:59`) — no fetch, no reset, no ancestry test. Note its invocation at `Dockerfile.reviewbot:125` sits OUTSIDE the PAT block, so new logic there runs even with the PAT unset.

**Chicken-and-egg:** `autodeploy.sh:186`'s rsync — which is what refreshes the box's copy of these scripts — runs only when `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS` changed (`:55` = `src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot pyproject.toml infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`). A commit touching only these two scripts would never reach the box. So this must land in the **same change** as an `src/rebar/` edit (A6-0a qualifies).

## Approach
1. Add diverged-detection to `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`: if `HEAD` is not an ancestor of
   `origin/tickets` and not strictly ahead, `fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets`. Safe because the
   bot never holds unpushed work (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`).
2. Add `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` to `autodeploy.sh:55`'s `BOT_PATHS`, so future
   edits to it deploy at all.

Vote safety is already guaranteed and must not regress: `voter.py:698` records the vote **before** `emit_code_review_artifact` (`:735`), and that call is wrapped in `except Exception` -> `_artifact_emit_error` + `logger.warning` + `return None` (`:368-371`) — documented as "the vote is already cast, so this never fails the review". A store failure cannot wedge the `LLM-Review` gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a clone diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared tip), the script re-converges it to
      `origin/tickets` and leaves no local commits. Tier: **shell integration** against two real
      temporary repos.
- [ ] Given an up-to-date or merely-behind clone, the script makes **no** destructive change
      (negative control). Tier: **shell integration**.
- [ ] With `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` unset, the new logic still executes (it sits outside the PAT
      block). Tier: **shell integration** with the env var unset.
- [ ] `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` appears in `autodeploy.sh`'s `BOT_PATHS`. Verify:
      grep assertion in a test.
- [ ] A rebar store write failure inside the bot still leaves the vote cast (regression guard). Tier:
      **unit** on `emit_code_review_artifact` with an injected store failure.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0a (and must ship in the same change as an `src/rebar/` edit).
baseline.summary: A6-0b: make the review-bot's tickets clone self-converge, and fix its deploy trigger

## Context / Problem
Rebar has hard-won structured-output behavior split between bespoke retry orchestration and Pydantic AI. The approved RP-01 plan makes Pydantic AI authoritative for Agent turns, structured-output retries, fallback, usage limits, and instrumentation while retaining Rebar policy for deterministic repair, provider safety, failure taxonomy, provenance, and artifacts. Recovery authority and the complete approved behavior ledger are recorded on `sandstone-fiendish-auk` and `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-research.md`.

## Scope Boundary
This epic implements RP-01 only. RP-02 through RP-06 are separate janitor findings with independent architecture, risk, approval, decomposition, and plan-review lifecycles; they are explicitly outside this epic. RP-07 through RP-28 remain unrecoverable and unapproved from the available session record.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Structured-output validation and recovery execute through one Pydantic Agent operation with the approved shared request budget; verified by the child retry-contract tests covering tool turns, output retries, and exhaustion.
- [x] Retry context never truncates authoritative input, accepted output, or stored history; the complete failed response is included only on proven fit and otherwise omitted whole, verified by the child complete/omit and oversize-input tests.
- [x] Rebar preserves deterministic extraction, fallback eligibility, terminal refusal/filter behavior, typed exhaustion, final-failure artifacts, and answering-model provenance; verified by the mapped child regression matrices.
- [x] Successful operations report complete Pydantic run usage exactly once, while fallback/downgrade candidates remain trace or journal events rather than a competing usage counter; verified by the child usage and trace contracts.
- [ ] The bespoke structured-output retry loop is removed only after the compatibility suite and authorized Anthropic/Bedrock cache canaries pass; verified by the cutover child source census, focused suite, and recorded live evidence.

## Child Decomposition
- The output-policy child adapts deterministic Rebar validation to Pydantic output processing and owns the first two policy-level acceptance outcomes.
- The bounded-operation child owns retry scheduling, request limits, complete-or-omit wire history, output-size guidance, and terminal refusal behavior.
- The compatibility child owns aggregate usage, narrow causal error restoration, diagnostics, and final-failure artifacts.
- The observability child owns candidate-identified fallback/downgrade traces without changing Pydantic usage semantics.
- The cutover child migrates remaining consumers, runs full and live parity evidence, and removes the obsolete retry path after its prerequisites land.

The children have non-overlapping RP-01 policy ownership. Their explicit dependency edges enforce the expand-contract order.
baseline.summary: RP-01 — Pydantic-native structured-output operation

baseline.description:
The plan-review gate's deterministic check **P2 ("resolution") abstained `no_repo_root`** on the normal `attested` CLI/library path, so the LLM plan-completeness findings could not be code-grounded and landed as `indeterminate / reason: no-verification` (validity 0, severity none) instead of being verified into advisory or dropped. The verdict still computed (PASS when 0 blocking), but the review was running effectively blind to the code.

## Root cause (proven via joe-debug, runtime evidence)
There is no single authoritative resolver for the gate's *code read-root*; it was threaded ad-hoc across five hops (`review_plan → produce_plan_review_verdict → run_workflow → StepContext → workflow op → assemble_context`) and dropped to `None` at the workflow boundary. The det-floor op `plan_review_precheck` called `assemble_context(tid, repo_root=None)` with no `cfg`, so `PlanContext.repo_root` was `None` and `det_floor.p2_resolution` abstained `no_repo_root` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:227`). The degraded/step-budget-fail path ran the det floor on the *original* ctx (which had `repo_root`), which is why a step-budget-failed run showed P2 **pass** — the inconsistency fingerprint. Runtime evidence: `precheck(repo_root=None)` → abstain `no_repo_root`; `precheck(repo_root=<dir>)` → P2 ran (11 refs, 9 resolved).

## Reproduction Steps
1. From the repo venv: `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50 rebar review-plan <task-id> -o json`.
2. Inspect `coverage.det.P2` → before the fix: `{"status": "abstain", "ran": false, "reason": "no_repo_root"}`.
3. Observe the LLM findings come back as `indeterminate` with `reason: "no-verification"`.

- **Expected:** in a gate run an attested snapshot is active (origin/main HEAD by default), so P2 runs against it (`ran: true`) and findings are code-grounded.
- **Actual:** P2 abstains `no_repo_root`; findings are parked as `no-verification` indeterminate.

## Fix (class-level, not just the immediate bug)
Centralize code-read-root resolution into a single resolver and use it at the assembly seam, so the "None → silent degrade" class is eliminated and the snapshot defaults to origin/main HEAD cleanly when nothing is specified:
- `rebar.llm.config.resolve_code_root(repo_root=None, *, cfg_repo_path=None, allow_checkout_fallback=True)` — cascade: explicit `repo_root` > `cfg.repo_path` > active attested snapshot (`current_code_root`, origin/main HEAD by default) > live checkout. Default never returns None; `allow_checkout_fallback=False` yields snapshot-or-None for lightweight builders that must not force a checkout root (which would induce cache writes).
- `orchestrator.assemble_context` resolves the `PlanContext.repo_root` **field** via the resolver (`allow_checkout_fallback=False` → snapshot-or-None) — so EVERY workflow det-floor/grounding op picks up the active snapshot, while the op's `repo_root` ARG (the ticket-store read-root) is untouched.

### Key invariant: code read-root vs ticket-store read-root are DISTINCT
The workflow's `repo_root` is the **ticket-store** read-root (it reaches `assemble_context`'s `rebar.show_ticket(repo_root=…)` via `StepContext`) — NOT the code read-root, which is a separate snapshot (`cfg.repo_path`/`current_code_root`). Threading the *code* snapshot through the workflow `repo_root` breaks ticket reads ("Ticket not found"), because the ticket store is not under the .git-less code snapshot. `produce_plan_review_verdict` therefore passes its ticket-store `repo_root` through UNCHANGED (a NOTE documents this); the code root is resolved at the `assemble_context` seam, and the agentic verifier reads code via `cfg.repo_path`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single `resolve_code_root` resolver exists with the documented cascade; never returns None by default; `allow_checkout_fallback=False` returns snapshot-or-None (unit test `test_resolve_code_root_cascade` covers all four levels + the None branch).
- [ ] `assemble_context` no longer yields `PlanContext.repo_root=None` when an attested snapshot is active; off-gate callers (no snapshot, no cfg) keep `None` (no checkout-write regression).
- [ ] The code read-root and the ticket-store read-root are kept distinct: `plan_review_precheck` grounds P2 against the active code snapshot WITHOUT hijacking the ticket-store root, and `produce_plan_review_verdict` passes the ticket-store `repo_root` through unchanged (never substitutes `cfg.repo_path`) — regression tests assert both, with a mutation check.
- [ ] A real `rebar review-plan` in attested mode reports `coverage.det.P2.ran == true` (not `no_repo_root`) and findings are grounded (the `no-verification` indeterminate set collapses). Verified: verdict PASS, P2 ran (11 refs, 9 resolved), indeterminate findings 6 → 1.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; the plan_review/workflow/config unit suites pass with no repo-root leak-guard failures.
baseline.summary: Plan-review gate: P2 abstains no_repo_root on attested path; centralize code-root resolution

baseline.description:
## Summary
Epic dark-acme-lumen (#98) added the kind-keyed `state['attestations']` projection in `reducer/_processors.py:process_signature`, but did NOT bump `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` in `reducer/_cache.py` (still 3). A build WITHOUT the attestations projection (e.g. an older global `pipx` install) writes a version-3 `.cache.json` that lacks `attestations`; a newer build sharing the same `.tickets-tracker` then serves that stale cache (matching dir_hash) and reports NO attestations.

## Impact
The plan-review CLAIM gate (`require_plan_review_for_claim`) verifies STRICTLY from `state['attestations']['plan-review']` (signing.verify_signature(kind=...)). A stale cache makes a genuinely-certified attestation read as 'unsigned', so `rebar claim` is BLOCKED on a validly-reviewed ticket. Observed live on b744 (the legacy `signature` mirror + `verify-signature` certify fine; the kind-keyed map is absent until the cache is deleted and the ticket re-reduced). Affects any mixed-build environment (the dogfood checkout's local build + the global pipx build / MCP server / hooks).

## Reproduction Steps
1. Earn a plan-review attestation on a ticket with a build that has the attestations projection.
2. Have an older build (no attestations projection, same `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION=3`) read the ticket (writes a stale cache).
3. `rebar claim <id>` -> 'no certified plan-review attestation (signature: unsigned)' despite `verify-signature` certifying.

Expected: a projection change invalidates prior caches (claim succeeds on a certified ticket).
Actual: stale cache served; claim wrongly blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` is bumped whenever the reduced-state projection changes (bump it for the attestations addition), so caches written by a build with different projection logic are never served.
- [ ] A test asserts that a ticket carrying a signed plan-review SIGNATURE event reduces to a populated `state['attestations']['plan-review']` even when a pre-projection `.cache.json` is present.
- [ ] Workaround documented for mixed-build checkouts (delete `.cache.json` / single-build env).

## Notes
Discovered while implementing the code-review epic (b744). Workaround in use: delete the ticket's `.cache.json` immediately before `rebar claim`. NOT fixed here (out of scope for the code-review capability).
baseline.summary: Reducer cache not invalidated by kind-keyed attestations projection (stale .cache.json hides state['attestations'])

## Reproduction Steps

1. Two tickets A, B bound to Jira with a `blocks`/`relates_to`/`depends_on` link present BOTH locally and as a Jira issuelink.
2. Remove the link locally: `rebar unlink A B`.
3. Run a reconcile pass.

**Expected:** the Jira issuelink is removed to match local; the unlink sticks.
**Actual:** the local unlink is silently reverted every pass (outbound `_diff_links` is ADD-only -> Jira keeps the link -> inbound `_diff_links_inbound` re-adds it locally).

## Root Cause

Same asymmetric-clear class as parent-detach: both link differs are ADD-only (`outbound_differ.py:983-1040`, `inbound_differ.py:440-514`); the applier has no remove-link path (`batch_dispatch.py:554-595`) and acli has no delete-link method.

## Design (consumes the shared managed-ref gate from parent story safe-luge-nog)

Make link removal LOCAL-AUTHORITATIVE via the shared, compaction-surviving managed-ref provenance gate:
- Outbound `_diff_links` emits a REMOVE for a Jira link of a mapped type, absent locally, ONLY when the ref is in `managed_refs` (deliberate unlink) — a never-managed Jira link is left for inbound ADOPT, never clobbered.
- New acli `delete_relationship(from_key, to_key, link_type)` (treat 404-on-already-gone as success).
- `batch_dispatch.update_one` routes the REMOVE through it, guarding HTTP errors non-fatally.
- Same-pass suppression: when outbound emits a link REMOVE for to_key, suppress the inbound link-ADD for that target (remove-wins) so local wins.
- NO inbound-remove dual (keeps links local-authoritative, consistent with parent).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_diff_links` emits a managed-ref-gated REMOVE for a Jira link absent locally; a never-managed Jira link emits NO remove (adopted inbound instead).
- [ ] New acli delete-relationship method removes a Jira issuelink; 404-on-gone treated as success; unit-tested.
- [ ] `batch_dispatch.update_one` applies the link REMOVE, HTTP errors non-fatal.
- [ ] Same-pass suppression drops the inbound link-ADD echo of an outbound link REMOVE.
- [ ] Regression tests (RED->GREEN, mutation-checked): local-unlink of a managed link emits an outbound remove and is not re-added inbound; a never-managed Jira link is adopted not removed; survives a compaction boundary.
baseline.summary: Issue-link/dep REMOVAL churn: same asymmetric-clear pattern as parent-detach (both differs ADD-only)

## Post-mortem follow-up for incident `1c0d-fe83-0254-444a` (defectible-cretinoid-ladybird)

Root cause CONFIRMED (see the RCA + reproducer on 1c0d). This ticket tracks the written post-mortem and the pre-incident-prevention analysis the operator requested. **Write the narrative after the immediate fix lands.**

## What happened (confirmed mechanism)
A Bedrock account-level throttle (429, *retryable*/`WAIT_AND_RETRY`) triggers `model_classes.should_fall_back` to FAIL THE FRONTIER CHAIN OVER from `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` to its configured `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` fallback. In these environments `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is absent, so the fallback raises a bare `TypeError: Could not resolve authentication method`. `should_fall_back(TypeError)` is False → pydantic-ai re-raises the `TypeError` → `failure.classify_llm_failure` maps an unmatched `TypeError` → `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` (non-retryable) → the gate emits a hard INDETERMINATE (not the retryable exit-11). Shared account ⇒ every session fails over at once ⇒ fleet-wide claim-gate stall. **The failover converted a benign retryable throttle into a hard INDETERMINATE.**

## Why it reached production (contributing factors)
- Concurrent frontier/opus `review-plan` fan-out across many sessions on ONE shared Bedrock account pushed it into account-level throttling (self-inflicted load — the orchestrator's own agent fan-out contributed).
- The failover path keeps only the terminal exception, so a retryable throttle is masked as a non-retryable INDETERMINATE (latent disposition-masking defect).
- Config chain fails over to a fallback that is not credentialed in these environments.
- No client-side concurrency limit / rate-limit on shared-account frontier gate ops.
- No failover on credential errors exists as a documented rule, but the analogous throttle case was not excluded from failover.

## Candidate origin
`8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8` ("Enable class-scoped Anthropic fallback", 2026-08-10) — deliberate operator-approved config; before it a throttle stayed exit-11 retryable on the primary. Same change previously implicated in prompt-cache bug 96f3.

## Timeline / detection / response (to expand)
- Detection: multiple sessions reported INDETERMINATE simultaneously; operator surfaced it.
- Response: rubied secret-work cleared as a cause; local resources verified healthy (load 3.5, disk 28%, no orphaned load); load-shed applied (paused new LLM gate ops on 8 running agents); incident ticket 1c0d filed; /rebar-debug root-caused WITHOUT adding Bedrock load (mocked provider). Corroborated by prior session log 4f6b (inner-amiable-grebe) + its operator workaround.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Immediate fix for 1c0d landed (throttle no longer surfaces as INDETERMINATE).
- [ ] Post-mortem narrative written (timeline, mechanism, contributing factors, blast radius, response, lessons).
- [ ] Pre-incident prevention remediations evaluated across plan-review / code-review / CI and each filed as a linked ticket (see below).

## Prevention remediations to evaluate (post-fix)
1. **CI/test:** an eval or unit test asserting a provider throttle/timeout/truncation degrades to the RETRYABLE disposition, never a hard INDETERMINATE — a regression oracle for this class.
2. **Code-review / lint:** guard that a failover target must be credential-reachable in the environments it runs, or that a retryable primary error is not silently upgraded to non-retryable by the fallback's own failure.
3. **Operational / architecture:** a client-side concurrency limiter or rate-limit on shared-account frontier gate ops (defense-in-depth against self-inflicted throttling); consider whether many-agent fan-out on one Bedrock account needs a shared budget.
4. **Plan-review:** whether portability/provider-availability criteria should flag a fallback chain whose terminal arm can be uncredentialed.
baseline.summary: Post-mortem: fleet-wide review-plan INDETERMINATE from throttle-triggered keyless failover

baseline.description:
## Context
Construction-time or preview-time repair would violate read-only commands. Retirement completion is safe only after provider preflight and exclusive pass ownership succeed and under-lock staleness validation passes, and it must precede any remote observation so the pass cannot interleave fresh liveness evidence with completion.

## Outcome
Invoke the S3 recovery operation once at the validated write-bearing reconcile boundary before remote observation; every read-only or filtered path stays zero-write for this operation.

## Verified invocation site (corrected from this task's original impact set)
The original plan named `run_differs.py`. That is wrong, and the ordering it asked for is unreachable there. Verified by reading the spine:

- `reconcile._load_snapshots` is called at `reconcile.py:222`; inside it the binding store is constructed (`:280`), the under-lock staleness gate runs (`:281-282`), `scoped_ids` is computed (`:287`), and the FIRST remote issue fetch happens (`:328-333`).
- `bind_operation_runtime` (the immutable operation/config snapshot) is composed at `:227`, after `_load_snapshots` returns and therefore after that fetch.
- `run_differs()` is invoked at `:231`, also after the fetch; the existing `recover_pending_bindings` call at `run_differs.py:418` already runs post-fetch.

So the invocation goes in `reconcile.py`, after the staleness gate and the `scoped_ids` computation and before the fetch. `run_differs.py` is NOT edited by this task. The real size constraint is `reconcile.py` at 794 of the 800-line cap — SIX lines of headroom, and RP-04 S7.3.a is editing the same file — so the spine gets ONE call line plus a short comment, and no new import.

## Plan
1. Add `BindingRecovery.repair_at_write_boundary(*, persist, scoped)` owning the guard: it returns an empty outcome without any classification or write unless the pass is write-bearing (`persist`) and unscoped (`not scoped`). Expose it through the facade so the spine needs no new import. The unguarded `complete_interrupted_retirements()` from T1 keeps its semantics and stays the direct-test entry point.
2. Call it from `reconcile.py` on one line, positioned after the under-lock staleness validation and before the first remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation.
3. Treat a durable tombstone as authoritative until explicit `unretire`; an automatic 200, `clear_absent`, or same-key confirmation cannot revoke it.
4. On completion failure, preserve the overlap for retry. Because the call precedes the fetch, a failure structurally cannot have made a remote call.

## Testing
- Order tests pin the call between the staleness gate and the first fetch, and assert zero provider calls when completion aborts.
- A read-only table drives construction, load, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered paths and asserts zero repository writes attributable to this operation.
- Guard tests exercise `repair_at_write_boundary` directly across the persist/scoped matrix and prove the non-write-bearing cases do no classification at all.
- AC5 and AC6 are verified at the PASS level in `test_recovery_write_boundary.py`, not only at the owner level: one test drives a write-bearing pass over a historical overlap whose live record was reconfirmed to the same key and cleared of absence, and asserts the tombstone still completes and survives; a second lifts the tombstone with an explicit `unretire` first and asserts the pass leaves the live binding alone. The owner-level twins already exist from T1 in `state/test_binding_recovery.py` (`test_a_same_key_confirm_does_not_revoke_the_tombstone`, `test_clear_absent_does_not_revoke_the_tombstone`, `test_an_explicit_unretire_removes_the_completion_candidate`); the pass-level pair proves the guarded entry point does not lose that behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A live write-bearing unscoped pass completes exact recovery after the under-lock staleness gate.
- [x] That completion happens before the pass's first remote issue observation.
- [x] Construction, load, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered paths perform zero writes from this operation.
- [x] A completion failure performs zero remote calls and preserves the overlap as recoverable evidence.
- [x] An automatic success, absence reset, or same-key confirmation does not override the tombstone.
- [x] Explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone and therefore removes the completion candidate.
- [x] `run_differs.py` is unmodified and the pre-existing create-recovery gate is unchanged.

## Out of scope
Rich-emission caller cutover, ADR finalization, and any change to the pre-existing create-recovery gate (its no-write-pass remote-write defect is filed separately as `easygoing-tremendous-frogmouth`).
baseline.summary: RP-02 S3 T2 — Invoke recovery only at the validated write boundary

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Parity sibling of ec1e-be67-8774-4eef (staged-index store-read-failure race).

The primary fix (Gerrit change 2118, commit 1c5d997487d) made `generation.sign_manifest` RETRY a transient `store-read-failure` from its pre-lock generation-baseline reads instead of aborting terminally, so a peer session's in-flight `git add` -> `git commit` staged index no longer blocks signing.

The `sign-review` recovery path (`resign_plan_review` in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py, the baseline collect at ~:179) establishes its OWN generation baseline with a single `generation.collect(..., ignore_untracked=True)` wrapped in a broad `except Exception` that returns the terminal refusal "plan review generation could not be collected: <exc>". A concurrent writer's staged index makes that collect() raise store-read-failure, so `sign-review` — the very command meant to recover a PASS-but-unsigned verdict under exactly these conditions — fails the same concurrency race, with no retry.

(resign's SUBSEQUENT signing step, attest.sign_plan_review -> generation.sign_manifest at resign.py:349, already inherits the primary retry fix; only the pre-signing collect is exposed.)

## Approach

Mirror change 2118's retry pattern EXACTLY around resign's baseline collect: extract the collect into a helper that loops `generation.MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS` times, catches `PlanRelationSnapshotError`, and on `reason == "store-read-failure"` logs a retry event and sleeps a jittered per-attempt backoff (`random.uniform(0, generation.STORE_READ_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS * attempt)`) before the next attempt — the same bounded attempts / backoff / classification as `sign_manifest`'s loop. Deterministic `PlanRelationSnapshotError` reasons (missing/ambiguous/malformed/reducer/ id-mismatch) and any other exception stay terminal via the existing structured refusal ("plan review generation could not be collected: <exc>") — resign remains a no-throw API. On exhaustion, return a structured refusal that names the transient store-read-failure and tells the caller to retry `rebar sign-review` (retry-after-repair), not the terminal one-shot message. The helper keeps `resign_plan_review`'s cyclomatic complexity flat (complexity-baseline ratchet).

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py — wrap the baseline `generation.collect` in the
  bounded store-read-failure retry helper.
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign_heldout.py (or test_plan_review_resign.py) — RED->GREEN
  tests mirroring tests/unit/test_plan_review_sign_transaction.py's `_raising_head` approach,
  driven through the `resign_plan_review` surface.

## Testing

Unit tests through the resign surface, mirroring test_plan_review_sign_transaction.py:
- transient store-read-failure (fails once, then clears) -> resign proceeds and signs
  (`ok=True, signed=True`) — RED under current code (terminal refusal), GREEN after the fix.
- persistent store-read-failure (never clears) -> exhausts the budget and returns a
  structured `ok=False` refusal whose reason names the transient store-read-failure and
  advises retrying sign-review, after exactly MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS collect attempts.
- deterministic PlanRelationSnapshotError reason (e.g. malformed-reference) -> terminal
  refusal on the FIRST attempt (no retry).
Run: `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign_heldout.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_sign_transaction.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A transient store-read-failure during resign's baseline collect is retried and, once it
      clears, sign-review signs (RED->GREEN unit test through the resign_plan_review surface;
      checked by running the new test against the pre-fix code = RED, post-fix = GREEN).
- [x] A persistent store-read-failure exhausts the retry budget (MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS)
      and surfaces as a structured, retry-after-repair refusal naming store-read-failure —
      not the one-shot terminal "could not be collected" abort (checked by unit test
      asserting the refusal reason and the attempt count).
- [x] Deterministic PlanRelationSnapshotError reasons (missing/ambiguous/malformed/reducer/
      id-mismatch) remain terminal on the first attempt (checked by unit test).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (new=0 increased=0) pass.
baseline.summary: sign-review baseline collect aborts on transient store-read-failure (parity sibling)

## Context / Problem

The `scanner-integration (pinned Semgrep + Gitleaks on the patchset)` job, added to `main` in `6125c5345f01` (Gerrit 2595, ticket aa9e), casts `Verified -1` on effectively every change pushed since it merged, blocking all merges.

**Root fault (Defect 1), quoted from a real job log** (branch-head lane, run 33834183836 job 100903189596, a tree that carries the scanner script):

```
review scanner locks: OK
/bin/sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail
make: *** [Makefile: scanner-integration] Error 2
```

The `scanner-integration` recipe opens with `@set -euo pipefail;`. The Makefile sets no `SHELL`, so GNU make runs the recipe under `/bin/sh` — dash on ubuntu-latest, which has no `pipefail`. `set -o pipefail` is a dash **runtime** error at the `set` builtin (NOT a parse error — `dash -n` does not validate `set` option arguments). The recipe body contains no pipeline, so `pipefail` is inert.

**Exact location (current tree, rebased on Gerrit 2600, which shifted Makefile line numbers):** the `scanner-integration` recipe header is at **Makefile:499** and the offending `@set -euo pipefail;` is at **Makefile:500**. (The quoted log's `Makefile:475` reflects the pre-2600 revision; the line has since moved to 500.)

**How it landed broken.** 2595's own Verified run 33831682168 contains 26 jobs and NO `scanner-integration` job at all: the Verified lane runs `gerrit-verify.yaml` from trusted `main`, which did not yet wire the lane, so 2595's `+1` was cast without the new job ever executing.

## Approach

Replace `set -euo pipefail` with POSIX `set -eu` in the `scanner-integration` recipe (Makefile:500). The recipe has no pipeline, so this is behaviour-preserving under bash and correct under dash. It is a one-line change and introduces no new script, config key, env var, feature flag, or lock, so the mechanism-delta ratchet sees nothing new.

Stacked on Gerrit 2600 so this change's OWN Verified run exercises the (now-fixed) `scanner-integration` job on a tree that carries the scanner script — so, unlike 2595, this change is validated by the very job it repairs.

## Scope

- `Makefile` — the `scanner-integration` recipe's `set` line (Makefile:500) only.

## Deferred to follow-up b973-b298-9b5d-4765 (discovered_from this ticket)

Intentionally OUT of scope for this incident fix:
- Defect 2: `_scanner-integration.yml` lacks the `[ -f scripts/install_review_scanners.py ]`
  predates-gate guard, so a change based before `6125c534` fails `No such file` until rebased.
- The vacuous-vote escape closure: derive `test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`'s guarded set from
  the `gerrit-verify.yaml`/`test.yml` local-`uses:` closure, plus a STATIC bash-only-construct scan
  over CI-reachable make recipes (a parse-only `dash -n` check does not catch `set -o pipefail`).

## Testing

- Defect-seeded RED/GREEN (executable, portable, no CI provider required): `sh -c 'set -euo pipefail'`
  exits nonzero with `Illegal option -o pipefail` — the exact production failure — while
  `sh -c 'set -eu'` exits 0. Verified locally under dash. (Executing the leading `set` line under
  dash is a valid detection oracle; a parse-only check is not.)
- No-pipeline check: the recipe body (Makefile:500-506) contains no `|`, confirming `pipefail` was
  inert and the change is behaviour-preserving.
- Integration proof: this change's own `scanner-integration` Verified job reaches `+1` (green),
  where it was `-1` on every change before the fix.
- Verification set: `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `scanner-integration` recipe at Makefile:500 reads `@set -eu;` (was `@set -euo pipefail;`);
      the citation matches the actual recipe location (header Makefile:499). Checked by reading the diff.
- [ ] Defect-seeded RED/GREEN recorded: `sh -c 'set -euo pipefail'` fails with `Illegal option -o
      pipefail` and `sh -c 'set -eu'` succeeds. Checked by the quoted shell output in a ticket comment.
- [ ] The `scanner-integration` Verified job passes on this change (was red on every change since
      `6125c534`). Checked by this change reaching `Verified +1` with the `scanner-integration` job green.
- [ ] No new mechanism is introduced (no script/config/env/flag/lock). Checked by the mechanism-delta
      ratchet staying green in `make lint`.
- [ ] The two deferred hardening items are captured in linked follow-up b973-b298-9b5d-4765. Checked
      by the `discovered_from` link.
baseline.summary: scanner-integration job fails on every change since it merged, blocking all merges: passed its own CI then broke everyone else's (trusted-main asymmetry)

Discovered by the plan-review gate while re-reviewing mirror F3 (contiguous-industrial-dugong), which consolidated the claim-time plan-review exemption into rebar.types.PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES.

## Problem

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:108 carries a hardcoded tuple:

    if pctx.ticket_type in ("session_log", "code_review", "identity"):

It short-circuits those types to a bare exempt PASS with no review run. The module imports nothing from rebar.types — verified by grep, no EXEMPT reference at all — so this is a seventh spelling list of the ticket-type vocabulary that nothing pins.

## Why F3 did not cover it, and why this is still a mirror

It is NOT a duplicate of PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES. That set is {bug, session_log, code_review, identity}; this one is the same set MINUS bug, because a bug no longer short-circuits — since epic 6982/R4 it gets a LIGHT ADVISORY review (DET floor + necessity probe). So the two answer different questions: "is this type exempt from the claim gate?" versus "does this type skip review entirely?". F3 correctly consolidated the first and left the second alone.

It is still a mirror worth closing: the three spellings must be TicketType members and nothing enforces it, so renaming code_review silently turns its short-circuit off and the type would start getting a full review with nothing failing — the same failure shape as the other mirrors in this epic.

## Approach — derive the subset

Name the bare-exempt set in rebar.types, derived from PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES rather than re-listed (it is the exempt set minus the types that take the bug review tier), and have workflow_ops consume it. Deriving is what keeps the two sets from drifting apart independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: workflow_ops.py:108 consumes a derived constant; no ticket-type spelling remains in that module. Verified by a test and by grep for the literals.
- [x] AC2: membership is UNCHANGED — exactly session_log, code_review and identity short-circuit, and a bug still takes the light advisory tier rather than a bare exempt PASS. Verified by a test pinning both.
- [x] AC3: every member of the derived set is a TicketType member. Verified by a test asserting the subset relation against get_args(TicketType).
- [x] AC4: the derived set stays consistent with PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES. Verified by a test asserting the intended relation between them, so adding an exempt type forces a decision about the short-circuit rather than silently diverging.

## Testing

- python -m pytest tests/unit -k "plan_review or workflow_ops or exempt" -q — AC1-AC4.
- make lint && make typecheck.
baseline.summary: Derive the bare-exempt short-circuit set in workflow_ops
