# Make the GENERATED doc/config surfaces self-identifying, so plans stop citing derived files

## Context / Problem

Story 316a (`common-middle-yearling`) needed FOUR CI iterations to land, and three of the four failures had the same root cause: the plan cited a **derived** file by line number, so the implementer edited the generated artifact instead of its source, and a drift gate failed.

Each wrong edit burns a full CI round-trip (10+ minutes of runner time plus a `Verified -1`), and the drift gates run early in the pytest job's pre-suite sequence, so a single stale derived file masks every gate behind it and the suite never runs.

## Current state (re-surveyed; supersedes this ticket's original survey)

A full sweep of `scripts/gen_*.py`, the `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` gate sequence, and the in-package regenerators found **nine** derived/parity-gated surfaces, not four. Since this ticket was filed, five of them have grown banners:

**Already self-identifying (no change needed, verified against `origin/main`):**

| File | Regenerate | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/cli-reference.md` | `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` | CLI-reference drift gate |
| `docs/env-vars.md` | `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` | Env-var registry drift gate |
| `docs/mcp-reference.md` | `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` | MCP-reference drift gate |
| `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` | `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` | Criteria-routing parity gate |
| `src/rebar/types.py` | `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` | Public-types drift gate |

**NOT self-identifying — the remaining gap:**

1. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` — derived from the packaged prompt front-matter;
   `python -m rebar.llm.prompting.prompts regenerate-index`. Gate: "Prompt-index drift gate".
   JSON, so it carries no banner and nothing in it says it is derived.
2. `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — derived digests of every criterion cited by the
   `src/rebar/_guides/*.md` prose guides;
   `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.guide_parity regenerate`. Gate: folded into the
   Criteria-routing parity gate (`registry validate-routing`). Same JSON blind spot.

**Adjacent surfaces that must be DOCUMENTED but must NOT get a "generated" banner** (banner-ing them would be actively wrong — they are hand-authored):

3. `server.json` — hand-authored EXCEPT its `packages[0].environmentVariables` block, which is a
   parity-checked mirror of `rebar.mcp_server.MCP_ENV_VARS`
   (`python scripts/check_server_manifest.py`).
4. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — hand-authored judgement
   (thresholds/`applies_at`), parity-gated against the canonical criteria vocabulary.
5. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md` — hand-authored prompt BODIES whose front-matter must be a
   FIXED POINT of `write_front_matter()` (`write(*split_raw(f)) == f`). Semantically-correct YAML
   wrapped by hand still fails
   `tests/unit/test_prompt_front_matter.py::test_built_in_prompt_round_trips_canonically`.

The second failure mode is that there is **no one place** that lists these surfaces, so an author must already know which of nine files is derived in order to look it up.

## Approach

Additive and behaviour-neutral throughout: no generator changes what it derives, and no drift gate changes how it compares.

**1. Make the two unmarked JSON files say so.** JSON has no comment syntax, so each gains a top-level `"_generated_by"` string naming its regenerate command — mirroring the wording of the markdown banners already in the tree. The marker must be a **fixed point**: it is emitted by the generator itself, so regeneration reproduces it byte-for-byte and the drift gate stays green.

- `index.json`: add a `build_index_document()` wrapper that returns
  `{"_generated_by": …, **build_prompt_index()}`; `regenerate_prompt_index` serializes the
  wrapper. `build_prompt_index()` stays pure so its invariant tests are untouched.
  `load_catalog()` skips `_`-prefixed keys so the reserved key never becomes a phantom reviewer.
  This mirrors the existing `compute_pins` (pure core) / `build_guide_pins` (document) split in
  `guide_parity.py`.

  **Two EXISTING tests assert `on_disk == build_prompt_index()` and therefore MUST be updated** —
  they compare the committed file (which will carry the marker) against the pure builder (which
  will not). Both are re-pointed at `build_index_document()`, the marker-bearing serialized shape
  that the file is actually generated from:

  - `tests/unit/test_prompt_index.py::test_index_on_disk_matches_regenerated`
    (`built = prompts.build_prompt_index()` → `prompts.build_index_document()`).
  - `tests/unit/test_prompt_library_writes.py::test_user_write_does_not_change_committed_index`
    (both `assert prompts.build_prompt_index() == committed` assertions → `build_index_document()`).

  Worked example of the expected post-change behaviour. Before: `index.json` is
  `{"code-quality": {...}, "ticket-quality": {...}}` and `build_prompt_index()` returns the same
  dict, so `on_disk == built`. After: `index.json` is
  `{"_generated_by": "python -m rebar.llm.prompting.prompts regenerate-index", "code-quality":
  {...}, "ticket-quality": {...}}`; `build_prompt_index()` still returns the marker-less dict
  (unchanged, so `test_index_rejects_two_defaults` / `test_index_retires_removed_prompt` /
  `test_index_rejects_dimension_collision` stay green untouched), while
  `build_index_document()` returns the marker-bearing dict — so the two re-pointed assertions
  read `on_disk == build_index_document()` and pass. `load_catalog()` returns the SAME reviewer
  set as before (the `_`-prefixed key is skipped), so every catalog consumer is unaffected.
- `criterion-pins.json`: the marker is added in `build_guide_pins()`, leaving the pure
  `compute_pins()` untouched. `diff_pins()` reads only `schema_version` and `guides`, so an extra
  top-level key is inert.

**2. Make the docs say so.** Add a "Generated artifacts" section to `docs/README.md`: one table with a row per surface giving the file, its SOURCE, its regenerate command, and the enforcing CI gate — including the three hand-authored-but-gated surfaces, explicitly flagged as such so nobody banners them by mistake. Point `CONTRIBUTING.md` at it from the commit checklist.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — new `build_index_document`, `regenerate_prompt_index`
  serializes it, `load_catalog` underscore guard.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/guide_parity.py` — marker in `build_guide_pins` (pure `compute_pins`
  untouched, so its idempotency test needs no edit).
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` and `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — the two
  regenerated outputs.
- `tests/unit/test_prompt_index.py` — EXISTING; `test_index_on_disk_matches_regenerated` compares
  against `build_index_document()`.
- `tests/unit/test_prompt_library_writes.py` — EXISTING;
  `test_user_write_does_not_change_committed_index`'s two equality assertions likewise.
- `docs/README.md` — the new table. `CONTRIBUTING.md` — one pointer line.
- `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` — new.

## Testing

- A new unit test that (a) parses the `docs/README.md` table, (b) asserts its row set exactly
  matches a canonical in-test registry of derived surfaces — so a surface added without a table
  row fails, which is the staleness this ticket fixes one level up — and (c) asserts each
  generated row's file carries its marker.
- Fixed-point tests for both JSON markers: regenerate in-process and assert the marker survives
  byte-identically (a stripped marker would fail the drift gate, which is worse than no marker).
- A `load_catalog()` test proving the reserved `_generated_by` key does not become a reviewer.
- Re-run the pytest job's whole pre-suite gate sequence (prompt-index, env-registry,
  CLI-reference, MCP-reference, docs-index, criteria-routing, server.json, public-types) and
  confirm every one stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` carries a top-level `_generated_by` naming its
      regenerate command; verified by reading the file and by the Prompt-index drift gate staying
      green after a regeneration.
- [x] `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` likewise; verified the same way against
      `registry validate-routing`.
- [x] Both markers are FIXED POINTS — running each generator leaves the committed file unchanged;
      verified by running the generator and seeing an empty `git diff`.
- [x] `load_catalog()` ignores the reserved key — the catalog is unchanged in size and content;
      verified by the existing prompt/catalog suites staying green plus a new explicit case.
- [x] `docs/README.md` contains a table with one row per derived surface giving source,
      regenerate command, and enforcing CI gate, and flags the hand-authored-but-gated surfaces as
      NOT to be bannered; verified by reading it and by the new test.
- [x] A test fails if the table omits a known derived surface or if a listed generated file lacks
      its marker; verified by deleting a row locally and seeing the test go red.
- [x] Every existing drift/parity gate still passes; verified by running the pre-suite gate
      sequence locally.
- [x] The two existing on-disk-equality tests still pass, re-pointed at `build_index_document()`,
      and `build_prompt_index()`'s own invariant tests (two-defaults, dimension-collision, retire)
      pass UNCHANGED; verified by running `pytest tests/unit/test_prompt_index.py
      tests/unit/test_prompt_library_writes.py`.
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s commit checklist links to the `docs/README.md` "Generated artifacts"
      section; verified by reading the file.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Mark the generated doc/config surfaces as generated

baseline.description:
# Make Serena the default path for source-code reference lookup (structural, not exhortative)

## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` §"Navigating the codebase" already says, explicitly: "**Prefer its symbol tools over `grep`** when finding or following references". During the S2 story of epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` an agent (Claude Code, with Serena configured and healthy) enumerated call sites **by hand with `grep`** across several turns and never invoked Serena until challenged by the operator. The guidance was present, explicit, and ineffective.

**Making it more forceful or more verbose is not a candidate fix** — the failure was not insufficient emphasis. Four concrete mechanisms caused it, and each needs a structural answer:

1. **Friction asymmetry.** Bash was already in-hand for `rebar`/`pytest` calls. Serena's symbol tools were
   *deferred* — using them cost an extra `ToolSearch` round-trip to load their schemas. grep cost zero extra
   steps. Under that gradient the cheap tool wins regardless of documentation.
2. **Launch-time decay.** `AGENTS.md` loads once at session start. Six review passes into a story, one line of a
   long document has no salience against what is in working memory.
3. **No trigger, no feedback.** "Prefer symbol tools" is a standing disposition, not a rule bound to a moment,
   and nothing detects a violation.
4. **The rule as written is incorrect in an important case, which is corrosive.** Serena/Pyright **cannot**
   resolve a symbol referenced as a *string literal*. Verified in this repo: `find_referencing_symbols` on
   `_anthropic_cache_settings` returned the import and all five real call sites but did **not** return
   `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:90`
   (`monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_anthropic_cache_settings", ...)`). That monkeypatch-string class is
   exactly what broke story S1's pre-flight (the identical pattern for `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`). An
   agent obeying "prefer Serena" *exclusively* would have missed the site that actually failed CI. A rule that
   is wrong some of the time teaches agents to discount it all of the time.

Also observed: Serena's index can lag edits. It reported the cache gate at `runner.py:336` and `test_structured.py:175` while the current tree had `:341` and `:176` (a prior commit in the same session had rewritten 79 lines of `runner.py`). And grep produced *false positives* Serena did not: two `output_mode()` mentions in **comments** (`runner.py:78`, `:160`).

Net: the two tools fail in opposite directions and neither alone is sufficient. The guidance must encode the division of labour, and the workflow must make the good default cheap.

## Approach

Three independent, individually-shippable changes. None of them is "reword the guidance more strongly".

1. **Re-surface the tool at the moment of the action** — a `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash` that prints a short
   reminder on **every** `grep` invocation. The trigger is deliberately kept as dumb as possible (does the
   command contain a grep-family invocation) rather than trying to classify "is this pattern a symbol?", because
   a clever predicate is fragile and a fragile hook gets disabled. The message must be **small** (a couple of
   lines, low context cost) and its job is only to re-surface that Serena exists and is preferred for source
   references — plus the one legitimate grep case, so the reminder is never wrong.
2. **Coach it in-band when it is actually missed** — a **project-only** criterion + coaching move so that when a
   review finds source-code references were enumerated by hand (or incompletely), the agent is directed to
   re-derive them with Serena. rebar already has the wiring for project-specific criteria and moves
   (`.rebar/criteria_routing.json` + `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json`); this story either uses it as-is or
   completes it where it turns out to be missing. Either outcome **dogfoods** the project-overlay feature.
3. **Remove the friction asymmetry** — make the Serena symbol tools non-deferred for sessions in this repo so
   using them costs no discovery step, deleting mechanism (1) above.

Nothing here forbids `grep`. The aim is to flip the default and keep the exception honest.

## Scope

- `.claude/settings.json` (or the repo's hook config) — the `PreToolUse` Bash hook + its message.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — a new `project.*` criterion, routed via the `activate` map.
- `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json` — the matching coaching move (`name` / `template` / `applies_when`), plus
  whatever is needed if code-review moves are not yet overlay-driven.
- `AGENTS.md` §"Navigating the codebase" — replace "prefer symbol tools over grep" with the corrected
  division-of-labour table (see AC3); this is a **correctness** fix to the rule, not an emphasis change.
- `docs/` — a short note on the LSP blind spot and the stale-index caveat, if a doc home already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running any `grep`/`rg` through Bash in this repo surfaces a reminder naming Serena's symbol tools; the
      trigger is a simple grep-family match (no pattern/AST classification), proven by an AUTOMATED TEST that
      executes the hook on a plain `grep -rn foo src/` (a session transcript is corroboration, never the sole
      evidence — it is ephemeral and not re-checkable by a reviewer or by CI)
- [ ] The reminder is at most ~3 lines and names BOTH the preferred path (`find_referencing_symbols`) and the
      legitimate grep exception (symbols referenced as string literals), so it is never misleading
- [ ] The hook is **non-blocking** — it never prevents a `grep` from running, and a false-positive reminder
      costs only the message
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` states the division of labour, not a bare preference: (a) who calls/imports a symbol ->
      Serena `find_referencing_symbols`; (b) symbol referenced as a **string** (`monkeypatch.setattr`,
      `getattr`, `importlib`) -> grep, because the LSP cannot resolve it; (c) line numbers after recent edits ->
      grep on the current tree, because the LSP index can lag
- [ ] A project-only criterion + coaching move exists such that a review finding "source-code references were
      enumerated by hand / incompletely" emits a move directing re-derivation via Serena; demonstrated by a
      real `rebar review-plan` run. **Amended by operator decision** (see story `84c7` and the committed run
      log): the move's APPEARANCE in a run's output is not achievable through the overlay — the overlay controls
      move applicability, the coach LLM controls selection, and the same incomplete-inventory evidence also fires
      the blocking built-ins `G1G2`/`G6`/`E4`, which Pass-4 coaches first. What is required and met: the
      criterion FIRES on a real hand-enumerated plan at validity 1.0 (naming the string-literal site the LSP
      cannot resolve), the move is proven APPLICABLE for its trigger set and silent otherwise, and the selection
      limitation is documented. The run log MUST be committed
      (`docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md`) so the evidence is repo-verifiable by a reviewer;
      the ticket comment is a convenience copy, not the artifact of record
- [ ] The criterion is scoped to THIS project via the `.rebar/` overlay only, proven by an AUTOMATED TEST
      asserting the new criterion id appears nowhere under `src/rebar/` — so it rides the project overlay and
      does not change the shipped default criteria set for other clients
- [ ] Serena's symbol tools require no `ToolSearch` discovery step in this repo: a TRACKED
      `.claude/settings.json` sets the one lever that exists (`env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` — all-or-nothing; there is
      no per-tool control), pinned by an automated test. Because project settings resolve to the operator's MAIN
      checkout and not to a worktree, the fresh-session transcript calling `find_referencing_symbols` as the
      first tool use is recorded on story C as a POST-LAND confirmation, not a pre-land gate
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite (`make test`) pass

## Notes

The originating evidence lives on epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76`'s session log (`535c-cfa2-f06d-4b07`), including the verified Serena-vs-grep comparison on `output_mode` and `_anthropic_cache_settings`. Sample size is one session: mechanisms (1) and (4) are directly evidenced there; the relative ranking of the three fixes is judgement, so prefer shipping them independently and observing which actually changes behaviour.

## Execution ordering (added during execution)

Two children write the same file, so the order is fixed by `blocks` links rather than left to chance:

- **C (`06ae`) first** — it creates the tracked `.claude/settings.json` AND the `.gitignore` negation that lets
  that one file be tracked while the rest of `.claude/` (operator-local `settings.local.json`, `scratch/`,
  `worktrees/`) stays ignored. Without that negation neither C's setting nor A's hook can be committed at all.
- **A (`4143`) after C and after D** — A only adds a `hooks` block to the file C created; and D corrects the
  `AGENTS.md` rule first so A's reminder text cannot contradict it (the pre-existing D-blocks-A edge).
- Final order: **C -> D -> A -> B**.

# S5 — Bound writable container layers and alarm on exited-container debris

## Why
Writable container layers can accumulate independently from BuildKit cache and image layers. Without a distinct cap/metric, exited-container debris can consume root while the operator only sees generic root pressure.

## What
Bound writable container layer growth. Prefer a Docker/runtime-supported storage quota when compatible with current overlay2/root filesystem; otherwise install a bounded periodic reaper for exited containers using Docker APIs such as `docker container prune --filter until=...`. Add observability for writable/exited-container footprint and a dedicated CloudWatch alarm at/near cap.

## Scope
In scope: runtime quota or stopped-container reaper, safety checks for live compose services and persistent volumes, metric emission, Terraform alarm, runbook updates, and tests. Out of scope: direct `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` deletion, BuildKit cache cap, journald, `/var/tmp`, and review scratch volume.

## Grounding
- Docker overlay2 docs describe writable container layers as the container `upperdir`/`diff` under `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` and warn Docker owns `/var/lib/docker`.
- Docker CLI docs support `docker container prune --filter until=...` for stopped containers.
- Compose services use persistent named/bind volumes for source-of-truth state, so stopped-container cleanup can be safe when scoped through Docker APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Writable container layer accumulation has an enforced bound or documented runtime quota; stopped-container cleanup is bounded and safe.
- [ ] Running containers, persistent named/bind volumes, and rollback images are not removed by the reaper.
- [ ] Observability emits writable/exited-container layer usage/cap metrics and Terraform declares a dedicated alarm wired to SNS.
- [ ] Runbook explains diagnosis/remediation and forbids manual overlay2 deletion.
- [ ] Targeted tests cover prune command construction/safety, metric emission, and alarm wiring.
- [ ] Portability criterion: solution uses Docker runtime APIs and local tests; no CI-provider-specific dependency is introduced.
baseline.summary: S5 — Bound writable container layers and alarm on exited-container debris

## The defect

Bug `2c4b-3cd9-8bb0-4493` (velvet-prebeloved-discus) proved a defect class: a function whose DEFAULT ARGUMENT is a name imported at module level freezes that binding at import time, so a test that patches the symbol on its DEFINING module only reaches the consumer when the consumer happens not to have been imported yet. Ticket `5ea3-76e5-480a-4464` already ruled this construct a defect and established the remedy — a named call-time indirection (`_retry_sleep`, and `acli_subprocess._backoff_sleep`) — documented in the `_retry_sleep` docstring at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py:44-58`.

A construct sweep run during `2c4b` found the 5ea3 remediation did NOT convert every site. These are LATENT (no test trips them today because every current call site injects the dependency explicitly), so they are filed rather than fixed inside a bug fix's authorisation:

* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:558` — `steal(..., sleep_fn=time.sleep)`
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:161` — `steal_pass_lock(..., sleep_fn=time.sleep)`
* `src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/_jscpd.py:18` — `run: Runner = subprocess.run`

Why they matter despite being latent: the suite contains GLOBAL `time.sleep` and `subprocess.run` patches that these frozen defaults would silently escape — notably the repo-isolation guard at `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:184`, whose `fail_sleep` exists to fail loudly if anything sleeps. A real sleep reached through a frozen default slips past it. The moment any caller stops injecting explicitly, each becomes the `2c4b` bug again.

Out of scope for `2c4b`: that bug fix is authorised to restore the invariant at the seam it proved (`access_check.py`), not to refactor three unrelated modules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Each of the three sites resolves its dependency at CALL time, mirroring the established
      `_retry_sleep` / `_backoff_sleep` indirection, with production behaviour byte-identical.
- [x] An explicitly passed `sleep_fn=` / `run=` still wins over the seam.
- [x] A test proves the seam is reachable: patch the symbol on its defining module AFTER the
      consumer module is resident in `sys.modules`, and observe the patch take effect.
- [x] No new dependency, no behaviour widening, no weakened test.
baseline.summary: Three call-time-seam sites missed by the 5ea3 frozen-default remediation

## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py::test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count` fails intermittently under CI's `-n 3 --dist worksteal` invocation (it -1'd Gerrit 1715 and 1716 in one hour, on both macOS and ubuntu shards) and passes 10/10 in isolation. The assertion wants the SUMMARY line `declined 1 inbound link removal`; `caplog` holds only the PER-ITEM line `declining the inbound removal of ...`.

**Root cause (reproduced deterministically, not a hypothesis).** The two lines differ in LEVEL, not in code path: the per-item decline is `logger.warning` in `apply_inbound_records._inbound_unlink_one`, the pass summary is `logger.info` at the end of `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links`. Both fire; only the INFO one can be dropped. Both use `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` = `rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records`.

`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:606` calls `install_stderr_handler("rebar_reconciler")`, and `rebar/_logging.py:88` does `logger.setLevel(level)` — pinning the shared **`rebar_reconciler`** root logger to WARNING, process-globally and never restored. Any test that drives the reconciler entrypoint in-process (e.g. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py`) leaks that level to every later test in the same xdist worker. `caplog.at_level(logging.INFO)` with no `logger=` argument raises the **ROOT** level only, so the INFO record is discarded at the originating logger by `isEnabledFor` before any handler is consulted — while the WARNING record still arrives. That is exactly the observed asymmetry.

The repo already documents this precise vector and already contains containment for it — `tests/_log_integrity.py` (`restore_level`) plus the autouse `_rebar_log_propagation_guard` in `tests/conftest.py` — but both are hard-coded to the single root `REBAR_LOGGER_NAME = "rebar"`. `rebar/_logging.py`'s own docstring names **two** shared roots ("the sibling `rebar_reconciler` root for the reconciler subprocess"). The guard simply misses the sibling, so reconciler-side INFO assertions are unprotected.

Confirmed RED locally, first try, deterministic: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -p no:randomly` => 1 failed, 15 passed, with the exact CI assertion text.

This is a TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE defect, not a production one: when the confirmation store is `None` the removal is not declined at all (it proceeds), so `declined == 0` and a suppressed summary is correct-by-design. No production logging change is warranted.

## Approach

Generalise the existing caplog coverage-integrity guard from one shared root to the set of shared roots, rather than papering over the symptom with a `logger=` argument on the one assertion. The mechanism is process-global and generic — every `rebar_reconciler.*` INFO/DEBUG assertion in the suite is exposed to it — so containment at the guard is the fix that closes the class; a per-test tweak would leave the next such assertion to flake.

In `tests/_log_integrity.py`, replace the scalar `REBAR_LOGGER_NAME` with `SHARED_LOGGER_NAMES = ("rebar", "rebar_reconciler")` and make the four primitives operate over that tuple: `propagation_failure` reports the first non-propagating root by name, `restore_propagation` re-enables all of them, `current_level` returns a `dict[str, int]` snapshot, and `restore_level` takes that snapshot and reports whether any root moved. The `tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture keeps its exact shape (snapshot at setup, restore in `finally`); only the value it carries becomes a mapping. Rationale for the tuple over per-test opt-in: the leak is caused by legitimate code (a real entrypoint installing its handler), so containment — every test starting from the same level — is what makes log assertions order-independent, which is the property CI needs.

## Scope

- `tests/_log_integrity.py` — multi-root primitives + docstring naming the reconciler root.
- `tests/conftest.py` — the autouse guard carries the per-root level snapshot.
- `tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py` — update the self-tests to the new signature
  and add a pytester pair proving the `rebar_reconciler` root is contained (without the guard
  a leaked reconciler level breaks a later INFO assertion; with it, green).

No `src/` change.

## Testing

- **Failure path first (the reproduction).** Run the polluter module and the flaky module in
  one process with `-p no:randomly`; assert it goes from 1-failed to 0-failed with the fix.
- **Guard self-test, both directions (pytester, in
  `tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py`).** New pair mirroring the existing `rebar`
  level pair, but poisoning `logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler").setLevel(WARNING)` and then
  asserting an INFO record from `rebar_reconciler.probe`: WITHOUT the guard conftest the later
  test FAILS; WITH it, both pass. Worked example of the poisoned file:
  `def test_poisoner(): logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler").setLevel(logging.WARNING)`
  followed by `def test_info(caplog):` doing `with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO):
  logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler.probe").info("hello")` and
  `assert any("hello" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)`.
- **Edge/no-op path.** `restore_level` on an unmoved snapshot returns `False`; a snapshot
  where only one root moved returns `True` and restores just that root.
- **Propagation vector unchanged.** The existing propagation self-tests keep passing, and a
  new case asserts a non-propagating `rebar_reconciler` root is also blamed by name.
- **CI invocation.** The enclosing module plus the reconciler subtree under
  `-n 3 --dist worksteal`, repeated, plus the full CI selection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The order dependency is named and demonstrated: a two-module invocation
      (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_entry.py` then the a4bd module,
      `-p no:randomly`) fails BEFORE the change and passes after — both runs recorded on this
      ticket.
- [x] `tests/_log_integrity.py` exposes `SHARED_LOGGER_NAMES` containing both `"rebar"` and
      `"rebar_reconciler"`, and `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse guard restores the level of both
      — verified by the new pytester self-test pair going red without the guard and green with
      it (`pytest tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py`, all pass).
- [x] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300` passes
      on the change, and the a4bd module passes across 10 consecutive
      `-n 3 --dist worksteal` runs of `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` (run count recorded in a
      ticket comment).
- [x] The `confirm_store is None` question is answered in a ticket comment with the code
      citation: it is correct-by-design (no store => no decline => `declined == 0`), and NOT
      the mechanism behind this flake, so no production logging change is made.
baseline.summary: Inbound decline-count test is order-dependent under xdist

## Target
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — **800 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (0 lines of headroom).

This file is AT the cap. Any edit at all currently fails CI.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

baseline.description:
## Why
ADR 0112 decisions 1+2, the Docker accumulator. At the 2026-09-02 outage `/var/lib/docker` was 17G (overlay2 16G over 67 layer dirs) while `docker system df` claimed ~9.5 GB with ZERO dangling images — ~**6.5 GB of orphaned overlay2 invisible to `docker prune`**. Four prune rounds reclaimed ~1.06 GB against a 29 GB problem: a cap reading Docker's own accounting cannot see the bytes that caused the outage.

## Design

### One budget, three DIFFERENT enforcement strengths
`infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` (new) is the single source of truth for a `/var/lib/docker` budget with an internal split (ADR 0112: "S2 and S5 are one budget, not two" — writable layers live INSIDE overlay2, so two caps are double-counted or mutually violable). Measured env-settable defaults (decision 6): 20 GiB total, 5 GiB of it the BuildKit share (today's `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP=5GB`, promoted to one place instead of duplicated), leaving 15 GiB of image/layer share S5 sub-divides.

1. **BuildKit share (5 GiB) — the daemon's OWN GC**, at the source, on its own schedule:
   `builder.gc` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`. `docker builder prune --keep-storage` applies
   the same cap on demand; a BuildKit-only flag, used for THIS share only.
2. **Image/layer share (15 GiB) — RETENTION, because Docker has no image-store ceiling.**
   No flag caps the image store, so the share is held by the repo's existing rollback-safe
   retention: `docker image prune -f` (dangling) each cycle, plus — only when the MEASURED
   footprint exceeds the share — a bounded sweep of the oldest per-release `compose-mcp:<sha>`
   tags beyond `DOCKER_IMAGE_RETAIN` (default 3) via `docker image rm` WITHOUT `-f`, so the
   daemon refuses while any container references the image and `:prev` plus the serving
   release survive by construction (autodeploy.sh `:554`). Weaker than a hard cap; the alarm
   makes the residual visible.
3. **Orphaned overlay2 — NEITHER.** Docker does not know those bytes exist, so no cap and no
   prune reaches them. ALARM-ONLY, and that is the point. Remediation is a daemon-level
   reclaim: hand-deleting under `/var/lib/docker` desynchronises the daemon's layer metadata
   from the tree, which is why the runbook bans it.

### The daemon.json schema is version-dependent, so it is PROBED
Engine 25.0 / BuildKit 0.13 added `policy[].reservedSpace|maxUsedSpace|minFreeSpace` and deprecated `defaultKeepStorage`/`keepStorage`. A wrong key is silently IGNORED — the cap would simply not exist — so the script reads the engine version (`docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'`, else `dockerd --version` on first boot) and renders what THAT engine honours: `maxUsedSpace` at >= 25.0, `defaultKeepStorage` below. Both are tested through a side-effect-free `--print-json --engine-version <v>` mode. An unreadable version renders the MODERN schema and logs it, and the merge is still validated — worst case "no new cap plus a loud log", never a broken daemon.

### Install point, and how a LIVE daemon picks it up
The merge goes into `compose-up.sh` **ahead of `systemctl enable --now docker`** (today's first side-effecting step, line 55), so a first boot starts the daemon with the cap in place. On a re-run against a LIVE daemon the write alone is inert, so `daemon.json` is BACKED UP and the merged file VALIDATED (`dockerd --validate --config-file`, else a JSON parse); **a failed validation restores the backup and changes nothing** — a malformed `daemon.json` stops `dockerd` starting, a self-inflicted outage on the host being protected. Only a validated CHANGE attempts `systemctl reload docker` (SIGHUP); if that fails the script WARNs naming the runbook step and **does not restart Docker** — a restart takes Gerrit, the review-bot and MCP down, so it stays an operator decision.

### Detecting the bytes `docker system df` cannot see
Two INDEPENDENT measurements of the same bytes: filesystem truth — a bounded `du -sx` over `/var/lib/docker` and one over `.../overlay2` (`-x` does not cross into a mounted `overlay2/*/merged`; one `du` run counts a file hardlinked across layers once) — and Docker's ledger, `docker system df` images + containers + build cache, parsed to bytes. `docker_unaccounted_bytes` is overlay2 truth − ledger, clamped at 0. Divergence is NORMAL: `du` counts allocated blocks including per-layer directory and whiteout overhead, while the ledger reports layer sizes with sharing accounted differently. So the threshold is not "any divergence": 2 GiB, far above that overhead on a 16 GiB tree and far below the 6.5 GB that went unnoticed — a terraform literal an operator retunes.

## Alarms — three, none implying another
1. `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high` — the whole budget saturating.
2. `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` — the BuildKit GENERATOR at its own cap. BuildKit at
   100% of its 5 GiB share is invisible inside a 20 GiB budget reading 60%; a runaway image
   set saturates the budget while BuildKit sits at 10%. The 3e92 argument: alarm on the
   generator, not only aggregate fullness.
3. `rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2` — orphaned bytes above 2 GiB. 1 and 2 say "how full";
   only this says "full of what prune cannot touch", changing remediation from "prune harder"
   (the measured ~1.06 GB failure) to a daemon-level reclaim.

All three: 300/3/2, breaching, `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions` on `aws_sns_topic.alerts`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docker-storage-cap.sh` holds the `/var/lib/docker` budget plus its BuildKit/image
      split in ONE place, measured env-settable defaults; no cap constant is duplicated.
- [ ] The rendered `builder.gc` matches the ENGINE VERSION: `maxUsedSpace` at >= 25.0,
      `defaultKeepStorage` below; both tested.
- [ ] `compose-up.sh` merges ahead of `systemctl enable --now docker`, backing up then
      validating; a failed validation restores the backup, changing nothing.
- [ ] A validated `daemon.json` change on a live daemon reloads Docker, never restarts.
- [ ] `autodeploy.sh` takes its BuildKit `--keep-storage` from the shared budget.
- [ ] Over-share retention sweeps only surplus per-release tags via `docker image rm`
      without `-f`; `:prev` and the serving release survive.
- [ ] `observability.sh` publishes, dimensionless in `rebar/host`, `docker_storage_bytes`,
      `docker_storage_used_percent`, `docker_buildkit_cache_bytes`,
      `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `docker_unaccounted_bytes` (= `du` truth minus
      `docker system df`) — ONLY on a successful measurement, so a failed probe publishes
      nothing and breaching missing-data pages rather than reading as a healthy 0.
- [ ] Terraform declares the three alarms, SNS-wired, breaching, pinned by name;
      `fmt -check` plus `validate` pass.
- [ ] The runbook documents per-generator diagnosis/remediation, the operator restart step
      for a changed `daemon.json`, plus a ban on deletion under `/var/lib/docker`.
- [ ] Portability: host config + local script tests; no CI-provider trigger.

## Testing
RED-first: each test is written and observed FAILING before implementation. pytest runs as `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q <file>`.
- `tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py` — budget/split derivation, per-engine-version
  `builder.gc` rendering, idempotent merge preserving pre-existing keys, backup-restore on a
  rejected config.
- `tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py` — emission over stubbed `docker`/`du`,
  size parsing, the unaccounted delta reproducing the incident's 16G-vs-9.5G shape, silence
  (not 0) on probe failure.
- `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py` — the budget drives `--keep-storage`; the sweep
  spares `:prev` and the serving release.
- `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` — three alarms, actioned, breaching.
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform`; `init -backend=false` + `validate`.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `test_mechanism_delta.py`,
  `test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`, `test_api_surface_gate.py`.
baseline.summary: S2 — Cap Docker overlay2 and BuildKit cache with per-generator alarms

baseline.description:
# S4b — Review-bot receiver logic + LLM-Review voter + backfill (the proven pipe)

## Why
Close the loop: on a new patchset the review-bot receiver reviews the change and casts the
deterministic `LLM-Review` vote. For d251 this proves the PIPE with a real-but-minimal review;
the full four-pass kernel reviewer + the real dogfood is **b744-WS6**, which plugs into this
same seam. Because submit REQUIRES the vote, the gate is **fail-closed**: a missed event, a
dropped vote, or a broken receiver only ever DELAYS review (the change stays unsubmittable) —
it can never let an unreviewed change merge. The receiver is a thin webhook->review->vote
service that IMPORTS the review code as a library (NOT the stdio MCP over HTTP).

## What
- **Receiver behavior (in `src/rebar/review_bot/`, the service stood up in S2).** On
  `POST /review/` from Gerrit's `webhooks` plugin: (1) validate the inbound secret token (and
  that the source is the allowed Gerrit host — the plugin has no HMAC, so this token+ACL is the
  inbound auth, per S4a); (2) **ACK fast (HTTP 202) and enqueue**, then process in a background
  worker. An LLM review takes 30s-minutes and blows Gerrit's webhook socket timeout (~5s) — so
  inline processing would time out and be re-delivered. (3) The worker imports the code reviewer,
  runs the minimal-but-real code review on the change diff, and casts the vote via the OUTBOUND
  Gerrit REST call.
- **The vote.** `POST /a/changes/{id}/revisions/current/review` (auth = the bot's SSM token from
  S4a) with `tag:autogenerated:rebar`, `notify:NONE`, and a `robot_comments` payload. For the
  minimal shim the reviewer may produce no file-anchored findings, so post a single patchset-level
  robot_comment (`path:"/PATCHSET_LEVEL"`, non-empty `message`, `robot_id`/`robot_run_id`/`url`)
  — a bare metadata robot_comment with no `path` is a 400.
- **Code-review verdict -> label mapping (one-way-door contract; record in the ADR).** The
  `LLM-Review` label gates CODE merges, so the verdict comes from the CODE-review path (NOT the
  plan-review gate). For the d251 proven pipe (pre-b744), the receiver invokes the EXISTING
  `rebar.llm.review_code(...)` — the single-pass code reviewer that ships today — on the change
  diff, and maps its outcome to the integer `LLM-Review` value, fail-closed:

  | Code-review outcome | `LLM-Review` value | Effect |
  |---------------------|--------------------|--------|
  | clean / no blocking findings | `+MAX` (submit-enabling) | change becomes submittable |
  | blocking issues found        | `-1`               | change stays unsubmittable |
  | error / no decision          | `-1` (fail-closed) | change stays unsubmittable |

  **b744-WS6 replaces `review_code`'s internals** with the four-pass kernel + a typed
  `code_review_verdict {verdict: PASS|BLOCK, ...}` via `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict`;
  the receiver then maps `PASS` -> `+MAX` and `BLOCK` -> `-1` over the SAME seam. The mapping (and
  the MAX value / label range, owned by d251 `project.config`) is config-driven (env/SSM/config
  under `infra/`), not hardcoded, because b744-WS6 changes the scoring logic.
- **Fail-closed on vote-cast failure.** If the REST POST fails (Gerrit 4xx/5xx, SSM token fetch
  failure, or the code reviewer returns no actionable decision), the change is left NOT submittable
  (no MAX is ever cast on failure); the failure is logged with the change id and trips the alarm.
- **Idempotency / dedup (at-least-once delivery).** Gerrit's `webhooks` plugin retries
  (`maxTries=5`, `retryInterval=1000ms`) — and since the review blows the socket timeout, the
  same event WILL be delivered multiple times. Dedupe by a stable key (change id + revision +
  event type) persisted in a small local SQLite file (or equivalent) on the box's data volume
  (single-box appropriate), keyed by (change id + revision + event type) with a uniqueness guard;
  before voting, check for an existing `LLM-Review` vote on the current revision and skip if present
  (and/or derive `robot_run_id` deterministically). A webhook + a backfill pass for the same
  patchset never double-vote.
- **Backfill reconciler.** `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py` (startup + a configurable cron,
  default 5 min) queries the `events-log` plugin for patchsets whose current revision has NO
  `LLM-Review` vote and re-invokes the SAME voter function — so a dropped webhook is recovered.
  events-log is a store, not an auto-replay; the reconciler is what closes the loop.
- **Observability.** Structured JSON logs (`timestamp, change_id, revision_id, vote_value,
  http_status, error`) + a CloudWatch alarm on a sustained voter error rate (e.g. >=3 failures
  in 5 min -> SNS) so an expired token / down LLM / unreachable receiver surfaces to an operator
  instead of silently stacking unsubmittable changes. Per the locked freeze-and-restore /
  no-break-glass posture, a persistently broken voter leaves `main` frozen until RESTORED (fix
  the receiver/LLM/token) — there is deliberately NO script to disable the submit requirement.

## Scope
In: the receiver's parse/auth-check/ACK/review/vote logic + verdict->label mapping +
fail-closed + dedup/idempotency + the events-log reconciler + observability + the seam ADR.
Out: the full four-pass kernel reviewer + overlays + dogfood (b744-WS6); the bot account +
plugins + inbound-secret config (S4a); the receiver service skeleton + nginx route (S2);
replication (S5). Depends on S4a (bot account, plugins, inbound secret) + S2 (receiver service).

## Files
- `src/rebar/review_bot/` — the receiver handler (auth-check, ACK-202-then-enqueue, background
  worker importing the code reviewer), the verdict->label mapping config, dedup store.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py` — the events-log backfill poller (startup + cron).
- `infra/` — the voter observability alarm (error-rate -> SNS) wiring.
- `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md` — ADR: the seam contract (bot/label/event boundary, dedup
  rule, verdict->integer mapping, robot_comments shape, inbound/outbound auth split) b744-WS6
  must conform to.

> Record `set_file_impact` + `set_verify_commands` (the offline FakeRunner tests below) before claiming.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Async happy path.** On `patchset-created`, the receiver validates the inbound token,
      returns 202 immediately, and a background worker casts an `LLM-Review` vote via REST with a
      structurally valid `robot_comments` payload (`path:"/PATCHSET_LEVEL"`, non-empty message,
      ids), `tag:autogenerated:rebar`, `notify:NONE`.
- [ ] **Vote -> submittability.** A clean code review (no blocking findings) casts `+MAX` and the
      change becomes submittable; blocking issues found, OR an error / no decision, casts `-1` and
      the change is NOT submittable (only MAX enables submit; error/no-decision is fail-closed).
      Pre-b744 the verdict comes from `rebar.llm.review_code`; b744-WS6 maps the typed
      `code_review_verdict` (`PASS`->`+MAX`, `BLOCK`->`-1`). Mapping is the table above and is
      config-driven, not hardcoded.
- [ ] **Vote-cast failure is fail-closed.** A simulated Gerrit 503 / missing token / no-decision
      leaves the change NOT submittable (no MAX on failure), logs the change id, and trips the alarm.
- [ ] **Idempotent vs retries.** A patchset delivered by BOTH a `webhooks` retry and a backfill
      pass yields exactly one `LLM-Review` vote and no duplicate robot_comment threads
      (existing-vote check and/or deterministic `robot_run_id`). Covered by an offline test.
- [ ] **Backfill via reconciler.** With a `patchset-created` webhook deliberately dropped,
      `reconcile.py` (querying events-log for patchsets lacking an `LLM-Review` vote) casts the
      missing vote within one poll interval — no patchset left permanently unreviewed.
- [ ] **Fail-closed invariant.** A missed event NEVER yields a submittable-but-unreviewed change;
      a persistently broken voter only delays review (main freezes until restored — no
      break-glass merge path, per the locked posture).
- [ ] **Seam documented.** `docs/adr/0009-review-bot-pipe.md` records the bot/label/event/auth
      contract and the seam b744-WS6 must conform to.


## Round-7 remediation
- **Decision rule over review_code findings (G6):** `rebar.llm.review_code()` returns a `review_result` (a `findings` list), NOT a verdict string. The receiver derives a binary decision: **BLOCK if any finding is at/above a configured blocking severity (default critical/high), else PASS** -> PASS->label MAX, BLOCK or error/no-result->-1 (fail-closed); the threshold is config-driven. b744-WS6 will ADD a code-review verdict producer to `gate_dispatch` (planned — e.g. `produce_code_review_verdict` returning a typed `code_review_verdict {verdict: PASS|BLOCK, ...}`); it does NOT exist yet (today `gate_dispatch` exports only `produce_plan_review_verdict` / `produce_completion_verdict`), so until b744 lands the pipe uses `review_code`'s findings + the decision rule above.
- [ ] The receiver maps `review_code()`'s `review_result.findings` to a vote via the documented severity-threshold rule (BLOCK if any finding >= threshold else PASS; PASS->MAX, BLOCK/error->-1), verified by an offline test with/without a blocking-severity finding.

## Round-9 remediation
- **Reconciler query mechanism (G6):** `events-log` is an append-only raw event STREAM, not a 'patchsets-lacking-a-vote' store. `reconcile.py` uses events-log ONLY to enumerate `patchset-created` events in the gap window, then for each candidate queries the Gerrit CHANGES REST API (e.g. `GET /a/changes/{id}/revisions/current/votes`, or `q=status:open label:LLM-Review=0`) to confirm it lacks an `LLM-Review` vote before re-invoking the voter. (events-log = what changed; changes API = which lack a vote.)
- **Webhook->diff bridge (G6):** a Gerrit webhook payload carries event metadata, NOT the diff, but `review_code()` needs a git range or explicit `diff_text=`. The receiver bridges by fetching the change diff via Gerrit REST (`GET /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch` (base64) or the files/diff API) and passing it as `diff_text=` to the review adapter.
- [ ] reconcile.py enumerates gap events from events-log THEN confirms missing votes via the changes REST API (not via events-log vote-state); and the receiver fetches the change diff via Gerrit REST and passes it as `diff_text=` to the adapter (offline test covers both).

## Round-10 remediation
- **review_code repo-context (G6):** `review_code()` resolves a gate handle (`gate_source.resolve_gate_handle(ref, source, repo_root)`) even when `diff_text=` is passed, so the receiver must ALSO give it a repo context — fetch the change at its target ref from Gerrit into a shallow checkout (or the attested snapshot) and pass that as `repo_root` (and the ref), not `diff_text` alone. Implementation note: align the exact call with `review_code()`'s current signature at build time (read `src/rebar/llm/code_review.py`); the proven pipe likely fetches+checks out the change ref and lets review_code resolve the diff itself.
- [ ] The receiver invokes `review_code()` with a valid repo context (a fetched checkout/snapshot at the change ref) so `resolve_gate_handle` succeeds — verified against review_code's actual signature.

## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)
- The diff is NEVER in the webhook payload (PROVEN, session_log a7e2 EXPERIMENT 2): the receiver fetches it via `GET /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch` which returns a BASE64-encoded git format-patch — it MUST base64-decode before passing as `diff_text`. (Clarifies the Round-9 AC.)
- The formal d251↔b744 adapter seam is now concrete (epic Round-11): `code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root, ref) -> {decision: PASS|BLOCK}` in `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`; error/no-result/unparseable → BLOCK (fail-closed). S4b implements it over `review_code()`'s findings + the severity-threshold rule; b744-WS6 reimplements the same signature.

Added ACs:
- [ ] Receiver base64-decodes the `/revisions/{rev}/patch` response before passing `diff_text` (offline test on a captured base64 patch)
- [ ] The `code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root, ref)->{decision: PASS|BLOCK}` adapter exists as a named module with the co-located fail-closed error rule; an offline test covers PASS, BLOCK, and error→BLOCK (this is the formal b744-WS6 seam, with a covering AC)
- [ ] The adapter calls `review_code(..., source="local")` (reads the already-cloned change-ref checkout in `repo_root`); a test asserts it does NOT use `attested` mode (which would `git fetch origin` against Gerrit and mis-resolve the change ref).
- [ ] Per-(change_id, revision) SINGLE-FLIGHT lock around the review+vote critical section (not just receipt-time dedup): a concurrent webhook retry while the first review is still running must NOT spawn a second review or cast a conflicting vote (Gerrit Set Review is last-write-wins). Offline test: two concurrent deliveries of the same revision → exactly one review execution + one vote.
- [ ] Reconciler is resumable+idempotent via a persisted cursor (last events-log event id) + per-(change,revision) vote-existence check; fallback if events-log absent/errors → log+alarm+rely on webhook, never submittable-but-unreviewed
- [ ] Adapter return carries `{decision, message, findings}` so the Gerrit vote COMMENT is assembled uniformly across d251's `review_code` and b744's `produce_code_review_verdict`



## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-30)
- **Dedup write semantics = WRITE-ON-SUCCESS (blocking):** the local SQLite "voted" row is written ONLY AFTER a confirmed successful vote cast (HTTP 2xx from Gerrit). A crash between review and a successful vote leaves NO row, so re-delivery (webhook retry or backfill) safely re-reviews — fail-closed, never a missed vote. The AUTHORITATIVE idempotency guard is a Gerrit-side check BEFORE voting (`GET /a/changes/{id}/revisions/current/review` → does the current revision already carry an `LLM-Review` vote from the bot?); the SQLite row is a fast local short-circuit, not the source of truth. So a lost SQLite file degrades to "re-check Gerrit", never a double-vote.
- **SQLite schema (defined):** `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS voted(change_id TEXT NOT NULL, revision TEXT NOT NULL, event_type TEXT, vote_value INTEGER, voted_at INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(change_id, revision));` — uniqueness on (change_id, revision). Opened in WAL mode (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`) for safe concurrent reader/writer. File on the data volume (`/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot/voted.db` or a configured path).
- **Single-flight lock (defined):** an in-process per-(change_id, revision) `asyncio.Lock` (keyed dict) guards the review+vote critical section. The webhook worker AND the backfill reconciler run in the SAME receiver process (the reconciler is an asyncio background task), so they SHARE the lock + the SQLite connection — a retry or a backfill firing mid-review cannot spawn a second concurrent review or a conflicting vote (Gerrit Set-Review is last-write-wins, so the lock + the pre-vote Gerrit check together prevent double/contradictory votes).
- **Voter-error metric pathway (defined):** on each vote failure the receiver increments a CloudWatch custom metric `rebar/host:voter_errors` (Count) directly via boto3 PutMetricData (the container runs under the EC2 instance role, which has cloudwatch:PutMetricData from S1); a `voter_errors` CloudWatch alarm (in `infra/terraform/`, dimensionless to match) fires on >=3 in 5 min. (Fallback also documented: the receiver's structured JSON error logs go to journald, greppable.)
- **events-log query uses the TRAILING SLASH** `GET /a/plugins/events-log/events/` (verified in S4a — without it, 404).
- **Live e2e AC (added):** beyond offline FakeRunner unit tests, a REAL patchset pushed to the rebar project triggers the webhook → the receiver reviews via review_code → casts the LLM-Review vote → the change becomes submittable (verified live on the running Gerrit), with the dedup/single-flight preventing a double vote on webhook retry.

Added/clarified ACs:
- [ ] Dedup is write-on-success + an authoritative pre-vote Gerrit-side existing-vote check; a crash before a successful vote re-reviews on redelivery (no missed vote, no double vote). SQLite schema is (change_id,revision) PK in WAL mode.
- [ ] An in-process per-(change_id,revision) single-flight lock is shared by the webhook worker and the in-process backfill reconciler.
- [ ] On vote failure the receiver publishes `rebar/host:voter_errors` (boto3, instance role) and a dimensionless CloudWatch alarm fires on a sustained error rate.
- [ ] LIVE e2e: a real patchset → webhook → review_code → LLM-Review vote → submittable, verified on the running Gerrit (not only FakeRunner); a duplicate webhook delivery does NOT double-vote.

baseline.description:
Make a stale clone's push **refuse** instead of silently re-unioning ~1 GiB of stripped history. This is the keystone that makes the reclaim safe, and it must be deployed everywhere before the window. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why a guard is needed at all, and why in two places
After the strip, `.bridge_state` still only appears from 2026-06-11, so the first **1,029 commits are byte-identical** and `merge-base HEAD origin/tickets` **SUCCEEDS** (measured). So `sync.py` does NOT take its unrelated-histories branch — it reaches the ordinary **diverged** path (`:100-112`) and unions normally. Quiescence does not close this.

And a guard in `sync.py` alone is **bypassed**: `push.py:203` and `:229` run an INDEPENDENT `git merge <remote>/<branch>` on non-fast-forward rejection and then re-push (<=3 attempts), never consulting `sync.py`. That is exactly the path a stale review-bot write takes. **[v2 CORRECTED — the earlier chain was wrong; plan-review caught it]** Verified chain: `voter.py:735 emit_code_review_artifact(...)` -> (within it) `rebar.create_ticket` -> `event_append.py:561 push.push_tickets_branch(...)` -> push rejected non-FF -> `push.py` merge -> retry **succeeds**. There is **no `push_after_commit` intermediary**: `push_after_commit` (`push.py:268`) is called only from `delete.py:337,397`, `compact.py:644,762` and `transition_close.py:757` — never from the create path. And `voter.py:735` is `emit_code_review_artifact(`, not `create_ticket`.

## Placement (precise — the wrong spot wedges every clone)
- Inside **`sync._union_merge`** (`sync.py:114`) — the sole shared callee of both `:97` and `:111`.
  **NOT** before the merge-base test at `:96`: that would also block the ff-adopt at `:101-104`,
  which is exactly how a merely-behind clone converges, wedging it permanently.
- Before **`push.py:203` and `:229`**.
- **NOT** at `lock.acquire()` (where `check_store_compat` already fires, `lock.py:296`): a blanket
  write block would also block the convergence operation, deadlocking the clone it rejects.

## Where the epoch lives
Add an `epoch` field to the **existing** `.store-compat.json` rather than a parallel marker. Verified safe: `compat.py`'s `_analyze` validates only `format_version` and `required_capabilities` via `.get()`, so **unknown keys are ignored** — an older binary neither crashes nor fails closed. Two precisions: `compat.write_compat_record` (`:184`) hardcodes the two keys, so a store it stamps is born epoch-absent (decide that deliberately); and `_record_path` reads only the **local worktree**, so the guard needs its own `git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json` reader for the other side.

## Expand/contract — the FULL state matrix (plan-review E2/T1 remediation)
The earlier wording said only "`absent == absent` => compatible, `absent vs present` => abort", which left two distinct absences conflated. Specify all of it. Two independent axes per side: the **record** (`.store-compat.json`) may be absent or present, and within a present record the **`epoch` field** may be absent or present.

| local | remote | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| record absent | record absent | **compatible** (pre-feature store both sides; union proceeds) |
| record absent | record present, epoch absent | **compatible** |
| record present, epoch absent | record present, epoch absent | **compatible** (today's state) |
| epoch present | epoch present, equal | **compatible** |
| epoch present | epoch present, different | **ABORT** |
| epoch absent | epoch present | **ABORT** (local predates the rewrite) |
| epoch present | epoch absent | **ABORT** (remote predates local; refuse rather than guess) |
| either side | record present but **corrupt/unparseable** | **ABORT** (never silently treat as absent — mirrors `compat.py`'s existing corrupt-record rule) |
| remote ref unreadable (`git show` non-zero) | — | **ABORT**, distinguished in the message from "file absent" |

Note the last two rows: `git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json` exits non-zero **both** when the file does not exist at that ref and when the ref itself cannot be read. These must be distinguished in the log message, because the remedies differ (re-clone vs fix the remote).

**Epoch value format (plan-review E2 remediation — previously unspecified).** `epoch` is a JSON **string**, opaque to comparison: compared for byte equality only, never ordered or parsed. Value = the ISO-8601 UTC instant of the rewrite plus a short random suffix (e.g. `"2026-08-14T09-31-07Z-4f2a"`), unique per rewrite and human-diagnosable in a log line. A non-string `epoch` (number, object, null) is treated as **corrupt** -> ABORT, matching `compat.py`'s existing type-strictness for `format_version`. Deliberately NOT a monotonic counter: ordering invites "newer is probably fine" reasoning, and the only safe response to any mismatch is refuse-and-re-clone.

The epoch **value** appears only in the reclaim's re-add commit. The epoch **value** appears only in the reclaim's re-add commit. That way pre-window clones (both absent) merge normally even holding unpushed work, while post-rewrite stale clones abort.

**The guard only binds binaries at or after this change** — older ones ignore the field. So the reclaim window additionally requires >=24 h plus an observed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run on a descendant SHA, and the review-bot convergence (A6-0b) stays in the protocol.

## Control flow at each guard site (plan-review G6 remediation)
`logger.warning` describes the *message*, not the *control flow* — and at the `push.py` sites both merges sit inside the `for attempt` retry loop, so warning-and-continuing would simply retry the push. Specify both sites explicitly:

- **`sync._union_merge`**: log and **return without merging**. `reconverge` is best-effort by
  contract (its sole caller `reads.ensure_fresh` swallows everything), so a no-op return is the
  correct degradation — the clone simply stays un-converged instead of unioning.
- **`push.py` (before the merges at the non-FF retry)**: log and **abort the retry loop
  immediately** — specifically **`return` out of `push_tickets_branch`, not `break`** (plan-review G6
  remediation): `break` would fall through to whatever follows the loop and could still report a
  completed push, whereas `return` exits with the push explicitly not-completed. Do not merge, do not
  re-push, do not consume further attempts. The push must
  surface as *not* completed so the existing `PUSH_PENDING` path (which `fsck` reports) is the
  operator-visible signal. Returning "success" would silently drop the local commits from the
  operator's view, and continuing the loop would burn attempts on a merge that must never happen.

## Message channel
`logger.warning`, **not** an exception: every caller of `sync.reconverge` is `reads.ensure_fresh` (`reads.py:255-262`), which wraps it in a bare `except Exception: pass` inside a second bare `except Exception: return`, so a raise is swallowed with **no output**. Visibility comes from the entrypoint handlers (`_cli/__init__.py:408`, `mcp_server.py:688`, `rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:438`), not Python's `lastResort` (`__init__.py:131` attaches a `NullHandler`, so lastResort never fires). Known gap: `sync.push=async` spawns the push with `stdout/stderr=DEVNULL` (`push.py:113-145`), so those clones get no message and rely on `fsck`'s `PUSH_PENDING`.

## Out of scope, declared
`fsck_recover.py` cherry-picks dangling ticket commits with no epoch awareness — it creates new commits rather than unioning a DAG, so blast radius is bounded. Also **not** covered: the CI bash unions at `reconcile-bridge.yml:321` and `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:439`, which are protected by the window protocol (workflows disabled + no in-flight run asserted), not by this guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A clone on a **stale epoch** attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites — asserted separately for `sync._union_merge` and for `push.py`'s non-FF retry.
      Tier: **integration** in two real temporary clones with divergent epochs. This is the RED case.
- [ ] Assert on the emitted **log record** (`caplog`), plus one **subprocess** run with
      `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` proving the message reaches a real operator's stderr.
      `sync.push=async` is excluded by design.
- [ ] At the `push.py` site the retry loop **terminates immediately** on epoch mismatch: exactly
      **zero** merge invocations and **zero** further push attempts, and the push reports
      not-completed so `fsck` surfaces `PUSH_PENDING`. Tier: **unit** with a counting shim on the git
      calls — the guard is a pure predicate plus a control-flow decision, so no real remote is needed;
      the earlier "integration" label contradicted its own unit proving command (plan-review COH).
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py -k push_retry -v`.
- [ ] At the `sync._union_merge` site the function **returns without merging** and the clone is left
      un-converged (not corrupted). Tier: **integration**.
- [ ] A merely-**behind** clone (matching epochs) still converges via ff-adopt, and a
      **strictly-ahead** clone still returns early — neither is blocked. Tier: **integration**. This
      is the negative control that catches the wedge-everything misplacement.
- [ ] **Every row of the state matrix** above is asserted, including the two distinct absences
      (record-absent vs record-present-epoch-absent) and the corrupt-record row. Tier: **unit**,
      table-driven over the matrix — one case per row, so a missing row fails the suite.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py -v`.
- [ ] `git show` failing because the **ref** is unreadable produces a different message than the file
      being **absent** at a readable ref. Tier: **unit** with two fixtures.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py -k remote_read -v`.
- [ ] An older binary reading a record that carries `epoch` does not error and does not fail closed.
      Tier: **unit** against `compat._analyze`.
- [ ] The remote side is read via `git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json`, not the local worktree.
      Tier: **unit** with a fixture where local and remote records differ.

## Files
`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`, `src/rebar/_store/sync.py`, `src/rebar/_store/push.py`, tests

Scope: M. No dependencies; must land and roll out before A6-1.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The live Jira DC harness cell `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py::test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` FAILS on current origin/main:

    AssertionError: binding/snapshot artifacts survived the scrub: ['.bridge_state']

Observed in the 'jira DC harness smoke' job of Live External Integration run 31807853902 (job 94790999602), 2026-08-14, against origin/main. The J11 store-copy fixture scrubs `.bridge_state*` from the copied store, but the artifact survives into the copy the isolation cell asserts is fully scrubbed, muddying the live DC signal for unrelated work.

## Root cause (regression origin)
The `dc_store_copy_repo` fixture (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py`) scrubs `.bridge_state*`, commits, and THEN calls `run_ensures()` to converge the `git archive` copy into a writable store. Commit 72731d3745 (2026-08-13, ticket 462d / epic 0303) added the `projects-seed` ensure unit (`rebar._store.project_ensures.seed_projects_mapping_unit`), which unconditionally re-creates and COMMITS `.bridge_state/projects.json` whenever its tree-check (`git show tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json`) misses — which is exactly the state the scrub leaves. That seed unit post-dates the J11 scrub (2026-08-07), so converging the copy silently resurrects the cache the scrub had removed. Before epic 0303, `run_ensures` created nothing under `.bridge_state`, so the scrub held.

## Approach
Extract the scrub into a small module-level helper `scrub_bridge_state(tracker, *, commit=False)` in `_dc_fixtures.py` (glob-matched, as before). Call it in the original position, and AGAIN after `run_ensures` converges the store — this second pass commits the removal so the `projects-seed` unit's resurrected `.bridge_state/projects.json` is removed from both the worktree and the tickets tree. This is a principled fix (re-scrub the whole `.bridge_state*` glob after convergence) rather than special-casing one filename, and it keeps the `.env-id` store marker that `run_ensures` creates intact.

## Scope
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py` — add `scrub_bridge_state` helper; re-scrub after `run_ensures`.
- `tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` — add a fast repo-tier regression test: the `projects-seed` unit resurrects `.bridge_state/projects.json`, and the committing re-scrub removes it (worktree + tickets tree).

## Testing
- Fast unit test (`TestBridgeStateScrub`) drives the real `seed_projects_mapping_unit` to reproduce the resurrection (negative control) and asserts the post-converge scrub leaves no `.bridge_state*` and a clean git tree — no live harness needed.
- The live cell `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` is the ultimate check; it runs in the operator-dispatched DC-harness job (~1h), not a per-commit gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The store-copy scrub removes `.bridge_state` (and any equivalent binding/snapshot cache) so `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` passes in the live DC-harness job — verified by the re-scrub after `run_ensures` and the fast unit regression test in `tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` (Gerrit change 1783 / commit 716454cbe5, merged). [operator-attested] live DC-harness confirmation is deferred to the operator's next dispatched run.
- [x] A root-cause note explains why `.bridge_state` began surviving the scrub (regression origin) — recorded in this description (## Root cause) and as a ticket comment.

## Notes
Independent of the rich-text epic (vigilant-erasable-pony); does NOT touch `test_dc_rich_text_live.py` (owned concurrently by graywolf-land).
