## Context
The generated configuration narrative says resolved configuration is exposed through an MCP configuration-transparency surface. Its adjacent heading also labels the topic as `MCP/CLI exposure`, although no MCP configuration tool exists. Both assertions originated in the accepted generator design on `consensual-ignored-ivorygull`.

## Plan
- In `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`, change the `Exposure (MCP/CLI exposure)` heading to `Exposure (CLI exposure)` and remove the `MCP config-transparency surface` clause so the paragraph describes only the implemented `rebar config` CLI view.
- Retain accurate `rebar config` CLI exposure guidance.
- Regenerate `docs/config-reference.md` and prove it is current with `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py --check`.
- In `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py`, rename the `REQUIRED_TOPICS` label from `mcp/cli exposure` to `cli exposure` while retaining positive coverage of the implemented CLI guidance.
- In `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py`, add an explicit negative assertion over the rendered configuration narrative that rejects each unsupported form: `MCP/CLI exposure`, `MCP config-transparency surface`, and `MCP configuration surface`.
- Do not add an MCP tool or change configuration behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The generated heading is `Exposure (CLI exposure)` and the paragraph contains no MCP configuration-surface claim.
- [x] Implemented CLI configuration inspection remains documented accurately.
- [x] `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py --check` proves `docs/config-reference.md` is current after regeneration.
- [x] Focused generator tests include the enumerated negative guard and fail on restoration of any removed MCP-exposure wording.
- [x] Configuration runtime and MCP tool inventory are unchanged.
baseline.summary: F19A remove nonexistent MCP configuration exposure claim

baseline.description:
Remove the refs that pin pre-rewrite history, and take a backup that lives outside the repo. Without this the reclaim lands at **167 MB instead of ~94 MiB**. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Measured: remote tag `pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` (`2a77dd48`) is an ancestor of `origin/tickets` and pins **22,317 commits / 63,202,159 bytes** of `.bridge_state`. A full clone fetches tags, so leaving it defeats most of the reclaim. It is absent from Gerrit and replication is `mirror = false`, so deletion sticks and will not be recreated. Also delete the host-local `pre-a3-remediation` tag (`0adbd40a`, ~64.8 MB reachable).

An **in-repo** archive branch or tag reclaims nothing — reachable objects are served and repacked forever (crates.io's receipts: 1.73 GB live index vs **6.94 GB** archive repo). So the backup must leave the repository: `git bundle create` from an **unfiltered** clone, stored off-repo, including the tag tips being deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `git ls-remote --heads --tags origin` (de-peeling `^{}` entries) is enumerated at run time and
      every ref whose ancestry intersects the old tip is listed. Do **not** hardcode a count — today
      it is 13 heads + 16 distinct tags. Tier: **repo-level script**.
- [ ] After deletion, **no ref a default clone fetches** has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier:
      `ls-remote` + `merge-base --is-ancestor` loop. (Scoped deliberately: origin also carries ~120
      `refs/pull/*` and ~2,671 `refs/changes/*`, but those descend from `main`'s root and a default
      clone fetches neither. `refs/reconciler/lock` is a **blob**, so it carries no ancestry.)
- [ ] The off-repo bundle exists, was created from an **unfiltered** clone, contains the old tip and
      both deleted tag tips, and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] Restoring the bundle into a scratch repo reproduces the old tip SHA exactly. Tier:
      **integration** in a throwaway clone.

## Files
`infra/scripts/` (hygiene + bundle helper), runbook notes

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0c (the bundle should be taken with the same unfiltered-clone helper).
baseline.summary: A6-0d: pre-window ref hygiene and off-repo backup bundle

baseline.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in **bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json` (1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40 consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x), and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git — an earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and dropped re-homing it off-branch (WS-1) because the convergence loop already self-heals binding drift. So the levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included (child A6) under an operator-approved quiescence protocol. Its mechanics are **proven, not theoretical**: `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` on the real branch produced 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%) with all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges preserved and the HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths. Stock git plumbing only — `git-filter-repo` is deliberately **not** used: it is an unwanted core dependency and it prunes empty commits, which would reshape the DAG that ancestry-based authorship verification walks.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` + write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`
2. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; read `max(new, legacy)`
3. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority (exclude `assignee`)
4. **A2-2** delete the legacy in-line `last_get_pass` field (gated on writer rollout)
5. **A4-1/2/3** `bridge_fsck` fence, then `prev_snapshot` -> key-set, then branch-3 empty-payload skip
6. **A5** ADR covering all three committed-format changes
7. **A6** one-time reclaim under the quiescence protocol (LAST; requires A1-A5 and Epic B's B6)

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes to a shared store file, each with a stated boundary. A2-1 is reversible (it never stops writing the legacy field). A3 is reversible because the read path canonicalizes both shapes idempotently. A2-2 and A4-2 are the irreversible steps: A2-2 is gated on observed writer rollout; reverting A4-2 requires the reverse-direction corpus diff recorded first. A6 is gated on an off-repo backup bundle plus a fail-closed epoch guard, and its resumability is explicitly **none** — mitigated by running every correctness assertion on a scratch clone before anything is published.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline today 12.79 KB.
      Verify: the measurement script recorded in the child ticket.
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: integration against a stateful fake asserting
      file bytes and commit count, not call counts.
- [ ] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference to it remains. Verify: `grep -r baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty) — the read-only path must not persist a migration.
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the same
      verdict as its normalized-string equivalent. This test does not exist today; the existing
      cells use flat strings only, so a no-op-on-strings normalizer would pass while proving
      nothing. Tier: integration through the real production comparison path.
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over >=4 real snapshot pairs shows zero
      difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect, **and** the reverse-direction
      diff is recorded as the A4-2 rollback artifact.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` is **<=800 LOC** after the rotation extraction (it is at exactly 800
      today; the locked module-size gate fails the build on 801).
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB**, `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded
      pre-rewrite tip tree, and commit and merge-commit counts are unchanged (measured at window
      time, not hardcoded).
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** (the assertion that actually proves non-resurrection) and
      `size-pack` growth is <1 MB.
- [ ] A clone on a stale epoch attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites (`sync._union_merge` and `push.py`'s non-FF retry). Tier: integration in two
      real temporary clones with divergent epochs.
- [ ] An ADR exists enumerating all three committed-format changes, the mixed-version protocol, the
      A2-2 gate, and each rollback boundary.
- [ ] The off-repo backup bundle exists and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] Operator has confirmed zero active sessions and all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped before the
      reclaim window. **[operator-attested]**
baseline.summary: Bound tickets-store growth: make the committed .bridge_state cache cheap + one-time reclaim of the spent ~1 GiB

## Context / Problem
Commit 9ba1e90 (bug 330c, "box flips no longer stale attestations") changed the material-fingerprint algorithm in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py::material_fingerprint` to normalize AC checkbox state (`[x]` -> `[ ]`) before hashing — but with NO grandfathering of attestations signed under the OLD (non-normalized) algorithm. `compute_validity` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`) recomputes the CURRENT fingerprint with the new algorithm and compares it to the `material:` hash frozen in the signed manifest. Every completion attestation signed pre-330c embeds `[x]` in its hash basis (the 433c close gate REQUIRES all boxes checked at close), so after 330c landed those attestations read `stale-material` ("materially edited since the completion verdict") even though the ticket never changed.

Observed blast radius: epic 2f4c-7e5c-e782-4e97 closed 2026-08-03 with a PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT but NO signed completion attestation — `child_closure_findings` (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py`) read 4 pre-330c children (433c, 9d07, a584, d3ed) as closed-but-uncertified, `gate_ops.completion_precheck` set `certifiable=False`, and `transition_close.py` (the `certifiable is False` early return) silently skipped signing. Proof: each of those children's signed `material:` hash equals a byte-exact recomputation with the LEGACY non-normalized basis, while post-330c child 1e95 matches the normalized recomputation. This violates 330c's own AC ("existing attestations ... remain valid" — backward compatibility) and the epic-level verdict-trust design (a child validly certified at close must keep counting).

## Approach
Validity-on-read grandfathering, no event mutation: where `compute_validity` compares the signed `material:` fingerprint against `current_material_fingerprint`, on mismatch ALSO recompute the fingerprint over the legacy (non-normalized) basis and accept an exact legacy match as not-materially-edited. A legacy match means the basis (description including box state, file_impact, children) is byte-identical to what was signed, which is strictly stronger than the normalized check — no weakening. Apply to both the completion-verifier and plan-review branches (same seam, same class). Additionally make the certifiable=False unsigned-close path observable: carry `certifiable` on the PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar payload and warn on stderr when a PASS close is left unsigned because certification was withheld (today it is fully silent, which is what forced this archaeology).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py (legacy fingerprint variant)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py (compute_validity: legacy fallback on mismatch)
- src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py (PASS payload carries certifiable)
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py (stderr warning on certifiable=False unsigned close)
- tests/unit (RED-first regression tests)

## Testing
RED first: a completion attestation whose manifest `material:` was computed WITHOUT checkbox normalization over a checked description must read valid=True from compute_validity (fails today with stale-material); a genuinely edited description must still read stale-material (negative control); the PASS sidecar payload must carry certifiable; the unsigned certifiable=False close path must emit a stderr warning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A completion attestation signed under the pre-330c (non-normalized) fingerprint over an unchanged ticket reads valid/certified from compute_validity.
- [x] A plan-review attestation signed under the pre-330c fingerprint over an unchanged ticket is likewise not invalidated as stale-material.
- [x] A real material edit (text change) still invalidates: legacy fallback does not weaken staleness detection.
- [x] The PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar records the verdict's certifiable flag.
- [x] A PASS close that skips signing because certifiable=False warns on stderr (no longer silent).
baseline.summary: Pre-330c completion/plan-review attestations read stale-material (no grandfathering) — epic closes silently unsigned

## Context / Problem
Bug cranial-sulfur-peafowl (a392-f630-7b25-4b14) added the `closed -> open` (reopen) edge to the parent-first cascade table `_CASCADING_EDGES` in `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`, closing the reopen hole. A SECOND edge into the same invalid state is still open: `transition <id> closed in_progress`, the direct closed-then-reactivate edge. `transition_compute`'s own comment acknowledges that edge exists ("reaching here with target in_progress means current is open/blocked/closed"), and `_CASCADING_EDGES` has no `(\"closed\", \"in_progress\")` entry, so reactivating a closed child under a closed parent leaves the parent closed — the same invalid closed-parent-with-non-closed-child state.

It was deliberately left out of a392-f630-7b25-4b14: that plan was reviewed and signed with an explicit "only the closed -> open edge is added" scope statement, and cascading a parent from `closed` straight to `in_progress` additionally drags the parent through its own plan-review start-work gate, which is a behavior change worth reviewing on its own.

## Approach
Add `(\"closed\", \"in_progress\"): \"closed\"` to `_CASCADING_EDGES` so the parent is reactivated on the same edge ahead of the child, and decide deliberately what the cascaded parent's gate interaction should be: the cascade runs the parent's FULL transition, so the parent's plan-review start-work gate fires and can block the child's reactivation, exactly as it already does on the `open -> in_progress` cascade (docs/concurrency.md I4a, "Gate interaction"). Document whichever behavior is chosen in that same section.

Why this approach: the edge table added by a392-f630-7b25-4b14 is already the single place both existing cascading edges are declared, so this is a one-entry extension plus its gate/doc decision, not new machinery.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — add the third entry to `_CASCADING_EDGES`.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py` — cases for the new edge.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — extend the I4a cascading-edge table and its gate-interaction note.

## Testing
- Reactivate a closed child under a closed parent -> both end `in_progress`.
- Reactivate under an already-`in_progress` parent -> parent untouched.
- Multi-level closed chain -> every ancestor reactivated.
- Parent's plan-review start-work gate blocking -> the child is NOT reactivated and the error names the parent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar transition <child> closed in_progress` under a closed parent leaves no closed parent with a non-closed child. Checked by the happy-path and multi-level tests asserting every ancestor is `in_progress`.
- [x] An already-`in_progress` or `open` parent is not disturbed by the new edge. Checked by the no-op tests.
- [x] The cascaded parent's plan-review start-work gate behavior is explicit and tested. Checked by the gate-blocking test asserting the child stays `closed` and the error names the parent.
- [x] docs/concurrency.md I4a lists all three cascading edges. Checked by reading the updated section.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, complexity ratchet reports no new/increased entries.
baseline.summary: closed -> in_progress reactivation lacks the parent-first cascade, still allowing a closed parent with an in_progress child

## Context / Problem

Daily plan-review cache reads in `.rebar/usage.jsonl` fell from ~80% of input tokens (2026-08-06..11) to 0 from 2026-08-12, and the median full plan review rose from ~$2.18 to ~$4.82 (Aug 6–29 logged spend ~$3,000). The transition coincides with commit `6d4f394195b2` (2026-08-10, ticket `esthetical-earthborn-vervet` / `8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8`), which added the Anthropic-direct fallback to the frontier/standard classes in `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]`.

`_intersect_capabilities` (`src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py`) computes ONE capability record for the whole fallback chain and collapses differing `prompt_cache_style` values to `"none"`. Both mixed chains are **Bedrock-primary, Anthropic-fallback** (`rebar.toml:223-224`), and the Anthropic hedge fires only **0.43%** of calls (51 of 11,902 logged rows), so the collapse disabled caching on the Bedrock target that serves ~99.6% of calls.

## Why reversing the documented intent is sound (detail in ticket comment)

The collapse-to-none is documented/approved intent in three sites, all updated by this change: the `_intersect_capabilities` docstring (`runner_support.py:56-58`, where the "keys would error on the non-sharing candidate" premise lives), the `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]` note (~190-193), and `docs/llm-framework.md` (~829-840). ADR 0059 §7 documents the per-provider key mechanics rather than that premise; it gets a superseding note, preserving §2's ModelProfile-not-provider-name invariant.

That premise is false for cache keys, proven at runtime: the cache directive is provider-scoped `ModelSettings` keys, `merge_model_settings` is an unvalidated dict union, and each provider model reads only its own `*_cache_*` keys via `.get(...)` — so a Bedrock-primary directive reaching a served Anthropic fallback is a silent no-op (uncached-but-correct), never an error. The full mechanism, runtime experiment, LangChain#37042 direction, and OSS grounding (LiteLLM, pydantic-ai) are in the pinned ticket comment.

Therefore only `prompt_cache_style` — advisory and inert cross-provider — follows the PRIMARY; fields that CAN hard-fail cross-provider (`supports_temperature` → HTTP 400, `native_structured_output`, `supports_thinking`, `native_output_with_thinking`, `native_web_search`) stay conservatively `all(...)`-intersected.

## Approach

Option **(a): fix the capability seam** (operator decision; option (b), homogenising the chains, is off the table — the Anthropic hedge is required functionality). In `_intersect_capabilities`, derive `prompt_cache_style` from `per_candidate[0]` (the primary/serving candidate) instead of collapsing to `"none"`; keep every hard-failing field `all(...)`-intersected. Update the three stale-intent sites and ADR 0059 §7. The runtime analysis establishes (a) does not destabilise the seam, so no escalation.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py` — seam fix + docstring rewrite (stale-intent site 1).
- `tests/unit/test_runner_support.py` — NEW focused module for `_intersect_capabilities` (defined in `runner_support.py`, so this is its natural home; `test_llm_capabilities.py` imports it via the `rebar.llm.runner` re-export for unrelated native-output-under-thinking assertions, left intact).
- `rebar.toml` — `[llm.model_classes]` caching comment (site 2).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — mixed-provider-chain caching stanza (site 3).
- `docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md` — superseding note in §7.

## Testing

Unit (`tests/unit/test_runner_support.py`): a mixed Bedrock-primary chain keeps `"bedrock"` (RED before fix); an Anthropic-primary chain keeps `"anthropic"`; a `"none"`-primary chain stays `"none"`; a homogeneous chain is unchanged; hard-fail fields still intersect conservatively; and a parametrized fallback-fires test proves the primary directive is inert on the Anthropic arm. Mutation-checked: seeding the historical collapse-to-none turns 5 of 7 tests RED. Live check: a post-fix `review-plan` logs `cache_read_tokens > 0` in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A regression test proves a mixed Bedrock-primary chain reports `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` (not `"none"`); RED before the fix, green after; runs in `make test`.
- [x] A test proves a served Anthropic fallback receiving the Bedrock-primary directive reads every `anthropic_cache_*` key as `None` with no `UserError` (uncached-but-correct).
- [x] A regression test asserts `supports_temperature` and `native_structured_output` still withdraw (intersect conservatively) on a mixed chain.
- [x] The `_intersect_capabilities` docstring is updated to cache-follows-primary.
- [x] The `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]` caching comment (~190-193) is updated to cache-follows-primary.
- [x] The `docs/llm-framework.md` caching stanza (~829-840) is updated to cache-follows-primary.
- [x] ADR 0059 §7 carries a superseding note recording cache-follows-serving-provider.
- [x] [non-codebase] After the fix, a production plan review logs non-zero `cache_read_tokens` (the pre-2026-08-12 cache-read fraction is restored).
  provenance: environment=production-plan-review-runtime; principal=rebar-review-bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — a post-deploy runtime observation of a real Bedrock-served plan review; not verifiable from the code snapshot. The in-repo mechanism (mixed chain yields prompt_cache_style=bedrock and emits cache breakpoints) is covered by the untagged test criteria above.
baseline.summary: Prompt caching silently disabled since 2026-08-12: mixed Bedrock+Anthropic class fallback collapses prompt_cache_style to none (~2x review cost)

baseline.description:
## Problem
`review_bot/adapter.py::_translate_findings` maps each finding's kernel severity (`critical/major/minor/none`) to the common vocabulary via its own copy of `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`, but nothing downstream ever renders that value to a human: `render_findings_block`/`_summarize` in `review_bot/finding_publish.py` render each finding as `- ({criterion}) {detail}[ {location}]` with NO severity word anywhere, and the Gerrit comment already conveys blocking vs advisory structurally (via the batch each call renders: `blocking` items under one header, `advisory` items under another). So the human-facing Gerrit comment ALREADY satisfies "blocking/advisory, never severity" -- `finding_publish.py` needs NO change.

The real defect: `_translate_findings` flattens `verdict["blocking"]` and `verdict["advisory"]` into ONE list with no field distinguishing which bucket a translated finding came from -- its `severity` computation is dead weight nothing reads. Separately, two CLI text renderers DO print a severity word today, for findings that (after the sibling ticket beaming-snively-urial) now also carry `priority`/`decision`: `_render_review_text` (`review_result` findings) prints `f.get('severity','?').upper()`; `_render_plan_review_text`'s advisory branch prints `sev={f.get('severity')}` (its blocking branch already prints no severity). `_render_verdict_text` (completion_verdict findings) is OUT OF SCOPE: those findings come from `completion_reconcile.py`'s independent module cluster, never pass through the review-kernel, and never carry `priority`/`decision` -- `severity` is their only signal and stays untouched.

`_render_review_text` is a SHARED renderer: besides code-review's `review_result` (from `shim.py`, which now carries `decision`), it ALSO renders `scan_epics_for_spec`/`scan-spec` results (`_llm_commands.py:222`) -- `spec_scan.py`'s free-form "spec-alignment" reviewer findings, which never pass through the code-review kernel/shim.py and carry `severity` but NEVER `decision`. A blind severity->decision swap would print a meaningless/fallback word for every spec-scan finding and discard the only real signal that population has.

## Approach
1. In `review_bot/adapter.py::_translate_findings`, replace the `severity` key with a
   `blocking: bool` (`True` for items from `verdict["blocking"]`, `False` for
   `verdict["advisory"]`) -- fixing the genuine gap that the flattened output cannot currently
   tell the two buckets apart. Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` from `adapter.py` (its only
   use site).
2. `review_bot/finding_publish.py` (`render_findings_block`/`post_review`) is NOT touched --
   confirmed it renders no severity word today and already conveys blocking/advisory via its
   `kind=` batching, satisfying the epic's human-facing design goal with zero code change.
3. Update `_render_review_text` in `_cli/_llm_commands.py`: when a finding's `decision` field
   is present (the code-review/`review_result` path), print `BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` derived from
   it (`"block"` -> `BLOCKING`, else `ADVISORY`) instead of the severity word; when `decision`
   is absent (the `scan-spec`/`spec_scan.py` path), KEEP printing the existing
   `f.get('severity','?').upper()` fallback unchanged -- this renderer must serve both
   producers correctly.
4. Update `_render_plan_review_text`'s advisory branch to drop the `sev={severity}` suffix
   entirely (the function's blocking branch already omits any per-finding tag beyond its
   `[BLOCK ...]`/`[advisory ...]` bucket label, so dropping the advisory branch's severity
   suffix makes the two branches consistent -- no replacement tag needed since bucket
   membership already conveys blocking/advisory). Add a new test (none currently exists) that
   feeds a non-empty advisory finding through `_render_plan_review_text` and asserts the
   post-change line contains no `sev=` substring.
5. `_render_verdict_text` is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE (see Problem) -- left unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY" src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` returns no
  matches; `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY" src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py` still
  finds it (unchanged, out of scope for this ticket).
- [x] `adapter.py::_translate_findings`'s output carries a `blocking: bool` key per finding
  instead of `severity`; `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_carry_forward.py -k test_adapter_carries_standing_through_to_the_receiver_shape`
  passes, strengthened with an assertion that a `verdict["blocking"]`-sourced finding has
  `blocking=True` and a `verdict["advisory"]`-sourced one has `blocking=False`.
- [x] `src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` has zero diff from this ticket
  (`git diff --stat src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` is empty); `pytest
  tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py` passes unchanged.
- [x] `_render_review_text` prints `BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` for a finding carrying `decision`, and
  still prints the uppercased `severity` word unchanged for a finding with no `decision` (the
  `scan-spec` case) -- a new test in `_cli/_llm_commands.py`'s test coverage (locate via
  `pytest --collect-only -q -k llm_commands`) asserts BOTH cases explicitly.
- [x] `_render_plan_review_text`'s advisory branch no longer prints `sev=...`; a NEW test
  (none of the existing plan-review-reuse/gate tests cover this line -- they use empty
  advisory lists) feeds a non-empty advisory finding through `_render_plan_review_text` and
  asserts the rendered line contains no `sev=` substring.

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit tests against the real `_translate_findings` and CLI renderer functions, fed production-shaped verdict/result dicts (contract test). Oracle: the exact `blocking`/`BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` values and text, asserted directly; and a negative check that `finding_publish.py`'s rendered output is byte-identical to before (zero diff to that file is itself the contrast/regression check). Contrast case (test-design.md sec.6): a `decision`- bearing finding (code-review) and a `decision`-absent finding (spec-scan) fed through `_render_review_text` must produce different label sources (derived-from-decision vs severity-fallback) while both remaining meaningful. Refactoring litmus: renaming an internal helper inside a renderer must not break these tests, since they assert on the printed text/output value, not on which helper produced it.
baseline.summary: Surface blocking/advisory instead of severity in review-bot and CLI renderers

baseline.description:
## Context

When the plan-review gate is enabled at the project level
(`verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true`, and/or `verify.allow_llm = true`), a plan review
whose **LLM tier cannot run because of a missing dependency or environment misconfiguration**
(the `[agents]` extra absent, `yaml`/`pydantic-ai` not importable, no API key, runner preflight
failure) **silently degrades to a deterministic-floor-only review and still returns `verdict:
PASS`** — and that hollow PASS is **HMAC-signed into a claimable attestation**. The whole point of
the gate (real, grounded review before work starts) is defeated without any signal.

This is distinct from — and should NOT be conflated with — the legitimate **fail-open on an
unsupported stack** (a polyglot language with no tooling, a per-criterion oracle abstain). Those are
intentional, per-check abstains recorded as coverage. A **missing dependency when the gate is
explicitly enabled is a misconfiguration**, not an unsupported stack, and must fail loud.

Root cause: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:393-403` wraps the entire LLM-tier run in a
broad `except Exception` that records `coverage["llm_error"]` + `coverage["llm_ran"] = False` and
then continues to assemble + sign a PASS verdict from the DET floor alone:

```
try:
    runner_sel.preflight()
    findings = _run_passes(...)
    llm_ran = True
except Exception as exc:  # LLM unavailable -> DET-only review (advisory still works)
    coverage["llm_error"] = str(exc)
    coverage["llm_ran"] = False
```

The verdict/signing path downstream does not gate on `llm_ran`, so `llm_ran: False` still yields a
signed PASS.

## Reproduction Steps

1. On a project with `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true`, run rebar from an environment
   that is MISSING the `[agents]` extra (e.g. `pydantic-ai-slim` / `yaml` not installed).
2. `rebar review-plan <ticket>`.
3. Observe the JSON result, then `rebar claim <ticket>`.

## Expected

The review **fails with a descriptive error** that names the missing dependency and how to install
it (e.g. "plan-review LLM tier could not run: the 'agents' extra is missing — install
`nava-rebar[agents]`; the gate is enabled, so a deterministic-floor-only review is not a valid
PASS"). **No PASS verdict and no signed attestation are produced** (verdict is a hard error /
`INDETERMINATE`), so the subsequent `claim` stays blocked.

## Actual

`verdict: PASS` with `llm_ran: false` and an `llm_error` buried in `coverage`; `signature.signed:
true`. The ticket is now claimable on a review where **zero LLM criteria ran** — a false sense of
security and a silent bypass of the gate (install nothing → every ticket "passes").

Observed directly while standing up repo-rebar to implement epic `boil-golem-veto`: the first
`review-plan` run returned `{"verdict":"PASS", ..., "llm_ran":false, "llm_error":"the pydantic_ai
runner needs the 'agents' extra ...", "signature":{"signed":true}}`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When the gate is enabled and the LLM tier cannot run due to a **missing dependency / preflight
      / environment** failure (as opposed to a per-criterion unsupported-stack abstain), the review
      returns a **non-PASS** result (hard error or `INDETERMINATE`) with a **descriptive,
      actionable** message naming the cause and remedy.
- [ ] No HMAC attestation is signed for such a run; a subsequent `claim` remains blocked.
- [ ] The legitimate fail-open path (genuinely unsupported stack / per-criterion oracle abstain)
      still works and is NOT turned into a hard failure — the two cases are distinguished (e.g.
      preflight/import/config error vs. recorded per-check abstain).
- [ ] The broad `except Exception` at `orchestrator.py:393-403` no longer lets a dependency/preflight

baseline.description:
## Problem

The bridge project mapping (`.bridge_state/projects.json` — mapped keys + `legacy_default`) can hold syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent or bot-invisible Jira project keys. Ticket F adds SYNTACTIC write-time validation only (deliberately: a live call in the `set_project` write path couples a local config write to Jira availability/auth, adds latency/flakiness, blocks legitimate bootstrapping/provisioning order, and is TOCTOU-insufficient anyway). Ticket D adds an at-pass-time EXISTENCE/visibility preflight inside the reconcile pass (the authoritative mutation guard).

Neither gives an operator an on-demand, non-blocking way to ask "are my mapped keys + legacy_default actually visible to the bot right now?" outside a full reconcile pass. The projects.json corruption incident (bug 05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27) would have been caught immediately by such a diagnostic.

## Scope (approved: additive diagnostic on the BRIDGE surface only)

Add an OPT-IN, credential-conditional, READ-ONLY, ADVISORY live mapped-key/legacy_default visibility check to the existing `rebar bridge fsck` verb, gated behind a new `--live-visibility` flag.

Hard constraints (separation of concerns — Jira stays an optional extra):
1. Live check lives ONLY on the bridge surface. Do NOT add it to core `rebar doctor`
   (`src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`) — that command is store/tracker health and MUST stay Jira-free
   (no reconciler / `[agents]` optional-extra import from core doctor).
2. Do NOT introduce a `bridge doctor` verb (epic 2f79 deliberately declined it — reuse `bridge fsck`).
3. Reuse D's mapped-project visibility helper — ONE shared helper answers "are the mapped keys +
   legacy_default visible to the bot?". Do NOT hand-roll a second Jira existence check (that is the
   duplicated-existence-check parity smell this epic has been eliminating). This is why G depends_on D.
   The shared helper is `rebar_reconciler.access_check.check_mapped_project_visibility(repo_root, *,
   probe=None, client_cls, env=None, query_project=None, projects_store_mod=None) ->
   ProjectVisibilityResult(status, required, visible, missing, detail)` where status is one of
   {ok, missing, transport_unavailable, skipped}.
4. Credential-conditional graceful degradation: the NEW fsck-layer step performs its OWN
   `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN` presence check FIRST (mirroring `run_access_check`'s
   `missing_credentials` contract in `access_check.py`) and, when any is absent/incomplete AND no
   `probe=` is injected, emits an advisory `skipped` verdict with `reason="missing_credentials"`
   WITHOUT calling the probe. Only when creds are present (or a `probe=` is injected for tests) does
   the step call `check_mapped_project_visibility(probe=...)`. This is the fsck layer bridging the
   helper's own `transport_unavailable`-on-absent-creds behavior into the operator-facing
   "skipped — no live credentials" advisory. The step MUST skip cleanly, NOT fail.
5. Read-only + advisory: no Jira writes; no bridge-state mutation; the new step reports drift but does
   NOT change `bridge fsck`'s existing pass/fail exit contract.

## Surfacing the verdict (data flow when `--live-visibility` IS passed)

To keep the pinned `bridge_fsck.schema.json` output contract UNCHANGED (its `required` set and the `test_bridge_fsck_schema_pins_new_required_fields_and_integrity_kinds` contract test both fix the top-level JSON to exactly `{unknown_event_types, binding_drift, store_integrity}` under `additionalProperties: false`), the `--live-visibility` advisory is rendered as human-readable lines to STDERR (a separate stream) in BOTH text and `--output json` modes. It is NOT added as a new field to the stdout JSON findings object, so no schema or schema-contract-test change is required and the default (no-flag) stdout is byte-identical to today. The step's structured verdict dict is returned by a directly-unit-testable helper (`audit_mapped_project_visibility(...)`) which main() renders to stderr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar bridge fsck --live-visibility` gains a mapped-project live-visibility step that, WHEN live
  creds are present, lists each mapped key + legacy_default and reports visible / NOT-visible-to-bot
  by calling the shared helper `access_check.check_mapped_project_visibility`; the advisory is written
  to stderr and does not alter the exit code.
- [x] WHEN live creds (`JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN`) are absent/incomplete AND no `probe=` is
  injected, the fsck-layer step's own presence check emits an advisory verdict
  `{"status":"skipped","reason":"missing_credentials"}` WITHOUT calling the probe, and `bridge fsck`
  behaves exactly as today (no crash, exit contract unchanged).
- [x] The visibility logic is the SAME helper D uses (`check_mapped_project_visibility`, injected via the
  `probe=` seam) — no duplicate existence check; verified by test.
- [x] Core `rebar doctor` imports remain Jira-free (no new reconciler/`[agents]` import reachable from
  `_commands/doctor.py`); verified by test.
- [x] The default `rebar bridge fsck` (no `--live-visibility`) stdout JSON contract is unchanged (exactly
  `unknown_event_types`, `binding_drift`, `store_integrity`); `bridge_fsck.schema.json` and its contract
  test are untouched.

## Testing

RED→GREEN always-on unit tests in `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck.py`, run with `python -m pytest tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck.py -q`:
- (a) creds-present path with a `probe=` injected showing a mapped key invisible → the step's verdict is
  `status="missing"` and names the invisible key.
- (b) creds-absent path (no probe, empty/partial `JIRA_*` env) → the step's own presence check returns
  `status="skipped"`, `reason="missing_credentials"`, no probe call, no hard failure, exit contract
  unchanged.
- (c) all-visible `probe=` → `status="ok"`.
- (d) core-`rebar doctor`-stays-Jira-free assertion (no reconciler import reachable from
  `_commands/doctor.py`).
Also `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; no real network calls in tests (patch the `probe=` seam).

## Notes
- Depends on D for the shared visibility helper (`access_check.check_mapped_project_visibility`).
- Same workflow as A/B/D: fresh worktree off origin/main, review-plan → sign-review → claim, RED→GREEN
  TDD, make lint/typecheck + targeted pytest, commit -s with rebar-ticket trailer, push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main.
baseline.summary: bridge fsck: opt-in live mapped-key visibility diagnostic

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A rebar ticket carries no record of which tracker project it syncs into, nor which repos it belongs to. The current ticket state fields are seeded in `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:29-81` and declared in `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`; neither includes a project. Today the project is only implicit — recoverable from a bound issue's key prefix in `bindings.json`, and absent entirely for a ticket that has never been bound. Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` needs it explicit, because a ticket that is deliberately not synced has no binding to infer from.

## Approach

Add two ticket state fields together, in one edit set: `bridge_project` (string) and `repos` (list of strings). They are one story rather than two because a field is not usable without its write path, and splitting them would put two children on `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`.

`bridge_project` is **tri-state**, mirroring the established `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths pattern (`docs/ticket-model.md:210-212`): absent means legacy, an explicit empty string means never sync, and a key means sync there. The three states are distinguished so a pre-feature store is not read as "every ticket is unsynced". Resolution of the absent state is not implemented here — it belongs to `resolve_project` in the mapping module.

Both fields are written into the CREATE event data by `create_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:169-220`), projected by the reducer, and seeded in `make_initial_state`. Create-time arguments `--bridge-project` and `--repos` are added to all three write surfaces — CLI (`composer.create_cli`), library (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:79-135`), and MCP (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:47-70`). Note the CLI flag loop rejects unknown options strictly (`composer.py:287-291`), so the new flags must be registered there or they are hard errors.

`bridge_project` is **promote-only**: setting it on a ticket with no binding is allowed, changing it on a ticket that already holds one is refused. That keeps the change free of any issue-move or unbind/rebind machinery. `repos` stays freely editable — it never reaches the tracker, so there is no binding to invalidate.

No schema version bump: `docs/event-schema.md:124-150` states additive fields on an existing event type do not require one. Types are generated from the schemas (`reducer/_state.py:11-13`), so the generator is re-run.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard: a producer/consumer contract test for the event→state path (real CREATE event fed through the real reducer, no stubbing), plus a real CLI subprocess test for the argument parsing, since the strict unknown-option rejection is itself part of the mechanism.

- Happy path: `create task "t" --bridge-project REB --repos rebar,api` produces a ticket whose state
  shows `bridge_project == "REB"` and `repos == ["rebar", "api"]` after a full replay.
- Three-state coverage: a ticket created without the flag replays with the field **absent**; one
  created with an explicit empty value replays with `""`. These must be distinguishable — asserting
  the absent case is not merely falsy is the point of the test.
- Cross-surface parity: the same ticket shape results from the CLI, the library, and MCP.
- Failure path: an edit setting `bridge_project` on a ticket that already holds a binding is refused
  with a non-zero exit and the stored value is unchanged; the same edit on an unbound ticket succeeds.
- Collateral invariant: replaying a ticket created before this change yields identical state apart
  from the two new keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge_project` and `repos` are declared in the ticket state schema, seeded in
      `make_initial_state`, and projected by the reducer; checked by a replay test asserting both on
      a freshly created ticket.
- [ ] `--bridge-project` and `--repos` exist on the CLI, library and MCP create paths and produce
      identical state; checked by a per-surface test comparing the resulting ticket state.
- [ ] The absent, explicit-empty, and set states are distinguishable after replay; checked by a
      parameterized test asserting each of the three separately.
- [ ] Setting `bridge_project` on a bound ticket is refused while setting it on an unbound ticket
      succeeds; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] A ticket created before this change replays to the same state apart from the new keys; checked
      by a fixture-based regression test.
baseline.summary: Ticket fields: tri-state bridge_project and repos, with create-time arguments on all three write surfaces

baseline.description:
Close the silent-success gap on the NativeOutput structured path (parity with PromptedOutput) plus two proven output self-heal tweaks on rebar's already-strong structured.py ladder. Small, cohesive, fully offline-verified.

## Why
A truncated / refused turn never raises at the model layer — it comes back as a complete-looking but unusable response — so exception classification can't see it; it needs a stop-reason check on the RESULT. rebar's PromptedOutput path already does this (`structured.check_stop_reason`, runner.py:519). But the **NativeOutput path (runner.py:497-502) returns `run_result.output` DIRECTLY with NO stop-reason check** — a truncated/refused NativeOutput response is returned as a hollow verdict. Separately, `structured.py` already implements almost the whole self-heal ladder (tolerant parse, deterministic json-repair before reask, error-fed reask, fast-fail on truncation, bounded `OUTPUT_RETRIES`) — it needs two cheap, proven additions.

## What
- **NativeOutput stop-reason parity (the core fix):** add `structured.check_stop_reason(getattr(run_result.response, "finish_reason", None))` on the NativeOutput branch (runner.py:497-502) BEFORE returning. A `length`/`max_tokens`/`content_filter`/`refusal` finish_reason then raises `UnretryableOutputError` (⊂ `StructuredOutputError` ⊂ `LLMError`) — exactly as the PromptedOutput path already does — so the gate degrades to an unsigned INDETERMINATE via `gate_dispatch`, never a hollow PASS/BLOCK. This REUSES the existing raise-based degrade path; it adds NO new routing, NO coverage-field change, NO truncation-vs-parse conjunction (the check runs BEFORE any parse, so truncation is always caught as the exception — there is no "parses-but-truncated" case). NOTE Anthropic (rebar's provider) uses PromptedOutput today; NativeOutput is the OpenAI-strict-schema path, fixed for correctness/parity.
- **Self-heal tweak 1 — schema-guided json-repair:** `structured.py:161` currently calls `repair_json(cand, return_objects=True)` WITHOUT a `schema=` arg. Add `schema=model_cls` (json-repair 0.61.2 accepts a pydantic v2 model directly; default `schema_repair_mode='standard'`) for schema-guided deterministic repair BEFORE any LLM reask, wrapped in a `try/except` that falls back to today's schema-less `repair_json` if the schema-guided call raises (never regresses current behavior). Requires threading `model_cls` into the tolerant-parse helper. Bump the `pyproject.toml` pin `json-repair>=0.30` → `>=0.61` (0.61.2 already installed — a floor raise, not a runtime change) so `schema=` is guaranteed.
- **Self-heal tweak 2 — faulty prior output in the reask:** `runner.py:530`'s reask sends instructions + schema_hint + the validation error, but NOT the model's raw faulty reply. Add a bounded snippet `str(result.output)[:_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS]` (named constant = 2000, truncated with an ellipsis marker) so the model can diff its own mistake (the LangChain RetryWithErrorOutputParser / Instructor pattern).
- **Deferred (follow-on, NOT here):** the #5221 case — a refusal returned as NON-EMPTY content with a NORMAL finish_reason and only an out-of-band `provider_details` signal — is NOT detected here; its exact Anthropic `provider_details` shape can't be characterized without a live refusal, so it is deferred IN FULL to a `discovered_from` follow-on ticket. This story adds NO speculative provider_details parsing. (Anthropic refusals today normalize to the finish_reason the parity fix already catches.)

## Scope
- The NativeOutput stop-reason parity fix + the two `structured.py`/`runner.py` self-heal tweaks + the pin bump. Cohesion: all are small, same-theme changes to the same structured-output reliability seam (`_pai_structured` + `structured.py`), share tests, and none is independently land-worthy — kept together to minimize integration overhead.
- NOT in scope: a second-interpreter "fixer" LLM (`structured.py` rejects it — keep that stance); verdict-schema edits (blackbear owns those); the deferred #5221 refusal-as-content case.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The NativeOutput path runs `check_stop_reason`, so a truncated/refused NativeOutput response raises `UnretryableOutputError` → INDETERMINATE (parity with PromptedOutput), not a hollow verdict — test `test_native_output_path_checks_stop_reason`. A zero-finding CLEAN NativeOutput/PromptedOutput review still passes untouched — test `test_zero_finding_clean_review_passes`.
- [ ] `repair_json` is called with `schema=model_cls`, with a `try/except` fallback to the schema-less call — tests `test_repair_json_receives_schema` and `test_repair_json_falls_back_when_schema_call_raises`.
- [ ] The targeted reask includes the bounded faulty prior output (`_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS`) — test `test_reask_prompt_includes_bounded_prior_output`.
- [ ] No second-LLM fixer; no verdict-schema files edited. The deferred #5221 follow-on is created during the work (not a close-gate criterion).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` (schema-guided repair; thread model_cls), `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (NativeOutput check_stop_reason; bounded faulty output in reask), `pyproject.toml` (json-repair pin), `tests/unit/test_silent_success.py` (new); read-only on `src/rebar/schemas/*`.

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
ModelResponse fields: [parts, usage, model_name, timestamp, kind, provider_name, provider_url,
                       provider_details, provider_response_id, finish_reason, run_id, ...]
  -> finish_reason present (truncation/refusal signal, read by structured.check_stop_reason)
  -> provider_details present (the STRUCTURED out-of-band filter signal drake keys on, NOT a regex)
rebar structured.check_stop_reason(stop_reason: str | None) -> None   (reused for the truncation conjunction)
```
json-repair schema-guided repair, VERIFIED offline:
```
json-repair 0.61.2: repair_json params = [json_str, return_objects, skip_json_loads, logging, json_fd,
    chunk_length, stream_stable, strict, schema, schema_repair_mode, json_dumps_args]  -> schema + schema_repair_mode present
```
The current pin `json-repair>=0.30` predates the `schema=` arg; this story bumps it to `>=0.61` (0.61.2 is already installed, so the bump is a floor-raise, not a runtime change). So the refusal-as-content detection keys on the structured provider signal (finish_reason + provider_details), never a regex over answer text; and the truncation conjunction reuses the existing check_stop_reason. A detected silent-success is routed through story mamba's shared LLMOutcome (resolution_class=CHANGE_INPUT + sanitized diagnostic) — one routing path, not a second. These are pydantic-ai LIBRARY response fields, not rebar symbols (bug succinct-formable-kite: repo-absence != non-existence). RED baseline (arawana, committed) pins today: canned content_filter/length finish_reason -> UnretryableOutputError; text mode does NOT read finish_reason (the silent-success gap drake closes).
baseline.summary: Silent-success detection + output self-heal (schema-guided repair, faulty-output reask)

baseline.description:
Delete `baseline_advanced_at` and stop rewriting an unchanged baseline. This is the single highest-value change in the epic: it cuts marginal packed cost per `bindings.json` version from **12.79 KB to 1.74 KB (7.4x)**, measured over 40 consecutive real revisions. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`binding_store.py:373-375` unconditionally rewrites `entry["baseline"]` and stamps `baseline_advanced_at = _now_iso()`. That field is written in exactly one place and **read nowhere in `src/`** (only asserted in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py:61`). Measured across consecutive committed revisions: baseline VALUES changed **0** entries while the stamp changed **1144** — a scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file, which is pathological for git delta compression.

Honest scoping: because baseline values change 0 entries/pass today, the write-when-changed guard is **byte-neutral** and the entire measured win comes from deleting the field. The guard is still worth adding — it is the correct behaviour once real Jira edits arrive, and it saves the rewrite CPU — but it must not be credited with the savings.

## Approach
In `set_baseline`: build the filtered baseline, compare to the existing one, return early if equal; never write `baseline_advanced_at`. Preserve `binding_store.py:374`'s `if k in fields` semantics (**not** `is not None`) — `outbound_field_diff.py:251` treats a MISSING key as "no ancestor -> local wins", so a key must stay present with a `None` value rather than being dropped.

Both callers must be covered: `reconcile._advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:506-523`) and the inbound-adopt path at `apply_inbound_records.py:209-212`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: **integration** against a stateful fake,
      asserting file bytes and commit count — not call counts. (`save()` uses
      `json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, so byte-identity is well-defined.)
- [ ] `grep -rn baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing; the stamp is absent from every entry
      written by `set_baseline`. Tier: **unit** + grep assertion.
- [ ] A baseline field present-but-null still round-trips as present (guards the `if k in fields`
      semantics). Tier: **unit** on `set_baseline` + `get_baseline`.
- [ ] `test_binding_baseline.py:61`'s assertion on the stamp is removed or inverted, and the suite is
      green. Verify: `make test`.
- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed version measured at **<=25% of the 12.79 KB baseline** by the
      recorded method (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo, repack
      `--window=250 --depth=50`, `(pack_N-pack_1)/(N-1)`). Tier: **repo-level measurement**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`

Scope: S-M.
baseline.summary: A1: delete the never-read baseline_advanced_at stamp and add a write-when-changed guard to set_baseline

baseline.description:
# The live-DC readiness gate (`serverInfo` 200) is too weak for the contract 3fe5 asserts, so a timing flake would be misattributed to an image degrade

## The gap

Both live-DC workflows gate on the same signal — poll `/rest/api/2/serverInfo` until 200:

* `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:526-536`
* `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml:50-60`

But `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py::_assert_project_capabilities` then asserts the instance exposes the **Jira Software (GreenHopper) custom fields** `Epic Link` and `Epic Name` (`_REQUIRED_FIELDS`). **`serverInfo` answering 200 does not imply those fields are registered.**

## Proof, measured on the probe workflow

Run 30944211742 shares the harness's readiness gate and queries the field inventory immediately after it passes:

```
Wait for Jira DC to become ready : 19:39:01 -> 19:47:33   (8m32s, serverInfo polling)
Run the Epic-Link clear probe    : 19:47:33 -> 19:47:34   (1 second later)

field 'Epic Link' absent from an inventory of 27 field(s); names present:
  ['Archived','Archiver','Attachment','Comment','Created','Creator','Images','Key','Last Viewed',
   'Log Work','Original Estimate','Progress','Project','Remaining Estimate','Resolved','Status',
   'Sub-Tasks','Time Spent','Time Tracking','Updated','Votes','Watchers','Work Ratio',
   'Σ Original Estimate','Σ Progress','Σ Remaining Estimate','Σ Time Spent']
```

27 fields, **every one a system field, zero `customfield_*`**. The read was authorised and well-formed; the plugin had simply not registered its fields one second after `serverInfo` went green.

## Why the harness has not failed on this — and why that is luck, not safety

The harness is not more careful than the probe; it is just **slower afterwards**. It installs dependencies and then runs a ~41-minute suite, so by the time the first test's fixture reaches `_assert_project_capabilities`, minutes have elapsed and GreenHopper is up. The probe asks in the first second and sees the real state.

So the harness's margin is incidental. If a run reached that fixture faster (dependency cache warm, fewer collected tests, a reordering) or the plugin initialised slower, `_assert_project_capabilities` would raise **`PROVISIONING FAILED: this instance exposes no ['Epic Link', 'Epic Name'] field(s)`** and its own message would tell the reader to *"Re-run the capability map against the current image and update `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` if the instance genuinely renamed them"* — i.e. it would be diagnosed as the **3fe5 image degrade** when the true cause is timing. A misattributing flake, and an expensive one: it points the next reader at the image and the declared contract instead of at readiness.

This is the same family as 3fe5 itself. 3fe5's lesson was that an unverifiable contract must not pass vacuously; this is the mirror — a contract asserted **too early** fails loudly for the wrong reason.

## Fix

Gate on the CAPABILITY, not a proxy. After `serverInfo` goes green, poll `/rest/api/2/field` until every name in `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` is present, under its own bounded budget, and fail with the inventory dump when it never arrives. `serverInfo` is the wrong predicate for anything depending on a plugin's fields.

Best placed in the readiness helper both tiers share (`conftest.wait_for_jira_dc_ready`) so the workflow step and the fixture cannot diverge, with the workflow-level curl loop kept as the cheap first gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] readiness for the live-DC tiers requires every `_REQUIRED_FIELDS` name to be present in
      `/rest/api/2/field`, not merely a 200 from `serverInfo`
- [x] the wait has its own bounded budget, and on expiry fails with the observed field inventory in the
      message so the failure is self-diagnosing
- [x] `_assert_project_capabilities`'s message no longer attributes a missing Epic field to an image
      degrade without first distinguishing "not registered yet" from "not offered by this image"
- [x] the probe workflow and the harness workflow share one readiness definition, so they cannot drift
- [x] a test pins that a field-inventory response containing only system fields is treated as NOT ready
      rather than as a degraded image

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py -q
    make lint && make typecheck

The load-bearing assertion is the negative one: a system-only inventory must read as "not ready". Without it this stays a latent flake that only appears when a run happens to be fast.
baseline.summary: Live-DC readiness (serverInfo 200) is too weak for 3fe5's declared field contract; a timing flake would be misattributed to an image degrade

Operator-approved early removal (pre-1.0 breaking pass #3), 2026-08-12. Source: the DEPRECATION REMOVAL-READINESS SURVEY, comment #11 on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1), Tier 2 item 2 — "strongest candidate for the next breaking window". Operator ruling (verbatim): "The two best candidates and the one ready now are all approved for removal."

## What

Remove the three deprecated single-pass review PUBLIC entry points (story 316a, deprecated 31f352d535, shipped v0.11.0):

- CLI verb `rebar review` — intercept `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:50,512-514` + handler `_review` at `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:133-207`.

## Context / Problem

Every other story in this epic is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake transport. That is the right tier for each of them, but it cannot exercise the failure modes that only appear against a real tracker: actual JQL evaluation over two projects, real per-project permissions and key allocation, real issue creation, and — the one that matters most — whether a pass scoped to one project can contaminate another. A multi-project bridge that is wrong in that direction writes real issues into the wrong project, which is expensive to detect and worse to undo. This story is the justified live canary the shared test-design standard allows for external-service mapping, run once the functionality is otherwise complete.

## Approach

Rehearse the whole feature live, against an **isolated store copy**, with dry-run gating at every step.

**Isolation comes first.** The rehearsal never runs against the production tickets branch. A copy of the tickets branch is published to an encrypted S3 remote — the capability delivered by epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`, which is why this epic depends on it — and the rehearsal store points its `sync.remote` at that copy. Before any mutating command, the harness asserts the configured remote is the S3 copy and not the production remote, and aborts otherwise. This is a precondition assertion, not a comment: it runs first and fails the test if the store is misconfigured.

**Dry-run gating is the contamination control.** Each scenario runs `bridge preview` first and asserts the previewed mutation set contains **only** targets in the intended project, with an empty intersection against every other configured project. Only then does `bridge sync` run. A preview that names a target outside the intended project fails the scenario before anything is written — which is the same fail-closed posture as the cross-project guard, applied at the harness level.

**Project configuration.** The mapping is loaded with the two live Jira Cloud projects, `REB` and `DIG`, plus dummy projects that exist only in the mapping and never in Jira — these exercise the "configured but empty" and "unknown to the tracker" paths without consuming real projects. Repo configurations deliberately vary: one project mapped to a single repo, one mapped to two repos, and one mapped to none, so the defaulting behaviour is observed across all three shapes rather than only the common one.

**Cleanup is designed in, not bolted on.** Every issue the rehearsal creates carries a run-scoped label. Cleanup is a single JQL sweep over that label across both live projects, and the run is not considered finished until a follow-up query for the label returns zero issues in each project. The label is generated per run so a failed earlier run cannot cause a later one to delete issues it did not create.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_multi_project/` (new) — the rehearsal harness and its scenarios
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — the operator runbook for performing and cleaning up the rehearsal

## Testing

Tier: a live end-to-end rehearsal against real Jira Cloud, which the shared standard permits for external-service mapping when a fake cannot reach the mechanism — here, genuine cross-project isolation. It is gated to an opt-in external suite so ordinary CI never touches live Jira.

Scenarios, each preview-gated then applied:

- **Inbound from both projects.** An issue created in `REB` and one in `DIG` are both ingested in a
  single pass; each resulting ticket records the project it came from and the repos mapped to that
  project.
- **Outbound to both projects.** Two rebar tickets, one per project, each land as an issue in their
  own project and nowhere else.
- **Not-synced.** A ticket with an explicit empty project produces no issue in either project, and no
  outbound mutation naming it appears in the preview.
- **Legacy resolution.** A ticket with the project field absent syncs to the recorded legacy default
  and to no other project.
- **Repo-config variety, both directions.** Inbound tickets from the single-repo, two-repo and
  zero-repo projects receive exactly those repo lists; outbound tickets created under each config
  reach the correct project regardless of their repos value, confirming repos never influences
  routing.
- **Contamination guard, the negative control.** An update aimed at a project absent from the mapping
  raises `CrossProjectTargetError` in preview and writes nothing — verified by querying both live
  projects afterwards and confirming no issue changed.
- **Promote-only.** Setting a project on an unbound ticket then syncing creates the issue; attempting
  to change a bound ticket's project is refused and the existing binding is unchanged.
- **Capability stamp.** With two projects in the mapping, `.store-compat.json` carries
  `multi-project-bridge`, and a binary lacking that capability refuses to write to the rehearsal
  store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The rehearsal aborts before any mutation if the configured remote is not the S3 store copy;
      checked by pointing it at a non-S3 remote and asserting it exits non-zero having written
      nothing.
- [ ] Issues created in `REB` and `DIG` are both ingested in one pass with the correct source project
      and repos recorded; checked by querying both live projects and asserting both tickets' fields.
- [ ] Rebar-created tickets targeting each project land in that project only; checked by querying
      both projects and asserting each issue exists in exactly one.
- [ ] A ticket with an explicit empty project creates no issue in either project; checked by a
      post-run query of both projects for the run label finding no issue for it.
- [ ] All three repo configurations produce the expected repos on inbound tickets and correct routing
      on outbound ones; checked per configuration.
- [ ] An update targeting an unmapped project is refused in preview and changes nothing live; checked
      by comparing both projects' issue state before and after.
- [ ] Every scenario's preview contained only targets in its intended project; checked by asserting
      an empty intersection against every other configured project for each preview.
- [ ] All issues created by the run are removed and a JQL query for the run label returns zero
      results in both `REB` and `DIG`; checked as the final step of the run.
baseline.summary: Live multi-project rehearsal against REB and DIG on an isolated S3 store copy

# Intermittent bridge_run_failures during 2026-08-26->28 sweep window

## Impact
The reconcile-bridge recorded **5 isolated single-hour failures** over the sweep window. Each self-cleared, so no sustained outage, but the pattern is recurring and there is no open ticket tracking it. Unlike the closed sustained-outage bug eab8 (exceedable-giant-mussel, a pydantic `SecretStr` import regression fixed 2026-08-18), these are sparse transient failures with a different signature.

## Evidence — CloudWatch (rebar/host:bridge_run_failures, Sum>0 per hour, PDT)
- 2026-08-26 20:00
- 2026-08-27 15:00
- 2026-08-27 19:00
- 2026-08-27 22:00
- 2026-08-28 01:00

Alarm `rebar-bridge-run-failures` (2-of-2 hourly datapoints > 0) flapped ALARM->OK three times:
- 08-27 19:09 -> 19:47 PDT
- 08-27 22:10 -> 23:09 PDT
- 08-28 01:12 -> 02:10 PDT

## Root-cause status — RESOLVED: env_integration (disk-pressure)
Attributed to ENOSPC during the box-wide disk-fill incident P1 `5a05-0e52-33a0-48bf` (rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high). All 5 failures fall inside the 5a05 disk-pressure window (alarm open since 08-26 17:55 unrecovered; root-disk ~18 flaps, peak 98%, 08-26..08-28). Under a full disk, a state write or the store git commit (reconcile child), or the strict commit-and-push delivery child, hard-fails to OPERATIONAL_FAILURE; the next hour, pressure eased, the pass succeeds, matching the scattered self-clearing signature. No bridge/reconciler code defect: failing loud under ENOSPC is correct. See the RCA + final comment. Orchestrator accepted the temporal correlation in lieu of unavailable on-box journald.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] Pull the reconcile-bridge journald/log lines for the 5 timestamps above and
      classify the failure(s).
      provenance: environment=production-box-observability rebar-tracker-plus-cloudwatch-metrics; principal=copilot-cli-reconciler-debug-session; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=static-analysis — on-box journald was not executable from this session because the box ships no bridge log group to CloudWatch and this session has no on-box access, so the failure classification was established by temporally correlating the 5 CloudWatch failure timestamps to the 5a05 disk-fill window recorded in ledger b2dc, which the orchestrator accepted in lieu of journald.
- [x] Determine whether they are disk-pressure-induced (correlate with the data-disk incident)
      or an independent transient (network/Jira/auth), and fix the class or document as benign.
      Determined DISK-PRESSURE-INDUCED: all 5 failures fall inside the 5a05 disk-fill window;
      documented as env_integration (benign, no reconciler defect, will not recur once 5a05 is
      remediated). Follow-up fe28-c6d0-b20c-4571 files the optional monitoring-contract enhancement.

## Notes
Filed by a READ-ONLY AWS ops sweep; no AWS mutation performed.

# P1.4 (rev) — Bounded git growth via stock gc + non-destructive (union) recovery

> Supersedes `seek-algae-reign` (a240-d692-a86f-411c). The original epic proposed a
> bespoke operator `rebar gc` with hand-tuned reflog/prune windows to protect a
> reflog-only recovery net. Critical evaluation + 7 git experiments + two Opus
> reviews (principal-engineer + peer-comparison) showed that design is an outlier:
> no comparable tool builds it, and it treats a symptom (a recovery path that
> orphans commits into the reflog) instead of the cause. This epic implements the
> peer-aligned design instead. Full design trail: session_log (see relates_to).

## Context (problem + why the rewrite)

Every ticket mutation is a committed file on the orphan `tickets` branch. The write path forces `gc.auto=0` (`_store/event_append.py:74-84 _ensure_gc_auto_zero`, also `compact.py:61`, `txn.py:217/413`, `init.py:182`) for ONE reason: to keep git's reflog alive, because `_store/sync.py` `_do_reconverge` does `git reset --hard origin/tickets` in the "unrelated histories" path (~71-85), which **orphans local-only commits** and relies on the reflog to recover them (the warning at `sync.py:81` literally says "recoverable: git reflog"). No durable ref is saved before the reset. Cost: unbounded loose-object/pack growth with no safe reclaim, and a recovery net that depends on an ephemeral, gc-governed structure the operator cannot see.

## Validated facts (our experiments — see session_log)

- Reachable commits survive even `git gc --prune=now`; only `reset --hard` orphans
  + reflog-expiry can lose data (EXP-A/B).
- On the append-only branch `git gc` is ~96% repack/delta (2.5M -> 104K, 600 objects
  intact) and `--prune` reclaims ~nothing; "deleted"/compacted blobs stay reachable
  from history so `--compact-first` reclaims nothing for gc (EXP-E/G).
- `git gc` produces cruft packs by default on git >= 2.41 (EXP-F).
- A durable ref makes an orphaned commit survive a FULL reflog wipe + `gc --prune=now`
  (EXP-H) — i.e. reachability, not the reflog, is the durable guarantee.

## Prior art (verifiable references — the patterns we follow)

- **git-bug** — leaves `gc.auto` on, ships NO gc command, recovers by DAG **union
  merge (fast-forward-only, both parents kept), never `reset --hard`**; batches many
  ops into one blob/commit (operationPack):
  https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/entity_actions.go ,
  https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/operation_pack.go
- **git-appraise** — git-notes unioned via `cat_sort_uniq` (never drops); before its
  one rewrite path it **archives the old head to a ref "to keep history from being
  garbage collected"** (ref-reachability, not reflog):
  https://github.com/google/git-appraise/blob/master/repository/git.go ,
  https://github.com/google/git-appraise/blob/master/review/review.go
- **git-issue** — one-commit-per-change, stock gc, no bespoke maintenance:
  https://github.com/dspinellis/git-issue
- **jujutsu (jj)** — recovery net is the op log materialized as real `refs/jj/keep/`
  refs; gc (`jj util gc`) is safe because it only collects objects unreachable from
  retained refs => "gc reachability == recovery guarantee" co-design:
  https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/operation-log/ ,
  https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/technical/architecture/
- **git itself** — `gc.auto` default (6700 loose) is the normal posture; cruft packs
  default since 2.37/2.41; `--prune=now` risks corruption under concurrent writers;
  `git maintenance` is the scale-up scheduler (disabling gc.auto WITHOUT out-of-band
  maintenance is the anti-pattern, cf. Scalar/GitLab):
  https://git-scm.com/docs/git-gc , https://git-scm.com/docs/git-maintenance ,
  https://github.blog/open-source/git/highlights-from-git-2-37/ ,
  https://devblogs.microsoft.com/devops/introducing-scalar/

## Design + the safety invariant

Adopt the universal peer pattern: **trust stock `git gc`, and make recovery non-destructive so the reflog is never load-bearing.**

> INVARIANT: after union recovery, every commit rebar cares about is ref-reachable;
> therefore stock `git gc` is safe by construction — it only ever collects truly
> unreachable objects.

This is jj's co-design lesson achieved for free: if commits are never orphaned, gc has nothing unsafe to collect.

## Implementation plan (work units)

- **WU-1 Re-enable stock gc.** Delete `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` (`event_append.py:74-84`)
  + its call (`:124`); drop the four `git config gc.auto 0` writes (`txn.py:217`,
  `txn.py:413`, `compact.py:61`, `init.py:182`). Set `gc.autoDetach=true` explicitly
  at init so a forked background gc never serializes a foreground write. Migration:
  idempotent `git config --unset gc.auto || true` at init/fsck.
- **WU-2 Union, don't discard.** Replace the `reset --hard origin/tickets` in
  `sync.py` Path 1 (unrelated histories) with
  `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories origin/tickets --no-edit`, **reusing the
  existing diverged-Path-3 conflict -> `merge --abort` -> keep-local -> hint
  handling** (extend proven code, do not invent). Keep `reset --hard` only for the
  ff-adopt path (discards nothing).
- **WU-3 Conflict policy for mutable shared root files.** uuid-named ticket dirs
  never collide, but `.bridge_state/bindings.json` and the reconciler lock/gate
  files are rewritten per pass and would conflict. Add a tickets-branch
  `.gitattributes` with `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`
  (the loser is a derived cache the reconciler rebuilds next pass — never ticket
  events). `merge=union` is WRONG (line-unions JSON into invalid JSON). NOTE:
  push.py already handles these conflicts today, so this only formalizes it.
- **WU-4 Docs + invariant.** Rewrite `docs/concurrency.md:165-196` and the `sync.py`
  module docstring (both assert the old reset+reflog design). State the safety
  invariant; note `git maintenance run` as the scale-up posture and that git's own
  30d-unreachable reflog window remains as a free backstop we no longer depend on.

## What this supersedes / drops from the old epic

- DROP the bespoke `rebar gc` command, `reflog expire --expire=<14d>`, the 14-day
  window rationale, `--compact-first` (reclaims nothing — EXP-G), and the
  `check_no_rebase_in_progress`-as-gc-guard (recovery is `reset --hard`, atomic, no
  marker — the guard cannot see it). None of this machinery exists in `src/` yet;
  this epic ensures it never gets built.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] WU-1: `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` + all four `gc.auto 0` writes removed; `gc.autoDetach=true` set at init; idempotent `--unset gc.auto` migration
- [ ] WU-2: `sync.py` Path 1 uses `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories` (reusing Path 3 conflict handling); ff-adopt path unchanged; no `reset --hard` that orphans local commits remains
- [ ] WU-3: tickets-branch `.gitattributes` with `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`; convergence test for two clones racing `bindings.json`
- [ ] WU-4: `docs/concurrency.md` + `sync.py` docstring rewritten to the invariant; `git maintenance` noted as scale-up
- [ ] Tests: union-recovery loses no tickets; `gc --prune=now` loses no reachable data; bindings.json race converges
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green
- [ ] `gc.auto` is re-enabled; stock background `git gc` reclaims loose/pack growth with
- [ ] Unrelated-history sync MERGES (never discards) local tickets; two clones each
- [ ] Docs assert the safety invariant; the reflog is no longer load-bearing.
baseline.summary: P1.4 (rev) — Bounded git growth via stock gc + union recovery
