## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` measures **771 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that fans the fetch out over several projects rewrites the query construction in `_build_snapshot` and will not fit in 29 lines.

## Approach

Extract the pagination cluster into a new `fetch_paging.py`: `_ACLI_CEILING` and `SilentTruncationError` (`:99-120`), `_extract_issues` (`:251-262`), `_iter_pages` (`:265-390`) and `collect` (`:392-399`).

The call chain is genuine and self-contained: `collect` calls `_iter_pages` (`:397`), which calls `_extract_issues` (`:296`) and raises `SilentTruncationError` (`:308,343,355`) against `_ACLI_CEILING` (`:354`). Nothing in the cluster calls back upward; `_build_snapshot` reaches it only through `_iter_pages` (`:554`). The new module's complete import list is `annotations` and a `TYPE_CHECKING` import of `TicketTransport` — the pagination code is otherwise pure.

This extraction is well matched to the incoming change, which rewrites the `queries` tuple at `_build_snapshot:548-554` into a per-project loop over `jqls_for` — all of which stays in `fetcher.py`.

**Three things must stay resident**, and getting any of them wrong breaks tests silently:

- `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (`:105`) stays — `_build_snapshot:550` uses it. Only `_ACLI_CEILING` moves.
- `_load_acli` and `_load_alert_store` stay — they carry **25** and **3** `patch.object(fetcher, ...)`
  sites respectively, and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move. Both are called
  from `_build_snapshot` (`:523,536`), which stays, so no patch site is disturbed.
- `fetcher.py` re-exports **all four** moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`,
  `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` — because every one of them is reached as an attribute
  of `fetcher` by existing tests, and an attribute access does not follow a moved symbol:
  - `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py:118,139`), plus further
    `fetcher._iter_pages` / `fetcher.collect` accesses in the same file and in
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py`;
  - `fetcher.SilentTruncationError`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_pagination_jql.py:133,165`) as well as the
    explicit `from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import SilentTruncationError` at
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:32`;
  - `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` (`test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:149`), which reads the constant
    directly to size its fixture. This one is easy to miss precisely because the constant looks
    private and unshared.

The re-export keeps roughly 48 existing references green across six test modules. Note that the two production mentions of `fetcher._iter_pages` — `_backend.py:62` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:139,153` — are **docstring prose** recording bug history, not runtime references, so no production module needs an edit.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~195 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — drops to ~606 lines, plus a re-export block

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. The risks are attribute presence and patch survival, so both are asserted rather than assumed:

- Attribute-surface assertion: `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
  both hold after the move, and `SilentTruncationError` still imports from `fetcher`.
- Patch survival: the tests that `patch.object(fetcher, "_load_acli")` and `"_load_alert_store"` pass
  unedited, proving those symbols stayed resident and are still resolved from `fetcher`'s globals.
- Truncation behaviour preserved: a fixture exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` still raises
  `SilentTruncationError` through the real `collect → _iter_pages` path — the contract most at risk
  from moving the constant away from its raiser.
- One-way import: `fetch_paging` must not import `fetcher`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fetcher.py` and `fetch_paging.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the module-size
      gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] All four moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`, `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` —
      still resolve as attributes of `fetcher`; checked by a test asserting each by attribute access,
      which covers the two existing `hasattr` assertions and the direct `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` read.
- [ ] `_load_acli`, `_load_alert_store` and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` remain defined in `fetcher.py`;
      checked by asserting each is in that module's own namespace, not merely importable.
- [ ] A fixture exceeding the ceiling still raises `SilentTruncationError` via the real paging path;
      checked by the existing pagination held-out test running unedited.
- [ ] `fetch_paging.py` does not import `fetcher`; checked by a test importing the two modules in
      both orders and asserting `fetcher` is absent from `fetch_paging`'s imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the pagination cluster from fetcher.py into fetch_paging.py

## Problem (resolved during this ticket's lifetime — this ticket now verifies the fix)

Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` (outrageous-uncultured-wildebeast) had a 10,135-character description, over the 8,000-char review admission cap (`7cf80009d9`). `review-plan` on the epic returned a single blocking P4 admission finding without running the LLM, so the epic could not earn a plan-review attestation — and the parent-first claim cascade therefore blocked EVERY child of the epic (discovered when `bloated-shadeful-lamprey`'s claim failed with "Parent error: no certified plan-review attestation").

## State at planning time

The epic's description has ALREADY been condensed by the session owner: the description field now measures 7389 characters (under the cap), and the full 10,135-char original is preserved verbatim as an epic comment dated 2026-08-13. Editing the epic changes only the epic's OWN material fingerprint — children's attestations bind their own material (material_diff.material_basis), not the parent's, so no sibling attestation was invalidated by the edit.

## Remaining work (verification only; no further edits prescribed)

Run the epic's plan review to earn the certified PASS the cascade requires, then prove the cascade is unblocked with a child claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `0e68-41eb-5782-4336`'s description field measures at most 8,000 characters; checked by reading the field and reporting the measured length.
- [x] `rebar review-plan 0e68-41eb-5782-4336` admits the plan — no P4 admission finding in the result; checked by inspecting the review output's blocking list.
- [x] `rebar review-plan 0e68-41eb-5782-4336` returns a certified PASS with zero blocking findings and a persisted, signed plan-review attestation (checked with `--status`; if a PASS fails to persist, `rebar sign-review` is the recovery), before the claim check below.
- [x] A child of the epic can be claimed without the parent cascade failing; checked by `rebar claim bloated-shadeful-lamprey` exiting 0 (its own plan-review attestation is already certified and its material unchanged).
baseline.summary: Oversized epic description blocks the parent-first claim cascade

# WS4 — Gate dispatch entry + source separation

## Why
The capability must be OFF by default and SOURCE-SEPARATED so it is inert when disabled, while preserving the existing public surface. This story adds the dispatch entry (parallel to plan-review) and isolates the code into its own optional package, retiring the throwaway single-pass route.

## What
- `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict(ctx, cfg, *, target_ticket=None, runner=None, repo_root=None)` running WS3's `gates/code-review.yaml` in-memory (parallel to `produce_plan_review_verdict`), wiring the `CodeReviewBatchRunner` (constructed with the assembled diff context) + a `RunnerAgentStep` + a `MemoryRecorder`, and returning the typed `code_review_verdict`.
- Source-separate into the optional `rebar.llm.code_review` package (already created in WS1-WS3); PRESERVE the public surface — `rebar.llm.review_code(...)`, the MCP `review_code` tool, and `rebar review-code` keep names/signatures and `review_result` output — via the re-export shim in `code_review/__init__.py`.
- RETIRE the single-pass `evidence + aggregate_findings`-only route (the gate replaces it); record the one-way-door removal in an ADR. When `single_pass.py` is retired, `code_review/__init__.py` is REWRITTEN so the public `review_code`/`select_code_reviewers` are provided by the GATE-backed shim (translating `code_review_verdict → review_result`), NOT lazily re-exported from `single_pass`: drop `"single_pass"` from `_SUBMODULES`, replace the `__getattr__` single-pass re-export with the gate shim, and a test asserts `review_code` still resolves + returns a `review_result` after retirement.

## Implementation sequencing — thin vertical slice first (resolves the G5 "too many concerns" BLOCK)
WS4 lands as ordered slices, each independently testable, smallest-risk-first:
1. **Slice 1 (MVP — the vertical slice):** register `code_review_verdict.schema.json` + `produce_code_review_verdict` (the ENABLED path) + the offline enabled-state test (FakeRunner → a schema-valid verdict for a sample diff). This proves the gate produces a verdict end-to-end before any surface change.
2. **Slice 2:** the `[code_review] enabled` flag + the disabled no-op path + the ZERO-LLM-call disabled test.
3. **Slice 3:** the `review_code` shim translation (`code_review_verdict → review_result` via `finalize_findings`) preserving the library/CLI/MCP surface + their tests.
4. **Slice 4:** retire `single_pass.py` + rewrite the `__init__` shim (drop it from `_SUBMODULES`) + the ADR + the docs/CLI-help stale-reference audit.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — `produce_code_review_verdict`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/code_review_verdict.schema.json` — the NEW typed verdict schema (registered + wired into OUTPUT_SCHEMAS or CONTRACT_SCHEMAS).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/` — the verdict finalizer + the disabled-path shim; `single_pass.py` is retired (the gate path supersedes it).
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — public surface unchanged.
- `docs/adr/` — ADR for retiring the single-pass demo; `docs/`/CLI-help stale-reference audit.
- OUT OF SCOPE: detectors (WS5), Gerrit (WS6).

## Sidecar mechanism (resolves the G6 BLOCK + the T1/T3/T8 sidecar advisories)
Plan-review's `sidecar.emit()` anchors on `verdict['ticket_id']` (the event-store key) and builds a plan-review-specific payload — code review reviews a DIFF, which has no ticket. So WS4 does NOT call `plan_review.sidecar.emit()` directly. Instead:
- The typed `code_review_verdict` (the return value) is the PRIMARY artifact — always produced.
- A sidecar EVENT is emitted ONLY when `produce_code_review_verdict` is given a `target_ticket` (e.g. a ticket-scoped review, or WS6's Gerrit path that associates a change with a ticket): a thin `code_review` sidecar emit reuses the `REVIEW_RESULT` event TYPE (not a new format) anchored on that ticket, with a code-review payload (verdict/blocking/advisory/coaching/coverage). Mirrors plan-review's emit but takes the anchor explicitly rather than reading `verdict['ticket_id']`.
- The diff-only path (the `rebar review-code` CLI / MCP `review_code` on a `(base,head)`/diff, no ticket) emits NO event — the verdict dict is the sole artifact. This is the v1 default; the sidecar event is the ticket-scoped extension.

## Prerequisite (WS3, CLOSED — shipped artifacts this story builds on)
WS3 already shipped (closed) the gate's runtime; WS4 wires the dispatch over it, it does NOT re-build it:
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the v3 workflow: `assemble_diff → triggers → base → round_a(batch) → union → round_b(batch) → merge → verify → decide → coach → verdict`; its terminal step (`code_review_coach` op) returns `{verdict, blocking, advisory, coaching, coverage}`.
- `code_review.batch_runner.CodeReviewBatchRunner(context: str)` — the `BatchRunner` (parallel to `ProductionBatchRunner`) that runs each included overlay's own prompt with the injected diff context; `produce_code_review_verdict` constructs it with the assembled diff context and passes it as `run_workflow(..., batch_runner=...)` (the `BatchRunRequest` seam is unchanged — the interpreter builds the request; the runner just executes per-overlay).
- `code_review.workflow_ops` scripted ops + the `code_review_findings`/`code_review_coach`/`code_review_base_output` contracts are registered.

## Re-export shim translation contract (resolves the G6 shim data-flow BLOCK)
`review_code()` must keep returning a `review_result` (its public contract), but the gate produces a `code_review_verdict` (a different shape). The shim's data-flow is pinned:
- **ENABLED:** `review_code(...)` assembles the diff context, calls `produce_code_review_verdict`,
  then TRANSLATES the `code_review_verdict` → `review_result` (reusing `findings.finalize_findings`
  so the result is schema-valid). Field mapping per blocking/advisory kernel finding →
  `common.finding`: `severity` ← the Pass-3 `severity`; `dimension` ← `criteria[0]` (else
  `"code-review"`); `detail` ← the `finding` claim text (+ any `merged_from` appended); `citations`
  ← a single best-effort file citation `{kind:"file", path, line_start}` parsed from `location`
  via the assembler's location parser (the `evidence` strings are folded into `detail`, since
  `common.citation` is a structured object, NOT a free string). Top-level: `summary` ← a one-line
  `"<verdict>: N blocking, M advisory"`; `reviewers` ← the distinct `reviewer_id`s carried on the
  findings (the overlays/base that produced them — available on each finding, not a separate
  verdict field); the raw `code_review_verdict` (incl. `coaching`/`coverage`) is attached under a
  `verdict` key. So `review_code()` does NOT keep the old single-pass path — it is a thin
  translator over the gate.
- **DISABLED:** `review_code()` returns a valid EMPTY `review_result` (`findings: []`) + a
  `summary`/note "code-review capability disabled", never an error/stub, and makes ZERO LLM calls.

## Feature flag (resolves the T8 flag advisories)
The capability is gated by `[code_review] enabled = false` in `rebar.toml` (default OFF), overridable by `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_ENABLED` (same truthy parsing as the other env gates). When disabled, `produce_code_review_verdict` returns the inert disabled result (see back-out) WITHOUT running the workflow (ZERO LLM calls).

## code_review_verdict schema (resolves the T8/T3/E1 schema advisories)
A NEW registered schema `code_review_verdict.schema.json` (parallel to `plan_review_verdict`): `{verdict: "PASS"|"BLOCK", blocking: [finding], advisory: [finding], coaching: [note], coverage: {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls, llm_ran}}`. `finding`/`note` reuse the shared `common.schema.json` shapes; `additionalProperties: true`. Wired into the schema registry (the every-schema-file-is-wired guard) and pinned by a test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `produce_code_review_verdict` runs `gates/code-review.yaml` on the v3 engine (CodeReviewBatchRunner + RunnerAgentStep + MemoryRecorder) and returns the typed `code_review_verdict`; OFF by default (`[code_review].enabled` / `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_ENABLED`), inert when disabled.
- [ ] ENABLED-state offline test: with the flag ON + a FakeRunner, `produce_code_review_verdict` returns a well-formed `code_review_verdict` (validates against the schema) for a sample diff.
- [ ] DISABLED-state test: with the flag OFF, `produce_code_review_verdict` returns the inert disabled result and makes ZERO LLM calls (FakeRunner call-count == 0); and `review_code()` returns a valid EMPTY `review_result` (+ a 'capability disabled' note), never an error/stub.
- [ ] Sidecar: a `target_ticket`-scoped call emits a `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar on that ticket; a diff-only call emits NO event (the verdict is returned). A test exercises both.
- [ ] `code_review_verdict.schema.json` is registered + wired into the schema registry; a test validates a real verdict against it.
- [ ] The public surface is preserved: `rebar.llm.review_code(...)`, MCP `review_code`, and `rebar review-code` keep names/signatures/`review_result`; a test exercises each (enabled→gate path, disabled→empty result).
- [ ] The single-pass GATE PATH is unreachable (no `evidence + aggregate_findings`-only route runs when enabled); an ADR records the removal.
- [ ] Stale references to the single-pass `code_review.py`/`single_pass.py` flow in docs / CLI-help / `docs/` are audited + updated.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` + the test suite pass.

## Back-out (one-way door — resolves the E1/T4/T7/COH contradiction)
The single-pass code is DELETED, so reverting the feature-flag default does NOT restore single-pass behavior — it makes the gate INERT. When OFF, the preserved `review_code()` surface returns a valid empty `review_result` (zero findings + a 'capability disabled' note), NEVER an error/stub. The ADR states honestly that retirement is a one-way door and the flag-default is the INERTNESS control, NOT a behavior-restore. (This supersedes any earlier "reverting the flag restores prior behavior" phrasing — that phrasing is removed as incorrect.)

## Rationale (resolves the G6 approach-rationale advisory)
A dedicated `rebar.llm.code_review` package (vs inlining in `llm/__init__` or reusing plan-review's dispatch) is chosen because: (a) source-separation is an explicit AC (inert + isolated when disabled); (b) it mirrors the shipped `plan_review` package structure (registry/contracts/workflow_ops), so the two gates are symmetric and the kernel-consumer pattern is one shape; (c) it lets WS4 retire `single_pass.py` without touching unrelated modules. Sequencing within WS4: register the schema → add the verdict finalizer + dispatch (enabled path) → wire the flag + disabled shim → retire single_pass + audit docs.
baseline.summary: WS4: gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict + source-separation (re-export shim, retire single-pass, ADR)

## Context
A deterministic relocated-store experiment confirmed that `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py::code_root_for` conflates tracker storage with the code repository. `attach_commits` reaches it through `_lib_mutations.py`; with an absolute `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` outside the code checkout, valid code commit SHAs are checked against the tracker parent and rejected. Runtime tracing observed `git -C <tracker-parent> rev-parse` while the same SHA resolved at the code root.

## Plan
- Add a real-git held-out regression oracle with a code repository and independently relocated ticket store.
- Resolve commit validation from `config.repo_root(repo_root)` (explicit root, then `REBAR_ROOT`, then cwd Git top-level), while retaining tracker reads/writes through `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`.
- Remove the obsolete tracker-parent code-root helpers so the invalid derivation cannot remain as unused prior art.
- Preserve all-or-nothing rejection for unknown SHAs and the default in-repo tracker path.
- Run RED to GREEN, exact-defect mutation, focused store and attach suites, lint, typecheck, and original CLI replication.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A valid code commit is accepted when the ticket store is outside the code worktree.
- [x] An unknown SHA remains rejected without recording a partial COMMITS event.
- [x] Default in-repo tracker behavior remains unchanged.
- [x] The held-out relocated-store test is observed RED before repair and GREEN after repair.
- [x] The exact tracker-parent mutation returns the held-out test to RED.
- [x] `code_root_for` and `unresolvable_shas` have no remaining production definitions or references, checked by repository search.
- [x] Focused tests pass.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.

## Testing
- `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_commits_on_ticket.py tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py`
- `grep -R "code_root_for\|unresolvable_shas" src/rebar` must return no matches.
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`

baseline.description:
Supersedes bug e983 (config_manual fire-and-forget) by generalizing it into an infra-health readiness gate for the review/landing pipeline.

PRINCIPLE: an unhealthy infra precondition (unapplied/invalid config, LLM-provider outage, GitHub outage, env error) makes LLM Review UNSOUND. Treat these as INFRA-CLASS conditions (per Zuul RETRY_LIMIT/NODE_FAILURE): block fail-closed, do NOT cast a content vote, and AUTO-RECOVER (re-run blocked reviews) when the signal returns healthy — no human recheck (author changed nothing; only the environment did).

DESIGN (OSS-grounded):
- Health registry: named checks, each tri-state healthy/unhealthy/unknown (never conflate 'check errored' with 'healthy'). Signals: config-applied (live-vs-desired refs-meta/replication probe), config-valid, llm-provider (Anthropic reachable/quota), github (API/Actions/mirror), deploy-host/replication, environment.
- Aggregator: per-signal blocking vs advisory severity; fail-closed on any blocking-unhealthy. (cf. Argo health assessment; K8s readiness gate.)
- Consumption points, one health source: (a) REVIEW boundary — review-bot ABSTAINS (casts no LLM-Review content vote) when infra unhealthy, instead of erroring/false-voting; (b) LANDING boundary — dedicated bot-cast Infra-Ready submit-requirement blocks submit with an explicit per-signal message. Keeps env-readiness OFF the code-content labels (avoids the 'environment masquerading as a review vote' anti-pattern).
- Recovery = infra-class retry loop: on signal recovery, auto-re-run blocked reviews + re-eval gate; bounded (RETRY_LIMIT), windowed (thundering-herd), same-patchset re-vote that cleanly REPLACES the stale -1, terminal alert on exhaustion. (cf. Zuul infra-class auto-retry.)
- Reliability: independent tri-state observation (Ansible/Puppet lesson: apply exit-0 != converged; only a zero-diff re-read proves it); Terraform-style tri-state so a probe ERROR never false-clears; marker bound to the config revision it was computed against (Terraform stale-plan rejection).
- Waiver + break-glass: audited per-signal/global override; guard-the-guard on who may waive (Gatekeeper); a guaranteed break-glass reachable when the gate itself is wedged.
- Rollout: WARN/detect-only first (emit signals, do not block) until detection proven reliable, THEN flip to fail-closed. Staged config-first.

CONTEXT: closes the e983 root cause properly (durable reconciled status, not a fire-and-forget event) and also turns today's ad-hoc LLM/GitHub-outage failures into one loud, self-healing, auditable signal. Related: 0e15 (--class propagation), and the plan-review calibration miss on epic 86ac/ed13 that let consumer-migration advisories ship sub-threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A health registry exposes each named infra check in tri-state (healthy / unhealthy / unknown) and never reports a probe error as healthy; verified by a unit test that feeds an errored probe and asserts the aggregate is unknown, not healthy.
- [ ] When any blocking signal is unhealthy the review-bot casts no LLM-Review content vote (abstains) and the Infra-Ready submit-requirement blocks submit with a per-signal message; verified by an offline test asserting no content vote is emitted and submit is blocked.
- [ ] On signal recovery a blocked review is automatically re-run under a bounded retry (RETRY_LIMIT) with windowed replay, replacing the stale vote without human recheck; verified by a test that drives unhealthy then healthy and asserts exactly one bounded re-run.
- [ ] Each health observation is bound to the config revision it was computed against and a stale observation is rejected rather than allowed to false-clear; verified by a test that presents a stale-revision observation and asserts rejection.
- [ ] Rollout ships in WARN/detect-only mode (signals emitted, submit not blocked) until a config flip enables fail-closed; verified by a test asserting detect-only emits signals without blocking and the flip enables blocking.
- [ ] An audited break-glass override can waive per-signal or global blocking and remains reachable when the gate itself is wedged; verified by a test exercising the waiver path and asserting the audit record is written.
baseline.summary: Infra-Ready health gate: fail-closed review/landing gate over infra-health signals with infra-class auto-recovery

baseline.description:
Build the one-time strip as a committed operational script, and prove it on a scratch clone before any window. **No new dependency**: `git-filter-repo` is deliberately not used. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why stock plumbing
`git fast-export --no-data --signed-tags=strip --export-marks=old.marks tickets` | filter | `git fast-import --export-marks=new.marks`. Verified on the real branch: the stream carries `M 100644 <sha> <path>` with **zero** inline blob data (26 MB stream for ~49,900 commits), so the filter is line-oriented text processing that never moves the ~1 GiB. No `deleteall`; no tags in a branch export (so `--signed-tags=strip` is a harmless no-op); merges ride `merge :n`; **empty commits are kept**, so DAG topology and every file's introduction point survive — which is exactly what ancestry-based authorship verification needs. filter-repo would prune them and reshape the graph.

**Proven result:** 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%), all commits and all merge commits preserved, HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths, ~30 s end to end.

## Required corrections (each was a real defect found in review)
1. Must run in a fresh **UNFILTERED** clone — `fast-import` hard-fails `fatal: blob not found` in a
   `blob:none` partial clone, and this host's `origin` is one.
2. Strip **both** `.bridge_state/` **and** `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` prefixes — B6 removes the
   latter at HEAD only; its 33 MB stays in history.
3. **Derive the re-add set DYNAMICALLY** — `git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state/` —
   never a hardcoded list. It is three files today but **A2-1 adds `get_rotation.json`**, so at window
   time it is four; a hardcoded list would fail the tree-identity assertion.
4. The filter must be **`data <n>`-length-aware**, not `grep -v`: commit messages live inside `data`
   blocks. (Today 0 of ~49,900 messages begin with `M `/`D `, but the script must not rely on that.)
5. Push with **`--force-with-lease`**, never `--force` — the remote tip moves constantly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a scratch unfiltered clone, the script produces a rewritten branch whose **commit count and
      merge-commit count are unchanged** (measured at run time, not hardcoded). Tier: **repo-level
      assertion in the dry-run harness**.
- [ ] `rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree}` **equals** the old tip tree after the dynamic re-add. Tier:
      **repo-level assertion**. This is the "not one byte of live content changed" invariant.
- [ ] The re-add set is discovered from `ls-tree`, proven by a fixture where a 4th `.bridge_state`
      file exists. Tier: **integration** with a synthetic 4-file store.
- [ ] Pack size drops to <=15% of the original. Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] The filter preserves a commit message that begins with `M ` (adversarial fixture). Tier:
      **unit** on the stream filter.
- [ ] The script refuses to run in a partial clone, with a clear message. Tier: **integration**
      against a `--filter=blob:none` clone.
- [ ] All assertions run **before** any push; the script has no push step of its own.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reclaim-bridge-history.sh` (or `.py`), dry-run harness, tests

Scope: M. No code dependencies; must exist before A6-1.
baseline.summary: A6-0c: build and dry-run the history-strip script using stock git plumbing

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The inbound fetcher can only see one tracker project. `jqls_for(project)` builds exactly one pair of queries — active and recent-done — from a single key (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:78-90`), and `_validate_project_key` refuses an empty or malformed key outright rather than searching unscoped (`fetcher.py:63-75`, bug `626d`). A store that lists several projects in its mapping still ingests only one of them.

## Approach

Fan out: call the existing `jqls_for` once per project in the store mapping and union the results into the snapshot, rather than building a single `project IN (A,B)` query. Two concrete reasons. First, the per-query truncation ceiling (`_ACLI_CEILING = 1200` at `fetcher.py:91`, raising `SilentTruncationError`) stays scoped per project instead of becoming a shared budget that a single busy project could exhaust on behalf of the others. Second, it reuses `jqls_for` and `_validate_project_key` unchanged, so the JQL-injection guard that bug `626d` added keeps applying to every key with no new interpolation site.

Inbound-created tickets record their source project in `bridge_project` and get their `repos` defaulted from that project's mapping entry. The existing local-id derivation already encodes the project (`_jira_key_to_local_id`, `inbound_translate.py:120-124`, `DIG-123` → `jira-dig-123`), so ids stay unique across projects with no change; this story makes the association explicit on the ticket rather than only implicit in the id.

The CREATE event for an inbound ticket is written directly rather than through `create_core` (`apply_inbound_records.py:150-222`, which stamps `creation_channel` at `:221`), so the two new fields are stamped at that same site.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful verified fake fed production-shaped Jira fixtures. The fake must record the queries issued, because "one JQL pair per project" is itself the contract under test and is invisible to a result-only assertion.

- Happy path: a mapping with two projects issues exactly two query pairs — one per key — and the
  resulting snapshot contains issues from both.
- Postcondition: each ticket created from the fetch records the project its issue came from, and its
  `repos` equal that project's mapping entry.
- Edge: a project listed in the mapping that returns zero issues contributes nothing and does not
  fail the pass.
- Failure path: one project exceeding the per-query ceiling raises `SilentTruncationError` naming
  that project, and the ceiling is evaluated per project — a second project under the limit is not
  penalised by the first. This is the contrast case that proves the budget is not shared.
- Collateral invariant: a store whose mapping holds exactly one project issues the same query pair as
  before this change, so single-project behaviour is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mapping with two projects issues one JQL pair per project in a single pass; checked by a fake
      transport recording the issued queries and asserting the exact pair count and contents.
- [ ] Each inbound-created ticket records its source project and the repos from that project's
      mapping entry; checked by asserting both fields on tickets created from a two-project fixture.
- [ ] The truncation ceiling applies per project, not as a shared budget; checked by a test where one
      project exceeds it and a second under-limit project still ingests successfully.
- [ ] A single-project mapping issues an identical query pair to the pre-change behaviour; checked by
      a regression test comparing the recorded queries.
- [ ] A configured project returning zero issues does not fail the pass; checked by an empty-result
      fixture.
baseline.summary: Multi-project inbound fetch: per-project JQL fan-out and source-project recording

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` measures **771 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that fans the fetch out over several projects rewrites the query construction in `_build_snapshot` and will not fit in 29 lines.

## Approach

Extract the pagination cluster into a new `fetch_paging.py`: `_ACLI_CEILING` and `SilentTruncationError` (`:99-120`), `_extract_issues` (`:251-262`), `_iter_pages` (`:265-390`) and `collect` (`:392-399`).

The call chain is genuine and self-contained: `collect` calls `_iter_pages` (`:397`), which calls `_extract_issues` (`:296`) and raises `SilentTruncationError` (`:308,343,355`) against `_ACLI_CEILING` (`:354`). Nothing in the cluster calls back upward; `_build_snapshot` reaches it only through `_iter_pages` (`:554`). The new module's complete import list is `annotations` and a `TYPE_CHECKING` import of `TicketTransport` — the pagination code is otherwise pure.

This extraction is well matched to the incoming change, which rewrites the `queries` tuple at `_build_snapshot:548-554` into a per-project loop over `jqls_for` — all of which stays in `fetcher.py`.

**Three things must stay resident**, and getting any of them wrong breaks tests silently:

- `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (`:105`) stays — `_build_snapshot:550` uses it. Only `_ACLI_CEILING` moves.
- `_load_acli` and `_load_alert_store` stay — they carry **25** and **3** `patch.object(fetcher, ...)`
  sites respectively, and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move. Both are called
  from `_build_snapshot` (`:523,536`), which stays, so no patch site is disturbed.
- `fetcher.py` re-exports **all four** moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`,
  `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` — because every one of them is reached as an attribute
  of `fetcher` by existing tests, and an attribute access does not follow a moved symbol:
  - `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py:118,139`), plus further
    `fetcher._iter_pages` / `fetcher.collect` accesses in the same file and in
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py`;
  - `fetcher.SilentTruncationError`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_pagination_jql.py:133,165`) as well as the
    explicit `from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import SilentTruncationError` at
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:32`;
  - `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` (`test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:149`), which reads the constant
    directly to size its fixture. This one is easy to miss precisely because the constant looks
    private and unshared.

The re-export keeps roughly 48 existing references green across six test modules. Note that the two production mentions of `fetcher._iter_pages` — `_backend.py:62` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:139,153` — are **docstring prose** recording bug history, not runtime references, so no production module needs an edit.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~195 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — drops to ~606 lines, plus a re-export block

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. The risks are attribute presence and patch survival, so both are asserted rather than assumed:

- Attribute-surface assertion: `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
  both hold after the move, and `SilentTruncationError` still imports from `fetcher`.
- Patch survival: the tests that `patch.object(fetcher, "_load_acli")` and `"_load_alert_store"` pass
  unedited, proving those symbols stayed resident and are still resolved from `fetcher`'s globals.
- Truncation behaviour preserved: a fixture exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` still raises
  `SilentTruncationError` through the real `collect → _iter_pages` path — the contract most at risk
  from moving the constant away from its raiser.
- One-way import: `fetch_paging` must not import `fetcher`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fetcher.py` and `fetch_paging.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the module-size
      gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] All four moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`, `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` —
      still resolve as attributes of `fetcher`; checked by a test asserting each by attribute access,
      which covers the two existing `hasattr` assertions and the direct `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` read.
- [ ] `_load_acli`, `_load_alert_store` and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` remain defined in `fetcher.py`;
      checked by asserting each is in that module's own namespace, not merely importable.
- [ ] A fixture exceeding the ceiling still raises `SilentTruncationError` via the real paging path;
      checked by the existing pagination held-out test running unedited.
- [ ] `fetch_paging.py` does not import `fetcher`; checked by a test importing the two modules in
      both orders and asserting `fetcher` is absent from `fetch_paging`'s imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the pagination cluster from fetcher.py into fetch_paging.py

## Context / Problem
Live completion runs directly attribute 135-235 seconds to full ticket-store materialization. The store has about 5,500 ticket directories and 132,000 tracked files, so donor hardlinks avoid blob duplication but still perform work proportional to the inode tree. We need evidence for a stable read-only completion environment that pins tracker state cheaply while close, sidecar, and signature mutations continue against the normal live store.

## Approach
Use the tracker commit OID as the immutable read identity, because Git already preserves an immutable tree and the current implementation already resolves that OID before creating a checkout. Prove the boundary with Git plumbing against the real tracker plus a standard-library disposable Git fixture. The experiments will read objects lazily or extract only the selected real ticket directory; no full-store copy or production implementation is needed. Canonical parity is a fixture-specific observation, not a claim that arbitrary isolated tickets can resolve alias-form links without namespace context; the experiment must record that resolver dependency as a design gotcha.

## Scope
- Read-only Git plumbing against the configured `.tickets-tracker` repository.
- A temporary standard-library experiment harness under `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`.
- Ticket comments containing timestamped measurements and conclusions.
- No repository source, test, guidance, or architecture-document edits.

## Testing / Verification
- Benchmark at least 30 invocations of `git rev-parse HEAD`, pinned `git ls-tree`, and batched `git cat-file` reads against the real tracker; record median, p90, and maximum wall time.
- Extract the selected real ticket directory from a captured commit and compare its canonical reduced-state hash with its live counterpart using `rebar.reducer.reduce_ticket`; separately test and record the alias-link case that requires sibling or pinned resolver context.
- In a disposable Git fixture, capture revision A, commit a live mutation producing revision B, and assert reads through A remain byte-identical while B exposes the mutation.
- In the fixture, run `git diff --name-only A..B` and semantic predicates for exact-ticket changes, new-child membership, unrelated changes, and non-ancestor history.
- Record command output, timestamps, environment facts, and cleanup outcome as ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Revision-capture timing for at least 30 trials is recorded on this ticket; checked from the harness summary for `git rev-parse HEAD`.
- [x] Pinned Git-tree lookup timing is recorded on this ticket; checked from the harness summaries for `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file`.
- [x] The selected real ticket fixture reduces to the same canonical target-state hash as its captured live counterpart; checked by the harness equality assertion. This fixture-specific result does not claim arbitrary alias-linked tickets work without pinned resolver context, which is recorded separately as a gotcha.
- [x] Pinned reads stay byte-identical after a later live commit; checked by the disposable revision-A/revision-B assertion.
- [x] The live view exposes the later mutation; checked by the disposable revision-B assertion.
- [x] Scoped extraction time, file count, and bytes are recorded on this ticket; checked by the harness summary.
- [x] An exact ticket edit invalidates its recorded read dependency; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] A newly matching child invalidates the recorded child-query dependency; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] An unrelated ticket mutation leaves the relevant dependency set valid; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] A non-ancestor live revision fails closed; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] Primary-source OSS prior art and design gotchas are recorded on this ticket; checked by cited URLs in the research comment.
- [x] No repository files change; checked by `git status --short` in the dedicated worktree.
baseline.summary: Experiment with a pinned read-only ticket view for completion verification

## Outcome: NOT A BUG (mechanism disproved)

Originally filed on the hypothesis that the completion verifier attributes a suppressed governed call's COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to repository file content, corrupting its verdict. Under operator decision B5 (test-and-approve only if the mechanism is proven) the hypothesis was tested first. It did not reproduce. No contract change was implemented.

## Original hypothesis

The completion wrapper returns COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to every losing governed call in a same-response batch (src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py:151-154). The claim was that the model treats that synthetic result as the read_file payload and concludes the target file itself is the notice, as suspected during the close of bug 0707-59ae-7db6-489b.

## What was done

Four independently designed held-out oracles, 22 live runs total, on a disposable fixture repo containing a real tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py; the unmodified shipped system prompt src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; real pai_tools.filesystem_tools; bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 pinned at temperature 0.0. Where arms were compared, the only varied variable was the text of the synthetic result given to a losing governed call.

- Oracle 1, message-level injection, 8 runs: model re-issued the read, got real content,
  recorded met=true; under persistent read_file suppression it routed around via search_files
  and still recorded met=true.
- Oracle 2, the REAL wrap_completion_evidence_policy with no injection, 5 runs: genuine
  batching occurred and a read_file genuinely lost the batch at run_step 1 in every trial. No
  misattribution in any recorded evidence.
- Oracle 3, starved condition, 6 runs: the notice was the only thing returned for the target
  file. The verifier reported this accurately rather than as file content.
- Oracle 4, realistic worst case, 3 runs: all three recorded met=true with correct citations,
  one stating explicitly that the steering text was untrusted data and was disregarded.

## Findings

1. The claimed attribution mechanism did not occur in any of the 22 runs. The verifier
   consistently classifies the steering string as a tool-scheduling message, not as content.
2. The incident wording in 0707 is best explained as a paraphrase. The verifier's true
   statement that its calls "returned only a COMMIT steering message with no actual file
   content" reads, when summarised, as a claim about the file. The 0707 record preserved the
   conclusion, not the verifier's verbatim evidence string.
3. The proposed remedy was measured to regress. An affirmative, cannot-be-scored-as-content
   steering result raised suppressed-call counts from 6 to 12 and 49 across matched trials, and
   one trial died with UsageLimitExceeded having recorded no verdict at all.
4. A real, different defect was identified: a false unmet caused by evidence starvation when a
   suppressed governed read is never recovered. Filed as dd41-239d-6e09-4a86
   (rutile-massive-spoonbill), linked discovered_from this ticket, left open for operator
   approval because the indicated fix is a behavior change.

Evidence artifacts are preserved at /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/6f8df6b5/tmp/waterdogs-artifacts/ (oracle.py, oracle2.py, oracle3.py, oracle4.py, results*.json, fixture/). The full reproduction record is the first comment on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] The attribution hypothesis is tested against the real completion policy, not only by
      inspection, and the result is recorded on this ticket with the exact rig, model,
      temperature and run counts.
- [x] [operator-attested] The recorded evidence shows a governed evidence call genuinely losing a same-response
      batch, establishing that the hypothesis was tested under its own precondition.
- [x] The outcome is recorded as disproved, with the alternative explanation for the original
      incident wording stated.
- [x] [operator-attested] The counter-evidence against the proposed notice-rewording remedy is recorded, so the
      change is not reattempted blindly.
- [x] [operator-attested] The genuine defect found during the investigation is filed as its own ticket and linked
      discovered_from this one.
- [x] No production code, prompt, schema, or public surface is changed by this ticket.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier can mistake COMMIT steering for repository file content

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py::test_emitted_bpmn_has_no_illegal_ids` intermittently fails in CI as `worker 'gw0' crashed` / `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated`, with no traceback and no assertion — a killed xdist worker, not a test failure. Observed on unrelated Gerrit changes 2592, 2593 and 2594 within ~30 minutes on 2026-09-03. It costs every contributor a red `Verified` vote on work that is not at fault, and AGENTS.md forbids retrying a flake instead of root-causing it.

## Root cause (measured, confirmed in the tree)

`tests/e2e/conftest.py::bpmn_harness` is session-scoped and provisions the Node toolchain lazily inside the FIRST e2e test's setup: `subprocess.run([npm, "install"], …)` at `tests/e2e/conftest.py:52` and `subprocess.run([npm, "run", "build"], …)` at `tests/e2e/conftest.py:58`. Neither carries a `timeout=`, unlike every other subprocess in the same file (`:74` `timeout=60`, `:118` `timeout=150`), so their only bound is the global pytest-timeout: `timeout = 300` / `timeout_method = "thread"` at `pyproject.toml:719-720`, deliberately without `timeout_func_only`, so the budget covers fixture setup. The `thread` method calls `os._exit(1)` — documented in-tree at `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:774` — so an over-run kills the whole worker instead of reporting `Failed: Timeout`. In passing CI run 33811108275 that setup is the slowest span in the suite (101.26s / 120.93s / 89.69s across py3.11/3.12/3.13); 90-120s of a 300s budget is a 2.5-3.3x margin that npm-registry variance can consume. There is no `setup-node` step and no npm cache in `.github/workflows/`, so every run pays a cold registry install, and under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:782`) each worker runs the session-scoped fixture independently, so several can race the same `tests/e2e/js/node_modules`.

## Approach

Charge provisioning to the build, not to a test, and make the in-fixture fallback bounded and race-safe. This shape is chosen because it fixes both halves of the defect class in the place each one lives: the unbounded subprocess is a code defect in the fixture, and the cold install on the critical path is a build-ordering defect in the workflow.

Portability is the constraint that rules out a CI-only fix (blocking `project.portability`): the provisioning must still work in a checkout with no CI provider. So the primary path is a plain `make e2e-deps` target that any developer or any CI system can invoke, and the fixture keeps provisioning as a fallback — now with explicit `timeout=` values and a file lock — rather than being deleted.

Extract the provisioning into `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` (a small module beside the fixture, so it is directly callable from a test without spawning pytest); `tests/e2e/conftest.py` calls it and converts its error into the existing self-skip. A `fcntl.flock` on a lock file in `tests/e2e/js/` serializes concurrent xdist workers, degrading to no lock where `fcntl` is absent (single-process correctness is unaffected).

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` (new) — `provision_toolchain()` with explicit per-step `timeout=`,
  a step-naming `ToolchainProvisioningError`, and the cross-process lock.
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py` — `bpmn_harness` delegates to it and self-skips with the named message.
- `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` (new) — the tests below.
- `Makefile` — `e2e-deps` target: `npm ci` + `npm run build` in `tests/e2e/js`.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — an npm cache keyed on
  `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json` plus a `make e2e-deps` step before the pytest step at
  `:781`.

## Testing

A stub `npm` on `PATH` (a shell script that sleeps, or that succeeds then sleeps) makes every case deterministic and fast; no network and no real Node install is involved.

- Happy path: `provision_toolchain` against a stub `npm` that exits 0 returns without error and
  the build step runs.
- Failure path (the one that reproduces the bug): a stub `npm` that stalls past the explicit
  `timeout=` makes `provision_toolchain` raise within the bound, with a message naming the
  step — `npm install` for the install stall, `npm run build` for the build stall — instead of
  running unbounded into the 300s pytest budget.
- Concurrency path: two independent processes call `provision_toolchain` on the same directory
  at once against a stub `npm` that records enter/exit; their install spans do not overlap.
- Build-ordering: assert the Makefile exposes `e2e-deps` and that the workflow invokes it in a
  step preceding the pytest step, and caches on `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json`.

Run with `pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q`, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both provisioning subprocesses carry an explicit `timeout=`, and exceeding one raises an
      error whose message names the provisioning step (`npm install` / `npm run build`) — never
      a worker kill and never a bare `node down`. Checked by
      `pytest tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py -q`, whose stalled-`npm` cases assert the
      call returns within the bound with the step named.
- [x] Toolchain provisioning is available as a portable pre-pytest step that needs no CI
      provider, and the in-fixture path still provisions in a checkout that never ran it.
      Checked by running `make e2e-deps` from a clean worktree, and by the fixture test that
      provisions from an empty directory with a stub `npm`.
- [x] CI caches the npm store keyed on `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json` and provisions with
      `npm ci` rather than `npm install`. Checked by the workflow/Makefile assertions in
      `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py` and by `make lint` (actionlint).
- [x] Concurrent provisioning by two or more xdist workers is serialized. Checked by the
      two-process test asserting non-overlapping install spans.
- [x] Verified in real time, not by waiting for a recurrence: with `tests/e2e/js/node_modules`
      and `tests/e2e/js/dist` removed, `make e2e-deps` followed by
      `pytest tests/e2e -n 4 --dist worksteal -q` completes with no worker kill and no
      `node down`, and the stalled-`npm` cases above show the diagnosable named failure instead.
      Both complete in one session.
baseline.summary: e2e Node toolchain is provisioned inside a test's timeout budget, killing an xdist worker

baseline.description:
# Cloud's `RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by `fetch_snapshot`'s three enrichment fail-opens

## Claim

Found in ticket 18a4's Phase-1 parity census (the fetcher-boundary axis).

DEFECT. Bug cabc's fix (ab7f, commit 30c522cde9) added `RunawayPaginationError` to Cloud's `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:29` and made its three readers re-raise it past their OWN fail-open handlers (`acli_graph.py:304, 394, 477`). That re-raise gets the error out of the transport — and straight into `fetcher.fetch_snapshot`'s three broad `except Exception` enrichment handlers (parent `fetcher.py:625`, comment `:672`, issuelink `:712`), which log a warning and degrade.

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; see the RCA comment)

`RunawayPaginationError` subclasses `RuntimeError`, NOT the core stall type. Live MRO:

    (RunawayPaginationError, RuntimeError, Exception, BaseException, object)
    issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError) == False

The three fetcher re-raise clauses match on the CORE type (`except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` at `fetcher.py:621, 668, 708`), so they MISS Cloud's error and control falls to the broad `except Exception` beneath each. Driving the real `fetch_snapshot` with a stub whose `get_parent_map` raises `RunawayPaginationError` produced `WARNING ... parent enrichment failed (RunawayPaginationError(...)); snapshot written without parent data (degraded)` and a written snapshot — no propagation. A stalled Cloud cursor therefore still yields a silently degraded snapshot that the differ treats as authoritative (missing parents read as parentless; missing issuelinks read as "no links", so link removals become undetectable).

Intended behaviour is stated authoritatively at `_backend.py:49-70` ("Readers must re-raise this PAST their fail-open handlers", naming bug cabc as an instance of the class), `acli_graph.py:29-38`, and `fetcher.py:511-516`. cabc's fix is incomplete at the layer above the transport.

## Fix

Ticket 18a4 fixed exactly this hole on the DC side and built the mechanism this ticket needs: `rebar_reconciler._backend.BackendPaginationStallError` (core, so `fetcher` can name it without importing `adapters/`), plus `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` clauses already in place ahead of all three fetcher enrichment handlers.

One-line change: make Cloud's error subclass the core one — `class RunawayPaginationError(BackendPaginationStallError)` in `acli_graph.py`. The three fetcher re-raise clauses then cover Cloud automatically. Keeping the Cloud-specific name preserves every existing `except RunawayPaginationError` site and its tests unedited; `BackendPaginationStallError` itself subclasses `RuntimeError`, so `except RuntimeError` sites are unaffected too. Adapters importing core is the established direction (`jira_datacenter/_base.py:19` already does it).

NOT folded into 18a4 deliberately: this changes observable behaviour on the CLOUD surface (stalls that previously degraded now abort the pass), which another work stream owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A stalled Cloud cursor propagates out of `fetch_snapshot` instead of degrading: a
      token-repeating Cloud stub driven through the REAL `fetch_snapshot` raises, for each of the
      three enrichment readers (`get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map`).
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`
- [x] `issubclass(RunawayPaginationError, BackendPaginationStallError)` is `True`, and
      `RuntimeError` remains in its MRO so existing `except RuntimeError` sites still catch it.
      Proof: asserted in the same test module.
- [x] Existing `except RunawayPaginationError` sites and their tests pass UNEDITED.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` with no edits to the pre-existing test bodies.
- [x] Ordinary (non-stall) enrichment failures still fail open and write a degraded snapshot
      (negative control: a plain `RuntimeError` from an enrichment reader must NOT propagate).
      Proof: negative-control case in the same test module.

## Testing

- RED-first held-out test added to
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`: a token-repeating Cloud
  REST stub driven through the real `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` (loaded from source, `_load_acli`
  patched), parameterized over all three enrichment readers, asserting the stall escapes. Verified
  failing before the fix and passing after; mutation-checked by restoring the `RuntimeError` base.
- Negative control in the same module: an ordinary `RuntimeError` enrichment fault still degrades
  and writes a snapshot carrying the base scan's issues.
- Regression: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Cloud RunawayPaginationError is swallowed by fetcher's three enrichment fail-opens

## Impact, stated first

The scheduled **Reconcile Bridge** workflow failed 12 times in 6 days. An evidence pass over all 12 failed runs (see the pinned comment) split them cleanly: **6 runs died on an ACLI authentication failure**, and 6 died on **git delivery** faults that the original sweep misattributed to ACLI. When the bridge stalls, only the Reconciler Heartbeat Canary notices.

This ticket now covers **the ACLI auth failure and how it is reported**. The other faults are filed as separate linked tickets — they are unrelated causes in a different subsystem.

## Confirmed signature (6/12 runs)

Runs 31481490100, 31358521998, 31350775907, 31263067299, 31222668500, 31179770156. Identical:

    ACLI stderr: ✗ Error: unauthorized: use `acli [product] auth login` to authenticate
    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: Command `[acli, jira, workitem, search, --jql, ...]`
        returned non-zero exit status 1
    Reconcile failed (exit 1)

It fails on the **very first** ACLI call, 15–20s in, with no reconcile work preceding it. The `acli jira auth login` workflow step **succeeded** earlier in the same job. So the token is rejected **at first use, not at login**.

## The code defect this ticket fixes

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py` fast-aborts on auth via:

    _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE: int = 401
    ...
    if cpe.returncode == _AUTH_FAILURE_CODE:
        raise cpe

ACLI is a **subprocess** and exits **1**, never 401 — that branch is **dead code**. So a deterministic auth failure:

1. burns the full 3-attempt retry budget with 2s+4s backoff, and
2. surfaces as the generic `reconcile_once raised: ... exit status 1`, indistinguishable from
   a data/operational failure.

Nothing in `rebar_reconciler/` matches the `unauthorized` / `auth login` stderr string.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (and why)

**Automatic credential renewal.** The token is rejected at first use, so re-running `acli jira auth login` with the same `JIRA_API_TOKEN` cannot succeed. Renewal requires **rotating the secret value** — an ops action needing a new secret, not a code change. No new auth flow is invented and no credential is stored anywhere new. Rotation is flagged to the operator, not automated here.

**The git-delivery failures** (TLS `server certificate verification failed`; rejected ref pushes on `refs/reconciler/last-pass` and `refs/heads/tickets`; `HTTP 422` re-dispatch onto a disabled workflow) and **the swallowed `command cancelled` noise** in the link-apply loop are filed as separate linked tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An ACLI failure whose stderr carries an authentication/authorization marker (the
      `unauthorized` / ``use `acli ... auth login` `` text) is detected **from stderr**, not from
      a subprocess exit code of 401 that ACLI never returns. Unit test asserts a
      `CalledProcessError` with `returncode=1` + that stderr is recognised as an auth failure.
- [x] Such a failure **aborts on the first attempt** without consuming the retry budget —
      retrying a rejected credential is deterministic and cannot succeed. Unit test asserts the
      subprocess was invoked exactly **once** (today: 3 times).
- [x] The failure raises a **distinct typed error** (not a bare `CalledProcessError`) carrying
      the failing command, so callers can `except` it specifically. Unit test asserts the type.
- [x] A pass failing this way emits an **operator-facing message that names the credential as
      the cause**, distinguishable from the generic `reconcile_once raised: ...` used for
      data/operational failures — so a credential problem is tellable from a data problem
      without opening the log. Unit test asserts the classifier's message/disposition.
- [x] **Non-auth** ACLI failures keep their existing retry-and-backoff behaviour unchanged.
      Regression test asserts a non-auth non-zero exit still makes 3 attempts.
- [x] The Mode 1 / Mode 2 relationship is **determined and recorded** on this ticket: they are
      independent (`unauthorized` count is 0 in all six `command cancelled` runs; the two
      signatures never co-occur). Recorded in the evidence comment.
- [x] The misattributed git-delivery faults and the swallowed `command cancelled` noise exist as
      **separate tickets linked `discovered_from`** this one.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the reconciler test suite pass.

## Notes

Originally filed by an automated ops error sweep, which hypothesised that `command cancelled` was a mid-pass abort caused by the credential expiring. The evidence pass **refuted** that: the string is non-fatal noise bracketed by successful `batch_outcome ... error=None` lines, and those runs actually failed in git delivery. The original AC about a "partially-applied reconcile" left by such an abort is therefore **moot** — no pass is aborted by that string.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge reports ACLI auth failure as a generic error: the fast-abort is dead code keyed on a 401 exit ACLI never returns

baseline.description:
Encode the agent-build invariants that guard against silently-disabled safeguards as tests plus a one-time construction check — not per-call runtime blocking. Every mechanism below is a CONCRETE, verified pydantic-ai 1.107.0 signal.

## Why
Several dangerous silent failures are static properties of rebar's OWN agent construction, not per-call events: tools silently stripped when a hook returns None (#5177), tools silently ignored on a non-tool-calling provider (#6186), `usage_limits` silently ignored if set on the `Agent(...)` constructor instead of `run*` (#1987), and usage silently zeroed on some provider adapters (#5360). Asserting these per-call wastes work and risks false-blocking a healthy run — they belong in tests + a one-time check.

## What (concrete mechanisms)
- **Construction-time provider tool-calling check.** VERIFIED signal: a pydantic-ai model exposes `model.profile.supports_tools` (a bool). The check is gated on `self._model_override is None` (the SAME guard as the anthropic model construction) — so the `model_override` test double is NEVER checked, concretely and by construction (no `.profile`-inspection heuristic to exclude it). It applies where rebar constructs an explicit model OBJECT (the anthropic path via `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, the primary path in practice). Guard: FOR A TOOL-USING op (`tools` non-empty) where `model` is a model OBJECT exposing the capability — read defensively as `supports = getattr(getattr(model, 'profile', None), 'supports_tools', None)` (so a missing/None profile is a safe skip, never an AttributeError) — assert that when `supports is False` it raises (a `True`/`None` value passes); else raise `LLMConfigError` (fail fast). It is a NO-OP for the string-model paths (OpenAI/Gemini pass a model STRING to `Agent`, which pydantic-ai builds + validates internally — rebar has no object to introspect there) and for `model_override` (a test double). So the check bounds the path rebar actually owns without false-positiving on provider-string paths. CACHE: a module-level `set()` `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` keyed by the resolved model string — the check runs ONCE per unique model per process (not per call), so a hot loop pays nothing.
- **Tests — tools actually offered.** rebar builds the agent's tools as `pai_tools.filesystem_tools(cfg.repo_path)` (callables `read_file`, `list_directory`, `search_files`) + `pai_tools.rebar_tools(cfg.repo_path, allow_comment=…)` (`show_ticket`, and `comment_ticket` when allowed). A test asserts these builders return callables whose `__name__`s are exactly the expected set (so a #5177 hook-returns-None regression that strips a tool is caught).
- **Tests — `usage_limits` on `run*`, not the constructor.** A spy on `Agent`/`run_sync` asserts (a) `run_sync` IS called with `usage_limits=`, and (b) the `Agent(...)` constructor kwargs do NOT include `usage_limits` (the #1987 mis-placement). Confirmed: `Agent.run_sync` accepts `usage_limits`; the constructor does not honor it.
- **Usage-plausibility telemetry WARNING (never a block).** After a successful REAL run (`self._model_override is None` — offline test doubles report zero usage and must never warn), if `_extract_usage` reports BOTH `input_tokens == 0` AND `output_tokens == 0` while `requests > 0` (a request was actually made), log a WARNING (`llm usage looks zeroed/implausible …`) — an observability signal for the #5360 zeroed-adapter cluster. It NEVER blocks a gate (usage is observability, not load-bearing); a genuinely tiny run is at worst a benign warning.

## Scope
- Tests + the construction-time capability check + the telemetry warning. NO per-call runtime blocking for these invariants.
- NOT in scope: changing the tool surface or provider adapters themselves; a per-call usage assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`/`rebar_tools` offer exactly the expected tool names — fails if a tool is stripped (`test_expected_tools_offered`).
- [ ] Test: `run_sync` is called with `usage_limits=` and the `Agent(...)` constructor is NOT — fails on the #1987 mis-placement (`test_usage_limits_on_run_not_constructor`).
- [ ] Construction-time check: a model OBJECT with `profile.supports_tools == False` used for a tool-using op raises `LLMConfigError`; a string-model path is a NO-OP (test asserts no raise); the check is cached in a module-level `set()` `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` (invoked once per model string; `test_capability_check_cached` spies on the `model.profile` access — or a counter in the check helper — asserting a repeated same-model run reads the profile only once) — `test_capability_check_fails_fast`, `test_capability_check_noop_for_string_model`, `test_capability_check_cached`.
- [ ] Usage-plausibility emits a WARNING (asserted via caplog) on an all-zero-usage successful run and NEVER blocks (`test_usage_plausibility_warns_never_blocks`).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (the cached construction-time capability check + the usage-plausibility warning), `tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py` (new).

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
FunctionModel.profile.supports_tools == True; AnthropicModel("claude-sonnet-4-6").profile.supports_tools == True (bool)
  -> VERIFIED on the ACTUAL AnthropicModel type rebar constructs (offline, no API call — just the model object)
model.profile also exposes: supports_json_schema_output, supports_json_object_output, supports_thinking, ...
Agent.__init__ has tools/toolsets: True         (tools offered via the constructor; introspectable)
Agent.run_sync accepts usage_limits: True       (#1987: usage_limits belongs on run*, NOT Agent(...))
rebar tool builders: pai_tools.filesystem_tools -> [read_file, list_directory, search_files];
                     pai_tools.rebar_tools -> [show_ticket, (comment_ticket when allow_comment)]
_extract_usage returns a dict with input_tokens/output_tokens (both 0 => the zeroed-adapter signal)
```
These are pydantic-ai LIBRARY symbols (`model.profile.supports_tools` etc.), not rebar symbols (bug succinct-formable-kite: a code-grounding pass must not read repo-absence as non-existence).
baseline.summary: Agent-build invariants as tests + one-time capability check

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A `caplog` assertion whose records never arrive DOES NOT FAIL — it passes vacuously. `assert not [unexpected]` is trivially true against an empty list, and even a positive `assert any(...)` only fails if someone wrote it that way. So a test can lose 100% of its coverage and stay GREEN, permanently and silently, with nothing in the run output distinguishing it from a test that genuinely verified something.

This is not hypothetical. It is happening in this repository right now.

## The live instance

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:145-146` (`configure_logging()`) sets

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.propagate = False

process-globally, and never restores it. pytest's `caplog` captures through a handler on the ROOT logger, so once propagation is off NO `rebar.*` record can reach it again for the remainder of the process. Every later `caplog` assertion on a rebar logger silently sees zero records.

Proven on a clean tree by a two-test probe: identical assertion, passes before `configure_logging()` and fails after; `caplog.at_level()` does not help because it adjusts LEVELS, not propagation. Full mechanism, both entry points, and the reproduction are on ticket b718-fb7f-b1a4-4feb — including that `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls `configure_logging()` at MODULE IMPORT time, so merely importing the app poisons the process (inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

b718 fixes THE POISONER. This ticket is about the far larger problem it exposed: THE SUITE CANNOT TELL THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PASSING ASSERTION AND AN UNREACHABLE ONE.

## Blast radius — measured, though the precise void count is unknown

    54 test files contain `caplog`
    255 total `caplog` occurrences

How many of those are currently void in a full run is NOT established, and establishing it is the first job of this ticket. The count depends on run order and on which logger each assertion targets, and `-n 6 --dist worksteal` distributes tests across workers nondeterministically — so the SAME assertion may be live in one run and void in the next, on the same commit. That non-determinism is itself part of the defect: coverage is not reproducible.

## Why this is severe rather than untidy

* IT FAILS OPEN. Every other gate in this repo fails closed. This one silently reports success.
* IT IS INVISIBLE. Nothing in the output marks a void assertion. Reviewers, CI and agents all see
  green.
* IT SURVIVED DETECTION. It was found only as a side effect of debugging an unrelated ticket, by an
  agent that noticed one victim test and traced it. Nobody was looking for it.
* IT IS ORDER-DEPENDENT, so a test can be genuinely verifying in isolation — which is how it was
  written and reviewed — and verify nothing in the suite that actually gates merges.
* THE VICTIM IS NEVER THE CULPRIT. The one test that DID go red pointed at
  `test_agent_call_seam.py`, nowhere near `review_bot/config.py`.

## Approach

Fixing the current poisoner (b718) removes today's instance but not the class — any future code that touches logger propagation, handlers or levels reintroduces it, with the same silence.

The durable fix is to make an unreachable log assertion FAIL LOUDLY instead of passing. Candidates to weigh, not yet decided:
  * an autouse fixture that asserts `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` is True at test setup, so
    the poisoning is caught at the point of damage rather than at a random later victim;
  * a `caplog` wrapper/fixture used by rebar tests that fails when zero records were captured for an
    assertion that expected some;
  * making `configure_logging()` scoped/restorable so no test can leak it in the first place (overlaps
    b718 — coordinate rather than duplicate).
The first is the smallest change that converts a silent fail-open into a loud fail-closed, and it protects against future reintroduction rather than just this instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The number of `caplog` assertions currently void in a full default-selection run is ESTABLISHED
      and recorded — not estimated. The 54-file / 255-occurrence figures above are the search space,
      not the answer.
- [x] An unreachable log assertion FAILS rather than passing vacuously, and a test proves it: with
      propagation deliberately disabled, a previously-green assertion must go RED.
- [x] The guard catches the poisoning AT ITS SOURCE, not at a random later victim — a test asserts the
      failure names the code that disabled propagation, not an unrelated downstream test.
- [x] Any assertion found to be void is either restored to working coverage or deleted; none is left
      passing vacuously. Deleting is acceptable where the assertion no longer earns its place, but
      leaving a green no-op is not.
- [x] Coordinated with b718 so the poisoner fix and the class guard do not implement overlapping
      mechanisms.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Unreachable caplog assertions pass vacuously: the suite cannot distinguish verified coverage from zero coverage

## Summary

There is no ongoing per-test performance signal in CI: slow tests are invisible until someone profiles by hand. Add lightweight, always-on per-test timing to the gate so the slowest tests surface in every run, and (optionally) persist a durations file usable for future cross-runner sharding (pytest-split). `--durations` and `pytest-split --store-durations` are both verified working on this suite.

## What

- Add `--durations=25` to the default-suite pytest invocation in `gerrit-verify.yaml`
  and `test.yml` so every gate run prints its 25 slowest tests (setup/call/teardown).
  Confirmed compatible with `-q`, coverage, and xdist.
- OPTIONAL (behind this task): add a scheduled/post-merge step that runs
  `pytest --store-durations --durations-path .test_durations` and uploads `.test_durations`
  as an artifact, so timing data is tracked over time and available if the team later shards
  across runners with pytest-split. Verified: `--store-durations` writes a valid JSON map
  (`{"<nodeid>": <seconds>, …}`).
- `.test_durations` must be gitignored (or artifact-only) so it never leaks into the
  checkout and never trips the repo-leak guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--durations=25` added to the default-suite pytest command in
      `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` and `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
- [ ] A gate run's log shows the 25 slowest tests.
- [ ] If a `.test_durations` store step is added, the file is artifact/gitignored (never
      committed, never leaks into the working tree).
- [ ] Change passes CI (`Verified +1`) and lands via Gerrit.
baseline.summary: Bake per-test performance logging (--durations) into the gate
