# Plan-review proportionate-scrutiny keys on ticket TYPE, not container/leaf — security overlay never fires on container epics

## Summary
Plan-review's proportionate-scrutiny routing decides which criteria run using ticket **type**
(epic/story/task), not the container(has_children)/leaf distinction. `PlanContext.level` is
literally derived from `ticket_type` (`det_floor.py:117`). Because the security overlay **T5c**
is routed `applies_at.levels: ["task"]`, it is filtered out for any `epic`/`story` — including
**container epics that stand up real infrastructure**. This let the AWS-hosted Gerrit epic
(`d251`) pass plan-review with **no authentication contract specified** for an internet-hosted
service (the `DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` default; now tracked as bug `f2d6`/WS8).

## Reproduction Steps
1. `applies(registry.by_id()["T5c"], level="epic")` → returns **False** (confirmed).
2. The Gerrit work `d251` is a container epic (children S1–S7) describing a networked service
   ("Gerrit HTTP 8080 + SSH 29418; reverse proxy on 443") with no user/admin auth model.
3. Its plan-review therefore never ran the security overlay against the epic's contents.
4. (Content layer) Even when T5c is forced to run against the epic, 3/3 live runs flag adjacent
   issues (unencrypted token volume, token-in-logs) but never the missing endpoint auth — the
   rubric's anti-false-positive text brands "declared access level"/"endpoint authn" as canonical
   false positives (calibrated for rebar-the-local-tool), suppressing the needed finding.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** Proportionate scrutiny keys on container vs leaf; a criterion representing a
  cross-cutting risk surface (security) runs wherever that surface is described — container or
  leaf. A container epic that stands up a networked service is reviewed for its auth contract.
- **Actual:** Scrutiny keys on ticket type; T5c is `task`-only; container epics standing up
  infrastructure are never security-reviewed at the epic altitude, and an under-specified auth
  contract passes.

## Scope
- IN: the proportionate-scrutiny **routing axis** only — `registry.applies()` (drop the
  type-derived `level`; key on has_children), `is_mechanical_leaf`, `size_factor`, `_ticket_size`,
  `PlanContext.level`, the sole `applies()` call site (`orchestrator.route_criteria`), and all 32
  criteria's `applies_at` (`levels`/`container_only` → a container/leaf `scope`). Fix the
  mis-scoped security overlay so it fires on containers. Plus a concise, generic content fix so the
  gate detects an under-specified endpoint auth contract (networked service, needs identity, no
  auth plan) WITHOUT false-positiving local/no-network tools (rebar's own review certification).
- OUT: the Gerrit auth remediation itself (`f2d6`/WS8); `det_floor._clarity_score` per-type
  headings and the bug/session_log gate exemption (separate type axes, documented follow-ups).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `registry.applies()` no longer takes/uses a type-derived `level`; proportionate scrutiny is
      decided by container(has_children)/leaf. `PlanContext.level` and its type→level mapping are
      removed (or no longer used by any routing path).
- [ ] `is_mechanical_leaf`, `size_factor`, `_ticket_size` no longer key on the `"task"`/`"epic"`
      type strings; they key on container/leaf (has_children).
- [ ] All 32 `applies_at` blocks in `criteria_routing.json` express scope as container/leaf, not
      epic/story/task levels; each criterion's scope is re-mapped faithfully (child-coverage
      criteria G3/G4 → container; code-grounding/impl-detail → leaf; cross-cutting → both). The
      security overlay T5c is no longer altitude-gated away from containers.
- [ ] A concise, generic criterion change (security and/or a non-security endpoint-contract
      completeness check, chosen by experiment) makes the gate flag an under-specified auth
      contract for a networked service, with a documented negative-control run proving no false
      positive on local/no-auth work.
- [ ] Validation on `d251`: the OLD criteria did not flag the missing Gerrit auth; the NEW criteria
      do. Negative controls (`8a1c`, `4702`) do not regress to false positives.
- [ ] `validate_packaged_routing()` passes; existing plan-review tests updated to the new
      container/leaf routing; new test(s) covering container-scoped security + the endpoint-contract
      check; `make lint` clean.
baseline.summary: Plan-review scrutiny keyed on ticket type not container/leaf — security overlay skips container epics

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Teams running several tracker projects against one codebase (or several repos against one ticket store) cannot use the bridge: it is hard-wired to exactly one project at three points — `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`_config_schema.py`), the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one (`fetcher.jqls_for`), and the applier aborts a pass when any outbound mutation targets a key outside that project (`applier.CrossProjectTargetError`). The only escape is the destructive one-way `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`. Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff` and taken as a dependency, not duplicated here.

(Full original description with line-anchored citations preserved verbatim as a ticket comment, 2026-08-13.)

## Approach

Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects. Each ticket records the project it syncs into and the repos it belongs to.

The STORE owns the project set — `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the tickets branch beside `bindings.json`/`prev_snapshot.json`. Reason (mechanical): `prev_snapshot.json` is last-known-remote state; if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would diff the other's projects as remote deletions. A store-owned project set removes that failure mode by construction and leaves no per-repo list to disagree.

Built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`) and the backend-neutral port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)`, `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`. `Backend.project` ("the backend's effective write/create project scope") is the per-repo default for rebar-created tickets; no new config key; generalizes beyond Jira.

Migration writes NO events. The ticket project field is tri-state — absent=legacy, explicit-empty= never sync, explicit key=sync there — mirroring `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths (`docs/ticket-model.md`). Absent resolves against the legacy default recorded in the mapping, seeded by an idempotent check-then-act ensure unit (`docs/migrations.md`, the sanctioned seam; the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built). A per-ticket EDIT migration was rejected: four-figure event writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot entry runs the ensure sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended — an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + the ensure seed. Delivers migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`. Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces; promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out + snapshot union; per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project. Delivers two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create; guard relaxed from single project to set membership. Delivers explicit-project + guard criteria.
- **Store-compat capability stamp** — conditional `required_capabilities` entry + fail-closed read. Delivers final criterion.
- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: rehearse against two live Jira Cloud projects on an
  isolated tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`,
  hence the depends_on); dry-run-gated, all created issues removed. Fixtures cannot reach the
  cross-project contamination failure mode this validates.
- **Module-size relief** — several files this feature edits sit within ~30 lines of the 800 hard cap.
  Behaviour-preserving extractions along existing seams, each ordered ahead of the story needing room;
  they deliver no epic criterion (preconditions; their own criteria are unchanged suite + measured LOC).

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive at every layer. Absent project = legacy; a pre-feature store behaves as today, no operator action. A single-project store never receives the capability stamp, so older binaries keep working; only a genuinely multi-project store fails closed on them — the intended protection (an older binary would fetch its one project, see other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicates in the wrong project). Rollback is per-change on Gerrit; the mapping and capability entry are inert to older binaries apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to implicit-legacy with the idempotent ensure re-stamping on the next covered write.
baseline.summary: Many-to-many tracker projects: per-ticket bridge project + repo association over one shared store

## What
Add an `mcp_registry` job to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that publishes `server.json` to the MCP Registry on a `v*` tag using **GitHub Actions OIDC** (`mcp-publisher login github-oidc`) — eliminating the interactive `mcp-publisher login github` device flow (whose cached Registry JWT expires and was the one manual, friction-prone channel during the v0.7.0 release).

## Why
PyPI already publishes via OIDC Trusted Publishing and (change 314/316) GitHub Releases are auto-created. The MCP Registry was the last channel still requiring a human browser login. OIDC needs no stored secret: the runner's OIDC token proves the `navapbc/rebar` repo identity, which authorizes the `io.github.navapbc/*` namespace.

## Implementation (per modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/github-actions)
- New job `mcp_registry`, `needs: publish` (runs after PyPI so the registry's
  package-ownership check resolves against the live version), same
  `if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` gate.
- `permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }`.
- Steps: `actions/checkout@v5` (server.json lives in the repo) -> install mcp-publisher
  (curl the release binary, os/arch-detected) -> `./mcp-publisher login github-oidc`
  -> `./mcp-publisher publish`.
- No version step needed: the `Release X.Y.Z` commit bumps server.json before the tag,
  so the tag tree already carries the correct version.
- Update `docs/releasing.md` section 4 to mark MCP Registry as automated (OIDC in CI),
  demoting the manual `mcp-publisher login/publish` to a fallback.

## Verification note (end-to-end)
Like the sibling `publish` and `github_release` jobs, this job runs ONLY on a real `v*` tag push and cannot execute in Gerrit branch CI (no tag, no OIDC token). So the live end-to-end path (login github-oidc -> publish -> registry updated) is verified on the NEXT tagged release (v0.7.1+), not at merge time. Pre-merge verification is necessarily static: YAML well-formedness + job wiring, and that the install/login/ publish commands match the canonical upstream recipe. This deferral is intentional and mirrors how the existing OIDC PyPI publish job is verified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` contains an `mcp_registry` job gated to `v*` tag push with `permissions.id-token: write`.
- [ ] That job checks out the repo, installs mcp-publisher, runs `mcp-publisher login github-oidc`, then `mcp-publisher publish`.
- [ ] The job declares `needs: publish` so it runs after the PyPI publish.
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` documents MCP Registry publishing as automated via OIDC, with the manual `mcp-publisher login github` path demoted to a fallback.
- [ ] The workflow YAML parses (validated with a YAML loader) and the commit lands on main through Gerrit (LLM-Review + Verified green).
- [ ] Live end-to-end confirmation is explicitly deferred to the next tagged release (v0.7.1+), per the Verification note above — not required at merge.
baseline.summary: release.yml: auto-publish to MCP Registry via GitHub Actions OIDC (no interactive login)

## Summary
The `verify-identity` job added to `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` in commit 5febe8274 ("run verify-identity as a PRE-MERGE whole-store gate") more than DOUBLED gerrit-verify CI runtime: runs jumped from ~12-27 min (through sha cb0f8ec3b) to 44-72 min, first spiking to 43.8 min on 5febe8274 itself. The `verify-identity` job is the sole long pole (66.2 min in a 66.6-min run); every other job is unchanged.

## Root cause (profiled against the real store: 2572 events in scope, 808 signed)
`rebar verify-identity` (the step) = 63.5 min; the git fetch is only 2.2 min. Phase timing:
- `_collect_all` (whole-store walk): 1.9s
- `build_introducing_commit_map` (batched git log, bug 1cc0): 2.3s
- classify UNSIGNED events: ~0ms each (short-circuits)
- classify SIGNED events: 1,780 ms EACH -> ~24 min local / ~63 min on slower CI runners

cProfile of one signed classify: ~100% of time in `subprocess.run`, via `_verify_signed -> verify_authorship_at_commit -> keys_valid_at_anchor -> resolve_event_commit` = a full-history `git log --diff-filter=A` PER keyring record, PER signed event (5 git spawns /event). This is the exact O(events × keyring × history) cost bug 1cc0's `build_introducing_commit_map` was built to kill, but the batched map was only wired into the enforcement/grandfather decision (`_resolve_commit`), NOT the era-verify hot path — verified events `continue` before reaching it.

Also: `_classify` runs UNCONDITIONALLY; `identity.require_authenticated` only gates the final pass/fail verdict, never whether the per-event git work runs. So enforcement being off does not avoid the cost.

## Config reality
require_authenticated = true (enforcement ON). enforce_since pinned to tracker HEAD at re-flip time, so only events introduced AFTER it are enforced; all earlier events are grandfathered (reported, never fail). The gate git-verifies all 808 signed events but only post-enforce_since events can change the verdict.

## Fix plan (3 parts)
1. Gate the expensive per-event era-verify when NOT enforcing (require_authenticated off):
   classify signed events cheaply (signed vs unsigned) in advisory mode. VERIFIED: the era
   result feeds only (a) the exit code when enforcement is ON and (b) informational counts /
   --format json (consumed only by unit tests). Both CI workflows gate on exit code only,
   which is unconditionally 0 in advisory mode. Safe.
2. Skip ARCHIVED tickets in `_collect_all` (reuse the reduce already done in
   `_is_gate_exempt_ticket`; status == "archived"). Free and authoritative.
3. Wire `--base`/grandfather-boundary scoping into the gate so collection is bounded to
   `enforce_since..HEAD` (via existing `_collect_range`), eliminating the git-heavy
   re-verification of provably-grandfathered history. Behavior-preserving for the enforced
   verdict.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Advisory mode (require_authenticated=false) does NOT run per-event git era-verification;
      exit code stays 0; whole-store scan drops to seconds.
- [ ] Archived tickets are excluded from the scan (with a regression test).
- [ ] With enforcement ON, collection is scoped so only enforce_since..HEAD events are verified,
      AND the security invariant holds: an unsigned/forged event introduced AFTER enforce_since
      still FAILS the gate (held-out test), while pre-boundary events are not git-verified.
- [ ] gerrit-verify `verify-identity` job wall-time returns to the low-single-digit minutes.
- [ ] Full suite + lint + typecheck green; landed via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: verify-identity whole-store gate: 63-min CI runtime (O(events×keyring×history) git subprocesses)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Under sustained write load the enrich drain holds its advisory lock across NO-TIMEOUT LLM calls (437s and 131s holds observed live), making it structurally single-flight: every per-write spawned drain child exits `{"skipped": "lock-held"}`. Ceiling: 5 tickets per multi-minute hold — below the enqueue rate, hence the ~1,046-entry standing backlog. The operator approved the "option 2" restructure designed and validated on bug 6148-5d81-8e80-41e8 (draughty-callous-tanager): the prototype cut the lock hold 19.8s -> 1.5-2.9s (13x), and two concurrent drains on 10 tickets made exactly 10 LLM calls. The shape is the Postgres SKIP LOCKED job-queue pattern: reserve-short -> process-unlocked -> finalize-short + lease recovery.

## Operator rulings (recorded before implementation)

- OQ1 (concurrent-drain cap): small cap per the design's recommendation — 2-3 concurrent drainers, bounded by a small guard in the collect phase.
- OQ2 (backlog): NO bulk backlog job — the ~1,046 standing backlog drains through normal workflow traffic; steady-state throughput must exceed the enqueue rate.
- OQ3 (batch cap): raised from 5 but BOUNDED, sized to the lease window (batch ~ lease_duration / worst-case per-item LLM time, concretely ~20-25) — unbounded means hours + ~1k LLM calls billed to one random write, lease expiry mid-run, large crash blast radius.
- OQ4: separate from the merged option-1 probe (change 2140) — `has_pending_enrichment` semantics are NOT touched.
- OQ5 (unruled, judgment): stale-at-writeback re-enqueue uses soak 0 (immediate retry), matching the validated prototype and the existing self-heal path's posture.
- OQ6 (unruled, judgment): no separate drain-call timeout knob — `cfg.timeout_s` (default 600s) already bounds each call, and with the lock released a hung provider blocks only its own batch.

## Approach

Restructure `drain()` in `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` into three phases (behavior-preserving extraction along the existing call-graph seams, which also serves the complexity ratchet):

- COLLECT (under the drain advisory lock; seconds): concurrency guard (skip with `{"skipped": "concurrency-cap"}` when >= 3 distinct live-lease drainer_ids already exist), self-heal re-enqueues, `pending_enrichment` scan, per-ticket optimistic `claim()` up to the batch cap, and a `digest_sidecar.content_hash` snapshot of each claimed ticket's state. Release the lock.
- ENRICH (NO lock held): run `enrich()` per claimed item; capture per-item result or exception.
- FINALIZE (no drain lock; store write lock per append as today, unchanged): re-read the ticket; if its content hash changed since collect -> skip the emit and re-enqueue with soak 0 (counted as `stale_skipped` in the summary); else `ds.emit` (with the revalidated state) + `mark_done`. Exceptions keep the existing disposition (`_record_item_failure`: transient -> lease-expiry retry; permanent CHANGE_INPUT -> tombstone).

Batch cap: raise `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH` 5 -> 20, and clamp the effective per-run batch to a lease-derived bound `max(1, lease_ttl_s // 40)` (= 22 at the default 15-min lease, inside the operator's ~20-25 window; 40s is the worst-case per-item budget for the trivial-class digest call) so a configured batch can never outrun its lease mid-run.

UNCHANGED: store write lock semantics, queue event schema (ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN` off|async|always semantics, the `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH` door's meaning (claim-window size), `has_pending_enrichment` (option-1, change 2140), the MCP surface, and the operation-linked trigger (portability holds: no CI-provider dependency). Existing per-write spawned drain children become productive concurrent drainers (bounded by the OQ1 guard) with no new spawner or scheduler.

Throughput argument (OQ2): pre-change ceiling is 5 items per multi-minute lock hold (single-flight). Post-change: up to 3 concurrent drainers x ~20 items per batch, the lock held only for the ~1.5-2.9s collect window. Enqueue sources (certifications + self-heal) produce well under that rate, so the backlog drains through normal traffic.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — `drain()` split into collect/enrich/finalize helpers + concurrency guard + lease-derived batch clamp.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH` 5 -> 20 (the env door keeps its name and meaning).
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` — new mechanism pins + updates to the two tests that hardcode batch=5 (pin the mechanism via `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH=5` instead).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — a short note on the three-phase drain and the concurrency bound.

## Testing

All deterministic (counted/instrumented, no wall-clock timing):

- Lock-not-held-across-LLM: a runner whose `run()` attempts `_acquire_advisory_lock` on the same tracker — acquisition must SUCCEED during every LLM call (it fails today), proving the drain lock is released before the enrich phase.
- Concurrent zero-duplicate: a re-entrant runner triggers a second `drain()` from inside the first drain's enrich phase (the exact concurrent-drainer shape); assert total LLM calls == ticket count and each ticket enriched exactly once (claim arbitration).
- Stale-writeback revalidation: a runner edits the ticket during `run()`; assert the digest emit is skipped (`stale_skipped == 1`, no digest recorded), the entry is re-enqueued pending, and a follow-up drain enriches it fresh.
- Lease-expiry recovery: a claim with an already-expired lease is re-picked and processed by the next drain.
- Concurrency guard: with 3 distinct live-lease drainer claims planted, `drain()` returns `{"skipped": "concurrency-cap"}`; with 2 it proceeds.
- Batch clamp: with `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH=1000` the effective batch reported by `drain()` equals the lease-derived bound (22 at default lease); default config yields batch 20.
- Existing suite (failure disposition, self-heal, lock-held skip, fairness, worktree lock identity) stays green — the phases are behavior-preserving for every pre-existing contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The drain advisory lock is never held across an LLM call: pinned by an instrumented-runner test that acquires the drain lock from inside `run()` and asserts success for every call in a batch (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`).
- [x] Two concurrent drains produce zero duplicate LLM calls: the re-entrant-runner claim-arbitration test counts exactly N calls for N tickets, each ticket enriched once (checked: pytest, counted not timed).
- [x] Stale-at-writeback revalidation: a ticket edited between claim and finalize gets NO stale digest emit; the entry is re-enqueued (soak 0) and the summary reports `stale_skipped` (checked: pytest).
- [x] Lease-expiry recovery: an entry claimed by a crashed drainer (expired lease) is processed by a subsequent drain (checked: pytest).
- [x] The effective batch cap is ~20-25 and lease-derived: default 20, and any configured value is clamped to `max(1, lease_ttl_s // 40)` (checked: pytest on the clamp + the config default).
- [x] Concurrent drainers are bounded: a 4th drainer skips with `{"skipped": "concurrency-cap"}` while <= 3 distinct live-lease drainers exist (checked: pytest).
- [x] Steady-state throughput exceeds the enqueue rate: argued quantitatively in a ticket comment from the measured collect-window hold (1.5-2.9s) x 3 drainers x batch 20 vs the enqueue sources; before/after lock-hold numbers recorded on the ticket (checked: evidence comment present before close).
- [x] Config doors, queue event schema, MCP surface, and `has_pending_enrichment` are unchanged: no new/renamed env keys or event types in the diff; option-1 probe untouched (checked: `git diff` review + existing config/queue tests green).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the targeted pytest all pass; the module-size gate (<=800 LOC) and complexity ratchet (new=0, increased=0) hold (checked: CI Verified +1).
baseline.summary: enrich-drain: collect/enrich/finalize restructure — LLM calls outside the drain lock

baseline.description:
# The comment dedup key is NOT normalized the way the description send value is

## Summary

The description path and the comment path have different convergence protections, and the missing piece is exactly the normalization half. Today this is LATENT — it costs nothing, because rebar does not currently model any content transformation on the comment send path. Any real Markdown/wiki converter activates it, and the symptom is duplicate Jira comments re-posted on every pass, forever.

Filed from a peer session's round-trip experiment over 5,568 real rebar bodies, verified here against the code rather than taken on report.

## The asymmetry, in code

**Descriptions are protected.** `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote` composes

    normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))

so the value sent is already its own fixed point under the round trip. The ordering is deliberate and documented in a long comment there, and it is PINNED by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py::test_cloud_send_path_composition_is_unchanged`, which includes an explicitly soft-wrapped case.

**Comments are not.** `outbound_comments._diff_comments` builds its comparison key with

    compare_body = sanitizer.fit_comment(_normalize_comment_body(raw))

There is no `normalize_outbound` equivalent. And `_normalize_comment_body` does NOT normalize both sides the same way — it calls `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`, which is:

    if isinstance(body, dict):  return adf_to_text(body)     # the JIRA side: decoded
    return str(body) if body is not None else ""             # the LOCAL side: pass-through

So the Jira side is decoded and the local side is handed back verbatim. The two sides are compared after DIFFERENT transformations.

## Why the truncation guard proves the shape of the bug

The comment path already carries one guard of exactly this kind, added after it bit:

> the send path truncates an over-length body ... Apply the SAME shared truncation to the expected
> local body before the membership test; otherwise the full local body never matches the truncated
> Jira body and the diff re-emits forever.

That is the identical failure mode, patched for the ONE transformation the send path was known to apply. Nothing generalizes it. A content transformation gets no such treatment, and the machinery that would notice — a comparison against what Jira will actually store — does not exist.

The `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` canary exclusion is a second instance of the same class patched per-symptom: a volatile timestamp never matches a prior body, so the comment re-added every pass.

## Why it is latent RIGHT NOW (do not "fix" a bug that is not firing)

Cloud comments go out through ACLI as `jira workitem comment create --body <text>` (`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`). rebar never computes the ADF that Jira will store, so it applies no content transformation of its own, and the dedup key happens to match. DC's `WikiTextCodec` is pure identity in all four operations, so DC transforms nothing either.

I could not establish whether ACLI's own text→ADF conversion alters bodies (e.g. rejoining soft wraps) — that is a live question about a third-party binary and only a live pass settles it. If it DOES, this is already firing on Cloud today. Empirically, rebar's own `text_to_adf` DOES rejoin soft wraps, so the transformation is not hypothetical for that encoder.

## What I verified empirically (so the future work is not built on a wrong premise)

Probing today's `adf.normalize_description` directly: `**/*.py`, `__pycache__`, `**a** **b**`, pipe tables, backticks, fenced blocks, `-`/`*` bullets and `__bold__` all round-trip BYTE-IDENTICALLY and are fixed points. Today's ADF path does no Markdown parsing at all — it only rejoins soft wraps and strips trailing whitespace. So the peer session's 9-19% flap rate is a property of the PROPOSED converter, not of anything shipping.

## The good news: the seam is already in the right place

`map_fields_to_remote` is SHARED and composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(...))` for both backends, so a pandoc-backed `WikiTextCodec` slots in by implementing the codec — no differ change. The `RichTextCodec` four-operation split is what makes that possible. This ticket is about the comment path catching up to the description path, not about redesigning the seam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the comment dedup key is computed from what the SEND PATH will produce, the same way the
      description value is — i.e. the local comparison key goes through the codec's outbound
      normalization, not just `fit_comment`
- [x] a test asserts the property directly: given a codec whose outbound transform is NOT the
      identity, a local comment already mirrored in Jira emits NO add. This is the cell that does
      not exist today — every current dedup test uses transformations applied to both sides
- [x] a corpus/property test over real rebar comment bodies asserts encode-then-decode is a fixed
      point for the comment path, not just unit examples
- [x] `RichTextCodec` implementations are pinned to `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`.
      `WikiTextCodec`'s identity satisfies this trivially TODAY, which is why a pandoc implementation
      that got it wrong would pass the existing suite
- [x] the dependency is DOCUMENTED: outbound has no origin-aware gate, and the reason it does not
      need one is that degradation is symmetric. If encode ever stops being decode's inverse, a body
      pulled from Jira starts being re-emitted and the human's Jira-native formatting is destroyed.
      That invariant is currently load-bearing and unwritten
baseline.summary: Comment dedup key is not normalized the way the description send value is

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at **800 lines against the hard 800-line cap** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which the CI module-size gate enforces with no allowlist. It is one line from red: the next change to any public library write verb fails the build. The sibling story adding two optional `create_ticket` arguments must widen two `@overload` signatures, the implementation, and their docstrings — it cannot land until this is relieved. This ticket buys that headroom by concern, not by line count.

## Approach

`_lib_writes` is the **aggregation point for every public library write**, so it grows on two axes: a new verb appends a wrapper, and an existing verb gaining an argument widens one in place. The facade split (S3/4532) cut the library **by direction** — writes vs reads vs gates vs ops — and that axis is exhausted: the write half alone carries seven concerns. The durable fix is to cut it **by concern**, per the `fsck` split (`defaceable-icy-antelope`), which took two cuts out of one 800-line file.

The seven concerns present today:

1. **Genesis** — `init_repo`, `create_ticket` (two `@overload`s + impl), `idea`.
2. **Identity & key material** — `create_identity`, `ensure_identity_for`, `create_placeholder`,
   `add_identity_key`, `revoke_identity_key`, `use_identity`, `resolve_current_identity`; all
   delegate to `rebar._commands.identity`, none touches ticket state.
3. **Status lifecycle** — `transition`, `claim`, `reopen`. The only place in the module that
   raises `ConcurrencyError`.
4. **Leaf mutations** — `_python_leaf` and its seven in-module callers `comment`, `edit_ticket`,
   `link`, `unlink`, `tag`, `untag`, `archive`.
5. **Session logs** — `append_session_log`, `start_session_log`; own `CommandError` mapping,
   NOT routed through `_python_leaf`.
6. **Store maintenance** — `compact`, `attach_commits`.
7. **Signing** — `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, delegating to `rebar.signing`.

**Two cuts**, mirroring `fsck`:

- **`_lib_mutations.py`** takes 4+5+6. Anchored on the `_python_leaf` call graph: one adapter,
  seven callers, all inside the block, nothing else in this module calling it. Stated honestly,
  5 and 6 **ride along** as the contiguous remainder of the post-genesis mutation surface, not
  because they call `_python_leaf`; the strict call-graph subset is ~130 lines and
  non-contiguous, forcing a scattered cut near the 100-line floor.
- **`_lib_identity.py`** takes 2+7 — the non-ticket, key-material surface. Identities own
  OpenSSH key lines, `use_identity`/`resolve_current_identity` select the current one, and
  signing binds a manifest to the environment key. Stated honestly, signing is ~52 lines and
  **cannot stand alone** under the 100-line floor; identity is the nearest concern by shape,
  and the module already banners signing apart from the write path.
- **`_lib_writes.py` keeps 1+3** — genesis and the status state machine.

The plan of record extracted only 4+5+6 and left `_lib_writes` at ~544 — sound at 778, but at 800 that lands **above** the 200-500 target band on a file that grew 22 lines in weeks. Hence two cuts.

Moved names are **re-exported** from `_lib_writes` with `# noqa: F401`, exactly as `fsck.py` re-exports from `fsck_scan`/`fsck_tracker_health`. That leaves `__init__.py` and `_lib_gates.py` **untouched**, so every `rebar.<name>` and `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` path survives — a smaller diff than re-pointing consumers.

**The pre-move surface, reconciled.** `_lib_writes` has 29 `def` statements = **27 distinct names** plus the two extra `@overload` stubs of `create_ticket`. `__init__.py` re-exports **all 27**, so the facade surface and the definition set coincide — no name defined here is omitted from the facade. `_python_leaf` is one of the 27: it resolves as **`rebar._python_leaf`** (its own `_python_leaf as _python_leaf` alias in `__init__.py`) *and* as `rebar._lib_writes._python_leaf`, the form `_lib_gates.py` imports. The 27 partition across the concerns above as 3 + 7 + 3 + 8 (leaf mutations, counting `_python_leaf`) + 2 + 2 + 2. Dependency direction is one-way — `_lib_writes` imports both new modules, neither imports back — so there is no cycle.

This is **behaviour-preserving**: bodies relocate byte-identically; no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` (new) — concerns 4+5+6
- `src/rebar/_lib_identity.py` (new) — concerns 2+7
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — keeps 1+3, gains the two re-export blocks

`__init__.py`, `_lib_gates.py`, and everything under `tests/` are deliberately **not** touched. The reference audit supports that: the only real-code importers of `_lib_writes` are `_lib_gates.py` (`_python_leaf`) and `__init__.py` (the 27-name re-export), and the string pass (`monkeypatch.setattr` / `getattr` / `importlib`) finds **zero** `_lib_writes` attribute references — every test patch targets the `rebar` facade or `rebar.signing`, both preserved.

`.github/complexity-baseline.json` holds **zero** entries for `_lib_writes.py`, so no moved symbol carries accepted debt and the `--lock` re-key hazard that cast `Verified -1` on the `fsck` change cannot arise. The baseline is therefore not in scope.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing with **no test file edited**. The specific risk is the **public API surface**, since all 27 names are re-exported as `rebar.<name>` and `_lib_gates` depends on `_python_leaf` at three call sites — a silently dropped re-export would still leave the suite green wherever the facade is imported lazily. Checked by name:

- every name previously importable as `rebar.<name>` still resolves after the move, asserted
  name by name against the pre-move list;
- `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` still resolves for all moved names, which is what makes
  `_lib_gates` and any `monkeypatch` target survive;
- the three modules import cleanly in **either** order, catching a cycle introduced by the
  re-export direction.

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the size oracle and needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_lib_writes.py` is at or below 450 lines; checked by
      `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_writes.py)" -le 450 ]` exiting 0.
- [ ] `_lib_mutations.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`.
- [ ] `_lib_identity.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_identity.py`.
- [ ] The repo's size oracle still passes; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve on the facade as `rebar.<name>` — 26 public wrappers plus
      `rebar._python_leaf`; checked by a script asserting `hasattr(rebar, n)` for every name in
      the pre-move list, exiting non-zero on the first miss.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve as `rebar._lib_writes.<name>`, which is the form
      `_lib_gates.py` imports; checked by the same assert-and-exit script against
      `rebar._lib_writes`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/__init__.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` are unchanged; checked by
      `git diff --exit-code HEAD~1 -- src/rebar/__init__.py src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] No file under `tests/` is changed; checked by `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 -- tests/`
      producing empty output.
- [ ] The three modules import cleanly in any order; checked by two fresh interpreters, one
      importing `_lib_identity`, `_lib_mutations`, `_lib_writes` in that order and one in
      reverse, both exiting 0.
- [ ] `make lint` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [ ] The CI test selection passes; checked by
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exiting 0.
- [ ] `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` reports no new entries; checked by running
      it with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=navapbc/rebar` and confirming exit 0.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the _python_leaf mutation block from _lib_writes.py into _lib_mutations.py

## Summary
The designed un-archive seam — rebar revert <id> <archived-event-uuid> — is broken end to end: ticket-revert.sh removes the .archived marker and _is_net_archived (ARCHIVED minus REVERT) is implemented for the list fast-path, but the reducer's process_revert only appends a revert record; replay still applies the ARCHIVED event, so compiled state stays status=archived/archived=True and the ticket remains hidden.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified in sandbox against installed 0.4.0 == HEAD engine, temp store; discovered while validating the fix for bug bored-grain-wok / f803)
1. rebar archive <id>; note the ARCHIVED event uuid (event file in .tickets-tracker/<id>/).
2. rebar revert <id> <archived-uuid> -> exit 0; .archived marker removed.
3. rebar list -> [] (ticket still hidden); rebar show <id> -> status: archived.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: reverting the ARCHIVED event restores the pre-archive state (visible in list, status open).
- Actual: revert is recorded but the archived projection survives replay.

## Source
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_processors.py process_revert (~:255) — appends to reverts, never touches state["archived"]/state["status"].
- Working halves: ticket-revert.sh:180-196 (marker removal), ticket_reducer/_api.py _is_net_archived (+ :281 fast path).

## Fix direction
In process_revert, after the append: if data.get("target_event_type") == "ARCHIVED" and state.get("archived"): state["archived"] = False; and if status is exactly "archived", restore "open" (preserves deleted semantics — process_archived keeps deleted status). Validated in sandbox. CAVEAT: .cache.json has no reducer-version key, so previously-cached reverted tickets stay hidden until cache invalidation — bump/add a cache version with this change (relates to bug fond-ulna-ball).

## Suggested RED test
Reducer-level: ARCHIVED then REVERT(target=ARCHIVED) replay -> archived=False, status=open, ticket present in reduce_all_tickets default projection. RED today.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] revert of an ARCHIVED event makes the ticket visible in default list with status open (RED test first)
- [ ] deleted tickets are NOT resurrected by reverting an ARCHIVED event
- [ ] Cache invalidation handled (version key or documented self-heal)
- [ ] test_ticket_reducer_marker.py and archive/revert suites green
baseline.summary: revert of an ARCHIVED event never un-archives: process_revert appends a record but leaves the archived projection intact

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` measures **771 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that fans the fetch out over several projects rewrites the query construction in `_build_snapshot` and will not fit in 29 lines.

## Approach

Extract the pagination cluster into a new `fetch_paging.py`: `_ACLI_CEILING` and `SilentTruncationError` (`:99-120`), `_extract_issues` (`:251-262`), `_iter_pages` (`:265-390`) and `collect` (`:392-399`).

The call chain is genuine and self-contained: `collect` calls `_iter_pages` (`:397`), which calls `_extract_issues` (`:296`) and raises `SilentTruncationError` (`:308,343,355`) against `_ACLI_CEILING` (`:354`). Nothing in the cluster calls back upward; `_build_snapshot` reaches it only through `_iter_pages` (`:554`). The new module's complete import list is `annotations` and a `TYPE_CHECKING` import of `TicketTransport` — the pagination code is otherwise pure.

This extraction is well matched to the incoming change, which rewrites the `queries` tuple at `_build_snapshot:548-554` into a per-project loop over `jqls_for` — all of which stays in `fetcher.py`.

**Three things must stay resident**, and getting any of them wrong breaks tests silently:

- `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` (`:105`) stays — `_build_snapshot:550` uses it. Only `_ACLI_CEILING` moves.
- `_load_acli` and `_load_alert_store` stay — they carry **25** and **3** `patch.object(fetcher, ...)`
  sites respectively, and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move. Both are called
  from `_build_snapshot` (`:523,536`), which stays, so no patch site is disturbed.
- `fetcher.py` re-exports **all four** moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`,
  `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` — because every one of them is reached as an attribute
  of `fetcher` by existing tests, and an attribute access does not follow a moved symbol:
  - `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py:118,139`), plus further
    `fetcher._iter_pages` / `fetcher.collect` accesses in the same file and in
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py`;
  - `fetcher.SilentTruncationError`
    (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_pagination_jql.py:133,165`) as well as the
    explicit `from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import SilentTruncationError` at
    `test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:32`;
  - `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` (`test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py:149`), which reads the constant
    directly to size its fixture. This one is easy to miss precisely because the constant looks
    private and unshared.

The re-export keeps roughly 48 existing references green across six test modules. Note that the two production mentions of `fetcher._iter_pages` — `_backend.py:62` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:139,153` — are **docstring prose** recording bug history, not runtime references, so no production module needs an edit.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~195 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — drops to ~606 lines, plus a re-export block

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. The risks are attribute presence and patch survival, so both are asserted rather than assumed:

- Attribute-surface assertion: `hasattr(fetcher, "_iter_pages")` and `hasattr(fetcher, "collect")`
  both hold after the move, and `SilentTruncationError` still imports from `fetcher`.
- Patch survival: the tests that `patch.object(fetcher, "_load_acli")` and `"_load_alert_store"` pass
  unedited, proving those symbols stayed resident and are still resolved from `fetcher`'s globals.
- Truncation behaviour preserved: a fixture exceeding `_ACLI_CEILING` still raises
  `SilentTruncationError` through the real `collect → _iter_pages` path — the contract most at risk
  from moving the constant away from its raiser.
- One-way import: `fetch_paging` must not import `fetcher`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `fetcher.py` and `fetch_paging.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the module-size
      gate with both counts recorded.
- [x] All four moved names — `_iter_pages`, `collect`, `SilentTruncationError` and `_ACLI_CEILING` —
      still resolve as attributes of `fetcher`; checked by a test asserting each by attribute access,
      which covers the two existing `hasattr` assertions and the direct `fetcher._ACLI_CEILING` read.
- [x] `_load_acli`, `_load_alert_store` and `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` remain defined in `fetcher.py`;
      checked by asserting each is in that module's own namespace, not merely importable.
- [x] A fixture exceeding the ceiling still raises `SilentTruncationError` via the real paging path;
      checked by the existing pagination held-out test running unedited.
- [x] `fetch_paging.py` does not import `fetcher`; checked by a test importing the two modules in
      both orders and asserting `fetcher` is absent from `fetch_paging`'s imports.
- [x] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the pagination cluster from fetcher.py into fetch_paging.py

## Context
Slice C1 recorded 12 below-seam ambient config reads in the reconciler JIRA adapter/credential surface as `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` rows in `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`, below the seams enforced by the in-process AST gate `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`. Parent C3a 6633-219e-988a-42f6; grandparent C3 075b-1479-dcb7-40ab. Disjoint file subtree from sibling C3a-CORE (ba8b).

The 12 flagged reads (path :: symbol), all under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:
- `access_check.py` :: JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, JIRA_PROJECT (probe scope + probe client)
- `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py` :: JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, JIRA_PROJECT (env fallback), load_config (`_acli_call_timeout` L86, `resolve_jira_settings` L119)
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` :: REBAR_RECONCILER_VERBOSE via the `_rebar_env` shim
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` :: load_config (`resolve_comment_max_chars` L83, `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` L97)
- `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` :: load_config (`cutover_clients` L90)
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` :: load_config (`_pandoc_timeout` L352)

Affected SOURCE files: the 6 above plus `src/rebar/config.py`/`_config_sources.py` (owned resolvers) and `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py` (remove rows).

## Why the JIRA_* reads are flagged (gate mechanism)
The gate classifies `os.environ.get("X")` as owner=**credential** only if X is a derived credential name (`rebar._child_env._ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES` = ONLY `JIRA_API_TOKEN`/`JIRA_PAT`; JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT are intentionally absent/non-secret), else owner=**composition**. So JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT are owner=composition reads: even as direct `os.environ.get` literals in a credential-boundary file they stay flagged. The correct cut routes them through an OWNED `config.py` resolver (composition root). The `JIRA_API_TOKEN`/`JIRA_PAT` reads are owner=credential, already owned, out of scope.

## Decision rule
- **(a) CUT-TO-SEAM (11 of 12).** A composed-config read is routed through an owned `config.py`/`_config_sources.py` resolver (reuse `compose_config()`/`load_config()`; add narrow named resolvers), so the ambient read moves into the composition root. Each adapter helper delegates to the owned resolver INTERNALLY (signature unchanged). Timing: the JIRA endpoint + reconciler knobs resolve LIVE per operation today (env over file, re-read each call); the resolvers read live per call — never composed once and threaded — so a mid-pass env override is not lost.
- **(b) OWNED-IN-PLACE via `# read-via:` marker (cap 1 read = 1 line).** `outbound_fields.py` `REBAR_RECONCILER_VERBOSE` — subsystem debug switch (`=1` emits a side-car RECON record; off by default; not in the config schema). No other listed read is marked.

## Cut details (each helper delegates internally, signatures unchanged)
- **`access_check.py` JIRA_URL/USER/PROJECT** (`_resolve_probe_scope`, `_build_probe_client`): read the non-secret trio from an injectable `env` mapping (default `os.environ`), live per probe, via owned `config.py` `resolve_jira_endpoint(env=None)->(url,user,project)`. `JIRA_API_TOKEN` stays in-boundary (owned).

Held-out `tests/scripts/test_reconciler_jira_seam_clean_heldout.py` (gate scripts imported by bare name: `import check_config_ownership`) asserts: (i) `check(REPO_ROOT)` returns no finding for any of the 6 listed files; (ii) `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` has zero entries for a listed file; (iii) `# read-via:` markers across the 6 files total exactly 1, confined to `outbound_fields.py`. ## What

`src/rebar/audit/page.py:329` computes `"lacking": kind == "operator-attested" and not met`. Widen to accept `"non-codebase"` as well.

## Why reader-first

827 of 4,285 tickets in the live store hold COMPLETION_VERDICT events carrying `kind: "operator-attested"`. Those are immutable. The reader must accept both BEFORE S5 changes what the verifier emits, or the audit page silently stops flagging un-attested criteria on either the old or the new records.

Blast radius verified: this is the ONLY site in the codebase comparing a criterion `kind` against the string; the schema declares `kind` as unconstrained `"type": "string"` with no enum, so nothing else validates it. `page.py` is 402 LOC with no complexity-baseline entry.

## How each AC is proved

Build a completion sidecar dict of the PASS shape — `{"verdict": "PASS", "criteria": [{...}]}` — and pass it through `src/rebar/audit/page.py`'s completion-rendering function, then assert on the returned criterion row's structured `lacking` field. Three fixtures, one per AC: `kind` set to `"operator-attested"`, to `"non-codebase"`, and to `"codebase-verifiable"`, each with `met: false`. Assert `lacking is True` for the first two and `lacking is False` for the third. No LLM, no network — the renderer is a pure dict-to-dict transform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A PASS verdict whose criterion carries `kind: "operator-attested"` and `met: false` renders
      with `lacking: true`.
- [x] The same verdict with `kind: "non-codebase"` renders identically.
- [x] A `codebase-verifiable` criterion is unaffected in both cases.

## Evidence — a REAL Jira DC instance, GitHub Actions run 30604756524

A writing reconcile pass (`--mode bootstrap-strict`) against the live J5 harness exits 1:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

Found by story J7's new live module (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`) on its FIRST real run. `--mode dry-run` passes; only the writing path crashes.

## Root cause — the PORT under-specifies what the CORE requires

`set_entity_property` is called from THREE core sites:

* `dispatch_one.py:321`     — `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, jira_key, 'local_id', local_id)`
* `binding_store.py:517`    — `client.set_entity_property(keyed, 'local_id', local_id)`
* `apply_inbound_records.py:279` — `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, ...)`

It is implemented in exactly ONE place: `adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:266` (Cloud).

And crucially it is **NOT a member of the `TicketTransport` Protocol** in `_backend.py`, which declares only create_issue / get_issue / update_issue / transition_issue_by_name / add_label / search_issues.

So the core depends on a transport method the PORT never declares. That is why every structural check passed while the real thing was broken: `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` is satisfied without it, the contract suite never calls it, and 1636 unit tests are green. The Protocol is not a faithful statement of the core's requirements, so conformance to it proves less than it appears to.

This is the SAME CLASS of defect as J6's `add_label` bug (a method called with a shape `jira.JIRA` never had). Both shipped because the only oracle was a fake that mirrored the author's assumption.

## Why it matters

Epic e369 exists to deliver Jira Server/Data Center support. With this defect a DC deployment cannot complete a writing reconcile pass at all — the headline capability does not work. `local_id` entity properties are the binding marker the reconciler plants to correlate remote issues with local tickets, so this is not cosmetic: without it, binding/correlation cannot be established on DC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterTransport` implements `set_entity_property` against DC's REST v2 entity-property
      endpoint, asserted by a live test that FAILS before the fix
- [ ] a full writing reconcile pass (`bootstrap-strict`) against the J5 harness exits 0/75 with no
      unhandled exception — i.e. J7's `test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` and
      `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` PASS
- [ ] **`set_entity_property` is added to the `TicketTransport` Protocol** so the port states what the
      core actually requires, and a backend missing it fails `isinstance` instead of failing at runtime
- [ ] an AUDIT of the remaining core call sites for other transport methods absent from the Protocol
      (same technique: grep `client.<method>` in core modules, diff against the Protocol's members),
      with anything found either added to the Protocol or explicitly justified — otherwise this exact
      bug recurs on the next backend
baseline.summary: DC writing reconcile pass crashes: transport lacks set_entity_property, which the port never declared

# J6 — Data Center transport on `pycontribs/jira`, behind an opt-in extra

## Context / Problem

The DC backend needs a transport satisfying rebar's `TicketTransport` role plus `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` (`_backend.py:80-282`). The Cloud transport is an ACLI subprocess (`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:31` shells out to the `acli` binary), which is Cloud-shaped and must not be disturbed. PR #120 hand-rolled a stdlib `urllib` REST v2 client for DC.

## Approach

Build the DC transport on **`pycontribs/jira`**, the maintained Python client that already handles Server/DC versus Cloud differences, PAT bearer auth, pagination, and payload quirks that a hand-rolled client would rediscover. It is confined to an opt-in `[jira-datacenter]` extra and imported **lazily inside the functions that need it**, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract holds and `import rebar` stays dependency-free; a missing extra raises a clear install-naming error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

Auth is a Personal Access Token read env-only from `JIRA_PAT` (DC PATs, Jira 8.14+), passed as `token_auth`; `url` and `project` come from the typed config so a `[tool.rebar.jira]` value is honored. A malformed config **fails loudly** rather than degrading to env-only — PR #120 swallowed `ConfigError`, which is against rebar's fail-loud posture.

The library's object model is unwrapped at this boundary: every method returns the **raw payload shapes** rebar's existing mappers already consume (`{"key": …, "fields": {…}}`), so nothing downstream learns about `jira.Issue`. Retry, timeout, and error typing are mapped onto rebar's existing transport contract — transient connectivity faults retried with the same 2s/5s backoff as `adapters/jira/acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry`, HTTP errors never retried, and assignee failures raised as `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (`_backend.py:48`).

This story also supplies the `NameIdentity` resolver's user-search lookup [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85].

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib client (PR #120).** Competent, but it re-owns Jira REST semantics that a widely-used library has already hardened, and confining the dependency to an extra means non-DC users pay nothing for it.

**Alternative rejected: reusing the ACLI transport for DC.** ACLI is the Cloud-validated path; pointing it at DC would risk the one transport we have live confidence in, which this epic explicitly must not do.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (new) — `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_PROJECT`
  from typed config, env-only `JIRA_PAT`, fail-loud on `ConfigError`.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_transport.py` (new); `tests/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py` (new).

## Testing

Two tiers. A stateful fake for fast unit coverage of shape mapping, and the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] as the real oracle — the test-design standard's "stateful verified fake plus a live canary where justified", and DC semantics are exactly where a fake's assumptions are most likely to be wrong.

- unit (fake library client): each `TicketTransport` method returns rebar's raw payload shape, not a
  `jira.Issue`; `JIRA_PAT` is sent as bearer token auth; a missing `[jira-datacenter]` extra raises naming the
  install command; a malformed config raises rather than degrading.
- unit failure paths: an HTTP error is NOT retried (call count is exactly 1) while a connection timeout IS
  retried with the documented backoff; an unknown assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`.
- live (J5 harness): create → read → update → transition-by-name → comment → link → probe a real issue and
  assert each observable postcondition on the server, including that a transition to a name the workflow does
  not offer raises rather than silently no-oping.
- live edge: the absence probe returns the classifier's not-found state for a deleted issue, and a distinct
  state for one that merely lost permission.
- collateral invariant: no Cloud test changes and `adapters/jira/acli*.py` are untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] every `TicketTransport`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` method has a
      passing live test against the J5 harness, output summarized in a ticket comment
- [ ] a test asserts an HTTP error is attempted exactly once and a timeout is retried per the documented backoff
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar` then `pip show jira` reports not-installed, and `import rebar` succeeds
- [ ] importing the DC transport without the extra raises an error naming `pip install nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]`
- [ ] a malformed `[tool.rebar.jira]` config raises `ConfigError` rather than falling back to env-only
- [ ] `git diff --stat` shows no change under `adapters/jira/acli*`
- [ ] the DC backend REJECTS a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` with a `ConfigError` naming the cleartext
      risk, unless `allow_insecure = true` is set; a unit test covers the reject branch with a non-loopback
      `http://` URL, and a second test asserts the override path emits a warning naming the risk (epic AC13)
- [ ] every live test against the J5 harness sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly (the harness serves plain
      `http://localhost:2990/jira`), so the loopback path exercises the override rather than bypassing the
      validator
- [ ] the `[jira-datacenter]` extra pins a minimum `jira` version with a compatible-release bound (e.g.
      `jira>=3.8,<4`), and a comment records which DC-vs-Cloud auth behavior that floor guarantees
- [ ] this story owns the `_config_schema.py` DC connection settings: the TLS/`allow_insecure` validator, the
      `ca_bundle` key, and `resolved_statuses` (J7 owns only the `reconciler.backend` choice widening)
- [ ] TLS certificate verification is never disabled: a test asserts the DC client is constructed WITHOUT
      `verify=False`, and that a verification failure raises an error naming the `ca_bundle` setting rather
      than silently proceeding. `allow_insecure` is asserted to affect the URL scheme check ONLY — a test
      confirms it does not relax certificate verification
- [ ] `reconciler.resolved_statuses` configures the DC absence-probe's resolved-status set, defaulting to
      `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset; a test covers both the default and a custom workflow's names
baseline.summary: J6 — Data Center transport on pycontribs/jira, behind an opt-in extra

## The defect

Found by the ticket-c5b3 sibling sweep after the same bug broke CI there.

`tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py:21` and `tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py:21` both do:

    from tests.unit import _audit_page_helpers as H  # noqa: E402

`tests` is not an importable package: neither `tests/__init__.py` nor `tests/unit/__init__.py` exists. A `tests.`-rooted absolute import therefore only resolves when the repository root happens to be on `sys.path`, which is true under `python -m pytest` (it inserts the cwd) and FALSE under the bare `pytest` console script that CI runs. Demonstrated on ticket c5b3 with an identical import:

    pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_module_size_reconciliation_heldout.py
      -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests'
    python -m pytest <same file>
      -> passes

## Why it is not failing today

It is MASKED, not correct. Both modules call `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")` and `pytest.importorskip("httpx")` on the two lines ABOVE the import (hence the `# noqa: E402`). The `[ui]` extra is absent from the lean CI suite, so the module skips before the broken import line is ever executed. Install the `[ui]` extra and run bare `pytest` and these two modules fail at collection.

That makes this worse than a plain breakage: the tests read as covered while providing no coverage in exactly the environment where the extra IS present.

## The fix

`_audit_page_helpers.py` lives in `tests/unit/`, the same directory as both importers, so the repo's established same-directory bare-name convention applies:

    from _audit_page_helpers import ...

pytest's prepend import mode inserts `tests/unit` into `sys.path` (it is the first ancestor without an `__init__.py`), so a bare name resolves. Every other bare-name test import in this repo is same-directory like this -- `metrics_polyglot_support`, `reviewbot_convergence_support`, `_dc_support`, `test_completion_gate`.

Alternatively, move the helpers to `tests/_audit_page_support.py`: `tests/` is on `sys.path` by DELIBERATE guarantee (`tests/conftest.py` inserts it), which is the mechanism c5b3 used for its cross-directory case via the new `tests/module_size_support.py`.

## Why it was not fixed inside c5b3

c5b3 is an scc-metrics bug fix. These two files are an unrelated feature area (the audit page, story ff6f), the defect cannot currently fire, and editing them there would have been scope creep on a change already at its third patch set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Neither audit-page test module uses a `tests.`-rooted import.
- [x] Both modules import and collect successfully under BARE `pytest` (not just
      `python -m pytest`) with the `[ui]` extra installed, verified from a cwd other than the
      repository root.
- [x] A repository-wide check confirms no `tests.`-rooted import remains anywhere under
      `tests/`; consider a lint rule or a guard test so the pattern cannot return, since the
      failure is invisible under the common `python -m pytest` invocation.
baseline.summary: audit-page tests use a 'tests.'-rooted import that cannot resolve under bare pytest

baseline.description:
## Context

Rebar's plan-review T10 and code-review IaC agents can inspect Terraform as text, but generic file search does not reliably answer module-wide questions: Terraform loads every `.tf` and `.tf.json` file in a module together, local modules cross directory boundaries, and computed values are unknowable without runtime context. That makes unsupported LLM claims about declarations, references, and sources a false-positive/false-negative risk.

This feature supplies query-scoped evidence for LLM findings. It does not duplicate mechanical Terraform validation that belongs in project CI, and it never executes Terraform, OpenTofu, a provider binary, or an apply/plan/validate operation.

## Outcome

Ship an optional `grounding-terraform` extra containing `python-hcl2==8.1.3`. When installed, Terraform tools are exposed only to Terraform-routed Pass-1 and Pass-2 agents in plan review and code review. Core Rebar and projects without Terraform retain the same dependency closure and tool surface.

The final tool surface is:

- `lookup_declaration`: locate a statically addressable declaration and its source location.
- `resolve_reference`: resolve conservative module-scope traversals, including local child outputs, without evaluating expressions or provider schemas.
- `probe_source`: inspect repo-contained local sources and positive registry metadata reachable with existing ambient credentials; it never downloads module contents.
- `corroborate_diagnostic`: independently match a narrow structural diagnostic using an audited `terraform-config-inspect` binary already on `PATH`.

Every call returns the existing `refuted | match | abstain` evidence shape plus a canonical receipt containing the normalized query, code/module digest, backend/version/config, outcome, and result digest. Tool output contains source paths, spans, structural classifications, and hashes, but never credentials or raw literal values.

## Scope and mechanics

- Scope starts from changed or declared `.tf` / `.tf.json` paths. Each affected directory is indexed as one whole Terraform module. The bounded closure follows literal, repo-contained local module sources forward and discovers in-repo literal reverse callers. A changed `.tfvars` file is inspectable directly but is never treated as selected input: Rebar cannot know which variable file Terraform would load.
- A per-agent-call session owns an immutable parse cache and query ledger. Pass 2 must issue its own tool query; it may reuse immutable parse data but cannot accept a Pass-1 receipt as verification.
- The parser receives already-read file bytes in the existing 60-second grounding worker boundary. Out-of-repo paths and escaping symlinks are rejected. Syntax errors, duplicate/ambiguous declarations, computed values, provider-defined attributes, dynamic sources, and runtime-dependent expressions abstain.
- The whole query abstains without partial conclusions if its closure exceeds 64 modules, 5,000 Terraform files, or 32 MiB.
- Actual repository reads are merged into agent usage as synthetic file reads. Membership globs for `**/*.tf` and `**/*.tf.json` use the existing signed read-set glob hashing so a later sibling file addition invalidates plan-review evidence without requiring the optional parser at claim time.
- Registry access is positive-only. Environment `TF_TOKEN_<hostname>` credentials and static Terraform credential files may be used with Terraform's precedence rules. Rebar never prompts, executes credential helpers, returns tokens, or treats 401/403/404, TLS/proxy failures, timeouts, rate limits, or malformed responses as proof that a source does not exist.
- V1 does not fetch remote module contents. The ADR records that remote fetch using ambient credentials is approved as a future extension if demand justifies it, with the same containment, redaction, and abstention rules.
- `terraform-config-inspect` is the only optional executable allowed in V1. It receives a minimal copied snapshot of approved module files, closed stdin, a scrubbed environment, and a bounded process group; its JSON is schema-checked and its absolute path, binary digest, and discoverable version are recorded. Absence, output skew, errors, or a non-match abstain. TFLint, Trivy, tfparse, terraform-ls, terraform-docs, Terraform, OpenTofu, and provider executables are not invoked.

## Positive rationale

Conservative structural evidence addresses the LLM's uncertainty while keeping deterministic validation in client CI. `python-hcl2` owns HCL parsing, HashiCorp's shallow `terraform-config-inspect` provides optional independent corroboration, and Rebar owns only safe orchestration, scope closure, redaction, receipts, and review routing. Abstention is preferable to recreating Terraform evaluation semantics.

## Out of scope

- Running `terraform validate`, `terraform plan`, `terraform init/get`, OpenTofu, providers, policy scanners, plugins, or repository-supplied executable/config hooks.
- Evaluating expressions, cloud state, provider schemas, variable precedence, or whether an arbitrary `.tfvars` file is selected.
- Accepting a caller-produced plan artifact; the subject is Terraform in the client project running Rebar.
- Downloading or executing remote module content in V1.
- Turning grounding into a scanner or a standalone CI validator. Tools answer agent queries and do not originate findings.

## Decomposition

1. A plan-review vertical slice ships the optional parser/index, `lookup_declaration`, `resolve_reference`, signed read receipts, and Terraform-only Pass-1/Pass-2 routing.
2. A dependent code-review slice reuses that session for the IaC overlay and its verifier.
3. A dependent source-probe slice adds local and positive registry-source evidence with ambient-credential redaction and access-error abstention.
4. A dependent authoritative-corroboration slice adds the sole allowlisted `terraform-config-inspect` adapter and live contract canary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Installing `nava-rebar[grounding-terraform]` adds exactly `python-hcl2==8.1.3`; lean-core subprocess tests prove `import rebar` and non-Terraform reviews neither import `hcl2` nor advertise Terraform tools.
- [ ] Plan-review T10 Pass 1 and evidence-bearing Pass 2 can independently call `lookup_declaration` and `resolve_reference` over the complete bounded affected-module closure; non-Terraform criteria cannot see those tools.
- [ ] Code-review IaC Pass 1 and evidence-bearing Pass 2 receive the same grounding operations for changed Terraform, while non-IaC overlays and reviews do not.
- [ ] `probe_source` returns positive local/registry evidence only from repo-contained files or metadata reachable with ambient credentials, and every access/error/ambiguity arm returns a closed abstention without asserting nonexistence.
- [ ] `corroborate_diagnostic` can report only a matching, schema-valid `terraform-config-inspect` result from the hardened snapshot; a clean/absent/skewed/error result abstains and no other Terraform-related executable is launched.
- [ ] Canonical receipts redact credentials and literal payloads, and signed plan-review read sets include every concrete Terraform file read plus membership protection that detects a newly added module sibling.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0111-terraform-structural-grounding.md` records the trust boundary, OSS rationale, V1 prohibitions, and approved future ambient-credential remote-fetch direction; `docs/grounding.md` documents install, routing, limits, outcomes, and abstentions.

## Verification

Each child carries tier-specific commands and observable oracles. The epic is verified by the union of those child criteria; no live Terraform/cloud execution is part of completion.
baseline.summary: Optional Terraform structural grounding for IaC review agents
