## Problem

The scheduled **Verify Authorship Identity** workflow (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`, job `verify-identity (authenticated-authorship gate)`) fails at the step **"Fail closed if the blobless checkout pack exceeds its limit"**. The guard compares `git count-objects -v` `size-pack:` against `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` (verify-identity.yml:47, value `102400` KiB = 100 MiB) and fails closed when exceeded.

Decisive log (run 33253701193, sha `5fb693345b0c`):
```
REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 102400
##[error]checkout pack is 492830 KiB; limit is 102400 KiB
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```
So the checkout pack is **492830 KiB ≈ 481 MiB**, ~4.8× the 100 MiB limit.

## This is a regression, not a chronic config

`Verify Authorship Identity` history (schedule, ~4×/day) shows a clean green→red boundary:
- last success: `2026-08-23T01:20:35Z`
- first failure: `2026-08-23T07:07:44Z`
- red on **every** run since (12+ consecutive at time of filing, through 2026-08-29T12:55).

So the pack crossed the 100 MiB threshold around 2026-08-23 and has kept growing. Failing runs in window: 33239620291, 33253701193 (both sha `5fb693345b0c`), plus the same failure every prior scheduled run back to 2026-08-23.

## Root cause hypothesis

Repo/tickets-branch object growth pushed the blobless checkout pack past the CI limit. This correlates with tickets-store growth — see closed P1 bug `absurd-zoometric-bobwhite` (f9ee-5ad5-4a78-4147, "tickets branch/store exceeds 1 GiB after history reclaim"). The reclaim there targeted a fresh clone ≤150 MB, but the CI gate's blobless checkout is now 481 MiB, so either growth resumed post-reclaim or the 100 MiB limit no longer reflects the store's steady-state size. It also plausibly correlates with the gerrit data-disk-high alarm / AWS data-disk sweep (repo growth on the box).

## What needs deciding

1. Is 481 MiB expected steady-state (limit too low → raise `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` deliberately), or is this unbounded growth that needs another reclaim/gc / packing-strategy fix?
2. Quantify current pack composition (blob vs tree vs history, tickets branch vs main) to attribute the growth — mirror the methodology used in f9ee.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Current `size-pack` for the exact CI checkout reproduced and attributed by object type / ref.
- [x] Root cause of the 08-23 crossing identified (growth event vs limit-too-low).
- [x] Either the limit is intentionally re-set with justification, or the growth is reclaimed so the gate is green, with evidence of a passing `Verify Authorship Identity` run.

## Evidence
- Failing run: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33253701193 (sha `5fb693345b0c`)
- Earlier same failure: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/33239620291
- Limit source: `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml:47` (`REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 102400`); guard at lines 62-63.

**AC completion evidence (see resolution comment 2026-08-29):** AC1/AC2 met by the Stage-1 dossier + Phase-1-exit RCA comments (481 MiB pack, ~90% tree objects; proven 08-23 organic growth step-change). AC3 met via the "limit intentionally re-set with justification" arm: budget raised 100→550 MiB by commit d0bcd6202789 (ticket a8ba, closed), restore tracked by 0894; passing run = Verify Authorship Identity scheduled run 33285210617 (sha 454f875e, 2026-08-30T01:14Z, success). Evidence is CI/history/cross-ticket (outside the code snapshot).
baseline.summary: Verify Authorship Identity scheduled gate red since 2026-08-23: blobless checkout pack (481 MiB) exceeds the 100 MiB limit

baseline.description:
Portable Python public-API surface drift gate (griffe-check-style, test-linked).

## Context / Problem

rebar's Python public API is described by two hand-authored docs (`docs/api-stability.md`, `docs/reuse-surface.md`). `docs/reuse-surface.md` needs recurring manual upkeep (touched by most RP-04 slices). The only automated guard is `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` (ticket f5df): it hardcodes a curated SUBSET of signatures (signing, prompt library, runner/contracts, workflow executor) and must be hand-edited in lockstep with every signature change — narrow, and a manual burden. The config-key half of the original audit is already delivered (sibling ticket 3199 shipped `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` + `docs/config-reference.md` with a portable test-based drift gate) and is OUT of scope here.

## Approach

Add a `griffe check`-style **public-API surface drift gate** — snapshot the current public surface into a committed baseline and fail on any diff — implemented with the same self-contained, pure-stdlib introspection the repo already uses (`inspect`/`importlib`, as in `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` and `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`). This is the direct analog of the existing config-key drift gate and avoids adding `griffe` (or any new) dependency; a self-contained approach is already proven portable and idiomatic here. We do NOT build a generated Markdown API reference — the OSS evidence (griffe/mkdocstrings ecosystem, setuptools-scm's `api-check`) shows the high-ROI move is a surface diff gate, not an auto-generated doc. The hand-authored `docs/api-stability.md` / `docs/reuse-surface.md` stay the curated narrative; the gate guards the surface, the prose stays human.

- New `scripts/gen_api_surface.py`: introspects the surface, `--update` writes the committed
  baseline JSON, `--check` (default) diffs live vs baseline and exits non-zero on drift with a
  clear "run `--update`" remediation message. Mirrors `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`'s
  `main([...])`/`--check` shape.
- New `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`: the committed baseline snapshot.
- New `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py`: the portable unit-tier test that fails under
  `make test` (no CI-provider dependency) when the surface drifts. It runs the authoritative
  check in a clean subprocess so it reflects the real installed surface (immune to the unit
  tier's autouse `rebar.append_session_log` monkeypatch in `tests/unit/conftest.py:86`).
- Delete `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`; the new baseline captures its whole subset
  automatically and dedicated subsumption assertions prove no coverage is lost.

**Source-of-truth rule (pinned):** the guarded surface is the union, over a pinned `MODULES` list, of each module's public members — `module.__all__` when defined (the `rebar` facade and `rebar.signing`/`rebar.llm.workflow.executor` define one), else every non-underscore attribute the module OWNS (`__module__` is that module/submodule, or a module-level constant with no `__module__`), excluding imported re-exports and submodules. `MODULES` = the `rebar` facade (`src/rebar/__init__.py:171` `__all__`) plus the reuse subsystems documented in `docs/reuse-surface.md`: `rebar.signing`, `rebar.llm.runner`, `rebar.llm.contracts`, `rebar.llm.findings`, `rebar.llm.prompting.prompts`, `rebar.llm.workflow.executor`. Per symbol the baseline pins: callable parameter list (name + kind + default-repr), class bases + dataclass fields + public-method signatures, and the value of pinned immutable constants (guards e.g. `prompts.FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `prompts.EXECUTION_MODES`). The baseline is stored as committed JSON at `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` and updated only via `python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --update`.

## Scope

- `scripts/gen_api_surface.py` (new) — the introspection + `--check`/`--update` gate.
- `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` (new) — the committed surface baseline.
- `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` (new) — the portable drift + subsumption test.
- `tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py` (deleted) — subsumed by the new gate.
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — update the one-line note that points readers at the old test so it
  names the new gate + baseline + update command.

## Testing

Portable unit-tier tests (`make test`, no CI-provider dependency):
- Committed baseline is current: the gate `--check` exits 0 in a clean subprocess.
- RED→GREEN drift detection: injecting a removed symbol, an added symbol, and a renamed
  parameter each makes `--check`/`diff_surface` report the drift (exit 1); an identical
  surface reports no drift.
- Baseline-update path: `--update` writes the surface then `--check` is clean; a deliberately
  stale baseline trips `--check` and re-running `--update` accepts the intended change.
- Subsumption: the exact signing / prompt-library / runner-contract / workflow-executor subset
  the deleted `test_reuse_surface_doc.py` hardcoded is still asserted present in the surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A portable test in `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` runs under `make test` with no
      CI-provider dependency and asserts the live public Python API surface matches the
      committed baseline `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`, failing on any removed/renamed
      public symbol or changed signature. Oracle: `make test` collects the test; the gate
      subprocess `python scripts/gen_api_surface.py --check` exits 0 on a clean tree.
- [x] The gate derives the surface from the pinned source-of-truth rule stated in Approach
      (`MODULES` public members via `__all__`-or-owned). Oracle: `test_baseline_file_is_committed_and_wellformed`
      asserts every pinned module appears in the baseline.
- [x] The hardcoded-subset assertions in `test_reuse_surface_doc.py` are removed and subsumed
      with no loss of coverage. Oracle: that file no longer exists; the four `test_subsumes_*`
      tests assert the same signing/prompt/runner/workflow signatures are guarded.
- [x] An intentional surface change is accommodated by the documented `--update` step,
      exercised by a test. Oracle: `test_intentional_change_is_accommodated_by_updating_the_baseline`
      shows a stale baseline fails `--check` and passes after `--update`.
- [x] RED→GREEN: a test proves the gate catches an injected surface drift (added/removed public
      symbol, renamed param). Oracle: `test_check_trips_when_a_public_symbol_is_removed` /
      `_added` / `test_check_trips_when_a_signature_changes` assert exit 1 and the named drift line.
baseline.summary: Portable Python public-API surface drift gate (griffe-check-style, test-linked)

baseline.description:
## Context
F09 found maintained guidance outside its approved file set that still describes current plan-review, completion-verifier, or `verify-signature` behavior as HMAC-based. ADR 0049 and `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md` record the asymmetric DSSE and SSHSIG contract. Historical ADRs, migration records, and experiment corpora must remain unchanged. Generic HMAC helpers remain supported for consumers outside the two gated operation-certificate kinds.

Known candidate paths include `docs/attest-substrate.md`, `docs/config.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, `docs/identity.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, `src/rebar/_lib_identity.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py`. Generated references must be changed only through their canonical sources (`scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` for `docs/mcp-reference.md`, `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` for `docs/cli-reference.md`).

## Plan
- Re-run a bounded search over maintained documentation, public help, docstrings, and developer comments.
- Classify each match as current operation-certificate behavior, generic HMAC behavior, legacy compatibility, or historical evidence.
- Correct current behavior to identify DSSE, SSHSIG, Ed25519, and environment attribution.
- State that legacy HMAC plan-review and completion-verifier records remain readable but cannot certify a current gated operation.
- Preserve accurate generic HMAC API documentation and historical records.
- Do not add mechanical prose or character enforcement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every maintained current-gate statement uses the implemented asymmetric operation-certificate model (checked: `grep -rn -i "hmac" docs/attest-substrate.md docs/config.md docs/exit-codes.md docs/identity.md docs/llm-framework.md src/rebar/_lib_identity.py src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` leaves only generic-HMAC API text, legacy-compatibility notes, or historical citations).
- [x] Public library and MCP descriptions match current return shapes and verdicts (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` passes after regeneration).
- [x] Generic HMAC documentation retains its implemented non-gate meaning.
- [x] ADRs, migrations, and experiment corpora remain unchanged (checked: `git diff --stat` touches no `docs/adr/`, `docs/migrations/`, or `docs/experiments/` path).
- [x] Canonical generators are used for generated artifacts (checked: `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` reports no staleness after the change).
- [x] Focused documentation and interface checks pass without a full suite when the final change is limited to Markdown; because source docstrings change here, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the targeted tests above must pass.

## Verification
- `grep -rn -i "hmac" docs/attest-substrate.md docs/config.md docs/exit-codes.md docs/identity.md docs/llm-framework.md src/rebar/_lib_identity.py src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — every remaining match is generic-API, legacy-compatibility, or a historical citation.
- `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py && git diff --exit-code docs/mcp-reference.md` — generated reference is regenerated through its canonical source and current.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck` — source docstring edits stay clean.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py tests/unit/test_signing.py` — reference staleness and signing-surface tests pass.
- `git diff --stat -- docs/adr docs/migrations docs/experiments` — empty: historical records untouched.
baseline.summary: Correct remaining maintained operation-certificate guidance

baseline.description:
ADR settling what ADR 0050 deferred: how a self-contained rebar MCP HTTP server runs on the AWS box (Gerrit + review-bot + opcert), so copilot/codex/claude can drive ALL rebar operations through it (dogfooding). Output: one accepted ADR under docs/adr/ + an ADR 0079 amendment. This ticket writes only the decision record; the infra/autodeploy/secrets/guidance slices implement it. No code, infra, AWS, or Jira mutation here.

## Decisions (settled with the operator 2026-08-24)

### 1. Exposure + auth — nginx `/mcp/` TLS edge + `static` verifier + per-client bearer PATs
Loopback-bound `rebar-mcp` HTTP (`transport=http`, `http_tls_at_edge=true`, allowed hosts/origins set, `auth_resource_server_url` set) behind an nginx `/mcp/` TLS-terminating location — the documented `docs/mcp-auth.md` §5 recipe, mirroring opcert's TLS edge. Verifier mode = **static**; each client (copilot/codex/claude) presents its own bearer PAT in the `Authorization` header. Rationale + prior art: research confirmed all three clients support a static `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header for remote HTTP MCP and none require OAuth, so `static` is the minimal mode that satisfies all three clients. This is a **standard self-contained rebar MCP server** (operator intent: analogous to a user MCP install), NOT the opcert SigV4/API-Gateway `proxy` pattern. Records the ADR-0050-required non-loopback-bind + TLS-at-edge acknowledgements.

### 2. Autodeploy drain — blue-green immutable-release, modeled on the LOCAL main-tracking updater
The MCP autodeploy target does NOT copy the review-bot's stop-and-health-drain (`docker compose up -d` + `/health` in_flight gate). It follows the local `origin/main`-tracking updater (`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh`, ticket sticky-genetic-narwhal): immutable release + atomic pointer swap + retire-when-idle. Concretely on the box (docker): build the new image → start a NEW `rebar-mcp` container → health-check it → **atomically flip the nginx `/mcp/` upstream** to it (the `current`-pointer rename analog) → **retire the old container off the critical path**, gated by a flock-style "still serving?" check (active connections / its own in_flight), with bounded retention + a hard cap + an SNS alert when a busy old container cannot be reclaimed. Overlap is capped **one-in / one-out** (never N parallel) and guarded by a memory-pressure alarm so the transient 2× `rebar-mcp` never forces the t4g.large (8 GiB) up to t4g.xlarge.

Positive rationale (why this over the review-bot pattern): it eliminates the review-bot's unsolved saturation gotcha (bug 7b4a) — a shared MCP server driven by N agents pipelines long billable LLM ops so `in_flight` may never reach 0; a gauge-gated bound would then be exhausted and kill an in-flight certified op, and a bigger bound only defers the same kill. Blue-green decouples retirement from the deploy, so a never-idle server never blocks a deploy or forces a kill. In-place reload is rejected outright because rebar lazy-imports late (e.g. `commit_impact` during `close`, after the minutes-long completion verifier), so swapping code under a running process risks an ImportError mid-op (two real local incidents). A killed MCP op is client-visible (dropped HTTP connection → the agent retries), and rebar's event-sourced writes are idempotent (an unpersisted op-cert is simply re-requested), so retirement is safe.

The `in_flight` gauge counts only long-running / certified / LLM ops (review_plan, verify_completion, review_code, scan_spec — 30 s to minutes); trivial sub-second reads are not counted (killing them is harmless, the client retries). The gauge is used for the RETIRE check, not to gate the deploy.

### 3. Certified-op routing — MCP signs under the box's EXISTING opcert env; code review stays the Gerrit vote
For plan-review + completion-verifier certs minted via MCP to be enforceable, the MCP server signs them under the box's **EXISTING** opcert signing environment — the same `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + signing key already pinned in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` on `main` and already named by the single-valued `verify.require_environment` (per ADR 0049). There is **no new env_id and no change to the single-valued enforcement gate**: the box is not a distinct third environment, so a cert minted via MCP verifies against the same env the opcert job-service already uses. (Operator ruling 2026-08-24, Option A: a distinct MCP env_id was rejected because it would require making `verify.require_environment` multi-valued — a behavioral change to ADR 0049's single-env model, out of scope here.) rebar issues exactly TWO op-cert kinds (plan-review at claim, completion-verifier at close, ADR 0049); there is **no code-review op-cert**. "Certified code review" = the existing Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot vote already on the box — NO new op-cert kind is introduced. The opcert job-service + `remote-cert` client are left coexisting (additive, not replaced). The epic's item-7 wording ("code review ... certified through the MCP server") is corrected accordingly in the guidance slice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A new `docs/adr/00NN-mcp-on-box.md` exists with status **Accepted**, deciding all three items above with the stated rationale, and cross-referencing ADR 0049 (two op-certs), ADR 0050 (RS-only, static verifier, deferred AWS recipe now filled), ADR 0079 (autodeploy), and the local main-tracking updater precedent (sticky-genetic-narwhal). Checked: `test -f docs/adr/*mcp-on-box*.md` and `grep -i 'Status: Accepted'` in it.
- [x] ADR 0079 carries an amendment describing the `mcp` blue-green pointer-swap target (immutable release + atomic nginx-upstream flip + retire-when-idle), explicitly contrasted with the review-bot stop-and-drain and noting the bug-7b4a saturation rationale. Checked: `grep -i 'mcp\|blue-green' docs/adr/0079-autodeploy-on-box-timer.md`.
- [x] The ADR names the concrete config keys the infra slice sets (`transport`, `http_tls_at_edge`, allowed hosts/origins, `auth_resource_server_url`, verifier `static`) and the trusted-env keys (`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`, `verify.require_environment`). Checked: `grep` the new ADR for each named key.
- [x] No behavioral code/infra change lands under this ticket. Checked: `git diff --stat` on the change shows only `docs/adr/` paths.

## Testing
Tier: **documentation** — an ADR/decision record with no runtime behavior, so the oracle is the record itself. Verification is by file inspection + `grep` exactly as named in each acceptance item above: the ADR file exists with `Status: Accepted`, contains the three decisions with the named config/trusted-env keys and the four ADR cross-references, the ADR 0079 amendment text is present, and `git diff --stat` shows only `docs/adr/` touched. No automated test tier applies (no code path changes); a lower tier is insufficient because there is nothing executable to assert.

Blocks every implementation slice (infra, autodeploy, secrets, client-config, guidance, trusted-env registration, live verification).
baseline.summary: ADR: MCP-on-box exposure + auth + autodeploy drain + certified-op routing

# J3 — Pin a `RichTextCodec` contract (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

Rich-text encoding is one of the three real differences between Jira Cloud and Data Center: Cloud's REST v3 requires Atlassian Document Format (a nested JSON document; sending a plain string returns 400), while DC's REST v2 carries descriptions and comment bodies as plain text / wiki markup. Today ADF is hardwired into the Cloud path — `adapters/jira/adf.py` provides `fit_text_to_adf_limit` and the decode, and `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72`'s `map_fields_to_remote` calls `outbound_fields._load_adf()` inline. PR #120's answer was to copy that whole method and change the single ADF line, which is the duplication this epic exists to prevent.

## Approach

Define a `RichTextCodec` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with two operations: `fit_outbound` (fit a local string to the deployment's rich-text limit, returning the deployment's wire shape) and `decode_inbound` (turn a wire body into plain text). Provide two implementations — `AdfCodec`, which delegates to the existing `adapters/jira/adf.py` with no logic change, and `WikiTextCodec`, a character-count fit plus an identity decode.

The shared `map_fields_to_remote` then takes the codec as a constructor dependency, so exactly one implementation of the mapping exists and the ADF-vs-wiki difference is a parameter. The same codec is the dependency J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] injects into the relocated `_sanitize_description`, whose `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call IS this seam — so if J2 lands first with a minimal `Callable[[str], str]` fit function as a placeholder, this story widens that placeholder to the full `RichTextCodec` and re-points the sanitizer at it. Either landing order works; what must not happen is `jira_family/` importing the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py` directly. Cloud is constructed with `AdfCodec` and its behavior is unchanged, proven by J1's pinned oracles [rebar:acb2-1823-2f0d-415b].

**Alternative rejected:** a boolean or enum flag (`use_adf=True`) threaded through the mapper. It puts the branch back inside the shared code, grows a branch per deployment type, and gives the codec no place to own its own limit constant.

**Alternative rejected:** copying `map_fields_to_remote` per adapter (PR #120). One line differs; the other thirty drift.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (new) — the Protocol + `WikiTextCodec`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py` — wrapped by `AdfCodec`, logic unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` — the shared mapper takes the codec.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier for each codec (pure transforms) plus a contract test run against BOTH implementations, since the point of the story is that they are interchangeable behind one Protocol.

- shared contract, parameterized over both codecs: a short string round-trips through
  `fit_outbound` → `decode_inbound` to itself; an over-limit string is fitted to at most the limit and its
  decode is a prefix of the original.
- Cloud-specific: `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` produces the same ADF document the current
  `fit_text_to_adf_limit` produces for the same input — asserted against J1's pinned value.
- DC-specific: `WikiTextCodec` truncates at its character limit and marks the truncation; `decode_inbound`
  returns `""` for `None` and passes a string through unchanged.
- contrast case: a non-`str` value is passed through untouched by both codecs rather than coerced, matching the
  current mapper's behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test runs against both `AdfCodec` and `WikiTextCodec` and passes for each
- [ ] `AdfCodec` output for the J1-pinned input equals the J1-pinned expected ADF document
- [ ] `grep -rn '_load_adf\|fit_text_to_adf_limit' src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` shows those names
      reached only from inside `AdfCodec`
- [ ] exactly one definition of `map_fields_to_remote` exists in the tree
baseline.summary: J3 — pin a RichTextCodec contract (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for Data Center)

# Guard the provider session: wrap run() in `with ProviderSession(...)`

ADR 0056 decision 2. A CORRECTNESS fix, not a refactor — independently valuable, and it should land even if the rest of the decomposition is descoped.

## The defect (RE-MEASURED at c1fc3cee4, after e6bd and 8229 landed)

    runner.py:294   provider_session = ProviderSession(cfg)   # its builders open httpx clients
    runner.py:445   try:                                       # <-- guard starts 151 lines later
    runner.py:495   finally:
    runner.py:501       provider_session.close()

Lines 294–444 sit OUTSIDE the guard, and code in that window raises BY DESIGN: `_check_tool_capability(...)` is called at runner.py:337 and raises `LLMConfigError`. Anything raising there leaks an opened `httpx.AsyncClient` — one per affected call.

`ProviderSession.__enter__` / `__exit__` ALREADY EXIST at **providers.py:323 and :326** and are never used: `grep -c 'with ProviderSession' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returns 0. Meanwhile providers.py:18–24 documents "`runner.run()` wraps its body in `with ProviderSession(cfg) as session:`" — a caller that does not exist. This ticket makes that docstring true.

NOTE ON COORDINATES: an earlier version of this plan cited 301/474/582 for the three sites and providers.py:295–299 for the dunders. Those were correct when written and are now ALL STALE — e6bd removed the except spine and 8229 removed the settings block, shifting everything. The numbers above are re-measured at c1fc3cee4. **Re-locate by CONTENT, not by these offsets** if the base moves again.

## Approach

Move construction into a `with` covering provider resolution through the call and teardown, and drop the now-redundant `finally: provider_session.close()` — `__exit__` owns it. Preserve the existing best-effort semantics (close logs, never raises).

CONSTRAINT: `assert_gated("agentic filesystem tools")` at **runner.py:261** is a FAIL-CLOSED security check and MUST stay AHEAD of provider construction. Do not reorder it into the guarded region in a way that opens a client before the refusal path runs.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — the `with`, and removal of the redundant `finally`.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` — **REQUIRED, and this ticket owns it.**
  See below; omitting it breaks that test at runtime.
- `tests/unit/` — the leak test.

### THIS TICKET OWNS ONE STUB REPAIR — it is not optional and not a "later child" problem

`tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:111` defines `_NoBuildProviderSession` and installs it at :124 via `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "ProviderSession", _NoBuildProviderSession)`. MEASURED: that stub implements `__init__`, `supports`, `is_resolvable` and `close` — and **NOT** `__enter__` / `__exit__`. The moment `run()` says `with ProviderSession(cfg) as ...`, the stub stops satisfying the context-manager protocol and that test fails at runtime.

**Add `__enter__` (returning `self`) and `__exit__` (calling `self.close()`) to that stub IN THE SAME COMMIT as the `with`.** This is a stub gaining the protocol the real object already has (providers.py:323/326) — NOT a weakened assertion, so it is compatible with the "no test ASSERTION changed" criterion.

This is a DIFFERENT failure mode from the six `monkeypatch.setattr` rebind hazards the parent story documents: nothing moved modules here, so re-importing a name fixes nothing. The stub's INTERFACE fell behind the call site. Do not go looking for a module-globals explanation.

## Testing

Unit tier with a stubbed builder recording opens/closes; no network.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts that when the pre-call window raises (e.g. `_check_tool_capability`), the
      session's client is STILL closed — this test FAILS against today's code, so it cannot pass
      vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the happy path closes EXACTLY once (a `with` plus a leftover `finally` would
      double-close, which the stub must be able to detect)
- [ ] `grep -c 'with ProviderSession' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is 1, so providers.py:18–24 no longer
      documents an absent caller
- [ ] a close that raises is still logged and never propagated (best-effort semantics unchanged)
- [ ] `_NoBuildProviderSession` in `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` gains
      `__enter__`/`__exit__` in THIS commit, and that test file passes
- [ ] `assert_gated("agentic filesystem tools")` still executes BEFORE any provider client is
      constructed — asserted by a test in which the gate refuses and NO client is opened, so the
      fail-closed ordering is proven rather than assumed
- [ ] the full suite passes with no test ASSERTION weakened, skipped or deleted
baseline.summary: Guard the provider session with a context manager in run()

## Context
115b/8c4f reconciled 13 benign fsck ORPHAN_EVENTs caused by a distributed write race: the Jira reconciler (env_id=reconciler) writes an assignee EDIT, a compaction in a DIFFERENT clone snapshots 3.7s-147s later without having observed that EDIT (so source_event_uuids omits it), then the reconciler re-emits an identical EDIT after the snapshot. fsck flags the pre-snapshot EDIT as orphaned. Live state is always correct (the post-snapshot duplicate drives it), so these are benign — but they recur and require manual retire-to-zero each time.

## Idea
A durable fix so the race stops generating orphans, e.g.: (a) compaction refuses to snapshot within N seconds of an unobserved remote write / syncs+refetches immediately before snapshotting; or (b) the reconciler's idempotent re-emit is suppressed when the value is unchanged; or (c) fsck learns to treat a pre-snapshot EDIT whose effect is superseded by an identical post-snapshot EDIT as non-orphan. Evaluate tradeoffs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause reproduced in a test (concurrent compaction + reconciler EDIT).
- [ ] A chosen mitigation implemented so the race no longer produces ORPHAN_EVENTs.
- [ ] Regression test pins that the previously-orphaning sequence now fscks clean.
baseline.summary: Durable fix: compaction-vs-reconciler snapshot write race produces benign fsck ORPHAN_EVENTs

# A stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently

## Context / Problem

Local `rebar reconcile` repeatedly fails with `reconcile: refs/reconciler/lock held by a live pass — yielding` (exit 3) even when the authoritative remote holds no lock and no holder process exists anywhere. Recovery required a manual `git update-ref -d refs/reconciler/lock`, and the condition kept recurring.

Proven mechanism, reproduced end-to-end in a clean sandbox (real bare remote + working clone, real `_ref_lock` primitives, no mocks):

1. The GitHub Actions bridge acquires the lock on the remote (it holds/heartbeats it near-continuously: `git ls-remote origin refs/reconciler/lock` returns a DIFFERENT oid on successive samples).
2. Any local pass calls `read(..., remote="origin")`. `_fetch_ref` (`_ref_lock.py:288-293`) runs `git fetch origin +<ref>:<ref>`, which PLANTS a local copy of the bridge's lock.
3. The bridge releases. `release` in remote mode (`_ref_lock.py:381-406`) pushes a delete to the REMOTE ONLY and never touches the local ref, so the local copy is STRANDED: remote free, local still held.
4. Every later local `read` reports `HELD holder=GHA-bridge` while the remote is free, because `_ref_oid` (`:301-315`) force-fetches and then falls back to `rev-parse` on the surviving local ref. Git cannot delete a local ref via a refspec whose source is absent, so the fetch failing (`fatal: couldn't find remote ref`, exit 128) leaves the orphan intact — contrary to `_fetch_ref`'s own comment claiming it "becomes absent locally = free".
5. `steal()` cannot break it either: `--force-with-lease` against an absent remote ref is rejected as `stale info`, which `_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS` (`:619`) classifies as a CAS mismatch, logged misleadingly as "CAS lost to another contender". Measured: `steal(...)` returns None with the orphan intact.

Net effect: the checkout is wedged FOREVER and manual break-glass is the only escape.

## Why this is a defect (authority)

`docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md` §"Distributed operation": "The lock must be authoritative across CI runners, manual invocations, and clones" and with `remote="origin"` "the remote is the truth". A stranded local ref overriding a free remote violates that invariant directly.

Same ADR §"Operator break-glass": "C2's relative-duration lease makes this rarely necessary — a crashed holder's lock becomes steal-able after one lease interval automatically." Here it is NEVER steal-able and break-glass is ALWAYS required. The ADR also names both halves of a clear (`git push origin :refs/reconciler/lock` AND `git update-ref -d refs/reconciler/lock`), showing the design knows the local ref is a separate artifact the release path must handle.

## Acceptance criteria

- After a remote holder acquires, a local pass reads, and the remote holder releases, a later local `read(..., remote="origin")` reports the lock FREE (not HELD).
- `release(..., remote="origin")` leaves no local `refs/reconciler/lock` behind.
- A stranded local ref is reclaimable without manual intervention — either it reads free, or `steal()` breaks it.
- A GENUINELY live remote holder still reads as HELD, so cross-machine mutual exclusion is preserved (the fix must not make every lock look free).
- No local pass source is introduced or required: the Reconciler Bridge runs on GitHub Actions only.

## Ruled out during investigation

- The steal kill-switch: `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_STEAL` defaults ON (`__main__.py:170-184`) and is unset locally; driving `steal_pass_lock` directly DID break a stale lease (fence 2 -> 3). Stealing is not disabled.
- A hidden local scheduler: no git hook, LaunchAgent (only a build updater + worktree GC), crontab, MCP tool, or implicit CLI path runs a reconcile pass. Operator-run local passes plus this bug fully explain recurrence.
- `_advisory_lock.py`'s fail-closed swallow: no exception is raised; `steal()` returns None cleanly.
baseline.summary: Stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently

## Context / Problem

Ticket e39f-5055-f5af-424a makes the reconciler's inbound link-removal path (G5, apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one) converge by removing exactly the mirrored (target, relation) link. The safety analysis surfaced a PRE-EXISTING blind spot inherited from 2b16's design: managed_refs marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY (reducer/_managed_refs.py — strictly monotonic), so G3 cannot distinguish a brand-new never-pushed local link from a peer-deleted one. G4 (same-pass outbound-ADD suppression) covers that blind spot ONLY when the outbound differ emits the re-ADD; outbound_links.py::_diff_links dedups ADDs direction-agnostically on (vendor_type, target_key) ('intentionally NOT deduped on relation'), so a local link whose vendor type collides with an existing remote link in the other direction (blocks vs inward Blocks) is never pushed AND not G4-protected — an inbound removal record for it can reach G5 and remove a never-pushed local link. This is order-dependently true TODAY (when the never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent, pair-scoped unlink removes it after G5's relation match passes); e39f makes the outcome order-independent but does not add a discriminator.

## Approach

Design pass: persist enough peer-link history (e.g. record (relation, target) as 'peer-confirmed' only after an outbound link ADD is successfully applied or the link is observed in a fetched snapshot) so _inbound_unlink_one can decline removals of never-peer-confirmed links. Must reconcile with managed_refs monotonicity and compaction (SNAPSHOT restore).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a removal record for a managed-but-never-peer-confirmed link is declined and logged.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k declines`
- [x] a removal for a peer-confirmed link still converges.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py -k converges`
- [x] behavior covered by behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations/_inbound_update_apply_links.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py`
- [x] all four children (S1-S4) are closed and their changes are Verified +1 on Gerrit.
      Proof: `rebar list --parent despotic-floriated-leopard` shows every child `closed`

## Testing

Each child carries its own suite and gate commands; the epic is proven by the union of them: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` green on the final child, plus the existing `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` regression suite staying green throughout.

## Chosen direction (operator-approved 2026-08-12; research comments above are the evidence base)

Follow the pattern both maintained comparisons converge on (GitHub ghas-jira-integration; contrast softrams/bulwark): **retain durable association/provenance and perform explicit managed mutations; never treat an unqualified missing link as deletion evidence.**

Concretely: persist a **full peer-confirmation record** per managed link (Jira linkId, direction, the confirming snapshot revision, confirmed-at time) — not a minimal boolean — because Jira exposes deletion as an explicit event keyed by stable linkId, and the completeness tracking S2 needs is impossible with a boolean. A partial/paginated/failed read is NON-EVIDENCE. Backfill grandfathers existing managed links as confirmed-at-upgrade (marked as such) so the first post-upgrade run does not decline every legitimate removal.

## Decomposition (children)
- S1: define + persist the peer-confirmation record (written on successful outbound link ADD; survives SNAPSHOT compaction; reconciled with managed_refs monotonicity).
- S2: populate confirmations from fetched authoritative snapshots, recording snapshot completeness; partial reads can never confirm nor deny.
- S3: _inbound_unlink_one declines-and-logs removal of never-peer-confirmed links (behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations).
- S4: backfill migration marking existing managed links confirmed-at-upgrade.
baseline.summary: Discriminate never-pushed managed links from peer deletions in the inbound removal path

## Context / Problem
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` (854 lines) mandates a fresh worktree from `origin/main` (lines 40-52) and a Step-7 sibling sweep (lines 741-785), but has **no step before Phase 1** that (a) searches the tracker for an existing report or (b) establishes which build the bug was reported against. Verified against the tree: `grep -c 'Step 0' SKILL.md` = 0; `grep -i duplicat SKILL.md` = no match; no mention of a reported-against version. The only tracker-search text is one advisory bullet inside Stage 1 (line 205, "Prior fixes & regression history … tracker search") which is about *prior fixes*, is not a gate, and records no link/resume/file decision. The search-before-file rule otherwise lives only in `AGENTS.md`.

Scale (verified, `rebar list --type bug`): 764 bug tickets, **759 closed**, 249 filed 7–21 Aug 2026 — closed tickets dominate, so an open-only sweep is nearly blind. Task `eac3-ed70-764a-4f9e` is the complementary tracker-side duplicate detection.

## Approach
Insert a top-level section `# Step 0 — Orient` into SKILL.md **after** the "Approval gate" section and **before** the "Triage: full protocol or fast path?" section, so it precedes `# Phase 1` on **both** the full protocol and the fast path. It has three actions; each writes one line into the Stage 1 dossier (which is prose in SKILL.md — there is no `phases/` directory and no separate template file).

**(a) Tracker sweep.** `rebar search "<symptom words>"` — full-text over titles/descriptions/comments/tags across **all statuses, including closed tickets** (759 of 764 bug tickets are closed, so `--status open` alone misses the corpus) — plus `rebar list --type bug --status open,in_progress` for in-flight work. Outcome is recorded either as "no existing ticket found for <queries>" or as a link/resume: link the new report `duplicates` the existing ticket (the `duplicates` relation exists — `rebar link --help`), or resume the existing one instead of filing.

**(b) The reported-against floor.** A rebar ticket has **no `rebar-version` field** (verified: absent from `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`; the only `rebar-version:` in the tree is the signing-manifest stamp in `src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py`, unrelated to tickets). Two real sources, in order:

1. **The report text** — a `rebar --version` output, a commit sha, or a release tag quoted in
   the bug's description or comments. Authoritative when present.
2. **The ticket's `created_at`** — `ticket_state.schema.json:42-44` documents it as an
   **integer of nanoseconds** (`time.time_ns()`), e.g. `1787354756915214001`. `git --before=`
   accepts an approxidate or `@<unix-seconds>` — it does **not** accept raw nanoseconds, and
   silently mis-reads a 19-digit value as far-future seconds, returning the tip. Measured in
   this checkout: `git rev-list -1 --before="1787354756915214001" origin/main` → `960fbfef2f`
   (the tip); `git rev-list -1 --before="@1787354756" origin/main` → `767bb3ead6` (a real
   historical floor). So the skill states the conversion explicitly:
   `git rev-list -1 --before="@$(( <created_at> / 1000000000 ))" origin/main`, and notes that
   `created_at` is nanoseconds and the divide is required.

The result is a **floor**, not the exact build, so the dossier line reads "reported on or after <sha>". Step 0 then runs `git log --oneline <floor-sha>..origin/main -- <suspect paths>` so the hypothesis stage knows whether the suspect code changed since the report. If **neither** source is available, Step 0 records "reported-against version unknown" explicitly and the hypothesis stage treats the whole history as in scope, rather than silently assuming `main`.

**(c) Worktree currency.** Confirm `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `git rev-parse origin/main`; if not, record that rather than proceeding silently on a stale tree.

**Approval-gate consistency.** The Step-0 `duplicates` link is an own-tracker writeback, so it is added to the pre-approved list in the "Carve-out — the project's own tracker" paragraph (SKILL.md lines 121-127), which today enumerates only the RCA comment, the `caused_by` link, the Step-7 sibling tickets, the not-a-bug comment, and the final report comment. Without this, Step 0 would mandate an action the same file gates behind user approval.

## Scope
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` — the new `# Step 0 — Orient` section and the
  carve-out list amendment.
- `tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step0.py` — new content gate (see Testing).

Not in scope: `docs/user-guide.md` (verified: mentions neither `rebar-debug` nor `agent-skills`); `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/phases/` (no such directory — that dir holds only `SKILL.md`, `llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md`, `test-design.md`); `examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md` (untouched, so the byte-identical-copy gate `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` is unaffected).

## Testing
A new unit test `tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step0.py`, modelled on the existing `tests/unit/test_flaky_test_guidance.py` doc-content gate, pins the load-bearing halves: Step 0 exists and is positioned before `# Phase 1`; all three actions are present; the nanosecond→seconds conversion is spelled out; the raw-nanosecond form is **absent**; the unknown-version case is present; the sweep is not open-only; and the carve-out lists the Step-0 link. Existing gates `tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py` (driver `scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py`) and `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` keep passing, as does `make lint`.

## Acceptance Criteria
Let `S = examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`.

- [x] Step 0 exists and precedes Phase 1: `grep -n '^# Step 0 — Orient' "$S"` returns exactly
      one line, and its line number is **less than** that of `grep -n '^# Phase 1' "$S"`.
- [x] All three actions are named in `S`: `grep -c 'rebar search'`, `grep -c 'rebar list --type
      bug --status open,in_progress'`, `grep -c 'git rev-list -1 --before="@'`, and
      `grep -c 'git rev-parse origin/main'` are each `>= 1`.
- [x] The nanosecond conversion is explicit **inside the runnable command**, and the broken
      form is gone: `grep -c 'nanoseconds' "$S"` >= 1,
      `grep -cF 'git rev-list -1 --before="@$(( <created_at> / 1000000000 ))" origin/main' "$S"`
      >= 1, and `grep -c -- '--before="<created_at>"' "$S"` equals `0`.
- [x] No ticket `rebar-version` field is referenced: `grep -c 'rebar-version' "$S"` equals `0`.
- [x] The unknown case is explicit: `grep -c 'reported-against version unknown' "$S"` >= 1.
- [x] The sweep is not open-only: `grep -c 'including closed tickets' "$S"` >= 1.
- [x] The approval-gate carve-out pre-approves the Step-0 link: the paragraph beginning
      `**Carve-out — the project's own tracker.**` contains `Step-0 duplicates link`
      (`grep -c 'Step-0 duplicates link' "$S"` >= 1).
- [x] Gates pass: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step0.py
      tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py -q`
      exits 0, and `make lint` exits 0.

## Review remediation (2026-08-21, rv9)
Blocking fixed: (1) floor source #2 piped a nanosecond `created_at` straight into `git --before=`, which silently returns the tip — the `@<unix-seconds>` conversion is now stated with the measured shas above; (2) Scope named a non-existent `tests/unit/test_skill_frontmatter.py`; the real file is `test_check_skill_frontmatter.py`. Advisories fixed: the non-existent `phases/` directory leaves Scope; the unverifiable "dossier template text" AC is replaced with anchored greps. Also corrected against the tree: the worktree mandate spans lines 40-52 (not 40-43); `docs/user-guide.md` has no rebar-debug content, so it leaves Scope; bug counts are reproduced from `rebar list --type bug`.
baseline.summary: rebar-debug Step 0: search the tracker and compare the reported-against version to main before Phase 1

## Problem

The set of ticket statuses has two masters:

- `src/rebar/types.py:21` `TicketStatus` (7 values), mirrored by
  `schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/ticket_status` — canonical
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:33` `_KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES` — the same 7, hand-copied

The copy does not merely describe; it ASSERTS completeness. `_processors.py:565` raises `ValueError(f"unknown ticket status in snapshot: {status!r}")` on anything outside it. So a status added to `TicketStatus` and written into a snapshot by a newer clone makes that snapshot UNREADABLE to this reducer — it raises rather than degrading. Nothing gates the pair (`grep _KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES tests/` returns nothing).

## Approach — generate-from-canonical

`_KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES = frozenset(get_args(TicketStatus))`. `rebar.types` imports only `typing`, so the reducer can reach it without a cycle; the in-tree precedent is `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py:119`, which already derives its type vocabulary the same way.

This does not collapse a distinct concept (epic AC2): the raise site's message says "unknown ticket status", i.e. it is asking exactly "is this a TicketStatus?", not a narrower question.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `_KNOWN_TICKET_STATUSES` is derived from `TicketStatus`, not re-listed. Verified by a
      test asserting equality with `frozenset(get_args(TicketStatus))` and by the literal tuple
      being gone from the module.
- [x] AC2: a status added to `TicketStatus` is accepted by the reducer with no second edit.
      Verified by a test that extends the compared vocabulary and asserts the derived set follows.
- [x] AC3: behavior is unchanged for all seven current statuses, including that an unknown value
      still raises. Verified by the existing reducer suite plus a test asserting the raise on a
      genuinely unknown status.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "processors or reducer or status" -q` — AC1-AC3 and the
  existing snapshot-replay paths, which are where a mistake here would surface.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Derive the reducer's known ticket statuses from TicketStatus (mirror F6)

## Context / Problem
Gerrit change 1757 (merged as 065af7c163, ticket small-delicious-loris) taught rebar._store.sync._union_merge to recover ONE merge-abort class: untracked files origin wants to create ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge") — quarantine the named paths, retry once. The second proven abort class, variant (b), remains unhandled: tracked files with local working-tree changes — in practice deletions of tracked per-ticket artifacts left by an interrupted compaction fold — make `git merge origin/tickets` abort with "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge". The abort leaves reconverge unable to advance and strands local ticket commits off origin (live recurrence recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73: 119 tracked `.archived` deletions wedged the store). Sibling story untrack-runtime-markers removes the marker sub-class at its source, but an interrupted fold can still leave tracked EVENT-file deletions (compact_txn renames sources to `*.retired` — a rename of a tracked file is a tracked deletion + an untracked creation), so reconverge must self-heal this class regardless.

## Approach
Extend the recovery seam 1757 added in src/rebar/_store/sync.py: on merge failure, additionally detect the "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the paths git names (same parsing pattern as the merged `_untracked_overwrite_paths`). For each named path, act by its status: a working-tree DELETION of a tracked file (`git status --porcelain` reports ` D`) is restored non-destructively via `git checkout -- <path>` (content already at HEAD — nothing can be lost); a working-tree MODIFICATION is first copied into the same quarantine directory 1757 established (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/`) and then restored via `git checkout -- <path>` (the local bytes are preserved in quarantine, the HEAD bytes unblock the merge). Then retry the merge once. Any other failure — including a genuine index/content conflict — keeps today's behavior exactly: `git merge --abort`, keep local, hint `rebar fsck-recover`. Positive rationale: this reuses the exact recovery shape already reviewed and merged for variant (a) (parse-what-git-names, move-never-delete, single retry, fall back to abort), extending one proven seam rather than adding a second recovery mechanism.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_store/sync.py — detect + parse the local-changes abort; restore/quarantine the named paths; single retry.
- tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py — extend the 1757 test module with RED-first coverage for variant (b): tracked-deletion fixture and tracked-modification fixture.

## Testing
- RED first: fixture tracker where HEAD tracks a file, the worktree deletes it, and origin/tickets modifies it; assert the union merge currently aborts and HEAD is un-merged, for the local-changes reason specifically.
- GREEN: same fixture after the fix — merge completes with both parents, the local-only commit stays reachable, the deleted file is back at its merged content.
- Modification path: worktree-modified tracked file named by the abort — quarantine copy exists with the local bytes, merge completes.
- Guard: a genuine content conflict (both sides commit different content) still aborts and keeps local (unchanged behavior); `.tmp-event-*` and paths git does not name are untouched.
- Mutation check: skipping the restore step returns the RED assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A reconverge whose union merge aborts only on local changes to tracked store-artifact paths now completes keeping both parents, with no local commit orphaned; checked by the new RED-to-GREEN tests.
- [x] A worktree modification named by the abort is preserved byte-for-byte in the quarantine directory before restore; checked by test comparing quarantined bytes.
- [x] A genuine merge conflict still aborts, keeps local, and hints fsck-recover; checked by the guard test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
baseline.summary: Reconverge variant (b): recover the local-changes merge abort on tracked store artifacts (restore deletions, quarantine modifications, retry once)

## The defect

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:538`, default `False`) has ZERO read sites in `src/rebar`. Nothing gates on it.

A code trace of the live path confirms it: `_commands/metrics.py:139-148` loads `config.load_config(root).code_health` and carries only `scan_roots` (:144), `size_cap` (:145) and `size_near_fraction` (:146) into the metrics context. `enabled` is never consulted, so the structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`) evaluate even at the default `enabled=False`.

The field is documented and settable, so an operator can set `enabled = false` and reasonably believe code-health analysis is off. It is not.

## Why it was never caught

The 6754 inert-config gate cannot see this one -- see the sibling bug on that gate. It matches bare attribute NAMES globally, and `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`, `LangfuseConfig`, under `llm/`), so this field passes without ever being read itself. That is also why it carries no `# read-via:` marker while the neighbouring `analyzers` field needed one.

## The decision this needs

Same shape as dce2: either HONOR the flag (gate structural metric evaluation on it) or DELETE it. Honoring it is a behavioral change -- metrics that run today would stop running for anyone on the default -- so this needs an explicit operator ruling, not an agent's judgment.

Note the interaction with dce2's ruling: the operator chose to DELETE the inert `analyzers` field rather than wire it, with intent preserved as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2. A consistent ruling here is plausible but must not be assumed, because the two differ -- deleting `analyzers` removes a knob that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes the only advertised off switch for the whole code-health subsystem.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An explicit operator decision is recorded: honor `enabled` or remove it.
- [x] If HONORED: structural metric evaluation is gated on it, with a test proving the metrics do
      NOT evaluate at `enabled=False` and DO at `enabled=True`; the default's behavior change is
      called out in the changelog.
- [x] If REMOVED: the field, its coercion row and its config-surface entries go, and the docs no
      longer advertise an off switch that does not exist.
- [x] Either way, a guard prevents it silently regressing to inert again (this depends on the 6754
      gate fix -- a same-named field cannot be policed until that lands). MOOT: nothing left to regress.

## Provenance

Found by a code-trace archaeology pass over the metrics/code-health system while scoping dce2.

## Operator ruling — RECORDED

**Decision: REMOVE `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`.** Ruled by the operator on 2026-08-05 and recorded as the first comment on this ticket ("OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: REMOVE the field", author `RebarBotNava`, `author_id` `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`) — that comment is the citable attestation this AC closes against.

The counter-argument was surfaced to the operator before the ruling: this differs from dce2 because deleting `analyzers` removed a knob that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes the only advertised OFF SWITCH for the whole code-health subsystem. The operator considered that tradeoff and chose removal knowingly. This is a one-way door for the advertised switch; the intent it expressed is not being preserved as a follow-up idea (unlike dce2, whose analyzer-dispatch intent survives as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2) because there is no surviving design for a code-health off switch — re-adding one later would be a fresh feature decision, not a restoration. Do not re-litigate the ruling.

## Fix plan (REMOVAL, per the recorded operator ruling above)

Pure removal — the field controls nothing today (zero read sites), so deleting it cannot change what runs.

1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — delete the `enabled: bool = False` field from
   `CodeHealthConfig`; delete its `"enabled": lambda v, k: _as_bool(v, k)` coercion row from
   the `code_health` entry of `_SECTIONS`; refresh the class docstring, which no longer
   describes an inert-by-default toggle.
2. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — add TWO warn-class tombstones to `_TOMBSTONE_REGISTRY` so a
   still-set input WARNs and exits 0 rather than being silently dropped: an `env` tombstone for
   `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` and a `cfg` tombstone for `code_health.enabled`. This is
   mandatory, not optional: `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` fails the build when a
   golden-pinned key exists in neither the live schema nor the tombstone registry.
3. `docs/config.md` — drop `enabled` from both TOML examples and from the prose type list in
   the `code_health.*` section (so the docs stop advertising an off switch that does not
   exist), and add both tombstoned inputs to the warn-class list.
4. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py` — drop only the plain `value.enabled is False` /
   `value.enabled is True` assertions from the two happy-path tests.
5. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` — drop the `-c code_health.enabled=true`
   CLI override argument, the `enabled` entries in the composed config/sources assertions, and
   `code_health.enabled` / `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` from the golden-surface expectation
   sets.
6. `tests/scripts/test_metrics_docs.py` — drop `enabled` from the documented-keys tuple.
7. `tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py` — add a RUNTIME test (the home of the existing
   tombstone/warn tests) asserting the new tombstones actually fire: loading a config with
   `[code_health] enabled = true` set, and separately with `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` set,
   emits the warn-class removed-input message and does NOT raise (warn class, not error
   class). Registry presence alone is not proof — the warn path is verified by execution.

Not touched: `tests/golden/config_surface.json` stays pinned (that is the point of the golden — the tombstones, not a golden edit, account for the removed entries).

`_as_bool` is NOT orphaned by this removal (dozens of other coercion rows in `_SECTIONS` use it), unlike dce2's `_as_str_dict`.

### How the removal is proved

- `grep -rn "code_health.enabled\|REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED" src/rebar` returns nothing.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py tests/unit/test_config_backcompat.py
  tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` passes.
- `rebar config validate` with the key still set exits 0 and reports it as a removed input.

### Evidence of no behavior change

`rebar metrics` before and after produces the same structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`, `duplication_summary`). A byte-identical whole-output diff is NOT achievable — two consecutive runs already differ in time- and store-driven ticket metrics (dce2 found the same) — so the evidence is per-metric attribution over the code_health lens.

### On the guard AC

MOOT for a deleted field: there is nothing left to regress to inert. It also depended on bug 2c58-e710-275e-4ff7 regardless — the current inert-config gate could never have caught this field, because `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`, `LangfuseConfig`).
baseline.summary: CodeHealthConfig.enabled is inert: structural metrics run regardless of it

# The review-bot container resolves NO AWS region — a Bedrock cutover fails at client construction

## MEASURED (from inside `compose-review-bot-1` on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, account 896586841071)

```
env | grep '^AWS_'        -> (nothing: no AWS_REGION, no AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, no keys)
env | grep '^REBAR_LLM_'  -> NO_REBAR_LLM_ENV   (so REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION is unset too)
boto3.session.Session().region_name        -> None
boto3.client('bedrock-runtime')            -> NoRegionError: You must specify a region.
converse(...) with no explicit region      -> NoRegionError: You must specify a region.
```

Every earlier Bedrock probe in this epic passed `region_name="us-east-1"` EXPLICITLY, which is exactly why this went unnoticed — those probes never exercised ambient resolution.

## Why this breaks the cutover

`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py::build_bedrock_provider` does:

```python
region = cfg.bedrock_region_name or None
return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)
```

`cfg.bedrock_region_name` comes from `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION`, which is UNSET in the container. So `region=None` and `BedrockProvider` falls through to boto3's own resolution — which, as measured, finds nothing and raises `NoRegionError`.

That is a HARD failure at client construction, before any model call, and story eb6e ships the cutover with **NO cross-provider fallback**. So flipping `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` to `bedrock:...` without also setting a region takes the `LLM-Review` gate down for every landing rather than degrading it.

**Notably, IMDS is NOT the region source here.** IMDS is reachable from the container (token PUT returns 200, role resolves — see 9249), yet `session.region_name` is still `None`. So region discovery is ORTHOGONAL to the IMDS/hop-limit contingency: fixing IMDS reachability would not supply a region, and region must be configured explicitly no matter what IMDS does. That distinction matters because it is easy to assume the instance-metadata path covers both.

## Approach (candidate)

Set the region explicitly for the bot service — `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` (rebar's own knob, which `build_bedrock_provider` already threads) or `AWS_REGION` in the container environment. Prefer the rebar knob so the value is visible to rebar's config layer and to `provider_provenance` (343b).

Consider ALSO failing loudly and early: today a missing region surfaces as a boto3 `NoRegionError` from deep inside provider construction. A pre-flight check that names `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` would turn a confusing runtime stack trace into an actionable config error — the same shape as the existing typed `LLMConfigError` for a missing bedrock package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the cutover runbook records the Bedrock region setting and its value
- [ ] [operator-attested] the bot service environment sets an explicit Bedrock region, evidenced by
      container `env` output in a comment
- [ ] a test asserts that building the bedrock provider with NO resolvable region raises a TYPED, actionable rebar error naming the region setting — not a bare boto3 `NoRegionError`
- [ ] [operator-attested] from inside the review-bot container, `boto3.client('bedrock-runtime')` with NO explicit region succeeds after the change, evidenced by command output in a comment
- [ ] the runbook states that IMDS reachability does NOT supply a region, so the hop-limit contingency and region config are independent concerns
baseline.summary: Bedrock cutover hard-fails with NoRegionError: the review-bot container has no region configured

## Why
Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S5 — the epic's close gate. The pattern's five requirements (R1–R5) must be proven live under multi-agent parallel conditions, not asserted from config. Scripted alongside `infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`; every scenario's change URLs + votes recorded on the EPIC ticket.

## What
Seven scenarios on the running Gerrit against a throwaway `feature/e2e-<date>` branch:
1. **Parallel siblings** — two agents in separate worktrees push independent story changes; both earn LLM-Review + Verified and submit WITHOUT either rebasing (second submit via MERGE_IF_NECESSARY, no manual rebase). Also live-proves webhook + g2p branch-agnostic dispatch.
2. **Stacking** — a third agent pulls the branch (both stories in history) and pushes on top; reviewed diff covers ONLY its delta (assert via robot comment/diff scope).
3. **Merge-back** — --no-ff merge change to main: bot reviews the auto-merge delta only (assert NOT the whole-feature diff), CI green on the merge tree, both votes present, submit lands atomically, replication advances GitHub main with all commits, branch deleted.
4. **Vote-carry on re-merge** — land an unrelated change on main mid-flight; re-merge (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE): LLM-Review +1 CARRIES, Verified RE-RUNS; then change the feature tip: BOTH wiped (REWORK).
5. **Textual conflict** — overlapping feature-vs-main edits resolved in the merge commit; bot reviews the non-empty auto-merge delta.
6. **Semantic conflict** — textually clean, semantically broken (rename on main + new call-site on feature): auto-merge diff empty, LLM-Review passes, CI red → Verified=-1 BLOCKS submit (two-vote complementarity).
7. **Races + negatives** — concurrent submits into the branch behave; merge push WITHOUT pushMerge refused; branch creation outside feature-branch-drivers refused; reconciler backfills a dropped webhook for a feature-branch change INCLUDING a merge change (transparent merge detection).

## Scope
E2E script + live evidence only. Depends on S1 (config/ACLs), S2 (bot merge path), S3 (CI coverage). Requirement mapping: R1: 2+3; R2: 3; R3: 1+3+6; R4: 1+4; R5: ADR + apt-otter-urn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scenario script committed alongside reviewbot-e2e.sh (reusing its helpers where sensible)
- [ ] All 7 scenarios pass live; change URLs + votes recorded on the epic ticket
- [ ] RED/BLUE/GREEN replay (1–3) shows zero vote wipes, zero manual rebases, zero re-reviews of attested stories, single atomic landing
- [ ] Scenario 6 demonstrates Verified=-1 blocking submit on an empty auto-merge diff
- [ ] Cleanup: e2e feature branch deleted; throwaway changes abandoned
baseline.summary: S5: Live multi-agent E2E validation — 7 feature-branch scenarios on the running Gerrit

## Context / Problem

The sibling children introduce a protocol with several non-obvious rules that a future contributor cannot infer from the code: which signals are admissible evidence and which are not, why an escaped-defect label is used positively but never negatively, why a fixture must reproduce before admission, why fixtures are excluded from the weekly live sweep, and why mined fixtures live in this repository rather than shipping as packaged defaults.

ADR 0109 is the precedent for exactly this problem. It records that a harness nobody is required to use changes nothing, and so fixes when each tier is required. The same reasoning applies here: an admission bar that is not written down is an admission bar that erodes, and the first contributor to add a fixture by hand will not reproduce rules that exist only as code.

`docs/plan-review-gate.md` is where a contributor already looks for the gate's contributor protocol, so a rule recorded anywhere else will be missed.

## Approach

Record the protocol as an ADR under `docs/adr/`, following ADR 0109's shape, and reference it from `docs/plan-review-gate.md` so it is reachable from the document contributors already read. The ADR states the decisions rather than restating the implementation: the admissible evidence signals and the positive-only rule for escaped-defect labels; the vintage gate and why prompt churn makes it necessary; the tiered blocking and advisory admission bars; the reproduce-before-admit rule and its reproduction consensus plus epoch-majority bar; the change-triggered execution rule and why the fixtures stay off the weekly cron; and the gap-only loop with its `unreliable-criterion:` breaker.

This child lands last because an ADR written before the siblings settle would record intentions rather than decisions.

## Scope

One new ADR file `docs/adr/0113-fixture-mining-and-admission-protocol.md`, and the reference to it from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. Documentation only.

## Non-goals

- Changing any behavior, command, spec, or workflow.
- Restating the implementation in prose; the ADR records decisions and their rationale.
- Superseding ADR 0109, which answers a different question (how to measure a proposed
  change, rather than what asserts a criterion's required behavior).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An ADR file `docs/adr/0113-fixture-mining-and-admission-protocol.md` exists whose body states each of the seven protocol
      items, verified by `grep -c` returning a non-zero count for a literal anchor per item:
      admissible evidence (`grep -c "Admissible evidence"`), the escaped-defect positive-only
      rule (`grep -c "escaped-defect"`), the vintage gate (`grep -c "vintage gate"`), the
      tiered admission bars (`grep -c "admission bar"`), the reproduce-before-admit rule

## What
Add a deterministic precheck to the completion-verification close gate: when a ticket records `file_impact` (a claimed code change) but no commit references it via a `rebar-ticket:` trailer, fail fast BEFORE the billable LLM verifier runs, with a message describing the reason and remediation.

## Why
A ticket recording file_impact claims a concrete code change. If no commit references it, the implementation has not landed and completion cannot be confirmed — so there is no point spending an LLM call. This mirrors the existing open-children structural guard.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`: new helper `_referencing_commit_exists()` (scans
  `git log`, resolves each commit's `rebar-ticket:`/`<id>:` refs through the shared resolver);
  the precheck wired into `_completion_precheck` after the bug-reason check, before the LLM call.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py`: coverage for block/pass/skip/force-close.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A ticket with file_impact and no referencing commit is blocked (exit 1) before the LLM call.
- [ ] The same ticket closes once a commit references it via a rebar-ticket trailer.
- [ ] A ticket without file_impact is unaffected (no commit check).
- [ ] `--force-close` bypasses the precheck (withholds signature, still closes).
- [ ] The error message names the reason (file_impact) and remediation (referencing commit).
baseline.summary: Fail completion verification fast when a file_impact ticket has no referencing commit

## The defect

`Makefile` line 128 (the `worktree` target) provisions the new worktree's venv with:

    python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && $(MAKE) install

It inherits whatever `python3` resolves to on the host. Nothing pins or checks the version, and `requires-python = ">=3.11"` (pyproject.toml:16) accepts anything from 3.11 upward, so `uv sync --locked` succeeds and the mismatch is silent.

## Measured on this host 2026-08-05

    system python3            -> Python 3.14.6   (/opt/homebrew/bin/python3)
    CI matrix                 -> 3.11, 3.12, 3.13   (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml)
    worktree c6c9-attest-split/.venv      -> Python 3.14.6
    worktree rebar-8a5e/.venv             -> Python 3.14.6
    worktree fix-c5b3-scc-byfile/.venv    -> Python 3.14.6
    main checkout .venv                   -> Python 3.12.13

Every worktree created by `make worktree` runs **3.14.6, which CI never tests**. The main checkout is on a tested version only by accident of WHEN it was created — its venv predates the host's python3 moving to 3.14.

## The cost, which is not hypothetical

This is the canonical local-vs-CI divergence, and it burned real time tonight. Multiple agents working in fresh worktrees hit local test failures that CI did not reproduce, then each spent cycles proving them "pre-existing and environment-specific" -- correctly, but only after the fact. Two failures repeatedly implicated:

    tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present
    tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone

Each agent rediscovered this independently. The failure mode is corrosive rather than loud: local red that CI does not show trains agents (and humans) to discount local failures generally, which is exactly backwards -- the next genuine local-only regression gets waved through with the same reasoning.

It also cuts the other way: a change that breaks on 3.11 but passes on the developer's 3.14 looks clean locally and only fails after push, which is the slowest possible place to learn it.

## Note on scope

The version floor is separately declared and enforced for **git** (ticket 980d added `.github/git-version-floor.txt` plus a conftest session-abort). There is no equivalent for Python, even though Python is the far more likely source of behavioral divergence.

## Candidate approaches (weigh; not prescribed)

1. Pin the worktree venv to a CI-tested interpreter, e.g. `uv venv --python 3.12` (uv can fetch
   it), so a fresh worktree matches the matrix by construction.
2. Warn or fail loudly in `make worktree` / `make install` when the resolved interpreter is
   outside the CI matrix, naming the mismatch. Cheapest, and mirrors the git-floor pattern
   980d already established.
3. Add the host's version to the CI matrix -- rejected as stated, since it grows CI cost for
   every contributor to accommodate one machine, and does not stop the next drift.

Option 2 alone leaves the developer to act; option 1 removes the failure mode. They compose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A venv created by `make worktree` runs a Python version the CI matrix actually tests, or
      the command fails/warns explicitly naming the mismatch and the supported set.
- [x] The supported set is single-sourced from the CI matrix rather than duplicated, so adding
      or dropping a version in CI cannot silently desynchronize the check (the same
      single-sourcing discipline as `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and
      `.github/git-version-floor.txt`).
- [x] A test proves the check fires for an out-of-matrix interpreter and stays silent for an
      in-matrix one.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` states the supported Python versions and how to provision a
      matching venv when the host default differs.
- [x] The two failures listed above are re-checked on an in-matrix interpreter and either
      confirmed genuinely pre-existing or filed as real bugs -- right now nobody knows which,
      because every observation of them has been on an untested Python.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the a573 agent, which noticed its worktree venv was 3.14.6 while explaining three local-only test failures. Independently verified here: system python3, the Makefile line, three worktree venvs, and the CI matrix all measured directly.
baseline.summary: make worktree builds its venv from ambient python3, so fresh worktrees run a Python CI never tests

One line of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING

  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
