## Context

The `COMMITS` event and `attach_commits` reducer already exist (`rebar.attach_commits`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697`, re-exported from `src/rebar/__init__.py`), used by the code-review workflow. Missing: an author-facing repair surface for a botched `rebar-ticket:` trailer, plus a consumer. Approved design (b902-18af-14ed-4da1): expose retroactive commit linking on CLI + library + MCP, document it, then add a deterministic close-gate check that linked commits' diffs match the recorded `file_impact`. OUT of scope: linked commits as a completion-verifier diff basis (they may be incomplete; CV already prefetches from `file_impact`).

## Plan

1. **Shared DET module** `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py` (new, ~120 LOC): (a) `invalid_commit_shas(shas, repo_root)` via `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`; (b) the step-4 path matchers, including `glob_match` — the `**/`-aware semantics (`fnmatch(p,g) or (g.startswith("**/") and fnmatch(p,g[3:]))`) from `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:746`. Its ONLY true mirror is `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:242`; `src/rebar/grounding/oracle.py:316` uses PLAIN `fnmatch`, is NOT a copy, and is left untouched. The DET close path must not import `rebar.llm` (optional `[agents]` extra), so the helper is hoisted here and BOTH real copies (`prompts._glob_match`, `registry._glob_match`) become thin delegating wrappers — one implementation, no third copy.

2. **CLI verb** `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the existing seam. Registration follows the established seam: add to `_WRITES_FULL` in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`; add a variadic handler (N SHAs) to `_ARGV_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`; ship pinned help `src/rebar/_cli/help/attach-commits.txt` + the `overview.txt` line (golden-pinned; `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` requires it). Thin body in `src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py`.

3. **Validation in the SEAM, not the CLI**, so all three surfaces inherit it identically: `rebar.attach_commits` calls `commit_impact.invalid_commit_shas` before appending. **ALL-OR-NOTHING** — the batch is validated first; if any SHA fails, NO `COMMITS` event is recorded and the call raises naming every offender. Union-add unchanged. Library: `rebar.attach_commits` is already re-exported — confirm and document. MCP: register `attach_commits` in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` with an `AttachCommitsResultOut` outputSchema in `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`, per the existing write-tool pattern (`mcp_server.py` only assembles registrars).

4. **DET close check** in the existing completion precheck `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — the module that today raises "cannot confirm the work landed" (there is no `src/rebar/workflow/close_gate.py`). Discovery unions the two existing sources: (i) `state.commits` from COMMITS events; (ii) the precheck's referencing-commit scan (`_referencing_commit_exists`, `close_precheck.py:94` — commits reachable from HEAD carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject for the ticket or any transitive descendant). It returns only a bool, so it is refactored into a SHA-returning `_referencing_commits(...)` with `_referencing_commit_exists` kept as a thin wrapper — the documented monkeypatch target and its call sites keep working unchanged. For each commit, `git show --name-only` gives changed paths; a path neither covered by `file_impact` nor matched by this check's OWN exemption globs (`tests/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — owned here, not inherited) is a deterministic BLOCK naming the commit and paths. Matching (via step 1, not re-derived): normalized repo-relative POSIX paths; a `file_impact` entry matches on exact equality, or as a directory prefix when it ends with `/` or names an existing directory; exemptions use `**/`-aware `glob_match`. No substring matching. No LLM.

   **Git errors, asymmetric by source:** a source-(ii) commit is local by construction, so a `git show` failure on it FAILS CLOSED (block, naming the SHA). A source-(i) SHA may legitimately be absent locally (attached from another clone, or unfetched), so it is SKIPPED — blocking a foreign SHA would be a false positive on a repair surface built to record commits.

   **Scope symmetry.** Source-(ii) discovery credits commits for the ticket OR any transitive descendant (`accepted_ids`, `close_precheck.py:361-367`), but `field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker)` (`field_reads.py:36`) reads only THIS ticket's — reusing it as-is would false-BLOCK a parent declaring `file_impact` when children's commits touch child-owned paths. So the check compares against the UNION of `file_impact` over the SAME id set discovery uses, making both scopes match by construction.

   A ticket with no discovered commits keeps today's behavior (the existing error). The check is skipped when that union is empty (no ticket in the set declares `file_impact`).

5. **Remedy for a legitimate block:** the message names the offending paths and says to declare them via `rebar set-file-impact <ticket> …`, after which close proceeds; `--force="<reason>"` stays the break-glass.

6. **Docs.** `docs/cli-reference.md` is GENERATED (`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, CI drift gate, subcommand count in header) so it is regenerated, not hand-edited. Hand-edited: `docs/mcp-reference.md` and `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md`. Each names the verb, its use, and the step-5 remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>` records a COMMITS event that `rebar show` reflects. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -x`.
- [ ] An invalid SHA is rejected with an error naming it. Verify: same file, test asserting the offending SHA appears in the error text.
- [ ] A batch containing any invalid SHA records nothing (all-or-nothing). Verify: test asserting `state.commits` is byte-identical before/after a mixed valid/invalid batch.
- [ ] The MCP server exposes `attach_commits` with an outputSchema, routed through the same seam. Verify: the MCP tool-inventory test asserts `"attach_commits"` is in the registered tool names.
- [ ] A commit touching a path outside the declared `file_impact` blocks close, naming the offending path. Verify: unit test asserting the exact path string in the raised message.
- [ ] A commit whose paths are all declared does not block close. Verify: unit test asserting close proceeds.
- [ ] An exempt path does not block, including at the repo root (`README.md` under `**/*.md`). Verify: unit test over each exemption glob.
- [ ] The DET check imports no `rebar.llm` module. Verify: test asserting `[m for m in sys.modules if m.startswith("rebar.llm")] == []` after running it in a fresh interpreter.
- [ ] The `**/`-aware glob semantics have one implementation. Verify: test asserting `prompts._glob_match` and `registry._glob_match` both delegate to `commit_impact.glob_match`.
- [ ] An unreadable source-(ii) commit fails closed naming the SHA; an unresolvable source-(i) SHA is skipped without blocking. Verify: one unit test per direction.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` names the `attach_commits` tool. Verify: `grep -qE '\battach_commits\b' docs/mcp-reference.md` exits 0.
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the verb. Verify: `grep -qF 'rebar attach-commits' src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` exits 0.
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the `set-file-impact` remedy. Verify: `grep -qF 'rebar set-file-impact' src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` exits 0.
- [ ] A parent close does not block on a path declared only in a child's `file_impact`. Verify: unit test closing a parent whose child commit touches a child-declared path, asserting no block.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` is regenerated and its drift gate passes. Verify: `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` exits 0.
baseline.summary: attach-commits repair verb on all three surfaces + DET file-impact-vs-diff close check

baseline.description:
## Why

E6 measures whether the plan-review gate's **LLM-as-judge is reliable** — the same judgment, re-run, must land the same way. Two documented judge failure modes threaten the shared Pass-2 verify / Pass-3 decide vocabulary that R3 and R5 build on:

- **Self-consistency drift.** An unstable per-finding decision injects noise into the
  Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary. R5 adds a new Pass-2 sub-answer
  (`asserted_capability_confirmed`) routed over the G6/E4/T3 cohort
  (`docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md:195-199`); it is only worth adding if
  the judge that emits it is stable across repeats. Our own research substrate records
  that "~3-vote self-consistency captures most of the available gain (+4pp, saturating)"
  and that "judges are systematically overconfident" (`sota:44`; refs at `sota:241` —
  Wang et al., *LLMs are not Fair Evaluators*, ACL 2024, arXiv:2305.17926; Zheng et al.,
  MT-Bench, arXiv:2306.05685; judge overconfidence, arXiv:2508.06225).
- **Order sensitivity.** Section-order permutation of the input plan should not flip the
  gate verdict. `sota:44` records order-swap flipping 82.5% of *pairwise* verdicts (Wang,
  ACL 2024). Our gate already uses the recommended mitigation — absolute rubric scoring,
  never pairwise — so E6 empirically confirms the **residual** order-sensitivity of the
  actual gate is below a floor before R3 lands a new (order-exposed) container criterion.

E6 **re-judges an existing sample and measures agreement (reliability), not accuracy against gold** (`runs/README.md:154-156`: "E6 re-judges these findings for self-consistency; it never needed the TP/FP labels"). This is why E6 survived the E1 descope (ticket comment 2026-07-16): re-running the gate's own judge to measure its *stochastic stability* is the textbook definition of a self-consistency test — it is **not** the circular-adjudication error that invalidated E1's finding-level TP/FP labeling (which mis-used the gate's judge as *gold truth for accuracy*). E6 never treats any judge output as truth; it only compares repeated judge outputs to each other.

E6 gates two downstream stories: R3 (with E2) and R5 (with E5).

## What

Two bounded judge-reliability experiments, each with an explicit metric + pass/fail floor, run over **committed, reproducible samples**. No `src/rebar` behavior changes — E6 is measurement over the *existing* gate (Pass-2 verify → Pass-3 decide → `orchestrator.finalize_verdict`).

### Grounded definitions (verified against the code/corpus, not assumed)

- **"decision"** (self-consistency unit of agreement) = the Pass-3 output field
  `decision ∈ {block, advisory, dropped, indeterminate}` produced by
  `three_pass.pass3_decide(...)` (the deterministic decision path; harness
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/three_pass.py`), whose vocabulary matches
  the persisted sidecar `decision` enum. Pass-3 is deterministic given Pass-2, so all
  measured variance is the judge's Pass-2 stochasticity.
- **"verdict"** (order-shuffle unit of agreement) = the gate's overall
  `verdict ∈ {PASS, BLOCK, INDETERMINATE}` on the `plan_review_verdict` dict returned by
  the public entrypoint `rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` (`__init__.py:387`), which
  computes it in `orchestrator.finalize_verdict` (`orchestrator.py:467-503`). A
  `PASS↔BLOCK` or `PASS↔INDETERMINATE` flip across permutations is a disagreement.
- **Infra-INDETERMINATE exclusion is defined concretely, not hand-waved.**
  `finalize_verdict` records *why* a verdict is INDETERMINATE on the verdict's `coverage`
  record: an INDETERMINATE carrying `coverage.get("llm_unavailable")` (systemic LLM-tier
  failure) or `coverage.get("verify_failed")` (Pass-2 verifier could not run — e.g. the
  agentic verifier exhausted its step budget, bug 59bc) is an **execution failure, not a
  stable judge outcome** (`orchestrator.py:491-501`). E6 **drops and re-runs** any
  permutation whose verdict is INDETERMINATE **with either flag set**, and **keeps**
  a genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (INDETERMINATE with *neither* flag — e.g. a preserved
  Pass-1 indeterminate on a blocking-enabled criterion) as its own agreement category.
  (A genuine unsupported-stack abstain where the tier ran but a criterion could not ground
  is *not* `llm_unavailable` and surfaces as PASS, `orchestrator.py:488` — so it never
  pollutes the INDETERMINATE category.) The exact fields/values were verified in
  `finalize_verdict`; the exclusion is not a guessed mechanism.

### Experiment A — self-consistency of the Pass-2/Pass-3 judge over the R5 cohort

- **Sample frame (concrete).** `runs/adjudication_corpus.jsonl` rows filtered by
  `criterion ∈ {G6, E4, T3}` — **exactly the R5 sub-answer's own routing cohort**
  (`sota:195-199` routes G6/E4/T3 through the agentic verifier for
  `asserted_capability_confirmed`). Verified in the committed file: **74 rows across 66
  distinct tickets** (advisory 47 / dropped 20 / block 7) — the cohort exists and clears
  the N≥50 floor with 24 rows of headroom. (Chosen over the CLAUDE.md "G1G2+E4" framing
  because E6 gates *R5*, and R5 itself is defined at `sota:195-199` as the G6/E4/T3
  cohort; the corpus has no `asserted_capability` label, so a criterion-set filter is the
  only grounded slice.)
- **N = 50** findings, sampled deterministically (fixed seed) from the 74-member cohort,
  deduped by `(ticket_id, finding_id)` (finding_id alone is non-unique: 388 unique of
  400). The 24-row headroom absorbs any ticket whose plan text cannot be snapshotted.
- **Re-judge inputs are frozen and committed** to defeat the "no plan-text corpus" gap:
  a build step snapshots, once, each sampled finding's ticket plan text via
  `rebar show <ticket_id>` (the replay-derived `description` == the reviewed plan) plus
  the finding record, writing `runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl`
  (`{finding_id, ticket_id, title, plan, criterion, finding, location, suggested_fix}`).
  A ticket whose plan is unretrievable (compacted/archived) is skipped and the sample is
  topped up deterministically from the cohort remainder to hold N=50. The N-vote harness
  reads **only this committed file** — no live-store dependency at judge time.
- **Judge run — the agentic Pass-2 path requires BOTH an explicit `repo_root` AND an
  active gate session (verified execution recipe).** The agentic verifier only activates
  when `agentic=True` **and** `repo_root` is non-empty **and** the finding's criteria are
  code-grounded (`three_pass.pass2_verify`, dispatch at `three_pass.py:185`); the harness's
  `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` set (`three_pass.py:34`) contains **all of `{G6, E4, T3}`**, so every
  cohort finding takes the agentic path. Wire the session with `gate_source` so the
  agentic verifier's read-only repo tools are permitted (`config.assert_gated`):

  ```python
  from rebar.llm import gate_source
  from harnesses import three_pass
  handle = gate_source.resolve_gate_handle(None, "local", REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT)  # gate_source.py:80
  with gate_source.gate_read_root(handle):        # gate_source.py:105 — marks the gate session; local mode reads the in-place checkout
      for inp in frozen_inputs:                    # runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl
          for _ in range(3):                       # 3 votes (sota:44 — 3-vote self-consistency saturates the gain)
              v = three_pass.pass2_verify(inp["title"], inp["plan"], inp,
                                          repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT, agentic=True)
              # pass2_verify returns {"verify": <inner dict|None>, "mode":..., "tool_calls":...}
              # (both the single-turn and _verify_agentic paths, three_pass.py); pass3_decide
              # consumes the INNER verification dict, so pass v["verify"], not v:
              d = three_pass.pass3_decide(v["verify"], block_threshold=..., blocking_enabled=...)
  ```

  `repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT` is passed **explicitly** to `pass2_verify` **and** the
  `gate_read_root(handle)` context is entered — both are required; in `local` mode the
  handle leaves the code root as the in-place checkout while still marking a deliberate gate
  session (`gate_source.py:105-118`). Record every vote's `decision` and the **existing**
  Pass-2 binary sub-answers in the current `PASS2_TOOL`/`GRADED` schema (`three_pass.py`).
  `asserted_capability_confirmed` is **R5's future addition** and does NOT exist yet — E6
  does not record it; E6 measures the reliability of the *existing* judge, which is the
  prerequisite R5 depends on. The agreement metric (below) is computed over `decision` —
  not over any R5 field.
- **Per-vote infra exclusion (defined concretely).** `pass3_decide` returns
  `{"decision": "indeterminate", "reason": "no-verification"}` **only** when its argument
  is falsy — i.e. when `v["verify"]` is `None` (Pass-2 returned no verdict: an error or
  agentic-no-verdict result; its sole indeterminate path, verified in
  `three_pass.pass3_decide`). That is an execution failure, not a stable judge decision, so
  E6 **drops and re-runs** any vote with `decision == "indeterminate"` until 3 substantive
  votes (`block`/`advisory`/`dropped`) are collected per finding, capping retries and
  recording any finding that cannot reach 3 votes as an excluded, reported row (never
  silently padded).
- **Metric + floor.** Over the N findings × 3 votes, compute **Fleiss' κ** (raters = the
  3 interchangeable votes; subjects = findings; categories = the 4-value `decision`
  space) **and raw exact-agreement** (fraction of findings where all 3 votes are
  identical). **PASS iff κ ≥ 0.6 (Landis–Koch "substantial") AND raw agreement ≥ 0.8;**
  below **either** → FAIL, recorded as an **R5 blocker**. Both floors are reported
  because κ deflates under skewed base rates (the cohort is advisory-heavy), so raw
  agreement is the prevalence-robust co-floor.

### Experiment B — order-shuffle stability of the gate verdict

- **Sample frame (concrete).** `runs/corpus_sample.json` — 19 committed plan-review
  inputs that **carry full plan text** (the only committed plan-text corpus; the outcome
  and adjudication corpora store no plan text). The order-shuffle inclusion criterion is
  **≥3 top-level `##` sections**, because a plan needs 3 *distinct* permutations and a
  2-section plan has only `2! = 2` orderings — so ≥3 sections (`3! = 6` orderings)
  guarantees 3 distinct permutations are available. Verified in the committed file: of the
  19 inputs, **14 have ≥3 top-level `##` sections** (the permutable set); the 5 plans with
  <3 sections (one =2, four =1) are excluded from the shuffle denominator. **N = 14 plans**
  (each judged over exactly 3 distinct permutations, below).
- **The "≥20 container plans" contradiction is resolved by DROPPING the
  container-specific requirement.** Only 5 of the 19 inputs are containers
  (`has_children=true`: 3 epics + 2 stories) and the run corpora hold exactly one
  container-type ticket — a container-only shuffle is under-powered and irreproducible.
  Order-sensitivity is a **general** judge property: if the gate verdict is unstable under
  section shuffle at large, any new criterion (including R3's container criterion)
  inherits that instability, so a stable general-plan result is a **prerequisite** for
  trusting R3. The 5-plan container subset is reported **descriptively only** (not a
  gate).
- **Mechanism (verified execution recipe — the PUBLIC entrypoint, not raw
  `finalize_verdict`).** For each plan, a pure helper `permute_sections` generates **exactly
  3 distinct section-order permutations** by reordering the plan's top-level `##` section
  blocks (content preserved verbatim — only the block order changes). **Deterministic
  selection rule:** permutation 0 is the **identity** (the plan's original section order);
  permutations 1 and 2 are drawn by repeatedly `random.Random(SEED).shuffle`-ing the list
  of section indices — with a **pinned per-plan seed** `SEED = int(plan_id.split("-")[0], 16)`
  — and taking the next ordering that is **not already selected** (dedup against permutations
  0..k-1), so all 3 are distinct. Since every qualifying plan has ≥3 sections (≥6 orderings),
  3 distinct permutations always exist; the identical seed makes the selection reproducible.
  The concrete `section_order` (an index list) of each of the 3 is committed (below), so the
  experiment is re-runnable without re-deriving the shuffle. `finalize_verdict` cannot be
  called standalone (it requires
  an assembled `PlanContext` + Pass parts), so E6 drives the whole gate through the public
  entrypoint `rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` (`__init__.py:387`). Because `review_plan`
  reads the plan **from the ticket store**, section order is varied by pointing the ticket
  reads at a **throwaway store clone** — the store root and the code-grounding root are
  separable (`config.py:119-136` — `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` wins for ticket reads;
  `gate_dispatch.py:141-147` — store-root vs code-root are independent). Per permutation:

  ```
  1. set REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=<tmp clone of the tickets store>            # ticket reads only; real store untouched
  2. write the permuted plan as the ticket's description:  rebar edit <ticket_id> --description=<permuted>
  3. verdict = review_plan(ticket_id, source="local", repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT,
                           sign=False, emit_sidecar=False, force=True)  # __init__.py:387
  ```

  `source="local"` + `repo_root=REAL_REPO_CHECKOUT` make code-grounding read the **real
  repo**; `sign=False` / `emit_sidecar=False` keep the run **non-mutating** (no attestation,
  no `REVIEW_RESULT` event) and `force=True` defeats idempotent review-reuse so every
  permutation is judged fresh (`__init__.py:508-518, 570-587`). Only the throwaway
  `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` clone is edited — the real tickets store is never written. Record the
  resulting `verdict`, applying the infra-INDETERMINATE exclusion defined above (re-run a
  permutation whose INDETERMINATE carries `coverage.llm_unavailable`/`verify_failed`).
  The frozen `{plan_id, permutation_index, section_order}` specs are committed to
  `runs/e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl` for reproducibility.
- **Metric + floor.** Over 14 plans × 3 permutations, compute **Fleiss' κ** and **raw
  exact-agreement** on the `verdict` categories. **PASS iff κ ≥ 0.6 AND raw agreement ≥
  0.8;** below → FAIL, recorded as an **R3 prerequisite failure**. Secondary descriptive
  metric: mean per-plan Jaccard of the fired-criteria set across permutations (not gated).

### LLM-spend honesty

E6 **does** make repeated live, billable LLM calls — self-consistency and order-shuffle inherently require re-runs; there is no persisted-sidecar shortcut for a *stability* measurement. Spend is bounded and stated: **A = 50 findings × 3 votes = 150 agentic Pass-2 calls** (Pass-3 is deterministic/free); **B = 14 plans × 3 permutations = 42 full-gate runs**. This is deliberately a bounded sub-sample — not the 400-finding adjudication corpus nor the 628-row outcome corpus.

## Scope

- **`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/e6_judge_reliability.py`** — the driver:
  builds frozen inputs (Exp A snapshot + Exp B permutations), runs the votes/permutations,
  and writes the agreement tables + summary. Exp A reuses `three_pass.pass2_verify` /
  `pass3_decide` inside a `gate_source.gate_read_root` session with an explicit
  `repo_root`; Exp B drives the public `rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` entrypoint
  against a throwaway `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` store clone (real store untouched). It does not
  modify any `src/rebar` code.
- **`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/`** — committed inputs + outputs (all paths
  in the ACs below).
- **`tests/unit/test_e6_agreement.py`** — CI-collectable golden test for the pure helpers
  (`fleiss_kappa`, `raw_agreement`, `permute_sections`) on fixed fixtures; **no LLM**.
- **README writeup** — a new "E6 — judge reliability" section in
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/README.md`.
- **No `src/rebar` changes.** E6 measures the existing gate; R3/R5 later consume E6's
  recorded verdicts. Consumes `runs/adjudication_corpus.jsonl` (Exp A cohort) and
  `runs/corpus_sample.json` (Exp B plans), both already committed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Exp A run recorded.** `runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl` (N≥50 frozen
  cohort inputs, each `criterion ∈ {G6,E4,T3}` with non-empty `plan`) and
  `runs/e6_selfconsistency.jsonl` (3 votes/finding, each with `decision` and Pass-2
  binary sub-answers) both exist and are consistent.
  Proving:
  `python3 -c "import json; ins=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl')]; assert len(ins)>=50 and all(r['criterion'] in {'G6','E4','T3'} and r['plan'] for r in ins); v=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_selfconsistency.jsonl')]; ids={r['finding_id'] for r in ins}; per={i:0 for i in ids}; [per.__setitem__(r['finding_id'], per[r['finding_id']]+1) for r in v]; assert all(c==3 for c in per.values()), per; print('OK', len(ins), 'findings x3 votes')"`

- [ ] **Exp A passes its floor (self-consistency).**
  `runs/e6_selfconsistency_agreement.csv` (one row per finding:
  `finding_id,criterion,decision_1,decision_2,decision_3,all_agree,modal_decision`) and
  `runs/e6_summary.json` record **Fleiss' κ AND raw agreement**; the summary states
  `self_consistency.pass == (kappa>=0.6 and raw_agreement>=0.8)`. A sub-floor result is
  recorded verbatim as an **R5 blocker** (not silently passed).
  Proving:
  `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_summary.json'))['self_consistency']; assert d['n_findings']>=50 and set(('fleiss_kappa','raw_agreement','pass'))<=set(d) and d['pass']==(d['fleiss_kappa']>=0.6 and d['raw_agreement']>=0.8); print('self-consistency', d)"`

- [ ] **Exp B run recorded (order-shuffle over the committed plan-text corpus).**
  `runs/e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl` (the 14 plans from `corpus_sample.json` with ≥3
  top-level sections, each with exactly 3 **distinct** section-order permutations —
  identity + 2 seeded, deduped) and `runs/e6_ordershuffle.jsonl` (one
  `verdict ∈ {PASS,BLOCK,INDETERMINATE}` per plan×permutation, produced via `review_plan`,
  with infra-INDETERMINATE — `coverage` `llm_unavailable`/`verify_failed` —
  excluded-and-re-run per the mechanism above) exist and are complete.
  Proving:
  `python3 -c "import json,collections; ins=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl')]; byp=collections.defaultdict(set); [byp[r['plan_id']].add(tuple(r['section_order'])) for r in ins]; assert len(byp)>=14 and all(len(s)==3 for s in byp.values()), {k:len(v) for k,v in byp.items()}; o=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_ordershuffle.jsonl')]; assert all(r['verdict'] in {'PASS','BLOCK','INDETERMINATE'} for r in o); print('OK', len(byp), 'plans x3 distinct permutations')"`

- [ ] **Exp B passes its floor (order-shuffle stability), with an explicit pass/fail … [truncated by reconciler]

# S5 — Config-driven priority mapping + str-valued per-project create_defaults (a881)

## Context / Problem

Epic 3d7a makes rebar↔Jira mappings config-driven over the S1 seam (`mapping_config.py`: `MappingLayer` axes, `SKIP`, `resolve_for_project`, `validate`). S2 made STATUS config-driven via `config.effective_status_map` (`config.py:77`), resolved per project by `outbound_differ._effective_status_map_for` (`:272`) and threaded through the backend wrapper/protocol on create+update as an OPTIONAL `status_map: dict[str,str] | None = None` kwarg.

S5 makes PRIORITY config-driven the SAME way and adds a str-valued per-project `create_defaults` axis. Both axes already exist in `MappingLayer` (both in `_AXIS_MAPS`, `mapping_config.py:44`). Priority is a SOFT field: an UNMAPPED priority DRIFTS (leave Jira's value, omit the field, warn) — it does NOT fail the sync. No priority VOCABULARY axis exists (`validate`, `config.py:328`), so this plan carries **no fail-closed claim for priority** — map-or-drift+warn only.

### Verified constraints
- **Parser is str/SKIP-only** — `_parse_axis_map` (`mapping_config.py:120`) raises
  on any non-`str`/`SKIP` value, so `create_defaults` is `Mapping[str,str]`;
  object/array values are inexpressible.
- **`config.py` imports nothing but `__future__`** and RE-DECLARES status literals
  in-module (`local_to_jira_status:35`, `jira_to_local_status:64`). Priority
  follows suit — NO top-level import of `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`.
- **Built-in priority map is INT-keyed** `dict[int,str]` 0–4 (`value_maps.py:22`);
  config `priority_map` is STR-keyed (`_parse_axis_map` does `out[str(key)]`).
- **ACLI does int-subscript arithmetic** — `acli_cli_ops.py:370`
  `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA[int(_id)-1]` (bug 5010-1c6a-9387-4b5b); `:359` +
  `acli.py:175` int `.get`. Str map breaks these → ACLI LEFT UNCHANGED.
- **New kwargs are OPTIONAL** (`priority_map=None`, `create_defaults=None`), typed
  identically to `status_map`, so any Protocol double that omits them still
  satisfies the Protocol (see Scope → test doubles).

## Approach

**Priority key-type reconciliation (in-module, no import).** Add to `config.py` a str-keyed baseline `local_to_jira_priority: dict[str,str] = {"0":"Highest","1":"High","2":"Medium","3":"Low","4":"Lowest"}`, re-declared like the status literals (a parity test pins it against `value_maps.LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`). New `config.effective_priority_map(project_key, root=None) -> dict[str,str]` mirrors `effective_status_map`; consumers look up by `str(priority)`. New shared helper `resolve_outbound_priority(value, priority_map) -> str|None` beside `resolve_outbound_status` (`outbound_mapper.py:47`): `priority_map.get(str(value))` (built-in when `None`); on miss → warn once (`reset_drift_warnings` sink, `:31`) and return `None` (DRIFT → OMIT field, never "Medium").

**Two named resolvers in `outbound_differ.py`, symmetric with S2's `_effective_status_map_for` (`:272`):**
- NEW `_effective_priority_map_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)` → `effective_priority_map`.
- NEW `_effective_create_defaults_for(ticket, mapping, repo_root)` →
  `config.effective_create_defaults` (create-only).

**Threading seam.** In `outbound_mutation_builders.py`:
- CREATE (`:88`): resolve both maps and pass `priority_map=` AND `create_defaults=`
  into the backend `map_local_to_remote` (alongside the existing `status_map=`).
- UPDATE (`:236`): pass `priority_map=` into `compute_update_fields`
  (`outbound_field_diff.py:235`, forwarded to `map_fields_to_remote`).
  `create_defaults` is NOT threaded to update (create-only, echo-safe).

## Scope

**CREATE carriers — gain optional `priority_map=None` + `create_defaults=None`:**
- `_backend.py:372` — `OutboundMapper` Protocol `map_local_to_remote`.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py:73` — Cloud `map_local_to_remote` (forwards into leaf).
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:121` — DC `map_local_to_remote` (forwards
  into `_map_local_to_dc_fields:134`).
- Leaf bodies: `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:_map_local_to_jira_fields`
  (`:101`, priority `:144`) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:
  _map_local_to_dc_fields` (`:60`, priority `:87`) — each maps priority via
  `resolve_outbound_priority` and MERGES resolved `create_defaults` FIRST, baseline
  computed fields winning on collision.

**UPDATE carriers — gain optional `priority_map=None`:**
- `_backend.py:393` Protocol `map_fields_to_remote`; `adapters/jira/backend.py:92`;
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:136`; leaf
  `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:94`
  `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote` (priority `:144`).

**Test doubles — mirror S2's status_map set.** S2 added explicit `status_map=None` ONLY to Protocol doubles with explicit signatures on the threading path; `**kw` doubles absorb new kwargs unchanged. The SAME set gains `priority_map=None` (create doubles also `create_defaults=None`):
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:271` `map_local_to_remote`
  (carries `status_map=None` at `:279`).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_canonical_outbound_equivalence.py:154`
  `map_local_to_remote` + `:166` `map_fields_to_remote` (both carry `status_map=None`).
- SAFE, no edit — the `*a,**k`/`**_kw` fakes already absorb new kwargs:
  `backend_support.py:148`, `test_rich_text_echo_suppression.py`,
  `test_rich_text_conflict_safety.py`, `test_inbound_rich_text_echo.py`,
  `diffing/test_inbound_field_sync_directionality.py:164`,
  `test_parent_drop_parity_8390.py:395`,
  `test_parent_emit_suppression_is_loud_9f26.py:89`,
  `test_live_path_direction_preservation_e6e9.py:50`,
  `state/test_baseline_advance_aba_e6e9.py:91`,
  `test_explicit_assignee_resolver_65d7.py:161`. New kwargs default `None` and
  thread through the identical carriers, so no double lacking `status_map` today
  (proven off-path by S2) receives `priority_map`.

**Core/config:** `config.py` NEW `local_to_jira_priority`, `effective_priority_map`, `effective_create_defaults`; `outbound_differ.py` NEW two resolvers; `outbound_mutation_builders.py` thread both maps; `outbound_field_diff.py: compute_update_fields` NEW `priority_map` param.

**LEFT UNCHANGED:** `adapters/jira/acli.py:175`, `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py: 359,370` (int-keyed int-subscript reverse-id lookup, bug 5010).

**create_defaults (str-valued ONLY).** New `config.effective_create_defaults( project_key, root=None) -> dict[str,str]` (three-layer merge, no vocab gating). Baseline (from code): Cloud (`outbound_fields.py:141-149`) summary/description/ issuetype/priority/assignee/(cond)status/parent; DC (`backend.py:79-92`) same minus parent; `project` added by caller. **required-beyond-baseline** = a createmeta-required field NOT in that set with a plain STRING value. Object/array requireds are inexpressible → OUT of scope, filed as `discovered_from` follow-up. UPDATE applies none. No file nears the 800-LOC cap.

## Testing
Unit only; offline; no network. Fixtures build a `[mapping]` overlay with `projects.<KEY>.priority_map` (str keys) and str-valued `.create_defaults`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `test_priority_config_effect` — a `projects.KEY.priority_map` str overlay
      (`"2"="P2"`) overrides the str built-in; effective map + all three payload
      consumers (Cloud create, DC create, update) emit the overlaid name.
- [x] `test_priority_drifts` — a priority absent from the effective map DRIFTS:
      `resolve_outbound_priority` returns `None`, the payload OMITS `priority`
      (never "Medium"), a warning is recorded, sync does NOT fail.
- [x] `test_create_defaults_applied` — exercises the
      `_effective_create_defaults_for` → `map_local_to_remote` → leaf-body seam:
      resolved str-valued defaults merge into BOTH create bodies for
      required-beyond-baseline fields, baseline fields win on collision, and UPDATE
      applies none.

Test tier: unit
baseline.summary: Config-driven priority mapping + per-project create_defaults

# S3 — Gerrit project + LLM-Review label + submit requirement + submitWholeTopic

## Why
This is the gate's integrity rule: a change is submittable ONLY when the deterministic
`LLM-Review` vote is MAX and there are no unresolved comments. `copyCondition` avoids re-paying
for an expensive LLM review on a no-code-change re-upload; `submitWholeTopic` lands whole
reviewed features atomically. The integrity property is not just "the label gates submit" but
"ONLY the bot can set the label" — so a human cannot cast `LLM-Review` and bypass the gate.
Gerrit is pinned to **3.14.1** (d251 docker-compose), so every predicate/feature used here
(`-has:unresolved`, `copyCondition`, submit requirements) is above its minimum and was
validated to parse against live 3.14.1.

## What
- Create the `rebar` project in Gerrit (NoteDb).
- `LLM-Review` label in `refs/meta/config` (project.config): `function=NoBlock`; values `-1..+1`;
  **`copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`** (peer-pattern correction). We deliberately do
  NOT include `changekind:TRIVIAL_REBASE`: a TRIVIAL_REBASE copies the vote even when the change
  was rebased onto a **different base** (diff is byte-identical but the base moved), which would
  certify a tree the LLM never reviewed against the new base — the "copyCondition certifies an
  unreviewed tree" risk the Opus red-team flagged. `NO_CODE_CHANGE` pins the parent tree, so it
  only carries the vote across a true no-op re-upload (e.g. commit-message-only edit). A real
  rebase therefore drops the vote and forces a fresh review (the safe default for a correctness
  gate). `function=NoBlock` is **required, not a free choice**: on 3.14.1 a blocking label
  function is rejected, so blocking comes from the submit requirement.
- Submit requirement (project.config): `submittableIf = label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved`.
  This is what blocks submit; the label is advisory on its own. Both predicates validated to
  parse (HTTP 200) on live Gerrit 3.14.1.
- `change.submitWholeTopic=true` — set in the **server-level** `gerrit.config` `[change]`
  section, NOT in project.config (it is a server-global key, silently ignored in project.config).
  GOTCHA (peer research): topics are **global + un-namespaced**, so a topic name reused in a repo
  the submitter can't see could silently block submit; for this single-repo PoC that risk is
  minimal, but adopt a topic naming convention (e.g. `rebar-<feature>`) and document it.
- Access controls: grant the auto-generated `label-LLM-Review` vote permission to the **Service
  Users** group; humans may push changes for review but cannot submit without the label and
  cannot themselves cast `LLM-Review`. The Service Users group is created/wired in **S4**; S3
  lands config that references it and is testable in S3 by an **admin** casting the vote.

## Scope
In: project + `LLM-Review` label (NO_CODE_CHANGE copyCondition) + submit requirement +
server-level topic config + the label ACL grant. The "only the bot votes" end-to-end proof is
completed in S4 (the bot account does not exist in S3); in S3 the vote is exercised by an admin.
Out: the bot account + event/vote wiring (S4); replication (S5); GitHub lockdown (S6). Gerrit
version is fixed upstream by d251 (3.14.1).

## Files
- `infra/gerrit/project.config` (pushed to `refs/meta/config`): label, submit requirement,
  `copyCondition=changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`, ACL grant.
- `infra/gerrit/gerrit.config` (server-level): `[change]\n  submitWholeTopic = true`. (Impl
  note: same gerrit.config d251 mounts; S3 owns/patches the `[change]` section.)
- `infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`: provisions the project + pushes `refs/meta/config`. Impl
  notes (not separate ACs): (a) **idempotent** — push a fully-declarative project.config via
  `git push HEAD:refs/meta/config`, guard project creation with check-before-create; (b)
  **auth** — needs Gerrit admin creds (HTTP password / SSH key), source documented (env/SSM),
  fail-fast if absent; (c) **dry-run/diff** mode before mutating the live instance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A change can be pushed for review to the `rebar` project; submit is BLOCKED until
      `LLM-Review=+1` (MAX) AND no unresolved comments — verified by an admin casting the vote
      (the bot-only path is proven in S4). Both predicates parse + enforce on 3.14.1.
- [ ] The `label-LLM-Review` vote permission is granted **exclusively** to the Service Users
      group: a regular developer cannot cast `LLM-Review` (push `%l=LLM-Review+1` is rejected /
      not applied) while a Service-Users member can.
- [ ] `copyCondition=changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE` carries the vote across a no-code-change
      re-upload (e.g. commit-message-only amend) BUT a genuine rebase onto a moved base
      (TRIVIAL_REBASE) does NOT carry it — the vote is dropped and re-review is required.
      Verified on 3.14.1 by (a) a message-only amend keeping the vote and (b) a real rebase
      dropping it.
- [ ] `change.submitWholeTopic=true` is set in server-level `gerrit.config` `[change]` (NOT
      project.config), and demonstrated: two changes under one topic submit atomically and
      neither submits independently while its topic partner is open.
- [ ] The submit requirement is the SINGLE code-review vote in v1 (no human Code-Review / CI
      Verified yet — follow-on epic 1fa8). Record this deliberate single-gate stance + planned
      evolution in a brief ADR/note.
baseline.summary: infra: S3 — Gerrit project + LLM-Review label + submit requirement + submitWholeTopic

## Context
rebar should run deterministic workflows that mix scripted + agentic (LLM) steps, defined as git-tracked text editable by both agents and humans, executed identically from the library, CLI, and MCP server, drawing from a git-native prompt library with evals, with a read-only rendered graph. Langflow is NOT adopted (engine/editor); Langfuse is optional (OTLP trace sink only). Direction (A) approved; the plan reached an Opus-APPROVED v3 after a 3-round review loop.

The deterministic gate's SECURITY (signing/attestation/protected-tags/trust-boundary) is OUT OF SCOPE and tracked in epic 8a1c-fdaf-f57a-4104. Here the gate is an ordinary, unsecured example step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Workflow DSL + JSON Schema + reference-integrity linter; `rebar workflow new/validate/show`.
- [ ] Thin linear executor (graphlib) with run_id + idempotency, run-state as events, async over MCP.
- [ ] Agentic steps: generalized runner output_schema, hardened git-ref snapshot, scoped ticket tool, per-step provider.
- [ ] Prompts-as-files (resolve_prompt inverted) + Inspect/promptfoo eval seam.
- [ ] Read-only render; setup wizard; optionality CI; built-in example workflows; LangflowRunner retired.
- [ ] Module-size policy respected; Burr tripwire CI test in place.
- [ ] Workflows are coordinate-free, schema-validated text (GitHub-Actions-style YAML),
- [ ] A thin linear in-process executor runs scripted+agentic steps across lib/CLI/MCP;
- [ ] Git-native prompt library + evals; multi-provider per step; read-only graph render;
- [ ] Stays a thin executor (Burr tripwire); no Langflow/Langfuse runtime dependency.

## Context / Proven Defect

The 8322 close incident was rebar-debugged to a strict-tag ordering issue, not a recovery failure. The second verifier FAIL occurred at event timestamp 1786063291486790001 while the Gerrit criterion was still untagged; the exact `[operator-attested]` edit followed 37.30 seconds later at 1786063328784010001. ADR 0043 and `completion_verifier.md:81-86` intentionally treat every untagged criterion as codebase-verifiable, so rejecting ticket-only external evidence was correct.

The actionable defect is `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE` in `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:48-65`. It tells every FAIL caller that adding concrete evidence to a ticket comment will be considered on retry, but omits the exact `[operator-attested]` tag prerequisite for evidence that inherently lives outside the repository. The operator followed that incomplete guidance and incurred a second 240-request verifier run that could not pass by contract.

## Approach

- Preserve the generic guidance and existing no-force posture.
- State the two evidence channels affirmatively: repository-verifiable criteria require repository evidence (a comment may point the verifier to it); external evidence is admissible from a concrete ticket attestation only when the criterion begins with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag.
- Keep malformed or untagged criteria on the existing codebase-verifiable default; do not weaken ADR 0043 injection boundaries or completion judgment.
- Strengthen the existing interface test for FAIL remediation so it requires the exact tag prerequisite and the untagged-external fallback.

## Testing

- RED: the existing remediation interface test, strengthened to require `operator-attested`, the exact tag, and the untagged external-evidence limitation, fails against current guidance.
- GREEN: focused interface test passes after the guidance-only change.
- Run focused completion-verifier interface tests, lint, typecheck, and the default test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every FAIL remediation distinguishes repository-verifiable evidence from external operator-attested evidence.
- [x] The remediation names the exact `[operator-attested]` tag prerequisite and says an untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone.
- [x] The guidance remains generic, does not advertise force/bypass, and does not change completion-verdict semantics.
- [x] [operator-attested] The strengthened remediation interface test is observed RED before the fix and GREEN after it.
- [x] [operator-attested] Lint, typecheck, and the default test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Completion FAIL remediation omits operator-attested tag prerequisite

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The completed fix on reportable-chalkstony-eeve skips full-history commit discovery only when accepted-scope file impact is empty. Impact-present closes still run the same unbounded path, and current end-to-end telemetry shows it now dominates the user-visible close command.

Frozen Codex-rollout sample (2026-08-22 through 2026-08-23T21:15Z), limited to canonical tracker closes with a matched Bedrock COMPLETION_VERDICT and metrics.llm_calls > 0: n=10 completed closes, p50=28.24m, p90=57.32m, p99=61.60m. The matched completion-verifier workflows themselves are generally 1-4m; recent 25-62m closes spend most of their time before the verifier sidecar.

Static mechanism: close_precheck._check_work_landed calls commit_impact.referencing_commits for every impact-present close. That helper reads all 2,690 commits and extract_ticket_refs produces 2,229 unique historical candidates. 702 candidates require alias/prefix resolution; _scan_alias walks the current 5,351-ticket store for each, implying roughly 3.8 million ticket-directory visits before completion verification. Ordinary subject prefixes and deprecated four-digit references enter the candidate set. This is the residual impact-present case left explicitly unchanged by reportable-chalkstony-eeve.

Post-diagnosis refinement: the alias sub-case was bounded by the sibling fix 4234-821b (commit 5c64deff, one alias-index build). The residual proven at runtime is that resolve_ticket_id's 8-hex short-id branch and its generic >=4-char prefix branch still call os.listdir(tracker_dir) once per candidate, so non-alias candidates (short-id-shaped tokens, ordinary subject prefixes, deprecated four-digit fragments) still scale O(unique_candidates x tracker).

## Plan
- Add a deterministic performance reproduction for an impact-present close with many historical reference candidates and a large tracker.
- Replace per-candidate full-store short-id/prefix resolution with a single indexed resolution strategy while preserving every accepted commit-ticket reference form and ambiguity behavior.
- Keep descendant credit, attached commits, --ref behavior, file-impact-vs-diff enforcement, and fail-closed git-error semantics unchanged.
- Measure the repaired pre-verifier scan and pin a scaling assertion that prevents history x tracker behavior from returning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Impact-present close commit discovery does not perform a full tracker walk per unique historical candidate.
- [x] The scan cost is bounded to one tracker index/build per invocation plus linear code-history parsing.
- [x] Full, two-quad short, alias, Jira, compatibility four-digit/prefix, trailer, and leading-subject reference forms retain current matching and ambiguity semantics.
- [x] Descendant ticket credit remains covered end to end.
- [x] File-impact-vs-diff enforcement remains covered end to end.
- [x] A scale-focused regression test fails on the current history-times-tracker implementation and passes on the repair.
- [x] Before/after wall-time and scan-count evidence is recorded on this ticket.

## Testing
- Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py::test_referencing_commits_bounded_scans_for_non_alias_candidates` — RED-first scan-count regression (counts tracker-root `os.listdir` calls; fails on the per-candidate implementation, passes bounded at <=1 on the repair).
- Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py::test_indexed_short_id_and_prefix_resolution_matches_per_call` — indexed short-id / generic-prefix / ambiguous-prefix resolution equals per-call scanning (AC#3).
- Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -k "resolver_scan_index or falls_back or work_landed"` — None-on-hard-failure fail-open contract, per-call fallback crediting, and descendant-credit / file-impact-vs-diff end-to-end checks.
- Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_referencing_commits_alias_scan_perf.py` — the alias-branch bound and indexed/per-call parity remain green.
- Gates: checked with `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.
- Before/after scan-count evidence recorded as a ticket comment (82 -> 1 tracker-root scans for 80 distinct non-alias candidates, target still credited).

## Context

The `Verify Authorship Identity` CI gate (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`) fails closed when the blobless CI-checkout pack of the `tickets` branch exceeds `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` (today `102400` = 100 MiB, a deliberate growth canary from commit `16a1a385` / ticket `037b`). The pack is currently ~481 MiB, so the gate is RED (bug `defensive-buckskin-rhino` / `a453-193b-2864-451b`).

The proof on parent epic `536b-8930-b922-4063` establishes that the ONLY lever that shrinks this blobless pack is reducing reachable commit+tree objects via causal-stability history collapse, and that even maximal SAFE coalescing (N=30d horizon) lands at ~365-380 MiB — it cannot reach 100 MiB without an unsafe <4-day horizon. Therefore a temporary budget-raise bridge is unavoidable to get the health lane green while the reclaim mechanism + structural fixes (W1 batch write lane, W2 root tree shard) land.

## Scope of THIS ticket (the bridge, this change only)

Raise `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` from `102400` (100 MiB) to `563200` (550 MiB) — ~70 MiB headroom over today's 481 MiB pack — and add a self-documenting comment immediately above the value that names the restore ticket (`fluorspar-comparable-zeren` / `0894-b9b8-6590-4904`) so the bridge is reversible and traceable. This is a temporary, deliberately-reversible loosening of the canary, NOT a permanent budget change; the restore is tracked separately.

One companion test is coupled to the declared budget: `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py::test_pack_guard_contract` reads the live workflow env and asserts it equals the parametrized value, so that expectation must move in lockstep (`102400` -> `563200`). The other `102400`/`_STANDALONE_LIMIT` occurrences in the test suite are subprocess-env fixtures passed as explicit guard overrides (not read from the workflow), so they are unaffected and stay as-is.

## Out of scope

The history-reclaim mechanism (S0-S3), W1/W2 structural fixes, and the eventual restore to 100 MiB are separate tickets under the epic. This ticket does no history rewrite and no prod mutation of the `tickets` branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` in `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` is set to `563200`.
- [x] A comment immediately above the value marks it as a TEMPORARY bridge and names restore ticket `fluorspar-comparable-zeren` (`0894-b9b8-6590-4904`).
- [x] The companion coupled expectation is updated: `test_pack_guard_contract` in `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py` moves its parametrized limit from `102400` to `563200` so it re-asserts the new declared budget.
- [x] The guard control flow is unchanged: only the threshold value, its self-documenting comment, and that one coupled test expectation change; the `git count-objects` fail-closed logic is untouched.
- [x] The commit carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer for this ticket and a DCO sign-off.
- [x] [non-codebase] The change is pushed to Gerrit for review (`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`) and is NOT self-submitted.
  provenance: environment=Gerrit (rebar.solutions.navateam.com) + GitHub Actions CI; principal=rebar review-bot (LLM-Review), CI (Verified), human operator (Submit); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — change 2392 received LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and merged to origin/main as commit d0bcd620; submitted by the human operator, not self-submitted.

## Portability

`REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB` is a plain workflow environment variable consumed by a POSIX `bash`/`git count-objects` guard; changing its value introduces no dependence on any single CI provider and no new capability. The `project.portability` criterion is satisfied because the guard remains a provider-agnostic shell check whose only input is a git object count.

## Context
Cloud summary writes currently cross ACLI subprocess behavior and a shared REST helper that retries three times with 2s/5s waits. The selected route must consume only the shared logical budget without weakening unrelated callers.

## Outcome
Implement one Cloud summary write invocation and primary-store observation under the S1 contract. Each write launches one ACLI process; summary recovery performs one REST request with no inner sleep.

## Plan
1. Add sanitized historical exit/stdout/stderr fixtures, including the real exit-1 unauthorized shape, and fail loud on unknown shapes.
2. Execute one `acli jira workitem edit` process per physical write invocation. Preserve POSIX process-group and non-POSIX child cleanup.
3. Thread a per-call retry policy from `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` up through its sole GET intermediary `_direct_rest_get` (both in `acli_rest.py`) to `get_issue_by_rest`. `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` gains an optional policy argument defaulting to today's three attempts with 2s/5s backoff; `_direct_rest_get` gains a matching optional pass-through argument with the same default. Only `get_issue_by_rest`'s summary-recovery call selects the one-attempt/no-sleep policy. Every other consumer of `_direct_rest_get` keeps three attempts with 2s/5s waits unchanged by omitting the argument: `get_issue_property` and `search_user_by_email` (in `acli_rest.py`), the status-transitions read (`acli.py`), and the issuelinks read (`acli_graph.py`). The direct `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` callers that bypass `_direct_rest_get` (the PUT/POST helpers and paged GETs in `acli_rest.py`) likewise omit the argument and are unchanged. `get_issue_by_rest` (in `acli.py`) is itself a shared entry point with production consumers OUTSIDE the `jira/` adapter dir, so the policy is a per-call pass-through argument on `get_issue_by_rest` too, defaulting to today's three-attempt/2s-5s behavior and forwarded to `_direct_rest_get`. ONLY the new summary-recovery observation call passes the one-attempt/no-sleep policy; every other caller of `get_issue_by_rest` omits the argument and is byte-for-byte unchanged. Those callers are enumerated explicitly: `outbound_differ.py:132` (`client.get_issue_by_rest(jira_key)`), `apply_handlers.py:259` (`ctx.client.get_issue_by_rest(str(jira_key))`), and `binding_store.py:108` (resolved dynamically via `getattr(client, "get_issue_by_rest", None)`). None of these three changes call signature or retry posture — each keeps three attempts with 2s/5s waits, and the pre-existing HTTP-error-not-retried contract that `outbound_differ.py:127` documents is untouched because the policy governs only connection-level retry, not HTTP-error handling.
4. Classify auth/TLS/permission/invalid requests as permanent; eligible network, 429, and retryable 5xx outcomes return metadata to the shared budget rather than replaying locally.
5. Observe the primary REST issue resource, never indexed ACLI JQL, before any ambiguous replay.
6. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. Include only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; cap the whole serialized log at 1,024 Unicode code points. Each terminal/exhausted outcome also carries a bounded operation-diagnostics collection holding AT MOST EIGHT entries (excess entries are dropped), and every diagnostic message is redacted through the shared diagnostics seam before the same 512-Unicode-code-point message cap — this is the collection AC7 bounds, distinct from the single completion-log message above.

## Testing
Stateful fakes and real child-process tests assert process/request counts, cleanup, classification, redaction, exact completion-log fields and bounds, one-log emission cardinality, and neighbor retry behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] One Cloud write invocation launches exactly one ACLI process.
- [x] Summary recovery performs one primary-store REST request with no inner sleep or JQL.
- [x] All unrelated REST callers retain three attempts with 2s/5s waits, verified for each `_direct_rest_get` sibling (`get_issue_property`, `search_user_by_email`, transitions read, issuelinks read), the direct PUT/POST callers, AND every existing `get_issue_by_rest` consumer outside the `jira/` adapter dir — `outbound_differ.py:132`, `apply_handlers.py:259`, and `binding_store.py:108` (via `getattr`) — each of which omits the policy argument and is asserted to retain the three-attempt/2s-5s default; only the summary-recovery call selects the one-attempt/no-sleep path.
- [x] Permanent and transient outcome classes map to the shared contract without adapter replay.
- [x] Historical triples decode deterministically and unknown triples do not retry.
- [x] Timeout cleanup passes for POSIX process groups and non-POSIX child processes.
- [x] Operation diagnostics hold at most eight entries and every message is redacted before its 512-Unicode-code-point cap.
- [x] Every terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log with only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Out of scope
Core dispatch cutover and Jira DC execution.

## Context / Problem
Advanced bridge/reconciler, audit, LLM/review, workflow, identity, and gate commands mix inline argparse construction with manual dispatch. Their current `--help` behavior is also the source of the 21 unsafe/incomplete top-level help forms. The grammar must become reusable without importing optional runtimes.

## Approach
Inventory every registered advanced grammar in `src/rebar/_cli/`, standalone verification/auth command modules, and the reconciler request CLI. For each family:

1. Extract existing argparse construction into the S2a side-effect-free factory contract; migrate manual nested dispatch where required.
2. Switch the selected runtime handler to the same factory in the same change.
3. Keep parser factories in lean modules: no Pydantic AI/provider, FastAPI/UI, Jira transport, workflow executor, metrics, tracing, or other optional runtime imports.
4. Reuse argument-definition helpers between canonical nested bridge forms and `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, `jira-onboard`, and hidden `bridge-status`; only `prog`, visibility, and replacement epilog differ.
5. Preserve handler-owned nested command selection, lean modes, backend/mode selection timing, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes. Optional capability enforcement remains S4 and never occurs during parser construction.
6. Register all parser references and make every visible advanced route generation-ready, without changing top-level help routing yet.
7. Reconcile the parse-failure seam. The S2a `RebarArgumentParser.error()` raises `ParseError`, not `SystemExit(2)`. Every migrated handler that today translates a parse failure through `except SystemExit` (currently `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` and `src/rebar/_commands/trusted_env_cmd.py`) is updated in the same change to also catch `ParseError` and reproduce the identical process exit code (2) and stderr/usage bytes it emits today — no traceback escapes and no exit-code delta.
8. Preserve bespoke parser presentation. Families that currently pass `usage=`, `formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter`, or `add_help=False` (`verify-opcert`, `verify-commit`, `verify-authorship`, `remote-cert`, `trusted-env`, and the nested bridge parsers) keep those exact behaviors. The S2a factory (`src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py`) is extended additively with optional keyword passthroughs — `usage`, `add_help`, and `formatter_class` (each defaulting to today's S2a behavior, i.e. `RebarHelpFormatter` and `add_help=True`) — so migrated factories request the preserved presentation explicitly while still producing a `RebarArgumentParser` (raises-not-exits) instance. The extension stays stdlib-only and changes no existing call site's behavior.

Families include bridge and reconcile, audit, prompt/criteria/LLM setup, review/scan/explain/sign operations, workflow, config/identity verification/trusted-environment/remote-certificate commands, and enrichment.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No top-level help cutover occurs here. Current execution behavior remains invariant. The later help normalization is approved, but generated bytes do not become authoritative until S2d. Each family reverts with its handler switch; no stored data changes.

## Testing
Use parser unit matrices plus real subprocess/interface tests for nested selection, help-safe parser construction, aliases, lean modes, failures, streams, and exit codes. Install import blockers for every heavy optional module and use negative controls that prove selected execution still imports what its mode actually requires.

Readiness proof (AC5): a registry-driven test iterates every advanced route, resolves its recorded parser-factory reference, invokes the factory, and asserts it returns a constructed `argparse.ArgumentParser` bound to the expected `prog` — with heavy optional runtimes import-blocked and without executing any handler — proving each route is deterministically S2d-generation-ready in-session.

Parse-failure parity (AC4): production-path tests feed malformed argv to each migrated command through its real entry point and assert the unchanged exit code (2) and stderr/usage bytes, covering the `ParseError`-vs-`SystemExit` seam. Presentation parity: a per-command test asserts `--help`/usage bytes are byte-identical to pre-migration for every command that carried `usage=`/`RawDescriptionHelpFormatter`/`add_help=False`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every registered advanced command and nested subcommand runtime uses one S2a parser factory; no inline/manual duplicate grammar remains.
- [x] Canonical and compatibility bridge spellings share argument-definition helpers while retaining approved `prog`, replacement, visibility, and historical usage behavior.
- [x] Parser construction succeeds in the no-extras environment and imports no handler executor, provider, UI, Jira transport, or other optional runtime.
- [x] Production-path tests show no unapproved delta in nested selection, accepted/rejected argv, diagnostics, streams, exit codes, help/usage byte output (byte-identical `--help`/usage for commands carrying `usage=`/`RawDescriptionHelpFormatter`/`add_help=False`), or lean-mode availability.
- [x] Every advanced route has a valid factory reference and is ready for deterministic S2d generation.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2c — Migrate advanced command grammars to lean argparse factories

## Summary

Discovered while fixing bug `unhelping-creviced-rhino` (`e127-a3ad-895a-4a2f`), which extended the JS-safe decimal-string wire form from the MCP surface to CLI `--output json`. The NDJSON export surface — `rebar export` and its library twin `rebar.export_tickets()` / `rebar.iter_export_states()` (`src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py:168`) — was deliberately left OUT of that change's scope and still emits bare 19-digit JSON integers.

## Evidence (measured, structural)

Against a freshly created ticket with a comment and a signature, using the e127 build (every other CLI `--output json` surface reads 0):

```
show   --output json   unsafe ints: 0
list   --output json   unsafe ints: 0
audit show --output json unsafe ints: 0
export                 unsafe ints: 4
    $.created_at
    $.comments[0].timestamp
    $.signature.signed_at
    $.updated_at
```

RFC 8259 §6 guarantees numeric agreement only inside `[-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1]`, so any float64 consumer of the export (jq, node, DuckDB/pandas via a JS-based loader) silently rounds these — the same hazard e127 documents with a runtime-proven `node` reproduction (stored `…898642` reads back as `…898600`).

## Why it was excluded from e127

Export is NOT `--output json`. It is a separately versioned interop projection carrying its own `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` and a round-trip contract against `rebar import` (`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`). Retyping the export side without a coordinated import-side coercion would break `export | import` round-trips, so it needs its own change and its own schema-version decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Decide the policy for the NDJSON export/import pair: adopt the same decimal-string wire form
      on export WITH matching `int()` coercion on import, or keep integers and document the hazard.
      → Adopted the decimal-string wire form: export emits via `js_safe_dumps`
      (`src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py:175`); import coerces `created_at`/`comments[].timestamp`
      provenance with `int()` via new `_coerce_ns` (`src/rebar/_io/_provenance.py`). Merged in
      `origin/main` `36ae045f41c3`.
- [x] If the representation changes, `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped and the change is recorded
      as BREAKING in `docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` (per `docs/api-stability.md`).
      → `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1→2; BREAKING entries in `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`,
      and `docs/import-export.md`.
- [x] A round-trip regression test proving `export | import` preserves the EXACT nanosecond digits
      (not merely the type) — a float64 round-trip gives `…600` for `…642`, so a type-only
      assertion would pass against a broken implementation.
      → `tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_import_round_trip_preserves_exact_ns`
      (digit-exact) + `test_export_timestamps_round_trip_exactly`.
- [x] Structural coverage pinning whichever behaviour is chosen so the surface cannot drift.
      → `tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py::test_export_emits_no_uninteroperable_integer`
      fails on any bare >2^53 number on the wire (proven via sandboxed mutation: bare `json.dumps`
      → RED).
baseline.summary: `rebar export` NDJSON still emits >2^53 nanosecond timestamps as bare JSON numbers

# S3 (a8ea): Config-driven type mapping + type-granular skip

## Context / Problem
Epic 3d7a adds a config-driven mapping seam (S1: `mapping_config.MappingLayer` with a `type_map` axis, `SKIP="skip"`, `resolve_for_project`, `validate`). S2 made STATUS config-driven — the template: `config.effective_status_map` (`config.py:77`) threads a per-project `status_map` through the Backend port into the field mappers; `rebar-status:` stamp in `outbound_labels.py`; reverse-map-free inbound `recover_status_label` (`:152`). TYPE is hard-coded: `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` (`adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py:40` = `{bug,story,task,epic}`), `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` (`config.py:13`). Distinct types can collapse to one Jira type (lossy). Syncable = `get_args(TicketType)` (`types.py:23`) − `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` = `{bug,epic,story,task}`. S3 is type-only.

## Approach
Three outcomes for `ticket_type`: **remap** (effective type map), **skip** (per-project via SKIP), **FAIL-CLOSED** on an undecided syncable type. Round-trip safety: NEW `rebar-type:` annotation label symmetric with `rebar-status:`, reverse-map-free inbound. Type resolution + fail-closed live in TWO upstream places — the up-front gate and the mapper. acli is UNTOUCHED.

### Finding — acli.create_issue stays a passthrough (NO rewrite)
On the differ path acli NEVER sees a raw local type: the mapper (`outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields:143`, DC `jira_datacenter/backend.py:86`) already sets `issuetype` to the mapped Jira NAME, and `dispatch_one.py:188-195` derives `ticket_data["ticket_type"]` FROM that name. Re-resolving via `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` inside acli would fail-close on EVERY differ create (`"Story"` isn't a key). ALL `client.create_issue` callers: `dispatch_one.py:209` and `apply_outbound.py:101` pass mapper output; `access_check.py:150` passes a FIXED probe `{"ticket_type":"task"}` relying on `.capitalize()`. None pass a config-mappable raw local type, so `acli.py:282` is CORRECT and unchanged.

### Finding 1 (G7) — fail-closed fires ONCE UP-FRONT, before the mutation loop
Parent AC ("load-time fail-closed on undecided types") is PRIMARY. `effective_status_map` is invoked LAZILY per-ticket in the differ loop, so a per-ticket gate would NOT fire before mutations. FIX:
- NEW `config.effective_type_map(project_key, root)` mirrors `effective_status_map` (`:77`):
  `builtin=MappingLayer(type_map=LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA)` ← `resolve_for_project`; returns
  `{k:v for k,v in resolved.type_map.items() if v != SKIP}`.
- NEW `config.assert_type_decisions_complete(project_key, root)`: every syncable type
  (`get_args(TicketType) − EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`) must be DECIDED — target OR `SKIP` — else
  raise `MappingConfigError` (guards a future TicketType; built-in covers all four today).
- WIRING (proves fail-closed-before-mutation): call it ONCE at the top of
  `compute_outbound_mutations` (`outbound_differ.py:298`) — after config load `:377`, BEFORE
  `_compute_outbound_select_absent_gets` (`:381`) and the per-ticket loop (`:430`) — over the
  DISTINCT project keys of `local_tickets` (via `projects_store.resolve_project`). (S1's
  `validate` stays uncalled — S4.)

### Finding 3 (E2) — where the per-project excluded set comes from (SKIP entries)
NEW `config.effective_excluded_sync_types(project_key, root)` = `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` UNION `{k for k,v in resolved.type_map.items() if v == mapping_config.SKIP}`, over the SAME `resolve_for_project` layer `effective_type_map` uses. Reuses S1's SKIP sentinel (`mapping_config.py:51`) as the type-granular skip signal — no separate axis. A local type mapped to `SKIP` is excluded for that project ON TOP of the built-in set.

### Finding — reverse TYPE map for the lossy-stamp rule (G6)
`_desired_type_annotation` stamps only when the forward target does NOT reverse to this local type — needs a Jira→local reverse map. `config.py` has none, and `outbound_labels.py` imports ONLY `config`. FIX: NEW `config.jira_to_local_type` mirroring `jira_to_local_status` (`:64`), lock-stepped with `inbound_fields._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_TYPE` (`:105`) via a parity test.

### Finding 4 (G1G2) — thread type_map through ALL THREE OutboundMapper impls
`type_map` must follow every one of S2's THREE `map_local_to_remote` bodies + the shared field mappers, or the differ's `type_map=` kwarg hits a signature lacking it → `TypeError`. Add `type_map: dict[str,str] | None = None` (beside `status_map`) to: (1) `OutboundMapper` Protocol (`_backend.py:372`); (2) Cloud `JiraBackend.map_local_to_remote` (`jira/backend.py:73`, forwards `status_map` `:89`); (3) DC (`jira_datacenter/backend.py:121`) — each forwards into its field mapper. Then (4) `outbound_fields._map_local_to_jira_fields` (`:101`) resolves issuetype via `type_map` (replacing coerce `:143`), fail-closed; (5) DC `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (coerce `:86`) same. NEW `outbound_differ._effective_type_map_for` mirrors `_effective_status_map_for` (`:272`); `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` (`outbound_mutation_builders.py:37`) passes it.

## Surface-parity census — stamp + inbound + prefix filters
- Stamp: NEW `outbound_labels._REBAR_TYPE_LABEL_PREFIX="rebar-type:"`,
  `_desired_type_annotation` (mirror `:89`, using `config.jira_to_local_type`),
  `_diff_type_annotation_labels` (mirror `:114`). Threaded at BOTH
  `outbound_mutation_builders.py` sites: create `:81`/`:138`; update `:276`/`:281`.
- Inbound: NEW `inbound_fields.recover_type_label` (mirror `recover_status_label` `:152`) +
  `_LOCAL_TYPE_VOCAB` from `get_args(TicketType)`; wired at `:311-313`, label-over-raw `:326`.
- Per-project excluded set replaces the single `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` read (`:377`) at BOTH
  consumers: `:430` (loop) and `:519` (`_compute_outbound_select_absent_gets`).
- `rebar-type:` added to ALL FOUR prefix tuples: `outbound_labels.py:34` (re-export
  `outbound_differ.py:77`); `inbound_collection_diffs.py:88` (re-export
  `inbound_differ.py:31`; read by `reconcile_check.py:96`); `differ.py:105`
  `_BRIDGE_INTERNAL_LABEL_PREFIXES`; `inbound_translate.py:58` `_BRIDGE_INTERNAL_TAG_PREFIXES`
  (keeps its `imported:` omission).

## Scope
New/changed: `config.py` (effective_type_map, assert_type_decisions_complete, effective_excluded_sync_types, jira_to_local_type); type_map signature thread through `_backend.py:372` + all three OutboundMapper impls + both field mappers (Finding 4); `outbound_labels.py`, `outbound_mutation_builders.py`, `outbound_differ.py`, `inbound_fields.py`, `inbound_collection_diffs.py`, `differ.py`, `inbound_translate.py` (census). **acli.py is NOT modified.** All additions small; module-size cap 800 LOC (target 200-500).

## Acceptance Criteria
(`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_type_mapping.py`)
- [x] `test_fail_closed_fires_before_mutation_loop` — undecided syncable type raises
  `MappingConfigError` from `compute_outbound_mutations` before any mutation is built.
- [x] `test_skip_is_a_valid_type_decision` — a `SKIP` type passes the gate, is in
  `effective_excluded_sync_types`, absent from `effective_type_map`.
- [x] `test_effective_type_map_default_equals_builtin` — no `[mapping]` ⇒ built-in; project
  `type_map` remaps.
- [x] `test_effective_excluded_union_builtin_and_skip` — == `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` ∪ SKIP keys.
- [x] `test_type_skip_excludes_ticket_both_consumers` — excluded at `:430` AND `:519`.
- [x] `test_type_map_threaded_through_all_three_mappers` — `type_map=` reaches all impls, no
  `TypeError`.
- [x] `test_rebar_type_label_stamped_when_lossy` — collapsing types stamp `rebar-type:` at
  create + update via `config.jira_to_local_type`.
- [x] `test_rebar_type_label_recovered_reverse_map_free` — `recover_type_label` restores it.
- [x] `test_rebar_type_prefix_excluded_all_four_tuples` — filtered by all four tuples.
- [x] `test_jira_to_local_type_parity` — == `inbound_fields._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_TYPE`.
- [x] `test_local_type_vocab_derived_from_ticket_type` — == `get_args(TicketType)`.

Test tier: unit
baseline.summary: Config-driven type mapping + type-granular skip (collapse round-trip via rebar-type label)
