## Context

The current tickets branch stores ticket event dirs flat at `tickets/<id>`, making the root tree about 270 KB and causing every single-ticket commit to re-emit that large root tree. W2 changes only the on-disk layout to reduce per-commit tree churn. S1 history reclaim, W1 batching, and any live shared-store cutover are out of scope.

## Scope

Implement a fan-out layout `tickets/<sha256-2>/<id>` for canonical ticket ids. New code must read legacy flat and sharded stores during the expand phase, preserve all ids/aliases/events, and provide an idempotent ensure-registry migration. Do not run this migration against the live shared `.tickets-tracker`; fixture/throwaway stores only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New ticket writes land at `tickets/<sha256-2>/<id>`; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves a fixture single-ticket mutation makes the top-level tree bytes at least 80% smaller than an equivalent flat layout.
- [ ] Alias, short-id, and full-id resolution are unchanged for flat, mixed, and migrated stores; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout_heldout.py` plus existing resolver selectors prove this.
- [ ] Event replay/listing is unchanged for flat, mixed, and migrated stores; targeted reducer/list tests prove the same states are returned.
- [ ] The migration maps every flat ticket dir to its deterministic shard, leaves no flat ticket dirs behind, preserves identities/event bytes, and a second run makes no commit; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves this.
- [ ] An interrupted migration working tree with some already-sharded dirs resumes safely on rerun without identity loss or duplicate commits; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves this.
- [ ] Migration collisions are fatal and atomic: two source paths mapping to the same sharded target abort before any partial commit/move; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py` proves this.
- [ ] Merge-as-union reconvergence still preserves both sides on a two-clone sharded fixture; `tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout_heldout.py` proves both commits remain reachable.

## Implementation Plan

1. Add `rebar._store.ticket_layout` as the single layout owner: sha256 first-2-hex shard/relpath derivation, existing-dir resolution, ticket-path-to-tracker-root reverse derivation, deterministic ticket iteration, shard-container recognition, pinned-tree path parsing, shard-container mkdir, and `migrate_flat_ticket_dirs_unit`.
2. Writers create the shard container with `exist_ok=True` under the write lock before the atomic `os.rename(staging_dir, ticket_dir)`, preserving ticket+first-event atomic publication while an empty shard container remains benign; rollback/unpublish may leave an empty shard container, which fsck classifies as store data.
3. Keep resolver outputs separator-free. `_ids.py` returns ids/names only; exact lookup and prefix/alias scans build the same sorted id index from flat and sharded dirs through the layout helper.
4. Route all flat ticket path consumers through the helper. Required inventory: `_store/{staging,gitutil,store_usability,compat,ensures,env_identity,hlc}.py`; `reducer/{_api,_inbound}.py` (including `reduce_ticket` reverse derivation); `_ids.py`; `_engine_support/{field_reads,lookups,reads,validate,next_batch,commit_impact}.py`; graph `{_cache,_graph,_hierarchy,_links,_status,_unblock}.py`; _commands `{_seam,gates,doctor,composer,composer_edit,leaf,link_revert,unlink,claim,transition,transition_close,txn,delete,recent_creates,completion_candidate,compact,compact_plan,compact_rebuild,compact_recovery,compact_trigger,compact_txn,close_precheck,close_disposition,fsck_scan,fsck_repair,fsck_tracker_health,fsck_recover,fsck_authorship,fsck_restore,identity,session_log,tracker_maintenance,trusted_env_cmd,verify_authorship}.py`; sidecar/bot readers `{attest/authorship,attest/authorship_resolution,signing,metrics/{blame,event_metrics,sidecar_metrics,bug_trends},_snapshot/{ticket_view,ticket_objects},llm/{completion_sidecar,code_review/sidecar,overlap/queue,overlap/digest_sidecar,enrich_drain,plan_review/claimability,plan_review/relation_snapshot,plan_review/sidecar,epic_bug_screen,workflow/recorder},_io/{export_ndjson,import_ndjson},_engine/rebar_reconciler/{__main__,transition_replay,local_label_intent,impossible_links,inbound_translate,reconcile_check,apply_inbound_events,apply_inbound_records}}.py`.
5. Register ensure id `ticket-layout-shards` in `_store.ensures`. It runs under the write lock, precomputes all moves before mutation, refuses target collisions as fatal/permanent, treats already-sharded dirs as no-ops on rerun, stages old+new paths, and commits once only when drift exists. If killed after renames but before commit, no partial commit exists; rerun completes the mixed working tree or an operator can reset it; targeted tests cover this resume path.
6. Register required-capability token `sharded-ticket-layout` in `compat.KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` before any store stamps it. The migration appends that token so older v1.0+ binaries fail closed while current binaries read the store.
7. Make fsck/store-health depth-aware at shared `foreign_store_path_list` / `_holds_events`, so valid two-hex shard containers are store data even when empty and unrelated top-level dirs remain `FOREIGN_STORE_PATH`.
8. Update pinned snapshot readers to parse both `<id>/<event>` and `<shard>/<id>/<event>` through the layout helper.
9. Document the durable layout scheme, sha256 shard derivation, migration, and compat-token semantics in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/migrations.md`.
10. Preserve expand-phase compatibility: before migration, readers handle both layouts and existing flat tickets may be updated in place; after migration, all tickets resolve to shards. Live cutover is deferred to the operator.
11. The migration holds the write lock for local filesystem renames and one local git commit only; no network push happens inside the lock. The live 6,008-ticket cutover is operator-scheduled for a maintenance window.
## Surface-Parity Census

- CLI: in scope via subprocess create/comment/show fixture tests.
- MCP/API: out of scope for live MCP because the server may run older code; accepted because tools delegate to the same library/core paths.
- Library: in scope via `import rebar` create/show/reduce tests.
- Automated callers: in scope through inventory updates and targeted unit selectors; no live Jira/LLM calls.
- Dual-direction: in scope for local read/write and import/export; outbound Jira field semantics unchanged.

## Testing / Verification

Run targeted RED/GREEN selectors: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout.py tests/unit/test_store_sharded_layout_heldout.py -q`, existing resolver/reducer selectors, and reconvergence/store path selectors. Final preflight: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`.

## Deployment / Rollback

This change ships mechanism only. Applying it to the live shared store is an operator decision and is not performed here. After an operator migrates a store, rollback is a tickets-branch revert or approved tracker-maintenance action that restores flat paths, relocates any post-migration sharded ticket dirs back to flat paths, and removes the capability stamp together; tests assert that post-migration tickets remain resolvable after the compensating rollback. No agent force/bypass.

## Portability

In-process layout/migration only; no CI-provider dependency.
baseline.summary: W2: shard the 6,008 flat ticket dirs to cut per-commit root-tree churn

## Problem

`tests/conftest.py`'s `_no_repo_commits` guard fails a test whose checkout HEAD moved and ends its message with an unconditional instruction:

    f"git repo. Undo the stray commit(s) with: git reset --hard {before[:10]}"

Like the REPO_ROOT leak guard next to it, this guard compares two snapshots of SHARED checkout state and therefore cannot tell a test that committed from a concurrent `git commit` made by another process in the same checkout. That second case is real and observed: the `carryable-basalt-beagle` scope-correction comment records `Test moved the repo HEAD (<sha> -> <sha>)` errors seen twice in one session from a concurrent commit, and `f0fb` established the same shared-checkout condition for the leak guard.

Followed literally by someone whose HEAD moved because ANOTHER process committed, `git reset --hard <sha>` discards that commit and every uncommitted change in the worktree. The guard is handing out a destructive remedy for a cause it cannot confirm.

This is **wording, not behaviour** — the guard itself deletes nothing. It is filed separately from `carryable-basalt-beagle` (which removed the leak guard's actual deletion) to keep that change tight around its proven root cause.

## Prior art for the fix shape

`tests/_isolation.py:leak_failure_message` was corrected under `f0fb` (commit `c9a5388a83`) to name both causes instead of asserting the one it cannot know, and `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py` pins that property. The same treatment applies here: name the concurrent-commit possibility, and condition the `reset --hard` on the reader having confirmed the commit is theirs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The HEAD-move message no longer prescribes `git reset --hard` unconditionally; the
      destructive step is explicitly gated on the reader confirming the commit came from the
      test rather than from another process sharing the checkout.
- [x] The message names the concurrent-external-commit possibility, mirroring
      `leak_failure_message`.
- [x] A test pins both properties, alongside the existing ones in
      `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py`.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: HEAD-move guard prescribes an unconditional git reset --hard

# Discovered while closing the map-staleness gap on [rebar:259b-b7da-a346-4785] (Gerrit 1394)

259b now makes the capability map's **provenance** checkable: `run_metadata.json` derives the harness digest from the Dockerfile's `FROM` line instead of a hand-copied constant, and `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` records the digest it was measured against, asserted against that pin by `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`. A re-pin now lands red until the map is regenerated.

## What that does NOT cover

The staleness gate keys on the **digest**. It detects "these answers describe a different image". It cannot detect **"these answers are wrong about THIS image"** — and that is the failure mode this epic has actually hit:

* `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` recorded that DC rejected a 255-char label. A dedicated live
  cell later posted 254- and 255-char labels to the SAME pinned image and both were accepted.
  The entry was retracted. The digest never changed, so no digest-based check could have caught
  it.

The mechanism is that the map's answers are produced by an **agentic LLM run** summarising raw REST evidence. The evidence in `evidence.json` was correct; the *reading* of it was wrong. So the map has a trust boundary at exactly the point the ticket wanted removed — 259b's own words: "otherwise we have swapped 'discovering from the instance' for 'trusting a model', which is worse."

## The shape of a fix (not prescribing it)

A **deterministic, non-LLM re-measurement** pass: a script that reads the committed contract and re-asserts each claim with a fixed REST call and an exact comparison, exiting non-zero on divergence — no model in the measurement path. `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` (bug 1019) is the existing precedent for a deterministic probe alongside the agentic map, and `_assert_project_capabilities` in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` is the precedent for "declared contract, fail loudly on divergence". The agentic run stays useful for DISCOVERY (open questions, new checklist items); it just should not be the last word on a value the harness then depends on.

## Also recorded: one measurement gap left open by 259b

`docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md` notes the description/comment 32767 boundary is a **coverage gap** — `jira.text.field.character.limit=32767` was read from the instance, but a literal 32K+ payload was never written, so the limit is confirmed as *configured*, not as *observed*. That needs an amd64 live run; it cannot be settled from a dev worktree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every claim the harness DEPENDS on is re-assertable by a deterministic (no-LLM) pass whose
      comparison is exact, and which exits non-zero on divergence
- [ ] the pass is runnable against the pinned image on demand, and its failure message names the
      committed claim that diverged
- [ ] the description/comment ceiling is measured with a real over-limit payload and read-back,
      closing the recorded coverage gap
- [ ] the agentic map's role is documented as DISCOVERY, with the deterministic pass as the
      authority for anything the harness relies on
baseline.summary: The capability map's answers are LLM-summarised, so a wrong answer at an unchanged digest is still undetectable

Scope: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` (95 files, 27,284 LOC, 42% comment density). ~970 lines leave — the largest shard.

Dominant category: 28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines), already single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, AGENTS.md and ADR 0058.

Four new ADRs proposed, each consolidating an argument restated 4-8 times: field-convergence fit-then-normalize (8 sites); pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers (3 independent arguments, 3 prior incidents); unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps. Plus amendments to ADR 0028, 0055 §(g), 0031, 0035.

Verified stale: `_backend_registry.py:3` 'STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented' while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; the S3/S4-not-landed notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`.

Headroom: `_ref_lock.py` 1 -> ~21, `dispatch_one.py` 14 -> ~57, `inbound_differ.py` 18 -> ~66, `binding_store.py` 18 -> ~33, `fetcher.py` 29 -> ~80.

This subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured external-API facts that cannot be re-derived from code. The do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G1G2/G6)

### 1. The dominant-category count was wrong — re-measured

The body claims "28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines)". That is not borne out by the tree. Measured over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

    $ grep -rn "RELOCATED VERBATIM" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # 6 sites, ALL under adapters/jira_datacenter/
    $ grep -rniE "800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # a SEPARATE, smaller set (transport.py, retry.py, transitions.py)
    $ grep -rliE "RELOCATED VERBATIM|800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" ... | wc -l
    10                      # 10 distinct files carry EITHER marker

No single site carries the quoted combined marker. The two families are disjoint, and neither is close to 28. The real figure is **~12 occurrences across 10 files**, not 28.

**Consequence for the shard's headline yield.** The "~970 lines leave" estimate was built on the inflated count for its largest single category. That estimate is therefore UNRELIABLE and must not be treated as a target. The implementer MEASURES the actual recoverable total and records it on this ticket; the number is an output of the work, not an input to it. Do not manufacture relocations to reach ~970.

### 2. Write-ordering must cover the ADRs, not just `do_not_move`

The plan requires the `do_not_move` list to be appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands, but says nothing about ordering for the four proposed new ADRs (field-convergence fit-then-normalize; pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers; unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps) or the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035.

Those ADRs are the single-source DESTINATIONS for the arguments currently restated 4-8 times. If a comment citing "see ADR NNNN" is collapsed before ADR NNNN exists, the citation dangles and the argument is simply LOST — which is the opposite of relocation and is not recoverable from the diff by a later reader.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] The shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it
      is collapsed or deleted — destination first, then the relocation
- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination; nothing is deleted
      without a destination that already exists
- [ ] The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the
      unreliable ~970 estimate. The measured marker counts (6 RELOCATED VERBATIM, 6 cap mentions,
      10 files) are the corrected baseline
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are CORRECTED where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete — specifically `_backend_registry.py`'s "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be
      implemented" (false: `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules) and the S3/S4-not-landed
      notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay VERBATIM (this subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured facts that cannot be
      re-derived from code — the do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard)
- [ ] No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged

## Why

GitHub CodeQL flags 28 remaining open code-scanning alerts on `main`: 27 `py/path-injection` and 1 `py/stack-trace-exposure`. All are genuine (the false positives were already dismissed under 5b57). They collapse to a small number of root causes:

1. **Unvalidated ticket-id → filesystem path.** `rebar._ids.resolve_ticket_id()` has a fast
   path that returns the caller's raw string verbatim when it happens to name an existing
   directory (`_ids.py:152`), *before* any regex/allowlist check. A traversing/absolute id
   (`../sibling`, `/etc/x`) is handed back as if canonical, then callers join it to the
   tracker dir. This is the source for ~18 sinks (the reducer read path + `reads.py`).
2. **Sidecar `resolve_ticket_id(id) or id` fallback.** The audit readers in
   `completion_sidecar.py` and `plan_review/sidecar.py` fall back to the *raw* id when
   resolution returns `None`, so even a hardened resolver is bypassed — the raw string builds
   a `os.path.join(tracker, id)` → `os.listdir`/`open` (sinks 112/119/156/163, 184/192).
3. **Editor prompt-id traversal.** The workflow editor server's `/prompt?id=` handler builds
   `<repo>/.rebar/prompts/{pid}.md` from an unvalidated query param (`editor_server.py`
   158/159); the packaged branch is allowlist-guarded but the project-override branch is not.
4. **Stack-trace exposure.** The review-bot `/rerun` 502 returns the Gerrit exception string
   in the response body (`review_bot/app.py:266`).

Trust model: rebar is a single-tenant local tool; the realistic vector is the MCP/CLI confused-deputy (an agent driven by untrusted ticket content passing a crafted id). Severity is Low–Medium, but the fixes are low-risk (no legitimate ticket id / prompt id contains a path separator, `..`, or is absolute) and retire the whole alert class.

## What

Four containment barriers, mirroring the taint map:

- **`_ids.py`** — add `_is_safe_segment(name)` and reject non-segment ids at the top of
  `resolve_ticket_id`; rewrite the fast path to normalize + containment-check the candidate
  against `tracker_dir` and return the directory's `basename` (separator-free by
  construction). Sanitizes the 18 downstream sinks that build paths from the return value.
- **`completion_sidecar.py` / `plan_review/sidecar.py`** — drop the `... or ticket_id`
  fallback in the filesystem-path readers; on `None` return the function's existing empty
  result (`None`/`[]`/`0`). The hardened resolver's fast path already subsumes the fallback's
  only legitimate purpose (an id that already names a real dir), so this is behavior-preserving
  for valid input.
- **`editor_server.py`** — contain the prompt-id path in `_raw_prompt_text` (resolve +
  `is_relative_to` the prompts dir) and reject separator-bearing ids at the handler entry.
- **`review_bot/app.py`** — log the Gerrit exception server-side; return a generic 502 body.

Default CodeQL query suite unchanged; this is a `src/rebar` change plus new unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolve_ticket_id` returns `None` for any id that is not a safe single path segment
      (rejects `../x`, absolute paths, `..`/`.`, `/`/`\` separators, and leading-dot names),
      and its fast path returns a separator-free canonical directory name — so no untrusted id
      escapes the tracker directory. Valid full/short/alias/Jira-key/prefix ids still resolve.
- [ ] The audit sidecar readers in `completion_sidecar.py` and `plan_review/sidecar.py` no
      longer fall back to the raw unresolved id; when resolution fails they return their empty
      result instead of building a filesystem path from unvalidated input.
- [ ] The workflow editor `/prompt` read (`_raw_prompt_text`) cannot read a file outside
      `<repo>/.rebar/prompts/`; a traversing prompt id yields no file (returns `None`/404).
- [ ] The review-bot `/rerun` 502 response body contains no exception/stack-trace text; the
      detail is logged server-side.
- [ ] New unit tests assert traversal rejection for the resolver, one sidecar reader, and the
      editor prompt read, and assert the review-bot 502 body carries no exception detail.
      `make lint` and the affected test suites pass.
baseline.summary: Harden ticket-id/prompt-id path handling + review-bot error body (retire remaining CodeQL path-injection & stack-trace alerts)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The completion verifier receives only the fenced ticket_context (description + comments, gate_ops.py assemble step) — zero file contents. Every file is discovered agentically: measured across five live verifier runs, 84-158 requests x ~4-6s each, dominated by read_file/search_files round-trips, and all four captured runaway loops were search_files repeat signatures — the model hunting for text it expects to exist. Wall-clock cost is round-trips, not tokens: runs already cache-read 8.7M of 8.8M input tokens, but that history was assembled one tool round-trip at a time. Overlap analysis of the four live gate traces against the closing subtree's file_impact union shows 67-82% of distinct file reads are covered by declared file_impact — the verifier spends its opening requests re-fetching files the tickets already name. NOTE: all four captured traces are CLOSE-path (graph=False) runaway loops; none exercise the graph=True deep-review path.

## Approach

PRE-FETCH, do not restrict (operator-ratified direction): append a bounded, clearly-labelled prefetched-content section to the byte-stable leading part of the fenced verifier context — the ticket's declared file_impact contents plus the referencing commits' diffs — while keeping the full tool surface untouched so the agent still explores beyond the prefetch. Assistance, not a ceiling.

### Which file_impact set each entrypoint prefetches (close gate is graph=False)

The completion CLOSE gate (`_commands.transition`) passes `graph=False` (gate_ops.py:133-143): an epic close verifies its OWN completion criteria, not its whole descendant subtree — re-deriving graph here was the removed runaway bug that blew the step budget (gate_ops.py:138-140). The prefetch MUST honour that same boundary, keyed off the `graph` flag `assemble_context` already receives (operations.py:78):

- **Close path (graph=False, the dominant runaway case):** prefetch ONLY the closing ticket's OWN declared file_impact contents + its referencing-commit diffs. No subtree union, no descendant walk.
- **Standalone deep-review path (`verify-completion --graph`, graph=True):** prefetch the subtree file_impact union, ranked (below). This is the only entrypoint that legitimately sees descendants.

### assemble_context is SHARED — prefetch is opt-in, default off

`operations.assemble_context` (operations.py:78) is also called by the generic dimension-review op `_review_ticket_impl` (operations.py:161) and its workflow wrapper (review_workflows.py:53), NOT only the completion gate (gate_ops.py:144). Keying the prefetch purely off the existing `graph` flag would inject the prefetched-file-contents section into a plain `review_ticket --graph` dimension review, where the completion-verifier trust paragraph does not apply. Therefore add an explicit opt-in parameter `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None` to `assemble_context`, default `None`. Only gate_ops.py (the completion gate) passes a spec; `_review_ticket_impl` / `review_workflows` keep passing nothing, so their assembled output stays BYTE-IDENTICAL. The `graph` flag then only selects own-file_impact vs subtree-union WITHIN a prefetch spec.

### Ranking rule for the budget clamp (graph=True path only)

The subtree union can exceed the budget (the e369 subtree union is 112 paths; the prefetch budget is 30,000 tokens, the upper end of the community-validated 8-30k pre-load range): (1) the closing ticket's OWN file_impact first, (2) subtree paths ranked by cross-descendant frequency (a path impacted by more descendants ranks higher), (3) skeleton-compress files over 500 lines (signatures + docstrings) BEFORE dropping any file, drop lowest-ranked last. On the close path the set is just the ticket's own file_impact, so ranking degenerates to (1) + the same skeleton/clamp rules. A PRE-LOAD MANIFEST records per-file full|skeleton so downstream consumers (the duplicate-call damping sibling's in-context nudge) never claim an elided body is in context.

### Cache mechanism: existing automatic prompt cache, NO hand-placed CachePoint

The prefetch sits in the byte-stable leading part of the fenced context so it is cache-READ under the EXISTING automatic message-tail prefix cache (capabilities.py:684-696, gated on execution_mode="agentic"); there is no separate per-block CachePoint to add (that arm applies a provider-managed whole-tail breakpoint, not a hand-placed cache_control). This aligns with story 2948's cache note: the completion-verifier prompt's STATIC prefix (everything before the `<!--volatile-->` marker, completion_verifier.md:269) is kept byte-identical across the primary and every successor so the automatic prompt cache hits; the prefetch rides the volatile fenced ticket_context, not the static prefix.

### Trust / anti-anchoring lives in the STATIC system-prompt prefix (reaches primary AND successors)

The verifier system prompt (completion_verifier.md:33-37) directs the agent to treat everything inside `<untrusted_ticket_context>` (gate_ops.py:158) as UNTRUSTED DATA, never as instructions. An anti-anchoring line placed inside that fence would be ignored by contract. Instead add a TRUSTED paragraph to `completion_verifier.md` positioned BEFORE the `<!--volatile-->` marker (i.e. in the static prefix). Because the recovery successor prompt is `successor_system_prompt()` = that same static prefix (before `<!--volatile-->`) + the banking addendum (completion_banking.py:75-85), the trusted paragraph appears in BOTH the primary verifier prompt AND every batched successor prompt from a SINGLE source — co-located with the prefetch data on both paths, no separate constant to maintain. The paragraph (a) names the new labelled `<prefetched_file_contents>` section, (b) states it is a convenience starting point pre-loaded from declared file_impact — still content-to-verify, NOT instructions — and (c) instructs the verifier to confirm every prefetched body against the live working tree before relying on it, and to re-read the full body for any file marked `skeleton`. The fenced prefetch section itself carries ONLY the labelled data + the PRE-LOAD MANIFEST + the explicit skeleton tool-call marker — no behavioural directive that depends on being trusted.

Misses in the trace analysis were dominated by test files, so the prefetch set includes a matching-test-glob heuristic (tests/**/test_<module>*.py for each prefetched module).

### Phase 0 — measure first

Extend the usage recorder to log the raw distinct fetch list per gate run — (tool, path/query) — not just hashed top-repeats. Today's records cannot validate overlap directly: signatures hash full args (line ranges, query strings), and brute-forcing 2,573 tracked paths resolved only 2 of 6 heavy read_file repeats. Record first; tune the prefetch set from measurement.

### Phase 1 — prefetch file_impact + referencing-commit diffs, bounded

Per-file char cap and the 30k-token aggregate cap mirroring completion_recovery's _MAX_* pattern; oversize files skeleton-compressed with an explicit marker naming the tool call to fetch the rest. Because the prefetch is part of the assembled `ticket_context`, it reaches the batched recovery successors automatically: post-2948 recovery is BATCHED successor runs (`_run_successors`/`_run_one_successor`, ceil(remainder/batch_cap), ≤8 criteria/batch — the per-criterion fan-out was deleted by story 2948), and `successor_instructions` (completion_banking.py:118) embeds the same `ticket_context` verbatim. The prefetch is therefore sent once per batch (a handful of batches, not per criterion) and cache-read after the first via the byte-stable static prefix. `physical_context_ceiling` (completion_recovery.py:108) already bounds `len(context)` for every primary/successor run; the 30k aggregate prefetch cap keeps the assembled context under that ceiling, and the prefetch bytes are included when the recovery inputs are validated against it so an oversize prefetch is trimmed (not overflowed into the hard "context bound exceeded" refusal).

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py — Phase 0: record raw distinct fetch list per gate run.
- src/rebar/llm/operations.py — add opt-in `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None` to `assemble_context` (default None → `_review_ticket_impl`/review_ticket callers byte-unchanged); build the prefetched-content section + manifest when a spec is passed, selecting own-file_impact vs subtree-union by the graph flag; include referencing-commit diffs.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py — Phase 1: pass a PrefetchSpec into assemble_context for the completion gate only; the fenced context now carries the labelled prefetch section.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — include the prefetch bytes in the physical_context_ceiling input validation so an oversize prefetch is trimmed; no separate cache_prefix (the prefetch rides ticket_context and the static system prefix already cache-hits across batches).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md — TRUSTED paragraph BEFORE the `<!--volatile-->` marker describing the prefetched-file-contents section and the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton rule (automatically inherited by successor_system_prompt).
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py — new: ranking, clamp, manifest, skeleton marker, toolset pin, graph=False-vs-True set selection, assemble_context prefetch=None no-op for the generic review callers, successor context carries the prefetch, ceiling accounting, and a static-prefix system-prompt test asserting the trusted paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` (so it is in both primary and successor prompts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Phase 0: every agentic gate run records its distinct fetch list (tool name + primary path/query arg) in the usage log by default; checked by a unit test asserting the recorded shape for a run with known tool calls.
- [x] Overlap measurement exists: an analysis entry point reports the fraction of recorded fetches covered by a ticket's file_impact; checked by running it on recorded data.
- [x] Phase 1: the completion verifier's context includes a labelled prefetch section with ranked file_impact contents and referencing-commit diffs, bounded per-file and by the 30k-token aggregate cap; unit test pins the assembly (ranking order, bounds, skeleton marker, label).
- [x] Entrypoint boundary honoured: on the close path (graph=False) the prefetch set is the closing ticket's OWN file_impact only (no subtree walk); the subtree union + frequency ranking applies only on the graph=True deep-review path; unit test pins both selections.
- [x] Opt-in / no-op for shared callers: `assemble_context` prefetch defaults to None, and `_review_ticket_impl` / review_workflows call sites produce byte-identical context to today (no prefetch section); unit test pins the no-op for a graph=True generic review call.
- [x] The pre-load manifest records per-file full|skeleton and is exposed to the tool-wrapping seam; unit test pins its shape.
- [x] The tool surface is unchanged: the verifier retains read_file/search_files/list_directory; unit test pins the toolset with prefetch enabled.
- [x] Trusted anti-anchoring: the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton guidance lives in the completion_verifier.md static prefix BEFORE `<!--volatile-->` (not inside the untrusted fence), and names the prefetched-contents section; a unit test asserts the paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` (so `successor_system_prompt` inherits it) and that the fenced section carries no behavioural directive.
- [x] Recovery successors receive the prefetch via the shared assembled ticket_context (batched successor runs, not per-criterion), and the prefetch bytes are included in the physical_context_ceiling input validation so an oversize prefetch is trimmed rather than raising; unit test pins that a successor's assembled context carries the prefetch and the ceiling accounting.
- [x] Post-clamp coverage recorded PER ENTRYPOINT: (a) the clamped CLOSE-path (own file_impact) set's coverage is computed against the four recorded live (graph=False) traces' distinct reads and recorded on this ticket; (b) the clamped graph=True (subtree-union) set's coverage is computed against a NAMED synthetic subtree fixture (the e369 112-path union), NOT the close-path traces, and recorded. The unclamped 67-82% figure does not carry over to either.
- [x] Live Bedrock A/B before ship (session experiment, not in unit suite): BASELINE is defined as a verifier-scale run on the same real closed ticket's material with prefetch DISABLED, captured immediately before the prefetch run (same tool surface, same ticket, same config otherwise); its request count and verdict class are recorded first. The prefetch run then reduces total request count by at least 20% versus that baseline and produces an equal verdict class; both request counts and verdicts recorded on this ticket.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck clean; full CI marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing

Held-out unit oracle for context assembly + toolset pins (python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ -q): ranking order over a synthetic subtree, close-path (graph=False) own-file_impact selection vs graph=True subtree-union selection, assemble_context prefetch=None no-op for the generic review callers, aggregate clamp with skeleton-before-drop, manifest shape, truncation marker text, successor context carries the prefetch, physical_context_ceiling accounting for prefetch bytes, and a static-prefix system-prompt test asserting the trusted anti-anchoring paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` and names the prefetch section. Phase-0 recorder shape test alongside existing usage_log tests. Live A/B on Bedrock recorded as ticket comments with usage-log figures: baseline (prefetch off) then prefetch run.

Update AGENTS.md + docs (epic items 6–7) once the ADR (deft-evolutive-mosasaur) and trusted-env registration land: require using the MCP server for all rebar operations EXCEPT operations that need local code (testing, investigation, debugging, validation), and state the certified-op policy correctly. Single concern: guidance + user-facing docs — no server/infra behavior here.

## Scope + rationale
1. **AGENTS.md MCP-required policy**: a rule that rebar tracker operations go through the MCP server,
   with the explicit carve-out for local-code ops (test/investigate/debug/validate). Because this
   introduces a new prohibition ("don't drive the tracker by ad-hoc local CLI when MCP is
   available"), do the new-prohibition **consumer scan**: enumerate the existing guidance/workflows
   that tell agents to run `rebar ...` tracker ops locally and reconcile each. The rule is written in
   AGENTS.md (rebar's canonical cross-vendor guidance) as an **umbrella** that explicitly governs the
   downstream guidance surfaces (`docs/`, `templates/`, `.agents/rules/`, packaged `rebar explain`
   guides, example skills): a `rebar <verb>` shown for a tracker op names the operation and routes
   through the MCP server when configured, so those surfaces are reconciled by reference rather than
   individually rewritten. The non-doc surfaces (templates/packaged-guides/vendor-rules/skills) get a
   per-file textual sweep under a linked follow-up ticket; this leaf edits AGENTS.md + docs only.
2. **Certified-op wording correction**: certified **plan-review** and **completion-verifier** ops
   (the only two op-cert kinds, ADR 0049) route through the MCP server and are enforceable because
   the box is a registered trusted signing environment (the trusted-env slice). **Code review is the
   Gerrit `LLM-Review` vote, NOT an op-cert** — record the code-review-vs-op-cert correction (the
   epic's item-7 "code review ... certified through the MCP server" phrasing) per **ADR 0104**
   (deft-evolutive-mosasaur, decision 3), so guidance doesn't imply a nonexistent code-review
   op-cert. Enforcement of the certified ops is **enableable but deferred**: describe them as
   enforceable-when-enabled via the trusted-env mechanism, and cite the operator flip runbook
   (`infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md`) — do NOT claim enforcement is live.
3. **docs/mcp-auth.md**: fill the §7 "AWS-specific deployment" gap with the ADR-decided recipe
   (nginx `/mcp/` TLS edge + `static` verifier + per-client bearer). Surface the client-connection
   guide (copilot/codex/claude config shapes from olm's `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`) from
   docs/mcp-auth.md, which currently lacks the link.

## Prior-art / doc-drift check (blocking prior-art overlay)
Git history shows the hand-authored MCP docs carry modest recurring upkeep; keep the AWS recipe and client guide close to the single-sourced config keys the ADR names so they don't drift. Match the existing docs/mcp-auth.md structure rather than inventing a parallel doc; reference the already-landed `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` and `infra/runbooks/*` rather than duplicating them.

## Testing / Verification
Docs-only leaf: no behavioral tests. Each acceptance criterion below carries its proof (a recorded tracker artifact or a greppable command). Run the greppable oracles plus `make lint` before pushing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AGENTS.md states the MCP-required rule + the local-code carve-out, written as an umbrella that
  names the downstream guidance surfaces it governs
  (checked: `grep -niE 'MCP server|local-code|carve-out' AGENTS.md` shows the rule + carve-out).
- [x] The consumer scan is recorded as the primary oracle: `rebar show inadequate-hydrated-starling`
  carries a comment enumerating each pre-existing tracker-op "run rebar locally" instruction surface
  and its reconciliation disposition (umbrella-covered / carve-out / follow-up ticket). A supporting
  `grep -rniE 'rebar (claim|transition|link|review-plan)' AGENTS.md docs/ .agents/ templates/`
  lists the candidate lines the reviewer confirms are each covered — the comment, not the grep, is
  the pass/fail record.
- [x] A follow-up ticket for the per-file reconciliation sweep of the non-doc surfaces
  (templates/, packaged `rebar explain` guides, `.agents/rules/`, example skills) is created and
  linked `discovered_from` this ticket (checked: `rebar show inadequate-hydrated-starling` lists an
  inbound `discovered_from` child).
- [x] The certified-op section names plan-review + completion-verifier as MCP-routed/enforceable-via
  trusted-env and code-review as the Gerrit vote (NOT an op-cert)
  (checked: `grep -niE 'plan-review|completion-verifier|LLM-Review' AGENTS.md` shows both op-cert
  kinds plus the Gerrit vote framing).
- [x] No reference asserting a code-review op-cert survives in guidance
  (checked: `grep -rniE 'code[- ]review.{0,40}op-?cert|code[- ]review.{0,40}certif' AGENTS.md docs/`
  returns only the ADR 0104 correction record, never an assertion that one exists).
- [x] Guidance describes certified-op enforcement as deferred/enableable, not live
  (checked: `grep -niE 'enforcement.*(defer|enable)|mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip' AGENTS.md` shows the
  deferred framing + runbook citation).
- [x] docs/mcp-auth.md §7 contains the AWS deploy recipe with the ADR-named config keys
  (checked: `grep -niE 'AWS|http_tls_at_edge|auth_static_tokens_file|auth_strategies' docs/mcp-auth.md`
  shows the recipe with the keys).
- [x] A client-connection guide documenting the three client config shapes is reachable from
  docs/mcp-auth.md (checked: `grep -ni 'mcp-client-setup' docs/mcp-auth.md` links the guide, which
  documents the copilot/codex/claude shapes).

## Compat / rollback
Docs-only; rollback = revert the doc edits. No behavior change.

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur (ADR 0104 decides routing/auth), and the trusted-env registration slice (guidance claims certified ops are enforceable via MCP, which is only true once the box is a trusted env).
baseline.summary: Guidance: require the MCP server for rebar ops (except local-code ops); document certified-op routing

# S1 — Isolate review-gate scratch on a dedicated EBS volume

## Why
Gate snapshots (`rebar-gate-snapshots`) and the review-bot's per-review `reviewbot-*` clones share the OS/root filesystem, so a review burst can wedge the whole Gerrit host (bug `3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd`, 5h outage). ADR 0112 decision 3 moves that workload onto its own EBS volume, mirroring the existing `/var/gerrit` split from ADR 0012.

## Design — mostly config + Terraform; ONE narrow code guard

`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` already parameterises the snapshot store's base dir (`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:peek_store_root`), and `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` honours `TMPDIR`, so RELOCATION needs no code: it is a Terraform volume + a host mount + two compose env vars + a bind mount. New code is needed for exactly one thing — the ADR consequence that an unreachable scratch volume must REFUSE, not silently fall back to root.

**Terraform** — `aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch` (gp3, `var.gate_scratch_volume_size_gb`, **no** `prevent_destroy`: scratch is rebuildable, unlike the data volume), `aws_volume_attachment.gate_scratch` at `/dev/sdg`, two new `user_data` template vars (`gate_scratch_volume_id`, `gate_scratch_mount`), an output, and two CloudWatch alarms.

**Host** — `user_data.sh` resolves the NVMe device by volume id with the SAME loop the data volume uses (extracted into a shell function so there is one copy, not two), formats idempotently, mounts by UUID via `/etc/fstab`, then asserts `mountpoint -q` and `exit 1` if the mount did not take. It writes the two marker files below.

**Container** — `docker-compose.yml` review-bot gains `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` and `TMPDIR` set to the scratch path and a host bind of the mount's PARENT (`/var/lib/rebar`), so both markers are visible inside the container. A plain bind, not an `external:` volume, so `config-check.sh` check 5's compose-up pairing is untouched. `compose-up.sh` pre-creates the parent dir.

**The refusal (AC3's teeth).** A bare mount point is an ordinary directory: if the volume is not mounted, `store_root()`'s `mkdir(parents=True)` silently recreates the store on ROOT — the exact regression the ADR forbids. Two marker files make the two states distinguishable without a new mechanism (no new env var, no new config key, so the mechanism ratchet stays at `new=0`):

- `<mount>/../.gate-scratch-required` — the DECLARATION. Lives on the root filesystem, so it
  survives an unmount.
- `<mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted` — the PROOF. Lives on the VOLUME, so it disappears with it.

`gate_admission()` checks this BEFORE `_slot_dir()` (which would otherwise mkdir on root) using the side-effect-free `peek_store_root()`; declaration present + proof absent raises S6's existing `GateScratchUnavailableError`, which already routes as a retryable non-verdict. Both markers absent = no dedicated volume declared = today's behaviour, so no laptop, CI runner, or existing operator is affected.

**Observability** — `observability.sh` §2e publishes `disk_used_percent` for the scratch mount (`InstanceId` + `mount` dimensions, following §2) and a `gate_scratch_mounted` 1/0 heartbeat (dimensionless, following §2b). Two alarms in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf` beside the root alarm, both `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` with the 300/3/2 window and both SNS actions, so bug `3276`'s missing-data fix is carried, not copy-pasted.

**Sizing.** Default 50 GiB, matching the data volume: the ADR measured gate/investigation scratch at 3.6 G on root, and S6 bounds concurrent gates at 4, so 50 GiB leaves ~42 GiB below the 85% alarm — an order of magnitude of headroom over observed peak. It is a variable, per ADR 0112 decision 6.

## Scope
IN: Terraform volume/attachment/variables/output, user-data mount, compose env + bind, compose-up dir, scratch metric + two alarms, the admission refusal, runbooks, tests. OUT: Docker/journald/`/var/tmp`/container-layer caps (S2–S5); no `terraform apply` — this change is written and validated only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Terraform declares a gate-scratch EBS volume, attachment, size variable, tags and an
      output; the volume carries NO `prevent_destroy` and its comment states it is rebuildable
      scratch rather than source-of-truth data.
- [x] `user_data.sh` resolves the scratch device by volume id, formats idempotently, mounts by
      UUID through `/etc/fstab`, and exits non-zero when the mount point is not a mount.
- [x] The review-bot's snapshot store AND its `reviewbot-*` clone tempdirs resolve to the
      scratch mount (`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` + `TMPDIR` in compose), not to root.
- [x] With the scratch volume declared but not mounted, `gate_admission` raises
      `GateScratchUnavailableError` instead of materialising a store on the root filesystem;
      with neither marker present, behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] The scratch mount publishes `disk_used_percent` and a `gate_scratch_mounted` heartbeat,
      each with its own CloudWatch alarm wired to `aws_sns_topic.alerts` and
      `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.
- [x] `review-bot-ops.md` and `provision-restore.md` document the steady-state location, the
      two alarms, the refusal behaviour, recovery, and the rebuildable-data posture.
- [x] `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports `new=0`: the refusal introduces no new env
      var, config key, or feature flag.
- [x] Portability: every control is Terraform + a Linux mount + env config, proved by local
      pytest and `terraform fmt/validate`; nothing requires a specific CI provider.

## Testing
Each command is run from the worktree with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"`.

- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` — new RED-first tests: the
  declared-but-unmounted refusal, the no-markers no-op, the mounted happy path, the compose
  env/bind wiring, and the Terraform volume/attachment/output/user-data shape.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` — extended (not duplicated) with the
  two new alarms in its `watched` set and raised anti-vacuity floors.
- `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_observability_disk_pressure.py` — the scratch metric and the
  mounted heartbeat are published by the real `observability.sh`.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py` — S6's admission suite still passes.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py
  tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` — the three gates `make lint` does not cover.
- `make lint && make typecheck`
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform && terraform -chdir=infra/terraform validate`

No `terraform apply`, and no `terraform plan` against live state: this story lands the IaC and its offline guards only.
baseline.summary: S1 — Isolate review-gate scratch on a dedicated EBS volume

## Summary

The outbound comment sync is **not idempotent**. Comments that have already been posted to Jira are re-posted on every hourly reconcile pass. Measured on run 32398224961 (2026-08-20T17:33Z): **205 comments re-posted in a single pass across 28 issues** — roughly **4,920 duplicate Jira comments per day** at the hourly cadence.

Discovered while root-causing `grievous-vulgar-sanderling` (bug 64a0-8768-038c-45b2), the heartbeat-canary alarm for reconcile-bridge.yml. That workflow's failure is a downstream consequence: REB-1861 accumulated duplicates until it hit Jira's hard cap of 5000 comments per issue, after which every `add_comment` for it fails and reds the run.

## Reproduction Steps

Compare per-issue comment counts across two reconcile-bridge runs several passes apart, for **closed** tickets with no new local comments:

1. Pull the run logs for two passes (e.g. runs 32344687307 at 07:35Z and 32398224961 at 17:33Z).
2. Grep `RECON: outbound_update key=<KEY> ... comments=<N>` and
   `RECON: batch_outcome ... key=<KEY> ... comments_applied=<M>`.
3. Observe N and M are identical across both passes, and M == N (they land every time).

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** after a comment has landed in Jira, subsequent passes compute 0 pending comments
  for it. A closed ticket with no new local comments converges to `comments=0`.
- **Actual:** the same comments are recomputed as pending and re-posted on every pass, forever.

Evidence (10 passes apart, all closed tickets):

| Jira key | local ticket | local comments | pending 07:35 | pending 17:33 | applied 07:35 | applied 17:33 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REB-1580 | adroit-deductible-kakapo | 24 | 21 | 21 | 21 | 21 |
| REB-1570 | fireless-schematic-gadwall | 25 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| REB-424 | orb-mantle-talon | 25 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| REB-1861 | nonmystic-topiary-toadfish | 40 | 39 | 39 | 7 (then capped) | 0 (capped) |

REB-1861 holds **5000** comments in Jira against **40** locally — a 125x divergence produced entirely by this loop.

## Suspected mechanism (NOT yet confirmed at runtime)

Two layers should independently prevent a re-post; both appear to be failing:

1. **PRIMARY — comment-id dedup.** `_record_comment_id`
   (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:309-334`, `emersed-specific-mutt`)
   persists the Jira comment id against the local COMMENT event's HLC so a re-sync skips it. It is
   guarded to be a **silent no-op** in four cases: `binding_store is None`, the entry carries no
   `local_comment_key`, the `add_comment` result carries no `id`, or the store predates
   `record_comment_id`. If any holds in production the primary skip never engages and nothing
   reports that it did not.
2. **FALLBACK — body-membership test.** `_diff_comments`
   (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:707`) treats a comment as needing to be
   added when the local body is not present in the Jira body set. Comments round-trip through
   ADF/wiki-text conversion, so a landed comment's Jira body may never string-match the local body.

Confirming which guard fires requires instrumenting a live pass — that is the first task here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Runtime evidence identifying which dedup layer fails (do not fix from static reading alone).
- [x] A reconcile pass over an unchanged closed ticket computes **0** pending comments.
- [x] Two consecutive passes with no local changes post **0** comments to Jira.
- [x] Regression test pinning idempotency: apply a comment, re-run the differ against the resulting
      Jira state, assert no re-emission — including for a body that is transformed on round-trip.
- [x] Decide and document the remediation for the ~5000 duplicate comments already in REB-1861 and
      the duplicates in the other 27 affected issues (operator decision; may be out of scope here).

## Notes

- Jira's per-issue cap is 5000 comments (`COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). REB-1580 at
  21/pass reaches it in roughly ten days, at which point it reds the bridge the same way REB-1861
  does now. This is progressive.
- A separate hardening item (worth its own ticket): rebar classifies the permanent cap refusal as a
  per-mutation failure, contrary to the project's documented skip-vs-failure split (ticket a3fa,
  `pass_io.record_capability_gap`) and the hierarchy-rejection precedent
  (`dispatch_one.py:525-558`). That is what converts the cap into a red workflow.
baseline.summary: Outbound comment sync is not idempotent — ~205 comments re-posted to Jira every hourly pass

# Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

## Context / Problem

A `/rebar-implement` run of epic `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` landed five changes through every gate. **The gates performed to their design envelope.** Plan-review blocked infeasible mechanics (a tenacity-transport claim that cannot wrap boto3; an `isinstance` against a botocore-dependent class; a live canary path that would have made billable AWS calls on every CI run). The completion-verifier twice refused a close whose stated criteria had no test. Full-suite pre-flight caught cross-module regressions `tests/unit` missed.

Every one of those catches shares a property: **the ground truth lived in the repo**, where the reviewer's read/grep tools could reach it.

Four escapes got through, and they are one defect wearing different clothes — **a green signal whose measurement could not have observed the failure it claims to rule out**:

1. **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching and model-availability measurements were taken in account
   `579718921998` / `us-east-2` and recorded as settled fact; the project runs in `896586841071` / `us-east-1`
   (named by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`). No gate compares a claim's observation
   context against the project's environment. A human caught it by asking "is that this project's account?"
2. **Instruments that cannot observe the failure — twice, in the same investigation.** This escape is the
   epic's sharpest example precisely because the *first correction was also wrong*.

   **2a.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls validated a *scoped* IAM grant while running under an identity
   holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than production is structurally unable to
   fail, so its success carries **zero information**.

   **2b.** The prescribed remedy — `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against the role — then produced a
   confident, recorded, and **wrong** conclusion: that `bedrock:Converse` was the action to grant. The
   simulator answered exactly the question asked ("would this policy permit the action *named*
   `bedrock:Converse`?", legitimately no, since that action genuinely exists) but **not** the question that
   mattered ("which action does the Converse API actually *check*?"). Only a real call FROM the instance
   revealed the truth — `AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel` — meaning
   the ORIGINAL plan was right and the "fix" broke it, on a role feeding `eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`, a cutover
   with no fallback.

   The pair is the lesson: a wildcard identity could not fail, and a simulator could not fail *for the reason
   that mattered*. **Evidence is only as good as its ability to have come out the other way for the reason
   you care about** — and swapping one instrument for a more rigorous-sounding one does not establish that.
3. **Tests that cannot fail** — the code-side form of the same defect: a contrast case whose discriminating
   conjunct was never exercised, and an oracle asserting on an object where production passes a string.
   **Both WERE caught** (mutation testing; the LLM reviewer) precisely because they are repo-checkable. That
   contrast is the evidence for this epic's thesis.
4. **Confidence outrunning method**: "verified by reading" was a hand-picked grep that missed a dependency;
   "18/18 green" was reported while typecheck was red.

## Why 1 and 2 are structural, not a calibration miss

`verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all. Plan-review runs **before** the evidence exists, so it cannot audit a measurement not yet taken; the completion-verifier accepts `[operator-attested]` evidence **on trust by design** (ADR-0043). One gate cannot audit it, the other is designed not to. The in-flight T5c rewrite pushes grounding toward current code and IaC state but still cannot observe a live cloud account — nothing in the current design can, and nothing should try.

## Approach

Do **not** make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it. Detail lives in the child story; the shape is:

1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and
   privilege posture relative to production.
2. Enforce their **presence** deterministically, zero LLM, mirroring
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (DET-first doctrine).
3. Let an LLM criterion judge the *declaration* against repo facts — once provenance is text, "plan attests
   account X, IaC names account Y" becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**, which is exactly what the
   gate's strongest criteria already do well.
4. Land the generalized rule as an **advisory** criterion per ADR-0054; corpus replay decides promotion.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, recursive — the verifier's
  own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the instrument under
  suspicion.
- **Escape 4 as gate scope.** Reported-green-while-red is *reporting discipline*, already covered by the
  orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success. Filing it as a
  gate gap would be mis-attribution.
- **Wording changes alone.** The contract was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the defect. This is
  the same lesson as epic `9109-2ad9-2477-4cf6` (Serena tool-choice), which is why that epic's structural
  framing is the model here rather than its subject matter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking measurement provenance is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check
      (no LLM) — `det_measurement_provenance.py`, surfaced advisory through `p6_ac_quality`, landed in
      change 1423 with a mutation-tested oracle (breaking the binding rule, placeholder detection or enum
      membership each kills tests)
- [x] the new criterion ships **advisory** (ADR-0054) and rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, leaving the
      shipped default criteria set unchanged for other rebar clients
- [x] an ADR records the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes
- [x] the completion-verifier is NOT made to re-run world measurements — the rejected alternative stays
      rejected, and a test or grep demonstrates it

## Descoped to `98df-3528-9b1f-405a` (ridiculous-expert-mouse), filed as an `idea`

AC-1 originally also required the wrong-account escape to be **reproduced as a regression fixture** from the real `579718921998` vs `896586841071` case. That clause is NOT delivered and is NOT claimed as done.

Reproducing it means exercising the AGENT criterion's rule (a) semantically, which needs an eval corpus (`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.eval.yaml`) plus a live run — the same behavioural half descoped from story `f161`. Both moved to `98df`, which also carries the rule (b)/(c)/(d) fixtures and the ADR-0054 corpus-replay false-positive rate that would justify promoting the criterion from advisory.

This epic therefore closes on its MECHANISM being delivered and proven — provenance is now forced into the record as text, deterministically enforced, and judged by a tool-enabled criterion — not on that criterion's firing behaviour having been calibrated. The distinction is safe because the criterion ships **advisory**: it cannot block any claim or close, so an uncalibrated advisory criterion is inert-but-useful rather than risky. Promotion is a separate ADR-0054 decision nobody has committed to, which is why `98df` is an `idea`.
baseline.summary: Gate blindness to world-grounded evidence: force measurement provenance into the record

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Nine real scanner integration tests skip when binaries are absent at `tests/unit/test_code_review_conflict_markers.py:97-158`, `test_code_review_public_exposure.py:109-151`, and `test_code_review_ws5.py:347-399`. Verified installs neither scanner although `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:43-71` makes them runtime prerequisites. The review-bot is deployed on Linux/arm64 Graviton while Verified runs on Linux/amd64, so their scanner pins must be platform-aware.

## Approach

Create one checked-in scanner lock manifest with separate `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` entries. Each entry records a Gitleaks version, its exact per-platform release URL, and SHA-256; the pinned checksum is taken from that release’s published `*_checksums.txt` asset at lock-update time. Each platform also references a fully resolved Semgrep requirements lock containing the same top-level Semgrep version and all platform-resolved distribution hashes. Provision Semgrep with `pip install --require-hashes`; do not represent this multi-wheel install as one fictional artifact hash.

Add one provisioning helper as the sole installation owner. It selects the manifest entry from Docker’s target OS/architecture or the CI runner’s actual OS/architecture, rejects an unsupported platform before installation, verifies the Gitleaks digest before extraction, and installs Semgrep only from the selected hash lock. The Graviton review-bot Docker build consumes `linux/arm64`; the Linux x64 reusable Verified lane consumes `linux/amd64`. Tests cover both selections rather than asserting that those different consumers share one binary artifact.

This deliberately supersedes dynamic-Gitleaks/latest and unpinned-Semgrep behavior. Stable per-release assets plus published checksums make reproducible, verified pins preferable; `docs/security.md` is generated, so the scanner-lock documentation is authored in `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`'s curated security narrative and then regenerated with `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`. The regenerated `docs/security.md` identifies the manifest, the checksum source, platform-lock update procedure, and the recovery action for a withdrawn asset (move both platform entries to an available verified release). Include a concrete worked example: bump Gitleaks by reading the release `*_checksums.txt`, updating each platform URL/SHA pair, regenerating Semgrep requirement locks with `pip --require-hashes`, running the installer validation target, and regenerating `docs/security.md`.

Add an explicit native-binary Make target that fails before its focused contracts for an unsupported platform, missing scanner, wrong Gitleaks version/digest, or missing/bad Semgrep requirement hash. It runs the nine real integration contracts only when a supported platform entry is provisioned. The existing skip-with-reason behavior remains for default local tests and unsupported developer platforms. Invoke the target from a reusable parallel workflow used by mirror CI and exact-patchset Gerrit verification, including the job in `vote.needs`.

Do not build Docker, install OpenGrep, or add this target to normal `make lint`/default local tests.

## Scope

- platform-aware scanner manifest, two Semgrep hash locks, and review-bot Dockerfile
- shared provisioning helper and explicit Make target
- scanner integration tests
- reusable mirror/Gerrit workflow and Verified parity guard
- `docs/security.md` scanner-lock ownership, update, checksum, and recovery procedure

## Testing

First prove the generated-document assumption: add a generator-level docs oracle that fails until `render_security()` emits the scanner-lock section, then prove the committed-doc drift check fails when the generator output changes without regenerating and passes after `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`. Exercise manifest selection for Linux/amd64 and Linux/arm64, unsupported-platform rejection, missing Gitleaks, a bad Gitleaks SHA-256, a missing or bad Semgrep requirement hash, and wrong scanner versions. Prove valid selected locks pass the real Semgrep and Gitleaks contracts, that unsupported local platforms retain the skip-with-reason path, and that workflow wiring plus `vote.needs` parity hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The manifest has independent `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` scanner entries, each with an exact Gitleaks URL and SHA-256 sourced from the matching release `*_checksums.txt` asset.
- [x] The review-bot Docker build selects and validates the `linux/arm64` entry; the reusable Linux x64 CI lane selects and validates the `linux/amd64` entry.
- [x] Every platform entry points to a fully resolved Semgrep requirements lock with an identical top-level Semgrep version and all required distribution hashes; the installer uses `pip --require-hashes`.
- [x] The installer rejects an unsupported platform, missing scanner, wrong Gitleaks version/digest, and invalid Semgrep hash before it runs the focused contracts.
- [x] Valid selected scanner locks allow the explicit native-binary target to pass all nine real Semgrep/Gitleaks integration contracts.
- [x] Default local tests on unsupported platforms preserve the existing skip-with-reason behavior and do not provision scanners.
- [x] `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` owns a curated scanner-lock security narrative; regenerated `docs/security.md` names the manifest as the update authority, the checksum source, a concrete per-platform bump example, and the withdrawn-asset recovery procedure.
- [x] One parallel reusable lane serves mirror CI and exact Gerrit patchsets and is required by the Verified vote.
- [x] A generator-level docs oracle proves the scanner-lock section appears in regenerated `docs/security.md`, and the existing drift check proves committed `docs/security.md` fails when generator content changes without regeneration and passes after regeneration.
- [x] OpenGrep, Docker-image builds, normal `make lint`, and default local tests remain outside scope.
- [x] The lane's expected cold-run cost is documented as approximately 1.5-3 runner-minutes without extending the existing 22-23 minute critical path when capacity is available.
baseline.summary: Run pinned deployed Semgrep and Gitleaks contracts in Verified

Scope: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` (95 files, 27,284 LOC, 42% comment density). ~970 lines leave — the largest shard.

Dominant category: 28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines), already single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, AGENTS.md and ADR 0058.

Four new ADRs proposed, each consolidating an argument restated 4-8 times: field-convergence fit-then-normalize (8 sites); pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers (3 independent arguments, 3 prior incidents); unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps. Plus amendments to ADR 0028, 0055 §(g), 0031, 0035.

Verified stale: `_backend_registry.py:3` 'STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented' while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; the S3/S4-not-landed notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`.

Headroom: `_ref_lock.py` 1 -> ~21, `dispatch_one.py` 14 -> ~57, `inbound_differ.py` 18 -> ~66, `binding_store.py` 18 -> ~33, `fetcher.py` 29 -> ~80.

This subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured external-API facts that cannot be re-derived from code. The do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G1G2/G6)

### 1. The dominant-category count was wrong — re-measured

The body claims "28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines)". That is not borne out by the tree. Measured over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

    $ grep -rn "RELOCATED VERBATIM" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # 6 sites, ALL under adapters/jira_datacenter/
    $ grep -rniE "800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # a SEPARATE, smaller set (transport.py, retry.py, transitions.py)
    $ grep -rliE "RELOCATED VERBATIM|800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" ... | wc -l
    10                      # 10 distinct files carry EITHER marker

No single site carries the quoted combined marker. The two families are disjoint, and neither is close to 28. The real figure is **~12 occurrences across 10 files**, not 28.

**Consequence for the shard's headline yield.** The "~970 lines leave" estimate was built on the inflated count for its largest single category. That estimate is therefore UNRELIABLE and must not be treated as a target. The implementer MEASURES the actual recoverable total and records it on this ticket; the number is an output of the work, not an input to it. Do not manufacture relocations to reach ~970.

### 2. Write-ordering must cover the ADRs, not just `do_not_move`

The plan requires the `do_not_move` list to be appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands, but says nothing about ordering for the four proposed new ADRs (field-convergence fit-then-normalize; pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers; unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps) or the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035.

Those ADRs are the single-source DESTINATIONS for the arguments currently restated 4-8 times. If a comment citing "see ADR NNNN" is collapsed before ADR NNNN exists, the citation dangles and the argument is simply LOST — which is the opposite of relocation and is not recoverable from the diff by a later reader.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] The shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it
      is collapsed or deleted — destination first, then the relocation
- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination; nothing is deleted
      without a destination that already exists
- [ ] The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the
      unreliable ~970 estimate. The measured marker counts (6 RELOCATED VERBATIM, 6 cap mentions,
      10 files) are the corrected baseline
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are CORRECTED where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete — specifically `_backend_registry.py`'s "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be
      implemented" (false: `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules) and the S3/S4-not-landed
      notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay VERBATIM (this subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured facts that cannot be
      re-derived from code — the do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard)
- [ ] No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged
baseline.summary: Comment triage: reconciler subtree
