## Context / Problem

The multi-project model changes things a reader currently learns from the docs as single-project facts: `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:74` presents `project` as one config line and has no section on multiple projects, `docs/config.md:216-260` documents the `[jira]` block as a single scalar project, and `docs/migrations.md` describes the ensure registry without the two units this epic adds. A user upgrading a client store also needs to know what the new `required_capabilities` entry means for older binaries in their fleet. None of that is documented by the implementation stories, which own code and tests only.

## Approach

Document the shipped behaviour and record the architectural decision. The ADR is warranted rather than decorative because two decisions here are load-bearing, non-obvious, and expensive to reverse: that the project set is a property of the **store** rather than of a repo, and that the legacy migration writes **no ticket events**. Both were chosen against plausible alternatives — per-repo project lists and an EDIT-per-ticket backfill — and a future reader who does not know why will be tempted back toward them.

The ADR is `docs/adr/0062-*` — the next number after `0061-measurement-provenance-in-attested-evidence.md`. It records the shared-`prev_snapshot` reasoning for store ownership, the short-lock-budget reasoning for the event-free migration, and the conditional-stamp reasoning for compatibility. It also notes the relationship to ADR 0060, whose churn constraint the mapping satisfies by construction.

Documentation updates cover the mapping and its `bridge projects` verb, the tri-state project field, the repos field, the two ensure units, and the upgrade note for fleets running mixed binary versions.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0062-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` (new)
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
- `docs/config.md`
- `docs/migrations.md`
- `docs/user-guide.md`
- `docs/ticket-model.md`

## Testing

No `## Testing` section beyond this note: this story adds no testable behaviour — it is documentation and an ADR, which `rebar explain plan` names as a legitimately test-free change class. Verification is by the repository's existing documentation gates rather than by new tests, and the acceptance criteria below name the command that checks each claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0062-many-to-many-tracker-projects.md` exists and records the store-ownership,
      event-free-migration, and conditional-stamp decisions with their rejected alternatives; checked
      by reading the file and confirming each of the three decisions names what it was chosen over.
- [ ] The Jira sync and config docs describe the project mapping and no longer present a single
      scalar project as the only option; checked by confirming no remaining passage states the
      single-project constraint as current behaviour.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` lists both new ensure units alongside the existing built-ins; checked by
      confirming each registered id appears in the doc.
- [ ] The docs state what the `multi-project-bridge` capability means for an older binary and what an
      operator does about it; checked by confirming the upgrade note names both the fail-closed
      behaviour and the remedy.
- [ ] The generated CLI reference includes `bridge projects`; checked by running the repository's
      documentation generation and confirming the verb appears without a manual edit.
baseline.summary: Document the multi-project model and record ADR 0062

baseline.description:
## Context

`tests/interfaces/store/test_git_contention_9305.py::test_concurrent_processes_through_seam_both_succeed` intermittently fails the Gerrit Verified matrix, on changes that touch neither `rebar._store.gitutil` nor the test:

- run 31290743251, ubuntu py3.12 — `AssertionError: writer beta failed`
- run 31349549323, ubuntu py3.13 — `AssertionError: writer alpha failed`

## ROOT CAUSE — PROVEN (test design; reproduced deterministically)

**The failing inner command is `git commit`, not `git add`.** The worker is a `python -c` program whose line 9 — the line both CI tracebacks name — is the COMMIT assertion:

    6  r = gitutil.run_git_write(repo, 'add', '--', f'{name}.txt')
    7  assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
    8  r = gitutil.run_git_write(repo, 'commit', '-q', '--no-verify', '-m', name)
    9  assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr

Both CI failures carry a **message-less** `AssertionError`, i.e. `r.stderr` was empty.

`_with_index_lock_retry` takes the per-store advisory lock around **each** `run_git_write` call, but the worker's add and commit are two separate calls — the PAIR is not serialized. So this interleaving is legal and occurs under load:

    alpha: add alpha.txt   -> index holds alpha.txt
    beta:  add beta.txt    -> index holds alpha.txt AND beta.txt
    alpha: commit          -> a bare `git commit` commits the WHOLE index (both files)
    beta:  commit          -> nothing staged -> "nothing to commit" -> rc=1

`git commit -q` writes "nothing to commit, working tree clean" to **stdout** and leaves **stderr empty** — exactly the empty-stderr rc=1 signature seen in CI.

Deterministic reproduction, forcing that interleaving through the real seam:

    alpha add rc=0 / beta add rc=0 / alpha commit rc=0 / beta commit rc=1
    beta commit stderr=''
    beta commit stdout='On branch main\nnothing to commit, working tree clean\n'
    git log: alpha, seed        alpha in log: True   beta in log: False
    HEAD contents: alpha.txt | 1 +   beta.txt | 1 +

alpha's commit **swept up beta.txt**: both writers' data lands and reachability is preserved — only beta's *commit* is a no-op. The test asserts `cp.returncode == 0` for both writers, which asserts something the product never promised: that two bare whole-index commits against one repository are both non-empty. The test also flakes locally at roughly 1 in 25-65 runs.

RULED OUT:
- **Retry classification / exhaustion** — rc=1 with empty stderr never reaches
  `_augment_lock_exhaustion`; no lock signature was involved at all.
- **Runner resource exhaustion** — all failing job logs across the cited runs grep clean for
  `No space` / `ENOSPC` / `Cannot allocate` / runner warnings (zero hits).
- **A product contention defect** — every git invocation through the seam behaved correctly,
  and git correctly reports an empty commit.

## Plan

Two test-only changes, in the order the acceptance criteria require:

1. **Observability first.** Each worker assertion reports only `r.stderr`, discarding both the
   git stdout that carries the diagnosis and the identity of the failing inner command. Make
   each assertion name its command and include stdout as well as stderr, so any future failure
   is self-diagnosing instead of a bare `AssertionError`.
2. **Remove the shared-index race.** Give each writer a commit that is non-empty regardless of
   interleaving, by committing its own pathspec rather than the whole index. This preserves the
   real oracle — two concurrent writers through `run_git_write` against one repository both
   succeed and both commits land — without weakening it.

No file under `src/rebar/` changes: the production contention policy is correct as proven above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A failing worker reports which inner git command failed.
- [x] A failing worker reports git's stdout as well as its stderr, so an empty-stderr failure
      such as "nothing to commit" is diagnosable from the CI log alone.
- [x] Each writer commits its own path, so a writer that loses the add/commit interleaving
      still has its own change to commit and does not observe "nothing to commit".
- [x] The test still requires that BOTH concurrent writers exit 0 through `run_git_write`.
- [x] The test still requires that BOTH commits are present in `git log`.
- [x] [operator-attested] The test passes repeatedly under load locally (>= 60 consecutive runs, and under `-n 4`
      xdist).
- [x] No file under `src/rebar/` is modified by this change.
baseline.summary: Flaky CI: git contention seam loses one concurrent writer

## Summary

Observed while fixing `royalistic-gorgeable-norwayrat` (the MCP image shipping without `acli`). When the `acli` transport binary is absent, the reconciler's bare `subprocess.Popen(["acli", ...])` (`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`) raises `FileNotFoundError`, and `bridge_check_access`'s `STEP_CREATE` catch-all (`access_check.py:237-241`) reports it verbatim as `reason=exception, detail="[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"`.

That is a raw, untyped leak of an infrastructure fault into the probe verdict. `access_check` already has a typed `TransportUnavailableError` path elsewhere (e.g. `access_check.py:467,486`); a missing-transport binary should map to that typed "transport unavailable" verdict rather than a bare `FileNotFoundError` string.

This is AC #4's *alternative* branch on the parent bug (only strictly required if `acli` were deliberately NOT installed). The parent bug installs `acli`, so this is a **latent robustness / graceful-degradation** improvement, not a live failure — filed so it is not lost.

## Resolution

Fixed in Gerrit change 2391 (MERGED). Added a dedicated `except FileNotFoundError` branch in `run_access_check`, ordered before the broad `except Exception`, that maps a missing/unresolvable transport binary to a typed `reason="transport_unavailable"` (mirroring the module's existing `TransportUnavailableError` / `ProjectVisibilityResult.status == "transport_unavailable"` vocabulary), with a detail naming the binary instead of the raw errno string. Verdict/exit code unchanged (FAIL / 1); PASS path and generic-provider-error path (`reason=exception`) unchanged. RED→GREEN held-out test: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_access_check_transport_unavailable.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] When the bridge transport binary (`acli`) is absent/unresolvable, `bridge_check_access`
      reports a typed `transport_unavailable`-style verdict, not a raw `FileNotFoundError` detail.
- [x] A unit test drives the missing-transport path (e.g. PATH without `acli`) and asserts the
      typed verdict.
- [x] No behavior change when `acli` is present.
baseline.summary: bridge_check_access STEP_CREATE surfaces raw FileNotFoundError instead of a typed transport-unavailable verdict

baseline.description:
## Summary

The blue-green deploy swaps the nginx `/mcp` upstream to the new container the moment it is healthy. MCP streamable-HTTP sessions are STATEFUL and STICKY to the container that created them, so every client holding an `Mcp-Session-Id` is instantly orphaned: its next request is routed to a container that has never heard of that session and answers **404 Session expired**. The client surfaces it as an opaque transport error, not as a reconnect signal.

Because autodeploy ticks every 2 minutes, ANY merge touching `MCP_PATHS` kills every live agent session on the box.

## Observed (GitHub Copilot CLI, same host)

Every tool call failed after the session had been working:

    ✗ fsck            MCP server 'rebar': Error: MCP request failed: Transport send error:
                      Transport [rmcp::transport::worker::WorkerT...
    ✗ grounding_info  ... same
    ✗ validate / show_ticket / audit_trail / summary / list_tickets  ... same

The client's own reasoning: 'All the subsequent calls now fail with "Session expired (HTTP 404)" — a different error than the transport issue seen before.'

**The session was demonstrably WORKING first.** The earlier `unreal-milky-sloth` BigInt failure is the proof: a serialization error means the server RETURNED a payload the client then failed to serialize. Transport was healthy. This is a functional -> dead transition, not a never-worked.

## Root cause — confirmed from the box, with timing

Landing Gerrit 2271 (an `MCP_PATHS` change) triggered an mcp redeploy:

    18:51:04Z  change 2271 submitted / merged
    18:54:09Z  autodeploy begins rebuilding the mcp image
    18:54:24Z  image built
    18:54:29Z  "mcp cutover complete: /mcp upstream now 127.0.0.1:8093
                (deploy DONE; not waiting on in-flight drain)"
    18:54:29Z  "mcp retire: 'docker stop --time 1260' rebar-mcp-9966198879a2-8092 in background
                (graceful SIGTERM self-drain; never rm -f a serving container)"
    18:54:31Z  "mcp redeployed + healthy at 127.0.0.1:8093"

The upstream moved 8092 -> 8093 at 18:54:29. Sessions created on 8092 could only ever be served by 8092.

**The graceful-drain design does not help, and its logs imply protection it cannot provide.** Retiring the old container with `docker stop --time 1260` (21 minutes) keeps it ALIVE, but the nginx upstream has ALREADY been switched, so no further client request is routed to it. The long grace period drains nothing for session continuity: what needed preserving was the ROUTE to the session's own container, not the container's lifetime. `not waiting on in-flight drain` is accurate and the retire message reads reassuringly, but together they describe a drain that cannot apply to sticky sessions.

## Secondary observation (may warrant its own ticket)

The retired container did NOT stop. `rebar-mcp-9966198879a2-8092` is still `Up 2 hours (unhealthy)` and the retire line repeats at 18:55:20 and 18:57:33 — autodeploy re-issues the retire on later ticks. Two containers are bound to 8092/8093 while one is wedged unhealthy.

## Impact

Any agent session using the MCP server dies without warning on any mcp deploy, mid-task, with an error that names a Rust transport internal (`rmcp::transport::worker::WorkerT...`) rather than telling the operator to reconnect. This directly undermines the AGENTS.md mandate to route tracker operations through MCP: the mandated path is unreliable by construction on a box that redeploys every 2 minutes.

## Operator decision (2026-08-27): STATELESS is the approved fix

Of the three ecosystem patterns (stateless mode / session affinity at the edge / externalized event store), the operator approved **stateless mode**. It makes this failure structurally impossible rather than less likely: with no per-container session state there is nothing for a blue-green cutover to orphan.

Implementation shape: pass `stateless_http=True` where rebar constructs its FastMCP app (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:624,645-655`; `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:310` builds a second app and must match, or health and serving diverge). Verified available in the installed SDK — `FastMCP.__init__` accepts `stateless_http`, and `Settings` exposes `stateless_http` / `json_response`.

MUST BE VERIFIED BEFORE LANDING, not assumed: whether any tool depends on session-scoped server-initiated messages. The long-running gates (`review_plan` 15-20 min, `verify_completion` 9-11 min) and `run_workflow`'s async run model are the candidates. If one of them streams progress over the session, stateless changes its behaviour and that must be surfaced rather than shipped quietly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A client session survives an mcp blue-green cutover, OR the client receives an explicit,
      actionable session-expired signal it can act on (reconnect) rather than an opaque
      transport error.
- [x] The retire path's logs accurately describe what SIGTERM drains (in-flight operations),
      and no log implies session protection.
      *(REWRITTEN 2026-08-28, not reinterpreted — a recorded scope change. The original wording
      was: "The retire path either preserves routing to the old container for the life of its
      existing sessions, or the logs stop describing a graceful drain that cannot protect sticky
      sessions." It asked for route preservation OR a log change. The operator decision of
      2026-08-27 — "STATELESS is the approved fix", landed as commit `4af91ec2e799` — dissolved
      that premise: the server mints no `Mcp-Session-Id`, so there are no sticky sessions to
      preserve or to mis-describe. The criterion was rewritten to the post-stateless question
      rather than stretched to fit the old text. Verified against `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`:
      the retire log says "graceful SIGTERM self-drain; never rm -f a serving container" and the
      cutover log says "deploy DONE; not waiting on in-flight drain" — both describe in-flight
      operations, and the word "session" does not appear anywhere in the script.)*
- [x] A retired container actually terminates; `docker ps` does not accumulate wedged unhealthy
      containers, and the retire is not re-issued every tick.
- [x] Regression coverage asserts the chosen behaviour (session survival or a clean expiry
      signal) across a simulated cutover.

## How it was found

Reported by an operator from a live Copilot CLI session; root-caused against the box's autodeploy journal. Discovered while working `unreal-milky-sloth`, whose BigInt error is what establishes the session was healthy beforehand.

- [x] **LIVE VALIDATION — REQUIRED TO CLOSE.** a client session issues MCP calls successfully ACROSS an mcp redeploy (trigger one, or use the next autodeploy tick), with no `Session expired` / `rmcp::transport::worker` failure.
      Evidence must be OBSERVED against the deployed server at
      `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` and recorded in a ticket comment naming
      the tool(s) called, the arguments, and the actual response. A passing local test is
      NOT sufficient, and neither is a merged change: the container must have redeployed
      and served the call. This exists because a fix here was previously reported complete
      on the strength of a merge while the deployed behaviour was still broken.
baseline.summary: MCP blue-green cutover destroys every live client session: upstream swaps mid-session, clients get opaque transport errors

# J1 — Freeze the Cloud adapter's behavior with characterization oracles before anything moves

## Context / Problem

The DC work requires moving shared units out of `adapters/jira/`, and the Cloud adapter is the battle-tested path validated against a live Jira tenant. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` exists as the held-out Jira oracle, but it was not written to pin the specific outputs of the units about to move, and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` asserts only the vendor-neutral port contract ("nothing satisfied by hard-coding Jira outputs", per its own docstring). So today a silent mapping change during extraction could pass CI.

## Approach

Extend the characterization suite until it pins, by exact expected value, the current output of every unit that the next story moves:

- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — `_map_local_to_jira_fields` for a representative ticket, plus
  `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` for every key AND the default-fallback value.
- `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` — `_sanitize_label` / `_sanitize_summary` / `_sanitize_comment` at, below, and
  above their limits, plus the invalid-label raise.
- `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` — `truncate_comment_body` at and above the limit.
- `adapters/jira/identity.py` — `JiraIdentityConvention` format/parse/predicate, including the legacy
  `rebar-id-` hyphen form.
- `adapters/jira/probe.py` — `classify_probe_response` for each status code it branches on.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` — `map_fields_to_remote` for each of its branches.
- `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link` + `jira_fields._RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` for every relation.

These are golden-value assertions deliberately, not behavioral abstractions: their whole job is to fail if a byte of output changes during a move that is supposed to change nothing.

**Alternative rejected:** relying on the existing contract suite. It is explicitly written to be backend-agnostic, so it cannot detect a Jira-specific mapping regression — that is what makes it a good contract suite and a useless extraction oracle.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` — extended.
- No `src/` change whatsoever in this story.

## Testing

Unit tier against the real functions (no doubles): these are pure mappers and sanitizers, so the smallest tier that crosses the mechanism is a direct call, and the oracle is the exact returned value.

- happy path: each unit's output equals a literal expected value recorded in the test.
- edge: every value map is asserted for all keys AND for an unmapped key hitting the documented default
  (`"To Do"` / `"Medium"`), since the default is the branch an extraction is most likely to drop.
- failure path: `_sanitize_label` still raises on an unfixable label, and `classify_probe_response` still
  classifies its error statuses.
- mutation check: for at least three pinned units, temporarily alter the source value (e.g. change a status-map
  entry) and record that the characterization test goes RED — proving the oracle actually gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every symbol listed in the Approach section has at least one exact-value assertion in
      `test_backend_characterization.py`
- [ ] `make test` passes with no `src/` modification in this change
- [ ] [operator-attested] for three pinned units, altering the source value makes the corresponding
      characterization test FAIL — the pytest failure output for each of the three is pasted into a
      ticket comment, naming the unit and the value altered
- [ ] a coverage check shows every branch of `map_fields_to_remote` and `classify_probe_response` is exercised
baseline.summary: J1 — freeze the Cloud adapter's behavior with characterization oracles before anything moves

## Why
Independent verification is the precision gate (Chain-of-Verification / SAFE); it filters Pass-1 false positives without rubber-stamping.

## What
- ONE aggregate call over all findings on a NON-FRONTIER model; per finding -> severity ATTRIBUTES
  {prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility} + typed BINARY sub-answers
  {yes|no|insufficient}.
- Skepticism aimed at the FINDING via charitable plan-reading (the finding stands only if it holds under the
  plan's most reasonable reading = evidence-entailment); atomic, independent, verdict-with-citation, allow insufficient.

## Scope
- Text verification over plan + findings; code-citation findings are rare in plan review (grounding owned by
  E4/G1G2/A1 per the agent-vs-single-turn bright line).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single aggregate verify call per review on a non-frontier model.
- [ ] Binary sub-question set + severity attributes per finding; independence rules in the prompt.
- [ ] Charitable-plan-reading / entailment precision gate implemented.
- [ ] PROVING CHECK that Pass-2 DISCRIMINATES (not rubber-stamps): a labeled set of {true finding, planted FALSE finding} where Pass-2 must return no/insufficient or LOWER confidence on the false ones while leaving true findings standing (independence holds; charitable-reading filters Pass-1 FPs without suppressing real findings) — wired into the `7284` eval suite as Pass-2's OWN cases, distinct from the per-criterion prompt cases.
baseline.summary: Pass-2 verifier (single aggregate, non-frontier)

# Jira reconciler correctness & the ticket-store corruption it caused

Broadened from the original store-only charter (f193 follow-ups). Root-cause work (bug saggy-pupil-plant / f193 and the 2026-07-07 reconciler deep-dive, session log spirited-balsamic-sealion) established the throughline: **the Jira reconciler is the epicenter**. Its 20-min CI pass is the busiest concurrent writer of the `tickets` branch, and its shallow-fetch + rebase workflow (RC1) *caused* the ~2,400-issue store corruption. Four bands: (A) store hardening + remediation, (B) convergence completion, (C) latent-gap closure, (D) comprehensive live validation.

## Context (current state)
- **RC1 (fixed, #1):** reconciler CI used shallow `--depth=1` fetch + `git rebase`, resurrecting
  compaction-deleted source files -> `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` (commit 5a7548a). Historical damage remains.
- **RC2b (band A):** a concurrent write on a stale base gets an HLC below a peer's snapshot horizon; a
  clean union-merge keeps it, but replay's positional skip drops it -> silent data loss.
- **Invariant gap (band A):** docs I1 says compaction RENAMEs folded files to `*.retired`; the code hard-`os.remove()`s them.
- **Convergence redesign (landed, epic file-lens-jewel; band B):** three-way-merge baseline + binding
  lifecycle (ADRs 0026-0029, 0031) shipped, but the per-binding baseline runs dual-write SHADOW — the
  Phase-3 consumer swap is not yet live, and two arbiters encode the rule twice.
- **Latent reconciler gaps (band C):** silent same-field clobber with no conflict signal; hard-delete
  -> re-create unreachable + false comment; silent field-allowlist drop; coarse bulk-path 429 handling.
- **Validation gap (band D):** correctness is argued from code + an OSS/commercial comparison but not
  PROVEN end-to-end against live Jira. Live validation is performed by an AGENT (ACLI access), with
  guaranteed cleanup of test artifacts in both Jira and the local store — not deferred to the operator.
- Design as a whole matches/beats OSS + commercial-tier peers. Single-hop status transitions are ACCEPTED / out of scope.

## Scope boundary
This epic is reconciler **correctness + validation**. Reconciler **maintainability/refactor** work — oversized-function extraction (fusible-mean-porcupine), central git adapter (sewable-authorial-eagle), vendor-adapter seam (ambery-tweed-grosbeak), invariant detect/remediate split (inherited-genealogic-haddock), config split (seedy-edema-groan) — lives under the Janitor Cleanup epic, NOT here. Separate reconciler epics also stay separate: GitHub parity (slimy-tuber-stoop), authenticated identity (gnu-whale-ichor), INDETERMINATE/LLM-gate handling (jira-reb-687).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Band A children landed: A1 (`*.retired`), A2 (RC2b horizon-safe; carries an approach decision), A3 (live-store remediation to zero fsck).
- [ ] Band B: B1 (Phase-3 baseline consumer swap; agent performs its live validation with cleanup).
- [ ] Band C children landed: C1 (clobber conflict signal), C2 (hard-delete re-create), C3 (field-allowlist alert), C4 (bulk-path 429 parity).
- [ ] Band D: D1 (comprehensive live validation + guaranteed bilateral cleanup).
- [ ] Dependency edges wired: A1->A2, A1->A3, A2->A3; C1 relates_to B1; D1 relates_to B1/C1/C2/C3/C4.
- [ ] Risk #5 (single-hop status transitions) explicitly accepted / out of scope.
- [ ] **A. Store hardened + remediated:** compaction non-destructive (I1 `*.retired`); no concurrent
- [ ] **B. Convergence fully live:** the per-binding baseline is the authoritative direction arbiter
- [ ] **C. Latent gaps closed:** true both-sides field conflicts recorded; hard-delete -> re-create works;
- [ ] **D. Proven live:** the full bidirectional surface is validated against live Jira by an agent, with


## Cross-child coordination (verified in plan review)
- SEQUENCING: A3's live remediation pauses the reconciler, which resets B1's >=10-consecutive-clean-shadow-pass
  streak. Do NOT run A3's live pass during B1's streak window — sequence them.
- SHARED FILE: C1 (feline-wandering-dassierat, `apply_outbound.py` conflict leaf ~207-232) and C3
  (nonglacial-tense-vulture, `apply_outbound.py` ~117-124) edit the same file in different regions — coordinate merge order (relates_to linked).
- VALIDATION ORDER: D1 (close-ferreous-cardinal) validates the POST-FIX behavior and runs AFTER the C-band lands;
  captured in D1's body rather than as hard depends_on edges to avoid blocking-link promotion across mixed-type siblings.
baseline.summary: Jira reconciler correctness & the ticket-store corruption it caused — convergence completion, latent-gap closure, and store hardening + remediation (f193 follow-ups)

## Problem
`rebar config validate` reports success for invalid typed configuration values because it scans only removed/tombstoned inputs from raw TOML and deliberately bypasses the coercing `load_config()` path. The command name and success message imply that the project configuration was validated, so operators can receive a false green result for malformed enum values.

## Reproduction
1. In `rebar.toml`, set `reconciler.rich_text_cutover = "clould"` (an invalid enum value).
2. Run `rebar config validate`.
3. Observe exit 0 / `OK — no removed inputs are set.`
4. Run `rebar config` and observe that the typed loader correctly rejects the invalid value.

## Expected
`rebar config validate` should validate the full supported configuration surface, including typed coercion and enum constraints, while still reporting all tombstoned inputs in one run. It should exit non-zero and identify invalid values such as `reconciler.rich_text_cutover = "clould"`.

## Actual
The command only calls the tombstone scan over raw TOML, so invalid enum values and potentially other malformed live keys pass.

## Evidence
- `src/rebar/_commands/show_config.py::_validate` only calls `scan_tombstones`.
- `_raw_toml_tables` explicitly bypasses the coercing/raising `load_config` path.
- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` enforces `rich_text_cutover` via `_as_choice(..., {"off", "cloud", "dc", "both"})`, but that path is not reached by `config validate`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar config validate` returns non-zero for invalid values on live typed keys and reports each invalid key with an actionable diagnostic.
- [x] Tombstone aggregation behavior remains intact; a single run reports removed inputs and typed-value errors rather than aborting after the first issue.
- [x] Tests cover an invalid `reconciler.rich_text_cutover` value and at least one non-enum typed-value failure.
- [x] Documentation accurately defines the command as full config validation.
baseline.summary: rebar config validate does not reject invalid typed config values

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Bugs are exempt from the claim-time plan-review gate (correct: no RCA exists at claim), and since epic 6982/R4 an explicit 'review-plan <bug>' is no longer a hollow exempt-PASS — it runs the LIGHT ADVISORY bug tier: the DET floor + the necessity probe only (workflow_ops.py bug branch; registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restricts the LLM criteria), with every DET finding downgraded to advisory (det_blocking=[]) so a bug always PASSes. That tier is right-sized for small fixes but means a complex fix plan is never substantively reviewed against the full rubric before landing — fixes shipping design changes (backtest: 13/113 bug-fix commits exceeded 150 non-test lines; all 13 adjudicated substantive, two shipped ADRs) flow to main with at most advisory findings.

## Approach
B1 (extend the bug review tier, not narrow an exemption): in the workflow_ops.py bug branch + orchestrator.route_criteria (~:190) — the SINGLE routing seam that keys the bug tier (registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction at ~:221) and is reached by BOTH the assemble step and the batch-runner's project-criteria fan-in, so escalation lands once and covers both callers —, key the tier on the ticket's PERSISTED declared blast radius, derived DETERMINISTICALLY at review time (no diff exists yet): escalate iff the ticket's recorded file_impact enumerates any non-test path (tests/**, conftest.py excluded). file_impact lives in ticket state, which BOTH enforcement steps already read — plan_review_precheck (workflow_ops.py ~:115, which forces det_blocking=[]) and plan_review_assemble_criteria -> route_criteria consume the assembled PlanContext/ticket state — so ONE shared derivation helper (module-level beside route_criteria, unit-testable) serves both steps AND the batch-runner fan-in (production_batch_runner._project_criteria -> route_criteria), which has no CLI surface. DESIGN DECISION, recorded: no --size-lines CLI flag — a transient flag cannot reach route_criteria (it takes only PlanContext, assembled from store reads), cannot reach the batch-runner caller at all, and would require amending two step-input schemas that declare additionalProperties:false (plan_review_precheck_input.schema.json / plan_review_assemble_criteria_input.schema.json); an author who wants escalation declares their blast radius in file_impact, which is also what makes the signal visible to OTHER agents. No non-test file_impact -> light advisory tier (deterministic default; B2 at Gerrit backstops with the REAL diff count, so an undeclared-blast-radius big fix is still caught before merge). When escalated, an explicit 'review-plan <bug>' includes the FULL LLM criteria set (not just BUG_TIER_CRITERIA) and stops forcing det_blocking=[] — findings can BLOCK. Small fixes keep the light advisory tier unchanged. The CLI claim-time bug exemption (rebar._commands.gates._PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES, consumed by plan_review_precheck) is untouched — bugs stay claimable with no attestation. B2: DET code-review criterion at Gerrit: commit trailer ticket is type=bug AND non-test diff >150 lines AND plan_review_status verdict is in the FLAG bucket -> BLOCKING finding teaching remediation (write fix plan into description -> review-plan -> re-push). Non-test line classification rule, load-bearing for both the gate and the backtest: a diff line is "test" iff its file path matches tests/** or conftest.py; everything else (src, scripts, workflows, docs) counts as non-test. Attestation read — CROSS-HOST, not own-env: the own-env verify wrapper (_opcert_signing.verify_opcert_record) returns foreign_key BY DESIGN for any record whose principal is not the verifying host's own env_id, so on a review-bot host distinct from the environment that ran review-plan (the NORMAL case) every legitimate attestation reads foreign_key — own-env reads (plan_review_status/claim_gate_check) are unusable for B2. Plan-review attestations are environment-signed rebar.opcert.v1 DSSE/SSHSIG op-certs (the symmetric HMAC scheme is retired — signing.py header), so B2 verifies CROSS-HOST with the op-cert trust machinery that trusted_env.verify_required_environment already composes for the completion-verifier merge gate (rebar verify-opcert, src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py): read the ticket's plan-review SIGNATURE record from the store (read-only, no LLM), decode envelope + signed-bound fields via attest.opcert.opcert_from_record, load the RECORD principal's pinned keyring via attest.trusted_env.trusted_env_keyring (.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml), and verify with attest.opcert.verify_opcert — which REQUIRES storage_anchor_commit/storage_anchor_position (not signed fields; the CLI's _opcert_anchor_event resolver is hardcoded to the completion-verifier kind, so B2 derives its own plan-review analog): anchor S = the ticket's terminal SIGNATURE event whose derived attestation kind (rebar.reducer._processors.attestation_kind) is the plan-review kind, its introducing tickets-branch commit resolved via authorship.build_introducing_commit_map + resolve_position_commit (the same machinery _commands/verify_opcert.py:227-234 uses); anchor-derivation failure (no live SIGNATURE event, compacted history, unresolvable commit) -> INFRA-FAIL-OPEN, same bucket as 'unavailable' — so an op-cert from ANY pinned trusted environment can reach certified; an unpinned principal fails as mismatch (trusted_env's not-pinned arm). Freshness/lifecycle then layers on via rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity (attest.py ~:513 — it lives under llm/plan_review, not rebar.attest) over the verify-shaped result built from the SIGNED bound fields (material_fingerprint / merged_log_commit / signed manifest), profile=DEFAULT, kind=plan-review. A record with no decodable envelope (pre-retirement legacy HMAC) is cross-host-unverifiable and classifies as unsigned. Verdict buckets, each literal attributed to its true source: (a) compute_validity's plan-review-reachable literals ('not-closed' is completion-verifier-only and excluded, stated in-test): {certified, unsigned, wrong-kind, malformed-pin, malformed-phase, stale-code, stale-head, stale-material, stale-reopened, stale-pin-drift, stale-pin-missing, unverifiable-material, incompatible-phase}; (b) the cross-host op-cert verification vocabulary (registry.Verdict / verify_signature_result.schema.json enum as emitted through verify_opcert and the scheme passthrough): {mismatch, key_not_valid_at_era, unknown_kind, unknown_scheme, invalid, unavailable}; (c) B2's own error handling {error} for read/exception paths. ACCEPTED = {certified, stale-code, stale-head} (code drift from implementing the reviewed plan is expected). FLAG = the rest of (a) + (b) minus {unavailable} — deterministic properties of the attestation itself (stale, malformed, replayed, era-invalid, or not trustworthy under the project trust root); tamper/authenticity signals are gate signal, NOT infra, and never fail open. INFRA-FAIL-OPEN = {unavailable} (verifier tooling missing on the bot host, e.g. ssh-keygen) + (c) + any verdict string in NO list (future enum growth): emit a non-blocking advisory naming the infra failure or unknown verdict, never BLOCK on infrastructure. A coverage unit test pins ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG ∪ INFRA-NAMED = (a) ∪ (b) ∪ {error} exactly — enum growth surfaces as a failing test, not silent fail-open. The 150 threshold is B2's (and the backtest's) — B1 keys on blast radius, not line count. It lives in ONE shared module-level constant in rebar imported by both its consumers — B2's review-bot criterion (the bot imports rebar) and scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py — not config-plumbed (config only if an operator-variable appears). plan_review_status (attest_gate.py) is read-only/no-LLM, callable from the review-bot checkout. Works for non-skill clients (keys only on ticket type + diff size + attestation state).

## Scope
- read-only consumers of rebar.attest.opcert / attest.trusted_env / rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity in the review-bot criterion (no changes to those modules)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py precheck bug branch + the shared blast-radius derivation helper beside orchestrator.route_criteria (both steps + batch-runner key on it; NO CLI flag, NO step-input schema changes — the signal is persisted ticket state)
- orchestrator.route_criteria (~:190/:221): lift the BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction when the helper escalates; criteria routing for the escalated path
- review-bot DET criterion (vote pipeline)
- rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook: fix-plan-to-description + review-plan for non-trivial fixes (coordinate with the debug-skill child 78f1 — writeback anchor points land there; this ticket only adds the review-plan invocation sentence)

## Testing
B1: review-plan on a bug whose file_impact names a non-test path runs the full rubric with blocking enabled (not the light tier) — asserted at BOTH seams: a fixture whose plan omits a required section (deliberately tripping a DET rule) AND declares non-test file_impact -> precheck det_blocking NON-EMPTY (escalation lifts the forced det_blocking=[] downgrade; the finding itself comes from the tripped DET rule, which is why the fixture must trip one) AND route_criteria returns the full set; no file_impact -> light tier; test-only file_impact -> light tier; batch-runner fan-in path escalates identically (route_criteria-level test); claim path unchanged (bug claims stay ungated). B2 unit tests over the predicate: bug+160 non-test lines+unsigned -> BLOCK; same with certified or stale-code or stale-head -> no finding; error/read-exception -> advisory only (fail-open); unknown verdict string -> advisory only; task ticket -> no finding; bug+40 lines -> no finding; test-vs-non-test classification cases (tests/** excluded, scripts/ counted). B2 integration: one review-bot pipeline-level test exercising the criterion end-to-end against a fixture checkout (attestation present vs absent), not just the predicate function.

## Acceptance Criteria

'Mechanical FP' means exactly: a flagged commit outside the adjudicated-substantive 13.
