baseline.description:
# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: E1 — Force measurement provenance into attested evidence

baseline.description:
## Problem
The codebase is jammed against the module-size gate. Measured on origin/main 2026-08-19, these `src/rebar` files sit within 20 lines of the 800-LOC HARD cap, two of them AT it:

| LOC | file | covered elsewhere? |
|---|---|---|
| 800 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` | no |
| 800 | `signing.py` | YES — `stealthy-appetizing-coelacanth`, excluded from this epic |
| 799 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` | no |
| 799 | `config.py` | claimed by in-flight work, excluded |
| 799 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` | YES — RP-03 S5, excluded |
| 798 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` | handled inline by Gerrit 1916, excluded |
| 795 | `_config_sources.py` | claimed by in-flight work, excluded |
| 793 | `llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` | no |
| 793 | `llm/plan_review/__init__.py` | YES — `sullen-famished-incatern`, excluded |
| 790 | `llm/workflow/executor.py` | no |
| 790 | `llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` | YES — two open tickets, excluded |
| 789 | `llm/prompting/prompts.py` | no |
| 786 | `_commands/init.py` | no |
| 782 | `_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` | YES — RP-03 + others, excluded |

The CI module-size gate is a HARD FAIL with no allowlist, and the limit in `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is LOCKED — a normal contributor change to it fails CI. So any edit to a file at 799 or 800, INCLUDING ADDING A COMMENT, fails the build.

This is not hypothetical. Gerrit change 1916 was failed by exactly this: it added a six-line justification comment to `__main__.py` (798) and landed at 804. That is a queue of latent CI failures sitting in front of anyone who touches these files next.

## Scope
This epic covers ONLY the six files with no other owner: `inbound_differ.py`, `apply_inbound_records.py`, `det_floor.py`, `llm/workflow/executor.py`, `llm/prompting/prompts.py`, `_commands/init.py`. Coverage was verified against the file_impact of all 101 open/in_progress tickets and against the prose of every open RP epic. Files owned by RP epics or by other open tickets are deliberately EXCLUDED so this epic never competes for the same file.

## Non-negotiable constraints on every child
- **Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS and ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES.** Extract a cluster of functions that
  already call each other, following a seam the call graph already has. Do NOT carve mechanically to
  get under a number. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary chosen.
- **Never raise the limit.** `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked and is not the fix.
- **No file under 100 LOC** may be created by a split; target 200-500 LOC per resulting file.
- **Leave real headroom.** Landing at 798 recreates this exact problem for the next person — which
  is how 1916 failed. A split that buys 2 lines has not done the job.
- **Behaviour-preserving.** Existing tests for the affected area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must
  change, that is evidence the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- **Both navigation tools.** Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for the reference set, THEN a plain
  `grep` for every moved symbol's name AS A STRING (monkeypatch.setattr, getattr, importlib).
  Serena returns EMPTY — not an error — for receivers typed `Any`, so the grep is mandatory.

## Provenance
Filed 2026-08-19 under explicit operator authorization to split files at or near the LOC cap that are not covered by existing RP epics, with the instruction that splits follow logical concerns and architectural boundaries.
baseline.summary: Restore headroom under the 800-LOC module-size cap (6 uncovered files at 786-800)

baseline.description:
## Context

scripts/check_docs_index.py currently enforces top-level docs index membership and checks relative Markdown links only when their resolved target remains under docs. tests/unit/test_check_docs_index.py carries a second parser for links that leave docs. F07 replaces that split with one deterministic repository-relative link checker over an explicit maintained-documentation boundary.

## Historical basis

Ticket mucky-like-elkhound deliberately limited its front-door remediation to top-level docs membership and links under docs. It was not intended as a site-wide linter. A dead outbound link was later repaired under illadvised-ropeable-huemul and protected by a separate unit-test parser. F07 absorbs that regression coverage without expanding into prompts, fixtures, anchor validation, external URL checks, or prose analysis.

## Source boundary

Include root Markdown files and Markdown under .agents, .github, docs, examples/agent-skills, infra runbooks, infra README files, scripts README files, src/rebar/_guides, src/rebar/llm/eval_specs, templates, tests/external README files, and tests/unit/fixtures/README.md. Exclude .joe-janitor, .rebar/prompts, src/rebar/llm/reviewers, tests/fixtures, tests/scripts/fixtures, tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/integration_gates, hidden root Markdown files, and local Markdown files. An excluded source may remain a valid link target.

## Parser contract

Retain top-level docs index membership as a separate rule. Scan inline Markdown links and images outside fenced blocks and inline code spans. Resolve each relative target from its source directory. Permit targets anywhere inside the repository. Reject targets that escape the repository. Strip query strings and fragments before file resolution. Ignore fragment-only and scheme-qualified targets. Do not validate heading anchors, external URL availability, reference-style links, HTML links, or bare path mentions. Sort sources and findings. Report the repository-relative source path, line number, raw target, normalized target path, and failure reason.

Document this source and parser boundary in docs/documentation-policy.md. Replace the script module text about a stub and held-out development history with current behavior. Keep the existing CI action because both CI routes already invoke this checker.

## Exclusions

- No audience classification, canonical-source inference, prose validation, or protected-content rewrite.
- No link correction is currently required. The surveyed boundary contains no broken active Markdown target.
- No docs/README.md, docs/generated-artifacts.md, workflow, prompt, fixture, or historical evidence edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The checker retains every existing top-level docs index-membership behavior.
- [x] The checker includes every declared source pattern and excludes every declared source exclusion.
- [x] An excluded Markdown source may resolve as a valid target from an included source.
- [x] Relative links and images resolve from their source directories to any target inside the repository.
- [x] A missing target and a target that escapes the repository each produce a deterministic finding with source path, line number, raw target, normalized target path, and failure reason.
- [x] Scheme-qualified targets, fragment-only targets, fenced blocks, and inline code spans produce no findings.
- [x] Query strings and fragments are removed before file resolution.
- [x] The duplicate outbound-link parser in test_all_docs_relative_links_resolve is replaced with the checker API.
- [x] docs/documentation-policy.md states the maintained source boundary, parser behavior, and exclusions.
- [x] The assembled repository indexes the F01 pages and passes scripts/check_docs_index.py --check.
- [x] tests/unit/test_check_docs_index.py, tests/unit/test_gerrit_docs_only.py, the documentation parity test, make lint, make typecheck, and the project test gate pass.
baseline.summary: F07 Expand deterministic documentation link validation

baseline.description:
## Summary
`rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` (the read-only online drift diagnostic in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`) loads local tickets by reading `<entry>/ticket.json` from each `.tickets-tracker/<id>/` directory. The event-sourced store NEVER writes `ticket.json` — a ticket dir contains event-log files (`*-CREATE.json`, `*-COMMENT.json`, …) plus a compiled `.cache.json` whose `state` key holds the ticket. So `local_tickets` is always empty, and every binding is classified 'bound but missing locally or in Jira'.

## Reproduction Steps
1. On a populated event-sourced store with N confirmed bindings, run `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check`.
2. Observe `bridge_state/reconcile-check.json`.

Expected: bindings whose local ticket AND Jira issue both exist are counted checked/in_sync.
Actual: `checked: 0`, `in_sync: 0`, `orphaned_bindings` = all N (e.g. 627/627), regardless of true state. Confirmed live 2026-07-03 against production Jira REB (~628 issues, 627 bindings): acli fetch works (30 active issues returned), yet reconcile-check reported all 627 orphaned.

## Root Cause
`__main__.py` reconcile-check branch: `meta_path = entry / "ticket.json"` — a file the event-sourced store does not produce. `ticket.json` is referenced ONLY here; no other reconciler code reads it. The compiled ticket is `.cache.json['state']` (fields keyed `ticket_id`, `status`, `ticket_type`, `tags`, …), or can be obtained by replaying the event log.

## Impact
The read-only drift diagnostic is unusable — it always reports 100% orphaned drift (false positive). It does NOT affect the live-acting pass (run_pass/the differs load local state through a different, correct path), so no bad mutations result; but any operator relying on reconcile-check for a go/no-go read gets a totally misleading census.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] reconcile-check's local loader reads the compiled ticket from `.cache.json['state']` (or replays the event log) instead of the nonexistent `ticket.json`, keying on `ticket_id`/`status`.
- [ ] On a store where a binding's local ticket and Jira issue both exist, reconcile-check counts it checked/in_sync (not orphaned); a RED unit test in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` reproduces the all-orphaned bug and passes after the fix.
- [ ] No regression to the live-acting pass (that path is unaffected).
- [ ] Landed on main via Gerrit (LLM-Review + Verified).
baseline.summary: reconcile-check reads nonexistent per-ticket ticket.json -> falsely reports ALL bindings orphaned

baseline.description:
## Test remediation: defensive autouse guard against global enforcement

Assessment: flipping `require_authenticated` in this project's `rebar.toml` does NOT break the suite (every test store is an isolated tmp `REBAR_ROOT`; config discovery never reaches the real `rebar.toml`; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is stubbed). But a global env `REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1` DOES break it broadly (empirically: every create/mutate of a non-exempt type fails with the "cannot be signed" CommandError).

- Add an autouse fixture to the repo-root `tests/conftest.py` that forces the gate OFF for the suite (mirroring the existing `_gate_source_local_by_default` / `_compaction_horizon_zero_by_default` idiom, `tests/conftest.py:200-232`): `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED", "0")`.
- Confirm it does NOT disturb the dedicated identity tests (`tests/unit/test_identity_*`), which build their own subprocess env with the flag ON (their explicit value wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/conftest.py` has an autouse fixture forcing `REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=0` for the suite, documented as a guard against a stray global default.
- [ ] The full suite is green both with and without a stray global `REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1` in the environment.
- [ ] The dedicated identity enforcement tests still pass unchanged.
baseline.summary: Test remediation: autouse conftest guard against global enforcement env

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`reconcile_check.py` is the last core module that compares local state against the vendor snapshot in vendor shape: it lazy-loads `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` and `adapters/jira/adf.py` by path (`reconcile_check.py:61-75`) and calls `_assignee_matches(str(local_val), jira_val)` on the raw Jira assignee dict (`reconcile_check.py:236`), `_extract_jira_field(jira_issue, "description")` + `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` for ADF description normalization (`:241-242`), and `_extract_jira_field(jira_issue, field)` for the nested status/priority `{"name": ...}` unwrap (`:247`). The neutrality gate documents this as deliberately out of its scope (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:94-99`). The epic bbf1 container review flagged it as an unrecorded second vendor reach-through — epic AC4 admits only the `inbound_fields.py` exemption, so reconcile-check must be canonicalized.

## Approach

Apply the epic's canonical-comparison principle, reusing the machinery the prerequisite canonical-differ story establishes — no new port surface:

- Canonicalize the snapshot entry once per bound pair with the configured backend's
  `InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local` (resolved via `select_backend(load_config())`, the
  seam proven at `outbound_differ.py:450-454`), and compare in local vocabulary:
  - assignee: neutral membership matching against the canonical `assignee_identity`
    dict `{display, email, account_id}` [rebar:625b-9cd1-1ce9-4e5f], replacing the
    `_assignee_matches` call at `reconcile_check.py:236`;
  - description: compare the port-sanitized local text (`FieldSanitizer.sanitize_description`)
    against the mapper-decoded remote text with the same rstrip tolerance, replacing the
    `_extract_jira_field`/`fit_text_to_adf_limit` pair at `reconcile_check.py:241-242`
    (mirroring the differ's description parity rule [rebar:625b-9cd1-1ce9-4e5f]);
  - status/priority: compare the local value against the canonically mapped remote value,
    replacing `_extract_jira_field` + `_values_match_with_mapping` at
    `reconcile_check.py:247-248`.
- The reported `jira_value` in each discrepancy record stays the RAW snapshot value
  (`reconcile_check.py:255-258`) — an opaque vendor payload passed through untouched, which
  the principle allows; report shape and consumers are unchanged.
- Delete the `_load_outbound_fields`/`_load_adf` sibling loads (`reconcile_check.py:61-75`);
  remove the gate's documented reconcile_check carve-out and extend the AST/lazy-load case in
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` to cover `reconcile_check.py`.

Rejected alternative: leaving reconcile_check as a second recorded exemption — unlike `inbound_fields.py` (which IS the Jira mapper implementation, kept at root only for loader location-pinning), reconcile_check is genuinely neutral core logic (a checker that must work for any backend), so exempting it would leave a real second-backend correctness hole: its discrepancy scan would mis-flag every binding on a non-Jira backend, exactly the runny-lens-strafe failure mode it was fixed for (`reconcile_check.py:217-224`).

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_check.py (canonical comparison; drop vendor sibling loads)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (remove the carve-out; cover reconcile_check.py)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (reconcile-check comparison behavior tests)

## Testing

- Happy path: a fully-in-sync bound pair yields zero discrepancies on a live-shaped snapshot
  (nested status/priority objects, dict assignee, ADF description) — the runny-lens-strafe
  regression case, now via canonical mapping.
- Edge/failure: assignee matching across accountId / email / displayName local values and
  both-empty; an oversized ADF-fitted description does not read as drift; a genuinely
  divergent field is reported with the RAW vendor `jira_value` (report shape unchanged);
  unmapped remote status compares as divergent.
- Gate: the extended neutrality case fails if `reconcile_check.py` re-grows an
  `adapters.jira` import or by-path vendor sibling load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reconcile_check.py` contains NO `adapters.jira`/`acli_subprocess` import (any nesting
      depth) and NO by-path load of a vendor sibling (`adapters/jira/...` path literal) —
      verified by the extended case in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`, whose reconcile_check
      carve-out comment is removed.
- [ ] Discrepancy decisions are identical to today's for Jira across the Testing cases
      (including the runny-lens-strafe live-shape regression) and the report's `jira_value`
      stays the raw snapshot value — verified by the behavior tests in Testing.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Plan-review remediation (drift re-review, G1G2 findings)

Three corrections, reusing 625b's now-merged canonical machinery verbatim:

1. **AC1 gate mechanism (by-path load detection).** The existing full-tree AST walker
   (`_all_imported_modules` / `test_scalar_core_imports_no_jira_adapter`) only detects
   `import`/`from ... import` nodes — it CANNOT catch reconcile_check's by-path load
   `_load_sibling("outbound_fields", "adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py")` (a string-literal
   path). So AC1 is enforced by TWO cases in `test_backend_neutrality.py`: (a) add
   `reconcile_check.py` to the `_ZERO_ADAPTER_IMPORT_SCALAR_CORE` AST-import tuple (catches any
   `adapters.jira`/`acli_subprocess` import at any depth), AND (b) a NEW deterministic
   source-text case asserting `reconcile_check.py` contains NO `"adapters/jira/"` path-literal
   string (catches the `_load_sibling(..., "adapters/jira/...")` by-path loads). Both go green
   only after the `_load_outbound_fields`/`_load_adf` sibling loads are deleted.

2. **Description comparison reuses 625b's parity EXACTLY — NOT `sanitize_description`.**
   `FieldSanitizer.sanitize_description` is the SEND-path sanitizer: it fits AND emits a
   `logger.warning` on truncation, which is wrong for a read-only diagnostic. Instead, mirror
   the canonical differ (`outbound_field_diff.py:270-279`): fit the local description via the
   injected `OutboundMapper.map_fields_to_remote({"description": local_desc}, ticket=ticket)`
   `.get("description")` (ADF-fit through the port, NO warning), and compare with rstrip
   tolerance (the differ's `_text_matches`) against the mapper-decoded `canonical_remote
   ["description"]`. reconcile_check therefore resolves BOTH `backend.inbound` (canonicalize the
   snapshot) AND `backend.outbound` (description ADF-fit + `resolve_assignee` for the assignee
   identity) via `select_backend(load_config())`. An injection seam (optional `inbound_mapper`
   / `outbound_mapper` params defaulting to the lazy `select_backend` resolve, mirroring
   outbound_differ / outbound_comments) keeps the spec-loaded unit tests working.

3. **AC2 scope: the annotation-label case is an intended CORRECTNESS improvement (B3).** For a
   ticket carrying a `rebar-status:blocked` / `rebar-status:cancelled` annotation label,
   `InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local` applies the annotation-label -> local-status precedence
   (inbound_fields), so the canonical comparison yields the local status the inbound differ
   actually dispatches — where the pre-ad44 RAW comparison (reading only the raw Jira workflow
   status) mis-flagged it. AC2's "identical decisions" is therefore scoped to exclude this one
   annotation-label case, which is recorded as an INTENDED improvement (reconcile-check now
   mirrors the real differ), not a regression. All other Testing cases remain byte-identical.

**Added acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The AC1 neutrality gate uses BOTH the AST-import case (reconcile_check.py in the tuple)
      AND a source-text case asserting NO `"adapters/jira/"` path literal in reconcile_check.py
      — the reconcile_check carve-out comment in test_backend_neutrality.py is removed.
- [ ] The description comparison uses `OutboundMapper.map_fields_to_remote` (no warning) + rstrip
      `_text_matches` against the canonical remote description — NOT `sanitize_description` —
      verified by a behavior test; no `logger.warning` is emitted on a normal reconcile-check pass.
- [ ] A ticket with a `rebar-status:blocked`/`cancelled` annotation label reconciles to the
      correct local status (annotation-label precedence via the canonical mapper) — verified by
      a behavior test documenting this as the one intended difference from the raw comparison.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 945 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1). Live-validated against real Jira (reconcile dry-run pass; Reconcile Bridge GHA job healthy).
baseline.summary: Canonicalize reconcile_check's vendor-shape comparison (reuse the canonical differ machinery)

baseline.description:
# J2 — Extract the Jira-family shared layer out of the Cloud adapter

## Context / Problem

`adapters/jira/` currently owns units that are Jira-family-general, not Cloud-specific: the local↔Jira value maps and sanitizers (`jira_fields.py`), the `rebar-id` identity convention (`identity.py`), the link relation vocabulary (`jira_fields._RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`), and the absence-probe classifier (`probe.py`). PR #120 consumed these from a second adapter as **private** cross-package imports, which ADR 0035 never sanctioned — its seam is one level deep, core ⇄ adapter, with `adapters/jira/` as one backend's concrete implementation.

## Approach

Create `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` and move the **non-location-pinned** units into it with **public** names, then re-point the Cloud adapter's imports. Behavior is unchanged and proven so by the characterization oracles pinned in J1 [rebar:acb2-1823-2f0d-415b], which must pass untouched across this change.

**The move is by SYMBOL, not by file** — and only symbols out of the three modules that carry no by-path load references. Verified at plan time with the ADR-prescribed grep (`lazy_load(|_load_sibling_keyed(|spec_from_file_location(`) plus a filename-string sweep over `src/` and `tests/`: `jira_fields.py`, `identity.py`, and `probe.py` appear in **no** by-path load site.

- `identity.py` → relocates whole (`JiraIdentityConvention`). Imports nothing from `adapters/jira/`.
- `probe.py` → `classify_probe_response` moves, **taking the resolved-status set as a parameter** instead of
  reading the module-level `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES`. Those names (`Resolved`/`Done`/`Cancelled`) are Cloud/DIG
  workflow states; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything, so baking them into the
  shared classifier would misclassify a resolved DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED`. Cloud passes today's exact
  frozenset (so J1's pin holds unchanged); DC passes its own configured set in J6/J7. The live `probe()` /
  `_resolve_env()` stay in `adapters/jira/`: they read Cloud's ACLI settings, which is Cloud-specific transport.
- `jira_fields.py` → **splits.** It cannot relocate wholesale, because it imports from two pinned modules:
  `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from `adapters/jira/adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
  `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` (used by
  `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the file would make `jira_family/` import `adapters/jira/`, inverting the
  dependency direction this story's own structural oracle forbids. So:
  - **Move to `jira_family/` outright:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
    `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, and the value-map literals (see de-duplication below). None touch ADF or comment
    limits — `_sanitize_summary` is a pure character truncation against `_JIRA_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`.
  - **Move in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and `_sanitize_comment`. Their vendor
    dependency is injected rather than imported — `_sanitize_description` receives the `RichTextCodec` (its
    `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the rich-text seam that J3 [rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66] formalizes), and
    comment truncation receives the vendor comment-limit contract. Cloud builds both objects in
    `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC builds wiki-markup/plain-text
    equivalents in J6/J7. Observable behavior for Cloud is unchanged and pinned by J1's oracles.
  - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` therefore **remains as a thin Cloud-side module** that constructs the Cloud
    contract objects and re-exports nothing — its ACLI-facing callers (`acli.py`, `acli_cli_ops.py`,
    `acli_graph.py`) are re-pointed at the `jira_family` symbols directly, so no shim remains.

  If J3's `RichTextCodec` shape is not yet settled when this story is implemented, inject a minimal
  `Callable[[str], str]` fit function and let J3 widen it to the full contract — do NOT import the pinned
  module from `jira_family/` as a stopgap.

**`outbound_fields.py`, `adf.py`, and `comment_limits.py` do NOT move** — they are location-pinned per ADR 0035 §(a), and the pin is live, not merely historical:

- `adapters/jira/adf.py` is loaded by path from `inbound_fields.py:36` and
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:69` (`lazy_load(_ADF_KEY, "adapters/jira/adf.py")`), plus ~13 test files.
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` is loaded by path from `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py:193`,
  `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_roundtrip.py:72`, and
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_commits_on_ticket.py:121`.
- `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` is loaded by path from ~9 test files.

So the units inside them — `_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, and the ADF encoder — are shared **by dependency inversion, not relocation**: the pinned module imports the `jira_family` contracts (never the reverse) and is parameterized by them, so DC reuses one implementation with no file moving and `_loader.py` untouched. Relocating them is ADR 0035 Phase 2's work and is out of scope; if this story appears to require *moving* a pinned file, stop and record the blocker rather than moving it.

**Pinned means "cannot change path", not "cannot be edited"** — replacing a dict literal inside `outbound_fields.py` with an import from `jira_family/` is safe, because the loader resolves the file by path and does not care about its contents.

### De-duplicating the value maps (the pre-existing violation this story must not preserve)

The local→Jira status/priority maps exist TODAY in two independently-referenced copies that have already drifted:

- `jira_fields.py`'s `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the ACLI transport
  (`acli.py:69-70,143,171`; `acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354`).
- the pinned `outbound_fields.py`'s `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by the `Backend`
  port through `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
- The drift: the `outbound_fields` status map has a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the `jira_fields` copy lacks.

Moving only the `jira_fields` copy would leave Cloud's backend reading a second copy, so this story makes `adapters/jira_family/` the **sole definition site**: both existing dict literals are deleted and replaced by imports from `jira_family/`.

**The `deleted` key is decided here, not deferred — one unified dict cannot preserve two disagreeing callers.** The unified map adopts **`"deleted": "Done"`**, i.e. the `outbound_fields` value. Rationale: there are actually **three** copies of this map in the tree, and two of them already agree on `Done` — `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py`'s `local_to_jira_status` (line 37). Only `jira_fields`'s ACLI-side copy omits the key, where it falls through to `status.replace("_", " ").title()` and yields the string `"Deleted"` — **not a state in the live DIG workflow** (`{To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}`), so that transition would be rejected by Jira rather than applied. `"Deleted"` is therefore a latent bug, not behavior worth preserving, and `deleted` is a real `TicketStatus` (`src/rebar/types.py:21`), so the path is reachable.

**This is the one deliberate observable change in this otherwise behavior-preserving story**, and it is called out rather than smuggled: after this change, transitioning a `deleted` ticket through the ACLI path resolves to `Done` instead of the invalid `"Deleted"`. A test in this story pins the new value and references this paragraph.

The ACLI call site **keeps** its `.title()` fallback for keys the map does not contain — that fallback is independently load-bearing, because `transition_issue` accepts either a local status name OR an already-Jira name (`"In Progress"` passes through it unchanged). Only the `deleted` outcome changes.

Bug `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) remains open for the part this story does NOT do: the missing ACLI-side characterization pins, and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.

Per ADR 0035 decision 4, **no re-export shims** are left at the old paths: tests patch module-qualified, so a shim would create a patch-binding bug. Every importer and every `mock.patch` string is updated in this same change, and each moved module keeps exactly one canonical path.

`adapters/jira/`'s ACLI transport (`acli*.py`) is explicitly **not moved**, and its *logic* is not modified: it is the Cloud-specific, live-validated part. Its **import lines do change**, because `acli.py:69-70` and `acli_cli_ops.py:34` import the value maps and sanitizers that this story relocates — with no shims left behind, those imports must be re-pointed at `jira_family/`. So the invariant is "no behavioral change to the ACLI transport", verified as an import-only diff, NOT byte-identity.

**Alternative rejected:** promoting these into the backend-neutral core. They are Jira-specific — a GitHub backend would want none of them — so the neutral core is the wrong home and would re-create the coupling ADR 0035's Phase 2 removed.

**Alternative rejected:** leaving them in `adapters/jira/` and importing across adapters (PR #120's approach). It makes a concrete backend double as a shared library with no contract, and points a dependency edge sideways between siblings.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new package).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/` — `identity.py` relocated; `probe.py`'s pure classifier
  relocated (live probe stays); `jira_fields.py` split by symbol (file stays as the Cloud-side contract
  construction site); `backend.py` and `outbound_fields.py` imports updated; `acli*.py`, `adf.py`,
  `comment_limits.py` untouched in location.
- Every internal importer and every test `mock.patch` string naming the old paths.
- **Out of scope:** moving any location-pinned module, and any edit to `_loader.py`.

## Testing

Contract tier plus the pinned characterization oracles: the mechanism is a relocation, so the oracle is that observable behavior is identical and that no import or patch target dangles.

- happy path: the full existing suite passes, including J1's exact-value characterization assertions, with no
  edits to those assertions.
- structural oracle: a test asserts no module under `adapters/jira/` imports a name from a sibling adapter
  package, and that `adapters/jira_family/` imports from neither `adapters/jira/` nor
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/` — pinning the acyclic direction this epic exists to establish.
- negative control: `grep` confirms no re-export shim module remains at any old path.
- collateral invariant: the reconciler's dynamic loader still resolves every by-path module (the existing loader
  tests pass unchanged), and a test asserts each pinned filename (`adapters/jira/adf.py`,
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`) still exists at its pinned path —
  proving no location-pinned file moved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make test` passes with J1's characterization assertions unmodified
- [ ] J1's oracle change is already merged, and its Gerrit change number is recorded on this ticket as a comment
      before this story is pushed for review — the epic's "oracles written before any code moved" proof (epic AC8)
- [ ] no module under `adapters/jira/` imports a name from a sibling adapter package, and no module under
      `adapters/jira_family/` imports from `adapters/jira/` or `adapters/jira_datacenter/` — verified by grep at
      this story's merge time (the reciprocal check on `adapters/jira_datacenter/` is J7's AC, since that
      package does not exist yet)
- [ ] no re-export shim exists at any pre-move path (verified by `grep` for the old module names)
- [ ] every `mock.patch(` string in `tests/` naming a moved module resolves to the new path (`make test` green
      is the check, since a stale patch target raises)
- [ ] `adapters/jira/acli*.py` change ONLY in their import lines: `git diff -U0 -- 'src/**/adapters/jira/acli*.py'`
      shows no added/removed line outside an `import`/`from … import` statement, so the transport's logic is
      provably untouched while its imports are re-pointed at `jira_family/`
- [ ] `adapters/jira/adf.py`, `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, and `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` still
      exist at those exact paths, and `_loader.py` is unchanged (`git diff --stat` shows neither a rename nor an
      edit to `_loader.py`)
- [ ] the import contract is installed as a PERSISTENT check, not a one-off grep inside a single test. Chosen
      mechanism, so the implementer does not have to decide: a **test in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` that
      walks the AST of every module under `adapters/` and asserts the permitted import graph**, because it runs
      inside the existing `make test` that CI's `Verified` gate already executes — no new CI job, no new dev
      dependency, and it matches how this repo already enforces structural rules (e.g.
      `test_backend_neutrality.py`). It fails when a module outside `adapters/jira/` or
      `adapters/jira_datacenter/` imports `adapters/jira_family/`, or when `jira_family/` imports either of
      them. Demonstrated by a deliberately violating branch failing locally before being reverted (epic AC7).
      An `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml` is an acceptable substitute ONLY if it is wired into
      `make lint`, since a config no CI target runs is not enforcement
- [ ] no module under `adapters/jira_family/` imports from `adapters/jira/` — specifically, `jira_family/`
      contains no import of `adf`, `comment_limits`, `outbound_fields`, or any `acli*` module; the
      ADF/comment-limit dependencies of `_sanitize_description` / `_sanitize_comment` arrive as injected
      contract objects (verified by grep over `adapters/jira_family/`)
- [ ] exactly one dict literal defines the local→Jira status map and one the priority map **within
      `adapters/`**: `grep -rn` for the map literals under
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/` finds them only in `adapters/jira_family/`, and both the
      ACLI transport and `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote` resolve to that single definition.
      `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status` is EXPECTED to still exist after this story
      (deferred to bug `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61`) — the grep must be scoped to `adapters/` so this AC and the
      story's stated scope agree
- [ ] observable behavior is unchanged for both callers EXCEPT the one declared `deleted` fix: J1's backend
      characterization pins pass unmodified, and a test pins the ACLI path's resolved value for every status it
      previously handled — plus the new `deleted` → `"Done"` (was the invalid `"Deleted"`), and the retained
      `.title()` fallback still passing an already-Jira name like `"In Progress"` through unchanged

baseline.description:
## Summary

The Gerrit Verified Gate's macOS `pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` cell fails fast (~1m30s) with **pytest exit code 5 ("no tests ran")** for any in-flight change whose patchset tree **predates the `platform_compat` auto-marker** landed by story omphacite-desertlike-coney. All three Ubuntu cells pass; only macOS fails, blocking `Verified +1` for otherwise-correct changes. Reproduced on runs 32927544184, 32927483100, 32927478228 (all testing `refs/changes/26/2226/*`, base `01ef008e`).

## Proven root cause (regression)

The macOS default-suite step selects `-m "platform_compat and not external"` via `DEFAULT_SUITE_MARKS`. The `platform_compat` marker is applied **only** at collection time by `tests/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` (path-fragment auto-marker). The Verified gate runs `_build-and-test.yml` from **trusted main** (reusable-workflow ref binding) against the **raw patchset tree**. A patchset whose base predates the auto-marker has **zero** tests carrying `platform_compat`, so the selection matches nothing → pytest exits 5 → the job fails.

Discriminating experiment (runtime oracle):

| tree state | collected | exit |
|---|---|---|
| current main (auto-marker present) | 909 | 0 |
| auto-marker neutralized (= pre-marker patchset tree) | 0 | 5 |

Restoring the marker → rc 0; removing it → rc 5. This isolates the conftest auto-marker as the necessary cause and rules out strict-markers (which errors as "unknown mark"), the invocation, and the integration tier.

## Defect origin

`caused_by` story omphacite-desertlike-coney (`3ba8-49d5-fee5-445d`, commit `920492b1`), class **regression**. That change split the contract across two halves — the workflow selection (`platform_compat`) and the conftest marker application — and the trusted-main workflow half applies to patchset trees that lack the conftest half. Before it, macOS ran the full suite and never spuriously exited 5. It escaped its own gate because A's gate run executed the pre-A full macOS suite (the reduction only takes effect after merge, by the same ref-binding).

## Approach

Make the macOS default-suite step **tolerate an empty `platform_compat` collection**: capture pytest's exit code and, **only on `macos-latest`**, map rc 5 → success. This restores the pre-regression behaviour (the gate does not spuriously fail on a pre-marker tree) while keeping A's speedup for current trees. It is safe because:

- Every patchset is still **fully exercised on the Ubuntu cells** (whole-suite
  selection, which does not depend on the marker).
- A **current-tree** marker regression is still caught on Ubuntu by
  `test_platform_compat_suite_covers_the_core_os_sensitive_seams`.
- On every **other** cell the selection is the whole suite, where rc 5 remains a real
  empty-suite failure that must stay red — the tolerance is macOS-only.

## Scope boundary

Changes only the macOS branch's exit-code handling in `_build-and-test.yml`'s default-suite step, plus a behavioural parity guard. No matrix, runner, fixture, or Python-version change. Does not touch the `external`-marker lanes (non-gate, scheduled, run on their own tree, path-pinned — no tree skew).

## Testing

New behavioural guard `test_macos_default_suite_lane_passes_when_platform_compat_collects_nothing` renders the step's GitHub expressions per cell, stubs `pytest` to exit 5, executes the real lane shell, and asserts **macOS → pass (0)** while **every Ubuntu cell → fail (5)**. Seen RED first (macOS returns 5) on the unfixed workflow; GREEN after the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The macOS default-suite lane treats pytest exit 5 (no `platform_compat` tests
      collected) as success, so a patchset whose tree predates the auto-marker gets a
      green macOS cell.
- [x] The Ubuntu cells still fail on an empty collection (rc 5 remains a real failure
      off the macOS cell).
- [x] A behavioural test executes the lane's real shell and asserts macOS→0 /
      ubuntu→5, verified RED before the fix.
- [x] `make lint` and the full `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` suite pass.
baseline.summary: Verified gate macOS cell fails (pytest exit 5) for patchsets predating the platform_compat auto-marker

## Context / Problem

Adding the `[code_review]` section re-export in ticket `unaroused-undead-ibisbill` took `src/rebar/config.py` from 799 to exactly 800 lines. The CI module-size gate fails on `loc > cap` with cap 800 (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so the file passes today but the NEXT line added to it — a new section class re-export, a new owned accessor — fails CI, and the limit is locked so it cannot be raised by a contributor.

## Approach

Split `src/rebar/config.py` along an existing call-graph seam, the same way `_config_schema.py` and `_config_sources.py` were already carved out of it, so the facade regains headroom without changing any public import path (`from rebar.config import X` must keep working — the module already re-exports every moved name).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/config.py` — extract one cohesive cluster into a sibling private module.
- the new sibling module.
- tests covering the moved surface, if any assert on the old location.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/config.py` is at most 700 lines (`wc -l`), leaving headroom under the 800 cap.
- [ ] Every name importable from `rebar.config` before the split is still importable after —
      verified by the existing config test suite passing unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0.
baseline.summary: src/rebar/config.py sits at the 800-line module-size cap with zero headroom

Store the baseline in the projection the comparison already computes: `description` as `normalize_rich_text(raw)`, `status`/`priority` as `.name`. Expected ~-66% on an **18.3 MB** (18,257,550-byte) file. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why this is safe without a comparator change
`outbound_field_diff.py:187,196` canonicalize BOTH sides at **read** time via `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` (docstring `:183`: "storage stays vendor-shaped, mapped at READ time only"), and both canonicalizers are idempotent on already-normalized values: `normalize_rich_text` (`inbound_fields.py:136-145`) returns `adf_to_text(body)` for dicts and `str(body)` otherwise; `_extract_jira_field_value` (`:92-96`) reads `name`/`displayName` for dicts and passes strings through. So ADF-dict and plain-text baselines canonicalize identically and a mixed store needs no new comparator. This also makes the change **revert-safe** — a normalized-string baseline round-trips unchanged through pre-A3 code.

CORRECTION carried forward: an earlier framing rested on `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields`, which have **zero production callers**. Validate against the live path only.

## Why assignee is EXCLUDED — data loss, not conflict noise
`_assignee_candidates` (`outbound_field_diff.py:56-67`) builds its match set from the scalar **plus every non-None identity form**, and `_suppressed_by_inbound` (`:250-256`) routes assignee through `_assignee_matches`. Collapsing three identity forms to one string shrinks that candidate set and loses inbound-directionality suppression, so local-wins **silently clobbers a concurrent remote assignee edit**. (The strict `assignee_identity` equality at `:390-394` is the lesser, secondary effect.) Keep assignee raw.

## Trap to pin
Store exactly `normalize_rich_text(raw)` — any other text extraction (fit/truncate/strip variants) diverges from what the same ADF decodes to on the read path and fabricates a permanent diff.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the **same
      verdict** as its normalized-string equivalent. Tier: **integration** through the real
      production comparison path. **This test does not exist today** —
      `test_binding_baseline.py:36-59` and `test_baseline_arbitration.py:91` use flat strings only, so
      a no-op-on-strings normalizer would leave them green while proving nothing. This is the RED case.
- [ ] The direction-preservation suite, extended with assignee shape cases (email / accountId /
      displayName), passes unchanged — proving assignee arbitration is untouched. Tier: **property/unit**.
- [ ] Baseline entries for `description`/`status`/`priority` are scalars after one pass; `assignee`
      remains a dict. Tier: **integration** asserting stored shapes.
- [ ] A corpus diff over real bindings shows **zero mutation delta** before vs after normalization.
      Tier: **repo-level corpus script**.
- [ ] `bindings.json` size drops by >=50%. Verify: byte comparison before/after one full pass.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py`

Scope: S-M. Depends on A2-1.
baseline.summary: A3: text-normalize baseline description/status/priority in set_baseline (assignee deliberately excluded)

## Problem

Discovered during the Step-7 sibling sweep of baldish-regainable-steed (e4a6-545b-36af-456d), which fixed the tickets-branch CAS push to back off with JITTER (not lockstep) before re-fetching.

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py` publishes the last-pass witness under a 3-attempt CAS loop:

```python
for attempt in range(3):
    if ref_lock._cas_advance(repo_root, LAST_PASS_REF, new_oid=new_oid, old_oid=old_oid, remote=remote):
        ...
        return record
    if attempt == 2:
        break
    sleeper((0.1, 0.2)[attempt])          # FIXED, unjittered schedule
    old_oid = ref_lock._ref_oid(repo_root, LAST_PASS_REF, remote=remote) or _ZERO_OID
```

This loop is STALENESS-correct (it re-reads `old_oid` after the sleep, so the next CAS is against fresh state — unlike the baldish tickets-push bug). But the backoff schedule `(0.1, 0.2)` is deterministic and unjittered: two reconciler passes that collide once on LAST_PASS_REF sleep identical durations, wake together, and re-collide — the same thundering-herd/lockstep class as the JITTER half of baldish.

## Scope / why not fixed in the baldish change

This is a DIFFERENT subsystem (the reconciler ref-lock publication) with its own concurrency model — reconciler passes are more serialized than tickets writes, so the exposure is lower and the fix warrants its own review rather than being folded into the tickets-push bugfix. The staleness half does NOT apply here (the loop already re-reads after the sleep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The last-pass CAS publication backoff is jittered (additive jitter on the base schedule) so colliding reconciler passes do not wake in lockstep, mirroring the additive-jitter idiom now used by the tickets-push `_cas_backoff` (`src/rebar/_store/push_classify.py`) and the Jira DC transport.
- [x] The staleness-correct re-read of `old_oid` after the sleep is preserved.
- [x] A test drives colliding publications and asserts the backoff delays vary (not a single lockstep value), with a negative control at zero contention.

## Notes on adjacent non-siblings (from the same sweep, recorded so they are not re-triaged)

- `_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS` (push_classify.py) rides out a transient TLS fault, not writer contention — thundering-herd does not apply, jitter would not help convergence.
- `_coordinated_fetch`'s `_FETCH_CAS_BACKOFF_S` (sync.py) re-fetches after the sleep (staleness-correct) and serializes rebar peers behind `fetch_coordination_lock`, so rebar-peer lockstep is already prevented; the residual racer is a non-rebar git peer.
baseline.summary: last-pass CAS publication retry uses an unjittered fixed backoff (0.1, 0.2), so competing reconciler passes re-collide in lockstep

# S8 — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping`: live Jira probe to pre-populate mapping config

## Context / Problem
Epic 3d7a (S1–S5) adds the mapping seam: a reserved `[mapping]` / `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block with per-layer vocabulary (`statuses`, `issue_types`, `link_types`, `hierarchy`) and axis maps (`status_map`, `type_map`, `link_map`, `priority_map`, `create_defaults`), parsed by `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py` (S1). Hand-authoring it is transcription-error-prone. S8 adds a READ-ONLY command that observes a live Jira project via the pycontribs client and emits a suggested `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block seeded with the project's real vocabulary and identity-seed axis maps.

Findings resolved:
- Verb `rebar bridge probe` COLLIDES with the retired alias `bridge-probe`
  (`_registry.py:579`; parser `_parsers/advanced/bridge.py:117`; handler `_bridge_probe`
  `_cli/__init__.py:103`, which CREATES+DELETES a throwaway issue — not read-only). New
  verb: **`rebar bridge suggest-mapping`** (verified free in `src/`+`tests/`).
- No private `_get_json` — it exists ONLY on the Gerrit client
  (`review_bot/gerrit_client.py:128`), not the jira adapter, which uses only HIGH-LEVEL
  `jira.JIRA` methods; the probe uses only such methods (below).
- No tomlkit; TOML read via stdlib `tomllib`; `_emit_toml` is fail-closed on nesting, so
  an orchestrator + dedicated nested emitter are added (below).

## Approach
New verb wired into the bridge group (NEW):
- Parser: `commands.add_parser("suggest-mapping", ...)` in
  `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/bridge.py` (beside `check-access` ~line 117), taking
  `<PROJECT>` and `--write`.
- Dispatch: add `"suggest-mapping"` to `bridge_cli`'s pass-through set
  (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:259`) + a `_passthrough`/`_passthrough_help`
  branch → NEW handler `_bridge_suggest_mapping` (`_cli/__init__.py`, sibling of
  `_bridge_probe`).

Probe (NEW `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_probe.py`, <800 LOC): a probe PORT with one narrow method per axis, each a thin call to a pycontribs `jira.JIRA` method. Default port built from `build_client_from_settings` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:155`); tests inject a FAKE port → offline. Pin `jira>=3.8,<4` (pyproject.toml:202).

Axis grounding — every axis uses a HIGH-LEVEL method (no private REST):
- `issue_types` + `hierarchy` → `jira.JIRA.issue_types()` (read each `hierarchyLevel`;
  if absent, `hierarchy` is DROPPED empty + note, not fabricated).
- `priority_map` vocab → `jira.JIRA.priorities()`; `link_types` →
  `jira.JIRA.issue_link_types()` (documented public).
- `statuses` vocab → `jira.JIRA.statuses()` (documented public). pycontribs exposes no
  per-PROJECT status list publicly, so this is the GLOBAL set — the block documents that
  honest limitation.
- `create_defaults` stubs → `jira.JIRA.createmeta_issuetypes(<KEY>)` +
  `createmeta_fieldtypes(<KEY>, <id>)` (public createmeta API); stub only for a
  `required: true` field NOT in the create BASELINE (see AC footer).
- transition hints (best-effort) → grounded in the ACTUAL transitions surface:
  `jira.JIRA.search_issues(jql)` (CONFIRMED in DC adapter) fetches one sample issue per
  discovered type, then `jira.JIRA.transitions(issue)` (CONFIRMED at
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/transitions.py:80`). Jira returns transitions only from each
  sample's CURRENT status, so the set is inherently partial → flagged best-effort.
  `status_map` stays identity-seeded; transition data is an ADVISORY marker, not complete.

Anchor: `search_issues`, `transitions`, `fields` are confirmed in-repo on this same `jira.JIRA` client (DC adapter); the vocabulary getters are documented pycontribs 3.x public API.

Emit: build `{"projects": {<KEY>: {<layer>}}}`.
- Default (no `--write`): serialize that block to stdout as TOML. NEVER writes; reads only.
- `--write`: mirror `write_jira_config`'s target-selection + read-whole/mutate/atomic-
  replace. Target via `config._discover_project_config` → existing `rebar.toml`, else
  create `<repo_root>/rebar.toml`; user `pyproject.toml` is NEVER edited. Read with
  `tomllib`, DEEP-MERGE under `data["mapping"]["projects"][<KEY>]` (EXISTING keys win,
  hand edits never clobbered), re-emit the WHOLE file via the orchestrator below, atomic
  `os.replace`.

Serialization — OPTION B, a top-level ORCHESTRATOR (a real `rebar.toml` mixes FLAT siblings `[jira]`/`[tracker]` with the NESTED `[mapping.*]`, so no single emitter can write the whole file). `_config_writer._emit_toml` (:188) fail-closes on any nested sub-table — pinned by `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py:149` (`_emit_toml({"jira": {"nested": {"k": "v"}}})` must raise `ConfigError`); UNTOUCHED. S8 adds two NEW helpers in `_config_writer.py`:
- `_emit_nested_toml(name, table)` — recurses one nested table into dotted-header
  sub-tables (`[mapping.projects.KEY.status_map]`); only ever handed the `mapping` table.
- `_emit_config_toml(data)` — orchestrator: split off the reserved `mapping` key, emit
  ALL remaining top-level items (scalars + the flat `[jira]`/`[tracker]` siblings it did
  NOT author) via the EXISTING `_emit_toml`, then append
  `_emit_nested_toml("mapping", data["mapping"])` when present, joined by a blank line.
`_emit_toml` never receives the `mapping` table, so its fail-closed contract + pinned test stand; flat siblings round-trip through the flat path, nested `[mapping.*]` through the nested path. The `--write` handler calls `_emit_config_toml`; `write_jira_config` keeps calling `_emit_toml` unchanged. HONEST SCOPE: `tomllib` drops comments (no tomlkit), so the merge keeps existing hand-edited VALUES (existing keys win) but inline comments in `[mapping]` are NOT preserved.

## Scope
- NEW `mapping_probe.py` (probe port + per-axis getters + layer builder + TOML emit),
  <800 LOC.
- NEW `_config_writer._emit_nested_toml` + `_emit_config_toml` orchestrator (per
  Serialization); `_emit_toml` (:188) + pinned `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py:149`
  stay UNTOUCHED.
- Wire: `bridge.py` parser, `_bridge_commands.py` dispatch, `__init__.py` handler (NEW).
- Out of scope: WRITE to Jira; live-credential CI gating; comment round-tripping.

## Testing
Tests use a FAKE probe port returning canned issue-type/priority/link-type/status/ createmeta/search+transitions data — fully offline, no live Jira or CI credential (portability rule). A live smoke run is manual, never a CI gate. New tests in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_probe.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `test_probe_emits_mapping` — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping <KEY>` against the fake
      port emits a `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block with discovered vocabulary (`issue_types`,
      `statuses`, `link_types`, priorities, `hierarchy` when `hierarchyLevel` present),
