## Summary

`_reads._tracker` raises `store_uninitialized` only when the tracker directory is ABSENT (`src/rebar/_reads.py`, `if not os.path.isdir(tracker)`). A directory that EXISTS but is not a usable store — no `.git`, or a `.git` with no resolvable HEAD, or one mid-clone — satisfies `isdir`, so every read returns `[]`. A broken store is indistinguishable from an empty one, the exact confusion the guard was added to remove. Hit three times: the deployed MCP server served an empty tracker (marker files, no `.git`); `fathomable-yester-thrip` change 2244 residual; and `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` AC3. Full RCA and escalation are in prior comments.

## Constraints

- An existing, empty, INITIALIZED store must still read `[]` — a real contract with an existing
  test. The discriminator cannot be emptiness.
- `.env-id` is ruled out as the predicate (git-ignored, absent right after a valid clone).
- A `.git`-LESS materialized ticket snapshot must READ: `_snapshot.materialize_tickets` checks the
  committed tickets tree out into a `.git`-less `.tickets-tracker/`, and the code-review gate
  agents read it in production. A `.git`+HEAD-only predicate breaks that surface (the escalation
  the operator resolved with Option A).

## Fix (operator-approved Option A — one shared content-based seam)

New stdlib-only leaf `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py::store_is_usable(tracker)`: usable when `isdir` AND EITHER (1) `.git` present with a resolvable HEAD (`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`), OR (2) it carries the store STRUCTURE — a committed `.store-compat.json` record (survives the snapshot checkout, present even in a zero-event store), or ≥1 non-dot event dir (legacy fallback, mirrors `reducer/_api.py` enumeration). `_reads._tracker` calls `store_is_usable` directly; the write guard `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` calls `store_is_writable` = `store_is_usable` AND `.git` present (the write's inherent precondition — it commits events). Both flow through the ONE shared usability predicate — no mode flag, no second path — so read and write cannot diverge on what an initialized store is, while a `.git`-less read-only snapshot stays READABLE but correctly non-writable. Clause 2 keeps the `.git`-less snapshot readable while the marker-file-only production incident still RAISES. Zero events + committed marker is VALID (reads `[]`); the predicate is never keyed on emptiness.

The HEAD probe reuses the store's bounded runner `gitutil.run_git_bounded` (folds `TimeoutExpired` to rc 124), so no unbounded git call enters the write path; a missing `git` binary (`OSError`) propagates as a distinct environment fault, not `store_uninitialized`. The write gate does NOT loosen: `_ensure_initialized` gates on `store_is_writable(tracker)` = `store_is_usable(tracker)` AND `.git` present. It shares the usability predicate (so read and write agree on what an initialized store IS) and then adds the write's inherent precondition — a write COMMITS events, so it needs a real `.git` repository. This preserves the original `.git`-requiring write gate exactly: a `.git`-less STRUCTURE-only snapshot is READABLE but NOT writable, and a mid-clone (`.git`, no HEAD, no structure) is rejected by `store_is_usable` itself. One usability seam, no bypass flag.

The sole `store_uninitialized` consumer, the read-only audit web index (`audit.server._audited_tickets`), still degrades a broken store to an empty page (must not 500) but now LOGS a warning and its docstring no longer claims such a store is never blanked — behavior unchanged; that promise held only while broken stores read `[]`. Caller sweep re-verified against the NEW predicate: all 7 `_tracker` entry points and the `.git`-less snapshot path behave correctly. Files: `store_usability.py` (new), `_reads.py`, `event_prepare.py`, `audit/server.py`, `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] READ: a dir with marker files only (no `.git`/`.store-compat.json`/event dirs) raises
      `store_uninitialized`, not `[]` — the production incident.
- [x] READ: a mid-clone store (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable, no structure) raises
      `store_uninitialized`.
- [x] READ: an existing empty INITIALIZED store (`.git`+HEAD) still reads `[]` (contract test
      unchanged).
- [x] READ: a valid clone with resolvable HEAD but no `.env-id` still reads (reads differ from
      writes on `.env-id`).
- [x] READ regression: a `.git`-LESS materialized snapshot with committed `.store-compat.json` +
      an event dir READS the ticket, not raises (the gate-agent path).
- [x] READ edge: a `.git`-less snapshot with `.store-compat.json` and ZERO events reads `[]`.
- [x] WRITE: `_ensure_initialized` (via `store_is_writable`) rejects a mid-clone store, rejects a
      `.git`-LESS materialized snapshot (readable but not writable — no repo to commit into), and
      still accepts an initialized one.
- [x] WRITE: every `stage_and_commit` git call incl. the new HEAD probe is timeout-BOUNDED
      (`test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba`).
- [x] PREDICATE: `store_is_usable` is False for absent/no-`.git`/mid-clone/empty-dir and True for
      an initialized store, a HEAD-resolvable clone without `.env-id`, a snapshot, an
      event-dir-only legacy store, and an empty-but-committed snapshot.
- [x] PREDICATE: a missing `git` binary (OSError) PROPAGATES rather than reporting
      `store_uninitialized` (T5b failure-taxonomy).
- [x] AUDIT: `audit.server._audited_tickets` renders empty AND logs a warning for a
      present-but-unusable store.
- [x] Mutation guard: stripping the store-structure clause returns the `.git`-less snapshot read
      to RAISING `store_uninitialized` (defect-seeded, sandboxed).

## Testing

RED→GREEN in `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`; run `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py -q` (all cases above green). Broad re-verification: `python -m pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces -q -n auto` — the 6 previously-red snapshot/next-batch/write-timeout tests are green; `make lint` (complexity ratchet new=0/increased=0) and `make typecheck` pass. The pre-existing sandbox-git failures (`show-ref`/`ls-tree refs/heads/tickets` → 128) fail identically on clean `origin/main` and are environmental, not from this change.

Out of approved scope (parity — discovered ticket): CLI read path (`reads_cli.py`) and other bare-`isdir` read sites → `free-slothful-fennecfox` (be80-8377-4b4c-44f4).
baseline.summary: reads return [] for a directory that exists but is not a usable store, so a broken store is indistinguishable from an empty one

## Context / Problem
While closing ticket 86a5-9221-0037-4e38 on current origin/main, the landed-work precheck scanned all reachable commit messages and printed three unrelated resolver errors such as `Error: Ambiguous prefix 2f3c matches multiple tickets`. The target ticket used a full ID and closed successfully, so these diagnostics came from unrelated historical commit references. `_referencing_commit_exists` calls the shared resolver for every extracted reference; the resolver writes ambiguity errors to stderr even though the precheck only needs to know whether a reference matches the accepted target IDs.

## Approach
Make the close precheck resolve unrelated historical candidates silently while preserving normal resolver diagnostics for user-facing commands. Add a regression test with an ambiguous historical short prefix before a valid full-ID trailer and prove close scanning neither emits the unrelated error nor misses the valid commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The close landed-work precheck does not print ambiguity diagnostics for unrelated historical commit references.
- [x] A later valid full-ID commit reference is still detected when earlier history contains an ambiguous short prefix.
- [x] Target-ID ambiguity remains visible in commands where the user explicitly supplies an ambiguous prefix.
- [x] Focused tests and `make lint` pass.

## Symptom
The live Jira DC lane (jira-dc-harness in external-integration.yml) fails on two rich-text tests after change 2266 (bug f449 lag-free snapshot overlay) landed: (1) test_live_rich_text_renders_and_echo_is_safe — after _push_and_converge of a rich body, renderedFields.description is EMPTY (''), so the <h1> assertion fails; (2) test_live_rich_text_both_sides_conflict_keeps_local — the converged settle pass computes outbound totals [1] when a converged repeat must compute nothing.

## Root cause (CONFIRMED — see RCA comment)
A `sync --only`-generic apply-dispatch drop, NOT a codec/differ/overlay defect. Under the PRIMARY route `sync --only=<local_id>` (Mode.LIVE, route="sync"), run_differs builds the outbound scalar UPDATE on a BOUND issue with `target = jira_key`, then hands `ticket_planner.plan_pass` a selection whose `ids` are the SELECTED LOCAL IDS only. `_scope_excluded` compares the jira-key target against those local ids (`target not in ids`), classifies the in-scope update `scope_deferred`, and the live coordinator+fuse reroute skips the deferred plan — the write is dropped. The legacy `--filter-local-ids` route works because it scopes via `_build_filter_target_set` (LOCAL IDS ∪ bound JIRA KEYS). Because the description write never lands, remote stays None and every pass re-emits (symptom 2) and renders empty (symptom 1).

## Fix
In run_differs, expand the selection ids handed to the shadow planner to LOCAL IDS ∪ their BOUND JIRA KEYS (new pure helper `_scoped_selection_ids`, sourced from the mutations' own provenance — no binding_store I/O), mirroring the legacy `_build_filter_target_set`. A bound-issue update (target=jira_key) is then recognized in-scope and planned `mutate`, so the coordinator executes the write. The same expansion also corrects a latent `--except` case (an excepted ticket's jira-key-targeted update was not being excluded).

## Attribution
regression, caused_by 67d4-ecba-cf95-4353 (commit d49466b5, "Wire live coordinator+fuse non-create reroute"), which made the coordinator+fuse reroute the authoritative dispatch path without ensuring in-scope bound-issue updates classify `mutate`. The defective scope check was authored shadow-only in 6bcf548d (85f8) where it dropped nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A scoped `sync --only` LIVE pass dispatches a bound issue's outbound scalar UPDATE to the transport write (RED before fix), verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_sync_only_scalar_update_dispatch_heldout.py`.
- [x] The `--filter-local-ids` parity guard stays GREEN in the same held-out oracle (no legacy regression).
- [x] The pure helper `_scoped_selection_ids` expands a selected bound local id to include its jira key, does NOT pull in unselected tickets, and leaves a create's local-id target unchanged, verified by `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_scoped_selection_ids_af1b.py`.
- [x] No regression in the reconciler unit suite: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- [x] The live Jira DC External Integration lane (all three rich-text tests) runs GREEN in GitHub Actions.

## Testing
- Held-out RED→GREEN oracle (subprocess-driven reconcile_once with an in-memory transport): `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_sync_only_scalar_update_dispatch_heldout.py`. Mutation check: reverting the id-expansion returns the `--only` test to RED.
- Pure-function teeth: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_scoped_selection_ids_af1b.py`.
- Regression sweep: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` (3631 passed), `make lint`, `make typecheck`.
- Live replication: the Jira DC External Integration lane exercises the real `sync --only` path against live Jira DC.

This file is AT the cap. Any edit at all currently fails CI.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.

# A stale installed build must fail loudly, not as a plain INDETERMINATE

## Context
A stale installed rebar build rejected the repository's dict-shaped `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` with `CriteriaError`, but plan review emitted an ordinary unsigned INDETERMINATE carrying `llm_ran: false` and `llm_unavailable: true`. The DET tier still appeared, so a broken install looked like a ticket that could not be reviewed. Predecessor `inexistent-tempting-nerka` repaired the machine-local updater; this ticket is the durable repository repair. Control flow must remain fail-closed and continue emitting a verdict.

## Confirmed root cause and authority
The deterministic assemble step loads effective criteria. The generic workflow interpreter stringifies its exception, then `produce_plan_review_verdict` routes every unrecovered workflow failure through the systemic-LLM degraded builder. That builder hardcodes `llm_unavailable: true`, even when the recorded failed frame is the scripted assemble step and no LLM/batch frame executed. Runtime differential proof and exact citations are recorded in the Phase 1 RCA comment.

This is a defect against original epic jira-reb-687, which explicitly replaced opaque LLM error collapse and scoped unavailable/disposition behavior to LLM failures. `docs/config.md` and ADR 0040 preserve the same boundary. Criteria configuration parsing is not an LLM call.

## Repair plan
- At the criteria-assembly boundary, catch the exact shared criteria exception and return a failed workflow step with a stable structured failure kind plus the original diagnostic. Do not classify by matching error-message text.
- Before the generic failed-tail LLM degradation, inspect the recorded failed assemble step. Route only the structured criteria/config failure kind to a dedicated plan-review config-fault verdict path. Genuine preflight and mid-run `LLMUnavailableError` paths remain byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged.
- Build the config-fault verdict from the same deterministic floor and partitioning path, preserving DET findings. Its coverage must mark a distinct config fault, omit the affirmative `llm_unavailable` label, and contain an actionable diagnostic that names the running installed rebar build as the suspect and points the operator to the repository checkout build.
- Teach terminal verdict assembly that a systemic config fault is INDETERMINATE unless an actionable deterministic blocker already makes it BLOCK. This preserves fail-closed behavior without reusing the LLM-outage flag.
- Document the structured failure marker in the assemble-step output contract.
- Add focused regression coverage through the public verdict seam, paired with genuine LLM-outage and healthy controls.

## Testing
The held-out oracle will drive the real workflow gate with a successful fake provider while injecting the exact shared criteria exception at effective-criteria assembly. It will prove the fixture reached the scripted assemble frame before any agent/batch work, assert the observable verdict/coverage contract, and compare against a genuine provider outage. The existing gate-cutover and LLM failure-matrix tests remain controls. Canonical lint, typecheck, focused tests, and the relevant workflow/plan-review suite must pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Injecting the shared `CriteriaError` during real criteria assembly yields an unsigned fail-closed verdict with `verdict: INDETERMINATE`, `llm_ran: false`, full DET coverage, a distinct config-fault field, and no affirmative `llm_unavailable` field.
- [x] The config-fault diagnostic explicitly names the running INSTALLED REBAR BUILD as the suspect and directs the reader to use the repository checkout build; it preserves the original parse diagnostic without using string matching to classify it.
- [x] A negative-control genuine `LLMUnavailableError` still produces `llm_unavailable: true`; a healthy fake-provider control still runs the LLM tier and never reports a config fault.
- [x] The structured failure kind is carried from the exact criteria exception at the assemble boundary and documented in that step's output contract. Other assemble/runtime failures are not silently reclassified as criteria config faults.
- [x] DET behavior is unchanged: the config-fault verdict carries the same deterministic findings/counts as the existing degraded path, and a deterministic blocker remains BLOCK rather than being masked by INDETERMINATE.
- [x] Focused regression tests, relevant workflow/plan-review tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` pass.
- [x] The change lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and no unresolved comments.
baseline.summary: A stale installed build must fail loudly, not as a plain INDETERMINATE

baseline.description:
## Context

Code review already routes changed Terraform to the `code-review-iac` overlay, but its Pass-1 overlay and Pass-2 verifier have only generic repository tools. This slice reuses the tool-session contract created by `forcible-diminished-lamb` [rebar:forcible-diminished-lamb] so IaC findings can cite and independently re-check whole-module evidence. It changes no behavior for other diffs.

## Scope

- Thread `assemble_diff.outputs.changed_files` into `CodeReviewBatchRunner`; its constructor already stores this field, but the production gate dispatcher currently omits it.
- In both Round A and Round B, create a fresh Terraform tool session only for an included `code-review-iac` criterion when the changed set contains `.tf`, `.tf.json`, or an explicitly changed `.tfvars`. Supply the `lookup_declaration` and `resolve_reference` tools from the prerequisite. The base reviewer and every other overlay receive no Terraform tools.
- Scope the session from changed paths, then use the prerequisite's whole affected-module/local-closure rules. A changed `.tfvars` remains direct evidence only and is never treated as an automatically selected input.
- After Pass-1 merge, expose a new session to `code-review-verify` only when a merged finding is attributed to `code-review-iac` and the changed set has Terraform scope. The verifier receives the Pass-1 receipt as evidence but must issue its own query; there is no inherited answer or query ledger.
- The coach and deterministic decision steps receive no Terraform tools.
- Merge concrete/module-membership reads into the call's `_usage.distinct_fetches`. Include the concrete Terraform files read in the code-review sidecar's reviewed-file `deps` so region-gated re-review memory cannot reuse evidence after a module dependency changes.
- Keep missing-extra behavior fail-open: code review continues through its existing generic path, with no advertised Terraform tools. An advertised tool failure returns the prerequisite's closed abstention and cannot itself create or block a finding.
- Do not add a scanner stage or originate findings from the index. The IaC overlay remains the finder; grounding only answers its explicit queries.

## Positive rationale

The slice is independently releasable after its prerequisite: a Terraform diff receives query-grounded IaC review end to end, while all non-IaC requests remain byte-compatible. It reuses the existing overlay routing and generic per-call tool-provider seam instead of creating a Terraform-specific review engine.

## Out of scope

No new parser, source-network logic, corroborator executable, prompt change, standalone validation, Terraform/OpenTofu/provider execution, or non-IaC tool exposure.

## Failure-disposition contract

- Missing `grounding-terraform` extra: non-fatal capability absence; advertise no tools and complete the ordinary review.
- Unsupported/ambiguous/dynamic Terraform question: return ABSTAIN; the LLM may verify directly from files but the tool supplies no positive claim.
- Parser/path/limit/timeout failure: return ABSTAIN and preserve the existing review result; do not reinterpret it as a clean module or nonexistent symbol.
- Internal routing/session construction defect: surface through existing gate error handling rather than silently attaching tools to a broader step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Production dispatch passes the exact assembled `changed_files` into `CodeReviewBatchRunner`, and a Round-A changed-`.tf` integration test observes both Terraform tools only on `code-review-iac`.
- [ ] A Round-B escalation test observes the same tool surface and whole-module resolution when IaC is recommended rather than glob-selected, without running the overlay twice.
- [ ] A merged IaC finding makes `code-review-verify` receive a distinct Terraform query session; a verifier tool call returns a fresh receipt rather than reusing the Pass-1 result.
- [ ] Base review, non-IaC overlays, coach, a Python-only diff, and an IaC review with no IaC findings advertise no Terraform tools.
- [ ] A changed `.tfvars` can be queried as direct structural evidence, and a test proves its value is not injected into module variables or used to resolve a computed reference.
- [ ] Code-review usage and sidecar dependency tests contain the concrete sibling/local-module files read; modifying one invalidates the recorded dependency hash while an unrelated non-Terraform file does not.
- [ ] Missing-extra and every prerequisite ABSTAIN outcome leave the ordinary code-review decision path intact and never become a synthetic IaC finding.

## Testing

Test contract card:

- Authoritative contract: REB-640, this ticket, and the prerequisite's tool/receipt contract [rebar:forcible-diminished-lamb].
- Preconditions: a real assembled diff with one changed root `.tf`, an unchanged sibling declaration, a local child module, and captured Round-A/Round-B/verifier requests.
- Production path: production gate dispatch → real `CodeReviewBatchRunner` → real tool session; only the model result is faked.
- Tier: workflow integration, because the contract crosses trigger selection, overlay batch dispatch, merge, verifier routing, usage, and sidecar dependency capture.
- Oracle: exact tool-name sets per request, distinct receipt/query-session ids across passes, resolved sibling evidence, and changed dependency digest after editing a read file.
- Negative controls: an equivalent `.py` diff and a Terraform diff with no IaC finding leave base/other overlays/verifier/coach tool-free.
- CI: `make test`.

## Verification

`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`
baseline.summary: Ground code-review IaC findings in changed Terraform modules

## Why
Collapse the reviewer-centric model into the unified prompt model: reviewers become a SUBSET of prompts; the catalog becomes a generated derived index. Validated by spike E5.

## What
- Migrate the 6 reviewers' `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/catalog.json` metadata into per-file front-matter
  using S2's writer (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`).
- Introduce a NEW unified resolver `get_prompt(prompt_id: str) -> Prompt` in `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` to replace `get_reviewer`. NAMESPACE (verified): `resolve_prompt(reviewer, variables, langfuse)` ALREADY EXISTS as the template-render step (RETAINED; adapted to accept the unified `Prompt`) and `load_prompt` ALREADY EXISTS — so the new resolver is `get_prompt`, NOT `resolve_prompt`/`load_prompt`. Signature:
  `get_prompt(prompt_id: str) -> Prompt` where `Prompt` exposes `{id, text, inputs, outputs,
  execution_mode, category, is_reviewer, dimension, applies_to}`; it raises `PromptNotFound` for an
  unknown id. Resolution order: project `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override > built-in packaged. Reviewer
  membership is EXPLICIT (`category: review` / reviewer flag), NEVER inferred from output-schema shape.
  MIGRATE the sole consumer `runs.py:RunnerAgentStep.run()` (calls `get_reviewer` at ~line 130) to
  `get_prompt` (then call the existing `resolve_prompt` render-step with the resulting `Prompt`); remove `get_reviewer`.
- Build the GENERATED + COMMITTED derived-index (scan front-matter -> index) enforcing invariants
  (exactly-one default; no `dimension` collision; preserve `langfuse_prompt`/`fallback_file`/
  `applies_to`). A RETIRE path: a removed prompt is dropped from the index on regeneration. Add a CI
  drift gate (`regenerate + git diff --exit-code`) in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. `applies_to` keeps
  stdlib `fnmatch`.

## Scope
In: migration + resolver(+removal) + index(+retire) + CI gate + regression-equivalence. Out: prompt CONTRACTS in the runner (S4), editor library (S6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The 6 reviewers carry front-matter; `get_prompt(id)` resolves project>built-in and returns the unified `Prompt`; reviewer flag explicit.
- [ ] `get_reviewer` is REMOVED, `catalog.json` is removed/fully-derived, and a grep confirms no remaining `get_reviewer` callers (caller migration complete).
- [ ] Derived index generated+committed; invariants enforced (two-default AND dimension-collision rejections both tested); a removed prompt is retired from the index; CI drift gate fails on a stale index.
- [ ] Existing reviewer behavior preserved (resolution/default/applies_to routing) — equivalence regression tests green.
- [ ] The new unified resolver is `get_prompt(prompt_id) -> Prompt` (NOT `resolve_prompt`/`load_prompt`, which already exist); the existing `resolve_prompt(reviewer,variables,langfuse)` render-step coexists with no name clash; `get_reviewer` is removed and grep-clean.
- [ ] Migration stamps `execution_mode` on EVERY migrated prompt (default `agentic`), so no migrated prompt relies on an implicit default.
baseline.summary: Reviewer->prompt migration + resolver generalization + derived-index lockfile

# Hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass the model-class config and go to direct Anthropic

## Scope: FOUR sites, one root cause, THREE take the class fix

Each builds a `RunRequest` by hand with `config=cfg` and declares no model class, so it inherits `cfg.model` regardless of how the three model classes are configured. MEASURED, not inferred — see the comments for the full experiment:

    llm/overlap/judge.py:46              op=overlap-judge    18 calls   <-- 18 of 23 in a plan review
    llm/enrich.py:81                     op=ticket-digest     1 call    <-- runs on the STORE WRITE path
    llm/operations.py:177                op=ticket-quality    1 call
    llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:571  op=code-novelty      1 call    <-- the site originally filed

Everything else honours the configuration: all four plan-review passes, the completion verifier, and all seven code-review workflow steps.

## Why this matters beyond consistency

Bedrock is normally chosen for data-residency, procurement or contractual reasons. These calls send real content to direct Anthropic: the diff and prior findings (`code-novelty`), ticket text (`ticket-digest`, `ticket-quality`), and ticket digests for pairwise comparison (`overlap-judge`).

**`overlap-judge` dominates plan-review traffic** — 18 of 23 calls. An operator who cuts over by configuring the three classes (the documented mechanism, and the one story eb6e will use) leaves the MAJORITY of plan-review traffic on direct Anthropic.

**`ticket-digest` is the most insidious** because it is not in a gate at all: `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` is called from `_store/event_append.py:609` and `_store/push.py:295`, so it runs on the ticket STORE WRITE path — on ordinary `rebar comment` / `rebar create` calls, with no gate invocation and nothing in any verdict to reveal it.

## The two configurations, and why both are needed

* classes on Bedrock, `cfg.model` left bare-anthropic → PRE-FIX, all four sites above show `anthropic`: they
  bypass the class config. This is the defect.
* classes AND `cfg.model` on Bedrock → 15 calls, 0 on anthropic: nothing is HARDCODED past config.

The second configuration passes even with this bug unfixed, because a bypassing call inherits `cfg.model`. Any regression test must therefore pin the FIRST configuration, or it proves nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with a model-class table configured to values that DIFFER from `cfg.model`, no hand-built
      SUB-CALL in review-plan, review-code or verify-completion resolves to `cfg.model` — verified
      IN-SESSION by `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`, which configures exactly such a
      table (the only configuration in which "honoured the class" and "fell through to cfg.model"
      are distinguishable strings — with no table configured both resolve to the same default and
      the observation carries no information) and asserts, per site, the model that reaches the
      runner. The two TOP-LEVEL one-call ops (`operations.py::review_ticket`,
      `spec_scan.py::_scan_epics_inner`) are EXCLUDED by design and registered in
      `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN`. Reframed from "asserted from a live run's usage log": the property is
      a durable invariant of the code, so it belongs in a test that fails the day a new bypassing
      sub-call is written, not in a one-off credentialed run that cannot be re-checked.
- [ ] each of the THREE hand-built sub-call sites selects its model from the class
      vocabulary, and the class chosen for each is stated in the code with its reason rather
      than left implicit: `enrich.py` (ticket-digest) -> trivial, `overlap/judge.py`
      (overlap-judge) -> standard, `code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty`
      (code-novelty) -> standard. The fourth site originally in scope,
      `operations.py::review_ticket`, is DELIBERATELY left on `cfg.model` and registered in
      `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` with that reason: it is a top-level op's single LLM call, so
      there are no passes to differentiate and the operator's configured model is the right
      knob. Narrowed from "four sites" after the operator decision that one-call top-level
      ops keep `cfg.model`; the code was already correct and the criterion was stale.
- [ ] `code-novelty`'s choice is consistent with plan-review's novelty sub-call, or the difference is
      documented as deliberate at both sites — `score_code_novelty`'s docstring currently claims it
      "mirrors" `_score_floor_novelty`, which uses `_verifier_cfg`, and that parity does not hold
- [ ] a test fails if ANY hand-built sub-call inherits `cfg.model` while a class table is configured
      — the general defect, so a future hand-built sub-call cannot silently reintroduce it. A test
      that enumerates today's four sites by name does NOT satisfy this
- [ ] the `overlap-judge` test constructs its trigger deliberately: `wire.py:overlap_findings` runs
      the judge only when BM25F retrieval returns candidates (`if not candidates: return []`, with
      the query's own graph excluded), so a test that merely runs a gate and hopes the judge fires
      will silently pass while testing nothing — both probes during the investigation hit exactly
      that and produced zero judge calls
- [ ] `ticket-digest`'s fix holds on the STORE WRITE path, not only inside a gate run
- [ ] fail-safe behaviour is preserved at every site: the novelty signal must still degrade to
      "keep more findings", and the overlap step must remain advisory and never block a review

## Not in scope

Sibling `03b0` (a configured Bedrock provider is dropped for colon-bearing model ids) is a different seam — that one breaks the configuration before it is read; this one ignores it after.
baseline.summary: Hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass the model-class config and go to direct Anthropic (4 sites; overlap-judge is 18 of 23 plan-review calls)

## Context / Problem

`inbound_probe.py` is wholly Jira-specific code living in the backend-neutral core: it builds the Jira REST URL shape (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}?fields=status,resolution`), sends a basic-auth GET, resolves `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN` via `adapters.jira.acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings()` (`inbound_probe.py:65-77`), and classifies by Jira status names (`RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = {"Resolved","Done","Cancelled"}`). It is called from `run_differs.py:369`, and its result vocabulary is consumed *neutrally* by `reconcile_helpers.route_inbound_probe` (`reconcile_helpers.py:291-355`). A second backend would need an entirely different probe, but there is no seam. Epic bbf1 AC3 requires zero `adapters.jira` imports in core.

## Approach

Split vocabulary from vendor mechanics:

- The neutral vocabulary — `ProbeBranch` (4 branches), `ProbeResult`, `ProbeConfigError` —
  stays in root `inbound_probe.py`. The file must remain at the package root: it is
  location-pinned (ADR 0035 context list) and loaded by filename at
  `reconcile_helpers.py:317` (`_load("inbound_probe", "inbound_probe.py")`).
- The Jira mechanics (URL construction, basic-auth GET, GET-only invariant, status-name
  classification, JIRA_* env resolution) move to a new `adapters/jira/probe.py`.
- A new `@runtime_checkable` capability Protocol `SupportsAbsenceProbe` in `_backend.py` with
  `probe_remote(remote_id: str) -> Any` (return documented as `inbound_probe.ProbeResult`;
  `_backend.py` stays a pure stdlib+typing interface module, consistent with its existing
  loosely-typed `dict[str, Any]` style, so it does not import the vocabulary module).
  `JiraBackend` implements it by delegating to `adapters/jira/probe.py`.
- `run_differs.py:369` routes through the backend: `isinstance(backend, SupportsAbsenceProbe)`
  guarded, matching the existing capability pattern (`SupportsLinks`/`SupportsComments`/
  `SupportsIncremental` in `_backend.py`). Wiring: today the backend is loaded at
  `run_differs.py:234` — AFTER the probe dispatch call at `:230` — so the
  `_load_reconcile_backend()` call (`run_differs.py:62-75`, a pure registry/config load with
  no remote side effects) is hoisted above the probe dispatch, and the backend object is
  passed into `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` as a new `backend` parameter, replacing
  that function's direct `probe_mod.probe(...)` call at `:369`. The later load site reuses
  the already-loaded instance. A backend without the capability yields
  `ProbeResult(UNREACHABLE)` — the conservative "do not classify, leave for retry" branch
  that `route_inbound_probe` already handles (`reconcile_helpers.py:351`).
- Extend the AST neutrality gate to assert zero `adapters.jira` imports in
  `inbound_probe.py`.

Rejected alternative: injecting url/user/token through scalar port accessors and keeping the GET + classification in core — that leaves the vendor REST URL shape and Jira status-name classification in neutral code, so a second backend still could not drop in; the port must own the whole probe as a capability.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (SupportsAbsenceProbe capability)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_probe.py (reduced to neutral vocabulary)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/probe.py (new: Jira GET + classification)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (implement probe_remote)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py (capability-guarded routing at the probe call site)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py (NEW adapter classification tests; the old test_inbound_probe.py is DELETED, its classification coverage migrated here)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py (new: the capability-routing tests — backend-with-capability runtime proof, capability-lacking UNREACHABLE degradation)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (AST gate extended to inbound_probe.py)

## Testing

- Happy path: 200 + resolved status → PRESENT_RESOLVED; 200 + other status →
  PRESENT_FILTERED (now exercised against `adapters/jira/probe.py`).
- Failure/edge: 404/410/403 → ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED; 5xx/401/timeout/URLError → UNREACHABLE;
  missing JIRA_* env → ProbeConfigError naming the missing vars; GET-only invariant asserted
  in the adapter.
- Capability routing (new file
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py`): with a FakeBackend
  implementing SupportsAbsenceProbe, run_differs uses the backend's probe (runtime proof);
  with a FakeBackend lacking it, the mutation is classified UNREACHABLE and left for retry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inbound_probe.py` contains NO `adapters.jira` import and no vendor REST code (URL
      shape, auth, status-name classification all live under `adapters/jira/probe.py`) —
      verified by the extended AST case in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` plus code review.
- [ ] `run_differs` reaches the probe only through `SupportsAbsenceProbe`; a
      capability-lacking backend degrades to UNREACHABLE — verified by the routing tests in
      Testing.
- [ ] Probe classification behavior is byte-identical for Jira (all branches) — verified by
      the migrated probe tests.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 927 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Vendor absence probe behind a SupportsAbsenceProbe capability (relocate Jira REST probe into adapters/jira/)

# Mutation gate has no "change predates the gate" guard, so it hard-fails older changes

The bounded mutation gate runs its reusable workflow from `refs/heads/main` but executes it against the CHECKED-OUT PATCHSET tree. When a change is based on a commit older than the one that introduced `scripts/mutation_gate.py`, the script is absent from that tree and the step dies:

    /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/.venv/bin/python3: can't open file
    '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/mutation_gate.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

The result is a `Verified -1` that says nothing about the change's own quality.

## Evidence

Two consecutive runs, both failing pre-analysis, on changes based on `c0bb6dcc` (which predates the walking-skeleton commit `57d19254` that added the script):

- change 1621 patchset 1 — run 31561319537, job 94004044... exit code 2
- change 1624 patchset 1 — run 31561579063, job 94005317237, exit code 2

On 1624 the checkout step itself SUCCEEDED ("Checkout the Gerrit patchset ✓"); the failure is in "Run changed mutation shards", so this is not a fetch race. It is deterministic for any change whose base predates the script.

## Why this is the gate's bug, not the author's

Every sibling gate in the same workflow already guards for exactly this, and skips with an explanatory message rather than failing. For example the env-var registry gate:

    if [ ! -f scripts/gen_env_registry.py ]; then
      echo "scripts/gen_env_registry.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) \
    — skipping; the gate re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change"
      exit 0
    fi

`scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` carries the same guard. The mutation gate is the only one missing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The mutation gate skips cleanly (exit 0, explanatory message) when
      `scripts/mutation_gate.py` is absent from the checked-out tree, matching the wording
      and behaviour of the sibling gates.
- [x] A change based before the walking-skeleton commit gets no `Verified -1` from this
      gate.
- [x] A change based at or after it still runs the gate for real — the skip must not
      become a silent bypass on current changes.

## Workaround

Rebase the change onto current `origin/main`; the script then exists and the gate runs (and correctly reports "no protected shard selected" for changes touching no shard).

## Provenance

Hit twice while landing the build-drift warning (`tasty-unappeased-leopard`, b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c). Filed at operator direction so the mutation-testing work has the signal.
baseline.summary: Mutation gate hard-fails changes that predate its own script

baseline.description: Detect a clone whose last convergence with the remote exceeds the N-day horizon and force it to override local state with remote on reconnect (rather than reintroducing pre-compaction events by rebase). This converts the remote-anchored horizon from probabilistic to enforced (closes the I1 hole). Accepted cost: discards the stale clone's divergent local work. Independently verifiable: a simulated >N-day-stale clone is overridden, not merged.
baseline.summary: Stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect

## Context / Problem

`rebar link <a> <b> depends_on` can silently record a different edge than the one requested, and can produce an edge in which a ticket blocks its own subtree. Bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 hit this while wiring epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864's dependency graph: an epic ended up `depends_on` its own child, the requested child-level dependency was never recorded at all, and the operator had to retype children and hand-unlink the bad edge. Self-blocking edges distort `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade, so parallel agents are handed a wrong work order.

The cause is a policy defect rather than a coding slip. `resolve_hierarchy_link` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:98`) decides "comparable level" for blocking links from the ticket's TYPE TIER (`_TYPE_TIER`, `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:26`) instead of from its position in the parent hierarchy. Bug jira-reb-1582 names the correct rule directly: comparability is structural, and any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency. This story supersedes both bugs and replaces the policy.

## Approach

Replace type-tier comparability with structural (nearest-common-ancestor) comparability; add a resolved-pair invariant that makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable regardless of how the edge was produced; then detect and repair the edges already written under the old rule.

Rejected alternative — keep the type tiers and special-case the failing shape by clamping promotion below the nearest common ancestor. That removes 1803's specific symptom but leaves comparability keyed on a ticket's *type*, so a task and a story that are genuine siblings still could not hold a direct dependency, and re-typing a ticket would silently rewrite the meaning of the dependency graph. jira-reb-1582 asks for the rule itself to change; patching the fallback at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:93` would leave the store's semantics wrong in the same way.

Rejected alternative — reject cross-subtree blocking links with an error instead of escalating them. Honest, but it breaks every caller relying on auto-escalation today, including the `link` MCP tool and the reconciler's inbound apply path (`rebar.link` at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502`). Escalation is retained, and its existing machine-readable redirect record (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`) is kept unchanged. Note it is NOT uniformly visible: `add_dependency` prints it to stdout, which the CLI surfaces, but the library facade `rebar.link()` calls `composer.link_core(..., quiet=True)` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615`), and `quiet` redirects stdout/stderr into a `StringIO` sink (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:628`) — so library and MCP callers have the record DISCARDED and see a silent substitution. That predates this story and is not changed by it, but it is the same silence bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 complained about, still present on the MCP path; recorded as follow-up on the doctor epics rather than fixed here.

## Success Criteria

- The blocking-link resolver decides comparability from the parent hierarchy alone; `_TYPE_TIER` no longer participates in that decision.
- No blocking edge can exist between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant, by any path into the resolver.
- Blocking edges already written under the type-tier rule are detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass.
- The escalation contract callers depend on — auto-escalate a cross-subtree link, emit the redirect record — is unchanged.

## Decomposition

Two children, in dependency order:

1. **Structural comparability and the ancestor invariant** (leaf) — rewrites the resolver in `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` and moves the redundancy guard in `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` onto the resolved pair. This is the fix for both superseded bugs.
2. **`doctor` detection and repair** (leaf, shipped as the first check of `rebar doctor`) — a store-wide scan plus one-shot repair for edges written under the old rule. It declares `depends_on` child 1, because the repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver and cannot be written before those semantics are final.

The split follows the deliverable seam: child 1 changes what a new link means, child 2 fixes data already on disk. Each lands as one reviewable change. Neither is large enough to split further, and combining them would put a store-wide data rewrite in the same change as the semantics that rewrite depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The repro from bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 (a task and a story that are both direct children of one epic) records the requested task-to-story edge unchanged and produces no epic-to-child edge; verified by the regression test added in child 1, run against the store fixture.
- [ ] The worked example from bug jira-reb-1582 resolves as that ticket specifies — Task D under Story C escalates to Story C when linked to Task B, while Task B to Story C records directly; verified by the regression test added in child 1.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar doctor` against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling; verified by listing each remaining finding's BLOCKED side (the source for `depends_on`, the target for `blocks`) and attesting on this ticket that every one is `closed`, since a closed blocked-side can never appear in `ready` or `next-batch`. Attested rather than asserted in-repo because it is a statement about live tracker state at a point in time, and the pre-repair count cannot be reconstructed from the post-repair store.
- [ ] Both children are closed, each with its Gerrit change at `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`; verified by the change status in Gerrit before each close.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/scripts/graph/` all pass; verified by running them in the worktree.
baseline.summary: Resolve blocking-link comparability structurally, forbid ancestor self-blocks, and repair existing edges

# `_llm_float` is invisible to the env-var registry scanner: 4 undocumented env vars

## Context / Problem
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py` generates `docs/env-vars.md` from env-var reads under `src/rebar`, and a CI drift gate fails the build when the committed doc disagrees (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:314`). The generator recognises a read only when the callee is a KNOWN helper AND the name argument is a STRING LITERAL (`gen_env_registry.py:117-124`); `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` at `:37-47` registers `"_llm_str": (2, "")` and `"_llm_int": (2, "")`.

**`_llm_float` is NOT registered.** So every env var read through it is silently absent from the generated registry. MEASURED by running the generator: `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE` (`llm/config.py:651`), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ` (`:692`), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` (`:699`) and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` (`:720`) are all real, settable, operator-facing knobs and NONE appears in `docs/env-vars.md`.

This is exactly the bug class the registry exists to prevent, and the gate is currently GREEN while incomplete — a clean `--check` is therefore not evidence of completeness. `_llm_float` is defined at `llm/config.py:459-476` alongside `_llm_str` (`:426-436`) and `_llm_int` (`:439-456`); the omission is an oversight, not a decision.

## Approach
Add `"_llm_float": (2, "")` to `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` and regenerate `docs/env-vars.md`.

Land this BEFORE any structural change to `config.py`, so the derived-doc diff caused by fixing the scanner is not tangled with the diff caused by moving code. That keeps both changes reviewable.

**Also close the hole that let this hide:** the existing test `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` asserts one specific var is statically visible to the generator. Generalize the idea — assert that the helper registry covers every `_llm_*` resolver defined in `llm/config.py`, so adding a fifth resolver without registering it fails a test rather than silently dropping knobs from the docs.

## Scope
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` — one entry in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated, not hand-edited.
- `tests/unit/` — the completeness assertion.

## Testing
- a test asserts each of the four named vars appears in the generated registry (fails today).
- a test asserts every `_llm_*` helper defined in `llm/config.py` is present in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`,
  so the next resolver cannot be added unregistered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ`,
      `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` are all present in
      the generated env registry. This criterion FAILS against the current implementation
- [ ] a test asserts every `_llm_*` resolver defined in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is registered in
      `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`, so an unregistered future resolver is caught
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean and `docs/env-vars.md` is committed
      as generated output
baseline.summary: _llm_float is invisible to the env-var registry scanner: 4 undocumented env vars

## Context / Problem

The S3 ticket-store backend (parent epic) is only usable if operators can discover the optional dependency and configure S3 from the docs alone — today `docs/config.md` documents `sync.remote` (line ~128) and `tracker.branch` (line ~154) only for the GitHub/git case, and nothing names the `git-remote-s3` dependency, the SSE-KMS bucket setup, or the auto-doctor behavior. This story documents the feature and records the architecture decision. It is documentation-only; the code lands in the sibling stories.

## Approach

1. **`docs/config.md`** — under the `sync` section, document that `sync.remote` may point at a
   git remote whose URL is `s3://bucket/prefix` (or `s3+zip://`), served by the optional
   `git-remote-s3` helper, and that this keeps ticket history entirely out of GitHub. Cross-
   link the new backend page.
2. **New `docs/s3-backend.md`** — the operator guide: (a) install the optional dependency
   (`pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`, minimum `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2`); (b) create the SSE-KMS bucket
   (default encryption with a customer CMK, versioning on, public-access-block on) and the
   IAM policy scoped to the bucket + CMK; (c) add the git remote (`git remote add <name>
   s3://bucket/prefix`) and set `sync.remote` to it; (d) the **trust boundary**: AWS
   credentials come from the standard boto3 chain (never stored in rebar config or events),
   data at rest is SSE-KMS in the customer bucket, S3 access is IAM/SigV4 (no anonymous
   access); (e) operational behavior: the non-interactive auto-doctor self-heals a
   multiple-bundles state by merge (no data loss), and a stale lock self-heals during the next
   push's lock acquisition (git-remote-s3 v0.3.2 `remote.py` `acquire_lock` deletes a lock older
   than the TTL and re-acquires in the same call; a manual `git-remote-s3 doctor --lock-ttl`
   path also exists per `remote.py:236-237`). The TTL is `DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS`
   = 60s (`remote.py:45`), overridable via the `GIT_REMOTE_S3_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS` env var — a
   rare, bounded delay we intentionally do not lower. Primary-source verified against the v0.3.2
   release tarball (tag `v0.3.2` = commit `9f3290e1f19090a9c11ae5b8c01ec8abe6184ab9`):
   `git_remote_s3/remote.py:95` reads `os.environ.get("GIT_REMOTE_S3_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS",
   DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS)`, and the string `GIT_REMOTE_S3_LOCK_TTL` (no `_SECONDS`) appears
   ONLY in upstream's README, in NO `.py` file of the release — so the code does not honor it.
   The docs use — and flag — the `_SECONDS` form the code actually reads, with a "verify against
   your installed version" note to remove any mislead hazard.
3. **New `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md`** — record the decision: use
   `awslabs/git-remote-s3` (Apache-2.0, maintained) below rebar's shell-out git layer so the
   event/data format is unchanged; SSE-KMS (not client-side) is acceptable per requirements;
   the multi-bundle risk is handled by a rebar merge-based auto-doctor because upstream's
   `git-s3 doctor` is interactive and discards a head; lowering the lock TTL was rejected.
   Follow the format of an existing ADR (e.g. `docs/adr/0091-*`); 0093 is the next free number
   (highest existing is 0091). **An ADR is not a standalone file:** after writing the prose file
   run `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py`, which (a) creates the per-number marker
   `docs/adr/.numbers/0093` (content = the ADR filename — the add/add-conflict uniqueness
   mechanism) and (b) regenerates the GENERATED, do-not-hand-edit index `docs/adr/README.md`
   (the new ADR sorts into the "Other decisions" fallback group, since its slug matches no
   workstream keyword). CI enforces both: `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` asserts the
   number↔file bijection and that no ADR cross-reference dangles, and `gen_adr_index.py --check`
   fails if the committed marker/index drift from a regeneration. Commit the ADR file, its
   `.numbers/0093` marker, and the regenerated `README.md` together, and ensure every link in
   the ADR resolves (no dangling target).
4. **`docs/README.md`** (docs index) and, if it lists extras, a one-line pointer — link the
   new backend page and ADR so they are discoverable.

Rationale: a dedicated backend page plus an ADR matches how rebar already documents optional capabilities and architecture decisions (the `docs/adr/` series), giving operators a single configuration entry point and preserving the decision record the maintainability criterion expects; keeping it docs-only avoids coupling the write-up to any one code story's landing.

## Scope

- `docs/config.md` — extend the `sync.remote` documentation for the `s3://` case.
- `docs/s3-backend.md` — new operator guide (install, bucket/KMS/IAM, config, trust
  boundary, self-heal behavior).
- `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md` — new ADR (prose file).
- `docs/adr/.numbers/0093` — new per-number marker (generated by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py`).
- `docs/adr/README.md` — regenerated ADR index (generated; not hand-edited).
- `docs/README.md` — add index links to the two new pages.

No source, schema, or test changes. Running `scripts/gen_adr_index.py` (a repo-provided generator) to produce the two derived ADR artifacts above is part of the mechanical ADR-add procedure, not a code change to the generator itself.

## Testing

Documentation-only; no automated test tier applies (mechanical prose changes, consistent with how other `docs/` and ADR changes land). Validation is by review against the acceptance checks below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/config.md` documents that `sync.remote` accepts an `s3://bucket/prefix` remote
      served by the optional `git-remote-s3` helper and links `docs/s3-backend.md`. Verified
      by the section being present and cross-linked.
- [x] `docs/s3-backend.md` exists and contains all five subsections: install (naming
      `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'` and the `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2` minimum), SSE-KMS bucket + IAM/CMK
      setup, remote + `sync.remote` configuration, the credentials/encryption trust boundary,
      and the auto-doctor + 60s stale-lock self-heal behavior. Verified by the named
      subsections being present.
- [x] `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md` exists, follows the existing ADR format, and
      records the git-remote-s3 choice, SSE-KMS decision, the merge-based auto-doctor
      rationale (vs upstream's interactive/discarding doctor), and the rejected TTL-lowering.
      Its per-number marker `docs/adr/.numbers/0093` and the regenerated `docs/adr/README.md`
      are committed, and `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` + `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`
      both pass (bijection holds, no dangling ADR cross-reference). Verified by the ADR sections
      being present and both ADR gates green in CI.
- [x] Both new pages are discoverable from the docs index (`docs/README.md`): the operator
      guide `docs/s3-backend.md` is linked directly, and ADR 0093 is discoverable via the
      project's standard ADR path — `docs/README.md` links the `adr/` directory, whose
      generated index `docs/adr/README.md` lists `0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md`. Per repo
      convention individual ADRs are indexed through the generated ADR index, not linked
      one-by-one from `docs/README.md`. Verified by the links being present.

--- **Delivery note (landing-time deviation):** ADR number bumped from the planned 0092 to **0093** because ADR 0092 was claimed on `main` at landing time by `0092-bridge-primary-vocabulary-compatibility-adapters.md`. The plan's intent ("next free ADR number") is preserved; only the concrete number changed. Delivered as `docs/adr/0093-s3-ticket-store-backend.md` + `.numbers/0093`, regenerated `docs/adr/README.md`. Merged as Gerrit change 1552 (LLM-Review+1, Verified+1), commit b7d29e58c7.
baseline.summary: Document the optional S3 dependency, S3/SSE-KMS configuration, and the backend ADR

## Context / Problem
Completion verification currently materializes the full Git-backed ticket store although a run reads only a small subset. Close traces attributed 135-235 seconds to this phase. Approved research on `shaven-censorable-sifaka` measured the real store: tracker-OID capture was 9.5 ms p50, tree/object reads about 11 ms p50, and fetching plus uncached reduction of one real ticket was 29.156 ms for 10 files / 62,426 bytes with exact state-hash parity. Revision A stayed byte-identical after a normal rebar write advanced the live tracker to B.

The close path also publishes PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT`, closing `STATUS`, and completion `SIGNATURE` through separate writes. A durable PASS can outlive a failed close, and a closed ticket can outlive a failed signature. We need one stable read basis and one atomic publication boundary.

## Contract
- `code_oid` is resolved once from `--ref`; `tickets_oid` independently identifies tracker state. Typed interfaces must prevent swapping them.
- The ticket view reads Git objects lazily at `tickets_oid`, never falls back to live state, and never writes caches inside the view.
- The read receipt records exact tickets, negative reads, direct-child membership, transitive descendants, inbound/outbound relations and consulted reachability, plus global resolver inputs such as `.bridge_state/bindings.json`.
- Atomic means one committed-store transaction contains PASS sidecar, closed STATUS, and completion SIGNATURE, or none is committed and HEAD/index/worktree return to their prior state. OID-pinned readers see the complete old or complete new commit.

## Plan
1. Add a pinned-ticket reader backed by `ls-tree`, batched `cat-file`, and the existing uncached reducer input seam. Resolve arbitrary IDs/aliases/Jira bindings at `tickets_oid`; record not-found as a negative read. Put derived resolver/graph indexes outside the immutable tree and key them by tracker OID plus schema version. Unsupported broad queries fail closed.
2. Thread this view through completion context assembly, deterministic ticket checks, and agent ticket tools. Keep code reads on the separate code snapshot. Bug `shimmery-customary-dorking` will experimentally test the suspected live-code gap; this story preserves typed separation without assuming that hypothesis is true.
3. Before mutation, validate the receipt from A against current descendant Tn. Reject non-ancestor history. Diff changed ticket/global paths and recompute affected predicates at both endpoints. Unrelated changes may continue; an exact, hierarchy, link, negative, or resolver conflict discards the verdict and restarts at Tn.
4. Outside the write lock, prepare the verdict, receipt digest, completion certificate payload, event UUIDs, and all work not requiring final HLC order. Each run owns `(run_id, code_oid, tickets_oid, receipt_digest)` and unique temporary paths.
5. Extend the status transaction to accept three prepared close events. Inside the lock, assert tracker HEAD still equals validated Tn and root status remains `in_progress`; finalize HLC/parent linkage/authorship, stage all three, and make one local Git commit. Any signing, staging, index, or commit fault rolls back only this bundle and restores pre-operation state. Preserve reducer/event compatibility.
6. Release the lock before ordinary fast-forward push. On rejection, fetch and revalidate: rebuild/retry an unrelated delta or restart verification for a relevant delta. Never force a ref update or push. A same-ticket race is idempotent only when the existing close binds an equivalent code OID, receipt, and attestation; a loser leaves no PASS sidecar.
7. Measure ticket-OID capture, lazy reads/reduction, receipt validation, bundle preparation, lock wait/hold, local commit, and push/retry. Metrics add only constant-time timestamps inside the lock. Document the receipt vocabulary, atomicity boundary, retries, rollout, and separate code/ticket revisions.

## Rollout / Back-out
Put the new completion path behind one configuration switch and retain the legacy path as an explicit operator back-out during dogfooding. Selection is fixed and recorded at operation start; a run never silently falls back after capturing `tickets_oid`. Default enablement is separate and evidence-based. The mechanism is in-process and CI-provider-independent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Given tracker A and later normal write B, a run pinned to A returns byte/state-identical ticket reads while live writes continue, without materializing the full ticket tree.
- [x] Any ticket requested at runtime loads from A and extends the receipt; missing returns not-found-at-A plus a negative dependency, never live fallback.
- [x] Direct/transitive hierarchy and inbound/outbound relation predicates invalidate on relevant create/remove/reparent/relink changes; a proven unrelated mutation remains valid.
- [x] Alias/Jira/global binding resolution is pinned to A; relevant binding changes invalidate. Unsupported queries fail closed.
- [x] Completion code evidence remains bound to separately resolved `code_oid`; tests reject swapped code/ticket roots.
- [x] LLM work, lazy reads, receipt validation, preparation, and push occur outside the write lock. Only final HEAD/status assertions, ordering/signing, staging, and one commit are inside; wait/hold are measured.
- [x] A successful close creates exactly one local commit containing PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT`, `STATUS in_progress -> closed`, and completion `SIGNATURE`, all bound to one run/code/receipt identity.
- [x] Fault injection at signing, staging, index, and commit boundaries leaves prior HEAD/status and no committed sidecar/signature; retry creates at most one equivalent bundle.
- [x] Two parallel reviews cannot publish mixed artifacts: one wins; the loser recognizes an equivalent close or restarts without leaving PASS. Unrelated reviews may both commit after revalidation.
- [x] Non-ancestor state, relevant receipt drift, and remote fast-forward rejection fail closed without force; unrelated descendant deltas can revalidate/retry.
- [x] Derived caches are OID/schema-keyed with per-run temporaries and do not write inside the pinned view.
- [x] Focused lazy-read parity, hierarchy/link phantom, negative-read, resolver, cross-process concurrency, and rollback tests pass in CI, followed by project lint, typecheck, and test gates.
- [x] Documentation covers the stable-read contract, full receipt vocabulary, committed-store atomicity, rollout/back-out, remote-writer limitation, and metric phases.

## Out of Scope
- Replacing Git or reducing the lock to `git update-ref` while the mutable checkout remains authoritative.
- Acting on either unproven bug (`shimmery-customary-dorking`, `lineny-barathea-ladybug`) before its experiment.
- Setting a lock-duration SLO before instrumentation produces a distribution.
baseline.summary: Use a lazy pinned ticket view and atomically publish completion-close artifacts

## Context / Problem
Source comments carry commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot: 8 of 18 cited SHAs in the tree are ALREADY unresolvable (Gerrit rebase-on-submit guarantees pre-land SHA death), and run IDs die with retention windows. Policy: source is for current state + concise rationale; the ticket system owns historical detail. The detector is NET-NEW code (the prototype that produced the corpus numbers ran in the planning session and was not committed; its measured results — 0 FPs, 15 violating sites, 47 compliant blocks on the then-current tree — are recorded here as design evidence, and the corpus is re-derived by running the new detector at the implementation worktree's HEAD, which is authoritative; the ticket comment records census drift to 16 sites already).

## Approach
(1) Remediate every detector hit at HEAD (17 pinned above as-of-plan: the original 15 census sites, of which 2 were later found under src/ in the PR-375 bucket, plus 3 post-plan RUN-id sites minus overlap) — each maps to a specific replacement already adjudicated: delete.py:188 drop dead-SHA mechanism sentence; classify.py:310 + test_frozen_census.py:79 cite epic 3006-e198; reconcile.py:588 + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_commit_binding_store_failure.py:10 (module docstring's 'cf93b2b7ad failure class') describe the failure class in behavioral terms (story findable via git log -S); test_ci_actionlint_install.py cite bug 4e99-b2ae; test_plan_review_explain.py:308 (docstring narrates 'the class of bug `62933ff62` fixed for plan-review deep-links' — a raw dead SHA) drop the SHA and cite bug c7e3-dd16; test_execution_mode_dispatch.py cite 454a-9266; test_inbound_differ_field_contract.py point at the live CONTRACT block + story a130-2b7c; 7 PR-#375 sites keep 'PR #375 review' and drop raw thread ids (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py:63/69/210/310/451 + src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/typed_dispatch.py:128 + src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py:233); test_at_most_one_invariant.py:199 drop e04e0b289c; 3 RUN-id sites from the post-plan J11/5200 work (tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py:163/1638-context + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_assignee_oracle_discriminates_5200.py:20-context, runs 30721408463/30763838558) get the same treatment — narrative to a ticket, cite the ticket. Line numbers are as-of-plan pins; the re-run detector census at HEAD is the authoritative remediation list and may add/retire sites (same adjudicated replacement rules apply). (2) CI guard (detector is NET-NEW per Context; prior art/reuse: it follows the repo's scripts/check_*.py guard convention — check()/main() shape, wired as a named step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml like check_verify_gate_parity.py — landing as scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py): block-level scan (comment blocks + AST docstrings); rot-prone = SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc), run/job/thread id >=8 digits after keyword, date+evidence-verb — defined as: a date token (YYYY-MM-DD or 'Month DD, YYYY') in the same block as a past-tense incident verb from the ENUMERATED set {failed, broke, regressed, fixed, caught, observed, hit, crashed, flaked} (the block narrates a dated incident); 'surfaced' is deliberately EXCLUDED from the verb set — the prototype's 'bug surfaced' FP introduces current-state explanation, not an incident date, and must not trigger. Acceptor interaction: triggers are evaluated first, then a triggered block is ACCEPTED iff it cites a qualifying id — the gotcha cases must not trigger at all (they never reach the acceptor); ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id — hex-grouped (4x4 like 3006-e198-…) or word-triple alias (three lowercase hyphen-joined dictionary words, e.g. robe-creek-zealot, the store's human alias form) — pointing history at the ticket system is the sanctioned pattern; escape hatch 'context: external' for vendor-pinned refs (changelogs, upstream issue SHAs). Self-exclusion (sibling-guard convention): the detector's own unit-test module (tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py, whose fixtures MUST contain live rot-prone tokens as RED/gotcha cases) is excluded from the tree scan by an EXCLUDED_FILES tuple in the script — the same mechanism check_criteria_vocabulary.py uses (scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:38); fixtures live only in that one excluded module, so 'zero suppressions' means zero IN-TREE escape-hatch uses, with the single structural exclusion visible at the top of the script.

## Scope
- the detector-hit sites listed above (src/ + tests/; authoritative list = detector re-run at HEAD)
- scripts/ or CI lint module implementing the detector + workflow wiring
- short policy note in CONTRIBUTING.md or docs (source=current state, tickets=history)

## Testing
Detector unit tests re-derived at HEAD (prototype-measured shape: ~15-17 pre-fix sites RED, ~47 compliant blocks green — exact counts pinned when the detector lands), the acceptor-arm gotchas ('bug surfaced', 'ticket dirs' must NOT accept; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases MUST accept), escape hatch honored. Post-remediation tree scans clean.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All detector-hit sites at HEAD remediated, each in one of three sanctioned forms: (a) cites a ticket/epic/story/bug id that RESOLVES in the ticket system (spot-check via rebar show), (b) drops the rot-prone token leaving durable current-state prose (PR-#375 bucket keeps 'PR #375 review', drops raw thread ids), or (c) replaces a SHA narrative with a behavioral description findable via git log -S (the test_commit_binding_store_failure.py form).
- [x] CI guard fails on reintroduced rot-prone refs, passes the current remediated tree with zero suppressions.
- [x] Escape hatch documented; policy note landed.
- [x] Detector unit tests cover the FP gotchas measured in the planning prototype ('bug surfaced'/'ticket dirs' NOT accepted; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases accepted; escape hatch honored).
baseline.summary: Comment hygiene: remediate rot-prone historical refs in code + CI guard

baseline.description:
## Why

Two work tickets (115b, 8c4f) burned close-gate cycles: their acceptance criteria had "done" evidence that lives OUTSIDE the codebase (live-store fsck surgery, phantom-dir deletion, changes landed through Gerrit) but were NOT tagged `[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043), so the completion verifier failed looking for code proof until the tag was added retroactively. A cheap DETERMINISTIC pass-1 lint that surfaces this at PLAN time — before claim — removes the whole round-trip. Rule-based lexicon checks are the proven high-recall/cheap tier for requirement-defect shape (AQUSA-grade prior art); this project already ships two such lexicon lints in the same P6/P7 family (`p6_ac_quality`'s vague-term + verify-command lint at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:686`, and `p7_destructive` at `:762`), so this is a well-precedented extension, not a new mechanism.

## What

Add an ADVISORY, prompt-less DETERMINISTIC lint (ADR-0016 `exec: DET`, the P6/AC family) that flags AC checklist items whose text carries operational-evidence markers (deploy / prod / live-run / IaC-apply / cloud-state / merge-gate / human-action / drill / store-surgery / recorded-attestation) but which are NOT tagged `[operator-attested]`. It NEVER blocks (advisory coaching only).

### Design decisions (grounded against the code)

- **It EXTENDS `p6_ac_quality`; it does NOT add a `P10` and does NOT touch
  `criteria_routing.json`.** The static DET floor (`DET_CHECKS`,
  `det_floor.py:880`) is hardcoded P1–P9 and enumerated in
  `registry.py:78 CANONICAL_DET`; DET checks are NOT routed through
  `criteria_routing.json`. `registry.validate_packaged_routing()`
  (`registry.py:445-446`) flags any routing key not in `CANONICAL_LLM` as an
  ORPHAN and fails CI, so a packaged DET routing entry is impossible without a
  larger, out-of-scope change. And `.rebar/`-overlay `exec:DET` criteria run
  through `det_invariants.run_project_det_checks` (`det_invariants.py:207`),
  which scans CODE with a grounding detector (`engine_b`) — structurally wrong
  for an AC-TEXT lexicon. The existing regression test
  `tests/unit/test_det_invariants.py:327` already pins "the lint EXTENDS p6 …
  DET_CHECKS stays exactly P1-P9", exactly matching how the verify-command lint
  (G-3a) was folded into p6. So the correct home is `p6_ac_quality`, keeping
  `DET_CHECKS` at 9 and `CANONICAL_DET` unchanged. The task's suggestion of a
  `criteria_routing.json` entry is refuted by the code and is deliberately NOT
  done; `p6_ac_quality` already ships in the packaged registry (no config flag),
  satisfying "advisory in packaged registry".

- **Single-source the tag matcher.** The canonical `[operator-attested]` matcher
  is `workflow_ops._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE` (`workflow_ops.py:61`), consumed by
  the completion-verifier enrichment path (`workflow_ops.py:80
  enrich_operator_attested`, `passes.py:769`). `det_floor` imports nothing from
  `workflow_ops`, and `workflow_ops` imports `det_floor` lazily
  (`workflow_ops.py:135`), so `det_floor` will OWN the regex as
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `workflow_ops` will import it — no import cycle,
  one source of truth, so the lint and the verifier agree on "tagged" by
  construction (guarded by a unit test).

- **Precision-first (advisory posture).** An advisory lint must not nag, so the
  lexicon is tuned for precision with a codebase-verifiable SUPPRESSION co-signal
  (drop items that name an in-repo proving command / test / doc / config-file
  deliverable, or carry a "… — landed on main" trailer) and a NEGATION guard
  ("no live", "read-only provisioning"). Recall is a reported figure, not a gate.

### Self-gate (DETERMINISTIC — no LLM anywhere)

Run the locked lexicon over the frozen historical AC corpus committed under `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/`. The corpus is the AC checklist items of the 556 E1 outcome-corpus tickets that resolve in the store (`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl` → 3091 AC items, 31 already tagged `[operator-attested]`). Ground-truth for precision is a frozen per-item TP/FP adjudication of the full flagged set (a census ≥ the required 50-item sample); recall is measured against the 31 tagged items with their tag stripped. Measured on this corpus: flag rate 2.07% (≤5%), recall 61% (19/31), precision ~92% (census of 64 flagged items, 6 adjudicated false-positive), and both known cases (115b, 8c4f) fire. NO LLM call runs in the eval or the lint.

### Landing order (pre-registration, git-ancestry)

Latent robustness gap found by the LLM code review of Gerrit 1905 (C4).

## Context / Problem

`scripts/gen_config_reference.py::_lifecycle_index()` uses `dict.setdefault` when mapping a canonical schema key to its lifecycle note, so if one canonical replacement key is ever the target of MORE THAN ONE cfg deprecation alias and/or tombstone, only the first-encountered note survives and the rest are silently dropped from the generated `docs/config-reference.md`. Confirmed in code: both loops in `_lifecycle_index` call `index.setdefault(replacement, ...)`.

No collision exists today (each cfg replacement key is targeted exactly once across `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` + `tombstones()`), so current generated output is correct. This is a defensive fix that stops a future deprecation from silently deleting doc content.

## Approach

Accumulate the notes per canonical key instead of `setdefault`: collect them into a list keyed by replacement, then join them into the single `Lifecycle` table cell. The single-note case must render byte-identically to today so `docs/config-reference.md` needs no regeneration and the committed-tree drift oracle stays green.

## Scope

- `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` — rewrite `_lifecycle_index` to accumulate.
- `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` — add the held-out collision guards.

No other module reads `_lifecycle_index`; `docs/env-vars.md` is out of scope because its generator only scans `src/rebar`.

## Testing

Held-out guards seed collisions by monkeypatching the generator's `_cfg_deprecations` / `_cfg_tombstones` accessors onto a real schema key, then assert both notes survive into that key's rendered table row:

- Two deprecated aliases sharing one replacement — both alias names appear in the row.
- One deprecated alias plus one tombstone sharing one replacement — both notes appear.
- Each guard is confirmed RED against unmodified `main` (the second note is absent) before
  the fix lands.
- Regression: the whole existing oracle, including the read-only committed-tree `--check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_lifecycle_index` accumulates every lifecycle note for a canonical key with no silent
  drop; checked by `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py -q` passing the
  new collision guards.
- [x] A test seeds a 2-alias collision and asserts both notes appear in that key's
  `config-reference.md` row; checked by the same pytest run, and by observing it FAIL on
  unmodified `main` first.
- [x] `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py --check` exits 0 against the committed tree and
  the pre-existing oracle stays green; checked by that command plus the full
  `tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py` run.
- [x] Gates stay green; checked by `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting new=0 increased=0 stale=0.
baseline.summary: Harden gen_config_reference _lifecycle_index against multi-alias canonical-key collisions
