baseline.description:
# Continuous auto-deploy: the running Gerrit environment reflects `main` without manual deploy or restart

## Why
Landing a change on `main` does NOT update the running environment. The **review-bot container's code**, the site `replication.config`, and the g2p config all require a MANUAL deploy (SSM / setup-*.sh) and sometimes a restart, causing drift + toil: epic 88ab S2's merge-review code landed on `main` but the running `compose-review-bot-1` still runs the pre-S2 image; the S3 `replication.config` fix had to be hand-applied via SSM. The deployed environment must AUTO-REFLECT `main` shortly after a change lands — WITHOUT ever destabilising the LIVE gate that contributors depend on to review + submit.

## What
### Trigger — RESOLVED: a systemd timer on the Gerrit host (option a; NOT GitHub Actions→SSM)
`rebar-autodeploy.timer` (every 2 min) runs `rebar-autodeploy.service` (oneshot). RATIONALE for the on-box timer over a GitHub-Actions `deploy.yml`→SSM: (1) NO new trust surface — the box already has an instance role and reads the PUBLIC mirror READ-ONLY (no GitHub→AWS OIDC/`ssm:SendCommand` grant, which would make the GH runner a lateral-movement path into the box); (2) self-contained + simplest to back out; (3) ~2-min poll latency is fine for a deploy loop.

### Deploy script (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, idempotent, flock-guarded)
- **flock** `/var/lib/rebar/deploy.lock` (`-n`) — overlapping fires skip; a long deploy is never re-entered.
- **deployed-sha** `/var/lib/rebar/deployed-sha`: on FIRST run (absent) INITIALIZE to the box's
  current HEAD WITHOUT deploying (adopt current state); write atomically (`mv` tmp) ONLY after success.
- **What to deploy (safety):** fetch `origin/main` from the mirror. The mirror's `main` only advances
  via Gerrit SUBMIT (post two-vote gate) → its tip is Verified BY CONSTRUCTION; deploy ONLY that tip,
  never an arbitrary ref. No-op when `origin/main == deployed-sha`.
- **Change detection (path-set per component):** `git diff --name-only deployed-sha..origin/main` ∩ a
  component manifest: review-bot (`src/rebar/**`, `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, `pyproject.toml`,
  `docker-compose.yml`), replication (`replication.config`), g2p (`gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`,
  `materialize-g2p-config.sh`).
- **Per-component apply (only if changed):** review-bot → `docker tag` current image `:prev`, then
  `docker compose up -d --build review-bot`; replication → re-materialise + autoReload (no restart);
  g2p → `materialize-g2p-config.sh`.
- **SCOPE BOUNDARY (v1):** covers review-bot container + replication.config + g2p config. `refs/meta/config`
  (project.config) is OUT of v1 (rare, security-sensitive, needs an operator-only Gerrit admin key):
  a change is DETECTED + signalled (metric + log), never auto-applied. Retry transient git/docker
  failures 3× w/ backoff; persistent failure → fail-safe (leave prior state + marker).

### Stability — live-pipeline safety (the load-bearing section)
The gate is FAIL-CLOSED: no LLM-Review vote ⇒ no submit. So a bad or careless deploy can FREEZE the whole pipeline. Hardening:
1. **Blast radius is bounded by construction.** Auto-deploy NEVER touches the `gerrit` container and
   NEVER modifies `refs/meta/config` (the labels/submit-rules/ACLs). `docker compose` is invoked with
   the EXPLICIT `review-bot` service only (never a bare `up` that could recreate `gerrit`); a guard
   asserts the `gerrit` container id is unchanged across the deploy. Gate INTEGRITY is thus not
   alterable by this mechanism — only the bot's code + replication/g2p config move.
2. **No Gerrit restart, ever.** Config changes use `autoReload` (replication) / materialise (g2p); only
   the review-bot CONTAINER restarts, and only when its code changed. Gerrit availability is untouched.
3. **In-flight reviews are delayed, not lost.** A bot restart drops in-flight webhook processing, but
   the EXISTING reconciler-backfill (events-log cursor) re-reviews any change missed during the
   restart window — so a contributor's vote is at most DELAYED by one restart, never dropped. The
   post-deploy health check confirms the reconciler loop is live.
4. **A broken bot deploy self-heals (never freezes the gate).** After `up -d --build`, an END-TO-END
   health check (30s timeout) verifies the bot is actually able to review (receiver `/health` + a
   probe that the review path is functional), NOT merely that the process is up. On failure →
   IMMEDIATE rollback to the `:prev` image + `up -d` + error marker; deployed-sha is NOT advanced. Max
   gate-frozen window = the health-check timeout, then service is restored to the known-good image.
5. **Circuit-breaker (no thrash on the live pipeline).** A per-target-SHA consecutive-failure counter:
   after 2 failed deploy attempts of the SAME `origin/main` tip, auto-deploy DISABLES itself
   (stop-file) + pages — it does NOT re-attempt the bad SHA every 2 min. An operator clears the
   stop-file after fixing forward. (Because the gate is fail-closed, thrashing restarts would be worse
   than pausing on a known-good image.)
6. **Config validated BEFORE it touches the running Gerrit.** replication.config / g2p config are
   parse-checked (`git config -f … --list`; g2p ini schema) BEFORE apply; a malformed config is
   SKIPPED (prior config retained) + alarmed — a bad config never breaks live replication/CI dispatch.
7. **Post-deploy pipeline-health gate.** deployed-sha advances only after a post-deploy check confirms
   the end-to-end gate still works (bot health OK; a canary confirms review + CI dispatch paths).

### Observability + back-out
Structured deploy log (from→to SHA + components) + `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (host-probe grep of an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, mirroring voter_errors) + a CloudWatch alarm w/ SNS action; the circuit-breaker stop-file is itself alarmed. Back-out: `systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer`; the manual path (compose-up.sh / setup-*.sh) is unchanged.

## Scope
The deploy orchestrator + systemd timer/service + stability guards + observability/back-out on the existing compose stack. Reuses the idempotent setup/materialise appliers. refs/meta/config auto-apply deferred (detect + signal). No change to gate semantics (S1/S2) or the feature-branch flow (88ab).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A change landing on `main` (post-gate + replicated) makes the running env reflect it with NO
      manual action, ≤ 5 min; live-measured latency recorded
- [ ] Idempotent + change-detected: a no-change run is a no-op; a relevant change re-applies ONLY the
      changed component(s) — verified for review-bot code, replication.config, and g2p separately
- [ ] review-bot rebuilt/restarted ONLY when its source-set changed (a docs-only `main` change does
      NOT rebuild it); after a code change the running bot reflects it end-to-end (a merge change gets
      the S2 merge-change tag from the auto-deployed bot)
- [ ] STABILITY — blast radius: the `gerrit` container is provably untouched across a deploy;
      `refs/meta/config` is never auto-modified; no Gerrit restart occurs (verified)
- [ ] STABILITY — self-heal: a deliberately-broken review-bot image triggers the health check to FAIL
      and rolls back to `:prev` (gate restored); deployed-sha not advanced (proven live)
- [ ] STABILITY — circuit-breaker: 2 consecutive failed deploys of a SHA DISABLE auto-deploy + alarm
      (no thrash); malformed replication/g2p config is rejected pre-apply (prior config retained)
- [ ] STABILITY — in-flight: a review dropped by the restart window is recovered by the reconciler
      backfill (delayed, not lost) — demonstrated
- [ ] Concurrency: overlapping fires serialized by flock; deployed-sha written atomically only on success
- [ ] project.config changes DETECTED + signalled (metric + log), not attempted (documented boundary)
- [ ] Deploy log + `deploy_errors` metric + alarm applied; back-out (disable the timer) tested; manual
      path still works
- [ ] Live-verified end-to-end on the running box (a real `main` change auto-deploys within the window)
baseline.summary: Continuous auto-deploy: running Gerrit environment reflects main without manual deploy or restart

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Stores that already exist — including client deployments, not just this one — have no `.bridge_state/projects.json` and no `bridge_project` on any ticket. Without a migration those stores would read every ticket as having an absent project, and there would be no recorded legacy default for the resolver to fall back to, so a store that syncs perfectly today would stop syncing on upgrade.

## Approach

Ship the migration as ensure units on the existing idempotent registry (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `REGISTRY_IDS` at `:66`, `_registry()` at `:82`), which is rebar's sanctioned seam: `docs/migrations.md:40-56` describes adding a unit, and the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built (`docs/migrations.md:14-16`). Units run at init/re-init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot (`docs/migrations.md:57-65`), so a client store converges without any operator action.

**The migration writes no ticket events.** A unit emitting an EDIT per ticket would be a four-figure event write under the store write lock on a store this size, and the MCP-boot entry point runs the sweep on a deliberately short lock budget and skips when contended (`docs/migrations.md:63-65`) — so an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points and converge unpredictably. Instead the unit records `legacy_default` once in the mapping, and the tri-state resolver treats every ticket with an absent field as belonging to it. One small write migrates the whole store.

Two units, both check-then-act and both safe to re-run:

1. **Seed the mapping.** If `.bridge_state/projects.json` is absent, write it with `legacy_default`
   and a single `projects` entry taken from the backend's configured project
   (`Backend.project`, documented as the effective write/create scope at `_backend.py:610-632`). If
   the record already exists, return `ok` and write nothing. Tree-check before committing so a
   converged store makes zero git commits, as `docs/migrations.md:45-46` requires of commit units.
2. **Stamp the capability.** When — and only when — the mapping holds more than one project, add
   `multi-project-bridge` to `.store-compat.json`'s `required_capabilities`. A single-project store is
   never stamped and stays usable by older binaries.

Ids are new and never reused, per `docs/migrations.md:50-51`.

**Where the unit bodies live.** The existing six units are implemented in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (for example `_store_compat_unit` at `:528`) and referenced from `_registry()` (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:93`). This story deliberately does **not** follow that placement: at the time of writing `_commands/init.py` measures 799 lines against the repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so adding two unit bodies there would fail CI on a limit that has no allowlist escape hatch. Because `_registry()` maps an id to any callable, the two new units live in their own `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` and are referenced from `ensures.py` — which is 253 lines and gains only its two registry entries. This keeps the change inside the gate without refactoring an unrelated 799-line module as a precondition.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` (new) — both unit bodies
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — two `REGISTRY_IDS` entries and two `_registry()` mappings
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's git row — real temporary git repositories and refs — because the units commit to the `tickets` branch and the zero-commit-when-converged property is only observable against real refs.

- Happy path: sweeping a store with no mapping creates one whose `legacy_default` equals the
  configured backend project, and every existing ticket resolves to it.
- The load-bearing assertion: the sweep writes **zero ticket events**. Assert the store's event count
  and the set of event files are identical before and after — this is what distinguishes this design
  from an EDIT-per-ticket migration.
- Idempotence: a second sweep on a converged store returns `ok` for both units and makes zero new git
  commits (assert the branch tip SHA is unchanged, not merely that no error was raised).
- Conditional stamp, as a contrast pair: a one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; a
  two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge`. The one-project half proves the stamp is
  genuinely conditional rather than unconditional.
- Failure path: a unit raising is recorded as `failed` and does not abort the sweep or the caller, per
  the registry's skip-and-continue contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A store with no mapping gains one whose legacy default is the configured backend project, and
      every pre-existing ticket resolves to it; checked by a real-git test asserting the record and
      the resolution.
- [ ] The sweep writes zero ticket events; checked by asserting the event file set is identical
      before and after.
- [ ] A second sweep returns `ok` for both units and leaves the tickets-branch tip SHA unchanged;
      checked by comparing the SHA across two sweeps.
- [ ] The capability is stamped only when the mapping holds more than one project; checked by a
      paired test over a one-project and a two-project mapping.
- [ ] Both unit ids are registered in `REGISTRY_IDS` and mapped in `_registry()`; checked by the
      existing registry-agreement test, which fails if they disagree.
baseline.summary: Legacy-store migration: ensure units seeding the project mapping without writing ticket events

# A gate run does not notice its own binary is older than the base ref it pins

`review-plan` (and every other code-reading gate) snapshots the base ref's tree into `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/<sha>/` and reviews against it, but nothing compares the RUNNING BUILD to that sha. A checkout that has drifted behind `origin/main` silently reviews new material with old code.

## Observed

Three consecutive `review-plan` runs were executed from `~/rebar/.venv` — a legitimate repo checkout venv, which is what AGENTS.md asks for — while that checkout sat 24 commits behind `origin/main`. The only symptom was one easily-missed line:

    WARNING rebar.config: rebar config (/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/2bce1407.../rebar.toml):
    unknown key 'verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets' ignored (typo? see docs/config.md)

That key is not a typo. Commit 74a7332606 ("9416: rename overlap_enabled for what it does") renamed `verify.overlap_enabled` -> `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`. The stale build predates the rename, so it read the CURRENT base ref's config, did not recognise the current key name, and silently ignored the operator's setting.

## Scope

Operator decision (2026-08-12): this ticket covers the build-drift warning only. The fourth criterion of the original report — surfacing repeated non-fatal LLM step failures in run summaries — is split out to `eclectic-industrial-argali` (61a1-ee49-3c42-4b09), linked `discovered_from`.

## Design

All code-reading gates converge on `rebar.llm.gate_source.resolve_gate_handle`, which resolves the base ref to a pinned sha and acquires the snapshot handle. That is the one seam where a drift check belongs.

The running build's commit is already resolvable: `rebar.signing._gate_commit_sha()` returns the live rebar source checkout's short sha, falling back to the build-baked `rebar._build_info.COMMIT` (written by `hatch_build.py`) for wheel installs, and `None` when neither exists.

Drift = the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the pinned sha, measured in the target repo. When the gate code and the target repo are different repositories the build sha simply is not present in the target repo, so the check finds nothing and stays silent — which is the correct behaviour, since drift is only meaningful when rebar is reviewing rebar.

The warning is advisory: reviewing from a slightly-behind checkout is legitimate, so this must never fail a run, never alter a verdict, and never change signing or provenance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — When the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the sha a gate pins,
      the gate emits ONE warning naming the build sha, the build commit's date, the pinned
      sha, and the drift count in commits. It does NOT fail and does NOT alter the verdict,
      exit code, signature, or provenance stamp.
- [x] AC2 — The warning is emitted at most once per (build sha, pinned sha) pair per
      process, so a run that resolves the handle more than once does not produce a warning
      storm.
- [x] AC3 — When build provenance is unavailable or drift cannot be established, the gate
      is SILENT: no warning when `_gate_commit_sha()` returns `None`, when the build sha is
      not present in the target repo (gate code and target are different repos), when the
      pinned sha is unknown, when git is unavailable, or when the build is at or ahead of
      the pinned sha.
- [x] AC4 — An unknown key in a config snapshot is reported differently when the running
      build is known to be behind the pinned ref: 'unknown key X (this build may predate
      it; see docs/config.md)' instead of the 'typo?' wording, which actively misdirects.
      The default wording is unchanged when no drift was detected.
- [x] AC5 — Held-out unit tests cover: behind -> warns once; at/ahead -> silent; provenance
      unavailable -> silent; build sha absent from the target repo -> silent; and the
      config unknown-key wording in both the drifted and undrifted states.
- [x] AC6 — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit + interfaces suites pass; every
      touched file stays under the 800-LOC module cap.

## Provenance

Found while re-running plan review for task b2bb during the store/signing remediation. Re-running from a worktree venv at origin/main is the workaround.
baseline.summary: Gate runs do not warn when the running build is behind the base ref

baseline.description:
## Summary

The environment-aware `resolve_symbol` grounding tool (`pai_tools.grounding_tools`, bug 406f) classifies a resolved symbol as `repo-local` vs `third-party/stdlib` by root-containment alone (`_within_root(origin, root)` at `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`). When the virtualenv lives INSIDE the repo (`<repo>/.venv/.../site-packages/<pkg>`), a third-party dependency's origin path is under the repo root, so it is wrongly labelled `repo-local` — defeating the tool's whole purpose of separating first-party symbols from installed dependencies.

The discovery tools already avoid this (their `skip_dir` prunes `.venv`/`venv` via `_NOISE_DIRS`), but the `resolve_symbol` locality check had no equivalent exclusion.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Have a repo-nested virtualenv (`<repo>/.venv`) with a third-party dep installed
   (e.g. PyYAML).
2. Call `grounding_tools(".")`'s `resolve_symbol("yaml")`.

- Expected: `EXISTS: … [third-party/stdlib (site-packages), origin=…]`.
- Actual: `EXISTS: … [repo-local, origin=…]` — the in-tree `.venv` origin is under
  the root, so it is misclassified as first-party source.

## Root Cause

`resolve_symbol` computes locality as `_within_root(realpath(origin), root)` only. A repo-nested `.venv`/site-packages path satisfies `_within_root`, so third-party deps installed in-tree read as `repo-local`.

## Fix

- Add `_is_dependency_path()` (+ `_DEPENDENCY_PATH_PARTS`) to `src/rebar/llm/fs_tools.py`
  detecting `site-packages`/`dist-packages`/`.venv`/`venv` path components.
- Gate the classification in `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`: `repo-local` requires
  under-root AND not a dependency path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolve_symbol` classifies a dependency installed in a repo-nested `.venv`
      (origin under `<repo>/.venv/.../site-packages/…`) as `third-party/stdlib`, not
      `repo-local`.
- [ ] Genuine first-party source under the root (e.g. `src/rebar/…`, not in a
      dependency root) still classifies as `repo-local` (no over-exclusion).
- [ ] `_is_dependency_path` in `src/rebar/llm/fs_tools.py` flags
      `site-packages`/`dist-packages`/`.venv`/`venv` path components.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the in-tree-`.venv` case and the first-party `src/` case.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the affected unit tests pass.
baseline.summary: resolve_symbol misclassifies repo-nested .venv deps as repo-local

baseline.description:
Scope: root-level `src/rebar/*.py` plus `attest/`, `metrics/`, `review_bot/`, `opcert_service/`, `audit/`, `grounding/`, `_guides/`. ~180 lines leave of 7,248 comment lines (2.5%) — this scope is in good health and the yield is concentrated, not diffuse.

SURFACED A LIVE DEFECT, filed separately: `_mcp_models.BridgeFsckOut` omits `binding_drift`, so the MCP outputSchema under-declares a field `bridge_fsck.py:217` always returns. The comment at `_mcp_models.py:31-34` claiming 'the cross-interface schema tests pin both to the canonical schema' is FALSE — those model names appear zero times in tests/. That false assurance is why the drift went unnoticed.

Two prior leads resolved AGAINST the hypothesis and belong in do_not_move: `_mcp_llm.py`'s 121 docstring lines are the literal wire-visible MCP tool descriptions FastMCP publishes to clients — API surface, not narration, zero recoverable. And `_config_schema.py`'s `# read-via:` markers are machine-consumed by `scripts/check_config_reads.py`, a CI gate — deleting one breaks CI.

Caveat that bounds this shard: 280 of `_config_schema.py`'s 792 lines are comments, and for many keys they are the ONLY documentation — `docs/config.md` has zero coverage for `completion_floor_active`, `comment_max_chars`, `auth_proxy_secret_env`. Recovering more than ~34 lines there requires writing those doc rows FIRST, or the trim destroys documentation rather than relocating it.

Three new ADRs proposed from `review_bot/`: bounded shutdown (drain/cancel/grace-period chain, test-pinned against docker-compose `stop_grace_period`); the deploy-safe in-flight counter and its deliberate over-count; retryable coverage gaps deferring vote-less under a bounded budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost
baseline.summary: Comment triage: root modules and services

baseline.description:
The agent step-budget default is too low for the agentic plan-review VERIFIER, causing routine INDETERMINATE plan reviews on code-grounded tickets.

## Why
`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 25` (env `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`, src/rebar/llm/config.py:237) is too low for the agentic verifier (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`), which re-grounds findings against real code with tools. On code-grounded tickets it routinely exceeds 25 steps mid-verify → the `verify` step fails → the gate degrades to INDETERMINATE (`llm_unavailable`) → no signed review → the claim is blocked. Observed this cycle on `tarry-creep-range` (c38b): default 25 → INDETERMINATE; `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50` → PASS + signed. Doubling the default to 50 removes the routine flake while staying well under the review-op floors that still apply.

## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` 25 → 50, and refresh the env-doc comment ("25 ~= 12 tool calls" → "50 ~= 25 tool calls").
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`, `src/rebar/llm/code_review.py`, `src/rebar/llm/operations.py` — refresh the stale "REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=25 ≈ 12 tool calls" comments to the new default (the flooring to `_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS=120` / `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS=240` is unchanged; the "far too low for review" sentiment still holds since 50 < 120).
- `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py` — the default assertion `(16000, 25, 600)` → `(16000, 50, 600)`.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_budget.py` — the `cfg.max_iterations == 25` preconditions → `== 50` (the `>= _FLOOR` assertions stay valid since 50 < 120).

## Scope
In: the default value + the stale doc/comment refresh + the two test updates. Out: the per-op floors (`_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS`/`_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS`), `max_tokens`, `timeout`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` is 50; `LLMConfig.from_env()` with no override yields `max_iterations == 50`.
- [ ] The `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` env override and the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` legacy alias still take precedence over the default (unchanged).

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` is 798 LOC (2 under the 800 cap) and a "god command": it bundles the compaction **transaction** (`_compact_locked`, CCN 24), **snapshot reconstruction** (`rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`, CCN 21), and the **CLI** surface in one file. Zero in-progress contention. Flagged by audit ae1b for both size and complexity. It also blocks bug `aea0`, whose one-line fix plus its rationale comment does not fit.

## Approach
Turn `compact.py` into a thin CLI facade over two extracted engines, decomposed by responsibility (the recurrence-preventing fix — future mechanism/format changes land in the engine module, not the command file). The public CLI entry points **stay in `compact.py`** so the contended `_cli/__init__.py` dispatcher is NOT touched.

1. **`compact_txn.py`** (NEW) — the compaction TRANSACTION: `_compact_locked`,
   `_sync_before_compact`, `_maybe_pause_at_rename_barrier`, `_git`, **and the snapshot
   primitives BOTH engines share**: `_git_author`, `_snapshot_strip_keys`,
   `_build_authorship_ledger`.
2. **`compact_rebuild.py`** (NEW) — snapshot reconstruction: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`,
   `_read_event_uuid`, and the rebuild counter. **Move the counter with its incrementer:**
   `_REBUILD_COUNT` and `get_rebuild_count` MUST live here, because
   `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` does `global _REBUILD_COUNT` — leaving `get_rebuild_count`
   in `compact.py` would read a different module global and silently report zero.
   `get_rebuild_count` is re-exported from `compact.py` to preserve its path.
3. `compact.py` retains the CLI facade: `compact_cli`, `compact_all_cli`,
   `_scan_snapshot_state`, `_usage`, plus the re-exports.

### Why the shared helpers live in `compact_txn`, not `compact_rebuild`
The dependency MUST run one way. `_compact_locked` needs `_build_authorship_ledger`, `_snapshot_strip_keys` and `_git_author`; `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` needs those SAME three plus `_git`. Splitting them — helpers in `compact_rebuild`, `_git` in `compact_txn` — makes each module import the other, i.e. a circular import. Hosting all four in `compact_txn` gives `compact -> {txn, rebuild}` and `rebuild -> txn`, which is acyclic, and puts the repair path in the natural position of depending on the normal path.

Complexity reduction rides on the move: `_compact_locked` gives up its candidate-parse, snapshot-envelope, retire/rollback and commit clusters to named helpers, and the rebuild gives up its source-partition and commit clusters. Update `.github/complexity-baseline.json` **downward only** (shrink-only ratchet).

Rationale (G6): the three responsibilities have different change-drivers (transaction safety, snapshot format, CLI ergonomics); separating them gives each a stable home.

## Preserve public + test import paths via re-export (G1G2)
Every consumer outside this module reaches the moved symbols through `rebar._commands.compact`, so `compact.py` must re-export them. The VERIFIED consumer set (semantic search + string grep, per AGENTS.md — the string grep matters because two sites name the symbol as a monkeypatch STRING):

- `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` — `_commands/fsck_repair.py:269` and
  `_commands/fsck_restore.py:202`, both importing INSIDE the function body (so the attribute
  is re-read per call and the string monkeypatch below still lands). Tests:
  `tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:78,138`,
  `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py:946`,
  `tests/unit/test_identity_4e9d_heldout.py:123` (via `_compact.`), and monkeypatched BY
  STRING at `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:46` and
  `test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py:97,131,189,229`.
  **NOT** imported by `_commands/fsck.py` — fsck.py:281 only MENTIONS the name in a comment.
- `_snapshot_strip_keys` — `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:9`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:14`, and
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py:138` (via `_compact.`).
- `_build_authorship_ledger` — `tests/unit/test_identity_gate_scope_and_ledger.py:362,401`
  and `tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:176,215,238,244`.
- `get_rebuild_count` — no consumer outside `compact.py` was found; re-exported anyway to
  keep the documented path stable.

  Also `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py:170` calls
  `_compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` — re-export-covered, no edit needed.

These are plain `from ... import` / attribute consumers, so the re-exports keep them passing with NO edit.

## `compact.py` also needs these symbols for ITSELF — not only as re-exports
Distinct from the public re-export list above: the functions that STAY in `compact.py` consume three symbols this split moves out, so the facade must bind them back or it will not even import.

- `compact_cli` calls `_sync_before_compact` and `_compact_locked`.
- `compact_all_cli`'s batch-commit block (`compact.py:778-782` pre-split) calls `_git`.

So `compact.py` does `from .compact_txn import _compact_locked, _git, _sync_before_compact` in addition to the re-exported names. `_git` is therefore bound for BOTH reasons — the facade's own use and the module-attribute seam a test patches — which is why it is listed twice and must not be pruned as "unused" by a lint pass.

## Two test seams MUST be repointed — the monkeypatch hazard
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` patches implementation internals ON THE `compact` MODULE OBJECT, and those internals move:

- `monkeypatch.setattr(_compact, "_git", ...)` — `_compact_locked` reads `compact_txn`'s
  module global, so a patch on the facade does not take. This does not merely fail loudly:
  the compaction SUCCEEDS, the test's `assert rc == 1` fails, and had the assertion been
  weaker the test would have passed while exercising nothing.
- `monkeypatch.setattr(_compact.lock, "acquire", ...)` — `compact.py` no longer imports
  `lock`, so the attribute does not exist (AttributeError).

Both are repointed at the symbol's new home (`compact_txn._git`; `_lock`, which the file already imports). This is the ONLY test change, it is mechanical, and it is REQUIRED — the earlier "no test edits" claim was wrong and is corrected here. Both failures were confirmed empirically by running the suite against the split before touching the tests.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — CLI facade + re-exports.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py` — NEW (transaction + shared snapshot primitives).
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_rebuild.py` — NEW (snapshot reconstruction).
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — shrink-only.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` — repoint the two seams above.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_rebuild_counter_b2bb.py` — NEW: the
  counter-increment proof (it needs the `rebar_repo` fixture, which is scoped to
  `tests/interfaces/`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` <= 500; both new modules >= 100 LOC; the
      module-size gate is green. MEASURED on the merged change: compact.py 275,
      compact_txn.py 448, compact_rebuild.py 238; `test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.json` entries for `_compact_locked` and
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` are <= their current values (24 / 21) or removed
      entirely, and `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.
      ALL THREE compact.py entries were REMOVED (decomposition put every function under the
      reporting threshold) — a pure shrink, which the locked ratchet accepts. `--check` now
      reports `active=65 new=0 increased=0 stale=0` and zero `compact.py::` entries remain.
- [x] `_cli/__init__.py` is unchanged (`git diff --name-only <commit>~1 <commit> --
      src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` returns nothing), and
      `python -c "import rebar._commands.compact as c; c.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log;
      c.compact_cli; c.compact_all_cli; c._snapshot_strip_keys; c._build_authorship_ledger;
      c.get_rebuild_count"` resolves all six names.
- [x] The counter co-location is PROVEN, not merely re-exported: a test calls
      `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` on a real ticket and asserts
      `compact.get_rebuild_count()` strictly increased across the call. Without this the
      suite could stay green while `get_rebuild_count` read a different module global and
      silently reported zero — the exact failure the co-location exists to prevent. (No
      consumer outside `compact.py` exercises the counter today, so nothing else covers it.)
- [x] Full default suite green — 11820 passed, 155 skipped. The only EDIT to an existing test
      is repointing the two monkeypatch seams in `test_compact_negative.py` (no assertion
      weakened); the other test file touched is the NEW counter proof, an addition.
baseline.summary: Split near-cap module _commands/compact.py (793 LOC) and reduce its local complexity

baseline.description:
## Summary
`rebar show` (and its JSON output) surfaces the internal `managed_refs` provenance
projection in a way that reads as a **live `relates_to` link**, even after that link
has been removed with `unlink`. This makes a correctly-removed link look like it is
still present, and makes `unlink` look broken when it is working correctly.

## Context / root cause
`managed_refs` (`src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py`) is a **strictly-monotonic**
projection of every logical reference a ticket has *ever* managed. Per its own module
docstring (lines 32-38) and `add_managed_ref` ("Never removes", lines 92-103) it is
**deliberately never pruned by UNLINK/detach** — it exists so a local link/parent
removal can be propagated to a peer system (Jira) without being resurrected by the
next inbound sync. That behavior is correct and intentional for reconciliation.

The problem is purely **presentation**: `show` renders `managed_refs` alongside the
live link data with a `relates_to <target>` shape indistinguishable from an active
relation, with nothing marking it as "removed / provenance-only." The live link set
(`deps`) is the source of truth for what links actually exist.

## Reproduction Steps
1. `rebar link A B relates_to`  (creates the link).
2. `rebar unlink A B`  (removes it; reciprocal side removed too for relates_to).
3. `rebar deps A`  → shows `deps: []` (link is genuinely gone).
4. `rebar show A`  → still shows `managed_refs: [["relates_to", "B"]]`.
5. `rebar unlink A B` again → `Error: no LINK event found …` (confirms nothing to remove).

- **Expected:** after unlink, `show` does not present B as a current `relates_to`
  relation of A. Any provenance/ever-managed info is either hidden from the default
  human view or clearly labeled as removed/provenance-only, distinct from live links.
- **Actual:** `show` presents `managed_refs` such that B looks like a current
  `relates_to` link of A, contradicting `deps: []` and misleading the reader into
  thinking `unlink` failed.

## Impact
- Users (and agents) reading `show` conclude an unlinked relation is still present,
  and that `unlink` is broken — wasted debugging (this bug was filed after exactly
  that confusion). It undermines trust in the unlink/link surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a successful `unlink`, the default human `rebar show` output does not
      present the removed relation as a current/live link.
- [ ] If provenance (`managed_refs`) is shown at all in user-facing output, it is
      clearly labeled as provenance/ever-managed (removed links distinguishable from
      active ones) — not rendered identically to live `deps` relations.
- [ ] The live link source of truth (`deps`) and the monotonic `managed_refs`
      projection are visually/structurally distinct in `show`/JSON so they can't be
      conflated.
- [ ] `managed_refs` remains monotonic (this bug must NOT be "fixed" by pruning it on
      UNLINK — that would reopen the Jira removal-resurrection window the field guards).
- [ ] A regression test asserts that `show` for a ticket with a removed relates_to
      link does not present it as an active relation.
baseline.summary: rebar show surfaces monotonic managed_refs as a live link, making removed (unlinked) relations look present

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
S2 needs a lean contract that can describe routes and locate one execution/help parser without importing handlers or optional dependencies. Existing command sets and parser styles cannot be migrated safely until factory, formatting, validation, and compatibility rules are fixed.

## Approach
Add a stdlib-only CLI parser foundation and immutable route registry.

- Define a narrow factory protocol equivalent to `build_parser(*, prog: str) -> argparse.ArgumentParser`.
- Provide one Rebar ArgumentParser/formatter customization for deterministic width/order/newlines and compatibility-preserving parse errors/return control. It extends argparse; it does not define another grammar.
- Let route records hold lazy handler and parser-factory references plus identity/alias/visibility/help, mount/init, confirmation/output, and possible-capability metadata.
- Validate duplicate spellings, illegal alias/retired collisions, contradictory policies, unknown capability ids, malformed references, and resource/parser census state without resolving command handlers.
- Derive the legacy policy-set exports from routes and run a shadow comparison against all current sets/arms. Do not cut help or execution over in this task.
- Define reusable argument-definition composition for canonical/nested/compatibility spellings so aliases can vary `prog`/epilog without copying options.

The formatter policy is an explicit byte contract: fixed width independent of terminal, deterministic command/option ordering, UTF-8 LF output, and one trailing newline.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No public behavior changes. Existing help files and execution ladder remain authoritative. Reverting this task removes only unused expansion scaffolding.

## Testing
Use in-process unit tests with synthetic factories/routes. Observable oracles are exact formatted bytes, parse success/failure without process termination, deterministic validation findings, derived-set parity, and blocked imports proving registry construction resolves no handlers or optional packages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The factory protocol and shared argparse customization produce deterministic help and compatibility-shaped parse errors from one parser object.
- [x] Frozen route records represent every current spelling and derive compatibility policy exports with zero shadow-census delta.
- [x] Registry validation rejects each synthetic duplicate, contradiction, unknown capability, malformed reference, and alias/retired collision deterministically.
- [x] Import blockers prove registry construction and route lookup import neither handlers nor optional dependencies.
- [x] No runtime help or execution path has cut over, and rollback is removal-only.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2a — Define the lean parser and route registry contract

# Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at 793 LOC against the absolute 800 cap, so SEVEN lines of headroom, and it is the most CENTRAL near-cap file in the repo (fan-in 93). Ticket d23e's entire scope is this file — a `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` deprecation alias, which must keep honouring the old name, warn, and prefer the new. MEASURED comparable: the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` tombstone (`3eb3e71337`) cost +8 lines, and an alias is strictly bigger than a tombstone, so realistically 10-16 lines. Per-knob cost in this file is MEASURED at 10-13 lines. d23e is genuinely blocked.

## Approach
**ADR 0056 §Decision 5 pre-diagnosed this file and its prescription does NOT hold. Do not follow it.** It said config.py's problem is "178 lines of FLAT independent env reads" wanting "a declarative field table". Verified against the tree:
 * The SPAN claim holds (`from_env` is `config.py:575-753` = 179 lines) but the characterisation does
   not. Only 125 of those lines are the flat `return cls(...)`; the other 53 are an ORDERING-COUPLED
   preamble (the tombstone raise at `:581-584` must precede everything; `table`/`cli` must precede
   every read; `current_code_root()` must beat the env var, `:617-625`). Of 29 kwargs, 22 are regular
   and SEVEN are irregular (a derived non-knob `runner`; `api_key` env-only by secret policy; a 3-way
   `repo_path` cascade rooted in a ContextVar; `tickets_path` with no env var at all; 20 lines of
   custom `mcp_servers` JSON parsing; a nested `LangfuseConfig`; an enum-validating `overlap_drain`),
   plus two field/env/file name mismatches a convention-driven table cannot derive.
 * **A TABLE WOULD BREAK THE ENV-VAR DRIFT GATE — this is the crux.** `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
   is a pure AST walk with no name resolution: it recognises a read only when the name argument is a
   STRING LITERAL (`:117-124`) and files anything else under "dynamically-constructed reads", where
   the variable DISAPPEARS from the table. A loop over spec rows makes that argument an
   `ast.Attribute`, so all 19 currently-resolved rows vanish from `docs/env-vars.md` and CI fails.
   `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` exists to catch this class and names the precedent
   ("exactly what happened on sibling task f844"); `llm/model_classes.py:112-130` spells out nine
   literal `os.environ.get` calls rather than one indirection for the same reason. **The repo has
   already tried the table shape here and rejected it.**
 * In-file, a table nets roughly ZERO lines anyway (~66 lines of rows replacing ~110, plus ~20 of
   dispatch). It relieves nothing.

**What the ADR missed, and what this ticket does instead: 219 of the 793 lines are not configuration at all.** `config.py:51-152` and `:190-269` are the gate read-root / snapshot-session domain — four ContextVars and eleven functions (`current_code_root`, `resolve_code_root`, `current_tickets_root`, `current_code_sha`, `in_gate_session`, `gate_session`, `assert_gated`, `use_code_root`, `use_tickets_root`). `assert_gated` (`:216-240`) raises about `rebar.llm.gate_source` — it is a RUNTIME FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY GUARD, not a config knob.

Three properties make this the right cut rather than a mechanical carve:
 1. **The seam already has a consumer proving it real.** `llm/gate_source.py:35` imports exactly
    `gate_session, use_code_root, use_tickets_root`, and its module docstring (`:1-18`) already
    documents the block being moved.
 2. **The domain is INERT.** All 154 lines of gate-context growth landed in five commits on or before
    2026-07-09; ZERO since. Every commit after that date landed in the knob region. So this moves
    cold mass out of the way of the hot region.
 3. **One-way dependency, no cycle.** `gate_context` needs only stdlib + `rebar.config` + a lazy
    `rebar.llm.errors`; it imports NOTHING from `llm.config`. `llm.config` imports it at module scope
    for `from_env`. This respects `model_classes.py:16-20`'s rule that config must never import back.

LEAVE `config.py:155-187` (`_active_gate_config`, `gate_config`, `resolve_gate_config`) IN PLACE — it is genuinely about `LLMConfig` and moving it buys a lazy import for no benefit.

**HONEST LIMIT, state it in the change and the ADR: this RELOCATES MASS, it does NOT REMOVE THE ABSORBER.** The absorber is the ~10-13 line per-knob cost in `from_env`, and the only structural fix for that is blocked by the scanner. This buys about 15 knobs of runway, not permanence. The durable follow-ups are (a) teach `gen_env_registry.py` to consume an exported spec list — precedent exists at `:150-160` where it already imports and unions `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` — and only THEN table-ify, or (b) domain-split the knobs per feature cluster (the 12 `overlap_*` fields are ~115 lines but change `cfg.overlap_k` to `cfg.overlap.k` at ~31 sites). Both are separate epics.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — remove `:51-152` and `:190-269`; add a re-export block.
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` — NEW, ~202 LOC (clears the 100-LOC floor).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — one regenerated cell: `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` moves file (`config.py:227`).
- `tests/unit/` — the headroom guard.

## Testing
**The relocation must require ZERO test edits. A required edit means the cut is wrong.** THE RULE THAT MAKES THAT TRUE: re-export the moved names from `llm.config` and repoint NO consumer in `src/`. 13 monkeypatch targets name a moved symbol, and every consumer of `current_code_sha` / `assert_gated` uses a FUNCTION-LEVEL `from rebar.llm.config import ...` (verified at `attest.py:123`, `:251`, `:429`, `sidecar.py:404`, `runner.py:259`), so the name is resolved in `config`'s globals at call time — exactly what `monkeypatch.setattr` rebinds. Repointing a consumer while a test patches `rebar.llm.config.<name>` is the silent-break mode ADR 0056 warns about.

Loud canaries, which fail at COLLECTION if the re-export is wrong: `tests/interfaces/store/test_pass1_fanout_gate_session.py:19` and `tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py:27` both do a module-scope `from rebar.llm.config import <moved name>`. `tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py:173` patches `llm_config.assert_gated` and fails loudly if the rebind stops taking effect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at or below 640 LOC and `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` is at least
      100 and under 800
- [ ] the seam guard for `llm/config.py` is TIGHTENED from the staged `<= 800` that sibling d8ef
      introduces to the `< 700` policy target, in this same change — the change that creates the
      headroom is the one that may assert it. (d8ef ships the staged bound because config.py is 793
      today; do not re-add a guard, tighten the existing one in
      `tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py`.)
- [ ] the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file
- [ ] no module under `src/` imports the moved names from `gate_context` — every consumer still reaches
      them through `rebar.llm.config`, so the monkeypatch targets keep working
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean, with the moved
      `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` row regenerated rather than hand-edited
- [ ] the NEW module's docstring states, IN-REPO, that this relocates inert mass and does NOT remove
      the per-knob absorber in `from_env` — so the next reader sizing up config.py's growth curve
      meets that caveat in the code rather than in a ticket they will not read
- [ ] `assert_gated`'s hardcoded `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config")` (`config.py:230`) is
      re-pointed to the module that actually contains it after the move, and a test asserts the
      REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED override warning is emitted on the `gate_context` logger rather than
      the `config` one. This is an AUDITED security-relevant warning — the message itself says the
      override is "audited" — so attributing it to a module that no longer holds the code sends
      whoever greps the logs to the wrong file. VERIFIED SAFE to change: `grep -rn '"rebar.llm.config"'
      src/ tests/` returns ONLY that one line, so no test filters on the name and no consumer keys
      off it. Swept the rest of the moved block for the same class: the only other identity literals
      are the three `ContextVar` debug names, which remain accurate under `rebar.llm` and need no
      change

- [ ] [operator-attested] the same caveat appears in the Gerrit commit message. Tagged because the
      completion verifier reads repository files ONLY and cannot read git history, so a criterion
      about a commit message is unconfirmable from the codebase and would burn a close cycle
baseline.summary: Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

# Compaction: rename folded events to `*.retired` (invariant I1)

## Why
Compaction hard-deletes the event files it folds (`compact.py:140-144` `os.remove`). A delete/add reconciliation (a rebase — the RC1 class) can resurrect a folded source event -> `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`. `docs/concurrency.md` I1 already SAYS compaction must rename folded files to `*.retired`; the code does not. Prerequisite for A2 (glandulous-potent-waxwing) rebuild backstop and A3 (entitled-unsweet-nutria) remediation.

## What
- Add ONE shared contract: `RETIRED_SUFFIX = ".retired"` + `is_active_event(name)` helper (in
  `reducer/_cache.py` or a small util), imported by compaction, the reducer, and fsck — single source of truth.
- `compact.py:140-144` — replace `os.remove(fp)` with `os.rename(fp, fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX)`.
- ORDERING/IDEMPOTENCY: write the SNAPSHOT atomically FIRST, then rename; a re-run after a mid-loop crash
  skips files already `*.retired` (the SNAPSHOT-present short-circuit at compact.py:227-231 / _scan_snapshot_state
  :266-268 makes a re-compact a no-op). Race guard: `if os.path.exists(fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX): continue`.
- ERROR HANDLING: do NOT silently swallow `OSError` — log WARNING per failure / INFO per success so a partial
  rename is observable; on failure, reverse already-completed renames before re-raising (atomic).
- `reducer/_cache.py` — exclude `*.retired` in BOTH listing paths: the `event_filenames` list (~line 97) AND
  the `*.json` glob (~line 102), via `is_active_event`.
- `fsck.py` — explicit `is_active_event` guard in the `_check_snapshot` loop; `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` must NOT
  fire on a retired source file.
- `docs/concurrency.md` (I1) — align doc with code; ADD a `.retired` lifecycle note: retention permanent for
  now (accepted storage tradeoff); branch-wide `.retired` GC is a documented FOLLOW-UP (new linked ticket),
  safe only past causal stability. State that `.retired` files are benign under a code rollback (old `*.json`
  glob ignores them).

## Scope
Compaction + reducer/fsck `.retired` exclusion + the shared constant/helper + the I1 doc. Does NOT change replay ordering (A2) or remediate the live store (A3).

## Acceptance Criteria

## Context / Problem

`docs/ticket-model.md:12` currently hand-maintains the ticket taxonomy and says there are five ticket types/statuses. The canonical vocabulary in `src/rebar/types.py:21-23` now defines seven statuses (`idea`, `open`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `closed`, `archived`, `deleted`) and seven ticket types (`bug`, `epic`, `story`, `task`, `session_log`, `code_review`, `identity`). The relationship prose below that intro is already current, so this ticket is limited to eliminating taxonomy drift while preserving the hand-maintained relationship documentation.

## Approach

Add a deterministic generator/checker at `scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py` that imports the canonical `TicketType` and `TicketStatus` literals from `src/rebar/types.py`, renders only a clearly marked taxonomy block in `docs/ticket-model.md`, and leaves all prose outside the markers byte-for-byte unchanged. The generated block will replace the stale introductory taxonomy sentence with tables/lists for the canonical type and status vocabularies plus a short note that the relationship sections remain hand-maintained. The script will support a write mode to regenerate the block and a check mode that exits non-zero when `docs/ticket-model.md` is stale after a vocabulary change.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/types.py`: read-only source of truth for `TicketType`/`TicketStatus`; tests may monkeypatch or copy a fixture to simulate a vocabulary addition, but the production vocabulary is not changed by this ticket.
- `docs/ticket-model.md`: receives one marked generated taxonomy section; all relationship/hierarchy/link/tag prose outside the markers must be preserved.
- `scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py`: new deterministic generator and drift checker with stable ordering from the canonical literal definitions.
- `tests/unit/test_gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py`: held-out oracle coverage for generation, stale-output detection, and simulated source-vocabulary drift.

## Testing

Held-out TDD will start with unit tests for the generator/checker rather than editing production code first. The oracle covers:

1. Rendering includes all seven live ticket types and all seven live statuses from `src/rebar/types.py:21-23`.
2. Running the generator against `docs/ticket-model.md` preserves relationship prose outside the marked taxonomy block.
3. A deliberately stale generated block makes check mode fail and report that regeneration is required.
4. A deliberate source-vocabulary addition in a copied/monkeypatched `types.py` fixture makes check mode fail when the documentation was not regenerated.
5. Re-running generation is deterministic/idempotent: a second run produces no diff.

Validation commands: the focused pytest for `tests/unit/test_gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py`, the documented script check mode, then the ticket's verify commands (`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` when required by the ticket gate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/ticket-model.md` contains a marked generated taxonomy section whose type/status content is derived from the canonical `TicketType` and `TicketStatus` literals in `src/rebar/types.py:21-23`.
- [x] The generated taxonomy lists all seven current ticket types and all seven current statuses, including `code_review`, `identity`, `archived`, and `deleted`; verified by `tests/unit/test_gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py`.
- [x] Hand-maintained relationship, hierarchy, link, and tag prose outside the generated taxonomy markers is unchanged by regeneration; verified by a preservation test.
- [x] `scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py --check` exits non-zero for both a deliberately stale generated block and a simulated source-vocabulary addition without regeneration.
- [x] Generation is deterministic/idempotent: running the write mode twice leaves `docs/ticket-model.md` unchanged on the second run.
- [x] The focused generator tests pass and the ticket verify commands pass before the Gerrit change is submitted.
baseline.summary: Generate ticket taxonomy documentation from the canonical schema

Discovered while fixing bug dca1-f641-caeb-4df4, which fixed ONE test. This covers the rest of the class, surveyed but left out of that change.

## Context / Problem

A fixture creates a bare git repo with a raw `git init --bare` and pushes into it. At git's defaults a bare repo's `receive-pack` runs `run_auto_maintenance()` after every push, spawning `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` — a process that OUTLIVES the push. So `subprocess.run([... "push" ...])` returning is NOT a happens-before edge for that object database. If the test then COPIES or byte-walks that directory it races a concurrent repack: entries vanish mid-walk and the copy raises. Measured signatures: a vanished `objects/maintenance.lock` (what CI caught) and whole loose-object fanout directories (`objects/2c`, ...) pruned as maintenance packs them.

rebar pins the two `autoDetach` keys on every store it OWNS (`_commands/_init_ensures.py`; bug 88eb, ADR 0051). A fixture-built bare remote is owned by no rebar code, so it runs at defaults. That asymmetry is the gap.

## Approach

The remedy is settled and measured — pin `gc.autoDetach=false`, `maintenance.autoDetach=false`, `receive.autogc=false` on the bare repo immediately after creating it, before anything is pushed. Measured postures, each with `receive-pack` confirmed present in a `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` trace: defaults -> 1 detached child; autoDetach pins only -> 1 foreground child; all three -> 0 children. Structural, not probabilistic. Three steps:

1. **One shared definition.** A new `tests/_git_upkeep.py` owns the pins
   (`BARE_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS`), the constructor applying them (`init_bare_remote`), and the trace
   helpers proving their effect (`maintenance_children`, `assert_no_detached_upkeep`), following the
   small single-purpose `tests/_*.py` convention (`_git_counts.py`).
   `test_concurrency_regression.py` and `test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` hold byte-identical copies of
   those keys under two names today; both are repointed at the helper, ending that drift.

2. **Fix the two HIGH-risk sites** by routing their bare-repo creation through that helper.

3. **Close the class at the amplifier.** `clone_topology_template` (`tests/_topology_template.py`)
   is the only mechanism in `tests/` copying a whole topology containing a bare remote — a
   `shutil.copytree(...)` plus two full-tree `rglob("*")` + `read_bytes()` passes. It gains a
   precondition REFUSING a template that holds an unpinned bare repository, naming the path and the
   missing keys, so a future fixture reintroducing the pattern fails loudly at setup instead of
   flaking under a race.

NOT acceptable, per dca1: retrying the copy, sleeping before it, or excluding `*.lock` from the walk — that filter is measurably insufficient, since the repack limb prunes whole fanout directories, not just lock files.

## The two HIGH-risk sites (push, then the tree holding the bare repo is copied)

1. `test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py` — raw `init -q --bare` in `_build_backup_fixture`, pushing
   immediately after (`push --all`, `push --tags`); the topology is copied via
   `clone_topology_template` once per test in the module. No pins in the file.
2. `test_inline_write_push.py` — raw `init -q --bare` in `_build_repo_with_origin`;
   `rebar.init_repo(...)` pushes under the default `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`; copied via
   `clone_topology_template`. No pins.

## The MEDIUM sites: bounded by the amplifier, not swept

The survey counted ~35 further sites pushing into an unpinned bare repo. They are NOT swept here, on a measured exposure predicate: a site is exposed only when the bare remote lives inside a tree later copied or byte-walked, and `clone_topology_template` is the only thing in `tests/` doing that to a whole topology. It has seven callers — two are the HIGH sites above, one is the already-pinned `test_concurrency_regression.py`, one is the module itself, and the remaining three (`tests/interfaces/_store_template.py`, `tests/interfaces/queries/test_list_filters.py`, `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py`) create no bare repository at all. Every other site pushes into a bare repo nothing copies, so there is no walk to race.

Sweeping three keys across ~35 unaffected files would be a large unreviewable diff whose bulk is unnecessary. Step 3 replaces that sweep with an enforced precondition: the moment any such site acquires a copy step, the guard converts a latent flake into a deterministic setup failure naming the fix. The exposed set closes by construction, not by an enumeration that decays.

## Scope

- `tests/_git_upkeep.py` (new) — the pins, the pinned constructor, the trace proof helpers.
- `tests/_topology_template.py` — the unpinned-bare-repo precondition on `clone_topology_template`.
- `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` — drop its local pins, use the helper.
- `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` — drop its pins and trace reader, use the helper.
- `tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py` — HIGH site: build through the helper, guard.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py` — HIGH site: build through the helper, guard.
- `tests/unit/test_topology_template_upkeep_guard.py` (new) — cover the precondition both ways.

Stacked on Gerrit 1952 (the dca1 fix, `Verified +1` / `LLM-Review +1`, unsubmitted), which introduces the second copy of the pins that step 1 collapses.

## Testing

- Happy path: a push into each newly-pinned remote leaves no detached upkeep, asserted from git's
  own `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` trace, behind a `receive-pack` positive control so it cannot pass against
  an empty trace.
- Failure path: `clone_topology_template` raises `AssertionError` naming the unpinned bare repo and
  the missing keys when handed such a template, and returns normally once it is pinned.
- Discrimination: per changed site, seed the defect its test guards, observe RED on the expected
  assertion, revert, observe GREEN; separately empty the pins and watch the trace guard fire.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/` holds exactly one assignment site for the upkeep pins, `tests/_git_upkeep.py`;
      checked by `[ "$(grep -rl 'receive.autogc' tests/ | wc -l)" -eq 1 ]`.
- [x] `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` consumes the shared definition instead of
      its own copy; checked by reading the diff.
- [x] `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` consumes the shared definition instead of its
      own copy; checked by reading the diff.
- [x] `tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py` creates its bare remote with the pins
      applied before its first push; checked by reading the diff.
- [x] `tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py` creates its bare remote with the pins
      applied before its first push; checked by reading the diff.
- [x] A push into each newly-pinned remote leaves no detached upkeep; checked by a test per site
      running the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, asserting no `git maintenance run` child carries
      `--detach`, with a `receive-pack` positive control against a vacuous pass.
- [x] `clone_topology_template` refuses a template holding an unpinned bare repository, and accepts
      that same template once pinned; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_topology_template_upkeep_guard.py -q`.
- [x] Each newly-pinned site's guard discriminates; checked by seeding the defect it guards,
      observing RED on the expected assertion, reverting, observing GREEN.
- [x] The touched modules are green; checked by `pytest -q
      tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py
      tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py
      tests/unit/test_topology_template_upkeep_guard.py`.
- [x] The repo gates pass; checked by `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
baseline.summary: Unpinned bare fixture remotes let a push leave detached git auto-maintenance racing the next copy

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Bug 8c8a fixed the disposition-drop defect: a retryable provider outage mid-run in the completion gate now surfaces as exit 11 ("transient — retry"). That is correct for an outage with an EMPTY criterion bank. But when the completion verifier has already banked an **operator-actionable BLOCK** (a genuine banked refutation on an evaluated criterion) and then hits a provider outage, the gate still fails closed to a verdict-less "could not run" (exit 11) instead of surfacing the available, actionable feedback — violating the module's own stated invariant (`completion_recovery.py:11-12`): "a deterministic no-LLM fallback so a run with any banked progress can never die verdict-less." The OPERATOR DECISION comment (2026-08-24) rescopes this: there is NO "sustained outage" detection; the trigger is simply "the bank already holds an operator-actionable BLOCK."

## Approach

In `CompletionAgentStep.run`'s `except LLMUnavailableError` arm (which today only stamps the disposition and re-raises), add a **no-LLM, bank-only degrade** step that runs BEFORE the re-raise:

1. Read the run's criterion bank (a filesystem read; unaffected by the LLM outage).
2. If the bank holds an **operator-actionable BLOCK** — an entry with `met=False` whose
   `evidence_sufficient` is not `False` (a genuine banked refutation, not an insufficiency
   placeholder and not a PASS) — read the ticket's expected criteria and finalize a
   full-coverage verdict via the EXISTING `assemble_deterministic_verdict` finalizer (no
   further LLM calls: successors/finalizer would only re-fail under the outage). That verdict
   is `verdict=FAIL`, `finalizer=deterministic_fallback`, `certifiable=False`. Return it as a
   normal `StepResult` so `close_precheck` takes its `verdict != PASS` branch: it does NOT
   close the ticket, surfaces the banked findings, and requires an operator decision.
3. Otherwise (empty bank, or only PASSes / insufficiency placeholders — nothing actionable),
   re-raise the SAME outage unchanged, preserving the exit-11 retryable posture (ADR 0040).

The degrade decision is wrapped so ANY fault in it (a bank read error, an unreadable ticket) falls through to the existing re-raise — the degrade is an enhancement, never a new failure mode on the outage path. The actionable-BLOCK predicate is added to `completion_verdict_assembly` (beside its existing `_entry_insufficient` seam) and re-exported through `completion_banking`, so the assembler module owns the bank-entry vocabulary.

Certified PASS remains unreachable without execution (unchanged): a degrade verdict is always FAIL and `certifiable=False`, so it can never sign or auto-close.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — the `except LLMUnavailableError` arm gains
  a guarded bank-only degrade call + a small private helper that reads expected criteria and
  assembles the deterministic verdict when the bank is actionable.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py` — add a `bank_has_actionable_block`
  predicate (met=False AND not insufficient) and export it.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_outage_degrade_b39a.py` — new held-out oracle.

No ADR change (per the operator decision). No change to `close_precheck`: a `FAIL` verdict already flows to its non-close, findings-surfacing branch (returncode 1), which IS the operator-actionable BLOCK.

## Testing

Offline, no billable call (mirrors `test_completion_outage_disposition_8c8a.py`). A fake primary runner banks a genuine actionable BLOCK through the record tool passed to it, then raises a retryable `LLMUnavailableError`:

- **Actionable-BLOCK bank + outage** → `run()` returns a `StepResult` whose outputs are
  `verdict=FAIL`, `certifiable=False`, `finalizer=deterministic_fallback`, and it made NO
  further runner calls (assert the runner's call count). The banked refuted criterion appears
  in `findings`.
- **Empty-bank outage** (and a **PASS-only / insufficiency-only** bank) → `run()` re-raises
  `LLMUnavailableError` (exit-11 posture preserved), `failure_diagnostic` retains the
  retryable disposition.
- **Defect-seeded mutation**: re-introduce the exact defect (make the arm re-raise
  unconditionally / drop the bank check) and confirm the actionable-BLOCK test returns to RED,
  then restore.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A completion verify run with a NON-EMPTY criterion bank holding an operator-actionable
      BLOCK/FAIL that hits a provider outage finalizes a deterministic BLOCK/FAIL verdict from
      the bank with **no additional LLM calls** — verified by the held-out test asserting the
      returned verdict is FAIL, `certifiable=False`, `finalizer=deterministic_fallback`, and
      the runner made zero further calls after the outage.
- [x] The degrade verdict is `certifiable=False` and does NOT close the subject ticket without
      an operator decision — verified by the verdict flowing to `close_precheck`'s
      `verdict != PASS` (non-close, returncode 1) branch; a `certifiable=False` FAIL can never
      sign or auto-close.
- [x] An EMPTY-bank outage (or a bank with no actionable BLOCK) keeps the retryable exit-11
      posture — verified by the held-out test asserting `run()` re-raises the outage and
      `failure_diagnostic` retains `retryable=True`.
- [x] Retryable errors keep bounded retries with backoff and emit a clear operator message on
      terminal exhaustion (the existing ADR-0040 exit-11 surface, unchanged) — verified by the
      empty-bank test still landing on the exit-11 "transient — retry" path.
- [x] RED→GREEN with a held-out oracle + a defect-seeded mutation (re-introduce the defect →
      test returns to RED → restore).

## Portability

No CI-provider coupling: the degrade path is pure in-process logic in the completion workflow (filesystem bank read + the existing deterministic assembler), triggered by the close/verify operation on every environment, with or without CI.
baseline.summary: Completion gate: retry-with-backoff + operator-actionable BLOCK from banked criteria (never verdict-less)

baseline.description:
## Symptom
Every `rebar transition ... closed` now detaches a compaction sweep (`rebar._commands.compact_trigger.run_sweep`, landed in `e0a55d5fac` / `d2dea317ec`). Observed today: a sweep held `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` for **24+ minutes**, during which every rebar write host-wide failed:

```
flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: pid=57999 held=47s pid_state=live)
WARNING rebar._store.lock: write lock still held after 60s (pass 1/3) — retrying
```

It blocked a `set-file-impact`, then a `transition ... closed` (which aborted with `could not acquire lock` after its completion verification had already run). A second sweep — spawned by a DIFFERENT worktree's close (`ci-config-schema-gate`) — did the same a few minutes later, so this is host-wide and recurring, not one bad run.

## The sweep is not hung; it is quadratic-ish
The process sits at **0.0% CPU** because it is I/O-bound on git. It spawns one child at a time:

```
git -c log.showSignature=false -C <tracker> log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames \
    --format=%H -- '*<event-id>*.json'
```

That is a `--full-history` pathspec walk of the ENTIRE tracker history, with a LEADING-WILDCARD glob (so no pathspec fast path), run once PER EVENT. Cost scales as (events to fold) x (history length), and both grow with the store.

## Why this contradicts the feature's own design
`run_sweep`'s docstring is explicit that compaction "is optional housekeeping and must yield to work someone is waiting on, never compete with it", and that "a skipped sweep is a no-op for correctness (the events stay live and the next trigger folds them)".

The stand-aside probe (`_lock.write_lock_is_busy`) implements that — but it runs **ONCE, before** taking the store lock. After that the sweep holds the lock for its whole multi-minute run, so a writer arriving one second later waits the full duration. The guard prevents the sweep from STARTING during contention; nothing makes it yield to contention that arrives afterwards.

The design's own correctness argument is what makes the fix cheap: because an abandoned sweep is a no-op, the sweep is free to bail at any point.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)
- **Re-probe and yield mid-sweep**: check `write_lock_is_busy` between units and abort when a writer is waiting. Aligns with the stated contract and is correctness-free.
- **Do not hold the store lock across the whole sweep**: take it per fold, or fold into a scratch area and take it only to commit.
- **Fix the per-event git walk**: one `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%H' --name-only` pass building an id->commit index costs one history walk total instead of one per event.
- **Bound the work per trigger** so a large backlog drains over several sweeps rather than one long hold.

## Impact
Closes, `set-file-impact`, comments and reviews all block behind it, and the failure mode reads as a mysterious multi-minute hang rather than 'housekeeping is running'. In this session it required manually SIGTERMing sweeps twice to make progress — safe per the design's own no-op guarantee, but not something every operator will know.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A foreground store write arriving while a sweep is running acquires the lock within seconds rather than waiting for the sweep to finish; verified by a test that starts a sweep over a store with pending folds and asserts a concurrent write completes promptly.
- [ ] The sweep detects a waiting writer mid-run and stands down, leaving the store consistent and the unfolded events live (the documented no-op outcome).
- [ ] Event->commit resolution does not run one `git log --full-history` per event; verified by asserting the number of git invocations does not scale with the event count.
- [ ] A sweep interrupted at any point leaves no partial state that a later sweep cannot fold.
baseline.summary: Out-of-band compaction sweep holds the shared store write lock for many minutes

baseline.description:
## Summary

The mcp entrypoint added by `kilted-nuclear-bronco` clones the `tickets` branch SYNCHRONOUSLY before `exec "$@"`. That branch has **199,846 commits**. The blue-green readiness gate allows **120 seconds** (`autodeploy.sh:130` `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT=120`). The clone cannot finish in time, so the server never starts listening, `/health` never answers, and autodeploy removes the new container and rolls back — on every deploy.

**`main` currently cannot deploy the mcp service at all.** This is a regression from my own merged change, not a pre-existing fault.

## Evidence (from the box, 2026-08-26)

    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "mcp-unhealthy", "detail": "new mcp container
      rebar-mcp-11f6e61c732b-8093 failed /health within 120s; removing it, leaving the OLD
      upstream live"}
    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "deploy_failed", "detail": "target=11f6e61c732b... fail#1 backoff=60s"}

`11f6e61c732b` is exactly "feat(mcp): provision the mcp ticket store" (Gerrit 2231).

    deployed-sha:    078ca376cee3...            (predates the merge)
    running:         rebar-mcp-078ca376cee3-8092  Up 43 minutes (healthy)
    nginx upstream:  server 127.0.0.1:8092;       (correct — pointing at the OLD container)
    tickets branch:  199,846 commits

The nginx upstream is CORRECT and the old container is healthy, so the rollback works exactly as designed. The endpoint is serving stale code because the new code cannot boot.

## Root cause of the design error

I modelled the entrypoint on the review-bot's (`Dockerfile.reviewbot:143-166`), which also clones at entrypoint. But the review-bot has NO blue-green readiness deadline — it is a stop-and-start service. The mcp service is promoted only after answering `/health` within a hard 120s window. Copying a blocking-clone pattern into a service with a readiness gate is what broke it. The soft-failure posture I designed ("no PAT ⇒ clone deferred, container still boots") only covers the ABSENT-credential case; with the credential PRESENT the clone runs and blocks.

## Fix

Do not block startup on the clone. Start the server first and converge the store in the background, so the container becomes healthy immediately and the store appears when it is ready.

This composes correctly with the read guard already on main: while the clone is still running, tracker reads raise `store_uninitialized` — an honest, machine-readable "not ready yet" — rather than returning `[]` and pretending the tracker is empty. That is exactly the degradation the read guard was built to provide.

Also worth bounding the clone cost itself (199k commits is expensive to re-clone on every fresh container), but correctness first: unblock the boot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The mcp container answers `/health` well within `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` regardless of whether
      a tickets clone is in progress, so blue-green promotion succeeds.
- [x] The store still converges: once the clone completes, tracker reads return real tickets.
      Verified LIVE on the box: 2763 tickets readable through https://.../mcp after convergence.
- [x] Reads degrade honestly for the case this ticket covers: with NO tracker dir present,
      reads report `store_uninitialized` rather than `[]`.
      The present-but-UNUSABLE case (directory exists, but no `.git` / no resolvable HEAD /
      mid-clone) is NOT covered here: `_reads._tracker` keys on `os.path.isdir`, so such a
      directory reads `[]`. That behaviour predates this ticket and is not a regression it
      introduced; fixing it changes core read semantics repo-wide and must preserve the
      contract that an existing but empty INITIALIZED store still reads `[]`. Split out to
      `rapt-dreadable-dromedary` (linked `discovered_from` this ticket), which carries all
      three observed instances.
- [x] A clone failure still leaves the container serving (soft posture preserved).
      `mcp-entrypoint.sh:140` reports the failure and provisioning returns; `exec "$@"` still runs.
- [x] Regression coverage asserts the entrypoint does not block `exec` on the clone.
