## Construct sweep from 7dea/d284: shared deterministic .tmp + os.replace across concurrent writers

The shared-deterministic-temp collision class proven in 7dea (completion_verdict_cache, Gerrit 2329) and d284 (plan_review/sizing.save_checkpoint, Gerrit 2334): a site composes a temp name deterministically from the target (tmp = f"{self.path}.tmp", NOT unique-per-writer), writes it, then os.replace(tmp, final). Under two concurrent writers for the same target the first os.replace consumes the shared temp and the second raises FileNotFoundError, which the site swallows (log+return) -> the losing writer silently loses its own write.

## Sweep outcome -- 2 CONFIRMED live siblings; others analyzed and excluded (see RCA comment)

Confirmed siblings (both in rebar_reconciler; the ONLY two of the package's seven atomic-write sites not already using unique-per-writer tempfile.mkstemp):
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_confirmations.py -- PeerConfirmationStore.save().
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/impossible_links.py -- ImpossibleLinkStore.save().

Concurrency: both write the per-repo committed .bridge_state/*.json sidecar; passes serialize on refs/reconciler/lock but the lease is steal-able and there is NO lock-lost guard before the persistence-phase save(), so the zombie/lease-steal window admits two concurrent writers. Fix: unique-per-writer tempfile.mkstemp + atomic replace onto the shared final (last-write-wins preserved); on failure unlink only the writer's own temp then log-and-return (fail-open contract PRESERVED -- these best-effort stores must never raise into a pass).

Excluded (documented in RCA comment): review_bot/reconcile._write_cursor (single sequential reconcile_loop task, single-box PoC), _config_writer/_cli config writes (one-shot), _opcert_signing (PID-unique + byte-identical .pub content -> no data loss), and all mkstemp/fsutil/write-lock sites.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] peer_confirmations.py::PeerConfirmationStore.save() uses a unique-per-writer temp via `tempfile.mkstemp`. Verified: `grep -n "tempfile.mkstemp" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_confirmations.py`.
- [x] impossible_links.py::ImpossibleLinkStore.save() uses a unique-per-writer temp via `tempfile.mkstemp`. Verified: `grep -n "tempfile.mkstemp" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/impossible_links.py`.
- [x] RED-first regression proves two concurrent same-target save() writers both persist (both `_dirty` cleared) with no `.tmp` residue. Verified: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py -q`.
- [x] Structural class check: re-introducing a deterministic shared `<path>.tmp` returns the regression to RED (mutation-checked). Verified: manual mutation run under an OS sandbox.
- [x] Fail-open behavior preserved: a save() write error is swallowed (logged), never raised into the pass. Verified: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_store.py -q`.
- [x] Excluded candidates each carry a documented concurrency verdict with evidence. Verified: checked in the RCA comment on this ticket.

## Testing
- Regression (both siblings): `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py -q` (RED before the fix, GREEN after).
- No-regression on the fail-open store contract: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/ -q`.
- Mutation teeth (sandboxed): re-introduce `tmp_path = f"{self.path}.tmp"` in each save() and confirm the regression returns to RED, then restore.
- Gates: `make lint` and `make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Sibling sweep: shared deterministic .tmp+os.replace collisions in reconciler/review-bot atomic writes

## Summary
`rebar review-plan <id>` unconditionally re-runs the full (billable, multi-turn LLM) plan review every time it is invoked, even when **nothing about the ticket has changed since the last successful review**. When several agents act on stale ticket state — or a single agent re-invokes after an unrelated `HEAD` advance — this burns tokens and wall-clock re-deriving an identical verdict. Plan review should be **idempotent against an unchanged ticket**: if the material the last review was computed over is unchanged, short-circuit and reuse the existing attestation, emitting a clear feedback message that explains why it did not re-run. A `--force` flag must let a client override and re-run unconditionally.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <id>` on a ticket and let it produce a passing attestation.
2. Without editing the ticket's description/acceptance criteria/type (i.e. the reviewed
   material is byte-identical), run `rebar review-plan <id>` again.
3. Observe a second full LLM review is performed (new billable call, ~minutes of wall-clock),
   producing a verdict equivalent to the first.

**Expected:** the second invocation detects the material is unchanged since the last review, **skips** the LLM call, and prints a feedback message (e.g. "plan review skipped: ticket unchanged since last review at <sha>/<ts>; pass --force to re-run"). The existing attestation is reused. `--force` bypasses the check and re-runs. **Actual:** a full re-review runs unconditionally regardless of whether anything changed.

## Notes / design pointers
- The plan-review attestation already records a `material` fingerprint (see the signed
  manifest, e.g. `material: c2b48241ad85a805`) and a `verified-at-sha`. The idempotence
  check should key on the **reviewed material fingerprint** (ticket content), NOT bare `HEAD`
  — a `HEAD` advance that does not touch the ticket's material must not force a re-run. Note
  the current claim gate treats an attestation whose `head_sha != HEAD` as "stale" and demands
  a re-run; that staleness definition is over-broad and is the root of the wasted work here.
- Decide the precise change-detection basis (material fingerprint vs. cited-code drift) and
  document it, so "unchanged" has one authoritative definition shared with the claim gate.
- `--force` must be plumbed through the CLI (`_review_plan`) and any MCP `review_plan` surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id>` short-circuits (no LLM call) when the ticket's reviewed
      material is unchanged since the last successful review, reusing the prior attestation.
- [ ] The short-circuit prints a clear feedback message explaining the behavior and how to
      override (`--force`).
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id> --force` re-runs the review unconditionally.
- [ ] A `HEAD` advance that does not change the ticket's reviewed material does NOT by itself
      trigger a re-run (idempotence is keyed on material, not bare HEAD).
- [ ] The MCP `review_plan` surface exposes the same `force` override.
- [ ] Regression test: two back-to-back reviews with no ticket change ⇒ exactly one LLM call;
      with `--force` ⇒ two calls.
- [ ] Docs (plan-review-gate.md) document the idempotence behavior and the `--force` escape hatch.
baseline.summary: plan review re-runs on unchanged ticket; add idempotence short-circuit + --force override

# Convergence rollout tail: Phase-3 consumer swap flip + live shadow-pass validation + capped live heal

## Summary
High-risk tail of the convergence rollout, carved from soar-quill-flare (7d23). Per epic adept-hedge-stain the AGENT (ACLI access) performs the live validation directly, with GUARANTEED cleanup of test artifacts in both live Jira and the local store (full-surface validation is centralized in sibling D1 close-ferreous-cardinal). The `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` workflow runs `rebar reconcile --mode live` every 20 min.

## What already landed (7d23, on main)
- Phase-1 baseline dual-write SHADOW (`baseline_shadow.py`) behind `reconciler.baseline_dual_write`, with per-pass
  `baseline_shadow_check` logging + `baseline_shadow_divergence` alert.
- Circuit breaker (`check_blast_radius`, default 0.10) before the first acting mutation.

## Remaining CODE
- [CODE] Phase-3 consumer swap: re-point `outbound_fields._local_matches_prev` (and its `outbound_differ` caller)
  from `prev_snapshot` to `BindingStore.get_baseline`, behind a NEW flag `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap`
  (bool, default false; add to `ReconcilerConfig` in `_config_schema.py`, distinct from `baseline_dual_write`).
  PRESERVE byte-for-byte: absent-baseline->local-wins; corrupt-store fail-closed abort. NOTE `get_baseline` returns
  None for a non-dict/absent entry, so map None -> the existing absent-baseline (local-wins) branch, and add an
  explicit corrupt-store detection (get_baseline cannot itself signal "corrupt") so fail-closed is preserved.
  Document the flag + flip procedure in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
- [CODE] RED-first direction-preservation property test running the SWAPPED consumer, covering the five mirrored
  fields as MAPPED (local title/description/priority/status/assignee <-> Jira summary/description/priority/status/
  assignee — reconcile the two field-name sets `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` and `baseline_shadow._MIRRORED_FIELDS`);
  name it distinctly from the existing `test_property_direction_preservation`.
- [CODE] Census key: expand-contract — emit BOTH `decision_census` and `binding_walk_census` for one release,
  migrate consumers to `decision_census`, then drop `binding_walk_census`. (Not a bare rename.)
- [CODE] classifier-vs-legacy divergence alerting: compare `classify()`'s per-binding decision against the
  PRODUCTION differ's action for that binding in the SAME pass, emitting `classifier_legacy_divergence`
  {classifier_count:int, legacy_count:int, divergent_pairs:list[str] of local_ids, pass_id:str}. If a per-binding
  production decision is not extractable for a given code path, scope the alert to the paths where it is and
  document the gap (do NOT invent a parallel legacy engine).

## Remaining OPERATIONAL (agent-run with ACLI; guaranteed cleanup)
- [OPERATIONAL] >=10 CONSECUTIVE clean shadow passes (`baseline_shadow_check` divergent==0) BEFORE flipping the flag.
  Streak is DERIVED from the sync-log history (query the last N `baseline_shadow_check` events), NOT an in-memory
  counter, so a fresh GHA process recomputes it; any divergent>0 OR a >20-min gap resets it and emits
  `baseline_shadow_divergence`. COORDINATION: A3's live remediation pauses the reconciler and will reset this streak
  — do NOT run A3's live pass during the streak window (sequence them).
- [OPERATIONAL] Capped live heal under bootstrap-strict incl. the GC-after-grace deletion (f8b5-2f30 -> REB-530).
  PRE-HEAL BACKUP covers BOTH sides: export affected Jira issue state (JSON via Jira API) AND tag the tickets branch
  (`git tag pre-heal-<date>`) so binding-store mutations are recoverable; if either backup fails, ABORT the heal.
  Store the artifacts in the workflow run artifacts (retention documented).
- [OPERATIONAL] Flip the flag only after BOTH gates. Rollback rehearsed: (a) revert the flag to false and confirm
  the reconciler reverts to `prev_snapshot` arbitration with no divergence, AND (b) force one `--mode dry-run` pass
  confirming zero mutations; record both workflow run-ids.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [CODE] `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap` flag added + documented in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`; `_local_matches_prev` reads `get_baseline` behind it; None->local-wins; corrupt-store fail-closed preserved (explicit detection).
- [ ] [CODE] RED-first direction-preservation property test (swapped consumer, five mapped fields) RED before, GREEN after.
- [ ] [CODE] Census emits both keys (expand-contract), consumers migrated to `decision_census`; `classifier_legacy_divergence` emitted with the typed fields above (or scoped+documented where per-binding legacy decisions aren't extractable).
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] >=10 consecutive clean shadow passes (log-derived streak, reset rule above) before the flip, NOT overlapping A3's live pass; evidence recorded.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Capped live heal with a bilateral pre-heal backup (Jira JSON + tickets-branch tag); heal aborts if either backup fails; artifacts stored.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Flip only after both gates; rollback rehearsed (flag-revert + dry-run run-ids recorded).
baseline.summary: Convergence rollout tail: Phase-3 consumer swap flip + live shadow-pass validation + capped live heal

## Context / Problem

Stores that already exist — including client deployments, not just this one — have no `.bridge_state/projects.json` and no `bridge_project` on any ticket. Without a migration those stores would read every ticket as having an absent project, and there would be no recorded legacy default for the resolver to fall back to, so a store that syncs perfectly today would stop syncing on upgrade.

## Approach

Ship the migration as ensure units on the existing idempotent registry (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `REGISTRY_IDS` at `:66`, `_registry()` at `:82`), which is rebar's sanctioned seam: `docs/migrations.md:40-56` describes adding a unit, and the ordered School-A ledger is explicitly not built (`docs/migrations.md:14-16`). Units run at init/re-init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot (`docs/migrations.md:57-65`), so a client store converges without any operator action.

**The migration writes no ticket events.** A unit emitting an EDIT per ticket would be a four-figure event write under the store write lock on a store this size, and the MCP-boot entry point runs the sweep on a deliberately short lock budget and skips when contended (`docs/migrations.md:63-65`) — so an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points and converge unpredictably. Instead the unit records `legacy_default` once in the mapping, and the tri-state resolver treats every ticket with an absent field as belonging to it. One small write migrates the whole store.

Two units, both check-then-act and both safe to re-run:

1. **Seed the mapping.** If `.bridge_state/projects.json` is absent, write it with `legacy_default`
   and a single `projects` entry taken from the backend's configured project
   (`Backend.project`, documented as the effective write/create scope at `_backend.py:610-632`). If
   the record already exists, return `ok` and write nothing. Tree-check before committing so a
   converged store makes zero git commits, as `docs/migrations.md:45-46` requires of commit units.
2. **Stamp the capability.** When — and only when — the mapping holds more than one project, add
   `multi-project-bridge` to `.store-compat.json`'s `required_capabilities`. A single-project store is
   never stamped and stays usable by older binaries.

Ids are new and never reused, per `docs/migrations.md:50-51`.

**Where the unit bodies live.** The existing six units are implemented in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (for example `_store_compat_unit` at `:528`) and referenced from `_registry()` (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:93`). This story deliberately does **not** follow that placement: at the time of writing `_commands/init.py` measures 799 lines against the repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so adding two unit bodies there would fail CI on a limit that has no allowlist escape hatch. Because `_registry()` maps an id to any callable, the two new units live in their own `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` and are referenced from `ensures.py` — which is 253 lines and gains only its two registry entries. This keeps the change inside the gate without refactoring an unrelated 799-line module as a precondition.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py` (new) — both unit bodies
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — two `REGISTRY_IDS` entries and two `_registry()` mappings
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's git row — real temporary git repositories and refs — because the units commit to the `tickets` branch and the zero-commit-when-converged property is only observable against real refs.

- Happy path: sweeping a store with no mapping creates one whose `legacy_default` equals the
  configured backend project, and every existing ticket resolves to it.
- The load-bearing assertion: the sweep writes **zero ticket events**. Assert the store's event count
  and the set of event files are identical before and after — this is what distinguishes this design
  from an EDIT-per-ticket migration.
- Idempotence: a second sweep on a converged store returns `ok` for both units and makes zero new git
  commits (assert the branch tip SHA is unchanged, not merely that no error was raised).
- Conditional stamp, as a contrast pair: a one-project mapping leaves `required_capabilities` empty; a
  two-project mapping adds exactly `multi-project-bridge`. The one-project half proves the stamp is
  genuinely conditional rather than unconditional.
- Failure path: a unit raising is recorded as `failed` and does not abort the sweep or the caller, per
  the registry's skip-and-continue contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A store with no mapping gains one whose legacy default is the configured backend project, and
      every pre-existing ticket resolves to it; checked by a real-git test asserting the record and
      the resolution.
- [ ] The sweep writes zero ticket events; checked by asserting the event file set is identical
      before and after.
- [ ] A second sweep returns `ok` for both units and leaves the tickets-branch tip SHA unchanged;
      checked by comparing the SHA across two sweeps.
- [ ] The capability is stamped only when the mapping holds more than one project; checked by a
      paired test over a one-project and a two-project mapping.
- [ ] Both unit ids are registered in `REGISTRY_IDS` and mapped in `_registry()`; checked by the
      existing registry-agreement test, which fails if they disagree.
baseline.summary: Legacy-store migration: ensure units seeding the project mapping without writing ticket events

## What happened

LLM-backed rebar operations hung **indefinitely** — 0.0% CPU, state `S` (sleeping), no output — for **3 to 5 hours**, until killed. `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` defaults to 600 s and is wired into both the Bedrock client (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:95` → `read_timeout`/`connect_timeout`) and a wall-clock guard (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:376`), so **the configured timeout did not fire**. This is not "no timeout exists" — it is "the timeout was bypassed or the hang is outside the region it guards".

## Evidence (observed 2026-08-19/20)

Affected THREE independent sessions in three different worktrees simultaneously, so it is not workspace-local:

| pid | op | worktree | elapsed | %CPU | state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80532 | `transition … closed` (completion verifier) | noncodebase-tag | 5h00m | 0.0 | S |
| 80534 | `transition … closed` (completion verifier) | noncodebase-tag | 5h00m | 0.0 | S |
| 33196 | `review-plan` | noncodebase-tag | 3h20m | 0.0 | S |
| 31254 | `transition … closed` | impl-obese-dihedral-ermine | 3h41m | 0.0 | S |
| 33211 | `review-plan` | rp05-cli-registry | 3h37m | 0.0 | S |

Discriminating observations:

1. **Only LLM-invoking operations hang.** Every wedged process was `review-plan` or a
   `transition → closed` (which runs the completion verifier). In the same period, non-LLM store
   writes — `rebar session-log append`, `rebar edit`, `rebar comment`, `rebar set-file-impact`,
   `rebar link` — all completed in seconds.
2. **It is NOT store-lock contention.** `lsof .tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` showed **no
   holder** while seven processes were wedged. No per-ticket `.write.lock` existed for the
   affected tickets.
3. **It is NOT slow progress.** 0.0% CPU sustained over hours; a fresh probe run produced
   **zero bytes of output and zero CPU** rather than progressing slowly.
4. **At least one process did LLM work first, then blocked.** pid 33196 (`review-plan`) was
   observed at **87.7% CPU** at t+1h18m and at **0.0% CPU** at t+3h03m — so it completed
   compute and then wedged, which suggests the hang may be AFTER the model call (persisting the
   attestation / a git or network step) rather than in the call itself. This is the main
   ambiguity a root-cause pass must resolve.
5. Killing the wedged processes left every affected ticket cleanly in its prior status with no
   partial event written — the store was not corrupted.

## Why it matters

Every gated operation is affected: no work ticket can be claimed (plan-review gate) or closed (completion-verification gate) while this is happening. It stalled an entire epic's board bookkeeping for hours across multiple agent sessions, and the only escape hatch is `--force=<reason>`, which records **no signed attestation** — i.e. the outage silently degrades the audit trail if operators work around it.

## Suggested first step

Do NOT assume the model endpoint. The 87.7%→0.0% transition on pid 33196 makes a post-call hang (attestation write, `git` subprocess, or a second uninstrumented network call) at least as plausible as a hung provider socket. `/rebar-debug` with a hypothesis-driven pass is the right protocol; a stack dump (`py-spy dump --pid <pid>`) of a live wedged process would settle it in one observation, so capture one before killing the next occurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exact blocking call is identified by direct observation (stack dump of a wedged
      process), not inferred.
- [ ] An LLM-backed operation cannot exceed its configured `REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT` wall clock,
      whatever the blocking layer, and fails with a clear error naming the timed-out stage.
- [ ] A regression test drives the identified blocking layer to hang and asserts the operation
      aborts within the configured budget instead of sleeping indefinitely.
baseline.summary: LLM-backed rebar ops hang for hours; REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT does not fire

## Context

Establish the nested `rebar bridge` CLI through a shippable vertical slice. The parent story originally proposed advertising all eight final verbs before their owning stories implemented them. That would expose broken placeholders on `main`. This task therefore registers only the two verbs it owns now: `preview` and `sync`. Later dependency-ordered stories extend the group only when each handler is functional.

`preview` is the read-only path over the existing reconciler dry-run mode. `sync` is the mutating path over the existing live mode. The legacy top-level `reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, and `bridge-fsck` spellings remain unchanged at this boundary.

## Approach

- Add `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` as the nested-group parser and shared reconciler subprocess launcher.
- Keep `_cli._reconcile` as a compatibility wrapper around that launcher until story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` retires the top-level verb.
- Route the help-backed `bridge` noun from `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`.
- Register only `preview` and `sync`: preview forces `dry-run`; sync forces `live`.
- Reject `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and arbitrary trailing arguments so callers cannot override the read/write distinction. The public `--max-changes`, `--only`, `--except`, and `--max-age` flags do not exist yet; story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` will add them together with their behavior and migration.
- Define exact discovery contracts: no nested verb prints group usage; `--help` prints usage; an unknown nested verb fails with the valid choices and never falls through to a same-named top-level command.
- Update `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` and regenerate `docs/cli-reference.md` for the nested group; add the new dispatcher arms and exit contracts to `docs/exit-codes.md`; update `docs/user-guide.md` with preview-versus-sync guidance; and update `docs/release-notes.md` to announce only the staged surface that actually ships.
- Keep public help free of the parent story's exact internal-vocabulary denylist: `mode`, `rank`, `gate`, `lock`, `cap`, `pass`, `binding store`, and numeric exit-code values.
- Preserve `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, the `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` round trip, top-level `doctor`, and all legacy bridge spellings.

## Surface parity

- CLI: in scope and exercised through the real `rebar` entrypoint.
- Library and MCP: out of scope; story `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` owns those surfaces.
- Automated workflows and scripts: out of scope; story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` owns their migration.
- Dual direction: both preview/read and sync/write are proven here.

## Testing

Use a real CLI subprocess against a temporary git-backed tracker plus a stateful fake Jira transport built from production-shaped fixtures. A unit-only dispatch test is insufficient because parsing, subprocess wiring, mode selection, and persisted state are contractual.

RED-first oracle:
- happy path: `rebar bridge preview` returns the real reconciler JSON plan;
- held out: exact before/after snapshots prove preview performs zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes;
- held out: sync starts from an unbound remote-only issue, creates the real local/binding mutation, and preserves unrelated event bytes;
- held out: no-verb, help, unknown verb, top-level-name collision, forbidden flag, phase-gate, doctor, legacy-command, generated-reference, and exit-code-table contracts; the help oracle lowercases captured output and rejects every literal denylisted term and any numeric exit-code value;
- mutation: routing preview to live must fail the no-write oracle; routing sync to dry-run must fail the persisted-mutation oracle.

This wrapper adds no new composed store operation, retry loop, or cache, so the shared contention suites remain the responsibility of the reconciler core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar bridge`, `rebar bridge --help`, `rebar bridge preview --help`, and `rebar bridge sync --help` expose only functional `preview` and `sync` verbs with pinned exit/stream contracts.
- [x] An unknown nested verb fails with valid choices and never dispatches a same-named top-level command.

baseline.description:
# Move fsck's shared filesystem primitives out of `fsck_repair.py`

## Context / Problem

Surfaced by the architectural analysis on `defaceable-icy-antelope`. Three pure filesystem primitives live in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`:

- `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` — resolve the tracker's git dir (handles the worktree pointer file);
- `_ticket_dirs` — the shared store-walk iterator (sorted ticket dirs, active-only by default);
- `_dir_is_archived` — the archival predicate `_ticket_dirs` filters with, and `fsck_scan`'s own
  import.

They are there for a historical reason, not a structural one: `fsck_repair` was the first module extracted out of `fsck.py`. The result is an inverted dependency — none of the three has anything to do with repair, yet **seven** production modules reach into the **repair** module for them:

| consumer | symbols | how |
|---|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py` | `_dir_is_archived`, `_ticket_dirs`, `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | module-level, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` | `_ticket_dirs`, `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | module-level re-export, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | **two** function-local imports, from `fsck` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | module-level, from `fsck` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` | `_ticket_dirs` | function-local, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/bridge_repair.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | function-local, from `fsck_repair` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py` | `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` | function-local, from `fsck_repair` |

So a store-layer module (`gitutil`) depends on a command-layer *repair* module to answer 'where is the tracker's git dir', and the diagnostic path cannot be read without loading the mutating one. A future non-fsck caller would have no reason to look for these under 'repair'.

## Approach

Move all three primitives to `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` and repoint every consumer.

**Why `gitutil`, and the circular-import check the move is conditioned on.** `gitutil` is a declared stdlib-only leaf: its module level imports `fcntl`/`logging`/`os`/`random`/`re`/ `subprocess`/`time` and **no** `rebar.*` module. Each moved primitive keeps that property: `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` and `_ticket_dirs` need only `os`, and `_dir_is_archived`'s `rebar.reducer._api._is_net_archived` import is already **function-local** and stays that way. Every consumer is a `_commands` module importing `_store`, which is the direction that already exists (`fsck_repair` imports `run_git` from `gitutil` at module level today). So the graph is acyclic and the `gitutil` default holds; a new `_store` leaf is not needed and would land under AGENTS.md's "never create files < 100 LOC by splitting" rule. AC6 checks this mechanically.

**Module size.** `gitutil` 614 -> ~665 LOC, `fsck_repair` 686 -> ~640 LOC; both stay under the 800-LOC hard cap.

**Compatibility surfaces that must survive — two, not one.**

1. `fsck.py` keeps re-exporting `_ticket_dirs` and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` (now imported from
   `gitutil`), so `fsck.<symbol>` attribute access keeps resolving. That surface is documented in
   the architectural-analysis comment on `defaceable-icy-antelope`, and is bound by
   `test_event_append_transient_retry.py`, `test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py`,
   `test_fsck_index_lock_reclaim_toctou.py` and `test_concurrency_regression.py`.
2. `fsck_repair.py` keeps **module-level bindings** for all three names (re-imported from
   `gitutil`). This is load-bearing and easy to miss: three tests bind the names as *module
   attributes on `fsck_repair`*, which the LSP cannot see — `monkeypatch.setattr(fsck_repair,
   "_ticket_dirs", ...)` / `..., "_resolve_tracker_git_dir", ...)` in
   `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` and
   `tests/interfaces/store/test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py`, and
   `_fsck_repair._ticket_dirs(...)` in `tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py`. Keeping them as
   `fsck_repair` module globals means those patches still take effect on `fsck_repair`'s own
   call sites (which resolve through the module global), so no test file needs editing (AC7).

The three function-local importers (`compact`, `bridge_repair`, `tracker_maintenance`) are repointed at `gitutil` rather than left riding `fsck_repair`'s compat re-import — leaving them would preserve the very inverted dependency this ticket removes.

Behaviour-preserving: no logic change, function bodies moved verbatim, imports repointed only.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the existing suite is the oracle and is run **unmodified** (AC7). The executable RED oracle for the move itself is the AC grep set: AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 all fail on `origin/main` and pass after the move, and that before/after run is recorded as a ticket comment.

The bindings at risk are the eight test files named above plus the fsck suites under `tests/interfaces/store/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: none of the three primitives is defined in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` —
      verified by
      `! grep -qE '^def (_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir|_dir_is_archived)' src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`
      exiting 0.
- [x] AC2: all three are defined in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — verified by
      `test "$(grep -cE '^def (_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir|_dir_is_archived)' src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py)" = 3`
      exiting 0.
- [x] AC3: no module under `src/rebar/` imports any of the three from `fsck` or `fsck_repair` —
      verified by
      `! grep -rqE 'from rebar\._commands\.fsck(_repair)? import.*(_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir|_dir_is_archived)' src/rebar/`
      exiting 0. (This covers the seven consumers, including the three function-local importers
      `compact.py`, `bridge_repair.py` and `tracker_maintenance.py`.)
- [x] AC4: the `fsck` re-export surface still resolves — verified by
      `python -c "from rebar._commands import fsck; fsck._resolve_tracker_git_dir; fsck._ticket_dirs"`
      exiting 0.
- [x] AC5: the `fsck_repair` module-attribute surface the un-editable tests patch still resolves —
      verified by
      `python -c "from rebar._commands import fsck_repair; fsck_repair._resolve_tracker_git_dir; fsck_repair._ticket_dirs; fsck_repair._dir_is_archived"`
      exiting 0.
- [x] AC6: the new home introduced no cycle and `gitutil` is still a stdlib-only leaf — verified by
      `python -c "import rebar._store.gitutil"` exiting 0 AND
      `! grep -qE '^(from|import) rebar' src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` exiting 0.
- [x] AC7: no test file is edited — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` producing
      no output.
- [x] AC8: `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] AC9: `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] AC10: `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0 (no `new`/`increased`).
- [x] AC11: `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exits 0.
- [x] AC12: every `src/rebar` file stays under the 800-LOC cap — verified by the CI module-size
      gate; locally `wc -l src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` both
      report < 800.
baseline.summary: fsck's shared filesystem primitives live in the repair module

## Summary

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`'s `mcp_run_new` carries `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'`, but NO test asserts it. Deleting that line leaves the whole suite green while every blue-green-deployed MCP container stops trusting nginx's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` — silently reinstating the HTTPS->HTTP downgrade that fernlike-toothsome-hen (79b2-6ebc-6c1d-4125) fixed, on the only path MCP actually ships through. The flag guards a P1 security fix and is itself unguarded.

Discovered while widening that ticket's file_impact: its plan claimed the compose-parity oracle covered this var. It does not. `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` has exactly one parity test, `test_autodeploy_mcp_run_new_passes_the_bedrock_region`, and it loops only over `_MCP_REGION_VARS = ("REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION", "AWS_DEFAULT_REGION")` (line 763). There is no `_ENV_FILE_ONLY` set in that file; the `.env` non-interpolation rationale lives separately in `test_autodeploy_carries_the_jira_variables_by_env_file_not_by_dash_e` (line 639).

Compose IS covered — `test_compose_mcp_trusts_the_edge_forwarded_proto` asserts `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS == "*"` on the `mcp` service. Only the autodeploy `docker run` is unguarded, and that is the path an actual deploy takes.

## Approach

Extend the existing parity coverage in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, reusing the helper that is already there:

1. `_mcp_run_new_body()` (line ~788) already extracts just the `mcp_run_new` body, so a match in
   a sibling function cannot count. Reuse it — do not re-read the script.
2. Add a test asserting the body contains the flag, mirroring the region test's substring form
   (`-e {var}=` or `-e "{var}=`), and additionally that the VALUE is the literal `*`, since a
   pinned bridge-gateway address is exactly the drift the compose test already rejects.
3. Keep it a separate named test rather than folding `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` into
   `_MCP_REGION_VARS` — that tuple is documented as the Bedrock region pair and is asserted
   against compose's region-agreement invariant, which does not apply to this var.

The mutation check that proves the test works: delete the `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'` line from `mcp_run_new` and confirm the new test goes RED (today nothing does), then restore it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` fails when `mcp_run_new`'s body does not
      pass `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`. Verified by deleting the `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'` line
      from `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` and observing that test go RED, then restoring it.
- [ ] That test also fails when the value is present but not the literal `*` (e.g. a pinned
      gateway address such as `172.17.0.1`). Verified by substituting that value and observing
      RED, then restoring.
- [ ] The test scopes its match to `mcp_run_new` only, via the existing `_mcp_run_new_body()`
      helper, so an occurrence in a sibling shell function cannot satisfy it. Verified by
      reading the test body.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` passes on unmodified `main`.

## Testing

Pure structural test over committed text — the same tier as the surrounding tests in that file. No nginx binary, no docker, no network.

## File impact

`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` (test-only; no source change — the flag it guards is already committed and deployed).

## Compat / rollback

Additive: one new test function. No production code changes. Rollback is deleting the test.

## Portability

Runs under plain `pytest` by parsing a committed file. No CI provider is involved and no deploy host is contacted, so it holds anywhere the repo is checked out.
baseline.summary: Guard the autodeploy FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS flag with a compose-parity test

## Why
The engine needs a lean DECLARATIVE IR expressing steps + conditionals + loops + map as DATA — the git source of truth, agent-editable, and projectable to a visual editor. v1 is a strict acyclic DAG whose only control flow is an `if:` skip-guard, which cannot express branching, loops, or fan-out.

## What
Define a v2 schema extending the v1 GitHub-Actions-style YAML: route/conditional edges, loop frames (mandatory max_iterations), and map/fan-out over a collection; stable step ids. Add a v1->v2 migration shim and update the linter so cycles are legal ONLY via declared loop frames (raw `needs` cycles still rejected), with frame-scoped reference integrity and map `as` binding checks.

## Scope
- src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v2.schema.json (additionalProperties:false retained)
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/schema.py, lint.py, migrate.py
Out: the interpreter (separate story).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] workflow.v2.schema.json adds route/loop/map constructs; additionalProperties:false retained.
- [ ] v1->v2 migrate shim registered in migrate.py with a golden round-trip test.
- [ ] Linter: raw `needs` cycles rejected; declared loop frames legal; frame-scoped reference checks; map `as` binding validated.
- [ ] Registry/coverage guard passes.
baseline.summary: v2 declarative IR: schema, linter, and v1-to-v2 migration

## Discovered from

CI run 32553346737 on Gerrit change 2065 (ticket d893-e003-0539-47fc): pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.12) failed tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_manifest_file_scope_contract_preserves_legacy_bytes with 'rebar-version: 0.12.0 (f5fb6e45-dirty)' != 'rebar-version: 0.12.0 (f5fb6e45)' — the -dirty suffix flipped BETWEEN two build_manifest calls inside one test. The same test passes locally.

## Root cause (confirmed by deterministic reproduction)

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:497 stamps every manifest with `_signing.gate_code_version()`, which shells `git status --porcelain` on the rebar source checkout PER CALL (src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py:_gate_commit_sha). Two byte-equality tests compare manifests built by SEPARATE calls:

- tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:965-966 (test_manifest_file_scope_contract_preserves_legacy_bytes)
- tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py:79 (equality of two build_manifest outputs)

Under pytest-xdist another worker that transiently creates/removes a file in the checkout (or any concurrent writer) flips the dirty-state between the calls, so the assertion compares racy live-git provenance rather than the file-scope/pins contract under test. Reproduced deterministically: creating a scratch file in the checkout between the two calls makes the equality fail with exactly the CI diff.

## Approach

Pin the provenance in the affected test: monkeypatch `rebar.signing.gate_code_version` to a constant in test_manifest_file_scope_contract_preserves_legacy_bytes — manifest.py binds `from rebar import signing as _signing` (manifest.py:475) and calls `_signing.gate_code_version()` at call time (manifest.py:497), so pinning the attribute on the `rebar.signing` facade module is what the call site actually resolves through; no production code changes. This is the exact pattern the OTHER byte-equality test already uses: tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py::test_no_pins_preserves_legacy_manifest_bytes already monkeypatches `rebar.signing.gate_code_version` to a constant around its line-79 equality, A second unpinned site exists in the same class: tests/unit/test_gate_engine_cutover.py::test_manifest_is_deterministic_and_path_independent byte-compares separately-built manifests (m1 == m2 at lines 48-50, and the m3 comparison after it) with no gate_code_version pin — pin it the same way. After this fix every manifest byte-equality test in the repo is pinned and the flake class is closed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] test_manifest_file_scope_contract_preserves_legacy_bytes pins
      `rebar.signing.gate_code_version` (monkeypatch, like
      test_no_pins_preserves_legacy_manifest_bytes) and passes even when a file is created in
      the checkout between its build_manifest calls — verified by running the test with the
      reproduction interleaving.
- [x] test_manifest_is_deterministic_and_path_independent (tests/unit/test_gate_engine_cutover.py)
      pins `rebar.signing.gate_code_version` the same way around its manifest equalities.
- [x] A repo grep shows no remaining test byte-compares two separately-built manifests without
      pinning gate_code_version (tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py:79 is already pinned by
      its enclosing test test_no_pins_preserves_legacy_manifest_bytes).
baseline.summary: Manifest byte-equality tests sample live git dirty-state and flake under xdist

## Context

`docs/your-first-change.md` downloads the Gerrit hook directly, permits a small patch to bypass Gerrit, and recommends `recheck` when a failure appears flaky. Ticket fat-leaflike-canary introduced the tutorial. Tickets sultanlike-doughty-civet and sure-starred-springtail superseded its hook and retry instructions. Current project policy requires `make hooks`, Gerrit passage for every change to main, and root-cause work for nondeterministic tests.

## Plan

- Replace the direct hook download in `docs/your-first-change.md` with the supported `make hooks` command and revise the related setup guidance. Explain that `make hooks` installs and verifies the Gerrit `Change-Id` hook.
- State that every change to main passes through Gerrit. Describe maintainer sponsorship as assistance with the ticket and contribution without permitting a review bypass.
- Reserve `recheck` for demonstrated environmental faults. Direct nondeterministic test failures to root-cause remediation through the `/rebar-debug` workflow in `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`.
- Add `tests/unit/test_your_first_change_guidance.py`. Positive assertions will require `make hooks`, Gerrit passage for every main change, sponsorship without a bypass, environmental-only `recheck` guidance, and the debugging workflow reference.
- Add negative assertions that reject the direct `curl` hook download, the phrase `skips Gerrit entirely`, instructions to use `recheck` when a failure only looks flaky, and the permissive `Likely a CI flake` guidance. These assertions ensure the new guidance cannot coexist with the superseded instructions.
- Run `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_your_first_change_guidance.py -q`, `python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check`, `python scripts/check_dco_identity.py`, and `git diff --check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The tutorial installs hooks only through `make hooks`, and direct hook download instructions are absent.
- [x] The tutorial states that every change to main passes through Gerrit.
- [x] Maintainer sponsorship is described without a Gerrit bypass, and the prior bypass language is absent.

# Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (approved pre-redesign changes)

## Why
Adjudication of would-block/near-block plan-review findings showed the gate UNDER-blocks: 15/20 findings in the 0.60-0.69 band on blocking criteria were block-worthy with ZERO false-positives, and four currently-advisory criteria (G1G2, T1, T8, E4) scored 75-100% block-worthy at their would-block slice. The 0.70 bar strands real blocks and the blocking set omits load-bearing criteria. (E1 and T3 also scored ~75% but are NOT promoted here — no threshold cleanly separates their borderline findings; deferred.)

## What
Apply the approved per-criterion thresholds/postures in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`:
- Lower `block_threshold` 0.70 -> 0.60 for exactly: COH, E2, F1, G5, G6, T5e.
- Keep T4 @ 0.70 (its band findings were fail-safe migrations).
- Promote to `default_posture: blocking`: G1G2 @0.70, T1 @0.70, T8 @0.70, and E4 @0.75.
- E1, T3, A1 remain advisory. No other criterion changes.

## Scope
- Edit only the routing JSON + the plan-review unit tests asserting per-criterion `block_threshold` /
  `default_posture`. No engine or aggregation changes here (the impact redesign is a separate child).
- This is a deliberate BREAKING behavioral change: plans that passed before may now BLOCK. Rollout is
  coupled to the permissive-rollout child (ship the wider set first, tune via the calibration harness);
  rollback is reverting the JSON (single-commit, trivially reversible).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `criteria_routing.json` matches the table above EXACTLY (per-criterion `block_threshold` +
      `default_posture`); a test asserts each of the SIX lowered (COH/E2/F1/G5/G6/T5e @ 0.60) + the FOUR
      promoted (G1G2/T1/T8 blocking @ 0.70, E4 blocking @ 0.75) + T4 UNCHANGED (@ 0.70, blocking).
- [ ] Plan-review unit tests updated and green; `make lint` passes. Proving command:
      `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py -v`.
- [ ] DETERMINISTIC simulation (no live corpus): using the packaged routing + the shared
      `threshold_for` / `pass3_decide`, a test asserts that for EACH of the six lowered criteria a synthetic
      finding at priority 0.65 now BLOCKS (>= 0.60) whereas at the OLD 0.70 it would NOT have; and that for
      EACH of the four promoted criteria the posture is now `blocking` and a finding blocks only at/above its
      NEW threshold (0.70 or 0.75). (Live-corpus block-rate delta on the accumulated sidecar corpus is
      measured by the calibration child raptorial-galloping-dragon, NOT gated here.)
- [ ] No criterion OUTSIDE the approved set {COH,E2,F1,G5,G6,T5e,T4,G1G2,T1,T8,E4} changes posture or
      threshold. A test pins the COMPLETE expected routing as an INLINE fixture inside
      `tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py` — a dict mapping EVERY criterion id to its expected
      `(block_threshold, default_posture)` — and asserts the packaged `criteria_routing.json` matches it
      exactly. Any unintended change to ANY criterion (approved or not) fails the assertion; the expectation
      lives in the test (versioned with it), so there is NO separate baseline snapshot file to drift.
baseline.summary: Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (approved pre-redesign changes)

## Why

`server.json` is the MCP registry front-door contract, but it has drifted from
the real config surface. It lists only `REBAR_ROOT`, `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`, and
the **deprecated** `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE`, while the actual gates are
`mcp.allow_llm` (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`) and `mcp.allow_jira_sync`
(`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`). Users see the LLM/reconcile tools appear but fail
at call time with no manifest hint, and new installs inherit deprecated
terminology. Nothing prevents this from re-drifting.

## What

- Update `server.json` `environmentVariables` to the current contract: add
  `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` with accurate
  descriptions; keep `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` only if explicitly labeled
  a deprecated alias (prefer replacing it with the current name).
- Add a **CI drift-guard** that compares the manifest's advertised env-var set
  against the canonical gate list in code (the `REBAR_MCP_*` env gates read in
  `mcp_server.py` / the readonly+allow gates), failing the build on divergence —
  mirroring the existing prompt-index / criteria-routing drift gates in
  `.github/workflows/test.yml`.

## Scope

`server.json` + one CI gate (a small script under `scripts/` or a step in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Identify the single source of truth for the env
gates so the guard has an authoritative list to diff against. No behavior change
to the server itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `server.json` advertises `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and
  `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` with correct descriptions.
- [ ] The deprecated `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` is removed or explicitly
  marked as a deprecated alias.
- [ ] A CI gate fails when `server.json`'s env-var set diverges from the
  canonical `REBAR_MCP_*` gate list in code.
- [ ] The gate passes on the corrected manifest; `make lint` stays green.
baseline.summary: Fix server.json MCP env/config contract and add a CI drift-guard

# WS-EVAL-EXISTING — make the migrated reviewers regression-gated

## Why

`verify_completion`, `review_ticket`, and `scan_spec` migrated onto the engine but
have NO standing eval coverage, so a prompt edit or migration is a blind cutover.
Worse, the eval LIVE tier is currently an unwired stub (`run_eval()` raises
NotImplementedError; deterministic scorer NAMES are inert strings with no registry
that executes them; the `eval-live` promptfoo step is a placeholder echo). So even the
4 existing plan-review/code-quality specs are validated for shape but never SCORED.

## What

Deliver eval coverage that actually gates, for the 3 uncovered reviewers, by also
finishing the shared eval-execution machinery (which benefits all 7 specs). Design
aligns with 2025-26 community consensus: a cheap DETERMINISTIC gate on every PR
(eval-discipline, zero-cost) and an expensive LLM-JUDGE tier OFF the PR critical path
(eval-live: manual + weekly schedule, non-blocking, cached, concurrency-capped).

## Scope (delivered via task children)

- Phase 1: author 3 eval specs (completion-verifier, ticket-quality, spec-alignment) + offline discipline tests.
- Phase 2: 2.1 deterministic-scorer registry + impls; 2.2 live solver w/ context-injection + repo-tool stubbing
  (the 3 reviewers read the store + repo via tools, so they are NOT inline-feedable); 2.3 per-reviewer dataset
  schema + validation (incl. scan_spec BATCH unit); 2.4 fixture corpus + label adjudication
  (completion-verifier FAIL findings need source-citation fixtures); 2.5 Inspect Task glue + eval-live CI wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 3 packaged eval specs exist and are validate_eval_spec-clean with disciplined cross-family judges (gates:false), at_least(k)/epochs, coverage threshold, non-empty gold_set.
- [ ] A deterministic-scorer registry exists; every scorer name used by all 7 specs maps to an implemented pure function; validate_scorer rejects unregistered names.
- [ ] `run_eval()` runs live for all dataset-bearing specs (no longer NotImplementedError) via a native loop over the eval solver (Inspect AI intentionally not used — rationale in eval.py); the 3 agentic reviewers run against a disposable fixture store via the solver.
- [ ] `eval-discipline` CI gates all 7 specs on every PR at zero API cost; offline tests assert dataset balance + non-empty gold_set (validate_eval_spec does not).
- [ ] `eval-live` runs on workflow_dispatch + weekly schedule, non-blocking, response-cached, concurrency-capped, fork-safe; provider spend-cap guidance documented.
baseline.summary: WS-EVAL-EXISTING: regression-gate completion-verifier/ticket-quality/spec-alignment (Phase 1+2)

baseline.description:
## Operator-stated north star (2026-08-14)
The completion verifier began as a SIMPLE harness-native subagent/background agent: an independent agent with read-only tool access verifying a ticket's ACs before close. It was reliable. Runaway tool calls and context-window overruns — the failure modes ALL the banking/budget/recovery machinery exists to contain — only appeared after the transition from harness-native (DSO) to harness-independent (rebar). The only intended conceptual addition since is [operator-attested], a minor qualifier. Constraint: the verifier MUST stay harness-independent, on the same machinery as the rest of rebar. Goal: step back from the emergent complexity and refocus on a relatively simple, reliable validation that the ACs described in a ticket have actually been completed.

## Investigation directions
1. Root-cause the gap: why does rebar's structured_run loop wander where harness-native agents did not? Hypotheses: harness loops provided context compaction, higher-level search, and model-tuned stopping; rebar hands the model low-level read tools with no evidence pre-assembly, so every verdict is an open-ended search under a budget.
2. Invert the architecture — deterministic evidence PREPACK: assemble the obvious evidence up front (ticket + ACs + evidence comments; file_impact diffs/blobs at HEAD; commits carrying the ticket trailer; referenced test files; direct-child ticket summaries + their manifests) into the verifier's context, then ask for a single-pass verdict with a small bounded follow-up read allowance. A human reviewer works this way; searching should be the exception, not the mechanism.
3. Validate against data: the 7-day failure mining (session artifact verifier-failure-mining.md) shows exhaustion-before-evidence dominates. Re-run the mined corpus through a prepack prototype; measure false-unmet rate and tool-call counts.
4. Success criteria: typical story/bug close verdicts in ONE model call + few follow-up reads; false-unmet ~0 on the mined corpus; banking/recovery demoted to rarely-exercised fallback and enumerated as deletion candidates; budget machinery becomes a dumb runaway backstop only.
5. Relationship to in-flight work: 8d74 (generous budgets + child term + PASS-verdict cache) is interim symptom relief and stays; this ticket aims to make that machinery mostly unnecessary. New verifier complexity must henceforth justify itself against the simple-core goal.
baseline.summary: Simplify completion verification: evidence-prepacked single-pass verifier (harness-independent)

baseline.description:
## Context
Dependabot PR **#131** ("deps: bump the uv-lock group with 5 updates", branch `dependabot/uv/uv-lock-4320b5f53c`, opened 2026-08-19) is open and CANNOT be merged where it sits. GitHub is a read-only mirror that rejects direct pushes and PR merges; every change to `main` flows through Gerrit. So a dependabot PR only lands if someone re-authors it as a Gerrit change.

Precedent: `woodblock-gnatty-xiaosaurus` (5a90-ec98-af5a-48d0) did exactly this for PRs #129/#130 via Gerrit change 1832, merged 2026-08-17. Dependabot then auto-closed both PRs when the mirror picked up the landed commit. Expect the same mechanism here — but see AC5: it must be VERIFIED, not assumed.

## What the PR changes
Two files:
- `pyproject.toml` — one line: `"ruff==0.16.2"` -> `"ruff==0.16.3"`
- `uv.lock` — +81/-73

Five package updates:

| package | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| `botocore` | 1.43.70 | 1.43.72 |
| `genai-prices` | 0.1.2 | 0.1.3 |
| `json-repair` | 0.63.1 | 0.63.2 |
| `mypy` | 2.3.0 | 2.3.1 |
| `ruff` | 0.16.2 | 0.16.3 |

## This is NOT a pure lockfile bump — read this before planning
`mypy` and `ruff` ARE the typecheck and lint gates. Bumping them can surface findings the previous versions did not report, anywhere in the tree, in code this ticket did not otherwise touch. That is the substance of the work, not an obstacle to it:

- New findings must be FIXED, not suppressed. Do not add `# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, or per-rule
  exclusions to make a new gate version quiet — that converts a tool upgrade into hidden debt and
  defeats the reason for upgrading.
- If a new rule is genuinely unwanted for this project, that is a DELIBERATE configuration decision
  and belongs in its own ticket with its rationale, not smuggled in beside a version bump.
- If the fallout is large enough to dominate the change, STOP and report rather than absorbing it.
  Splitting "bump the tools" from "fix what the new tools found" into stacked changes is the correct
  response to a big blast radius, and is cheaper than one unreviewable change.
- The complexity ratchet (`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py`) is shrink-only. A newer ruff may
  score an unchanged function differently; if that trips the ratchet, fix by behaviour-preserving
  extraction, NEVER by editing `.github/complexity-baseline.json` (`--lock`/`--update-stale` are
  maintenance-only, not a contributor escape hatch).

## Verify before acting
Dependabot may supersede #131 with a newer grouped PR before this ticket is worked. Re-check `gh pr view 131 --repo navapbc/rebar` first. If it is closed or superseded, do NOT re-apply stale pins — record the finding and close this ticket as superseded, naming the PR that replaced it. Re-pinning versions that a later PR has already moved past actively fights dependabot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] PR #131 is confirmed still open and current at the time work begins; if superseded, this
      ticket is closed as superseded naming the replacement PR, and no code change is made.
- [x] `pyproject.toml` pins `ruff==0.16.3`, and `uv.lock` records botocore 1.43.72,
      genai-prices 0.1.3, json-repair 0.63.2, mypy 2.3.1 and ruff 0.16.3. The lock is regenerated
      with the project's own uv workflow, not hand-edited.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass under the NEW ruff and mypy. Any newly-surfaced finding
      is fixed in the code; no `# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, or rule exclusion is added to silence
      one. The complexity baseline file is unmodified.
- [x] **The change LANDS**: pushed to Gerrit, `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` with no unresolved
      comments, submitted, and merged to `main`. The ticket records the change number and the
      merged commit sha.
- [x] **PR #131 is CLOSED**: verified closed after the merge via
      `gh pr view 131 --repo navapbc/rebar --json state`. If dependabot has not auto-closed it
      within a reasonable window after the mirror syncs, close it manually with a comment naming
      the Gerrit change and merged commit that superseded it. Do not leave it open on the
      assumption that automation will get to it.

## Testing
`make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite must pass on the new pins. Because the bump touches the lint and typecheck tools, a green run is the evidence that the upgrade is complete — not merely that the lockfile parses.
baseline.summary: Land dependabot PR #131 (uv-lock group: botocore, genai-prices, json-repair, mypy, ruff) via Gerrit and close the PR

baseline.description:
## Why

Cross-system sync (Jira today; Linear / GitHub Issues planned) must propagate a LOCAL removal of a reference (detach a parent, unlink a dependency) WITHOUT it being resurrected by the next inbound pass. The naive approach — gate outbound DELETE on an 'ever-seen' set projected from raw event history (as `local_label_intent` does for labels) — fails CLOSED across `compact_ticket`: compaction collapses the event log to a SNAPSHOT whose `compiled_state` holds only CURRENT refs, so a removal performed at/after the compaction boundary is re-resurrected (the exact churn). We also found the shipped parent CLEAR (drum-ruler-suit / PR #54) is un-gated and clobbers a human-set-in-Jira parent on a locally-parentless ticket.

The field (Unito/Exalate/FolderSync/Syncthing/ghas-jira-integration) validates the intent-gate concept; the load-bearing risks are state DURABILITY and unbounded growth. This story builds the durable, reusable primitive ONCE so parent + links (and future peers) share one provider-agnostic pattern.

## What

A monotonic, compaction-surviving `managed_refs` provenance set maintained by the reducer in `compiled_state` (so `process_snapshot` restores it for free across compaction), plus a shared, provider-agnostic gate the outbound differ uses to decide REMOVE-vs-ADOPT for any reference kind.

- `managed_refs`: the union of every logical reference this ticket has ever managed — normalized `(kind, target_local_id)` where kind in {parent, blocks, depends_on, relates_to}. Folded in process_create (initial parent + deps), process_link, and parent EDIT (incl. inbound-adopted refs); STRICTLY MONOTONIC — never reduced by UNLINK/detach. Deterministically serialized (sorted list) for SNAPSHOT byte-parity.
- Shared gate `should_propagate_removal(ref, managed_refs) -> bool`: a peer ref present + locally absent => propagate DELETE iff ref in managed_refs; else ADOPT inbound. Provider-agnostic (operates on local logical refs; each provider maps to its entity). Missing/absent managed_refs defaults to EMPTY => the gate returns False (degrade to additive-only: no remove, no clobber, no churn-delete). This is also the back-out posture — disabling the fold leaves the gate a safe no-op.

## Migration (existing + pre-feature tickets)

On the FIRST reduce/restore where `managed_refs` is absent (old SNAPSHOT, pre-feature ticket), the reducer SEEDS it from the ticket's CURRENT deps + parent_id. Seeding is safe in both directions: a ref already in local deps was either created locally or inbound-ADOPTED (rebar owns it -> removable); a Jira-only ref never in local deps is not seeded -> still adopted, never clobbered. A new event type / field is preserved-and-ignored by older clones (forward-compatible rollout; fsck WARNs on newer-than-binary state).

## Reclamation (bounded growth)

managed_refs is strictly monotonic in the reducer (no prune there — pruning in the UNLINK path would contradict monotonicity and re-open the resurrection window). Per-ticket ref cardinality is small (tens), so unbounded growth is not a practical concern at this scale. A safe reclamation requires the PEER snapshot (a ref converged = absent locally AND absent on the peer) and therefore must be a reconcile-time step emitting an explicit prune event — that is documented as a FUTURE hook and is OUT OF SCOPE for v1 (deferring it avoids the prune-vs-fold concurrency hazard entirely).

## Scope

In scope: the reducer `managed_refs` field + compaction preservation + byte-parity + migration-seeding; the shared provider-agnostic gate helper (with its own unit tests); docs establishing the reusable pattern. The parent + link CONSUMER integrations are delivered by the child tickets (tan-elbow-mica, wake-inn-parse) which import this gate; THIS story verifies the gate's API + decision via unit tests, not cross-ticket call-sites. Out of scope: active reclamation/GC (future reconcile-time prune); actual Linear/GitHub providers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reducer maintains `compiled_state.managed_refs` as a strictly-monotonic, deterministically-sorted union of normalized (kind, target) refs, folded from CREATE/LINK/parent-EDIT (including inbound-adopted), never reduced by UNLINK/detach.
- [ ] When `managed_refs` is absent on reduce/restore (pre-feature / old SNAPSHOT), the reducer seeds it from current deps + parent_id; a test proves a pre-feature compacted ticket's existing refs become managed (its later unlink propagates).
- [ ] `managed_refs` survives `compact_ticket` (restored by process_snapshot): a removal performed before OR after a compaction boundary still propagates and does NOT resurrect — covered by a compact-then-reconcile test.
- [ ] SNAPSHOT byte-parity is preserved (deterministic serialization; the existing byte-parity guard passes).
- [ ] A shared `should_propagate_removal(ref, managed_refs)` gate exists, is provider-agnostic (no Jira-specific logic), defaults missing managed_refs to empty (returns False = no removal), and is unit-tested for the REMOVE-vs-ADOPT decision: a managed ref absent locally => propagate; a never-managed peer ref => adopt.
- [ ] An operator-facing regression proves the churn is observably fixed: unlink a managed ref locally, run two reconcile passes, the ref stays removed (not resurrected).
- [ ] docs/ documents the pattern (the gate contract + the managed_refs field + the future reconcile-time reclamation hook) as the template for future peer-sync providers.
- [ ] A reusable, provider-agnostic managed-ref provenance primitive both parent and link removal sync consume, with no Jira-specific logic in the shared gate.
baseline.summary: Managed-reference provenance: a compaction-surviving, provider-agnostic removal-sync gate
