## Summary
The scheduled **Live External Integration** run on 2026-08-17 (run 32000764439, job "jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)") failed `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py::test_capability_stamp_and_fail_closed` with:

```
E   subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git', 'commit', '-q', '--no-verify', '-m', 'commit scratch mapping (368f scenario 9)']' returned non-zero exit status 1.
...
nothing to commit, working tree clean
```

Scenario 9 writes a bridge-project mapping via `rebar.bridge_projects_set(...)` into the throwaway store worktree, then commits it with `git commit -q --no-verify -m 'commit scratch mapping (368f scenario 9)'`. The commit exits 1 because the tree is **clean** — `bridge_projects_set` left nothing to commit — so `subprocess.run(check=True)` raised.

Story 368f documented the scenario's assumption explicitly: *"`bridge_projects_set` writes the mapping to the WORKTREE but never commits it."* The "nothing to commit" failure means that assumption no longer holds — most likely `bridge_projects_set` now **auto-commits** the mapping itself (so the harness's explicit commit finds a clean tree), or it writes to a path the harness does not stage.

## Regression window
NEW regression, same window as sibling bug superior-pinelike-garpike:
- 2026-08-15 run 31879125045 (jira DC job 94999114642): **73 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed**.
- 2026-08-17 run 32000764439: **2 failed, 71 passed, 1 xfailed** — this is the second new failure.

A change between 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-17 altered `bridge_projects_set`'s write/commit semantics (or the store-copy staging). Bisect `bridge_projects_set` and `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` (cf. epic 0e68 / story 368f).

## Impact
The multi-project capability-stamp + fail-closed live rehearsal is red. If `bridge_projects_set` changed to auto-commit, the behavior change is undocumented and the harness must be aligned; if the mapping write silently no-ops, it is a product regression. Either way the "commit the mapping, then assert the capability stamp + fail-closed" scenario cannot run.

## The regression escaped because only a LIVE test covered it
Per triage guidance: a live-external regression must be reproducible by a NON-external test so CI catches it without the live suite. Today only the live DC rehearsal exercises this.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Determine the actual post-change write semantics of `bridge_projects_set` (does it commit internally now, or leave a dirty tree?) — record the finding.
- [x] A **RED** non-external test (unit/integration, no live DC/creds) pins the intended `bridge_projects_set` write-and-commit contract (whether it commits, and what the worktree state is afterward) — asserted to FAIL against current `main` if this is a product regression; if the change is intended, the test encodes the NEW contract and the rehearsal harness is corrected to match.
- [x] Root cause fixed (product write path) OR harness/scenario corrected to the intended contract, with the reason recorded.
- [x] The new non-external test passes.
- [x] The live rehearsal `test_capability_stamp_and_fail_closed` passes in the next Live External Integration run. [operator-attested]

## Evidence
- Failing run: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/32000764439 (job: jira DC harness smoke)
- Test: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py::test_capability_stamp_and_fail_closed`
- Delivered by story 368f (gasolinic-microbian-puffin), epic 0e68 (outrageous-uncultured-wildebeast).
baseline.summary: Live Jira DC rehearsal: bridge_projects_set leaves nothing to commit — test_capability_stamp_and_fail_closed fails (git commit exit 1, 'nothing to commit')

baseline.description:
Reported by a rebar client (report archived at `~/rebar-archived-child-claim-bug.md` on the operator host) against `nava-rebar 0.10.1` (source build at `f0cf30a0e` + `bcb735630`) with `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true`. **The divergence is reproduced in current `main`**, so this is not fixed by upgrading.

## Symptom

When a container ticket has a child whose status is `archived`, `rebar review-plan <container>` signs a material fingerprint computed over a child set that **includes** the archived child, while the claim gate recomputes the fingerprint over a child set that **excludes** it. The two can never agree, so every `review-plan` → `claim` sequence fails with:

```
Error: cannot start work on <id>: the plan was materially edited since review
(description/AC/file_impact/children changed).
```

Re-running `review-plan` cannot break the loop: each new attestation re-signs the same larger basis the gate will again recompute smaller. The recovery the error itself prints ("run the plan review to earn an attestation, then start work") is non-terminating for this ticket shape.

## Impact

Any container that has ever had a child archived — a normal board outcome when a child is superseded or found to be a duplicate — becomes permanently unclaimable through the supported path. The only exits are `claim --force` (which discards the very gate the config exists to enforce) or mutating the board to detach/unarchive the child. The message is also actively misleading: it reports a plan edit that did not happen, sending the operator to hunt a phantom description change.

## Reproduction

1. Create an epic with N children, each with a `file_impact`.
2. Archive one child. It keeps `parent_id=<epic>`, gains `status=archived`.
3. `rebar review-plan <epic>` → `PASS`, signed.
4. `rebar claim <epic>` → fails with "the plan was materially edited since review".
5. Repeat 3–4 any number of times; identical failure, no edit in between.

## Reporter's evidence (measured, not inferred)

Epic `5bb5-2a98-b054-4d66` in the reporter's store: 12 live children plus archived child `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d` (`parent_id=5bb5-2a98-b054-4d66`, `status=archived`). Both fingerprints were reproduced by re-implementing the basis from `material_fingerprint`:

| child set | fingerprint | computed by |
|---|---|---|
| 13 ids (incl. `fb45`) | `084b676f66849bab` | value embedded in the signed attestation |
| 12 ids (excl. `fb45`) | `236d5fa9f6944e87` | `attest.current_material_fingerprint()` at claim time |

- `rebar._reads.list_tickets(parent=<epic>)` returns 12 deterministically (three separate
  processes); `fb45` is absent.
- The stored attestation's `material:` manifest line is `084b676f66849bab`.
- The epic's *original* attestation (signed earlier, by a different operator) carries 13
  `plan-material-pin: child …` lines including `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d` — the review side has been
  enumerating the archived child **consistently**, not intermittently.

## Root cause (confirmed in this checkout, current `main`)

The reporter narrowed the divergence to "somewhere below `list_tickets`" and named a relation snapshot as a likely candidate. That is correct — the two sides do not in fact share an enumeration:

- **Gate side** — `attest.current_material_fingerprint()`
  (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:771`) calls
  `_reads.list_tickets(parent=canonical)`, whose default is `include_archived=False`
  (`src/rebar/_reads.py:87`) → **archived children excluded**.
- **Signer side** — the signed generation's `own_material` is computed in
  `generation.from_snapshot()` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:84`) from
  `snapshot.child_ids`, which `collect_plan_relation_snapshot()` builds by scanning reduced
  states and admitting every candidate whose parent resolves to the subject and whose
  `status != "deleted"` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:283`) → **archived
  children included**.

So the divergence is the archived-vs-deleted predicate: the snapshot filters only `deleted`, while `list_tickets` filters `archived` too. `current_material_fingerprint`'s docstring claims it is "matching `orchestrator.material_fingerprint`" — that stated invariant is what is broken, and nothing enforces it because the child predicate is spelled independently at each site.

## Fix direction

Exclude non-live children (archived, deleted) from the material basis, and apply that policy in **one shared helper both the signer and the gate call** rather than independently at two sites. Material is meant to capture *the plan*, and an archived child is no longer part of the plan; this is also what the gate already does, so the gate becomes correct by definition and only the signer changes.

Deliberately **not** choosing the symmetric alternative (include archived on both sides): that would make archiving a child a *material edit*, invalidating a parent's attestation for a board action that changed no plan content — trading this bug for a subtler one. The reporter reached the same conclusion independently.

Note `relation_snapshot.child_ids` also feeds `related_material` and the per-child `plan-material-pin` manifest lines, so the change must keep those consistent with the new basis (archived children should stop being pinned), and existing attestations that pin an archived child must not be treated as forgeries — only as stale in the ordinary way.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A single shared helper defines "children that count as plan material" (live only: excludes
   `archived` and `deleted`), and both `generation.from_snapshot()`/`collect_plan_relation_snapshot()`
   and `attest.current_material_fingerprint()` obtain their child set through it — no
   independently spelled status predicate remains at either site.
2. Regression test: archive a child of a container, then `review-plan` → `claim` succeeds.
   Currently fails.
3. ~~Regression test: archiving a child alone does **not** invalidate a container's existing
   valid attestation (material fingerprint unchanged across the archive).~~
   **AMENDED — the original AC3 was unsatisfiable together with AC1.** Once archived children
   are excluded from the material basis (AC1's "live only"), archiving a child necessarily
   removes it from that basis and so necessarily MOVES the fingerprint. The rationale above had
   this inverted: it is the *include-archived-on-both-sides* option that would leave the
   fingerprint untouched, not the exclude option that was chosen. Replacement AC3:

   **Regression test: the signer-side and gate-side fingerprints agree BOTH before and after a
   child is archived.** That is the invariant that actually cures the bug. The accepted residual
   cost is explicit: archiving a child invalidates the container's attestation and requires a
   fresh `review-plan`. That is recoverable, unlike the permanent unclaimable loop this bug
   caused, and it is the price of keeping "material" mean "the live plan".
4. Regression test asserting the docstring invariant directly: for a container with a mix of
   live, archived, and deleted children, the signer-side fingerprint and
   `current_material_fingerprint()` are equal.
5. `plan-material-pin` manifest lines for the container no longer include archived children,
   and an attestation signed *before* the fix (pinning an archived child) is handled as stale /
   re-reviewable, not as a signature failure.
6. Full suite, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` green.

## Workarounds until fixed

- Detach the archived child from the parent (`rebar edit <child> --parent=null`) so both sides
  enumerate the same set, then re-run `review-plan` and `claim`. The reporter applied this to
  `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d`, which is now unparented in their store.
- `rebar claim <id> --force="<reason>"` works but discards the gate.
baseline.summary: Archived child permanently blocks claim on its parent: signer includes it in the material basis, claim gate excludes it

baseline.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in **bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json` (1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40 consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x), and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git — an earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and dropped re-homing it off-branch (WS-1) because the convergence loop already self-heals binding drift. So the levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included (child A6) under an operator-approved quiescence protocol. Its mechanics are **proven, not theoretical**: `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` on the real branch produced 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%) with all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges preserved and the HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths. Stock git plumbing only — `git-filter-repo` is deliberately **not** used: it is an unwanted core dependency and it prunes empty commits, which would reshape the DAG that ancestry-based authorship verification walks.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` + write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`
2. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; read `max(new, legacy)`
3. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority (exclude `assignee`)
4. **A2-2** delete the legacy in-line `last_get_pass` field (gated on writer rollout)
5. **A4-1/2/3** `bridge_fsck` fence, then `prev_snapshot` -> key-set, then branch-3 empty-payload skip
6. **A5** ADR covering all three committed-format changes
7. **A6** one-time reclaim under the quiescence protocol (LAST; requires A1-A5 and Epic B's B6)

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes to a shared store file, each with a stated boundary. A2-1 is reversible (it never stops writing the legacy field). A3 is reversible because the read path canonicalizes both shapes idempotently. A2-2 and A4-2 are the irreversible steps: A2-2 is gated on observed writer rollout; reverting A4-2 requires the reverse-direction corpus diff recorded first. A6 is gated on an off-repo backup bundle plus a fail-closed epoch guard, and its resumability is explicitly **none** — mitigated by running every correctness assertion on a scratch clone before anything is published.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline today 12.79 KB.
      Verify: the measurement script recorded in the child ticket.
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: integration against a stateful fake asserting
      file bytes and commit count, not call counts.
- [ ] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference to it remains. Verify: `grep -r baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty) — the read-only path must not persist a migration.
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the same
      verdict as its normalized-string equivalent. This test does not exist today; the existing
      cells use flat strings only, so a no-op-on-strings normalizer would pass while proving
      nothing. Tier: integration through the real production comparison path.
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over >=4 real snapshot pairs shows zero
      difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect, **and** the reverse-direction
      diff is recorded as the A4-2 rollback artifact.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` is **<=800 LOC** after the rotation extraction (it is at exactly 800
      today; the locked module-size gate fails the build on 801).
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB**, `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded
      pre-rewrite tip tree, and commit and merge-commit counts are unchanged (measured at window
      time, not hardcoded).
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** (the assertion that actually proves non-resurrection) and
      `size-pack` growth is <1 MB.
- [ ] A clone on a stale epoch attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites (`sync._union_merge` and `push.py`'s non-FF retry). Tier: integration in two
      real temporary clones with divergent epochs.
- [ ] An ADR exists enumerating all three committed-format changes, the mixed-version protocol, the
      A2-2 gate, and each rollback boundary.
- [ ] The off-repo backup bundle exists and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] Operator has confirmed zero active sessions and all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped before the
      reclaim window. **[operator-attested]**
baseline.summary: Bound tickets-store growth: make the committed .bridge_state cache cheap + one-time reclaim of the spent ~1 GiB

baseline.description:
# Surface the ref + source controls on the CLI and MCP tool schemas

## Why

The new `ref` + `source` controls must be reachable by both human (CLI) and agent (MCP)
clients, so a distributed team can target the exact code version a gate runs against.

## What

- Add `--ref <branch|tag|sha>` (default `origin/main`) and `--source {attested|local}` to the
  code-reading surfaces, with the CLI<->MCP mapping pinned explicitly (no "surfaces as they
  exist"):
  - MCP tools: `review_plan`, `verify_completion`, `review_ticket`, `review_code`, `scan_spec`.
  - CLI counterparts (the same five operations as exposed by the CLI); enumerate the exact
    command names in the implementation and keep the two surfaces in lockstep (resolve the
    review/review_plan and code-review/review_code naming so coverage matches one-to-one).
- Document defaults + surface `verified_at_sha` in attested results (outputSchema/text).
- Decouple the verified-code path from the MCP server's cwd/branch; document that `REBAR_ROOT`
  only locates the object DB to fetch from.
- **Validation / failure paths** (not just happy path): an unresolvable or absent `ref`, an
  invalid `--source` value, and an unreachable/missing object DB at `REBAR_ROOT` each produce
  a clear, actionable error (attested fails closed; cf. S1 descriptive fetch/auth errors).
- **De-risk by vertical slice:** land ONE CLI command + ONE MCP tool end-to-end first
  (default `origin/main` resolve + attested `verified_at_sha` + `local`=unsigned) before
  fanning the two controls out across all five surfaces.

## Scope

- In: CLI flags, MCP tool-schema args, the pinned CLI<->MCP mapping, default wiring, failure/
  validation handling, surfacing `verified_at_sha`, the vertical-slice-first sequencing.
- Out: the underlying behavior (S1-S4); prose docs (S6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every code-reading CLI command AND its MCP tool counterpart accept `--ref`/`ref` and
      `--source`/`source` with documented defaults; the CLI<->MCP mapping covers the same five
      operations one-to-one (no naming-drift coverage gap).
- [ ] Omitting `--ref` resolves `origin/main` -> SHA (attested) and still signs (pin recorded);
      `--source=local` is reachable from both surfaces and reflected as unsigned in the result.
- [ ] Attested results surface `verified_at_sha`.
- [ ] An unresolvable/absent ref, an invalid `--source` value, and an unreachable object DB at
      `REBAR_ROOT` each return a clear actionable error (attested fails closed) — covered by tests.
- [ ] An AC verifies the cwd/branch decoupling: the verified-code path does not depend on the
      MCP server's checked-out branch; `REBAR_ROOT` only locates the object DB.
- [ ] A thin vertical slice (one CLI cmd + one MCP tool, end-to-end) lands before the full fan-out.

## Additional notes + Acceptance Criteria (advisory remediation)

- Pinned CLI<->MCP names (mirror the MCP tool names, confirm against the command registry):
  `review-plan`<->`review_plan`, `verify-completion`<->`verify_completion`,
  `review-ticket`<->`review_ticket`, `review-code`<->`review_code`, `scan-spec`<->`scan_spec`.
- `--source` default is `attested` (stated explicitly); `--ref` default is `origin/main`.
- The cross-surface contract (one-to-one CLI<->MCP mapping) and the cwd/branch decoupling
  (`REBAR_ROOT` only locates the object DB) are captured in the architecture ADR (S2/S4), so
  future maintainers don't re-couple the verified-code path to the server's checkout.
- Error recovery: each actionable error names the remedy target — an unresolvable/absent ref
  -> how to name a valid ref; an invalid `--source` -> the allowed enum; an unreachable
  `REBAR_ROOT`/object DB or missing credentials -> the setup-docs section (S6).

- [ ] The five CLI commands and five MCP tools are the pinned one-to-one set above (no
      naming-drift gap); `--source` defaults to `attested`, `--ref` to `origin/main`.
- [ ] Each failure-path error names its recovery target (valid-ref guidance / allowed --source
      enum / REBAR_ROOT+credentials docs), consistent across both surfaces.
- [ ] The cwd/branch decoupling + CLI<->MCP mapping are recorded in the architecture ADR.
baseline.summary: Surface the ref + source controls on the CLI and MCP tool schemas

baseline.description:
Move GET-rotation stamps into `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` so a later rollout step can remove them from the large sort-ordered `bindings.json`. A2-1 is the compatibility half: new binaries write both formats and read `max(new, legacy)`; A2-2 removes the legacy write after its observable rollout gate. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** contains the measured facts.

## Why

`set_last_get` stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit` (default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly 20 entries change per affected pass. The full A2 saving is realized only after A2-2 removes this scattered legacy write. During A2-1, dual-write is intentional compatibility cost: an old binary cannot read the sidecar, so it must still observe progress made by new binaries.

## Approach — compatibility first

Write every new stamp to the sidecar and the legacy inline field, and read the chronological `max(sidecar, legacy)`. Under mixed versions an old binary may advance only the inline field; `max()` ensures a following new binary does not use stale sidecar state. Conversely, dual-write ensures an old binary following a new one sees the new progress. Values are fixed-width zero-padded timestamps, so lexicographic `max()` is chronological.

Load legacy-only rotation state in memory and persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`. This covers all production save paths: end-of-pass persistence, the write-ahead saves in `dispatch_one.py`, and the recovery/retirement saves in `binding_store.py`. Saving unchanged canonical state must remain byte-stable. `reconcile-check` runs with `persist=False`, never reaches save, and must not create the sidecar.

Add `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE`, characterize its path, and include it in both `reconcile_helpers.py` explicit staging and basename membership checks. This is required because local reconciliation does not use `git add -A`. The existing `.gitattributes` glob covers the new file. Update the `_store/push.py` docstring that enumerates regenerable files.

`outbound_differ.py` is at the locked 800-line cap. Move the existing last-GET and best-effort bookkeeping wrappers across the new rotation seam so the module remains at or below the cap.

## Rollback

Reverting A2-1 is safe: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but every new-binary pass also advanced the inline legacy field. The orphaned sidecar is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Tier: integration in a real temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances identical selected-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Tier: integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Tier: real-git integration.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] Rotation order after an interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence matches the all-new sequence. Tier: integration; it must fail for either sidecar-first lookup or missing dual-write.

## Context
After family cutovers, reachable generic retry, `_best_effort` swallowing, duck-typed dispatch, or duplicate SDK/adapter retry would preserve the original failure class and invite future bypass.

## Outcome
Prove every supported Cloud/DC mutation has exactly one typed coordinator/adapter owner, remove obsolete production fallbacks, and fail unsupported live actions before any effect.

## Plan
1. Build a dispatch census over every `MutationDirection`/`MutationAction` and Cloud/DC provider route. Require one typed owner or an intentional provider-neutral pre-effect unsupported result.
2. Remove generic whole-operation retry, `_best_effort` write swallowing, production class-name/duck fallbacks, and duplicate SDK/adapter retry owners after their route is covered.
3. Keep compatibility only at serialized/public read boundaries; tests use explicit protocol fakes.
4. Add static/string and runtime poison tests that fail when removed helpers remain reachable from production.
5. Preserve rollback as code/routing reversion plus remote re-observation; never compensate by deleting successful Jira work.

## Testing
The census must fail on missing, duplicate, or fallback owners. Effect spies prove unsupported actions fail before local/remote writes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every supported Cloud/DC mutation route has exactly one typed coordinator/adapter owner.
- [x] Unsupported production actions return a typed provider-neutral error before any effect.
- [x] Generic whole-operation retry and `_best_effort` write swallowing are unreachable from production.
- [x] Production class-name/duck dispatch and duplicate SDK/adapter retry owners are unreachable.
- [x] Tests use explicit declared protocols rather than production fallback paths.
- [x] Rollback guidance requires re-observation and never remote deletion.

## Out of scope
Final output contracts, state advancement, end-to-end validation, and docs.

## Why
The agent landing contract only works if agents adopt it: the old "watch the 2 votes" model is now broken (two green votes no longer means "it will land" — a conflict blocks it while votes stay green). Docs must teach the new contract or the conflict case silently reintroduces babysitting.

## What
Rewrite this repo's landing section in `CLAUDE.md` + `CONTRIBUTING.md` to the new contract, and record the design in `docs/adr/0042-*.md`.

## Dependencies
Depends on **S1** (`sterilized-papery-horse`, 843b-801f-9ef9-442d) — the `Autosubmit` label — and **S4** (`brightish-growable-dodo`, 73f5-4df7-4fac-4738) — the `land` command: the docs must not merge to `main` until the label and command they instruct agents to use are actually live — otherwise the guide points at tooling that does not yet exist.

## Scope
Docs + ADR only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` + `CONTRIBUTING.md` landing section rewritten: "set `Autosubmit` / run `land`; act on the single typed outcome; do NOT watch votes or treat two green votes as 'it will land'."
- [ ] **Grep the whole repo** for the deprecated "two green votes" / "watch votes" pattern (e.g. in `docs/your-first-change.md`) and update **ALL** occurrences to the new contract — not only `CLAUDE.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0042-*.md` records the auto-lander design AND the rationale behind the key decisions, so future idea-epics inherit the "why", not just the "what". It MUST capture: the agent contract + outcome enum; the R5 safety invariant (tested tree = merged tree) and how each mechanism preserves it; the **eight key design decisions with their prior-art grounding** (Zuul / LUCI CV-Chromium CQ / Gerrit primitives / Prow-Tide) — the `Autosubmit`↔`CQ+2` label, the two-channel status surface, the CQ-reset hand-back, the raw time-to-land timer, the autoheal hang-recovery, the stdlib-not-pygerrit2 client choice, `rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader`, and the sentinel+drain stop; the separation-of-concerns boundary (project infra, not `rebar` core); the reliability posture + accepted single-instance SPOF tradeoff; and the **deferrals with their promotion triggers** — the provider-seam (idea `1701-8bc1-e3b7-4984`, promote on a 2nd landing platform), bounded-speculation batching (idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`, promote only on MEASURED serial-treadmill pain), and HA/external-state (promote if single-instance availability is insufficient). **Confirm both idea ids resolve in the store** and anchor ADR-0042 to them. (A full drafted record is attached as a comment on this ticket — land that content.)
- [ ] Docs cross-reference ADR-0040 (FFO) + ADR-0041 (LLM-Review `TRIVIAL_REBASE` carry) as the gate substrate the lander sits on.

baseline.description:
## Problem

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py::test_main_without_repo_root_passes_resolved_repo_root` failed CI (`AssertionError: check_pass_lock must be called when main() runs`), costing Gerrit change 1658 a spurious `Verified -1` in a file that change does not touch.

## Mechanism (confirmed against current main)

The suite already isolates every test from the enclosing checkout: an autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` (lines 268-281, bug dd62) defaults `REBAR_ROOT` to a sandbox repo, and its own docstring notes that a test which `delenv`s it escapes that default.

This test does exactly that (line 530) — deliberately, because the genuine depth-fallback `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]` is the thing under test. So `main()` runs against the REAL repository root. It patches `check_pass_lock`, `check_phase_gate`, `acquire_pass_lock` and `release_pass_lock`, but NOT `read_pause`.

In `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`, `_pause_exit_code` (line 160) runs BEFORE `_post_pause_preflight` (line 189), which is what calls `check_pass_lock`. `_pause_exit_code` calls `advisory.read_pause(repo_root)`, which raises `ReconcileGateError` on a corrupt gate ref (`_advisory_lock.py:232-238`) and returns early. So when the runner's checkout carries a corrupt or leftover `refs/reconciler/gate`, `main()` returns before `check_pass_lock` and the assertion fails through no fault of the code under test. The job log carries exactly that path's message. A merely PRESENT (uncorrupt) pause marker derails it the same way, via the PAUSED branch.

The defect is the unmocked `read_pause`: a unit test's outcome must not depend on the ambient refs of whatever checkout it happens to run in.

## Fix

Stub `read_pause` alongside the advisory calls already stubbed, so ambient gate state cannot reach `main()`, while `REBAR_ROOT` stays cleared and the repo-root RESOLUTION assertion the test exists for is preserved unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — The test no longer depends on the enclosing repo's `refs/reconciler/gate`:
      `read_pause` is stubbed, and the existing assertion that the resolved root contains
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` still holds. The test additionally
      asserts the stubbed `read_pause` was called with that same resolved root, so the
      resolution path stays pinned at the FIRST advisory call rather than only the later one.
- [x] AC2 — A regression test exists that injects the corrupt-gate condition at the layer
      BELOW the stub (`_advisory_lock._load_ref_lock` returning a ref-lock whose `read_pause`
      raises `RefLockCorruptError`) and asserts both that the resolution assertions still hold
      and that the corrupt layer is never reached.
- [x] AC3 [operator-attested] — Audit of the suite for tests that clear `REBAR_ROOT` and
      leave an advisory call unmocked; the result is stated in a comment on this ticket.
- [x] AC4 [operator-attested] — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the affected file pass.
baseline.summary: Reconciler main test reads real repo gate ref; corrupt ref flakes CI

baseline.description:
Delete `baseline_advanced_at` and stop rewriting an unchanged baseline. This is the single highest-value change in the epic: it cuts marginal packed cost per `bindings.json` version from **12.79 KB to 1.74 KB (7.4x)**, measured over 40 consecutive real revisions. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`binding_store.py:373-375` unconditionally rewrites `entry["baseline"]` and stamps `baseline_advanced_at = _now_iso()`. That field is written in exactly one place and **read nowhere in `src/`** (only asserted in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py:61`). Measured across consecutive committed revisions: baseline VALUES changed **0** entries while the stamp changed **1144** — a scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file, which is pathological for git delta compression.

Honest scoping: because baseline values change 0 entries/pass today, the write-when-changed guard is **byte-neutral** and the entire measured win comes from deleting the field. The guard is still worth adding — it is the correct behaviour once real Jira edits arrive, and it saves the rewrite CPU — but it must not be credited with the savings.

## Approach
In `set_baseline`: build the filtered baseline, compare to the existing one, return early if equal; never write `baseline_advanced_at`. Preserve `binding_store.py:374`'s `if k in fields` semantics (**not** `is not None`) — `outbound_field_diff.py:251` treats a MISSING key as "no ancestor -> local wins", so a key must stay present with a `None` value rather than being dropped.

Both callers must be covered: `reconcile._advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:506-523`) and the inbound-adopt path at `apply_inbound_records.py:209-212`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: **integration** against a stateful fake,
      asserting file bytes and commit count — not call counts. (`save()` uses
      `json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, so byte-identity is well-defined.)
- [ ] `grep -rn baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing; the stamp is absent from every entry
      written by `set_baseline`. Tier: **unit** + grep assertion.
- [ ] A baseline field present-but-null still round-trips as present (guards the `if k in fields`
      semantics). Tier: **unit** on `set_baseline` + `get_baseline`.
- [ ] `test_binding_baseline.py:61`'s assertion on the stamp is removed or inverted, and the suite is
      green. Verify: `make test`.
- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed version measured at **<=25% of the 12.79 KB baseline** by the
      recorded method (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo, repack
      `--window=250 --depth=50`, `(pack_N-pack_1)/(N-1)`). Tier: **repo-level measurement**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`

Scope: S-M.
baseline.summary: A1: delete the never-read baseline_advanced_at stamp and add a write-when-changed guard to set_baseline

baseline.description:
# The stale-material message omits the checkbox note on its PRIMARY path

`material_diff.CHECKBOX_NOTE` is introduced with this comment:

    #: The advice every material-staleness reason carries, because it is the single most
    #: frequently mis-believed fact about the gate (bug 94a3, observations 1 and 3).

It is not carried by every reason. `explain_material_change` emits it on only TWO branches:

  * material_diff.py:301 — the "no material component differs" branch (an attestation that
    predates AC-checkbox normalization);
  * material_diff.py:323 — the degraded branch (an attestation that predates component-level
    fingerprinting).

The PRIMARY branch — `delta = describe_delta(signed, current); if delta is not None: return delta` (material_diff.py:295-297) — returns the named delta with NO note. That is the branch a current attestation takes, so it is the one almost every author actually sees.

## Observed
Closing task b2bb after ticking its ACs *and* appending evidence prose to each AC item produced, verbatim:

    plan-review close gate: stale-material: the plan was materially edited since review —
    changed: description (8208 -> 8829 chars). Health: current (no related material)
    (enforced); phase planning -> execution (compatible)
    Run rebar review-plan b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5 separately, then retry close.

No checkbox note. The author had just been REQUIRED by the close precheck to tick boxes, so the tick is the salient recent edit and the natural (wrong) conclusion is that ticking staled the review. That is exactly the misconception bug 94a3 recorded three agents making; this one made a fourth, with the preventing sentence present in the codebase but not on this path.

## This is a MESSAGE defect, not a gate defect
The gate is correct and its behaviour should not change:
  * ticking `- [ ]` -> `- [x]` is normalized out of the fingerprint and is attestation-SAFE;
  * editing the TEXT of an acceptance criterion IS a change to the plan and SHOULD require a
    fresh review. That is the point of binding the material.
Only the explanation is deficient, and only on the branch that matters most.

## Secondary: the delta names the component but not what moved inside it
`changed: description (8208 -> 8829 chars)` identifies WHICH basis key changed, not what within it. An author who ticked boxes AND edited prose in one `rebar edit` cannot tell from the message which of the two is responsible — the char delta is consistent with both.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The named-delta branch of `explain_material_change` carries `CHECKBOX_NOTE` too, so
      every `stale-material` reason states that a tick is never the cause. (The module
      comment already claims this is true; make it true.)
- [x] When the changed component is `description`, the message distinguishes "checkbox state
      changed as well" from "item text changed" — enough for the author to know which edit
      staled the attestation, without printing the diff.
- [x] Held-out test: a description edit that ONLY flips checkbox state yields no staleness; an
      edit that changes AC item text yields `stale-material` AND a reason containing the
      checkbox note.

## NOT part of this ticket — the documentation is adequate
An earlier draft of this bug claimed the docs fail to tell an author to record AC evidence in a COMMENT rather than in the AC text. That claim was withdrawn on review: the guidance is already present and sufficient.
  * `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:209` shows evidence recorded as a ticket
    comment;
  * `:304` states that comments are non-material and do not stale an attestation;
  * the completion verifier's own failure text instructs the author to "add a comment to this
    ticket that documents the concrete artifacts".
Annotating AC text with evidence instead is an author error, not a doc gap, and editing that text SHOULD stale the review because it changes the plan. Nothing here asks for a doc change.

## Provenance
Hit while closing b2bb during the store/signing remediation. Cross-references bug 94a3 (the three prior agents) and bug 330c (the normalization that makes ticking safe).

## Implementation plan
All changes in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` (+ manifest feed), message text only — no gate outcome changes.

1. **AC1 — note on the primary branch.** In `explain_material_change`, the
   `delta is not None` early return gains the same `CHECKBOX_NOTE` tail the other two
   branches already carry, so every `stale-material` reason states that a tick is never the
   cause.
2. **AC2 — say what moved inside `description`.** Box state is normalized out of the signed
   component hash, so the signed side carries no box information today. Add a DIAGNOSTIC
   (non-basis) component `description_boxes` = (hash of the checkbox-state sequence, number
   ticked), emitted alongside the existing `material-part:` lines. It is NOT a basis key: it
   is absent from `COMPONENT_ORDER`, so `describe_delta` ignores it, the composite
   fingerprint is untouched, and `material_components` keeps returning exactly the basis
   keys (asserted by `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py:81`). A new helper
   feeds `reviewed_material_parts` / `_current_components` the basis PLUS the diagnostic.
3. When `description` is among the changed components, the message appends whether the
   checkbox state also changed (with a ticked count delta) or is unchanged; when the
   attestation predates the diagnostic line, the clause is omitted (graceful degradation,
   same posture as the existing degraded branch). No ticket content is ever printed.

## Verification
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` gains held-out cases:
  a description edit that ONLY flips box state produces NO staleness (composite unchanged);
  an edit to AC item text produces a delta whose reason contains `CHECKBOX_NOTE` and the
  text-vs-box discrimination; an old (pre-diagnostic) manifest still explains without it.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/plan_review/` all green.

## File impact
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py`

baseline.description:
## Impact, stated first

Every live Reconcile Bridge pass re-attempts inbound (Jira -> rebar) link writes that **cannot ever succeed**: the source is closed, the relationship is redundant with the hierarchy, or the link would create a cycle. Each fails, logs a WARNING, and is forgotten; the next pass derives the identical set and tries again. The bridge **never converges**, and its log carries a permanent error floor that must be filtered before a real fault is visible.

## Evidence (measured 2026-08-12, live workflow logs)

Four consecutive live runs (31568815075, 31569179421, 31569723185, 31570037358, ~30 min) each emit exactly **19** failed inbound link writes: 5 `is closed`, 13 `redundant — ancestor-descendant`, 1 `would create a cycle`. Normalising and diffing two passes yields a **byte-identical** failing set. Passes re-dispatch every ~5-6 min: 200+ doomed writes/hour, indefinitely.

**Correction to the filing:** these are *local* `rebar link` subprocess writes, not Jira round-trips — real waste, but CPU/log cost rather than Jira API cost.

## Confirmed mechanism

- **Emitter:** `inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound` dedups an ADD only against the ticket's *current* local deps. A failed link never lands a LINK event, so the identical record is re-emitted every pass.
- **Applier:** `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links`, `add` branch — `try: rebar.link(...) except Exception: logger.warning(...)`. That warn-and-continue is the whole handling.
- **Why permanent:** all three are raised by `graph/_links.py::add_dependency` from reduced local state — deterministic verdicts, not I/O faults; they re-raise identically until the *local structure* changes.
- **No durable memory anywhere:** the binding store holds only jira_key/state/baseline/peer-parent; `managed_refs` records only refs successfully created. Nothing records an attempt or a failure.

## Approach

Give the applier a durable, self-healing memory of *permanently impossible* inbound link ADDs, and consult it before spending the write.

1. **New module** `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/impossible_links.py`:
   - `classify(exc) -> reason | None` — classifies the three permanent shapes (`closed_source`, `redundant_ancestry`, `cycle`). Anything else returns `None`, behaviour unchanged. The safety valve: only provably-structural shapes are recorded.
   - `deciding_digest(source, target, relation, tracker_dir, reason)` — a stable digest over the structural inputs the *relevant* validator reads. This is the invalidation key: when it stops matching, the record is pruned and the link is attempted once more.
     - `closed_source` / `redundant_ancestry` are decided by the two endpoints, so those digests cover each endpoint's status, parent chain and dep set, undisturbed by edits elsewhere.
     - `cycle` is NOT endpoint-local: `add_dependency` walks the TRANSITIVE graph, so unlinking or reparenting an INTERMEDIATE ticket can break the cycle while both endpoints stay byte-identical. A cycle record therefore keys on the global structural projection (every ticket's status/parent/deps). Over-invalidating costs one extra attempt; under-invalidating would suppress a legitimate link indefinitely — the asymmetry decides it.
     - Non-structural edits (comments, titles) are excluded from every digest, so an unchanged structure converges to zero writes.
   - A JSON store at `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/impossible_links.json` (`version: 1`), keyed `source|target|relation` -> `{reason, digest, first_seen, last_seen, attempts}`. A **separate file** from `bindings.json`: no schema collision with the binding store or with the peer-confirmation record planned by epic despotic-floriated-leopard.
   - **The file must be COMMITTED to the tickets branch.** Each pass runs in a fresh CI checkout, so a record living only in the working tree is discarded between passes and the skip would never take effect in production — the bug would survive the fix with every unit test still green. `git_adapter.IMPOSSIBLE_LINKS_FILE` is added to the files `reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot` stages, and to its per-file idempotency basename set so a pass changing only this file is still committed.
   - **The endpoint fingerprint covers every ticket on the parent chain, not just the endpoint.** `add_dependency` calls `resolve_hierarchy_link` FIRST, which can REDIRECT an endpoint to a type-tier ancestor; the validators then run against that promoted ticket. So the deciding status/deps may belong to an ancestor. Fingerprinting the whole chain covers the redirect target wherever the promotion lands, without this module re-deriving the promotion rule and drifting from it.
2. **Applier change** (`_inbound_update_apply_links`, `add` branch only): before calling `rebar.link`, skip when a record matches the triple *and* its digest still matches. Otherwise attempt as today; on failure classify, and record only a permanent reason.
3. **Fail-open and hygiene:** a corrupt store, an uncomputable digest, or an unreducible ticket all degrade to "attempt the write", never "suppress it". Written by temp-file + atomic `os.replace`, only when something changed, so a converged pass touches the file zero times. A record whose digest stops matching is deleted, so dead entries cannot accumulate.
4. **Operator visibility:** a newly-recorded impossible link still WARNs exactly once, so a genuinely new one is loud. Subsequent skips log at DEBUG, plus one INFO summary per pass naming the count and store path. Deleting the JSON file re-qualifies everything — the manual clear.

**Out of scope:** the REMOVE branch, `_inbound_unlink_one`, and the differ's G3/G4/G5 suppression — that surface belongs to epic despotic-floriated-leopard. This change touches only the ADD branch and a distinct state file, so the two are complementary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `classify` returns the correct reason for each of the three real error texts above, and `None` for a transient/unknown exception (unit test per shape).
- [x] With a matching record and unchanged digest, `_inbound_update_apply_links` does **not** call `rebar.link` for that triple and does not count it in `links_applied`.
- [x] When the deciding inputs change (the closed source is reopened), the digest stops matching and the link **is** re-attempted once.
- [x] A failure that is not one of the three permanent shapes is **not** recorded and is retried next pass exactly as today.
- [x] A first-time impossible link logs at WARNING; a subsequent skip does not.
- [x] Steady-state evidence, not log suppression: over an unchanged store, pass 1 attempts the write and pass 2 performs **zero** `rebar.link` invocations (test counts facade calls, not log lines).
- [x] The record survives a process restart — read back from the JSON by a fresh store instance.
- [x] A structural change to an ANCESTOR of an endpoint (the ticket `resolve_hierarchy_link` promotes to) invalidates the record, even though the endpoint itself is unchanged (unit test).
- [x] `impossible_links.json` is staged by `_commit_binding_store_snapshot` and present in its per-file idempotency set, so the record survives to the next pass (unit test).
- [x] A `cycle` record is invalidated by a structural change to an INTERMEDIATE ticket (unlinking a third ticket that breaks the chain), even though both endpoints are unchanged — the under-invalidation trap (unit test comparing digests directly).
- [x] A record whose digest stops matching is pruned from the store rather than left behind (unit test reading the JSON back).
- [x] A corrupt/unparseable store degrades to empty and the link is still attempted (unit test).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the existing inbound-link test files (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_inbound_links.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_lands_locally_5200.py`) all pass unchanged.
baseline.summary: Reconciler re-attempts the same structurally-impossible Jira->rebar links on EVERY pass, so the bridge never converges and its log is permanently noisy

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The bridge has nowhere to record which tracker projects a store syncs, nor which repos each project's tickets belong to. Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` needs that mapping to be a property of the **store** rather than of any one repo, because `.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json` is shared by every repo using the store: if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would see the other's projects as vanished from the remote and diff them as deletions.

## Approach

Add `.bridge_state/projects.json` beside the committed bridge state already there (`bindings.json`, `get_rotation.json`, `prev_snapshot.json` — all present on the `tickets` branch), owned by a new `projects_store.py` module rather than by extending `binding_store.py`. The two records have very different write cadences, and keeping them separate means an operator editing the mapping never rewrites the large bindings record.

Record shape:

```json
{"version": 1, "legacy_default": "REB", "projects": {"REB": {"repos": ["rebar"]}}}
```

The `projects` key set **is** the store's sync list, so there is no second list to keep in agreement. `legacy_default` is the project that tickets predating this epic resolve to.

This choice sits well with ADR 0060 ("Keep bridge state committed, but make its formats cheap"): that ADR's constraint is per-pass churn on the tickets branch — it measured 12.79 KB per changed `bindings.json` version and ~4.5 MB/day for `prev_snapshot.json`. The mapping changes only on an operator edit, so it adds no per-pass growth at all.

Surface it as `bridge projects` under the verb group established by story `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a` (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py`), with the library and MCP parity epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3` requires of every bridge verb. The bridge library surface is `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py` (`bridge_fsck` at `:75`). The MCP layer is split by mutation, not by feature: `register_read_tools` (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:36`) hosts tools annotated `_ANN["READ_ONLY"]` — where the existing `bridge_fsck` tool lives at `:259` — while `register_write_tools` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:33`) hosts mutating tools, and `mcp_server.py:663` registers both. The `projects` verbs therefore split across both modules: `list` is a read tool, `set` and `remove` are write tools. Sub-verbs: `list`, `set <KEY> --repos a,b`, `remove <KEY>`. `set` on a key that is already present **replaces** that key's repos list rather than merging into it, so the command is idempotent and a repo is removed by re-issuing `set` without it.

The bridge group's help is a **pinned byte-exact contract**, not generated text: the group listing lives in `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` (which today names only `preview` and `sync` at lines 5-7) and is served verbatim by `_help.subcommand_help` (`src/rebar/_cli/_help.py:52`), while the parser hardcodes the verb set a second time as `metavar="{preview,sync}"` (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:52-53`). Adding a verb therefore means editing three places, not one; omitting either of the two help sites ships a group whose own help does not mention the command it just gained.

The module exposes two functions so that I/O and rule are separable: `load_mapping(repo_root)` reads and validates the record, and `resolve_project(ticket, mapping) -> str | None` is a pure function over an already-loaded mapping, which keeps the tri-state rule unit-testable without a store on disk.

**Read behaviour when the record is missing or bad** follows the precedent `compat.py` already sets for `.store-compat.json` (`docs/migrations.md:155-165`): an **absent** record is legal and reads as an empty mapping with a `legacy_default` of `None`, while a **malformed** one raises rather than being silently treated as absent — a corrupt record must never degrade into a permissive default. Absent is legal because the record is seeded by an ensure unit that runs at init, `fsck --repair`, and MCP boot; until it does, every ticket resolves to `None` and nothing syncs, which is the fail-safe direction — the bridge writes nothing rather than writing somewhere wrong.

`resolve_project` implements the tri-state rule so the inbound and outbound stories consume one implementation instead of each re-deriving it. The states map to concrete return values:

| ticket `bridge_project` | returns | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| key absent from state | the mapping's `legacy_default` (a `str`) | legacy ticket, predates this epic |
| `""` (explicit empty) | `None` | deliberately not synced |
| `"REB"` | `"REB"` | sync into that project |

`None` is the not-synced sentinel, so every consumer branches on a single defined value: callers treat `None` as "emit no mutation for this ticket" and any non-`None` result as a project key safe to target. A `legacy_default` that is itself empty — a store whose backend had no configured project — also yields `None`, so an unconfigured store degrades to "nothing syncs" rather than to a malformed query.

`--repos` is **required** on `set`; omitting the flag is an argument error and exits non-zero. `--repos ""` is the explicit way to store an empty list, which keeps "no default repo" a deliberate statement rather than an accident of a forgotten flag.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` — the subcommand, and the hardcoded `metavar` verb set at `:52-53`
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` — the pinned byte-exact group help listing
- `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — the `list` read tool
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — the `set` and `remove` write tools
- tests under `tests/`

This story owns the mapping module; the parent epic's file impact is updated to name `projects_store.py` rather than `binding_store.py`, so parent and child agree that the mapping does not extend the bindings record.

`_mcp_writes.py` is the one file this story shares with its sibling that adds the ticket create arguments. The overlap is forced by the codebase's own read/write registrar split rather than chosen, and it is safe because that sibling `depends_on` this story: the two are strictly ordered and can never be edited concurrently. Introducing a third MCP module purely to avoid the shared file would break the established registrar convention for no benefit.

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's CLI row — a real CLI subprocess with a persisted-state assertion — because the mechanism spans argument parsing, the on-disk JSON record, and exit codes; an in-process unit test would not cross the parsing or exit-code components.

- Happy path: `bridge projects set REB --repos rebar` in a fresh store, then `bridge projects list`
  returns the entry and `.bridge_state/projects.json` on disk contains it.
- Cross-surface contract test: an entry written through the library surface is read back byte-equal
  through the CLI and through MCP — proving one record, not three parallel stores.
- Failure path: `bridge projects remove NOPE` on a store without that key exits non-zero, names the
  key, and leaves the record byte-unchanged.
- Edge: `set REB --repos` with an empty list is accepted and stores `[]` — a project with no default
  repo is legal, not an error.
- Replace-not-merge: `set REB --repos a,b` followed by `set REB --repos a` stores exactly `["a"]`,
  proving the second call replaced rather than merged.
- Pinned help: `rebar bridge` with no verb, and `rebar help bridge`, both render text naming
  `projects`, and the argparse `metavar` matches the pinned listing — asserted against the file so a
  future verb cannot drift the two apart silently.
- Collateral invariant: after any mapping write, `bindings.json` and `prev_snapshot.json` hash
  identically to before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects set|list|remove` exist under the bridge verb group and operate on
      `.bridge_state/projects.json`; checked by a CLI subprocess test asserting the on-disk record
      after each verb.
- [ ] The library and MCP surfaces read and write the same record as the CLI; checked by a test that
      writes through one surface and reads the identical entry through the other two.
- [ ] `resolve_project` returns the `legacy_default` string for an absent field, `None` for an
      explicit empty value, and the key itself for a set value, and returns `None` when the
      `legacy_default` is itself empty; checked by a parameterized unit test asserting the exact
      return value for all four cases.
- [ ] `set` without `--repos` is an argument error exiting non-zero, while `--repos ""` stores `[]`;
      checked by a paired CLI subprocess test.
- [ ] An absent record reads as an empty mapping with a `None` legacy default while a malformed one
      raises; checked by a paired test over a store with no record and one with truncated JSON.
- [ ] `list` is registered as a read tool and `set`/`remove` as write tools; checked by asserting
      `list` carries the READ_ONLY annotation and that `set`/`remove` are registered by
      `register_write_tools`.
- [ ] A mapping write leaves `bindings.json` and `prev_snapshot.json` byte-identical; checked by
      hashing both before and after in the CLI test.
- [ ] `remove` of an unknown key exits non-zero and mutates nothing; checked in the same test.
- [ ] `set` on an already-present key replaces its repos list rather than merging; checked by
      asserting the stored list equals exactly the second call's argument.
- [ ] The pinned group help in `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` and the parser `metavar` both name
      `projects`; checked by a test asserting the rendered `rebar bridge` help contains the verb and
      that the pinned file and the `metavar` verb set agree.
baseline.summary: bridge projects: store-level project-to-repos mapping and its CLI, library and MCP surface

## Report (from a rebar client)
A Rebar CLI quirk treated `create task --help` as a literal task and created an accidental placeholder ticket.

## Observed
Running `rebar create task --help` (an attempt to view help for the create-task command) does NOT print help — instead the parser consumes `--help` as the positional title argument, so a ticket titled `--help` (a placeholder) is actually CREATED.

## Expected
`create task --help` (and `--help`/`-h` on any create subcommand) should print the command's usage/help and create NOTHING. Help must never be interpreted as ticket content.

## Impact
Accidental placeholder tickets pollute the store and require cleanup; the write side-effect on a help request is surprising and violates least-astonishment.

## Notes / possible cause
The create command path likely reads the first positional as the title before any --help interception. Compare with the argparse standardization landed for the write commands (claim/transition, ticket fd48-7a80-33e9-4400): --help there is served byte-exact by the top-level dispatcher and never reaches the handler. The create path may bypass that dispatcher help interception, or accept a bare positional that swallows `--help`. Needs repro + root-cause.

## Repro
1. `rebar create task --help`
2. Observe: no help text; a new ticket titled `--help` is created (verify via `rebar list`).

## Confirmed root cause
`rebar._cli.main` only treats `--help`/`-h` as a help request when it is the FIRST token after the subcommand (`rest[0]`): the guard is `if rest and rest[0] in ("--help", "-h") and sub not in _HIDDEN_ALIASES:`. For `create task --help`, `rest == ["task", "--help"]`, so `rest[0] == "task"` and the guard is skipped; dispatch falls through to `composer.create_cli`, whose hand-rolled parser reads `rest[0]` as the ticket type and `rest[1]` (`--help`) as the title, then performs the CREATE write. The commands that "own" their `--help` (review-plan, workflow, audit, …) are intercepted earlier and are unaffected; the bug hits the fall-through write commands.

## Fix
In `rebar._cli.main`, recognise `--help`/`-h` appearing ANYWHERE in `rest` before a `--` terminator (not only at `rest[0]`) as a help request for a routable subcommand, matching argparse semantics (help short-circuits regardless of position). A `_wants_help(rest)` helper scans `rest`, stopping at `--`. A `_help_requested(sub, rest)` wrapper makes this family-aware: nested-dispatch families (the `bridge` group) own their children's help, so they honour only a LEADING `--help`/`-h` (a later flag belongs to a child such as `bridge preview --help`, served by `bridge_cli`) — keeping `bridge --help` identical to `help bridge`. Every other command uses the any-position scan. `_HIDDEN_ALIASES` stays excluded and the earlier own-their-help intercepts are untouched. Help serves the byte-exact pinned usage via the existing `_emit_subcommand_help(sub)` and performs NO write.

## Testing
- Regression: `main(["create", "task", "--help"])` returns 0, prints the create usage to
  stdout, and creates NO ticket (store unchanged).
- Position parity: `-h` in a later position and `--help` after a title are also honoured.
- `_wants_help`/`_help_requested` unit contracts: any-position scan for leaf commands,
  leading-only for the `bridge` family, `--` terminator respected.
- Unchanged: `rebar create task "real title"` still creates; `bridge --help` == `help
  bridge`; `bridge preview --help` shows preview usage; unknown subcommand still errors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar create task --help` prints the create usage (exit 0) and creates NO ticket.
- [x] `--help`/`-h` anywhere before a `--` terminator triggers subcommand help for routable
      write commands (create/edit/comment/link/…), not just at `rest[0]`.
- [x] The `bridge` nested-dispatch family keeps its own help: `bridge --help` equals
      `help bridge` and `bridge preview --help` shows preview usage.
- [x] Commands that own their own `--help` and unknown-subcommand handling are unchanged.
- [x] A regression test (tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py)
      covers the no-write help behavior and the `_wants_help`/`_help_requested` contracts;
      bridge parity is covered by tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli_argparse.py and
      test_bridge_cli_heldout.py.
baseline.summary: create task --help treated as a literal task title, creating an accidental placeholder ticket

baseline.description:
Discovered while landing Gerrit change 1640 (ticket sole-curbable-stinkpot); it cost that change a spurious Verified -1.

## The defect

TEST: tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py:: test_cli_keyset_is_informational_and_keeps_json_envelope_read_only

The test proves `bridge fsck --keyset` does not mutate the tracker store. Its oracle is a byte-for-byte snapshot of the tracker directory taken before and after the command:

    full_before = _file_bytes(full_tracker)
    ...
    assert _file_bytes(full_tracker) == full_before

`_file_bytes` walks the directory with `rglob("*")` and excludes nothing, so `.git/` internals are part of the oracle. Git background auto-maintenance mutates those internals on its own schedule, independent of the command under test, so the comparison flips while the read-only property being asserted still holds. The failure diff observed in CI was a single stray entry `.git/objects/maintenance.lock`.

## Root cause is broader than the observed symptom (measured, not assumed)

Injecting the two things auto-maintenance does, against the current helper:

- creating `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` -> snapshot comparison flips
- `git gc` object packing -> snapshot comparison flips, 16 paths differ
  (loose objects collapse into a packfile, `.git/info/refs` rewritten), with no logical change

So a fix that ignores only `*.lock` files would still leave the test flaky via the packing limb. The oracle's problem is that it reaches into git's private storage representation at all, not that one particular scratch file exists.

## The fix

Snapshot what "read-only" actually claims, in two parts:

1. Every file OUTSIDE `.git/` byte-for-byte (the store payload: event files, `.bridge_state/`,
   bindings) - unchanged strictness for everything the store owns.
2. Git's LOGICAL state rather than its storage bytes: `HEAD` plus the full `for-each-ref`
   listing, so a commit or ref move made by the command is still caught.

This is deliberately not "drop `.git/` and lose the check". Repacking is invisible to (2) because packing does not move refs; a commit made by `bridge fsck` would move `HEAD` and fail (2) immediately. The oracle keeps its teeth and loses its dependence on git's scheduler.

Rejected alternative: `git config maintenance.auto false` / `gc.auto 0` in the fixture. It suppresses this repo's symptom while leaving the oracle fragile to the next transient file, and it does not hold for maintenance already in flight or triggered by another process.

## Scope

Test-only change; no `src/rebar` behaviour is touched. The command under test is not modified, and the read-only property it is asserted against is not weakened.

The second flake recorded in the comments (test_plan_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union, a fixture-precondition sync race on ubuntu) is a DIFFERENT defect with a different mechanism and a different fix. It is split into its own ticket and linked, rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A new regression test in the same file asserts the snapshot helper is stable across git
   auto-maintenance: after injecting `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` AND running `git gc` in the
   fixture tracker, the snapshot compares equal to the pre-injection snapshot. This test FAILS
   against the current helper (verified: both limbs flip) and PASSES after the change.
2. The same regression test asserts the oracle still detects real mutation: writing to a store
   payload file makes the snapshot compare unequal, and a commit that moves `HEAD` makes it
   compare unequal. Read-only detection is proven retained, not assumed.
3. test_cli_keyset_is_informational_and_keeps_json_envelope_read_only still passes and still
   asserts the read-only property via the corrected oracle.
4. Assertions are ordering/content facts only - no wall-clock budgets or timing upper bounds.
5. `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the full bridge fsck test module passes.
baseline.summary: Flaky: bridge fsck keyset read-only test races git auto-maintenance on macOS

baseline.description: During CI for Gerrit change 2249 the macos-latest/py3.13 pytest leg failed with 4 COLLECTION errors (not test failures; 900 passed): ModuleNotFoundError: 'rebar_reconciler.classify' is not a package, collecting tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/{test_frozen_census,test_matrix,test_multipass_stateful,test_properties}.py. ROOT CAUSE (deterministic mechanism, non-deterministic trigger): the engine ships rebar_reconciler/classify.py as a MODULE, while the test tree tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ is a PACKAGE sharing the top-level name. _engine_module (src/rebar/_lib_ops.py) seeds sys.modules['rebar_reconciler'] = the ENGINE package; tests/unit/conftest.py::_bridge_reconciler_shadow_package() compensates by putting BOTH shadow-dir and engine-dir on __path__, but under some xdist worker orderings the engine package is seeded WITHOUT the shadow path before a classify test imports, so rebar_reconciler.classify resolves to the engine MODULE and the test package cannot collect. Passes locally (py3.12) and on the ubuntu legs; surfaced only on macos-py3.13. Adding two test files in change 2249 perturbed xdist work-distribution enough to surface this LATENT pre-existing collision; the classify dir is untouched by that change. FIX DIRECTION: harden _bridge_reconciler_shadow_package() to also repair the engine package's __path__ deterministically (append the shadow dir) regardless of seed order, OR rename one side to remove the module-vs-package name collision. Repro aid: run tests/scripts + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify together under xdist -n and vary worker count.
baseline.summary: xdist ordering flake: rebar_reconciler.classify module vs test-package shadow collision

## Context
Analysis-only record of LLM gate economics since the Bedrock switch. No production or repository code change is part of this ticket. The work measured per-gate and per-ticket cost, evaluated quality-neutral and model-swap levers, ran cheap-model experiments, and produced a phased ordinal-to-binary migration plan.

## Durable deliverables
- Existing ticket comments record experiment rounds 1 through 6, costs, gold-set outcomes, rejected levers, and follow-up tickets.
- The full report is published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/725e8b52-688d-49ed-a286-4571bedce34d.
- The comment marked ORDINAL_MIGRATION_PLAN_DURABLE_COPY records the phased migration plan and its validation/approval boundaries.
- Local research files under reports/llm-gate-cost-2026-08-11 are intentionally gitignored working artifacts, not committed deliverables and not closure evidence.

## Results
Plan review measured mean 3.02 dollars per run, code review 1.42 dollars, completion verification 2.24 dollars, and mean 11.85 dollars per completed ticket. The experiments rejected Haiku for agentic review, rejected per-criterion re-review after the historical audit, retained Sonnet for completion verification, and identified bounded Nova pilots and terminal-failure fixes as the credible next levers. Execution of any migration remains separate work requiring operator approval.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Cost analysis and per-gate/per-ticket figures are durably recorded. Verify: `rebar show childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet | grep -F "cost per ticket COMPLETED"` exits 0.
- [x] Cheap-model experiment outputs and dispositions are durably recorded. Verify: `rebar show childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet | grep -F "Follow-up experiments complete"` exits 0.

None. This is an analysis record; evidence lives in the shared ticket history and published artifact.
