## Context / Problem
S1-S6 establish a shared policy and execution path across two mature gates. Unit coverage inside each story is necessary but cannot prove that the combined default path uses one policy authority, makes no duplicate shadow calls, preserves narrow outputs, survives the real provider boundary, or remains centralized after later edits. RP-06 therefore needs a permanent cross-gate cutover guard and live exercise.

## Approach
Add a deterministic shadow comparator that consumes the same observed call/result set as the legacy and RP-06 projections. Compare criterion selection and exclusion, order, prompt/contract identity, context hash, model/mode, dependencies, budgets, posture, usage, checkpoint decisions, and final disposition. Its allowlist names only the approved deltas: effective built-in retune/disable, project DET inclusion, project LLM applicability, positive code-review budget enforcement, typed partial-failure continuation, and success-only checkpointing. Shadowing never issues a model call and never controls the final verdict.

Add a repository-policy/contract guard that fails when a review gate bypasses `CriteriaSnapshot` to read packaged/project routing directly, when a second discovery scheduler is introduced outside the shared kernel, or when per-unit trace fields enter review/review-status schemas. Use semantic imports/contracts where possible and a narrowly scoped AST/source policy only for the prohibited direct-reader pattern.

Exercise both defaulted gate paths through the existing external LLM provider matrix. The canary uses real workflow dispatch and a minimal bounded fixture, proves at least one discovery call reaches the configured provider, and asserts the final narrow verdict plus stored internal trace. It must not print secrets, raw prompt/context bodies, or the trace. Record the provider arm, run URL, timestamp, call count, and result on this ticket.

Document the final ownership and rollback boundary in `docs/review-kernel.md`: authored topology and gate strategy remain gate-owned; snapshot and execution facts are shared; RP-01 owns provider-turn retry; rollback is a code revert to the retained compatibility projection, not an operator configuration flag. New code ignores legacy checkpoints and the retained legacy projection never writes the new journal.

## Testing
The deterministic comparator and architecture guard run in the normal unit/repository-policy gate. Response-schema tests assert exact public keys. The live canary lives under `tests/external/`, carries the existing `external` and `llm_live` confinement, and is selected by the configured provider matrix. One tier lower cannot prove the provider/workflow cutover because a fake can bypass the default runtime path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The shadow comparator uses one observed call set, emits no provider calls, and reports exact field-level mismatches with only the approved delta allowlist accepted.
- [x] Cross-gate fixtures for no overlay, effective disable/retune, scoped/global project LLM, project DET, budget shed, local failure, systemic failure, cancellation, and legacy checkpoint produce the approved final dispositions and trace outcomes.
- [x] A repository-policy/contract test fails on direct gate reads that bypass `CriteriaSnapshot`, a second discovery scheduler outside the shared kernel, or per-unit trace/debug fields added to review or review-status output schemas.
- [x] Public response-schema tests prove `review-plan`, `review-plan --status`, and code-review outputs remain narrow while their reducer-ignored journals retain versioned internal traces.
- [x] New code ignores legacy checkpoint envelopes, the retained compatibility projection cannot write new envelopes or decide a final verdict, and a revert to that projection requires no journal rewrite or data cleanup.
- [x] `docs/review-kernel.md` states final snapshot/executor/gate/RP-01 ownership, approved deltas, sensitive-data boundary, shadow behavior, and revert-based rollback.
- [x] A live provider canary at `tests/external/test_review_discovery_live.py`, confined to the `external`+`llm_live` markers and selected by the provider matrix, drives the real default discovery path and asserts a narrow final verdict (PASS/BLOCK) with `coverage.llm_ran` true and the reducer-ignored internal journal retained (`sidecar_emitted`), printing no secrets, prompt/context bodies, or trace.
- [x] [operator-attested] The external provider matrix run exercised that real default plan-review/code-review discovery path against live providers, recorded at least one provider call per exercised arm, and this ticket records provider, run URL, timestamp, call count, and final result.
  provenance: environment=external-provider-matrix; principal=configured CI workload identity; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the external provider matrix issues real credentialed provider calls (OIDC-scoped CI identity), equivalent to production discovery; run URL and per-provider result attached to this ticket.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Three agents on 2026-08-05 reported contradictory answers to "does ticking an AC checkbox invalidate a plan-review attestation?". The contradiction is a DIAGNOSTIC defect, not a behavioral one, and the empirical answer is now settled (see Findings). Every attestation staleness message today names a fixed, partly-fictional list of inputs, so a reader cannot tell which input actually changed and hunts for an edit that could never have been the cause. The operator has approved fixing this broadly: wherever rebar reports an attestation error, it must say WHAT CHANGED. That approval covers this ticket's whole scope, including the additive manifest change described below.

## Findings that fix the scope (verified in this checkout)

- The material basis is a SINGLE composite sha256, built in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` `material_fingerprint()` over exactly four keys —
  `ticket_id`, `description`, `file_impact`, `children` — plus `file_impact_scope` when the
  scope is `none`. Verified by reading `pass1.py:750-777`.
- AC checkbox STATE is normalized out of that basis by
  `pass1.py::_normalize_checkbox_state` (`pass1.py:741-747`, bug 330c). Ticking `- [ ]` to
  `- [x]` therefore does NOT invalidate an attestation. Confirmed by running
  `material_fingerprint` over a tick-only description pair: the hashes are equal.
- "AC" is NOT a basis component. Acceptance criteria live inside `description`. Every current
  message says "description/AC/file_impact/children", naming an input that does not exist.
- A pre-330c attestation hashed the RAW description, so after a tick neither the normalized
  recompute nor the `attest.py::_legacy_material_ok` grandfather (`attest.py:614-631`) can
  match, and it reads `stale-material` with no component actually edited. This is the residual
  cause the current message hides, and it reconciles observation 3 in the original report.
- `children` is derived from OTHER tickets' `parent_id` at read time
  (`relation_snapshot.py::live_material_children`), not from this ticket's own event log.
- The signed manifest ALREADY carries per-child/prerequisite pins —
  `plan-material-pin: <role> <id> <fingerprint>` parsed by `manifest.py::manifest_pins`
  (`manifest.py:428-457`) — so the signed child-id set is recoverable from any pinned
  attestation without any schema change.

## Approach

Add per-component fingerprints to the signed manifest and diff them component-wise on read.

Concretely:

1. New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` holding two functions.
   `material_components(ctx)` returns `{name: hash16}` for each basis key, hashing exactly the
   same per-key values `material_fingerprint` already feeds into the composite (so the two can
   never disagree). `explain_material_change(attestation, ticket_id, repo_root)` returns a
   compact human string naming the components that differ.
2. `manifest.py::build_manifest` emits one additive, deterministic line per component:
   `material-part: <name> <hash16>`, sorted by name. `manifest.py` gains
   `manifest_material_parts()` to parse them back. The lines are additive, so an existing
   verifier ignores them and a pre-change manifest simply parses to `{}`. The prefix cannot
   collide with `manifest_material()`, which matches `startswith("material:")`.
3. `attest.py::compute_validity` calls `explain_material_change` for BOTH `stale-material`
   returns (plan-review at `attest.py:588-601` and completion-verifier at `attest.py:527-538`)
   and puts the named components in `reason`. It also names the reopen timestamp on
   `stale-reopened` and keeps the already-specific `stale-code` / `stale-head` wording (both
   already name the drifted paths / the two SHAs).
4. `attest_gate.py::claim_gate_check`'s `unsigned` message (`attest_gate.py:121-126`) states
   both remedies, because rebar cannot distinguish "never reviewed" from "review PASSed but
   signing aborted": run `rebar review-plan <id>`, or `rebar sign-review <id>` if a review
   already passed. `claim_gate_check` already forwards `compute_validity`'s `reason` verbatim,
   and `_commands/transition_close.py::_raise_plan_review_close_gate_error` and
   `_commands/claim.py` render that same string, so fixing the source fixes the claim gate, the
   close gate and `review-plan --status` together.
5. The sites that re-word or drop the reason instead of forwarding it are pointed at the same
   helper or made to carry the data they already hold:
   - `generation.py:265-269` and `resign.py:198-208` — replace the fixed list with the named
     components.
   - `generation.py:270-273` — "a dependency's plan material changed since the review" names no
     dependency, although the changed pin set is in hand; `resign.py:262-270` already names the
     ids, so this one is brought to parity.
   - `completion.py:178` — a child's closure-validity detail is currently
     `f"signature: {sig.get('verdict')}"`, dropping the reason that explains it; it forwards the
     reason too.
   - `_cli/_llm_commands.py:118-141` — a `plan_review_sign_aborted` signing failure currently
     renders the generic "run `rebar sign-review`" advice, which is wrong for the
     `store-read-failure` reason (a re-sign hits the same unreadable read). It gets its own
     branch naming the reason and the correct remedy.
   - `attest_gate.py:166-167` — the docstring's verdict vocabulary omits `not-closed`,
     `malformed-phase`, `incompatible-phase` and the `stale-pin-*` values; corrected so the
     documented list matches what `compute_validity` can actually return.

   These were found by an exhaustive sweep of every attestation refusal surface. Surfaces
   deliberately left unchanged because they already forward the reason verbatim:
   `_commands/gates.py::_claim_gate_reason`, `_commands/transition_close.py`, and
   `llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`. `attest/opcert.py` and `signing.py` are also left
   alone: their verdicts are cryptographic (`mismatch` / `foreign_key`), not staleness, and
   already name the two keys or ids that differ.

Why this approach: the composite hash is one-way, so naming a changed component requires the old per-component values, and the only trustworthy source for them is the SIGNED manifest — anything reconstructed at read time could disagree with what the reviewer actually saw. The alternative of replaying the event store to `signed_at` is rejected: `children` comes from other tickets' state, so it would need a whole-store replay, and compaction squashes exactly the old events where legacy attestations live. Adding the parts to the manifest is additive, authenticated by the existing HMAC, and deterministic (no timestamps), so re-signing stays reproducible.

Attestations signed before this change carry no `material-part:` lines. For them `explain_material_change` degrades in two useful steps rather than falling back to the old fixed list: it uses the signed `plan-material-pin:` child ids to report a `children` add/remove diff when one exists, and when no component difference can be named it says so plainly and points at the pre-330c normalization basis as the likely cause, with the remedy.

No gate outcome changes: every edit is inside the `reason` string of an already-failing branch, or is a new additive manifest line. No branch condition, threshold or verdict value is touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` (new) — component hashing + the diff/explain
  helper.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — emit and parse `material-part:` lines.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — component-named `stale-material` reasons (both
  kinds); timestamp-named `stale-reopened`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` — actionable `unsigned` message.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — replace the fixed-list wording.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — forward the child-closure validity reason, not just the
  verdict.
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` — a dedicated render branch for a `plan_review_sign_aborted`
  signing failure that names the reason and the correct remedy.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — state plainly that ticking a checkbox is attestation-safe, and
  document the component-named staleness reasons.
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` (new) — the tests below.

`pass1.py` is at 776 of the 800-line cap, so the new hashing helper goes in `material_diff.py` and `pass1.py` is not touched.

## Testing

- Happy path: an attestation whose `file_impact` changed reports a reason containing
  `file_impact` and NOT `description` or `children`; likewise a description-only edit and a
  children-only edit, one test each.
- Checkbox pin (330c): an attestation over a description whose boxes are then ticked reports
  `certified`, not `stale-material` — pinning the normalization that is currently only implicit.
- Legacy/grandfather regression: a pre-330c attestation (raw-description basis) over an
  unchanged ticket still reports `certified`, and one that cannot be grandfathered reports the
  "no component differs" wording rather than a spurious component name.
- Edge: an attestation with no `material-part:` lines and no pins still produces an actionable
  reason and never raises.
- Gate-outcome invariance: for each of the stale verdicts, assert `valid is False` and the
  `verdict` value is unchanged from the current code — the same inputs are still refused.
- The full existing suites `tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_material_grandfather_96d1.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` and `tests/unit/test_plan_material_pins.py`
  pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `material_diff.material_components(ctx)` returns a per-component hash map whose keys are
      exactly the `material_fingerprint` basis keys; verified by a test that asserts the key set
      matches and that changing one component changes only that component's hash.
- [ ] `build_manifest` emits sorted `material-part: <name> <hash16>` lines and
      `manifest_material_parts()` round-trips them; verified by a test asserting the round-trip
      and that a manifest without the lines parses to `{}`.
- [ ] A `stale-material` reason from `compute_validity` NAMES the differing component(s) with a
      compact magnitude (for example `file_impact: 13 -> 16 paths`) and does not contain the
      string `description/AC/file_impact/children`; verified by one test per component, plus a
      repo-wide grep asserting that literal no longer appears in `src/`.
- [ ] Ticking checkboxes only leaves the verdict `certified`; verified by a test that signs over
      an unticked description, ticks every box, and asserts `compute_validity` returns
      `verdict == "certified"`.
- [ ] A pre-330c (raw-description) attestation over an unchanged ticket still returns
      `certified`, and an un-grandfatherable one returns a reason that says no component differs
      rather than naming a component; verified by two tests.
- [ ] `stale-reopened` names the reopen timestamp and `unsigned` names both `review-plan` and
      `sign-review` remedies; verified by asserting those substrings in the reasons.
- [ ] A `plan_review_sign_aborted` signing failure renders its reason (for example
      `store-read-failure`) and does NOT advise `sign-review`; verified by a test that feeds a
      verdict carrying that event to the renderer and asserts both facts.
- [ ] A dependency-material change from `generation.py` names the changed dependency ticket
      ids, matching `resign.py`'s existing wording; verified by asserting the ids appear in the
      raised message.
- [ ] No gate outcome changes: for every branch touched, a test asserts the same
      `(valid, verdict)` pair as before, and `pytest tests/unit tests/integration` passes.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states plainly that ticking an AC checkbox is
      attestation-safe; verified by a grep for that statement in the file.

## Provenance

Three independent agent reports on 2026-08-05, recorded in the original description above. Related: bug 858c-786a-13be-4332 (the close gate cannot express an N/A criterion).
baseline.summary: Whether ticking an AC checkbox invalidates a plan-review attestation is inconsistent across tickets

## Problem

The working amd64 Jira Data Center harness only boots inside a CI runner (arm64 hosts stall under emulation — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md`). So every live DC reconcile observation currently costs a full ~2h push→CI cycle, which makes root-causing live-only DC defects (e.g. bug `reckless-diabolic-kob` — rich-text stored as `None` + perpetual re-emit) prohibitively slow.

## Approach

Reuse the EXISTING agentic-in-CI pattern (`scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py` + `.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml`, ticket 259b): boot the ephemeral DC ONCE, then run an Opus agent on rebar's own `rebar.llm` runtime that performs MANY live experiments in that single boot. Where capability-map's agent drives raw REST to *map* the image, this one drives rebar's OWN reconcile primitives to *root-cause* a defect.

New files (test + CI only — no `src/rebar` change):
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_richtext_agentic_probe.py` — an opt-in pytest module
  that reuses the proven `bound_dc_issue` fixture chain (so the agent starts from the exact
  `(repo, local_id, key)` the failing rich-text tests use, cutover `dc` on) and boots the
  agent with two tools: `run_python(code)` (a persistent in-process REPL warm-started with the
  transport, `compute_update_fields`, `WikiTextCodec`, `cutover_clients`, `dc.run_bridge`,
  `rebar`) and `jira_rest(method, path, body)` (raw REST ground-truth). Returns a structured
  `RichTextRca` finding, each experiment cited to evidence ids.
- `.github/workflows/jira-dc-richtext-probe.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch`-only driver, same
  guardrails as capability-map (throwaway ephemeral instance, `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`, agent
  instructed to REPORT not fix), installing `[dev]` (LLM runtime) + `[jira-datacenter]`
  (transport), uploading the finding + evidence artifact.

## Portability

The investigator is a **pytest module gated by env** (`REBAR_DC_RICHTEXT_PROBE=1` + `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` + an LLM credential + the harness skip markers), so it runs against ANY reachable live DC — a local `make jira-dc-up` instance or CI — not a single CI provider. The GitHub Actions workflow is one convenient trigger, not the only path; a contributor with a local DC + key runs the same test directly with `pytest`. It is inert on every ordinary run (opt-in off → skips), never on push/PR/schedule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `test_dc_richtext_agentic_probe.py` exists, lint/format clean, and collects + skips
      cleanly when the opt-in env is unset (no live DC required for collection).
- [x] The module reuses the existing `bound_dc_issue` / `dc_store_copy_repo` / `dc_transport`
      fixtures rather than re-porting the bound-store bootstrap.
- [x] The agent is given `run_python` (persistent namespace) + `jira_rest` tools and returns a
      registered structured `RichTextRca` contract; it asserts only that a finding was
      produced (an investigation, not a correctness assertion — it must not fail merely
      because the bug still reproduces).
- [x] `jira-dc-richtext-probe.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only (no push/PR/schedule), boots
      the pinned DC image, installs both `[dev]` and `[jira-datacenter]`, requires an
      `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (loud fail if absent), sets `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`, and uploads the
      finding + evidence artifact.
- [x] [non-codebase] A `workflow_dispatch` run of the probe on `main` completes and uploads a
      `RichTextRca` finding with cited experiment evidence.
      provenance: environment=github-actions ubuntu-latest runner with the digest-pinned ephemeral Jira DC (run 33129851229, main); principal=github-actions workflow_dispatch job probe-jira-dc-richtext under the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repo secret; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — Run 33129851229 concluded success and its jira-dc-richtext-probe artifact holds rca.json (all RichTextRca contract fields; 10 experiments citing 20 evidence ids) plus evidence.json (51 entries, kinds run_python + jira_rest).
baseline.summary: Reusable agentic in-CI Jira DC investigator (rich-text root-cause probe)

## Why this exists

`src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` is at **exactly 800 lines** — the hard cap. Sibling `elfin-decagonal-polarbear` (F11, mirror F11) must add a `warn_cross_session` flag to `Route` and fold it into `derive_policy_sets`, which cannot be done without going over.

This is filed as its own ticket deliberately. Splitting a module is a structural change with its own review surface; folding it into a mirror-remediation change would put an unrelated refactor inside a change whose reviewed plan is about single-sourcing a policy set, and would make both harder to review and to revert.

**This has already bitten this epic twice.** `_commands/composer.py` was likewise at exactly 800; the F3 change added an import and a comment, took the whole stack to `Verified -1`, and the recovery mis-amended a commit and opened a duplicate Gerrit change. F7 then had to express its fix in ZERO net lines to fit. That is code shaped around a cap rather than around meaning.

Four other `src/rebar` files sit at exactly 800 today (`llm/plan_review/sizing.py`, `llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`, `_commands/composer.py`), so this is a general hazard; this ticket addresses only the one the epic is blocked on.

## The seam

Not a mechanical cut to hit a number. `_registry.py` holds three clusters, and one is already self-contained:

- **route TABLE construction** — `_core_factory`, `_reads_init_only`, `_simple_read_groups`,
  `_lifecycle`, `_writes_full`, `_intercepts`, `_bridge_and_arms`, `_build_routes` (~520 lines)
- **types + lookup** — `Route`, `Finding`, `_index`, `route_for`, `derive_policy_sets`
- **registry VALIDATION** (`:684-795`, ~112 lines) — `_is_valid_reference`, the six `_check_*`
  functions, `_CHECKS`, `validate`

The validation cluster is the seam: its functions call only each other, take `routes: tuple[Route, ...]` as a PARAMETER, and yield `Finding`. It reads the registry; it does not build it. Extracting it leaves `_registry.py` at roughly 688 with ~112 lines of headroom, and the new module lands well above the 100-LOC floor, so this is a split along an existing call-graph seam rather than one invented for the cap.

The consumer surface is verified rather than assumed. 22 files reference `rebar._cli._registry`, and across named imports and module-handle access they consume exactly eight names: `ROUTES`, `Route`, `validate`, `route_for`, `derive_policy_sets`, `ADAPTER_KINDS`, `INIT_POLICIES`, `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. Of the cluster being moved, only `validate` is consumed from outside, so `validate` must stay importable from `rebar._cli._registry`. `Finding` is consumed NOWHERE outside the module — it is the validation cluster's own return type, named only by the `_check_*` functions that move with it — so it needs no re-export. (`test_capabilities` and `test_cli_registry` import `Route, validate`; `test_cli_registry_dispatch` imports the module handle. None of the three imports `Finding`.) The in-tree precedent for the back-compat re-export is `gate_dispatch.py`, which re-exports the `plan_review_recovery` cluster and documents the re-export as load-bearing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: the validation cluster moves to a new `src/rebar/_cli/_registry_checks.py`, and
      `_registry.py` is under the cap with real headroom. Verified by `wc -l` on both and by the
      CI module-size gate passing.
- [x] AC2: the eight externally-consumed names remain resolvable on `rebar._cli._registry`
      after the split. Verified by a test that asserts each of `ROUTES`, `Route`, `validate`,
      `route_for`, `derive_policy_sets`, `ADAPTER_KINDS`, `INIT_POLICIES` and
      `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is present on the module, and by the existing consumer suites
      (`test_capabilities`, `test_cli_registry`, `test_cli_registry_dispatch`) passing
      untouched.
- [x] AC3: behavior is byte-identical — the same findings, in the same order, for the same
      routes. Verified by a test asserting `tuple(validate(ROUTES))` is unchanged and by
      `validate()` still returning empty on the committed registry.
- [x] AC4: the new module is above the 100-LOC floor, so this is a seam extraction and not a
      fragment. Verified by `wc -l`.
- [x] AC5: no route definition, alias, or policy set is altered. Verified by a test asserting
      the `ROUTES` name/alias sets and every `derive_policy_sets` output are identical to
      before, so the split cannot have moved behavior.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "registry or capabilities or dispatch or cli" -q` — AC2, AC3,
  AC5 and the existing registry suites.
- `wc -l src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py src/rebar/_cli/_registry_checks.py` — AC1, AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Split _cli/_registry.py at its validation seam so the registry has headroom

## Why

The bespoke `verifier_cfg` downgrades the verify pass from the default frontier model (Opus) to a
decisive non-frontier model (Sonnet) unless the operator explicitly chose a model. The workflow verify
step does NOT apply this today (it uses the runner default), so migrating drift-refresh off bespoke
(WS1) would lose the downgrade. Reproduce it declaratively via the existing per-step `model:` key
(`resolve_model`, WS-D3: step > workflow > cfg). Because this makes a per-step `model:` key first-class
on a shipped gate workflow, it must also be reflected in the visual editor UX — today only the
workflow-level model is carried in BPMN, so editing the workflow in the visual editor could silently
drop a step's model.

## What

- Pin the workflow verify step's `model:` to the decisive non-frontier verifier (Sonnet) by default,
  resolved via the existing per-step `model:` / `resolve_model` path; honor an explicit operator model
  override (parity with `verifier_cfg`).
- Visual editor: surface the per-step `model` field in the properties panel (a select over the known
  model ladder), and make a per-step `model` round-trip through BPMN export/import so a visual edit +
  save never drops it.
- BPMN back-compat: importing a pre-existing BPMN document that lacks the per-step model attribute
  defaults gracefully to "no per-step override" (the step falls back to the workflow/cfg model via
  `resolve_model`), never errors.
- Document the per-step `model:` knob in the workflow-authoring + editor docs.

## Scope

In scope: the verify-step model pin + override, the editor properties-panel field, BPMN round-trip +
back-compat, and docs. Out of scope: drift-refresh migration / bespoke deletion (WS1), token chunking
(WS3 sizes against the model this story pins), the coach-gate nit (WS4). Touches:
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml`, `runs.py` (`resolve_model`), `bpmn.py`, `editor.py`,
and the workflow-authoring/editor docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The workflow verify step pins the decisive non-frontier verifier model (Sonnet) by default,
      resolved via the existing per-step `model:` / `resolve_model` path.
- [ ] An explicit operator model override is honored on the verify step (parity with `verifier_cfg`).
- [ ] The visual editor properties panel lets a user view/edit a step's `model`.
- [ ] A per-step `model` survives a BPMN export → import (visual-edit → save) round-trip unchanged; a
      regression test asserts the round-trip.
- [ ] Importing a legacy BPMN document that lacks the per-step model attribute succeeds and falls back
      to the workflow/cfg model (no error, no per-step override).
- [ ] Authoring + editor docs document the per-step `model:` knob.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: WS2: Per-step verifier model:key (Sonnet downgrade) surfaced in the visual editor UX

# s3 doctor should fold bundle heads into the published ref, not the worktree HEAD

## Context

Split out of bug `gnarled-acardiac-bettong` (landed as Gerrit 1628), which proved the defect and closed the silent-corruption door with a loud refusal. This ticket is the proper fix that refusal stands in for, and retires the refusal.

Today `_fold_heads` (`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:232-261`) merges every fetched bundle head into the tracker WORKTREE's HEAD with `git merge` and returns `git rev-parse HEAD`. Because `git merge` only merges into the checked-out branch, the heal's result is a function of whatever branch the tracker happens to be on. `_require_tracker_on_ref` (`s3_doctor.py:167-195`) therefore refuses the heal outright whenever `current_branch != ref` (detached HEAD included), so the doctor is SAFE but cannot heal such a tracker at all.

## Premise validated against origin/main (cc69cc1179)

- The guard and its "retires with envious-metal-budgie" docstring are present at
  `s3_doctor.py:167-195`; `_heal_locked` calls it at `s3_doctor.py:136`.
- `_publish_and_prune` (`s3_doctor.py:264-317`) now relies on that guard: its docstring records
  that the `git branch -f` fallback was removed, and it bundles `HEAD` + `refs/heads/<ref>` at
  `s3_doctor.py:285`.
- Regression floor is GREEN today: `tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py` +
  `test_s3_doctor_heldout.py` = 18 passed, 1 skipped.

## Mechanism decision (experimentally settled, not assumed)

The ticket left the mechanism open (`merge-tree`/`commit-tree` vs a scratch worktree). Probed both concerns on Git 2.55 in a throwaway repo shaped like the tracker:

- `git merge-tree --write-tree A B` DOES honour the tracker's configured `ours` driver
  (`merge.ours.driver=true`, set by `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:559`) together with the
  tickets-branch `.gitattributes` `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` line
  (`_commands/init.py:62`). It produced a tree byte-identical to the worktree `git merge` on the
  same inputs, and it CONFLICTS identically when the driver is absent. So the merge policy AC is
  satisfiable without a worktree.
- A real content conflict exits non-zero and names the conflicted paths — and, unlike `git
  merge`, leaves NO worktree/index state, so no `merge --abort` is needed.
- `git commit-tree <tree> -p <ref-tip> -p <head>` builds the 2-parent merge commit; unrelated
  histories need `--allow-unrelated-histories` on `merge-tree`. That flag is NOT a new version
  requirement: git-merge-tree(1) documents both `--write-tree` and `--allow-unrelated-histories`
  as of 2.38.0 (checked against the 2.38.0 manual page), which is exactly the floor the repo
  already enforces — so no version fallback is needed and none is planned.

A scratch worktree was rejected: it costs a full checkout of the event tree on every heal. `merge-tree` needs no checkout and never touches the worktree. Git floor is already 2.38 for `merge-tree --write-tree` (README.md:143-147, `tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py`).

## Plan

1. **Rewrite `_fold_heads` (`s3_doctor.py:232-261`)** to fold into the published ref, not HEAD:
   start from `refs/heads/<ref>`'s tip; for each head ref, skip if already an ancestor of the
   running tip; else `git merge-tree --write-tree [--allow-unrelated-histories] <tip> <head>`
   then `git commit-tree <tree> -p <tip> -p <head> -m "Merge <head> (s3 doctor auto-heal of ref
   <ref>)"`. A non-zero `merge-tree` still raises `S3DoctorConflict` with the same message shape
   (the existing hint carrying `fsck-recover` is preserved). Keep the existing write lock and the
   iterated 2-parent shape. Both flags are inside the repo's existing 2.38 Git floor, so no
   version probe or fallback path is introduced.
2. **Move the ref (`_heal_locked`, `s3_doctor.py:136-143`)**: publish the folded sha onto
   `refs/heads/<ref>` under the same lock. When `ref` is NOT checked out:
   `git update-ref refs/heads/<ref> <merged> <old-tip>` — a compare-and-swap, so a concurrent
   mover aborts the heal instead of clobbering. When `ref` IS the checked-out branch: `git reset
   --hard <merged>`, so index and worktree stay consistent with the branch exactly as the old
   `git merge` left them.
3. **Replace the refusal guard**: delete `_require_tracker_on_ref` (`s3_doctor.py:167-195`) and
   its call (`s3_doctor.py:136`). In its place, a much narrower pre-download guard: when `ref` IS
   checked out and the worktree is dirty, refuse before downloading anything (today's `git merge`
   already fails on a dirty worktree, later and less clearly — this keeps that refusal and makes
   it early). A tracker on another branch or detached HEAD is no longer refused at all.
4. **Fix `_publish_and_prune` (`s3_doctor.py:264-317`)**: its docstring's "guard has established
   ref IS the checked-out branch" reasoning is retired. Bundle `refs/heads/<ref>` explicitly
   rather than relying on `HEAD` agreeing (`s3_doctor.py:285`); off-branch, HEAD no longer names
   the merged tip.
5. **Tests** (`tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py`): convert the three refusal tests
   (`:206`, `:235`, `:251`) into HEAL tests — a side-branch tracker and a detached-HEAD tracker
   both heal losslessly, and no commit reachable only from the side branch becomes reachable from
   the published ref. Keep `:275` (single-bundle no-op off the ref). Add: the side branch and the
   worktree HEAD are UNMOVED by an off-branch heal; the dirty-worktree refusal; and an
   on-branch heal still advances HEAD/index/worktree.
6. **Add the missing `merge=ours` regression.** The merge-policy AC has NO existing coverage:
   grep for `merge=ours` / `bridge_state` across `tests/integration/test_s3_doctor*.py` and
   `s3_doctor_harness.py` returns nothing, and the harness builds a bare `git init` tracker with
   `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` (`s3_doctor_harness.py:33-50`), so no `ours` driver and no
   `.gitattributes` are in play today. Add a test that commits the tickets-branch
   `.gitattributes` (`.bridge_state/* merge=ours`, as `_commands/init.py:62` writes) and sets
   `merge.ours.driver=true` in the tracker (as `_commands/init.py:559` does), then folds two
   heads that modify the SAME `.bridge_state/*` file differently: the heal must succeed with the
   tracker's own side kept, not conflict. This test is written FIRST against today's `git merge`
   fold, so it pins the policy the `merge-tree` rewrite must reproduce.
   The real-conflict/no-delete behaviour at `test_s3_doctor_heldout.py:109` must stay green
   unchanged (line 81 is the unrelated-history union test, not a merge-policy test).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The heal folds heads into the published ref's tip regardless of the tracker's checked-out
      branch.
- [x] No commit reachable only from the checked-out branch becomes reachable from the published
      ref.
- [x] A new regression test proves the fold resolves a `.bridge_state/*` collision via
      `merge=ours` (keeping the tracker's side) rather than conflicting; it passes on today's
      fold and on the rewritten one.
- [x] A real content conflict raises `S3DoctorConflict` and deletes no bundle, rather than
      resolving silently.
- [x] A tracker with a different branch checked out heals successfully.
- [x] A detached-HEAD tracker heals successfully.
- [x] `_require_tracker_on_ref` is deleted, and the off-branch/detached heals are proven by
      tests that fail before this change.
- [x] After an on-branch heal, `git status --porcelain` in the tracker is empty (index and
      worktree consistent with the moved ref).
- [x] After an off-branch heal, the checked-out branch's tip and the worktree are unchanged.
- [x] The 18 existing s3_doctor tests stay green.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: s3 doctor should fold bundle heads into the published ref, not the worktree HEAD

## Context / Problem

The `concurrency` overlay prompt (prerequisite story) needs registration before it can run: `OVERLAY_IDS` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:38) is the closed enum the base reviewer may escalate to; the overlay union is `glob ∪ content ∪ recommend` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:98-110); and `content_triggered_overlays` (registry.py:321) currently fires only `deletion-impact`. Registration is sequenced AFTER the prompt so the workflow can never escalate to a dimension with no reviewer behind it.

## Approach

Five additive edits. (1) Add `"concurrency"` to `OVERLAY_IDS` — the base-output schema enum derives via `overlay_id_enum()` (registry.py:73), so no schema file edit; the `overlay_union` step then auto-emits `include_concurrency` (it derives one `include_<overlay>` flag per `OVERLAY_IDS` member via `overlay_flag_key`, workflow_ops.py:117-119), and `overlay_union_output.schema.json` is dynamic-keyed (`patternProperties` on `^include_[a-z0-9_]+$`), so no schema edit there either. (2) Add a committed HIGH-PRECISION cross-stack token tuple and extend `content_triggered_overlays` to scan BOTH added and removed diff lines (file headers excluded) for these literal substrings, returning `concurrency` alongside the existing deletion-impact result. Token list (decided; survey-grounded in Lu et al. ASPLOS'08, Tu et al. ASPLOS'19, the RacerD trigger heuristic, and CodeQL CERT concurrency packs): `Mutex`, `RwLock`, `Lock(`, `Semaphore`, `synchronized`, `volatile`, `@GuardedBy`, `Interlocked.`, `Atomics.`, `pthread_`, `flock`, `fcntl.`, `O_EXCL`, `mkstemp`, `Thread(`, `go func(`, `tokio::spawn`, `Task.Run(`, `worker_threads`, `new Worker(`, `multiprocessing.`, `asyncio.create_task`, `asyncio.gather`, `concurrent.futures`, `os.fork(`, `cluster.fork(`, `sync.WaitGroup`, `sync.Once`, `make(chan `, `atomic.`, `FOR UPDATE`, `SKIP LOCKED`, `SERIALIZABLE`, `advisory_lock`, `NOWAIT`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `start_new_session`, `compare-and-swap`, `coroutineScope`, `launch {`. Deliberately EXCLUDED as too noisy for the committed tier (decided): the async/await family, bare `fork`, `retry`, `.lock`, `Popen`, `Promise.all(`, `setInterval(`, `select {` — that noisy tier is project-overlay material, delivered by the sibling dogfood story. (3) Add the one-line catalog entry to `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md`: `concurrency — threads, async tasks, multiprocessing, locks, channels, shared/global mutable state, file/DB locking` (recognition cue only; the base reviewer does no concurrency analysis). (4) Add the routing entry to `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`: `exec: AGENT`, `applies_to: []`, `default_posture: advisory`, `block_threshold: 0.95`, `blocking_enabled: false`, with a `_comment` citing the survey and the calibrate-then-flip path. (5) Wire the gate dispatch: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` enumerates every overlay explicitly, so add the two dispatch lines — `- { prompt: code-review-concurrency, when: "${{ steps.triggers.outputs.include_concurrency }}" }` to the `round_a` batch and the `steps.union.outputs.include_concurrency` twin to the `round_b` batch — following the existing per-overlay pattern (e.g. the `code-review-security` lines at code-review.yaml:94 and :133); without these lines a registered overlay is authored-but-unreachable. Positive rationale: RacerD's production precedent — a single lexical cue flips on the expensive analysis — and the recall-biased list is safe because an over-fire costs one advisory pass, never a wrong verdict. Measured fire rate of this tier on this repo's last 300 main commits: 14% (43/300); recorded here as calibration context.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — `OVERLAY_IDS`, token tuple, `content_triggered_overlays` extension.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — catalog line.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` — routing entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the `round_a` + `round_b` dispatch lines.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py` — trigger and routing cases (module created by the sibling trigger-extension story; if this story lands first, create it here).

## Testing

Unit tier (pure functions; no live boundary). Oracles: returned overlay-id lists and `threshold_for` output.

- Recall, corpus-derived: a diff hunk adding `start_new_session=True` (distilled from 9ad46965bd, the `eclectic-spotted-barb` introducing change) fires `concurrency`.
- Removal path: a diff REMOVING a `sync.Mutex` line fires (survey consequence: deleting synchronization is concurrency-introducing).
- Negative controls: a diff containing only `async def`/`await` lines does NOT fire `concurrency`; a token appearing only on a context (unprefixed) line does NOT fire; the existing deletion-impact behavior is unchanged on its current test corpus.
- Routing: `threshold_for("concurrency")` returns the advisory 0.95 / blocking-disabled posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `"concurrency"` is in `OVERLAY_IDS` and returned by `overlay_id_enum()`; checked by unit test.
- [x] `content_triggered_overlays` returns `concurrency` for the corpus-derived added-line hunk AND for a removed `sync.Mutex` line; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py`.
- [x] Negative controls pass: `async def`/`await`-only diffs and context-line-only tokens do not fire; deletion-impact results unchanged.
- [x] `code-review-base.md` lists `concurrency` in the overlay catalog with the one-line cue; checked by grep.
- [x] `code-review.yaml` carries the `code-review-concurrency` dispatch line in BOTH the `round_a` batch (gated on `steps.triggers.outputs.include_concurrency`) and the `round_b` batch (gated on `steps.union.outputs.include_concurrency`); checked by grep, and the workflow lint (`make lint`) passes over the edited gate.
- [x] `threshold_for("concurrency")` asserts advisory/0.95/blocking-disabled; checked by unit test.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py` pass.
baseline.summary: Register the concurrency overlay: high-precision content trigger, base catalog, advisory routing

## Context / Problem
origin/main HEAD trips the C901 complexity ratchet added by c9f7 (scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check reports increased=1, so make lint exits non-zero). Root cause: commit aec1 (ff4c5600) raised src/rebar/llm/runner.py::PydanticAIRunner.run cyclomatic complexity from its baseline ceiling 24 to 25 via a success-path run-shape try/except. aec1 merged before c9f7, but c9f7's Verified gate ran on a pre-aec1 patchset; Gerrit's submit-time rebase stacked the gate on aec1 without re-verifying (ADR-0047 rebase-without-reverify hazard). A pre-existing failure of our quality ratchets on current origin/main; must be resolved before the epic's ratchet stories can close.

## Approach
Extract aec1's success-path shape-capture try/except (usage_log.run_shape + shape_only + telemetry-safe except) out of PydanticAIRunner.run into a small module-level helper (_merge_success_run_shape) that mutates the usage dict in place. Behavior-preserving; removes one try + one except branch from run, bringing its C901 back to <=24. No baseline regeneration; shrink-only invariant restored, not conceded.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py
- tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py

## Testing / Verification
- python3 scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check exits 0
- make lint exits 0 on current origin/main
- pytest -q tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py (the success-path shape tests plus the new swallow-and-warn test) and the pydantic_ai runner suite pass

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] PydanticAIRunner.run C901 complexity <= committed baseline ceiling (24)
- [x] Extracted helper preserves the success-path key merge, proven by the existing tests test_the_success_row_records_the_tool_call_shape_too and test_the_success_row_carries_the_limits_and_duration_it_ran_under (both drive a full success run() and assert the shape_only keys/limits reach the recorded row)
- [x] The helper swallows a run_shape/shape_only failure with the same warning log and leaves the authoritative usage dict unchanged, proven by test_success_shape_capture_swallows_reducer_failure_and_warns in tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py
- [x] python3 scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check exits 0 against current origin/main (increased=0, new=0, stale=0)
- [x] make lint exits 0 against current origin/main
- [x] pytest -q tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py exits 0
baseline.summary: Restore C901 ratchet green on origin/main: extract runner run-shape capture

baseline.description:
## Context
During the F07 documentation-link validation run, the full test suite failed while a fixture created a ticket in an isolated temporary store. `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py` terminated `git commit` after the 30-second `_GIT_TIMEOUT`. The completion-attestation behavior under test did not run. The exact node passed alone in 55.48 seconds.

Closed ticket `moldavite-evasive-elephant` classifies the earlier occurrence as runner I/O contention during a long test job and directs maintainers to track a recurrence separately. Closed ticket `royal-weariless-zebrafish` addresses store-lock acquisition before the write body. It does not address a timeout after acquisition while `git commit` is running.

## Plan
- Reproduce the timeout under controlled concurrent temporary-store writes and capture subprocess timing.
- Distinguish host I/O contention from incorrect timeout or fixture behavior.
- Correct the proven failure class without retrying an unexplained intermittent failure.
- Add focused regression coverage for the confirmed mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The root cause is demonstrated with repeatable evidence.
- [x] A regression test fails for the confirmed mechanism before the fix.
- [x] The fix addresses the failure class rather than one observed run.
- [x] Focused store and lifecycle tests pass.
- [x] The ticket records the relationship to `moldavite-evasive-elephant` and `royal-weariless-zebrafish`.

## Fix Plan (Phase 2 — re-investigation; bound STAYS 30s, c2ba parity test untouched)
Root cause (RCA comment): on git >=2.47 the lock-held `git commit` runs `git maintenance run --auto` FOREGROUND (ADR 0051), so an O(store) repack is charged to `event_commit_git._GIT_TIMEOUT=30`; on a mature store it exceeds 30s and the commit is SIGKILLed (lost write + mid-repack corruption hazard). Fix decouples maintenance from the latency-bounded commit:
- `gitutil.run_auto_maintenance(tracker)`: explicit `git maintenance run --auto` bounded by watchdog-grade `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (not the per-commit bound); best-effort; plus an `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` tuple (`-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false`).
- `event_commit_git._git_commit`/`_git_commit_paths`: inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` so the 30s covers only the commit. COMPLETE ENUMERATION of the event-append path's OTHER lock-held `git commit` invocations that bypass those two helpers and build their own argv — both are covered by injecting `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` directly: `event_append._recover_from_unmerged` (the UU-recovery retry commit) and `event_append._recover_from_invalid_object` (the poisoned-index reset+retry commit). No lock-held commit on the event-append path charges a foreground repack to `_GIT_TIMEOUT`.
- `event_append`: after a successful lock-held commit, call `run_auto_maintenance` UNDER the write lock (ADR 0051 serialization preserved; loose-growth still bounded).
- `txn.py` claim/transition commit (the OTHER lock-held write surface): apply the same maint-suppression + explicit post-commit maintenance. NOTE this surface is bounded at the watchdog-grade `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (120s, via `gitutil.run_git_write`), NOT the 30s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` — so it is far LESS exposed than the event-append path and this edit is defense-in-depth for AC-3 class-completeness, not a 30s fix: it removes the SAME corruption class (a foreground O(store) repack charged to a bounded, lock-held commit, whose watchdog SIGKILL lands mid-`git repack` regardless of whether the bound is 30s or 120s).
- `delete.py` (DELETE + UNLINK-cleanup) and `compact_plan.py` (`commit_ticket_dir`): these run through `gitutil.run_git_write` (120s watchdog, like txn.py). Inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` on their commits (SUPPRESS-ONLY, no deferred maintenance): `delete.py` deliberately holds NO store write lock (its own comment: a `git reset --hard` could clobber a concurrent writer), and `compact_plan.py` IS the store-maintenance/fold path — so running `git maintenance run --auto` there would be the UNSERIALIZED foreground repack ADR 0051 forbids. Suppression alone removes the corruption class on these surfaces; their loose objects are repacked by the next LOCKED event_append/txn write's deferred `run_auto_maintenance` (git's `--auto` threshold makes that safe and sufficient).
- `compact.py` (`ticket-compact-all` SNAPSHOT-backfill commit) and `fsck_repair.py` (the a3-remediation batch commits, one per 200-ticket batch): the remaining lock-held store-commit surfaces that build their own `commit` argv. Inject `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` SUPPRESS-ONLY, for the same reason as `compact_plan.py`/`delete.py` — `compact.py` IS the compaction/fold path, and `fsck_repair.py` is a repair batch loop, so an inline foreground `--auto` repack there would be exactly the O(store) cost charged to a bounded lock-held commit that this fix removes; their loose objects are repacked by the next LOCKED event_append/txn write's deferred `run_auto_maintenance`.
- Regression test: with a store past the loose threshold and `_GIT_TIMEOUT` monkeypatched small, the write SUCCEEDS after the fix and FAILS ("git timed out") before it.

## Acceptance Criteria (updated)
- [x] Root cause demonstrated with repeatable evidence (RCA comment).
- [x] A regression test fails for the confirmed mechanism before the fix.
- [x] The fix addresses the failure class across ALL lock-held store-commit surfaces, not one run: event_append primary (`_git_commit`/`_git_commit_paths`) + its two recovery commits (`_recover_from_unmerged`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`), txn.py claim/transition, delete.py (DELETE + UNLINK-cleanup), compact_plan.py (`commit_ticket_dir`), compact.py (`ticket-compact-all` backfill), and fsck_repair.py (a3-remediation batch commits).
- [x] Focused store and lifecycle tests pass.
- [x] Records the relationship to moldavite-evasive-elephant and royal-weariless-zebrafish.
baseline.summary: Diagnose temporary-store git commit timeout under suite load

baseline.description:
## Why

13 Jira issues are pinned at Jira's 5000-comment HARD cap, inflated by the pre-P1 non-idempotent re-posting bug (local truth 22-76 distinct comments each; Jira holds ~65 copies of each until it hit 5000). P1 (landed a6cdad0e2) STOPS new duplication, but the caps remain — so NEW comments on these 13 tickets still silently fail to sync (`COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`) until the duplicates are purged.

13 issues (rebar-id -> Jira key, local-distinct / Jira-total): REB-155(5fd2, 76/5000), REB-352(e0e2, 64), REB-428(8937, 31), REB-341(db7b, 30), REB-289(b744, 29), REB-427(822a, 27), REB-183(7284, 25), REB-327(d251, 25), REB-424(2359, 25), REB-425(33d0, 25), REB-190(75a9, 22), REB-426(59ef, 22), REB-453(b4d4, 22).

## Concrete mechanisms (resolve the plan-review blocks — code-grounded, reused not reinvented)

**Bot-authored identification (safety-critical filter).** Jira REST returns each comment `body` as an Atlassian Document Format (ADF) dict, NOT a plain string, so the marker must be detected on the RENDERED text, never by substring-searching the raw ADF object. A comment is bridge-bot-authored IFF `adf.adf_to_text(body)` contains the reconciler marker `RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py:43`), appended to every outbound comment by `_decorate_outbound_comment` (`:140-147`) as its own paragraph — which survives the ADF round-trip and re-renders to the literal marker text (`outbound_comments.py:144-145`). Reuse `adf.adf_to_text` (the same renderer `_normalize_comment_body` uses) to render before the marker check; note `_normalize_comment_body` STRIPS the marker for the dedup key, so marker DETECTION uses the pre-strip rendered text while the dedup GROUPING uses the marker-stripped normalized text. This intrinsic marker is the PRIMARY and authoritative identifier — robust to accountId / display-name changes, unlike an author field. A comment whose rendered text lacks the marker is treated as human/foreign and is NEVER a deletion candidate. Secondary cross-check: the backup captures every comment's `author.accountId`; the script asserts that all marked (candidate) comments across the 13 tickets resolve to a single bot `accountId` and records it — a divergent accountId on a marked comment aborts the run for manual review (defense in depth; the marker still governs).

**Dedup key = the reconciler's OWN normalization (parity guarantee).** Group candidate comments by `outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body(body)` — imported and reused verbatim, NOT re-implemented — which does ADF->text via `adf.adf_to_text` then strips the marker and leading/trailing whitespace (`outbound_comments.py:116-137`). Using the identical function the reconciler uses to decide "already mirrored" guarantees the cleanup's notion of "distinct body" matches the reconciler's, so post-cleanup the reconciler sees exactly one copy per distinct body and emits zero re-adds. Machine-canary comments (`_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES`: "BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT:", "Still stale as of") carry volatile timestamps -> each is a distinct normalized body -> each is kept (never a "duplicate" to purge) — correct and safe.

**Pagination (fetch ALL 5000, not the first page).** Reuse the live-validated `acli.py::get_comments(key)` with `--paginate` + `_parse_paginated_comments` (the P1 fix, confirmed returning 5000/5000 for REB-155) to build the full comment set for backup + delete-list. Do NOT hand-roll a single-page fetch. NOTE: `_parse_paginated_comments` returns only a flat `list[dict]` and DISCARDS the response envelope, so it does NOT surface Jira's reported `total`. The completeness check therefore obtains the total via a SEPARATE, dedicated metadata call — `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?maxResults=0` returns `{total, maxResults, startAt, comments: []}`; the script reads `total` from that envelope (new script-level work, not provided by the reuse target) and reconciles `len(fetched) == total` per ticket, REFUSING to proceed if they differ (guards a silently-truncated fetch producing an incomplete/dangerous delete list).

**Keep-one rule.** For each distinct normalized body among MARKED comments on a ticket: keep the OLDEST copy (min `created` timestamp) and delete the rest via `DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id}`. A distinct body with only ONE marked copy is NEVER deleted. Unmarked (human) comments are never touched.

**Rate limiting + transient-failure handling.** Jira Cloud enforces API rate limits over ~64k+ DELETEs (≈4900 × 13). Throttle to a conservative default (≤10 req/s, i.e. ≥100ms inter-call sleep). IMPORTANT: the existing `_direct_rest_delete` -> `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` path does NOT retry HTTP 429/5xx — it re-raises 4xx/5xx immediately as deterministic (`acli_rest.py:62-64`). SINGLE chosen route (no alternatives): wrap each DELETE call through `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, which is the repo's one existing 429+Retry-After-aware retry (honors `Retry-After`, exponential backoff). Do NOT hand-roll a second retry layer. Deletions are logged (ticket, comment id, normalized-body hash, outcome) to an append-only artifact `artifacts/jira-cleanup/deletions-<ts>.jsonl` (one JSON object per line) as they happen, so a mid-run rate-limit stall is resumable.

**Idempotent + resumable.** Re-running is safe: a comment already deleted (404 on DELETE) is treated as success. On partial failure, re-run `--dry-run` to see the remaining duplicates and resume `--execute`; the keep-one grouping is recomputed from the live paginated set each run.

**Rollback (irreversible-op mitigation).** Jira comment deletion cannot be undone via API. The pre-deletion backup JSON (id, body, author, created, per ticket) is the restore artifact. Concrete restore procedure: a `--restore <backup.json> --ticket <key>` script mode re-POSTs each DELETED comment's ADF body (`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment`, cross-referencing the deletions-<ts>.jsonl log to restore only what THIS run deleted). Target state after restore: the ticket again holds one instance of each restored distinct body (content-restore, NOT id-restore — re-created comments get NEW ids/timestamps, and the reconciler marker is re-appended by the normal outbound decorate path on the next sync). The backup MUST exist and pass its completeness check before any DELETE fires. Because restore only re-creates content (not the exact 5000-copy inflated state), rollback is a safety net for accidental over-deletion, not a bit-exact undo.

## What — irreversible; execute ONLY under this T4 safety plan (inlined)

- [ ] **Pre-deletion backup:** export FULL comment payload (id, body, author.accountId,
      author.displayName, created) for all 13 tickets to a versioned JSON artifact under
      `artifacts/jira-cleanup/backup-<ts>.json` BEFORE any deletion. Proving command: the script
      asserts, per ticket, `len(backup[key]) == jira_reported_total` and that the artifact is
      non-empty and parses; deletion is refused if the assertion fails.
- [ ] **Dry-run default:** the script defaults to `--dry-run`; it prints, per ticket, the count
      of marked comments, the count of distinct normalized bodies, the kept (oldest) id per body,
      and the delete-id count — and a machine-readable diff artifact. `--execute` is required to
      delete and runs ONLY after explicit human approval of the dry-run diff.
- [ ] **Keep-one dedup:** oldest-`created` kept per distinct normalized body; marker-authored
      only; single-copy bodies and all unmarked comments excluded (per mechanisms above).
- [ ] **Operator flow / rejection:** dry-run -> human review -> approve|reject. On reject or
      abort, NO deletion occurs and the run exits cleanly (backup + dry-run artifacts retained).
- [ ] **Sequencing:** run ONLY after P1 is live in the reconciler (CONFIRMED: reconcile-bridge
      run 29625135085 on commit a6cdad0e2 = green) — else the reconciler re-inflates within
      minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Backup artifact exists and passes its per-ticket completeness check — `len(fetched)` from
      the paginated `get_comments` equals `total` read from the dedicated
      `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?maxResults=0` envelope — BEFORE any deletion. Proving
      command: `python -m json.tool artifacts/jira-cleanup/backup-<ts>.json >/dev/null` + the
      script's count-reconciliation log line per ticket.
- [ ] Dry-run diff (delete-id list + kept-oldest-id per distinct body, per ticket) is produced
      and human-approved before `--execute`. [operator-attested]
- [ ] Deletion filter provably respects: (a) marked-only (RECONCILER_MARKER present), (b)
      keep-oldest-per-distinct-body, (c) never single-copy, (d) never unmarked/human. A unit test
      over a synthetic comment set asserts the delete-list the planner computes matches (a)-(d);
      RED if the filter mislabels a human/unmarked or single-copy comment as deletable.
- [ ] Rate-limit safety: the DELETE loop routes through `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
      (the single chosen 429/Retry-After route); a unit test asserts a 429 is retried (not
      dropped) and `Retry-After` is honored.
- [ ] Completeness-gate enforcement: a unit test asserts the script REFUSES to proceed (non-zero
      exit, no DELETE issued) when the paginated fetched-count != the `?maxResults=0` reported
      `total` for any ticket (guards a silently-truncated fetch).
- [ ] accountId cross-check: a unit test asserts (a) a marked comment whose `author.accountId`
      diverges from the single resolved bot accountId ABORTS the run for manual review (no DELETE),
      and (b) a homogeneous marked set records the bot accountId and proceeds.
- [ ] Approval-gate enforcement: a unit/integration test asserts `--dry-run` (default) issues
      ZERO DELETE calls, and that `--execute` is the ONLY path that issues DELETEs; on operator
      reject/abort no DELETE is issued and artifacts are retained.
- [ ] Reconciler quiescing during `--execute`: the run window is coordinated so the live
      reconciler does not write to the 13 tickets mid-deletion (either the pass cadence is paused,
      or the window is chosen between passes). [operator-attested]
- [ ] Post-execution, each of the 13 tickets is below the 5000 cap AND a reconcile pass emits 0
      comment re-adds for them (idempotent steady state). [operator-attested against a green
      reconcile-bridge run]
- [ ] The deletion-log artifact `artifacts/jira-cleanup/deletions-<ts>.jsonl` (one JSON object per
      line: ticket, comment id, normalized-body hash, outcome) exists for the executed run.
      Proving command: `wc -l artifacts/jira-cleanup/deletions-<ts>.jsonl` matches the reported
      delete count.
baseline.summary: Jira data cleanup: purge duplicate comments on the 13 capped tickets (after P1 deploys; dry-run+approval first)

baseline.description:
## Context
The plan-review gate (`5fd2`) reviews ONE ticket's plan in isolation. It deliberately does NOT detect SEMANTIC overlap, duplication, or undeclared dependencies BETWEEN SEPARATE tickets across the store. Existing coverage is partial and different in kind: `G4` checks consistency WITHIN one epic's children; `next_batch` schedules around DETERMINISTIC file-impact conflicts; `duplicates`/`supersedes` are MANUAL links. The residual — semantic overlap / duplication / hidden cross-ticket dependency across UNRELATED tickets — is uncovered.

## Scope
A store-wide overlap detector for the ticket UNDER PLAN REVIEW, comparing it against the whole store (cross-epic AND non-epic; any other ticket may overlap). It runs as a distinct STORE-WIDE step during the plan-review invocation window (before claim), NOT as a per-ticket `5fd2` criterion — a per-ticket reviewer cannot see the whole store, which is exactly why this is a separate step. It is ADVISORY ONLY and never affects the claim-gate verdict.

## Design (plan of record — full detail + research + experiment evidence in the comments)
Two-stage retrieve-then-rerank: (0) each ticket gets a cached, LLM-extracted Cupid digest (no embeddings, no vector DB); (1) brute-force BM25F over corpus digests narrows to ~20 candidates, excluding the query ticket's own graph; (2) a bounded LLM pairwise judge classifies each candidate and surfaces ≤3 advisory link suggestions for human confirmation. Enrichment is async via an event-sourced queue drained opportunistically (Tier 1). Child stories S1–S7 implement it; Tier-2/Tier-3 drain and a Jira-reconciler drain are spun out as linked ideas.

### Derisking experiments (run 2026-07-09 — see the experiment-results comment)
- **Recall (the load-bearing bet): VALIDATED.** digest-BM25F retrieved 8/8 heavy paraphrases at rank 1, recall@20 = 1.0, STABLE as corpus grew 60→200 (raw-BM25 baseline decayed 0.875→0.75). No embedding stage is needed for recall. Caveat: N=8 (≥0.8 demonstrated, not 1.0 guaranteed); the residual risk is PRECISION at scale, which the S6 judge is the mitigation for.
- **Latency: VALIDATED.** brute-force BM25F single-query top-20 = 0.69 ms at 800 digests (~14× under the 10 ms budget) → no ANN / vector DB.
- **Enrichment economics: VALIDATED.** ~$0.0024/ticket, ≈ $1.90 one-time for all 793 tickets, cached and re-run only on edit.
- **Store primitives: CONFIRMED.** the manual write-lock (`lock.acquire`/`LockHandle`, `txn.py` precedent) supports the queue's read-check-append AND atomic enqueue; `_ticket_text` is the canonical hash normalizer to reuse; Windows detach requires an `os.name` guard (API-derisked, not live-tested).

## Config placement (consistent across ALL children)
The single gate ENABLE flag `overlap_enabled` (bool) lives on `VerifyConfig` (`_config_schema.py` `[tool.rebar][verify]`, with its `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer). ALL other tunables (proposition bounds, BM25F weights, K, max_doc_freq, conf_threshold, surface_cap, soak, lease, drain mode/batch) are LLM-feature tunables and live on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`) — `_config_schema.py` reserves `llm.*` for that layer, so tunables must NOT go on `VerifyConfig`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detects semantic overlap/duplication between separate tickets store-wide (cross-epic AND non-epic), beyond deterministic file-impact and manual links (delivered across S1–S7).
- [ ] Surfaces ≤3 candidate duplicate/supersede/dependency relations for human confirmation with copy-paste `rebar link` commands; does not auto-mutate links (S6, S7).
- [ ] Runs as a store-wide step during the plan-review window; advisory-only; does NOT run as a `5fd2` per-ticket criterion and does NOT affect the claim-gate verdict (S7).
- [ ] The architecture is captured in an ADR under docs/adr/ (owned by S7).
- [ ] For the ticket under review, overlap is detected against every non-graph-excluded ticket in the store (cross-epic AND non-epic), beyond deterministic file-impact and manual links — measured by the S6 labeled precision/recall fixture.
- [ ] Candidate `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`depends_on` relations are surfaced for HUMAN confirmation (each with a ready-to-run `rebar link` command); the tool NEVER auto-mutates links. Rationale for suggestion-only: link semantics require human judgment of intent, and a false auto-link corrupts the dependency graph that `ready`/`next_batch`/the completion gate depend on — a false suggestion costs one ignored line, a false auto-link costs silent graph corruption.
- [ ] Low false-flagging of legitimately-related-but-distinct work: precision is measured on a labeled fixture of ticket pairs (S6), and a related-but-distinct pair must not be surfaced. (This is the experiment-identified residual risk; S6 is its owner.)
- [ ] It is a store-wide step run during the plan-review window, advisory-only, never blocking or altering the claim-gate verdict.
- [ ] An ADR (docs/adr/) captures the architecture (Cupid-digest-without-embeddings, event-store-as-enrichment-queue, digest-as-REVIEW_RESULT-style-sidecar, overlap-at-review-time-not-as-a-5fd2-criterion) — DELIVERED in child S7 (precious-spy-hellbender).
baseline.summary: Cross-ticket overlap & dependency detection (store-wide: cross-epic + non-epic) — outside the plan-review gate

baseline.description:
Build the one-time strip as a committed operational script, and prove it on a scratch clone before any window. **No new dependency**: `git-filter-repo` is deliberately not used. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why stock plumbing
`git fast-export --no-data --signed-tags=strip --export-marks=old.marks tickets` | filter | `git fast-import --export-marks=new.marks`. Verified on the real branch: the stream carries `M 100644 <sha> <path>` with **zero** inline blob data (26 MB stream for ~49,900 commits), so the filter is line-oriented text processing that never moves the ~1 GiB. No `deleteall`; no tags in a branch export (so `--signed-tags=strip` is a harmless no-op); merges ride `merge :n`; **empty commits are kept**, so DAG topology and every file's introduction point survive — which is exactly what ancestry-based authorship verification needs. filter-repo would prune them and reshape the graph.

**Proven result:** 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%), all commits and all merge commits preserved, HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths, ~30 s end to end.

## Required corrections (each was a real defect found in review)
1. Must run in a fresh **UNFILTERED** clone — `fast-import` hard-fails `fatal: blob not found` in a
   `blob:none` partial clone, and this host's `origin` is one.
2. Strip **both** `.bridge_state/` **and** `.bridge_state.bak-retarget/` prefixes — B6 removes the
   latter at HEAD only; its 33 MB stays in history.
3. **Derive the re-add set DYNAMICALLY** — `git ls-tree -r --name-only <old-tip> -- .bridge_state/` —
   never a hardcoded list. It is three files today but **A2-1 adds `get_rotation.json`**, so at window
   time it is four; a hardcoded list would fail the tree-identity assertion.
4. The filter must be **`data <n>`-length-aware**, not `grep -v`: commit messages live inside `data`
   blocks. (Today 0 of ~49,900 messages begin with `M `/`D `, but the script must not rely on that.)
5. Push with **`--force-with-lease`**, never `--force` — the remote tip moves constantly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a scratch unfiltered clone, the script produces a rewritten branch whose **commit count and
      merge-commit count are unchanged** (measured at run time, not hardcoded). Tier: **repo-level
      assertion in the dry-run harness**.
- [ ] `rev-parse <new-tip>^{tree}` **equals** the old tip tree after the dynamic re-add. Tier:
      **repo-level assertion**. This is the "not one byte of live content changed" invariant.
- [ ] The re-add set is discovered from `ls-tree`, proven by a fixture where a 4th `.bridge_state`
      file exists. Tier: **integration** with a synthetic 4-file store.
- [ ] Pack size drops to <=15% of the original. Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] The filter preserves a commit message that begins with `M ` (adversarial fixture). Tier:
      **unit** on the stream filter.
- [ ] The script refuses to run in a partial clone, with a clear message. Tier: **integration**
      against a `--filter=blob:none` clone.
- [ ] All assertions run **before** any push; the script has no push step of its own.

## Files
`infra/scripts/reclaim-bridge-history.sh` (or `.py`), dry-run harness, tests

Scope: M. No code dependencies; must exist before A6-1.
baseline.summary: A6-0c: build and dry-run the history-strip script using stock git plumbing

# Single-source the ticket-type map and extend the one-literal guard to cover it

## Context

This is the SAME defect class as the just-closed bug fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61, still live in a third map — and the guard that was supposed to prevent recurrence does not cover it.

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` enforces "exactly one dict literal defines each value map within `adapters/`" for the STATUS map (`test_exactly_one_status_map_literal_within_adapters`, the assert at `:300`) and the PRIORITY map (`test_exactly_one_priority_map_literal_within_adapters`, the assert at `:308`). There is no such assertion for the TICKET-TYPE map, and it is duplicated:

* `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:88` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE: dict[str, str] = {...}`, read at
  `:129` for the Cloud create path.
* `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:43` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE = {"task": "Task", "story": ...}`,
  read at `:61` for the DC create path.

Both were verified present in the tree. `config.py:11` also references a `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` in a comment, which is worth checking for a third copy while doing this.

### Every consumer of the symbol, enumerated

A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites, and the plan accounts for all of them:

1. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:88` — definition (Cloud). Moves.
2. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:129` — Cloud create-path read. Unchanged if the alias is kept.
3. `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:43` — definition (DC). Moves.
4. `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:61` — DC create-path read. Unchanged if the alias is kept.
5. `rebar_reconciler/config.py:11` — a COMMENT only, no literal. Confirms there is no third copy in
   config; the finding is recorded here so the check need not be repeated.
6. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py:8` — a
   docstring mention. No code impact.
7. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py:87` —
   **a live external consumer**: `assert "session_log" not in _of._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`, where `_of`
   is the `outbound_fields` module. This reads the name as a MODULE-LEVEL ATTRIBUTE on
   `outbound_fields`. If the relocation leaves the canonical map bound only under a new name (e.g.
   `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`) or referenced inline, this test breaks with `AttributeError`.

**Required binding strategy (this is not optional):** in `outbound_fields.py`, import the canonical map under the historical private name, exactly as J2 did for the other two maps at `outbound_fields.py:35-36`:

```python
from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA as _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE
```

That keeps `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` resolvable, so site 7 and the create-path read at site 2 need no edit. The DC backend gets the same treatment for its own call site. If the implementer instead chooses to rename, then site 7 MUST be updated in the same change and the suite re-run to prove it — the choice is free, leaving site 7 broken is not.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The two copies are read by the two CREATE paths. A divergence means the same local ticket type becomes a different Jira issue type depending on deployment — silently, at creation, with no comparison anywhere that would notice. fe15's status map had already drifted by one key (`"deleted"`) before anyone looked; there is no reason to assume this one is luckier, and nothing would tell us.

## Approach

Follow the **J2** pattern (story 62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743), which is the established local idiom for a map that lives on BOTH sides of the `adapters/` boundary and was reviewed when it landed: relocate the single definition into `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` alongside `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` and `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`, have both create paths import it under an alias, then extend the boundary guard so a future third copy fails the build.

Note explicitly that fe15 is NOT the precedent to copy for the mechanism, only for the defect class. fe15 deliberately used a **parity test rather than a shared import**, because its third copy lived in `rebar_reconciler/config.py` — a zero-dependency core module that must not import a vendor adapter package. That constraint does not apply here: both copies of the TYPE map already live under `adapters/`, so the shared import J2 used is available and is the right move.

**Compare the two copies BEFORE unifying them.** If they have already drifted, the unification is a BEHAVIOUR change for one deployment and needs the divergence decided explicitly and recorded — the way J2 decided `"deleted" -> "Done"` — not silently resolved by whichever copy is moved.

## Scope

- `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` — the single definition (and its export from the package
  `__init__`, matching how the status/priority maps are exposed).
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — delete the literal, import under the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`
  alias.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — delete the literal, import under the same alias.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` — extend the one-literal guard
  to the type map.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` — touched ONLY
  if the alias strategy above is not followed; unchanged if it is.
- the characterization pins for the type mapping on both create paths (see Testing) — **this ticket
  owns them unconditionally**.

## Testing

* the guard must FAIL when a second literal is reintroduced. "Mutation-checked" here means a
  concrete manual mutation, not a mutation-testing tool: re-add a literal
  `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE = {"task": "Task", "story": "Story", "bug": "Bug", "epic": "Epic"}` to
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`, run the boundary-guard module, record that the new test is
  RED (and note the pass/fail counts), revert the mutation, record that it is GREEN again.
* both create paths keep producing their current issue-type values, pinned BY VALUE — an assertion
  on the built `"issuetype"` field for each of `task`/`story`/`bug`/`epic` through the Cloud create
  path and through the DC create path, not an assertion on the map's shape.
* `test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` still passes unmodified (the alias check).
* the full `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` suite is green after the relocation.

Ownership note: sibling story cedc (DC backend characterization suite) also touches DC create-path characterization. To remove the ambiguity, the type-mapping pins are **owned here**; cedc depends on this ticket and should reuse these pins rather than re-author them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the two existing copies are DIFFED and the result is recorded in a comment on this ticket
- [ ] if the two copies diverge, the chosen value is decided explicitly with its rationale recorded,
      not defaulted to whichever copy was moved
- [ ] exactly one `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`-equivalent literal exists under `adapters/`, and it lives in
      `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`
- [ ] both create paths (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`)
      read that single definition, imported under the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` alias
- [ ] `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` still resolves as a module attribute, proven by
      `test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` passing UNMODIFIED — or, if the implementer
      renamed instead, that test is updated in the same change and passes
- [ ] the boundary guard covers the ticket-type map
- [ ] that guard is MUTATION-CHECKED by the concrete procedure in Testing, with the RED and GREEN
      verdicts recorded in a comment
- [ ] the type mapping is pinned by value for the Cloud create path, for all four local types
- [ ] the type mapping is pinned by value for the DC create path, for all four local types
- [ ] the `config.py:11` comment reference is checked for a backing third copy, and the finding is
      recorded either way
baseline.summary: Single-source the ticket-type map; guard it like the others
