baseline.description:
## Summary

The CLI read handlers `_cmd_list` and `_cmd_session_logs` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py`) gate initialization on a bare `os.path.isdir(tracker)` and call `_engine_support/reads.py` state functions (`list_states` / `recent_session_logs_state` → `reduce_all_tickets`) **directly**, bypassing the hardened read chokepoint `_reads._tracker` that `rapt-dreadable-dromedary` (`aefe-614a-2631-4117`) switched to `store_is_usable`. A tracker directory that satisfies `isdir` but is **not a usable store per the shipped `store_is_usable` predicate** — i.e. it is one of: (a) has neither a `.git`-with-resolvable-HEAD nor rebar store structure on disk (a marker-files-only directory), or (b) has `.git` with an **unresolvable** HEAD (mid-clone) and no store structure — passes the bare `isdir` check, so these paths print `[]` at exit 0 instead of rejecting it. (A `.git`-**less** but *structured* materialized snapshot — carrying `.store-compat.json` or a ticket event dir — remains a **usable** store and must keep reading; the defect is specifically the unusable shapes above.) This is the exact fallback-masking rapt-d removed from the library, surviving on the CLI surface.

## Root cause & attribution (see RCA comment)

Unmet-obligation / missed-consumer-update: rapt-d hardened the library/MCP read chokepoint + write gate and created the "reads reject a present-but-unusable store via `store_is_usable`" obligation; the CLI consumers were never updated. `caused_by = aefe-614a-2631-4117`, close-class `regression` (parity/consistency regression introduced by rapt-d's asymmetric hardening). Date test: the isdir lines predate rapt-d (2026-06-24 vs 2026-08-29), so they are the correct-at-the-time consumer, not the origin.

## Fix (faithful parity — reuse the authority predicate, invent nothing)

Replace the bare `os.path.isdir(tracker)` reject gate at `reads_cli.py:340` (`_cmd_list`) and `:384` (`_cmd_session_logs`) with `rebar._store.store_usability.store_is_usable(tracker)` — the same stdlib-only predicate the parent fix made the read/write source of truth. This is a zero-contract-change extension: an ABSENT store still rejects (rc 1, unchanged), a valid EMPTY store still returns `[]` rc 0 (unchanged), a `.git`-less **structured** snapshot still reads (unchanged), and only the unusable cases above (marker-files-only, or mid-clone with unresolvable HEAD and no structure) flip from `[]` rc 0 → rc 1 "not initialized", matching the library.

## Parity census (Step 7, Axis 2) — full channel disposition

- **`_cmd_list` (`reads_cli.py:340`)** — FIX (observable rc 0→1 for the unusable shapes).
- **`_cmd_session_logs` (`reads_cli.py:384`)** — FIX (observable rc 0→1).
- **`src/rebar/_engine_support/descendants.py:25`** — N/A: deliberately tolerant read (`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_error_envelope.py:17`), consumed by `close_precheck` + `llm/overlap`; swap provably unobservable; rejecting would alter intended tolerant behavior.
- **`src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py:154`** — N/A: not a readiness gate (guards `os.scandir` for tombstones, reached only after epic resolution); broken store already fails closed rc 1 (`EpicNotFound`, runtime-proven).
- **`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:619`** — N/A: SHA-pinning helper with its own stronger `git -C tracker rev-parse --git-dir` probe after the isdir.
- **`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:251`** — N/A: best-effort background-sync guard, not a readiness/init gate.
- **MCP / library channel** — OK: funnels through `_reads._tracker` → `store_is_usable` (rapt-d).
- **CLI `search`/`ready`** — separate finding (no gate at all; also masks absent), filed as `97e9-e663-a94e-4038` (`discovered_from`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `_cmd_list` (`reads_cli.py:340`) gates on `store_is_usable`: a present-but-unusable store
      (marker-files-only: `isdir` true but no `.git`-with-HEAD and no store structure) reports
      rc 1 "not initialized", not `[]` rc 0. (SHIPPED: reads_cli.py:340 now `store_is_usable`;
      test_cli_read_rejects_present_but_unusable_store_without_git[list] GREEN; e2e `rebar list`
      on broken store → rc 1.)
- [x] `_cmd_session_logs` (`reads_cli.py:384`) gates on `store_is_usable`: same for a
      present-but-unusable (marker-files-only) store. (SHIPPED: reads_cli.py:384 now
      `store_is_usable`; test[session-logs] GREEN; e2e `rebar session-logs` → rc 1.)
- [x] Both reject a mid-clone store (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable, no store structure) with
      rc 1. (test_cli_read_rejects_midclone_store_unresolvable_head[list, session-logs] GREEN.)
- [x] An existing, empty, INITIALIZED store still returns `[]` rc 0 for both (contract preserved,
      anchored so a vacuous empty cannot pass) — and an ABSENT store still rc 1 (unchanged).
      (test_cli_read_still_returns_empty_for_initialized_empty_store +
      test_cli_read_still_rejects_absent_store GREEN; e2e valid store → `[]` rc 0.)
- [x] Regression per site: reverting either gate to bare `os.path.isdir` returns the
      unusable/mid-clone case to RED (defect-seeded mutation guard). (Sandbox-exec mutation:
      seeded bare-isdir → 4 behavioral tests RED; restored → GREEN.)
- [x] Structural class guard: a test asserts no CLI reject-gate in `reads_cli.py` uses bare
      `os.path.isdir(tracker)` for the readiness decision (fails if a new instance appears).
      (test_cli_read_arms_do_not_gate_on_bare_isdir GREEN.)

## Landing

Gerrit change 2412 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2412), merged as origin/main `91cf9b46ec74`. LLM-Review +1 (PASS), Verified +1 (CI success), 0 unresolved. Plan-review certified.
baseline.summary: CLI/read-support init gates still use bare isdir(tracker) — parity with rapt-dreadable-dromedary

baseline.description:
A cancelled or timed-out job in the Gerrit Verified Gate casts `Verified -1` with a message that is exactly `CANCELLED: <run URL>`. It names no job and gives no reason, so triage means opening the run and reading job conclusions by hand.

OBSERVABILITY ONLY: when the gate votes +1/-1 must not change, only what the -1 carries.

## Why the message is empty

`gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `vote` job casts with `lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action`, which self-builds `MESSAGE="${STATUS}: ${SERVER_URL}/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}"` and has no input for custom text (checked at pin a1c036a5 = v1.1.2 and on the action's current main; v1.1.2 is its latest tag). Its `comment-only: true` input does NOT help — it only suppresses labels and still posts that same self-built text. It is a label switch, not a message switch, so the detail cannot be delivered through that action at all.

Two real causes produced the identical `CANCELLED: <url>`: the `bounded mutation gate` hitting `timeout-minutes: 30`, and `select mutation shards` failing with `invalid choice: 'select'` on a stale base. Only the second needs author action (a rebase), and the vote cannot tell them apart.

## Approach

1. `scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py` (new, trusted): pure `summarize()` maps a list-jobs
   payload plus check-run annotations to one line per non-successful job — job name, TIMED OUT
   vs cancelled vs failed, duration, `html_url`. Returns "" when all jobs succeeded.

2. A `Summarize the jobs that did not succeed` step in `vote`, guarded on the normalized
   vote-type not being `success`, gathering both inputs with `GITHUB_TOKEN`:
   - jobs: `gh api --paginate repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/jobs`,
     collected via `jq -s -c '{jobs: .}'`, passed as `JOBS_JSON`;
   - annotations: for each failure/cancelled/timed_out job,
     `gh api repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` (a job id IS its
     check-run id), assembled into a `{"<job id>": [...]}` map passed as `ANNOTATIONS_JSON`;
     best-effort, a failed read degrades wording but must not fail the step.
   This is why the workflow needs `checks: read`: GitHub reports a timed-out job as
   `conclusion: cancelled` and says "exceeded the maximum execution time" ONLY in the
   annotation, so without it a timeout is indistinguishable from a supersede.

3. A `Post the triage detail to Gerrit` step posting via a dedicated SSH
   `gerrit review <change>,<patchset> --message '<text>'` — the call the action makes
   internally — with NO `--label`, so it comments rather than votes. A raw `ssh` must
   reproduce what the action does internally: port `29418` (the default 22 is closed on the
   Gerrit host); `secrets.GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY` written with `chmod 600` and
   `vars.GERRIT_KNOWN_HOSTS` written to `~/.ssh/known_hosts` with
   `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, as `vars.GERRIT_SSH_USER`@`vars.GERRIT_SERVER`; change and
   patchset rejected unless they match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, mirroring the action's own guard; the
   key removed in an `if: always()` step. REST is unavailable — per ADR-0023 the CI account is
   SSH-key-only with no HTTP password.

Both new steps run AFTER the cast and are `continue-on-error`, so the vote is already on the change before they execute and a fault cannot redden a passing run.

The script is sparse-checked-out from the default branch like `scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.py`, so patchset code never runs in the vote job. Because the summary is interpolated into a single-quoted remote argument and matrix job names derive from `.github/mutation-shards.toml` (patchset-controlled), `summarize()` strips `'`, `\` and all control characters except newline.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (summarize + SSH comment + key-cleanup steps;
  sparse-checkout list; `checks: read`)
- `scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py` (new)
- `tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py` (new)
- `tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion_port_heldout.py` (sparse-checkout assertion
  becomes structural now that the step fetches two scripts)

Does NOT touch `_mutation.yml` or `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — change 1627 owns those.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: a job whose annotation says it exceeded its maximum execution time renders as timed
      out, naming the job and its duration; unit test asserts the text.
- [x] AC2: timed out, cancelled-without-annotation, and failed render with different wording;
      unit tests cover all three.
- [x] AC3: an all-successful payload returns "", so a `+1` run posts no comment; unit test.
- [x] AC4: the summary is posted by an SSH `gerrit review --message` step passing no `--label`
      (casting neither Verified nor Code-Review), guarded on vote-type != `success`; a test
      parses the workflow and fails if `--label`, `Verified=` or `Code-Review=` appears there.
- [x] AC5: the cast step's `vote-type` still reads `steps.normalize.outputs.vote-type`, and
      `normalize` is unchanged; asserted by a test.
- [x] AC6: `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` still passes — `vote.needs` unchanged.
- [x] AC7: both new steps are `continue-on-error` and ordered after the cast; asserted by
      tests, so a fault in the comment path leaves the vote already cast.
- [x] AC8: a job name containing a single quote cannot escape the remote command's quoting;
      unit test feeds a hostile shard name through `summarize()`.
- [x] AC9: the SSH step uses port 29418, installs the key with `chmod 600` plus `known_hosts`,
      validates change/patchset against `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, and removes the key in an
      `if: always()` step; asserted by tests parsing the workflow.
- [x] AC10: the summarize step fetches this run's jobs from `actions/runs/<id>/jobs` and
      per-job annotations from `check-runs/<id>/annotations`, passing them as `JOBS_JSON` /
      `ANNOTATIONS_JSON`; asserted by tests parsing the workflow.

## Verification

    python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py -q
    python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py -q
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py
    make lint && make typecheck
baseline.summary: Verified -1 from a cancelled or timed-out job carries no triage signal

baseline.description:
## Problem
`rebar explain plan` / `explain review` (and `explain <criterion-id>`) read their guide markdown from `config.repo_root(...)/docs/...`. `repo_root` resolves to the *consuming project's* git toplevel (or cwd), never the rebar install. So when rebar is installed as a library/CLI/MCP and run against another project, the `docs/` tree is absent and every `explain` guide lookup fails with missing-file. A client hit exactly this ("the author guide lives in the rebar source repo, not this project").

## Goal
Make the plan-authoring guide (writing-a-passing-plan.md) and code-authoring guide (passing-code-review.md) accessible through rebar's CLI, MCP, and Python library surfaces from any installation, matching the established OSS convention for runtime-needed data files: the canonical copy lives *inside* the import package, read via `importlib.resources` (the same pattern rebar already uses for `criteria_routing.json`).

## Approach
1. Move the two prose guides to `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and
   `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` (canonical, in-package) and add
   `src/rebar/_guides/__init__.py`. Hatchling ships all files under `src/rebar`, so they land
   in the wheel automatically.
2. Change `AUTHOR_GUIDES` from `dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]` (path components under `docs/`) to
   `dict[str, str]` mapping guide name -> bare filename, e.g.
   `{"plan": "writing-a-passing-plan.md", "review": "passing-code-review.md"}`.
   `explain_guide(name)` resolves via `resources.files("rebar._guides") / AUTHOR_GUIDES[name]`
   and drops the `repo_root_path` parameter (resolution is repo-root independent). Unknown name
   still raises `ExplainError("unknown-id", ...)`; a genuinely absent packaged resource raises
   `ExplainError("missing-file", ...)`.
3. `explain_criterion(id)` renders the section directly from the packaged registry via the
   existing `_guide_section_body(criterion)` (the same content `regenerate_criteria_guide`
   builds the doc from) instead of reading `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`. Overlay
   project criteria still resolve via `load_criteria(repo_root=repo_root_path)`; unknown-id and
   malformed-registry states are preserved; the repo-root missing-file state is removed.
4. Leave `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `docs/passing-code-review.md` as thin pointer
   files to the in-package canonical source so existing links (docs/README.md, AGENTS.md)
   resolve.
5. Keep the dev/CI machinery unchanged: `regenerate_criteria_guide`, `validate_criteria_guide`,
   `_guide_path`, and the Pass-4 coach deep-links to the docs anchor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `REBAR_ROOT` set to a directory containing no `docs/`, `rebar explain plan`,
      `rebar explain review`, and `rebar explain <criterion-id>` (e.g. F1) each exit 0 and print
      the guide/section (installability guarantee).
- [ ] The library calls `registry.explain_guide("plan"|"review")` and
      `registry.explain_criterion("F1", repo_root_path=<dir-without-docs>)` return the content
      without raising (no dependency on repo-root `docs/`).
- [ ] The MCP `explain_criterion` tool returns `{criterion_id, section}` for a guide name and a
      criterion id under the same repo-root-independent condition.
- [ ] Both guides are present as packaged resources: `resources.files("rebar._guides")` contains
      `writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `passing-code-review.md`.
- [ ] `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `docs/passing-code-review.md` still exist as pointer
      files (existing links do not 404).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; `tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py` passes,
      updated to assert repo-root independence instead of the old "missing-file when the repo
      has no docs" behavior, plus a test that both guides are packaged.
baseline.summary: explain guides accessible from any install (package the author guides)

baseline.description:
# Where the unsigned events come from

The project intends to sign every event, but ~11.2k ACTIVE events carry no `author_sig`. Broken down by `env_id`, the cause is NOT diffuse — it is one environment.

## Evidence — signed rate per environment (active, non-SNAPSHOT events)

| env_id | signed | unsigned | signed% | last seen | top author |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| b2b5c498 | 0 | 8880 | 0.0% | 2026-08-09T16:16 | Unknown (8880) |
| ade0f2ef (this host) | 9617 | 2186 | 81.5% | 2026-08-09T18:22 | RebarBotNava |
| reconciler | 95 | 93 | 50.5% | 2026-08-07 | reconciler |
| 4d084713 | 243 | 0 | 100% | 2026-08-08 | RebarBotNava |
| rebar-bridge[bot] envs | 10 | 0 | 100% | — | rebar-bridge[bot] |

**env b2b5c498 is the problem**: 8880 events, ZERO signed, every one authored "Unknown", and still writing. Its envelopes carry `author: "Unknown"`, `author_id: null`, `author_email: ""`, `author_sig: null`, `creation_channel: null` — i.e. NO identity is configured in that environment at all, so both the authorship stamp and the signature are skipped, and the creation-channel provenance feature is also a no-op there.

It is GROWING: 2818 events in 2026-07, 6062 in 2026-08.

Event types it writes: CLAIM_ENRICH 1500, TICKET_DIGEST 1496, DONE_ENRICH 1496, REVIEW_RESULT 1187, CREATE 1185, LINK 1100, ENQUEUE_ENRICH 912, COMMENT 4. First seen 2026-07-10 20:58, right after the event-sourced enrichment queue landed (75d1a4672d, 2026-07-09) — so it looks like a headless drainer/automation environment. Note it also CREATEs tickets and writes REVIEW_RESULTs unsigned, so the gap is not limited to the enrichment queue.

## This host is NOT the problem
ade0f2ef's 2186 unsigned events are legacy: 772 from 2026-06, 1412 from 2026-07, and only **2** in 2026-08. Signing works here now. Store-wide the June rate was 0% signed (the feature did not exist), July 51%, August 48% — and the August figure is dragged down almost entirely by b2b5c498.

## Not to be confused with the b636 restore
The b636 remediation restored 5041 unsigned historical events, which moved fsck's raw tally. That was benign (they predate signing). THIS ticket is the separate, ongoing gap.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Identify the host/process behind env_id b2b5c498 (its events are the only lead:
      enrichment-queue drainer + CREATE/LINK/REVIEW_RESULT, first seen 2026-07-10).
- [x] That environment writes events with a resolved author identity AND an `author_sig`.
- [x] ~~`creation_channel` is stamped there too~~ — NOT DELIVERED, split to bug
      ed5c (hemophobic-vegetarian-mynah). Measured after this fix: 5 post-deploy
      CREATEs, creation_channel still None on all 5. Signing and channel-stamping
      are independent; fixing the identity did nothing for the channel.
- [x] ~~A guard makes an identity-less writer loud rather than silent~~ — NOT
      DELIVERED, split to bug ed5c. Still worth doing: the silence at three layers
      is exactly why this ran a month undetected.
      refuses, or fsck reports an env whose signed-rate is 0%, so this cannot recur unnoticed.
- [x] Disposition of the 8880 existing unsigned events: ACCEPTED AS-IS by operator
      decision. No backfill (signatures cannot be created retroactively). If
      enforcement is ever enabled, grandfather via identity.enforce_since.
      impossible — signatures cannot be forged retroactively; document them as an accepted
      pre-fix cohort scoped out of verify-authorship).
baseline.summary: One environment writes every event unsigned and identity-less (author=Unknown, 8880 events, ongoing)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`reconcile-check` still packages several distinct observables together: field-diff discrepancies, orphaned bindings, unbound counts, summary tallies, text formatting, exit behavior, and the persisted report. The legacy follow-on removals in `82bb` and `c195` both depend on first proving which of those observations belong to `bridge preview`, `bridge fsck`, or `bridge status`, whether any observable truly lacks a home among those three existing owners, how the runnable compatibility wrapper in `src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py` behaves while the legacy mode string still exists, and which named readers (for example `last_pass._read_reconcile_diagnostics`) still require the on-disk artifact during the compatibility window.

## Approach

1. Add RED-first characterization coverage that captures the current `reconcile-check` contract for healthy, discrepant, orphaned, and unbound cases, including the fact that a successful run exits 0 regardless of findings and only unexpected failures exit 1.
2. Build an observable-to-owner matrix that assigns each current `reconcile-check` observation to an existing canonical bridge owner:
   - `bridge preview`: field-diff discrepancies and their preview-oriented formatting
   - `bridge fsck`: orphaned bindings, orphaned Jira references, unbound local/Jira counts, and integrity-oriented formatting
   - `bridge status`: summary tallies, operational witnesses, and the persisted-report replacement metadata
   - exit behavior: no new aggregate exit is introduced; each canonical owner keeps its pre-existing native exit contract, and the migration documentation records that `reconcile-check` itself did not have a findings-driven exit signal to preserve
3. Implement the bridge-side routing needed to expose those preserved observables through the canonical owners. Introduce a new bridge diagnostic subcommand only if the observable-to-owner matrix proves that a named current observable cannot be expressed through preview, fsck, or status; if that happens, record the forcing observable and rationale in the ticket comment and migration doc.
4. Migrate persisted report construction away from `bridge_state/reconcile-check.json` by making status-owned metadata/result fields the canonical bridge-status replacement while retaining or dual-writing the on-disk artifact only for named compatibility consumers such as `last_pass._read_reconcile_diagnostics` during the window before `c195` contracts the surface.
5. Preserve `_bridge_runner` compatibility in this ticket: its `MODE_COMMANDS['reconcile-check']` entry and captured stdout remain intact unless the characterization matrix proves a bridge-owned replacement can preserve the observed contract without widening scope. Any actual mode-string or wrapper removal stays deferred to `c195`.

## Scope

- direct `reconcile-check` report construction and output shaping in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler`
- canonical `bridge preview` / `bridge fsck` / `bridge status` CLI result contracts in `src/rebar/_cli`
- `_bridge_runner` compatibility behavior while `reconcile-check` is still a runnable profile
- bridge diagnostics surfaced through library/MCP shims only where needed to preserve the canonical bridge result contract before `c195` removes compatibility entrypoints
- migration docs and characterization tests covering healthy, discrepant, orphaned, and unbound cases

## Testing

Write RED-first characterization tests for the current `reconcile-check` report fields, formatting, persisted output, `_bridge_runner` wrapper behavior, and exit-0-on-findings contract. After the migration, prove that preview, fsck, and status expose the preserved diagnostics at their assigned owners; that any retired field/output is absent with explicit migration evidence; that `_bridge_runner` still preserves its observed compatibility behavior until `c195`; and that each owner retains its native exit contract without inventing a new aggregate reconcile-check exit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every current `reconcile-check` observable is assigned to `bridge preview`, `bridge fsck`, or `bridge status`; if any observable is retired instead, the migration doc and ticket comment name the retired observable, rationale, replacement owner or explicit absence, and the characterization assertion that proves the retirement.
- [x] `bridge preview` exposes field-diff discrepancies and preview-specific formatting under its existing result contract.
- [x] `bridge fsck` exposes orphaned-binding, orphaned-Jira, unbound-count, and integrity-formatting diagnostics under its existing result contract.
- [x] `bridge status` exposes summary tallies, operational witnesses, and the persisted-report replacement metadata under stable names; status-owned metadata is the default replacement unless a named consumer proves an on-disk artifact is still required during the compatibility window.
- [x] The migration preserves the source fact that `reconcile-check` had no findings-driven exit signal: preview/fsck/status keep their existing native exits, and the migration doc plus characterization coverage record that there is no new aggregate exit parity contract to preserve.
- [x] `_bridge_runner` continues to invoke the legacy `reconcile-check` profile and preserves its observed compatibility output unless a bridge-owned replacement is proven equivalent within this ticket's scope.
- [x] A new bridge diagnostic subcommand is introduced only if the observable-to-owner matrix proves a named current observable has no home in preview/fsck/status, and the ticket comment records that forcing case.
- [x] Characterization and canonical bridge tests cover healthy, discrepant, orphaned, and unbound cases, including the compatibility wrapper behavior.
baseline.summary: Canonicalize reconcile-check diagnostics

baseline.description:
## Resolution discovered during plan review

No production change is warranted. A4-1 already solved the operational defect at the correct boundary and deliberately preserved the raw differ contract.

The raw `compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state)` API must treat its first argument as real local state. For `local_state = {"RB-8": {}}` and `jira_state = {"RB-8": {"summary": "remote"}}`, it emits a `field_drift` update. That behavior is a load-bearing positive control for callers that honor the API contract.

The sole production snapshot caller does not honor that contract: it passes `prev_snapshot` and `curr_snapshot`, both remote Jira state. A4-1, merged as Gerrit 1256 / `6cdd4b00d9ee` with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, filters differ-owned `field_drift` and `unbound_local` emissions immediately at that call site. The source and tests explicitly require the filter to remain there so a future migration to real local state can remove it without weakening the pure differ.

Changing `_compute_mutations_emit_both` as originally proposed would contradict that decision and break the raw-differ positive control. This ticket therefore verifies the already-landed behavior and records the no-change decision.

## Verification plan

- Run `test_key_set_prev_field_drift_never_survives_the_production_filter`; it proves the raw positive control emits and the production call-site result contains zero outbound updates.
- Run `test_a_genuinely_new_remote_key_still_plans_its_inbound_create` and `test_seed_mutations_survive_the_suppression`; they prove the filter does not swallow genuine work or invariant repairs.
- Run the converged `reconcile_once` and real-repository idempotency tests; they prove persisted `mutation_count == 0`.
- Execute an in-session counting probe around the real production path with a key-set previous snapshot. Prove the counter observes a representative `git rev-parse` call in its positive control, then assert zero per-mutation calls after the A4-1 filter.
- Record exact commands and outcomes on this ticket and the epic session log. No source, test, or documentation file is changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] The raw differ emits its documented field-drift positive control while the production snapshot call-site result contains zero outbound updates for the same key-set entry.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Genuine inbound-create and invariant-seed mutations survive the call-site filter.

# The completion gate cannot verify a large epic: step budget exhausts at 480 AND at 1600

> **Scope note.** The title states the reported end-state. THIS ticket delivers only the
> `search_files` file-path fix — the loop's fuel and an independent signed-gate false-FAIL vector.
> Full epic-verifiability is restored jointly with the four sibling tickets linked
> `discovered_from` this one (loop breaker, recovery reachability, diagnostic sidecar,
> `--force-close` remedy).

## The failure

Closing epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb] (59 descendants, all closed and certified) fails:

    Error: cannot close e369-a449-4773-48fb: completion verification could not run
    (completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed:
     agent exceeded its step budget (max_iterations=480; ~1 model request per tool call).
     Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or narrow the task.)

Retried with `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=1600` (3.3x the default). **Exhausted again**, after ~50 minutes, identical message, `max_iterations=1600`.

## MEASURED root cause (rebar-debug Phase 1 — see the RCA comment)

An instrumented reproduction (every agent tool call logged; 264 calls, 1074s, `max_iterations=480`) settled the question by measurement: **the verifier LOOPS; it does not converge at any budget.** Novelty by quartile: calls 1-132 are 94-98% novel, calls 199-264 are **0% novel**. From call #121 (t=537s) the agent is in a closed 4-call cycle repeated 31-37x against a single file.

The loop's engine is a tool defect: **`search_files` silently returns `"(no matches)"` when its `path` argument names a FILE rather than a directory** (and likewise for a path that does not exist). `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:109` walks `os.walk(base)`; `os.walk` on a file yields nothing, so control falls through to `return "\n".join(hits) or "(no matches)"` at `pai_tools.py:141`. There is no file/directory discrimination and no existence check.

Ground-truthed live in-run false negatives: `search_files("J1", ".../test_backend_characterization.py")` -> `(no matches)` while `J1` is on line 116 of that file (this is the loop); `allow_insecure` in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` -> `(no matches)` with **21 real hits**; `resolved_statuses` in the same file -> `(no matches)` with 5 real hits. Aggregate: **48% of `search_files` calls passed a file path, 100% of those returned `(no matches)`, and 26 of 29 had the literal genuinely present** — 29% of every tool call in the run was a guaranteed-false negative.

Beyond the wasted budget this is a **false-FAIL vector on a signed gate**: the packaged `completion-verifier` prompt tells the agent that `(no matches)` means "only that *that literal string* is absent", and encourages narrowing the search path — the exact move that returns a lie.

## Scope of THIS ticket

This ticket fixes **only** the `search_files` path-handling defect. It is the smallest change that removes the loop's fuel and closes the signed-gate false-FAIL vector. Four further defects were proven in the same investigation and are filed separately (linked `discovered_from` this ticket) because each changes gate control flow or operator messaging and deserves its own review:

* no loop breaker — `RunRequest.tool_step_limit` is never set for the primary verify step;
* the bounded completion recovery is unreachable for a step-budget `LLMRunnerError`;
* the repetition diagnostic is computed and then dropped (no `gate_error_v1` sidecar);
* the close gate offers `--force-close` as the remedy for a RESOURCE exhaustion.

`read_file`'s inverted-range fallback (`pai_tools.py:63`) is also deliberately **out of scope**: it was not part of the proven mechanism (the inverted read actually returned text containing the sought literal), and changing a second function's contract in this repo-wide shared module would materially widen the review surface. Filed separately.

## The fix

In `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`, `search_files` must resolve its `path` argument before walking:

* `path` names an existing **file** -> scan that single file and return its `file:line: text` hits,
  applying the `_SCAN_MAX_FILES` / `_SEARCH_MAX_HITS` caps. It must **not** apply the DISCOVERY
  filter: `skip_file` (`fs_tools.py:124-127`) hides gitignored files via `_git_tracked`
  (`fs_tools.py:95-113`), and applying it to an explicitly named path would answer `"(no matches)"`
  for a file that plainly contains the literal — this bug's lie in different clothes. `read_file`
  already settled the precedent (`fs_tools.py:42-43`): "an explicitly named file is always readable
  (only the security deny-list blocks it)";
* `path` names an existing **directory** -> **unchanged** `os.walk` behaviour (every existing caller
  depends on this; the contract must not move);
* `path` does not exist -> return an explicit `Error: ...` string, never `"(no matches)"`, so an
  agent can tell "I mistyped the path" from "the literal is absent".

`"(no matches)"` must from now on mean exactly one thing: the literal was searched for and is absent.

`search_files`'s **docstring must be updated in the same change**. Pydantic AI binds plain functions and reads their signature + docstring as the model-facing tool description (`pai_tools.py:46`), so the docstring IS the contract the agent is given. Today it says only "search across text files under `path`". Fixing the behaviour without the docstring would leave agents still believing a file path is not a valid `path`, which defeats the point of the fix — the looping verifier narrowed to a file path precisely because the packaged prompt told it to.

## Blast radius

`pai_tools.py` supplies the read-only tools to **every** LLM gate (plan-review, code-review, completion), so the change is repo-wide in effect even though the diff is one function. The directory-path branch is therefore held byte-identical in behaviour and is pinned by a regression test, and the change is additive: it converts two cases that currently return a false `"(no matches)"` into a true hit list and an explicit error respectively. No caller passes a file path today expecting `"(no matches)"` — that value is indistinguishable from the honest-absence answer, so nothing can be relying on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names an existing FILE that contains `query` returns
      the `file:line: text` hit(s), not `"(no matches)"`
- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names an existing FILE that does NOT contain `query`
      still returns `"(no matches)"` (honest absence is preserved)
- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` names a DIRECTORY is unchanged — same hits, same
      ordering, same caps (regression pin; every existing gate depends on it)
- [x] `search_files(query, path)` where `path` does not exist returns an explicit `Error: ...`,
      never `"(no matches)"`
- [x] a **gitignored** file named explicitly as `path`, which contains `query`, returns its hits —
      the discovery filter must not hide a file the caller named (pinned with a git fixture that
      asserts the filter is genuinely armed before trusting the result)
- [x] the repo-root confinement and deny-list of `_safe_path` still apply to a file path — a file
      outside the root or on the deny-list is refused exactly as a directory is
- [x] `search_files`'s docstring states that `path` may name a file (scanned as one file) or a
      directory (walked), and that an unsearchable path returns `Error: ...` — the docstring is the
      model-facing tool contract Pydantic AI passes to the agent (`pai_tools.py:46`)
- [x] the RED test is shown failing for the right reason before the fix exists, and passing after
- [x] the full CI selection (`pytest -m "not integration and not external"`) stays green

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_pai_tools_search_files_bf31.py -q
    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
baseline.summary: Completion gate cannot verify a 59-descendant epic: step budget exhausts at 480 and at 1600, leaving --force-close as the only exit

# Remediate validated findings from the behavioral/contractual test-coverage audit

An external test-coverage audit (static, pinned to commit `2d1524ad8`) identified a cluster of tests that assert against **source text / private structure / mere existence** rather than behavior ("change-detector" tests), plus several documented contracts with **no behavioral regression test**, and two documentation-vs-code drifts. We re-verified every finding against the actual codebase with five independent review passes: **all findings validated** (two downgraded to "partial — the mechanism is partly tested but the specific gap is real"), and the grep-against-source inventory surfaced **additional** anti-pattern tests beyond the report's list.

This epic converts the false-confidence regressions into real behavioral coverage, adds the missing data-safety/concurrency tests, hardens two thin production paths the audit exposed, and reconciles the stale docs.

## Context

- The audit's core thesis is correct: the largest residual risk is **not** broad
  lack of testing — core coverage (CRUD parity, deterministic replay, two-clone
  reconvergence, no-loss writer storms, claim contention, detector verdict
  semantics) is strong — but **false confidence** in narrowly-targeted regressions
  whose tests inspect source structure instead of exercising the promised behavior.
- Verification method: five parallel read-only audit passes over production source,
  existing tests, docs, and CI config. Findings that were already covered were
  dropped; only genuinely-missing/miswired coverage is ticketed here.
- Grep-against-source is **not** universally an anti-pattern here: 59 of 77
  source-inspecting tests are JUSTIFIED (the source text *is* the observable
  contract — exact git argv an adapter builds, layering/import invariants via
  `ast.parse`, prompt/YAML/Terraform/CI "config-as-artifact" drift guards,
  runtime-produced artifacts). This epic only touches the ~9 ANTI-PATTERN and the
  handful of BORDERLINE cases where a behavioral test is feasible and stronger.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories are closed (signed), each landing through the Gerrit gate
      (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1).
- [ ] No test in the changed set asserts only `hasattr(...)`, an exact private
      constant value, or a source substring where the underlying behavior is
      executable and was previously untested.
- [ ] Newly-added concurrency/race tests are deterministic (barrier/instrumented
      seams, not sleep-timing races that can pass on a slow runner).
- [ ] Every P0 finding (index.lock stale-reclaim TOCTOU; detached-HEAD local-ahead
- [ ] Each "change-detector" regression test named by the audit is either replaced
- [ ] The two documentation drifts (Jira link-sync inventory; dual-lock portability
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` stays green; no net loss of

## Context / Problem
`structured.parse_structured` and `structured.check_response` preserve deterministic repair, schema and sentinel extraction, and provider stop/refusal safety (`src/rebar/llm/structured.py:361-443,630-677`). `_pai_structured` currently wraps those rules in its own attempt loop (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:87-178`). RP-01 needs the policy expressed through Pydantic output processing before retry scheduling can move safely.

## Approach
Add a focused Pydantic output-policy adapter in new `src/rebar/llm/pai_output.py`. It expresses the two existing deterministic authorities through documented Pydantic AI seams (version 1.107.x), with NO new retry loop, provider selection, usage projection, or persistence:

1. **Deterministic parse + validation → a Pydantic `TextOutput` output function.** The adapter exposes a `TextOutputFunc` (wired by the caller as `output_type=TextOutput(fn)`) that runs the existing `structured.parse_structured(text, model_cls)` (deterministic tolerant-parse + sentinel/decoy selection + Pydantic validation) and returns the typed instance on success. On a retryable `StructuredOutputError` it raises Pydantic's `ModelRetry(str(err)) from err` so the ORIGINAL Rebar error object is preserved in the exception `__cause__` chain and Pydantic AI drives its own bounded output retry — the adapter itself schedules nothing.

2. **Stop/refusal safety → an `after_model_request` capability hook.** Because a Pydantic output function conventionally receives only the output VALUE (a `str`) — not the `ModelResponse` that `structured.check_response` needs (it reads `response.finish_reason` and `response.provider_details`, `structured.py:671-676`) — the guard is placed in a small capability implementing `pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_model_request(ctx, *, request_context, response)`, whose signature receives the full `ModelResponse` after every model request and returns it unchanged. The adapter builds this capability and the caller attaches it via `Agent(model, output_type=TextOutput(fn), capabilities=[cap])`. Inside the hook the adapter calls `structured.check_response(response)`: a refusal / `max_tokens` / `length` / `content_filter` turn raises the terminal Rebar `UnretryableOutputError`, and a transient `error` raises the retryable `StructuredOutputError`. Because `UnretryableOutputError` is NOT a `ModelRetry`, it propagates out and aborts the run after ONE model call — it never becomes a Pydantic retry prompt. This runs BEFORE the output function processes the text (the hook fires per model request), preserving today's "guard before parse" ordering (`structured_run.py:168-169`).

Keep `structured.py` as the pure parser and safety authority — `parse_structured` and `check_response` stay the public pure entry points the adapter calls; this story exposes no new pure entry beyond what already exists and preserves parser behavior byte-for-byte. This story does not change scheduling, fallback, usage, or serialized result shapes; those move in [rebar:kingsize-unfair-blackbird]. This narrow adapter lets the next story use documented Pydantic validation and the Pydantic-driven bounded retry without cloning repair policy.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/pai_output.py` — new: the `TextOutput` output function (parse+validate, raises `ModelRetry from StructuredOutputError`) and the `after_model_request` capability carrying the exact Rebar stop/refusal guard. No retry loop, provider selection, usage, or persistence.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` — retain `parse_structured` and `check_response` as the pure parser/guard authority the adapter calls; preserve parser behavior. Add no retry integration.
- `tests/unit/test_pai_output.py` — new real-Pydantic `FunctionModel` contract tests exercising a real `Agent` wired with the adapter's `TextOutput` function and `after_model_request` capability.
- `tests/unit/test_structured.py` — retain the historical deterministic repair and extraction oracle (unchanged).

## Testing
- Happy path: native and prompted valid responses produce the typed object through a real Pydantic Agent output path wired with the adapter (`FunctionModel` emitting valid JSON → `agent.run_sync(...).output` is the expected typed instance).
- Recovery path: repairable JSON, sentinel content, and decoy-plus-valid-object cases retain current deterministic selection (same values before/after the adapter, cross-checked against `tests/unit/test_structured.py`).
- Retry-cause path: a `FunctionModel` emitting invalid-then-valid output drives Pydantic's bounded output retry; assert the typed object returns AND that the intermediate failure surfaced the exact Rebar `StructuredOutputError` object in the `ModelRetry.__cause__` chain (identity assertion `is`).
- Failure path: refusal / content-filter responses (a `FunctionModel` returning a response whose `finish_reason`/`provider_details` signal refusal) cause the `after_model_request` guard to raise the existing terminal Rebar subtype (`UnretryableOutputError`) after ONE model call, emitting NO Pydantic retry prompt (assert model-call count == 1 and no `RetryPromptPart` in messages).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A real Pydantic `Agent` using the adapter (`output_type=TextOutput(fn)`, `capabilities=[cap]`) returns the expected typed object for valid native and prompted fixtures; verified by `tests/unit/test_pai_output.py` native and prompted cases.
- [x] The historical repair, sentinel, and decoy corpus produces the same values before and after the adapter; verified by the focused `test_pai_output.py` matrix plus `tests/unit/test_structured.py`.
- [x] A retryable validation failure preserves the exact Rebar `StructuredOutputError` object in the Pydantic cause chain (`ModelRetry.__cause__ is err`); verified by an identity assertion in `test_pai_output.py`.
- [x] Refusal and content-filter responses raise the existing terminal Rebar subtype (`UnretryableOutputError`) from the `after_model_request` guard without emitting a Pydantic retry prompt; verified by one-call, no-`RetryPromptPart` failure cases.
- [x] No retry loop, provider selection, usage projection, or persistence code is added to `pai_output.py`; verified by direct review and the module-size and complexity gates.
baseline.summary: RP-01 S1 — Adapt Rebar output policy to Pydantic validation

## Context / Problem
The extras-enforced default suite intermittently timed out in tests/unit/test_test_suite_store_isolation.py after the captured nested pytest child had already printed 100%. The child was launched by tests/_store_isolation.py with a 90-second timeout but without a private --basetemp, so pytest session shutdown joined the user-global numbered temp root and synchronously scanned or deleted unrelated retained trees. This could consume the entire child timeout after the selected test itself succeeded.

## Proven Mechanism and Repair
A controlled real-filesystem A/B poisoned the shared numbered root with 400,000 stale entries: the shared-root child took 10.800s while the private-basetemp child took 0.882s and left the poison untouched. SIGUSR1 at the post-100% boundary captured the main thread in pytest cleanup_numbered_dir through recursive rmtree. The repair gives the nested child a caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest basetemp without changing selection, environment, capture, timeout, or ambient-store assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The liveness owner is proven: a live stack capture names pytest session-finish numbered-root cleanup, and controlled shared/private basetemp A/B shows cleanup cost scales with retained entries.
- [x] The nested pytest child uses a caller-owned private basetemp and preserves the ambient tracker HEAD/directories plus a sentinel in another run's temp tree.
- [x] Held-out real-subprocess coverage was RED before the repair because the nested child deleted another run's sentinel, GREEN after the repair, and RED again under the exact omitted-basetemp mutation before restoration.
- [x] Repeated extras-enforced stress completed 25/25 real nested-pytest runs without timeout; the poisoned shared root remained unchanged.
- [x] The in-scope focused tests, lint, typecheck, and full local suite are green (13,584 passed, 17 skipped, 288 deselected); no production code, dependency, timeout, or assertion was weakened.

# Durable write path drops concurrent locked writes: background git auto-gc races the object DB

## Summary
Under heavy concurrent write load, the rebar durable write path (`event_append`) loses committed writes. Writers holding the exclusive index lock fail their `git commit` with `error: invalid object <sha> for '<...>.json' ... error: Error building trees` and the write is silently dropped. The regression test `tests/interfaces/store/test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py::test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` catches it (e.g. `intended=250 persisted_on_disk=233 lost=17`), and it is **currently red on `main` repo-wide** — it fails ~9 of the last ~12 `main` post-merge CI runs, including the CI run of the very commit that tried to fix it (`485873652`, post-merge run `29593239791`, `lost=17`). Because it fails Verified on unrelated changes, it is friction on every Gerrit landing (mitigated today only by probabilistic `recheck`).

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run the integration tier under parallel xdist load, e.g.
   `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py -q`
   repeatedly, or observe `main`'s post-merge `test` workflow across several pushes.
2. The test spawns `_WRITERS=5` writers × `_BURSTS=25` (`intended=250`) concurrent
   lock-serialized writes while the enrich-queue prune runs.
3. Intermittently (load-dependent), some writes raise the `invalid object / Error building
   trees` `CommandError` while holding the lock and are swallowed → `lost>0`.

**Expected:** every lock-acquiring write persists to disk; `swallowed_write_raises == 0` and `persisted_on_disk == intended_total`. **Actual:** under load a fraction of writes are lost (observed losses 17/26/94/146 across runs/workers — the varying count is itself a signature of a load-dependent race).

## Root Cause (diagnosed)
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (~L96–117) deliberately re-enabled **stock git background gc**
  on the tracker repo — `--unset gc.auto` + `gc.autoDetach=true` (commit `f63d72662`,
  "WU-1 — re-enable stock git gc (drop gc.auto=0 forcing)", 2026-06-18).
- Under this test's heavy parallel commit load the loose-object count crosses git's `gc.auto`
  threshold; git forks a **detached background `gc --auto`** that repacks/prunes loose objects
  **concurrently with the writers** — an object can vanish between `git add` and `git commit`.
- `485873652` added `_recover_from_invalid_object` (Mode D, `event_append.py:713`): on an
  `invalid object / error building trees` commit failure it runs `git read-tree HEAD`, re-adds
  the current write's path, and retries. This reduced the damage ~6–8× (146 → ~17) but does
  **not** cover the case where the missing object is **reachable from HEAD** (a committed
  object caught by the background repack): `read-tree HEAD` reinstates the broken reference, the
  retry commit fails identically, and the recovery is one-shot (no bounded loop / escalation).
  The failing logs show the **same object sha for the same path cascading across sequential
  bursts**, which is the HEAD-reachable signature.

## Fix Direction (candidate; needs maintainer judgment on the gc trade-off)
1. **Neutralize the trigger on the durable write path:** force `gc.auto=0` (or at minimum
   `gc.autoDetach=false`) on the tracker repo so a background repack cannot run concurrently
   with commits. This revisits the deliberate `f63d72662` decision — understand *why* WU-1
   re-enabled gc (loose-object growth? perf?) before reverting; a scoped
   "no auto-gc while the exclusive write lock is held" is preferable to a blanket revert.
2. **Harden the recovery to the HEAD-reachable case:** after `read-tree HEAD`, if the missing
   object is still referenced from HEAD, regenerate it from the intact worktree file
   (re-`git add` the committed path from disk) before retry; make `_recover_from_invalid_object`
   a **bounded loop** rather than one-shot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause confirmed: a targeted repro demonstrates a background `gc --auto` (or manual
      `git gc` under load) is what prunes the object referenced by the failing commit.
- [ ] The durable write path no longer loses writes under the test's load: 
      `test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` passes **50/50 consecutive
      runs locally** under xdist parallelism (currently flakes).
- [ ] `main` post-merge CI passes this test across **10 consecutive** pushes after the fix lands
      (was failing ~9/12).
- [ ] The chosen gc trade-off is documented (a code comment + the ticket) explaining the
      interaction between WU-1's gc re-enablement and the write path, so it is not silently
      re-reverted.
- [ ] No regression in the durable-write / enrich-drain unit + integration tiers
      (`make test` green).

## Notes / Provenance
Discovered while landing epic 6982's R6 change (`5dac`, Gerrit #760): #760 touches nothing in `src/rebar/_store/*` yet failed this test on CI, while sibling #761 (superset runtime tree) passed — i.e. a probabilistic store-layer race, not a defect in the plan-review changes. Full diagnosis captured here so a maintainer can pick it up; not in epic 6982's plan-review scope.
baseline.summary: Durable write path drops concurrent locked writes: background git auto-gc races object DB

# Config schema + layered-merge core + capability descriptor (provider-neutral)

## Context / Problem

The reconciler's rebar↔Jira mappings are hardcoded literals in `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`, `config.py`, and `inbound_fields.py` (all under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`). Before any axis can become config-driven, the seam needs a provider-neutral foundation: a config schema, a layered overlay/merge, fail-closed validation, and a capability descriptor declaring which axes a target has. This is the walking skeleton every other child depends on; it ships with **no axis wired yet** — S2–S5 move each axis onto it.

## Approach

Add a provider-neutral module (new file `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py`) that:

1. **Parses** the mapping block as a **reserved config section**, not as keys on the typed
   `JiraConfig` — the coercer would route them through `_warn_unknown`, which hard-errors
   under `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error`. Add a new reserved section name `mapping` to
   `_RESERVED_SECTIONS` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:633`, today `{"llm", "snapshot"}`) so
   `[tool.rebar.mapping]` is recognised (not coerced or warned), read raw via
   `rebar.config.read_reserved_section("mapping")` (`src/rebar/config.py:597`) — as the
   optional `llm.*` layer does. Shape:
   a `default` block and a `projects.<KEY>` table, each carrying axis sub-tables
   (`status_map`, `type_map`, `link_map`, `priority_map`, `create_defaults`) plus
   discovered-vocabulary declarations: three string lists (`statuses`, `issue_types`,
   `link_types`) plus a `hierarchy` **table** mapping level-name → integer level. Absent
   section ⇒ empty overlay (today's behavior). Cross-file precedence is whole-section,
   project-file-wins — rebar's reserved-section convention (`read_reserved_section`, as
   `llm`/`snapshot`); the deep merge below applies to the layers within that section.
2. **Resolves** an effective mapping per project key with two merge rules (load-bearing for
   validation): (a) the **five axis maps** **deep-merge per key** — built-in ← `default` ←
   `projects.<KEY>` — so an overlay entry overrides only the key it names and unnamed keys
   inherit; (b) the **vocabulary declarations** (the three lists + the `hierarchy` table)
   **replace wholesale, most-specific wins** (NOT unioned): a project's declared vocabulary
   is authoritative-complete, so `projects.<KEY>.statuses` fully supersedes
   `default.statuses`, and a layer with no declaration inherits the next-outer one (unioning
   would wrongly accept a default-only value).
3. **Validates** fail-closed at load against the **effective** (resolved) vocabulary from
   rule (b): every axis-map value must appear in its declared vocabulary set when one is
   declared (e.g. every `status_map` value ∈ effective `statuses`); a value referencing a
   capability-absent axis is rejected; a **malformed block** raises — a sub-table that is
   not a mapping, an axis-map value that is neither a string nor the `skip` sentinel (the
   reserved literal `"skip"`, a named constant in `mapping_config`, the sole non-vocabulary
   value an axis-map entry may hold), a vocabulary **list** that is not a list of strings,
   or a `hierarchy` that is not a string→integer mapping. The raised type is a new
   `MappingConfigError` subclassing `rebar._config_coercion.ConfigError`
   (`src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:20`), failing closed on the same load path as every
   other config error. Validation is **offline** — config only, never the network.
4. Defines a **`Capability` descriptor** dataclass declaring which mapping **axes** the
   target's vocabulary has (`has_types`, `has_transitions`, `has_hierarchy`,
   `has_link_types`, `has_priorities`) — data about the target's vocabulary, distinct from
   the backend role/behaviour Protocols in `_backend.py` (`@runtime_checkable`
   `SupportsLinks`/`SupportsComments`), which describe operations a backend implements. Each
   flag gates one axis: `has_types`→`type_map`, `has_link_types`→`link_map`,
   `has_priorities`→`priority_map`, `has_hierarchy`→the `hierarchy` table,
   `has_transitions`→transition replay (S6). `status_map` and `create_defaults` are ungated.

The module imports nothing from the Jira adapter (provider-neutral); the adapter injects its built-in defaults and capability values, respecting the vendor-adapter seam's one-way dependency direction (concrete backends import the neutral core, never the reverse) — `docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` (cite the filename; bare "ADR 0035" is ambiguous), amended by `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md`.

Relationship to the existing per-project surface: `.bridge_state/projects.json` (`projects_store.py`, ADR 0097) binds a store to a Jira project **identity**; `projects.<KEY>` here declares that key's **vocabulary/semantics** — orthogonal concerns joined on the same Jira key without duplicating identity data.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add `"mapping"` to `_RESERVED_SECTIONS`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py` (new) — schema dataclasses,
  `MappingConfigError`, `load_mapping_config`, `resolve_for_project`, `validate`,
  `Capability`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_mapping_config.py` (new).
- `docs/config.md` — document the `[tool.rebar.mapping]` section shape, three-layer merge,
  and its orthogonality to `.bridge_state/projects.json`.

## Testing

- **Reserved-section recognition (unit, real parser):** a `[tool.rebar.mapping]` section
  is neither warned as unknown nor coerced into `JiraConfig`, and is returned raw by
  `read_reserved_section` — even under `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error`.
- **Merge precedence (unit):** a `projects.REB.status_map` entry wins over
  `default.status_map` over an injected built-in default, an unnamed key inherits; a
  `projects.REB.statuses` list wholesale-replaces `default.statuses` (not unioned), and a
  layer with no declaration inherits the outer one.
- **Fail-closed validation (failure path):** a `status_map` value outside declared
  `statuses`, a malformed block, and an axis-absent reference each raise
  `MappingConfigError`, with the nearest valid config as the negative control (must NOT
  raise).
- **Neutrality:** `mapping_config` imports no `adapters.jira*` module and contains no Jira
  value literal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `[tool.rebar.mapping]` is registered as a reserved section and read raw via
  `read_reserved_section`, so its keys do not trip `_warn_unknown` even under
  `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error` — verified by
  `test_mapping_config.py::test_reserved_section_not_unknown`.
- [x] Axis maps deep-merge per key (built-in ← default ← project; unnamed key inherits) and
  vocabulary declarations replace wholesale (most-specific wins, not unioned) — verified by
  `::test_perkey_merge_precedence` and `::test_vocab_lists_replace_wholesale`.
- [x] A non-default overlay yields a different effective mapping than the built-in default
  through the real resolve path — verified by `::test_config_effect_contrast`.
- [x] `validate` fails closed offline with `MappingConfigError` on a value outside the
  effective vocabulary, a malformed block (non-mapping sub-table, non-string map value, or
  non-string-list vocabulary), and a capability-absent axis reference; the nearest valid
  config does not raise — verified by `::test_validate_fails_closed`.
- [x] The core is provider-neutral: `mapping_config` imports no `adapters.jira*` module,
  carrying no Jira value literal — verified by `::test_core_is_provider_neutral`.
- [x] `docs/config.md` documents the `[tool.rebar.mapping]` shape plus its three-layer
  merge, with a note on orthogonality to `.bridge_state/projects.json`.

Test tier: **in-process unit** — the mechanism is config parse/merge/validate over real functions (the real reserved-section parser plus the new pure resolve/validate); no external boundary is crossed, so no lower or higher tier applies.
baseline.summary: Config schema + layered-merge core + capability descriptor (provider-neutral)

## Context

Discovered while driving `3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd` (cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin), the 2026-09-02 root-disk outage. That ticket's Defect 2 was a dead-man's-switch inversion: `rebar-root-disk-pressure` watched a metric published BY THE HOST THAT WAS DYING, under `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`, so CloudWatch read the publisher's silence as health and the alarm went GREEN at the moment the host became unreachable. Nobody was paged for 5 hours.

That was fixed for exactly TWO alarms. `root_disk_pressure` (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) and `gerrit_data_disk_high` (monitoring.tf) are now `breaching` on main and live. **Eleven other alarms in the same `rebar/host` namespace were left at `notBreaching`.**

## The measured finding: none of the eleven is a sparse counter

The inline Terraform comments justify `notBreaching` with a belief about the publisher — e.g. 'No X errors published in a period is the healthy steady state'. **The publisher contradicts that comment.**

`infra/scripts/observability.sh` implements every host counter as an OFFSET-DELTA, not an event emit: it greps a cumulative journal, subtracts a persisted offset, and UNCONDITIONALLY publishes the delta (`--value "$new"`), which is `0` when nothing happened. `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` (~line 296) is the shared helper for six of them. The probe is a systemd timer at `OnUnitActiveSec=5min` (infra/scripts/install-observability.sh:31).

So a healthy period publishes `0` — it does NOT publish nothing. Missing data therefore means THE PUBLISHER IS DEAD, exactly as with the disk alarms.

Live CloudWatch confirms it. Sampling 2026-09-01 12:00-14:00Z at 5-min periods returned dense datapoints, all `0.0`, for every one of the eleven.

## The eleven, by blast radius

1. **mirror_out_of_sync** (monitoring_ws7.tf) — WORST, and defective beyond host-death. Its publish sits inside `if [ -n "$gerrit_sha" ] && [ -n "$github_sha" ]`; the else branch logs and publishes NOTHING. So a LIVE, healthy host whose Gerrit REST call or `git ls-remote` breaks silently stops the signal and the alarm reads OK forever while GitHub main drifts. The Terraform comment calls this fail-safe; it is fail-OPEN. monitoring_ws7.tf itself states no other alarm covers mirror drift.
2. **replication_errors** (monitoring_s5.tf) — same alive-host gap via a `[ -f "$REPL_LOG" ]` guard: a moved, renamed, or rotated-away replication log mutes the alarm permanently.
3. **review_interrupts_signal_unavailable** (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) — this is the 'deploys are running blind' signal. Its documented archetype (bug 34cd) is a live-locked review gate sitting behind green alarms; muting it silently reproduces that.
4. **deploy_errors** (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) — probe death means 'the box is not tracking main' goes unpaged.
5. **voter_errors** (monitoring_s4b.tf), **review_bot_merge_change_errors** (monitoring_88ab.tf), **g2p_dispatch_errors** (monitoring_1fa8.tf) — both merge-gate legs (LLM-Review and Verified) go dark together.
6. **mcp_retire_cap**, **mcp_mem_abort** (monitoring_foxterrier.tf), **review_interrupts_bound_exceeded** (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) — degradation rather than outage.
7. **bridge_run_failures** (monitoring_bridge.tf) — also a heartbeat, but the ONLY one whose tradeoff is explicitly named and compensated: monitoring_bridge.tf:40-45 states the stop-entirely case is owned by the Reconciler Heartbeat Canary. Treat separately.

For 3-6 the pure host-down case is partly backstopped by `GerritReachable` and the two fixed disk alarms. The residual uncovered case for ALL of them is **the probe dying while the host lives** — a rebar-observability.timer failure, IAM/credential revocation, or `aws` erroring — which mutes ten alarms at once with nothing else firing.

## Explicitly OUT of scope

`monitoring_eb6e.tf:109` (Bedrock client-error rate) is correctly `notBreaching`: its source is an AWS-published Bedrock metric, genuinely absent when idle, with FILL(m,0) and a divide-by-zero guard. Any rule must be scoped to `namespace = "rebar/host"` so it stays out.

## Tuning constraint — do NOT flip these blind

The risk is not false pages from sparseness (a healthy period publishes 0, so a breaching alarm stays OK). The risk is TIMER JITTER: a 2-hour sample showed ~22 of 24 periods present, so isolated missing periods are normal. Five alarms are `evaluation_periods = 1, datapoints_to_alarm = 1` (g2p_dispatch_errors, review_bot_merge_change_errors, replication_errors, and both review_interrupts_*) and WOULD FLAP on a single jittered tick. Flipping must be paired with `evaluation_periods >= 3`, matching how root_disk_pressure is configured (300s / 3 periods).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: every `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` in namespace `rebar/host` either sets `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` or carries an explicit opt-out marker stating why. Verified by the guard test in AC4 passing with no unexplained exceptions.
- [x] AC2 [REWRITTEN 2026-09-03 — the original form was defective]: the widened windows are proven not to flap by REPLAYING the recorded metric series against the new alarm configuration, showing zero state transitions across a window chosen for worst-case jitter. The original wording asked for a 24-hour observation period, which is waiting rather than verifying: it samples whichever day happens to elapse, proves nothing about a worse day, and cannot be re-run. Flap behaviour is DETERMINISTIC given a metric series and an alarm config, so it is answerable immediately and repeatably. Verified by replaying each flipped alarm's own recorded series (the pre-change 2-hour sample showed ~22 of 24 periods present, so isolated missing periods are the normal condition to replay against) and reporting the transition count per alarm.
- [ ] AC3: `mirror_out_of_sync` publishes a THRESHOLD-CROSSING value on its else branch (the branch taken when the Gerrit REST read or `git ls-remote` fails) instead of publishing nothing. Given the alarm's `threshold = 0` with `GreaterThanThreshold`, that value is `1`. Publishing `0` would NOT close the gap: it reads as in-sync and preserves exactly the fail-open this ticket is about. Flapping on a transient blip is suppressed by the alarm's existing `datapoints_to_alarm = 2` together with AC2's widened window — that blip risk is precisely what the current comment in `infra/scripts/observability.sh` ("On a fetch failure we publish NOTHING (the alarm treats missing data as healthy) rather than risk a false alarm from a blip") was written to avoid, so that comment must be rewritten in the same change to state the new disposition. Verified by inducing a fetch/REST failure and observing the alarm actually reach ALARM state, NOT merely by observing that some datapoint appeared.
- [ ] AC4: the rule is encoded as a test, not left to review vigilance — `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` already asserts the disk-alarm case and already has `_TREAT_MISSING_DATA_RE` plus an `# rebar:allow-actionless-alarm:` opt-out convention, so this is a small extension of an existing guard, not new machinery. Verified by the test failing on a deliberately reverted alarm.
- [ ] AC5 [non-codebase]: `bridge_run_failures` is explicitly decided — either left notBreaching with its existing documented compensating control, or flipped with an evaluation window >= 3 hours. Verified by a comment recording the decision.
- [ ] AC6 [non-codebase]: the false "missing data means healthy" rationale is corrected wherever it appears. It is NOT a single phrase and a one-phrase grep will not find it — it takes three distinct forms: (a) "no X published in a period is the healthy steady state", in monitoring_1fa8.tf:74, monitoring_s5.tf:50, monitoring_s4b.tf:78 and monitoring_88ab.tf:57 (with a cross-reference in monitoring.tf); (b) "the probe fails safe", in monitoring_ws7.tf:48-49; and (c) ABSENT ENTIRELY — monitoring_foxterrier.tf:68 and :104 carry a bare `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` with no justifying comment at all, so there is nothing to correct and a rationale must be ADDED. Verified by enumerating all eleven alarms individually and confirming each one either carries a corrected rationale or an explicit opt-out marker — not by grepping for one phrase.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py -q`
- `terraform plan` showing only the intended alarm changes
- post-apply: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` confirming the new settings, and a 24h flap check

## AC2 evidence — replayed, not waited for (2026-09-03)

Replayed 24 hours of each alarm's OWN recorded series against its LIVE configuration, modelling CloudWatch's evaluation exactly (period grid with gaps materialised, `treat_missing_data` applied to missing periods, `datapoints_to_alarm` of `evaluation_periods` for both the ALARM and OK transitions):

    alarm                                                  per/ep/dta  pts  miss  transitions
    rebar-autodeploy-errors                                  900/4/2    96     0       2
    rebar-autodeploy-mcp-mem-abort                           900/4/2    96     0       0
    rebar-autodeploy-mcp-retire-cap                          900/4/2    96     0       0
    rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-bound-exceeded        900/4/2    96     0       2
    rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-signal-unavailable    900/4/2    96     0       0
    rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high                              300/3/2   261    27       0
    rebar-gerrit-g2p-dispatch-errors                         300/3/2   261    27       0
    rebar-gerrit-mirror-out-of-sync                          300/3/2   261    27       2
    rebar-gerrit-replication-errors                          300/3/2   261    27       0
    rebar-gerrit-voter-errors                                300/5/3   261    27       0
    rebar-review-bot-merge-change-errors                     300/3/2   261    27       0
    rebar-root-disk-pressure                                 300/3/2   261    27       0

**The jitter is real and was absorbed.** Every 300s alarm saw **27 missing periods** out of ~288 — the ~22-of-24 pattern measured before the change, now confirmed over a full day. Under the OLD 1-of-1 configuration each of those 27 gaps would have been an immediate page once `treat_missing_data` became breaching. Under the widened 3-of-2 windows, eight of them produced **zero** transitions.

**The three alarms that DID transition are TRUE POSITIVES, not flaps.** Checked each against its raw series for nonzero readings:

    mirror_out_of_sync                 1.0 at 09-02 17:19, 09-02 19:34, 09-03 15:29
    review_interrupts_bound_exceeded   1.0 at 09-02 16:09, 09-02 16:54
    deploy_errors                      2.0-4.0 across 09-02 15:39-16:29 (the febd uv-pin build failures)

So every transition in 24 hours was driven by a genuine breaching VALUE. **Zero transitions anywhere were caused by missing data.** That is precisely what the widened windows were for.

## Why this replaces the original 24-hour-observation wording

The operator's point, and it is correct: an acceptance criterion that depends on time passing is defective. Waiting samples whichever day happens to elapse, proves nothing about a worse one, cannot be re-run, and — as this replay shows — would not even have distinguished a flap from a true positive without exactly this analysis anyway. The replay is deterministic, repeatable, took minutes, and covers a window deliberately chosen to include the worst churn on record (a 5-hour Gerrit outage, a 12-hour MCP outage, five failed deploys and three MCP cutovers).

Worth flagging separately: `mirror_out_of_sync` fired again at **09-03 15:29 today**, a genuine mirror divergence — the alarm is doing real work, not sitting decorative.
baseline.summary: Dead-man inversion survives in 11 host-published alarms: every rebar/host counter is a heartbeat that publishes 0, not a sparse event

## Why
Epic AC7 specifies the enforcement merge-gate as `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <identity.enforce_since>` that (a) exits non-zero when any enforced event is not `certified`, (b) emits one structured report entry `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author, verdict, display}` per non-certified event, (c) **grandfathers** pre-cutover events, and (d) runs as a CI merge-gate workflow. The delivered gate (3183 / change 580) meets the SPIRIT (`rebar verify-authorship`, opt-in via config, non-zero exit, replay-never-rejects, fsck/show grouping) but not the LETTER: wrong command name, no `--require-authenticated`/`--since` flags, text-only output (no JSON report), no `enforce_since` grandfathering, and no CI workflow file. The epic completion-verifier flagged AC7 unmet. This story builds AC7 in full. (Remediation of epic gnu-whale-ichor; user chose "build it".)

## What
Build the AC7 enforcement surface on top of the delivered merge-gate, in `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` (+ config + a report schema + a CI workflow):

- **`rebar verify-identity` command.** Make `verify-identity` the canonical command name
  (add it to the CLI intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`), keeping `verify-authorship`
  as a back-compat alias routing to the same `cli()`. Regenerate the CLI reference
  (`docs/cli-reference.md`) + INTERCEPT_COMMANDS/_LADDER so the drift gate stays green.
- **`--require-authenticated` flag.** Forces enforcement ON for the run regardless of
  `identity.require_authenticated` config (the CI job passes it explicitly). Without it,
  config governs (unchanged).
- **`--since <ref>` grandfathering.** Default from a new `identity.enforce_since` config
  key (env `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE`). An event is ENFORCED iff its introducing commit
  is `<ref>` or a descendant of `<ref>` (at/after cutover, via `git merge-base
  --is-ancestor <ref> <event_commit>`); an event whose commit does NOT descend `<ref>` is
  **grandfathered** — its verdict is still computed and reported, but it never fails the
  gate. With no `--since`/`enforce_since`, all events are enforced (current behavior).
- **`--format json` report.** Emit a JSON array of entries
  `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author, verdict, display}` — one per NON-`verified`
  in-scope event (with a `grandfathered: bool`), validated against a new
  `src/rebar/schemas/verify_identity_report.schema.json`. `display` is the grouping
  (`verified`/`unverified`/`unsigned`); `verdict` is the raw verdict. Default output stays
  the existing human text.
- **CI merge-gate workflow.** Add `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` (or a gated step)
  that runs `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <identity.enforce_since>`
  over the merged log and fails the build on a non-zero exit.
- Exit semantics: non-zero iff an ENFORCED (non-grandfathered) event is not `verified`
  (`certified`), under `--require-authenticated` (or config). Grandfathered/advisory → 0.

## Scope
In: the `verify-identity` command name + alias, `--require-authenticated`/`--since` flags, `enforce_since` config + env, the JSON report + its schema, grandfathering by commit ancestry, and the CI workflow. Out: the per-event classification itself (delivered + TS2/TS3, unchanged) and the schema verdict enum (AC10). Folds into the 3183 commit (change 580); the CI workflow + report schema are new files in that commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity --all` behaves as the merge-gate (same classification), and
  `rebar verify-authorship --all` still works as an alias (test both dispatch).
- [ ] `--require-authenticated` forces enforcement: with config off, `rebar verify-identity
  --require-authenticated --all` still exits non-zero on an unsigned/non-verified enforced
  event (test asserts exit code).
- [ ] `--since <ref>` grandfathers pre-cutover events: with an unsigned event introduced
  BEFORE the cutover ref and another AFTER, `--require-authenticated --since <ref>` fails
  ONLY for the post-cutover one; the pre-cutover event is reported `grandfathered` and does
  NOT fail the gate (test asserts exit code + that the pre-cutover event is grandfathered).
- [ ] `--format json` emits an array of `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author, verdict,
  display, grandfathered}` entries for the non-verified events, validating against
  `verify_identity_report.schema.json`; a test asserts an entry's field set + that `display`
  is the grouping value and `verdict` the raw verdict.
- [ ] A CI workflow file exists under `.github/workflows/` that invokes `rebar
  verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <…>` as a gating job (test/asserts the
  file exists and references the command).
- [ ] The CLI-reference drift gate passes (verify-identity documented; alias noted).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` (verify-identity name + --require-authenticated/--since flags + JSON report + grandfathering)
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (intercept verify-identity + alias verify-authorship)
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (identity.enforce_since + env REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE)
- `src/rebar/schemas/verify_identity_report.schema.json` (new report schema)
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` (new CI merge-gate workflow)
- `docs/cli-reference.md` (regenerated: verify-identity)
baseline.summary: identity: verify-identity enforcement CLI + --since grandfathering + JSON report + CI gate (epic AC7)
