## Bootstrap the shared Rebar Bot signing identity

No identity ticket or SSH authorship key exists yet. Create the one the AWS + GitHub bot environments will share, and provision its private key into both secret stores.

- Generate an ed25519 keypair for the bot (private key never committed to the repo).
- Create the identity: `rebar identity create --name "Rebar Bot" --email joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com --key "ssh-ed25519 …"` (the `identity` type is gate-exempt, so this bootstrap write is not blocked even under enforcement).
- Declare the SSM parameter in IaC: add `"/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key"` to the
  `rebar_secret_params` list in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf` (so Terraform owns the parameter's
  existence + SecureString type, matching every other `/rebar/prod/*` secret; the resource is
  created as a `CHANGEME` placeholder with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`, and the
  real value is populated out-of-band). This is the one code change in this task (→ Gerrit).
- Provision the PRIVATE key VALUE into both secret stores (operator has AWS + GH CLI access):
  - AWS SSM SecureString `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` (`aws ssm put-parameter --type SecureString`;
    bootstrapped now so the AWS bots can use it — Terraform adopts it on the next apply via the
    `ignore_changes = [value]` lifecycle, `terraform import` if a create-conflict arises, an operator/deploy step).
  - GitHub Actions secret `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` on `navapbc/rebar` (`gh secret set`).
  The per-env consumption wiring (fetch-secrets.sh materialization + container config in 245e; workflow env injection in 9e76/1787) references these already-provisioned secrets.
- Verify TOFU registration and that a `git config user.email = joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` resolves to this identity via the seam's resolver.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Rebar Bot identity ticket exists with its ed25519 PUBLIC key registered; `rebar list --type identity` (JSON) includes it with the key present.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Git-email resolution verified (runtime resolution, attested by recorded command output): with the store repo's `git config user.email = joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` and no overriding `.rebar/current_identity` pointer, `python3 -c "from rebar._commands.identity import resolve_current_identity; print(resolve_current_identity())"` returns the Rebar Bot identity ticket id (the resolver does a case-insensitive git-email match against identity tickets).
- [ ] `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` is added to `rebar_secret_params` in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf` so the parameter is IaC-tracked (not created purely out-of-band).
- [ ] [operator-attested] The PRIVATE key is provisioned (out-of-band infra state, attested by recorded aws/gh output) as an SSM SecureString `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` AND a GitHub Actions secret `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` (both verifiable: `aws ssm get-parameter --name /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key --with-decryption` succeeds; `gh secret list --repo navapbc/rebar` shows `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY`). Nothing secret is committed to the repo; the private-key file used for provisioning lives only outside the repo tree and is discarded after.
baseline.summary: Bootstrap the shared Rebar Bot signing identity (ed25519 + identity ticket)

# J7 — Assemble `JiraDataCenterBackend` and hold it to the backend contract suite

## Context / Problem

With the shared Jira-family layer, the two codecs, the two identity models, and the DC transport in place, the DC backend itself is an assembly — but it must actually be *proven*. ADR 0035's "Proof-of-seam" makes the backend-agnostic contract suite the artifact that certifies a backend, and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` parametrizes its `backend` fixture over `["fake", "jira"]`. PR #120 added registry and transport tests but never touched that fixture, so its new backend was never held to the port contract at all.

## Approach

Add `JiraDataCenterBackend` composing the shared layer [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `WikiTextCodec` [rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66], `NameIdentity` [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], and the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56]. It advertises `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and deliberately **not** `SupportsIncremental` — DC gets a full inbound scan in v1, since incremental fetch is an optimization with its own correctness surface and no client need yet.

Register the factory under `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` via `_backend_registry.register`, imported as a side-effect of `adapters/__init__.py`, and widen the `_as_choice` set in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:697` to `{"jira", "jira-datacenter"}`.

Provenance follows the epic's decision: DC-created tickets carry the shared `jira` creation channel and `jira-` local-id prefix, with the deployment distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance`. Nothing in the store vocabulary changes, so no migration and no compatibility gate are involved.

**Then extend `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture params to include the DC backend** (constructed with an injected fake transport, exactly as `JiraBackend` already is at that fixture), so every generic port assertion runs against it.

**Alternative rejected:** adapter-local tests only (PR #120). They prove the adapter does what its author expected, not that it satisfies the port the core drives.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/__init__.py` — register the DC factory.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (`:697`) — widen the backend choice set; update the field comment at `:498`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` — fixture params.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — a DC fake transport if the existing one does not fit.
- `tests/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract tier for the port, plus a live end-to-end pass on the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] because this story is the point at which the whole assembly first drives a real instance.

- contract: every existing assertion in `test_backend_contract.py` passes with the DC backend in the fixture

- live end-to-end: a full reconcile pass against the harness creates a remote issue from a local ticket,

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes with no assertion

- [ ] a test asserts the backend is NOT an instance of `SupportsIncremental`
- [ ] [operator-attested] a full reconcile pass against the J5 harness converges, and an immediately repeated pass writes nothing

baseline.description:
# `sign-review` aborts on stray UNTRACKED tracker files — a missed site of already-fixed bug d7cb

## Symptom

`rebar review-plan <id>` returns **PASS** but cannot sign, and the documented recovery `rebar sign-review <id>` fails **deterministically** (3/3, not contention):

```
{"ok": false, "signed": false, "verdict": "PASS",
 "reason": "plan review generation could not be collected: store-read-failure"}
```

Net effect: a plan that PASSED cannot be signed, so `claim` and the plan-review CLOSE gate stay blocked on a clean PASS. The billable LLM review runs and passes, and only then can the result not be persisted — the work is paid for and discarded.

## CORRECTION to this ticket's original filing

This ticket originally named `attest.py:406` as the cause. That was a **lead, and it is refuted** as the source of this symptom: the message text is emitted only at `resign.py:153`, wrapping `generation.collect`, and `attest.py` is not on that path. `attest.py` is a *sibling* (below), not the cause.

## PROVEN root cause

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:146` calls

```python
initial_generation = generation.collect(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)
```

omitting `ignore_untracked`, which defaults to `False` (`generation.collect(..., ignore_untracked: bool = False)`). That reaches `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(ignore_untracked=False)` → `tracker_head_sha(tracker)` strict, which runs

```python
("status", "--porcelain")            # untracked INCLUDED
```

instead of `("status","--porcelain","--untracked-files=no")`. Any untracked file makes the output non-empty → `_store_error` → `store-read-failure` → resign's wrapper reports "plan review generation could not be collected".

## Experimental proof (runtime, isolated temp git repo)

| condition | strict (`ignore_untracked=False`) | lenient (`True`) |
|---|---|---|
| clean tree | OK (control) | OK |
| untracked `.tmp-event-*` (partial JSON) | **RAISE store-read-failure** | OK |
| untracked file, UNRELATED name + content | **RAISE store-read-failure** | OK |
| TRACKED dirty (modified file) | RAISE | **RAISE** |

Row 3 **refutes** the competing "partial-JSON parse failure" hypothesis: the failure is entirely content- and name-agnostic, purely the `git status` check. Row 4 shows the flag does NOT weaken the real guarantee — tracked dirty state still fails, as it must.

Field observation that opened the case: two orphaned `.tmp-event-*` files (~16h stale, 0 tracked-dirty / 2 untracked) in the shared tracker; moving them out made the identical `sign-review` succeed with nothing else changed.

## Why it is a DEFECT (cited authority, not the reporter's expectation)

This is a **missed site of an already-fixed bug class**. Bug `d7cb-22ae` (commit `1475e2868`, "d7cb: plan-review tolerates unrelated untracked shared-tracker files") fixed exactly this in two places and landed two regression tests that state the contract:

- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_review_plan_preflight_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files`
- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_sign_manifest_fence_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files`
  — labelled "**sibling on the SIGNING path**", and stating that otherwise a stray artifact
  "aborts signing (`store-read-failure`), so no durable attestation is persisted and the plan-review
  claim gate cannot pass even for a clean plan".

That fix touched `__init__.py` and `generation.py` but **never `resign.py`**. The intended behaviour is therefore already established and this site violates it.

## Blast radius

`.tickets-tracker` is symlinked into every session, so ONE crashed writer anywhere blocks signing for every concurrent session on the machine — the same machine-wide collapse d7cb was raised to prevent.

## SIBLINGS found by sweeping every untracked-sensitive call site

| site | call | symptom when an untracked file exists |
|---|---|---|
| `resign.py:146` | `generation.collect(...)` | HARD FAIL — `sign-review` refuses (this ticket's confirmed cause) |
| `orchestrator.py:650` | `generation.collect(...)` | SILENT COST — wrapped in `except Exception: return None` ("unstable generation falls back to a full review"), so a stray file forces a full multi-pass LLM re-review instead of the cheap drift-refresh probe |
| `attest.py:139` | `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(...)` | aborts signing on the fallback path (when no `initial_generation`/snapshot is supplied) |
| `attest.py:406` | `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(...)` | same, in `refresh_attestation` |

Already correct (fixed by d7cb): `__init__.py:495`, `generation.py:131/133/173`.

`orchestrator.py:650` is the most insidious: it fails INVISIBLY and the only symptom is money and latency — a full LLM review where a cheap probe was intended.

## Approach

Pass `ignore_untracked=True` at each of the four sites. These are all READS that fingerprint the COMMITTED head, which untracked files cannot change; the authoritative under-lock re-check (`generation.py:173`) already tolerates them, so this makes the class consistent.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — the confirmed defect.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — siblings.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py` — regression tests beside the two existing d7cb siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts `resign_plan_review` still signs a valid PASS when an UNRELATED untracked file
      exists in the tracker, and fails RED before the fix
- [ ] a test asserts TRACKED dirty state still blocks these paths — the flag must not weaken the
      real guarantee
- [ ] the orchestrator drift-refresh path does not silently fall back to a full review because of an
      untracked file
- [ ] every `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` / `generation.collect` call site in `src/rebar` either
      passes `ignore_untracked=True` or carries a comment saying why strictness is intended
baseline.summary: sign-review fails on stray untracked tracker files: attest.py omits ignore_untracked

## Problem

Surfaced while fixing `anatomical-arbored-oyster` (e3e0-2e7c-b280-4b4a). With the mirror sweep's collection/install errors removed, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py` now runs and fails on the non-editable macOS and floor legs:

```
AssertionError: Resolved repo_root PosixPath('/Users/runner/work/rebar/rebar/.venv/lib/python3.13')
does not contain src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py — default root resolution is wrong;
expected Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] from __main__.py
```

## Root cause (CONFIRMED)

`src/rebar/config.py::reconciler_repo_root()` derives the default repo root (when `REBAR_ROOT` is unset) as `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` — the **package location**. Under an **editable** install the package lives inside the checkout, so this is the repo root. Under a **non-editable / wheel** install the package lives in `site-packages`, so `parents[2]` is `<venv>/lib/pythonX` — not a checkout. Confirmed at runtime (see RCA comment). `invariants._default_repo_root()` delegates here; all 13 reconciler sites reach it. Production is unaffected because it sets `REBAR_ROOT`; the sweep's non-editable/floor legs (which unset it) expose it.

## Fix plan (Option C — VALIDATED LAYERED FALLBACK; operator-approved, decision CLOSED)

Reimplement `reconciler_repo_root()` to resolve, in order:
1. `REBAR_ROOT` env, if set → use it **verbatim** (`Path(env)`, unchanged first-priority behavior).
2. else the package root `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` **IF it is a real checkout** → use it (preserves the editable-install path AND documented CWD-independence: package root is still tried before any CWD-based resolution).
3. else the **git toplevel of CWD** (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) **IF that resolves to a real checkout** → use it (last-resort convenience for non-editable dev installs launched from inside a checkout).
4. else raise a CLEAR, actionable error naming BOTH `REBAR_ROOT` and `--repo-root`. NEVER silently return a non-checkout path.

Design constraints honored: package root (step 2) is tried BEFORE CWD (step 3) so daemon-from-anywhere and editable installs behave exactly as today when the package root is valid; CWD is only a fallback and only when it is itself a checkout (a daemon in an arbitrary non-checkout CWD errors clearly at step 4 rather than reconciling the wrong tree). "Real checkout" = `.git` entry (dir or worktree file) AND `src/rebar` package dir at the candidate root — the pair a venv/site-packages tree lacks. Behavior-preserving for the two cases that work today: `REBAR_ROOT` set, and editable install with unset `REBAR_ROOT`.

Helper extraction: `_is_repo_checkout(root)` (the `.git` + `src/rebar` validator) and `_git_toplevel_of_cwd()` (step-3 subprocess), so `reconciler_repo_root` stays under the mccabe ceiling.

## Test plan (RED→GREEN)

New RED test asserting the layered behavior at the owned seam:
- Non-editable-shaped package root (not a checkout) + non-checkout CWD, `REBAR_ROOT` unset → **raises** the clear error (TODAY: returns the wrong venv path). This is the discriminating RED.
- Non-editable-shaped package root + CWD inside a real checkout → returns **that checkout** (step 3).
- Behavior-preserving controls: `REBAR_ROOT` set → returns it verbatim; editable/source package root → returns it (step 2). Existing `test_reconciler_repo_root_unset_fallback_is_cwd_independent` and `test_reconcile_main.py` legs must stay green.

## Attribution
`caused_by = ba8b-c728-8c62-48e9` (C3a-CORE `d361eb28`, deliberate owned-default design that authored the current line); class `plan_defect`. Bootstrap origin `b534f47a` (untrailered) recorded in RCA as the carrier chain root.

## Evidence
- Mirror run 33299427686: `sweep (macos, full suite)` job 99224621948 (4x), `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` job 99224621821 (6x).
- Also failing in pre-fix run 33285143350 macOS leg (pre-existing, masked by the collection error).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `test_reconcile_main.py` repo-root resolution assertions pass under both editable and non-editable installs.
- [x] The reconciler's default repo-root behavior under a non-editable install is defined and documented (no silent resolution into the venv tree): validated layered fallback, else a clear error naming `REBAR_ROOT`/`--repo-root`.
- [x] `REBAR_ROOT`-set and editable-install behavior is unchanged (behavior-preserving).
- [x] New RED test proves the raise-on-non-checkout and CWD-fallback legs; held out from the fixer and mutation-checked.

## Step-7 sibling scope (class-review: confirmed siblings become declared scope)

The construct swept is the `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]` package-location-as-repo-root assumption. Sweep confirmed two siblings in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` (lines ~507, ~626): `repo_root = Path(repo_root_env() or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4])`. When `REBAR_ROOT` is unset this is the SAME defect (package-location default → non-checkout venv path under a non-editable install), bypassing the owned `reconciler_repo_root()` resolver. `__main__.py:52` (`_pkg_parent = ...parents[3]`) is a sys.path import bootstrap resolving the package PARENT, not a repo root — NOT a sibling.

Disposition: fix both fetcher sites IN SCOPE by routing through the validated `config.reconciler_repo_root()` (this both removes the raw fallback AND closes the parity gap — every reconciler surface then resolves repo-root through the single owned validated resolver), under the same RED→GREEN discipline.

### Additional acceptance criteria (siblings)
- [x] `fetcher.py` both repo_root fallbacks route through `config.reconciler_repo_root()`; no reconciler module derives repo-root from a raw `Path(__file__).parents[N]` package-location fallback.
- [x] A construct-uniqueness guard test fails if any reconciler site reintroduces the raw package-location repo-root fallback (RED before the fetcher fix, GREEN after).
baseline.summary: Reconciler default repo-root fallback (__main__.py parents[4]) assumes an editable checkout; wrong under non-editable install

## Summary

Step-7 class review under auspicial-friended-merganser (2ec7-be89-9b01-496a) found ADDITIONAL members of the same construct class beyond that ticket's explicitly enumerated 9 sites. These derive a REPO/CONFIG root from the store path via variants the enumerated list and the AC guard (scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py, which matched only the bare `dirname(tracker)` and `dirname(tracker_dir())` forms) do NOT cover:

### Config/gate reads (str(tracker) variant) — advisory-only impact, closest siblings
- src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:274 and :286 — cfg_root=os.path.dirname(str(tracker)) into description_cap_warning() and duplicate_create_warning(); cfg_root feeds compose_config() (verify.max_ticket_description_chars, verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets) AND _plan_review_gate_applies(). On a relocated store these read an empty config, so the save-time description-cap heads-up and duplicate probe are silently suppressed. ADVISORY only (never blocks a write), which is why it is milder than the enumerated AC#1 gate escape. repo_root is in scope in create_core (composer.py:125).
- src/rebar/_commands/composer_edit.py:141 — same cfg_root=os.path.dirname(str(tracker)) in _edit_description_warning(); needs repo_root threaded from edit_core (composer.py:553, calls at :647).

### Config reads (realpath()/abspath() variant) — NEEDS A DESIGN JUDGMENT per site
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:238 — _sync_disabled(dirname(realpath(tracker))) -> compose_config(root).sync.pull (reads.py:220).
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:249 — tickets_branch(dirname(tracker_abs)) -> tickets.branch config.
- src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:374 — _load_scratch: repo_root = dirname(abspath(tracker)) -> compose_config(root).scratch.base_dir (reads.py:381).

The realpath/abspath family is genuinely nuanced: these operate on the STORE's OWN git repo (git -C tracker_abs for sync/branch), so for a relocated store the tracker's parent may LEGITIMATELY be the correct root for sync.pull / tickets.branch (the store is its own repo), whereas scratch.base_dir arguably should follow the CODE repo. Resolving each is AC#3's 'or documents why the tracker's parent is correct for it' clause and requires a per-site design decision — which is why it is split OUT of the enumerated-9 ticket rather than folded into that behavior-preserving change.

Other realpath(tracker)-root sites to TRIAGE for the same question (likely legitimate store-repo roots for git/attribution, but verify): compact_txn.py:523, compact_rebuild.py:138, compact_plan.py:211, fsck.py:252, fsck_tracker_health.py:82/:203/:373, _proc.py:141, _store/sync.py:311/:312.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC#1 — composer.py:274/:286 and composer_edit.py:141 resolve `cfg_root` from the repo root (`repo_root` in scope / threaded), NOT `os.path.dirname(str(tracker))`. Proven by a RED→GREEN test that the description-cap warning fires on a relocated store with a low `verify.max_ticket_description_chars` (`tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py`).
- [x] AC#2 — Extend `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` to also flag the `str()`-wrapped store argument (`dirname(str(tracker))` / `dirname(str(tracker_dir()))`), and sanction the legitimate store-repo sites (`_store/sync.py:301/302`) with `# repo-root-ok:`, so a new instance of the fixed class fails `make lint`. Proven by the guard self-test (`tests/unit/test_repo_root_from_tracker_guard.py`).
- [x] AC#3 — The `realpath()`/`abspath()` design-judgment family (reads.py sync/branch/scratch; compact_*; fsck_*; _proc.py) is triaged and split to a linked follow-up ticket with the per-site design decision recorded, because those are NOT behavior-preserving (they require threading `repo_root` through read-path helpers that hold only `tracker`). The `realpath`/`abspath` half of the guard extension is contingent on those decisions and deferred with them.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py tests/unit/test_repo_root_from_tracker_guard.py -q` — the create-path AND edit-path description-cap warnings fire on a relocated store (RED before the fix, GREEN after); the guard flags the `str()` variant and passes the sanctioned sites.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` — the extended guard is green on the fixed tree.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && make typecheck` — no regressions.
- Sandboxed mutation check: re-seeding `cfg_root=os.path.dirname(str(tracker))` returns the held-out create-path test to RED; restoring the fix returns it to GREEN.

---

## EXECUTED SCOPE (debug session — construct sweep, Axis 1 class fix)

The construct sweep confirmed the members of this class split cleanly into a behavior-preserving `str()`-variant subset (fixed here) and a design-judgment `realpath()`/`abspath()` subset (escalated to a follow-up). Root cause proven at runtime; see the RCA comment.

### Fixed in this change (behavior-preserving, `repo_root` already in scope)
1. **composer.py:274** — `description_cap_warning(cfg_root=...)` resolves
   `cfg_root=str(config.repo_root(repo_root))`, not `os.path.dirname(str(tracker))`.
2. **composer.py:286** — `duplicate_create_warning(cfg_root=...)`, same resolution.
3. **composer_edit.py:141** — `_edit_description_warning` takes `repo_root` (threaded
   from `edit_core`) and resolves `cfg_root=str(config.repo_root(repo_root))`.
4. **Structural guard (AC#2, `str()` half)** — `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py`
   also flags the `str()`-wrapped store argument (`dirname(str(tracker))` /
   `dirname(str(tracker_dir()))`), so a new instance of the fixed class fails `make lint`.
5. **_store/sync.py:301/302** — `tickets_branch`/`tickets_remote(dirname(str(tracker)))`
   carry a `# repo-root-ok:` sanction: they operate on the STORE's own git repo
   (`git -C tracker`) and name refs within it, and no code `repo_root` is threaded to
   that read-path helper (matches this ticket's "likely legitimate store-repo roots" lean).

### Escalated to a follow-up (design judgment — NOT auto-landed, AC#3)
The `realpath()`/`abspath()` family (reads.py:238 sync.pull, :249 tickets.branch, :374 scratch.base_dir; compact_txn/rebuild/plan; fsck/fsck_tracker_health; _proc.py) needs a per-site design decision: resolve from the code root (requires threading `repo_root` through read-path helpers that hold only `tracker` — a signature change) OR a documented store-repo sanction. The `realpath`/`abspath` half of the guard extension is contingent ("once the legitimate store-repo sites carry a sanction") on those decisions, so it is deferred with them. These are not behavior-preserving, so per the debug protocol they are split to a linked follow-up rather than auto-landed.

## Summary

The sandbox enforcement tests added by `e668-b496-e264-4283` in `tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` assert only that a file is ABSENT after running a wrapped subprocess:

```python
assert not target.exists()          # denial "proven"
```

Nothing asserts the sandboxed child actually launched and reached the write attempt. If `sandbox-exec`/`bwrap` fails to start at all — bad profile, missing binary, a namespace refusal, an argv regression — the write never happens, the file is absent, and the test PASSES. A total failure of the sandbox wrapper is indistinguishable from correct enforcement.

`test_the_incident_shape_rm_rf_is_denied` has the same shape in reverse: it asserts a pre-existing `keep.txt` still exists. A sandbox launch failure trivially leaves the file in place, producing a false pass.

## Why this matters more than a normal test gap

These are the ONLY tests that demonstrate the sandbox works. `e668`'s acceptance criteria deliberately required observed enforcement rather than argv assertions, precisely so the control could not be satisfied by construction alone. A test that passes when the mechanism is absent silently reintroduces the weakness those criteria were written to exclude — the evidence for the whole feature rests on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every enforcement test asserts positive LIVENESS of the sandboxed child through
      an artifact the CHILD ITSELF produced after starting — a sentinel it wrote to an
      ALLOWED path, or a marker it printed to stdout — asserted before the denial is
      read. The wrapper's exit status does NOT qualify: a sandbox that fails to launch
      also exits non-zero, so exit code cannot distinguish executed-and-denied from
      never-ran, which is the exact ambiguity this ticket removes.
- [x] The liveness assertion is proven load-bearing: with the sandbox mechanism forced
      unavailable so the child never launches, the test goes RED rather than green.
      Demonstrated by real substitution, not asserted.
- [x] `test_the_incident_shape_rm_rf_is_denied` gains the same liveness check, so a
      launch failure cannot pass as "the target survived".

## Acceptance Criteria — blast radius

An enforcement test asserts that a control DENIES something. If the control silently does nothing, the denied action HAPPENS — which is the incident's own mechanism, re-created inside the test suite. These tests must therefore be fail-safe: a total sandbox failure must produce a red test, never damage.

- [x] Write-denial is proven with a CREATE, not a DELETE, wherever the proof does not
      require deletion. A leaked create is inert; a leaked delete destroys. Verified by
      inspection: no enforcement test removes anything except the single incident-shape
      test below.
- [x] The incident-shape test is bounded so a TOTAL sandbox failure cannot escape the
      pytest tmp dir. The target is passed via the environment and dereferenced as
      `"${VAR:?}"`, so an empty or unset variable ABORTS the shell instead of expanding
      to `rm -rf /*` — the exact guard whose absence caused the 2026-08-26 incident —
      and the path is never interpolated into the shell string.
- [x] Python refuses to launch the destructive child unless the target is non-empty,
      absolute, and strictly inside `tmp_path`. Verified by a test asserting the
      guard raises when handed a path outside `tmp_path`.
- [x] The `${VAR:?}` guard is itself proven, not assumed: with the variable set empty
      the shell aborts non-zero and the canary survives, asserted by a test that runs
      that case WITHOUT a sandbox — so it demonstrates the guard alone is sufficient to
      stop the incident's expansion.

## Definition of Done

- No enforcement test in the file can pass when the sandbox fails to launch.
- Each liveness check is shown RED under a forced launch failure.
- No enforcement test can damage anything outside the pytest tmp dir even if the
  sandbox enforces NOTHING at all.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Found by the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on change 2256 (patch sets 4 and 7; advisory, so it did not block the merge). Discovered from `e668-b496-e264-4283`.
baseline.summary: Sandbox enforcement tests pass when the sandbox fails to launch

baseline.description:
The review-bot's structured operational logs (the `_emit()` INFO events — `voter_voted`, `voter_skip`, `merge_detection`, and all `reconcile_*`) are silently dropped in production, so operators are blind to what the bot decides. Configure a logging handler for rebar's loggers so these reach stdout/journald.

## Why
`src/rebar/review_bot/` contains NO logging setup (`grep` for `basicConfig`/`dictConfig` in `src/rebar/` returns nothing). The container runs `uvicorn rebar.review_bot.app:app`; uvicorn configures only its own `uvicorn.*` loggers and never the root or `rebar.*` loggers. So a `logging.getLogger("rebar.review_bot.voter").info(...)` record has no handler and falls through to Python's `logging.lastResort`, which emits **WARNING and above only** — every INFO `_emit` line is discarded. This was directly observed during incident triage: `journalctl` showed uvicorn's own access lines and the `print()`-to-stderr markers (`VOTER_ERROR`, `ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR`) but ZERO `voter_voted`/`reconcile_*` lines, making a healthy-but-slow reconciler look dead. The `_emit` docstrings call these "observability markers" — dropping them violates that documented intent.

## What
Add a `_configure_logging()` to `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`, called once at module import (before `app = FastAPI(...)`), that attaches a `StreamHandler(sys.stdout)` to the `rebar` logger at level `INFO` (overridable via a `REVIEW_BOT_LOG_LEVEL` env var), with a bare `"%(message)s"` formatter (the `_emit` payload is already JSON), an idempotency marker on the handler (so repeated imports/reloads don't stack handlers), and `propagate=False` (so records do NOT double-log through uvicorn/root). Targeting the `rebar` logger specifically — not root — avoids duplicating uvicorn's access logs.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`: add `_configure_logging()` + `import sys`; call at import.
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`: add a test asserting a `rebar.review_bot.*` INFO record
  reaches stdout after the app module configures logging (RED before the fix).
- Non-goal (separate follow-up): shipping logs to a shared service (CloudWatch Logs group).
  This change makes the logs *emitted*; centralizing them is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `logging.getLogger("rebar.review_bot.voter").info(...)` record is written to stdout
      once the review-bot app module has configured logging; before the fix the same record
      produces no stdout output (proving the drop).
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k configure_logging -q`
      passes, and the test is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] The handler is idempotent: importing/configuring twice does not attach a second handler
      (no duplicate log lines).
      Proving command: assert `len([h for h in logging.getLogger("rebar").handlers if marker])
      == 1` after two `_configure_logging()` calls (in the test).
- [ ] `REVIEW_BOT_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` lowers the effective level (env override honored); an
      absent/invalid value falls back to INFO.
      Proving command: covered by a parametrized assertion in the test.
- [ ] Existing gates stay green.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q` all exit 0.
baseline.summary: review-bot: configure logging so structured _emit INFO events reach stdout/journald

## Context / Problem

Code-review overlay prompts are guarded by standing eval specs (pattern: `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` — seeded recall + no-fire diff families, deterministic scorers, validated offline with `rebar prompt eval <prompt-id>`). The concurrency overlay's rubric was designed against a corpus of real races traced to their introducing commits; without a standing eval, prompt edits can silently regress exactly the recall/precision behavior that corpus established.

## Approach

Author `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-concurrency.eval.yaml` mirroring the tests-overlay spec shape (`epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, deterministic scorers `code_review_emits_valid_findings` / `code_review_recall` / `code_review_no_fire`). Dataset entries are MINIMAL DIFF HUNKS distilled from the traced corpus (each with a provenance comment naming the source commit), not full historical replays.

Grounding in the eval harness (`rebar.llm.evals.eval.run_eval`), NOT assumed: a gating deterministic scorer passes an EPOCH iff every APPLICABLE case passes it (all-or-nothing per epoch); an epoch passes iff `coverage_ok` AND every gating scorer passes; `coverage_threshold` is the fraction of cases that RAN without erroring (a run-success floor, not a pass-rate lever); the ONLY per-run tolerance is `gate: at_least(2)` over `epochs: 3` (a whole-epoch nondeterminism budget). Consequently a persistently-failing gating recall case fails the gate regardless of `coverage_threshold`.

Scored gating dataset:

- RECALL R1 — unlocked twin (`expect: finding`): a `subprocess.run(["git", ..., "commit"])` write to the shared tracker bypassing the locked `event_append` seam sibling writers use (distilled from 9ad46965bd, `eclectic-spotted-barb`).
- RECALL R2 — check-then-act TOCTOU (`expect: finding`): `os.path.getmtime(lock)` -> judge stale -> `os.remove(lock)` with no identity re-validation (distilled from 56e130ff71, `fine-wisteria-solenodon`).
- NO-FIRE F1 (`expect: pass`) — a write lock ADDED around a previously unlocked merge (distilled from 7853af7698).
- NO-FIRE F2 (`expect: pass`) — an atomic-write seam conversion of process-local scratch state (distilled from 95f97cbeb6).
- NO-FIRE F3 (`expect: pass`) — the hard FP control: a DELIBERATE probe-then-skip where the skipped work is explicitly optional and the subsequent operation still takes the real lock (distilled from abbc65adf4).

Known-hard stretch, deliberately NON-GATING:

- RECALL R3 — fail-open guard (distilled from 3938c7ed2d, `greisen-draconian-annelid`): drift between two reads is detected, a warning is emitted, and the operation proceeds anyway on the stale read. This is the hardest case for a less-capable reviewer (the warning reads as "handled"). Because the harness has no per-case exemption for a scored case, R3 is included as a NON-GATING documented stretch — a commented hunk block in the dataset section (provenance + rationale), NOT a scored `- id:` case — so it is tracked but, being unscored, cannot fail the gate by construction. Promoting it to a scored recall case is a future step once the prompt reliably fires on it.

Positive rationale: seeding from traced production bugs makes the eval a regression oracle for the defect classes that actually occurred here (and their nearest benign neighbors), rather than synthetic strawmen; the distilled-hunk form matches the existing eval-spec format exactly.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-concurrency.eval.yaml` (new file).

## Testing

The spec IS the test (LLM behavioral eval per the shared test-design standard section 10): pinned model in the spec, 3 epochs, deterministic scorers, a predeclared gate. In-session oracle: `rebar prompt eval code-review-concurrency` (validate-only in this codebase — it checks the spec is well-formed and the scorers/gate resolve) exits 0; the LIVE behavioral run happens in eval CI, exactly as for every sibling overlay spec. The no-fire family is the negative control by construction. The spec is also held to the strict packaged-spec discipline gate (`validate_dataset_and_gold`: unique ids, `expect` in the known vocabulary, a balanced fire/pass dataset, a non-empty gold_set).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-concurrency.eval.yaml` exists and `rebar prompt eval code-review-concurrency` exits 0; checked by the command's exit code.
- [x] The spec has at least 2 scored recall cases (`expect: finding`), each with a provenance comment naming its source commit; checked by reading the file.
- [x] The spec has at least 3 scored no-fire cases (`expect: pass`), each with a provenance comment naming its source commit; checked by reading the file.
- [x] The hard FP control F3 (deliberate probe-then-skip that still takes the real lock) is a scored `expect: pass` case; checked by reading the file.
- [x] R3 (fail-open guard) is present as a NON-GATING documented stretch — a commented hunk block carrying its provenance and known-hard rationale, and NOT a scored `- id:` case — so it cannot fail the gate; checked by reading the file.
- [x] A header comment states that `coverage_threshold` is a run-success floor and that the only per-run tolerance is `gate: at_least(2)` over `epochs: 3`; checked by reading the file.
baseline.summary: Standing eval spec for the concurrency overlay from the traced bug corpus

## Prevention remediation for incident 1c0d (code-review lane)

Post-mortem: `9097-2741-6462-424c`. Origin change `8fbd` ("Enable class-scoped Anthropic fallback") passed code review, yet it enabled a fallback whose terminal arm masks a retryable primary. This ticket evaluates a **code-review criterion** that would have flagged it.

### Candidate criterion
When a change adds or edits a fallback chain / provider failover / error-classification path, the reviewer flags: (a) a fallback leg's own failure that can upgrade a retryable primary to non-retryable (disposition-masking), and (b) a failover target that may be unreachable/uncredentialed in a target environment.

### Open decision (BEHAVIOR CHANGE — escalate before implementing)
Adding an `LLM-Review` criterion alters what the code-review gate blocks/advises on. Needs a go/no-go on: is this a **blocking** or **advisory** criterion; is it a general "error-handling change" criterion or narrowly scoped to fallback/classification code; false-positive surface. Do NOT implement until the disposition (scope + blocking level) is decided.

### Acceptance criteria (pending decision)
- [ ] Decision recorded on criterion scope and blocking level.
- [ ] If approved: criterion authored + registered; a fixture change reproducing 8fbd's shape is flagged; a benign fallback edit is not.

# Tier-1 opportunistic detached drain + `rebar enrich` CLI

## Why
The feature must run async across server/PC/Mac/cloud with ZERO client setup — no daemon, broker, or scheduler. The proven pattern (git gc --auto, npm update-notifier) piggybacks a cheap, detached drain on ordinary invocations. rebar ships the POSIX half of this already for async push (`src/rebar/_store/push.py:108`).

## What
- A `maybe_drain()` gate on ordinary invocations: a cheap "is anything soaked+unclaimed?" check that no-ops in the common case, else DETACHES the enrichment to a child that outlives the command.
- **Detach, POSIX in v1 (Windows drain is a documented no-op):** POSIX reuses push.py's approach (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`) + its PYTHONPATH bootstrap. **Windows drain is explicitly a NO-OP in v1** and `maybe_drain` returns early on `os.name == "nt"` (logging "windows drain deferred"), for a concrete reason the reviewer surfaced: the store's write lock `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` imports `fcntl` UNCONDITIONALLY at module top, so a detached drain child on Windows would crash at import the moment it touched the write path (`append_event` → `stage_and_commit` → `lock`). Rather than spawn a doomed child, v1 gates the detach to POSIX. The Windows `creationflags=subprocess.DETACHED_PROCESS | subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW` branch is still AUTHORED (API-derisked; these constants exist only on Windows — referenced ONLY inside the `os.name == "nt"` branch so the POSIX import never AttributeErrors) and unit-tested by kwargs selection, but is not reached by `maybe_drain` in v1. Making `lock.py` Windows-safe (conditional `fcntl` import) is spun out as a follow-up idea — Tier-1 targets server/PC/Mac; Windows drain is deferred, not blocking.
- **Observability:** the child configures a `logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler` (maxBytes+backupCount bounded) writing to `.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log` (git-ignored) and redirects its own stderr there; stdout/stdin are DEVNULL — drain failures stay diagnosable.
- **Drainer loop (owns DONE + self-healing + growth-bound, moved here from S3):** from `pending_enrichment(now)` PLUS the fallback scan (tickets certified but with absent/stale digest — the defense-in-depth), claim one via the queue's OPTIMISTIC `queue.claim(ticket_id, drainer_id, …)` (append + earliest-live-lease arbitration — NOT a held `lock.acquire`, because `append_event` self-serializes writes under the store write lock and a claim cannot hold that lock across its own append; "one drainer lands, losers retry" is realized by post-append arbitration, per S4), run `enrich` (S1), write `TICKET_DIGEST` (S2), append `DONE_ENRICH`, then `prune` the ticket's queue events so log growth is bounded. **Prune rule (concrete, no "cycle" ambiguity):** keep=1 — retain ONLY the single latest queue event per ticket by HLC (the `DONE_ENRICH` tombstone just written), and drop ALL superseded queue events for that ticket (every prior `ENQUEUE_ENRICH`, `CLAIM_ENRICH`, and older `DONE_ENRICH`). The retained `DONE_ENRICH` means "not pending" to the reducer until a later `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` (a re-certification) supersedes it. This bounds each ticket's queue footprint to one event (mirrors the digest-sidecar `prune(keep=1)`). Process UP TO `DRAIN_BATCH` per run, then exit.
- **The drain's OWN lenient advisory lock (distinct from the store write lock AND from the optimistic queue-claim):** to stop two concurrent drain PROCESSES from doing redundant work, the drain takes a best-effort advisory lock file `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` (a non-blocking `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` create, or an equivalent flock with immediate timeout). If it is already held, the drain exits SILENTLY with code 0 (logged to the drain log) — it does NOT block/wait. This is a separate, drain-level lock: it is NOT the store write lock (`_store/lock.py`, held only briefly inside each `append_event`) and NOT the queue claim (which is optimistic append + arbitration, holding no lock). `test_lock_held_skip` exercises THIS advisory lock: a second drain invocation with the lock already held returns 0 without processing. Per-item error handling: an `enrich` exception (LLM timeout/rate-limit) releases the claim (lease expiry) and is logged; the batch continues to the next ticket; the failed ticket is re-picked on a later drain.
- **CLI `rebar enrich`:** `--drain` (bounded drain, the detached target), `--once` (claim+process one entry, in-process, tests), `status` (prints JSON `{"pending":int,"claimed":int,"soaking":int}` from the queue reducer). **Bucket predicates (co-located with the CLI spec, computed by `queue.reduce_ticket(now)` per ticket, mutually exclusive):** `soaking` = has a latest `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` with `not_before_ns > now` and no later `DONE_ENRICH` (still in the soak window); `claimed` = past soak with a latest `CLAIM_ENRICH` (after the latest enqueue) whose `lease_expires_ns > now` and no later `DONE_ENRICH` (a live lease); `pending` = past soak, unclaimed-or-lease-expired, and no `DONE_ENRICH` after the latest enqueue (exactly what `queue.pending_enrichment` returns). A ticket with a `DONE_ENRICH` after its latest enqueue is in NONE of the three buckets. `overlap_drain ∈ {off, async, always}`, DEFAULT `async` (`async` = the opportunistic detached drain of this design; `always` = synchronous inline drain for tests/CI; `off` = no drain). Opt-out is `overlap_drain = "off"` on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`), env `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN` (the ONE canonical name — used in What, Scope, and ACs identically). `overlap_drain` is a STRING enum (`off|async|always`) so it lives on `LLMConfig` (read via `from_env`), NOT `VerifyConfig` (which is bool-only via `_as_bool`).

## Constants (defaults stated)
`DRAIN_BATCH = 5`, `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS = 20` — both on `LLMConfig`.

## maybe_drain injection point (decided)
`maybe_drain()` is invoked from `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py::write_and_push` immediately after `push.push_tickets_branch` — the HIGH-FREQUENCY write path taken by create/edit/comment/link/tag/sign/set_* (the bulk of ordinary invocations), behind a cheap soaked?-check that no-ops on the common event. NOTE (reviewer-surfaced): the status-only writes `transition`/`reopen`/`claim`/`compact`/`delete` use a SEPARATE push path (`push.push_after_commit`, `push.py:267-286`), so a `maybe_drain` in `write_and_push` does NOT fire for those. That is ACCEPTABLE and deliberate: the drain is OPPORTUNISTIC and SELF-HEALING — a soaked ticket does not need every write to trigger a drain; it WILL be drained on the next create/edit/comment anywhere in the store (and the fallback scan re-picks any cert-without-fresh-digest ticket regardless). To avoid a rare cold-store gap where ONLY status-only writes occur, `maybe_drain()` is ALSO called at the end of `push.push_after_commit` (the same one-line cheap-gated call), so both push paths carry it. `test_gate_latency` asserts the cheap gate no-ops within `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS` and spawns nothing when nothing is soaked.

## Dependencies
S1 (enrich op), S2 (digest store), S3/S4 (queue + claim primitive + event types). This story WIRES them; they are prerequisite sibling stories, not existing code.

**Event-type ownership (resolves the "DONE_ENRICH unregistered" concern):** the three queue event types — `ENQUEUE_ENRICH`, `CLAIM_ENRICH`, `DONE_ENRICH` — are added to `event_append.EVENT_TYPES` (write allow-list) and `reducer._version._NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` by the QUEUE story S4 (`vegan-forgetful-tiger`, `e1f4`), which this story `depends_on`. This story only **emits** `DONE_ENRICH` (and appends `CLAIM_ENRICH`) via the drainer loop — it does NOT re-register the types. Because S4 lands below S6 in the stack, the types exist before this story's writes run; `test_done_enrich_registered` asserts `DONE_ENRICH in event_append.EVENT_TYPES` as a guard so a missing prerequisite fails loudly rather than raising a StoreError at drain time.

## Scope
- New `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py`; CLI arm in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` (`rebar enrich` with `--drain`/`--once`/`status`); **CLI dispatch intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`** — add `if argv and argv[0] == "enrich": return _llm_commands.cmd_enrich(argv[1:], tracker)` alongside the existing `review`/`review-plan`/`verify-completion` intercepts (~line 375-400); without it `rebar enrich` is unroutable. The `maybe_drain` hook called from `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py::write_and_push` (after `push_tickets_branch`) AND from `src/rebar/_store/push.py::push_after_commit`, so BOTH write push paths carry the opportunistic drain; plus the drain's advisory lock file `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: add `overlap_drain` (str enum `off|async|always`, default `async`), `overlap_drain_batch` (int, default 5), `overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms` (int, default 20) as `LLMConfig` fields AND wire them in `from_env()`: `overlap_drain=_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN", "overlap_drain", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN)` (validate the value is in `{off,async,always}`, else fall back to default), `overlap_drain_batch=_llm_int(..., "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH", "overlap_drain_batch", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH)`, `overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms=_llm_int(..., "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS", "overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS)`, with the three `DEFAULT_*` module constants.
- OUT: native scheduler (idea Tier-2), CI drain (idea Tier-3).

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`: `test_once` (one entry end-to-end, FakeRunner); `test_batch_cap` (`DRAIN_BATCH` bound, backlog drains over runs); `test_gate_latency` (maybe_drain no-op < `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS`, no spawn when nothing soaked); `test_lock_held_skip` (silent exit 0, logged); `test_enrich_error_continues` (one enrich() raises → claim released, batch continues); `test_no_key_noop` ([agents]/key absent → clean no-op); `test_opt_out` (`REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off`); `test_self_heal` (certified-but-stale-digest ticket picked up by fallback scan); `test_windows_detach_kwargs` (the authored os.name=="nt" branch selects the DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW creationflags — mocked, not spawned); `test_windows_noop` (with `os.name` mocked to "nt", `maybe_drain` returns early WITHOUT spawning any child — the documented v1 Windows no-op, since lock.py's fcntl import would crash a Windows drain child); `test_status` (`rebar enrich status` prints JSON `{"pending":int,"claimed":int,"soaking":int}` derived from the queue reducer over a seeded store — exact counts asserted); `test_done_enrich_registered` (`DONE_ENRICH in event_append.EVENT_TYPES` — the S4-prerequisite guard); `test_always_mode` (with `overlap_drain="always"`, a write-path `maybe_drain` runs the drain SYNCHRONOUSLY inline — no detached child — and the entry is processed before the call returns; the CI/test mode); `test_cli_dispatch` (`rebar enrich status` routes through the `_cli/__init__.py` intercept and returns 0); `test_config` (sets `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS`; `LLMConfig.from_env()` resolves them; an invalid `overlap_drain` value falls back to the default).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar enrich --drain` processes up to `DRAIN_BATCH` (default 5) soaked+unclaimed entries then exits; backlog drains over successive runs; `pytest ...::test_batch_cap`.
- [ ] `maybe_drain` no-ops with no spawn when nothing soaked, within `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS` (20 ms); detaches a surviving child otherwise; `::{test_gate_latency}`.
- [ ] A single `enrich` failure releases the claim, logs, and the batch continues; the ticket re-drains later; `::test_enrich_error_continues`. Self-healing fallback picks up cert-without-fresh-digest tickets; `::test_self_heal`.
- [ ] `[agents]`/key absent → clean no-op; `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off` disables the opportunistic drain (single canonical env name); `::{test_no_key_noop,test_opt_out}`.
- [ ] Detach is `os.name`-branched and POSIX-only in v1: POSIX `start_new_session`; the Windows `DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW` branch is authored (referenced only in the nt branch) but `maybe_drain` no-ops on Windows — no child is spawned, because `lock.py`'s unconditional `fcntl` import would crash a Windows drain child; `::{test_windows_detach_kwargs,test_windows_noop}`. Each processed ticket gets a `DONE_ENRICH` append + a `prune` of its queue events (bounding growth); verified by `::test_batch_cap` observing DONE + a post-drain pending count of 0.
- [ ] `rebar enrich status` prints JSON `{"pending":int,"claimed":int,"soaking":int}` with the mutually-exclusive bucket predicates defined above (soaking = not-yet-past-soak; claimed = live lease; pending = past-soak unclaimed-or-expired) computed from `queue.reduce_ticket`; `::test_status`.
- [ ] Concurrent drain PROCESSES don't double-work: a second drain with the advisory `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` held exits 0 silently (logged), without waiting or processing — distinct from the store write lock and the optimistic queue-claim; `::test_lock_held_skip`.
- [ ] `overlap_drain` (`off|async|always`), `overlap_drain_batch`, `overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms` are read from the env by `LLMConfig.from_env()` (invalid `overlap_drain` → default); `DONE_ENRICH` is registered (by S4) before drain writes; `::{test_config,test_done_enrich_registered}`.
- [ ] `overlap_drain="always"` runs the drain synchronously inline (no detached child), processing the entry before the write returns; `::test_always_mode`. `rebar enrich` is routed via the `_cli/__init__.py` dispatch intercept; `::test_cli_dispatch`.
- [ ] The prune step retains exactly the latest queue event per ticket (the `DONE_ENRICH` tombstone), dropping superseded `ENQUEUE_ENRICH`/`CLAIM_ENRICH`/older `DONE_ENRICH` (keep=1, bounded growth); verified by `::test_batch_cap` (post-drain per-ticket queue-event count == 1).
baseline.summary: Tier-1 opportunistic detached drain + `rebar enrich` CLI

## Context / Problem

`next_batch` returns a ticket as available for work while `ticket_deps` reports that same ticket has open blockers and `ready_to_work: false`. The two readiness answers disagree, and `next_batch` is the one agents are told to use to pick work, so an agent following it can claim a ticket whose prerequisites have not landed.

## Reproduction

Observed 2026-09-01 on the live store, epic `spin-cub-usher` (`65dd-e93b-666a-4caa`).

The epic's ADR child `eaved-lighted-hedgehog` (`a5bf-c1f8-3950-4f87`) was linked with two prerequisite edges recorded from the prerequisite side:

```
link modern-loathful-snake        eaved-lighted-hedgehog blocks
link divinatory-offensive-groundhog eaved-lighted-hedgehog blocks
```

Both prerequisites are open. Then:

- `ticket_deps eaved-lighted-hedgehog` returns
  `{"deps": [], "blockers": ["1cef-7fbc-e402-467c", "5169-ab69-9c23-4f8b"], "ready_to_work": false}`
- `next_batch spin-cub-usher` returns that same `a5bf-c1f8-3950-4f87` inside `batch`, with
  `available_pool: 2`, and does not list it under any `skipped_*` key.

Expected: a ticket with an open blocker is excluded from `batch` (it belongs in a skipped bucket). Actual: it is offered as available work.

## Root cause

`src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` derives readiness solely from a ticket's OUTGOING `depends_on` relations. At `next_batch.py:176-182` it builds `open_depends_on` by filtering that ticket's own `deps` for `relation == "depends_on"` and skips the ticket only when that list is non-empty; the blocked-id set at `next_batch.py:220-228` applies the same outgoing-`depends_on` test.

A `blocks` edge recorded from the prerequisite (`A blocks B`) leaves B with an INBOUND edge and no outgoing `depends_on`, so B passes both filters. `ticket_deps` computes `blockers` from the inbound direction and therefore disagrees.

This matters because both link directions are sanctioned: `AGENTS.md` documents `blocks` and `depends_on` as two of the canonical relations, and the brainstorm/authoring guidance tells authors to "record their parent and prerequisite relationships with `blocks` or `depends_on`". Only one of those two spellings is honored by the scheduler.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py` readiness derivation, plus its tests. The fix is to treat an open inbound `blocks` edge as blocking, exactly as `ticket_deps` already does — not to change the link vocabulary or the recorded edges.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ticket_deps`, which is the surface that already answers correctly.
- Altering blocking-link promotion or the link relation vocabulary.
- Reworking the file-impact conflict scheduling in the same module.

## Compatibility and rollback

Behavior-narrowing: tickets that were previously offered while blocked stop being offered. No stored data or event shape changes, so back-out is reverting the readiness predicate. Any consumer relying on the current over-permissive batch would have been scheduling unclaimable work.

## Testing

Unit tests against the real `next_batch_state` over a temporary store seeded with a prerequisite pair, covering both edge spellings and the symmetry with `ticket_deps`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A ticket whose only prerequisite edge is an inbound `blocks` from an OPEN ticket is
      absent from `batch` and present in a skipped bucket; verified by `pytest` over a
      seeded temporary store asserting the returned `batch` ids.
- [x] The same ticket becomes available once that prerequisite closes; verified by `pytest`
      asserting it appears in `batch` after the blocker transitions to closed.
- [x] `next_batch` and `ticket_deps` agree for every child of a seeded epic: no id appears in
      `batch` while `ticket_deps` reports `ready_to_work: false`; verified by `pytest`
      asserting the intersection is empty.
- [x] The existing outgoing-`depends_on` behavior is unchanged; verified by `pytest` over a
      seeded pair using `depends_on`, asserting the same exclusion as before.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the live reproduction above no longer offers `a5bf-c1f8-3950-4f87` while its blockers are open.
baseline.summary: next_batch schedules a blocked ticket: readiness ignores inbound blocks edges

# Concurrent reducer cache writers can publish a current hash with stale state

## Context and authoritative intent

The reducer cache is a rebuildable optimization over deterministic event replay. `write_cache` promises an atomic cache publication, the cache invalidation tests require a newly added event to be reflected, and the original plan-review fan-out epic `sulky-pane-flag` requires concurrency without fidelity regression.

The report originally attributed a cap=12 plan-review abort to the `.cache.json.tmp` rename race. Phase-1 experiments rejected that fatality claim for immutable gate snapshots: redundant writers log caught warnings but do not escape or corrupt the equal result. The confirmed defect is reachable when concurrent reductions observe different event generations.

## Proven root cause

Two reducer cache writers use the same fixed `.cache.json.tmp` artifact: `write_cache` in `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py` and corrupt-CREATE handling in `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`. Overlapping writers can hold file descriptors to the same inode; after one renames it into place, another can keep mutating the now-visible final file. Runtime proof through real `reduce_ticket` appended an EDIT between old-generation and new-generation reductions and produced a valid cache with the current hash but stale `authorship`. A subsequent normal reduction returned the stale cached state without replay. Serialized controls produced no false hits.

## Repair plan

1. Replace `write_cache` fixed-temp publication with the canonical `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write`, preserving the surrounding best-effort OSError handling.
2. Route the inline corrupt-CREATE cache publication in `process_create` through `write_cache`, so every reducer cache writer shares the isolated same-directory temp, atomic replace, cleanup, and failure policy.
3. Extend the canonical tracker gitignore ensure-registry for `atomic_write` private cache temp names and pin that registry/staging contract.
4. Add deterministic threaded reducer regressions through the real cache seam: capture coherent old/new states around a controlled event append, release at least eight writers, and assert the current-hash read equals a cache-bypassing replay oracle. Add an immutable-writer control and a corrupt-CREATE writer control so no fixed `.cache.json.tmp` writer remains.
5. Run the focused reducer/cache and init/gitignore suites, then lint and typecheck.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Concurrent reductions of different event generations publish only complete coherent envelopes; a current-hash cache hit equals cache-bypassing deterministic replay.
- [x] At least eight concurrent reductions of one immutable ticket complete without `FileNotFoundError` cache-write warnings.
- [x] The normal and corrupt-CREATE cache paths both publish through the canonical `atomic_write` mechanism.
- [x] Publication failure cleanup leaves no private cache temp files.
- [x] Every private cache temp artifact shape is covered by the canonical tracker gitignore/ensure-registry contract.
- [x] A `git add -A` staging probe excludes every private cache temp artifact shape.
- [x] Cache publication failure is logged and does not prevent independently replayed ticket state from returning.
- [x] Focused reducer/cache and init/gitignore tests pass.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
baseline.summary: Concurrent reducer cache writers can publish a current hash with stale state

## Context / Problem

`rebar claim` (via `claim_gate_check` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py`, which calls `signing.verify_signature` -> `verify_opcert_record` in `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`) unconditionally rejected a plan-review op-cert whose `principal` differed from the local environment's `own_principal`, returning `verdict: "foreign_key"` and refusing the claim — before any trust root was built, and without consulting `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` or the enforcement config keys.

Reproduced 2026-08-28: `review_plan` run through the rebar MCP server (principal `9f1c8e42-…`) signed and returned a genuine PASS. The subsequent `rebar claim` from this checkout's local CLI/venv (principal `b8a354e0-…`) failed with `foreign_key`. Re-running `review-plan` locally succeeded, confirming the attestation itself was valid — only the environment mismatch blocked it.

## Operator policy decision (authoritative — do not re-litigate against the docs)

> "Certification environment should not currently be a gate. Any certification is as good as any
> other certification right now. Limited to a trusted set of environments is a future feature, but
> not currently in use."

Several docs (`docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`) encode the *future* trusted-set restriction as if it were live policy. **That encoding is the defect**, in code and in docs alike. Direct precedent: bug `stuffed-custommade-nuthatch` (846b) made exactly this call for the bugfix-size gate — gate on the FACT of certification, never on its SOURCE.

## Design

**`src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py`** — add `embedded_public_key(signature)`: parse the armored SSHSIG blob (`MAGIC || version || publickey || namespace || reserved || hash_alg || signature`) and return the signer's own public half as an `authorized_keys` line. Every SSHSIG blob carries it. This is NOT `-Y check-novalidate` (still never used): the key is fed to the normal `-Y verify` path, so the signature, the namespace, and the principal binding are all still checked in full.

**`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`** — replace the unconditional foreign-principal short-circuit in `verify_opcert_record` with:

1. `_required_environment(repo_root)` — reads `verify.require_environment` (unset here). When SET,
   a cert from any other environment is still `foreign_key`: the deferred future feature is
   preserved, not deleted. Fails OPEN on an unreadable config, so a broken `rebar.toml` cannot
   silently turn a restriction ON that the operator never configured.
2. `_opcert_trust_root(...)` — pick the strongest available key and LABEL it: `own_key` (this
   environment is the signer) -> `pinned_environment` (`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`) ->
   `envelope_key` (the signer's own embedded key). Under enforcement the `envelope_key` fallback is
   WITHHELD, so enforcement binds to the pinned key and never to a key the certificate supplies
   about itself.
3. Surface the chosen basis as a new `trust_basis` result field.

### The unobtainable-signer-key decision, made explicitly

`docs/plan-review-gate.md` argued there is "no coherent middle where signatures are checked but unpinned signers are waved through". That names the real trade-off but is mechanically wrong: an SSHSIG blob carries its own public key, so an unpinned signer's signature *can* be fully checked — just not tied to a KNOWN environment. **Chosen: accept on self-consistency, with the weaker basis made visible** (`trust_basis: "envelope_key"`) rather than silently folded into `certified`. A key that cannot be obtained at all (no own key, nothing pinned, nothing parsable in the envelope) is `foreign_key` with a reason naming that — never a silent pass.

**Not loosened:** the signature itself. A forged/altered envelope is still `mismatch`; `unsigned` keeps its meaning; subject binding (ticket + kind) is untouched.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py` — the policy change.
- `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py` — `embedded_public_key`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` — document `trust_basis`, narrow `foreign_key`.
- `docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`,
  `docs/reuse-surface.md`, `docs/concurrency.md`, `infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md` —
  state current policy; mark the trusted-set restriction future + opt-in.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py` (new), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: With `verify.require_environment`/`opcert_enforce_since` unset, `rebar claim` accepts a certified plan-review attestation signed by a different registered environment (no `foreign_key` denial).
- [x] AC2: With `verify.require_environment` + `opcert_enforce_since` both set, a cert from an environment other than the required one is still rejected, and the required environment must verify against its PINNED key (no envelope-key fallback under enforcement).
- [x] AC3: A regression test in `tests/unit/` covers both the advisory (AC1) and enforced (AC2) configurations for the claim-gate path specifically (not just `verify-opcert`). Cross-environment cases are constructed for real — a distinct Ed25519 key under a distinct principal — never by mocking the principal comparison away.
- [x] AC4: A negative control proves only identity was loosened: a forged envelope (signed content rewritten) is still `mismatch`, and a key substitution under a pinned environment is still `mismatch`.
- [x] AC5: `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and the other docs that asserted the old rule state the current policy and mark the trusted-set restriction as a future, opt-in feature.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py` — 10 cases: cross-environment acceptance, the
  claim gate specifically, the pinned-key basis, four negative controls, and both enforcement-on
  directions. RED-first; 7 seeded mutants all killed.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py` — the two cases that pinned the old rule updated to
  the new policy (coverage kept, not deleted).
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`.
baseline.summary: Claim gate hard-rejects cross-environment plan-review op-certs even when environment enforcement is not configured
