# Land PR #128 safe subset via Gerrit: json-repair 0.63.0 + genai-prices 0.1.2 + botocore 1.43.69; mcp 2.0 deferred to 732b (4th re-proposal)

## Context / Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot PRs never merge there; content is re-applied locally and landed via Gerrit, then the PR is closed. PR #128 (branch `dependabot/uv/uv-lock-bfcc8af838`) proposes 4 uv-lock updates:

* `mcp` `1.29.0` -> `2.0.0` (MAJOR) — the FOURTH re-proposal (PRs #124/#125/#127),
  rejected each time under ticket 1dfd-…: mcp 2.0 renames `FastMCP` -> `MCPServer`,
  replaces transport+`ClientSession`+`initialize()` with `Client`, splits types into
  `mcp-types`, and diverts stdout while serving — all breaking for `mcp_server.py` +
  `gen_mcp_reference.py`. Migration is epic `732b-51df-acf2-477b`; the pyproject
  ceiling stays `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` (core L22 floor via `[mcp]` extra L82 + agents L215).
  NEW urgency fact (recorded on 732b as part of this work): v2.0.0 is now the STABLE
  release and v1.x is in maintenance mode (security fixes only), so `<2` is
  time-bounded — but that changes the epic's priority, not this ticket's scope.
* `json-repair` `0.62.0` -> `0.63.0` (minor) — SAFE. Usage surface:
  `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` calls `repair_json(cand, return_objects=True[, schema=…])`
  (L387-408); 0.63.0 adds None->null repair + fixes a `TrueBlue` mis-repair — both
  strictly improve the tolerant-parse ladder; the called API is unchanged. pyproject
  floor `json-repair>=0.61` (L132) already admits it: LOCK-ONLY.
* `genai-prices` `0.1.1` -> `0.1.2` (patch) — SAFE. Pricing-data-only additions (new
  model prices); consumed via optional lazy import in `usage_report.py`/`usage_log.py`
  (`Usage` + `calc_price`, unchanged). pyproject has no pin (L150): LOCK-ONLY.
* `botocore` `1.43.68` -> `1.43.69` (patch) — SAFE. Routine service-model update;
  lazy imports only (`bedrock_model.py`, `structured.py`, `remote_cert.py`). Floor
  `botocore>=1.43.0` (L291) admits it; boto3 1.43.68's botocore range (`<1.44`)
  accepts 1.43.69, so boto3 itself need not move: LOCK-ONLY.

This ticket lands the three safe bumps only. No new mcp migration ticket is filed — epic 732b already owns it (per the #125/#127 precedent, tickets carnivoral-consistent-lhasaapso and reclinable-ammonitic-hound / change 1812).

## Approach

In a fresh worktree branched from `origin/main` (`../deps-128`, venv on PATH):

1. NO pyproject.toml edit — verify with `git diff` that all three bumps are admitted
   by existing constraints (floors listed above; exact pins exist for none of them).
2. `uv lock --upgrade-package json-repair --upgrade-package genai-prices
   --upgrade-package botocore` — the lock is regenerated by uv, never hand-edited
   (CI gates on `uv lock --check`); then `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra agents`
   so gates run against the bumped versions.
3. Verify the lock moved exactly the three intended packages to the PR's versions
   (0.63.0 / 0.1.2 / 1.43.69) and `mcp` stayed 1.29.0; `git diff uv.lock` must show
   no other version churn beyond uv's transitive bookkeeping for these three.
4. Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `uv lock --check`, and targeted tests for
   each usage surface: `pytest tests/unit/test_structured.py
   tests/unit/test_silent_success.py tests/unit/test_usage_log.py
   tests/unit/test_usage_log_pricing_qualified_2ca9.py` (json-repair + genai-prices
   consumers) plus `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` if present (botocore lazy
   import). Full `pytest tests/unit` is CI's job (host has pre-existing env git
   failures documented on dc89-cd11-acd6-4e61); CI Verified +1 is the authoritative
   full-suite gate.
5. Commit (subject <=50 chars, body wrapped at 72) with trailer
   `rebar-ticket: <this ticket's full canonical id>` + DCO `-s`;
   `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`. Leave the ticket in_progress for the bots;
   the change is submitted only after LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.
6. Comment on PR #128 (mcp rejected again per 732b, citing #124/#125/#127; safe
   subset landing via the new Gerrit change); comment the v2-stable/v1-maintenance
   urgency fact on epic 732b. Do NOT close the PR.

7. SCOPE ADDITION (operator-approved 2026-08-15): stop the recurring mcp 2.0
   re-proposals at the intake source. In .github/dependabot.yml's uv block, add
   an ignore rule: dependency-name "mcp", update-types
   ["version-update:semver-major"] — scoped to semver-major ONLY so 1.x
   patch/security bumps still flow and security alerts stay on. Append a
   one-line rationale to the header comment block: mcp major pinned out per
   epic 732b-51df-acf2-477b (fastmcp import removal); remove the ignore when
   the migration epic lands. Same commit as the safe-subset bump (same
   intake-noise lane).

## STOP / defer rule (explicit fallback done-state)

If ANY of the three bumps fails its targeted tests or lint/typecheck in step 4: drop ONLY that package from the bump (re-run `uv lock --upgrade-package …` with the remaining packages from a clean `git checkout uv.lock`), record the failure evidence as a ticket comment, and land the remaining safe packages. The fallback done-state is AC2b: the ticket closes legitimately with a PARTIAL subset landed, provided every dropped package has a recorded-on-ticket failure reason. If ALL three fail, no lock change is pushed, but the dependabot.yml ignore rule (step 7 / AC7) still lands — as a standalone change carrying only .github/dependabot.yml — so the done-state is that standalone change merged plus the recorded failure evidence; the ticket then closes on AC2b's evidence path with zero lock bumps landed and AC7 satisfied.

## Out of scope

* mcp 2.0 migration (epic 732b) — the ceiling `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` is untouched.
* boto3 version bump — not in PR #128 and not required by botocore 1.43.69.
* Any src/rebar code change — nothing in the three deltas requires one.
* `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — never touched by a deps change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: `uv.lock` on merged main records json-repair 0.63.0, genai-prices 0.1.2,
  botocore 1.43.69 (or a documented AC2b subset), with mcp still 1.29.0 and
  pyproject.toml unchanged; `uv lock --check` exits 0.
- [x] AC2: targeted usage-surface tests pass against the bumped versions
  (test_structured.py, test_silent_success.py, test_usage_log.py,
  test_usage_log_pricing_qualified_2ca9.py), and `make lint` + `make typecheck`
  exit 0.
- [x] AC2b (fallback path): every package dropped under the STOP rule has a ticket
  comment recording the concrete failure evidence and the re-lock excluding it; the
  landed subset satisfies AC1 for the packages it retains. (Vacuously satisfied when
  all three land.)
- [x] AC3: the change lands through Gerrit with a `rebar-ticket:` trailer for this
  ticket's full canonical id + DCO sign-off, after LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.
- [x] AC4: PR #128 carries a comment citing epic 732b + prior PRs #124/#125/#127 for
  the mcp rejection and pointing at the Gerrit change; the PR is left open.
- [x] AC5: epic 732b-51df-acf2-477b carries a comment recording that mcp v2.0.0 is
  the stable release and v1.x is maintenance-mode (security fixes only), i.e. the
  `<2` ceiling is now time-bounded.
- [x] AC6: this ticket records a relates_to link to dc89-cd11-acd6-4e61
  (reclinable-ammonitic-hound, the #127 precedent).
- [x] AC7: .github/dependabot.yml's uv block carries the mcp semver-major
  ignore rule (patch/minor still flow; security alerts unaffected) and the
  header comment records the 732b rationale + the removal trigger.
baseline.summary: deps: PR #128 safe subset (json-repair 0.63.0, genai-prices 0.1.2, botocore 1.43.69); mcp 2.0 deferred to 732b

## Context / Problem

ADR 0056 already extracted `interpret_failure`, settings/usage builders, Agent kwargs, success logging, spend recording, and the provider session guard. ADR 0058 later removed per-file headroom assertions and made the locked 800-LOC module limit the only LOC ceiling. Current `origin/main` nevertheless has a 785-line `runner.py` and a 388-line `PydanticAIRunner.run()`.

This second pass must identify an ownership improvement in today's call graph. It must not repeat prior extraction, duplicate `ProviderSession` or `ExitStack`, introduce a generic hook/plugin bus, revive rejected frozen carriers without new evidence, or add a function-size ratchet.

## Approach

- Map the exact effect/resource timeline: event-loop displacement; config/preflight; tracing; provider/session construction; model/fallback scope; capability/cache/web settings; Agent execution; failure accounting; answer attribution; pre-finalization logging; finalization; run-shape/spend recording.
- Inventory semantic references plus string imports, monkeypatch targets, compatibility re-exports, globals mutated by alias, and tests that inspect source.
- Build a fault matrix for every raising boundary and identify the current owner of cleanup, accounting, provenance, and error translation.
- Compare candidate seams against `providers`, `model_classes`, `structured_run`, `agent_call`, `runner_support`, and ADRs 0056/0058. Prefer strengthening an existing owner.
- Record the ADR disposition before implementation. If the structure changes an accepted decision, complete the full ADR lifecycle.
- "No change is the right answer" is a licensed outcome of this research: if the census and fault matrix show the current decomposition already keeps every seam with a single, correct owner (ADR 0056 decision 4 argues `_check_tool_capability` and the fallback/capability sequencing must stay in `run()`'s body), the record states that conclusion and its evidence instead of manufacturing a marginal seam to satisfy this ticket.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, `agent_call.py`, `structured_run.py`, `providers.py`, `model_classes.py`, and `runner_support.py`.
- Runner/provider/cache/fallback/telemetry tests under `tests/unit/` and `tests/interfaces/`.
- `docs/adr/0056-*.md`, `docs/adr/0058-*.md`, and one new/amending ADR only if the research changes an accepted boundary.

## Testing

Build the fault matrix as executable characterization where possible. Happy path records the current effect/telemetry order. Each edge injects a raise at one boundary and observes resource closure, failure accounting, provenance, and downstream effects. Red-prove any proposed new guard against a deliberately broken local variant before treating it as useful.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The research record names every effect/resource boundary, its owner, its required ordering, and the observed behavior when it raises.
- [x] Semantic and text/string consumer censuses agree or every discrepancy is explained; monkeypatch and compatibility hazards are assigned to the change that moves/removes them.
- [x] A red-capable fault matrix covers raises before/after provider creation, fallback entry, external execution, finalization, and telemetry/accounting.
- [x] The selected design states exactly which existing module/class/function gains responsibility and which code is deleted; it does not create a second session owner or generic lifecycle framework.
- [x] Mutable provenance/settings and post-call answer attribution are modeled as the call graph actually treats them: the record states, for each, whether it is constructed once and read-only thereafter or mutated after construction, and any proposed seam keeps a mutated value mutable (no decorative frozen/immutable carrier wrapped around a value the call graph still mutates post-construction).
- [x] No function-NLOC ratchet, per-file headroom assertion, or new hard size threshold is proposed. Size measurements may be reported as advisory debt signals only.
- [x] The research critique identifies unanswered assumptions and conflicts; any necessary ADR amendment is explicitly approved/merged before implementation, or the record explains why ADR 0056 already authorizes the seam.
- [x] This ticket states explicitly, before close, which of two outcomes applies: (a) research-only — the record concludes no restructuring is warranted (or the identified improvement is deferred to a named, `discovered_from`-linked follow-on ticket), and this ticket closes on the research record and any characterization tests added under Testing above, with no further production change required; or (b) implemented — a selected seam is actually applied to the Scope's source files and `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces` (scoped at least to the llm/runner/provider/telemetry suites) is green before close. The record names which outcome occurred and why.
baseline.summary: Revalidate PydanticAIRunner lifecycle ownership against current architecture

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The plan-review gate re-reviews a ticket's plan on entry into `in_progress`, including EXECUTION-phase re-reviews (a claimed ticket re-reviewed before close). At execution time a Pass-1 finder can flag a plan-vs-code discrepancy that is actually the *expected* result of the plan's own directed work already having been done: the plan directs "remove X", the agent removed X, and the re-review flags "the plan references X but no symbol X exists". During a PLANNING review that is a legitimate true positive; during an EXECUTION review it is a false positive that can block a correct, completed ticket from closing. Pass-2 has no way to drop it.

## Approach

Add a single-answer Pass-2 VETO, mirroring the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto, that drops such a finding only during an execution-phase review. A new plan-review-only binary sub-answer `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` (na-default, OUTSIDE `GRADED_BINARY` so it never affects validity arithmetic) is set by the verifier via a present-state check: does the code AS IT IS NOW already satisfy the plan's directed end state? `pass3_decide` drops the finding (`reason="veto:plan-goal-satisfied"`) only when a keyword-only `execution_review` flag is True AND the answer is a definite `yes`. The `execution_review` phase signal ALREADY flows from `decide_ops` into `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings`; this change adds the kernel-level `execution_review` kwarg (on `pass3_decide` and `review_kernel.pass3_over_findings`) and forwards the existing orchestrator flag into that kernel call. The kwarg defaults False, so planning reviews and every code-review call are byte-unchanged.

Because a definite `yes` is a PRESENT-STATE code check that only the code-grounded verifier can actually perform, the veto is COHORT-RESTRICTED to `registry.CODEBASE_GROUNDED` — the set `{E4, G1G2, A1, G6, asserted-capability}`. This is analogous in intent to the `asserted_capability_confirmed` cohort restriction (a code-grounded gate), though it uses a DIFFERENT cohort set (`asserted_capability_confirmed`'s cohort is G6/E4/T3, not CODEBASE_GROUNDED). It is enforced deterministically in the plan-review wrapper (`_restrict_on_target_veto_to_grounded` forces the answer to `na` for any finding outside the cohort before delegating to the kernel), not only by prompt, so a tool-less single-turn verification can never fire the veto.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py` — add the na-default plan-review-only binary.
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` — add the `execution_review` kwarg to `pass3_decide` +
  `pass3_over_findings`; add the veto branch.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — forward `execution_review` into the kernel call
  and enforce the code-grounded cohort restriction (`_restrict_on_target_veto_to_grounded`).
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md`,
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` — document the sub-answer + cohort.
- `tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — tests.

## Testing

- Happy path: `execution_review=True` + code-grounded finding + `yes` at full validity/impact
  ⇒ dropped with `reason="veto:plan-goal-satisfied"`.
- Edge (planning preserved): same finding with `execution_review=False` ⇒ NOT dropped.
- Edge (definite-yes only): `no`/`insufficient`/`na`/absent under execution ⇒ NOT dropped.
- Edge (cohort restriction): a finding whose criteria are NOT in `registry.CODEBASE_GROUNDED`
  with `yes` under execution ⇒ NOT dropped (the wrapper forces it to `na`); a grounded finding
  with the same answer ⇒ dropped.
- Contract: the plan-review verification model carries the field, it is na-default, and it is
  absent from `GRADED_BINARY` and from the base/code-review models.
- RED/GREEN verified against the source diff; the decide veto branch is mutation-tested.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A code-grounded Pass-2 finding with `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal="yes"` is dropped
  with `reason="veto:plan-goal-satisfied"` when `pass3_decide` runs with `execution_review=True`,
  even at validity 1.0 and impact 1.0.
- [x] The same finding is NOT dropped when `execution_review=False` (planning-phase true
  positive preserved).
- [x] Under `execution_review=True`, answers `no`, `insufficient`, `na`, and an absent key do
  NOT drop the finding.
- [x] Under `execution_review=True`, a finding whose criteria are NOT in
  `registry.CODEBASE_GROUNDED` is NOT dropped even when its answer is `yes` (cohort restriction
  enforced in `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings`), while a grounded finding IS dropped.
- [x] `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` is present on the plan-review verification model,
  defaults to `"na"`, and is NOT a member of `GRADED_BINARY`; the base and code-review models do
  not carry it.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass. [operator-attested]
baseline.summary: Execution-phase Pass-2 on-target veto for completed-work false positives

baseline.description:
`rebar review-plan` reports `signature` present (the JSON `signature` field is non-null, and batch tooling reads `signed=True`) even when the **verdict is BLOCK**. The documented contract is that it "signs a plan-review attestation on a **non-blocking PASS**" — so a BLOCK verdict should NOT carry a passing signed attestation. Either the signing-on-BLOCK is a bug, or the `signature` field means something other than "passing attestation"; either way it is misleading, because the signature is meant to be the trustworthy proof-of-PASS that downstream gates (the claim gate) and CI rely on. A consumer that checks "is there a signature?" to decide claimability would be misled by a signed BLOCK.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Author a ticket whose plan trips a blocking criterion (or use any ticket the four-pass gate
   BLOCKs).
2. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json` (default source = attested, signing on).
3. Inspect the result JSON: `verdict` and `signature`.

## Expected
- On `verdict == BLOCK`, no passing attestation is signed — `signature` is null/absent (or the
  field is unambiguously labeled as a non-passing attestation), so "has signature" reliably
  means "passed".

## Actual
- Observed repeatedly this session: tickets with `verdict=BLOCK` returned `signature` populated
  (`signed=True`). Concretely, Round-2/3/4 runs on the S4/S6/S7 d251 children showed e.g.
  `s6: BLOCK block=6 ... signed=True` and `s4: BLOCK block=2 ... signed=True` — a signature on a
  BLOCK.

## Notes
- Inferred from the JSON `signature` field, not the signing internals — possible the field is
  populated-but-not-a-passing-attestation; that distinction is exactly what's unclear and should
  be made explicit. Surfaced while dogfooding the plan-review gate on epic d251 (alto-fruit-punch).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar review-plan <id>` on a BLOCK verdict does NOT emit a passing signed attestation
      (either `signature` is null/absent on BLOCK, or the field/type is explicitly distinct from
      a passing attestation and documented as such).
- [x] `verify_signature` / the claim gate cannot be satisfied by an attestation produced on a
      BLOCK verdict (a BLOCKed plan is never claimable on the strength of its signature).
- [x] The behavior is documented (docs/plan-review-gate.md): exactly when a signature is emitted
      and what its presence guarantees.
- [x] A regression test asserts: BLOCK verdict -> no passing signature; PASS verdict -> signature present.
baseline.summary: plan-review: signed attestation emitted on BLOCK verdict (signature should certify PASS only)

baseline.description: test_narrow_operation_persists_the_same_bytes_as_the_legacy_sequence (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_rich_reemit_state.py) asserts byte-equality between two independently-saved reconciler stores. The saved JSON embeds created_at/updated_at wall-clock timestamps, so when the two save() calls straddle a 1-second boundary the bytes differ (observed on Gerrit change 2209 CI, ubuntu-latest py3.13: 'At index 72 diff: 4 != 3', created_at 06:04:43Z vs 06:04:44Z). Passed on py3.11/py3.12/macos-3.13 in the same run. Root cause: wall-clock dependency the check_wall_clock_asserts gate did not catch. Fix: freeze/inject a fixed clock across both stores' saves so timestamps are deterministic. Discovered while landing olm (MCP client configs); unrelated to that change.

baseline.description:
## Problem
Findings carry a `severity` string (`severity_label(impact)` -> critical/major/minor/none, `review_kernel/decide.py`) that is derived from IMPACT ALONE, so it does not order the same way as the authoritative `priority = validity x impact`. A high-impact/low-validity finding shows as `critical` while ranking below a `major`. This is a foot-gun: it invites reading the label as the gate signal when it is not. It also caused a field misread - via `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` (major->high, minor->medium, none->info) the review-bot surfaced the same finding as INFO then MEDIUM across identical runs, reading like a severity change when only impact drifted.

## Idea
Make findings blocking / not-blocking + numeric priority, mirroring the intent that priority is the single source of truth. Remove or rename the impact-only severity label so nothing mistakes it for the decision.

## Corrected scope (post-decomposition research)
The review-kernel (`pass3_decide`) stops STAMPING `severity` onto its own emitted findings, and every consumer of THOSE findings (aggregation/dedup where live, the Gerrit review-bot comment, the CLI renderers, the workflow gate) is migrated to `priority`/`decision` instead. This does NOT mean severity disappears everywhere: `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES`/`normalize_finding` vocabulary remains intact and untouched, because it also serves an entirely separate completion-verification module cluster (`completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`, `epic_bug_screen.py`, `workflow/gate_ops.py`, `workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py`) and the `spec_scan.py` "spec-alignment" reviewer -- neither of which ever computes `priority`/ `validity`/`impact`/`decision` and neither of which has anything to do with the impact-only severity_label bug this epic is fixing. Two research-driven corrections during decomposition: `aggregate.py::aggregate_findings` (originally named as a consumer) is confirmed dead code (no caller since ADR 0075) and needs no change; `workflow/steps.py`'s `gate`/`fail_on_severity` is not wired into any real production gate workflow (only a demo/sample and a test fixture use it) so its migration is additive (a new `priority_threshold` alongside `fail_on_severity`, not a replacement).

## Decomposition (each child independently reviewable, linear depends_on stack)
1. `pudgy-jolly-guppy` - ADR recording the decision (certified, closed, landed).
2. `uncheering-uncivil-pig` - assign fixed priority to DET-tier findings (secrets detector,
   bugfix-size gate) (closed, landed).
3. `beaming-snively-urial` - thread priority/decision through shim.py's `_to_common_finding`
   for the `review_result`/`review_code()` consumer (closed, landed). (`aggregate.py` and
   `spec_scan.py` are explicitly untouched -- see Corrected scope above.)
4. `patriotic-abdicative-arrowana` - fix `adapter.py::_translate_findings` to carry a
   `blocking: bool` (replacing a `severity` value nothing ever rendered), and update the CLI
   renderers that read `priority`/`decision`-bearing findings to show blocking/advisory
   instead of severity where such findings exist.
5. `camlet-exodermal-kodiakbear` - add a `priority_threshold` option to the (non-production,
   demo-only) `fail_on_severity` workflow gate policy, additive alongside the existing
   severity check.
6. `byzantine-spinelike-penguin` - stop the review-kernel from stamping `severity`; relax
   (not remove) the `severity` requirement on `review_result`'s schema-shared finding def
   (`completion_verdict`'s findings never come from the review-kernel, so its `severity` stays
   always-required and unaffected); remove the vestigial `BLOCKING_SEVERITIES` config and the
   duplicated `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`/`_SEVERITY_DEFAULT` machinery in `shim.py`; amend
   ADR 0108 to record this corrected, narrower scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All child tickets are closed, each behind its own `Verified +1` / `LLM-Review +1`
  Gerrit change (`git log --grep "rebar-ticket: <child-id>"` finds a landed commit per child).
- [x] No finding produced by the review-kernel (`pass3_decide`, code-review or plan-review)
  carries a `severity` key once ticket 6 lands (`grep -rn '"severity"' src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`
  finds no finding-shape references outside historical comments/docstrings). Findings from
  OTHER producers (completion-verification cluster, `spec_scan.py`) continue to carry
  `severity` unchanged -- this is intentional, not a residual gap.
- [x] Every review-kernel-produced finding (LLM-scored and DET-tier) carries a `priority`
  float and a `decision` (`block`/`advisory`) key, and both the Gerrit comment and the CLI
  renderers for review-kernel-sourced findings show only blocking/advisory tags, never a
  severity word.

## Provenance
Discovered from the upstream review-code false-positive report (client project). Sibling of the merge-base diff fix (ticket 8559-44c3-e08a-4bb9). Discovered work: ticket `broken-spirited-dorado` (spec_scan.py priority migration) was created then obsoleted once the corrected scope above was established -- see its ticket record for the reasoning.

## Context
Current recovery handles interrupted creates but not the retired-first/live-replace crash state where one exact identity remains both live and tombstoned. Recovery must never guess across mismatched identities.

## Outcome
Extract create recovery and add a pure interrupted-retirement classifier plus repository-backed completion operation behind the `BindingStore` facade. Do not invoke it automatically yet.

## Plan
1. Move keyed/keyless create recovery into `binding_recovery.py` without changing labels, immutable known-key behavior, three-miss plus 3600-second grace, failure tally, or continue behavior. Keep the facade's `recover_pending_bindings` signature and return value so the existing `run_differs.py` call site is untouched.
2. Build real fault-cut fixtures for a tombstone persisted before live replacement fails.
3. Classify retirement completion only when the tombstone, the live forward entry, and the live reverse entry agree on exact local id and Jira key.
4. Complete by removing the redundant live forward/reverse pair while retaining the tombstone; repeat is a no-op. Mismatch, corruption, or replace failure safety-aborts and retains evidence.

## Testing
Use fresh store reloads, identity-mismatch tables, replacement cuts, and keyed/keyless create-recovery regressions. The existing create-recovery suites (`test_write_ahead_recovery.py`, `test_recovery_loud_failures.py`, `test_index_lag_duplicate_heldout.py`, `test_identity_write_retention_heldout.py`) are the extraction's regression oracle and must pass unmodified; new tests add a direct-module tier rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Exact tombstone/forward/reverse overlap completes to coherent retired-only bytes while retaining the tombstone.
- [x] Repeating completion performs no write.
- [x] Any identity mismatch, corrupt live file, or replace failure retains evidence and returns a typed safety abort.
- [x] Keyed pending recovery performs no search.
- [x] Keyless pending recovery still requires both three misses and 3600 seconds, and one entry failure does not stop others.
- [x] The pre-existing create-recovery invocation gate is behaviorally unchanged by this move: it stays UNSCOPED-passes-only (guarded solely by `if not scoped_ids`) with no write-bearing/persist gate, and no new write-bearing or scope condition is attached to it.

## Out of scope
Automatic invocation boundary for retirement completion, rich-emission caller cutover, and ADR finalization.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Closing a **bug** ticket sprays `Error: Ambiguous prefix '<4hex>' matches multiple tickets` lines at the terminal and then leaves the CLI running for minutes after the close has already committed durably. Reproduced twice (2026-08-08, 2026-08-10) with fragments `b2bb`, `28f9`, `a9dd`, `dbb2`, `3e8b`, `03ef`, `94a3`, `c5b3`, `18ae`, `4527`; each time the operator had to interrupt the process after confirming the status change had landed.

This ticket originally attributed the noise to the enrichment drain. That is **wrong**, and the correction is recorded in a triage comment: the drain subtree (`_store/event_append.py:606` -> `llm/enrich_drain.py:216` -> `drain` -> `llm/enrich.py`) resolves only ticket ids that came from `os.listdir(tracker)`, i.e. already-canonical directory names that short-circuit on the fast path at `_ids.py:239-241` and never reach the prefix branch that prints. It has no prose scanner at all, and in async mode its stderr goes to `.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log`.

## Approach

Both symptoms are ONE defect in `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, the optional `caused_by` derivation invoked from `_commands/transition_close.py:246-248` **after** a bug close commits. `_find_fixing_commit` walks the entire branch history and calls `_resolves_to` per commit; `_resolves_to` re-resolves `bug_id` on **every** commit, and every candidate from `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs` (whose second source is the leading `<token>:` of the commit subject) is resolved with no `quiet=`, no cache, and no shape filter. Any candidate that is not a full/short/Jira id falls through to `_scan_alias`, which opens up to two JSON files for each ticket directory.

Measured on this checkout: 3823 ticket directories, 2137 commits, 620 of them carrying a bare `<4hex>:` subject (487 distinct), and ~0.26s per unresolvable candidate. The per-commit `bug_id` re-resolution alone is ~2137 x 0.26s ~= 9 minutes of pure alias scanning. That is the "hang": an unbounded O(commits x tickets) scan, not a deadlock.

Four changes, none of which alter WHICH id forms resolve:

1. Pass `quiet=True` at EVERY scanner call site in the module — `_resolves_to` (`blame.py:53`
   and `:55`), `_commit_ticket` (`:100`, the culprit commit's own subject), and the final
   self-comparison in `derive_caused_by` (`:135`) — using the seam `_ids.py:221-230` already
   documents for "scanners resolving candidates the user never supplied", the same treatment
   `_commands/close_precheck.py:119` already applies. Kills the terminal noise. All four are
   required: `_commit_ticket` is a SECOND scanner over commit-message candidates, so leaving it
   loud would keep a residual path that violates AC 1.
2. Hoist the `bug_id` resolution out of the per-commit loop (it is loop-invariant).
3. Memoize ref -> resolution for the duration of one derivation, as `close_precheck` does.
4. Short-circuit on a **necessary condition** before touching the store: a ref of hex-quad
   shape can only resolve to the target if the target's canonical id starts with it. This is
   provably semantics-preserving and is restricted to 1-, 2-, and 4-quad hex forms, which
   cannot collide with an alias (aliases are `adj-noun` or `adj-noun-noun` from the wordlist,
   or an 8-hex no-dash fallback) — 3-quad forms are deliberately excluded and still take the
   real resolver. Because that is a cross-module invariant owned by `_ids`/`_alias`, the guard
   carries a comment naming its source and a test asserts no generatable alias can take the
   hex-quad shape the short-circuit rejects, so the optimization cannot silently drift.

Separately, sweep the docs to stop advertising bare 4-digit (single-quad) references, per the operator decision: name alias (preferred), 8-digit two-quad prefix, full canonical id, and Jira/bridge ids as the reference forms. Compatibility resolution is unchanged and stays documented as compatibility.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py` — the four changes above.
- `tests/unit/` — new regression tests.
- `src/rebar/_ids.py` — **module docstring only** (no code change): it is the one place that
  literally advertises "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as a supported form.
- `AGENTS.md` — the ticket-identifier authoring paragraph (:66-73). It does NOT advertise a
  bare 4-digit form today (it already discourages copying a short hex prefix and already frames
  short forms as compatibility), so this is an ADDITION: positively name the preferred forms,
  including the 8-digit two-quad prefix, which the file never mentions.

A repo-wide survey found the advertising surface is small: those two places. The ~420 bare 4-hex mentions elsewhere in `docs/` are incidental HISTORICAL citations of specific tickets ("epic 716f", "bug 84aa"), not guidance telling a reader to use that form, so they are out of scope — rewriting them would be a large no-value diff. `docs/cli-reference.md:387` (`rebar resolve <id_or_alias_or_prefix>`) is generated from `src/rebar/_cli/help/resolve.txt` and says "prefix" generically, which correctly includes the PREFERRED 8-digit two-quad prefix, so it is left alone.

Explicitly NOT changed: `_ids.py` resolution semantics, `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs` (commit-subject candidates keep resolving exactly as today), the close gate, and the `Verified` trailer check. No id form gains or loses the ability to resolve.

## Testing

- A commit message whose subject is a bare `<4hex>:` prefix that matches multiple tickets
  produces **no** `Ambiguous prefix` text on stderr during `derive_caused_by`.
- A bounded-work test: over a synthetic history of many commits carrying distinct 4-hex
  subjects, the number of underlying `resolve_ticket_id` calls stays small and constant rather
  than growing with the commit count (asserted by counting calls through a patched resolver).
- Behavior preservation: `derive_caused_by` still finds the fixing commit and the culprit
  ticket when the commit cites the bug by full canonical id, by 8-hex two-quad prefix, by
  alias, and by an unambiguous bare 4-hex prefix.
- A ref that is a hex-quad shape but NOT a prefix of the target still returns "no match", and a
  3-quad hex form still reaches the real resolver.
- A culprit commit whose OWN subject is an ambiguous bare 4-hex prefix also produces no
  `Ambiguous prefix` text (the `_commit_ticket` path).
- An alias-shape guard test: no alias generatable from the wordlist can take the 1-, 2-, or
  4-quad hex shape the short-circuit rejects.
- Docs: an assertion-style check that the swept files no longer present bare 4-digit ids as a
  recommended reference form.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Closing a bug emits no `Ambiguous prefix` diagnostics for commit-subject candidates the
      user never supplied.
- [x] `derive_caused_by` performs work bounded by the number of DISTINCT candidate refs rather
      than re-resolving per commit, proven by a call-count regression test.
- [x] Every id form that resolves today still resolves: full canonical id, 8-hex two-quad
      prefix, alias, Jira key, and unambiguous bare 4-hex.
- [x] The original post-close reproduction, replayed as a regression test over a synthetic
      multi-commit history, emits no `Ambiguous prefix` text and resolves each DISTINCT ref at
      most once (no per-commit re-resolution of the bug id).
- [x] A regression test asserts that no alias generatable from the wordlist (`adj-noun`,
      `adj-noun-noun`, or the 8-hex no-dash fallback) can take the 1-, 2-, or 4-quad hex shape
      rejected by the short-circuit, so the optimization cannot silently drift.
- [x] `src/rebar/_ids.py`'s module docstring no longer presents "unique prefix >= 4 chars" as
      a plain supported form, and `AGENTS.md`'s ticket-identifier paragraph positively names the
      preferred forms (alias / 8-digit two-quad prefix / full canonical id / Jira ids) while
      retaining its existing compatibility framing.
baseline.summary: Enrichment drain treats unrelated short hex fragments as ticket prefixes and hangs post-write commands

baseline.description:
## Why
The record/fold path (S2) and read surface (S3) handle a single opaque session id, but a bare session id collides across tools (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor). To make the feature genuinely multi-harness, claims must also record WHICH harness produced the id, and the resolver must recognise the other OSS harness session vars.

## What
- **Resolver var-list extension (`src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py`).** Extend
  `_SESSION_ID_VARS` with the OSS harness var OpenCode ships, in popularity order between the
  Claude and ambient vars:
  `REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> OPENCODE_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID`.
  **Codex is deliberately NOT added as a native var:** story 7656 establishes that Codex
  exposes no supported readable session env var, so it is covered by its SessionStart shim
  exporting `REBAR_SESSION_ID` (not a `CODEX_THREAD_ID`). SAFETY: an absent or unrecognised var
  simply falls through (the resolver skips unset vars), so it degrades to a lower-precedence
  var or `None` — never an error.
- **Harness provenance tag.** Add `resolve_harness()` returning the opaque, rebar-owned
  `AI_AGENT` env var (verbatim, never interpolated) or `None`. `AI_AGENT` is rebar's
  harness-provenance convention, holding e.g. `claude-code_<ver>` / `opencode` / `codex` /
  `cursor`. **Population contract (closes the DOA gap):** the capture shims in stories S4
  (ec5c) and S6 (7656) are extended by THIS epic to export `AI_AGENT` alongside
  `REBAR_SESSION_ID`; until then `AI_AGENT` may also be set directly by an operator/hook. When
  unset, `claim_harness` folds to `None` (no error) — the feature degrades gracefully.
  On an `open -> in_progress` STATUS, stamp `data["harness"]` when present; fold to
  `state["claim_harness"]`. Each provenance field folds `data.get(<its key>)` INDEPENDENTLY on
  the edge (same fork-winner gating as `claimed_session`), so a re-claim clears `claim_harness`
  to `None` iff `AI_AGENT` is absent for THAT claim — independent of whether a session id is
  present.
- **Secondary remote session.** Add `resolve_remote_session()` returning
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` or `None`; stamp `data["remote_session"]` and fold to
  `state["claim_remote_session"]` (same gating). This is a secondary field, independent of the
  primary `claimed_session`.
- **State + schema + read surface.** Default `claim_harness` and `claim_remote_session` to
  `None` in `make_initial_state`; enumerate both in `ticket_state.schema.json` and (as compact
  keys `chn` / `rsn`) in `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` + `KEY_MAP` (+ docstring); add both to
  the MCP `TicketStateOut` model; regenerate `types.py`. `rebar show` JSON includes them
  automatically (state keys).
- **Existing-test updates.** Update `tests/unit/test_session_id.py` for the extended list:
  broaden its hardcoded `_ALL_VARS` tuple + autouse clear fixture to the 4 vars, and update
  `test_docs_document_unified_contract`'s exact-string assertion to the extended ordered
  contract (normalising whitespace so doc line-wrapping is irrelevant). Add an
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` precedence case, and a case asserting `CODEX_THREAD_ID` is NOT
  recognised (Codex has no native var).
- **Docs.** Extend `docs/config.md` (the ordered var list + `AI_AGENT` +
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`) and `docs/event-schema.md` (the `harness` / `remote_session`
  data keys -> `claim_harness` / `claim_remote_session` state). Env-var name provenance:
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (OpenCode-shipped) and `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (Codex convention) come from
  the epic OSS survey (Codex has no readable var, hence no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`); because an
  unrecognised name simply falls through, a wrong guess degrades to a lower-precedence var or
  `None` with no runtime error.

## Scope
- IN: resolver var-list extension + `resolve_harness` / `resolve_remote_session`; the write
  stamps + reducer folds for `claim_harness` / `claim_remote_session`; state defaults; both
  JSON schemas + `types.py` regen + `to_llm` keys + MCP model; docs; the existing
  `test_session_id.py` updates AND a NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py` module.
- OUT: the per-harness CAPTURE shims that POPULATE `REBAR_SESSION_ID` / `AI_AGENT` — Claude
  Code (S4 / ec5c) and Codex + Cursor (S6 / 7656), both extended by this epic to also export
  `AI_AGENT`. This story is the store/record side only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_session_id()` recognises `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` at its precedence, and does NOT
      recognise `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (Codex has no native var). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -k "opencode or codex" -q`.
- [ ] A claim records `claim_harness` (from `AI_AGENT`) in compiled state, distinguishing the
      source tool; absent `AI_AGENT` -> `None`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k harness -q`.
- [ ] `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`, when set, is captured as `claim_remote_session`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k remote -q`.
- [ ] Both fields default to `None` in `make_initial_state`, are enumerated in
      `ticket_state.schema.json` + `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` (`chn` / `rsn`), and appear
      in `TicketStateOut`; `types.py` is not stale. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k "schema or read" -q` and
      `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_public_types.py -q`.
- [ ] Fork-winner + session-less-clear semantics apply to both new fields (never the loser's;
      cleared to `None` on a provenance-less re-claim). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k fork -q`.
- [ ] `docs/config.md` and `docs/event-schema.md` document the extended var list, `AI_AGENT`,
      and the two new fields. Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k docs -q`
      asserts `docs/config.md` contains `AI_AGENT` and `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (Codex has no
      readable var, so there is intentionally no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`), AND `docs/event-schema.md`
      contains `claim_harness` and `claim_remote_session`.
- [ ] The existing `test_session_id.py` is updated for the extended list and stays green
      (4-var `_ALL_VARS` + clear fixture; unified-contract doc assertion updated). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -q`.
- [ ] A NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py` module is created covering the resolvers,
      write-stamp/fold, fork-winner + provenance-less-clear, schemas + read surface, and docs.

## Depends on
- S2 (68ef) record/fold path + S3 (199b) read surface — landed in this stack.
baseline.summary: Multi-harness session capture: extend resolver var-list + record harness provenance tag

## Reproduction Steps
Discovered during the fix for dying-verastile-quelea (the observability probe going stale). `install-certbot-timer.sh` materializes a host artifact (systemd timer + any /usr/local/bin helper) OUTSIDE the compose build context, exactly like `install-observability.sh`. The autodeploy loop only rebuilds the review-bot container (BOT_PATHS) and now re-materializes the observability probe (OBS_PATHS); it does NOT refresh the certbot timer when `infra/scripts/install-certbot-timer.sh` changes.

2. autodeploy advances `main` on the box but never re-runs the certbot installer.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a change to the certbot-timer installer is materialized on the box on next deploy.
- **Actual:** the installed certbot timer silently goes stale (same class as the observability bug).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] autodeploy re-materializes the certbot timer when `infra/scripts/install-certbot-timer.sh`
      (or its inputs) change between deployed..target — e.g. add it to a host-materialize trigger.
- [ ] A hermetic regression test asserts the installer is re-invoked on a certbot-source change.

      should also be covered, or is deliberately excluded.

baseline.description:
## The defect

`src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/scc_loc.py:41` builds the command:

    command = ["scc", "--format", "json", str(scan_root)]

It omits `--by-file`. Without that flag scc emits per-language SUMMARIES whose `Files` key is present but EMPTY (`"Files":[]`). `_parse_files` (:76) therefore raises nothing -- the key is a list, it is simply empty -- and iterates zero entries.

The adapter then returns `AnalyzerResult(loc={"files": {}, "max_loc": 0})` at :59.

## Why this is worse than a crash

It fabricates a CONFIDENT ZERO. `rebar metrics` reports:

    module_size_distribution: {"count": 0, "near_cap_count": 0, "over_cap_count": 0, "max_loc": 0}
    oversized_module_count: 0

A reader concludes this repository has no oversized modules. It has 729 analyzable files, the largest at 7011 lines. The metric is not merely wrong, it is wrong in the reassuring direction, and it carries `confidence: high` and `source: structural`.

This is precisely the failure epic 839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051 was created to ELIMINATE. Its motivating audit finding was that the old code_health readers "fabricated authoritative zeros for non-Python clients". The replacement stack fabricates authoritative zeros too, by a different mechanism.

## Verified, not inferred

With scc 3.7.0 on this machine, run from the repo root:

    scc --format json src/rebar          -> 9 language groups, every "Files" is []
    scc --by-file --format json src/rebar -> 729 file entries, max Code = 7011

Direct adapter call `scc_loc.analyze(Path('.'), ['src/rebar'])` returns AnalyzerResult with `files: 0, max_loc: 0`.

Note this was invisible until now because scc was not installed anywhere -- the metric reported `unavailable: scc executable is unavailable`, which is honest. Installing scc is what exposed the bug: an honest Unavailable became a dishonest zero.

## A second defect the fix will expose

With `--by-file` the largest entries are NOT source modules:

    7011  src/rebar/_engine/resources/ticket-wordlist-v2.txt
    2341  src/rebar/_engine/resources/ticket-wordlist.txt
    1932  src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js
    1528  src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/src/rebarProvider.jsx

So simply adding the flag makes `module_size_distribution` report max_loc 7011 from a word list. That does not match the module-size POLICY, which is about Python modules -- the CI gate counts only `src/rebar/**/*.py` against `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The two would report irreconcilable numbers for the same concept.

## OPERATOR RULING on AC3 -- match the CI gate via PER-PROJECT CONFIG, not a hardcoded filter

Recorded verbatim, because it decides the shape of the fix:

  "matching CI gate. the point of adoption was that it could be polyglot to support diverse
   clients. configuration for this project can be specific to this project's tech stack."

So the adapter does NOT get a Python-only filter baked into it. Epic 839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051's motivating finding was that the old readers hardcoded `src/rebar/**/*.py` and therefore fabricated zeros for non-Python clients; re-hardcoding a language in the replacement stack would recommit that exact defect one layer down. scc was adopted BECAUSE it is polyglot, and it stays polyglot. The file set is PER-PROJECT CONFIGURATION, and this project is configured to its own stack so its metric agrees with its own gate.

BINDING CONSTRAINT on any new knob: it MUST have a live read site and MUST be dogfooded in the same change. Ticket dce2-b93d-4112-451c was closed for the opposite -- `CodeHealthConfig. analyzers` shipped as config with no reader and rotted inert for six weeks. Idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2 records the operator's standing condition that selection must never ship as configuration alone. A new inert knob here would be the same mistake under a new name.

### Why the narrowing cannot live in `scan_roots` (checked first, as instructed)

`scan_roots` is a DIRECTORY axis: `_scan_roots` resolves each entry to a path and hands it to scc as the positional argument. The files that must be excluded are INTERLEAVED inside the directory that must be kept -- `src/rebar/_engine/resources/*.txt`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/*.js` and `.../src/*.jsx` all live under `src/rebar`. No set of directories can express "only Python files under src/rebar". The missing axis is file TYPE, orthogonal to the directory axis, so it needs its own expression.

## Plan

1. AC1 -- add `--by-file` to the scc argv.
2. AC2 (load-bearing) -- an empty aggregated file map returns `Unavailable` via the module's
   existing `_unavailable` helper, never a zero-valued `AnalyzerResult`. A zero must mean
   "measured zero", not "measured nothing". Every pre-existing unavailable path is unchanged.
3. AC3 -- add `code_health.include_extensions` (`list[str]`, default `[]` = polyglot, so
   behaviour is unchanged for every other client), read LIVE in `scc_loc.analyze` where it
   becomes scc's `--include-ext` argument, threaded `_commands/metrics.py` -> ctx ->
   `git_metrics._scc_analysis` and folded into that function's analysis cache key so two
   differently-narrowed runs cannot collide. Dogfooded in the SAME change via this repo's
   `rebar.toml` `[code_health]` table (`scan_roots = ["src/rebar"]`,
   `include_extensions = ["py"]`, `size_cap = 800`).
4. AC4 -- read scc's `Lines` (raw line count) rather than `Code` (which excludes blanks and
   comments). The CI gate measures `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l` against
   `.github/module-size-limit.txt`; scc's `Lines` equals `wc -l` exactly, measured at 0
   mismatches over all 435 files, so the metric reconciles with the gate BY CONSTRUCTION
   rather than leaving a documented gap. `size_cap = 800` is the same integer as the limit
   file, so `near_cap_count`/`over_cap_count` stop being null.
5. AC5 -- a regression, run against real scc, asserts a scan root that demonstrably contains
   files never produces a zero-valued result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The scc invocation includes `--by-file` (or whatever the installed scc requires) so file
      entries are actually returned; proven RED-first with a test that fails on the current argv.
- [x] An EMPTY file list is reported as `Unavailable`, never as a zero-valued AnalyzerResult --
      a zero must mean "measured zero", not "measured nothing". This is the load-bearing AC.
- [x] The file set is filtered so `module_size_distribution` measures what the module-size
      policy measures; a test asserts a bundled asset and a resource .txt are excluded.
- [x] The metric's numbers are reconciled with the CI module-size gate on this repository -- if
      they still differ, the difference is documented and justified rather than left silent.
- [x] A regression asserts the adapter does not return a confident zero for a scan root that
      demonstrably contains files.

## Provenance

Found immediately after installing scc/lizard/jscpd on the operator's machine to enable code-health metrics for this project. Complexity (lizard) and duplication (jscpd) began producing real values; the scc-backed size metrics did not, which surfaced this.
baseline.summary: scc adapter omits --by-file, so module-size metrics report a confident ZERO instead of Unavailable

baseline.description:
## Context

Two consecutive successful macOS Gerrit Verify jobs after change 1730 still report tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass at 21.05s and 29.38s. Closed ticket curricular-mean-cuckoo already removed the dominant redundant work and explicitly locks this contract at 3,000 tickets, 3,000 comments, 24 crash-safe import commits, and >=10x commit reduction. This follow-up must preserve that exact behavioral/performance-scale contract and remove only proven redundant work.

## Plan

1. Reproduce the exact N=3000 node on current origin/main with repeated wall-time samples and a full call-count/cumulative-time profile. Separate test construction, importer composition, validation, filesystem writes, Git index/commit subprocesses, materialization, and cleanup.
2. Form competing hypotheses from the profile and run one controlled experiment per hypothesis. Compare against the already-landed author-cache and stale-sweep optimization; do not infer from aggregate suite time.
3. Cross-check the ticket store for prior decisions and compare the proven mechanism with popular maintained OSS bulk-import/test patterns before proposing a change. The curricular-mean-cuckoo workload and durability constraints remain controlling.
4. If the remaining cost is redundant setup or production-path work, add a deterministic held-out oracle for the exact call/effect count, prove RED, implement the narrow optimization, and prove GREEN plus exact-defect mutation RED. If the remaining time is irreducible work needed for the locked scale contract, report that result and evaluate scheduling/tier placement without removing the test from macOS unless equivalent platform assurance is proven.
5. Verify the unchanged N=3000/6000-event/24-commit assertions, import idempotency, rollback, crash-resume, clean-index, author and stale-sweep lifecycle, focused unit/interface suites, lint, typecheck, and the full Gerrit Verify matrix. Report before/after macOS runner-seconds and overall critical-path effect.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: curricular-mean-cuckoo and tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py preserve N=3000, 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe import commits, >=10x commit reduction, complete state, rollback, and resume. trigger_preconditions: fresh real Git-backed store importing the fixed synthetic corpus through public rebar.import_tickets. production_path: rebar.import_tickets through import composition, batch staging/commit, and materialization. test_tier: real-Git integration on every supported CI platform currently executing this node. observable_postcondition: identical ticket/comment state, event attribution, commit graph/count, clean index, and deterministic collaborator/effect counts with lower measured wall time. negative_control: independent interactive writes, failure rollback, later-chunk resume, and existing-ticket imports retain current semantics. collateral_invariants: no test, platform cell, mutation shard, coverage measurement, event validation, durability boundary, or contractual assertion is removed or weakened. ci_gate: focused repeated benchmark evidence plus full Gerrit Verified gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Current macOS time over 20s is reproduced and individually attributed to concrete operations with call counts and cumulative time.
- [ ] The exact N=3000, 6,000-event, 24-commit, >=10x, complete-state, rollback, and crash-resume contracts remain unchanged and green.
- [ ] Any implementation is guarded by a held-out deterministic oracle, exact-defect mutation evidence, and negative controls for interactive/failure behavior.
- [ ] Ticket-store prior decisions and relevant maintained OSS practice are documented before remediation.
- [ ] Repeated same-host before/after results quantify test and runner-time savings; time remains evidence, not a flaky threshold.
- [ ] Focused suites, lint, typecheck, full Gerrit Verify, LLM-Review, and merge are green before closure.
baseline.summary: Eliminate remaining macOS N=3000 import benchmark long pole

## Symptom

`provision_toolchain` in `tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` (around `:151`) runs its fast-path `_satisfied()` check **before** taking the `flock`, and treats the bundle as ready on mere existence. A worker can therefore observe a partially-written `node_modules`/`dist`, conclude provisioning is done, return early, and run tests against a bundle another worker is still writing.

Flagged as an advisory by the LLM reviewer on Gerrit change 2600 patchset 3, and judged a real defect rather than a style note by the implementing agent.

## Why it was not fixed in 2600

Change 2600 is the fix for bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`, which was failing ~46% of CI runs repo-wide and blocking every open change. Pushing a further patchset would have reset its `LLM-Review +1` and cost another full review plus CI cycle on the change that was unblocking the repository. The deliberate call was to land 2600 and track this separately.

**This is not a regression introduced by 2600.** Before that change there was no lock at all and workers raced freely; 2600 narrowed the window substantially. This ticket closes the remainder.

## Fix shape

Drop the unlocked fast path and perform the `_satisfied()` check **inside** the lock. An `flock` on a local file costs microseconds and is taken a handful of times per run, so the fast path buys negligible time while creating the window.

## Acceptance criteria

All deterministic and verifiable in a single run — no "run it a few times and see".

1. A test demonstrates the race deterministically **before** the fix: one worker is made to observe
   the partially-written state (e.g. hold the lock while a bundle is half-created, or stub the
   filesystem state the fast path inspects) and is shown returning early. RED first — a race
   asserted only by repetition is not a reproduction.
2. After the fix, the same test shows the second worker blocking on the lock and observing only a
   complete bundle.
3. The existing provisioning behaviour is unchanged for the uncontended case: `tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py`
   still passes in full, and a cold single-worker run still provisions exactly once.
4. **Defect-seeded**: restoring the unlocked fast path makes AC1's test fail again. Demonstrated by
   mutation, then reverted.
5. No new mechanism is registered — this should be a movement of an existing check, not new
   machinery. Verify with `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` **and** `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`
   (the latter is not covered by `make lint`).

## Note

`tests/e2e/_toolchain.py` and its lock were introduced by change 2600; read that change first for the surrounding design, including why provisioning moved out of the fixture into `pytest_collection_modifyitems` and why a failed pre-provision must degrade to the in-fixture path rather than fail the step.
baseline.summary: e2e toolchain provisioning has an unlocked fast path: a worker can run against a bundle another worker is still writing

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (2026-08-13): "The tickets branch should never trigger CI. The branch is noisy and doesn't contain code." rebar auto-pushes the `tickets` branch to `origin` on EVERY write (comment/edit/claim/close), so each ticket event fires the four workflows that push- trigger on all-branches-but-two. During the 2026-08-12/13 bug bash this starved the org-wide GitHub Actions runner pool (navapbc is on GitHub Free: 20 concurrent jobs, 5 macOS, shared across the org), queueing a Gerrit `Verified` pytest matrix ~2 hours behind tickets-push runs.

## Approach
Audit every file in `.github/workflows/` for an `on.push` trigger. Measured today, exactly four have one — `test.yml`, `optionality.yml`, `prompt-eval.yml`, `verify-identity.yml` — and all four already use the SAME idiom: `branches-ignore: ["feature/**", "main"]`. The ticket's original finding that `reconcile-bridge.yml` push-triggers is STALE: it is schedule + `workflow_dispatch` only today. Every other workflow is `workflow_call`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, `pull_request`, or `pull_request_target`.

So the change is minimal and idiom-preserving: append `"tickets"` to those four `branches-ignore` lists (keeping `branches-ignore` as the ONE consistent idiom rather than converting anything to explicit allow-lists), each with a one-line comment citing `refractive-conceptual-sunbear`. No `schedule:` block is touched, so the replacement cadences the directive relies on are unchanged by construction: reconcile-bridge `*/20 * * * *`, verify-identity `53 */6 * * *`, test `41 */6 * * *`, optionality `47 */6 * * *`, prompt-eval weekly `0 7 * * 1`.

Enforcement: the sibling policy module `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` already models GitHub's branch filtering in its `_push_matches_branch` helper but only pins the four known workflow NAMES. A future workflow added with a bare `push:` would silently regress this invariant, so the new test module ENUMERATES every `*.yml`/`*.yaml` under `.github/workflows/` from disk and asserts none of them push-matches `tickets`, plus that non-tickets topic-branch push CI still fires (the scratch-branch push lane is the only pre-merge validation path for a workflow change — the Gerrit Verified lane resolves `uses: ./.github/workflows/...` from the default branch and therefore cannot exercise a workflow edit).

Out of scope, stated as a deliberate default: `pull_request:` filters on the BASE branch, not the head, so a tickets-headed PR cannot be excluded by branch filter — and `lockdown.yml` auto-closes PRs on this mirror anyway. Leave `pull_request` triggers alone.

Not changed, by operator instruction: `gerrit-verify.yaml` stays `workflow_dispatch`-only (it is the sole `Verified` source, dispatched by Gerrit per patchset).

**Adopter documentation (operator scope addition).** This hazard is not specific to this repo: ANY rebar adopter whose CI watches all branches turns every comment into a workflow run, because the store auto-pushes on every write. Document it once where an adopter configures the store's remote, and cross-link rather than triplicate. The canonical warning goes in `docs/concurrency.md` under "Outbound — push (on every write)" (the mechanism section that already states every write auto-pushes); `docs/user-guide.md` gets a short pointer at the "The store **auto-pushes**" paragraph; `docs/config.md` gets a one-line pointer in the `sync.remote` annotation. Wording is adopter guidance — "configure your CI so the tickets branch never triggers workflows; use a schedule for anything that must read the store" — not a retelling of this repo's incident.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — add `"tickets"` to `on.push.branches-ignore` + citation comment.
- `.github/workflows/optionality.yml` — same.
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` — same.
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` — same.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_push_policy.py` — NEW: the enumerate-all-workflows invariant.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — canonical adopter warning in the outbound-push section.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — short pointer at the auto-push/comment paragraph.
- `docs/config.md` — one-line pointer in the `sync.remote` annotation.

## Testing
- Happy path: for each workflow file discovered on disk, a push to `tickets` does not match its
  `on.push` filter (a workflow with no `push` key trivially passes).
- Regression/edge: a hypothetical `on: push:` with NO branch filter, and one with
  `branches: [tickets]`, are both classified as matching by the shared filter model, so the
  enumerating test would fail if such a workflow were added later.
- Preserved-behaviour path: the four edited workflows still push-match an ordinary topic branch
  (`wip-some-topic`) and still skip `feature/**` and `main`.
- Schedule path: each edited workflow's cron list is asserted unchanged against its literal.
- Live end-to-end (post-merge, AC2): make a trivial rebar write (a comment on this ticket),
  capture the resulting `tickets` head SHA, then query
  `/repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs?branch=tickets` and confirm zero runs exist for that SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No file in `.github/workflows/` triggers on a push to `tickets` — checked by the new
      enumerating test, which reads the directory rather than a hard-coded name list, so an
      added workflow cannot regress it silently.
- [x] A tickets-branch push made AFTER the change merges produces zero new workflow runs —
      checked by the GitHub Actions API for that push's head SHA, evidence recorded as a
      comment on this ticket.
- [x] Every `schedule:` cron in the repo is byte-identical to its pre-change value — checked by
      `git diff` showing no change inside any `schedule:` block, and by the cron literals
      asserted in the new test (reconcile-bridge `*/20 * * * *` and verify-identity
      `53 */6 * * *` explicitly).
- [x] `gerrit-verify.yaml` remains `workflow_dispatch`-only — checked by the existing
      `test_gerrit_verify_stays_a_dispatch_only_patchset_gate` in
      `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` still passing.
- [x] Push CI for ordinary topic branches is preserved — checked by the new test asserting
      `wip-some-topic` still matches all four edited workflows.
- [x] Client-facing docs warn adopters against CI triggered by tickets-branch pushes — checked
      by `grep` finding the warning in `docs/concurrency.md` (canonical, naming the schedule
      alternative) and a cross-link to it in both `docs/user-guide.md` and `docs/config.md`,
      with the guidance phrased for any adopter rather than as this repo's incident report.
- [x] Full local gate set green (ten `check_*` gates, generators no-diff, `make lint`,
      `make typecheck`, CI-equivalent pytest tier) and the change lands with `LLM-Review +1`
      and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Tickets-branch pushes must trigger no CI (operator directive)

## Context and final-epic intent

Gerrit change 1517 retired two dead implementations: the file-backed top-level `bridge-status` handler, which read an unproduced `.bridge-status.json`, and `purge-bridge`, which had no supported caller and exposed an inverted `--keep` contract. That removal merged as commit `318903aa37` after LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and zero unresolved comments.

A later dependent story deliberately reintroduced the spelling `rebar bridge-status` as a hidden compatibility alias for the new durable `rebar bridge status` operation. This does not resurrect the removed implementation. At the final epic tip, the old file-backed module remains absent, while the alias routes through the same parser/core/schema as canonical status so workflows and environments using old vocabulary continue to function. `purge-bridge` remains fully retired.

## Completed implementation and continuity

The legacy artifacts removed by change 1517 remain absent:

- `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge.py`, including its dangling epic citation and unproduced file reader.
- `src/rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py` and its concurrency-only worker/tests.
- top-level help pages `help/bridge-status.txt` and `help/purge-bridge.txt`.
- the old bridge-status-only tests and schema exemption.
- purge-bridge dispatch, help, docs surface, and schema references.

The final code intentionally retains or recreates these successor surfaces:

- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` contains hidden `bridge-status` compatibility routing to the canonical nested bridge parser; `purge-bridge` remains absent.
- `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_status.schema.json`, `schemas.BRIDGE_STATUS`, and `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["bridge_status"]` now describe the surviving durable status snapshot, not the deleted file-backed report.
- `rebar.bridge_status`, `types.BridgeStatus`, MCP `bridge_status` / `BridgeStatusOut`, `schemas/check_mcp_models.py`, and `schemas/gen_types.py` are retained consumers of that durable schema.
- canonical and hidden status entrypoints share output, errors, and exits across CLI, Python library, and MCP; the alias stays absent from top-level help.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` lists only purge-bridge as retired. Bridge-status continuity is proved by the bridge facade/contract suites.
- current user guide, release notes, ADR 0094, CLI reference, and output-schema docs distinguish the historical dead-handler removal from the later durable compatibility alias.

Surviving bridge alert reads use neutral guidance. Top-level `rebar doctor`, `bridge-fsck`, bridge preview/sync/pause/resume, legacy reconcile adapters, and persisted ticket formats are unchanged.

## Verification

Historical change-1517 evidence: held-out retirement oracle 7/7; focused help/schema/alert contracts 41 passed; lint and typecheck passed; full suite 11,149 passed with 40 skipped and 228 deselected; CI run 31218769114 passed all required matrices.

Final-epic continuity evidence is codebase-verifiable at `694cf894def36241724e7049e3308d782037ef6d`: help coverage proves purge remains retired; bridge CLI/library/MCP contract suites prove the hidden alias and durable schema consumers remain functional; schema/type/MCP drift generators remain current; generated CLI/output docs and ADR index checks pass. Gerrit change 1595 merged after LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

## Rollback and safety

No persisted data, migration, external integration, authentication boundary, or shared-state format was removed by change 1517. Reverting only the old removal is no longer a valid rollback because it would restore the obsolete file-backed handler beside the durable successor. Any rollback must preserve the current compatibility alias and durable schema while addressing a concrete successor defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The obsolete file-backed bridge-status implementation and its dangling citation remain absent.
- [x] Purge-bridge remains an unknown command, absent from help, implementation, and active docs.
- [x] Hidden bridge-status now routes only to canonical durable bridge status and remains absent from top-level help.
- [x] Durable bridge_status schema, Python facade/type, MCP tool/model, and generator registries remain intact.
- [x] Help/schema/docs distinguish historical retirement from the retained compatibility alias.
- [x] Surviving alert guidance, bridge-fsck, doctor, bridge operations, and reconcile adapters remain compatible.
- [x] Removed-only tests are gone and replacement behavioral/contract tests prove both retirement and continuity.
- [x] Historical Gerrit/CI evidence and final epic LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1 establish the completed contract.
baseline.summary: Retire the two dead bridge verbs (bridge-status, purge-bridge)
