## Context
Codex currently has no Serena MCP entry, while this project relies on Serena/Pyright for semantic navigation. The tracked `.claude/settings.json` does not configure MCP servers. Separately, this operator machine's untracked Claude project config (`~/.claude.json`) launches Serena via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena`; that machine-local fact was inspected only to identify the existing server. The delivery design is independently grounded: the current Codex manual supports project-scoped MCP servers in trusted `.codex/config.toml`, and Serena 1.6.2.dev0 exposes a `codex` context plus `--project-from-cwd` specifically for CLI agents/worktrees.

## Verified inputs
- `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena -V` returned `Serena 1.6.2.dev0`.
- `git ls-remote https://github.com/oraios/serena.git HEAD` returned `c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e`.
- `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e serena start-mcp-server --help` succeeded and documented `--context` plus `--project-from-cwd`.
- `codex mcp list` in the current worktree confirms no `serena` entry exists before the change.

## Plan
- Add a project-scoped `mcp_servers.serena` STDIO entry to `.codex/config.toml`; project scope is intentional so every contributor/worktree gets the repo-required semantic navigation server after trusting the repo, without mutating each operator's global config.
- Launch the same Serena distribution currently used on this machine, but pin the verified upstream commit: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e`.
- Pass `serena start-mcp-server --context codex --project-from-cwd` so each checkout/worktree activates itself; commit no user-specific project path.
- Set `startup_timeout_sec = 120` to bound and accommodate a cold uvx resolution. Keep `required` unset/false so a Serena startup failure is reported by Codex without preventing all Codex work.
- Validate TOML with Python 3.11+ `tomllib`; run `codex mcp list` from the isolated worktree and require an enabled `serena` row containing the pinned command/args; run the pinned `serena start-mcp-server --help` command and an MCP initialize/list-tools smoke test from the worktree, bounded by a test harness timeout.
- Negative control: run `codex mcp list` from a temporary untrusted/non-rebar directory and confirm the project-scoped server is not injected there.
- Land the single-file config change through Gerrit with DCO and the ticket trailer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `codex mcp list` from a trusted rebar worktree discovers an enabled `serena` STDIO server from `.codex/config.toml`, using the pinned upstream commit.
- [ ] The server argv uses Serena's `codex` context and `--project-from-cwd`; no user-specific rebar path is committed.
- [ ] `python -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('.codex/config.toml', 'rb'))"`, the pinned Serena CLI smoke command, and an MCP initialize/list-tools smoke test all succeed.
- [ ] `codex mcp list` outside the trusted rebar project does not expose the project-scoped `serena` entry; Serena startup remains non-required so failure does not block Codex itself.
- [ ] The config diff contains no secrets, and `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite remain green; a same-base full-gate result may be reused because this task changes only static Codex configuration.

## References
Current Codex manual: trusted projects may scope MCP servers in `.codex/config.toml`; STDIO entries accept `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `startup_timeout_sec`, and optional `required`. Serena CLI help at the pinned commit documents `--context codex` and `--project-from-cwd`.
baseline.summary: Configure Codex to use the project's Serena MCP server

baseline.description:
## Why
Code review reviews a DIFF fresh with NO memory across runs. The durable `code_review` artifact (per Gerrit change/revision) today persists SURFACED findings write-only (a calibration corpus). This story adds the READER + the content-addressed STATE the region-gated novelty floor (blameless-grindable-noctule) needs, and extends the `code_review_result_v1` payload with the two new fields that state.

## What
- **Payload extension (`code_review_result_v1`, `build_payload`).** Add two fields, both read
  off the verdict dict so they are populated once and flow to EVERY emit path unchanged:
  - `session_id`: TOP-LEVEL, nullable. `build_payload` reads `verdict.get("session_id")`
    (None for Gerrit reviews; set for local session-keyed reviews by the persistence story
    paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish). Makes local memory queryable by session.
  - `deps`: a `{reviewed-file path: sha256}` content-hash map. `build_payload` reads
    `verdict.get("deps")` (defaulting to `{}`).
- **deps collector + computation seam (`produce_code_review_verdict`).** A thin collector hashes
  each reviewed-file path once and stashes the map on the verdict (`verdict["deps"]`) in
  `_run_code_review_gate`, computed UNCONDITIONALLY after the verdict is produced and BEFORE the
  sidecar emit. This requires importing `code_review.sidecar` (for the collector +
  `_cited_paths_code_review`) EARLIER in `_run_code_review_gate` — at the top of the finalize block
  rather than only inside the existing `if request.target_ticket:` block (an explicit new import in
  `gate_dispatch.py`, enumerated here). Because it lives on the verdict dict, BOTH
  emit callers pick it up via `build_payload` with NO change to either call site:
  - the produce-path emit (`_run_code_review_gate` → `sidecar.emit`), and
  - the Gerrit voter emit (`voter.py::emit_code_review_artifact` → `sidecar.emit`), which passes
    the SAME verdict object it received — so it inherits `deps`/`session_id` for free (voter.py
    stays OUT of scope; it needs no edit).
  - **Reuse boundary:** the collector REUSES the private `attest._hash_file(path, base=…)`
    primitive (raw file-bytes sha256; a missing/unreadable path → the `absent` sentinel, so a
    create/delete is itself detectable) and `attest._hash_basis(repo_root)` for the base. This
    reuse of a private symbol is EXPLICITLY sanctioned by the epic design ("private `_hash_file`
    primitive reused; NOT `dependency_hashes`, which is plan/ticket-coupled"). It does NOT reuse
    `dependency_hashes()` (that pulls ticket file_impact + plan-verdict citation buckets).
  - **Scope of `deps`** = the review's `changed_files` UNION its cited-file paths. NOTE:
    `attest._cited_paths(verdict)` is NOT reusable here — it reads a `citations` list with
    `kind == "file"`, but code-review findings carry no such list (they only have a `location`
    string, e.g. `path` or `path:line`). So define a small `_cited_paths_code_review(verdict)`
    in `code_review/sidecar.py` that extracts the FILE path (strip any `:line` suffix) from each
    finding's `location` across the `blocking` + `advisory` buckets, ignoring empty/non-file
    locations. `deps` = `sorted(set(changed_files) | _cited_paths_code_review(verdict))`.
  - **Basis:** hashed via `attest._hash_basis(repo_root)` at the emit point. Because deps are
    computed AFTER the workflow's `gate_read_root` context has exited, `current_code_root()` is
    already `None`, so `_hash_basis` resolves to the in-place WORKING TREE (`_config.repo_root`) —
    NOT the attested snapshot. This is correct for both keyspaces: a LOCAL `review-code` reviews the
    working tree (so the working tree IS the reviewed basis), and the Gerrit voter bot checks out
    the patchset revision (so its working tree IS the reviewed revision). The content-addressed
    region gate only ever compares hashes WITHIN one keyspace, and each keyspace hashes its own
    working-tree basis consistently across runs, which is all it needs.
  - **Failure posture:** the collector is best-effort — a per-file hash failure yields the
    `absent` sentinel (never raises); a total failure leaves `deps` empty and is logged. It must
    NEVER fail the gate (mirrors the sidecar's best-effort posture).
- **Artifact addressing (title schemes, TYPED keyspaces).** Local artifacts use title
  `code-review: session:{session_id}`; Gerrit artifacts keep `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}`
  (unchanged). These are two disjoint keyspaces so a prior LOCAL review can never seed a change's
  FIRST Gerrit review.
- **Reader `latest_code_review_result(key, *, repo_root=None)`.** `key` is a TYPED string:
  `session:<id>` or `change:<id>`. Resolution by artifact title:
  - `session:<id>` → the artifact whose title == `code-review: session:{id}` (exact; one artifact).
  - `change:<id>` → STRIP the `change:` tag to get the bare `change_id`, then match artifacts whose
    title starts with `code-review: {change_id} @ ` (spans revisions of the same change; the change
    is the memory key, the revision only makes each artifact idempotent). An unknown key kind → None.
  Artifacts are enumerated via `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review")` and matched by title
  in-process (no new list-filter API). Across the matched artifact(s), the reader returns the
  most-recent usable `code_review_result_v1` sidecar payload's SURFACED findings + its `deps` map.
  - **SURFACED-only (mandatory; see old-frilly-plankton).** `code_review_result_v1` stores findings
    in SEPARATE top-level buckets (`blocking`, `advisory`, `coaching`) with NO per-finding
    `decision` field (unlike `plan_review_result_v1`). Therefore "surfaced" is DEFINED as the union
    of the `blocking` and `advisory` buckets; the reader returns ONLY those two buckets (never
    `coaching`, never any future dropped bucket). Dropped findings are never persisted into
    blocking/advisory, so they can never re-enter the novelty prior set.
  - **Posture:** mirrors `plan_review.sidecar.latest_review_result` — best-effort, NEVER raises,
    schema-guarded (only `code_review_result_v1` payloads), walks newest→oldest over each artifact's
    sidecar events tolerating a malformed/foreign newest file, returns None when nothing usable.
    A reader/hash/compare error degrades to None (⇒ the floor runs un-narrowed = no drops).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — payload extension (`build_payload`), the thin deps
  collector, and the `latest_code_review_result` reader.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — the `deps` computation seam in
  `produce_code_review_verdict` / `_run_code_review_gate` (stash on the verdict before emit).
- OUT of scope: local persistence wiring / setting `session_id` (paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish);
  the region_gated_floor consumer (blameless-grindable-noctule); `voter.py` (inherits via the
  verdict — no edit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `build_payload` adds a nullable top-level `session_id` (read from `verdict.get("session_id")`)
      and a `deps` `{path: sha256}` map (read from `verdict.get("deps")`, default `{}`).
- [ ] A thin deps collector reuses `attest._hash_file` (NOT `dependency_hashes`) and the `absent`
      sentinel; scope = `changed_files` ∪ `_cited_paths_code_review(verdict)` (paths parsed from
      each finding's `location`, since code-review findings have no `citations[kind==file]` list).
- [ ] The deps map is computed ONCE in `produce_code_review_verdict`, UNCONDITIONALLY (regardless of
      `target_ticket`), and stashed on the verdict — importing `code_review.sidecar` earlier in
      `_run_code_review_gate` — so both the produce emit and the Gerrit voter emit carry it via
      `build_payload` (voter unchanged).
- [ ] `latest_code_review_result(key)` resolves `session:<id>` (exact title `code-review: session:{id}`)

## Summary
The reconciler preflight (`preflight_status_mapping`, `reconcile.py`) raises `StatusMappingError("local status {status!r} not in local_to_jira_status mapping ...")`. But the same function's Bug-85a1 logic deliberately accepts a value that is EITHER a local-status KEY or a Jira-status VALUE, failing only when it is in neither. So the offending value is frequently a **Jira** workflow status (e.g. `IDEA`, added Jira-side), not a local status. Labeling it "local status 'IDEA'" is misleading and misdirects debugging toward a non-existent local `idea` ticket. The `StatusMappingError` docstring (reconcile.py) makes the same wrong "references a local status" assumption.

## Reproduction Steps
1. A Jira issue is in a workflow status with no reconciler mapping (e.g. `IDEA`).
2. Reconcile → `ERROR: ... local status 'IDEA' not in local_to_jira_status mapping (target=REB-716)`.

Expected: message accurately states the status is unmapped in `local_to_jira_status` in EITHER direction (could be a local-status key or a Jira-status value) — not that it is a "local status". Actual: message asserts it is a "local status", which is false for a Jira-origin status.

## Scope
LOGGING/ERROR-MESSAGE FIX ONLY. Does NOT add the `idea`->`IDEA` mapping (that is story 6173 / tawny-herb-bug, out of scope here).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — the `StatusMappingError` message +
  the `StatusMappingError` / `preflight_status_mapping` docstrings.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_status_preflight.py` — assert the message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `StatusMappingError` message no longer calls the value a "local status"; it
      states the status is not mapped in `local_to_jira_status` (neither a local-status
      key nor a Jira-status value), and still includes the status value + target.
- [ ] The `StatusMappingError` and `preflight_status_mapping` docstrings no longer assert
      the value is a "local status".
- [ ] A test asserts an unmapped Jira status (e.g. `IDEA`) is not reported as a "local
      status" and the message acknowledges the Jira-status possibility.
- [ ] No mapping/behavior change (the raise condition is unchanged); existing preflight
      tests still pass.
- [ ] make lint passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: reconciler preflight mislabels an unmapped Jira status as a 'local status'

Three follow-ups on the unit-tier subprocess-isolation guard, all raised as non-blocking advisories by the LLM code review on Gerrit 2506 and deferred there.

1. _check_home_escape may OVER-FLAG. It treats any argv element referencing a name or attribute in
   _HOME_ESCAPE_NAMES (home, mkdtemp, TemporaryDirectory) as a hazard. An unrelated local named
   `home`, or a tmp_path-rooted mkdtemp that is perfectly harnessed, would be reported. Zero live
   sites hit it today, so it is latent rather than active — but the guard s whole design premise is
   that a false positive is as costly as a false negative, because reddening innocent files is how a
   guard gets reverted. Narrow it to the attribute forms that actually escape (Path.home(),
   os.environ["HOME"]) and add both a positive and a negative case.
2. The UsageError contract is verified only by GREPPING conftest.py text for the string within a
   window. That asserts the source, not the behaviour: it would pass if the arm raised something
   else while the word appeared nearby. The contract matters (from the xdist controller a
   pytest.fail escapes as a 20-line INTERNALERROR), so it deserves a real assertion on the raised
   type.
3. The file-level opt-out fallback for hazards found in MODULE-LEVEL HELPERS is untested. That path
   exists so a marked test s shared helper is covered when the finding carries no test name of its
   own; five live sites rely on it via a module pytestmark. It was verified once by hand during
   implementation and never pinned.

See tests/_subprocess_isolation.py and tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py.

## Context

An attested gate against a locally present full commit SHA still performs a general fetch before resolving the SHA. In a checkout whose `remote.origin.fetch` maps every head, this becomes `git fetch --no-filter origin`. Git applies the broad refspec and fetches every configured head, including `tickets`, although the gate will materialize one code commit.

The current snapshot contract states that attested mode fetches first when needed and materializes the committed tree at the selected SHA. A locally present full SHA does not need remote freshness. The general fetch adds unrelated transfer cost and can prevent the gate from reaching model execution.

## Rebar-debug orientation

- Step 0(a). Searches for `promisor`, `broad-fetch performance`, `snapshot no-filter partial clone pack bloat`, and the exact timeout found related closed tickets but no bug with this scope. `suave-constant-cow` handles byte-starved transport stalls. `agrologic-oval-bobolink` handles uncoordinated ref updates. Neither limits the ref set of a successful no-filter fetch.
- Step 0(b). The occurrence was reported against `813baac9b01524a024523a8516d563b17f395358`.
- Step 0(c). The F30A worktree matched `origin/main` at that revision.

## Confirmed mechanism

`resolve_ref` calls `fetch_origin` without a target before it attempts `rev_parse`, at `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` lines 262 through 266. Materializing callers pass `blobless=False`. `fetch_origin` therefore constructs a general `git fetch --quiet --no-filter origin` and bounds the subprocess at 300 seconds, at `src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py` lines 256 through 283. The configured `remote.origin.fetch` decides which heads that command transfers.

The affected checkout uses `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`. A main-only comparison checkout uses `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`. The remote currently has 19 heads. The broad checkout contains about 12 GB of Git objects, 115 packs, and recent packs ranging from about 160 MB to 338 MB. One unfinished pack is about 2.3 GB.

## Proof

- F30A completion verification against the full SHA made no model call and failed after the production 300 second fetch timeout. A direct `git fetch origin main` had completed in 3.9 seconds shortly before.
- Ticket `unromantic-ferny-arawana` records an independent run at the same revision. Its broad partial-clone checkout made zero model calls and failed after 512.139 seconds because the general fetch reached the 300 second timeout. Its main-only comparison checkout crossed the fetch boundary and completed with signed PASS in 133.411 seconds.
- The F30A isolated main-only clone also crossed this boundary and completed an attested plan review with signed PASS.
- The target commit tree contains 3,550 objects and zero missing objects in the affected checkout. Materialization did not require a general fetch to acquire this tree.
- Source inspection and process sampling rule out the enrich drain as the direct blocker. Enrich drain releases its advisory lock before model work at `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` lines 358 through 428. It does not own the code snapshot fetch lock.

The configuration differential distinguishes broad ref selection from provider latency, credentials, an absent target object, and the enrich-drain lock. Transport stalls remain possible in general, but they do not explain why the main-only comparison passes while the broad checkout fails at the same revision.

## Defect legitimacy

`docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` states that attested mode fetches first when needed and materializes the selected SHA. It also defines the full SHA as the code version the gate verifies. Fetching unrelated heads is outside that contract and prevents supported gates from completing. This is a defect.

## Remediation constraints

- Preserve freshness for moving branches and tags.
- Preserve targeted recovery for a full SHA that is absent locally.
- Preserve complete blob acquisition for the selected tree.
- Preserve `--end-of-options` protection for client-supplied refs.
- Do not narrow or rewrite the checkout owner's configured refspec as a side effect.
- Keep attested mode fail-closed when the selected ref or required object cannot be obtained.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A locally resolvable full SHA does not trigger a general fetch whose scope expands through `remote.origin.fetch`.
- [x] A moving branch or tag is refreshed before resolution.
- [x] A missing full SHA uses a targeted fetch and either resolves or fails closed with an actionable error.
- [x] Materialization acquires every missing blob for the selected tree without fetching unrelated heads.
- [x] A deterministic local-remote test uses a broad refspec and a large unrelated branch, then proves that resolving and materializing a present SHA does not transfer the unrelated objects.
- [x] Existing snapshot security, partial-clone, timeout, and concurrency tests remain green.
- [x] Current snapshot documentation describes fetch scope for full SHAs, moving refs, and missing objects.
- [x] Focused tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.
baseline.summary: Attested exact-SHA snapshot performs a broad no-filter fetch across every origin head

# `plan_review/attest.py` is at the hard cap with ZERO headroom

## Context

Landing bug c083 (untracked-tolerance on four plan-review snapshot reads) hit this immediately: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` was **799** lines on `origin/main` against the **800** hard cap enforced by `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py::test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` (limit single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`).

A two-call-site change — adding `ignore_untracked=True` to two existing calls — could not be landed in the natural form:

- appending the kwarg inline made the line 114 chars, over the ruff E501 limit of 100;
- wrapping the call to satisfy E501 cost +2 lines -> 801, over the cap;
- adding the explanatory comments the change deserved cost more -> 803.

It only fit by importing `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` directly (+1 line for the import, which let the call fit on one line at 95 chars), landing the file at **exactly 800** — passing only because the gate is `> limit`, with **zero** remaining headroom. The file currently sits at **794** on `origin/main`; the headroom problem is unchanged.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The next change to this file — any change, including a one-line bug fix — cannot land without first splitting it. The cost is not paid by whoever grew the file; it is paid by whoever next needs to fix a bug in it, under time pressure, as an unrelated blocker. That is exactly the situation task `2682` was raised for when `runner.py` hit 800 in the LLM-provider-seam epic, and it was resolved there by a real call-graph split (`runner.py` 800 -> 655 + `structured_run.py`).

It also actively degrades the code: in c083 the comments explaining WHY untracked files must be tolerated had to be cut from `attest.py` and replaced with a pointer to `resign.py`, purely to save lines. The cap is now shaping documentation quality, not just structure.

## Approach — the DECIDED seam (analysis complete)

**This is a pure refactor: zero behavioral change.** No function body is rewritten; a contiguous call-graph cluster moves to a new sibling module and is re-exported so every existing call site and monkeypatch target keeps resolving.

**Seam chosen: the remediation-mode eligibility cluster.** Extract `remediation_mode_candidate` and its single private helper `_sidecar_branch_decision` from `attest.py` into a new sibling `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/remediation_mode.py`.

Why this seam and not the others considered:

- It is a **pre-existing, isolated call-graph cluster**: `_sidecar_branch_decision` has exactly
  ONE caller in the entire repository — `remediation_mode_candidate`, directly above it — and
  `remediation_mode_candidate` is a call-graph LEAF within `attest.py` (nothing else in the file
  calls it). Verified with both Serena `find_referencing_symbols` and a repo-wide string `grep`.
- It is a **distinct concern**: "is this re-review eligible for the remediation floor?" — a
  Pass-3 floor input — as opposed to `attest.py`'s core job of signing attestations and computing
  claim-gate validity.
- The **drift-refresh cluster was evaluated and rejected**: `drift_refresh_candidate` calls
  `compute_validity` and `_authoritative_manifest` (which must stay in `attest.py`), and
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` monkeypatches `attest._rehash` and then calls
  `attest.refresh_attestation`, so moving that cluster would silently break the patch seam.
  This seam has no such inward dependency.

Dynamic-reference safety (the failure mode that broke epic `061c` S1):

- `remediation_mode_candidate` is reached ONLY through the module attribute
  `attest.remediation_mode_candidate` (`plan_review/__init__.py` and four test modules), including
  a `monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "remediation_mode_candidate", ...)`. Re-exporting the moved name
  from `attest.py` keeps every one of those sites resolving unchanged.
- The moved code calls `current_material_fingerprint` and `registry_version`, both of which the
  tests monkeypatch **on the `attest` module object**
  (`monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "current_material_fingerprint", ...)`,
  `monkeypatch.setattr(attest, "registry_version", ...)`). The new module must therefore resolve
  both **through the `attest` module at call time** (`from . import attest` inside the function
  body, then `attest.<name>(...)`) — a `from .attest import <name>` would bind the original and
  silently ignore the patch. The deferred import also keeps the new module import-cycle safe
  against `attest.py`'s re-export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` is under 700 LOC (real headroom, not 799) — landed at **656** on main (094c4c4525)
- [x] any extracted module is at least 100 LOC (no sub-100-LOC fragmentation) — `remediation_mode.py` is **182**
- [x] `attest.remediation_mode_candidate` still resolves (re-exported), so no call site or
      monkeypatch target in `src/` or `tests/` changes — verified at runtime
      (`attest.remediation_mode_candidate is remediation_mode.remediation_mode_candidate` -> True)
      and by repo-wide grep: every residual reference is either prose or a live
      `attest.remediation_mode_candidate(...)` call
- [x] zero test edits are required by the move, or each required edit is justified in the commit message — **zero** test files touched; the change is 3 files, all under `src/`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus any new
      seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines quoted in a comment
baseline.summary: attest.py sits at exactly 800/800 LOC — zero headroom blocks the next edit

## Context

The prior slices establish a bounded structural index and Terraform-only tool sessions in both review pipelines [rebar:depraved-classless-rooster]. This slice adds optional independent corroboration from HashiCorp's `terraform-config-inspect` when it is already on `PATH`. The audited upstream basis is commit `2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d`: its shallow loader extracts stable top-level metadata with a nil expression context and does not register Terraform filesystem functions, fetch modules, load providers, or run Terraform.

## Scope

Add `src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py` and expose `corroborate_diagnostic(module, diagnostic, subject, expected=None)` through established Terraform Pass-1 and Pass-2 sessions.

### Closed query and result contract

Accepted diagnostics are:

- `declaration_present`: named variable, output, managed resource, data resource, module call, or required provider.
- `module_source_equals`: a named module call has the normalized expected literal source.
- `required_provider_present`: a named provider requirement exists.

An exact schema-valid entry returns `match` at T1. Missing or unequal entries, absence claims, and unsupported/computed semantics return `abstain`; upstream silence never proves correctness or absence. Results contain only normalized names, classes, positions, and hashes—not descriptions, defaults, constraints, diagnostics, or other upstream literal payloads.

### Hardened execution

- Resolve only the exact `terraform-config-inspect` basename from inherited `PATH`; canonicalize once and reject non-regular/non-executable or repo/snapshot-contained candidates. Invoke its absolute path without a shell using only `--json <snapshot>`; never pass `--after-init`, `--stack`, repository arguments, or shell text.
- Copy the immutable indexed whole-module bytes into a fresh directory: regular `.tf` and `.tf.json` files only, no symlinks. Make it read-only, run there, and never pass the repository path.
- Close stdin, create a process group/session, and allow only locale, OS-required process variables, and temporary `HOME`/`TMPDIR`. Strip Terraform/OpenTofu, provider/cloud credential, proxy, plugin, CLI-config, and repository variables.
- Apply the existing 60-second deadline; cap stdout at 4 MiB and stderr at 64 KiB. On timeout, overflow, cancellation, or error, terminate then kill and reap the whole group and remove the snapshot. Hash the executable before and after; replacement abstains.
- Record backend, canonical path, SHA-256, discoverable version or `unknown`, invocation profile, snapshot digest, normalized query, outcome, and result digest. Never log child streams or environment values.

Validate stdout against a Rebar-owned schema for the audited JSON fields. Every reported filename must remain inside and name a copied snapshot file. Unknown/malformed shapes, upstream diagnostics, nonzero exit, overflow, path mismatch, binary replacement, or version/schema skew produce one closed abstention with no partial facts. A corroborator can strengthen a positive Pass-1 fact or independently support Pass-2; it cannot originate a finding, veto ordinary review, or turn abstention into negative evidence.

### Pinned upstream canary

Extend the optionality workflow with a gating lane that installs `github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d`, exposes only that binary on the test `PATH`, and drives the real adapter over a module containing every supported declaration. Assert positive matches, absence-as-abstention, schema acceptance, provenance, and cleanup. Document an identical local command. Normal unit tests remain network-free and substitute an executable fixture only at the process boundary.

## Positive rationale

HashiCorp's deliberately shallow extractor provides a narrow authoritative cross-check. A minimal snapshot and fixed process contract prevent repository config, plugins, cached modules, and ambient credentials from affecting it; match-only semantics absorb upstream incompleteness safely.

## Out of scope

Terraform/OpenTofu and provider execution; validate/plan/init/get; TFLint, Trivy, tfparse, terraform-ls, or terraform-docs; module fetch; after-init and stack modes; arbitrary diagnostics; absence claims; expression evaluation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests through the production adapter prove the closed diagnostic enum and exact-match T1 outcomes for every supported class; missing, unequal, absence-claim, and computed controls return `abstain`.
- [ ] Parent/child subprocess tests capture argv, cwd, stdin, environment, permissions, and bytes, proving only canonical `terraform-config-inspect --json <snapshot>` launches and no repo path, symlink, credential/config variable, or forbidden executable reaches it.
- [ ] Timeout, overflow, cancellation, nonzero-exit, and parser-failure fault tests observe process-group reaping and snapshot removal before return; a clean retry succeeds.
- [ ] Producer/consumer contract tests prove diagnostics, unknown/malformed fields, escaping filenames, changed binary digests, and version/schema skew yield one redacted abstention without partial facts.
- [ ] Receipt tests assert provenance fields and byte-scan results, receipts, logs, and exceptions to prove fixture literals, credentials, streams, and environment values never escape.
- [ ] Terraform plan-review and code-review Pass 1/Pass 2 advertise `corroborate_diagnostic`; non-IaC and missing-extra sessions do not, and abstention leaves the ordinary decision path unchanged.
- [ ] The optionality workflow runs the real adapter against the exact audited commit and fails on drift; `docs/grounding.md` gives the same opt-in local canary.
- [ ] ADR 0111 records the executable trust boundary, audited commit, match-only semantics, and prohibition on every other Terraform-related executable.

## Testing

Test contract card:

- Authoritative contract: REB-640, upstream README/JSON at the pinned commit, and [rebar:depraved-classless-rooster].
- Preconditions: indexed module; executable fixtures for success, skew, secret-bearing output, overflow, hang, signal-resistant child, and self-replacement; pinned real binary in the canary.
- Production path: real snapshot, discovery, launcher, bounded capture, schema parser, receipt, and routing; unit tests replace only the executable.
- Tiers: schema unit, real parent/child subprocess, workflow integration, and live upstream contract canary.
- Oracles: exact outcome/tier/reason; captured child contract; child absent, snapshot removed, retry successful; exact receipt; byte-level non-disclosure.
- Negative controls: exact positive matches, nearest absence/inequality abstains, and non-Terraform routes expose no tool.
- CI: `make test` plus the gating pinned-upstream optionality canary.

## Verification

`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_plan_review_tools.py tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py`
baseline.summary: Corroborate Terraform diagnostics with terraform-config-inspect

# Engine-wide caching: extend the runner cache to RunnerAgentStep (all workflow agent steps)

## Why
S1 caches plan-review's Pass-1 calls. The same stable-prefix waste exists in every workflow agent step
(verify/decide/coach/grounding) and other workflows (completion-verification, code-review) — they re-send a
stable system prompt + tool surface across runs. Extending caching there is the engine-wide win pulled into scope.

## What
- In the engine `RunnerAgentStep` (`workflow/runs.py:207`, builds RunRequest), populate S1's cacheable-prefix
  boundary: the static system prompt (+ stable inputs) is the cached prefix; per-run ticket data is the
  volatile suffix.
- Add a prompt-model convention to mark which part of an assembled workflow prompt is the byte-stable prefix vs
  per-run volatile inputs, so the boundary is set generically (not per call site).
- Apply `anthropic_cache_instructions` for the system prompt across steps; keep dynamic per-run content OUT of
  the cached prefix (after the CachePoint / a separate message part).

## Scope
- In: RunnerAgentStep prefix wiring; the prompt-model stable-vs-volatile convention; applying to all workflows.
- Out: the runner mechanism itself (S1, dependency); container parallelization (S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RunnerAgentStep populates the cacheable prefix; verify/decide/coach cache their stable system-prompt/tool
      prefix on anthropic (`cache_read > 0` on repeats), unchanged on other providers.
- [ ] completion-verification and code-review workflows benefit (cache reads non-zero on repeats).
- [ ] Per-run volatile inputs are excluded from the cached prefix (stability test).
- [ ] `make lint` + tests pass; no finding change.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 6)
- The workflow system prompt interpolates PER-RUN ticket data (`workflow/runs.py:146 resolve_prompt`), so it is

baseline.description:
## Context
Jira DC summary updates can retry in both pycontribs/Jira and `_with_connection_retry`. The selected route needs a dedicated no-SDK-retry client and per-call wrapper policy without changing legacy callers.

## Outcome
Implement the DC summary executor with a guarded `max_retries=0` client and fixed GET -> PUT -> GET invocation. Ambiguous PUT recovery uses a separate single-attempt GET under the shared budget.

## Plan
1. Construct a dedicated executor client through the pinned public `jira.JIRA(..., max_retries=0)` argument; fail fast unless `_session.max_retries == 0`. Preserve legacy client construction.
2. Add an injected one-attempt/no-sleep policy to `_with_connection_retry` for selected executor calls; preserve legacy wrapper defaults.
3. Make one write invocation issue exactly GET/PUT/GET. A fault on the initial (pre-mutation) GET ends the invocation with `request_count=1`, classified as retryable (a transient transport fault mutated nothing, so replay is safe) or permanent (a definitive HTTP error). A fault on the PUT is ambiguous (the write may have landed) and ends the invocation `commit_unknown` with `request_count=2`, no read-back. On a successful PUT the read-back GET is authoritative and IS INSPECTED by comparing its observed summary against the intended new summary: the outcome is `applied` (`request_count=3`) ONLY when the observed summary EQUALS the intended new summary; if the read-back GET cannot be fetched, or its observed summary does NOT equal the intended value, the outcome is `commit_unknown` (`request_count=3`) — the write was accepted, so this layer neither claims success nor auto-replays.
4. After an ambiguous PUT, consume another physical invocation for one GET observation, mapped through the shared `decide_replay` table by the SAME comparison rule: the observation is `desired` when the observed summary EQUALS the intended new summary (→ `recovered`, no further write); `conclusive old state` when the observed summary is present but does NOT equal the intended value (→ replay within remaining budget, else exhausted); and `failed`/`inconclusive` when the GET itself raises (→ non-replaying `commit_unknown`).
5. Return classification/delay metadata to the shared owner; do not sleep or replay in SDK/adapter layers.
6. Emit exactly one redacted completion log for every DC terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure. Include only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; cap the whole serialized log at 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Testing
Use fake sessions with raw request counters and poison sleepers/retry adapters. Include the proven Jira 3.10.5 constructor/session guard plus completion-log field, cardinality, redaction, and size assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The dedicated executor client passes `max_retries=0` and rejects a nonzero session value.
- [x] Legacy DC client SDK retry remains unchanged.
- [x] Each selected write invocation is exactly GET/PUT/GET without hidden repeats.
- [x] Selected wrapper calls perform one attempt and no sleep, while legacy wrapper behavior remains unchanged.
- [x] Desired observation recovers without another write.
- [x] Conclusive old state permits only remaining-budget replay.
- [x] Failed or inconclusive observation returns non-replaying `commit_unknown`.
- [x] Every DC terminal/exhausted outcome or cleanup failure emits exactly one completion log with only logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, `retry_not_before`, and one redacted message capped at 512 Unicode code points; the whole log is at most 1,024 Unicode code points.

## Out of scope
Core dispatch/handler integration and other DC operation families.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S1 T3 — Execute and observe one Jira DC summary postcondition

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The `PreToolUse:Bash` hook fails intermittently with

    PreToolUse:Bash hook error
    Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py: No such file or directory

The failure is non-blocking, so tool calls still run — but the Serena-vs-grep navigation guidance the hook exists to inject is SILENTLY ABSENT for those calls, which is the whole point of the hook.

## Root cause — established by construction, not inferred

`.claude/settings.json` configures the hook with a RELATIVE command path:

    "matcher": "Bash",
    "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py" }]

A relative command is resolved against the SHELL'S CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY at hook time, not against the project root. So the hook works or fails depending purely on where the preceding tool call left the shell.

MEASURED on this host:

    MISSING  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat-c403-overlap-batch
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/fix/1157-ladder-windows
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat/0d76-bedrock-parity

`.tickets-tracker` is the ticket store — a separate git worktree with no `scripts/` directory. Any Bash call issued while the shell sits there fails the hook. That matches the observed occurrences exactly: the errors appeared in a run immediately after ticket-store commands, which leave the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker`.

This is not a missing file. The script is present and executable in the main checkout and in every code worktree checked; only the resolution path is wrong.

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic warning

* It fails OPEN and QUIET. The guidance simply does not appear, and nothing in the transcript says
  "you are now operating without the navigation reminder" — an agent cannot tell a call that got the
  hint from one that did not.
* It is CWD-dependent, so it is intermittent and looks flaky. That invites the wrong diagnosis
  ("transient hook error") instead of the real one.
* It affects any repo-adjacent working directory, not just `.tickets-tracker` — any tool call run
  from `/tmp`, a scratch dir, or a non-repo path hits the same thing.

## Approach

Make the command path independent of the caller's cwd. Claude Code exposes `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for exactly this, so the command should be `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py"` (quoted). An absolute path would also work but is not portable across checkouts, and this repo is routinely used from multiple worktrees, so the project-dir form is preferable.

Worth checking in the same pass whether any OTHER hook in `.claude/settings.json` uses a relative command and has the same latent defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The hook resolves and runs from ANY working directory, including `.tickets-tracker` and a
      directory outside the repository entirely.
- [x] A check or test asserts no hook in `.claude/settings.json` is configured with a relative command
      path, so the defect cannot silently return.
- [x] Every other hook entry in the file is audited for the same relative-path issue and fixed or
      explicitly confirmed safe.
- [x] Verified by running a Bash tool call with the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker` and observing the
      hook's guidance appear rather than an error.
baseline.summary: PreToolUse Bash hook uses a relative command path, so it silently fails from any cwd without scripts/

## Problem

Three defensive `except`/`isinstance` arms that decide whether an LLM-tier failure ABORTS or DEGRADES have **no test that reaches them** (found by the Step-7 parity sweep in bug `wolflike-chevroned-haddock`, `43d4-b8f5-4bb2-417b`). Mutation-proven: reverting each arm to its pre-43d4 form (dropping `LLMInputRejectedError`) leaves the entire unit suite green.

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`: the mid-run
  `except (LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError)` arms around `_ex.run_workflow` in
  `produce_plan_review_verdict` (~:189) and `_run_code_review_gate` (~:522).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/container_stage.py` warm-call abort in `_run_container` (~:209).
  `container_stage` has zero referencing tests — its abort-vs-degrade ruling is unpinned.

## Context — reachability (resolves the original "dead code?" question)

The original probe raised in the **agent-step** path, which `interpreter._run_leaf` absorbs into a failed `StepResult` — never escaping `run_workflow`. The **batch-step** path is the raw seam: `interpreter._run_batch` calls `runner.run(req, rc.runner)` with **no try**, so batch runner raises propagate raw. Plan-review's `ProductionBatchRunner` -> `run_pass1` **re-raises** `LLMUnavailableError` from the chunk pool, and the container warm abort raises **both** types up through it — so the plan-review arm is reachable in production (NOT dead code), fed by the container arm. Code-review's `CodeReviewBatchRunner._run_criterion` translates `LLMUnavailableError` into `SystemicDiscoveryError`, which `discovery.execute_stage` absorbs (`systemic_abort=True`, no re-raise) — no in-tree raw raiser found, so that arm is a **defensive contract at the run_workflow seam**. Per the coverage-only mandate it is pinned, not removed; the finding is recorded as a ticket comment.

## Approach — coverage only, zero production-code change

1. `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_midrun_fail_closed.py`
   - Plan-review arm: monkeypatch `executor.run_workflow` to raise (a) `LLMUnavailableError`,
     (b) `LLMInputRejectedError` (the established `test_gate_engine_cutover.py` seam, incl.
     the `_gate_doc` skeleton); drive `produce_plan_review_verdict` with `FakeRunner`; assert
     the degraded INDETERMINATE verdict (never PASS, `llm_ran is False`) AND the
     `emit_gate_error` sidecar call (kwargs-tolerant recorder — the arm threads `diagnostic=`).
   - Code-review arm: same injection through `produce_code_review_verdict` (`enabled=True`,
     `target_ticket` set so the sidecar fires, WS4's `_local_gate_source` autouse fixture
     copied to avoid the CI shallow-checkout hang); assert INDETERMINATE + sidecar for both
     types.
   - Seam-fidelity: a REAL `run_workflow` over a minimal valid batch-step doc (the
     `test_batch_step.py` `_wf` shape) with an injected batch runner that raises — assert both
     types propagate RAW (`pytest.raises`), pinning `_run_batch`'s no-try contract that makes
     the mid-run arms reachable.

2. `tests/unit/test_container_warm_abort.py` (sibling of `test_container_roster.py`)
   - Drive the REAL `_run_container` with `passes.pass1_container` monkeypatched at the
     model-call boundary. Fixture: `PlanContext(largest_window_tokens=50_000)` (budget 13_000
     tokens), plan text ~20_000 chars (~5_000 tokens >= the 4_096 cache floor), two children
     ~28_000 chars each (~7_000 tokens) -> `pack_container_bins` yields two single-child bins
     -> the warm gate is MET; the warm call is the first `pass1_container` invocation.
   - `LLMUnavailableError` on warm -> `pytest.raises` + exactly ONE call (abort, no fan-out).
   - `LLMInputRejectedError` on warm -> same abort assertions (the 43d4 arm).
   - Negative control: `ValueError` on warm -> no raise; degrades to direct fan-out of ALL
     pairings (3 calls: failed warm + 2 pool re-runs), `coverage["container"]["warmed"]` False.

## Scope

- IN: the two new test files; ticket comments recording the reachability analysis and the
  mutation-check transcript.
- OUT (non-goals): any change to `gate_dispatch.py`, `container_stage.py`, `pass1.py`,
  `interpreter.py` or any production module; removing the code-review arm; new lint/CI
  machinery. If a test exposes a genuine behavioral divergence, a new bug ticket is filed and
  linked `discovered_from` this one instead of changing gate behavior here.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN mutation protocol)

RED — each new test must FIRE against the gap it covers, then the mutation is reverted:
- Mutant A: revert both gate_dispatch arms to `except LLMUnavailableError` only -> the two
  input-rejected mid-run tests FAIL (the exception escapes).
- Mutant B: narrow the container isinstance to `LLMUnavailableError` only -> the
  input-rejected abort test FAILS (degrades instead of raising).
- Mutant C: remove the container abort arm entirely -> both abort tests FAIL.
Outputs recorded in a ticket comment; tree restored (`git diff --stat` clean on `src/`).

GREEN — on unmutated code: both new files pass, plus `tests/unit/test_gate_engine_cutover.py`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_batch_step.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_warmup.py`. Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0 increased=0). No production file changes -> module-size cap unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Tests reach the mid-run plan-review arm for BOTH `LLMUnavailableError` and
      `LLMInputRejectedError`, asserting the degraded INDETERMINATE verdict plus the emitted
      `gate_error_v1` sidecar (`pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_midrun_fail_closed.py -q`).
- [x] The same for the mid-run code-review arm; its reachability status (defensive seam
      contract — systemic errors are translated and absorbed upstream; no in-tree raw raiser)
      is recorded as a ticket comment, resolving the remove-or-test question as test-as-contract.
- [x] A seam-fidelity test proves batch-runner `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMInputRejectedError`
      propagate RAW out of a real `run_workflow` (pinning `_run_batch`'s no-try contract).
- [x] Tests drive `_run_container`'s REAL warm-call path: both systemic types abort the
      fan-out (raise, exactly one model call); a non-systemic failure degrades to direct
      fan-out (negative control).
- [x] Each new test is shown to FAIL under its arm's mutation (Mutants A/B/C), transcript
      recorded in a ticket comment, mutations reverted.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the complexity ratchet pass; no `src/rebar` file is
      modified by this change.
baseline.summary: Untested mid-run/warm-call fail-closed arms in gate_dispatch and container_stage

## Why
Catch wiring bugs without a (near-undecidable, no-good-library) subsumption engine. Validated by spike E2.

## What
- Extend `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint_refs.py` with a 3-state SHALLOW structural check: top-level
  required-field presence + primitive kind compatibility -> OK / UNKNOWN / ERROR; ABSTAIN (UNKNOWN)
  on `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`not`/`$ref` (no subsumption).
- Add RUNTIME validation in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py`: a produced value is validated
  against the downstream CONSUMER's input contract via the registry validator (the real safety net).
- VALIDATOR-FAILURE handling (parity with S7's endpoint-failure fix): if the runtime validator itself
  errors (unresolvable `$ref`, registry miss, validator exception) — as opposed to producing a
  validation finding — the step run surfaces a distinct, visible "validation unavailable / errored"
  signal and does NOT silently treat the value as valid (fail-loud, never false-pass).
- Editor: render an "unchecked" badge for UNKNOWN/opaque sources (`editor.py`).

## Scope
In: shallow static + runtime validation + validator-failure handling + badge. Out: MCP opaque handling (follow-on epic).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shallow check returns ERROR on missing-required / kind-mismatch, UNKNOWN on `oneOf`, OK on a matching shape (port spike E2).
- [ ] Runtime validation checks a produced value against the CONSUMER's input contract; a mismatch surfaces.
- [ ] A runtime VALIDATOR failure (unresolvable `$ref` / registry miss / validator exception) surfaces a distinct "validation errored" signal and never silently passes the value (fail-loud), tested.
- [ ] The inspector shows an "unchecked" badge for UNKNOWN/opaque-typed sources.
baseline.summary: Validation depth: 3-state shallow static + runtime-against-consumer

## Prevention (plan-review) for incident 1c0d — DECIDED, ready to implement

Post-mortem: `9097-2741-6462-424c`. Design spike + escalation resolved (see decision comment). The old "extend project.portability" framing is superseded: portability is the wrong lens (credential reachability is an environment fact, not a plan fact). We ship a distinct criterion.

### Necessity (why this change is needed)
Incident 1c0d escaped because a plan (bug 8fbd's config flip) introduced a fallback chain whose terminal arm degraded to an uncredentialed/unreachable provider, and no gate required the plan to state what happens when that arm fails. The gate has no criterion that forces a plan altering failure/timeout/exception/retry/fallback semantics to declare its failure-disposition contract. Reproduced in the post-mortem; the seeded 1c0d cluster (d209 regression oracle) is the concrete motivating case.

### What to build
A **project-scoped, ADVISORY, single-turn (exec: 1-TURN)** plan-review criterion `project.failure-disposition-contract`, authored in this repo's `.rebar/` overlay (NOT a packaged built-in), mirroring the `necessity` criterion (docs/plan-review-gate.md §R4) as the architectural precedent.

- **Applicability (LLM is the authority, per the rubric):** applies only when the plan adds or alters failure/timeout/exception/retry/fallback/circuit-breaker semantics; otherwise PASS. Detected from plan text + declared file_impact. rebar-vocabulary hints in the rubric: INDETERMINATE, WAIT_AND_RETRY, NEEDS_INVESTIGATION, exit-11, classify_llm_failure, should_fall_back — plus generic retry/fallback/timeout terms. No separate DET detector in v1 (keeps blast radius small; matches necessity, a pure 1-TURN advisory).
- **PASS condition:** for each affected failure arm the plan states its disposition (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) AND, when a fallback chain is present, which leg wins on fallback-failure and the disposition of the terminal arm (the exact 1c0d root cause).
- **Posture:** `default_posture: advisory` — never blocks. Pre-ship validation = HAND-AUTHORED bounded sanity fixtures (eval spec + committed baseline), NOT a batch corpus eval (permanently rejected on cost per §R4). Auto-monitored by the standing effectiveness recorder (zero wiring); advisory→blocking promotion deferred to the field-data gate.
- **Bug handling:** do NOT add to `registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA` and do NOT set `suppress_types:["bug"]`. Net effect: fires on task/story/epic plans and on **escalated bugs** (non-test file_impact, like 8fbd) reviewed under the full rubric via `ticket_type=None`; the claim-time bug exemption is untouched, so it never evaluates raw second-hand claim-time bug content — only a debugger's authored fix plan.
- **Portability:** the concept (retryable-vs-fatal disposition per arm; preserve the most-recoverable leg) is universal; the trigger vocab is rebar-specific by design (a `project.*` criterion). Being an in-process LLM criterion it has no CI-provider dependency, so it satisfies `project.portability`.

### File impact
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — register the criterion (exec:1-TURN, facet, applies_at, default_posture:advisory, block_threshold).
- reviewer rubric prompt for the criterion (`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-failure-disposition-contract.md`, path per docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md).
- `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-failure-disposition-contract.eval.yaml` + committed `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/failure_disposition_sanity.json` — hand-authored sanity fixtures (the project-criterion analog of the necessity built-in's `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` + `runs/` pair).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — document the criterion (the auto-generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is CANONICAL_LLM-only; a project criterion is documented in the gate guide + `rebar explain <id>`, never as a `## <id>` guide section, which `validate_criteria_guide` rejects as an ORPHAN).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Criterion `project.failure-disposition-contract` registered in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (advisory, 1-TURN) with a reviewer rubric authored per the criteria guide.
- [x] Rubric applicability is self-gating (PASS when the plan does not touch failure/timeout/exception/retry/fallback semantics); PASS requires a stated disposition per affected arm + the fallback-failure winner when a chain exists.
- [x] (CI-provable) The eval spec `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-failure-disposition-contract.eval.yaml` and committed baseline `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/failure_disposition_sanity.json` exist with the correct TP/TN corpus shape (seeded 1c0d/8fbd-shaped positives + clean-control negatives) AND pass the injected-perfect-solve calibration arithmetic (recall 1.0 / false-accept 0.0) — proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_project_failure_disposition_contract.py -q`. This is the shape/arithmetic proxy, NOT proof of the live LLM's classification.
- [x] (operator-attested, billable — deliberately NOT run in CI per §R4) The live `rebar criteria eval project.failure-disposition-contract` run fires on the seeded positives and stays clean on the control negatives; its evidence is the frozen baseline committed at `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/failure_disposition_sanity.json`.
- [x] Verified advisory (never blocks); auto-included by the standing effectiveness recorder.
- [x] Documented in the gate guide (`docs/plan-review-gate.md`) and reachable via `rebar explain project.failure-disposition-contract`.
- [x] `rebar review-plan` on this task passes (full rubric; non-test file_impact).

## Testing
- Offline (no-LLM) unit test — the CI-provable proxy: `pytest tests/unit/test_project_failure_disposition_contract.py -q` pins registration (activated project criterion, advisory, 1-TURN, facet project-invariants, scope container+leaf; NOT canonical/agent-tier/codebase-grounded/bug-tier), the rubric front-matter + the two GATE/REQ checklist sub-answers + the T5b anti-double-flag clause, the eval-corpus TP/TN shape and its calibration arithmetic under an injected perfect solve (recall 1.0 / false-accept 0.0 — corpus shape/arithmetic only, tautological by construction), the escalated-bug-vs-light-bug-tier routing (`route_criteria` includes it for a non-test-file_impact bug and excludes it for a test-only bug), and zero-wiring auto-inclusion in `criterion_effectiveness.py`.
- Parity gates stay clean: `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry; assert registry.validate_criteria_guide('.')==[]; assert registry.validate_packaged_routing()==[]"`.
- Lint + types: `make lint` and `make typecheck`.
- Operator-attested live semantic sanity (billable — NOT run in CI): `rebar criteria eval project.failure-disposition-contract`; the frozen baseline evidence is `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/failure_disposition_sanity.json`. This — not the injected-solve arithmetic above — is what proves the real rubric classifies the seeded case correctly.
- Gate self-check: `rebar review-plan c789-e1bb-4c7b-496c` returns PASS (full rubric; non-test file_impact).
baseline.summary: Prevention (plan-review): new criterion — a plan that adds/alters failure/timeout/exception semantics must state its failure-disposition contract

baseline.description:
LLM completion-verification close gate: an optional, signed agentic gate that verifies a ticket's completion criteria are met before closure.

## Context
rebar ships an optional LLM agent-operations framework (`rebar.llm`: review_ticket / review_code / scan_epics_for_spec) over library/CLI/MCP, plus an environment-bound HMAC signing module (`rebar.signing`: sign_manifest / verify_signature, with key-fingerprint attribution and HEAD binding) and an opt-in story/epic close `_signature_gate`. This epic adds a **completion-verifier** agent (adapted from the DSO `completion-verifier`) that, on a close attempt, verifies every acceptance/success/close/completion criterion (and, for bugs, that the bug is resolved) is demonstrably met, then — on PASS — produces a **signed** completion attestation that the close gate certifies.

Trust model (per design): security is only meaningful when rebar runs as the MCP server, whose environment signing key is canonical; CLI/library installs sign with a local key that CI reads as `foreign_key` (accepted-as-insecure by design). CI verifies the attestation under the MCP server's key. `--force-close` closes the ticket but withholds the signature, so a closed-without-signature ticket is the durable signal that validation did not pass.

This is distinct from (but composes with) epic 8a1c (cryptographic gate hardening / protected tags).

## What changes
- A pluggable per-operation structured-output **contract** (the runner stops hardcoding the findings model; each op/workflow selects its contract via `output_schema`).
- A `completion_verdict` schema + contract: `{verdict: PASS|FAIL, findings[], summary}` where each FAIL finding cites the failing criterion, an explanation, and (if applicable) a source-code citation.
- A `completion-verifier` reviewer prompt covering epics/stories/tasks/bugs (read-only fs + read-only rebar ticket access).
- `verify_completion` operation over library/CLI/MCP (MCP gated by `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`).
- A close-time gate (`verify.require_completion_verification_for_close`, default off) that runs the verifier OUTSIDE the write lock, blocks on FAIL/missing-LLM (fail-closed, `--force-close` bypass), and signs the verdict on PASS.
- Enable the gate + LLM module in THIS project's rebar config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pluggable output contract: runner builds the structured-output model from `RunRequest`/step `output_schema` (default = findings), registry-based and tested.
- [ ] `completion_verdict.schema.json` added + registered in the schemas registry; Pydantic mirror pinned by a test.
- [ ] `completion-verifier` reviewer prompt added (catalog + packaged `*.md`); handles epic/story/task/bug; bug → "resolved" check.
- [ ] `verify_completion` exposed on library (`rebar.llm.verify_completion`), CLI (`rebar verify-completion`), and gated MCP (`verify_completion`).
- [ ] Close gate wired into `transition_compute` (outside lock, lazy import): FAIL or missing-LLM blocks (fail-closed) with `--force-close` bypass; PASS signs via `sign_manifest` then closes; force-close skips verify+sign.
- [ ] `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` typed config flag (default off) with coercion + tests.
- [ ] This project's tracked `rebar.toml` enables the gate (`[verify] require_completion_verification_for_close`) + `[mcp] allow_llm` (`.rebar/config.conf` is git-ignored, so a tracked config is used).
- [ ] Docs updated (docs/llm-framework.md + CLAUDE.md tool set); optionality + schema-pin + gate-behavior + fake-runner tests pass.
- [ ] Closing a task/story/epic/bug with the gate on runs the verifier; PASS attaches a certified signature and the close proceeds; FAIL blocks with findings.
- [ ] `--force-close="reason"` closes without running the verifier and without a signature (no signed confirmation of passing validation).
- [ ] The optionality contract still holds: `import rebar` / `import rebar.llm` pull no heavy deps; a missing `[agents]` extra degrades cleanly on every interface.
- [ ] Each operation/workflow can declare its own output contract; findings remains the default; `completion_verdict` is the first alternate.
- [ ] This project's config enables the gate and the LLM module.
baseline.summary: LLM completion-verification close gate (signed, optional)

## What

Three follow-ups spun out of dc3f (puzzling-obsidian-bunny) after its core gap — 3 undeployed CloudWatch alarms — was fixed by a terraform apply: (1) confirm the alert SNS subscription actually delivers, (2) add terraform drift-detection CI so committed-but-unapplied HCL cannot sit unnoticed (the root cause of dc3f), and (3) bring a live-but-unmanaged alarm under IaC.

These are bundled deliberately: all three harden the SAME alerting/IaC chain for the rebar-gerrit host and are small. Each AC below names a single unambiguous disposition (no open design choice left to the executor).

## Scope

- rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS email subscription (the alert sink).
- No terraform CI exists (apply is manual per infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md), so committed
  HCL can silently sit unapplied — the dc3f root cause.
- One live alarm (rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high) exists in AWS but is absent from HCL/state and has
  an EMPTY alarm_actions list (never notifies).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] AC1 — SNS subscription delivers. The rebar-gerrit-alerts email
  subscription to joeoakhart@navapbc.com is CONFIRMED (not PendingConfirmation) so alarms
  actually deliver. Evidence: a ticket comment recording the get-subscription-attributes result
  (PendingConfirmation=false) with the SubscriptionArn and date. NOTE: verified 2026-07-11 —
  PendingConfirmation=false; this AC is already met and needs NO destructive replacement sink.
- [ ] AC2a — OIDC role (least-privilege, plan-only). The GitHub OIDC provider
  (token.actions.githubusercontent.com) ALREADY EXISTS in account 896586841071 (verified); this
  ticket adds a NEW IAM role `rebar-terraform-plan` in infra/terraform/iam.tf whose trust policy
  is scoped to `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` (sub condition) with aud=sts.amazonaws.com, and whose
  permissions are AWS-managed ReadOnlyAccess + one inline statement granting kms:Decrypt
  constrained by kms:ViaService=ssm (for the alert-endpoint SecureString data source). No apply
  or write permissions — plan-only, least privilege.
- [ ] AC2b — drift-detection CI. `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` runs
  `terraform plan -input=false -lock=false -detailed-exitcode` in infra/terraform, authenticating
  via GitHub OIDC to `rebar-terraform-plan`. `-detailed-exitcode` makes a non-empty plan (exit 2)
  FAIL the check. Triggers: pull_request touching infra/terraform/**, push to main touching
  infra/terraform/** (catches already-committed-but-unapplied drift, not just PR diffs), a daily
  schedule, and workflow_dispatch.
- [ ] AC3 — codify + import the orphan alarm (keep coverage; non-destructive). Add
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high` (name rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high;
  namespace rebar/host, metric disk_used_percent published by observability.sh, dims
  InstanceId=data.aws_instance.gerrit.id + mount=/var/gerrit, threshold 85, GTE) to
  infra/terraform/monitoring.tf WITH alarm_actions/ok_actions = the SNS topic (closing the
  silent-alarm gap), then `terraform import` it into state so HCL/state/reality agree. The alarm
  is KEPT (data-volume disk pressure is real coverage), not deleted.

## Verification

- AC1: `aws sns get-subscription-attributes` shows PendingConfirmation=false (recorded as a
  comment).
- AC2/AC3: `terraform validate` passes and `terraform plan` (ReadOnlyAccess creds) shows the new
  role/policies/alarm apply cleanly with no errors — run pre-merge in the worktree.
- Post-merge operator step (needs live creds): `terraform import
  aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` then
  `terraform apply` to wire the alarm actions and create the role; the terraform-drift CI then
  reports green (no drift) on the next run.

## Notes / decisions (resolve prior plan-review BLOCKs)

- Shared S3 state backend (rebar-tfstate-896586841071) means terraform writes (import/apply) MUST
  follow the HCL merge — importing to shared state before merge would make an un-branched plan
  read the alarm as "to destroy". So this ticket lands the reviewed HCL/CI via Gerrit; the
  import/apply is the documented post-merge operator step above.
- AC1's original "OR replace with a confirmation-free sink" option is dropped: the subscription is
  already confirmed, so no destructive substitution (which risked dark alerting) is needed.
baseline.summary: rebar-gerrit alerting hardening: confirm/replace SNS subscription + add terraform drift CI

## Context
The exhaustive current-main macOS census found remaining multi-second costs caused by test-scale wall-clock windows rather than useful production work: review-bot ticket bootstrap is about 10.15 worker-phase seconds per cell, lock-retry coverage totals about 15.56s per cell, review-bot shutdown cases are about 9s per cell, and autodeploy coverage includes an explicit 3s sleep plus an 8.25s unreachable-health case. Production timeout, retry, drain, and health budgets are contractual and must remain unchanged.

Closed classless-dainty-lamprey already proved and landed the same pattern for snapshot low-speed and retry tests. Maintained OSS consensus supports the direction: CPython uses 0.05-0.1s trigger windows with generous cleanup deadlines, and urllib3 injects or scales backoff while retaining real sockets. Ticket history requires retaining real subprocess, lock, process-group, and health behavior: royal-weariless-zebrafish, odorful-epidemic-shelduck, balsamy-eloquent-iggypops, equestrian-clueless-cowbird, and unskillful-supportive-lion.

## Plan
- Reprofile each named family alone on current main and record wall and worker-phase baselines.
- Freeze behavioral contract cards for attempt counts, logical backoff schedules, real lock/process/socket behavior, terminal states, cleanup, and exact error/observability output.
- Inject or scale only test-owned clocks/windows; retain real boundary execution and generous teardown polling.
- Prove each final oracle RED against an exact-defect mutation before implementation, then GREEN.
- Run focused suites, lint, typecheck, and full Gerrit Verify; report per-cell and aggregate runner savings and the first post-merge organic observation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Production timeout, retry, drain, health, and backoff defaults are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [x] Real subprocess, lock, process-group, and health boundary coverage remains enabled.
- [x] Each shortened case preserves attempt counts, logical schedule, terminal state, cleanup, and observability assertions.
- [x] Each case has legitimate RED-to-GREEN and exact-defect mutation evidence.
- [x] Same-host before/after timings report macOS wall and total runner savings.
- [x] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and merge are recorded before closure.
baseline.summary: Shorten remaining test-only real-time windows without changing production budgets
