# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review … [truncated by reconciler]

## Why
The delivered epic (Gerrit stack 558/560/561/563/576/579/580/581, NOT landed) diverged from the APPROVED epic design on the authorship-payload format. bde5 (change 561, commit c31fc7eb5) signs the event's RAW canonical bytes; the approved epic AC requires an **in-toto Statement** payload whose `subject` binds `{event_uuid, content_hash}`. This story transitions the authorship *machinery* to the approved design. (User rejected the delivered design; full divergence record in session_log d7c0.)

## Stack scoping (why this story is authorship.py ONLY)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 561 = commit c31fc7eb5 (bde5), which touches `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` and NOTHING else. At that commit the authorship functions have **no consumers yet**: the write-time signing call site (`_seam.py`), the merge-gate content-binding (`verify_authorship.py`), and the SNAPSHOT ledger (`compact.py`) are all introduced later in commit 721702e91 (3183). Therefore the consumer cutover to the in-toto payload — and the epic-AC-named `create_placeholder` alias (which wraps `ensure_identity_for`, introduced in commit ec3aff507 / 2f13) — is handled in **TS3 (117b, change 580)**, the story that reworks that commit. Keeping the edits in the commit where the symbols actually exist is what keeps every intermediate patchset internally green.

## What (authorship.py machinery)
Add the in-toto Statement layer as NEW functions, and PRESERVE the existing low-level primitive so KEY-op signing (`identity.py._verify_keyop_signature`, which signs `keyop_payload` bytes, not events) and any other caller keep compiling unchanged:

- KEEP `sign_authorship(payload, key_path, principal)` and `verify_authorship(envelope,
  identity_id)` as the low-level SSHSIG-over-DSSE primitive (used by KEY-op signatures).
- `authorship_content_hash(event: dict) -> str`: **SHA-256, lowercase hex** over the
  event's canonical JSON with the `author_sig` key EXCLUDED (the signature never covers
  itself).
- `build_authorship_statement(event_uuid, content_hash) -> dict`: an in-toto Statement:
  - `_type`: `"https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1"`
  - `subject`: `[{ "name": "<event_uuid>", "digest": { "sha256": "<content_hash>" } }]`
  - `predicateType`: `"application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json"`
  - `predicate`: `{}`
- `sign_event_authorship(event: dict, key_path, principal) -> dsse.Envelope`: computes the
  content_hash, builds the Statement, and signs its canonical JSON bytes via the primitive
  (DSSE payloadType `application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json`, PAE-signed under the pinned
  authorship namespace). The Statement JSON is the DSSE payload.
- `verify_event_authorship(event: dict, envelope, identity_id, *, repo_root=None) ->
  Verdict`: (1) parse the DSSE payload as an in-toto Statement, (2) check
  `subject[0].name == event['uuid']` AND `subject[0].digest.sha256 ==
  authorship_content_hash(event)`, (3) THEN verify the DSSE signature against the identity's
  in-band keys (reusing `resolve_trust_root`). Any parse/shape failure or subject/hash
  mismatch yields a non-verified Verdict; it NEVER raises on a lookup problem (mirrors the
  existing fail-closed contract).

## Scope
In: the in-toto Statement authorship machinery in `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (content_hash + Statement build + `sign_event_authorship` + `verify_event_authorship`), with the low-level `sign_authorship`/`verify_authorship` primitive preserved for KEY-ops. Out: the write-seam stamping + merge-gate content-binding + SNAPSHOT ledger cutover to the new payload AND the `create_placeholder` alias (all TS3/3183, commit 721702e91); the era/validity model (TS2/e165); docs/ADR (TS4/b134).

## Landing / sequencing
TS1–TS4 land as ONE ATOMIC Gerrit stack submit (relation chain), so there is no runtime window where a reworked commit is live without the others. Write-time signing is opt-in and the stack is unlanded, so no persisted event carries an old-format `author_sig` — no migration/backfill. Docs/ADR for this pivot are rewritten in TS4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sign_event_authorship` produces a DSSE envelope whose payload is an in-toto
  Statement (`_type` https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1, `predicateType`
  application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json) with `subject[0] = {name: event_uuid,
  digest: {sha256: content_hash}}`; a test asserts the structure + payloadType.
- [ ] `authorship_content_hash` is SHA-256 hex over the canonical event with `author_sig`
  EXCLUDED; a test proves adding/removing an `author_sig` key does not change the hash,
  and mutating any other field DOES change it.
- [ ] `verify_event_authorship` returns verified for an event signed by identity A against
  A's in-band keys; a test asserts it does NOT verify against identity B, FAILS on a
  tampered event body (content_hash mismatch), and FAILS on a tampered signature.
- [ ] `verify_event_authorship` returns a non-verified Verdict (never raises) when the
  envelope payload is not a valid in-toto Statement (malformed / missing subject) and when
  the identity is unknown/keyless (test).
- [ ] The low-level `sign_authorship(payload,...)` primitive is unchanged: a KEY-op-style
  signature over `keyop_payload(...)` bytes still verifies via the primitive path (test),
  proving the Statement layer did not break KEY-op signing.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (in-toto Statement build/parse + content_hash + event sign/verify; primitive preserved)
baseline.summary: transition: authorship payload -> in-toto Statement (subject binds {event_uuid, content_hash})

# J5 — A Dockerized Jira harness as the Data Center verification oracle

## Context / Problem

There is no way to buy a Jira Data Center license to test against: Atlassian ended new DC purchases on 30 March 2026 and no longer issues DC trial licenses. There is also **no official OpenAPI/Swagger spec for Jira DC** — Atlassian publishes only WADL, and the long-standing requests for one (JRASERVER-65954, JRASERVER-68539) remain open — so spec-driven contract testing is unavailable. Cloud's v3 swagger is not a substitute: different auth, ADF vs wiki markup, accountId vs name. Without an oracle, a DC adapter is unverifiable except against fakes that encode our own assumptions.

## Approach

Use the **purpose-built test image the pycontribs/jira project uses for exactly this problem** — a thin wrapper over `addono/jira-software-standalone` that stands up a real Jira 8.17.1 at `http://localhost:2990/jira` with default credentials `admin`/`admin`. It is unaffected by the DC trial shutdown, and it is the substrate the most widely used Python Jira client validates itself against. Jira 8.17.1 is **≥ 8.14**, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so the PAT bearer auth the DC transport uses is exercised for real.

**The image must be BUILT, not pulled — corrected against the registry, not assumed.** An earlier draft of this plan said to `docker run pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and called it "a pinned, pullable image". That is false and was verified false before this plan was rewritten:

- `docker pull pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` → `pull access denied ... repository does not exist`.
- The Docker Hub API for `pycontribs/jira-test-image` returns `{"message": "object not found"}`. The
  `pycontribs` Hub namespace contains exactly seven repositories, all OS base images (centos, fedora, ubuntu,
  debian, alpine, opensuse, voidlinux). There is no `jira-test-image`.
- That tag is a **local build name**. `pycontribs/jira` carries `docker/jira-test-image/{Dockerfile,README.md}`,
  and the upstream README's own instruction is
  `docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image`. It is published to no registry.
- Its base, `addono/jira-software-standalone`, **is** pullable, and the exact digest pycontribs pins
  (`sha256:04326628dc4ac36b2bfc1d0f2ebe5ba3807c1ec9cf9b18307d3c2ad7222537e9`) resolves.

Feasibility was proven before this rewrite: the upstream Dockerfile was fetched and built on the target host (879 MB image, container starts and stays up). So the oracle is real; only the acquisition mechanism changes.

**Decision: vendor a ~15-line Dockerfile in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`** that `FROM`s the addono base **by digest** and reproduces the two things the upstream wrapper adds, with attribution to pycontribs/jira in a comment. Rationale: building from a third-party repo at test time would make the harness depend on another project's directory layout and default branch staying put; vendoring the few lines is self-documenting and pins our own supply chain. The alternative — a `git clone` of pycontribs/jira in the fixture — is rejected for that reason.

**Three details are load-bearing and must survive into the vendored file as comments**, because each looks like removable noise and each breaks the harness if removed:

1. **`-DskipAllPrompts=true` on the `atlas-run` ENTRYPOINT is MANDATORY.** Atlassian shut down the Marketplace
   v1 REST endpoint that AMPS hardcodes for its SDK update check, so without this flag **every cold container
   start** fails with `FileNotFoundException` on `https://marketplace.atlassian.com/rest/1.0/plugins/...`. The
   failure looks like a transient network fault, so a maintainer "tidying" the flag away would produce a
   confusing, seemingly-flaky breakage.
2. **`-dit` (equivalently compose's `tty: true` + `stdin_open: true`) is REQUIRED** — AMPS exits without a
   controlling TTY. A plain compose service block is not sufficient.
3. **Only Jira 8.x is supported.** `JIRA_VERSION` is overridable across 8.x patch versions, but 9+/11+ fail
   Maven resolution because the upstream pom is anchored to the 8.x dependency graph. The README must say so,
   or a future reader will assume the harness can track a client's newer Jira by bumping a variable.

**The image does NOT contain Jira — `atlas-run` downloads it at runtime.** Verified by running it: the container log shows `Configured Artifact: com.atlassian.jira.plugins:jira-plugin-test-resources:8.17.1:zip` followed by ~917 `Downloading from atlassian-public: https://maven.atlassian.com/...` lines before Tomcat and H2 come up. Four consequences the harness must design around:

- **Egress to `maven.atlassian.com` is a hard RUNTIME dependency**, not a one-time image pull. An
  egress-restricted CI runner cannot start this harness at all.
- **`pinning the image digest does NOT pin Jira itself`.** If Atlassian withdraws the 8.17.1 artifacts from
  their public Maven repo, the harness stops working despite our pinned base digest. That, not the image, is
  the real fragility, and the README must say so — it also strengthens the case for the separately-tracked
  real-instance validation (`9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`).
- First start is dominated by that download, so the readiness budget must cover a large artifact fetch, not
  just JVM boot.
- The fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache (`~/.m2`) as a volume, or every fresh container
  re-downloads ~900 artifacts.

**No licensing claim is made.** An earlier draft said the image "carries its own license". That is a legal characterization this story has not verified, so it is replaced by the observed behaviour: no license key is supplied to build or start the instance, and the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run` provisions a local developer instance. The README states it that way.

**Local runs on Apple Silicon are the constrained path, and were measured.** Three attempts on an arm64 workstation failed: two killed by Cargo's default 600000 ms deploy ceiling, and a third — with `-Dproduct.start.timeout` correctly lifting that ceiling — still never reached Jira startup in 55 minutes. Two compounding causes, both recorded so a future reader does not repeat the runs: (a) the amd64 base under arm64 **emulation**, and (b) **resource starvation** — the colima VM was 2 vCPU / 4 GiB with seven other containers already resident, against a Jira that wants ~2 GB of heap by itself. A local run therefore needs BOTH a larger, Rosetta-backed VM (e.g. `colima start --cpu 6 --memory 12 --vm-type vz --vz-rosetta`) AND spare capacity; since that restarts the VM and evicts every running container, it is an operator decision, not something the harness can assume. Prefer the CI job.

**Platform is a real variable, not a footnote.** The base image is `linux/amd64`. On an `arm64` host (Apple Silicon, ARM CI runners) it runs under emulation, and the upstream README's "first responsive request within ~3-5 minutes" does not hold — observed startup on an emulated arm64 host is materially slower. So the compose file sets `platform: linux/amd64` **explicitly** (making behaviour deterministic instead of dependent on the host's default resolution), and the readiness probe's timeout is generous and overridable by env var rather than a hardcoded few minutes. The README records that a native-amd64 runner is strongly preferred.

**Stated limitation, deliberately accepted:** 8.17.1 is older than the version a client such as CMS is likely running, so this harness proves REST v2 protocol semantics, not deployment-specific behavior (workflow names, custom fields, permission schemes, user directories). Closing that gap requires access to the real instance and is tracked separately as ticket `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`; this story's README records the exact image tag so that comparison has a baseline.

Add the harness under **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`** with a compose file, a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST, and a fixture that provisions a scratch project and tears down everything it created.

**The tier is `external`, NOT `integration` — corrected against the CI workflow.** An earlier draft marked these `integration`, reasoning that `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (**`Makefile:178`** — verified; an earlier draft cited 154, which is inside the `actionlint-bin` recipe) and so would exclude them. That reasoning is wrong, and dangerously so: `_build-and-test.yml` runs **`pytest -m integration` as its own dedicated CI step on every commit** ("Run the integration tier (concurrency + reconciler; network-guarded)"), explicitly because those tests "need no live services (mocked acli / local git)". So the `integration` marker is an **INCLUSION into CI**, not an exclusion — Docker-requiring tests marked that way would be collected and run on every commit against a runner with no container, no Jira and no egress, breaking CI for everyone.

The `external` tier is the one genuinely fenced off, and it is enforced structurally rather than by convention: `tests/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` (a) **auto-applies** the `external` marker to every item under `tests/external/`, so no per-file marker is needed, and (b) **hard-fails collection** if any item carries `external` while living outside `tests/external/` — so a live test cannot hide elsewhere in the tree. `external` runs only from `external-integration.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` + a weekly cron), never on a commit. Living under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` therefore satisfies the gating requirement AND supplies the structural backstop for free.

**Living under `tests/external/` means INHERITING that tier's contract — three mechanisms, all enumerated here because each silently changes how this suite behaves:**

1. **`_require_external_opt_in` (autouse, `tests/external/conftest.py`) SKIPS every test under
   `tests/external/` unless `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`.** It is a deliberate leak-guard (bug
   `4a48-6dd5-aef3-4c8e`): external tests must stay inert on a default invocation even when credentials happen
   to be present. Consequence for this story: `make jira-dc-up && pytest tests/external/live_jira_dc/` **skips
   everything** without the env var. The README must lead with the full invocation, and the readiness probe's
   error message is only reachable in an opted-in run.
2. **The `_live_jira_ready` sentinel drives the `jira_live` auto-marker and the all-skip canary.**
   `tests/external/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` applies `jira_live` to any module defining a
   module-level `_live_jira_ready`, and `pytest_sessionfinish` **fails the session** when at least one
   `jira_live` test was collected but none executed — the guard against a scheduled run that validated nothing.
   Every existing live-Jira module defines it (`test_reconcile_live.py`, `test_link_sync_live.py`,
   `test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`, `test_verified_fake_contract_live.py`). **`test_harness_smoke.py` MUST
   define `_live_jira_ready` too**, or it opts out of the canary and a silently-all-skipped harness run would
   look green.
3. **`_allow_live_model_requests`** re-enables pydantic-ai's global kill-switch for this tier. Irrelevant to
   this harness (it makes no model calls) but noted so the inherited fixture set is fully accounted for.

**Skip-vs-fail is settled here, because the tier forces it.** An earlier draft's "failure path" said the suite should FAIL with a "harness not running" message when the instance is down. That is wrong for this tier and would break the existing `external-integration.yml` job, which already runs `pytest -m external tests/external` with no Docker anywhere. The correct contract: **absent harness ⇒ SKIP with a clear, actionable message** (naming `make jira-dc-up` and `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`), and the **canary** — not a hard failure — is what prevents a vacuous green, because a run that collected `jira_live` tests and executed none fails the session. That gives both properties: no CI breakage when Docker is absent, and no silent nothing-ran success.

Teardown follows **`docs/adr/0037-reconciler-live-validation-harness.md` §3** (named in full because FIVE ADRs share the `0037-` prefix — code-review-novelty-convergence, cross-ticket-overlap, oss-contribution-intake-posture, reconciler-live-validation-harness, transport-retry — so a bare "ADR 0037" is unresolvable), which **prohibits post-deletion search-index assertions** because Jira's index lags creates and deletes by an unbounded interval and can return stale results either way. So the teardown oracle is not "query the project and find it empty": it asserts each delete call's HTTP status and then polls each issue's **direct REST endpoint** (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}`) until it returns 404, which is index-independent.

**Alternative rejected: fixtures and a stateful fake alone.** rebar's test-design standard allows a verified fake for external-service mapping, but a fake verified only against fixtures we recorded cannot falsify assumptions we never thought to record — transitions, permission errors, link direction. The fake is still built (J6 uses it for fast unit tests); this story gives it something real to be verified against.

**Alternative rejected: reusing pycontribs/jira's test assertions as the oracle.** Their tests assert their client's behavior, not rebar's field mapping. The reusable asset is the image and harness pattern, which is what this story takes.

**Alternative rejected: the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run-standalone`.** It also yields a licensed local Jira, but it needs the full SDK toolchain and its licenses are short-lived (3-day timebombs requiring `atlas-mvn clean` recycling), which is hostile to repeatable CI. A pinned Docker image has neither problem.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile` (new) — the vendored wrapper: `FROM` the addono base **by digest**, the
  `-DskipAllPrompts=true` entrypoint, and the three rationale comments above plus attribution to
  pycontribs/jira.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`, `conftest.py`, `README.md` (new) — compose `build`s the local
  Dockerfile (it does NOT reference an unpullable image), sets `platform: linux/amd64`, `tty: true`,
  `stdin_open: true`, mounts a persistent Maven cache volume, and publishes
  **`127.0.0.1:2990:2990`** — loopback-scoped, NOT the bare `2990:2990` an earlier draft said, which Docker
  binds on `0.0.0.0` and would expose a well-known-`admin`/`admin` Jira to the whole network.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_harness_smoke.py` (new).
- **`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` — a NEW, SEPARATE job, modelled on the `langfuse-trace` job
  that already exists in this same file.** This is the key practical finding: the workflow ALREADY implements
  this exact shape at lines ~159-251 for an ephemeral self-hosted Langfuse — `docker compose ... up -d`, poll
  until healthy with an `::error::` + `logs --tail` on timeout, run the tests, dump logs `if: failure()`, and
  `docker compose ... down -v` under `if: always()`. So the Jira job is a direct adaptation of a working
  in-repo precedent rather than novel CI engineering; copy its structure and swap the compose file, the health
  URL (`/jira/rest/api/2/serverInfo`) and the test path.

  **`ubuntu-latest` resolves the platform problem entirely.** GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners are native
  **x86_64**, so the amd64 base image runs WITHOUT emulation — which was the sole reason this harness could not
  be verified on an Apple-Silicon workstation. rebar is a PUBLIC repo, so the standard runner is 4 vCPU /
  16 GB, comfortably above Jira 8.17.1's needs. And because this workflow triggers only on
  `workflow_dispatch` + a weekly cron, a 10-20 minute harness never touches per-commit CI.
  **CI — specifically a new job in this workflow — is therefore the PRIMARY intended home for this harness's
  acceptance evidence**, and a local run is the optional convenience path, not the reverse. This workflow is an unenumerated
  consumer in earlier drafts: at line 141 it already runs `pytest -m external tests/external -q`, so the new
  directory is collected by it the moment the files land, and it has **no** docker build/up/down steps. It also
  gates its existing job on an LLM API key, which this harness does not need. So the harness gets its **own
  job** (not an extension of the LLM-keyed one) that: builds the vendored Dockerfile, brings the instance up,
  waits on the readiness probe, runs ONLY `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and tears down in an `if: always()`
  step. It must run on a **native amd64 runner** (see the platform note above). The pre-existing job is left
  alone, and because the harness tests skip cleanly without `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` plus a reachable instance,
  its collection of them stays harmless.
- `Makefile` — a `jira-dc-up` target only; the `test:` target is NOT modified (the `integration` marker is
  already excluded by its existing `-m` expression at **`Makefile:178`**), and `jira-dc-up` is added to the
  `.PHONY` list at `Makefile:30` — without that, a file or directory named `jira-dc-up` would make the target
  silently no-op.

## Testing

Real-external-service tier by construction — this story *is* the harness. Its own oracle is that the harness starts, is usable, and provably cleans up.

- happy path: the harness starts, the readiness probe reports REST answering, and a smoke test creates and
  reads back one issue through raw REST v2.
- auth path: a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via
  `Authorization: Bearer`, proving the DC auth mode the transport will use is exercised, not assumed.
- teardown oracle (index-independent, per ADR 0037 §3): after a deliberately failing test, every issue the
  fixture created returns 404 from its direct `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}` endpoint, and each delete call's HTTP
  status was 2xx. Search is never consulted.
- gating oracle: `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` collects zero tests from
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — and, separately, the `external` marker is auto-applied by
  `tests/external/conftest.py` rather than written per-file, with misplacement hard-failing collection.
- canary participation: `test_harness_smoke.py` defines `_live_jira_ready`, so its tests carry `jira_live` and
  an opted-in run in which every one of them skipped **fails the session** instead of reporting a vacuous pass.
- failure path (absent harness): with the instance down, the suite **SKIPS** with a message naming
  `make jira-dc-up` and `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` — not a raw connection traceback, and not a hard failure, which
  would break the pre-existing `external` CI job that has no Docker.

**The `allow_insecure` obligation is NOT this story's — it belongs to J6/J7.** A draft of this plan added an AC requiring every live test here to set `allow_insecure = true` and assert the cleartext warning. That was wrong on two counts, recorded so nobody restores it: (a) the `allow_insecure` config key and its warning-emitting validator DO NOT EXIST yet — they are **J6's** deliverable ([rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], which already carries exactly that AC), so J5 could not satisfy it while J6 is open, contradicting this story's whole point of being independently claimable; and (b) it does not even apply here — J5's smoke tests speak **raw REST v2** to the instance and never construct rebar's DC backend or read rebar's config, so no validator is on their path. The epic's step-7 obligation attaches to the stories whose live tests drive rebar's DC transport against this harness (J6/J7), which is where it is already recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the harness **builds from the vendored `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile`** and starts (via the compose
      file or the `jira-dc-up` target), and the readiness probe reports REST v2 answering at
      `http://localhost:2990/jira`. The criterion is explicitly BUILD-and-start, not pull-and-start: no
      acceptance step may depend on `pycontribs/jira-test-image` being pullable, because it is not published
- [ ] the vendored `Dockerfile` pins the addono base **by digest** (not by tag), keeps
      `-DskipAllPrompts=true` on the `atlas-run` entrypoint, and carries a comment explaining that removing
      that flag breaks every cold start via the retired Marketplace v1 endpoint
- [ ] the compose service sets `platform: linux/amd64`, `tty: true` and `stdin_open: true`, and the readiness
      timeout is env-overridable — so an emulated arm64 host is slow rather than spuriously failing
- [ ] a smoke test creates and reads back an issue via REST v2, and a PAT-authenticated request succeeds
- [ ] `test_harness_smoke.py` defines a module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel, so its tests receive the
      `jira_live` marker from `tests/external/conftest.py` and participate in the all-skip canary — an opted-in
      run where every harness test skipped must FAIL the session rather than report a vacuous pass
- [ ] with no instance running, the suite SKIPS with a message naming BOTH `make jira-dc-up` and
      `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` (the tier's autouse opt-in guard), and does NOT fail — verified by running the
      directory with the harness down, which must not break the pre-existing `external` CI job
- [ ] `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gains a SEPARATE amd64 job that builds the Dockerfile,
      waits on the readiness probe, runs only `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and tears down under
      `if: always()`. The pre-existing LLM-keyed job keeps its steps, secrets and gating untouched with
      exactly ONE deliberate exception: `--ignore=tests/external/live_jira_dc` is added to its pytest
      invocation. That exception is required and was decided during execution (recorded in this ticket's
      comments): `tests/external/conftest.py`'s all-skip canary counts `jira_live` items GLOBALLY, and that
      job runs `pytest -m external tests/external` over the whole tree with live Cloud creds. Without the
      flag the DC tests are collected there, skip for want of a harness, and their all-skip is MASKED by the … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: J5 — a Dockerized Jira harness as the Data Center verification oracle

baseline.description:
Build a behavioral CONFORMANCE ORACLE that mechanically asserts write-op parity across the lib, CLI, and MCP adapters, so surface drift is caught without an LLM, without a change-detector, and without a hand-maintained NxM matrix. It implements the behavioral-oracle design validated by a session prototype (design + empirical results recorded on ticket restoring-shallow-blobfish; the prototype script is a throwaway session artifact, NOT a committed repo file, so this ticket builds the durable suite from scratch rather than promoting a checked-in file).

## Context / Problem
The write ops (transition/claim/create) are exposed through three adapters — the Python lib, the CLI, and the MCP server — but their input surfaces are hand-mirrored. A param present on one can silently be missing on another (exactly the MCP gaps captured in sibling scratchy-leprous-galago: reason/caused_by/ref/force). Nothing mechanically guards against this drift today; it is caught only by chance or by LLM review.

## Approach
Build a durable pytest CONFORMANCE ORACLE (Pattern B, proven in OSS: Python DB-API / SQLAlchemy dialect compliance, the CommonMark spec suite, WSGI/ASGI validators). ONE transport-agnostic contract table holds rows of (op, inputs, expected accept | reject-with-rule, expected effect). Each row is executed through every adapter against a fresh temp store and classified ACCEPTED / REJECTED(rule) / PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED; any divergence between adapters on the same row fails the suite. This asserts BEHAVIOR — including the runtime conditional-required rules (close_class required iff bug-close; reason required for REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) — which shape/signature generation cannot express. We deliberately do NOT generate the surfaces (Pattern A): behavior is already single-sourced through composer.create_core / transition_compute / claim_compute, and the adapters carry irreducible hand-written value (MCP LLM-facing docstrings, CLI ergonomics), so regenerating them would risk agent/user-visible contract breaks.

The contract covers the SANCTIONED surface: `force` (str | None — the reason-carrying `--force[=<reason>]` param, matching `claim`), `reason` (str, close_reason role only), `caused_by`, `ref`, `close_class`. `force_close` is intentionally EXCLUDED from the contract — it is a redundant param being removed by sibling blusterous-earthly-kitten; the oracle tests the consolidated `--force[=<reason>]` bypass (force carries its own audit reason), not the legacy param.

Cross-ticket sequencing (declared, not undeclared): the reason-carrying `--force[=<reason>]` / `force: str | None` shape ALREADY exists on `claim` today, but on `transition` it is INTRODUCED by blusterous-earthly-kitten (today transition's lib force is a bool + separate reason + force_close). The oracle therefore encodes the transition coupled-force rows as strict-xfail citing blusterous-earthly-kitten — exactly the same mechanism as the MCP gaps below — so the suite is GREEN in CI before blusterous lands and the rows xpass (forcing their un-xfail) once it does. This keeps the oracle independently landable in either order rather than hard-blocking on blusterous. Known current MCP gaps (reason/caused_by/force not exposed on transition_ticket/claim_ticket) are likewise encoded as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago, so the suite is GREEN in CI today and closing a gap makes the strict xfail fail (xpass) — the intended forcing function for cleanup. Because both scratchy (MCP) and blusterous (transition force) are in flight, the un-xfail of their rows is expected on convergence and is the signal to delete the corresponding xfail markers in the same or a fast-follow change; the oracle does not depend on either landing first.

## Scope
- tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py — new conformance suite.
- tests/interfaces/write_parity_contract.py — new shared contract table (the single source of cases).
- REUSE and EXTEND the existing three-adapter harness tests/interfaces/adapters.py (already imported across the interfaces tier): it provides `Outcome`, the `Adapter` protocol, and `LibraryAdapter` / `CliAdapter` / `McpAdapter` with a shared ACCEPTED/REJECTED rejection-identity mapping — exactly the substrate the oracle needs. The existing `transition(tid, current, target)` / `claim(tid, assignee=None)` signatures do NOT yet thread the write-op inputs under test, so extend the `Adapter` protocol and its three implementations to pass `force`, `reason`, `close_class`, `caused_by`, `ref` through each transport. Do NOT build fresh parallel drivers or reuse the ad-hoc _FakeMCP/_FakeCtx capture; the interfaces sandbox-repo bootstrap (tests/interfaces/conftest.py) already backs adapters.py.
- Cover the transition, claim, and create write ops across all three adapters via the extended adapters.py drivers.
- Treat source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root as adapter-bound internals (NOT contract params) so they do not register as false divergences.
- No CI-provider-specific trigger: runs as an ordinary pytest (portability).

## Testing
- Run `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py`: green in CI, with the current MCP reason/caused_by/force gaps recorded as strict-xfail rows referencing scratchy-leprous-galago.
- Include one reason-required bug-close row and one close_class-missing row to assert the runtime conditional rules behaviorally on every adapter (both REJECTED consistently across adapters).
- Include a negative-control row over an adapter-bound internal (e.g. source) to confirm it is NOT flagged as a divergence.
- A committed, re-runnable in-suite check (a simulated-parity fixture, not a one-time manual step) flips a strict-xfail row to xpass, proving the oracle detects convergence and would then require the marker's removal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A single shared contract table drives all three adapter drivers; adding a new op is one new row (verified by inspecting the module: one table, three drivers).
- [x] The contract covers `force`(str, the `--force[=<reason>]` reason-carrying param)+`reason`+`caused_by`+`ref`+`close_class` and does NOT include the legacy `force_close` param (grep the table).
- [x] `pytest tests/interfaces/test_write_parity_oracle.py` passes in CI, with the current MCP reason/caused_by/force gaps captured as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago (visible in the test output).
- [x] Runtime rules (close_class-required, reason-required) are asserted behaviorally for every adapter (the two rows exist and reject consistently).
- [x] Adapter-bound internals (source/return_alias/_creation_channel/repo_root) produce no false divergence (negative-control row passes).
- [x] The suite reuses and extends the existing tests/interfaces/adapters.py three-adapter harness (Outcome + Adapter protocol + Library/Cli/Mcp adapters), threading force/reason/close_class/caused_by/ref through it — no fresh parallel drivers (verified by inspecting imports).
- [x] The transition coupled-`--force[=<reason>]` rows keep the suite green regardless of landing order: they were designed as strict-xfail citing blusterous-earthly-kitten only while it was unlanded; blusterous LANDED before this oracle, so per the convergence protocol the marker is elided and those rows now pass normally on lib/CLI (the only remaining xfails cite scratchy-leprous-galago for the MCP gaps).
- [x] A committed, re-runnable simulated-parity check flips a strict-xfail row to xpass in-suite (not merely recorded as a ticket note), proving the oracle detects the fix.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green.
baseline.summary: Behavioral conformance oracle for write-op parity across lib/CLI/MCP adapters

## Context
Post-mortem of epic a88f (LLM Workflow Engine) via two validation subagents: a
coverage audit (behavioral+contractual × hermetic+external) and a prior-art
comparison (GHA / Argo / Inspect / dotprompt / tarfile CVE). Several verified
defects + coverage gaps to address.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] #1 bare `if:` (no `${{ }}`) no longer silently always-true (lint rejects)
- [ ] #4 duplicate YAML keys rejected by the loader
- [ ] #19 tarfile data_filter guarded on Python < 3.11.4
- [ ] #20/#21 snapshot proc.wait after kill; sweep restores write bits; file-count cap
- [ ] #24 JUnit wrapped in `<testsuites>` with quoteattr + failure body
- [ ] #25 eval grader snapshot cross-checked against model id
- [ ] #30/#31 prompt front-matter survives CRLF/BOM
- [ ] #32 declared-optional prompt vars default to empty (match schema)
- [ ] #33 variant overlay unions required/variables (no base-var drop)
- [ ] #14/#15/#16 runner doc-vs-impl drift removed (include_raw/parsing_error/pairing)
- [ ] run_eval raises NotImplementedError (not EvalError) when harness unwired
- [ ] external: live workflow-run test under tests/external (marked external)
- [ ] contract: CLI run/status/result `--output json` validates vs workflow_run schema
- [ ] golden: workflow.v1.schema.json + code_review.yaml frozen
- [ ] all new/changed paths covered by hermetic tests; full suite green
baseline.summary: Post-epic hardening: workflow engine prior-art gotchas + coverage gaps

baseline.description:
`update_priority` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:417`) accepts a keyword-only `acli_cmd: list[str] | None = None` and never reads it. The caller at `adapters/jira/acli.py:180` passes it **by keyword**:

```python
acli_cli_ops.update_priority(jira_key, priority_name, acli_cmd=acli_cmd)
```

The sibling path in the same module does honour it — `_verify_created_issue(result.stdout, acli_cmd=acli_cmd, client=client)` at `:410`.

## Be precise about what is and is not wrong

The function's docstring explains it deliberately bypasses ACLI:

> ACLI does not support priority edit — uses direct REST API:
> PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key} with {"fields":{"priority":{"name":"..."}}}

So `acli_cmd` — an ACLI invocation vector — is **structurally inapplicable** to this function, not merely unimplemented. The confirmed defect is therefore a signature that advertises a parameter it cannot use, with a caller passing it as though it matters. That is the same false-promise shape as `7504-a127-e9b0-42bb`.

## The open question that decides severity

Instead of using anything the caller supplied, the body resolves credentials ambiently:

```python
_s = acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings()
jira_url, user, api_token = _s.url, _s.user, _s.api_token
```

**If `acli_cmd` can encode a non-default Jira target** (a different site, instance, or credential set), then a deployment that configures one target would have priority updates go to the *ambient* target while every other write goes to the configured one — a cross-target write, which is a correctness bug rather than signature hygiene. **If `acli_cmd` only ever carries the ACLI binary path or invocation flags**, this reduces to removing a dead parameter.

This was NOT determined. Resolve it first; the remediation follows from the answer. Do not assume the benign reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Determine whether `acli_cmd` can encode a Jira target distinct from what
      `resolve_jira_settings()` returns; record the finding on this ticket with a citation
- [x] If it can: priority updates resolve their target the same way the rest of the adapter does,
      and a test pins that a non-default configured target is honoured
- [x] If it cannot: `acli_cmd` is removed from `update_priority`'s signature and from the call site
      at `acli.py:180`
- [x] Either way, no function in this module accepts a parameter it cannot act on
- [x] The docstring states how this REST path resolves credentials, since it differs from the
      ACLI-based siblings around it
baseline.summary: update_priority accepts acli_cmd and cannot use it; credential resolution is ambient

# S4 — RFC 7662 token-introspection verifier

## Why
Introspection completes the "validate against an external Authorization Server" story for providers that issue **opaque** access tokens (or where instant revocation matters) — Keycloak, Okta, Auth0, WorkOS all expose a standard `/introspect` endpoint. It is the pattern the SDK's own `simple-auth` example demonstrates.

## What
Add an **`IntrospectionTokenVerifier`** to `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, activated by including `introspection` in the `mcp.auth_strategies` list (the strategy-selection config key **introduced by S2**, this story's dependency — not a pre-existing seam), with flat config keys THIS story registers: `auth_introspection_endpoint`, `auth_introspection_client_id`, `auth_introspection_client_secret_env` (NAME of an env var holding the client secret — no plaintext secret in config), `auth_introspection_allow_private_host` (bool, default `false`), and `auth_introspection_allow_missing_aud` (bool, default `false`). It does not take a per-verifier audience — it validates against the single `auth_resource_server_url` (S2). It POSTs the token (RFC 7662) with client authentication, accepts only `active: true`, and maps the response into an `AccessToken` (all RFC 7662 response fields are OPTIONAL, so each has a defined fallback): `scope` (a space-delimited string per §2.2) is split into the scopes list (absent → empty list), `exp`→`expires_at` (absent → `None`, per Expiry below), `sub`→`subject` (absent → `None`), and `client_id`→`client_id` (absent → falls back to `sub`, else `"unknown"`); and stamps `resource=auth_resource_server_url` so the composite check passes. NOTE: the SDK's `IntrospectionTokenVerifier` is an **example, not an exported/hardened class** — this story WRITES its own (adapting the example), it does not import it. Adds the `auth_introspection_*` fields to the `McpConfig` dataclass + the `_SECTIONS['mcp']` coercer in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`; these auto-derive the `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_*` **env-var names**, which are added to `MCP_ENV_VARS` (in `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) and `server.json`; `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes. (The generated `mcp-reference.md`/`env-vars.md` are regenerated for the full key set by S7; S1 fixes the generators to iterate `MCP_ENV_VARS`.)

## Approach & rationale
Adapt the SDK `simple-auth` example (the blessed reference) and add the production hardening its docstring says it lacks: client authentication on the introspection call, strict audience handling, and fail-closed transport errors. Reuse the already-present `httpx`.

## Scope
The introspection verifier only, on the S2 seam. Subset of the epic. Depends on S2. Independent of S3/S5/S6.

## Security
Boundary-crossing. Requirements:
- Call the introspection endpoint over authenticated TLS (`client_secret_basic`, secret from
  `auth_introspection_client_secret_env`, which MUST be present and non-empty at startup or the
  verifier refuses to start — fail-closed), **HTTPS-only** (an `http://` endpoint is rejected at
  construction), a **bounded HTTP timeout (default connect 5s / read 10s)**. Private/link-local
endpoint hosts (RFC 1918, loopback,
  `169.254.0.0/16`) are **rejected by default**; an operator with a legitimate internal AS sets
  `auth_introspection_allow_private_host=true` to opt out.
- Accept only `active:true`. **Audience:** RFC 7662 §2.2 permits `aud` to be a JSON string OR an
  array of strings — the check passes if `auth_resource_server_url` equals the string form or is a
  member of the array form. If the AS omits `aud` (many do), the default is to **reject**
  (fail-closed); an operator whose AS scopes tokens to this resource by other means sets
  `auth_introspection_allow_missing_aud=true` to accept aud-absent tokens (documented risk in S7).
- **Fail-closed transport:** a non-200 status, a timeout, or a **malformed response** — a 200 whose
  body is not valid JSON, or valid JSON lacking a boolean `active` field — **raises** (composite
  treats as non-acceptance → deny); it never yields acceptance.
- **No caching in v1:** every request re-introspects the token with the AS, giving instant
  revocation. A positive-response cache (hashed key, bounded TTL) is a documented follow-on
  optimization, deliberately out of scope here to avoid the revocation-delay tradeoff.
- **Expiry:** when the response includes `exp`, set `AccessToken.expires_at` from it (a real
  positive value). When `active:true` but `exp` is absent (RFC 7662 permits it), set
  `expires_at=None` — validity is then bounded by re-introspection (every request re-checks the AS in v1). Never emit
  `expires_at=0` (the SDK reads a falsy value as no-expiry while looking like a set value).
- Tokens/secrets never logged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `auth_introspection_*` config fields exist in `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']`
      (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`); their derived `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_*` env-var names are
      present in `MCP_ENV_VARS` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) and `server.json`; and
      `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (observable oracle: the manifest drift test is green
      and both files contain the new env-var names).
- [ ] Unit test (tier: unit against the real verifier; the irreducible boundary — the introspection
      HTTP call — is a stateful fake fed production-shaped RFC 7662 responses) asserts an `active:true`
      response with a matching `aud` and an `exp` → an `AccessToken` with expected scopes,
      `resource==auth_resource_server_url`, and a positive `expires_at`; and that an `active:true`
      response OMITTING `exp` yields `expires_at=None` (never 0), with validity bounded by
      re-introspection (observable oracle: `expires_at is None`).
- [ ] Unit tests assert rejection for: `active:false` (returns None); a response OMITTING `aud` when
      `auth_introspection_allow_missing_aud=false` (fail-closed reject) — and acceptance of the same
      response when the key is `true`; a mismatched `aud`; and an `aud` supplied as an ARRAY that
      does/does not contain `auth_resource_server_url` (accept/reject respectively) — each a distinct
      negative control. Also assert `scope` given as a space-delimited string is split into the
      expected scopes list.
- [ ] Unit test asserts a non-200 status, a timeout, and a malformed response (200 body that is not
      valid JSON; and valid JSON lacking a boolean `active` field) each **raise** (→ composite
      non-acceptance/deny) and never yield acceptance, and that every request re-introspects with no
      caching in v1 (observable oracle: the stateful fake's request count increments once per request
      — two identical requests hit the fake twice).
- [ ] Unit test asserts construction-time guards: the introspection request carries
      `client_secret_basic` (secret sourced from `auth_introspection_client_secret_env`); an `http://`
      endpoint is rejected; and a private/link-local host is rejected by default and accepted only
      with `auth_introspection_allow_private_host=true` (observable oracle: the fake receives Basic
      auth; rejection at construction for the http/private cases). Also assert the verifier refuses
      to start when the env var named by `auth_introspection_client_secret_env` is absent or empty
      (observable oracle: startup raises a clear message).
- [ ] Component test (tier: component — the `IntrospectionTokenVerifier` inside a
      `CompositeTokenVerifier`, invoked through the composite's verify path, with the external
      `/introspect` endpoint as the SAME stateful fake) asserts an active, matching-audience token
      → an accepted `AccessToken`, and an `active:false`/absent token → None (→ composite deny).
      End-to-end HTTP behavior (401/200 through the ASGI transport) is exercised once for all
      verifiers by S2's transport harness, not re-tested here.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive verifier, opt-in via the `introspection` strategy. No change to other verifiers or stdio.
baseline.summary: S4 — RFC 7662 token-introspection verifier
