# Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

## Context / Problem

CMS and similar federal clients run **self-hosted Jira Data Center**, which rebar cannot reconcile against. DC differs from Cloud on three axes: REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies instead of v3 + ADF, Personal Access Token bearer auth instead of the ACLI subprocess, and name-based user identity instead of `accountId`.

GitHub PR #120 proposed a second adapter package for this. It rides ADR 0035's `Backend` port correctly, but it reaches into `adapters/jira/` privates (`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, `_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `classify_probe_response`) and forks `map_fields_to_remote` as a verbatim copy of `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` with one line changed. That creates a de facto "Jira family" layer with no contract: `adapters/jira/` becomes simultaneously a concrete backend and a shared library, with nothing pinning what is shared and nothing stopping a Cloud change from breaking DC.

## Approach

Make the Jira family an **explicit sub-seam** rather than an accident, in an order that never puts the live-validated Cloud path at risk.

1. **Freeze Cloud first.** Extend the existing held-out characterization tests
   (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`) to pin the current outputs of every unit
   about to move, so any behavior change during extraction fails a pinned oracle.
2. **Extract a `adapters/jira_family/` shared layer** — and re-point the Cloud adapter at it. Cloud's ACLI
   transport is not touched at all.

   **Only non-location-pinned symbols may physically move.** ADR 0035 §(a) pins `adf.py`,
   `outbound_fields.py`, and `comment_limits.py` as **Jira-coupled *and* location-pinned**: they are loaded by
   filename relative to `_PACKAGE_DIR` (via `_loader.lazy_load(` / `_load_sibling_keyed(` /
   `spec_from_file_location(`), so physically moving them breaks the dynamic loader unless the loader is taught
   the new sub-package in the same change — deferred to ADR 0035's Phase 2, explicitly **out of scope here**.
   **Location-pinned means "cannot change path" — NOT "cannot be edited."** Editing a pinned module's
   *contents* (e.g. replacing a dict literal with an import) is safe and is how the pinned units get
   single-sourced; only *relocating* the file breaks the loader.

   **Move by SYMBOL, not by file.** `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` cannot relocate wholesale: it imports
   `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from the pinned `adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
   `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from the pinned `comment_limits.py` (used by
   `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the whole file would point `jira_family/` at `adapters/jira/` — the exact
   dependency inversion the import contract in §6 forbids. So the file is split by symbol, and the two coupled
   sanitizers are **parameterized by the contracts this epic already introduces** rather than importing a
   vendor module: `_sanitize_description` takes the `RichTextCodec` (its `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the
   rich-text seam), and comment truncation takes the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract. Cloud
   constructs those contract objects in `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC
   constructs wiki-markup/plain-text equivalents. `jira_family/` imports neither.

   Concretely, of the six symbols PR #120 reached for:
   - **Movable to `jira_family/` in this epic:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
     and `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` (all in `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`, not location-pinned and not
     ADF/limit-coupled), `classify_probe_response` (`adapters/jira/probe.py`, not location-pinned), and the new
     `RichTextCodec` / `UserIdentityModel` contract objects.
   - **Moves to `jira_family/` only in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and
     `_sanitize_comment` — same observable behavior, but the ADF/limit dependency arrives as an injected
     contract instead of a direct import of a pinned module.

   - **Stays put (path-wise):** `_map_local_to_jira_fields` in the pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`,
     and the ADF encoder in the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. These are shared **by dependency-inverting
     instead of moving**: the pinned module is parameterized by the `jira_family` contracts (it imports *from*
     `jira_family/`, never the reverse), so DC reuses one implementation without any file relocating and
     without the loader changing. Any story that would *move* a pinned file must instead stop and record the
     blocker.

   One more unit needs parameterizing rather than sharing verbatim: `classify_probe_response` hardcodes
   `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})`. Those are Cloud/DIG workflow state
   names; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything. So the classifier moves to
   `jira_family/` taking the resolved-status set **as a parameter**, with Cloud passing today's frozenset
   (pinned unchanged by J1's oracle) and DC passing its own configured set. Sharing it with the Cloud names
   baked in would silently misclassify a DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED` when it is in fact resolved.
   The DC set is **operator-configured** via a `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config key (a list of workflow
   state names), defaulting to the same `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset so an operator whose workflow
   uses the conventional names configures nothing. Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not
   made configurable by this change.

   **The value maps are a special case — they are ALREADY duplicated, and this epic must not preserve the
   duplication.** There are today **three** independently-referenced copies of the local→Jira status map (and
   two of the priority map):
   - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the
     ACLI transport (`acli.py:69-70,143,171`; `acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354`).
   - `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (pinned): `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by
     the `Backend` port via `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
   - `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`: `local_to_jira_status` — the engine-level config copy.

   They have **already drifted**: `outbound_fields` and `config.py` both carry a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the
   `jira_fields` copy lacks. So simply moving the `jira_fields` copy to `jira_family/` would leave Cloud's
   backend still reading a second copy — the exact "two places" the epic exists to eliminate. This epic
   consolidates the two `adapters/` copies; `config.py`'s is folded in by bug `fe15` (its call sites are
   engine-level config, a wider blast radius than this epic's seam).

   **Resolution: `adapters/jira_family/` holds the ONE definition of each value map. Both current copies are
   deleted and replaced by imports from it** — `jira_fields.py` (whose map literals move out, the file itself
   staying put for its ADF/limit-coupled sanitizers) and `outbound_fields.py` (pinned, so it stays at its path
   but its dict literals become an import). After this,
   grep finds exactly one dict literal per map, reachable from the ACLI transport, the Cloud backend port, and
   the DC backend alike.

   The `deleted`-key drift **must be decided in J2**, because a single unified dict cannot preserve two
   callers that currently disagree. J2 adopts `"deleted": "Done"` — the value **two of the three** existing
   copies already use (`outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status`).
   The ACLI-side omission produces `"Deleted"` via a `.title()` fallback, which is not a state in the live DIG
   workflow, so Jira would reject that transition: a latent bug, not behavior to preserve. This is the one
   declared observable change in an otherwise behavior-preserving extraction, pinned by its own test. Bug
   `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) keeps the remainder: the missing ACLI-side
   characterization pins and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.
3. **Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts**: a `RichTextCodec` (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for
   DC) and a `UserIdentityModel` (`accountId` for Cloud, `name` for DC). Cloud is parameterized by its existing
   behavior; DC is a different configuration, not a fork.
4. **DC transport builds on the maintained `pycontribs/jira` library**, gated behind a `[jira-datacenter]`
   extra and imported lazily, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract and the battle-tested Cloud path are
   both untouched.
5. **Verify against a real Jira.** Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026, so the oracle
   is a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK at `localhost:2990` — the same approach pycontribs/jira itself
   uses in its `tests/conftest.py`.
6. **Keep the new boundary structurally enforced, not conventional.** The drift this epic exists to prevent can
   recur the moment a contributor adds Cloud-specific logic to the shared layer. So the seam ships with a
   machine-checked import contract (an `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml`, or an equivalent CI grep
   check): only `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` may import `adapters/jira_family/`, and
   `jira_family/` may import neither of them.
7. **Security posture for the DC connection.** Self-hosted DC is frequently served over plain HTTP inside
   corporate networks, which would put ticket bodies and the PAT on the wire in cleartext. The DC backend
   therefore **requires `https`** for `reconciler.base_url` and rejects a non-TLS URL unless an explicit
   `allow_insecure = true` override is set (which logs a warning). Operator docs state the least-privilege
   expectation: a **dedicated service account** whose PAT is scoped to only the projects rebar reconciles
   (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments / Link Issues on those projects), never an
   admin-level token.

   **Certificate verification stays ON.** Self-hosted DC commonly presents a self-signed or internal-CA
   certificate, and the tempting fix — disabling verification — turns the `https` requirement into theatre. So
   the DC transport never sets `verify=False`: an operator with an internal CA points rebar at their CA bundle
   (a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client), and
   a verification failure surfaces as a clear error naming the CA-bundle setting rather than being silently
   downgraded. `allow_insecure` governs the URL *scheme* only; it does NOT relax certificate checking.

   **The J5 harness is the intended `allow_insecure` case, not an exception to it.** The Dockerized Jira serves
   plain `http://localhost:2990/jira`, so every live test against it sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and
   asserts the warning is emitted. That is deliberate: it means the loopback-only test path exercises the
   override rather than bypassing the validator, and the validator's reject-by-default branch is covered by a
   unit test with a non-loopback `http://` URL. The override is **not** narrowed to loopback — an operator on a
   private network is a real use case — but the warning text names the cleartext risk.

**Provenance decision.** DC and Cloud share the single `jira` creation channel, `jira-` local-id prefix, and `jira_key` binding; deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this. They are the same vendor. Generalizing the store vocabulary is epic `be74`'s work, where a genuinely different vendor (GitHub) makes it necessary; doing it here would mean a store migration for no user-visible benefit.

**Alternative rejected: PR #120's separate adapter package.** Two copies of the field maps and sanitizers drift, and cross-adapter private imports are a dependency direction ADR 0035 never sanctioned.

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib REST client.** PR #120's client is competent, but pycontribs/jira already absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks that thousands of users have found. Confining it to an opt-in extra keeps the cost off every rebar install.

**Alternative rejected: `atlassian-python-api`.** It was surveyed in ADR 0004 and does support DC with PAT auth, but `pycontribs/jira` is the better fit here for two reasons: it ships the Dockerized-Jira-SDK test harness pattern this epic adopts as its verification oracle (its own `tests/conftest.py`), and its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object. Either would work; picking one and confining it to an opt-in extra is what matters.

**Alternative rejected: generalizing `jira_key` / the `jira-` prefix / the channel vocabulary now.** That is epic `be74`'s spine and touches 50+ binding-store sites; pulling it forward delays the CMS delivery for no behavioral gain.

**Alternative rejected: moving the location-pinned modules now.** Relocating `outbound_fields.py` / `adf.py` into `jira_family/` would be the tidier file layout, but it requires teaching the dynamic loader the new sub-package and re-targeting every `mock.patch("rebar_reconciler.<mod>.<attr>")` site in the suite (ADR 0035 §(a)–(b)). That is ADR 0035's Phase 2; doing it here would couple a live-Cloud-risking refactor to a delivery epic for no DC-visible benefit. Dependency inversion gets the same single-implementation guarantee at a fraction of the risk.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new), `adapters/jira/`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (new).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen `reconciler.backend` (**owned by J7**), add the TLS/`allow_insecure`
  validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (**owned by J6**). Split deliberately: J6 lands the
  DC connection settings with the transport that consumes them; J7 lands the backend-choice widening with the
  assembly that makes the choice valid.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra, and the import contract.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`, `test_backend_contract.py`.
- A new ADR amending ADR 0035.
- **Out of scope:** relocating any location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`,
  `comment_limits.py`) or touching `_loader.py` — ADR 0035 Phase 2 owns that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit
- [ ] `test_backend_contract.py`'s backend fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes for it
- [ ] an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon
- [ ] [operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at
      `localhost:2990`, selected by `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` with `reconciler.base_url`
      pointing at that instance: at least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound
      pass, and one local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions
      in the reconcile log
- [ ] No mapping logic exists in two places: the field/value maps, the label sanitizer, the link-relation
      vocabulary, the probe classifier, the rich-text codec, and the user-identity model each have exactly one
      implementation reachable by both backends — `adapters/jira_datacenter/` defines none of its own and
      imports each from `adapters/jira_family/` (or, for the location-pinned modules, consumes the pinned
      module parameterized by a `jira_family` contract). Enforced by the machine-checked import contract, which
      fails CI on a violation
- [ ] The Cloud adapter's observable behavior is unchanged: characterization oracles pinning every unit that
      moves or is re-pointed were committed **before** the extraction change was pushed for review (the oracle
      change's Gerrit number recorded on the extraction story), and the full oracle set passes against the
      post-extraction Cloud adapter
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` is exercised by the backend-agnostic contract suite, not only by adapter-local tests.
- [ ] Installing rebar without the `[jira-datacenter]` extra pulls in no new dependency — `pip install
      nava-rebar` then `pip list` shows no `jira` package and `import rebar` still works — **and the existing
      clean-core CI check enforces it**: `jira` is added to the absent-module list in
      `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` (today it checks only `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`,
      `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`, so without this the guarantee has no CI teeth).
- [ ] No location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `comment_limits.py`) changed path, and
      `_loader.py` is untouched — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main` on the landed stack (their
      *contents* may change to import from `jira_family/`; only a rename is forbidden)
- [ ] Exactly one dict literal defines the local→Jira status map and one the priority map **within
      `adapters/`** — the pre-existing `jira_fields` / `outbound_fields` duplicate pair is gone, and the ACLI
      transport, the Cloud backend port, and the DC backend all read the single `jira_family` definition
      (verified by grep for the map literals under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/`).
      `rebar_reconciler/config.py`'s third copy is the ONE knowingly-remaining literal outside `adapters/`,
      deferred to bug `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` because its call sites are engine-level config with a wider blast
      radius than this seam — so the grep is scoped to `adapters/`, not the whole engine
- [ ] The DC backend rejects a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` unless `allow_insecure = true` is set, warns
      when the override is used, and never disables TLS certificate verification
- [ ] The operator docs state the least-privilege service-account/PAT scope and how to point rebar at an
      internal CA bundle
baseline.summary: Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

## Confirm + document the verify-identity CI gate (store mount, posture, grandfathering)

`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` runs `rebar verify-identity` as a read-only merge gate. Investigation of the CURRENT file corrected the original premises:

- **Store mount is ALREADY implemented** (lines 41–52): a "Mount tickets branch as a
  worktree" step does `git fetch origin '+tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets'` then
  `git worktree add -B tickets .tickets-tracker origin/tickets`, so the gate scans real
  events and does NOT exit 2 ("store not found"). This task is therefore a CONFIRM, not an
  addition.
- **Enforcement is CONFIG-DRIVEN, not hard-forced.** The gating step (lines 53–57) passes
  NO `--require-authenticated` / `--since` flags; posture comes from
  `identity.require_authenticated` in `rebar.toml` (currently **false → advisory**, exit 0)
  and the boundary from `identity.enforce_since`.
- **The CI grandfathering override is the ENV var `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE`**, settable
  in the workflow's `env:` block — there is no `vars.ENFORCE_SINCE` GitHub Actions repo
  variable (that reference was incorrect).

Work:

- Confirm the mount step scans the store (a `verify-identity` run does not exit 2).
- Confirm + document the current gate posture: advisory (exit 0) because
  `identity.require_authenticated=false`; it re-verifies and reports authorship but cannot
  block landing until the flag is flipped (out of scope here).
- Document the grandfathering-boundary mechanism and the CI-vs-local distinction:
  `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE` (env var, settable in the workflow `env:` block) overrides
  `identity.enforce_since` (rebar.toml); when enforcement is later flipped on, this boundary
  must be set to an appropriate ref (e.g. the earliest tickets-store event, or the
  enforcement-cutover commit) so pre-enforcement unsigned events are grandfathered and the
  gate is not spuriously red. Put this in `docs/identity.md` (the verify-identity gate
  section).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Confirmed (and noted in `docs/identity.md`) that `verify-identity.yaml` mounts the tickets store via the worktree step (lines 41–52) and `rebar verify-identity` scans real events rather than exiting 2 (store-not-found).
- [ ] `docs/identity.md` documents the current CI gate posture — config-driven via `identity.require_authenticated` (currently false → advisory/exit-0), NOT a hard-forced `--require-authenticated`.
- [ ] `docs/identity.md` documents the grandfathering boundary and the distinction between `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE` (CI env override, set in the workflow `env:` block) and `identity.enforce_since` (rebar.toml), including that the boundary must be set appropriately before enforcement is flipped on so historical unsigned events are grandfathered.
baseline.summary: Confirm verify-identity CI gate mounts the tickets store

## Why
With many attestations every consumer must address a specific kind, without breaking the existing single-verdict API/CLI/MCP/schema.
## What
`verify_signature(ticket_id, kind="plan-review")` ALWAYS returns a SINGLE verdict dict
(schema `verify_signature_result.schema.json` UNCHANGED); `kind` defaults to `"plan-review"`
so existing no-kind callers keep back-compat. Internally it reads
`state["attestations"][kind]`, falling back to the legacy `state["signature"]` mirror when
the map is absent. Add a SEPARATE `verify_attestations(ticket_id) -> {kind: verdict}`
entry-point for the verify-all map (NOT a new return shape of `verify_signature`). CLI:
`--kind K` = single-gate exit code; no `--kind` = human-readable listing via
`verify_attestations` (exit 0 iff all certified). MCP `verify_signature` stays single
(kind defaults to plan-review). SCOPE BOUNDARY: this story owns the `verify_signature` MCP
tool + its (unchanged) result schema; the `attestations` field in the ticket-state MCP
response is owned by ed26.
## Scope
`src/rebar/signing.py` (`verify_signature` add `kind=`, `verify_attestations`,
`verify_signature_cli`), `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` (verify tool only).
## Depends on
Requires 114f merged (reads `state["attestations"]`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `verify_signature(ticket_id, kind="plan-review")` returns a single verdict; reads `attestations[kind]` with legacy `signature` fallback; schema unchanged.
- [ ] `verify_attestations(ticket_id)` returns `{kind: verdict}` over all present attestations.
- [ ] CLI `--kind K` exit 0 iff that kind certified; no `--kind` lists all, exit 0 iff all certified.
- [ ] Existing no-kind library/MCP callers keep single-verdict back-compat (default kind plan-review).
- [ ] Legacy single-signature ticket verifies under its derived kind.

## Clarification (impl): no-kind = mirror (back-compat), not list-all
- `verify_signature(ticket_id, kind=None)` verifies the most-recent `signature` MIRROR
  (exact pre-attestations behavior) so every existing no-kind caller + the single-verdict
  JSON/CLI contract is preserved; an explicit kind verifies that kind STRICTLY from the map.
- CLI `verify-signature <t>` (no --kind) returns the legacy SINGLE verdict; `--kind K`
  verifies kind K (single verdict, exit 0 iff certified — the CI-gate form). The full
  per-kind set is exposed via the library `verify_attestations` and the `attestations`
  field of `show` (ed26), NOT as a CLI map (which would break the single-verdict contract).
- [ ] no-kind library/CLI verify is byte-compatible with prior single-verdict behavior; verify_attestations(ticket_id) returns the {kind: verdict} map for programmatic all-kinds.
baseline.summary: Verification surface: per-kind verify + verify-all map

# Per-class fallback chains

## Context / Problem
A class may name a model that is not always reachable — a local endpoint that is down, a provider being throttled. Today a single unreachable model fails the gate outright; there is no way to say "use the local trivial model, but fall back to a hosted one".

## Approach
Consume the `fallback` array that the schema ticket already parses, constructing pydantic-ai's `FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...)` per class. Fallback entries are INLINE model configs (same shape as a slot), not references to named presets, so nothing requires the operator to look up rebar vocabulary.

`fallback_on` must be set deliberately rather than left at its default. pydantic-ai's own docs warn that provider SDK retry logic can delay failover substantially — a 429 may be retried inside the SDK for up to ~60s before the fallback is ever reached — so the condition is narrowed to the errors where switching providers actually helps (availability/rate-limit classes), not every exception.

**Alternative rejected — rebar-implemented retry/failover.** pydantic-ai already ships this and rebar already depends on it; a second implementation would diverge from the runner's error taxonomy.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/` — construct `FallbackModel` from a class's fallback list where the model is built.
- `tests/unit/` — construction and selection tests.

## Testing
Unit tier with a stubbed model: no network, no live provider.
- a class with no `fallback` builds the plain model (no FallbackModel wrapper) — today's behaviour.
- a class with one fallback builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary.
- an error in the configured `fallback_on` class selects the fallback.
- an error OUTSIDE that class propagates instead of silently failing over.

## DECIDED — the five runtime questions, against the VERIFIED pydantic-ai API

The first revision of this section asserted mechanisms without checking pydantic-ai's actual surface, and the review correctly blocked all three. Every claim below now cites the installed source at `.venv/.../pydantic_ai/models/fallback.py` and `.../messages.py`.

**1. `endpoint` on a fallback entry IS honored.** `resolve_fallback_chain` returns `provider:model` STRINGS, which structurally cannot carry an endpoint, so it is NOT the construction input — it stays as the human-readable / provenance view. Construction consumes the full `FallbackTarget` (`model` + `provider` + `endpoint`) and builds each entry through the same provider path as the primary. Dropping it would defeat the main reason to configure a fallback (a local OpenAI-compatible proxy backing a hosted primary).

**2 + 3. Lifecycle is SPLIT, and the split is the point.** VERIFIED: `FallbackModel.__aenter__` (fallback.py:167) enters every sub-model through an `AsyncExitStack` and `__aexit__` closes them — its own docstring says "Enter all sub-models so their providers can manage HTTP client lifecycle". So clients created by pydantic-ai's OWN providers are pydantic-ai's to close, and the `FallbackModel` MUST be used as an async context manager or those sub-providers are never entered at all.

That does NOT cover rebar-created transports. `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` constructs an `httpx.AsyncClient` that REBAR owns and passes in; those still register on `ProviderSession._closeables` (`providers.py:102`, appended at `:214`/`:276`, drained at `:289`), one per Anthropic-typed entry. Rule: whoever CREATES the client closes it. Registering pydantic-ai's own clients on `_closeables` would double-close; omitting rebar's would leak one per call.

**4. Capabilities are the conservative intersection, computed BEFORE the wrapper exists.** VERIFIED: `FallbackModel` has no `.profile`; its `.provider` property returns `None` (fallback.py:191) and `.base_url` returns `models[0].base_url`. So calling `capabilities_for()` on the wrapper — as `runner.py:365` does today for a single model — would silently yield primary-flavoured or default capabilities rather than failing. Therefore capabilities, cache settings and tool-capability guards are computed from the RESOLVED CANDIDATE LIST (primary + every fallback) before the wrapper is built, and a capability holds only if EVERY candidate has it. `capabilities_for` is never called on a `FallbackModel`. Concretely: a chain containing Bedrock `claude-opus-4-8` (MEASURED `supports_temperature: False`) withdraws `temperature` for the whole chain — otherwise the run succeeds or raises depending on which candidate answered, a failure reproducing only under provider degradation.

**5. `ran_model` comes from the RESPONSE, not from the model object.** VERIFIED: `FallbackModel.model_name` (fallback.py:194) returns the synthetic combined string `f"fallback:{...}"` and is USELESS for attestation. But `ModelResponse.model_name` (`messages.py:2106`) carries the name of the model that actually produced the response. So `provider_provenance` records the ordered `candidates` (known at build time) and `ran_model` read from the returned `ModelResponse`. A verdict recording only the primary would ATTEST THE WRONG MODEL whenever a fallback fired — the misattribution 343b exists to prevent, which this feature must not reintroduce.

**6. `fallback_on` is a CALLABLE PREDICATE over the EXISTING retryable set.** Two errors in the previous revision, both caught: (a) "derive from `ResolutionClass`" while also naming exception TYPES was a category error — `_map()` classifies an INSTANCE into a class, it does not yield a tuple of types; (b) the trigger set omitted `RETRY_NOW`, which is where `failure.py:259` maps `httpx.ConnectError` / `httpx.ConnectTimeout` — i.e. A DOWN LOCAL ENDPOINT, the exact scenario this ticket's opening sentence motivates. The chain would not have fired for its own primary use case.

VERIFIED resolution: `fallback_on` accepts a callable (fallback.py:92-107). rebar passes a predicate:

    fallback_on = lambda exc: classify(exc) in _RETRYABLE or classify(exc) is CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL

`_RETRYABLE` is the EXISTING frozenset at `failure.py:51` — `{WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW}` — not a new list. That is what makes the no-drift claim true: a future taxonomy change updates the fallback behaviour automatically, whereas any hand-maintained set (including the one this plan carried until now) drifts silently.

What that covers, traced through `failure.py` rather than asserted:

| class | reached by | falls back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RETRY_NOW` | `httpx.ConnectError`, `ConnectTimeout` (:259) — a down endpoint | YES |
| `WAIT_AND_RETRY` | 429 rate-limit, 529, 5xx (:215-220); Read/Pool/Write timeouts (:261) | YES |
| `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL` | `FallbackExceptionGroup` (:272), model-unavailable | YES |
| `CHANGE_SETTINGS` | 401/403 (:223), `UserError` | no |
| `CHANGE_INPUT` | 400 context-length, 413 (:225-228) | no |
| `INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS` | 402, and 429 WITH `insufficient_quota` (:216-217) | no |
| `FIX_AGENT_DESIGN`, `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` | agent/schema defects | no |

Note the 429 SPLIT, which the review surfaced and a naive "429 -> fall back" rule gets wrong: a plain rate-limit 429 is `WAIT_AND_RETRY` and DOES fall back, but a 429 whose body carries `insufficient_quota` is `INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS` and does NOT. Rationale for excluding it: quota or payment exhaustion is a SPEND problem, and silently relocating spend to another provider is worse than failing loudly. This is a deliberate, arguable call — recorded here so it is revisited on purpose rather than discovered by surprise.

Excluded for the same fail-loudly reason: `CHANGE_SETTINGS` (a credential problem must not be masked by shopping for a provider whose key happens to work) and `CHANGE_INPUT` (another provider will not fix an oversized request — the SIZE LADDER owns that path, and falling back would hide it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts a class without `fallback` builds an unwrapped model (no behaviour change)
- [ ] a test asserts a class with `fallback` builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary entry
- [ ] a test asserts an error in the configured condition selects the fallback entry
- [ ] a test asserts an error outside the condition PROPAGATES rather than failing over
- [ ] the chosen `fallback_on` condition is documented in-code with the SDK-retry caveat

- [ ] a test asserts a fallback entry carrying `endpoint` produces a model object built against THAT
      endpoint — not one silently built against the provider default
- [ ] a test asserts every fallback client is registered on the SAME `ProviderSession` and is closed
      on teardown: with N Anthropic-typed fallbacks, `_closeables` holds N+1 clients and all are
      closed exactly once (this fails against a per-entry-session implementation, which leaks)
- [ ] a test asserts a chain containing a model with `supports_temperature: False` withdraws
      `temperature` for the WHOLE chain, not just when that model is the primary
- [ ] a test asserts `provider_provenance` records the ordered `candidates` AND a `ran_model` equal
      to the model that actually answered — so a verdict produced by a fallback does not attest the
      primary
- [ ] a test asserts `fallback_on` fires on a 429/529/5xx and on a transport error, and does NOT
      fire on 401/403 or on a 400 context-length error (the loud-failure cases)
- [ ] a test asserts the `fallback_on` predicate is derived from `failure.py`'s `_RETRYABLE`
      frozenset plus `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL` — NOT a hand-maintained tuple of exception types
- [ ] a test asserts the predicate returns True for `httpx.ConnectError` (RETRY_NOW — the down-local-
      endpoint case this ticket exists for), True for a 529/5xx, and False for 401/403 and for a 400
      context-length error
- [ ] a test asserts the 429 SPLIT: a plain rate-limit 429 falls back, a 429 carrying
      `insufficient_quota` does NOT (it classifies as INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS)
- [ ] a test asserts `capabilities_for` is NEVER called with a `FallbackModel` instance (it has no
      `.profile` and its `.provider` is None, so it would silently return default capabilities)
- [ ] a test asserts `ran_model` is read from the returned `ModelResponse.model_name`, NOT from
      `FallbackModel.model_name` (which is the synthetic `fallback:a,b` string)
- [ ] a test asserts the `FallbackModel` is used as an async context manager, so its sub-models'
      providers are entered and exited (pydantic-ai closes ITS clients; rebar-created retrying
      transports remain on `ProviderSession._closeables`, closed exactly once, never double-closed)
baseline.summary: Per-class fallback chains

baseline.description:
Own the Pass-3 **deterministic novelty score + rising-floor drop rule** (task 3). Consume the
task-150b novelty score (`decide.novelty` / `verify.score_novelty`, both landed by 150b) and the
task-ec89 remediation-mode eligibility decision, then apply the deterministic floor. This task
adds the drop math, the narrowed coverage, the sidecar write of dropped findings, the runtime
defaults, and the activation guard. (Note: `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS`, `decide.novelty`, and
`verify.score_novelty` are 150b deliverables already merged on this branch — a re-review that
grounds against `origin/main` will not see them; they exist in the work branch.)

## Where the floor is applied (Pass-3 stays pure)

The floor is applied in the `_run_plan_review` WRAPPER (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`),
AFTER the deterministic verdict is produced and the ec89 eligibility decision is computed — NOT
inside `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings` / the `plan_review_decide` workflow step (those stay
pure arithmetic with no LLM). So **no existing caller of `pass3_over_findings` changes**. The
wrapper, when (and only when) eligible AND active, scores novelty over the surfaced advisory
findings (the droppable surface — blocking findings are high-priority and never dropped) via the
150b sub-call, then moves the dropped findings out of `advisory` into the verdict's `dropped`
bucket before the sidecar is emitted.

## Drop rule (deterministic — no LLM holistic severity)

A finding is dropped **iff** `novelty ≥ T_novel` AND `priority < floor`, where
`priority = validity × impact` (the existing Pass-3 score). Carryover findings (novelty < T_novel)
use the normal threshold and must still be resolved. A novel high-priority finding is preserved
(and may block). Implemented as a pure predicate `decide.rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty, *,
t_novel, floor) -> bool` so it is unit-testable in isolation.

## Defaults this task owns (derived, not guessed)

- `verify.novelty_drop_threshold` (`T_novel`) = **0.7** — the runtime drop threshold,
  config-overridable. House precision-first default; DISTINCT from the `discriminates_novelty`
  eval bar (0.5 midpoint, task 150b). It is the documented default; per-corpus calibration is
  explicitly deferred (epic "Defaults & calibration").
- `verify.novelty_priority_floor` = a **scalar** constant (config-overridable), set to the **p40
  impact percentile of the 245-event corpus** (≈ the "below major" band). It is a single number,
  NOT a per-finding adaptive value: the drop test is `priority < floor`, and since
  `priority = validity × impact`, the validity factor is already in `priority` — the floor itself
  is a fixed impact-percentile scalar. `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` is extended to
  print the impact PERCENTILES (incl. p40) so the chosen number is reproducible, not asserted.

## Activation guard (the evidence gate — explicit mechanism)

Activation is a **config key** `verify.novelty_drop_active` (default **False**). Mechanism (a):
the operator flips it to true MANUALLY after validating that 150b's `discriminates_novelty` eval
has cleared its bar (`rebar prompt eval plan-review-novelty` → the labeled pairs discriminate at
`gate: at_least(2)`/`epochs:3` + `coverage_threshold:0.8`). Until then the gate runs full/
un-floored. The drop path in `_run_plan_review` is reached only when ALL of: config
`remediation_mode` on (ec89), the ec89 eligibility decision `eligible`, AND
`novelty_drop_active` true — so the floor is triple-gated and inert by default. A test asserts the
drop rule is inert while `novelty_drop_active` is False even when eligibility holds.

## Narrowed coverage + sidecar (observability)

On a narrowed verdict the wrapper sets, on `verdict["coverage"]` (an open dict — no schema file
change), `narrowed: true`, `floored_criteria` (the criteria carried by the dropped findings), and
`floored_finding_ids` (the dropped findings' ids). These keys are ABSENT on a normal/un-floored
review (byte-identical to today). Every dropped novel finding is moved into the verdict's
`dropped` bucket, which `sidecar.build_payload` already persists (slimmed, WITH `norm_id`) — so
suppression is always observable and joinable by `norm_id`, and the dropped findings are NOT in
the surfaced verdict's `advisory`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Deterministic `decide.rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty, *, t_novel, floor)`: drop iff `novelty ≥ T_novel` AND `priority < floor`; carryover (novelty < T_novel) → normal threshold; novel high-priority → preserved (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py`)
- [ ] `verify.novelty_drop_threshold` (default 0.7) and `verify.novelty_priority_floor` (a scalar = the stated corpus p40 impact percentile) are committed config-overridable defaults in `src/rebar/config.py`; `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` prints the impact percentiles the floor is derived from
- [ ] Activation guard `verify.novelty_drop_active` (default False, operator-flipped after the 150b eval clears its bar); the floor is inert while False; a test asserts un-floored behavior when the flag is False even though eligibility holds
- [ ] The floor is applied in `_run_plan_review` (post-verdict), gated on ec89 eligibility AND `novelty_drop_active` AND `remediation_mode`; `pass3_over_findings` and the `plan_review_decide` step are unchanged (Pass-3 stays pure)
- [ ] Coverage on a narrowed verdict sets `narrowed: true` + `floored_criteria` + `floored_finding_ids` on `verdict["coverage"]` (absent on a normal review)
- [ ] Every dropped novel finding is moved to the verdict's `dropped` bucket (persisted to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar with `norm_id`), and removed from the surfaced `advisory`
- [ ] Consumes task ec89's remediation-mode eligibility decision (`coverage["remediation"]`); does NOT re-implement the freshness-window/precondition check
- [ ] Offline tests (no live LLM): the pure drop predicate (all four quadrants), the inert-when-flag-False guard, the narrowed-coverage assembly + sidecar dropped bucket with an INJECTED novelty map (so no LLM call is needed to prove the wrapper)
baseline.summary: Pass-3: deterministic novelty score + rising-floor drop rule

baseline.description:
Mechanical per-surface follow-up to inadequate-hydrated-starling (aa0b-92f6-c132-4c23, merged as 90967aa7ff3d), which added the MCP-required tracker-op umbrella rule to `AGENTS.md` (the "## Drive the tracker through the MCP server (local-code ops are the carve-out)" section) governing every guidance surface by reference. This ticket does the textual sweep of the non-doc surfaces that starling's consumer scan enumerated.

## Context / Problem
starling reconciled the guidance semantically at the umbrella level, but the individual non-doc guidance surfaces still instruct tracker ops as bare local `rebar <verb>` invocations with no pointer to the umbrella. A reader landing on one of those surfaces does not learn that, when an MCP server is configured, tracker ops route through MCP (the local CLI being the carve-out/fallback). This is the enumerated mechanical follow-up starling deferred.

## Approach
For each in-scope surface, add a single one-line pointer at its tracker-op instruction(s) of the form "route tracker ops through the MCP server when one is configured; the local `rebar` CLI is the carve-out/fallback for local-code ops", cross-referencing the `AGENTS.md` umbrella section — without restating the whole rule (AGENTS.md stays canonical/lean). This is additive-pointer-only: no semantics change, and local-code-op instructions (`review-code`, `verify-commit-ticket`, `explain`, tests, git, `review-plan --status`) are left as-is or noted as the carve-out. One well-placed pointer per surface (at its primary tracker-driving section) matches the umbrella's "governs by reference" model and keeps each surface lean. Each pointer matches its file's existing voice/format.

`templates/rebar-usage.md` is the byte-identical canonical source for the generated region in `templates/AGENTS.md` (guarded by `tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py`), so the template edit is made in `rebar-usage.md` and re-synced into the delimited `<!-- BEGIN rebar-usage -->`/`<!-- END rebar-usage -->` region of `templates/AGENTS.md`. That test also enforces `FORBIDDEN_INTERNAL = ("Gerrit", "module-size", "Serena")`, so the template pointer stays client-generic and names none of those, and references the rebar MCP capability generically rather than rebar-internal specifics.

## Scope
- `.agents/rules/rebar.md` — the "Track work in rebar" bullet.
- `templates/rebar-usage.md` — the canonical rebar-usage source (the loop / "Working over MCP" section).
- `templates/AGENTS.md` — re-sync the generated region byte-for-byte from `templates/rebar-usage.md`.
- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` — the loop that runs `review-plan`/`claim`.
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — the bug-fix `review-plan`/`sign-review` block (leaving the `review-code`/`--status`/`verify-commit-ticket` local-code ops as the carve-out).
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md` — the "Discover the project's rules first" section.
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md` — the "Before recording tickets" section (`create`/`link`/`ready`/`review-plan`).
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` — the tracker-writeback carve-out section.

No behavioral code changes; these are Markdown guidance files.

## Testing
- Run `pytest tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py` — the template drift gate must stay green (the region in `templates/AGENTS.md` byte-matches `templates/rebar-usage.md`, and no `FORBIDDEN_INTERNAL` string leaks into the client template).
- Run `make lint && make typecheck && make test` — all green; the .md edits are no-ops for typecheck/test apart from the template-sync unit test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Each of the eight in-scope files gains an additive one-line pointer at its tracker-op instruction stating tracker ops route through MCP when an MCP server is configured with the local CLI as the carve-out/fallback; verified: `git diff --stat` on merged commit lists exactly those 8 files (44 insertions, 2 deletions) and each added line was read.
- [x] Local-code-op instructions (`review-code`, `verify-commit-ticket`, `explain`, tests, git, `review-plan --status`) are unchanged or explicitly noted as the carve-out; verified: HEAD touches no `.py` files and each diff hunk adds only tracker-op routing pointers, naming those local-code ops as the carve-out.
- [x] `templates/AGENTS.md`'s generated region is byte-identical to `templates/rebar-usage.md` and contains no `FORBIDDEN_INTERNAL` ("Gerrit", "module-size", "Serena") string; verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py` passed (13 passed) locally and in CI.
- [x] The full gate passes on the authoritative isolated CI runners: Gerrit change 2217 earned `Verified +1` (all lint/typecheck/pytest shards green, run 32843691099 = success) and `LLM-Review +1`. Locally `make lint` and `make typecheck` exited 0 and the template-sync test passed; the local `make test` had 3 unrelated git-isolation/tracker-footprint flakes (test_rebar_repo_isolation, test_tracker_footprint_cli, test_overlap_retrieve) from ~20 concurrent git-heavy sessions on this shared overloaded machine (load avg ~50-85) — HEAD touches no `.py` files, and the same full suite passed green on clean CI runners.

baseline.description:
## Claim

The core reconciler passes its transport around as an UNANNOTATED parameter. That is why the Backend port can silently under-declare what the core requires — the defect class behind [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5], where a DC writing reconcile pass crashed on a method (`set_entity_property`) that the core calls from three sites and `TicketTransport` never declared.

This is not an adjacent tidiness issue. It is the ENABLING CONDITION.

## Proof — three-way mypy probe (RE-VERIFIED, and the enabling detail it omitted)

    def current_shape(client, ...):                     # today's core
        client.set_entity_property(...)                 # -> NO ERROR

    def annotated_any(client: Any, ...):                # what the ratchet alone accepts
        client.set_entity_property(...)                 # -> NO ERROR

    def annotated_port(client: TicketTransport, ...):   # typed as the PORT
        client.definitely_not_a_member(...)
        # -> error: "TicketTransport" has no attribute "definitely_not_a_member"  [attr-defined]

Run with the repo's own settings — `mypy src/rebar`, i.e. exactly what `make typecheck` runs.

**The third row only holds when mypy can RESOLVE the annotation, and inside this package that is not automatic.** Every core reconciler module imports its siblings absolutely as `from rebar_reconciler.X import …` (87 such imports), because the package is executed as the top-level name `rebar_reconciler` with `src/rebar/_engine` injected on `sys.path`. mypy is never told about that injection, `rebar_reconciler` is not an importable distribution, and `ignore_missing_imports = true` is set — so **`from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport` resolves to `Any`**, and a parameter annotated with it is exactly as blind as `client: Any`. Measured with `reveal_type`, both forms in one file:

    from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_shim
    from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport as TT_real
    def f(a: TT_shim, b: TT_real) -> None:
        reveal_type(a)   # -> "Any"                    <- silently unchecked
        reveal_type(b)   # -> "rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._backend.TicketTransport"

A **relative** import inside a reconciler module resolves correctly and restores the check:

    # src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/<any module>.py
    from ._backend import TicketTransport
    def f(a: TicketTransport) -> None:
        a.definitely_not_a_member("x")       # -> error: ... has no attribute ...  [attr-defined]
        a.set_entity_property("K-1", "p", 1) # -> no error

So the requirement is sharper than the original plan stated: **annotate as the port AND import the port by a path mypy resolves.** Getting only the first half ships annotations that look rigorous and enforce nothing — the exact failure this ticket exists to prevent, arriving by a different route.

## The metaclass is NOT the obstacle (a prior blocking finding on this ticket, now refuted)

An earlier investigation recorded that `class TicketTransport(Protocol, metaclass=_TransportPortMeta)` (`_backend.py:195`, with `# type: ignore[misc]` on the metaclass at `:138`) makes mypy stop attribute-checking the annotated type, and concluded the class had to be split before this story could proceed. **That measurement was confounded by the import path**, not by the metaclass: its probe reached `TicketTransport` through the unresolvable `rebar_reconciler` shim (→ `Any`) and compared it against a Protocol declared locally in the same file (→ resolved). Re-run with the import path held constant, mypy attribute-checks the metaclass-bearing Protocol normally — the `[attr-defined]` error above is against today's `TicketTransport`, metaclass and all. Composition also survives: a `class X(TicketTransport, SupportsComments, Protocol)` view is likewise attribute-checked.

`_TransportPortMeta` therefore stays exactly as it is, and this story does not touch it. It is load-bearing for the RUNTIME side and independently verified as such: `isinstance` against a plain `@runtime_checkable` Protocol goes through `ABCMeta`'s subclass cache and keeps answering `True` after a member is deleted (measured), whereas `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` correctly flips to `False`. Note also that `assert_transport_conforms()` ([rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]) is `hasattr`-based and never calls `isinstance`, so it is immune to the cache by construction; the metaclass is what keeps the *`isinstance` spelling* honest for the held-out conformance tests.

## The important subtlety — the EXISTING ratchet does not fix this

`pyproject.toml` documents a shrink-only mypy strictness ratchet (per-package `disallow_untyped_defs`, enforced by `test_mypy_ratchet.py`), currently enabling `rebar.graph.*` and `rebar.grounding.*`, with `_engine` in the exempt set awaiting promotion.

**Promoting `_engine` through that ratchet would NOT have prevented a357** — see the middle row above: `client: Any` satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` and remains completely blind. The requirement is not 'annotate the params', it is 'annotate them AS THE PORT, resolvably'. A promotion done the easy way (spraying `Any`) — or done with a port annotation imported through the `rebar_reconciler` shim, which mypy widens to `Any` for you — would close the ratchet ticket while leaving this defect fully intact. That is the outcome to guard against, and it now has two routes, not one.

## Scale (measured)

15 functions in `rebar_reconciler` take a `client`/`transport` parameter with NO annotation; 10 already annotate one. Sample untyped: `dispatch_one.create_one`, `dispatch_one.update_one`, `dispatch_apply_phases._update_one_apply_reporter`, `batch_dispatch.delete_one`, `apply_inbound.inbound_repair_property`. Any existing annotation that names a port type through the `rebar_reconciler.` shim path counts as untyped for this story's purpose and must be re-pointed.

**Sizing probe, run:** annotating `client` on `dispatch_one.create_one` and `update_one` with a relatively-imported `TicketTransport` produced exactly ONE new mypy error — `"TicketTransport" has no attribute "add_comment"` at `dispatch_one.py:461`. That single finding is informative out of proportion to its size; see the next section.

## The finding the sizing probe surfaced — capability members

`add_comment` is one of the four OPT-IN capability members (`set_relationship`, `get_issuelinks_map`, `add_comment`, `get_comment_map`) that `_TransportPortMeta` carries as metaclass attributes rather than class-body members, deliberately: `hasattr(TicketTransport, "add_comment")` is `True` so the AST audit can attribute them, while `typing`'s protocol-attribute collection never sees them, so a links-less or comment-less transport still conforms.

mypy does not consult metaclass attributes for a Protocol-typed value, so it reports these sites — and it is RIGHT to. The existing AST audit (`test_every_transport_member_the_core_reaches_for_is_declared`) cannot report them, because `hasattr` says `True`. **mypy is strictly stronger than the audit here**, and this is the first concrete demonstration of that.

The correct resolution at such a site is to NARROW the annotation to a composed view that names the capability the site actually requires — verified to type-check:

    class _CommentingTransport(TicketTransport, SupportsComments, Protocol): ...

It is NOT to add `add_comment` to the `TicketTransport` class body (that would force every future transport to provide a feature it was never obliged to have), and NOT to widen back to `Any`.

## Interaction with J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36], settled

J9 already landed `assert_transport_conforms()`, a RUNTIME conformance guard wired into both backend factories, plus the AST audit. This story is their STATIC complement, not their replacement. All three stay, and they catch different things:

* runtime guard — a transport ASSEMBLED without a required member, caught at construction, before
  any write.
* AST audit — a core module reaching for a member no port declares, caught for the always-required
  set.
* mypy — a core CALL SITE reaching for a member its annotated view does not offer, caught at
  authoring time, including the capability members the audit structurally cannot see.

Removing or weakening any of them is out of scope.

## Also explains [rebar:dbf9-3fc8-625d-4730]

The same `Any` is why Serena/Pyright returns a FALSE EMPTY for `find_referencing_symbols('set_entity_property')` — no resolvable receiver type, so no references. Note this cuts the same way as the mypy finding: the unresolvable `rebar_reconciler.` import is a second, independent source of that blindness, so navigation only recovers where BOTH the annotation and its import path are fixed.

## Approach

**Annotate as the PORT, import the PORT resolvably, then let mypy find the gaps.**

1. **Re-point the port import** in each core module that will carry an annotation: replace
   `from rebar_reconciler._backend import …` with `from ._backend import …` for the types used in
   annotations. Relative imports are already used in this package
   (`adapters/__init__.py`) and are correct at runtime under both module names, so this is not a
   runtime behaviour change. A `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded relative import is an acceptable variant
   where a module has a reason to keep its runtime import absolute.
2. **Annotate** each unannotated `client`/`transport` parameter with `TicketTransport`, or with a
   composed/capability Protocol where the site genuinely needs one.
3. **Probe before editing.** Run the annotation pass and record the resulting `[attr-defined]` list
   on this ticket BEFORE resolving it, so the change's size is known rather than discovered halfway.
   Expected shape, from the sizing probe: mostly capability members, a small tail of genuine port
   gaps.
4. **Treat every `[attr-defined]` as a FINDING, not noise.** Resolve each by either DECLARING the
   member on `TicketTransport` (the core genuinely always requires it) or NARROWING the annotation
   to a composed capability view (the member is opt-in). Never by widening back to `Any`, and never
   by reverting to the shim import path — those are the two ways this change can silently
   self-neutralise.

**Do NOT promote `_engine` through the strictness ratchet in this story.** The ratchet enables `disallow_untyped_defs`, which `client: Any` satisfies while remaining completely blind. Promotion and port-typing are separate changes and conflating them is how the easy version ships and closes both.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` — re-point port imports to a mypy-resolvable path and
  annotate the `client`/`transport` parameters.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — declare any member mypy proves the core
  ALWAYS requires and the port omits; add composed capability views where sites need them. The
  `_TransportPortMeta` metaclass and `assert_transport_conforms()` are NOT modified.
- tests pinning that neither self-neutralising route passes (see Testing).
- a note in `pyproject.toml` / `docs/architecture.md` per the last AC.

**NOT in scope:** promoting `_engine` through the mypy strictness ratchet; changing `_TransportPortMeta`, `assert_transport_conforms()`, or the AST audit; converting the package's other 80-odd non-annotation imports to relative form (a separate, larger clean-up — this story re-points only what its annotations need); any behaviour change whatsoever.

## Testing

* `make typecheck` is clean at the resulting strictness, and `make lint` passes.
* the full reconciler unit suite passes UNEDITED — this is a pure annotation + import-form change,
  so any test that needs editing means behaviour moved and the change has failed its own premise.
* the backend contract / conformance suites pass unchanged, demonstrating the runtime guard and the
  AST audit are untouched.
* **the blindness guard, which is the load-bearing test.** A check over the core reconciler that
  fails if a `client`/`transport` parameter is annotated `Any`, left bare, OR annotated with a port
  type imported through the unresolvable `rebar_reconciler.` path. All three are equivalent to no
  annotation at all under `mypy src/rebar`, and the third is the one a reviewer will not see.
* a NEGATIVE mypy probe, run and recorded: a scratch call to an undeclared member through a
  port-typed parameter in a core module must produce `[attr-defined]`, proving the annotation
  enforces something rather than merely being present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every `client`/`transport` parameter in the core reconciler is annotated with the PORT type
      (`TicketTransport`, or a capability/composed Protocol where the site needs one), NOT `Any`
- [ ] every such annotation names a type mypy actually RESOLVES — verified by `reveal_type`
      returning a `rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler...` type, never `Any`, for at least one parameter
      per touched module
- [ ] a scratch call to an undeclared member through one of those parameters produces
      `[attr-defined]` under `mypy src/rebar`; the transcript is recorded on this ticket
- [ ] every `[attr-defined]` the annotation pass produced is resolved by declaring the member on
      `TicketTransport` or by narrowing to a capability view — none by widening to `Any` and none by
      reverting an import to the `rebar_reconciler.` path; the full list and its per-item resolution
      is recorded on this ticket
- [ ] a test fails if a core `client`/`transport` param is annotated `Any`, left bare, or annotated
      through the unresolvable shim import path, so a future 'annotate it to pass the ratchet'
      change cannot silently reintroduce the blindness
- [ ] `_TransportPortMeta`, `assert_transport_conforms()`, and the AST audit are byte-unchanged, and
      the held-out conformance tests still pass — the static check is added ALONGSIDE the runtime
      guard, not in place of it
- [ ] `mypy src/rebar` is clean, and the reconciler unit + contract suites pass unedited
- [ ] the ratchet note in `pyproject.toml` / `docs/architecture.md` records BOTH defeat routes: that
      annotating as `Any` satisfies `disallow_untyped_defs` while defeating its purpose at port
      boundaries, AND that a port annotation imported via `rebar_reconciler.` is silently widened to
      `Any` by `ignore_missing_imports`
baseline.summary: Reconciler transport params are untyped, so mypy cannot enforce port completeness (root cause of a357's class)

## Context
The hardening byte-equivalence test executes both production `_convert` and a copied `_legacy_convert` for all 884 prepared corpus units. The copied oracle shares conversion constants with production; changing `_PANDOC_TO` to `plain` made both sides agree, demonstrating coupling. Combined corpus+hardening invokes Pandoc 3,421 times under xdist; the legacy half adds 884 subprocesses. Immutable expected outputs detect 799/884 of that mutation while production `_convert` still invokes the real pinned Pandoc for every unit. This preserves ADR 0095 because every conversion assertion continues to cross the real production binary. Golden fixtures match Pandoc, Kubernetes, and Rust practice. No prior rejection was found; `dimmed-supersweet-xenarthra` defers production spawn redesign, not independent test oracles.

## Plan
- Inventory the 884 prepared corpus inputs and pin their ordering/cardinality.
- Produce an immutable legacy-output fixture containing generator Pandoc version and SHA-256 binary fingerprint. Add a deterministic regeneration command/script and a fast installed-version drift assertion.
- Replace only the copied `_legacy_convert` subprocess call with lookup of the immutable output. Continue to invoke production `_convert` with real Pandoc for every prepared unit on every per-change run.
- Strengthen the oracle so a production format mutation fails against the independent expected output; preserve timeout/group-reap tests unchanged.
- Run held-out RED→GREEN, the `_PANDOC_TO=plain` defect-seeded mutation, full focused corpus/hardening suites, gates, and paired timing. Back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring live legacy subprocess comparisons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 884 prepared corpus units still pass through production `_convert` and real Pandoc in per-change CI.
- [ ] The copied legacy Pandoc subprocess implementation is removed from the byte-equivalence oracle and replaced by immutable expected output.
- [ ] Fixture metadata records the exact generating Pandoc version and SHA-256 fingerprint of the generating binary.
- [ ] A documented runnable generator reproduces the fixture deterministically.
- [ ] A fast assertion fails when the installed Pandoc version differs from fixture metadata.
- [ ] Mutating production output format to `plain` makes the independent byte-equivalence oracle RED.
- [ ] Corpus cardinality/order and all timeout/group-reap hardening tests remain covered.
- [ ] Paired timing quantifies eliminated subprocesses and runner time.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] The final ticket comment records RED/GREEN/mutation evidence and measured savings.
baseline.summary: Replace duplicate legacy Pandoc executions with golden outputs

# BUG: session-log auto-rotation fails to rotate off a fingerprint-less pointer

## Summary
A session WITH a session fingerprint (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` set) does NOT auto-rotate the current-session-log pointer when the pointer was previously written WITHOUT a fingerprint (`session=None`) — so the new session's entries pollute the prior session's log instead of starting a fresh one. The rotation guard only fires when BOTH the pointer's session and the current session are non-None (`src/rebar/_commands/session_log.py:160-165`), so a fingerprint-less pointer (written by a prior run that had no session id) permanently suppresses rotation for later fingerprinted sessions.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Session 1 with NO `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`/`REBAR_SESSION_ID`/`SESSION_ID`:
   `rebar session-log append "..."` → writes pointer `{"id": <log>, "session": null}`.
2. Session 2 WITH `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` set: `rebar session-log append "..."`.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: session 2 auto-rotates to a fresh log (`created:true`), matching the feature's
  purpose (prevent cross-session pollution, bug kooky-graft-cap / commit e98a82de1).
- Actual: session 2 appends to session 1's log (`created:false`) — confirmed by controlled
  reproduction and observed live (my entry landed in unrelated log 95f1).

## Fix (option 1, approved)
Rotate whenever the current session HAS a fingerprint that differs from the pointer's, INCLUDING when the pointer's session is None: drop the `current.get("session") is not None` clause so the condition is `current is not None and now is not None and current["session"] != now`. A session with no fingerprint (`now is None`) still never rotates (degrade-safe preserved). Update the CLAUDE.md degrade-safe wording to match.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fingerprinted session rotates off a `session=None` pointer (new RED->GREEN test in
      tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_session_log_capture.py).
- [ ] A session with no fingerprint still does NOT rotate (existing
      test_no_session_id_degrades_to_single_log stays green).
- [ ] Same-session append still does not rotate (test_same_session_appends_to_one_log green).
- [ ] Distinct fingerprinted sessions still rotate (test_distinct_sessions_produce_distinct_logs green).
- [ ] CLAUDE.md degrade-safe wording updated to reflect that a fingerprinted session rotates
      off a fingerprint-less pointer.
baseline.summary: session-log auto-rotation fails to rotate off a fingerprint-less pointer

## Why
Bug pelt-mead-aeon showed the review bot can serve /health 200 (pure liveness, app.py:113-116) while every review silently fails (the .tickets-tracker runner-config regression). Because autodeploy.sh's HEALTH_URL health gate (line 48) only probes /health, ADR-0026 auto-rollback never fired during a functional outage — the bad build stayed live. The root-cause fix (change 264) is landed, but this defense-in-depth gap remains: a functional failure is invisible to the deploy/rollback layer.

## What
- Add a functional readiness endpoint (e.g. /ready) to the review-bot app that exercises the review path wiring (ticket-store clone materialization + runner config re-root) — NOT just process liveness.
- Point autodeploy.sh's post-deploy health gate at /ready so a review-path regression triggers ADR-0026 auto-rollback to :prev.
- Keep the VOTER_ERROR CloudWatch alarm as the slower backstop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /ready (or equivalent) exercises the review path and fails when ticket-store/runner wiring is broken
- [ ] autodeploy.sh gates the deploy on /ready; a broken build auto-rolls-back to :prev
- [ ] Test/proof that a simulated review-path failure trips the gate
baseline.summary: Review-bot functional readiness probe so ADR-0026 auto-rollback catches review-path (not just /health) failures

baseline.description:
Follow-up recorded by ae96-f114-5363-4d57, which brought `scripts/` under `ruff check` and `ruff format` but NOT under mypy.

## Context / Problem

`Makefile:241-242` defines `typecheck:` as `mypy src/rebar`, while `Makefile:13` already sets `sources = src tests scripts` for ruff only. So the 47 `.py` files under `scripts/` are lint-clean but type-unchecked. `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:108` runs `make typecheck` as the gating "mypy — full library" step behind the `Verified` vote, and that same workflow invokes several `scripts/*.py` gate implementations directly (e.g. `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py`, referenced at `_build-and-test.yml:124`). The programs that enforce the `Verified` vote are themselves outside the type gate.

## Approach

**Decision: include `scripts/` in the typecheck scope** rather than excluding it. Widen the `typecheck` target to `mypy src/rebar scripts`, then fix the type errors it surfaces in the script sources themselves — no per-module mypy override, no blanket `# type: ignore`.

This is the honest option because the measured error volume is small: running `mypy src/rebar scripts` in this checkout reports **15 errors in 6 files** out of 490 files checked (`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` x7, `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` x4, plus one each in `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py`, `scripts/probe_rebar.py`, `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py`, `scripts/t5c_calibrate.py`). Every one is a missing container annotation or a lost `X | None` narrowing — several are latent bugs (e.g. `capture_jira_fixtures.py:221` calls `.strip()` on a `str | None`, `check_complexity_baseline.py:574` passes `dict[str, int] | None` where `dict[str, int]` is required). Relaxing flags for `scripts/` would suppress exactly the findings worth having.

ae96 flagged the `sys.path` bootstraps (9 files under `scripts/` mutate `sys.path`) as the structural obstacle. Verified empirically that they are already accommodated by existing config and need no change: `pyproject.toml` sets `follow_imports = "silent"` (errors are reported only for files named on the command line) and `ignore_missing_imports = true`, so a path-injected import degrades to `Any` instead of erroring. None of the 15 errors is an import error.

## Scope

- `Makefile` — `typecheck` recipe becomes `mypy src/rebar scripts`; update its help text/comment to say the scope now includes `scripts/`.
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — type the `_resolve_argv`/`_resolve_elements` opaque-sentinel return and the `ast` node params so `.lineno`/`.value` resolve; drop the two now-unused `# type: ignore` comments.
- `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` — annotate the bare `collections.Counter()` locals and key `tier_sev` with a `str` key.
- `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py` — narrow `value` before `.strip()`.
- `scripts/probe_rebar.py` — annotate `task_row`.
- `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py` — preserve the `base is None` narrowing at the `lock_against_base` call.
- `scripts/t5c_calibrate.py` — make `plan_text` return `str`.
- `tests/unit/test_typecheck_scope.py` (new) — guard that `scripts/` stays in the `typecheck` recipe.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — the type-gate hook description says "mypy over the full src/rebar" (line 57) and is named "typecheck (mypy — full library; never mutates)" (line 63); reword both to name the widened `src/rebar` + `scripts/` scope, since `Makefile:1-2` declares the Makefile is "mirrored 1:1 by CI and the pre-commit hook".
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — the same stale scope description in the gating step's comment ("`make typecheck` now covers all of src/rebar", lines 104-107) and step name ("mypy — full library (gating)", line 108); reword to match.

## Testing

New guard test `tests/unit/test_typecheck_scope.py`, modelled on the existing `tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_scope.py` (which parses the `lint:` recipe out of the Makefile the same way):

- Happy path: parse the `typecheck:` target's recipe from `Makefile` and assert it invokes `mypy` with both `src/rebar` and `scripts` as arguments.
- Failure path: assert the guard actually fails on a re-narrowed recipe — feed the recipe parser a synthetic `typecheck:\n\tmypy src/rebar` body and assert the scope assertion rejects it, so the test cannot silently pass if the target is later reverted.

`make typecheck` itself is the end-to-end check that the widened scope is green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The include-vs-exclude decision is recorded durably in the tree: the `Makefile` `typecheck` target carries a comment naming this ticket and stating that `scripts/` is in scope and why — verified by reading `Makefile`.
- [x] `make typecheck` runs mypy over `scripts/` as well as `src/rebar` — verified by `grep -nE '^\tmypy src/rebar scripts$' Makefile` returning exactly one line.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0 with `scripts/` in scope — verified by running it in the worktree venv.
- [x] No new `# type: ignore` comment is added — verified by `git diff | grep -c '^+.*type: ignore'` returning 0.
- [x] No `[[tool.mypy.overrides]]` block relaxing strictness for `scripts/` is added — verified by `git diff -- pyproject.toml` being empty.
- [x] The CI-invoked scripts are covered, since directory-level `mypy scripts` names every `scripts/**/*.py` — verified by cross-checking two enumerable counts: `find scripts -name '*.py' | wc -l` (currently 47) equals the source-file count in `mypy scripts 2>&1 | grep -Eo '[0-9]+ source files'`.
- [x] The stale "full library" / "full src/rebar" type-gate scope descriptions are corrected in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — verified by `grep -n 'full library' .pre-commit-config.yaml .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` showing BOTH remaining hits now read "full library + scripts/" (accurate), and no hit reads "full src/rebar" or a bare "full library" without the scripts qualifier. (Oracle corrected during close: the original wording asked for "no match", which was wrong — the corrected description legitimately still contains the substring "full library".)
- [x] `tests/unit/test_typecheck_scope.py` passes — verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_typecheck_scope.py -q` exiting 0.
- [x] That guard rejects a re-narrowed recipe — verified by a test case in the same file that feeds the recipe parser a synthetic `typecheck:` body of `mypy src/rebar` and asserts the scope check fails on it.
- [x] `make lint` is green — verified by running it in the worktree venv.
baseline.summary: Type-check scripts/ too: make typecheck is still mypy src/rebar only

## Context / Problem
`bridge_status` (and the bridge last-pass detail reader) resolve the tracker as `<repo_root>/.tickets-tracker`, hard-coded. They ignore the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` override and the `tracker.dir` config key that every other read path honours, so on any deployment whose tracker lives outside the repo tree the tool fails.

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server (`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, container `compose-mcp-1`):

```
bridge_status {}
  -> Error executing tool bridge_status: {"error": "command_failed",
     "message": "cannot read bridge status: cannot read local environment id from
      /app/.tickets-tracker/.env-id: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
      '/app/.tickets-tracker/.env-id'", "exit_code": 1}
```

That path does not exist. The container's env sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, and `docker exec compose-mcp-1 ls -a /app/.tickets-tracker` returns `No such file or directory`. `fsck` on the same server reads the env id fine (it reports `this environment ('eea68b7f-6697-488b-ac52-744e2ed8e96f')`), so the env id IS readable — only this code path looks in the wrong place.

## Mechanism
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:89`

```python
path = repo_root / ".tickets-tracker" / ".env-id"
```

and the sibling constant at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:35`

```python
DETAIL_RELATIVE = Path(".tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/last-pass.json")
```

Both join the literal `.tickets-tracker` under the repo root. The caller `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:288` passes `root = Path(config.repo_root(repo_root))` and never the resolved tracker. The correct resolver is `rebar._engine_support.reads.tracker_dir()` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:100-120`), which returns the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` override verbatim when set and otherwise joins the configured `tracker.dir` name under the repo root.

## Impact
`bridge_status` is a read-only tool documented as always available. It is unconditionally broken for every deployment using an out-of-tree tracker — which is the live server's own configuration. The bridge freshness assertion (`max_age_seconds`) and the durable last-pass/pause snapshot are therefore unreadable in production, and the error text misleadingly points the operator at a path that is not the tracker.

## Reproduction
1. Set `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` to a tracker outside the repo root (as the deployed MCP server does).
2. Call `bridge_status` with no arguments.
3. Observe the failure naming `<repo_root>/.tickets-tracker/.env-id` instead of the configured tracker.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: `bridge_status` reads the env id from the tracker resolved by `reads.tracker_dir()`, so it succeeds when `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` points outside the repo root.
- [ ] AC2: `DETAIL_RELATIVE`'s last-pass detail file is likewise resolved under the configured tracker, not the hard-coded `.tickets-tracker` name.
- [ ] AC3: `bridge_status` also succeeds unchanged in the default in-tree layout (no `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`, default `tracker.dir`).
- [ ] AC4: A regression test sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` to an out-of-tree tracker and asserts `bridge_status` returns a snapshot rather than raising.
- [ ] AC5: No remaining literal `".tickets-tracker"` join in `last_pass.py`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DD1: AC1-AC3 hold, demonstrated by the AC4 test.
- [ ] DD2: `grep -n "\.tickets-tracker" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py` returns no path-construction hit.
baseline.summary: bridge_status hard-codes <repo_root>/.tickets-tracker and ignores REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, so it is broken for out-of-tree trackers
