## Context

Historical audit (analysis ticket b902-18af-14ed-4da1): of 894 BLOCK→re-review transitions, 13-14% re-blocked ONLY on the same persisting criteria — the author re-submitted without addressing the outstanding findings, paying a full review (~$3-7) to learn nothing new. A staged-LLM re-review was modeled and rejected (net negative: 45% of re-reviews PASS and would pay an extra serial call). The approved compromise is a zero-LLM deterministic pre-check, WARN-ONLY (operator decision 2026-08-11): it must never hard-block, because ~8% of BLOCK→PASS flips occur with no material change at all (verdict flap) and a hard decline would freeze those recoveries. This mirrors the escape-hatch posture of the shipped BLOCK-verdict-reuse (`plan_review/reuse.py`).

## Plan

1. When `review-plan` runs on a ticket whose LATEST attested verdict is BLOCK with recorded blocking findings, extract each blocking finding's cited evidence anchors (the finding's `evidence` strings and quoted plan fragments recorded in the sidecar).
2. DET check (no LLM): compare the current plan material against the material fingerprinted at the blocking review. If the plan text containing every cited anchor is UNCHANGED (all anchors still present verbatim and description component fingerprint unchanged per `material_parts`), print a WARNING before the review runs: the outstanding blocking findings cite text the revision did not touch, naming the findings and their criteria, and noting the review will likely re-block. Then RUN THE REVIEW ANYWAY (warn-only; no new flag, no decline, no exit-code change).
3. Anchors that cannot be matched verbatim (paraphrased evidence, structural findings with no quote) are treated as unmatchable and NEVER trigger the warning on their own — the warning fires only when at least one anchor matched the old text AND all matched anchors are untouched.
4. Record `precheck.cited_anchor_warning: true|false` in the review's sidecar metrics so the warning's hit rate and predictive value are measurable offline (per ADR 0054).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Re-reviewing a ticket whose plan is unchanged since a BLOCK (same description component fingerprint) prints the warning naming the persisting findings' criteria, and the review still runs to a verdict. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -k "cited_anchor" -x` passes with a test pinning warning text + review execution.
- [x] Re-reviewing after an edit that changed cited text does NOT warn. Verify: covered in the same test module.
- [x] Findings with no verbatim-matchable anchors never trigger the warning alone. Verify: covered in the same test module.
- [x] The sidecar metrics block records the warning flag on every plan review. Verify: unit test pins the field.
baseline.summary: Warn-only DET cited-anchor pre-check before re-reviewing an unaddressed BLOCK

## Context

Parallel rebar operations can run Git fetches against one Git common directory without common coordination. Three concurrent plan reviews failed before verdict with `cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/tickets` and the comparison `is at <new> but expected <old>`. The failure is present on `origin/main` commit `3d41015574baa18a6ee6a25c7271be87fde1a3a5`. The authoritative concurrency contract in `docs/concurrency.md` lines 3 through 12 states that rebar is operated concurrently across interfaces and that every invariant gates every change.

## Duplicate sweep

Searches for the exact failure and for concurrent fetch coordination found no open or in-progress bug with this scope. `chordal-quasilegal-pipit` records the same failure during four concurrent reviews, but its accepted scope addressed plan-review verdict convergence. `icicled-unstable-urial` handles local Git contention on routed write calls. `honest-repulsive-blackfish` consolidates Git failure classification while preserving each caller action. `eclectic-spotted-barb` fixes an unlocked enrichment prune. None fixes this fetch race.

## Confirmed mechanism

`rebar._store.sync.reconverge` runs a forced-refspec fetch in `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` lines 281 through 295 before taking the store write lock at line 304. The snapshot fetch path serializes through a separate lock in the snapshot store. The store Git advisory lock introduced by `icicled-unstable-urial` covers routed index-mutating calls and explicitly leaves sync and push fetch legs outside its domain in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` lines 300 through 307. Neither fetch path retries the stale-reference comparison failure.

Git fetch updates remote-tracking refs with compare-and-swap semantics. When two uncoordinated fetches update the same ref, one process can observe the ref after its peer changed it and fail with `is at <new> but expected <old>`. The snapshot path raises `SnapshotFetchError`, which aborts an attested operation. The sync path treats the fetch as a failed best-effort call and skips that freshness round.

## Proof

- A controlled experiment drove the production `sync._git` seam against fresh local repositories. Parallel execution produced 82 exact stale-reference comparison failures in 128 attempts. Serialized execution produced zero failures in 128 attempts.
- A second controlled experiment drove production snapshot fetches and production sync fetches against the same Git common directory. Nine of twelve snapshot fetches aborted with the exact comparison failure. Sync recorded 113 exact failures in 132 calls. The serialized control produced zero failures. This experiment proves that operation-specific locks do not coordinate paths that share refs. It does not assume that the standard code checkout and tracker clone share one object database.
- Fresh local repositories removed network behavior, credentials, missing objects, and ticket-store state as alternative explanations.
- Linked code worktrees share one Git common directory. Concurrent sessions also share the symlinked `.tickets-tracker` clone. Multiple operations can therefore update the same remote-tracking ref within either domain.

## Historical boundaries

Commit `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a` introduced tracker reconvergence with fetch deliberately outside the write lock. It predates the commit-trailer convention and has no recoverable ticket. Commit `57114212cf0112c43e571ded7cf8e16bc2a0e425` later ported that policy into `rebar._store` under `chilly-hyena-jet`. Commit `2a3abe6abde9` added the explicit destination refspec under `scorpioid-important-thylacine`. That refspec is required for narrow clones and must not be removed as a workaround.

`icicled-unstable-urial` records the operator decision that transient local Git contention should recover automatically and that only exhausted bounded recovery should surface an actionable error. Its accepted implementation was narrower than ref-updating fetches. `honest-repulsive-blackfish` provides shared failure vocabulary, but its acceptance criteria preserved existing caller actions and did not add fetch recovery. No attempted and reverted fix for this mechanism was found.

## Remediation constraints

- Coordinate rebar fetches by canonical Git common-directory identity, or apply bounded retry that safely re-reads state after the exact stale-reference comparison failure. The design may combine both mechanisms.
- Do not hold the ticket write lock across network I/O. Preserve the existing requirement that a slow fetch cannot block local ticket writers.
- Preserve the explicit tickets refspec required by `scorpioid-important-thylacine`.
- Preserve the context-specific Git outcomes established by `honest-repulsive-blackfish`. A local ref race, a remote policy rejection, and a ref CAS mismatch remain different outcomes.
- Treat non-rebar Git processes as possible peers. An advisory lock alone cannot provide recovery when another Git client does not take it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Parallel tracker synchronization calls against one Git common directory complete without exposing or silently discarding the stale-reference comparison failure.
- [x] An attested snapshot fetch racing with another ref-updating fetch against the same Git common directory completes through bounded recovery or returns one actionable exhausted-recovery error.
- [x] Coordination identity follows symlinks and linked worktrees to the canonical Git common directory.
- [x] Network fetches do not hold the ticket write lock, and a blocked remote does not block local ticket writes.
- [x] The explicit tickets destination refspec remains in place and narrow-clone synchronization tests remain green.
- [x] Deterministic tests use local repositories, observe the failure before the fix, and exercise parallel and serialized controls at both affected entry points.
- [x] Current concurrency documentation names the ref-fetch coordination and recovery policy.
- [x] Focused tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.

## Attribution

The first introducing commit is `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a`. Searches by full SHA, exact policy text, `WS3`, and `REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL.md` found no originating ticket. The later Tier D story is a carrier. The explicit-refspec ticket is a required correctness fix rather than the origin. Attribution is therefore recorded as pre-ticket and no `caused_by` edge is asserted.
baseline.summary: Concurrent ref-updating fetches are not coordinated by Git common directory

# Code-review impact model redesign: two-lane tier-tagged MAX with re-anchored scale

## Why
Production-severity axes + the mean structurally mis-measure code-review's maintainability/latent-regression findings: a feature silently dead in prod (untested wiring) scores 0.415 because prod_impact is 'none' and reversibility 'easy' drag it down. Landmines and nits overlap so no scalar threshold separates them.

## What
A code-review-specific, verifier-embedded impact model (`decide.impact_code`) dispatched per-gate off the shared `decide.pass3_decide` via the `impact_fn` param (that param ALREADY EXISTS — it landed with the plan-review impact redesign child fishable-apivorous-redhead; code-review now passes `impact_fn=impact_code`).
- TIER VALUES: each consequence binary carries the severity it implies if true — minor=0.3, moderate=0.6,
  serious=0.9. Lane-severity = MAX of the tiers of the TRUE binaries (no dilution; a minor/moderate binary
  cannot alone reach the block zone). No cross-binary compounding (conservative default).
- TWO LANES: `prod_lane = MAX(correctness tier-tagged binaries) * trigger_likelihood_mult`; `maint_lane =
  MAX(maintainability tier-tagged binaries) * freq_mult`. Each binary is assigned to EXACTLY one lane + one
  tier by an explicit table (below).
- TRIGGER-LIKELIHOOD (LLM-emitted enum on the NEW field `trigger_likelihood`, deliberately NOT named
  `likelihood` — the base SeverityAttrs already declares `likelihood`=low|medium|high mapped by _LIKE01, so a
  distinct name avoids a field-override collision): `common=1.0 / sometimes=0.6 / rare=0.25`; absent =>
  `common` (1.0) so a serious correctness binary is not silently dampened by missing metadata.
- CHANGE-FREQUENCY MULTIPLIER: `freq_mult = 0.5 + 0.5 * min(churn_90d, 30) / 30` where churn_90d = commits
  touching the finding's file in the last 90 days (`git log`, DET). Linear, saturates at 30. Applies to
  maint_lane only. FALLBACK: git unavailable / shallow clone / no file attributable => churn_90d = 0 =>
  freq_mult = 0.5 (the minimum). Best-effort; never fails the review.
- REVERSIBILITY FLOOR (det/hybrid), GATED: `reversibility_floor = 0.6` iff BOTH (a) `impact_base > 0` (the
  finding identifies at least one true consequence) AND (b) the finding's file is a HARD-TO-REVERSE SURFACE by
  these DET path rules (else 0): migration = a path segment `migrations/` or a segment starting `migration`;
  released-artifact/packaging = basename in {pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg} or path contains `CHANGELOG`;
  serialization/schema = extension in {.proto, .sql} or basename matching `schema*.json`/`*.schema.json`;
  deletion = the file is removed in the diff (only `-` lines / git status D). 'exported public API' is
  best-effort (undetectable from paths alone -> treated as NOT hard-to-reverse; conservative floor 0).
  The `impact_base > 0` gate is deliberate: it lifts a GENUINE defect on a one-way-door surface to >=0.6 but
  does NOT manufacture impact for a clean/no-consequence finding on the same file (fixes the "fires
  unconditionally, over-inflates nits" hole).
- DETECTION AMPLIFIER: `amp = 1.0 if (silent_failure or escapes_automation) else 0.8`. Both are LLM-emitted
  booleans in `code_review_verification_model` (a code-review detection judgment), defaulting to false (=>
  amp 0.8) when absent.
- EXPLICIT COMPOSE ORDER (single expression, no ambiguity):
  `impact_base = MAX(prod_lane, maint_lane); impact = max(min(1.0, impact_base * amp), reversibility_floor)`.
- RE-ANCHOR: drop the 0.33 attribute floor; co-calibrate tier values + block threshold on the labeled set
  (below) so a maintainability landmine reaches ~0.8+ and a nit ~0.15-0.2.
- CARVED SUB-QUESTION SET (audit-approved) with EXPLICIT lane + tier (ADD to, do NOT replace, the existing
  severity_attributes — CodeSeverityAttrs extends the base five):
    prod lane:  data_loss_without_recovery=0.9, security_bypass_not_enforced_elsewhere=0.9,
                silent_wrong_feeding_a_decision=0.9, capability_degraded=0.6
    maint lane: unversioned_published_contract_break=0.9, safety_net_removal_without_replacement=0.9,
                contract_drift=0.6, hidden_invariant=0.6, implicit_coupling=0.3, dead_code=0.3
  Each serious binary carries its charitable carve-out in its verify-prompt definition.

## Implementation mechanics + calibration data
- SUB-ANSWER SCHEMA: emit the tier-tagged binaries (bool) + `trigger_likelihood` (enum: common|sometimes|rare) + `silent_failure` /
  `escapes_automation` (bool) as NEW fields on a `code_review_verification_model()` whose severity_attributes
  is `CodeSeverityAttrs` EXTENDING the shared 5 attrs — a SINGLE aggregate Pass-2 verify call, no added LLM
  calls. Wired in THREE named places: (i) register a `code_review_verification` contract in
  `code_review/contracts.py` -> code_review_verification_model; (ii) change the verify step's `output_schema`
  in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` (~line 147) from `verification` to
  `code_review_verification`; (iii) update the `outputs:` front-matter key in
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-verify.md` from `verification` to `code_review_verification`. The
  kernel `verification` contract (plan-review + default) is untouched. Each new binary defaults false / trigger_likelihood 'common' /
  detection false, so an older/absent verifier ABSTAINS (no true binary => lane 0 => impact 0).
- VERIFY-PROMPT INSTRUCTION TEXT (required so the LLM knows how to populate the new fields): `code-review-verify.md`
  gains an ADDITIVE 'CODE-REVIEW CONSEQUENCE BINARIES' block (kept alongside the existing severity-attribute
  instructions) that names each of the 10 tier-tagged binaries under its lane with its tier (serious/moderate/
  minor) and a one-line 'set TRUE only when the change genuinely exhibits this' rule, plus a 'TRIGGER LIKELIHOOD +
  DETECTION' block defining `trigger_likelihood` (common|sometimes|rare, default common) and the `silent_failure` /
  `escapes_automation` booleans. It instructs the verifier to leave a binary FALSE unless earned (a false binary
  contributes nothing; a minor/moderate binary alone cannot reach the block zone), mirroring the additive axes
  block plan-review's `plan_review_verifier.md` gained.
- DET ENRICHMENT (merge target = the VERIFICATION dict, NOT the finding dict): `pass3_decide` reads its
  attrs from the *verification* dict (`verification.get("severity_attributes")`), NOT from the finding
  dict (in `pass3_over_findings`, the finding `f` is used only for `threshold_for(f.get("criteria"))`;
  the attrs `impact_code` receives come from `verifs.get(i)`). So `code_review_decide` computes `churn90`
  (90-day git commit count for the finding's file) + `hard_to_reverse_surface` (from the changed-file
  path / deletion) per finding and injects them IN PLACE into `reshape.verifications[i]["severity_attributes"]`
  (the exact dict `impact_code` receives) BEFORE calling `pass3_over_findings`. Writing to the finding's
  own `severity_attributes` would silently no-op (impact_code would read only defaults). Best-effort: any
  git/path failure leaves the signal at its safe default (churn 0 => freq_mult 0.5; surface False => no floor).
- PER-GATE DISPATCH: `code_review_decide` passes `impact_fn=impact_code`. Plan-review is byte-unchanged
  (it threads impact_plan; nothing here touches it) — asserted by test.
- CALIBRATION/LABELED SET: a curated fixture at a NEW `tests/unit/fixtures/` directory (created by this ticket, with a provenance README) — `tests/unit/fixtures/code_review_impact_labels.jsonl` — of
  code-review findings each tagged HIGH (block-worthy) or NIT, provenance = the dogfooded code-review corpus +
  this program's held-out adjudication (initial ~31 labeled findings; grows via the data-capture child).
- ADR: this novel two-lane model is an architectural decision — record it under `docs/adr/`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` (`impact_code`), `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`
  (`code_review_verification_model` + CodeSeverityAttrs), `src/rebar/llm/code_review/` (verify-step contract
  wiring, the DET enrichment in the decide op, the verify prompt), the labeled fixture + re-anchoring
  calibration test, and the ADR. Plan-review impact unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `impact_code = max(min(1.0, MAX(prod_lane, maint_lane) * amp), reversibility_floor)` per the explicit
      compose above, with tier-tagged-binary MAX within each lane using the stated tier values and the stated
      trigger_likelihood_mult / freq_mult / reversibility_floor (impact_base>0 gated) / amp formulas. Unit-tested for
      each multiplier + the gate. Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_code.py -v`.
- [ ] Carved serious/moderate/minor sub-question set implemented with charitable carve-outs, ADDED to (not
      replacing) severity_attributes via CodeSeverityAttrs; emitted in ONE aggregate Pass-2 call (no added
      LLM calls); reversibility/reach/change-frequency are DET/hybrid (diff + git) with a churn=0/freq=0.5
      fallback when git is unavailable. Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_code.py -v`.
- [ ] Per-gate dispatch via `impact_fn=impact_code`; a test asserts plan-review's decide path is unchanged
      (impact_plan still dispatched; impact_code never touches it); an ADR under docs/adr/ records the model.
      Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_impact_code.py tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py -v`.
- [ ] `tests/unit/fixtures/code_review_impact_labels.jsonl` exists (each row HIGH/NIT, provenance in a header
      comment or sibling README). A test asserts impact_code SEPARATES the classes on the fixture with a
      CONCRETE margin (NO "or explained" escape): `median(impact_code[HIGH]) - median(impact_code[NIT]) >=
      0.30`, AND that this median gap is strictly GREATER than the old mean `impact`'s gap on the same
      fixture (the redesign beats the old scalar). Validated diff-grounded before any threshold-down tuning
      (the tuning itself is the calibration child raptorial-galloping-dragon).
baseline.summary: Code-review impact model redesign: two-lane tier-tagged MAX with re-anchored scale

baseline.description:
Observed during bug 941b-f049-5f29-4410's rebar-debug pass.

AGENTS.md sets a target of 200-500 LOC per file and a **hard cap of 800**. The CI module-size gate that enforces it covers `src/rebar` only, so this file is over the cap without failing the build.

    932 tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py

It was 917 before 941b and is 932 after (941b removed the session-start field gate and the `_CAPABILITY_FIELD_CONFIRM_BUDGET_S` cap, and added the provisioning evidence that explains why). So 941b did not create the condition and did not meaningfully worsen it, but it also did not fix it, and splitting it was out of that bug's scope.

## The binding constraint: the monkeypatch surface must not move

Two unit tests load this conftest **by path** (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`) and drive it as `harness.<name>`. Critically they do not merely *read* attributes, they **rebind** them:

    tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py:101  monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_request", _fake)
    tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py:104  monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_random_project_key", ...)
    tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py:92       monkeypatch.setattr(harness, "_request", _fake)

A patch on the conftest module object only reaches callers whose **own module globals** are that same namespace. So moving a *stubbed callee* (`_request`) or any of its *callers* (`_create_scratch_project`, `_assert_project_capabilities`, `_leaked_harness_tokens`, `_sweep_leaked_harness_tokens`, `wait_for_jira_dc_ready`, `jira_dc_project`) out of conftest silently un-stubs the network: the moved function resolves `_request` in the NEW module's globals, which the test never patched. That fails open — the unit tests would attempt real HTTP instead of erroring clearly.

The two seams the original filing suggested (the PAT sweep cluster and the scratch-project provisioning cluster) are therefore both **unsafe**: every member of both is either a patch target or a patched-through caller.

## The seam that is safe

The **J11 store-copy / DC-client fixture cluster** — `dc_transport`, `dc_store_copy_repo`, `bound_dc_issue` — already carries its own banner comment in the file explaining it lives in conftest solely because two sibling suites need it. It is a genuine existing call-graph cluster (`bound_dc_issue` consumes `dc_store_copy_repo` and `dc_transport`; all three draw on `_dc_support`), and no member of it is referenced by either unit test, patched or otherwise. Roughly 205 LOC, so the extracted module clears the 100-LOC floor and conftest lands near 730.

## Plan

- Extract `dc_transport`, `dc_store_copy_repo`, and `bound_dc_issue`, with their explanatory
  banner comment, into a sibling `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py`.
- **Re-export them into conftest's namespace** with a top-level
  `from _dc_fixtures import bound_dc_issue, dc_store_copy_repo, dc_transport`, so pytest
  still collects them from conftest exactly as today (pytest registers fixtures found as
  attributes of the conftest module, regardless of where they were defined).
- Resolve the package-less sibling import the same way the file already resolves
  `_engine_path` and `jira_dc_field_readiness`: insert the conftest's own directory on
  `sys.path` before the import, rather than relying on pytest's prepend-mode insertion.
- Thread the base URL through the **fixture graph** rather than duplicating the `_BASE`
  constant into the new module: add a session-scoped `jira_dc_base_url` fixture in conftest
  and have the extracted fixtures depend on it. This avoids a second copy of the env-var
  default drifting from the first.
- Leave `_request`, `_field_request`, `wait_for_jira_dc_ready`, `_random_project_key`,
  `track_issue`, `dc_request`, the PAT cluster, and the provisioning cluster **in conftest**,
  untouched, so the monkeypatch surface above is bit-for-bit preserved.
- Add a regression test asserting the loaded-by-path conftest still exposes the fixture
  surface, so a future move that breaks re-export fails at the unit tier instead of 35
  minutes into a live harness run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` is at or under 800 LOC
- [x] the split follows an existing call-graph seam and creates no file under 100 LOC
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py` and `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py`
      still pass (both load the conftest by PATH, so a move must keep the loaded module's
      surface intact)
- [x] every symbol the unit tests monkeypatch, and every caller that must observe those
      patches, remains defined in conftest
- [x] the moved fixtures are re-exported into conftest's namespace and remain resolvable by
      `pytest --fixtures tests/external/live_jira_dc/`
- [x] lint and typecheck pass
baseline.summary: tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py is 932 LOC, over the 800 hard cap

## Context / Problem
After S2b/S2c, runtime and factories agree, but users still see hand-maintained package help and the old two-family intercept behavior. Canonical generated artifacts may become authoritative only after the complete parser/route census is proven.

## Approach
Add `scripts/gen_cli_help.py` with write and `--check` modes.

- Enumerate canonical/compatibility/hidden routes from the immutable registry; resolve parser factories only in generation/check execution.
- Render with S2a's fixed `prog`, width, formatter, ordering, UTF-8 LF, and trailing-newline policy.
- Write one artifact per canonical help key; exact aliases reuse canonical bytes. Compatibility/hidden spellings render the same argument-definition helpers with approved alias `prog` and replacement epilog.
- Generate the grouped overview from route group/order/visibility plus parser summaries. Canonical visible commands appear once; aliases are annotated rather than duplicated; hidden routes are omitted.
- Fail `--check` on any missing/stale/stray artifact, unresolved factory, non-deterministic second render, registry/parser census mismatch, generated package-data diff, or any PRESENT-but-empty/blank per-command overview one-liner (a command whose factory summary was not enriched — a blank summary is a hard `--check` failure, never silently emitted).
- Keep curated explanations/examples inside parser descriptions/epilogs or later editorial reference sections; no hand-authored usage line or option table may be concatenated after generation.

Cut top-level overview/help/unknown routing to the registry and committed artifacts. The lexical pre-scan handles global config-prefix token shape, command identity, `rebar help <command>`, and a first `--help`/`-h` token after the spelling. It must complete before RP-04 snapshot, config parsing/materialization, mount, handler/factory resolution, or optional imports. Free-text `--help` later in argv remains data/handler input as today.

Approved behavior changes: the 21 formerly intercept-only help forms now succeed safely; overview grouping changes; help output becomes deterministic parser-rendered text; and help artifact bodies are regenerated from the true post-S2b/S2c factory grammar, correcting hand-captured drift (only the capitalized Usage: prefix is preserved byte-for-byte). Unknown/help streams and exit codes, historical `jira-onboard`, hidden `bridge-status`, and unknown `purge-bridge` remain as specified.

## Out-of-directory consumers of the help surface (census + disposition)
The cutover changes package help data read by consumers OUTSIDE `src/rebar/_cli/help/`. Each gets a disposition:

- `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` + its `docs/cli-reference.md` drift gate — reads `_help.known_subcommands()`/`subcommand_help()` and drift-gates `INTERCEPT_COMMANDS` against its OWN `ladder_intercepts()` (at `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py:305`, which parses `_cli/__init__.py` source — not a `rebar._cli.__init__` symbol). Disposition: KEPT WORKING — those `_help` reader signatures are unchanged (they now read GENERATED `help/*.txt`), so no script code change; `docs/cli-reference.md` REGENERATED via its `--check` gate (approved doc delta).
- Tests pinning `known_subcommands()`/`overview()` shape or the intercept set — `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` (`^  <sub>` shape, `_OVERVIEW_ALLOWLIST`), `test_schema_coverage.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes_doc_conformance.py` + `_heldout.py` (`known_subcommands() | _INTERCEPTS`), `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli_argparse.py`, `test_central_mount_gate_ad9f.py` (its pre-operation-boundary sentinels extend to the new help pre-scan). Disposition: UPDATED as approved deltas for new grouping/uniqueness and retired intercept forms. `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py` re-runs, updated only where re-sourcing changes a value.
- Literal `Usage: rebar <cmd>` PREFIX consumers — `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` (81/91/106/112/122), `scripts/probe_rebar.py:585`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py`. Disposition: KEPT VALID by the ONE byte-parity invariant preserved — the CAPITALIZED `Usage:`. Argparse renders lowercase `usage:`, so `gen_cli_help.py` MUST emit `Usage: ` capitalized (a lowercase `usage:` in any artifact fails `--check`). Generation-only; runtime `--help` serves committed txt.
- subcommand_help() BODY-content consumers (not the prefix) — `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_force_unification_blusterous.py:131` (selects `transition`'s `--reason` line), `tests/unit/test_bridge_projects_surfaces_heldout.py:124` (asserts `bridge` help has `projects`). Disposition: KEPT VALID because the enriched `transition`/`bridge` factories genuinely render those same option/subparser lines; verified by exact-artifact-bytes assertions. Two PRODUCTION runtime sites also render the regenerated body: `_bridge_commands._group_help()` (`_bridge_commands.py:63` → `subcommand_help("bridge")`, written to stdout at :257 as `rebar bridge` bare-invocation help) and `transition.py:748` (`subcommand_help("reopen")` → stderr on reopen-no-args). Both are KEPT VALID via the regenerated factory bytes, each verified by an exact-artifact-bytes subprocess assertion.
- Help artifact BODIES (below the `Usage:` line) — APPROVED REGENERATION DELTA, not byte-exact with today's committed text (that hand-captured drift is what this task eliminates). Proof they must be corrected to the factory's real grammar: `help/show.txt` shows `[--output llm] [--no-pull]` but `build_show()` (`_parsers/core/reads.py`) has `--output {json,llm}`, `--include-scratch`/`--include-provenance`, and NO `--no-pull`; `help/list.txt` carries per-option help + `--no-pull` absent from `build_list()`; `help/overview.txt` carries curated one-liners absent from factory summaries. The factory (true runtime grammar) wins; `--check` pins the regenerated bytes.
- Factory enrichment (home for curated prose) — core factories carry ZERO argument `help=` text/`description`, so the curated per-option/per-subcommand text now in the artifacts has no render home. This task ENRICHES `_parsers/core/` and `_parsers/advanced/` with per-argument `help=`, `description`/`epilog`, and `argparse.SUPPRESS` for hidden args — so the prose lives in the parser and the generator renders it (no hand-authored table concatenated after generation).

## Compatibility and Rollback
The existing execution ladder remains active. Commit generator, artifacts, route-help lookup, and subprocess tests together. Reverting this task restores the old help family without changing runtime grammar or stored data.

## Testing
Use generator unit tests and real CLI subprocess tests in a fresh attachable checkout. Sentinels raise if help/unknown paths compose an operation snapshot, read config, mount/create a store, resolve a parser/handler, or import heavy optional modules. Assert exact artifact bytes, streams, exit codes, overview uniqueness/grouping, every alias class, malformed global syntax, free-text negative control, and a normal execution control that still crosses operation/mount boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check` proves every registered help artifact and overview are deterministic, parser-derived, complete, and free of stale/stray resources.
- [x] Every visible canonical command appears once in the grouped overview; exact aliases reuse bytes and compatibility/hidden/retired spellings follow the approved rules.
- [x] Both top-level help forms return exact committed generated bytes before operation/config/store/parser/handler/optional-import boundaries.
- [x] Free-text later `--help`, malformed global syntax, unknown commands, streams, and exit codes match the explicit compatibility contract.
- [x] A normal execution negative control still reaches RP-04 operation composition and established mount/init behavior through the old execution ladder.
- [x] No hand-maintained usage or option table remains in package help.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2d — Generate and serve canonical help from runtime parser factories

## Client report
`AGENTS.md` and the setup/onboarding documentation do not tell a new contributor to run `rebar identity create --self` before using gates that sign attestations. A correctly installed checkout can therefore reach a signing gate without the local identity prerequisite and fail only at gate time.

The documentation gap is reported by a client project. Investigation must first confirm which supported bootstrap flows create an identity automatically, which gates require one, and whether `identity create --self` is universally correct or conditional on repository policy.

## Plan
- Reproduce onboarding from a clean temporary home/config using the documented setup path and the first signing gate.
- Trace the identity lookup/error path and inventory every authoritative setup surface (`AGENTS.md`, local-dev/setup guides, contributor guide, packaged explanations).
- Confirm the intended prerequisite and placement before editing docs.
- Add a documentation/CLI contract test or rendered-help assertion at the smallest tier that fails when all setup paths omit the prerequisite.
- Update each authoritative onboarding surface without duplicating contradictory guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A clean-environment reproduction identifies the first signing operation that fails and the exact missing identity state.
- [ ] The intended use and scope of `rebar identity create --self` are cited from implementation/help or an approved identity contract.
- [ ] Every authoritative setup/onboarding path either creates the identity or instructs the user when and how to run `rebar identity create --self`.
- [ ] The guidance explains how to verify the identity and distinguishes repository-local versus user-global state as applicable.
- [ ] A gating test detects regression of the prerequisite guidance without asserting incidental prose formatting.
- [ ] Existing install/bootstrap flows that already provision identity remain accurate and are not duplicated or contradicted.
baseline.summary: Setup docs omit rebar identity create --self before signing gates

## Context
The GitHub About description currently says Rebar is an LLM-first event-sourced ticket system and Jira reconciler, then identifies GitHub as a read-only mirror. It does not explain the capability that distinguishes Rebar from conventional trackers. ADR 0018 and the plan-review gate guidance establish enforceable review before claim. The completion gate and operation-certificate guidance establish signed verification before close.

## Plan
- Replace the `navapbc/rebar` repository description with concise client-facing wording that leads with plan review.
- State the observable mechanisms rather than make an unsupported superiority claim.
- Preserve the read-only GitHub mirror and Gerrit code-review facts.
- Keep the description within GitHub limits and avoid internal implementation terms.
- Read the repository metadata back after the update and record the exact value.
- Change GitHub repository metadata only.

## Proposed Description
Rebar can block work until an AI plan review passes, require signed completion verification before close, and reconcile its event-sourced ticket record with Jira across CLI, Python, and MCP. GitHub is a read-only mirror. Code review runs in Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The GitHub About description leads with enforceable plan review before work begins.
- [x] It names signed completion verification, event-sourced history, Jira reconciliation, and the CLI, Python, and MCP interfaces.
- [x] It preserves the read-only mirror and Gerrit review facts.
- [x] It fits the GitHub repository-description limit.

  provenance: environment=GitHub repository metadata for navapbc/rebar; principal=JoeOakhartNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — authoritative GitHub repository metadata readback for the About description

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase` (`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and `process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds, at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and `_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22` is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus `_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker: `_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [ ] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [ ] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the STATUS cluster from reducer/_processors.py into _processors_status.py

baseline.description:
## The documented guarantee is false

`docs/user-guide.md` states, as a SECURITY property of the DC backend:

> `JIRA_PAT` is read from the environment and is **not** accepted from a committed config file, so
> the credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident; the transport never logs it, and **a
> missing `JIRA_PAT` fails with an error naming the variable rather than falling back to anonymous
> access.**

The first two clauses hold. The third does not.

## Mechanism, read from the code

* `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:76` — `pat=os.environ.get("JIRA_PAT", "")`. Absent variable
  yields the EMPTY STRING. There is no validation anywhere that the PAT is non-empty.
* `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:95` — `jira_cls(server=settings.url,
  token_auth=settings.pat, options=...)`. The empty string is passed as the bearer token. The client
  constructs successfully, and requests go out with no usable credential, so Jira treats the caller as
  ANONYMOUS.

## Observed live — GitHub Actions run 30652534806, job "jira DC harness smoke"

`test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` removes `JIRA_PAT` from the environment (leaving it only in the config file, which must NOT be honoured) and runs the documented `rebar reconcile --dry-run`. Expected: a failure naming `JIRA_PAT`. Actual:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 400: JiraError HTTP 400
      url: .../rest/api/2/search?jql=project+%3D+RBJUXFD+AND+...
      response text = {"errorMessages":["The value 'RBJUXFD' does not exist for the field 'project'."]}

Jira returns exactly "does not exist for the field 'project'" when the caller lacks Browse permission — it deliberately does not distinguish absent-from-forbidden, to avoid leaking project existence. So an anonymous request against a real project produces precisely this message.

Corroborating evidence from the SAME run: `test_the_documented_config_and_dry_run_work_against_a_real_dc_instance` PASSED against the same harness, same fixture, same scratch-project machinery, with `JIRA_PAT` SET. The only difference between the passing and failing case is the credential.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

1. **The failure MISATTRIBUTES, in the most expensive possible direction.** An operator who forgets to
   export `JIRA_PAT` is told their PROJECT does not exist. They will go and check project keys,
   permissions and JQL — everything except the credential. This is the same misattribution class that
   cost this epic a debugging session on the PAT-cap bug, where the error surfaced in an untouched
   module.
2. **It is a documented SECURITY guarantee that nothing enforces.** The guide is telling operators
   that rebar fails closed on a missing credential. It fails OPEN, to anonymous.
3. **An anonymous pass can look benign.** On an instance where anonymous CAN browse the project, a
   credential-less run would not error at all — it would read a partial or empty view and report a
   converged pass. That is the "green but broken" shape this epic keeps finding.

## Approach

Validate the PAT at CLIENT-CONSTRUCTION time (`build_client_from_settings`) and fail with an actionable error naming the variable — the behaviour the guide already promises.

**REVISED after CI falsified the first placement.** An earlier draft put the check in `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` and rejected client-construction on the reasoning that "the invariant belongs where the value is resolved". That reasoning was wrong, and the evidence is concrete: resolution is reached from PROPERTIES (`JiraDataCenterBackend.query_project`), and on Python <= 3.11 `isinstance(x, SomeRuntimeCheckableProtocol)` evaluates properties via `hasattr`. A raise there breaks every Protocol conformance check. Python 3.12+ switched to `inspect.getattr_static`, which does NOT execute properties — so the breakage is INVISIBLE on a modern local interpreter and appears only on the CI matrix's 3.11 leg. Measured: two backend-facade tests (`test_isinstance_backend_facade[jira-datacenter]`, `test_dc_backend_satisfies_the_backend_facade`) passed on 3.14 locally and failed on 3.11 in CI run 30653881576, earning a Verified -1.

Client construction is strictly better anyway: it is the LAST point before the network, it is the one place an anonymous client can come into existence, and it cannot be reached by an attribute probe. Settings resolution therefore stays TOTAL — it must not raise merely because a credential is absent — and a regression test asserts that via `hasattr` on the property, so the guarantee holds regardless of which interpreter runs the suite.

Note `Backend.assert_env_ready` ALREADY makes this check and names JIRA_PAT, but it is only reached from the bootstrap-band path (`_attestation.py:68`), which is why dry-run and ordinary reconcile passes still went anonymous.

The error must name `JIRA_PAT` explicitly and say it is environment-only, because the most likely mistake is putting it in the config file — which is exactly what the guide forbids and what this test simulates.

**Rejected: validating at settings resolution.** It is the more obvious home and was the first attempt; it breaks Protocol conformance checks on Python <= 3.11 for the reason above. Any future move back must first explain how `query_project` stays probe-safe.

**Rejected: allowing an empty PAT for read-only/anonymous instances.** Anonymous access is not a supported deployment for this backend (the guide's least-privilege section mandates a dedicated service account), and the failure mode above shows an anonymous run is indistinguishable from a working one on a permissive instance.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — reject an
  empty/missing PAT in `build_client_from_settings`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` — keep resolution TOTAL
  (a comment records why the guard is not here).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — unit coverage for the new guard.

## Testing

* **unit** — `build_client_from_settings` with an empty / whitespace / blank PAT raises an error whose
  message contains `JIRA_PAT` and names the anonymous-fallback consequence; with a real value it
  builds a client and passes the token through as `token_auth`.
* **unit** — the error is raised BEFORE any client is constructed or any network call is attempted,
  asserted by a client factory that fails the test if it is invoked.
* **unit, the py3.11 regression guard** — `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings` stays TOTAL with
  `JIRA_PAT` unset, asserted the way Python 3.11's Protocol check exercises it
  (`hasattr(backend, "query_project")` must be True and must not raise). Written as a direct `hasattr`
  assertion rather than an `isinstance` so it holds on ANY interpreter — a 3.12+ runner would not
  reproduce the failure through `isinstance` at all, which is precisely how this shipped a Verified -1.
* **live** — `test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config`, already written and
  currently FAILING in the harness job, passes. That test is the regression oracle and it was authored
  before this defect was known, so it is not fitted to the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with `JIRA_PAT` absent, BUILDING THE DC CLIENT fails with an error whose text contains
      `JIRA_PAT` and names the anonymous-fallback consequence, asserted by unit test
- [ ] a whitespace-only `JIRA_PAT` is rejected the same way, since an accidental empty export is the
      same failure with a different shape
- [ ] the failure happens BEFORE any network call, asserted by a client factory that fails the test
      if it is invoked
- [ ] settings resolution stays TOTAL — it does not raise on a missing credential — asserted the way
      Python 3.11 exercises it (`hasattr` on `query_project`), so `isinstance(backend, Backend)` keeps
      working on the 3.11 CI leg. This is the specific regression that earned a Verified -1
- [ ] a PAT present ONLY in the config file does not satisfy the check — the env-only contract the
      guide promises is preserved
- [ ] the live `test_the_documented_setup_refuses_to_read_the_pat_from_config` passes in the
      `jira DC harness smoke` job, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the guide's wording and the code now agree; no doc change should be needed, so if one IS made
      it must be because the code cannot deliver the promise, and that must be stated explicitly
baseline.summary: Missing JIRA_PAT falls back to ANONYMOUS access instead of failing with a named error

## Context / Problem
Split out of bug adb6-4762-90f6-4e30 (peach-chemic-hairstreak) by operator ruling (2026-08-21): the fresh-shell fix pins bedrock_region_name = "us-east-1" in rebar.toml's [llm] table, but the verdict's provider provenance cannot yet truthfully record that the region came from repo config.

RCA finding (proven statically on the bug ticket, 2026-08-17): LLMConfig.from_env collapses CLI/env/config-file resolution of bedrock_region_name into ONE string via _llm_str (src/rebar/llm/config.py), discarding the value's origin. resolve_bedrock_region (src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py) then labels EVERY configured non-empty value as region_source=REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION — so a rebar.toml pin is mislabeled as the env var in provenance records (pinned today by tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py, which asserts region_source == "REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION" for a configured region).

## Approach
Add source metadata/plumbing so provenance records region_source truthfully ("repo-config" for the config-file table, "cli" for `rebar -c llm.bedrock_region_name=…`, and the existing "REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION" / "AWS_DEFAULT_REGION" / "AWS_REGION" labels), without changing which value wins. The label is derived from the SAME single resolution pass that produced the value (a source-returning variant of _llm_str that _llm_str delegates to), carried on LLMConfig as bedrock_region_source, and threaded to resolve_bedrock_region / provenance_for — never re-derived independently, so record and runtime cannot diverge. Operator caution (recorded on the bug ticket): provenance labeling may interact with config wiring and env-var handling — design to avoid regression there, and maintain portability across diverse environments (no CI-provider-specific trigger; see project.portability).

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/config.py — carry the resolved region's origin (do not regress _llm_str precedence: CLI > env > file > default)
- src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py — resolve_bedrock_region labels the configured value by its true source
- src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py — provenance_for threads the configured source into the resolver
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py — thread cfg.bedrock_region_source alongside cfg.bedrock_region_name
- tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py, tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py — update/extend the pins

## Testing
RED first: extend `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` and `tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` with the truthful-label pins (they fail against the current always-REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION labeling), then implement. Prove with:
- `pytest tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` — the full precedence+label matrix and the provenance record pins.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_llm_config.py tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_removal.py` (or the nearest config-layer suites) — no regression in the CLI > env > file resolution wiring.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — the complexity ratchet and types stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A region resolved from the config-file table is recorded in provider provenance as region_source="repo-config", not "REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION" (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py`).
- [x] A region resolved from the REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION env var keeps region_source="REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION"; AWS_DEFAULT_REGION / AWS_REGION keep their existing labels (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`).
- [x] A region resolved from `rebar -c llm.bedrock_region_name=…` is labeled "cli" (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`).
- [x] Resolution precedence is unchanged: CLI > REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION > config file, then AWS_DEFAULT_REGION > AWS_REGION; every source combination's precedence+label pair is pinned (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`).
- [x] The resolved region VALUE and every provider build path are byte-identical for identical inputs — the label is additive metadata only (verified: the existing build-path tests in `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` pass with no wiring changes).
- [x] Works with no CI provider present: pure in-process labeling with nothing CI-specific (checked: the diff touches only library code + unit tests, no CI-provider hooks).
baseline.summary: Label Bedrock region provenance (region_source) accurately when the region comes from repo config

## Status

**Parked as an idea mid-brainstorm (2026-07-18).** The design is NOT final. We paused at
Decision 2 (freshness). "Open decisions" at the end records exactly where to resume. This
ticket is the durable, self-contained capture of the research, discussion, and decisions so
far, per the user's request to "park this as an idea with full details."

## Purpose

Standardize a **mandatory, compact handoff structure** for interrupted or reassigned agent
work. Rebar already has durable tickets, comments, scratch, git state, and claims; what is
missing is a fixed, small contract that lets a fresh context (the same agent after its window
dies, a different agent, or an orchestrator) **reproduce a known-good baseline and understand
the in-flight state** instead of reconstructing assumptions from scratch.

## Two failure modes it kills

1. Treating partially-completed work as a sound foundation **without validating it**.
2. Spending a new context window **reconstructing assumptions that should have been
   externalized**.

It also gives the orchestrator a structured way to distinguish **ordinary continuation** from
a **plan-invalidating event** (baseline no longer reproduces).

The originally-proposed 10 fields: (1) Known-good commit, (2) Baseline verification command,
(3) Baseline result, (4) Current change objective, (5) Files/contracts changed, (6) Unresolved
observations/hypotheses, (7) Currently failing checks, (8) Next bounded action,
(9) Stop/escalation condition, (10) Rollback point.

---

## Research — existing rebar building blocks (reuse vs off-limits)

Verified against source by three exploration passes. Key file:line anchors preserved so a
resumer can go straight to them.

- **`verify_commands`** event/state + `set_verify_commands`/`get_verify_commands` lib API —
  already stores per-ticket verification commands, synced, first-class. This IS field #2
  (baseline verification command). Shape: `{dd_id?, dd_text?, command}`.
- **`commits`** / `attach_commits` (lib) — commit provenance on a ticket. Home for field #1
  (known-good commit / rollback point).
- **`file_impact`** event/state (`{path, reason}`) + `get/set_file_impact` — home for field #5
  (files/contracts changed). Note: it records *intended impact*; the resumer wants the *delta
  since baseline*.
- **`session_log`** ticket type (`docs/event-schema.md:69-100`) — the existing append-only
  **handoff trail** (narrative history). Gate/lifecycle-exempt; cannot be claimed/transitioned;
  searchable but hidden from `list`; non-blocking links only; never synced to Jira. Content
  lives in COMMENTs. Local git-ignored pointer `.rebar/current_session_log` **auto-rotates per
  session fingerprint** (`REBAR_SESSION_ID → CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID → SESSION_ID`); degrade-safe
  when no fingerprint. This is the *history/trail*; the resumption contract is the *current
  distilled state* — complementary (tiered-memory pattern).
- **`scratch`** (`src/rebar/_commands/scratch.py`) — per-ticket key/value string store, BUT
  **filesystem-only, never synced, no lock, purged on ticket close/delete**, 96 KiB/value.
  **OFF-LIMITS as the substrate** — a resumer on another machine would never see it. The
  handoff MUST live in the synced store (events on the `tickets` branch, auto-committed +
  auto-pushed to `sync.remote`).
- **Comments** — freeform `body` string + fixed metadata (`author`, `timestamp`); non-string
  bodies are JSON-coerced to a string. No first-class structured payload — structure must be
  serialized into the body.
- **Claim** — one-shot `open → in_progress`; stamps only scalar session-provenance keys
  (`claimed_session`, `claim_harness`, `claim_remote_session`). **There is NO pause / release /
  yield / un-claim operation, and no `resumed_by`/`resumed_at`.** Transition *into* `in_progress`
  (from `open`, `blocked`, or reactivating `closed`) is gated identically to claim.
- **Gates** — inline, **opt-in, default-OFF**, funneled through one seam
  (`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`, keyed `verify.<flag>`, fail-open on unreadable config). Two
  today: the **plan-review claim gate** (on claim + transition-to-in_progress) and the
  **completion-verifier close gate** (on `→ closed`, fail-closed). This seam is the natural
  wiring point if "reproduce baseline before continuing" becomes an enforced gate. NB: default-off
  cuts against calling anything "mandatory by default."
- **Description "templates"** — NOT a stored scaffold; enforced as a **clarity-gate scoring
  heuristic** (`_clarity_score`, `gates.py:110-167`) that rewards per-type `##` headings.
- **Naming collision:** "checkpoint" and "baseline" are already taken — by the plan-review LLM
  engine and the reconciler three-way-merge respectively. Pick a distinct name (e.g.
  "resumption", "handoff").

## Research — prior-art synthesis (what to keep, add, avoid)

**The reproducibility trio (#1 commit, #2 command, #3 result) is the design's genuine
differentiator.** Most human and AI handoff formats only *soft drift-check* and assume the
workspace is intact; re-deriving a verified baseline is the strongest, best-established idea in
the body of prior art and this design has it front-and-center. Backing: git bisect
known-good/known-bad + adjudicating test; CI "last-known-good / green trunk"; TDD RED→GREEN
("one small step from green"); SLSA provenance + in-toto ("verify before trust"); reproducible
-builds ("same source + env + instructions"); "Reflections on Trusting Trust" / diverse
double-compiling (don't trust inherited state; independently reproduce).

**Additions prior art demanded (ranked), and our disposition:**

- **Receiver read-back / re-verification step** (I-PASS "Synthesis"; SBARR/ISBARR read-back;
  aviation challenge-response; ICS face-to-face transfer; SLSA VSA digest-match). The single
  biggest structural pattern: the contract as proposed is **write-only**; every mature protocol
  added a receiver step. The user's spec ALREADY includes this ("the resumer first reproduces
  the baseline") — it is the strongest part, so enforcement should bite HERE. → **Decision 4
  (open).**
- **Decisions / dead-ends layer** (Cognition "Don't Build Multi-Agents": compress history into
  *decisions*; Anthropic context-engineering: preserve architectural decisions;
  `claude-handoff` format calls "Failed Approaches" its "most valuable part"; blameless
  postmortem "who decided X and why"). → **Folded into field #6 (open + closed), with a pointer
  to the comment trail** (my recommendation; standing unless vetoed).
- **Freshness stamp** (SHA + timestamp + branch on the record; SLSA identity; SRE
  "last-updated by jennifer"; docs-rot). Kills the "note written at step 3, read at step 30,
  silently lies" mode. → **APPROVED.**
- **Environment / toolchain fingerprint** (reproducible-builds "same commit ≠ same baseline";
  hermetic builds; MCVE env). → **DROPPED** (project builds not env-sensitive enough to earn a
  usually-noise field).
- **Owner / next-owner / escalation target** (ICS, SRE, PagerDuty, OPORD). Partially covered by
  field #9. → **not yet decided.**
- **Definition-of-done / desired end-state / commander's intent — the "why"** (SRE Exit
  Criteria; Agile DoD; OPORD end-state). The fallback when field #8's next-action turns out
  wrong. → **not yet decided (tie to field #4).**
- **Severity / blast-radius**, **in-flight/pending work** (running CI, spawned sub-agents,
  awaited reviews — field #7 captures failing, not pending). → severity not adopted; pending-work
  noted as a #7 refinement.

**Field refinements prior art suggests (not yet locked):** #3 baseline result should be
*evidence* (exit code / digest), state what "green" covers, and have a **third "unverifiable"**
state (git bisect exit 125), not a boolean. #4 should separate *what* (objective) from *why*
(intent/end-state). #7 should carry expected-vs-actual and a deterministic-vs-flaky qualifier.
#8 should be specific, measurable, idempotent/safe-to-replay. #9 should be plural if-then +
named escalation target.

## Research — failure modes to design around

- **Mandatory write-side template = documented failure.** Ontario mandated the WHO surgical
  checklist: 92–100% compliance, **zero** measurable benefit (NEJM 2014) — pure box-ticking.
  Goodhart's / Campbell's law, normalization-of-deviance, and cargo-cult process all predict a
  "template completed" target becomes a plausible fill, not truth. A 20k-session study found
  agents "prematurely claim success" 27.6% of the time; agents emit "all tests pass" even when
  hidden tests fail. → **Put the mandate on the machine-verifiable resume action (re-run the
  baseline), keep the self-authored fields lean and evidence-bearing, grade *resumption
  success*, not fields-filled.**
- **Handoff is written at the worst moment** — interruption coincides with a full window /
  context rot (least-reliable model) and human-factors omission-under-load. → maintain the
  record continuously; derive machine fields from git/test output, not degraded recall.
- **Staleness / docs-rot** — a note read late actively misleads. → freshness stamp; resumer
  diffs stamp vs reality first.
- **Checklist bloat / "lost in the middle"** — 10 fields is at Gawande's 5–9 ceiling; long
  handoffs are partially ignored (U-shaped attention, arXiv 2307.03172). → killer items only;
  front-load the resume point; cut re-derivable/usually-empty fields.
- **Trusting-trust circularity** — never trust inherited "result: green"; the resumer
  independently re-derives.

**Two structural patterns the research repeatedly points to:** (a) **split by direction** —
*writing* = DO-CONFIRM (short verification pause on killer items); *resuming* = READ-DO (an
ordered recipe of commands the resumer executes to re-establish + confirm the baseline before
continuing). (b) **tier memory** — compact contract PLUS a pointer to the full searchable trace
(session_log / comments).

---

## Decision log (locked so far)

1. **Freshness stamp — ADDED.** Record carries its own commit SHA + timestamp + branch.
2. **Rollback point merged into known-good commit** — one field (CI treats last-known-good as
   both baseline and revert target).
3. **Environment fingerprint — DROPPED.**
4. **Decisions/dead-ends — folded into field #6** (reframe as open + closed items, with a
   pointer to the comment trail), not a new 11th field. *My recommendation; standing unless the
   user vetoes.*

## Current field list (evolving)

1. **Known-good commit** (also the rollback point) — reuse `commits`/`attach_commits`.
2. **Baseline verification command** — reuse `verify_commands`.
3. **Baseline result** — evidence (exit code/digest); three states incl. "unverifiable" *(refine)*.
4. **Current change objective** — possibly split what vs why/end-state *(open)*.
5. **Files/contracts changed** — reuse `file_impact`; foreground delta-since-baseline.
6. **Open + closed items** — unresolved observations/hypotheses AND ruled-out approaches /
   settled decisions, with a pointer to the comment trail *(folded, per Decision 4 above)*.
7. **Currently failing checks** — + expected-vs-actual, deterministic-vs-flaky, pending/in-flight *(refine)*.
8. **Next bounded action** — specific, measurable, idempotent/safe-to-replay *(refine)*.
9. **Stop / escalation condition** — plural if-then + named escalation target *(refine)*.
10. **Freshness stamp** — NEW, approved.

## Open decisions (RESUME HERE)

- **Decision 2 — freshness (PAUSED HERE).** Continuous-at-checkpoints *(my lean: robust to
  ungraceful interruption; stamp makes lag visible)* vs write-at-interruption *(simpler, but the
  interruptions you most need to survive are the ungraceful ones)*.
- **Decision 3 — who fills it in.** Hand-typed vs auto-derive the mechanical fields
  (commit / failing checks / changed files) from git/test output, agent adds only judgment
  fields. (Determines whether "continuous" is realistic or ceremony.)
- **Decision 4 — what the resumer MUST do.** Read only vs must re-run the baseline before it is
  allowed to continue (the receiver read-back the prior art most strongly endorses).
- **Decision 5 — what "go into diagnosis" is.** A real recorded task state the orchestrator can
  see, vs behavioral guidance only.
- **Decision 6 — how mandatory, enforced by what.** Rebar code gate (via the `gates.py` seam)
  vs skill/convention. This also decides whether rebar core changes at all, or it's a protocol
  layered on existing primitives (session_log + verify_commands + a description convention).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Brainstorm resumed and Decisions 2–6 settled before any implementation.
- [ ] Final design records purpose, edge-case behavior, and a high-confidence implementation
      plan for the chosen substrate/enforcement.
- [ ] (When built) implementation tickets authored to pass the plan-review gate.
baseline.summary: Session-resumption contract — standardize a compact handoff for interrupted/reassigned work (DESIGN IN PROGRESS)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py:47-69` currently proves only that a name already enrolled in `tests/golden/config_surface.json` is still live or explicitly retired. It intentionally permits a new canonical schema key or canonical environment name to be absent from the golden, so that name can later disappear without ever reaching the removal oracle. The repository has a hand-maintained golden file; there is no existing generator to update.

## Approach

Add a named deterministic generator/check at `scripts/generate_config_surface_golden.py`. It will derive the live canonical `config_keys` from `_SECTIONS` and `canonical_env_vars` from `_canonical_env_name`, sort both lists, and serialize the committed golden with stable JSON formatting and a trailing newline. Its `--check` mode will independently regenerate the expected structured data and fail when `tests/golden/config_surface.json` differs, without rewriting it.

Keep the golden as the canonical live inventory only: aliases and tombstones are not generator output. Extend the focused golden tests with both set directions: `golden - (live | explicit aliases | tombstones)` continues to reject unrecorded removals, and `live - golden` rejects unenrolled canonical additions. Preserve explicit config and environment alias/tombstone controls, and verify the existing held-out config-health consumer continues to read the regenerated data.

## Scope

- `scripts/generate_config_surface_golden.py` (new deterministic generator and `--check` contract)
- `tests/golden/config_surface.json`
- `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py`
- `tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py`
- canonical config/environment registries only if a deterministic read-only inventory seam is genuinely required

## Testing

Run the generator twice and compare byte-identical output; run `--check` against the committed golden; exercise missing-live-schema-key, missing-live-environment-name, stale-golden-name, explicit-alias, and tombstone controls; then run both config-surface and held-out config-health tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `scripts/generate_config_surface_golden.py` deterministically derives and stably serializes the canonical config-key and environment-name inventories; two runs produce byte-identical `tests/golden/config_surface.json`.
- [x] `scripts/generate_config_surface_golden.py --check` exits nonzero without rewriting when the committed golden differs from the derived inventory, and exits zero for the regenerated committed file.
- [x] A focused test fails when a live canonical schema key is absent from the golden.
- [x] A focused test fails when a live canonical environment name is absent from the golden.
- [x] A golden name removed from the live inventory remains accepted only when its explicit alias or tombstone record accounts for it; unaccounted removals fail.
- [x] The config-surface suite and `tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py` pass against the regenerated golden.
baseline.summary: Make config-surface golden enrollment bidirectional

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase` (`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and `process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds, at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and `_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22` is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus `_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker: `_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [x] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [x] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [x] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [x] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the STATUS cluster from reducer/_processors.py into _processors_status.py
