## Status — RESCOPED + CLOSED (operator-approved 2026-07-18)

This story is closed against a **rescoped** acceptance set. It had two separable halves:

1. **A DETERMINISTIC half — DESIGNED AND BUILT.** The seeded-defect **mutant corpus**, the
   **mutation-assembly + benchmark-driver harness**, the **pure counting helpers**, the
   **pre-registered thresholds**, and their **golden tests**. This lives as WIP in the `cal-e2`
   worktree on branch `calib/6982-e2` (`assemble_e2_mutants.py`, `run_e2_benchmark.py`,
   `e2_counting.py`, `runs/e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl`, `runs/e2_thresholds.json`,
   `tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_counting.py`, `test_e2_benchmark.py`). It is **not landed on
   main** — the harness's only runtime purpose is to drive the rejected batch (below), so landing
   it would ship a moot LLM-spend entry point. It is recorded here as documented WIP.

2. **An EXPENSIVE LLM BATCH BASELINE — PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost, and SUPERSEDED.** The
   ~100-run live scoring of the mutant/control corpus by the current gate (`run_e2_benchmark.py`'s
   `review_plan` sweep, and the `e2_baseline.json` / `e2_run_validity.json` / `e2_verdicts.jsonl`
   it would emit) is **dropped**. It is superseded by story **d8a5** (change **#798, MERGED**):
   the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder (`criterion_effectiveness.py`, on main),
   which accumulates the SAME detection / blocking-FP signal from real production reviews at **$0
   marginal LLM cost**. Baseline **mining** from history is also dead: only ~4 `plan-v3` sidecar
   baselines exist against the ~200 needed — the `impact_model_version` bump stranded the history.

The design record below (Why / classes / mechanism) is retained as the account of what was built;
the Acceptance Criteria are rescoped to the delivered deterministic WIP only.

## Why

R1 (asserted-capability probe), R3 (decomposition-shape), and R4 (necessity gate) all gate on
DETECTION POWER, which can only be measured against plans whose defects are KNOWN. This story
builds that ground truth by CONSTRUCTION: take real cleanly-closed plans, seed exactly one defect
per class, and the mutation itself is the label — no fresh LLM adjudication (which would duplicate
the gate's own sidecar and be circular; that is why E1's finding-level LLM labeling was
invalidated). The unmutated originals are the controls that bound blocking false positives.

Named verbatim in `docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md` §6 R3: "Seeded-flaw eval: take
10 real historical epics that closed cleanly; generate mutated variants ... Pass condition: ≥7/10
mutants flagged, ≤1/10 originals flagged." E2 generalizes that to all five defect classes.

**Five defect classes** (each mutated mechanically from a real cleanly-closed base plan):

1. **absent asserted capability** — plan asserts a named module provides a capability it lacks.
2. **layer-cake split** — children re-partitioned by architectural layer so no single child
   yields an end-to-end observable outcome.
3. **consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge** — a child names an artifact a sibling creates with
   no `depends_on`/`blocks` edge.
4. **unnecessary mechanism** — one over-action line injects a NAMED mechanism the plan does not
   need (FixedBench over-action), selected deterministically by `hash(base_id) % len(templates)`.
5. **untagged operational AC** — mutation strips the `[operator-attested]` tag from an AC whose
   completion evidence lives outside the codebase.

The corpus was built from `runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl` under a codebase-grounded "cleanly-closed"
filter (`post_claim_edit_class=="none"` AND `reopen_count==0` AND `force_close==false` AND live
`closed` status AND, for container classes 2 & 3, ≥2 children). Counting rule pinned in the pure,
golden-tested `e2_counting.py` (`classify_pair`, `run_validity`) which handles the gate's
PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE verdicts and the ≥0.20 INDETERMINATE run-validity cap. Store isolation is
by construction: the harness runs the gate against a standalone `git clone --local --branch tickets`
of the store (its own `.git` directory), so mutation commits never touch the real `.tickets-tracker`.

**Why the batch was never worth its cost.** The corpus + harness + counting helpers are complete
and construct-valid, but the ONLY thing running them adds is a one-shot snapshot of today's gate's
detection/FP numbers — which d8a5's standing recorder now produces continuously from real reviews
for free, and which mining cannot reconstruct (stranded history). The operator therefore rejected
the ~100-run batch permanently and accepted the deterministic build as the deliverable.

## Scope (delivered as WIP on `calib/6982-e2`; NOT landed on main)

- `harnesses/assemble_e2_mutants.py` — mutation-assembly script (deterministic, no LLM).
- `harnesses/e2_counting.py` — pure `classify_pair` / `run_validity` counting helpers (no LLM).
- `harnesses/run_e2_benchmark.py` — benchmark driver. Its store-clone/isolation and `emit_baseline`
  run-validity-guard SEAMS are built and unit-tested offline; its live `review_plan` sweep is the
  rejected batch and is NOT to be executed.
- `runs/e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl`, `runs/e2_thresholds.json` — corpus + pre-registered thresholds.
- `tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_counting.py`, `test_e2_benchmark.py` — golden/synthetic tests
  (offline; no LLM).
- README section documenting the design as WIP + the batch deferral.
- NO `src/rebar` gate/source changes (E2 was measurement, not a gate change).

## Acceptance Criteria (rescoped — delivered deterministic WIP only)

- [ ] **Mutant corpus BUILT.** `runs/e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl` holds ≥10 mutant rows for each of
  defect classes 1–4 (class 5 degrades to N≥5 with the shortfall recorded per the class-5 ladder),
  each paired with exactly one control row; every row carries `pair_id`, `defect_class`, `role`,
  `source_ticket_id`, `plan_text`, `children`, and (mutants) `mutation_op` + `mutation_diff`; each
  class-5 control's `plan_text` retains an `[operator-attested]` AC line the mutant strips. Built
  and verifiable in the `calib/6982-e2` worktree; deterministic (no LLM).
- [ ] **Thresholds pre-registered.** `runs/e2_thresholds.json` pins per-class detection /
  blocking-FP targets for all 5 classes plus the INDETERMINATE run-validity cap. Built as WIP;
  deterministic.
- [ ] **Counting helpers BUILT + golden-tested.** `e2_counting.py`'s pure `classify_pair`
  (INDETERMINATE→FN not FP; multi-criteria set-intersection attribution) and `run_validity`
  (≥0.20 INDETERMINATE-cap) pass `pytest tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_counting.py` offline (no
  LLM). Built as WIP on `calib/6982-e2`.
- [ ] **Baseline-emit guard BUILT + tested.** `run_e2_benchmark.emit_baseline` enforces (not merely
  computes) the run-validity guard — returns non-zero and writes no `out_path` when any class
  exceeds the INDETERMINATE cap — proven by the synthetic-fixture integration test
  `pytest tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_benchmark.py` (offline; imports the seam only, no LLM).
  Built as WIP.
- [ ] **Store-isolation implemented BY CONSTRUCTION.** The harness sources its mutant store as a
  standalone `git clone --local --branch tickets` (own `.git` DIRECTORY, not a linked-worktree
  pointer) and asserts standalone-ness before any injection, so the real `.tickets-tracker` cannot
  be contaminated. Implemented in `run_e2_benchmark.py`; verified by code inspection (the
  live `--self-check-isolation` run is part of the deferred batch and is NOT executed).
- [ ] **[operator-attested] Batch baseline DEFERRED — permanently rejected on cost, superseded by
  d8a5.** The live ~100-run `run_e2_benchmark.py` gate sweep and its `e2_baseline.json` /
  `e2_run_validity.json` / `e2_verdicts.jsonl` outputs are intentionally NOT produced. The
  detection / blocking-FP signal they would have measured is now accumulated at $0 marginal LLM
  cost by d8a5's standing `criterion_effectiveness.py` recorder (change #798, MERGED, on main), and
  history-mining is dead (~4 `plan-v3` baselines vs ~200 needed). Evidence lives outside this
  codebase: operator decision 2026-07-18 + d8a5 / change #798. This AC is closed by operator
  attestation, not machine check.
- [ ] **Design documented as WIP.** The README section records the seeded-defect design, the
  counting/run-validity rules, the store-isolation mechanism, and the batch deferral +
  d8a5-supersession, so the WIP status and the drop rationale are auditable.
baseline.summary: E2: seeded-defect benchmark from real closed plans (5 defect classes + controls)

## Why
Audit OSS finding #6 bucket (versioning honesty): Python 3.13 has been the current stable for over a year, but the project tests/advertises only 3.11 and 3.12 — test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml matrices stop at 3.12, and pyproject classifiers list 3.11/3.12 only. For a published PyPI package that leaves 3.13 (the default interpreter in many new environments) untested/unadvertised.

## Current matrix (exact, both workflows)
`os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`, `python-version: ["3.11", "3.12"]`, with `exclude: (macos-latest, "3.11")`. Net effect today: **Linux runs 3.11 + 3.12; macOS runs 3.12 only** (the newest — the exclude drops the lower rev). macOS's value is platform-compat coverage (flock/mkdir lock, gtimeout), not the Python rev, so it stays single-interpreter for runner cost.

## What / files
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` and `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`:
  - add `"3.13"` to `python-version` → `["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]`
  - to KEEP macOS single-interpreter on the newest rev (preserving the existing pattern where the exclude drops all but the highest on macOS), CHANGE the exclude block to drop BOTH lower revs on macOS: `(macos-latest, "3.11")` AND `(macos-latest, "3.12")`. Net after change: Linux runs 3.11/3.12/3.13; macOS runs 3.13 only. (Simply adding "3.13" without a matching exclude would wrongly give macOS two jobs — 3.12 and 3.13.)
  - update the matrix comment to say macOS runs 3.13.
- `pyproject.toml`: add `"Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13"` classifier (after L35) once the matrix is green. `requires-python = ">=3.11"` already admits 3.13; unchanged.
- README supported-version wording: README states "Python ≥ 3.11" (floor) — already satisfied by 3.13, so no correction required (optional "(3.11–3.13 tested in CI)" clarifier). docs/api-stability.md is NOT edited — it has no Python-version wording.

## Local-interpreter note
The local dev interpreter here is Python 3.14, not 3.13, so the authoritative 3.13 green signal is the CI matrix job (Gerrit Verified). Local `make lint && make typecheck && make test` on 3.14 is additional evidence; if a real 3.13-specific blocker surfaces in CI, the fallback remedy is to document 3.13 as excluded and withhold the classifier.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml `python-version` include "3.13"; the macOS `exclude` drops 3.11 AND 3.12 (macOS stays single-interpreter on 3.13); the 3.13 Linux jobs run green in CI
- [ ] pyproject classifiers include `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13`; build/`twine check` passes
- [ ] README supported-version statements remain consistent with the matrix (floor "≥ 3.11" retained)
- [ ] `make lint` green locally; CI 3.13 job green (authoritative) — or a real 3.13 blocker documented and the classifier withheld
baseline.summary: Add Python 3.13 to the CI matrix, classifiers, and supported-version docs

baseline.description:
## Context (measured 2026-08-11, analysis ticket b902-18af-14ed-4da1)

Zero of 2,093 recorded plan reviews carry a non-empty `overlap` block — the overlap feature (ADR 0086; ~13% of local usage-log LLM spend, ~$165/5 days plus its historical failure storms) has never surfaced a finding to a reviewer. An instrumented probe of `wire.overlap_findings` on 3 live tickets plus a controlled near-duplicate probe isolated a stacked root cause:

1. **Batch-path verdicts systematically carry `confidence=0.0`.** Live `judge_batch` calls SUCCEED (no exception) and return entries with a real `relation` but `confidence=0.0` — including an unmistakable near-duplicate pair (same artifact, same feature, paraphrased titles), and every non-abstained real-pipeline verdict observed. `aggregate` requires BOTH orderings ≥ `overlap_conf_threshold` (0.7), so every pair dies. This has plausibly been fatal since batching landed (c403): the single-pair prompt/contract was calibrated for a confidence field the batched prompt path does not elicit.
2. **Since 7fa8102477 (08-08), `output_token_limit=1024` truncates any real multi-candidate batch** (K up to 20 candidates → 10-pair batches; ~100+ tokens per verdict entry): the truncated response abstains the WHOLE batch. Probe: ordering-1 batches abstained for 31/31 candidates across 3 tickets. The fix for the 48k retry storms silently zeroed the surviving output path.

Unit tests pass because they use canned runners; no live calibration case pins "a near-duplicate pair actually surfaces".

## Plan

1. Fix the batch contract so the model emits a meaningful `confidence` per entry (prompt-side: the overlap-judge prompt's confidence instructions must survive the batched rendering; verify with a live near-duplicate probe emitting confidence >= 0.7).
2. Right-size the batch output budget: replace the flat `output_token_limit=1024` with a per-batch bound derived from the code's own batch cardinality constant (`_CANDIDATES_PER_CALL`) and a measured per-entry token allowance (measure a real verdict entry's token size in the calibration probe and add headroom), keeping `structured_retry_limit=0` and `transport_attempt_limit=1` so the 48k-storm class stays dead.
3. Add a live calibration case (T5c discipline) asserting the near-duplicate pair surfaces and an unrelated pair does not, so this failure class cannot regress silently.
4. Re-measure after landing: surfaced-findings rate over the next N reviews; if still ~0 with the mechanism healthy, THEN have the scrap-vs-keep conversation with working-feature data.

Operator note: until this lands, the drain burns spend with provably zero output — pausing via the documented `overlap_drain = "off"` kill switch is reversible and recommended, but is the operator's call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A live near-duplicate probe (two digests naming the same artifact and paraphrased scope) run through `judge_batch` in both orderings yields a non-abstain verdict with `confidence >= 0.7` in each ordering, and `aggregate` surfaces it. Verify: the new calibration script/test output committed with the change.
- [x] `judge_batch`'s output budget scales with the batch's pair count (no flat 1024), with `structured_retry_limit=0` and `transport_attempt_limit=1` retained. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py -x` passes including a new bound-scaling assertion.
- [x] An unrelated-pair probe still yields no surfaced finding (false-flag guard intact). Verify: same calibration evidence.
baseline.summary: Overlap detection has never surfaced a finding: batch-path verdicts carry confidence=0.0 and post-08-08 output cap truncates whole batches

baseline.description:
# A gate whose spend is never recorded cannot be tuned: per-run request/tool-call counts are not persisted

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]. The operator asked a simple, decisive question about the completion gate: **how many model requests did the epics that PASSED this gate actually consume?** That question is the control group for "is e369 abnormal, or is the budget just too small?" — and it **cannot be answered from anything this system records.**

## What is actually recorded (checked in both directions, not assumed)

* `usage_log.record()` (`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:259-318`) appends one JSONL row per LLM call —
  but **only to `$REBAR_USAGE_LOG`, and it is a no-op when that env var is unset**, which is the
  default: *"No-op when the env var is unset (the default) or `usage` is empty."* It is unset in this
  environment and is documented with no default (`docs/env-vars.md:152`). So by default **no per-run
  spend record is written at all.**
* Even with the opt-in enabled, the recorded fields are
  `_FIELDS = ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "requests")`
  (`usage_log.py:32`). **`tool_calls` is not among them** — and `tool_calls` is precisely the axis
  that (a) discriminates a loop from genuine breadth and (b) is the SECOND, independent kill path
  (`tool_calls_limit`, `structured_run.py:399-412`) that `requests` cannot see.
* The signed attestation records the verdict, not the cost: the completion sidecar
  (`rebar audit show <id> --output json` -> `completion.sidecar`) carries criteria and citations and
  **no request or tool-call counts**; `completion.attestation.step_count` is WORKFLOW steps (7), not
  model requests.
* Nothing is on disk to fall back to: `.rebar/logs/` contains only `enrich-drain.log` (0 bytes).

## The asymmetry that makes it worse

`usage_log.failure_usage` (`usage_log.py:136-190`) DOES compute `tool_calls` plus the full repetition summary — but only on the **failure** path, and [rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e] shows that value is then discarded one frame from the surface. So:

* a run that **fails** computes rich spend/repetition data and throws it away;
* a run that **succeeds** never computes it at all.

The net effect is that the gate's cost profile is invisible in both directions. This is the same "computed then discarded" shape as the dropped diagnostic, one level up: not a missing metric, but a **missing durable record of what the gate actually spent**.

## Why it blocks real decisions

Concretely, during [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] these questions were all unanswerable retrospectively and had to be replaced with ~70 minutes of fresh instrumented live re-runs:

* how many requests did `2f4c` / `a492` / `86ac` / `716f` / `e68d` consume when they PASSED?
* is e369's consumption abnormal, or in line with them?
* has per-run spend trended up as the runtime changed (LangChain -> pydantic-ai, budget raises)?

The only available proxy was realized-evidence volume reconstructed from the sidecars (criteria count and distinct cited files: 3-9 criteria, 2-9 files), which measures the OUTPUT, not the spend.

## Scope

Observability only. This ticket does not propose changing any budget, gate or verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] a durable per-run record of LLM spend for gate runs exists WITHOUT requiring an operator to
      have set an env var beforehand — a gate's own spend must be recoverable after the fact
- [x] the record includes `tool_calls` alongside `requests`, since the two ceilings are independent
      and only `tool_calls` can distinguish a loop from breadth
- [x] the record is written for BOTH outcomes — a successful verification and a failed one — so a
      control group of passing runs exists to compare a failing run against
- [x] the record is attributable to the ticket and the gate that ran, so "what did the completion
      gate spend on ticket X" is answerable
- [x] the privacy contract of `usage_log` is unchanged: counters and hashed signatures only, never
      prompt/response/tool-argument content
- [x] a test pins that a gate run leaves a retrievable spend record with `requests` and `tool_calls`
      populated
baseline.summary: Gate spend is never durably recorded: per-run request/tool-call counts unavailable after the fact

baseline.description:
## Context

The `COMMITS` event and `attach_commits` reducer already exist (`rebar.attach_commits`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697`, re-exported from `src/rebar/__init__.py`), used by the code-review workflow. Missing: an author-facing repair surface for a botched `rebar-ticket:` trailer, plus a consumer. Approved design (b902-18af-14ed-4da1): expose retroactive commit linking on CLI + library + MCP, document it, then add a deterministic close-gate check that linked commits' diffs match the recorded `file_impact`. OUT of scope: linked commits as a completion-verifier diff basis (they may be incomplete; CV already prefetches from `file_impact`).

## Plan

1. **Shared DET module** `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py` (new, ~120 LOC): (a) `invalid_commit_shas(shas, repo_root)` via `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`; (b) the step-4 path matchers, including `glob_match` — the `**/`-aware semantics (`fnmatch(p,g) or (g.startswith("**/") and fnmatch(p,g[3:]))`) from `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:746`. Its ONLY true mirror is `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:242`; `src/rebar/grounding/oracle.py:316` uses PLAIN `fnmatch`, is NOT a copy, and is left untouched. The DET close path must not import `rebar.llm` (optional `[agents]` extra), so the helper is hoisted here and BOTH real copies (`prompts._glob_match`, `registry._glob_match`) become thin delegating wrappers — one implementation, no third copy.

2. **CLI verb** `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` wrapping the existing seam. Registration follows the established seam: add to `_WRITES_FULL` in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`; add a variadic handler (N SHAs) to `_ARGV_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`; ship pinned help `src/rebar/_cli/help/attach-commits.txt` + the `overview.txt` line (golden-pinned; `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` requires it). Thin body in `src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py`.

3. **Validation in the SEAM, not the CLI**, so all three surfaces inherit it identically: `rebar.attach_commits` calls `commit_impact.invalid_commit_shas` before appending. **ALL-OR-NOTHING** — the batch is validated first; if any SHA fails, NO `COMMITS` event is recorded and the call raises naming every offender. Union-add unchanged. Library: `rebar.attach_commits` is already re-exported — confirm and document. MCP: register `attach_commits` in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` with an `AttachCommitsResultOut` outputSchema in `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`, per the existing write-tool pattern (`mcp_server.py` only assembles registrars).

4. **DET close check** in the existing completion precheck `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — the module that today raises "cannot confirm the work landed" (there is no `src/rebar/workflow/close_gate.py`). Discovery unions the two existing sources: (i) `state.commits` from COMMITS events; (ii) the precheck's referencing-commit scan (`_referencing_commit_exists`, `close_precheck.py:94` — commits reachable from HEAD carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading `<id>:` subject for the ticket or any transitive descendant). It returns only a bool, so it is refactored into a SHA-returning `_referencing_commits(...)` with `_referencing_commit_exists` kept as a thin wrapper — the documented monkeypatch target and its call sites keep working unchanged. For each commit, `git show --name-only` gives changed paths; a path neither covered by `file_impact` nor matched by this check's OWN exemption globs (`tests/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — owned here, not inherited) is a deterministic BLOCK naming the commit and paths. Matching (via step 1, not re-derived): normalized repo-relative POSIX paths; a `file_impact` entry matches on exact equality, or as a directory prefix when it ends with `/` or names an existing directory; exemptions use `**/`-aware `glob_match`. No substring matching. No LLM.

   **Git errors, asymmetric by source:** a source-(ii) commit is local by construction, so a `git show` failure on it FAILS CLOSED (block, naming the SHA). A source-(i) SHA may legitimately be absent locally (attached from another clone, or unfetched), so it is SKIPPED — blocking a foreign SHA would be a false positive on a repair surface built to record commits.

   **Scope symmetry.** Source-(ii) discovery credits commits for the ticket OR any transitive descendant (`accepted_ids`, `close_precheck.py:361-367`), but `field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker)` (`field_reads.py:36`) reads only THIS ticket's — reusing it as-is would false-BLOCK a parent declaring `file_impact` when children's commits touch child-owned paths. So the check compares against the UNION of `file_impact` over the SAME id set discovery uses, making both scopes match by construction.

   A ticket with no discovered commits keeps today's behavior (the existing error). The check is skipped when that union is empty (no ticket in the set declares `file_impact`).

5. **Remedy for a legitimate block:** the message names the offending paths and says to declare them via `rebar set-file-impact <ticket> …`, after which close proceeds; `--force="<reason>"` stays the break-glass.

6. **Docs.** `docs/cli-reference.md` is GENERATED (`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`, CI drift gate, subcommand count in header) so it is regenerated, not hand-edited. Hand-edited: `docs/mcp-reference.md` and `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md`. Each names the verb, its use, and the step-5 remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>` records a COMMITS event that `rebar show` reflects. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_attach_commits.py -x`.
- [ ] An invalid SHA is rejected with an error naming it. Verify: same file, test asserting the offending SHA appears in the error text.
- [ ] A batch containing any invalid SHA records nothing (all-or-nothing). Verify: test asserting `state.commits` is byte-identical before/after a mixed valid/invalid batch.
- [ ] The MCP server exposes `attach_commits` with an outputSchema, routed through the same seam. Verify: the MCP tool-inventory test asserts `"attach_commits"` is in the registered tool names.
- [ ] A commit touching a path outside the declared `file_impact` blocks close, naming the offending path. Verify: unit test asserting the exact path string in the raised message.
- [ ] A commit whose paths are all declared does not block close. Verify: unit test asserting close proceeds.
- [ ] An exempt path does not block, including at the repo root (`README.md` under `**/*.md`). Verify: unit test over each exemption glob.
- [ ] The DET check imports no `rebar.llm` module. Verify: test asserting `[m for m in sys.modules if m.startswith("rebar.llm")] == []` after running it in a fresh interpreter.
- [ ] The `**/`-aware glob semantics have one implementation. Verify: test asserting `prompts._glob_match` and `registry._glob_match` both delegate to `commit_impact.glob_match`.
- [ ] An unreadable source-(ii) commit fails closed naming the SHA; an unresolvable source-(i) SHA is skipped without blocking. Verify: one unit test per direction.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` names the `attach_commits` tool. Verify: `grep -qE '\battach_commits\b' docs/mcp-reference.md` exits 0.
- [ ] The commit-trailer guide names the verb. Verify: `grep -qF 'rebar attach-commits' src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` exits 0.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Outbound sync can only write to one tracker project, and it fails closed on anything else. Both create transports take their project from a single construction-time value — Cloud `AcliClient.create_issue` uses `self.jira_project` (`adapters/jira/acli.py:274-330`); DC `_IssuesMixin.create_issue` uses `self.project` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:163-189`). And the applier scans every outbound mutation pre-flight and raises `CrossProjectTargetError` — aborting the whole pass — if any update or delete targets a key outside the one configured project (`applier.py:230-255`, `_cross_project_targets`, bug `626d`); its sole caller (`applier.py:593-610`) passes a single string `select_backend(load_config()).project`. With a mapping listing several projects, correct mutations to the other projects would be treated as the misconfiguration that guard exists to catch.

## Approach

Three changes: resolve the create target per ticket (covering BOTH transports), relax the guard to set membership, and change the guard's caller to supply the set.

**Create targets the ticket's resolved project — resolved once, above both transports.** The resolution happens where the create mutation is BUILT, in `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` (`outbound_differ.py:502`), which already receives the full local `ticket` (so it can read `bridge_project`). It calls `resolve_project(ticket, mapping)` (`projects_store.py:97-110`) against the store mapping, loaded once via `projects_store.load_mapping(repo_root)` (the `Mapping` that `resolve_project` and the `mapping.projects` membership check both require) and threaded into `compute_outbound_mutations` as a new optional field on `OutboundDiffConfig`, populated by that function's sole caller `run_differs.py:466` (which already holds `repo_root`). Three outcomes:
  * resolves to "not synced" (absent→no legacy_default, or explicit `""`) → NO create mutation;
  * resolves to a key **NOT in `mapping.projects`** → NO create mutation (a stale/typo binding must
    not create against an unsynced project — this closes the create-side gap the guard cannot, since
    creates are guard-exempt: their key is a local-id placeholder, so `_JIRA_KEY_RE` never matches);
  * resolves to a valid in-set key → stamped into the mutation's `fields` under the reserved key
    `_bridge_target_project`.

Because the create mutation's `fields` reach whichever `TicketTransport` is active (`dispatch_one.create_one` copies `mutation["fields"]` into the `ticket_data` it hands `client.create_issue`), resolving here covers Cloud AND Data Center from one site. Each transport reads `ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project")` and falls back to its construction-time value when the key is absent (legacy single-project behaviour preserved): Cloud `project = ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project") or self.jira_project`; DC `fields.setdefault("project", {"key": ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project") or self.project})`. The transports handle the reserved key explicitly, because they treat unknown payload keys DIFFERENTLY. Cloud's `create_issue` EXTRACTS only the fields it names and ignores the rest, so the key never reaches ACLI. DC's `create_issue` splats the whole TRANSLATED dict into `self._client.create_issue(**fields)` — so the key must be DROPPED before the splat or it is sent as a bogus Jira field id (the `HTTP 400 … Field … cannot be set` class of bug 18a5). It is added to `_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS` (`_issues.py:29`) alongside the bridge-only names `title`/`ticket_type`, so `_translate_create_fields` reads it for the project then drops it — that drop is what keeps the reserved key off the tracker by construction, exactly as the bridge-only names already are.

**The guard relaxes from equality to set membership.** `_cross_project_targets` currently compares each target key's prefix against one `configured_project` string; it instead checks membership in the mapping's project set. This is the smallest possible weakening: the guard stays fail-closed and still aborts pre-flight before any tracker write, so a stale binding pointing at a project the store does not sync is caught exactly as today. Only keys the store legitimately owns now pass.

**The guard's caller supplies the set.** The sole caller (`applier.py:593-610`) currently computes a single `_project = select_backend(load_config()).project`. It instead loads the store's project set via `projects_store.read_projects(repo_root)`, whose keys ARE the project set, and passes that set. An empty/absent mapping falls back to the single configured project so single-project stores are unchanged.

**Module size.** All touched files stay under the 800-line gate with headroom; each edit is small and local.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — resolve + validate + stamp the target
  project on the create mutation; new optional `OutboundDiffConfig` mapping field
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py` — populate the new config field from the loaded
  mapping (the sole caller of `compute_outbound_mutations`)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py` — Cloud create reads the payload target
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py` — DC create reads the
  payload target AND drops the reserved key in `_translate_create_fields`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` — guard set-membership + caller supplies the set
- Read-only dependency: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` — `load_mapping`/`Mapping`,
  `resolve_project`, `read_projects` (the authoritative project set)
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful fake transport fed production-shaped mutations, recording the create calls it receives, because the destination project carried on the call is the contract under test. Both transports are covered.

- Happy path (both transports): a ticket resolving to project `B` in a store whose mapping lists `A`
  and `B` produces a create call carrying `B`, not the repo default `A` — asserted against the Cloud
  fake AND the Data Center fake.
- DC leak guard: the DC fake's recorded create fields do NOT contain `_bridge_target_project`,
  proving the reserved key is dropped and never sent as a Jira field.
- Validation edge: a ticket whose `bridge_project` names `Z` (NOT in the `A`/`B` mapping) emits no
  create mutation — proving a stale/typo binding cannot create against an unsynced project.
- Contrast case (the guard, both directions in one paired test): an update targeting `B-1` where the
  mapping lists `A` and `B` proceeds; an update targeting `C-1` still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An outbound create targets the ticket's resolved project rather than the client default on the
      Cloud transport; checked by a Cloud fake asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [x] An outbound create targets the ticket's resolved project on the Data Center transport; checked
      by a DC fake asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [x] The reserved `_bridge_target_project` key is dropped from the DC create field set; checked by
      asserting it is absent from the DC fake's recorded create fields.
- [x] A ticket whose resolved project is absent from the mapping set emits no create mutation;
      checked by asserting an empty mutation list for it.
- [x] An update inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [x] When the guard raises, no tracker write has occurred; checked by asserting the fake recorded
      zero writes.
- [x] Single-project behaviour is unchanged; checked by a regression test running the guard against a
      one-project mapping in both directions.
baseline.summary: Multi-project outbound dispatch and cross-project guard relaxation to set membership

## Problem / opportunity

The source audit measured a 72.3% first-pass completion-verification rate, but non-PASS outcomes conflate implementation defects, unmet acceptance criteria, missing proof, plan/scope gaps, environment failures, and verifier defects. Treating the aggregate as a code-quality or bug-escape measure would be invalid.

## Prior decisions that constrain this idea

olivine-married-kodiakbear made FAIL verdicts durable; chief-sizeable-skua requires exhaustive unmet-criterion findings; cinnamoned-tzarist-kangaroo added a distinct ERROR outcome; crumply-denim-pitbull persists PASS criteria; earthen-flayed-baboon distinguishes insufficient evidence; beryl-orange-oropendola tallies survived step failures; paralyzed-sane-flyingfox derives gate economics; depressant-amethyst-wasp exposes the audit trail. The historical evaluation's independent reviewer counted 351 failure sidecars with 682 structured findings carrying criterion, dimension, severity, detail, citations, and remediation.

The project already has the evidence channel. This idea must test derivation before proposing another telemetry or schema surface.

## Outcome hypothesis

Historical first-non-PASS completion records can be classified into a small, stable cause taxonomy that separates implementation quality from evidence, planning, environment, and verifier failures. The taxonomy can guide targeted prevention and make completion first-pass metrics interpretable.

## Candidate taxonomy

- Code or implementation defect.
- Acceptance criterion genuinely unmet.
- Missing test, citation, or other evidence.
- Plan or scope gap.
- Environment or integration failure.
- Verifier or tool failure.

These are hypotheses, not yet a committed schema.

## Guardrails

- Use existing FAIL, PASS, ERROR, insufficient_evidence, and survived-step records as the primary source.
- Classify the first non-PASS attempt separately from later remediation outcomes.
- Preserve source citations and uncertainty; do not force ambiguous findings into a confident category.
- Do not add required author input or a parallel telemetry channel.
- Add durable reason codes only if offline derivation is unreliable and the categories prove operationally useful.
- Keep code defects distinct from missing proof and verifier/tool failures.

## Questions before promotion

- What sampling design covers common and rare sidecar shapes without overrepresenting high-attempt tickets?
- What labeling rubric yields acceptable independent agreement?
- Can deterministic rules classify high-confidence cases before an LLM or human-coded adjudicator handles the remainder?
- Which records legitimately need multiple causes, and what should be primary versus contributing?
- What agreement/stability threshold justifies durable reason codes?
- Which downstream metrics or planning checks would consume each category?
- How will schema/version changes remain additive if derivation proves insufficient?

## Evidence

Discovered from unpleasing-hairy-yellowlegs; source audit bleakish-stational-cob. Prior work: olivine-married-kodiakbear, chief-sizeable-skua, cinnamoned-tzarist-kangaroo, crumply-denim-pitbull, earthen-flayed-baboon, beryl-orange-oropendola, paralyzed-sane-flyingfox, depressant-amethyst-wasp.
baseline.summary: Derive a completion non-PASS cause taxonomy from existing sidecars

# Explore VCS-derived versioning (hatch-vcs / setuptools-scm) as the single source of version truth

Parked design idea (Option E from the api-stability version-marker analysis). Investigate
adopting **VCS-tag-derived versioning** so the version is computed from the git tag at build
time and is NOT hard-coded anywhere — not in `pyproject.toml`, not in `server.json`, not in
docs. `git tag vX.Y.Z` would become the entire version-bump action, eliminating the
multi-file lockstep bump the release currently performs by hand.

## Context

rebar currently hard-codes the version in `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` and mirrors
it into `server.json` (top-level + `packages[].version`), kept in lockstep manually and
asserted by the release workflow's `authorize` version-lockstep guard. rebar builds with
**Hatchling** and already bakes `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` provenance via `hatch_build.py`. The
mainstream zero-touch pattern is `hatch-vcs` (a thin wrapper over `setuptools-scm`) which
derives `project.version` from the latest git tag.

## Why this is an idea, not ready-to-implement

Several open design questions must be resolved before committing:
- **server.json is not covered.** `hatch-vcs` sets the Python package version, but the MCP
  `server.json` version (top-level + packages) still needs to be produced/synced from the
  same source — how? (generate it at build time, a small sync step, or a check).
- **Interaction with the new release-authorization workflow.** The `authorize` job asserts
  `version_input == pyproject == server.json`. With a VCS-derived version there is no static
  `pyproject.version` to compare — the lockstep guard's contract changes. And the release is
  dispatched-from-`main` with a `version` input BEFORE any tag exists (the tag is created
  post-publish), which is the opposite ordering from tag-derived versioning. Reconcile these.
- **CI must fetch tags** (`fetch-depth: 0` / `fetch-tags: true`) everywhere the version is
  needed, or the version resolves to a dev/`0.0.0` string (a known setuptools-scm failure
  mode). rebar's build-once/test jobs run without full history in places.
- **Interaction with `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` baking** and the build-once artifact-identity flow
  (story 6168) must be checked so provenance stamping still works.
- **Blast radius vs. payoff.** This is a large change to fix what is otherwise a small
  lockstep bump; weigh against simply keeping the current manual bump (now that the drift-prone
  docs marker is removed under Option A).

## Acceptance Criteria (for promoting this idea to designed work)

- [ ] A short design note that resolves: how `server.json` versions are produced/synced from
  the VCS-derived version; how the dispatch-from-`main` `version` input + post-publish tag
  ordering reconciles with tag-derived versioning; and the CI `fetch-tags` requirements.
- [ ] A prototype or spike showing `hatch-vcs` deriving `project.version` from a tag without
  breaking the build-once / `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` provenance flow.
- [ ] A go/no-go recommendation with the tradeoff vs. the status quo (manual lockstep bump).

Discovered from the api-stability version-marker design discussion; sibling of the
version-agnostic-marker change (Option A).
baseline.summary: Explore VCS-derived versioning (hatch-vcs/setuptools-scm) as the single source of version truth

## What

Write `docs/adr/0101-*.md` amending ADR 0043. ADR 0043 itself is NOT edited — it is a historical record, and ADR 0061 already set the precedent of amending it rather than rewriting.

## Must record

- Why `operator` mis-signalled: it means a human throughout this repo, so agents inferred a
  person was required, when an agent recording a Gerrit vote attests equally well.
- Why `[non-codebase]`: it is the missing half of a pair the vocabulary already had. The
  `[codebase]` token is already recognized at exactly three sites — `docs/adr/0043-...md:45`
  ("anything else — untagged, an explicit `[codebase]`, or a malformed near-miss"),
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md:95`, and
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_evidence_kind.md:56`. (It is NOT in
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, which uses the category name
  `codebase-verifiable` rather than the bracket tag — the two are different vocabularies and the
  ADR must not conflate them.) `[codebase]` is prompt-level only: no regex parses it.
  `[non-codebase]` also resists attestation laundering by construction — to tag a criterion whose
  proof is `tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py`, an author must assert that file is "non-codebase",
  which is self-evidently false.
- Why `attested` alone was rejected: `SOURCE_ATTESTED = "attested"` is the snapshot gate
  read-root mode meaning "pinned to an immutable in-repo SHA" — near-opposite sense, same
  readers, though no functional conflict.
- That `[operator-attested]` remains accepted and is deliberately UNDOCUMENTED, because 827 of
  4,285 live tickets carry it in immutable event records.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] ADR 0101 exists, is Accepted, and records the four points above.
- [x] ADR 0043 is unmodified.
- [x] `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py` run; `docs/adr/README.md` and `docs/adr/.numbers/` updated.
- [x] `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` and `scripts/check_docs_index.py` pass.

## Prevention remediation for incident 1c0d (CI/test lane)

Post-mortem: `9097-2741-6462-424c`. This is the **detection guard that would have caught the incident before prod**: a contract/regression test asserting that *any* provider transient failure degrades to a **retryable** disposition, never a hard INDETERMINATE.

### Problem it guards
A throttled primary (429/`WAIT_AND_RETRY`) that fails over to an uncredentialed fallback surfaced as `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` → INDETERMINATE. The 1c0d fix (change 2404) added a held-out oracle for the specific keyless-`TypeError` case, but there is no *broad* contract test pinning the class invariant.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test drives a real `build_fallback_model` chain (mocked providers, **zero live Bedrock**) where the primary raises each retryable transient (throttle 429, timeout, 5xx) and the terminal fallback arm raises a non-retryable error (credential `TypeError`, config error). Asserts the classified disposition is retryable (exit-11), never INDETERMINATE.
- [ ] A vocabulary/closure assertion: a `FallbackExceptionGroup` is classified by its most-recoverable leg (retryable wins); an all-non-retryable group maps to `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL`, never `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION`.
- [ ] The test would have failed against the pre-2404 tree (confirm by reverting the two fix seams behind the sandbox).
- [ ] Runs in the normal `make test` matrix (portable — no CI-provider-specific trigger, no network).

### Notes
This is test-only, adds no behavior — ready to implement. Complements epic 3405-c0b7's exhaustive `exception→code` contract test (same discipline, different taxonomy: this pins the `ResolutionClass` disposition, 3405 pins the workflow error-code vocabulary).
baseline.summary: Prevention (CI/test): regression oracle — provider transient must degrade to retryable, never INDETERMINATE

## Surface
GitHub Actions, repo navapbc/rebar, workflow **Terraform Drift** (scheduled), job `plan`.

## Signature
`terraform init` succeeds configuring the s3 backend, then fails:
```
Error: Unsupported Terraform Core version
  required_version = ">= 1.11"
This configuration does not support Terraform version 1.10.5.
```
The runner/setup provisions Terraform **1.10.5**, but the config requires **>= 1.11**. The workflow cannot reach the drift `plan` at all — drift detection is blind while broken.

## First/last seen in-window
Run 33297247070 @ 2026-08-30T06:35Z (scheduled). Fails every scheduled run (deterministic version mismatch, not transient).

## Dedup
No existing ticket found (searched "terraform drift / unsupported core version / setup-terraform"). Distinct from the last sweep's noted "9350 drift" item (that is a drift-content blocker, not a Core-version init failure). New signature.

## Severity: P3
Monitoring-only workflow; no user/merge/production impact. But it is a hard, deterministic failure — infra drift goes undetected until the Terraform version pin (setup-terraform) is bumped to satisfy `>= 1.11` (or the constraint relaxed).

## Provenance
Periodic ops-error sweep (window 2026-08-29T10:00 → 2026-08-30T17:36 PDT). Triage only — not fixed.
baseline.summary: [terraform-drift] Terraform Drift workflow red: runner Terraform 1.10.5 does not satisfy required_version ">= 1.11" (init fails before plan)

# Deprecate REBAR_LLM_MODEL, add ADR and example configs

## Context / Problem
Once classes are the interface, `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a second, ambiguous way to say the same thing — a single scalar that cannot express a per-tier mapping. Keeping both indefinitely reintroduces the ambiguity this epic removes. It is also load-bearing today: the production cutover's kill switch [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] is documented as "point `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back at `anthropic:...`".

## Approach
Deprecate with a MIGRATION WINDOW, registered via `_scheduled(...)` with the default `remove_in=_MAJOR` (v1.0.0). THIS IS THE PARENT'S DECISION, not a default I chose: eb58 states in bold that "`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is DEPRECATED with a migration window rather than kept as a permanent alias", with the rationale that there are few clients today and it is a single-scalar knob. An earlier draft switched to `_permanent(...)` because all six existing env deprecations use it — a real observation, but the WRONG authority AND a miscategorisation. The registry itself says those six are kept forever because they are RENAMES of established names (`_deprecations.py:71-73`); `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a SUPERSESSION by a different interface, which is what `_scheduled` is for. The parent CONSIDERED the permanent alias and rejected it deliberately, so the six precedents are the repo's general habit and this is a considered exception. Approach and Scope now agree on the window. Within the window `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is still honoured, emits a deprecation warning through `warn_deprecated` (per call — see AC2, the once-per-process form was withdrawn as unmechanised), and maps to ALL THREE classes — the widest-compatibility reading, so an operator who set one model keeps getting exactly that model everywhere and nothing breaks mid-window.

Deprecation (rather than keeping it as a permanent shorthand) is a deliberate operator-approved call: there are few clients today, and it yields a single unambiguous config model.

Because the kill switch's current wording goes stale the moment this lands, rewriting it in class terms is part of THIS ticket's contract — a kill switch that is wrong during an incident is worse than none.

Ships example configs per provider in docs, so the easy path is documentation rather than presets shipped in code that clients select by name.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — **HOSTS A `warn_deprecated` CALL AT ITS OWN ENV READ (`:469`), plus the
  docstring corrections at `:10` and `:195`.** Two earlier drafts both got this wrong and the reasoning
  matters, so it is recorded: draft 1 put the call here and ONLY here, which misses the fan-out path;
  draft 2 over-corrected to model_classes.py ONLY, claiming "one call site at the read covers every
  reachable path". THAT CLAIM IS FALSE. VERIFIED: `config.py:469` performs its own read —
  `_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_MODEL", "model", DEFAULT_MODEL)` inside `from_env()` — so a
  model_classes-only warning is silent on every path that builds a config without touching the
  fan-out.
  AND THE WARNING CANNOT LIVE IN `resolve_model_string` AT ALL, which is the deeper reason: `:205-207`
  calls `resolve_model_string(step or workflow or cfg.model)`, passing an ALREADY-RESOLVED STRING. By
  that point the value is indistinguishable from a config-table `model` key or a per-step `model:` —
  so warning there would fire FALSELY for operators who never set the env var at all. Provenance
  exists ONLY at the env read. Therefore: **the warning goes at EVERY env read of `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`
  and nowhere else** — `config.py:469` today, plus the new read in `model_classes.py` that the fan-out
  needs. Two call sites is CORRECT and costs nothing, because emission is per-call by design (AC2) and
  needs no dedup.
  `config.py` must still NOT host the class fan-out:
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — **the map-to-all-three fan-out belongs HERE, and it READS
  `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` ITSELF** (a literal `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_MODEL")`, exactly as `:118-126`
  already reads the nine per-class vars — which is also what keeps it visible to
  `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, whose AST scan only records STRING-LITERAL env names). Reading it
  here is what gives this site the provenance needed to warn correctly, and it carries the second
  `warn_deprecated` call, beside the slot
  resolution it has to compose with: `load_class_slots` (`:207`), `parse_class_slots` (`:166`) and
  `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS` (`:47`). A bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` becomes the default for all three slots
  at the point slots are built, which is also where the documented per-field precedence
  (CLI > env > config table > built-in default) is already applied — putting it in `config.py`
  behind a lazy import would duplicate that precedence logic on the far side of the seam.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — **REQUIRED, and previously missing from this Scope.** The
  deprecation must be REGISTERED here via `_scheduled(...)` in `REGISTRY` (`:62`, `:100`) and emitted
  through `warn_deprecated` (`:299`), per the parent's migration-window decision. **AND THE BLOCK COMMENT AT `:75-79` MUST BE CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE** — previously
  unscoped, and adding the entry makes it FALSE. It currently reads: "This registry now holds ONLY
  these permanent renames: every remaining SCHEDULED (removable) surface has been removed in the
  pre-1.0 breaking passes." This ticket adds the FIRST scheduled entry since that drain, so the
  comment must say so instead of asserting the registry is permanent-only.
  **WHY `_scheduled` IS RIGHT HERE AND THE SIX `_permanent` PRECEDENTS DO NOT APPLY — this closes the
  question, which has been flipped twice.** The registry documents its own reason for those six at
  `:71-73`: they are "stable REBAR_-prefixed renames of established names" that "warned 'deprecated'
  historically, which was a contradiction — they are kept forever." That is a RENAME: the same knob
  under a better name, so it must never be removed. `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is NOT a rename — it is a knob
  SUPERSEDED by a different interface (per-class slots), which is precisely what `_scheduled` exists
  for and what the two pre-1.0 breaking passes recorded at `:87-99` actually used and then drained.
  So the six precedents are precedent for RENAMES, not for supersessions, and an earlier draft of this
  plan that switched to `_permanent` on the strength of their COUNT was wrong twice over: it
  contradicted the parent's explicit decision AND miscategorised the change. State this reasoning in
  the corrected comment so the next reader does not re-litigate it. This is ENFORCED, not stylistic:
  `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py:125::test_no_raw_deprecation_emissions` source-scans all
  of `src/rebar/` and fails any deprecation signal that does not route through `warn_deprecated`.
  A hand-rolled `warnings.warn` in `config.py` would fail that test AND be invisible to
  `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, which imports `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` and unions it into the
  generated env docs.
- **USER-FACING STRINGS presenting `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the CURRENT interface — previously missing from
  this Scope, and NOT mere comments.** I earlier cleared these as "comments/docstrings, inert"; that
  was WRONG for the first two, which render to operators:
  * `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:160` — the `argparse` `description=` for `rebar review`, i.e.
    `--help` TEXT: "Needs the 'agents' extra + a model API key (provider per REBAR_LLM_MODEL)".
  * `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:64` — an MCP TOOL DESCRIPTION surfaced to MCP clients.
  * `src/rebar/llm/config.py:10` — the module docstring's env table, presenting it as "model id
    (default ``claude-opus-4-8``)", i.e. THE model knob.
  * `src/rebar/llm/config.py:195` — `resolve_model`'s docstring, describing it as current precedence.
  `llm/completion.py:72` and `llm/gate_context.py:14` are genuinely internal comments and need no edit.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the class model and the deprecation window.
- `docs/` — example configs (Anthropic-only, Bedrock-only, mixed-provider, local+fallback).
- ~~The cutover runbook's kill-switch entry — restated in class terms.~~ **REMOVED FROM SCOPE, and
  this resolves a contradiction in an earlier draft.** The S8 section below states that this ticket
  does NOT redesign S8's recovery path, and `infra/runbooks/` is deliberately absent from
  `file_impact` — yet Scope listed the runbook restatement as a deliverable here. It belongs to S8
  (`eb6e`), which owns `infra/runbooks/`. This ticket's only obligation toward it is the durability
  note already recorded on `eb6e` for the operator to resolve there.

## Testing
Unit tier for the mapping and the warning; docs assertions for the rest.
- `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set and no classes configured: all three classes resolve to that model.
- BOTH env-read paths warn, tested SEPARATELY — this is the round-6 defect and needs a test each:
  (a) `config.from_env()` with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set and the fan-out never invoked -> warns (the
      `config.py:469` read);
  (b) `load_class_slots()` / `resolve_model_string()` reached WITHOUT `config.from_env()` -> warns (the
      `model_classes.py` read). A model_classes-only or config-only implementation passes one and fails
      the other, which is exactly the gap two earlier drafts shipped.
- CLI PRECEDENCE, pinned because two semantics are possible and the suite cannot tell them apart
  otherwise: `_llm_str` resolves CLI > env > file > default and RETURNS EARLY on a CLI hit, so
  `os.environ.get` is never reached when `--model` wins. THE CHOSEN SEMANTIC IS WARN-WHEN-SET —
  check `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_MODEL") is not None` at the `:469` call site. An operator who has
  exported a deprecated variable should be told even when a CLI flag overrides it this run, because the
  export is still a migration item. Warn-when-env-WINS is rejected: it cannot live inside `_llm_str`,
  which serves ~a dozen variables and must not learn about one of them, and implementing it at the call
  site would duplicate the precedence logic this plan already refuses to duplicate for the fan-out.
  TEST: `--model` set AND `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set -> the CLI value wins AND the warning still fires.
- NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the reason the warning cannot live in `resolve_model_string`: a config-table
  `model` key (or a per-step `model:`) with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` UNSET must emit NO warning. A warning
  placed on the resolved string would fire here falsely.
- the deprecation warning is emitted whenever `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is consulted, PER CALL. Not
  once-per-process: that requirement was withdrawn (see AC2) because `warn_deprecated` has no dedup
  and none of the six existing env deprecations has any either.
- classes configured AND `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set: classes win, warning still emitted.
- with neither set, resolution is unchanged from today's defaults.

## Interaction with S8's kill switch (eb6e) — NOT a safety conflict, but it must be handled

S8 (`eb6e`) documents its production recovery path as "a documented one-line kill switch (`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back to `anthropic:…`)", scopes `infra/compose/` and `infra/runbooks/` around it, and has an AC to EXECUTE it end-to-end. S8 is blocked behind `eb58`, which cannot close until THIS ticket does — so the deprecation lands FIRST and S8 would then build a recovery path on a deprecated variable.

**That does not break the kill switch, and this ticket must not be read as breaking it.** VERIFIED: `_scheduled(...)` sets `permanent=False` with `remove_in=_MAJOR` (v1.0.0), so within the window the variable WARNS and keeps working — S8's kill switch is unaffected BY THIS TICKET. But be exact about the limit, because an earlier draft of this plan overclaimed here: under a migration window `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` IS scheduled for removal, so any S8 runbook naming it as the recovery lever WILL rot at v1.0.0. That durability concern is REAL, is recorded on eb6e for the operator to resolve there, and was briefly withdrawn by a draft that had switched to `_permanent` — reverting to the parent's window reinstates it. This ticket does NOT redesign S8's recovery path.

The paragraph above is the CURRENT and FINAL position on durability. An earlier UPDATE block here claimed the concern "dissolves under the permanent-alias decision" — written while this plan briefly used `_permanent`, and now WRONG, because the parent's window means the variable IS scheduled for removal. So the resolution is documentation, not mechanism — no change to S8's safety behaviour:

- this ticket's docs criterion covers recovery documentation too, so nothing it writes presents the
  deprecated variable as the way to recover;
- `eb6e` should express its kill switch in CLASS terms (the class slots, or
  `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL`), which is a strictly equivalent one-line operator action. Recorded as a
  comment on `eb6e` rather than edited into it, since redesigning another ticket's production
  recovery path is the operator's call and not a side effect of a deprecation ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is registered in `_deprecations.REGISTRY` via `_scheduled(...)` (NOT
      `_permanent(...)`), and a test asserts the entry exists with `permanent=False` and a non-None
      `remove_in`. Previously no criterion covered the REGISTRATION itself — only that a warning is
      emitted — so the required form could have been silently wrong.
- [ ] the block comment at `_deprecations.py:75-79` no longer asserts the registry holds ONLY
      permanent renames, and states why this entry is scheduled (a SUPERSESSION, not a rename). A
      test or grep assertion pins this: Scope mandates it in bold, but with no criterion an executor
      could close every AC and ship a comment the code contradicts.

- [ ] the four RENDERED references named in Scope no longer present `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the current
      model-selection interface: `_cli/_llm_commands.py:160` (`rebar review --help`),
      `_mcp_llm.py:64` (MCP tool description), and `llm/config.py:10` and `:195`. These are
      OPERATOR-VISIBLE, not comments — the first two render in `--help` output and in MCP clients — so
      a grep assertion pins them and a reader of `--help` is not sent to a deprecated knob.

- [ ] the four example configs named in Scope exist under `docs/` — Anthropic-only, Bedrock-only,
      mixed-provider, and local+fallback — and each is a COMPLETE `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]`
      table a reader can paste, not a fragment. Added because Scope listed this deliverable with no
      criterion covering it, so it could have shipped as prose about configs rather than configs.
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` alone maps to all three classes
- [ ] TWO SEPARATE tests assert the deprecation warning, one per env-read path — NOT one test. This
      is stated as two because a single test is exactly the round-6 defect: (a) `config.from_env()`
      with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set and the fan-out never invoked warns (the `config.py:469` read), and
      (b) `load_class_slots()`/`resolve_model_string()` reached WITHOUT `config.from_env()` warns (the
      `model_classes.py` read). A config-only or model_classes-only implementation passes one and
      fails the other; an implementer reading a singular criterion would write one test and ship the
      gap. Both route through `warn_deprecated` so the registry is the single source of the message.
- [ ] a test asserts the NEGATIVE CONTROL: a config-table `model` key (or per-step `model:`) with
      `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` UNSET emits NO warning. This is the criterion that FORBIDS placing the warning
      in `resolve_model_string`, where the value's provenance is already lost.
- [ ] a test asserts the CLI-PRECEDENCE semantic: with `--model` AND `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` both set, the
      CLI value wins AND the warning still fires (warn-when-SET, not warn-when-env-wins). Without this
      the two semantics are indistinguishable to the suite and either could ship.
- [ ] a test asserts that with NEITHER classes nor `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set, resolution is unchanged from
      today's defaults and NO warning is emitted.
- [ ] a test asserts explicit class config takes precedence over `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`
- [ ] an ADR exists recording the class model, the deprecation window, and the rejected alternatives
- [ ] every doc that presents `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the way to choose a model presents the class
      configuration instead, with the env var marked deprecated. The SIX below are the PROSE (`.md`) files ONLY — the four rendered `--help`/tool/docstring strings
      named in Scope are a SEPARATE class with their own criterion, because an earlier draft of this
      criterion counted only `.md` files while reading as if the whole repo were covered.
      RE-MEASURED with `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL` over the repo root excluding `.git/`, `.venv/` and
      `tests/` (tests are covered by AC2, not by this prose criterion) — stated as a command rather
      than as a claim about coverage, because an earlier
      version of this criterion said "MEASURED five files" from a grep scoped to `docs/` and
      `infra/` only and therefore MISSED THE PROJECT README. There are SIX prose files:
      `README.md` (line 239 — the front page, presenting `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as THE documented
      multi-provider interface, so the most important of the six), `docs/llm-framework.md`,
      `docs/config.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/workflow-authoring-v2.md`, and the
      generated `docs/env-vars.md` (regenerated, never hand-edited). Retargeted from an earlier version of this criterion that named the cutover
      runbook's kill-switch entry: VERIFIED VACUOUS — `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL infra/runbooks/`
      returns NOTHING, so no runbook ever offered it as a recovery lever and that criterion would
      have passed without any work. The kill-switch entry itself belongs to S8 (eb6e), which owns
      `infra/runbooks/`

baseline.description:
## Summary

The FIRST `initialize` handled by a freshly deployed mcp container takes far longer than the 30-second default startup timeout most MCP clients use, while every later client connects instantly. Reported as a cold-start problem; it is not one.

## Root cause (CONFIRMED — full evidence in the RCA comments)

**Every rebar MCP tool is a synchronous `def`, and the MCP SDK calls a sync tool body directly inside the ASGI request coroutine** (`mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py:93-96` — `if fn_is_async: await fn(...) else: fn(...)`). Behind the shared HTTP transport a tool call therefore occupies the uvicorn event loop for its entire duration, and the server answers nothing else meanwhile — not `initialize`, not `tools/list`, not even the unauthenticated `/health` route.

Measured on the deployed box: a `CallToolRequest` began at 21:03:00.590 and the process logged nothing at all for **3 minutes 56 seconds**; at 21:06:56.275 six `/health` responses and five 401s completed within **5 milliseconds** of each other — a backlog draining the instant the loop was released. From outside, that window is `http=000` after 70 s and 401s taking 12 s / 28 s / 50 s / 63 s against a 0.25 s steady state. Independently corroborated by the coordinating session: the container pinned at 100.4% CPU on a 2-core box with `/health` at `FailingStreak: 19` while `docker ps` still reported it `Up`.

rebar's own budgets make this routine: `AGENTS.md` documents `review_plan` at 15-20 minutes and a completion-verifier close at 9-11 minutes, and one unfiltered `list_tickets` has been measured at 177 seconds.

It reads as a startup bug only because a redeploy makes every agent reconnect at once, so the first client to `initialize` after a cutover is the one most likely to land behind another client's long tool call. The handshake itself is not slow: a cold authenticated `initialize` fired at the exact cutover instant against a 5.5-second-old container measures **0.030 s**. Store size, boto3 / `--extra bedrock`, static-token auth, and background provisioning were each measured and refuted.

## Fix

Run every synchronous tool body on a worker thread instead of on the event loop. This is the remedy this codebase already applied to the sibling service: ticket `c2ba` (`melting-resting-serpent`) moved the review-bot's `emit_code_review_artifact` off the event loop with `asyncio.to_thread` "so the drain bound can actually fire" (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`).

All of it lands in `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, which already owns the tool-`fn` wrapping seam (`instrument_certified_tools`) and is already wired from `build_server` via `wire_health`, so no other module changes.

1. `_thread_offloaded(fn)` returns an async wrapper that runs `fn` via
   `anyio.to_thread.run_sync`, under `functools.wraps` so the SDK's already-built `fn_metadata`,
   argument model, and output schema stay valid.
2. `offload_sync_tools(mcp)` walks `mcp._tool_manager.list_tools()`, replaces each SYNC tool's
   `fn` with that wrapper, sets `is_async = True` so the SDK awaits it, and returns the count.
   Already-async tools are skipped, never double-wrapped.
3. `wire_health` calls it AFTER `instrument_certified_tools`, so the certified tools keep their
   in-flight gauge instrumentation (that wrapper is sync and would be skipped if the order were
   reversed). The gauge is then incremented on the worker thread, which is exactly what its lock
   has always been for; its docstring is corrected to say so.

`anyio.to_thread.run_sync` rather than `asyncio.to_thread`: the SDK's transport runs under anyio, and anyio copies the caller's contextvars into the worker thread (verified). That is load-bearing — `run_http_with_grace` binds the box's op-cert signer as a ContextVar inside the serving thread and the certified tools mint op-certs from it. It also carries anyio's default 40-slot thread limiter, bounding concurrent tool bodies instead of allowing unbounded thread growth.

Applied to ALL tools, not only the certified ones: the gauge only needs billable work, but the loop is blocked by any slow body, and the 177-second `list_tickets` that motivates this is an ordinary read.

Deliberately NOT in scope: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`, the clarity/quality gate code, and the separate `/health` readiness gap (a real but distinct defect, filed on its own ticket).

## Portability

No CI provider is involved. The offload happens in-process at server construction on any host and any transport, with or without a deployment pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] The dominant contributor to first-`initialize` latency is identified BY
      MEASUREMENT, with the cold-start / store-size / boto3 / auth / provisioning hypotheses each
      explicitly refuted with numbers. (Recorded in the RCA comments.)
      provenance: environment=deployed rebar mcp container on rebar.solutions.navateam.com (production, read-only SSM session); principal=RebarBotNava operator session; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the dominant contributor is a CONCURRENT long-running tool call holding the uvicorn event loop, NOT cold start: 530 bearer-401 samples at 2 s spacing sat flat at 0.245-0.280 s until a CallToolRequest began at 21:03:00.590, after which the process logged nothing for 3m56s and then at 21:06:56.275 drained six /health responses and five 401s within 5 ms of each other; a cold authenticated initialize fired at the exact cutover instant against a 5.5 s-old container measured 0.030 s, and 60 samples across a real cutover were flat with no spike, refuting cold start (0.030 s vs 8.43 s reported), store size (0.030 s against the 2.2 GB store vs 0.010 s against a 1-commit store), boto3/bedrock (first /mcp request costs 8.9 ms vs 1.8 ms warm and imports only encodings.idna and stringprep; boto3 is imported at process start before uvicorn binds), auth (static strategy hashes the token file at build_server() time, no network on the request path), and background provisioning (volume persists, provision_store finishes in ~5.3 s alongside boot, pswpin 0 pswpout 0, 4.4 G available) — none of which is reproducible on the request path and none of which can be proved from the repository snapshot.
- [x] While a slow synchronous tool body is executing, the server still completes another request.
      This is the regression test, and it fails without the fix.
- [x] A synchronous tool body runs on a worker thread, not on the event-loop thread.
- [x] Contextvars bound by the caller (the op-cert signer binding) are visible inside the offloaded
      tool body.
- [x] An already-async tool is left untouched and is not double-wrapped.
- [x] The certified tools keep their in-flight-gauge instrumentation after the offload is applied,
      so the SIGTERM drain still observes in-flight billable work.

## Definition of Done

- [x] RED-first regression test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_tool_offload.py`, mutation-checked:
      reverting the fix turns it red.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, and
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` all pass.
- [x] Change pushed to Gerrit for review.

## Interim mitigation already applied

`~/.codex/config.toml` sets `startup_timeout_sec = 120`. That is a client-side tolerance for waiting behind someone else's tool call, and is not what closes this.
baseline.summary: First MCP initialize after a redeploy exceeds 30s, so the first client to connect always fails
