baseline.description:
## Summary

`/health` on the MCP server returns 200 without ever touching the ticket store, so a container with **no store at all** passes both the container HEALTHCHECK and the blue-green readiness gate. A structurally broken deploy is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

## Evidence

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:118-120` — the handler returns `JSONResponse({"in_flight": gauge.value})`
  and nothing else.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:56-57` — the container HEALTHCHECK is a plain 200 check on
  `/health`.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:130` — the blue-green readiness gate promotes on that same probe.
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:759-761` — the boot sweep is guarded by `if os.path.isdir(_tracker)`
  and emits NOTHING when the store is absent; the comment at `:752` states the intent
  ("a missing store / import / sweep error never aborts boot"), so not even the `debug` line at
  `:769` fires (that needs an exception).

Corroborating log evidence: 60 SSM invocations spanning 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-25 contain zero matches for `tickets-tracker`, `not initialized`, or `ticket init` — exactly what the code predicts. (Container logs use `driver: journald` at `docker-compose.yml:72,258,306,383` and no CloudWatch log group exists for them, so there is no remote log trail either.)

## Why this matters

This is the reason the missing-store defect went unnoticed since deployment. Log-and-continue on boot is a defensible posture on its own; combining it with a health probe that cannot observe the store means nothing in the pipeline can ever report the failure.

## How `expected` is computed (the field the whole refusal turns on)

`expected` is TRUE iff the deployment has EXPLICITLY declared where its store lives — concretely `config.tracker_dir_override()`, i.e. the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` env override is set and non-empty. It is FALSE when nothing is configured and the path is merely the default relative `.tickets-tracker` resolved against the repo root.

Deliberately read from the ENV OVERRIDE ALONE, not the parsed config, for two reasons: a health probe must not be able to fail (or hang) on config parsing, and the repo's `check_config_ownership` gate reserves `load_config` to approved seams. A project that instead declares a non-default `tracker.dir` in config therefore reports `expected: false` and simply does not get the strict gate — it degrades to the pre-change behaviour rather than misreporting. The deployment surface that matters here (the mcp compose service) sets the env var explicitly.

This is what makes the safety story concrete — and the STATE OF THE BOX MATTERS, so state it as of now rather than as a standing property. When this was first written the mcp service set no tracker dir, so `expected` was false and the gate was inert. That is NO LONGER TRUE: the sibling change kilted-nuclear-bronco now sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, verified on the live container. The store is meanwhile absent (a partial clone with no resolvable HEAD), so the box currently sits at `expected=true, present=false` — exactly the refusal condition.

The gate is therefore LIVE, not inert, and landing this before the store works would refuse promotion of every mcp container with `mcp-store-missing`, blocking mcp deploys entirely. That is the gate behaving as designed; the ordering is the thing that must be controlled. This ticket accordingly `depends_on` fathomable-yester-thrip (the poisoned-volume fix) and must not land until a real clone is in place.

## What `present` means, and why it is not HEAD-strict

`present` is exactly `os.path.isdir(path)` — the directory exists. It is deliberately NOT "a usable store" (a resolvable HEAD), and that choice is load-bearing:

Provisioning is BACKGROUNDED (`provision_store &` then `exec "$@"`) because the ~200k-commit clone outruns the 120s blue-green readiness deadline. A freshly started container therefore has a legitimately empty, HEAD-less tracker dir for MINUTES while its clone runs. A HEAD-strict `present` would report that healthy container as not-ready, the gate would roll it back, and the next tick would start another — reproducing the rollback loop `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` documents. The probe answers "is a store dir here at all", not "is it converged".

**Residual limitation, stated rather than implied:** a POISONED store — files but no usable `.git`, the state observed in production — satisfies `isdir` and reports `present: True`. This probe does not detect that and is not the mechanism that should: `fathomable-yester-thrip` (change 2244, merged) re-clones a store whose HEAD does not resolve. This gate catches the ABSENT-store deploy; the entrypoint catches the poisoned-store deploy. Neither subsumes the other, and the acceptance criteria below are scoped to the absent case only.

## Acceptance Criteria

All proven by `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py` (8 tests), each mutation-checked.

- [x] `/health` reports the store as a structured object — `{path, present, expected}`.
      Proof: `test_present_store_is_reported_present`,
      `test_absent_store_is_reported_absent_and_expected_when_a_dir_is_configured`
- [x] The gate FAILS OPEN on an unreadable or malformed signal, matching autodeploy's posture.
      Proof: `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`
- [x] The refusal is keyed on `expected AND NOT present`, never on absence alone, so a
      deployment that never configured a tracker dir is not marked unhealthy.
      Proof: `test_no_configured_dir_is_not_expected`
- [x] The refusal is observable under its own name (`mcp-store-missing`).
      Proof: `test_autodeploy_gate_names_the_storeless_refusal`
- [x] Boot emits one log line naming the tracker path when the store is absent, and is quiet
      when it exists. Proof: `test_boot_sweep_warns_naming_the_path_when_the_store_is_absent`,
      `test_boot_sweep_is_quiet_and_does_not_raise_when_the_store_exists`
- [x] `store_status()` never raises for an ordinary resolution fault, with ONE deliberate
      exception: a removed-but-still-set load-bearing input fails hard rather than being
      reported as merely degraded.
      Proof: `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`,
      `test_a_removed_load_bearing_input_fails_hard_instead_of_being_reported` — mutating the
      handler to swallow it yields DID NOT RAISE.


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py -q -p no:randomly
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py -q -p no:randomly

Per-criterion proving tests:

| criterion | proving test |
|---|---|
| gate consumes the field and refuses | `test_storeless_container_is_not_promoted_when_a_store_is_expected` |
| fails open on a body with no store field | `test_health_without_a_store_field_still_promotes` |
| keyed on expected, not absence | `test_storeless_container_IS_promoted_when_no_store_is_expected` |
| named refusal reason | `test_autodeploy_gate_names_the_storeless_refusal` |
| boot names the absent path | `test_boot_sweep_warns_naming_the_path_when_the_store_is_absent` |
| probe never raises / present-store branch runs | `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`, `test_boot_sweep_is_quiet_and_does_not_raise_when_the_store_exists` |

Teeth: gating on `present` alone (dropping `expected`) turns the two promote-cases RED; removing the gate turns the refusal case RED; an early return in the sweep turns the liveness anchor RED.
baseline.summary: MCP /health returns 200 with no ticket store, so a storeless deploy passes the blue-green readiness gate

## Why
Leftover VCS conflict markers in committed source are unambiguous, polyglot, and zero-FP — deterministic check territory, not an LLM pass. This is the #5 reclassification: a detector, not prompt text.

## What
Add a deterministic DET criterion (exec: DET) that flags VCS conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) and obvious encoding corruption (NUL bytes). Advisory / fail-open (blocking_enabled false). Reuses the Engine B detector consumer pattern (engine_b.scan -> apply_failclosed) and criteria_routing.json routing. Granularity note (grounded from plan review): engine_b.scan + apply_failclosed operate whole-file with diff-scoping applied as a post-filter on match LOCATION, not a native added-lines-only match. Reconcile this: either (a) accept file-scoped match with a location post-filter to changed files (simplest), or (b) add an added-line filter in the detector consumer. Decide and document; do NOT silently assume added-lines-only. Drops the fuzzy dso parts (truncation stubs, pasted-non-code-text) as too FP-prone.

## Scope
A builtin detector rule + criteria_routing.json entry (SHARED — coordinate with C, E); detectors.py wiring (and the added-line-scoping decision).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Conflict markers in changed files produce an advisory finding; clean diffs do not.
- [ ] The match-granularity decision (whole-file+location-filter vs added-line) is implemented + documented.
- [ ] Detector is polyglot and fail-open; no new BLOCK source.
- [ ] Recall+no-fire eval passes (marker present vs a legitimate '=======' inside a string/heredoc).
baseline.summary: Deterministic conflict-marker detector (DET criterion)

baseline.description:
## Why / Vision
The visual editor should let a human **compose workflows by selecting prompts and scripted operations that carry clear contracts, and by authoring prompts in place**. The unifying requirement: **every workflow step kind advertises an INPUT contract, an OUTPUT contract, and a description**, so the editor can present a typed palette and validate edits. Today the prompt system is reviewer-centric (a workflow agent step's `prompt:` resolves via `get_reviewer(id)`, which raises unless the id is in `reviewers/catalog.json`), no step kind declares I/O contracts, and there is no in-UI prompt library or authoring. This epic builds the contract-bearing prompt/step model and the editor authoring experience on top of it.

This is the FOUNDATION epic. The **MCP-call step track** (external MCP servers as a workflow step kind) is carved out to a **follow-on epic** that `depends_on` this one — it is a separable subsystem (allowlist/secrets/manifest), env-gated, with its own security surface, and nothing here depends on it. The design below was settled via /joe-brainstorm and derisked with spikes (see the decision-log comments E1–E5/E8: all pass, zero new runtime dependencies).

## What (the settled plan)
- **Decomposed-triple prompt model.** A prompt declares `input` contract + `output` contract +
  `execution_mode` (`single_turn` | `agentic`, fixed on the prompt). `category` is an ADVISORY
  grouping label for the palette. **Reviewers are a subset** identified by an EXPLICIT
  `category: review` / reviewer flag (never inferred from output-schema shape), so transform
  prompts can't accidentally enter the security-sensitive close gate. `single_turn` = zero tools
  (pure transform on `with:` inputs); `agentic` = the current tool-using pydantic_ai path.
- **Contract home = closed-set front-matter + schema-registry names.** Each prompt's `.md`
  YAML front-matter carries the contract using Prompty-aligned spellings (`inputs`, `outputs`,
  `description`, `model`, `tags`) plus rebar extensions (`execution_mode`, `category`, reviewer
  `dimension`/`applies_to`, `schema_version`). Heavy JSON Schemas stay referenced BY NAME in
  `src/rebar/schemas/` (reusing today's `output_schema` name-indirection and the existing
  `referencing.Registry`). Front-matter keys are a CLOSED set owned by rebar; unknown keys
  **warn + preserve** (kept verbatim, appended after known keys, deterministic order) for
  forward-compat — not an extensible meta-schema.
- **Front-matter read/write = parse-split-rejoin built over PyYAML (~40 LOC, no new dep).**
  Split on the `---` fence, parse/mutate the front-matter, re-emit `---\n<canonical dump>---\n`
  + body; **body preserved byte-for-byte**. Canonical key order, LF, single trailing newline,
  no BOM, idempotent. Reviewer-catalog metadata MIGRATES into per-file front-matter (the 6
  shipped reviewers gain front-matter; the parser exists but files don't use it today).
- **Derived-index lockfile.** `reviewers/catalog.json` collapses into a GENERATED, COMMITTED
  index built by scanning prompt front-matter, enforcing global invariants the per-file
  front-matter can't (exactly one default reviewer; no `dimension` collisions; preserve
  `langfuse_prompt`/`fallback_file`/`applies_to`). CI drift gate: regenerate + `git diff
  --exit-code` (the npm-ci / poetry.lock pattern). `applies_to` keeps stdlib `fnmatch`.
- **Scripted-op contracts (built FIRST as the reference impl).** Extend `@register_step` to
  declare `input_schema`/`output_schema` (names) + `description`; backfill the 8 existing ops.
  This anchors the contract vocabulary the prompt model reuses.
- **Validation = name-existence + 3-state shallow static + runtime-against-consumer.** Extend
  `lint_refs.py`: for a `with:` field mapped to `${{ steps.A.outputs.foo }}`, check (a) A's
  output contract produces `foo` and (b) a SHALLOW structural compatibility (top-level required
  presence + primitive kind), returning OK / UNKNOWN / ERROR — abstaining (UNKNOWN) on
  `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`not`/`$ref` (no subsumption engine; that is near-undecidable and has no
  popular maintained lib). A distinct `${{ inputs.* }}` namespace addresses engine-injected vars
  (ticket_id/ticket_context/repo_path). At runtime, produced values are validated against the
  **consumer's** input contract via rebar's registry-wired `jsonschema` (the real safety net).
- **Editor inspector + library + authoring.** Connections stay BPMN control-flow (no drawn
  dataflow ports). The inspector shows each step's consumes/produces (read-only) + autocompletes
  available upstream outputs. A **library dropdown** lists built-in + project prompts; the user
  can **select** one, **create a new** prompt, and **edit prompt text**. On Save, write-back
  AUTO-DETECTS a writable `nava-rebar` source checkout (→ edit the packaged built-in `.md`) vs a
  client project (→ write a `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override; never touch read-only
  site-packages); the resolved target path is always shown before Save. An override (or variant)
  that changes a prompt's `output` contract is a BREAKING change (new name/version);
  `validate` flags override-vs-builtin contract drift. Round-trip golden tests prove no corruption.
- **In-editor JSON validation + help.** Live validation of the step config field via a debounced
  server round-trip to the existing Python `jsonschema` (single source of truth, no client/server
  validator drift; measured p99 ~0.5ms so it's imperceptible — no `ajv`/Monaco validator added).
  Per-kind help walks element types + expected JSON shape (driven by the contracts/descriptions).
- **Properties panel (structured per-field entries).** Once contracts exist, replace the single
  config-JSON textarea with structured fields (uses/prompt/mode/model/with/loop bounds). The
  existing story `roomy-spine-mirth` (editor layout/nesting/properties panel) folds in here.
- **Branch/connection UX.** Keep the current representation (condition labels + default-flow slash
  + "after" continuation; no synthetic gateways — round-trip-fragile). Optional, lower-priority
  revisit only if a clearer representation is wanted; underspecified by design.

## Terminology (one model, three surfaces)
A step's CONTRACT = its declared input + output shapes. For PROMPTS the contract lives in front-matter keys `inputs`/`outputs`; for SCRIPTED OPS it is the `input_schema`/`output_schema` args on `@register_step`. In BOTH cases the value is a NAME resolving to a JSON Schema in `src/rebar/schemas/`. "contract", "input/output contract", the front-matter `inputs`/`outputs`, and the decorator `input_schema`/`output_schema` all denote this same thing at different surfaces.

## Cross-cutting decisions
- **Zero new *Python runtime* dependencies** (validated across all spikes). The editor already VENDORS its
  front-end bundle (bpmn-js + bpmn-js-properties-panel, built to `editor_assets/dist/`); using those
  vendored packages is NOT a new dependency. The constraint is about Python runtime deps. Reuse the already-present
  PyYAML (core), `jsonschema`+`referencing` (registry already wired in `schemas/__init__.py`),
  and stdlib `fnmatch`. Build the small bespoke pieces (front-matter writer, derived-index +
  invariants, shallow compat check). Rejected: ruamel.yaml / python-frontmatter / jsonsubschema /
  pathspec / ajv (fail the import bar or already solved by existing deps/stdlib).
- **Conform to JSON Schema 2020-12 everywhere** (pydantic v2 + MCP both emit it; rebar's schemas
  and the registry are already 2020-12). Migrate any stray Draft-07 (don't relabel).
- **`schema_version` stamped from day one**; older binaries gate on it (like TAG_DELTA, upgrade
  reconcile hosts first). Ship `.gitattributes` pinning prompt/index files to `eol=lf`.
- **`execution_mode` fixed on the prompt** is a conscious divergence from DSPy/BAML/pydantic-ai
  (which keep the typed contract swappable from the execution strategy); documented as deliberate.

## Out of scope (→ follow-on MCP epic)
The `mcp_call` step kind (external MCP servers), the two-tier allowlist + secrets/trust model, the cached tool manifest, and MCP output handling (opaque-`any` + structuredContent/isError). That epic `depends_on` this one and is env-gated (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_MCP_CALL`).

## Relevant code
- Prompts/resolver: `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` (`parse_front_matter`, `resolve_prompt`,
  `_glob_match`), `reviewers/catalog.json` + `reviewers/*.md`; runtime resolution in
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` (RunnerAgentStep — reviewer-centric, generalize).
- IR + validation: `src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v2.schema.json`,
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/{schema,lint,lint_refs}.py`. Scripted ops: `.../workflow/steps.py`
  (+ `@register_step` in `executor.py`).
- Schema registry: `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` (`registry()`/`validator()` — already
  `referencing.Registry` + `Draft202012Validator`; extend with input/contract schemas).
- Editor: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` (+ `resolve_prompts`) + `editor_assets/`; serializer
  `.../workflow/bpmn.py`.

## Context
Settled via /joe-brainstorm with prior-art research, an adversarial design review, a build-vs-import triage against the project import bar (popular-on-GitHub AND actively maintained), and six derisking spikes (E1 front-matter writer, E2 validation, E3 real-serena MCP mechanics, E4 validation latency, E5 derived-index, E8 merge) — all recorded in this epic's decision-log comments. The earlier "placeholder/provisional" framing is superseded by this spec.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Unified prompt model: a prompt declares `input`/`output` contracts + `execution_mode`;
      reviewers are an explicitly-flagged subset; built-in non-reviewer prompts are first-class
      and resolvable (project `.rebar/prompts/` override > built-in packaged).
- [ ] Prompts AND scripted ops each declare input contract + output contract + description,
      surfaced in the editor palette/inspector.
- [ ] `single_turn` vs `agentic` represented as a closed enum in the PROMPT FRONT-MATTER (distinct from the
      existing step `mode:[findings,structured,text]`), surfaced in the editor, and honored by the runner.
- [ ] Front-matter writer: canonical, body byte-for-byte, idempotent, unknown-key warn+preserve,
      with round-trip golden tests over the migrated built-in prompts (no corruption).
- [ ] Derived-index lockfile generated + committed, invariants enforced, CI drift gate fails on staleness.
- [ ] Validation: name-existence + 3-state shallow static check at author time; runtime validation
      against the consumer's input contract; engine-injected `${{ inputs.* }}` namespace resolved.
- [ ] Editor: select a prompt from a library dropdown (project + built-in); author a new prompt
      saved to the correct location (auto-detected, path shown); edit prompt text with safe write-back.
- [ ] In-editor JSON validation (debounced server round-trip) + per-kind element/contract help.
- [ ] Properties panel: structured per-field entries driving the step config (no raw JSON textarea).
- [ ] Zero new Python runtime dependencies; schemas conform to JSON Schema 2020-12; `schema_version` stamped.
- [ ] Docs/ADR deliverable: the front-matter format + closed key set, the `execution_mode` divergence (ADR),
      the `.rebar/prompts/` override mechanism, and the CI drift gate are documented (docs/ + CLAUDE.md as fit).
- [ ] A human can compose a workflow end-to-end in the editor by selecting contract-bearing
- [ ] The reviewer-catalog → front-matter + derived-index migration preserves all existing

## Cross-cutting policy (from the per-child plan-review)
- **Accessibility:** the workflow editor is an INTERNAL developer tool; a full a11y done-definition is
  DEFERRED as an explicit, documented decision (not silent) — revisit if it becomes user-facing.
- **Rollback / feature-flag:** rebar is an internal, git-versioned, single-deployment tool, so rollback
  = git revert. Runtime-behavior changes (S4 runner `execution_mode`, S5 executor runtime-validation)
  sit behind the existing config/gate pattern; no per-ticket canary/flag infra is built.
- **Test failure-paths:** every child's tests include failure/invalid/empty-path cases, not only the happy path.
- **Documentation:** the new conventions are captured in a dedicated docs/ADR child story (below).
baseline.summary: Workflow authoring v2: contract-bearing prompt/step model + editor authoring (foundation)

baseline.description:
The Gerrit review bot fetches the tree from webhook-supplied `patchSet.ref` (`voter.py:366,374` → `gerrit_client.py:368`) but casts its vote against `patchSet.revision` (`voter.py:657`). Those are two independently-supplied fields, so the tree that was reviewed and the revision the vote attaches to need not be the same commit — on one of the two mandatory merge gates.

Verified during approval and deliberately reframed: this is NOT a live vulnerability. Gerrit always emits the pair consistently (each patchset has its own immutable `refs/changes/NN/CCCC/P`), so a contributor cannot decouple them. Decoupling requires forging a webhook, which requires `WEBHOOK_TOKEN` (`app.py:280`, correctly compared with `hmac.compare_digest`).

The durable justification is non-adversarial: `clone_change_ref` fetches into `repo_root`, and the reviewed tree is whatever ends up there. A stale or reused clone dir, a partial fetch, or a future refactor of the checkout logic all produce a tree that is not the voted revision, with no signal.

Scope refined by the maintainer to the assertion only. The `--end-of-options` hardening was dropped: HTTPS transport already blocks the exploit path, and both proposers had independently scoped the other ~89 git call sites out as a separate sweep.

`review_bot/adapter.py:184` takes `ref` as a required positional and never reads it. Both proposers independently chose to give it this job rather than delete it, preserving the seam contract that `adapter.py:6`, ADR 0009, ADR 0015, and `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:411-413` all describe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] After fetch and checkout, the resolved `FETCH_HEAD` is asserted equal to `patchSet.revision`
- [x] A mismatch refuses to vote, fail-closed, with an actionable message
- [x] `adapter.py`'s `ref` parameter performs that assertion instead of being unread
- [x] A test covers the mismatch path (a false mismatch would block all reviews)
baseline.summary: Bind the reviewed tree to the voted revision in the review bot

# Plan-review fidelity-eval: add G3/G4 to the eval suite (reuse existing infra; non-blocking)

## Why
S4 (merge G3+G4) and S5 (bin-packing) need a SEMANTIC check (real findings: new container path vs baseline).
rebar ALREADY has the eval infra — do NOT build a new harness:
- the Inspect-AI / promptfoo EVAL SEAM (workflow WS-G);
- the per-criterion plan-review eval suite `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml` (built under epic 5fd2);
- `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` parallel-run-and-diff (recall + false-accept on a gold set, `min_gold` floor).
The container criteria G3/G4 are NOT covered by any eval spec today — a real gap. This story FILLS it and plugs
into epic 6f2d (soupy-spool-revel) WS-EVAL-EXISTING's standing parallel-run-and-diff discipline (relates_to 6f2d).

## What
- Add G3/G4 (container) eval specs (e.g. `eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml`) with discrimination/recall
  fixtures over the shared corpuses (DSO read-only / snap-oakhart / rebar's own tickets), mirroring the existing specs.
- Reuse `parity.py` (recall / false-accept, `min_gold`) as the "merged-vs-separate" (S4) and "packed-vs-per-child"
  (S5) diff. Baseline = current separate-call (G3,G4)/one-child-per-call findings; candidate = merged/packed.
- Metric = finding recall + G3/G4 attribution accuracy; explicit, documented tolerance.

## CI posture (cautious: evals are non-deterministic + cost live $)
- The OFFLINE discipline check (spec validity + grader discipline; deterministic, no model) runs on every PR and
  is a REQUIRED check today — the new G3/G4 specs simply join it (cheap, safe to block).
- The LIVE semantic eval (billable, non-deterministic) stays OPT-IN — `workflow_dispatch`, optionally PATH-SCOPED
  to `reviewers/**` + `eval_specs/**` + `plan_review/**` so it never runs on irrelevant changes — and is NEVER a
  required/blocking CI status check.
- For S4/S5 the live eval is a HUMAN-REVIEWED DEVELOPMENT GATE (run it, review recall/attribution, pass before
  merge), NOT a CI blocker — a flaky run can't block the build and it costs nothing on unrelated PRs.

## Scope
- In: G3/G4 eval specs in the existing suite; reuse of parity.py + the Inspect seam; the candidate-vs-baseline
  metric/tolerance; the CI-posture wiring (offline discipline validates the new specs; live eval gated/path-scoped/
  non-blocking).
- Out: the merge (S4) / bin-pack (S5) implementations it gates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] G3/G4 container eval specs are added to `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs` and pass the OFFLINE discipline check
      (deterministic, runs on every PR).
- [ ] The eval reuses `parity.py` (recall + false-accept, `min_gold`) to diff a candidate container path vs the
      baseline, reporting finding-recall + G3/G4-attribution accuracy.
- [ ] An explicit numeric tolerance is defined + documented.
- [ ] The LIVE semantic eval is OPT-IN (workflow_dispatch / path-scoped) and NON-BLOCKING — NOT a required CI
      status check; documented as a human-reviewed development gate for S4/S5.
- [ ] No new live LLM cost is incurred on PRs that do not touch plan-review/reviewer/eval_specs.
- [ ] `make lint` + tests pass.
baseline.summary: Plan-review fidelity-eval harness (semantic: new container path vs baseline)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`docs/releasing.md` tells a release operator that the `pypi` GitHub environment's required-reviewers rule is "the second human approval on every publish" (line 76-77) and that step 2 finishes by approving "the `pypi` deployment when prompted" (lines 82-83, 325). Both overstate the control. Verified read-only against the live GitHub API on 2026-08-19:

- `GET /repos/navapbc/rebar/environments/pypi` returns a `required_reviewers` rule whose
  `reviewers` list holds exactly **one** entry — the user `JoeOakhartNava`, which is this
  project's configured release identity — with `prevent_self_review: false`, and the
  environment itself has `can_admins_bypass: true`.
- `GET /repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/31916566035/approvals` (the 0.12.0 release) shows
  `state: "approved"` cast by `JoeOakhartNava` — granted non-interactively through the
  pending-deployments REST API, not by a person answering a UI prompt.

So the gate is neither a *second* approval (the sole required reviewer is the same identity that dispatches the run, and self-review is permitted) nor an *interactive human* one. A runbook that says otherwise teaches an operator to wait for a prompt that never arrives, or to believe a second party reviewed a release that in fact nobody but the dispatcher touched.

## Approach

Correct the three passages in `docs/releasing.md` so they describe the mechanism that exists, without replacing one overstated claim with another. The corrected text must state:

- **What the gate does guarantee** — the `publish` job, and therefore the environment-scoped
  OIDC token that Trusted Publishing mints, is held until an identity on the `pypi`
  environment's required-reviewers list explicitly approves that specific run. Combined with
  the `main`-only deployment-branch policy and the `authorize` job's ref/ancestry guards, no
  run from another ref and no run lacking that identity's approval can reach PyPI.
- **What it does not guarantee** — it is not independent second-party review. The sole
  required reviewer is the configured release identity, `prevent_self_review` is off (so the
  dispatcher approves their own run), and repository admins can bypass the environment
  (`can_admins_bypass: true`). The "the published source was reviewed" property comes from
  releasing only from Gerrit-reviewed `main`, which the doc already states correctly — the
  environment rule adds identity control over *who can release the publish job*, not a
  content review.
- **How to approve non-interactively**, since that is the path actually used: a complete
  `gh api --method POST .../pending_deployments` invocation carrying its required body
  (`environment_ids`, `state`, `comment`), plus the companion `GET .../pending_deployments`
  that discovers the environment id. The bare path with no body returns 422. The body is
  supplied with `--input -` and an explicit JSON document, **not** with `-f`/`-F` field flags:
  `environment_ids` must serialize as a JSON array of integers, and `gh api -f
  environment_ids=<n>` sends a string while `-F environment_ids='[<n>]'` sends the literal
  string `[<n>]` — both are rejected by the API. An explicit JSON body removes that
  flag-typing hazard from the runbook entirely.

Keep the env-preflight description load-bearing and unchanged in substance: `release_guards.py` still fails the release closed when the required-reviewers rule or the `main`-only branch policy is missing. What changes is the description of who approves and how, never the guard.

**Sweep decision (explicit).** `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `AGENTS.md` were grepped and contain **no** occurrence of this framing, so neither needs an edit; `CONTRIBUTING.md` stays in the file-impact list only to record that the sweep covered it. `.github/workflows/release.yml` line 294 carries the identical claim in a comment ("the second human gate on every publish") and **is** in scope: leaving it would let the workflow source contradict the corrected runbook one grep away. It is a comment-only edit; no test asserts that line.

## Scope

- `docs/releasing.md` — rewrite the "Release-source authorization" closing paragraph and
  step 2's approval sentence; add the non-interactive approval recipe.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — correct the line-294 `publish`-job comment to match.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — swept, no occurrence found; no edit expected.

## Testing

Documentation-only correction; it adds no testable behavior, so no new test is written. The existing `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py` drift assertions over `docs/releasing.md` and `release.yml` are the regression oracle and must keep passing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/releasing.md` step 2 documents approving the pypi pending deployment as the
      configured release identity and includes a complete, runnable REST form whose request
      body types `environment_ids` as a JSON array of integers. Checked:
      `grep -n "pending_deployments" docs/releasing.md` returns a hit, and
      `grep -nE '"environment_ids": *\[' docs/releasing.md` and
      `grep -n '"state": "approved"' docs/releasing.md` each return a hit, while
      `grep -nE '\-f +environment_ids|\-F +environment_ids' docs/releasing.md` returns
      nothing (no string-typed field flag for the array).
- [x] The runbook also shows the companion read that discovers the environment id, so an
      operator can fill the body without guessing. Checked:
      `grep -n "pending_deployments" docs/releasing.md` returns at least one line that is a
      `GET`/read invocation (`gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/.../pending_deployments`)
      distinct from the `--method POST` line.
- [x] The "Release-source authorization" section no longer calls the environment rule a human
      or second approval, and instead names both the guarantee (only a listed reviewer can
      release the publish job for a run) and its limits (single configured reviewer,
      self-review permitted, admin bypass). Checked:
      `grep -nEi "second human|human approval" docs/releasing.md` returns nothing, and
      `grep -nEi "prevent.self.review|self-review|admin" docs/releasing.md` returns a hit.
- [x] The env-preflight remains documented as load-bearing and fail-closed. Checked:
      `grep -n "fails closed\|fail the release closed\|fails the release closed" docs/releasing.md`
      still returns a hit, and `grep -n "required_reviewers" docs/releasing.md` still does.
- [x] No file in the repository retains the interactive-human-approval framing. Checked:
      `grep -rnEi "second human|human approval|approve the .?\`?pypi\`?. deployment when prompted" docs/ CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md .github/workflows/release.yml`
      returns no matches. (The earlier literal `approve the pypi deployment` never matched:
      the real text is backticked, `approve the \`pypi\` deployment`, so the pattern is
      backtick-agnostic.)
- [x] Gates pass on the whole tree: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting `new=0 increased=0
      stale=0`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py`.
baseline.summary: docs/releasing.md: pypi environment approval is executed by the configured release identity, not an interactive human prompt

## Context / Problem

From a `make worktree` worktree, the tracker resolves to the WORKTREE's path, not the canonical store's — because `.tickets-tracker` there is a symlink that nothing resolves:

```
cwd               : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug
repo_root(None)   : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug
tracker_dir(None) : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug/.tickets-tracker
realpath of that  : /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker          <-- the real store
```

Every per-store sidecar in `.rebar` is then derived from `os.path.dirname(tracker)` (`enrich_drain._rebar_dir`), so it lands in the WORKTREE's own `.rebar`, which is a real directory and not a symlink:

```
drain lock : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug/.rebar/enrich-drain.lock
drain log  : /Users/joeoakhart/fix-drain-cwd-spittlebug/.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log
```

Three consequences, in descending severity:

**1. The drain advisory lock does not serialise drains on the shared store.** Two agents working in two worktrees hold two DIFFERENT lock files while draining the SAME queue. The lock's whole purpose — "an advisory lock so two drainers do not overlap" (`enrich_drain._acquire_advisory_lock`) — is defeated exactly when it matters. This host currently has 105 worktrees.

**2. The drain log is scattered and disposable.** A drain child spawned from a worktree logs into that worktree's `.rebar/logs`, which is deleted with the worktree. This is why `3198-438c-72a5-470f` recorded only four tracebacks in the canonical log for a condition that recurs by design — most of the evidence was thrown away with the worktrees that produced it.

**3. A long-lived child can be handed a tracker path that vanishes.** The detached child gets the unresolved worktree path as `argv[1]`, so after the worktree is retired it fails with

```
Error: cannot list '/Users/joeoakhart/split-config-writer/.tickets-tracker'
```

— which is the one symptom in that log NOT explained by the cwd bug fixed in `3198-438c-72a5-470f`. That fix deliberately changed only the child's `cwd` and left the argv tracker alone, because moving it would relocate the lock and the log too, which is this ticket.

## Scope (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)

Decide where the boundary belongs, then apply it in one place — either resolve the tracker through symlinks at the point sidecar paths are derived (`enrich_drain._rebar_dir` and its equivalents), or resolve it at `config.tracker_dir`, which is broader and needs care because `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` and decoupled stores also flow through it. Whichever is chosen, the invariant to establish and test is: **one store means one drain lock and one drain log, regardless of which worktree the write came from.**

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Two writes from two different worktrees of the same store contend on the SAME drain
      advisory lock.
- [x] A drain spawned from a worktree writes to the canonical store's drain log, and that log
      survives the worktree's removal.
- [x] A detached child is never handed a tracker path that lives inside an ephemeral worktree.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while fixing `3198-438c-72a5-470f`. Same underlying theme — ephemeral worktree paths outliving their worktree — but a different artifact (the tracker path and everything derived from it, rather than the child's inherited cwd) and a different blast radius, so filed rather than folded in.
baseline.summary: worktree-local drain lock does not serialise a shared store

## Context
Research ticket melancholy-couped-turkey concluded that the fixed-count compaction cadence (`compact.threshold`, default 10) makes retained full-state snapshot bytes grow **Θ(N²)** for a growing ticket (measured: 5.36 GB of retired-snapshot bytes at 8,000 events). It recommends a **byte/replay-cost-aware cadence** (`compact_plan.needs_folding` folds when `pending_source_bytes >= alpha * active_snapshot_bytes`, plus a count floor and the existing first-snapshot arm), gated by a new default-off `compact.snapshot_alpha` config, which bounds retained-snapshot bytes to **Θ(N)** (~1/alpha amplification; 344× reduction at alpha=1.0) while keeping read cost within (1+alpha)× of a snapshot load. All ADR-0035 contracts (conservative horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, mixed-version rollback, two-clone union) are preserved because only the WHEN trigger changes.

This is a **design decision** and per AC5 of the research ticket must NOT be implemented until an ADR completes RESEARCH → DRAFT → HOLD → MERGE with human approval.

## Plan
- Author an ADR for the byte/replay-cost-aware snapshot cadence + `compact.snapshot_alpha` config; carry it through RESEARCH → DRAFT → HOLD → MERGE with human sign-off.
- Add a two-clone reconvergence test proving byte-cost cadence divergence is absorbed by merge-as-union + gap-timestamp + rebuild-on-stray (the one contract the single-clone benchmark could not exercise).
- Calibrate `alpha` against the live store's ticket-size distribution.
- Once the ADR MERGEs, decompose implementation into independently reviewable tasks with binary acceptance criteria (config field + coercer; `needs_folding` trigger; default-off rollback safety; tests).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An ADR for the adaptive snapshot cadence is authored and completes RESEARCH → DRAFT → HOLD → MERGE with recorded human approval: `checked: docs/adr/ contains the merged ADR`.
- [ ] A two-clone reconvergence test for byte-cost cadence divergence exists and passes.
- [ ] `alpha` default is calibrated and justified against the live ticket-size distribution.
- [ ] Implementation is decomposed into linked child tasks, each with binary acceptance criteria, before any code lands.

DO NOT start implementation before the ADR reaches MERGE. Escalated from melancholy-couped-turkey research.
baseline.summary: ADR + implement adaptive byte/replay-cost snapshot cadence (compact.snapshot_alpha)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Outbound sync can only write to one tracker project, and it fails closed on anything else. The create client takes its project from a single value set once at construction (`AcliClient.create_issue` uses `self.jira_project`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:271-327`), and the applier scans every outbound mutation pre-flight and raises `CrossProjectTargetError` — aborting the whole pass — if any update or delete targets a key outside the one configured project (`applier.py:217-258`, `_cross_project_targets`, added by bug `626d`). With a mapping that lists several projects, correct mutations to the other projects would be treated as the misconfiguration that guard exists to catch.

## Approach

Two changes, both narrow.

**Create targets the ticket's project.** The outbound create path resolves the destination through `resolve_project` from the mapping module rather than from the client's single construction-time value. A ticket that resolves to "not synced" produces no create mutation at all.

**The guard relaxes from equality to set membership.** `_cross_project_targets` currently compares each target key's prefix against one `configured_project` string; it instead checks membership in the mapping's project set. This is deliberately the smallest possible weakening: the guard stays fail-closed and still aborts pre-flight before any tracker write, so a stale binding pointing at a project the store does not sync is caught exactly as it is today. Only keys the store legitimately owns now pass. Creates remain exempt for the existing reason — their `key` is a local-id placeholder, not a real key, so `_JIRA_KEY_RE` does not match them.

This is the only existing safety property the epic loosens, which is why it is its own story with a paired test rather than folded into another change.

**Module size.** Two files here are close to the repository's hard 800-line gate, and they are treated differently on purpose. `dispatch_one.py` is at 796 lines, so the sibling size-relief story that extracts its `update_one` sub-tree is a prerequisite of this one — four lines of headroom cannot absorb the create-path change. `applier.py` is at 772 and is deliberately **not** split. A structural seam exists there (`_apply_batch` and its helpers), but taking it would relocate `_load_acli` and `_load_concurrency` out of the module against which roughly 62 `patch.object(applier, ...)` test sites are written — and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move, so those tests would keep passing while silently exercising the real Jira and git paths instead of their fakes. Against that, the change needed here is roughly five lines inside `_cross_project_targets` (`:232-257`), which fits comfortably in the 28 lines available. Splitting `applier.py` for this change would be the mechanical split the module-size policy forbids; if it ever must be split, the honest first move is the 67-line `__all__` and the ~126 lines of banner prose in `:1-198`, which disturb no call graph at all.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful fake transport fed production-shaped mutations, recording the create calls it receives, because the destination project carried on the call is the contract under test.

- Happy path: a ticket resolving to project `B` in a store whose mapping lists `A` and `B` produces a
  create call carrying `B`, not the repo default `A`.
- Contrast case (the guard, both directions in one paired test): an update targeting `B-1` where the
  mapping lists `A` and `B` proceeds; an update targeting `C-1` still raises
  `CrossProjectTargetError`. The negative half is what proves the relaxation did not disable the
  guard.
- Precondition assertion: the guard is shown to run **pre-flight** — the fake transport records zero
  writes when the out-of-set mutation raises, proving no partial leak.
- Edge: a ticket resolving to "not synced" produces no outbound mutation of any kind.
- Collateral invariant: with a single-project mapping the guard behaves exactly as before — an
  out-of-project key raises, an in-project key passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An outbound create targets the ticket's own resolved project rather than the client default;
      checked by a fake transport asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [ ] An update inside the configured set proceeds and one outside it raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] When the guard raises, no tracker write has occurred; checked by asserting the fake recorded
      zero writes.
- [ ] A ticket resolving to not-synced emits no outbound mutation; checked by asserting an empty
      mutation list for it while a synced sibling produces one.
- [ ] Single-project behaviour is unchanged; checked by a regression test running the guard against a
      one-project mapping in both directions.
baseline.summary: Multi-project outbound dispatch and cross-project guard relaxation to set membership

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Merge-abort recovery for the tickets branch is written twice.

`_store/sync.py` (reconverge) owns the whole toolkit: the abort-message parser (`_merge_abort_named_paths` + `_untracked_overwrite_paths` + `_local_change_paths`), the quarantine dir arithmetic (`_quarantine_dir_under`), the quarantine MOVER (`_quarantine_untracked`) and the local-change restore (`_restore_local_changes`) — roughly `sync.py:221-339`.

`_store/push_recovery.py` re-implements the mover as `_quarantine_untracked_paths` (`push_recovery.py:236-260`) and reaches sideways into sync for the two pure pieces (`from rebar._store.sync import _quarantine_dir_under, _untracked_overwrite_paths`, line 56, under a seven-line comment explaining why the mover could NOT be shared). The stated reason is real: every git call in `push_recovery` must run through the late-bound `core._git` seam that ~25 `push._git` monkeypatch sites depend on, while sync's mover shells through sync's own module-level `_git`.

The two movers have already DRIFTED. `push_recovery._quarantine_untracked_paths` checks `git status --porcelain -uall` for `??` on every named path before it moves anything (a mis-parse must never relocate TRACKED data); `sync._quarantine_untracked` has no such fence, and neither does the third caller, `_commands/doctor.py::_quarantine_leftovers`, which calls sync's mover directly. Bugs `small-delicious-loris` (6ccc) and `sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey` (573a) are the same defect landing in the two paths one at a time — exactly the instalment pattern the parent epic was opened for.

Prior work has already shared the ADJACENT pieces, and this ticket must not re-do them: `d6e3-548c-37eb-4c45` made `_store/git_outcome.py` the single failure-marker table and `gitutil.run_git_bounded` the single synthetic-timeout fold, and both merges already retry a TRANSIENT_FS fault through the shared `gitutil._with_transient_fault_retry` / `git_outcome.classify`. What is left is the merge-abort recovery toolkit above.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_store/merge_recovery.py` as the neutral owner, taking the git runner as a plain callable (`git(path, *args) -> CompletedProcess`) so BOTH the sync module-level `_git` and the late-bound `core._git` fit without either side losing its patch point:

- `abort_named_paths` / `untracked_overwrite_paths` / `local_change_paths` and the
  trailer-prefix table — moved verbatim from `sync.py` (pure, no subprocess).
- `quarantine_dir_under` / `quarantine_dir` — moved from `sync.py`.
- `quarantine_untracked(git, tracker, paths)` — ONE mover, unifying the two on
  push_recovery's stricter shape: resolve `--git-common-dir`, verify `??` for every
  named path BEFORE moving any, then `shutil.move` each into the timestamped
  quarantine; any refusal answers `False` with nothing moved.
- `restore_local_changes(git, tracker, paths)` — moved from `sync.py`.

Do NOT fuse the two merge control flows into one `merge_remote()`. They are genuinely different (sync: union merge, unrelated-histories case, restore-from-HEAD, warn-and-keep-local; push_recovery: stash-commit set-aside, transport-retry loop, `_raise_if_strict` reason codes, tri-state return), and a single function parameterised over those is a worse module than two callers of one toolkit.

`sync.py` keeps `_quarantine_untracked`, `_restore_local_changes`, `_untracked_overwrite_paths`, `_local_change_paths` and `_quarantine_dir_under` as thin delegating adapters — the names `doctor.py` and the pinning tests bind, and the names `sync._recover_merge_abort` resolves at module scope so its monkeypatch keeps working. `push_recovery` KEEPS `_quarantine_untracked_paths(core, base_path, paths)` with its exact current signature, also as a thin delegating adapter that resolves `core._git` at call time — `tests/unit/test_push_recovery_untracked.py` calls it directly (lines 286, 358, 372) and `monkeypatch.setattr`s the name (line 311), and `_retry_untracked_overwrite` resolves it at module scope, so the SYMBOL must survive even though its body does not. `push_recovery`'s `from rebar._store.sync import ...` line goes away; both adapters' bodies become one call into `merge_recovery`.

## Latent divergence converged (epic AC2)
The `??` fence reaches `sync` and `doctor` for the first time. It is a no-op on every path that exists today — sync's inputs come from git's own "untracked working tree files would be overwritten" list, and doctor's come from `dirty_tracker_classes()["leftovers"]`, which is built from `??` status lines — so no pinned behaviour changes. A NEW test covers the convergence directly: sync's mover must refuse, and move nothing, when handed a TRACKED path.

## Guard construction
See the 'Guard construction (moved from description)' comment on this ticket for the full guard spec (moved to fit the 8000-char review admission limit).

## Scope
`src/rebar/_store/merge_recovery.py` (new), `src/rebar/_store/sync.py`, `src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py`, `tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py` (new). `_engine_support/reads.py` and `_commands/doctor.py` are NOT touched — they call `sync.reconverge` / `sync._quarantine_untracked`, both of which keep their signature.

## Testing
New (`tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py`): the shared mover moves an untracked leftover into quarantine and answers True; refuses a tracked path and moves nothing; refuses an unresolvable `--git-common-dir`; refuses a path that vanished; the parser returns [] when the marker is absent; the uniqueness guard plus its three mutation cases (unmarked copy fails, reasoned marker passes, bare marker fails).

Pinning, to pass with NO assertion edits: `tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py`, `tests/unit/test_sync_union_recovery.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_recovery_untracked.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_retry_stash_pop.py`, `tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch.py`, `tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_strict.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_strict_happy.py`, `tests/unit/store/test_git_outcome.py`, `tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Exactly one quarantine mover and one merge-abort parser exist under `src/rebar`;
      checked by `tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py` uniqueness guard passing in
      the default `Verified` tier, and by
      `test -z "$(grep -rl 'shutil\.move\|shutil\.copy2' src/rebar | grep -v merge_recovery.py)"`
      exiting 0.
- [x] `push_recovery.py` no longer imports from `sync.py`, while still exposing
      `_quarantine_untracked_paths`; checked by
      `! grep -q "from rebar._store.sync import" src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py`
      exiting 0 AND
      `python -c "from rebar._store import push_recovery as p; assert p._quarantine_untracked_paths"`
      exiting 0.
- [x] No pinned behaviour changes: every pinning suite named above passes with no edit
      to any assertion; checked by `git diff origin/main -- <the ten pinning files
      named in Testing>` printing NOTHING (they are untouched; the only tests/ change
      is the new `tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py`), and by
      `pytest <those ten files> -q` reporting 0 failures.
- [x] The net non-test line delta is RECORDED (not gated) on the ticket, per the epic's
      measured finding that extraction costs more in the documented owner than it
      recovers; checked by a `rebar comment` carrying `git show --numstat`.

## Close verification (orphan takeover, 2026-08-22)
Commit 037d4da8373 merged to main (verified at 8a036765705). AC1: shutil.move/copy2 grep clean outside merge_recovery.py, tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py 11/11 pass. AC2: no sync import in push_recovery.py; _quarantine_untracked_paths importable. AC3: pinning suites pass post-merge, no assertion edits (change landed via Gerrit review). AC4: numstat delta recorded in comment. Boxes checked with this evidence.
baseline.summary: One merge-recovery path shared by sync.reconverge and push_recovery

## Why
Specialist overlays are where domain expertise belongs. Per the locked principle, each overlay carries BOTH halves — recall patterns and FP-discrimination — so the generic Pass-2 verifier stays domain-blind.

## What
Enrich six overlays with dso content (tests first to prove the pattern, then the five):
- tests: full behavioral-testing standard — recall (change-detector, tautological, over/under-mocking,
  source-grepping, existence-only) AND FP-guards (Four-Criterion test, Rule-5 structural-artifact
  exception, the VALID-patterns-not-to-flag). NOT-flag base rules do not apply to test-correctness.
- security: dso's 8 red-team concerns + hard exclusions deferring to the gitleaks/opengrep DET criteria
  by name + rationalizations-to-reject.
- performance: 8 AI-advantaged concerns; bright-line reasoning captured as evidence for Pass-2.
- api-compat: asymmetric-change / producer-consumer drift.
- db-migrations: delete+replace symmetry, destructive/backfill/lock-duration.
- llm-prompts: ui-artifact + domain-mismatch + contract-drift for rebar's own prompt seam.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-{tests,security,performance,api-compat,db-migrations,llm-prompts}.md. Each task lands with its overlay's eval (recall + no-fire).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each of the six overlays enriched with both recall patterns and FP-guards.
- [ ] Each overlay lands with a passing recall + no-fire eval; overlays do not over-suppress.
- [ ] Overlays remain advisory; Pass-2 verifier receives no domain-specific rubric.

Scope: `src/rebar/llm/**` excluding plan_review and workflow — the package root plus code_review, prompting, review_kernel, evals, criteria, overlap. ~218 lines leave.

Contains the repo's #1 hotspot: `runner.py` 797/800, 88 commits, 12 in five days, with a 371-line method at its C901 ceiling. Recovering ~45 lines takes headroom from 3 to ~48 — roughly 4-5 stories of runway WITHOUT another split. ADR 0056 measured prose at 40% of `run()` and 50% of its pre-call region.

A self-contradicting module: THREE sites assert Anthropic 400s when extended thinking meets a native output constraint, while `structured.py:228-238` — 210 lines below one of them, in the same file — explicitly calls that 'a stale rationale' and 'a relic'.

A dead field found via its own comment: `runner.py:94-97` says `extra_tools` 'is always None in practice'; grep confirms no caller sets it. Delete the field, not the comment.

Confirmed exemplar for the maintainer's original finding: `capabilities.py:166-198` is structurally a complete ADR (security posture for a BLOCKING gate, three numbered bounds, an explicitly accepted limitation on domain controls) and NO ADR in the 83-file corpus mentions web search in any form.

85 lines are free wins — history already citing b690, b300, 2682, 3a98, 7a79, e3cd, 8455. `providers.py:3-16` duplicates ADR 0059 §1 verbatim including its file:line citations.

capabilities.py:295-316 is a matrix that cost real AWS accounts to produce and says so; capabilities.py:269-281 carries a rejected-alternative warning sitting exactly where the next reader would reintroduce it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim
## CORRECTION (plan defect + plan-review preempt, parent 373f disposition vocabulary)

The plan's `extra_tools` premise is FALSE and would cause a regression if executed literally. `extra_tools` is LIVE, not dead: `llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:469,665` set it (the token-recovery record tool, story 2948), `llm/workflow/runs.py` threads it end-to-end, and `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py:491` asserts `captured.get("extra_tools")` ("the record tool is still wired"). The STALE unit is the `runner.py` comment claiming it "is always None in practice" — that is CORRECTED in place; the field is DO_NOT_MOVE (load-bearing). Superseding ACs below encode this and the 373f disposition rules.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one parent-373f
      label: RELOCATE (to an ADR / docs / ticket, reduced to a one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP,
      DO_NOT_MOVE, or CORRECT-IN-PLACE.
- [x] Decision rule CORRECT-vs-DELETE: a comment documenting CURRENT runtime behavior / a live
      invariant is CORRECTED in place; a comment is DELETED only when the thing it describes no
      longer exists (artifact removed, or superseded). Every DELETE records its reason
      (referenced-artifact-gone / superseded) in the commit body or a ticket comment.

# J1 — Freeze the Cloud adapter's behavior with characterization oracles before anything moves

## Context / Problem

The DC work requires moving shared units out of `adapters/jira/`, and the Cloud adapter is the battle-tested path validated against a live Jira tenant. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` exists as the held-out Jira oracle, but it was not written to pin the specific outputs of the units about to move, and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` asserts only the vendor-neutral port contract ("nothing satisfied by hard-coding Jira outputs", per its own docstring). So today a silent mapping change during extraction could pass CI.

## Approach

Extend the characterization suite until it pins, by exact expected value, the current output of every unit that the next story moves:

- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — `_map_local_to_jira_fields` for a representative ticket, plus
  `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` for every key AND the default-fallback value.
- `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` — `_sanitize_label` / `_sanitize_summary` / `_sanitize_comment` at, below, and
  above their limits, plus the invalid-label raise.
- `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` — `truncate_comment_body` at and above the limit.
- `adapters/jira/identity.py` — `JiraIdentityConvention` format/parse/predicate, including the legacy
  `rebar-id-` hyphen form.
- `adapters/jira/probe.py` — `classify_probe_response` for each status code it branches on.
- `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` — `map_fields_to_remote` for each of its branches.
- `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link` + `jira_fields._RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` for every relation.

These are golden-value assertions deliberately, not behavioral abstractions: their whole job is to fail if a byte of output changes during a move that is supposed to change nothing.

**Alternative rejected:** relying on the existing contract suite. It is explicitly written to be backend-agnostic, so it cannot detect a Jira-specific mapping regression — that is what makes it a good contract suite and a useless extraction oracle.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` — extended.
- No `src/` change whatsoever in this story.

## Testing

Unit tier against the real functions (no doubles): these are pure mappers and sanitizers, so the smallest tier that crosses the mechanism is a direct call, and the oracle is the exact returned value.

- happy path: each unit's output equals a literal expected value recorded in the test.
- edge: every value map is asserted for all keys AND for an unmapped key hitting the documented default
  (`"To Do"` / `"Medium"`), since the default is the branch an extraction is most likely to drop.
- failure path: `_sanitize_label` still raises on an unfixable label, and `classify_probe_response` still
  classifies its error statuses.
- mutation check: for at least three pinned units, temporarily alter the source value (e.g. change a status-map
  entry) and record that the characterization test goes RED — proving the oracle actually gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every symbol listed in the Approach section has at least one exact-value assertion in
      `test_backend_characterization.py`
- [ ] `make test` passes with no `src/` modification in this change
- [ ] [operator-attested] for three pinned units, altering the source value makes the corresponding
      characterization test FAIL — the pytest failure output for each of the three is pasted into a
      ticket comment, naming the unit and the value altered
- [ ] a coverage check shows every branch of `map_fields_to_remote` and `classify_probe_response` is exercised

baseline.description:
## Summary

The review bot dequeues a review event and starts reviewing it immediately, without first checking whether the revision that event describes is still the change's CURRENT revision. With a single serial worker and reviews taking tens of minutes, a queued event is routinely obsolete by the time it runs: the bot clones, reviews, and votes on a patchset the contributor already replaced.

The queue should DISCARD a queued review before starting it when a newer patchset has been pushed for that change.

## Mechanism

- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:218-247` — `_worker` does `event = await queue.get()` and then
  goes straight to `_voter.review_and_vote(event, ...)`. Nothing between the dequeue and the
  review re-reads the change's current revision. The event still carries the revision that was
  current when the webhook fired, which may be many minutes or hours earlier.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:80` — `WORKER_COUNT = 1`, with the rationale "One is enough for a
  single-box PoC (reviews serialize on the per-(change,rev) lock anyway)". That is what makes
  the staleness window large rather than theoretical: every review waits behind every other one.
- The capability to detect this ALREADY EXISTS but is not wired into this path:
  `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:258-275` — `get_change_event(change_id)` queries
  `/a/changes/{id}?o=CURRENT_REVISION` and shapes an event from the CURRENT revision. Its
  docstring scopes it to the manual `/rerun` path ("which has only a change id, not a live
  webhook payload"). The webhook path never consults it, so the one component that knows what
  "current" means is not asked.

## Observed evidence (2026-08-26, changes 2226/2231/2232)

The bot votes consistently ONE PATCHSET BEHIND:

    2226: PS6 uploaded 05:01:18 -> review bot voted on PS5 at 05:22:18   (superseded 21m earlier)
    2232: PS7 uploaded 05:59:01 -> review bot voted on PS6 at 06:10:12   (superseded 11m earlier)
    2232: PS8 uploaded 06:21:35 -> review bot voted on PS7 at 06:30:30   (superseded  9m earlier)

Each of those votes consumed a full LLM review of a tree that no longer existed.

## Impact

1. **Wasted spend and wall-clock.** Every stale review is a full clone + multi-pass LLM run
   against a superseded tree. On a single worker that time is not merely wasted, it is time the
   queue could not spend on current work.
2. **Contributors act on findings that are already fixed.** A `-1` arrives citing a defect the
   author corrected in the patchset the bot skipped. In this session that produced real churn:
   fixes were authored, and re-pushed, in response to superseded findings — which enqueued MORE
   reviews and deepened the backlog. The failure mode is self-amplifying.
3. **Head-of-line blocking for unrelated changes.** Because the worker is serial, stale reviews
   delay everyone. During this session changes 2225 and 2234 sat at `LLM-Review +0` for 90+
   minutes behind a queue whose head was doing obsolete work.

## Proposed fix

In `_worker`, between the dequeue and the review, read the change's current revision and drop the event when it no longer matches — logging a countable marker in the same greppable style as the existing `VOTER_ERROR` timeout path (`app.py:252-265`), so discards are observable rather than silent.

Discarding is SAFE and does not lose the review: the newer patchset fired its own `patchset-created` webhook, so an event for the current revision is already in the queue behind this one. The change still gets reviewed — at the revision that actually exists. The existing backfill reconciler (`reconcile.reconcile_once`, already the stated safety net for the abandoned -on-timeout case) covers the residual risk of a genuinely lost event.

Design points the implementer should decide explicitly:

- **Cost:** one extra REST read per dequeue, against a 15-45 minute review. Negligible, but it
  should fail OPEN — if the current-revision read errors, review the event rather than dropping
  it, so a Gerrit blip cannot silently swallow reviews.
- **Force/rerun events** (`_rebar_force`, and `manual-rerun` from `get_change_event`) are built
  from the current revision by construction; they should bypass the check rather than race it.
- **Do not discard the newest event for a change** — only ones strictly superseded by a later
  revision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A queued review event whose revision is no longer the change's current revision is
      discarded BEFORE the clone/LLM work starts, not after.
- [x] The discard is observable: a countable, greppable marker (sibling to the existing
      `VOTER_ERROR` timeout marker) naming the change and the superseded revision.
- [x] An event for the CURRENT revision is still reviewed normally — the discard must not cause
      a change to go unreviewed.
- [x] The staleness check fails OPEN: an error reading the current revision results in the
      review running, never in a silent drop.
- [x] Force / manual-rerun events are not dropped by this check.
- [x] Regression coverage: a queued event for revision N with the change now at revision N+1 is
      discarded; an event at the current revision is not.

## Verification

Every criterion above is proven by a named test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`. Run it with the worktree interpreter — the `reviewbot` extra supplies fastapi, and WITHOUT it these tests SKIP rather than fail, so a skipped run is NOT a pass:

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q -p no:randomly

Per-criterion proving tests:

| criterion | proving test |
|---|---|
| superseded revision discarded BEFORE the review | `test_worker_discards_a_superseded_revision_before_reviewing_it` |
| the discard emits a countable marker | same test — asserts a `_voter_error` marker was emitted |
| current revision still reviewed | `test_worker_reviews_the_current_revision` |
| unreadable current revision FAILS OPEN | `test_worker_fails_open_when_the_current_revision_cannot_be_read` |
| forced / manual rerun bypasses the check | `test_worker_does_not_discard_a_forced_rerun` |

Gates that must also pass:

    env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint
    env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck
    python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check

Proof the oracle has teeth rather than being a tautology: with the staleness check removed, `test_worker_discards_a_superseded_revision_before_reviewing_it` must FAIL while the other three still PASS. The first test proves the bug exists; the other three prove the fix did not over-correct into dropping live work, failing closed on a Gerrit blip, or killing manual reruns.

## Outcome (landed)

Gerrit change **2236**, commit `73c45f16cfe2`, merged 2026-08-26 10:47:05Z; an ancestor of `origin/main`. Re-verified from a clean worktree at `origin/main` with the `[reviewbot]` extra installed so the tests RUN rather than skip: 113 passed (`test_review_bot.py` + `test_review_bot_stale_vote_baa8.py`), `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean (684 files), complexity `new=0 increased=0`. Per-criterion proving tests, the non-vacuity anchor (`assert ['old_rev'] == []` pre-fix), and the four mutation results (M1 whole guard, M2 fail closed, M3 bypass removed, M4 marker removed — each killed by exactly its own test) are recorded in this ticket's `/rebar-debug` comment.

**Scope note.** This ticket closes the PRE-REVIEW window ("don't start"). The residual TOCTOU — a patchset landing DURING the 15-45 minute review — is closed by bug `baa8-6a40-7052-46c2` (Gerrit 2330, `afe01efaa8b2`), which re-reads the current revision immediately before `post_review` and suppresses the vote ("don't publish"). Both are on `main`; both fail open and both exempt forced reruns.
baseline.summary: Review bot reviews superseded patchsets: the queue never re-checks current revision before starting a review
