# Land PR #127 via Gerrit: pypandoc-binary 1.17 + ruff 0.16.2; mcp 2.0 deferred to 732b

## Context / Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot PRs never merge there; content is re-applied locally and landed via Gerrit, then the PR is closed by hand. PR #127 proposes: `pypandoc-binary` `1.15` -> `1.17` (pinned EXACTLY, `wiki` extra + `dev` group); `ruff` `0.16.1` -> `0.16.2` (pinned EXACTLY in `dev` — hook, local lint, CI identical); and `mcp` `1.29.0` -> `2.0.0` (major), loosening the pyproject ceiling `<2` -> `<3`.

The `mcp` half is the third re-proposal (PRs #124/#125/#127), rejected under ticket 1dfd (mcp 2.0 removes `mcp.server.fastmcp`, imported by mcp_server.py + gen_mcp_reference.py); migration is epic `732b-51df-acf2-477b`: stay on `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` until 2.0.x stabilizes. This ticket lands the safe subset only.

## Approach

Land the `pypandoc-binary` + `ruff` bumps; the `mcp` ceiling stays `<2`. In a fresh worktree branched from `origin/main`:

1. `pyproject.toml`: `pypandoc-binary==1.15` -> `==1.17` in BOTH `wiki` and `dev`;
   `ruff==0.16.1` -> `==0.16.2` in `dev`. Keep both pins exact.
2. `uv lock --upgrade-package pypandoc-binary --upgrade-package ruff` — the lock is
   regenerated by uv, never hand-edited (CI gates on `uv lock --check`); sync the venv.
3. **Pin-provenance consumers**: read the new BUNDLED pandoc version empirically
   (`pypandoc.get_pandoc_version()`), then update EVERY hard-coded pin site (inventory:
   `grep -rn '3\.6\.1|1\.15'` over the whole tree, excluding only uv.lock and captured
   fixture data):
   * `NOTICE` — the `Version:` line + the `pypandoc-binary==1.15` wheel reference; and
     the `"3.6.1" in text` assertion in `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py`.
     Do NOT touch its upstream-URL assertion (`"pandoc.org" in text or ...`) — a
     parallel change owns that exact line.
   * `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render.py` — NON-skipping provenance asserts
     `pypandoc.__version__ == "1.15"` (L55) + banner `pandoc 3.6.1` (L59), and ADR
     asserts `"3.6.1" in adr` / `"1.15" in adr` (L326-327).
   * ADR 0095 — the "Pin provenance" pin + bundled-pandoc line (what L326-327 read).
   * ADR 0096 — the Finding recording the pins + both fingerprints (lockstep with 4b).
   * `wiki_render.py` module docstring's `pandoc 3.6.1` mention (accuracy only).
   * `tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py` — passes hard-coded "3.6.1"
     to `validate_pandoc_provenance` against provenance built from
     `generator.LEGACY_PANDOC_VERSION` (L103/111/193/201/203/247); after 4a the
     version-match check raises — update the literals (or derive from the constant).
   `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/code_arrow.json` mentions the old pins too but is
   captured ticket data — leave byte-identical.
4. **Byte-safety corpus**: `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py` freezes
   `LEGACY_PANDOC_VERSION = "3.6.1"` + a per-platform `SUPPORTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256`
   map (darwin-arm64, linux-x86_64); test_wiki_render_hardening.py's provenance test
   validates the installed binary's version + SHA-256 against the provenance in
   `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.json` + the three replay files. Bumping the
   wheel = deliberately re-establishing the reviewed baseline (sanctioned by the
   generator's docstring):
   a. Update `LEGACY_PANDOC_VERSION` to the new bundled version.
   b. Recompute BOTH fingerprints: darwin-arm64 = SHA-256 of the locally installed
      pandoc; linux-x86_64 = download the exact 1.17 manylinux x86_64 wheel recorded
      (URL + hash) in `uv.lock`, extract, hash the `pandoc` inside — no Linux host
      needed; wheel integrity is attested by uv.lock.
   c. Regenerate the legacy manifest + three replay files with the generator (supported
      binaries of one version emit byte-identical fixtures, so a darwin regeneration is
      valid for CI's linux gate; the provenance test enforces this).
   d. Confirm with the script's non-writing `--check` + test_wiki_render_hardening.py.
   If the bytes churn implausibly (unit count deviates from 884, or `--check` disagrees),
   STOP: defer the pypandoc half too (land ruff alone) rather than commit an unreviewed
   baseline. STOP fallback done-state: pypandoc half moves to a
   discovered_from follow-up ticket; this ticket completes on the ruff-only subset
   (AC1/AC3/AC4 re-scoped to the follow-up; AC2 = ruff only; AC5-AC7 unchanged).
   (Not exercised: the bump landed cleanly.)
5. **ruff verdict drift**: run `make lint`; if 0.16.2 flags or reformats existing code,
   apply the minimal fix and note it in the commit message. NEVER touch
   `.github/complexity-baseline.json`.
6. Do NOT touch `mcp` constraints, `_optionality.yml`, ADR 0050 — 732b's edit-set.
7. Verify (`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `pytest tests/unit tests/scripts`, generator
   `--check`), commit with a `rebar-ticket:` trailer + DCO sign-off, push
   `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`; leave the ticket `in_progress` while the bots
   vote; close only after merge, with PR #127 closed by a comment pointing at 732b.

## Scope

* `pyproject.toml` — the two `pypandoc-binary==` pins (`wiki` + `dev`) + the `dev`
  `ruff==` pin.
* `uv.lock` — regenerated entries + incidental churn.
* Pin-provenance consumers (step 3): `NOTICE`, notice test (version string only, never
  the upstream-URL line), test_wiki_render.py pin asserts, ADR 0095 "Pin provenance" +
  ADR 0096 pin/fingerprint findings, `wiki_render.py` docstring,
  `tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py` version literals.
* `scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py` — `LEGACY_PANDOC_VERSION` + both
  `SUPPORTED_PANDOC_BINARY_SHA256` entries, nothing else.
* `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.json` + three `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_replay/`
  files — regenerated wholesale by the generator, never hand-edited.
* Minimal source fixes ONLY if ruff 0.16.2 changes a lint/format verdict.
* OUT: the `mcp` bump and its `<2` -> `<3` ceiling move (deferred to epic
  `732b-51df-acf2-477b` — already filed, no new ticket needed);
  `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`; ADR 0050; `.github/complexity-baseline.json`;
  dependabot config; other open dependency PRs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `pyproject.toml` has `pypandoc-binary==1.17` (twice), `ruff==0.16.2`, and
  still `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` in both places
  (`grep -nE 'pypandoc-binary==|ruff==|mcp>=' pyproject.toml`).
- [x] AC2: `uv.lock` records pypandoc-binary 1.17, ruff 0.16.2, mcp 1.29.0
  (`grep -A1 -E '^name = "(pypandoc-binary|ruff|mcp)"$' uv.lock`); `uv lock --check`
  exits 0 (CI's gate).
- [x] AC3: every pin-provenance consumer names the versions 1.17 actually ships (per
  `pypandoc.get_pandoc_version()`): `NOTICE`, the notice test's version string,
  test_wiki_render.py's provenance asserts, ADR 0095 Pin provenance, ADR 0096
  fingerprints; `pytest tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render.py` exits 0 (non-skipping).
- [x] AC4: baseline re-established: `LEGACY_PANDOC_VERSION` + both fingerprints match
  the 1.17 wheels (darwin from the installed binary, linux from the uv.lock-pinned
  manylinux x86_64 wheel), fixtures regenerated by the script (never hand-edited),
  `python scripts/generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py --check` exits 0, and
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py` exits 0.
- [x] AC5: `make lint` (ruff 0.16.2), `make typecheck`, `pytest tests/unit`, and
  `pytest tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py` all exit 0 with the
  worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [x] AC6: a Gerrit change carrying this diff exists on refs/for/main with this
  ticket's `rebar-ticket:` trailer and DCO sign-off (`git log -1 --format=%B HEAD`).
- [x] AC7: mcp 2.0 NOT landed (no edit to the `mcp` constraints, `_optionality.yml`, or
  ADR 0050 per `git diff origin/main --stat`); deferral recorded as a ticket comment
  naming epic `732b-51df-acf2-477b`.
baseline.summary: Land dependabot PR #127 through Gerrit: pypandoc-binary 1.17 + ruff 0.16.2 (mcp 2.0 deferred to 732b)

baseline.description:
Cost Gerrit change 1942 (ticket silken-stealthful-narwhal) a spurious Verified -1: 1 failed, 14508 passed. The failure is unrelated to that change, which touches only scripts/gen_config_reference.py and tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py.

## Context / Problem

TEST: tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated

FAILURE (run 32327846364, job 96302879852, ubuntu py3.13, xdist worker gw3):

    shutil.Error: [('.../source/origin.git/objects/maintenance.lock',
                    '.../destination/origin.git/objects/maintenance.lock',
                    "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../source/origin.git/objects/maintenance.lock'")]

## Mechanism (CONFIRMED by measurement, not inferred)

The test creates a bare `source/origin.git` with a raw `git init --bare`, pushes into it, and on the VERY NEXT statement runs `shutil.copytree(source_origin, destination_origin, symlinks=True)`.

At git's defaults a bare repository's `receive-pack` runs `run_auto_maintenance()` after every push, which spawns `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` — a background process that OUTLIVES the push. So `subprocess.run([... "push" ...], check=True)` returning is NOT a happens-before edge for that repository's object database. The copytree then walks a directory tree that a detached git process is concurrently rewriting.

Measured on this exact test with `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`:

- 3 `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` children (the repos the TEST creates itself)
- 11 `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --no-detach` children (rebar-OWNED trackers, already pinned foreground by `_commands/init.py`'s gc-config ensure unit — bug 88eb, ADR 0051)

A bare remote built by a test fixture is owned by no rebar code, so it runs at git's defaults. That is the entire gap.

## The mechanism is BROADER than the observed signature

A standalone deterministic reproduction (bare repo + push, `transfer.unpackLimit` raised so receive-pack explodes the push into loose objects, `gc.auto=1` so auto-maintenance has real work, then copytree immediately after the push returns) fails like this:

    post-push maintenance.lock observed: True
    copytree failure: shutil.Error: [('.../origin.git/objects/2c', ...,
      "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../origin.git/objects/2c'"),
     ('.../origin.git/objects/2d', ...), ...]

The entries that vanish mid-walk are whole loose-object FANOUT DIRECTORIES being pruned as maintenance packs them. `objects/maintenance.lock` is merely the entry CI's walk happened to reach first.

Consequence for the fix: filtering `*.lock` out of the copy would NOT de-flake this test. The repack limb remains wide open. The same second limb was measured on bug chewed-illicit-blacklemur, where ignoring `*.lock` was likewise shown insufficient.

## Approach — remove the mutator, do not narrow the window

Pin the fixture bare remote's upkeep posture immediately after `git init --bare`, before anything is pushed into it:

- `receive.autogc=false` — the direct fix. A throwaway fixture remote has no reason to run upkeep at all; measured, this drops the push's maintenance children to ZERO.
- `gc.autoDetach=false` and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` — defence in depth for any other trigger. These do not suppress maintenance, they force it into the FOREGROUND, so the git command that triggered it cannot return while it is still running.

Either way no mutator survives the push. Measured postures, all with `receive-pack` confirmed present in the trace:

| posture | maintenance children | detached? |
|---|---|---|
| git defaults | 1 | yes — background mutator |
| autoDetach pins only | 1 | no — foreground, push waits |
| all three pins | 0 | n/a — no upkeep at all |

This is the same three-key remedy `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` already applies to its own fixture remote (`_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS`, bug 5b74-5d8f-a6b4-4674). Explicitly NOT doing any of: retrying the copytree, sleeping before it, excluding `*.lock` from the copy, or relaxing any assertion. Each of those makes the flake rarer without making the test correct, and a rarer flake is worse — harder to diagnose, and it trains people to retry instead of investigate.

## Guarding the fix against silent regression

Asserting that the copy "works" cannot prove the mutator is gone — the race is a coin flip, so a green copy is consistent with the mutator still existing. So a new sibling test asserts the mutator's ABSENCE directly from git's own process trace: the push runs under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, and no `git maintenance run` child it spawns may carry `--detach`. A positive control first asserts the trace actually recorded the push's `receive-pack` child, so the guard cannot pass against an empty or unwritten trace. The assertion is a content fact about an argv list — no timing bound, no polling.

## Scope

- tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py

The same "raw `git init --bare` fixture remote at git defaults" pattern exists elsewhere in the suite. A survey found two further HIGH-risk sites (a bare remote pushed into and then copied by `clone_topology_template`). Per scope discipline those are filed as a separate ticket with the evidence rather than absorbed into this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The fixture bare remote in this test is created with `receive.autogc=false`, `gc.autoDetach=false` and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` pinned before anything is pushed into it; checked by reading the diff.
- [x] A push into that remote leaves no detached background upkeep running; checked by a new test that runs the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` and asserts no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`, with a `receive-pack` positive control so it cannot pass vacuously.
- [x] That new guard genuinely discriminates; checked by removing the pins and observing it go RED with the detached child in the failure message, then restoring them and observing GREEN.
- [x] The existing test still proves what it guards; checked by seeding a defect that stops the copy being re-pointed at its own sibling origin, observing RED on the test's own assertion, reverting, and observing GREEN.
- [x] The fix removes the race rather than tolerating it; checked by review of the diff for the absence of any retry loop, sleep, timing bound, or `*.lock` ignore predicate.
- [x] `pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -q` is green; checked by that command.
- [x] The whole `tests/interfaces` tier is green; checked by `pytest tests/interfaces -q`.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` all pass; checked by running each at close (`active=48 new=0 increased=0 stale=1` — the original `stale=0` wording amended at close 2026-08-21: a stale entry is the ratchet's sanctioned PASS state per AGENTS.md and is unrelated drift on main; this change is test-only. See the verification comment).
baseline.summary: Flaky: test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin races git auto-maintenance's objects/maintenance.lock

# Remove the dead per-language analyzer dispatch and its inert config field

## Scope WIDENED 2026-08-05 by operator decision, after an archaeology pass

Originally scoped to `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` alone. Widened to the whole dead dispatch, because story `c23c-c32b-982c-4196` already sanctioned exactly this and the clause was never executed.

## What the record shows

Epic `839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051` designed per-language analyzer dispatch selected by per-project config. Story `3b30-2168-ba16-41fc` built the seam and shipped the registry INTENTIONALLY EMPTY -- its AC says "import registers nothing into REGISTRY as a side effect (opt-in wiring lands in 0734)". That wiring never happened.

`0734-ceae-be55-4fa7` then bypassed it for size, with a stated reason: "module size is POLYGLOT aggregate LOC, so it uses the single language-agnostic LOC analyzer directly -- NOT resolve_analyzer(lang)".

`c23c-c32b-982c-4196` retired the design outright: "implement direct adapter composition, not the unused language-dispatch table... If ANALYZERS/resolve_analyzer/analyze_or_unavailable remain unused after this direct composition, REMOVE THAT DEAD DISPATCH while retaining AnalyzerResult/Analyzer protocol compatibility." c23c implemented the composition but never executed the removal clause -- it was conditional and was not an acceptance criterion, so no gate held it. This ticket executes it.

The seam was also never viable as designed: `analyze_or_unavailable` calls `analyzer.analyze(repo_root, languages=languages)` BY KEYWORD, but `scc_loc.analyze`'s second parameter is named `scan_roots`. Verified at runtime: TypeError, unexpected keyword argument 'languages'. mypy --strict does not catch it because module-as-protocol checking is lenient about parameter names. So populating the registry would have crashed on the scc adapter.

## DELETE

- `ANALYZERS` (src/rebar/metrics/analyzer.py:32) -- never populated in src/, only monkeypatched by tests
- `resolve_analyzer` (:44) -- dead in production
- `analyze_or_unavailable` (:50) -- ZERO production callers
- `load_lizard` (:35) -- dead, and duplicates the guard `lizard_complexity.analyze` already does at :27-30
- `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers` (src/rebar/_config_schema.py:541) and its coercion row (:716)
- the self-referential escape marker `# read-via: inert pending bug dce2-b93d-4112-451c` (:540)
- the now-dead tests that exercise only the removed symbols (tests/unit/metrics/test_analyzer.py,
  test_analyzer_heldout.py) -- keep any that cover retained symbols

## KEEP -- do NOT remove

- `AnalyzerResult` -- LIVE, imported by git_metrics.py:14 and all three adapters
- the `Analyzer` Protocol -- c23c explicitly said "retaining AnalyzerResult/Analyzer protocol
  compatibility". It becomes documentation-only once its callers go; that is intended.
- the whole live path in git_metrics.py (`_scc_analysis`, `_lizard_analysis`, `_jscpd_analysis`,
  `_cached_analysis`, `_structural_spec`) -- this is the working composition and must not change
- `code_health.enabled` -- separately inert, tracked by its own bug; NOT in scope here

## NOT in scope

Reviving selection is idea `94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2`, which carries the operator's condition that it must ship with a dogfooded project-specific analyzer rather than as config alone. The inert `code_health.enabled` field is bug `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1`. The 6754 gate's global-name-matching weakness is bug `2c58-e710-275e-4ff7`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All six deletion targets above are removed; `grep -rn "ANALYZERS\|resolve_analyzer\|analyze_or_unavailable\|load_lizard" src/` returns nothing.
- [x] `AnalyzerResult` and the `Analyzer` Protocol still exist and `git_metrics.py` still imports `AnalyzerResult`.
- [x] `rebar metrics` produces byte-identical output before and after on this repo (all four structural metrics remain Unavailable for the same reasons -- the tools are not installed here -- proving a pure removal with no behavior change).
- [x] The `# read-via:` marker is gone AND `scripts/check_config_reads.py` passes without it, because the field it exempted no longer exists.

- [x] Reference sets confirmed with BOTH a semantic search and a plain string grep, per AGENTS.md -- the removed symbols are reached via `monkeypatch.setattr`/`setitem` in tests, which the LSP does not see.

## Why
The GitHub mirror lock (S6) is a one-way-door change to a PUBLIC repo. De-risk it by doing
the no-live-repo-change pre-work FIRST: capture a restorable snapshot of the current
protection, record the decision + accepted risk in an ADR, and confirm the IaC backend +
token scope — so S6's live apply is fast, ordered, and reversible. This story makes NO change
to the live repo.

## What
- Snapshot the existing `main-protection` ruleset (DERISK E5: id 18048287 — `pull_request` +
  `required_status_checks` + `deletion` + `non_fast_forward`, admins bypass-via-PR) to a
  committed `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json`
  (`gh api /repos/navapbc/rebar/rulesets/18048287`), so the prior PR-based protection can be
  restored on rollback. Snapshot ONLY — the live ruleset is not modified here.
- Write `docs/adr/0011-github-mirror-lock.md`: the repo-level-vs-org-level trade-off (free org

## Scope

enforcing the rulesets + mirror hygiene (S6); the Gerrit-side replication (S5).

## Context / Problem

On the AGENTIC path the growing tool-result history is re-sent UNCACHED every turn, so input cost grows O(N^2) in turns — and rebar's own telemetry cannot see it.

`capabilities.py:333-355` `cache_settings_for` sets exactly two of the four available breakpoints:

    anthropic_cache_instructions=True
    anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True

and its docstring says so outright: "neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched." Applied once at `runner.py:394`.

BOTH UNUSED KNOBS ALREADY EXIST in the pinned dependency — verified by introspection against the repo's own `.venv` at pydantic-ai 1.107.1, not from docs:

    AnthropicModelSettings: anthropic_cache, anthropic_cache_instructions,
                            anthropic_cache_messages, anthropic_cache_tool_definitions
    BedrockModelSettings:   bedrock_cache_instructions, bedrock_cache_messages,
                            bedrock_cache_tool_definitions

## The failure, concretely

`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 250` (`config.py:127`) yields `request_limit = 125` (`structured_run.py:331`). The agentic Pass-1 criteria and container calls (`plan_review/passes.py:330, 434`) run a tool loop in which EVERY turn re-sends the full accumulated message history. With only a system breakpoint that history is never written to cache and never read. On a 40-turn review whose file-read tool results average 2k tokens, turn 40 re-sends ~80k uncached tokens that turn 39 also sent.

IT IS INVISIBLE TO OUR TELEMETRY. `warn_if_cache_ineffective` (`structured_run.py:417-422`) requires `cache_read_tokens == 0`, but the SYSTEM block IS hitting cache, so the counter is nonzero and the predicate never fires. We would never learn this from a usage log.

## Consensus — this is the documented multi-turn shape, not an exotic optimisation

* Anthropic's prompt-caching doc recommends TWO breakpoints for multi-turn: system AND "the final
  block of the final message... so the conversation can be incrementally cached", and names automatic
  caching the "recommended starting point" for multi-turn.
* LangChain's `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`
  (`libs/partners/anthropic/langchain_anthropic/middleware/prompt_caching.py`) tags system + last tool
  and delegates the tail to `model_settings["cache_control"]`.
* pydantic-ai's own Anthropic docs recommend the same triple.
System-only is the documented minimum for a STATIC-PROMPT workload; it is not the shape for an agent.

Corroborating that this was once in scope and got dropped: story REB-458 is titled "Prompt caching at the shared runner seam (CachePoint + anthropic_cache_*, provider-safe)" and is marked Done, but the shipped `cache_settings_for` sets two of four knobs and no CachePoint.

## Approach

Thread the execution mode into `cache_settings_for` and, for `agentic` ONLY, add `anthropic_cache=True` on the Anthropic arm and `bedrock_cache_messages=True` on the Bedrock arm.

MIND THE PROVIDER ASYMMETRY — this is the trap: Bedrock has NO `bedrock_cache` automatic key. LangChain hit exactly this (langchain#37042): `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware` regressed on Bedrock in 1.4.1 because it switched to top-level automatic caching, which Bedrock rejects with `cache_control: Extra inputs are not permitted`. So the two arms need different keys, not one shared setting.

Breakpoint budget is safe: pydantic-ai's `_limit_cache_points()` sets `MAX_CACHE_POINTS = 3 if automatic_caching else 4`, and this change puts rebar at 3.

Single-turn paths must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL — that is the regression risk and the thing to pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] On the AGENTIC path the message tail is cached: a captured multi-turn request shows a breakpoint
      after the accumulated history, and a live run records nonzero `cache_read_tokens` attributable to
      the message tail rather than only to the system block.
- [x] The Anthropic and Bedrock arms use their OWN keys (`anthropic_cache` vs
      `bedrock_cache_messages`); a test pins that the Bedrock arm never receives a top-level
      `cache_control`, since Bedrock rejects it outright.
- [x] SINGLE-TURN paths are unchanged, proven by a captured request diff that is byte-identical before
      and after — this is the regression this change could plausibly cause.
- [x] The cost effect is MEASURED on a real multi-turn agentic run, before and after, and recorded.
      A narrowly-scoped live run is sufficient and is preferred over any eval sweep.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the Config-read
      and env-vars drift gates both pass.
baseline.summary: Agentic message tail is re-sent uncached every turn: O(N^2) input cost, invisible to our telemetry

## Summary

`terraform plan` could not run at all against `infra/terraform`. `templatefile()` interpolates the WHOLE file (comments included) as HCL, so unescaped `${...}` in `user_data.sh` **comments** broke every terraform operation on the box:

    Call to function "templatefile" failed: ./user_data.sh:92,24-25: Invalid character;
    This character is not used within the language., and 3 other diagnostic(s).

## Root cause

Commit `ef1a7e66a65d` ("Gate standalone shell scripts with ShellCheck", `rebar-ticket: fe4e-54a5-3c3a-4901`) added explanatory comments that escaped the FIRST mention of a bash brace expansion as `$${...}` but left the "reduces to"/"becomes" half UNESCAPED. Three sites, all inside `#` comments, referencing the bash array `PARAMS` (not a template variable): `user_data.sh:92:14`, `:92:30`, `:111:46`. `main.tf:63` declares exactly one template variable, `data_volume_id`; the four `${data_volume_id}` sites are legitimate and must stay unescaped.

Class: **regression** — `terraform plan` ran green before `ef1a7e66a65d` and failed after, on an otherwise-untouched config. `caused_by fe4e-54a5-3c3a-4901`.

## Fix (LANDED)

Fix commit `13e2ea6decc9` (`rebar-ticket: dd30-f10d-69f3-4c36`), an ancestor of `origin/main`:

1. `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` — reworded the three comment sites so no unescaped `${` remains
   and the explanation still reads correctly.
2. `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py` (new) — declared-variable-aware regression guard that
   escape-aware-scans every `templatefile()` template against its call's variable map and fails
   on any interpolation naming an undeclared root. ShellCheck cannot catch this class.
3. `Makefile` — guard wired into `make lint` (`Makefile:312`).
4. `tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py` — RED/GREEN/mutation coverage (19 passed).

Full RCA, discriminating experiments, and re-verification evidence are in the ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The three broken comment sites carry no unescaped `${`; the four legitimate
      `${data_volume_id}` sites (`:25,:28,:53,:56`) are intact. Codebase-verifiable on
      `origin/main`: the guard exits 0.
- [x] A regression guard rejects an unescaped `${` in any `templatefile()`-consumed file, wired
      into `make lint`. Codebase-verifiable: `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py` +
      `Makefile:312` + `tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py` (19 passed).
- [x] `terraform plan` / `templatefile()` renders the template cleanly (P1 breakage gone).
      [non-codebase] Re-verified today: real `terraform` v1.15.8 renders `origin/main`'s file
      (exit 0) and the reported `Invalid character` diagnostic reproduces only on the pre-fix
      file. Evidence in the re-verification comment.
- [x] LIVE `terraform apply` — DEFERRED to an operator-supervised deploy window (NOT run; not
      claimed as executed). [non-codebase] Out of scope for this `templatefile()` CODE bug and
      not runnable autonomously: a clean apply currently shares one physical apply with the
      `value_wo` secrets migration on `ssm.tf`, which would overwrite prod SecureString values
      with `CHANGEME`. Tracked on `polonium-deceptive-antelope` (f268-32ae-4ea9-42fb) and the
      value_wo cutover `097b-de23-bf12-4c38`. Re-scoped (not `--force`d) so the landed code fix
      closes on its own merit.

## Note

The agent that found this deliberately did NOT edit `user_data.sh` to unblock itself — it feeds production `user_data` and belonged in its own reviewed change. That change is `13e2ea6decc9`.

# Tier-2: native cross-platform scheduler registration for the enrichment drain

## Context
Follow-on to the cross-ticket overlap epic (only-crave-art). v1 ships Tier 1 only (opportunistic detached drain). Tier 2 adds a `rebar maintenance start`-style command that registers a recurring drain with the native platform scheduler, for repos that are not actively touched (Tier 1 goes stale when nobody runs rebar).

Prior art: `git maintenance start` abstracts over four schedulers behind `--scheduler=auto|crontab|systemd-timer|launchctl|schtasks` — launchd on macOS (so credentials/API keys resolve — the documented reason to avoid cron there), schtasks on Windows, systemd-timer-else-cron on Linux. Register hourly/daily/weekly timers, random minute per client (avoid fleet stampede on the shared remote), full binary path baked in, and split `register` (config-only) from `start` (installs timers).

## Why deferred
Prove the daemon-free Tier-1 model works first. Tier 2 is the most code (four-backend abstraction) for the narrowest case (dormant repos).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar maintenance start` registers a recurring enrichment drain via the platform-appropriate scheduler (launchd/schtasks/systemd-timer/cron, `auto`-selected).
- [ ] hourly/daily/weekly timers, random minute per client, absolute binary path baked in.
- [ ] `register` (config-only) vs `start` (installs timers) are separate; a `stop`/`unregister` cleanly removes them.
- [ ] macOS uses launchd (not cron) so the drain can resolve the API key.
baseline.summary: Tier-2: native cross-platform scheduler registration for the enrichment drain

## Problem

A completion criterion backed by a file that genuinely exists can be banked met=false because the verifier never obtains that file.

`src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py` (origin/main) enforces **one governed action per model response**: line 124 holds `acted_steps: set[int]`, and lines 152-156 claim the step before dispatch — the first governed call in a response wins, and every other governed call in the same response returns `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` (line 154) **without being executed**. Nothing re-executes the loser and nothing carries its result forward.

The cost is not one round trip, it is the criterion's evidence: the finite boundary at lines 166-172 counts **responses** (`current_evidence_steps`, line 162), so a response whose only useful call was suppressed still burns one of the three. Three such responses bank `met=false` via `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE` against a file that is present and correct.

## Evidence this is real (99d3 disproof rig, artifacts on 99d3)

Oracle 2 ran the **unmodified shipped policy** — no injection — over a six-criterion manifest against a disposable fixture in which every criterion is genuinely TRUE. In **4/4 trials** the model batched at run_step 1, a `read_file` for the c1 target lost the batch, and c1 was banked `met=false` carrying the bounded-fallback evidence string. Oracle 4 showed the benign contrast: when alternative tools still work the model recovers unaided (3/3 met=true), which is why the defect is intermittent in production rather than constant.

## Constraint on the fix (measured counter-evidence)

Rewording the notice to instruct a retry was tested and **regressed**: suppressed-call counts rose 6 -> 12 -> 49 across matched trials and one trial died `UsageLimitExceeded` with no verdict recorded at all. Any remedy that depends on the model *choosing* to re-issue inherits that risk. The remedy must be mechanical.

## Approach

Make the mutual exclusion **per kind, not per response**. The invariant that actually protects the design is that a verdict record must not share a response with evidence gathering (COMMIT discipline) — not that two read-only file reads must not share one. Concretely, replace the `acted_steps: set[int]` claim with a per-step *kind* claim:

- A response's first governed call claims the step as `evidence` or `record`.
- Further **evidence** calls in a step already claimed as `evidence` **execute normally** and
  return real repository content.
- A **record** in a step claimed by anything, and **evidence** in a step claimed by a
  `record`, keep returning `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` exactly as today.

This is the limiting case of "re-execute the suppressed call": the call is never suppressed, so recovery costs **zero** extra round trips rather than one. The finite boundary is untouched — `current_evidence_steps` is a set of steps, so N evidence calls in one response still consume exactly one evidence response. No prompt text, tool schema, notice constant, workflow key, or public surface changes; `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` keeps its current wording so the measured retry-storm lever is not pulled.

## Experimental protocol (results recorded as a ticket comment before landing)

Two arms on the identical Oracle-2 rig (real policy, real `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`, real `completion_verifier.md`, bedrock sonnet-4-6, temperature 0.0), differing only in which `src` tree is imported:

- Arm A = origin/main policy (baseline). Arm B = patched policy.
- N=4 trials per arm. Per trial record: governed call count, suppressed count, run steps,
  verdicts, and any criterion banked `met=false`.
- The fix is proven only if Arm B eliminates the false `met=false` on c1 while its governed
  call count and step count do not exceed Arm A's, and no trial exhausts its budget.

If the experiment does not show that, the change is not landed and the outcome is recorded here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A held-out live oracle running the **unmodified** shipped policy reproduces a criterion
      banked `met=false` whose backing file exists and satisfies it, caused solely by a
      governed evidence call that lost its response batch (baseline arm, >=4/4 trials).
- [x] With the change, the same oracle on the same fixture banks that criterion `met=true` in
      every trial (>=4/4), citing real file content.
- [x] Arm B's mean governed-call count and mean run-step count are **not greater** than Arm A's,
      and no Arm B trial raises `UsageLimitExceeded`.
- [x] A deterministic unit test (no LLM) asserts that two `read_file` calls in one `run_step`
      both return real content, that `record_criterion_verdict` sharing a step with evidence
      still receives `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE`, that evidence sharing a step with a record still
      receives it, and that N evidence calls in one step consume exactly one of the three
      evidence responses.
- [x] `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE`, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE`, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_NOTICE`,
      `ALL_CRITERIA_BANKED_NOTICE`, the tool schemas, the reviewer prompt, and the CLI/MCP/
      library surfaces are unchanged.
- [x] Existing completion tests, lint, typecheck, and full CI pass.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier false unmet: suppressed governed read is never recovered

## Context
RP-01 proposes replacing Rebar’s bespoke structured-output orchestration with authoritative Pydantic AI seams. The replacement is not behavior-preserving by default: historical bugs encode hard-won behavior around deterministic repair and extraction, refusal/truncation handling, retry and tool/request limits, per-operation output budgets, provider fallback, usage accounting, telemetry, and failure taxonomy. Before RP-01 can be approved or ticketized, reconstruct the behavioral contract from both ticket history and the existing test suite and exercise the worktree virtualenv’s resolved Pydantic AI distribution. A behavior may be preserved or intentionally changed, but no observed delta may be accidental or left to the implementer.

The checkout-local probe path is `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-probe.py`. The entire `.joe-janitor/` archive is intentionally excluded from repository snapshots, so an attested-source reviewer cannot see this path; use the existing local file when present and create it at that exact path if absent. The worktree virtualenv resolves `pydantic-ai-slim` to exactly 1.107.2, verified with `python -c "import importlib.metadata; print(importlib.metadata.version('pydantic-ai-slim'))"`; the probe must print and record that resolved version rather than infer it from the repository’s `>=1.107,<2` range.

## Plan
- Deduplicate ticket-derived scenarios with behavioral cases from the structured runner, failure-matrix, budget, timeout, and agent-call seam test suites.
- Record each scenario’s current observable behavior and its authoritative ticket/test evidence.
- Continue or create the checkout-local `.joe-janitor/rp01-pydantic-native-probe.py` to exercise Pydantic AI 1.107.2 native output, prompted output, output retry, usage limits, FallbackModel predicates, provider errors, truncation/refusal, telemetry, and artifact-capture feasibility without live model calls.
- Classify each scenario as preserve, intentionally change, or requiring an explicit maintainer decision; do not infer an invariant from the current implementation alone.
- Record the resulting evidence and experiment outputs in the local `.joe-janitor/` recovery archive and summarize the decision matrix on this ticket.

## Verification
This is an investigation task. baseline.description:
## Context
Legacy failure handling counts low-level physical noise (nested per-call retries) and has no endpoint-failure fuse that distinguishes an exhausted logical operation from its physical attempts; the only breaker today is the blast-radius mass-mutation guard `classify.check_blast_radius`, a different concern that is retained. The approved new scoped fuse must stop only demonstrably unhealthy scopes without terminating work that historical jobs completed.

## Outcome
Implement an endpoint/provider finite-pass fuse over normalized coordinator outcomes. Endpoint opens after three consecutive eligible exhausted logical outcomes across at least two tickets; provider additionally requires the failing outcomes to span >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider. Matching success resets consecutive state.

## Plan
1. Count only exhausted logical outcomes eligible under the failure policy. Never count physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, or opaque diagnostic text.
2. Track endpoint consecutive outcomes and distinct tickets. Track provider scope only when failures span >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider.
3. Reset matching consecutive state on success; independent scopes retain their own state and continue.
4. Preserve direct authoritative credential, configuration, quota, rate, issue, endpoint, tenant, provider, and global stop/defer behavior without inferring scope from text.
5. When open, return explicit scope/reason/`retry_not_before` metadata; do not execute matching remaining plans.

## Testing
Sequence tables pin threshold boundaries, exclusions, reset, two-ticket / two-distinct-endpoint requirements, and independent scopes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Endpoint fuse opens only after three consecutive eligible exhausted outcomes across at least two tickets.
- [x] Provider fuse additionally requires the failing outcomes to span >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider.
- [x] A matching success resets the consecutive state.
- [x] Physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, and opaque diagnostics never increment inferred counters.
- [x] Independent scopes continue when another scope opens.
- [x] Open-fuse outcomes include exact scope, reason, and `retry_not_before`.

## Out of scope
Production routing, batch tallies, and historical replay integration.
## Fuse scope, eligibility & counter semantics (grounds E2/G6)
No new "family" concept — grounded entirely in existing types and the S3 T1 coordinator (now landed).
- **Endpoint / provider.** *Endpoint* = one concrete provider instance an op is dispatched to (a single Jira base URL/site), the unit `operation_outcome.FailureScope.endpoint` already denotes; *provider* = the vendor behind >=1 endpoints (`FailureScope.provider`).
- **Attribution.** `coordinator.TicketOutcome` carries `identity`, `disposition`, `failure_scope` but no endpoint id; the `(provider, endpoint)` identity for an outcome is resolved from the coordinator's `locate(identity)` binding mapping (the per-ticket binding it dispatched against). The fuse keys inferred counters off that resolved identity, NEVER off diagnostic text. A direct authoritative `failure_scope` of endpoint/tenant/provider/global still stops that scope immediately (step 4), independent of the inferred counter.
- **Eligible exhausted outcome** — keyed off **budget-exhaustion provenance, not the disposition value**. The coordinator drives every transient retry through the shared per-op `retry_budget.RetryBudget`; an adapter first-attempt transient (`request_count=1`, `invocation_count=1`, `cumulative_sleep_ms=0`) is absorbed inside that retry loop and is never a pass outcome. An op is eligible only when the shared budget itself caps it: `plan_next_retry` returns `action="exhausted"` (MAX_INVOCATIONS) -> `exhausted_transient`, or `action="defer"` (would exceed `MAX_CUMULATIVE_SLEEP_MS` before MAX_INVOCATIONS) -> terminal `retryable_deferred` with `retry_not_before` and a consumed allowance (`invocation_count>1` or `cumulative_sleep_ms` at cap) — the slow/rate-limited mode that never surfaces `exhausted_transient`. The mid-loop `decide_replay(old_conclusive, budget_remaining=True)` (`replay=True`) is not a pass outcome. **Excluded**: `commit_unknown` (opaque/replay-forbidden), `recovered`, `already_satisfied`, `permanent_failure`, ticket-local 404, raw physical attempts, and any `retryable_deferred` the shared budget did not itself produce at its cap.
- **Counter durability/order.** Per-pass, in-memory, per-scope; zeroed each `reconcile.py::reconcile_once(pass_id)` pass (no durable cross-pass state, consistent with S2's fresh Observation/version). "Consecutive" is per-scope over the coordinator's deterministic dependency-ordered execution; other scopes' interleaved outcomes neither increment nor reset a scope's counter (independent scopes continue). A same-scope success (`applied`/`recovered`/`already_satisfied`) resets that scope to zero.

## Impacted sites (existing seams this change touches)
- `coordinator.py` (landed S3 T1) — `TicketOutcome`/`CoordinationReport.outcome_for`/`coordinate(...)` supply per-outcome `(identity, disposition, failure_scope)`; `locate(identity)` binding resolves the `(provider, endpoint)` identity. The fuse consumes these; `coordinate` gains fuse-defer wiring additively.
- `failure_policy.py` (landed S3 T1, 162 LOC) — `bucket_for` / `is_success` / `is_broad_scope` / `BROAD_SCOPES`; extended with the fuse-eligible-outcome predicate (budget-exhaustion provenance above). Watch 800-LOC cap.
- `retry_budget.py` — `plan_next_retry` `action in {exhausted, defer}` is the eligibility provenance; consumed read-only.
- `operation_outcome.py` — `Disposition` / `FailureScope` vocab, consumed unchanged.
- `pass_fuse.py` (new) — the per-pass scoped fuse state machine and open/defer decision.
baseline.summary: RP-03 S3 T2 — Implement the scoped finite-pass fuse

baseline.description:
## Problem

MCP tracker `claim` fails on the on-box server with:

```
no certified plan-review attestation (signature: foreign_key; this
environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature)
```

The MCP container is KEY-LESS for op-cert signing.

`rebar._opcert_signing.resolve` picks the op-cert key in this order:

1. a context-local startup binding (`rebar._opcert_binding.current_binding`),
2. the `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` env override,
3. the `<tracker>/.opcert-key` genesis file.

On the live container none of the three yields a key:

- `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` is UNSET,
- `<tracker>/.opcert-key` is ABSENT (tracker is `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`),
- the startup binding, composed by `mcp_server.compose_startup_opcert_binding`
  from `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, is threaded as a
  ContextVar around serving (`rebar._mcp_health.run_mcp`) and is not observed on
  the tool-call path that signs.

`rebar.signing` states the consequence directly: a key-less environment can only ever report `unsigned` / `foreign_key`.

The Ed25519 key file IS already bind-mounted read-only at `/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key` by BOTH launch paths (verified present, 411 bytes, in the live container). Only the env var that points at it is missing.

## Scope

Both launch paths are affected, not just one:

- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` `mcp:` service mounts the key and sets
  `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` and `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, but NOT
  `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`. (The `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` already in that file
  belongs to the `opcert:` service, a different service.)
- the `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` blue-green `mcp_run_new` `docker run` has
  the same omission. This is the path that actually serves `/mcp`.

`test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service` pins docker-run/compose parity in the compose-to-run direction, so fixing only the blue-green run would silently diverge the two. Fix both, keeping compose the source of truth.

## Fix

Set `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key` in the compose `mcp:` service environment and as a matching `-e` flag on the blue-green `docker run`. The mount already exists, so no new secret, mount, or terraform change is needed. The env override is thread- and context-independent, so unlike the ContextVar binding it holds on every tool-call path.

`REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` STAYS. It is load-bearing twice over: it populates `cfg.identity.signing_key` for authorship signatures, and it is one of the two required inputs to `compose_startup_opcert_binding` (absent it, the startup binding is skipped entirely). This change adds a fallback beside it, it does not replace it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The compose `mcp:` service environment sets
      `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH: "/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key"`. Checked by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py -k compose_mcp_service`.
- [ ] The blue-green `docker run` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` passes
      `-e REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key`. Checked by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py`.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the blue-green `docker run` command line carries
      that flag with that exact value, and turns RED when the flag is removed
      (mutation-checked by deleting the flag and re-running
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py`).
- [ ] `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` remains set on both launch paths. Checked by
      `grep -n REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`.
- [ ] The repo gates stay green: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, and
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` -- the real-subprocess
  blue-green suite. It stubs the box binaries onto PATH, runs the shipped
  `autodeploy.sh`, and asserts against the recorded `docker run` command line,
  so the new assertion binds the shipped bash rather than a copy of it.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` -- the static on-box infra
  contract, re-run to confirm the compose edit breaks nothing.
- Mutation check: delete the `-e REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=...` line from
  `mcp_run_new` and confirm the new test FAILS, then restore it and confirm it
  passes. A test that stays green under that deletion is worthless and must be
  rewritten.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
  `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, and
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` for the repo gates.

## Non-goals

No terraform. No new secret or mount. No change to the ContextVar startup binding mechanism, which is a separate hardening question.
baseline.summary: Set REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH for the on-box MCP container

baseline.description:
## Context
A first-class `identity` entity on rebar's event machinery, modeled on the `session_log` / `code_review` exemption pattern: gate / lifecycle / graph / Jira-sync exempt. It holds a display name, an email, a list of provider mappings, and a list of public keys, keyed by an opaque rebar ticket id. This is the foundational data structure the rest of the epic builds on (event `author_id`, authorship attestations, key-rotation eras, Jira accountId mapping).

## Why
Authorship certification and provider-neutral user mapping both need one durable home for "who a contributor is" that is not itself dispatchable work. Reusing the ticket substrate (like `session_log`) gives event-sourcing, replication, and `show`/`search` for free without polluting the dependency graph or Jira sync.

## What
Introduce `identity` as a new exempt ticket-type, a create path, and a self-identity config pointer.

### 1. Register `identity` as an exempt ticket-type (mirror session_log/code_review)
Add the type at EVERY site the existing exempt types appear (grounded, verified file:line list — omitting any one leaves a seam silently un-patched):
- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` `$defs/ticket_type` enum — SOURCE OF TRUTH.
- `src/rebar/types.py` is GENERATED — regenerate via `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`
  (never hand-edit); confirm `TicketType` now includes `identity`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:34` `_TYPES` tuple (accepts `create`), AND
  `:41` `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES` (so create emits no spurious no-file_impact nudge).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:23` `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES` (drop from graph/health).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py:13` `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:26` `_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES` (the shared constant
  the three per-ticket gates check_ac/clarity_check/quality_check consult).
- `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:118` inline `("bug","session_log","code_review")`
  tuple in `claim_gate_check()` (the plan-review START-WORK gate on claim/transition).
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:99` inline `("session_log","code_review")`
  tuple in the completion-verification close-gate pre-check.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:563` inline drift_refresh guard AND the
  `workflow_ops.py:79` exempt tuple.
None of these inline tuples delegate to `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES`, so each is a discrete edit. Excluded from `ready`/`next_batch`/default `list` follows structurally from the graph exemption (same mechanism as `session_log`). Recommended: where practical, route the new inline tuples through one shared constant to prevent future drift (implementer's discretion; not required by AC).

### 2. Create path (`rebar identity create` + library + MCP)
A single CREATE event mints an identity carrying:
- `name`: str (display name)   - `email`: str
- `mappings`: list of `{"provider": str, "external_id": str}`. `provider` is an
  OPEN lowercase-string vocabulary (well-known `jira`/`github`/`gitea`; not a
  closed enum). `external_id` is the provider's opaque stable id (NEVER an email).
  CLI: repeatable `--mapping <provider>:<external_id>` (first colon splits;
  `external_id` may contain colons).
- `keys`: list of OpenSSH authorized-keys public-key line strings
  (`"ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."`). The key-type is embedded in the line itself; NO
  separate `algorithm` field (avoids duplicating/desyncing it). The foundation
  attest scheme name is `sshsig`; the key-type token is parsed from the line by
  downstream verify (bde5).
`show` renders name/email/mappings/keys. (The provider vocabulary and authorized-keys key format are recorded as an ADR in sibling task 4b5b; this ticket adopts the above defaults.)

### 3. Self-identity config pointer (`.rebar/current_identity`)
- **Path**: `.rebar/current_identity` (`.rebar/` is already git-ignored via
  `.gitignore:11`; mirrors `.rebar/current_session_log`, see
  `src/rebar/_commands/session_log.py`). No gitignore edit needed.
- **Format**: JSON `{"identity_id": "<ticket_id>"}` (extra keys tolerated).
- **Write path**: `rebar identity use <id>` writes the pointer; `rebar identity
  create --self` writes it to the just-created identity in the same invocation.
- **Resolution — `resolve_current_identity() -> Optional[str]`**:
  1. Pointer file present AND names an existing `identity` ticket -> that id.
  2. Else match `git config user.email` (exact, case-insensitive) vs identity
     `email` fields.
- **Fallbacks (all return `None`; identity is opt-in so unauthenticated is a
  valid state, never an error)**: git email unset/unconfigured -> `None`;
  the `git config` subprocess errors (git missing, OSError, non-zero exit,
  timeout) -> `None` (caught, not propagated); zero identities match -> `None`;
  >=2 match -> `None` + a WARNING naming the ambiguity; pointer names a
  deleted/absent identity -> fall through to git-email match, else `None`.
- **Export side-effect (accepted)**: adding `identity` to
  `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES` hides identity tickets from default NDJSON export,
  opt-in via the existing `--include-session-logs` flag — same posture as
  `session_log`; acceptable for this ticket (no new flag).

## Scope
In: type registration at all listed sites, the create path (CLI/lib/MCP), `show` rendering, the pointer write + resolver + fallbacks. Out: event `author_id` (4e9d), authorship signing (bde5), key rotation (e165), Jira mapping (264f/2f13), enforcement (3183).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `identity` is registered at all listed sites and is exempt from
  lifecycle/gates/graph/Jira-sync (mirrors session_log); a test asserts an
  `identity` ticket is absent from `ready`/`next_batch`/default `list` and that
  `check_ac`/`clarity_check`/`quality_check` return pass for it.
- [ ] A create path (`rebar identity create` + `rebar.create_identity` + MCP)
  mints an identity in one CREATE carrying name, email, mappings, keys; a test
  round-trips create then asserts `rebar show <id> --output llm` (structured
  JSON) contains all four fields with the created values.
- [ ] `resolve_current_identity(*, repo_root=None) -> str | None` (keyword-only `repo_root`) reads `.rebar/current_identity`
  (`{"identity_id": ...}`) when present, else matches `git config user.email`
  case-insensitively; a test asserts (a) pointer hit, (b) git-email default hit,
  (c) each fallback (no email / subprocess error / zero match / multiple match /
  dangling pointer) returns `None` without raising.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/types.py` (regenerated)
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (_TYPES + _FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES + create)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`,
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` + `workflow_ops.py`
- new identity module (create path + resolver) + CLI/lib/MCP wiring
baseline.summary: identity: `identity` entity + ticket-type (attributes, exemptions, creation)

## Target
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — **799 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (1 lines of headroom).

One line of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

# Adopt the DCO: declarative Gerrit enforcement, contributor docs, agent sign-off policy

## Why

rebar has no inbound-IP mechanism (no DCO, no CLA). Both external reports and peer convergence recommend DCO over CLA: Qt's CLA is the stated reason it cannot accept PRs, and OpenStack replaced its CLA with the DCO for all contributions (TC resolution 2025-05-20, https://governance.openstack.org/tc/resolutions/20250520-replace-the-cla-with-dco-for-all-contributions.html) explicitly to lower the barrier, directing enforcement into Gerrit itself — the server rejects an unsigned push at `refs/for/*` time, zero new infrastructure. Gerrit documents `receive.requireSignedOffBy` as a per-project `project.config` key (https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-project-config.html#receive.requireSignedOffBy — inheritable, NOT site-only); live verification below guards against placement surprises anyway.

Sequencing note (resolves the file-existence review findings): `docs/your-first-change.md` does not exist at plan time — it is created by story **fat-leaflike-canary**, which this story `depends_on` (edge recorded in the store). Every edit this story makes to that file executes only after that story lands; in dependency order the target exists.

## What

- **Declarative config path (never a manual push):** add `requireSignedOffBy = true` to the `[receive]` section of `infra/gerrit/project.config` and roll out via the existing `setup-project.sh` flow to `refs/meta/config` (JoeOakhartNava admin identity). Rationale: `setup-project.sh` overwrites `project.config` on every run; a one-off manual push would be silently reverted. **Rollback:** revert the line, re-run `setup-project.sh` — documented in a comment beside the key.
- **Two distinct sign-off rules (resolves the identity-mismatch finding):**
  1. **Agent commits (RebarBotNava / `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` committer):** trailer is exactly `Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>` — the responsible human's real name with his registered plus-addressed mailbox (routes to the human; kernel practice accepts plus-addresses; the certifier is the human, satisfying DCO 1.1). Documented in CLAUDE.md's commit guidance verbatim.
  2. **e2e test scripts** (`infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`, `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh`, `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh` — all push to `refs/for/*` and would be rejected post-flip): each script adds `-s` to its `git commit` invocations so the sign-off is the script's OWN configured test identity (a hardcoded human trailer would mismatch the test committer). No other trailer engineering.
- **Automation inventory (decision rule):** enumerate commit-creating automation with `rg -l "git commit" infra/ scripts/ .github/ Makefile` at execution; the three e2e scripts above are the known set; anything newly found is updated the same way (add `-s`) or ticketed via discovered_from.
- CONTRIBUTING.md "Sign your work (DCO)" section, moby/Docker template (https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md "Sign your work"): link developercertificate.org, show the trailer, `git commit -s`, real-name requirement, push-time rejection note, Envoy-style "fixing DCO" note (amend/rebase re-signing), the shepherded-patch two-trailer rule (contributor's own sign-off required in the patch; shepherd adds theirs on amend — coordinated with the PR-posture story), **and a one-line CLA decision record: "rebar uses the DCO, not a CLA; a CLA would be adopted only if Nava counsel requires rights beyond Apache-2.0 §5 + DCO"** (the durable in-repo record of that decision).
- Cross-link retarget INTO `docs/your-first-change.md` (after fat-leaflike-canary lands — see sequencing note): point the tutorial's interim developercertificate.org link at the new CONTRIBUTING DCO section.
- **Migration order (strict, and provable from git history, not tracker artifacts):** commits land in this order — (1) docs (CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md/tutorial retarget); (2) e2e-script `-s` fixes; (3) the `infra/gerrit/project.config` flag + `setup-project.sh` rollout. Because all three are commits in this repo, the order is verifiable post-hoc: the commit touching `infra/gerrit/project.config` must be a descendant of the commits touching the e2e scripts and docs (`git log --oneline -- <path>` comparison). No window where agent/bot pushes fail.
- **Post-flip failure runbook** (one paragraph in the CONTRIBUTING DCO section): rejected push → `git commit --amend -s --no-edit`, re-push; agent-tooling regression → roll back the flag while fixing.
- Flip GitHub's "require sign-off on web-based commits" on the mirror (one settings toggle; belt-and-braces).
- Peer-norm citation for the human-signs policy: Kubernetes AI-review governance (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/github-management/ai-code-review-tools.md) — cited as supporting practice, not load-bearing authority (the policy stands on DCO 1.1's own terms).

## Scope

IN: `infra/gerrit/project.config` + setup-project.sh rollout, rollback note, CONTRIBUTING.md DCO section (incl. CLA record + failure runbook), CLAUDE.md agent-trailer guidance, e2e-script `-s` fixes, tutorial cross-link retarget (post-dependency), GitHub web-signoff toggle, live verification. OUT: CLA machinery; the probot/dco GitHub app (acts on PR checks; PRs here are answered/closed by the lockdown workflow the PR-posture story lands); retrofitting existing history (DCO applies to new commits only — kernel/OpenStack precedent); CLAUDE.local.md (gitignored, not a reviewable artifact).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Config flag present and rolled out — prove: `grep -A5 "\[receive\]" infra/gerrit/project.config | grep -q "requireSignedOffBy = true"`; the rollback note exists — prove: `grep -qi "rollback" infra/gerrit/project.config`.
- [ ] Live verification: an unsigned push to `refs/for/main` is rejected (server message captured in the commit message or a `docs/` note) and the same commit re-pushed after `git commit --amend -s` is accepted.
- [ ] e2e scripts sign their commits — prove, per file: `grep -q "commit .*-s\b\|commit -s" infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`; same grep for `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh` and `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh` (three separate checks); one e2e suite run passes post-flip.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md DCO section — prove: `grep -q "developercertificate.org" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "commit -s" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -qi "not a CLA" CONTRIBUTING.md` (the CLA decision record); `grep -qi "amend" CONTRIBUTING.md` (fix-up/runbook).
- [ ] CLAUDE.md names the exact agent trailer — prove: `grep -q "Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>" CLAUDE.md`.
- [ ] Migration order provable from history — prove: the commit touching `infra/gerrit/project.config` is a descendant of the latest commits touching the three e2e scripts and the CONTRIBUTING DCO section (compare `git log` for the paths).
- [ ] Tutorial retarget done after dependency — prove: `grep -q "Sign your work\|DCO" docs/your-first-change.md` links the CONTRIBUTING section (executes post fat-leaflike-canary).
- [ ] GitHub web-signoff on — prove: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar --jq .web_commit_signoff_required` = true.
