baseline.description:
# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: E1 — Force measurement provenance into attested evidence

## Why
Every prompt/detector change in this epic must be measured, or we repeat dso's mistake of uncalibrated drift. This is the gating foundation: no prompt story merges without a passing eval.

## What
Build eval specs for the four-pass code-review prompts (base, overlays, verify) in the existing rebar eval harness. Seed two families from dso's documented corpus:
- NO-FIRE cases (must not flag): sourced-bash functions, subdirectory scripts, list-form subprocess,
  Rule-5 structural greps on declarative artifacts, moved-code renames with callers updated,
  already-public config reads, valid observable-postcondition tests.
- SEEDED-DEFECT recall cases (must flag): tautological test, dangling deletion, asymmetric signature
  change, hallucinated API, VCS conflict marker, ticket scope drift.
Deterministic gating scorers (a deterministic scorer GATES; an llm-judge only REPORTS).

## Scope
Eval specs + fixtures under src/rebar/llm/evals and eval_specs; no gate behavior change here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Eval specs exist for base, verify, and at least the tests+security overlays.
- [ ] No-fire and recall case families seeded from the dso incidents listed above.
- [ ] At least one deterministic gating scorer per spec; specs pass on the current gate as baseline.
- [ ] The nit-framing experiment result (positive-framing recall lift) captured as a case.
baseline.summary: Eval foundation for the four-pass code-review prompts

baseline.description:
## Why
rebar records cross-cutting review-gate design in ADRs (plan-review's novelty rising floor is ADR 0008). The code-review novelty convergence mechanism — its divergence from plan-review (per-citation region gate; typed local/Gerrit keyspaces; content-addressed resilient region detection), the reuse boundary (shared kernel primitives vs gate-specific orchestration), and the deliberate NON-additions — needs a durable ADR + docs so future work does not re-litigate or accidentally fork the novelty definition.

## What
Write **`docs/adr/0037-code-review-novelty-convergence.md`** (status Accepted — it documents DECISIONS that are IMPLEMENTED on this epic's stack) and cross-link the docs. The ADR documents, each citing its backing implementation module so a reader can verify it:

- **Reuse the novelty sub-call + `rising_floor_drop`** — the shared kernel primitives
  (`review_kernel.verify.novelty_model` / `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` / `reshape_novelties`,
  `review_kernel.decide.novelty` / `rising_floor_drop`) reused UNCHANGED. Code-review-specific
  orchestration: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty` +
  `apply_region_gated_floor`, the `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md` prompt + the
  `code-novelty` reviewer id, and the `code_review_novelty` contract registered in
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py`.
- **The new `region_gated_floor` conjunct + its tri-state fail-safe (UNKNOWN == raise)** —
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py` (constants `REGION_UNCHANGED` / `REGION_CHANGED` /
  `REGION_UNKNOWN` + the detector); the floor drops iff `rising_floor_drop(...)` AND region is
  `REGION_UNCHANGED`, and CHANGED/UNKNOWN always raise (fail-safe direction).
- **Surfaced-only prior set** — the reader `latest_code_review_result`
  (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py`) returns only the persisted `blocking` + `advisory`
  buckets, so a dropped finding never re-enters the novelty prior set (the code-review counterpart
  of child c3e4 / bug old-frilly-plankton).
- **Permanent low-impact drop = the intended compromise; the priority floor is the escape hatch.**
  Define "permanent" PRECISELY: the drop persists across RE-REVIEWS FOR THE SAME KEY (session or
  change) — it does NOT reset per review the way plan-review's floor re-scores each run — because
  the surfaced-only reader excludes a dropped finding from the prior set, so on recurrence it scores
  as NOVEL and is dropped again (as long as it stays low-priority + region-unchanged). Permanence is
  WITHIN one keyspace, not cross-key. The priority floor (`verify.novelty_priority_floor`) is the
  escape hatch: a higher-impact finding is never eligible, so it keeps surfacing. Trust the priority
  score — no categorical criterion exemption.
- **Typed session/change keyspaces, and why local must NOT seed a change's first Gerrit review** —
  `session:<id>` (local, `code-review: session:{id}`) vs `change:<id>` (Gerrit,
  `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}`); the reader (`latest_code_review_result`) matches only
  its own title scheme, so the keyspaces are disjoint and a prior LOCAL review can never seed a
  change's FIRST Gerrit review.
- **Content-addressed region detection and its resilience to rebase/force-push** — the artifact
  stores `{path: sha256}` (reusing `plan_review.attest._hash_file`, computed in
  `code_review/sidecar.py::reviewed_file_hashes`); comparison keys on CONTENT, not a reachable
  commit, so it survives a rebase/force-push. File-level in v1; line-level deferred.
- **Explicit NON-additions (AC2).** Record the decision to add NO "dso-style
  arbiter/relation-taxonomy/oscillation-loop", DEFINING those terms inline so the rejection is
  evaluable: a **DSO-style arbiter** = a standalone decision/signal orchestrator that ADJUDICATES
  between competing findings/signals; a **relation-taxonomy** = a typed model of relationships
  BETWEEN findings (duplicates/supersedes/refines/…); an **oscillation-loop** = a detector that
  tracks a finding surfacing→dropping→resurfacing across runs to break cycles. The ADR records WHY
  the lightweight novelty floor suffices instead: a permanent, priority-gated drop of novel
  low-impact findings on unchanged regions monotonically narrows the surfaced set across
  patchsets without modeling oscillation or inter-finding relationships — so the heavier machinery
  buys no demonstrated benefit for added failure modes. This positively discharges the epic's
  original oscillation/convergence-signal criterion as a DESIGN decision, not a deferral.

Also update the docs to cross-link: **`docs/review-kernel.md`** (its "Code-review consumer" section — documenting the novelty convergence behavior: carryover labeling, region-gated drop, keying, resilience) and **`docs/reuse-surface.md`** (pointing the shared kernel primitives at the code-review-specific region-gate seam).

## Scope
- `docs/adr/0037-code-review-novelty-convergence.md` (NEW), `docs/review-kernel.md` (the
  "Code-review consumer" section — the code-review gate doc), and `docs/reuse-surface.md`.
- Documents the IMPLEMENTED behavior landed by c639 / 3bff / e51b + the c3e4 surfaced-only fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ADR 0037 captures the design decisions above, INCLUDING the deliberate divergence from
      plan-review's whole-artifact floor (the per-citation region gate), each element citing its
      backing implementation module.
- [ ] ADR 0037 records the explicit decision to add NO dso-style arbiter / relation-taxonomy /
      oscillation-loop (terms DEFINED inline) and why the lightweight novelty floor suffices.
- [ ] ADR 0037 defines "permanent" drop precisely (within-key, via the surfaced-only prior set) and
      how it diverges from plan-review's per-review re-scoring.
- [ ] `docs/review-kernel.md` (Code-review consumer section) documents the novelty convergence
      behavior (carryover labeling, region-gated drop, keying, resilience).
- [ ] The docs cross-link the shared kernel primitives vs the code-review-specific region gate
      (`docs/reuse-surface.md`).
baseline.summary: ADR + docs: code-review novelty convergence (mirror plan-review ADR 0008)

## Problem
`tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py::test_mcp_startup_sweeps_before_run` fails intermittently under CI's pytest-randomly (observed on a py3.13 shard: assertion `order == ['ensures','run']` got `['run']`, i.e. run_ensures was never called). It passes in isolation and on other py-version shards (different random seed).

## Root cause
`mcp_server.main()` only calls `run_ensures` when `os.path.isdir(_config.tracker_dir())` (src/rebar/mcp_server.py ~line 717). Under an unlucky test order a sibling test leaves cwd / tracker-dir resolution state such that `tracker_dir()` does not point at an existing dir, so the ensures sweep is silently skipped and only 'run' is recorded. The test relies on ambient cwd/config state the `repo` fixture does not fully isolate.

## Fix direction
Make the test hermetic (chdir into / point config at the fixture's repo within the test, or assert the tracker-dir precondition) OR make main()'s sweep decision independent of ambient cwd. Root-cause the isolation leak; do not paper over with a retry.

## Impact
Not caused by RP-06 code_review/plan_review changes — surfaced while landing RP-06 S3 (change 2047); the failing test is disjoint from those files. Pre-existing latent flake on main affecting concurrent sessions.

## Evidence — reproduced, not inferred

`fetcher._iter_pages` (the pager behind `fetcher.collect`, which builds the INBOUND SNAPSHOT the entire inbound differ runs on) terminates on a SHORT page and advances by the REQUESTED page size:

    src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:324-326
        if len(page) < page_size:
            return
        start_at += page_size

Jira Data Center silently truncates `maxResults` when it exceeds `jira.search.views.default.max` — a common hardening, and the same server behaviour already established for this codebase when the identical defect was fixed in `get_parent_map` (change 1105). A truncated FIRST page therefore reads as "that is all there is".

Measured against a client that serves 250 issues but caps every page at 20 (default `page_size=100`):

    issues recovered: 20 of 250
    CONFIRMED DEFECT: 230 issues (92%) silently lost from the inbound snapshot

## Why this is more serious than its two siblings

This is the THIRD instance of one defect class. The first was `get_parent_map` (fixed, change 1105). The second is [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` / `get_comment_map`, which lose links and comments. This one loses THE ISSUES THEMSELVES.

`collect()` feeds `_build_snapshot`, so a truncated read is not a missing attribute on a present issue — it is an issue the pass never sees at all. Every unseen bound issue is a candidate for the absence/deletion path, and every unseen unbound issue simply fails to reconcile. A run in that state reports success: it raises nothing, and "converged" is true of the 8% it looked at.

## Blast radius — wider than the DC adapter, which is why this is NOT folded into 9263

9263 is confined to `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`. This is CORE `fetcher.py`, on the shared inbound path, so a change here reaches the live Cloud bridge as well as DC. That is a different risk profile and deserves its own review and its own live verification rather than riding along on an adapter-local fix.

Cloud reaches the same lines but is not known to be affected in practice: its ceiling and `same-token-twice` cursor-stall guards target a different truncation mode, and no short-page truncation has been observed there. The fix must therefore be verified as SAFE FOR CLOUD, not merely correct for DC.

## Approach

Advance by `len(page)` and terminate only on an EMPTY page — the same correction already applied to `get_parent_map`, whose docstring records the reasoning.

One thing the `get_parent_map` fix did not have to handle and this one does: `_iter_pages` must not spin forever if a server ignores `startAt` and returns the same non-empty page indefinitely. The existing `same-token-twice` guard covers the Cloud CURSOR stall, not an OFFSET stall. Add an offset-stall guard that raises `SilentTruncationError` (the type this function already raises for truncation it refuses to hide) rather than looping.

`cap` and ceiling semantics are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — the pager's advance/terminate conditions, plus the
  offset-stall guard.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.

## Testing

- a client serving N issues while capping every page below the requested size yields ALL N (the
  reproduction above, which currently returns 20 of 250)
- an exactly-full final page followed by an empty page terminates without an extra spurious request
- a server that ignores `startAt` raises `SilentTruncationError` rather than looping forever
- `cap` still clips, and the ACLI ceiling still raises — asserted so the Cloud contract is pinned
  unchanged by this fix

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the 250-issue/20-cap reproduction recovers 250, asserted by a held-out unit test that FAILS on
      the current code
- [ ] termination is on an EMPTY page only, and the advance is by `len(page)` — read from the source
- [ ] a `startAt`-ignoring server raises `SilentTruncationError` instead of looping, asserted by test
      with a bounded-time guarantee
- [ ] the existing `cap`, ACLI-ceiling and `same-token-twice` behaviours are unchanged, each asserted
      by a test that exercises them — this touches the shared Cloud path, so "DC is fixed" is not
      sufficient evidence
- [ ] the full unit suite passes, and the live DC harness job stays green
baseline.summary: fetcher._iter_pages truncates the inbound snapshot on a short page: 92% of issues silently lost

## Summary
_has_rebar_id_label (binding_walk.py) matches ANY label with the rebar-id:/rebar-id- PREFIX, including a malformed empty 'rebar-id:' (no local id). The L10 adopt guard then stands down (treats it as identity-bound) and defers to binding-recovery — but with an empty id there is nothing to re-link, so the key is never adopted AND never bound, and bridge-fsck reports it as unbound_jira on every run. Surfaced by REB-659 (a manual 'assignee clobber' experiment carrying label 'rebar-id:'), which produced a perpetual bare-forge-tapir drift alert.

## Reproduction Steps
1. A Jira issue has label 'rebar-id:' (empty value) and no binding-store entry.
2. Run the binding walk / bridge-fsck.
3. The issue is neither adopted (L10 stands down) nor bound → perpetual unbound_jira drift.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: an empty/malformed rebar-id: marker is treated as UNMARKED (adoptable), so the key adopts (create+bind) normally.
- Actual: the empty marker counts as a binding marker → adoption stands down → the key is stranded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] _has_rebar_id_label returns True only for a WELL-FORMED marker (non-empty id after the prefix).
- [ ] A key with an empty 'rebar-id:' label is adopted (inbound create); a well-formed 'rebar-id:<id>' still stands down (no double-bind).
- [ ] Regression test in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_binding_walk.py; reconciler suite green.
baseline.summary: reconciler: malformed empty rebar-id: marker traps a Jira issue in unbound-drift limbo

## Context
ADR 0043 defines exactly two completion-evidence kinds: untagged acceptance criteria are codebase-verifiable, while criteria whose evidence inherently lives outside the repository must use the exact `[operator-attested]` tag. The current P6 deterministic lexicon only coaches on a subset of untagged operational phrases and cannot semantically inspect every criterion or detect an incorrectly applied tag. A1 `f7ee-572b-1eb0-4af8` demonstrated the gap: plan review passed a repo-level benchmark criterion without the required tag, then completion verification failed after the work was already merged.

## Approach
- Add an explicit plan-review criterion that evaluates every acceptance-criterion checkbox independently and classifies where its completion evidence can truthfully be verified.
- Preserve ADR 0043 fail-safe semantics: untagged and malformed tags remain codebase-verifiable; only the exact case-insensitive `[operator-attested]` token selects ticket-attestation evidence.
- Find both error directions: externally verifiable criteria missing the exact tag, and codebase-verifiable criteria incorrectly tagged operator-attested (which would weaken completion proof to a comment).
- Require evidence specific to the criterion, not keyword-only classification. Reuse the existing deterministic detector as candidate/coverage input where useful, but keep semantic judgment in the new criterion and leave the P6 lexicon fail-open/advisory.
- Route and document the criterion through the canonical registry, reviewer prompt/contract, criteria routing, generated criteria guide, and frozen evaluation corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The new plan-review criterion visits every `- [ ]` / `- [x]` acceptance item and returns one of two evidence kinds, `codebase-verifiable` or `operator-attested`, with criterion-specific evidence for the classification. Tier: reviewer contract/unit test plus behavioral eval.
- [x] An inherently external criterion with no tag or a malformed near-miss produces a finding whose remediation names the exact `- [ ] [operator-attested] …` syntax; an exact tag on an external criterion is accepted. Tier: prompt-contract fixtures and behavioral eval.
- [x] A codebase-verifiable criterion carrying `[operator-attested]` produces a finding explaining that ticket comments cannot substitute for repository proof; the same criterion untagged is accepted. Tier: prompt-contract fixtures and behavioral eval.
- [x] A criterion that bundles repository proof and outside-world proof is not silently assigned one evidence kind: review tells the author to split it into independently certifiable criteria. Tier: behavioral eval with a mixed-evidence fixture.
- [x] High-confidence misclassification findings participate in the normal validity × impact blocking policy, while deterministic keyword detection remains advisory/fail-open and records abstentions. Tier: policy/registry unit tests.
- [x] Registry completeness, criteria routing, reviewer resources, generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`, and author guidance describe the new check and ADR 0043 exact-tag semantics without drift. Verify with the repository generation/drift gates.
- [x] [operator-attested] A pinned multi-sample before/after evaluation over a frozen corpus that includes A1, the historical 115b/8c4f cases, codebase negatives, malformed tags, over-tagged code criteria, and mixed-evidence items meets these predeclared thresholds: 100% precision (zero false positives) on the genuine-external negative set; 100% recall on the named A1, 115b/8c4f, malformed-tag, and over-tagged-code fixtures; macro precision and recall ≥ 0.90 across the full frozen corpus; and no previously passing fixture regresses; record model/config, sample counts, per-class results, and the run artifact on this ticket.
      provenance: environment=rebar plan-review production-equivalent workflow at the ticket verified_at_sha; principal=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the frozen corpus runs through the same signed plan-review workflow and model/runtime configuration used by this repository gate
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass, including focused tests proving the completion verifier still treats untagged criteria as codebase-verifiable and exact-tag criteria as operator-attested.

## Scope
Plan-review criterion and its tests/eval/documentation only. Do not broaden the completion verifier’s trust boundary or add external-service access.
baseline.summary: Validate acceptance-criteria evidence classification in plan review

## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` currently changes up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this deliberately covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

Author the behavioral oracle RED-first. Hold out the interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases from the implementer; expose only the basic dual-read happy path. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs is expected to advance and commit both rotation representations; claiming that such a pass makes no commit would contradict the required dual-write compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- new `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (docstring only)
- focused unit/integration/CLI tests

Estimated scope: M. Depends on closed A1 through the parent story.

baseline.description:
## Status — RESCOPED + CLOSED (operator-approved 2026-07-18)

This story is closed against a **rescoped** acceptance set. It had two separable halves:

1. **A DETERMINISTIC half — DESIGNED AND BUILT.** The stratified **sample**, the frozen
   **baseline**, the **FP-control pool**, the **replay driver** (clone + REVIEW_RESULT-strip +
   manifest seams), the **pure LLM-free metrics library**, and its **golden tests**. This lives as
   WIP in the `cal-e3` worktree on branch `calib/6982-e3` (`replay_candidate.py`, `e3_metrics.py`,
   `runs/e3/sample.jsonl`, `runs/e3/baseline.jsonl`, `runs/e3/fp_control_pool.jsonl`,
   `tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py`). It is **not landed on main** — the driver's only runtime
   purpose is to drive the rejected batch (below), so landing it would ship a moot LLM-spend entry
   point. It is recorded here as documented WIP.

2. **An EXPENSIVE LLM BATCH REPLAY — PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost, and SUPERSEDED.** The
   ~450-run live gate replay (the coarse ~200-ticket single sweep PLUS the precise ~50-ticket ×3
   candidate + ×3 current fresh runs, and the `raw_verdicts.jsonl` / `transition_matrix.json` /
   `criterion_deltas.jsonl` / `fp_control.json` they would emit) is **dropped**. It is superseded
   by story **d8a5** (change **#798, MERGED**): the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder
   (`criterion_effectiveness.py`, on main), which accumulates the SAME detection / blocking-FP
   perturbation signal from real production reviews at **$0 marginal LLM cost**. Baseline **mining**
   is also dead: only ~4 `plan-v3` sidecar baselines exist against the ~200 needed — the
   `impact_model_version` bump stranded the history (which is exactly why a live replay, not a
   sidecar re-score, would have been required, and why the cost was unjustifiable).

The design record below (Why / definitions / mechanism) is retained as the account of what was
built; the Acceptance Criteria are rescoped to the delivered deterministic WIP only.

## Why

R1 (asserted-capability grounding probe) edits the Pass-1 finder rubric, so it changes what EVERY
plan review surfaces. Before any gate candidate is exposed to production, we must measure how much
it perturbs the verdicts of plans that already passed and closed cleanly. E3 was the counterfactual
replay that would produce that measurement; with E2 it was the evidence R1 is gated on.

The gate has a hard false-positive bar (`docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md` §5 / R1):
R1 FAILs if, on 30 sampled historical plans that PASSed and closed with zero post-claim edits,
>3/30 gain a new blocking finding, or the median new-advisory count rises by >1 per review; the
epic also reports a PASS→BLOCK flip rate ≤2% on the wider cleanly-closed sample.

**The design removes two confounds** (both verified in code): recall contamination (`review_plan`
re-surfaces a ticket's own prior findings via `prior_concerns`, which `emit_sidecar=False` does
not disable) and baseline drift + LLM nondeterminism. It does so with a **recall-stripped clone**
(copy the store, delete every `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` under sampled tickets, run over the clone),
a **material-fingerprint drift guard**, and a **two-tier** structure: a coarse descriptive ~200
sweep, plus a precise 30-plan FP-control that replays BOTH the candidate and the current gate fresh
(N=3, two-level median, current-vs-current null floor) to isolate the candidate's true effect.

The deterministic pieces — the reproducible stratified sample, the frozen `plan-v3` baseline, the
over-sampled 50-ticket FP-control pool, the clone/strip/manifest driver seams, and the entire pure
`e3_metrics` library (`build_matrix`, `criterion_deltas`, `tkey`, `pass_to_block_flip_rate`,
`fp_control_eval`, `fp_control_valid`) — were completed and golden-tested offline.

**Why the batch was never worth its cost.** The only thing the ~450 live gate runs add is a
one-shot snapshot of one candidate's verdict perturbation — a signal d8a5's standing recorder now
produces continuously from real reviews for free, and which mining cannot reconstruct (the
`plan-v3` bump stranded the sidecar history to ~4 rows). The operator therefore rejected the batch
replay permanently and accepted the deterministic build as the deliverable.

## Scope (delivered as WIP on `calib/6982-e3`; NOT landed on main)

- `harnesses/replay_candidate.py` — driver (`sample` / `run` / `analyze` / `--verify`), incl. the
  clone + REVIEW_RESULT-strip + manifest seams. Its `sample`/`analyze`/metrics paths are offline;
  its live `run` gate replay is the rejected batch and is NOT to be executed.
- `harnesses/e3_metrics.py` — pure, LLM-free metrics library (golden-tested).
- `runs/e3/{sample.jsonl, baseline.jsonl, fp_control_pool.jsonl}` — deterministic sample + frozen
  baseline + over-sampled FP-control pool.
- `tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py` — CI-collectable golden tests over synthetic fixtures (no LLM).
- README (E3 section) documenting the design as WIP + the batch deferral.
- NO `src/rebar` behavior change (E3 was measurement).

## Acceptance Criteria (rescoped — delivered deterministic WIP only)

- [ ] **Sample + frozen baseline BUILT and reproducible.** `runs/e3/sample.jsonl` (stratified,
  deterministic `random.Random(1729)`) satisfies the cleanly-closed filter on every row
  (`post_claim_edit_class=="none"` AND `reopen_count==0` AND `force_close==false`);
  `runs/e3/baseline.jsonl` carries a `plan-v3` `baseline_verdict ∈ {PASS,BLOCK}` +
  `material_fingerprint` per ticket; `runs/e3/fp_control_pool.jsonl` is the 50-ticket over-sampled
  FP-control pool. Built and verifiable in the `calib/6982-e3` worktree; deterministic (no LLM).
- [ ] **Pure metrics library BUILT + golden-tested.** `e3_metrics.py`'s `criterion_deltas`
  (COMPUTED `sidecar.norm_id` join), `tkey` (criteria-independent text key), `build_matrix`,
  `pass_to_block_flip_rate`, `fp_control_eval` (two-level-median candidate↔current pairing;
  `null_floor` current-vs-current; `r1_pass = new_blocking_median <= max(3, null_floor) AND
  new_advisory_median_delta <= 1`), and `fp_control_valid` (usable≥30 boundary) pass
  `pytest tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py` offline (no LLM). Built as WIP on `calib/6982-e3`.
- [ ] **Replay driver seams BUILT.** `replay_candidate.py` implements the recall-stripped clone
  (copy store + delete `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json`), the material-fingerprint drift guard, the
  over-sampling ticket-drop rule, and the manifest/candidate-build-verification write. These seams
  are present and offline-exercisable (`sample`, `analyze --verify`); the live `run` gate replay is
  the deferred batch and is NOT executed. Verified by code inspection.
- [ ] **[operator-attested] Batch replay DEFERRED — permanently rejected on cost, superseded by
  d8a5.** The live ~450-run gate replay (coarse ~200 sweep + precise ~50×3 candidate + ~50×3
  current) and its `raw_verdicts.jsonl` / `transition_matrix.json` / `criterion_deltas.jsonl` /
  `fp_control.json` outputs are intentionally NOT produced. The verdict-perturbation signal they
  would have measured is now accumulated at $0 marginal LLM cost by d8a5's standing
  `criterion_effectiveness.py` recorder (change #798, MERGED, on main), and history-mining is dead
  (~4 `plan-v3` baselines vs ~200 needed). Evidence lives outside this codebase: operator decision
  2026-07-18 + d8a5 / change #798. This AC is closed by operator attestation, not machine check.
- [ ] **Design documented as WIP.** The README E3 section records the baseline source + chosen
  round, the cleanly-closed filter, the recall-strip + fresh-both-gates design, the
  material-fingerprint drift control, the two-tier nondeterminism/cost story, and the batch
  deferral + d8a5-supersession, so the WIP status and drop rationale are auditable.

## Context / Problem

The graph loader/BFS centralization (985c-32d2-e828-4e6a, Gerrit 1708, merged 1c3e945cb8) named two behaviours as explicit helpers that had previously been inline, and the rebar code-review bot flagged both as untested. The gaps are PRE-EXISTING — the same logic was uncovered while inline — but naming them made them visible. Nothing regresses today; the risk is that a future traversal or loader refactor silently drops either behaviour with the suite still green.

## Approach

Characterization tests ONLY — no `src/rebar` change. Follow the pattern of `test_get_all_blocked_by_accumulates_targets_without_a_ticket_dir` (added by 985c in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py`): assert the behaviour that exists today so the tests pin the contract rather than propose a new one. Each new test was validated by mutating the production branch locally, observing the test go red, and reverting — the mutation results are recorded per criterion below.

### Gap 1 — the cross-level traversal refusal (`rebar.graph._graph`)

`_same_level_neighbors` confines the walk with two separate guards. The CURRENT-side guard is an inline `state.get("ticket_type", "").lower() != level` early-return on the node being expanded (`_graph.py` L251). The TARGET-side guard is the single call to `_is_at_level`, on each candidate dep (`if target and target not in visited and _is_at_level(...)`, L257). Every existing `check_cycle_at_level` test in `test_graph_cycles.py` uses a single uniform level, so the target-side guard is never exercised.

The two guards are not interchangeable, and this dictates the test shape: for an `epic → task → epic` chain the inline CURRENT-side guard alone already stops the walk, so deleting the `_is_at_level` call leaves that case still returning False. The only mutation-sensitive probe is a DIRECT cross-level edge whose far end IS the queried `source_id`: `check_cycle_at_level("task-M", "epic-B", level="epic")` where `epic-B depends_on task-M`. Today `bfs` (in `rebar.graph._relations`) accumulates nothing, so the answer is False; with the target-side `_is_at_level` deleted, `task-M` is yielded and accumulated and the answer flips to True. Both shapes get a test: the direct one pins the guard, the `epic → task → epic` hop one pins the end-to-end "a lower-level hop cannot reconnect two same-level nodes" contract.

### Gap 2 — the three tombstone-loader branches (`rebar.graph._unblock`)

All three are driven through the public `detect_newly_unblocked`, not the private `_load_states_with_tombstones`. One shared fixture shape makes each branch observable: a target ticket carrying two `depends_on` LINK events (so the blocking edges live in the TARGET's dir and survive an unreducible blocker dir), one blocker closed by the batch and one blocker tombstoned. `_was_already_unblocked` then cannot short-circuit, so the verdict turns entirely on how the tombstoned blocker's status is loaded.

- (a) reduce-returns-None + tombstone present yields a status-only stub. Observable only when
  the recorded status is NON-terminal: with the stub the blocker reads `open` and the target
  is NOT newly unblocked; without it the blocker is absent and
  `_is_closed_after_batch`'s "missing dir → tombstoned, treat as closed" fallback unblocks
  the target. The test therefore uses a tombstone recording `open` — `_read_tombstone_status`
  takes `.get("status", "deleted")` verbatim with no validation, and that verbatim
  propagation is exactly what the test pins.
- (b) a present tombstone's status OVERRIDES the reduced status: an `open` blocker dir with a
  `{"status": "deleted"}` tombstone (the payload `rebar._commands.delete` writes) counts as
  closed and unblocks the target.
- (c) a malformed tombstone degrades to `deleted` rather than to "no tombstone": the same
  `open` blocker dir with unparseable tombstone bytes still counts as closed.

## Scope

- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` — two tests for the level-confined traversal,
  reusing the existing `_helpers._make_ticket` / `_write_link_event` / `_get_check_cycle_at_level`.
- `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` — three tests, reusing the file's existing
  `_write_ticket` and `_write_depends_on_link` helpers. No new helper: `_write_ticket(deps=...)`
  is unusable here because it writes `blocks` links into the BLOCKER's dir, which an
  unreducible blocker dir cannot carry, but `_write_depends_on_link` already writes the LINK
  into the DEPENDENT's dir — exactly the shape these fixtures need.

No file under `src/rebar` is modified. If a test reveals a real defect, it is recorded and filed as a `discovered_from` bug rather than fixed here.

## Testing

The new tests ARE the deliverable; each is validated by mutation rather than by assertion of a guess:

- delete the `_is_at_level(...)` call from `_same_level_neighbors` → the direct
  cross-level test goes red (verified: verdict flips False → True).
- delete the `state is None` + tombstone stub branch → test (a) goes red (verified: `[]` →
  `['tkt-target']`).
- delete the `state["status"] = tombstone_status` override → test (b) goes red (verified:
  `['tkt-target']` → `[]`).
- make `_read_tombstone_status`'s `except` return `None` instead of `"deleted"` → test (c)
  goes red (verified: `['tkt-target']` → `[]`).

Edge/negative coverage inside the new tests: an unreducible ticket dir, unparseable tombstone bytes, and a cross-level dep that must NOT be traversed. No new production behaviour, so there is no happy path beyond the existing suite, which must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` contains a test asserting
      `check_cycle_at_level("task-M", "epic-B", "epic", tracker) is False` for an
      `epic-B depends_on task-M` tracker; checked by deleting the `_is_at_level` call from
      `_same_level_neighbors` and observing that exact test fail, then reverting.
- [x] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` contains a test asserting
      `check_cycle_at_level("epic-A", "epic-B", "epic", tracker) is False` for an
      `epic-B depends_on task-M depends_on epic-A` chain, so a lower-level hop cannot
      reconnect two same-level nodes; checked by running that test against the unmodified
      tree and seeing it pass.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when the
      `state is None` + tombstone-present stub branch of `_load_states_with_tombstones` is
      deleted; checked by that deletion + `pytest` on the single test, then reverting.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when the
      `state["status"] = tombstone_status` override is deleted; checked the same way.
- [x] `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` contains a test that fails when
      `_read_tombstone_status`'s exception handler stops returning `"deleted"`; checked the
      same way.
- [x] `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only the two test files — no `src/rebar` path.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, and
      `pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`
      is green.
baseline.summary: Cover graph traversal seams surfaced by the loader/BFS refactor

## Summary (bug)
The host-local hourly updater (`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh`, NOT in this repo) pruned non-current release dirs with an unconditional `rm -rf`, deleting code out from under running rebar processes (lazy imports then fail mid-op). Seen twice in the wild; the updater was PAUSED as a stopgap, leaving this host drifting from `origin/main`.

## The hard constraint
Two goals conflict: (a) never delete a release a live process is using, AND (b) keep disk bounded (the `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` disk-pressure incident). A liveness-only prune cannot reclaim under this host's continuous load; a retention-only prune can still delete a live release. The fix satisfies both. The full three-layer design, edge cases, execution steps, verification oracles, and rollback are recorded in the pinned implementation comment on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] **The updater is RE-ENABLED on this host and confirmed running** — `launchctl list` shows
      `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update` again, and a forced run
      (`launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`) completes successfully.
      This ticket is not done while the host is still drifting from `origin/main`.
      provenance: environment=host-local macOS (this dev box, ~/.local/state/rebar-dev); principal=joeoakhart (operator); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — launchctl bootstrap+list show com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update loaded; kickstart -k completed exit 0; a by-hand run built origin/main 6e282021, swapped current, installed shims.
- [x] [non-codebase] A long-running `rebar` operation spanning at least one updater cycle COMPLETES successfully
      while the updater is active — demonstrated, not argued. The natural probe is a real close
      (whose LLM completion verifier takes minutes) with a forced update fired mid-run.
      provenance: environment=host-local macOS; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — a live global rebar-mcp (via the shim) pinned its release across 3 forced kickstart cycles and stayed up; 12 continuous global-shim `rebar list` calls across 3 cycles → 0 failures; pinned release intact.
- [x] [non-codebase] Disk usage remains BOUNDED under continuous rebar use: releases do not accumulate without
      limit when operations are always in flight. State the bound (count or bytes) and show it
      holding, so this does not recreate the `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` disk-pressure incident.
      provenance: environment=host-local sandbox exercising the real prune_releases() + real flock; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — 12 seeded dead releases, KEEP=3 → reclaimed to 4 (current+newest3), no alert; bound CAP=10×~346MB≈3.5GB; live run logged prune summary remaining=2.
- [x] [non-codebase] When the two goals genuinely conflict — a release cannot be reclaimed because it is in use and
      the retention bound is reached — the behaviour is an explicit ALERT, not a silent deletion and
      not a silent unbounded grow. Name where that alert surfaces.
      provenance: environment=host-local sandbox (real prune + flock + REBAR_DEV_ALERT_CMD capture) plus live SNS; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — 13 flock-held releases >CAP=10 → release-cap alert emitted AND all live releases survived; unlocked control pruned to 2, no alert; live SNS publish to rebar-gerrit-alerts verified (MessageId bdc90c6e).
- [x] [non-codebase] The chosen mechanism and its rationale are documented for the next operator,
      including how to pause and resume, so nobody rediscovers this. The record lives in a host-local
      operator doc that is deliberately git-ignored (via `.git/info/exclude`, pattern `*.local.md`)
      and is NOT part of the committed repository tree.
      provenance: environment=host-local macOS (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` working tree, untracked file); principal=joeoakhart (operator); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `git check-ignore -v` confirms the operator doc is excluded and on-disk (11699 bytes); it documents mechanism, tunables (RELEASES_KEEP/RELEASES_CAP), pause/resume via launchctl, alerting, rollback, and the failure signature. Not committable by design (it embeds host paths).
- [x] [non-codebase] The failure signature is recorded where a future reader will find it: an
      `ImportError` naming a module that exists in the source tree, at a `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases/`
      path that no longer exists, means a pruned-mid-run release — not a packaging defect (two sessions
      mis-diagnosed it as packaging). Recorded in the same host-local git-ignored operator doc, outside
      the committed repository tree.
      provenance: environment=host-local macOS (untracked operator doc under the working tree); principal=joeoakhart (operator); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the operator doc's "failure signature" section spells out the ImportError-with-missing-release-path pattern and its correct diagnosis. Deliberately non-codebase (git-ignored host-local doc).

## Scope note
The defective script `~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh` is HOST-LOCAL and outside this repository, so the fix may land with no repo file impact. If investigation shows rebar itself should participate (for example a launcher that pins a resolved release for the process lifetime), that is a distinct in-repo change and should be filed separately rather than absorbed here.

Related: `shady-blueblack-whale` traces the same mechanism under the `uv tool install --force` trigger; `frangible-irongray-adouri` (closed duplicate) carries the original traced RCA; `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` is the disk-pressure incident that constrains the retention side.


---
