# Consolidate cross-session duplicated primitives (canonical-JSON/hash + retry/backoff)

## Context

A codebase-health audit (joe-janitor, 2026-06-24; report at `.joe-janitor/report-2026-06-24.md`) found a **cross-session duplication** pattern — many independent agent sessions each solving the same sub-problem locally instead of reaching for a shared primitive — in two determinism-adjacent clusters: canonical-JSON/content-hash (6+ sites) and retry/backoff (7+ sites).

## Revised scope (2026-06-25, post-brainstorm — supersedes the original framing below)

A grounded brainstorm + adversarial digest trace (recorded as comments on this epic) **revised the original premise**: there is **no live cross-clone determinism bug**. Each digest is produced by a single encoder for a single purpose and is never compared against a *different* encoder's output; sign/verify and plan/apply both run the same code version, so every domain is self-consistent. The one persisted-and-recompared site (`signing.py`) already uses the proposed canonical kwargs, so it migrates **byte-identically**. Therefore this epic is a **pure DRY / maintainability consolidation**, and the governing rule is **freeze every site's output bytes** (changing any digest is the only way to introduce a regression). Two original citations were also corrected: `_store/canonical.py` is the live serialization home (6 importers + a byte-parity contract), **not** "imported by nobody"; and `orchestrator.py:688-689` contains **no** canonical-JSON code (stale citation, dropped).

The retry cluster is **right-sized rather than universally consolidated**: only the one genuine in-file duplication is unified; sites that solve genuinely different problems are left bespoke (no universal `retry()` framework — that was judged over-generalization).

## Scope

In scope:
- **Cluster 1 (canonical-JSON/hash):** make `_store/canonical.py` the single seam — extend it with
  backward-compatible `canonical_str(doc, *, ascii_only=False, default=None)` + `content_hash(...)`,
  migrate the real digest/serialization sites (`signing.py`, `llm/workflow/schema.py`,
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/conflict_resolver.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/mutation.py`) onto it,
  delete the local copies, and **preserve each site's exact output bytes** (every retained variant is
  an explicit, justified parameter — `ascii_only=True` for `mutation.py`, `default=str` for
  `conflict_resolver.py` — with a cited consumer).
- **Cluster 2 (retry/backoff), right-sized:** unify only the two near-identical `_advisory_lock`
  backoff functions (`_compute_backoff_seconds` + `_cas_backoff_seconds` — same `base·factor^n`
  capped + ±jitter formula, differing only in constants) into one parameterized pure function,
  preserving both budgets' constants and behavior.
- Characterization tests that **prove output bytes are unchanged** across the migrated canonical
  sites (incl. non-ASCII / nested / unicode-key inputs) and that signing verify round-trips
  unchanged; the existing advisory-lock jitter test continues to pin the unified backoff.

Out of scope (intentionally left bespoke / deferred):
- A universal `retry(...)` helper or a new `src/rebar/_retry.py` leaf module — **rejected** as
  over-generalization of genuinely different problems.
- The other retry sites stay as-is, each with a one-line rationale: `push.py` (git merge-CAS loop,
  no sleep-backoff), `jira-capability-probe.py` (polls on an *empty result* — eventual consistency,
  not exception retry), `runner.py`/`structured.py` (stateful prompt-feedback retry), and the
  intentionally distinct `acli_subprocess` / `acli_rest` transient-fault *policies*.
- Any change to the wire format / value of any existing signature or digest (this is behavior-
  preserving; `mutation.py`'s `ensure_ascii=True` is **preserved**, not "fixed").
- A third-party retry lib (`tenacity`) — keep core deps tiny.
- The other audit findings (jsonschema dep, file-size splits) — tracked separately.

## Plan (child tickets)

- **Child 1 — Cluster 1 (canonical-JSON/hash consolidation).** Extend `_store/canonical.py` with the
  documented one-true-encoding + `content_hash`; migrate the 4 real sites byte-identically; add the
  characterization + signing-round-trip tests.
- **Child 2 — Cluster 2 (advisory-lock backoff unify).** Collapse the two `_advisory_lock` backoff
  functions into one parameterized pure function; keep the two retry budgets as config; preserve
  behavior under the existing jitter test.

## Child tickets (delivered)

Both child tickets were created, **parented to this epic** (via `parent_id`, the containment hierarchy — not a `deps` edge, so this epic's `deps` is correctly empty), and each passed the plan-review and completion-verification gates with an HMAC-signed PASS verdict:

- **Cluster 1** — `blunt-tramp-kale` (`1c66-6644-4dfb-4afa`): consolidate canonical-JSON/content-hash
  onto the `_store/canonical.py` seam (byte-preserving). Status: **closed**; completion-verifier:
  **PASS** (signed @ commit `756a88a2`). Has its own AC + file-impact + verify-commands.
- **Cluster 2** — `snag-reek-ember` (`325a-8036-2069-4ed4`): unify the two `_advisory_lock` backoff
  functions into one parameterized helper. Status: **closed**; completion-verifier: **PASS** (signed
  @ commit `1e701b46`). Has its own AC + file-impact + verify-commands.

Both shipped in PR #21 (navapbc/rebar), merged to `main` 2026-06-25.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_store/canonical.py` is the single seam for "sorted-key compact JSON (+ sha256)": it exposes
      `canonical_str`/`canonical_bytes` (extended with `ascii_only` / `default` keyword params,
      defaults reproducing today's bytes) and `content_hash`; the real sites (`signing.py`,
      `llm/workflow/schema.py`, `conflict_resolver.py`, `mutation.py`) import it and their local
      reimplementations are deleted. (`schema.py`'s public `canonical_json`/`content_hash` names are
      preserved as re-exports/delegators.)
- [ ] The one true encoding (`ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":")`) is
      documented, and every retained variant is an explicit, justified parameter with a cited
      consumer: `ascii_only=True` for `mutation.py`, `default=str` for `conflict_resolver.py`. No
      silent divergence remains.
- [ ] A characterization test proves every migrated caller's **output bytes are unchanged** vs the
      pre-refactor snapshot for a fixed input set incl. non-ASCII, nested, and unicode-key payloads;
      and signing sign→verify round-trips are unchanged. (No digest value changes — behavior-
      preserving DRY, per the no-live-bug analysis on this epic.)
- [ ] The two `_advisory_lock` backoff functions are unified into one parameterized pure function
      that preserves both budgets' constants and behavior (pinned by the existing jitter test). The
      other retry sites are left bespoke, each carrying a one-line documented rationale; **no**
      universal `retry()` helper or `_retry.py` module is introduced.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass; no new module exceeds the 800-LOC soft cap; no new
      sub-100-LOC leaf module is created (the canonical seam stays in `_store/canonical.py`; the
      backoff unify stays in `_advisory_lock.py`).
- [ ] Two child tickets (Cluster 1; Cluster 2 backoff-unify) are created and parented to this epic,
      each with its own AC + file-impact, and each passes the plan-review and completion-verification
      gates.
- [ ] One tested home each for canonical-JSON/hash and the advisory-lock backoff formula; a future audit
- [ ] Behavior is provably preserved: a byte-equality characterization test guarantees no migrated
- [ ] Net LOC decreases (duplication removed) with zero wire-format/digest changes.

## Original framing (superseded — retained for provenance)

The original description asserted a live cross-clone determinism hazard and a full retry-helper consolidation (child tickets A1–A4 + B1–B4, a new `src/rebar/_retry.py`, and a `mutation.py` `ensure_ascii` drift "fix"). The post-brainstorm analysis above supersedes that: no live bug exists, the encoding is frozen rather than normalized, and the retry work is narrowed to the single genuine duplication. See the epic comments for the digest-by-digest BENIGN/HAZARD trace.
baseline.summary: Consolidate cross-session duplicated primitives (canonical-JSON/hash + retry/backoff)

## Why

The MCP `run_workflow` docstring in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` claims the run
"executes in the background so it survives client timeouts" and "Run-state
persists durably ... (resumable on crash)". The implementation is a
`threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True)` (around `_mcp_writes.py:297`). A
daemon thread does NOT survive process exit, and there is no reaper or
`workflow resume` entrypoint that re-drives an orphaned run — so if the MCP host
exits, the run is stranded at `running` forever. The docstring oversells a
durability guarantee the code does not provide. Since MCP tools are
model-controlled, that inaccuracy can mislead an agent into relying on
non-existent crash-durability.

## What

Correct the honesty of the durability wording (documentation only — the durable
runner itself is explicitly OUT of scope):

- Rewrite the `run_workflow` docstring to state true semantics: the background
  work runs on a **daemon thread that does not survive MCP-process exit**; there
  is **no automatic reaper**; step records are persisted with idempotency keys so
  a run **can be resumed only if re-invoked**, but nothing auto-resumes it.
- Align any adjacent claims that imply automatic crash-resumption
  (e.g. `llm/workflow/runs.py` "durable; resumable" phrasing) so they describe
  the persistence substrate, not an automatic guarantee.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` (the `run_workflow` docstring)
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` (align wording if it overstates)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `run_workflow` docstring no longer implies the daemon thread survives
  process exit or that runs auto-resume after a crash.
- [ ] It accurately states: daemon thread, no reaper, resume requires
  re-invocation, step records are idempotent.
- [ ] Any adjacent "resumable on crash" wording is aligned to describe the
  persistence substrate, not an automatic guarantee.
- [ ] No runtime/behavior change; `make lint` stays green.
baseline.summary: Fix run_workflow durability docstring to state true crash semantics

## Summary

Discovered by the Step 7 parity census while fixing bug `unreal-milky-sloth` (6fe7-956f-4901-45cf), which fixed the **MCP** surface only. The **CLI** `--output json` surface has the same exposure and was deliberately left out of that fix's scope.

## Evidence (measured, structural — parsed as JSON, not grepped from prose)

```
$ rebar show <ticket> --output json | python -c '<scan for |n| > 2**53-1>'
CLI show --output json, STRUCTURAL unsafe ints: 3
    $.created_at            = 1787856371950409998
    $.comments[0].timestamp = 1787856976224609473
    $.updated_at            = 1787857168766976021
```

RFC 8259 §6 guarantees implementations "agree exactly on their numeric values" only for integers in `[-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1]`. Any float64-based consumer of this output — `jq`, Node, Ruby, most JSON tooling — silently rounds these (measured −42 ns drift), and a lossless BigInt consumer (GitHub Copilot CLI) instead dies re-stringifying with `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt`. The CLI's public JSON output is the one surface where a user *is* invited to pipe rebar JSON into jq.

## Approved remediation — Option A (operator-approved contract evolution)

Extend the SAME proven `js_safe_result` conversion (already shipped for MCP under 6fe7) to the CLI `--output json` path: an integer outside the JS-safe range (`|n| > 2**53-1`) is emitted as its EXACT decimal STRING; in-range ints, bools, floats, strings and null are untouched; the conversion is lossless (same digits, different JSON type). Recorded as **BREAKING (pre-1.0)** in `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` — `int()`/`BigInt()` consumers are unaffected, exactly as for the MCP change.

### Design — a SINGLE choke point, not per-verb patches

The CLI has many scattered `json.dumps(...)` emitters (reads_cli, signing, _commands/*, _cli/*, _engine_support/*), unlike MCP's single `mcp.tool` seam. Rather than patch only the timestamp verbs:

1. Add ONE converter `rebar._mcp_errors.js_safe_dumps(value, **kwargs)` =
   `json.dumps(js_safe_result(value), **kwargs)`, beside the existing `js_safe_result`
   (`_mcp_errors.py` has no heavy MCP import, so it is safe to import broadly across the CLI).
2. Route EVERY CLI `--output json` / `--output llm` store-data emitter through it.
3. Add an AST gate `scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py` (mirrors
   `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py`), wired into `make lint`, that FAILS if a CLI emitter
   writes store data to stdout through a raw `json.dumps` — so a future site cannot reintroduce a
   bare big-int. Sanction marker `# js-safe-ok: <reason>` (mandatory reason).

### Declared-int caveat (handled)

Per the `js_safe_result` docstring, a field DECLARED as int on a pydantic output model is re-coerced to a bare number by `model_validate`. The CLI path applies the conversion to PLAIN dicts (from `show_state` / `to_llm` / the sign manifest) with NO `model_validate` afterwards, so the string form does not revert. The schema already types `created_at`/`updated_at` as `["integer","string","null"]`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] SINGLE choke point `js_safe_dumps`; all CLI `--output json`/`llm` store emitters routed through
      it (not only timestamp verbs); AST guard wired into `make lint` prevents reintroduction.
- [x] Declared-int caveat confirmed non-applicable (plain-dict path, no `model_validate`); wire string
      does not silently revert to a bare number.
- [x] RED-first regression test asserts BOTH (a) `int(wire_value) == stored_value` (lossless, no
      rounding) AND (b) the wire value is a JSON STRING, not a bare number — the direct guard against
      the BigInt-serialization failure; plus an end-to-end Node `BigInt` parse assertion.
- [x] Recorded as BREAKING in `docs/release-notes.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, per-surface, noting
      `int()`/`BigInt()` consumers are unaffected.

## Notes

Also probed and found clean / not applicable:
- Library facade (`import rebar`) — returns Python ints; arbitrary-precision, no JSON boundary. The
  `export_ndjson` helper is tracked separately as `guilty-pusslike-wyvern`.
- Reconciler/Jira outbound payloads — searched for nanosecond integers in outbound JSON, found none.

Classification: CONTRACT EVOLUTION (pre-existing wire-shape gap), not a defect-escape — close with `--class=preexisting`, no `--caused-by` (the parity gap was an intended-behaviour decision at the time of the MCP fix).

## Summary

`tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py::test_push_loop_converges_under_contention` (added one commit ago by 4c4f, `f7aa0d5b5`) failed in CI on a change that provably cannot affect it, then the same test passed 18/18 locally on that same patch set.

Observed once so far: GitHub Actions run **30665788197** (Gerrit change 1134, patch set 1, `gerrit-verify`), worker `popen-gw1`, ubuntu-latest, py3.13, git 2.54.0.

## Evidence

Failure output:

```
rc=1
competitor pushes fired=1
stdout:
Local tickets branch is ahead by 1 commit(s) — pushing.
stderr:
Push failed (non-retryable, exit 1): To .../origin.git
 ! [rejected]        HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
```

That message is emitted at `reconcile-bridge.yml:321`, the ELSE arm of the classifier at `:314`:

```sh
if echo "$push_stderr" | grep -qiE 'non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first'; then
```

The stderr shown contains BOTH `rejected` and `fetch first`, so the classifier should have matched and taken the retry arm. It did not. On attempt 1 the competitor had already pushed (`competitor pushes fired=1`), so this is the ordinary benign-contention path the test exists to cover.

## What has been ruled out

- **Not caused by change 1134.** Its only in-loop edit is `:319`, inside the THEN arm —
  unreachable in a run that took the ELSE arm. Its other edit (the pre-loop fetch)
  demonstrably worked, since `:299` printed an ahead-count that requires `origin/tickets`
  to have resolved.
- **Not the classifier's pattern.** 20,000 iterations of the exact `grep -qiE` against the
  exact stderr text from the failing run, under `set -euo pipefail`, produced 0
  misclassifications — so a `pipefail`/SIGPIPE interaction on that pipeline is not
  reproducible at this payload size.
- **Not reproducible locally.** 18/18 passes on the failing patch set (10 serial, 8 under
  parallel load), macOS, git 2.55.0.

## Leads not yet tested

- Whether `push_stderr` was actually EMPTY at classification time and the text in the
  `:321` message came from a later expansion — i.e. `push_stderr=$(git push ... 2>&1)`
  losing its capture under load. This is the leading hypothesis and is untested.
- git 2.54.0 (CI) vs 2.55.0 (local) behavioural difference in what `git push` writes to
  stderr vs stdout under `2>&1` capture.
- CPU starvation on a loaded runner perturbing the competitor shim's 6-subprocess sequence.

## Why this matters

The test gates every change through `gerrit-verify`, so a flake here costs a full CI cycle per occurrence and trains reviewers to `recheck` reflexively. It also guards a real convergence property (bug 4c4f), so weakening or skipping it is not the answer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism is reproduced deterministically (e.g. under enforced CPU contention or
      git 2.54.0) rather than inferred.
- [ ] Root cause named at a specific changeable artifact — the workflow's stderr capture,
      the classifier, or the test harness's shim.
- [ ] Fixed without weakening the convergence assertions the test exists to make.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py`.
baseline.summary: test_push_loop_converges_under_contention flakes in CI: push classified non-retryable on attempt 1

## Dependencies (STACKED — read against the stack tip, not origin/main)
e165 builds directly on two ANCESTOR changes in this review stack that are NOT yet merged to origin/main: **ddbe** (identity entity + the `rebar identity` `main()` intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`) and **bde5** (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` with `sign_authorship`/`verify_authorship`/`resolve_trust_root`). Both exist at e165's implementation base (the stack tip). Review this plan with `--source local` so those ancestors are visible; against origin/main alone they will (correctly) appear absent.

## Context
Give an `identity`'s public keys a LIFECYCLE with cryptographic continuity: a trust-on-first-use (TOFU) genesis key, and subsequent key add/rotate/revoke changes that must each be signed by a currently-valid key of that identity (fills git-bug's unimplemented `IsProtected`). A key's validity is scoped to its ERA — its position in the authoritative MERGED event log — never to an attacker-set event timestamp. Builds on ddbe (identity + `keys`) and bde5 (authorship sign/verify via `rebar.authorship.v1`).

## Why
Without a signed rotation chain, anyone who can append a KEY event to an identity could inject their own key and forge authorship. Anchoring validity to merged-log position (not wall-clock) stops an attacker from backdating a forged event into a revoked key's window.

## What
### 1. KEY lifecycle events on the identity (TAG_DELTA precedent)
Add key-management event types folded by the reducer into an era-scoped keyring:
- Event types (new constants in `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`, added to the
  known-event-type set; bump the reducer version so older clones
  preserve-and-ignore — see the TAG_DELTA v3 note): `KEY_ADD` and `KEY_REVOKE`
  (a rotate = a `KEY_REVOKE` of the old key + a `KEY_ADD` of the new, or a single
  `KEY_ADD` that supersedes; keep the two primitive events, model rotate as their
  composition).
- `KEY_ADD` data: `{public_key: <authorized-keys line>, signature: <DSSE envelope
  or null for genesis>}`. `KEY_REVOKE` data: `{public_key: <line>, signature:
  <DSSE envelope>}`.
- New reducer processor `process_key_event` (in `_processors.py`, dispatched from
  `_replay.py`) folds these into `state["keyring"]`: a list of
  `{public_key, added_epoch, revoked_epoch|null}` records, where `epoch` is the ordinal
  position (see §2). `state["keys"]` (from ddbe) becomes the DERIVED set of keys
  whose validity window contains the CURRENT (latest) epoch — i.e. currently-valid
  keys — so existing readers keep working.

  SEEDING + MIGRATION (required): (a) `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`'s
  `make_initial_state()` must seed `keyring = []` and `keyring_epoch = 0` (as it
  seeds `managed_refs`/`claimed_session`), so a ticket that never had a KEY event
  has canonical zero-values, not absent keys. (b) BOOTSTRAP for identities created
  by ddbe: `process_create` for an `identity` whose CREATE carried a static `keys`
  list seeds an implicit GENESIS keyring — one `{public_key, added_epoch:0,
  revoked_epoch:null}` record per CREATE key (all genesis keys share epoch 0 — the
  genesis is ONE lifecycle step regardless of key count), and sets the cursor
  `keyring_epoch = 1` (epoch 0 consumed by genesis; the next real KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE
  gets epoch 1). So a pre-existing identity's `keys` are all valid from epoch 0 and
  `resolve_trust_root`/`verify_authorship` work with no explicit KEY event. An
  identity created with NO keys has an empty keyring and `keyring_epoch = 0` (genesis
  happens later, at the first KEY_ADD, which is then the TOFU epoch-0 step).

### 2. Era = a snapshot-safe keyring EPOCH counter (NOT event timestamp, NOT the raw replay loop index)
Maintain a monotonic `state["keyring_epoch"]` integer = the NEXT epoch to assign (a cursor, not a per-key id). Each key-lifecycle STEP consumes one epoch: the reducer records the change at the CURRENT `keyring_epoch`, THEN increments it by 1. MULTIPLE keys may be valid at the same epoch (a keyring legitimately holds several concurrently-valid keys); an epoch does not uniquely own one key — it is only a validity-window boundary. A key added at epoch `a` and revoked at epoch `r` is VALID for epochs in `[a, r)` (open at `r`: a key cannot sign at/after its own revocation); a never-revoked key has `revoked_epoch = None`.

CRITICAL — snapshot safety (the raw replay loop index is WRONG): `replay_events()` starts from the latest SNAPSHOT and skips pre-snapshot events, so the loop index is NOT the absolute ordinal. Therefore: (a) `process_snapshot` FREEZES `keyring_epoch` (and the full `keyring`) into the SNAPSHOT `compiled_state` and RESTORES them on replay; (b) `process_key_event` increments the RESTORED `keyring_epoch` counter, not any loop index. This keeps epochs stable across compaction.

Epoch is derived purely from the canonical fold ORDER (the reducer's HLC-filename replay order — identical on every clone after sync, see reducer/_cache.py, _processors.py:538), NEVER from the attacker-controllable `data`-level timestamp.

Canonical signed content of a KEY op (what the authorship signature covers): the epoch is NOT signed (it is assigned at fold time). The signature covers `canonical.canonical_str({"op": "KEY_ADD" | "KEY_REVOKE", "identity_id": <id>, "public_key": <authorized-keys line>}).encode("utf-8")` (sorted-keys canonical form from `rebar._store.canonical`). This binds a specific key operation to a specific identity; the write-gate checks it was authorized by a currently-valid key (the trust root at the latest epoch BEFORE this op).

### 3. Write-time refusal of unsigned/invalidly-signed KEY changes
A `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` after genesis is REFUSED (the write raises, no event is appended) unless its `signature` is a valid `rebar.authorship.v1` authorship envelope (bde5 `verify_authorship`) over the KEY event's canonical content, produced by a key that is CURRENTLY valid for this identity (valid at the era immediately preceding this change). The GENESIS `KEY_ADD` (the first key event for an identity that has no keys yet) is TOFU: accepted WITHOUT a signature (nothing to chain to). Surface this via a new command/library seam `add_identity_key` / `revoke_identity_key` (CLI `rebar identity key add/revoke`) that performs the signature check before appending.

### 4. Epoch-scoped authorship verification (extends bde5)
Add `verify_authorship_at_epoch(envelope, identity_id, epoch, *, repo_root=None) -> Verdict`: resolve the identity's keyring, build the trust root from ONLY the keys whose `[added_epoch, revoked_epoch)` window contains `epoch`, and verify. An event whose signing key was revoked before the event's epoch fails; one within the key's valid epoch passes. (`verify_authorship` from bde5 stays as the "current-era" convenience.)

Epoch derivation for an arbitrary (non-KEY) event: the epoch that GOVERNS an event's authorship is the number of the identity's KEY lifecycle events whose canonical fold position precedes that event. Provide a helper `epoch_for_position(identity_id, event_position, *, repo_root=None) -> int`. It must be SNAPSHOT-AWARE (KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE are KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES and are folded into the identity's SNAPSHOT by compact.py, whose files are then retired — so a naive file scan under-counts). Compute it by folding the identity's keyring the same way the reducer does — start from the latest SNAPSHOT's restored `keyring_epoch` (the epoch as of compaction) and add only the POST-snapshot KEY events whose canonical `{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` position precedes `event_position`. Equivalently: reduce the identity's KEY history (SNAPSHOT base + live KEY events) truncated at `event_position` and read the resulting `keyring_epoch`. Reuse the reducer's snapshot-start logic (do not re-scan raw files independently). e165 defines this derivation + the `verify_authorship_at_epoch` primitive (which takes the resolved epoch); WIRING it into live event verification at the write/merge path is 3183's job. The AC tests call `verify_authorship_at_epoch` with explicit epochs on a constructed keyring, so the primitive is exercised independent of the derivation helper.

### 5. Write-path allowlist + CLI wiring (grounded consumer list)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` MUST be added to the
  hardcoded `EVENT_TYPES` frozenset (~line 50) or `_validate_event` raises
  a `StoreError` (invalid event_type; ~line 120) and the write seam fails before any
  event lands. Separate from the reducer known-type set in `_version.py` — BOTH need
  the new types (the TAG_DELTA precedent touched both).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py`: bump `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` so stale `.cache.json`
  files (which lack `keyring`/`keyring_epoch`) are invalidated.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py`: `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` must be placed in one of
  its orphan-type frozensets (`_AUTO_RECOVER_ORPHAN_TYPES` or
  `_HUMAN_TRIAGE_ORPHAN_TYPES`) — a test asserts these together cover every
  KNOWN_EVENT_TYPE except CREATE/SNAPSHOT. KEY events onto an identity are not
  orphans in the graph sense; classify them under human-triage (or a dedicated
  exempt path) so the coverage assertion holds.
- CLI `rebar identity key add|revoke`: extend the identity subcommand `main()`
  intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (the seam ddbe used) — NOT the
  `_ARGV_REGISTRY`/`_WRITES_FULL` golden-file path (which would touch `tests/golden`).

## Scope
In: the KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE events + reducer keyring fold + epoch computation, the signed-rotation write gate (add/revoke seam), TOFU genesis, and `verify_authorship_at_epoch`. Out: auto-signing every normal event / the merge-gate enforcement (3183), Jira mapping (264f/2f13). Key material lives in `keys` as before; private keys are operator-held (signatures are produced out-of-band via the bde5 signing seam).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` on an identity that already has a genesis key is
  REFUSED unless accompanied by a valid authorship signature from a currently-valid
  key of that identity; a test asserts an UNSIGNED key-add is refused (raises / no
  event appended) while the genesis key-add (first key) is accepted TOFU.
- [ ] An event whose authorship envelope was produced by a key REVOKED at an
  earlier era fails `verify_authorship_at_epoch` for that event's epoch, while an event
  signed within the key's valid era PASSES (test builds a keyring with an add then
  a revoke and checks both sides of the boundary).
- [ ] Validity is computed from the keyring EPOCH (fold order), NOT the event's
  `data` timestamp: a test with a misleading/backdated `data` timestamp does NOT
  change which epoch (key set) governs it.
- [ ] Snapshot safety: an identity whose keyring events are COMPACTED into a
  SNAPSHOT reduces to the SAME keyring + `keyring_epoch` as the uncompacted log,
  and a KEY event ADDED AFTER the snapshot gets the correct next epoch (a test
  compacts then adds a key and asserts the epoch is contiguous, not reset).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` (KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE constants + version bump + known-type set)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (process_key_event: fold keyring + epoch counter + derive current keys; process_snapshot freezes/restores keyring+keyring_epoch)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (dispatch KEY events)
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (verify_authorship_at_epoch + era-scoped trust root)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (add_identity_key/revoke_identity_key seam with the signed-rotation write gate; CLI wiring)
baseline.summary: identity: TOFU genesis + G2 signed key-rotation chain + era-scoped validity

# `tool_step_limit` empty-filter cutoff 400s on Bedrock/Anthropic — forced landing is provider-broken

## Context / Problem

LIVE-proven (Bedrock us-east-1, haiku-4.5): `build_agent_kwargs` (`src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:64`) implements `tool_step_limit` by rewriting toolsets to `.filtered(lambda ctx, _: ctx.run_step <= limit)`. When the filter trips after any tool call has occurred, pydantic-ai omits `tools`/`toolConfig` from the next request while the message history still contains `toolUse` blocks. Bedrock Converse rejects that request: ValidationException 400 "The toolConfig field must be defined when using toolUse and toolResult content blocks." Anthropic direct has the equivalent documented constraint (tools must be defined when history contains `tool_use`), and pydantic-ai maps `tool_choice='none'` on Bedrock to omitting `toolConfig` entirely — the same 400. So the convergence boundary NEVER lands a run that has already made a tool call — it converts it into a provider error, which `interpret_failure` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:58`) then sweeps into `LLMUnavailableError` ("provider call failed").

Blast radius: every armed site. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:471` passes `tool_step_limit=_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS` (16) — the bounded-recovery fallback itself dies with the same 400 if an evidence run reaches step 17.

Why tests miss it: `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` and `tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py` drive the cutoff with `FunctionModel`, which accepts a tools-less request over a `tool_use` history; the provider protocol constraint is unrepresented offline.

## Approach

Keep the `tool_step_limit` request field and its meaning (a convergence boundary after N run steps) but change the mechanism from *hiding tools* to *steering with synthetic tool results*: wrap the toolsets in a `WrapperToolset` subclass whose `call_tool`, once `run_ctx.run_step > limit`, stops executing the tool and instead returns a fixed steering notice telling the model that tool results are no longer provided and it must produce its final answer from the evidence already gathered. Tool definitions stay advertised for the whole run, so the request is always protocol-valid on both first-class providers; nothing raises mid-protocol; the model lands naturally through the existing output path.

**Terminal backstop — a model that ignores steering cannot spin forever.** Steering is advisory to the model, so the terminal bound for a non-cooperative model is the one that exists today: `runner.py` sets `UsageLimits(request_limit=ceil(max_iter/2), tool_calls_limit=max(8, max_iter))` on every run, so a model that keeps re-issuing tool calls against steered results exhausts that budget and raises `UsageLimitExceeded` exactly as it does now — steering never weakens the budget, it only adds a graceful exit before it. (Routing that exhaustion into bounded recovery is [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911]; tripping early on the repeat pattern such spinning produces is [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]. This ticket's obligation is only: steering must not remove or extend the existing budget.)

LIVE-proven end to end: a deliberately tool-happy agent landed cleanly after 3 real + 7 steered calls, and a structured `completion_verdict` parsed through the prompted-output path after 4 real + 2 steered calls (experiments exp_g/exp_h, recorded on [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] 2026-08-05). This fits the problem because it is the one shape that keeps the Bedrock/Anthropic constraint satisfied by construction — industry equivalents (LangChain `early_stopping_method="generate"`, smolagents `provide_final_answer`, CrewAI `handle_max_iterations_exceeded`) all converge on "stop executing, force a final answer" rather than "remove the tools"; pydantic-ai itself offers no graceful-landing primitive (issue #2605 open).

`FunctionToolset` and `WrapperToolset` are both importable from `pydantic_ai.toolsets` (confirmed in the installed pydantic-ai 1.107.1: `pydantic_ai/toolsets/__init__.py` exports both; `WrapperToolset.call_tool` is the documented override seam). The steering text is a module constant beside the wrapper.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — replace the `.filtered()` empty-cutoff branch in `build_agent_kwargs`
  with the steering wrapper; module constant for the steering text.
- `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` — rewrite the cutoff-shape tests to pin the new invariant (tool
  definitions persist past the limit; execution is steered instead).
- `tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py` — update the truncation test to assert steering semantics
  through the runner.

Out of scope: the runaway detector and its trip wiring ([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]); the recovery catch-miss ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911]). `completion_recovery.py:471` needs no edit — it passes `tool_step_limit` through `RunRequest`, and this ticket fixes what that field does.

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py -q

Happy path: a run under the limit executes tools normally and lands its output. Edge: a run that exceeds the limit gets steering results, keeps its tool definitions advertised on every request, and still lands. Failure-shape regression: a test asserts that after the limit trips, the toolset still advertises non-empty tool definitions (the exact condition whose violation produced the 400) — the assertion is on the request-visible tool surface, not on implementation internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] no code path empties the advertised tool surface mid-run after a tool call has occurred: a test
      drives a `FunctionModel` run past the limit and asserts every request's tool definitions remain
      non-empty for the whole run
- [x] past the limit, tool calls are not executed — the tool returns the steering notice instead; a test
      asserts the underlying tool function is not invoked after the limit and the model receives the
      steering text as the tool result
- [x] a run that exceeds the limit still lands a final output through the normal output path (no
      exception, no empty result); pinned by a `FunctionModel` test whose model calls tools until it
      receives a steering result, then emits its answer
- [x] a run that never reaches the limit behaves exactly as before: tools execute, output lands; pinned
      by the existing happy-path tests passing (updated only where they asserted the old filtered shape)
- [x] `tool_step_limit=0` and negative values steer from the first tool call (the existing clamp
      semantics are preserved); verified by a test
- [x] a steered model that never lands is still terminally bounded: a `FunctionModel` test drives a
      model that keeps issuing tool calls after receiving steering results and asserts the run ends
      with the existing budget exhaustion (`UsageLimitExceeded`-derived failure), not an infinite
      loop — pinning that steering does not remove or extend `UsageLimits`
- [x] [operator-attested] the steering mechanism is LIVE-proven against the real Bedrock Converse
      boundary: experiments exp_g (tool-happy agent landed cleanly after 3 real + 7 steered calls)

## Context

A 200 from `/health` does not establish that this container can serve an MCP request, yet it is all the blue-green cutover waits for: the route sits OUTSIDE the auth middleware and the DNS-rebinding guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, `register_health_route`), and `autodeploy.sh` flips the nginx upstream on a 200 without issuing one `/mcp` request (on the box 2026-08-28: a container was promoted 54 s before serving its first). A container whose `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not admit the hostname real traffic carries answers 200 while 421-ing every real request, and is promoted — the class of `mobile-groovy-badger`.

## Approach

Drive one real `initialize` through this server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` inside the ASGI lifespan — after the session manager runs, before Starlette answers `lifespan.startup.complete` — and publish the outcome as a `handshake` object on `/health`. Uvicorn accepts no connection until lifespan startup completes (Starlette's `Router.lifespan` sends that message only after entering the context), so a later `/health` 200 proves by construction that this container has already served an MCP handshake — which is why this is no background task or lazy field.

**Conclusive.** The probe calls `mcp.session_manager.handle_request(scope, receive, send)` — the entry point the `/mcp` route serves through (`StreamableHTTPASGIApp(self._session_manager)`, `mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:970`). A 200 needs the guard to admit the Host, the transport to parse the body, the session manager to start a server task, and `Server.run` to answer. Boundary: calling the session manager directly does not traverse `RequireAuthMiddleware`/`ProxyAuthMiddleware` (the server holds no credential to present to itself), so an auth-enabled boot is UNAFFECTED — same truthful result (pinned by an AC), and the gate cannot freeze it. This proves the transport + protocol path, not auth config.

**Bounded.** The drive runs under `anyio.fail_after(budget)` with module constant `DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10`, wrapped so a `TimeoutError`, any `Exception`, or a non-200 status is a reported failure record, not a raise; boot continues. The timeout scope and clock are injected — the `drain_then_exit(..., sleep=, monotonic=)` seam — so the bound is provable with a fake clock, not by sleeping.

**Probe Host** (`select_probe_host`), in precedence, from this server's OWN settings: (1) the host of the declared public resource URL, `mcp.settings.auth.resource_server_url` (`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL`; on the box `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, `docker-compose.yml:400`), port appended only when not the scheme default — declared INDEPENDENTLY of the allowlist, so an allowlist admitting a DIFFERENT hostname is caught with a 421: the deploy-promotes-a-421-container case; (2) else the first literal `allowed_hosts` entry; (3) else the first `host:*` entry as `host:<bind port>`, the form `_validate_host` matches; (4) else the bind address, `0.0.0.0`/`::` -> `127.0.0.1`. LIMIT: with no declared resource URL nothing independent checks the allowlist, so a pass then proves the request path works, not that the right hosts are admitted.

The deploy gate closes like the store gate (`autodeploy.sh` 5b): after `/health` 200, refuse the flip when `handshake.ok` is present and false; an absent field promotes (mixed-version safety, as the `store` gate treats an older container). The refusal calls `record_mcp_backoff_failure`, NOT the `record_backoff_failure` 5b uses: `$BACKOFF_FILE` gates the whole script, so recording there lets an mcp failure suppress the review-bot deploy (`autodeploy.sh:64-69`). 5b's own wrong recorder is a separate defect, `prespinal-gem-kinkajou`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — `select_probe_host`, the ASGI drive, the bounded never-raising
  `run_startup_handshake`, `install_startup_handshake` (wraps `app.router.lifespan_context`,
  unwrapping any `ProxyAuthMiddleware`), the `handshake` field on `/health`, and its call from
  `run_http_with_grace`. 463 LOC today, under the 800 cap.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` — the unit tests.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` — the `handshake` key + auth case.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — readiness gate on `handshake.ok`.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — deploy-gate tests on the `mcp_box` harness,
  which stubs per-port `/health`.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py:441` — the other direct `run_http_with_grace`
  caller, UNCHANGED by design: install is a guarded no-op when the app has no `.router` (its fake
  returns a bare `object()`) and reads `settings.auth` defensively. Run with the affected modules;
  an AC pins the guard.

No new config key: the budget is a module constant, per the `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` rationale.

## Testing

Every assertion is anchored: each test proves the handshake actually RAN (a drive counter, or the record's presence) before asserting its outcome — an assertion that passes when it never ran is this bug restated. Both directions are covered, the bound uses an injected clock not a sleep, and each production edit is reverted with its targeted test required to fail (rc checked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A correctly configured server reports a successful startup handshake on `/health`:
      `test_correctly_configured_server_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts the drive counter
      incremented, record `{"ok": True, "status": 200}`.

- [x] A server whose host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports the handshake failed
      with the refusing status instead of ready:
      `test_unadmitted_probe_host_is_reported_as_failed_with_421` asserts `ok is False`,
      `status == 421`.
- [x] A handshake exceeding its budget is a reported failure and boot continues:
      `test_a_hanging_drive_is_bounded_by_the_budget` (injected clock, no sleep) asserts a record
      naming the timeout.
- [x] A handshake whose drive raises never propagates it:
      `test_a_raising_drive_is_reported_not_propagated` asserts the record carries the message,
      the lifespan still yielding.
- [x] The handshake completes inside the ASGI lifespan before uvicorn accepts a connection:
      `test_handshake_is_recorded_before_lifespan_startup_complete` drives the raw lifespan
      protocol, asserting the record exists before `lifespan.startup.complete` is sent.
- [x] An auth-enabled server still reports a successful handshake, so the gate cannot freeze its
      deploys: `test_an_auth_enabled_server_still_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts
      `ok is True` with a verifier configured.
- [x] The cutover refuses a container reporting a failed handshake:
      `test_failed_handshake_container_is_not_promoted` asserts `mcp-handshake-failed` logged,
      upstream byte-identical, nginx not reloaded, container removed.
- [x] A container whose `/health` predates the field is still promoted (mixed-version safety):
      `test_container_with_no_handshake_field_still_promotes` asserts the flip.
- [x] A server whose allowlist admits a hostname OTHER than its declared public resource URL
      reports the handshake failed: `test_allowlist_that_admits_the_wrong_hostname_fails` asserts
      `ok is False`, 421.
- [x] Installing against a server with no Starlette app / no auth settings never raises:
      `test_install_is_a_no_op_without_a_starlette_app`, plus
      `tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py` unchanged and passing.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
- [x] The affected tests pass.
- [x] Each production edit reverted individually makes its targeted test fail (rc checked).

# A failed tickets push is UNDELIVERABLE on the async, library and MCP paths

RC-3 split out of bug 2a76-c9d9-4e8a-471b, which fixed the CLI/synchronous path: the terminal warning now names the git rejection reason and the backlog. This ticket covers the surfaces where that warning is never DELIVERED at all, so 2a76's fix is a no-op for them.

## Proven at runtime (rebar-debug Phase 1; a real `pre-receive` decline, local bare origin)

1. **`sync.push = async`** — `push.py` re-spawns the push as a detached
   `Popen(..., stderr=DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)`, never waited, so every warning the child
   emits is discarded by the OS; only an `OSError` at SPAWN time is logged. MEASURED: against a
   rejecting hook → exit 0, stderr COMPLETELY EMPTY, backlog still incremented.
2. **Library embedders** — `rebar/__init__.py` attaches a `NullHandler` to the `rebar` root;
   `install_stderr_handler` runs only from the CLI and MCP server. MEASURED: in-process
   `rebar.comment(...)` → returned normally, stderr EMPTY, no push status in the return.
3. **MCP** — the handler targets the SERVER's stderr; the agent reads only the tool result.
   CONFIRMED end-to-end here (see comments): `comment_ticket` against a real declining origin
   returned `{"result": "ok"}` with two commits stranded.
4. **Reconciler subprocess** — installs its handler on the `rebar_reconciler` root while
   `rebar._store.push` logs under `rebar`, so its pushes are mute even in the foreground.

## Contract constraint (load-bearing)

`docs/concurrency.md` makes "a failed push never fails the caller" AUTHORITATIVE INTENT, pinned by `push_tickets_branch`'s "ALWAYS returns None" and `tests/unit/test_store.py` (`# no raise`). The remedy must be a SIGNAL, never an exception or a non-zero exit.

## Approved remedy (operator decision B4)

**An MCP `push_status` field on write-tool outputs plus a durable pending/unpushed marker.** OUT of scope: changing CLI behaviour or any exit code, raising on the default path, and the compaction/lock-contention work (tracked separately on 7084).

## Design

**D1 — new module `src/rebar/_store/push_state.py`.** `push.py` is at the hard 800-LOC cap, so the new logic gets its own unit and `push.py` sheds `_unpushed_summary` into it (backlog counting IS push state — an existing seam). Best-effort: every entry point swallows its own errors. API: `record_failure` / `clear` / `read_status` → `{state: ok|pending, reason, detail, remote_ref, unpushed, since}`.

**D2 — marker location.** The tracker's **git dir**, not its working tree. `push.py` sets a dirty tree aside (stash-commit → merge → restore) to reconcile a non-fast-forward, and existing tests pin that a failed push leaves the tracker's `git status` byte-identical — a working-tree marker perturbs exactly that state. The git dir also makes "can never be committed or pushed" structural: a record that the remote is unreachable must not itself need the remote.

**D3 — where it is recorded.** Every terminal failure already funnels through the single `_raise_if_strict(strict, reason, detail, base, remote_ref)` choke point carrying the closed set of `PushDeliveryError` reasons, so recording happens there — no call site changes, no path missed. That function's body is today a no-op unless `strict=True`; it becomes record-unconditionally, raise-only-for-strict, so the default path (and the detached child, same function) records while still returning `None`. That is what makes limb 1 observable despite `/dev/null` stderr. A successful push clears the marker.

**D4 — which reasons are recorded.** The choke point carries the whole delivery taxonomy, so the split is explicit. NOT recorded — the four meaning no push was ATTEMPTED: `push-disabled`, `async-delivery-unobservable`, `remote-not-found`, `invalid-destination`; otherwise every local-only store (a supported mode) reports pending forever, the alarm-fatigue failure that would make this worse than the defect. RECORDED, deliberately, is everything else, including the COMMIT-phase reasons (`stage-failed`, `commit-failed`, `commit-lock-timeout`) and the recovery ones (`merge-recovery-blocked`, `push-multi-bundle-conflict`, `store-epoch-*`, `lock-timeout`, `push-policy-declined`, `push-transport-failed`, `final-push-rejected`). A write that never got COMMITTED also never reached the remote and is invisible on the same surfaces, so `pending` plus a `reason` naming the phase beats silence; a later successful push clears it either way.

**D5 — surfaces.** `rebar.push_status()` for library embedders (no logging handler needed). For MCP, a `push_status` field on write-tool results. `_mcp_writes.py` defines ELEVEN `-> str` write tools: comment/edit/link/unlink/tag/untag/archive/compact `_ticket(s)`, `set_file_impact`, `set_verify_commands` and `declare_no_file_impact`. TEN migrate to a shared `WriteAckOut {result, push_status}` — a strict SUPERSET of the `{result: <str>}` FastMCP already advertises. `declare_no_file_impact` is EXCLUDED: it is `structured_output=False` and pinned in `NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT` by `test_no_schema_exempt_set_is_accurate`, so it advertises no outputSchema to extend and migrating it would regress that guard; it keeps its bare `"ok"` — the one documented gap. The typed models (`CreateResultOut`, `ClaimResultOut`, `SignResultOut`) gain the field, and the schema-less dict tools (`transition_ticket`, `reopen_ticket`) get the key. The ten stay classified as generic acks in `test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`, whose EXEMPT_GENERIC reasons are updated. On the async path the guarantee is that a SUBSEQUENT write or read reports it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 — **async path observable.** With `sync.push=async` against a real bare origin whose
      `pre-receive` hook declines, a write leaves a durable marker naming the reason. The child is
      detached with `start_new_session=True` and deliberately NEVER waited, so the test cannot join
      it: it synchronizes by POLLING the marker path on a bounded deadline (≤60s, 0.1s interval),
      failing if the deadline elapses. That poll is the synchronization contract for this limb, so
      the assertion is deterministic, not racy. Before the fix: no marker, empty stderr.
- [x] AC2 — **MCP limb confirmed, then fixed.** First driven END-TO-END through the MCP
      `comment_ticket` tool against the rejecting origin and its result inspected (recorded as a
      comment); the result then carries `push_status` state `pending` naming the reason, asserted
      by a test on the MCP surface.
- [x] AC3 — **library limb.** `rebar.push_status()` returns `state == "pending"` with the reason
      after an in-process `rebar.comment(...)` whose push was really rejected, with NO logging
      handler installed — asserted by a test driving a real rejecting remote.
- [x] AC4 — **the marker clears.** After the remote stops declining and a later write pushes
      successfully, the marker is gone and status reports `ok` — asserted by a test, so the signal
      cannot latch permanently.
- [x] AC5 — **best-effort contract preserved.** `push_tickets_branch` still returns `None`, never
      raises on the default path, no CLI exit code changes, and an unwritable marker does not fail
      the write. Regression-asserted.
- [x] AC7 — **reconciler limb (4) covered by the same mechanism.** Fixed STRUCTURALLY, not by
      a fourth code path: `push_state` records to disk regardless of which logger root holds a
      handler — the sole reason limb 4 was mute. Pinned by asserting recording works with NO
      handler on the `rebar` root (the AC3 drive), so it cannot regress to logger-dependent. No
      separate reconciler integration test is in scope.
- [x] AC6 — **gates green.** [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, MCP output-schema
      coverage, the schema drift gate, the mcp-reference drift gate and the module-size gate pass;
      the change is `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1` on Gerrit before this ticket closes.
baseline.summary: A failed tickets-branch push is undeliverable on the async, library and MCP write paths

# Event-sourced enrichment queue: cert-triggered enqueue, 60-min soak, latest-wins, lock-guarded claim

## Why
Enrichment must be async and off the hot write path. rebar's event store is already a durable, shared, serialized-write queue substrate — better than a bolted-on SQLite/broker (which cannot live on a shared path nor be visible to all clients). Modeling the queue as sidecar events makes "a new certification replaces the old entry" the natural latest-wins reduce.

## What
Three sidecar events keyed by `ticket_id`, reduced to queue state:
- `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` `{ticket_id, not_before_ns}` appended on plan-review CERTIFICATION, `not_before_ns = cert + SOAK` (SOAK default 60 min). A re-cert appends a new one that supersedes the prior (latest-wins by HLC) and bumps `not_before_ns` — the soak/debounce as a stored timestamp filtered at drain, NOT an in-process timer.
- `CLAIM_ENRICH` `{ticket_id, drainer_id, lease_expires_ns}`, `DONE_ENRICH` `{ticket_id}`.
- Reducer `pending_enrichment(now_ns)` → entries past soak, unclaimed-or-lease-expired, with no later DONE.

## Atomicity + claim (accurate to the store's ACTUAL locking model — DERISKED)
`append_event` (`_commands/_seam.py`) SELF-SERIALIZES every write: it goes through `stage_and_commit`, which acquires the store write lock (`_store/lock.py::write_lock`) for its own append. So a claim CANNOT hold `lock.acquire` across its own `append_event` — the non-reentrant mkdir leg of the lock would deadlock/timeout. The claim primitive is therefore OPTIMISTIC (the epic's stated model: "one drainer lands, losers retry"), not a held-lock read-check-append.
- **Enqueue placement (no false atomicity):** `sign_plan_review` writes the SIGNATURE via `sign_manifest`→`append_event`, which takes its OWN per-event lock; there is no shared held-lock spanning cert+enqueue, and refactoring the signing path to provide one is out of scope. So `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` is a SEPARATE append immediately after `sign_plan_review` returns. Correctness does NOT depend on atomicity: the S4 drain's self-healing fallback treats any certified ticket with an absent/stale digest as enqueable, so a crash between cert and ENQUEUE cannot permanently miss it.
- **Race-free claim (OPTIMISTIC append + arbitration):** the drainer re-reduces the ticket's queue state and, only if still pending (unclaimed or lease-expired), appends `CLAIM_ENRICH` (with a fresh `lease_expires_ns`) via `append_event` (which self-serializes under the store write lock). It then ARBITRATES: among the `CLAIM_ENRICH` events after the latest `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` whose lease is STILL LIVE, the earliest `(timestamp, uuid)` wins. THIS drainer won iff it is that earliest live claim; losers re-read and pick another. Filtering contenders by live lease is what makes lease expiry self-healing (an expired prior claim is not a contender). Exactly one drainer lands per soak window.
Lease `LEASE_TTL` (default 15 min); a claim with `lease_expires_ns < now` is treated as unclaimed on the next drain (self-healing, no separate reaper process). Defense-in-depth fallback (owned/implemented by the S4 drain, see below): the drain ALSO treats a ticket that is certified but whose digest is absent/stale as implicitly enqueable, so even a crash between cert and ENQUEUE cannot permanently miss it.

## Scope (exact edit targets)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` `EVENT_TYPES` (+ StoreError message): add the three types. `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`: add to `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` (sidecar; like REVIEW_RESULT/TICKET_DIGEST).
- Enqueue hook in the `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` certification path (`attest.sign_plan_review`, best-effort after the SIGNATURE append), using the HLC clock (`hlc.physical_now()`) for `not_before_ns`. No held-lock cert-critical-section (the enqueue is a separate append; correctness rests on the self-healing fallback, not atomicity).
- Config field target `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: `overlap_soak_min` (60), `overlap_lease_ttl_min` (15) on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`) — LLM-feature tunables, not `VerifyConfig`.
- This story owns ENQUEUE + CLAIM + the reducer. It does NOT own DONE-emission, the growth-bound retention, or the self-healing scan — those require the drain runner and are OWNED BY S4 (leggy-heedless-mosquito).

## Dependencies
S2 (wispy-cheerless-tick) for the digest freshness the enqueue/drain consult. S4 owns the drain that appends DONE + runs the fallback scan.

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_queue.py`: `test_enqueue_and_recert` (not_before = cert+SOAK; re-cert supersedes+bumps); `test_soak_and_latest_wins` (pending honors soak + ≤1/ticket); `test_claim_race` (two claimers in one critical section → exactly one CLAIM lands); `test_lease_reclaim` (expired lease reclaimable, idempotent).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Certifying appends `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` with `not_before_ns = cert + SOAK` (a separate append after `sign_plan_review`); re-cert supersedes+bumps; `pytest ...::test_enqueue_and_recert`. A crash between cert and enqueue is recovered by the S4 self-healing scan (no permanent miss).
- [ ] `pending_enrichment(now)` returns only past-soak, unclaimed-or-expired, ≤1/ticket; `::test_soak_and_latest_wins`.
- [ ] Two concurrent claimers → exactly one wins via optimistic append + earliest-live-lease arbitration; the loser re-reads and picks another; `::test_claim_one_winner`.
- [ ] Lease-expired claim reclaimable on next drain (self-healing); re-processing idempotent; `::test_lease_reclaim`.
- [ ] The three event types are in `EVENT_TYPES` + `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES`. (DONE-emission, growth-bound, and the self-healing scan are S4's ACs, not this story's.)
baseline.summary: Event-sourced enrichment queue: cert-triggered enqueue, 60-min soak, latest-wins, optimistic claim

## What

Purge STALE present-tense bash-engine/bash-seam language from CI comments and the `_commands` package module docstrings. These describe machinery that no longer exists: the bash test-suite collector was removed, and the bash write seam was retired in Tier D (`_seam.append_event`'s OWN function docstring already says: "Tier D retired the bash seam; `rebar._store` is the sole write core") — yet several MODULE docstrings and CI comments still assert the bash path in present tense, contradicting reality.

Verified stale spots (each confirmed against `origin/main`):
1. `.github/workflows/test.yml:8` — comment references "standalone bash suite under
   `tests/scripts/test-*.sh`, which the `test_bash_suites.py` collector runs" — BOTH the
   collector and `tests/scripts/test-*.sh` are GONE (verified: no such files).

   "initializes a git-backed store via the bash engine, which shells out to jq + git".
   The engine is Python/in-process now. Reword the comment (do NOT silently drop the jq
   install unless verified unused — reword its justification instead).
3. `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py:1-9` — the WHOLE module docstring (not just line 9) is
   stale: it claims the functions are "reached behind `REBAR_LEAF_WRITES=python`" and
   "append through the bash write seam (`_seam.append_event` → `ticket-append-event.sh` →
   `write_commit_event`) so the locked write path is unchanged until Tier D", and "the
   per-command bash suite passes against either implementation". All retired.
4. `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:1-11` — the MODULE docstring still says appends route
   "through ONE narrow seam — the bash `ticket-append-event.sh` wrapping
   `write_commit_event`" and "Python writes route through the bash core so invariant I5

5. `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:1-10` — references the "`ticket-commands.py` engine
   entrypoint) when `REBAR_LEAF_WRITES=python`" bash dispatcher path. (Discovered during

**Out of scope (deliberately NOT purged):** `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:4` and `src/rebar/_store/lock.py:7,22` reference the bash core as documented lineage / the `docs/bash-migration.md §6` dual-window interop rule — these are historical/interop references, not stale present-tense claims, and are left as-is. Legitimate references to `docs/bash-migration.md` as a HISTORICAL record are kept everywhere.

## Scope

Do not change behavior — comments/docstrings only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `test.yml` comment no longer references the removed `test_bash_suites.py` collector
      or `tests/scripts/test-*.sh`; it describes the current pytest layout.
- [ ] `external-integration.yml` comment no longer claims a "bash engine … shells out to
      jq"; the jq step's justification is reworded (jq kept only if still used).
- [ ] The `_commands` module docstrings (leaf.py, _seam.py, __init__.py) describe the
      current in-process `rebar._store` write path, consistent with `_seam.append_event`.
- [ ] **Completeness proof (in-session, single command):**
      `grep -rn 'REBAR_LEAF_WRITES\|ticket-append-event.sh\|per-command bash suite\|route through the bash core\|test_bash_suites\|bash engine' src/rebar/_commands .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/external-integration.yml`
      returns NOTHING (all five stale spots purged; `_store` lineage refs are outside this
      grep's paths and intentionally untouched).
- [ ] No behavioral change: `make lint && make typecheck && make test` stay green.

Files: `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`, `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Rebar resolves configuration through multiple authorities during one operation, and some backends reread ambient state after receiving explicit config. Authentication is also composed inconsistently across LLM, Git, bridge, MCP, review-bot, observability, and op-cert boundaries. This can change behavior mid-operation, discard an explicit choice, expose static credentials to unrelated children, or fall back through an unintended identity. RP-04 establishes one application-wide composition contract without making Rebar a credential store.

The approved research is on `relevant-liberal-xantus`; ADR 0098 is authoritative. Landed RP-01 (`08bcb1f9`–`f0275172`) is the LLM baseline RP-04 must extend.

## Approved design
- Resolve one immutable, serializable, non-secret `OperationSnapshot` at each operation boundary. Precedence is explicit operation input > environment > project config > user config > schema default.
- Resolve repository root separately: explicit `repo_root` > `REBAR_ROOT` > Git top-level/current directory. Interpret winning relative paths against that root.
- CLI composes once per invocation; MCP and Python once per operation; long-running processes also own startup deployment policy and live runtime bindings. An in-progress operation does not reread environment, files, cwd, or global config.
- Compose subsystem-local `GitRuntime`, `LLMRuntime`, and selected `BridgeRuntime` bindings. SDKs/helpers own credential issuance, storage, refresh, expiry, invalidation, and native precedence; Rebar-owned factories retain transport/output policy. `LLMRuntime` enters only RP-01's existing `PydanticAIRunner` -> per-run `ProviderSession` -> one-Agent path. Preserve its budget, complete-or-omit retry history, cache/accounting, typed exhaustion, artifacts, tracing, usage, and failure translation. No arbitrary client/runner injection or second scheduler/owner/path.
- Represent unavoidable static material with provider-specific, non-serializable Pydantic `SecretStr`/`SecretBytes` carriers, revealing it only in the sending adapter. Do not add a universal secret broker, central credential union, automatic keyring fallback, or application-owned cloud-secret retrieval.
- Trusted same-capability children inherit ambient environment for Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA compatibility. Rebar never installs credentials through global `os.environ` mutation. An owning child receives its adapter overlay; unrelated sibling children remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters. Deployment/container/process boundaries remain the primary isolation mechanism.
- Static bindings rotate on restart/redeploy; SDK-native refresh remains SDK-owned.
- Op-cert accepts exactly one of `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` (preferred) or `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY`, validates before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, and copies the key into a process-owned 0700 directory/0600 file. Jobs receive context-local signer/principal/push-policy bindings. Remove runtime SSM/boto3/region coupling and per-job retrieval. Deployment may retain ADR 0049's SSM-at-rest source by injecting/mounting the resolved secret before process startup.
- Fail closed when explicit provider/profile/project/auth composition fails; never retry anonymously or as another ambient principal. Preserve optional write-only Langfuse/OTLP observability's fail-open/no-op behavior.
- Add a portable-local-and-CI AST ownership gate beside `check_config_reads.py`. It derives config/credential names from authoritative registries, rejects reads/reloads/defaults below approved seams, red-proves aliases/access shapes, permits only exact path/symbol+rationale exceptions, and reaches zero legacy exceptions at cutover.

## Scope
RP-04 only: central non-secret resolution/provenance, operation projections, runtime bindings, provider-native auth injection, static-secret handling, op-cert startup composition, all affected CLI/library/MCP/reconciler/hosted consumers, ownership gates, generated operator documentation, migration, and canaries. RP-02/RP-03 and RP-05/RP-06 remain separate.

Explicit corrections: CLI input outranks environment for `tracker.dir`; malformed config fails before effects; backends stop reloading; supplied Python config stays authoritative; defaults move to the schema; tracker layout reaches every owner; Jira Cloud write scope loses `DIG`. Other auth, redaction, retry, TLS, and output behavior changes require an explicit child decision and test.

## Migration / rollback
Expand in shadow mode, prove parity/deltas and non-leakage, cut consumers over behind compatibility facades, add gates/docs/canaries, then remove legacy paths. Before write cutover, disable shadow composition to roll back; afterward require the snapshot-aware compatibility floor. Stored ticket/bridge formats do not change, and parity diagnostics never persist credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CLI, MCP, Python, and direct reconciler paths produce equivalent non-secret behavior from the approved precedence/root contract; a captured operation is stable across environment/file/cwd mutation while the next operation observes the change.
- [x] Every affected consumer receives an immutable projection/runtime binding and no in-progress operation rereads ambient state.
- [x] A portable-local-and-CI AST ownership gate derives names from authoritative registries and rejects direct/aliased `load_config`, ambient config/credential reads, backend reloads, and configurable adapter defaults below approved seams; exact path/symbol+rationale exceptions contain no post-cutover legacy entry.
- [x] The LLM cutover injects provider-native auth/session capability only through the landed RP-01 `ProviderSession` builders; RP-01's one-run/one-Agent request budget, complete-or-omit retry history, cache/accounting, typed exhaustion, final artifacts, candidate tracing, usage, and failure behavior remain green in authoritative offline oracles and bounded live Anthropic/Bedrock cache/auth canaries.
- [x] Git and bridge factories preserve provider-native auth lifecycles and instantiate only the selected integration; missing/conflicting decision-bearing auth fails before network/write without anonymous, cross-provider, or alternate-principal fallback.
- [x] Secret canaries are absent from repr, equality/hash, serialization, snapshots, fingerprints, caches, provenance, exceptions, logs, output, argv, URL/query strings, subprocess siblings, and CLI/MCP schemas, verified at behavioral boundaries.
- [x] Same-capability children preserve unknown ambient/native-chain variables, owning children receive only their overlay, unrelated siblings lose exact Rebar-declared secret names, and concurrent operations observe no global environment mutation.
- [x] Op-cert enforces its exclusive startup sources, fails invalid composition before service work, uses a stable process-owned 0700/0600 copy and context-local signer, observes replacement only after restart, deletes only its copy, and has no application runtime SSM/boto3/region dependency.
- [x] Generated config/security/operator docs cover precedence, lifecycles, restart/redeploy rotation, provider ownership, observability's exception, subprocess limitations, and deliberate behavior deltas; drift checks detect schema/docs divergence.
- [x] Legacy ambient/per-job composition is removed only after focused suites and bounded live paths pass; rollback retains accurate non-secret diagnostics.
- [ ] [operator-attested] AWS review-bot and reconciler check/dry-run/bounded-live canaries pass after cutover without credential leakage or unauthorized fallback. Epic comments record run/change IDs, timestamps, selected provider/auth-source kind, retry counts, and redacted outcomes.
  provenance: environment=hosted-production; principal=review-bot-and-reconciler; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — live post-cutover canaries passed; no unauthorized fallback or leakage; redacted evidence in the epic comment.
baseline.summary: RP-04 — Operation-scoped configuration and provider-auth composition

# T3 — NDJSON import core: rebar import / rebar.import_tickets() (two-pass, composed events)

## Context

P1.2 epic rule-swamp-pupil (ab74-b205-72af-4ce1). Consume our own NDJSON and reproduce the same logical state in a fresh repo via the NORMAL locked write path (no raw-event injection). Depends on T1 (provenance plumbing) and T2 (NDJSON format + schema to consume). Idempotency + deferred-push perf are split into T4; this ticket delivers a correct working importer (re-runs may duplicate — that gap is closed by T4 and documented here).

## What

- New `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`, `src/rebar/_io/_provenance.py`.
- `rebar.import_tickets(...)` library fn + `rebar import` CLI (dispatch in
  `_cli/__init__.py`, help `_cli/help/import.txt`, `--dry-run`, `--output`).
- Two-pass:
  - Pass 1: `create_ticket(type, title, description, priority, tags, assignee)` for every
    line (do NOT set parent in CREATE — parent must be open/in_progress); capture
    `{source_id → new local_id}` id-map. Pass source_* (T1) into the CREATE.
  - Pass 2 (per ticket): `edit_ticket(parent=…)`; `link(…)` (dedup by
    `(source,target,relation)`); `transition(open→in_progress|closed)` to reproduce non-open
    STATUS; `comment(…)` with per-comment source fields; `set_file_impact`/`set_verify_commands`.
- Dangling parent/link target not in the import set → skip + warn (never fail the run).
- `_provenance.py` maps export line → create/comment kwargs (source_* extraction).

## Scope

In: correct two-pass importer + STATUS reproduction + dry-run + dangling skip. Out: idempotent skip-by-source_id, deferred-push perf, large-import docs (all T4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round-trip: `export` a store then `import` into a fresh repo reproduces the same
      logical state (status, assignee, parent, links, tags, comments, file_impact,
      verify_commands) modulo fresh ids, with original date/author preserved as `source_*`.
- [ ] Non-open statuses (closed/in_progress) reproduced via STATUS events.
- [ ] Provenance surfaced on imported tickets/comments (source_id/created_at/author/env).
- [ ] Dangling parent/link target → skipped with a warning; run still succeeds.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports create counts without writing.
- [ ] Tests: round-trip ≡ logical state, status reproduction, provenance surfacing,
      dangling-link skip, dry-run; `pytest` green.
baseline.summary: T3 — NDJSON import core: rebar import (two-pass, composed events)

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — **793 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (7 lines of headroom).

Seven lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

Scope: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` (95 files, 27,284 LOC, 42% comment density). ~970 lines leave — the largest shard.

Dominant category: 28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines), already single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, AGENTS.md and ADR 0058.

Four new ADRs proposed, each consolidating an argument restated 4-8 times: field-convergence fit-then-normalize (8 sites); pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers (3 independent arguments, 3 prior incidents); unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps. Plus amendments to ADR 0028, 0055 §(g), 0031, 0035.

Verified stale: `_backend_registry.py:3` 'STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented' while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; the S3/S4-not-landed notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`.

Headroom: `_ref_lock.py` 1 -> ~21, `dispatch_one.py` 14 -> ~57, `inbound_differ.py` 18 -> ~66, `binding_store.py` 18 -> ~33, `fetcher.py` 29 -> ~80.

This subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured external-API facts that cannot be re-derived from code. The do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G1G2/G6)

### 1. The dominant-category count was wrong — re-measured

The body claims "28 sites carrying 'RELOCATED VERBATIM ... forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap' (~75 lines)". That is not borne out by the tree. Measured over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`:

    $ grep -rn "RELOCATED VERBATIM" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # 6 sites, ALL under adapters/jira_datacenter/
    $ grep -rniE "800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler | wc -l
    6                       # a SEPARATE, smaller set (transport.py, retry.py, transitions.py)
    $ grep -rliE "RELOCATED VERBATIM|800-line|LOCKED 800|module-size cap" ... | wc -l
    10                      # 10 distinct files carry EITHER marker

No single site carries the quoted combined marker. The two families are disjoint, and neither is close to 28. The real figure is **~12 occurrences across 10 files**, not 28.

**Consequence for the shard's headline yield.** The "~970 lines leave" estimate was built on the inflated count for its largest single category. That estimate is therefore UNRELIABLE and must not be treated as a target. The implementer MEASURES the actual recoverable total and records it on this ticket; the number is an output of the work, not an input to it. Do not manufacture relocations to reach ~970.

### 2. Write-ordering must cover the ADRs, not just `do_not_move`

The plan requires the `do_not_move` list to be appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands, but says nothing about ordering for the four proposed new ADRs (field-convergence fit-then-normalize; pagination-stall aborts past fail-open handlers; unmapped relations skipped not approximated; core owns the value maps) or the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035.

Those ADRs are the single-source DESTINATIONS for the arguments currently restated 4-8 times. If a comment citing "see ADR NNNN" is collapsed before ADR NNNN exists, the citation dangles and the argument is simply LOST — which is the opposite of relocation and is not recoverable from the diff by a later reader.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] The shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it
      is collapsed or deleted — destination first, then the relocation
- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination; nothing is deleted
      without a destination that already exists
- [ ] The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the
      unreliable ~970 estimate. The measured marker counts (6 RELOCATED VERBATIM, 6 cap mentions,
      10 files) are the corrected baseline
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are CORRECTED where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete — specifically `_backend_registry.py`'s "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be
      implemented" (false: `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules) and the S3/S4-not-landed
      notes in `_backend.py` and `adapters/jira/backend.py`
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay VERBATIM (this subtree's comments are overwhelmingly measured facts that cannot be
      re-derived from code — the do_not_move list is the most valuable output of the shard)
- [ ] No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged
