baseline.description:
Add primary `bridge`-noun spellings for the three surviving bridge verbs, migrate every enumerated in-tree consumer, and preserve the old spellings as compatibility entrypoints for workflows and environments that have not migrated yet:

* `rebar bridge-fsck`   -> `rebar bridge fsck`
* `rebar bridge-probe`  -> `rebar bridge check-access`
* `rebar jira-onboard`  -> `rebar bridge setup`

Carved out of `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a`, which now owns only the `bridge` verb-group registration. `depends_on 4752` because the noun and its dispatch must exist before verbs can attach to it.

## These are RENAMES, not new features — this is what the reviews caught

`check-access` is NOT new work. `bridge-probe` already ships the identical create/label/search/ delete Jira round-trip (`src/rebar/_engine/jira-capability-probe.py`, launched via `_cli/__init__.py:163`'s `_bridge_probe`), so this is a rename plus consumer migration, not an implementation. `bridge setup` is likewise the EXISTING `jira-onboard` wizard renamed (`src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py`), which already implements persist-config-then-probe. Scoping these as renames is the whole point of the split: the work is enumerating and migrating consumers, and each rename's consumer set is listed below rather than left implicit.

## Why `check-access` stays its own verb rather than becoming a flag (carried from `4752`)

All three narrowing-flag precedents — `flux check --pre`, `dbt debug --connection`, `gh auth status` — are READ-ONLY, and none mutates the remote. The precedent therefore does not transfer to an operation that CREATES AND DELETES A REAL JIRA ISSUE. `fsck` audits your records; `check-access` proves your access. They are different questions with different blast radii.

`setup` calls `check-access` as its final validation step (this is already how `jira-onboard` ends, via `_jira_onboard.py:196-200` invoking `_bridge_probe` with the just-persisted settings injected as an env overlay; the rename must preserve that overlay behaviour and the `--no-validate` escape hatch).

## Enumerated consumers — `bridge-fsck` -> `bridge fsck`

CLI: `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (`_BRIDGE` frozenset ~121, the `_dispatch_bridge` arm at ~255-264 calling `bridge_fsck.main(rest)`), `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge-fsck.txt`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt`. Schema: `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_fsck.schema.json` — BOTH the `$id` (`.../schemas/bridge_fsck.schema.json`) and the `description`, which names `rebar bridge-fsck --output json`. Scripts/CI: `scripts/canary_bridge.py:375` (`runner(["rebar","bridge-fsck","--output","json"])`) plus its ticket-body strings at 412/427/429/460/494; `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (header comment :8, step comment :186); `scripts/probe_rebar.py:505,515,516`. Tests: `tests/unit/test_canary_bridge_wiring.py:78` (asserts the literal `"rebar bridge-fsck"`), `tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py` (FakeRunner keys `("rebar","bridge-fsck")` and the drift title assertion at ~510), `tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge_heldout.py`, `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck.py`, `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_binding_drift.py`, `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conftest.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`. Docs: `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md:78`, `docs/output-schemas.md:50`, `docs/mcp-reference.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md`, `docs/adr/0027-reconciler-binding-lifecycle.md`. OUT OF SCOPE: the LIBRARY/MCP `bridge_fsck` symbol names (`src/rebar/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:84`, `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`, `src/rebar/types.py`) belong to sibling `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d`, which owns the library and MCP bridge surface. This ticket renames the CLI verb and updates the shared JSON-schema text only.

## Enumerated consumers — `bridge-probe` -> `bridge check-access`

CLI: `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:163` (`_bridge_probe` launcher + its docstring) and the dispatch arm at `393-394`; `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge-probe.txt` (renamed); `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt:31`. Implementation docstring: `src/rebar/_engine/jira-capability-probe.py:7` ("Run it as a preflight before relying on Jira sync (`rebar bridge-probe`)"). In-tree caller: `src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py:14,94,102,182,186,191,196-200` — the wizard's help text, its `--no-validate` help string, its two user-facing "run `rebar bridge-probe`" hints, and its actual `_bridge_probe(...)` call. Tests: `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py` — asserts the literal string `"bridge-probe"` in wizard output (239, 266, 274) AND monkeypatches the symbol BY NAME at 251, 268, 280 (`monkeypatch.setattr("rebar._cli._bridge_probe", ...)`), so a symbol rename must be grepped for as a string, not just resolved by the LSP; `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py:59` (verb inventory). Docs: `docs/cli-reference.md:30,33`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:52,55,59-62,69,257`, `docs/releasing.md:430,433` (the release checklist runs the six-step round-trip).

## Enumerated consumers — `jira-onboard` -> `bridge setup`

CLI: `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:66` (the intercept-verb list) and the intercept at `584-589`; `src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py:1,87-90` (module docstring, `jira_onboard()` entry, and its argparse `prog="rebar jira-onboard"` — the `prog` string is user-facing in `--help`). NOTE the established precedent recorded when the wizard shipped (`b5db-7433`): it is an INTERCEPT, so argparse owns `--help`, and there is intentionally NO pinned `help/jira-onboard.txt` and no `overview.txt` entry. Moving it under the `bridge` noun must either preserve that intercept shape or wire overview + routing + a `.txt` together — adding a `.txt` alone BREAKS `test_help_overview_coverage`. Reference generator: `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py:62` (the `"jira-onboard"` entry) and its pin `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py:39`. Tests: `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py` drives `main(["jira-onboard", ...])` at 183, 203, 212, 228, 236, 252, 270, 281, 294, 305 — every one migrates. Docs: `docs/cli-reference.md:479`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:51,58,59,61`, `docs/config.md:259` (the https-only note), `docs/adr/0070-jira-onboard-config-write.md` (its title and body name the verb; the ADR is amended with a rename note rather than rewritten, since ADRs record history).


## Compatibility and migration contract

This change is additive at the command boundary. The new noun-based spellings become canonical in help, generated references, workflows, scripts, runbooks, and examples, but the three old spellings remain executable compatibility entrypoints. Each old spelling delegates to the exact same parser and implementation path as its new spelling; it does not fork behavior, state, exit policy, or output schema. Behavioral parity tests exercise both spellings for success, representative failure, options/arguments, output, and exit status. Any future removal requires a separately tracked deprecation decision and cannot occur in this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar bridge fsck`, `rebar bridge check-access` and `rebar bridge setup` are the primary
      documented spellings and all dispatch; the old spellings `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, and
      `jira-onboard` remain functional compatibility entrypoints routed through the identical
      implementations so existing workflows and environments do not break. Top-level help may hide
      the compatibility spellings, but invoking them must continue to work.
- [x] Each rename is proven to be BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, not a reimplementation: `bridge
      check-access` performs the same create/label/search/delete Jira round-trip `bridge-probe` did
      (same `jira-capability-probe.py` code path), and `bridge setup` runs the same
      detect/prompt/persist/validate wizard, with `--no-validate`, `--reset`, `--yes`,
      `--url/--user/--project` all still accepted
- [x] `bridge setup` calls `bridge check-access` as its FINAL validation step, still injecting the
      just-persisted settings as an env overlay, and still skipping the check when
      `JIRA_API_TOKEN` is unset (exit 0) or `--no-validate` is passed
- [x] `check-access` ships as its own primary verb — there is no `bridge fsck --check-access` flag
      spelling. The legacy `bridge-probe` compatibility entrypoint routes to the same operation;
      the rationale (all three narrowing-flag precedents are read-only, while this creates and
      deletes a real Jira issue) is recorded in the shipped help text or docs.
- [x] `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_fsck.schema.json` has BOTH its `$id` and its `description` updated
      to the new verb name, and the schema-coverage / schema-output / MCP-schema contract tests pass
      against the new registration
- [x] Every consumer enumerated above is migrated in the same change. In particular the STRING-named
      sites are covered: `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py`'s
      `monkeypatch.setattr("rebar._cli._bridge_probe", ...)` (3 sites) and
      `tests/unit/test_canary_bridge_wiring.py:78`'s literal `"rebar bridge-fsck"` — a symbol-graph
      search alone misses these, so the change is validated with a plain grep for each old verb name
- [x] A test greps current docs, workflow invocations, and primary help for stale uses of
      `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`, or `jira-onboard`, while explicitly allowing the
      compatibility registrations, parity tests, release/migration notes, CHANGELOG,
      `docs/archive`, and ADR history.
- [x] `scripts/canary_bridge.py` and `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` invoke the new
      verb, and the canary still classifies binding drift identically (exit 1 with valid JSON is
      still DRIFT DATA, not an error)
- [x] `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` + `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py` are updated together
      and the regenerated `docs/cli-reference.md` matches
- [x] The library and MCP `bridge_fsck` entrypoints are UNCHANGED by this ticket and still callable
      at its boundary; their rename belongs to `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d`
- [x] Release notes record all three old -> new mappings, identify the new spellings as primary,
      and document that the old spellings remain supported compatibility entrypoints for continuity.

## Binding review remediation

The following decisions and inventory corrections supersede any earlier ambiguous or stale references in this plan.

### `bridge setup` dispatch shape

`bridge setup` is a real child in the `rebar bridge` argparse group, but it is a pass-through child: `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` registers `setup` with `add_help=False` and one `argparse.REMAINDER` argument, then delegates those remaining arguments to `_jira_onboard.jira_onboard`. The wizard therefore continues to own all of its options, validation, interactive flow, and `--help`; the bridge parser owns only noun-child discovery. `bridge` group help and `help/bridge.txt` list setup, but no standalone `help/bridge-setup.txt` is created and the top-level overview continues to list the bridge group rather than every child. The legacy top-level `jira-onboard` intercept remains and delegates to the same wizard. The `test_help_overview_coverage` contract is updated/preserved for this exact shape.

### Correct ADR and consumer inventory

The Jira onboarding ADR was renumbered under the repository convention. Amend `docs/adr/0070-jira-onboard-config-write.md`; `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md` is unrelated and must not be edited. This is an amendment, not a new ADR, so the existing number marker and generated index remain authoritative and their checks must pass.

The string-reference sweep adds these live sites to the migration/allowlist inventory:

- `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py` docstrings/comments naming `rebar bridge-fsck`;
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:22` report-profile docstring naming `bridge-fsck`;
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` `_bridge_probe` docstring naming `rebar jira-onboard`;
- `docs/user-guide.md` compatibility note naming all three old spellings;
- `docs/exit-codes.md` rows for `bridge-probe` and `jira-onboard` as well as `bridge-fsck`;
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` and `.github/workflows/test.yml` comments naming
  `bridge-probe`.

Primary help, examples, scripts, workflow commands/comments, implementation docstrings, and current reference docs migrate to `bridge fsck`, `bridge check-access`, and `bridge setup`. Compatibility registrations, parity tests, release/migration notes, CHANGELOG, `docs/archive`, immutable `docs/experiments` review corpora, and historical ADR cross-references may retain the old spellings only through explicit categorized allowlist entries. The current `docs/user-guide.md` compatibility sentence is rewritten to present the noun spellings as primary and the old spellings as retained compatibility entrypoints.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [x] `bridge setup --help` and all setup arguments are owned by the unchanged onboarding parser
      through the pass-through subparser; no double parse and no orphan help file exists.
- [x] The corrected ADR 0070 is amended and ADR marker/index checks pass; ADR 0007 is untouched.
- [x] The added source/doc/workflow string sites are migrated or explicitly categorized as
      compatibility/history, and a repository-wide stale-vocabulary test proves no uncategorized
      live old-spelling reference remains.

### Explicit nested dispatch for `fsck` and `check-access`

`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` registers `fsck` and `check-access` as children of the same required bridge subparser group and includes both in its metavar/group help. Their dispatch arms pass the untouched remainder to the existing implementations: `fsck` calls `bridge_fsck.main(rest)` with the same auto-init policy as legacy `bridge-fsck`, and `check-access` calls the existing `_bridge_probe(rest)` launcher. Neither child may fall through to `launch_reconciler`; that launcher remains limited to preview/sync. The legacy top-level `bridge-fsck` and `bridge-probe` arms delegate to those same call paths. Parity tests assert both names preserve help, options, stdout/stderr, and exit status.

### Entrypoint-specific setup help

`_jira_onboard.jira_onboard` accepts an entrypoint-specific `prog` value while retaining `rebar jira-onboard` as its default. The canonical `bridge setup` dispatch passes `prog="rebar bridge setup"`; the legacy top-level intercept uses the default. Both entrypoints therefore share the exact same parser and wizard implementation while each `--help` usage line names the command the operator invoked. Parity tests assert both usage lines and all existing options.

- [x] `rebar bridge setup --help` starts its usage with `rebar bridge setup`, while `rebar jira-onboard --help` remains functional and starts its usage with `rebar jira-onboard`; both expose the same option set and wizard behavior.

baseline.description:
## Symptom

On 2026-08-12T09:48:03Z the host observability probe published, in a SINGLE run:
  rebar/host:review_interrupts_bound_exceeded      = 7
  rebar/host:review_interrupts_signal_unavailable  = 1

No corresponding events occurred in that interval. Evidence:
  - journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy retention reaches back to 2026-07-03T19:50:40Z (no rotation loss).
  - Full-journal totals at investigation time: bound-exceeded = 8, signal-unavailable = 1.
  - The ONLY signal-unavailable marker in the entire journal is dated 2026-08-04T00:36:41Z — 5.5 days BEFORE it was published as 'new this interval'.
  - Offset files /var/lib/rebar/autodeploy-interrupt-bound-offset and -signal-offset now hold 8 and 1.

## Mechanism

infra/scripts/observability.sh publish_autodeploy_marker_delta() turns a cumulative full-journal grep -c into a per-interval delta using a persisted offset file:

    total=$(journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy.service --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE "$token")
    prev=$(cat "$offset_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    new=$((total - prev))

When the offset file does not yet exist (a NEWLY INTRODUCED counter), prev defaults to 0, so new = total = every matching marker in the whole retained journal. The counter's first run republishes the entire journal history as if it all happened in that one interval.

The function already guards the OPPOSITE direction — 'new < 0' (lost history / rotation) is clamped to 0 with a documented rationale (bug 2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2, and the rotation double-count clamp 1648). The cold-start case (offset ABSENT rather than journal SHRUNK) is the complementary gap and is not guarded at all.

## Why this matters (near-miss)

The two reason-scoped alarms (junco/1650) are 1-datapoint, threshold>0 latches. They were created at 2026-08-12T11:40:58Z — roughly two hours AFTER the probe's first run at 09:48:03Z. That ordering is luck. Had terraform applied before the probe shipped (the usual order), BOTH alarms would have fired immediately from stale history, including rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-signal-unavailable — the alarm whose own description calls it 'the URGENT one ... the drain check itself is broken, EVERY deploy is running blind' — from a single, already-resolved 2026-08-04 event. That is a false page against a pristine system.

This is a FALSE-POSITIVE-generating defect in metric emission, not an alarm-threshold problem: the alarms are correct to fire on a nonzero count; the count itself was fabricated. The bug is latent and will recur on every future new counter added to this shared helper, and on any offset-file loss (fresh /var/lib/rebar, host rebuild, disk restore).

## Scope

publish_autodeploy_marker_delta is the shared helper for deploy_deferrals, review_interrupts, review_interrupts_bound_exceeded, review_interrupts_signal_unavailable. The same cumulative-minus-offset shape (with the same cold-start gap) is duplicated in observability.sh §3 (replication_errors), §4 (voter_errors), and §4b (g2p_dispatch_errors). Those counters' offset files already exist, so they are not currently mis-emitting — but they carry the identical defect on offset loss or host rebuild.

## Suggested fix direction (not prescriptive)

Seed the offset on cold start instead of publishing history: when the offset file is absent, write total to it and publish 0 for that run. Optionally record a one-line 'counter initialised at N' log so the seeding is auditable. Applying it inside the shared helper covers all four autodeploy counters at once; the three open-coded copies should get the same treatment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With the offset file absent and a journal containing N matching markers, the counter publishes 0 (not N) and seeds the offset to N. Verify: unit/integration test over publish_autodeploy_marker_delta covering the absent-offset case.
- [x] A marker emitted AFTER the seeding run still publishes 1 on the next run (seeding must not swallow genuinely new events).
- [x] The existing negative-delta (lost-history) clamp behaviour is preserved and still covered by its test.
- [x] The open-coded counters in §3 (replication_errors), §4 (voter_errors) and §4b (g2p_dispatch_errors) either share the fixed helper or apply the same cold-start seeding.

## Verification

Discovered by ops sweep of AWS alarm firings since 2026-08-12T04:00Z; full evidence trail recorded as a comment on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1). All investigation was read-only (CloudWatch describe/get + SSM read-only journalctl); nothing in AWS or on the box was mutated.
## Implementation plan (current main 3c1972e9c0)

Mirror bug 1648 (change `34759270dd`): a minimal bash delta at every offset site, one full rationale comment at §3 and one-line back-references elsewhere.

### Change — infra/scripts/observability.sh (6 sites)

Each site today reads:

    prev=$(cat "$OFFSET" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    case "$prev" in '' | *[!0-9]*) prev=0 ;; esac

An ABSENT file yields the literal `0` from the `|| echo 0` fallback, so `new = total - 0` = the whole retained journal. Replace the fallback with a cold-start seed:

    prev=$(cat "$OFFSET" 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$prev" in '' | *[!0-9]*) prev=$total ;; esac

`prev=$total` makes `new=0` for that run, and the existing publish-then-persist block writes `$total` to the offset, so the counter starts measuring from the next interval. An empty or non-numeric offset takes the same branch: an unreadable offset is indistinguishable from none, and the fabrication risk is identical. A file holding a real `0` still parses as 0 (unchanged).

Sites (line numbers on 3c1972e9c0):
- 101-102 §3 `replication_errors` (`REPL_OFFSET_FILE`) — carries the full rationale comment
- 142-143 §4 `voter_errors`
- 167-168 §4c `review_bot_merge_change_errors`
- 190-191 §4d `deploy_errors`
- 242-243 `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta()` — covers deploy_deferrals, review_interrupts,
  review_interrupts_bound_exceeded, review_interrupts_signal_unavailable
- 302-303 §4b `g2p_dispatch_errors`

Invariant, stated once at §3 and referenced at the rest: no offset means this counter has never observed the source, so every marker in the journal predates monitoring by it — the cold-start complement of 1648's "lost history is already-counted". Under-counts at most the markers emitted inside the single initialising interval; self-heals in one run.

### Tests — tests/scripts/test_observability_coldstart_e2a6.py

New file mirroring `test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py` (same stub harness: curl/git/logger/ journalctl/aws stubs, `_values()` reader, the seven-target parametrisation).

1. `test_cold_start_publishes_zero_and_seeds_the_offset` — parametrised over all seven metrics:
   offset files ABSENT, journal populated with N markers -> published value is `[0]` and the
   offset file now holds `N`.
2. `test_markers_after_initialisation_still_publish` — the journalctl stub reads its marker count
   from a file, so run 1 initialises at N and run 2 (N+1 markers) publishes `1`. Seeding is not
   sticky.
3. Regression: `test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py` and `test_observability_offsets_6a65.py` must
   still pass unchanged (negative-delta clamp and publish-then-persist preserved).

RED-verified against unfixed main first (expect N, get 0).

### Deploy

No manual box action: autodeploy.sh watches `OBS_PATHS` and re-runs install-observability.sh on a probe-source change (as 1648 noted).

### Out of scope

Alarm thresholds/definitions (they are correct); the offset-file storage location; any change to the negative-delta clamp.
baseline.summary: observability.sh marker-delta counters republish ALL journal history on cold start (absent offset file), producing false alarm firings

# Claim-gate <-> plan-review ref-resolution coherence (shared boundary, ADR 0002)

## Why

Plan-review binds the `file_impact` `{path:hash}` map AT the pinned SHA (ADR 0002); the claim-gate freshness re-check must hash those paths at the SAME ref basis. If the two gates resolve the ref independently (two hash sites), they can diverge (whole-HEAD vs pinned-SHA), re-introducing the staleness false-positive ADR 0002 set out to prevent. Split from the attested-signing pin so each is a thin, independently-reviewable slice.

## What

- Introduce ONE shared ref-resolution boundary consumed by BOTH the signing/plan-review gate
  and the claim-gate freshness re-check — not two independently-coded resolution sites.
- Update ADR 0002 to record the consolidation (and the manifest-channel binding cross-ref).
- Rule-of-Three / YAGNI check: there are exactly two consumers today (plan-review hashing +
  claim-gate re-check); the consolidation is justified by the divergence risk above and is
  de-risked by an explicit back-out.
- Back-out: the shared boundary is reversible to the prior per-site resolution (a flag/revert),
  stated explicitly.

## Scope

- In: the shared ref-resolution boundary, the claim-gate freshness re-check wired through it,
  ADR 0002 update, the back-out path.
- Out: the attested-signing manifest pin (sibling story); snapshot/cache (S1/S2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Plan-review `file_impact` hashing and the claim-gate freshness re-check resolve the ref
      through ONE shared boundary (same pinned-SHA basis) — not two hash sites.
- [ ] A negative test asserts both gates hash at the SAME ref (guards whole-HEAD divergence),
      asserting the behavioral contract rather than snapshotting current output.
- [ ] ADR 0002 is updated to record the shared-resolution consolidation.
- [ ] The consolidation has a documented back-out to the prior per-site resolution (reversible).
baseline.summary: Claim-gate <-> plan-review ref-resolution coherence (shared boundary, ADR 0002)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Operator directive (verbatim, 2026-08-13): 'Update our contribution flow to note that Gerrit changes that have known issues like these should be marked as "work in progress" to avoid erroneous submission.'

The incident it encodes: during a fleet pause, change 1727's revision f34549d099 carried five known review defects (including a silent compaction-suppression bug). The hold was recorded in ticket comments and a session log — and a peer session, correctly following the standing "both votes +1 => Submit" rule, submitted it anyway (merged as d2dea317ec, fixed forward by 8fd5166a7b). This session watched the second-order cost directly: d2dea317ec also pushed `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` to 808 lines over the locked 800-LOC cap, turning main red and costing change 1731 a `Verified -1` it had nothing to do with.

The lesson is a mechanism gap, not a discipline gap. A hold recorded in a ticket or a session log is invisible to the submitter; nothing in the contribution flow tells an author how to make a hold ENFORCEABLE. Gerrit already has that mechanism — a change in Work In Progress state cannot be submitted — and none of our contribution docs mention it.

## Approach
One authoritative wording in CONTRIBUTING.md §2d (the iterate-and-re-push step, where an author is by definition holding a change with known findings); the other two surfaces point at it.

1. **CONTRIBUTING.md §2d** — after the amend/re-push recipe, add the rule: when a pushed change has known unresolved issues — review findings still being folded in, a defect found after pushing, or any deliberate hold — mark it WIP immediately. Give both forms, because which one applies depends on whether the change exists yet: `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main%wip` at push time, and `POST /a/changes/<n>/wip` (or the Gerrit UI's "Mark as work in progress") for a change already up. Unmark with `%ready` / `POST /a/changes/<n>/ready` once resolved. State the rationale in one sentence: ticket comments and session logs are advisory and invisible to a submitter, while WIP is the only hold every submitter — human, bot, or another agent session — is structurally forced to respect. Cite the 1727 incident in one clause as the worked example.
2. **The packaged code-review guide** — `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, surfaced by `rebar explain review`, has an iterate-on-findings paragraph ("Iterate by **amending the same commit**…"). Mirror the rule there in two sentences with both spellings, pointing at CONTRIBUTING.md §2d for the full text. This guide is the on-ramp an agent reads before pushing, so the rule has to be reachable without opening CONTRIBUTING.md.
3. **AGENTS.md** — one line in the existing Git-workflow bullet list, in that list's style, pointing at CONTRIBUTING.md §2d.
4. **Regenerate the guide pin manifest, don't hand-edit** — `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` is GENERATED (`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.guide_parity regenerate`) from digests of the criteria cited by the guides, and `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` fails if the committed file differs. The edit cites no criterion, so the expected outcome is NO diff; run the regenerate and commit whatever it produces rather than assuming.

**Deliberately not done.** No tooling, hook, or automation to apply WIP — the directive is a documentation change, and an auto-WIP heuristic would fight the normal flow. No change to the submit rule itself: "both votes +1 and no unresolved comments" stays exactly as it is, because WIP is an additional gate on top of it, not a replacement for it.

## Scope
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — §2d gains the WIP rule (the authoritative wording).
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — mirrored two sentences in the iterate section.
- `AGENTS.md` — one pointer line in the Git-workflow list.
- `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — regenerated (expected: unchanged).
- `tests/unit/test_wip_hold_guidance.py` — new; pins the rule across all three surfaces.

## Testing
The testable behavior is that the rule is present and reachable on every surface an author or agent actually reads, so a future edit cannot quietly drop it from one of the three.
- **Happy path:** a new `tests/unit/test_wip_hold_guidance.py` asserts CONTRIBUTING.md §2d carries both spellings (`%wip` and the `/wip` REST endpoint), the unmark path (`%ready` / `/ready`), and the rationale clause; that `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` carries the mirrored rule; and that AGENTS.md carries the pointer.
- **Reachability, not just presence:** the same module asserts the rule is reachable through the packaged surface by loading the guide the way `rebar explain review` does (`rebar.llm.plan_review.registry`'s `review -> passing-code-review.md` mapping) rather than by reading the file path directly — a file-path-only assertion would still pass if the guide stopped being packaged.
- **Failure path:** verified by deleting the `%wip` sentence from CONTRIBUTING.md locally and confirming the suite goes red before restoring it.
- **Generator no-diff:** `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.guide_parity regenerate` leaves the tree clean, and `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py` passes.
- **Gates:** `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `check_*` gates, and the CI unit selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` §2d documents the WIP hold with BOTH the push-time `%wip` form and the REST toggle, names the unmark path, and states the rationale that comments and tickets are advisory while WIP is enforceable.
- [x] `rebar explain review` surfaces the same rule — asserted by loading the guide through the packaged registry mapping, not by reading the file path — and the guide-pin manifest is regenerated with no hand edits.
- [x] `AGENTS.md` carries a one-line pointer in the Git-workflow list, restating no CONTRIBUTING text.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_wip_hold_guidance.py` passes, and the deletion check in Testing confirms it fails when the rule is removed.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the CI unit selection are green.
baseline.summary: Contribution flow: mark known-issue changes WIP in Gerrit

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Outbound sync can only write to one tracker project, and it fails closed on anything else. The create client takes its project from a single value set once at construction (`AcliClient.create_issue` uses `self.jira_project`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:271-327`), and the applier scans every outbound mutation pre-flight and raises `CrossProjectTargetError` — aborting the whole pass — if any update or delete targets a key outside the one configured project (`applier.py:217-258`, `_cross_project_targets`, added by bug `626d`). With a mapping that lists several projects, correct mutations to the other projects would be treated as the misconfiguration that guard exists to catch.

## Approach

Two changes, both narrow.

**Create targets the ticket's project.** The outbound create path resolves the destination through `resolve_project` from the mapping module rather than from the client's single construction-time value. A ticket that resolves to "not synced" produces no create mutation at all.

**The guard relaxes from equality to set membership.** `_cross_project_targets` currently compares each target key's prefix against one `configured_project` string; it instead checks membership in the mapping's project set. This is deliberately the smallest possible weakening: the guard stays fail-closed and still aborts pre-flight before any tracker write, so a stale binding pointing at a project the store does not sync is caught exactly as it is today. Only keys the store legitimately owns now pass. Creates remain exempt for the existing reason — their `key` is a local-id placeholder, not a real key, so `_JIRA_KEY_RE` does not match them.

This is the only existing safety property the epic loosens, which is why it is its own story with a paired test rather than folded into another change.

**Module size.** Two files here are close to the repository's hard 800-line gate, and they are treated differently on purpose. `dispatch_one.py` is at 796 lines, so the sibling size-relief story that extracts its `update_one` sub-tree is a prerequisite of this one — four lines of headroom cannot absorb the create-path change. `applier.py` is at 772 and is deliberately **not** split. A structural seam exists there (`_apply_batch` and its helpers), but taking it would relocate `_load_acli` and `_load_concurrency` out of the module against which roughly 62 `patch.object(applier, ...)` test sites are written — and a module-attribute patch does not survive a module move, so those tests would keep passing while silently exercising the real Jira and git paths instead of their fakes. Against that, the change needed here is roughly five lines inside `_cross_project_targets` (`:232-257`), which fits comfortably in the 28 lines available. Splitting `applier.py` for this change would be the mechanical split the module-size policy forbids; if it ever must be split, the honest first move is the 67-line `__all__` and the ~126 lines of banner prose in `:1-198`, which disturb no call graph at all.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful fake transport fed production-shaped mutations, recording the create calls it receives, because the destination project carried on the call is the contract under test.

- Happy path: a ticket resolving to project `B` in a store whose mapping lists `A` and `B` produces a
  create call carrying `B`, not the repo default `A`.
- Contrast case (the guard, both directions in one paired test): an update targeting `B-1` where the
  mapping lists `A` and `B` proceeds; an update targeting `C-1` still raises
  `CrossProjectTargetError`. The negative half is what proves the relaxation did not disable the
  guard.
- Precondition assertion: the guard is shown to run **pre-flight** — the fake transport records zero
  writes when the out-of-set mutation raises, proving no partial leak.
- Edge: a ticket resolving to "not synced" produces no outbound mutation of any kind.
- Collateral invariant: with a single-project mapping the guard behaves exactly as before — an
  out-of-project key raises, an in-project key passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An outbound create targets the ticket's own resolved project rather than the client default;
      checked by a fake transport asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [ ] An update inside the configured set proceeds and one outside it raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] When the guard raises, no tracker write has occurred; checked by asserting the fake recorded
      zero writes.
- [ ] A ticket resolving to not-synced emits no outbound mutation; checked by asserting an empty
      mutation list for it while a synced sibling produces one.
- [ ] Single-project behaviour is unchanged; checked by a regression test running the guard against a
      one-project mapping in both directions.
baseline.summary: Multi-project outbound dispatch and cross-project guard relaxation to set membership

baseline.description:
Compute GC-eligibility for a below-horizon reclamation unit — PRIMARILY a commit/tree **collapse checkpoint** (and, secondarily, a `.retired` tombstone): its folding compaction/collapse commit has been reachable from the sync remote's tickets ref for >= N days (config key from ADR 0106). Read-only; no deletion, no rewrite. Independently verifiable: eligibility true/false against synthetic remote-reachability + age fixtures, for both a collapse-checkpoint commit and a `.retired` tombstone. (Re-scoped 2026-08-29: the eligibility primitive is lever-agnostic and now gates commit/tree collapse, not only `.retired` GC — see epic comment 'Child-roster re-scope'.)

## Implementation plan

Add a small read-only predicate module under `src/rebar/_store/` that evaluates ADR 0106 C3 horizon eligibility for two target forms:

1. `checkpoint_commit_eligible(repo_root, checkpoint_commit, *, now=None)` resolves the configured tickets branch (`tracker.branch`) and sync remote (`sync.remote`), checks the corresponding remote-tracking tickets ref, and returns true only when the checkpoint commit is an ancestor of that ref and the checkpoint commit's committer timestamp is at least `[reclaim].horizon_days` old.
2. `retired_tombstone_eligible(repo_root, retired_path, *, now=None)` resolves the tombstone's folding commit by read-only git history inspection (the commit that introduced the `.retired` path), then delegates to the same remote-anchored age predicate.
3. Add typed config support for ADR 0106's `[reclaim].horizon_days` (default 30, env `REBAR_RECLAIM_HORIZON_DAYS`) without inventing a new key.
4. Do not fetch, push, update refs, delete files, rewrite history, compact, or sweep. All git operations are read-only (`rev-parse`/`merge-base --is-ancestor`/`show`/`log`) against the current local view of the configured sync remote's tickets ref.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Given a synthetic tickets remote where an old checkpoint commit is reachable from `refs/remotes/<sync.remote>/<tracker.branch>`, `checkpoint_commit_eligible` returns true.
- [x] Given the same reachable checkpoint commit is newer than `[reclaim].horizon_days`, `checkpoint_commit_eligible` returns false.
- [x] Given a checkpoint commit is not reachable from the configured sync remote tickets ref, `checkpoint_commit_eligible` returns false even when it is old.
- [x] Given a synthetic `.retired` tombstone whose introducing/folding commit is old and reachable from the sync remote tickets ref, `retired_tombstone_eligible` returns true.
- [x] Given the tombstone's introducing/folding commit is reachable but newer than `[reclaim].horizon_days`, `retired_tombstone_eligible` returns false.
- [x] Given the tombstone's introducing/folding commit is not reachable from the configured sync remote tickets ref, `retired_tombstone_eligible` returns false even when it is old.
- [x] Tests prove `[reclaim].horizon_days` changes eligibility through the real config read path.
- [x] The predicate is strictly read-only: no deletion, no sweep, no compaction, no ref update, no fetch/push, and no history mutation.

## Testing

- RED first: add `tests/integration/test_reclaim_eligibility.py` with real synthetic git repos/remotes covering old-reachable, recent-reachable, and old-unreachable cases for both checkpoint commits and `.retired` tombstones; run the new nodes and confirm they fail because `rebar._store.reclaim_eligibility` does not exist yet.
- GREEN: implement the read-only predicates and rerun those integration nodes.
- Config proof: add unit coverage in `tests/unit/test_config_typed.py` and `tests/unit/test_config_loader.py` for default, file, env, and invalid `[reclaim].horizon_days` behavior.
- Preflight before push: run targeted tests, `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py --check`, `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check`, then the repo verification command(s) from `rebar get-verify-commands able-tidy-massasauga` or the documented default (`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`) as needed.
baseline.summary: Remote-anchored eligibility check for .retired GC (horizon computation)

## Summary

Discovered while proving bug `5931-78a3-95d2-44cd` (marker dropped by truncation). The Cloud outbound comment path fits the SAME body with TWO different rules, so the body-equality dedup can never match for an over-length comment.

- **Differ / comparison key** — `outbound_comments._diff_comments` computes
  `sanitizer.fit_comment(body)`. Cloud's `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment`
  (`adapters/jira/backend.py:152-154`) is `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`, a
  PLAIN-CHARACTER cap at `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767`.
- **Send path** — `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.add_comment` fits with
  `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` -> `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`, which measures the SERIALIZED
  ADF against `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000`.

## Runtime evidence

Driving both with a 40,000-char body (worktree `fix-illadopsis-marker`, repo venv):

```
compare key len:      32767
landed jira key len:  31887
BODY-EQUALITY SECONDARY SKIP HITS (today): False
```

The two keys can never be equal for any over-length comment.

## Why it matters

`emersed-specific-mutt` made the ID-based skip (`binding_store.is_comment_mapped` / `jira_comment_id`) PRIMARY, so this is the belt-and-suspenders layer — but that layer is exactly the guard against a lost map write (a crash between `add_comment` and `record_comment_id`). For over-length comments it is structurally dead, so a lost map write re-posts every pass. `comment_limits.py`'s own docstring states the convergence requirement this violates: "If the two paths used different truncation logic they could never agree on the landed body, and the loop would persist."

Not fixed under 5931 — that bug's fix is confined to preserving the marker and does not change any comparison key. This divergence predates it and is unchanged by it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The differ's comment comparison key and the Cloud send path apply the identical fit.
- [x] A test drives both and asserts the landed body equals the comparison key for an
      over-length comment (RED on current code).

## Fix plan (added after runtime confirmation on current main)

**Restore the shared-fitter invariant on the CLOUD side only.** `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` becomes byte-identical to the text the Cloud send path actually lands — the same shape Data Center already has (`_DCSanitizer.fit_comment` is pinned byte-identical to `sanitize_comment`'s truncation).

1. `outbound_comments.py` — add `fit_comment_as_sent(text, fit)` beside `fit_preserving_marker`:
   the marker-free content the send path lands, i.e. `fit_preserving_marker(decorate(text), fit)`
   with the decoration removed. Backend-neutral: `fit` arrives as an injected
   `Callable[[str], str]`, exactly as `fit_preserving_marker` takes it, so the core module still
   names no vendor and no numeric limit. The decoration's separator length comes from
   `_decorate_outbound_comment` itself, so there is still one source of truth.
2. `adapters/jira/backend.py` — `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` returns
   `fit_comment_as_sent(body, AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients()).fit_outbound)`
   instead of `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(body)`. Built exactly as `_fit_description`
   builds its codec, so the flag governs both.

**Deliberately NOT changed.** `_diff_comments` keeps calling `sanitizer.fit_comment` rather than `codec.fit_outbound`: bug 049e makes Data Center's comment fitter deliberately distinct from its description fitter, and coupling them in the shared layer would retarget DC's comment ceiling to its description fitter. Data Center's `fit_comment`, its send path, and `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body` are all untouched — so this does not absorb `community-sediment-snipe` (DC outbound comments never length-fitted), which remains open and separate.

## Blast radius — no key migration, no re-post storm

The dedup key is computed in memory on every pass and is never persisted (`binding_store` stores `local_comment_key` -> Jira comment id, never a body or a body hash), so there is no stored key to migrate.

Verified by driving the old key, the new key and the actual landed body over a corpus (short, multi-line 20k, markdown, unicode, empty, 32,200, 31,800, 43k single-line, 60k multi-line) in both rich modes: **every case where the old key matched the landed body, the new key matches it too.** The change can only ADD dedup skips, never remove one, so no already-landed comment can be re-posted as a result. Under the shipped default (`rich_text_cutover = off`) the new key converges on the whole corpus; under this project's `cloud` setting the over-length cases still diverge for an unrelated reason recorded on this ticket (the inbound decode asymmetry), which is filed separately.

## Two existing tests must be RETARGETED (not weakened)

Both currently pin the model of the send path that commit `27b868ba55` invalidated, so both pin the defect. Neither can hold alongside the restored invariant; each is rebuilt to derive its expectation from the real send path so it cannot go stale the same way again, and each is mutation-checked to confirm it still returns RED when the fix is reverted.

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_richtext_port_heldout.py::test_fit_comment_truncates_over_limit_byte_identical`
  asserts `sanitizer.fit_comment(huge) == comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(huge)` — a direct
  pin of the plain 32,767 cap. Rebuilt against `fit_preserving_marker(decorate(huge),
  AdfCodec.fit_outbound)`, keeping the "actually truncated" assertion and ADDING an assertion
  that the result is no longer the old cap.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py::test_oversize_comment_converges_over_two_passes`
  simulates the landed Jira body as `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(emitted_body)`. That
  stale stub is why this "convergence" test stayed green while live convergence was broken.
  Rebuilt to call exactly what `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` calls.
baseline.summary: Cloud comment dedup key is fitted at 32767 while the send path fits at the 32000 ADF limit

Discovered while resolving item 3 of story 2127-348c-c41d-472e (probe resolved-status decision).

## Problem
Cloud's absence probe hardcodes `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({'Resolved','Done','Cancelled'})` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/probe.py`. The DC side already sources its equivalent from config (`ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`; consumed via `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py`). A Cloud tenant whose workflow uses non-standard resolved-status names (e.g. 'Closed', 'Complete', "Won't Do") has those issues MISCLASSIFIED as PRESENT_FILTERED instead of PRESENT_RESOLVED — with no way to fix it short of a code change.

## Decision
A runtime/config hook IS warranted for Cloud<->DC parity: Cloud should read a `jira.resolved_statuses` config key (defaulting to the current three names) the same way DC reads `reconciler.resolved_statuses`. This is already recorded as a repo-artifact comment at probe.py `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES`.

## Plan
1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`: add `resolved_statuses: list[str]` to the `JiraConfig` dataclass, defaulting via `field(default_factory=lambda: ["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"])`, mirroring `ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses`. Register the coercer `"resolved_statuses": _as_str_list` under `_SECTIONS["jira"]` so the value is parsed from `[tool.rebar.jira]` and the `REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES` env override is auto-derived (no canonical-name override needed).
2. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/probe.py`: resolve the resolved-status set from `load_config().jira.resolved_statuses` at classify time, keeping module-level `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` as the fallback. Mirror DC's `settings.py` guard: fall back to the default when the configured list is EMPTY as well as unset or malformed (`ConfigError`) — bind `frozenset(configured) if configured else RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` inside a `try/except ConfigError`, since `_as_str_list` coerces `[]`/`[""]` to `[]` without raising. `classify_probe_response` binds the resolved set into the shared `jira_family` classifier. Update the DECISION comment to note the hook now exists.
3. `docs/config.md`: document the new `resolved_statuses` key in the `[tool.rebar.jira]` block.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `JiraConfig` exposes `resolved_statuses: list[str]` defaulting to `["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"]`.
- [x] The key is coerced from `[tool.rebar.jira]` via `_as_str_list`, with `REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES` auto-derived as its env override.
- [x] A tenant configuring `jira.resolved_statuses = ["Closed","Complete"]` classifies a "Closed" issue as PRESENT_RESOLVED.
- [x] Under that same custom config, a "Done" issue (absent from the custom set) classifies as PRESENT_FILTERED, proving the configured set is consulted rather than merged with the default.
- [x] With the key unset, a "Done"/"Resolved"/"Cancelled" issue still classifies as PRESENT_RESOLVED via the module-level default fallback, so a stock DIG tenant is unaffected.
- [x] An explicitly empty configured list (`jira.resolved_statuses = []`) falls back to the module default rather than binding an empty set, mirroring DC's `settings.py` guard.
- [x] A held-out test pins the custom-name PRESENT_RESOLVED behavior and the default fallback; mutation-checked RED/GREEN.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the probe/config test modules are green.
baseline.summary: Cloud probe RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES should be configurable (parity with DC reconciler.resolved_statuses)

# 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on keys shared by up to 9 files

## Provenance

Measured by AST walk over `tests/` while auditing bug 2bc7 (which repaired three files sharing the `"mutation"` key). The audit's scope was that key; this is the surface it revealed.

```
total by-path loaders under tests/  : 213
using sys.modules.setdefault        :   0   (the original 9f0b/2bc7 defect is eradicated)
cache-first (name AND __file__)     :   4
```

The four are `test_differ.py`, `test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`, `test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py` (2bc7's three) and `test_reconcile_filter.py::_stub_modules`. 2bc7 additionally fixed `test_differ_emits_probe.py` and `test_apply_list_of_mutations.py`.

## The collision surface

`sys.modules` keys registered by more than one test file:

```
outbound_differ   9 files        mutation    6 files
inbound_differ    8 files        reconcile   4 files
differ            5 files        applier     3 files
```

**None** of the loaders for `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `reconcile` or `applier` validates `__file__`. The original bug surfaced on `mutation` only because that is where a cross-file `isinstance` assertion happened to exist — the same latent coupling sits on keys with more registrants and no such assertion to expose it.

## Why this is latent rather than broken

pytest executes module-by-module, so a file that overwrites a shared key is self-consistent while its own tests run: its module-scoped fixture was built when its registration was current. The failure needs two things to coincide — a cross-file identity comparison, and an execution order that puts the other registrant first. 2bc7 was exactly that coincidence, and it presented as a macOS-only `isinstance` failure on an object that WAS of the asserted class.

## What 2bc7 deliberately did not attempt

A shared helper, so the loader exists once. It is the right fix and it is not mechanical: the registrants span `diffing/`, `mutate/`, `apply/`, `state/`, `fetch/`, `conflict/` and `orchestrate/`, and pytest puts only each test's OWN directory on `sys.path`, so a bare-name import does not resolve across them. Two workable shapes, both with costs:

* a module at the `tests/` root plus the `sys.path` plumbing `tests/_engine_path.py` already
  establishes — works for every caller including module-level constants;
* a conftest FIXTURE — inherited by subdirectories automatically, but cannot serve the call sites that
  load at module scope, and several do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ONE cache-first by-path loader exists, reachable from every directory under `tests/` that needs
      it, with the `sys.path` mechanism it depends on documented at its definition
- [ ] every loader registering a key that MORE THAN ONE file registers is converted to it — the
      `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `differ`, `mutation`, `reconcile` and `applier` keys at
      minimum
- [ ] a guard test fails when a new by-path loader registers a SHARED key without validating
      `__file__`, so the count cannot regress silently (the audit above was a one-off scan; a scan
      nobody re-runs is not a guard)
- [ ] loaders that deliberately want an ISOLATED copy keep it, and say so — `test_mutation.py`
      returns an unregistered private copy and `test_differ.py` registers
      `mutation_for_diff_purity` under a distinct name; both are correct and must not be swept into
      the shared helper
- [ ] the full suite passes under a REVERSED collection order for the affected directories, not just
      the default alphabetical one

## Not urgent, and why

Nothing fails today. This is a latent-coupling cleanup whose value is that the next instance fails locally and deterministically instead of as a platform-specific surprise in CI.
baseline.summary: 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on sys.modules keys shared by up to 9 files

baseline.description:
# Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

## Context / Problem

CMS and similar federal clients run **self-hosted Jira Data Center**, which rebar cannot reconcile against. DC differs from Cloud on three axes: REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies instead of v3 + ADF, Personal Access Token bearer auth instead of the ACLI subprocess, and name-based user identity instead of `accountId`.

GitHub PR #120 proposed a second adapter package for this. It rides ADR 0035's `Backend` port correctly, but it reaches into `adapters/jira/` privates (`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, `_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `classify_probe_response`) and forks `map_fields_to_remote` as a verbatim copy of `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` with one line changed. That creates a de facto "Jira family" layer with no contract: `adapters/jira/` becomes simultaneously a concrete backend and a shared library, with nothing pinning what is shared and nothing stopping a Cloud change from breaking DC.

## Approach

Make the Jira family an **explicit sub-seam** rather than an accident, in an order that never puts the live-validated Cloud path at risk.

1. **Freeze Cloud first.** Extend the existing held-out characterization tests
   (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`) to pin the current outputs of every unit
   about to move, so any behavior change during extraction fails a pinned oracle.
2. **Extract a `adapters/jira_family/` shared layer** — and re-point the Cloud adapter at it. Cloud's ACLI
   transport is not touched at all.

   **Only non-location-pinned symbols may physically move.** ADR 0035 §(a) pins `adf.py`,
   `outbound_fields.py`, and `comment_limits.py` as **Jira-coupled *and* location-pinned**: they are loaded by
   filename relative to `_PACKAGE_DIR` (via `_loader.lazy_load(` / `_load_sibling_keyed(` /
   `spec_from_file_location(`), so physically moving them breaks the dynamic loader unless the loader is taught
   the new sub-package in the same change — deferred to ADR 0035's Phase 2, explicitly **out of scope here**.
   **Location-pinned means "cannot change path" — NOT "cannot be edited."** Editing a pinned module's
   *contents* (e.g. replacing a dict literal with an import) is safe and is how the pinned units get
   single-sourced; only *relocating* the file breaks the loader.

   **Move by SYMBOL, not by file.** `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` cannot relocate wholesale: it imports
   `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from the pinned `adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
   `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from the pinned `comment_limits.py` (used by
   `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the whole file would point `jira_family/` at `adapters/jira/` — the exact
   dependency inversion the import contract in §6 forbids. So the file is split by symbol, and the two coupled
   sanitizers are **parameterized by the contracts this epic already introduces** rather than importing a
   vendor module: `_sanitize_description` takes the `RichTextCodec` (its `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the
   rich-text seam), and comment truncation takes the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract. Cloud
   constructs those contract objects in `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC
   constructs wiki-markup/plain-text equivalents. `jira_family/` imports neither.

   Concretely, of the six symbols PR #120 reached for:
   - **Movable to `jira_family/` in this epic:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
     and `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` (all in `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`, not location-pinned and not
     ADF/limit-coupled), `classify_probe_response` (`adapters/jira/probe.py`, not location-pinned), and the new
     `RichTextCodec` / `UserIdentityModel` contract objects.
   - **Moves to `jira_family/` only in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and
     `_sanitize_comment` — same observable behavior, but the ADF/limit dependency arrives as an injected
     contract instead of a direct import of a pinned module.

   - **Stays put (path-wise):** `_map_local_to_jira_fields` in the pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`,
     and the ADF encoder in the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. These are shared **by dependency-inverting
     instead of moving**: the pinned module is parameterized by the `jira_family` contracts (it imports *from*
     `jira_family/`, never the reverse), so DC reuses one implementation without any file relocating and
     without the loader changing. Any story that would *move* a pinned file must instead stop and record the
     blocker.

   One more unit needs parameterizing rather than sharing verbatim: `classify_probe_response` hardcodes
   `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})`. Those are Cloud/DIG workflow state
   names; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything. So the classifier moves to
   `jira_family/` taking the resolved-status set **as a parameter**, with Cloud passing today's frozenset
   (pinned unchanged by J1's oracle) and DC passing its own configured set. Sharing it with the Cloud names
   baked in would silently misclassify a DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED` when it is in fact resolved.
   The DC set is **operator-configured** via a `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config key (a list of workflow
   state names), defaulting to the same `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset so an operator whose workflow
   uses the conventional names configures nothing. Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not
   made configurable by this change.

   **The value maps are a special case — they are ALREADY duplicated, and this epic must not preserve the
   duplication.** There are today **three** independently-referenced copies of the local→Jira status map (and
   two of the priority map):
   - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the
     ACLI transport (`acli.py:69-70,143,171`; `acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354`).
   - `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (pinned): `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by
     the `Backend` port via `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
   - `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`: `local_to_jira_status` — the engine-level config copy.

   They have **already drifted**: `outbound_fields` and `config.py` both carry a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the
   `jira_fields` copy lacks. So simply moving the `jira_fields` copy to `jira_family/` would leave Cloud's
   backend still reading a second copy — the exact "two places" the epic exists to eliminate. This epic
   consolidates the two `adapters/` copies; `config.py`'s is folded in by bug `fe15` (its call sites are
   engine-level config, a wider blast radius than this epic's seam).

   **Resolution: `adapters/jira_family/` holds the ONE definition of each value map. Both current copies are
   deleted and replaced by imports from it** — `jira_fields.py` (whose map literals move out, the file itself
   staying put for its ADF/limit-coupled sanitizers) and `outbound_fields.py` (pinned, so it stays at its path
   but its dict literals become an import). After this,
   grep finds exactly one dict literal per map, reachable from the ACLI transport, the Cloud backend port, and
   the DC backend alike.

   The `deleted`-key drift **must be decided in J2**, because a single unified dict cannot preserve two
   callers that currently disagree. J2 adopts `"deleted": "Done"` — the value **two of the three** existing
   copies already use (`outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status`).
   The ACLI-side omission produces `"Deleted"` via a `.title()` fallback, which is not a state in the live DIG
   workflow, so Jira would reject that transition: a latent bug, not behavior to preserve. This is the one
   declared observable change in an otherwise behavior-preserving extraction, pinned by its own test. Bug
   `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) keeps the remainder: the missing ACLI-side
   characterization pins and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.
3. **Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts**: a `RichTextCodec` (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for
   DC) and a `UserIdentityModel` (`accountId` for Cloud, `name` for DC). Cloud is parameterized by its existing
   behavior; DC is a different configuration, not a fork.
4. **DC transport builds on the maintained `pycontribs/jira` library**, gated behind a `[jira-datacenter]`
   extra and imported lazily, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract and the battle-tested Cloud path are
   both untouched.
5. **Verify against a real Jira.** Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026, so the oracle
   is the Jira 8.17.1 test instance the pycontribs/jira project uses, reachable at
   `http://localhost:2990/jira` — the same substrate that project validates itself against.

   **It is BUILT, not pulled — corrected against the registry.** An earlier version of this step said to
   `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and called it a pinned *pullable* image.
   That is false: `docker pull` returns "repository does not exist", the Docker Hub API returns
   `object not found`, and the `pycontribs` namespace publishes only seven OS base images. The tag is a LOCAL
   BUILD NAME — pycontribs/jira ships `docker/jira-test-image/Dockerfile` and its README's own instruction is
   `docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image`. Its base,
   `addono/jira-software-standalone`, IS pullable and the digest pycontribs pins resolves. J5
   [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] therefore vendors a small Dockerfile pinned to that base digest; the mechanism
   and its three load-bearing details (`-DskipAllPrompts=true`, the TTY requirement, 8.x-only) live there.

   Two consequences worth recording at epic level because they shape what this oracle can promise: the image
   does NOT contain Jira — `atlas-run` downloads it from `maven.atlassian.com` at first start, so egress to
   Atlassian is a hard runtime dependency and **pinning the image digest does not pin Jira itself** — and the
   base is `linux/amd64`, so an arm64 runner emulates it and starts far slower than upstream's quoted 3-5
   minutes. Jira 8.17.1 is ≥ 8.14, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so PAT
   bearer auth is exercised for real. J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] owns the harness and records the
   version-drift limitation (8.17.1 is older than a client such as CMS is likely running, so it proves REST v2
   protocol semantics, not deployment-specific workflow/field/permission behavior — tracked separately as
   `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`).
6. **Keep the new boundary structurally enforced, not conventional.** The drift this epic exists to prevent can
   recur the moment a contributor adds Cloud-specific logic to the shared layer. So the seam ships with a
   machine-checked import contract (an `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml`, or an equivalent CI grep
   check): only `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` may import `adapters/jira_family/`, and
   `jira_family/` may import neither of them.
7. **Security posture for the DC connection.** Self-hosted DC is frequently served over plain HTTP inside
   corporate networks, which would put ticket bodies and the PAT on the wire in cleartext. The DC backend
   therefore **requires `https`** for `reconciler.base_url` and rejects a non-TLS URL unless an explicit
   `allow_insecure = true` override is set (which logs a warning). Operator docs state the least-privilege
   expectation: a **dedicated service account** whose PAT is scoped to only the projects rebar reconciles
   (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments / Link Issues on those projects), never an
   admin-level token.

   **The PAT is env-only, never file-config.** Like Cloud's `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, the DC PAT is read from a
   `JIRA_PAT` environment variable and is NOT accepted from `[tool.rebar.jira]` in a committed config file, so
   the credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident. The DC transport never logs the token, and a
   missing `JIRA_PAT` raises a config error naming the variable rather than falling back to anonymous access.

   **Certificate verification stays ON.** Self-hosted DC commonly presents a self-signed or internal-CA
   certificate, and the tempting fix — disabling verification — turns the `https` requirement into theatre. So
   the DC transport never sets `verify=False`: an operator with an internal CA points rebar at their CA bundle
   (a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client), and
   a verification failure surfaces as a clear error naming the CA-bundle setting rather than being silently
   downgraded. `allow_insecure` governs the URL *scheme* only; it does NOT relax certificate checking.

   **The J5 harness is the intended `allow_insecure` case, not an exception to it.** The Dockerized Jira serves
   plain `http://localhost:2990/jira`, so every live test against it sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and
   asserts the warning is emitted. That is deliberate: it means the loopback-only test path exercises the
   override rather than bypassing the validator, and the validator's reject-by-default branch is covered by a
   unit test with a non-loopback `http://` URL. The override is **not** narrowed to loopback — an operator on a
   private network is a real use case — but the warning text names the cleartext risk.

**Provenance decision.** DC and Cloud share the single `jira` creation channel, `jira-` local-id prefix, and `jira_key` binding; deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this. They are the same vendor. Generalizing the store vocabulary is epic `be74`'s work, where a genuinely different vendor (GitHub) makes it necessary; doing it here would mean a store migration for no user-visible benefit.

**Alternative rejected: PR #120's separate adapter package.** Two copies of the field maps and sanitizers drift, and cross-adapter private imports are a dependency direction ADR 0035 never sanctioned.

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib REST client.** PR #120's client is competent, but pycontribs/jira already absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks that thousands of users have found. Confining it to an opt-in extra keeps the cost off every rebar install.

**Alternative rejected: `atlassian-python-api`.** It was surveyed in ADR 0004 and does support DC with PAT auth, but `pycontribs/jira` is the better fit here for two reasons: it ships the Dockerized-Jira-SDK test harness pattern this epic adopts as its verification oracle (its own `tests/conftest.py`), and its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object. Either would work; picking one and confining it to an opt-in extra is what matters.

**Alternative rejected: generalizing `jira_key` / the `jira-` prefix / the channel vocabulary now.** That is epic `be74`'s spine and touches 50+ binding-store sites; pulling it forward delays the CMS delivery for no behavioral gain.

**Alternative rejected: moving the location-pinned modules now.** Relocating `outbound_fields.py` / `adf.py` into `jira_family/` would be the tidier file layout, but it requires teaching the dynamic loader the new sub-package and re-targeting every `mock.patch("rebar_reconciler.<mod>.<attr>")` site in the suite (ADR 0035 §(a)–(b)). That is ADR 0035's Phase 2; doing it here would couple a live-Cloud-risking refactor to a delivery epic for no DC-visible benefit. Dependency inversion gets the same single-implementation guarantee at a fraction of the risk.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new), `adapters/jira/`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (new).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen `reconciler.backend` (**owned by J7**), add the TLS/`allow_insecure`
  validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (**owned by J6**). Split deliberately: J6 lands the
  DC connection settings with the transport that consumes them; J7 lands the backend-choice widening with the
  assembly that makes the choice valid.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra, and the import contract.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`, `test_backend_contract.py`.
- A new ADR amending ADR 0035.
- **Out of scope:** relocating any location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`,
  `comment_limits.py`) or touching `_loader.py` — ADR 0035 Phase 2 owns that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit
- [x] `test_backend_contract.py`'s backend fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes for it
- [x] an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon
- [x] [operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at
      `localhost:2990`, selected by `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` with `reconciler.base_url`
      pointing at that instance: at least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound
      pass, and one local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions
      in the reconcile log
- [x] No SHARED mapping logic exists in two places, and each VARYING unit has exactly one shared CONTRACT:
      (a) the field/value maps, the label sanitizer, and the link-relation vocabulary
      each have exactly one implementation in `adapters/jira_family/`, imported by both backends (or, for
      the location-pinned modules, consumed parameterized by a `jira_family` contract); and (b) the
      rich-text codec and the user-identity model each have exactly one shared CONTRACT in
      `adapters/jira_family/` with one implementation PER DEPLOYMENT. `adapters/jira_datacenter/` defines no
      copy of any unit in (a). Cross-imports between `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` are
      forbidden and machine-checked, failing CI on a violation.
      **AMENDED — the original wording required "exactly one implementation reachable by both backends" for
      ALL SIX units including the codec and the identity model. That prescribes an outcome that would be
      WRONG if achieved:** Cloud is ADF and DC is wiki/plain text; Cloud identifies users by `accountId`
      and DC by `name`. Two implementations of one pinned contract IS the correct design
      (`jira_family/rich_text.py:36 RichTextCodec` → `WikiTextCodec` / `AdfCodec`;
      `jira_family/identity_model.py:42 UserIdentityModel` → `NameIdentity` / `AccountIdIdentity`). Two
      further corrections folded in, both recorded in this epic's AC-verification comment: the create-path
      field map legitimately exists twice (`jira_datacenter/backend.py:53 _map_local_to_dc_fields`, because
      Cloud's version lazy-loads the location-pinned `adf.py` BY FILE PATH — a coupling DC must not carry),
      so the "defines none of its own" clause is scoped to the units in (a); and the enforcement clause is
      narrowed to what the checker actually does — it forbids cross-IMPORTS and pins one dict literal per
      value map, but cannot prevent a re-DEFINITION, so four of the six units rest on convention plus
      review. The substance was verified: cross-imports are empty on `gerrit/main`, the boundary checker
      fires on 11 forbidden edges and stays silent on 4 permitted ones, and the value-map single-sourcing
      is asserted by object IDENTITY (`... is LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`), not equality
      **AMENDED AGAIN (task `f020-0960-2c42-4d61`, 2026-08-12) — the probe classifier
      (`classify_probe_response`) is REMOVED from the (a) list.** Bug `3b5f` removed every consumer of the
      inbound absence-probe chain, leaving the port dormant; `f020` deleted the port and the classifier
      together, so `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` no longer exists and neither backend imports it. The
      "one shared … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)
