baseline.description:
# rebar bug-trend analysis (2026-08-01, reviewed)

Data baseline: 344 bug tickets (77 Jun, 260 Jul, 7 Aug 1); 333 closed. Bug-close `--class` enum (regression | plan_defect | env_integration | flaky | preexisting | not_a_bug | duplicate | escalated | undetermined) became required ~07-19 (ed13); 214 closed bugs carry no class — ~207 predate the requirement, ~7 post-date it via then-unenforced close surfaces (the 376d class: MCP transition / NDJSON import). Of the 119 classified: preexisting 57, plan_defect 15, env_integration 14, duplicate 12, regression 12, not_a_bug 4, flaky 4, undetermined 1. Caveat: every classified close is a July/Aug-created bug (the June cohort closed pre-taxonomy), and the class is closer-self-reported, unaudited. Tags: 237/344 untagged, ad-hoc vocab. creation_channel: unknown 209 / cli 126 / jira 5 / python 4. file_impact set on 100/344. `rebar metrics` registry lenses: agent_process (attempts_per_ticket, first_pass_rate, reopen_recovery, revert_recovery, rework_within_7_days), code_health (churn, refactor_to_addition_ratio), gate_economics (cost_per_accepted_change, first_pass_verification, env_diagnosis_intervals); module-size metrics show `unavailable`. No bug lens exists.

Title-keyword clustering (overlapping, 261/344 matched): reconciler/Jira sync 77; concurrency/locking/git-store races 76; plan-review/attestation gate defects 55; CI/test flakiness+isolation 41; silent-failure/fail-open 39; infra/deploy 27; code-review gate 24; completion-verifier/close gate 22; config/env-var 19; truncation/pagination/limits 15; direction-inversion/asymmetry ~7.

Recurring same-class families (explicit in titles): unlocked raw git commits bypassing the canonical locked write seam (3a33, 3435, 4dd2, 3b4e); pagination truncation (9263, 1f3d, deac); link-direction inversion (3b86 → 4b59 → 32cc); asymmetric ADD-only differs (7f42, 908c); lock wedges/reclamation (620c, a4b2, 304e, ac26, 1a47, 9305, 449f — 449f documents 7 post-fix recurrences as residual, not regression); mtime-less cache staleness (1d76, e995, 908b); wall-clock perf assertions in tests (edfe, b228, 19d7, 5e94, 85c3); missing subprocess timeouts (c16f, d843, 747f); "exists on CLI only, not lib/MCP" parity (6e88, 1598, 5199, d21b; close --class rollout misses 0e15, 376d); unread config/env keys (281f, 9d7a; b00f is the adjacent scanner-blind-spot case).

---

## Q1 — Additional observability/traceability? YES, three low/zero-friction gaps.

What already exists and costs users nothing extra: bug-close `--class` (bounded enum, enforced); the **blame-hunt subsystem** — every bug close best-effort auto-derives a `caused_by` link to the culprit ticket (`src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, `transition_close.py:490`, ticket 555e) with retroactive backfills (`scripts/backfill_caused_by.py`, `scripts/backfill_bug_class.py` — structural, no-LLM close_class backfill from reverts/REVIEW_RESULT/gate_error signals, ticket 5062); `discovered_from` links; tags; session logs; auto-filed canary tickets (binding-drift, heartbeat) with a find-existing-then-comment dedup pattern; the code-review FP ledger (`fp:code-review` bug tickets with a `root-cause:` enum, compiled into NO-FIRE eval cases); `rebar metrics` lenses.

Gaps:
1. **The close taxonomy captures relationship-to-work, not mechanism or escape channel.**
   `preexisting` (57/119) tells you it wasn't a regression; it does not tell you it was a
   concurrency bug that escaped because no gate looks at raw git writes. Recommendation:
   a **batch auto-classifier** extending the 5062 backfill pattern — structural signals
   where they suffice, the `rebar.llm` framework for the rest — writing bounded
   `mechanism:*` / `detected-by:*` tags to closed bugs on a schedule, spot-checked. Zero
   author burden. Do NOT add a second *required* close flag: the `--class` rollout itself
   broke every automated close surface (0e15 red main; 376d MCP/NDJSON gaps; the canary
   closes bugs programmatically — reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:300), and automation would
   stamp a constant value anyway, polluting the data.
2. **Nothing aggregates.** Answering "top bug mechanism this month" required re-mining 344
   titles by hand; the registry has agent_process/code_health/gate_economics lenses but no
   bug lens. Recommendation: a `bug_trends` metrics lens over data already in the store —
   close_class distribution over time, mechanism-tag distribution, open-bug age,
   `caused_by` fan-in (shared culprits), canary time-to-detect. Read-only; zero burden.
3. **Class-level recurrence is prose; only culprit-level links are structured.**
   `caused_by` gives queryable bug→culprit-ticket links, but "same class as the
   enrich-queue prune race", "sibling sweep of 5546", "9305 rec #1" live in titles —
   recurrence-of-a-mechanism across channels is unqueryable. Recommendation: a link/tag
   convention (`relates_to` to the anchor bug + a `class:<anchor>` tag) written by the
   debug skill automatically (see Q4), so recurrence rate per class becomes a query.
Also: extend the FP-ledger pattern (proven for code review) to plan-review false positives — a large fraction of the 55 plan-review bugs are FP/noise reports; making each a NO-FIRE eval case compounds precision. Anti-recommendation: no new mandatory fields at bug **create** time (canaries and agents must file cheaply), and no mandatory prose root-cause field (comments already carry it).

## Q2 — Fragility/decay trends? Mostly surface-expansion + latent-defect discovery, with four real structural weaknesses.

The July spike tracks new subsystem activation (review-bot, auto-lander, Bedrock cutover, Jira DC, live tiers); the June baseline was itself audit-driven (audit-2026-06-09 filed ~17 on 06-10; antipattern-audit). In the classified (July-created, self-reported) subsample, `preexisting` outnumbers `regression` 57:12 — consistent with latent-defect discovery rather than decay, though that subsample excludes the June cohort and is unaudited. Four structural fragility patterns are real and mitigable regardless:
1. **A bespoke concurrent database on git** (~76 bugs). Many writers (CLI, MCP, review-bot,
   reconcile-bridge, enrich queue, janitors, retention) re-discover the locking contract;
   failures: unlocked whole-index commits, auto-gc/maintenance corrupting the shared object
   DB, unreclaimable locks in containers. Mitigation: one canonical locked write seam
   (`run_git_write` exists; delete/txn/compact/init already route through it), **enforced
   deterministically in CI** — forbid raw `git commit`/index mutation outside an
   allowlisted seam, scoped to store-touching code AND workflows/scripts:
   reconcile-bridge.yml:283 does a raw `git commit` of ticket events in CI and is the live
   instance behind 449f's dominant failure mode; a src/rebar-only lint would miss it.
   Allowlist the seam files and test-fixture repos (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py).
   Plus the contention policy 9305 asks for.
2. **Hand-written per-field, per-direction reconciler differs** (~77). Asymmetric ADD-only
   differs, direction inversions, silent pagination truncation, untyped transport (cc77
   names the type gap as the root cause of a357's class). Mitigation: typed transport
   protocol (mypy-enforced port completeness — cc77), roundtrip/property invariants
   (inbound∘outbound identity, direction preservation), pagination-by-construction (one
   paged iterator, no raw page calls).
3. **The gates are themselves a top bug surface** (~100 across plan-review/code-review/
   verifier): attestation staleness/races, verdict non-determinism (620b, e458), token-cap
   INDETERMINATEs, FP classes. Meta-fragility: guardrail bugs erode trust and consume the
   bug budget. Mitigation: treat gate reliability as a product area (it is trending that
   way), keep the FP-ledger/eval loop growing, prefer deterministic pre-checks before LLM
   passes.
4. **Silent-failure default** (~39): fail-open checks, exit-0-on-error, unread env keys,
   integrations broken for weeks unnoticed (1630: 4119 mail errors since 06-30; 8070:
   canary red since 07-14). Mitigation: fail-loud policy for gate/infra code paths +
   auto-file tickets on canary red transitions (pattern already exists for binding-drift/
   heartbeat).

## Q3 — Gate levers, precision-first. Yes: mostly deterministic, narrowly-scoped ones.

Current posture is good: code review blocks only on security + secret/high-critical detectors; the rest is advisory; plan-review criteria carry applicability gates and ANTI-FP clauses; an FP ledger polices code-review noise. Levers, ranked by signal-to-noise:
1. **Deterministic CI lint: no raw git writes outside the canonical store seam** (catches
   the 3a33/3435/4dd2 class; low-FP *with* an allowlist for the seam itself and
   test-fixture repos, and scoped to include workflows/scripts — see Q2 §1 for why).
2. **Engine-layer enforcement rule as a code-review project criterion** (narrow): new
   validation/gates must live in the engine, not the CLI layer — catches the 0e15/376d and
   "CLI-only flag" parity class. Deterministic alternative: a parity test template.
3. **"Config key must be observably read" check** — for each new config/env key, require a
   test or a registry entry proving a behavioral effect; the env-registry drift gate
   already exists but checks documentation only (`scripts/gen_env_registry.py`), and b00f
   shows scanner blind spots.
4. **Auto-file P1 tickets on external/live canary red transitions** (8070 sat red for two
   weeks) — observability, but it closes the "merged broken, nobody looked" channel.
   Reuse the reconcile-bridge canary's find-existing-open-ticket→comment dedup pattern
   (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:259-267) so it cannot spam; external-integration.yml has
   no such path today.
5. **Narrow advisory code-review criterion: absolute wall-clock assertions in tests**
   (edfe/b228/19d7/5e94/85c3 class) — textually detectable, low FP as a scoped rule.
6. **Extend the FP-ledger pattern to plan review** — precision lever for existing criteria
   rather than a new detector; build on the adjudication corpus + FP-proxy harness already
   in docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/.
7. Candidate only — needs a security design first: completion verifier executing a
   ticket's recorded `verify_commands` deterministically before the LLM pass would turn
   "AC satisfied" from pure judgment into judgment + executed evidence and catch
   proxy-validation escapes at close. But verify_commands are agent-authored arbitrary
   shell run in whichever environment closes the ticket: it needs sandboxing/allowlisting
   and a staleness story (plan-time commands vs post-merge tree) before it is a lever, not
   a liability.
Anti-levers: no new blocking LLM dimensions (T9/T5b stay advisory — concurrency/reliability review by LLM is FP-prone); no mutation-testing gate in CI (keep manual/scoped); no mandatory local review-code preflight (cost without vote).

## Q4 — rebar-debug: strong on single-bug rigor; four gaps for class-level closure.

The two-phase protocol, falsifiability, dynamic-proof rule, parsimony/exit gate, not-a-bug guard, and Step 7 sibling sweep are all present and good. Gaps vs "sibling issues, recurrence through different channels, residual fragility":
1. **No ticket-store writeback.** The skill never claims the bug ticket, records the proven
   root cause + experiment log as a comment, closes with the right `--class`, or files
   sibling/residual tickets with links. Note this is partly deliberate: the skill's
   Approval gate (SKILL.md:94-106) requires user approval before writing to "Jira or other
   trackers". So the fix must reconcile with that gate, not bypass it: add a "Record the
   outcome" section that treats the project's own rebar store as the sanctioned write
   surface when project guidance (AGENTS.md) mandates recording work there, keeping the
   approval gate for external trackers (Jira). Content: root-cause comment (mechanism,
   citations, experiments), close with the taxonomy class, siblings → tickets linked to
   the anchor bug, residual risks → tickets. This is also what makes Q1's recurrence
   observability free.
2. **Step 7 sweeps constructs, not channels.** It greps for the same code construct; the
   observed recurrences are the same *invariant* violated via a different surface (CLI vs
   MCP vs import; local vs CI — a4b2 fixed the local wedge, 449f documents the CI-side
   residue). Add: derive the sweep from the violated invariant, and enumerate parallel
   surfaces (CLI/lib/MCP/workflow/import/CI scripts) and other writers of the same state —
   "who else enforces or relies on this invariant?"
3. **Residual-fragility disposition.** Reporting covers bounded sweeps, but confirmed
   adjacent weaknesses from Phase 1 (dossier leads that weren't the root cause but are real)
   and known-uncovered residue of the fix have no required disposition. Add: a "residual
   risk" line in Reporting + file tickets for confirmed adjacent defects instead of
   dropping them (449f is the exemplar of why).
4. **No class-prevention hook.** When the cause is a repeatable pattern, Step 7 fixes live
   instances but never asks "can this class be made impossible or detectable?" (lint, type,
   constructor, CI gate, FP-ledger entry when a gate mis-fired). Add one paragraph: propose
   the structural guard as a ticket (not inline scope-creep).
Keep additions conditional (writeback only where a rebar store exists — the skill is cross-project) and short; the skill already warns against ceremony inflation.

## Q5 — rebar-implement: five escape-rate additions that don't duplicate gates.

Held-out TDD, RED-first, mutation/refactoring litmus, preflight, stacked landing are all in place; plan review owns plan quality, code review owns security/tests/scope advisories, the verifier owns AC satisfaction, CI owns lint/type/module-size/suite. Escaped classes that none of those own, addressable in the skill:
1. **Surface-parity enumeration in 4a.** When the behavior exists on multiple surfaces
   (CLI/lib/MCP), the spec must enumerate them and either cover each or explicitly file a
   follow-up ticket (create + link discovered_from). Targets the proven parity class
   (6e88/1598/5199/0e15/376d). No gate checks this today.
2. **"New config is read" oracle rule in 4b.** Any new config key/env var/flag gets one
   test proving behavior differs when it is set (kills 281f/b00f "parsed but read by
   nothing"). The CI env-registry gate checks documentation, not effect.
3. **Contention edge case in tier selection.** If a leaf mutates the ticket store or other
   shared state, the held-out edge set includes one second-writer/contention case —
   authored to test-design §7's deterministic-barrier discipline (multiple real processes,
   barrier/failpoint, no sleeps), else waived. The discipline matters: the repo's newest
   flaky-test close (08-01) is itself a contention test, and an undisciplined mandate here
   would feed the ~41-bug CI-flakiness cluster. Scoped to the store's dominant bug class,
   not a general mandate.
4. **Gate-finding → oracle upgrade loop in 4g.** On any post-push Verified -1 or LLM
   finding that is real, record in the session log which held-out test should have caught
   it and add that case before amending — converts every escape into a permanent oracle
   member.
5. **Residual-gap disposition at close.** If an edge/E2E case was deliberately descoped,
   file the ticket before closing the leaf (extends the existing discovered_from rule from
   "missing dependency" to "known untested residue").
Anti-additions: no mandatory local `review-code` preflight, no mutation-testing runs per leaf, no re-statement of module-size/lint (already in the 4d brief and CI).
baseline.summary: Bug-trend program: mechanism/escape observability, fragility mitigations, gate levers, and debug/implement skill upgrades (2026-08 retrospective)

baseline.description:
Block direct commits to `main`/`master` at commit time by enabling the pre-commit framework's built-in `no-commit-to-branch` hook, so the "never commit to main" rule this repo already enforces server-side (GitHub ruleset + Gerrit gates) also fails fast locally — at `git commit` instead of only at push/review.

## Why
CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md mandate that no change land on `main` except through Gerrit's two gates. Today nothing stops a local `git commit` while `HEAD` is on `main`; the mistake is only caught later at push. Catching it at commit time is cheaper and matches the repo's "errors happen early" posture.

## What
Add the packaged `no-commit-to-branch` hook (id from `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks`, already pinned at `rev: v6.0.0` in this repo) to the existing hooks list in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, with an EXPLICIT `args: [--branch, main, --branch, master]`.

Rationale for explicit args (chosen over relying on the hook default): the tool default at v6.0.0 is `frozenset(args.branch or ('master', 'main'))` — verified by inspecting the installed hook source `pre_commit_hooks/no_commit_to_branch.py` — so a bare entry already protects `main`. But passing the branches explicitly (a) documents intent inline for the next reader, and (b) is robust to any future change of the upstream default. The cost is two lines; the robustness/clarity gain is worth it. Because the repo already depends on that pinned repo, this adds no new dependency and requires no `rev` bump.

## Scope
- One file: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- Add a single `- id: no-commit-to-branch` entry (with the explicit `args`) under the
  existing `- repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` block (the one
  holding `check-yaml`, `check-toml`, etc.).
- No change to the `local` lint/typecheck hooks; no Makefile change (the hook is
  activated by the existing `pre-commit install` in `make hooks`).
- Non-goal: server-side enforcement (already covered by the GitHub ruleset + Gerrit);
  this is a local fail-fast convenience only, and remains bypassable with
  `git commit --no-verify` by design.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.pre-commit-config.yaml` contains a `no-commit-to-branch` hook id with an
      explicit `args` listing both `main` and `master`, under the
      `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` repo block.
      Proving command: `grep -q 'no-commit-to-branch' .pre-commit-config.yaml && python -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.pre-commit-config.yaml')); hs=[h for r in d['repos'] for h in r['hooks'] if h['id']=='no-commit-to-branch']; a=hs[0].get('args',[]); sys.exit(0 if hs and 'main' in a and 'master' in a else 1)" && echo OK`
- [ ] The config still parses and the hook is registered; running it on the current
      (non-protected) working branch passes.
      Proving command: `pre-commit run no-commit-to-branch --all-files` prints
      `Passed` and exits 0 while `HEAD` is on the feature branch.
- [ ] A `git commit` attempted while `HEAD` is on a protected branch is rejected.
      Proving command (negative path, exit code asserted):
      `git switch -c __scratch_main main 2>/dev/null; git branch -f main; git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main; pre-commit run no-commit-to-branch --all-files; test $? -ne 0 && echo BLOCKED-OK` — i.e. the hook exits non-zero (prints `Failed`) when HEAD is `main`. Restore HEAD to the feature branch afterward. (Run manually in a scratch checkout; not a CI step.)
- [ ] Existing gates are unaffected: `make lint && make typecheck` stay green and the
      YAML hygiene hooks still pass.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && pre-commit run check-yaml --all-files`
      all exit 0.
baseline.summary: Block direct commits to main via pre-commit no-commit-to-branch hook

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The operation-linked compaction sweep is not crash-atomic, and this is the root wedge-generator for the store (parent epic becoming-berserk-grunion; live wedges recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73 and 6ccc-0577-198c-44fa). rebar._commands.compact_trigger.maybe_compact() fires on the tail of every ticket CLOSE and spawns a DETACHED sweep worker (run_sweep → compact.compact_all_cli → compact_txn). The fold performs snapshot-write → retire-rename (tracked source → `*.retired`) → git commit as SEPARATE steps with no rollback. If the detached worker dies, is killed, or races a concurrent writer between the rename and the commit, the SHARED tracker working tree is left DIRTY: tracked deletions plus untracked `*-SNAPSHOT.json` / `*.retired` files. A dirty tree then aborts the next reconverge union merge ("local changes / untracked files would be overwritten"), stranding local ticket commits — the chronic wedge. Interim mitigation `[compact] trigger="off"` is active on the affected host and must be removable once this lands.

## Approach
Make the fold crash-atomic with an intent journal + rollback + startup recovery (the classic write-ahead-intent pattern):
1. **Intent journal**: before mutating anything, `_apply_fold` writes a journal record (ticket dir, snapshot path, sources to retire) to a store-local journal location; if the journal cannot be written, the fold REFUSES (logs, stderr Error, exit 1) without mutating the store.
2. **Ordered mutation + rollback**: perform snapshot-write, then renames, then ONE commit; on any failure after mutation begins, `_rollback_fold` reverse-renames and removes the uncommitted snapshot. If a reverse-rename itself fails (incomplete rollback), RETAIN the uncommitted snapshot rather than delete it — dropping it would lose folded events; the retained state is exactly what fsck reports as SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT and doctor can repair.
3. **Recovery**: compact_recovery.recover_abandoned_folds scans for journals with no matching commit at startup/next sweep entry, discriminating: journal + uncommitted artifacts present → revert (restore sources, remove snapshot, clear journal); journal whose snapshot already reached HEAD → clear journal (fold landed); journal whose snapshot is gone from disk (superseded or fsck-repaired) → clear journal without touching ticket files.
4. Transient-fault discipline: git probes used for discrimination must distinguish "object absent" from transient failures (index.lock contention, timeout) so recovery never mis-classifies a transient fault as "snapshot absent" and reverts a landed fold.
The journal lives with the store and is cleaned in the same locked scope as the fold; the sweep remains operation-linked (portable — no CI dependence).

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py — intent journal write, ordered fold, `_rollback_fold` with the retain-on-incomplete-rollback guard.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact_recovery.py — abandoned-fold discrimination + recovery.
- src/rebar/_commands/compact.py — recovery invocation at sweep entry.
- tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py (new) — kill-at-each-step coverage.
- tests/unit/test_lock_holder_labelling.py — lock label update.

## Testing
- Crash injection at each step boundary (after journal, after snapshot-write, after renames, before commit): the next sweep entry recovers to a clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty) with no ticket events lost.
- Refusal path: journal write failure → exit 1, store untouched (zero mutations, zero commits).
- Incomplete rollback: a failing reverse-rename retains the uncommitted snapshot; assert the snapshot bytes survive and fsck reports the state.
- Recovery discrimination: landed-fold journal is cleared without reverting; superseded/fsck-repaired journal (snapshot gone from disk) is cleared without touching ticket files; transient git failure during the probe does NOT trigger a revert.
- Idempotence: recovery on a clean store makes zero changes; double recovery is safe.
- Manual mutation pass over journal/rollback/recovery branches; every mutant killed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A fold killed at ANY step boundary leaves a store that the next sweep entry converges to clean (no dirty tracked deletions, no stray snapshots, no lost events); checked by the crash-injection tests.
- [x] A fold that cannot journal refuses without mutating the store; checked by the refusal test.
- [x] Recovery never deletes folded-event bytes: incomplete rollback retains the snapshot, and landed/superseded journals are cleared without reverting ticket files; checked by the discrimination tests.
- [x] Transient git faults during recovery probes are not treated as "snapshot absent"; checked by the fault-injection test.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close; after merge the `[compact] trigger="off"` mitigation is removed on the affected host.
baseline.summary: Defense-in-depth: make compaction crash-atomic — detached sweep that dies after write/retire but before commit leaves the tracker tree dirty (source of the untracked leftovers that wedge reconverge)

baseline.description:
Mirror inventory finding F3 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), HIGH, comments already drifted.

## Problem

Which ticket types the plan-review gate reviews is one fact with SIX masters, and nothing asserts they partition `TicketType`:

**Exempt** — `("bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity")`
- `_commands/gates.py:45` `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` (start-work gate)
- `_commands/composer.py:47` `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES` (create-time file-impact nudge)
- `llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:560` — inline literal

**Complement** — `("task", "story", "epic")`
- `llm/plan_review/claimability.py:38` `_REVIEWED_TYPES`
- `_commands/transition_close.py:46` `_PLAN_REVIEW_CLOSE_TYPES`
- `_commands/gates.py:215` — inline literal


## A seventh consumer, deliberately OUT of scope

`llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:108` short-circuits `("session_log", "code_review", "identity")` to a bare exempt PASS, importing nothing from `rebar.types`. The plan-review gate flagged it as a seventh master of this vocabulary, and it is a real unpinned spelling list — but it is NOT another copy of the set above. It is that set MINUS `bug`, because since epic 6982/R4 a bug no longer short-circuits: it takes a LIGHT ADVISORY review tier. The two answer different questions — "is this type exempt from the CLAIM gate?" (this ticket) versus "does this type skip review ENTIRELY?" (that one). Folding a set with different membership and different meaning into this consolidation would change behaviour, not single-source it.

It is tracked as its own child, `florid-cookable-fly` (`90cb-fe23-266e-41ac`), linked `discovered_from` this ticket, with the derivation approach recorded there.

`TicketType` (`types.py:23`) has exactly seven members, so 4 + 3 partitions it TODAY. The defect is that nothing holds it that way: an eighth type lands in NEITHER set and is then neither gated nor exempted. This decides whether the plan-review claim gate runs at all.

The single-sourcing claims are false, and one is drifted beyond being merely optimistic:
- `gates.py:42-44` — "Single-sourced here so ... cannot drift". It is not; five other sites exist.
- `composer.py:42-46` — admits "Kept in lockstep with", and MISDESCRIBES its counterpart: it cites
  the orchestrator as a "bug/session_log short-circuit before P9", but `orchestrator.py:560` sits
  inside the attestation DRIFT-REFRESH candidate path, not P9. Verified by reading the enclosing
  docstring.
- `claimability.py:40-41` prose names 2 of the 4 exempt types.

The only test is `assert "bug" in ...` (`test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py:199`).

## Approach — single-source the pair, then assert the partition

`types.py` already owns `TicketType` and is a true leaf (its only import is `typing`), so it is the canonical home. Declare the exemption there and DERIVE its complement, so the two can never disagree:

    PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES = frozenset({"bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity"})
    PLAN_REVIEW_REVIEWED_TYPES = frozenset(get_args(TicketType)) - PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES

Then point all six sites at them.

**On epic AC2 (do not collapse a distinct concept).** The six sites serve four consumers — the start-work gate, the create-time file-impact nudge, drift-refresh applicability, and the close gate. They are not four different rules; they are four consumers of ONE predicate: "is this a type whose plan the plan-review gate reviews?" Drift-refresh refreshes a plan-review ATTESTATION, which only exists for reviewed types, so it is the same question. `composer`'s own comment states the lockstep intent explicitly, so referencing one constant is faithful to the author's intent rather than a merge of unrelated sets. If a consumer ever needs to diverge, that becomes an explicit reviewed change instead of silent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `types.py` declares the exemption and derives the complement, and a test asserts the
      two are disjoint and their union is exactly `set(get_args(TicketType))`. Verified by that
      test failing if a member is added to `TicketType` without being placed in either set.
- [x] AC2: all six sites reference the canonical constants; no ticket-type literal tuple remains
      at any of them. Verified by a test that greps the six modules for a re-listed exempt or
      reviewed tuple and finds none.
- [x] AC3: adding a hypothetical eighth `TicketType` member fails the partition test rather than
      silently defaulting. Verified by the test parameterizing over an extended member set.
- [x] AC4: the three false/drifted comments are corrected — `gates.py`'s "cannot drift" claim,
      `composer.py`'s misdescription of `orchestrator.py:560` as a P9 short-circuit, and
      `claimability.py`'s partial enumeration. Verified by reading each against the code it cites.
- [x] AC5: behavior is unchanged for all seven current types. Verified by the existing gate and
      close-gate suites passing untouched, and by a test asserting the resolved exempt/reviewed
      sets equal the literals the six sites carried before this change.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "ticket_type or plan_review_exempt or partition" -q` — the
  partition, no-literals, and eighth-type tests (AC1, AC2, AC3).
- `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` — proves the six call sites still gate identically (AC5); these
  constants sit on the claim and close paths, so a mistake here is broad and loud.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
baseline.summary: Plan-review ticket-type exemption is split across six sites with no enforcement (mirror F3)

## Context / Problem
The first proposal mixed forward validity with historical convention. Revise it to a small deterministic floor intended to have no false positives, then use accepted history only as an adversarial counterexample corpus.

## Approach
Test failure patterns rather than preferred prose style. A rule qualifies for the floor only when the detected state is structurally incompatible with an executable plan; otherwise it remains advisory. Search closed tickets carrying signed plan-review and completion evidence, inspect every matching candidate in context, and narrow or remove any rule with a legitimate match.

## Criteria Under Review
1. An Acceptance Criteria checkbox must contain non-whitespace text after the checkbox marker.
2. Two Acceptance Criteria items must not be exact duplicates after joining continuations and normalizing whitespace/case.
3. Active execution prose must not contain a bare unresolved sentinel (`TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, or `???`) in Approach, Scope, Testing, or Acceptance Criteria; ignore fenced code, inline code, quotations, examples, explicit removal/prohibition assertions, and superseded/history sections.
4. Structured file-impact entries, when present, must have a nonempty path and nonempty reason; absence of file impact is allowed.
5. A `[rebar:<id>]` prerequisite citation used as plan evidence must resolve to a direct verified upstream dependency; ignore literal examples in code spans/fences.

## Scope
Read-only ticket-store analysis. The only mutation is the final findings comment on this ticket; no repository files or other ticket material will be changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every criterion under review has a documented historical search and cited matching tickets, verified by the final findings comment.
- [ ] Every legitimate matching ticket is treated as a counterexample and causes the rule to be narrowed or rejected, verified by before/after detection wording in the final findings.
- [ ] The final recommendation clearly separates hard-floor rules from advisory signals, verified by a structured classification table in the final findings.
- [ ] If a rule has no historical match, the finding says that explicitly without claiming proof of soundness, verified by the final findings comment.
baseline.summary: Adversarially validate a revised deterministic clarity floor

baseline.description:
# Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes

## Context / Problem

At 2026-08-03 19:13 an agent session posted a comment on ticket 129e containing a full zsh environment dump. The dump embedded SEVEN live credentials (Anthropic, 2x GitHub PAT, Gemini/Google, Jira/Atlassian, OpenAI service-account, PyPI). GitHub push protection then rejected `refs/heads/tickets` (GH013) on the Anthropic key, so EVERY session's store writes queued local-only — 153 commits at diagnosis. One comment caused a full store-sharing outage for all concurrent agents, and it presented as transient contention: the only symptom was `WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed after 3 retries`.

This is urgent now because the store auto-pushes to a single shared ref, so any agent that pastes an environment dump into a comment wedges the branch for everyone until a human intervenes.

## Root cause

There is no content screening anywhere in the write path. `_store/event_append._validate_event` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:126`) checks the envelope shape and `event_type` membership only, and never inspects `data`. Confirmed RED before any fix: `leaf.comment(<ticket>, "KEY=<live-shaped anthropic key>")` returns 0 and the COMMENT event lands on disk.

Corollary the original diagnosis got wrong, and which this plan corrects: `append_event` is NOT the single write seam. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:258-276` writes Jira-sourced COMMENT/EDIT bodies — untrusted EXTERNAL input — by calling the halves of `finalize_event` directly, deliberately bypassing `append_event` because that helper commits+pushes eagerly. The txn and delete cores bypass it too. A screen at `append_event` would therefore have left a credential pasted into a Jira comment able to reproduce this exact wedge.

## Approach

Add a deterministic, pure secret screen and enforce it at `_seam.finalize_event` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:329`) — the one function `append_event` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:405`), the txn/delete cores, and the reconciler's inbound translate all route through. Inbound translate is changed to call the seam rather than its halves, and a test pins that routing so it cannot regress into a bypass again.

On a match the write is REFUSED — the event does not land — per the operator decision recorded on this ticket (2026-08-07). Redaction was considered and rejected: silently rewriting a caller's payload makes the stored event differ from what the caller believes it wrote, and in an append-only store that divergence is unrecoverable after the fact. Refusal is loud, reversible, and leaves the caller in control. A force override (`--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>`) keeps a false positive from ever being a permanent hard block; it is the same escape-hatch shape as `--force-close`, is CLI-only (never exposed over MCP), and records who forced and why on the event itself so a forced write is auditable.

Refusal must be safe to leave ON by default, which drives two design constraints:

- It names WHICH family fired and WHERE (field + line), so using the override is an informed
  choice rather than a blind retry.
- It never echoes the secret. `SecretFinding` (`src/rebar/secret_screen.py:116`) carries
  family/field/line and structurally has NO value field, so the value cannot leak through the
  refusal message, logs, stderr, or the event on disk. Payload dict KEYS are redacted before
  they reach the printed field path, since a credential used as a key would otherwise leak
  through the path itself.

Detection is tuned by measurement against the live store rather than by argument. Patterns match a FIXED-WIDTH window rather than a greedy `{80,}` quantifier, so same-class padding appended after a real key (400 `-` characters — an ASCII rule in a log or env dump) cannot dilute the entropy average below the floor and make the screen miss a genuine credential. The PEM pattern is line-anchored, because a real paste puts the banner on its own line whereas prose enumerating banners does not.

`llm/workflow/lint.py` consumes the shared pattern table instead of keeping a second copy, which had already drifted — it lacked the Anthropic/OpenAI/Atlassian/PyPI families the incident actually carried.

## Scope

Recorded via `set-file-impact` (paths). New: `src/rebar/secret_screen.py` (pattern table, pure `scan_text`/`screen_event_data`, override audit record, refusal message) and `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py`. Modified: `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (enforce at `finalize_event`), `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` (parse the override above BOTH dispatch routes so every write verb honours it, not just `comment`), `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (thread the override through), `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint.py` (consume the shared table), `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py` (route through the seam), `docs/user-guide.md` (the command-substitution hazard + the screen/override).

Out of scope: surfacing the GH013 push-rejection detail. That was bug 2a76 and already landed on main (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`); AC5 below records it rather than duplicating it.

## Testing

- Fire: each of the families the incident dump carried is refused, asserted via the family name
  in the refusal. Credential-shaped fixtures are ASSEMBLED AT RUNTIME (`_fake_secret`,
  `_pem_banner`) so this repo never commits a live-shaped literal and the repo's own secret
  scanner stays fully armed on the test file.
- No-fire: the verbatim benign strings the live-store sweep found — a truncated placeholder
  (`sk-ant-api03-...`), a regex literal (`sk-ant-api03-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{93,}`), and prose
  enumerating PEM banners — all still write.
- Padding: a real key followed by 400 same-class padding characters is still refused (the
  fixed-width-window regression).
- No-echo: the secret value AND its head/tail fragments are absent from five channels — the
  exception message, stdout, stderr, the log records, and every byte on disk. The forced-write
  path is checked separately because it is the only path that logs, so asserting on log records
  in the refusal path alone would be vacuous. A positive control proves the on-disk assertion
  can actually observe a landed value.
- Bypass: a test pins that the reconciler's inbound translate routes through `finalize_event`,
  and another pins that the override is absent from the MCP surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A write whose event data matches a high-confidence credential pattern is REFUSED at
      `_seam.finalize_event` and the event file does not exist on disk afterwards — verified by
      a test that asserts the command's non-zero exit and the absence of the event.
- [x] The refusal names the matched secret family and the field+line, and does NOT echo the
      secret value — verified by asserting the value and its head/tail fragments are absent from
      the exception message, stdout, stderr, log records, and all on-disk bytes.
- [x] Benign look-alike text (truncated placeholders, regex literals, prose enumerating
      banners — the verbatim strings from the live-store sweep) still writes successfully, so
      the screen is safe to leave on by default — verified by explicit negative-case tests.
- [x] The screen covers writers that do NOT go through `append_event`, specifically the
      reconciler's inbound Jira translate — verified by a test asserting inbound translate
      routes through `finalize_event`.
- [x] `--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>` allows the refused write for every write verb, records
      the reason and bypassed families on the event, and is absent from the MCP tool surface —
      verified by tests over the CLI verbs and a test asserting MCP non-exposure.
- [x] The shell command-substitution hazard that produced the incident is documented in
      `docs/user-guide.md` with the exact wrong and right forms.
- [x] The incident is recorded on this ticket with its blast radius, including that the only
      control which actually stopped the leak (GitHub push protection) was outside this project.
- [x] Surfacing the GH013 push-rejection reason is confirmed ALREADY satisfied on main by bug
      2a76 (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`) and is not duplicated here.

## Absorbed from e4f4 (closed as duplicate)

e4f4-295b-2c03-44c4 described the same underlying defect (the store accepting secret-bearing event bodies) and was filed about 8 minutes apart from this ticket with no link between them. Its two ACs with no counterpart here — documenting the shell command-substitution hazard for agents, and recording the incident with its blast radius — are folded into the Acceptance Criteria above so nothing is lost by closing it.
baseline.summary: Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. Take epic `1386-5e7c-391d-4a74` (tearful-cleansable-gopher) and its children as authored.
2. Run `rebar review-plan` on the epic and on children `35bc-aef6-efd5-4df5` and
   `2aa6-726a-ea56-4d6c`.
3. Observe every one returns **PASS with 0 blocking findings** and signs a certified
   attestation. The epic's own signed manifest records `plan-review: PASS` / `blocking: 0` /
   `advisory: 11`.
4. Implement the tickets exactly as specified.
5. Observe that **seven acceptance criteria across the three tickets cannot be satisfied**, and
   that the contradictions are visible in the plan text itself — no implementation knowledge is
   needed to see them.

**Expected:** a plan whose acceptance criteria contradict each other, contradict their own
Scope, or contradict a sibling's acceptance criteria is not certifiable. Plan review should
either block or, at minimum, raise these as findings.

**Actual:** all three passed with zero blocking findings. Every contradiction surfaced later —
either mid-implementation or at the completion-verifier close gate, after the work was done.

## Why the plans were not completeable

Seven instances, in four distinct failure classes. All quotes are the ORIGINAL text as
reviewed; each has since been amended.

### Class A — an AC contradicts its OWN ticket's Scope or another AC in the SAME ticket

The strongest class: both halves of the contradiction sit in a single document the reviewer
read in full.

1. **Epic `1386` AC1 vs its own Scope.** AC1: *"No live source file under `src/rebar/` matches
   `Success Criteria` / `success criteria` / `success criterion` (case-insensitive)"*, granting
   exclusions only for frozen fixtures and the vendor bundle. Its own **OUT OF SCOPE** section,
   ~15 lines earlier, defers *"the `dod_uncertifiable` / 'definition-of-done' vocabulary in the
   verifier prompts"* — three live files under `src/rebar/` that therefore keep matching
   forever. AC1 could never pass.

2. **Story `2aa6` AC1 vs its own Scope AND its own AC6.** AC1 required
   `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ ...` to return **no
   matches**. Its Scope has a section headed **"EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED"** naming
   `plan_review_T2.md:10`, and its **AC6** states that a grep on that same file *"still returns
   its one match"*. AC1 and AC6 are directly contradictory: one demands zero matches in a
   directory, the other demands one match in a file inside it.

3. **Story `2aa6` AC3 vs AC6.** AC3 required the generated criteria guide's SC grep to be
   *"empty"*. The guide is generated from the criteria registry and embeds each criterion's
   prompt verbatim, so T2's AC6-protected phrase necessarily echoes into it.

4. **Story `35bc` AC3 vs the epic's design.** AC3: *"No test file under
   `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, `tests/interfaces/store/` or
   `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` contains `## Success Criteria`."* But
   sibling `5f4d`'s AC1 requires its reintroduction guard be *"proven by a test that injects
   one"*. The epic therefore REQUIRES a file containing the literal string, and the natural home
   is the contract test `35bc` itself adds. The completion verifier blocked the close on exactly
   this, twice.

### Class B — an AC contradicts a mechanical, checkable property of the artifact

5. **Epic `1386` AC5.** *"`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is REGENERATED (not hand-edited)
   ... and contains no SC vocabulary."* The same criterion asserts the file is generated from
   the registry, and the registry contains T2's excluded prompt. The criterion contradicts
   itself in one sentence: regenerate from a source containing X, and contain no X.

### Class C — an AC hard-codes a count that the plan elsewhere says to recompute

6. **Epic `1386` AC4.** *"The **108** store tickets carrying `## Success Criteria` are
   migrated."* Child `0a8c`'s Scope explicitly says *"the migration recomputes the set rather
   than hard-coding it"*. The real number at run time was **106**. A literal reading of AC4 can
   never be satisfied, and a count in an AC is guaranteed to drift between authoring and
   execution.

### Class D — unowned scope: a parent AC that no child covers

7. **Epic `1386` AC1 vs the decomposition.** AC1 requires clearing SC vocabulary from every live
   file under `src/rebar/`, but `src/rebar/llm/completion.py:288` (*"its success criteria are met
   across children"*) was covered by **no child story**: `35bc` took the detectors, `2aa6` the
   reviewer prompts, `93d0` the eval specs, `44c7` the guides/docs. The union of children did not
   cover the parent's AC, so the epic could not close however perfectly each child was executed.
   This is notable because the criteria registry already contains **G3**, whose stated checklist
   is *"The union of children covers each parent acceptance/success criterion"* — the exact
   condition that was violated — and G3 routes at container scope. G3 ran and did not flag it.

## Cost of late detection

Each instance was found DURING implementation or at the close gate, not at review:

- `35bc` AC3 — the completion verifier refused the close twice. Resolution required amending the
  criterion, which invalidated the attestation as `stale-material` and forced a **full LLM
  re-review** before the ticket could close.
- `2aa6` AC1 and AC3 — found while implementing; same amend-plus-re-review cost.
- Epic AC1/AC4/AC5 and the unowned `completion.py` site — found only by hand-auditing the epic's
  AC against the real tree after three of six children were already closed and merged.

So the failure mode is not merely "a bad plan shipped": it is that **plan review certifies plans
that the completion verifier later refuses**, and the disagreement surfaces at the most expensive
possible moment — after the code is written, reviewed, and in `35bc`'s and `0a8c`'s case already
merged. Every correction also costs a re-review, because amending a description invalidates the
attestation.

## Signal that the reviewer CAN catch a neighbouring class

On re-review, `2aa6` was correctly **BLOCKED** for a stale cross-ticket factual claim (its plan
asserted prerequisite `1f32` *"has NOT yet merged"* when `show_ticket` showed it closed). So
cross-ticket fact-checking against live ticket state does fire. The seven failures above are a
different class — internal consistency between an AC and its own Scope, its sibling ACs, or the
decomposition — and none of them fired.

## Out of scope for this ticket

**Do not** analyse or redesign the plan-review process here. No investigation of criteria
prompts, routing, or detectors. This ticket exists to RECORD the evidence in detail; a follow-up
session owns the diagnosis and the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] This ticket records all seven instances with the ORIGINAL criterion text, the specific
      text it contradicts, and the ticket each belongs to — enough for a follow-up session to
      reproduce the analysis without re-deriving it.
- [ ] The four failure classes (A: intra-ticket contradiction; B: contradiction with a mechanical
      property of a generated artifact; C: hard-coded count vs recompute-at-run-time; D: parent AC
      not covered by any child) are each named with at least one worked example.
- [ ] The evidence that these plans PASSED is recorded — epic `1386`'s signed manifest showing
      `plan-review: PASS`, `blocking: 0`, `advisory: 11`.
- [ ] The observation that G3 ("the union of children covers each parent acceptance/success
      criterion") exists, routes at container scope, ran, and did not flag the class-D gap is
      recorded as an observation only, with no diagnosis attached.
- [ ] The late-detection cost is recorded: which gate actually caught each instance
      (completion verifier / mid-implementation / manual audit) and that each fix forced a
      re-review via `stale-material`.
- [ ] No change is made to any plan-review prompt, criterion, routing entry or detector under
      this ticket.
baseline.summary: Plan review certified an epic whose acceptance criteria were mutually unsatisfiable

## Summary

Found by the Step 7 (Axis 1 construct) sibling sweep while fixing `satiated-activated-aardwolf` (5524-e353-2e2d-4dbe). Same detect-only drift class as `CONFIG_PATHS`, but on the gerrit deploy-key materializer, which was overlooked when `materialize-g2p-config.sh` was added to `CONFIG_PATHS`.

`infra/gerrit/materialize-deploy-key.sh` is an SSM→file materializer (it puts the replication deploy key into the gerrit user's dir), a direct sibling of `infra/gerrit/materialize-g2p-config.sh`. `materialize-g2p-config.sh` IS enumerated in `CONFIG_PATHS` (detect-only, `reason=config_manual`); `materialize-deploy-key.sh` is in **no** manifest. So a merged change to the deploy-key materializer rsyncs to `/opt/rebar` and silently does nothing — the same drift class `CONFIG_PATHS` detect-only was created to make visible.

## Class-level plan (PRIMARY ticket for the manifest-omission class)

This ticket is the primary for a ONE class-level change fixing both confirmed instances of the class "an infra SOURCE that affects the running environment is absent from every path manifest in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, so a merged change to it drifts silently". The change touches ONLY `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (two manifest additions) plus the new/extended regression tests. Sibling ticket `5d4c-a25b-b612-4aca` (broke-choleric-hound) is fixed in the same change.

Both instances proven at runtime with a discriminating contrast against the sibling source that IS in the manifest (see RCA comments on each ticket).

## Acceptance criteria (both instances are criteria)

- [ ] **Instance 1 (this ticket, DETECT-ONLY):** `infra/gerrit/materialize-deploy-key.sh` is enumerated in `CONFIG_PATHS` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, so a deploy-key-materializer-only change emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR reason=config_manual` (parity with `materialize-g2p-config.sh`). Applying it touches gerrit — the same operator-judgement boundary as the rest of `CONFIG_PATHS` — so signal only, no auto-reload.
- [ ] **Instance 2 (sibling 5d4c, APPLY-PARITY):** `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` is enumerated in `MCP_PATHS`, so an entrypoint-source-only change rebuilds the MCP image via the EXISTING blue-green mcp deploy path (ADR 0079 v1 mcp auto-apply scope; reuse the existing path exactly — no new apply semantics).

- [ ] `make lint` (incl. shellcheck) + full `tests/scripts` suite green.

## Structural guard (decided separately — NOT in this change)

A structural manifest-completeness guard for this class is being evaluated separately and is intentionally out of scope here. This change closes the two confirmed instances; any further same-class instances found are enumerated in the final report, not filed, per the sweep-containment directive.

## Evidence

- `grep -oE "^[A-Z_]+_PATHS='[^']*'" infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh | grep materialize-deploy-key` → no match.

baseline.description:
## Why

Completion-verification is single-pass and, by contract, emits findings ONLY for FAILING criteria (`reconcile_verdict` flips a PASS-with-findings to FAIL). On a PASS it persists just signed counts via the attestation — no per-criterion record exists anywhere, and the FAIL-only sidecar never fires. So a successfully-closed ticket has no durable per-criterion completion audit, unlike its plan and code reviews.

## What

1. Extend the verifier's output contract with a positive per-criterion `criteria[]` array — one
   `{criterion, met, citation, kind}` entry per acceptance/success criterion evaluated (met
   status, a source-code or attestation citation, and its codebase-verifiable / operator-attested
   kind). This rides ALONGSIDE the failures-only `findings`; a PASS keeps `findings == []`.
2. Emit a completion sidecar on PASS (not only FAIL) persisting that array plus the verdict,
   runner, model, and material fingerprint.

Completion stays single-pass — this adds a per-criterion result list, NOT a four-pass structure.

## Schema-version strategy (explicit)

Do NOT bump the existing FAIL schema. Keep `SCHEMA_FAIL = "completion_verifier_fail_v1"` unchanged (so `latest_fail_verdict` and the existing FAIL-record tests are untouched). Add a SECOND constant `SCHEMA_PASS = "completion_verifier_pass_v1"` for PASS records; `build_payload` picks the schema by verdict. This keeps `test_fail_close_persists_durable_verdict` and `test_pass_close_leaves_no_fail_record` green (a PASS record is a different schema, so `latest_fail_verdict` still returns None on a PASS).

The `kind` field vocabulary is the CLOSED set `{"codebase-verifiable", "operator-attested"}` (matching ADR 0043's two criterion kinds); `met` is a bool; `citation` reuses the shared `Citation` shape (nullable).

## Scope (enumerated edit targets)

- `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py` — **load-bearing**: `CompletionVerdict` is a pydantic `BaseModel`
  with no `extra="allow"`, so pydantic v2 DROPS any `criteria[]` the agent emits unless it is a
  declared field. Add a `Criterion` sub-model (`{criterion: str, met: bool, citation: Citation |
  None, kind: str}`) and a `criteria: list[Criterion] = Field(default_factory=list)` field to
  `CompletionVerdict`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — add the OPTIONAL `criteria[]` property
  (items `{criterion, met, citation, kind}`); `findings` stays required, `criteria` optional. The
  model↔schema PARITY test
  (`tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py::test_completion_verdict_pins_to_schema`)
  asserts the model's field set equals the schema's property set, so it MUST be UPDATED in lockstep
  to include `criteria` (it will NOT pass unchanged) — this is an expected, in-scope test edit.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_reconcile_input.schema.json` — **required because this schema is
  `additionalProperties: false`**: add a `raw_criteria` (array) property, else the workflow's
  `completion_reconcile` step would reject/not-carry the criteria. (The verify step's `criteria`
  output must be threaded into the reconcile step — see the YAML edit below.)
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml` — in the `completion_reconcile`
  step's `with:`, thread `raw_criteria: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.criteria }}` (alongside the
  existing `raw_verdict`/`raw_findings`), so the agent's positive array reaches the reconcile op.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py` — `completion_reconcile(ctx)` reads `raw_criteria` from
  `ctx.inputs` and sets `result["criteria"] = list(ctx.inputs.get("raw_criteria") or [])` on the
  reconciled verdict BEFORE `validate_structured`, so the workflow (close-gate) path carries
  `criteria[]` end-to-end — not only the bespoke `verify_completion` path.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md` — update the prompt: instruct the agent to
  emit `criteria[]` with one met-record per evaluated criterion (each with citation + kind).
  `findings` stays failures-only.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — `reconcile_verdict` must NOT flip a PASS that carries a
  populated `criteria[]` but empty `findings` (it keys the flip on `findings`; ensure `criteria[]`
  is not stripped and add the regression test).
- `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` — the existing constant is named `SCHEMA` (value
  `"completion_verifier_fail_v1"`). Do NOT rename it (that would churn the FAIL reader + its
  tests); keep `SCHEMA` as the FAIL schema and ADD a second constant
  `SCHEMA_PASS = "completion_verifier_pass_v1"`. `build_payload` branches on the verdict
  (PASS → `SCHEMA_PASS` + `criteria[]`; FAIL → unchanged `SCHEMA` + `findings`); add
  `latest_pass_record(ticket_id)` mirroring `latest_fail_verdict` but schema-guarded to
  `SCHEMA_PASS`. `latest_fail_verdict` (guarded to `SCHEMA`) is untouched, so a PASS record is
  invisible to it and the existing FAIL tests stay green.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — on the PASS path (after the verdict is confirmed
  PASS, before `_verdict_manifest` signs), add a best-effort `completion_sidecar.emit(result,
  material=…, repo_root=repo_root)` (swallow its own errors — persistence is observability, never
  load-bearing on the close). Set `result.setdefault("ticket_id", resolved_id)` first.

## Compatibility & rollback

`criteria[]` is OPTIONAL — an older agent/response that omits it yields today's behavior (PASS counts only), and the failures-only `findings` invariant is unchanged, so nothing regresses. No backfill. Reverting stops the PASS-path emit and drops the field; existing FAIL records stay readable (their schema is untouched).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A completion PASS returns a `criteria[]` array with one met-record per evaluated criterion
      and `findings` stays empty. Oracle: a unit test on `reconcile_verdict` feeding a PASS
      verdict with a populated `criteria[]`, asserting it is NOT flipped to FAIL and the array
      survives; plus a test that the `CompletionVerdict` pydantic model round-trips `criteria[]`
      (proving it is not dropped).
- [ ] A completion PASS emits a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` sidecar persisting the per-criterion
      array. Oracle: an integration test that closes a ticket through the gate with a stub verifier
      returning the new PASS shape and asserts on the emitted event JSON (via the real sidecar
      emit path), plus that `latest_pass_record` reads it back.
- [ ] Live end-to-end: running the real completion verifier (`[agents]` extra + API key) on a
      fixture ticket whose criteria are met produces a PASS with a populated `criteria[]`
      persisted to the sidecar. Oracle: a live/E2E test exercising the real agent path, gated on
      LLM availability (skipped with a recorded reason otherwise).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: completion-verification lossless PASS capture (per-criterion record)

## Context
The GitHub About description currently says Rebar is an LLM-first event-sourced ticket system and Jira reconciler, then identifies GitHub as a read-only mirror. It does not explain the capability that distinguishes Rebar from conventional trackers. ADR 0018 and the plan-review gate guidance establish enforceable review before claim. The completion gate and operation-certificate guidance establish signed verification before close.

## Plan
- Replace the `navapbc/rebar` repository description with concise client-facing wording that leads with plan review.
- State the observable mechanisms rather than make an unsupported superiority claim.
- Preserve the read-only GitHub mirror and Gerrit code-review facts.
- Keep the description within GitHub limits and avoid internal implementation terms.
- Read the repository metadata back after the update and record the exact value.
- Change GitHub repository metadata only.

## Proposed Description
Rebar can block work until an AI plan review passes, require signed completion verification before close, and reconcile its event-sourced ticket record with Jira across CLI, Python, and MCP. GitHub is a read-only mirror. Code review runs in Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The GitHub About description leads with enforceable plan review before work begins.
- [x] It names signed completion verification, event-sourced history, Jira reconciliation, and the CLI, Python, and MCP interfaces.
- [x] It preserves the read-only mirror and Gerrit review facts.
- [x] It fits the GitHub repository-description limit.
- [x] [non-codebase] `gh repo view navapbc/rebar --json description` returns the approved description exactly.

baseline.description:
Provide an explicit capture helper that lets agents record verbose session logs without hand-assembling `create` + `comment` calls — one call that creates a `session_log` on first use and appends an entry — available from all three interfaces.

## Why

Beyond plain `create` / `edit` / `comment`, agents benefit from a single convenience call that creates the session log (if needed) and appends activity to it, so verbose logging is low-friction and consistent. It is thin sugar over the existing shared write path, so it flows to library, CLI, and MCP uniformly.

## What

- A core helper that resolves/creates the current `session_log` (carrying a short
  work-summary title) and appends an entry as a COMMENT, via the existing
  `composer.create_core` + `leaf.comment` write path.
- Library: `rebar.append_session_log(entry, *, summary=None)`.
- CLI: `rebar session-log append "<entry>"` (and a `start --summary` to create the
  log explicitly).
- MCP: a write-gated `log_session(entry)` tool (no-op/refused under
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`).
- Allow optional `relates_to` / `discovered_from` links from the log to the work
  it documents.

## Scope

Explicit, agent-invoked capture helper only. Relies on the foundation (the type + write-path rules). An automatic per-session hook is **explicitly out of scope** for this epic (no honest cross-interface trigger — the CLI has no long-lived process — and it introduces write amplification).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A capture helper can create a `session_log` and append entries to it from the
      library, the CLI, and MCP, all through the single shared write path.
- [ ] First use creates exactly one log (with the summary title); subsequent calls
      append rather than recreating.
- [ ] Logs may carry `relates_to` / `discovered_from` links; blocking links remain
      refused.
- [ ] The MCP tool is refused/no-op under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`.
- [ ] Tests cover create-then-append and the three-interface parity.
baseline.summary: Session-log capture helper (explicit, all three interfaces)

baseline.description:
With a key-set prev, keys present in both prev and curr route to `_compute_mutations_emit_both` with an empty `local_fields`, producing ~516 mutations per pass that are provably inert but not free. Skip them. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Each inert mutation still traverses `_apply_one`, which calls `_recheck_drift` -> `concurrency.snapshot_head(repo_root)` — **a `git rev-parse` subprocess per mutation**. So ~516 extra git invocations per pass, ~516 `RECON: batch_outcome` stderr lines, ~516 outcome records in the manifest, and an inflated `mutation_count` so a converged pass reports 516 instead of 0. It also enlarges the HEAD-drift window. Under `BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` (cap 10) or `BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE` (cap 100) these compete for cap slots with genuine work (`apply_planning.py:90-101`) and can starve it — production defaults to `LIVE` (cap `None`), so that risk is latent, not live.

## Approach
Short-circuit `_compute_mutations_emit_both` when `local_fields` is falsy, or equivalently skip the `_emit` at `differ.py:590` when the resolved `changed` dict contains no field that survives `_mutation_to_batch_dict`. ~5 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With a key-set prev over a real corpus, `(outbound, update)` mutations with an empty effective
      payload are **0** (down from ~516). Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations` + the corpus script.
- [ ] Mutations with a genuine non-empty effective payload are still emitted unchanged — the
      negative control. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `mutation_count` on a converged pass is 0. Tier: **integration** asserting the pass record.
- [ ] `git rev-parse` invocation count per pass drops correspondingly. Tier: **integration** with a
      counting shim.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/differ.py`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A4-2.
baseline.summary: A4-3: skip the differ's branch-3 emit when the resolved payload cannot reach Jira

baseline.description:
## Context

`model_max_output_tokens` (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`, `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) knows only the three Claude ladder models and falls back to `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` (16,000) for an unmapped model. Amazon Nova models on Bedrock accept at most 10,000 output tokens, so every review call that rides the "raise to model max" seam with a Nova model is rejected by Bedrock with `ValidationException: The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 10000` before it runs — measured live during the 2026-08-11 model-comparison experiments (rebar ticket b902-18af-14ed-4da1), where the whole plan-review LLM phase collapsed to INDETERMINATE until the table was patched in-process. Nova Pro subsequently completed 8/8 end-to-end plan-review replays, so the ceiling entry is the only blocker to running these models through rebar.

## Plan

Add four entries to `MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`: `("nova-pro", 10_000)`, `("nova-2-lite", 10_000)`, `("nova-lite", 10_000)`, `("nova-micro", 10_000)`. The lookup is a plain substring match, and `nova-lite` is NOT a substring of `nova-2-lite` (the `-2-` breaks it), so both forms are listed explicitly; the full Bedrock inference-profile ids (`us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` etc.) are covered by the same substring semantics. Values per the AWS Bedrock model documentation: Nova family max output tokens = 10,000. No behavior change for any currently-configured model: the table is consulted only when the resolved model matches an entry, and the existing conservative fallback stays for everything else.

Extend the existing unit coverage of `model_max_output_tokens` with the Nova ids (full Bedrock profile-id form and bare form).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `model_max_output_tokens("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` returns 10000. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from rebar.llm.review_kernel.verify import model_max_output_tokens as f; assert f('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')==10000 and f('us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0')==10000 and f('claude-sonnet-4-6')==128000"` exits 0.
- [x] A unit test pins the Nova entries alongside the existing Claude entries. Verify: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_max_tokens_model_ceiling_1019.py -x` passes.
- [x] Unknown models still fall back to the configured default (existing behavior pinned by an assertion in the same test). Verify: same pytest run passes.
baseline.summary: Teach MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS the Amazon Nova output ceilings (10k) so Bedrock Nova calls stop 400ing

Steering a resumption away from already-searched places (or toward where credited evidence was found) requires an argument-level tool-call transcript that the verifier telemetry does not currently carry. baseline.description:
## What

Generate `docs/cli-reference.md` from the CLI's OWN help data, so the command reference cannot drift, and gate it in CI like `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`.

## Source of truth (verified — the CLI surface is two disjoint families)
1. **50 help-backed subcommands** — fully enumerable, RELIABLE help text:
   - `rebar._cli._help.known_subcommands() -> frozenset[str]` (returns 50).
   - `rebar._cli._help.subcommand_help(sub) -> str|None` — the full pinned usage text
     (package data under `rebar._cli.help/*.txt`). Reliable; use this for full help.
2. **16 intercept-arm commands** — handled in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` main() before the
   `known_subcommands()` check (~lines 372-447), with NO `help/*.txt` and no overview row:
   `reconcile, review, review-code, scan-spec, verify-completion, review-plan, sign-review,
   enrich, explain, verify-commit-ticket, workflow, llm, jira-onboard, prompt, criteria,
   config`.

**Do NOT subprocess-capture `rebar <cmd> --help` for the intercepts.** Verified gotcha: `rebar enrich --help` has no argparse parser (`cmd_enrich()` in `rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py`) — it calls `drain()` and prints JSON with exit 0, so a "non-empty + exit 0" guard would silently store JSON garbage as "help". Subprocess capture across 16 heterogeneous commands is fragile. Instead: carry a hardcoded **curated one-line description** for each of the 16 intercept commands in the generator (`INTERCEPT_COMMANDS: dict[str,str]`), and DRIFT-GATE the dict's key set against the `if argv[0] == "..."` ladder in `_cli/__init__.py` so a newly-added intercept without a curated entry fails the generator loudly.

Total ~66 commands, all listed; the 50 with full pinned help, the 16 with a curated one-liner (marked as advanced/intercept commands, "see `rebar <cmd> --help`").

## Scope
- Add `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` (new): Family 1 via `_help.known_subcommands()` +
  `subcommand_help()`; Family 2 via the `INTERCEPT_COMMANDS` curated dict. Emit
  `docs/cli-reference.md` with a "Generated by … do not edit" header (mirror
  `gen_env_registry.py`), each command name rendered backtick-wrapped for exact matching.
- The generator asserts `set(INTERCEPT_COMMANDS) == <ladder set parsed from _cli/__init__.py>`
  and exits non-zero on mismatch (so a new/removed intercept is caught — no subprocess).
- `--check` mode: regenerate in memory, exit non-zero if committed file differs.
- Wire a drift gate into BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND
  `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (the actual Verified gate; a parity test
  `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` ENFORCES every `scripts/*.py` in test.yml also
  appears in gerrit-verify.yaml — omitting the latter breaks `make test`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` is generated (marked generated) and lists BOTH families:
      every `known_subcommands()` entry (50) with its full help AND all 16 intercept
      commands with a curated one-liner.
- [ ] Completeness proof, EXACT backtick match (no substring false positives like
      `review` vs `review-plan`), prints nothing:
      `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py && for c in $(python -c "from rebar._cli import _help; print(' '.join(sorted(_help.known_subcommands())))") reconcile review review-code scan-spec verify-completion review-plan sign-review enrich explain verify-commit-ticket workflow llm jira-onboard prompt criteria config; do grep -qF "\`$c\`" docs/cli-reference.md || echo "MISSING $c"; done`
- [ ] Intercept-drift guard: `set(INTERCEPT_COMMANDS)` equals the ladder set parsed from
      `_cli/__init__.py`; a mismatch makes the generator exit non-zero. DETERMINISTIC proof
      (prints `CAUGHT`): temporarily remove one key from the dict in memory and confirm the
      generator's self-check fails — covered by a held-out unit test that mutates the dict
      and asserts a non-zero/raise. (The generator runs this parity check on every run.)
- [ ] Drift gate works — a stale committed reference fails `--check` (prints `CAUGHT`):
      `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py; printf '\nstale\n' >> docs/cli-reference.md; python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo MISS || echo CAUGHT; python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`
- [ ] The gate is wired in BOTH CI files (prints nothing):
      `for f in .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml; do grep -qF 'gen_cli_reference.py' "$f" || echo "NOT WIRED: $f"; done`
      and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q` passes.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` stay green.

Files: `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` (new), `docs/cli-reference.md` (new/generated), `.github/workflows/test.yml`, `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
baseline.summary: P1: Generate the CLI command reference (generator + drift gate)
