baseline.description:
## Context

Designed under 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d (see its design comment for the full argument and Limits).

`llm/overlap/queue.py::_events_of` opens and `json.load`s EVERY matching event file, and `reduce_ticket` calls it three times per ticket. `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` calls `pending_enrichment` as its "cheap gate" on every write against a 20 ms budget (`overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms`). Measured on this repo's live tracker (3,727 ticket dirs): the gate does 11,181 `listdir` calls and 4,977 file opens per invocation, and logs `enrich drain gate check took 404.9 ms (> 20 ms budget)` on every rebar command (observed 404-654 ms). The opens term grows without bound as enrichment re-runs accumulate; the budget does not.

`digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest` is already bounded (sorts dirents, walks newest-first, returns on the first parseable payload) and needs no change. This ticket is the queue side only.

## Plan

Make the queue reduce read newest-first and lazily, changing no on-disk behaviour.

The event filename is `{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json` where the prefix is the same monotonic timestamp the reducer compares (`_store/event_append.py::event_filename`, built by `_prepare_event` from the validated event's own timestamp). Timestamps are fixed-width ns integers, so lexicographic filename order is timestamp order. Therefore:

- `_latest(dir, TYPE)` reads only the LAST matching dirent, falling back to the next-older on a
  parse failure - the same shape `latest_ticket_digest` already uses. 1 open per type per ticket.
- `claim()` arbitration needs only CLAIM events newer than the latest ENQUEUE, which are a
  contiguous suffix of the sorted names; walk newest-first and stop once a filename's timestamp
  prefix is `<=` the enqueue timestamp. Bounded by the contention window, not history.

This deletes nothing, renames nothing and writes nothing, so `docs/concurrency.md` invariant I1 and cross-clone union merges are untouched.

Also pin the implicit coupling the optimisation depends on: a test asserting that the filename timestamp prefix equals the event body's `timestamp` field for an appended event. Without it a future writer that names files differently would silently mis-reduce.

Scope note: this fixes the ASYMPTOTE (the opens term), not today's constant - `listdir` dominates at current scale, so the gate will still breach 20 ms. Do not claim the budget breach is resolved; that needs a separate lever (a store-level index, or a cheaper drain gate).

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/unit/test_ticket_digest_store.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q` (the two-clone union-merge regression from be8a0c0595 must stay green)
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `reduce_ticket` opens at most one file per event type per ticket in the no-corruption case, proven by a test that counts `open` calls against a ticket dir seeded with many ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE events.
- [x] `claim()` arbitration reads only CLAIM events newer than the latest ENQUEUE, proven by a test that seeds pre-enqueue CLAIM events and asserts they are not opened.
- [x] A corrupt newest event file falls back to the next-older one, proven by a test that writes invalid JSON as the newest file and asserts the reduce still resolves.
- [x] A test asserts the appended event's filename timestamp prefix equals its body `timestamp` field, pinning the ordering assumption the suffix read depends on.
- [x] Existing claim/drain semantics are unchanged: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q` passes.
- [x] No event file is deleted or renamed by this change, verified by the diff touching no `os.unlink`/`os.remove`/`os.rename` call.
baseline.summary: Bound the enrichment queue reduce read: newest-first suffix scan in overlap/queue.py

baseline.description:
Operator ruling (2026-08-22): the rebar-gerrit-voter-errors alarm fired 5 times in 2 days; investigation proved every incident was a transient, self-healing event handled by designed recovery paths (review timeout -> backfill retry; curl-28 clone stalls under merge-burst load; retryable-gap budgets escalating to the designed fail-closed -1). All affected changes merged with LLM-Review +1; none required operator attention. Ruling: recalibrate the alarm to reduce noise — transient self-healing errors should not page; a SUSTAINED voter failure (the fail-closed gate actually stuck, e.g. expired token, LLM outage, Gerrit down) must still alarm loudly.

Current shape (aws describe-alarms, 2026-08-22): metric rebar/host:voter_errors, Sum over period 300s, threshold 0, GreaterThanThreshold, 1 evaluation period, TreatMissingData=notBreaching. I.e. a single marker in any 5-minute window alarms. Terraform source: infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf.

Evidence base (2-day sample, journald + CloudWatch):
- Transient incidents: 1 isolated marker (double-counted to 2 pre-dedup-fix; companion bug fixes that), clearing within one interval. 5 such incidents in 48h under 4-session heavy load.
- A sustained failure mode emits markers on EVERY review attempt: the webhook queue + backfill reconciler retry continuously, so an expired token / LLM outage produces a continuous marker stream across consecutive intervals, not an isolated spike.
- Precedents: mirror-guard 969acad79b4b (sustained-divergence window); 3ff9 ruling (suppress expected-contention noise); monitoring_ws7.tf 2x5-min sustained.

Design constraints:
- The discriminator is PERSISTENCE, not magnitude: alarm on markers present across consecutive evaluation periods (e.g. N-of-M datapoints > 0, sized so an isolated self-healing error never fires but a stuck gate fires within ~15 minutes), rather than raising the count threshold (a burst of distinct transient errors is still transient; one error repeating forever is the outage).
- Keep OK/ALARM actions and the fail-closed rationale in the alarm description; update the description to name the calibration rationale and this ticket.
- Coordinate with the double-count bug fix (companion ticket, blocks this one): calibrate against deduplicated counts.
- Terraform-only change (monitoring_s4b.tf + any doc). Landing the .tf through Gerrit does NOT apply it: flag in the close comment whether apply happens via the existing drift/apply workflow or needs the operator; do not run terraform apply against AWS yourself without checking how this repo's terraform changes are applied (read infra/ runbooks + terraform-drift.yml first). If apply requires a human, land the change, comment what remains, and close only if the ticket ACs are met by the landed change per repo convention for infra changes (check how prior monitoring_*.tf changes were handled — e.g. the adb6/58a3/mirror-guard lanes).

## Approach

Recalibrate `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.voter_errors` in `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` from single-period (1x300s, Sum>0) to a sustained N-of-M shape — 3-of-5:

- `period = 300`, `evaluation_periods = 5`, `datapoints_to_alarm = 3`,
  `threshold = 0`, `comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"`, `statistic = "Sum"`,
  `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"` (all other attributes — namespace/metric,
  alarm_actions/ok_actions to the shared SNS topic per ticket 9baf, tags — unchanged).

Why 3-of-5 (grounded in the ruling's "N-of-M datapoints Sum>0, sized so an isolated self-healing error never fires but a stuck gate fires within ~15 minutes"):
- Isolated-transient immunity: the evidence base shows transients clear within one
  interval — 1 breaching period, or 2 when the event straddles a period boundary.
  datapoints_to_alarm=3 means even a boundary-straddling transient (2 breaching
  periods) never pages. The house 2-of-2 shape (monitoring_ws7.tf / mirror-guard
  969acad79b4b) WOULD page on that straddle, so this alarm needs the wider shape.
- ~15-min sustained detection: a stuck gate (expired token / LLM outage) produces
  markers on every review attempt — the webhook queue and the backfill reconciler
  (RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300, src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:279) retry
  continuously — so under a continuous stream the 3rd breaching period completes at
  ~15 min and the alarm fires.
- Why M=5 not N-of-N consecutive: the marker stream (~5-min reconciler cadence, plus
  the probe's own 5-min offset-delta sampling, OnUnitActiveSec=5min) is NOT
  phase-aligned with CloudWatch period boundaries, so a genuine sustained outage can
  yield an occasional zero-marker period (two markers landing in one period, none in
  the next). N-of-N consecutive would reset its streak on such a gap and could fire
  late or never; 3-of-5 tolerates up to 2 gap periods (worst-case fire at 25 min,
  nominal 15) while keeping the isolated-transient immunity above.
- The probe publishes a datapoint every 5 min including zeros (observability.sh §4),
  so all M periods have data; notBreaching keeps a probe outage non-paging (fails
  safe, matching S5).
- Known inherent limitation (unchanged here): the metric is error-driven — a stuck
  gate with zero review traffic emits no markers and cannot alarm under any shape;
  that would need a synthetic health probe (different metric, out of scope).
- Calibration assumes deduplicated counts: companion bug f829-152a-b415-44a4 (merged,
  change 2117 / 9b060923451) removed the logger-copy double emission, so Sum now counts
  real errors 1:1.

Also rewrite the alarm_description heredoc: keep the fail-closed rationale (ADR-0013), add the sustained-detection calibration rationale and this ticket id ea5d-4932-8554-4544.

## Scope

- `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` — the only file changed (evaluation_periods,
  datapoints_to_alarm, comments, alarm_description). No new resources, no variables,
  no other .tf files, no probe/emitter changes.
- Out of scope: running `terraform apply` (applies are MANUAL per
  infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md §plan-before-apply); any change to the metric
  pipeline; other alarms' shapes.

## Testing

Test tier for monitoring .tf changes in this repo (per terraform-drift.yml and prior monitoring_*.tf changes, e.g. 24ec1e6d8ac): static validation — CI has no alarm-behavior simulation tier, so the two behavioral ACs are covered by the shape arithmetic above (3rd breaching period at 15 min nominal; isolated marker breaches ≤2 < datapoints_to_alarm=3) plus:
- Local: `terraform fmt -check -recursive`, `terraform init -backend=false`,
  `terraform validate` (Terraform 1.10.5, matching CI).
- CI (Verified gate): repo lint/typecheck/tests as usual; the terraform-drift workflow
  runs on GitHub PRs + daily cron, not on Gerrit verify — after merge the DAILY drift
  sweep will FAIL on the non-empty plan until an operator applies; that is the designed
  committed-but-unapplied signal (workflow header), recorded on the ticket as the
  application path.

## Application path (recorded per AC)

Landing via Gerrit does NOT apply to AWS. Applies are manual: infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md §"plan-before-apply on the shared remote backend" (`terraform plan -out plan.tfplan` → review → `terraform apply plan.tfplan`). The daily terraform-drift sweep flags the pending apply until the operator runs it. I will not run terraform apply myself.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Alarm no longer fires on an isolated self-healing marker; fires within ~15 min of a sustained marker stream (covered by the 3-of-5 shape arithmetic + static validation — see Testing).
- [x] Both behaviors covered by whatever test tier monitoring .tf changes get in this repo (terraform fmt/validate locally; drift plan in CI's daily sweep).
- [x] Description text updated with rationale + ticket reference.
- [x] Application path (auto vs operator apply) explicitly recorded on the ticket (manual operator apply per provision-restore.md; drift sweep flags until applied).
baseline.summary: Recalibrate voter-errors alarm to sustained-failure detection

baseline.description:
Delete `baseline_advanced_at` and stop rewriting an unchanged baseline. This is the single highest-value change in the epic: it cuts marginal packed cost per `bindings.json` version from **12.79 KB to 1.74 KB (7.4x)**, measured over 40 consecutive real revisions. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`binding_store.py:373-375` unconditionally rewrites `entry["baseline"]` and stamps `baseline_advanced_at = _now_iso()`. That field is written in exactly one place and **read nowhere in `src/`** (only asserted in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py:61`). Measured across consecutive committed revisions: baseline VALUES changed **0** entries while the stamp changed **1144** — a scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file, which is pathological for git delta compression.

Honest scoping: because baseline values change 0 entries/pass today, the write-when-changed guard is **byte-neutral** and the entire measured win comes from deleting the field. The guard is still worth adding — it is the correct behaviour once real Jira edits arrive, and it saves the rewrite CPU — but it must not be credited with the savings.

## Approach
In `set_baseline`: build the filtered baseline, compare to the existing one, return early if equal; never write `baseline_advanced_at`. Preserve `binding_store.py:374`'s `if k in fields` semantics (**not** `is not None`) — `outbound_field_diff.py:251` treats a MISSING key as "no ancestor -> local wins", so a key must stay present with a `None` value rather than being dropped.

Both callers must be covered: `reconcile._advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:506-523`) and the inbound-adopt path at `apply_inbound_records.py:209-212`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: **integration** against a stateful fake,
      asserting file bytes and commit count — not call counts. (`save()` uses
      `json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, so byte-identity is well-defined.)
- [ ] `grep -rn baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing; the stamp is absent from every entry
      written by `set_baseline`. Tier: **unit** + grep assertion.
- [ ] A baseline field present-but-null still round-trips as present (guards the `if k in fields`
      semantics). Tier: **unit** on `set_baseline` + `get_baseline`.
- [ ] `test_binding_baseline.py:61`'s assertion on the stamp is removed or inverted, and the suite is
      green. Verify: `make test`.
- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed version measured at **<=25% of the 12.79 KB baseline** by the
      recorded method (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo, repack
      `--window=250 --depth=50`, `(pack_N-pack_1)/(N-1)`). Tier: **repo-level measurement**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`

Scope: S-M.

baseline.description:
## Problem
Duplicate tickets are filed for work that already exists and only discovered mid-implementation. Twice in one session (2026-08-19/20) a duplicate carried the SAME TITLE as its twin and passed creation unflagged: `elfish-saltwater-pika` (ea16-dd54) and `decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` (baeb-4f4b). The /rebar-debug Phase-1 investigation (first comment) measured the store: every same-title true duplicate was created within 171 s of its twin, and "same normalized title + <5 min window" scored 100% precision (7/7) on the full 2679-ticket store. The operator ruling (2026-08-21 comment) reclassified this bug -> task: absent create-time detection is intended current behaviour (ADR 0086 placed the heavy overlap detector at review time, off the hot write path), so this is designed new capability.

## Design — create-time advisory same-title duplicate warning (bounded, O(1))
Matches mainstream OSS trackers (GitHub/GitLab surface similar issues at filing time; Kubernetes/VS Code triage bots flag likely duplicates immediately after creation): detection at CREATE, advisory-only (never blocks), reusing cheap existing signals.

**Mechanism.** A small rolling "recent creates" journal — a store-wide sidecar (`StorePaths(tracker).sidecar("recent-creates.json")`, the canonical-store keying the overlap enrich gate marker uses, bug da68-fc7c) — records `{ts_ns, id, alias, title, title_norm}` for each create, pruned to a fixed recency window (600 s, ~3.5x the largest observed true-duplicate delta of 171 s). On every create, `create_core` probes the journal for a normalized-title match (case/punctuation/whitespace folded) BEFORE appending its own entry, then rewrites the journal atomically (same-dir temp file + `os.replace`). **Concurrency: the whole read-prune-probe-append-rewrite is one critical section under a dedicated exclusive `fcntl.flock` on the sidecar `recent-creates.lock`** — the `_hlc_lock` pattern proven for the HLC sidecar RMW (`src/rebar/_store/hlc.py`): held only for the one small-file RMW, never nested with the store write lock (no ordering hazard), and dropped by the kernel if the holder dies. Two near-simultaneous creates therefore serialize: the second's probe observes the first's entry (the burst case the feature targets) and no rewrite clobbers a just-appended row. Cost is one flock + one small-file read + one write — O(window), never O(store); no title index, no store scan, honouring the moist-short-lionfish write-path budget lesson (bug 6148 class). On a match, the single candidate ticket is reduced (one-ticket `reduce_ticket`, O(1)) to report its LIVE status in the message.

**Gating.** The probe runs only when `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is true — the existing advisory duplicate-detection key (on for this project); no new config surface. Flag off = no journal, no probe, zero write-path footprint.

**Surfacing (the description_cap_warning pattern, ticket 594b).** `create_core` returns a new `duplicate_warning` key; each surface emits it on its own channel after the write commits: CLI stderr via `_warn_stderr` in BOTH CLI creates — `create_cli` (`composer.py`) and `idea_cli` (`src/rebar/_commands/idea.py`, which calls `create_core` directly) — keeping stdout pure in both output modes; library logger + `duplicate_warning` in the `return_alias=True` dict (`create_ticket` and `idea`); MCP `CreateResultOut.duplicate_warning`. The message names the candidate's id/alias, its current status, the age of its create, and states the create still succeeded (advisory, exit 0). Every probe failure (unreadable journal, config error, reduce failure) degrades to no-warning — an advisory must never fail a completed write.

**Portability.** The trigger is operation-linked and in-process (inside `create_core`, the single seam every create funnels through: CLI, library, MCP, `idea()`); no CI dependency. `fcntl` matches the existing HLC-sidecar precedent in-tree.

**Secondary AC (duplicates links for the two named tickets).** Phase-1 proved the sanctioned post-close path works end-to-end: `reopen -> link <src> <target> duplicates -> transition open closed --class duplicate` (the re-close is completion-verification-exempt via the `_administrative_disposition` short-circuit). No code change; execute that runnable path on `elfish-saltwater-pika` -> `woodblock-gnatty-xiaosaurus` (5a90-ec98) and `decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` -> `039b-d179-b669-4439` so both carry machine-readable `duplicates` links.

## File impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py` (new): journal read/prune/append + probe +
  `duplicate_create_warning`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`: call the probe in `create_core` beside
  `description_cap_warning`; CLI stderr emit in `create_cli`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/idea.py`: stderr emit of `duplicate_warning` in `idea_cli` (calls
  `create_core` directly, so it needs its own `_warn_stderr` call).
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`: log + carry `duplicate_warning` on `create_ticket`/`idea`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py`: MCP result field.
- `src/rebar/types.py`, `src/rebar/schemas/create_result.schema.json`: result shape.
- `docs/config.md`: note the create-time advisory under `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`.
- `tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py` (new).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Establish and record whether `rebar create` currently consults the overlap detector, with
      the file and line that does or does not. (Phase-1 answer: it does NOT — `create_core`,
      `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`, no `rebar.llm.overlap` import; record final line
      numbers in the close comment.)
- [x] A ticket whose title matches an existing ticket's is SURFACED at creation time — the author is
      told, with the candidate ticket's id and status. Proven by creating a same-title ticket in a
      test and asserting the signal appears. Title match is the minimum bar (normalized: case,
      punctuation, whitespace folded), bounded to the 600 s recency window per the measured design.
- [x] The signal does not block creation. Legitimate same-title tickets exist (follow-ups, retries,
      per-environment variants); the requirement is that the author is INFORMED, not prevented —
      exit code 0, ticket created, warning on stderr/logger/result-field only.
- [x] `rebar link <closed-source> <target> duplicates` is permitted, or a sanctioned alternative
      exists for recording a duplicate relation after the source is closed. Whichever is chosen,
      `elfish-saltwater-pika` and `decagonal-indisposed-tamarin` end up with machine-readable
      `duplicates` links rather than prose comments. (Sanctioned alternative proven by Phase-1:
      reopen -> link -> re-close `--class duplicate`; execute it on both tickets.)
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.

## Testing / Verification
- RED-first unit tests in `tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py` (modeled on
  `test_description_cap_warning.py`): same-title create within the window warns with the
  candidate's id and status on all surfaces (library dict, `create` and `idea` CLI stderr
  with pure stdout, MCP result field); distinct titles are silent; normalization folds
  case/punctuation/whitespace; an entry older than the window is silent; flag off = silent
  and no journal writes; a corrupt journal never fails the create; the warned create still
  succeeds (exit 0, ticket readable); two processes creating the same title concurrently
  serialize on the journal flock so at least one observes the other.
- Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py -q`,
  `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0 increased=0).
- Manual: in a scratch store with the flag on, create two same-title tickets seconds
  apart and observe the stderr advisory naming the first.

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase` (`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and `process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds, at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and `_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22` is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus `_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker: `_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [ ] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [ ] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the STATUS cluster from reducer/_processors.py into _processors_status.py

## Context / Problem
Most core ticket, store, read/write, config, import/export, maintenance, and gate commands parse argv imperatively. Adding docs-only argparse definitions would create the duplicate grammar RP-05 is meant to eliminate.

## Approach
Inventory every registered core grammar owned by `src/rebar/_commands/`, `src/rebar/_engine_support/`, and `src/rebar/_io/`, PLUS the two consumers that make a migrated grammar live: the per-`Route` `parser_factory` field in `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` (core Routes in `_reads_init_only`/`_simple_read_groups`/`_lifecycle`/`_writes_full`/`_bridge_and_arms` currently carry NO `parser_factory`; only advanced/intercept routes set it) and the runtime handler switch in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (the `_dispatch_*` family, which selects and invokes each command's handler). For each command:

1. Capture current production-path positive, negative, boundary, surplus/missing argument, option-space/equal, global-output, and `--` behavior from existing tests and focused additions.
2. Move the grammar into a side-effect-free factory in the new `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/` package using the S2a argparse contract, extracting shared argument-definition helpers where canonical and compatibility forms overlap.
3. Switch the runtime handler to parse with that same factory in the same change, wiring the `parser_factory` reference onto the command's core `Route` in `_registry.py` and routing its `_dispatch_*` handler through that factory. Keep domain execution and initialization outside the parser module.
4. Preserve command-specific diagnostic text, stdout/stderr, and exit codes through the shared parser seam; do not accept an option merely because argparse can parse it.
5. Register the parser reference and prove only the selected parser/handler is resolved during execution (assert via a real production-path invocation that no unrelated parser factory or handler is constructed).

Cover the leaf positional registry, reads/lookups/gates, create/edit/lifecycle, compaction/fsck/doctor/maintenance, config, import/export, identity-adjacent core store commands, and static reads. EXCLUDE `metrics`: its route already carries `parser_factory="rebar._cli._parsers.advanced.metrics:build"` from S2c and is out of scope here (re-migrating it is forbidden). Split files only along existing command-family call graphs and respect module-size rules.

### Router global-flag/end-of-options seam (layering)
The router-level global extraction (`--output`/`-o`, `--quiet`, `--allow-secret-pattern`, applied to the pre-`--` segment only) runs in `_cli/__init__.py` BEFORE the per-command factory sees argv, exactly as today. Per-command factories parse only the command-local tail after that extraction; this ordering is invariant and no factory re-declares a global flag.

### Unknown-token semantics (per-family, preserved)
Core families currently have OPPOSITE unknown-token behavior: some parse via `parse_known_args` (silently skipping unknown tokens) while the positional-only leaf registry REJECTS stray option tokens with exit 2. Stock argparse reproduces neither by default. Each migrated factory MUST preserve its own family's pre-migration unknown-token semantics (skip vs reject-with-exit-2), proven by a negative test per semantics class; a family's semantics is not silently normalized to argparse's default.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No help cutover occurs here. Accepted grammar and execution behavior are invariant unless this ticket records and receives approval for a specific delta. A parser family, its `Route` `parser_factory` wiring, and its handler switch are ONE revertable unit; no stored data changes.

## Testing
Use the smallest production path crossing each parser. Pure parser tables may be unit-tested, but public oracles run real CLI subprocesses or existing interface tests and assert return code, exact relevant stream, parsed effect/persisted state, and unchanged state on refusal. Include nearest controls and verify tests run under `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every registered core command runtime (its `_dispatch_*` handler) calls its S2a parser factory via a `parser_factory` reference wired onto its core `Route` in `_registry.py`; no parallel imperative grammar remains for that command. `metrics` is excluded (already migrated in S2c).
- [x] Accepted/rejected argv matrices cover missing/surplus values, space/equal options, `--`, global confirmation/output extraction, per-family unknown-token semantics (skip vs reject-exit-2), and representative malformed input.
- [x] Existing persisted effects, no-effect refusals, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes show no unapproved behavior delta, verified through real production-path (subprocess/interface) tests.
- [x] Parser construction imports no domain executor or optional dependency, and a real selected execution resolves no unrelated parser factory or handler (proven by a construction-exclusion probe plus a dispatch-isolation assertion).
- [x] All touched modules meet module-size/complexity policy, and each family is proven revertable as one unit (parser factory + `Route` wiring + handler switch) — demonstrated by confirming the family's parser module, its single `_registry.py` wiring line, and its `_dispatch_*` switch form one self-contained hunk with no cross-family coupling.
baseline.summary: RP-05 S2b — Migrate core command grammars to shared argparse factories

# Publish governance: GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md, CoC contact fix (CODEOWNERS explicitly skipped)

## Why

Governance is implicit today; an outsider cannot see who decides, how maintainers are added, or where a Code of Conduct report goes if it concerns the maintainer himself. Peer convergence (curl's GOVERNANCE.md https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/master/docs/GOVERNANCE.md; the CNCF small-project template https://github.com/cncf/project-template/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md; opensource.guide) gives a one-page recipe. The one thing no template covers — and the thing readers of an org-backed solo project probe — is the Nava-PBC-backed-but-individual-led ambiguity, so it gets its own section.

## What

- `GOVERNANCE.md` (~1 page) with the seven convergent sections:
  1. Overview — maintainer-led, created and stewarded at Nava PBC; names the current lead maintainer; one-line reorientation: review happens on Gerrit, GitHub is a read-only mirror.
  2. Roles — contributor / maintainer / lead maintainer, with rebar-specific powers: Gerrit submit rights (Contributors group), ticket-store write access, release authority.
  3. Decision-making — consensus among maintainers; lead maintainer has final say (curl's model in role language); routine decisions happen in Gerrit review and rebar tickets; ADRs under `docs/adr/` record architectural choices.
  4. Becoming a maintainer — sustained quality contributions through Gerrit review ("a few quality changes merged as proof" — curl's bar), invited by the lead maintainer.
  5. Stepping down / emeritus — inactivity → access removed for security reasons, non-punitive, listed as emeritus.
  6. Nava PBC's role — what the org provides (Gerrit host, maintainer employment) and does not control (contributors participate as individuals — CNCF framing). Includes the succession decision (see open decisions).
  7. Changing this document — via a Gerrit change, lead maintainer approves.
- `MAINTAINERS.md`: table (name, GitHub handle, Gerrit username, scope, affiliation), one row today; "Emeritus maintainers" placeholder section; "changes are proposed as a Gerrit change against this file — see GOVERNANCE.md". Separate file despite one row (health-file scanners look for it by name).
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`: keep the Contributor Covenant; change the enforcement contact to role-based with a Nava backstop and add: "if a report concerns the lead maintainer, contact <Nava backstop> instead." **Also update the matching contact line in `SUPPORT.md` (~line 31 hard-codes hello@navapbc.com as the CoC contact)** so the two files never disagree.
- Assess CC 2.1 → 3.0 (3.0 is the 2026 default — Django/Mastodon/Hanami adopted; https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/3/0/code_of_conduct/); record the upgrade decision.
- Decision persistence (in-repo, not ticket-only): record the three design decisions — lead-maintainer-vs-BDFL language; CC version; CODEOWNERS non-goal — in ADR `docs/adr/0038-governance-artifacts.md` (one ADR, three short sections), with a ticket comment pointing at it.
- CODEOWNERS non-goal rationale (tense-correct: the ruleset exists today; the bot is sibling-story work, not yet live): GitHub PRs cannot merge here (a repository ruleset rejects PR merges today; story nonsecular-arthritic-sidewinder additionally adds an auto-answer bot) — CODEOWNERS only auto-requests reviewers and gates merges on PRs, so it would be dead config falsely implying PR review. Gerrit's code-owners plugin likewise skipped (one human owns everything).
- Open org decisions to resolve with Nava before close (record answers in GOVERNANCE.md §6 + the ADR): (a) succession — whether project authority (PyPI name `nava-rebar`, the Gerrit host, the GitHub org repo) rests with the person or with Nava PBC; (b) the named Nava CoC backstop contact.

## Scope

IN: GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md contact + version assessment, SUPPORT.md contact-line sync, ADR 0038. OUT: CODEOWNERS (either flavor); formal voting machinery; a foundation-style CoC committee; the rest of SUPPORT.md (owned by the intake story).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GOVERNANCE.md present with all seven sections — prove: grep for section headings incl. "Nava" and "emeritus"; Gerrit-mirror reorientation in the first ~10 lines.
- [ ] MAINTAINERS.md present — prove: `grep -qi "emeritus" MAINTAINERS.md` and the table has ≥1 row + change-process pointer.
- [ ] CoC enforcement contact is role-based with a backstop and the maintainer-concerning-report escape — prove: `grep -q "lead maintainer" CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` and the contact address appears identically in CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and SUPPORT.md (extract and diff the two address strings). If Nava has not yet designated a named backstop at execution time, the doc ships with hello@navapbc.com as the backstop address and GOVERNANCE.md §6 notes the designation is pending — that interim wording SATISFIES this AC (the org answer upgrades it later; not a blocker).
- [ ] ADR 0038 committed with the three decisions + rationale — prove: `test -f docs/adr/0038-governance-artifacts.md`.
- [ ] GOVERNANCE.md §6 (Nava's role) is present and non-empty in all cases — prove: `grep -qi "succession" GOVERNANCE.md`. It contains either the org's answers (authority/PyPI/Gerrit-host ownership; named backstop) or an explicit "pending designation" sentence naming the interim arrangement — both forms satisfy this AC; silent omission does not.
baseline.summary: Publish governance: GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md, CoC contact fix (no CODEOWNERS)

# Model classes: trivial / standard / frontier as the universal LLM interface

## Context / Problem

rebar's gates deliberately run different model tiers per pass, but the selection is not expressible as configuration. It is INFERRED, and the inference inverts off the default provider:

- `review_kernel/verify.py:269` is `verifier_default if model == default_model else (model or
  verifier_default)`. Any model that is not the literal framework default — every Bedrock id — is
  read as an explicit operator choice, so the Pass-2/Pass-4 downgrade SILENTLY STOPS APPLYING.
- `completion.py:332` repeats the same equality test on a separate path, so the completion verifier
  loses its downgrade the same way.
- `workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` declares no `model:` on any step, so ALL FOUR of code review's
  passes take `cfg.model` and it never downgrades at all.
- `plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder` to BARE names (`claude-haiku-4-5`,
  `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`), and `config.py:333-341` maps the prefix `claude` to
  provider `anthropic`. So on a Bedrock run the Pass-1 finders still resolve to DIRECT ANTHROPIC —
  a split-brain in the pass that does most of the work (MEASURED on a real review: 41 of 42 calls).

The root cause is one knob for four passes. `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a single scalar, and a scalar cannot express a per-tier mapping. That is also why `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` was deleted [rebar:281f-3336-c668-4979] — a second scalar does not help.

## Approach

Introduce THREE capability classes — `trivial`, `standard`, `frontier` — as the universal interface every rebar LLM call site resolves against. Each class is a config SLOT the operator fills with a model/provider/endpoint (and an optional fallback chain); rebar's internals reference the class, never a model id.

**Prior art (this shape is not invented).** LiteLLM's proxy config is exactly this: a `model_list` of `{model_name: <alias>, litellm_params: {model, api_base, api_key, ...}}` plus `router_settings.fallbacks` mapping alias -> [alias]. Callers reference the alias; deployment details and failover live in config. Aider solves the same problem role-wise (`--model` / `--weak-model` / `--editor-model`, with each main model carrying a default weak model). pydantic-ai supplies the runtime half but no config schema: `FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...)` takes model instances or `provider:model` strings, so rebar constructs one per class from config.

**Rebar already thinks in these tiers**, which is why the axis is right: `DEFAULT_MODEL` is the frontier model and `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` is documented in-code as "the decisive NON-FRONTIER model". This formalizes a distinction the code already makes implicitly.

**Alternative rejected — a second scalar (`REBAR_LLM_VERIFIER_MODEL`).** It fixes only the verifier half, leaves the Pass-1 ladder routing to Anthropic, and would be a config surface we ship and then deprecate once classes land. Rejected as knowingly short-lived.

**Alternative rejected — provider-qualifying the ladder in the gate YAML.** Most explicit, but it hard-codes one provider into the gate definition, which is exactly what makes today's ladder non-portable.

**Config shape.** The three names are SLOTS the client fills, not presets rebar ships and the client selects. Nothing requires the operator to know rebar's internal vocabulary beyond the three slot names:

    [tool.rebar.llm.frontier]
    model = "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
    provider = "bedrock"

    [[tool.rebar.llm.trivial.fallback]]
    model = "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5"
    provider = "bedrock"

Secrets are NOT part of this structure. rebar's config layer deliberately keeps API keys env-only (`config.py:388-398` states secrets are not config-file keys); LiteLLM puts `api_key` inline in `litellm_params` and rebar must not copy that.

**Config discovery is unchanged**, with one addition: `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` names a file that LAYERS over the discovered config (pyproject `[tool.rebar.llm]` / `rebar.toml` / XDG). It layers rather than replaces so an environment overriding one key does not have to restate the whole config — duplication is the likelier source of drift than precedence subtlety. No new discovery path is invented; the pointer IS the escape hatch.

**The merge is DEEP over tables and REPLACING over arrays.** This is the decision, not a preference:

- **Tables merge recursively, leaf key wins.** Setting only `frontier.model` in the pointed-to file
  keeps the discovered `frontier.provider`, `frontier.endpoint` and `frontier.fallback`. Anything
  shallower defeats the stated purpose — a table-level replace would force CI to restate an entire
  class slot to change one field, which IS the duplication this pointer exists to avoid.
- **Arrays are replaced wholesale, never appended.** A `fallback` chain in the pointed-to file
  REPLACES the discovered chain; `fallback = []` explicitly disables fallbacks. Appending is
  rejected because a chain that can only grow can never be shortened, reordered, or cleared by an
  environment — CI could not pin "no fallback, fail loudly" over a project default.
- **Precedence, unchanged in shape:** CLI `-c` > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered config
  file > built-in default. The pointer slots directly above the discovered file. Secrets stay
  env-only at every layer.

**This does NOT change `read_reserved_section`.** That helper's `merged.update(sub)` (`config.py:588-600`) is a SHALLOW merge shared by every reserved section, and deepening it would silently alter layering for unrelated consumers. The deep merge is implemented in the llm config resolver over the section dict it receives, leaving the shared helper's contract untouched. Any child that finds itself editing `read_reserved_section` has mis-scoped the change.

**`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is DEPRECATED with a migration window** rather than kept as a permanent alias. There are few clients today and a single-scalar knob alongside a class model is precisely the ambiguity this work removes.

## Scope

This parent's contract, delivered by its children:

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the three class slots, their parsing from the existing layered config,
  and the class resolver.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` / `_config_sources.py` — the `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointer and its
  per-key layering.
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`,
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the three verifier paths resolve `standard`
  instead of inferring from an equality test.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` and the batch runners — the Pass-1 ladder is
  expressed in classes, not bare model names.
- `src/rebar/llm/` — per-class fallback chains constructed as pydantic-ai `FallbackModel`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `docs/` — the `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` deprecation, an ADR, and example configs
  per provider.

## Testing

Unit tier for resolution and layering (pure config, no model calls); contract tier for the gate paths (the observable is which model id each pass resolves to); and one live [operator-attested] run for the end-to-end claim. Per-child tiers are stated on each child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every child ticket is closed
- [ ] a test asserts the pointed-to file DEEP-merges tables: a file setting only `frontier.model`
      over a discovered config carrying `frontier.provider` + a `frontier.fallback` chain yields the
      overridden model AND the discovered provider and fallback chain (the shallow-merge failure
      mode drops them, so this test fails against `dict.update` semantics)
- [ ] a test asserts arrays REPLACE rather than append: a `fallback` chain in the pointed-to file
      yields exactly that chain, and `fallback = []` yields no fallbacks
- [ ] a test asserts `read_reserved_section`'s own shallow-merge behaviour is UNCHANGED for a
      non-llm reserved section, so the deep merge did not leak into shared config machinery
- [ ] a test asserts each of the three verifier paths (plan-review Pass-2/Pass-4, completion) resolves
      the `standard` class rather than inferring from an equality against the framework default
- [ ] a test asserts no bare `claude-*` id resolves to provider `anthropic` during a run whose classes
      are configured for another provider
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real gate run with classes configured across two providers records the
      per-pass model ids actually used, cited from the run's usage log in a comment
baseline.summary: Model classes: trivial/standard/frontier as the universal LLM interface

baseline.description:
## Context

Implement the accepted scope from architecture recommendations 2, 4, and 6, following the evidence on `expecting-renowned-buzzard`.

Current `origin/main` still has three related sources of protocol complexity:

- Reconciler `Mutation` has typed direction/action but a generic `Mapping[str, Any]` payload. Outbound typed mutations are converted through `_mutation_to_batch_dict()` into the legacy batch shape; two CREATE shapes and a polymorphic `applier.apply()` remain.
- `PydanticAIRunner.run()` has regrown after ADR 0056. Existing ownership seams already include `ProviderSession`, `model_classes`, `structured_run`, `agent_call`, `runner_support`, capability modules, and ordered success/failure telemetry. The next change must improve those boundaries, not duplicate them.
- ADR 0098's `OperationSnapshot` is authoritative for reconciler runtime bindings, but CLI/shared command paths still call `emit_shadow_snapshot()`, and many LLM operations independently resolve `LLMConfig.from_env()`.

This epic completes these migrations. It extends ADR 0103 rather than reopening its retry/coordinator decision, works within ADRs 0056 and 0058 unless the runner research child proves an amendment is needed, and completes ADR 0098's expand/contract migration.

## Outcomes

### A. One typed reconciler representation and one production route

Define payload types as a discriminated union by `(direction, action)`, carry them through planner/coordinator/adapter boundaries, prove behavior against a broad corpus in side-effect-free shadow mode, then cut production over and delete dictionary translation and legacy dispatch in this epic. Deletion is part of the cutover, not a follow-up.

### A1. Reconciler runway and producer inputs

Restore <=700-line headroom in the uncovered spine modules, then eliminate the loose 24-value producer seam using Brant/RP-03 types and owners—never a second generic context.

### B. Runner lifecycle ownership grounded in current architecture

First produce a current effect/resource timeline and fault matrix. Then reshape only call-graph seams that the evidence supports, preserving `ProviderSession` as provider-resource owner, fallback `ExitStack` ordering, failure accounting, pre-finalization success logging, final spend/result-shape updates, provider provenance, and existing injection contracts.

No new function-NLOC ratchet or per-file headroom gate is in scope. ADR 0058's single 800-LOC ceiling remains the hard gate and debt signal. The reconciler's one-time prerequisite extractions restore room under that existing gate; they do not create another enforcement mechanism. Any future function-size metric requires separate evidence and approval.

### C. Authoritative operation configuration

Make the existing `OperationSnapshot` and focused runtime bindings behavior-bearing at the CLI, MCP, Python, shared command/store, and LLM operation boundaries. An operation composes once; downstream code consumes projections/context and cannot reread environment, files, or CWD. Remove diagnostic shadow composition and migrated ambient-resolution paths after parity.

## Verification strategy (executed; see AC evidence below for outcomes)

Portable/default-CI shadow replay; ephemeral Jira DC exact-patchset differential/convergence; runner fault-injection across lifecycle boundaries; consumer-level metamorphic config tests. The Jira DC lane is additive evidence, not the only gate.

## Constraints

- No production dual-write/double-send comparison.
- Reuse the existing ephemeral Jira DC harness and isolation assertions; do not build a second DC test environment.
- Preserve Jira Cloud behavior with verified fakes/transport contracts even though large-scale live mutation testing uses disposable DC.
- Reuse `OperationSnapshot`, central schema/provenance, `LLMRuntime`, `ProviderSession`, and current runner leaf modules; no second config schema, generic hook bus, plugin framework, or decorative frozen lifecycle carriers.
- Reuse reconciler `Observation`, `TicketPlan`, and current pass/runtime owners; no generic option-bag replacement.
- String imports, monkeypatch targets, and compatibility re-exports require a census before movement/deletion.
- New structural decisions complete the ADR lifecycle before dependent implementation; accepted ADRs are constraints, not prose to reimplement.
- Keep every intermediate Gerrit change independently testable and green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every supported reconciler `(direction, action)` has one typed payload contract; planners/coordinator/adapters/tests consume it without generic dicts. Evidence: f448 (spec) -> e9d5 (typed payloads+corpus) -> 6452 (converged inputs) -> 3f27 (cutover). `outbound_pass.py` builds every Mutation with a typed `Outbound{Create,Update,Delete}Payload`.
- [x] Portable shadow corpus covers create/update/delete/probe/conflict, inbound-only, links/comments/labels/status/parent/binding, retries, malformed input, suppression, multi-project routing; traces match. Evidence: `test_payload_shadow_corpus.py`+`test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py` (36 tests, green post-cutover).
- [x] Exact-patchset ephemeral Jira DC CI run proves isolated differential parity and typed-only post-deletion convergence, no live-remote route. Evidence: `jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` (3f27), live-run 33455991406: 74 passed, 1 skipped (LLM-gated), 1 xfailed (pre-existing, 2b16), 0 failed. Verified SHA matched pushed revision.

## Context / Problem

Every operator-seeded SSM `SecureString` secret in `infra/terraform` persists its CLEARTEXT value in the remote terraform state (S3 `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`, key `rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate`, SSE-S3 not a CMK). The `value = "CHANGEME"` + `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` pattern stops terraform WRITING the secret from git, but terraform still READS the live value into `attributes.value` on every refresh/import, so the plaintext lands in state — `terraform state pull` renders 23 secrets in cleartext to any state-bucket reader, collapsing the secret tier to the bucket ACL. Root cause is proven (see evidence comments).

## Decision (operator-approved — Option 1)

Migrate every operator-seeded `SecureString` SECRET from `value = "CHANGEME"` + `ignore_changes = [value]` to terraform WRITE-ONLY arguments `value_wo` + `value_wo_version`, which the AWS provider NEVER stores to state ("write-only values are never stored to state"). Non-secret `String` params (`jira-url`, `jira-user`, `jira-project`) and the terraform-GENERATED `SecureString` `opcert_origin_guard` (value = `random_password.opcert_guard.result`, already in state via the random resource + API-Gateway header, so `value_wo` gives no net benefit) stay as-is.

## Approach

Three resources carry the antipattern and move to `value_wo` + `value_wo_version = 1` (dropping `value` and the `ignore_changes` lifecycle block):
- `aws_ssm_parameter.rebar_secrets` (for_each, 18 params) — `infra/terraform/ssm.tf:90`
- `aws_ssm_parameter.opcert_ed25519_key` — `infra/terraform/opcert.tf:52`
- `aws_ssm_parameter.cookie_signing_secret` — `infra/terraform/auth_sso.tf:39`

`value_wo` needs AWS provider ≥ 5.79 and write-only args need terraform ≥ 1.11 (host: terraform 1.15.8, provider/lock 5.100.0). `versions.tf` floors sit below both today, so raise them: `required_version >= 1.10` → `>= 1.11`; AWS `~> 5.0` → `~> 5.79`. Rationale: write-only args are the provider-native mechanism purpose-built for keeping a secret out of state — no new dependency, secrets-manager, or KMS CMK; minimal blast radius.

**Steady-state vs. cutover (G6, addressed):** in steady state the write-only value is re-sent only when `value_wo_version` changes, so an out-of-band-seeded value is never reverted and `user_data.sh`'s `CHANGEME` fail-fast still fires on an unseeded slot. The ONE migration apply is different: because `value_wo_version` goes ABSENT→1, the provider re-sends `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` once and RESETS each already-seeded live value to the placeholder. That is intended and safe here because the exposure mandates ROTATING these secrets anyway — the deferred operator ticket does the apply + re-seed/rotate in one window; the code change runs no apply. Detail in the round-1 comment + the new runbook.

**Unenumerated consumers (G1G2, addressed):** `infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh` (f) and `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` assert the opcert key's `ignore_changes = [value]`; both move to the `value_wo` invariant in lockstep. Directly-related docs `infra/runbooks/sso-auth-host.md` and `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` are refreshed off the stale `ignore_changes` wording.

## Scope (files)

- `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`, `opcert.tf`, `auth_sso.tf` — migrate the three secret resources.
- `infra/terraform/versions.tf` — raise terraform + AWS-provider floors.
- `infra/terraform/opcert-plan-assertions.sh` — assertion (f) → `value_wo` invariant.
- `scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py` (NEW) — hermetic structural guard (no live AWS) over
  `infra/terraform/*.tf`: every `SecureString` `aws_ssm_parameter` is flagged for a quoted
  string-literal `value` and/or `ignore_changes = [value]`, must pair `value_wo` with
  `value_wo_version`, and the generated-value case (unquoted-expression `value`, no `ignore_changes`)
  is allowed. Modeled on `scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py`.
- `Makefile` — wire the guard into `make lint` (next to `check_templatefile_escapes.py`, line 302).
- `tests/unit/test_check_ssm_secret_state.py` (NEW) — RED→GREEN + mutation teeth + committed-tree
  clean + make-lint wiring, mirroring `tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py`.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` — the two consumers → `value_wo` invariant.
- `docs/adr/0105-ssm-secrets-never-in-terraform-state.md` + `docs/adr/.numbers/0105` + regenerated
  `docs/adr/README.md` — record the decision, extending ADR 0008, relating to ADR 0046.
- `infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` (NEW) — declare/seed/rotate + remediation cutover.
- `infra/runbooks/sso-auth-host.md`, `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` — refresh stale wording.

## Testing

- RED first: guard/test fail on the CURRENT tree for the right reason (three secrets persist a
  `value` literal + `ignore_changes`), proven before the fix.
- GREEN after: guard + test pass once the three resources use `value_wo`/`value_wo_version`.
- Mutation teeth: reverting any one param to `value = "…" + ignore_changes = [value]` returns the
  guard to RED (asserted by the new test).
- `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` passes (static; no plan/apply against the real backend).
- Updated `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` passes; `make lint` passes.
- No secret VALUE is printed, logged, or committed — the guard inspects HCL structure only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The three seeded-secret resources use `value_wo` + `value_wo_version` and carry no
      `value`/`ignore_changes = [value]`; verified by `scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py` exit 0 + diff.
- [x] The guard is RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix, and RED again on a one-param revert; verified by
      `tests/unit/test_check_ssm_secret_state.py`.
- [x] The guard is wired into `make lint`; verified by a wiring test and `make lint` exit 0.
- [x] `versions.tf` floors are terraform `>= 1.11` and AWS `~> 5.79`; verified by reading the file.
- [x] `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` exits 0.
- [x] `opcert-plan-assertions.sh` (f) + `tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py` assert the `value_wo`
      invariant and pass; verified by running the opcert test file.
- [x] ADR 0105 + marker `docs/adr/.numbers/0105` exist, the index is regenerated, and
      `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` + `python scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` pass.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` covers declare/seed/rotate + the remediation cutover
      and cross-links ADR 0105; verified by reading it.
- [x] A deferred OPERATOR `task` ticket (apply → re-seed/rotate in one window → verify no SecureString
      value in `terraform state pull` → rotate crown-jewels) exists, linked `discovered_from` this
      ticket; verified by `show_ticket`. [non-codebase] evidence: the new ticket id in a comment.
- [x] No credential value is printed, logged, or committed by the fix or its verification.
