# S8 — Cut the production review bot over to Bedrock Claude (dogfood, no cross-provider fallback)

## Context / Problem

The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main`, and today it runs against the direct Anthropic API. The epic's premise is that our clients will predominantly reach Claude through Bedrock, so the path rebar develops against is not the path rebar's users run; dogfooding closes that gap. State the premise honestly: it is an asserted product judgement, not a measured one — no survey or citation backs it anywhere in the epic. What IS measurable is the consequence: if Bedrock throttles, mis-caches, or returns differently shaped structured output, we find out on our own repo before a client does.

This ticket was written early in epic 061c and its original Scope and Approach have been overtaken by the epic's own deliverables. The rewrite below replaces them. What changed:

* the per-pass model split it worried about **now exists in code**, so the cutover is a configuration
  act rather than a design problem;
* the single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` knob it named is **deprecated** [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00] and cannot
  express a per-class mapping, so it is no longer the instrument;
* the `observability.sh` alarm it listed as a deliverable **already shipped** under S4b;
* the Anthropic-key retirement it promised is **not expressible** against the current `.env` layout
  and would break the kill switch it also promises.

## What is already established — do NOT re-measure or re-build

* **The per-pass class split has LANDED.** `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` now
  declares `base: model: frontier` (:74), `round_a`/`round_b`: `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:92, :130),
  `verify: model: standard` (:174) and `coach: model: standard` (:209); `plan-review.yaml` Pass-1 is
  `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:70-71) and the verifier paths resolve `standard`
  [rebar:172e-b207-4c18-4243, rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74, rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0,
  rebar:3768-789c-11ed-48be, rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468]. The gate no longer reads a single
  `cfg.model` for all four passes. **The obsolete-plan hazard is therefore inverted from what this
  ticket used to say: the risk is no longer "one knob for four passes", it is choosing an instrument
  that COLLAPSES the split that now exists.**
* **No bare `claude-*` id survives on either gate's executed path.** The only remaining bare ids under
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/` are `examples/review_skeleton.yaml:44` (an example, never executed by the
  bot) and JSX placeholders in `editor_assets/`. The split-brain this ticket previously warned about
  is closed.
* **Escalation no longer crosses providers.** `plan_review/sizing.py:400` `models_at_or_above` maps
  every at-or-above rung through its model class via `_rung_target`, which drops a rung it cannot name
  in the run's provider [rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0]. A Bedrock-configured run escalates to Bedrock.
* **`pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError` is now caught** (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:250,271`), so a
  Bedrock client-construction failure reaches rebar's typed failure path instead of escaping every
  `except LLMError` handler [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9].
* **Both region variables are ALREADY SET in the review-bot service.**
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:151` `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION: "us-east-1"` and `:157`
  `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: "us-east-1"`. They are NOT interchangeable and both are required: rebar's own
  knob threads into `BedrockProvider` while botocore reads only `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
  (`AWS_REGION` alone does not work on boto3/botocore 1.43.58), and IMDS supplies credentials but never
  a region [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9]. Verify, do not re-derive.
* **IAM is granted and exercised.** `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` grants `bedrock:InvokeModel` +
  `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on `*.anthropic.claude-*` inference profiles, scoped to the instance
  role, verified by a real call rather than the policy simulator
  [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67].
* **The VOTER_ERROR alarm chain already exists and is live.** `review_bot/voter.py` `_voter_error()`
  writes a greppable line to journald; `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 (:113, :135) publishes
  `rebar/host:voter_errors`; `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` declares
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.voter_errors` = `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` (`period = 300`,
  `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0`, :48-54); `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:110` documents
  reading it. `describe-alarms` returns `StateValue: OK` with a fresh datapoint. **Nothing in
  `observability.sh` is a deliverable of this story** — an implementer who takes the old Scope at face
  value will rebuild it and may double-publish the metric.
* **Only INFERENCE PROFILES are invokable**, and caching works on them. Plain on-demand
  `anthropic.claude-*` ids return `ValidationException: … on-demand throughput isn't supported`;
  `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` measured `cache_write=4017` then read on the next attempt
  [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550]. The verified id triple is checked in at
  `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
* **All three local gates already run clean on Bedrock** — `review-plan` (27/27 Bedrock calls,
  `cache_read` 226,668), `review-code` (5/5 Bedrock, `cache_read` 18,292), `verify-completion`
  (1/1 Bedrock, `cache_read` 45,122), all with structured output validating and zero direct-Anthropic
  calls [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7]. This cutover is a confirmation, not a first contact.
* **The parity bar is cleared as the epic defines it** [rebar:0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac]: same payloads,
  same tools, provider-clean routing, both inference profiles invoke. The operator hold recorded on
  this ticket ("DO NOT claim until 0d76 records a cleared bar") is therefore RELEASED. Carry the
  nuance: the residual `gating_failures` are informational cross-model verdict comparisons, so the
  slots read `passed=False` while no acceptance criterion is unmet.

## Approach

Fill the review-bot's **model-class slots** with Bedrock inference-profile ids, in the service's own `environment:` block in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
      REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
      REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"
      REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL:  "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"
```

These are the literal names in `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:105-115`. Because the gates name classes rather than model ids, filling the slots re-points Pass-1 onto the Bedrock opus profile and Pass-2/Pass-4 onto the Bedrock sonnet profile in one act, preserving the split that [rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74] restored and the standing operator rule behind it (standard is the default for verification/judging; frontier needs justification). No `src/` change is expected. The ids are copied from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` so there is exactly one authoritative triple, and a test pins the two together so they cannot drift.

**The cutover is purely ADDITIVE and the kill switch is purely SUBTRACTIVE.** `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` appears nowhere under `infra/` today (verified: `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL infra/` returns nothing), so the bot currently runs on the built-in class defaults, which resolve to `anthropic:claude-*`. Deleting the three lines above and recreating the container therefore restores the Anthropic path with no other edit — the exact both-directions revert already proven token-free in [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] AC7.

**THE IMAGE DOES NOT INSTALL THE BEDROCK PROVIDER PACKAGE — a second, non-config deliverable.** `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:83` is `RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot`, and `bedrock` is a **distinct extra** that is not in that list (`pyproject.toml:133-135`, `bedrock = ["pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1,<2"]`). `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:60-66` imports `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock` and raises `LLMConfigError` when it is absent, so — with no cross-provider fallback, deliberately — the class-slot flip ALONE would make the first Bedrock call fail and the `LLM-Review` gate would stop voting on every landing on `main`. The fix is one flag: add `--extra bedrock` to that `uv sync`.

*The gap is PARTIALLY masked, which is what defeats the obvious probe.* `pyproject.toml:93` is `reviewbot = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]", "boto3"]`, so the container ALREADY has boto3, and both region vars and IMDS credentials are already in place. Any probe of the form "can this container reach Bedrock with boto3?" — including the boto3 region resolution that the provider builder itself pre-checks at `bedrock_model.py:76-79` — therefore SUCCEEDS on an image that still lacks the provider module. The dependency is partially satisfied, so the container reads as healthy right up to the first gate call. The pre-cutover check must probe the IMPORT, not AWS reachability.

*Why this was invisible:* [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved all three gates clean on Bedrock (33 calls, zero direct-Anthropic) — but LOCALLY, in a dev env whose `[dev]` extra resolves `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,bedrock,openai,retries]`. A local proof cannot see a container packaging gap.

*The lockfile does NOT need regenerating — checked, not assumed.* `uv.lock` already carries the bedrock extra fully resolved: the `nava-rebar` entry has `bedrock = [{ name = "pydantic-ai-slim", extra = ["bedrock"] }]`, and `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.1's own `bedrock` extra resolves to `boto3==1.43.62`, already locked. `uv lock --check` passes against the committed lock, and `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot --extra bedrock --dry-run` resolves with no drift complaint — so `--locked` is satisfied by the existing lock and no `uv lock` regeneration is part of this story. One adjacency worth knowing: `uv.lock`'s `[conflicts]` declares `bedrock` mutually exclusive with `eval` (and `dev` with `eval`); the image installs neither `eval` nor `dev`, so adding `--extra bedrock` does not trip it.

**THE ANTHROPIC CREDENTIAL IS RETAINED. This story retires the DEFAULT USE, not the credential.** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` is **out of scope and unchanged**, for two independent reasons:

1. *The kill switch needs it.* A recovery path that flips back to Anthropic without a key is a no-op,
   and it would be discovered at exactly the wrong moment. The credential must outlive the cutover.
2. *It is not per-container in the first place.* `fetch-secrets.sh:81` reads `anthropic-api-key` as a
   REQUIRED param and :116 writes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` into ONE shared `.env`, which is `env_file` for
   both `review-bot` (docker-compose.yml:113-114) and `opcert` (:196-197); opcert consumes it for its
   own gate LLM ops (:193). "Retire the key for this container" is not expressible against that layout,
   and deleting the line breaks opcert.

So the post-cutover container still carries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, deliberately, unused. The old acceptance criterion asserting the container env contains **no** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is **withdrawn**: it contradicted the kill switch, and it was the wrong oracle anyway. The property actually worth proving is positive and measurable — that no call on the Bedrock path reaches Anthropic — and `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`'s per-call tally proves it directly, as it did for all three local gates.

**No cross-provider fallback**, unchanged from the original plan and still the right call: a `FallbackModel` to direct Anthropic would mask exactly the failures this cutover exists to surface, and a persistently degraded Bedrock could run unnoticed behind it. Note the asymmetry that makes this coherent rather than dogmatic: the INTRA-provider fallback chain accepted in [rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468] (`model_classes.py:388`) stays available; it is only the cross-provider hop that is refused.

**The transient-fault posture on Bedrock, stated accurately.** The original plan claimed "the existing tenacity transport retry absorbs transient faults". That is false on this path. `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:88` is `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` and its docstring says so explicitly: "No custom client/transport is opened here (unlike the retrying Anthropic path)". There is no `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no `"adaptive"` mode and no `aws_read_timeout` anywhere in `src/rebar/llm/` — the tenacity envelope and `RetryConfig` live only in `anthropic_model.py:114-150`. So:

* Bedrock's transient-fault handling is **botocore's stock client defaults**, which do retry throttling
  and transient 5xx, but are NOT configured by rebar and are NOT driven by `llm_retry_max_attempts` or
  `timeout_s`.
* The epic's "first_class = full fidelity ⇒ equivalent retry and timeout per transport" is an **unmet
  intention, not a landed property**. This story does not claim it and does not fix it: closing it means
  changing the provider builder, which belongs in a `src/` ticket rather than inside a production
  cutover. It is filed as its own defect, linked `discovered_from` this ticket, and the posture is
  written into the runbook so an operator debugging a throttle is not looking for a retry envelope that
  does not exist.
* Related honesty correction: inference profiles are **not** a throttling mitigation, which is how the
  original Approach justified them. Zero throttle events were observed across ~1,400 parity requests,
  the 33 local gate calls, and a 19-call plan-review. The evidenced reason is simpler and stronger —
  on-demand ids are not invokable at all [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].

**Provenance oracle: `e951` is a hard prerequisite.** [rebar:343b-4fdc-6722-469b] delivered `provider_provenance` for the plan-review and completion gates only. The code-review gate — the one that produces the `LLM-Review` vote — still does not stamp it: `code_review/finalize.py:245` sets `model` and nothing sets `provenance`, while `code_review/sidecar.py:106` reads `verdict.get("provider_provenance")` and gets `None`. [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e] fixes exactly this and is already implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 1307, so depending on it is cheap. The `provider == "bedrock"` criterion below is gated on e951 landing; the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` tally is an independent second observation that does not depend on it, so the cutover is not un-evidenced if e951 slips.

**Alternatives rejected**

* **`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` re-pointed at a Bedrock id** — the original plan's instrument. Rejected on three
  independent grounds: it is deprecated with a migration window [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00,
  rebar:d23e-1012-6749-4181], its deprecation shim fans a single value out to ALL THREE classes, which
  collapses the Pass-1/Pass-2 split back into one model, and a scalar cannot express a per-class mapping
  at all. Concretely: sonnet-everywhere silently downgrades the Pass-1 finder; opus-everywhere loses the
  Pass-2 cost downgrade and renders the `temperature: 0` greedy pin at `code-review.yaml:185`
  inoperative, since Bedrock opus accepts only the default temperature. Both single-model outcomes are
  wrong, in opposite directions. A runbook naming it would also rot at v1.0.0.
* **`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointed at `/app/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`** — genuinely
  attractive: it is the instrument [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved end-to-end, it is what the CI
  provider matrix uses, and it makes the id triple single-sourced by construction. Rejected for the
  container specifically. The file is present in the image only incidentally —
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot:82` is `COPY . /app` and `.dockerignore` happens not to exclude `.github` — so a
  future context-trimming change would delete it and the pointer would fail at gate time in production,
  after the deploy that caused it. Env class slots also OUTRANK the file pointer in the precedence order
  (CLI > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered file > default), so keeping both layers live invites
  two configurations that silently disagree. The single-sourcing benefit is recovered by the drift test
  instead of by indirection.
* **Per-service Anthropic key retirement via a `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ""` override in the review-bot
  `environment:` block** — technically expressible (compose `environment:` outranks `env_file`), and it
  would satisfy the old "no Anthropic credential in this container" criterion without touching opcert.
  Rejected because it disables the kill switch for the sake of a criterion we have withdrawn, and buys
  nothing: the credential is unused either way, and "unused" is what the usage-log tally proves.

## Scope

- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — the three class-slot env vars in the `review-bot` service's
  `environment:` block, AND `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`. Region vars are already present and are not re-added.
  The usage-log var is IN SCOPE because THIS TICKET'S OWN acceptance criteria require a
  `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-call tally proving every call reached a Bedrock profile and none reached
  Anthropic — and that was unsatisfiable as written: recording is OPT-IN (`usage_log.record()` is
  a no-op with the var unset) and the var was set NOWHERE under `infra/`, so this container had
  never written a usage log. The Approach anticipates the need ("Write the usage log to a durable
  path outside the job workspace") without ever saying to enable it. So the earlier, narrower
  wording contradicted this ticket's own criteria; the scope-intent finding on change 1327 caught
  exactly that seam and this is the correction. The path sits on the bind-backed volume because
  auto-deploy recreates the container.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — add `--extra bedrock` to the `uv sync --locked` line (:83),
  so the image contains `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock`. No `uv.lock` edit accompanies it (see
  Approach: the lock already resolves that extra and `--locked` is already satisfied).
- `infra/terraform/` — a Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error alarm built on AWS/Bedrock NATIVE metrics via
  a `metric_query` metric-math expression, NOT a host-published custom metric. MEASURED in this account:
  the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace already publishes `InvocationClientErrors` and `Invocations`, dimensioned by
  `ModelId` (values include `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` from this epic's own traffic), so the rate is
  computable as `InvocationClientErrors / Invocations` with no publisher to add. THIS IS WHY
  `observability.sh` STAYS OUT OF SCOPE: the alternative — a `rebar/host` custom metric — would require a
  new publisher there and would re-open a scope claim this plan deliberately makes. It also means the
  DIMENSIONLESS-ON-BOTH-SIDES contract that `monitoring_s4b.tf` and `monitoring_s5.tf` document does not
  apply here: those are host-published custom metrics, whereas a native metric is dimensioned by AWS and
  the alarm must MATCH that dimensioning (`ModelId`) rather than avoid it. State the dimension explicitly
  in the resource so it cannot silently stop matching.
  This is the one signal the existing
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` alarm cannot give: `voter_errors` fires only when the gate fails to vote
  at all, so a partially degraded Bedrock that still produces votes is invisible to it. Thresholds per
  the epic's criterion (client-error rate > 25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive
  periods), with the alarm ARN and a forced test notification recorded on this ticket — the evidence
  gap the epic's AC has been carrying unresolved.
- `infra/runbooks/` — the kill-switch entry (class slots, not `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`), stating that the
  Anthropic credential is retained by design and why, and recording the actual Bedrock retry/timeout
  posture.
- a test pinning the compose class-slot values to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
- **NOT in scope:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (see Approach), `infra/scripts/observability.sh`
  (already shipped under S4b), and any `src/rebar/llm/` change — including the botocore retry/timeout
  parity gap, which is filed separately.

## Testing

Live end-to-end, because this is a cutover of a production gate: the oracle is a real vote on a real change, not a local invocation. The drift test is the only unit-tier item.

- **container packaging, pre-cutover:** rebuild the review-bot image from the amended
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot` and run
  `docker compose exec review-bot python -c "import pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock"`, capturing the exit
  status and output. This runs BEFORE the class slots are set, so a missing provider package surfaces as
  a build-time finding rather than as a gate outage. What is probed is the IMPORT; a boto3/AWS
  reachability probe is not a substitute (see Approach).
- **safety net, pre-cutover:** induce a real `VOTER_ERROR` on the CURRENT Anthropic path and observe
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` transition `OK → ALARM`. Access for this is confirmed (CloudWatch read
  plus SSM to the prod host). Design caveat: per [rebar:c943-1b38-d613-4013] a 409 "change is closed"
  deliberately does NOT emit `VOTER_ERROR`,  … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: S8 — cut the production review bot over to Bedrock Claude (dogfood, no fallback)

## Summary
A `rebar link` write returned **exit 0 but did not persist** when its stdout was piped to an early-closing reader (`| head -3`). Re-running the identical command WITHOUT the pipe persisted the link. In the same piped batch a `relates_to` link DID persist, which complicates a pure SIGPIPE explanation, so **root cause is UNCONFIRMED**. A write command that reports success without committing is a silent data-integrity risk for scripted/agent callers.

## Reproduction Steps (as observed; not yet cleanly isolated)
1. Create three epics E1, E2, E3 in one script.
2. Immediately run, each piped: `rebar link E1 E3 blocks 2>&1 | head -3`; `rebar link E2 E3 blocks 2>&1 | head -3`; `rebar link E2 <other> relates_to 2>&1 | head -3`.
3. `rebar deps E3` -> **blockers empty** (the two `blocks` links did not persist); the `relates_to` link DID persist.
4. Re-run `rebar link E1 E3 blocks` and `rebar link E2 E3 blocks` WITHOUT the pipe -> `deps E3` now shows both blockers.

- **Expected:** a write either persists the event or exits non-zero; robust to stdout closing early.
- **Actual:** exit 0 with no event committed (intermittent; correlated with piping to `head` and/or rapid successive writes right after create).

## Candidate root causes (to isolate)
- SIGPIPE in the write/auto-push path aborting the commit without surfacing an error.
- Race when linking a just-created ticket before its create event/commit fully settles.
- Auto-push / `.ticket-write.lock` contention across rapid successive writes (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reproduce and root-cause the non-persistence (isolate SIGPIPE vs race vs push/lock contention).
- [ ] Invariant: a write command must EITHER commit the event OR exit non-zero — never exit 0 without persisting.
- [ ] The commit path is robust to stdout being closed early (SIGPIPE ignored for the durable-write section).
- [ ] Regression test: a `link`/`create` with stdout closed immediately still persists (or fails loudly).

## Environment
- **rebar:** NOT pip-installed (`pip show nava-rebar` -> "Package(s) not found"; `import rebar` fails without `PYTHONPATH`); `rebar.__version__` = `0+unknown`. Source checkout: branch `claude/llm-code-review-commits-m0flss`, HEAD `91fe853`.
- **How rebar was called** (not on PATH): `PYTHONPATH=src python -c "from rebar.cli import main; import sys; sys.argv=['rebar', <args>]; main()"`, run from `/home/user/rebar`, with `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR="$PWD/.tickets-tracker"`.
- **Python:** 3.11.15 (`/usr/local/bin/python`).
- **OS/kernel:** Linux 6.18.5 x86_64.
- **Shell:** `/bin/bash` (GNU bash 5.2.21(1)-release).
- **Context:** non-interactive container (Claude Code on the web); fresh clone; `origin/tickets` present but no local `.tickets-tracker` initially (created manually via `git worktree add .tickets-tracker -B tickets origin/tickets`).
baseline.summary: rebar write ('link') exits 0 but does not persist when stdout is piped to an early-closing reader (root cause unconfirmed)

## Why
`test_leaves_registry_coverage.py::test_every_leaf_has_real_body` (`:83-100`) defines "real body" as ≥3 AST statements OR a regex match for effect-shaped tokens (`client.`, `.append`, `subprocess.run`, …) over `inspect.getsource`. It passes while a leaf sends the WRONG target, DROPS a field, returns the WRONG follow-on, or SWALLOWS a required error — a structural proxy, not behavior. VALIDATED.

## What
Add a per-leaf behavioral effect matrix that drives each leaf in the `_LEAVES` registry with a mock Jira client and asserts its OBSERVABLE effect: the exact client/store call made (method + key arguments), the returned `ApplyResult`, any follow-on effects, and its failure behavior.

Completeness (so coverage cannot silently lag the registry): the matrix is enumerated FROM `_LEAVES` itself (parametrize over `_LEAVES`), and a test asserts EVERY id in `_LEAVES` has a matrix entry — a newly-added leaf with no behavioral entry fails that test.

Do not blindly duplicate existing coverage: several leaves already have behavioral tests elsewhere (e.g. `test_apply_outbound_*`). Where a leaf is already behaviorally covered, the matrix entry may be a thin assertion that references the same observable effect (or the existing test is folded into the matrix) — the goal is one complete, enumerated behavioral matrix over `_LEAVES`, not redundant tests. The AST heuristic, if kept, is RELABELED as an explicitly-supplemental structural guard (not counted as behavioral coverage).

## Scope
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_leaves_registry_coverage.py` (and/or a new
  per-leaf matrix module) — the behavioral matrix + the `_LEAVES`-completeness test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The behavioral matrix is enumerated from `_LEAVES`; a test asserts every `_LEAVES` id has
      a matrix entry (a new uncovered leaf fails it).
- [ ] Each leaf's entry asserts its observable effect via a mock Jira client with SPECIFIC
      assertions that structurally catch the named failure modes: (a) the EXACT client/store
      method invoked AND the EXACT target entity id/key it was called with (so a wrong-target
      defect necessarily fails); (b) the EXACT payload field set sent (assert the full dict or
      the specific fields, so a dropped/renamed field necessarily fails); (c) the returned
      `ApplyResult` value and any follow-on call (so a wrong follow-on necessarily fails). The
      catch-the-defect property is a consequence of this assertion specificity, not a separate
      manual step.
- [ ] Failure-behavior coverage is quantified: EVERY leaf that has an error/exception path
      (raises, or returns a failure/error-shaped `ApplyResult`) asserts that path's observable
      behavior (the exception type or the error `ApplyResult`); a leaf with no error path
      asserts its success `ApplyResult`.
- [ ] If the AST heuristic is retained, it is relabeled as a supplemental structural guard, not
      behavioral coverage.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` green.
baseline.summary: Replace leaf-registry 'real body' heuristic with a per-leaf effect matrix

# Reduce the import-cycle SCC (facade-read reroute — parts 1 & 2 landed; this ticket now = part 3 / item 9.3)

## Context
A verified AST+Tarjan analysis found a large strongly-connected import component spanning the
facade, `_commands`, `signing`, and most of `llm`, held together by function-local lazy imports.
Layering was enforced only by docstrings. Three remediations were approved. **Two have already
shipped to `main`; this ticket now tracks ONLY the remaining part 3 (item 9.3).** The live baseline
(`.import-cycle-baseline.json`) records the current surface: `largest_scc_size = 36`,
11 cross-package cycle pairs, 49 modules-in-cycles. (The original "~69-module" figure predated the
part-1/part-2 landings; 36 is the current truth.)

## What
1. **[DONE — change 208]** Import-cycle CI strangler contract: `scripts/check_import_cycles.py` +
   `.import-cycle-baseline.json` + CI wiring (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) + `tests/unit/
   test_import_cycles.py`. Freezes the surface; fails only NEW cross-package cycles.
2. **[DONE — change 205]** Reducer layering-inversion fix: the shared id/alias primitive lives in
   the leaf `src/rebar/_ids.py`; `_engine_support/resolver.py` re-exports it; `reducer/_processors.py`
   imports from `rebar._ids` (no longer UP into `_engine_support`). Guarded by
   `tests/unit/test_no_reducer_engine_support_cycle.py`.
3. **[THIS TICKET — item 9.3]** Route leaf **read** callers off the `rebar` facade onto `rebar._reads`,
   and make `rebar._reads` itself a leaf so the reroute measurably shrinks the SCC.

## Item 9.3 — concrete scope (grimp-verified in worktree janitor/item-9.3-facade-reads)
- `rebar._reads` is currently IN the 36-SCC. Its ONLY `→rebar` (facade) back-edge is the lazy
  `from rebar import RebarError` (line 45); `from rebar import config` is a submodule edge
  (`→rebar.config`, a leaf) and does not bind it to the facade.
- **Make `_reads` a leaf:** move `RebarError` + `ConcurrencyError` into a new stdlib-only leaf
  `src/rebar/_errors.py`; `rebar/__init__.py` re-exports them (full back-compat); `_reads` imports
  them from the leaf. grimp simulation: largest SCC **36 → 35** (`_reads` leaves the cycle); the
  import-cycle baseline ratchets down.
- **Reroute read call-sites:** for each function-local `import rebar` whose `rebar.*` calls are ALL
  exported by `_reads` (`show_ticket`/`list_tickets`/`deps`/`ready`/`next_batch`/`search`/

  `llm/plan_review/pass1.py`, `llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `llm/plan_review/attest.py`,
  `llm/workflow/steps.py`, `llm/workflow/gate_ops.py`. `spec_scan`/`operations`/`pass1`/`orchestrator`/

  (`comment`/`tag`/`edit_ticket`) or reads not in `_reads` (`verify_signature`/`get_file_impact`).
- **Out of scope:** the larger 36→18 collapse needs routing WRITES through a leaf too — not a
  reads-only change; not attempted here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Import-cycle CI contract in place; passes current state, fails a new cross-package cycle (change 208).
- [x] `reducer` no longer imports `_engine_support`; shared resolution in the leaf `rebar._ids`; reducer/replay tests green (change 205).
- [ ] `rebar._reads` no longer imports the `rebar` facade (`RebarError` sourced from the new leaf `rebar._errors`); `rebar._reads` is OUT of the largest SCC.

# Bridge publish fails on rejected refs: a GitHub 500 is misread as a stolen lease

## Premise correction (read first)

The original report described the witness failure as "a stale `--force-with-lease` expectation". **The raw run log disproves that.** It was never a stale lease — it was a GitHub **server-side error** that rebar's CAS classifier mistook for lease movement.

## Evidence

### Fault 1 — witness publication (run 31455622724, 2026-08-11T03:30Z)

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler._ref_lock: ref-lock: push to origin refs/reconciler/last-pass
  (expected oid 22cd71bd...) classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved) —
  stderr: remote: fatal error in commit_refs
 ! [remote rejected] 1e5caeb7... -> refs/reconciler/last-pass (failure)
WARNING rebar_reconciler._ref_lock: ref-lock: git push to origin refs/reconciler/last-pass
  failed (exit 1) — fail-closed: remote: Internal Server Error
ERROR: cannot publish reconciler last-pass witness: Command '[... --force-with-lease ...]'
```

Attempt 1 was `remote: fatal error in commit_refs` + `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)`. `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` matched the broad `rejected` marker, found nothing in `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS`, and therefore reported **"classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved)"** — a false claim that another process stole the lease. Attempt 2 returned `Internal Server Error`, which *is* in the marker list, so it correctly fell through to fail-closed and killed the pass.

This is exactly the failure shape bug 4afc's subtractive classifier exists to prevent; the marker list simply does not know GitHub's `fatal error in commit_refs` or the bare `(failure)` ref-status. Misclassification is not cosmetic: a "stolen lease" verdict is a statement about **concurrency** that operators use to reason about racing passes.

### Fault 2 — tickets-branch delivery (run 31244501098, 2026-08-08T06:41Z)

```
final-push-rejected: To https://github.com/navapbc/rebar
 ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/tickets':
   is at e45f61a9... but expected 9ecaaa40...)
 (6 unpushed commits on origin/tickets..HEAD)
```

This one **is** a genuine lost CAS race, and it *was* retried — `cannot lock ref` is correctly classified retriable, so the loop spent its budget. It still lost every time, because `src/rebar/_store/push.py` has **no backoff anywhere**: the retries fire back-to-back and keep colliding with the same concurrent `tickets` writer. Under the continuous-loop cadence this contention is routine.

## Plan

1. In `_ref_lock.py`, extend `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS` with the observed server-side
   failure signatures (`fatal error in commit_refs`, and the generic `(failure)`
   ref-status) so a server fault can no longer be reported as lease movement. Keep the
   subtractive shape and the fail-closed default: `stale info` stays conclusive for a
   genuine lease move, and ambiguity still fails closed.
2. In `push.py`, spend backoff between non-fast-forward / CAS retries, reusing the
   injectable backoff seam added for `subzero-locustal-junebug` (this change stacks on
   it), so a lost `cannot lock ref` race gets a real chance to converge instead of
   re-colliding immediately.

**Constraint that shapes step 1:** `_ref_lock.py` sits at exactly the repo's 800-LOC hard cap, so the markers are appended in a single `+=` statement (with the tuple annotated `tuple[str, ...]`) rather than added inline with a comment block. The file stays at the cap. A proper split of that module along a call-graph seam is owed but is deliberately NOT bundled into this bug fix — it is a refactor with its own risk profile (the reconciler loads siblings through a custom loader, and existing tests bind to module identity and logger names).

## Deliberate non-change (and why)

The ticket also asks "whether the last-pass witness failure should be fatal at all (it is a witness, not the payload)". **This change does NOT downgrade it.** Witness fatality is the fail-loud contract described in `docs/adr/0094-reconciler-last-pass-two-witness-status.md`, and the heartbeat canary is the downstream detector that depends on it; relaxing it is a user-visible alerting change, not a reliability fix, and belongs in its own ticket with an ADR amendment. This change fixes the **mechanism** that produced the failure (a misclassified server error, and unbacked-off retries) while leaving the contract intact.

## Scope / non-goals

- No change to `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr`'s subtractive shape, to the `stale info`
  conclusive marker, or to the fail-closed default.
- No change to `finalize_process`'s return contract in `last_pass.py`.
- No change to the CAS retry COUNT anywhere (`_MAX_RETRIES = 5`; the witness's 3 attempts).
- No new secrets, credentials, permissions, or infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: A test proves the exact run-31455622724 stderr (`remote: fatal error in
  commit_refs` with `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)`) is **not** classified as a CAS
  mismatch, i.e. it is no longer reported as a stolen lease.
- [x] AC2: A test proves a genuine lease move (`stale info`) is **still** classified as a
  CAS mismatch — the bug 4afc contract is not weakened by the new markers.
- [x] AC3: A test proves the existing non-CAS markers (`hook declined`,
  `internal server error`, `rate limit`, `file exists`) still classify as non-CAS.
- [x] AC7: `_ref_lock.py` stays within the 800-LOC hard cap (the module-size gate is
  green), and the complexity ratchet reports no new debt.
- [x] AC4: A test proves a `cannot lock ref … is at X but expected Y` rejection sleeps
  between retry attempts (via the injected sleep seam) rather than retrying back-to-back,
  and that the number of push attempts is unchanged.
- [x] AC5: The existing ref-lock classification suite
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`) and the push
  contract suite pass unchanged.
- [x] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge delivery fails on rejected ref pushes (stale force-with-lease + lost tickets race)

## Problem

`make amend-msg` exists because `git commit --amend -F/-m` REPLACES the whole message and so silently drops the `Change-Id` trailer. It carries the `Change-Id` forward correctly — and then drops `Signed-off-by` by the same mechanism it was built to prevent.

`scripts/amend_commit_message.py`:

```python
def compose_message(new_message: str, change_id: str) -> str:
    return _git_stdout("interpret-trailers", "--trailer", f"Change-Id: {change_id}",
                       stdin=strip_change_id_lines(new_message))

def amend_head(message: str) -> int:
    ...
    ["git", "commit", "--amend", "--file", str(tmp)]
```

Only `Change-Id` is read off HEAD and re-attached. Everything else comes from `FILE`, and `--file` replaces the message wholesale — so a `Signed-off-by` present on HEAD but absent from the author's new message file is gone.

Observed: an agent rewriting a commit message with `make amend-msg` lost its `Signed-off-by` while the `Change-Id` survived. It noticed only because it happened to re-inspect the trailers, and restored it with `git commit --amend --no-edit -s`.

## Why this is a defect and not a usage error

The tool's own docstring anticipates the trailer block containing `Signed-off-by` — it is named as the neighbour `interpret-trailers` appends next to. So the code knows the trailer is there and preserves only its sibling.

More to the point, the wrapper's stated rationale applies verbatim to the trailer it drops. From the Makefile target:

> `git commit --amend -F/-m` REPLACES the whole message, dropping the Change-Id … No hook can
> catch it … the remedy is a wrapper that makes the failure unreachable.

Same argument, same file, same failure mode, other mandatory trailer. The wrapper makes one failure unreachable and leaves the other reachable through itself.

## The loss is silent — nothing catches it

- No CI job asserts a commit HAS a `Signed-off-by`. `scripts/check_dco_identity.py` is a
  different check: it scans **docs** for hardcoded personal sign-off identities.
- `scripts/check_commit_message_wrap.py` treats `Signed-off-by:` as a trailer for wrapping
  purposes only; it does not require one.
- The `commit-msg` hook stamps `Change-Id`, not sign-off.

So the amend succeeds, looks correct, and the missing DCO attestation surfaces later or not at all. CONTRIBUTING.md requires the sign-off; the sanctioned tool for rewriting a message removes it without saying so.

## Scope

Carry `Signed-off-by` forward from HEAD the same way `Change-Id` already is, when the new message does not supply one. Preserve existing behaviour when the author's file DOES include a sign-off — including multiple sign-offs, which are legitimate — and do not duplicate it.

Explicitly OUT of scope: adding a CI gate that requires sign-off on every commit. That is a separate, larger policy decision about enforcement; this ticket is only that the tool must not silently destroy a trailer that was already there. Also out of scope: changing which identity signs, or `check_dco_identity.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Amending with a message file that omits `Signed-off-by` preserves HEAD's existing
      sign-off — verified by a test asserting the trailer survives the amend
- [x] A message file that DOES carry a sign-off is respected and the trailer is not duplicated —
      verified by a test
- [x] Multiple distinct `Signed-off-by` trailers on HEAD all survive — verified by a test
- [x] `Change-Id` carry-forward is unchanged, including the existing refusal when HEAD has none
      — verified by the existing tests continuing to pass unmodified
baseline.summary: make amend-msg drops Signed-off-by, the same silent trailer loss it was built to prevent for Change-Id

## Summary

`doctor` now scans the OPERATOR'S HOME for MCP client configs (`~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, `~/.claude.json`). Any test that invokes `doctor_cli` therefore reads live machine state it does not control, which makes those tests non-hermetic. Three were observed failing and then passing across repeat runs on an unchanged tree.

## Almost certainly my own doing — recorded so nobody hunts a ghost

I introduced the HOME scan (change 2272, `doctor_mcp_client.py`). While another session's test tier was running, I was CONCURRENTLY REWRITING those exact files for the Layer 1 credential migration: `~/.claude.json` and `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` rewritten via `json.dumps`, `~/.codex/config.toml` edited twice, `~/.zshrc` appended.

A `json.dumps` rewrite is not atomic — there is a window where the file is truncated or partial. A concurrent `doctor` read landing in that window gets a parse error rather than the config, and takes a different code path. That fits the observed signature exactly: intermittent, unreproducible on a quiet machine, and correlated with nothing in the tree.

The other agent initially reported these as deterministic and host-coupled, then corrected itself to intermittent after three clean repeat runs, and declined to retry them away. Both calls were right.

## Why it is still a real defect, not just my interference

Even with nobody editing anything, these tests depend on whatever client configs happen to exist on the machine running them. That means:

- they pass or fail based on developer-local state that is not in the repo;
- a developer with a broken personal Codex config sees failures unrelated to their change;
- CI passes only because runners have no such configs — i.e. the coupling is invisible where it
  would be caught.

I deliberately made the client findings ADVISORY (excluded from `doctor`'s exit code) for exactly this reason, and added `--strict-mcp-clients` as the opt-in. That prevents the findings from FAILING a store-health gate, but it does not make the tests hermetic — the scan still runs, still reads HOME, and can still misbehave on malformed input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `doctor` tests are hermetic: they inject a `home` (the scanner already takes one) or set
      `HOME` to a fixture directory, so no test reads the real operator's configs.
      DONE (change 2327, merged): tier-wide autouse fixture `_isolated_mcp_client_home` in
      `tests/unit/conftest.py` redirects `doctor_mcp_client.scan_mcp_clients`'s default `home`
      (the `home=None` CLI path) to an empty per-session directory, so every `doctor_cli`-driven
      unit test — present or future — sees an unconfigured home and never touches the operator's
      real configs. `$HOME` itself is left untouched (git identity, `~/.aws` and other
      home-derived resources other unit tests rely on are unaffected), mirroring the tier's
      existing `_no_real_session_log_writes` seam neutralization.
- [x] A malformed or partially-written client config degrades to a clear finding and cannot
      change `doctor`'s exit code or raise — concurrent-write safety, not just parse safety.
      DONE (pre-existing by design, confirmed): the scanner never raises — every fault (missing,
      unreadable, truncated/partial, or unparseable config) becomes a finding — and `doctor.py`
      excludes the MCP-client findings from its exit code (advisory). Reader-side concurrent-write
      safety: a `json.dumps` writer's truncation window yields a parse error that degrades to a
      finding, not an exception. Held-out coverage:
      `tests/unit/test_doctor_mcp_client.py::test_malformed_config_degrades_to_a_finding_not_an_exception`
      (parametrized over each client relpath and several malformed/truncated bodies) and
      `::test_missing_config_degrades_to_a_finding_not_an_exception`.
- [x] The three affected tests (`test_doctor_dirty_tree` ×2, `test_doctor_mapping`) pass
      deterministically with an arbitrary HOME state.
      DONE: with the fixture in force these tests no longer read the real HOME at all, so their
      result is independent of operator HOME state. Verified GREEN locally and — decisively — on
      CI across ubuntu py3.11 / py3.12 / py3.13 (change 2327 `Verified +1`). A new held-out oracle
      `tests/unit/test_doctor_mapping.py::test_doctor_cli_mcp_client_scan_is_hermetic` locks the
      invariant: every MCP-client finding path must resolve under the injected isolation dir
      (never under `Path.home()`); it is RED against the pre-fix code and GREEN with the fixture.

## Note on the atomic-write half

If the concurrent-rewrite theory is right, the durable lesson is about the WRITER, not only the reader: rewriting a config with `json.dumps` straight over the original leaves a window where any concurrent reader sees a truncated file. Write to a temp file and `os.replace` it. That applies to any tooling this project ships that edits user config in place. This ticket fixes the READER-side hermeticity (the test-integrity defect); the WRITER-side atomic-write hardening is a separate concern for whatever rebar tooling edits user config in place, out of scope here.
baseline.summary: doctor tests are non-hermetic: they read the operator's real HOME configs, so they flake when those change

# `review-plan` PASS but signing aborts with `store-read-failure` under concurrent store writes

## Symptom (observed this session)

Remediating the plan-review gate on a **reopened** epic (`3d7a-7795-efde-4df7`, `ravenous-dirt-widgeon`) while **several other sessions wrote the shared store concurrently**: `rebar review-plan` repeatedly computed a **PASS** (`signable: True`) but **failed to persist a signature**, exit **11**, with `{"signed": false, "error": "store-read-failure", "event": "plan_review_sign_aborted", "retryable": false}`. So `--status` stays `stale-reopened` and the only close path left is `--force` â exactly what we must avoid.

## Proven root cause (rebar-debug Phase 1 â see RCA comment for full evidence)

`sign_manifest`'s generation loop (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:289-291`) treats a transient `store-read-failure` from its **pre-lock** reads (`tracker_head_sha`/`collect`) as **terminal** â it immediately `raise PlanReviewGenerationError(exc.reason)`. The sibling transient just below (moving committed HEAD, `before != after`) is instead **retried** (`continue`, then `PlanReviewGenerationRetryable` on exhaustion). Same class of concurrency artifact, handled asymmetrically.

Why it fires: rebar's ticket-event write path stages tracked entries with `git add` then `git commit` on the ONE shared `.git/index` every session symlinks. The signing preflight reads run `git status --untracked-files=no` / `git ls-files -u` **without** the store write lock, so they can observe a peer session mid `add`->`commit`: a staged tracked entry -> non-empty status -> `store-read-failure`. Rate scales with concurrency (matches the symptom). Runtime-confirmed: a staged tracked entry makes `tracker_head_sha(ignore_untracked=True)` raise `store-read-failure` even though the untracked half was already tolerated (d7cb-22ae).

Origin: commit `94e605a29d2` (ticket `5967-4476-7f9f-442d`, "Add phased plan-review attestations") introduced the asymmetric handler; d7cb-22ae is a partial fix that closed only the untracked trigger.

## Fix

In the `except PlanRelationSnapshotError` handler, retry a `store-read-failure` within the existing `MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS` loop (`continue`, mirroring the moving-HEAD path); on exhaustion the loop's final `raise PlanReviewGenerationRetryable` surfaces it as retryable. Deterministic reasons (missing/ambiguous/malformed/reducer/id-mismatch) stay terminal â retrying cannot fix a genuinely broken reference. The authoritative under-lock re-check (`under_lock_check`, run while holding the store write lock, so no writer can be mid `add`->`commit`) remains the fence, so retrying the pre-lock reads is safe.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A transient `store-read-failure` during plan-review signing is retried within the
      generation loop and, once it clears, the PASS ends **signed** (held-out RED->GREEN test).
- [x] A persistent `store-read-failure` exhausts the retry budget and surfaces as
      `PlanReviewGenerationRetryable` (retryable), not a terminal one-shot abort.
- [x] Deterministic `PlanRelationSnapshotError` reasons remain terminal.
- [x] The held-out test has teeth (mutation check: reverting the fix returns it to RED).

## Scope / portability

Fix is a single-site change in `generation.py`, exercised by a unit test that drives the real `generation.sign_manifest`; no CI-provider-specific trigger. The `sign-review` recovery path has a parity gap in its pre-signing baseline `collect()` tracked separately as `90c1-c112-d076-4c96` (discovered_from this bug).
baseline.summary: review-plan PASS but signing aborts with store-read-failure under concurrent store writes, blocking non-force close

## Why
Init-time `_migrate_*`/`_ensure_*` steps run only at init/re-init, so config fixes never reach already-existing stores. A first-class idempotent ensure-registry generalizes them (School B desired-state) so every non-hot entry point converges an existing install.

## What
Create `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`: a registry of ensure units, each `{stable, immutable id, callable(tracker: str) -> EnsureOutcome}` where `EnsureOutcome` is a small dataclass `{id, status: Literal["ok","changed","failed"], detail: str}` and the callable is check-then-act (no-op when converged). `run_ensures(tracker)` runs ALL units unconditionally under the STORE write lock (`_store/lock.py` write_lock — init_core does NOT currently hold it; this is a new dependency), catches a raising unit (skip-and-continue → `failed`), returns the outcome list, and atomically rewrites `.ensure-applied` to contain ONLY the ids of non-failed (ok/changed) units via the existing `fsutil.atomic_write` helper (temp-in-SAME-dir + os.replace, so it is never a cross-device rename; a full rewrite, not an incremental append; absent/garbage/ non-list JSON on read → empty set). Add `.ensure-applied` to `_GITIGNORE` (init.py:38-48).

`run_ensures()` NEVER raises: besides catching per-unit exceptions, a `write_lock` acquisition failure (LockTimeout) is caught and treated like a whole-sweep no-op (logged; the caller — init or MCP boot — continues, never aborts), and a failure to write the `.ensure-applied` marker itself (OSError, e.g. disk-full/permission) is swallowed best-effort (the sweep's git-level convergence already happened; the marker is only a hint) — it never fails the sweep or the caller.

Migrate exactly the 5 re-init idempotent units (init.py:209-213): `env-id`, `gc-config`, `merge-ours driver`, `gitattributes` (COMMIT), `gitignore` (COMMIT). BOTH commit units tree-check before committing. Wire `run_ensures()` at ALL init entry points and remove the hand-listed calls: the re-init arm (209-213), the fresh-init arm (eight calls at init.py:241-248: the migrated units are gitignore(242), gitattributes(245), gc(247), merge(248); the bootstrap _ensure_branch_user_config(241)/_exclude_scratch_in_tracker(243)/_commit_precommit(244)/ _gen_local_files(246) stay — note `.env-id` is created by _gen_local_files(246) on fresh-init, so the env-id unit no-ops there and `_ensure_env_id` is NOT among these calls), placing `run_ensures()` AFTER the fresh-init bootstrap so ordering is preserved.

In `_init_via_symlink`, the two `_ensure_env_id` call sites sit in structurally distinct branches and each gets its OWN independent `run_ensures(tracker)` call (the function is NOT restructured to a single unified return): replace `_ensure_env_id(tracker)` at line 564 with `run_ensures(tracker)` immediately before that branch's `return 0` (the already-symlinked early-return guard), and replace `_ensure_env_id(tracker)` at line 582 with `run_ensures(tracker)` immediately before the final `return 0` (the fresh-symlink-creation path); control flow is otherwise unchanged. Confirm no OTHER callers of the 5 helpers remain after removal (no double-execution).

The fresh-init-only bootstrap (`_commit_precommit`, `_gen_local_files`, `_exclude_scratch_in_tracker`, `_ensure_branch_user_config`) is NOT part of the registry and stays. init_core logs any `failed` units (warning) and NEVER aborts on an ensure failure. Post-rollback: old code ignores the git-ignored `.ensure-applied` file; committed `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` content stays on the tickets branch (harmless/idempotent — old code tree-checks before committing, so it neither re-commits nor errors on the extra committed content). Update the stale docstring refs to `_migrate_gc_config` in BOTH `sync.py:17` and the init.py module docstring (line 8) to point at the ensure registry.

## Scope
In: `ensures.py`, registry + 5 check-then-act units (EnsureOutcome), `run_ensures()` under the store write lock, `.ensure-applied` format+write + `_GITIGNORE` entry, init wiring at all entry points (replace + remove old calls incl. symlink-init). Out: pending-hint + `.ensure-hinted` (WS2), fsck/server wiring (WS3), docs (WS4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ensures.py` registry: each unit has a stable/immutable id + `callable(tracker) -> EnsureOutcome`; a test asserts the registry's id set equals a frozen expected set (so a rename/typo is caught and applied units can't silently reappear as pending)
- [ ] `run_ensures()` runs all units under the store write lock and returns typed `EnsureOutcome`s; a raising unit is caught (skip-and-continue → `failed`) and excluded from `.ensure-applied`; init logs failures and never aborts
- [ ] `run_ensures()` never propagates an exception to its caller: a `write_lock` acquisition failure (LockTimeout) is caught and logged as a whole-sweep no-op, and an OSError writing `.ensure-applied` is swallowed best-effort; a test asserts init/boot continues (returns 0) when the write lock cannot be acquired
- [ ] All 5 units migrated; BOTH gitattributes and gitignore tree-check before committing; a second `run_ensures()` on a converged store makes zero changes and zero git commits (git-log assertion)
- [ ] Hand-listed calls removed from the re-init arm and the fresh-init arm; in `_init_via_symlink` each of the two `_ensure_env_id` sites (564, 582) is independently replaced by `run_ensures(tracker)` before its own `return 0` (structure otherwise unchanged); no double-execution; no other callers of the 5 helpers remain
- [ ] `.ensure-applied` written atomically via `fsutil.atomic_write` (temp-in-same-dir + os.replace, no cross-device rename) as a JSON array of ONLY non-failed unit ids; it is added to `_GITIGNORE`; absent/garbage/non-list degrades to empty set without crashing
- [ ] An end-to-end test drives `init_core` AND `_init_via_symlink` after the cutover and asserts the store converges (all 5 units applied, `.ensure-applied` written) — not just `run_ensures()` in isolation
- [ ] Stale docstring refs to `_migrate_gc_config` are updated in both `sync.py:17` and the init.py module docstring (line 8)
- [ ] Fresh-init bootstrap steps (_commit_precommit/_gen_local_files/_exclude_scratch/_ensure_branch_user_config) remain and are NOT in the registry
baseline.summary: WS1: ensure-registry (ensures.py) + migrate 5 check-then-act steps + init wiring

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Complete ADR 0098 for LLM execution after the command/store cutover. Many LLM operations currently call `LLMConfig.from_env()` independently, even though `LLMRuntime`, `ProviderSession`, gate config scoping, and snapshot composition already exist.

The goal is one behavior-bearing snapshot/context per public operation, not deletion of a legitimate top-level composition convenience. Ambient compatibility may remain only at an explicitly approved boundary and must delegate to the central composer.

`emit_shadow_snapshot`/`_shadow` (the RP-04 S1 diagnostic shadow ticket 3a08 retained) has SIXTEEN production call sites, not five: five in `_mcp_llm.py` (LLM), ten in `_lib_ops.py` (three LLM workflow ops — `run_workflow`/`get_workflow_status`/`get_workflow_result` — plus seven NON-LLM bridge/reconciler-mapping call sites covering the eight public bridge ops, since `bridge_preview`/`bridge_sync` share one call inside `_bridge_run`), and one in `_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py::_emit_operation_shadow`. Deleting the shared functions (AC5) requires ALL sixteen migrated first — see Scope. Four existing test modules assert on the retired symbols directly (`tests/unit/test_operation_snapshot.py`, `tests/unit/test_single_definition_helpers.py`, `tests/scripts/test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py`) and are updated in lockstep — see Scope.

## Approach

- Derive a focused LLM config projection from the existing snapshot/schema/provenance; pair it with existing non-serializable `LLMRuntime`.
- Thread that context through gate/workflow/runner entry points so subcalls inherit policy rather than re-resolving it.
- Preserve ProviderSession/provider-native auth, budgets, cache/output/retry behavior, tracing, secret exclusions.
- Add consumer-level metamorphic tests for multi-step runs and failure/retry paths.
- Delete the shadow switch/function and migrated ambient-resolution branches after parity; tighten the existing ownership gate and documentation.

**Call-site classification:** LLM sites bind the NEW `compose_and_bind_llm_config` — FOUR public entry points make an actual LLM call: `rebar.llm.review_code`/`verify_completion`/`review_plan`/`scan_epics_for_spec` (each reached by both the CLI and the matching `_mcp_llm.py` tool, so one binding covers CLI/MCP/Python), plus `_lib_ops.py`'s `run_workflow` (binds inside `workflow/runs.py::run()` itself — `get_workflow_status`/`get_workflow_result` are pure replay, no LLM call, no config needed). The `_mcp_llm.py` `sign_review` tool wraps `resign_plan_review`, which makes NO LLM call — EXCLUDED from the LLM binding and the parity artifact's compose-once list; like every MCP tool it still gets the general `compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot` for ticket/store reads. Non-LLM sites (`_lib_ops.py`'s seven bridge/reconciler-mapping call sites, the reconciler's `_emit_operation_shadow`) bind the EXISTING general `compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot` (ticket 3a08's composer, no new machinery), completing the cutover 3a08 deferred here; the `_mcp_llm.py` registrar is also wrapped with this same general binding (closing 3a08's noted 'pending ec44' gap), independent of the LLM-specific composer. Once no production caller remains, `emit_shadow_snapshot`/`_shadow`/`shadow_enabled`/`SHADOW_ENV` are deleted, and any re-export (`rebar/config.py`) removed with them.

**AC3 fail-fast vs. the general snapshot's fail-open (deliberately DIFFERENT contracts):** `compose_and_bind_operation_snapshot`, reused verbatim for the non-LLM sites, keeps its established fail-open swallow — unchanged, already-accepted 3a08 behavior for CLI/store ops. The NEW `compose_and_bind_llm_config` for LLM sites does NOT inherit that swallow: `LLMConfig.from_env()`'s `ConfigError`/credential/provider-resolution failures propagate uncaught, so an LLM op with unresolvable auth fails before any external call (AC3) rather than degrading to unbound ambient resolution. The two composers are independent; only the LLM one is held to AC3's fail-fast bar.

**Parity-verification artifact:** `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_llm_config_authoritative_binding.py` (new, mirrors 3a08's `test_operation_snapshot_authoritative_binding.py`) asserts through production entry points: (1) compose-once/reentrancy — `review_code`/`verify_completion`/`review_plan`/`scan_epics_for_spec`/`run_workflow` (NOT `resign_plan_review`, see classification above) each bind exactly one `LLMConfig`, nested gate/workflow steps observe the identical (`is`) instance; (2) value parity vs. pre-cutover `LLMConfig.from_env()`; (3) the metamorphic/failure-edge/secret-boundary cases below. This file, plus the existing focused suites passing unchanged, is the "parity" gate AC5's deletion is conditioned on.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_operation_config.py` — remove diagnostic shadow machinery (`emit_shadow_snapshot`, `_shadow`, `shadow_enabled`, `SHADOW_ENV`) after every call site below is migrated.
- `src/rebar/llm/` (incl. `config.py`'s `gate_config`/`resolve_gate_config` and a new LLM config-binding module) plus `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py` — migrate all ten `_shadow(...)` sites: three LLM workflow ops (`run_workflow` delegates to `workflow/runs.py::run()`'s own binding; the two replay-only ops need no binding), seven non-LLM bridge/reconciler-mapping sites (covering eight public bridge ops) onto the existing general snapshot binding.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` — migrate its one `emit_shadow_snapshot(surface="reconciler")` site onto the existing general snapshot binding.
- `src/rebar/config.py` — remove any `SHADOW_ENV`/`shadow_enabled` re-export once the underlying symbols are deleted.
- Focused LLM/provider/cache/fallback/workflow tests and cross-surface contract tests, incl. the new `test_llm_config_authoritative_binding.py` parity/metamorphic/failure-edge suite, and the four existing test modules named above.
- `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`, `docs/config.md`, and `docs/architecture.md`.

## Testing

Happy path: CLI, MCP, Python multi-step gates use one snapshot, preserving current provider/cache/retry/output behavior. Metamorphic edge: mutate every behavior-bearing LLM setting after composition; the active run stays stable, the next observes it. Failure edges cover missing/conflicting auth, retries, fallback, workflow subcalls, secret/non-secret boundary leakage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Each public CLI, MCP, and Python LLM/gate operation composes one snapshot/context; every subcall and workflow step receives its projection/runtime without rereading environment/files/CWD.
- [x] Mutating model/provider class, timeout, retry, cache, headers, tracing, or repository settings after composition cannot change an in-progress multi-step run; the next operation observes the mutation.
- [x] Explicit supplied config/snapshot stays authoritative, and missing/conflicting decision-bearing provider/auth composition fails before an external call without anonymous/cross-provider fallback.
- [x] `LLMRuntime` and `ProviderSession` remain the live-auth and provider-resource owners; no secret/live capability enters snapshot bytes, fingerprints, repr, logs, exceptions, or schemas.
- [x] `emit_shadow_snapshot`, its migration switch, diagnostic-only production call sites (LLM AND non-LLM — see Scope), and migrated below-boundary `LLMConfig.from_env` branches are deleted. Any retained `from_env` public composition wrapper delegates once to the central composer and is structurally allowlisted by exact symbol/rationale.
- [x] The ownership gate fails on synthetic direct/aliased ambient reloads and carries zero post-cutover legacy exceptions.
- [x] Consumer-level metamorphic tests plus focused LLM/provider/cache/fallback/workflow suites, default suite, lint, typecheck, complexity, and module-size gates pass; docs and ADR 0098 describe the authoritative state rather than shadow mode.
baseline.summary: Make OperationSnapshot authoritative for LLM operations and retire shadow resolution

## Why
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is exposed as an env var ONLY in the remote/cloud runner; the LOCAL Claude Code CLI does not export it. Without a shim the session-provenance feature silently no-ops for local-CLI users — the most common case. The robust, harness-agnostic capture is a Claude Code SessionStart hook that reads the hook's `session_id` from stdin and exports it as the portable `REBAR_SESSION_ID`, plus the harness tag `AI_AGENT=claude-code`.

## What
- **Hook script (`scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh`).** Reads the
  SessionStart JSON envelope from stdin (field `session_id`) and, when `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is
  set, APPENDS `export REBAR_SESSION_ID=<id>` and `export AI_AGENT=claude-code` to it. These
  are the Claude Code hook-contract facts — the SessionStart stdin `session_id` field and the
  `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` env-injection file — per the **Claude Code hooks reference**
  (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), cited in the script header + docs page. GRACEFUL
  DEGRADATION: this is the only external-API coupling, and if a future Claude Code renames the
  field/var or changes the mechanism, the shim simply no-ops (no `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` / unparsed
  `session_id` → exit 0) — it never errors or blocks the session, so a wrong assumption fails
  safe. To make that fail-safe OBSERVABLE (not silently inert), the docs ship a **manual
  verification procedure** (`echo "$REBAR_SESSION_ID"` in a fresh session; claim + `show` and
  check `claimed_session`/`claim_harness`) so an operator can confirm the hook is actually
  wired and diagnose an env-mechanism mismatch. This external-integration coupling is
  irreducible — a shim MUST name the harness's env-injection var — and is grounded in the
  cited official reference plus that verification step. The harness tag is the base name
  `claude-code` (the `AI_AGENT` vocabulary permits an optional `_<version>` suffix, but the
  local hook has no reliable version source, so it emits the bare base name). Uses `python3`
  (the interpreter rebar itself runs on — a system prerequisite, `requires-python >= 3.11`, not
  a packaged dependency; if it is somehow absent on PATH the parse yields empty and the hook
  no-ops) to parse the JSON
  robustly — any parse failure, a missing/blank `session_id`, or an absent `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is
  a silent no-op with exit 0 (fire-and-forget; NEVER blocks the session). Idempotent: re-firing
  on resume/clear/compact first STRIPS this hook's own prior `REBAR_SESSION_ID`/`AI_AGENT`
  exports from the env file (preserving other hooks' lines) then re-writes the current values,
  so the file never accumulates duplicate/stale lines and always reflects the CURRENT session
  (whose id may differ across resume per gotcha G1 — not "the same value").
- **Vocabulary alignment.** Update the `claude-code_<ver>` examples in `docs/config.md`,
  `docs/event-schema.md`, and the `session_id.py` comment to present the harness tag as a base
  name with an OPTIONAL `_<version>` suffix, so bare `claude-code` is consistent with the
  documented vocabulary.
- **Docs (`docs/session-id-shims.md`).** A new install guide: the `settings.json`
  `hooks.SessionStart` snippet pointing at the script, the caveat that the id is NOT stable
  across `--resume`/`--continue`/fork/subagents (epic gotcha G1 — treat it as "the session
  that emitted the claim event"), and guidance to keep it session-scoped (do NOT export
  `REBAR_SESSION_ID` from a shell profile — gotcha G3). Cross-links `docs/config.md`.

## Scope
- IN: the Claude Code SessionStart hook script; the `docs/session-id-shims.md` install page;
  the small vocabulary-alignment edits (`docs/config.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`,
  `session_id.py`); and a NEW `tests/unit/test_session_shims.py` validating the script (valid
  shell + env-file output for mock stdin, malformed JSON, idempotent re-fire, unwritable-file,
  and no-op cases) AND asserting the base-name vocabulary form across all three doc/comment
  targets.
- OUT: Codex/Cursor shims (S6 / 7656, which extend the same docs page); the record/read core
  (S1-S3, S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh` exists and is valid shell. Proof:
      `bash -n scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh` (asserted in
      `tests/unit/test_session_shims.py`).
- [ ] Given stdin `{"session_id":"abc123"}` and a `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` temp path, the script
      writes `export REBAR_SESSION_ID=abc123` AND `export AI_AGENT=claude-code` to that file.
      Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_session_shims.py -k claude_code_exports -q`.
- [ ] Robust no-op (exit 0, never blocks the session) for each of: a blank/missing
      `session_id`, MALFORMED/unparseable JSON on stdin, an unset `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, AND an
      UNWRITABLE `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` (path under a non-existent dir). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_session_shims.py -k "noop or malformed or unwritable" -q`.
- [ ] `docs/session-id-shims.md` includes a "Verifying the hook is wired" section (the
      `echo "$REBAR_SESSION_ID"` + claim/`show` procedure), so the fail-safe design is

baseline.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in **bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json` (1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40 consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x), and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git — an earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and dropped re-homing it off-branch (WS-1) because the convergence loop already self-heals binding drift. So the levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included (child A6) under an operator-approved quiescence protocol. Its mechanics are **proven, not theoretical**: `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` on the real branch produced 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%) with all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges preserved and the HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths. Stock git plumbing only — `git-filter-repo` is deliberately **not** used: it is an unwanted core dependency and it prunes empty commits, which would reshape the DAG that ancestry-based authorship verification walks.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` + write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`
2. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; read `max(new, legacy)`
3. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority (exclude `assignee`)
4. **A2-2** delete the legacy in-line `last_get_pass` field (gated on writer rollout)
5. **A4-1/2/3** `bridge_fsck` fence, then `prev_snapshot` -> key-set, then branch-3 empty-payload skip
6. **A5** ADR covering all three committed-format changes
7. **A6** one-time reclaim under the quiescence protocol (LAST; requires A1-A5 and Epic B's B6)

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes to a shared store file, each with a stated boundary. A2-1 is reversible (it never stops writing the legacy field). A3 is reversible because the read path canonicalizes both shapes idempotently. A2-2 and A4-2 are the irreversible steps: A2-2 is gated on observed writer rollout; reverting A4-2 requires the reverse-direction corpus diff recorded first. A6 is gated on an off-repo backup bundle plus a fail-closed epoch guard, and its resumability is explicitly **none** — mitigated by running every correctness assertion on a scratch clone before anything is published.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline today 12.79 KB.
      Verify: the measurement script recorded in the child ticket.
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: integration against a stateful fake asserting
      file bytes and commit count, not call counts.
- [ ] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference to it remains. Verify: `grep -r baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty) — the read-only path must not persist a migration.
- [ ] A **dict-shaped** baseline fed through the live `compute_update_fields` path yields the same
      verdict as its normalized-string equivalent. This test does not exist today; the existing
      cells use flat strings only, so a no-op-on-strings normalizer would pass while proving
      nothing. Tier: integration through the real production comparison path.
- [ ] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over >=4 real snapshot pairs shows zero
      difference in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect, **and** the reverse-direction
      diff is recorded as the A4-2 rollback artifact.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` is **<=800 LOC** after the rotation extraction (it is at exactly 800
      today; the locked module-size gate fails the build on 801).
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB**, `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded
      pre-rewrite tip tree, and commit and merge-commit counts are unchanged (measured at window
      time, not hardcoded).
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** (the assertion that actually proves non-resurrection) and
      `size-pack` growth is <1 MB.
- [ ] A clone on a stale epoch attempting to push **aborts and performs no merge** at **both**
      guarded sites (`sync._union_merge` and `push.py`'s non-FF retry). Tier: integration in two
      real temporary clones with divergent epochs.
- [ ] An ADR exists enumerating all three committed-format changes, the mixed-version protocol, the
      A2-2 gate, and each rollback boundary.
- [ ] The off-repo backup bundle exists and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] Operator has confirmed zero active sessions and all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped before the
      reclaim window. **[operator-attested]**
baseline.summary: Bound tickets-store growth: make the committed .bridge_state cache cheap + one-time reclaim of the spent ~1 GiB
