baseline.description:
Own the **remediation-mode GATE**: the freshness-window + precondition check that decides
whether a re-review runs in floored (remediation) mode or as a normal full review, and wire
it parallel to `drift_refresh` in `_run_plan_review`. (This is the task-4 candidate-check; the
Pass-3 drop math it gates is task cc5b. Body/title were previously swapped with task 3689 —
this restores the epic's 6-task decomposition.)

## Preconditions (ALL required, else byte-identical full review)

- config enabled (`remediation_mode` key; see rollout note below)
- plan changed since the prior review
- **code UNCHANGED since baseline** — detected deterministically by comparing the gate's
  attested `verified_at_sha` (the origin/main snapshot SHA the gate signs into the prior
  review's manifest) against the current run's `verified_at_sha`. Equal ⇒ code unchanged;
  differ ⇒ code drifted. This reuses the already-signed snapshot ref — no new diff machinery.
- registry unchanged (criteria-routing material fingerprint equal to the prior review's)
- a prior `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar WITH finding text is available (task e344)
- the last review of ANY kind (full or partial) is within the window (default 60 min),
  measured from that last review and **reset on each review** so the loop persists across a
  series of edits and lapses to a normal full review only after the agent goes idle.

Code-changed / both-drifted → full review (`drift_refresh` path byte-unchanged, out of scope).

## Rollout (resolves the default-on advisory)

The `remediation_mode` config key ships **default-OFF** for one release (expand-contract:
ship off → validate on the dogfood corpus → flip the default on in a follow-up), so existing
consumers do not silently get a narrowed verdict on upgrade. Setting the key off (or absent)
restores byte-identical full-review behavior at any time — the back-out.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Candidate check enforces ALL preconditions; any failure → full review (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, `attest.py`)
- [ ] `remediation_mode` config key (default-OFF for v1) + window minutes (default 60) in `src/rebar/config.py`; key off/absent → byte-identical full review
- [ ] "code unchanged" is the `verified_at_sha` equality check (prior manifest vs current run); registry-unchanged is the routing material-fingerprint equality check
- [ ] Window measured from the last review of any kind, reset on each review
- [ ] both-drifted → full review; `drift_refresh` path byte-unchanged
- [ ] Wiring is parallel to `drift_refresh` in `_run_plan_review`; the Pass-3 drop math itself lives in cc5b (this task only decides remediation-mode eligibility)
baseline.summary: Remediation-mode gate: freshness window + preconditions + wiring

baseline.description:
# A tracker re-clone silently re-identifies the environment, invalidating every attestation

`.env-id` is git-ignored local state (tracker `.gitignore` lines 1, 13, 14 cover `.env-id`, `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`) that is STAMPED INTO EVERY EVENT and is the `principal` of every op-cert attestation. Re-cloning the tracker without carrying it over mints a NEW environment identity, and every attestation signed by the old one becomes unverifiable.

## Context / Problem

Operators re-clone or rebuild the tickets tracker (this happened on 2026-08-09 while remediating bug 2fa6). A fresh clone carries the events but not the git-ignored local state, so `.env-id` is absent and rebar mints a new uuid with no signal at all. Hours later the claim gate reports `verdict: foreign_key` on a ticket that had already earned an attestation, and it reads as a per-ticket problem when it is store-wide. The prior session's handoff note warned about this in capitals and the operator still hit it, which is the argument for a mechanical signal at the moment of the act rather than more documentation.

## Observed

`.env-id` was regenerated at 20:39 (`b8a354e0-…`, replacing `ade0f2ef-…`) and a new `.opcert-key` at 20:50. Store scan: 2498 ticket directories carry material referencing the OLD env id, 7 carry both, 4 carry only the new one.

    rebar review-plan b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5 --status
    verdict: foreign_key — "op-cert signed by a different environment
    (principal 'ade0f2ef-…'; this environment is 'b8a354e0-…')"

## Confirmed root cause

`rebar._commands.init._ensure_env_id_unit` (the `env-id` ensure-registry unit, run from every init entry point, the MCP boot path and `fsck --repair`) and `init._gen_local_files` both mint a fresh uuid whenever `.env-id` is absent, with NO check for whether the store already holds events written by a different environment. Event files carry the writing environment at the top level (`env_id`), so the prior identity IS discoverable on disk — nothing consults it.

## Why 'just accept both env ids' does NOT fix it

Verifying a signature made by the old environment needs THAT environment's op-cert public key, which is git-ignored, was never committed, and is gone. An accept-list would only move the failure from `foreign_key` to `mismatch`; making it PASS would mean accepting the principal WITHOUT verifying the signature, which defeats the gate. Publishing per-environment public keys is the principled fix and is OUT OF SCOPE — a trust-model change needing its own ADR (operator decision 2026-08-12). Full analysis in the comments.

## Approach

Operator decision (2026-08-12, B7): **warn loudly with an explicit override — do not refuse outright, do not silently migrate identities.**

1. Extract the environment-identity concern into a new leaf module
   `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py`: read/mint, the bounded scan for env ids already in the
   store, the override, the warning text, the relocated `env-id` ensure unit, and the
   divergence report. A new module because `init.py` is already at the module-size cap.
2. Minting into a populated store WARNS loudly on stderr — naming the prior env id(s), the
   attestation consequence, and the git-ignored state to carry over — and still completes.
   It warns rather than refuses because a second clone mounting a shared tickets branch is a
   first-class workflow that legitimately needs its own identity, and the store cannot tell
   that from a re-clone; only the operator can.
3. `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` acknowledges it and quietens the warning. An env var, not a
   CLI flag, because the mint happens inside the ensure registry, which runs from the CLI, the
   MCP boot path and the library alike.
4. `rebar fsck` gains a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` check, scoped by AUTHOR (this environment's
   own author also writing under another env id) so it does not fire on the healthy
   multi-clone topology. It reuses the pairs the authorship tally already collects.
5. Document the re-clone carry-over list and what breaks per file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` (new) — env-id read/mint/scan, override, warning text,
  divergence report, and the relocated `env-id` ensure unit.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — `_ensure_env_id_unit` moves out; `_gen_local_files` delegates
  its `.env-id` mint to the new module (net LOC decreases, keeping the module under the cap).
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — `_registry()` maps `env-id` to the relocated unit.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — collect event `env_id`s during check 1 and emit the counted
  `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — the re-clone carry-over list (`.env-id`, `.opcert-key`,
  `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`) and what breaks per file.
- `tests/` — new tests for the guard, the override, and the fsck check.

Nothing else changes. Ticket history is NOT rewritten: events are append-only and correctly stamped with the environment that actually wrote them. No `.env-id` restoration and no identity migration.

## Testing

- Happy path: a store with events all carrying the CURRENT env id runs the ensure unit as `ok`
  and produces no `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line from fsck.
- Guard path (held-out): a tracker with existing events stamped `E1` and NO `.env-id` — the
  ensure unit does not write `.env-id`, returns a non-`ok` outcome, and the message names `E1`
  and the override.
- Override path: the same fixture with `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` mints `.env-id` and still
  warns.
- Empty/edge: a store with NO events (genesis init) mints silently — no warning, no regression
  to first-time `rebar init`.
- Detector path: a tracker with events stamped `E1` and `.env-id` = `E2` makes `rebar fsck`
  emit a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` issue naming both ids, present in `--output json`.
- Unreadable/garbage event files are skipped by the scan and never crash the ensure unit or
  fsck.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Minting `.env-id` into a store that already holds events from another environment is
      never silent: a stderr warning names the prior env id(s), the attestation consequence,
      the git-ignored files to carry over, and the override. Verified by a test asserting the
      message contains the prior id, `attestation`, `.opcert-key` and the override name.
- [x] The mint still COMPLETES, so a second clone mounting a shared tickets branch stays
      writable. Verified by a test that mints over a foreign-event store and then creates a
      ticket, and by the existing two-clone integration test staying green.
- [x] `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY=1` acknowledges the situation and quietens the warning to a
      one-line note that still records what was written over. Verified by a test asserting no
      `WARNING` and the prior id present.
- [x] A store with no prior events (genesis `rebar init`) mints with no warning. Verified by a
      test on an emptied store.
- [x] `rebar fsck` emits a counted `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` issue, naming both ids and present in
      `--output json`, when THIS environment's author also wrote events under a different env
      id. Verified by a test over a fixture store.
- [x] That check does NOT fire on the healthy multi-clone topology (several env ids, different
      authors). Verified by a dedicated false-positive test.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` lists the local state a re-clone must carry over (`.env-id`,
      `.opcert-key`, `.opcert-key.pub`, `.ensure-applied`), what breaks per file, and why the
      guard warns rather than refuses. Verified by reading the rendered section.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full `pytest` suite pass in the worktree.

## Provenance

Found when the claim gate blocked task b2bb during the store/signing remediation session.
baseline.summary: Tracker re-clone silently re-identifies the environment, voiding attestations

## Why

Audit Maintainability finding #1: `reconcile.py:697` (and the reconciler's `_loader` helper) loads sibling modules by file path (`_load("reconcile_run_differs", "run_differs.py")`) instead of normal package imports. This defeats every static tool the repo relies on — Pyright/Serena reference resolution, import-linter layering checks, IDE navigation, and the grounding oracle — in the repo's largest and most change-heavy subsystem (~40 modules, 5 of the 10 biggest files). The audit rated the reconciler the highest-onboarding-cost area partly because of this. The mechanism predates the reconciler shipping as a proper package; it is now pure legacy.

## What

Convert the `_engine/rebar_reconciler` path-based `_load()` calls to ordinary `from . import …` / `import rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.…` package imports, delete the `_load()` helper once callerless, and let the existing lazy-import pattern (module-level function-local imports with rationale comments) handle any genuine circular-import seams the conversion surfaces.

## Scope

In: all `_load()` call sites under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, the loader helper itself, and any import-cycle untangling the conversion forces. Out: any behavioral change to reconciliation, module splits/renames (janitor epics own refactors — this story changes only *how modules are referenced*, which is why it rides this epic despite the scope boundary; flagged at creation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zero path-based `_load(` call sites remain under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (grep-verifiable)
- [ ] The `_load` helper is deleted outright — the file-path loader (`spec_from_file_location`-based `_load()` and the `_loader.py` `lazy_load` bootstrap) is removed once callerless, with no deprecation stub left behind (deletion is final; there is no future migration path to preserve)
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; reconciler test suites (`tests/scripts/bridge/`, reconciler units) pass unchanged
- [ ] Pyright/Serena can resolve references into the converted modules (spot-check: find-references on a converted symbol returns its call sites)
- [ ] No new import cycles: `python -c "import rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler"` and the optionality guard stay green
baseline.summary: Reconciler: replace path-based _load() module loading with package imports

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Once a store actually syncs more than one tracker project, an older rebar binary reading it is dangerous rather than merely limited: it would fetch only its single configured project, see every other project's bound tickets as having no corresponding remote issue, and create duplicate issues in the wrong project. There is a shipped mechanism for exactly this — `.store-compat.json` with a fail-closed read (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`) — but `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is still an empty frozenset (`compat.py:60`), so no capability has ever been declared through it.

## Approach

Register `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. That single addition is what makes a binary able to *recognise* the capability; a binary that predates it hits the "required capability this binary does not provide" branch and raises `StoreIncompatibleError`, refusing writes rather than corrupting the store (`docs/migrations.md:158-165`).

This is the expand half of the expand/contract rollout `docs/migrations.md:138-149` describes: teach binaries to read and fail closed **before** anything writes the requirement. Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story, so shipping it changes no behaviour for any existing store. The conditional stamp lands separately, which is why the two are ordered rather than combined.

Reads deliberately stay available: the gate is on the write lock only (`docs/migrations.md:174-178`), so `list`/`show`/`search` keep working against a store an old binary may not write, and `fsck` surfaces the condition as a structured `compat_error` without changing its exit code.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's pure-branch row: an in-process unit test against the real classification function, since the mechanism is entirely a validation branch with no I/O of its own — plus one real-store test for the write-gate, because the gate fires inside lock acquisition and a unit test would not cross that component.

- Happy path: a record declaring `multi-project-bridge` classifies as compatible on a binary that
  registers it.
- Contrast case: a record declaring an unregistered capability name still raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError` — proving the registration widened the known set by exactly one entry and
  did not disable the check.
- Absent-record regression: a store with no `.store-compat.json` still passes through as implicit
  legacy, so pre-feature stores are unaffected.
- Write-gate path: a store whose record declares an unknown capability refuses a write through the
  real lock acquisition, while `list`/`show` against the same store still succeed. The read half is
  the contrast case that proves the gate is scoped to writes.
- Corrupt-record path: a malformed record still raises rather than being treated as absent, which is
  the bypass the gate is designed to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `multi-project-bridge` is in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` and a record declaring it classifies as
      compatible; checked by a unit test over the classification function.
- [ ] A record declaring an unregistered capability still raises `StoreIncompatibleError`; checked by
      the paired negative case.
- [ ] A store with no compat record still passes through as implicit legacy; checked by an
      absent-record regression test.
- [ ] A store declaring an unknown capability refuses writes while reads still succeed; checked by a
      real-store test exercising the write lock and a read command against the same store.
- [ ] A corrupt record raises rather than being treated as absent; checked by a malformed-record test.
baseline.summary: Register the multi-project-bridge store-compat capability (expand half)

baseline.description:
Make `idea → closed` a reject/drop transition that bypasses the completion/attestation close gates, keyed on the from-status being `idea`.

## Why

Closing a ticket that is in `idea` means "reject/drop this undesigned idea," not "this work is complete." Running the completion/attestation gates on it is nonsensical — there is nothing built to verify or attest — and would block the reject. Only the from-status `idea` is exempted; every other close path is unchanged.

## What

- Place the bypass in `close_ticket()` (transition_close.py) as a guard **after**
  the open-children guard block and **before** the `_completion_precheck` call:
  when the from-status (`current_status`) is `idea`, skip the precheck and return
  a normal close result. `_completion_precheck` does not receive `current_status`,
  so the check belongs at the call site — this keeps the open-children guard
  unconditional and threads no new parameter into `_completion_precheck`. Skipping
  the precheck covers the completion verifier, the file-impact→referencing-commit
  precheck, and the reason-guard copy inside the precheck.
- In `transition_core` (txn.py), skip the bug-close-reason guard and the
  story/epic signature gate when the from-status is `idea`.
- Keep the structural open-children guard active for `idea → closed` (integrity,
  not completion): a parent in `idea` with non-closed children is still refused.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — `close_ticket()` from-status guard
  placed after the open-children guard and before `_completion_precheck`; the
  open-children guard itself is left in place.
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — `transition_core` skips the bug-reason guard and
  signature gate when from-status is `idea`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Closing a ticket from `idea` does not invoke the completion verifier
      (test-verified, e.g. via a spy/no-LLM assertion).
- [ ] Closing a ticket from `idea` does not run the file-impact→referencing-commit
      precheck.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` bug does not require a `Fixed:`/`Escalated:` close reason.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` story does not require a certified signature under the
      signature gate.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` epic does not require a certified signature under the
      signature gate.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` parent that has a non-closed child is still refused by the
      structural open-children guard (test-verified).
- [ ] A normal (non-`idea`) close path still runs the completion verifier
      unchanged (regression test-verified).
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.
baseline.summary: Bypass completion/attestation close gates for idea-to-closed

## Target
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — **793 LOC** vs the 800-LOC hard cap: 7 lines of headroom.

## The concern boundary: BLOCKING checks vs NEVER-BLOCKING checks

The module's own docstring already states the invariant this split cuts along: "The only sound, unambiguous blockers are therefore **P1, P4 (description), P5 (cycle), P8, P10, and P11**. Everything else is advisory or coverage-only."

That documented boundary is also a real seam in the CALL GRAPH. The four never-blocking checks — **P2 resolution**, **P3 package-existence**, **P6 AC/DD quality**, **P7 destructive-sniff** — have ZERO call edges, inbound or outbound, to any other function that stays in `det_floor.py`:

- `p2_resolution` and `p3_package_existence` call only `rebar.grounding.refute_absence` (lazily
  imported) plus their own private extraction regexes `_FILE_REF_RE` / `_PKG_REF_RE`.
- `p6_ac_quality` is a pure aggregation hub over the ALREADY-EXTRACTED advisory-lint siblings:
  `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines`, `det_clarity.vague_hits_in_line`,
  `det_lint._verify_command_strings` / `_lint_verify_command`,
  `det_operator_attested.operator_evidence_issues`,
  `det_measurement_provenance.provenance_issues`, `det_citation.unbacked_citations`. Moving it puts
  the hub in a module beside its spokes instead of in the floor's core.
- `p7_destructive` calls nothing; it owns `_DESTRUCTIVE_RE` / `_SAFEGUARD_RE` outright.

The checks that STAY are the ones that are actually connected: `p1_readiness_shape` and `p4_oversize` both call `_count_ac_items`; `p1_readiness_shape` calls `_clarity_score`; `p4_oversize` calls `_description_limit`; `p8_reviewability` calls `est_tokens`; `p5_task_dag` calls `det_lint._find_cycle` / `_file_interference`. Cutting between those two sets removes 246 lines without severing a single existing call edge.

## Established precedent
`det_clarity.py` (P10/P11) and `det_lint.py` (P9 + helpers) were extracted from this module on this same seam and re-exported from `det_floor.py`. This is the third application of that pattern, including its cycle-avoidance contract: `from __future__ import annotations` + `TYPE_CHECKING` for the `DetResult` / `PlanContext` annotations, and a lazy `from .det_floor import DetResult` inside each function body, so there is no runtime import back into `det_floor`.

## What moves
New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_advisory.py` receives these definitions verbatim: `_FILE_REF_RE`, `p2_resolution`, `_PKG_REF_RE`, `p3_package_existence`, `p6_ac_quality`, `_DESTRUCTIVE_RE`, `_SAFEGUARD_RE`, `p7_destructive`.

Function bodies alone are not self-contained: `p6_ac_quality` calls `vague_hits_in_line(ln)`, `_verify_command_strings(ctx)` and `_lint_verify_command(cmd)` as BARE names, bound today by `det_floor.py`'s module-level import block. So `det_advisory.py` declares its own module-level imports, mirroring those bindings:

```python
from .det_clarity import vague_hits_in_line
from .det_lint import _lint_verify_command, _verify_command_strings
```

plus `import re`, `from __future__ import annotations`, and `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any` with `DetResult` / `PlanContext` under `TYPE_CHECKING`. p6's other dependencies (`det_citation`, `det_measurement_provenance`, `det_operator_attested`, `rebar._reads`) are already IN-BODY lazy imports and travel with the body untouched; `p2_resolution` / `p3_package_existence` likewise carry their in-body `from rebar import grounding`. Each moved function gains one line — the lazy `from .det_floor import DetResult` — exactly as `det_clarity.p10_verification_presence` and `det_lint.p9_file_impact_coverage` already do.

Symmetrically, `det_floor.py` DROPS the three imports whose only consumer was `p6_ac_quality`, while keeping `_find_cycle` / `_file_interference` (used by the retained `p5_task_dag`) and the `decomposition_state_block` / `veto_undecomposed_g5` re-exports `pass1.py` reaches through it.

`det_floor.py` stays the ENTRY MODULE and dispatcher: it keeps `DetResult`, `PlanContext`, `est_tokens`, `DET_CHECKS`, `run_det_floor` and the finding/coverage aggregation (`det_finding_has_subject`, `det_blocking_findings`, `det_advisory_findings`, `det_coverage`), and re-exports all four moved checks so every existing import point and every `det_floor.<check>` attribute access keeps resolving unchanged.

## Why the retained half is the half that stays
Three tests bind to the `det_floor` MODULE OBJECT and would silently stop testing anything if their target moved: `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` monkeypatches `det_floor.DET_CHECKS`; `tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py` monkeypatches `det_floor.run_det_floor`; `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py` and `..._heldout.py` monkeypatch `sizing.det_floor.est_tokens`. All three targets are in the RETAINED half. `_clarity_score`, `_count_ac_items` and `_description_limit` are imported by name from `det_floor` by lockstep/migration tests and also stay. No moved symbol is monkeypatched anywhere; every reference to a moved symbol is a call through the re-export or a `from ... det_floor import` the re-export satisfies.

## Sizes
`det_floor.py` 793 -> ~550 (approx 250 lines / 31% headroom); `det_advisory.py` ~300. Both in the 200-500 target band; neither under 100.

## Registry sweep (path-keyed artifacts)
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — **zero** entries keyed to
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`, so no moved symbol carries a ceiling and the ratchet
  cannot report `new>0`. Re-verified with `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.
- `tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py` `_OWNED_FILES` / `_MARKER_BUDGET` — lists
  `llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`. No config read moves (`_description_limit`, the module's only
  `compose_config` call, stays), so the new module must report zero config-ownership findings and
  zero `# read-via:` markers; verified via `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`.
- `.github/module-size-limit.txt` — NOT touched. The gate and `tests/module_size_support.py` are
  path-agnostic (`rglob`), so the new file needs no registration.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` name `det_floor.py` as the
  layer-1 home; prose repointed to name the new sibling. Prose only, no assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py) -le 720` exits 0.
- [x] `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_advisory.py) -ge 100` exits 0.
- [x] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_advisory import p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive"` exits 0.
- [x] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive"` exits 0, proving the re-export preserves the old import point.
- [x] `python -c "import rebar.llm.plan_review.det_advisory as m; m.vague_hits_in_line; m._lint_verify_command; m._verify_command_strings"` exits 0, proving p6's bare-name dependencies are bound at module level in the new home.
- [x] `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` reports no changed test file other than a prose-only docstring repoint.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_clarity.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py tests/unit/test_g5_decomp_det.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py tests/unit/test_a8e5_det_hygiene_edge.py tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` exits 0.
- [x] `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt` exits 0.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0 reporting `new=0 increased=0`.
- [x] The commit message names the blocking-vs-never-blocking concern boundary as the seam, with its call-graph evidence.
baseline.summary: Split llm/plan_review/det_floor.py (793 LOC) along its concern boundary

baseline.description:
## Summary
`rebar show <id>` intermittently returns EMPTY stdout with an apparently-successful (zero) exit instead of the ticket JSON. Downstream consumers that pipe/redirect `show` into a parser receive empty input and crash. The store itself is intact — the same ticket `show`s correctly moments later, and `fsck` is clean — so this is a read-output bug, not data loss.

## Circumstances under which we observed it
Seen repeatedly during a session doing scripted read→transform→write loops on tickets (fetch a description with `rebar show`, edit it, push with `rebar edit --description`):
- It manifests during a BURST of rapid back-to-back rebar invocations — several `rebar edit` (writes) immediately
  followed by `rebar show` (reads) — with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` (the default), so each write spawns a
  background push to `origin/tickets`.
- The empty return correlates with those in-flight background pushes/git activity on the `tickets` worktree
  (`.tickets-tracker/`): a tight retry loop of `rebar show <id> > file` can fail on EVERY attempt (8/8) during the
  contention window, while a single `rebar show` after a multi-second quiet period succeeds.
- DECISIVE SIGNAL: setting `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` for the read/write burst made `rebar show` succeed reliably every
  time (single piped call) — strongly implicating background-push / git-lock contention as the cause.
- During the same window, `rebar clarity-check <id>` and `rebar check-ac <id>` on the SAME id SUCCEED (a different
  read path), and `rebar fsck` reports "no issues found" — so the data is present; only `show`'s stdout comes back
  empty.
- Environment: macOS (darwin) / zsh; rebar over the `tickets` orphan branch (worktree `.tickets-tracker/`); an
  `origin` remote present; default `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`.

## Reproduction Steps
1. With `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` (default) and an `origin` remote, run a burst: `rebar edit` on several tickets,
   then immediately `rebar show <id> > out.json` (or `rebar show <id> | python3 -c "import sys,json;json.load(sys.stdin)"`).
2. Repeat in a tight loop.
3. Observe `out.json` intermittently empty / the parser failing with `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`,
   despite a success-looking exit.
4. Set `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and repeat → `rebar show` succeeds every time.

## Expected vs Actual
- EXPECTED: `rebar show` is read-consistent under concurrent background push — it returns the full ticket JSON,
  or on genuine failure exits NON-ZERO with a diagnostic on stderr. It must NEVER emit empty stdout with exit 0.
- ACTUAL: intermittently emits empty stdout with a success exit during background-push contention, silently
  breaking read→transform→write pipelines.

## Impact
- Silently breaks scripted pipelines that consume `rebar show`. It is also a latent DATA-LOSS vector in
  combination with `edit --description`: an empty `show` feeding an unguarded `edit --description "$(...)"` would
  erase content — the edit-side empty-value guard (bug `e78f-9f79`) mitigates the clobber, but the empty `show`
  is the upstream root cause and should be fixed directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar show` never returns empty stdout on a zero exit; under read/push contention it returns the complete
      record or exits non-zero with a clear error to stderr.
- [ ] `show` reads a consistent snapshot (or retries internally) so a concurrent background push to
      `origin/tickets` cannot truncate its output; reproduced + fixed under `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the burst-of-writes-then-`show` pattern and asserts `show` output is always
      complete-or-erroring (never empty+exit0).
- [ ] Audit the other read paths (clarity-check/check-ac/fsck observed unaffected) for the same race; fix
      uniformly or document why only `show` is affected.
baseline.summary: rebar show intermittently returns empty stdout (exit 0) under concurrent background auto-push

baseline.description:
The mcp service in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` does not set `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL`. On a fresh deploy the container crash-loops before serving: `AuthSettings` (pydantic) raises a ValidationError because `issuer_url` is empty (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py` ~L609, `AuthSettings(issuer_url=mcp_cfg.auth_issuer_url, ...)`), and `/health` never comes up.

## Root cause (surfaced by jackal live deploy)
The compose mcp `environment:` block sets `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL` (compose ~L347) but omits the sibling `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL`. `fetch-secrets.sh` does not inject it either, so the container boots with an empty issuer URL and fails auth-settings construction.

## Live impact
On the prod box the endpoint only came up after a temporary `.env` hotfix appending `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL=https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`. Autodeploy rsync from main will drop that hotfix and can re-crash the mcp container on the next blue-green tick.

## Fix
Add to the mcp `environment:` block, mirroring how RESOURCE_SERVER_URL is set: `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL: "${REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL:-https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp}"`

## RED-first oracle
A compose-assertion test that parses docker-compose.yml and asserts the mcp service environment defines a non-empty `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL` (fails today, passes after the fix). Note: `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py` always sets `auth_issuer_url` explicitly, so unit tests never caught the compose omission — the gap is deploy config, not the auth code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] RED compose-assertion test proves the mcp service env omits a non-empty issuer URL, then passes after the fix.
- [x] docker-compose.yml mcp environment sets REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL (default to the prod /mcp URL, overridable).
- [x] [operator-attested] Lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1).
  provenance: environment=Gerrit main gate (rebar.solutions.navateam.com) + GitHub Actions Verified Gate; principal=rebar review bot + rebar CI bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — change 2222 (patchset 2, commit 799ba486196f) merged to main with LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1.
baseline.summary: mcp compose service omits REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL -> AuthSettings crash-loop on fresh deploy

baseline.description:
## Context

Gerrit change 2169 (parent task 0754-cfc5-e451-4e9b) added the explicit, opt-in, read-only `rebar tracker-footprint` command. LLM review recorded four non-blocking hardening opportunities. This task addresses them without changing the command's opt-in, read-only, unscheduled, non-gating, threshold-free contract.

Findings:
1. Correctness/misuse: the mounted `pack` layer measures only the primary common Git object
   database (`objects/pack/*.pack`). An alternates-backed shared clone (`git clone --shared`)
   keeps its objects in the borrowed alternate object database, so the primary pack layer can
   report near-zero. The report already labels the object database `shared`, but a reader can
   still mistake the small `pack.logical_bytes` for an exclusive/complete whole-object-store
   measurement.
2. Portability: an interface assertion (`checkout_allocated > pack_logical * 4`) assumes each
   one-byte file is charged a full filesystem block; this fails on block-suballocating /
   tail-packing filesystems.
3. The allocation-unavailable text rendering path has no direct test.
4. The CLI bad-argument (argparse) exit-2 path has no direct test.

## Decision (recorded)

Retain **primary-only** pack scope rather than enumerating alternate object databases. Enumerating alternates would count borrowed, shared objects as this clone's local footprint and contradict the established whole-clone inode-dedup philosophy (shared bytes are not this clone's cost). Instead make the primary-only measurement **explicitly non-exclusive**: add a `complete` boolean to the `pack` layer — `true` when the measured `.pack` files are the complete object store backing this checkout, `false` when the checkout borrows objects from an unmeasured alternate object database (`"alternates"` present in `shared_reasons`). A linked worktree's pack is measured from the common dir and remains `complete: true` (shared across worktrees but complete). The `pack` definition string is updated to state this, and the text renderer surfaces `complete` with a clarifying note when false.

## Plan

- footprint.py: `_pack_layer` gains `complete: bool`; `measure_tracker` computes
  `complete = "alternates" not in reasons`. Update `DEFINITIONS["pack"]` to describe the
  primary-only, non-exclusive semantics.
- schema: add required `complete` boolean to `pack_layer`.
- tracker_footprint.py `_render_text`: render `complete=…` for the pack layer, with a
  parenthetical when non-exclusive.
- Tests (RED→GREEN):
  - Unit: standalone and linked-worktree pack `complete: true`; alternates pack `complete:
    false`.
  - Unit: injected-`st_blocks` assertion proves allocation = Σ(st_blocks·512) deterministically
    (replaces the filesystem-ratio assumption).
  - Unit (new tests/unit/commands/test_tracker_footprint.py): `_render_text` renders the
    allocation-unavailable label.
  - Interface: replace the `* 4` ratio with portable assertions (allocation available, small
    file count, pack complete/standalone, pack>0); add a bad-argument exit-2 CLI test.
- docs/user-guide.md, docs/reuse-surface.md: document the pack `complete` field.
- Preserve opt-in, read-only, unscheduled, non-gating, threshold-free behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `pack` layer carries a `complete` boolean; an alternates-backed mounted clone reports
      `complete: false` so it cannot be mistaken for an exclusive whole-object-store pack
      measurement; standalone and linked-worktree report `complete: true`. (unit + schema)
- [x] A real `git clone --shared` fixture proves the alternates ownership/dedup semantics
      without double-counting shared objects. (unit)
- [x] Allocation-unavailable text rendering and CLI bad-argument exit 2 have direct tests.
- [x] Allocation assertions use injected/stat capability rather than a filesystem block policy.
- [x] The command stays opt-in, read-only, unscheduled, non-gating, and threshold-free.
- [x] make lint, make typecheck, and focused tests pass; generated help/reference stay green.
baseline.summary: Harden tracker-footprint shared-clone semantics and edge-path coverage

baseline.description:
# CHANGELOG.md: git-cliff, prepend-scoped generate-then-curate from conventional commits

## Why

No user-facing changelog exists: `docs/release-notes.md` is the agent-facing contract-change log, and GitHub Releases notes are auto-generated. Across nine surveyed Python tools, towncrier (pip/pytest) solves a many-contributor merge-conflict problem rebar doesn't have; ruff/uv generate from PR labels (needs a PR workflow rebar doesn't have); git-cliff converts the conventional-commit discipline rebar already pays for into a changelog. Keep-a-Changelog is the convergent shape (rich's CHANGELOG.md is the exemplar). Rejected alternatives — towncrier (double-entry ceremony), PR-label generation (no PRs), GitHub-Releases-only (no in-repo artifact) — recorded in cliff.toml header comments.

## What

- Add `cliff.toml`. Keys under their proper sections (a top-level key is silently ignored): `[git] conventional_commits = true`, `filter_unconventional = false`, plus a catch-all commit parser so mixed-history commits are kept. The normative `commit_parsers` mapping (each line individually grep-provable in the AC): `feat` → "Added"; `fix` → "Fixed"; breaking (`!`/BREAKING CHANGE) → "Breaking" (own group, listed first); `perf` → "Changed"; `refactor` → "Changed"; `docs` → "Documentation"; skipped: `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `test`.
- **Pin the tool with an explicit version variable:** Makefile gains `GIT_CLIFF_VERSION := <exact 2.x pin chosen at execution>` and a `make changelog` target that (a) errors clearly if `git-cliff` is missing or its `--version` mismatches the pin, and (b) errors if `VERSION` is not supplied. Install path documented in docs/releasing.md as `pipx install git-cliff==<pin>` (standalone Rust binary; NOT a pyproject dev extra).
- **Invocation interface (resolves the missing-parameter finding):** `make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z` → runs exactly `git cliff --unreleased --tag $(VERSION) --prepend CHANGELOG.md`. Full-file regeneration is forbidden after initial generation: the initial run (once, back through v0.1.0; ledger quality accepted for history) is executed manually and documented as one-time; thereafter only the prepend-scoped target is sanctioned, so committed hand-curated sections are never touched. The maintainer hand-curates the newly prepended section before tagging.
- Include `## [Unreleased]` and the compare-link block (rich pattern).
- `docs/releasing.md` gains the step: `make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z` → curate the top section (~5 min) → commit → tag; plus the pin + install line. Dial position recorded there: generate-then-edit (pure-generated rejected as ledger-like; mypy-style prose rejected as unsustainable solo).
- **Repoint `[project.urls]` Changelog** (required edit; currently `docs/release-notes.md`, pyproject.toml:78) → `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md`.
- Pointer line at the top of `docs/release-notes.md`: "User-facing changelog: CHANGELOG.md; this file tracks agent-visible contract changes" (the epic's cross-link AC, owned here).
- Known consumer, acknowledged: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:310` classifies CHANGELOG-touching diffs as a hard-to-reverse surface, so curation commits score higher review impact — accepted; no code change.

## Scope

IN: `cliff.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, Makefile (`GIT_CLIFF_VERSION` + `changelog` target), `docs/releasing.md` step, pyproject urls repoint, release-notes pointer line. OUT: towncrier/news fragments; changing commit conventions; back-editing published GitHub Releases; the auto-generated GitHub Releases notes (complementary, unchanged); any change to workflow_ops.py.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` exists — prove: `grep -c "^## \[" CHANGELOG.md` ≥ 8 and `grep -q "\[Unreleased\]" CHANGELOG.md` and a compare-link block at the bottom (`grep -q "compare/" CHANGELOG.md`).
- [ ] `cliff.toml` normative mapping — prove, each individually: `grep -q "feat" cliff.toml && grep -q "Added" cliff.toml`; `grep -q "fix" cliff.toml && grep -q "Fixed" cliff.toml`; `grep -qi "breaking" cliff.toml`; `grep -q "refactor" cliff.toml`; `grep -q "Documentation" cliff.toml`; skips present: `grep -q "chore" cliff.toml`; structure: `grep -A3 "\[git\]" cliff.toml | grep -q "filter_unconventional = false"`; catch-all parser present (a trailing `message = ".*"`-style rule) — prove: `grep -q '"\.\*"' cliff.toml`; header comments record the rejected alternatives — prove: `grep -qi "towncrier" cliff.toml`.
- [ ] Makefile interface — prove: `grep -q "GIT_CLIFF_VERSION" Makefile`; `grep -q -- "--unreleased" Makefile`; `grep -q -- "--prepend" Makefile`; `grep -q "VERSION" Makefile` with a guard that errors when unset (`grep -qi "VERSION is required\|VERSION not set" Makefile`); no bare full-regen invocation in the target.
- [ ] Idempotence of the sanctioned path: running `make changelog VERSION=<current>` twice with no new commits produces no second diff.
- [ ] docs/releasing.md — prove: `grep -q "git-cliff==" docs/releasing.md` (the literal pinned install spec) and `grep -q "make changelog" docs/releasing.md`.
- [ ] URL repoint + pointer — prove: `grep "^Changelog" pyproject.toml | grep -q "CHANGELOG.md"`; `head -5 docs/release-notes.md | grep -q "CHANGELOG.md"`.
baseline.summary: CHANGELOG.md: git-cliff generate-then-curate from conventional commits

# Make a silent, identity-less writer LOUD (scoped to AC2 + AC3)

Split out of bug beb1. **Operator decision 2026-08-12: implement AC2 and AC3 ONLY.** The original limb 1 ("review-bot CREATEs carry `creation_channel=null`") was **disproven by measurement** and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — see the re-measurement comment: production CREATEs carry `creation_channel="python"` (52/52 post-deploy, zero nulls store-wide for 25 days); the null reading came from reading a top-level key that lives in `event["data"]`. "Loud" here means **logged and counted**; `identity.require_authenticated` stays advisory per ADR-0045 — this ticket does NOT make any write fail.

## Why this matters

beb1 (a review bot writing ~8900 unsigned, `Unknown`-authored events) ran for a MONTH undetected because the failure was silent at two layers that this ticket closes: `_apply_authorship` returns with no log at all when no identity resolves, and `fsck`'s authorship line is a single store-wide tally, so one env writing 0% signed is invisible behind another env's healthy volume.

## Confirmed mechanism (read from the code, 2026-08-11)

- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:327-359` — `_apply_authorship` signs only when
  `author_id AND signing_key`. When `signing_key` IS configured but `author_id` is falsy,
  control falls to the cannot-sign branch; with `require_authenticated` off (the default)
  it **returns silently**. Only the signing FAILURE path (line 341) logs.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:111-122, 259-264` — the authorship tally is summed
  store-wide into one advisory, uncounted text line. There is no per-`env_id` breakdown,
  so the per-env signed-rate analysis that eventually found beb1 remains a one-off script.

## Measured baseline (live store, read-only, 2026-08-11)

18 envs. Four are 0%-signed (`a7f6c5e0` 6 events, `37a1e8e8` 5, `00000000-…` 4, `58e9f32e` 2) and **all four are dormant** — their last event predates the store's first signed event. No env is both 0%-signed and active after signing was adopted. So the adoption-gated rule below reports **zero** issues on today's store (no legacy noise), while beb1's env `b2b5c498` (0 signed, 8914 `Unknown`-authored, writing concurrently with the signing env `ade0f2ef`) WOULD have been reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

The approved subset only — AC1 (creation_channel) is out of scope, see below.

- [x] **AC2** — `fsck` reports, as a **counted** issue (`UNSIGNED_ENV:` line, `issue_count`
      and `--output json` `issues[]`), any `env_id` that has at least one event and either
      **0 signed events** or **every event authored `Unknown`/absent**, gated so it fires
      only when the store has adopted signing AND that env wrote at or after the store's
      earliest signed event. Dormant pre-signing envs are NOT reported.
- [x] **AC3** — `_apply_authorship` emits a `logger.warning` when signing is **SKIPPED**
      for lack of a resolvable identity (or a missing signing key under the gate), naming
      the event uuid, the ticket, and which of the two inputs was missing. It must remain
      best-effort: no write may start failing because of this ticket.
- [x] Held-out tests for each: an fsck test asserting a 0%-signed active env is counted AND
      that a dormant pre-signing env is not (the false-positive guard), and a `_seam` test
      asserting the skip path logs at WARNING with the reason and still writes the event.

## Implementation notes

`fsck.py` is 779 LOC against the hard 800 cap, so the tally lands in a new leaf module `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py` (an `EnvAuthorshipTally` that `_scan` feeds from the JSON it ALREADY parses in Check 1 — no extra I/O pass) and `fsck.py` gains only the wiring. The new `unsigned_env` kind is deliberately NOT added to `_STRUCTURED_KINDS`: that set makes the transform parse the line head as a `ticket_id`, and this head is an `env_id`.

## Out of scope

creation_channel (disproven), backfilling the 166 legacy `unknown`-channel review CREATEs, and any change to `identity.require_authenticated` enforcement.
baseline.summary: No guard makes an unsigned, identity-less writer loud

# 59 of the 63 tickets orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconcile incident are STILL parentless

The **code defect** that destroyed these edges is fixed (`88d9-fe42-e50f-4067`, landed `25ead49f3e`). The **data** was never restored. This ticket tracks that outstanding restoration backlog, which no open ticket currently owns.

## What happened (re-confirmed independently in this investigation)

Reconcile run **30828160906** (GitHub Actions, `workflow_dispatch`, `MODE: live`, 2026-08-03 15:37:59-15:38:10 UTC) wrote 63 `EDIT` events with `{"fields": {"parent_id": ""}}`, author `reconciler`, all in one commit `b8062b10e97b0c891deefbefa87934bb37c66d84` on the `tickets` branch.

**All 63 destroyed a real parent edge. Zero were no-ops.**

The mechanism, cited:
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:138-139` - outbound
  **OMITS** the parent field whenever the local parent's `ticket_type != "epic"`,
  so Jira is never told about it.
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` `diff_inbound_parent` - inbound
  then read Jira's honest "no parent", classified it `PARENT_NO_PARENT`, and **CLEARED**
  the local edge. Its only guard, `should_propagate_removal`, answers the *outbound*
  question (absent locally -> delete on peer) and structurally cannot answer the inbound
  one. `add_managed_ref` is folded by the **local** parent-set event
  (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:87-90`, `:526-528`), so "managed" never proved Jira
  ever had the parent.
* Omit-vs-clear asymmetry is documented on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b`.

**Discriminating evidence (this investigation).** Of tickets holding a parent immediately before the run: **every one of the 63 lost parents is a `story` (62) or `bug` (1) - not one `epic`**; 600+ epic-parented children in the same pass were untouched. Story/bug-parented tickets that survived had **no Jira binding**, so the inbound differ never saw them. The rule is exact: `cleared <=> bound AND parent is not an epic`. No unexplained residual.

## Why it was never repaired

`8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955` - 61 of the 63 prior parents are **closed**, and `rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent` validation cascade. `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (a dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`) is still an **`idea`**, so no repair route exists today.

## Current state (measured 2026-08-04)

* **59 of 63 still parentless**; 4 restored ad hoc.
* The full child -> lost-parent map is recoverable from the event log and is posted as a
  comment on this ticket.
* The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow is currently `disabled_manually` (last run
  2026-08-04 16:05 UTC), so nothing is re-clearing anything right now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the recovered child -> lost-parent map is verified against the event log
- [ ] a supported write path exists for re-parenting onto a **closed** parent (depends on
      `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` / `8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955`)
- [ ] all 59 remaining edges are restored, or each exception is recorded with a reason
- [ ] a post-restore sweep confirms 0 tickets from the incident set remain parentless
- [ ] restoration is done with the reconciler's peer-evidence fix in force, and a
      subsequent reconcile pass is confirmed not to re-clear them
baseline.summary: Restore the 59 tickets still orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconciler parent-clear incident

## Context / Problem
Slice C1 (ticket 29a9-3cf7-3ded-42d8) recorded 11 below-seam ambient config/credential reads across the residual scattered readers (_logging, _opcert_signing, _operation_config, mirror_guard, review_bot/app, signing — 7 rows) AND the grounding subsystem (grounding/harness, grounding/oracle, grounding/resolve — 4 rows) as entries in `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS`. These grounding rows belong to no earlier slice, so this residual slice folds them in alongside the other scattered readers. RP-04 is not complete while these ambient reads sit below the approved composition/credential/backend seams enforced by `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`. Parent: 075b-1479-dcb7-40ab.

Affected files (relative to `src/rebar/`):
  - `src/rebar/_logging.py`
  - `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`
  - `src/rebar/_operation_config.py`
  - `src/rebar/mirror_guard.py`
  - `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`
  - `src/rebar/signing.py`
  - `src/rebar/grounding/harness.py` (L56: dynamic `os.environ.get`)
  - `src/rebar/grounding/oracle.py` (L170: `load_config()` below seam)
  - `src/rebar/grounding/resolve.py` (L62 import-time `REBAR_CTAGS_BIN` default capture; L543 `load_config()` below seam)

This slice drains the 11 residual/grounding rows (9 files). It does NOT assert whole-tree EMPTY: two `binding_lifecycle.py` rows (`RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` + its `_env_int`/`os.environ.get` parser) are OUTSIDE this slice's scope — they were MOVED into `binding_lifecycle.py` by RP-02 S2 and their cut-to-seam is the RP-04 S7.3.a retarget tracked by ticket `01d8-c18d-b229-419a` (best-kingly-monkey). The whole-tree list reaches EMPTY only once BOTH this slice and that retarget land; whichever lands last observes EMPTY.

## Outcome
Every below-seam read in the files above is either (a) CUT to compose through the approved seam that already assembles config — the operation snapshot (`rebar._operation_config.OperationSnapshot` / `compose_operation_snapshot`), a startup binding, or the provider-credential boundary — or (b) for a genuine subsystem kill-switch / test-only control that has no place in the operation snapshot, annotated in place with an inline `# read-via: <reason>` marker on the reading line — the same established mechanism used by `_store/hlc.py`, `llm/gate_context.py`, and `_commands/session_id.py` — so the read is owned and self-documenting rather than whitelisted. Either way their `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` entries are removed (no path remains as a `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` row). `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` reports zero findings for these paths with those entries gone and no path-glob exception. The subsystem's behavioral suites stay green; redacted operation-snapshot fingerprints / provider-neutral outcomes are unchanged except recorded, justified deltas.

## Plan
1. For each below-seam read in the listed files, classify as cut-to-seam or register-owned; for cut-to-seam, thread the value from the composition seam rather than reading ambient `os.environ`/`os.getenv`/`load_config` below it.
2. Remove the corresponding entries for these files from `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` in `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py`.
3. Run `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` and the subsystem behavioral suites (tests/unit signing/opcert/logging suites); keep green.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- Held-out test `tests/scripts/test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout.py` asserts `check_config_ownership.check(check_config_ownership.REPO_ROOT)` returns no finding string containing any of the 9 listed paths, AND that none of the 9 listed paths remain as `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` rows (per-path membership check). It does NOT assert the whole list is EMPTY — the 2 residual rows are `binding_lifecycle.py` (owned by S7.3.a / `01d8-c18d-b229-419a`), outside this slice. RED now (entries present + reads below seam).
- The subsystem behavioral suites (tests/unit signing/opcert/logging suites + the grounding suites) stay green after the cutover — they are the correctness oracle the AST gate supplements.
- Redacted operation-snapshot fingerprints before/after are equal except recorded deltas.

## Compatibility / rollback
No stored ticket/event/binding format changes. A legacy facade is removed only after its focused suite passes; until then rollback selects the facade.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No direct ambient config/credential read, backend reload, or configurable default remains below the approved seam in the 9 listed files; each is either cut-to-seam or annotated in place with an inline `# read-via: <reason>` marker (kill-switch / test-only control), and no path remains as a `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` row.
- [x] The `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` entries for these 9 files are removed from `scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py` (the only residual rows are the 2 `binding_lifecycle.py` entries owned by S7.3.a / `01d8-c18d-b229-419a`), and `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` passes with no path-glob exception (proven by the held-out `test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout.py`).
- [x] The subsystem behavioral suites (tests/unit signing/opcert/logging + grounding suites) pass after the cutover; redacted operation-snapshot fingerprints / provider-neutral outcomes are unchanged except recorded approved deltas.

Live capture (2026-08-06, closing c827-2a23-cd00-473e from the loop-breaker checkout, main at 9a27202837): the primary completion-verifier run looped and was correctly aborted by the c827 actuator (requests=119, distinct_ratio_window=0.5). Bounded recovery started, but the evidence agent for ONE criterion hit its own step budget with a perfectly HEALTHY profile — 'completion-verifier-evidence ... hit step budget (request_limit=20 max_iterations=40) requests=20 tool_calls=35 distinct=35 max_consecutive_repeat=1 distinct_ratio_window=1.0 top_repeats=[]' — and that single LLMBudgetExhaustedError propagated out of the per-criterion loop in CompletionAgentStep._recover (completion_recovery.py ~:519-536), discarding all evidence already gathered and failing the whole recovery. The gate then reported 'bounded evidence recovery also failed' and offered --force-close: the exact exhaustion-is-not-a-verdict trap this cluster removes, one layer down.

The defect: the per-criterion evidence loop treats a single criterion's budget exhaustion as fatal to the aggregate, when the bound is a per-criterion safeguard. Partial evidence must be preserved rather than discarded — the finalizer already renders per-criterion verdicts and can mark a criterion unverifiable-within-bounds.

Plan: catch LLMBudgetExhaustedError, RunawayToolLoopError, and token-exhaustion UnretryableOutputError (guarded by _is_token_exhaustion, mirroring run()) around the per-criterion runner.run in _recover; substitute a content-free placeholder evidence entry that names the failure class and its usage counters (from the exception diagnostic), mark the entry exhausted=true; continue with remaining criteria; recovery fails outright only if EVERY criterion's evidence run fails. Placeholder text must never be presentable as affirmative evidence — it must state that evidence could not be gathered within recovery bounds so the finalizer scores the criterion unmet/indeterminate, not met. Aggregate char bound and finalizer input bound stay as-is. CompletionRecoveryError raised only when zero criteria produced evidence, carrying counts {criteria_total, criteria_exhausted}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A single criterion's LLMBudgetExhaustedError no longer aborts recovery: with N criteria and one evidence run exhausting, the finalizer still runs and receives N evidence entries, the exhausted one carrying an explicit could-not-gather-within-bounds placeholder (unit test, held-out oracle style).
- [x] A RunawayToolLoopError raised by an evidence run is handled the same way (unit test).
- [x] A token-exhaustion UnretryableOutputError from an evidence run is converted to the exhausted placeholder, mirroring the primary path; a NON-token UnretryableOutputError still propagates (unit test).
- [x] The placeholder is content-free (no exception prose interpolated beyond the failure class name and numeric usage counters) and can never read as affirmative evidence (unit test asserts wording).
- [x] If EVERY criterion's evidence run fails, recovery raises CompletionRecoveryError with diagnostic {criteria_total, criteria_exhausted} (unit test).
- [x] Successful-evidence behaviour is byte-identical: runs where no evidence agent fails produce the same finalizer input as before (unit test).
- [x] Live Bedrock proof before ship: a real gate-style recovery over multiple criteria where at least one evidence run exhausts completes with a verdict instead of failing whole (session experiment, not in unit suite).
- [x] make lint and mypy clean; full CI marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing
Held-out unit oracle in tests/unit/workflow/ (written before the fix, RED first): `python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ -q`. Mutation checks on the fix. Live Bedrock experiment (session artifact, not in unit suite) proving a multi-criterion recovery with one exhausted evidence run still reaches a verdict. `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; full marker suite matches pre-existing baseline.
baseline.summary: Bounded recovery dies whole when one criterion's evidence run exhausts its budget

## Problem

The provider-parity corpus includes the `code-review-verify` spec, whose output carries NO decision polarity, so the two-bucket parity mapping cannot score it. Every verify case is therefore scored `advisory` regardless of its gold label, which makes the gold-block case `V-real-defect` a GUARANTEED recall miss on BOTH arms.

Confirmed empirically in the committed artifact `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`: `V-real-defect` has `label: "block"` with `v1.decision == v2.decision == "advisory"`, `valid: true`, `errored: false`, on BOTH the standard and frontier slots. Both verify cases sit inside the scored gold set (30 records, `n_gold` 28; the two excluded are the `G3-*` container fixtures).

Mechanism: `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` (imported by `provider_parity.py:52` so the two cannot drift) keys only on `verdict == "FAIL"` or a non-empty `findings`. The verifier emits neither — its output vocabulary is `{verifications: [...]}` — so it falls through to `advisory`.

## Why the obvious fix is WRONG

"Treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block`" looks right and is not. `code-review-verify.eval.yaml` states the contract twice:
  - header: "Per the T8-advisory contract it is scored on PRESENCE of verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK
    verdict ... either way the verifier must emit a graded answer set."
  - dataset: "the gating scorer is presence-based, so the verifier must emit verifications for both."
BOTH cases — `V-real-defect` (gold block) and `V-clean-rename` (gold advisory) — are REQUIRED to emit a non-empty list. Mapping presence to `block` would fix the recall miss and simultaneously score the clean case as a block, manufacturing a FALSE ACCEPT. The arm has no polarity to read; no adapter can invent one.

## Approach

EXCLUDE `code-review-verify` from the parity corpus, for a reason DISTINCT from the existing `AGENTIC_SOLVERS` exclusion (that one excludes agentic ops; this one excludes a polarity-free scorer). Keep the two reasons separately named so a future reader does not collapse them.

## Impact on the recorded run

Excluding both verify cases takes `n_gold` 28 -> 26, still above `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20`. It removes one guaranteed miss from each arm, so recall rises on both. The miss was SYMMETRIC, so no gating verdict flips — the v2-vs-v1 noninferiority comparison is unaffected and false-accept is untouched (the affected case is a gold-block case, not a safe one). This corrects measurement ACCURACY, not a pass/fail outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `code-review-verify` is excluded from the parity corpus by a named, separate mechanism from
      `AGENTIC_SOLVERS`, with the reason (no decision polarity) stated at the definition.
- [x] A test asserts NO case from a polarity-free spec is eligible, and that the exclusion reason is
      distinct from the agentic exclusion — i.e. removing the agentic set does not silently cover this.
- [x] A test pins the SPECIFIC failure this fixes: a `{verifications: [...]}` output does NOT map to
      `block`, AND a gold-block verify case is no longer scored as a live miss because it is excluded
      rather than mis-scored. It must fail before the fix.
- [x] The recorded artifact is RE-SCORED OFFLINE with zero model calls; the new `n_gold` and recall are
      recorded, and it is stated explicitly whether any GATING verdict changed (expected: none).
- [x] The gold floor still holds after exclusion (`n_gold >= MIN_GOLD_ITEMS`), asserted by a test so a
      future corpus shrink cannot silently drop below it.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, the default selection is green, and the
      config-read and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: Parity corpus scores the polarity-free code-review-verify arm, guaranteeing a recall miss

## Context
Research on lead-unpleasing-kitten (7da8-9d47-9604-4257) measured 57.707s (68.4%) savings across three matched immutable-fixture scan-reuse cohorts (Python-oracle x5, mixed coverage x5, Engine-B JS x3), but the operator ratified (2026-08-22) implementing ONLY call-local validation dedup (landed as Gerrit change 2130 / commit 8481a057b696). Cross-worker scan-result reuse was explicitly deferred to this ticket as an unresolved DESIGN QUESTION, not an implementation task.

## The caching-boundary design question
- pytest-xdist fixtures are worker-local under `-n 3 --dist worksteal`; ordinary module/session fixture scope CANNOT share an expensive scan result across workers. Realizing the measured savings requires one of: consolidating assertions into fewer nodes (moves coverage location), an explicit cross-process immutable artifact/cache, or a distribution change.
- STALE-RESULT RISK: any cache keyed on a fixture tree must prove the tree is immutable for the cache lifetime. If the tree (or detector registry, or tool version) changes mid-run, a reused result silently tests the wrong state. A sound design needs a content-addressed key (tree hash + detector-source hash + binary version) or a guaranteed-immutable fixture contract, plus invalidation semantics.
- Contractual constraints from shockproof-twill-porpoise (tool presence/absence + explicit coverage accounting) and crushable-choosable-llama (real scanner/process integration retained): at least one real invocation per external boundary and environment state must survive any reuse design.
- Residual gaps recorded on the parent: no direct exact-defect tests yet for malformed OpenGrep SARIF / ast-grep JSON / metric JSON; broad invocation removal must not be approved until those are pinned.

## Acceptance criteria (for whoever picks this up)
- [ ] A written design choosing and justifying a caching boundary (node consolidation vs cross-process artifact cache vs distribution change), with an explicit staleness/invalidation story.
- [ ] The design preserves every unique real analyzer boundary and both tool-present/tool-absent states per the parent's fault/equivalence matrix.
- [ ] Operator approval before any test-boundary or coverage-location change.
baseline.summary: Design caching boundary for cross-worker grounding scan-result reuse

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` is at **800 lines against the hard 800-line cap** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which the CI module-size gate enforces with no allowlist. It is one line from red: the next change to any public library write verb fails the build. The sibling story adding two optional `create_ticket` arguments must widen two `@overload` signatures, the implementation, and their docstrings — it cannot land until this is relieved. This ticket buys that headroom by concern, not by line count.

## Approach

`_lib_writes` is the **aggregation point for every public library write**, so it grows on two axes: a new verb appends a wrapper, and an existing verb gaining an argument widens one in place. The facade split (S3/4532) cut the library **by direction** — writes vs reads vs gates vs ops — and that axis is exhausted: the write half alone carries seven concerns. The durable fix is to cut it **by concern**, per the `fsck` split (`defaceable-icy-antelope`), which took two cuts out of one 800-line file.

The seven concerns present today:

1. **Genesis** — `init_repo`, `create_ticket` (two `@overload`s + impl), `idea`.
2. **Identity & key material** — `create_identity`, `ensure_identity_for`, `create_placeholder`,
   `add_identity_key`, `revoke_identity_key`, `use_identity`, `resolve_current_identity`; all
   delegate to `rebar._commands.identity`, none touches ticket state.
3. **Status lifecycle** — `transition`, `claim`, `reopen`. The only place in the module that
   raises `ConcurrencyError`.
4. **Leaf mutations** — `_python_leaf` and its seven in-module callers `comment`, `edit_ticket`,
   `link`, `unlink`, `tag`, `untag`, `archive`.
5. **Session logs** — `append_session_log`, `start_session_log`; own `CommandError` mapping,
   NOT routed through `_python_leaf`.
6. **Store maintenance** — `compact`, `attach_commits`.
7. **Signing** — `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`, delegating to `rebar.signing`.

**Two cuts**, mirroring `fsck`:

- **`_lib_mutations.py`** takes 4+5+6. Anchored on the `_python_leaf` call graph: one adapter,
  seven callers, all inside the block, nothing else in this module calling it. Stated honestly,
  5 and 6 **ride along** as the contiguous remainder of the post-genesis mutation surface, not
  because they call `_python_leaf`; the strict call-graph subset is ~130 lines and
  non-contiguous, forcing a scattered cut near the 100-line floor.
- **`_lib_identity.py`** takes 2+7 — the non-ticket, key-material surface. Identities own
  OpenSSH key lines, `use_identity`/`resolve_current_identity` select the current one, and
  signing binds a manifest to the environment key. Stated honestly, signing is ~52 lines and
  **cannot stand alone** under the 100-line floor; identity is the nearest concern by shape,
  and the module already banners signing apart from the write path.
- **`_lib_writes.py` keeps 1+3** — genesis and the status state machine.

The plan of record extracted only 4+5+6 and left `_lib_writes` at ~544 — sound at 778, but at 800 that lands **above** the 200-500 target band on a file that grew 22 lines in weeks. Hence two cuts.

Moved names are **re-exported** from `_lib_writes` with `# noqa: F401`, exactly as `fsck.py` re-exports from `fsck_scan`/`fsck_tracker_health`. That leaves `__init__.py` and `_lib_gates.py` **untouched**, so every `rebar.<name>` and `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` path survives — a smaller diff than re-pointing consumers.

**The pre-move surface, reconciled.** `_lib_writes` has 29 `def` statements = **27 distinct names** plus the two extra `@overload` stubs of `create_ticket`. `__init__.py` re-exports **all 27**, so the facade surface and the definition set coincide — no name defined here is omitted from the facade. `_python_leaf` is one of the 27: it resolves as **`rebar._python_leaf`** (its own `_python_leaf as _python_leaf` alias in `__init__.py`) *and* as `rebar._lib_writes._python_leaf`, the form `_lib_gates.py` imports. The 27 partition across the concerns above as 3 + 7 + 3 + 8 (leaf mutations, counting `_python_leaf`) + 2 + 2 + 2. Dependency direction is one-way — `_lib_writes` imports both new modules, neither imports back — so there is no cycle.

This is **behaviour-preserving**: bodies relocate byte-identically; no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` (new) — concerns 4+5+6
- `src/rebar/_lib_identity.py` (new) — concerns 2+7
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — keeps 1+3, gains the two re-export blocks

`__init__.py`, `_lib_gates.py`, and everything under `tests/` are deliberately **not** touched. The reference audit supports that: the only real-code importers of `_lib_writes` are `_lib_gates.py` (`_python_leaf`) and `__init__.py` (the 27-name re-export), and the string pass (`monkeypatch.setattr` / `getattr` / `importlib`) finds **zero** `_lib_writes` attribute references — every test patch targets the `rebar` facade or `rebar.signing`, both preserved.

`.github/complexity-baseline.json` holds **zero** entries for `_lib_writes.py`, so no moved symbol carries accepted debt and the `--lock` re-key hazard that cast `Verified -1` on the `fsck` change cannot arise. The baseline is therefore not in scope.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing with **no test file edited**. The specific risk is the **public API surface**, since all 27 names are re-exported as `rebar.<name>` and `_lib_gates` depends on `_python_leaf` at three call sites — a silently dropped re-export would still leave the suite green wherever the facade is imported lazily. Checked by name:

- every name previously importable as `rebar.<name>` still resolves after the move, asserted
  name by name against the pre-move list;
- `rebar._lib_writes.<name>` still resolves for all moved names, which is what makes
  `_lib_gates` and any `monkeypatch` target survive;
- the three modules import cleanly in **either** order, catching a cycle introduced by the
  re-export direction.

`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the size oracle and needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_lib_writes.py` is at or below 450 lines; checked by
      `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_writes.py)" -le 450 ]` exiting 0.
- [ ] `_lib_mutations.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py`.
- [ ] `_lib_identity.py` is between 100 and 500 lines inclusive; checked by an exit-code
      comparison on `wc -l < src/rebar/_lib_identity.py`.
- [ ] The repo's size oracle still passes; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve on the facade as `rebar.<name>` — 26 public wrappers plus
      `rebar._python_leaf`; checked by a script asserting `hasattr(rebar, n)` for every name in
      the pre-move list, exiting non-zero on the first miss.
- [ ] All 27 names still resolve as `rebar._lib_writes.<name>`, which is the form
      `_lib_gates.py` imports; checked by the same assert-and-exit script against
      `rebar._lib_writes`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/__init__.py` and `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` are unchanged; checked by
      `git diff --exit-code HEAD~1 -- src/rebar/__init__.py src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] No file under `tests/` is changed; checked by `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 -- tests/`
      producing empty output.
- [ ] The three modules import cleanly in any order; checked by two fresh interpreters, one
      importing `_lib_identity`, `_lib_mutations`, `_lib_writes` in that order and one in
      reverse, both exiting 0.
- [ ] `make lint` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` is green; checked by it exiting 0.
- [ ] The CI test selection passes; checked by
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` exiting 0.
- [ ] `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` reports no new entries; checked by running
      it with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=navapbc/rebar` and confirming exit 0.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the _python_leaf mutation block from _lib_writes.py into _lib_mutations.py

Discovered while landing e9d5-c850-d505-4a5a (Gerrit change 2436). CI's build-and-test / pytest job failed 3 consecutive times (all 3 python versions each time) on the exact same test:

tests/unit/test_audit_serve_heldout.py::test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket

Failure: RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests... raised despite the test carrying @pytest.mark.allow_network, which should make tests/conftest.py's autouse _network_guard fixture skip patching socket.socket.connect for this test.

Root-cause evidence gathered (not yet fully diagnosed):
- The test passes 100% reliably when run in isolation, or in small subsets,
  including with -n 4 --dist worksteal (5+ repeated local runs, 0 failures).
- The test only fails as part of a FULL-suite parallel run (pytest -m "not
  integration and not external and not repo_policy" -n 4 --dist worksteal
  against the whole tests/ tree) -- reproduced identically on 2 separate
  local full-suite runs, which is consistent with the CI failure signature.
- The same full-suite run also non-deterministically fails several OTHER,
  unrelated tests under load (test_atomic_completion_close.py,
  test_rebar_repo_isolation.py, test_tracker_footprint_cli.py) -- none of
  which share any code path with the audit-serve test or with e9d5's
  change, suggesting a general resource-contention/timing sensitivity
  across several tests when the full suite runs under xdist worksteal,
  not a defect specific to any one test or diff.
- This test spins up a REAL uvicorn server on a background thread and
  polls for readiness with a 10s deadline, then makes a REAL HTTP request
  to it -- exactly the kind of test that is sensitive to CPU/scheduler
  contention under a busy parallel test run.

Not fixed as part of e9d5 -- unrelated to that ticket's scope (typed reconciler payload contracts), and per this repo's flaky-test policy a flake must be root-caused rather than silently retried; this ticket is the tracking vehicle for that root-cause.

Suggested follow-up:
- Confirm whether this and/or the other tests observed failing under load
  are known-flaky (check CI history across other recent changes for the
  same signature).
- If confirmed timing-sensitive under contention, consider widening the
  10s startup deadline model, isolating this test from -n xdist parallel
  scheduling (xdist_group), or another fix appropriate to its actual root
  cause once diagnosed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Root cause identified for why test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket
  (and, if related, the other full-suite-only failures named above) fail
  under parallel/full-suite load but never in isolation.
- A fix applied (or a documented decision not to fix, e.g. an accepted
  ADR on test parallelism tradeoffs) and the affected test(s) demonstrated
  stable across N repeated full-suite CI runs.
baseline.summary: Flaky test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket under full-suite parallel load
