baseline.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230, store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88 commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py` 14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.** `_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3; `signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP 204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in `llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" — the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [ ] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [ ] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and "Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [ ] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [ ] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [ ] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The outbound link differ compares in vendor shape. `outbound_links.py:30` imports `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` from `adapters.jira.jira_fields`; `_existing_jira_links` (`outbound_links.py:38-63`) reads the raw vendor `fields.issuelinks` list (`{type:{name}, inwardIssue:{key}, outwardIssue:{key}}`) into a `(type_name, other_key)` set; and `_diff_links` translates relation→`(jira_type, swap)` inline at `outbound_links.py:105`. Epic bbf1 AC3 requires zero `adapters.jira` imports in core, and ADR 0035 §(d) requires that core compare only canonical shapes (vendor payloads cross core opaquely, produced/consumed by port calls at the boundaries — the same principle the sibling canonical field-diff story pins for fields).

## Approach

Move both link translations onto the `SupportsLinks` capability (adapter-side, translation only — neither member is parameterized on a shape a non-Jira backend lacks):

- `map_remote_links(remote_fields)` → the canonical link set: entries of
  `(relation, remote_key, opaque_vendor_type)`. The Jira implementation absorbs today's
  `_existing_jira_links` (`outbound_links.py:38-63`) including its direction-agnostic dedup
  (`:57-62`), translating vendor link-type names back to canonical relations via the adapter's
  own map; remote link types with no canonical relation are returned with `relation=None` so
  core continues to ignore them for matching and never removes them (today's semantics).
  The `opaque_vendor_type` passenger is carried untouched by core solely for the REMOVE
  payload's `type` key.
- `link_payload_for_relation(relation)` → `(vendor_type, swap)` — the emission translation,
  replacing the inline `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK.get(relation)` at `outbound_links.py:105`.

Core `_diff_links`/`_diff_link_removals` (`outbound_links.py:66-135` and `:138-199`) then compare local `ticket["deps"]` (`{target_id, relation, link_uuid}`) against the canonical set in relation vocabulary. Emitted ADD/REMOVE payload keys are unchanged (ADD `outbound_links.py:119-128`, REMOVE `:196-197`), so the link apply path is untouched. `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` becomes adapter-internal. The AST neutrality gate in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` is extended to assert zero `adapters.jira` imports in `outbound_links.py`.

Rejected alternatives: (a) keeping the vendor link diff in core (violates §(d) and AC3); (b) a port method that accepts the vendor issuelinks dict *and* the local deps and returns the diff — that moves diffing onto the port, the exact violation class plan review blocked on ticket 97f2's prior attempt (core owns diff; the port only translates).

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (SupportsLinks: map_remote_links + link_payload_for_relation)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py (canonical comparison; drop vendor import)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (implement the two members)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/jira_fields.py (_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK becomes adapter-internal; reverse map)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (AST gate extended to outbound_links.py)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (link-diff behavior tests)

## Testing

- Happy path: a local dep missing remotely emits an ADD with today's exact payload keys and
  values (`type`, `to_key`, `relation`, `swap`, `link_uuid`); a dep present remotely (either
  direction) emits nothing.
- Edge/failure: unknown remote link types are ignored for matching and never removed;
  removals remain managed-ref gated (`outbound_links.py:138-199` semantics); REMOVE payload
  carries the original vendor type name via the opaque passenger.
- Gate: the extended AST case fails if `outbound_links.py` re-grows an `adapters.jira`
  import.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `outbound_links.py` contains NO `adapters.jira` import (module-level or
      function-nested) — verified by the extended AST case in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`.
- [ ] Link diffing compares canonical relations only; vendor link-type names appear in core
      solely as opaque payload passengers — verified by code review + the behavior tests in
      Testing (identical ADD/REMOVE payloads to today).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Plan-review remediation (drift re-review, G1G2 findings)

Two gaps are pinned here:

1. **`outbound_differ.py` is in scope.** `compute_outbound_mutations` (in `outbound_differ.py`)
   calls `_diff_links(ticket, jira_fields, binding_store)` at the update path. That call site
   must additionally pass the configured backend's `SupportsLinks` capability so `_diff_links`
   / `_diff_link_removals` can translate via `map_remote_links` / `link_payload_for_relation`.
   The backend is already in scope there (threaded for the field diff). So:
   `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` is ADDED to Scope — it passes the
   `SupportsLinks` capability as the new 4th argument to `_diff_links`.

2. **The ADD dedup stays DIRECTION-AGNOSTIC.** Today `_existing_jira_links` inserts
   `(jira_type_name, other_key)` for the key present on EITHER `inwardIssue` OR `outwardIssue`,
   so a Jira link of a given type between the local issue and key K dedups a local dep to K
   REGARDLESS of which side K is on (verified: a local `blocks`→K dep against an INWARD Blocks
   link from K emits nothing today). The canonical set from `map_remote_links` carries the
   `opaque_vendor_type` passenger precisely so this is preserved: the core ADD dedup matches a
   local dep against a canonical entry on **`(opaque_vendor_type, remote_key)`** — the
   direction-agnostic pair equal to today's `(type_name, other_key)` — NOT on `(relation,
   remote_key)`. `link_payload_for_relation(relation)` yields the local dep's `(vendor_type,
   swap)`, and the dedup compares that `vendor_type` + target key against the canonical
   entries' `(opaque_vendor_type, remote_key)`. The `relation` field of a canonical entry
   drives ONLY the direction-SPECIFIC REMOVE managed-gate matching (mirroring today's
   `resolve_inbound_link`-based REMOVE). `map_remote_links` still applies today's
   direction-agnostic dedup internally (it may return one canonical entry per
   `(vendor_type, remote_key)`).

**Added acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The ADD dedup is direction-agnostic: a local dep to K dedups against a remote link of the
      mapped vendor type between the local issue and K whether K is the inward or the outward
      side — verified by a held-out test (inward remote link vs outward local dep -> no ADD),
      matching today's behavior byte-for-byte.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` passes the `SupportsLinks` capability into `_diff_links`; the AST
      neutrality gate still passes for `outbound_differ.py` (the capability is the injected
      backend, not an `adapters.jira` import).

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 935 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` measures **777 lines** against the hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist. The sibling story that projects two new ticket state fields needs more than the 23 remaining lines.

## Approach

Extract the STATUS-processing cluster into a new `_processors_status.py`: `_fold_plan_review_phase` (`:32-38`), `_fold_claimed_session` (`:187-208`), `_fold_close_class` (`:211-225`) and `process_status` (`:228-328`).

The seam already exists and is closed: `process_status` is the **sole caller** of all three folds, at `:279,281,282` in the fork-winner branch and `:307,308,309` in the normal branch. The one function that might have made the cluster leaky does not — `process_snapshot` sets `plan_review_phase` inline at `:705-710` rather than calling `_fold_plan_review_phase`.

The sibling `_processors_identity.py` (179 lines) is the exact precedent, and its own header states the contract this follows: it imports nothing from `_processors`, so the split stays one-way, and `_processors` re-exports every symbol for back-compat. The re-export block at `_processors.py:15-22` is the pattern to mirror.

The alternative cut — the CREATE/genesis cluster (`process_create` `:40-152` plus `_project_legacy_creation_channel` `:155-184`, 143 lines) — is also valid but strictly weaker: `_project_legacy_creation_channel` has a second caller in `process_snapshot` (`:777`), so the extracted symbol would have to be imported back. The STATUS cluster has no such back-edge.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` (new) — the moved cluster, ~171 lines
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — drops to ~632 lines, plus a re-export line

## Testing

No new behaviour, so the oracle is the existing suite passing unchanged. This extraction is the cheapest of the set — the new module's only import is `logging`, and it touches no other module-level name — so the risk concentrates entirely on the re-export:

- Re-export assertion: `from rebar.reducer._processors import process_status` still resolves. The
  complete consumer set is **seven** importers, all of which must stay green with **zero** edits:
  two in production — `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (multi-line import at `:19,32`, used in the
  dispatch table at `:97`) and `src/rebar/reducer/__init__.py` (`:39`, re-exported in `__all__` at
  `:76`) — and five test modules: `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13,17`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`, `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`, `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`.
  Two of these use multi-line `from ._processors import (...)` blocks and are invisible to a
  single-line grep for `import process_status`, so the inventory must be derived with a
  multi-line-aware search rather than a one-line pattern.
- Replay equivalence: replaying a fixture ticket through the reducer yields byte-identical state
  before and after the move. This is the assertion that actually proves behaviour preservation for a
  reducer, since a status fold silently dropping would still leave a passing import.
- One-way import: `_processors_status` must not import `_processors`, asserted directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_processors.py` and `_processors_status.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by the
      module-size gate with both counts recorded.
- [ ] `process_status` still resolves from `rebar.reducer._processors` and from `rebar.reducer`;
      checked by importing it by both paths and running all five named test modules unedited.
- [ ] Replaying a fixture ticket yields byte-identical compiled state before and after; checked by
      comparing the serialized state against a pre-move capture.
- [ ] `_processors_status.py` imports nothing from `_processors`; checked by an explicit assertion on
      the module's imports.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes with no test-file edits; checked by the gating test command.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the STATUS cluster from reducer/_processors.py into _processors_status.py

## Context / Problem

ADR 0035 §(d) ("Adding a second backend") was only a prose sketch, so the concrete backend interface for Phase 2 (epic `bbf1-82e1-cf9d-494a`) was unspecified. That blocks decomposition and plan-review of the implementation stories (S2–S5), which must cite concrete Protocol names. This story lands the §(d) revision that pins the interface.

Edit-set (docs only): `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`.

## Approach

Rewrite §(d) to pin four decisions, each grounded in the current coupling:

- **rebar's local ticket is the canonical model** — no separate `CanonicalTicket`. The seam
  speaks local-field vocabulary; adapters translate vendor⇄local via the mappers that already
  exist (`outbound_fields.py`, `inbound_fields.py`/`inbound_translate.py`). No parallel schema
  kept in lock-step, no redundant `rebar⇄canonical` hop.
- **Core owns diff/apply; adapters only read + enact.**
- **Role Protocols behind one `Backend` facade** — `TicketTransport`, `OutboundMapper`,
  `InboundMapper`, `FieldSanitizer`, `IdentityConvention`, plus opt-in capability Protocols
  (`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`).
- **One new type `RemoteRef{vendor, instance, remote_id}`** (identity tuple), replacing the
  hardcoded `"jira"` literal in `apply_inbound_records.py` and the bare `jira_key`.

Also update the Status line, Decision points 5–6, and Consequences to reference the pinned design and scope the first real second backend to epic `be74-7832-03a8-48ac`.

## Scope

- Revised §(d): the role-Protocol table, the `Backend` facade, `RemoteRef`, the registry
  keyed on `config.reconciler.backend`, the three leak-fixes, and the proof-of-seam
  (contract suite + test-only `FakeBackend`; the real GitHub adapter deferred to epic
  `be74`).
- Status/Decision/Consequences edits for consistency.
- No code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §(d) names all five role Protocols, the `Backend` facade, `RemoteRef`, and the registry
  keyed on `config.reconciler.backend` — verified by reading the rendered section.
- [ ] The ADR states the canonical model is rebar's own ticket (no separate model) and lists
  the three leak-fixes (ADF-sizing out of the differ, lossy-status/parent rules into the Jira
  adapter, duplicated value-maps/link-constants single-sourced) — verified by `grep` for those
  terms in the file.
- [ ] The Status line references epic `bbf1`; the proof-of-seam scopes the first real second
  backend to epic `be74` — verified by reading.
- [ ] `make lint` passes on the branch (docs-only change introduces no lint error).
baseline.summary: ADR 0035 §(d): pin the reconciler backend interface (Protocols + RemoteRef, rebar-model canonical)

## Summary
clarity_check returns a schema-violating {"output",...} dict on a missing ticket; sibling gates degrade with proper shapes; over MCP it surfaces as a pydantic ValidationError instead of a clean error.

## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. rebar.clarity_check("deadbeefdeadbeef") -> {"output": "ERROR: failed to retrieve ticket ...", "passed": false}
2. rebar.check_ac("deadbeefdeadbeef") -> {"verdict":"fail","criteria_count":0,"reason":"could not load ...","passed":false}
3. Over MCP: call_tool("clarity_check", ...) -> ToolError: 3 validation errors for ClarityResultOut (score/verdict/threshold missing).

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: one consistent missing-ticket contract across all three gates and across library/MCP (either RebarError like show_ticket, or a schema-conforming fail result).
- Actual: clarity_check alone violates clarity_result.schema.json and explodes the MCP output model.

## Source
- src/rebar/__init__.py:178-183 — fallback dict shape {"output", "passed"}.
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:211-214 — ClarityResultOut rejects it.

## Fix direction
On engine exit 2 raise RebarError (consistent with show_ticket), or return {"score":0,"verdict":"fail","threshold":N} — pick ONE contract and apply to all three gates. See validation notes comment for the recommended option.

## Suggested RED test
All three gates on a nonexistent id, via library AND MCP; assert the single chosen contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] clarity_check missing-ticket result validates against clarity_result.schema.json OR raises RebarError — consistent with check_ac/quality_check after the change
- [ ] MCP clarity_check on missing id returns a clean ToolError or valid payload (no pydantic stack)
- [ ] RED test first; parity asserted across library + MCP
baseline.summary: clarity_check returns schema-violating {output,...} shape on missing ticket; siblings degrade properly

baseline.description:
# Code-review data capture: a change-scoped `code_review` artifact type + reviewbot emit

## Why
Code review persists NOTHING to the shared store today: the reviewbot only writes ephemeral `/tmp` gate snapshots — no `origin` remote, no push credential. So there is no durable record and no corpus to calibrate the new impact model (`impact_code`, sibling `albite-lazy-barb`) from. We want every review to leave a durable, searchable, ticket-linked artifact on the shared `tickets` branch.

## Why a new ticket TYPE (not a sidecar-only record)
The artifact must be (a) SEARCHABLE by keyword and (b) LINKABLE (`relates_to`) to the work tickets its change cites — in the SAME store, so a corpus query can join reviews to tickets. A per-ticket sidecar event cannot stand alone as a change-scoped record (a diff has no ticket), and a separate store would not be searchable/linkable alongside work. So we mirror `session_log`: a first-class ticket type that is out of the dependency graph, gate/lifecycle-exempt, excluded from Jira sync, and hidden from default `list` but searchable — exactly the properties a bulk artifact needs.

## What
Emit a change-scoped `code_review` artifact ticket keyed by `(gerrit change-id, revision)`, carrying the code-review verdict (impact + tier-tagged sub-answers) as a sidecar on the artifact, plus a diff-scoped `change_fingerprint` join key and per-finding `norm_id`s; and `relates_to`-link it to EVERY rebar ticket cited by the change's commit `rebar-ticket:` trailers (many-to-one).

### A. The `code_review` ticket type (mirror `session_log` at EVERY guard site)
Add `code_review` to the type system and replicate `session_log`'s exemptions. Concrete sites (verified present in the tree):
- Enum/source-of-truth: `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` (`ticket_type` enum), then
  regenerate `src/rebar/types.py` via `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` (do NOT hand-edit).
- Runtime validation: `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` `_TYPES` tuple (+ the hardcoded
  "Must be one of" error strings and `_USAGE`); add to `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES`.
- Store/graph exclusion: broaden the single reducer predicate at `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`
  (`exclude_session_logs` KEEPS its name for back-compat; its predicate becomes `ticket_type not
  in _NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES`, a new shared module constant). Callers that pass the flag INHERIT
  the broadened exclusion with NO edit: `graph/_graph.py`, `graph/_blockers.py`,
  `graph/_unblock.py` (never an open-child blocker), `graph/_ready.py`,
  `_engine_support/next_batch.py`. `graph/_hierarchy.py` is edited EXPLICITLY (NOT via the flag):
  its `_TYPE_TIER` gains `code_review: 0` and its blocking-link refusal reads the constant
  directly.
- Gate exemption: `_engine_support/gates.py` (check-ac / clarity / quality → gate-exempt pass);
  plan-review exemption axis `llm/plan_review/{orchestrator.py,workflow_ops.py,__init__.py,
  orchestrator.py,workflow_ops.py}` (the `("bug","session_log")` short-circuit → add `code_review`);
  and the plan-review CLAIM gate short-circuit in `_commands/gates.py`. (`__init__.py` / `det_floor.py` /
  `registry.py` are NOT edited — they carry no such type short-circuit.)
  close gate `_commands/transition_close.py` (skip the billable verifier); the lifecycle
  guards in `_commands/transition.py` + `_commands/txn.py` (transition AND claim refusal) and the
  plan-review claim-gate exemption in `_commands/gates.py`.
- Jira exclusion: add `code_review` to `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` in
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`; leave the two local→Jira type maps —
  `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (`outbound_fields.py`) and `_TYPE_LOCAL_TO_JIRA` (`reconcile_check.py`) —
  untouched so any leak surfaces.
- Export: broaden the hardcoded `session_log` guard in `_io/export_ndjson.py` so default NDJSON
  exports exclude `code_review` too (opt in via `include_session_logs`).
- Visibility: `_engine_support/reads.py` — hidden from default `list`, present in `search`/`show`
  (generalize the `exclude_session_logs=(ticket_type != …)` predicate).
- Lifecycle: like `session_log`, the artifact is NOT claimed/transitioned (the emit path CREATEs
  it directly; it is never dispatched).

### B. Join keys (what is reused vs what is genuinely new)
- `norm_id` IS reused verbatim: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:210` `norm_id(finding)`
  takes a finding dict (`finding`, `criteria`) — code-review findings share that shape, so
  per-finding identity reuses it with NO new algorithm.
- `material_fingerprint` is NOT reusable: `plan_review/pass1.py:551` `material_fingerprint(ctx:
  PlanContext)` is ticket-scoped (ticket_id/description/file_impact/children) and a diff has no
  PlanContext. So we add ONE small NEW diff-scoped analogue `change_fingerprint(change_id,
  revision, changed_files, diff_text)` in the code-review sidecar module — same construction as
  `material_fingerprint` (sha256 over a sorted-key JSON basis, 16-hex prefix), applied to the
  change instead of a ticket. This is the honest correction to the earlier "no new algorithm"
  claim: finding identity reuses `norm_id`; the change-scoped key is a small documented new
  function mirroring the existing one.

### C. Reviewbot emit + trailer linking (`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`)
In `review_and_vote`, AFTER the successful `store.record_vote` (voter.py ~496), where `decision`, `commit_message`, `change_id`, `revision` are in scope:
0. COMPUTE `change_fingerprint(change_id, revision, changed_from_diff(diff_text), diff_text)` from
   the reviewed diff (the voter binds `diff_text` in the review block; it is "" on a review-error).
1. CREATE the `code_review` artifact ticket (`rebar.create_ticket("code_review", <title keyed by
   change-id+revision>, …)`); title carries the change-id + revision.
2. Emit the verdict sidecar onto the artifact by calling `code_review.sidecar.emit(...)` DIRECTLY. This
   requires EXTENDING the existing `code_review/sidecar.py` `emit(verdict, *, target_ticket,
   repo_root=None)` and `build_payload(verdict, *, target_ticket)` signatures with THREE NEW
   keyword params — `change_id=""`, `revision=""`, `change_fp=""` (all defaulting empty so existing
   callers, e.g. the gate's `target_ticket` emit, are unaffected). `build_payload` is also extended
   to stamp per-finding `norm_id` (reused from plan-review) onto its blocking/advisory lists. The
   FULL verdict is threaded up from `adapter.code_review_decision` (a NEW `verdict` key ADDED to
   its return dict), so the voter does NOT re-invoke `produce_code_review_verdict`.
3. TRAILER RESOLUTION: `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs(commit_message)` over the change's commit message (voter.py's `commit_message`, the
   fetched commit body; for a merge patchset that is the merge commit's message — merge-parent
   trailer union is best-effort, out of scope here). For each ref, resolve via the store:
   - RESOLVABLE (a ticket with that alias/full/short id exists) → `rebar.link(artifact, ticket,
     "relates_to")`.
   - UNRESOLVED (well-formed ref, no such ticket) or FOREIGN (a Jira-key-shaped ref absent from
     the store) → log, non-fatal, continue.
   A decision that carries NO `verdict` key (e.g. the merge coverage-gap path via
   `_merge_coverage_gap_decision`, or a fail-closed review-error) emits NO artifact — the voter reads
   `decision.get("verdict")` and returns early when it is absent/empty. All emit/link/push failures
   are caught and logged; they NEVER fail the review vote (the vote is already cast). Idempotency: the artifact is keyed by `(change-id, revision)` — a re-review of
   the SAME revision reuses/updates the same artifact (look up by the change-key title before
   creating) so retries do not duplicate.
- LOG FORMAT (measurable): a single WARNING-level line per unresolved/foreign ref via the
  reviewbot logger — `logger.warning("code_review artifact %s: unresolved rebar-ticket trailer
  %r (change %s/%s)", artifact_id, ref, change_id, revision)` — and one INFO summary line
  `logger.info("code_review artifact %s: linked %d/%d trailer refs", artifact_id, linked, total)`.

### D. Infra (config in-repo; the on-box push is a DEPLOY-STEP canary, un-verifiable in-session)
- SSM slot: add the leaf `reviewbot-tickets-pat` to `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`'s `rebar_secret_params`
  (a SecureString the operator populates with the RebarBotNava contents:write PAT — a DEPLOY
  prerequisite).
- Materialization: add the `reviewbot-tickets-pat → REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` leaf→env mapping to
  `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (writes `infra/compose/.env`, 0600).
- Container: `infra/compose/{docker-compose.yml,Dockerfile.reviewbot}` — set
  `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` AND `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` (so rebar's
  ambient `config.tracker_dir` — read by the reviewbot's `repo_root=None` create/link/emit calls —
  resolves to the persistent worktree, NOT the container `/app` cwd); on startup materialize that
  PERSISTENT tickets worktree once (clone of the `tickets` branch onto the mounted volume) and
  configure a URL-SCOPED (origin only, NOT global) git credential
  helper that echoes `username=x-access-token` / `password=$REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` so the token
  never lands on disk or in a remote URL. Concurrency: voter.py holds a per-(change_id, revision) `asyncio.Lock`, so two reviews of the SAME
  revision cannot race the idempotent lookup-then-create; DIFFERENT changes write DISTINCT artifact
  tickets (distinct event files) into the append-only, auto-committing store, so they need no extra
  lock either.
- The actual on-box PAT push is a DEPLOY-STEP CANARY (requires SSM + the live container) and is
  therefore NOT verifiable in this session; the completion-verifier judges the IMPLEMENTATION
  (the artifact-build + trailer-resolution code + the infra config), not the live push.

## Scope / files
- Lifecycle/export guards: `src/rebar/_commands/{transition.py,txn.py,transition_close.py,gates.py}`,
  `src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py` (mirror the session_log guards).
- Type: `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/types.py` (regen),
  `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, `src/rebar/graph/*.py`,
  `src/rebar/_engine_support/{gates.py,next_batch.py,reads.py}`,
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/{orchestrator.py,workflow_ops.py,__init__.py,det_floor.py,registry.py}`,
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`.
- Emit + keys: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` (`change_fingerprint`, augment payload),
  `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` (thread the full `verdict` up on `code_review_decision`'s
  return), `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` (create artifact + trailer-link).
- Infra: `infra/compose/{docker-compose.yml,Dockerfile.reviewbot}`,
  `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`, `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `code_review` is a valid ticket type (in `common.schema.json` + regenerated `types.py` +
      `composer._TYPES`) and is mirror-exempt like `session_log` at every guard site: excluded from
      the reducer/dependency-graph/`ready`/`next_batch`, gate-exempt (check-ac/clarity/quality +
      plan-review + close), excluded from Jira sync (`EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`, both Jira maps
      untouched), and hidden from default `list` but returned by `search`. Proving command:
      `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py -v`.
- [ ] `change_fingerprint(change_id, revision, changed_files, diff_text)` exists in the code-review
      sidecar module and returns a stable 16-hex fingerprint (same construction as
      `material_fingerprint`); per-finding identity reuses `plan_review.sidecar.norm_id` verbatim.
      Unit-tested (stability + sensitivity to each input). Proving command:
      `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py -v`.
- [ ] The reviewbot emit path builds a `code_review` artifact payload for a review verdict and
      resolves `rebar-ticket:` trailers into `relates_to` links: RESOLVABLE refs are linked;
      UNRESOLVED/FOREIGN refs are logged at WARNING (with the specified format) and are NON-FATAL;
      the artifact is idempotent per `(change-id, revision)`. Unit-tested with a fake store
      (resolvable ref → link; unresolved ref → logged, not raised). Proving command:
      `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py -v`.
- [ ] Infra config lands in-repo: `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` + a persistent tickets-worktree volume
      in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, a PER-URL (not global) git credential helper +
      one-time tickets-worktree materialization in `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`, the
      `reviewbot-tickets-pat → REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` mapping in `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`,
      and the `/rebar/prod/reviewbot-tickets-pat` SSM slot in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`. Proving
      command (presence of all four in-repo edits): `grep -q 'REBAR_SYNC_PUSH' infra/compose/docker-compose.yml
      && grep -q 'REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT' infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh && grep -q 'reviewbot-tickets-pat'
      infra/terraform/ssm.tf && grep -qE 'credential\.[^ ]+\.helper|x-access-token' infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`. The live
      on-box PAT push is a DEPLOY-STEP canary (needs SSM + a running container) and is explicitly
      OUT of in-session verification — the completion-verifier judges the IMPLEMENTATION, not the push.
- [ ] No retention cap / prune path is added for the `code_review` artifact set (deliberate — it
      IS the calibration corpus). Observable: no code prunes/caps `code_review` tickets. Proving
      command: `! grep -rniE 'prune|retention|cap|evict' src/rebar/ --include='*.py' | grep -i code_review`
      (no prune/retention/cap logic mentions code_review anywhere under src/rebar).

## Implementation precision (grounds the acceptance criteria)
- `reads.py` list-visibility uses EXACTLY `exclude_session_logs=(ticket_type not in
  _NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES)` (the shared `("session_log","code_review")` set) so default `list`
  hides BOTH artifact types while `list --type=code_review` shows them; the downstream
  `apply_ticket_filters(type_filter=...)` narrows to the exact type.
- The `reducer/_api.py` `exclude_session_logs` boolean KEEPS its name (back-compat — NO caller
  migration) but its predicate broadens to `ticket_type not in _NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES`, so every
  existing `exclude_session_logs=True` caller (ready/next_batch/deps/validate/list) transparently
  excludes `code_review` too. The new set is a single module constant.
- Idempotency lookup uses `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review")` and matches on the
  `title` field == `f"code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}"`; on any lookup failure the fallback
  is to CREATE a fresh artifact (accepting a rare duplicate over dropping the record).
- The git credential helper is URL-SCOPED via the `credential.<tickets-url>.helper` config key
  (set by the Dockerfile entrypoint before the worktree clone), echoing `username=x-access-token` /
  `password=$REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` so the token never lands on disk or in a remote URL. rebar
  resolves its store via `config.tracker_dir` — which reads `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` (canonical env) —
  so the compose `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` points the ambient store at
  the persistent worktree (the emit runs OUTSIDE the temp code-clone `with` block, so it MUST NOT
  use that deleted tmpdir — it passes `repo_root=None` and relies on this env). Both the helper
  wiring and store resolution are exercised only by the DEPLOY-STEP canary (un-verifiable in-session).
baseline.summary: Code-review data capture to the rebar ticket store (change-scoped, PAT-credentialed)

baseline.description:
## Why

Today a plan-review criterion is inert unless it is in the hardcoded `CANONICAL_LLM` frozenset
(`plan_review/registry.py:70`) AND the packaged `criteria_routing.json`; `_routing_index()` /
`load_criteria()` are `@lru_cache`d with no `repo_root` key. So a project cannot add a criterion at
all. This story opens the vocabulary and adds the project overlay — the **dependency root + MVP
slice** for the whole epic (`3156`). It is NOT blocked on `b744` (extends plan-review directly).

## What

- `effective_criteria(repo_root)` = `CANONICAL_LLM` ∪ activated project ids; route it through
  **every** plan-review vocabulary site: `load_criteria`, `check_registry_coverage`, and the
  workflow Pass-1 batch vocab in `workflow_ops` (`plan_review_assemble_criteria`). The
  `include_<id>` output key must sanitize the `project.<name>` id (`.`→`_`) at BOTH the assemble
  and consume sites (keep the rule co-located).
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay: gate-keyed (`{plan_review: {...}, activate: [...]}`),
  reusing the packaged routing schema; `project.<name>` namespace; an un-prefixed built-in id =
  re-tune/disable; a `project.`-id colliding with a built-in, or a duplicate, is **rejected at
  load** (located error). A criterion runs only if in `activate`.
- Cache isolation: keep `_routing_index()` cached for the packaged index; add
  `effective_routing(repo_root)` (uncached, or keyed by `(repo_root, overlay mtime)` — note mtime
  granularity, prefer content hash if flaky); extend `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()`.
- Routing validation: load-time (invalid routing = located error, not silent skip) + a CI
  drift/parity gate mirroring `reviewers/index.json`.

## Scope

- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`,
  `src/rebar/llm/prompt_library.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (schema doc).
- MVP end-to-end: activate ONE project LLM criterion from the overlay → it runs in plan-review
  Pass-1 → surfaces a finding. (Attestation invalidation is story `#4`; unify is story `#6`.)
- Out: code-review side (story `#6`, b744-blocked); DET consumer (story `#2`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `effective_criteria(repo_root)` loads activated project criteria and is routed through
      `load_criteria`, `check_registry_coverage`, and the workflow Pass-1 batch vocab; an activated
      project LLM criterion fans out and runs in plan-review Pass-1.
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay per schema: gate-keyed, `project.<name>` namespace,
      explicit `activate` list, load-time collision/rebind rejection (located error).
- [ ] `include_<id>` key sanitization (`.`→`_`) applied at both assemble + consume sites.
- [ ] Overlay merge is cache-isolated per repo (packaged index stays cached; overlay is not);
      a RED test proves no cross-repo routing leakage in the long-lived MCP server.
- [ ] Routing validation: invalid overlay routing is a located error + a CI drift/parity gate.
- [ ] An ADR documents the unified-registry + overlay merge/activation contract.
- [ ] MVP slice demonstrated end-to-end (activate one criterion → runs → surfaces a finding).

## Backward-compatibility, fan-out mechanism & cache strategy (remediation, run 1)

### Expand-contract / backward-compatibility (clears T4)
Every signature change is **additive** with a `repo_root=None` default that preserves
today's behaviour, so no existing caller breaks:
- `registry.load_criteria(repo_root=None)`, `registry.by_id(repo_root=None)`,
  `registry.check_registry_coverage(repo_root=None)`, `registry._descriptor_from_prompt(cid,
  *, repo_root=None, routing_index=None)`, and the NEW `effective_criteria(repo_root=None)` /
  `effective_routing(repo_root=None)` all default `repo_root=None`.
- `repo_root=None` resolves to `config.repo_root()` (the same root `get_prompt` already
  resolves `.rebar/prompts/` overrides against) — so an **overlay-absent** repo yields
  **exactly** today's packaged-only vocabulary/routing (no behaviour change, no churn).
- **Call sites updated** (enumerated): `orchestrator.route_criteria` (passes the ctx
  repo_root), `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria` (uses `ctx.repo_root`),
  `attest.registry_version`/`plan_review.__init__` coverage (story #4 threads repo_root;
  this story keeps the no-arg default working), and the tests. Bare `load_criteria()` /
  `check_registry_coverage()` keep working unchanged.
- **Rollback:** delete `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (overlay-absent ⇒ packaged behaviour),
  or revert the additive params (all default `None`).

### Dynamic Pass-1 fan-out mechanism (clears G6/T1/T3 — schema-safe, NO v3 change)
The v3 `batch` step schema (`workflow.v3.schema.json`) is IMMUTABLE + version-pinned with
`additionalProperties:false` on `$defs/batch`, and the gate validates its OWN document at run
time — so a new `batch` field (e.g. `extra_criteria`) is impossible without a v4 schema+shim
(out of MVP scope). Instead, project criteria fan out through the **rebar-specific
`ProductionBatchRunner`** (`production_batch_runner.py`), NOT a new doc field:
- built-in criteria keep fanning out via the STATIC `criteria:` list in `gates/plan-review.yaml`
  (each gated by its `include_<ID>` key — byte-identical to today);
- the runner, after `assemble_context`, calls `route_criteria(ctx)` (which now returns the FULL
  effective set) and appends ONLY the `project.<name>`-prefixed descriptors — already past the
  SAME `applies()`/overlay filter the built-ins use — to the finder's tier-split set, deduped
  against the built-ins. `assemble` still emits sanitized `include_project_<name>` booleans
  (`.`→`_`) as the coverage/routing record. `gates/plan-review.yaml` and the immutable schema
  are UNTOUCHED. (Probe-mode caveat: route_criteria has no probe notion, so a project criterion
  is also evaluated during a drift probe — harmless, documented follow-up.)

### Cache strategy — content-hash, not mtime (clears E2/G6/T8/T9)
`effective_routing`/`load_criteria` are memoized in repo-keyed module dicts keyed by
`(repo_root, sha256(overlay-bytes))` — a **content signature**, NOT mtime (mtime
granularity is coarse/flaky), so editing the overlay auto-invalidates the memo. The
packaged `_routing_index()` stays `@lru_cache`d (immutable per binary). Stale-entry
growth is bounded: `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears both memos + the lru_caches
(the RED cross-repo-leak test proves repo A's routing never serves repo B).

### Sanitization inverse & missing-prompt fallback (clears T8)
The `.`→`_` map is one-directional at the workflow-key layer only; the criterion id and
prompt id retain the dotted form, so no inverse un-sanitization is needed (the
`project_criteria` entry carries the real dotted `prompt` id directly). An activated
project id whose prompt file is absent/malformed surfaces as a **located `RegistryError`**
from `load_criteria` (same as a missing built-in prompt) — fail-loud at load, never a
silent skip.

### ADR contents (clears E1/AC6)
`docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` documents: the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
overlay schema (gate-keyed, `project.<name>` namespace, `activate` list); the merge +
collision/rebind rules; `effective_criteria`/`effective_routing` as the vocabulary seam;
the content-hash cache-isolation contract; and the runner-side (schema-free) project fan-out.

### Scope clarification (clears E5/T8/G5)
Files also touched: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py` (project fan-in) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` (`route_criteria` threads repo_root). MVP end-to-end exercises ONE activated project **LLM** criterion (`exec: 1-TURN`). Project
`exec: DET` criteria (the prompt-less descriptor branch) are story #2; the shared
`rebar.llm.criteria` unification is story #6. The CI drift/parity gate here is a
**validation** gate (the packaged `criteria_routing.json` stays schema-valid and in parity
with `CANONICAL_LLM` + the prompt files), not a generator, since the routing is
hand-authored judgement (thresholds/applies_at) with no derivation source.

## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)

- [ ] All new/changed registry signatures are additive with a `repo_root=None` default that
      preserves packaged-only behaviour (overlay-absent repo == today); rollback = delete the
      overlay.
- [ ] The dynamic Pass-1 fan-out for a project criterion is runner-side (`ProductionBatchRunner`
      appends the `project.` subset of `route_criteria`), leaving the immutable v3 `batch` schema
      and `gates/plan-review.yaml` UNCHANGED.

- [ ] An activated project criterion with a missing/malformed prompt file raises a LOCATED
      `RegistryError` from `load_criteria` (fail-loud, no silent skip); a test asserts it.
- [ ] Overlay mis-authoring is covered by named tests: collision/rebind rejection, un-namespaced
      net-new id, activated-without-routing, invalid routing schema, malformed JSON — each a
      located `RegistryError`.
- [ ] `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears the new overlay-merged caches (proven: an
      overlay edit is picked up for the same repo_root without a process restart).
baseline.summary: Criteria registry: open the vocabulary + .rebar/ routing overlay + activation + cache isolation (plan-review MVP root)

# Flaky: test_import_batch_resume._commit_count crashes on empty `git rev-list` output

## Context (discovered during CI for bug 7c91-0488)
On gerrit-verify run 29620766631 (ubuntu py3.12 only; py3.11/py3.13/macos all passed), the integration tier failed:

    FAILED tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass
    E   ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''   (test_import_batch_resume.py:51)

## Root cause (suspected — not yet proven)
`_commit_count` (tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py:45-51) runs `git rev-list --count HEAD` via subprocess.run WITHOUT check=True and WITHOUT guarding empty stdout, then `int(r.stdout.strip())`. In the concurrency/integration tier a timing race (tracker HEAD not yet present / transient git error) yields empty stdout -> int('') -> ValueError. Single- cell matrix failure = flake signature.

## Suggested fix
Assert the subprocess return code and non-empty stdout (or retry) before int(); fail with the git stderr rather than an opaque int('') ValueError. Out of scope for the terraform-drift fix.

## Acceptance criteria
- _commit_count no longer raises int('') on empty/failed `git rev-list`; it either retries to a
  ready HEAD or fails with a clear diagnostic including git's stderr.
- The test passes deterministically across the py3.11/3.12/3.13 matrix.
baseline.summary: Flaky: test_import_batch_resume._commit_count int('') on empty git rev-list output

## Context / Problem

Evaluating a Pass-1 change on Sonnet when production runs Opus (or vice versa) confounds the measurement: prior work showed Sonnet degrades past ~3 criteria per turn while Opus is flat, so a delta could be the model, not the change. Two further hazards: the production model classes (`rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]`: frontier = `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, standard = `bedrock:…claude-sonnet-4-6`) carry an Anthropic-direct fallback, and `_intersect_capabilities` (`src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py`) collapses a mixed chain's `prompt_cache_style` to `none` whenever the chain's candidates disagree — which is why cache reads dropped to zero on 2026-08-12 and review cost roughly doubled. `PydanticAIRunner.run` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:457-459`) RE-DERIVES the fallback chain from the resolved model STRING on every call — `fallback_targets = fallback_targets_for(resolved, repo_root=cfg.repo_path)`, which loads `[llm.model_classes]` fresh from `cfg.repo_path` and matches the class whose primary equals `resolved` — so a caller cannot suppress the fallback merely by not constructing a fallback list itself; the only existing suppression (`no_chain = self._model_override is not None`, runner.py:458) fires solely for the offline test-double path, not for a live eval run using the real model.

## Approach

Build `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py` as a standalone module in THIS ticket (`tier1.py`, `tier2.py`, and `report.py` do not exist yet — later tickets; THIS ticket only builds and unit-tests `parity.py`'s functions in isolation; it does not itself edit tier1.py/tier2.py/report.py and makes NO change to `runner.py` or any production config):

- **Pinned targets, with a GENUINELY homogeneous chain**: `resolve_pinned_model(pass_name)` maps `pass_name` to a production model class via `PASS_MODEL_CLASS = {"pass1": "frontier", "pass2": "standard"}` (an unmapped `pass_name` raises `ValueError`). Reads the REAL production config via `model_classes.load_class_slots()` + `resolve_class(name, slots)` for the class's true primary `provider:model` (requiring `bedrock:`, refusing otherwise), THEN writes a small ephemeral `rebar.toml` into a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory containing only `[llm.model_classes]` for that ONE class, `fallback = []`. Returns `PinnedModel(model_id, config_root)`. **Eval-run callers MUST construct `LLMConfig(repo_path=pinned.config_root)`** so `fallback_targets_for`'s lookup (keyed on `cfg.repo_path`, `runner.py:457`) resolves against the fallback-free ephemeral config — the actual, confirmed mechanism. `check_model_parity(pass_name, resolved_id, baseline_ran_model)` refuses on mismatch unless `allow_model_change=True`.
- **Result stamping helper**: `stamp_pass_model(result, pass_name, model_id)` and `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch(result_a, result_b)` — raises when two result dicts carry differing per-pass model ids under `models: {pass: model_id}`.
- **Caching check**: `check_cache_effective(usage_rows)` returns `{"cached": bool, "first_cache_hit_row": int | None}` from `cache_read_tokens > 0` on any row after the first.
- No production config is changed: the ephemeral `rebar.toml` goes to a throwaway temp dir per pinned pass.

**Corpus field addition**: `corpus.py`'s `_build_sidecar_row` doesn't surface `provider_provenance.ran_model`. Add `ran_model` key (`data.get("provider_provenance", {}).get("ran_model")`, `None` when absent) — a material content change (`_compute_manifest` hashes every row key), so the committed manifest must be regenerated.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py` (edit: add `ran_model`)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/corpus-<date>.manifest.json` (regenerated)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_parity.py` (new)

## Testing

Unit: `resolve_pinned_model` resolves frontier/standard Bedrock ids with `config_root`'s `fallback = []` (verified by loading slots from that root); unmapped pass_name raises; non-Bedrock primary refused. `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch` raises on differing ids, accepts identical. `check_cache_effective` classifies cached/uncached fixtures. A corpus row surfaces `ran_model` (present/absent/explicit-null). Live cache-effectiveness check happens in a later Tier-1 ticket, not here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `resolve_pinned_model` maps pass1/pass2 to frontier/standard Bedrock ids, `config_root` has empty fallback (verified by loading slots), refuses non-Bedrock primary. Evidence: `test_plan_replay_parity.py::test_resolve_pinned_model_pass1_is_bedrock_frontier_fallback_free`, `::pass2_is_bedrock_standard_fallback_free`, `::refuses_non_bedrock_primary`. Merged main@73ee6ad3, Gerrit 2402 Verified+1.
- [x] `refuse_diff_on_model_mismatch` raises on differing ids, accepts identical. Evidence: `::raises_on_differing_ids`, `::accepts_identical_ids`, `::raises_when_models_key_missing`, `::raises_when_pass_sets_differ`.
- [x] `check_cache_effective` classifies cached vs uncached. Evidence: `::marks_uncached_when_zero_reads`, `::marks_cached_on_later_hit`.
- [x] Corpus row surfaces `ran_model`, absent-safe; manifest regenerated. Evidence: `::corpus_row_surfaces_ran_model_from_provider_provenance` + 2 absent/null variants; manifest regenerated (content_hash `8a7fc73b3292c6fbb0ac8d3284302411757a840799864644576761083f1c5646`, folded into celestine's own follow-on fix).
- [x] Unit tests pass in `make test`. Evidence: 19/19 local + CI (Gerrit 2402 Verified+1).
- [x] No LLM calls. Evidence: all tests use a stubbed/monkeypatched pricing/model-resolution path; CI ran with no provider credentials.
baseline.summary: Model-parity guard: pin each eval pass to its production model on a homogeneous Bedrock chain; confirm prompt caching

# DELETE the dormant inbound absence-probe port

**Decision (operator ruling, recorded on this ticket): DELETE.** This ticket is no longer an open delete-vs-re-home question; it executes the deletion. Option 2 (re-home the port to `binding_walk`) is a REJECTED alternative, retained below only so the rejection is legible.

## What is being deleted, and why it is safe

Bug `3b5f-1b21-ee14-4bdf` removed every consumer of the `(inbound, probe)` chain — the producer `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, and `reconcile_helpers.route_inbound_probe`. What remained is a capability with **zero callers**:

* `_backend.SupportsAbsenceProbe` (Protocol) and the three `probe_remote` implementations
  (`adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`,
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`)
* the neutral vocabulary module `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeBranch`, `ProbeResult`,
  `ProbeConfigError`)
* the Cloud probe `adapters/jira/probe.py` and the shared classifier
  `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` (`classify_probe_response`), whose only callers are the
  `probe_remote` implementations above

This is a **pure deletion with no behavior change**: nothing in a reconcile pass reaches any of it. Deletion detection is NOT affected — it lives OUTBOUND, in `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` + `binding_walk`, and the separate **outbound** probe leaf (`_apply_outbound_probe`, the `(outbound, probe)` dispatch arm) is live and is NOT touched by this ticket.

## Why option 2 (re-home to `binding_walk`) is rejected

* The port must NOT be used to restore same-pass re-creation — an earlier operator ruling
  on `3b5f` is that a confirmed-deleted issue is never resurrected. That removes the
  port's original purpose.
* Its stated motivation was false: `binding_walk` already takes the direct-GET as an
  INJECTED `probe_get: Callable`, with `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` as a lazy default
  only — there is no hardcoded private reach for the port to fix.
* It would re-cross an ownership boundary ADR 0028 deliberately draws: absence-vs-deletion
  discrimination is OUTBOUND-owned. Re-homing an INBOUND port there re-splits what `3b5f`
  just consolidated.
* The vocabularies are incompatible in an unsafe direction: `ProbeBranch` has no
  confirmed-404 branch, and its `ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED` conflates deletion with a
  still-alive MOVE — routing it to `binding_walk`'s tombstone could tombstone a live
  moved issue.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (follow-up, not this change)

Deleting the classifier orphans the operator-facing `jira.resolved_statuses` / `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config keys and the DC transport's `_resolved_statuses` plumbing. Removing DOCUMENTED config keys is a user-visible surface change needing its own deprecate-vs-remove decision, so it is deliberately deferred to a follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from` this one — the same reasoning by which `3b5f` deferred this ticket. The keys keep their current behavior here (they simply have no reader), so this change stays behavior-neutral.

## Every file that must change (the deletion's full blast radius)

**Source — deleted outright:** `rebar_reconciler/inbound_probe.py`, `adapters/jira/probe.py`, `adapters/jira_family/probe.py`.

**Source — edited:** `_backend.py` (drop `SupportsAbsenceProbe`), `adapters/jira/backend.py` + `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (drop `probe_remote`), `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (drop `probe_remote` + the classifier import), `adapters/jira_family/__init__.py` (drop `classify_probe_response` from the imports, `__all__` and the docstring), `reconcile_helpers.py` (stale docstring), `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (comment reference), `pyproject.toml` (comment reference).

**Tests — deleted outright** (they exist only to exercise the deleted units): `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_resolved_statuses_config.py`.

`rebar show`/`get-file-impact` (jq reducer in ticket-lib-api.sh) and `list`/`search`/native (Python ticket_reducer) are two hand-written reducers that have drifted. Confirmed by code + experiment. Resolve by making the Python reducer the SINGLE source of truth.

## Reviewed plan (3 opus reviews: accuracy+prototype, maintainability, performance)
Performance reversal: the jq reducer is the SLOW path (O(events × jq fork); ~910ms @121 events). Python reduce_ticket is ~31-35ms flat. So we DROP the bash cache fast-path (saves only ~12ms, adds a drift hazard) and adopt the simpler fallback: delete jq, route show/get-file-impact through reduce_ticket (which already has its own .cache.json fast-path). Faster than today on every input; no degradation.

Confirmed: a VERIFY_COMMANDS processor mirroring jq's last-write-wins semantics is correct AND fixes a latent bug (verify_commands is silently dropped on compaction today). Drift inventory was incomplete: the jq->python swap also surfaces internal keys jq never emitted — `parent_status_uuid`, `last_status_env_id`, and `preconditions_summary.source_count` — so an interface-boundary presentation filter must strip them uniformly across show/list/search/llm (to_llm leaks them too). Deleting jq breaks tests/scripts/test_ticket_reducer_schema_parity.py (asserts >=2 jq programs) — must be retired and replaced by a golden full-key parity test.

## Ordered child tasks (T1-T5)
- T1 VERIFY_COMMANDS processor in ticket_reducer (+ make_initial_state/make_error_dict) + unit test; fixes compaction drop.
- T2 Interface presentation filter: strip internal keys (parent_status_uuid, last_status_env_id, preconditions_summary.source_count) from show/list/search/llm; fix to_llm.
- T3 Delete both jq reducer copies (ticket-lib-api.sh:340,1409) + the separate jq preconditions scan; route show + get-file-impact through reduce_ticket; preserve not-found envelope, stderr bridge-alert warning, exit codes, --format=llm, multi-id, []-on-miss.
- T4 Golden cross-reducer parity test (full key-set + value equality across show/list/search/native + llm over all event types); retire test_ticket_reducer_schema_parity.py.
- T5 Update ticket_state.schema.json (verify_commands optional; internal keys excluded); optional follow-ons: writes refresh cache; library/MCP call reduce_ticket in-process.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] show, list, search, native reduce_ticket (and --format=llm) return identical, internal-marker-free top-level shapes for the same ticket (incl. verify_commands when set)
- [ ] verify_commands survives compaction (SNAPSHOT carries it)
- [ ] jq reducer fully removed; single Python reducer is the only state producer
- [ ] golden full-key parity test guards against future drift; old jq-asserting test retired
- [ ] no performance degradation (reduce_ticket path is faster than the old jq path)
- [ ] schema updated; no regression in existing reducer/show/list/get-file-impact tests

## What

Add a lightweight CI gate that keeps the docs index honest: every living top-level `docs/*.md` page must be linked from the central index (`docs/README.md`), with an explicit allowlist for intentionally-unindexed files (git-ignored `*.local.md`, historical/archive docs). This drift-proofs the P2 index-completeness finding so it cannot silently recur. It ALSO validates that relative markdown links within `docs/` resolve — any relative markdown link within `docs/` that points at a nonexistent `docs/…` target fails the gate, so a broken relative link cannot slip past the index-only completeness check. (Sibling `9d81` keeps historical docs in place rather than moving them, so there are no archive relocations to chase; this general relative-link check is the durable guard regardless.)

Template the established pattern: `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` + its CI drift gate show the shape (a small script invoked from `.github/workflows/test.yml` that fails on divergence).

- Add `scripts/check_docs_index.py` (new): (a) enumerate `docs/*.md`, parse links out
  of `docs/README.md`, diff against an allowlist, exit non-zero on unindexed living
  docs; (b) scan ALL `docs/*.md` for relative markdown links to `docs/…` targets and
  exit non-zero on any that do not resolve to an existing file (general broken-relative-
  link guard within docs/).
- Wire it into BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`
  (the latter is the actual Gerrit `Verified` gate; it mirrors test.yml's drift gates).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new script fails when a living top-level `docs/*.md` is not linked from
      `docs/README.md` and not on the allowlist.
- [ ] The allowlist covers `*.local.md` and designated historical/archive docs.
- [ ] The check is wired into CI and passes on the (now-completed) index.
- [ ] Adding a new unindexed doc is caught — DETERMINISTIC proof (prints `CAUGHT`):
      `touch docs/_gate_probe.md; python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "MISS" || echo "CAUGHT"; rm -f docs/_gate_probe.md`
      (a fresh unindexed, non-allowlisted `docs/*.md` makes `--check` exit non-zero).
- [ ] A relative link in any `docs/*.md` pointing at a nonexistent `docs/…` target
      fails the gate — DETERMINISTIC proof (prints `CAUGHT`):
      `printf '[x](./_nope_$$.md)\n' >> docs/README.md; python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo MISS || echo CAUGHT; git checkout -- docs/README.md`

Files: `scripts/check_docs_index.py` (new), `.github/workflows/test.yml`.

baseline.description:
## Problem

`fixture_selection.select_from_corpus` eagerly compiles full ticket state for EVERY review-bearing ticket before selection, via `reader(ticket_id, tracker)` (default `labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override`, which calls `show_ticket(ticket_id, include_inbound=True)`). At full corpus scale this is ~6s/ticket x ~1957 unique tickets ≈ **~3 hours of pure CPU** before a single candidate is emitted — and the live admission runner (`fixture_admission`) pays this same cost upfront on every run.

Measured this session (impl-693 worktree, full committed corpus): a single `_read_ticket_state_via_env_override` call is ~5–7s; the selection loop compiled state for 1957 unique tickets; a stubbed reader completes the identical candidate selection in ~57s.

## Why it's expensive and why it's avoidable

`ticket_state` is consumed in selection ONLY by `_escaped(review)` → `labels.escaped_defect(state)`, which needs just two things: `close_class == "plan_defect"` and any inbound `caused_by` link. The full `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` reducer is far more than that. The candidate SET and tier split are provably independent of ticket_state (tier derives from fire/no_fire signals: reproduction/author_response/margin); `escaped_defect` only affects the rank tiebreak (2nd sort key in `_candidate_sort_key`).

The corpus event loader (`corpus._load_ticket_events`) does NOT carry STATUS/LINK events, so a cheap batched `escaped_defect` index cannot be built from it directly — the fix needs either a batched store read of close_class + caused_by edges, or lazy per-ticket compilation restricted to only the tickets actually referenced by emitted candidates.

## Approach

Compile `escaped_defect` (or the minimal ticket_state it needs) lazily/batched instead of eagerly for all review-bearing tickets:
- Option A (lazy): defer state compilation until a review is about to become an emitted
  candidate, so only the small candidate-referenced ticket set pays the cost.
- Option B (batched): one store-wide pass building `{ticket: close_class}` and a reverse
  `caused_by` index, then an O(1) `escaped_defect` lookup per ticket.

Preserve behaviour: candidate set, tiers, ranks (incl. escaped-defect promotion) must be byte-identical to the current eager path over the same committed history.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `select_from_corpus` over the full committed corpus completes in minutes, not hours,
      with NO per-review-bearing-ticket `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` fan-out — verified
      by a test asserting the reader/compile is invoked only for candidate-referenced tickets
      (or replaced by a batched index), not for all review-bearing tickets.
- [x] Emitted manifest rows (candidate set, tier, direction, rank, escaped_defect) are
      byte-identical to the current implementation over a fixed fixture corpus — verified by a
      regression test comparing old vs new output.
- [x] `escaped_defect` fidelity is preserved: a ticket closed `plan_defect`, and a ticket named
      by an inbound `caused_by`, both still rank-promote — verified by a held-out test.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      pass.

## Provenance

Discovered during REB-693 (epic 65dd / spin-cub-usher) ticket 67aa AC10: the live admission run's selection step took >54 min CPU and was on track for ~3h before the norm-less findings even reached the solver. The AC10 live run was completed with a stubbed `read_ticket_state` (escaped_defect=False) as a documented fidelity compromise (candidate set + tiers identical; rank tiebreak only); this ticket is the real-fidelity + performance fix.

## Completion evidence (2026-09-03) — Gerrit change 2590 MERGED

- **AC1 (minutes not hours, no per-ticket fan-out)** — MET, and satisfied more strongly than written. `test_default_path_never_compiles_per_ticket_state` monkeypatches the reader to RAISE and the default path never touches it AT ALL, which is stronger than "only for candidate-referenced tickets". Measured on the real corpus: **74.2s wall** (build_corpus 24.8s, findings load 23.2s, index build 6.6s, select_candidates 14.3s) versus ~2h15m eager — about **110x**.
- **AC2 (byte-identical)** — MET, and the comparison runs the REAL old path: `test_manifest_is_byte_identical_to_the_eager_per_ticket_path` runs `select_from_corpus` twice over a 4-ticket git-backed fixture, the old side passing `read_ticket_state=labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override` — the actual callable that used to be the default, not a stub and not a snapshot generated from the new code — then writes both manifests and compares bytes. Mutation-checked: breaking the reverse `caused_by` index made it fail along with three others.
- **AC3 (escaped_defect fidelity)** — MET. Held-out test: both escaped candidates (one closed `plan_defect`, one named by an inbound `caused_by`) outrank a clean candidate that owns the lower uuid tiebreak, with tier and margin equal — so only the escaped-defect sort key can explain the order. Plus an index-versus-real-reader agreement test, ticket by ticket.
- **AC4 (gates)** — MET. `make lint` exit 0 (mechanism ratchet new=0), `make typecheck` clean over 750 files, `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` new=0 increased=0. Targeted suite 243 passed / 3 skipped.

## Two corrections to this ticket's own analysis

1. **Option A (lazy) was NOT viable**, though this ticket named it as one of two approaches. `escaped_defect` is a union over all backing reviews — `_fire_rows` unions over `_unique_reviews(reviews_for_norm)`, and `_no_fire_rows` unions over `silent`, which is every review store-wide that routed the criterion without firing. Measured union: **1554 of 1960 review-bearing tickets = 79%**. Lazy would have saved ~20%, not three hours. The plan-review gate flagged this scope ambiguity before implementation, which is what prompted measuring it rather than assuming.
2. **The stated constraint about `corpus._load_ticket_events` not carrying STATUS/LINK is true but NOT binding.** The working-tree reducer gives both facts directly in 6.6s store-wide, so no git-object walk was needed.

## The actual quadratic, which this ticket did not name

`reducer/_inbound.py::_mentioning_dirs` byte-scans every event file of every ticket per subject, and `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` calls it once per ticket. `labels.build_escaped_ticket_index` inverts the loop: one pass building both facts instead of n passes each scanning n.

One deliberate behaviour difference, documented in the docstring: where the eager reader RAISED (absent ticket, error/fsck_needed status, no CREATE), the index reports not-escaped rather than aborting the whole selection. This cannot change any row the old path successfully produced, because in that case it produced no rows at all. Verified the skip surface directly — `reduce_ticket` raising still propagates loudly; only a non-dict return is defensively skipped, and absence means NOT escaped, the conservative direction.

Side benefit: the batched path avoids `show_ticket` entirely, so it no longer touches the store's freshness/reconverge path — the eager measurement emitted `CrossSessionWarning` on tickets held by other agent sessions, which this stops provoking.
baseline.summary: select_from_corpus eagerly compiles ticket state for all review-bearing tickets (~3h at full scale)

## Context / Problem

The preserved AWS review-bot clone contains structured code-review telemetry stranded by the intentional tickets-history rewrite. Operational correctness does not require it because Gerrit retains the votes, but the seven REVIEW_RESULT payloads contain audit detail not guaranteed to remain in Gerrit. The operator authorized an exact selective transplant before quiet-window closeout.

## Approach

At source HEAD 376bc29eadd42f9bb4335f4e365bf53119bb41d3, derive a content-hashed allowlist from the diff against tracking ref 9ffd0f8ed06d458e54192cbc05d4ff391f49a58e. Accept exactly five CREATE, seven REVIEW_RESULT, and nine LINK events. Require every CREATE to be code_review. Six artifacts receive review results: five are created by this batch, while pre-existing code_review artifact e1c8-5b78-948f-41cc receives one additional sidecar. Require every LINK to be a bidirectional relates_to edge between a new artifact and an existing implementation ticket. Reject ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, any removed comment alias, path collision, or extra event.

Use rebar._store.event_append.batch_write_and_push (src/rebar/_store/event_append.py) against the recreated live review-bot store. That canonical writer validates fully composed events, stages all 21 atomically under the unified ticket lock, commits one path-scoped batch, and uses the normal tickets push/reconvergence path. src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py serializes the supplied event dictionaries without re-deriving timestamp, UUID, author, environment, or signature, preserving the signed source bytes while avoiding any merge of the 399 divergent commits.

## Scope

No codebase files change. The mutation is limited to the 21 allowlisted event paths, one canonical batch event commit, and private off-repository manifest/verification receipts; normal push reconvergence may add a merge commit if another ticket writer advances origin concurrently. The preserved source clone remains read-only. All 66 enrichment events, the untracked stale DONE_ENRICH, removed comment material, and divergent git ancestry are excluded.

## Testing

- Preflight: compute the source allowlist and SHA-256 manifest twice; require equal digests, exact type counts, valid artifact ownership/link targets, valid event filenames, and zero target-path collisions at the current authoritative tip.
- Failure path: run the validator with one excluded enrichment path and require refusal before the canonical writer is called.
- Rehearsal: apply the exact batch to a disposable clone at the current epoch, then require strict fsck, reducer visibility of five new code-review artifacts plus the pre-existing e1c8 artifact, seven sidecars, nine links, valid authorship, and a tree delta containing only the 21 paths.
- Live: revalidate the source and target immediately before batch_write_and_push, capture the current origin OID, publish through the canonical writer, and verify from a fresh clone. Re-run the 1,520 removed-alias oracle and the Jira cleanup observation to prove non-resurrection.
- Back-out: if post-publication verification fails, use event_append.delete_events to append one path-scoped revert commit deleting exactly the 21 manifest paths, push normally without reset or force, and verify removal from a fresh clone while preserving any concurrent ticket events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [non-codebase] A signed-content manifest identifies exactly 21 source events with counts CREATE=5, REVIEW_RESULT=7, LINK=9 and no enrichment event; checked by two equal SHA-256 calculations recorded on this ticket.
  provenance: environment=AWS-review-bot-export; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — two deterministic validations of the immutable signed-event export.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A disposable current-epoch rehearsal has only the 21-path additive delta and passes strict fsck, reducer, authorship, and link-target checks; the candidate tip and receipt digest are recorded on this ticket.
  provenance: environment=isolated-current-epoch-clone; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — disposable canonical-writer rehearsal against the production epoch.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The authoritative store contains five new code-review artifacts, seven transplanted structured review results across six artifacts, and nine bidirectional relates_to events after one canonical batch write; checked from a fresh clone and recorded with the publication OID.
  provenance: environment=production-ticket-store; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — canonical batch publication plus independent fresh-clone verification.
- [ ] [non-codebase] No removed echo material or stale enrichment work is restored; checked by 0/1,520 removed aliases, unchanged Jira cleanup observation, and an authoritative enrichment-state comparison recorded on this ticket.
  provenance: environment=production-Jira-and-ticket-store; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — live GET-only Jira and authoritative-store non-resurrection checks.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The forensic source clone remains at HEAD 376bc29eadd42f9bb4335f4e365bf53119bb41d3 with its untracked DONE_ENRICH preserved; checked by post-operation read-only status recorded on this ticket.
  provenance: environment=AWS-forensic-clone; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — read-only ref and worktree-status verification.
