## Report — NOT independently reproduced yet, read the caveat
An agent landing Gerrit 1943 reported that running pytest **detached via `nohup`** produced errors that **did not reproduce in a foreground shell**:

- two bpmn-io browser e2e tests, and
- `test_partial_clone_refusal_names_fresh_unfiltered_clone_remedy`

all errored under the detached run, then **passed on a foreground re-run** (12 passed / 6 passed). It recorded that it "nearly chased those as real regressions."

**I have not reproduced this myself.** This ticket is filed to establish whether the effect is real and what causes it — not to assert a defect. Investigation should start by reproducing the foreground/detached difference on an unmodified tree before touching anything.

## Why it is worth establishing rather than shrugging off
Agents in this project routinely run the full suite detached, because a serial local run takes hours and exceeds tool timeouts. If a detached run reports errors a foreground run does not, then the cheap validation path produces false positives, and the expensive path is the only trustworthy one. Two costs follow:

1. **Wasted investigation.** At least one agent nearly root-caused phantom regressions. Time spent
   chasing an artifact is time not spent on the actual change.
2. **Erosion of the signal.** The dangerous direction is the inverse of (1): once "errors in the
   detached run are probably spurious" becomes folklore, a REAL regression in a detached run gets
   waved through with the same shrug. That is the same failure mode the withdrawn ticket
   `bitesized-fluorite-aruanas` warned about for `tests/interfaces` — dismissing a class of failure
   by reputation rather than by diagnosis.

## Distinguish this from a KNOWN and different artifact
Several agents this session reported errors in long background runs that were **self-inflicted and fully explained**: the run raced the agent's own `git commit` / `git reset --hard` / branch switch in the same worktree, and repo-hygiene guards fired with messages naming the exact HEAD move (e.g. "Test moved the repo HEAD (a9cbc2d34e -> 74daf58e52)"). Those are not this. They are correct guards catching a genuinely mutating tree.

The report here is different in kind: no HEAD move was implicated, and the same commit passed foreground. Investigation must not conflate the two — establishing which of the reported errors belong to which class is itself part of the work.

## Candidate mechanisms to discriminate between
- Process-group / TTY differences under `nohup` (browser e2e tests in particular may need a session
  or display that a detached process lacks).
- Working-directory or environment differences between the detached process and the foreground shell.
- Resource contention: a detached full-tree run may overlap other work in a way a foreground run does
  not, hitting timeouts that read as errors.
- Harness reaping: a detached runner being partially killed and its teardown reported as errors.

The bpmn-io **browser** e2e tests are the strongest lead — a browser harness is exactly the kind of thing that behaves differently without a controlling terminal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The foreground/detached difference is either REPRODUCED on an unmodified tree, or shown not to
      reproduce — with the exact invocations for both runs recorded so a later reader can repeat them.
- [x] If it reproduces, each affected test is classified: genuinely environment-dependent (and why),
      versus a real defect the detached run exposes. Do not stop at "spurious."
- [x] The reported errors are separated from the KNOWN self-inflicted HEAD-move class, so the two are
      not conflated in whatever guidance results.
- [x] Whatever the outcome, the recommended way for an agent to validate the whole tree locally is
      recorded in `docs/local-dev-env.md` — including whether detached runs are trustworthy, and if
      not, what to do instead given a serial run exceeds tool timeouts.
- [x] No detachment-keyed skip is introduced. **Investigation result (2026-08-20): the original
      premise of this criterion is DISPROVEN.** No test here is unable to run detached — 15 detached
      runs at load average 9-13, with `stdin=/dev/null` and no controlling terminal, were entirely
      clean, including `pytest tests/e2e` reporting the same `12 passed` the report cites. The
      failures are caused by a **concurrent external actor mutating the shared checkout** while the
      suite runs (proven deterministically), not by detachment; detachment is only the mode in which
      such an actor can exist, because a foreground run blocks the agent that would otherwise be
      mutating the checkout. A skip keyed on detachment would therefore suppress a real signal for a
      cause that does not exist — precisely the "erosion of the signal" this ticket was filed to
      prevent. This criterion is met by NOT adding such a skip, and by the diagnostics instead being
      made honest about the external-actor cause (see the two criteria below).
- [x] `tests/conftest.py`'s REPO_ROOT leak-guard message no longer asserts that a test leaked an
      entry it may not have created; it names the concurrent-external-process possibility. Additive
      to the message only — no detection is weakened, and the deletion behaviour is deliberately NOT
      touched here (it is owned by `746c-185a-0e48-4b83`, `carryable-basalt-beagle`).
- [x] The `tests/e2e` browser-probe failure diagnostic reports the child's `returncode`, so a
      signal-killed child (a reaped detached run) is distinguishable at a glance from a genuine
      product failure. Additive; changes no pass/fail outcome.

## Provenance
Reported 2026-08-20 by the agent on ticket `visionary-pernicious-ynambu` (Gerrit 1943, merged), which recorded it as a method note rather than absorbing it. Filed here so it is investigated rather than becoming folklore.
baseline.summary: Detached (nohup) pytest runs report errors that do not reproduce in a foreground shell

`docs/exit-codes.md` declares itself "the single source of truth" (`:5`) covering "each public dispatcher arm" (`:69`). It has 41 table rows against 75 real commands — independently re-derived from `_cli/_help.known_subcommands()` union `_cli/__init__._INTERCEPTS`. The 34 omissions include `review-plan`, `review-code`, and `verify-completion`, whose exit-11 semantics the same document defines four lines into its own codes table.

Grounding found worse: codes **75** (`RebaseGuard`/`EXIT_RESCHEDULE`) and **78** (`StoreIncompatibleError`) reach the process exit status via `_seam.py:419` → `_commands/__init__.py:160` and appear nowhere in the document. 75 is the one code a CI workflow actually branches on. Codes 3, 4, 12 and `validate`'s 0-4 severity bucket are also undocumented.

The doc's own scope note is stale: it says only five commands validate unknown options, but `metrics`, `doctor`, `composer` and `fsck` all exit 2 on unknown options today.

A separate candidate finding — "define an exit-code vocabulary and standardise usage" — was run through the pipeline and FAILED both floors (impact 0.415). The one exit-code defect in this repo's history (`show`/`list` returning 1 instead of 2) was caught by writing the doc and a conformance test, not by constants. That is the mitigation already in place, and this ticket extends it rather than replacing it. Do not add a named exit-code enum.

Full generation was assessed and rejected: the command list is derivable, but per-command *semantics* have no machine-readable source, and exit 11 is produced at the CLI layer (`_cli/_llm_commands.py:129-171`), not in `_commands/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Rows exist for all 75 dispatcher arms
- [x] Codes 3, 4, 12, 75 and 78 are documented with their meanings
- [x] The stale "only five commands validate options" note is corrected
- [x] A CI check asserts every dispatcher arm has a row, so a new command without one fails
- [x] The document carries a forward-compatibility sentence: an unknown non-zero code MUST be treated as failure
baseline.summary: Make docs/exit-codes.md complete and keep it that way

## Why

The deterministic decision math (Pass-3) is the most divergence-dangerous part of the four-pass
framework: if two gates compute "what blocks" differently, the gate guarantee silently forks.
`pass3_decide` + `pass3_over_findings` already live in `plan_review/orchestrator.py`/`passes.py`
and are *already* shared across the (former) bespoke and workflow paths — this lifts them into a
named shared kernel module as the framework's single decision core, with per-criterion thresholds
parameterized so a consuming gate can set its own posture without forking the math.

## What

- Create the kernel package (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`) and move the deterministic
  Pass-3 core into it: `pass3_decide` (validity = graded fraction of the binary sub-answers;
  impact = mean of ordinal-mapped severity attributes; priority = validity×impact; the
  conditional cited-reference veto; block/advisory against per-criterion thresholds) +
  `pass3_over_findings`.
- Parameterize the per-criterion `block_threshold` / posture so consumers pass their own
  thresholds; keep plan-review's current defaults intact.
- Rewire the plan-review workflow's `plan_review_decide` op to call the kernel (no behavior
  change). Keep a thin re-export from `plan_review` if needed for back-compat.

## Scope

In scope: the Pass-3 decision function + math + the binary→validity / attrs→impact maps, moved to
the kernel; plan-review consumes it. Out of scope: Pass-2 verify (WS2), the coach (WS3), the seam
doc + evals (WS4), and threshold *calibration* (deferred). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`/`passes.py`, the new kernel module, and
`workflow_ops.py` (the decide op).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A kernel module exists and houses `pass3_decide` + `pass3_over_findings` + the
      validity/impact/veto math; per-criterion thresholds are a parameter, not hardcoded.
- [ ] The plan-review `plan_review_decide` op consumes the kernel; an offline test asserts the
      decided partition (blocking/advisory/dropped/indeterminate) is unchanged vs before.
- [ ] No second copy of the decision math remains; any `plan_review` references are thin
      re-exports, not duplicated logic.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: WS1: Extract Pass-3 deterministic decision into the shared review kernel

## Summary

`mutation_sandbox.wrap()` has TWO independent fail-open branches when no OS sandbox mechanism is available:

1. **ambient `CI` truthy** — proceeds UNSANDBOXED with a warning;
2. **`REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1`** — the explicit, documented opt-out.

The first is the problem. `CI` is inheritable and trivially set, so a workstation with `CI=1` exported — say, while debugging a CI script — silently runs mutation tests with no sandbox. That is the configuration the 2026-08-26 incident happened in, and nothing about it is a deliberate choice by the person running the command.

## Approach: remove the branch, do not add a knob

The fix is SUBTRACTIVE. Delete the `CI`-keyed branch, leaving the explicit opt-out as the single waiver surface. Adding a new config key — as this ticket originally proposed — would create two overlapping unsandboxed-waiver surfaces with divergent semantics, which is worse than the gap it closes.

After this, disabling the sandbox requires naming `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED`, which is deliberate, greppable, and already documented.

## The lane that relies on the CI branch today

`.github/workflows/_mutation.yml` runs the mutation gate on a plain `ubuntu-latest` runner. It installs bubblewrap, and its comment claims "Without it the gate fails CLOSED" — but those runners deny unprivileged `CLONE_NEWUSER`, so `probe()` returns `None` and **the gate currently runs UNSANDBOXED via the `CI` branch**. The protection that comment describes does not hold there.

That lane must therefore declare the waiver explicitly before the branch is removed, or it will start aborting. Making it genuinely sandboxed (as `0d22-f664` did for the enforcement lane) is the better end state and is tracked separately — this ticket must not silently convert a working lane into a failing one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `CI`-keyed fail-open branch is REMOVED from `wrap()`, together with its now
      sole-purpose helper `_ci_environment()` — leaving the helper would be dead code
      whose docstring argues FOR the behaviour just deleted. Ambient `CI` alone can no
      longer disable the sandbox. Verified by a test asserting that with `CI` truthy, no
      mechanism, and no opt-out, `wrap()` raises `SandboxUnavailable`.
- [x] The tests that asserted the removed behaviour are removed or inverted, not left
      asserting a contract that no longer exists:
      `test_ci_runner_proceeds_unsandboxed_with_a_warning` (inverted: CI must NOT waive),
      `test_falsey_ci_values_do_not_waive_the_sandbox` (subsumed — no CI value waives),
      `test_the_ci_fail_open_warning_names_the_variable_and_its_value` (the warning is
      gone with the branch). `test_workstation_still_aborts_when_no_sandbox` and
      `test_a_working_sandbox_is_used_even_on_ci` remain meaningful and stay.
- [x] `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED` remains the single waiver, unchanged in name
      and semantics. No second opt-in surface is introduced. Verified by a test that the
      opt-out still permits an unsandboxed run and still logs at WARNING.
- [x] `.github/workflows/_mutation.yml` sets the explicit opt-out, with a comment
      stating that the gate runs UNSANDBOXED there and why, so the exposure is visible
      in a reviewed file rather than implied by an ambient variable. Its stale
      "fails CLOSED" comment is corrected.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` no longer describes a CI fallback that does not exist.
- [x] Every other lane is checked for reliance on the removed branch and shown not to
      need it: the enforcement lane has a working `bwrap` (`0d22-f664`), macOS cells have
      `sandbox-exec`, and the pytest cells only run `@live` tests that skip without a
      mechanism. Verified by naming each lane and its mechanism.

## Definition of Done

- Ambient `CI` alone cannot disable the sandbox, and no new waiver surface exists.
- The one lane that relied on it declares the waiver explicitly instead.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Split from `baf9-eea0`, whose plan review refused a criterion claiming to require "more than ambient CI alone" while verifying only warning text. This ticket's own first review then corrected its central premise: `CI` was never the SOLE condition — the explicit opt-out already existed — which is what turned the fix from additive to subtractive. Discovered from `e668-b496`.
baseline.summary: Ambient CI alone can disable the mutation sandbox

# S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers

## Context / Problem

The external integration suite is the only place rebar exercises a REAL provider end to end, and it runs on ONE provider. `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gates every live job on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (lines 46, 124, 185, 247; the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback appears only in the guard message, not as a matrix arm), and `prompt-eval.yml` likewise. So the provider seam this epic built — first-class Anthropic AND Bedrock, best-effort OpenAI-compatible — has exactly one arm under live test. A Bedrock-only regression (throttling shape, a `cachePoint` envelope change, an inference-profile id that stops resolving, structured output degrading) cannot be caught by CI today. It can only be caught by a human running the gates locally, which is what S7b makes possible and is NOT a substitute for automation.

This is the THIRD of the three permanent provider switches, the other two being the repo config / local environment [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] and the AWS review bot [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]. It is deliberately NOT "flip CI to Bedrock": the goal is live-grounded confidence across every provider we hold credentials for, so a MATRIX, not a switch. Flipping the single arm from Anthropic to Bedrock would trade one blind spot for another.

## Approach

Make provider a MATRIX DIMENSION of the external suite rather than an ambient default. Run the live jobs once per credentialed provider — Anthropic, Bedrock, and OpenAI where a key exists — and have each arm SKIP LOUDLY when its credential is absent, so a missing secret is visible as a skip rather than indistinguishable from a green run.

SELECT THE PROVIDER THROUGH `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, the layered config-file pointer, rather than bespoke per-arm CI wiring. Each matrix arm writes a small config file setting only `[llm.model_classes]` and points the env var at it. This is the right instrument for three reasons: it is the mechanism rebar already documents for exactly this purpose (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, landed by S7b), it DEEP-MERGES over the discovered config instead of replacing it so the arm overrides provider and model and nothing else, and it means CI DOGFOODS the same override path a developer uses — so the pointer itself gets live coverage on every run instead of being exercised only by hand. The deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is explicitly not the instrument: it cannot express per-class models.

Bedrock authenticates from the AWS credential chain, not an API key, so the matrix cannot key on "an API key secret exists"; the Bedrock arm needs its own credential presence check.

THE S7 PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and an earlier draft of this plan wrongly said it did. S7 [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67] grants an EC2 INSTANCE ROLE reached via IMDS from inside `compose-review-bot-1` (caller identity `assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/<instance-id>`). The external suite runs on `ubuntu-latest` (`external-integration.yml:32`) — a GitHub-hosted runner with no instance role and no IMDS path to that host. So the CI arm needs its OWN credential mechanism, named explicitly: OIDC federation — `permissions: id-token: write` plus `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` assuming a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path). Static long-lived keys in a secret are the rejected alternative: they would put a durable AWS credential in CI to save a one-time role setup.

REGION MUST BE SET EXPLICITLY, and the `[llm.model_classes]` file cannot carry it. Bug [rebar:a574] established by measurement that IMDS does NOT supply a region and that Bedrock hard-fails with `NoRegionError` at client construction when none resolves — and that rebar's own `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` alone was insufficient, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` was also required. The Bedrock arm therefore sets BOTH as job env. This is a real trap, not a hypothetical: it already broke a Bedrock cutover once.

Cost is the real constraint: N providers multiplies the live spend of a suite that already runs weekly. Decide and record whether every provider runs on every trigger, or whether non-default providers run on a reduced cadence or a reduced case subset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The external suite runs its live jobs for MORE THAN ONE provider, with provider as an explicit
      matrix dimension rather than an ambient default read from whichever key happens to be set.
- [x] Anthropic and Bedrock are both covered. OpenAI is covered where a credential exists, or its
      absence is recorded as a deliberate decision with the reason.
- [x] Each arm selects its provider via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointing at a config file that sets
      ONLY `[llm.model_classes]`, NOT via the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`. A test or CI assertion
      pins that the override changes provider/model and leaves the rest of the discovered config intact.
- [x] An arm whose credential is ABSENT skips LOUDLY and is distinguishable in the run output from an arm
      that ran and passed — a missing secret must never read as green.
- [x] The Bedrock arm obtains credentials by a NAMED mechanism valid on a GitHub-hosted runner — OIDC
      role assumption via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to a dedicated scoped role (the S7 EC2
      instance-role path is NOT reachable from `ubuntu-latest`) — and a test or CI assertion pins that it
      does not silently fall back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- [x] The Bedrock arm resolves an AWS region explicitly, setting BOTH `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` and
      `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` as job env, and FAILS LOUDLY with the typed configuration error (per
      [rebar:a574]) when no region resolves — it must never skip silently or read as green.
- [x] The per-trigger COST of the matrix is measured and recorded, and the cadence decision (every
      trigger vs reduced cadence/subset per provider) is stated with its rationale.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the config-read
      and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers, not just Anthropic

Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

baseline.description:
# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).** The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning `[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).** The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and `plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` (coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated (`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: E1 — Force measurement provenance into attested evidence

## Summary
Two related gaps in the workflow reference-linter (`workflow/lint_refs.py`), surfaced reviewing the code-review gate (epic b744 / WS3):
1. `check_string` is routed over a step's `with:` values + the `if:` guard, but NOT over a `batch:` step's `criteria[].when` expressions (lint_refs.py ~378-407). So a typo'd `${{ steps.X.outputs.include_typo }}` in a batch criterion's `when:` is NEVER name-checked — it only surfaces at runtime.
2. `_output_fields_map` (lint_refs.py ~547) reads only `schema.properties.keys()`, ignoring `patternProperties`. So an output whose dynamic keys live in `patternProperties` (e.g. `overlay_union_output`'s `include_<overlay>` keys, or `plan_review_assemble_criteria_output`'s `include_<ID>`) is invisible to the reference check.

## Impact
The code-review gate (gates/code-review.yaml) leans on 22 `${{ steps.triggers/union.outputs.include_<overlay> }}` refs in batch `when:` clauses; none are linted. A typo would pass `rebar workflow validate` and only fail/misbehave at runtime (silently skipping an overlay). Pre-existing (plan-review's include_<ID> refs have the same blind spot); not introduced by b744.

## Reproduction Steps
1. In a v3 workflow, add a batch criterion `{prompt: X, when: '${{ steps.s.outputs.nonexistent_key }}'}`.
2. `rebar workflow validate <file>` → passes (no 'output not produced' finding), despite the bogus ref.
Expected: the linter flags the unknown output ref (as it does for `with:`/`if:`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `lint_refs` walks `batch.criteria[].when` expressions through `check_string` (same as `if:`/`with:`).
- [ ] `_output_fields_map` consults `patternProperties` (a ref matching a pattern is considered produced), so dynamic-keyed outputs aren't falsely flagged AND a non-matching typo IS flagged.
- [ ] A test: a typo'd batch `when:` ref fails `workflow validate`; a valid `include_<overlay>` ref passes.

## Notes
Discovered reviewing WS3 (8855) of the code-review epic (b744). Not fixed there (linter is shared infra; out of scope for the gate). Workaround: the code-review gate's offline test exercises the real `when:` resolution, catching typos at test time.
baseline.summary: Workflow linter doesn't name-check batch.criteria[].when refs + is patternProperties-blind

# BUG: Concurrent access to the ticket store produces corruption (inconsistent compaction snapshots + orphan events)

## Summary

Concurrent writers to the shared `tickets` branch are producing a **corrupted / internally-inconsistent store**, which should not be possible. The store's design — per-store `flock` serialization plus an append-only JSONL event log with last-writer-append semantics and merge-on-push reconciliation — is supposed to make concurrency safe: writes serialize under the lock, events only append, and divergent clones converge on replay. Observed behavior contradicts that guarantee.

## Reproduction Steps

Observed live on 2026-07-05 while closing epic REB-601 (`9322-f84a-e047-4471`) with a second agent session concurrently active on the same store (its commits show `CREATE/CLAIM/FILE_IMPACT/REVIEW_RESULT/SIGNATURE/COMPACT` on ticket `4563-d974-5166-419b`, plus `chore: sync events from rebar reconciler` and `Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during push retry)` commits).

1. Two sessions write to the same store (`tickets` branch), auto-committing + auto-pushing.
2. Session A closes `seedy-edema-groan` (`b043-9490-32ca-4548`) through the completion
   verifier: the event log records `STATUS(closed)` then `SIGNATURE(completion-verifier)`.
   A `COMPACT b043-9490-32ca-4548` event lands afterward (compaction rewrites history into a
   snapshot).
3. Read the ticket back (`rebar show b043-9490-32ca-4548` / `rebar list --parent 9322…`).
4. Run `rebar fsck`.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** Reads reflect the last committed events. `b043` replays to
  `status=closed` (its only status/signature events are the close + completion-verifier
  sign; there is **no** `REOPEN`/`STATUS(open)` event after them). `fsck` reports a clean
  (or near-clean) store. Concurrent writers converge without corruption.
- **Actual:**
  - `rebar show b043` and `rebar list` report `status: open` **while the same ticket
    still carries its `completion-verifier` signature** (a signature only produced at
    close) — an impossible pair. Its event log contains **no reopen event** after the
    close, so the `open` state is a bad **compaction snapshot**, not a real transition.
  - `rebar fsck` reports **2920 issues**, including many `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`
    (snapshot references a source UUID that still exists as a separate EDIT event) and
    `ORPHAN_EVENT` (pre-snapshot event not captured in `source_event_uuids`).
  - Reads flip-flop between invocations (same ticket read as `closed` then `open`),
    indicating nondeterministic replay against an inconsistent snapshot set.
  - Net: a `closed` epic (REB-601) with a child that reads `open` — a graph-integrity
    violation the completion gate is supposed to prevent.

## Suspected Area

The corruption clusters around **compaction/snapshot generation** and the **merge-during-push reconciliation** path, not the base append path:

- Compaction may snapshot a stale/partial event set when events arrive (or are merged from
  `origin/tickets`) concurrently with the compaction — `source_event_uuids` then omits
  events that still exist independently (`SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` / `ORPHAN_EVENT`), and the
  snapshot's materialized status can predate later events (the `open`-vs-signed
  contradiction).
- The `Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during push retry)` path may interleave a
  remote compaction with local un-compacted events (or vice versa) such that replay is no
  longer deterministic across clones.
- Investigate whether `flock` actually covers the compaction + push/merge critical section
  (vs only individual event appends), and whether it holds across the read-modify-write of a
  snapshot. Note: the running binary also emits `unknown key 'verify.require_ticket_for_commit'
  ignored` — confirm the compaction code path under test is the current build, not a stale one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented: the precise interleaving (compaction vs
      concurrent append / origin merge) that yields `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` /
      `ORPHAN_EVENT` and a snapshot status that contradicts later events.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the corruption deterministically: concurrent
      writers + a compaction (and/or a merge-during-push) drive at least one
      `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`/`ORPHAN_EVENT` or a status/signature contradiction,
      failing before the fix.
- [ ] Fix ensures compaction + push/merge reconciliation is serialized (or otherwise
      made atomic) with event appends so a snapshot's `source_event_uuids` always
      captures every superseded event and replay is deterministic across clones.
- [ ] `flock` (or the equivalent guard) is verified to cover the full
      compaction/snapshot read-modify-write and the merge-during-push critical section.
- [ ] After the fix, replaying the store yields a single consistent status/signature per
      ticket (no `open`-with-completion-signature); `b043-9490-32ca-4548` and REB-601's
      children read consistently across repeated `show`/`list` calls.
- [ ] A remediation/repair path exists for the already-corrupted store: `fsck` on the
      current store no longer reports `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`/`ORPHAN_EVENT` (either a
      `fsck --repair`-style rebuild of snapshots from the event log, or documented manual
      steps), driving the current 2920-issue count to zero for these classes.
baseline.summary: Concurrent access to ticket store produces corruption (inconsistent compaction snapshots + orphan events)

# Split outbound_differ.py below the module-size cap (prerequisite for S3/S6)

## Context / Problem

`outbound_differ.py` sits at **799/800 LOC** — the hard module-size cap enforced by the CI-only gate in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` against `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (=800; strict `>`). S2 (438a) drove it to 799 via `repo_root` threading. S3 (`a8ea`, config-driven type mapping) and S6 (`d458`) both MUST add code here — S3 needs a `rebar-type:` stamp invocation site (mirroring the `rebar-status:` stamp invoked ~line 763) and per-project type-skip threading through `compute_outbound_mutations` (~line 374, where `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` is loaded and passed to `_compute_outbound_select_absent_gets`). Any addition breaches 800 and fails CI `Verified`. This is a pure prerequisite refactor — no behaviour change.

## Approach

Extract along an EXISTING call-graph seam (per AGENTS.md module-size policy — never mechanically, never a <100-LOC fragment). The two per-ticket mutation builders, `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` (lines 525–632, ~108 LOC) and `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` (lines 633–799, ~167 LOC), form a natural cluster: both are called ONLY by the `compute_outbound_mutations` orchestrator and both build a single `OutboundMutation` from a local/Jira ticket pair. Move the pair into a new sibling module `outbound_mutation_builders.py`. `compute_outbound_mutations` imports them back. Shared helpers they use (`OutboundMutation`, `_load_config`, `_effective_status_map_for`, the mapper imports, `_best_effort`, `_is_retired`) either move with the cluster or are imported by the new module from `outbound_differ` / their existing homes — the implementer resolves the exact import edges so both modules type-check and no cycle forms. Result: `outbound_differ.py` ≈ 525 LOC, new module ≈ 290 LOC — both comfortably in the 200–500 target band.

Public API is unchanged: `compute_outbound_mutations`, `OutboundDiffConfig`, `OutboundMutation` keep their import paths (re-export the mutation builders from `outbound_differ` if any test imports them by their private name). `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` mirrors the gate and must stay green.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — remove the two builder functions;
  import them from the new module; keep the orchestrator + dataclasses + top helpers.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py` (new) — the extracted
  `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` + `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` cluster.

## Testing

Pure behaviour-preserving refactor — the EXISTING outbound-differ suite is the oracle, run UNCHANGED (no new behavioural test is authored; a refactor that needs a new behavioural test was not behaviour-preserving). The module-size contract test is the structural oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `outbound_differ.py` and `outbound_mutation_builders.py` are EACH < 800 LOC and within the
  200–500 target band — verified by
  `find src/rebar -name '*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>800'` (empty) and
  by `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passing.
- [x] The reconciler outbound suite passes GREEN unchanged — verified by
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -k outbound` (no observable-behaviour change).
- [x] The extraction is a single existing call-graph seam (the two `compute_outbound_mutations`
  builders); no symbol's public import path changed (private-name importers get a re-export).

Test tier: **refactor** — no new behaviour; the existing suite + the module-size contract are the full oracle. Discovered during S3 (`a8ea`) plan-review round 1.
baseline.summary: Split outbound_differ.py below module-size cap (prerequisite for S3/S6)
