## Context / Problem

Pass 1 (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py`, `passes.pass1_chunk`, prompts `reviewers/plan_review_finder.md` + one `plan_review_<ID>.md` per criterion, routing in `criteria_routing.json`, frontier class = Opus on Bedrock) is the expensive pass. A criterion edit cannot be judged from stored data alone, so Tier 2 re-runs finders on a small fixed sample. Per-criterion edits are far cheaper in single-criterion mode; prior work (`docs/experiments/plan-review-model-tradeoff.md`) showed Opus is flat to 12 criteria/turn while Sonnet degrades.

**Execution tier is per-criterion — exact contract.** `registry.exec_tier(crit)` (registry.py:604-610) returns ONLY one of `"AGENT"` / `"2-STEP"` / `"1-TURN"` — there is NO `"CONTAINER"` return value. It returns `"AGENT"` for any id in `AGENT_TIER` (registry.py:97-116 — the FULL frozenset: `G1G2, E4, A1, G6, G3, G4, G7, T1, T3, T5c, T8, T10, T11, asserted-capability, evidence-kind, decomp-shape`) or when `crit["exec"] == "AGENT"`. `G3`/`G4` therefore resolve to `"AGENT"` from `exec_tier`, NOT a container value — the container fan-out (`pass1_container`) is a SEPARATE downstream step: `production_batch_runner._resolve_criteria` (production_batch_runner.py:198-248) splits criteria into `(single, agent, skipped)` purely by `exec_tier(desc) == "AGENT"`, and its own docstring states G3/G4 are "pulled out of `agent` by `run_pass1` itself" — i.e. `run_pass1` inspects the resolved `agent` list afterward and routes G3/G4 to `pass1_container` from there. Tier-2 derives its own single/agent/container split the same way: resolve via `exec_tier`, then separately check membership in the (small, hardcoded in `run_pass1`) G3/G4 container set.

**Single-criterion filtering — exact mechanism.** `BatchRunRequest.criteria` (workflow/runners.py:66, `tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]`, each entry `{prompt, with?}`) is what `_resolve_criteria` actually filters on. `req.with_inputs["probe_criteria"]` (a SEPARATE field) is consumed ONLY by `_project_criteria` for `project.*`-prefixed fan-in criteria (production_batch_runner.py:114-118) — it does NOT filter `req.criteria`/`_resolve_criteria`'s built-in dispatch. To run exactly one named criterion against `ProductionBatchRunner` directly, Tier-2 constructs `req.criteria = ({"prompt": f"plan-review-{id}"},)` (a single-entry tuple) itself — `_resolve_criteria` then correctly routes that one descriptor through `exec_tier` into `single` or `agent`. (The workflow-level PROBE MODE that reads `ctx.inputs["probe_criteria"]` to filter built-ins, `workflow_ops.py:254-263`, is a different, higher-layer mechanism for workflow-driven runs and is not used here since Tier-2 invokes the runner directly.)

Cost varies by resolved tier: `1-TURN`/`2-STEP` criteria cost ≈ $0.17-0.25/sample (the AC's ceiling, applies ONLY to ids resolving to `1-TURN`/`2-STEP`); `AGENT`-tier criteria (including the G3/G4 container subset) cost their real production rate and are reported separately in the ledger, with no fixed per-sample ceiling assumed.

**Tier-1 chaining, corrected.** `tier1.replay_review` requires a STORED `verification` on each finding to build `stored_answers` — a freshly-generated Tier-2 candidate finding has none, so Tier-1's `per_question_agreement`/`distribution_shift` cannot run on it directly. Tier 2's "downstream" instead reuses Tier-1/Tier-0's COMPUTATION functions: candidate findings are verified fresh via the SAME `verify_findings` seam Tier-1 uses, then `review_kernel.decide.pass3_decide`/`pass3_over_findings` computes a CANDIDATE VERDICT from them, compared against the STORED verdict already recorded in the original review's sidecar — a verdict-level flip matrix (Tier-0's shape), not a per-question agreement table.

## Approach

Build `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py`:

- **Fixed sample**: ~20 review ids drawn once by the Tier-1 stratified sampler (additional strata: ≥5 containers, ≥8 with ≥10 findings, ≥3 from the LMN store), committed as `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/tier2-sample.json`. Plan text from reconstructed material; code-grounded AGENT criteria run against the pinned `verified_at_sha` snapshot via `source=attested`.
- **Full mode**: run the candidate registry/prompts through `ProductionBatchRunner`, frontier class pinned to Bedrock Opus; compare candidate Pass-1 finding sets to stored findings by `norm_id` (Jaccard, gained/lost per criterion); verify candidate findings via `verify_findings`, compute their verdict via `pass3_decide`/`pass3_over_findings`, compare to the stored verdict (flip matrix).
- **Single-criterion mode**: `--criteria T5c` constructs `req.criteria = ({"prompt": "plan-review-T5c"},)` on a `BatchRunRequest` and runs it directly through `ProductionBatchRunner`/`_resolve_criteria` (real single/agent dispatch by `exec_tier`, with G3/G4's container split applied same as `run_pass1`) over the sample; compares only that criterion's findings.
- Baseline for a criterion whose stored findings predate the current `regver`: a one-time baseline run recorded in the ledger; otherwise stored findings are the baseline.
- Budget pre-flight from stored per-criterion usage (`coverage.usage.per_criterion`) × current price.

`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/__main__.py`: add a `tier2` subparser (`--candidate <registry-dir>`, `--criteria <id>`, plus shared `--store`/`--cache-dir`/`--out-dir`) and a `_run_tier2` dispatch branch, mirroring `tier0`/`tier1`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/__main__.py` (edited — `tier2` subparser + dispatch)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/tier2-sample.json`, `tier2-*.md` (new/generated)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_tier2.py` (new)

## Testing

Unit: with a `FakeRunner` returning canned `P1Output`, gained/lost findings per criterion match expectations; single-criterion mode for a `1-TURN` id (`req.criteria` single-entry) issues exactly one chunk per sampled review; single-criterion mode for an `AGENT`-tier id (e.g. `T5c`) dispatches agentically via `ProductionBatchRunner`'s `agent` bucket, NOT forced single-turn; G3/G4 route to the container path the same way `run_pass1` does; a run is refused when the frontier model is not the Bedrock Opus id; the sample file is validated against the corpus manifest; a candidate finding set is verified via `verify_findings` and its verdict computed via `pass3_decide`, compared correctly against a fixture's stored verdict. Live (commissioning, ≤$60): one full-mode baseline over the fixed sample. `__main__.py`'s `tier2` subcommand dispatches correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A committed fixed sample of review ids exists with the strata above; checked by the sample file and manifest cross-check.
- [x] `tier2 --candidate <registry-dir>` produces finding-set Jaccard and gained/lost-per-criterion tables plus a candidate-vs-stored verdict flip matrix; checked by one generated report.
- [x] `tier2 --criteria <1-TURN-or-2-STEP-id>` costs ≤ N × $0.25 in the ledger; checked by the ledger. An AGENT-tier `--criteria` run (including G3/G4) is priced at its real production rate and reported separately, with no fixed per-sample ceiling assumed.
- [x] Commissioning spend for this ticket ≤ $60 and every call uses the Bedrock frontier model id; checked by the ledger.
- [x] Unit tests pass in `make test`.
baseline.summary: Tier-2 harness: replay Pass-1 criteria on a fixed stratified sample (Opus via Bedrock, budgeted; single-criterion mode)

baseline.description:
Run the one-time reclaim. **Do not start until A1-A5, A6-0a..0d and Epic B's B6 are closed**, and until A6-0a has been on `main` >=24 h with an observed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run on a descendant SHA (older binaries ignore the epoch field, so they would sail past the guard). session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Protocol
1. **Agent** disables `reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (`gh workflow disable`,
   which also blocks `workflow_dispatch` and therefore `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` self-redispatch);
   **asserts** no reconcile run is in progress (poll `gh run list`, not drain-and-hope); asserts the
   **Gerrit review queue is empty** — zero sessions stops new pushes, but a patchset pushed just
   before the window can still have its `LLM-Review` vote fire during it, and every vote writes a
   ticket; break-glasses `refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}` if held.
2. **Agent** pauses the AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` and the host LaunchAgents
   `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` (04:00) and `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update` (whose hourly
   rollback-guarded pipx reinstall could silently revert the global `rebar` to a pre-A6-0a build
   mid-window). **[operator-attested] Operator** confirms **zero active sessions** and all
   **`rebar-mcp` servers stopped** (a long-running MCP holds an in-process store handle and does not
   hot-reload). Gerrit needs no separate confirmation: every Gerrit push comes from a session.
3. **Agent** converges the local tracker (`fetch` + `reset --hard origin/tickets`, 0-ahead verified).
   This covers all 48 sibling worktrees at once — their `.tickets-tracker` are **symlinks to the one
   store**. The four other real trackers on the host point at different GitHub repos.
4. **Agent** deletes the pre-rewrite ref pins (A6-0d), runs the strip in a fresh **unfiltered** clone,
   verifies the pre-push assertions, and pushes with **`--force-with-lease`**.
5. **Agent** asserts non-resurrection: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is
   **false**, and no clone-fetched ref has the old tip as an ancestor.
6. **Agent** converges the review-bot clone over SSM (`fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets` on
   `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`). Reverts to **[operator-attested]** if the issued AWS
   credentials do not permit `ssm send-command` against `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`.
7. **Agent** lands the `enforce_since` re-pin through Gerrit, mapped via the commit-map.
   `rebar.toml:115` is the only literal SHA in the system; with `require_authenticated = false`
   (`:106`) `verify_authorship.py:531-550` returns early and never reads it, so there is **no CI
   deadlock** and the change lands normally. `verify.opcert_enforce_since` is unset.
8. **Agent** re-enables the GitHub workflows, the AWS timer, and both LaunchAgents.
9. **Agent** verifies the ACs below and **notifies the operator** that the tickets branch is
   available for sessions again.

## T11 migration-safety answers
- **Expand/contract:** yes — A6-0a's reader ships and is deployed before the epoch value exists.
- **Batching:** n/a, single atomic ref update.
- **Resumability: NONE, stated.** A force-push is not resumable. Mitigation: all correctness
  assertions run on the scratch clone **before** publishing, so a wrong graph never reaches origin;
  the push itself is atomic per-ref.
- **Dual-write window:** none — the store is quiesced; the epoch guard replaces dual-write as the
  stale-writer defence.
- **Rollback:** restore from the A6-0d bundle + `--force-with-lease` back to the old tip. Known
  limit: rollback re-diverges anything already converged, so consumers must be re-converged in the
  same order as the forward path. **No event bytes are ever altered** — only commit SHAs — so the
  rewrite itself cannot lose ticket data.
- **T4 destructiveness:** an irreversible force-push to the authoritative store of a live system,
  chosen deliberately to reclaim 92% of the branch, gated on operator-confirmed quiescence, an
  off-repo bundle, a fail-closed epoch guard, and pre-push assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB** (from 1.04 GiB; the measured strip
      result is ~94 MiB) and `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree.
      **Holds only because B6 landed first.** Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] Commit count and merge-commit count on `tickets` are **unchanged** versus the pre-rewrite
      recording (measured at window time, never hardcoded). Tier: **repo assertion**.
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <sha> --format json`, run pre-rewrite
      against the old SHA and post-rewrite against the mapped SHA: the **stderr summary counts** are
      identical AND the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` from the JSON report is
      identical **ignoring `commit`**. (JSON mode puts only the report array on stdout and the summary
      on stderr; the report lists only non-verified events; every `commit` is a rewritten SHA. The
      command **exits 1** when `enforced_not_verified > 0`, so do not require exit 0.) Tier: **CLI
      subprocess, both sides**.
- [ ] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** and `size-pack` growth is **< 1 MB**. The ancestry assertion is
      what actually proves non-resurrection. Tier: **repo measurement after an observed vote**.
- [ ] No ref a default clone fetches has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier: `ls-remote` +
      `merge-base` loop, computed at window time.
- [ ] Operator confirmation of zero active sessions and stopped MCP servers is recorded as a comment
      before step 3. **[operator-attested]**
- [ ] A reconciler pass completes green after step 8, and `rebar fsck` is clean. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
Operational — no `src/` changes. Uses the A6-0c script and A6-0d helpers; touches `rebar.toml` (`enforce_since`) via Gerrit in step 7.

Scope: M (operational). Depends on A5, A6-0b, A6-0c, A6-0d, and Epic B's B6.
baseline.summary: A6-1: execute the reclaim window (quiesced, guarded, agent-executed except the zero-sessions confirmation)

baseline.description:
Same class as [rebar:a371-fb42-32c5-48bd] (an `importorskip`-masked test that is broken the moment its extra IS installed). Found while running the full unit suite with the `[ui]` extra installed to verify a371's fix.

`tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py:147` `test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail` builds a fake request as:

    req = types.SimpleNamespace(
        app=types.SimpleNamespace(state=types.SimpleNamespace(config=cfg)),
        query_params={"token": "tok", "change": "12345"},
    )
    resp = asyncio.run(rerun(req))

`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:101` reads `request.headers.get(TOKEN_HEADER, "").strip()`, and the fake has no `headers`, so the test dies with:

    AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'headers'

Reproduced deterministically at origin/main (c89a2ddcc4), py3.12, with `--extra ui` installed (which pulls fastapi):

    pytest tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py -q -p no:randomly
      -> 1 failed, 54 passed

Line 148 is `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")  # the reviewbot extra; absent in the lean CI suite`, so the lean CI suite skips it and the breakage is invisible. As with a371, the test reads as covering the `/rerun` 502-body containment barrier while providing no coverage in any environment where the extra is present.

Presumably the fake request stopped matching `app.rerun` when header-token auth was added to that handler; the fake needs a `headers` mapping (and whatever else the current handler reads).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_path_injection_guards.py` passes with the reviewbot/ui extra
      installed
- [ ] The test still asserts the same containment barrier (502 body carries no exception or
      stack-trace detail) -- do not weaken it to make it pass
- [ ] Sweep the other `importorskip`-guarded tests for the same rot, since none of them run in
      the lean CI suite
baseline.summary: importorskip-masked: test_rerun_502_body_has_no_exception_detail fails when the reviewbot extra IS installed

baseline.description:
## Why
AGENTS.md is the canonical, cross-vendor agent guidance. CLAUDE.md bridges Claude Code to it via an @AGENTS.md import, and .codex/config.toml points Codex's project_doc_fallback at it. GitHub Copilot's coding agent already reads AGENTS.md natively, but other Copilot surfaces (Copilot Chat, Copilot CLI) look at .github/copilot-instructions.md first and had no pointer back to AGENTS.md, so they could silently drift from the canonical guidance.

## What
Add .github/copilot-instructions.md as a thin bridge file (mirroring CLAUDE.md's role): it declares AGENTS.md authoritative, summarizes the key sections (ticket workflow, Gerrit git flow, module-size policy, code-navigation tooling), and explicitly says not to duplicate content that could drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/copilot-instructions.md` exists in the tracked tree and states that `AGENTS.md`
      is canonical/authoritative for this repo.
- [ ] The new file summarizes rather than restates `AGENTS.md` (ticket workflow, Gerrit git
      flow, module-size policy, code-navigation tooling) and says `AGENTS.md` wins on conflict.
- [ ] No local-only Copilot state is added to the tracked tree (mirrors the posture where
      `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.codex/worktrees` stay untracked/local-only).
- [ ] Change lands through Gerrit per CONTRIBUTING.md: commit carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer
      and DCO sign-off, pushed to `refs/for/main`, and reaches `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Add .github/copilot-instructions.md bridge file for provider-guidance parity

baseline.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230, store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88 commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py` 14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.** `_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3; `signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP 204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in `llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB: signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules; `_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8 times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" — the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [ ] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [ ] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and "Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [ ] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [ ] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [ ] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.
baseline.summary: Comment triage: relocate history, rationale and contracts out of src

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
probe-rebar.sh accumulated stale assertions (08ce: 3 stale asserts against removed flags/keysets). Its missing 'set -e' is DELIBERATE harness design (continue past failures, report all) — a naive port or hardening pass would break it.

## Approach
Port to a Python probe harness (scripts/probe_rebar.py) preserving the continue-on-failure design (collect results, report all, exit non-zero if any failed — the same contract, now explicit). Assertion-parity review required: every current assertion enumerated and carried over or retired with a reason (the 08ce class came from silent drift). Do NOT add set -e semantics.

Shell deletion and consumer re-pointing happen in the SAME change, after the side-by-side parity run: every consumer that hard-wires the shell path is re-pointed to the Python entry point in this change, so CI and the anti-rot gate track the new harness atomically.

## Scope
- scripts/probe-rebar.sh -> scripts/probe_rebar.py (port; the shell path is retained as a 7-line transitional exec shim because gerrit-verify.yaml executes from MAIN's workflow definition, whose golden-path step still invokes the shell path until this change lands — discovered on patchset 1, Verified-1 exit 127; deletion is follow-up d772-6007-5d04-4101)
- Consumers re-pointed in the same change (enumerated by grep for 'probe-rebar'):
  - .github/workflows/test.yml:128 — 'bash scripts/probe-rebar.sh </dev/null' -> python invocation
  - .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:209 — same re-point
  - .github/workflows/external-integration.yml:54 — comment mentioning the path; update wording
  - tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py — _PROBE_JOBS asserts substring 'scripts/probe-rebar.sh' in golden-path jobs; update the pinned substring to the Python entry point so the anti-rot gate keeps guarding
  - docs/releasing.md:401,405,407 — invocation examples -> Python equivalents
  - CHANGELOG.md + docs/experiments corpus jsonl are historical records — NOT touched.
- Assertion inventory table in the change description (commit message).

## Testing
Self-test: inject one failing probe -> harness continues, reports it, exits non-zero. Parity: run both harnesses against the same build before deletion, identical pass/fail verdict per assertion. tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py green against the updated substring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Python harness replaces the shell probe with continue-on-failure preserved.
- [x] Assertion-parity table: every shell assertion mapped to ported/retired-with-reason.
- [x] Side-by-side run shows identical verdicts; shell path reduced to a transitional exec shim (full deletion tracked in d772-6007-5d04-4101, required because gerrit-verify.yaml executes from main's workflow definition) with ALL enumerated consumers (workflows, anti-rot test, docs) re-pointed to the Python entry point.

## 2026-08-08 resolved-report consolidation

Fresh resolution experiment on current `origin/main`: `python scripts/probe_rebar.py` ran the full isolated end-to-end CLI probe and reported `PROBE RESULT: 140 passed, 0 failed`. baseline.description:
## Context

Parallel agent sessions race to land changes on the Fast-Forward-Only `main` (ADR-0040). The loser of each race must manually rebase-to-tip and retry, and with a large feature **stack** this update-and-retry causes many CI re-runs on non-conflicting changes — burning **wall-clock** (GitHub Actions minutes are free for this OSS repo, but concurrency is capped) and **agent tokens/attention** (sessions hand-roll the rebase + poll for submittability).

This epic builds the **auto-lander**: agents set an opt-in intent and walk away; changes land autonomously (or are handed back with a single actionable outcome), while the strong two-vote gate is never weakened.

> **Terminology.** "stack" (the agent's view of a related series) and "chain" (a Gerrit
> relation chain) are used synonymously throughout this epic and its children.

**Separation-of-concerns scope (the load-bearing decision):** landing/merge-queueing is **platform-specific and maintainer-owned**, NOT part of rebar's platform-agnostic ticket/workflow/gate/reconcile mission. So everything here is **THIS project's infrastructure** (Gerrit + GitHub Actions), living in `infra/` + a project CLI/script — it MAY `import rebar` for ticket ops (e.g. close a ticket on merge) but adds **no Gerrit-specific landing logic to `src/rebar` core**. The platform-agnostic generalization is deliberately deferred to a separate `idea` (the landing provider-seam, `1701-8bc1-e3b7-4984`).

**Design settled in the brainstorm (all grounded in OSS prior art):**
- **Phase 1 = serial lander (this epic's committed scope).** Land the front `Autosubmit`
  change/chain: rebase to tip → await fresh Verified → ancestor-atomic submit.
- **Phase 2 = throughput, DEFERRED.** Cross-stack batching was evaluated by a design spike and
  **rejected** on this infra (the gerrit-to-platform bridge fires CI per-patchset → N runs not one;
  landing N off one run needs a GerriScary-class Verified direct-cast; wins only in rare bursts of
  ≥4 + a bisection tax + WIP-hook fragility). The recommended throughput approach — **bounded
  speculation** (speculate ≤ the GHA concurrency cap; each candidate a clean single-change-on-tip
  verified on its own tree) — is deferred to idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`, promoted only if the serial
  treadmill becomes a MEASURED pain.
- **Gate substrate stays:** FFO as the R5 backstop; strict `Verified` copyCondition
  (drops on rebase → CI re-runs); LLM-Review carries `TRIVIAL_REBASE` (ADR-0041) so a
  conflict-free rebase re-runs ONLY CI, not the LLM review.
- **`Autosubmit` opt-in label = a lease the agent hands the bot;** coexists with manual submit.
- **The stack is the atomic unit for landing AND failure:** never partial-land, never evict a
  change from *within* a stack; on failure the **whole stack is handed back to its owning agent**
  to remediate (Goal-2 exception: agent is pulled in only when code must change).
- **Agent contract = one command → one typed outcome** (`merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed |
  review_failed`); the `land` command is the single point that *returns* the outcome, so agents
  never correlate votes/labels/status themselves. Delivered as project tooling reading Gerrit
  primitives. **Outcome provenance (the deliberate split model — NOT co-located; this is the
  authoritative statement, superseding any looser "single source of truth" phrasing elsewhere):**
  the one outcome the bot must *decide and persist* — `needs_rebase` (a rebase conflict /
  FFO-not-landable state, which is NOT a native Gerrit vote and so has no live signal) — is
  **recorded by the lander into its own state (S3)** and read back by `land`; the three outcomes
  that ARE native Gerrit facts — `merged` (change status MERGED), `ci_failed` (a post-rebase
  `Verified -1` on the current patchset) and `review_failed` (an `LLM-Review -1`) — are **derived
  live by the `land` command from Gerrit primitives (S3/S4)**, not stored by the bot. (This
  matches S3 AC3 + S4 AC5, which own the code: only `needs_rebase` is persisted; `ci_failed` is
  read live from the current `Verified` vote.) So `land` is the single *reporter* of a unified
  typed outcome, composed from one bot-state read (`needs_rebase`) + live Gerrit reads.

## Greenfield note

This epic is greenfield: the `Autosubmit` label, the autolander service + its `wipChain` and state dir, the `land`/`land-status` command + outcome enum, the outcome-record schema, and ADR-0042 are all NEW artifacts created by this epic's stories. Cross-story references to them are forward-references to sibling deliverables (see each story's `## Dependencies`), not references to existing code.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Phase 1 — serial auto-lander (first deliverable)
- [ ] `Autosubmit` Gerrit label authored in `infra/gerrit/project.config` / pushed to
      `refs/meta/config`: **requester-votable ACL** (vote granted to group `Contributors`, so an
      agent sets the label under its OWN identity via the land command — the bot casts no votes;
      the grant is tightly scoped, not a bot-only or open grant), **non-gating** (informational;
      gating is redundant under FFO),
      **non-sticky** (empty copyCondition).
- [ ] Serial auto-lander service (project infra; deploys like the review-bot —
      `infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` + compose): for the front `Autosubmit`+submittable change/chain
      it rebases to the current tip (`POST /changes/{id}/rebase` / `/rebase:chain`,
      `RebaseInput.rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader=true` to preserve author/DCO/`rebar-ticket` trailers) → awaits a fresh
      `Verified +1` → ancestor-atomic submits the exact tested SHA. Single `wipChain` (serialized,
      one instance).
- [ ] **No gate-semantics change** — the serial lander reads existing `Verified` votes and casts
      NO votes (the bot never casts Verified in this epic's committed scope).
- [ ] Failure handling: CI-fail → remove `Autosubmit`, rely on the native `Verified -1` + run
      logs; rebase-conflict (`409`) → remove `Autosubmit` and record a conflict outcome. **Never
      partial-land; never evict a change from within a stack** — the whole stack is handed back to
      its owning agent.
- [ ] **Agent landing contract (the lead story):** a single **project** command that requests a
      land and returns ONE typed terminal outcome (`merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed |
      review_failed`) + distinct exit code; blocking (`--wait`) and single-shot status variants.
      `land` is the single **reporter** of the outcome, composing it per the split-provenance
      model above (one bot-state read for `needs_rebase`; live Gerrit reads for
      `ci_failed`/`merged`/`review_failed`) so the agent never correlates primitives itself. The command
      lives in **project tooling** (repo CLI/script), NOT `rebar` core; it may `import rebar` for
      ticket ops.
- [ ] Observability: the bot logs to **its own service logs** (container stdout → existing
      CloudWatch monitoring), NOT `session_log` (which is for agentic sessions only).
- [ ] Docs: rewrite this repo's landing section (`CLAUDE.md` + `CONTRIBUTING.md`) to the new
      contract — "set `Autosubmit` / run the land command; act on the single typed outcome; do
      NOT watch votes or treat two green votes as 'it will land'." ADR-0042 (created by S6
      `broken-checkered-tiger`) records the auto-lander + agent contract.
- [ ] **Pre-cutover access baseline (captured by S1 `843b`, BEFORE the `Autosubmit` label is
      pushed to `refs/meta/config`):** save the current `GET /a/projects/rebar/access` response to
      `infra/gerrit/access-snapshot-pre-autolander.json` and **commit it in the same change that
      adds the label to `project.config`**, so the ADR-0042 security-invariants diff below has a
      committed baseline to diff against. Without this baseline captured before cutover, the
      access-diff check is unperformable. (S1 owns the capture; S6/ADR-0042 owns the diff.)
- [ ] **Security-invariants artifact:** an ADR-0042 **Security invariants** section enumerating
      each invariant — non-gating `Autosubmit`; requester-votable (`Contributors`) vote ACL, tightly scoped; re-verify `is:submittable` on
      the exact tested SHA immediately before submit; two-vote gate unweakened — and, per
      invariant, the concrete check that proves it (a `grep` of `infra/gerrit/project.config`, a
      `GET /a/projects/rebar/access` diff vs the committed
      `infra/gerrit/access-snapshot-pre-autolander.json` baseline, and/or a test asserting the
      re-verify logic) (CVE-2025-1568 / GerriScary posture).

### Phase 2 — throughput (DEFERRED to idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`)
- [ ] No Phase-2 work is in this epic's committed scope. Cross-stack batching was evaluated and
      **rejected** by the design spike (stories S7-S9 archived); the throughput follow-on is
      **bounded speculation**, promoted from the idea only on a measured serial-treadmill pain.
- [ ] An agent sets the landing intent and walks away; in the common (non-conflicting) case the
- [ ] On any failure the agent receives **one typed, actionable outcome** — it never watches votes or
- [ ] **Nothing lands whose to-be-merged tree wasn't CI-tested** (FFO + strict Verified preserved;
- [ ] Redundant CI runs from the parallel-landing race are eliminated (each change/stack is CI'd only
- [ ] **No Gerrit-specific landing logic in `src/rebar` core** — rebar stays platform-agnostic.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (separate tickets)

- **Cross-stack batching** — evaluated by the Phase-2 design spike and **rejected** on this infra
  (per-patchset CI dispatch → N runs not one; a GerriScary-class `Verified` direct-cast; rare wins +
  bisection tax + WIP-hook fragility). S7-S9 archived; throughput deferred to **bounded speculation**
  (idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`) — the correctly-shaped follow-on, not "speculation ruled out."
- **Platform-agnostic landing provider-seam in `rebar` core** (Gerrit/GitHub/GitLab adapters +
  portable outcome enum) — deferred to a separate `idea` (`1701-8bc1-e3b7-4984`; YAGNI until a
  second platform needs to land; consistent with rebar's provider-neutral identity/reconciler
  direction).
baseline.summary: Parallel-agent auto-lander for main — serial lander (project infrastructure)

baseline.description:
## Why

PyPI/wheel installs have no rebar git checkout, so live-git SHA resolution
(story 1) yields version-only there. Baking the release commit SHA at build time
gives consistent gate-code provenance across dev/editable and PyPI installs
(epic jira-reb-596).

## What

- Add `hatch_build.py` at the **repo root** implementing `BuildHookInterface`; it
  runs `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at wheel/sdist build and writes a generated,
  git-ignored `src/rebar/_build_info.py` (`COMMIT = "<sha>"`, or `COMMIT = None`
  when built outside a git tree).
- Register it in `pyproject.toml` with a `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` stanza
  (WITHOUT this, hatchling silently skips the hook and the baked SHA never ships).
- Add `src/rebar/_build_info.py` to `.gitignore` AND to the `artifacts` glob under
  `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]` (git-based source discovery drops git-ignored
  files from the wheel otherwise — the baked SHA would never reach PyPI).
- Extend the story-1 resolver fallback to **live-git-first, build-baked-second,
  omit-last**: with no live checkout, import `_build_info.COMMIT`.
- Keep package version STATIC (`pyproject.toml` `version`); do NOT adopt hatch-vcs.

## Scope

Build-time SHA capture + fallback wiring only. Depends on story 1's resolver.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `hatch_build.py` writes `src/rebar/_build_info.py` with the build-time short
      SHA; a non-git build writes `COMMIT = None` (graceful).
- [ ] `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` is registered AND `_build_info.py` is in
      the wheel `artifacts` glob and `.gitignore`.
- [ ] Resolver falls back to the baked SHA on a non-git install, still preferring
      the live checkout SHA when one exists.
- [ ] Package version remains static (no hatch-vcs).
- [ ] Tests: baked-fallback resolves the SHA when live git is absent; version-only
      when both absent; a built wheel actually contains `_build_info.py` with a SHA.
baseline.summary: Bake release commit SHA at build time for non-git installs

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Once a store actually syncs more than one tracker project, an older rebar binary reading it is dangerous rather than merely limited: it would fetch only its single configured project, see every other project's bound tickets as having no corresponding remote issue, and create duplicate issues in the wrong project. There is a shipped mechanism for exactly this — `.store-compat.json` with a fail-closed read (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`) — but `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is still an empty frozenset (`compat.py:60`), so no capability has ever been declared through it.

## Approach

Register `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. That single addition is what makes a binary able to *recognise* the capability; a binary that predates it hits the "required capability this binary does not provide" branch and raises `StoreIncompatibleError`, refusing writes rather than corrupting the store (`docs/migrations.md:158-165`).

This is the expand half of the expand/contract rollout `docs/migrations.md:138-149` describes: teach binaries to read and fail closed **before** anything writes the requirement. Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story, so shipping it changes no behaviour for any existing store. The conditional stamp lands separately, which is why the two are ordered rather than combined.

Reads deliberately stay available: the gate is on the write lock only (`docs/migrations.md:174-178`), so `list`/`show`/`search` keep working against a store an old binary may not write, and `fsck` surfaces the condition as a structured `compat_error` without changing its exit code.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's pure-branch row: an in-process unit test against the real classification function, since the mechanism is entirely a validation branch with no I/O of its own — plus one real-store test for the write-gate, because the gate fires inside lock acquisition and a unit test would not cross that component.

- Happy path: a record declaring `multi-project-bridge` classifies as compatible on a binary that
  registers it.
- Contrast case: a record declaring an unregistered capability name still raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError` — proving the registration widened the known set by exactly one entry and
  did not disable the check.
- Absent-record regression: a store with no `.store-compat.json` still passes through as implicit
  legacy, so pre-feature stores are unaffected.
- Write-gate path: a store whose record declares an unknown capability refuses a write through the
  real lock acquisition, while `list`/`show` against the same store still succeed. The read half is
  the contrast case that proves the gate is scoped to writes.
- Corrupt-record path: a malformed record still raises rather than being treated as absent, which is
  the bypass the gate is designed to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `multi-project-bridge` is in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` and a record declaring it classifies as
      compatible; checked by a unit test over the classification function.
- [ ] A record declaring an unregistered capability still raises `StoreIncompatibleError`; checked by
      the paired negative case.
- [ ] A store with no compat record still passes through as implicit legacy; checked by an
      absent-record regression test.
- [ ] A store declaring an unknown capability refuses writes while reads still succeed; checked by a
      real-store test exercising the write lock and a read command against the same store.
- [ ] A corrupt record raises rather than being treated as absent; checked by a malformed-record test.
baseline.summary: Register the multi-project-bridge store-compat capability (expand half)

# WS8 — Harden Gerrit auth (replace DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT with GitHub OAuth)

## Why
The live Gerrit (`rebar.solutions.navateam.com`, 3.14) runs `auth.type =
DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` — a dev-only mode where anyone can impersonate any account (no
real IdP). It CANNOT be the sole gate on production GitHub `main` (WS7) until real auth is in
place. **Confirmed strategy (2026-07-01): GitHub OAuth via the `gerrit-oauth-provider` plugin
(GitHub backend), no reverse-proxy org gate** — access curated via a short account roster + Gerrit
ACLs. Precedent: GerritHub authenticates its whole user base this way; the plugin is actively
maintained (3.13.x, tracks the Gerrit release train). Blocks WS7.

## Config (the target state)
`infra/compose/gerrit.config`:
```ini
[auth]
    type = OAUTH
    gitBasicAuthPolicy = HTTP        # bots + git-over-HTTP keep working via HTTP passwords
[plugin "gerrit-oauth-provider-github-oauth"]
    root-url = "https://github.com/"
    client-id = "<GitHub OAuth App client id>"     # non-secret; from SSM
```
`etc/secure.config` (secrets, NOT committed — materialized from SSM like the S5 deploy key):
```ini
[plugin "gerrit-oauth-provider-github-oauth"]
    client-secret = "<GitHub OAuth App client secret>"
```
Plus: install the pinned `gerrit-oauth-provider` jar into `$GERRIT_SITE/plugins`, and remove ALL
`DEVELOPMENT_*` auth.

## Deliverables — split by access boundary
### In-repo (committed; applied on a fresh redeploy) — DELIVERABLE THIS SESSION
- A runbook `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md`: the full procedure (OAuth App, plugin,
  gerrit.config/secure.config, SSM params, redeploy, bot HTTP-password provisioning, account
  migration, verification, rollback).
- `gerrit-oauth-provider` pinned-jar provenance in `infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md` +
  install-plugins scaffolding.
- The `[auth]` block comment in `infra/compose/gerrit.config` points at the runbook + WS8 (the
  live flip to `type = OAUTH` lands with the plugin+secrets chain, per the runbook — flipping it
  in isolation would break a fresh Gerrit boot).

### Access-gated (needs org admin + working AWS) — HANDOFF
- Create the **GitHub OAuth App** on `navapbc` (callback `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/oauth`)
  → client-id/secret. (Needs GitHub org admin via the web UI; this session's token lacks `admin:org`.)
- Put client-id/secret in **SSM** under the Gerrit secret prefix; add the params to `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`.
- **Apply to the live host** (AWS SSM/SSH — this session's AWS session is EXPIRED): install the
  plugin, seed the OAuth config into the live `site/etc/gerrit.config` + `secure.config`, remove
  become-any-account, restart Gerrit.
- **Provision bot credentials BEFORE cutover**: give the `rebar-review-bot` service account an HTTP
  password (dev-mode required none), so its git/REST access survives the auth change.

## Acceptance Criteria
### In-repo (this session)
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` documents the complete GitHub-OAuth hardening procedure (OAuth App → plugin → gerrit.config/secure.config → SSM → redeploy → bot passwords → account migration → verify → rollback).
- [ ] The `gerrit-oauth-provider` jar is pinned + provenance-documented (plugins/README.md) and wired into the plugin install path.
- [ ] `infra/compose/gerrit.config` `[auth]` comment points at the runbook + WS8 (records that the live flip to OAUTH lands with the plugin+secrets chain).
### Live (access-gated)
- [ ] GitHub OAuth App created; client-id/secret in SSM; `ssm.tf` params added.
- [ ] Live Gerrit switched to `auth.type = OAUTH` (become-any-account removed); Gerrit restarts healthy; a human logs in via GitHub OAuth.
- [ ] `rebar-review-bot` has an HTTP password; its REST/git access verified post-cutover.

## Dependencies
- Blocks WS7 (the Gerrit-only cutover must not precede real auth).
- Live steps need `navapbc` GitHub org admin + working AWS access to the Gerrit host (d251 infra).
baseline.summary: WS8: Harden Gerrit auth (GitHub OAuth, replace DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Once a store actually syncs more than one tracker project, an older rebar binary reading it is dangerous rather than merely limited: it would fetch only its single configured project, see every other project's bound tickets as having no corresponding remote issue, and create duplicate issues in the wrong project. There is a shipped mechanism for exactly this — `.store-compat.json` with a fail-closed read (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py`) — but `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is still an empty frozenset (`compat.py:60`), so no capability has ever been declared through it.

## Approach

Register `multi-project-bridge` in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. That single addition is what makes a binary able to *recognise* the capability; a binary that predates it hits the "required capability this binary does not provide" branch and raises `StoreIncompatibleError`, refusing writes rather than corrupting the store (`docs/migrations.md:158-165`).

This is the expand half of the expand/contract rollout `docs/migrations.md:138-149` describes: teach binaries to read and fail closed **before** anything writes the requirement. Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story, so shipping it changes no behaviour for any existing store. The conditional stamp lands separately, which is why the two are ordered rather than combined.

Reads deliberately stay available: the gate is on the write lock only (`docs/migrations.md:174-178`), so `list`/`show`/`search` keep working against a store an old binary may not write, and `fsck` surfaces the condition as a structured `compat_error` without changing its exit code.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's pure-branch row: an in-process unit test against the real classification function, since the mechanism is entirely a validation branch with no I/O of its own — plus one real-store test for the write-gate, because the gate fires inside lock acquisition and a unit test would not cross that component.

- Happy path: a record declaring `multi-project-bridge` classifies as compatible on a binary that
  registers it.
- Contrast case: a record declaring an unregistered capability name still raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError` — proving the registration widened the known set by exactly one entry and
  did not disable the check.
- Absent-record regression: a store with no `.store-compat.json` still passes through as implicit
  legacy, so pre-feature stores are unaffected.
- Write-gate path: a store whose record declares an unknown capability refuses a write through the
  real lock acquisition, while `list`/`show` against the same store still succeed. The read half is
  the contrast case that proves the gate is scoped to writes.
- Corrupt-record path: a malformed record still raises rather than being treated as absent, which is
  the bypass the gate is designed to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `multi-project-bridge` is in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` and a record declaring it classifies as
      compatible; checked by a unit test over the classification function.
- [ ] A record declaring an unregistered capability still raises `StoreIncompatibleError`; checked by
      the paired negative case.
- [ ] A store with no compat record still passes through as implicit legacy; checked by an
      absent-record regression test.
- [ ] A store declaring an unknown capability refuses writes while reads still succeed; checked by a
      real-store test exercising the write lock and a read command against the same store.
- [ ] A corrupt record raises rather than being treated as absent; checked by a malformed-record test.
baseline.summary: Register the multi-project-bridge store-compat capability (expand half)

# S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of `transport.py` (behaviour-preserving)

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260], whose plan hit BLOCK ten times. The round-by-round record is on that ticket; the structural finding is that it carried TWO independent changes — a mechanical relocation and a new 429 policy — and every round found new surface because a fix to one re-opened the other. Rounds 6-7 were about THIS half's mechanics; rounds 1, 4, 8, 9, 10 were about the policy half (now S2). Splitting is the same move that turned J9's eight BLOCKs into a first-try PASS as J10.

This story is the mechanical half and is **forced by the module-size cap, not by taste**: `transport.py` is **789 lines on `origin/main`** against the LOCKED 800-line cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so there are ELEVEN lines of headroom and the 429 policy cannot be added in place. (Recording the measurement because this file's LOC has been misquoted twice in epic e369: the earlier "792 vs 789" disagreement was a pre-/post-9263 base difference, and now that 9263 is merged both readings agree at 789.)

## Approach

**Relocate, do not redesign.** Move the retry/error cluster from `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` into a new `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`, changing no behaviour. The cluster is `_connection_retry_exceptions`, `_jira_http_error_types`, `_as_backend_http_error`, `TlsVerificationError`, `_tls_verification_error`, and `_with_connection_retry`.

**`TlsVerificationError` MUST move with the rest.** `_tls_verification_error` returns it, so leaving the class behind in `transport.py` makes `retry.py` import from `transport.py` while `transport.py` imports `_with_connection_retry` from `retry.py` — a circular import. The class and its factory are one unit.

**Re-export from `transport.py` so existing importers keep working.** `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` imports `TlsVerificationError` from the transport module; that test must pass UNEDITED, because editing it to chase the move would convert a regression signal into a rubber stamp.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — NEW; the moved cluster.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — cluster deleted,
  cluster imported, names re-exported.

**NOT in scope:** any behaviour change, and specifically any 429 / `Retry-After` handling — that is S2. If this story changes what any call does, it has failed.

## Testing

The oracle for a pure relocation is that the EXISTING suite passes unedited — a new test asserting the code moved would only restate the diff.

* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` DC transport tests pass with NO edits.
* `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes with NO edits (proves the re-export works).
* The module-size gate passes, and `transport.py` is measurably smaller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry.py` exists and contains all six named members, and `transport.py` no longer defines
      them
- [ ] `TlsVerificationError` lives in `retry.py` WITH `_tls_verification_error`, and a test or a
      clean `python -c "import ..."` proves there is no circular import between the two modules
- [ ] `transport.py` re-exports the moved names, and `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes
      **with zero edits to that file** — asserted by `git diff --exit-code` on it
- [ ] the full DC transport unit suite passes with zero test edits; if any test needed an edit,
      this story is not behaviour-preserving and must be reworked rather than the test adjusted
- [ ] `transport.py` is under the 800-line cap with headroom for S2, and the measured before/after
      line counts are recorded on this ticket
- [ ] NO diff hunk changes control flow, retry counts, backoff values, or exception types — a
      reviewer can confirm the change is a move by reading the diff alone
baseline.summary: S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of transport.py (behaviour-preserving)

With a key-set prev, keys present in both prev and curr route to `_compute_mutations_emit_both` with an empty `local_fields`, producing ~516 mutations per pass that are provably inert but not free. Skip them. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
Each inert mutation still traverses `_apply_one`, which calls `_recheck_drift` -> `concurrency.snapshot_head(repo_root)` — **a `git rev-parse` subprocess per mutation**. So ~516 extra git invocations per pass, ~516 `RECON: batch_outcome` stderr lines, ~516 outcome records in the manifest, and an inflated `mutation_count` so a converged pass reports 516 instead of 0. It also enlarges the HEAD-drift window. Under `BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` (cap 10) or `BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE` (cap 100) these compete for cap slots with genuine work (`apply_planning.py:90-101`) and can starve it — production defaults to `LIVE` (cap `None`), so that risk is latent, not live.

## Approach
Short-circuit `_compute_mutations_emit_both` when `local_fields` is falsy, or equivalently skip the `_emit` at `differ.py:590` when the resolved `changed` dict contains no field that survives `_mutation_to_batch_dict`. ~5 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With a key-set prev over a real corpus, `(outbound, update)` mutations with an empty effective
      payload are **0** (down from ~516). Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations` + the corpus script.
- [ ] Mutations with a genuine non-empty effective payload are still emitted unchanged — the
      negative control. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `mutation_count` on a converged pass is 0. Tier: **integration** asserting the pass record.
- [ ] `git rev-parse` invocation count per pass drops correspondingly. Tier: **integration** with a
      counting shim.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/differ.py`, tests

Scope: S. Depends on A4-2.

## Summary

The 2026-08-26 `rm -rf /*` incident came from an **ad-hoc, agent-authored mutation script** (`/tmp/mut.py`: `EP.write_text(orig.replace(old, new, 1))` then `subprocess.run([... pytest ...])`). It never touched `scripts/mutation_gate.py`.

`e668-b496-e264-4283` sandboxes the CI mutation gate. That is worth having, but it **does not cover the path the incident took**. The path the incident took is the defect-seeded mutation check that `rebar-debug` and `rebar-implement` instruct agents to perform as a routine part of TDD — and neither skill requires any sandbox.

## Evidence

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md:786` — *"perturb the fix with a
  **defect-seeded mutation** … confirm the held-out test returns to **RED**, then
  restore the fix."*
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md:291` — *"perturb the implementation
  … A test that stays green under mutation is a tautology."*
- `grep -rilE "sandbox-exec|bwrap|bubblewrap" examples/agent-skills/` returns
  **nothing**. No skill mentions an OS sandbox anywhere.

These skills are symlinked into `~/.claude/skills/`, so the rule ships to every operator who installs them.

## Why an inline invocation, not a dependency on the wrapper

The rule must not wait on `e668`'s `scripts/mutation_sandbox.py` landing: the skills are the live instruction agents follow today, and the exposure is present on every run until the rule exists. The skills therefore carry the sandbox invocation inline. A follow-on ticket adds a reusable CLI wrapper and can simplify the skill text later.

## The invocations, in full

Both were measured today, not composed from memory.

**macOS** — the profile is written by the snippet itself, so nothing external is referenced. Verified on macOS 26.5.2: a write outside `$SBX` was denied (`Operation not permitted`, file absent), a write inside succeeded, and `rm -rf <protected>/*` was denied with the target surviving.

```sh
SBX="$(mktemp -d)"
cat > "$SBX/p.sb" <<EOF
(version 1)
(allow default)
(deny file-write*)
(allow file-write*
  (subpath "$PWD")
  (subpath "$SBX")
  (literal "/dev/null") (literal "/dev/stdout") (literal "/dev/stderr"))
EOF
sandbox-exec -f "$SBX/p.sb" <your mutation test command>
```

**Linux** — verified in an `ubuntu:24.04` container: the write inside the bind succeeded and a write outside failed with `Read-only file system`.

```sh
bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --bind "$PWD" "$PWD" -- <your mutation test command>
```

`bwrap` presence on PATH is NOT capability: Ubuntu 23.10+ restricts unprivileged user namespaces via AppArmor, so an installed `bwrap` can fail with "Creating new namespace failed". Confirm it works first:

```sh
bwrap --ro-bind / / -- /bin/true || echo "bwrap cannot namespace here"
```

## When no sandbox is available

Neither mechanism present, or `bwrap` present but unable to namespace: **do not run the mutation step against code that performs real filesystem deletion, and do not proceed unsandboxed.** Assert on an injected seam instead — point the deletion at a stub that records its argv and assert on what *would* have been deleted. That is a strictly better oracle than observing a wiped directory, and it needs no sandbox.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both `rebar-debug` and `rebar-implement` require any step that perturbs code and
      then executes tests to run inside an OS sandbox denying writes outside the
      worktree and a scratch dir. Verified by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_skill_mutation_sandbox_rule.py`.
- [x] Each skill carries the **complete, self-contained** macOS snippet above,
      including the heredoc that writes the profile — no reference to a profile file
      whose provenance or content is unstated. Verified by the test asserting the
      `(deny file-write*)` and `sandbox-exec -f` literals are present in both files.
- [x] Each skill carries the **complete** Linux `bwrap` invocation above, including
      `--ro-bind / /`, `--dev`, `--proc` and the `--bind "$PWD" "$PWD"` pair — not an
      abbreviated fragment. Verified by the same test.
- [x] Each skill states that `bwrap` on PATH is not capability, and gives the
      `bwrap --ro-bind / / -- /bin/true` capability probe. Verified by the same test.
- [x] Each skill specifies the **no-sandbox fallback**: assert on an injected seam,
      never proceed unsandboxed. Verified by the same test.
- [x] Each skill states that a seeded defect is arbitrary code, so the run executes
      hostile code — with the 2026-08-26 outcome as the reason. Verified by the test.
- [x] A regression test fails if either skill loses the requirement. Verified by
      removing it from one skill and observing RED.
- [x] No existing guidance is weakened: RED-first, held-out-oracle and mutation-teeth
      discipline unchanged; the sandbox is added around them. Verified by diff review.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_skill_mutation_sandbox_rule.py` — both skills carry the
  requirement, both platform invocations, and the hostile-code framing; the test goes
  RED when the rule is removed from either file.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — green.
- `python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` — the skills still parse (Copilot CLI
  silently drops a skill whose frontmatter fails).

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion above is checked by the command it names.
- The regression test is proven RED by removing the rule, then restored.

## Notes

Filed after the operator asked whether the skills needed updating — they did, and this is the gap `e668` left open. Sibling: `e668-b496-e264-4283` (CI gate sandbox). Follow-on: a reusable `scripts/mutation_sandbox.py` CLI wrapper, which stacks on `e668` and can then replace the inline invocation in the skill text.
baseline.summary: Require an OS sandbox for defect-seeded mutation runs in the TDD skills

## Summary
The MCP blue-green autodeploy emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {reason: deploy_failed}` (→ `rebar/host:deploy_errors`, which pages the `rebar-autodeploy-errors` alarm) on TWO conditions that are *documented as routine, non-error backoffs that must be kept OUT of deploy_errors*: `port-exhausted` (retire-cap) and low-memory abort. This false-pages the general "deploys are failing" alarm during a normal landing burst, when the deploy is in fact correctly, safely deferring.

## Evidence (live, 2026-08-30 ~03:33–04:05 UTC on i-00880b2c7f13527c5)
During a burst of merges, both blue/green MCP ports (8092/8093) were held by un-reaped containers still in their 21-min graceful drain (`docker stop --time 1260`). Each deploy tick logged BOTH markers for the same event:
```
AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP {reason: port-exhausted, ...}
AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {reason: deploy_failed, detail: component=mcp target=... fail#1..4 backoff=60s..480s}
```
`rebar-autodeploy-errors` (deploy_errors, Sum>0 / 4 periods) and `rebar-autodeploy-mcp-retire-cap` BOTH went ALARM. It self-resolved (~04:15). No outage — MCP served the old build throughout; only the cutover was delayed.

## Root cause
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`: `record_mcp_backoff_failure` (~L668) calls `err deploy_failed "component=mcp ..."` → emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` → inflates `deploy_errors`. It is invoked on the two routine backoff paths — low-mem abort (~L915, after `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT`) and port-exhausted (~L924, after `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`). This contradicts the documented contract in `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (~L284-291, L355): the retire-cap and mem-abort markers are "each kept out of AUTODEPLOY_ERROR so a routine retire-cap / memory abort never inflates deploy_errors." The sustained case is already covered by the dedicated `mcp_retire_cap` / `mcp_mem_abort` alarms. Introduced by the blue-green commit `2a0a4b19f2ab` (ticket 6964), which shipped both the contract and the violating code — an internally-inconsistent plan (`plan_defect`).

## Standing intent — this is a fix, not a behavior decision
The intended behavior is documented in observability.sh. The code simply doesn't match it. No ADR / design decision required.

## Fix
Factor the backoff-timer bookkeeping (write `$MCP_BACKOFF_FILE` + prune) out of the `err deploy_failed` emission via a shared `schedule_mcp_backoff` helper. Add a `record_mcp_routine_backoff` variant (schedule + log, no `err deploy_failed`) and switch the two routine paths to it. Genuine-failure paths (build/tag/run/unhealthy/handshake/flip) keep `record_mcp_backoff_failure` and still page. The throttle still applies on all paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A routine `port-exhausted` (retire-cap) backoff does NOT emit `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/deploy_failed` and does NOT increment `deploy_errors`; the `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` marker + `mcp_retire_cap` metric remain the signal.
- [ ] A routine low-memory abort likewise does NOT inflate `deploy_errors`; `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` + `mcp_mem_abort` remain the signal.
- [ ] GENUINE MCP deploy failures (build-failed, tag-failed, run-failed, unhealthy, handshake, flip) STILL emit `deploy_failed` and page `deploy_errors` (no regression to real-failure alarming).
- [ ] The mcp backoff throttle (timer/prune) still applies on the routine paths so ticks don't hammer during a drain — only the erroneous deploy_errors emission is removed (the `mcp-deploy-backoff` file is still written).
- [ ] A regression test asserts the observable outcome: the retire-cap/mem-abort paths emit their own marker but NOT `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`, while a real failure emits `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — includes new `test_port_exhausted_routine_backoff_does_not_inflate_deploy_errors` and `test_low_memory_routine_backoff_does_not_inflate_deploy_errors` (assert routine marker present, no `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/deploy_failed`, throttle file still written), plus existing `test_mcp_failure_keeps_the_deploy_failed_metric_and_names_the_component` and `test_unhealthy_new_container_leaves_old_upstream_current` (genuine failures still emit `deploy_failed`).
- Verified: `make lint` (shellcheck), `make typecheck`, `make test` all green. Mutation check: reintroducing `record_mcp_backoff_failure` on the routine sites returns both new tests to RED.

## Notes
Checked for duplication against the blue-green target ticket (6964) and the graceful-drain-contract bug (b580) — not duplicates. The plan-review overlap detector flags shared artifact `record_mcp_backoff_failure` with e1d9 (handshake gate, already landed in origin/main) and the held-back sibling `prespinal-gem-kinkajou` (dbf0); this change edits disjoint lines (function def + the two routine call sites) and lands first in the autodeploy.sh cluster.
baseline.summary: Autodeploy MCP routine backoff (retire-cap port-exhausted / mem-abort) inflates deploy_errors, false-paging the general deploy alarm

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A rebar ticket carries no record of which tracker project it syncs into, nor which repos it belongs to. The current ticket state fields are seeded in `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:29-81` and declared in `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`; neither includes a project. Today the project is only implicit — recoverable from a bound issue's key prefix in `bindings.json`, and absent entirely for a ticket that has never been bound. Epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336` needs it explicit, because a ticket that is deliberately not synced has no binding to infer from.

## Approach

Add two ticket state fields together, in one edit set: `bridge_project` (string) and `repos` (list of strings). They are one story rather than two because a field is not usable without its write path, and splitting them would put two children on `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`.

`bridge_project` is **tri-state**, mirroring the established `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths pattern (`docs/ticket-model.md:210-212`): absent means legacy, an explicit empty string means never sync, and a key means sync there. The three states are distinguished so a pre-feature store is not read as "every ticket is unsynced". Resolution of the absent state is not implemented here — it belongs to `resolve_project` in the mapping module.

Both fields are written into the CREATE event data by `create_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:169-220`), projected by the reducer, and seeded in `make_initial_state`. Create-time arguments `--bridge-project` and `--repos` are added to all three write surfaces — CLI (`composer.create_cli`), library (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:79-135`), and MCP (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:47-70`). Note the CLI flag loop rejects unknown options strictly (`composer.py:287-291`), so the new flags must be registered there or they are hard errors.

`bridge_project` is **promote-only**: setting it on a ticket with no binding is allowed, changing it on a ticket that already holds one is refused. That keeps the change free of any issue-move or unbind/rebind machinery. `repos` stays freely editable — it never reaches the tracker, so there is no binding to invalidate.

No schema version bump: `docs/event-schema.md:124-150` states additive fields on an existing event type do not require one. Types are generated from the schemas (`reducer/_state.py:11-13`), so the generator is re-run.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard: a producer/consumer contract test for the event→state path (real CREATE event fed through the real reducer, no stubbing), plus a real CLI subprocess test for the argument parsing, since the strict unknown-option rejection is itself part of the mechanism.

- Happy path: `create task "t" --bridge-project REB --repos rebar,api` produces a ticket whose state
  shows `bridge_project == "REB"` and `repos == ["rebar", "api"]` after a full replay.
- Three-state coverage: a ticket created without the flag replays with the field **absent**; one
  created with an explicit empty value replays with `""`. These must be distinguishable — asserting
  the absent case is not merely falsy is the point of the test.
- Cross-surface parity: the same ticket shape results from the CLI, the library, and MCP.
- Failure path: an edit setting `bridge_project` on a ticket that already holds a binding is refused
  with a non-zero exit and the stored value is unchanged; the same edit on an unbound ticket succeeds.
- Collateral invariant: replaying a ticket created before this change yields identical state apart
  from the two new keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge_project` and `repos` are declared in the ticket state schema, seeded in
      `make_initial_state`, and projected by the reducer; checked by a replay test asserting both on
      a freshly created ticket.
- [ ] `--bridge-project` and `--repos` exist on the CLI, library and MCP create paths and produce
      identical state; checked by a per-surface test comparing the resulting ticket state.
- [ ] The absent, explicit-empty, and set states are distinguishable after replay; checked by a
      parameterized test asserting each of the three separately.
- [ ] Setting `bridge_project` on a bound ticket is refused while setting it on an unbound ticket
      succeeds; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [ ] A ticket created before this change replays to the same state apart from the new keys; checked
      by a fixture-based regression test.

# BUG: code-review vote renders a fail-closed DET detector match as "BLOCK — finding / 0 blocking issues"

## Reproduction Steps
1. Push a change touching a file that a fail-closed DET detector (gitleaks secret-detection) matches on.
2. The 4-pass LLM gate returns PASS (no LLM blocking findings), but apply_failclosed forces BLOCK.
3. The Gerrit vote is LLM-Review-1 tagged "[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]" with message "rebar code review found 0 blocking issue(s):" — and NO robot comment names the match.

Root cause: src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:123-151 apply_failclosed sets
verdict["verdict"]="BLOCK" on a match but never appends the match to verdict["blocking"]
(it only records it under coverage.security_detectors). review_bot/adapter.py then counts
len(verdict["blocking"])==0 and renders "found 0 blocking issue(s)"; adapter.py:183-191 tags
it "finding". voter.py posts only the message. So a genuine detector block is unnamed and
non-actionable — and a REAL leaked secret is hidden from the author identically.

Expected: a fail-closed detector match is surfaced as a named, counted blocking finding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] apply_failclosed appends a kernel-shaped finding (criterion + file + remediation hint) to verdict["blocking"] when blocking_enabled and there is a match; the finalize invariant holds.
- [ ] Gerrit message reads "found N blocking issue(s):" (N>=1) and names the match; review_code CLI/MCP render it too.
- [ ] RED-first regression tests: test_failclosed_forces_block_on_detector_match asserts verdict["blocking"] non-empty + names the criterion; an adapter-seam test asserts the message never reads "found 0".
- [ ] make lint + code-review suites green; commit carries a rebar-ticket trailer.
baseline.summary: BUG: code-review vote renders a DET detector match as 'BLOCK — finding / 0 blocking issues'
