## Why

Surfaced by the plan-v4 divergence-grading calibration (story doggish-nonorganic-tsetsefly), from the same plan-v3 sidecar corpus (18,085 verified findings).

`undecomposed` fires on **12 of 18,085 findings (0.07%)** — two orders of magnitude below every other axis — while holding full HARD-OVERRIDE power (any non-none grade floors impact at 0.85 and auto-blocks). Comparison across the seven axes on plan-v3:

| axis | non-none |
|---|---|
| vague_directive | 31.03% |
| ac_unverifiable | 15.79% |
| internal_conflict | 10.17% |
| divergent_implementation | 7.72% (fixed in plan-v4) |
| dod_uncertifiable | 5.36% |
| irreversible_without_rationale | 1.97% |
| **undecomposed** | **0.07%** |

Two candidate explanations, both worth confirming before touching anything:

1. **Working as intended / correctly suppressed.** The axis's own prompt text says a deterministic
   signal (G5) already suppresses false 'flat plan' findings on tickets that HAVE children, and
   most reviewed tickets do have children. If so, 0.07% is the correct residual and the axis
   simply has a narrow true population — no change needed, just documentation.
2. **Mis-specified / unreachable.** The grading instruction may be so hedged ('Grade ONLY a
   genuine gap') that verifiers never assign it, in which case a real class of flat-plan defects
   is scoring 0.0 the same way the divergence class did before plan-v4.

## What

Investigate, do not pre-commit to a fix:

- Pull the 12 firing findings from the corpus and read them — are they genuine flat-plan defects,
  and did they block?
- Determine how often the G5 deterministic suppressor fires, to separate 'correctly suppressed'
  from 'never assigned'.
- Look for the inverse population: findings whose TEXT describes an undecomposed/flat plan but
  which scored the axis `none` (the same ~90%-missed analysis that motivated plan-v4's
  divergence grading).
- Only if (2) is confirmed, propose a change — and note that any impact-model shape change costs
  an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump that closes the plan-v4 cohort, so batch it per ADR 0054 §4.

## Testing / Verification

This is an analysis ticket: the deliverable is a recorded finding, so verification is read-only replay over the persisted sidecar corpus plus source reads. No code changes, no new eval suite, no bulk re-review sweep (ADR 0054 §4).

- Locate the corpus and count its records with an asserting command, e.g.
  `test -n "$(find .rebar -name '*sidecar*' -o -name '*.jsonl')" && echo CORPUS_PRESENT || echo CORPUS_ABSENT`,
  then a `python3 -c` record count over whatever sidecar/journal path is found. If no corpus is
  reachable from this checkout, that absence is itself recorded as a limit and the analysis is
  scoped to source-level evidence.
- Read the axis definition and the G5 suppressor at source:
  `rg -n 'undecomposed|G5' src/rebar/llm/` — the root must be `src/rebar/llm/`, not
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`, because `decide.py` and `verify_models.py` live under the
  sibling `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`. Files to read: `plan_review/det_floor.py`,
  `plan_review/det_lint.py`, `plan_review/pass1.py`, `review_kernel/decide.py`,
  `review_kernel/verify_models.py`, and the two reviewer prompts.
- Distinguish the TWO separate 'undecomposed' mechanisms before measuring anything: (a) the
  PASS-1 finder-side deterministic veto `veto_undecomposed_g5` (`plan_review/det_lint.py`,
  invoked from `plan_review/pass1.py`), which suppresses G5-criterion FINDER findings on tickets
  that have children; and (b) the review_kernel VERIFIER severity axis `undecomposed`
  (`review_kernel/verify_models.py`) whose non-none grade is floored to 0.85 in
  `review_kernel/decide.py`. The 12/18,085 statistic is about (b). If the sidecar corpus does not
  co-record a per-finding G5/has-children signal alongside the verifier axis grade, record that
  as a limit rather than reporting a suppression rate for a mechanism that does not gate the axis.
- Replay the corpus (or the reachable substitute) with a read-only `python3` script that
  tabulates: per-finding `undecomposed` grades, the G5/has-children signal state where recorded,
  and the text-match inverse population. Zero LLM calls.
- Inverse-population match rule (stated, not deferred): case-insensitive regex over each
  finding's `finding` / `evidence` / `suggested_fix` text for
  `undecomposed|flat plan|monolith|not decomposed|no subtasks|no children|single (giant |large )?step|should be (split|broken|decomposed)`;
  report the count of matching findings whose `undecomposed` axis grade is `none`.
- Checked by inspection: the resulting comment on this ticket contains the three readouts named
  in the acceptance criteria below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A comment on this ticket reports the 12 firing findings (criteria, decision, whether the
      floor was load-bearing) and the measured G5 suppression rate — or, if the corpus is not
      reachable from this checkout, states that plainly and reports the equivalent readout from
      the evidence that IS reachable. Verified: run `rebar show f391-5a20-4593-4405 --no-pull`
      and confirm the comment exists and cites per-finding ids (or names the missing corpus).
- [x] The comment states which explanation the evidence supports (correct-residual vs
      mis-specified) with the counts backing it, and either (a) records 'no change needed' with the
      rationale, or (b) links a follow-up story scoped to the fix. Verified: checked by reading the
      comment in `rebar show f391-5a20-4593-4405 --no-pull` — exactly one of the two outcomes is
      explicitly recorded.
- [x] A comment reports the inverse population: the count of findings whose text matches the
      flat/undecomposed regex stated in Testing but whose `undecomposed` axis grade is `none`,
      together with the match rule used and a sample of matched finding ids — or, if the corpus is
      unreachable, an explicit statement of that with the substitute evidence used. Verified:
      checked by reading the comment in `rebar show f391-5a20-4593-4405 --no-pull` for a stated
      count (or explicit unreachable statement) and the match rule.
- [x] Method is ADR-0054-compliant: driven off the persisted sidecar corpus at zero marginal LLM
      cost — no purpose-built eval suite and no bulk re-review sweep. Verified: checked by reading
      the comment's Method section, which names the corpus path + replay script as its instrument,
      and by confirming `git status --porcelain src/ tests/` is clean (no code or eval-suite
      changes were made for this ticket).

## Notes

Analysis-only ticket; it may legitimately close with 'the axis is fine, here is why'.

# live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap

## Context / Problem

The live Jira DC harness tier dies at SETUP, so no live acceptance evidence can be produced at all — and every remaining story in epic e369 (notably J11, the epic's headline live proof) runs on this harness. Reproduced across two independent CI runs (30604756524, 30623000498), same signature:

    ERROR at setup of test_add_label_and_the_links_surface_against_a_real_instance
    AssertionError: PAT creation failed: 403
      {'exception': 'com.atlassian.pats.exception.UserTokenLimitExceededException',
       'error': "You can't create more than 10 tokens."}

`jira_dc_pat` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:355`) is declared `@pytest.fixture` with NO scope, so it is FUNCTION-scoped: every test that requests it mints a brand new Personal Access Token via `POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens` and never deletes it. Jira Data Center caps a user at 10 PATs. Consumption therefore grows as O(tests) while the budget is fixed at 10.

Two properties make this expensive to diagnose, and both are reasons to fix it properly rather than by trimming test count:

* **It mis-attributes.** The ERROR surfaces at setup of a test in `test_transport.py` — a module
  nobody touched — because that is merely the test that happened to run once the budget was
  spent. The cause is session-wide.
* **It looks flaky but is deterministic.** The fixture mints with `expirationDuration=1`, so
  tokens self-clear after a day. Whether a run fails depends on how recently the instance was
  used, not on chance.

## Approach

**Make `jira_dc_pat` SESSION-scoped**, turning PAT consumption from O(tests) into O(1).

This is the fix that scales, and scaling is the actual requirement: J11 adds substantially more live tests to this tier, so any fix whose budget is still proportional to test count merely moves the cliff. Every consumer needs only *a* valid PAT — no test in this tier asserts per-token behaviour (verified: the fixture's only assertions are on `rawToken`, and its sole consumers use it as a bearer credential) — so one token per run is behaviourally identical to one per test.

**Rejected: per-test teardown via `DELETE /rest/pat/latest/tokens/{id}`.** It preserves per-test isolation that nothing here needs, costs an API call per test, and — decisively — it is not verified to be implementable: the creation response is only asserted to carry `rawToken`, and whether it also returns an `id` has NOT been confirmed against a live instance. Choosing it would make the fix depend on an unverified response field. Session scope depends on nothing new.

**Complementary: sweep leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` tokens at session start**, mirroring `_leaked_scratch_projects()` (`conftest.py:181`), which already does exactly this for scratch PROJECTS left by interrupted runs. Session scope alone fixes consumption WITHIN a run; it does not help a run that starts against an instance already holding 10 tokens from a crashed predecessor. Both layers are required for the ACs below, and they address different failures.

The sweep uses the same defensive posture the project fixture already establishes: read the token list from its direct REST endpoint and, if it cannot be enumerated, **return empty rather than invent a failure** — a sweep that cannot see is not evidence of cleanliness, and the harness-readiness assertion remains authoritative for usability. Deleting a leftover token is likewise best-effort: a failed delete is reported, not fatal, because the session-scoped mint that follows is the real test of whether headroom exists.

**Raw `urllib` REST is correct here and is not a divergence from "never hand-roll REST".** That rule governs the DC *transport*, which must go through `pycontribs/jira`. This conftest deliberately speaks raw REST v2 with stdlib `urllib` only (see its module docstring) so the harness does not depend on the client library the harness exists to validate. The sweep reuses the existing `_request` helper.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` — change `jira_dc_pat` to `scope="session"`,
  document the 10-token cap in its docstring, and add a `_leaked_harness_tokens()` helper plus
  its invocation from the existing session-scoped `_jira_dc_harness_ready` autouse fixture.
- `tests/unit/` — unit coverage for the sweep helper's parsing and its
  cannot-enumerate/failed-delete degradation, exercised against a stubbed `_request` so it runs
  in the normal (non-live) tier.

No production `src/rebar` code changes: this is a test-harness defect.

## Testing

The live tier cannot run on this workstation (its base image is linux/amd64 only and this is Apple Silicon — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:54-73`), so the split is deliberate:

* **Unit (runs everywhere, in CI on every change):** the sweep helper returns the leftover
  token names/ids from a well-formed list response; returns EMPTY when the endpoint errors or
  returns a non-list (the cannot-enumerate path); ignores tokens not carrying the
  `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix (so it never deletes a human's unrelated PAT — the failure mode
  that would make this fix worse than the bug); and does not raise when a DELETE fails.
* **Live (GitHub Actions `jira DC harness smoke` job):** the acceptance evidence. The full
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite completes with no `UserTokenLimitExceededException`.
  Because session scope makes consumption O(1), one token is consumed regardless of test count,
  which is what supplies headroom rather than a coincidence of the current count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `jira_dc_pat` is `scope="session"`, verified by reading the fixture declaration, so a run
      mints exactly ONE PAT no matter how many tests request it
- [ ] the full `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite runs in the GitHub Actions
      `jira DC harness smoke` job with ZERO `UserTokenLimitExceededException`, confirmed by
      reading that job's log — not the overall run status
- [ ] headroom is structural, not coincidental: because consumption is O(1) in test count, the
      run above passes with MORE live tests present than the count that first triggered the cap
- [ ] a leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` token from a crashed run is deleted at session start, so
      it does not break the next run — covered by a unit test against a stubbed `_request`
- [ ] the sweep never deletes a token lacking the `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix, asserted by unit
      test
- [ ] the sweep degrades safely: a non-200/non-list list response yields an empty result rather
      than an exception, and a failed DELETE does not abort the session — both unit-tested
- [ ] the 10-token cap and the session-scope decision are documented in the `jira_dc_pat`
      docstring, since the cap is a non-obvious Jira DC limit
baseline.summary: live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap; jira_dc_pat is function-scoped

baseline.description:
## Summary

Subagents investigating timing-dependent test failures spawn CPU saturation workers (`python -c "while True: pass"`) to reproduce failures under load. Nothing bounds their lifetime or reaps them. On this host **38 such workers** spawned in a single batch on **2026-08-22 10:02:11**, orphaned to PID 1, and ran continuously for **four days** at ~**1341% combined CPU** until manually killed on 2026-08-26.

## Evidence (observed 2026-08-26)

- 38 processes matching `python -c "\nwhile True: pass\n"`, each ~35–45% CPU.
- Every one had **PPID 1** — the spawning harness exited without reaping them.
- All shared start timestamp `Aug 22 10:02:11` — one batch, never cleaned up.
- Combined CPU 1341% on an 18-core host with only **6 performance cores**.
- Contributed to a load average of **58.49**; after `pkill -f 'while True: pass'`
  load fell to 26 and then to ~10.
- Applications could not launch while this was running (dock bounce, no window).
  Killing the workers restored launch.

## Provenance — which sessions, and why

Traced to three Claude Code sessions' subagent transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/-Users-joeoakhart-rebar/`. Their own task descriptions state the intent:

| Session | Recorded task description |
|---|---|
| `e50ec61e-3a77-4eb8-b56b-c1d0f90ff9bc` | "Reproduce crash on pristine main under saturating load"; "Run crashing tests under CPU pressure with repo ini budget" |
| `6f8df6b5-44f6-4ea4-b224-1eac4c95b0a7` | "Measure test runtime unloaded"; "Measure runtime under CPU pressure" |
| `eff19c3d-071a-47b5-bae6-8b48a3343a8c` | "Watch socket + CPU time over 50s"; "Per-thread CPU and leaf summary" |

This lines up with the `debug-ci-timeout` and `debug/ci-hang-99pct` worktrees. Saturating the CPU to reproduce a timing-dependent failure is a legitimate technique — the defect is that the workers outlive the investigation.

`while True: pass` appears **nowhere in the rebar codebase** (verified by grep over `*.py`/`*.sh`/`*.md`). These were ad-hoc `python -c` invocations, so no repo-side fixture is responsible and no repo-side change alone can prevent recurrence.

## Why it went unnoticed

- The workers are `nice`d (`RN`/`SN` state), so they yield rather than freeze the
  UI outright. Degradation is gradual and reads as "the machine feels slow."
- PPID-1 orphans have no session affinity — nothing associates them with the
  finished investigation that created them.
- No sweep exists for long-lived compute processes with no parent.

## Impact

- Four days of a workstation running at ~3x oversubscription.
- Compounded with an unrelated `fseventsd` blowup (see related ticket) to exhaust
  swap and block application launch entirely.
- Any timing-sensitive test run during that window produced unreliable results —
  including, plausibly, the CI-timing investigations that spawned the load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Agent guidance (`AGENTS.md`) states that any background load generator or
      long-running helper a subagent spawns must be bounded in wall-clock time AT
      SPAWN, not merely killed at the end. Verified by the text being present in
      `AGENTS.md`.
- [x] The guidance gives a copy-pasteable bounded pattern (for example
      `timeout 120 python -c '...' &`) and a process-group teardown
      (`trap 'kill 0' EXIT INT TERM`), with one line on why an unbounded loop
      outlives harness death. Verified by those literals appearing in `AGENTS.md`.
- [x] The guidance forbids leaving PPID-1 orphans: a subagent reaps what it spawned
      before returning, including on error paths. Verified by the text in `AGENTS.md`.
- [x] A detection check reports compute processes whose parent is PID 1 and whose
      accumulated CPU time exceeds **3600 CPU-seconds by default**, overridable via a
      `--min-cpu-seconds` argument. 3600 is chosen because the leaked generators had
      accumulated roughly 138,000 CPU-seconds (38 processes x ~40% CPU x 4 days) while
      a legitimate orphan rarely passes an hour of CPU. Runnable on demand as a plain
      command with no dependency on any CI provider (`project.portability`). Verified
      by `python scripts/check_orphaned_load.py --help` exiting 0.
- [x] The check flags a bounded decoy process it is given and does NOT flag a
      normally-parented process. Verified by
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_check_orphaned_load.py`.
- [x] The check's process-inspection seam is injectable so the test never depends on
      real system process state or on spawning a real long-lived CPU burner. Spawning
      a real unbounded CPU burner in a test would reproduce the very defect this
      ticket tracks. Verified by the same test module passing deterministically.
- [x] The real (non-injected) adapter is exercised at least once against live process
      state in a READ-ONLY smoke assertion — it returns a list without raising, and
      the current process is not reported. This covers the parsing path the injected
      seam bypasses. Verified by that test in the same module.
- [x] An operator note documents how to reclaim an already-leaked batch
      (`pkill -f 'while True: pass'` cleared this host's 38), and where the guidance
      lives. Verified by the note being present in `AGENTS.md`.
- [x] System-owned executables are excluded by default, with `--include-system` to
      opt back in. Measured on the affected host: PPID-1 processes above the threshold
      total **33**, of which **29 are launchd-managed system daemons** (WindowServer at
      111.6h, the Virtualization VM at 86.7h, JamfDaemon, Terminal). Every launchd
      daemon has PPID 1, so the unfiltered contract is structurally noisy on macOS and
      a report of 33 legitimate daemons would be ignored — meaning it would not have
      surfaced this incident either. Excluding system paths leaves **4**, one of which
      is a real orphaned agent-job script
      (`/bin/bash ~/.claude/jobs/*/tmp/watch-tracker.sh`, 3.0h). Verified by a test
      asserting a system-path record is filtered by default and reported under
      `--include-system`.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_check_orphaned_load.py` — the check flags an orphaned
  high-CPU process, ignores a normally-parented one, ignores a short-lived orphan
  below the CPU threshold, and honours the threshold argument.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — green.
- `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` and
  `python scripts/check_import_walk.py` — green.

## Definition of Done

- Guidance merged in the canonical agent file, not only in a machine-local note.
- Detection check implemented and covered by the test in AC 5.
- A short operator note on reclaiming an already-leaked batch
  (`pkill -f 'while True: pass'` was sufficient here, but the general form should be
  documented).

## Notes

Found while triaging a host-wide starvation incident. Two independent resource leaks — this one and unbounded gate-snapshot accumulation driving `fseventsd` — compounded to make the machine unusable. They are separate defects with separate fixes; this ticket tracks the orphaned-load-generator half.

Remediation already applied on this host: `pkill -f 'while True: pass'` (38 killed, 0 remaining, load 58 -> 10). Nothing respawns them; the batch was a one-time leak.
baseline.summary: Agent-spawned CPU load generators leak as PPID-1 orphans and run unbounded for days

## Context / Problem

This store's enrichment queue holds **898 pending entries across 4,903 tickets** (measured 2026-08-21). `enrich_drain.drain` processes at most `overlap_drain_batch` (default 5) SUCCESSES per run, and `overlap.queue.pending_enrichment` returns ids **sorted**, so each run works a fixed prefix of the same sorted list. Entries late in sort order are reached only once everything ahead of them drains.

Two consequences, both observable today:

**1. Late-sorted entries starve.** The three tickets from bug `569c-931f-69a2-4c1d` sit at sorted indices **458 / 499 / 786**. Even with that bug fixed — their prompts now bound correctly and they enrich in ~8 s against the real provider — they will not reach `done` until the ~458-deep backlog ahead of them clears.

**2. The O(1) gate marker can never engage, so every store write pays a full scan.** `pending_enrichment` clears the gate marker whenever it finds anything pending (`queue.py:374-375`). With 898 entries permanently pending, the marker is cleared on every probe, `958e-f4b3-275c-4154`'s fast path is unreachable on this store, and ordinary writes log:

```
WARNING rebar.llm.enrich_drain: enrich drain gate check took ~900-1200 ms (> 20 ms budget)
```

That warning fires on essentially **100% of writes** here. It is frequently misattributed to whichever enrichment bug is currently open; the actual dominant cause is the backlog depth.

## Open questions for whoever claims this
- Is 898 a transient backlog draining down after bug `3198-438c-72a5-470f` (detached drain
  children dying at `getcwd()`) was fixed, or is enqueue outpacing a 5-per-write drain?
  Measure the trend before changing anything.
- If it is steady-state, the batch cap and/or the sorted iteration order are the levers:
  sorted order makes starvation deterministic rather than fair. Oldest-`not_before_ns` first,
  or a rotating start offset, would at least make it uniform.
- Should the gate marker record "nothing pending BEFORE index N" rather than being all-or-
  nothing, so a deep backlog does not permanently disable the fast path?

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The backlog trend is measured and reported (draining vs steady-state vs growing).
- [x] No queue entry can be starved indefinitely by sort position while other entries drain.
- [x] On a store with a deep backlog, the write-path gate check is back inside its budget (or
      the budget/warning is re-justified for that regime).
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while debugging `569c-931f-69a2-4c1d`. It was tested and REJECTED as that bug's root cause — the three entries were observed being claimed and failing the provider 400 on demand, which starvation alone cannot explain — but it is a real independent problem, and it is the reason that bug's AC3 ("the three entries reach `done` on this store") is not satisfied by that bug's fix alone.
baseline.summary: deep enrichment backlog starves late entries

# Hard-remove the deprecated `resolved_statuses` config keys

Removal half of task [rebar:549c-032f-6cb0-4258], which decided DEPRECATE-not-remove and executed the deprecation half (change 1670). It was blocked on operator sign-off because removing a documented operator-facing config key is a user-visible surface change.

**OPERATOR SIGN-OFF IS GIVEN** (2026-08-12, verbatim: "delete the old config settings is approved"; provenance recorded in the first comment on this ticket). This is the fourth change of the pre-1.0 breaking window that also landed tickets 97d4 and 6cc4.

## Background

`jira.resolved_statuses` fed the inbound absence probe (`adapters/jira/probe.py:: _resolve_resolved_statuses`), reachable as recently as shipped v0.10.1; the probe went with task f020 and 549c removed the write-only transport plumbing. Both keys are now **inert** — accepted, coerced and validated, read by nothing. Resolved/unresolved discrimination is outbound-owned (ADR 0028), so there is **no replacement setting**: operators simply delete the line.

## Plan (line numbers against origin/main @ abf3817187)

### 1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — delete the fields and coercers

* Delete `ReconcilerConfig.resolved_statuses` (L465) with its 5-line DEPRECATED comment
  block and `# read-via:` marker (L460-464).
* Delete `JiraConfig.resolved_statuses` (L489) with its 5-line comment block and
  `# read-via:` marker (L484-488).
* Delete the two `_as_str_list` coercer entries: `reconciler` section L696, `jira`
  section L706.
* Check `_as_str_list` for other callers; if this removes its last one, delete the helper
  too rather than leave a dead coercer.

### 2. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — swap deprecation rows for tombstones

* Delete the two `_scheduled("cfg", …)` rows (L106-107) and the 549c comment block that
  introduces them (L91-105).
* Append a historical NOTE in the "removed scheduled surfaces" block recording
  **operator-approved removal, 2026-08-12**, matching the wording pattern of the
  neighbouring 97d4 / 6cc4 NOTEs.
* Add to `_TOMBSTONE_REGISTRY`, in the existing `cfg, warn` group:
  `_tomb("cfg", "jira.resolved_statuses", "", "warn")` and
  `_tomb("cfg", "reconciler.resolved_statuses", "", "warn")`.
* Add the auto-derived env twins to the `env, warn` group:
  `_tomb("env", "REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES", "", "warn")` and
  `_tomb("env", "REBAR_RECONCILER_RESOLVED_STATUSES", "", "warn")` — env names derive
  generically as `REBAR_<SECTION>_<KEY>` (config.py L273), so both were real usable inputs.
  This follows the `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` precedent.

**Tombstone class is `warn`, deliberately.** `_deprecations.py` codifies the rule: `error` for an operationally load-bearing removed input (store location, write/sync gate, auth, security, lifecycle policy), `warn` for an inert one. These keys are inert — nothing reads them and the behaviour they configured no longer exists — so a still-set key must not abort the command. This matches every comparable cfg precedent (`code_health.enabled`, `code_health.analyzers`, `reconciler.lock_backend`, `reconciler.lock_max_retries`). It deliberately does NOT follow 6cc4's `error` choice for `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`, whose stated rationale — "silently ignoring a still-set model id would quietly change which model every operation runs" — is a load-bearing argument that does not transfer to an inert key.

### 3. Tests

* `tests/unit/test_config_resolved_statuses_deprecation.py` — the whole module asserts the
  deprecation semantics that no longer exist. Replace it with a removal module (mirroring
  6cc4's `test_llm_model_env_deprecation.py` -> `test_llm_model_env_removal.py` rename)
  asserting: the fields are gone from both dataclasses; a config still carrying either key
  loads and warns rather than raising; the key is dropped from the parsed config; and the
  env twins warn.
* `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py` L318-331 — the docstring and the
  `assert all("resolved_statuses" in r for r in reports)` assertion both encode the
  now-deleted `# read-via:` markers. Retarget to whatever the config-read gate reports once
  the markers are gone (expected: an empty report for these keys).
* `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py` L41 — comment references the 549c rows; update.

### 4. Docs

* `docs/config.md` — delete the `resolved_statuses` line (L285) and its 9-line DEPRECATED
  comment block (L276-284) from the `[tool.rebar.jira]` sample.
* `docs/user-guide.md` — delete the `resolved_statuses` row (L510) from the DC settings table.
* `docs/release-notes.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` — add the removal entry alongside the sibling
  pre-1.0 pass #3 entries.

### 5. Gates

Run the full local CI gate set from the worktree venv: the ten `check_*` gates, the six generators (regenerate all generated registries and commit the diff), and CI's pytest invocation. Two specific risks: the **config-read gate** may flag orphaned `# read-via:` bookkeeping once the markers go, and the **module-size gate** — `_config_schema.py` sits at 798/800, so this removal should pull it down; verify it does rather than assuming.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] operator sign-off for the removal is recorded on this ticket
- [x] both schema fields and their `_as_str_list` coercers are deleted
- [x] both keys are tombstoned warn-class, so an existing config still loads with a warning
- [x] the auto-derived env twins are tombstoned warn-class
- [x] the deprecation registry rows are gone and a historical NOTE records the
      operator-approved 2026-08-12 removal
- [x] the `# read-via:` markers are gone and the heldout marker test matches
- [x] neither key is documented any more
- [x] all ten `check_*` gates, the six generators, `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's
      pytest invocation are green; `Verified +1` before close
baseline.summary: Remove the deprecated resolved_statuses config keys (needs operator sign-off)

## What
Add proactive detection in the reconciler fetcher: when `_build_snapshot` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`) encounters a Jira workflow status absent from `config.jira_to_local_status`, emit a stderr WARNING and an observable `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` bridge_alert (deduped per 24h) naming the offending status and an example issue.

## Why
A Jira-side workflow status with no reconciler mapping (e.g. an `IDEA` status added to the Jira workflow) is otherwise discovered only downstream, when it reaches an outbound mutation and trips `reconcile.preflight_status_mapping`. A stale such status in `prev_snapshot.json` once stalled the entire bridge. The per-mutation isolation fix already makes an unmapped status non-fatal; this adds early, proactive visibility at snapshot-build time so the missing mapping is flagged and can be added before it causes churn.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`: add `_known_jira_statuses()`
  and `_flag_unmapped_statuses()`; call the latter from `_build_snapshot`
  (fail-open — detection must never break the fetch).
- Fires once per distinct unmapped status per pass; alert is deduped across
  passes via `alert_store.is_deduped` (24h window).
- Out of scope: adding the `idea`/`IDEA` mapping itself (owned by the in-flight
  idea-status epic).

  `alert_store.append` naming any Jira status not in `config.jira_to_local_status`.

## Context / Problem

The current reconciler has typed `MutationDirection` and `MutationAction`, but `Mutation.payload` remains `Mapping[str, Any]`. Outbound typed mutations are translated back into the legacy batch dictionary, two CREATE shapes coexist, and string/monkeypatch consumers make deletion non-local. ADR 0103 already owns retry, coordinator, and observe-before-replay policy; this story must not redesign those decisions.

This is the architecture prerequisite for the typed cutover. It completes RESEARCH and any required ADR lifecycle before dependent implementation begins.

## Approach

- Enumerate every valid `(direction, action)` pair, producer, consumer, serialization/manifest field, compatibility re-export, string import, standalone-loaded test module, and transport boundary. Use semantic references plus string search.
- Define the smallest discriminated payload union that makes invalid field/action combinations unrepresentable while preserving necessary provenance and canonical comparison.
- Decide ownership of payload validation, canonical serialization, adapter projection, follow-ons/suppression, binding identity, and provider-neutral outcomes.
- Treat producer-construction inputs as part of the contract: inventory the current 24-value `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` seam and its 14/11-value field-diff collaborators; decide how observation, transport/runtime, mapping policy, diagnostics, and output construction flow through cohesive existing domain owners. Reject a wrapper that merely repackages the same loose bundle or introduces a second generic pass/ticket context.
- Specify expand/compare/cut/delete sequencing, rollback, and exact legacy deletion targets. Production dual-send is forbidden.
- Reconcile the design with ADRs 0004, 0026–0029, 0083, 0092, and 0103. If a new structural decision is required, complete the architecture-decision RESEARCH -> critique -> DRAFT -> HOLD -> MERGE lifecycle before closing this story.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mutation producers, planners, coordinator, adapters, manifests, and compatibility surfaces.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — consumer census and existing contract evidence.
- `docs/adr/` — one atomic decision record only if accepted ADRs do not already decide the representation boundary.

## Testing

This story produces architecture evidence rather than production behavior. Verify the consumer census with both Serena semantic references and repository text search; verify the direction/action matrix against the enum allowlist and every planner/adapter route; run plan review on the resulting implementation stories after the ADR disposition is settled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A checked-in or ticket-recorded census covers every mutation producer/consumer and all string, dynamic-load, monkeypatch, manifest, and transport consumers; an empty semantic result is confirmed by text search. — Delivered in ADR 0107 §"Census" (Serena `find_referencing_symbols`/`find_symbol` across `mutation.py`, `outbound_mutation_builders.py`, `outbound_differ.py`, `batch_dispatch.py`, `applier.py`, `apply_base.py`, `typed_dispatch.py`, `apply_inbound.py`, `apply_outbound.py`, `differ.py`, `observation.py`, `ticket_plan.py`, `outbound_field_diff.py`, reconciled against `grep` for string/monkeypatch/dynamic-load sites); confirms `(inbound, delete)` and `(inbound, probe)` are enum-valid but dead (no producer, no `_LEAVES` handler; removed by bug 3b5f per `apply_inbound.py`'s own docstring).
- [x] Every valid direction/action pair has a named payload contract with required/optional fields and validation rules; no proposed contract relies on one option-heavy generic action payload. — ADR 0107 §"Discriminated payload union" defines all 10 live `(direction, action)` payload types with required/optional field tables and validation-ownership assignment; explicitly rejects a single generic payload.
- [x] The design states which current canonical bytes/hashes are compatibility requirements and which normalized representation is comparison-only. — ADR 0107 §"Canonical bytes vs. comparison-only representation" distinguishes the serialized-manifest compatibility surface from the shadow/live comparison's normalized view.
- [x] Retry/idempotency/fuse ownership remains with ADR 0103's coordinator; no adapter or payload type introduces a second retry owner. — ADR 0107 explicitly reaffirms ADR 0103 as sole retry/idempotency/fuse owner; no payload type is assigned retry responsibility.
- [x] Shadow comparison is side-effect-free, and live comparison uses isolated Jira targets/instances rather than dual-sending to one issue. — ADR 0107 §"Migration sequencing" states this explicitly and forbids production dual-send.
- [x] The migration has explicit entry/exit criteria and names `_mutation_to_batch_dict`, legacy batch dispatch, duplicate CREATE handling, obsolete re-exports, and compatibility tests as deletion targets. — ADR 0107 §"Migration sequencing" (expand/compare/cut/delete) names each of these as explicit deletion targets with entry/exit criteria per phase.
- [x] The design explicitly dispositions the current 24/14/11-value producer seams and names the cohesive input boundaries the implementation will use; it does not merely wrap the same values or duplicate `Observation`, `TicketPlan`, or the current pass/runtime owner. — ADR 0107 §"Producer-seam disposition" assigns the 23/14/11-parameter seams to four existing owners (`OutboundDiffConfig`, `Observation`/`TicketPlan`, Backend-port collaborators, observability sinks); explicitly rejects a new generic context object.
- [x] Any required ADR is merged with explicit approval before dependent code work; otherwise the evidence records why accepted ADRs already decide the shape. — No accepted ADR already decides the `Mutation.payload` representation boundary (0004/0026-0029/0083/0092/0103 reconciled and found silent on this boundary), so ADR 0107 was authored. It is recorded as **Proposed (DRAFT)**, not Accepted: an autonomous agent session cannot self-certify a MERGE per the architecture-decision RESEARCH->DRAFT->HOLD->MERGE lifecycle's explicit-authorization requirement. The ADR itself states, and this ticket's closing comment states, that the dependent implementation story (`earthborn-statuelike-boutu`) must not begin until a human operator moves ADR 0107 to Accepted — this is the evidence recording why the gate is open, satisfying this AC's "otherwise" branch honestly rather than fabricating an approval.

# Live DC rich-text lane: outbound echo re-diffs against stale JQL search snapshot

## Observed failure
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_rich_text_live.py::test_live_rich_text_renders_and_echo_is_safe` and `::test_live_rich_text_both_sides_conflict_keeps_local` fail on the dispatched Live External Integration run (33052311279, DC lane), both with: `AssertionError: the index never reflected the pushed body ... within 240s (120 attempts)`. The indexed doc shows `description: None` and `updated` stuck at the binding step.

## Corrected root cause (supersedes the "index lag / widen the wait" framing of bug 2c60)
The test's `_push_and_converge` blocks on `_wait_until_search_reflects` — waiting for the JQL SEARCH index to reflect the pushed `description`. That guards a REAL dependency: the outbound FIELD differ (`compute_outbound_mutations`, outbound_differ.py) diffs local tickets against the FETCHER'S JQL-SEARCH SNAPSHOT (`fetcher.fetch_snapshot` -> `search_issues`). For a key PRESENT in the snapshot (ours is — its key is indexed for existence via `wait_until_searchable`), the differ compares local `description` against the SNAPSHOT's `description`, which is STALE (`None`) until the background Lucene reindex catches up. Direct GET (`_safe_get_issue` / `get_issue_by_rest`, immediately consistent) is used ONLY for bound-but-ABSENT keys, not bound-and-present ones. So on the ephemeral DC — whose background reindex is UNBOUNDED (ADR 0085 §3; see also ADR 0055's `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` "Search-index lag" row for the Jira-family sub-seam) and, on a starved instance, never reflects the write within any fixed budget — the echo pass re-diffs the just-pushed field as changed and would churn, and the wait times out.

Two prior fixes (2c60: widen to 240s; then force a per-issue reindex) both targeted search VISIBILITY. Widening cannot bound an unbounded wait, and the forced-reindex helper had NO effect (and no observability — it no-ops silently), likely because `/rest/api/2/reindex/issue` is not an effective synchronous foreground reindex on DC 8.17. The fix must remove the dependence on unbounded search visibility, not chase it.

## Candidate resolutions (to be decided by investigation + history)
1. PRODUCT: outbound differ confirms a snapshot-detected field change via a bounded direct GET
   before emitting the mutation, so a stale-snapshot false-positive cannot cause churn (extends
   the existing bound-but-absent direct-GET seam to bound-and-present keys). Robust for ANY
   eventually-consistent remote.
2. HARNESS: configure the ephemeral Jira DC for synchronous/fast indexing at boot.
3. TEST: verify the landed body via a direct GET (immediately consistent) and re-express echo-
   safety so it does not depend on unbounded search visibility.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Root cause confirmed (which of 1/2/3, with history/ADR support).
- [x] Fix removes the unbounded-search-visibility dependency; a held-out test proves it with teeth.
- [x] The repo snapshot contains live rich-text echo-safety coverage: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_rich_text_live.py` defines `test_live_rich_text_renders_and_echo_is_safe` and `test_live_rich_text_both_sides_conflict_keeps_local`, and both tests exercise the reconciler overlay while checking rich-text echo/conflict behavior.
- [x] [non-codebase] A dispatched Live External Integration run shows the Jira DC lane GREEN and the Jira Cloud mutation lane GREEN. Run URL commented here.
      provenance: environment=github-actions external-integration.yml run 33137402410 on main at 6fe5c0d54574; principal=github-actions workflow_dispatch runner; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — dispatched run job 98740362395 concluded success for the ephemeral Jira DC lane (74 passed, none skipped), and the Jira Cloud coordinator mutation lane also concluded success.
- [x] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.
baseline.summary: Live DC rich-text echo re-diffs against stale JQL search snapshot

baseline.description:
## Why

The parent-first claim/transition cascade is thoroughly covered for the sequential, single-process case (parent-first, multi-level, already-progressed/blocked parent, parent-failure-aborts-child, child-failure-after-parent, cycle termination, exit-code propagation). There is no test for a cross-process / two-clone race where two agents work different children of the same open parent. The report is right that the expected semantics must be written down before a test can assert them (e.g. may children be claimed independently once the parent is in progress? does a losing parent claim after merge invalidate the corresponding child claim?).

## What

Committed policy (to be documented, then tested) for two same-parent/different-child sub-cases:
- **(a) Same-tracker, serialized:** agent A claims the parent (cascade) then child A.
  Agent B, seeing the parent already `in_progress`, does NOT cascade and may claim
  child B independently under its own assignee. Parent ownership does NOT constrain
  sibling child assignees. This is fail-fast: if B's parent-claim were attempted while
  the parent is `open` and lost, B's child is never attempted.
- **(b) Two offline clones:** both independently claim the (open) parent + a child. On
  merge, forks are resolved **independently per ticket** by the reducer's UUID tie-break:
  - The PARENT's STATUS fork resolves to one winner (surfaced as `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`
    on the parent); the losing agent's parent ownership is thereby signaled.
  - If both clones claimed the SAME child, the CHILD also has a concurrent STATUS fork,
    resolved by the same tie-break INDEPENDENTLY of the parent — so the child's winner may
    differ from the parent's winner. If they claimed DIFFERENT children, each child simply
    carries its own single claim.
  - In all cases the losing agent's already-written claim (parent and/or child) is **left
    in place (orphaned under the losing assignee); it is NOT retroactively rolled back or
    tombstoned.** The signal is `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` on the affected ticket(s).

Document this in `docs/concurrency.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, then encode it in two tests.

## Scope

- `docs/concurrency.md` and/or `CLAUDE.md` (policy statement)
- `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` (or sibling) — new race tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ownership policy for BOTH sub-cases above is written down in
      `docs/concurrency.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, including the explicit rule that a losing parent
      claim leaves the losing agent's child claim in place (orphaned), detected via the
      parent's `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`.
- [ ] Same-tracker process race test (sub-case a): two real processes race on one
      tracker; confirms lock serialization, that B does not cascade a parent already
      `in_progress`, and both children end claimed under their respective assignees.
- [ ] Two-clone offline race test (sub-case b): both clones claim parent+child offline,
      then merge; confirms deterministic convergence, the parent `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`
      signal, that a SAME-child claim produces an independently-resolved child STATUS fork
      (child winner may differ from parent winner), and that the losing agent's claim(s)
      remain in place (not rolled back).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Define parent-cascade race policy + cross-clone race tests

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` measures **796 lines** against the repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), which CI enforces with no allowlist escape hatch. Four lines of headroom is not enough for the sibling story that makes the outbound create path target a per-ticket project, so that story cannot land until this file has room.

## Approach

Extract the entire `update_one` sub-tree — lines **432-796** — into a new `dispatch_update.py`. This is a pre-existing call-graph seam, not a mechanical cut: `update_one` (`:447`) calls `_update_one_apply_parent` (`:497`), `_update_one_scalar_update` (`:500`), `_update_one_dispatch_labels` (`:506`) and `_update_one_dispatch_links` (`:510`), and `_update_one_scalar_update` is the sole caller of `_is_illegal_transition_400`. Nothing above line 432 calls into the block; the only dependency runs downward, through `_call_with_retry` (`:71-143`), which stays put.

The repository has already made this exact split twice: `dispatch_apply_phases.py` (226 lines) holds three other `update_one` phases, and `batch_dispatch.py` (148 lines) is the stable re-export facade. This extraction follows the pattern rather than inventing one.

**The import edge the new module must carry.** `update_one` does not only call the four helpers that move with it — it also calls `_update_one_apply_reporter` (`:498`), `_update_one_filter_fields` (`:499`) and `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:507`), which already live in `dispatch_apply_phases` and are imported at `dispatch_one.py:53-55`. Those three imports move to `dispatch_update.py` with their caller; `dispatch_one` drops them, since nothing left in it uses them. This is what makes the extraction land in the module that already owns the other `update_one` phases.

**The one hazard, and how it is avoided.** `dispatch_one.py` must **not** re-export `update_one` back for convenience — that would create `dispatch_one → dispatch_update → dispatch_one`, because `dispatch_update` imports `_call_with_retry` from `dispatch_one`. Instead `batch_dispatch.py`'s import block (`:31-40`) is re-pointed at `dispatch_update` for `update_one` and `_is_illegal_transition_400`. That is the only production re-point needed: `applier.py:122-130` already imports both symbols **from `batch_dispatch`**, not from `dispatch_one`, so its `__all__` at `:329` keeps resolving with no edit.

`batch_dispatch` is the established public surface. Its import block at `:31-38` currently takes six names from `dispatch_one` — `_call_with_retry`, `_find_link_id`, `_index_existing_links`, `_is_illegal_transition_400`, `create_one` and `update_one`. (`delete_one` is **not** among them; it is defined in `batch_dispatch` itself at `:54`.) After the move that block splits three ways: `_call_with_retry` and `create_one` still come from `dispatch_one`; `_is_illegal_transition_400` and `update_one` come from `dispatch_update`; and `_find_link_id` / `_index_existing_links` are taken directly from `dispatch_apply_phases`, where they are actually defined (`:206` and `:180`) and from which `dispatch_one` only re-exports them. Every edge then points from `batch_dispatch` downward and from `dispatch_update` to `dispatch_one`, never back, so the direction stays acyclic.

**The new module's complete import inventory**, derived by scanning the moved range rather than by inspection:

- stdlib: `json`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `urllib` — and only these four. `logging`, `time`, `os`,
  `random` and `pathlib` are imported by `dispatch_one` but unused inside `432-796`, so they stay.
- `typing`: `Any`, `cast`.
- from `rebar_reconciler._errors`: `JiraAPIError`, `http_status`.
- from `rebar_reconciler.dispatch_apply_phases`: `_update_one_apply_reporter`,
  `_update_one_filter_fields`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`, `_find_link_id`,
  `_index_existing_links`.
- from `rebar_reconciler.pass_io`: `record_parent_divergence` only. That module is imported at
  `dispatch_one.py:57` alongside `_write_mapping_atomic`, which the moved range does **not** use, so
  `dispatch_one` keeps its own `pass_io` import for that name.
- from `rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one`: `_call_with_retry`.

**One CI gate keys on the symbol's file.** `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records per-symbol ceilings keyed as `<file>::<symbol>`, and two of its keys name this module — `dispatch_one.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` and `dispatch_one.py::create_one`. The first symbol moves, so its key must be re-pointed to `dispatch_update.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` or the complexity gate fails on a file that no longer defines it; `create_one` stays and its key is untouched. This consumer lives outside the source tree and is invisible to any symbol- or import-level search, which is why it is called out explicitly.

**One consumer does need an edit.** `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py:36` imports `update_one` **directly** from `dispatch_one`, so it breaks the moment the symbol moves and the no-re-export rule forbids papering over it. That import is re-pointed at `batch_dispatch`, which is where every other consumer already gets it. This is the single test edit this story makes, and it is enumerated rather than discovered during implementation — an earlier draft of this plan wrongly claimed no test changes were needed.

This is a behaviour-preserving move: no logic is rewritten.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_update.py` (new) — the moved sub-tree, ~405 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — drops to ~431 lines
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/batch_dispatch.py` — the `:31-38` import block split across
  `dispatch_one`, `dispatch_update` and `dispatch_apply_phases`; the only production re-point
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — the `_update_one_dispatch_links` ceiling re-keyed to the new
  file
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py` — its direct
  `from ... dispatch_one import update_one` at `:36` re-pointed at `batch_dispatch`

`applier.py` is deliberately **not** in scope: it already imports the moved symbols from `batch_dispatch` (`:122-130`), so it needs no change.

## Testing

No new behaviour, so no new behavioural tests: the oracle is the existing suite passing **unchanged**, which is what proves the move preserved behaviour. Two specific hazards are verified rather than assumed:

- Monkeypatch survival: there are **five** module-attribute patch sites on `dispatch_one`, across
  three test modules — `apply/test_applier_identity_write.py:156,195`,
  `test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py:258,279` and `test_error_taxonomy.py:61` — and every one of
  them patches the same attribute, `dispatch_one.time`. All five stay safe: `time` is consumed by
  `_call_with_retry` and `create_one`, both of which remain resident, and `dispatch_update` reaches
  the retry helper by importing `_call_with_retry` from `dispatch_one`, so the sleep call still
  resolves against `dispatch_one`'s globals where the patch is applied. Confirm all five pass
  unedited — this is the assertion that proves the split did not silently defeat a patch.
- Import-cycle check: importing `dispatch_one` and `dispatch_update` in either order must succeed,
  asserted directly so a future re-export cannot silently reintroduce the cycle.
- Direct-importer coverage: the one re-pointed test
  (`test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py`) passes after its import is changed, and a repository-wide
  grep for `from rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one import update_one` returns no remaining hit. The grep
  is part of the oracle because this consumer was missed by symbol-level analysis and only a string
  search surfaced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatch_one.py` and `dispatch_update.py` are each at or below 650 lines; checked by running
      the module-size gate and recording both counts.
- [ ] The full existing test suite passes, with exactly one existing test file edited —
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_synced_fields_reporting_e6e9.py`, whose direct import
      is re-pointed — and one file added,
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dispatch_update_split.py`, which holds this story's
      structural assertions; checked by the gating test command plus confirming the diff under
      `tests/` touches only those two paths.
- [ ] All five `dispatch_one.time` patch sites pass unedited; checked by running the three named
      test modules.
- [ ] `dispatch_update.py` carries the full import inventory named in the Approach and `dispatch_one`
      no longer imports what it stopped using; checked by asserting both modules' import lists.
- [ ] The complexity gate passes with `_update_one_dispatch_links` re-keyed to
      `dispatch_update.py::_update_one_dispatch_links` and `create_one`'s key unchanged; checked by
      running the complexity-baseline gate and inspecting both keys.
- [ ] `batch_dispatch` resolves all six previously-imported names after its block is split; checked
      by importing each from `batch_dispatch` and asserting no `ImportError`.
- [ ] No `from rebar_reconciler.dispatch_one import update_one` remains anywhere in the tree; checked
      by a repository-wide string grep returning zero hits.
- [ ] `dispatch_one.py` does not import from `dispatch_update.py`; checked by a test that imports the
      two modules in both orders and asserts no `ImportError`.
- [ ] `update_one` and `_is_illegal_transition_400` remain reachable through `batch_dispatch` **and**
      through `applier`'s existing re-export; checked by asserting both resolve from each module
      after the move, which confirms `applier.py` needed no edit.
- [ ] No behaviour change: checked by confirming the moved functions' bodies are identical to their
      pre-move text apart from import lines.
baseline.summary: Size relief: extract the update_one sub-tree from dispatch_one.py into dispatch_update.py

baseline.description:
## Summary

The three-probe sandbox enforcement suite never runs on Linux in CI. It skips, silently, and a green `Verified +1` cannot be distinguished from the tests having executed.

## Mechanism

- `scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:113-115` records it in the merged code's own words: GitHub's
  ubuntu runners ship bubblewrap but DENY unprivileged user namespaces
  (`bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied`), so the functional probe `_bwrap_works()`
  correctly reports no usable mechanism.
- With `probe()` returning `None`, the `@live` skipif at `tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:61-64`
  fires and all four enforcement tests skip.
- Under `-q` a skip prints as a dot-adjacent 's' and is invisible in the CI summary.

## Why this matters

The macOS Seatbelt path is verified on-host (28 passed, zero skips, real deny observed). The Linux path is therefore an UNVERIFIED CAPABILITY: bwrap's write-deny has never been observed executing anywhere. `chiffon-venomous-annelida` AC6 was written precisely to prevent inferring the Linux result from the macOS one, and it is not met.

## Contradiction worth resolving

Two commits disagree. `b63cf799ed90` installs bubblewrap in the workflow specifically so these tests would NOT skip on Linux. `a26a73277c8a` then documents that they still find no mechanism there. One of the two is stale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three-probe enforcement test is OBSERVED executing (not skipping) on a Linux runner,
      with the outside-deny probe exiting non-zero and the file absent afterward.
- [ ] If GitHub-hosted ubuntu cannot grant the required namespaces, the chosen resolution is
      recorded with its reasoning — e.g. a different mechanism, a container with the capability,
      or an explicit decision that Linux enforcement is out of scope.
- [ ] A skip of these tests is made LOUD rather than silent, so a future regression to
      'no mechanism' cannot pass as green.
- [ ] The b63cf799ed90 / a26a73277c8a contradiction is resolved in whichever direction is true.
baseline.summary: Mutation-sandbox enforcement tests SKIP on ubuntu-latest, so the Linux write-deny is unproven

baseline.description:
## Report

`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` can print an error to stderr **with exit code 0**, ~60s AFTER the close is durably committed, silently downgrading the ticket to closed-WITHOUT-signature. Seen in the field: an agent reported its final `rebar transition` failed with a lock error; re-reading showed the transition had LANDED.

## Premise verified in current `origin/main` (cc69cc1179)

In `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `close_ticket` (line **263**): the STATUS event commits and releases the lock BEFORE the signing tail runs. Line **433** calls `sign_completion_verdict(...)`, whose append takes a fresh 60s `write_lock` via `write_and_push` -> `event_append`. Line **434** catches `_signing.SigningError`; lines **439-445** write `Warning: closed <id> WITHOUT a completion signature — <exc.message>` to stderr and fall through, so `close_ticket` returns its normal success payload (lines **492-498**: `ticket_id`, `from`, `to`, `newly_unblocked`, `noop`) and the command exits **0**. That payload carries **no field at all** about the signature outcome, so no library, MCP or CLI consumer can detect the loss programmatically. The sibling drift refusal (lines **421-429**) lands unsigned the same way, likewise unreported.

The `except` comment (lines **435-438**) justifies the exit-0 degrade for a *missing ssh-keygen* — permanent and operator-fixable — which does not transfer to the **transient lock timeout** the field incident hit; the appended `exc.message` ("flock: could not acquire lock after 60s") reads as the CLOSE failing when it succeeded. Zebrafish (cc69cc1179) added bounded retry there, mitigating frequency but not the reporting shape.

## Direction

Make the loss **machine-readable and honestly worded** for the caller that suffered it, without changing the process exit code.

1. **Payload marker.** `close_ticket` returns an additional
   `completion_signature: {"signed": bool, "cause": str, "error": str}`, mirroring the
   machine-branchable `PlanReviewAttestation.as_dict()` idiom used for this same problem at
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:457`, so callers branch on `cause` without parsing
   English. The `cause` vocabulary is **closed and total** over the close path, and `error` is
   empty wherever there is no failure text:

   | outcome | `signed` | `cause` | `error` |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | signature persisted | `True` | `signed` | `""` |
   | `SigningError` at line 434 | `False` | `sign_failed` | `exc.message` |
   | drift refusal at line 421 | `False` | `material_drifted` | `""` |
   | `--force` close (signing deliberately skipped) | `False` | `force_bypassed` | `""` |

   The key is present only where a completion signature is in play: **absent** for a non-close
   transition, and absent for `idea -> closed`, which line **325**
   (`target_status == "closed" and current_status != "idea"`) excludes from the signing block
   entirely — a REJECT/DROP of an undesigned idea is not a completion, so it has no signature
   outcome and inventing a `cause` would misreport a deliberate non-event. Consumers treat the
   key as optional, absence meaning "not a completion close".

   `sign_failed` deliberately covers BOTH the transient lock timeout and the permanent
   missing-`ssh-keygen` degrade: they differ in remedy but not in the fact reported, and the
   distinguishing text is carried verbatim in `error`. Splitting it would make this layer
   classify `SigningError`s it does not construct — that belongs with the signing layer.

   **Consumers that must forward it.** The payload is re-projected field by field at two
   boundaries that would otherwise silently strip the new key, so both are in the edit set:
   `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:414-419` (public `rebar.transition()`) and
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:580-591` (CLI `--output json`). MCP `transition_ticket`
   (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:190-195`) forwards the library result and inherits it once
   `_lib_writes` does — asserted, not assumed. The shared
   `src/rebar/schemas/transition_result.schema.json` gains `completion_signature` as an
   OPTIONAL property (out of `required`: `reopen` shares the schema and has no close path);
   it already sets `additionalProperties: true`, so this is additive. The `TransitionResult`
   TypedDict at `src/rebar/types.py:205-213` mirrors that schema field by field and is the
   declared return type of public `transition()`, so it gains the same key as `NotRequired` in
   this change — otherwise the typed and JSON contracts disagree and mypy rejects the new key
   at the `_lib_writes` return.
2. **Honest message.** The stderr text leads with the close having **LANDED** and only the
   signature having failed, then names the recovery — rather than appending a bare lock error
   that describes the succeeded operation as failed.
3. **No durable read-side record here — split out.** The first draft proposed a best-effort
   audit comment. That is unsound: it appends through the SAME `event_append` -> `write_lock`
   path whose 60s timeout produced the `SigningError`, so under the contention that causes
   this bug it fails too, and the record would be missing in exactly the case it exists for.

   The sound mechanism is to record the EXPECTATION at close time in the same locked write
   that already commits the STATUS event (line **377** `txn.transition_core`, which already
   carries `close_class` and `force_close_reason`), so a reader can compare "a signature was
   expected" against "a valid completion attestation exists". That is an event-schema addition
   (schema + reducer + `docs/event-schema.md`) — materially more cross-cutting than this
   reporting fix — so it is tracked as its own bug, **mechanical-coherent-wolverine**
   (`23b2-1a94-6a01-466b`), linked `discovered_from` this one, rather than hand-waved here.

   This ticket therefore makes the loss visible to the CALLER that suffered it, across all
   three public surfaces. Making it visible to an unrelated LATER reader is wolverine's job.

### Why NOT a nonzero exit code (deliberate, recorded)

The report offers "a nonzero exit **or at minimum** a machine-readable failure marker"; the exit path is rejected here. `docs/exit-codes.md` declares the contract **frozen** as of the 2026-06-09 window, pinned by `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`, with the table at `docs/exit-codes.md:158` fixing `transition` at 0/1/10 — a NEW code is additive-only in a future window, a release decision rather than an implementation one. Reusing exit **1** would be actively harmful: agents read 1 as "the transition failed" and re-run it, which then exits **10** (already closed), trading a silent loss for a louder wrong answer. The marker route meets the reporting need within the frozen contract; a new code is out of scope here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A close whose signature append raises `SigningError` returns
      `completion_signature.signed == False` with `cause == "sign_failed"` — verified by a
      test that forces the append to fail
- [x] A successful close returns `completion_signature` `{signed: True, cause: "signed",
      error: ""}` — verified by a test
- [x] A `--force` close returns `signed == False`, `cause == "force_bypassed"` — test
- [x] The marker survives to all three public consumers: `rebar.transition()` returns it,
      `rebar transition … --output json` prints it, and MCP `transition_ticket` carries it —
      verified by a test per surface
- [x] The stderr text on that failure states the close LANDED and only the signature did not,
      and does not present the lock error as the close failing — verified by a test asserting
      the message text
- [x] `idea -> closed` returns no `completion_signature` key — verified by a test
- [x] The material-drift refusal path reports `signed == False` with
      `cause == "material_drifted"` — verified by a test
- [x] Exit code is unchanged (0) throughout — verified by a test pinning that decision
baseline.summary: transition close reports a lock error with exit 0 after the close landed, silently dropping the completion signature

baseline.description:
Delete `baseline_advanced_at` and stop rewriting an unchanged baseline. This is the single highest-value change in the epic: it cuts marginal packed cost per `bindings.json` version from **12.79 KB to 1.74 KB (7.4x)**, measured over 40 consecutive real revisions. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`binding_store.py:373-375` unconditionally rewrites `entry["baseline"]` and stamps `baseline_advanced_at = _now_iso()`. That field is written in exactly one place and **read nowhere in `src/`** (only asserted in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py:61`). Measured across consecutive committed revisions: baseline VALUES changed **0** entries while the stamp changed **1144** — a scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file, which is pathological for git delta compression.

Honest scoping: because baseline values change 0 entries/pass today, the write-when-changed guard is **byte-neutral** and the entire measured win comes from deleting the field. The guard is still worth adding — it is the correct behaviour once real Jira edits arrive, and it saves the rewrite CPU — but it must not be credited with the savings.

## Approach
In `set_baseline`: build the filtered baseline, compare to the existing one, return early if equal; never write `baseline_advanced_at`. Preserve `binding_store.py:374`'s `if k in fields` semantics (**not** `is not None`) — `outbound_field_diff.py:251` treats a MISSING key as "no ancestor -> local wins", so a key must stay present with a `None` value rather than being dropped.

Both callers must be covered: `reconcile._advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:506-523`) and the inbound-adopt path at `apply_inbound_records.py:209-212`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce a **byte-identical**
      `bindings.json` and create **no commit**. Tier: **integration** against a stateful fake,
      asserting file bytes and commit count — not call counts. (`save()` uses
      `json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, so byte-identity is well-defined.)
- [ ] `grep -rn baseline_advanced_at src/` returns nothing; the stamp is absent from every entry
      written by `set_baseline`. Tier: **unit** + grep assertion.
- [ ] A baseline field present-but-null still round-trips as present (guards the `if k in fields`
      semantics). Tier: **unit** on `set_baseline` + `get_baseline`.
- [ ] `test_binding_baseline.py:61`'s assertion on the stamp is removed or inverted, and the suite is
      green. Verify: `make test`.
- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed version measured at **<=25% of the 12.79 KB baseline** by the
      recorded method (rebuild N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo, repack
      `--window=250 --depth=50`, `(pack_N-pack_1)/(N-1)`). Tier: **repo-level measurement**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`

Scope: S-M.
baseline.summary: A1: delete the never-read baseline_advanced_at stamp and add a write-when-changed guard to set_baseline

baseline.description:
# Make the API-stability version references version-agnostic (remove drift-prone markers)

Adopt the mainstream OSS pattern (FastAPI/attrs/httpx): state the stability **policy** without naming a current version in prose, and point readers to the CHANGELOG / GitHub Releases for live numbers. This removes the duplicated `currently X.Y.Z` package-version marker in `docs/api-stability.md` — and with it the drift it caused and the guard that policed it (`tests/unit/test_version_sync.py`) — so no version must be hand-bumped in the doc each release. (Design Option A from the api-stability version-marker analysis; Option E — VCS-derived versioning — is parked separately as idea deficient-eastmost-hoopoe.)

## Why

`docs/api-stability.md` hard-codes `(currently 0.8.0)`, duplicating `pyproject.toml`'s version. That duplication silently drifted before (the doc once read 0.6.0 while the package was 0.7.1), which is why `tests/unit/test_version_sync.py` exists to fail CI on a mismatch. The specific number adds nothing over the "0.x ⇒ any minor may break" statement that carries the real meaning; the live version belongs in the CHANGELOG / Releases, which the release flow already maintains. Removing the marker eliminates the duplication at its source, so the consistency test is correctly removed WITH it (removing the test while keeping the marker would reopen the drift bug). The same anti-pattern already bit the same file a second time: the Event-schema row reads `SCHEMA_VERSION (currently **3**)` while the code is at **5** — a live, wrong literal — so this change de-literals those parentheticals too. Popular actively-maintained projects write pre-1.0 stability policy this way: FastAPI's "About FastAPI versions" and attrs' "Backward Compatibility" name no current version and defer to the changelog.

## What / Scope

- `docs/api-stability.md`:
  - Reword the opening so it states the 0.x SemVer policy WITHOUT a `currently X.Y.Z` version
    literal, and links to the CHANGELOG and GitHub Releases for the current version.
  - De-literal the Event-schema row: replace `SCHEMA_VERSION (currently **3**, in
    rebar/reducer/_version.py)` and `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 1)` with references to
    those constants in their source files WITHOUT a hard-coded number (fixes the stale `3`,
    which is actually 5, and removes the same drift-prone anti-pattern).
  - Keep the rest of the page (the per-surface stability matrix content) unchanged.
- `tests/unit/test_version_sync.py` — DELETE. Its sole purpose was to keep the now-removed
  package-version marker in sync; with no marker there is nothing to check.
- `docs/releasing.md` — remove ONLY the two dangling references added when cutting v0.8.0:
  drop `docs/api-stability.md` from the step-1 `git add` bump command, and delete the
  `test_version_sync.py` / `(currently X.Y.Z)` mentions in that step. **Preserve** the
  unrelated 1.0-declaration section's reference to `docs/api-stability.md` (the "remove the
  Pre-1.0 caveat" instruction near line 434) — it is not about the version marker.
- Out of scope: any change to `pyproject.toml`/`server.json` version handling (that is
  Option E, parked as idea deficient-eastmost-hoopoe).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/api-stability.md` contains NO `currently <number>` literal of any kind — neither
  the package version nor the schema versions (verify:
  `! grep -Eiq 'currently[* _]*[0-9]' docs/api-stability.md`) — and DOES link to the
  changelog/releases for the version (verify: `grep -Eiq 'CHANGELOG|releases' docs/api-stability.md`).
- [ ] The Event-schema row still names `SCHEMA_VERSION` and its source file but with no
