## Context
Gerrit Verify run 31846417650 dynamically attributed the recurring macOS long pole: `socket.getfqdn` consumed 35.013s inside `ThreadingHTTPServer` construction for the loopback editor fixture; constructor and fixture setup were 35.014s/35.020s. TCP bind was below the 1s instrumentation threshold. The test contract needs a real loopback HTTP server but does not consume `server_name`, so reverse DNS changes no asserted behavior. This violates the operator requirement that individual tests remain negligible and that average Verify duration stay within 20–30 minutes without reducing coverage. pip explicitly bypasses the same ~30s HTTPServer reverse-DNS path; aiohttp and urllib3 likewise bind literal loopback/raw sockets.

## Proven root cause
CPython `HTTPServer.server_bind` calls `socket.getfqdn(host)` after binding. On GitHub macOS runners, reverse resolution of numeric `127.0.0.1` repeatedly waits about 35 seconds. The editor workflow constructs `ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), ...)`, so every affected test worker pays a network-environment-dependent lookup even though only loopback bind/address behavior is contractual.

## Plan
- Inventory existing editor-server tests and freeze a held-out behavioral oracle: editor workflow starts a real loopback server even when `socket.getfqdn` raises, and still publishes the literal bound address/port needed by clients.
- Prove the oracle RED against current main for the expected reverse-DNS reason.
- With the oracle held out from the fixer, introduce a local ThreadingHTTPServer subclass whose bind path delegates to `socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind` and derives `server_name`/`server_port` from the already-bound literal address, matching the established pip pattern without adding a dependency.
- Restore the oracle and prove GREEN; defect-seed the original HTTPServer bind path to return it to RED, then restore the fix.
- Run focused editor tests, lint, typecheck, and applicable workflow/action guards.
- Land through Gerrit, then use a full macOS Verify run to confirm the 35-second span disappears while real editor behavior remains covered.

## Caller safety
Expected post-fix behavior: all editor-workflow callers receive the same localhost URL, token, request handling, and shutdown behavior; only an unused reverse-DNS-derived `server_name` value becomes the literal bound host. Before repair, sweep all `ThreadingHTTPServer` and editor workflow callers up to three levels for any dependency on reverse-resolved `server_name`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A behavioral oracle is observed RED first because current server construction invokes `socket.getfqdn`.
- [ ] Editor workflow starts and serves over real loopback without invoking reverse DNS.
- [ ] Bound address/ephemeral port, request handling, authentication, and shutdown coverage remain intact.
- [ ] No new dependency, external call, skip, xfail, or weakened assertion is introduced.
- [ ] The defect-seeded original bind path makes the held-out oracle RED again.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, and applicable CI policy gates pass.
- [ ] Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 precede merge.
- [ ] A post-fix macOS Verify observation records the removed span and wall-clock effect.
baseline.summary: Avoid reverse DNS in loopback editor test server

baseline.description:
`pyproject.toml:375` omits the `ARG*` family from `select`, so nothing detects a parameter that is accepted and never read. `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` reports **72** (56 ARG001, 14 ARG002, 2 ARG005). This backlog concealed three real accepted-then-dropped values, which is the defect class that motivated this run's unwired-functionality sweep.

**Scope: a one-off sweep. No permanent gate is enabled by this ticket** — see "Revisit" below.

## Classification (a decision procedure covering every violation)

`ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` currently reports **64** (48 ARG001, 14 ARG002, 2 ARG005) — down from the 72 measured when this ticket was written, because `c61a` ("Retire dead bridge verbs") landed on `main` and deleted `purge_bridge.py`/`bridge.py`. Rather than a fixed count that drifts, EVERY violation is dispositioned by the procedure below, applied site-by-site with `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` as the completeness oracle. Each of the 64 falls into exactly one bucket, and each bucket names a concrete action, so no violation is left without a disposition:

1. **Tracked real defect — EXCLUDED, left in place.** An accepted-then-silently-dropped value that
   *should* be consumed is a real bug, tracked separately and NOT fixed in this sweep. Exactly
   three are known: `timeout_s` (`7504-a127-e9b0-42bb`), the discarded close reason
   (`3803-8e04-7c32-4b80`, CLOSED), and the `acli_cmd` bug. Their residual ARG sites —
   `close_precheck.py:166` `_completion_precheck(*, reason)` (keyword-only, body never reads it)
   and `txn.py:189` `force_close_reason` — belong to the close-reason defect's surface; leave the
   violation in place (do not `_`-prefix or `# noqa` it). **If execution surfaces a NEW
   accepted-then-dropped value that looks like a genuine defect, do not fold its fix into this
   sweep:** `create` a ticket, `link <new> fc0c-e218-8b34-4858 discovered_from`, and leave that
   violation in place.
2. **Cluster-1 — reconciler leaf handlers (10 sites), normalize to `**_kwargs`** (see below).
3. **Cluster-2 — `OutboundMapper` Protocol conformance (7 sites), `# noqa: ARG002`** (see below).
4. **Rename UNSAFE (keyword-passed, string-referenced, or keyword-only) — resolve with
   `# noqa: ARG00x` + a one-line reason, never a bare rename.** The parameter is passed by keyword
   at a call site, referenced by string name (`getattr`/`setattr`/`monkeypatch.setattr`/
   `sig.parameters`/`**kwargs` unpacking), or declared keyword-only (after `*`), so `_`-prefixing
   it breaks a caller. Each such site must name the keyword call site or string reference that
   makes it unsafe. (Confirmed example: `_completion_precheck(*, reason)` is keyword-only — but it
   is bucket 1, excluded.)
5. **Interface/Protocol/callback-registry unused, dispatched POSITIONALLY — safe to `_`-prefix.**
   The parameter is pinned by a shared signature (e.g. the eval-scorer registry `case`, the
   reducer `_processors` `event`, the provider-factory `provider_name`, dispatch-table callbacks)
   but unused in this implementation, and every dispatch site calls positionally. `_`-prefix it.
6. **Plain mechanical (SAFE-RENAME) — `_`-prefix the parameter (zero-touch).** No keyword call
   site, no string reference, not keyword-only, not interface-pinned. Where the value is genuinely
   dead and the parameter is purely local, delete the parameter and its call site(s) instead.

The load-bearing safety check is the bucket-4 test: a rename is applied ONLY after confirming with `grep` (not semantic search alone — Serena omits string references) that the name is neither passed by keyword nor referenced as a string. The executor records the final per-bucket counts and the irreducible `# noqa`/excluded total on this ticket (see AC).

### CLUSTER-1 — reconciler leaf handlers (10 violations)

`apply_inbound.py:135,177,205,224` and `apply_outbound.py:92,127,168,190,215`, all dispatched from `_LEAVES` in `typed_dispatch.py:56-70` and invoked at `:142` as `handler(mutation, **_leaf_kwargs)`.

Two hazards that make a naive rename unsafe:

- `client` is passed **unconditionally** (`typed_dispatch.py:137`: `_leaf_kwargs = {"client": client}`).
  Renaming it to `_client` is an immediate runtime `TypeError`, caught by no type checker.
- `repo_root` is gated by **runtime string introspection** (`typed_dispatch.py:128`:
  `accepts_repo_root = "repo_root" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw`). Renaming flips this to
  `False` and the dispatcher silently stops passing it — a cosmetic lint fix changing dispatch
  behaviour through a string comparison.

**Preferred resolution: normalize the leaves to `**_kwargs`.** This removes all 10 violations without a rename and decouples dispatch from parameter spelling. Decide once for all ten; do not rename piecemeal.

**Normalize only the UNUSED parameters — keep the ones the body reads.** "Normalize to `**_kwargs`" does not mean stripping every named parameter: several leaves DO read `client` (e.g. `apply_outbound.py` create/conflict) or `repo_root`, and those must stay as explicit named parameters (keeping them named is itself rename-free and ARG-clean because they are used). The `**_kwargs` catch-all replaces only the parameters that are accepted-but-unused in that leaf, so each leaf ends as `def _leaf(mutation, *, client=..., **_kwargs)` or `def _leaf(mutation, **_kwargs)` depending on what its body actually consumes. The invariant to preserve: every parameter the body reads is still delivered (the dispatcher passes client unconditionally and repo_root/binding_store by the string-introspection gate), and every unused one is absorbed by `**_kwargs`.

**Third string-introspected kwarg — `binding_store`.** `typed_dispatch.py` gates a THIRD kwarg by the identical runtime string check: `accepts_binding_store = "binding_store" in sig.parameters or _has_var_kw` (`:129`), and per ticket 1577 only leaves that explicitly declare `binding_store` receive it. Normalizing a leaf to `**_kwargs` sets `_has_var_kw=True`, so `accepts_binding_store` flips to `True` and EVERY normalized leaf now also receives `binding_store` (and `repo_root`). This is behaviour-preserving because the leaf body ignores the extra keyword — but it IS a change in what the dispatcher passes, so it must be pinned by a test (see AC): the observable reconciler result is identical, and a leaf that previously did not receive `binding_store` still produces the same events/effects when it now does.

### CLUSTER-2 — `OutboundMapper` Protocol conformance (7 violations)

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:89,90,91,93` and `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:44,45,46`. Names are pinned by the Protocol at `_backend.py:370-392`, implemented by two backends, and call sites pass **by keyword** (`outbound_field_diff.py:285-287,346-348`). Renaming is a contract break across a Protocol, two backends and two keyword call sites. `suppressed_out` (`jira_datacenter/backend.py:93`) is documented as accepted-and-ignored on purpose (ticket 8390) and the Protocol docstring at `_backend.py:379-383` mandates that behaviour.

**Resolution: `# noqa: ARG002` with a Protocol reference.** This is correct code that ARG cannot model — ruff concedes the general case is blocked on type inference (astral-sh/ruff#15952, open).

## Why no gate

`_`-prefixing is NOT a universally safe remediation here, contrary to a common assumption. Ruff's lead maintainer, astral-sh/ruff#10409: *"You could change `name: str` to `_name: str`, but that also carries some risk, since it will break for users that pass keyword arguments."* This codebase proves it: Cluster-1 renames break runtime dispatch, Cluster-2 renames break keyword call sites.

A survey of ~15 major Python projects found **no project that adopted ARG and later reverted** — but also that the exclusion is near-universal and always added in the same commit that first enabled ruff (attrs: `"ARG",  # unused arguments are normal when implementing interfaces`; pythondotorg: `# Django views/signals/admin methods have required unused args by framework contract`; Home Assistant: `# generic callbacks and setup methods create a lot of warnings`). Counter-examples exist and matter: beancount/fava runs ARG fully enabled with no exemptions at all, PlasmaPy for 3+ years.

Enabling ARG here would require carrying roughly **17 permanent inline `# noqa: ARG00x`** — a discretionary per-site exception mechanism, which this project has ruled against in favour of restrictions that are absolute or bounded by an invariant. If Cluster-1 is normalized to `**_kwargs` the irreducible count drops to about 7, which may change that calculus.

## Revisit

Record the irreducible exception count after the sweep. **The next rebar-janitor run must revisit whether to enable an ARG gate**, using that measured count rather than an estimate. That count and the revisit note are recorded as a `comment` on THIS ticket (`fc0c-e218-8b34-4858`) — the durable, queryable home for janitor findings — not in an out-of-tree scratch file. (An earlier draft cited `.joe-janitor/tools.md`, which does not exist in the repo; the ticket comment supersedes it.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every one of the 64 `ARG` violations is dispositioned by the Classification decision
      procedure — each into exactly one of buckets 1-6, with the bucket-appropriate action applied.
      After the sweep, `ruff check --select ARG src/rebar` reports ONLY the deliberately-retained
      set: the bucket-4 `# noqa`'d sites and the bucket-1 tracked-defect sites (no unclassified
      residual remains).
- [x] Every rename (buckets 5-6) is verified safe against keyword call sites AND against the
      parameter name appearing **as a string** (`getattr`, `setattr`, `monkeypatch.setattr`,
      `sig.parameters`, `**kwargs`), using `grep`, not semantic search alone.
- [x] Every bucket-4 (rename-unsafe) site carries a `# noqa: ARG00x` with a one-line reason that
      names the keyword call site or string reference making a rename unsafe.
- [x] Cluster-1 is resolved by one decision covering all ten leaves; with `**_kwargs`
      normalization, `typed_dispatch.py`'s `accepts_repo_root` introspection still selects the
      right handlers, and a test pins it.
- [x] The `binding_store` side effect of `**_kwargs` normalization is pinned: a test proves that a
      Cluster-1 leaf which (pre-change) did NOT receive `binding_store` now receives it yet
      produces an identical observable result (the extra keyword is inert), so `accepts_binding_store`
      flipping to `True` is behaviour-preserving.
- [x] Cluster-2 carries justified `# noqa: ARG002` referencing the Protocol, or an equivalent that
      does not break the Protocol contract or its keyword call sites.
- [x] The three real defects are NOT folded into this sweep — they remain tracked as

## Context / Problem
After S1, persistence has a cohesive owner but `BindingStore` still embeds forward/reverse identity transitions, pending/confirmed state, numeric-ID re-key, comment identity, absence grace, tombstones, and unretire policy. Production rich-text convergence also reaches through shallow `all_bindings()` and mutates an inner dictionary, bypassing any future policy seam.

## Outcome
Extract lifecycle decisions into a private policy owner operating on the repository original dictionaries, with the public facade retaining every existing method/signature. Add a narrow facade operation for rich-text emission state. Preserve shallow `all_bindings()` compatibility, but make the narrow operation the supported production mutation seam for the later caller cutover.

## Plan
1. Move cohesive forward/reverse, pending/confirmed, immutable-ID re-key, comment-map, absence/retirement, tombstone, suppression, and unretire call clusters into `binding_lifecycle.py`.
2. Keep the facade authoritative: it coordinates the lifecycle owner and repository unit-of-work; no adapter or reconciler caller receives a writable repository object.
3. Use open typed views over the same dictionaries. Unknown and legacy fields remain present and writable only through named policy operations.
4. Add `BindingStore.note_rich_emit(local_id, wire)` (or an equivalently narrow name) that preserves the current counter/hash behavior and missing-binding fail-open result. Do not change `all_bindings()` copy depth.
5. Preserve exact current failure choices: confirmed 404 grace/reset, moved-key repair, retired corruption fail-open, live corruption fail-closed, append-only comment identity, tombstone suppression, and explicit unretire.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Direct policy tests exercise both-index transitions and reload through the real repository after each state change.
- Table-driven tests cover duplicate bind, stale reverse cleanup, missing/corrupt forward state, three-404 retirement, 200 reset, numeric-ID move, legacy no-ID behavior, tombstone suppression/unretire, and changed/unchanged comment IDs.
- A narrow-operation test compares rich-emission hashes/counters and save behavior to the existing production sequence.
- Signature and shallow-query regression tests pin the facade compatibility surface.

## Compatibility / rollback
Facade delegates can be moved back without changing bytes or callers. This slice adds the narrow mutation operation but does not yet modify RP-04-owned apply files. No lifecycle thresholds, corruption disposition, copy-depth, stored schema, or identity-marker writer changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Given valid and corrupt forward/reverse combinations, every lifecycle operation preserves at-most-one identity and removes stale reverse entries only in the existing permitted cases (targeted single-key pops, never a guessed sweep).
- [x] Three confirmed 404s retire, a successful read resets absence, immutable numeric-ID lookup re-keys instead of retiring, and legacy entries retain current behavior.
- [x] Tombstoned issues suppress recreate with an alert until explicit unretire; retired corruption and alert-write failures retain their current fail-open boundaries.
- [x] Comment IDs remain append-only/change-gated and old records without the field remain readable without rewrite.
- [x] The narrow rich-emission operation matches current hash/counter/save behavior while missing bindings remain nonfatal.
- [x] Existing facade signatures and shallow `all_bindings()` semantics remain unchanged; no production adapter obtains direct repository mutation access.

## Correction: "safety-aborts ambiguous double binds" was not existing behavior
AC1 originally required that lifecycle operations "safety-abort ambiguous double binds". Verified against the reviewed base: no such abort exists. `bind_confirm` unconditionally overwrites the forward entry's `jira_key` and pops the old reverse key only when it differs; `unbind` and the numeric-ID re-key path likewise never refuse or raise. A repo-wide search for ambiguity/abort handling in `binding_store.py`, `binding_repository.py` and `peer_state.py` returns nothing.

AC1 is therefore corrected to the invariant that IS real and testable: at-most-one identity, maintained by targeted single-key reverse pops rather than by detecting or refusing ambiguity. Introducing an abort would be a behavior change, which this extraction slice is explicitly forbidden from making ("no lifecycle thresholds, corruption disposition, copy-depth, stored schema, or identity-marker writer changes"); if one is wanted it needs its own ticket and risk analysis. The genuine safety-abort in this epic belongs to S3, where interrupted-retirement completion aborts on any tombstone/forward/reverse mismatch - that is new behavior there, and the term is reserved for it to avoid two meanings across the tree.
baseline.summary: RP-02 S2 — Extract binding lifecycle policy and narrow mutation operations

## Problem
7-day store mining (2026-08-07..14) found 33 FORCE_CLOSE audit records, ~25 of them ADMINISTRATIVE closes — duplicate, obsolete, wontfix, stale-premise — where completing the described work is not the intent, so the completion verifier can never PASS them and operators reach for --force. A narrow attested-disposition path exists but is doubly scoped down: (a) class set — `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` = {duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated} only; (b) ticket type — close_precheck.py:64 gates the path to bugs, so an obsolete task/story/epic has NO truthful exit today. And the completion-FAIL message never mentions the path that exists: "it offered only 'complete the work' or '[operator-attested]' — attesting would have been a FALSE claim" (9b70). This is the single largest FORCE_CLOSE class.

## Fix (extends the EXISTING --class mechanism; no new flag)
1. Vocabulary: add obsolete (premise no longer holds; reason required), superseded (replaced by a named live ticket), wontfix (deliberate decision; reason required) to the single-sourced `CLOSE_CLASSES` (txn.py:168). Enumerated co-edits: common.schema.json#/$defs/close_class enum+description (same order), ticket_state.schema.json close_class description (:196-198), `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` AND `close_precheck._NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (both gain the three; their equality drift-guard tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:26 updated), the `transition.py` parser (existing `--class` gains the values; NO new --disposition flag), and `types.py` CloseClass.
2. Administrative subset, single-sourced: a new frozenset `close_disposition.ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES = {duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix}` — the classes valid on NON-BUG closes (not_a_bug/escalated stay bug-only vocabulary). Drift-guarded by a test asserting ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES < DISPOSITION_CLASSES and exact membership.
3. Write-side enforcement (gate-independent — cannot be skipped by --force or a disabled completion gate): extend `txn.transition_core`'s close-class guard (txn.py:260, today `ticket_type == "bug"`-gated) so (a) a non-bug close MAY carry --class only from ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES (anything else refused naming the allowed values — the enforcement point for not_a_bug/escalated staying bug-only); (b) obsolete/wontfix REQUIRE a reason (refusal when missing). The reason REUSES the existing `--reason` flag (transition.py:152-158) — today force-only, with an active refusal on plain transitions ("--reason is only meaningful with --force", transition.py:549-554): that guard is AMENDED to also admit `--reason` WITHOUT `--force` when the close carries a reason-capable administrative class (obsolete/wontfix; unchanged refusal otherwise). On a non-force administrative close the reason persists as a NEW `close_reason` key on the close STATUS event (present-only, mirroring close_class at txn.py:287; NOT force_close_reason, which stays the --force channel's fold). Threading co-edits: transition_core (and transition_compute) gain a `close_reason` parameter threaded from close_ticket/the CLI parse; reducer fold `_fold_close_metadata` (reducer/_processors_status.py:49) folds it; types.py ticket-state TypedDict (:138 area) + ticket_state.schema.json declare it.
4. Verification skip for administrative closes: a NEW explicit `_completion_precheck` branch — a close whose class is a reason-only ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASS (obsolete/wontfix, no replacement link) skips the AC/file-impact/billable-verifier checks and returns the disposition verdict (widening `_has_live_replacement_link`'s type-gate at close_precheck.py:64 alone would NOT route them: that function detects replacement links, which reason-only classes lack). Replacement-bearing classes route through the widened :64 gate; `_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked` (close_precheck.py:139, called at :508) widens from duplicate-only to {duplicate, superseded} so both demand a live replacement link (existing `find_replacement`, close_disposition.py:47); the plan-review claim gate is untouched.
5. Attestation for reason-only classes: `close_disposition.verdict()` (:92) today returns None unless find_replacement resolves a live ticket, and `decorate_manifest` (:114) signs that replacement — so obsolete/wontfix as-written would close UNSIGNED (the 738a trap). Extend both signatures: verdict() gains a `close_reason: str = ""` parameter (threaded from its precheck call site) and mints the reason-only verdict from (class + close_reason); decorate_manifest signs a `disposition: <class> reason: <text>` line for reason-only classes; replacement-bearing classes unchanged.
6. Discoverability: the close refusal surface is `close_precheck`'s CommandError assembly, which HAS ticket context — it appends the applicable-class enumeration (`--class` values valid for THIS ticket_type) to the completion-FAIL/refusal message; the static COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE constant stays generic (no per-ticket data in a module constant). The 9b70 incident is the RED oracle: a wontfix-shaped ticket's failure message must present a truthful exit.
7. Migration: existing FORCE_CLOSE records stay as-is; new administrative closes should have no reason to use --force.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The three new classes appear in every single-sourced consumer — txn.CLOSE_CLASSES, common.schema.json + ticket_state.schema.json, DISPOSITION_CLASSES, _NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES, types.py CloseClass — with the 738a equality drift-guard updated; ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES exists in close_disposition with exact membership {duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix} and a subset drift-guard test.
- [x] Non-bug tickets (task/story/epic fixture each) close with an administrative class without completion verification — reason-only classes via the new explicit precheck branch returning the disposition verdict; a non-bug close with not_a_bug/escalated (or any non-administrative class) is REFUSED in txn.transition_core naming allowed values; bug closes keep today's behavior.
- [x] obsolete/wontfix demand a reason (write-side refusal when missing, enforced in transition_core even with the completion gate off); the transition.py:549-554 "--reason only with --force" guard admits --reason WITHOUT --force for these classes (refusal unchanged otherwise); the reason threads close_ticket -> transition_core/transition_compute, persists as close_reason on the close event (distinct from force_close_reason), folds via _fold_close_metadata into reduced state, and typechecks (types.py); superseded/duplicate demand a live replacement link (_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked widened); store-event tests per class.
- [x] A reason-only disposition close mints a SIGNED disposition attestation whose manifest carries the class+reason line; replacement-bearing closes keep the replacement line; an unsigned close for a valid disposition is RED.
- [x] The close_precheck refusal/FAIL message enumerates the applicable --class values for the ticket's type; message test asserts the 9b70 wontfix scenario is offered a truthful exit; --force on an administrative-shaped close hints the disposition alternative.
- [x] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean (CI gate ran them on the merged change).
- [x] [operator-attested] Lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
  provenance: environment=Gerrit+GitHub Actions; principal=session operator (git-credential REST); privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — /a/changes/1794/detail showed LLM-Review +1, Verified +1; MERGED as 9844f6de35 on origin/main.
baseline.summary: Sanctioned administrative-disposition close path (duplicate/obsolete/superseded/wontfix/...) discoverable from the close-gate failure message

# OSS v1.0.0 community front door — contribution intake, governance, and release artifacts

## Context

rebar is technically near-1.0 (PyPI Trusted Publishing + PEP 740 attestations, immutable releases, `docs/api-stability.md` stability matrix, event-schema forward-compat) but the public contribution funnel is closed: GitHub (navapbc/rebar) is a read-only mirror with Issues and Discussions disabled (verified via API 2026-07-09: `has_issues: false`), and while CONTRIBUTING.md already documents an external Gerrit path (§1–§3), there is no GitHub-side intake, no governance/DCO/review-policy artifacts, and no user-facing changelog. Three converging assessments (internal repo audit; an external deep-research report; peer research across Go, Chromium, Qt, LibreOffice, Wikimedia, OpenStack, Eclipse) identify public intake + written governance as the only blockers to a credible v1.0.0.

Peer convergence establishes the design: KEEP Gerrit — Wikimedia reversed its GitLab migration in June 2024 over the review model (https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/GitLab/Migration_status), JGit/EGit migrated TO GerritHub rather than accept PRs (https://gitenterprise.me/2023/11/21/14-years-of-jgit-egit-code-reviews-migrated-to-gerrithub/) — and pair the wall with a ramp: bot-answered PRs (LibreOffice/Wikimedia pattern), a first-change tutorial, a shepherded-patch fallback, GitHub Issues as zero-friction intake (Go's model), DCO enforced at the Gerrit server (OpenStack TC resolution 2025-05-20, https://governance.openstack.org/tc/resolutions/20250520-replace-the-cla-with-dco-for-all-contributions.html), and skipped non-convergent ceremony (CODEOWNERS, GPG-signed tags, RC trains — each a recorded non-goal with rationale in a child).

Stars/forks/contributor counts are explicitly OUT of scope; success is artifact completeness and funnel quality.

Cross-child protocols (binding on all children):
- **Vote-semantics single source:** `docs/review-policy.md` (child wrathful-preregal-blobfish) is the sole authoritative DOCUMENT for Gerrit vote semantics; its table's content is transcribed from the code enums (`_TAG_SUFFIXES` in adapter.py + the merge-path tags in voter.py) — document-of-record and source-of-truth are distinct and both are named. Every other doc links to it rather than duplicating the table. Until it lands, CONTRIBUTING.md §2c remains the interim authority.
- **Ownership inversion for cross-links:** a child that CREATES a doc never forward-links to a sibling's not-yet-existing doc; the sibling that creates the later doc owns adding links into earlier docs. Dependency edges: PR-posture and review-policy each depend_on the onboarding tutorial (their artifacts link it).
- **Decisions live in the repo**, not only on tickets: design decisions are recorded as ADRs under `docs/adr/` or in the owning doc (e.g. `docs/releasing.md`), with a ticket comment pointing at the artifact.
- **Shepherded-patch DCO interplay:** a shepherded contribution needs the ORIGINAL author's `Signed-off-by` (contributor runs `git commit -s` before `git format-patch`) plus the shepherd's own sign-off added on amend — the OpenStack two-trailer convention; documented in both the DCO and PR-posture children.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All nine child stories closed: GitHub intake; PR posture; onboarding tutorial + CONTRIBUTING; README front door; DCO; governance docs; review policy; CHANGELOG; release hygiene / 1.0 declaration.
- [ ] The four pre-flight experiments (E1 fork-side UX with has_pull_requests=false; E2 Gerrit Forge Author ACL; E3 PR-event dependency audit; E4 rebar-ticket trailer policy for shepherded patches) are executed AND each dependent child's design is updated or explicitly confirmed against the outcome (outcome-framed: an experiment that invalidates an assumption must change the affected child before that child is worked). E3-discovered breakage is fixed (or ticketed via discovered_from) by the PR-posture child.
- [ ] The `docs/api-stability.md` pre-1.0 caveat flip and the Development Status classifier bump are staged for the v1.0.0 release change (release-hygiene child names the landing vehicle).
- [ ] Final consistency audit (epic-level, before epic close, owned by the epic executor): re-read CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, SUPPORT.md, README.md, and all new docs as one set; verify no artifact contradicts the Gerrit-primary workflow or another artifact (including the vote-semantics single-source rule); record the audit result as an epic comment.
- [ ] Cross-link completeness: `docs/release-notes.md` carries a pointer to CHANGELOG.md (owned by the changelog child); every new doc is reachable from CONTRIBUTING.md or README.md.
- [ ] GitHub intake works and is self-explanatory: Issues enabled with structured forms; an issue can be filed with no Gerrit account, no local checkout, and no knowledge beyond the form itself (verifiable from the rendered chooser, not a timing claim).
- [ ] The path from GitHub to a merged Gerrit change is documented end-to-end in one tutorial an outsider can follow with zero Nava-internal knowledge (measured by concrete checks in the onboarding child, e.g. no references to internal-only groups/layouts on the happy path).
- [ ] A no-Gerrit patch fallback is published. Authorship preservation via `git am` is promised only if experiment E2 confirms Gerrit's Forge Author permission is (or can be) granted; if E2 fails, the documented fallback is `Co-authored-by:` credit and the policy text says so (go/no-go, not an unconditional promise).
- [ ] Governance, review policy, DCO, and maintainer info are published, each grounded in a named peer convention (curl/CNCF, Chromium-CQ/Zuul, OpenStack/moby — URLs in the children).
- [ ] Release artifacts (CHANGELOG, dependabot, README front door, 1.0 declaration mechanics) match documented 2026 Python-tool convergence.
baseline.summary: OSS v1.0.0 community front door — contribution intake, governance, and release artifacts

## Context
Before merged Change 1847, at the parent of commit 034e17209c, tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py constructed `env = dict(os.environ)` and returned that mapping inside the `box` fixture value. A deliberate nested-pytest RED probe against that pre-fix revision placed a synthetic sentinel before PATH and observed pytest default-long traceback rendering print it; no real credential value was used or recorded. Commit 034e17209c repaired that defect: the current file at lines 149-165 now constructs a narrow PATH-plus-harness allowlist. This ticket records and verifies the already-landed repair; it does not claim the current fixture still copies the full environment. The performance ticket must not absorb this unrelated security fix.

## Plan
- Reproduce on the pre-fix revision with a synthetic first-position sentinel in the ambient environment and a deliberate assertion failure.
- Change the fixture boundary to pass only required environment variables while preserving the real bash subprocess environment needed by the tests.
- Audit sibling subprocess fixtures for the same `dict(os.environ)`-inside-rendered-fixture shape.
- Prove on the repaired revision that the synthetic sentinel never appears in pytest default-long failure output while the autodeploy suite remains behaviorally green.

## Scope and alternative rationale
The construct sweep separates two runtime carriers rather than deferring equivalent leaks. This parent and child dumbstruck-wonderful-xiphosuran own the eight decorated fixtures whose returned values pytest renders as function arguments; explicit allowlists are correct there because minimal-parent runs prove their consumers need only declared harness values. The remaining broad mappings are test-local or helper values exposed only when subprocess startup itself raises. Some intentionally forward the invoking pytest environment or environment-only live-service credentials, so applying the fixture allowlist would break their contract. Follow-up antiutopic-toadyish-goldfinch owns all 103 of those sites as one atomic shared representation-safe mapping migration, with a repository guard and exact child-value preservation test. A repo-wide allowlist was rejected because it would drop required values; independent per-file wrappers were rejected because they would duplicate the same diagnostic boundary without enforcement. Pytest `--tb=short` was a useful negative control but was rejected as remediation because it globally reduces debugging detail and only masks this traceback carrier; the repaired fixture boundary remains safe under the default long traceback. ADR 0041 governs durable LLM diagnostic fields rather than pytest fixture representations; its fail-closed allowlist posture is nevertheless followed for these decorated fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] A deterministic regression test fails on the pre-fix revision because a synthetic ambient secret appears in captured pytest failure rendering.
  provenance: environment=sanitized-red-probe-034e17209c; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=simulation — real nested pytest default-long traceback with first-position synthetic sentinel
- [x] The synthetic secret is absent from failure output after the fix.
- [x] Required PATH and autodeploy environment behavior remains covered through the real bash subprocess.
- [x] Sibling occurrences are inventoried and either fixed or linked as follow-ups.
- [x] [operator-attested] Repository gates and Gerrit votes pass before closure.
  provenance: environment=gerrit-ci-run-32101886011; principal=rebar-ci-bot; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — canonical Gerrit Verified and LLM-Review gates for merged change 1847
baseline.summary: Prevent autodeploy test failures from printing ambient credentials

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`criterion_prompt_id` — the single logical→physical criterion-id map both review gates delegate to — hardcodes the plan-review prompt prefix (`PLAN_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "plan-review-"` at `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:31`, applied unconditionally at `ids.py:42`). So a project **code-review** criterion resolves into the plan-review prompt namespace, the first of five seams that drop project code-review criteria (root cause on superseded bug 8a4b). This is the shared abstraction the other four seams consume, so it lands first.

## Approach

Make the resolver gate-aware, additively:

- Add a keyword-only `gate_key: str = "plan_review"` parameter to
  `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id, *, gate_key="plan_review")`.
- Introduce a `_PROMPT_PREFIX = {"plan_review": "plan-review-", "code_review": "code-review-"}`
  map in `ids.py`; select the prefix by `gate_key`; an unknown `gate_key` raises `CriteriaError`
  (imported from `rebar.llm.criteria.model`, confirmed present at
  `src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py`).
- The `.`→`-` namespace rewrite is unchanged, so `project.foo` + `code_review` →
  `code-review-project-foo` and stays filesystem-safe and injective per the existing charset
  invariant documented in the module docstring.

The default `"plan_review"` preserves today's behavior byte-for-byte, so the two existing callers (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:302`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:487`) need **no** change and plan-review parity is guaranteed by construction. Code-review call sites (introduced by the fan-in and eval children) pass `gate_key="code_review"` explicitly.

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Making `gate_key` *required* — it would force editing `eval.py:419`'s existing call, colliding with the eval-admission child's file set and breaking the disjoint-file decomposition; the default is the historically-correct value, not a silent bug. (b) Registering the prefix on the gate via `criteria.overlay.register_gate` — adds import-order coupling to gate registration for no caller benefit; the forward-only map is the pattern the module docstring already commits to.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py` — add `gate_key` param + `_PROMPT_PREFIX` map.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` — NEW file; the shared test file later
  children extend. This child adds the resolver unit tests only.

## Testing

- Happy path: `criterion_prompt_id("project.foo", gate_key="code_review") == "code-review-project-foo"`;
  `criterion_prompt_id("F1", gate_key="plan_review") == "plan-review-F1"`.
- Parity/default: `criterion_prompt_id("F1") == "plan-review-F1"` (no `gate_key` given) — existing
  plan-review behavior unchanged.
- Edge: an unknown `gate_key` raises `CriteriaError`; cross-gate injectivity — no code-review
  project id collides with any plan-review physical id.

Tier: unit (pure function, no I/O).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `criterion_prompt_id("project.foo", gate_key="code_review")` returns
      `"code-review-project-foo"`; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k resolver`.
- [ ] `criterion_prompt_id("F1")` (no gate_key) still returns `"plan-review-F1"`, proving
      plan-review parity; verified by the same `-k resolver` selector.
- [ ] An unknown `gate_key` raises `CriteriaError`; verified by the same `-k resolver` selector.
baseline.summary: Gate-key the criterion-id resolver (criterion_prompt_id)

baseline.description:
## Problem
`workflow/steps.py::GATE_POLICIES` (`default`/`strict`/`advisory`) fails a workflow step by exact string membership of `finding["severity"]` in a fixed list. Research confirmed this `gate` step is NOT wired into any of the three real production gate workflows (plan-review, code-review, completion-verification each use their own bespoke `_decide`/`_reconcile` ops instead) -- `steps.gate` is exercised only by a retained sample workflow (`workflow/examples/review_skeleton.yaml`) and a schema-round-trip test fixture (`tests/e2e/fixtures/roundtrip-demo.yaml`), both of which feed it plain, severity-only findings (a generic finder+verify pass, not `pass3_decide` output) with no `priority`/ `decision` field at all. Migrating `fail_on_severity` to a priority-only check would silently make the demo/fixture gate never fail (every finding would default to `priority: 0.0`), losing its illustrative value with no live behavior actually fixed (nothing real depends on this gate's severity check today).

## Approach
ADD priority-threshold support to `GATE_POLICIES` ALONGSIDE the existing `fail_on_severity` (expand, not a replacement) so the gate step works correctly for both today's severity-only inputs (the demo/fixture) and any future caller that supplies `pass3_decide`-shaped findings carrying `priority`: each policy gains a `priority_threshold: float | None` key (`None` = never fails on priority, matching `advisory`'s empty `fail_on_severity: []`). Concrete values: `default: 0.95` (`review_kernel.decide.DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` -- the same source of truth `pass3_decide` uses for its own BLOCK decision, imported not duplicated as a literal); `strict: 0.5` (a concrete, lower-than-default value -- `strict` is meant to catch more than `default`); `advisory: None` (never fails on priority, matching its existing empty `fail_on_severity: []`). The `gate` step (`steps.py:215-239`) fails a finding if EITHER its `severity` is in the policy's `fail_on_severity` list (unchanged behavior) OR its `priority` (when present and numeric) is `>= priority_threshold`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Each policy in `GATE_POLICIES` gains a `priority_threshold` key: `default: 0.95` (import
  of `review_kernel.decide.DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`, not a duplicated literal), `strict: 0.5`,
  `advisory: None`. `fail_on_severity` is NOT removed from any policy.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_steps.py` passes unchanged for every existing
  severity-only test case (`test_gate_fails_on_high_severity`,
  `test_gate_strict_fails_on_any_finding`, `test_gate_advisory_never_fails`,
  `test_gate_unknown_policy_falls_back_to_default`) -- proving this is additive, not a
  behavior change for findings that only carry `severity`.
- [x] A new test proves the additive priority path using the `default` policy at two priority
  values (NOT `strict`, whose `max_findings: 0` already fails any non-empty finding set
  regardless of priority and so cannot isolate the priority-threshold effect): a finding with
  no `severity` key and `priority: 0.99` fails `default`; the same shape with `priority: 0.5`
  does not.
- [x] A new test confirms `strict` still fails on a priority-only finding purely via its
  existing `max_findings: 0` clause (a consistency check that the additive `priority_threshold`
  field does not interfere with `strict`'s pre-existing behavior).
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_review_skeleton.py` passes unchanged (the demo workflow
  that actually exercises `steps.gate` end-to-end keeps working exactly as before, since its
  severity-only findings never trigger the new priority path).

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit test against the real `gate` workflow step function. Oracle: the step's returned pass/fail verdict for a finding carrying `severity` only, `priority` only, or neither, under each named policy. Contrast case (test-design.md sec.6, config-effect): run a severity-less, priority-only finding through `default` at `priority=0.99` (fails, `>=0.95`) and at `priority=0.5` (passes, `<0.95`) -- the two outcomes differing proves the `priority_threshold` read path is real, not merely parsed. Regression check: the existing severity-only test suite and the `review_skeleton.yaml` end-to-end test both stay green, proving additive-not-breaking.
baseline.summary: Migrate fail_on_severity workflow gate to a priority threshold

# 1.0 release hygiene: dependabot, classifier bump, stability-promise flip, RC skip (tag signing: explicit skip)

## Why

Final mechanical artifacts for the 1.0 declaration, sized to what 2026 peers actually do — which REVERSES two earlier assumptions. (1) Signed git tags are no longer convergent: of CPython/pip/ruff/uv/pytest/httpx, zero sign new release tags in 2026 (CPython dropped GPG at 3.14 per PEP 761; ruff/uv/httpx use lightweight tags); the baseline is annotated tags + GitHub immutable releases + PEP 740 attestations — all already in place here. (2) RC trains are not convergent: pydantic v2 shipped beta→final in 13 days with zero rcs; attrs/structlog skipped 1.0 entirely; the load-bearing artifact is the written compatibility policy, which `docs/api-stability.md` already is.

## What

- `.github/dependabot.yml`: `github-actions` ecosystem ONLY, `interval: monthly`, one catch-all group. The `cooldown` key is **intentionally omitted** — it is in production use in pip's own config (https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml), but its schema status was disputed in review and its value here is marginal (it only delays update PRs a few days); omitting it removes any dependence on a contested feature. Revisit trigger: update-PR noise. Record this omission decision as one line in the file header.
- **Mirror-interaction decision (recorded in the file header + docs/releasing.md):** this config shape is the pip/pydantic GitHub-native pattern — NOT what Gerrit peers do (they run bespoke bots pushing bumps as Gerrit changes: Wikimedia LibraryUpgrader, OpenStack requirements automation). Since Dependabot's output is a GitHub PR and PRs cannot merge here, Dependabot PRs are ADVISORY NOTIFICATIONS: the maintainer reads the diff, lands the equivalent bump via a Gerrit change, and closes the PR — Dependabot is another shepherded patch author under the PR-as-intake posture. The lockdown workflow exempts `dependabot[bot]` — owned by story **nonsecular-arthritic-sidewinder** (artifact: `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml`, job-level actor guard); this file's header names that workflow file explicitly. Rejected alternatives, one line each in the header: bespoke Gerrit-pushing bot (peer pattern; overkill for a monthly actions-only stream — captured as idea misogynic-cerulean-goldfish); alerts-only with no version-update PRs (loses the ready-made diff; security alerts fire regardless and remain on). No `pip` ecosystem entry — version updates act on pins/lockfiles; rebar's unpinned `>=` core deps give them nothing but noise (rationale in header). Add a `uv` block only if a `uv.lock` is ever committed.
- Staged for the v1.0.0 release change: bump `Development Status :: 4 - Beta` → `5 - Production/Stable` (pyproject classifier) and flip the pre-1.0 caveat in `docs/api-stability.md` so the stability matrix becomes the operative SemVer promise. **Durable staging record (in-repo, not a ticket promise):** `docs/releasing.md` gains a "1.0 declaration" subsection stating exactly these two edits land in the v1.0.0 release change itself, so the requirement survives independent of any tracker.
- `docs/releasing.md` decision records:
  - Tag signing: SKIPPED, with rationale (2026 peer baseline; attestations cover artifact provenance) and revisit triggers (workflow compromise entering the threat model, or a downstream consumer asking to verify tags). Confirm annotated tags remain the practice and immutable releases stay on.
  - RC: SKIPPED (the recorded decision). Rationale: an RC only yields data if someone runs it; with no external adopters, `--pre` installs ≈ 0 and `1.0.1` is the de-facto rc. Revisit trigger: an external adopter volunteering to test. Conditional constraint recorded alongside (today's automation is RC-unsafe): `release.yml` fires on ALL `v*` tags, passes `--latest` unconditionally to `gh release create`, and runs the MCP-registry publish job — a hypothetical `v1.0.0rc1` tag would be marked Latest AND published to the MCP registry. The note must state: no rc-form tag may be pushed unless release.yml first gains a prerelease guard (detect `rc` in the tag → `--prerelease`, not `--latest`; skip the MCP-registry job). PEP 440 spelling (`1.0.0rc1`, not `-rc.1`) used in the constraint text. This story does NOT modify release.yml.
  - Deferral list as non-goals: SBOM/license-scan tooling beyond GitHub's dependency-graph export; Renovate (see idea misogynic-cerulean-goldfish); a lockfile for optional extras (revisit post-1.0).
- Verify at execution: `git tag -l 'v*'` shows no pre-existing rc-form tags contradicting the note.

## Scope

IN: `.github/dependabot.yml`; docs/releasing.md decision records (tag signing, RC skip + guard constraint, 1.0-declaration staging subsection, deferrals). OUT: modifying release.yml; executing the release (the classifier bump + api-stability flip are EXECUTED in the 1.0 release change, not here — here they are only recorded as staged); contract-freeze code work (exit codes / error envelope / MCP schema pin — tracked elsewhere); SBOM tooling; CI matrix changes (Windows explicitly out — classifiers claim POSIX/macOS, consistent today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dependabot.yml` committed — prove: `test -f .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -c "package-ecosystem" .github/dependabot.yml` = 1; `grep -q "github-actions" .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -q "interval: monthly" .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -q 'patterns' .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -qv "cooldown" .github/dependabot.yml` (key omitted) and the header comment records the omission decision — prove: `grep -qi "cooldown" .github/dependabot.yml` matches only in a comment line.
- [ ] Advisory-PR flow documented — prove: `grep -qi "advisory" .github/dependabot.yml` and `grep -q "lockdown.yml" .github/dependabot.yml` (header names the exemption artifact); `grep -qi "gerrit" .github/dependabot.yml`.
- [ ] Dependabot accepts the config — prove: after push, the Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot view shows the update job scheduled with no config-parse error.
- [ ] docs/releasing.md decisions present — prove: `grep -qi "tag signing" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -q "1.0.0rc1" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -q -- "--latest" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -qi "SBOM" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -qi "renovate" docs/releasing.md`.
- [ ] 1.0-declaration staging subsection present — prove: `grep -qi "Production/Stable" docs/releasing.md` and `grep -q "api-stability" docs/releasing.md` (the subsection names both staged edits and their landing vehicle).
- [ ] No rc-form tags exist — prove: `git tag -l | grep -c rc` = 0.
baseline.summary: 1.0 release hygiene: dependabot, classifier bump, stability-promise flip, RC decision

## Context

rebar hard-codes the git remote name `origin` at every ticket-branch network site, so the shared ticket store MUST be reachable as `origin`. In our split-residency setup (code reviewed via a `gerrit` remote; the `tickets` branch's source of truth on GitHub for the GitHub Actions -> Jira sync) this forces `origin`=GitHub and leaves no config seam. Parallels the earlier `tickets_branch()` migration (closed task `rich-gravel-twain`) which centralized the *branch* name; this does the same for the *remote* name.

## What

Add a `sync.remote` config key (default `"origin"`), resolved through the normal precedence (config-file `[sync] remote` + `REBAR_SYNC_REMOTE` env, the same generic mechanism as `sync.push`), exposed via a `tickets_remote()` helper mirroring `tickets_branch()`, and thread it through every currently-hardcoded site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SyncConfig` gains `remote: str = "origin"` and `_SECTIONS["sync"]` coerces it
      in `src/rebar/config.py`; `REBAR_SYNC_REMOTE` works via the existing generic
      env layer (no bespoke env wiring) and participates in the config-cache signature.
- [ ] New `config.tickets_remote(root)` helper mirrors `config.tickets_branch(root)`.
- [ ] Every hard-coded `"origin"` network site uses the resolved remote:
      `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (presence guard + push/fetch/ref),
      `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` (`reconverge` fetch/verify + `_do_reconverge`),
      `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` (`_push_pending`),
      `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (`_mount_or_create_branch` and
      `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`).
- [ ] Default behavior is unchanged when unset (still `origin`); the existing suite passes.
- [ ] New unit tests cover: default resolves to `origin`; `[sync] remote` config and
      `REBAR_SYNC_REMOTE` env each override; a network site uses the configured remote.
- [ ] Project docs updated for our actual setup (origin=GitHub tickets+mirror,
      gerrit=Gerrit code review): `CLAUDE.md` git-workflow section + the new key in
      `docs/config.md`.

## Out of scope

- Tier-2 init "split-residency awareness" (warn when the sync remote looks like a
  Gerrit host) — tracked separately.
- Changing this repo's actual remote layout (`origin` stays GitHub).
baseline.summary: Make the tickets sync remote configurable (sync.remote, default origin)

## Target
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — **786 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (14 lines of headroom).

Fourteen lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer. Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the complexity ratchet shows no new or increased entries.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.
baseline.summary: Split _commands/init.py (786 LOC) along its concern boundary

## Why
Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S1. The feature-branch pattern needs Gerrit-side changes: vote-carry for re-merges after main advances (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE), an explicitly pinned submit type (currently unset/inherited — FF-only or cherry-pick would defeat atomic merge-back), and a bounded write path for merge commits + feature branches.

## Context / Problem
LLM failure classification is duplicated in exactly ONE place: the context-length phrase list is byte-identical in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py:148-157` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:316-329`; `failure.py:144-147` records why ("kept local so this low-level boundary module has no dependency on the plan_review package — the two must stay in sync"). A fix to one silently leaves the other stale — the instalment pattern the review found.

## Approach
**Scope reduction — read this first.** The genuine content is ONE duplication: the eight-phrase `_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS` tuple copied byte-for-byte into `sizing.py`. The other three consolidations the original plan proposed are WITHDRAWN, not deferred: the retryable→exit-code mapping is ALREADY centralised in `_cli/_llm_commands.py:45` (`_llm_error_exit_code`) and `:64-100` (`_disposition_exit_code`), called by three verbs (`:147`, `:157`, `:231`, `:336`) plus `_commands/claim.py:120-123` and `_commands/composer.py:778-781`, so there is no fourth hand-rolled copy; the `structured.py` message merge is harmful and was decided against in a closed, merged bug (see Deliberate divergences); and the MCP payload helper composes no exit code at all. What remains is a one-line import change plus its guard.

`sizing.is_context_limit_error` stops carrying its own tuple and reads `failure._CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS` instead. The `def is_context_limit_error` MUST STAY in `sizing.py` — `orchestrator.py:72` binds `_is_context_limit_error = sizing.is_context_limit_error` at import time and `test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:45` monkeypatches the name as a string, so a re-export in its place would desynchronise both. The direction `sizing → failure` introduces no cycle (`failure.py` imports only `rebar.llm.errors`; `sizing.py:26-32` already imports `rebar.llm.config`, `.errors`, `.model_classes`, `.runner`) and preserves the boundary constraint `failure.py:144` records.

Guard: the eight-phrase CONJUNCTION appears in exactly one file. Match the co-occurrence of all eight literals within a single expression (per the epic's rule 2 — never a single common token such as `"context"`), exempt the owner `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, honour a `# context-hints-ok: <reason>` line marker.

### Deliberate divergences this story must NOT collapse
- `workflow/completion_failures.py:46-79` `_is_token_exhaustion` is a THIRD, intentionally different
  classifier: it omits the bare `"context"` substring the other two carry ("without mistaking
  generic context text") and keys off a normalized `finish_reason` set (`:52-60`). Folding it in
  would make any message containing the word "context" read as token exhaustion.
- `structured._BAD_STOP_REASONS` (`structured.py:616-627`) is NOT a copy of `failure.message_for`
  (`failure.py:355`): it is keyed by finish/stop reason (`refusal`/`max_tokens`/`length`/
  `content_filter`/`error`) with EXCEPTION text as values (raised at `structured.py:646,648,676`),
  while `message_for` is keyed by the disjoint 8-member `ResolutionClass` vocabulary and returns
  operator remedy prose. The key spaces share no member, so `message_for("refusal")` is `None` and
  `check_stop_reason` would raise with no message. Bug `injurious-definable-badger` (closed, landed
  `0e41876787` via Gerrit 1525) decided this: "Leave `check_response`'s raise text unchanged."
- `_llm_commands.py:188-190` (`scan-spec`) returns a flat exit **1** on `LLMError`; its MCP twin
  `_mcp_llm.py:109-133` has no `except` at all. Neither joins the disposition mapping.
- `_llm_commands.py:244-246` (`verify-completion`) carries an extra rule from bug 2a6f
  (`verdict_obtainable is False → 11`) and no INDETERMINATE→2 arm.
- `close_precheck.py:691-714` additionally calls `failure.log_degrade` and
  `failure.close_gate_remedy`, and embeds the message in a `CommandError` instead of writing
  `llm-degrade: …` to stderr as the CLI helpers do.
- `_disposition_exit_code` reads `result["verdict"]` (both the plan-review string and the nested
  code-review dict) and calls `plan_review.resign.classify_plan_review_attestation`; neither is
  reachable from an `LLMOutcome` or a `coverage` dict, so no `exit_code_for(...)` can replace it.

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` (drop the local tuple, import the owner's); `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (comment update only — the tuple is already correct); `tests/unit/test_context_hints_single_source.py` (new; flat, as `tests/unit/llm/` does not exist).

Explicitly OUT of scope, for the reasons above: `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py`.

## Testing
Guard: the conjunction resolves to one file under `src/rebar` with the owner exempt, and is proven to FLAG by reintroducing a second copy in a temp fixture, not just to pass. Namesakes it must leave untouched: `run_failure.py:190-191`, `enrich.py:47` (docstrings quoting the phrases as prose), `completion_failures.py:56,59,73`.

Pinning — must pass with no assertion edits, all under `tests/unit/`: `test_llm_failure_classifier.py` (`:188-211`, both classifiers agree on a wrapped context error, disagree on a refusal); `test_change_input_not_an_outage_43d4.py::test_the_new_prefix_does_not_itself_look_like_a_context_limit` (`:245-266`, the sharpest guard on this tuple); `test_plan_review.py::test_is_context_limit_error_and_ladder` (`:1331`, reaches the predicate via the import-time alias `orchestrator._is_context_limit_error`); `test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py` (`:45`, monkeypatches `sizing.is_context_limit_error` by string — the `def` must survive); `test_llm_failure_matrix.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The eight-phrase list has exactly one definition under `src/rebar`; checked by
  `grep -rln 'too many tokens' src/rebar` returning exactly `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, and by the
  new guard test.
- [x] `sizing.is_context_limit_error` still exists as a `def` in `plan_review/sizing.py` and reads
  the owner's tuple; checked by
  `grep -c 'def is_context_limit_error' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` returning `1` and
  `grep -n '_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` returning a hit.
- [x] The three legitimate namesakes survive; checked by `grep -rln 'token limit' src/rebar`
  returning exactly `llm/failure.py` and `llm/run_failure.py`, and by
  `grep -c 'context_length_exceeded' src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` returning `3`.
- [x] `completion_failures.py::_is_token_exhaustion` is unchanged; checked by
  `git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` being empty.
- [x] No exit-code or message behaviour changes; checked by `git diff origin/main` over
  `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`,
  `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` and `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` being empty.
- [x] The guard FAILS when a second copy is introduced, not merely passes clean; checked by the
  guard test's own negative case.
- [x] The five pinning suites named in Testing pass with no assertion edits; checked by `pytest`
  over them and by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` showing only additions.
- [x] Net non-test line count is negative (the epic's consolidation guarantee); checked by
  `git show --numstat` on this story's commit, excluding tests.

baseline.description:
## Why

MCP tools carry no behavior annotations, so clients cannot present safe UI or
confirmation flows. rebar already has the semantic information internally —
reads are separate from writes, writes are hidden under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`,
Jira-live and LLM tools are call-gated — but none of it is exposed as the MCP
`ToolAnnotations` hints (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`,
`openWorldHint`) that the spec defines for exactly this purpose.

## What

Annotate every registered tool via `FastMCP.tool(annotations=ToolAnnotations(...))`
across the three registrars (`register_read_tools` in `_mcp_reads.py`,
`register_llm_tools` in `_mcp_llm.py`, `register_write_tools` in `_mcp_writes.py`).
Confirmed feasible: `mcp` 1.28.1 exposes `ToolAnnotations` with all four hint
fields and `FastMCP.tool` accepts `annotations`.

Mapping policy:

- **Read tools** -> `readOnlyHint: true`.
- **Additive writes** (create/comment/tag/link/edit/claim/transition/set_*) ->
  `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`; `idempotentHint: true` where
  the op is idempotent (e.g. tag/untag).
- **Destructive/irreversible** (archive/delete/compact, reconcile-live) ->
  `destructiveHint: true`.
- **Outward-reaching** (LLM review/verify, Jira reconcile, `run_workflow`) ->
  `openWorldHint: true`.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `_mcp_llm.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`. Annotations are hints
only — no behavior change. Add/adjust a parity test if the interface suite pins
tool metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `@mcp.tool()` in the three registrars carries a `ToolAnnotations`
  consistent with the mapping policy above.
- [ ] Read tools are `readOnlyHint: true`; delete/archive/reconcile-live are
  `destructiveHint: true`; LLM/Jira/workflow tools are `openWorldHint: true`.
- [ ] The server still builds and starts; existing MCP/interface tests pass.
- [ ] No functional behavior of any tool changes.
baseline.summary: Annotate MCP tools with behavior hints (read-only/destructive/idempotent/open-world)

baseline.description:
Activity-based liveness for LLM gate ops using `agent.run_sync()`-compatible mechanisms: a per-request READ timeout (bounds a hung MODEL, at the HTTP layer) + a per-TOOL timeout (bounds a hung ASYNC/MCP tool), layered on the step caps the runner ALREADY derives. NO total-runtime timeout, NO async stream-event watchdog (deferred).

## Why
A single hard total-runtime timeout truncates healthy multi-minute / large-context (1M-token) runs; liveness must be gauged by ACTIVITY, not total elapsed time. But the runner uses `agent.run_sync()` exclusively — a blocking synchronous call with no concurrent stream-event hooks. The async idle-watchdog pattern (LangGraph/Claude-SDK) needs `agent.run()`/`run_stream_events` + an event loop this runner does not have. So liveness is achieved at request+tool granularity WITHOUT asyncio.

## What
- **Per-request READ timeout (both execution modes — `single_turn` structured calls AND `agentic` tool-using runs) — the PRIMARY, verified mechanism.** Set `httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s, connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` (a total of `cfg.timeout_s` with a tight connect) on the shared `httpx.AsyncClient` story arcticduck constructs, passed in via the EXISTING seam `_build_retrying_anthropic_model(..., http_timeout=<httpx.Timeout>)` (arcticduck committed that param in `runner.py` — review this story with `--ref` at the stack HEAD). This REUSES `cfg.timeout_s` (already the per-request budget, today wired only to `model_settings['timeout']`) — NO new `llm_request_timeout_s` key (would duplicate it). Bounds a HUNG MODEL (no bytes) — the real, common failure. VERIFIED under `run_sync` by arcticduck's spike (an httpx read/timeout fires at the transport). It is Anthropic-path-only (OpenAI/Google build their own httpx clients — acceptable; the gates run on Anthropic). NO duplication with `model_settings['timeout']`: on the ANTHROPIC path rebar uses arcticduck's CUSTOM `httpx.AsyncClient`, so THIS client's `httpx.Timeout` is the authoritative per-request bound; the pre-existing `model_settings['timeout'] = float(cfg.timeout_s)` (runner.py:288-289) governs the OTHER providers (OpenAI/Google), which use pydantic-ai's internally-built client, not ours. Same value, different provider paths — one authoritative mechanism per path, not two competing on one path. Interaction with the retry transport (correct, not a bug): a per-ATTEMPT read timeout raises `httpx.TimeoutException`, which is in arcticduck's retry set — so a transiently-slow model is retried; a PERSISTENTLY hung model times out each attempt, exhausts `llm_retry_max_attempts`, and surfaces `LLMUnavailableError` (classified WAIT_AND_RETRY by mamba). Bounded either way, no total-runtime cap.
- **Per-TOOL timeout — bounds ASYNC/MCP tools (an honest, verified scope).** Add `tool_timeout=cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s` to the shared `Agent(...)` construction kwargs (flows to all three `Agent(model, **kwargs)` sites; a no-op on `single_turn` where `tools=[]`). VERIFIED offline: `Agent(tool_timeout=0.3)` CANCELS an ASYNC tool (`await asyncio.sleep(3)`) at ~0.3s — but is a NO-OP for a SYNC blocking tool (`time.sleep(3)` waited the full 3s), because pydantic-ai uses async cancellation which cannot interrupt sync code that blocks the loop. rebar's in-process tools (`filesystem_tools`, `rebar_tools`) are SYNC, so `tool_timeout` primarily protects MCP/network toolsets (async); the sync in-process tools are fast (file/ticket reads) and a looping/slow one is bounded instead by the step caps. When `tool_timeout` fires it CANCELS the tool and feeds a soft timeout error back to the MODEL (which adapts / can finish) — it is a liveness BOUND, not a run-aborting classified failure — it raises NO exception into the runner (so NO new classification arm is needed); the model simply receives a tool error and proceeds. This honest scope (async-tool bound + sync-tool caveat) is the correction over an earlier over-claim.
- **Step caps: ALREADY PRESENT — reused, not re-added.** The runner already derives `request_limit = max(1, ceil(max_iterations/2))` and `tool_calls_limit = max(8, max_iterations)` from `cfg.max_iterations` and applies them via `UsageLimits` on `run_sync` (pinned by arawana). Those DERIVED caps ARE the runaway-loop bound and the backstop for a repeatedly-slow sync tool; this story adds NO duplicate limit config knobs.
- **Deferred (ADR content only, NOT built):** the sub-event stream-idle-watchdog needs the async `agent.run()` migration, conflicting with the exclusive `run_sync` design. This story authors the ADR CONTENT at `docs/adr/00XX-async-liveness-watchdog.md` (placeholder number; blackbear, sole ADR owner, records/numbers it) with Context/Decision/Consequences on why it is deferred.

## Verification (probes that actually cross the mechanism)
- **Read timeout:** a MockTransport whose handler sleeps past a small `read` timeout trips `httpx.ReadTimeout` UNDER `agent.run_sync()` (the arcticduck seam), proving it fires in the synchronous runner; a MockTransport that responds JUST UNDER the read timeout completes normally (healthy-long-run not aborted).
- **Tool timeout:** an `Agent(tool_timeout=<small>)` with a deliberately-sleeping ASYNC tool is CANCELLED at ~the timeout (asserted by elapsed << tool sleep); the run continues (soft error to the model). A companion assertion documents that a SYNC blocking tool is NOT interrupted (the known caveat) — so the test pins reality, not an over-claim.
- **No total-runtime / no-asyncio:** a test greps the gate path to assert no total-runtime timer and no new event loop / `asyncio.run` in the agentic run path beyond the existing teardown.

## Scope
- ONE new `LLMConfig` key: `llm_tool_timeout_s` (default 120), read via `_llm_int` from `[llm]` + `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S`. The per-request read timeout REUSES `cfg.timeout_s` (no new key). Regenerate `docs/env-vars.md`; add `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S` to `test_config_llm.py`'s `_clean` fixture; document both in `docs/config.md`.
- Wire `httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s, connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` into arcticduck's `_build_retrying_anthropic_model(http_timeout=...)`; add `tool_timeout=cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s` to the shared `Agent(...)` kwargs.
- NOT in scope: any total-runtime cap (rejected); the async stream-event watchdog (deferred, ADR content only); new step-cap config knobs (derived caps already exist); making rebar's sync tools async or thread-cancellable (a follow-on if sync-tool bounding is ever needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `LLMConfig.llm_tool_timeout_s` (120) exists, read from `[llm]` + `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S`; the per-request read timeout reuses `cfg.timeout_s` (no duplicate key). `docs/env-vars.md` regenerated (drift gate passes); `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S` in `test_config_llm.py`'s `_clean` fixture.
- [ ] `httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s, connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` is passed into `_build_retrying_anthropic_model(http_timeout=...)` for both execution modes (single_turn + agentic); a sleeping MockTransport trips `httpx.ReadTimeout` under `run_sync` (probe), and a just-under-timeout MockTransport completes normally (healthy run not aborted).
- [ ] `tool_timeout=cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s` is on the shared `Agent(...)` kwargs; a sleeping ASYNC tool is cancelled at ~the timeout (probe), with a companion assertion documenting the sync-tool no-op caveat.
- [ ] No total-runtime timeout and no new asyncio event loop are introduced in the gate path (asserted by a grep/structural test); the existing derived step caps (arawana) are unchanged.
- [ ] The deferred-async-watchdog ADR CONTENT exists at `docs/adr/00XX-async-liveness-watchdog.md` (Context/Decision/Consequences; numbered/recorded by blackbear).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (build+pass `httpx.Timeout`; add `tool_timeout` to the shared Agent kwargs), `src/rebar/llm/config.py` (one LLMConfig key + `from_env`), `docs/config.md`, `docs/env-vars.md` (regenerated), `docs/adr/00XX-async-liveness-watchdog.md` (content), `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py` (`_clean`), `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py` (new — read-timeout + async-tool-timeout + sync-caveat + no-total-runtime probes).

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, httpx 0.28.1, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
Agent.__init__ has tool_timeout: True;  Agent.run_sync has usage_limits: True
httpx.Timeout(600.0, read=300.0, connect=10.0).read == 300.0   (per-request read timeout settable)
UsageLimits fields include total_tokens_limit
Agent(tool_timeout=0.3) + ASYNC tool (await asyncio.sleep(3)) -> CANCELLED at 0.31s, run continues ('done')
Agent(tool_timeout=0.3) + SYNC  tool (time.sleep(3))        -> NOT interrupted, waited 3.02s (async cancel can't stop sync)
rebar tools (filesystem_tools/rebar_tools) are SYNC defs    -> tool_timeout bounds MCP/async tools, not these
arcticduck committed _build_retrying_anthropic_model(..., http_timeout=) in runner.py (the wiring seam)
```
These are pydantic-ai/httpx LIBRARY facts (not rebar symbols; bug succinct-formable-kite). The read timeout on the shared client is the primary hung-MODEL bound (verified via arcticduck's spike); the tool timeout is an honest async/MCP-tool bound with a documented sync no-op caveat.
baseline.summary: Activity-based liveness: per-request timeout + step caps + idle-watchdog (no total-runtime timeout)

baseline.description:
## The defect

The scheduled **Terraform Drift** workflow runs `terraform fmt -check` as its FIRST step, before `terraform plan`. `fmt -check` exits non-zero on any formatting deviation, so a purely cosmetic whitespace difference aborts the job and **`terraform plan` never executes**. The workflow's entire purpose — detecting infrastructure that has drifted from, or was never applied to match, the declared configuration — is silently skipped.

VERIFIED from run history on `main`:

```
2026-09-04T06:39 UTC  Terraform Drift  FAILURE  22s    (sha 6b034b9f)
2026-09-03T06:40 UTC  Terraform Drift  FAILURE  29s    (sha 3e04025b)
2026-09-02T06:44 UTC  Terraform Drift  success  6m07s
```

Failure log (run 33845247102):
```
plan  terraform fmt -check   monitoring_9ea3.tf
plan  terraform fmt -check   ##[error]Process completed with exit code 3.
```

Note the durations: 22s and 29s versus 6m07s for the successful run. The short runtime is the signature — the job died before doing any real work.

## What it cost

This is not hypothetical. While drift detection was blinded, story S1 of epic 6202 landed code declaring a dedicated gate-scratch EBS volume, its attachment, and two CloudWatch alarms — and **none of them were ever applied**. The volume does not exist in AWS or in Terraform state; the live metric `gate_scratch_mounted` has read 0 on all 51 datapoints since it began publishing, never once 1. Gates continued writing scratch to the root filesystem, which is the exact state ADR 0112 exists to prevent.

**Drift detection is the control that would have reported those declared-but-unapplied resources, and a whitespace nit switched it off for two days.** The story closed green on code evidence in the meantime.

## The general shape

This is the "absence of execution reported as success/failure without anyone noticing WHAT did not run" class that has now recurred repeatedly in this repo (9a17's worker kill, 90c7's vacuous vote, 1ef8's vacuously-passing AC3, docker-storage-cap's SIGHUP reload reporting a cap "in effect"). Here the run did go red, so it was not falsely green — but it went red for a cosmetic reason that reads as trivial, and nothing distinguished "formatting is off" from "we have not looked for drift in 48 hours".

## Current status

The formatting fix has landed: `cad66dd237cc` "Format monitoring_9ea3.tf to satisfy fmt gate" (2026-09-04 09:54 UTC, present on origin/main). `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform` now exits 0 locally. The next scheduled run (~2026-09-05 06:40 UTC) should clear fmt and reach `plan` — **but that has not yet been observed**, and when it does run it should report the two missing gate-scratch resources as drift.

So the immediate blockage is cleared. This ticket is about the ORDERING, which is unchanged and will do the same thing the next time any `.tf` file is misformatted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A formatting-only defect in any `infra/terraform/*.tf` file no longer prevents
      `terraform plan` from running in the Drift workflow. Prove it with a run (or a test
      harness) in which `fmt -check` would fail and `plan` still executes and reports.
- [ ] AC2 — A formatting failure is still SURFACED, not silently dropped. Whatever the fix
      (reorder, `continue-on-error` with an explicit later gate, split into independent jobs),
      the run must still tell an operator that formatting is wrong.
- [ ] AC3 — Drift findings and formatting findings are DISTINGUISHABLE in the run's outcome, so
      "we did not look for drift" can never again be indistinguishable from "whitespace is
      wrong". A reader must be able to tell which occurred without opening logs.
- [ ] AC4 — A test or documented check pins AC1, so a future edit cannot silently restore the
      blocking order.

## Non-goals

Not changing what drift is checked, not changing alarm or volume definitions, and not applying any Terraform — `terraform apply` is operator-only. This ticket is purely about the workflow's step ordering and result legibility.
baseline.summary: Terraform Drift workflow runs fmt -check before plan, so a whitespace defect blinds drift detection entirely: 2 days blind, hid an entire unapplied EBS volume + 2 alarms
